b11ecf768e1d4b63736e2bfc970b478883245310.abstract: Artificial intelligence is transforming assistive technologies, yet many systems remain reactive, fragmented, and insufficiently personalized for individuals with disabilities and neurodivergent conditions. This chapter examines the architectural, design, and governance foundations of trustworthy agentic assistive systems. It synthesizes limitations of conventional approaches, including restricted adaptability, low interoperability, and weak support for user autonomy, and introduces a taxonomy of agentic architectures to guide scalable deployment. The chapter proposes a multi-agent framework integrating multimodal interaction, hybrid reasoning, explainable AI, and health-aware data to enable context-sensitive support. It further addresses privacy, ethical governance, and responsible institutional adoption while outlining future research directions. By bridging architectural innovation with human-centered design, this work advances a forward-looking vision for inclusive intelligent environments.

title: Empowering Visually Disabled Users Through Web Accessibility
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Improving Disability Support and Institutional Performance With AI
2a981e51dafd42d4a65ac7fb41751a1eaef0fc09.abstract: The Indian Institutes of Technology (IITs), often categorised as Institutions of Eminence (IoE) in India, are set as the standards of measurement for the rest of academia. In this regard, the purpose of this paper is to evaluate the accessibility standard of the IIT Library websites in terms of the perceivable guidelines of the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (v. 2.1) using the Siteimprove Accessibility Checker. To improve the level of analytical precision based on the policy, technological, and user layers' conceptual frameworks, the study employs an artificial intelligence (AI)-based evaluation. The results indicate that there are considerable accessibility barriers in the various success criteria, such as non-textual content, information organisation, colour use, contrast ratio, and text images. Functional and visually organised designs notwithstanding, there are still critical gaps in ensuring the inclusion of visually impaired users. It also suggests the use of evidence-supported measures to enhance digital inclusivity and fair access in academic library settings.

title: AI-Driven Mindfulness-Based Mental Health Support for Mothers of Children With Autism
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Improving Disability Support and Institutional Performance With AI
10df4f7f68f110e4f51b72d7d7994767a18827d5.abstract: Mothers caring for children with Autism Spectrum Disorder often face ongoing stress, emotional challenges, and significant caregiving responsibilities. These factors can affect family dynamics and the quality of support services available for disabilities. Although traditional counselling can offer some psychological relief, it may lack personalization, scalability, or ongoing monitoring. This chapter presents a mindfulness-based intervention enhanced by artificial intelligence, utilizing established techniques like Mindfulness-Based Stress Reduction to provide flexible and accessible mental health resources. By combining AI with structured mindfulness practices, this approach seeks to improve emotional regulation, promote increased caregiver engagement, and foster better collaboration with disability service organizations. The chapter emphasizes that AI-enhanced mindfulness can serve as a valuable resource to bolster caregiver resilience and facilitate more efficient and responsive delivery of disability services.

title: Leveraging Artificial Intelligence for Financial Accountability and Disability-Inclusive Resource Management
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Improving Disability Support and Institutional Performance With AI
b0a48873a40bf2af1d77ea9bc6a2a13250d09444.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming institutional financial management by improving transparency, accountability, and evidence-based decision-making. This chapter examines how AI strengthens budgeting, financial reporting, fraud detection, procurement, and performance measurement while advancing disability-inclusive resource management. It discusses the conceptual foundations of AI adoption, relevant theoretical perspectives, and practical applications that support equitable resource allocation and accessibility investments. The chapter also addresses governance, ethical considerations, data privacy, implementation strategies, emerging technologies, and persistent challenges affecting AI adoption. It concludes that responsible AI implementation, supported by effective governance, skilled personnel, quality data, and inclusive policies, can enhance financial accountability, optimise institutional performance, and promote sustainable disability-inclusive financial management across educational and public institutions.

title: AI-Enabled Assistive Ecosystems

62cd247f331f83f1c0f26038f320b16ed7a2729a.abstract: Higher education institutions worldwide are increasingly prioritizing inclusive learning environments that accommodate the diverse needs of students with disabilities. Advances in artificial intelligence (AI) have introduced transformative opportunities for developing assistive ecosystems that support accessibility, personalized learning, and institutional efficiency. AI-enabled technologies—including intelligent tutoring systems, speech recognition, computer vision, and predictive analytics—can significantly enhance disability support services while improving educational outcomes and institutional performance. This chapter explores the concept of AI-enabled assistive ecosystems within higher education and examines how integrated AI technologies can support students with physical, sensory, cognitive, and learning disabilities. The chapter analyzes the potential benefits of AI-driven accessibility tools, institutional data analytics, and adaptive learning platforms for promoting inclusive education.

title: AI-Powered Predictive Analytics for Early Identification of Learning Disabilities

709271a44ff17eea59ee0f82fd0b253589129b6d.abstract: Learning disabilities (LDs) need to be identified at an early age so that they can be addressed promptly so that they can utilize their academic performance and inclusive learning. Conventional diagnostic procedures are mostly reactive, time-consuming and subjective and rely on the use of standardized tests, teacher observations, as well as, clinical evaluations. The development of artificial intelligence (AI) and predictive analytics allows active risk screening based on machine learning and deep learning, and explainable AI models. This chapter investigates predictive pipelines, benchmarking models (SVM) and random forests, (CNN and LSTM) and validation, ethics, privacy, and adaptive intervention frameworks in an attempt to encourage equitable, transparent, and scalable learning intervention systems.

title: AI-Supported Inclusive Teaching, Learning, and Assessment Practices

Improving Disability Support and Institutional Performance With AI
35362e4a8904c70026ade7220de44f279205c36f.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is rapidly transforming educational systems, offering innovative pathways for enhancing inclusive teaching, learning and assessment practices. In the context of disability support, AI-driven tools provide opportunities to personalize instruction, improve accessibility and strengthen institutional performance through data-informed decision-making. However, despite these potentials, some educational institutions face challenges in effectively integrating AI into inclusive education practices. This chapter therefore examines how AI-supported instructional strategies, adaptive learning systems and intelligent assessment tools can address diverse learner needs. It critically analyzes ethical concerns, implementation barriers and capacity gaps associated with AI adoption in education. The chapter proposes a conceptual framework linking AI integration, inclusive pedagogy and institutional outcomes. It further provides actionable suggestions for stakeholders seeking to leverage AI for sustainable disability support and improved institutional effectiveness.

title: Artificial Intelligence-Enabled Early Warning Systems for the Psychosocial Wellbeing of Students With Hearing Loss in Inclusive Educational Settings
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Improving Disability Support and Institutional Performance With AI
669f7e03da104421b0a6e663e8a37fcc1dd968f9.abstract: Students with hearing loss in inclusive settings frequently face psychosocial challenges including social isolation, communication fatigue, and emotional disengagement that develop gradually and evade conventional monitoring systems focused solely on academic metrics. This chapter proposes an AI-enabled early warning system (EWS) to proactively identify emotional distress and social withdrawal among deaf or hard of hearing (DHH) students. Integrating multimodal data streams, machine learning, transformer-based NLP, and explainable AI (XAI), the system generates actionable risk indicators for educators and counselors. Grounded in Social Inclusion Theory, Universal Design for Learning, Ecological Systems Theory, and Affective Computing Theory, it functions as a human-centered decision-support platform rather than a surveillance tool. Ethical dimensions including data privacy, algorithmic bias, transparency, and informed consent are critically examined alongside a roadmap for evidence-based implementation.

This chapter examines the landscape of AI-driven assistive tools—including speech recognition, adaptive learning platforms, natural language processing, and predictive analytics—and their role in advancing inclusive education. Drawing on recent systematic reviews and empirical studies, it critically evaluates opportunities such as personalized accommodation, improved accessibility, and universal design for learning (UDL) integration, alongside challenges including algorithmic bias, data privacy, and digital equity. Frameworks for ethical AI deployment and institutional policy recommendations are presented. The chapter concludes with future directions for sustainable, human-centered AI assistive ecosystems in higher education.

title: Assistive Tools to Intelligent Systems

Improving Disability Support and Institutional Performance With AI
81d3092bd2629e50c4d7d76daf5535aa4c41a4b1.abstract: Artificial intelligence is changing how disability assistance systems work by combining personalized institutional services with proactive, data-driven methods. This chapter reviews the old support systems that often react slowly and create extra work and looks at how AI tools like predictive analytics, natural language processing, and intelligent decision-support systems can improve how institutions operate and provide help for disabilities. It discusses applications including automated management of reasonable accommodations, AI-powered virtual assistants, and accessible learning environments that enable earlier identification of support needs. The chapter also analyzes how institutions can use AI-generated insights to optimize resource allocation, strengthen regulatory compliance, and operationalize inclusive policies. Finally, it addresses key ethical challenges, including algorithmic bias, data privacy, and disability-inclusive design, and outlines principles for responsible implementation of AI in disability assistance.

This chapter explores AI tools—such as adaptive learning platforms, NLP assistants, early-alert systems, and automated accommodations—used to address barriers faced by students with diverse disabilities. Grounded in Universal Design for Learning and the social model of disability, it reframes AI as a means to enhance student autonomy rather than just improve services. It also examines risks like algorithmic bias, surveillance, and data misuse. The chapter proposes a governance framework emphasizing equity, transparency, and student agency, and outlines key directions for future research.

title: A Critical Exploration of How Artificial Intelligence Enhances Accommodation for Learners With Learning Barriers

11fdfb17830b101b6c7daa5ba02b67cf843b3cbd.abstract: The purpose of this chapter is to critically explore how Artificial Intelligence (AI) can enhance curriculum design, content delivery and assessment strategies to accommodate learners with barriers to learning. The chapter identify sources and types of barriers to learning, pointing out the relevance of AI to teaching and learning as research studies have shown that it can personalize instruction, automate timely feedback, generate formative assessment and identify learning achievement and challenges. The chapter shows the readers how AI can enhance curriculum design, content delivery and assessment strategies to accommodate learners with barriers to learning by using planned Individual Educational Programme (IEP), data-driven analysis, adaptive learning platforms that dynamically adjust content difficulty, sequencing, and presentation formats in real time. Also, AI-powered tools are used such as speech-to-text, text-to-speech, to establish flexibility, personalization and promotes equitable participation for all learners to uphold equity, ethics, and human values in education.

title: Solar Thermal District Heating and Cooling for Smart, Sustainable, AI-Optimized Cities
container-title: Renewable Energy Systems for Smart Cities and Urban Sustainability
e1b09c035b4f62c4219b35e79df5a81dce545160.abstract: Rapid urbanization and climate imperatives place cities at the center of energy transformation, yet thermal demand roughly half of urban energy end-use remains under addressed by electricity focused renewable strategies. This chapter, per the authors, examines solar thermal district heating and cooling (STDHC) systems as foundational infrastructure for sustainable smart cities. It reviews collector technologies and seasonal thermal storage configurations, then analyzes integration across the physical, cyber, and application layers of smart city architecture, emphasizing digital twins, IoT sensing, and machine-learning optimization including model predictive control and reinforcement learning. International case studies from Canada, Denmark, Croatia, and China demonstrate solar fractions above 50% and substantial carbon reductions. Lifecycle, cost, and energy-justice analyses benchmark performance and equity, while the closing sections identify deployment barriers and propose a research agenda spanning compact storage, federated learning, and policy alignment with SDG 7 and SDG 11.

title: AI-Driven Smart Microgrids and Electric Mobility Integration for Sustainable Urban Energy Systems in Smart Cities
container-title: Renewable Energy Systems for Smart Cities and Urban Sustainability
ad526fc230936b72f961c3c06eae6c95043b0400.abstract: For the development of sustainable urban energy systems in smart cities, this chapter focuses on the integration of electric mobility systems with AI-driven smart microgrids. It demonstrates the contribution of electric vehicles (EVs) through vehicle-to-grid (V2G) capabilities and variable demand, while smart microgrids enable effective management of dispersed energy resources and dispersed energy generation. The role of Artificial intelligence towards energy distribution optimization, real-time decision-making, and demand forecasting is emphasized along with identifying major obstacles including consumer acceptance, regulatory restrictions, interoperability problems, and discussing worldwide policy trends, the chapter provides an integrated conceptual framework offering insights into how the sustainability, dependability, and energy efficiency might improve urban settings through the integration of artificial intelligence (AI), EVs, and microgrids.

title: AI-Driven Federated Learning Frameworks for Privacy-Preserving Smart Urban Energy Management
container-title: Renewable Energy Systems for Smart Cities and Urban Sustainability
f3701a620a132989be535b1f5024487d68b902b2.abstract: The growing complexity of urban energy systems with smartness requires intelligent solutions that are privacy friendly to manage the distributed energy resources efficiently. This chapter introduces a federated learning model that is AI-powered and in this system, model training is performed in an intelligent grid, micro grid, and IoT-based devices, without the exchange of raw data. The strategy improves accuracy in load forecasting, efficiency of energy use, and lessens the amount of overhead in communication besides maintaining data privacy and security. The framework combines edge computing and state-of-the-art AI to promote scalable and adaptive energy management to add to sustainable, resilient, and human-centric smart city ecosystems.

title: Beyond Green Promises
container-title: Enabling Human Transformation Through Socio-Technical Systems in Industry 4.0
474dc4312b293994049b37e3019b72b04cfc3411.abstract: This chapter examines the evolving relationship between artificial intelligence and sustainability in tourism within the broader context of Industry 4.0 and ongoing digital transformation processes. While AI-driven technologies are widely recognized for their capacity to enhance operational efficiency, optimize resource utilization, and support sustainable development goals, they simultaneously introduce significant conceptual, ethical, and governance-related challenges. Drawing on a socio-technical perspective, this study moves beyond purely technological or outcome-oriented approaches and explores how artificial intelligence reshapes not only the operationalization of sustainability but also its meaning, representation, and lived experience within tourism systems. The chapter introduces the concept of rehumanizing sustainability as a conceptual and practical framework for addressing these challenges. This approach emphasizes the reintegration of human values, agency, and experiential dimensions into AI-driven systems.

title: AFRIKA TARIGʻIDA JOʻXORI PASHSHASI (ANTHOMYIIDAE)GA QARSHI KURASHNING BIOLOGIK SAMARADORLIGI
container-title: Agro ilm
582c81d30ddfbf9e19997a9ac90076167e641264.abstract: The corn moth overwinters primarily in the soil in the pupal stage. In the spring, as temperatures rise, the adults emerge and lay eggs on newly sown plots. Upon hatching, the larvae penetrate the soil and feed on germinating seeds, root collars, and young stems. As a result, seedling growth ceases or the plants wither. Development takes 20—40 days, depending on climatic conditions. Most species produce 2—4 generations per year. This article examines the development of the corn moth (Anthomyiidae) and the biological efficacy of control measures against it.

title: СИММЕНТАЛ ЗОТЛИ СИГИРЛАРНИНГ ПУШТДОРЛИК ХУСУСИЯТЛАРИ

ccdb02224fa42451b83471c55b37d01ffeb8ae95.abstract: The article presents information on the characteristics of Simmental cows belonging to different production types. The study found that the age at first calving was 789.5 days for cows of the dairy type and 795.1 days for those of the dairy-beef type; these figures were 11.1 and 5.5 days lower, respectively, than the age at first calving for cows of the beef-dairy type. Additionally, the service period lasted 78.3 days for dairy-type cows and 81.2 days for dairy-beef-type cows—4.2 and 1.3 days shorter, respectively, than the service period for beef-dairy-type cows. Research findings regarding the duration of the service period indicate that the cow itself is a primary factor determining reproductive performance; this highlights the importance of effectively utilizing cows of dairy and dual-purpose (dairy-beef) types for milk production.

c07429793f1242d6e73e04acbb422ad582a3fa1d.abstract: The article examines the dynamics of sediment deposition at the intake section of the Qarshi Main Canal (QMC) under damless (free) water intake from the Amudarya River, together with the role of dredgers in the overall volume of cleaning works. Based on field monitoring data, the distribution of sediment along the canal length, as well as the technical condition and placement of the fleet of 17 dredgers along the canal, were analysed. It was found that the PK 0-40 segment of the canal intake accumulates more than 85% of the total sediment volume, making it the most heavily loaded section. Recommendations are proposed for the rational placement of dredgers along the canal and for adjusting the cleaning schedule to seasonal sediment inflow.

0cba3c6a2b51e67e9600d4233ff865069da94d2c.abstract: The article evaluates the pre-irrigation soil moisture regimes (70-70-70, 75-75-75, and 80-80-80% of FC) and the dynamics of leaf cell sap concentration (CSC) in winter wheat grown on non-saline soils during 2020–2021. The results indicated that as pre-irrigation soil moisture increased, leaf CSC values proportionally decreased (13.82–16.31%), whereas toward the end of the growing season, values rose to 17.36–19.50% due to physiological tissue senescence. The study substantiates the high efficacy of using a refractometric method for rapid determination of irrigation timing based on CSC to enhance water-use efficiency.

The highest yield, 29.2 t ha⁻¹, was obtained at 0.4 mm min⁻¹, compared with 22.7 t ha⁻¹ under furrow irrigation.

Separating current and potential suitability and using GIS zoning makes it possible to select irrigation technologies that better match local conditions.

de5c8f6b87e3fd2e38c05b7f6f98a1efc6421451.abstract: This article highlights the agrochemical properties of irrigated gray-earth meadow soils of Sharaf Rashidovsky district of the Jizzakh Free Economic Zone (JEZ), reserves of humus, total nitrogen, total phosphorus, and potassium. There is a high probability of heavy metal pollution in the region near industrial zones, free economic zones, and irrigation networks. Since these soils have a relatively humic layer, as well as a unique water-retaining structure, heavy metals can accumulate in the soil and negatively affect its agrochemical properties. Heavy metals adhere to soil colloids and retain their activity in the soil for a long time. In the soil under study, the lead content of Pb is 40-80 mg/kg (the norm is 32 mg/kg or more), cadmium CD is 0.5 - 2.0 mg/kg (the norm is 0.5 mg/kg or more), zinc Zn is 150-220 mg/kg (the norm is 100 mg/kg or more). This situation indicates an increase in the level of pollution combined with salinization and carbonate content of irrigated gray-earth meadow soils.

c509063f35d9011ed66639c6c18d0a92b4359972.abstract: The article presents research on optimizing the design and operating parameters of a rotary ripper for minimum tillage of the ridge top using mathematical planning methods. The effects of the number of ripper discs, vertical load, and travel speed on the degree of soil crumbling and draft resistance were studied. Based on the obtained regression equations, the optimal values for the working organs were determined, ensuring high-quality tillage of the ridge top in accordance with agrotechnical requirements.

title: LEGUME CROP PRODUCTION IN UZBEKISTAN: AN EMPIRICAL ANALYSIS OF DETERMINANTS
container-title: Agro ilm
03504e16fb7ff633b3ad6671704c4e70d6e34612.abstract: This paper examines factors affecting legume production in Uzbekistan using cross-sectional data from 1,225 farmers across 12 districts in the UzFarmBarometer 2024 database. A probit model identifies factors associated with the probability of legume adoption. Results show that older farmers are less likely to cultivate legumes, while larger households and more experienced farmers are more likely to adopt them. Earlier-established farms also show lower adoption. Distance to input markets is positively associated with adoption, whereas distance to output markets is negatively associated with it, reflecting differences in input dependence and transaction costs. We suggest that improving rural market infrastructure, extension services, and stable labor arrangements could support legume cultivation.

title: AI adoption in purchasing and supply management: how institutional voids rewire the UTAUT framework
container-title: Modern Supply Chain Research and Applications
0bcd714cb04d0b263189b430cff3e961768ff573.abstract: Purpose This study investigates how institutional voids and behavioral factors jointly drive artificial intelligence (AI) adoption in purchasing and supply management (PSM) within emerging economies. Design/methodology/approach Survey data from 200 PSM professionals in Morocco were analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) to test an integrated UTAUT–institutional theory framework. Findings Performance expectancy (PE) (ß = 0.530) and social influence (ß = 0.453) primarily drive behavioral intention (BI), while coercive pressure is non-significant (ß = 0.050, p = 0.260). Facilitating conditions (FC) (ß = 0.472) and (BI) (ß = 0.497) exert near-equal direct effects on actual use, confirming an “infrastructure imperative”. Post-hoc multi-group analysis reveals that PE dominates predictive AI adoption, whereas effort expectancy dominates Generative AI. Practical implications Organizations in emerging economies must pair AI software procurement with dedicated infrastructure, data governance and peer-led change management rather than relying on unsupported mandates. Originality/value This study demonstrates that institutional voids modify the UTAUT nomological network by elevating FC to a primary co-determinant of technology use, proving infrastructure readiness equals user intention in driving adoption.

title: Future of work in the era of AI: how technology strategy shapes daily job roles
container-title: International Journal of Organizational Analysis
31a1acb996d897d7876f2aa832ce5ad1572c2f0e.abstract: Purpose This study aims to explore the impact of organizational technology strategies, particularly in the context of artificial intelligence (AI), on employees’ daily job activities. It also looks at the extent of the transformation and the role of leadership, supportive of innovation and cultural change, in reinforcing the transformation. Design/methodology/approach The researcher adopted a quantitative research design based on the survey data collected from employees in various industries in Pakistan. The researcher used structural equation modeling to analyze the relationships among technology strategies, organizational facilitators and the transformation of job roles. Findings The research shows that organizations that implement AI and automation alongside digitized processes and advanced data analysis capabilities will experience fundamental changes in their employees’ work functions, skills and job duties. The implementation of digital strategies enhances operational efficiency, but their impact extends beyond this benefit, as they completely transform how work is executed. The presence of an innovation-supportive culture together with strong leadership commitment creates an enhanced effect. The combination of encouragement of organizational experimentation and active leadership support for technological change results in more visible and positive changes in job responsibilities. Practical implications The research findings demonstrate that organizations need to combine technology investments with operational changes to achieve successful digital transformation outcomes. Organizations must establish supportive cultures together with proactive leadership to assist employees throughout the process of organizational change. Organizations need to develop their employees’ skills and build adaptable workforces while maintaining open communication to implement meaningful job role changes that last over time. Originality/value The research contributes to the future of work literature by examining how workers change their job functions at the individual-employee level rather than observing outcomes at the organizational level. The research describes how organizations use technology strategies and organizational enablers to create distinct work environments for the AI age by integrating Job Demands–Resources and Socio-Technical Systems perspectives.

title: The copilot paradox: configurational pathways to human-AI symbiosis in knowledge work
container-title: International Journal of Organizational Analysis
10429646653846e10fef0781eea8935c49efcda2.abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine the “Copilot Paradox” in safety-critical operations, offering insights into how the chronic tension between the algorithm’s increased efficiency and operational vulnerability is subdued through socio-cognitive configurations across time. Design/methodology/approach With the use of a two-wave longitudinal fuzzy-set Qualitative Comparative Analysis (fsQCA), the paper explores the changing dynamics of human–artificial intelligence (AI) symbiosis in the oil and gas industry. Findings Analysis of necessity shows that there is no single condition required in all cases. Sufficiency analysis reveals three distinct, equifinal pathways: buffering, synergy and substitution. At early adoption, institutional re-skilling coupled with psychological safety acts as a buffering mechanism against job insecurity induced by AI. As integration progresses, synergy (fuelled by empowering leadership) and substitution (where team resources fill the gaps in leadership) come to dominate. Practical implications Team psychological safety and capability building are structural safeguards for managers in high-reliability sectors, not optional cultural flourishes. These lessons point to pathways for realising AI copilots while preserving human agency and operational resiliency. Originality/value This paper contributes to paradox theory by developing a socio-cognitive infrastructure that highlights its dynamic, temporal configuration and causal asymmetries. Methodologically, it showcases the new promise of longitudinal fsQCA to model dynamics in algorithms’ infusion by capturing their embeddedness through time.

title: From risk management to AI-enabled governance: five intellectual orientations in EPC and infrastructure project risk governance
container-title: Journal of Engineering, Design and Technology
262b73632bb16a2f06249b0dfe727ae37edc8674.abstract: Purpose This study aims to synthesise the intellectual development of engineering–procurement–construction and infrastructure project risk governance and examine whether bibliometric evidence supports five overlapping intellectual orientations. Design/methodology/approach The study combined bibliometric analysis with Bibliometrix/Biblioshiny, VOSviewer and a scripted workflow to examine 173 Scopus-indexed publications (1999–2026). The analytical corpus was derived through relevance validation of 678 candidate records, with provenance checked against an 801-row master ledger. Fifteen provisional 2026 records were excluded from temporal comparisons. Findings The analysis identified five orientations: risk analysis and control (53 documents), performance and overrun (80), governance and relational mechanisms (52), digital information integration (7) and artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled decision support (18). The share of period publications addressing performance and overrun increased from 34.7 % in 1999–2018 to 59.7 % in 2023–2025, whereas the digital and AI orientations remained comparatively limited. These patterns concern the published literature and do not establish organizational maturity or realised capability. Research limitations/implications Scopus coverage, title/abstract-based relevance validation, citation lag, analytical thresholds and interpretive coding delimit the findings. Project-level research is required to test the proposed relationships. Practical implications The orientations provide structured review prompts for risk processes, outcome linkage, decision rights, information integration and human oversight of predictive systems; they are not intended as a diagnostic maturity instrument. Originality/value The study connects construction risk, megaproject governance and construction AI through an auditable corpus and an evidence-bounded conceptual framework.

title: Digital and AI tools in informal care: understanding caregivers’ experiences in rural Nigeria
container-title: Working with Older People
3d95ea5e81a5dd3ac98c9f9e80e04a8c952edbad.abstract: Purpose Although informal caregiving for older adults is well-researched, a significant gap exists in understanding how informal caregivers navigate their caregiving roles with the help of digital technologies, especially in rural Nigeria, where internet connectivity is poor and access to digital devices is limited. This study aims to explore how informal caregivers in rural Nigeria use digital technology to support care for older adults. Design/methodology/approach The study adopted a qualitative descriptive approach, data were collected from 10 informal caregivers, using semi-structured interviews. The data were further analysed thematically using NVivo 14. Findings Results identified that caregivers use digital technology for communication and care coordination, learning and self-empowerment, responding to emergency situations, improving efficiency, reducing stress and maintaining contact between older adults and their diaspora family members. The study also found poor access and limited internet infrastructure as barriers to the use of digital technology to improve caregiving. Research limitations/implications Only caregivers in rural areas were interviewed. This excluded the experiences of caregivers in urban areas, who may face urban economic stressors that shape their overall caregiving experience and their use of digital technology for caregiving. Practical implications The findings highlight the potential of digital technology to support informal caregiving in rural Nigeria. Improving access to affordable digital devices, reliable internet connectivity and digital literacy can enhance care coordination, caregiver support, emergency response and communication with older adults and their families. Originality/value This study is important because it provides new insight into how informal caregivers in rural Nigeria use digital technology to support older adults despite limited connectivity and access to digital devices. It highlights both the potential of digital tools to strengthen caregiving and the infrastructural barriers that must be addressed.

title: Integrating System-Oriented Concept Map Extension (SOCMEs) in collaborative online international learning to develop system thinking among undergraduate chemistry students in Indonesia and United States
container-title: Chemistry Teacher International
a98acf9db48f94f18b4c2d74fc8fb7c03804ffde.abstract: Abstract The integration of innovative pedagogical approaches in environmental chemistry education is essential to foster a comprehensive understanding of global environmental issues. This study explores the application of System-Oriented Concept Map Extension (SOCME) within the context of a collaborative online international learning (COIL) program involving students from Indonesia and the United States of America (USA). The study involved a subset of undergraduate students ( N = 33) enrolled in various chemistry courses (general chemistry, organic chemistry, and environmental chemistry) who volunteered to participate in supplemental instruction offered jointly by an Indonesian university and a USA college. Students were organized into small groups and tasked with creating SOCMEs related to specific environmental issues. These SOCMEs were then presented and discussed during synchronous video conferencing sessions as part of the COIL activities. Data collection included post intervention surveys, SOCME diagram analysis, and observations of group interactions during the collaborative learning activities. The results showed that both the analysis of SOCME diagrams and the post-intervention questionnaire results indicate that Indonesian and USA students were able to develop meaningful connections between chemical concepts, environmental impacts, economic considerations, and societal issues.

title: Librarians' perspectives on AI for environmental sustainability in Ghanaian academic libraries
container-title: Library Hi Tech
931d99d9c196e1b88e58ba8390c4eca27c050aac.abstract: Purpose This study examined academic librarians' perspectives on the potential of artificial intelligence to advance environmental sustainability through sustainable library practices and efficient service delivery. Design/methodology/approach A qualitative approach was adopted, drawing on semi-structured interviews with 21 academic librarians and guided by the Technology Acceptance Model. Thematic analysis was used to identify key patterns and perspectives on AI adoption for environmental sustainability in academic libraries. Findings The study found that academic librarians recognize AI's potential to advance environmental sustainability through intelligent energy management, predictive maintenance, environmental monitoring, and sustainability planning, yet its practical implementation remains limited. Research limitations/implications The qualitative design and small sample limit generalizability; however, the findings provide contextual insights and a basis for broader research across diverse library settings. Practical implications The findings recommend that universities and library management integrate AI into sustainability planning through effective governance, improved digital infrastructure, and continuous AI literacy training, supported by national policies and investment in responsible AI innovation. Social implications The study highlights the value of AI in advancing environmental sustainability in libraries, emphasizing the need for educational initiatives, institutional policies, and responsible technology adoption. Originality/value This study provides timely empirical insight into AI-enabled environmental sustainability in Ghanaian academic libraries, highlighting the critical gap between librarians' awareness and perceived potential of AI and its limited practical implementation.

title: Efficacy of Stellate Ganglion Block for Preventing Postoperative Atrial Fibrillation After Cardiac Surgery: A Randomized, Double‐Blind, Placebo‐Controlled Trial
container-title: Journal of the American Heart Association
47d160a0277168adf9351a8df9bee14429b106b7.abstract: Background Stellate ganglion block (SGB) may reduce postoperative atrial fibrillation (POAF) by modulating the autonomic nervous system. This study evaluated the efficacy of preoperative SGB in preventing POAF following cardiac surgery. Methods In this single‐center, randomized, double‐blind, placebo‐controlled trial, 140 patients undergoing valve surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass were assigned (1:1) to ultrasound‐guided right SGB with 7 mL of 0.5% ropivacaine or 7 mL of normal saline. The primary outcome was the incidence of POAF from postoperative day 0 to day 7 or until discharge. Results A total of 132 patients completed the study and were included in the modified intention‐to‐treat population (SGB group: n=65; saline group: n=67). POAF occurred in 43% of the SGB group and 40% of the saline group (odds ratio [OR], 0.99 [95% CI, 0.46–2.15], adjusted P =0.989). The SGB group demonstrated a lower incidence of intraoperative ventricular fibrillation/ventricular tachycardia requiring defibrillation after aortic cross‐clamp release (6% versus 19%; OR, 0.21 [95% CI, 0.06–0.80]; adjusted P =0.022), lower postoperative high‐sensitivity troponin I levels (median difference: −2562 ng/L [95% CI, −4301 to −45]; P =0.045), and a reduced risk of postoperative acute kidney injury (5% versus 18%; OR, 0.24 [95% CI, 0.06–0.98]; adjusted P =0.046). Conclusions While preoperative SGB did not reduce the incidence of POAF, it was associated with potential benefits, including a lower requirement for intraoperative defibrillation attributable to ventricular arrhythmias, attenuated myocardial injury (as indicated by lower high‐sensitivity troponin I levels), and a decreased risk of postoperative acute kidney injury. Registration URL: https://www.chictr.org.cn ; URL Identifier: ChiCTR2300068572.

title: Capabilities shaping institutional adoption: modeling generative AI adoption in higher education
container-title: Journal of Knowledge Management
08a009fe077bc5af12d714b4d60c2ab8c6973296.abstract: Purpose Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is rapidly transforming higher education, yet its successful institutional adoption extends beyond technological capability to require effective knowledge governance, organizational readiness and coordinated decision-making. This study aims to structurally model the CSFs for GenAI adoption in education using an integrated interpretive structural modeling (ISM)–DEMATEL approach. The authors frame GenAI adoption explicitly as a knowledge management problem, analyzing how governance, infrastructure and privacy conditions enable or inhibit institutional capabilities for creating, sharing and governing GenAI-empowered knowledge. Design/methodology/approach The authors identified ten CSFs through a structured literature review and classified them as enablers, capabilities or outcomes across governance, infrastructure, data privacy, analytics, user experience and academic integrity. To analyze the causal and hierarchical relationships among CSFs, an expert validation was conducted through DEMATEL analysis by 20 experts, followed by ISM modeling, which involved 16 experts. Findings DEMATEL identifies technical infrastructure and scalability (CSF-V), data privacy and security (CSF-VII) and integration with LMS/SSO/enterprise systems (CSF-IX) as prominent causal factors. ISM further positions CSF-V at the deepest foundational level, followed by AI governance, policy and ethics (CSF-III), while assessment integrity and academic honesty (CSF-X) occupies the terminal dependent level. The findings identify assessment integrity (CSF-X), prompt literacy (CSF-IV) and user experience (CSF-VI) as dependent factors, confirming that they emerge from structural readiness rather than acting as independent adoption determinants. Research limitations/implications Results are restricted to expert judgment and defined CSFs, which can reduce generalizability across diverse educational settings. Future research must involve larger samples, validate empirically and use longitudinal designs to study changing relations while also testing the knowledge governance mechanisms revealed in this research. Practical implications The model enables phased prioritization of CSFs for optimal implementation of GenAI. Foundational readiness requires infrastructure, system integration and data governance, followed by governance policies and faculty capacity development, before addressing user experience and academic integrity as dependent outcomes. Originality/value The research provides a systems approach to GenAI adoption in education by presenting an integrated ISM–DEMATEL framework based on TOE and DOI, grounded in knowledge governance theory. It aids authors’ understanding of how technological, organizational and knowledge governance dimensions must be sequentially aligned to enable better implementation of GenAI.

title: Optimising sleep regularity during shiftwork is important for cognitive performance, sleepiness and mood
container-title: SLEEP Advances
326808b9eddddc4876ce0bc2e746aab2575e2734.abstract: Abstract Sleep regularity is important for performance and wellbeing. Sleep regularity is underexplored in shiftworkers, a population that may struggle to maintain regular sleep timing due to unstable work hours. It is important to understand how sleep regularity relates to wellbeing and performance outcomes for shiftworkers. Using the sleep regularity index (SRI), we assessed the relationship of sleep regularity to performance and wellbeing in maritime watchstanding shiftworkers who worked two different schedules (known as “watchbills”). Active-duty sailors (N = 23, aged 25.96 ± 3.13 years, [mean ± standard deviation]) wore an actiwatch for ~14 days while underway on the 5-hrs on/10-hrs off watchbill, and four months later for ~10 days while on the 3-hrs on/9-hrs off watchbill. The psychomotor vigilance task (PVT) was administered 2 to 4 times daily during both underway periods; the Epworth Sleepiness Scale (ESS), Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI), and Profile of Mood States (POMS) were administered at the end of both data collection periods. High variability in SRI score was observed for shiftworkers on the same shift of the same schedule. Higher SRI scores were associated with faster reaction times (Spearman’s rho [ρ] = -0.73, p = .019) and better cognitive performance on seven other PVT metrics (all p &lt; .05), and reduced daytime sleepiness (ρ = -0.512, p = .013) and total mood disturbance (ρ = -0.634, p = .005). The study found that sleep regularity is an important dimension of sleep to optimise during shiftwork to improve cognitive performance and reduce daytime sleepiness and mood disturbance.

title: Facilitating generative mentoring in higher education: a systematic review and measurement framework for mentoring, generativity, and the minority tax
container-title: International Journal of Mentoring and Coaching in Education
1c4576303f7dc7a655cd1b351ac0a3834966b1b5.abstract: Purpose The purpose of this study is to synthesise how faculty mentoring in higher education has been evaluated in relation to mentor generativity and equity-related pressures (including the minority tax) and to propose a minimum measurement framework for valid evaluation. Design/methodology/approach A Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses 2020-guided systematic review was registered on the International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews (CRD42025647836). The review question was developed using a Sample, Phenomenon of Interest, Design, Evaluation, Research-informed approach appropriate to the inclusion of both quantitative and qualitative evidence. Scopus, Web of Science, ScienceDirect and EBSCOhost were searched from database inception to June 2025. Two reviewers independently screened and extracted data, study quality was appraised using design-appropriate tools, and findings were narratively synthesised. Findings Eight studies met the inclusion criteria (six quantitative, two qualitative), with most of the evidence from the USA. No study directly measured mentor generativity using validated generativity instruments; instead, studies relied on proxy outcomes (e.g. satisfaction, productivity, promotion). This limits conclusions about the construct validity of generativity and may obscure costs when mentoring demands are high and recognition is low, especially for historically marginalised faculty. Research limitations/implications The evidence base was small (eight studies), predominantly U.S.-based, methodologically heterogeneous, and reliant on proxy outcomes rather than validated measures of mentor generativity. These limitations precluded meta-analysis and causal inference. Future research should directly measure generativity alongside mentoring load, institutional recognition, strain, and equity-related indicators across more diverse regions, disciplines, and institutional contexts. Practical implications The framework provides institutions and researchers with a concise set of indicators to evaluate mentoring programmes, inform workload crediting and promotion criteria, and monitor equity in the distribution and recognition of mentoring labour. Originality/value This review reframes the evaluation of faculty mentoring as a construct-measurement problem and proposes a minimum measurement framework that distinguishes direct generativity from commonly used proxy outcomes. By integrating mentoring load, institutional recognition, strain, and equity considerations, the framework also provides a basis for empirically testing the proposed “generativity paradox”, the conditions under which mentoring may be experienced as renewing, burdensome, or both.

title: The relationship between AI awareness and thriving at work: exploring the moderated mediation model
container-title: European Journal of Training and Development
cfd18b7156538271965b458c0a8e74dbffca959e.abstract: Purpose Drawing on the socially embedded model of thriving and the conservation of resources model, this study aims to investigate the relationship between artificial intelligence (AI) awareness, seen as a hindrance stressor, and thriving at work. In particular, it explores how AI anxiety mediates this relationship and how self-efficacy moderates the mediating effect. Design/methodology/approach To securitize the study hypotheses, data were obtained from banking employees via an electronic questionnaire, yielding 320 valid responses. The proposed model relationships were assessed through partial least squares structural equation modeling and process analysis. Findings The results uncover that while AI awareness is not significantly linked to vitality, it is negatively correlated with learning. Furthermore, AI anxiety mediates the direct influence that AI awareness has on dimensions of thriving at work. In addition, self-efficacy acts as a buffer, mitigating the adverse indirect influence of AI awareness on thriving at work through AI anxiety. Practical implications This study highlights the need for organizations adopting AI-driven systems to execute‎ initiatives that mitigate AI-induced stress, thereby fostering employee thriving. It is recommended that organizations offer targeted training and digital literacy programs, alongside interventions designed to enhance self-efficacy, to bolster employee well-being amid rapid technological change. Originality/value This study highlights the need for organizations adopting AI-driven systems to execute‎ initiatives that mitigate AI-induced stress, thereby fostering employee thriving. It is recommended that organizations offer targeted training and revise their role descriptions, alongside interventions designed to enhance self-efficacy, to bolster employee well-being amid rapid technological change.

title: Managing critical raw materials supply chains: aligning capabilities and strategic levers for effective strategy formation under uncertainty
container-title: International Journal of Physical Distribution & Logistics Management
3b79bec66e149196eeab7e3db690a1396d564c66.abstract: Purpose This study examines how firms should design supply chain strategies to secure Critical Raw Materials (CRM), which are scarce, geographically concentrated, and exposed to geopolitical and institutional interference. These features generate structural uncertainty that amplifies normative and mimetic pressures on strategic decision-making, exposing firms to strategic isomorphic bias and leading organizations to replicate legitimized sourcing templates rather than formulate strategies calibrated to their specific dependence structure. Design/methodology/approach Drawing on Resource Dependence Theory, the study links key strategic levers (Supplier Substitutability, Discretion over the Resource, and Importance of the Resource) to underlying supply chain capabilities (resilience, agility, flexibility, sustainability, efficiency). A rank-ordered logit choice experiment with supply chain managers elicits preferred capability configurations in CRM supply scenarios, allowing the inference of the associated strategic levers while reducing strategic isomorphic bias in self-reported strategies. Findings Results show that Supplier Substitutability emerges as the dominant strategic lever for CRM-intensive supply chains. Resilience and sustainability are identified as the core capabilities underpinning this lever, supporting rapid reconfiguration of the supply base and the maintenance of legitimacy and stakeholder support under uncertainty. Originality/value The study theorizes an inside-out, bottom-up capability-driven strategy formation process, in which supply chain capabilities serve to infer effective strategic postures. It also demonstrates the value of experimental choice designs to reduce strategic and institutional bias in supply chain management research, particularly in politically sensitive domains such as the energy transition.

title: Demystifying generative AI adoption in higher education: an integrated GRAI–AKM framework
container-title: Journal of Knowledge Management
2d81d35ddbb0a163d25a04512796c4f2fe000a1d.abstract: Purpose Generative Artificial Intelligence (Gen AI) is rapidly transforming higher education, yet successful institutional adoption requires effective knowledge governance, organizational readiness and coordinated decision-making. Existing studies have predominantly relied on individual-level technology acceptance models, providing limited insight into organizational and knowledge management capabilities for sustainable implementation. Design/methodology/approach A qualitative research design was employed using open-ended written responses from 20 academic professionals recruited through Prolific. The qualitative responses were analyzed using thematic analysis, and the resulting themes were mapped onto the proposed graphs with results and actions interconnected (GRAI) and active knowledge models (AKM) framework (GRAI–AKM). Findings Six themes were identified: (1) professional training and AI literacy, (2) ethical governance and academic integrity, (3) structural capital flexibility and knowledge processes, (4) trust, transparency and relational capital, (5) platform maturity and technological infrastructure and (6) human–AI complementarity. Professional training and AI literacy emerged as the most-discussed themes. The findings suggest that Gen AI adoption depends on the interaction of human, structural, technological, and knowledge resources rather than technology acceptance alone. Research limitations/implications Although based on a qualitative sample and self-reported written responses, the study advances knowledge management research by integrating Intellectual Capital (IC) and the Knowledge-Based View (KBV) into a comprehensive framework. Practical implications The findings highlight the importance of AI literacy, ethical governance, organizational learning and human–AI collaboration for sustainable adoption of Gen AI in higher education. Originality/value The study provides qualitative empirical support for the GRAI–AKM framework, offering a multidimensional perspective on knowledge management for sustainable adoption of Gen AI.

title: Organizational AI orientation, AI self-efficacy and value co-creation: a human-AI collaboration perspective in healthcare
container-title: Journal of Health Organization and Management
6445e52cab7175f314892526d760c6e1d1251ed8.abstract: Purpose Artificial intelligence (AI) is vital to healthcare system transformation. Existing research mainly focuses on the macro-level technological empowerment of AI, yet insufficiently explores how healthcare organizations’ strategic commitment to AI translates into better medical service outcomes through individual psychological mechanisms. Design/methodology/approach From the perspective of human-AI collaboration, we utilize survey data collected from medical staff working in Chinese medical institutions to examine the mediating mechanisms and boundary conditions linking organizational AI orientation and AI value co-creation outcomes. Findings Drawing on social cognitive theory, the results reveal that healthcare organizations’ AI orientation is positively related to medical staff’s AI value co-creation outcomes, and AI self-efficacy mediates this relationship. Moreover, their creative self-efficacy positively moderates the relationship between AI self-efficacy and AI value co-creation. Originality/value This study clarifies the micro-level transmission paths between organizational AI orientation and medical staff’s value co-creation outcomes. It provides new insights for hospitals to enhance medical service quality and optimize human-AI collaboration during AI-driven healthcare organizational transformation.

title: Evolutionary dynamics of AI-driven enterprise digital transformation: a cybernetic perspective
container-title: Kybernetes
406b79671b63af881cd115f6a281bbe0560605cc.abstract: Purpose In the AI era, digital transformation has become essential for enterprises to adapt as complex systems to uncertain business environments. In this work, we aim to analyze the evolutionary dynamics of AI-driven enterprise digital transformation (EDT), focusing on its evolution and impact on enterprise performance from a system cybernetics perspective. Design/methodology/approach We employ evolutionary dynamics analysis grounded in game theory to model the EDT process, and perform an econometric and empirical analysis on a sample of Chinese A-share-listed enterprises from 2009 to 2023. The approach encompasses heterogeneity analysis, moderation effect models, such as testing enterprise environmental, social, and governance (ESG) factors and market concentration, and threshold effect analyses. Findings The evolutionary dynamics analysis finds that increasing the risk-averse benefits of traditional enterprises and reducing the additional benefit coefficient would hinder EDT. Increasing the investment of technology enterprises in internal resource restructuring accelerates the transformation process. Empirically, AI significantly contributes to EDT. ESG positively moderates the relationship between AI and EDT, while market concentration exerts a negative moderating effect. Furthermore, AI and EDT show an inverted U-shaped trend when R&D intensity exceeds a specific threshold, while a U-shaped trend is observed when enterprise performance exceeds a specific threshold. Originality/value In this work, we uncover the complex, non-linear cybernetic feedback loops, such as U-shaped and inverted U-shaped, and boundary conditions, such as ESG and market concentration for AI-driven EDT, offering systemic strategies for enterprises adapting to the digital ecosystem.

title: Neuro-symbolic AI for proactive risk forecasting: bridging large language models and dynamic Bayesian networks
container-title: Smart and Sustainable Built Environment
9a1bf248111e208571dfad68b70369f36fefa354.abstract: Purpose Periodic risk reports constitute a substantial repository of operational data for project management. Despite the inherent informational value, archived records remain largely unstructured and highly fragmented. This study proposes a fully local neuro-symbolic approach for dynamic risk forecasting by translating qualitative project narratives into a quantifiable predictive engine to support decision-making. Design/methodology/approach The proposed methodology adopts a mixed-methods architecture including four layers: (1) spatial morphology reconstruction using a Y-axis density clustering algorithm; (2) a hybrid pseudonymization filter; (3) a local large language model (LLM) with chain-of-thought reasoning; and (4) a symbolic causal engine powered by a dynamic Bayesian network (DBN) to quantify causal propagation into a dynamic risk index. Findings An empirical evaluation across 28 reporting cycles spanning a 33-month large-scale infrastructure project indicates that the symbolic layer provides a temporally coherent aggregation of the output of a zero-shot perception layer operating at a macro F1-score of 53.62%. By quantifying causal risk propagation, the DBN captured a 93.59% risk-saturation state, for which the retrieved evidence identifies chronic site-clearance bottlenecks. Notably, using an alert threshold selected by sensitivity analysis together with an analytic constraint on the posterior mass attributable to the critical state (talert = 70.0%), the model outputs Bayesian probabilities alongside LLM-extracted textual evidence, yielding an anticipation interval of 1.33 reporting cycles relative to the documented administrative response. Originality/value The neuro-symbolic framework bridges the gap between deep learning perception and causal inference in construction management. By coupling LLM-driven zero-shot ordinal extraction with DBN causal reasoning, the research establishes an auditable framework for risk documentation. The integrated framework transitions AI from an opaque prediction model into an accountable decision-support tool, providing stakeholders with transparent explainable AI diagnostics and supporting a shift from reactive mitigation to proactive, evidence-based risk prevention.

title: NO‘XATNI SUG‘ORISHNING ILDIZ TIZIMIDAGI TUGANAK BAKTERIYALARI SHAKLLANISHIGA TA’SIRI
container-title: Agro ilm
328c2811455766f15c52fe23724799c45e0d5bbc.abstract: The article investigates the effect of irrigation on the formation and accumulation of nodule bacteria in the root system of the chickpea varieties “Yulduz” and “Milyutin-6” under meadow sierozem soil conditions in the Samarkand region. Field experiments were conducted using non-irrigated control and irrigated treatments. In the irrigated treatment, three irrigations were applied during the growing season at rates of 700, 1200, and 1200 m³/ha, respectively. The results showed that irrigation had a positive effect on the formation and accumulation of nodule bacteria in the chickpea root system. In the “Yulduz” variety, the mass of nodules on the roots of 10 plants was 3.2 g in the non-irrigated treatment and 10.3 g in the irrigated treatment, while in the “Milyutin-6” variety, the corresponding values were 3.2 and 10.1 g. Irrigation maintained an optimal soil moisture level, contributing to better root system development and increased activity of nodule bacteria. It was also established that a soil temperature of approximately 18 °C is favorable for active nodule development.

title: JANUBIY CHEGARA HUDUDLARINING ATROF-MUHIT OBYEKTLARI VA OZIQ-OVQAT MAHSULOTLARI  TARKIBIDAGI PESTITSIDLAR QOLDIQ MIQDORINI GIGIYENIK TAHLILI
container-title: Agro ilm
8ccb89ea325892c326bce90450f85ae81d2fa37a.abstract: An analysis of samples from 18 types of food products collected in 2020, 2021, and 2022 showed that in 2020, out of 1,859 samples, pesticides were detected in 30 fruit and vegetable samples, with concentrations remaining within permissible limits. In 2021, out of 6,825 samples, pesticides were detected in 5,707 food samples; of these, 56 were fruits and vegetables (with 32—or 57.1%—being potatoes), and 9 (47.3%) were potatoes. In 2022, out of 3,226 samples, pesticides were detected in 18 (47.3%) fruit and vegetable samples, but concentrations did not exceed permissible limits.

title: IPAK QURTI ZOT, LINIYA VA DURAGAYLARIDA BIOLOGIK KO‘RSATKICHLAR HAMDA TUXUM QO‘YMALARINING MIKROSKOPIK TAHLILI
container-title: Agro ilm
905bc87a5e41fa59c09045e84504aa164095a6ca.abstract: The article presents a comprehensive scientific analysis of the viability dynamics and the proportion of defective cocoons across various silkworm breeds, lines, and their inter-family hybrid combinations. The study confirmed the complete absence (0%) of pathogens causing highly dangerous diseases—such as nosemosis and nuclear polyhedrosis—in all samples. Hybrids belonging to the Line 31 group, as well as certain reciprocal combinations (13x57, 30x46, 314x191, 165x74, 5x155), demonstrated an absolute result: 100% healthy silkworm egg batches. The data obtained constitute a valuable practical and theoretical resource for selecting highly resistant genotypes and establishing breeding stock in sericulture.

title: ОСАЖДЕНИЕ НЕОДНОРОДНЫХ ПО КРУПНОСТИ НАНОСОВ ПРИ ДЕЙСТВИИ ВЕТРОВЫХ ВОЛН
container-title: Agro ilm
c962443678f7a1c69c2acae52901d1b4024d9f8e.abstract: A mathematical model of the settling of non-uniform sediment particles in water under wind-wave action is considered. Using the momentum and continuity equations for the solid and liquid phases, relationships are obtained for the variation of particle concentration with depth and time. Accounting for wave action makes it possible to refine the sequential settling behavior of sediment fractions. The resulting relationships can be applied to hydraulic calculations of settling basins and reservoirs by jointly considering flow parameters, wind velocity, and wave characteristics.

title: ЗАРАРЛАНГАН ТУПРОҚДА Pb(II) ИОНЛАРИНИ МОДИФИКАЦИЯЛАНГАН БЕНТОНИТ–САПРОПЕЛ КОМПОЗИТЛАРИ БИЛАН ИММОБИЛИЗАЦИЯЛАШ
container-title: Agro ilm
e8e7fffabfcb5dc5b6a429ba8a7278312e06d35f.abstract: The paper reports the Pb immobilization efficiency of composites prepared from Navbahor bentonite and Tashkent sapropel by mechanical and thermal activation, in a soil spiked with 1500 mg/kg of lead. Two mobile Pb fractions were determined at seven B:S ratios, five doses and three incubation times; the results were compared with three commercial humic sorbents and the advantage of the thermally activated composite is shown quantitatively.

title: TЕХНОЛОГИЯ И МАШИНА ДЛЯ УЛУЧШЕНИЯ АРИДНЫХ ПАСТБИЩ

title: KARTOSHKA YETISHTIRISHDA URUG‘–TUPROQ–O‘SIMLIK MAJMUIGA ULTRABINAFSHA NURLANISH BILAN ISHLOV BERISHNING SAMARADORLIGI

b836279870e98a6986e89e7d12b58dc4a5615095.abstract: The paper examines the effect of combined pre-sowing ultraviolet (UV) irradiation of soil and seed tubers on potato emergence. Five irradiation variants at 10–50 cm from the source (0.42–0.76 mJ/cm²) and an untreated control were tested on cv. Santa in three replications. On day 15 after planting, emergence in all UV variants exceeded the control (56.7 %), reaching 63.3–83.3 %. The best result was obtained at 30 cm and 0.56 mJ/cm² (83.3 %; +26.6 percentage points over control, p = 0.047). Treated plots showed little Colorado potato beetle infestation; the trial used no fertilizers or chemical protection.

title: MONITORING OF SOURCES OF INDUSTRIAL TECHNOGENIC HAZARDS IN THE SAMARKAND REGION, ASSESSMENT OF THEIR TERRITORIAL DISTRIBUTION AND IDENTIFICATION OF HAZARDOUS OBJECTS BASED ON GIS

eca09e7672449a9e53a6a065f219da9165f3cb10.abstract: This study is devoted to monitoring the sources of industrial techno genic risks in the Samarkand region, assessing the features of their territorial distribution and identifying dangerous objects based on geographic information technology (GIS). As part of the research, information about industrial enterprises and facilities that pose a potential anthropogenic hazard in the region is being collected, systematized and entered into a geoformation database. A comprehensive analysis of the spatial location of sources of danger, their technical condition, the likelihood of accidents, population density, environmentally sensitive areas and other factors is carried out. GIS technologies are used to map man-made risk zones and identify objects with a high level of potential danger. The results obtained can be used to assess territorial risks, prevent emergencies, ensure environmental safety and improve the management of sources of anthropogenic hazards.

title: Academic librarians' perceptions of new skills, competencies and professional development needs in the AI age
container-title: Library Hi Tech
3610c8c0f0d1c535e41c0b71849dce304d1c7a28.abstract: Purpose This study examined academic librarians' perceptions of new skills and competencies, use of AI tools and professional development needs. Design/methodology/approach An online survey was distributed via professional networks, and data were collected and analysed from 155 valid respondents across Australia, European countries and the USA. Findings The findings demonstrate that the highly ranked new skills needed by academic librarians included AI tools and output evaluation, application of data governance and management, AI literacy instruction and integration of AI into curricula. The new competencies consisted of ethical implementation and governance, critical analysis and evaluation of AI tools and AI literacy and conceptual understanding of AI. AI tools could be used to improve information service provisions through responsible and ethical information management and discovery. Key training and knowledge areas included critical evaluation of AI-generated content. Hands-on tutorials with case studies and in-person or hybrid workshops were the most suitable training formats. Practical implications The findings are helpful and practical for academic librarians to develop new skills and competencies and support professional development and curriculum renewal. Originality/value The new contribution of this study lies in the identification of important new skills and competencies that academic librarians need to utilise AI tools in a successful way, mitigate associated potential risks and adapt to changing professional roles.

title: Beyond the laggard myth: time-series analysis of AI job market dynamics in construction
container-title: Smart and Sustainable Built Environment
4e1908c31127b7c180069c373440c5cd8dc5cf0e.abstract: Purpose This study presents one of the first time-series, cross-industry analyses of the artificial intelligence (AI) job market for the construction sector. It benchmarks construction against both digital and traditional industries to interrogate prevailing assumptions of linear diffusion and temporal catch-up in AI workforce adoption. Design/methodology/approach Drawing on 51 months of Lightcast job postings (January 2021–March 2025), with construction defined as ANZSIC Division E, the study employs an interpretable analytical toolkit comprising Seasonal-Trend decomposition using Loess decomposition (period = 12), month-of-year bootstrap tests on detrended series, cross-correlation analysis with bootstrap confidence bands, Newey–West trend estimation on sectoral share ratios and conservative one-step Exponential Smoothing State-Space (ETS) forecasts. All results are re-estimated excluding the partial final month (March 2025) as a sensitivity check. Findings Construction's AI hiring is very sparse, accounting for under 1% of AI postings and is more volatile than hiring in peer sectors, but it grew fastest: annual construction postings rose more than fourfold between 2021 and 2024, against increases of 13% and 9% in the digital and traditional sectors, whose postings peaked in 2022. Construction's share of AI postings relative to both comparators therefore rises (converges) rather than falls. No delayed-follower pattern is detected: no lag at which the comparator sectors lead construction is statistically reliable, and the short-run associations that are detected are weak, near-contemporaneous and sensitive to the sample end. Unlike the comparator sectors, construction shows no statistically significant within-year seasonality and short-horizon ETS forecasts do not improve on a seasonal-naïve benchmark. These findings are robust to the exclusion of the partial final month of data. Construction thus appears as a low-base, fast-growing entrant with its own hiring dynamics, not a “laggard” following digital-sector cycles with a delay. Practical implications The findings suggest that construction firms should prioritise internal capability building and domain-specific AI skills where external hiring is thin, support flexible, year-round upskilling, and design policy and vendor strategies tailored to the sector's operational realities rather than importing digital-sector playbooks. Originality/value This study provides among the first data-driven, time-series evidence that qualifies the dominant “late adopter” narrative in construction. It shows that construction's low level of AI hiring coexists with the fastest growth and a rising share, without a delayed-follower timing pattern, distinguishing a low starting point from a lagging trajectory and offering an empirically grounded alternative to technologically deterministic accounts of cross-industry AI adoption.

title: When adaptation has no endpoint: cognitive flexibility under prolonged organizational strain
container-title: International Journal of Organization Theory & Behavior
50cce1d5f439b416b4a35246b07794dc2aaa28c6.abstract: Purpose This paper examines how cognition operates under conditions of prolonged organizational strain where demands persist, interpretations do not converge and disengagement does not occur. It challenges the dominant assumption in organizational behavior that cognitive processes under strain are inherently directional and oriented toward resolution, coherence or withdrawal. Design/methodology/approach The paper develops a conceptual framework through integrative analysis of stress and coping, sensemaking and burnout literatures. It identifies a shared directional assumption across these perspectives and demonstrates its limitations under conditions of sustained and indeterminate strain. A new construct is introduced and formalized through a set of theoretical propositions. Findings The analysis shows that individuals may sustain cognitive engagement without reducing demands, achieving interpretive coherence or disengaging. To account for this pattern, the paper introduces cognitive flexibility under prolonged organizational strain, defined as a mode of functioning characterized by interpretive openness, non-directional engagement and ongoing meaning adjustment without convergence. Originality/value The paper contributes by identifying prolonged organizational strain as a distinct condition and re-specifying adaptation as sustained cognitive functioning without directional progression. It extends organizational behavior theory by explaining how cognition operates when resolution, coherence and disengagement do not structure activity.

title: Cognitive styles and resource orchestration capability: pathways to innovation and competitive advantage under environmental dynamism in hotels
container-title: Journal of Hospitality and Tourism Insights
b6196c6b8693f18211a46c1997a5f8e4ea1f1be2.abstract: Purpose The study examines how hotel management uses cognitive styles to optimize resource allocation and gain competitive advantage amid rapid technological advances, changing customer needs, and intensified market competition. The study focuses on how the three cognitive styles-creating, planning, and knowing-influence organizational agility and resource orchestration capability. Design/methodology/approach The research used a quantitative survey design. The researchers collected survey data from 325 hotel managers and used structural equation modelling to test the proposed theoretical framework. Findings The results are in line with the framework suggested. The three cognitive styles have positive effects on both organizational agility and resource orchestration capability. The relationship between these capabilities and competitive advantage as well as organizational growth is mediated by organizational innovation. Environmental dynamism reinforces the effects of organizational agility and resource orchestration capability on innovation. Practical implications The results give hotel leaders practical information about innovation that suggests that workforce development strategies and managerial practices should be in line with the latest market trends. It shows that managerial cognitive styles are central to developing dynamic capabilities, and that leadership training, recruitment, and strategic planning have implications to develop the creating, planning, and knowing styles to increase the agility of the organization, its resource management, and ability to innovate. Originality/value The paper combines the Dynamic Capabilities Theory and the Resource Orchestration Theory in explaining how hotels gain competitive advantage as a result of innovation in an environment of market instability. It also determines managerial cognitive styles to be the core microfoundations of dynamic capability development and provides a new understanding of how organizations develop strategic flexibility and economic value in the hospitality industry.
