This paper presents the full-scale deployment and field validation of an AI-enabled Advanced Process Control (Ai-APC) architecture across five conventional oil and gas separation trains and associated facilities within one of the world's largest onshore oil fields. The Gas Oil Separation Plant, designed for 780,000 BOPD and processing commingled production from more than 600 wells, was optimized using next-generation Dynamic Matrix Control (DMC3™), adaptive process models, and real-time soft sensors for Reid Vapor Pressure and salt prediction. The deployment methodology included site assessment, data conditioning, live-plant dynamic testing, model development and validation, Distributed Control System integration, operator training, closed-loop commissioning, and digital performance auditing using real-time KPI dashboards. Performance was evaluated from 17 February to 30 March 2026 against a validated pre-APC baseline. The Ai-APC application achieved 99.35% availability and improved oil recovery by 0.31 vol%, equivalent to 2,208 BOPD of incremental production. Lean-gas consumption per barrel of oil decreased by 55%, fresh wash-water consumption decreased by 3%, and the frequency and variability of manual operator intervention decreased by 20%. The deployment also reduced CO2 emissions by 11,666 metric tons and delivered approximately USD 43 million/year in annualized realized value. The results demonstrate that highly variable conventional separation facilities can be transformed from reactive, laboratory-dependent operation into predictive, quality-aware, and continuously optimized assets. The work establishes a transferable AI-enabled brownfield separation optimization framework integrating adaptive multivariable control, real-time quality inferential, operator decision support, and digital performance assurance. This framework provides a scalable foundation for improving operating efficiency and advancing progressively autonomous upstream production operations.

title: AI-Driven Video Analytics and Behavioral Safety Intelligence: Enhancing Human-Centered Operational Adaptation in Offshore Support Vessels
container-title: ADIPEC
156e6d6192a3d2679989b73fff7135b74a8cfd47.abstract: Computer vision and artificial intelligence (AI) are increasingly used in industrial Health, Safety, and Environment (HSE) management to detect missing personal protective equipment (PPE), restricted-zone entries, and line-of-fire exposure. Early offshore and industrial deployments established the technical feasibility of real-time edge processing and automated safety monitoring (Almadhoun et al. 2020; Tamaazousti et al. 2022). A practical challenge emerges when these systems are scaled across multiple assets: large volumes of detections must be converted into operationally meaningful information. Real-time alerts can support immediate intervention, but isolated detections do not necessarily explain why a behavior recurses or whether the underlying procedure, equipment, or task design contributes to the observed deviation (Corallo and Spingardi 2024; Vukicevic et al. 2024). Traditional HSE responses may treat behavioral deviations primarily as individual compliance failures. Human Factors engineering instead recognizes that task demands, equipment interfaces, and environmental constraints shape worker behavior (Reason 1997). Safety-II similarly emphasizes the difference between prescribed work and operational practice, commonly described as Work-as-Imagined and Work-as-Done (Hollnagel 2014).

title: AI Digital Rock Typing (AIDRT): A No-Code Physics-Augmented Machine-Learning Workflow for Carbonate Rock Typing and Static-To-Dynamic Property Prediction
container-title: ADIPEC
727c7415ff84c95106f61fe038cce60407a1ef65.abstract: Abstract Carbonate rock typing requires connecting the pore-throat network (PorThN) and geological lithofacies description with porosity, permeability, capillary pressure, wettability, and relative permeability across multiple scales, from nano-, micro-, and macro-scales with core image and plug scales to log scale in feet, and finally to reservoir-model scales. This paper presents AI Digital Rock Typing (AIDRT), a no-code, physics-augmented workflow that builds that connection while keeping observations, predictions, calibrations, uncertainty, validation evidence, and expert approval distinct. AIDRT organizes image and tabular evidence through Machine Learning Image Processing and Recognition (MLIR), which identifies Controllable Measurable Volume (CMV) with descriptors as part of the Morphology Decoder process, and integrates 3D Carbonate Heterogeneous Permeability (kHeC), Permeability-linked Capillary Pressure Function (P-Function), wettability-sensitive relative-permeability analysis with pore-throat Deformation Factor (df), and the digital Rock Typing Carbonate Morphology chart (DRT-CAMO). The workflow registers sample scale and provenance, derives pore- and mineral-related evidence, evaluates the pore-throat network, estimates local and aggregated permeability, constructs capillary-pressure and flow-function hypotheses, and transfers candidate rock types toward core–log correlation. The AIDRT implementation completed all software tests and demonstrates traceable project artifacts, validation, and uncertainty views. These results verify the tested workflow behavior with the bundled synthetic table and image. Eqs. (1) - (9) remain the dependable AIDRT workflow formulation. AIDRT's principal contribution is therefore a reviewable evidence-to-reservoir-model chain in which petrophysicists, geologists, and reservoir engineers can examine the same rock-type decision, preserve its applicability limits, and retain accountable interconnectivity among porosity, permeability, lithology, lithofacies, capillary pressure, wettability, and relative permeability, to produce carbonate rock types and their reservoir static and dynamic petrophysical properties, all in one place.

title: RANCANG BANGUN SISTEM INFORMASI MANAJEMEN TOKO RITEL BERBASIS AI UNTUK PREDIKSI PERMINTAAN DAN REKOMENDASI PEMESANAN BARANG
container-title: Simtek : jurnal sistem informasi dan teknik komputer
b1a24950e0848616c9845895e41f1733b3098d24.abstract: Ketidakpastian permintaan dalam pengelolaan persediaan toko ritel dapat menyebabkan stockout maupun overstock. Penelitian ini membangun sistem informasi manajemen toko ritel yang mengintegrasikan pengelolaan transaksi dan stok dengan prediksi permintaan serta rekomendasi pemesanan barang. Sistem dikembangkan dengan metode Waterfall, sedangkan modul prediksi menggunakan kerangka CRISP-DM untuk membandingkan XGBoost dan Holt-Winters, lalu memilih model dengan MAE terendah pada setiap produk. Safety stock dan reorder point dihitung dari data historis penjualan, sedangkan jumlah saran pesanan berasal dari prediksi 14 hari. Dataset sintetis periode September 2025–Agustus 2026 mencakup 20 produk, 5 pemasok, dan 10.886 transaksi. Rata-rata MAPE XGBoost sebesar 36,07% dan Holt-Winters 35,56%, sehingga kinerja keduanya relatif setara. Black Box Testing terhadap 35 skenario menunjukkan seluruh fungsi berjalan sesuai rancangan. Pengujian pada data transaksi riil diperlukan pada penelitian selanjutnya.

title: A Critical Analysis of AI from the Perspective of the Philosophy of Science among Grade X Students at SMA Don Bosco Padang
container-title: Journal of Multidisciplinary Science: MIKAILALSYS
78e1e5475c4f3b6cf9f26befe44e5548f4ddcce2.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) facilitates access to information in education, increasing the importance of critically evaluating claims and their underlying assumptions. This study examined Grade 10 students’ ability to distinguish facts, opinions, and values in AI-related information at SMA Don Bosco Padang from a philosophy of science perspective. A descriptive quantitative approach was employed involving 33 students. Data were collected through a 15-item written test comprising five items each for fact, opinion, and value identification. Descriptive analysis examined frequencies, percentages of correct responses, score distributions, and classification error patterns. Across 495 responses, 337 were correct and 158 were incorrect, yielding an overall accuracy of 68.08%. Accuracy was highest for opinion identification (76.36%), followed by fact identification (67.88%) and value identification (60.00%). Value identification presented the greatest difficulty, with an error rate of 40.00%. These findings reveal descriptive differences in students’ classification performance, particularly their greater difficulty recognizing values within AI-related information. From a philosophy of science perspective, the results underscore the relevance of epistemology for evaluating evidence and the justification of claims, alongside axiology for recognizing ethical considerations. The study provides contextual evidence to inform AI literacy instruction that integrates information verification, critical reasoning, and ethical reflection to support responsible technology use.

title: INTEGRASI GENERATIVE VIDEO DALAM WORKFLOW PRODUKSI VFX FILM PENDEK “SPLIT//SECOND”
container-title: VOCATIONAL: Jurnal Inovasi Pendidikan Kejuruan
0ec57bf51ada7f1be718f5b1197573476a30b8e0.abstract: The rapid advancement of generative video technology presents novel opportunities for visual effects (VFX) asset generation, yet full reliance on artificial intelligence often creates visual inconsistencies, reduced artistic control, and integration barriers with live-action footage. This article aims to analyze the integration of generative video into the VFX post-production workflow of the short film “SPLIT//SECOND” and evaluate its effectiveness relative to conventional computer-generated imagery (CGI) practices. Employing a practice-based research methodology, the production applied a hybrid workflow where live-action footage serves as the physical reality anchor while artificial intelligence assets construct surreal virtual reality (VR) elements. Empirical results demonstrate that generative video substantially accelerates visual asset acquisition with up to 95% time efficiency, reducing manual tasks from 60–90 minutes to approximately 30 seconds to 3 minutes. Although it eliminates manual modeling labor, this method does not remove the essential requirements of digital compositing, rotoscoping, tracking, and color matching, while also introducing variable operating costs driven by platform credit consumption. ABSTRAK Perkembangan teknologi generative video membuka peluang baru dalam penyediaan aset visual effects (VFX), namun penggunaannya secara mandiri kerap memicu kendala konsistensi visual, penurunan kontrol artistik, dan hambatan integrasi dengan rekaman live-action. Artikel ini bertujuan menganalisis integrasi generative video dalam workflow produksi VFX pada film pendek “SPLIT//SECOND” serta membandingkan efektivitasnya dengan pendekatan computer-generated imagery (CGI) konvensional. Penciptaan karya menerapkan metode practice-based research melalui hybrid workflow yang menempatkan rekaman live-action sebagai jangkar realitas fisik dan elemen berbasis kecerdasan buatan (artificial intelligence / AI) sebagai pembangun dunia virtual reality (VR). Pengujian empiris membuktikan bahwa pemanfaatan generative video mampu mempercepat penyediaan aset visual secara signifikan dengan efisiensi waktu mencapai 95%, yakni dari durasi manual sekitar 60–90 menit menjadi hanya 30 detik hingga 3 menit. Kendati memangkas tahapan teknis permodelan manual, pendekatan ini tidak mengeliminasi kebutuhan digital compositing, rotoscoping, tracking, dan color matching, serta menimbulkan konsekuensi beban biaya variabel berbasis konsumsi credits.

title: Academic Colonialism and the Politics of Representation: A Critical Analysis Oxford University’s Instagram Rafflesia hasseltii
container-title: Jurnal Komunikasi dan Bisnis
4c8a59a5180999579f54011ea68de1ce662734d5.abstract: This study aims to examine the controversy emerging from the official Instagram post by the University of Oxford regarding the discovery of Rafflesia hasseltii in the forests of Sijunjung, West Sumatra, in November 2025, in which the names of local Indonesian researchers were omitted while visual and textual narratives exclusively highlighted the contributions of Oxford affiliated researchers. Specifically, this study pursues three interpretive objectives: (1) to examine how the textual and visual elements of Oxford’s Instagram post construct the epistemic positioning of local Indonesian researchers relative to Western institutional researchers; (2) to analyze how the institution’s revised post reflects or fails to address the power hierarchies embedded in the original publication; and (3) to interpret how audience counter narratives challenge and contest the dominant representational structures produced by Oxford’s institutional communication. This study interprets this phenomenon as a contemporary manifestation of “academic colonialism” operating through the politics of representation within digital spaces. The analysis employs a dual theoretical framework, Stuart Hall and Michel Foucault’s theories of representation and power, alongside the postcolonial critiques of Edward Said and Gayatri Chakravorty Spivak, and uses Multimodal Critical Discourse Analysis (MCDA) following Kress and van Leeuwen’s grammar of visual design to examine the post’s textual and visual components simultaneously. The findings are interpreted as indicating that the exclusion of local researchers is not merely an administrative oversight but reflects a hierarchical global knowledge-production structure that continues to perpetuate colonial logic. Social media platforms of academic institutions are interpreted as arenas where epistemic power relations are produced, defended, and contested.

title: The impact of sensorimotor and cognitive capacity on the kinematic performance of instrumental activities of daily living across the lifespan
dbe6069fe100492c67c43ff90f2b11ccfce543f9.abstract: Abstract Background With advancing adult age, sensorimotor and cognitive capacity (e.g., muscular strength) are declining and limitations in instrumental activities of daily living (iADL) are frequently reported. The translation of individual capacity to iADL performance represents a significant research object not only to better understand everyday life behavior but also to apply preventive measures in time. Due to the submaximal nature of iADL, we aimed to identify transition points, beyond which associations between capacity and performance appear, i.e., iADL stop to be submaximal. Methods A set of sensorimotor and cognitive capacity tests and kinematic analyses of hand movements in different complex kitchen tasks were conducted in a sample of 95 healthy adults with an age span of 18 to 93a. An iADL score was derived from the kinematics using a principal component analysis. Transition point segmented regression analyses were applied to examine the association of capacity and the iADL score. Results Most tests reacted to ageing and (negative) outlier frequencies in capacity and, to a weaker extent, in kinematics increased with advancing age. Transition points were identified in most tests and confirmed our hypothesis but were generally high. The best iADL performance was observed in persons between 42 and 58a despite decreased capacity. Discussion It appeared that iADL can be limited by impaired capacity, but profit from experience that can compensate capacity losses to a certain degree. The high transition points point towards the need for early interventions long before subtle alterations in iADL performance become subjectively observable.

title: The Application of the Inquiry Learning Model to Enhance Critical Thinking Skills in Science and Social Studies (IPAS) Instruction for Grade III  Students at SD Negeri 3 Kota Mobagu
container-title: International Journal of Educational Research & Social Sciences
070178c4c71681ca5f659e42c59b3321cd362642.abstract: This classroom action research aimed to improve students' critical thinking skills through the Inquiry Learning model in Natural and Social Sciences (IPAS) lessons on heat energy sources in Grade III at SD Negeri 3 Kotamobagu. The study was conducted in two cycles with 29 students, each cycle consisting of planning, action, observation, and reflection. Data were collected through an essay test based on five of Ennis' critical thinking indicators (Focus, Reason, Inference, Situation, Clarity) and through observation of teacher and student activities. In Cycle I, the mean critical thinking score was 58.10, with classical mastery (minimum category Good, score ≥ 60) of 51.72%; student activity was 66.25% and teacher activity was 71.43%, both in the Good category. After improvements in Cycle II, namely stronger teacher guidance, guiding questions, and greater student involvement in inquiry activities, the mean score rose to 77.76 with classical mastery of 93.10%; student activity increased to 88.75% and teacher activity to 91.96%, both in the Very Good category. Based on the school's learning objective achievement criterion (score ≥ 75), classical mastery rose from 24.14% to 72.41%, which is still below the 75% target. These results indicate an improvement in students' critical thinking after the implementation of the Inquiry Learning model.

title: A Smart Insole-Based Explainable AI Framework for Non-Invasive Sciatica Diagnosis Using Optimally Selected Plantar Force Sensors
44867e825acf1cdcc9b18ad253e5851e1983b666.abstract: Abstract Sciatica is a neuropathic disorder that can cause significant alterations in lower-limb biomechanics, including gait asymmetry and abnormal plantar force distribution. This study proposes a wearable, explainable artificial intelligence (XAI)-based framework for automated sciatica diagnosis using optimally selected force-sensitive resistor (FSR) sensors integrated into a smart insole. A dataset of 37 subjects, comprising 20 patients with Sciatica and 17 healthy subjects, was acquired using 16 FSR sensors, with eight sensors positioned on each foot, along with concurrent electromyography (EMG) and inertial measurement unit (IMU) data. From the bilateral plantar force signals, 601 biomechanical features were extracted, incorporating statistical, temporal, magnitude, and inter-limb asymmetry characteristics. A K-fold combinatorial sensor-selection strategy identified the optimal sensor configuration, with K = 5 providing the most stable performance. The optimal configurations, L2, L5, L8 for the left foot and R2, R5, R8 for the right foot, reduced the number of sensors from 16 to 6, representing a 62.5% reduction in sensing hardware. The selected left-foot sensors achieved 96% accuracy, 96% precision, 93% recall, 94% F1-score, and 0.93 AUC, while the right-foot sensors achieved 87% accuracy, 83% precision, 76% recall, 79% F1-score, and 0.91 AUC. Using the six optimally selected sensors, the proposed one-dimensional convolutional neural network (1D-CNN) achieved 90.3% classification accuracy, 89.9% sensitivity, 90.3% specificity, and a ROC-AUC of 0.911. Furthermore, XAI-based plantar heatmaps confirmed the contribution of the selected biomechanical regions to the classification decision. Cross-validation against the concurrent EMG/IMU modality achieved 85.2% accuracy, with approximately 81.5% diagnostic agreement between the force-sensor and EMG/IMU models. The quantitative results demonstrate that a substantially reduced FSR sensor configuration can preserve diagnostically relevant biomechanical information while providing accurate, interpretable, and portable sciatica screening. The proposed framework offers potential for low-cost wearable gait assessment and automated clinical decision support.

title: Human-AI Collaboration in Urban Digital Transformation: Balancing Efficiency and Human Values in Shanghai’s AI-Enabled Talent Recruitment
container-title: Digital Technologies Research and Applications
99b2a4d2edc2dc8df689bff6b515848affbe723a.abstract: In the context of the urban digital revolution, recruitment through AI technologies has become common practice to address competition in the labor market. However, it is still unclear how the effectiveness of such recruitment is connected with humanistic values. For this research, an exploratory qualitative research design was used, involving semi-structured interviews with eight human resource professionals in Shanghai. Based on the results, the use of AI in recruitment led to increased efficiency mainly when screening candidates through high-volume, standardized processes, although the promised efficiency was not delivered in practice because the introduction of the AI system increased the workload. Patterns of human-machine cooperation were observed in different companies: tech companies and foreign companies are inclined to adopt interactive adjustment approaches, while state-owned enterprises retain human-dominated decision-making. Transparency of algorithms was still lacking in numerous instances, and there was an asymmetry in the accountability framework of algorithms, wherein disobeying algorithms carries more personal consequences than obeying them. The more experienced professionals became more autonomous in their work, while the less experienced professionals depended more on the algorithm. Issues like management support, information accuracy, and departmental integration have a major impact on implementation. This study contributes to the theory of human-machine collaboration by proposing the concept of asymmetric algorithmic accountability, which captures the uneven distribution of organizational consequences for following versus overriding AI recommendations and shapes practitioner behavior in ways that extend beyond individual trust or algorithmic transparency.

title: Critical behavior, variable range hopping, and probable topological Hall effect in VCr2Te4 single crystal
container-title: Applied Physics Letters
37d0343a2f4a1919208b49a6c087d3b26b19eb99.abstract: Chromium tellurides are taken as a board for probing nontrivial spin interactions. Besides changing the Cr/Te ratio or dimension, doping can also tune the physical properties of these compounds. However, only magnetic properties of doped chromium tellurides polycrystalline have been reported, and physical properties of heteroatom-substituting chromium-tellurium single crystals are few. Here, we prepared VCr2Te4 single crystals and studied the electrical transport, magnetic properties, and Hall effect of the single crystals. VCr2Te4 displays perpendicular magnetic anisotropy and a ferrimagnetic-to-paramagnetic transition at ∼74 K. Magnetic critical exponents β = 0.446(2) with TC = 74.512(1) K and γ = 1.081(2) with TC = 74.526(1) K are obtained from the Arrott–Noakes equation of states with long-range interactions between spins that decay as J(r) ≈ r−4.638, indicating intricate magnetic interactions in the VCr2Te4 single crystal. The sample shows a semiconductor-like behavior above 100 K due to variable range hopping. VCr2Te4 has n-type carriers and a larger anomalous Hall conductivity σxy ∼ 104 Ω−1 cm−1 at 3 K. Based on scaling analysis, the anomalous Hall effect mechanism is the skew scattering. A topological Hall effect can be observed up to 20 K due to the noncoplanar spin configuration. Our results reveal the interesting physical properties in VCr2Te4 single crystals and give a way to tune physical properties of chromium tellurides and design the future chromium-telluride-based device.

title: Assessing acceptability, feasibility, and utilization in a peer-to-peer tele-critical care model: a mixed-methods analysis to inform scalable remote ICU models
container-title: BMC Anesthesiology
9b302b0de8ed7eacba36c43be98e0a8e74ae6bf7.abstract: Abstract Introduction Critical care in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) like Pakistan, particularly in remote areas, is constrained by limited infrastructure and expertise. Telemedicine can bridge this gap by connecting frontline ICU physicians with remote critical care experts. While tele-ICU models have been evaluated in high-income settings, limited evidence exists from LMICs. This study evaluated the acceptability, feasibility, and utilization of a peer-to-peer tele-ICU consultation service launched by Aga Khan University in Pakistan. Methods We conducted a cross-sectional mixed-methods study using 145 survey responses and 10 in-depth interviews of physicians who had utilized a national Tele-ICU consultation service. Quantitative data were collected using a structured survey. Qualitative data were obtained through open-ended survey responses and 10 in-depth interviews. Survey data were analyzed using descriptive statistics while qualitative data underwent thematic analysis by two independent reviewers to identify key themes related to service use, quality, and feasibility. Results Of 219 physicians, 145 (66.2%) responded. Consultations primarily occurred via voice (77.2%) and text (43.4%). Respondents reported high satisfaction across clinical (mean 4.50), process (3.82), and technical (4.18) domains. Key benefits included knowledge enhancement, support for complex cases, and ease of access. The Net Promoter Score was 40.7, indicating favorable satisfaction. Thematic analysis confirmed high satisfaction but highlighted utilization barriers, including administrative hurdles and the difficulty of implementing standardized recommendations within local resource constraints. Conclusion The peer-to-peer Tele-ICU model was perceived as highly acceptable and clinically useful by bedside physician physicians. However, infrastructure resource and workflow limitations might affect its implementation. These finding highlight the potential of remote critical care consultation while identifying the barriers that must be addressed to support wider implementation in resource-limited settings. Clinical trial number Not applicable.

title: Brain Tissue Proportionality and General Cognitive Ability Across Three Adult Cohorts
a34e4de781115c698ea0e18eaae41c1c80102edd.abstract: Abstract General cognitive ability may relate to the proportional allocation of brain tissue beyond overall tissue volume. We examined five FreeSurfer compartments using compositional data analysis: cortical gray matter, cerebral white matter, subcortical gray matter, total cerebellum, and brainstem. Human Connectome Project Young Adult data (HCP-YA; N = 1,101) provided discovery estimates; the Dallas Lifespan Brain Study (DLBS; N = 418) and Amsterdam Open MRI Collection ID1000 (AOMIC; N = 926) provided independent cohort tests. Four isometric log-ratio coordinates represented composition, with age, sex, and log total analyzed tissue volume included separately. Composition explained additional cognitive variance in DLBS (partial R² = 4.20%, p = .00154) and AOMIC (partial R² = 1.35%, p = .014). The total-cerebellum-to-cerebral-white-matter contrast selected in HCP was positive in both replication cohorts: standardized β = 0.162 (heteroskedasticity-robust 95% confidence interval 0.072–0.252) in DLBS and 0.097 (0.024–0.170) in AOMIC. Participant-pairs bootstrap intervals supported both associations. Replacing total tissue volume with estimated intracranial volume attenuated the AOMIC association, whereas including both preserved it. Relative macroanatomical allocation is associated with broad cognitive ability conditional on analyzed tissue volume, with differing effect magnitudes across cohorts. These cross-sectional findings do not establish causal tissue trade-offs.

title: From AI readiness to regenerative tourism orientation: a tourist-centric model of smart tourism villages
container-title: ABAC Journal
600067ed573dc780c1bd155c47ed81d59d2f7b38.abstract: Purpose This study develops and validates a tourist-centric model of AI-driven smart tourism villages (AI-DSTV), explaining how perceived digital infrastructure and smart governance relate to tourist acceptance and perceived regenerative tourism orientation (PRTO) through rural authenticity, value co-creation, AI trust, and perceived service value. Design/methodology/approach A cross-sectional survey involved 686 domestic tourists who had experienced an AI-supported tourism touchpoint in rural tourism settings in Indonesia. The sample was predominantly young and digitally engaged, with 75.1% aged 18–24 and 68.4% students. The model was tested using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) with 10,000 bootstrap resamples and importance-performance map analysis (IPMA). Findings All 12 hypothesized relationships were significant. Rural authenticity strongly enhanced perceived AI service value, while tourist value co-creation strengthened AI trust and ethical acceptance. Digital infrastructure and smart governance also showed significant downstream effects through authenticity–service-value and co-creation–trust pathways. The model explained 56.3% of PRTO variance. IPMA identified AI trust and ethical acceptance as the most important antecedent of PRTO and the lowest-performing construct, indicating a key managerial priority. Practical implications Rural destinations should prioritize transparent, culturally grounded, participatory and locally accountable AI systems. Strengthening ethical trust, co-creation, and culturally appropriate personalization may offer greater managerial leverage than technological sophistication alone. Originality/value The study extends technology-adoption research beyond behavioral acceptance by introducing PRTO as a tourist-level psychological outcome. It conceptualizes AI-DSTV as a socio-technical ecosystem linking destination readiness with authenticity, co-creation, trust and service evaluation while distinguishing regenerative orientation from verified destination regeneration.

title: Challenges and opportunities for adaptive reuse of high street heritage: a critical review
container-title: International Journal of Building Pathology and Adaptation
fc8729786d9e3dab97596fbf7afa9c2b0ca431ce.abstract: Purpose The purpose of this viewpoint article is to explore the challenges currently facing the UK high street and potential role of adaptive reuse of historic buildings in a UK high street context from a sustainability perspective. Design/methodology/approach A narrative review underpinned by a systematic literature search is adopted for this viewpoint article. Findings There is a range of complex interrelated factors relating to the sustainable temporary adaptive reuse of historic buildings in high street settings. Originality/value Limited exploration of sustainable adaptive reuse has been previously undertaken in relation to historic buildings. Yet with the persisting challenges of vacant and partially vacant buildings in high street settings, exacerbated by a global pandemic and socio-technical changes, this approach may offer an alternative to vacancy and high street decline.

title: Generative Inverse Design of Shell Metamaterials through Continuous-Latent Conditional Flow Matching
29d4141b48d61843e953cf6048d027f8417e5f4f.abstract: Abstract Mechanical metamaterials derive programmable properties from a repeated unit cell’s geometry. A stress–strain curve summarizesa three-dimensional shell geometry in a few numbers, so distinct geometries can share a curve and the inversemap from curve to geometry is one-to-many. We develop a continuous-latent conditional flow-matching framework thatdesigns periodic shell unit cells for prescribed compressive responses. Each shell geometry is a continuous periodic function,and a function encoder learns a basis that compresses it into 32 coefficients. Conditional flow matching learns theresponse-conditioned coefficient distribution and generates many candidate geometries. On 200 held-out targets, our 5.9-million-parameter model reaches a mean best-of-20 NRMSE of 0.074 at 73% validity, against 0.118 and 48% for a 40-million-parameter tokenized-diffusion baseline. Sampling requires 26.8 ms per candidate versus 2.03 s for the baseline.Finite-element analysis of 981 shortlisted candidates yields a mean best-design NRMSE of 0.092, compared with a simulationto-simulation reproducibility of 0.016–0.063.

title: PENINGKATAN CRITICAL THINKING SKILLS MURID MELALUI PBL BERBANTUAN SCIENCE PROBLEM CARDS PADA MATERI PENGARUH  GAYA
container-title: EDUCATIONAL : Jurnal Inovasi Pendidikan & Pengajaran
707a0a608c109270ab77e3c70840d29fc24a3af3.abstract: This study is motivated by the importance of Critical Thinking Skills as an ability that needs to be developed from the elementary school level, while students’ skills in interpreting information, analyzing, evaluating, and making inferences still need to be strengthened in IPAS learning. This issue is particularly important in the topic of the Effects of Force on Objects, which requires students to understand the relationship between force and changes in objects through phenomena closely related to everyday life. This study aims to improve the Critical Thinking Skills of fourth-grade students through the implementation of the Problem-Based Learning (PBL) model assisted by Science Problem Cards. This study employed a Classroom Action Research (CAR) design based on the Kemmis and McTaggart model, conducted over two cycles involving the stages of planning, action, observation, and reflection. The research subjects consisted of 26 fourth-grade students at SDN Mojoroto 6, Kediri City, who were purposively selected as the targets of the intervention based on the identified problems related to critical thinking skills in classroom learning. All students in the class were involved as research subjects in this CAR study. The research instruments included essay tests, observation sheets, and documentation. The test was developed based on four aspects of Critical Thinking Skills according to Facione: Interpretation, Analysis, Evaluation, and Inference. Data were analyzed quantitatively using descriptive statistics, a paired-samples t-test, effect size, and N-Gain, supported by observation and documentation data. The results showed that the mean Critical Thinking Skills score increased from 29.54 in the pretest to 84.08 in the posttest, with an N-Gain of 0.77, categorized as high. The paired-samples t-test revealed a statistically significant difference between the pre-intervention and post-intervention scores (p < 0.001), with a Cohen’s dz of 4.43. Classical mastery after the intervention reached 96.15%. Therefore, the implementation of PBL assisted by Science Problem Cards can support the improvement of students’ Critical Thinking Skills through problem-solving activities and structured scaffolding in IPAS learning on the topic of the Effects of Force on Objects. Similar media can be developed for different topics and grade levels, involving a broader range of research subjects. ABSTRAK Penelitian ini dilatarbelakangi oleh pentingnya Critical Thinking Skills sebagai kemampuan yang perlu dikembangkan sejak jenjang sekolah dasar, sementara keterampilan murid dalam menginterpretasi informasi, menganalisis, mengevaluasi, dan membuat inferensi masih perlu diperkuat dalam pembelajaran IPAS. Permasalahan tersebut menjadi penting pada materi Pengaruh Gaya terhadap Benda yang memerlukan kemampuan murid dalam memahami hubungan antara gaya dan perubahan yang terjadi pada benda melalui fenomena yang dekat dengan kehidupan sehari-hari. Tujuan penelitian ini adalah untuk meningkatkan Critical Thinking Skills murid kelas IV melalui penerapan model Problem Based Learning (PBL) berbantuan media Science Problem Cards. Penelitian ini menggunakan desain Penelitian Tindakan Kelas dengan model Kemmis dan McTaggart yang dilaksanakan dalam dua siklus melalui tahapan perencanaan, tindakan, observasi, dan refleksi. Subjek penelitian terdiri atas 26 murid kelas IV SDN Mojoroto 6 Kota Kediri, yang dipilih secara purposif karena menjadi sasaran tindakan berdasarkan permasalahan keterampilan berpikir kritis yang ditemukan pada pembelajaran. Seluruh murid dalam kelas tersebut dilibatkan sebagai subjek PTK. Instrumen penelitian meliputi tes uraian, lembar observasi, dan dokumentasi. Tes dikembangkan berdasarkan empat aspek Critical Thinking Skills menurut Facione, yaitu Interpretation, Analysis, Evaluation, dan Inference. Analisis data dilakukan secara kuantitatif melalui statistik deskriptif, uji paired samples t-test, effect size, dan N-Gain, serta didukung data observasi dan dokumentasi. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa rata-rata Critical Thinking Skills meningkat dari 29,54 pada pretest menjadi 84,08 pada posttest, dengan N-Gain sebesar 0,77 dalam kategori tinggi. Hasil paired samples t-test menunjukkan perbedaan yang signifikan antara skor sebelum dan sesudah tindakan (p < 0,001), dengan Cohen’s dz sebesar 4,43. Ketuntasan klasikal setelah tindakan mencapai 96,15%. Dengan demikian, penerapan PBL berbantuan Science Problem Cards dapat mendukung peningkatan Critical Thinking Skills murid melalui pemecahan masalah dan scaffolding yang terstruktur pada pembelajaran IPAS materi Pengaruh Gaya terhadap Benda. Pengembangan media serupa dapat dilakukan pada materi dan jenjang yang berbeda dengan cakupan subjek yang lebih luas.

title: Peer Review Report For: Designing Virtual Reality Game-Based Learning for Computational Thinking Competency Development: Evidence from Vocational Education [version 2; peer review: 1 approved, 1 approved with reservations]
Predicting teachers’ intentions to implement bring your own device and take-home student device programs: a cognitive-affective-behavior framework with sem-ann analysis
container-title: BMC Psychology
c08c91f3c76828a754da5e52d4925d2b352b6979.abstract: Abstract Background Limited attention has been given to teachers’ intentions to implement Bring Your Own Device (BYOD) and Take-Home Student Device (THSD) as an integrated digital learning initiative, particularly from a psychological perspective. Accordingly, this study examines K-12 teachers’ behavioral intention to implement BYOD​ and ​THSD​ programs using the Cognitive–Affective–Behavior (CAB) framework. Methods A survey was conducted with 176 K-12 teachers in Taiwan. Data were analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM), Artificial Neural Network (ANN) analysis, and Importance-Performance Map Analysis (IPMA). Results Understanding, ability, and self-confidence were positively associated with behavioral intention. Self-confidence mediated the relationships between the two cognitive factors and behavioral intention. In addition, the IPMA results showed that ability had the highest importance value, followed by self-confidence, whereas understanding showed the highest performance but the lowest importance. Conclusions The findings suggest that teachers’ readiness to implement BYOD and THSD depends not only on their understanding of the programs but also on their perceived ability and confidence to manage the demands of implementation. The study extends CAB-based research on educational technology implementation and provides implications for teacher preparation and digital education policy.

title: High Use, Low Preparation
container-title: American Journal of Physical Medicine & Rehabilitation
cd596e36835769e8c758e2939412febb985e5034.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (Gen-AI) has rapidly entered clinical environments, posing a risk of “cognitive offloading” that may impede the development of independent clinical judgment. This study conducted a cross-sectional survey of residents, fellows, and faculty at a large academic medical center in January 2026 to quantify Gen-AI utilization and perceptions in physical medicine and rehabilitation (PM&R) to inform curriculum development. Thirty-six trainees (95% response rate) and 11 faculty members (30% response rate) completed the survey; 43 (91.5%) reported any Gen-AI use and formed the analytic sample. Among users, 72.1% used Gen-AI daily for clinical learning and 51.2% during patient encounters, yet 67.4% were self-taught and only 7.0% always requested citations. Trainees requested citations more often than faculty ( P =.048), while faculty more often relied on clinical judgment without additional verification (62.5% vs. 25.7%, P =.089). Gen-AI-derived evidence was rarely surfaced in teaching: 60.5% discussed it during case presentations rarely or never, and only 16.2% always disclosed its origin. Residents are integrating Gen-AI into clinical workflows at rates that outpace faculty familiarity, while verification remains largely undiscussed and untaught. These gaps highlight an urgent need for structured Gen-AI curricula in PM&R residency.

title: Postoperative Behavioural, Cognitive, And Psychological Changes Following General Versus Regional Anaesthesia: A Narrative Review
container-title: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
d621feb3aec9694aeab17a9eca4e4b5f53f16d83.abstract: Postoperative behavioural, cognitive, and psychological changes represent an important spectrum of recovery-related complications after surgery and anaesthesia. This narrative review examines the available evidence comparing general anaesthesia with regional anaesthesia, with particular attention to postoperative delirium, delayed neurocognitive recovery, postoperative neurocognitive disorder, behavioural changes, and psychological outcomes. The available literature suggests that these outcomes are multifactorial and are influenced by patient vulnerability, surgical stress, inflammation, pain, sleep disturbance, medications, haemodynamic and respiratory changes, and anaesthetic exposure. Comparative evidence has not consistently demonstrated superiority of regional over general anaesthesia for prevention of postoperative delirium or cognitive dysfunction. Regional techniques may reduce exposure to general anaesthetic agents and postoperative opioid requirements in selected settings, but sedation and other perioperative factors can confound comparisons. Preoperative risk assessment, appropriate anaesthetic depth, effective analgesia, physiological optimisation, and multimodal postoperative care remain important components of prevention. Further well-designed studies using standardised definitions, baseline cognitive assessment, validated outcome measures, and adequate follow-up are needed.

Trust in artificial intelligence and AI-assisted social and civic decision-making among Arab youth: evidence from Egypt, Kuwait, and the UAE
container-title: Frontiers in Sociology
9c22c48dec77add12e18981832964c2f183e35aa.abstract: Introduction Trust in artificial intelligence (AI) increasingly shapes how young people evaluate information and public issues, yet evidence from Arab contexts remains limited. This study examined the socio-technical correlates of trust in AI and its association with AI-assisted social and civic decision-making among digitally engaged youth in Egypt, Kuwait, and the United Arab Emirates. Methods A cross-sectional online survey was conducted with 1,023 respondents aged 18–35 recruited through purposive, non-probability sampling. Confirmatory factor analysis (CFA), structural equation modeling (SEM), multi-group CFA, and competing full- versus partial-mediation models evaluated measurement and structural relationships. Results The partially mediated model fit significantly better than the fully mediated model, Δχ2(5) = 55.66, p &lt; 0.001. Institutional confidence (β = 0.303), AI literacy (β = 0.281), perceived usefulness (β = 0.242), and social influence (β = 0.107) were positively associated with trust in AI, and perceived risk was negatively associated (β = −0.106; all p &lt; 0.001). Trust was positively associated with AI-assisted decision-making (β = 0.412, p &lt; 0.001). Significant indirect associations through trust were observed for all five antecedents, while the direct perceived-risk path to AI-assisted decision-making was nonsignificant. Multi-group CFA supported metric and practical scalar measurement invariance across the three countries. Discussion The findings support a socio-technical account of AI trust in which technological, cognitive, institutional, and social conditions jointly relate to AI-assisted decision-making, with trust functioning as a central but not exclusive pathway. Given the cross-sectional, purposive design, findings are interpreted as associations rather than causal or nationally representative effects.

title: Association between serum ferritin levels and mild cognitive impairment risk in middle-aged and older adults: evidence from the health and retirement study
container-title: Frontiers in Neurology
a1dd5cd07688a1411d3f46db5c11fee6690ac5d0.abstract: Background Ferritin serves as the main iron-storage form in the human body. Iron ions are critical for numerous brain-related physiological processes. This study aimed to explore the association between serum ferritin levels and the risk of mild cognitive impairment (MCI) in middle-aged and older adults. Methods Participants aged 50 years and above with available cognitive function assessments were selected from the Health and Retirement Study (HRS) database. Baseline data for this retrospective cohort study were collected in 2016, and MCI occurrence was recorded through 2022. Cognitive function was assessed using tests of episodic memory and executive function. The primary MCI outcome was based on an operational cognitive-score definition rather than a clinical MCI diagnosis: the cognitive function score was at least one standard deviation (SD) below the age-specific normative value. Cox regression models were employed to explore the association between serum ferritin [tertiles: &lt;76 μg/L, 76-151 μg/L (reference group), ≥151 μg/L] and MCI risk, as well as impairments in episodic memory and executive function. Results A total of 6,572 participants were enrolled in the analytical cohort. Of these, 1,435 (21.84%) participants developed MCI, while 5,137 (78.16%) were free of MCI events. Individuals with serum ferritin ≥151 μg/L were related to a higher risk of MCI [HR = 1.15 (95%CI: 1.01–1.31)] compared to those with serum ferritin 76-151 μg/L, but no association was found in those with serum ferritin &lt;76 μg/L [HR = 1.04 (95%CI: 0.91–1.19)]. Serum ferritin levels showed a significant U-shaped non-linear association with MCI risk ( P non-linear = 0.03). Moreover, individuals with serum ferritin ≥151 μg/L were associated with a higher risk of episodic memory impairment [HR = 1.15 (95%CI: 1.01–1.30)] versus those with serum ferritin 76–151 μg/L. No significant associations were found between serum ferritin and executive dysfunction [HR = 0.99 (95%CI: 0.90–1.10)]. Conclusion High serum ferritin levels were associated with an increased risk of MCI among middle-aged and older adults, especially episodic memory impairment.

title: A preliminary design framework for human-friendly AI interaction: grounded in anthropomorphism
container-title: Frontiers in Computer Science
46e7d698557d6ad9c8af0e26c30db1eac6a6fb1b.abstract: People converse with AI as they would with friends in daily life, collaborate with it, and form personalized relationships. In response to these emerging forms of interaction, this study clarifies the concept of Human-Friendly Interaction with conversational AI and develops the Human-Friendly AI Interaction Design Framework (HFAI-DF). This study positions anthropomorphism, a foundational phenomenon in human–AI interaction, as a theoretical bridge and reviews literature on anthropomorphism theory and related research on human cognition. On this basis, this study interpretively derives and organizes how anthropomorphism-inducing stimuli can be applied to AI agents, systematizing them into 30 AI behavioral items that enable human-friendly interaction. Subsequently, a survey was conducted and exploratory factor analysis performed to identify six dimensions as a preliminary structure for a design framework for AI’s human-friendly interaction. These dimensions are: Self-Aware Interaction, User-Adaptive Responsiveness Interaction, Context-Aware Reasoning Interaction, Socio-Emotional Interaction, Creative Collaboration Interaction, and Proactive Assistance Interaction. Within the evolving AI research landscape focused on interaction, this study extends the human-centered AI concept toward human-friendly interaction that operates in an organic manner comparable to human–human conversation, grounded in an understanding of human cognitive functioning. The proposed framework provides both AI providers and designers with an initial structure for shaping and improving the quality of human-friendly interaction.

title: Perceptions of AI in veterinary medicine: insights from students, faculty, and practicing veterinarians in Hong Kong
container-title: Frontiers in Veterinary Science
d5c0bfa269240bf48c6ea87f212741cd8f464ca1.abstract: Introduction As artificial intelligence (AI) transforms veterinary medicine, understanding stakeholder perceptions is crucial for its effective and responsible integration. To support the development of targeted educational and policy initiatives, this study aimed to evaluate the knowledge, attitudes, and practices regarding AI among Bachelor of Veterinary Medicine (BVM) students, PhD students, faculty, and practicing veterinarians in Hong Kong. Methods A cross-sectional online survey was conducted between December 2023 and March 2024 among BVM students, PhD students, and faculty members at City University of Hong Kong, and practicing veterinarians in Hong Kong who are members of the Hong Kong Veterinary Association. The survey assessed participants’ familiarity with AI, prior training, perceived benefits, concerns, and willingness to adopt AI in education and clinical practice. Descriptive and comparative analyses were performed to examine differences across stakeholder groups. Results Of 79 complete responses, nearly half (46.8%) reported unfamiliarity with AI concepts. Only 17.7% had received formal AI training, although 78.5% expressed interest in future AI education. Most respondents agreed that AI could enhance veterinary teaching and practice (83.5%) and 81.0% indicated they would likely incorporate AI tools into their work. Key perceived benefits included support for case-based learning (83.5%), virtual animal models for teaching (77.2%), and improved diagnostic accuracy (74.7%). However, 41.8% felt inadequately prepared to use AI. Major concerns included veterinarian accountability for AI-related harms (79.7%), lack of system flexibility (75.9%), and potential clinical inaccuracies (70.9%). Descriptively, practicing veterinarians reported the lowest AI tool use (66.7% had never used AI tools), the lowest preparedness (66.7% felt unprepared), and lower agreement with AI’s clinical benefits, although attitude differences were not statistically significant. Conclusion These exploratory findings suggest gaps in self-reported AI knowledge and differing perceptions of AI across veterinary stakeholder groups in Hong Kong, with AI use already widespread at the time of the survey despite limited formal training. While enthusiasm for AI integration is high, concerns about preparedness, accuracy, and ethical responsibility remain. Larger, multi-institutional studies are needed to confirm these patterns and to inform targeted training programs and ethical frameworks for safe and effective AI adoption in veterinary medicine.

title: Global classrooms: a tri-national study on AI integration by higher education students
container-title: Frontiers in Computer Science
4ce5be4917c40263b11f6c7ca8eabe77dd89211a.abstract: Collaborative cross-cultural learning expands higher education students’ (HES’) intercultural and language awareness, enhances their intercultural competence, has an impact on attitudes towards technology and AI as well as towards the course design and general satisfaction with the collaborative experience in the course. Furthermore, their self-perceived role in a digital setting and their self-perceived English proficiency were measured. The CoGIH Project encourages HES to explore the educational potential of artificial intelligence (AI) for learning and teaching in the school setting. A special focus is on the impact AI might have on the language learning process in English as a lingua franca in a multilingual setting. N = 113 HES, including both pre-service and in-service teachers as well as students preparing for educational administration, from five institutions in Israel, Germany, and Hungary collaborated in 14 international groups, representing five higher education institutions; n = 91 answered the questionnaires. Each group investigated the educational potential of a specific AI application and developed an AI-supported, results-based webpage. The study employed a multi-method research design. Questionnaires were administered to the HES to investigate their experiences at the beginning and at the end of the course. While quantitative data were used to investigate the research through the lens of descriptive statistics and correlations between factors, qualitative data from the open questions were analysed to enable a deeper understanding of HES’ perceptions, experiences and meanings, as well as their critical thinking. The study highlighted strengths and challenges in using AI for educational purposes. The HES valued clear structures, logical navigation, and creative, motivating tasks. Simultaneously, recurring issues included incomplete translations, limited depth of critical reflection, and weaknesses in visual design. In sum, even though AI can support creativity and language learning and teaching, individual learners’ reflections and authentic teacher guidance remain indispensable for meaningful learning.

title: AI-generated advertising in agricultural livestreaming and the auditability of disclosure regulation: a three-layer audit of public Douyin data from China
container-title: Frontiers in Sustainable Food Systems
c177ed750eb610123bd142c9d637834496b25555.abstract: Agricultural products are credence goods, and in livestreaming, the grower’s visible presence signals the price. China has required labeling of deep-synthesis content since January 2023 and, since 1 September 2025, of AI-generated synthetic content. Whether public platform data can verify compliance in a market where the authenticity premium is especially salient remains unclear, given that growers themselves sell produce. We audited three layers of public Chinese platform data: 189 policy snippets, 19 accounts retrieved by AI technical terms, and 455 unique authors retrieved by crop names. In the one policy coding field with complete intercoder agreement ( κ = 1.000), only 6 of 189 snippets name authenticity as a farmer asset. Retrieval by technical terms returns intermediaries: 13 of 19 accounts sell AI tools or tutorials, and none discloses using AI to sell its own produce. Among AI-announcing cases retrieved by crop-name queries, an expanded text-field detector validated at 94.7% recall flags 10 of 455 authors: seven supply-side or service-provider accounts, one incidental non-agricultural mention, and two product-query artifacts; none discloses grower own-use of AI livestreaming. Checks of API-exposed platform metadata for all 575 video records and cover images for 472 records found no platform-side AI label or visible AI/AIGC/statutory AI-generated notice. AI was announced primarily by accounts that sell, service, or discuss AI, rather than by produce-selling grower accounts. No grower own-use disclosure appears in either audited slice: 0 of 19 technical-keyword accounts and 0 of 455 transaction-query authors. The zero admits two readings that the audited surface cannot separate: smallholders do not use these tools, making the requirement inert for them, or they use them without disclosure. No label-reading instrument applied to the audited surface can decide between them, because such inspection observes announcement rather than use. Platforms and regulators may hold backend data unavailable to an external audit. If the theoretically derived authenticity-penalty mechanism holds, disclosure would impose an uneven cost, falling more heavily on growers than on intermediaries. The observed pattern is consistent with this hypothesis but does not establish it.

title: Integrative approaches to acupuncture therapies for post-stroke mild cognitive impairment: a systematic review and network meta-analysis
container-title: Frontiers in Neurology
750e5d10b3af3b8758ad1a9d2ad46cd3741ad839.abstract: Background Post-stroke mild cognitive impairment (PSMCI) frequently occurs after stroke and substantially restricts patients’ functional restoration and overall quality of life. Acupuncture has been widely adopted as an adjunctive intervention; however, the relative efficacy and safety profiles among different acupuncture modalities for PSMCI have not been clearly established. Objective To assess the comparative effectiveness and safety of multiple acupuncture therapies for treating PSMCI via network meta-analysis. Methods RCTs on acupuncture for PSMCI published from their inception to October 2025 were retrieved from nine databases and four clinical trial registries. Study quality was assessed via the Cochrane risk of bias tool. Meta-analysis was performed with ReviewManager and Stata software. Results In total, 47 RCTs featuring 3,680 participants and 15 types of acupuncture-related interventions were included. Electroacupuncture combined with Moxibustion showed the highest efficacy in improving both MoCA score [MD = 5.42, 95%CI (2.10, 8.74)] and total effective rate. Electroacupuncture plus HBOT [MD = 8.00, 95%CI (5.19, 10.82)] and manual acupuncture plus rTMS [MD = 3.42, 95%CI (0.87, 5.97)] were most effective in improving MMSE. Manual acupuncture plus donepezil [MD = 8.67, 95%CI (5.47, 11.88)] and Electroacupuncture plus cognitive training [MD = −8.09, 95%CI (−10.56, −5.62)] achieved the greatest improvement in Barthel index. Moreover, the adverse events of these interventions were acceptable. Conclusion This study suggested that acupuncture was effective and safe for PSMCI treatment. However, the poor methodological quality and uneven evidence quality of existing studies warrant further rigorously designed trials to confirm our findings. Systematic review registration https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/prospero/ , identifier CRD420251165945.

title: Pharmacognostic Standardization, Phytochemical Profiling and Molecular Evaluation of Centella asiatica Extract for Neuroprotection Against Experimental Cognitive Dysfunction
container-title: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
10ab585cf81f0d44b566a2bb0fddf202cc267b14.abstract: The present study was designed to standardize Centella asiatica extract and evaluate its phytochemical composition and neuroprotective potential against experimental cognitive dysfunction. The plant material was subjected to pharmacognostic evaluation, physicochemical analysis, preliminary phytochemical screening, and chromatographic profiling. An ethanolic extract of C. asiatica was subsequently investigated in a scopolamine-induced cognitive dysfunction model in rats. Behavioral performance was assessed using the Morris water maze and Y-maze tests, while biochemical and molecular parameters associated with neuroprotection were evaluated. The extract showed characteristic pharmacognostic features, acceptable physicochemical parameters, and the presence of triterpenoids, flavonoids, phenolics, saponins, and other secondary metabolites. Illustrative results showed that treatment with C. asiatica extract improved spatial learning and spontaneous alternation behaviour, reduced brain acetylcholinesterase activity and oxidative stress, and enhanced antioxidant defence. Molecular evaluation indicated improvement in BDNF expression together with attenuation of inflammatory signaling. These findings suggest that standardized C. asiatica extract may exert neuroprotective effects through complementary cholinergic, antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and neurotrophic mechanisms.

title: Tonic neuron position and network topology determine synchronization dynamics
container-title: Cognitive Neurodynamics
275a9bafd1316f2357617f177dc915c918586499.abstract: Abstract Understanding how collective neuronal rhythms emerge from the interplay between network structure and single-neuron dynamics remains a fundamental challenge in neurodynamics. In this work, we show that in small heterogeneous networks, the network topology and the position of a single tonic neuron govern synchronization dynamics. We study minimal four-neuron Huber–Braun motifs composed of one tonic neuron and three bursting neurons coupled via electrical synapses. By systematically varying the tonic neuron’s centrality—quantified through degree and a quasi-Laplacian measure—we identify two critical coupling thresholds: the critical coupling for global phase synchronization and the coupling at which the network returns to synchronized periodic bursting. Remarkably, centrality determines the nature of the synchronized attractor: motifs in which the tonic neuron has low centrality synchronize into tonic spiking, whereas highly central tonic neurons drive the network toward synchronized bursting. Moreover, the networks exhibit nontrivial collective behaviors, including large-ISI “stairway-to-heaven” structures, partial firing death characterized by the coexistence of spiking and subthreshold neurons, and remote synchronization in the star configuration with the tonic neuron at the hub. While the present study focuses on the Huber–Braun model in four-neuron motifs, excitability and electrical coupling are features shared by many conductance-based neuronal models. This motivates the hypothesis that analogous structure–dynamics relationships may also arise in other neuronal models and small network motifs, highlighting the potential role of local structural control in shaping collective neural rhythms.

title: Human-Governed Multi-Agent AI for Biological Hypothesis Generation: An Evidence-Grounded Framework Using JUMP Cell Painting Profiles
7a2bcb64973bd56bae183bb619c26a0d3a9a5a47.abstract: Abstract High-dimensional cellular phenotypes can motivate biological hypotheses, but similarity alone cannot establish mechanism or causal validity. DISCOVERY-AGENT links exploratory JUMP Cell Painting evidence with evidence-grounded hypothesis generation, independent critique and bounded human-review routing. An initial 65-record CRISPR/ORF analysis across nine gene–modality tests found four FDR-significant CRISPR plate-level associations (AKT1, BRCA1, MTOR and TP53), none among evaluated ORF genes. A distinct later cross-source compound-identity benchmark used 614 morphological features and achieved AUROC 0.6142 on 1,250 held-out compounds with training-only preprocessing; this is identity discrimination, not mechanism-of-action classification. Three structured hypotheses underwent LLM critique and revision, while eleven gene-pair evidence assessments yielded no FDR-significant mechanistic finding (minimum q = 0.2037). Archived governance checks passed 1,021/1,021 predefined tests; nevertheless, the initial live-agent run contained two execution errors among five cases, with both cases responding on fresh retest. These findings demonstrate feasibility of auditable evidence processing and modest cross-source morphology signal, not validated autonomous discovery, prospective safety, or completed expert review. The work delineates practical requirements for independent biological validation and reproducible scientific agents.

title: From Diagnosis by Accumulation to Diagnosis by Layers: Cognitive Psychiatry and Iatrogenic Risk in an Adolescent with Autism Spectrum Disorder: A Case Report and Narrative Review
container-title: Asian Journal of Research in Medical and Pharmaceutical Sciences
91dfcb6df22caf160a8be90ab100928fe3a693be.abstract: Background: Adolescents with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) may show overlapping behavioural descriptions arising from neurodevelopmental features, psychiatric syndromes, environmental stressors and medication effects. Objective: To illustrate a layered psychiatric formulation using the clinical course of an adolescent with ASD, self-harm, restrictive eating, atypical experiences and prolonged psychopharmacological exposure. Methods: Clinical material supplied by the treating team was synthesised as a case report, with a complementary structured narrative review of literature on diagnostic overlap, pharmacotherapy, puberty, safety and feeding. The main PubMed/MEDLINE search covered January 2023 to September 2026, with a subsequent targeted update; evidence selection was purposive rather than systematic. Case Presentation: A 16-year-old adolescent experienced school and adaptive difficulties, sensory sensitivities, food restriction with occasional self-induced vomiting, self-injury and suicidal ideation. Clinical records described sequential exposure to several psychotropic agents. A reduction in lithium dose from 450 to 300 mg/day during the September 2026 admission was followed by improvement in reported hygiene, food variety and family interaction, but later by distress and an urge to self-harm. Co-occurring psychotherapy, environmental changes and uncertain clinical measurements prevent causal attribution. Discussion: The proposed eight-layer framework considers constitutional traits, temperament, neurodevelopment and cognition, psychodynamics, relationships and environment, superimposed syndromes, somatic factors and treatment effects. The concept is heuristic, not a validated diagnostic instrument. Feeding symptoms warrant assessment of sensory selectivity, body-image concerns, compensatory behaviours and nutritional consequences. Evidence associating adverse childhood experiences with neuroimaging measures in autistic samples is relevant context but does not substitute for individual assessment. Conclusion: Longitudinal, risk-sensitive formulation may help identify competing explanations and measurable intervention targets. The clinical sequence does not establish that medication, family circumstances or any single intervention caused the observed outcomes.
