title: From generation to judgment: the multidimensional structure of design thinking mindset and differences across learning stages in AIGC-supported fashion film design learning
container-title: Frontiers in Psychology
e6e79bc6cb105e45a63939887b04adcfcbb9b1ae.abstract: Introduction Artificial intelligence-generated content (AIGC) is changing how design alternatives are generated in fashion film design learning, enabling students to obtain large numbers of comparable and iteratively refinable visual outcomes within a short period. However, expanded generative capacity does not, by itself, determine how learners interpret, evaluate, experiment with, and select among uncertain outcomes. In this human–AI collaborative creative environment, empirical evidence remains limited on whether learners’ design-related psychological tendencies form a distinguishable multidimensional structure that is comparable across learning stages. Design Thinking Mindset (DTM) provides a multidimensional psychological framework for addressing this issue. Methods Drawing on Vignoli et al.’s DTM framework, this study examined five dimensions—Uncertainty and Risk, Empathy, Experimentation, Abductive Reasoning, and Creative Confidence—through a cross-sectional survey of 409 first-year and third-year students from three Chinese universities who had experience with AIGC fashion film design projects. Confirmatory factor analysis and measurement invariance testing across year groups were used to examine the five-dimensional structure and its measurement comparability, followed by latent mean comparisons. Results The five DTM dimensions formed a correlated yet distinguishable structure and demonstrated measurement comparability across year groups. Third-year students had significantly higher latent means on all five dimensions, with the largest descriptive standardized difference point estimates observed for Abductive Reasoning and Creative Confidence. Discussion These findings provide empirical support for the applicability of five selected DTM dimensions in AIGC-supported fashion film design learning and reveal distinct patterns of self-reported psychological tendencies across year groups. From an educational perspective, the results suggest that AIGC-supported design education should attend not only to the generation of creative alternatives but also to learners’ psychological orientations toward uncertainty, experimentation, audience understanding, creative reasoning, and confidence in creative work.

title: Teachers’ attitudes and behavioural intentions towards AI integration in Chinese higher education: a qualitative interview study
container-title: Frontiers in Psychology
c6fe4330bbf5fd4fe3ac0771cb768c511236b747.abstract: Introduction The rapid expansion of generative AI has intensified scholarly and policy debate over its role in higher education, yet university teachers’ attitudes towards its integration remain complex and context-dependent. This study explores how university teachers perceive, experience, and respond to AI integration in their teaching. Guided primarily by the three-component attitude model and informed by the technology acceptance model and the theory of planned behaviour, the study examines cognitive appraisals, affective responses, behavioural intentions, and perceived support needs. Methods The study draws on semi-structured interviews with 14 university teachers from four higher education institutions in China. The interview data were analysed using codebook-informed thematic analysis combining deductive and inductive coding. Results The findings indicate that teachers generally perceive AI as a supportive rather than substitutive educational tool, valuing it for improving efficiency, supporting lesson preparation, and enriching pedagogical design. Emotional responses varied from enthusiasm and a sense of accomplishment to caution, neutrality, and, in some cases, declining satisfaction. Across the interviews, teachers’ primary concerns centred less on their own replacement than on the perceived risks of inappropriate AI use for students’ independent thinking, reasoning, originality, and authentic understanding. Teachers’ intentions to adopt AI were therefore conditional and bounded, shaped by pedagogical purpose, disciplinary context, student readiness, and the need to maintain teacher control. Teachers also emphasised that sustainable AI integration requires more than general encouragement, calling instead for AI literacy development, discipline-sensitive support, specialised tools, and enabling institutional infrastructure. Discussion Overall, these findings extend contextual understandings of teachers’ AI acceptance by showing how adoption intentions are pedagogically negotiated and highlight the importance of supporting professional judgement and students’ independent thinking in higher education.

title: Automated assessment of healthcare de-escalation communication skills in a conversational AI virtual reality simulation
container-title: Frontiers in Digital Health
9bc424b8b0ee6bc350b4296b68f692e3f29c8284.abstract: Introduction Digital health training environments increasingly require scalable methods for assessing communication skills in realistic, interactive scenarios. This paper presents a comparative study of automated assessment approaches within a conversational AI virtual reality simulation designed for verbal de-escalation training. Methods A total of 20 nursing students completed the simulation, where their spoken responses were captured and converted to text through a speech-to-text system, and were evaluated across 11 de-escalation competencies. The evaluation compared three fine-tuned deep learning models (BERT, RoBERTa, and XLNet) with a modified RATAS, a rubric-driven framework that leverages large language models. Two experiments were conducted: one using controlled 100-item validation datasets for each section, and another using the real-world responses collected during the user study. Results On the validation datasets, the deep learning models achieved the highest performance, with RoBERTa obtaining an average accuracy of 0.9927, followed by BERT at 0.9900 and XLNet at 0.9790, while RATAS achieved 0.8554. On the student-response dataset, performance decreased for all approaches, with RoBERTa obtaining 0.8590 accuracy, RATAS 0.8181, BERT 0.8000, and XLNet 0.7681. Discussion These results suggest that transformer-based models perform best under controlled conditions, whereas RATAS demonstrated stability in grading across different dataset types. These preliminary findings support the feasibility of integrating deep learning and rubric-driven LLM-based automated assessment approaches for communication and de-escalation training in nursing education.

title: Associations between cognitive reserve, glymphatic function and cognitive function in mild cognitive impairment
container-title: Frontiers in Aging Neuroscience
b07439303012bc223b7ba87f2dabecd86d618b0c.abstract: Objective To evaluate the association between cognitive reserve (CR) and glymphatic function in mild cognitive impairment (MCI), and to examine whether the relationship between CR and cognition is mediated by glymphatic function. Methods 113 MCI individuals and 91 healthy controls (HC) were enrolled to assess the glymphatic function by using diffusion tensor imaging along the perivascular space (DTI-ALPS), perivascular space (PVS) ratings, and choroid plexus volume (CPV). Cognitive reserve index questionnaire (CRIq) was employed to evaluate the comprehensive CR of participants in both groups. The glymphatic function was compared between the two groups and Spearman correlation analyses were performed among the CR, glymphatic function and cognition. Mediation analyses were further conducted to explore potential mediating effects. Results The MCI group had significantly lower bilateral ALPS index and mean ALPS index than the HC group, while the bilateral CPV, basal ganglia (BG)-PVS and centrum semiovale (CS)-PVS scores were significantly higher in the MCI group than the HC group. After controlling for age and sex, bilateral and mean ALPS index were positively correlated with MoCA, MMSE, and VFT scores; mean ALPS index and left ALPS index were positively correlated with AVLT-immediately performance. BG-PVS was negatively correlated with MMSE and VFT scores, and right CPV was negatively correlated with VFT scores. Meanwhile, CRIq was positively correlated with bilateral and mean ALPS index, but was negatively correlated with BG-PVS, and mean ALPS partially mediated the association between CRIq and cognition in the MCI group. Conclusion Mild cognitive impairment individuals exhibit reduced glymphatic activity relative to HC. Comprehensive CR is associated with cognitive function in MCI, with the mean ALPS index statistically mediating a portion of the CR–cognition association.

title: Uneven automation: comparing authorship anxiety and generative AI use among art and design undergraduate students
container-title: Frontiers in Psychology
8942b2ac014d5d2bac7e05011f209f96a5fce870.abstract: Art and design education expects students to develop a sense of authorship over original work, but generative AI (GenAI) complicates how students understand and claim that authorship. This study examined whether these experiences differ across creative fields through a mixed-methods design. The survey included 2,441 GenAI-using students from seven field categories at 33 art and design institutions in China and assessed authorship anxiety, creative agency, perceived usefulness, dependence on GenAI, and frequency of use. The quantitative analysis first examined variation across all seven categories and then compared fine art with the five applied design fields. Interview data from 22 survey participants were also examined thematically. The main findings include that (1) authorship anxiety did not differ significantly across the seven categories or between fine art and pooled design; the latter comparison met the equivalence criterion at ±d = 0.20, but not at tighter bounds; (2) clearer differences emerged in how students used GenAI. Compared with fine-art students, design students considered GenAI more useful and used it more frequently; (3) across the interviews, most students described authorship as retaining control over the creative idea while delegating parts of its execution to GenAI. Specifically, fine-art students often grounded authorship in embodied making and human imperfection, whereas design students placed greater emphasis on judgement, selection, and control. We call this pattern uneven automation: concern about authorship was broadly shared, but students in different fields responded to GenAI in different ways, potentially reflecting the varying labour-market pressures surrounding their disciplines.

title: Digital transformation, traceability, and supply chain resilience in food manufacturing SMEs: a review of AI, blockchain-IoT, and institutional mechanisms
container-title: Frontiers in Sustainable Food Systems
c0821ee379eb16d2e0252633d6030dd152fbd833.abstract: Food supply chains in China face persistent challenges of food safety risks, inadequate transparency, and supply disruptions, with food manufacturing small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) disproportionately vulnerable due to limited resources and non-standardized internal processes. Digital transformation encompassing artificial intelligence (AI), blockchain, Internet of Things (IoT), and digital twin technologies is increasingly regarded as a strategic solution to strengthen supply chain resilience, yet the organizational and institutional conditions under which these digital investments translate into tangible resilience improvements for food manufacturing SMEs remain poorly understood. This review conducts a PRISMA 2020-compliant systematic review and thematic synthesis of 40 multidisciplinary sources spanning the food safety, supply chain management, and information systems literatures. Drawing on Dynamic Capabilities Theory and Institutional Theory, we propose an integrative conceptual framework comprising six research propositions, in which traceability capability acts as a food-safety-specific mediating mechanism linking digital transformation to supply chain resilience, while regulatory stringency moderates the strength of this indirect pathway. A central argument of this framework is that deploying blockchain, IoT, or AI hardware does not itself constitute traceability capability the institutional and organisational conditions under which digital tools are adopted determine whether firms build substantive traceability capability or engage in symbolic compliance without genuine food safety governance improvement. Three key contributions distinguish this framework: conceptualizing traceability capability as a distinct dynamic capability rather than a generic digitalization mechanism; directing analytical focus explicitly toward food manufacturing SMEs, a population largely overlooked in existing large-firm panel studies; and introducing regulatory stringency as a first-stage moderator within a moderated mediation structure. Critical research gaps are identified, including the absence of SME-calibrated digital transformation measurement instruments, the lack of a validated multi-item traceability capability scale, and a complete empirical vacuum for testing the proposed moderated mediation model in food manufacturing SME contexts. This review provides a structured future research agenda for scholars and delivers actionable insights for practitioners and policymakers seeking to direct digital technology investments toward improved food safety governance in China’s food manufacturing sector.

title: Opportunities for creative thinking in an out-of-school learning environment: perceptions and experiences of children attending the Discovery Campus
container-title: Frontiers in Psychology
5b061da5aee0a14356de53f31c3b9eaea1527678.abstract: Creative thinking emerges as a critical skill that adds meaning to individuals’ lives in today’s competitive world. One of the learning environments aimed at developing this skill is the Discovery Campus, which serves as a children’s university. This qualitative study aimed to investigate the perceptions and experiences regarding creative thinking of 32 children aged 11–13 who regularly attend the Discovery Campus in Gaziantep, Türkiye. The participants were selected through criterion sampling, a purposive sampling method. Data were collected via written interview forms and analysed using the content analysis method. The findings indicated that participants perceive the Discovery Campus as a learning environment where, in addition to acquiring new knowledge, they can apply what they have learned, discover their own potential, and develop original ideas. It was determined that creative project ideas aim to develop solutions to problems based on the needs of humans, society, and living organisms; and that experiences at the Discovery Campus are associated with an approach based on hands-on learning, material use, enquiry, observation, and imagination, which differs from formal school environments. Furthermore, in the children’s narratives, it was observed that opportunities for creative thinking are shaped by the processes of conducting research, focusing on areas of interest, participating in workshop activities, transforming ideas into projects, and sharing the developed designs. Accordingly, in order to support children’s creative thinking processes, it is recommended to expand science centres that bring together different disciplines and provide opportunities for practical application and project production.

title: Sensorimotor recovery, neuropathic pain reduction, and neuroplasticity changes following cognitive multisensory rehabilitation or adaptive fitness in adults with spinal cord injury: a feasibility pilot randomized controlled trial
container-title: Frontiers in Pain Research
9fed6f696e20c514887fb0d7b80050475f38e976.abstract: Introduction Spinal cord injury (SCI) often causes partial or complete sensory and motor loss, disrupting the afferent integration needed for accurate mental body representations (MBR, i.e., body awareness and visuospatial body map). MBR deficits compromise sensorimotor recovery and contribute to neuropathic pain in about 69% of adults with SCI. Medications for neuropathic pain are often ineffective and can cause adverse reactions. Our previous pilot clinical trial showed that Cognitive Multisensory Rehabilitation (CMR), a physical therapy that restores MBR, produced significant, lasting reductions in neuropathic pain, improved sensorimotor function, and enhanced brain function. Building on these results, we examined feasibility and whether 8 weeks of CMR or adaptive fitness (1) improves sensorimotor function and reduces pain; (2) increases sensorimotor- and MBR-related brain activity and connectivity in adults with SCI. Methods Sixteen participants (52 ± 8 years old, 13 ± 10 years post-SCI) were randomized to CMR or adaptive fitness (45 min, 3x/week, 8 weeks); one withdrew. Ten participants had neuropathic pain of ≥3/10. Pain and sensorimotor function were assessed at baseline, post-intervention, and 3-month follow-up using the Numeric Pain Rating Scale (NPRS), ASIA Impairment Scale (AIS), and Neuromuscular Recovery Scale (NRS). Functional MRI included resting-state and 4 tasks: imagining feeling the left leg, imagining moving the left leg, whole-body movement imagery, and a sensation task (i.e., gently brushing the big toes with a towel). Results Post-CMR ( n = 8), participants showed significant large within-group AIS effect sizes (touch: d = 1.54; pinprick: d = 1.83; lower limb motor function: d = 1.32) and large (core: d = 2.19) to moderate (arm function: d = 0.69; leg function: d = 0.74) NRS effect sizes. Adaptive fitness ( n = 7) showed non-significant small/moderate AIS (touch: d = 0.49; pinprick: d = 0.53; lower limb motor function: d = 0.74) and NRS effects (core: d = 0.73; arm function: d = 0.34; leg function: d = 0.00). Benefits persisted at follow-up. MCID was exceeded for average pain post-CMR and highest pain at 3-month follow-up. Pain virtually did not change after fitness. CMR increased brain connectivity and activation during leg imagery. During whole-body imagery, CMR increased widespread activation; adaptive fitness showed spatially limited increases. Discussion These preliminary results support CMR's potential to improve function and reduce neuropathic pain in adults with SCI, warranting larger confirmatory trials. Clinical Trial Registration : https://clinicaltrial.gov/ , identifier NCT05167032.

title: Human-in-the-loop semantic learning analytics for assessing moral-value reasoning in university AI ethics education
container-title: Frontiers in Psychology
4c153cd19693204269d4536c8e62024e2ea30575.abstract: Introduction University AI ethics education addresses fairness, privacy, accountability, transparency, human autonomy, and academic integrity, but the semantic structure of students' moral-value reasoning and its connection to responsible solutions remain insufficiently characterized. This study examined a human-in-the-loop semantic learning analytics framework for task-specific moral-value reasoning. Methods Ninety science and engineering graduate students completed an online explicit-reflective AI ethics module in a one-group pre–post multimethod study without a control group. Assessments comprised an AI ethics knowledge test, a perceived-awareness scale, and open-ended ethical reasoning tasks. Expert annotations informed transformer-based multi-label coding, descriptive value coverage and balance metrics, problem–solution coupling, and baseline-only nested cross-validated prediction of subsequent raw problem-solving change. Results Within-participant pre–post increases were observed in ethical knowledge, perceived moral-value awareness, actual ethical awareness, problem–solving skills, value coverage, value balance, and problem–solution coupling. Automated semantic coding achieved participant-grouped cross-validated macro-F1 = 0.83 (95% CI [0.78, 0.87]; micro-F1 = 0.86; macro-AUPRC = 0.82). The baseline-only prediction model yielded cross-validated R 2 = 0.30 (95% CI [0.11, 0.45]) for subsequent raw problem-solving change. Discussion Expert-supervised semantic analytics can characterize value representation and issue–solution reasoning in AI ethics assessments. Coverage and balance describe response structure rather than moral quality. The absence of a control group, repeated use of one scenario, and modest sample size preclude causal and broad trait-level conclusions.

title: Persistent neutrophil maturation deficits associate with cognitive impairment in individuals with post-acute sequelae of COVID-19
container-title: Frontiers in Immunology
ac0aa8b9c9650b24069967ccaa55123144767865.abstract: Introduction Post-COVID-19 condition, or post-acute sequelae of COVID-19 (PASC), is characterized by persistent cognitive impairments and immune dysregulation. While neutrophils are critical in acute COVID-19, whether their long-term functional dysregulation contributes to PASC, remains unclear. Thus, we investigated the links between immune system changes, symptom severity and cognitive impairment in PASC. Methods In this cross-sectional study, we enrolled 40 individuals with self-reported issues with COVID-19 recovery (PASC) and 37 fully recovered (REC) volunteers. Participants were post-infection at either TP1 (from 6 up to 18 months post-infection, 7 PASC, 20 REC) or at TP2 (from 19 up to 36 months post-infection, 33 PASC, 17 REC). We evaluated the Newcastle post-COVID-19 Syndrome Follow Up Screening (NC) scores for symptom severity, and neuropsychological tests for memory, attention, and executive function. Peripheral blood was analyzed using multicolor flow cytometry, ELISA, clustering, and multivariate regression. Results PASC participants in both the TP1 cohort and the TP2 cohort, demonstrated increased NC scores and significant changes in neutrophil numbers and subset composition. In the TP1 cohort, the PASC group showed an increased frequency of activated CD16 + CD62L low neutrophils and a reduced frequency of CXCR4 + TREM-1 + CCR2 + polymorphonuclear myeloid-derived suppressor cells (PMN-MDSCs). This was accompanied by elevated soluble TNF receptor 1 (sTNFR1) and decreased sTNFR2 and CXCL12. In the TP2 cohort, PMN-MDSC levels were comparable between REC and PASC groups, alongside increased emergency granulopoiesis regulators IL-3 and IL-6. Multivariate regression revealed significant associations between PMN-MDSC signatures, granulopoiesis-related markers, NC scores, and cognitive test scores in either the TP1 or the TP2 cohort. These results represent cross-sectional observations in participants assessed within the respective post-infection intervals, rather than longitudinal evidence of persistence. The results show that dysregulated granulopoiesis and neutrophil maturation are present even at 18 and 36 months in PASC individuals, potentially associating with overall symptom severity and cognitive impairment. Conclusions Despite limitations in cohort size, requiring validation of the associations in larger cohorts, our findings may contribute to the further understanding of PASC and future new transitional perspectives for PASC management.

title: Perceived AI literacy and TPACK in pre-service teacher education: mediating roles of perceived usefulness, ease of use, and value in blended learning
container-title: Frontiers in Psychology
1bad51d2ab1c081fcbf1788c8c81f98f9ce0044c.abstract: Background The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into blended learning requires pre-service teachers to develop AI-related competencies and the ability to integrate technology into pedagogy. This study examines how perceived AI literacy and technological pedagogical content knowledge (TPACK) are associated with deep learning through perceived usefulness, perceived ease of use, and perceived value of AI use. Methods A cross-sectional survey was completed by 423 pre-service teachers enrolled in blended learning courses at a university in China. Data were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM), with covariance-based structural equation modeling and fuzzy-set qualitative comparative analysis (fsQCA) used as complementary robustness and configurational analyses. Results Perceived usefulness, perceived ease of use, and perceived value of AI use significantly mediated the relationships between the two competencies and deep learning. All six indirect pathways were significant in both the PLS-SEM and covariance-based SEM analyses. The fsQCA revealed an equifinal and asymmetric structure: multiple, partly substitutable conditions were sufficient for high deep learning, and no single condition was necessary for either high or low deep learning. Conclusions The findings integrate the technology acceptance model and expectancy-value theory to explain how pre-service teachers' competencies and perceptions relate to deep learning in AI-enhanced blended environments. Teacher education should support technical competence alongside positive perceptions of AI's utility, usability, and value. Because the measures were self-reported and collected cross-sectionally at one university, the findings are interpreted as associational and configurational rather than causal.

title: Effectiveness of an AI-Based Educational Video Generator in Enhancing Oral Health Knowledge and Behavior Among Children: A Randomized Controlled Trial
container-title: Al-Rafidain Journal of Medical Sciences ( ISSN 2789-3219 )
025217a90eae33a9efbb4f3e4378042549e3202e.abstract: Background: Artificial intelligence (AI) is a new innovation that presents an opportunity for oral health education in children. Objective: To evaluate the effectiveness of an AI-assisted educational video versus standardized in-person oral health education for children regarding oral health knowledge and behaviors. Methods: This randomized controlled trial included 300 children aged 10-12 years (n=150 per group), both boys and girls, who were divided into AI video and standardized face-to-face oral health education groups. Baseline and 2-week follow-up evaluations were conducted for knowledge scores, four behavioral items, and the Silness and Löe Plaque Index. The internal consistency of the knowledge scale was checked (Cronbach's α=0.79). Wilcoxon signed-rank and Mann–Whitney U tests were the primary non-parametric tests used for statistical evaluations, with a median, (IQR), and effect size r provided. Chi-square tests with a Bonferroni adjustment at α=0.0125 were used to evaluate behavioral items. Results: There were significant enhancements in intra-group knowledge (p<0.0001 for both groups; r=0.663 for AI; r=0.345 for Control). The clinical efficacy was similar for both strategies with significant reduction of intra-group plaque (AI: p< 0.001, r= 0.425; Control: p< 0.001, r= 0.331), but no inter-group difference at the end of the intervention (p= 0.608; r= 0.030). In the conventional group, the utilization of dental floss was significantly improved (p=0.0056), and no other behaviors showed significant improvement across groups. Conclusions: The AI-assisted educational video demonstrated better knowledge retention than the standardized face-to-face oral health education, achieved similar clinical plaque reduction, and can be easily scaled for pediatric preventive dentistry.

title: Invisible Reasoning: What Early Childhood Teachers Notice,and Overlook, in Children'S Scientific Thinking
container-title: Journal of Social and Scientific Education
474f1d12b70df12e2cf02ad2fb94af03b392bcc0.abstract: Early childhood teachers are increasingly asked to assess and support children's scientific thinking, yet little is known about what teachers actually attend to when they describe a child's thinking in their own words. This study examined how teachers' spontaneous narrative notes about preschool children correspond to their structured ratings of scientific thinking, with particular attention to hypothesis and experimentation skills. A convergent mixed-methods design was used. Teachers from 277 early childhood institutions in Indonesia rated 295 children aged 4–6 years on a 24-item instrument covering attention, working memory, problem solving, observation, and hypothesis and experimentation, and 225 child-specific open-ended notes were analysed with directed content analysis; the two strands were integrated through cross-tabulation, correlation, and regression. Hypothesis and experimentation was the lowest-rated dimension (M = 3.31), yet it was almost absent from teachers' narratives: no note mentioned prediction, hypothesising, or revising an idea, and only 11.1% referred to any scientific reasoning process. Notes were dominated by global evaluations (43.6%) and attention or behavioural-regulation concerns (22.7%). For children in the lowest quartile of rated hypothesis and experimentation, teachers wrote about attention or regulation problems in 30.6% of notes but about reasoning in only 4.8%; in the highest quartile, reasoning was mentioned in 23.9%. Attention concerns did not predict hypothesis scores once rated attention was controlled, whereas mentions of reasoning added unique information beyond all four other rated dimensions. The findings suggest that children's emerging scientific reasoning is largely invisible in teachers' everyday descriptions, and that difficulties in this domain tend to be described as problems of focus, although the cross-sectional, correlational design cannot establish whether this reflects genuine attentional constraints, teachers' perception, or both. Professional development should therefore train teachers to notice and document children's predictions, explanations, and revisions explicitly.

title: Early childhood students perspective on climate change education and sustainability through the lens of critical and sustainability pedagogies
container-title: Journal of Childhood, Education & Society
05c4d5ea6879a09fb18f83525647dc051fb6a586.abstract: Climate change is recognised as a pressing global environmental challenge, disproportionately affecting children’s development, wellbeing, and rights. This study investigates final-year early childhood studies students’ perspectives on climate change education and sustainability in two national contexts, the United Kingdom and Hungary, which differ in the extent to which environmental and sustainability education is explicitly reflected in early childhood curriculum guidance. In England, while the Department for Education’s sustainability and climate change strategy recognises the importance of developing children’s understanding of nature, sustainability, and climate change, these themes are not explicitly identified as areas of learning within the Early Years Foundation Stage statutory framework. In contrast, Hungarian early years teacher education systematically integrates environmental pedagogy into professional training. Therefore, the aims of the study were to explore how early childhood studies students interpret their role in addressing climate change education and sustainability when working with children, how they perceive the curriculum, and develop pedagogical practices in climate change education they consider age-appropriate and meaningful. Across both contexts, students valued early engagement with climate awareness but highlighted challenges including lack of explicit awareness of the early childhood education workforce how to address children’s emotional readiness, developmental appropriateness, and limited pedagogical resources. The findings underscore the importance of higher education in preparing future practitioners to teach climate change effectively and suggest the need for clearer curriculum guidance, structured pedagogical support, and practical resources.

title: HESS Opinions: Operationalizing sociohydrology from systems thinking to systems doing for sustainable and resilient water management
container-title: Hydrology and Earth System Sciences
248d074c40030f917c8ac78c5d9716bce693e541.abstract: Sociohydrology has advanced explanations of coupled human-water systems, but its translation into decision support remains uneven. We propose two complementary approaches to move from systems thinking to systems doing: (i) canonical feedback structures, which describe the main components of human-water systems and how they interact and enable comparison across cases while accounting for important local differences; and (ii) critical pathways, which trace how management actions propagate through these components to produce outcomes, including unintended consequences. Drawing on cases such as the levee effect and reservoir effect, these approaches connect system understanding with intervention design, monitoring, and adaptive learning. We then propose a minimal “systems-doing loop” that links the decision setting, feedback mapping, pathway tracing, indicator selection, and iteration, with equity and legitimacy treated as explicit constraints on useful knowledge and acceptable action. This framing complements predictive modelling and integrated water resources management by accounting for potential unintended consequences in decision-making and clarifying what to monitor and revisit as systems change.

title: Evaluasi Efisiensi dan Keandalan Sistem Pembangkit Listrik Tenaga Panas Bumi (PLTP) Sebelum dan Sesudah Turn Around pada Critical Equipment dengan Kajian Ekonomi
container-title: ARMATUR : Artikel Teknik Mesin & Manufaktur
4bb460d884954a0b049df73f287901a89092cfb1.abstract: Geothermal Power Plants provide reliable baseload electricity and are essential for supporting Indonesia’s renewable energy transition. However, long-term operation may cause performance degradation of critical equipment, resulting in reduced efficiency, reliability, and productivity. This study evaluates the impact of Turn Around (TA) maintenance on the efficiency, reliability, and economic performance of Kamojang Unit 4 Geothermal Power Plant with an installed capacity of 60 MW. A quantitative comparative approach was employed using actual operational data collected before and after Turn Around implementation. The evaluated parameters included output power, turbine efficiency, condenser performance, cooling tower effectiveness, Mean Time Between Failure (MTBF), Mean Time To Repair (MTTR), Equivalent Availability Factor (EAF), Equivalent Forced Outage Rate (EFOR), energy production, Capacity Factor, Cost of Downtime, and revenue. The results show that output power increased from 53.44 MW to 59.19 MW (10.76%), while turbine efficiency improved from 71.59% to 78.51%. Cooling tower effectiveness increased from 61.52% to 82.78%. Reliability performance also improved significantly, with MTBF increasing by 135.78%, MTTR decreasing by 75.17%, EAF increasing from 95.97% to 99.84%, and EFOR decreasing from 3.15% to 0.28%. These improvements resulted in an 8.52% increase in net energy production, additional revenue of IDR 61.69 billion, and a 90.94% reduction in Cost of Downtime.

title: Improving Learner Performance Through Score Based Analysis on a Gamified AI Driven Cybersecurity Learning Platform
d2b1981b0d01f6ee261a12a86c8c602586119c26.abstract: Abstract This study examines whether structured engagement with instructional content improves learner performance on Cyber Security Academy, an AI-driven, gamified cybersecurity learning platform. Activity logs covering 1,500 completed assessments from users in ten Anglophone and Francophone countries were analyzed by comparing learners who consulted the lessons and completed the full learning pathway (n = 900) with those who engaged only partially with the platform (n = 600). Group differences were tested with Welch's t-test, the Mann Whitney U test, one-way ANOVA, Spearman correlations, and Cohen's d as a measure of effect size. Learners who read the lessons before assessment obtained a mean score of 71.27 % versus 60.41 % for non-readers (Δ = +10.86 points; t(1192) = 12.21; p < 0.001; d = 0.650; 95 % CI [9.12, 12.60]), committed fewer errors (2.50 vs. 4.85; d = -1.069), and responded faster (9.85 vs. 12.69 minutes; d = -0.807), indicating greater fluency of cognitive processing. The effect decreased monotonically with age (d = 1.205 for learners aged 13 and under; d = 0.387 for those 22 and over) and with digital literacy (d = 1.434 for beginners; d = 0.524 for experts), while remaining positive in all ten countries. These findings indicate that structured, AI-personalized, and gamified learning environments substantially enhance cybersecurity learning outcomes, particularly for younger and less experienced users.

title: AI Labour Rights Awareness and Career Adaptation Confidence among Respondents in Bangladesh
4bebd9cda335afcb1b14dbb90e41e4c4857a6c33.abstract: Abstract Artificial intelligence changes both the skills used at work and the conditions under which employment decisions are made. Awareness of these changes does not necessarily coincide with confidence in adapting a career. This study examines that distinction in 385 adult, AI-aware survey records from Bangladesh, including 238 law students and 61 respondents classified as law graduates. Five statements separately assess awareness of workplace rights and responsibilities, recognition of protection from unfair automated decisions, reported complementary skill development, adaptation confidence and the perceived preparedness benefit of understanding labour issues. Analyses combine full response distributions, joint endorsement patterns, paired comparisons, ordinal correlations and an exploratory proportional-odds model. Recognition of the need for protection was endorsed by 79.2%, compared with 48.8% endorsing adaptation confidence, a paired difference of 30.4 percentage points (95% bootstrap interval 23.9–36.6). General rights awareness and skill development had small positive ordinal associations with confidence. In the adjusted ordinal model, their odds ratios were 1.30 (95% interval 1.04–1.61; Holm p = 0.038) and 1.40 (1.09–1.79; Holm p = 0.024) respectively. The protection-recognition estimate was less certain, although the two awareness coefficients were not demonstrably different. The findings distinguish rights recognition, reported action and confidence rather than establish a causal awareness-to-adaptability pathway. They support evaluating legal-literacy education alongside practical career tasks and institutional safeguards. The mixed sample, study-specific single items, undocumented recruitment and fieldwork dates, and source-documentation limitations constrain inference. A subsequent study should use verified graduate eligibility, independent legal-knowledge assessments and longitudinal career outcomes.

title: Digital Technology Use, Cognitive Engagement and Perceived Learning Effectiveness Among Adult Learners in Non-Formal Education in Uzbekistan
45a1f4b7c88044561b62fd4240d2f0ed18697212.abstract: Abstract Although digital technologies are increasingly embedded in adult education policy, evidence from post-Soviet Central Asia remains scarce. This sequential explanatory mixed-methods study examined how digital technology use relates to two proximal indicators of learning processes – cognitive engagement and perceived learning effectiveness – among adults in non-formal education programmes in Uzbekistan. Survey data from 312 learners nested in 26 programmes across three provinces were analysed with two-level random-intercept models, followed by semi-structured interviews with 22 learners and two facilitators, analysed through reflexive thematic analysis. After adjustment for age, gender, educational attainment, urban–rural location and programme type, digital technology use was positively associated with cognitive engagement (β = .38, 95% CI [.27, .49]) and perceived learning effectiveness (β = .35, 95% CI [.24, .46]). Between 17% and 18% of the variance in each outcome lay at the programme level. Four qualitative themes – socially produced digital self-efficacy, peer-mediated learning, institutional culture and structural barriers – helped to explain these patterns. Interpreted through self-directed learning theory and the capability approach, the findings suggest that the educational value of digital tools depends on the social and institutional conditions in which adults use them. The cross-sectional design and reliance on self-report preclude causal inference.

title: A Critical Review of Machine Learning Approaches for Credit Risk and Loan Default Prediction
container-title: Social Sciences Futures
33e517e6c207c355e2e221a9633c8ce40edebcbb.abstract: Approval or rejection of loans continues to be difficult decisions, and these decisions are becoming more difficult as financial markets continue to become globalised and interconnected. This review will look at research papers that examine how machine learning can assist with establishing more effective predictions of loan defaults in various lending environments, including U.S. traditional commercial banks (using both conventional and nonconventional forms of borrowing), P2P lending platforms (like Kiva and Lending Club), and mobile money networks in Sub-Saharan Africa. A common theme emerges across different studies referenced, which is that machine learning algorithms such as Gradient Boosting and XGBoost outperform traditional regression techniques (e.g., logistic regression) with a significant safety margin (generally 10%–15%), with 10% being the lowest margin of error for any study, and 30% being the highest margin of error across studies measuring AUC (area under the curve). The more significant findings are found when comparing average AUC measurement results to the AUC results of a dataset of behavioural signals (including factors related to how many times borrowers are late on payments, velocity of spends made by borrowers, and downloadable applications added to their mobile devices), all of these factors combined have produced much better predictive power than traditional financial ratios have produced on their own. When treating class imbalance - namely using methods such as SMOTE and ENN for resampling - recall has garnered considerable attention; similarly many of the major concerns are addressing issues including but not limited to: inequitable distributional burdens on various groups, the prevalence of model validation only using one dataset, the issue of temporal drift and the negative impact that changing economic conditions are having on how models perform. As part of this systematic review, previously published research will be systematically organized into categories according to their respective findings/gaps and ideas for areas of future research of the greatest potential. Keywords: Loan default prediction; Credit risk modelling; Machine learning; Ensemble methods; Explainable AI; Class imbalance

title: Dynamic Business Impact Analysis and Dependency-Aware Recovery Optimization for Mission-Critical Banking Operations
57f5e38597fd2abdcfcf4efaa1ad575dad9edfe1.abstract: Abstract This study develops a Dynamic Business Impact Analysis and Dependency-Aware Recovery Optimization framework for mission-critical banking operations. The objective is to assess time-dependent service impact, model cascading disruption across interconnected banking resources, and prioritize recovery actions under constrained technical, financial, and human resources. The methodology combines operational and incident data preparation, multilayer dependency-network modeling, scenario-based simulation, dynamic impact scoring, and multi-criteria recovery optimization using service impact, customer exposure, financial loss, RTO breach, RPO breach, and recovery cost. Evaluation covers core account services, payment processing, online banking, ATM and card services, customer authentication, and fraud monitoring across cyber, infrastructure, communication, payment-network, and third-party disruption scenarios. Compared with criticality-only, shortest-recovery-time, and static business impact analysis baselines, the proposed method reduced mean recovery time to 4.6 hours and cumulative impact to 0.47, while increasing RTO compliance to 82.9% and RPO compliance to 88.6%. The findings show that dependency-aware, time-sensitive recovery prioritization provides more reliable system-level decisions than fixed service rankings. The framework supports resilience testing, impact-tolerance assessment, incident command, recovery planning, and investment decisions for banking infrastructure.

title: Practical Bedside Tests for Assessing Postoperative Cognitive Dysfunction (POCD) in Anesthetized Patients
container-title: Journal of the Medical Association of Thailand
89bb02a8d8803dc56f0474315a1d0c943e80e694.abstract: Postoperative cognitive dysfunction (POCD)—characterized by deficits in memory, executive function, and processing speed—is a prevalent yet frequently underrecognized complication of surgery and anesthesia. POCD is associated with protracted recovery, diminished quality of life, and adverse long-term outcomes, particularly among elderly and high-risk populations. While early detection via bedside cognitive tests is vital for optimizing postoperative care, more comprehensive gold-standard neuropsychological batteries remain largely unfeasible in routine clinical practice due to significant time, cost, and resource constraints. This narrative review evaluates the clinical utility of practical bedside cognitive assessments for identifying POCD. Commonly employed tools—including the Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA), Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE), Trail Making Test (TMT), Digit Span, Clock Drawing Test (CDT), and Abbreviated Mental Test Score (AMTS)—are critically appraised regarding their sensitivity, limitations, and suitability for the perioperative environment. The review specifically addresses feasibility in acute postoperative settings, accounting for confounding factors such as age, literacy, and sensory or motor impairments. Furthermore, the necessity of establishing baseline cognitive status and the urgent need for tool validation within surgical cohorts are highlighted. No single bedside instrument offers a sufficiently comprehensive assessment for POCD. Rather, a multimodal approach—integrating high-sensitivity tools like the MoCA or TMT with rapid screening instruments—represents a more robust and clinically viable strategy for early detection. Future research must focus on standardizing assessment protocols and validating these tools across diverse surgical populations to ultimately enhance the quality of postoperative cognitive care.

title: Regulating AI-Generated Inventions in Tanzania: A Comparative Analysis of BRELA and South Africa’s CIPC
container-title: East African Journal of Law and Ethics
97d91fe2e65b9b432b752d3e2552b57b2f5ca94f.abstract: Artificial intelligence systems now produce technical solutions with little or no human contribution to the inventive step, and the DABUS applications filed by Dr Stephen Thaler have tested whether patent law can accommodate an inventor that is not a person. Courts and offices in the United Kingdom, the United States, Europe, Australia and Germany have refused, while South Africa’s Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC) published the grant of a patent naming DABUS as inventor in July 2021. This article asks whether Tanzania’s Business Registrations and Licensing Agency (BRELA) could follow that example under the Patents (Registration) Act, Cap 217, and, if not, what reform is required. Using doctrinal analysis and functional comparison, it finds that the two statutes are closer than is usually assumed: neither defines ‘inventor’, and both require an applicant who is not the inventor to show a right derived from the inventor. The decisive difference is administrative. The South African grant followed a formalities-only check in which, on the published record, the applicant’s entitlement was not tested, leaving validity to revocation proceedings. Section 25(7) and (8) of Cap 217, by contrast, require the Registrar to examine every request for compliance with section 18(3) and (4) and to reject one that is not corrected. An application naming DABUS would therefore fail at the formal stage, and one naming a human who did not devise the invention would be open to invalidation under section 64(2)(d). BRELA cannot reproduce the CIPC outcome by discretion. The article recommends, in order of priority, statements of practice on AI-assisted inventions, revised forms, a statutory definition of inventor and, after regional consultation through ARIPO and the East African Community, a deliberate legislative choice on whether AI-generated inventions should be protected.

title: Teacher Education and Sustainable Development: A Critical Review of the Policy-Practice Divide
container-title: Journal of Sustainable Research and Development
c19cc8b01bafefca56e35166936bcafe7b4832b4.abstract: It has been common knowledge that teacher education is key to the attainment of education and sustainable development, but the incorporation of sustainability in teacher preparation remains unbalanced and limited. The paper is a critical review of the recent literature in teacher education and sustainable development and how sustainability is conceptualised, operationalised, and constrained in teacher education programmes. Approximately 40 peer-reviewed publications and international policy documents were analysed thematically to inform this synthesis. The review applies peer-reviewed research and international policy models to identify the prevailing approaches to sustainability skills, pedagogical and institutional strategies, as well as to outline the common challenges encountered by the method, such as conceptual vagueness, lack of assessment capacity, disconnection between coursework and practicum, and dependence on small-scale projects. The results indicate that sustainability is usually addressed as a supplemental issue instead of being a fundamental organising principle of teacher education, which leads to a lack of evidence of sustainable changes to teaching practice. To make a meaningful step forward, the review proposes the need for whole-programme integration, enhancing the capacity of teacher educators, and conducting more longitudinal and context-sensitive research, especially in underrepresented areas, to make teacher education a long-term force of sustainable development.

title: A Hybrid Convolutional Recurrent Neural Model for Noise Detection and Automated Calibration of Medical Devices via Molecular Vibration Analysis
518557eedb6ff36ea9b47c24553d6afd51c850c8.abstract: Abstract Accurate noise detection and calibration are essential for maintaining the measurement reliability of medical devices. This study proposes a hybrid convolutional recurrent neural network (CRNN) framework for noise detection and automated calibration of ventilators and electrocardiogram (ECG) machines using molecular vibration analysis. A molecular vibration model was developed to characterize mechanical vibration, electromagnetic interference, and environmental conduction noise, achieving an average noise classification accuracy of 96.2%. The proposed CRNN with hybrid attention maintained 91.5% accuracy under low signal-to-noise conditions. A deep deterministic policy gradient-based calibration strategy was subsequently employed to optimize calibration parameters automatically, reducing calibration time by 72.5% and improving calibration accuracy by 78.5% compared with conventional methods. After calibration, the average relative errors were 1.9% for ventilator tidal-volume measurements and 0.92% for QRS-complex amplitude measurements in ECG devices. Cross-device validation achieved 94.3% accuracy across different equipment brands. The results demonstrate that integrating molecular vibration analysis, hybrid deep learning, and automated calibration provides an effective approach for reliable noise detection and precision calibration of medical devices.

title: Editorial: generative AI and the small business frontier – charting pathways toward meaningful social impact
container-title: Journal of Social Impact in Business Research
c4b06f07519c890d4aa7881d2f5de009595df712.abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine how small and medium-sized enterprises can leverage generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) to create social impact, by developing a multidimensional framework linking GenAI adoption with social-value creation. Design/methodology/approach This editorial adopts a conceptual synthesis approach, that integrates insights from the special-issue papers with emerging research and identifies principal domains of social impact. Findings Social impact is not a property of GenAI but a contingent outcome of how it is applied and adopted. While firms may have similar GenAI potentialities across various impact domains, success is dependent on human, organisational, sectoral and institutional contexts. Practical implications This editorial provides a framework for assessing where GenAI can support social-value creation whilst managing ethical, organisational and workforce risks. Impact accrues through organisational processes rather than through adoption itself. Originality/value The social impact of GenAI is extended beyond productivity and efficiency and positioned as a multidimensional and contingent outcome of technology adoption. A four-element framework links GenAI capability, organisational mechanisms, enabling and constraining conditions and stakeholder outcomes, which then informs a research agenda.

title: From awe to emotional brand attachment: a cognitive appraisal perspective on VR brand experiences
container-title: Journal of Product & Brand Management
2a02739e2da8b57381342589a61ac9c76d3c74b0.abstract: Purpose Prior research on awe in relation to virtual reality (VR) has treated awe as a response to technological stimuli, leaving the consumer appraisals through which awe arises underexplored. Drawing on cognitive appraisal theory, this paper aims to address this gap by investigating whether aesthetic, sensory and content appraisals of a VR brand experience predict awe and whether awe mediates the relationships between these appraisals and emotional brand attachment. Design/methodology/approach Data were collected via a survey of 334 Generation Z participants who experienced an in-person brand encounter via a VR headset and were analysed using covariance-based structural equation modelling in LISREL. Findings Aesthetic, sensory and content appraisals positively predict awe, which, in turn, predicts emotional brand attachment. Awe also mediates the relationships between each of the three appraisal and emotional brand attachment. Originality/value At the intersection of the cognitive psychology of VR and emotional branding, this paper reframes the origins of awe in VR brand experiences, shifting from a stimulus-centred to an appraisal-centred account. It also identifies aesthetic, sensory and content appraisals as the experiential predictors of awe and extends emotional branding to self-transcendent emotions by showing how awe translates experiential appraisals into emotional brand attachment.

title: Trustworthy Federated Clinical Intelligence with Homomorphic Encryption and  Explainable AI
container-title: International Journal on Advanced Computer Engineering and Communication Technology
e9efaf7e4de70a4bb9a5e76e1dc2d37a457ecb6d.abstract: Cross-institutional clinical artificial intelligence is constrained by fragmented patient data, non-identically distributed (non-IID) populations, leakage from shared model updates, and limited interpretability. Federated learning (FL) preserves data locality, but ordinary FL neither makes model updates confidential nor guarantees stable optimization under heterogeneous clients. This paper proposes a defense-in-depth framework that coordinates Federated Proximal (FedProx) optimization, record-level differential privacy (DP), Cheon–Kim–Kim–Song (CKKS) approximate homomorphic encryption, and explainable artificial intelligence (XAI). FedProx limits local model drift; DP-SGD bounds the influence of an individual training record; and CKKS permits weighted aggregation while client updates remain encrypted. A key-separated design keeps the aggregation server from being provisioned with the secret key used to reveal individual contributions; only the aggregate is released for global-model construction. Grad-CAM and SHAP/LIME provide clinician-facing explanations, while an audit dashboard reports convergence, privacy-accounting inputs, encryption status, and systems overhead. We formalize the learning objective, privacy mechanism, encrypted aggregation, threat model, numerical approximation error, communication footprint, and an evaluation protocol spanning IID and controlled non-IID partitions. The contribution is a reproducible system-level co-design and evaluation framework rather than a new cryptographic primitive or optimization algorithm.

title: A critical discourse analysis of TikTok on parliamentary processes: Unpacking language ideologies in South Africa
container-title: Inkanyiso
a3a0ea1a6af23698c73038c4705939714d651152.abstract: There is no doubt that South African parliamentarians have embodied English, even though 12 languages are spoken in South Africa and are constitutionally protected. This insidious embodiment of English speaks to language ideologies that set it above other African languages, and it is important to highlight this on the African continent, where languages of colonisers remain more dominant. The article sets out to analyse language ideologies as reflected in TikTok discourses responding to South African parliamentary processes, particularly following a few notable incidents that occurred in Parliament in July 2024. Furthermore, the dominance of English in public discourse is examined as realised and reflected on social media platforms such as TikTok. We argue that, based on parliamentary discourses in South Africa, the TikTok comments analysed show a complex interplay of language ideologies that reflect broader societal debates about language, power and identity. We conclude that there is still a need to highlight the importance of recognising and valuing linguistic diversity as a key component of social justice and access. Contribution: The article extends language ideology scholarship into the South African digital context, using TikTok discourse to show how ordinary citizens interpret and contest the dominance of English within a formal political institution such as Parliament. In doing so, it demonstrates the value of social media as an underused site for tracking public sentiment on multilingual policy tensions that often remain hidden in official parliamentary discourse.

title: AI-Driven Predictive Maintenance for Institutional Electrical Systems
container-title: Journal of Technology and System Information
743e0632b4637f415786ff15de8256d3f95412a3.abstract: High-voltage power distribution networks in institutional settings are increasingly vulnerable to age-related degradation, operational volatility, and unexpected service disruptions. Conventional maintenance practices—dominated by reactive repairs and static time-based servicing—impose significant financial burdens and risk over-servicing intact assets. To address these operational constraints, this study employs a thematic literature synthesis of smart grid prognostics and IIoT asset telemetry (2015–2025) to formulate an end-to-end four-layer predictive maintenance (PdM) framework. The architectural continuum is established by systematically mapping physical multi-sensor acquisition to edge-cloud analytics (GRU and Bi-LSTM engines), dynamic Asset Health Index (AHI) tracking, and automated, cyber-secure Computerized Maintenance Management System (CMMS) dispatch. Synthesizing literature performance baselines reveals that deep bidirectional recurrent networks—notably Bi-LSTM models—achieve superior degradation tracking for Remaining Useful Life (RUL) estimation, attaining an F1-score of 91.0%, a Mean Absolute Error of 4.3%, and a Root Mean Squared Error of 4.2. Furthermore, multi-modal feature fusion significantly sharpens Asset Health Index (AHI) modeling, driving prediction errors down to an RMSE of 0.052, lengthening warning lead times to 37 days, and maintaining false alarm rates at 6.2%. The transition to an AI-enabled prognostic strategy yields up to a 50.0% decrease in overall operational and maintenance costs while extending high-voltage asset longevity by 40%. The inclusion of Explainable AI (SHAP and LRP) alongside robust Operational Technology cybersecurity measures guarantees operational transparency and cyber resilience.

title: TECHNOLOGICAL EMPOWERMENT AND VALUE BALANCE: DUAL PATHWAYS IN CHINA’S TECHNOLOGY GOVERNANCE POLICIES FOR THE AI ERA
container-title: Trends in Social Sciences and Humanities Research
046a4b825efe15b9ca51cb520c373729b94ebde6.abstract: The deep embedding of artificial intelligence (AI) technology is reshaping global governance. The tension between “technological empowerment” and “value balance” has become a common governance challenge for countries worldwide. Based on a dual-pathway framework of “technology-driven modernization of state governance” and “technology-embedded multi-actor social co-governance,” this paper systematically analyzes the internal logic and operational mechanisms of technology governance in China in the AI era. The study finds that China’s technology governance is not a single efficiency-oriented application of technology; rather, through the coordinated operation of dual pathways, it comprehensively achieves four major governance functions: efficiency improvement, equity promotion, security assurance, and institutional reconstruction. In terms of model characteristics, China has developed a distinctive paradigm centered on “enabling governance”-one that takes state capacity as its foundation, institutional flexibility as its safeguard, and plural public values as its goals. This paradigm transcends the single efficiency-oriented governance logic of the West and offers a non-Western pathway with both theoretical inspiration and practical reference for global digital governance. This paper argues that the core of “enabling governance” lies in resolving the tension between technological empowerment and value balance through institutional design, and that the transferability of its experience depends on the conditions of fit in specific institutional contexts.

title: Bridging critical knowledge and action gaps in urban health: A call for transdisciplinary approaches in urban studies in the era of global population aging and climate change
container-title: Urban Studies
2e4af69af0722e606720f73f3fc21a523ab6374c.abstract: Urbanization and population aging are two “mega-trends” posing significant challenges to global health, particularly under climate change. Despite extensive evidence on the links between the built environment and health, urban planning scholars and practitioners still miss valuable opportunities to contribute to public health and urban health equity—which often remain marginal or only implicit topics in urban planning discourses and practices. Against this background, we organized the transdisciplinary workshop “Global Health Challenges Related to Demographic & Climate Changes: Implications for Urban and Territorial Planning” (Basel, 2024), convening scholars and practitioners to co-develop a research agenda addressing knowledge-to-action gaps in urban health equity and climate resilience. Building on the workshop’s discussions, this commentary highlights current challenges in reconnecting urban planning and public health while presenting opportunities to bridge this gap. We argue for an “ultra-local” approach that acknowledges the chronic lack of granular data necessary to address spatial justice and urban health inequities, emphasizing the importance of evidence- and place-based planning. To illustrate this approach, we present two recent experiences: the BH-Viva project in Brazil, which assessed impact of slum-upgrading projects on urban health equity, and the Saint-Louis Master Plan in Senegal, a pioneering effort integrating climate resilience into urban policy and planning. Ultimately, we present what we identified as priority research paths in urban studies, having transdisciplinarity as a precondition for urban planners to effectively tackle pressing global health challenges.

title: Beyond Human-Centered Design: Toward Ecocentric Thinking
container-title: Research into Ecological Transformation in Architectural Sciences: From Anthropocentric Design to Ecology-Focused Design
a833e128e65689a4edbb525a260c7dc42756ce8d.abstract: The chapter reflects on the limits of the human-centered approach to design amid the ecological crisis and the potential of ecocentric thinking to inform architectural production. It employs a qualitative methodology based on conceptual analysis of selected literature and comparative case studies of Bosco Verticale in Milan and The High Line in New York. The cases are examined through four aspects: the human subject in (re)design, ecological interdependence, multispecies coexistence and non-human agency, and the built environment as an ecological interface. The analysis highlights the need to reconsider anthropocentric attitudes in architecture. It also identifies opportunities for using vegetation and landscape features to support non-human life, while emphasizing the importance of maintenance, resource consumption, habitat connectivity, and environmental impacts. The built environment as an ecological interface is proposed as a conceptual framework for architectural practice in the context of ecology.

title: Ecological Systems Thinking in Architecture
container-title: Research into Ecological Transformation in Architectural Sciences: From Anthropocentric Design to Ecology-Focused Design
83380e21a423296d5b365ab34c5e48dfa4d35323.abstract: This study examines ecological systems thinking as a conceptual framework for redefining architecture in response to contemporary environmental challenges. Moving beyond the conventional understanding of buildings as isolated physical objects, it conceptualizes architecture as an interconnected system operating across building, urban, ecosystem, and planetary scales. The study draws on systems thinking, socio-ecological approaches, ecological design, regenerative design, and planetary perspectives to explore the relationships among energy flows, material cycles, water systems, user behavior, biodiversity, and environmental processes. Through a qualitative design that combines a literature review with comparative analyses of three pairs of traditional Anatolian and contemporary ecological examples, selected according to explicit criteria, it demonstrates how local knowledge, climate-responsive strategies, and resource-conscious practices can inform current architectural approaches. The study further proposes a Multi-Scalar Ecological Design Framework that integrates environmental impacts across different scales. Ultimately, it argues that architecture should evolve from minimizing environmental harm toward actively supporting ecological regeneration, resilience, and long-term planetary well-being.

title: From Vernacular Ecological Intelligence to Planetary Design: Life Cycle Thinking as a Framework for Ecological Transformation in Architecture
container-title: Research into Ecological Transformation in Architectural Sciences: From Anthropocentric Design to Ecology-Focused Design
8c713823c70f94c725f6482bb0c297b9e934319d.abstract: The ecological transformation of architecture requires reconsidering how architectural knowledge is produced, environmental consequences are evaluated, and responsibility is addressed across spatial, temporal, and ecological scales. This chapter brings vernacular ecological knowledge into dialogue with Life Cycle Thinking and Planetary Design. Vernacular architecture is approached as a dynamic socio-ecological knowledge system shaped by culture, climate, materiality, and collective practices. Maintenance, repair, adaptability, and intergenerational learning are examined as forms of situated ecological intelligence rather than historical models to be replicated. Life Cycle Thinking provides a framework for integrating place-based knowledge into contemporary architectural decisions, extending environmental assessment beyond carbon to circularity, biodiversity, regeneration, cultural continuity, and resilience. The relationship with Planetary Design is understood as a scalar and epistemic connection through which local knowledge informs decisions affecting broader ecological and material systems. Rather than prescribing a universal method, Planetary Design is presented as a boundary-aware, sufficiency-led, regenerative, justice-oriented, and adaptive approach. The chapter argues that ecological transformation depends on combining quantitative assessment with local knowledge, social needs, interconnected system boundaries, and long-term stewardship.

title: Generative artificial intelligence drives large model generation algorithm for enhancing Chinese modern traditional cultural knowledge
container-title: Discover Artificial Intelligence
f48c63c87e8ab5a4802a0daf6c6d06f0de6ee24c.abstract: Abstract To address outdated knowledge, cultural-context mismatch, weak evidence linkage, and unsupported expansion in general-purpose large language model generation of traditional-cultural content, this study proposes a generative AI-driven knowledge-enhanced generation algorithm. The method decouples a frozen Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct generator from an external dynamic knowledge base and uses a four-field semantic tag scheme covering cultural category, historical stage, regional origin, and application scenario. Candidate evidence is ranked by vector similarity, graph relations, tag consistency, source credibility, and conflict penalties, then assembled into a constrained prompt without modifying the internal attention layers of the frozen model. An incremental update mechanism combines source verification, conflict detection, and expert review, while factual consistency, cultural-context adaptability, and evidence coverage are used for post-generation verification. Experiments cover classical texts, cultural heritage objects, intangible cultural heritage crafts, traditional Chinese opera, and folk culture, with 1,080 factual question-answering samples and 360 contextual generation tasks. The proposed system achieves 88.61% factual accuracy, 95.28% answer relevance, 94.17% evidence faithfulness, and 92.50% cultural-context adaptability. After knowledge updating, accuracy on update-dependent questions rises from 58.67% to 91.33%. These results indicate that the proposed framework provides a traceable, context-sensitive generation pipeline while retaining a frozen generation model; between-system differences are interpreted descriptively because complete paired baseline predictions were not retained.

title: A CRITICAL ANALYSIS OF R.G COLLINGWOOD'S CONCEPTION OF HISTORY IN THE IDEA OF HISTORY
container-title: ShodhSamajik: Journal of Social Studies
2a32446bc42cfc329fcdbea14b51ed3ffa1c8a83.abstract: This paper is a critical analysis of R.G. Collingwood’s conception of history as presented in his seminal work The Idea of History. Collingwood’s philosophy of history introduces the concepts of re-enactment and historical imagination, positing that understanding history requires more than recounting events. It demands reliving the thoughts of historical characters and personalities. This paper explores the strengths and limitations of Collingwood’s theories, assessing their influence on modern historiography and their implications for historical methodology. Through a close analysis of his work, the paper concludes that while Collingwood’s approach to history has greatly enriched historiographical practices, it also raises questions about objectivity and interpretive limits.
