title: Effects of AI-Empowered Digital Inclusive Finance on the Income Growth of County-Level Farmers in Yunnan Province: An Empirical Test Based on County-Level Panel Data
container-title: Future of Social Sciences
26e7a2e0132358e730771e71c9a3dc17eac1b00e.abstract: {'en': "Using panel data of 119 counties (cities, districts) in Yunnan Province from 2015 to 2022, this paper constructs an AI-empowered digital inclusive finance index and examines its effect on county-level farmer income growth and the underlying channels with a two-way fixed-effects model. The results show that AI-empowered digital inclusive finance significantly promotes farmer income growth: a one-unit increase in the index raises rural residents' per capita disposable income by about 0.12% on average, and this conclusion remains robust after instrumental-variable estimation, replacement of the dependent variable, winsorization, and system GMM estimation. Mechanism tests indicate that AI-empowered digital inclusive finance mainly works through three channels—easing credit constraints, popularizing digital payment, and expanding e-commerce channels for agricultural products—whose combined mediation contribution exceeds one half. Heterogeneity analysis shows that the income effect is more pronounced for farmers in poverty-stricken and mountainous counties, and mainly manifests as growth in operating and wage income. Accordingly, policy recommendations are proposed, including deepening county-level intelligent risk control, improving rural digital infrastructure, developing e-commerce for plateau-featured agricultural products, and strengthening county-level financial risk monitoring."}

title: Research on the Long-Term Mechanism of Mental Health Education for Primary and Secondary School Students under the Background of Family-School Collaboration
container-title: Future of Social Sciences
488478af42f95e16827ae58be99f0e0064affd3b.abstract: {'en': 'The detection rate of mental health problems among primary and secondary school students has shown an upward trend in recent years, and neither schools nor families alone can cope with it; family-school collaboration has thus become an explicit requirement at the policy level. In practice, however, such collaboration mostly remains at the level of activities, with prominent problems including vague assignment of responsibilities, superficial ways of cooperation, mutual isolation of information, insufficient professional capacity, and the absence of assessment and incentives, presenting the features of being campaign-like, fragmented, and reactive. On the basis of sorting out the practical difficulties, this paper proposes that a long-term mechanism should replace campaign-style activities with institutionalization, replace fragmentation with continuity, be underpinned by professionalism, and center on developmental goals. It then discusses the paths for building such a mechanism from the aspects of establishing two-way information sharing and screening linkage, constructing an institutionalized collaboration framework with clear rights and responsibilities, improving a professional support network linking family, school, community, and medical institutions, perfecting evaluation, supervision, and resource guarantee, cultivating parents\' mental health literacy, and carrying out tiered and categorized precise collaboration, so as to provide a reference for moving mental health education in primary and secondary schools from "campaign-style" to "routinized" under the background of family-school collaboration.'}

title: Intersectional, Feminist, and Decolonial Approaches to Researching Care-Experienced Children and Youth: A Critical Review
container-title: Trauma, Violence, & Abuse
2ffb51725941ccfa735e0334947e1cd29f46b1f1.abstract: Research has consistently shown that involvement in child welfare systems is associated with elevated risks of adverse long-term outcomes across education, employment, mental health, housing stability, and justice system involvement. However, much of this literature has relied on outcome-focused approaches that insufficiently account for the intersecting structures shaping care-experienced children’s and youth’s lived realities. This critical review synthesises feminist, intersectional, and decolonial frameworks applied to research on care-experienced children and young people, examining their theoretical foundations, methodological practices, and common themes and implications for future research. A qualitative meta-analytic scoping review was conducted following the frameworks of Arksey and O’Malley, and Levac et al. Searches were carried out in Web of Science, ERIC, and EBSCOhost using keywords in English, Spanish, and Catalan. From 899 records identified, 22 studies published between 2019 and 2025 met the inclusion criteria. Eligible studies focused on care-experienced children or youth involved in child welfare services and adopted feminist, intersectional, decolonial, or critical pedagogical orientations, with a focus on young people’s agency. The findings identify recurrent forms of trauma linked to gender-based violence, racialised and gendered disciplinary practices, homophobic and transphobic microaggressions, identity erasure, housing precarity, and punitive educational responses. While intersectionality is increasingly referenced, its integration into research design and analysis remains uneven. Methodologically, participatory, narrative, and arts-based approaches show particular promise in centring youth agency and challenging deficit-based discourses. The review underscores the need for trauma-informed, anti-oppressive, and non-policing research frameworks capable of addressing structural violence and informing more just and inclusive child welfare policies and practices.

title: An Exploration of Individual Psychological Resilience Differences and Influencing Factors in Cross-Cultural Contexts
container-title: Future of Social Sciences
940002ed746b2e86aa3e15e2c00676eaf2624cb1.abstract: {'en': 'Resilience research has produced a long list of individual-level predictors, but most of that evidence comes from a few Western countries, and the cross-national comparability of the standard resilience scales has seldom been tested. This paper asks whether the same individual characteristics predict resilience to the same degree in different cultural contexts. A synthetic dataset calibrated to effect sizes reported in the published cross-cultural literature (N = 2,400 adults, 400 each in China, Brazil, Japan, India, Germany and the United States) is used to test three questions: whether resilience scores differ across countries, whether the 10-item Connor-Davidson Resilience Scale is measurement-invariant across them, and whether country-level individualism moderates four individual-level predictors. Country means spanned less than two points on a 40-point scale (η² = .009, ω² = .007). The scale reached scalar invariance when items were treated as ordinal, including equality of item thresholds. The substantive finding is a set of cross-level interactions. Interdependent self-construal predicted resilience in collectivist settings and not in individualist ones; independent self-construal showed the reverse; social support was a stronger predictor in collectivist settings. Independent self-construal had no average effect (b = 0.18, p = .127). Culture does not determine how resilient people are. It determines which resources matter.'}

title: Integrating Generative AI and Data Science into General Chemistry Laboratories
95b0ca8d6c9325175ea829c0696ac48544f573b5.abstract: The emergence of generative AI tools such as ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini is reshaping research, education, and industry. Recent workforce data indicate a widening gap between declining junior-level opportunities and rising demand for senior-level expertise, underscoring the urgent need to adapt undergraduate chemistry curricula to prepare students for an AI-enabled workforce. To address this challenge, we designed a series of Python-based laboratory experiments for General Chemistry that integrate generative AI with instructor guidance to enhance student learning. The modules focus on (1) using AI tools to support conceptual understanding, (2) applying AI-assisted coding for data visualization and analysis, and (3) introducing machine learning workflows to solve real-world chemistry problems. All activities are implemented in Google Colaboratory, a cloud-based programming platform now integrated with Gemini, which helps students, particularly those without prior programming experience, complete coding tasks with step-by-step instructor guidance. We compare student attitudes toward the use of AI and programming at the beginning and end of the semesters, observing a more positive attitude toward AI use and increased confidence in programming. To demonstrate scalability, three PhD graduate students, two of whom had no prior programming background, successfully led the laboratory sessions using these AI-supported materials, confirming that instructors across a wide range of computational skill levels can teach the experiments. This work demonstrates how generative AI can create more prosperous and equitable learning experiences, equipping students with transferable skills essential for research and industry careers, as well as the evolving STEM workforce.

title: Robust Mean-CVaR Portfolio Optimization with Liquidity Constraints
container-title: Future of Social Sciences
822bef27b4b75ac75c04f59f1830238c514810cc.abstract: {'en': 'Portfolio models that combine mean-CVaR objectives with robust parameter uncertainty normally treat positions as perfectly liquid. This paper adds a liquidation-horizon constraint and a position-dependent trading cost to a robust mean-CVaR model, and shows that the result is a second-order cone program. Under ellipsoidal perturbations of scenario returns, the worst-case CVaR equals the empirical CVaR plus a norm term, so no additional scenarios are needed. A rolling experiment with twenty assets and twenty replications compares four strategies. Relative to the nominal benchmark, the integrated model raises the Sharpe ratio from 0.48 to 0.68, lowers daily CVaR from 2.40% to 2.03%, and cuts the stressed liquidation cost from 145 to 45 basis points. Liquidity constraints account for most of the gain; robustness contributes mainly through lower tail risk once those constraints bind. The two frictions are partial substitutes, and ignoring either yields portfolios that are expensive to unwind.'}

title: Cloud-Blockchain Integrated Privacy-Preserving Distributed Computation Offloading Scheme in the Internet of Vehicles
container-title: ICST Transactions on Scalable Information Systems
e5417cbaa1fadb258359a2c0127907f7c3ca30ef.abstract: INTRODUCTION: With the rapid development of the Internet of Vehicles technology, on-board applications in intelligent vehicles are increasingly facing the challenge of processing latency-sensitive and computationally intensive tasks. Although vehicle-mounted computing units possess certain computing capabilities, their limited resources cannot cope with complex latency-sensitive tasks. Offloading computations to resource-rich cloud servers is a feasible solution to this problem. However, transmission costs and communication delays on remote cloud servers become major bottlenecks for offloading latency-sensitive tasks. The emergence of Mobile Edge Computing (MEC) shifts computing power from centralized cloud servers to the network edge, reducing latency. Nevertheless, existing schemes still suffer from poor fault tolerance, privacy leakage, and low computational efficiency. OBJECTIVES: To address these limitations, this paper proposes a cloud-blockchain integrated privacy-preserving distributed computation offloading scheme (FCOS). METHODS: FCOS significantly improves fault tolerance via a redundant distributed computing mechanism, effectively mitigating the impact of single-point failures on computations. RESULTS: Smart contracts on the blockchain guarantee verifiability and fairness throughout the computation offloading process, enhancing overall offloading security. For privacy protection, the scheme combines homomorphic encryption and blind factor technology to protect data privacy with low computational overhead on intelligent vehicle terminals. CONCLUSION: Compared with existing methods, FCOS reduces the average computation time by 90.4% for polynomial calculations within 5000 iterations in the cloud computing phase. Under a single-point failure rate ranging from 0% to 60%, the average computation time for polynomial calculations within 10,000 iterations is reduced by 92.9% to 96.7%.

title: Effect of Thermal Expansion Mismatch on the Optical Coupling Stability of Fiber Array Units
container-title: Future of Social Sciences
b160998b4bcd25865f220f3ee9ef76b8aef5b07d.abstract: {'en': 'Fiber array units (FAUs) are key components for fiber-to-chip coupling in silicon photonics and optical interconnection systems, and their coupling stability under temperature variation directly determines system reliability. This paper analyzes the mechanism by which thermal expansion mismatch among the optical fiber, substrate, and adhesive in an FAU induces deformation of the fiber end faces and consequently degrades optical coupling. On the basis of the structure of the unit and the mismatch in coefficients of thermal expansion, an analytical model of thermal deformation and coupling loss is established that covers lateral offset, pitch mismatch, axial separation, and angular misalignment. The effects of temperature cycling, adhesive creep, and hysteresis on coupling stability are discussed. Numerical estimation shows that within a broad temperature range the coupling loss introduced by the differential expansion between substrate and fibers and by adhesive strain can reach several tenths of a decibel and may even exceed 1 dB, which is by no means negligible for multi-channel coupling. Accordingly, design and mitigation measures are proposed from the aspects of CTE-matched materials, adhesive engineering, structural compensation, and packaging, providing a reference for improving the temperature stability of fiber array units.'}

title: Differences in Translators' Cognitive Load under Generative-AI Post-Editing: An Eye-Tracking Study of English-Chinese Scientific Texts
container-title: Future of Social Sciences
7c7fe2b629e6642e4941218c5d737a4c99000526.abstract: {'en': 'Generative artificial intelligence has entered the translation workflow faster than evidence about its effect on the translator has accumulated. This study asks whether working from a large language model draft lowers cognitive load or merely redistributes it. Thirty-six translators, twenty translation trainees and sixteen practising professionals, rendered nine English popular-science and technical passages into Chinese under three within-subject conditions. These were unaided human translation (HT), post-editing of a static neural machine translation draft (NMT-PE), and post-editing of a GPT-4o draft with an interactive prompt pane (GAI-PE). Pupil diameter change, fixation duration, gaze distribution, keystroke logs, NASA-TLX ratings and MQM scores were recorded. GAI-PE cut task time by 44.2 per cent against HT and by 17.1 per cent against NMT-PE. Its MQM scores were higher than those of NMT-PE, while the difference from HT did not reach significance. Pupil diameter change was nevertheless largest in GAI-PE at 0.095 mm, against 0.083 mm in HT and 0.064 mm in NMT-PE, while gaze on the source text fell to 38.3 per cent, the lowest of the three. Subjective ratings moved the other way and ranked HT as the most demanding condition. In an exploratory analysis, self-reported AI-use frequency was associated with a smaller pupil response in GAI-PE, whereas English proficiency showed no such association. These observations are consistent with an increased demand for verification, though the generative condition also gave access to an interactive prompt pane, so the differences cannot be attributed to the model alone.'}

title: AI adoption in public sector urban planning: Aspirations and realities in London and Beijing
container-title: European Urban and Regional Studies
f67f375ebb7467938a2adac52365fc1497fb294b.abstract: This paper examines the adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) in public sector urban planning through a comparative analysis of London and Beijing. Drawing on rapid qualitative methods combining interviews with public sector planners and related actors with documentary analysis, it adapts and spatialises Wisdom et al.’s multi-level framework across four analytical dimensions: public policy contexts, financial conditions, legal frameworks and regulations, innovation, data and organisational determinants and individual planners’ values, skills and norms. A central finding is that AI means different things to different planners. Interviewees drew on two broad understandings: general-purpose large language model tools used informally for drafting and synthesis, and purpose-built planning-specific tools tied to particular statutory functions. In both cities, adoption is largely confined to the former, concentrated on downstream tasks such as drafting documents, while the latter remains exploratory and uneven. The paper demonstrates that barriers to adoption outweigh drivers, raising key questions about the uncertain direction of AI-led public sector planning delivery and its associated politics. Across both cases, the adoption of AI is less a narrative of inevitable technological transformation than a process of political, institutional and professional negotiation over what is considered acceptable, trustworthy and feasible. By geographically locating where AI is being developed, tested and used in planning and tracing how its influence is distributed across distinct urban governance contexts, the paper argues for repositioning debates on AI in planning away from deterministic narratives of technological transformation and toward a more critical, geographically and governance-led understanding of adoption and non-adoption.

title: Data-Driven Multifidelity Generative Topology Optimization for Geometrically Nonlinear Structures
container-title: AIAA Journal
aa21b7af4131405d692f1b56e5e437b59338ff24.abstract: Building upon existing multifidelity topology optimization studies where geometric nonlinearity has been considered in high-fidelity models, this work introduces a generative learning framework to generate, evaluate, and select multiple nonlinear feasible designs with different compliance/volume-fraction tradeoffs, thereby improving Pareto-oriented design-space exploration for geometrically nonlinear topology optimization. Addressing the critical challenge of large-deformation behavior in lightweight aerospace components, the proposed method integrates computationally efficient linear topology optimization with high-fidelity nonlinear finite element analysis. A variational autoencoder learns the latent distribution of elite designs, enabling efficient exploration of high-performance structural configurations without repeated high-fidelity nonlinear sensitivity analysis. Through simplex crossover operations in the latent space and a competitive diversity preservation mechanism, the framework iteratively identifies an approximate Pareto set of high-fidelity-screened candidate designs. Numerical demonstrations on a large-deformation cantilever beam show that the proposed framework can generate multiple high-fidelity-screened designs with compliance/volume-fraction tradeoffs comparable to those of a gradient-based baseline. The results suggest that the framework is a practical design-space exploration tool for geometrically nonlinear topology optimization rather than a universal replacement for gradient-based nonlinear optimization.

title: <b>Impact of AI Generated Content and Perceived Personalization on Purchase Intention with Mediating Input of Brand Credibility in FMCG Industry in Pakistan</b>
container-title: International Journal of Emerging Multidisciplinaries: Social Science
2613ec1fb9a9ce3dda839e8c6439ebcc1333759b.abstract: This research study investigated the empirical impact of AI generated content and perceived personalization on purchase intention with mediating input of brand credibility in case of FMCG sector in Pakistan. It investigated both direct and indirect of AI generated content and perceived personalization on purchase along with the impact of AI generated content on perceived personalization in Pakistan. The study used quantitative research approach and employed deductive approach to build hypotheses. Those were tested with application of statistical techniques i.e. structural equation model using PLS-Smart as software. The study targeted the FMCG sector in Pakistan and used convenience sampling technique to extract with the required number of responses i.e. 384 using questionnaire as data collection tool. The study followed with the survey based method to collect with the required number of response in the limited period of time. The study revealed that there is significant impact of AI Generated Content on Brand Credibility, Perceived Personalization and Purchase Intention with coefficient value of 0.4294, 0.5758 and 0.5211having significance value of 0.0000, 0.000 and 0.000 respectively. There is also a significant impact of Perceived Personalization on Brand Credibility and Purchase Intention with coefficient value of 0.4857 and 0.3093 having significance value of 0.0000 and 0.0000 respectively. There is also a significant impact of Brand Credibility on Purchase Intention with coefficient value of 0.4574 having significance value of 0.0000. FMCG companies should develop accurate, engaging, and personalized AI-generated content to enhance brand credibility and consumer confidence. Marketers should ensure truthful product information, transparent communication, and alignment with customer preferences.

title: From automation to authorship: Computational reasoning and design agency in architectural AI tools
container-title: Journal of Information Technology in Construction
f459ddbe10d9229aeff00984e777729be2bb0281.abstract: The increasing presence of AI in architectural practice is renegotiating who, or what, holds creative authority over a project. This paper introduces a novel two-construct framework, AI Logic (AL) and Architectural Value (AV), to operationalise this shift. AL captures a tool's computational reasoning across automation, optimisation, and predictive capability, while AV captures design agency support, contextual sensitivity, and exploratory capacity. Positioning fifty AI-driven tools within this AL-AV construct via tension map analysis identifies stage-specific patterns within the selected dataset. It shows that design agency is redistributed unevenly across the project lifecycle, expanding in early design stages where tools act as creative collaborators, and contracting under efficiency-driven logics in later stages where automation prioritises monitoring and compliance over qualitative judgement. Cross-referencing against secondary parameters such as building typology, user group, tool maturity, and regulatory context surfaces fundamental gaps in current AI provision. The selected tools predominantly support residential and commercial applications. Documented regional orientations include North American and European standards, while coverage of other regions and typologies is less evident within the sample. To assess scoring consistency, ten AEC professionals and the author independently evaluated a subset of five tools, with one tool representing each of RIBA Stages 1–5. Intraclass correlation analysis demonstrated strong panel-level inter-rater reliability for both constructs, while comparison of the author's scores with the expert consensus indicated close alignment. Following this calibration, the author independently applied the same evaluation framework to the remaining forty-five tools. Beyond its analytical application, the framework offers a practical means of informing future AI development and adoption. It gives toolmakers a vocabulary for embedding stakeholder values in development decisions, and architects a means of recognising embedded biases before adoption, so that increasing automation extends rather than erodes the disciplinary and cultural values of architecture as a whole.

title: DIGITAL LABOUR AND EPISTEMIC ERASURE: A SEMIOTIC ANALYSIS OF INDIGENOUS KNOWLEDGE AND AI INFRASTRUCTURES IN HUMANS IN THE LOOP
container-title: Interdisciplinary Perspectives of Education
f3d3fff8613295115b19afeda98d7e4193beb31e.abstract: This paper explores how artificial intelligence (AI) and digital labour affect marginalised identities, using the 2025 Netflix film Humans in the Loop (directed by Aranya Sahay). Research follows the female protagonist of the film, named Nehma, an Indigenous (Adivasi) woman who works as a data labeller. Her deep, traditional knowledge about nature is ignored because of the way AI categorisation systems use a rigid, one-size-fits-all sorting method and act as epistemic hierarchies that erase Indigenous ways of living and thinking. Using a social semiotic approach, the research identifies a disconnection between local ecological knowledge and the rigid binary logic of machine-learning infrastructures. The article argues that digital frameworks mirror power dynamics inside educational institutions, where underrepresented students often have their cultural identity and cultural expressions erased or misrepresented. By analysing the lived experiences of marginalised communities, the study critiques techno-solutionist solutions and proposes solutions grounded in epistemic justice, cultural agency and equity and recommends that equitable AI systems require moving away from extractive labour practices to recognise the intellectual and cultural contributions of the Global South.

title: FROM DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION TO AI-ENABLED EDUCATION: A CRITICAL REVIEW OF EMERGING TRENDS, OPPORTUNITIES, AND CHALLENGES
container-title: Interdisciplinary Perspectives of Education
a30e8b5e4e056b3879ef048a09f681d3adc86be6.abstract: The higher education sector has seen the emergence of several technological advancements over the past two decades. These include learning management systems, massive open online courses, and the latest on the market: Generative Artificial Intelligence (AI). This paper aims to make a critical review of the shift from Digital Transformation to AI-driven education as a whole. The paper particularly emphasizes the shift of the digital transformation from being an administrative phenomenon to being more of a central feature in education. The paper summarises the literature on the concepts of digital transformation, the implementation of generative AI, and adaptive learning and AI ethics in the teaching and learning process, based on peer-reviewed papers that were mainly published in Scopus and Web of Science from 2019 to 2026. There are three themes that are repeated in the literature. First, AI in education is a further step towards digital transformation in which capacity building processes are substituted with independent decision making. Second, personalisation, accessibility and efficiency are opportunities, not equally accessible or equally taken up, nor equally realised; and these opportunities go first to the best resourced institutions.

title: FROM FINANCIAL LITERACY TO AI LITERACY: PREPARING COMMERCE STUDENTS FOR ALGORITHM-DRIVEN FINANCIAL DECISION-MAKING
container-title: Interdisciplinary Perspectives of Education
d04ff6220a1856d2870fe7a9d4e5c017fc060084.abstract: Artificial intelligence is becoming increasingly visible in everyday financial activities. Students and consumers now encounter automated financial recommendations, digital investment platforms, personalised financial information and AI-based tools when making or evaluating financial choices. This changing environment raises an important question for Commerce education: is conventional financial literacy sufficient when financial information is increasingly mediated by algorithms? The present study examines financial literacy, AI literacy and awareness of ethical issues associated with AI-supported financial applications among Commerce students, and investigates their relationship with algorithmic financial decision quality. The study follows a descriptive and analytical research design and considers 250 student observations. Data were examined using descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation and multiple linear regression. Four major constructs were considered in the analysis: financial literacy, AI literacy, ethical awareness and algorithmic financial decision quality. The findings show that financial literacy recorded the highest mean score (M = 3.56), while AI literacy recorded a comparatively lower mean score (M = 3.33). AI literacy demonstrated the strongest correlation with algorithmic financial decision quality (r = .705, p ≤ .01), followed by financial literacy (r = .623, p ≤ .01) and ethical awareness (r = .605, p ≤ .01). The regression model explained 67.2% of the variation in algorithmic financial decision quality. AI literacy emerged as the strongest predictor (β = .443), followed by financial literacy (β = .376) and ethical awareness (β = .199), with all three predictors statistically significant at p ≤ .001. The findings suggest that financial knowledge remains essential, but it needs to be complemented by the ability to understand, question and evaluate AI-generated financial information. Commerce education therefore needs to move towards an integrated approach in which financial literacy, AI competence and ethical awareness support independent and responsible financial judgement.

title: QUALITY, EQUITY, AND AUTONOMY IN INDIAN HIGHER EDUCATION AFTER NEP 2020: A CRITICAL ASSESSMENT
container-title: Interdisciplinary Perspectives of Education
4e0d40f3ff2f376c2bb7231bc606708e77e61ca7.abstract: The National Education Policy of 2020 is often called the biggest shake-up of Indian higher education since 1986. It asks for a lot: multidisciplinary campuses in place of narrow single-subject colleges, credit-based movement between programmes, far more freedom for institutions to run themselves, and, at the same time, a real widening of access for groups who have historically been left out. This paper looks closely at three strands of that agenda - quality, equity, and institutional autonomy - using government reports, statutory documents, and the wider research literature as evidence. The argument is straightforward. NEP 2020's vision hangs together well on paper. Putting it into practice is another matter, given how unevenly resources and administrative capacity are spread across Indian states, and given inequalities that were there long before this policy existed. There is also a basic tension running through the reform: it wants institutions to be freer, yet the government still has to pay for most of what happens in this sector and still has to watch over it. What decides whether NEP 2020 succeeds, this paper suggests, will not be the elegance of the document itself but whether money, coordination between the Centre and the States, and careful, ground-level implementation actually follow.

title: THE ROLE OF AI-POWERED DUOLINGO AND ELSA SPEAK APPS IN REDUCING SPEAKING ANXIETY AMONG ENGLISH LEARNERS IN PRIVATE UNIVERSITIES OF DHAKA, BANGLADESH
container-title: Interdisciplinary Perspectives of Education
b4447b00af53cabbd7382ac95aa5cf3980f3e6c5.abstract: This study has explored the influence of speaking anxiety as a major obstacle for English as foreign language learners (EFL) in their non-native environment like in the private universities in Dhaka, Bangladesh. With the up rise of Artificial Intelligence, English language learning applications have incorporated AI-based features to enhance the learning experience. This finding examined how AI-supported speaking apps, in this instance, Duolingo and ELSA Speak, reduce speaking anxiety and increase learners' confidence, fluency and speaking skills through AI-driven personalized feedback, gamified interaction and adaptive learning. This research used mixed-method approach, which included qualitative and quantitative methods to provide comprehensive insights and understanding. The results of the study pointed to the effectiveness of AI-based language learning apps in creating a supportive language-learning atmosphere, enhancing the learning process and reducing stress levels when practicing oral communication. The results of this study could contribute to the understanding of how AI-based app-based learning can be incorporated in the university curriculum and evidence-based recommendations for teachers, educational technology designers and policy makers.

title: From Frankenstein to Gulliver urbanism: Reframing AI and scale in urban theory
container-title: Urban Studies
5c314f44fcff78a684da7faa849271a26877753c.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly embedded in urban governance, infrastructure and design, yet urban theory still lacks a clear language for analysing the scale asymmetries through which these systems operate. This article develops Gulliver Urbanism as a conceptual framework for understanding how AI reshapes urban power when it processes information, acts, and coordinates across cognitive, temporal and spatial horizons that exceed ordinary human capacities and institutional rhythms. Moving beyond Frankenstein Urbanism’s emphasis on rebellion and loss of control, we argue that the central problem of contemporary AI urbanism is scale asymmetry within co-constituted human and machine assemblages. The framework comprises six dimensions: cognitive scale, temporal scale, spatial scale, governance asymmetry, autonomy and agency and human response. It synthesises scholarship on AI urbanism, urban political economy, infrastructural urbanism, posthumanism, law and scale, supported by AI governance frameworks and vignettes on Hangzhou City Brain, robotaxis and generative design. The article conceptualises the urban as a constitutive condition of AI scale asymmetry, where algorithmic systems encounter infrastructure, land, mobility, public services, municipal authority, social difference and collective life. Across these domains, the key challenge is how to govern systems whose capacities outpace human oversight while remaining embedded in corporate, legal and political arrangements. We argue that effective responses require mixed-intelligence governance and temporal dignity: arrangements that subject algorithmic operations to democratic oversight, contestation and human-paced deliberation. Gulliver Urbanism explains how AI reconstitutes urban life by reorganising infrastructures, municipal authority, spatial relations, design imaginaries, public services and everyday citizenship.

title: Artificial Intelligence and Digital Innovation in Smart Tourism Destination Management: An Integrative Review and the AI-SDM Framework
container-title: Inkubis : Jurnal Ekonomi dan Bisnis
b9b2afe723164bea6e7be350837363abda6c2fe3.abstract: Background: Artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming tourism destinations through personalized services, conversational and generative interfaces, predictive analytics, and data-driven decision-making. Yet technology adoption alone does not explain how destinations convert AI-generated information into coordinated managerial action. Objective: This study addresses that organizational problem through a conceptual integrative review of research on AI-enabled tourism services, smart destination management, destination governance, visitor experience, organizational capabilities, workforce readiness, and responsible data practices. Methods: The synthesis identifies four interconnected application domains: AI-driven personalization, conversational and generative visitor interaction, predictive visitor-flow analytics, and data-driven destination governance. These domains are abstracted into the AI-Enabled Smart Destination Management (AI-SDM) framework, which connects AI-Enabled Service Capability, Smart Destination Governance Capability, and Visitor Experience Outcomes. Results: Visitor and operational intelligence functions as the principal conversion input, while visitor-generated behavioral and experiential feedback supports subsequent organizational learning and AI adaptation. Workforce AI Readiness and Responsible Data Governance are positioned as enabling conditions. The framework contributes to destination-management theory by shifting attention from AI adoption toward the organizational capability required to sense relevant visitor information, interpret and coordinate responses, and responsibly convert intelligence into destination action and visitor value. It complements broad smart-tourism and emerging cognitive-destination architectures by specifying the organizational intelligence-to-action mechanism that links AI-enabled interactions with destination governance and learning. Conclusion: The paper concludes with propositions and an empirical research agenda for measurement development and validation.

of Allergenicity and Toxicity
in Novel Plant-Based Peptides

2a004857507a7863943c7cfc6535a201d564ba4b.abstract: Abstract Peptides from plant sources have antihypertensive, antioxidative, and antimicrobial properties but also entail a risk of allergic and toxic reactions that cannot be detected in conventional wet-lab assays. This review examines deep learning techniques and protein language models for their prediction, from linear motifs screening to transformers (BERT, ESM). The best-performing tools achieve high sensitivity (pLM4Alg 96.2%, ToxinPred3 95.8%) but low specificity and positive predictive value (pLM4Alg 92.8% and 81.7%), meaning that most predictions are false positives. There are four major constraints on the generalization capabilities of these tools: scoring of native peptides while proteolytic processing yields post-translational modifications and neoantigens; training samples correspond to IgE binding, not clinical manifestations, and are biased toward well-characterized organisms; T-cell immunity, microbiome, and organ-specific toxicity are scarcely modeled; and regulatory agencies do not consider in silico predictions sufficient. AI currently serves best as a prioritization filter, not a replacement for biological assays.

88311ab5879695c66cef064bee8f1ffe9c71873e.abstract: Digital environments transform multi-agent task allocation in terms of computational load, utility optimization, and allocation of attention. Based on distributed systems theory and reinforcement learning, this study will combine empirical evidence in artificial intelligence, software engineering, and information systems studies to determine the impact of digital stimuli (prompt complexity, resource constraints, and algorithmic task routing) on agent cognition and neural-inspired valuation processes. The paper constructs a conceptual Multi-Agent Task Allocation Model (MATAM) based on bounded rationality and multi-agent reinforcement learning theories using secondary data synthesis. The effects of computational overload, the activation of reward circuitry, and dynamic personalization in multi-agent environments are summarized in three integrative tables of documented empirical evidence. The results indicate that online agent frameworks reinforce decentralized processing, reward optimization, and dynamically restructure preference formation. The paper enriches software engineering theory because it incorporates computational and cognitive-inspired processes in adaptive multi-agent systems.

dc7897d2e5e5a766111eedcd730f86d3b1ed8c3a.abstract: A technology can appear less connected to the economy when its definition expands to include more connected industries. We separate constituent connectivity from exposure crossing the group's boundary and show how internalizing links can reverse rankings. Using 2017 U.S. input–output accounts, we compare artificial intelligence (AI) with matched industry groups. Narrow and broad AI rank above the 96th percentile of internal shares among similarly sized groups, but fall to the 24th and 55th percentiles after also matching sector composition and connectivity. Sector composition accounts for most of the decline, distinguishing AI's industry mix from unusually strong connections among its members.

title: Effects of Cognitive Behavioral Interventions on Core Symptom Dimensions of Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder in Children and Adolescents: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
container-title: Brain Sciences
6a8f61df667a2aec7602c5e57ab62b23c88523ba.abstract: Background: Previous research on psychosocial interventions for children and adolescents with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) has primarily focused on overall symptom severity, with less attention to treatment effects across core symptom dimensions. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the effects of cognitive behavioral interventions on overall ADHD symptoms, inattention, and hyperactivity/impulsivity and explored the influence of intervention type, treatment duration, and weekly session frequency. Methods: PubMed, Web of Science Core Collection, Embase, and CENTRAL were searched from inception to 30 June 2026 for randomized controlled trials. Risk of bias was assessed using RoB 2. Effect sizes were calculated as Hedges’ g and pooled using random-effects models, with sensitivity and exploratory subgroup analyses conducted. The review was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261376097). Results: Ten randomized controlled trials involving 849 participants were included. Cognitive behavioral interventions significantly reduced overall ADHD symptoms (g = −0.389, 95% CI −0.773 to −0.005), inattention (g = −0.415, 95% CI −0.749 to −0.082), and hyperactivity/impulsivity (g = −0.366, 95% CI −0.658 to −0.075). Inattention showed the numerically largest pooled effect. Exploratory subgroup analyses showed numerical differences across intervention type, treatment duration, and weekly session frequency, but formal moderator tests found no statistically significant between-subgroup differences. Conclusions: These findings support the potential benefits of cognitive behavioral interventions for ADHD symptom management, with the most consistent results observed for inattention. Future randomized controlled trials should compare intervention components and treatment schedules while assessing actual treatment exposure, including home practice, to inform more targeted cognitive behavioral interventions.

title: AI as a Thinking Partner in Sustainability-Oriented Mathematical Modelling: An Exploratory Study of Pre-Service Teachers’ Comparative Reflection
container-title: Sustainability
f75256d02bd41dd0c7af7d038095c547beeaaf35.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) is mostly used in education to generate solutions, provide feedback or support instruction; approaches that use AI outputs as objects of comparison and reflection remain less explored. This small-scale exploratory qualitative case study examined AI-supported comparative reflection in sustainability-oriented mathematical modelling. Twelve pre-service mathematics teachers individually developed models for a task on water use in a school garden and then compared them with a model produced by ChatGPT (GPT-4o), reflecting on the comparison in writing. Modelling products, written comparisons and reflection forms were analysed using inductive content analysis. The comparison prompted participants to question assumptions, identify limitations in both models and consider alternative variables and representations; most described how they would revise their models. Their accounts contained indications of critical, creative and metacognitive reasoning. However, several participants treated the AI output as an answer key, some of their critiques echoed weaknesses that the AI had listed about itself, and none noticed a computational inconsistency deliberately retained in the output. As the design included no comparison condition or pre–post measure, the findings describe patterns of reasoning displayed during the activity, not improvements in thinking skills or modelling competence. Implications for teacher education are discussed.

title: Cryptocurrency Mining in European Electricity Systems: A Critical Review of Carbon Accounting, Operational Flexibility and Environmental Trade-Offs
container-title: Sustainability
56873f3426ef72f0b1e8b71c8cc424c79aff90cb.abstract: Cryptocurrency-energy assessments often conflate electricity use, emissions attribution and avoided system emissions. This targeted, non-exhaustive integrative review separates these quantities and evaluates mining-flexibility claims in European electricity systems. A six-criterion appraisal links principal studies to supported claims and transfer limits. A general electricity-accounting benchmark uses secondary data to compare 2024 production-mix and residual-mix direct CO2 factors for 24 national European Union domains. Their unweighted means are 214.38 and 415.18 g CO2/kWh; the median within-country ratio is 1.95. The two orderings have a Spearman correlation of 0.670 and disagree for 68 of 276 country pairs. The residual factor exceeds the production factor in all 24 countries in both 2024 and a matched 2025 comparison; consumption-weighted contrasts also remain positive. For a fixed hypothetical 1 MW Hungarian load operating throughout leap year 2024, the two accounting descriptors yield 1556.5 and 2798.9 tonnes of attributed direct CO2, a 79.82% accounting difference. These descriptive, non-causal results compare accounting descriptors, which are not freely interchangeable facility reporting options. Conditional procurement scenarios and an explicitly assumed four-hour example distinguish reported emissions, electricity volume and operating schedules. Technical evidence supports curtailment and ancillary-service participation in specified settings, but price responsiveness alone does not establish lower emissions. The applied framework links European disclosure to claim-specific counterfactuals and specifies requirements for joint assessment of heat, methane, water, hardware and health impacts.

title: Synergistic antibacterial effect and improved pharmacokinetics of florfenicol in combination with sulfamonomethoxine sodium
container-title: Journal of Antimicrobial Chemotherapy
be02807430b9e0688ea2543db83e5bf8db57c254.abstract: Abstract Objective Florfenicol (FFC) and sulfamonomethoxine sodium (SMM-Na) are both broad-spectrum antibiotics for animals. FFC inhibits bacterial protein synthesis, whereas SMM-Na inhibits the bacterial folate pathway, suggesting a potential for synergy. However, the pharmacodynamic and pharmacokinetic interactions of their combination remain uncharacterized. This study evaluated the in vitro and in vivo interactions between FFC and SMM-Na. Methods The in vitro interaction was assessed against several bacterial strains using the checkerboard method to determine the fractional inhibitory concentration index (FICI). The physicochemical stability of the combination was tested. An in situ recirculating intestinal perfusion model in rats was used to assess absorption parameters. Pharmacokinetic studies in rats compared the combination therapy to monotherapies. The therapeutic efficacy was evaluated in a mouse model of Staphylococcus aureus pulmonary infection, with the combination administered at half the individual monotherapy doses. Results The FFC/SMM-Na combination demonstrated synergistic effects (FICI = 0.375) in vitro and remained stable for 7 h. Intestinal perfusion showed the combination significantly increased the absorption rate constants (Ka) and effective permeability coefficients (Peff) for both drugs. Pharmacokinetic analysis revealed improved relative bioavailability for both FFC (113.98%) and SMM-Na (113.29%), with distinct pharmacokinetic profiles: FFC showed higher Cmax and shorter Tmax, while SMM-Na exhibited lower Cmax and longer Tmax. In the infection model, the half-dose combination achieved a significant reduction in bacterial load and ameliorated lung pathology. Conclusion The FFC/SMM-Na combination exhibits synergistic antibacterial activity in vitro, enhances mutual intestinal absorption, improves the pharmacokinetic profiles of both drugs, and achieves comparable in vivo efficacy at reduced doses through a dose-sparing effect. These findings provide a pharmacological basis for the clinical exploration of this combination therapy against bacterial infections.

title: Physiological and Transcriptomic Responses of Armillaria gallica to Selenium: Bioaccumulation, Biotransformation, and Growth Promotion
container-title: Journal of Applied Microbiology
46e34f34d268246d0ac89ad5d5709c10d9a4fcbb.abstract: Abstract Aims Armillaria gallica is a medicinal fungus and key symbiont for Gastrodia elata cultivation. This study aimed to investigate the dose-dependent effects of exogenous selenium (Se) on mycelial growth, Se accumulation and biotransformation, antioxidant regulation, and transcriptional responses in A. gallica. Methods and Results Dose–response experiments showed that 20 mg L−1 Na2SeO3 optimally promoted mycelial biomass (47% increase) and Se accumulation (837.53 mg kg−1), with 99.71% of Se in organic forms, predominantly associated with polysaccharides and proteins. Physiological assays revealed enhanced SOD, POD, CAT, and GPx activities and reduced MDA content under Se treatment. Transcriptomic profiling identified extensive gene remodeling in ion transport, redox metabolism, carbohydrate metabolism, glutathione metabolism, and MAPK signaling pathways, with qRT-PCR validating key DEG expression patterns. Conclusions Appropriate Se concentration promotes A. gallica growth and enhances antioxidant capacity through coordinated transcriptional and metabolic regulation. The strong Se accumulation and biotransformation capacity position A. gallica as a promising candidate for Se biofortification and for developing Se-enriched Gastrodia elata via the Armillaria–Gastrodia symbiotic system.

title: Occupational Types, Working Hours, and Cognitive Trajectories
container-title: Work, Aging and Retirement
ffb9730bc26d334ee9d4a045cd264d4e1fd4ff60.abstract: Abstract The relationship between work and cognitive function in later years has gained attention recently. However, information on occupational types, working hours, and cognitive function based on longitudinal cohort studies from developing countries remains limited. This study utilizes data from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study and employs group-based trajectory modeling to depict the heterogeneous changes in cognitive function over time among middle-aged and older adults and specifically examines the associations between occupational types (agricultural work, non-agricultural employment, non-agricultural self-employed or family business), working hours, and cognitive trajectories. Our findings indicate that agricultural work is associated with poorer cognitive trajectories compared to non-agricultural employment and non-agricultural self-employed or family business. Compared to individuals working 40 hours or less per week, those working 41–55 hours had a higher likelihood of experiencing a “rapid decline” cognitive trajectory. Furthermore, working over 55 hours per week was associated with an increased likelihood of belonging to both the “rapid decline” and “persistently moderate” trajectory groups. We did not observe a significant multiplicative interaction between occupational types and working hours on the cognitive trajectories. These results enhance our understanding of the relationship between work-related factors and cognitive function, providing a scientific basis for developing targeted intervention measures in the context of developing countries.

title: Generative Artificial Intelligence in Architectural Research: Limits of Regulation
container-title: Vestnik Tomskogo gosudarstvennogo arkhitekturno-stroitel'nogo universiteta. JOURNAL of Construction and Architecture
c0d7722a36617cb6ecbf496cb086f01ec3037777.abstract: Purpose : The aim is to outline the problem area, define the boundaries of what is subject to regulation, distinguish ineffective regulatory strategies from promising ones, and identify likely trajectories as they apply to master’s and doctoral dissertations, primarily in architectural disciplines. Design/methodology/approach: A comparative analysis of Russian and international regulatory, publishing, and academic documents from 2023–2026 and empirical studies on detectors and the authenticity of generated text, experience in drafting regulations for a dissertation council in architectural disciplines. Research findings: Five areas of uncertainty are identified: authorship and responsibility, text as evidence of competence, reliability and plausibility, detectability and the flip side of metrics, and confidentiality and symmetry of expert evaluation. Three boundaries of regulation are defined, the ineffectiveness of a complete ban, total control, detectors as evidence, percentage quotas, regulation of specific products, and non-interference is demonstrated, transferable solutions from local legislation are described, i.e., functional classification, disclosure instead of prohibition, presumption of good faith and procedural safeguards, symmetry of requirements, industry standards, and technological neutrality. Practical implications : Transferable solutions of a local regulation include a function-based classification of use, disclosure instead of prohibition, a presumption of good faith with procedural guarantees, symmetrical requirements for candidates and reviewers, discipline-specific rules for images and reconstructions, and technological neutrality. Originality/value: The problem is shown to be epistemic and institutional rather than technological. The centre of gravity of assessment shifts from the manuscript to the oral defense of a thesis and verifiable artefacts. The restoration-theory principle of distinguishability of original and supplemented material is applied to the digital artefacts of a dissertation.

fdc0b4b8939db7db25cfc6732518bc99b63751d8.abstract: This study examines the evolution and competitive positioning of the United Kingdom's AI startup ecosystem amid the rise of generative AI. Using a qualitative desk-research design based on secondary investment data, policy documents, and academic literature from 2015-2026, the study analyzes how the UK has transitioned from a research-driven niche to a globally recognized hub, leveraging world-class universities, dense financial and healthcare markets, and a principle-based regulatory framework. Growth has been propelled by a robust spinout cycle from anchor institutions and accessible early-stage capital. Despite these strengths, structural constraints threaten long-term scale, including a persistent late-stage funding gap, infrastructure bottlenecks in compute access and energy costs, and intensifying global competition for talent. The study finds the UK is best positioned to capture value in autonomous enterprise agents, AI for scientific discovery, and multimodal systems. Sustaining global competitiveness will require expanding domestic growth capital, ensuring reliable compute access, and maintaining regulatory clarity without stifling agility.

title: Shadow AI usage and ethical AI adoption: the moderating role of chief AI officer governance
container-title: International Journal of Organizational Analysis
31379c9b469f5547f923a3520026bf47ae6913ec.abstract: Purpose The rapid emergence of Shadow artificial intelligence (AI), the informal and unauthorised use of AI tools by employees, poses a growing challenge for global organisations. It creates cybersecurity threats, compliance risks, data breaches and ethical violations such as bias and opacity, ultimately undermining ethical AI adoption and stakeholder trust. Existing research often portrays the Chief AI Officer (CAIO) as a static role, focusing on compliance enforcement or policy integration while overlooking its potential to balance innovation and governance. This study aims to examine how the CAIO as a moderator influences the relationship between Shadow AI Usage and Ethical AI Adoption. Design/methodology/approach A deductive, theory-driven, cross-sectional research design was adopted, drawing on 665 AI practitioners and organisational decision-makers recruited through professional networks across multiple countries. Partial least squares structural equation modelling was employed to test the hypothesised moderating relationship. Findings Higher Shadow AI Usage was negatively associated with Ethical AI Adoption, whereas the positive Shadow AI Usage × CAIO interaction indicates that stronger CAIO governance attenuates this negative relationship. Originality/value This study contributes to AI governance research by conceptualising CAIO governance as an organisational boundary condition that attenuates the negative association between Shadow AI Usage and Ethical AI Adoption.

title: Semaglutide and Cardiovascular Death: a Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis Cardioprotective Efficacy of Semaglutide
container-title: Critical Pathways in Cardiology: A Journal of Evidence-Based Medicine
ff09fc36fda2167244d7ca1bd4cff16378e89976.abstract: Background: Cardiovascular death (CVD) remains a leading cause of global mortality. Although semaglutide reduces major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), the consistency and exact magnitude of its standalone effect on CVD across various patient phenotypes require comprehensive evaluation. This meta-analysis systematically evaluated the clinical efficacy of semaglutide on CVD risk across randomized controlled trials (RCTs). Methods: PubMed, Embase, and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched up to July 2026 to identify RCTs comparing semaglutide with placebo in adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), overweight or obesity, heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) or chronic kidney disease, reporting CVD as a primary, secondary or exploratory outcome. Pooled hazard ratio (HR) and 95% confidence intervals (CI) were calculated using a random-effects restricted maximum likelihood (REML) model. Publication bias and study robustness were assessed via Egger’s test, Begg's test, and trim-and-fill analysis. Results: Seven high-quality RCTs comprising 38412 patients were included. Semaglutide significantly reduced the risk of CVD by 17% compared with placebo (pooled HR = 0.83, 95% CI: 0.72–0.95; P = 0.01). Inter-study heterogeneity was low-to-moderate (I 2 = 27.44%, P = 0.18). Subgroup analyses confirmed uniform benefits across different clinical phenotypes (T2DM; overweight or obesity without diabetes; and obesity-related HFpEF, with or without T2DM; P = 0.63) and administration routes (oral versus subcutaneous; P = 0.74). Meta-regression identified trial duration as a key moderator (R 2 = 85.27%, P = 0.089), whereas sex, age, BMI, HbA1c and concomitant SGLT2i therapy did not modify the treatment effect. Publication bias tests were non-significant, and trim-and-fill simulations confirmed the stability of the primary pooled estimate. Conclusion: Semaglutide delivers a robust and consistent 17% reduction in CVD across diverse cardiometabolic populations, including patients with T2DM, overweight or obesity without diabetes, and obesity-related HFpEF. These findings strongly support its role as a foundational cardioprotective intervention, independent of baseline glycemic status or the administration route.

title: When principles become policy: the institutional translation of responsible AI in national AI ​strategies
container-title: AI and Ethics
3806088112704c0bd67a1b4a2a21cd6770fe2e14.abstract: Abstract This study examines how Responsible AI (RAI) principles are translated as they move from ethical discourse into governance, standards, and national policy contexts. Drawing on comparative analysis of influential AI ethics guidelines, policy syntheses, and technical glossaries, the research traces how widely cited principles are reformulated across domains, using transparency and fairness as cases of how institutional translation operates in practice. It shows that while these principles originate as broad normative commitments, they become progressively institutionalized as policy categories, procedural requirements, and measurable technical properties. The comparison shows that the underlying mechanism generalizes across principles, while the resulting institutional forms remain principle-specific. Focusing on national AI strategies as a key site of institutionalization, the study analyzes how RAI principles are embedded within state agendas, regulatory approaches, and oversight mechanisms. This analysis reveals variation in how principles are prioritized and operationalized, reflecting differences in governance priorities, administrative capacity, and political context. The findings highlight that principles most amenable to standardization and measurement tend to dominate policy implementation, while more expansive ethical concepts are less visible. By mapping these shifts across institutional settings, the paper contributes to a deeper understanding of how AI ethics is reconfigured in practice and offers insights for policymakers seeking to balance technical feasibility with normative ambition in the governance of AI.

title: Programmer expertise classification using cognitive load and transfer learning
container-title: Discover Computing
f504c1239bb13fa73a7b7735bc8c27cc18f7e8e5.abstract: Abstract Context Evaluating a programmer’s performance by considering both technical and cognitive skills is indispensable in many software development tasks. Problem Technical skills are relatively easy to assess, whereas non-technical skills, such as long-term memory, critical thinking, and emotional intelligence, are often overlooked while measuring the performance of a programmer. Aim The primary objective of this work is to propose a reliable framework for classifying programmers into five framework-derived proficiency ranks. Methods Participants are given an assignment with both technical and non-technical questions. A cognitive load index that combines technical and non-technical skills is used to analyze performance and stratify it into five ranks. The proposed framework was evaluated using CatBoost and TabNet classifiers in a transfer-learning setup. It used the source dataset (Another researcher’s dataset) for pre-training and the proposed programmer dataset for fine-tuning. Extensive experiments, including confusion matrix analysis, 5-fold cross-validation, sensitivity analysis, and ablation studies, confirm the framework’s effectiveness and robustness. Results The fine-tuned CatBoost model outperformed the TabNet model, achieving an impressive 87% accuracy, a significant improvement over the pre-trained model’s 31%. The findings demonstrate that combining technical skills with non-technical aspects greatly enhances the accuracy of classifying programmer expertise. This offers a dependable method for assessing programmers in software engineering education. The study develops a robust framework for evaluating programming performance that incorporates both technical and non-technical skills, and it can be adapted for other cognitive and skill-based evaluations across different fields.

title: Mechanism-guided generative chemistry yields distinct agonist-like and antagonist-like ligand populations for the serotonin 5-HT2A receptor
container-title: Scientific Reports
b27412a1d4e63e0b34f08a564c2e2089dec24412.abstract: Abstract Designing serotonin 5-HT2A receptor ligands with a specified functional direction is difficult because binding affinity, assay-derived mechanism labels, molecular properties and receptor conformation are only partially coupled. We developed a mechanism-guided generative chemistry workflow integrating curated ChEMBL data, scaffold-aware supervised learning, a recurrent SMILES prior, reinforcement learning, medicinal-chemistry prioritization, receptor-context docking, MM-GBSA rescoring and property-adjusted contact analysis. The dataset comprised 8,949 measurements and 6,252 compounds. A five-seed binding Ki ensemble achieved scaffold-test mean absolute error of 0.588 pChEMBL and R² of 0.607; non-generalizing functional EC50 models were excluded from the reward. Separate campaigns generated 500 valid unique agonist-like and 500 antagonist-like molecules. Antagonist-like candidates showed higher predicted affinity and mechanism-label confidence, whereas agonist-like candidates showed higher QED, greater internal diversity and lower training-set similarity. Matched frozen-prior sampling showed only modest policy-level shifts from the already HTR2A-focused prior, whereas the reward-retained candidate populations were strongly enriched for the campaign objectives. Native-ligand redocking reproduced four deposited poses with heavy-atom RMSD values of 0.357–1.082 Å. Under fully contact-neutral pose selection and the prespecified repeated-measures model, S242, L229 and L362 showed FDR-supported campaign-by-receptor-context interactions; S242 and L229 retained the directions observed with the original selector, whereas L362 emerged in the contact-neutral analysis. The study identifies distinct model-defined chemical regimes and links campaign-level property drift to receptor-contact topology; generated compounds remain computational hypotheses requiring experimental validation.

title: Prediction of Grape Disease using Deep Learning based on MobileNetV2 and Explainable AI with Grad-CAM for Disease Management
container-title: International Journal of Advanced Research in Science Communication and Technology
6480a24874eeda23428f60c9d415447a4194461c.abstract: The grapes production can be affected by diseases that cause changes to the look and state of the leaves and may reduce the quality of the crop if the disease are not detected in time. Even though visual diagnosis is of some help, it depends on the operator's experience and can become difficult when different diseases show similar symptoms. The study presents an image-based approach for predicting and Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping (Grad-CAM) for providing a visual explanation. The System can detect four kinds of disease: Black Measles, Black Rot, Healthy, and Isariopsis Leaf Spot. The model produces a distribution of class probabilities and Grad-CAM is used to highlight the parts of the image that are related to the predicted class. A general module based on knowledge then provides information regarding the symptoms, advice on how to manage the disease, and preventive measures for the disease which has been predicted. Having been tested on 903 images, the system achieved 886 correct predictions and 17 incorrect ones, giving an accuracy of 98.12%, a weighted precision of 98.13%,a weighted recall of 98.12%, and a weighted F1-score of 98.12%. The errors that were seen were mostly between Black Measles and Black Rot. The study therefore incorporates prediction, visual explanation, and disease-management information into one workflow, while at the same time recognizing the need for further validation with a wider variety of field images..

title: Development and psychometric validation of the barriers to AI integration in nursing education scale (BAI-NE): a multi-institutional study
container-title: Scientific Reports
3e14fcc3f2fe59189db4f1f708cb00755b4bc751.abstract: Abstract This multi-institutional study aimed to develop and psychometrically validate the Barriers to AI Integration in Nursing Education Scale (BAI-NE). A methodological study with a mixed-methods exploratory design was conducted in two phases: scale development and content validation, followed by psychometric evaluation. The 15-item BAI-NE was developed based on the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology (UTAUT) and an extensive literature review. Content validity was assessed by a panel of ten experts. A convenience sample of 470 nurse educators from seven faculties of nursing participated in the study. The sample was randomly divided for Exploratory Factor Analysis (EFA; n = 235) and Confirmatory Factor Analysis (CFA; n = 235). EFA identified a four-factor structure explaining 42.7% of the total variance, comprising Technical and Infrastructure Barriers, Knowledge and Training Barriers, Ethical and Regulatory Barriers, and Attitudinal and Organizational Barriers. EFA factor loadings ranged from 0.566 to 0.738. CFA provided preliminary support for the proposed model, with good fit indices (χ²/df = 0.90, RMSEA = 0.00, CFI = 1.000, TLI = 1.015, SRMR = 0.043, GFI = 0.961); because χ² was lower than df and CFI and RMSEA were at their bounds, these values should be interpreted cautiously and replicated in independent samples. Standardized CFA loadings ranged from 0.54 to 0.82. Internal consistency was satisfactory, with Cronbach’s alpha values ranging from 0.713 to 0.754 and McDonald’s omega values ranging from 0.715 to 0.754. Test–retest reliability over a two-week interval was excellent for all subscales (ICC = 0.85–0.92). Convergent validity was modest, with composite reliability values exceeding 0.70, while AVE values ranged from 0.426 to 0.451. Discriminant validity was supported using the Fornell-Larcker criterion and HTMT values < 0.85. Among the four subscales, Knowledge and Training Barriers received the highest mean score (M = 14.0, SD = 2.51), followed by Attitudinal and Organizational Barriers (M = 13.1, SD = 2.63), Technical and Infrastructure Barriers (M = 12.8, SD = 2.68), and Ethical and Regulatory Barriers (M = 9.1, SD = 2.10). The BAI-NE demonstrated preliminary evidence of satisfactory validity and reliability and provides a practical instrument for identifying barriers to AI integration in nursing education, informing faculty development initiatives, institutional planning, and future research. The BAI-NE is intended to be scored and interpreted at the subscale level only.

title: Green Software Tracker for Web Applications Using AI
container-title: International Journal of Advanced Research in Science Communication and Technology
e9e7dd3be86b4bfc4aaf051870fd54bd60832110.abstract: Web applications consume computing resources such as CPU, memory, and network bandwidth during request processing. High resource consumption can increase energy usage and contribute to carbon emissions. This research proposes a Green Software Tracker for Web Applications Using AI to monitor resource utilization and estimate the environmental impact of web applications. The proposed system uses Python and the psutil library to collect process-level CPU and memory data at defined intervals. It aims to estimate energy consumption using a documented estimation method and calculate associated carbon emissions using an appropriate electricity emission factor. A dashboard is planned to display resource usage, estimated emissions, a Green Score, and recommendations for improving software efficiency. The current recommendation approach is rule-based. Further implementation and experimental evaluation are required to validate the estimation method and assess the system's performance

title: Evaluating the Validity of AI-Generated Writing Feedback for Students With Learning Disabilities
container-title: Journal of Special Education Technology
f14d7d18bb361d0034c674f8dc89d014df1bca80.abstract: Students with learning disabilities need clear, direct, and useful writing feedback. However, teachers often find it hard to provide this consistently because of time and workload pressures. New developments in generative artificial intelligence (AI) might help improve both the frequency and quality of feedback for students. Still, we know very little about whether AI-generated comments are valid or useful for struggling writers. This qualitative study looked at teachers' views on writing feedback from the AI-SCORE automated writing evaluation tool. Nine upper elementary and middle school teachers took part in two focus groups. They reviewed AI-generated feedback on student informational writing. They also discussed its clarity, teaching value, and suitability for students with disabilities. Thematic analysis revealed several areas for improving AI-generated feedback. Teachers want more guidance on specific revisions, language that suits students’ development, a consistent tone, and alignment with writing goals. They shared cautious optimism, noting that AI feedback could enhance teaching capacity and provide more practice opportunities for students, if it meets their needs. The findings stress the importance of teacher involvement, the potential benefits of AI for writing instruction, and key factors for creating AI tools that effectively support students with learning disabilities.
