title: The Effect of AI Absorptive Capacity of Organizations on Workers’ Perceptions About Smart Work Environment Perception Towards Digital Innovation Behavior.
container-title: WSEAS Transactions on Information Science and Applications
743b00c8552a137b4c5e81a5f74226040cc68957.abstract: This study investigates the effect of organizational artificial intelligence (AI) absorptive capacity on employees’ perceptions of the smart work environment and how these perceptions influence their digital innovative behavior in the telecommunications industry, with Digital Transformational Leadership as a moderating variable. In this study, two important theoretical perspectives were utilized: Absorptive Capacity Theory, which highlights how organizations acquire, assimilate, and apply their knowledge related to AI, and Socio-Technical Systems Theory, which addresses the connection between technology and the social aspect of the working environment. A quantitative research design was used through partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM). The data were gathered from 279 respondents working in the telecommunication industry in Jordan. These respondents worked for internet service providers, network operators, and mobile network operators. The findings show that organizational AI absorptive capacity has a strong positive effect on Smart Work Environment Perception (β = 0.742), which in turn enhances Digital Innovative Behavior (β = 0.681). Smart Work Environment Perception partially mediates the relationship between AI absorptive capacity and Digital Innovative Behavior (indirect effect β = 0.506), while Digital Transformational Leadership positively moderates the relationship between AI absorptive capacity and the smart work environment (β = 0.276) and between the smart work environment and Digital Innovative Behavior (β = 0.241). The current research adds value to the literature surrounding AI adoption within organizations by examining how technical capabilities and organizational leadership help foster Digital Innovative Behavior in the telecommunications industry.

title: HUBUNGAN PEMANFAATAN KECERDASAN BUATAN (AI) SEBAGAI SUMBER BELAJAR DENGAN KEMANDIRIAN BELAJAR SISWA PAI DI SMP
container-title: EDUCATOR : Jurnal Inovasi Tenaga Pendidik dan Kependidikan
a72b4739b1bea39fca6a1a6f81145bf37f0c034b.abstract: ABSTRACT The use of generative artificial intelligence in education creates opportunities for students to access information and understand learning materials more flexibly. However, such accessibility does not necessarily correspond to students’ ability to manage their own learning independently, particularly in Islamic Religious Education (PAI) at the junior secondary school level. This study aims to examine the relationship between the use of ChatGPT as a learning resource and students’ learning independence at SMPN 5 Ambarawa. A quantitative approach with a correlational design was employed, involving 64 students selected through purposive sampling. Data were collected using a four-point Likert-scale questionnaire measuring ChatGPT utilization and learning independence. The data were analyzed using IBM SPSS Statistics version 27 through descriptive statistics, instrument validity and reliability testing, and Spearman’s rho correlation analysis. The results revealed a positive and statistically significant relationship between ChatGPT utilization and students’ learning independence, with a correlation coefficient of 0.598 and a significance value of p < 0.001. These findings indicate that better utilization of ChatGPT tends to be associated with higher levels of learning independence. Nevertheless, this relationship does not establish a causal effect. The use of ChatGPT in Islamic Religious Education should therefore be accompanied by teacher guidance, information verification, and active student engagement to ensure that the technology is used critically and responsibly. ABSTRAK Pemanfaatan kecerdasan buatan generatif dalam pembelajaran membuka peluang bagi siswa untuk memperoleh informasi dan memahami materi secara lebih fleksibel. Namun, kemudahan akses tersebut belum tentu sejalan dengan kemampuan siswa mengelola proses belajarnya secara mandiri, khususnya dalam mata pelajaran Pendidikan Agama Islam (PAI) di jenjang sekolah menengah pertama. Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis hubungan antara pemanfaatan ChatGPT sebagai sumber belajar dan kemandirian belajar siswa di SMPN 5 Ambarawa. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif dengan desain korelasional yang melibatkan 64 siswa melalui teknik purposive sampling. Data dikumpulkan menggunakan angket skala Likert empat pilihan yang mengukur pemanfaatan ChatGPT dan kemandirian belajar. Data dianalisis menggunakan IBM SPSS Statistics versi 27 melalui statistik deskriptif, pengujian validitas dan reliabilitas instrumen, serta korelasi Spearman’s rho. Hasil analisis menunjukkan hubungan positif dan signifikan antara pemanfaatan ChatGPT dan kemandirian belajar siswa, dengan koefisien korelasi sebesar 0,598 dan nilai signifikansi p < 0,001. Temuan ini menunjukkan bahwa pemanfaatan ChatGPT yang lebih baik cenderung berkaitan dengan kemandirian belajar yang lebih tinggi. Meskipun demikian, hubungan tersebut tidak membuktikan sebab-akibat. Penggunaan ChatGPT dalam pembelajaran PAI perlu disertai bimbingan guru, verifikasi informasi, dan keterlibatan aktif siswa agar teknologi dimanfaatkan secara kritis dan bertanggung jawab.

title: Beyond accuracy and time saved: implementation outcomes for generative AI in hospital administrative and clinical-administrative workflows—a mini review
container-title: Frontiers in Medicine
08dce28882ef374649f8c6426650ed7cc9e2048e.abstract: Although hospitals are introducing generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) into documentation, messaging, and administrative workflows, model accuracy and time saved do not establish safe or sustainable implementation. This Mini Review examines which implementation and downstream outcomes should inform decisions to pilot, scale up, sustain, modify, or discontinue these workflows. A PubMed-led structured narrative search through 25 August 2026, with an update on 27 August, informed a purposive core of 17 empirical studies: seven direct administrative studies and 10 clinical-administrative studies. Supporting reviews and established implementation frameworks informed the interpretation of the findings. Perceived workload, logged efficiency, adoption, safety, and downstream outcomes did not improve consistently together. Favourable average quality could coexist with consequential errors and substantial verification work. Within this selected core, cost, penetration, and sustainability were measured less often than early fit, use, and feasibility. No study was coded as providing an operationalised equity assessment. We present a literature-informed outcome-to-decision crosswalk that links these findings to clinical workflow governance. This distinguishes non-compensable stop rules from minimum progression criteria and comparative value targets, with explicit ownership, denominators and reassessment. Illustrative stop rules address serious uncorrected errors, unauthorised data disclosure and bypassed human review. The crosswalk is an unvalidated normative synthesis, not a universal stage model. Its value requires prospective testing against patient safety, workforce burden and service outcomes.

title: How patient and professional characteristics mediate between innovative work behavior and hospital performance: the moderating role of AI use
container-title: International Journal of Pharmaceutical and Healthcare Marketing
9761830e77f32d8204aaf31e513b1eae2a86a9a0.abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine how innovative work behavior (IWB) influences hospital performance (HP), with professional characteristics (ProC) and patient characteristics (PtC) as mediating factors. Furthermore, it examines whether the adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) moderates this relationship. Design/methodology/approach A structured questionnaire was used to collect data from 351 healthcare professionals in Pakistan. Partial least squares structural equation modeling was applied to test the hypotheses. Findings The results reveal that IWB has a significant, positive effect on HP, both directly and indirectly through ProC and PtC. These characteristics act as important underlying mechanisms through which IWB enhances performance outcomes. While AI adoption does not directly improve HP, it positively moderates the IWB–HP relationship, indicating that AI strengthens the performance outcomes of innovation-supportive environments. Originality/value This study integrates the resource-based view and job demands–resources into a nomological framework. It contributes to healthcare innovation research by showing that technological adoption alone is insufficient; employee innovative behavior and human-related characteristics are crucial drivers of HP.

title: Dissolve What Extracts: AI, Wellbeing, and the Composition of Economic Life (A Compositional Theory of the AI Wellbeing Dividend, with a Constructive Policy Triad)
container-title: Wellbeing Futures: Innovation, Policy and Research
ead5af38728ef070e5c4239426fc5709d2826de9.abstract: AI's most important wellbeing dividend may not come from producing more output, but from changing the composition of economic life. By reducing the administrative, cognitive, financial, and procedural burdens that absorb human capacity without building capability, AI can dissolve forms of extractive friction. But unless the resulting gains are protected from rent migration and redirected into formative infrastructure, extraction will not disappear; it will reappear in AI-native form. This paper develops a compositional theory of AI and wellbeing, distinguishing the philosophical hinge between extractive friction (burdens that drain capacity without building it) and formative friction (difficulty that develops judgment, skill, relationship, and responsibility). The wellbeing dividend is mapped across four BANI channels, with Brittleness treated explicitly as a hypothesis-generating channel rather than an established mechanism. The paper distinguishes theory from prescription. The prescription is a triadic policy mechanism: dissolution compresses extractive friction; anti-recapture prevents migrated rents from forming a new layer of extraction (taxation is its principal fiscal instance, alongside interoperability mandates, fiduciary duties, antitrust scrutiny, and public AI provision); and formation funding directs released capacity into relational and developmental infrastructure. The triad is operationalised through a five-test evaluative toolkit (Capability, Proportionality, Distribution, Migration, Formation) designed to assess whether any AI deployment or proposed policy actually advances compositional change rather than merely automating the existing equilibrium.

title: The Relationship Between Metacognitive Reading Strategy Awareness and Critical Reading Self-efficacy in Gifted Middle School Students
container-title: HAYEF: Journal of Education
5d0f75ace0c0dee623aa9d7b4688f6d4b682d04f.abstract: This study examined the relationship between metacognitive reading strategy awareness and critical reading self-efficacy among gifted middle school students and investigated the unique contributions of different dimensions of metacognitive reading strategies to critical reading self-efficacy. Examining this relationship in gifted learners is important for understanding how high cognitive potential relates to strategic reading awareness and to students' beliefs about their capability to perform critical reading tasks. The study was conducted with 218 gifted sixth- and seventh-grade students attending Science and Art Centers in Istanbul, Türkiye. Using a correlational survey design, data were collected through the Critical Reading Self-Efficacy Scale and the Metacognitive Awareness of Reading Strategies Inventory and analyzed using Pearson correlation, multiple linear regression, and independent-samples t tests. The Metacognitive Awareness of Reading Strategies Inventory total score showed a small, positive, but nonsignificant correlation with critical reading self-efficacy (r = .127, p = .060). The regression model was statistically significant yet explained only 4.0% of the variance, F(3214) = 2.953, p = .034. Among the dimensions, only global reading strategies made a statistically significant unique contribution to critical reading self-efficacy (β = 0.194, p = .004), whereas problem-solving and support strategies did not make significant unique contributions. Neither variable differed significantly by gender or grade level. The findings suggest that, among gifted students, critical reading self-efficacy is linked less to overall metacognitive awareness than to planning-and evaluation-oriented global strategies. This dimension-specific pattern underscores the value of dimension-based, planning- and evaluation-focused approaches in reading instruction for gifted learners and indicates that self-efficacy warrants study alongside further cognitive, motivational, and affective variables Cite this article as: İşlekeller Bozca, A., & Özcan, S. (2026). The relationship between metacognitive reading strategy awareness and critical reading self-efficacy in gifted middle school students. title: Identity, Knowledge, and Power: A Critical Discourse Analysis of Morality and Ethics in U.S. Teacher Education Textbooks
container-title: Journal of Teacher Education
3563cf64fb730b50fe864d59fd23059df9e2b55a.abstract: This study examines how morality and ethics are discursively constructed in 43 U.S. teacher education textbooks, focusing on the intertwined themes of identity, knowledge, and power. Drawing on Fairclough’s three-dimensional critical discourse analysis, the study analyzes how textbook discourses could shape ethical teacher subjectivity. Findings show that textbooks predominantly construct teachers as moral role models and ethicists-in-community. Ethical knowledge is legitimized through an integrated repertoire of professional codes, legal frameworks, moral dilemmas, and developmental theories. Power operates through normative professional standards and disciplinary practices of reflection that encourage self-regulation within institutional boundaries. While these discourses promote ethical professionalism, they largely privilege micro-ethical concerns and marginalize sociopolitical macro-ethics and systemic power relations. The study argues for textbooks that more deliberately function as social practices, cultivating critical moral agency and ethical resilience so that teachers are prepared not only to navigate existing systems but also to question and, when necessary, challenge them.

title: Radiographic manifestations of pneumatosis intestinalis and construction of an AI-assisted diagnostic system
container-title: APL Bioengineering
6792c84be7cb66eda42f89872f286c5a397871a0.abstract: Pneumatosis intestinalis (PI) has a wide range of etiologies, and the imaging differentiation between benign and ischemic PI is difficult, leading to a high risk of missed diagnosis. This study systematically summarizes the CT (Computed Tomography) imaging manifestations of PI and constructs an AI (Artificial Intelligence)-assisted diagnostic model that integrates multidimensional features. This study retrospectively collected CT and x-ray data from 612 patients with PI (398 benign and 214 ischemic cases) from three tertiary hospitals, and included an external validation set of 106 cases. Imaging analysis established a five-level PI-CT severity scoring system based on gas morphology, distribution, portal venous gas (PVG), intestinal wall enhancement, mesenteric edema, and ascites. The AI system adopted a two-level architecture: The first level used EfficientNet-B3 for rapid screening on x-ray films; the second level used 3D nnU-Net (No-new-Net) to segment intestinal wall gas, and then fused the data through a three-branch network (gas morphology, accompanying signs, and clinical metadata) via cross-attention to output the probability of ischemic PI. In the internal test set, the model achieved an AUC (Area Under the Curve) of 0.947 for ischemic PI (sensitivity 91.3%, specificity 93.6%), significantly outperforming senior radiologists (AUC = 0.876); the AUC on the external validation set was 0.931. SHapley Additive exPlanations analysis showed that PVG and blood lactate were the most important predictors. This two-tiered AI system can significantly improve the early identification of the causes of critical PI, providing a reliable method for intelligent diagnosis of emergency imaging.

title: Critical Algorithmic Literacy
0b6f3348614dc3e95e0f43fb974b970ee1e8164a.abstract: Abstract Critical Algorithmic Literacy explores the complexity of what it means to know algorithms and what such insight affords individuals, communities, and society. It suggests that algorithmic literacy involves understanding what algorithms do and why but also what they mean to and for people as they navigate them in specific contexts. Drawing on a theoretical framework informed by feminist epistemologies, literacy studies, critical algorithm studies, and science and technology studies, the book illustrates how critical algorithmic literacy both shapes and is shaped by membership in different social worlds. Rather than a value-neutral, universal skill set, it conceptualizes algorithmic literacy as relational, contextual, and socially situated. Through case studies of communities entangled with algorithms in distinct ways, the book challenges prevailing visions of algorithmic literacy that privilege technical mastery and are driven by progress narratives serving powerful interests. It reorients critical algorithmic literacy around the goal of just social transformation, positioning it as a foundation for bottom-up governance. The book argues that critical algorithmic literacy plays an essential role in supporting individual agency and building collective momentum toward institutional action—but is a necessary, not sufficient, condition for broad-scale change, given the structural power platforms continue to wield. In line with the broader participatory turn in governance, the book contends that governance of algorithms at the institutional level requires recognition of algorithmic expertise as diverse, contextual, and interwoven with negotiations of power.

title: Critical Validation of Deep Learning-Based Cervical Vertebral Fracture Detection on Computed Tomography Localizer Radiographs
container-title: Journal of Imaging Informatics in Medicine
0d1bbb1e44cdcc74d24ecc990eb86612e6282202.abstract: Abstract Localizer radiographs are low-resolution two-dimensional overview images acquired prior to computed tomography (CT) scans. Their automated analysis could support the early detection of cervical vertebral fractures in trauma patients and thus enable immediate adjustment of imaging protocols. This study investigated to what extent deep learning-based methods can reliably detect such fractures on localizer radiographs, with a focus on critically validating model behavior beyond standard performance metrics. On a custom-annotated dataset of 346 trauma patients, two approaches were compared: a full-image binary classification and a two-step pipeline that first localizes the cervical spine and then classifies the cropped region. Model validity was assessed through a permutation test, occlusion testing, gradient-weighted class activation mapping, an analysis of potential confounders, and a subgroup analysis by anatomical fracture location. The full-image classifier formally achieved the highest test-set performance with a precision-recall area under the curve (PR-AUC) of 0.477, compared with 0.349 for the cervical-spine-level classifier. Our validity analysis indicates that the full-image classifier does not primarily rely on the fracture region itself, rendering it unsuitable for clinical use. This work therefore presents a case study of shortcut learning and illustrates validation methods that may be of value for comparable studies on small datasets with visually subtle targets.

title: Leveling-Up Job Offer Negotiations: Presenting an AI Chatbot Exercise
container-title: Management Teaching Review
2b6c2971c2ea6bb7a3f8d15865e2df856d26bef2.abstract: The purpose of this article is to help students prepare for job offer negotiations. Although resources to help students practice job offer negotiations exist, these activities primarily use peer role-play and may be constrained by synchronous scheduling and limited individualized feedback. We present a fully customizable artificial intelligence negotiation chatbot that supplements, rather than replaces, peer role-play. The exercise provides late undergraduate and graduate students with a low-stakes, repeatable setting in which to rehearse job offer negotiation preparation, requests, and responses at their own pace while receiving individualized feedback. Because chatbot practice does not reproduce the nonverbal communication, reciprocal interpersonal responses, perspective-taking, and relationship-management demands of a human negotiation partner, instructors should use the exercise alongside peer role-play and related human interaction.

title: The cicada genus Albanycada Villet, 1989 (Hemiptera, Cicadidae): systematic revision
container-title: African Invertebrates
91d539f1e77cc488143e368c149620a27925ad73.abstract: Phylogenetic analysis of the nucleotide sequences of the cytochrome oxidase I gene of specimens of Albanycada Villet, 1989 supported the hypothesis that the genus includes more than one species-level lineage. Comparison of the syntype of Platypleura albigera Walker, 1850, the type species of Albanycada , with the syntypes of Platypleura membranacea Karsch, 1890 confirmed that the two species are synonyms, so the other lineage is described under the name Albanycada bellinganorum Villet & Price, sp. nov . Lectotypes are designated for P. albigera Walker, 1850 and P. membranacea Karsch, 1890 to reflect these comparisons. Its morphology, geographical distribution, and calling song are illustrated. Ecological and conservation notes are summarised for both species, and their phylogenetic origins are discussed.

title: Green AI for Telehealth
container-title: Healthcare Management Forum
7b0a606b53c98d3d725366c54edc67aca709604e.abstract: Telehealth is increasingly supported by connected devices, remote monitoring, Artificial Intelligence (AI), and distributed computing. These tools can extend access and support more responsive care, but their computational and environmental demands are rarely considered alongside clinical and organizational needs. We describe the current Canadian telehealth landscape, including remote care management, virtual visits, patient portals, and remote monitoring, and identify opportunities and gaps for AI integration. We then define Green AI in healthcare and explain how an IoT–fog–cloud architecture can support resource-aware telehealth. For health leaders, Green AI is not only an engineering issue. It affects procurement, infrastructure planning, workforce capacity, clinical workflow, environmental responsibility, and equity. Evaluation should consider clinical performance, resource use, organizational fit, and sustainability. Responsible AI-enabled telehealth requires more than technical performance. A Green AI perspective can help health organizations improve computational efficiency while maintaining patient safety, usable workflows, resilience, and equitable access.

title: Explainable AI-Based Pulmonary Nodule Classification from Computed Tomography Images with an End-to-End Clinical Decision Support Interface
88c30d289bf1b961035f9e444a0fba8d0eecea5a.abstract: Abstract Early and accurate detection of pulmonary nodules in computed tomography (CT) imaging is critical for reducing lung cancer mortality. Although deep learning-based computer-aided detection (CAD) systems have demonstrated promis-ing diagnostic performance, their widespread clinical adoption has been impeded by two persistent limitations: the absence of visual explainability and the lack of deployable end-to-end interfaces that integrate prediction, explanation, and clinical workflow. This paper presents an explainable, end-to-end CAD system for pulmonary nodule classification that addresses both shortcomings. The proposed system employs a transfer-learned ResNet-50 architecture, fine-tuned on 2,372 balanced CT patches extracted from the publicly available LUNA16 dataset. Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping (Grad-CAM) is integrated into the inference pipeline to generate per-prediction heatmaps that visually localize the discriminative regions driv-ing each classification decision. The complete system is deployed as a production-grade web application featuring a FastAPI backend and a React frontend, complete with authentication and database persistence. On a held-out test set of 356 samples, the proposed system achieves an accuracy of 90.45%, precision of 90.91%, recall of 89.89%, F1 score of 90.40%, and an AUC-ROC of 0.9615. A confidence-based abstention mechanism returns an “Inconclusive” verdict for predictions below a 60% probability threshold, reducing the risk of unreliable automated decisions. Rather than claiming state-of-the-art raw accuracy, this work’s principal contribution is demonstrating that competitive classification performance, real-time visual explainability, and a fully deployed, browser-accessible clinical interface can be integrated into a single reproducible, open-source system, contributing a practical baseline for future hospital validation studies.

title: Human Socialization (and Dis-Socialization) by AI and Robotic Companions in Educational Ecosystems
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI and Robotic Companions for Human Socialization
21e354c94bb2573462d54359bd698db08de31a01.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter interrogates how AI chatbots, social robots, and ambient agents function as companion technologies that reconfigure human socialization and dis-socialization in educational ecosystems. Drawing on socialization theory, ecological systems, sociocultural mediation, sociomaterial assemblages, and posthuman subjectivity, it constructs a multi-level lens spanning micro interactional dynamics, meso institutional architectures, and macro political economies. The chapter develops typologies of companion configurations, maps learner needs to companion affordances, and analyses interactional quality through constructs such as social presence, parasociality, and epistemic justice. It then articulates normative, rights-based, and governance frameworks that distribute responsibilities across learners, educators, institutions, vendors, regulators, and civil society. The chapter positions humane companionable education as an agenda that seeks to harness machine companionship for inclusion and flourishing while resisting surveillance, stratification, and civic erosion.</jats:p>

title: Emotional and Social Intelligence in AI Systems
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI and Robotic Companions for Human Socialization
6a2e01dfa5708795013bf97dce0351890b7ec891.abstract: <jats:p>As artificial intelligence increasingly engages emotional and social dimensions of human life, its ability to recognize and respond to emotion raises important ethical and philosophical concerns. This chapter examines the development of emotional and social intelligence in AI, highlighting the shift from rational computation toward affective interaction. Drawing on cognitive psychology, affective computing, and moral philosophy, it explores whether machine empathy reflects genuine understanding or performative simulation. The discussion addresses risks such as emotional surveillance, manipulation, dependency, and cultural misrecognition, while acknowledging benefits of emotionally responsive AI in education, healthcare, and assistive contexts. To address ethical gaps, the chapter proposes a Computational Compassion Framework (CCF) integrating moral intentionality, transparency, human oversight, and contextual sensitivity into AI design. It argues that the future of emotional AI lies not in humanizing machines, but in embedding ethical responsibility within technological systems.</jats:p>

title: Attention, Obligation, and the Rootedness of Human Identity in the AI Renaissance
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Reconfiguring Human Identity and Social Contracts in the AI Renaissance
e4417ce1339c12cc05dc70011ea7ae674c983fe8.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter examines how the AI renaissance is reconfiguring fundamental anthropological conditions of human existence and how Simone Weil's ethics of attention, obligation, and rootedness can provide a normative framework for understanding these transformations. Methodologically, the analysis combines conceptual reconstruction, philosophical-hermeneutic updating, and critically reflected conceptual engineering to translate Weil's categories into contemporary AI contexts. The analysis identifies three interconnected transformations: AI-mediated environments can reshape the conditions for sustained attention; distributed human-machine agency can create responsibility and obligation gaps; and digital infrastructures can weaken the conditions for social, economic, and political rootedness. The chapter develops a Weilian governance framework that deepens human-centered AI by identifying the anthropological conditions that underlie rights, human oversight, accountability, and participation.</jats:p>

title: Human Rights in the AI Renaissance
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Reconfiguring Human Identity and Social Contracts in the AI Renaissance
b6cc6cdaede90b65d88551af1e19e431b12e7088.abstract: <jats:p>Artificial intelligence is an innovation that is fast changing society, economy, and government structures. Although it is extremely advantageous, it also triggers the issue of human rights, fairness, and accountability. This chapter focuses on the discussion of the manner in which human rights will be protected in the ascendancy of AI. It raises the red flag over perilous algorithms, the absence of transparency and surveillance technologies proliferation. Legal frameworks and considerations that can be used to steer innovation towards dignity, equality, and justice are also addressed. Healthcare, employment, policing case studies gives an example of how AI affects the basic freedom. The chapter proposes a right based regulation of AI, stating that innovation should be moderated and should not harm people and society. It concludes with the policy suggestions that can make AI advocacy to social justice and maintain human freedoms.</jats:p>

title: Emotional Intelligence and Mental Well-Being in AI-Driven Hospitality
container-title: Experience Economy Insights on Human-Centric Hospitality 5.0
53a8b9399dccecdf1d6c3cc1543b58d05b5ccf4c.abstract: <jats:p>The rapid integration of artificial intelligence (AI), robotics, and digital service systems within the hospitality sector has ushered in an era known as Hospitality 5.0. While these advancements enhance efficiency, personalization, and guest satisfaction, they also increase emotional labor, psychological strain, and occupational stress among employees. This chapter analyzes, using major theories and frameworks, how emotional intelligence and mental well-being mediate sustainable workforce outcomes in AI-intensive hospitality. An original conceptual model, the Emotionally Sustainable Hospitality Workforce Model (ESHWM), is introduced, highlighting sustainable HRM as critical for maintaining emotional and psychological health amid digital disruption. The chapter summarizes empirical evidence linking AI adoption to increased workplace stress and shows how high emotional intelligence protects and boosts frontline hospitality worker performance. Practical implications are offered for managers, HR practitioners, and policymakers, aligning with UN SDGs 3, 8, and 9.</jats:p>

title: Construction and Case Study of a Quality Evaluation Model for Intelligent Information Systems in a Generative Artificial Intelligence Environment: The Case of Bilibili
container-title: Computers and Artificial Intelligence
c7d63252644539de3df39bb8cce6761d736c89be.abstract: <jats:p>After generative artificial intelligence (AI) was embedded in search, content generation, and user interaction, traditional information system quality evaluation faced new boundaries. Based on the DeLone and McLean (D&M) Information Systems Success Model, this study adopts literature research and a single-case study, takes Bilibili as the case, and constructs and applies a six-dimensional evaluation framework based on public materials, observations of platform functions, and publicly available user feedback. The findings show that system quality, information quality, and service quality can still explain basic platform operation, information output, and service support, but they cannot fully cover AI’s semantic understanding and task completion, the trustworthiness of generated results, and continuous human-computer interaction. Therefore, this study introduces AI intelligence quality, trustworthiness quality, and interaction quality on the basis of the three traditional dimensions and clarifies the boundary of each dimension. The Bilibili case shows that the framework can identify both basic capabilities and AI-specific quality, thereby helping to avoid conflating technical performance, content quality, intelligent capability, and trust issues. The study provides a structured analytical framework for evaluating the quality of intelligent information systems in a generative AI environment and a reference for platforms to optimize AI functions and governance mechanisms.</jats:p>

title: Exploration of the mechanism by which quorum sensing signals AI-2 and AIP enhance ethanol tolerance of Lacticaseibacillus paracasei 5
container-title: Food Science and Human Wellness
dcc785851cee11e3f907af2e094a4b78d8d567f7.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Lacticaseibacillus paracasei (L. paracasei) plays an indispensable role in food fermentation and probiotic formulations. Nonetheless, its industrial utilization is frequently limited by its low tolerance to ethanol. Given that biofilm formation constitutes a critical survival mechanism for bacteria under stress conditions, this study sought to examine the impact of exogenous autoinducer-2 (AI-2) and autoinducing peptides (AIP) on the biofilm formation of L. paracasei in the presence of ethanol stress. The findings revealed that both AI-2 and AIP substantially enhanced biofilm formation, increased membrane fluidity, and augmented exopolysaccharide (EPS) production under ethanol stress conditions. Transcriptomic analysis further revealed distinct regulatory mechanisms: AI-2 primarily upregulated genes encoding ABC transporters (e.g., potABCD, phnCDE, oppABCDF), which support ATP-driven uptake of compounds essential for cellular homeostasis under ethanol stress. In contrast, AIP mainly activated genes involved in the phosphotransferase system (PTS) (e.g., BglF, MtlA, CelB, CelC), facilitating carbohydrate uptake and central carbon metabolism to meet the biosynthetic demands of EPS and biofilm matrix assembly. This work would provide important insights into the stress adaptation mechanisms mediated by quorum sensing (QS) in L. paracasei 5.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Green AI-Driven Synthetic Data Generation for Improved Industrial Metal Surface Defect Detection
container-title: INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF COMPUTERS  COMMUNICATIONS & CONTROL
7cb4bdcba33492ba6826438a8e4421a4967bef1a.abstract:
<jats:p>Defect detection of industrial metal surfaces is often limited by the scarcity of annotated data and the high cost of manual labeling, which limits the performance of data-driven inspection systems. This paper presents a Green AI-driven framework for synthetic data generation that efficiently augments industrial defect datasets while minimizing computational and annotation costs. The proposed approach employs a deterministic procedural pipeline to generate synthetic defect images together with aligned segmentation masks at the pixel-level, providing accurate supervision without the computational overhead of deep generative models. The framework is evaluated on the Kolektor Surface-Defect Dataset 2 (KSDD2), which is extended into a hybrid dataset through synthetic augmentation followed by human-in-the-loop validation, to ensure the realism and reliability of the generated samples and annotations. A lightweight state-of-the-art anomaly detection model, SuperSimpleNet, is trained under controlled ablation settings on both the original and hybrid datasets using identical test splits for fair comparison.
Performance is evaluated using both image-level and pixel-level metrics, including AUROC and average precision. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed hybrid dataset consistently improves defect detection and localization performance while substantially reducing the need for costly data acquisition and manual annotation. Unlike computationally intensive generative approaches based on GANs or diffusion models, the proposed procedural framework synthesizes defects directly within predefined regions, enabling automatic generation of pixel-accurate ground-truth annotations without human intervention. The resulting hybrid dataset improves all evaluation metrics, achieving the largest gain in anomaly localization performance, with AP-loc increasing by 5.3%, while image-level AUROC increases from 0.9840 to 0.9907. By combining efficient synthetic data generation with precise automatic annotation, the proposed approach provides a resource-efficient solution that aligns with Green AI principles.</jats:p>

title: Known by the Machine: Building Relational Presence with AI NPCs for Stigma-Free Mental Health Literacy in Games
container-title: Proceedings of the ACM on Human-Computer Interaction
4c9c9964378a64482a43967764b54ff15bb6fa76.abstract: <jats:p>Mental Health (MH) remains a global priority, yet low literacy and stigma frequently limit open discussion and help-seeking behaviors. While game-based education has shown promise in supporting stigma reduction and literacy improvement, the potential for Large Language Models (LLMs) to support non-judgmental, playful exploration of sensitive topics remains underexplored, specifically, the role of conversational memory to support trust-building in MH discussions. We conducted a four-session, longitudinal mixed-methods study to evaluate how the relational presence of AI characters, powered by GPT-4o-mini with varied memory designs, relates to player experience and learning. Moving beyond an evaluation of learning, we examine how the perception of being known by an AI NPC is associated with engagement with stigmatized content. Results indicate that while participants achieved significant and sustained gains in Mental Health Literacy (MHL), these improvements did not differ by memory condition. Instead, memory appeared to operate as a relational design feature that shaped participants’ perceptions of social presence, with many describing conversational NPCs as supportive companions. We also identify interactional risks, such as algorithmic vagueness and privacy-induced hesitation, that participants described as reducing their comfort during conversations. We conclude by offering design recommendations for leveraging LLM memory to create more relational and stigma-sensitive environments for MH education.</jats:p>

title: Guards & Wards: The Creative Labour of GMs and Considerations for Designing with AI
container-title: Proceedings of the ACM on Human-Computer Interaction
97f59e27090381539a8186baf42b7de0cca1bb39.abstract: <jats:p>Tabletop role-playing games (TTRPGs) provide a complicated environment for creativity. Game masters (GMs) co-create a story along with their players and many choose to complete significant labour both prior to and during a gaming session. However, the boundaries that GMs may have about generative artificial intelligence (AI) being used in this creative hobby have not been examined. We examine the perceptions of GMs on the use of AI for creativity support in TTRPGs. We conducted a survey of GMs to discover the labour they completed in preparation for and play of TTRPG sessions, the existing creativity support tools (CSTs) that they use for this labour, and their opinions on the use of AI in TTRPGs. We performed both qualitative and quantitative analysis to examine survey data. We contrasted our results across two participant groups: those who have or have not been paid to GM a gaming session, and those who have or have not used AI as GMs. From our data, we created twelve distinct orientation groups encompassing the opinions of participants on AI for use in TTRPGs. We propose thirteen design considerations in the form of questions AI tool developers should ask when creating AI-based CSTs for TTRPG use.</jats:p>

title: Age Matters: Age-Differentiated Playtesting for AI Educational Games
container-title: Proceedings of the ACM on Human-Computer Interaction
51c2ffec725312491c89a2f2140899598712ae8b.abstract: <jats:p>Playtesting is widely employed in educational game design as a post-hoc method for game design validation within the age groups that the learning goals target. For domains such as AI literacy, age-targeted educational games testing may be limiting, as AI learning goals are relevant and frequently misunderstood by children, adolescents and young adults. Designing educational games that teach AI to a wider audience of ages requires playtesting with players of different ages to better interpret gameplay and narrative appropriateness of AI in AI educational games. In this study, we playtested four AI educational games with middle, high school, and college aged students, and analyzed playtesting data, including verbal discourse, in-game behaviors, and post-playtesting reflections. Our findings demonstrate that playtesting can serve as an asset-based practice which reveals how players of different age groups make sense of educational games during play. We provide critical reflections from multi-age playtesting of AI educational games that inform design, and recommendations for engaging AI educational game design.</jats:p>

title: Does Trust Spill Over?: Exploring Asymmetric Trust Dynamics Between Teammate AI and Guide AI in Cooperative Games
container-title: Proceedings of the ACM on Human-Computer Interaction
aa082ec48f7a3ea66734c5c6aa6b23a8c21c5b8a.abstract:
<jats:p>
                    Cooperative games increasingly feature multiple AI agents serving distinct roles, yet how players form and transfer trust across such agents remains unclear. We investigated trust spillover between a task-executing Teammate AI and an advisory Guide AI in a web-based cooperative cooking game (within-subjects, N = 23). Teammate AI ability (high vs. low) and Guide AI accuracy (high vs. low/absent) were experimentally manipulated. Results revealed a directional asymmetry in trust spillover. Teammate AI ability significantly influenced trust in the Guide AI (
                    <jats:inline-formula content-type="math/tex">
                      <jats:tex-math notation="LaTeX" version="MathJax">\(\eta _p^2 =.220\)</jats:tex-math>
                    </jats:inline-formula>
                    ), whereas Guide AI accuracy and presence had no effect on trust in the Teammate AI (
                    <jats:inline-formula content-type="math/tex">
                      <jats:tex-math notation="LaTeX" version="MathJax">\(\eta _p^2 =.002\)</jats:tex-math>
                    </jats:inline-formula>
                    ). This suggests that, under cognitive constraints, trust propagates from high-salience task agents to lower-salience advisory agents, but not vice versa. Additionally, the presence of the Guide AI improved performance and perceived control independent of advice accuracy, suggesting an attentional cueing effect. Finally, congruent agent quality levels enhanced perceived relatedness, highlighting the importance of system-level coherence. These findings demonstrate asymmetric trust spillover in cooperative games with role-differentiated AI, where execution-focused agents anchor system-wide trust formation, with implications for multi-agent AI systems in which agents serve distinct functional roles.
                  </jats:p>

title: Player Perceptions of Generative AI in Games: A Steam Review Analysis
container-title: Proceedings of the ACM on Human-Computer Interaction
08911279f04c0994a25c0ab11145fcff09c60790.abstract: <jats:p>The rapid adoption of generative AI in game development has created large discussions among players, yet little empirical work has examined how players actually perceive AI-generated content. Employing quantitative methods, we study the adoption of generative AI in games in the Steam marketplace, using procedural content generation (PCG) as a baseline of a generative technology that was successfully integrated into games over several decades. Furthermore, using qualitative methods, we study player reception of generative AI by analyzing 508,192 English-language reviews. We found that games disclosing generative AI use receive lower recommendation rates and more negative overall sentiment than PCG games. Thematic analysis of 600 reviews shows that players perceive the use of generative AI in games as low developer investment in the game. Drawing on human-centered AI frameworks, we argue that successful generative AI adoption requires deploying generative AI for what players need, not for what makes development cheaper.</jats:p>

title: Meritocracy and generative AI in higher education: institutional pathways and use–response alignment across four systems
container-title: Advances in Social Behavior Research
1d18258e5287d5117654b68c5dc746e92d867f48.abstract: <jats:p>This study examines how higher education systems respond to the rapid adoption of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) under different institutional conditions, asking how meritocratic competition is translated into assessment and credential pressure and how student GenAI use aligns with institutional responses. Using a comparative qualitative case-study design, the study analyzes secondary evidence from China, the United Kingdom, the United States, and Germany through two a priori frozen indicator frameworks. The first framework traces how meritocratic competition is institutionalized through admissions, grading, and credential differentiation; the second maps student GenAI use patterns against institutional responses in teaching, assessment, and support. Strong credential differentiation and education–labour-market linkage emerge in all four systems, but through distinct pathways: state-coordinated in China, marketized in the United Kingdom, decentralized and market-oriented in the United States, and state–professional in Germany. Partial use–response alignment is the cross-system norm; systems differ mainly in pedagogical integration, regulatory adaptation, and institutional support. AI literacy and support provision lag behind student adoption in all four cases, making institutional capacity the most persistent source of misalignment, while limited comparable measurement of equity alignment and of guarded and compensatory use shows that monitoring capacity is itself part of governance. GenAI governance therefore converges less on common rules than on common capability gaps. The findings suggest that governing GenAI in meritocratic systems depends less on uniform rules than on sustained investment in institutional monitoring and support capacity.</jats:p>

title: Generative AI-enabled writing feedback in primary school English instruction: application landscape, practical dilemmas, and a teacher-led collaborative framework
container-title: Advances in Social Behavior Research
46a2a0e62e833b05feb28298ad275d5b27608889.abstract: <jats:p>Writing feedback is a pivotal yet chronically constrained component of primary school English writing instruction, squeezed by large class sizes, low marking frequency, and homogeneous comments. Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI), with its immediacy, personalization, and dialogic interaction, opens new possibilities for reconstructing writing feedback. Drawing on a narrative synthesis of 52 Chinese and international sources, and addressing a literature in which research on AI writing feedback concentrates on higher education and on the learner side, this paper maps the application landscape of GenAI-enabled writing feedback in primary school English, consolidates and examines five practical dilemmas concerning accuracy, appropriateness, teacher literacy, ethics, and evaluation orientation, and proposes a Teacher-led, AI-assisted, Student-centered Collaborative Feedback Framework (TAC-F). The framework assigns teachers responsibility for goal setting, affective support, and feedback verification, positions GenAI as an initial assessor and material provider, and treats students as reflective revisers within a pre-writing, while-writing, and post-writing closed loop, supported by prompt-template libraries, feedback-verification routines, school-based teacher AI literacy development, and ethical data norms. Preliminary multi-tool observations, together with a six-dimension observation framework and a same-prompt pilot protocol, are developed to help teachers screen AI-generated feedback; the observations suggest that current tools are reliable on explicit errors but unstable at the discourse level. Six implementation suggestions are advanced to inform the digital transformation of primary school English writing instruction.</jats:p>

title: Visual Sexual Health Communication Assisted by AI: The Case of Synthetic Menstruation Images
container-title: Archives of Sexual Behavior
08fb882f77177fa29f70584626a13ad9137367d1.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    Public communication about sexual and reproductive health and rights (SRHR) relies on both text and images. A recent development is the proliferation of artificial intelligence (AI) image generators, which enable rapid, cost-effective, and highly customizable images with appealing aesthetics based on textual requests (prompts). To examine the opportunities and challenges of AI-generated images in SRHR communication, we used the topic of menstruation and developed six research questions (RQs) anchored in the current state of research on AI-supported visual health communication. These questions addressed key areas of concern, such as unsuccessful image creation (RQ1), objective image flaws (RQ2), lack of diversity of human representation (RQ3), stereotypical portrayals of women (RQ4), use of visual symbols (RQ5), and image valence (RQ6). Our study applied 15 AI image generators, 2 user accounts per generator, 5 menstruation-related prompts, 2 prompt languages, and 2 images per prompt, resulting in a sample of
                    <jats:italic>N</jats:italic>
                     = 600 AI outputs generated in Autumn 2025. All outputs were manually coded using a reliability-tested codebook developed through both deductive and inductive approaches. In 20.0% of cases, menstruation prompts did not produce the requested image but only text output (RQ1). When images were generated, they often (78.1%) exhibited visual and/or textual flaws (RQ2). The images showed a lack of diversity in some human attributes (e.g., body type) but not in others (e.g., skin tone; RQ3). Stereotypical depictions of women were observed but not predominant (RQ4). Common menstruation-related visual symbols (e.g., blood, pain) were identified (RQ5), but most images did not convey a negative portrayal and instead a neutral or positive portrayal of menstruation (RQ6). While results show that initial outputs from AI image generators are often not directly suitable for visual sexual health communication, they might work with targeted refinement. Further research is required to examine the production, characteristics, consumption, and effects of AI-generated images in SRHR communication.
                  </jats:p>

title: Secure Edge-AI Sensing on an FPGA SoC: Lightweight ASCON Authentication of Model Updates and Interface-Bound Inference for Bearing-Fault Detection
container-title: Computers
303d4ba538744ba35fa73581feb18063f5c07d26.abstract: <jats:p>Vibration monitoring increasingly classifies on the sensing node. We ask where the cost of running and securely updating a small classifier on an FPGA system-on-chip node lies. One Q4.12 multilayer perceptron for bearing-fault detection, trained on 40 CWRU recordings over four loads and three severities, is deployed bit-exactly on an ESP32-S3, a Cortex-A53 and a custom AXI4-Lite accelerator of the same Zynq UltraScale+ device (Kria KV260), checked on all 2132 windows. The fabric computes one inference in 36 cycles (0.36 µs), yet the latency under the PYNQ driver is 133.2 µs; a native-C driver reduces it to 3.59 µs, placing 95–97% of the per-transaction cost in the host software stack. Moving the update decision into the fabric, with the ASCON-AEAD128 tag check, version freshness and staging enforced in hardware, rejects every tested forgery, replay and direct write, and cuts a 608-byte authenticated update from 148.7 to 66.0 µs in native C. The full chain runs in real time, with no deadline miss over 552 windows (worst case 1.8% of the 171 ms window), and feature extraction dominates its cost. The model reaches 98.2% on unseen segments but generalizes poorly to unseen fault severities and to real damage of unseen Paderborn bearings, which makes field updates a requirement.</jats:p>

title: Edge AI Imitation of Event-Triggered Model Predictive Control for an Inverted Pendulum
container-title: Computers
05938ee211a2e0d7b4b9a7b07cb4c17bb8bcfd63.abstract: <jats:p>Event-triggered model predictive control (MPC) updates the control input only when needed, but it still solves an optimization problem at every event, which on the studied cart–pole can exceed its 10 ms control period. We propose a compact multi-task neural network that replaces the whole scheme: it decides when to update the input and which value to apply, using only online measurements. It is trained on 500 physical recordings, adapted to a simulated teacher and refined with DAgger. Feeding it the held input produces a copycat policy that is accurate in open loop but sluggish in closed loop; in a matched comparison over four training seeds, removing that input raises full-episode success from three to 39 of 40 episodes. In simulation, at the default sensor noise, the final network completes all swing-up and tracking episodes, with time to upright and tracking error close to the teacher’s, whereas on the simulated teacher, tree ensembles have 1.4–1.6 times its open-loop error. In an open-loop replay on an ESP32-S3 microcontroller, a step takes under 40% of the period. In tracking and full episodes, it updates the input 33–39% more often than the teacher, mainly because it does not learn the rule’s sparsity.</jats:p>

title: Explainable Machine Learning for Analyzing AI Adoption and Teachers’ Professional Development Needs: Evidence from TALIS 2024 in Kazakhstan
container-title: Computers
d995276851023c13b6f90d18faa245a7956a09a2.abstract: <jats:p>The growing use of artificial intelligence (AI) in education highlights the need to distinguish teachers’ AI adoption from their professional development needs. This study examined these outcomes as separate predictive tasks using OECD TALIS 2024 data for 7360 teachers in Kazakhstan at ISCED level 2. After excluding invalid outcome records, the analytical samples comprised 2430 teachers for AI adoption and 4868 for professional development needs. Population estimates and confidence intervals were calculated using teacher weights and 100 Fay-BRR replicate weights, while predictive performance was assessed using out-of-fold predictions and school-grouped validation. The weighted prevalence of AI adoption was 59.0% (95% CI: 56.1–61.9). Logistic Regression and CatBoost demonstrated comparable discrimination (ROC-AUC = 0.754 and 0.753, respectively), with no clear performance advantage for CatBoost. SHAP analysis identified prior AI-related professional learning, uncertainty regarding AI attitudes, and perceived AI benefits as prominent predictive factors. Moderate or high professional development need was estimated at 80.3% (95% CI: 78.7–81.9). However, individual prediction was weak, with balanced accuracy of 0.268 and a quadratic weighted kappa of 0.082. These findings indicate that TALIS variables provide a moderate predictive signal for AI adoption but are insufficient for reliable, individualized professional development decisions.</jats:p>

title: Generative AI in English Language Teaching: A Systematic Review of Its Impact on Teaching Practices and Learning Outcomes
container-title: International Journal of Social Science and Human Research
8fb433a0a2295e097a0eab7db1db828dcf5bf252.abstract: <jats:p>Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) tools are now common in English classrooms, but the research on them is spread thinly across different tools, settings and skills, and most of it records what people think rather than what learners actually gained. This review looks at how GenAI is changing the way English is taught and what learners gain from it. Using the PRISMA procedure, the review drew on Web of Science, Scopus, ScienceDirect and Springer, selecting peer-reviewed journal papers from 2024 to 2026; 28 studies were analysed in full. In most studies GenAI served as a helper for teachers in lesson planning, materials, feedback and classroom activities, but how far it was taken up varied with teachers’ own attitudes, self-assurance and preparation. Assessment was the area most challenged, prompting teachers to rethink task design and academic integrity. In terms of learning, GenAI is associated with perceived improvements in writing, grammar, vocabulary, pronunciation, motivation, confidence, and autonomy, but most evidence is perception-based rather than measured. The review concludes that GenAI is best used as a supplement to teacher-guided instruction, with teachers checking its output and guiding learners towards critical use. Future research should adopt longitudinal and controlled designs that measure language outcomes directly.</jats:p>

title: A Study on the Coupling Relationship Between AI Personalization and Long-Context Management
container-title: Computers and Artificial Intelligence
49889832b6f70b95f1a638c748d37b18136de351.abstract: <jats:p>With the large-scale deployment of large language models (LLMs) in various intelligent assistants and agent systems, homogenized outputs and the loss of user preferences across sessions have become key bottlenecks restricting improvements in user experience. Personalization technology aims to adapt LLMs to the language habits, thinking patterns, and subjective preferences of different users, while long-context and agent memory management addresses the underlying technical problems of storing, filtering, and reusing temporal information for LLMs. Current academic research mostly treats the two directions as independent fields, and systematic reviews of their internal coupling relationship are relatively scarce. This study first defines the core concepts of LLM personalization and long-context memory management and systematically reviews the technical principles, advantages, and existing limitations of four personalization paradigms: prompt-engineering personalization, lightweight parameter fine-tuning, user-preference alignment, and dynamic user profiling. It then divides long-context and agent-memory technologies into five routes: native-window expansion, context pruning and compression, adaptive context extraction, hierarchical memory architectures, and external retrieval-augmented memory, and analyzes the applicable scenarios and technical shortcomings of each route. On this basis, this study reviews progress in four intersecting directions: preference-aware memory updating, structured persona-memory representation, long-horizon personalization evaluation benchmarks, and training-free collaborative control at inference time. It further analyzes the internal coupling mechanism through which the two directions empower each other and summarizes three core conflicts: the capacity-accuracy trade-off, the conflict between general governance rules and personalized characteristics, and the conflict between computational cost and personalization stability. The study also summarizes five research challenges: difficulty in adapting to the dynamic evolution of user preferences, failure to recall implicit preferences, memory errors and preference drift, fragmented evaluation systems, and difficulty balancing engineering implementation costs. It proposes subsequent research paths in six dimensions: cognitively inspired memory architectures, preference-aware context compression algorithms, multimode hybrid indexing and retrieval, unified long-horizon personalization evaluation protocols, memory-error verification mechanisms, and multimodal long-term personalization. The findings indicate that long-term personalized intelligent systems cannot optimize the personalization module or memory module in isolation. Their coupling relationship should serve as the underlying design logic to promote the iterative upgrading of LLMs toward adaptation to individual user characteristics and to provide a reference for the theoretical research and engineering development of long-term agents and personalized dialogue assistants.</jats:p>

title: Budget-Aware Adaptive Test-Time Compute with Hierarchical Self-Verification for Semantic ID Generative Recommendation
container-title: Computers
ad812a7a10cc5144461b6cebf5c51d87590389d3.abstract: <jats:p>Semantic identifier (SID) generative recommenders cast retrieval as autoregressive decoding over short sequences of residual-quantized codewords. Most published SID recommenders decode all requests with one fixed beam width, which is optimal only if the marginal utility of compute is constant across requests. We find that it is not; additional search changes little for users with consistent histories, but improves accuracy substantially for cold start, interest-drifting, and long-tail users. The main methodological contribution of this paper is request-level allocation of decoding compute, in which a router predicts the accuracy gain of each configuration in a finite decoding menu over the cheapest configuration and selects the configuration with the largest gain net of a priced cost. The selection rule follows from standard Lagrangian arguments, which we use as tools; what is specific to this work is the use of this per-configuration gain as the routing target for SID decoding instead of a difficulty or uncertainty score. The resulting framework, called Bastion, combines the router with a hierarchical process verifier over the quantization levels, a listwise terminal verifier, codeword consistency voting, and budget-constrained group relative policy optimization. On five benchmarks built from Amazon Reviews 2023, MovieLens, and MicroLens, Bastion improves NDCG@10 by 5.7% to 8.7% over the strongest baseline. Its mean latency on Amazon-Beauty is 14.5 ms, against 14.6 ms for a beam-20 TIGER decoder, while its median and 99th-percentile latencies are higher by 0.9 ms and 7.0 ms. At every evaluated budget, its accuracy exceeds that of all baselines on the three datasets for which accuracy versus latency frontiers was measured.</jats:p>

title: Offloading Thoughts to the Bots: How Generative AI Access Influences Cognitive Reflection
container-title: Proceedings of the Human Factors and Ergonomics Society Annual Meeting
89abf0f54d025ddf7e06b07b896cddba60561ff9.abstract:
<jats:p>
                    Generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) systems are increasingly used to support reasoning and decision-making, raising questions about how AI influences reflective cognition and trust. This study examined how AI pedigree and reliability influenced cognitive reflection performance, cognitive load, trust, and performance overestimation during a verbal Cognitive Reflection Test (CRT-V). Participants (
                    <jats:italic toggle="yes">N</jats:italic>
                     = 148) were assigned to a no-AI control condition, a low-pedigree AI condition, or a high-pedigree AI condition. Participants in the high-pedigree AI condition demonstrated significantly greater trust and CRT performance than participants in both other conditions while also exhibiting lower performance overestimation. AI access did not significantly reduce perceived cognitive load, although greater cognitive load predicted poorer CRT performance overall. Importantly, trust interacted with AI condition such that greater trust predicted lower CRT performance in the low-pedigree AI condition but not in the high-pedigree AI condition. These findings support theories of calibrated reliance rather than indiscriminate cognitive offloading.
                  </jats:p>

title: A Study on AI Digital Competency and the Perceived Need for AI Utilization Education among Physical Therapy Students
container-title: Journal of Clinical Movement Science in Human
f8b52f591df875ac1c2019dd4f4b18ce9752e66d.abstract: <jats:p>Purpose This study aimed to examine AI digital competency and the perceived need for AI utilization education among physical therapy students and to analyze the relationship between the two variables. Methods This crosssectional correlational survey was conducted with 232 physical therapy students at S University using an online survey. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics and Pearson correlation analysis. Results The mean score for AI digital competency was 3.48±0.57, with communication and collaboration showing the highest score at 3.84±0.62 and digital content creation showing the lowest score at 3.03±0.71. The mean score for the perceived need for AI utilization education was 3.91±0.71. AI digital competency was positively correlated with the perceived need for AI utilization education (r=0.320, p<.001). Conclusion These results suggest the need for systematic educational support to help physical therapy students effectively use AI in majorrelated learning and clinical problemsolving.</jats:p>

title: From Code-Centric to Intent-Centric Software Engineering: A Reflexive Thematic Analysis of Generative AI, Agentic Systems, and Engineering Accountability
container-title: Computers
b8b475504b37ed3bec01880f6991e5586b1ec8f1.abstract: <jats:p>Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) and agentic systems are shifting software engineering from code-centric production toward intent-centric human-agent work, in which natural language, repository context, tools, tests, and governance shape delivery. Prior studies examine code generation, AI pair programming, and software engineering agents, but less is known about how public technical discourse and peer-reviewed evidence jointly frame the profession’s near-term transition. This study addresses that gap through a reflexive thematic analysis (RTA) of public-discourse and document analysis. The corpus combines peer-reviewed software engineering and AI literature, technical benchmarks, public talks and interviews, essays, product-facing technical announcements, and X-originated discourse. The corpus contains 49 unique artifacts across three evidentiary layers: 28 peer-reviewed sources, 6 technical preprints/benchmarks, and 15 public discourse artifacts. Sources were organized using a corpus register, codebook, coding matrix, theme-to-source traceability table, DOI/reference audit, and reproducibility protocol. The analysis indicates that GenAI lowers the cost of producing plausible code while increasing the importance of intent specification, context curation, architecture knowledge, verification, security, provenance, governance, and accountable human judgment. Software engineering is consequently becoming less about isolated code authorship and more about supervising, validating, and governing socio-technical systems of humans, agents, tools, and evidence gates. Bounded autonomy can preserve quality, security, maintainability, and trust while limiting hidden technical debt and accountability gaps.</jats:p>

title: Quantum-secure and AI-driven UAV-enabled 6G networks: a unified architecture for communication, intelligence, efficiency, and resilience
container-title: The Computer Journal
2706b267c202c5d2b4e0d881162c56dccf975efc.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>The sixth generation (6G) of wireless networks is expected to meet stringent requirements such as ultra-low latency, massive connectivity, global coverage, and intrinsic security. Unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) are emerging as key enablers of space–air–ground integrated networks, providing flexible and on-demand communication support for beyond-5G and 6G applications. In parallel, advances in quantum communication introduce new opportunities for achieving information-theoretic security against postquantum threats. This paper proposes a unified framework for quantum-secure and artificial intelligence (AI)-driven UAV-enabled 6G networks, integrating communication, intelligence, energy efficiency, and resilience into a coherent architecture. Beyond the design perspective, the paper evaluates network performance through Quality of Service and Grade of Service metrics, comparing 5G and 6G systems with and without AI and quantum-security capabilities. A ranking-based analysis is developed to assess the impact of these technologies on latency, reliability, scalability, and overall service performance. The results highlight the performance gains enabled by AI-driven optimization and quantum-secure communication, while also revealing trade-offs related to energy consumption, system complexity, and deployment constraints. Key challenges such as interoperability, hardware limitations, and scalability are discussed, along with design directions for realizing efficient, secure, and resilient UAV-enabled 6G networks.</jats:p>

title: Revisiting the diffusion of innovations theory: artificial intelligence adoption in social media
container-title: Online Media and Global Communication
449a974a4bc897e7abdf866fa890c855a1b3ed29.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec id="j_omgc-2026-0013_abs_001">
                    <jats:title>Purpose</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The present study aims at revisiting the applicability of Rogers’ diffusion of innovations theory in the digital era, particularly in relation to recent advancements in Artificial Intelligence and their use in social media. It further explores the role of generational differences in shaping AI adoption patterns.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec id="j_omgc-2026-0013_abs_002">
                    <jats:title>Design/methodology/approach</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Drawing on rich qualitative data, the researchers adopt a multi-method approach comprising eighteen interviews with academic and professional experts across different countries, and four focus group discussions among different generations to collect first-hand insights on GenAI adoption. AI was itself used during qualitative data analysis following our AI-Assisted Data Analysis Procedure (ADAP), including generating and categorizing codes, themes, and excerpts.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec id="j_omgc-2026-0013_abs_003">
                    <jats:title>Findings</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The findings provide updated insights into the elements of the diffusion process, establishing potential grounds for modernizing the theory in light of AI-driven innovations. Shifts in innovation attributes, decision-making processes, and generational influences are identified, revealing how AI adoption transforms communication practices within digitally networked environments that increasingly shape contemporary global communication. The study further highlights patterns of resistance and reasons for non-AI adoption.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec id="j_omgc-2026-0013_abs_004">
                    <jats:title>Practical implications</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The study offers insights for communication professionals, platform designers, policymakers, and technology developers seeking to design and implement AI tools in social media environments in ways that account for generational differences in adoption patterns and decision-making processes.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec id="j_omgc-2026-0013_abs_005">
                    <jats:title>Social implications</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>By examining GenAI adoption within digitally mediated societies, the study contributes to broader discussions about technological change, generational divides, societal consequences of GenAI integration, and the evolving diffusion of AI-driven innovations.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec id="j_omgc-2026-0013_abs_006">
                    <jats:title>Originality/value</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The study advances diffusion scholarship by empirically reassessing Rogers’ framework in the context of global AI-mediated communication and by proposing ADAP as a methodological contribution to qualitative communication research.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Trustworthy Federated Clinical Intelligence with Homomorphic Encryption and  Explainable AI
container-title: International Journal on Advanced Computer Engineering and Communication Technology
52dc2d5fa5cc8d54dabc189da8b019169d1f9138.abstract: <jats:p>Cross-institutional clinical artificial intelligence is constrained by fragmented patient data, non-identically distributed (non-IID) populations, leakage from shared model updates, and limited interpretability. Federated learning (FL) preserves data locality, but ordinary FL neither makes model updates confidential nor guarantees stable optimization under heterogeneous clients. This paper proposes a defense-in-depth framework that coordinates Federated Proximal (FedProx) optimization, record-level differential privacy (DP), Cheon–Kim–Kim–Song (CKKS) approximate homomorphic encryption, and explainable artificial intelligence (XAI). FedProx limits local model drift; DP-SGD bounds the influence of an individual training record; and CKKS permits weighted aggregation while client updates remain encrypted. A key-separated design keeps the aggregation server from being provisioned with the secret key used to reveal individual contributions; only the aggregate is released for global-model construction. Grad-CAM and SHAP/LIME provide clinician-facing explanations, while an audit dashboard reports convergence, privacy-accounting inputs, encryption status, and systems overhead. We formalize the learning objective, privacy mechanism, encrypted aggregation, threat model, numerical approximation error, communication footprint, and an evaluation protocol spanning IID and controlled non-IID partitions. The contribution is a reproducible system-level co-design and evaluation framework rather than a new cryptographic primitive or optimization algorithm.</jats:p>

title: Assessment of Taraba Broadcast Journalists Knowledge, Adoption and Usage of Artificial Intelligence in Journalistic Practices
container-title: RESEARCH JOURNAL OF MASS COMMUNICATION AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY
3d595057b3e03ea8fa7b358699deebe39aca77a9.abstract:
<jats:p>Artificial Intelligence (AI) has become an essential tool in various fields, including journalism.
However, the extent to which broadcast journalists in Taraba State, Nigeria embraced and utilized
AI in their practices remains a subject of debate. It is on the above premise that this research
examined Taraba State broadcast journalists' knowledge and usage of AI in journalistic practices.
The paper was built on the technology acceptance model, diffusion of innovation theory, and social
learning theory. The study adopted a qualitative approach where in-depth interviews were used.
The in-depth interviews were conducted until the results reached saturation point. Findings of the
study revealed that in journalists in Taraba State, Nigeria are slowly beginning to embrace AI for
journalistic practice. However, there knowledge of AI usage for journalistic practices is low hence
there is a significant knowledge gap that needs to be bridged. Therefore, the study recommends
among other things that journalists in Taraba State need to gain more knowledge about AI and its
potential applications in journalistic practices. The paper concludes that with proper training and
guidance, journalists in Taraba State can harness the power of this AI technology to improve their
reporting practices while ensuring ethical standards are upheld.</jats:p>
