title: The effectiveness of Schema therapy on Alexithymia, Cognitive flexibility, Body image, and Food craving in individuals with type 2 diabetes: A randomized controlled trial
1b4268729b6cfc9acbb2bb965df1838f26be78ed.abstract: Abstract Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is a chronic metabolic disorder accompanied by alexithymia, cognitive inflexibility, body image disturbances, and food craving. Schema therapy targets maladaptive cognitive-emotional schemas and may improve these psychosocial factors. We assessed group schema therapy for alexithymia, cognitive flexibility, body image, and food craving in adults with T2DM. Fifty adults were randomized to eight weekly 90-minute sessions of schema therapy or diabetes self-management education (DSMES), matched for therapist contact and format. Self-report measures (TAS-20, CFI, BICI, FCQ-T) were administered pre- and post-intervention. Data were analyzed using intention-to-treat with multiple imputation. ANCOVA adjusted for baseline scores. Schema therapy produced significant improvements over DSMES in alexithymia (adjusted means 49.31 vs 60.09; p < 0.001; η²p = 0.352), body image (32.92 vs 39.21; p < 0.001; η²p = 0.258), and food craving (92.30 vs 106.85; p < 0.001; η²p = 0.340). Cognitive flexibility total improved (100.81vs 94.47; p < 0.001; η²p = 0.085), but the Control subscale did not (p = 0.128). All subscales of alexithymia, body image, and food craving improved. Group schema therapy may be a useful adjunct for selected psychosocial barriers in T2DM, but sample size, no follow-up, and self-report measures limit conclusions. Trial registration: IRCT20251201068177N1 (registered 31 December 2025).

title: Enhanced inter-network morphological coordination in high-order association networks: MIND derived cortical morphological similarity signatures for successful cognitive aging
e0849dd3d67d0aa248ea9a97c589e2a95134aee6.abstract: Abstract Background Cognitive aging exhibits substantial individual heterogeneity, and successful cognitive aging (SCA) describes older adults retaining relatively intact cognitive function. Conventional regional morphometric analyses cannot fully capture brain interactions across regions that underpin cognitive preservation. The Morphometric Inverse Divergence (MIND) supports construction of multivariate morphometric similarity networks at the vertex level to probe brain structural organization at the system level. Methods The present study included 63 participants, comprising 24 SCA individuals and 39 normal aging (NA) individuals. MIND networks were constructed from five morphological features at the vertex level using the Schaefer 400‑region atlas. Nodal metrics for graph theory were calculated, and values for the area under the curve (AUC) were adopted for statistical tests. Partial correlation analyses examined associations between imaging indices and episodic memory performance, with FDR correction applied for multiple comparisons. Results Compared with the NA group, SCA participants exhibited higher inter‑network cortical morphological similarity, which was concentrated in high‑order association networks (DMN, CON, DAN, VAN). Participants with SCA also showed elevated Module_Z (AUC) in the left VAN.PFC1.1. Inter‑network morphological similarity and nodal modularity of VAN.PFC1.1 were positively correlated with episodic memory scores. Conclusions Enhanced multidimensional morphological coordination across high‑order association networks and specialization of key prefrontal nodes characterize SCA. These structural connectome signatures may act as neural markers of cognitive resilience and yield potential targets for neuroprotective interventions related to aging.

title: Optimization of Signal Features in EEG-BCI Based on Multi-Class Subject-Specific Motor Imagery Classification
container-title: Big Data and Cognitive Computing
b5b6dbfd8e2be31ebf377873604d307bc85346ba.abstract: Motor Imagery (MI)-based Brain–Computer Interfaces (BCIs) often rely heavily on subject-specific feature selection to achieve high classification accuracy. However, this introduces substantial computational overhead and calibration friction that can limit clinical translation. This study benchmarks three distinct feature selection algorithms (Genetic Algorithm (GA), Differential Evolution (DE), Relief-F) to determine whether a universal feature set comprising common, shared features identified across subjects can be reliably established, thereby reducing or eliminating the need for subject-specific feature optimization. To evaluate this utilizing a within-subject approach, the methodology analyzes multi-class MI data sourced from the BCI Competition IV Dataset 2A and the PhysioNet EEGMI dataset. The processing pipeline applies Independent Component Analysis (ICA) for artifact removal, selecting a single clean representative component for each subject for analysis. Data augmentation is applied to increase trial size and improve classifier generalization. Features are extracted across multiple domains, consisting of time-domain metrics, Wavelet Packet Decomposition (WPD) nodes, band ratios, and absolute and relative spectral power. Classification is performed using K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), Support Vector Machines (SVM), Linear Discriminant Analysis (LDA), and a hybrid deep learning model leveraging the combined strengths of EEGNet and DeepConvNet. The evaluation reveals that DE-SVM achieves the best overall performance on the BCI Competition dataset with an average accuracy of 93.48%, while GA-SVM emerges as the top performer on PhysioNet with an accuracy of 89.71%. Furthermore, an ablation study confirms that SVM is the top-performing classifier across both datasets with average accuracies of 88.29% (BCI Competition) and 90.26% (PhysioNet). Statistical analysis of these ablation results confirms that a universal feature set can be robustly utilized within an MI-BCI system. The findings demonstrate that fixed, generalized feature subsets can effectively replace dynamic subject-specific optimization, offering a streamlined pathway toward more efficient and scalable BCI deployment.

title: The impact of retirement on cognitive function of urban women under China's age-50 retirement policy: a fuzzy regression discontinuity study
container-title: Journal of Applied Economics and Policy Studies
48b0ea4b65a0c8c90f39ba49f81e0392c9f66172.abstract: Existing evidence on retirement and cognitive function is inconclusive. Thus, using five national waves (2011-2020) of the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS), this study examines urban female employees aged 45-65 covered by China's age-50 statutory retirement policy. A fuzzy regression discontinuity design uses the age-50 as an instrument for retirement. Accordingly, the identified Local Average Treatment Effect (LATE) applies primarily to urban women subject to the age-50 retirement rule, mainly blue-collar or non-managerial workers, rather than all urban women in China. At the cutoff, no statistically significant immediate net effect of retirement is observed on either mental intactness or episodic memory. Donut regression excluding individuals aged 50 shows a significant negative effect of retirement on mental intactness. This is consistent with a potential delayed manifestation. Therefore, a zero immediate net effect does not mean that retirement is entirely unrelated to cognition. However, because this study employs a pooled cross-sectional regression discontinuity design and does not track changes in the same individuals over time, these results should be interpreted cautiously.

title: Tracing memory suppression and transformation: interplay of cognitive, neural, and cultural dynamics
container-title: Frontiers in Psychology
cf9da9978f7844a301077d8c74a1d47b42f63b02.abstract: Episodic memory plays a fundamental role in shaping cognition, identity, and decision making, yet it is not a fixed record of past experiences and can be actively modified through various cognitive processes. What people remember about their own lives, and what they report to others, is shaped by processes that weaken, block, or displace competing traces. This narrative review integrates three related but distinct forms of forgetting: denial induced forgetting (DIF), retrieval induced forgetting (RIF), and suppression induced forgetting (SIF). For each, we summarize the behavioral evidence, the available neurophysiological markers, and the implications for criminological, clinical, and cultural questions. DIF, a comparatively recent phenomenon, shows that repeatedly denying details of an experienced event can undermine later memory for the interview in which the denial occurred, and sometimes for the event itself, yet it currently lacks direct neurophysiological evidence. RIF and SIF are better characterized in terms of neuro-electrophysiological activity, with converging work on prefrontal control, theta and alpha/beta oscillations, and hippocampal down-regulation. We propose that the three phenomena can be conceptualized along a continuum from incidental to intentional memory control, while recognizing that their underlying mechanisms may differ. Their forensic relevance lies in how testimony is elicited and evaluated, and cultural norms may shape when, how, and why people deny, selectively retrieve, or suppress memories. We close by identifying gaps in ecological validity, neural evidence for DIF, the separation of voluntary and involuntary control, and cross-cultural work, and by proposing multimodal, interdisciplinary research to address them.

title: Awareness of Generative AI Limitations and Students’ Intention to Use ChatGPT: A Moderated Mediation Analysis
container-title: Journal of Advanced Research in Education
6a29822b5091b20f84859c65b429b87a63d695ea.abstract: This research examined the importance of understanding generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) limitations in predicting college students’ likelihood of using ChatGPT, based on a modified Technology Acceptance Model. It treated awareness, perceived usefulness, and perceived anxiety about skills deterioration related to GenAI as independent variables, with intention to use ChatGPT as the dependent variable. The first-stage moderated mediation model was applied to analyze participants’ responses, with cooperation from 931 college students from different fields of study at a private higher education institution in the Philippines. The findings revealed that the awareness of GenAI limitations exerted a positive impact on the intention of college students to use ChatGPT, in particular, both its direct positive effect (c’ = 0.169, p < .001) and an indirect effect through the mediation of perceived usefulness. Conditional process analysis confirmed that skill-erosion concern moderated the relationship between awareness and perceived usefulness (moderated mediation index = -0.075, 95% CI [-0.107, -0.046]). Although perceived usefulness remained a significant mediator of the relationship between awareness and intention, the indirect effect diminished as skill-erosion concern increased, dropping from 0.233 for students with low-little concern to 0.105 for students with great concern. The collinearity analysis confirmed that the predictors were empirically distinguishable. The findings show that beliefs about risks regulate the technology acceptance process, and that AI-literacy training can be pursued alongside measured caution about dependency rather than treating these goals as alternatives.

title: Establishing the Construct of Storyboard Methodology: A Synthesis of Narrative Cognition, Cognitive Science, and Systematic Design
container-title: TechTrends
0afd2a8f4b046c4589bc935475af5c734b21861f.abstract: Abstract Storyboarding is widely used in instructional design, eLearning development, curriculum planning, and training; however, it is typically described as a tool, strategy, or framework rather than a formalized methodology. This conceptual article addresses that gap, establishing storyboard methodology as a disciplined, theory-informed, repeatable process for externalizing and testing instructional design coherence. Drawing on research in narrative cognition, cognitive load theory, multimedia learning, and systematic design, this paper articulates theoretical foundations of storyboard methodology, distinguishing it from flexible visual frameworks. A dual-component model, with story as narrative engine and board as visual architecture, is proposed, with four defined phases, fidelity indicators, and a practitioner-facing comparison framework. Illustrative applications in eLearning development, curriculum design, and doctoral research are described. The article identifies limitations and directions for empirical validation and offers implications for instructional designers and educational technologists.

title: The Instagram paradox: a mediation analysis of consumer orientations, psychological, cognitive and deep structure dimensions & Instagram motivations shaping purchase intention of sustainable apparel in India
container-title: Frontiers in Communication
db5447f15776071d77e5b42565da7bde6d900853.abstract: Introduction This study examines how distinctive consumer orientations - Thrifty, Frugal, Moral, and Shopper influence sustainable apparel purchase intention among Indian Instagram users. Grounded in Uses and Gratifications theory and the Theory of Planned Behaviour, the study examines the parallel mediating roles played by inherent psychological, cognitive and deep structures and external stimuli of Instagram motivation in rendering consumer orientation to purchase intention, thus presenting an empirical justification for the ‘Instagram Paradox’ in the framework of sustainable fashion. Methods A quantitative survey was administered to 285 Instagram users and followers of sustainable apparel brands in India, recruited via snowball sampling. Factor Analyses was conducted to validate constructs spanning consumer orientation, psychological, cognitive and deep structure dimensions, Instagram motivations, and purchase intention. Results K-means cluster analysis identified four distinct consumer orientation segments. Four parallel mediation models tested whether psychological, cognitive and deep structure dimensions along with Instagram motivation mediated the relationship between each consumer orientation and purchase intention. Discussion Across all the mediation models, psychological, cognitive and deep structure constructs emerged as the sole significant mediator, while Instagram motivation consistently failed to generate a significant indirect effect on purchase intention in any model, constituting the central empirical evidence for the Instagram Paradox.

title: The somato-cognitive action network in parkinsonian gait dysfunction and closed-loop neuromodulation
container-title: Frontiers in Aging Neuroscience
aaf80658979f6154e1f7d976a6361093c9482a3d.abstract: Parkinsonian gait dysfunction and freezing of gait (FoG) emerge from interactions among motor, cognitive-control and neuromodulatory systems. The somato-cognitive action network (SCAN) adds an anatomically defined cortical component to these distributed accounts. This narrative review examines its contribution across disease associations, targeted perturbation, state-contingent treatment, and incremental clinical value. SCAN-subcortical hyperconnectivity in Parkinson’s disease and its treatment sensitivity link inter-effector cortex to established disease circuits. A randomized comparison of individualized SCAN and effector-region intermittent theta-burst stimulation supports target-dependent improvement in total motor scores; FoG-specific efficacy remains unresolved because the axial outcome combined gait and non-gait items. In parallel, gait-phase and activity-dependent deep-brain stimulation demonstrate that neural signals can guide behaviorally timed treatment, with early benefits in selected gait outcomes. Across these accounts, neurochemical and distributed-network measures characterize vulnerability, while episode-linked decoupling identifies candidate state markers. SCAN contributes a more specific cortical hypothesis: transition-related activity in individually mapped SCAN may distinguish impending freezing beyond neighboring cortex and established gait signals. Cortical target selection and adaptive timing have separate empirical support; their combination is a proposed therapeutic strategy. Matched input and stimulation comparisons can determine whether SCAN adds predictive information or clinical benefit to existing controllers.

title: Does a moral injury framework enhance our understanding of OCD?
container-title: Behavioural and Cognitive Psychotherapy
ecbcfd6d2014012881351f8c0fd8781bfe899de1.abstract: Abstract Background: Obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD) is characterized by intrusive thoughts that are appraised as signalling harm, evoking distress and efforts to reduce distress and/or prevent harm. It has long been observed that obsessions often reflect moral themes and that many people with OCD experience strong moral emotions, particularly guilt and shame. Aims: Drawing on social functionalist models of moral emotions and the literature on moral injury (MI), we propose that in some people with OCD, symptoms can be conceptualized as an MI. Method: We reviewed leading theoretical models of OCD, moral emotions, and MI, and identified areas of overlap in phenomenology, development, and persistence. Results: When an obsessional thought is itself a moral transgression, and/or failure to resolve the obsessional concern via the compulsion is viewed as a moral transgression, it evokes moral emotions and threatens social standing, reputation, and trust. This increases the stake in avoiding the obsession and in ensuring the compulsion is done properly. Conclusions: The integration of moral injury concepts with established cognitive behavioral models may enhance case formulation, reduce treatment ambivalence, and support recovery processes that extend beyond symptom reduction to restoration of moral coherence and self-trust. Clinical implications are discussed.

title: Oxidative balance and cognitive function in Chinese older adults: the mediating role of plasma 25-hydroxyvitamin D
container-title: British Journal of Nutrition
bbb5defe82e4a2b4498c69db8528428242b14eef.abstract: Abstract Rapid global ageing is increasing the burden of cognitive impairment. Oxidative stress may contribute to cognitive decline, and the oxidative balance score (OBS), which integrates dietary and lifestyle pro- and antioxidants, has an unclear relationship with cognitive function in older adults. This study aimed to investigate the association between the OBS and cognitive function among older adults and to examine potential indirect pathways through circulating oxidative stress-related biomarkers. We used data from 1891 adults aged ≥60 years who participated in the 2011–2014 Chinese Longitudinal Healthy Longevity Survey. Cognitive function was assessed using the Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE). Oxidative stress markers, including albumin, superoxide dismutase, malondialdehyde and plasma 25-hydroxyvitamin D [25(OH)D], were measured at baseline and follow-up. Associations were examined using mixed-effects linear regression models and semi-longitudinal cross-lagged mediation analysis. The median cognitive score was 28 (interquartile range, 23–29). Each one-point higher OBS was associated with a 0·16-point higher MMSE score ( β = 0·16, 95 % CI 0·06 to 0·26), and participants in the highest OBS tertile had a 1·12-point higher MMSE score than those in the lowest tertile ( β = 1·12, 95 % CI 0·50 to 1·73). In mediation analysis, higher baseline OBS predicted lower plasma 25(OH)D at follow-up (path a = –1·015), and higher baseline 25(OH)D was associated with better cognitive scores at follow-up (path b = 0·025). The indirect effect of OBS on cognition through 25(OH)D was significant ( a × b = –0·025). OBS was positively associated with cognitive function, partially mediated by 25(OH)D. Further research is warranted to clarify these mechanisms and implications for cognitive aging.

title: The ontogeny of hippocampal spatial memory is supported by postnatal Cajal-Retzius cells
9cb8f44e4f984bb91b28effe3a49771aa4526c87.abstract: Abstract The functional capabilities of the adult hippocampus depend on specialized circuits that are established during development. Cajal–Retzius (CR) cells persist in the hippocampus long after their disappearance from the neocortex and contribute to the postnatal maturation of hippocampal circuits, but how this developmental role shapes adult hippocampal function remains unknown. Here, we selectively ablated CR cells from the postnatal hippocampus and examined the consequences for spatial learning, navigation, and CA1 spatial representations. CR-cell ablated animals learned reward locations and adapted to changing task conditions, but learned more slowly and made more errors. Reinforcement-learning models suggest that these behavioral differences reflect less stable internal representations guiding behavior. Consistent with this, CA1 spatial representations remained present but were more unstable and showed reduced differentiation of reward locations, particularly when task conditions changed. Our findings identify postnatal CR cells as key developmental contributors to the stability of hippocampal spatial representations and the adaptive behavior they support.

title: SaRoHead: Detecting Satire in a Multi-Domain Romanian News Headline Dataset
container-title: Big Data and Cognitive Computing
883082007e0bc8c33ac27e593fc1f76c12993446.abstract: News headlines mainly aim to summarize an event in a news article in a few words. Media outlets may use them either to summarize objectively or to attract attention. For the latter, they may employ stylistic devices such as sarcasm, irony, and exaggeration, the key elements of satire. Consequently, even a headline may reflect that tone. Romanian approaches typically detect non-conventional tones (i.e., satire and clickbait) by combining the article and the headline, so headline-only analysis remains largely unexplored. To address this gap, we introduce SaRoHead, a dataset of 20,676 Romanian news headlines spanning social, politics, and sports domains, and analyze satirical tone in headlines alone. We benchmark standard machine learning algorithms, transformer-based classifiers, and large language models (LLMs), each with five random seeds. Bidirectional transformer models outperform standard machine learning approaches. Among BERT-based settings, the meta-learning Reptile approach performs best (pooled F1 90.42 for Romanian BERT). LLMs struggle under few-shot in-context learning, but parameter-efficient fine-tuning makes them competitive, with LoRA RoGemma and RoLlama3 achieving the highest pooled F1-scores (92.7 and 92.0). Because all satirical headlines originate from a single outlet, we treat the reported scores as an upper bound and restrict our claims to this benchmark setting.

title: Usability and Acceptability of Digital Cognitive Behavioural Therapy for Insomnia (Sleepio) in People with Cognitive Impairment: A Mixed-Methods Study
container-title: Clocks & Sleep
835b4550810c150d77e92c6c47c7c4b9ed326c84.abstract: Insomnia and dementia are major public health issues. Although cognitive behavioural therapy for insomnia (CBT-I) is the recommended first line treatment for insomnia, few studies have examined its usability or effectiveness in people with cognitive impairment. Digital CBT-I (dCBT-I) is an effective and easily accessible alternative to CBT-I. We undertook a mixed-methods analysis of the usability and acceptability of dCBT-I (SleepioTM) in patients attending a memory clinic. Participants were community dwellers aged ≥50 years with insomnia (Sleep Condition Indicator score ≤ 16) and subjective cognitive decline (SCD), mild cognitive impairment (MCI) or dementia. The Mobile Device Proficiency Questionnaire (MDPQ) assessed digital literacy. The System Usability Score (SUS) and Usability Metric for User Experience–Lite (UMUX-Lite) assessed usability. Acceptability was assessed by analysing adherence to the intervention and subjective reports of perceived benefit. Both usability and acceptability were further explored in semi-structured interviews. Among 24 participants (median age 69; 17 females), 2 had SCD, 14 MCI, and 8 dementia. Overall response to SleepioTM was positive. Participants favoured relaxation-based aspects of the programme. Behavioural elements, such as sleep restriction, were generally less favoured. Lack of digital literacy was the main barrier to engagement, though this could be surmounted by assistance from caregivers or family members in certain instances. Regardless of cognitive status, those with above-average digital literacy (MDPQ > 20) undertook a median 6/6 sessions, while those with below-average digital literacy (MDPQ < 20) undertook a median 3/6 sessions. Among those with above-average digital literacy, median SUS and UMUX-Lite were 72.5 and 75, respectively, representing acceptable usability, while overall scores were 63.75 and 56.25, respectively, representing marginally acceptable usability. Our findings may suggest that SleepioTM is usable and acceptable for people with SCD, MCI and selected individuals with mild dementia, particularly where digital literacy is preserved. Additional caregiver support may facilitate usability among people with MCI and lower digital literacy. Usability appears limited in more advanced dementia. However, as some subgroups were small, more research is required to confirm these findings.

title: Progressive Resistance Exercise, Cognitive Performance and Circulating Biomarkers in Older Women Receiving Statins: A Randomized Comparison with an Additional Non-Randomized Exercise Group
container-title: Life
db7a5ed001feedd40a60f40a517cea41ffafae88.abstract: Evidence regarding the cognitive and circulating biomarker responses to progressive resistance exercise in older women receiving statins remains limited. This study examined cognitive performance in statin users assigned to exercise or no exercise and explored changes in biological markers. Forty-four sedentary older women completed the study. Statin users were randomly assigned to a statin-treated control group (ST; n = 14) or a statin-treated progressive resistance exercise group (STPE; n = 15). Non-statin users were recruited separately (NSPE; n = 15). The exercise groups trained three times weekly for eight weeks. Cognitive performance, pBDNF, and oxidative stress and antioxidant markers were assessed before and after the study period. Compared with ST, STPE showed more favorable changes in Stroop incongruent task completion time (p = 0.002), interference (p = 0.005), and combined incongruent and neutral task completion time (p = 0.018). Changes in Digit Span performance and the TMT-B/TMT-A ratio did not differ significantly between the randomized groups. In baseline-adjusted sensitivity analyses, the between-group difference remained statistically significant for interference (p = 0.029), but not for incongruent task completion time (p = 0.075) or combined task completion time (p = 0.151). pBDNF increased within both ST and STPE, while POX increased and total antioxidant capacity decreased within both groups. None of the biological markers, including catalase, showed a significant difference in change between ST and STPE, although catalase increased within NSPE. Progressive resistance exercise was associated with more favorable changes in selected Stroop measures among women receiving statins, without corresponding between-group differences in biological responses. These findings provide no evidence that increased circulating pBDNF contributed to the observed cognitive benefits. The sample size, multiple outcomes, and baseline differences warrant cautious interpretation and confirmation in larger trials.

title: COGNITIVE TRANSFORMATION OF METAPHORICAL MODELS IN THE TRANSLATION OF ELKE HEIDENREICH’S “EIN SENDER HAT GEBURTSTAG” AND “KARL, BOB DYLAN UND ICH”
container-title: Writings in Romance-Germanic Philology
0a66757a501cedddb17bc3a5a75fec3b72904a9d.abstract: This article examines how metaphorical expressions in two short stories by Elke Heidenreich from the collection Der Welt den Rücken, “Ein Sender hat Geburtstag” and “Karl, Bob Dylan und ich”, can be rendered in Ukrainian. It focuses on how the choice of a Ukrainian equivalent affects the figurative model, narrative perspective, and characterization. The study draws on the German texts and proposes Ukrainian renderings for analysis; these renderings are not quotations from a published translation. The method compares the contextual and basic meanings of figurative expressions, identifies their source and target domains, and examines their function within each episode. Translation choices are assessed according to whether they retain or alter an image, how much they make explicit, and how they affect irony or a speaker’s emotional voice. Metaphorical usage, biblical allusion, and literal references to space are distinguished. The analysis of a promotional slogan shows how the contrast between a promise of accessibility and restricted physical access creates irony without turning the literal scene into a further metaphor. In “Karl, Bob Dylan und ich”, images of decline, bodily injury, the boundary of the home, and light connect experiences of loss with the possibility of closeness. Translating them requires attention to their recurrence across episodes, rather than to isolated expressions alone. In “Ein Sender hat Geburtstag”, metaphors of conflict and rapid consumption contribute to a satirical portrayal of a media institution, while the editor’s assessment does not always coincide with the narrator’s perspective. The analysis suggests that a familiar Ukrainian idiom may preserve a conceptual relationship while weakening an individual speaker’s register. An explanatory rendering, in turn, may improve clarity at the expense of concision. The findings concern selected examples and proposed translations; they establish neither the frequency of metaphors in the collection nor the strategies of a published translator.

title: TRANSLATION OF ETYMOLOGICAL CALQUES IN MACHINE TRANSLATION SERVICES GOOGLE TRANSLATE, DEEPL, CHATGPT
container-title: Writings in Romance-Germanic Philology
f5bc3fa7ff9f1f03b78b9696233e72855bc2c7ae.abstract: This article addresses the issue of translating etymological loan translations (calques) using machine translation services. The object of the study is the process of machine translation of etymological calques by contemporary automated translation systems. The subject of the research is the analysis of the methods used to render etymological calques in machine translation systems. The primary aim of the study is to examine the translation of 200 sentences using the machine translation services DeepL, ChatGPT, and Google Translate and to identify the errors made by these systems in translating etymological calques. The study clarifies the concepts of calque and literal translation, characterizes the operating principles of machine translation services, compiles a corpus of etymological calques for comparative analysis, conduct a comparative evaluation of translations produced by DeepL, Google Translate, and ChatGPT, and identifies the most common translation errors and difficulties with rendering etymological calques. The findings indicate that all three systems demonstrated a relatively high level of translation accuracy. ChatGPT achieved the highest performance, producing 164 correct translations out of 200, which suggests a superior ability to account for contextual and semantic nuances. Google Translate ranked second, while DeepL showed a slightly lower result, with 146 correct translations. None of the systems achieved perfect accuracy. The number of translation errors amounted to 36 for ChatGPT, 45 for Google, and 54 for DeepL. The analysis demonstrates that, despite the considerable progress made in modern machine translation technologies, the adequate rendering of etymological calques remains a challenging task. All of the selected services employ algorithms capable of recognizing context and reducing the likelihood of overly literal translation. Nevertheless, the overall quality of translation depends on the complexity of the expression, the context, and the availability of relevant training corpora. The results confirm that machine translation cannot fully replace human post-editing, particularly in the translation of phraseological units, idioms and culturally specific expressions as well as calques.

title: Ant-Colony-Inspired Dwell Memory for Traffic-Aware Idle Repositioning in Multi-Agent Pickup and Delivery
container-title: Biomimetics
f96657f5d29edf69317eb21a053dc033073de28d.abstract: In lifelong Multi-Agent Pickup and Delivery (MAPD), an agent that has just delivered must occupy some cell while it waits, and that cell fixes the distance to its next pickup; current solvers leave the choice to the path planner as a by-product. The choice is cheap to optimise—given estimated demand it is a weighted 1-median, solvable in polynomial time—but its myopic solution is collectively poor: the best cell for one agent lies on the corridor that loaded traffic must cross, so agents that each decide well obstruct one another, and more accurate demand prediction sharpens the convergence rather than relieving it. An ant colony meets the same difficulty when a trail crowds, and resolves it through a medium that is shared, that evaporates, and that is written by events in the world rather than by the individuals reading it, so that acting on it cannot corrupt it. This paper isolates idle repositioning as a third decision layer, below task assignment and space–time path finding, and equips it with such a medium: a single decaying field of task-arrival intensity, written by releases alone and called the dwell memory, which drives a weighted 1-median in which every candidate cell also carries a price, computed once and offline from the map, for the loaded traffic it intercepts. Decay is adapted online, and a bounded reachability filter whose fallback scans the admissible free cells restores the reachability invariant whenever the fleet’s own occupancy has not already broken it—exactly, at fleets up to sixteen agents, and with a residual below 0.06 of decisions up to thirty-two. Across nine layouts and 8499 runs, with assignment and path finding untouched, mean service time falls by up to 32: the gain accrues to the response leg rather than to the delivery leg, demand memory and the structural price dominate opposite ends of the fleet-size range instead of accumulating, and the boundary of the effect tracks idle time rather than map size. The operating envelope is part of the result rather than an omission: nothing is gained below about 10 idle time, where no agent has an interval in which to move, and the layer loses in one of the twenty-four scale cells—the largest fleet on the densest benchmark map, at 74 idle—by 24.3 , through a planner-congestion channel that the structural price does not cover.

title: Evaluation of Plasma Soluble CD 40 Ligand (sCD40L) Levels as a Biomarker for Autism Spectrum Disorder: A Link to the Severity of Cognitive, Social, and Sensory Dysfunctions
container-title: Journal of Clinical Medicine
fda7011b3c088be642724da3548111b76e4a79ef.abstract: Background: Soluble CD40 ligand (sCD40L) plays an important role in inflammation and autoimmune disorders, including a variety of neurological and neurodegenerative disorders. However, evidence regarding the role of sCD40L in autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is limited. Therefore, the aim of this study was to assess the clinical significance of plasma sCD40L levels in individuals with ASD and to examine their relationship with the severity of ASD, social impairments, and sensory dysfunction. Materials and Methods: Plasma levels of sCD40L were measured using an enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA). The severity of ASD, social impairments, and sensory dysfunction was assessed in all children with ASD using the Childhood Autism Rating Scale (CARS), the Social Responsiveness Scale (SRS), and the Short Sensory Profile (SSP), respectively. Results: Plasma sCD40L levels were significantly increased in children with ASD (83.77 ± 24.76) compared with controls (68.28 ± 12.74), with p = 0.001. Plasma sCD40L levels were significantly higher in children with severe ASD-related symptoms. The mean sCD40L levels were 87.23 ± 20.93 among children with severe ASD according to the CARS, 86.45 ± 25.53 among those with greater social impairment according to the SRS, and 89.74 ± 27.22 among those with atypical sensory processing according to the SSP (p ≤ 0.05). These results indicate that sCD40L levels increased with greater severity of the symptoms. Additionally, receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis revealed significant discriminatory ability of plasma sCD40L between the two groups, with an AUC of 0.701 [95% confidence interval (CI), 0.583–0.819, p < 0.001]. Conclusions: Our study suggests that sCD40L may contribute to the pathophysiology of ASD and be associated with the severity of ASD symptoms. This association suggests that sCD40L may serve as a promising biomarker for neuroinflammatory processes associated with ASD. However, further studies with larger sample sizes are warranted to validate these findings.

title: Visuospatial orienting in working memory is preserved in adults with ADHD symptoms
container-title: Psychological Research
02ce9c60f79cc1d8e31f66ee14414b8452c80634.abstract: Abstract People with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) are reported to have pervasive deficits in working memory (WM), yet mechanistic explanations for such deficits are lacking. Research suggests that attentional mechanisms such as reward-based prioritisation and visuospatial orienting are intact in this population (Atkinson et al., 2025; Superbia-Guimarães et al., 2022, 2023). To further examine these mechanisms, we investigated the hypotheses that deficient visuospatial orienting during encoding and maintenance are at the root of WM deficits in adults with ADHD symptoms. Eighty-four symptomatic participants ( M age = 28.4 years, SD = 4.6) and 107 controls ( M age = 29.4, SD = 4.4) had their symptoms assessed with the Adult ADHD Self-Report Scale. They each took part in one of two experiments involving an item (colour or unfamiliar shape) recognition memory task that incorporated pre- and retro-cues. Across both experiments, we found strong evidence of beneficial pre- and retro-cueing effects upon memory accuracy and reaction time (RT). However, we found no evidence for the expected group differences nor the interaction between symptom status and cueing condition. There was also no evidence for correlations between ADHD symptom scores, recognition accuracy, RT, and cueing benefits. Therefore, failure in attentional orienting is unlikely to explain deficits in WM in individuals with symptoms of ADHD.

title: Brain Decoding from a Deep Neural Network of Visual Memory Reveals the Maturation Trajectory of Memory Systems across Ages 3-7
e9c79b60ccd3b557066dc11fa1ec85733ce37f62.abstract: Abstract Memories from the first four years of life are largely inaccessible by adulthood, yet these early experiences profoundly shape cognition throughout development. Understanding this phenomenon of infantile amnesia is critical for revealing the mechanisms of early memory development. Here, we developed a new content-based behavioral measure of memory that quantifies how closely children’s memory patterns resemble those of adults, which we term the memory maturation score . Using a movie-watching fMRI dataset spanning age 3 to adulthood, we trained a cross-validated model on adults’ movie-evoked brain activity to predict adult’s propensity to remember each movie snippet, estimated by ResMem, a deep neural network trained to predict visual memorability. We then applied the model to each child’s brain activity while viewing the same movie to assess their memory maturation (i.e., cross-decodability from adult patterns). Children exhibited adult-like neural patterns of memory around age 4, extending prior behavioral findings. Structural analyses showed that the volume of the left posterior hippocampus, but not age or total brain volume, significantly predicted children’s memory maturation. Memory maturation around age 4 thus likely reflects age-related neural development of hippocampal memory systems, rather than an age increase itself. Functional searchlight analyses revealed a trajectory of memory maturation: the inferior temporal gyrus reflected mature memory-related processing from age 3 onward, the left posterior hippocampus by age 5, and higher-order regions involved in social-affective processing and multimodal integration by age 7. Together, these findings suggest that hippocampal maturation between ages 3 and 5 drives the maturation of memory patterns. Significance Statement Despite decades of research establishing potential mechanisms of infantile amnesia, little is known about the maturation of neural memory representations across development, limiting progress in developmental memory research and educational applications. This study reveals a developmental trajectory of memory: children show adult-like processing in the IT area by age 3, the hippocampus by age 5, and higher-order regions by age 7, reflecting mature perceptual, memory, and multimodal and social-affective processing, respectively. The left posterior hippocampus is crucial for the maturation of adult-like memory patterns. These findings show that (i) ResMem DNN can help educators select dynamic stimuli that are memorable to children by age 4, and (ii) our cross-validated model enables assessment of memory maturation without explicit memory measures.

title: Effects of Increased and Decreased Cognitive Social Capital on Depressive Symptoms Along the Income Gradient During the COVID-19 Pandemic: Evidence from Asymmetric Fixed-Effects Models
container-title: International Journal of Disaster Risk Science
32a4283e0707a74d0921051dc07fac02e06d7a98.abstract: Abstract Social capital is considered to protect health when facing natural hazard-related disasters and pandemics. We further differentiated the effects of increased and decreased cognitive social capital (measured using generalized trust, trust in neighbors, trust in local government officials, and reciprocity) on depressive symptoms in the context of the COVID-19 pandemic and examined the moderating effect of household income on these effects, while controlling for unobserved time-invariant factors. Using follow-up data from the 2018 and 2020 China Family Panel Studies (N = 14,908), we conducted asymmetric fixed-effects regression. We found that decreased generalized trust and decreased reciprocity were associated with greater depressive symptoms, whereas their increased components were not associated with depressive symptoms. Furthermore, decreased equivalized household income exacerbated the effect of decreased reciprocity on greater depressive symptoms. Therefore, attention should be paid to preventing cognitive social capital decline to safeguard mental health during a pandemic, especially for people with declining household income. Future studies and policies should consider the distinct health effects of increased and decreased social capital when facing a pandemic.

title: From chronic airway injury to lung cancer: epithelial memory, field cancerization, and premalignant evolution
container-title: Frontiers in Oncology
a5753e1208e3654a0dd27f19c4d19c762627eaad.abstract: Chronic airway injury induced by tobacco smoke, environmental pollutants, and persistent inflammatory lung diseases provides a biological foundation for lung carcinogenesis, yet the cellular and molecular trajectory from repeated epithelial damage to invasive malignancy has only recently come into focus. Here we synthesize three interconnected concepts that together define this trajectory: epithelial memory, the capacity of airway basal and secretory cells to retain epigenetic and transcriptional scars long after the initial insult has ceased; field cancerization, whereby histologically normal-appearing airway epithelium harbours widespread clonal alterations that expand the pool of at-risk cells; and premalignant evolution, the Darwinian selection and diversification of clones as genetic, epigenetic, immune, and metabolic pressures reshape the altered field. We review evidence from single-cell genomics, spatial transcriptomics, and longitudinal human cohort studies that reveals how smoking-associated DNA methylation marks, persistent chromatin accessibility changes, and rewired transcriptional programmes establish an epigenetically primed epithelial landscape. Within this landscape, somatic driver mutations in TP53, KRAS, NOTCH1, and chromatin remodelling genes confer competitive fitness advantages, enabling clonal expansion across large territories of the bronchial tree. We propose an integrative model in which epigenetic priming, somatic mutation, clonal competition, immune surveillance, and metabolic constraints interact over years to decades, without assuming a universal fixed sequence across all lung cancer subtypes. This framework identifies actionable interception windows — from epigenetic reversal of injury memory to targeted elimination of premalignant clones — and highlights the need for longitudinal single-cell atlases and lineage-resolved models to resolve the causal ordering of molecular events. We conclude that lung cancer is best understood not as an abrupt cellular transformation but as the end point of a protracted, spatially distributed evolutionary process whose earliest stages may be reversible.

title: Modeling and simulation enabling concept development and experimentation applied to cognitive warfare concept validation
container-title: The Journal of Defense Modeling and Simulation: Applications, Methodology, Technology
c6e524b842bd599ffdc80c5e83289f854f5b07dd.abstract: North Atlantic treaty organization (NATO) considers Cognitive Warfare to be deliberate, synchronized military and non-military activities throughout the continuum of competition designed to shape the Information Environment and affect audience attitudes, perceptions and behaviors to gain, maintain and protect cognitive superiority. A validation project, conducted with Headquarters Supreme Allied Commander Transformation Modelling and Simulation, explored how modeling and simulation could enhance NATO’s capabilities in the cognitive domain, strengthen defense against cognitive warfare threats, and improve resilience to such activities, delivering an agent-based simulation system, built on human behavior models, that validated key Cognitive Warfare concept elements. This paper presents the project’s design, execution, findings, and resulting recommendations and lessons learned on applying Modeling and Simulation within concept development and experimentation (CD&E). Simulation results underscore the centrality of Training to operational readiness: robust training programs improve individual and group performance and support the Cognitive Warfare Concept’s Protect Supporting Idea. Motivation likewise had a marked positive effect on readiness and effectiveness; its interplay with Training emerged as a key determinant of Blue Force success, with compounded effects when combined. The main lessons learned from Modeling and Simulation employment in concept development are that, despite a recommended process, each concept’s unique nature means Modeling and Simulation use must be tailored to best fit the concept stakeholders’ needs.

title: Closing the Gap in Early Mathematics: Domain and Cognitive Insights from TIMSS 2023 in South Africa and Singapore
container-title: F1000Research
a903669e4efe33ec14be99ae129c4679b2710a39.abstract: Background South Africa continues to underperform in primary mathematics, yet overall mean comparisons obscure the distribution of achievement differences across mathematics content and cognitive domains. This study examines domain-specific patterns of mathematics achievement using data from the Trends in International Mathematics and Science Study (TIMSS) 2023, benchmarking South African Grade 5 learners against Singaporean Grade 4 learners assessed on the same TIMSS Grade 4 mathematics framework. Methods A quantitative secondary analysis was conducted using nationally representative TIMSS 2023 datasets comprising 10,424 South African learners from 285 schools and 6,530 Singaporean learners from 181 schools. South Africa assessed Grade 5 learners using the TIMSS Grade 4 mathematics instruments, reflecting its approach of assessing learners at a higher grade to achieve a closer match between TIMSS content and national curriculum coverage. Mathematics achievement was analysed across content domains (Number, Measurement and Geometry, Data) and cognitive domains (Knowing, Applying, Reasoning). Weighted estimates, replicate-based variance estimation, and effect sizes (Cohen’s .) were computed in accordance with IEA technical guidelines. The analysis is descriptive and comparative rather than causal. Results South African learners performed substantially below the international centre point across all domains. The largest content-domain gap relative to Singapore was observed in Measurement and Geometry, while the largest cognitive-domain gap occurred in Knowing. Although Applying was relatively stronger within the South African profile, it remained substantially below benchmark levels. Substantial achievement differences were evident across all content and cognitive domains, with the largest descriptive differences observed in Measurement and Geometry and Knowing. Conclusions Substantial achievement differences were evident across all mathematics content and cognitive domains, with comparatively larger differences observed in Measurement and Geometry and Knowing. The results provide a structured diagnostic profile of domain-specific achievement disparities, highlighting variation across mathematics content and cognitive domains.

title: How do senior software engineers learn soft skills? A narrative study based on social cognitive theory
container-title: Empirical Software Engineering
fe9f4efc34a740df8f1dd665453936756df0a694.abstract: Abstract Soft skills are critical to effective software engineering, yet limited empirical understanding exists of how experienced practitioners retrospectively make sense of their learning and development. This study examines how Senior Software Engineers (SSEs) interpret these processes through the lens of Social Cognitive Theory (SCT). We conducted episodic narrative interviews with 28 SSEs across diverse organizational contexts and analyzed their accounts through theory-informed reflexive thematic analysis, using six SCT constructs as interpretive lenses. Our analysis showed that soft skills are often developed not through formal training, but through situated practice (such as mentoring, conflict management, and leadership transitions) typically shaped by contextual demands or turning points. Participants also described learning as a socially embedded and dynamic process involving observation, reflection, and adaptation. This work (i) strengthens the empirical basis for understanding soft skills in software engineering by illustrating how SCT constructs manifest in practice, (ii) identifies distinct developmental pathways of soft skills growth, including modeling, reinforcement, and mastery through progressive roles, and (iii) demonstrates how organizational and sociotechnical contexts create affordances and constraints that shape which soft skills can be learned, practiced, and sustained.

title: Immune cells and inflammation as mechanisms underlying cognitive dysfunction and Alzheimer’s disease–related dementia
container-title: Frontiers in Aging Neuroscience
b9630e489beb75acb670b869c8d6b2616a94b4d8.abstract: Alzheimer’s disease-related dementias (ADRD) are progressive neurodegenerative disorders and the most common cause of dementia worldwide. Despite extensive research into their underlying molecular and cellular mechanisms, therapeutic options remain limited. Current pharmacological treatments offer only modest symptomatic relief and may slow progression in early stages. More recently, anti-amyloid monoclonal antibodies, including aducanumab and donanemab, have been developed to target amyloid-β pathology; however, their clinical benefits remain limited, with marginal effects on progression primarily in prodromal Alzheimer’s disease (AD). These outcomes have prompted a shift toward identifying disease modifying strategies beyond amyloid accumulation. Neuroinflammation and immune dysregulation have emerged as critical contributors to ADRD pathogenesis. Resident central nervous system (CNS) immune cells, such as microglia and astrocytes, along with peripheral immune cells drive disease initiation and progression through sustained inflammatory signaling, altered immune surveillance, and impaired clearance of pathological proteins. Furthermore, neurovascular unit dysfunction, including blood–brain barrier breakdown and vascular inflammation, further exacerbates immune cell infiltration, promotes neuroinflammatory cascades, and accelerates neuronal injury. This review examines molecular and cellular mechanisms that may independently or synergistically interact with established ADRD risk factors to influence disease onset, severity, and progression. These mechanisms include peripheral immune cell signaling and CNS infiltration, neurovascular dysfunction, microglial activation, astrocyte reactivity, and increased BBB permeability. Multiple inflammatory cytokines and signaling pathways, including IL-1β, IL-6, and NLRP3, represent potential modifiable therapeutic targets. Although FDA approved IL 6 and IL 1 inhibitors could be repurposed for ADRD, their involvement in complex CNS and systemic processes may limit their use. Clarifying these interconnected pathways may advance our understanding of ADRD pathophysiology and support development of neuroimmune and neurovascular disease modifying therapies before substantial amyloid accumulation.

title: White matter hyperintensity burden and post-stroke cognitive impairment: a systematic review and meta-analysis of clinically comparable estimates
container-title: Frontiers in Aging Neuroscience
7e9290c1a23564696c2215ebb09581fa79910e48.abstract: Introduction White matter hyperintensity (WMH) burden is a common marker of cerebral small vessel disease and may identify stroke survivors with reduced cognitive reserve. Published estimates, however, use different imaging thresholds, cognitive definitions, follow-up periods, and effect measures. Methods We searched PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Web of Science Core Collection, and the Cochrane Library from database inception through 13 August 2026. We defined a principal clinically comparable estimand as an adjusted odds ratio comparing high/pathological WMH or white matter lesion burden with lower/normal burden for categorical post-stroke cognitive impairment. Ordinal, volumetric, regional, dementia-specific, and time-to-event estimates were retained in separate evidence strata. The protocol was registered on 16 April 2026 in PROSPERO (CRD420261367226). Results Twenty-one studies were included. Four studies contributed to the principal synthesis, which yielded an adjusted odds ratio of 2.87 (95% confidence interval 2.10–3.92; I 2 = 0%; τ 2 = 0; Q = 0.85). The modified Hartung–Knapp 95% confidence interval was 1.73–4.75, and leave-one-out estimates ranged from 2.72 to 3.10. Broader dichotomous, score-based, volumetric, vascular-dementia-specific, and time-to-event findings were directionally supportive but were not pooled with the principal estimand. Conclusion High/pathological WMH burden was associated with higher odds of post-stroke cognitive impairment in a small set of clinically comparable adjusted studies. WMH may help identify cognitive vulnerability after stroke, but current evidence does not support WMH as a causal factor or stand-alone prognostic test. Systematic review registration PROSPERO , CRD420261367226.

title: A cognitive mathematical modeling method for comparing stacked bar graphs in descriptive visual data science
container-title: Information Visualization
8504ebc4f40b1f0a6244944135e808721dbcbe41.abstract: A great deal of research in data science has been devoted to data visualization techniques but not to their effectiveness from a perceptual, and more generally, cognitive standpoint. This is important because the way that human observers perceive and judge the graphic representation of numerical data can ultimately determine its interpretation. As proof of concept, we introduce and test a quantitative method for replacing human judges in the comparative assessment of simple stacked bar graphs (SBGs). As suggested, the method involves the application of Shepard’s similarity assessment model, a well-known cognitive mathematical model which determines similarities between exemplars as a function of their distance in psychological space. In addition, the method involves a simple technique for transforming each SBG into an appropriate representation that makes the application of the model possible and a cognitively meaningful method for scaling the representation. Specifically, the method assumes that humans form a psychological distance baseline (computed as a median or a mean across the SBGs) as the basis for scaling the representation. The effectiveness of the method was tested with an experiment on similarity judgments between SBGs. Results indicate that our method effectively predicts people’s similarity judgments with respect to pairs of SBGs ( r 2 = 0.88, p < 0.001). Bootstrapping tests confirmed the stability of the model fit. Among other applications, this method may be used to replace human judges with AI agents in situations where researchers wish to determine how well a SBG representing quantitative predictions from some model reflects the proportional distribution of the SBG representing the empirical data. The method also contributes to the automated quantitative interpretation of visual data in ways that are consistent with the perception of proportional visual relations by humans. Such automation may eventually find wide applications in the interpretation of visual data by AI agents, model evaluation, and UX design.

title: “Effectiveness of Combination with Motivational Interviewing and Integrated with Cognitive Behavioral Therapy on Clinical and Functional Outcomes in Substance Use: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis”

858ddb1bc007f4a551916e4f11cc0de44f2f7da2.abstract: Introduction: Cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) and motivational interviewing (MI) are two common psychosocial therapies for substance use disorders (SUDs). Objectives: We aimed to synthesize the efficacy of in combination MI with CBT for the treatment of drug abuse. Methods: A systematic review and meta-analysis were carried out using the PRISMA standards. From the beginning of PubMed until January 2026, searches were conducted using the Cochrane Library, Scopus, and Web of Science. The results included the identification test for alcohol use disorders, relapse rate, global evaluation of functioning scale score, and syndrome scale score.

title: Mechanisms of impaired cerebral hemodynamics and memory resilience differ by sex: A role for mineralocorticoid receptors in VCID
811130b88a0712cc6bafae208ee48c832cfe6f6f.abstract: Abstract INTRODUCTION Chronic hypertension is associated with cerebral hypoperfusion and is a primary risk factor for vascular contributions to cognitive impairment and dementia (VCID). Aldosterone, a key mediator of hypertension, causes cerebrovascular dysfunction via its mineralocorticoid receptor (MR). METHODS The effects of MR signaling during hypertension on hemodynamics in two cognition-centric brain regions were determined in both sexes using an established model of VCID (spontaneously hypertensive rat, SHR) and MR antagonist eplerenone. Long-term and spatial working memory were tested, and absolute brain blood flow and brain oxygenation were measured in vivo in CA1 of dorsal hippocampus and medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC). RESULTS: Hypertension differentially impaired hemodynamics in a sex- and region-dependent manner. Female SHR had more pervasive hypoperfusion than males that did not affect flow-metabolism coupling. Eplerenone treatment in females restored perfusion in mPFC and hippocampus, improved working memory, but did not protect hippocampal-dependent memory. Eplerenone had no effect in male SHR, indicating the MR-dependent mechanism of VCID is sex-specific. DISCUSSION This study advances our understanding of how chronic hypertension compromises brain blood flow, suggests that resilience of memory function differs by domain, and that efficacy of interventions depend upon sex.

title: Exploring Media Students’ Engagement with Digital Libraries and Cognitive Outcomes
container-title: Middle East Journal of Communication Studies
dc21aae4a3e8c700f6fb2341286c89dbd9d15cc2.abstract: The study examines the use of digital libraries by media students in Iraq for academic and reference purposes. It focuses on digital libraries available through the applications Facebook and Telegram that specialize in communication and media sciences. The research sample consists of randomly selected students from various media departments, including Radio and Television, Public Relations, and Journalism. The study adopts the descriptive method, which is one of the most used approaches in media research, to measure the extent to which media students use digital libraries on Facebook and, Telegram and to identify the cognitive gratifications achieved through this use. The study was applied to a random sample of 250 respondents from different departments using a questionnaire distributed to the participants. The researchers concluded that textbooks on media research methodologies and communication theories are the most needed sources for media students, representing 63% of the total sample. In addition, the “College of Media / University of Baghdad Library” on Telegram was found to be the most beneficial resource according to 71% of respondents. Meanwhile, the “Media Library” on Facebook ranked first among Facebook-based libraries, with 82% of respondents indicating its usefulness. Furthermore, the results revealed that 59% of supervisors guide their students toward digital libraries, while the actual source-based benefit gained by the student sample reached 67% during the preparation of their research at various academic levels

title: Understanding Audiovisual Affective Processing: Behavioral Effects and Neural Underpinnings
container-title: Social Cognitive and Affective Neuroscience
0a9ccbd4f6fb698d4a09cb9d606b7065b6316d0b.abstract: Abstract Emotional signals are typically conveyed jointly through vision and audition. This article reviews behavioral, electrophysiological, and neuroimaging evidence on audiovisual affective processing, addressing what its core effects are, when they unfold, and where they occur in the brain. Congruent audiovisual cues often facilitate emotion recognition, although benefits vary across emotions, tasks, measures, and unimodal comparisons. Audiovisual input can also shape affective appraisals and subjective emotional experience. Modality dominance is context-dependent, varying with cue reliability and the affective dimension judged. Cross-modal influences can persist when one modality is task-irrelevant, suggesting limited goal dependence. Electrophysiological findings reveal audiovisual affective interactions at both early and later stages of neural processing. Neuroimaging work implicates posterior superior temporal cortex (pSTC) within a distributed network of sensory, subcortical, and frontal regions. Building on this evidence, we consider Anderson's information integration theory as a computational framework for characterizing modality-related and value-dependent contributions to affective judgments. We propose a hypothesis-generating dual-pathway framework predicting that reliability-related changes in cue influence will covary with sensory-pSTC interactions, whereas value-dependent changes will additionally involve amygdala and prefrontal systems. These hypotheses concern relative rather than exclusive network contributions and require direct testing through independent manipulations of cue reliability and affective value.

title: Operationalizing Cognitive Frailty: A Systematic Review of Definitions, Tools, and Measurement Inconsistencies
container-title: The Gerontologist
4043d4a0dc391a7e95940afd50bc7ecc72ae715e.abstract: Abstract Background and Objectives Cognitive frailty (CF), the co-occurrence of physical frailty and cognitive impairment without dementia, is a potentially reversible condition associated with adverse outcomes in older adults. However, heterogeneity in operational definitions and measurement approaches limits comparability and clinical translation. This review examined how CF has been defined and operationalized, including adaptations to established criteria. Research Design and Methods PubMed, Web of Science, and PsycINFO were searched for English-language studies published from 2013 through 2025. Eligible studies explicitly referred to CF in adults aged 50 years or older. Risk of bias was assessed using Joanna Briggs Institute tools. Definitions, assessment tools, thresholds, and operational criteria were synthesized descriptively. Fried Phenotype (FP) implementation was examined using an adaptation-equivalence typology classifying domain-level measurement and threshold deviations. Results Among 257 studies, 13 frailty and 26 cognitive assessment tools were identified. The FP was predominantly utilized (n = 164/257; 64%), although 68% (n = 112/164) modified the measurement method, threshold, or both in at least one domain. The Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) and Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA) thresholds used to define cognitive impairment varied substantially, whereas all studies using the Clinical Dementia Rating (CDR) used a threshold of 0.5. Dementia was not explicitly excluded in 50 studies, despite its exclusion being a defining criterion of CF. Discussion and Implications CF remains operationally heterogeneous. Updated international consensus and minimum reporting standards are needed to clarify core criteria and acceptable adaptations. FP-based studies should explicitly report domain-level modifications to improve comparability, reproducibility, and evidence synthesis.

title: Association of Cerebral Arteriosclerosis with Premortem Dementia Severity across Braak Stages
container-title: Dementia and Geriatric Cognitive Disorders
42d5c3e5dfa8db645407a2316baa247af22e90f2.abstract: Abstract Introduction: Cerebrovascular pathology often coexists with Alzheimer’s disease neuropathologic change, but the association between cerebral arteriosclerosis and dementia severity may vary with neurofibrillary pathology. We examined this association across Braak stages in a large autopsy cohort. Methods: We included 7,701 autopsy participants with cerebral arteriosclerosis ratings, Braak stage, and premortem Clinical Dementia Rating Sum of Boxes (CDR-SB). Multivariable linear regression estimated associations between moderate/severe versus none/mild arteriosclerosis and CDR-SB within Braak 0–II, III–IV, and V–VI strata, adjusting for demographic, genetic, and neuropathologic covariates. Interaction and sensitivity analyses were performed. Results: Moderate/severe arteriosclerosis was present in 3,494 participants (45.4%). Its association with higher CDR-SB was strongest at Braak 0–II (β = 1.56, 95% CI 0.98 to 2.14, p &lt; 0.001), weaker at III–IV (β = 0.89, 95% CI 0.33 to 1.45, p = 0.002), and not statistically significant at V–VI (β = 0.22, 95% CI −0.14 to 0.58, p = 0.223). The V–VI versus 0–II interaction contrast was significant (p = 0.029), but the joint 3-level interaction test was not (2 df; p = 0.085). The V–VI confidence interval remained compatible with a modest positive association. Low-Braak findings were consistent across sensitivity analyses. Conclusion: Moderate/severe cerebral arteriosclerosis was associated with greater premortem dementia severity, primarily among participants with low Braak stage, with attenuation at higher Braak stages. These findings suggest that the clinicopathologic relevance of cerebral arteriosclerosis may be more apparent when Alzheimer-type neurofibrillary pathology is limited.

title: How Habitual Language Mode Shapes Self-Stigma Perception Process in Deaf Individuals: Evidence from an Event-Related Potentials Study
container-title: Social Cognitive and Affective Neuroscience
dca3cbd13a47df0bc861055e35961c1bb05a02e3.abstract: Abstract Deaf individuals often experience public stigma from the hearing majority due to communication barriers, which may further evolve into internalized self-stigma. However, how habitual language mode shapes self-stigma-related processing remains unclear. In the present study, 20 signing deaf and 21 oral deaf individuals completed a semantic priming task while event-related potentials (ERPs) were recorded. Deaf-identity (“I am deaf”) primes were presented subliminally or supraliminally before positive and negative trait words. Among oral deaf participants, negative words elicited a larger N400 than positive words under supraliminal priming, while a negative-over-positive LPC effect emerged in the no-priming and subliminal conditions but disappeared under supraliminal priming. Signing deaf participants showed no N400 valence effect but exhibited a negative-over-positive LPC effect across all conditions. These findings provide no clear evidence of self-stigma in either group. Instead, they suggest that habitual language mode and conscious accessibility of deaf identity jointly shape the temporal dynamics of self-evaluative processing, potentially reflecting different ways of resisting the internalization of negative societal evaluations. Signing deaf individuals may derive protection from a culturally and collectively grounded Deaf identity, whereas oral deaf individuals may rely more on individualized, self-protective processing to prevent negative evaluations from being incorporated into the self.

title: Targeting cognitive control and affective processing in aggression: neuromodulation approaches in CRC/TRR 379
Kognitive Kontrolle und affektive Verarbeitung bei Aggression: Neuromodulationsansätze im CRC/TRR379
container-title: Der Nervenarzt
137a30da113d4033fcac6309e253dd0eec3173e7.abstract: Abstract Interventions aimed at reducing aggression in mental disorders remain insufficiently addressed by current research, despite the substantial individual and societal burden associated with aggressive behavior. Consequently, strategies for modulating aggressive behavior are of high clinical relevance but are not yet adequately represented in the currently available intervention approaches. The Collaborative Research Center (CRC) TRR 379 is dedicated to exploring the modulation of aggressive behavior through neuromodulation. Four projects employ complementary methodologies to investigate whether neural systems involved in cognitive control and affect regulation can be modulated to reduce aggressive behavior in patients with mental disorders and violent offenders. These techniques include transcranial direct current stimulation, low-intensity focused transcranial ultrasound stimulation, and real-time functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) neurofeedback. Through these multimodal approaches, the projects aim to advance the understanding of the modifiability of aggressive behavior, identify factors that contribute to successful neuromodulation, and support the development of individualized interventions.

title: Industrial Product Surface Defect Detection via Memory-Bank Feature Matching and Lightweight Diffusion Reconstruction
container-title: Processes
4c86a4e1d57c8474e68e3077232d71c2b502a6b2.abstract: Surface defect detection of industrial products is a critical component of intelligent manufacturing quality control. However, existing unsupervised anomaly detection methods still struggle to achieve a favorable balance among image-level detection accuracy, pixel-level localization performance, and inference efficiency. To address this issue, this paper proposes a Fusion PatchCore with Lightweight Diffusion Reconstruction (FPC-LDR) framework for industrial surface defect detection, exploiting the complementary properties of discriminative feature matching and generative reconstruction. The proposed method first constructs a memory-bank module based on deep semantic features to identify anomalies via feature matching. Then, a lightweight latent diffusion reconstruction module is developed, in which single-step reconstruction replaces conventional multi-step diffusion processes, reducing computational overhead while maintaining reconstruction quality. Furthermore, an adaptive fusion strategy is introduced to integrate feature distance and reconstruction residuals, improving detection robustness and localization accuracy. Extensive experiments on the MVTec AD dataset demonstrate that FPC-LDR achieves an image-level AUROC of 94.65%, a pixel-level AUROC of 94.54%, and a PRO score of 95.28%. Cross-dataset evaluations on the VisA dataset further verify its generalization capability. The proposed method achieves an effective trade-off among accuracy, localization performance, and inference efficiency, demonstrating its potential for real-time industrial defect inspection.

title: One digit too many: brain rhythms and autonomic responses at the limits of working memory capacity
75cdcaf36bae293abd760f5e6c87a12a1245f26e.abstract: Physiological measures vary with working memory load, but whether they identify when demands exceed a person's working memory capacity remains unclear. We assessed neural and autonomic responses to exceeding digit span by one digit. During an adaptive digit span task, we recorded EEG, pupillometry, and photoplethysmography from 123 participants. We compared each participant's digit span (approximately 70% correct full-sequence recall) with sequences one digit longer (span+1), operationally defined as overload. Full-sequence accuracy decreased from 74.1% to 51.5%, and subjective mental demand increased. Baseline-normalized pulse wave amplitude (PWA) was lower in span+1 from the first digit through terminal retention period. PWA was lower on correctly recalled than erroneous span+1 trials. Phasic pupil responses increased across serial positions but were smaller in span+1 at late span-matched positions; responses did not differ between conditions at their final digits. Non-baseline-corrected pupil diameter was larger in span+1 before sequence onset and during terminal retention, whereas non-baseline-corrected PWA did not differ. Frontal midline theta increased with serial position and was greater during terminal retention in span+1. Alpha and beta power decreased with serial position, and differed between conditions only at late positions. Terminal beta suppression was greater on correctly recalled span+1 trials. Thus, exceeding calibrated span impaired recall without producing a common physiological breakpoint. The findings suggest that reaching this limit does not immediately lead to resource exhaustion or disengagement. Physiological responses showed shifts in timing consistent with adjustments in preparation for recall of the longer sequence, along with increased effort before and during longer sequences.
