title:
Differentiation and Pathological Significance of Tissue‐Resident Memory‐Like
                    <scp>CD8</scp>
                    <sup>+</sup>
                    T Cells in Systemic Lupus Erythematosus
container-title: Arthritis & Rheumatology
ca8c4d001f4f3dfa455ad7f45eefbc99350776f3.abstract: Objective Tissue‐resident memory T (T RM ) cells have been implicated in organ‐specific immune pathology; however, the pathological relevance of T RM ‐like CD8 + T cells in systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) remains unclear. We investigated their differentiation mechanisms and pathological significance in SLE, including associations with disease activity and organ involvement. Methods Peripheral blood samples from 30 treatment‐naïve patients with SLE, 40 patients with rheumatoid arthritis (RA), and 30 healthy donors (HDs) were analyzed by flow cytometry. Renal biopsy specimens from 20 patients with SLE were examined by immunofluorescence. Naïve CD8 + T cells from HDs were stimulated with cytokines to induce T RM ‐like differentiation, followed by phenotypic, functional, transcriptional, and metabolic analyses. The effects of Janus kinase (JAK) inhibitors were assessed. Results Circulating CD8 + CD69 + CD103 + T RM ‐like cells were more frequent in SLE than in RA and HDs ( P=0.022 and P<0.001 , respectively) and correlated with anti‐dsDNA antibodies (rs=0.468, P=0.016 ) and CH50 (rs=−0.397, P=0.045 ). Patients with active kidney involvement (renal BILAG A/B; n=17) had higher T RM ‐like cell proportions than those without active kidney involvement (n=13; P<0.05 ). CD3 + CD103 + cells in renal lesions expressed granzyme B or interferon‐γ. Patients with baseline T RM ‐like cell proportions ≥0.40% had higher urine protein‐to‐creatinine ratios and SELENA‐SLEDAI scores at week 24 (both P<0.05 ). IL‐15 plus TGF‐β1 induced T RM ‐like differentiation with effector, transcriptional, survival, and metabolic features, whereas JAK inhibition suppressed differentiation and granzyme B expression. Conclusion Circulating T RM ‐like CD8 + T cells were associated with SLE activity and kidney involvement. IL‐15/TGF‐β1‐dependent differentiation partly involved JAK/STAT signaling, supporting further evaluation as a biomarker and therapeutic target. image

title: Digital Governance as a Strategic Engine for Reaping Financial Performance: Evidence from the Global Healthcare Segment
container-title: Big Data and Cognitive Computing
b1ad924e7a035b4fde9e9331f973af58f256e6e2.abstract: Digital government initiatives have become a central feature of contemporary governance, reshaping institutional environments and influencing firm behavior across industries, including the global healthcare sector. The study empirically examines the effects of e-government development on healthcare firms’ performance across countries, with liquidity serving as a mediating variable. Grounded in institutional theory, transaction cost economics, and the resource-based view, the analysis assesses how variations in digital governance environments influence firm-level financial performance. Using an unbalanced panel of 14,942 firm-year observations from healthcare firms across 74 countries over the period 2016–2024, the study employs fixed-effects panel regressions to assess the effects of the E-Government Rank, E-Government Index, and E-Participation Index on return on assets. The findings reveal that e-government development exerts heterogeneous effects on firm performance. Higher numerical E-Government Rank (EGR) values are positively associated with firm profitability but negatively associated with liquidity, indicating that a deterioration in relative digital-governance standing corresponds to higher profitability and lower liquidity. Conversely, higher e-government index scores enhance liquidity, which in turn improves performance, suggesting a potential liquidity-mediated relationship. E-participation shows no direct performance impact, though liquidity remains a critical channel, particularly for smaller firms. Overall, the results highlight liquidity as a key transmission mechanism through which digital governance influences healthcare firm performance. The study offers important implications for policymakers and managers seeking to leverage digital governance reforms for sustainable healthcare sector development.

title: HSF/HSP Networks and Environmental Memory: From Molecular Persistence to a Recovery-Associated State
container-title: International Journal of Molecular Sciences
f4cd933da974f4c8249cc98195977a34217e71cf.abstract: Plants encounter environmental stresses in sequences of exposure, recovery, and subsequent challenge. Persistent molecular changes alone do not establish how previous exposure influences later responsiveness. Sustained protection may contribute to memory, whereas unresolved physiological disturbance can complicate its interpretation. The heat shock factor/heat shock protein (HSF/HSP) system links transcriptional regulation with protein folding, quality control, and recovery, providing a framework for examining these distinctions. We assess evidence for HSF/HSP-dependent environmental memory through its temporal organisation. Recurrent heat provides the strongest causal evidence, implicating HSF activity, transcriptional and chromatin regulation, chaperone persistence, and protein turnover in distinct aspects of thermomemory. Broader stress histories reveal altered subsequent responses, but causal HSF/HSP involvement remains less clearly resolved. We define experimental criteria for characterising recovery, demonstrating history-dependent functional responses, and identifying when candidate processes contribute causally. We then propose a recovery-associated state as a heuristic working model, rather than a demonstrated discrete cellular entity, to examine how previous exposure changes the configuration of regulatory and proteostatic processes during recovery. Persistent protective components, altered relationships among processes, or consequences outlasting the initiating molecular change may shape the later response. This framework guides experiments across stress sequences and species while distinguishing established thermomemory mechanisms from hypotheses about broader environmental memory.

title: A Memory-Based Model for Evaluating Trap and Removal Strategies Against the Red Palm Weevil
container-title: Insects
1471fc989c1df821cae0bfb28191cd5280a903d7.abstract: The red palm weevil (Rhynchophorus ferrugineus, RPW) is one of the most destructive pests of date palms worldwide. Its larvae feed inside the stem, so damage is often irreversible before any symptoms are visible. Early detection and rapid removal of infested palms are therefore essential. We develop a five-compartment fractional-order mathematical model that tracks healthy palms, infested palms, larvae, adult weevils, and pheromone traps. The model uses fractional-order (Caputo) derivatives, which allow past infestation history to influence current dynamics. We use this memory as a phenomenological representation of delayed and cumulative effects, such as the 2–4 month larval development cycle, and we test it against integer-order, Erlang-distributed, and fixed-delay alternatives. We provide mathematical proofs that the model is well posed and identify a threshold, the basic reproduction number R0, that separates eradication from persistent infestation. The model is calibrated to two UAE datasets: the 1994/95 Al Ain survey of about 1.1×106 palms (R0 > 1) and the 2025 national program outcomes (R0 < 1), using the reported first and last counts of each series and a reconstructed monthly trajectory between them. This drop in R0 corresponds to three control improvements: sensor-based early detection, endotherapy (localized insecticide injection into the stem), and preventive stem injection. Model comparison supports a fractional order of about 0.95 only for the 1994/95 epoch, whereas the 2025 data are described equally well without memory. Sensitivity analysis shows that faster removal of infested palms, lower RPW-to-palm contact rates, and reduced larval production are among the most effective control tactics. Model simulations of suspended and restored control suggest, as a hypothesis-generating scenario derived from hypothesized data, that a lapse in control can allow a transient resurgence, which supports continued monitoring. These results give quantitative guidance for planning pest management programs.

title: Healthy Sleep Mitigates the Association Between Cardiometabolic Disease and Poorer Cognitive and Brain Health
container-title: Journal of the American Heart Association
730ec9eb10ef1cac9256961446a52eda66db8e1f.abstract: Background Cardiometabolic diseases (CMDs), including type 2 diabetes, heart disease, and stroke, are important risk factors for dementia. We examined whether healthy sleep can support cognitive and brain health in people with CMDs. Methods The study included data from 408 977 adults from the UK Biobank. CMDs were defined using medical records, medication use, and medical history. Sleep patterns were defined using a composite score incorporating sleep duration, chronotype, insomnia symptoms, snoring, and daytime sleepiness. A subsample (n=34 913) underwent brain magnetic resonance imaging; volumes of total brain, gray matter, white matter, hippocampus, and white matter hyperintensities were ascertained. Associations of joint CMD (yes/no) and sleep (healthy, intermediate, poor) status with global and domain‐specific cognitive scores and brain magnetic resonance imaging measures were examined using linear regression models. Results At baseline, 54017 (13.2%) participants had at least one CMD. In joint exposure analysis, performance in global cognition (β=0.02 [95% CI, 0.01–0.05]), verbal/numeric reasoning (β=0.07 [95% CI, 0.01–0.12]), and processing speed (β=0.07 [95% CI, 0.04–0.10]) was significantly higher among individuals with CMDs and a healthy sleep pattern, compared with those with CMDs and a poor sleep pattern. Similarly, in neuroimaging analyses, participants with CMDs and a healthy versus poor sleep pattern showed significantly larger total brain volume (β=0.22 [95% CI, 0.08–0.35]), gray matter volume (β=0.23 [95% CI, 0.09–0.36]), and white matter volume (β=0.19 [95% CI, 0.05–0.33]). Conclusions Healthy sleep may attenuate the associations of CMDs with poorer cognitive performance and markers of brain atrophy. The findings highlight sleep as a modifiable factor that may support cognitive and brain health in individuals with CMDs.

title: Transcranial direct current stimulation combined with aerobic exercise for motor, mood and cognitive symptoms in long COVID: a randomized, sham-controlled feasibility trial
container-title: Brain Imaging and Stimulation
0dab2a974daf3a2f0ffaed94b853fe0455562b34.abstract: INTRODUCTION: The COVID-19 pandemic left millions of people with persistent disorders. Among these, long COVID is frequently associated with motor, mood, and cognitive impairments, significantly reducing quality of life. OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the feasibility of a randomized, sham-controlled trial of a two-week protocol combining transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) and aerobic exercise in individuals with long COVID, against pre-specified criteria for recruitment, retention, adherence, assessment burden, acceptability and safety. Motor, mood and cognitive outcomes were exploratory. METHODS AND MATERIALS: Participants were randomized (1:1) to real (2 mA, 30 min, left M1) or sham tDCS, both combined with treadmill exercise (64–76% max heart rate). Randomization used a computer-generated sequence, with allocation concealed in sealed opaque envelopes; participants and outcome assessors were blinded. The protocol comprised 13 sessions: baseline, 10 interventions, and two follow-ups. Feasibility was assessed through resources, management, and safety; clinical outcomes included motor, mood, and cognitive functions. RESULTS: Of 76 individuals contacted, 44 were assessed for eligibility and 10 were randomized (5 per group). All participants completed the intervention and post-intervention reassessment, and 8 completed the follow-up (80% retention). Adherence was high, and assessments remained under 120 minutes. All participants reported perceived benefits after the intervention (90% at follow-up); no serious adverse events occurred, and mild adverse effects were reported by all participants in both groups (most commonly drowsiness, tingling and fatigue), with no between-group differences. Fatigue decreased in both groups, with no significant between-group differences in any clinical outcome. CONCLUSION: A randomized, sham-controlled trial of tDCS combined with aerobic exercise in long COVID is feasible, and the protocol was safe and acceptable. The pre-specified feasibility criteria were met, supporting progression to an adequately powered trial with adjustments to recruitment strategies and delivery format.

title: A complementary learning system for continual episodic memory in large language models
15779d01907248b86433c7ea789f364071cb21cb.abstract: Humans retain memories of individual experiences for a lifetime, an ability attributed to a complementary learning system in which a fast process encodes episodes and a slow process integrates them into semantic knowledge. In classical Hebbian models such as Hopfield networks, memory traces are superposed in shared weights. This makes learning naturally continual but causes strong interference among correlated memories, a failure that reappears as catastrophic forgetting in deep networks. Here we use a large language model as a model system for continual episodic memory, with its pretrained weights supplying the semantic context in which new episodes are embedded. Fast learning is implemented by a hippocampus-like module that assigns each episode to a dedicated, extremely sparse low-rank adapter; competitive gating then selects among these separated traces during recall. Across streams of up to 1,000 factual and autobiographical episodes, each adapter requires only 2–3 parameters per token while preserving excellent recall. An internal retrieval-augmented generation mechanism reconstructs the selected episode in context and supports high-accuracy question answering over stored memories. Finally, slow cortical consolidation is modeled by fine-tuning the base weights through batch replay, enabling reconstruction and direct question answering without episodic adapters. Together, fast storage and slow consolidation implement both components of a complementary learning system within a single language model, yielding a neural-network model that stores, recalls, and consolidates naturalistic episodic memories, thereby capturing key functional features of human memory.

title: Blood Plasma Coenzyme Q10 and P-Selectin Are Predictive Factors for Mild Cognitive Dysfunction in Elderly Women
container-title: Antioxidants
0460e11357ee2e47c330a72d1bddb08997a842a6.abstract: Detection of the early phases of cognitive dysfunction is critical for identifying individuals at risk of neurodegeneration before irreversible damage occurs. High levels of coenzyme Q10 (CoQ10) in plasma are associated with high cognitive and executive capacities. Plasma CoQ10 has been associated with the prevention of oxidative damage and maintenance of mitochondrial health in the endothelium. Maintenance of endothelial function is also an important factor in the prevention of neurodegeneration and dementia. Therefore, this study aimed to determine plasma markers of endothelial health that, in conjunction with CoQ10, can effectively serve as predictors of cognitive dysfunction in a cohort of 45 elderly women (78.36 ± 8.41 years) from Seville, Spain. Utilizing a cross-sectional design, we assessed cognitive and executive capacities via the widely used MMSE-30 and FAB-E scales. Physiological health was evaluated through plasma biomarkers (including GDF-15, GFAP, BDNF, P-selectin, NfL, and p-Tau181) and the determination of CoQ10 levels. Furthermore, the study also analyzed exosome levels by measuring CD63 and their content in DNA and mtDNA. Our results indicate that low plasma CoQ10, elevated P-selectin (P-sel), and reduced exosomal DNA content can serve as early warning signs of neurodegeneration, appearing before traditional markers like GFAP, NfL, or p-Tau181. Our results indicate a link between CoQ10 levels, endothelial damage, and cognitive dysfunction risk.

title: Short-Long Temporal Normality Deviation for Weakly Supervised Video Anomaly Detection
container-title: Big Data and Cognitive Computing
d645a04397c6bcc11b8d7d309fc204c5162dd8a8.abstract: Weakly supervised video anomaly detection (WSVAD) tries to find abnormal events in untrimmed videos, while only video-level labels are given. However, many existing methods still have two main problems. First, abnormal events may last for different lengths of time, and their temporal changes are also not always the same; therefore, it is hard for one single time scale to collect enough useful anomaly information. Second, most current methods select abnormal segments mainly according to high anomaly scores, but these scores may be influenced by obvious visual regions, background changes, or scene-related bias, so the final anomaly localization may become unstable. To deal with these problems, this paper proposes STND-VAD, a short-long temporal normality-deviation framework for WSVAD. In this framework, a multi-scale dilated temporal feature enhancement module is first used to obtain contextual information from different temporal ranges. Then, this paper builds short-term and long-term MLP discriminative branches, so that local instant changes and longer temporal changes can be modeled separately. Besides, a normality-deviation evidence calibration mechanism is designed, which learns normal prototypes and measures how much each segment deviates from these normal patterns; in this way, it provides extra constraints for anomaly responses and reduces the influence of unreliable high-response segments. Experiments on three public benchmark datasets show that STND-VAD is effective and can achieve competitive anomaly detection results.

title: The behaviour bends, the code holds: working-memory category information in the multiple-demand network across graded interruption
5d0a5a955a4efbbda9fac6e37fe92b21fa22b86a.abstract: Abstract Protecting working memory (WM) from interference is essential for goal-directed behaviour, yet its neural mechanisms remain unclear. The multiple-demand (MD) network — a set of frontoparietal regions recruited by diverse cognitive demands — is a candidate system for maintaining WM content under interference. We examined how the MD network represents a memorandum when an unrelated task interrupts maintenance. Participants memorised an image of a tool or animal and, during the delay, performed a digit task whose difficulty was parametrically varied (passive, easy, hard), allowing us to test how task engagement and associated cognitive demands affected concurrently maintained information. Using fMRI and multivariate pattern analysis, we decoded the maintained category (tool vs. animal) from 13 MD regions and early visual cortex. Behaviourally, interruption reduced recall accuracy, while the most demanding interrupter slowed responses. Neurally, category information was present during the delay, most strongly in visual cortex and bilateral intraparietal sulcus. This information was unaffected by task engagement (active vs. passive), consistently across decoding accuracy and cross-validated Mahalanobis (crossnobis) distance, with Bayesian evidence supporting the null effect. Increasing the demand of the active interrupter, however, produced a modest, network-wide reduction in crossnobis distance that was not detectable in decoding accuracy. Together, these findings reveal a dissociation between the behavioural costs of interruption and the neural representation of maintained category information. Although interruption impaired recall, engaging in an interrupter did not measurably alter category-level information in the MD network or visual cortex. Increasing the interrupter’s demand produced only a modest, network-wide reduction in representational distance, without affecting decoding accuracy, suggesting that the behavioural costs of interruption may not be fully explained by changes in the categorical representation of the memorandum.

title: HL-02: Cognitive function and brain outcomes in T1D, 30 years after diagnosis- the CLARiFY study
container-title: Hormone Research in Paediatrics
d13466f6dfee78a414ebde15f0937e9b98b4c618.abstract: Abstract Background Thirty years ago, newly diagnosed patients with Type 1 Diabetes (T1D) and non-T1D controls were recruited into a longitudinal study of neurocognition and brain development. The Cognition and Longitudinal Assessments of Risk Factors over 30 Years (CLARiFY) Diabetes Complications Study is the most recent component of that study. Objectives To assess cognition and brain microstructure and morphology in mid-adulthood in a cohort of T1D patients diagnosed during childhood. Methods These are fully described in BMJ Open 2025 Jun 25;15(6):e105887. At baseline, 135 youth with newly diagnosed T1D and 129 age-matched non-T1D controls were recruited sequentially between 1990-1992 and completed assessments to evaluate cognition. These participants were re-evaluated with cognitive assessments using Wechsler Abbreviated Scale of Intelligence (WASI-II) and self-reported functional health outcomes. They also underwent structural and functional MRI scans to assess brain microstructure and morphology. In the T1D group, life-time HbA1C data were collected. Results Data were available for 105 T1D participants, 46 original and 155 new non-T1D controls. The T1D group had significantly lower FSIQ scores (as measured by WASI-II) when compared to non-T1D controls p=&lt;0.001 (95% CI 2.269, 7.992) adjusted for age, sex and education levels. MRI revealed reduced subcortical gray matter volume and cortical thickness in participants with T1D. Conclusions Significant differences are observed in both brain structure and cognition at 30 years post diagnosis in a cohort of T1D participants in comparison to non-T1D control participants.

title: Parental Longevity and Cognitive Ability in Older Mexican Adults
container-title: Journal of Aging and Health
bc7cb2243e5dce0d950424abb9e94448e3dcda2e.abstract: Background Parental longevity is linked to better offspring cognition, with limited evidence from middle-income countries. We examined associations between parental longevity and cognition in Mexico while controlling for health, socioeconomic status (SES), and genetic factors. Methods We used the 2018 wave of the Mexican Health and Aging Study ( n = 5,049; age 65+). Maternal/paternal longevity was based on survival to age 85 or older. We used latent variable regressions to estimate associations with offspring cognition, adjusting for demographics, parental characteristics, health, health behaviors, SES, and APOE-ε4 carrier status. Results About 31% of respondents had a mother and 31% had a father who survived to age 85 or older. Maternal, but not paternal, longevity was independently associated with better offspring cognition. The maternal association persisted after full adjustment. Conclusions Maternal longevity was positively linked to offspring cognition independent of health, health behaviors, SES, and APOE-ε4. Intergenerational support and broader genetic factors may contribute to this association.

title: P-98: Cognitive impairments in children and adolescents with type 1 diabetes: the role of acute metabolic episodes
container-title: Hormone Research in Paediatrics
528b34878f8a1ad20bfb2c1115a0670138c76cb3.abstract: Abstract Introduction Type 1 diabetes (T1D) in children and adolescents is associated not only with metabolic dysregulation but also with potential alterations in neurodevelopment. Acute metabolic episodes, particularly clinically significant hypoglycemia (CSH) and diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA), may adversely affect cognitive functions, including attention and executive functioning. Objectives To evaluate the impact of acute metabolic episodes on attentional functioning in pediatric patients with T1D. Methods A total of 117 children and adolescents with T1D (47.0% female; mean age 12.86 ± 3.16 years; mean diabetes duration 5.64 ± 4.01 years; mean HbA1c 7.49 ± 1.53% were included. Participants were stratified into four groups based on the presence of DKA and/or CSH. Attentional functioning was assessed using the MOXO Continuous Performance Test (MOXO-CPT), evaluating sustained attention, timeliness, impulsivity, and hyperactivity. Associations between acute metabolic episodes and cognitive outcomes were analyzed. Results A history of CSH was associated with significantly lower sustained attention scores and slower timeliness (both p &lt; 0.001). Patients with a history of DKA demonstrated significantly higher impulsivity scores compared to those without DKA (p = 0.008). No significant differences were observed in hyperactivity. Conclusions Acute metabolic episodes in pediatric T1D are associated with impairments in specific domains of attentional functioning. Prevention and careful monitoring of CSH and DKA may be important for preserving cognitive outcomes in this population.

title: Effort, Efficiency, and Strategic Direction in Nonlinear Doctoral Training
container-title: Innovative Higher Education
f945014181d640245bac42211abe921b24a5f40a.abstract: Abstract Doctoral training is often judged through visible, linear indicators such as publication count, time to degree completion, and technical productivity, yet these measures do not explain why students with comparable preparedness, effort, and ability diverge sharply in their long-term trajectories. We argue that doctoral development is better understood as a nonlinear interaction between accumulated effort (a summation function), accelerated efficiency (a multiplicative function), and strategic direction (a power law). Effort builds capacity, efficiency converts accumulated work into momentum, and strategic direction determines whether that momentum is amplified, maintained, or constrained. To clarify the developmental structure of doctoral training, we frame it through three hierarchical stages (alignment, productive, and independence), which can be delineated by the three progressive functions, respectively. This framework synthesizes scholarship on doctoral socialization, mentoring, and independence with the growing reality that AI can substantially amplify efficiency without replacing the human judgment required to identify consequential questions, recognize significance, and exercise strategic judgment under uncertainty. We anticipate that this hierarchical, non-linear model can not only describe the doctoral process but also offer a broader way to think about development processes in individuals and societies.

title: Adaptive Difficulty and Cognitive Gains in Multi-Domain Cognitive Training: A Randomized Active-Controlled Study
container-title: Behavioral Sciences
d1e20875508badc550c296ff88f958b6032186c1.abstract: Cognitive training is widely delivered in gamified formats, but it remains unclear whether adaptive adjustment of task difficulty contributes to cognitive gains beyond participation in the same training at a fixed level of difficulty. We investigated this question using Pavlov: The Brain Is On, a functional cognitive-training game. In Experiment 1, 107 young adults were randomly assigned to 19 days of adaptive-difficulty training (ADT) or the same training maintained at low difficulty (LDT), with the same games and the same prescribed daily training time. Cognitive performance was assessed before and after training across working memory, mental rotation, attention, inductive reasoning, and response inhibition. ADT showed a suggestive advantage over LDT in the N-back response-time load effect (group × time interaction, p = 0.017, uncorrected), though this result was marginal after FDR correction (pFDR = 0.084) and should not be interpreted as confirmatory. No significant between-group differences emerged for attention, inductive reasoning, or response inhibition; mental rotation showed a similar but non-significant pattern (p = 0.076). In Experiment 2, ADT showed a greater improvement in mental rotation than recreational gaming in the full sample (pFDR = 0.045), and this estimate was unchanged after adjustment for age; no other outcome differed between groups. Because Experiment 2 was non-randomized, this finding is exploratory. These findings suggest that adaptive difficulty may be a candidate active ingredient of gamified cognitive training, particularly for working memory, but the evidence remains preliminary and requires confirmation in preregistered studies.

title: A Domain-Specific Memory Bank-Enhanced Framework for Remote Sensing Image Captioning
container-title: Remote Sensing
9999422e005788cae095d8434d05bd04c30e4db6.abstract: Remote sensing image captioning enables automated interpretation of remote sensing data for applications such as environmental monitoring and urban planning. However, general-purpose multimodal models exhibit suboptimal adaptability on remote sensing imagery due to domain discrepancies in data distribution, resolution, and rotation invariance. We propose a domain-specific memory bank-enhanced framework for remote sensing image caption, built upon the lightweight EVCap architecture with three core innovations: (1) a remote sensing-specific visual memory bank providing domain-representative visual–semantic alignment; (2) a staged transfer training strategy that leverages pretrained knowledge while mitigating overfitting from limited remote sensing data; and (3) a K-means clustering-based small-sample memory bank that preserves performance while reducing memory footprint for resource-constrained deployment. Extensive experiments on the NWPU, RSICD, and Sydney datasets demonstrate substantial improvements over baselines. On the test sets, the domain-specific memory bank (R1) improves CIDEr by 1.87% on RSICD (0.3255 to 0.3316), and the clustering-based variant (R4) by 11.7% on Sydney (0.1422 to 0.1589) using only 39% of the full bank, despite decreases on NWPU and RSICD, with about 3.97 million trainable parameters.

title: P-32: Healthy body mission memory game
container-title: Hormone Research in Paediatrics
e6bfda8a5bf1d5ad9c2bde91b27d609316e15ff5.abstract: Abstract Introduction Healthy eating, regular physical activity, adequate sleep, and insulin therapy are fundamental pillars in the management of diabetes in children. Health education in childhood should be tailored to cognitive developmental stages, and play-based strategies are effective tools to enhance understanding and promote behavioral change. Objectives To develop an educational memory game for children aged 3–10 years, addressing nutrition, physical activity, and sleep. Methods This descriptive study presents the development of educational technology created by four pediatric nutrition specialists. The material includes three domains: nutrition, sleep, and physical activity. It consists of paired cards with illustrations and complementary phrases that form health messages. The activity encourages interaction, reading aloud, and reflection. Content follows current pediatric health recommendations, with illustrations selected digitally and layout developed by an editorial team. Results Tab. Content of the Educational Memory Game by Domain Conclusions Play-based strategies support engagement and understanding of healthy habits. Further studies are needed to evaluate the effectiveness of this tool in promoting lifestyle changes in children with diabetes.

title: Classical and mediterranean-modified ketogenic diets distinctly shape the gut microbiota composition and function in scopolamine-induced cognitive impairment model
container-title: Frontiers in Microbiology
03a0341b586d74de70c07997d561e24c0dfd885a.abstract: Background Mild cognitive impairment (MCI) is associated with impaired cerebral glucose metabolism, and ketogenic diets may influence cognitive impairment (CI) via the gut-brain axis. We investigated whether classical ketogenic (KD) and Mediterranean-modified ketogenic diet (MMKD) differentially affect gut microbiome composition and function, as well as cognitive performance, in a rat model of scopolamine-induced CI. Methods Twenty-eight male Wistar rats were assigned to a cognitively normal control group (CN), a scopolamine-induced CI group (SCOP) on standard diet, and two scopolamine-treated groups receiving either a classical KD (KD; 84% fat, 16% protein) or a MMKD (60% fat, predominantly olive oil, 30% protein, 10% carbohydrate, resveratrol, and inulin-supplemented) for 9 weeks. Spatial and recognition memory were assessed using the Morris Water Maze and Novel Object Recognition Test. Caecal microbiome composition and function were profiled by shotgun metagenomic sequencing. Short-chain fatty acid (SCFA) analysis was conducted from caecal contents of rats. Brain and hippocampal brain derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF) and phosphorylated cyclic AMP response element-binding (p-CREB) protein levels were evaluated by Western blotting. Results MMKD significantly improved spatial memory relative to other groups. MMKD had higher alpha diversity in the gut microbiome compared to the KD group. KD showed the most distinct gut microbiome profile, marked by enrichment of Bacteroides and Parabacteroides species and reduced carbohydrate and amino acid metabolism. MMKD was characterized by enrichment of lactic acid bacteria with elevated coenzyme A and pyrimidine biosynthesis. Moreover, MMKD was associated with higher SCFA levels compared to the KD group. No significant differences in brain or hippocampal BDNF or p-CREB protein levels were observed among groups. Conclusion These findings show that KD and MMKD produce distinct gut microbiome compositional and functional signatures, with MMKD associated with higher microbial diversity, SCFA levels, and spatial learning performance.

title: Lead impairs long-term memory by disrupting mitochondrial redox homeostasis in Drosophila
container-title: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
33cb98cb342f82617d0c4469c10592ac4c9eb8ed.abstract: Lead (Pb) exposure remains a major environmental risk factor for cognitive dysfunction, yet the cellular mechanisms underlying Pb-induced memory impairment are poorly understood. Here, we show that both developmental and adult-onset Pb exposure selectively disrupts protein-synthesis-dependent long-term memory (LTM) in Drosophila melanogaster while sparing other memory forms. Using a mitochondria-targeted redox biosensor (mito-roGFP2-Orp1), we found that Pb elevates mitochondrial oxidative stress and disrupts redox homeostasis in cholinergic neurons and in dorsal-anterior-lateral (DAL) neurons, a critical locus for LTM consolidation. Pb-induced redox imbalance suppresses training-induced de novo protein synthesis in DAL neurons, thereby impairing memory consolidation. Antioxidant treatment with epigallocatechin gallate restores mitochondrial redox balance and rescues LTM by reinstating activity-dependent protein synthesis in DAL neurons. These findings identify mitochondrial redox dysregulation as a key mechanism linking environmental Pb exposure to impaired memory consolidation. Our results further establish a genetically tractable platform for dissecting neurotoxic mechanisms and for evaluating antioxidant-based strategies to mitigate Pb-induced cognitive dysfunction.

title: Comparative Benchmarking of ChatGPT, Claude, and Grok on Persian General Surgery Promotion Examinations With and Without an Uploaded Surgical Reference Package
0dbc53b82abae367d3d800c22f5963537cebf72a.abstract: Abstract Background Large language models are increasingly used in medical education, yet their observed agreement with answer keys on locally developed, non-English surgical examinations remains incompletely characterized. Methods This comparative benchmark evaluated ChatGPT (Luna High), Claude Opus 5, and Grok 4/5 on 456 original Persian four-option questions from the 2024 (1403 Persian calendar), 2025 (1404 Persian calendar), and 2026 (1405 Persian calendar) Iranian General Surgery Residency Promotion Examinations. Each annual question file was submitted once to each model in two separate user-facing workflows: question file only and question file plus an uploaded surgical reference package. Responses were scored against the official Sanjesh answer keys using a strict single-option rule. Results With the uploaded reference package, aggregate answer-key agreement was 71.27% for ChatGPT, 75.44% for Grok, and 80.04% for Claude. In the question-file-only workflow, the corresponding values were 67.11%, 72.59%, and 79.82%. Claude had the highest observed aggregate agreement in both workflows. Conclusion In this single-run, web-enabled benchmark, Claude showed the highest observed aggregate agreement with the official answer keys. The uploaded reference package was associated with a positive change in ChatGPT agreement across all three years, whereas the direction of change varied for Grok and Claude. These findings are descriptive and do not establish a general model ranking or a causal effect of document upload.

title: Challenging the Femininity Stigma of Flexible Work: Gender and Effort in Part-Time Employment
c87d2ec8a29a879ea474c450a88d463349dc8edb.abstract: Abstract Flexible work arrangements are stigmatized as feminine, and employees who use them – particularly women – experience workplace bias. This paper tests the assumption that non-traditional work arrangements signal reduced effort among women, compared with men. Drawing on Social Role Theory, Self-Determination Theory, and flexibility stigma research, I argue that because women face comparatively less breadwinner pressure than men, women (compared with men) construe employment through a less instrumental lens, predicting stronger work effort, especially in part-time roles. Two representative samples support this pattern. Study 1, using panel data consisting of U.S. adults finds that employment status interacts with gender to predict work effort, such that men exhibit lower work effort in part-time (vs. full-time) roles, while women's work effort remains high across both. Study 2, using a nationally representative sample spanning 20 countries, demonstrates that women's weaker instrumental orientation toward work helps partially explain their stronger work effort in part-time roles. Implications for performance management and flexible work policies are discussed.

title: Bridging the QC–QA Cognitive Handoff: An Agentic Verification Harness for Error Detection, Specification Cross-Checking and Quality Documentation Assembly in Pharmaceutical Quality Assurance
1307954b9361f738208ba539447d4d1c8326617b.abstract: Abstract Background. Quality control (QC) results reach regulatory dossiers through manual transcription and review. Such a benchmark does not yet exist. No collection of pharmaceutical quality documents carries discrepancies of known class and location, so automated verification cannot yet be evaluated against measured performance across realistic transfer errors and document types. Objectives. To specify (i) an architecture in which large language models only read and propose values, deterministic code performs every calculation and acceptance test, and a qualified reviewer makes every decision; (ii) a protocol for building a reference corpus and evaluating such systems; and (iii) sensitivity estimates from three dossiers. The plan covers design, evaluation, and measurement. Methods. Records from three ASEAN Common Technical Dossier Part II submissions (13, 14 and 10 records) were de-identified, and 112, 100 and 120 discrepancies across nine classes were introduced into dossiers A, B and C. A finding counted as a detection when it identified an injected discrepancy at the correct location with the correct class. The framework ran blind to the register. Sensitivity to injected discrepancies is reported per dossier with Wilson 95% confidence intervals and pooled by random-effects meta-analysis; clustering within records is not accounted for. Results. The harness detected 95 of 112 (84.8%; 95% CI 77.0–90.3), 80 of 100 (80.0%; 71.1–86.7) and 105 of 120 (87.5%; 80.4–92.3) injected discrepancies, a pooled sensitivity of 84.1% (72.4–91.5), with detection in every class in every dossier. False-positive rate, specificity, precision, run-to-run repeatability and performance relative to human reviewers or baseline systems were not measured, and the injection registers have not been independently validated. Conclusions. The architecture detected a similar share of injected discrepancies in three dossiers, one run each. Although single runs across three dossiers cannot show reduced reviewer workload or superiority over existing practice, the observed pattern supports further testing rather than any claim of practical benefit. The protocol defines the required next experiments.

title: Designing ESOP for corporate startups: aligning risk, effort, and equity expectations in a Thai conglomerate
container-title: Journal of Asia Business Studies
e1346c7c60f002df23027a0b5ba23bf3c2b3636d.abstract: Purpose This paper asks how employee stock ownership plans (ESOP) should be designed for corporate startups, and why such designs so often fail to align expectations. It aims to examine the tension between employees who ground equity claims in effort and leaders who ground them in risk-bearing. Design/methodology/approach A qualitative case study was conducted at a major Thai conglomerate operating two parallel innovation tracks: a relationship-based flagship venture and a merit-based stage-gate programme. Twenty-three semi-structured interviews covered 15 internal and eight external informants. Data were analysed thematically following Braun and Clarke (2006). Findings Employees and leaders reasoned from different premises about what equity compensates: effort versus risk-bearing. A convergent theme was reluctance to trade salary for equity – but that equity had never been specified. Its amount, the contribution required to obtain it, and the route by which it could become cash were all undefined. Differing accountability across the two tracks destabilized the design further. Research limitations/implications Findings derive from a single Thai conglomerate, so analytical rather than statistical generalization applies. Future research could test whether the effort–risk tension persists once the equity offered is fully specified. Practical implications The paper offers a four-step framework: classify the venture by intended destination; define what risk equity compensates; apply consistent rules across tracks; and define how ownership becomes cash. Unrealizable equity is not compensation. Originality/value To the best of the authors’ knowledge, this is the first inside-the-firm account of ESOP design across parallel corporate startup programmes in an Asian conglomerate, identifying an institutional precondition – an exit market – that equity practice assumes but rarely examines.

title: Acute effects of orally administered Δ8-THC and Δ9-THC on simulated driving ability, cognitive performance, and subjective drug effects
a6d170fb582bfd090963b6239c362ba1a1d3ed8b.abstract: ∆8-Tetrahydrocannabinol (∆8-THC), a structural isomer of ∆9-THC, is a growing drug of concern often marketed as a “milder” alternative to ∆9-THC. No controlled studies have evaluated doses above 40mg ∆8-THC or examined its acute effects on driving. Healthy adults (N=20) with no past 30-day cannabinoid use completed four double-blind, outpatient drug administration sessions, self-administering oral doses of ∆8-THC (30mg, 60mg), ∆9-THC (30mg), or placebo. Simulated driving was assessed at baseline and at 2 hrs post-dosing. The primary outcome Global Drive Score (GDS), a composite measure of driving performance, and secondary driving outcomes were examined. Subjective drug effects, cognitive and psychomotor performance, vital signs, and whole blood cannabinoid concentrations were assessed at baseline and over 8 hrs post-administration. ∆8-THC and ∆9-THC significantly impaired driving relative to placebo with decrements in coherence during the car following and poor maintenance of lane positioning. 30mg ∆9-THC produced the greatest impairment but was not significantly different from 60mg ∆8-THC. Subjective effects generally peaked between 2-3 hrs post-dosing. ∆8-THC produced effects that were qualitatively similar to ∆9-THC, but at approximately half the potency on most outcomes. ∆8-THC significantly impaired driving performance, notable given its widespread availability and common perception as less psychoactive than ∆9-THC. At the same dose, ∆8-THC produced similar types of impairment and physiological effects, but at a lower magnitude than ∆9-THC, likely driven, in part, by higher concentrations of the psychoactive 11-OH metabolite following ∆9-THC relative to ∆8-THC administration. These findings can inform ∆8-THC policy and public safety initiatives that deter drugged-driving.

title: Chronic Subdural Hematoma as a Potentially Reversible Cause of Cognitive and Gait Decline in Older Adults: Clinical Recognition, Treatment, and Functional Recovery
container-title: Journal of Clinical Medicine
66c20108a096f55f3803cf76d84829da76d357a4.abstract: Chronic subdural hematoma (cSDH) is an increasingly common neurological disorder in older adults and may present with cognitive decline, gait instability, recurrent falls, and loss of independence rather than overt focal deficits. Because these symptoms overlap with dementia, delirium, parkinsonism, and frailty, diagnosis may be delayed despite the potential for meaningful recovery after treatment. This narrative review summarizes evidence on clinical recognition, treatment, early mobilization, rehabilitation, and patient-centered recovery in older adults with cSDH. A targeted search of PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and Web of Science identified randomized trials, observational studies, systematic reviews, meta-analyses, guidelines, and consensus statements available through July 2026. Surgical decompression may improve cognition and mobility, but the magnitude and durability of recovery vary. Premorbid cognitive and functional status, frailty, malnutrition, postoperative delirium, and complications are associated with outcomes, although causal effects are incompletely established. Postoperative drainage reduces recurrence; selected randomized trials suggest that middle meningeal artery embolization reduces recurrence or treatment failure, whereas evidence for independent cognitive and gait benefits remains limited. Early mobilization may reduce medical complications. Evidence specific to cSDH remains insufficient to prescribe a standardized exercise dose or progression. Multidimensional follow-up and prospective trials using cognitive, gait, quality-of-life, and participation outcomes are needed to determine whether successful hematoma treatment translates into restored independence and meaningful daily function.

title: Design a Model for Assessing the Impact of ChatGPT on Enhancing Teaching and Learning in Iraqi Education
container-title: Journal of Al-Farabi for Engineering Sciences
d663ef9723c3b4d9a230a79aefff097b887d3dcb.abstract: Iraqi educational establishments continue to encounter ambiguity over the successful incorporation of artificial intelligence (AI) tools such as ChatGPT. Due to the insufficient research on the implications of GPT in Iraq, this study introduces a relevant model to explore the benefits and risks of using GPT for academic activities among university students. The model is made up of four levels, in addition to the components that have an increasing influence. The research used a mixed-methods strategy, using SmartPLS for data analysis due to the capability to handle various sample sizes, in conjunction with thematic analysis to identify and assess the pivotal topics included in the interview transcripts. This research demonstrates GPT's ability to promote self-improvement and provide customized, immediate responses. As a result, it might improve accessibility, foster uniqueness, and alleviate the instructional workload, thereby optimizing critical processes and tasks. The study also found that educational issues consist of a shortfall in contextual insight, compromising academic integrity, maintaining bias within educational institutions, normalizing cheating, and weakening sophisticated cognitive functions. In addition, via a collection of recommendations, this study enriches the existing literature on the effects of chatbots in educational settings, delivering crucial insights for educational organizations, policy strategists, researchers, and AI developers.

title: A review of deployment and optimization of lightweight neural networks on resource-constrained edge devices: from efficient architectures to memory scheduling and on-device benchmarks
container-title: International Conference on Communication, Sensing, and Intelligent Computing (CSIC 2026)
8b1c54866767018ad24921bbf073ac0952bf2fa6.abstract: Deep learning models are moving from the cloud to mobile systems, MCUs, and edge GPUs. On‑device deployment is limited by latency, peak memory, energy, toolchains, and reproducibility, rather than merely parameters or FLOPs. This paper introduces lightweight CNNs, CNN-Transformer hybrids and lightweight Transformers, and examines compression, scheduling, memory scheduling, toolchains, and benchmarks. Latency is determined by the regularity of the graph, operator support, memory access and toolchain implementation; MCU peak memory is mainly consumed by activations and buffers. MLPerf Tiny enhances comparability but only partially covers streaming input, long‑term energy, multimodal tasks and cross‑toolchain reproducibility. Future work should strengthen deployment-pipeline comparison, automated memory scheduling, energy evaluation, collaboration, and benchmarks.

title: A semantic-aware intelligent computing framework for cognitive understanding of structured indicator data via large language models
container-title: International Conference on Communication, Sensing, and Intelligent Computing (CSIC 2026)
7e9a3c944f7f957248c832129f46580baef8c6f2.abstract: The value “7” is not interchangeable across assessment scales: its meaning depends on the instrument, threshold, and neighboring indicators. We test whether making that context explicit changes classification. A three-layer serializer attaches severity levels, published risk associations, and the study’s decision rule to 21 indicators from 10,000 risk-screening records. GPT-4o, DeepSeek-V3, and Qwen-Max are evaluated under three controlled prompt conditions on the same balanced 200-record test set and compared with five tabular ML baselines. The strongest condition, GPT-4o with few-shot chain-of-thought, records 77.5% accuracy and 0.769 F1. Its 0.750 recall contrasts with the precision-heavy ML baselines, and the output also exposes the indicator phrases used in each decision. These results concern one constructed screening task; they do not establish clinical validity.

title: Effects and mechanisms of exercise timing on cognitive function in older type 2 diabetes mellitus patients with mild cognitive impairment: A magnetic resonance imaging-based randomized controlled trial protocol
container-title: PLOS One
fb4235d335ef48abed180df14c27399616183401.abstract: Background Mild cognitive impairment (MCI) is a prevalent complication of type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). Cognitive impairment progressively impairs self-care abilities, thereby triggering a vicious cycle of poor glycemic control and further cognitive decline. Exercise has been widely recognized as an effective strategy to improve both glycemic control and cognitive function; however, an optimal time of day for exercise to mitigate this neurodegenerative trajectory has not been determined. This trial aims to determine the most effective exercise timing to maximize cognitive benefits in older T2DM patients with MCI (T2DM-MCI) and to investigate the underlying neurobiological mechanisms using multimodal magnetic resonance imaging. Methods In this randomized controlled trial, patients 60–75 years of age with T2DM‐MCI will be assigned to a morning exercise group (09:00–10:10), an evening exercise group (19:00–20:10), or a health education group. The exercise groups will complete a 12-week, home-based, remotely supervised exercise program comprising aerobic and resistance exercises. The health education group will receive a 12-week health education program. Cognitive function will be evaluated at baseline and post-intervention using the Montreal Cognitive Assessment, Color-Word Stroop Test, N-back task, Trail making Test, Attention Network Test, and Digit Symbol Substitution Test. Additionally, brain structure and function based on imaging, blood biomarkers, and physical fitness will also be assessed. Discussion In this study, we aim to identify the optimal time of day for exercise to maximize cognitive benefits in patients with T2DM‐MCI and to elucidate underlying neurocognitive mechanisms. We will examine whether glycemic control mediates the relationship between exercise and cognitive function improvement. This research is expected to provide “time-specific” evidence for exercise prescription to maximize the neurocognitive benefits and mitigate dementia risk in this population. title: Team Cognition Under Extreme Time Pressure: A Dynamic Communication Analysis of the US Airways Flight 1549 Emergency
container-title: Journal of Cognitive Engineering and Decision Making
6433dc711b62b74431f6d92d76ed98fa0a4474a8.abstract: Expert teams coordinate under extreme time pressure, yet it remains hard to quantify how their communication reorganizes and what cognition drives that reorganization. Communication analysis characterizes what teams say. Newer temporal methods characterize how that talk is organized in time. The two are rarely joined, and the cognitive dynamics of a real emergency with a successful outcome remain unmeasured. We applied a six-category content typology and a four-component expert-decision model to the cockpit voice recorder transcript of US Airways Flight 1549 (the 2009 Miracle on the Hudson), reliably coding 276 statements (1,982 words) across six flight phases, and characterized reorganization with lag-sequential analysis, entropy, and burstiness. During the 213-second emergency, factual (36.84%) and action (27.63%) statements dominated and non-task talk vanished; attention (43.42%) and alternatives (22.37%) led the cognitive categories. Pace more than doubled (0.99 to 2.41 words per second), communication shifted from clustered to near-continuous (burstiness +0.36 to −0.06), and sequential dependencies tightened (conditional entropy 1.93 to 1.83 bits) as acknowledgment-anchored checklist loops gave way to uncertainty-to-factual and action-to-uncertainty cycling. The study characterizes the communication and cognitive dynamics of one crisis with a successful outcome, integrating content and temporal-dynamic measures with an explicit expert-decision model.

title: A functional connectome identifies vulnerability to cognitive decline and Alzheimer’s disease progression
container-title: Science Advances
68dc240b354f710829ee835ffee1d05c140fb241.abstract: Identifying the neurobiological basis of cognitive vulnerability is essential for preventing Alzheimer’s disease (AD). We derived the Alzheimer’s Resilience-Vulnerability Connectome (ARC) by contrasting SuperAgers (SA), an extreme phenotype of preserved late-life memory, with AD using resting-state fMRI. ARC distinguished SA from AD in a discovery cohort ( N = 290; AUC = 0.85) and replicated independently ( N = 143), involving prefrontal, temporal, and insular networks and associating with brain age. Applied to cognitively unimpaired adults (discovery: N = 818; replication: N = 497), ARC-based subtyping revealed SA-like and AD-like subgroups with comparable baseline cognition but divergent longitudinal trajectories. AD-like individuals exhibited faster cognitive decline, greater amyloid-β accumulation, and higher AD conversion risk. Exploratory GWAS nominated CLYBL and FRMD6 as candidate novel loci associated with the subtype difference. These findings suggest that ARC captures a continuous connectomic dimension of cognitive aging spanning SA, cognitively typical aging, and AD, highlighting the potential of functional connectomic variation for early risk stratification in AD.

title: Response Inhibition in an Affective Context and Its Relation to Psychopathic Traits
container-title: Cognitive and Behavioral Neurology
aabb7c9f758457907fa6384206ab8a0846b91dee.abstract: Background: Psychopathic traits are associated with affective deficits and elevated impulsivity levels, such as those measured by Go/No-go tasks. Previous research assessing the combined effects of psychopathic traits and emotional processing on response inhibition has focused on low cognitive load task designs and found little evidence of valence-dependent effects. Objective: To investigate whether assessing affective response inhibition under low and high cognitive load manipulations reveals interactive effects between psychopathic traits and valence processing on response inhibition. Methods: We assessed 146 student and community participants using the Psychopathic Personality Inventory—Revised (PPI-R). Response inhibition was measured under low and high cognitive load using the parametric Go/No-go task (PGNG) alongside positive, negative, and neutral distractor images. Results: Cognitive load and valence affected performance. Response times were faster and accuracy rates were higher for the low-load (easier) task stage. Negative and positive trials slowed response times and reduced response inhibition performance compared with neutral trials. In terms of psychopathic traits, the PPI-R Self-Centered Impulsivity factor and two of its subscales, Machiavellian Egocentricity and Blame Externalization, correlated negatively with response inhibition across valences and load. Correcting for other psychopathic traits accounted for the effect of Machiavellian Egocentricity, while the associations between inhibition and Self-Centered Impulsivity as well as Blame Externalization remained significant. Conclusion: Psychopathic traits were associated with reduced response inhibition performance irrespective of the affective context, even when measured under increased cognitive load. These findings add to the existing evidence against an interaction between psychopathic traits and emotional processing during response inhibition.

title: A benchmark dataset of null-calibrated streamflow spectral-memory diagnostics for five CAMELS-family archives, with open rainfall-runoff model outputs for CAMELS-GB v2
d5aa3e3a6fd6c6ab37d34aa817c2d7bdb7453aa6.abstract: Abstract. This article describes a reusable benchmark dataset, rather than a standalone methods paper, of streamflow spectral-memory diagnostics computed from daily discharge records in five CAMELS-family archives (CAMELS-US, CAMELS-GB v2, CAMELS-BR v1.2, CAMELS-AUS v2 and CAMELS-DK; 3,010 gauges in total). For each gauge the release provides the positive-integral autocorrelation time of discharge anomalies, local spectral-slope curves on the raw frequency axis and on the release-defined memory-normalized coordinate De =τacf f, dispersion statistics with gauge- and region-cluster uncertainty, and matched stochastic reference products. For CAMELS-GB v2 it also provides the outputs of three open rainfall-runoff models and two seasonal references under a common chronological split. The De coordinate and the null-calibration ladder are operational fields and reference products defined for this release from standard signal processing and transparent simulations; they are not presented as previously validated, universal techniques. The archive-level characterization is intentionally bounded: memory scaling reduces cross-catchment spectral-curve dispersion in US, GB and BR (24.0 %, 14.7 % and 11.8 %), is weak and uncertain in AUS (7.7 %, region-cluster 95 % interval -0.7–27.6 %), and shows no reduction in the lowland DK archive (-4.7 %, -20.2–11.1 %). The matched references quantify how much alignment can arise from serial correlation alone. A CAMELS-GB worked reuse case, based on three independent models and 544 gauges (308 disagreement gauges), does not support spectral distance as a universal model-selection rule (median decision delta +0.124, bootstrap 95 % CI +0.085 to +0.163). The release is intended for catchment-scale spectral characterization, frequency-specific model comparison and reproducible benchmark construction; it does not establish a storage mechanism or a cross-archive ranking rule. The curated dataset is available from Zenodo at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22055294 (Ren, 2026).

title: Sediment-dynamics indicators for assessing fluvial-memory controls on suspended-sediment routing and deposition in a valley-type reservoir
450d0456cb3eb539e2de7df3eb854834f47a0189.abstract: Abstract. River impoundment fundamentally alters hydraulic conditions and sediment-transfer processes, but the extent to which pre-impoundment fluvial morphology continues to structure sediment dynamics remains insufficiently quantified. In valley-type reservoirs, submerged channels, islands, bars and floodplain surfaces may preserve an inherited geomorphological template that influences contemporary flow pathways and depositional patterns. This study examines the persistence and sedimentary significance of this fluvial memory in the Włocławek Reservoir, a lowland through-flow reservoir on the Vistula River, Poland, more than five decades after impoundment. Reconstructed pre-dam morphology, measured bathymetry and suspended-sediment grain-size distributions were combined with two-dimensional hydrodynamic modelling (AdH) and Lagrangian particle tracking (PTM) under low-, medium- and high-flow conditions. Three dimensionless indicators—Relative Sedimentation Efficiency (RES), Sediment-deposition Stability Index (SDI) and Redeposition Index (RI)—were developed to quantify spatial contrasts in sediment capture, primary-deposit stability and secondary redistribution among inherited morphodynamic zones. Simulated sediment retention increased from 66 % during high flow to 73 % during medium flow and 94 % during low flow. Former thalweg and island/bar zones exhibited disproportionately high sediment capture, with maximum RES values of 4.10 and 2.63, respectively, whereas former floodplain surfaces showed relatively low sedimentation efficiency. Higher flows reduced the stability of primary deposits and enhanced resuspension–redeposition processes. These findings indicate that inherited channel–island–floodplain morphology remains an important spatial organizer of sediment routing and deposition long after the transition from riverine to reservoir conditions. The proposed indicators offer a quantitative framework for investigating the sedimentary expression of geomorphological inheritance in valley-type reservoirs and for distinguishing depositional efficiency from sediment-storage stability.

title: Silent but deadly? Physics says seldom, memory says mostly
bdc137c16bdd865f88ae091c87d194e6351c23be.abstract: The belief that a silent passage of flatus smells worse than an audible one appears in many languages but is untested. We follow a passage from sound through dispersion to a bystander's memory with a lip-reed model of the anal valve, dispersion models and observer models from the literature. Most releases, 85%, never set the valve oscillating. We prove that under linear transport a slower release of the same gas cannot give a higher peak, in any room or flow. In computational fluid dynamics of seated and standing people, the warm air rising along the body takes a slow release and lets a fast one pass, so momentum decides which nose a release reaches. With passages as emitted and settings weighted by how often people share them, a bystander finds the silent passage worse in 0.5% of pairs and the audible one in 6.9%; only in a closed lift are the two about equal. A silent passage is noticed only if smelled, and this selection alone can explain the belief: among remembered pairs the silent passage seems worse in 88%. It predicts that releasers hold the belief less firmly than bystanders and that anosmic people never remember a silent passage.

title: Fraud, Effort, and Data Quality Across Four Online Recruitment Modes: A Head-to-Head Protocol Comparison for a Minority Subpopulation Cohort Study
ca877f8e7739486f54c678850278b56b2d9853ac.abstract: Comparisons of online recruitment sources are rarely conducted under a unified protocol; literature-based comparisons confound recruitment mode with variation in eligibility criteria, survey instruments, incentives, and data-quality controls. We compared four concurrently fielded recruitment modes (text-message invitations, targeted digital advertising, social media advertising, and a commercial nonprobability panel) using a common screener, instrument, incentive, and quality-flagging system to establish a large cohort of a minority subpopulation: young adults (aged 18-25) in California who use electronic nicotine delivery systems. Screener completion per invitation/impression ranged from 0.8% to 11.1% with 12,547 completed screeners. Two quality-flagging systems were applied with 806 retained respondents. Screener fraud flags were 4 to 9 times more frequent for social media advertising than for any other mode (p &lt; .001). Across all recruitment modes except social media, endorsing eligibility items was associated with a higher likelihood of screener flags, with one exception (ps &lt; .008), a pattern consistent with eligibility fraud. Baseline assessment insufficient effort responding (IER) flags were most frequent among panel respondents (p &lt; .001) and least frequent among respondents recruited via text-message and targeted digital advertising, the two probabilistic sampling modes. Paradata-based and content-based screening were complementary rather than interchangeable data-quality tools with weak overlap (Jaccard index = .20); most respondents exceeding the baseline threshold were already excluded via screener flags, whereas most screener-flagged respondents produced internally consistent reports, indicating the screenings captured distinct validity threats. Recruitment mode systematically shaped both fraudulent responding and response effort. Social media advertising yielded the largest and most demographically diverse sample but also the highest screener fraud rates; the commercial panel showed little evidence of fraud but the highest IER. Multi-modal recruitment of minority subpopulations into large longitudinal studies is feasible and, with layered quality controls, can yield cohorts with acceptable fraud and IER profiles.

title: US–China Differences in Children's Reasoning, Visual Attention, and Social Cognition
container-title: Topics in Cognitive Science
9892f6328b0ac09979af12ede31076df49096f25.abstract: Abstract Outward differences between cultures are very salient, with Western and East Asian cultures as a prominent comparison pair. A large literature describes cross‐cultural variation in cognition, but relatively less research has explored the developmental origins of this variation and those findings that are reported have not typically been replicated. This study helps to fill this empirical gap by replicating four prominent findings documenting cross‐cultural differences in children's relational reasoning, picture description, causal attribution, and uniqueness preference in a cross‐sectional sample of 240 3–12‐year‐olds from the United States and China. We observed cross‐cultural differences in picture description, causal attribution, and uniqueness preference, though the uniqueness preference result was in the opposite direction of the predicted direction. Performance in each task followed a different developmental trajectory, but we did not observe interactions between age and cultural differences. We also did not observe strong associations in performance across tasks, or between task performance and a range of demographic factors. Overall, these results suggest that existing developmental measures may be insufficiently precise to support strong mechanistic inferences about cognitive differences across cultures.

title: A fibroblast-CD8+ T cell circuit drives a Type 1 shift in allergic inflammatory memory
04c9fd92a679272ac62ed2ce2f26caea81f166f2.abstract: Abstract Inflammatory memory in barrier tissues often manifests as exaggerated recall responses to previously encountered stimuli 1,2 . While recall is generally thought to reinforce the Type of inflammation (e.g., Type 1 (T1), Type 2 (T2), or Type 17 (T17)) induced in the primary encounter, whether and how memory responses engage programs beyond the initiating Type is unclear. Here, we adapted well-characterized murine models of T2 atopic dermatitis (AD)-like 3 and T17 psoriasis-like 4 inflammation into repeated challenge paradigms to compare how inflammatory memory is stored and recalled through longitudinal single-cell RNA-sequencing. In T17 inflammation, a network of IL-17-producing γδT cells, IL-17-responsive keratinocytes and myeloid cells established in primary challenge re-emerged in recall with increased abundance and accelerated kinetics. By contrast, allergic T2 memory drove a particularly exacerbated and durable recall response in which hallmark features of T1 immunity, including interferon (IFN) signaling and cytotoxic lymphocyte recruitment, were unexpectedly layered onto amplified T2 responses. This T2-to-T1 shift was initiated by CD8+ tissue-resident memory T (Trm) cells that expanded with repeated challenge, produced IFNγ, TNF-α and IL-13, and closely resembled treatment-refractory Trm cells in AD. Tissue rewiring was supported by Trm-derived T1 cytokines and the IL-4-rich T2 milieu whose synergy on fibroblasts amplified allergic recall via IL-15 and CCL19 . By tuning fibroblast IFN responsiveness in vivo, we mechanistically dissect how this fibroblast-CD8+ T cell circuit supports cytotoxic CD8+ T cell responses. In human AD, both arms of allergic recall amplification by this two-cell circuit featuring T1 and T2 effector responses were conserved. Our findings reveal how a stromal-immune circuit drives a clinically relevant T1 immune axis to support allergic inflammatory memory.

How many sounds is a picture worth? A dual process perspective on the differences between memory for environmental sounds and pictures
d41fbed49413657a0b501276da555edc7e4c9c4f.abstract: Recognition memory on standard old/new tests is typically better for pictures than for sounds. To investigate this modality effect, we examined the contributions of recollection and familiarity processes to recognition memory of auditory and visual objects (environmental sounds and colored line drawings, respectively). To gain some insight into the source of the modality difference, we investigated whether the modality effect was larger for one process than the other. Indeed, in Experiment 1, recollection was greater for visual than auditory objects, but the modality effect on familiarity was much smaller. We replicated this pattern in all subsequent experiments. Focusing on recollection, we examined the consequences of hindering encoding during study with a divided attention task. Surprisingly, Experiments 2 - 4 showed that divided attention at study substantially reduced visual recollection but had little effect on auditory recollection, to the point that visual recollection in the divided attention condition was similar to auditory recollection in the full attention condition. This unusually small effect of divided attention on auditory recollection aligns with prior research showing fundamental differences in recognition of sounds and pictures. Further, it suggests that effects we have taken as regularities in recognition (such as divided attention) may not apply to all modalities.

title: Examining Factors that Influence Acceptability of Mindfulness-Based Cognitive Therapy: Experimental and Correlational Approaches
a3b3e2553b5586416d6251234d34c9213359d693.abstract: Objectives. Mindfulness-based interventions (MBIs) are widely used treatments that aim to increase clients' awareness and acceptance of their present-moment experiences. Although delivered as secular treatments, their practices have roots in East and South Asian religious traditions, raising concerns about acceptance among diverse religious or atheistic clients. Other MBI features, such as meditation and group-based formats, may also pose barriers to participation. We report two pre-registered experiments examining factors influencing acceptability of Mindfulness-Based Cognitive Therapy (MBCT). Methods. Study 1 (N = 305) tested whether scientific versus religious framings of MBCT influenced treatment acceptability, and whether effects were moderated by religiosity, existential quest (tendency toward exploratory engagement with existential questions), and scriptural literalism. Study 2 (N = 705) examined whether addressing participants' concerns about MBCT increased acceptability. Results. Contrary to hypotheses, Study 1 found no effects of scientific or religious framing on acceptability. However, regardless of framing, MBCT acceptability was higher among participants with greater existential quest (significantly) and greater religiosity (marginally). In Study 2, addressing participants' concerns (whether tailored to their specific concerns or covering all possible concerns) reduced concerns about MBCT and increased acceptability relative to no intervention. Similar to Study 1, religiosity was positively associated with acceptability regardless of condition. Conclusions. Together, these findings suggest that religiosity and existential quest may shape receptivity to MBCT, and that addressing client concerns, rather than adjusting how treatment is framed, may offer a promising route to increasing acceptability. Understanding these individual differences can inform strategies for engaging diverse populations in MBIs.

title: Threat-related gamma as a mechanism linking childhood maltreatment and adult anxiety
container-title: Cognitive, Affective, & Behavioral Neuroscience
753ddaf6f54150ce99708a12f3f559dbc7d05417.abstract: Abstract Hypervigilance to threats has been a proposed latent vulnerability to developing anxiety disorders in individuals who experienced childhood maltreatment (CM). While the neural mechanisms are increasingly being understood, their ecological and clinical validity remain limited. To address this issue, the current study aimed to elucidate novel mechanisms by combining the threat imminence continuum framework with computer-based virtual reality to examine electrophysiological indices of high (right posterior theta, 4–8 Hz) and low (posterior midline gamma, 30–60 Hz) imminence threats. University students ( N = 84, aged 18–34) self-reported anxiety symptoms by using the Beck Anxiety Inventory and State-Trait Anxiety Inventory, while CM history was indexed with the Childhood Trauma Questionnaire. EEG was collected while participants engaged in the Risk-Reward Interaction task, where right posterior theta and posterior midline gamma power were extracted as oscillatory markers. Structural equation modeling assessed the mediating effect of marker activity on the relationship between CM and anxiety. Posterior midline gamma power fully mediated the association between CM and anxiety (β = 0.1, p < .05), such that greater CM severity predicted increased gamma activity, in turn predicting increased anxiety. Right posterior theta power was not related to either anxiety or CM. Distortions of the threat imminence continuum, observed in posterior midline gamma activity, is a novel mechanism that may reflect a latent vulnerability to anxiety. These findings provide a new perspective with which to understand the emergence of CM-related psychopathology and has the potential to inform interventions to build resilience in this vulnerable population.
