title: Quantum resetting with memory
container-title: Journal of Physics A: Mathematical and Theoretical
3b279bb54a520fd66d5f862fd6a63ac23b7b9e63.abstract: Abstract We introduce a quantum stochastic resetting protocol with uniform memory, in which each resetting event returns the system to a state visited at a time chosen uniformly from its entire history. The resulting dynamics is nonunitary, non-Markovian and a direct quantum generalization of the classical preferential relocation model. Working in the energy eigenbasis, we derive the exact evolution of every densitymatrix element for an arbitrary time-independent Hamiltonian and show that the Hamiltonian enters the dynamics only through the corresponding Bohr frequencies. This leads to a natural distinction between two classes of quantum systems: gapped and gapless. In gapped systems (systems with a discrete energy spectrum), while the diagonal elements remain unchanged, the off-diagonal elements of the density matrix in the energy eigenbasis decay algebraically with a continuously varying exponent and with an amplitude that oscillates periodically in log t. The system therefore approaches a stationary state that is independent of the resetting rate and retains a strong memory of the initial state. In gapless systems (systems with a continuous energy spectrum), arbitrarily small Bohr frequencies prevent stationarity. Instead, the position distribution spreads on the universal (ultra-slow) scale log(rt)/r, independently of the initial state and of the details of the Hamiltonian. We illustrate these results with a two-level system, a harmonic oscillator, and a free quantum particle, and contrast them with their classical counterparts.

title: The Construction and Inheritance of Urban Memory through Visual Communication in the Context of Cultural Heritage
container-title: Academic Journal of History and Culture
b7a33a752c7d8b3f0a2d9c34a2aa47661ed95230.abstract: This paper will explore how visual communication can help to build and pass down urban memory in the context of cultural heritage conceptually. Archival photographs, maps, exhibitions, public interpretation and digital interfaces are selected representations of urban history, not comprehensive records of it. Based on the existing research of collective memory, cultural representation and heritage interpretation, this paper proposes an analytical path connecting source selection, visual organisation, public interpretation and opportunities for continuous engagement. Particular attention has been paid to the origin, the connection between material culture and daily life, and the addition of contradictory memories. There are no new interviews, surveys, observations or quantitative analyses in the paper. Therefore, the practical recommendations are design proposals rather than implemented measures. Responsible visual communication should make historical evidence accessible, retain a sense of the unknown, be mindful of representational choices, and enable community participation in the interpretation of urban history.

title: Digital Ancestralism: Reimagining Presence, Memory, and Spiritual Mediation among African Christian Youth in the Age of Social Media
container-title: International Journal of Business Ecosystem & Strategy (2687-2293)
e191fd684a7ec23399bae9d3a9ffcdefc3702180.abstract: Digital ancestralism has emerged as a significant theological and socio-cultural phenomenon among African Christian youth in South Africa, particularly through the increasing influence of social media and digital communication platforms. While African theology has long emphasised relational continuity between the living and the “living-dead,” limited attention has been given to how digital technologies reshape these relationships. Using a qualitative, literature-based and interpretive methodology, the study draws on interdisciplinary perspectives from African theology, digital religion and media studies to examine how digital platforms function as spaces of presence, memory and communal engagement. The paper argues that practices such as social media memorialisation, WhatsApp prayer groups and virtual funerals represent new forms of mediated relationality that extend traditional understandings of ancestry into digital environments. These practices are conceptualised as “digital ancestralism,” a hybrid theological condition that challenges binary distinctions such as sacred versus secular, presence versus absence and physical versus spiritual reality. Drawing on African relational ontology, mediatisation theory and networked religion, the study demonstrates how digital technologies do not merely transmit religious meaning but actively reshape theological experience and expression. The article highlights how African Christian youth act as agents of theological innovation, constructing spirituality within digitally networked contexts. The findings suggest that digital ancestralism is not a departure from tradition but a contextual reinterpretation of enduring African cosmological beliefs. The study concludes by proposing a constructive theological framework that calls for critical engagement with digitally mediated spirituality in relation to doctrines of presence, mediation, ecclesiology and eschatology within contemporary African Christianity.

967a0b028616881a92f247a0e78621c7ffaf8eea.abstract: يركز هذا البحث على تطبيق مفهوم "الأنطولوجيا الطيفية" (hauntology) -الذي صاغه جاك دريدا- من منظور نقدي؛ إذ يطرح أن الماضي في رواية "بيلوفد" (Beloved) للكاتبة توني موريسون لا يعود بوصفه حدثاً تاريخياً منقضياً أو شيئاً ينتمي حصراً إلى زمنٍ مضى، بل يظهر في هيئة "طيفية" تُربك الحاضر وتزعزعه. وتُبيّن التقنية السردية التي وظفتها موريسون -المتمحورة حول شخصية "بيلوفد" والمنزل المسكون في "124 بلوستون رود"- كيف يرفض الماضي، بذاكراته الحية، أن يطويه النسيان؛ وكيف تظل الصدمة حاضرة في تجسدٍ ملموس، وكيف تحمل المجتمعات في طياتها إرثاً قلقاً لمظالم الماضي. كما يتيح هذا المفهوم للباحث تفكيك الكيفية التي جرى بها تقويض التصور الخطي للزمن، وطمس الحدود الفاصلة بين الموتى والأحياء، مما يفرض على القارئ الانخراط في هذا العالم. وتكشف الدراسة -من خلال الاستعانة بدراسات الصدمة، ومناقشات الذاكرة، والنظرية الطيفية- كيف يعكس البناء السردي لدى موريسون -بما يتسم به من تفتت وتكرار وصمت وحضورٍ للأشباح- حتمية بقاء جروح الماضي؛ وبذلك، تُظهر كيف تحوّل الأدب، بفضل هذه التقنية السردية، إلى "مساحة للحداد".

title: Effects of Non-pharmacological Interventions on Cognitive Function and Quality of Life in Older Adults with Cognitive Impairment: A Systematic Review
container-title: International Journal of Public Health and Medical Research
8624c843c51c4e3817e216bd508a176c0e2cb5ca.abstract: Aim: To review changes in cognition and quality of life (QoL) following non-pharmacological interventions for older people with cognitive impairment, considering assessments conducted within one year of intervention. Methods: We searched PubMed, CINAHL and MEDLINE for English-language primary studies from 2015 to 14 April 2025. Eligible quantitative studies examined interventions relevant to nursing practice and reported cognition, QoL, or both. We used the 2018 Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool (MMAT) to assess methodological quality and compared findings through narrative synthesis. Results: The review included six randomised trials and five non-randomised studies. The 11 studies evaluated reminiscence, exercise, cognitive stimulation, music and programmes combining several activities. Some reported improvements in cognitive scores or well-being, but these were not consistent across measures or populations. In particular, gains in a memory subdomain or life satisfaction did not necessarily coincide with improvements in overall cognition or QoL. Assessment periods extended to six months. Conclusion: These studies suggest that selected non-pharmacological activities may support cognition or well-being over short periods. They do not establish a preferred intervention or demonstrate sustained benefit. Differences in study design and outcome measurement, together with methodological weaknesses, warrant cautious interpretation.

title: Cognitive impairment, medial temporal lobe changes, and fluid biomarkers of Alzheimer’s disease and neurodegeneration following herpes simplex virus type 1 encephalitis
container-title: Alzheimer's Research & Therapy
db422a17efb2e4a08e6e6dc49ac98535c7ffeba2.abstract: Abstract Background Herpesvirus encephalitis is a severe brain infection, in adults most often caused by herpes simplex virus type 1 (HSV-1). It predominantly affects the medial temporal lobes (MTL), which are critical for memory functions. Links have been discussed between herpes virus infections and Alzheimer’s disease (AD). We therefore investigated cognitive function, structural brain changes, and fluid biomarkers related to AD and other neurodegenerative processes in individuals with previous herpes simplex virus type 1 encephalitis (HSE). Methods Eleven patients with prior HSE were retrospectively identified using a clinical CSF laboratory database. Control groups included 44 cognitively unimpaired (CU) individuals, 44 mild cognitive impairment (MCI), and 22 AD dementia patients from the Swedish BioFINDER-2 study. Groups were stratified by amyloid-β (Aβ) status using CSF Aβ42/Aβ40. All participants underwent neuropsychological testing. Structural brain changes were assessed using 7T or 3T MRI including visual evaluation of lesions and automated segmentation of MTL subregions. Plasma biomarkers (tau phosphorylated at position 217 (p-tau217), p-tau181, glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP), and neurofilament light (NfL)) were measured using immunoassays. Results The mean follow-up time since infection was 6.5 years. The encephalitis group (mean age 49 years, 55% females) was age-matched to the CU Aβ- group but younger than other groups. MRI findings in the encephalitis group ranged from marked unilateral MTL atrophy to no visible changes. Compared with CU individuals, encephalitis patients showed significantly impaired episodic memory (delayed recall) and lower global cognition, comparable to MCI but less severe than AD dementia. Within the encephalitis group, episodic memory impairment was associated with visually assessed MTL atrophy ( p = 0.0185). In hemispheres without gross atrophy, MTL subregional volumes resembled CU and MCI but were larger than in AD dementia. Plasma p-tau217 and GFAP levels were elevated in the full HSE-group compared with Aβ-negative CU and MCI, but lower than in AD dementia. P-tau181 and NfL levels were similar to CU. P-tau217 was not significantly different between Aβ-negative HSE and Aβ-negative CU. Associations between GFAP and cognitive performance were no longer significant after exclusion of the two patients with Fazekas grade 3 white matter lesions. Conclusions Previous HSE was associated with substantial heterogeneity in long-term cognitive performance, with poorer delayed recall associated with longer time since infection. Cognitive findings were also related to focal MTL atrophy, supporting a contribution of structural injury to long-term cognitive outcomes. Only a minority of the patients had signs of AD pathology by CSF biomarkers. Larger longitudinal studies are needed to determine the trajectories and mechanisms of cognitive change following HSE.

title: Model for Long-Term Monitoring of Geological Processes in Kazakhstan Using Intelligent Drone Ports
container-title: Journal of Computational and Cognitive Engineering
cadf711f748149feb61cfec53452ca2675309b0e.abstract: The creation of autonomous systems for geomonitoring using unmanned aerial vehicles (UAV) and smart drone ports provide new possibilities for problem solving in geology, particularly in remote and geodynamically active areas of Kazakhstan. During the study, a multi-criteria mathematical model was created to compare drones with and without artificial intelligence (AI). The model contains ten standardized indicators of performance (autonomy, route planning, productivity, risk management, predicting geo-anomalies, scalability, etc.) with relative weights defined by experts. Analysis of the results revealed the high efficiency of the AI-oriented approach in processing time, spatial analysis, autonomy and scalability. The comparative assessment framework consists of 10 evaluation criteria weighted, namely autonomous management, route optimization, data processing efficiency, GIS integration, geoanomaly forecasting, resistance to external risks, operational efficiency, maintenance costs, data acquisition speed, and potential scalability. As a result, scientifically justified recommendations were made, and research areas were identified, such as the development of trend forecasting AI, the migration of drone ports to distributed mission planning, and the creation of a digital ecosystem of geomonitoring. The proposed framework offers a solid base of moving toward scalable, intelligent, as well as data-driven geomonitoring systems. The development of AI-powered drone-port infrastructure should play a crucial role in improving geological safety, facilitating timely hazard identification, and ensuring sustainable land-use planning in remote and geodynamically active areas. 5386e2eb173db472ec98b59a846cee832129db3b.abstract: Este artigo analisa criticamente as possibilidades e os limites da inteligência artificial generativa (IAG) como apoio à metacognição matemática na Educação Básica, considerando também as necessidades de acessibilidade de estudantes neurodivergentes. O problema de pesquisa indaga em que condições ferramentas conversacionais podem favorecer o planejamento, o monitoramento e a avaliação do próprio raciocínio, em vez de induzir dependência de respostas prontas. Desenvolve-se uma revisão narrativa crítica e documentada, de natureza qualitativa, com prioridade para publicações de 2022 a 2026 e documentos internacionais de referência. A análise distingue resultados de aprendizagem, autorregulação e autonomia intelectual, categorias frequentemente aproximadas de maneira indevida. A literatura aponta oportunidades de feedback e mediação, mas também riscos de imprecisão, desigualdade de acesso e terceirização cognitiva. Como contribuição propositiva, apresenta-se o ciclo pedagógico Antecipar–Argumentar–Verificar–Refletir (AAVR), com exemplos, critérios formativos e possibilidades de adaptação inclusiva para estudantes neurodivergentes. Conclui-se que a IAG pode funcionar como instrumento de diálogo crítico quando subordinada à validação matemática, à acessibilidade, à mediação docente e à proteção de dados. O modelo é teórico e necessita de validação empírica, inclusive em contextos educacionais inclusivos.

04283d155fc94f1d1ad6a075bebd83eb05de6716.abstract: This study examined the relationship between ChatGPT use and English-major students’ perceived improvement in English speaking. It focused on three aspects of ChatGPT use: frequency of use, speaking purposes, and interaction level. Data were collected from 238 English-major students at the Academy of Policy and Development in Vietnam using a 5-point Likert-scale questionnaire. Descriptive statistics, Cronbach’s alpha, exploratory factor analysis, Pearson correlation, and multiple regression were used for data analysis. The results showed positive associations between all three aspects of ChatGPT use and perceived improvement. Speaking purposes had the strongest association (r = .709), followed by interaction level (r = .699) and frequency of use (r = .614), with all p < .001. The multiple regression model was statistically significant, F(3, 234) = 239.977, p < .001, with the three predictors accounting for 75.5% of the variance in perceived improvement. Speaking purposes (β = .397), interaction level (β = .382), and frequency of use (β = .336) were significant predictors of perceived improvement. Students also reported relatively high perceived improvement across the five speaking dimensions, with fluency receiving the highest mean score (M = 4.01). Given the cross-sectional and self-reported nature of the data, the findings indicate statistical associations rather than causal effects.

title: Aprendizagem por Tensão Cognitivo-Identitária: fundamentos e proposição do modelo da curva crítica
Learning through Cognitive-Identity Tension: Foundations and the proposal of a critical curve model
Aprendizagem por Tensão Cognitivo-Identitária
container-title: Revista Educação, Psicologia e Interfaces
cb215373fd39c75f6685cdc7114e9461b988af44.abstract: A aprendizagem tem sido historicamente compreendida como um processo de aquisição, processamento e retenção de informações, sendo amplamente analisada por perspectivas cognitivas e socioculturais. Contudo, tais abordagens tendem a atribuir menor centralidade aos impactos do conhecimento sobre a identidade do sujeito. Este artigo tem como objetivo apresentar os fundamentos da Teoria da Aprendizagem por Tensão Cognitivo-Identitária (TTCI), propondo um modelo teórico para compreender a aprendizagem como resultante da tensão entre novos conhecimentos e estruturas identitárias previamente consolidadas. Metodologicamente, trata-se de uma pesquisa qualitativa, de abordagem teórica e caráter exploratório, fundamentada na revisão e articulação crítica de referenciais da psicologia do desenvolvimento e psicologia social. Como principais resultados, o estudo propõe os conceitos de inércia identitária e curva de tensão crítica como operadores analíticos para compreender os processos de resistência, reorganização subjetiva e aprendizagem significativa, além de discutir o papel da mediação pedagógica na regulação da tensão cognitivo-identitária. Conclui-se que a aprendizagem pode ser compreendida como um fenômeno simultaneamente cognitivo, subjetivo e formativo, cuja efetividade tende a depender do equilíbrio entre tensão, identidade e mediação pedagógica, contribuindo para ampliar a compreensão dos processos educativos na educação básica e superior.

title: Children with ADHD recruit perceptual over meaningful memory
7d39b6cb9fda5edfba9ce3e01865d071610e8cf3.abstract: Abstract Memory is formed through two distinct forms: reactivation of perceptual traces and meaningful reconstruction into conceptual representations. How memory diverges across development remains unclear in humans. Here, we applied representational similarity analysis (RSA) to electroencephalography (EEG) data from 114 children with attention deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) and 109 typically developing (TD) children (aged 6–12 years) while they performed a recognition memory task. We revealed distinct neural mechanisms for perceptual memory and meaningful memory. Specifically, children with ADHD predominantly engaged in sensory reactivation in parietal‒occipital regions, whereas TD children engaged prefrontal areas to support meaningful memory transformation. Deep neural networks (DNN) further revealed that memory transformation occurred during encoding through semanticization of images. Further, intersubject correlation (ISC) revealed differences in memory patterns between both groups of children, providing potential neurobiological evidence for impaired memory transformation in children with ADHD. Our findings reveal that children with ADHD recruit perceptual reactivation over meaningful memory, highlighting the critical role of semantic transformation in the developmental emergence of meaningful memory.

title:
Ferroelectric
AlScN Four-Mode Reconfigurable Transistors
Enabling Unified Logic, Memory, and Neuromorphic Computing
container-title: ACS Nano
6976b3d1eb3e24679465eb0c90c253ecc7304aa4.abstract: Abstract The increasing demand for data-centric and artificial intelligence workloads has intensified the need for device platforms that integrate logic, memory, and adaptive computing beyond conventional von Neumann architectures. Here, an aluminum scandium nitride (AlScN)-based nonvolatile four-mode reconfigurable field-effect transistor is demonstrated as a multifunctional device platform. By combining the large remanent polarization of AlScN with the ambipolar transport of the MoTe2 channel, the same transistor can be persistently programmed into logic nFET, logic pFET, memory-on, and memory-off states. These modes arise from polarization-controlled modulation of carrier injection and channel electrostatics, enabling a single device to function as a polarity-reconfigurable logic element, nonvolatile memory cell, and analog synaptic element. Programming is performed through voltage pulses applied to the source, drain, and back gate, while top-gate readout is decoupled from AlScN programming, enabling stable nonvolatile operation. Based on this device, a single-transistor ternary content-addressable memory cell concept and two-input reconfigurable multifunctional logic gates are demonstrated. The wide polarization-tunable memory window further supports multilevel cell memory and nearly linear long-term potentiation and depression for neuromorphic synaptic operation. These results establish ferroelectric AlScN as a robust platform for integrating reconfigurable logic, nonvolatile memory, associative search, and neuromorphic computing within a common device framework.

title: Four‐Year Cognitive Outcomes in Multiple Sclerosis: Associations With Lesion Myelin Integrity
container-title: Annals of Clinical and Translational Neurology
08949470161dcce0382c6c2e76c067bde8bcfc46.abstract: ABSTRACT Objectives Cognitive impairment is prevalent in patients with multiple sclerosis (MS) but whether lesion myelin integrity influences future cognitive outcomes remains unclear. We investigated the relationship between baseline lesion myelin water fraction (MWF) and cognitive performance 4 years later. Methods We conducted a longitudinal study of 118 patients with MS. Cognitive function was evaluated annually for 5 years using the symbol digit modalities test (SDMT), California verbal learning test–II (CVLT‐II) immediate recall, and brief visuospatial memory test–revised (BVMT‐R). Lesion level MWF maps were the primary variable of interest, while paramagnetic rim lesions (PRLs) and structural imaging measures were included as covariates. We used a functional linear regression model with both scalar and functional covariates, followed by a stepwise variable selection procedure. Results After adjustment for baseline cognition and clinical covariates, participants with higher baseline lesion‐level MWF values in the mid‐range of the lesion distribution exhibited better SDMT at 4 years ( p = 0.006). Greater heterogeneity in lesion‐level MWF was associated with worse visuospatial memory performance on the BVMT‐R at Year 4. Conversely, lesion MWF was not associated with CVLT‐II performance. Additional covariates in the final models included PRLs and cortical thinning for SDMT, PRLs and disease duration for BVMT‐R, and thalamic atrophy for CVLT‐II. Interpretation Lesion myelin integrity was associated with future cognitive performance, particularly in domains of processing speed and visuospatial memory. These findings suggest that lesion demyelination contributes to cognitive outcomes in MS, which may provide a potential focus for future work improving risk stratification for cognitive impairment.

Intermittent Fasting and Cognitive Performance in Adults: A Narrative Review
container-title: International Journal For Multidisciplinary Research
4f5bcc67c97c66b71919b04e9dc5d2934e59a4f8.abstract: ABSTRACT Background: Intermittent fasting (IF) is widely promoted for metabolic and brain health, and mechanistic research suggests that fasting-induced metabolic switching could influence brain function. Human evidence on cognition is, however, limited and heterogeneous, and acute (single) fasting episodes differ from repeated IF regimens in their physiological and behavioural effects. Objective: To review human evidence on IF and cognitive performance in adults, focusing on acute responses, repeated interventions, potential cognitive adaptation, and proposed mechanisms. Methods: This narrative review considered human experimental studies, randomised controlled trials, observational studies, and systematic reviews identified through scholarly searches on IF, time-restricted eating, alternate-day fasting, experimental fasting, and cognitive performance. Animal and laboratory studies were included to explain potential mechanisms. Findings were synthesised by fasting approach and cognitive domain. Results: Human studies suggest that cognitive performance is generally maintained during the acute fasting conditions investigated, although responses vary according to fasting duration, participant characteristics, and cognitive domains. Repeated IF interventions have generally shown no consistent cognitive advantage over control diets or continuous calorie restriction. Nevertheless, selected studies have reported improvements in specific cognitive outcomes, particularly among adults with obesity and older adults with mild cognitive impairment. Potential mechanisms include altered ketone utilisation, neurotrophic signalling, regulation of oxidative stress, and modulation of neuroinflammation. Although experimental findings support these biological pathways, their contribution to cognitive improvements in humans remains incompletely understood. Conclusion: Intermittent fasting represents an emerging area of research in nutritional approaches to brain health and cognitive function. Current human findings suggest that cognitive performance is generally preserved under several studied fasting conditions, with preliminary evidence of improvements in selected cognitive domains. IF may be explored as a potential adjunctive lifestyle approach alongside appropriate medical care; however, the relationship between fasting duration, repeated exposure, and cognitive adaptation remains an important area for further investigation. Larger, longer-duration clinical trials using standardised cognitive assessments are needed to clarify these effects and their potential relevance to cognitive health.

20f152a141ba44dc8872dd287c4138dbea04dee1.abstract: ABSTRACT To improve the elongation at break of poly (lactic acid) (PLA) and retain its shape memory properties, in this study, polyethylene glycol (PEG) was employed as a plasticizer and incorporated chain extenders ADR‐4370 and ADR‐4400. The effects of PEG and chain extender on the microstructure, mechanical properties, shape memory properties, thermal properties, stability, and optical properties of the ADR/PEG/PLA films were investigated. The results showed that the chain extenders improved the interfacial compatibility and further increased the elongation at break. The shape memory recovery ratio ( R r ) of the films was highest at a recovery temperature of 80°C. The composite films with higher PEG molecular weight exhibited better shape memory performance. With increasing ADR‐4370 content, R r first increased and then decreased, whereas with increasing ADR‐4400 content, R r increased continuously, and orientation‐induced crystallization was generated. PEG promoted PLA crystallization; chain extender‐induced chain extension/branching and interfacial coupling inhibited crystal growth. ADR‐4370 enhanced the thermal stability of the films at the high‐temperature stage, and ADR‐4400 improved the thermal stability at the initial stage. UV–Vis spectroscopy showed that the ADR‐4370‐modified films exhibited significantly enhanced UV shielding and markedly reduced visible‐light transparency, whereas ADR‐4400 caused relatively small changes.

title: Seismic Performance of Reinforced-Concrete Beam-Column Joints With Conventional Steel and Hybrid Shape-Memory-Alloy/Fiber- Reinforced-Polymer Reinforcement: A Critical Review
18fde61182463c7c834fc1e98a46da247093c94e.abstract: Abstract Background Reinforced-concrete (RC) beam-column joints are critical regions in moment-resisting frames because they must transfer large cyclic moments, shear forces, and axial forces while maintaining anchorage integrity and structural continuity during earthquakes. Conventional steel-reinforced joints can provide substantial strength and hysteretic energy dissipation when properly detailed, but severe cyclic loading may produce reinforcement yielding, bond deterioration, joint shear damage, corrosion-related durability problems, and permanent residual deformation. Purpose —This review critically evaluates conventional reinforcement, shape-memory-alloy (SMA) reinforcement, fiber-reinforced-polymer (FRP) systems, and emerging SMA+FRP hybrid concepts for improving the seismic performance and resilience of RC beam-column joints. Coverage Particular emphasis is placed on literature published from 2023 to 16 August 2026, supplemented by landmark earlier studies required to establish joint mechanics, SMA constitutive behaviour, FRP strengthening principles, and the origin of hybrid SMA-FRP concepts. Findings —The literature indicates that SMA reinforcement is particularly effective for self-centering and residual-deformation control, whereas FRP systems are attractive for corrosion resistance, joint shear strengthening, confinement, and minimally invasive rehabilitation. However, SMA systems can provide narrower hysteresis than yielding steel, while FRP performance is strongly controlled by bond, anchorage, fiber orientation, substrate condition, and brittle failure. Hybridization offers a rational means of combining restoring capability with strength, confinement, durability, and energy-dissipation mechanisms. Research gap —Direct, recent, full-scale experimental validation of true SMA+FRP RC beam-column joints remains sparse, particularly under bidirectional loading, variable axial force, slab participation, temperature effects, aftershocks, and multi-hazard exposure. Conclusion —SMA+FRP hybrid joints represent a promising resilience-oriented structural concept, but standardized detailing, validated nonlinear models, probabilistic performance assessment, life-cycle evaluation, and code-ready design procedures are required before routine engineering implementation.

title: Roadmap for cognitive neurorehabilitation: challenges and opportunities
container-title: Current Opinion in Neurology
0bb7242df07a9973f6f18c6e72a4268bad7037de.abstract: Purpose of review Cognitive deficits affect 40–50% of patients after acquired brain injury, with a profound impact on participation, work capacity and quality of life. Cognitive neurorehabilitation is a relevant and promising approach to promote cognitive recovery, but the evidence remains limited. This review discusses the clinical state-of-the-art, open questions in clinical research, and outlines a roadmap for future development of this rapidly evolving domain. Recent findings While optimal contemporary cognitive neurorehabilitation is multimodal and interprofessional, the currently available evidence is diluted by heterogeneous treatment content and patient characteristics, as well as by inadequate methodology and reporting. Several questions remain open: the optimal dose and frequency of therapy, the preferable sequence of treatments, and the factors that moderate treatment effects. We highlight the pressing need for rigorously designed randomized controlled trials (RCTs) with active control conditions, everyday-relevant outcome measures, time by group interaction analyses and long-term follow-up. Summary Future development of cognitive neurorehabilitation depends on RCTs and single-case experiments using cutting-edge methodology. We propose a roadmap with four tiers: mechanisms and efficacy, assessment of moderating factors, clinical validity as well as consideration of socio-economic impact and implementation from the outset. International collaboration in designing, developing and validating the approaches is warranted to ensure standardization and broad uptake. These efforts will promote the quality and accessibility of cognitive neurorehabilitation.

Drawing on the hermeneutic legacies of Paul Ricoeur and Richard Kearney, it analyses the models of «hospitality of translation», «memory exchange», and «forgiveness». title: Deep Learning in Education: Socioeconomic, Cognitive and Metacognitive Predictors of Academic Achievement and Learning Retention—A Structural Equation Modelling Study
container-title: International Journal of Advanced Research in Science Communication and Technology
9ace06254a29903fd87636334016381c69b0ab44.abstract: Deep learning in education denotes an approach through which students seek meaning, connect new knowledge with prior understanding, critically evaluate ideas and apply concepts beyond immediate assessment. It differs from surface learning centred on reproduction and memorisation. Foundational investigations distinguished qualitative differences in students’ learning approaches (Marton & Säljö, 1976), while subsequent frameworks connected deep, surface and strategic approaches with learning environments and academic outcomes (Entwistle & Ramsden, 1983; Biggs, 1987). Evidence from higher education suggests that learning approaches and study behaviours have meaningful, though not necessarily large, associations with achievement (Richardson et al., 2012).

title: Analysis of Risk Factors and Development of a Prediction Model for Cognitive Dysfunction Associated with Pediatric Sepsis
38a8f0a24ad688aa8d1d11f86ff38689e36ba194.abstract: Abstract Objective To investigate the risk factors for cognitive dysfunction in pediatric patients with sepsis, to develop a visualized risk prediction nomogram model, and to validate it. Methods A total of 206 pediatric patients with sepsis admitted to the PICU of Gansu Maternal and Child Health Hospital between January 2021 and December 2024 were enrolled as study subjects. Based on their Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA) scores obtained 12 months after discharge, these patients were divided into a cognitive impairment group (n = 78) and a normal cognition group (n = 128). Using a stratified random sampling method at a ratio of 7:3, the patients were further subdivided into a training cohort (n = 144) and a validation cohort (n = 62). The training cohort was used to identify risk factors for cognitive dysfunction and to establish a predictive model, while the validation cohort was used to evaluate the predictive performance of the model. Within the training cohort, differences in general clinical data and laboratory parameters between the two groups were analyzed and compared; LASSO regression was employed for variable selection; multivariate logistic regression analysis was conducted to identify independent risk factors; and a nomogram prediction model was constructed. The discriminative ability of the model was evaluated using the receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve and the area under the ROC curve (AUC); the calibration performance was assessed using calibration curves and the Hosmer–Lemeshow test; and the Decision Curve Analysis (DCA) was used to evaluate the clinical utility of the model. Internal validation was subsequently performed on the validation cohort. Results Among the 206 pediatric patients, 78 cases (37.86%) developed cognitive dysfunction. In the training cohort, statistically significant differences were observed between the two groups of pediatric patients regarding duration of mechanical ventilation, admission PCIS score, proportion of patients with septic shock, NE%, CRP, PCT, D-dimer, Lac, CK, Cys-C, Cr, Glu, and Ca levels (P < 0.05). Multivariate logistic regression analysis revealed that septic shock (OR = 3.267, 95% CI: 1.611–6.625), CRP (OR = 1.006, 95% CI: 1.003–1.009), Lac (OR = 1.135, 95% CI: 1.001–1.287), Cys-C (OR = 2.006, 95% CI: 1.287–3.128), and Glu (OR = 1.234, 95% CI: 1.087–1.400) were independent risk factors for cognitive dysfunction in pediatric patients with sepsis. The nomogram model constructed based on these factors demonstrated AUC values of 0.810 in the training cohort and 0.795 in the validation cohort. The Hosmer–Lemeshow goodness-of-fit test results indicated good model performance. with P = 0.973 in the training cohort and P = 0.843 in the validation cohort. The DCA curve showed that the model exhibited favorable clinical net benefit within the probability threshold range of 0.1–0.9. Conclusion Septic shock, CRP, Lac, Cys-C and Glu are independent risk factors for cognitive dysfunction in pediatric patients with sepsis. The nomogram prediction model developed based on these factors demonstrates excellent discriminative ability, calibration, and clinical utility.

title: AI Literacy among Undergraduate Chemistry Students from a Social Cognitive Perspective
cf071f618f19832fe3808f5ce3407ca96dd9f73d.abstract: AI literacy is increasingly important in undergraduate chemistry education, where students must evaluate generated explanations against chemical principles and evidence. However, the conditions shaping chemistry students’ engagement with AI remain insufficiently understood. Guided by Social Cognitive Theory, this qualitative study examined semi-structured interviews with 36 undergraduate chemistry students from 22 higher education institutions in China. Thematic analysis identified interrelated personal, behavioral, and environmental influences. Participants who expressed confidence in using AI also described selective reliance and deliberate efforts to retain responsibility for academic work. Expected benefits included efficiency and opportunities to ask questions with less perceived interpersonal judgment. Peers and senior students were prominent sources of practical guidance, often preceding formal instruction amid inconsistent institutional expectations. These findings suggest that AI literacy involves self-regulation, affective considerations, and informal social learning. For chemistry educators, they highlight the importance of supporting students’ judgment about AI-assisted explanations, creating space to discuss conceptual uncertainty, and making standards for evaluating chemical claims explicit within peer interactions. The study contributes a qualitative account of how undergraduate chemistry students understand and negotiate AI use within their learning environments.

title: Progressive task-oriented extended reality in a cognitive stimulation programme for older adults with mild or early cognitive impairment: a pragmatic clinical trial of patient adaptation, usability and cognitive-functional outcomes
container-title: Frontiers in Virtual Reality
15da1ef5122134e255e45e1cb72ab55909517e8b.abstract: Objective Extended reality (XR) can incorporate cognitive training into sensory, cognitive-motor and functionally oriented tasks, but delivery depends on matching task and interaction demands to participants. We examined how a progressively introduced XR component could be integrated and adapted within routine cognitive stimulation for older adults with mild or early cognitive impairment, with exploratory comparison of cognitive and functional change against computerised cognitive training alone. Methods This single-centre, non-randomised controlled trial included 70 rehabilitation courses from 59 individuals. Both groups received supervised computerised cognitive training for 12 weeks; 45 courses allocated 15–20 min of scheduled sessions to XR, while 25 received computerised cognitive training alone. XR progressed from familiarisation and guided 360° environments to mixed-reality cognitive-motor tasks, immersive everyday-task virtual reality and controller-based cognitive exercises. Exposure, task and interface difficulties, adaptations, adverse symptoms and usability were recorded. Exploratory comparisons of the trial’s prespecified primary cognitive and functional outcomes used generalised estimating equations (GEE) with participant-level clustering and Holm adjustment. Results Across 45 XR-supported courses, 729 participant-exposures were recorded and 715 (98.1%) were fully delivered. Task understanding or execution difficulties affected 25/43 controller-based XR courses, compared with 5/40 mixed-reality and 6/43 immersive everyday-task virtual reality courses. Interaction or interface difficulties occurred only with controller-based XR (4/43, 9.3%). Patient-perceived usability was 68.50 ± 16.57/100 and headset comfort and tolerability 81.99 ± 14.54/100. Professional-perceived usability was 85/100 (n = 4). Adverse symptoms occurred in 30/729 exposures (4.1%), affecting 14/45 XR participants (31.1%), with no serious adverse events or symptom-related discontinuations. In 38 XR-supported and 23 non-XR pre-post courses, exploratory adjusted between-group differences remained after Holm adjustment for the Mini-Mental State Examination (+1.62, p = 0.013) and Montreal Cognitive Assessment (+1.88, p = 0.030), but not Lawton-Brody or other cognitive outcomes. Conclusion Progressively introduced, clinician-supervised XR was repeatedly deliverable within routine cognitive stimulation, with adverse symptoms uncommon at the exposure level and no serious events. Rather than treating XR as a uniform intervention, these findings support selecting and adapting configurations according to their immersion, interaction and task demands, participant capabilities and practical delivery conditions. Exploratory MMSE and MoCA between-group differences warrant further controlled study but do not establish an XR-specific treatment effect. Clinical Trial Registration NCT06977815, https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06977815 .

title: Validity, diagnostic accuracy, and feasibility of trail making test in virtual reality for mild cognitive impairment
container-title: Frontiers in Digital Health
2306211350bff1696f993042a99158fef0f321cd.abstract: Background Immersive virtual reality (VR) adaptations of neuropsychological tests change how participants respond and must be validated in each clinical population. We evaluated the Trail Making Test in Virtual Reality (TMT-VR), a head-gaze version of the paper-and-pencil Trail Making Test (hereafter, TMT) that records completion times and wrong-target selections automatically, in older adults with and without mild cognitive impairment (MCI). Methods In this case–control evaluation, 84 adults aged 60–89 years (42 with clinically diagnosed MCI, 42 healthy comparison participants) completed the TMT-VR, the TMT and the Mini-Addenbrooke's Cognitive Examination (M-ACE). Planned analyses examined feasibility, convergence, group differences and diagnostic accuracy for all 26 TMT-VR scores against their TMT counterparts and the M-ACE, with demographic adjustment, multiplicity correction and sensitivity analyses. Results All participants completed both TMT-VR parts, and cybersickness ratings decreased over the session. Part B completion times correlated moderately across formats, more clearly in healthy participants. Participants with MCI were slower and made more wrong-target selections on TMT-VR Part B but not Part A. Part B completion-time discrimination did not differ detectably between formats. The Part B, total and B − A error scores and the Part B-specific derived scores discriminated MCI more strongly in the TMT-VR, with paired differences excluding zero for the error scores but none surviving Holm correction. The TMT's advantage lay in Part A completion time; its Part B difference depended more on education than the TMT-VR's. Education-matched and comparison-group sensitivity analyses showed the same direction. The M-ACE discriminated more accurately than any single trail-making score of either format. Conclusions In this initial case–control evaluation the TMT-VR was feasible and well tolerated, converged partially with the TMT and showed known-groups validity for MCI. Its Part B-specific and error-based scores showed higher point estimates of discriminative accuracy than the corresponding TMT scores, consistently across related scores, so it is a candidate trail-making format for neuropsychological batteries in MCI, albeit one that requires further examination. Residual confounding by education cannot be excluded, and the reference standard was asymmetric; test–retest reliability, reference values and incremental value beyond a global screen remain to be established in consecutive clinical referrals.

title: A Robust and Lightweight Deep Learning Framework for Cooperative Spectrum Sensing in Cognitive Radio Ad Hoc Networks Under Dynamic Channel Conditions
container-title: Computer and Decision Making: An International Journal
64905d73cd16b1c6c0621f4e16f7c5abebbeae3b.abstract: Cognitive Radio Ad Hoc Networks (CRAHNs) provide a flexible approach to improving spectrum utilization by enabling secondary users (SUs) to access licensed frequency bands whenever primary users (PUs) are inactive. The effectiveness of this approach depends on accurate spectrum occupancy detection, as missed detections can cause harmful interference to licensed communications, whereas false alarms unnecessarily restrict spectrum access for secondary users. Although deep learning has demonstrated potential for processing complex radio-frequency signals, modulation recognition and binary spectrum occupancy detection represent distinct tasks, and results obtained under limited simulation conditions may not adequately reflect real-world network variability. To address these challenges, this study proposes an evaluation framework for cooperative spectrum sensing based on a Convolutional Neural Network–Bidirectional Gated Recurrent Unit with an attention mechanism (CNN–BiGRU–Attention). The convolutional component extracts discriminative local features from in-phase and quadrature (I/Q) signal samples, while the bidirectional recurrent layer captures temporal dependencies and the attention mechanism emphasizes informative representations relevant to primary-user detection. To improve cooperative decision-making, the framework incorporates both majority-voting and confidence-weighted fusion strategies for combining sensing information from multiple secondary users. The proposed approach will be evaluated against conventional energy detection and representative deep learning architectures, including 1D-CNN, LSTM, GRU, Temporal Convolutional Network (TCN), and a lightweight Transformer. The experimental design considers variations in signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), noise uncertainty, fading environments, the number of cooperating secondary users, reporting-channel impairments, and previously unseen channel conditions. Evaluation will focus on probability of detection at a specified false-alarm rate, missed-detection probability, receiver operating characteristic area under the curve (ROC-AUC), computational latency, model size, and cooperative reporting overhead. A controlled binary occupancy dataset with explicitly defined signal-presence labels and scenario-level data separation will be used to support reproducible experimentation and reduce data leakage between training and evaluation sets. The study is intended to assess not only detection performance but also the trade-offs between sensing reliability, computational cost, and cooperative communication requirements. Experimental results and comparative conclusions will be reported only after implementation and systematic testing; therefore, this abstract makes no claims of measured performance improvement or established superiority over existing methods.

title: Study protocol for evidence-based LIFEstyle interventions for the delay of COgnitive DEcline among Singaporean older adults (LIFECODES): a randomized controlled trial
container-title: Frontiers in Aging Neuroscience
2e0973bd0e12c1106dd30d0d1f2e39d1be3275f5.abstract: Background Singapore’s rapidly aging population has led to a widening gap between total and healthy life expectancy. Dementia affects approximately 10% of adults aged ≥ 60 years, and 152,000 people are projected to be living with dementia by 2030. Up to 45% of dementia cases may theoretically be prevented or delayed by addressing 14 modifiable risk factors across the life course. However, evidence on clinically effective, culturally tailored multidomain interventions for older Singaporeans remains limited. The LIFEstyle interventions for the delay of COgnitive DEcline among older Singaporean adults (LIFECODES) trial evaluates the effects of a multidomain lifestyle intervention on cognitive decline and the added value of individualized health coaching. Secondary aims examine epigenetic aging and systemic inflammation. Methods LIFECODES is a three-arm proof-of-concept randomized controlled trial at the National University of Singapore (NUS) aiming to enroll 120 community-dwelling adults aged 60–75 years with signs of cognitive decline. Participants are randomized to group-based health education (GHE), GHE plus individualized health coaching (HC), or general care. The two-year intervention comprises 27 in-person sessions addressing eight lifestyle domains relevant to dementia risk: diet, physical activity, cognitive activity, social engagement, mental well-being, sleep, smoking and alcohol consumption. The primary outcome is cognitive processing speed. Secondary outcomes include memory, executive function and other cognitive domains, DNA methylation (DNAm) age, inflammatory biomarkers, functional status, psychosocial well-being, and sleep quality. Interim Results As of 14 September 2026, 190 individuals had been screened, and 110 (57.9%) met the eligibility criteria. Seven eligible individuals withdrew before randomization and 12 withdrew after randomization. A total of 91 participants are currently enrolled in the study (GHE, n = 30; HC, n = 30; control, n = 31). The first rolling intervention cohort began on 15 May 2025. Among the 91 participants, the mean age is 68.7 years (SD 4.2), and 66 (72.5%) are female. Recruitment and follow-up remain ongoing. Conclusion Interim recruitment and randomization indicate that a community-based multidomain dementia-prevention trial can be initiated in Singapore. Planned analyses will determine intervention efficacy and the added value of individualized health coaching for cognitive health and biological aging. Clinical trial registration https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06661486 , identifier NCT06661486.

title: PRISM-AD quantifies clinical and genetic contributions to cognitive risk prediction
978abe5defc77ee89cd5d242dbbed39eaa2e156f.abstract: Abstract Background Older adults with high inherited Alzheimer’s disease (AD) susceptibility can still be cognitively normal (CN). An overall risk estimate alone does not show the cognitive and genetic contributions within a forecast. Objective To quantify clinical and genetic contributions to cognitive prognosis. Methods PRISM-AD combined nonlinear clinical functions and a polygenic risk score (PRS) term in 4,435 European-ancestry participants. Participant-level internal validation evaluated first recorded mild cognitive impairment (MCI) after CN in 908 participants and AD dementia after MCI in 714, within three or five years. Separately fitted comparators used identical inputs. Post hoc clinical-course comparisons used regression with robust standard errors and Benjamini–Hochberg (BH) correction. Results PRISM-AD using current assessments achieved average precision of 0.2996 and 0.4094 for three- and five-year CN-to-MCI, with estimates close to logistic regression. No PRISM-AD PRS increment met BH q < 0.05. Three-year first-MCI forecasts characterized risk contributions in 893 initially CN participants. A retrospective comparison over available follow-up included 95 participants with later AD and 701 with CN at their last diagnostic assessment. Modeled genetic factors were higher in later AD in nine of ten shared cognitive-risk deciles. After adjustment for modeled cognitive risk and fold, the genetic-factor ratio was 1.135 (nominal 95% CI, 1.073 to 1.201, BH q < 0.001). Conclusions Higher genetic contributions were associated with later AD at comparable modeled cognitive risk. These exploratory profiles require independent validation before use in cognitive follow-up or prevention research.

title: Himalayan Tartary Buckwheat Sprout Powder, Perceived Cognitive Abilities, and Objective Processing Speed: A Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled Trial
8ec2d6e6d87f2b1325fb8a85a181b1ef5c52a59c.abstract: Abstract Subjective cognitive difficulties are common in midlife and later life, and flavonoid-rich foods may support everyday cognitive function. Tartary buckwheat ( Fagopyrum tataricum ) sprouts are rich in rutin and other flavonoids, but their cognitive effects have not been tested in humans. In this randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial, US adults with self-reported cognitive difficulties received 18 g per day of Himalayan Tartary buckwheat (HTB) sprout powder or matched placebo for 12 weeks. Of 848 randomized participants, 662 were analyzed. While the rate of change in the primary outcome, PROMIS Cognitive Function, did not differ between arms (contrast = 0.03, 95% CI −0.07 to 0.13; p = .59), PROMIS Cognitive Abilities improved nominally faster with HTB (contrast = 0.12, 95% CI 0.00 to 0.24; p = .046), but not after Bonferroni adjustment. Among participants with final-week data (n = 296), more HTB than placebo participants achieved a meaningful (≥0.5 SD) improvement in Cognitive Abilities (68.7% vs 52.5%; RR = 1.32, 95% CI 1.10 to 1.59; p = .003). Fatigue, sleep-related impairment and depressive symptoms did not differ between arms. In exploratory computerized testing (n = 512), HTB participants had faster reaction times on the Flanker and Stroop tasks, without loss of accuracy. Exploratory epigenetic analyses (n = 34) identified hypothesis-generating signals in epigenetic age and immune-cell composition, none surviving multiple-testing correction. Side-effect rates were similar between arms. HTB sprout powder did not improve the primary outcome, but findings for perceived cognitive abilities and processing speed warrant confirmation in adequately powered trials. Trial registration: NCT07245784 .

title: How Does Cognitive Dissonance Explain Why Consumers Justify Expensive Purchases After the Fact (Post-Purchase Rationalization), And What Does This Mean for Return-Policy Design?
container-title: Journal of Economics, Finance And Management Studies
a1f823ae1a8f2f0a9453d97a6b885ecffdac6134.abstract: This paper explores the cognitive dissonance theory developed by Leon Festinger (Festinger, 1957) as an answer to explain why consumers in their normal practices justify their high-cost purchases after they make them. This is often referred to as post-purchase rationalization and/or "buyer's remorse management". Based on the social-psychological literature on dissonance reduction, the consumer-behaviour research on post-purchase evaluation (Oliver, 1980; Sweeney, Hausknecht, & Soutar, 2000), and the current literature on retail returns (National Retail Federation & Happy Returns, 2024, 2025), the paper proposes a framework that integrates purchase involvement, decision irreversibility, and self-concept threat with the intensity of post-purchase dissonance and the rationalization strategies consumers use to manage it. The paper then moves on to the implications of this psychology for the firm, that is, the design of return policies. The ease at which a consumer can reverse a purchase decision has a direct effect on the psychological dynamics of dissonance, with lenient return policies making customers more likely to convert to a purchase and causing a window where dissonance can arise as an actual return. The paper utilizes data from the National Retail Federation, Janakiraman, Syrdal, and Freling (2016) meta-analysis of the U.S. retail return literature, and other secondary sources to illustrate that there were an estimated $890 billion worth of U.S. retail returns in 2024 (16.9% of sales), a slight decrease to estimated $849.9 billion worth of U.S. retail returns in 2025 (15.8%), and leniency dimensions (e.g. monetary, temporal, effort, scope and exchange) have an asymmetric influence on purchase and return behaviour. The paper ends with a section on policy design that proposes a framework for structuring the return windows, restocking fees, exchange vs refund default, and post-purchase communication that strikes a balance between the benefits of conversion and the costs of return, while also promoting real satisfaction for customers, not just the suppression of regret.

title: Attachment Styles, Cognitive Distortion and Interpersonal Problems Among Emerging Adults
container-title: Adolescência e Saúde
75f62ee6ecc646f4f175f8bb684dc8451c1fd1e1.abstract: The beginning of adulthood is a stage of life that is marked by a persistent reliance on parents in the face of unpredictable changes in relationships, employment, education, and finances. The present article is an attempt to understand whether emerging adults' interpersonal problems, cognitive distortion, and attachment style are related in any way. A sample of 200 developing adults was chosen on purpose. Assessments were conducted on interpersonal problems, cognitive distortion, and attachment styles. We employed Spearman's correlation test. The findings indicate a positive correlation between cognitive distortion and the interpersonal problem subscales measuring dependence and difficulty in providing support. Hard to be supportive and fearful attachment styles are positively correlated. Interpersonal problems and attachment styles are positively correlated.

title: Postoperative Cognitive Dysfunction in Elderly: A Literature Review
container-title: Adolescência e Saúde
0059989468caf95d98fb067257b9c0d9d3b527d4.abstract: The increasing number of older adults undergoing surgery poses significant challenges for clinicians involved in perioperative care, particularly regarding the risk of postoperative cognitive impairment. Postoperative cognitive dysfunction (POCD) in the elderly is notably more prevalent and associated with poor outcomes, highlighting the need for effective management strategies. As neuroinflammation has been described as a fundamental mechanism in neurodegenerative diseases, this literature review summarizes the role of neuroinflammation in relation to surgical stress and age-related changes, identifies risk factors, with emphasis on preventive care through comprehensive assesment, prehabilitation and optimisation during the perioperative period to preserve cognitive function.

title: An Empirical Study of Cognitive Behavioural Therapy, Mindfulness, Mental Health and Cognitive Performance Among Secondary School Students in Vadodara
container-title: Adolescência e Saúde
dd14391fd25bd99dd928291109c2f015a2b866d1.abstract: Background: Anxiety, low mood and difficulties with memory, problem solving and decision making are common concerns during adolescence, and school-based psychological approaches such as Cognitive Behavioural Therapy (CBT) and mindfulness are increasingly considered as responses. Evidence from city schools in India, including Vadodara, remains limited. Objective: To examine whether self-reported engagement with CBT-based and mindfulness-based practices is associated with mental health outcomes (anxiety, depression and emotional regulation difficulty) and cognitive performance (overall performance, attention, memory, problem solving and decision making) among secondary school students. Methods: A quantitative cross-sectional survey was conducted with 300 students (aged 15–18 years; classes 10–12) from four private schools in Vadodara, Gujarat, selected by purposive sampling (700 students approached; 300 valid responses retained). Structured Likert-scale questionnaires, adapted from established measures of depression, anxiety and perceived stress, were administered in school. Data were analysed in SPSS using descriptive statistics and linear models, with CBT and mindfulness entered together as predictors of each outcome. Results: CBT significantly predicted lower anxiety (β = −.25, p = .002), depression (β = −.30, p < .001) and emotional regulation difficulty (β = −.22, p = .009). Mindfulness predicted lower anxiety (β = −.16, p = .038) but not depression or emotional regulation difficulty. Both approaches predicted higher overall cognitive performance (CBT β = .19; mindfulness β = .33) and lower memory, problem-solving and decision-making difficulty; neither predicted attention. The models explained between 7.6% and 25.3% of the variance in the significant outcomes (attention: 0.8%). Conclusion: Higher self-reported use of CBT and mindfulness practices was associated with better mental health and cognitive outcomes, with CBT the more consistent correlate of mental health and mindfulness the stronger correlate of cognitive outcomes. Because the design is cross-sectional and self-reported, the findings indicate association rather than causation; longitudinal and controlled studies are needed.

title: Pengaruh Mindfulness Based Cognitive Therapy (MBCT) untuk Menurunkan Illness Uncertainty pada Orang Tua sebagai Caregiver Anak dengan Kanker
container-title: Jurnal Locus Penelitian dan Pengabdian
66339e7dd9017a543c2cbb5dd431517603ae0e0c.abstract: Orang tua yang berperan sebagai caregiver anak dengan kanker menghadapi berbagai ketidakpastian terkait diagnosis, pengobatan, prognosis, dan kemungkinan kekambuhan penyakit. Kondisi tersebut dapat memunculkan illness uncertainty yang berdampak pada meningkatnya distress psikologis. Penelitian ini bertujuan menguji pengaruh Mindfulness-Based Cognitive Therapy (MBCT) terhadap illness uncertainty pada orang tua sebagai caregiver anak dengan kanker. Penelitian menggunakan desain kuasi eksperimen dengan pendekatan one-group pretest-posttest pada empat ibu caregiver yang tinggal di Rumah Singgah Tangan Baik Insani Bandung. Intervensi yang diberikan yaitu delapan sesi MBCT yang dilaksanakan setiap minggu. Pengukuran dilakukan menggunakan Parents' Perception of Uncertainty Scale (PPUS) dan dianalisis dengan uji Wilcoxon Signed Rank Test. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa MBCT tidak memberikan pengaruh yang signifikan secara statistik terhadap penurunan illness uncertainty (p = 0,066; p > 0,05). Namun, seluruh partisipan mengalami penurunan skor illness uncertainty dengan rerata sebesar 31,4% (Negative Ranks = 4), yang didukung oleh hasil observasi dan wawancara mengenai perubahan positif dalam menghadapi ketidakpastian selama proses perawatan anak. Oleh karena itu, MBCT berpotensi membantu orang tua sebagai caregiver dalam menghadapi illness uncertainty, meskipun efektivitasnya masih perlu dikaji lebih lanjut melalui penelitian dengan jumlah partisipan yang lebih besar dan kelompok kontrol.

title: Communication Difficulties and Participation in Police Interviews: Experiences of Suspects with Cognitive Disabilities
container-title: Journal of Police and Criminal Psychology
cdc6cbe04c6752161a03c21efa4c93b02c3c48ce.abstract: Abstract Police interviews place considerable demands on suspects, who must understand questions, recall events, communicate clearly and assess their legal situation under conditions of stress and uncertainty. For individuals with cognitive disabilities these demands can be especially challenging. Drawing on twelve qualitative interviews with individuals in Norway who had been suspects in criminal investigations and who reported cognitive disabilities, this study examines how participants experienced police questioning through their own accounts of these encounters. The participants described difficulties with communication and understanding, but these challenges did not necessarily bring the interaction to a halt. On the contrary, suspects often continued to cooperate and provide information even when they were unsure about what was happening or how their statements were being understood. In some cases, misunderstandings became difficult to correct once they had entered the investigative process. This evidentiary risk arises when misunderstandings or compliance-based responses enter the investigative record and are treated as more reliable than they are, potentially shaping the course of the criminal case in unintended ways. The study adds empirical knowledge about how communication problems and limited opportunities for correction may develop during questioning, and highlights some of the challenges involved in identifying such difficulties while interviews are taking place. Using reflexive thematic analysis, four themes were identified: understanding and exercising rights, communication breakdowns, pressure and production of unreliable statements, and resignation and loss of corrective capacity.

title: Not-only-cognitive and more-than-cognitive humanities
container-title: Prace Kulturoznawcze
2f6681790255ee5ab61399a22c970e8079a9b890.abstract: This article offers a partial summary of the project titled Cognitive and Non-Cognitive Humanities and the Axiological Nature of Acts of Understanding. The axiological dimension of understanding is examined in relation to the identity of the humanities, which are becoming increasingly fragmented. I approach this issue through the distinction proposed by Stanisław Pietraszko, who argued for a distinction between the cognitive and non-cognitive humanities.This article presents examples of both types of humanities, highlighting not only the differences but also the similarities between them. I argue that it is still possible to speak of the humanities as a unified field and, in order to capture their unity in diversity, propose the terms “not-only-cognitive humanities” and “more-than-cognitive humanities.” I conclude by suggesting that Pietraszko’s axiological theory of culture, reinterpreted within the framework of cultural ontology, can provide a research perspective for studying the cultures that shape the practice of the humanities.

title: Gray Matter Atrophy and Cognitive Symptoms in Alzheimer's Disease: Concordance, Mismatch, and the Moderating Role of Cognitive Reserve
container-title: Health and Molecular Frontiers
6137f9750ea357145f701138698d8e45679e9035.abstract: Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is characterized by progressive gray matter (GM) atrophy, which is typically detected using structural MRI. Although atrophy is often associated with cognitive impairment, the relationship is not absolute: individuals with similar levels of atrophy may exhibit considerable differences in cognitive performance. This review discusses the correlations and inconsistencies between GM atrophy and cognition in AD, as well as the factors that influence this relationship. Evidence supports this correlation, particularly between medial temporal lobe structures and memory function, and it can be observed even before clinical diagnosis. However, mismatches occur across whole-brain and regional measurements and at different disease stages, indicating that atrophy severity alone cannot fully account for the severity of cognitive impairment. Cognitive reserve (CR) is an important factor that may explain part of this mismatch. Individuals with higher CR may show more severe pathology at comparable levels of cognitive performance. However, the explanatory power of CR is limited and appears to depend on the brain region, reserve indicator, and disease stage. Other factors, including vascular burden, sex, and differences in imaging and cognitive assessment methods, may also contribute to these inconsistencies. Therefore, structural MRI should be interpreted together with CR, disease stage, and other pathological factors. Longitudinal imaging and multimodal approaches may help clarify individual differences in the relationship between atrophy and cognitive symptoms.

title:
Preferential Improvement of Trauma‐Related Distressing Dreams Following Traumatic Memory Reactivation in Severe
                    <scp>PTSD</scp>
                    : A Secondary Analysis of a Randomized Placebo‐Controlled Trial
container-title: Journal of Sleep Research
78da34044321d4d887263b58c850cd007993b22d.abstract: ABSTRACT Trauma‐related distressing dreams are among the most frequent and persistent symptoms of posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD). Propranolol has been proposed to modulate the reconsolidation of reactivated emotional memories through beta‐adrenergic blockade, providing a rationale for its combination with traumatic memory reactivation procedures (TMRP). In this exploratory post hoc secondary analysis of the REDUCTRAUMA2 randomized double‐blind placebo‐controlled trial, we examined changes in distressing dreams severity during and after TMRP administered under propranolol or placebo in 66 patients with PTSD. Distressing dreams were assessed using item 2 of the PTSD Checklist‐Specific (PCL‐S). Distressing dreams severity decreased markedly following the intervention in the whole cohort, with large within‐subject effects maintained up to 3 months. No significant differences were observed between propranolol and placebo. In the overall cohort, distressing dreams improved preferentially compared with the remaining PTSD symptoms at one‐week and one‐month follow‐up. Subgroup analyses showed that this preferential improvement was sustained across all follow‐up assessments in participants with severe PTSD at baseline, whereas no preferential effect was observed in the non‐severe subgroup. Distribution‐free RIDIT analyses yielded convergent findings. These exploratory findings suggest that trauma‐related distressing dreams may represent a particularly treatment‐responsive symptom dimension in PTSD, especially among patients with more severe symptomatology. No additional benefit of propranolol over placebo was observed; however, in the absence of a non‐reactivation control condition, the specific contribution of TMRP to the observed improvement cannot be determined. Prospective studies using dedicated nightmare measures and appropriate control conditions are needed to confirm these findings. Trail Registration: ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT01713556.

title: No association between five-factor personality model and 5-year all-cause mortality in patients with subjective cognitive decline and mild cognitive impairment
Kein Zusammenhang zwischen dem Fünf-Faktoren-Persönlichkeitsmodell und der 5-Jahres-Gesamtmortalität bei Patienten mit subjektivem kognitivem Leistungsabfall und leichter kognitiver Beeinträchtigung
container-title: neuropsychiatrie
071670549d8ee62298d52d114befb2dcfec05e32.abstract: Summary Background Alzheimer’s disease is the most common form of dementia and is preceded by prodromal stages including subjective cognitive decline (SCD), non-amnestic mild cognitive impairment (naMCI), and amnestic mild cognitive impairment (aMCI). While associations between personality traits and cognitive decline have been reported, their impact on mortality in these early disease stages remains unclear. Objectives This study aimed to investigate whether personality traits differ between patients with SCD, naMCI, and aMCI and whether these traits influence 5‑year all-cause mortality. Methods In this retrospective single-center study, data from 353 patients aged 50 and older diagnosed with SCD ( n = 72), naMCI ( n = 156), or aMCI ( n = 125) were analyzed. Personality traits were assessed using the Big Five Plus One (B5PO) questionnaire. Survival probabilities were estimated using Kaplan–Meier analysis, group differences were assessed by log-rank test, and the impact of personality traits on mortality was examined using Cox proportional hazards model. Results The overall 5‑year survival probability was 87.1%. No significant differences in all-cause survival were observed between diagnostic subgroups ( p = 0.629). No significant differences in personality traits were found between SCD, naMCI, and aMCI patients. Personality traits assessed by the B5PO showed no significant association with mortality. Apart from personality traits, exploratory analyses suggested that certain cognitive performance measures, namely, selective attention, were associated with survival probability, whereas higher age was associated with increased mortality risk. Conclusion Personality traits according to the B5PO do not appear to significantly influence mortality or differ between the subgroups of early cognitive impairment. Further studies with larger cohorts are necessary to clarify potential associations between personality, cognition, and long-term outcomes.

title: From Cognitive Processing to Daily Functioning: Language, Visuomotor Integration, and Adaptive Behavior in Children With Coffin‐Siris Syndrome
container-title: American Journal of Medical Genetics Part A
1561d93dc568eab5e8a08d96d7811746e9bd8cb9.abstract: ABSTRACT Studying Mendelian neurodevelopmental disorders (NDDs) from a bottom‐up perspective, in which neurocognitive functioning is conceptualized as a mediator between genotype and behavioral phenotype, may facilitate early identification of syndrome‐specific vulnerabilities. This study characterizes the neurocognitive phenotype and adaptive functioning of children with Coffin‐Siris syndrome (CSS), a rare Mendelian NDD with unknown effects on brain development. Thirty‐five children with CSS (Mage = 9.74 years, SD = 4.22) underwent performance‐based assessment of global cognition, receptive and expressive language, and visuomotor integration. Parents completed standardized questionnaires assessing adaptive functioning. The predictive value of age and cognitive performance for adaptive outcomes was explored. Children with CSS showed marked developmental delays across global cognition and domain‐specific skills. Receptive language emerged as a relative strength, whereas expressive language and visuomotor integration were prominent vulnerabilities. Adaptive functioning was broadly impaired, particularly in communication, self‐regulation, being part of the community, and daily functioning. Older children showed larger divergence from age‐expected norms, consistent with a growing‐into‐deficit pattern. Receptive language, expressive language, and visuomotor integration each uniquely contributed to adaptive behavior, independent of global cognitive level. These findings underscore the importance of individualized neurocognitive assessment to guide targeted interventions improving daily functioning in children with CSS.

title: EU-Accession Sentiment and Cognitive Biases in Coastal Real Estate Investment: Evidence from Albania
container-title: International Journal of Financial Studies
9ffd8e6ec91eece4033a51ba956555d54066ced3.abstract: This paper looks into cognitive biases in real estate investment decisions in an emerging market in Europe on the optimism of Albania joining the European Union. Based on a cross-sectional survey of 462 respondents from the Vlora coastal region, this study employs partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) to test the nexus between EU-accession optimism, anchoring, overconfidence, herding, price expectation and investment intention. EU-accession optimism has a strong and statistically significant positive influence on both investment intention and price expectations. Anchoring plays a meaningful mediating role in translating optimism into investment behavior, while overconfidence and herding further amplify sentiment-driven investment intentions. The multi-group analysis (MGA) indicates behavioral heterogeneity across investor groups; differences should be interpreted with caution considering the absence of formal measurement invariance testing. By looking at EU accession as a sentiment-based process rather than a macroeconomic factor, this study contributes to the behavioral finance literature by explaining how institutional optimism works with the cognitive mechanism in investment decisions on real assets.

title: Cognitive Predictors of AI-Related Textual Change in Upper-Intermediate L2 Russian Writing: Working Memory, Attention Control, and Critical Thinking
container-title: Journal of Intelligence
460bdbd6b50001ed6fdcf70e059bf88f7141d88f.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) can alter final second-language (L2) texts, yet cognitive differences may shape which changes emerge. This exploratory study examined 38 upper-intermediate learners of Russian who each produced one composition with AI assistance and one without it. Working memory, attention control, and critical thinking were measured continuously, and 11 textual outcomes were calculated from paired compositions. AI-assisted texts showed higher lemma-based lexical-diversity values, longer words, more connectives per 100 words, and substantially fewer first-person markers, while total word count, sentence measures, and formulaic-expression rate did not differ in the full sample. The higher POS-based content-word density was attenuated after first-person forms were excluded, suggesting a contribution from the change in person marking. Exploratory models suggested negative working-memory associations with lexical-diversity and connective-rate change, and negative attention-control associations with lexical-diversity change. The positive working-memory coefficient for word-count change was sensitive to HC3 estimation and leave-one-out refitting. Critical thinking showed no clear independent association in the primary change-score models, while positive coefficients for MATTR and HD-D appeared in the outcome-conditioned models. Under this supervised, student-mediated procedure, AI assistance was associated with lexical, discourse-marking, and stance differences in completed L2 texts.

title: Generalization of fine-tuned uncertainty communication and metacognition in large language models
container-title: Communications AI & Computing
154e57f5f7092b3bd93d9d564b79eeda87e92985.abstract: Abstract Large language models are increasingly used in settings where confident but incorrect answers can mislead users. Reliable uncertainty communication requires a form of metacognition: monitoring when one’s own answers are likely to be correct. Yet models’ stated confidence is often poorly aligned with answer correctness. We test whether supervised fine-tuning improves uncertainty communication and whether gains transfer across domains and task formats. We fine-tuned two models on general knowledge, mathematics, and open-ended trivia questions. We evaluated single-question confidence estimation, in which the model reports numeric confidence for one answer, and pairwise confidence comparison, in which it chooses which of two questions it is more likely to answer correctly. We tested held-out questions from training domains and new medical, legal, and truthfulness benchmarks. We assessed calibration, discrimination, and answer accuracy before and after fine-tuning. Here we show that fine-tuning improves alignment between stated confidence and observed accuracy and increases the model’s ability to assign higher confidence to correct than to incorrect answers. Gains occur within training domains and, to a lesser extent, in new domains. However, single-task training does not reliably transfer between single-question confidence estimation and pairwise confidence comparison. Multitask fine-tuning produces broader gains in the models and tasks studied here. Uncertainty communication in large language models is trainable, but transfer across metacognitive tasks is limited. Joint training on multiple confidence tasks may support broader generalization, although further tests across model families and metacognitive tasks are needed.
