title: Re‐Signifying Soviet Monuments: State Self‐Description, Memory Politics and Ontological Security in Estonia
container-title: Nations and Nationalism
11ffb218b5c19e7b7696f446a719be026c8fcf30.abstract: ABSTRACT Since the restoration of independence, Soviet‐era monuments in Estonia have remained contested sites through which historical legitimacy, political belonging and national identity are publicly negotiated. Following Russia's full‐scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, these monuments acquired renewed salience as Estonia moved to regulate symbols that had become flashpoints in struggles over memory and the symbolic order of the nation‐state. This article examines how Soviet monuments in Estonia are re‐signified. Drawing on a data‐driven typology‐building approach and an analytical reconstruction of salient interventions since 1991, it develops a fourfold typology of re‐signification strategies and identifies the conditions under which they de‐escalate contestation, intensify it or displace it onto other symbolic sites and issues. The article shows how semiotic mechanisms of state self‐description shape these processes and argues that monument re‐signification is central to the symbolic reproduction of political community under conditions of ontological insecurity.

title: Artificial intelligence and clinical work: Designing GenAI mentoring to support decision making in cognitive rehabilitation
container-title: WORK: A Journal of Prevention, Assessment & Rehabilitation
3de4d322b5e5608b8eae3c50616c36a74da6844c.abstract: Background Occupational therapists working in cognitive rehabilitation may face high cognitive demands, and professional isolation. Although AI is used for information retrieval and decision support, its role in supporting reflective clinical reasoning remains insufficiently conceptualized. As scholarly attention shifts from automation toward augmentation of professional judgment, the next step is to understand how AI may support reflective reasoning in complex rehabilitation work. Objective To examine key challenges in cognitive rehabilitation and explore how these needs may inform a conceptual design for GenAI-mediated mentoring within clinical work. Methods A qualitative study grounded in Design Thinking methodology was conducted with 30 female occupational therapists (age range 24–64 years, M = 41.26, SD = 10.35) with wide range of clinical experience (less than one year to more than 20 years) from diverse settings. They completed a demographic questionnaire and participated in two Design Thinking workshops (n = 14; n = 16). Seven participants subsequently engaged in follow-up interviews to refine design implications. All sessions were audio-recorded, transcribed, and analyzed thematically. Results The thematic analysis yielded four themes: (A) The Therapist's role (B) Challenging therapist-client interactions, (C) Loneliness of the Therapist (D) Expectations for guidance or support aspects. These findings informed the conceptualization of a GenAI mentoring framework grounded in real-world clinical demands. Conclusions The findings support the design of generative AI systems as dialogic, context-sensitive tools intended to strengthen professional judgment, warranting further examination of their integration within real-world clinical workflows.

title: The Cognitive Infrastructure of Economic Action: Monetary Stability, Deregulation, and the Reflexivity Trap of the Open Society in Milei’s Argentina
container-title: Economies
246801bc426f74500c9c1ed04987923a95872508.abstract: This article develops the concept of cognitive infrastructure to capture a dimension of institutional performance that the incentive-focused tradition in institutional economics has largely neglected. Cognitive infrastructure comprises three dimensions: a stable unit of account, traceable causal links, and correctable feedback loops. When inflation reaches extreme levels, it destroys these conditions, dissolving the capacity of economic agents to perceive causal connections between their actions and their outcomes. Applying this framework to Javier Milei’s Argentine reform program, the article draws on Hayek and Eucken to show how monetary stabilization, deregulation, and currency competition restore the cognitive conditions for economic calculation, and on Popper and Soros to identify a structural tension this reconstruction generates. The cognitive infrastructure the reforms seek to rebuild is depoliticized in its ideal form. Its reconstruction has nevertheless been pursued through highly personalized political methods that may themselves reintroduce the unpredictability the framework is designed to eliminate. This tension, the article argues, is a structural feature of post-collapse institutional reconstruction that the open society tradition has not adequately theorized.

title: Human–AI Semantic Identification of Components in Traditional Chinese Floor-Standing Interior Timber Screens: Expert Effort and Record Agreement
container-title: Heritage
1e6d6127d06a631b55e28de657a7595d5b8ccf37.abstract: Semantic documentation of traditional Chinese interior timber screens requires integrating local form, spatial position, and constructional relations. We compared human-only labeling (H), comprehensive AI assistance (HA), and risk-oriented selective review (RH) for components in five floor-standing screens at three heritage sites. Among 188 candidate masks, 30 measured agreement among six independent experts, and 158 entered a counterbalanced crossover experiment. Machine labels and self-reported review flags were frozen before expert assessment. Complete agreement on the shared set was 90.00% (Fleiss’ κ = 0.9396). Matching labels from two H experts defined an internal operational consensus for 154 formal candidates. Agreement with this reference was 64.94% for AI-only, 97.08% for HA, and 75.32% for RH. HA exceeded AI-only by 32.14 percentage points (95% CI, 24.68–39.61). RH routed 20.89% of formal candidates to experts and reduced recorded expert decision time by 81.54% relative to H in this experiment. The frozen review flag captured 33.33% of machine–consensus disagreements, while experts realigned 88.89% of routed disagreement records. For these screen components, comprehensive assistance achieved the highest consensus agreement, whereas selective review under the tested routing strategy reduced expert effort but left most machine–consensus disagreements unreviewed.

title: Depressive Symptoms, Spiritual Well-Being, Healthy Aging, and Health-Related Quality of Life in Older Adults with and Without Mild Cognitive Impairment: A Cross-Sectional Multi-Group Path Analysis
container-title: Journal of Ageing and Longevity
a2026f9554af377e6c43f88412d7be32366a8485.abstract: Depressive symptoms are common among older adults with mild cognitive impairment (MCI) and are associated with poorer health-related quality of life (HRQoL) and lower healthy-aging scores, yet the pathways underlying these associations remain unclear. Drawing on stress-and-coping and meaning-making perspectives, this study examined whether spiritual well-being statistically accounted for part of the associations of depressive symptoms with healthy aging and HRQoL, and whether these indirect associations differed by cognitive status. In this cross-sectional comparative study, 281 older adults with MCI and 295 older adults without a diagnosed cognitive impairment (aged 65–75 years) were recruited from a geriatric outpatient clinic. A just-identified multi-group path model was estimated with age as a covariate and 5000 bootstrap resamples. The MCI group had higher depressive symptom scores, poorer HRQoL, and lower healthy-aging and spiritual well-being scores than the comparison group (all p < 0.001, |d| = 0.45–0.67). In both groups, depressive symptoms were directly associated with lower healthy-aging scores and poorer HRQoL. A statistically significant but modest indirect association through spiritual well-being was observed between depressive symptoms and healthy aging (standardized indirect effect: −0.18 in the MCI group and −0.08 in the comparison group); this association was robust to adjustment for sociodemographic and clinical covariates and to the exclusion of conceptually overlapping healthy-aging subscales. The indirect association with HRQoL was small, and no indirect association differed significantly between groups. Because the design was cross-sectional, these findings do not establish causal mediation; they indicate that spiritual well-being is a psychosocial correlate of healthy aging that warrants examination in longitudinal and intervention studies.

title: Subjective Cognitive Decline with Financial Interference: Associations with Money Management and Satisfaction in Older Adults
container-title: Journal of Ageing and Longevity
4e5a2c0fd76606cc5fd2f33c6df13e191d5cef05.abstract: Subjective cognitive decline (SCD) has been linked to a range of health outcomes, but little is known about its relationship to how older adults manage their money. This study extends SCD with financial interference (SCD-F), a brief, person-centered classification introduced in earlier work, to two money management outcomes in older adults: assistance with money management and satisfaction with current arrangements. Participants (n = 1392) completed an online survey through the Older Adult Nest Egg website and were classified as having no subjective memory complaint (SMC), an SMC only, or SCD-F. The groups differed in money management (χ2(4) = 70.00, p < 0.001) and satisfaction with their money management arrangement (χ2(4) = 100.84, p < 0.001). Participants with SCD-F more often received help managing their finances or had someone else manage them (42.09%) than those with an SMC only (24.47%) or no SMC (19.35%), and were less often satisfied (61.87% vs. 77.66% and 87.02%). Findings held after adjusting for age, gender, race, and education, supporting both hypotheses. These findings suggest that financial interference adds information beyond a general memory complaint. Future longitudinal studies with objective measures of financial capacity should test the direction of these associations.

title: Development, Cognitive Interview Testing, and Content Validation of the PERCH-BC Survey for Perceived Weight-Related Effects of Hormonal Contraception
container-title: Obesities
5a369704a636bdd69b5a8b98569a107cd2eb8bfc.abstract: Concerns about weight gain may influence hormonal contraception selection, satisfaction, and discontinuation, yet no validated patient-centered instrument assesses perceived weight-related effects across methods. We developed the Perceived Changes with Hormonal Birth Control (PERCH-BC) survey using sequential face-validity and content-validity phases. Initial items were informed by the literature, questionnaires, and expertise. Fifteen premenopausal women aged 20–45 years—purposively sampled across normal-weight, overweight, and obesity categories—evaluated Versions 1–3 over three rounds of cognitive interviews. Participants completed the survey before retrospective probing focused on comprehension, interpretation, response processes, response-option fit, format, and usability. Interviews were audio-recorded, transcribed, and qualitatively coded; round-specific findings informed sequential revisions. Participants found the survey understandable and acceptable. However, limited contraceptive-method familiarity, difficulty responding under uncertainty, and interpretation of items as factual knowledge questions reduced response confidence. Revisions included a contraceptive-method visual aid, uncertainty response options, belief- and experience-focused instructions, revised wording, and side-effect items. The resulting 25-item Version 4 underwent structured content review by eight interdisciplinary experts evaluating 27 prompts for relevance, clarity, and completeness. All prompts met the prespecified relevance threshold (item-level content validity index [I-CVI], 0.875–1.00); the scale-level average content validity index (S-CVI/Ave) was 0.98. Expert feedback informed minor refinements before subsequent quantitative psychometric validation.

title: Hyperspectral Video Object Segmentation Based on Spectral–Spatial Interaction Enhancement and Adaptive Correlation Memory Selection
container-title: Remote Sensing
6b3b576f00cb97833f8d00d747ed05935ead8a03.abstract: Hyperspectral imaging (HSI) is an important imaging modality in the field of optical remote sensing, capable of simultaneously capturing spatial structures and continuous spectral responses related to material properties. Therefore, compared with conventional red-green-blue (RGB) images, it can provide richer representations for understanding dynamic scenes. However, most existing video object segmentation methods have been developed for RGB videos, while high-quality hyperspectral video datasets with frame-by-frame pixel-level annotations remain scarce. To address this gap, this study constructed a hyperspectral video object segmentation dataset, comprising hyperspectral videos and their corresponding three-channel false-color RGB videos derived from the same HSI data, with pixel-level annotations provided for each frame. The dataset contains three spectral subsets: visible (VIS), near-infrared (NIR), and red-edge near-infrared (RedNIR). Using this dataset, we developed SSAM-SAM2, a hyperspectral video object segmentation network built on Segment Anything Model 2 (SAM 2). The network includes a spectral–spatial interaction enhancement (SSIE) module designed to identify informative spectral bands, suppress interference from redundant and noisy spectral channels, and integrate hyperspectral cues with the spatial-structure features of the corresponding false-color RGB images. In addition, the network introduces an Adaptive Correlation Memory Selection (ACMS) module that regulates memory sampling and selection according to variations in target state and inter-frame feature correlation. This design reduces the influence of redundant or unreliable historical information and improves temporal memory reliability under target deformation, motion variations, and background interference. Extensive experiments show that SSAM-SAM2 outperforms the selected comparison methods on the VIS, NIR, and RedNIR subsets under the evaluated settings. These results demonstrate the value of the proposed dataset and indicate that spectral–spatial enhancement and temporal adaptive memory mechanisms contribute to improving hyperspectral video object segmentation performance.

title: Sorbus commixta Fruit Extract Ameliorates Corticosterone-Induced Cognitive Impairment by Activating the BDNF-TrkB-PI3K-Akt-CREB Pathway
container-title: Journal of Medicinal Food
42a9007bc69283d898b99b943dba6ed7b9b8c025.abstract: Elevated corticosterone (CORT) levels from chronic stress or depression impair cognitive function and neuronal survival by suppressing brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF), tropomyosin receptor kinase B (TrkB), and the cAMP response element-binding protein (CREB) signaling pathway. The present study evaluated the neuroprotective effects of Sorbus commixta fruit extract (SCE) in CORT-induced HT22 hippocampal cells and a CORT-induced depression-like mouse model. In vitro , SCE pretreatment (100 or 200 μg/mL) protected against CORT-induced cytotoxicity and intracellular stress. Notably, SCE prevented CORT-mediated downregulation of microtubule-associated protein 2 ( Map2 ) and Bdnf mRNA and BDNF protein levels, and maintained the phosphorylation ratios of TrkB, phosphoinositide 3-kinase (PI3K), serine/threonine protein kinase B (Akt), and CREB. Wortmannin diminished the SCE-associated restoration of PI3K, Akt, and CREB phosphorylation, supporting the involvement of PI3K-Akt signaling. In vivo , oral administration of SCE (100 or 300 mg/kg) attenuated CORT-induced anhedonia-like behavior and impairments in learning and spatial working memory. These behavioral effects were accompanied by preservation of hippocampal BDNF-TrkB-PI3K-Akt-CREB signaling. Collectively, these findings suggest that SCE attenuates CORT-induced cellular stress, disruption of neuroplasticity-related signaling, and behavioral impairments, potentially by modulating the BDNF-TrkB-PI3K-Akt-CREB pathway. Therefore, SCE is a promising functional food-derived material for supporting neuronal plasticity under chronic stress conditions.

title: CD8+ T cells drive neuroinflammation and cognitive decline in Alzheimer’s disease
container-title: Frontiers in Immunology
011c20d2ed204a4370428b28e6b5464637af68aa.abstract: Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is the most common neurodegenerative disease in the world, and its pathogenesis is very complex, posing a serious threat to human health. The reciprocal regulation of the nervous and immune systems plays a key role in driving AD progression, although the specific mechanisms remain to be elucidated. In recent years, attention has increasingly focused on the role of adaptive immune cells in AD. Among them, CD8 + T cells have been found to infiltrate the brain parenchyma of AD patients, and this phenomenon is closely associated with neuronal injury and cognitive decline. This review first outlines the epidemiology and pathomechanisms of AD and systematically summarizes CD8 + T cell activation, cytotoxicity, migration, and function. It emphasizes the dual potential role of these cells in AD. These cells may exacerbate neuronal injury and cognitive dysfunction through multiple pathways, including direct cytotoxicity, release of pro-inflammatory cytokines, disruption of the blood–brain barrier, and inhibition of neuroplasticity. However, under specific microenvironmental conditions, CD8 + T cells may also exert immunomodulatory functions and confer potential protective effects. This review also discusses related therapeutic strategies based on these mechanisms. Finally, we discuss the difficulties currently facing research and future directions for clinical translation. We believe that in-depth exploration of the immunoregulatory mechanisms of CD8 + T cells in AD can provide theoretical foundations and new perspectives for developing innovative immunotherapies targeting neuroinflammation and cognitive impairment in AD.

title: A Memory-Safe eBPF/GPU Data Plane for Adaptive 5G Backdoor Detection
34de39990340d54a67fe33c91bf34eb6c329bb5a.abstract: Abstract The evolution of 5G towards cloud-native deployments exposes the User Plane Function (UPF) to persistent host-resident implants, of which the BPFDoor backdoor is a documented telecommunications-sector example. This work presents a tiered, memory-safe detection data plane that couples in-kernel extended Berkeley Packet Filter (eBPF/XDP) filtering with a memory-safe Graphics Processing Unit (GPU) Cloud-Native Network Function (CNF) written in NVIDIA cuTile-Rust. The proposed data plane is evaluated against adversarial Large Language Model (LLM) agents on a live six-node Open5GS/UERANSIM testbed. A Red Agent autonomously mutates the implant while a Blue Agent hunts it; the presented behavioral invariant, which requires a functional passive backdoor to hold an AF_PACKET/ETH_P_ALL/iface=0 socket, is shown to be a kernel fact that the attacker cannot mutate away. A GPU mutation-space sweep evaluates the full space of 2,555,904 signature variants, over which a static signature is evaded in approximately all cases while the invariant is evaded by none. The proposed placement is measured rather than assumed: eBPF/XDP reaches a hard verifier ceiling, whereas the memory-safe CNF reaches parity with hand-written CUDA C at moderate arithmetic intensity and, at higher intensity, outperforms a straightforward hand-written CUDA C implementation, at an edge power envelope of about 66 W. Across six adversarial memory-safety bug classes the cuTile detector reports zero sanitizer errors, and the invariant holds at 25/25 under three distinct attacker LLMs.

title: Ideophones in Nepali: Perceptual Iconicity, Affective and Cognitive Expressiveness, and Implicational Hierarchy
container-title: Nepalese Linguistics
a6f76ec26cb2f2ecb229b0eb350522c29d16b060.abstract: This paper investigates the nature of Nepali ideophones which are a crucial component of the Nepali language. It teases out the previously unexplained and unexplored facets of Nepali ideophones from a clearer theoretical perspective. The main approach adopted to study Nepali ideophones is the implicational hierarchy for ideophonic systems of languages (Dingemanse 2012). Data is presented in tabular form, associating ideophones and their corresponding verbal or nominal matches. The main findings of the study are that the Nepali ideophones meet the implicational hierarchy as proposed by Dingemanse (2012). These ideophones cover and serve a wide range of linguistic and cognitive functions. Even there have been some attempts at the study of Nepali ideophones, this is the first time that these ideophones are presented with a clear theoretical perspective and the multifaced expressive richness they infuse in the language. Ideophones are special cases that enrich linguistic expressions. However, they have received little attention in Nepali academia. This study, for the first time, brings out the significance of the study and investigation of Nepali ideophones.

title: Human–AI Cognitive Division of Labor: A Structured Narrative Review and Integrative Framework
container-title: Applied Sciences
fc6d0a5c3824f34753280f092a43facbc5dd564f.abstract: AI-assisted systems redistribute cognitive work before final decisions are made, yet broad labels such as assistance, automation, and human involvement do not fully describe these arrangements. This theory-led structured narrative review connects Function Allocation with research on complementarity, appropriate reliance, cognitive offloading, delegation, mixed initiative, agency, and recovery. It draws on concept-driven retrieval, citation chaining, and selected theoretical foundations. Source selection and coding were AI-assisted, with verification boundaries reported separately. Framework A is a configuration-oriented integrative reporting framework and design space organized around allocation object, performer, allocation authority, change dynamics, and recovery architecture. Framework B provides a conditional temporal process lens on enactment, monitoring, recovery, and reallocation. Together, they support comparison of configuration descriptions across heterogeneous studies while separating configuration, operating conditions, process, and outcomes. The five dimensions build on established constructs. Coding reproducibility, comparative usefulness, and effects on interface design have not been empirically established.

title: Inference of Tacit Meeting Knowledge via LLMs: Toward Emotion-Enriched Organizational Memory
container-title: Information
c63599472c58c49b4d5aea736cdb9e364bab57b1.abstract: Organizations risk losing critical tacit knowledge when meeting records capture only what was said rather than how it was expressed, such as emotional tone, tension, or unspoken dynamics. We investigate whether integrating tacit knowledge into Large Language Model (LLM)-based meeting summaries can enrich organizational memory. Following a Design Science Research approach, a prototype was developed to transform meeting audio into tacit-enriched knowledge outputs. Initial experiments explored audio-only Speech Emotion Recognition but revealed significant reliability issues in realistic, multilingual and interruption-rich environments, particularly Swiss German. Consequently, the solution pivoted toward a text-based LLM framework using structured, role-based prompt engineering to extract tacit insights from transcribed meetings. The artefact generated two summaries, one capturing explicit and the other capturing implicit emotional and tacit cues. The exploratory evaluation involved 32 participants across 17 workplace meetings and examined perceived accuracy, additional insight, usefulness, and ethical acceptability. Participants frequently perceived additional contextual insight beyond conventional factual summaries, while also expressing concerns about unsupported interpretations and potential surveillance. As no independent ground truth or controlled comparison was used, the results provide evidence of perceived usefulness rather than verified improvements in organizational knowledge retention.

title: ‘Anger’ In English and Nepali Conceptual Metaphors: A Cognitive Perspective
container-title: Nepalese Linguistics
8afdaa3cb3f3db1684301a5c7fbe49edc86aaf25.abstract: This paper deals with a cognitive study of near-universal primary metaphor ‘anger’ in English and Nepali. The cross cultural and metaphorical conceptualization of anger emotion with linguistic embodiment, is compared to validate that the abstract anger emotion is described by concrete bodily- experience. The secondary data is collected from the survey report of Nepali idioms (Paudel,2061 B.S) and Oxford English idiom dictionary. The analysis is based on conceptual metaphor theory (Lakoff & Koveches, 1987) to compare anger-emotion for finding out similarities and dissimilarities to show the universality and specificity across two different cultures. The upper part of the body ‘head’ container, is the central and common locus point for embodied ‘anger’ in both English and Nepali embodied idiomatic expression. The similarities among with ‘anger is heat, heated fluid, substance and spatial in body container’ is that ‘anger is spatial in the container’ shared more classified body part container with greater number of idioms in both English and Nepali. The center-periphery (in- out) from landmark to trajector orientation with spatiality in body container are the most commonly expressed embodied anger metaphor in both English and Nepali embodied idioms. English has less specific separate body -part container activated overtly in idiomatic expression, but Nepali has more separate and classified body container activation overtly among over all embodied ‘anger’ metaphor conceptualization in given data. However, the similarity is that both languages conceptualize ‘anger is heat’, ‘anger is heated fluid’ ‘anger is substance’ and ‘anger is spatial’ in the body container.

title: Within‐person dual‐pathway model linking optimism to depression: A random‐intercept cross‐lagged panel study of cognitive bias and loneliness among Chinese university students
container-title: British Journal of Developmental Psychology
108be0784ff4bf66270899072d832ed6164b8f68.abstract: Abstract This 1‐year longitudinal study applied a random intercept cross‐lagged panel model (RI‐CLPM) to examine how optimism influences depression through negative cognitive bias and loneliness among Chinese college students, disentangling within‐person processes from stable between‐person differences. 886 college students completed the Beck Depression Inventory, Optimism Scale, Negative Cognitive Bias Questionnaire and UCLA Loneliness Scale at three time points over 1 year. (1) All four variables (optimism, negative cognitive bias, loneliness, depression) were significantly correlated across three time points (p < .001). (2) RI‐CLPM revealed: within‐person surges in optimism predicted lower negative cognitive bias ( β = −.28, p < .001) and loneliness ( β = −.35, p < .001) at the next wave; these reductions predicted lower depression ( β = .36 and .41, p < .001). Mediation was partial through negative cognitive bias (indirect β = −0.11, 95% CI [−0.18, −0.05]) but complete through loneliness (indirect β = −0.15, 95% CI [−0.23, −0.08]). Optimism at T1 negatively predicted negative cognitive bias and loneliness at T2, which positively predicted depression at T3. After accounting for between‐person variability, within‐person increases in optimism predicted subsequent decreases in depression through two concurrent pathways: negative cognitive bias and loneliness.

title: Normative Data on Cognitive Performance in Urban and Rural Populations of Kazakhstan: A Cross-Sectional Analysis
container-title: Journal of Cross-Cultural Gerontology
e4ada825858eb4bceb39f111ce67605320a4b070.abstract: Abstract Objectives. Evidence on cognitive performance among older adults in Kazakhstan and Central Asia remains limited. This study aimed to establish normative values for neuropsychological tests among adults living in urban and rural areas of Kazakhstan, stratified by age and educational attainment. Methods. This cross-sectional study included 1,648 adults aged 50–75 years randomly selected from urban and rural communities in Central and East Kazakhstan between 2012 and 2016. Four standardized neuropsychological tests assessed verbal memory and learning, verbal fluency, attention, and concentration. Normative values were calculated separately by urban-rural residence, age group, and educational level. Results. Cognitive performance generally declined with increasing age and was higher among participants with greater educational attainment. Urban residents demonstrated higher mean scores than rural residents on immediate word recall (18.98 vs. 16.49), animal naming (18.17 vs. 16.37), and delayed word recall (6.32 vs. 5.71), whereas rural residents scored higher on letter cancellation (22.06 vs. 19.76; all p < 0.001). Age-, education-, and residence-specific percentile norms were established for all four cognitive tests. Discussion. This study provides some of the first population-based normative data for multiple cognitive domains among urban and rural adults in Kazakhstan. These reference values may support the interpretation of cognitive assessments in comparable Central Asian populations, although further validation and studies involving older age groups are needed.

title: Chatgpt In Higher Education:  Structural Relationships between the Compatibility of Learning Styles, Perceived Usefulness and Continued Use Intention
container-title: Journal of Educational and Social Research
16532b7d843d305788128bea11bd5ff40384753d.abstract: The integration of generative artificial intelligence (AI) tools, such as ChatGPT, is transforming learning dynamics in higher education. In this context, the aim of the present study was to analyze the structural relationships between the compatibility of ChatGPT with learning styles, ease of use and perceived usefulness (EUPU), and continued use intention among teacher-training university students and to explore possible gender-based variations. The research was developed via a quantitative approach, with a nonexperimental, cross-sectional and correlational-explanatory design. University students were selected for participation by nonprobabilistic convenience sampling, and data collection was performed using a structured questionnaire. A structural equation model (SEM) was used for data analysis. The results revealed that compatibility with learning styles positively and significantly predicted EUPU. Similarly, EUPU significantly predicted continued use intention. However, the direct path from CLS to continued use intention was positive but not statistically significant, suggesting that the influence of compatibility operates mainly through EUPU. The exploratory multigroup analysis showed small descriptive variations by gender, which should be interpreted with caution. These findings indicate that students have a greater predisposition to continue using ChatGPT when they perceive that the tool adapts to their learning needs, is simple to use and provides concrete academic benefits. In addition, the potential of ChatGPT to support information search, resolve doubts and promote autonomous learning was identified. ChatGPT has important use potential in higher education contexts. 021ef2d7acd1123c014720416e909df6848029f5.abstract: Namen: Namen raziskave je bil analizirati in primerjati uporabniške vmesnike treh digitalnih portalov kulturne dediščine: Kamre, Digitalne knjižnice Slovenije (dLib) in Europeane. Zanimalo nas je, katere značilnosti uporabnosti se pojavljajo pri različnih tipih uporabnikov ter na katerih področjih se izbrani portali med seboj razlikujejo. Metodologija/pristop: Raziskava je temeljila na ekspertni metodi kognitivnega spreho­da. Oblikovane so bile štiri persone, ki so se razlikovale glede na stopnjo izobrazbe, digitalne veščine, motivacijo in cilje uporabe. Persone so bile postavljene v vnaprej pripravljene scenarije iskanja fotografij Bleda. Uporabniški vmesniki portalov Kamra, Europeana in Digitalna knjižnica Slovenije so bili vrednoteni glede na strukturo, navi­gacijo, iskanje, rezultate in metapodatke. Največ razlik med portali se je pokazalo pri navigaciji, preglednosti rezultatov in kakovosti metapo­datkov. Kamra se je izkazala kot portal z bogatim vsebinskim kontekstom, Europeana z velikim številom zadetkov in možnostmi nadaljnjega raziskovanja, Digitalna knjižni­ca Slovenije pa z učinkovitim iskanjem in filtriranjem rezultatov. Digitalno bolj vešči uporabniki so bili občutljivejši na kakovost metapodatkov, digitalno manj vešči pa na navigacijo in orientacijo po sistemu. Omejitve raziskave: Raziskava temelji na ekspertni oceni enega raziskovalca in uporabi person namesto dejanskih uporabnikov, zato ugotovitev ni mogoče neposredno po­splošiti na celotno populacijo uporabnikov. Izvirnost/uporabnost raziskave: Raziskava predstavlja primer uporabe kognitivnega sprehoda, person in scenarijev za vrednotenje portalov kulturne dediščine. Ugotovitve so lahko podlaga za izboljšave uporabniških vmesnikov ter nadaljnje raziskave upo­rabniške izkušnje na področju digitalne kulturne dediščine.

title: Can Generative AI Crush It? A Systematic Comparison of ChatGPT Plus (GPT-4o) and Google Gemini Pro vs. Human Expert Analysis for Oral Dosage Form Crushability Analysis
container-title: American Journal of Health-System Pharmacy
98a478467a1fc5d4a043bea8d613c2271d13a2ad.abstract: Abstract Purpose To systematically evaluate ChatGPT Plus (GPT-4o) and Google Gemini Pro as decision-support instruments for the crushability analysis of immediate-release (IR) oral solid dosage forms, benchmarked against a human expert reference using a validated four-question analytical checklist. Methods Sixteen IR oral solid dosage forms approved by the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) in 2024 were independently assessed for crushability (YES/NO) by a human expert team and each AI tool using an identical structured prompt. Evaluator reasoning was coded across four analytical domains. Inter-rater agreement across all three evaluators was quantified using Fleiss kappa (κ) with a 95% confidence interval (CI) and two-tailed z-test; kappa values were interpreted using the Landis and Koch scale. All computations were performed in Microsoft Excel. Results Human experts classified 11 of 16 products (68.8%) as crushable and 5 (31.3%) as not crushable. Eight products achieved unanimous three-way agreement. The Fleiss κ was 0.329 (Fair; 95% CI, 0.046-0.612; z = 2.28; p = 0.023), indicating statistically significant agreement above chance. Both tools substantially over-identified pharmacokinetic concerns relative to human experts (Gemini, 11/16; ChatGPT, 8/16; Human, 3/16), the primary driver of disagreement. Gemini's identification of QTc interval prolongation risk for mavorixafor prompted expert revision of the crushability recommendation to not crushable. ChatGPT's false positive recommendation for lazertinib, failing to detect a reactive acrylamide degradation pathway, represents the highest-risk error in the cohort. Conclusion Generative AI demonstrated statistically significant but fair overall agreement with human expert analysis. Systematic scope deviations, including out-of-scope pharmacokinetic reasoning and hallucination-adjacent misclassification, suppressed concordance and produced clinically consequential errors. These findings support AI as a structured first-pass screening tool, contingent on pharmacist-led verification, institutional governance, and heightened scrutiny for hazardous drugs and novel formulation-technology products.

title: Spaceborne radiation-tolerant atomic-layer memory with on-orbit real-time testing
container-title: National Science Review
9d352b5f9c36ae959b61388d42487899ef400509.abstract: Abstract The human endeavor in space exploration has never ceased, where space electronics with high radiation tolerance are of paramount importance. Due to the atomic-level thin-layer characteristic, atomic-layer material electronic devices exhibit extremely high radiation tolerance compared with traditional bulk material devices. However, on-orbit testing on atomic-layer electronics is still lacking, restricting the understanding of their online performance in the space environment. Here we report a spaceborne radiation-tolerant and low-noise atomic-layer MoS2 memory array. Deployed on the Fudan No.1 Satellite in a low Earth orbit, this work enables the first demonstration of on-orbit real-time testing on atomic-layer memory. To date, after 23 months of on-orbit testing, the accuracy of the returned memory data has remained at 100%, indicating impressive radiation tolerance. This work presents a substantial step forward for the practical application of atomic-layer space electronics.

title: Smiling Muscle Stimulation Alters Neural Processing During Emotional Face Comparison
container-title: Social Cognitive and Affective Neuroscience
20bebc9054b03ad0b211c48294e0f2c945c612c1.abstract: Abstract Within embodied and predictive-processing frameworks, emotional face perception is informed by bodily states, such as proprioceptive facial feedback. In line with this, our earlier work showed that activation of smiling muscles with facial neuromuscular electrical stimulation (fNMES) can induce a happiness bias in emotional face perception, and reduce visual face processing demands. Here, we extended this research to examine whether the same facial muscle stimulation biases the emotional representation of a face when it serves as a perceptual template (prime) for comparison with a following target face. In a delayed matching-to-sample task, 53 participants judged which of two sequentially presented faces appeared happier (or more female, in a control sex task). On half of trials, fNMES was applied bilaterally to the zygomaticus major during encoding of the prime face. Performance was held constant using an adaptive staircase. fNMES altered comparison judgments only when emotion was task-relevant, flattening the relation between emotion difference and choice. Across tasks, fNMES reduced N170 amplitudes and increased Early Posterior Negativity (EPN) differences between happy and sad faces. The prime EPN predicted choice only when emotion was task-relevant, whereas fNMES modulated emotion effects on the target N170 only in the control task. Facial feedback may thus increase the perceptual salience of emotion-relevant information, with task-dependent consequences for decisions.

title: Joint Search of CNN Training Parameters and Training Images Preserving Discriminative Features Required for Generalization Performance of CNN Models Using Interactive Genetic Algorithms
container-title: Big Data and Cognitive Computing
a79fd0b679b897b152eb63c61d58b2debd384c01.abstract: Selecting hyperparameters for training convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and determining the amount of training image data required for reliable generalization remain challenging and often time-consuming tasks, typically relying on manual trial-and-error. Generally, image datasets used to train CNNs often contain redundant images; so, there is a need to remove them and reconstruct a slimmed smart dataset using a reduced portion of the available training data. While genetic algorithms (GAs) have been applied to hyperparameter tuning, less attention has been given to how feature-rich images are systematically extracted from an original full dataset and how the usage rate of training data influences generalization performance. In this study, we propose an interactive GA-based framework that simultaneously optimizes key training parameters and the image usage rate, defined as the proportion of training images used during learning. By applying the interactive GA, for example, an operator can not only change the search range of each parameter for optimization even in GA running but also finish the process as needed while observing the optimization process performed by the GA. The approach is implemented within a MATLAB-based environment, allowing parameters to be adjusted dynamically during the optimization process. The experimental results on four different datasets, including CIFAR-10 and EuroSat, show that the proposed method can achieve a classification performance comparable to that of manually tuned models while using a reduced portion of the available training data. Although this is a dataset-specific observation and not a general minimum data threshold, it suggests that, depending on the dataset, similar accuracy levels can be achieved even with an image utilization rate of approximately 43%, suggesting that not all training samples contribute equally to the model’s performance. These findings demonstrate that the proposed interactive GA-based framework can reduce training-data utilization while maintaining comparable classification performance across multiple datasets.

title: Task-Matched Memory, Not Criticality, Decides Which Frozen Reservoir Helps
container-title: Entropy
8e0d9df87205511e3715cefdf7befe85e98c0654.abstract: The edge-of-chaos hypothesis holds that recurrent systems near criticality maximize memory capacity and expressivity, motivating a natural proposal: replace the non-chaotic linear recurrence of state-space models with a learnable chaotic one. We test this with a gain-tunable chaotic cell whose expansion is set by one calibrated parameter, instrumented with a validated Lyapunov estimator, and measure delay-resolved memory capacity against the lagged mutual information each target demands. Trained end to end, the chaotic recurrence confers no benefit over a gated RNN or its own periodic-regime ablation; a gate dose–response identifies the learned gate as the suppressing mechanism. Frozen under the canonical reservoir-computing protocol, it decisively outperforms a matched linear reservoir, yet a regime-pure control (n=20) shows that this is not criticality: an ordered reservoir (λ≈−0.30) matches or exceeds the critical one, and across six chaotic reservoir constructions, the ordered arm leads on 21 of 30 paired seeds. Criticality pays only where the target reaches far enough back, on Mackey–Glass and the Santa Fe laser, and delay-resolved measurement explains why: the ordered reservoir retains more at lags 1–3, the critical one retains two to three times more at lags 4–12, and across six targets, the critical margin tracks long-lag demand (Pearson r=+0.97), changing sign. We propose a two-factor account: bounded nonlinearity under contraction is necessary, and among nonlinear reservoirs, task-matched memory decides.

title: Functional Near-Infrared Spectroscopy Brain Network Dynamics Reveal Cognitive Function Variability During Acute High-Altitude Exposure
container-title: Phenomics
e83a0f95c2d22af2c71aa99f1b802b0507509662.abstract: Abstract After acute exposure to high altitude (HA), the mechanism underlying hemodynamics-related cerebral function remains unclear and comprehensive and systematic studies are lacking. In this paper, functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) was used to characterize cerebral activation and brain network dynamics during acute exposure to HA. Thirty healthy volunteers were recruited and divided equally into two groups, the HA group and the low-altitude (LA) control group, to perform a resting-state experiment. The amplitude of low-frequency fluctuation (ALFF, 0.09-0.8 Hz) and signal complexity were calculated to evaluate spontaneous neural activity. Moreover, the small-world networks were established to describe the corresponding brain network dynamics. Compared with the LA control group, the ALFF values of the HA group in the left middle frontal gyrus (L-MFG), left inferior frontal gyrus (L-IFG) and right inferior frontal gyrus (R-IFG) were significantly decreased $$\:\left(p<0.05\right).$$ Meanwhile, the HA group's signal complexity was significantly higher than that of the LA control group in the L-MFG, left superior frontal gyrus (L-SFG) and right superior frontal gyrus (R-SFG). This pattern can be described as higher chaotic complexity with lower fluctuation amplitude in spontaneous brain activity. Brain network results indicated altered brain network patterns in the prefrontal cortex with significantly reduced efficiency and increased randomness. During acute exposure to HA, abnormal changes in hemodynamics-related cerebral function were confirmed, which can potentially reveal the neurodynamic mechanisms underlying physiological responses to HA. These findings may contribute to a further understanding of abnormal neural function during acute exposure to HA.

title: Historical Groundwater Memory Predicts Site‐Specific Persistence Horizons Across Germany
container-title: Geophysical Research Letters
e4e81086d2032e1d522cea400767676e4ebe4150.abstract: Abstract Groundwater levels retain memory of antecedent hydrologic conditions, but whether this memory defines a persistent timescale of later groundwater behavior remains unclear. We analyzed weekly records from 3207 wells across Germany, estimating groundwater memory during 1991–2005 and persistence during 2013–2022. Historical autocorrelation‐implied timescales strongly predicted later persistence horizons (Spearman = 0.851; 95% confidence interval, 0.819–0.877), with a median absolute difference of 2 weeks. A well's own historical memory was much more closely related to later persistence than memory reassigned among hydrogeologically and spatially similar wells, indicating strong site specificity. Historical hydroclimatic–groundwater coupling was also associated with departures from the autocorrelation‐based expectation, and this relation persisted after removal of seasonal and trend components. These site‐specific timescales inform persistence‐based forecasting and provide a temporal perspective for groundwater resilience assessment and climate adaptation planning.

title: Task-Dependent Prefrontal Cortex Activation During Balance–Cognitive Dual Tasks in Ice Hockey Players: Evidence From Functional Near-Infrared Spectroscopy
8eb0d83a95e3a971cfc68664463086f780319df1.abstract: Abstract This study compared prefrontal activation in ice hockey players and non-athlete adults during balance and cognitive dual-task conditions and examined its relationship with balance performance. Seventeen male ice hockey players and 17 age-matched healthy controls completed five randomized tasks: static and dynamic balance single tasks, a cognitive single task, and static and dynamic balance–cognitive dual tasks. Functional near-infrared spectroscopy measured prefrontal oxygenated hemoglobin (HbO), while balance indices and cognitive performance were recorded. Repeated-measures analysis of variance and Pearson correlations were conducted. Players showed superior balance performance across balance tasks (P < 0.05), whereas cognitive performance did not differ (P > 0.05). A significant group × task interaction was found for left dorsolateral prefrontal cortex HbO changes (F = 5.303, P = 0.002, q = 0.022, η²p = 0.142). Compared with controls, players showed greater HbO changes during the static dual task but lower changes during the dynamic dual task. During the dynamic dual task, DLPFC-L HbO changes correlated positively with balance indices in players (r = 0.721, P = 0.001) and controls (r = 0.674, P = 0.003). Ice hockey players may achieve better balance through task-dependent, efficient prefrontal resource allocation.

title: Proceso del diseño y protocolo de una intervención cognitivo-conductual para disminuir el consumo del cigarro electrónico en jóvenes universitarios
The design process and protocol for a cognitive-behavioral intervention to reduce electronic cigarette use among university students
container-title: Revista Española de Salud Pública
7f3d5330cf91150ff7278de02fa3011b3576a32b.abstract: FUNDAMENTOS // El consumo de cigarrillos electrónicos constituye un problema emergente de Salud Pública entre los jóvenes universitarios debido al incremento de su uso y los riesgos asociados a la exposición a la nicotina. Las intervenciones cognitivo-conductuales han mostrado utilidad para abordar esta conducta; sin embargo, existe limitada evidencia de intervenciones estructuradas adaptadas al contexto mexicano. El objetivo del presente estudio fue diseñar una intervención para disminuir el consumo del cigarrillo electrónico en jóvenes universitarios y establecer el protocolo para su implementación. MÉTODOS // La intervención fue diseñada mediante las etapas de descubrimiento, diseño y refinación; los componentes incluidos se fundamentaron en la Teoría de la Conducta Planeada y las actividades a partir de la taxonomía de métodos de cambio de comportamiento. Posteriormente, se realizará un estudio piloto experimental y longitudinal con mediciones pretest, postest y seguimiento a tres meses. Se incluirá a sesenta estudiantes universitarios de entre dieciocho y veinticuatro años de una universidad pública mexicana, seleccionados mediante muestreo por conveniencia y asignados aleatoriamente a los grupos de estudio. La intervención constará de seis sesiones presenciales de cincuenta minutos con componentes educativos, reestructuración cognitiva y entrenamiento en habilidades sociales y personales. Los análisis estadísticos serán exploratorios e incluirán comparaciones entre grupos, mediciones repetidas y estimación de tamaños del efecto. CONCLUSIONES // El protocolo permitirá obtener evidencia preliminar sobre la factibilidad y evaluación inicial de una intervención para disminuir el consumo de cigarrillos electrónicos, aportando información para el diseño de estudios posteriores y estrategias de prevención en población universitaria mexicana.

title: Literal and abstract metaphorical framing in public welfare lottery advertising: cognitive and affective responses in welfare communication
container-title: Journal of Social Marketing
33abc54dae0a195b0a63e9c7e88b05e75ab3c572.abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine how literal-explicit welfare framing and abstract metaphorical framing influence cognitive, affective and behavioral responses toward the Taiwan Public Welfare Lottery. Moving beyond treating welfare advertisements as different metaphor types, the study distinguishes these two message frames to clarify how public welfare messages communicate social value. It also examines the cognition–affect–behavior process linking welfare-related brand understanding, brand attitude and behavioral intention. Design/methodology/approach A within-subjects experiment was conducted with 142 participants who viewed two official Taiwan Public Welfare Lottery advertisements representing literal-explicit welfare framing and abstract metaphorical framing. Paired-samples t-tests were used to compare framing effects. Confirmatory factor analysis and structural equation modeling were then used to assess the measurement model and examine the relationships among welfare-related brand understanding, brand attitude and behavioral intention. Findings No significant construct-level differences were found between the two framing conditions for welfare-related brand understanding, brand attitude or behavioral intention. Exploratory item-level analyses indicated differences in responses to several individual items. Structural equation modeling supported the proposed cognition–affect–behavior relationships. These item-level findings are exploratory and should not be interpreted as evidence of robust differential framing effects. Originality/value This study distinguishes literal-explicit welfare framing from abstract metaphorical framing rather than treating welfare advertisements as different metaphor types. It integrates Keller’s Brand Knowledge Model with a cognition–affect–behavior framework and offers a theoretically grounded and empirically cautious interpretation of framing effects in public welfare advertising.

title: Cognitive-Professional Resource Configurations for AI-Mediated Teaching: Perceived Teacher-Education Support and Intelligent Professional Action
container-title: Journal of Intelligence
0b58e753e8ba8dae3f0d3ce821012c77d5a81c38.abstract: AI-mediated teaching requires teachers to evaluate uncertain information, respond to changing conditions, and integrate AI with pedagogical judgment. This study examined four cognitive-professional resource domains relevant to intelligent professional action: digital literacy, digital resilience, AI-mediated epistemic agency (AMEA), and AI-TPACK. Variable-centered and person-centered analyses drew on a cross-sectional survey of 942 YouShi Plan preservice teachers at one Chinese university. Perceived structured teacher-education support was positively associated with all four resources. Self-reported teaching innovation competence was positively associated with jointly higher digital literacy and digital resilience, with the response surface primarily reflecting their combined level. Four resource profiles mainly differed in overall level and showed graded differences in perceived teaching innovation competence. Higher perceived support was also associated with membership in higher-resource profiles. Together, these findings connect perceived teacher-education support, cognitive-professional resource configurations, and self-reported teaching innovation competence, positioning the latter as a domain-specific perceived capability relevant to intelligent professional action in AI-mediated teaching.

title: The Shape of Memory
db4a32e636809a4af096b0fc8377d3d383bf4770.abstract: ‘The Shape of Memory offers a compelling new perspective on the very old tradition of thinking about memory in terms of space. […] With its geometry-informed readings of memory narratives by Günter Grass, Georges Perec, Patrick Modiano, and Martin Walser, The Shape of Memory is a major contribution to literary memory studies.’ – Astrid Erll, Author of Memory in Culture and Travels in Time ‘As elegant as it is erudite, Paul Leworthy’s extended meditation on the multiple forms and shapes memory takes in post-war European literature is an extraordinary achievement. By turns philosophical and profoundly analytical, The Shape of Memory will become a standard work in critical memory studies. And it is a pure pleasure to read!’ – James E. Young, Author of The Texture of Memory and The Stages of Memory Objects and spaces often feature prominently in literary narratives about memory, but what is the role of such objects and spaces when they serve neither as memory media nor metaphors? To answer this question, this book explores how our embodied experience of the physical world has shaped how we talk and think about memory, exposing the essential importance of spatial dimensions. The concept of the ‘memory chronotope’ is introduced and put to use in analyses of novels by Günter Grass, Georges Perec, Patrick Modiano and Martin Walser, revealing how container and surface spaces in the texts articulate distinct conceptions of memory and attitudes towards specific histories. Combining memory theory, cultural history and literary analysis, this book surveys the role of objects and spaces in memory discourse, exposes the impact of embodied experience on thinking about memory, and offers a new lens for reading memory work in literary narratives – one focused on the ‘shape’ of memory.

title: From Analogue to Digital Experiences: Rethinking Cognitive Reserve in Older Adults
container-title: Geriatrics
de0630545853eaefdfb17dd504d9001c07104a00.abstract: The construct of cognitive reserve (CR) has traditionally been grounded in analogue life-course indicators, including years of education, occupational complexity, lifestyle, and cognitively stimulating activities. However, the rapid digital transformation of recent decades has introduced a pervasive environmental factor that may reshape the experiences through which CR is built: sustained interaction with digital technologies. This narrative review examines the emerging relationship between CR and digital experiences, with particular attention to heterogeneity within the older population. We distinguish between older adults whose adult and working lives were predominantly analogue, currently in their eighties, and new older adults, currently in their sixties and seventies, who encountered digital technologies during adulthood and progressively integrated them into their personal and professional lives. Available evidence suggests that engagement with digital environments may be associated with better executive functioning, attention, visuospatial abilities, and memory, although most studies are observational. Existing CR instruments, developed within a predominantly analogue framework, do not systematically capture these experiences. We therefore propose an integrated analogue–digital model of CR, in which digital experiences expand rather than replace traditional reserve dimensions. Within this model, we introduce Digital Cognitive Reserve (DCR) as a framework for assessing digital experiences as possible proxies of reserve and outline four preliminary dimensions (digital exposure, diversity, cognitive complexity, and adaptability), together with testable predictions that may inform future studies and assessment tools. Longitudinal, psychometric, and neurobiological studies are needed to test whether digital experiences contribute to cognitive resilience and to guide technology-based interventions tailored to cohort-specific profiles.

title: 2D Memory Transistors for Neuromorphic Computing
container-title: Materials
3f7a9dfee5437959ac78b4a460fb5d6ec2ff40d9.abstract: The boom in artificial intelligence has driven in-memory computing for high speed and power efficiency. Motivated by the need, neuromorphic computing (NC)—mimicking biological spike neural networks—ies a promising alternative that requires artificial neurons and synapses to construct NC circuits. 2D memory transistors have received intensive interest in recent research for NC applications as both artificial neurons and synapses with additional advantages for high device density and energy efficiency. This review intends to highlight recent progress made in the exploration of 2D memory transistors and their implementation into electrical and optoelectronic NC circuits. Discussions of remaining challenges and future perspectives are also provided.

title: Development of generalization outpaces memory specificity in early childhood
6d3fab1754625937180b65b551bb69fa55279301.abstract: A hallmark of the mature human memory system is the ability to extract commonalities across experiences while preserving details that distinguish individual events. Although research suggests that memory generalization emerges earlier than memory specificity, their developmental trajectories and interrelations remain poorly understood. Here, we examined the development of generalization and multiple aspects of memory specificity in children aged 4 to 8 years, assessed at two timepoints one year apart (N (TP1) = 170; N (TP2) = 119). We found that generalization improved more rapidly than memory specificity during early childhood. Moreover, longitudinal changes in generalization and specificity were unrelated, suggesting distinct developmental trajectories. These findings reveal an early developmental advantage for generalization over specificity, potentially reflecting an adaptive prioritization of extracting environmental regularities over retaining unique details of individual experiences.

27ed79eeba1dbf4baad03d667c5fb9e2fe1556c5.abstract: Purpose The current research examined the association between teacher support and students’ effort and persistence in mathematics, with particular attention to the mediating role of mathematics self-efficacy. Methods The research employed a cross-sectional model, utilising the international large-scale dataset from the Programme of the International Student Assessment (PISA) 2022 cycle. The sample was consisted of a total of 7,250 15-year-old students from 196 schools in Turkey. The research employed a simple mediation model, using the PROCESS macro for SPSS in order to examine the associations between teacher support and effort and persistence in mathematics through mathematical self-efficacy. Results Teacher support was positively associated with mathematics self-efficacy, while mathematics self-efficacy demonstrated a particularly strong association with students’ effort and persistence. Furthermore, the substantial indirect effect indicated that mathematics self-efficacy partly mediated the association between teacher support and effort and persistence in mathematics. Conclusion The results provided support for the proposed theoretical framework, indicating that teacher support is associated with students’ motivational engagement in mathematics both directly and indirectly.

title: Dependencia cognitiva de la inteligencia artificial en estudiantes de ciencias de la salud: una revisión de alcance
Cognitive dependence on artificial intelligence among health sciences students: a scoping review
container-title: Salud Medicina e Innovación Journal
acc7660cce582dc86ebb8b44802786f3eb4493f0.abstract: Introduction. The rapid incorporation of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) into university education has shifted the debate from academic integrity toward a deeper question: what happens to the cognitive processes of learners who habitually delegate reasoning tasks to conversational systems. In the health sciences, where professional competence is built upon clinical reasoning and judgement under uncertainty, this question carries clinical and not merely pedagogical relevance. Objective. To map and critically synthesise the available evidence on cognitive dependence on artificial intelligence among health sciences students, identifying its prevalence, the proposed explanatory mechanisms, its cognitive and affective correlates, and the moderating factors that condition its effects. Methods. Scoping review conducted according to PRISMA-ScR guidance. PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, SciELO, Redalyc and ERIC were searched, together with the academic meta-search engines Consensus, Elicit and SciSpace, covering literature published between January 2022 and October 2026 in Spanish and English. Empirical studies, systematic and scoping reviews, and conceptual works on university students’ use of GenAI were included, with preferential analysis of those conducted in health sciences populations. Extraction was organised into eight thematic domains through narrative synthesis. Results. GenAI adoption among health sciences students is virtually universal, with use prevalences between 83.9 % and 96.3 %, and self-reported dependence exceeding 60 % in the largest series. Quantitative evidence converges on a small-to-moderate inverse association between AI dependence and critical thinking. The proposed mechanisms include substitutive cognitive offloading, cognitive debt, metacognitive laziness, cognitive fatigue and automation bias, and all of them share a common core: the transfer of epistemic agency from the learner to the system. In the clinical domain, three stage-specific risks are described: never-skilling, deskilling and mis-skilling. Dependence is further associated with anxiety and depressive symptoms, and with high uncritical acceptance of fabricated content and references. The effect is not deterministic: mode of use, AI literacy, metacognitive scaffolding and assessment design consistently moderate the direction of the outcome. Conclusions. Cognitive dependence on GenAI is a plausible and measurable educational risk, but a conditional one. The evidence supports neither prohibition nor uncritical adoption, but rather curricular and assessment redesign aimed at preserving students’ epistemic agency. Longitudinal studies with objective measures of unassisted competence are needed, as is an Ibero-American body of research that remains scarce.

title: Developing a Contextual Framework for Cognitive Digital Twins in Surgery: An Exploratory Interdisciplinary Survey to Inform a Delphi Consensus Study (Preprint)
a3ac410f83cd666cd33465aa2bc6a5827ebded44.abstract: BACKGROUND Cognitive digital twins (CDTs) represent a subset of digital twins, which are dynamic digital representations of real-world objects or processes, generated using data collected from sensors. CDTs using cognitive or neurophysiological data i.e. data reflecting human cognitive processes have huge potential within the surgical field, they could model how different intraoperative scenarios affect the mental workload of the surgeon or wider operating team. This could provide a platform for identifying and modifying factors contributing to excessive or insufficient cognitive demand, with the aim of maintaining workload within an optimal range. OBJECTIVE The aim of this study was to use the results of survey disseminated to a multidisciplinary audience to devise a framework to guide a future Delphi consensus study on the topic of CDTs in surgery. METHODS A survey was conceived highlighting key areas with an information-gap pertaining to CDTs. This was disseminated to participants of a multi-disciplinary workshop titled ‘Physics- and AI-Driven Digital Twins for Patient-Specific Robotic Diagnosis, Interventions and Therapies’. Demographic data was collected and open-ended questions were used in four domains. Qualitative data were analysed by content analysis by two independent reviewers, who then collated their results after review. A framework was created using the results. RESULTS There was a response rate of 13/27 (48%) participants, with an equal distribution of clinicians and researchers/academics. 12 coded domains were derived from content analysis and found to vary in frequency throughout the four survey sections. No single domain was represented as a majority amongst respondents. The analysis from the survey was used to create a robust framework centred around the translational pathway and key challenges from conception to clinical application. CONCLUSIONS More work needs to be achieved on identifying key issues and solutions to hurdles within the translational pipeline and multidisciplinary collaboration are vital. The framework could be used to help a steering group guide formation of the Delphi first round/qualitative questions

title: Prefrontal Activation and Cognitive Heterogeneity in Pediatric Sleep-Disordered Breathing
container-title: JAMA Otolaryngology–Head & Neck Surgery
087470215be2278d7f6d4a848ace5685c8be9606.abstract: Importance Activation of the prefrontal cortex during attention and executive-function tasks can moderate associations between sleep-disordered breathing (SDB) symptoms and parent-reported behavior. However, conventional severity measures do not explain why cognitive outcomes vary among children with SDB. Objective To assess whether prefrontal cortex (PFC) activity, reflecting attention and impulse control, is associated with SDB severity and cognition, and whether it distinguishes children whose cognition diverges from their SDB severity. Design, Setting, and Participants This cross-sectional study included patients aged 5 to 11 years who were referred for evaluation of SDB at 2 academic pediatric otolaryngology centers from January 2024 to March 2026. Patients with neuromuscular disorders, prior airway surgery, continuous positive airway pressure treatment, sickle cell disease, stimulant use, or developmental delay were excluded. Exposures SDB severity measured by the Pediatric Sleep-Related Breathing Disorders Questionnaire, Apnea-Hypopnea Index (AHI), and oxygen saturation (SpO 2 ) nadir. PFC activation measured by functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) during a computer-based go or no-go task in which children respond to frequent cues and withhold responses to infrequent ones. Main Outcomes and Measures Parent-reported executive function (Behavior Rating Inventory of Executive Function) and cognition (US National Institutes of Health [NIH] Toolbox Cognition Battery), and their associations with PFC activation. Linear mixed-effects models with false discovery rate (FDR) correction tested associations and moderation effects. Results Among 284 children (mean [SD] age, 7.9 [1.8] years; 130 [45.8%] female), 237 (83.5%) were at high risk for SDB. The mean (SD) AHI was 11.7 (14.5) events per hour and SpO 2 nadir was 86.4% (8.2%). Higher AHI was associated with greater left dorsolateral PFC activation (oxyhemoglobin: β, 0.08; 95% CI, 0.03 to 0.12; deoxyhemoglobin: β, −0.07; 95% CI, −0.11 to −0.03), and lower SpO 2 nadir was associated with greater activation (β, 0.14; 95% CI, 0.06 to 0.23). Greater activation in the right dorsolateral PFC was associated with worse parent-reported executive function after FDR correction. No severity measure was directly associated with NIH Toolbox performance after correction. However, PFC activation moderated the SDB severity-cognition association: children with greater activation maintained comparable performance despite more severe SDB. Conclusions and Relevance In this cross-sectional study, task-related PFC activation was associated with SDB severity and moderated the severity-cognition association. fNIRS may help identify children whose cognitive profiles deviate from conventional severity metrics, thereby supporting individualized cognitive risk assessment.

title: Migration, Memory, and the Politics of Cultural Survival: A Philosophical Analysis of the Xibe Belun Dance as a Site of Identity Negotiation
container-title: Kalagatos
e0c1e6147fdced48a4db11c7c75e6e7b0328f851.abstract: In 1764, over four thousand Xibe (Sibe) banner officers and their families were dispatched by the Qianlong Emperor from Shengjing across the Mongolian steppes to the Ili frontier of Xinjiang. This geopolitical relocation provoked a foundational historical trauma and radical spatial rupture. Paradoxically, while their remaining kinsmen in Northeast China underwent rapid cultural assimilation, the isolated garrison community in Qapqal preserved their Tungusic-Manchu language, script, and cosmological rituals. This paper conducts an ontological and politico-aesthetic interrogation of the traditional Xibe Belun dance. Moving beyond standard ethnomusicological typologies, the study synthesizes Merleau-Ponty’s phenomenology of the lived body (corps propre), Paul Connerton’s somatic memory, and Diana Taylor’s concept of the “repertoire.” Drawing on Guimarães’s (2021) analysis of Walter Benjamin in Kalágatos, the paper argues that the Belun’s signature kinetic vocabulary—the rapid shoulder trembles (shouerken), sudden kinetic freezes, and rhythmic rebounds—operates as a bodily manifestation of Benjaminian Eingedenken, rupturing the homogeneous, empty time of historicist forgetting. Furthermore, incorporating Sahd’s (2023) critique of Jacques Rancière’s aesthetics of creative action in Kalágatos, the analysis reveals how the dance radically reconfigures the imperial “distribution of the sensible” (partage du sensible). The subaltern military body, originally designated as a silent instrument of border defense, transforms itself through kinetic enunciation into an autonomous aesthetic subject. The Belun dance emerges not as an inert folkloric relic, but as an active, counter-hegemonic somatic archive and an ongoing site of identity negotiation, ethical recognition, and cultural survival.

title: Decidua-accumulated effector-like memory CD8+ T cells orchestrate localized antimicrobial defense without compromising fetal tolerance
container-title: Journal of Clinical Investigation
a1b62fb8bd6e447e8235aed1cacb113c137953a4.abstract: Deciphering immune privilege at the maternal-fetal interface is essential for understanding how reproductive success and host defense are simultaneously maintained. Decidualization, occurring within the specialized stromal tissue encapsulating the fetus and placenta, shapes local immune adaptation required for healthy pregnancy. Here, we identify a decidua-enriched effector-like memory CD8 + T cell subset marked by CD45RA in humans and CX3CR1 in mice. These cells preferentially accumulate in the decidua, which harbors a CX3CL1-dominant chemokine niche, and disruption of Cx3cr1 or uterine Cx3cl1 impaired their decidual recruitment and tissue localization. Human CD45RA + and murine CX3CR1 + decidual memory CD8 + T cells shared conserved transcriptional and functional features, including enhanced cytotoxic potential and limited inflammatory cytokine production. Functionally, CX3CL1-mediated CD8 + T cell accumulation improved local control of prenatal Listeria monocytogenes infection and reduced infection-associated fetal loss. In contrast, fetal antigen-specific CD8 + T cell accumulation and fetal resorption occurred independently of uterine CX3CL1. Together, our findings define the maternal-fetal interface as an active immunological gatekeeper, that compartmentalizing CD8 + T cell-mediated antimicrobial adaptive immunity through the conserved CX3CL1-CX3CR1 axis, supporting pathogen-specific defense while preserving fetal tolerance.

title: Disentangling cognitive and emotional load in interpreting
container-title: Target. International Journal of Translation Studies

b9d7460fc7105026bd08e8f304e7eebedefde8f5.abstract: Abstract This study employs a multimodal approach to investigate how emotional and cognitive load differentially impact interpreter stress. Twenty student interpreters consecutively interpreted four Turkish-to-English mental healthcare narratives of varying emotionality and difficulty, constructed using a 2×2 factorial design. Stress responses were measured using galvanic skin response (GSR), voice parameters (pitch and voice intensity), and self-report scales (PANAS, STAI, and NASA-TLX). Stimuli were normed for emotional valence and linguistic complexity using readability indices, expert ratings, and natural language processing (NLP) tools. Results showed that primarily cognitive load drove GSR arousal, particularly during later interpreting stages, whereas emotional load was reflected in pitch and self-reported negative affect. A pitch convergence between speaker and interpreter also emerged. None of the stress indicators predicted interpreting accuracy, suggesting a possible role for individual coping strategies.

title: Memory Self-Awareness Phenotypes are Associated with Alzheimer’s Disease Biomarker Burden and Clinical Progression in Amnestic Mild Cognitive Impairment
6998a28886ba638bf67c9bc3d2123488ec274c7d.abstract: STRUCTURED ABSTRACT Background Altered memory self-awareness is common in mild cognitive impairment (MCI), but its relationship to Alzheimer’s disease (AD) pathology and progression remains unclear. Methods Using 590 amnestic MCI ADNI participants, memory self-awareness was derived from participant–informant discrepancies on the memory subdomain of the Everyday Cognition questionnaire. Heightened awareness and unawareness subscores were calculated, and k-means clustering identified four phenotypes. Associations with cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) and positron emission tomography (PET) were examined, and clinical progression was assessed using Cox models. Results Aware and Unaware groups showed lower CSF amyloid-β, and higher CSF phosphorylated tau and PET amyloid. The Unaware phenotype was associated with increased progression risk (hazard ratio 2.41, 95% CI 1.48–3.92), whereas the Worried Well phenotype showed reduced risk (hazard ratio 0.58, 95% CI 0.34–0.99). Conclusions Multidimensional assessment of memory self-awareness identifies biologically and prognostically distinct subgroups within MCI and may improve risk stratification in prodromal AD.

title: Collective directional memory controls the range of epithelial cell migration
e4f664987b8cbc7ab0bd90509b65d484bd4f4c15.abstract: Cell migration is a fundamental behavior in multicellular development, regeneration, and homeostasis, which is deregulated in cancer. Epithelial cells migrate individually when isolated and collectively within a tissue. However, how interactions between cells affect their ability to explore space and their sensitivity to guidance signals is poorly understood. We show that isolated cells that are persistent random walkers adopt a super-diffusive behavior in an epithelium. The effect is stronger than external guidance cues and enables cells to reach greater distances than when isolated. This behavior is consistent with a fractional Brownian motion that emerges from velocity coordination between neighboring cells with intact intercellular adhesion. Furthermore, we show how the molecular stability and mechanosensitivity of adhesion complexes, both linked to the ability of the adhesion protein vinculin to dimerize, ultimately regulate the speed of collective migration and the sensitivity to guidance signals. Together, our results show how cell speed, persistence, and directionality define the efficiency of spatial cell exploration on short, intermediate, and long time scales, respectively.

Disconnected Neighborhoods: Segregated Interactions and Cognitive Health in Middle-Aged and Older Adults
cd238e5c5fb36cdc595073e3a8ee928b751a4137.abstract: Residential segregation constrains interaction across social lines, operating as an established place-based risk factor for health. Yet, studies conventionally operationalize segregation through static residential composition rather than active patterns of interaction. This study examines segregation by capturing both residents’ characteristics and their movement through broader neighborhood networks, as inferred from collective travel patterns. We use the Spatial Preference in Local Interaction (SPLIT) index – a mobility-based, tract-level measure of cross-neighborhood segregation – and link it to American Community Survey data on tract-level prevalence of cognitive impairment among middle-aged and older adults from 2018 to 2023. We find that cognitive impairment is significantly lower in tracts where mobility networks are economically diverse yet racially and ethnically homogeneous – a pattern consistent with the protective effects of in-group cohesion (bonding) and cross-area resource acquisition (bridging). These findings suggest that the cognitive consequences of cross-neighborhood interaction resist simple characterization, underscoring how residential ties regulate access to both proximate community supports and wider economic opportunity structures.
