title: Facets of connectivity change: tracing the dynamics of attraction and differentiation in the rise of the English deverbal prepositions given and considering
container-title: Cognitive Linguistics
9b6b81e8b4ee83240d59caad71a2ce94bad9042f.abstract: Abstract Although the emergence of deverbal prepositions has been well documented in studies on grammaticalization, existing research has largely focused on individual items, paying limited attention to their interactions over time. Addressing this gap, this article examines whether the rise of the past participle given as a deverbal preposition over the past century reflects attraction to or differentiation from the paradigmatically related and more established form considering . Using two tree-based machine-learning methods, namely Boruta Feature Selection and Conditional Inference Trees, the present study reveals that the two constructions exhibit attraction in the formal and pragmatic dimensions, as evidenced by their distributions across left-peripheral positions and modal contexts. By contrast, the two constructions display differentiation in the discourse dimension, as evidenced by a clearer division of labor across genres. Taken together, these findings advance the theoretical understanding of connectivity change by showing that it cannot be reduced to a simple strengthening-versus-weakening dichotomy. Instead, it involves a probabilistic interplay of both attraction and differentiation across distinct linguistic dimensions.

title: Compassionate and Self-Critical Self-Relating Following Interpersonal Trauma: Differential Associations With Cognitive Emotion Regulation and Interpersonal Competence
container-title: Journal of Social and Personal Relationships
9a0c58d8ad0bc8b7d2040bcac5ecd1ea95955fab.abstract: Interpersonal trauma poses enduring challenges for relational functioning in early adulthood, yet substantial heterogeneity exists in how individuals adapt interpersonally following such experiences. Drawing on self-compassion theory and emotion-regulation flexibility perspectives, this study examined how self-compassion—conceptualized as a multidimensional construct comprising positive (self-kindness, common humanity, mindfulness) and negative (self-judgment, isolation, over-identification) components—relates to interpersonal competence, and whether adaptive and maladaptive cognitive emotion-regulation strategies differentially accounted for these associations. Participants were 1,004 South Korean young adults (49.8% male; M age = 29.47) who had experienced a subjectively distressing interpersonal event or relational loss. They completed measures of self-compassion, cognitive emotion regulation, and interpersonal competence. Path-analytic models examined direct and indirect associations among these variables. Additional moderation analyses examined whether the associations between self-compassion and cognitive emotion regulation differed by sex. Overall self-compassion was positively associated with interpersonal competence, with this association driven primarily by positive components of self-compassion. Positive components of self-compassion exhibited robust indirect associations with interpersonal competence via greater use of adaptive cognitive emotion-regulation strategies (e.g., acceptance, positive reappraisal). In contrast, negative components of self-compassion were associated with reduced use of adaptive strategies and greater use of maladaptive strategies (e.g., rumination, self-blame). Negative components also showed small positive indirect associations with interpersonal competence through maladaptive strategies, suggesting that these strategies were not uniformly associated with lower interpersonal competence. Tests of moderation by sex showed that the associations between self-compassion and cognitive emotion regulation were largely comparable across male and female participants. Together, these findings suggest that individual differences in self-relating and cognitive emotion regulation may help explain heterogeneity in interpersonal competence and are broadly consistent with emotion-regulation flexibility perspectives on adaptation following interpersonal trauma.

title: Memory-Enhanced Visible-Light Photonic Synapses in Interface-Engineered ZnON/IGZO Oxide Transistors

8567c79e2efcd5fb245dabd55984fbd239faaf47.abstract: Abstract Zinc oxynitride (ZnON) thin-film transistors (TFTs) are attractive visible-light photoactive devices owing to their narrow and tunable optical bandgap; however, the limited population of deep-level trap states can restrict post-illumination carrier retention, resulting in weak photonic synaptic retention. Here, memory-enhanced visible-light photonic synapses are demonstrated using interface-engineered ZnON/Indium gallium zinc oxide (IGZO) double-layer oxide TFTs. A thin IGZO capping layer is integrated onto the ZnON channel to preserve ZnON-dominated red, green, and blue (RGB) photoresponse, while modifying the interfacial electronic environment and carrier-relaxation dynamics. The ZnON/IGZO TFT exhibits RGB responsivities of 2.93, 11.0, and 17.6 A W–1 and specific detectivities of 1.10 × 1012, 3.82 × 1012, and 6.08 × 1012 Jones under red, green, and blue illumination, respectively. The device also exhibits enhanced short- and long-term synaptic retention behavior under pulsed optical stimulation, wavelength-dependent synaptic plasticity, and analogue synaptic weight modulation. Spectroscopic ellipsometry and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy reveal that the IGZO capping layer preserves ZnON-dominated visible-light absorption, while inducing changes in oxygen-related bonding environments across the bilayer structure. Photoinduced current transient spectroscopy reveals a redistribution of electrically active trap states toward both relatively shallow- and deep-level regions after IGZO capping. The shallow-level states are correlated with enhanced photoresponse, whereas the deep-level states are consistent with delayed carrier relaxation and prolonged post-illumination retention. These results demonstrate that ZnON/IGZO bilayer engineering provides an effective strategy for coupling broadband visible-light sensitivity with tunable carrier-retention dynamics in oxide photonic synapses.

title: Self-Paced Robust Sparse Non-Negative Matrix Factorization with Optimal Graph Learning
container-title: Big Data and Cognitive Computing
c9a55ce1b7551597919bd8eda67e539b0dba25ff.abstract: Non-negative matrix factorization (NMF) is a well-established parts-based representation learning paradigm for high-dimensional data. However, existing NMF methods often struggle to capture the intrinsic structure of data and lack sufficient robustness when dealing with corrupted data. To address these limitations, we propose a self-paced robust sparse NMF framework with optimal graph learning, termed SPRSNMF. Specifically, we integrate ℓ2,1 norm minimization with non-convex sparse regularization into a unified framework. To be specific, the ℓ2,1 norm-based reconstruction loss is utilized to enhance the robustness against noise and outliers, while ℓ2,1/2 is imposed on the representation matrix to promote sparsity. Furthermore, the self-paced learning progressively selects samples from “easy” to “hard” so that the influence of noise and outliers is suppressed during optimization. Moreover, by combining adaptive graph learning with the low-rank constraint, we derive an optimal graph learning scheme to effectively uncover the intrinsic structure of data. We develop an effective block coordinate descent (BCD) algorithm to solve the resulting non-convex optimization problem, and theoretically establish its convergence and computational complexity analysis. Extensive experiments on nine benchmark datasets from various domains demonstrate the superiority of SPRSNMF over state-of-the-art approaches.

title: THE AI LEARNING PARADOX: REVEALING HOW UNIVERSITY STUDENTS NAVIGATE LEARNING CONVENIENCE, COGNITIVE EFFORT, DIGITAL CONTENT INFLUENCE, ACADEMIC CONFIDENCE, AND EDUCATIONAL ENGAGEMENT
container-title: JOURNAL OF SOCIAL SCIENCES DEVELOPMENT
70381f8c9c0c1fb7ece5e9c53fdfd185f4968b08.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has introduced a significant paradox in higher education by simultaneously enhancing learning accessibility, personalization, and academic confidence while creating concerns regarding reduced cognitive effort and technological dependency. This study explores how university students navigate AI-supported learning experiences by examining five key dimensions: learning convenience, cognitive effort, digital content influence, academic confidence, and educational engagement. Adopting a qualitative research design, the study investigates the lived experiences of 18 Pakistani university students through semi-structured interviews. Data were analyzed using reflexive thematic analysis to identify patterns within students’ perceptions and practices of AI use. The findings reveal six major themes: AI as an educational accelerator, convenience versus intellectual struggle, confidence versus competence, transformation of digital learning consumption, risks of AI dependency, and purposeful AI-supported learning. The study demonstrates that AI can enhance educational engagement when used as a cognitive partner but may weaken independent learning when relied upon excessively. The findings highlight the importance of AI literacy, responsible technology integration, and pedagogical strategies that preserve students’ cognitive autonomy while maximizing the benefits of AI in higher education.

title: Crafting of physical exhibits by undergraduate medical students: A mixed method study to assess the acquisition of higher-order cognitive skills and student perceptions
container-title: PLOS One
219dd7be132c912d1267263cdbbbb4ebdf4eeb2b.abstract: Active learning engages students in some activity that induces them to reflect upon ideas and how they are using these ideas. It also involves the process of keeping students mentally, and often physically, active in their learning through activities that engage them in gathering information, thinking, and solving problems. This study was conducted to determine if creating physical exhibits fosters higher-order cognitive skills like problem solving and critical thinking (application and analysis, respectively). In this study, carried out in the Department of Physiology, 50 medical undergraduate students were divided into four batches of 12–13 students each. Each batch was supervised by a faculty mentor and assigned a topic for the preparation of a physical exhibit. Multiple-choice questions (MCQ) testing higher-order cognitive skills were used to assess the gain in knowledge post-intervention. The qualitative component of the study consisted of open-ended questions and a Focus Group Discussion to ascertain students’ perceptions regarding the creation of physical exhibits. The students created physical exhibits related to the sensory pathway, the light reflex & the conjunctival reflex, the micturition reflex mechanism, and the automatic bladder. Median post-test scores showed significant improvement compared to pretest scores (16 vs 12, p < 0.01). Students reported that the active learning strategy promoted deep learning, enhanced memory, and helped them apply theory to practice. Secondly, it cultivated teamwork skills. The learning experience was enjoyable and led them to score higher on the post-test exams. Students also suggested that tightening the nuts and bolts, as in prior meticulous planning, would make the experience more enjoyable.

title: Harpagide alleviates neuroinflammation and cognitive dysfunction in sepsis-associated encephalopathy: Association with the MMP9/NF-κB signaling pathway
container-title: PLOS One
2f2bf9110d155f9d82d80bd29894e0de16d52a13.abstract: Background Sepsis-associated encephalopathy (SAE) is a severe neurological complication of sepsis, characterized by uncontrolled neuroinflammation and cognitive decline, yet no specific therapy is currently available. Harpagide, a naturally occurring iridoid glycoside, has been reported to possess anti-inflammatory and neuroprotective activities; however, its therapeutic potential in SAE remains unexplored. This study aimed to investigate whether Harpagide exerts neuroprotective effects in SAE and to elucidate the underlying molecular mechanisms. Methods A mouse model of SAE was established by intraperitoneal injection of lipopolysaccharide (LPS, 18 mg/kg). Cognitive performance was assessed using behavioral assays. Brain tissue morphology and neuronal survival were evaluated through histopathological examination. Glial cell activation and the production of pro-inflammatory cytokines (TNF-α, IL-1β, IL-6) were measured. Network pharmacology was employed to predict potential targets, followed by molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations to predict binding interactions with core targets. Western blotting was performed to determine the expression levels of key proteins involved in the MMP9/NF-κB signaling pathway. Results Treatment with Harpagide significantly improved behavioral performance, ameliorated brain pathological changes, preserved hippocampal neurons, suppressed glial activation, and reduced the levels of TNF-α, IL-1β, and IL-6 in SAE mice. Network pharmacology analysis predicted four core targets: GAPDH, CASP3, MMP9, and ICAM1. Molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations suggested stable binding between Harpagide and MMP9. Western blot analysis further showed that Harpagide treatment was associated with reduced expression of MMP9 and phosphorylated NF-κB p65 in both hippocampal and cortical tissues. Conclusions The present study demonstrates that Harpagide exerts neuroprotective effects in SAE, which are associated with mitigated neuroinflammation and reduced MMP9/NF-κB signaling, supporting its potential as a promising therapeutic candidate for this devastating condition.

6d9355f32d64c5db3146f0bae30dddbeb586cfc9.abstract: هدفت الدراسة إلى التعرف على مستوى العبء المعرفي ومستوى الدافعية للإنجاز، والكشف عن طبيعة العلاقة الارتباطية بينهما لدى طلاب الشهادة الثانوية بمدينة طبرق. واعتمدت المنهج الوصفي الارتباطي، واستخدمت مقياس العبء المعرفي لحلمي الفيل (2015)، ومقياس الدافعية للإنجاز المنسوب إلى الشعراوي (2000) والزغبي (2003) ، واعتمدت الدراسة في التحليل الإحصائي على عينة قوامها (348) طالبًا وطالبة وحُللت البيانات باستخدام اختبار «ت» لعينة واحدة ومعامل ارتباط بيرسون، وأظهرت النتائج أن متوسط العبء المعرفي بلغ (52.53) بانحراف معياري (8.47)، وهو أعلى من المتوسط الفرضي (48)، وكانت قيمة «ت» (9.97) عند مستوى دلالة أقل من (0.001). كما بلغ متوسط الدافعية للإنجاز (84) بانحراف معياري (10.62)، مقارنة بالمتوسط الفرضي (72)، وكانت قيمة «ت» (21.06) عند مستوى دلالة أقل من (0.001). وكشفت النتائج عن علاقة ارتباطية موجبة دالة إحصائيًا بين العبء المعرفي والدافعية للإنجاز، إذ بلغ معامل ارتباط بيرسون (0.143) عند مستوى دلالة (0.008). وتشير هذه النتيجة إلى ارتباط موجب محدود القوة ، ولا تثبت وجود علاقة سببية بين المتغيرين ، كما بينت النتائج وجود فروق في العبء المعرفي لدى طلاب الشهادة الثانوية تبعا لمتغير النوع لصالح الاناث ، ايضا وجود فروق في العبء المعرفي لدى طلاب الشهادة الثانوية تبعا لمتغير المدرسة ، وذلك لصالح طلاب المدارس العامة . وبينت النتائج عدم وجود فروق دالة احصائياً في الدافعية للإنجاز لدى طلاب الشهادة الثانوية تبعا لمتغير النوع ، وعدم وجود فروق دالة إحصائيا في مستوى الدافعية للإنجاز لدى طلاب الشهادة الثانوية تبعا لمتغير المدرسة .

title: Pipelining the Memory Hierarchy for Ultra-Long-Context Language Model Training
container-title: GetMobile: Mobile Computing and Communications
218602c78f7bfcd3719c82154ddeffbcc5e66baf.abstract: Long-context language models are attractive because they can read whole documents, code repositories, conversations, and scientific sequences. However, a long inference window is not the same as a model that was trained to use millions of tokens reliably. Direct long-context training is blocked by temporary memory spikes from activations, attention buffers, communication workspaces, and the final loss computation, even when model parameters and optimizer states are already sharded. Our proposed method, Fully Pipelined Distributed Transformer (FPDT), treats the long sequence problem as a memory-hierarchy scheduling problem. It chunks each sequence before distributed attention, stages inactive query/ key/value tensors in host memory and uses double buffers to overlap transfers with attention computation. FPDT democratizes long sequence training, making it accessible on mobile and commodity hardware, such as high-end local machines. In our evaluation, FPDT trains contexts up to 16x longer than prior sequence-parallel baselines on the same hardware. It reaches a 2M-token context for an 8B model on four A100-80GB GPUs, and a 4M-token context for 8B Llama 3 on eight A100-80GB GPUs while sustaining 55.7% Model FLOPs Utilization (MFU) [1].

title: CONTRIBUIÇÕES DA TERAPIA COGNITIVO-COMPORTAMENTAL PARA O TRATAMENTO DE PESSOAS COM DIAGNÓSTICO DE ESQUIZOFRENIA
CONTRIBUCIONES DE LA TERAPIA COGNITIVO-CONDUCTUAL AL TRATAMIENTO DE PERSONAS DIAGNOSTICADAS CON ESQUIZOFRENIA
CONTRIBUTIONS OF COGNITIVE-BEHAVIORAL THERAPY TO THE TREATMENT OF PEOPLE DIAGNOSED WITH SCHIZOPHRENIA
container-title: RECIMA21 - Revista Científica Multidisciplinar - ISSN 2675-6218
e1ab12830c21a7e2fa309659dbf2e7e08a94363a.abstract: Este trabalho analisa as contribuições da Terapia Cognitivo- Comportamental (TCC) para o tratamento de pessoas com diagnóstico de esquizofrenia, com ênfase em sua eficácia na redução de sintomas e na melhoria da qualidade de vida. A esquizofrenia é um transtorno mental grave e persistente, caracterizado por alterações no pensamento, na percepção, no comportamento e no funcionamento psicossocial, podendo apresentar sintomas positivos, como delírios e alucinações, sintomas negativos e déficits cognitivos. Nesse contexto, a TCC constitui uma intervenção psicoterapêutica complementar à farmacoterapia, contribuindo para o manejo de manifestações clínicas que nem sempre são suficientemente controladas pelos psicofármacos. Por meio de revisão bibliográfica, este estudo sistematiza evidências acerca da utilização da TCC no tratamento da esquizofrenia, destacando seus efeitos sobre a redução da intensidade e do impacto de delírios e alucinações, a atenuação de sintomas negativos e a prevenção de recaídas. As evidências também apontam benefícios relacionados ao fortalecimento da adesão ao tratamento, ao desenvolvimento de estratégias de enfrentamento, à ampliação das habilidades sociais e à promoção de ganhos funcionais e psicossociais. Conclui-se que a TCC apresenta relevância como intervenção complementar no cuidado de pessoas com esquizofrenia, especialmente quando integrada a uma abordagem multidisciplinar. Sua utilização pode favorecer melhores desfechos clínicos e psicossociais, contribuindo para a autonomia, o funcionamento cotidiano e a qualidade de vida dos indivíduos.

title: A Metacognição no Ensino de Ciências da Natureza: Um Mapeamento Sistemático da Produção Científica Brasileira
Metacognition in Natural Science Teaching: A Systematic Mapping of Brazilian Scientific Production
container-title: Investigações em Ensino de Ciências
f367ca4a1006fc9d7dd139563c95425a8b7148fa.abstract: Este estudo teve como objetivo analisar, por meio de uma revisão sistemática da literatura nacional, os estudos sobre metacognição, com foco em sua caracterização e suas implicações para o ensino e a aprendizagem de Ciências da Natureza. Foram identificadas 109 produções (artigos, teses, dissertações e trabalhos de eventos), organizadas por meio de Análise do Conteúdo em três categorias: o cenário da metacognição no Ensino de Ciências; o papel do professor como mediador; e os processos metacognitivos dos estudantes. Os resultados indicam que, apesar do número ainda reduzido de estudos, a metacognição desponta como um campo promissor para compreender a autorregulação, a autonomia e a reflexão crítica. Evidenciam-se o papel central do professor na mediação das estratégias metacognitivas e a necessidade de inserir a metacognição na formação inicial e continuada. Também são destacadas contribuições para uma educação inclusiva e para o desenvolvimento de estratégias de ensino metacognitivas. Entre as limitações, observam-se a predominância de estudos nas áreas de Física e Química, a fragmentação conceitual e a ausência de articulação teórica. Recomenda-se, como perspectiva futura, o aprofundamento teórico-metodológico da metacognição em diferentes áreas do conhecimento e sua efetiva integração ao currículo escolar.

title: Effects of Cognitive Orientation to Daily Occupational Performance (CO-OP) Intervention on Executive Functioning for Activities of Daily Living in Patients With Stroke: A Randomized Controlled Trial
container-title: Hong Kong Journal of Occupational Therapy
afd2b27678e2bde310ffb6bc5e17f94025742550.abstract: Objective This study aimed to examine the effects of the Cognitive Orientation to Daily Occupational Performance (CO-OP) intervention on executive functioning to promote the performance of activities of daily living in patients with stroke using a randomized controlled trial. Methods Thirty-eight patients with stroke who met the inclusion criteria were randomly assigned to either an experimental (n = 19) or a control (n = 19) group using a computer-generated randomization program. The experimental group received the CO-OP intervention, whereas the control group received conventional occupational therapy. Both interventions were delivered over 12 sessions, 5 times per week, with each session lasting 60 min. The Executive Function Performance Test - Korean version, Canadian Occupational Performance Measure, Performance Quality Rating Scale, Korean version of the Modified Barthel index, and Korean version of the Instrumental Activities of Daily Living Scale were administered for pre- and post-intervention assessments. Results Both groups showed significant improvements in executive function, occupational performance, and activities of daily living following the interventions (p < .001). However, when comparing the magnitude of change between the two groups, the experimental group demonstrated significantly greater improvements across all measures (p < .05, p < .01, p < .001). These findings indicate that the CO-OP intervention led to statistically greater enhancement than conventional occupational therapy. Conclusion This study provides evidence that the CO-OP approach in occupational therapy can effectively improve executive function, occupational performance, and activities of daily living in patients with stroke. Therefore, the CO-OP intervention, as a client-centered and evidence-based approach, may be a valuable therapeutic method in future clinical practice.

title: Binding Memory and Relational Mechanisms: The Central Role of Binding in Fluid Intelligence
55e35680ba87ebfb069475a3637c021c5a31c914.abstract: Fluid intelligence (Gf) and working memory (WM) are strongly correlated, with the binding hypothesis suggesting that this relationship is driven by the capacity to bind content to context. However, it remains unclear how various binding functions overlap and relate to Gf. This study investigates the extent of overlap between five binding functions (item-to-location binding, item-to-item binding, relational integration, relation processing, and perceptual feature binding) and their relationship with Gf. A sample of 174 young adults completed three visuospatial variants of tasks measuring these five binding functions alongside three Gf tasks. Data were analyzed using structural equation modeling and latent network analysis to evaluate shared and unique variances. Results indicated significant overlap among the binding functions, with item-to-location and item-to-item binding best modeled as a single latent variable termed binding memory. The shared variance among binding memory and the remaining binding functions was represented by a higher-order, process-general latent factor labeled Binding which was found to be statistically isomorphic with Gf. Latent network analysis further revealed that binding memory, relational integration, and relation processing each exhibited unique, direct relationships with Gf, whereas perceptual feature binding related to Gf only indirectly. These findings indicate that an overarching, domain-general ability to form and utilize bindings in a goal-directed manner is deeply intertwined with Gf, supporting theories emphasizing binding and relational mechanisms in Gf.

title: A Topology of the Psilocybin Experience Reveals Cognitive-Emotional Drivers, Unitive State Divergence, and Psychometric Feature Cancellation
9b60cc12e9552e83a617dffe97ef9f5802799faa.abstract: Background: Traditional psychometrics collapse rich psychedelic experiences into aggregate composite scores, masking the structural dynamics that drive therapeutic outcomes.Methods: An unsupervised Natural Language Processing framework mapped a substance-specific corpus of psilocybin narrative reports (n = 5,498; ~5.19M tokens) into a continuous seven-dimensional thematic state space, using semantic embeddings and cluster-level differential TF-IDF feature extraction. Spatial topology metrics, multivariable logistic regression, and substructure analyses characterized its organization, dynamics, and functional roles.Results: The resulting topology revealed four functional roles across the continuous state space: modulators (e.g., visual patterns, environment, body-object features), a threshold marker (temporal distortion), a peak state (ego dissolution), and a distributed state (unity). Cognitive-emotional processing emerged as the dominant driver of transitions across this topology, promoting internally-oriented states while suppressing environmental tracking. Within unity, this topology resolves into two mutually inhibitory pathways: internal cognitive-temporal transcendence and external somatosensory-environmental merging. Because legacy composite scales like the MEQ30 sum across these opposing channels, feature cancellation masks divergent phenomenological trajectories behind identical composite scores.Conclusions: Psilocybin phenomenology organizes into a structured, cognitive-emotionally anchored topology rather than unconstrained variation. Resolving unity into opposing pathways exposes a mechanism of feature cancellation in legacy aggregate psychometrics, whereas the global state-space architecture aligns with neuroimaging evidence of network reorganization and provides a quantitative framework for optimizing dose, set-and-setting, and targeted clinical protocols.

title: When Effort Invigorates:  Instrumental Effort History Increases Cue-Evoked Response Vigour While Preserving Outcome-Specific Transfer
1f2e605b92de5ffc0aeed184a74be588dc5f62b1.abstract: Environmental cues can influence action through outcome-related information learned elsewhere, but whether features of the instrumental acquisition history associated with those outcomes remain behaviourally relevant when the outcomes are later predicted by Pavlovian cues is unknown. Across two experiments, one conducted in the laboratory (N = 54) and one online (N = 67), we separated instrumental acquisition under low- and high-effort response requirements from Pavlovian cue learning. Participants first learned that different actions produced outcomes under relatively low or high effort requirements and separately learned cues predicting those same outcomes. Pavlovian-to-instrumental transfer (PIT) was then tested under extinction, with neither outcomes nor response requirements present. In both experiments, reward-predictive cues elicited greater response vigour than a control cue. Critically, cues predicting outcomes previously obtained under high-effort response requirements elicited greater responding than cues predicting outcomes obtained under low-effort requirements. Specific PIT was robust under both acquisition conditions, with cues selectively promoting actions associated with their predicted outcomes. There was also suggestive evidence that high-effort acquisition amplified the magnitude of specific PIT, but this modulation was not consistently supported across experiments or statistical approaches. No corresponding effect emerged for initial outcome-congruent action selection. Overall, response vigour was modulated by instrumental effort history more consistently than outcome-specific action selection, indicating that features of prior effortful instrumental experience can remain behaviourally relevant when the associated outcomes are later predicted by separately learned Pavlovian cues.

title: White Matter Integrity and Default Mode Network Disruption in Cognitive Impairment: A Multimodal Imaging Study From the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative
container-title: Med Research
a4e52b17e16ec0af272ebf108d159ba77f334a49.abstract: ABSTRACT Cognitive impairment involves large‐scale brain systems, but the relation between white matter microstructure and default mode network (DMN) organization remains unclear in clinically heterogeneous populations. In this secondary analysis of Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative data, we examined structural abnormalities, DMN organization, and cognition. The structural analysis included 1431 classified participants with diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) data. After deduplication, the multimodal source merge yielded 1452 unique participant‐visits from 905 participants. Primary analyses used participant‐level random‐intercept models adjusted for scan age, sex, education, and diagnosis, alongside first‐available‐visit HC3‐robust sensitivity analyses. Global fractional anisotropy (FA), DMN within‐network connectivity, DMN segregation, and Mini‐Mental State Examination (MMSE) scores were lower in Alzheimer's disease than in cognitively normal participants. Global FA was positively associated with DMN within‐network connectivity in the primary model (standardized beta = 0.080, 95% confidence interval [] 0.022 to 0.137, p = 0.006; q = 0.019). The prespecified tract analysis identified FDR‐supported associations for splenial, callosal, and cingulate‐cingulum FA. The global association attenuated after scanner‐platform adjustment (beta = 0.052, 95% CI −0.007 to 0.112, p = 0.082), quantifying an important multicenter limitation. DMN within‐network connectivity was not independently associated with MMSE in the primary mixed model (beta = 0.035, 95% CI −0.003 to 0.073, p = 0.071). In a same‐visit amyloid/tau subset (216 observations, 180 participants), diagnosis‐adjusted analyses showed no non‐monotonic imaging pattern. In this audited multimodal cohort, we identified diagnosis‐related group differences and a positive participant‐level structure–function association between white matter integrity and DMN organization, underscored by anatomically heterogeneous tract‐level effects. Acknowledging cross‐sectional and scanner‐variance constraints, these findings provide a hypothesis‐generating basis for future investigations into coupled structural‐functional network disruptions across the Alzheimer's continuum.

title: The impact of social exclusion on social and non-social working memory
6c43cf4aec1248cdf00f4278b32ad880cfa38f76.abstract: Humans rely on social-cognitive processes, such as social working memory, to maintain and manipulate information about social relationships. While social and self-relevant information is often prioritised over non-social information, it remains unclear whether these processes are sensitive to social exclusion. Therefore, this preregistered study investigated whether social exclusion influences working memory for social and non-social information. A total of 125 participants (age: M = 37.4 years, SD = 13.8; 49.6% female) first completed Cyberball, an online task inducing feelings of social inclusion or exclusion, followed by the Network Memory Task assessing memory for social (e.g., friendship) and non-social (e.g., flight paths) networks.Consistent with previous findings, we found that social, relative to non-social information was processed faster in working memory. We also replicated a self-reference effect, whereby self-relevant information was remembered more accurately and processed more quickly than non-self-relevant social and non-social information. Contrary to our hypotheses, social exclusion did not directly impact working memory performance. However, exploratory analyses showed that higher rejection sensitivity was associated with slower reaction times across all conditions, following exclusion. Overall, our results suggest that the direct effects of social exclusion on working are limited and potentially dependent on individual difference in rejection sensitivity.

title: <b>EFEITOS DA INTERVENÇÃO FISIOTERAPÊUTICA ASSOCIADA A ANÁLISE DO COMPORTAMENTO APLICADA NA FUNCIONALIDADE MOTORA E DESEMPENHO COGNITIVO EM CRIANÇA COM TRANSTORNO DO ESPECTRO AUTISTA: RELATO DE EXPERIÊNCIA</b>
EFFECTS OF PHYSIOTHERAPEUTIC INTERVENTION ASSOCIATED WITH APPLIED BEHAVIOR ANALYSIS ON MOTOR FUNCTIONALITY AND COGNITIVE PERFORMANCE IN A CHILD WITH AUTISM SPECTRUM DISORDER: AN EXPERIENCE REPORT
container-title: Revista Ibero-Americana de Humanidades, Ciências e Educação
1da29743303706819e0f4f332a5c692a0e1d3acf.abstract: O objetivo deste estudo foi analisar a intervenção fisioterapêutica associada a Análise do Comportamento Aplicada (ABA) na funcionalidade motora e desempenho cognitivo em crianças com Transtorno do Espectro Autista (TEA), por meio de um relato de experiência. Trata-se de um estudo descritivo, de abordagem qualitativa, caracterizado como relato de experiência, realizado com uma criança do sexo masculino, de 6 anos, diagnosticada com TEA. A intervenção fisioterapêutica associada à ABA foi realizada semanalmente, utilizando atividades lúdicas, estímulos sensoriais, treino de coordenação motora, atividades de autocuidado, interação social, sequência lógica e reforço positivo. Foram consideradas as observações realizadas antes e após as intervenções, com enfoque nos aspectos motores, cognitivos, comportamentais e funcionais. Após as intervenções, observaram-se melhorias na comunicação verbal, contato visual, expressão de afetividade, interação, redução da agitação e maior autonomia nas atividades de vida diária, incluindo uso do banheiro, higiene pessoal e vestuário. Conclui-se que a associação entre fisioterapia e ABA apresentou resultados positivos no desenvolvimento funcional, motor, cognitivo e comportamental da criança, favorecendo maior autonomia. Entretanto, por se tratar de um relato de experiência com curto período de acompanhamento, os resultados devem ser interpretados com cautela.

title: DA AUDIÇÃO À MEMÓRIA: UMA REVISÃO INTEGRATIVA DA LITERATURA SOBRE A INTEGRAÇÃO NEUROFISIOLÓGICA DA PERCEPÇÃO E DA APRENDIZAGEM
FROM HEARING TO MEMORY: AN INTEGRATIVE LITERATURE REVIEW ON THE NEUROPHYSIOLOGICAL INTEGRATION OF PERCEPTION AND LEARNING
DE LA AUDICIÓN A LA MEMORIA: UNA REVISIÓN INTEGRADORA DE LA LITERATURA SOBRE LA INTEGRACIÓN NEUROFISIOLÓGICA DE LA PERCEPCIÓN Y EL APRENDIZAJE
container-title: Revista Ibero-Americana de Humanidades, Ciências e Educação
fb13fb452f3853552027e1194d01b34ab29abf31.abstract: Este artigo teve como objetivo analisar as evidências científicas sobre a integração neurofisiológica entre a percepção auditiva, a atenção e os processos de aprendizagem e memória em seres humanos. Trata-se de uma revisão integrativa da literatura, com análise descritiva e narrativa, realizada na PubMed e na Biblioteca Virtual em Saúde (BVS), considerando publicações entre 2016 e 2026. Os resultados sugerem que a percepção auditiva se articula com redes neurais envolvidas na atenção, na avaliação emocional e na memória. O treinamento e as experiências auditivas e multissensoriais foram associados a alterações no processamento neural e a melhorias em habilidades perceptivas e cognitivas específicas. Destacaram-se a aprendizagem perceptiva, a melhora da compreensão da fala no ruído e da memória de trabalho, a redução do esforço de escuta e a maior diferenciação neural entre fala atendida e não atendida em condições específicas. Conclui-se que o processamento auditivo participa ativamente da aprendizagem e de processos relacionados à memória. Entretanto, o número reduzido de estudos e a diversidade de populações, tarefas e delineamentos limitam a generalização dos achados para o desempenho cognitivo global e a retenção de informações.

title: Effects of Combined Blood Flow Restriction and Inter‐Effort Recovery Hypoxia On Repeated‐Sprint Performance And Physiological Responses: A Randomized And Single‐Blinded Crossover Trial
container-title: European Journal of Sport Science
e3949e19c7e51ee30ccec51855062e0086d020cc.abstract: ABSTRACT We investigated the acute effects of local and/or systemic hypoxia on performance and psycho‐physiological responses during repeated cycle sprints. Eleven physically active young adults (six men, five women) performed four sessions on separate days, each involving three sets of five 5‐s all‐out efforts on a cycle ergometer (25 seconds rest between efforts and 5 minutes rest between sets). Sessions were conducted under four conditions, combining blood flow restriction [BFR; 45% of arterial occlusion pressure (AOP)] or control (CON; 5% of AOP) applied bilaterally to the legs during sprints, with inter‐effort recovery hypoxia [IEH; inspired oxygen fraction (FiO 2 ) = 13.5%] or normoxia (NOR; FiO 2 = 20.9%). Power output decreased across sprints and heart rate increased over sets, with no differences between conditions (Δ = −9.18%). IEH resulted in lower peripheral oxygen saturation (Δ = −8.0%) but higher oxygen uptake (Δ = 6.7 mL·kg −1 min −1 ) and minute ventilation (Δ = 6.1 L·kg −1 min −1 ), compared to normoxic conditions. Blood lactate concentration increased (Δ = 6.5 mM) post‐session similarly across all conditions. Vastus lateralis muscle oxygenation during sprints and inter‐set recovery was comparable across conditions, although the mean tissue saturation index during inter‐set recovery was lower in BFR + IEH versus CON + NOR conditions (Δ = −4.0%). Ratings of perceived exertion (Δ = 22.5%), limb discomfort (Δ = 34.2%), and breathing difficulty (Δ = 43.7%) increased throughout the sets, independently of conditions. Despite physiological and perceptual adjustments across sprint repetitions, neither BFR during sprints nor systemic hypoxia during recovery altered mechanical output in physically active individuals.

title: Students’ Interaction Patterns with ChatGPT in Solving Image-Based Mathematics Problems
container-title: Kognitif: Jurnal Riset HOTS Pendidikan Matematika
1e7d031da7ac7501457d2c369b869f6408837525.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) tools such as ChatGPT are increasingly used by students to obtain explanations and solutions to mathematics problems. However, access to answers does not necessarily mean that students examine the underlying reasoning. This study aimed to describe students’ interaction patterns with ChatGPT when solving image-based mathematics problems, variations in these patterns across two problems, and how students responded to, sought clarification of, or challenged ChatGPT-generated solutions. A qualitative descriptive design was employed. The participants were Grade 9 students of one intact class (total sampling), and the records of 31 students who worked on two image-based problems, concerning the area of a trapezoidal footpath and the painted area of a photo frame, were analyzed. The primary data consisted of student–ChatGPT conversation transcripts exported from shared conversation links. The transcripts were analyzed descriptively and qualitatively using six predefined interaction patterns: requesting a solution and then ending the interaction; seeking clarification; requesting a re-explanation; checking an answer or testing a method; following a solution step by step; and connecting or redirecting the interaction. The unit of analysis was the student–problem episode, and overlapping codes were permitted. The findings indicate that students did more than request answers. Some asked for the rationale behind a solution step, proposed strategies for confirmation, requested further explanations, responded to practice questions posed by ChatGPT, and made connections between the two problems. Two students questioned the complexity or necessity of ChatGPT’s chosen method. Differences between the problems were primarily reflected in the content of students’ questions. These findings are descriptive and are not intended to establish the prevalence of interaction patterns, learning outcomes, or causal relationships. The findings suggest a need for task design and teacher guidance that encourage students to verify and evaluate AI-generated solutions.

title: Analysis of driver memory with V2X-enabled weighted speed in car-following traffic flow model
container-title: International Journal of Modern Physics C
626c4881749e6b456220965047ff3ec686671bf8.abstract: In connected vehicle environments, drivers no longer rely solely on their own perception of the vehicle ahead, Vehicle-to-Everything (V2X) communication now allows them to access real-time weighted speed information from surrounding traffic, while their car-following decisions are still influenced by recollection of past driving states, referred to here as driver memory. This study explores how these two factors, cognitive memory and V2X-based weighted speed awareness, jointly govern car-following dynamics by extending the classical Full Velocity Difference (FVD) model to include both effects explicitly. Through linear stability analysis, the stability criterion of the proposed model is derived and the results show that the combined inclusion of memory and weighted speed information enlarges the stable traffic flow region well beyond what is achieved by the conventional FVD model. Near the neutral stability boundary, a nonlinear analysis based on the reductive perturbation approach is used to derive the modified Korteweg–de Vries (mKdV) equation, whose kink–antikink soliton solution captures the density wave behavior that develops close to this critical threshold. The energy consumption is calculated to check how much memory and V2X information affect traffic disturbances. The simulation results agree with the analytical results, confirming that the proposed model exhibits markedly reduced stop-and-go oscillations and lower energy dissipation than earlier models.

title: Biomimicry-informed deconstruction of the cognitive system for Sino–Western hybrid architecture: A case study of Lushan UNESCO Global Geopark
container-title: Journal of Chinese Architecture and Urbanism
684f91e2a665751948f6036a29544ba2da2a4f40.abstract: Sino&ndash;Western hybrid architecture serves as a medium for cross-cultural exchange; however, its preservation faces two major challenges: unclear conservation standards and differing perceptions of cultural value. The hybrid architectural forms at Lushan developed in response to local terrain and climate, but the difficulty in defining authenticity for such buildings complicates conservation efforts. This study examines the villa cluster in Guling town, Lushan, employing biomimicry not as a design methodology but as an analytical framework to evaluate hybrid heritage through characteristics of environmental adaptation. Based on a literature review, field surveys of 45 villas, and interviews with 15 participants, including residents, heritage managers, and scholars, the study analyzes environmental adaptation, hybrid architectural styles, typological classification, and preservation challenges. The investigation reveals that, despite differing cultural origins, both Chinese and Western building traditions in Guling town developed similar responses to mountainous conditions, suggesting that environmental adaptation provides common ground for heritage evaluation that transcends cultural boundaries. Accordingly, a four-dimensional preservation framework is proposed that integrates function and culture, coordinates ecology and heritage, links landscape and narrative, and incorporates community participation. The framework addresses the methodological challenge of evaluating buildings rooted in multiple cultural traditions without privileging either lineage. Limitations of the study include its qualitative approach and focus on a single site. Nevertheless, the findings offer insights for conserving comparable hybrid architecture in other mountainous areas and point toward future research on developing quantitative indicators of environmental adaptation.

title: Telerehabilitation with or Without Transcranial Direct Current Stimulation in Older Stroke Survivors with Cognitive Impairment: A Three-Arm Randomised Trial
a918497f570bd3d340b0e51f82c93dbd50e50b18.abstract: Background/Objectives: Evidence on telerehabilitation combined with transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) in older stroke survivors with cognitive impairment remains limited. This study compared Brunnstrom-based telerehabilitation (TRB), TRB plus tDCS, and a conventional physiotherapy intervention (CON). Methods: In this single-centre, assessor-blinded randomised trial, 87 participants were allocated equally to three eight-week programmes. Pain, motor recovery, balance, mobility and cognition were assessed at baseline and weeks 4 and 8. Repeated-measures analyses included 83 participants and adjusted for education, hypertension and diabetes. Results: Group-by-time effects were significant for Timed Up and Go (TUG; p < 0.001), Brunnstrom hand stage (p = 0.008) and lower-limb stage (p = 0.027). Only the TUG effect remained significant after accounting for the nine outcomes assessed. TUG improvement was greater with TRB plus tDCS than with TRB by 2.74 seconds (95% CI 1.32-4.17) and CON by 2.51 seconds (1.19-3.83). At week 8, hand-stage scores favoured the combined intervention over both comparators. Pain scores were lower than with TRB at weeks 4 and 8, but pain trajectories did not differ significantly. The Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) group-by-time effect was not significant (p = 0.880). Conclusions: Adding tDCS to telerehabilitation produced greater improvements in TUG performance than telerehabilitation alone or the conventional physiotherapy intervention over eight weeks. This mobility benefit remained statistically significant after accounting for the nine outcomes assessed. Telerehabilitation alone and conventional physiotherapy showed improvements in hand recovery, mobility and cognitive scores, without significant differences in their changes. No additional cognitive benefit from tDCS was demonstrated.

title: EvoMemState: Evolving Memory State for Personal Agents
af7da94a655da594f25d339f2cf31421017400c9.abstract: Long-term memory enables large language model (LLM) agents to provide continuous personalized assistance by retaining user information across interactions. Existing systems support this process through fact extraction, organization, updating, and retrieval, but largely maintain memories as independent facts. This fact-centric paradigm may overlook how new facts update, constrain, or conflict with earlier ones, while leaving their applicability, role, and priority for the current request implicit. In this paper, we introduce EvoMemState, a state-centric framework that augments persistent facts with two complementary states: Relational States that capture how facts remain valid and relate to one another as memory evolves, and a Reasoning State that determines how these facts should be applied to the current request. Specifically, EvoMemState consists of three key components: (i) Ontology-Guided Memory State Induction extracts Persistent Facts and constructs Relational States that maintain their validity, scope, and evolving relations. (ii) RL-Based State Evolution internalizes memory-use experience into a policy through reinforcement learning to generate a request-specific Reasoning State. (iii) State-Aware Reasoning then combines the relevant facts with their Relational States and the generated Reasoning State to guide the personal agent. Extensive experiments on long-term dialogue and memory-use benchmarks demonstrate consistent improvements over existing memory systems in retrieval completeness and memory-grounded response accuracy. Our code and implementation details are available at https://github.com/XMUDeepLIT/EvoMemState.git.

title: Generative AI and Cognitive Processes in Education: A Narrative Review and Conceptual Framework
cf58154945110f40f63a0a14c08437dc34219809.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is increasingly being integrated into educational practices, transforming how students access information, develop ideas, and carry out cognitive tasks. While GenAI offers opportunities to foster critical thinking and creativity, its use raises concerns regarding "cognitive offloading"—the delegation of reasoning processes that are fundamental to learning. This study presents a review based on 108 documents from Scopus and Web of Science, which allowed for an examination of the relationships between GenAI, critical thinking, creativity, and cognitive offloading, as well as their pedagogical and institutional implications. The evidence analyzed suggests that GenAI can improve immediate task performance, facilitate idea generation, and support content development. However, these benefits do not necessarily translate into autonomous learning or greater creative originality. Outcomes appear to depend on students' prior knowledge, their AI literacy, task design, metacognitive regulation, and the nature and timing of pedagogical support. Based on this review, an AI-Mediated Cognitive Infrastructure Framework (AMCIF) is proposed, which links GenAI usage patterns with cognitive processes, educational practices, and institutional conditions. This framework distinguishes between forms of assistance that promote cognitive engagement and those that might replace the mental activity necessary for learning, emphasizing the essential role of instructor mediation, source verification, reflective practices, and process-oriented assessment. The AMCIF provides a conceptual foundation for analyzing how to integrate GenAI into educational settings while preserving critical judgment, creativity, and the capacity for independent reasoning. The proposed relationships require rigorous empirical validation.

title: The Guarded Memory Plane: Agentic Memory for Long-Horizon Workflows
3554403eb0f6f6a6370ccdb9f4b49063ea67a802.abstract: Agent platforms routinely combine three different capabilities: durable execution state, retrieval over a document corpus, and memory. On a LangGraph-based platform, the checkpointer provides only the first. It saves a full state snapshot at each step and supports thread isolation, resume, replay, and fork. That makes it working memory with durability, scoped to a single thread. The cross-thread store beside it has no provenance, no validity window, no conflict resolution, and no handling rules for personal data. This report describes what to build on top. It separates three meanings of “memory tier” that the literature uses interchangeably: content type, access locality, and representation format. Treating them as one idea leads to poor architecture, because only the last one decides whether a stored fact can still be inspected, redacted, or deleted. The report then specifies the memory lifecycle as a guarded plane. Typed stores sit behind a write guard, and every retrieval passes through a read guard. Every record carries provenance and bi-temporal validity. Retention is bounded and scored by utility, supersession is deterministic, and retrieval is hybrid and iterative. On tiering, the report follows the published evidence. A study of twelve memory systems across five workloads finds no dominant architecture. A search policy over raw, uncompressed history also outperforms compression-based tiering on the benchmark that tiered systems cite as their own evidence. The recommendation is to start flat and add tiering only as a measured, A/B-tested decision with an explicit trigger condition. The report applies the same approach to four failure modes: context rot, lossy-summarization drift, contextual-integrity violations that grow with usage, and memory poisoning. Poisoning is a separate risk class, because a written record becomes a privileged input on the next turn and input guardrails never see it. The report closes with a build sequence ordered by retrofit cost and a measurement plan.

title: Temporal Variability in Brain Connectivity for Estimating Two-Year Clinical Severity in Mild Cognitive Impairment
4954e585e3c4e09f82c4ef216e839ca482575ee0.abstract: Abstract Resting-state functional MRI measures coordinated activity across brain networks and may reveal early changes relevant to cognitive decline. Conventional ‘static’ functional connectivity analyses often compute time-series correlations across an entire scan, missing informative fluctuations over shorter timescales. We investigated whether these fluctuations, in fMRI scans collected at baseline, improve estimation of clinical severity two years later in mild cognitive impairment (MCI). In 48 ADNI participants with MCI, we summarized temporal variability using the standard deviation of windowed correlations between 21 pairs of brain networks. Using repeated nested cross-validation, the mean absolute error in predicting follow-up Clinical Dementia Rating Sum of Boxes (CDR-SB) was 1.62 points with clinical covariates alone, 1.66 after adding static connectivity, and 1.51 after adding connectivity variability. With additional motion covariates, the corresponding errors were 1.70, 1.73, and 1.59. Connectivity variability outperformed both conventional models in all three cross-validation repetitions, while randomized signals preserving the complete cross-spectrum did not reproduce the improvement. Perhaps surprisingly though, most of the gain occurred in participants without subsequent clinical worsening, and results were sensitive to the choice of temporal windows. These preliminary findings suggest that compact measures of connectivity variability may capture clinically relevant information beyond conventional measures of ‘static’ functional connectivity, motivating larger studies to evaluate their value for predicting future cognitive impairment.

title: Simple, static, spiking nonlinearities can account for seemingly complex interactions between visual, motor and cognitive variables in the visual cortex.
15cba32bdea2e4f4fe3f6878c9b7255496a39db2.abstract: Neural activity in the visual cortex is driven by the stimulus and modulated by multiple task-related variables, including spatial attention, eye movements, and perceptual decisions. These multiple influences are each typically described as nonlinear interactions such as gain or normalization, raising the question of how these diverse signals can be combined through cellular or circuit mechanisms. Here we address this problem by examining neuronal responses in macaque visual areas V2 and V3 during a visual discrimination task that dissociates spatial attention from motor planning and microsaccadic eye movements. Using a statistical modeling framework, we show that attentional, microsaccade-related, and choice-related influences on neural activity are best explained by a simple additive stimulus-independent input modulation, which manifests as a gain via a spiking nonlinearity. In addition to explaining how interactions between variables might be accomplished mechanistically, this framework also resolves a controversy about the relationship between microsaccades and spatial attention. We find that neither microsaccade direction nor microsaccade-related neural activity accounts for attentional modulation, although these variables are often correlated, leading to apparent interactions. Thus, visual cortex can integrate sensory, motor-related, and cognitive signals through a parsimonious mechanism that preserves stable stimulus representations while supporting flexible, context-dependent modulation.

title: Identifying Structural Drivers of Crime Using Statistical Inference and Machine Learning Models
container-title: Journal of Computational and Cognitive Engineering
9b7110cfa1634650d99319f2c4dbd3021c49494e.abstract: This study identifies structural socio-economic correlates of crime investigation activity in Kazakhstan and examines how interpretable composite indicators relate to it. The dependent variable is the annual volume of pre-trial investigations recorded in the Unified Register of Pre-Trial Investigations over 2015–2025. It is modeled against 70 explanatory factors that span socio-economic, demographic, institutional, legal, healthcare, education, agriculture, and digitalization domains. The analysis combines Pearson correlation, one-way analysis of variance, simple and multivariate linear regression, and regularized ensemble machine learning (Gradient Boosting, Random Forest, Ridge, Support Vector Machine). A category-based dimensionality reduction then aggregates the 70 factors into 8, and subsequently 10, standardized composite indices. Because only about 10 aggregated annual observations are available, findings are reported in associational rather than causal terms. The strongly negative cross-validated R2 of the ensemble models is flagged as direct evidence of overfitting in this small-n, high-dimensional setting. Digitalization, education, poverty, and healthcare indicators emerge as the leading correlates of crime. A parsimonious regression on the composite indices accounts for 97.6% of insample crime variance while improving interpretability and stability. Interpretable index-based models therefore appear better suited than high-capacity learners for policy-relevant inference in this setting. title: ENHANCING MANAGEMENT STUDENTS' COMPETENCIES IN PITCHING: AUTHENTIC ASSESSMENT WITH CHATGPT AND POWERPOINT MEDIA
container-title: EDUPEDIA
d4a6c1101bbfd16bc8c204fcfd9a7791985928a6.abstract: Authentic assessment is crucial in Human Capital Management (HCM) education to develop student competencies to meet industry demands. This study explores the integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools, specifically ChatGPT, and PowerPoint presentations into authentic assessments to enhance students' pitching competencies. This study employed a descriptive quantitative approach through a 4-point Likert-scale questionnaire distributed to 102 management students. The results showed that ChatGPT integration was highly effective in helping students brainstorm ideas (Mean 3.52), while PowerPoint presentations significantly increased motivation and visual engagement during presentations (Mean 3.31). The results of the data analysis showed consistent positive perceptions across all variables, with the following mean values: pitching competence (Mean = 3.29; SD = 0.70), authentic assessment (Mean = 3.18; SD = 0.74), use of ChatGPT (Mean = 3.28; SD = 0.85), and use of PowerPoint media (Mean = 3.31; SD = 0.79). These findings indicate that the integration of AI and presentation media in authentic assessment is effective in strengthening students' work readiness, although it still requires pedagogical guidance to optimize the use of technology logically and ethically.

title: Experiment on Cognitive Ability, Behavioural Preferences and Improved Seed Technology Adoption
container-title: Australian Journal of Agricultural and Resource Economics
a9f942eeddf720d2b27c1a3c5de186c0f5e59c70.abstract: ABSTRACT Seeds are the ‘chips’ of agriculture; the use and promotion of improved seeds are crucial for ensuring food security. This study employs Rehmannia glutinosa as a case study and conducts a joint measurement experiment on farmers' risk and time preferences in rural China. This study aimed to assess the contribution of cognitive ability to farmers' adoption of agricultural technology and to identify potential underlying channels. The study builds upon and extends prior research on the determinants of farmers' adoption of agricultural technologies. The results indicate that higher cognitive ability increases the likelihood of adopting improved seed technology. Farmers with greater cognitive ability exhibit lower risk aversion and greater patience, making them more likely to adopt such innovations. Overall, this study has substantial practical implications for advancing the dissemination of improved agricultural seeds.

title: How Is Cognitive Behavioural Therapy for Insomnia Provided in Randomized Controlled Trials? A Scoping Review
container-title: Journal of Sleep Research
8278b19c51e1bdf620ba7bc0a4135944539642b5.abstract: ABSTRACT Cognitive behavioural therapy (CBT) in general has demonstrated efficacy in treating insomnia, but there is some variation in the content of CBT for insomnia (CBT‐I) across studies. We therefore conducted a scoping review of randomized controlled trials on CBT‐I to determine how CBT‐I is usually provided in randomized controlled trials. This knowledge is essential for writing evidence‐based treatment guidelines and ensuring that clinical practice reflects interventions with proven effectiveness. The search was performed in Pubmed, Embase and Web of Science. A total of 514 publications were included. Excluding the secondary analyses, this left 375 unique randomized controlled trials on CBT‐I. A total of 197 focused on comorbid insomnia. The most frequently reported components were stimulus control (86.93%), time‐in‐bed restriction (84.53%), cognitive therapy (83.20%) and sleep hygiene (78.13%). In a few randomized controlled trials, CBT‐I did not include its three core components time‐in‐bed restriction, stimulus control and cognitive therapy. The reasons for omitting one of these components were rarely reported. The intervention is generally delivered in six sessions, which is more than the previously identified ideal amount of four sessions. When delivered individually, sessions typically lasted 60 min. However, in a group format, they usually lasted 90 min and involved four to six patients. CBT‐I was usually delivered in person and by a psychologist. Guidelines on the report of CBT‐I in RCTs were formulated.

title: Directional brain-heart interaction during cognitive workload: a permutation conditional mutual information approach
container-title: Frontiers in Network Physiology
42f50f9940b3f6b85d6fec876fcad3c5b67364ed.abstract: The functional interaction between the central nervous system and autonomic cardiovascular regulation, commonly referred to as Brain-Heart Interaction (BHI), has gained increasing attention in neurology and psychology through the joint analysis of Electroencephalography (EEG) and Electrocardiography (ECG) signals. However, the nonlinear and time-varying nature of EEG and ECG signals requires approaches that can capture directional interactions between physiological systems. In this study, we investigated the use of Permutation Conditional Mutual Information (PCMI) for the characterization of directional BHI. First, the method was evaluated on synthetically generated coupled time series to assess its ability to detect the dominant direction of interaction. Next, PCMI was applied to simultaneous EEG and ECG recordings acquired during baseline and mental arithmetic tasks from a cohort of 36 subjects. The results show that BHI complexity increases during mental arithmetic tasks compared with baseline, supporting the role of cognitive workload in modulating brain–heart dynamics. These changes primarily involved anterior and posterior scalp regions, and affected both vagal- and sympathovagal-related HRV components. These findings demonstrate that PCMI provides a framework for studying directional BHI during cognitive tasks, and highlight its potential translational value for investigating broader brain–body interactions.

title: Offloading Thoughts to the Bots: How Generative AI Access Influences Cognitive Reflection
container-title: Proceedings of the Human Factors and Ergonomics Society Annual Meeting
428828c5eaafe30a707ba6e05b660cb692fab1dc.abstract: Generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) systems are increasingly used to support reasoning and decision-making, raising questions about how AI influences reflective cognition and trust. This study examined how AI pedigree and reliability influenced cognitive reflection performance, cognitive load, trust, and performance overestimation during a verbal Cognitive Reflection Test (CRT-V). Participants ( N = 148) were assigned to a no-AI control condition, a low-pedigree AI condition, or a high-pedigree AI condition. Participants in the high-pedigree AI condition demonstrated significantly greater trust and CRT performance than participants in both other conditions while also exhibiting lower performance overestimation. AI access did not significantly reduce perceived cognitive load, although greater cognitive load predicted poorer CRT performance overall. Importantly, trust interacted with AI condition such that greater trust predicted lower CRT performance in the low-pedigree AI condition but not in the high-pedigree AI condition. These findings support theories of calibrated reliance rather than indiscriminate cognitive offloading.

title: Cognitive and Structural Social Capital as Determinants of Oral Health‐Related Quality of Life in Older Brazilians
container-title: Gerodontology
ec707764284bda08e49d674aaaeeb0964e352907.abstract: ABSTRACT Objective To evaluate the association between the structural and cognitive dimensions of social capital and oral health‐related quality of life (OHRQoL) among older Brazilians. Methods This cross‐sectional study used baseline data from the Brazilian Longitudinal Study of Aging (ELSI‐Brazil), involving 9412 individuals aged 50 years or older. OHRQoL was assessed using the Oral Impacts on Daily Performance (OIDP) instrument. Social capital was evaluated in two dimensions: structural (volunteer work and participation in social groups) and cognitive (trust in the neighbourhood and perception of friendships). Adjusted Poisson regression models were used to estimate prevalence ratios (PR) and 95% confidence intervals (95% CI). Results The sample consisted predominantly of women (53.9%), participants of Black or Brown race/skin colour (56.0%), and individuals aged 60 years or older (52.4%); 73.1% had 8 years of education or less. Cognitive social capital was associated with oral health‐related quality of life (OHRQoL), whereas structural social capital was not. Participants who reported a lack of neighbourhood trust had a higher prevalence of oral impacts than those who trusted their neighbours (PR 1.21, 95% CI 1.13–1.29), and those without friends had a higher prevalence of oral impacts than those with friends (PR 1.13, 95% CI 1.04–1.22). Conclusion The cognitive dimension of social capital is associated with oral health‐related quality of life in older Brazilians. Public health strategies aimed at strengthening social trust and interpersonal networks can be effective in improving oral health outcomes in aging populations.

title: Systematic Review of the Convergence and Divergence of Cognitive Workload Measures
container-title: Proceedings of the Human Factors and Ergonomics Society Annual Meeting
3ea96d818974beaab0a77017f06588d37566605d.abstract: Cognitive workload, or the mental effort required to perform a task, has been used across many fields, yet variability in measurement and theoretical framing complicates the synthesis of findings. Within the same study, proxy measures for the term often find contradictory outcomes. This review examines empirical research on cognitive workload over the last 25 years in monitoring tasks. We categorize the incidence of multiple measures and measure types (i.e., subjective, performance-based, and physiological) and highlight patterns of convergence and divergence across studies. We also evaluate how the number and type of workload measures influence sensitivity and interpretability. We find that measure type has no detectable effect on convergence of measures, but that the number of measures increases the probability of convergence in our samples. Finally, we provide recommendations for future research to improve measurement consistency and enhance understanding of cognitive workload.

title: The plurality of metacognition: Historical origins and research traditions
7511bc85797e01e9d85446adb5f809b9607b9973.abstract: Metacognition is commonly defined as the monitoring and control of one’s own cognition, yet the term covers related phenomena that differ in their theoretical organisation, assessment, and application. This historically oriented narrative review examines how the convergence of cognitive, developmental, and educational research traditions produced this plurality. It reconstructs the construct’s empirical and theoretical antecedents in memory monitoring, children’s knowledge of cognition, and strategic regulation of learning, and compares influential accounts in terms of their explanatory aims, central components, and levels of analysis. The comparison shows that different traditions came to emphasise metacognitive knowledge, experiences, monitoring, regulatory activity, or the functional relation between object- and meta-level cognition. These differences are interpreted not as competing definitions of an identical phenomenon, but as reflecting the distinct problems and methods from which each account developed. The review argues that metacognition is best approached as a historically assembled family of related but partially non-interchangeable facets, without assuming either complete unity or fragmentation. This interpretation clarifies why indicators derived from different traditions often diverge, and why specifying the facet, function, and level of analysis intended by the term should be a condition for cumulative research across theory, measurement, and application.

title: Memory strength drives hybrid search efficiency
a86ae379b5bb2c18ed72e5a2b414b02624182e11.abstract: In hybrid search tasks, observers search for any of multiple targets held in memory (e.g., finding all of the ingredients for a recipe in the supermarket). Performance declines with the log of the number of memorized targets, a cost often attributed to a serial scan through memory. In standard models of recognition memory, however, holding more items in memory weakens the match strength between each memory representation and the corresponding visual item – independent of any serial search process. Here we propose an account of hybrid search based on memory strength, testing how memory strength affects hybrid search separately from memory set size. We found that strengthening memories through repetition and deeper encoding improved hybrid search at matched set sizes (Exp. 1). Taking advantage of NFL and NHL fans' pre-existing memory strength for sports logos (Exps. 2–3), we next found search was better for a larger set of familiar items (16 logos) than for a smaller set of unfamiliar items (12 logos), a reversal of the usual memory set-size effect. A standard global matching model (REM), with encoding parameters fit only to memory performance, not search data, reproduced these results and the canonical, approximately log-linear set-size cost in discriminability. Memory strength is thus a potentially strong determinant of hybrid search efficiency, with set-size effects not necessarily reflecting any serial memory search. Instead, models of recognition memory may provide a productive framework for the memory component of hybrid search.

title: Emerging Insights into Cognitive Control from Computational Models of Choice
ff045d6a1c9f83f5461d37cefa135970c5b1c781.abstract: Research into cognitive control has flourished over the last three decades across many areas of the psychological and neural sciences, but problems have recently emerged that raise foundational questions about what cognitive control is, how individual differences should be measured, and the validity of cognitive control as an explanation for variation in behavioral traits and clinical conditions. Here, we outline a novel perspective that is rooted in evidence accumulation models, formal mathematical models that explain how individuals make choices across many contexts. We review model-based work that distinguishes conflict-specific processes, which are selectively engaged to address goal-conflicting information, from task-general processes that facilitate goal-relevant responding irrespective of the presence of conflict. This review reveals an emerging consensus that task-general, but not conflict-specific, processes show validity as coherent individual difference dimensions. We then highlight the computationally-derived measure we call efficiency of evidence accumulation (EEA) that reflects the amplification of goal-relevant information across many tasks and contexts. EEA shows strong validity as a trait-like individual difference dimension, explains individual differences in performance in cognitive control tasks, and shows clear relevance to behavioral traits and clinical conditions in which cognitive control, as traditionally defined, is thought to be impaired. These findings help address multiple theoretical, methodological, and empirical challenges in the study of control processes in cognition, indicate that characterizing processes that enhance goal-relevant responding across contexts is a promising way forward, and suggest important ways in which theories of control’s role in behavioral outcomes could be revised.

title: The impact of meditation on cognitive flexibility: A critical review and the case for investigating True Self Meditation
a11071722c57e051b86def2f851f6e33a364bb17.abstract: Cognitive flexibility, the capacity to adapt thinking and behavior in response to changing environmental demands, is a critical component of psychological resilience and executive functioning. Meditation, particularly attention-based practices, has been associated with improvements in core cognitive processes, such as sustained attention, emotion regulation, and metacognitive awareness. Neuroimaging and behavioral evidence suggests that meditation activates neural networks involving the prefrontal cortex, anterior cingulate cortex, and limbic regions, which are crucial for set-shifting, adaptive learning, and executive control. While much of the current literature centers on Mindfulness Meditation, this focus has primarily served as a foundational framework for understanding meditation's cognitive effects. Other meditation modalities remain comparatively less explored in scientific literature, particularly in Western academic contexts. True Self Meditation (TSM), a practice rooted in systematic emotional and cognitive reflection, represents a compelling but under-recognized area for investigation. TSM involves the active identification and systematic discarding of maladaptive emotional images, promoting positive, resilient cognitive patterns. Existing research suggests that TSM may directly target cognitive flexibility mechanisms by engaging neural processes related to memory storage, emotional regulation, and executive functioning. Moreover, TSM-based interventions have demonstrated significant improvements in psychological well-being, social adjustment, and neurocognitive activation. While a substantial body of self-report and observational research-particularly within South Korea-has examined TSM's psychological outcomes, limited work has investigated its neurocognitive mechanisms or broader applicability across diverse populations. This review synthesizes existing research on TSM's potential impact on cognitive flexibility , focusing on neural mechanisms and methodological strengths and weaknesses in the literature. Addressing these gaps could offer valuable insight into how specific meditation practices differentially influence cognitive functioning. Future research should prioritize experimental, neuroimaging, and longitudinal approaches to clarify TSM's cognitive effects and potential as a targeted intervention. Expanding TSM's research will help capture the diversity of meditative practices and their unique contributions to cognitive and clinical outcomes.

title: Do thoughts actually drive symptoms? Testing cognitive theories of posttraumatic stress with natural language processing in daily diaries
013dab5d526bfe5c608c813a9a57c57c37a47039.abstract: Cognitive theories are among the leading conceptualizations of posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD). The core perspective shared by these theories is that distorted thinking (e.g., “no one can be trusted”) is involved in maintaining symptoms. However, the proximal mechanisms linking cognition and PTSD symptoms remains unclear due to two major methodological limitations: 1) lack of research on cognition-symptom dynamics at the daily level, and 2) reliance on self-reported thought distortions, which is a method ill-suited for capturing biases that people often do not have insight into or are outside of their awareness. The present study helps address these limitations in a sample of trauma-exposed patients (N=510) who completed daily video diaries and symptom ratings for 90 days (n=30,958 days). We used two natural language processing techniques to assess cognitive distortions from the diary transcripts: a lexica-based and large language model (LLM) approach. We then established the day-to-day sequencing of cognitive distortion and symptom fluctuations using dynamic structural equation models. Across the lexical and LLM models, distorted thinking did not predict worsening symptoms (bs=-.02–.01). Instead, worsening symptoms predicted more distorted thinking (bs=.03–.07). Also, symptoms and cognitive distortions tended to fluctuate together (bs=.08–.41). The current findings suggest that cognitive distortions do not precede PTSD symptoms as many theories have assumed, but may instead be a consequence or correlate of them. If replicated, our results could help refine cognitive and related models of PTSD.
