title: Developing and Validating a Measurement Scale to Assess Knowledge of Memory and Learning Processes Among Italian Teachers
b0856adc9c96df8c14ef242be41dba5fe63b4c93.abstract: Knowledge of memory and learning processes may inform teachers’ educational decisions. However, to our knowledge, no psychometrically validated instrument specifically assesses teachers’ procedural knowledge of these processes through realistic classroom scenarios.This Stage 1 Registered Report aims to develop and validate a scenario-based measure of Italian teachers’ procedural knowledge of memory and learning processes.Approximately 600 Italian teachers, from preschool to upper-secondary education, will be recruited through proportional stratified quota sampling based on sex, geographical area, and school level.Following two pilot studies and iterative revisions, 30 original items were retained and paired with conceptually matched items to create two intended parallel forms. All participants will complete the 60 multiple-choice items online. Exploratory and confirmatory factor analyses will be conducted separately for each form in independent subsamples. Measurement invariance across forms will be examined if corresponding factor structures are supported. Internal consistency will be estimated using Cronbach’s alpha. Mixed-effects logistic regression will examine associations between item-level accuracy and teaching experience, educational attainment, and, among teachers with tertiary qualifications, academic field.We expect interpretable, replicable factor structures and adequate internal consistency, with measurement invariance providing additional evidence of comparability across forms. Higher accuracy is tentatively expected with higher educational attainment, psycho-pedagogical qualifications, and fewer years of teaching experience.The study will provide initial evidence on the psychometric properties of the proposed measure. If the findings support its validity and reliability, the instrument could subsequently be used to identify teachers’ knowledge gaps and inform teacher education initiatives.

title: Globalising higher education in Africa through artificial intelligence: student acceptance of ChatGPT in an open distance and e-learning context
container-title: Frontiers in Education
999a53fd58f082433ef284dd92b05c0a0584f6a5.abstract: Introduction Higher education is increasingly globalised through digital technologies, Open Distance Learning, e-Learning, and emerging generative AI. In the absence of research examining the acceptance and use of ChatGPT by students in an Open Distance and e-Learning higher education setting, this study evaluated a UTAUT2 model comprising seven standard predictors and Personal Innovativeness, as well as moderating variables age, gender, work status, and year of study. Methods Data collected from 294 students at the largest distance education institution in Africa were analysed using partial least squares structural equation modelling. Results Four relationships with Behavioural Intention were significant, with Habit emerging as the strongest predictor, followed by Facilitating Conditions, Personal Innovativeness, and Performance Expectancy. Effort Expectancy was found to be negatively associated with Behavioural Intention. Social Influence and Hedonic Motivation were not significantly associated with Behavioural Intention. For Use Behaviour, Habit was once again the strongest predictor, followed by Facilitating Conditions, with Behavioural Intention negatively associated. Neither Social Influence nor Hedonic Motivation returned a significant relationship with Behavioural Intention. The interaction between Year and Hedonic Motivation was the only significant moderator of Behavioural Intention. Discussion As the first UTAUT2 study on the intention and actual use of ChatGPT in an ODeL environment, this study not only offers new insights into ChatGPT use but also leaves ample scope for further research.

title: Adaptive Moral Theory: Toward an Evolutionary Cognitive Neuroscience of the Moral Sense
dff350438cb6bcc045e3da519df8faf60e867ef8.abstract: Integrating evolutionary science, neuroscience, and cognitive science, adaptive moral theory (AMT) offers a consilient account of our evolved moral sense. It proposes two functionally distinct moral systems: the foundational mammalian CARE system and the phylogenetically newer duty network, advancing a working definition of morality centered on the well-being of other living entities. AMT also reconceptualizes the emotion/reason debate and provides a new account of the relationship between consequentialism and deontology; it also challenges cooperation-centered evolutionary accounts, naturalizes situation ethics, and introduces a taxonomy of eight moral frames that offers a different lens on sacrificial dilemmas.

title: Seasonal memory in Hudson Bay sea ice: autumn freeze-up predicts spring break-up, 1990–2026
fcebd6dede8acee7bb2e196b12bc6e1a492a9b0a.abstract: Abstract Hudson Bay is one of the largest seasonally ice-covered seas in the Northern Hemisphere, and the timing of its ice season structures the regional climate, its marine ecosystems and the communities that depend on them. Between 1990 and 2026 the ice-free season lengthened by 6.8 days per decade. Most of that change is conventionally attributed to warming in the season in which it occurs, but here we show that the spring half of the signal cannot be explained that way: April–May air temperature over the bay has not risen, yet the date on which half the bay is open water has advanced by 2.8 days per decade. Using 37 ice seasons of daily 25-km satellite ice concentration, we develop a seasonal-memory model in which the preceding autumn's freeze-up date predicts the following spring's break-up independently of spring temperature. The relationship is strong (β = −0.50 days per day, p < 0.001, R² = 0.59) and survives first- differencing (β = −0.29, p = 0.025), instrumental-variable estimation (β = −0.58) and double machine learning (β = −0.40). The memory coefficient is negative in 89% of 1,428 grid cells and has grown from about −0.15 in 1990–2007 to −0.61 in 2008–2026, consistent with thinning ice. A two-predictor physical model outperforms gradient boosting with eleven predictors out of sample (R² = 0.48 versus 0.36), indicating that the relationship is additive and low-dimensional. Autumn freeze-up accounts for roughly 70% of the observed spring advance. Hudson Bay's ice-free season is therefore lengthening as a coupled two-season process, and autumn ice formation carries information about the following spring at a lead time of six months.

title: Protective effects of AKBA against hypoxia-induced cognitive dysfunction: potential involvement of SLC2A1, PTGS1, and BCL2L1
container-title: Frontiers in Pharmacology
bad311d4ef413324348294fb487c935a5119d194.abstract: Introduction Hypoxia-induced cognitive impairment (HICI) is associated with neuroinflammation, oxidative stress, and gut microbiota dysbiosis, highlighting the need for effective neuroprotective interventions. Acetyl-11-keto-β-boswellic acid (AKBA), a bioactive triterpenoid derived from frankincense, possesses anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties, but its protective effects against hypoxia-associated cognitive dysfunction remain insufficiently understood. Methods This study investigated the neuroprotective potential of AKBA administered concurrently with hypoxic exposure and explored its associated molecular alterations. Network pharmacology, transcriptomic analysis, molecular similarity assessment, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulations were integrated to identify and prioritize candidate proteins. The protective effects of AKBA were subsequently evaluated in mice exposed to normobaric hypoxia (12.7% O 2 ) for 10 days. Results AKBA administration attenuated hypoxia-associated cognitive deficits, accompanied by reduced inflammatory and oxidative stress markers, increased BDNF levels, decreased TUNEL-positive staining, and preservation of MBP immunoreactivity. These effects were associated with changes in cortical SLC2A1, PTGS1, and BCL2L1 expression, together with alterations in NF-κB- and Keap1/Nrf2-related protein levels. AKBA administration was also associated with changes in gut microbial composition, and exploratory correlation analyses suggested associations between selected bacterial taxa and cortical protein expression. Conclusion Collectively, these findings indicate that concurrent AKBA administration provides protection against hypoxia-associated cognitive dysfunction, potentially involving coordinated changes in inflammatory, antioxidant, and neurotrophic responses. However, the causal roles of the candidate proteins and gut microbiota alterations remain to be established through further functional investigations.

title: Perioperative esketamine is associated with attenuated sleep deprivation-related cognitive dysfunction: a retrospective biomarker cohort study of the ferroptosis–neuroinflammation axis
container-title: Frontiers in Cell and Developmental Biology
7faf93b71854664fcf13e95e8eba5211d8bbb7bb.abstract: Background Sleep deprivation is common in older surgical patients and may increase vulnerability to postoperative neurocognitive dysfunction through oxidative stress, neuroinflammation, and regulated cell-death pathways. Experimental studies increasingly implicate hippocampal ferroptosis, particularly disruption of the SLC7A11–GSH–GPX4 defense axis, in sleep-deprivation-related cognitive injury. Esketamine has antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties, but whether its perioperative neurocognitive benefit is associated with a ferroptosis-related molecular phenotype in clinical patients remains uncertain. Methods We conducted a retrospective biomarker cohort study of 398 adults aged 60–80 years who underwent elective major non-cardiac surgery between January 2022 and December 2025. Patients were classified according to preoperative sleep deprivation (total sleep time &lt;4 h and sleep efficiency &lt;70% during the night before surgery) and perioperative esketamine exposure, generating four groups: NSD-C, NSD-E, SD-C, and SD-E. The primary outcome was early postoperative cognitive decline on postoperative day (POD) 7, defined by a ≥1-SD deterioration in a composite neuropsychological Z score. In a biomarker subcohort, plasma 4-hydroxy-2-nonenal (4-HNE), malondialdehyde (MDA), glutathione (GSH), glutathione peroxidase activity, inflammatory cytokines, neuronal injury markers, and PBMC expression of GPX4, SLC7A11, and ACSL4 were analyzed. Confounding was addressed using multivariable models and inverse-probability-of-treatment weighting. Bootstrap mediation models examined a ferroptosis-related redox score and IL-6 as candidate mediators. Results In the cohort, cognitive decline occurred in 32.5% of sleep-deprived patients without esketamine and 17.7% of sleep-deprived patients exposed to esketamine. After adjustment, esketamine exposure in the sleep-deprivation subgroup was associated with lower odds of cognitive decline (adjusted OR 0.49, 95% CI 0.26–0.92). Sleep deprivation was associated with higher 4-HNE, MDA, ACSL4, IL-6, TNF-α, and NSE and lower GSH, GPX activity, GPX4, and SLC7A11; these abnormalities were attenuated in the esketamine-exposed group. The exploratory ferroptosis-related redox score was independently associated with cognitive decline. Under the specified exploratory mediation model, the estimated total mediated proportion was 54%; this model-based decomposition does not establish causal biological mediation. Conclusion Perioperative esketamine was associated with less pronounced early postoperative cognitive decline in sleep-deprived patients and a less pronounced peripheral ferroptosis-related/inflammatory phenotype.

title: Influence of mobile games on cognitive development among Somali children
container-title: Frontiers in Public Health
00bf0071142df0f00dd2bd9414bdcd9abc24d17f.abstract: Introduction and aims The increasing availability of smartphones and internet access in Somalia has contributed to the growing use of mobile games among children. Mobile gaming may influence cognitive development positively or negatively depending on gaming habits and supervision. This study aimed to assess the influence of mobile games on cognitive development among Somali children aged 6–15 years. Methods A descriptive cross-sectional survey was conducted among 200 Somali children, with their accompanying parents or guardians, recruited from selected primary and secondary schools in Mogadishu by multistage sampling. A structured questionnaire recorded gaming habits, parental supervision, and perceived positive and negative cognitive effects on a 5-point Likert scale. Data were summarised as frequencies, percentages, means, and standard deviations (SD). Results More than half of the children (55.0%) played daily, and 70.0% played for 1–2 h per day. Action (45.0%) and sports (35.0%) games predominated, educational games were played by 5.0%, and only 25.0% of children were always supervised. Positive-effect items had an overall mean of 3.71; agreement was highest for “games make learning more interesting” (4.00 ± 0.95). Negative-effect items had an overall mean of 3.56. Among perceived cognitive and academic difficulties (domain mean 3.54), reduced study time scored highest (3.80 ± 1.13). Indicators of problematic gaming had a domain mean of 3.66, and 60.0% of children found it difficult to stop playing. Fatigue and reduced school engagement had a domain mean of 3.55. Discussion Somali children in this sample perceived mobile gaming as having both beneficial and harmful effects on cognitive development. The evidence is descriptive and self-reported and does not establish causation. Balanced gaming, closer parental supervision, and greater use of educational games are recommended, and longitudinal studies with objective cognitive measures are needed.

title: Վահանաձև գեղձի ֆունկցիոնալ խանգարում ունեցող անձանց հիվանդության ներքին պատկերի կոգնիտիվ, հու­զական և անձնային-իմաստային առանձնահատկությունները
Cognitive, Emotional, and Personal-Meaning Features of the Internal Picture of Illness in Individuals with Functional Thyroid Disorders
Когнитивные, эмоциональные и личностно-смысловые особенности внутренней картины болезни у лиц с функциональными нарушениями щитовидной железы
container-title: Bulletin of Yerevan University E: Philosophy, Psychology
9c1764cb137e36e2c89a99dd8eb986e8c88715ed.abstract: Functional disorders of the thyroid gland occupy an important place in the healthcare sector. These disorders have a significant impact not only on physical health but also on mental health, causing substantial changes in the cognitive and emotional domains of an individual. In this context, particular importance is attached to how a person perceives their own illness, what meaning they attribute to it, and how they respond to its manifestations. An important theoretical framework for studying these issues is the concept of the “internal picture of illness,” which reflects the totality of an individual’s perceptions of the illness, attitudes toward it, and emotional responses. The article systematizes the existing theoretical approaches to the concept of the “internal picture of illness,” providing a basis for studying the perception of the disease and responses to it among individuals with functional disorders of the thyroid gland. Within the framework of the present study, an attempt was made to examine the perceptions and attitudes of individuals with functional disorders of the thyroid gland toward their illness, how they perceive the illness, and how they respond to it. The analysis revealed a number of statistically significant positive associations between individual components of the internal picture of illness. Within the structure of illness perception, symptom severity and concern play a key role, as they are closely associated with the impact of the illness and the emotional response to it. The findings indicate that understanding the components of the internal picture of illness and the relationships between them may contribute to improving the effectiveness of treatment for these disorders and to a deeper understanding of psychological factors associated with the disease.

title:
Memory Window Improvement
in Ferroelectric Thin-Film
Transistors with HfZrO2/AlN Bilayers Grown by Atomic Layer
Deposition
container-title: ACS Nano
3ffafe77aa820f6e20009a8fc49f36f785ef9ed0.abstract: Abstract This study demonstrates proximity-induced ferroelectric switching in a stacked ferroelectric film composed of fluorite-structured HfZrO2 (HZO) and wurtzite-structured AlN, which are grown by thermal atomic layer deposition (ALD) and plasma-enhanced ALD (PEALD), respectively. The stacked film shows remanent polarization close to that of HZO but with a much higher coercive field, desirable for enhancing the memory window of ferroelectric thin-film transistors (FeTFTs) for storage applications. The FeTFT with a 5 nm-thick amorphous In–Ga–Zn–O (a-IGZO) channel layer, also grown by ALD, shows a memory window of ∼6.1 V, and data retention over 10 years. It also shows stable endurance cycles of ∼104. These enhancements over the single-layer HZO or stacked HZO/Al2O3 films, which show a minimal memory window of ∼0.3 V and ∼−0.3 V, respectively, are ascribed to the proximity ferroelectric effects between the soft ferroelectric HZO and hard ferroelectric AlN. These results, together with the conformal deposition of the HZO/AlN stack in high-aspect-ratio structures, demonstrate the feasibility of extending the ALD/PEALD-based Prox-FE materials platform toward three-dimensional (3D) process integration.

title: Attention-Derived Dependency Cut for Independent KV-Cache Reuse in Agent Memory
container-title: International Journal of Network Dynamics and Intelligence
7be3cb8b21c8e7b13f8d287100eac3bd097c3cfa.abstract: Long-term agent memory grows continuously with interaction, making full-memory prefill increasingly costly in terms of time to first token (TTFT) and redundant computation. KV-cache reuse could avoid repeatedly prefilling the accumulated memory, but KV caching relies on exact prefix matching. When memory is updated, reorganized, or assembled from reusable units, prefix mismatches prevent direct reuse of existing KV caches and force the model to recompute a long memory prefix. Existing methods largely assume that memory blocks are already given and address the prefix-matching limitation by concatenating their KV caches and then repairing the resulting mismatch. We therefore argue that the primary question for agent-memory KV reuse is where to segment the memory. We propose AD-CUT, an Attention-derived dependency Cut method for training-free, independence-oriented segmentation. AD-Cut computes attention-derived dependency signals over sentence-level atomic units, including an incoming signal Ain and an outgoing signal Aout, and selects boundaries where both signals are low. The signals exhibit stable positive associations with intervention-derived KV and NLL sensitivity, with Spearman ρ ranging from 0.615 to 0.868 and context-cluster bootstrap intervals remaining positive, supporting their use as predictive proxies. In block-KV serving for agent QA, AD-Cut achieves a 16.17× Online TTFT speedup with a QA Quality Retention of 0.7675. It also improves task quality over naive sentence-level reuse in a controlled agent-memory evaluation. These results show that AD-Cut substantially reduces online computation while mitigating the quality loss caused by KV-cache reuse.

title: From Whole Number Bias to Gap Thinking: University Students’ Strategy Choices in Fraction Comparison and Relations to Math and Cognitive Abilities
container-title: International Journal of Science and Mathematics Education
aebb4b3bf79c6283b565a313fcf45f47a6955233.abstract: Abstract Fractions pose a significant challenge for many students. Several flawed strategies have been identified in elementary and secondary students when selecting the larger of two fractions: the whole number strategy (choosing the larger numerals), the reverse strategy (choosing the smaller numerals), and the gap strategy (choosing the smaller difference between numerator and denominator). The prevalence of these strategies among university students is unknown. In the present study, we used specially designed stimuli and cluster analysis to identify fraction comparison strategy use among 90 university students. We assessed potential contributing factors to fraction understanding: general math achievement, inhibitory control, and visuospatial working memory. The results revealed three clusters: a Whole-Number-Strategy group (14%), who primarily used the whole number strategy; a Partial-Reverse-Strategy group (30%), who used the reverse strategy for challenging fractions; and a Gap-Tendency group (56%), who showed high accuracy when the gap strategy succeeds, and lower but above chance accuracy when the gap strategy fails. Regarding the contributing factors, the Gap-Tendency group performed better than the Whole-Number-Strategy group, but did not differ from the Partial-Reverse-Strategy group, on all measures. These findings extend prior research on strategies by showing that many university students have overcome whole number bias but have not yet achieved a complete understanding of fraction magnitude. Moreover, the lack of differences in math and cognitive factors between the better-performing groups shows that strong math and cognitive abilities are necessary but not sufficient for full fraction understanding among university students.

title: Benchmarking ChatGPT Against Human Expertise in Health Communication Assessment: Organizational Implications of Feasibility-Oriented Evaluation
container-title: Health Education & Behavior
086dcf6ac1aa503bfe976a64a8a02eab29391449.abstract: Prominent narratives of generative artificial intelligence (AI) highlight these tools’ cost-saving potential for health organizations via more efficient communication. However, even if a particular tool were to perform adequately at one point in time, evaluating models across updates and upgrades is complex. There are few examples from industry that are feasible enough and few examples from academia robust enough for health organizations. To help fill this gap, we examined the performance of ChatGPT to identify the presence or absence of 6 evidence-based practices from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) Clear Communication Index (CCI) in short-form texts. First, we carried out a prompt engineering process to identify optimal approaches for prompting ChatGPT to correctly label the clear communication practices in a test dataset of 27 tweets, from simulated front-end user and back-end developer perspectives. Using expert labels as comparison points, we found front-end users and back-end developers would reach different conclusions about how to best prompt ChatGPT. Then, we investigated how accurately different versions of ChatGPT’s models could label these clear communication practices in a data set of 260 tweets. Using expert labels as comparison points, we found stable performance across two dated GPT-3.5 model versions, albeit with wide confidence intervals. Even so, we found that GPT-4 models could actually perform significantly worse on some CDC CCI labeling tasks. Our results imply the need for increased investment in health communication experts to evaluate generative AI performance over time, which may be less practical than investing in such experts to communicate with patients and engage communities directly.

title: Scientific Objectivity and Human Effort
container-title: Boston Studies in the Philosophy and History of Science
Portuguese Studies in Philosophy of Science
acb1c3a59c268b809afd7016ba5960f6217501f1.abstract: Abstract Drawing on examples ranging from Renaissance humanism to present-day laboratory science, this chapter develops a threefold framework for understanding scientific objectivity. First, impersonal objectivity treats facts as speaking for themselves, effacing the agency of the investigator. Second, laborious objectivity grounds credibility in painstaking intellectual, manual, and social work. Third—and most distinctive—I identify an effortless path to objectivity, in which credibility is enhanced when important findings are presented as having emerged with striking ease. By bringing these strands into a single frame, the chapter shows how ideals of objectivity have shifted between erasing human involvement, demanding disciplined labour, and imagining labour-free insights. This account revises previous histories of objectivity and clarifies some conceptual tensions that continue to shape scientific practice.

title: Explainable Machine Learning for Cross-Sectional Classification of Cognitive Impairment: A Leakage-Safe Study with Independent-Cohort External Validation across OASIS-1 and OASIS-2
container-title: International Research Journal on Advanced Engineering and Management (IRJAEM)
a5b93cde8f3ff6e78d1b16bff72b4f73ddd9cef2.abstract: Machine learning models built on routinely collected clinical variables have been proposed as a low-cost alternative to neuroimaging for identifying cognitive impairment, but many published studies report optimistic performance because of preprocessing leakage, participant-level leakage, or validation within a single cohort. This study developed and externally validated a leakage-safe machine learning framework for classifying concurrent cognitive impairment, and quantified the contributions of the Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) and MRI-derived brain-volume measures. Models were developed on the OASIS-1 cohort (n = 235) and evaluated, without refitting, on the independent baseline OASIS-2 cohort (n = 150), with impairment defined as a Clinical Dementia Rating (CDR) above zero. All preprocessing was fitted only within cross-validated training pipelines, and five classifiers were tuned by grid search. A random forest using age, sex, education, socioeconomic status and the MMSE achieved an external area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.920 (95% CI 0.868–0.964) and a Brier score of 0.111. Removing the MMSE reduced the AUC to 0.749. Compared with the conventional MMSE < 24 threshold, which identified only 32% of impaired participants, the model achieved 80.0% sensitivity at 91.8% specificity. Adding brain-volume measures raised the external AUC to 0.963. Baseline clinical and imaging variables did not distinguish participants who later converted to impairment. Under leakage-safe development and independent-cohort validation, the framework is best suited as a calibrated case-finding aid rather than an early prediction tool.

title: Harnessing Neuroscience in Social Advertising: From Emotional Impact to Cognitive Understanding and Intentional Behavior in Children and Adolescents
container-title: Psychology & Marketing
c2df9e77f3d1a946069410902c50b1b32aec31fe.abstract: ABSTRACT This study examines emotional responses and their associations with Cognitive Understanding and Intentional Behavior following exposure to a social advertising video featuring historical female role models. Using a mixed‐methods approach that combines near‐infrared spectroscopy with survey data, it investigates how emotional responses observed during exposure to a femvertising stimulus are associated with subsequent Cognitive Understanding and Intentional Behavior. The research contributes to the understanding of emotional and cognitive responses to social advertising among children and adolescents and examines whether these relationships differ between male and female respondents. The model analyzes the relationships among emotional responses, cognitive engagement, and behavioral predisposition, using gender as a grouping variable. Results highlight the critical influence of both positive and negative emotions in responding to social messages and the potential of femvertising narratives to engage gender‐related awareness among young audiences. Practical implications for marketing and education are discussed, along with directions for future research.

title: From Effort to Learning Expectations: How Habit Connects Technology Acceptance and Self-Regulated Learning in MOOCs
0fe65b2e72c088af05c7d40e89fa349272c64bd8.abstract: Abstract Higher education institutions now rely on MOOCs as a delivery channel for adult learners, lifelong learning, and SDG-4 commitments, yet the evaluation of MOOC effectiveness still leans on completion rates, satisfaction surveys, and platform analytics. These proxies say little about how learners actually experience the platform, or about the behavioural processes through which that experience feeds into expected outcomes. This study reconceptualises MOOC effectiveness from a learner-centred perspective and examines the behavioural pathway through which learners’ perceptions of the platform translate into expected performance gains. We used a two-study design with independent cohorts. Study 1 developed and validated a learner-centred measurement instrument through expert content validation and exploratory factor analysis (n = 2,442). Study 2 used a two-wave design (n = 2,471) to test the relationships among the validated constructs in a structural model grounded in technology acceptance and self-regulated learning perspectives. Perceived effort expectancy influenced outcome performance expectancy roughly twice as strongly as learning process expectancy, indicating that ease of engagement matters more to learners’ performance expectations than perceived pedagogical superiority of the format. Habitual learning behaviour was the behavioural mechanism through which both effort and process beliefs fed into outcome expectations. The findings shift MOOC effectiveness research in higher education away from platform features and completion rates and towards validated learner-centred constructs and the behavioural processes that produce sustained engagement. We draw implications for institutional evaluation practice, digital course design, and SDG-4 policy in developing-country higher education systems.

title: Mechanobiology of osteoarthritis: from mechanical-dose sensing to organelle homeostasis and the emerging concept of mechanical memory
container-title: Frontiers in Cell and Developmental Biology
7159d98c9cad6bf321080857f8c61ae42d6b40a0.abstract: Osteoarthritis (OA) is a heterogeneous whole-joint disease in which mechanical, inflammatory, metabolic, and age-related factors converge to disrupt tissue homeostasis. Mechanical loading is essential for cartilage maintenance, whereas excessive or insufficient mechanical stimulation may disrupt cartilage homeostasis depending on the loading modality, magnitude, frequency, duration, recovery conditions, and tissue context. In this review, we integrate OA mechanobiology across scales, from whole-joint load redistribution and tissue-level mechanical filtering to chondrocyte mechanosensing and intracellular responses. The mechanistic emphasis is on cartilage and chondrocytes within the broader whole-joint context of OA. We discuss how integrin-focal adhesion complexes, PIEZO1/2, TRPV4, primary cilia, the cytoskeleton, and nuclear mechanotransduction regulate matrix metabolism, mitochondrial redox homeostasis, autophagy and mitophagy, regulated cell death, and cellular senescence. We further highlight mechanical unloading, immobilization, and microgravity-related models as distinct experimental contexts and discuss epigenetic, epitranscriptomic, and ubiquitin-dependent regulation as potential mechanisms underlying persistent cellular reprogramming, while recognizing that mechanical memory after stimulus withdrawal remains insufficiently established in OA. Finally, we outline how subject-specific modeling, spatial multi-omics, joint-on-chip systems, and multimodal mechanical phenotyping may support mechanobiology-guided OA stratification and therapy. Restoring patient-specific mechanical homeostasis, rather than simply reducing loading, may provide a framework for precision management of OA.

title: Mindfulness‐Based Intervention Improves Cognitive Function in Patients With Schizophrenia in Remitted: A Randomized Controlled Trial
container-title: International Journal of Methods in Psychiatric Research
e0b3e8b7be28bc60eeb0c3af8341bcc5926ea616.abstract: ABSTRACT Background Patients with schizophrenia exhibit deficits in facial emotion recognition (FER), attention, P300, and quality of life (QoL), which severely hinder functional recovery. This study aims to explore the effects of mindfulness‐based intervention (MBI) on these outcomes and the potential mediating mechanisms. Methods In this 8‐week randomized, single‐blind, controlled study, a total of 70 remitted patients with schizophrenia were randomly assigned to the MBI group or the control group. The Five‐Factor Mindfulness Scale (FFMQ), FER, P300 indices, Continuous Performance Test‐Identical Pairs (CPT‐IP), and Schizophrenia Quality of Life Scale (SQLS) were measured at baseline and week 8 to assess mindfulness levels, cognitive function, neurophysiological parameters, and QoL. Linear mixed models evaluated intervention effects. Mediation analyses used pre‐post change scores with bootstrap resampling. Results For the primary outcome, MBI significantly improved FFMQ ( β = 16.750, 95% CI [7.769, 25.731], p < 0.001). For the exploratory outcomes, significant improvements were observed for P300 latency ( β = −63.602, 95% CI [−88.651, −38.554], p < 0.001) and CPT‐IP ( β = 8.219, 95% CI [4.004, 12.433], p < 0.001). FER and P300 amplitude showed nominal improvements only, and SQLS showed a non‐significant trend. A significant indirect effect through FER change was observed for change in SQLS (indirect effect = −6.343, 95% CI [−11.467, −2.288]), but CPT‐IP change did not mediate P300 amplitude improvement. Conclusion MBI significantly improved the primary outcome of mindfulness (FFMQ) and showed promising exploratory improvements in processing speed (P300 latency) and sustained attention (CPT‐IP). FER change may represent a potential indirect pathway associated with change in SQLS. These findings support MBI as a promising cognitive rehabilitation intervention. Trial Registration https://www.chictr.org.cn , identifier ChiCTR 2500106735, registered on: 29/07/2025

title: Integrated Cognitive Workload and Musculoskeletal Exposure Modeling for Adaptive Ergonomic Work Design
4209266bfc0b53d818daa0ccf8e4ed463f1c5858.abstract: Abstract Cognitive workload, musculoskeletal exposure, fatigue, and limited recovery can jointly affect worker comfort and task performance. However, these factors are often assessed separately, limiting the evaluation of cumulative ergonomic risk over time. This study proposes an integrated ergonomic modeling framework that combines cognitive workload, physical exposure, fatigue accumulation, and recovery within a common assessment structure. Normalized state variables are used to calculate a composite ergonomic risk index, and a proposed multi objective optimization procedure provides a basis for examining alternative task schedules and recovery intervals. Illustrative scenarios compare low, moderate, and high combined demands under specified model assumptions. The proposed analytical design also specifies a procedure for future sensitivity analysis of workload intensity, exposure duration, recovery rate, and worker susceptibility. The illustrative values indicate that higher modeled cognitive workload, physical exposure, and fatigue correspond to greater composite risk under the specified weighting scheme. However, these values are hypothetical and do not represent observed worker data or verified simulation outputs. The framework provides a methodological basis for examining relationships between modeled ergonomic risk and task performance during work schedule planning. Further research should implement reproducible computational experiments, conduct sensitivity analyses, and validate model predictions against measured workload, physical exposure, fatigue, and performance data before practical application.

title: Effectiveness of multidomain versus single-domain non-pharmacological interventions for cognitive decline in mild cognitive impairment and dementia: a systematic review protocol
container-title: JBI Evidence Synthesis
123e133361725debdc459b64b9f8e771e3d1456f.abstract: Objective: This review will assess whether multidomain non-pharmacological interventions are more effective than single-domain strategies in mitigating cognitive decline for people with mild cognitive impairment (MCI) and dementia. Introduction: MCI and dementia are suboptimal conditions that significantly reduce quality of life for affected individuals and their families. Non-pharmacological, lifestyle-based interventions have shown promise in attenuating cognitive decline in these populations by targeting modifiable risk factors associated with cognitive performance. However, it remains unclear whether multidomain interventions that simultaneously address numerous risk factors are more effective than single-domain approaches in these individuals. Eligibility criteria: Experimental and quasi-experimental studies evaluating the effects of non-pharmacological multidomain versus single-domain interventions on cognitive test performance in adults diagnosed with MCI or dementia will be included. Methods: This review will be conducted according to the JBI methodology for reviews of effectiveness. The databases to be searched include PubMed, CINAHL, Embase, PsycINFO, Web of Science, Scopus, and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, as well as multiple sources of unpublished evidence and gray literature. Two reviewers will independently perform study selection, and screen titles, abstracts, and full-text records that meet the eligibility criteria. Assessment of studies’ methodological quality using JBI critical appraisal tools and AI-assisted data extraction will be completed by 2 reviewers independently. Where appropriate, meta-analyses will be performed per cognitive domain and population group. Certainty of findings will be determined by following the Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) approach. Registration number: PROSPERO CRD420261398271

title: Cognitive biases and clinical reasoning errors among medical students in a simulated leprosy case: a cross-sectional decision-tree study
39d4d66b7c08ba529f2594e4cb5d2d5fad791302.abstract: Abstract Background Neglected tropical diseases carry a substantial global burden yet remain underrepresented in medical curricula. Leprosy poses a particular stress test for clinical reasoning: diagnosis depends on careful neurological assessment, yet training increasingly privileges imaging and laboratory investigations over bedside evaluation. We examined how medical students at different training stages reason through an atypical presentation of leprosy. Methods We mapped the clinical decision-making of 405 medical students from 14 Brazilian medical programmes using an interactive decision tree with 22 diverging pathways, simulating an atypical neurological presentation of leprosy. Participants were sampled across three training stages: basic sciences (n = 104), clinical clerkship (n = 101), and internship (n = 200). Trajectories were classified into seven distinct decision-making profiles using deductive framework analysis. Associations with training stage and institutional leprosy exposure were tested using Pearson’s chi-square test, the Cochran–Armitage test for trend, and Monte Carlo simulation. Results Only 12.8% (52/405) of participants navigated the complete target management pathway (pathway 9), with selection rates remaining low across all training stages ( X ²= 0.65, p = 0.72; linear trend p = 0.51). The distribution of clinical reasoning profiles varied across the curriculum, although this overall association was exploratory ( X ² = 20.43, p = 0.059). Pre-clinical students showed an excess of cognitive-bias errors (standardised residual + 2.48), whereas interns showed a deficit in these novice errors (-3.03) alongside an excess of early diagnoses followed by inappropriate management (+ 3.07). Most students (71.4%, 289/405) completed the case without performing the physical examination, having requested high-complexity imaging first. Conclusions Linear curricular progression did not inherently foster adaptive clinical problem-solving on this simulated case. Advanced training produced a pattern of confident incompetence: senior students avoided novice heuristic biases yet frequently diverged into non-guideline management regimens, a pattern consistent with technological over-reliance and automated decision-making. Developing diagnostic autonomy requires shifting from passive content accumulation toward cultivating cognitive flexibility and metacognitive awareness.

title: Review of: "Walking Through Memory, Myth, and Heritage: A Socio-Cultural Animation Framework via Cultural Walks and Reflective Journals at Quinta das Lágrimas"
Effects of Anesthesia on Alzheimer’s Disease–Related Biomarkers and Postoperative Cognitive Outcomes: A Review
container-title: Advances in Geriatric Medicine and Research
08f9430ac7c8191357d5bbd50df7df9e1c3035af.abstract: Cognitive changes after surgery, including postoperative delirium and postoperative neurocognitive dysfunction, are common in older adults. These observations have raised concerns that anesthetic exposure may interact with biological pathways associated with Alzheimer’s disease (AD). This review summarizes in vitro, preclinical, and clinical studies examining the relationship between anesthetic exposure, amyloid-beta, tau-related measures, and postoperative cognitive outcomes. Experimental studies suggest that selected volatile anesthetics can influence amyloid-beta aggregation, tau phosphorylation, phosphatase activity, and neuronal signaling. However, these effects vary according to the anesthetic agent, exposure conditions, temperature, animal model, and underlying susceptibility. Human studies have yielded conflicting results. Some report short-term changes in cerebrospinal fluid or blood biomarkers, whereas others find no sustained changes in AD-related biomarkers or no association between postoperative biomarker trajectories and cognitive decline. Interpretation is further complicated because amyloid-beta and phosphorylated tau are not specific to AD and may also reflect other neurodegenerative diseases, neuronal injury, inflammation, altered clearance, or perioperative physiological stress. Current evidence does not establish that anesthesia accelerates AD progression in humans. Nevertheless, pre-existing neurodegenerative vulnerability may increase the risk of postoperative delirium or cognitive decline. Larger longitudinal studies using multimodal biomarkers, nonsurgical controls, standardized cognitive outcomes, and long-term follow-up are needed to determine whether perioperative exposures influence AD-specific pathology or primarily produce transient and nonspecific markers of brain stress.

title: Resisting Settler Colonial Erasure Through Collective Memory
container-title: The International Journal of Literary Humanities
51e96fb6c1fe02f62864bcdbd8a11631bfaad3bf.abstract: Memory plays a significant role in preserving the history, knowledge, and cultural practices of a land, particularly in the context of colonialism, migrations, and dispossessions. In this context, this study examines Sheela Tomy’s Valli: A Novel with particular attention given to how memory is embedded in the social, cultural, and ecological fabric of Kalluvayal, the village in which the novel is set. Drawing on Maurice Halbwachs’ theory of collective memory, Jan Assmann’s distinction between communicative and cultural memory, and Patrick Wolfe’s theory of settler colonialism, the study examines how individual memories, shaped through social interactions and cyclical cultural practices, become incorporated into collective memory and how such collective memory challenges the cultural and historical erasure produced by settler interventions. While existing scholarship on Valli has examined themes of Indigenous displacement and environmental concerns, limited attention has been given to the relationship between collective memory, the land as a mnemonic space, and settler colonial process. Adopting a qualitative approach, this analysis finds that Valli represents land as a repository of lived experiences, intergenerational knowledge, and cultural practices. The preservation and transmission of memory enable the tribal community to challenge dispossession, ecocide, historical amnesia, and cultural erasure. By foregrounding the lived realities, the novel challenges dominant narratives that legitimize settler intervention and presents memory as a means of sustaining cultural continuity and resistance.

title: Misconceptions to Mathematical Understanding: Synthesizing the Roles of Cognitive Conflict, Reflection, and Conceptual Reconstruction
container-title: Journal of Multidisciplinary Science: MIKAILALSYS
f25a61595b75ec456a1019010b24ed5e0957e1b5.abstract: Mathematical misconceptions can hinder the development of deep and lasting conceptual understanding. This study aimed to analyze and synthesize the roles of cognitive conflict, reflection, and conceptual reconstruction in transforming misconceptions into mathematical understanding. A systematic literature review employing a descriptive qualitative approach examined relevant scholarly articles published between 2020 and 2026. The analysis focused on the characteristics of misconceptions, mechanisms of cognitive conflict, functions of reflection, and processes of conceptual reconstruction. The synthesis indicates that cognitive conflict promotes learners’ awareness of discrepancies between their existing conceptions and mathematical evidence; reflection supports the evaluation and refinement of their thinking processes; and conceptual reconstruction enables the development of more accurate, coherent, and meaningful knowledge structures. Together, these components provide an integrated account of how misconceptions can be transformed into mathematical understanding. The study contributes an integrative synthesis framework that connects these mechanisms through the theoretical perspectives of conceptual change, constructivism, and metacognition. This framework highlights the complementary roles of the three components and provides a theoretical and pedagogical basis for developing mathematics instruction that addresses misconceptions and strengthens conceptual understanding.

title: The Legacy of Urban Sculpture in Yogyakarta
container-title: The International Journal of Interdisciplinary Cultural Studies
9931f27bdb0f2891715184f0ebbd8297a032ea65.abstract: Urban sculptures constitute cultural heritage that connects material space, historical memory, and collective identity, yet their continuity is increasingly challenged by urbanization, tourism, spatial transformation, mobility, and digitalization. Existing scholarship has examined spatial memory, cultural governance, and cultural resilience largely as distinct dimensions, leaving insufficient explanation of how these processes interact within living urban monument systems. This study examines how spatial memory, cultural governance, and the transformation of cultural meaning collectively shape the resilience of urban sculpture heritage in Yogyakarta, Indonesia. Using a qualitative case study, the research integrates field observation, spatial mapping, visual documentation, historical archives, policy documents, digital media, and semi-structured interviews with ten Millennials and Generation Z informants. Data were analyzed through reflexive thematic analysis and triangulation. Findings show that urban sculptures operate as socio-spatial memory infrastructure through spatial configuration, historical narratives, landmark functions, symbolic representation, and everyday interaction. Their continuity is institutionally supported through cultural regulation, spatial planning, legitimization, conservation, and community participation, while cultural meaning is sustained through intergenerational reinterpretation, spatial adaptation, tourism recontextualization, and digital reproduction. Based on these interconnected processes, the study proposes Dynamic Monumental Resilience, conceptualizing monument sustainability as the capacity to maintain cultural identity through continuous reinterpretation, recontextualization, and reproduction of meaning across changing social contexts.

title: Transformed Memory Estimators for the Mean of Population in Time-Based Surveys
container-title: Model Assisted Statistics and Applications
c6ef613e6076d80c923b717d6755fc554213abea.abstract: Incorporating ancillary information increases the precision and reliability of the estimators by reducing the sampling variability. Besides current ancillary information, past information available in different forms can also be utilized to get more accurate and stable estimators. The objective of the current research work is to improve the efficiency and precision of estimators of population mean in time-based surveys by using both current and past ancillary information. The aim of study is to design estimators which may minimize the sampling variability and mean square error (MSE) and improve the performance as compared with the existing classical and memory type ratio and product estimators. To obtain this aim, we have developed transformed memory-type ratio and product estimators by employing the exponentially weighted moving average (EWMA) statistic. The EWMA statistic is an important statistical tool that efficiently combines present and past information, thereby improving the overall performance of estimators. Under appropriate approximations, the expressions are obtained for the bias and MSE of the developed estimators. Moreover, mathematical conditions have been derived to show the superiority and dominance of the developed estimators over some of the available estimators existing in the literature. To validate the theoretical results, both empirical and simulation studies have been carried out. Empirical investigation is carried out on a real-world data set and simulation study is carried out on a population generated using R programing language. The outcomes of both the empirical and simulation analysis clearly demonstrate that the developed memory-type estimators outperform the existing estimators under appropriate conditions.

title: ALT-index+: An Efficient Hybrid Learned Index for Concurrent Memory Systems
container-title: ACM Transactions on Storage
6be71abedd0fbbb741b6322f806d24bed06d02b8.abstract: The learned index technique has been widely explored as a strong competitor to traditional indexes. However, frequent retraining is required when it comes to insertion scenarios, and the read-write performance of the learned index still falls short of expectations, especially in concurrent conditions. In this paper, we first propose a novel hybrid index scheme that combines a read-efficient learned index with an insert-efficient Adaptive Radix Tree (ART) to realize high read-write performance. However, it is not trivial due to expensive model prediction errors, complicated retraining process, redundant node traversals, and slow bulkload speed. Therefore, we introduce ALT-index, an efficient hybrid learned index structure with a delicate two-tier architecture, a compact pointer buffer, and an efficient segment algorithm to address these issues. Nevertheless, its performance is still limited by blocking retraining process, and the bulkload time cannot exploit multithreading. To address these limitations, we present ALT-index+ with two major extensions. First, we develop a stepped lazy eviction scheme to support a non-blocking retraining process. Second, a parallel recursive construction scheme is designed to accelerate bulkloading in both layers. Experimental results show that ALT-index+ achieves 1.4x–2.5x throughput improvement in read-write-balanced scenarios, with a maximum 80.2% reduction in bulkload time compared to state-of-the-art learned indexes.

title: Association of the Geriatric Nutritional Risk Index with incident cognitive impairment and longitudinal cognitive trajectories in older adults
container-title: Journal of Alzheimer’s Disease
64f3ada6f0cdfb73d9c8369a020de1602c074c31.abstract: Background Malnutrition is a modifiable risk factor for cognitive deterioration. The Geriatric Nutritional Risk Index (GNRI) objectively assesses nutritional status, but its longitudinal association with incident cognitive impairment and distinct cognitive trajectories remains insufficiently characterized. Objective To assess the association between baseline GNRI and incident cognitive impairment. Methods We analyzed data from 2596 community-dwelling adults aged ≥60 years from the Health and Retirement Study (2016–2022). Baseline nutritional status was assessed by GNRI. Incident cognitive impairment was defined using the modified Telephone Interview for Cognitive Status. Group-based trajectory modeling identified longitudinal cognitive patterns. Cox proportional hazards regression and multinomial logistic regression models examined associations, adjusting for sociodemographic, lifestyle, and clinical covariates. Results Compared with the high GNRI group (≥98), low GNRI (<98) was associated with a higher hazard of incident cognitive impairment (HR = 1.25; 95% CI: 1.05–1.49). This association was linear (p for nonlinearity = 0.62). Longitudinal modeling identified four trajectory groups: “High-stable” (21.7%), “High-decline” (29.6%), “Moderate-decline” (41.4%), and “Low-rapid decline” (7.3%). In multinomial analyses, low GNRI (<98) was specifically associated with higher odds of the “Low-rapid decline” trajectory (OR = 1.61; 95% CI: 1.06–2.46) versus the “High-stable” reference, whereas intermediate-pattern associations were not significant. The association was consistent across subgroups, including those defined by body mass index and alcohol consumption (p for interaction > 0.05). Conclusions Low baseline GNRI was associated with a higher hazard of incident cognitive impairment and greater odds of membership in an adverse cognitive trajectory. The predictive and screening utility of GNRI requires further evaluation.

title: Location matters: The link between regional white matter hyperintensity burden and subjective cognitive decline in those at risk of Alzheimer's disease
container-title: Journal of Alzheimer’s Disease
80833ecd7ec3ada159ce9af566d60bc6bd74a9bb.abstract: Background Subjective cognitive decline (SCD) is a potential early indicator of Alzheimer's disease (AD). While SCD has been linked to white matter hyperintensity (WMH) burden, it is unclear whether regional WMH lesion volume is differentially associated with domains of cognitive complaints. Objective Examine whether regional WMH burden is associated with domain-specific SCD (memory, executive function) in cognitively unimpaired older adults with a family history of AD. Methods Participants were 150 cognitively unimpaired older adults (65–89 years) with subjective memory complaints and a first-degree family history of AD. Cognitive complaints were assessed with the Cognitive Change Index (CCI-20). WMHs were quantified from T1-weighted and FLAIR MRI using an automated pipeline and categorized into sample-based tertiles for total, subcortical, and lobar regions. Hierarchical regressions examined associations between WMH burden and CCI-20 memory, executive, and total scores, while adjusting for demographics, total intracranial volume, MRI site, APOE ε4 status, and mood symptoms. Results Greater WMH burden in the left temporal lobe was associated with increased memory complaints and total SCD, whereas no WMH region was associated with executive function complaints. APOE ε4 status and depressive symptoms were associated with greater memory and total cognitive complaints across models. Apathy was uniquely related to memory complaints. Conclusions Among older adults with elevated risk of AD, memory-SCD was associated with greater region-specific left temporal cerebrovascular lesion volume. Findings highlight the clinical relevance of left temporal WMH burden and the importance of considering regional vascular pathology, genetic risk, and mood when characterizing early subjective cognitive changes.

For [Formula: see text] and nonnegative memory kernels [Formula: see text], a modal decomposition is used to derive an exact spectral stability criterion. We prove that the zero solution is spectrally stable if and only if [Formula: see text], where [Formula: see text] denotes the total hereditary mass. Equality corresponds to a critical zero characteristic root, whereas violation of the inequality produces a unique positive real root in the first spatial mode. For exponential memory, the instability transition occurs through a zero-frequency crossing. Although the stability threshold is independent of the temporal fractional order [Formula: see text], the unstable branch obeys a near-critical power law with exponent [Formula: see text]. title: Understanding Cognitive Load in Digital Cultural Heritage: An Explainable AI-Driven Multimodal Analysis
container-title: Applied Sciences
56c5bedaa54c06c867ae9058d23069513d8d5958.abstract: Digital cultural heritage (DCH) platforms deliver complex multimedia narratives, but their cognitive demands remain insufficiently evaluated. We recorded electroencephalography (EEG) and eye tracking (ET) from 19 valid participants (of 30 recruited) interacting with seven authentic material formats from a national public service platform. Labels were three tiers derived from material-level NASA-TLX means; modeling used leave-one-subject-out validation (LOSO) with data-driven steps fitted within training folds. The primary three-tier model, using ET with random forest, reached 0.669 accuracy (permutation p = 0.0033; 95% CI [0.595, 0.743]; macro-F1 0.66). A complementary two-tier analysis retaining all trials reached 0.737 accuracy (macro-F1 0.73). Nested LOSO with inner-fold model selection yielded three-tier accuracy 0.632 (95% CI [0.564, 0.707]; macro-F1 0.630) and two-tier accuracy 0.684 (95% CI [0.632, 0.744]; macro-F1 0.676). EEG differentiated material formats at the group level (frontal theta, p = 0.0023) but did not improve trial-level classification. Fold-internal TreeSHAP and permutation importance converged on attentional narrowing under high load: shorter saccades, longer dwell, and fewer unique gaze regions. Objective information-density measures attributed the highest load to cross-channel integration demand, not information amount. These findings support design principles for cognitively sustainable digital cultural platforms and delineate the evidentiary boundaries of small-sample multimodal load modeling.

title: A Socio-Reflective Dimension of Intelligent Functioning: Linking Theory of Mind and Metacognition
container-title: Journal of Intelligence
f8f5999be9f169c94b0014e372703fd66f4d8066.abstract: Intelligent adaptation in social contexts can require people to assess their own knowledge while representing what others know, believe, or misunderstand. Self–other mental coordination is proposed as a context-dependent functional relation between these processes. The framework distinguishes other-oriented mental-state representation associated with Theory of Mind from self-oriented monitoring and regulation associated with metacognition. It organizes their proposed coordination across three interacting functional levels: mental-state representation, monitoring and regulation, and social-adaptive use. These levels describe functions rather than fixed developmental stages. A tentative process account specifies how information about one’s own uncertainty and another person’s informational position may guide comparison, response revision, and help seeking. Developmental predictions concern reduced dependence on comparison prompts, selective adjustment when informational roles change, and transfer to new partners or content requiring the same comparison. The evidence comes chiefly from childhood and educational contexts; adult functioning requires separate testing. The framework adopts neo-Piagetian constraints on processing capacity and cognizance as boundary conditions and uses developmental cycles to order the predicted changes. Testing requires longitudinal, measurement-invariant latent models combined with experimental manipulations that separate coordination from its components and shared resources. Its explanatory value for a socio-reflective dimension of intelligent functioning remains unestablished.

title: The Sounds of San Diego Bay May Affect Bottlenose Dolphins (Tursiops truncatus) During Cognitive Tasks
container-title: Journal of Marine Science and Engineering
89c24858cca7e8af0e4ccc7e31faaf1101178992.abstract: Attention is a process that guides organisms to engage in goal-directed behavior, such as seeking food when hungry. However, attention is subject to distraction, which can impact the execution of these behaviors. The ocean is full of auditory stimuli that are potentially distracting. Bottlenose dolphins (Tursiops spp.), who rely on sound as their primary sensory and communicative modality, have been shown to be impacted by noise, especially anthropogenic noise. In our study, we assessed whether louder background noise, including both natural and anthropogenic noise, was associated with worse performance on two common cognitive tasks. Using previously recorded cognitive task data, we collected information on how long it took dolphins to make a choice, how many times they considered each alternative, whether they succeeded at the trial, and the root-mean-squared amplitude of the background noise across three frequency bands while they were making a choice. In both datasets, longer choice times and more oscillations between alternatives were associated with louder noise in the highest frequency band, which mostly consists of social sounds produced by nearby dolphins. Worse performance was also associated with this higher frequency band in one of the datasets. Results were mixed for low and middle frequency bands. Our results suggest that social sounds may be more distracting than vessel noise for dolphins in San Diego Bay, though these data are correlational and should be further investigated. Future experiments should manipulate the types and magnitudes of noise that are most distracting across additional types and difficulties of cognitive tasks. This would further shed light on both welfare considerations and comparative cognition.

title: Dance-based exercise for healthy brain aging in older adults: integrating neuroplasticity, cognitive reserve, physical fitness, social engagement, and mental well-being
container-title: Frontiers in Psychiatry
5d608a550fbf3367bb6cb7fe668398fe3fb874ed.abstract: Population aging brings rising difficulties associated with cognitive deterioration, diminished physical capabilities, social isolation, and increased susceptibility to mental health problems. Finding accessible, multidomain approaches to promote healthy brain aging has become a major priority. Dance-based exercise is a distinctive form of physical activity that combines aerobic movement, motor coordination, cognitive involvement, social interaction, and emotional expression. Previous systematic reviews and meta-analyses have largely quantified isolated physical or cognitive outcomes following dance interventions. However, an accurate understanding of healthy brain aging requires synthesizing how these separate domains interact. This narrative review adds to the current literature by providing an integrated conceptual framework that connects the neurobiological, physical, and psychosocial dimensions of dance-based exercise. Rather than pooling isolated effect sizes, we examine theoretical mechanisms (e.g., task-specific neuroplasticity and cognitive reserve) that plausibly link multidomain elements of dance to brain aging; these mechanisms are primarily hypothesis-generating in the context of existing dance trials. This narrative review examines the potential mechanisms by which dance-based exercise may support healthy brain aging in older adults, emphasizing neuroplasticity, cognitive reserve, physical fitness, social participation, and psychological well-being. The evidence available indicates that dance-based interventions may be linked to gains in cognitive functioning, especially executive abilities and attention, along with improvements in balance, mobility, and functional performance. In addition, the social and enjoyable character of dance may help foster better psychological outcomes and emotional well-being, although current evidence specifically concerning loneliness remains mixed. However, differences across study designs, intervention protocols, participant characteristics, and outcome measures constrain the ability to draw definitive conclusions about causality and the most effective intervention parameters. New evidence suggests that dance-based exercise may offer a promising multidomain strategy for strengthening resilience and supporting brain health throughout aging. Further rigorously designed longitudinal studies and randomized controlled trials are required to elucidate the underlying mechanisms, determine which populations are most responsive, and develop evidence-based guidance for incorporating dance-based interventions into healthy aging and geriatric mental health approaches.

title: BEYOND EQUIVALENCE: COGNITIVE SELF-REGULATION IN TRANSLATION AS AN ADAPTIVE DECISION-MAKING PROCESS
container-title: ShodhKosh: Journal of Visual and Performing Arts
a724cdbff3441b8ecee5b93b87a565aa144322f7.abstract: Translation has been historically viewed as a process involving the transfer of language or the resolution of problems. Recent advancements in cognitive translation studies have significantly enhanced our comprehension of the cognitive processes engaged by translators; nevertheless, the intricate mechanisms by which translators constantly monitor, adjust, and refine their decisions remain inadequately theorized. This article presents the Adaptive Cognitive Regulation Model (ACRM), an innovative theoretical framework that defines translation as a self-regulated cognitive process characterized by ongoing cycles of anticipation, problem identification, strategic inhibition, adaptive decision-making, and metacognitive validation. Grounded in cognitive psychology, metacognitive theory, and decision-making research, the model posits that translation transcends the mere application of linguistic knowledge; rather, it constitutes an adaptive cognitive system that responds to fluctuating textual, contextual, and communicative demands. By synthesizing insights from cognitive science with modern Translation Studies, the proposed framework not only broadens the scope of existing process-oriented methodologies but also offers a thorough explanation of translators' strategic behaviors. The article concludes by examining the implications of this model for translator education, cognitive process research, and forthcoming empirical studies utilizing think-aloud protocols. Ultimately, this research introduces a novel theoretical lens that situates adaptive cognitive regulation as a pivotal element in elucidating translation expertise and professional decision-making.

title: Deep Learning Modeling of Persuasion by ChatGPT-Powered Virtual Influencers: An Artificial Neural Network MLP Test
container-title: Big Data and Cognitive Computing
3ff07085a8e6b24791894eed216a50cc2e04489e.abstract: Using an artificial neural network (ANN) multilayer perceptron (MLP) analysis, this study examined predictors of AI users’ behavioral intention to buy products recommended by ChatGPT-enabled virtual influencers. The findings from an ANN MLP analysis demonstrated that trust in ChatGPT, empathy, perceived convenience, perceived superior functions, loneliness, existential threats to human identity, education level, and socio-economic status are predictors (input layers) of AI users’ intention to buy items endorsed by ChatGPT-enabled virtual influencers (output layer). A comparative analysis between multiple linear regression (MLR) and ANN MLP methods indicates 9.88% increase in the explained variance (R2) in purchase intention and a significant reduction in the prediction error (MLR RMSE of 1.02041 to MLP RMSE of 0.3784 for the training set and 0.3689 for the testing set). The results provide strong evidence for the methodological advantages and outperformance of the deep learning ANN MLP over the MLR in the current study for modeling and capturing intricate and non-linear relationships among the variables, by demonstrating improved model fit, more variance explained, and reduced prediction error. Theoretical contributions to the burgeoning literature on AI-enabled virtual personas are highlighted. AI-powered virtual personas as business model innovation and evolving monetization frameworks are explicated in view of AI-driven digital transformation. Practical suggestions, management slant, and executive insights for AI-empowered digital marketing and synthetic personas embedded within the creator economy are also discussed.

title: Reconstructing Konkani Migration: Literary Memory, Historical Evidence and the Politics of the Past
7fe8ff2926f718f76c9f49d57483170b0c5ec905.abstract: Abstract This paper critically examines the recurrent migration narrative of Konkani communities from Goa to the Kanara coast through a comparative reading of seven Konkani or Konkani people-related novels: Uday Bhembre’s Vhoddlem Ghor ; V. J. P. Saldanha’s Saiba Bhogos and Devache Kurpen ; Mahabaleshwar Sail’s Yugasamvar ; Kasturi Mohan Pai’s For the Love of Mandovi and Mahaprasthan ; and the Kannada novel Swapnasaraswata . Though differing in language and literary context, these works largely reproduce a popular oral narrative structured around colonization, conversion, destruction and consequent migration. The paper argues that this literary memory is historically selective, foregrounding Goud Saraswat Brahmins (GSBs) and the Catholic elite— Bamons and Chardos —while marginalizing other Konkani-speaking communities that also migrated from Goa. The study employs the Historical-Critical Method, juxtaposing textual readings of the novels with archival evidence and historiographical scholarship. It places these narratives alongside Anant Kakba Priolkar’s The Goa Inquisition: The Terrible Tribunal for the East (1961), written against the political background of the movement for Goa’s merger with Maharashtra, and later modern scholarship by Alan Machado Prabhu, Dale Luis Menezes, Panduranga Pissurlencar, Angela Barreto and others, which reveals the complexity of Konkani migration to coastal Karnataka. Archival evidence further challenges the novels’ linear narrative of displacement by examining the role of local elites and their collaboration with Portuguese structures. The paper questions whether migration can be explained simply through persecution and flight and argues that the term “historical novel” becomes problematic when literary memory is treated as historical fact, rather than as a selective reconstruction of the past.

title: Plant stress memory: epigenetic mechanisms for abiotic stress acclimation
container-title: Frontiers in Genetics
30a2e887c9601fc60452da8e50389327b3cf2aeb.abstract: Plants, being sessile organisms, have to endure unfavourable environmental conditions, thus they have developed exceptionally refined molecular systems that can sense, react and even recall stress signals. Stress memory, the ability to store information about previous stress treatments for faster and stronger reactions in the case of new exposures, is an indispensable adaptive mechanism that not only increases plant survival but also their overall fitness. Over the past few years, a considerable amount of evidence has been indicating the significance of epigenetic control in both the formation and the sustainability of stress memory, especially in the case of abiotic stress. This article presents an overview of the latest development on the epigenetic origin of plant stress memory with a focus on the mechanisms that play key role in the acclimatization to abiotic stress. The various molecular layers that are involved in the formation of stress memory viz. DNA methylation, chromatin remodelling, modifications of histones at post-translational level and the regulatory activities of non-coding RNAs have been elaborated. The stress specific epigenetic reactions due to abiotic stresses have been discussed to uncover regulatory attributes. Moreover, the review discusses the merging of cutting-edge technologies such as multi-omics tactics, the CRISPR/dCas9-targeted epigenome editing and machine learning solutions, with the aim of developing stress tolerant and high yielding crops. Despite the substantial progress made in identifying key epigenetic components, the major hurdles exist such as causal relationships being unclear, transgenerational stress memory over multiple generations being stable over time and eventually converting lab results into practical use in agriculture.

aa0caa61ee454ae3b74aeaf49db7be253dbb26a0.abstract: Objectives This study aimed to investigate the effects of two different doses of berberine (BER; 50 and 100 mg L -1 ) on caffeine (CAF; 50 mg L -1 )-induced anxiety-like behaviors and cognitive dysfunction in adult zebrafish ( Danio rerio ). Material and Methods Adult male Danio rerio were divided into 5 groups: control (CTRL), CAF (CAF, 50 mg L -1 ), BER (BER,100 mg L -1 ), (CAF+BER 50), & (CAF+BER100). Fish were exposed to CAF, BER, or their combination for 14 days. Behavioral assays were evaluated as Novel Tank Diving (NTD), Open Field (OF), Light-Dark Preference (LDP), Boldness Assay (BA), Novel Object Recognition (NOR), & T-maze (TM). Results The co-treatment significantly reduced anxiety-like behaviors, boosted exploration as well as boldness, and enhanced cognitive function in a dose-dependent manner, with 100 mg L -1 resulting in higher recovery to CTRL group than BER50. Conclusion BER demonstrated anxiolytic, neuroprotective, and cognitive-enhancing effects, effectively mitigating CAF-induced neurobehavioral impairments. These results highlight its therapeutic potential and support the use of zebrafish as a model in neurobehavioral pharmacology.

title: Why Groundwater Systems Remember the Past Through Hydrogeological Memory, Legacy Effects, and Delayed Environmental Consequences
b047730ff7403345aaf72a1b0918de3361c83cdb.abstract: Abstract Groundwater systems frequently continue responding long after the original disturbance has ceased. Groundwater recovery is therefore often assumed to represent environmental recovery; however, hydraulic recovery, contaminant persistence, groundwater connectivity, and receptor exposure commonly operate on different timescales. As a result, environmental risks may remain active despite apparent groundwater-system recovery. This phenomenon is referred to here as groundwater memory and is expressed through delayed hydrogeological responses, persistent connectivity, contaminant migration, and long-term environmental consequence. This paper examines the concepts of groundwater memory, hydrogeological lag, and groundwater legacy, and develops a framework for understanding delayed groundwater-system behaviour. The study integrates groundwater recovery, groundwater budgets, groundwater connectivity, travel-time behaviour, contaminant persistence, receptor exposure, and environmental consequence. Practical examples from mine closure, groundwater contamination, and recharge propagation are used to demonstrate how hydrogeological responses can continue for decades or longer after the initiating disturbance has disappeared. The results show that groundwater recovery should not be interpreted as evidence of environmental recovery. Instead, environmental consequence depends on the interaction between groundwater storage, migration pathways, connectivity, contaminant persistence, and receptor sensitivity. A practical groundwater-memory framework is proposed to improve long-term groundwater assessment, closure planning, environmental risk evaluation, and sustainable groundwater management.

title: Memory-Efficient Deep-Learning-Matching Full Waveform Inversion for Field-Scale Datasets
container-title: Geophysical Journal International
a2ec095dcf7ea40d401cd7a68c07a7819592150c.abstract: Summary Classical full waveform inversion (FWI) is sensitive to kinematic inaccuracies in the initial velocity model, converging to local minima due to cycle skipping when low-frequency data are absent. The recently developed deep-learning-matching FWI (DLM-FWI) framework mitigates this by dynamically bridging the phase gap between synthetic and observed data, utilizing a convolutional neural network (CNN) within the inversion loop as a robust kinematic preconditioner. However, because standard deep learning (DL) automatic differentiation (AD) engines scale poorly to large-scale wave equations, deploying DLM-FWI on practical field-scale data has been computationally prohibitive. To overcome this, we introduce a memory-efficient, hybrid computational workflow that interfaces the Flux machine-learning ecosystem with the Julia Devito Inversion framework (JUDI) finite-difference library. By decoupling the network’s AD graph from the physical solver and evaluating the chain rule strictly in the data domain, we avoid storing massive spatiotemporal wavefield histories. After verifying that this decoupled architecture maintains resilience to source-wavelet mismatch and ambient noise on the Marmousi2 synthetic model, we apply the workflow to the Mobil AVO Viking Graben Line 12 marine dataset to evaluate its practical scalability. Compared to classical L-BFGS FWI, the field-scale DLM-FWI results exhibit robust convergence, mitigation of shallow cycle-skipped artifacts, and geologically coherent structural continuity. This study addresses the gap between small-scale synthetic DL studies and field-scale 2D implementations, demonstrating that physics-guided matching strategies can be deployed in practice to improve FWI robustness on complex field datasets.
