title: Dissociable Effects of Sleep and Memory Suppression on Emotional Memory Processing
36748a138f842f5955634c455a86ffe2951ad488.abstract: The ability to retrieve memories of adverse events without fully reinstating their associated emotional charge is a hallmark of an adaptive memory system. This decoupling of emotional reactivity from episodic memory has been linked to two key processes: memory suppression during wakefulness and memory consolidation during sleep. Yet, the combined influences of wakeful suppression and sleep-associated memory processing on emotional affect during retrieval are unknown. We sought to address this gap in the current study. Participants learned to associate images of faces with emotionally negative and neutral scenes and then either suppressed or retrieved the scenes when presented with the faces as reminder cues. They then took a nap monitored with polysomnography (nap group) or remained awake for an equivalent period of time in the laboratory (wake group). Before and after the delay, emotional responses to the negative and neutral scenes were evaluated using self-report, skin conductance responses (SCRs) and heart rate deceleration (HRD) to index changes in emotional affect that were attributable to memory suppression and/or sleep-associated consolidation. Memory suppression had no impact on self-reported emotion, SCRs or HRD in either the nap or wake group. However, subjective emotional responses decreased significantly more after sleep than wake. These findings support a role for sleep-associated consolidation in reducing the affective salience of emotional memories.

title: Sideband-mediated nuclear-spin-wave memory for an Andreev spin qubit: required coherence and Floquet feasibility
container-title: Quantum Science and Technology
b8571dcdbd0d4f0a08b5bac64783d113bb81cfbc.abstract: Abstract A Floquet-driven red-sideband architecture is proposed and quantitatively analyzed that couples an Andreev spin qubit (ASQ) in a semiconductor Josephson junction to a collective nuclear spin-wave bright mode of the host, establishing a parameterized feasibility map and actionable design criteria for an ASQ–nuclear-spin quantum memory. The frequency-modulated exchange bridges the GHz ASQ transition and the MHz nuclear&#xD;Larmor frequency with effective coupling g eff = g mg J 1 (β), where β = Ω d /ω d is the modulation index. An analytical model of a single-isotope 75 As (I = 3/2) bright-mode envelope with N eff = 10 5 –10 6 nuclei gives g eff /2π in the 9–367 kHz range for two explicit parameter sets, with SWAP times of 0.7–28 μs. A next-order Floquet expansion identifies, within the single-circular-component limit g− ≪ g+, the n = 0 Jaynes–Cummings dispersive dressing as the dominant off-resonant contribution, decomposing into a static (β = 0) component δ static ≃ 2g 2 mg /ω d and a drive-induced increment δ AC ≃ −g 2 mg β 2 /ω d that are distinguishable by modulation-on/off spectroscopy combined with an independent bare-reference calibration. A diagnostic M≡ 2π(g eff /2π)T 2,ASQ = 1 requires T 2,ASQ ∼ 0.4–17 μs, while a high-fidelity write–read cycle (FWR ≳ 0.9, M≳ 30) requires T 2,ASQ ∼ 13–520 μs. A two-mode stroboscopic Lindblad simulation independently reproduces the M≳ 30 crossover at fixed g eff /(2π) = 100 kHz and shows the direct counter-rotating g− contribution is sub-percent at the baseline resolved-sideband point (ε − = g −,eff /(2ω n ) = 0.025), while worst-case g − /g + = 1 at the optimistic coupling produces a 2.3-percentage-point penalty. Currently demonstrated T 2,ASQ ∼ 10–100 ns lie two to five orders of magnitude below the M≳ 30 regime; the analysis identifies sweet-spot operation, phase-bias engineering, and Floquet-dressed subspace protection as concrete engineering directions to close the gap.

title: Evaluating the Effectiveness of Songs-Based Recall Strategies Correlated with Short-Term Memory Retention of Mind Rubrics of Repertory in 1st Year BHMS Students
container-title: Adolescência e Saúde
515ea4b295a8d9aa1dafb52a553a44538cc88e53.abstract: Background: Effective learning and retention of Mind rubrics are important in homoeopathic education. First-year BHMS students may experience difficulty recalling abstract repertorial concepts when taught through conventional lecture-based methods. Song-based recall strategies using rhythm, repetition, and emotional association may provide an engaging alternative teaching approach. Aim: To evaluate the effectiveness of song-based recall strategies in improving short-term memory retention of Mind rubrics of Repertory among first-year BHMS students compared with conventional lecture-based teaching. Materials and Methods: An interventional, comparative educational study using a pre-test and post-test design was conducted among first-year BHMS students at Ashokrao Mane Homoeopathic Medical College and Hospital, Peth Vadgaon, Maharashtra. A total of 100 students were enrolled and divided into two groups according to roll numbers. Group A received song-based teaching, whereas Group B received conventional lecture-based teaching. A common multiple-choice questionnaire based on 10 selected Mind rubrics from Kent’s Repertory was administered before and after the respective teaching interventions. Pre-test and post-test scores were analyzed to compare the teaching methods. A crossover session was subsequently conducted solely to ensure equitable exposure to both teaching methods; it was not included in the comparative outcome analysis. Student feedback was collected to assess engagement, interest, and perceived recall. Results: Data from 44 students in Group A and 39 students in Group B were included in the analysis. The mean score in Group A increased from 5.84 to 7.50, a mean improvement of 1.66 marks. In Group B, the mean score increased from 5.95 to 6.56, a mean improvement of 0.61 marks. The reported within-group improvements were statistically significant (Group A: p < 0.001; Group B: p = 0.021). The difference in mean improvement between groups was reported as statistically significant (p = 0.0049). Feedback was received from 98 students, with the majority reporting greater interest, engagement, and recall with song-based learning. Conclusion: Song-based recall strategies demonstrated greater improvement in post-test scores than conventional lecture-based teaching in this study. The crossover session ensured that all participating students had an opportunity to experience both teaching methods, while comparative analysis focused on the initial teaching interventions. Song-based learning may be a useful adjunct to conventional teaching for learning Mind rubrics in homoeopathic education. Further studies with larger samples and delayed retention assessments are recommended.

title: Hearing Loss, Not Tinnitus, Predicts Cognitive Performance in Hispanic/Latino Adults
container-title: American Journal of Audiology
a210e86863a80dd33a6408eafefcb11c212ca584.abstract: Purpose: Despite growing evidence linking sensory impairment and cognition, the role of tinnitus in cognitive aging remains unclear, particularly in Hispanic/Latino adults who have been historically underrepresented in this research. Our goal was to examine the associations among tinnitus, hearing loss, and cognitive performance in a large cohort of Hispanic/Latino adults and to determine whether tinnitus contributes additional cognitive risk beyond that associated with hearing loss. Method: This cross-sectional study used data from the publicly available Study of Latinos cohort, which includes audiometric assessments, tinnitus history, sociodemographic information, and cognitive testing for 12,647 participants aged 45–75 years from San Diego, Chicago, Miami, and the Bronx. After applying the inclusion criteria and excluding participants with missing data, the final analytic sample comprised 6,536 adults. Multivariable generalized linear models were used to evaluate the independent and interactive associations of tinnitus and hearing loss with global and domain-specific cognitive performance, adjusting for demographic and health-related covariates. Results: Hearing loss was independently associated with a lower global cognitive score, even after adjusting for demographic and health factors (Cohen's d ≈ −0.12, p < .001), a modest but statistically meaningful effect at the population level. In domain-specific analyses of cognition, hearing loss was selectively associated with poorer episodic memory performance (Cohen's d ≈ 0.063, p = .017), reflecting a small effect, but was not associated with verbal learning, executive control, or working memory. Tinnitus showed no independent association, nor did the interaction of hearing loss with tinnitus. Conclusion: Our findings underscore hearing loss as an important correlate of cognitive health in aging Hispanic/Latino adults and indicate that comorbid tinnitus does not add to the cognitive risk posed by hearing loss. Supplemental Material: https://doi.org/10.23641/asha.34845576

title: Agreement and Bias in ChatGPT-Assisted Grading of Undergraduate Nursing Examinations: A Method-Comparison Study
container-title: Nurse Educator
168e5a0c58e5adc3873f9ffc010d7bcab8db9adb.abstract: Background: Agreement between ChatGPT-assisted and faculty grading of nursing examinations remains uncertain. Purpose: To compare ChatGPT-assisted and faculty grading across item types and examine bias, repeatability, pass–fail classification, and major scoring discrepancies. Methods: We analyzed 506 undergraduate nursing examinations using paired comparisons, intraclass correlation coefficients, error measures, and Bland–Altman analysis. Multiple-choice repeatability and 150 constructed-response scoring units with major overestimations were also examined. Results: Multiple-choice grading showed minimal bias (−0.05 points) and excellent agreement with faculty grading (intraclass correlation coefficient = 0.949). ChatGPT overestimated the constructed-response subtotal and total scores by 7.48 and 7.43 points. Of the 59 examinations with faculty total scores below the institutional passing threshold of 60 points, ChatGPT classified 40 as passing. Major overestimations mainly reflected insufficient deductions and over-crediting of generalized or rubric-external content. Conclusions: ChatGPT showed high agreement for fixed-key multiple-choice scoring but systematically overestimated constructed-response scores. Faculty review remains necessary for consequential assessment decisions.

title: The Role of ChatGPT in English Language Learning: A Review of Recent Research
container-title: International Journal of Transformative Multidisciplinary Studies
d464745c5ba89524e84f6f68168f54b21632fa75.abstract: This narrative review synthesizes research on ChatGPT and English language learning published from November 2022 through the review’s stated early-2025 window. Google Scholar, Scopus, and Web of Science were the named search sources, but the original search log did not preserve database-level record totals, duplicate counts, the exact final search date, or stage-by-stage exclusion counts; these historical details cannot be reconstructed and no counts have been estimated. The core synthesis includes eight ChatGPT-specific primary studies and the directly relevant systematic review by Lo et al. (2024). Zhai et al. (2024), a broader systematic review of AI dialogue systems, and Fathi et al. (2024), which studied the Andy English Chatbot rather than ChatGPT, are used only as contextual sources and are not counted as direct ChatGPT-specific primary evidence. Full-text verification confirmed that Algaraady and Mahyoob (2023) is an empirical error-analysis study of 88 student texts, but it did not measure learner gains. Two studies published later in 2025 (Alnemrat et al., 2025; Behforouz et al., 2025) were checked to resolve the editor’s query and excluded from the core synthesis because they fall after the stated early-2025 window. No formal quality-appraisal instrument was applied; evidence judgments are provisional author assessments. The review examines writing, vocabulary and grammar, learner perceptions, and reported risks, while identifying a lack of eligible ChatGPT-specific speaking and listening evidence.

title: Transcranial pulse stimulation in the treatment of cognitive disorders of aging: a systematic review
container-title: Frontiers in Psychiatry
9c5b73b262db575980f749c4d19ab426e670a8ab.abstract: Introduction Non-invasive brain stimulation techniques, specifically transcranial pulse stimulation (TPS) are of increasing interest due to their potential to fill in gaps left by current pharmacological treatments in cognitive disorders of aging. The current review’s aims were to systematically determine what cognitive disorders of aging have been studied with TPS as a treatment and to narratively summarize what is known about the effectiveness of TPS treatment in the aging subpopulation through neurocognitive performance metrics and neuroimaging metrics. Methods This review is PRISMA 2020 compliant. Searches were conducted in PubMed, PsycINFO (through PsycNET to include all APA Databases), Embase, and Scopus. Title/Abstract screening, full text screening, and extraction were completed by two independent reviewers with discrepancies worked out through discussion. Outcomes were systematically chosen for formal analysis where dual reviewers completed risk of bias and certainty of evidence assessments, and remaining outcomes were synthesized narratively. Results 11 studies were included, consisting of 10 nonrandomized studies and 1 randomized controlled trial (RCT). Due to follow ups and suspected cohort overlap, the 11 studies are not representative of 11 independent patient cohorts. Included studies examined Alzheimer’s Disease and related dementias, mild neurocognitive disorder, mild cognitive impairment and Parkinson’s Disease through a variety of neurocognitive performance metrics and neuroimaging metrics. Formal synthesis showed a preliminary trend for positive change from before to after stimulation, particularly in neuropsychological batteries measuring global cognition, however number of contributing results and overall certainty of evidence were both very low. Neuroimaging results varied with trends of statistically significant functional changes, though also limited by limited literature and low certainty. Discussion Though there is a continued need for high quality research and randomized controlled trials using TPS in the treatment of neurocognitive disorders of aging, the current evidence indicates potential for promising changes in neurocognitive performance metric outcomes and functional neuroimaging measures from before to after stimulation pending additional controlled trials. Though there is currently not enough high quality evidence to support clinical recommendations, what is known could support the use of TPS in the treatment of neurocognitive disorders of aging should RCTs continue to support positive improvements associated with this non-invasive intervention. Systematic review registration https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/ , identifier CRD420251246424.

title: Rapid, accurate and memory-frugal sub-gene-level quantification of probe-based, multiplexed single-cell data
5aa71de4b6b9e4f381bf9cdce094c943778a3c0e.abstract: Probe-based, multiplexed single-cell assays enable accurate transcriptome profiling while processing multiple samples in parallel. Their predefined probe sequences and additional sample barcodes introduce computational requirements that differ from those of poly(A)-based assays, for which many existing single-cell quantification tools were developed. We extend simpleaf to enable efficient demultiplexing and quantification of probe-based single-cell libraries. A new, cache-friendly dictionary specializes lookup to small probe references, while a shared thread budget balances parallel decompression and mapping. We extend RAD and downstream tools with reusable sample-scoped correction plans and external-memory collation of hierarchically barcoded data, retaining probe identities through quantification to enable rapid mapping and quantification with a small working memory budget. Across five 10x Genomics Flex datasets comprising 44 samples, simpleaf had the shortest runtime and lowest peak memory use of the three tools on every library, while producing gene-expression estimates, cell clusters, and marker genes concordant with cyto and Cell Ranger . Compared with cyto , simpleaf was on average 2 times faster and used approximately one-thirteenth as much memory. simpleaf also exports probe-level quantification results, allowing a range of analyses at sub-gene resolution. Here, we show that individual probe counts reveal expression changes obscured by gene-level aggregation, identify the transcript groups contributing to gene-level changes, and provide insight into splicing dynamics across cell types. These results demonstrate the computational and biological value of retaining probe-level information in multiplexed single-cell analysis.

title: Cognitive-Inspired Recognition of Traditional Chinese Pleated Clothing Using Dual Visual Features
container-title: International Journal of Cognitive Informatics and Natural Intelligence
84a561920da75f75d5173859d5efcb3ba3a7bb25.abstract: Traditional Chinese pleated clothing carries rich cultural meaning; however, its digital preservation has been challenged by labor-intensive manual annotation and limited generalization of existing computer-vision models. This study proposed a dual-visual-feature framework for pleat recognition by integrating global shape features and local pleat details. Based on a custom-built dataset of real-world Chinese traditional clothing images, the framework combined preprocessing, dual-feature extraction, dynamic fusion, and vision transformer base with 16 × 16 patch size and a multi-layer perceptron classification head for multilabel classification. Experimental results demonstrated effective recognition of traditional clothing pleats, including subtle hidden pleat structures. Visual attention heatmaps enhanced the model's interpretability, providing technical support for the digital documentation and preservation of traditional garments.

title: Associations of internet use and specific patterns with cognitive function in older adults: a systematic review and meta-analysis
container-title: Frontiers in Public Health
b3b8bae93b3899292851dd401373cd1b5ab28547.abstract: Background Global aging is accompanied by cognitive decline. While the “technological reserve” hypothesis suggests internet use may mitigate this, prior meta-analyses have not clarified the specific effects of different usage patterns. This study aims to systematically evaluate associations between distinct dimensions of internet use and cognitive function in older adults. Methods Conducted in accordance with PRISMA 2020 guidelines, we searched PubMed, Embase, CINAHL, PsycINFO, and Web of Science from inception to March 15, 2026. Two Reviewers independently extracted data. Pooled Odds Ratios (ORs) or Hazard Ratios (HRs) served as primary effect measures; Correlation coefficients ( r ) or standardized beta coefficients (β) were converted into unified OR-scale estimates for meta-analysis, acknowledging inherent limitations introduced by combining mixed effect measures from original studies. Results Thirty-one studies comprising 158,648 participants (cross-sectional and longitudinal observational designs) were included. The random-effects meta-analysis of 25 studies yielded a pooled OR of 1.49 (95% CI: 1.31–1.70), indicating general internet use was significantly associated with better cognitive function ( z = 5.97, P &lt; 0.001 ). Substantial heterogeneity was observed ( I 2 = 99.51%). A 95% prediction interval (1.15–1.93) was further calculated to quantify uncertainty. Subgroup analyses showed significant positive associations for social ( OR = 1.55), entertainment ( OR = 1.46), and instrumental use ( OR = 1.38). However, meta-regression revealed no statistically significant differences among these categories ( F (2, 24) = 0.36, P = 0.63). Sensitivity analysis excluding outliers yielded a similar pooled point estimate, although substantial heterogeneity persisted. (pooled OR = 1.46, 95% CI: 1.29–1.67). Conclusions Internet use was positively associated with better cognitive function among older adults. This positive association was observed across social, entertainment, and instrumental internet use patterns. Given high between study heterogeneity and the observational nature of available evidence, further longitudinal and interventional research is needed to clarify whether diverse digital engagement may support healthy cognitive aging. Systematic review registration https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/recorddashboard , identifier: CRD420261359423.

title: Adaptive Metacognition in AI: From Monitoring to Learned Control
container-title: Proceedings of the AAAI Symposium Series
82d24899a6dd659fcbe55f68bad6e7e172c56d3d.abstract: Current AI systems possess limited metacognitive capabilities such as confidence estimation, error detection, and self-critique. These capabilities often remain fragmented rather than integrated into adaptive control. As a result, systems may persist with ineffective strategies or waste resources on additional reasoning that is unlikely to help. To bridge this gap, this paper proposes an architecture that links internal monitoring with learned control. Drawing on human metacognition and computational cognitive architectures, the architecture integrates cues related to fluency, conflict, and progress into signals that guide decisions about whether to persist, switch strategies, verify an answer, seek information, or stop. Outcome feedback allows the system to learn which cue-control mappings improve performance in different contexts relative to their costs. With practice, these mappings could support faster, less demanding control. This framework connects internal processing cues, metacognitive monitoring, control decisions, and learning to provide a more integrated account of adaptive metacognition in AI.

title: From Impasse to Adaptation: An Integrated LLM Supporting Meta-Cognition in a Cognitive Architecture
container-title: Proceedings of the AAAI Symposium Series
e48629df3cb8e6f6911f96c05eb6d7e6f87048e3.abstract: Autonomous cognitive systems deployed in real-world settings will inevitably encounter unknown and novel scenarios that require knowledge acquisition through exploration, adaptation, and recovery. We argue that successfully navigating such scenarios will require meta-cognition and that meta-cognitive capabilities can be realized in a cognitive architecture by integrating a large language model (LLM) as the engine for generating potential solutions when the agent encounters impasses during task performance that its regular planning and reasoning capabilities cannot solve. We propose a particular such integration that is focused on enabling three meta-cognitive capacities: performance prediction, model introspection, and corrective replanning. We provide a proof-of-concept demonstration of the operation of the integrated architecture on an autonomous robot, showing how it can solve a problem that it would otherwise not have been able to tackle.

title: Metadata for Metacognition: Supporting Self-Regulation Capabilities in Soar
container-title: Proceedings of the AAAI Symposium Series
85ca775c5dfc1bf103574b489678ee86053f44d2.abstract: Metacognition, the ability to represent, monitor, and modulate cognitive processing, is realized in the Soar cognitive architecture through the interaction of metadata and standard architecture mechanisms for reasoning, now applied to reasoning (metareasoning). To explore enabling the wider range of self-regulatory metacognitive capabilities reported in humans, we examine what metadata is required and the current support (or lack thereof) in Soar for this metadata. We propose an approach where metadata is produced by appraisal processes that evaluate agent state in the context of current tasking. We present an initial investigation, where we implement a limited set of appraisals that signal agent progress (or lack thereof) in a troubleshooting domain, facilitating agent strategy change when it is unable to make progress.

title: Explaining Cognition and Communication in Cognitive Robots
container-title: Proceedings of the AAAI Symposium Series
f17a38f8d378259b3283861ed3dc486bdf913d01.abstract: Cognitive robots of the class called LEIAs can explain their cognition and action using a language generation process that is, itself, explainable. This transparency contrasts sharply with the opaque operation of systems whose cognition relies on language models. This paper describes recent advances in the neurosymbolic modeling of LEIAs at the intersection of metacognition, language generation, and social agency. It answers the question: How can we prepare robots to produce the kinds of explanations that people will want using the most generalizable, best-engineered, scalable solutions? We argue that the symbolic modeling of cognition, including the process of language generation itself, is both realistic and scalable when guided by strong methodology, clear objectives, and the support of modern technology — including language models, but used only for carefully selected tasks that are resistant to hallucinations.

title: Fatigue-Resistant Post-Training: Mitigating Cognitive Fatigue in Autoregressive Transformers via FI-Guided Optimization
container-title: Proceedings of the AAAI Symposium Series
8750dec09e0bb49efa32bbf2f2ec58a668970df8.abstract: Autoregressive language models frequently degrade during long-horizon generation producing repetitive text, loosing instruction adherence, and exhibiting unstable entropy. We formalize this as Cognitive Fatigue and introduce the Fatigue Index (FI), an online diagnostic aggregating attention decay, entropy miscalibration, and representational drift. We study whether resistance to this degradation can be induced before generation through FI-guided post-training. FI is used as an auxiliary signal rather than a standalone objective, since directly optimizing an imperfect diagnostic may encourage proxy optimization without improving generation quality. We apply FI conditioning across supervised fine-tuning (SFT), and reinforcement learning (FI-GRPO, FI-DAPO) via LoRA adapters, pairing every FI-conditioned configuration against a FI-ablated twin. We evaluate six untrained open models from three architectural families and two parameter scales per family, then conduct post-training experiments on the three small-scale checkpoints across three task tiers. GRPO on Granite-3.1-2B shows accuracy gains alongside delayed fatigue onset and reduced repetition, demonstrating feasibility. However, improvements frequently decouple from task accuracy. These results indicate that FI can provide useful training signal in specific settings, but must be evaluated jointly with task quality rather than treated as a universally reliable objective.

title: Metacognition and Cognitive Transparency for Trustworthy Human-Robot Teams
container-title: Proceedings of the AAAI Symposium Series
684d6a6b791585a43491946dcc649d04ea8dc236.abstract: Effective human-robot teaming in safety-critical, risk-averse contexts benefits from more than tactical proficiency. It is supported by metacognition and cognitive transparency, which allow robotic teammates to recognize gaps in their own knowledge, assess whether their current understanding is sufficient to act, and expose their reasoning to human partners. We present an architectural approach to these capabilities and demonstrate them in a functioning system built on HARMONIC, a dual-layer architecture that integrates the OntoAgent cognitive architecture with reactive tactical control. We evaluate the system through a simulated collaborative search task involving two heterogeneous robots and a human operator. A controlled comparison with six large language models (LLMs) in the same strategic role, using identical tactical infrastructure and a prompt that did not enumerate plan preconditions, shows that metacognitive self-assessment, the most critical of these capabilities, was absent in 27 of 30 LLM trials, with models acting on incomplete information and hallucinating details rather than detecting knowledge gaps. High LLM task success often co-occurred with malformed or hallucinated action commands that were caught by the tactical layer's validation and fallback behaviors, showing both the risk of statistical planners and the value of architecturally enforced guardrails. These results suggest that metacognitive self-assessment and hallucination-free reasoning in collaborative human-robot teams are more readily supported by knowledge-grounded cognitive architectures, which provide them by design, than by language model scale alone.

title: Persistent hippocampal traces of lifelong spatial memory
1e2173391b8cc2a913d41f309327f5af56536260.abstract: ABSTRACT Memory presents a biological paradox: the brain changes continuously, yet a brief experience can influence behavior for a lifetime. How such memories are stored in brain circuits remains unclear. Here we show that two days in a binary-tree maze leave mice with spatial memories that survive repeated 90-day absences over as much as a year. Across return visits, mice explored the maze more efficiently than when naive and resumed direct runs to a reward location sooner, both by a factor of 3. Chronic calcium imaging of the same hippocampal CA1 neurons showed that although most neurons had changed their preferred locations, the population activity at a given maze location still resembled the pattern from 90 days earlier. Furthermore, even when a neuron’s place fields changed location, they tended to remain at the same branching level of the binary tree, reflecting the local geometry of the maze. In return sessions where the neural tuning for branching level was preserved more accurately, the mouse explored the environment more efficiently. Population patterns were best preserved near the reward location, and more reliable neural activity there accompanied earlier direct runs to the reward. With repeated experience, spatial representations changed less, both within a visit and across the long absences. A brief experience thus left selective hippocampal traces that survived months of absence despite drift, grew more durable with each return, and were correlated with memory in navigation behavior.

title: Integrating a self-guided cognitive behavioral therapy app (CONEMO) into Brazilian primary health care: protocol for a hybrid type III implementation-effectiveness study
700815932509f71ef32987524ba1b08dbba38d19.abstract: Background: Depression and anxiety are common and disabling mental health conditions. Although cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) is an evidence-based treatment, access remains limited, particularly in low- and middle-income countries. Internet-delivered CBT (iCBT) may expand access to psychological interventions, but integrating digital interventions into routine primary care remains challenging. This study protocol describes the implementation of CONEMO (Emotional Control), a self-guided iCBT app for depression and anxiety symptoms, in primary care units in 2 municipalities in Brazil. Methods: This mixed-methods hybrid type III implementation-effectiveness study is being conducted in primary care units in Indaiatuba and Jaguariúna, São Paulo, Brazil. Adults screening positive for depression (Patient Health Questionnaire-9 score ≥10) or anxiety (Generalized Anxiety Disorder-7 score ≥10) are offered a six-week CONEMO app-based intervention supported by a WhatsApp chatbot and a monitoring dashboard for primary care professionals. Primary outcomes are implementation outcomes, including penetration, acceptability, feasibility, and safety, assessed using app usage data, self-report measures, and focus groups with users, health professionals, and managers. Secondary outcomes include changes in depression, anxiety, and insomnia symptoms, quality of life, and behavioral activation over 12 weeks. Quantitative data will be analyzed using mixed-effects models. No formal sample size calculation was performed because the intervention is offered to all eligible users in participating units. Discussion: Recruitment began in January 2026 and is expected to continue through December 2026. As of October 2026, approximately 400 participants had been enrolled, and the intervention was available in 21 primary care units across the 2 municipalities. Expansion to additional units in Jaguariúna is planned, with 28 units expected to participate. The study will generate evidence on the integration of a digital mental health intervention into routine primary care and identify barriers and facilitators to implementation and scale-up in Brazil. DECLARAÇÃO DE USO DE INTELIGÊNCIA ARTIFICIAL (IA): During the preparation of this work, the authors used Claude Haiku 5.5 (Anthropic), a generative artificial intelligence (AI) tool, to assist with organizing and formatting the references and revising the manuscript for adherence to the journal’s guidelines, including rewording sections. The authors reviewed and edited all AI-assisted content and take full responsibility for the content of the published article.

title: Interpreting Functional Connectivity in Alzheimer’s Disease as Cognitive Processes: Multinomial Processing Trees and the Common Model of Cognition
e1014e77e454a7fcf281356ebf6c6c4543b378e3.abstract: Abstract Cognitive process models and brain connectivity analyses both provide a higher resolution into what cognitive functions are engaged during cognitive tasks than traditional methods. However, the two methods are typically applied in isolation. Our goal is to combine them, and ask which impaired cognitive functions are associated with a specific connectivity signature. Participants were 1,127 participants from the Alzheimer’s Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI), of varying cognitive status at their last included time point: Cognitively Normal = 554, Mild Cognitive Impairment = 386, Alzheimer's Disease = 187. We combine Bayesian multinomial processing tree (MPT) cognitive modelling with resting-state functional connectivity analysis guided by the Common Model of Cognition. MPT modelling showed that Learned and Delayed Retrieval processes had the largest diagnostic differences (η² ≈ 0.40), while Short-term Retrieval was unaffected. MPT parameters were correlated with widespread brain connectivity changes. However, brain connectivity changes were collinear, and mostly attributable to the diagnostic group. The exception was the Delayed Retrieval process parameter, which was associated with functional connectivity between areas associated with Working Memory and areas associated with Long-Term Memory, even when corrected for all other parameters. Combining the two analyses allowed us to link a function defined at the neural level to a function defined at the behavioral level. This article describes the potential and current limits of joining the two classes of models.

title: La lectoescritura en la adquisición de habilidades cognitivas en estudiantes de Educación Básica
container-title: Revista Multidisciplinar de Estudios Generales
cc3acc963940a50246ffa50e05225c4786b58058.abstract: La lectoescritura constituye un proceso fundamental durante la Educación Inicial, debido a su relación con el desarrollo del lenguaje y con diferentes habilidades cognitivas necesarias para el aprendizaje. En este contexto, el presente estudio tuvo como objetivo analizar cómo las actividades significativas de lectoescritura incidieron en el desarrollo de las habilidades cognitivas de los niños de 3 a 5 años de la Unidad Educativa Fiscal “La Pradera”, ubicada en la ciudad de Manta, durante el período 2024-2025. Se desarrolló una investigación de enfoque cualitativo, bajo el paradigma interpretativo y con un diseño de investigación-acción. La población estudiada estuvo conformada por 49 niños, distribuidos en los grupos de 3 a 4 y de 4 a 5 años, además de dos docentes. Para la recolección de información se emplearon la observación, entrevistas a docentes y revisión documental de las planificaciones pedagógicas. Posteriormente, los datos fueron organizados mediante codificación y triangulación metodológica, considerando las habilidades de atención, memoria, lenguaje, planificación y creatividad. Los resultados iniciales evidenciaron dificultades principalmente en atención, memoria y lenguaje, asociadas con períodos cortos de concentración, dificultades para recordar secuencias e información y empleo de expresiones verbales simples. A partir de estos hallazgos se diseñaron actividades significativas de lectoescritura con carácter lúdico y creativo, adaptadas a las características y necesidades de cada grupo etario. Después de su implementación, se observó una evolución positiva en la atención sostenida, memoria secuencial, comprensión verbal y organización del pensamiento, acompañada de mayor participación y motivación infantil. Se concluyó que las actividades significativas de lectoescritura incidieron favorablemente en el desarrollo de las habilidades cognitivas, especialmente cuando fueron adaptadas al nivel de desarrollo, intereses y necesidades de los niños.

title: From effort intolerance to functional gain: double product and exercise response in heart failure rehabilitation
container-title: Advances in Rehabilitation
59817168de535f342cbc304e2d7fb7f89060fe13.abstract: Abstract Introduction Heart failure (HF) is associated with exercise intolerance, functional decline and frequent hospitalization. Although cardiac rehabilitation (CR) improves functional capacity, the double product (DP) remains a relevant marker of hemodynamic response. Methods This retrospective observational study included 79 patients older than 60 years with HF, who completed an outpatient CR program between 2017 and 2023. Functional capacity was assessed with the 6-minute walk test (6MWT) at baseline and after Phase IV, including distance walked, estimated VO 2 and metabolic equivalents (METs). DP and the rating of perceived exertion (RPE) were assessed during sessions across Phases II–IV. Baseline and final 6MWT changes were analyzed using the Wilcoxon signed-rank test, and DP with repeated-measures analysis of variance. Results Most participants were male (63.3%) and had a high comorbidity burden, mainly hypertension (62%), coronary heart disease (57%) and sedentary lifestyle (55.7%). Significant improvements were observed between baseline and final 6MWT assessments: distance increased from 419 m to 523 m, estimated VO 2 from 10.5 mL/kg/minute to 12.2 mL/kg/minute and METs from 3.0 to 3.5 ( p < 0.001). RPE increased slightly from 11 to 12 ( p = 0.003). DP showed no overall differences across phases ( p = 0.600), but significant effects of time and phase-by-time interaction were found (both p < 0.001). No significant change was observed in Phase II, whereas significant increases occurred in Phases III and IV. Conclusion CR was associated with improved functional capacity in patients with HF. DP changes varied across phases and may help monitor exercise response. Controlled prospective studies are needed to confirm causality.

title: Redundancy maximization as a principle of associative memory learning in Hopfield networks
container-title: Nature Communications
18f5fe76673008b382ce6a0f279473e585bd59c6.abstract: Abstract Associative memory, traditionally modeled by Hopfield networks, enables the retrieval of previously stored patterns from partial or noisy cues. Yet, the local computational principles which are required to enable this function remain incompletely understood. To formally characterize the local information processing in such systems, we employ a recent extension of information theory—Partial Information Decomposition. It decomposes the contribution of different inputs to an output into unique information from each input, redundant information across inputs, and synergistic information that emerges from combining different inputs. Applying this framework to individual neurons in classical Hopfield networks we find that below the memory capacity, the information in a neuron’s activity is characterized by high redundancy between the external pattern input and the internal recurrent input, while synergy and unique information are close to zero until the memory capacity is surpassed and performance drops steeply. Inspired by this observation, we use redundancy maximization at each neuron as an information-theoretic learning goal. This increases the network’s memory capacity to 1.59, a more than tenfold improvement over the 0.14 capacity of classical Hopfield networks, and also outperforming recent state-of-the-art implementations of Hopfield networks. Overall, this work establishes redundancy maximization as a design principle for associative memories and opens pathways for new associative memory models based on information-theoretic goals.

title: A Bi-Factor Generalized Cognitive Diagnosis Model Framework
73276ed773356b3c0f4753eb53f0692423107e7d.abstract: Cognitive diagnosis models (CDMs) are often applied to constructs that are largely unidimensional in nature (e.g., mathematics, reading, mental health status) where a set of discrete attributes coexists with a dominant general proficiency dimension. This article presents the bi-factor CDM model (BF-CDM), which partitions item responses into a direct effect of continuous general proficiency and a discrete attribute-mastery tier, allowing mastery classifications to be made beyond what is attributable to general ability. By modeling both tiers explicitly, the BF-CDM makes it possible to evaluate the contribution of the discrete tier itself. Specifically, it can show whether the hypothesized attributes carry diagnostic information beyond general proficiency, both through model comparison with the nested unidimensional model and through the reliability of the attribute-specific component. A simulation study manipulating sample size, test length, number of attributes, and attribute-tier discrimination shows accurate recovery of item and person parameters, and of the model-implied response functions. An application to reading comprehension data from PISA illustrates the practical value of the model: reliability of attribute-mastery classifications drops substantially once variance attributable to general proficiency is partialled out, indicating that much of the apparent diagnostic precision obtained under a saturated attribute structure reflects a single dominant general factor.

title: Hippocampal transformations occur along dimensions of memory interference
container-title: Nature Communications
f4d20f6a514f2e6b05b2a35c6795d6348907b0b2.abstract: Abstract The role of the hippocampus in resolving memory interference has been greatly elucidated by considering the relationship between the similarity of visual stimuli (input) and corresponding similarity of hippocampal activity patterns (output). However, these input-output functions can take surprisingly different forms. Here, we reconcile seemingly conflicting findings by considering the possibility that the hippocampus prioritizes different dimensions of visual similarity across different stages of learning. First, we generated a set of natural scene images from two visual categories and rigorously characterized visual similarity using a wide array of methods: neural networks, artificial intelligence models, and human perceptual and memory decisions. We then identified two orthogonal dimensions of visual similarity that each predicted memory interference, but that did so at distinct stages of learning. Using high-resolution fMRI, we then tested for dimension-specific input-output functions within the hippocampus. Within CA3 and dentate gyrus (CA3/DG), we show that dimensions of visual similarity were inverted (repulsion) at stages of learning when they contributed to memory interference. In contrast, CA3/DG preserved similarity when dimensions did not contribute to interference. These findings reveal that hippocampal representations of visually-similar stimuli are highly dynamic and critically depend on the dimensions of similarity that currently contribute to memory interference.

title: Customising ChatGPT for chemistry education: A domain-grounded chatbot to support pharmacy students in medicinal chemistry
container-title: Pharmacy Education
b51212e4ea59ac933a25c3df56226ba88aa5efe3.abstract: Background: This study develops and evaluates ChemIA, a course-specific GPT that supports pharmacy students in undergraduate Medicinal Chemistry. Customised with instructor-authored materials, it better matches the syllabus and reduces generic-model inaccuracies. Methods: The exploratory evaluation assessed technical performance and student perceptions. Technical performance was tested with 15 multiple-choice questions from course assessments. Across repeated interactions, ChemIA largely matched instructor-validated answers; discrepancies mainly involved information found only in images. It also handled a small set of questions based on English-translated materials. These findings indicate basic multilingual functionality in the tested conditions, not comprehensive multilingual capability. ChemIA supported course activities including quizzes, pre-class study, podcast-style content, and a pharmacological case study. Results: Survey responses indicated that students perceived ChemIA as useful for clarifying medicinal chemistry concepts, preparing for examinations, and obtaining supplementary explanations. Students also reported greater confidence in ChemIA’s responses than in those generated by a generic GPT model. In the case-study activity, students rated ChemIA's explanations more often as very clear than those from the non-custom model. Conclusion: These findings offer exploratory evidence that a domain-grounded GPT can complement Medicinal Chemistry education. Its simple setup and adaptability may support similar applications in other disciplines. However, findings are limited by the exploratory design and the absence of direct measures of learning or academic performance.

title: A spectral partial information decomposition framework for quantifying information about cognitive variables in oscillatory brain networks
container-title: The Journal of Neuroscience
5c53c35246e49994d2e9bc7d2f9af22e9c96af65.abstract: Neural oscillations are thought to play a central role in encoding and transmitting cognitive information across large-scale brain networks, yet the relative contributions of phase synchrony and amplitude co-modulations to distributed coding remain unclear. A key obstacle is the absence of tools that can simultaneously quantify task-relevant information in the frequency domain and disentangle its phase and amplitude co-modulation components across pairwise and higher order interactions. Here, we introduce a spectral partial information decomposition framework (NeOPID) for quantifying information about cognitive variables in amplitude co-modulation and phase contributions, and to quantify redundant and synergistic information in brain relations, from pairwise to higher-order interactions. We validated the approach on Kuramoto and Stuart- Landau oscillator networks, including a whole-brain model constrained by macaque anatomical connectivity. NeOPID accurately recovers ground-truth encoding schemes and reveals that phase relations and amplitude co-modulations act as complementary coding channels with both redundant and synergistic components. NeOPID further extends this decomposition to higher-order functional interactions enabling the characterization of how cognitive information is collectively distributed across multiple oscillatory edges via redundant and synergistic encoding. To illustrate biological applicability, we applied NeOPID to local field potentials (LFPs) recorded from the macaque fronto-parietal network during a working memory task. In this dataset, NeOPID identified beta-band amplitude co-modulations as the primary carrier of stimulus information, and revealed that higher-order phase interactions exhibit both redundant and synergistic structure during the memory delay. These results establish NeOPID as a principled tool for dissecting the informational architecture about cognitive processes of oscillatory brain networks. Significance Statement Understanding how the brain coordinates large-scale communication to support cognition remains a fundamental challenge in neuroscience. Characterizing the distinct roles of phase synchrony and amplitude co-modulation has been hindered by a lack of computational approaches capable of separating these components across pairwise and higher-order interactions. Here, we introduce NeOPID (neural spectral Partial Information Decomposition), a framework designed to isolate phase and amplitude co-modulation contributions and quantify redundant and synergistic information contained in pair-wise and higher order functional interactions. NeOPID was validated on simulated oscillator models and on macaque local field potentials (LFPs) during a working memory task. Overall, the results establish NeOPID as a principled tool for dissecting the informational architecture underlying cognitive processes in oscillatory brain networks.

title: Gaze reinstatement during working memory for natural scenes
container-title: The Journal of Neuroscience
437da6194905c78938be8fd3972d1ef60191f2aa.abstract: The information we hold in mind with working memory (WM) may propagate beyond the cortex and out to the peripheral motor system. For instance, directionally biased hand and eye movements can express simple visuo-spatial features during WM maintenance. If such sensorimotor inflections are a form of WM representation, they may also express more detailed and task-adaptive information about WM content. Here, we ask whether gaze patterns carry item-specific detail about complex stimuli held in mind, and whether gaze during WM maintenance adapts to upcoming behavioral demands. To do this, we tracked male and female human eye movements during WM for naturalistic images, and we manipulated which image properties were most task-relevant (visual or semantic). In two experiments, we found that the eyes moved in item-specific spatiotemporal sequences during WM maintenance. Delay period gaze patterns retraced the scanpaths from stimulus encoding, echoing the ‘gaze reinstatement’ that has been observed during long-term memory retrieval. Therefore, gaze patterns during WM may reinstate visual encoding processes for maintenance. We also used time-resolved representational similarity analyses, guided by convolutional neural network modeling, to test the specificity of WM gaze patterns across a trial. We found that gaze representations were more distinct when the task prioritized visual detail, and they also ramped up in anticipation of the WM probe. Therefore, oculomotor WM signals are malleable to when and how the content will be used. WM may recruit the most primary structures in sensorimotor processing, where eye movements reflect flexible and future-oriented WM content information. Significance Statement The eyes are an outwardly accessible extension of the brain. They filter sensory input and enact motor output, but may also offer a rich window into underlying cognition. For instance, pupil dilation can reflect changing cognitive load, and biased eye movements can reflect basic spatial information about content held in mind with working memory (WM). WM is a critical neuro-cognitive function, but its physiological bases remain under debate. Here, we show that during WM the eyes can move in intricate patterns that read out the complex, real-world stimuli held in mind. This work shows how cognitive states influence oculomotor functions, and also advances theories of WM maintenance to include the most basic structures in sensorimotor processing.

title: Shape-memory scaffold targets inflammation and fibrosis to restore endometrium and fertility in intrauterine adhesions
container-title: Science Advances
c38db6d2011383844e7a60f079cfff98d9e188c6.abstract: Intrauterine adhesion (IUA) is a major cause of infertility, yet current treatments remain limited in preventing fibrosis and restoring functional endometrium. We report a bi-drug, bifunctional, biodegradable shape-memory regenerative (BiSMR) scaffold enabling minimally invasive implantation, sequential drug release, and barrier protection. Proteomic profiling of chemical, mechanical, and combined injury models revealed inflammatory activation, extracellular matrix remodeling, and impaired regenerative programs, providing a molecular rationale for combining epigallocatechin gallate (EGCG) with 17β-estradiol (E 2 ). BiSMR couples an E 2 -loaded PLTG [poly( l -lactide)- co -trimethylene carbonate- co -glycolic acid] backbone with a PDA-EGCG@HAMA coating, enabling rapid EGCG release followed by sustained E 2 delivery. In vitro, BiSMR promoted cell proliferation, migration, angiogenesis, and M2 polarization while suppressing myofibroblast transition. In rat IUA models, BiSMR restored endometrial structure and vascularization, reduced fibrosis, and improved implantation and live birth rates. Proteomics revealed down-regulation of fibrosis- and inflammation-related effectors and restoration of protein biosynthesis and regenerative pathways. BiSMR offers a promising strategy for IUA therapy and fertility restoration.

title: Cognitive Offloading to Generative AI: A Theoretical Framework for Memory, Metacognition, and Consumer Decision-Making
e64673e133955f3e7d2b380a51bffc24e10189e0.abstract: As generative artificial intelligence (Gen-AI) increasingly mediates product search, evaluation, and choice, consumer cognition is becoming distributed across human–AI systems. This shift challenges a largely unexamined assumption in advertising theory: that persuasion operates through cognitive elaboration within the individual consumer. Drawing on cognitive offloading research from cognitive psychology, we develop the CogOffload framework to explain when consumers delegate cognitive work to Gen-AI and what consequences follow. A seven-stage delegation continuum maps increasing levels of offloading, and a value-based cost-benefit framework identifies its antecedents and the moderators that shape how consumers weigh them. We propose three clusters of outcomes. First, offloading weakens memory for brands and product attributes while strengthening memory for AI-generated summaries. Second, it inflates metacognitive self-esteem and decision confidence, producing AI-induced overconfidence that reduces further information-seeking. Third, effects on decision quality depend on AI reliability: when AI is unreliable, verifying AI recommendations imposes cognitive and emotional costs but can restore impaired memory and recalibrate inflated confidence. Seven propositions and three long-term conjectures extend these effects to consumer autonomy, competence erosion, and brand loyalty. Together, the CogOffload framework positions advertising in the era of Gen-AI as operating within a distributed system of human and artificial cognition.

title: Memory Overlap Shapes General and Specific Memory Differently in Adolescents and Adults
ebe70976ee255a6bc654635230a4a770608bf241.abstract: Over time we accumulate many interrelated memories which we draw upon to remember both generalities and specifics of our experience. While both aspects of memory improve through childhood, their maturation into adolescence remains poorly understood. Here, we compared how 39 adolescents (12-13 years old) and 36 adults managed differing levels of relatedness (“overlap”) among learned associations to remember shared (general) and unique (specific) features. Across age groups, greater overlap boosted memory for shared features but hindered memory for specifics. However, adolescents showed a reduced benefit of overlap for shared feature memory, suggesting they generalized across related memories differently than adults. Adolescents were also slower than adults to recognize unique features of highly overlapping memories, consistent with prolonged refinement of specific memory. Our results reveal continued maturation of both general and specific memory into adolescence while demonstrating how the overlaps among our experiences shape what we remember.

title: Educational attainment and Montreal Cognitive Assessment performance among adults in southern Ecuador
e3272a176718bb09808f2b65bd37a2a9fab3d2be.abstract: Abstract Objective To examine educational differences in Montreal Cognitive Assessment performance in a community health project in southern Ecuador. Results The analysis included 174 adults recruited by convenience sampling. Median raw scores were 19.0, 23.0, and 25.0 for primary, secondary, and higher education, respectively (Kruskal–Wallis H(2) = 36.65; p < 0.001). In linear regression with heteroscedasticity-consistent standard errors, primary education was associated with a 5.30-point lower score than higher education after adjustment for age and recorded gender (95% confidence interval − 7.22 to − 3.37). The corresponding difference for secondary education was − 1.83 points (− 3.68 to 0.02). Using the education correction recorded in the dataset, 137 of 174 participants (78.7%) scored below 26. The primary–higher difference persisted in sensitivity analyses, while the secondary–higher comparison varied across specifications. These findings support considering educational context when interpreting screening scores. They do not establish cognitive decline or the prevalence of clinically diagnosed cognitive impairment.

title: Contributions of ChatGPT Adoption and Academic Integrity to Learning Engagement among Undergraduates
be6b08c2f7809ee1f759f0dc9f41332cbed42a2e.abstract: Abstract This research work examined how the adoption of ChatGPT relates to learning engagement among undergraduates in public universities in Cross River State, Nigeria, namely, the University of Calabar, the University of Cross River, and the University of Education and Entrepreneurship, and whether self-regulated learning and academic integrity serially mediate this relationship. The study further compared the structural relationships across gender using multigroup analysis (MGA); a companion analysis of the same dataset examining age-group differences is reported in a separate paper. The study is grounded in theories of technology acceptance and self-regulated learning. Literature was reviewed based on the variables under study. The study adopted a cross-sectional survey design. The population of the study comprised 1,507 final-year undergraduate students. The sampling technique utilized for this research was proportionate stratified sampling. A serial mediation model was specified and tested on survey data from 452 undergraduates. Partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM) was estimated in Smart PLS. The instrument for data collection was a questionnaire titled “ChatGPT Adoption, Academic Integrity, and Learning Engagement” (CAAILEQ). The measurement model satisfied reliability, convergent, and discriminant validity standards. Analyses were conducted using SmartPLS 4. Results show that ChatGPT adoption positively predicted self-regulated learning, academic integrity, and learning engagement; self-regulated learning predicted academic integrity; and academic integrity was the strongest predictor of learning engagement. The hypothesized four-step serial chain (ChatGPT adoption, self-regulated learning, academic integrity, and learning engagement) was statistically significant, and the model explained 38.7% of the variance in learning engagement. The multigroup analysis indicated that one structural path (adoption → integrity) differed significantly by gender, while all other paths were invariant across the gender groups compared. The findings inform the responsible integration of generative AI in Nigerian university education and in Cross River State specifically.
