title: Cognitive Screening in Illiterate and Low-Literate Adults: Normative Data Study in Iranian Older Adults
container-title: Journal of Geriatric Psychiatry and Neurology
4ce1d68c0b100689b4d48d32227f7d4c2ec1d689.abstract: Background The present study sought to establish normative data for five brief, education-fair cognitive screening instruments—the Abbreviated Mental Test Score (AMTS), A Quick Test of Cognitive Speed (AQT), the Picture Memory Impairment Screen (PMIS), the Clock Drawing Test (CDT), and Verbal Fluency (VF)—in a population of Iranian older adults with illiteracy or limited formal education and to investigate age, sex, and education differences in performance on these screening tests. Methods A total of 220 participants aged 58-86 years, with either no formal education or up to six years of schooling, were recruited from municipal health houses across multiple districts of Tehran to ensure representation of diverse socioeconomic strata. Following a comprehensive psychiatric evaluation, eligible individuals completed the AMTS, AQT, PMIS, CDT, and VF assessments, administered by trained psychologists. Participants were stratified into three age groups: 58-64, 65-69, and ≥70 years. Between-group differences were evaluated using analysis of variance (ANOVA) and independent samples t-tests. Linear regression analyses were conducted to assess the impact of each additional year of education on cognitive test performance. Regression-based normative values were derived using models incorporating age (as a continuous variable) and years of education as predictors. Results Inter-rater reliability ranged from moderate to perfect (κ = 0.44-1.00), indicating acceptable to excellent agreement across measures. A total of 220 participants aged 58 to 86 years were included in the analysis. Age and sex did not show significant effect for most instruments; however, significant differences were identified for AQT-CF and PMIS. Educational attainment exerted a significant effect on performance across most measures, with the exception of PMIS. Regression-based normative data were subsequently generated. Conclusion The derived normative data could facilitate the interpretation of cognitive performance in this population through the use of standardized scores ( z -scores and percentiles) in clinical settings.

title: Caso de estudio de carboncillos fabricados con maderas regionales que influyen en respuestas sensoriales, emocionales y cognitivas ejecutado en horas de tutoría a estudiantes de la carrera de artes plásticas de la ULEAM

A case study on charcoal drawing sticks made from regional woods—and their influence on sensory, emotional, and cognitive responses—conducted during tutorial sessions for students in the Visual Arts program at ULEAM
container-title: Revista Veritas de Difusão Científica
3f2b5fd26566a2c44cf916c9b9568ddafec9bdc3.abstract: La pasividad ante el material estandarizado representa una brecha constante en la formación artística contemporánea. Este estudio se propuso evaluar cómo la fabricación experimental de carboncillos a partir de maderas regionales de Manabí (Ecuador) influye en la activación simultánea de respuestas sensoriales, emocionales y cognitivas en estudiantes de Artes Plásticas. Bajo una metodología de Caso de Estudio e Investigación-Acción Participativa (IAP), se empleó un enfoque mixto, triangulando datos de la caracterización técnica (dureza, tonalidad) con análisis estadísticos de la Activación Triuna (Escala Likert 1-5) y el registro cualitativo de la experiencia. Los resultados validaron una correlación directa entre la densidad botánica (Cacao, Palo Santo, Cítricos) y el rendimiento artístico, ofreciendo un espectro tonal y de dureza amplio (H a 8B), y demostrando la estabilidad del material como medio híbrido (óleo monocromático con aceite de linaza). Crucialmente, el análisis de varianza (ANOVA) reveló que el proceso de fabricación y experimentación activa de manera significativa los tres sistemas cerebrales (p < 0,01), confirmando que la inmersión sensorial genera un fuerte vínculo emocional (Sistema Límbico) y promueve el pensamiento crítico (Sistema Neocortical). Se concluye que el carboncillo regional no solo es un material técnicamente viable y superior a los referentes comerciales, sino una metodología pedagógica efectiva (Teoría ASACL) que refuerza la identidad territorial del estudiante y promueve un diálogo transdisciplinario esencial entre el arte, la botánica y la ciencia aplicada.

title: Abstract 10464: Cardiovascular Risk Factors and Episodic Memory in Harmonized Lifestyle Trials: The InLife Study
container-title: Circulation
cea91f1bd3f1d59c1e4c685af4095ce63829813b.abstract: Background: Elevated cardiovascular (CV) risk, including high scores on clinical indicators like the AHA-defined Atherosclerotic Cardiovascular Disease (ASCVD) 10-year risk score, has been linked with increased risk of Alzheimer’s disease and related dementias in aging. Pooling and harmonizing existing data from randomized controlled trials (RCTs) for de novo analysis can improve power beyond that of a single RCT to elucidate the impact of CV risk factors. Here, we examine the association between ASCVD risk factor scores and episodic memory derived from harmonized RCT data in U.S. older adults. Methods: This was a cross-sectional analysis of baseline data from the InLife data harmonization study. InLife reflects data from lifestyle RCT participants aged ≥50 years at baseline and availability of pre/post measurement of cognition. We harmonized available ASCVD risk variables–including age, systolic blood pressure (SBP), smoking (Y/N), diabetes (medications or diagnosis), HDL, total cholesterol, hypertension medication use, and race (black vs not black)–based on self-report, electronic health records, lab values, and adjudication across trials by re-coding, creating variable crosswalks and collaborating with CV domain experts/statisticians. The AHA’s ASCVD risk score was computed for each participant. Episodic memory was previously harmonized using different standardized tests, including delayed story recall, verbal learning, and computerized visuospatial tests. Pearson ( r ) and partial correlations adjusted for other previously harmonized sociodemographic variables (education, marital status, employment), used to cross-sectionally investigate associations between ASCVD risk and episodic memory. Results: Participants ( n = 4,172 ) reflected four U.S. lifestyle RCTs ( M age = 72.1, SD = 7.1). The mean ASCVD risk score was 0.24 ( SD =0.17), reflecting a 24% 10-year risk of CVD, on average. ASCVD risk was inversely associated with episodic memory ( r = -0.14, 95% CI : -0.11, -0.16, p <0.001). The highest quintile (Q5) of ASCVD risk had an average of -0.45 lower (95% CI : -0.51, -0.39; p <0.001; medium effect size) standardized episodic memory scores as compared to the lowest quintile (Q1). Results were similar in multivariable models accounting for education, employment, marital status and trial ( r partial = -0.17; -0.57 lower episodic memory in Q5 vs. Q1). Additional multivariable statistical model results suggest that ASCVD risk associations with episodic memory scores include variation attributable to ASCVD risk components beyond simply age, sex, and race. Conclusion: Results in this harmonized analysis of lifestyle RCTs further support the link between ACSVD risk and episodic memory in aging. Future work will examine associations across other cognitive domains in the entire InLife sample (>10,000).

title: Abstract 10952: Association of Cognitive Impairment with Palliative Care Consultation and Post-Discharge Healthcare Utilization in Patients Hospitalized for Heart Failurein a Large Multi-System Electronic Health Record Database
container-title: Circulation
a10e3468a976e8f5872a2037589b635afdb4c37e.abstract: Background: Prevalence of heart failure (HF) and cognitive impairment (CI) are increasing with associated population-level burdens of rehospitalization and mortality. Guidelines recommend palliative care consultation to improve quality of life in HF, especially among patients with co-morbid CI. There is limited real-world data examining palliative care consultation, healthcare utilization (ED visits and hospital admissions) and mortality among persons with HF with CI vs normal cognition. Hypothesis: Persons with HF and CI will be more likely to receive palliative care consultation, have higher healthcare utilization, and have higher mortality compared to HF alone. Methods: This longitudinal study used the Truveta electronic health record research database to identify adults hospitalized for HF between 2022 and 2025 using ICD10 and SNOMED codes. Demographics, clinical characteristics, specialty palliative care consultation, and healthcare utilization were compared among for patients with HF and CI vs normal cognition. Cox proportional hazards models examined differences in time to hospital admission and death by comparing HF and CI to normal cognition, controlling for demographic (age, sex, race) and clinical (HF hospitalization length of stay and ICU stay (yes/no) characteristics. All results presented were significant (p<0.001). Results: Among 1,568,745 HF hospitalizations, 14% of patients had CI-related diagnostic codes at admission. Among persons with HF and any CI, 85% had dementia of whom 15% had Alzheimer’s. Persons with HF and CI vs normal cognition were older (mean 79 vs 71 years), more likely to be female (55% vs 46%) and white (75% vs 68%); they were more likely to have prior history of COPD (38% vs 34%), diabetes (52% vs 50%) and cancer (33% vs 25%) than those with normal cognition. Length of stay was longer among persons with HF and CI vs. normal cognition (6.5 days vs 6.2 days). Persons with HF and CI were more likely to have an ICU stay (9.3% vs 8.8%) and less likely to receive cardiology consultation (9% vs 11%). Persons with HF and CI had higher rates of ED visits, 30- and 90-day readmission. Among persons with HF and CI, receipt of palliative care consultation was higher in HF and CI vs without CI (26% vs 14%). Based on a proportional hazards model, time to all-cause hospitalization increased by 3% among HF with CI, 2% for HF hospitalization and time to death increased by 26% compared to normal cognition. Conclusions: Using real world HF hospitalization data, we demonstrate the association of comorbid CI with worsened HF clinical outcomes. Our findings clarify the value of cognitive assessment to support personalized HF care. While palliative care consultation was higher among persons with HF and CI, the persistently increased rates of readmission suggest efforts to increase guideline-directed palliative care may be warranted.

title: Abstract 11581: Association of MRI-Derived Left Atrial Dysfunction with Cerebrovascular Injury and Cognitive Performance: The Hispanic Community Health Study / Study of Latinos (HCHS/SOL)
container-title: Circulation
da2f6b948aa204a5d54b2558c8c8edb80d2e711e.abstract: Background: Hispanics/Latinos have a high burden of cardiometabolic risk factors and correspondingly high prevalences of subclinical cardiovascular and cerebrovascular disease, but this ethnic population from varied national backgrounds remains understudied. Left atrial (LA) dysfunction is a measure of cardiac end-organ damage that has been linked, principally through echocardiography, to brain vascular injury and lower cognitive performance. Cardiac MRI provides more precise LA phenotyping than echo, which we leveraged to study its association with cerebrovascular disease and cognitive performance in a heterogeneous cohort of Hispanics/Latinos across the U.S. Methods: We tested whether LA dysfunction is cross-sectionally associated with cerebrovascular disease and cognitive performance among participants who completed cardiac MRI, brain MRI and standardized neurocognitive testing in the community-based HCHS/SOL. Exposures were MRI-determined LA minimum volume index and LA strain, examined per SD increment. Outcomes included brain infarct, total white matter hyperintensity (WMH) volume, and global cognition score, analyzed on original scales. Multivariable linear and logistic regression adjusted for demographic and cardiometabolic risk factors and left ventricular (LV) mass, LV ejection fraction, and LV global longitudinal strain. Data on atrial fibrillation (AF) are pending in HCHS/SOL, and were not included in the present analysis. Results: Of 1,047 total participants, the number included in each analysis ranged from 719 to 758 based on data availability. Mean age 64 (SD 8) years; women 69%; Mexican 41%, Puerto Rican 17%, Central/South American 18%, Dominican 13%, Cuban 8%, Other 3%. After adjustment for demographic and cardiometabolic risk factors, higher LA minimum volume was associated with greater odds of brain infarct (OR 1.07, 95% CI 1.02-1.12; p=0.004) and higher total WMH volume (Beta 0.08, 95% CI 0.01-0.15; p=0.021). These associations persisted after additional adjustment for LV parameters. LA strain was not associated with brain infarct (OR 0.97, 95% CI 0.91-1.03; p=0.31) or WMH volume (Beta –0.04, 95% CI –0.11-0.03; p=0.23). Neither LA minimum volume nor LA strain was associated with global cognition. Conclusion: In this HCHS/SOL analysis, greater MRI-derived LA minimum volume, but not LA strain, was independently associated with presence of brain infarct and greater WMH burden after adjustment for cardiometabolic risk factors and LV structure and function. These findings support the primacy of MRI-determined LA minimum volume index as a determinant of cerebrovascular disease risk. Given that Hispanics/Latinos have lower risk of AF than other populations, additional work is necessary to examine the basis for this association in this ethnic group, which will be facilitated by an ongoing HCHS/SOL ambulatory ECG monitoring study.

title: Abstract 13978: Feasibility of Telephone Recruitment Using Electronic Health Records Data from a Cognitive Intervention Clinical Trial in Heart Failure
container-title: Circulation
56824f63830025bdf94e350b737bb35c76d4c9e3.abstract: Introduction: Recruitment is a common challenge in clinical trials, especially in seriously ill populations, such as patients with heart failure (HF). The traditional clinic-based recruitment method can be labor-intensive and costly. Electronic health records (EHR) data-based telephone recruitment is a potentially feasible alternative recruitment strategy. Research Questions: (1) What are the implementation strategies to retrieve EHR data and place recruitment calls? (2) Is EHR data-based telephone recruitment feasible (≥ 6 enrollments/month)? Methods: EHR-facilitated telephone recruitment was implemented in a 2X2 factorial RCT that tested cognitive interventions among older adults with HF and mild cognitive impairment (MCI). Inclusion criteria were: age ≥ 55 years, HF stage C, communicating in English, capacity to consent or legally authorized representative, and trouble with memory or thinking. Exclusion criteria were: HF stage A, B, or D, vision or hearing problems, major neurological (e.g., dementia) or psychiatric conditions, life-threatening unstable illness (e.g., end-stage cancer), and exposure to computerized cognitive training in the past year. Results: Recruitment was performed from 8/29/2023 to 12/17/2025. The EHR data were retrieved to create lists of potentially eligible individuals at Indiana University Health Systems (N = 5,732) by the Regenstrief Institute, a research institute associated with the health system. Data retrieval criteria included: HF ICD codes, age ≥ 55 years, home address in counties proximal to the study site, health system visit ≥ 1 in the past 3 years, and no neurological/psychiatric conditions or death records. Telephone recruitment was prioritized for patients with an ICD code for MCI, age ≥ 65 years, and home address in the study county. Next priorities were having an ICD code for HF only, ages 55 - 64 years, and living in surrounding counties. Two staff were hired for recruitment: one verifying HF stage C in the EHR such as echocardiography (≈ 10 hrs/week); and the other placing recruitment calls from the lists (≈ 10 hrs/week). The enrollment rate was 5.8/month supporting feasibility of our recruitment strategies. As shown in Figure 1, 2,253 of 5,732 were potentially eligible based on the EHR screening for HF stage C (39.3%). Recruitment calls were made for 1,109 individuals. Of those, 239 (21.6%) verbally consented during the call; and 157 of 239 (65.7%) were eventually enrolled. The major reasons patients were lost to follow-up after verbal consent included: being too sick, lost to contact, no longer interested, and too busy. Conclusion: EHR data-based telephone recruitment is feasible with careful planning to approach the targeted study population. This recruitment strategy yielded a higher recruitment rate than traditional clinical-based recruitment in prior HF studies and can be useful for studies with limited staff and clinics access.

title: Abstract 14107: Cardio Effort: A Heart-Rate-Based Wearable Metric for Characterizing Exercise Dose-Response Relationships at Scale
container-title: Circulation
dcc111e7fdc8c385a80f11cb165068c24c00a10a.abstract: Background: Quantifying cumulative exercise stimulus and its relationship with biometric changes accounting for both intensity and duration across diverse activity types remains an open challenge in exercise science. This work introduces Cardio Effort (CE) designed to capture cumulative exercise stimulus and enable its estimation at scale from a smart ring. We explore the associations of year over year (YoY) changes in CE with cardiovascular health metrics. Methods: We analyzed de-identified data from 215,568 Oura Ring users meeting a wear compliance criteria (≥20 hours/day, ≥22 days/month, ≥2 activities/week) across Jan-Mar 2025 and 2026, yielding 9,536,457 workouts. CE is calculated as the cube of the workout heart rate (HR) minus 2 month average resting HR, integrated over time. CE was computed from ring HR time series during automatically detected workouts scaled so that 1.0 is approximately a 30 minute jog. YoY changes in CE and overnight HR, HR variability (HRV), estimated VO2max (eVO2max), and estimated pulse wave velocity (ePWV) were computed. Using raw data we compared stable (CE < 0.02) and large (CE > 0.15) effort change groups via Mann-Whitney U test across four age stratified groups. Results: Higher CE associated with lower HR and ePWV, and higher HRV and eVO2max. Within subject analyses revealed nonlinear dose response relationships. A YoY 0.1 unit increase in daily CE was associated with a YoY 0.5 bpm reduction in HR and 1.0 ms HRV increase; a 0.3 unit increase was associated with a 1.0 bpm reduction in HR and >2.0 ms HRV gain. At +0.2 and +0.5 CE units, eVO 2 max increased 0.5 and 1.4 mL/kg/min YoY, respectively; ePWV decreased 0.1 m/s at +0.5 units. Benefits showed diminishing returns beyond roughly 0.5 daily CE units.Group differences (stable vs large CE change YoY) were significant (p < 0.001) for all metrics. The large increase group showed favorable YoY changes relative to stable: HRV +1.94 ms (Cohen’s d = 0.20), eVO2max +1.69 ml/kg/min (d = 0.51), HR –2.09 bpm (d = 0.39), and ePWV -0.01 m/s (d = 0.08). Effect sizes were small to medium, largest for eVO2max and smallest for ePWV. These differences were also significant in all age cohorts except for eVO2max and ePWV in the age 60+ cohort. Conclusion: CE captures dose response relationships between wearable derived exercise load and cardiovascular biomarkers across a large real world cohort. Modest daily increases (~15-30 min jogging equivalent) account for the majority of measurable benefits.

title: Abstract 14142: Dnase1L3 Deficiency Drives Stroke-Relevant Cognitive Impairment in Pristane-Induced Lupus-Like Mouse Model
container-title: Circulation
c032109d7bac92224e377d76de7a55817e2a6d49.abstract: Introduction: Strokes and seizures occur in ~20% of patients with Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE) and accounts for ~15% of SLE related deaths, yet the mechanisms underlying this elevated risk remain unclear. One source of inflammation is the accumulation of DNA due to deficiencies in nucleases like Dnase1L3. While Dnase1L3-deficient mice develop lupus-like phenotypes, which are accelerated with pristane, the contribution of Dnase1L3 to cerebrovascular injury and stroke remains unknown. Thus, it is important to define how Dnase1L3 deficiency contributes to cerebrovascular complications during lupus. Hypothesis: Loss of Dnase1L3 worsens cerebrovascular injury in lupus, leading to behavioral deficits consistent with stroke-related motor and cognitive dysfunction. Methods: Dnase1L3 knockout (KO) and control B6 mice received intraperitoneal pristane and were evaluated in the open field maze, novel object recognition and Morris water maze to assess locomotion, anxiety- like behavior, recognition memory, and spatial learning. Splenocyte flow cytometry was performed to profile SLE-associated immune populations, including activated B- and T cell subsets. Statistical analysis was performed using Two-way ANOVA. Results: Pristane-treated Dnase1L3-deficient mice developed significant stroke-relevant behavioral deficits. Open field testing revealed reduced center exploration and slower movement in both genotypes (P ≤ 0.05), with knockout mice showing increased time in corner (P ≤ 0.01) and heightened anxiety-like behavior. In the novel object recognition task, knockout mice exhibited reduced exploration and increased freezing (P ≤ 0.01), while wild-type females and both knockout sexes showed decreased novel object preference after pristane exposure. Morris water maze performance confirmed sever spatial learning and memory impairment in pristane-treated knockout mice compared with wild-type controls. These behavioral deficits occurred alongside B- and T-cell activation, suggesting that Dnase1L3 deficiency exacerbates lupus associated immune activation and contributes to stroke- relevant motor and cognitive dysfunction. Conclusions: Dnase1L3 deficiency in pristane-induced lupus-like mice produced a chronic ‘pre-stroke’ neurobehavioral phenotype, with marked anxiety-like behavior and severe recognition and spatial memory deficits in standard stroke-relevant tests, accompanied by activation of autoreactive and inflammatory splenocyte population. These preliminary data support impaired extracellular DNA clearance and immune-mediated neuroinflammation as promising targets for neuroprotective strategies to lower cerebrovascular risk and cognitive sequelae in SLE.

title: Abstract 17062: Beyond Stroke: Measuring Cognitive Impairment in Carotid Artery Stenosis
container-title: Circulation
9b64f8a2995ee839ee1199848afd9185721c1fcb.abstract: Objectives: Treatment of carotid artery stenosis (CAS) is aimed at preventing death or grave disability from a stroke. However, the cognitive impact of CAS, particularly the long-term effects on cognition in aging adults, has not been well-studied. We sought to identify a cognitive assessment that was easy to deliver and could be used to track domain-specific cognitive changes overtime. Methods: Patients seeking medical care for CAS at a single academic center were prospectively recruited. Patients were asked if they had ever been diagnosed with cognitive impairment or dementia and then completed two questions about cognition from the NIH Patient-Reported Outcome Measurement Information System (PROMIS). Virtual cognitive assessments were collected, the Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MOCA) and the NIH Mobile Toolbox (MTB). Published cut-points for severity of dysfunction were used for MOCA and PROMIS. MTB scoring varies for each domain, without published normative values at this time. Therefore, MTB scores were compared between patients with MOCA scores suggesting cognitive dysfunction and those within normal limits. Results: All patients denied a diagnosis of cognitive dysfunction (N=22). All completed PROMIS, with MOCA and MTB testing in 19 and 18 patients respectively. The mean age was 71+/-10.3 years. PROMIS suggested normal cognition in 20 patients, mild impairment in 1, and moderate impairment in 1. MOCA suggested at least cognitive impairment in 57.8% of patients (Figure 1). Patients with abnormal MOCA scores performed less well on all MTB measures, compared to those within normal limits (Table 1). Conclusions: Cognitive impairment was identified in over half of patients with CAS. Self-report and a 2-item PROMIS assessment were inadequate to detect cognitive dysfunction in this population. The NIH MTB provided domain-specific comparison of patients with and without abnormal MOCA scores. The MTB is a promising measure to assess multiple cognitive domains via remote self-administration in this population with a high proportion of cognitive dysfunction. Greater attention to cognitive function in CAS patients will help clinicians and researchers better understand neurologic changes associated with this common disease process and may identify the impact of treatment on non-stroke outcomes which may otherwise be overlooked. Figure 1. Impairment by Assessment Method PROMIS: Patient-Reported Outcome Measurement Information System; MOCA: Montreal Cognitive Assessment Table 1. Mobile ToolBox Scores for those with and without dysfunction on MOCA. Higher scores indicate higher cognition. MOCA: Montreal Cognitive Assessment; SEM: Standard Error of the Mean

title: Abstract 17222: Endothelial Cu Transporter CTR1 Drives Blood-Brain Barrier Dysfunction and Cognitive Decline via Cuproptosis in Diabetes
container-title: Circulation
fe70bdd152f042d4e4507a850fa41ca32e1e0a0a.abstract: Introduction: Type 2 diabetes (T2D) is a risk factor for cognitive impairment and Alzheimer’s Disease (AD), in which amyloid beta (Aβ42) accumulation and blood-blood barrier (BBB) dysfunction play key roles. Mitochondrial (mito) dysfunction in brain endothelial cells (ECs) contributes to BBB breakdown in T2D, but the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Copper (Cu) dyshomeostasis has been implicated in T2D-associated brain dysfunction. We previously demonstrated that the Cu importer CTR1 and Cu levels are elevated in the AD hippocampus and mediate Aβ42 -induced EC junctional disruption. Recently, cuproptosis, a novel form of programmed cell death triggered by excessive mito Cu accumulation and subsequent mito dysfunction, has been identified. However, the role of endothelial CTR1-Cu axis and cuproptosis in T2D-induced BBB dysfunction and cognitive decline remains unknown. Result: The hippocampus of T2D mice generated by low-dose streptozotocin and high-fat diet for 3 months exhibited increased CTR1 expression (3.5-fold) and Cu accumulation (ICP-MS, 4-fold). T2D mice also showed increased APP (3-fold) and BACE1 (4-fold) expression, accompanied by elevated Aβ42 levels (2.5-fold), suggesting enhanced amyloidogenic processing. These changes were associated with BBB dysfunction, measured by NHS-SS-biotin leakage, and cuproptosis-related responses, including aggregation of the lipoylated mitochondrial TCA cycle enzyme DLAT and loss of Fe-S clusters, in both T2D and Aβ42-injected (i.c.v) AD mouse models. Importantly, inducible EC-specific CTR1-deficient (iEC-Ctr1 -/- ) mice exhibited reduced cuproptosis-related responses,restored BBB integrity, and improved cognitive performance in NOR and RAWM tests in the Aβ42-induced AD model. In brain microvascular ECs, Aβ42 stimulation increased mito Cu levels (ICP-MS, 2-fold), reduced oxygen consumption rate, and impaired barrier function, measured by trans-endothelial electrical resistance (TEER). These responses were inhibited by CTR1 silencing or the Cu chelator TTM. Furthermore, Aβ42 or T2D mimetic stimulation (high glucose plus palmitate) induced cuproptosis-related responses, leading to EC death and barrier dysfunction in a CTR1- and Cu-dependent manner. Conclusion: These findings identify the endothelial CTR1-mito Cu-cuproptosis axis as a novel mechanism underlying diabetes-associated BBB dysfunction and cognitive decline and suggest CTR1 as a therapeutic target for neurovascular complications of T2D.

title: Counter-propagating opposite polarity guided streamer interactions: EFISH electric fields, propagation thresholds, and memory effects
container-title: Plasma Sources Science and Technology
47e905ccc7e15bd9523372b4505713933f49eb8a.abstract: Abstract Interactions between counter-propagating guided streamers are important in multi-jet atmospheric pressure plasma jet (APPJ) systems used to extend plasma treatment over larger areas and complex three-dimensional targets. Here, two geometrically identical helium APPJs are operated in ambient air with opposite polarity and independently controlled voltages, and their interactions are investigated using time-gated ICCD imaging and electric-field-induced second harmonic (EFISH) generation. We found that the voltage of the positive polarity jet required for streamer head merging decreases as the magnitude of the negative polarity jet voltage increases, showing that the presence of the opposing streamer strongly modifies the environment governing positive streamer propagation. Reducing the pulse repetition rate from 5 kHz to 50 Hz increases the voltage required for the positive streamer to form and reduces the positive streamer’s propagation distance, consistent with reduced memory effects. However, enhanced propagation persists at low repetition rates when the negative jet is present, consistent with an increasing relative importance of streamer interaction driven effects as memory effects weaken. Measurements of EFISH electric fields provide direct benchmarks for these opposite polarity guided streamer interactions. When the fields during dual-jet operation are compared to single-jet operation, the peak field at the positive guided streamer head is unchanged within the uncertainty of the diagnostic, whereas the field distribution ahead of the peak is elongated and approximately doubled by the presence of the negative guided streamer.

title:
Broad Cognitive and Motivational Enhancement through M
                  <sub>4</sub>
                  -Selective Muscarinic Modulation
b20806c606c00cb07404ef9668318c1c0a944295.abstract: Abstract The muscarinic M 4 subtype of acetylcholine receptors is part of agonist compounds considered treatment options for Schizophrenia and Alzheimers disease, but how M 4 -subtype selective modulation affects cognition and motivation is largely unknown due to dose-limiting side effects, a scarcity of receptor-selective compounds, and missing multi-domain assessments of cognition. Here, we surmount these constraints by utilizing a M 4 -selective positive allosteric modulator (PAM) to assess in nonhuman primates a broad array of endpoints spanning motivational effort control and multiple executive function domains. We found broad dose-dependent performance improvements of set shifting indexing cognitive flexibility, visual search indexing selective attention, antisaccade performance indexing inhibitory control, visuospatial maze learning, and temporal order serial object learning, while working memory span was non-systematically modulated. In addition, the M 4 PAM reduced effort avoidance in an effort-based choice task documenting a pro-motivational effect. Task-composite performance scores showed pro-cognitive effects across multiple doses and an effective dose range for individual subjects in the absence of adverse dose-limiting cholinergic side effects. Together, the broad pro-cognitive and pro-motivational multi-task profile of M 4 PAM modulation suggests that the M 4 receptor is a master regulator of executive cognitive functioning, possibly acting on domain-general neural processes across the prefrontal-striatal circuits.

title: Loss-Responsive Dual-Memory Graph Models for Fraud Drift: A Controlled Temporal Stress Test
container-title: Journal of Computing and Electronic Information Management
6fe5947ad1e2901f3600abc8430ad50b06995fc7.abstract: Adaptive graph fraud detectors must decide both when to update and how strongly to trust an updated model. This study isolates those decisions through a fully reproducible synthetic temporal-transaction benchmark. Following the ATGNN-SP design, we implement directed two-hop simplified graph propagation, a frozen stable model, an incrementally updated plastic model, a validation-calibrated loss gate, and anchor replay. We extend the fixed stable–plastic mixture with a delayed-label exponential expert-weighting rule. Across five seeds and 15 future snapshots, the adaptive mixture attains average precision 0.4170 and F1 0.4021, versus 0.3469 and 0.3189 for a fixed mixture; however, it updates on all 15 snapshots, compared with 7.8 for the fixed mixture. Plastic-only adaptation is competitive (AP 0.4163; F1 0.3965), showing that retaining a frozen predictor in the final score need not always improve outcomes. All results are computed from a synthetic generator with deliberately changing label and connectivity mechanisms; they should be interpreted as a controlled stress test, not empirical validation on banking or cryptocurrency transactions.

title: AI & Cognitive Work
2b61e74f84ac0a89e56b038ec2936fb9963fc816.abstract: Artificial systems now perform a striking range of cognitive tasks. This Element defends three claims. First, the status quo for cognitive work cannot survive. Whatever AI's trajectory, the package of features defining cognitive work – high skill requirements, credentials, wage premiums, resistance to automation, and low productivity growth – will be radically transformed. Second, the widespread displacement of humans from cognitive work, though it sounds alarming, may pose no special threat to human flourishing. Whatever makes work good for people is equally available outside cognitive work, and displacement enables leveraged gains in research and access to justice. Third, a world of ubiquitous cognitive assistance, though it sounds benign, carries distinctive moral risks, especially for children. Cognitive assistance works by reducing cognitive difficulty. But cognitive difficulty is necessary for the normal development of executive function – the capacities constitutive of autonomous agency. This title is also available as Open Access on Cambridge Core.

title: THE SUITCASE OF KNOWLEDGES - CREATION PROCESSES, MEMORY AND INTANGIBLE HERITAGE IN BANDO DE TEATRO OLODUM
container-title: New Perspectives Across Scientific Fields
d6901045545a98c1d504f4edcdc63f989f173f85.abstract: This article reflects on the creative processes of Bando de Teatro Olodum from the author’s experience as an actress, director, and museologist. Taking the group’s recognition as intangible cultural heritage as a starting point, the discussion shifts its focus from the performances themselves to the modes of creation that made them possible. In dialogue with studies on memory, performance, orality, Black theatre, and African epistemologies, the article argues that one of Bando’s major legacies lies in its collective know-how. Through the notion of the “suitcase of knowledges” (mala dos saberes), an authorial formulation developed in this essay, it proposes that each artist enters the creative process carrying memories, experiences, territories, ancestralities, and ways of knowing the world, which are subsequently shared and transformed into theatrical language. The character Dona Raimunda is taken as a case study to reflect on observation, listening, improvisation, recording, and collective construction, without reducing the diversity of the group’s creative processes to a single experience.

title: Increased Cognitive Load Expands, Stabilizes, and Aligns Visual Representation Across the Human Brain
818dd058380c29244eb8075565b8f2e89685c20e.abstract: Abstract Cognitive load refers to the mental effort required to perform a task. While previous research has extensively examined its detrimental effects on neural and behavioral performance, much less is known about how the brain actively adapts to heightened demands. Across two fMRI experiments involving visual n-back tasks, we identified several fundamental properties of this adaptive process. First, higher load enhanced and expanded visual representations beyond localized visual regions, leading to widespread visual coding. At the global scale, heightened load promoted cross-regional coordination by increasing representational alignment and strengthening information encoded in interregional functional connectivity patterns. Beyond facilitating stronger visual representation, increased load also reduced neural pattern variability, which led to more stable information coding. Finally, load was encoded independently of other task-relevant information as a separate brain state, supporting its overarching role in guiding visual processing. Together, these findings revealed that the brain adapts to heightened cognitive demands by globally reorganizing neural processing to support flexible cognition. Highlights The brain employs multiple neural mechanisms to adapt to heightened cognitive demands. Increased cognitive load strengthens and expands visual representations beyond visual regions. Higher cognitive load enhances cross-regional coordination through increased representational alignment and stronger information coding in interregional connectivity patterns. Neural pattern variability decreases under greater load, promoting more stable representations Load is encoded as a distributed brain state, with minimal interaction with other variables

title: Clinical expertise and cognitive reflection predict fewer misconceptions in Bayesian diagnostic reasoning
container-title: BMC Medical Education
c2b5c50130daf164ca1cca6d8bb81820a196e48d.abstract: Abstract Background For many years, research has consistently confirmed that even medical experts fail to solve Bayesian diagnostic tasks. These tasks require correctly estimating a diagnostic test’s positive predictive value based on sensitivity, specificity, and the disease’s prevalence. Previous research has primarily focused on improving task presentation, for example by using natural frequencies or visual aids. The present study introduces the Medical Bayesian Performance Score (MBPS), a confidence-weighted measure that distinguishes confidently held misconceptions from missing concepts. Participants completed eight medical Bayesian diagnostic tasks and rated their confidence after each response. Using this approach, we examined whether medical knowledge, clinical expertise, and cognitive reflection are associated with performance in Bayesian diagnostic reasoning. Methods In an online survey, we compared MBPS values via t tests along two independent variables: (a) medical knowledge (physician group: N p = 30 vs. student control group: N s = 56) and (b) clinical expertise within the physician group (specialists and senior physicians: N e = 19 vs. resident physicians: N r = 11). Furthermore, we analyzed correlations between MBPS values and Cognitive Reflection Test (CRT) scores. Results Physicians did not achieve significantly higher MBPS values than the student control group. In contrast, specialists and senior physicians scored significantly higher than resident physicians. Across all groups, average MBPS values were negative, indicating that confidence-weighted incorrect responses outweighed confidence-weighted correct responses, a pattern consistent with misconceptions. Furthermore, higher CRT scores correlated significantly with higher MBPS values. Conclusions The MBPS provides a complementary perspective to conventional accuracy measures by distinguishing misconceptions from missing concepts and linking Bayesian diagnostic reasoning research with conceptual change theory. Consistent with this perspective, our findings suggest that formal medical knowledge alone was not associated with fewer misconceptions, whereas greater clinical expertise and higher cognitive reflection were. Future research should evaluate evidence-based conceptual change interventions for medical education, such as specific refutation-based training, as a means of improving Bayesian diagnostic reasoning.

title: Generative AI and the community of inquiry framework
container-title: Online Learning
4335ece8079aad2b90b8c80755ec77080ca649a0.abstract: This scoping review synthesizes empirical studies examining how generative AI is associated with teaching, cognitive, and social presence within the Community of Inquiry (CoI) framework. Although generative AI has rapidly entered educational practice, its impact on teaching, cognitive, and social presence remains conceptually fragmented. To address this gap, we systematically searched for eligible literature following PRISMA guidelines and reviewed 21 peer-reviewed empirical studies published after the emergence of large language model-based AI systems (between November 2022 and July 2026) to identify research trends, AI roles in teaching and learning, and patterns of presence activation related to learning experiences. Findings indicate that first, generative AI has evolved beyond conversational agents to include pedagogical agents, AI-generated instructors, collaborative cognitive tools, and AI-supported learning environments, while teaching presence remains comparatively underexplored as an independent construct. Second, the distribution of presence dimensions is uneven: cognitive presence was most frequently associated with AI-supported exploration and integration processes, whereas resolution and independent examinations of teaching presence remained comparatively limited. Third, the reviewed studies suggested that presence-related outcomes varied by instructional approaches. Discussion and task-based activity were more often associated with reported indicators of cognitive presence, whereas pedagogical agents and socially expressive AI designs more frequently supported perceived social presence. The findings suggest that generative AI should not be regarded as a universal solution for strengthening the CoI framework. Rather, its educational value depends on how it is pedagogically configured within specific instructional contexts. The review contributes to a more nuanced understanding of AI-mediated learning by positioning generative AI as a design-sensitive pedagogical mediator and identifying directions for future theoretical and empirical research.

title: Cognitive Psychiatry and the dichotomy between the science of matter and the science of Being: Necessity, propositionality, problematicity and a critique of psychiatric materialism
Psiquiatría Cognitiva y la dicotomía entre la ciencia de la materia y la ciencia del Ser: Necesidad, proposicionalidad, problematicidad y crítica al materialismo psiquiátrico
Psiquiatria Cognitiva e a dicotomia entre a ciência da matéria e a ciência do Ser: Necessidade, proposicionalidade, problematicidade e crítica ao materialismo psiquiátrico
container-title: Research, Society and Development
646283ef4fa699f47e54a93ecb48d36a75e87631.abstract: Western science was built on principles of determination, necessity, identity and non-contradiction, which proved highly effective in the study of matter but produce distortions when applied to the self and to human existence. This article aims to propose, from the standpoint of Cognitive Psychiatry, a distinction between a science of matter and a science of Being and to examine its consequences for Psychiatry. It is a theoretical proposition essay supported by a narrative review of the philosophical, psychopathological and clinical literature, with emphasis on works published between 2021 and 2026. Matter admits relatively stable conceptual delimitations, whereas the self presents conative unity, historical continuity, significance and openness to existential possibilities. The ontological intuition of a single Being is proposed to derive, in part, from the experience of this conative unity. The propositions Socrates is bald and Socrates is wise, formally equivalent, show that propositional logic does not establish the processual hierarchy of attributes in the essentialization of an entity. Conceptual apodicticity, the coagulation of concepts and the closure of problematicity explain part of the reification of human manifestations. A psychological and cultural hypothesis is formulated according to which the preference for control and formalization expresses obsessive tendencies in the organization of knowledge. In Psychiatry, materialistic predominance favours the reduction of existential conflicts to pharmacological problems, sustained by commercial conditioning and by a shared therapeutic illusion. A processual science of Being is needed, integrating history, conflict, moral engagement and personal transformation into biological investigation.

title: An algebra of proper observables at null infinity: Dirac brackets, memory and Goldstone probes
container-title: Journal of High Energy Physics
78e2255e7a27a2bb0580e3ded42042707cc48642.abstract: A bstract We develop a rigorous evaluation of Dirac brackets for classical observables on the phase space of radiative gravitational modes at null infinity that naturally incorporates memory effects. Considering the Ashtekar-Streubel phase space, with boundary conditions in time given by vanishing news and purely electric shear , and taking into account the infinite dimensionality of the phase space, we identify the algebra of proper observables (understood as functions on phase space that can be associated with smooth symplectic flows). We show that the action of supertranslation charges generates the correct transformations on the shear. We also show that the conventional definition of the “Goldstone mode” adopted in the literature cannot be associated with a proper observable, but nevertheless there exists an infinite family of proper observables, which we call Goldstone probes , that are capable of measuring the Goldstone mode. We notice that there are no Goldstone probes constructed only out of the shear or the news, providing a possible explanation for why attempts to construct a (separable) Hilbert space with different memory states have failed so far. Finally, we derive formulas for distributional Dirac brackets between local shear and news, and show that they contain non-local corrections.

title: Cognitive Performance in Prodromal Neuronal α-Synuclein Disease
0324f2b99c75c95b6f2fe97df3f385c181837295.abstract: Abstract Importance Cognitive abnormalities may emerge during prodromal neuronal α-synuclein disease (NSD), but their domain specificity and longitudinal course are uncertain. Objective To characterize baseline cognition and longitudinal change in prodromal NSD compared with healthy controls, NSD-negative genetic carriers, and sporadic Parkinson disease (PD). Design Longitudinal cohort study using Parkinson’s Precision Medicine Initiative (PPMI) data, with first visits from July 2010 through April 2026 and up to 4 years of follow-up. Setting Multicenter cohort. Participants Healthy controls (HC; n=244), GBA1 or LRRK2 nonmanifesting carriers without NSD (n=323), prodromal NSD participants recruited through hyposmia or isolated rapid eye movement sleep behavior disorder cohorts (n=1640), and sporadic PD (n=824). Exposures NSD status and clinical cohort. Main Outcomes and Measures Cognitive summary scores for verbal memory, executive function, processing speed, language, and visuospatial function, and PPMI-defined mild cognitive impairment (MCI). Models adjusted for age, sex, education, and APOE ε4 status. Results: Among 3031 participants (mean [SD] age, 66.6 [7.0] years; 1322 female [43.6%]), prodromal NSD participants had lower baseline verbal-memory performance than HC (adjusted difference, −0.20 SD; 95% CI, −0.34 to −0.07; adjusted P = .007); NSD-negative genetic carriers did not differ from HC. No other cognitive domain was lower than HC at baseline or longitudinally. In the primary age-adjusted analysis, verbal-memory trajectory differed from HC over 4 years ( P = .009), whereas in a smaller age-matched sensitivity subset through year 3, it did not ( P = .62); the baseline difference persisted (adjusted difference, −0.28 SD; 95% CI, −0.46 to −0.10; P = .003). Adjusted MCI probability increased from 10.2% to 15.1% in prodromal NSD, compared with 8.4% to 5.0% in HC and 13.4% to 17.7% in PD. The increase was greater than in HC (ratio of annual odds ratios, 1.28; 95% CI, 1.04 to 1.58; adjusted P = .04) but not PD ( P = .62). Conclusions and Relevance Prodromal NSD was associated with modestly lower verbal memory and increasing MCI probability relative to HC, without lower performance in other cognitive domains. The baseline verbal-memory difference was robust, whereas the longitudinal trajectory finding was not reproduced in the smaller age-matched sensitivity subset. Key Points Question What cognitive differences characterize prodromal neuronal α-synuclein disease, and how do they change over time? Findings In this longitudinal cohort study of 3031 participants, prodromal neuronal α-synuclein disease was associated with lower verbal memory at baseline than healthy controls, while other cognitive domains were not lower. In the primary age-adjusted analysis, the verbal-memory trajectory differed from healthy controls over 4 years; in a smaller age-matched sensitivity subset through year 3, it did not differ significantly. Meaning Cognitive involvement in prodromal neuronal α-synuclein disease may be detectable as a modest verbal-memory signal, while longitudinal changes require confirmation.

title: Longitudinal Participation and Cognitive Score Interpretation in the J-TRC Webstudy
7de1877d7e21786c00c47f60990854c69cc21a32.abstract: Abstract INTRODUCTION Web-based registries support remote cognitive assessment for Alzheimer’s disease research, but participant-driven reassessment raises questions about long-term data yield and interpretation of repeated scores. We evaluated data contribution, selective observation, and retest-dependent estimates of cognitive change in the Japanese Trial-Ready Cohort (J-TRC) Webstudy. METHODS We analyzed over six years of J-TRC Webstudy data (launched October 2019; registrations through March 31, 2025; assessments through May 31, 2026). We examined data contribution, inactivity, reactivation, score-associated observation, first-exposure contrasts, and sensitivity to retest models and estimators. RESULTS Among 14,912 registered accounts, 10,863 participants were eligible; 10,645 (98.0%) completed the Cognitive Function Instrument (CFI), 6,419 (59.1%) completed Cogstate, and 5,792 (53.3%) contributed assessments on multiple days. Among those with sufficient opportunity, 19.4% and 14.1% contributed data at or beyond three and five years. After 365 days without assessment, the estimated probability of resuming within two years was 7.2%. Worse prior cognitive scores were associated with lower odds of subsequent assessment (adjusted odds ratios per standard deviation: CFI, 0.952; Cogstate, 0.845). By assessment 12, returnee changes were +0.43 and +1.14 favorable baseline standard deviations (CFI, Cogstate), versus −0.06 and +0.08 in first-exposure contrasts. Marginal CFI time estimates differed under categorical versus flexible retest adjustment (+0.080 versus −0.227 standard deviations/year). DISCUSSION High initial completion was accompanied by limited long-term data contribution. Subsequent assessment was associated with prior scores, and estimated time trends varied by retest model. Reporting assessment histories and testing model sensitivity are important for interpreting repeated online cognitive scores.

title: Reading–Writing Integration Through ChatGPT-Supported Feedback: Growth, Associations, and Mediated Pathways of Student Engagement in Chinese Classrooms
2cffaae6a3503d43ca0d9d15f211f18147657ddf.abstract: Although reading–writing integration has been increasingly advocated in Chinese language education, limited empirical evidence explains how reading, writing, and student engagement become integrated, particularly under AI-supported feedback. To address this issue, this study examined whether ChatGPT-supported feedback improved reading outcomes, writing outcomes, and student engagement, while investigating their interrelationships, the mediating role of student engagement, and the corresponding pathways in reading–writing integration. A total of 400 middle school students from eight intact classes in Shenzhen participated, with 200 students receiving ChatGPT-supported feedback and 200 receiving human-generated feedback. Using a quasi-experimental pretest–posttest design, data were analyzed within a quantitative longitudinal framework integrating baseline equivalence tests, 2 × 2 mixed-design ANOVAs, factor-level correlation analyses, and multi-group cross-lagged path analysis to examine changes and temporal relationships among reading, student engagement, and writing across two groups (N = 400). Findings showed that Group 1 demonstrated significantly greater pretest–posttest gains in reading, student engagement, and writing, with significant Time × Group interactions and large effects. Correlations further indicated stronger posttest associations among engagement, reading, and writing in Group 1, whereas these relationships remained weak in Group 2. Longitudinal analyses revealed stronger T2 within-time direct and mediating pathways in Group 1, alongside several significant cross-lagged effects, but cross-lagged mediating effects were generally nonsignificant in both groups. The findings theoretically highlight student engagement as a potentially time-sensitive mechanism through which AI-supported learning may strengthen the integration of reading and writing. Practically, they suggest the pedagogical value of AI-supported learning environments for fostering engagement and connecting literacy processes, while emphasizing sustained instructional exposure to consolidate these relationships over time.

title: Music-Synchronized Gamma Light Stimulation Strengthens Theta-Gamma Coupling in Older Adults with Cognitive Impairment: Results from a Randomized Feasibility Trial
7d07bdb0722d5c75bbcc621832ad09a64e4d7929.abstract: Abstract Noninvasive clinical innovations for restoring gamma activity via sound and light stimulation have the potential to improve memory and cognitive abilities in Alzheimer’s disease. We assessed whether pairing music with theta- and gamma-band light changes memory-supporting neural dynamics, and whether those changes track cognition. In an ongoing randomized feasibility trial, 38 older adults with cognitive impairment completed eight weeks of an audiovisual intervention. The treatment group (n = 19) listened to self-selected music while viewing light stimulation that consisted of a 39-Hz gamma-band signal modulated by delta- and theta-band musical rhythms. The control group (n = 19) listened to podcasts while viewing synchronized lights without the gamma frequency (delta-band only). Before and after the 8-week intervention, participants completed a face-name association task and the Alzheimer’s Disease Assessment Scale-Cognitive (ADAS-Cog). Individuals in the treatment group showed significant improvements on a face-name association task and the ADAS-Cog. Cluster-based permutation testing showed a larger increase in phase-amplitude coupling between acoustic theta phase and frontal EEG gamma amplitude in the treatment group compared to the control group. Across participants, increases in stimulus-driven theta to EEG-gamma phase-amplitude coupling were associated with improvements in memory. These preliminary results suggest that theta-gamma stimulation delivered through music and lights strengthens cross-frequency coupling, and may correspondingly strengthen associative memory.

title: Applicability of cognitive decline risk scores in a high socioeconomic preventive medicine cohort
container-title: Journal of Alzheimer’s Disease
ceb900688d799cc4ce07329dea38bdf34ef390b4.abstract: Background Validated cognitive decline and Alzheimer's disease risk scores (CAIDE, ANU-ADRI, LIBRA, LIBRA2) were developed in general-population cohorts; how they behave in the high-socioeconomic, health-selected populations typical of preventive-medicine programs and over-represented in ageing cohorts is undescribed. Objective Lacking a cognitive outcome, we did not test predictive validity but described score distributions, inter-score concordance, the components driving variance, and complementary biological data. Methods Four scores were computed for 895 participants aged ≥45 years in the Zoī cohort, a self-referred, self-funded preventive-medicine sample. Concordance was assessed by Spearman correlations and, after dichotomization, by pairwise agreement (percentage agreement, Cohen's κ). Principal component analysis identified components accounting for most between-person variance. Complementary data (DEXA body composition, HbA1c, erythrocyte omega-3) were cross-tabulated with score-derived risk categories. Results Concordance was moderate (ρ = 0.39–0.60), and dichotomized categories were fairly-to-moderately concordant across families (Cohen's κ 0.33–0.52). Protective variables showed ceiling effects (education ≥10 years, 86%; social/cognitive activity, 100%), leaving cardiovascular factors (BMI, hypertension, coronary heart disease) to account for most variance. Despite 91% having normal BMI (≤30 kg/m 2 ), DEXA-measured fat mass showed a dose-response gradient across all scores (CAIDE 4.36–6.26); HbA1c revealed a glycemic gradient invisible to self-reported diabetes. Conclusions In this high-socioeconomic cohort, the scores were moderately concordant and varied almost solely by cardiovascular components, protective factors being saturated. Whether this reflects uniformly low risk or reduced ability to separate individuals cannot be determined without a cognitive outcome. Complementary biological measurements added stratification, supporting augmented risk-assessment tools to be validated against cognitive endpoints.

title: The cognitive profile of the schizophrenia-associated 3q29 deletion syndrome and the reciprocal 3q29 duplication syndrome
764cf47571d180edf281e9c17fd27e21ad14e3e3.abstract: Abstract 3q29 deletion syndrome (3q29del) and the reciprocal 3q29 duplication syndrome (3q29dup) are associated with a range of neuropsychiatric phenotypes, including impaired cognition. However, previous sample sizes have been small, and cognitive performance has not been systematically compared between 3q29del and 3q29dup. For both disorders, the impact of familial background on cognition is unknown. 3q29del is associated with high risk for schizophrenia; in the general population individuals at Clinical High Risk (CHR) for psychosis exhibit impaired cognition, but the relationship between CHR status and cognition in 3q29del is unexplored. Here we address these questions in the largest sample of 3q29del and 3q29dup ever evaluated. Individuals with 3q29del (n=103, 58.3% male), 3q29dup (n=38, 55.3% male), and controls (n=54, 42.6% male) were assessed with the Peabody Picture Vocabulary Test, 5 th Edition (PPVT-5) and the Penn Computerized Neurocognitive Battery (Penn-CNB). Total PPVT-5 scores and global, domain-level, and task-level Penn-CNB scores were compared across groups. Compared to controls, 3q29del participants scored an average of 24.6 and 22.9 points lower on the PPVT and Penn CNB, respectively (p<3E-16); 3q29dup participants scored an average of 18.8 and 14.2 points lower on the PPVT and Penn CNB (p<4E-6). In addition, 3q29del and 3q29dup exhibit unique profiles of cognitive deficits. To assess the impact of familial background on cognition, we evaluated unaffected relatives of 3q29del (n=140, 38.6% male), 3q29dup (n=25, 24.0% male), and controls (n=45, 11.1% male). The average familial shift on the Penn-CNB was 22.4 points for 3q29del and 16.7 points for 3q29 dup. Individuals with 3q29del+CHR exhibited greater cognitive deficits than 3q29del-CHR. These results demonstrate that both 3q29del and 3q29dup are associated with significant cognitive impairment and indicate that cognitive testing should be standard of care for individuals diagnosed with 3q29del or 3q29dup.

title: Artificial Intelligence and Human Cognitive Development: A Thematic Analysis
container-title: International Journal For Multidisciplinary Research
7cb24eb237153565a9d07e7552ddabd578c5d933.abstract: There is still uncertainty surrounding whether generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) enhances or decreases human cognition, as the proof is scattered all around. This thematic analysis synthesises 46 core peer-reviewed articles (2011–2026), selected from 165 Scopus records after an assessment, to conclude how AI applications affect the development of human cognition in learning. The six-phase process proposed by Braun and Clarke (2006) yielded six themes: (1) AI-assisted performance does not equal productive learning; (2) cognitive offloading is mixed in quality and dependent and autonomous vary in approach; (3) critical and higher-order thinking depend on usage of AI rather than simply on AI existence; (4) metacognition, self-regulation, and calibration play the main role; (5) either strengths of creativity and cognitive agency depend on process of engagement; and (6) pedagogical design has implications for all listed above. The proof of a long-lasting, self-sufficient gain is scarce and varies, whereas the data largely comprise cross-sectional opinions of university undergraduates. The final evaluation shows that the cognitive influence of artificial intelligence is variable. It's dependent on the governing behaviour and the teaching method. The research gives rise to a human-centred agenda, which aims to maintain productive effort, use artificial intelligence indirectly, and assess the process besides the result.

title: Cognitive materiality & cultural reproduction: Metonymy at the heart of cultural cognition
container-title: Ethos
a25548ab56642961d6ac685eee22a798856f88ae.abstract: Abstract Why do some cultures exhibit recognizable modal patterns while others mere fragments? Why do some private schemas become embedded in practices referential across time and space, while others die out? Embodied or ‘4E’ cognition (cognition as embodied, embedded, extended and enacted) presents a compelling paradigm for individual cognition but fails to adequately explain cultural, or shared cognition. Despite advances, most 4E theories explain cultural reproduction in terms of socialization, which does not fully explain cultural patterning. Building on Clark and Chalmers' (1998) extended cognition, Hutchins' (2005; 2012) material anchoring, and Strauss and Quinn's (1997) shared task solutions, this essay argues cultural models spread and become referential, in part, through cognitive‐material metonymies. These mostly preconscious features of cognition (not just language) fuse mental representation with material experience in one simplified, optimized cognitive operation through mechanisms of indexing, multimodality, meaning elaboration, abstraction, and ideation. This reproduces cultural models across domains and reconciles longstanding body/mind‐culture dualism, also offering new approaches for applied cultural models work in fields like social change, among others.

title: Physical activity and cancer-related cognitive impairment: Is physical activity associated with perceived difficulties and unmet needs?
container-title: Supportive Care in Cancer
4df22a54959337c9664a36009bccc58acdac54f9.abstract: Abstract Purpose Cancer-related cognitive impairment (CRCI) is associated with significant functional difficulties and unmet needs. Physical activity (PA) is a promising approach for reducing perceived CRCI; however, its relationship with perceived CRCI-related difficulties and unmet needs remains unclear. This study examined the associations between PA, perceived cognitive functioning, and perceived CRCI-related difficulties and unmet needs, and assessed whether PA explained additional variance in perceived CRCI-related difficulties and unmet needs after controlling for perceived cognitive functioning. Methods In this cross-sectional study, adult cancer survivors receiving curative-intent treatment ( n = 418) who self-identified as experiencing CRCI completed the PROMIS-Cog, MASCC COG-IMPACT, and modified Godin-Shephard Leisure-Time Physical Activity Questionnaire. Bivariate correlation analyses and hierarchical multiple regression analyses were conducted to examine associations between physical activity, perceived cognitive functioning, and CRCI-related difficulties and unmet needs, and to determine whether physical activity explained additional variance in CRCI-related difficulties and unmet needs beyond perceived cognitive functioning. Results Greater engagement in light-, vigorous-, and resistance-based PA was associated with better perceived cognitive functioning ( r = 0.10–0.14; p < 0.05) with small effects. PA was also associated with fewer psychological ( r =− 0.11; p < 0.05) and verbal communication ( r =− 0.13; p < 0.05) CRCI-related difficulties, but more CRCI-related informational need difficulties ( r = 0.13–0.17; p < 0.01) with small effects. PA was not associated with CRCI-related unmet needs ( p > 0.05). After controlling for perceived cognitive functioning, greater PA was associated with greater perceived CRCI-related difficulties and unmet needs in several domains ( p < 0.05). Conclusions Physical activity was associated with reduced perceived CRCI severity, supporting its recognition as a promising supportive care strategy. However, associations between greater physical activity participation and lower levels of perceived CRCI may not correspond with lower levels of CRCI-related difficulties and unmet needs. PA-based CRCI interventions should be embedded within holistic survivorship care models that proactively identify and address perceived CRCI-related difficulties and unmet supportive care needs.

title: Stability and Bifurcation Analysis for a Two-Species Diffusive Model with Memory-Based Diffusion
container-title: International Journal of Bifurcation and Chaos
3c05ed3f5570a7fe75407c355a60e4aa7902b774.abstract: Spatial memory has important influence on the mechanistic modeling of animal movements. In this paper, we study a model of two interacting species with sensitivity function and spatial memory. We first show the existence and global boundedness of positive solutions. We explore the influence of the sensitivity function on the stability and Turing bifurcation. Then the joint effect of the sensitivity function and the memory delay on the stability and spatio-temporal dynamics is investigated. We find that the high sensitivity of spatial memory is easier to induce Hopf bifurcation, generating spatially inhomogeneous periodic solutions, which is a new mechanism to induce Hopf bifurcation. Finally, the normal form of Hopf bifurcation is also derived.
