title: The dynamic relationship between L2 possible selves and learning experience during study abroad: A longitudinal multiple case study of Chinese language learners
container-title: International Review of Applied Linguistics in Language Teaching
fd7e0e31548a49c75d937704fa0f2b84198e17c9.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    This multiple case study employed the L2 motivational self-system (L2MSS) (Dörnyei, Zoltán. 2005.
                    <jats:italic>The psychology of the language learner: Individual differences in second language acquisition</jats:italic>
                    . Mahwah, NJ: Lawrence Erlbaum Associates, Inc; Dörnyei, Zoltán. 2009. The L2 motivational self-system. In Zoltán Dörnyei & Ema Ushioda (eds.),
                    <jats:italic>Motivation, language identity and the L2 self</jats:italic>
                    , 9–42. Clevedon, UK: Multilingual Matters) to understand the motivational dynamics of Chinese (Mandarin) language learners during a study abroad (SA) sojourn. It examined the qualitative changes in learners’ L2 possible selves by adopting the complex dynamic system theory (CDST) (Larsen-Freeman, Diane & Lynne Cameron. 2008.
                    <jats:italic>Complex systems and applied linguistics</jats:italic>
                    . Oxford: Oxford University Press) and the person-in-context perspective (Ushioda, Ema. 2009. A person-in-context relational view of emergent motivation, self and identity. In Zoltán Dörnyei & Ema Ushioda (eds.),
                    <jats:italic>Motivation, language identity and the L2 self</jats:italic>
                    , 215–228. Bristol: Multilingual Matters). Participants were three undergraduate Chinese language learners from different countries (Salvador, Myanmar, and Solomon Islands) enrolled at a Chinese university. Data were collected through a motivational questionnaire administered upon arrival, followed by four semi-structured interviews with each participant conducted over a four-month period during the first semester of their SA sojourn. Through thematic analysis, the study illustrates the process of how learners’ L2 possible selves were constantly refined during SA (e.g., developed more capable actual L2 selves, extended perceived ideal L2 selves, strengthened and internalized ought-to L2 selves). An ongoing interplay between L2 possible selves and learning experience was found: while learning experience abroad shaped learners’ L2 possible selves, their enriched possible selves further guided learners’ behaviors and, in turn, created new learning experiences.
                  </jats:p>

title: Research on support system and construction methods for super-large span tunnels based on NPR compensation effect
container-title: Engineering Computations
5967555765036b3795e476951856e13a6583732b.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Purpose</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The purpose of this study is to address the challenges associated with super-large span tunnels, which currently lack a clear definition and scientifically grounded construction methods and support system designs. To achieve this, the study aims to establish an innovative mechanical model for anchor cable compensation arches, investigate the performance of conventional versus negative Poisson's ratio (NPR) anchor cables and compare the effectiveness of different construction methods.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Design/methodology/approach</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Based on the innovative anchor cable compensation arch mechanical model developed for super-large span tunnels, this study employs a combined methodology of theoretical analysis and numerical simulation to systematically investigate tunnel stability and support efficiency. The research design involves establishing the nonlinear relationship between the arch's bearing capacity and excavation span, formulating stability criteria and support parameter principles, and conducting comparative numerical analyses of conventional versus NPR anchor cables' performance, along with evaluating the reserved core soil and double side heading construction methods through comparative assessment.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Findings</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The findings reveal a nonlinear negative correlation between the compensation arch's bearing capacity and the tunnel excavation span. Numerical comparisons demonstrate that NPR anchor cables significantly outperform conventional ones in enhancing support effectiveness and optimizing stress distribution in the surrounding rock. Furthermore, the reserved core soil method exhibits superior performance and broader applicability, especially in projects with limited longitudinal space, compared to the double side heading method.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Research limitations/implications</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study assumes the surrounding rock mass is isotropic, homogeneous and continuous, which may not fully capture the effects of joints, bedding planes or faults on local stress redistribution and deformation patterns. The critical span threshold (=16 m) and the observed advantages of NPR anchor cables are specific to Grade V granite conditions, the considered in situ stress state and the support parameters used. The conclusions should not be directly generalized to other geological environments, rock types, tunnel geometries or stress conditions without further validation.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Originality/value</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The originality of this study lies in the establishment of an innovative mechanical model for anchor cable compensation arches that accurately captures the nonlinear negative correlation between bearing capacity and excavation span in super-large span tunnels. Its value is demonstrated through the development of a comprehensive stability evaluation framework and the numerical verification of NPR anchor cables' superior support performance, together with the identification of the reserved core soil method as the optimal construction technique for spatially constrained projects, providing scientifically grounded solutions for the design and construction of super-large span tunnels.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Enabling large language models for automated compliance checking of BIM models in architectural engineering through semantic modelling and linking
container-title: Engineering, Construction and Architectural Management
5db3fef24b5354ab367e8b0aa6a854a486cc5a9c.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Purpose</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study examines how standardised Building Information Modelling (BIM) data modelling can support large language models (LLMs) in automated compliance checking of architectural project information requirements. The focus is the Level of Information Need (LOIN) for design deliverables. The study addresses the disconnect between LLM reasoning and standardised project information.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Design/methodology/approach</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>A constructive research approach is adopted to develop and evaluate an LLM-based compliance checking framework. BIM resources and LOIN-based requirements are transformed into semantic data through information modelling and linking. An Information Container for Linked Document Delivery (ICDD) organises project documents and semantic links. The Model Context Protocol (MCP) connects LLM interaction with graph querying, compliance checking and issue reporting services. The prototype uses data from a single architectural project. A controlled benchmark compares direct review, Graph Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) and MCP review.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Findings</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Direct review based on raw Turtle snippets showed limited performance because compliance evidence was often interpreted conservatively. Graph RAG achieved higher checking performance through structured graph retrieval, while MCP review achieved the best overall result by combining LLM-based task interpretation with tool-mediated checking. Performance varied across rule types. Explicit-data and derived-value rules were checked more reliably than extended data-structure rules, which were sensitive to alternative relation patterns.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Originality/value</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study presents a prototype approach to BIM–LLM integration for compliance-oriented project information management. Project resources, information requirements and checking rules are organised through ICDD and semantic graph data. MCP-mediated interaction links requirement interpretation with executable checking services, evidence retrieval and issue reporting, enabling traceable compliance review in project delivery.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: When adaptation has no endpoint: cognitive flexibility under prolonged organizational strain
container-title: International Journal of Organization Theory & Behavior
92698333062c10aa1921da14210cc39e769836e4.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Purpose</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This paper examines how cognition operates under conditions of prolonged organizational strain where demands persist, interpretations do not converge and disengagement does not occur. It challenges the dominant assumption in organizational behavior that cognitive processes under strain are inherently directional and oriented toward resolution, coherence or withdrawal.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Design/methodology/approach</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The paper develops a conceptual framework through integrative analysis of stress and coping, sensemaking and burnout literatures. It identifies a shared directional assumption across these perspectives and demonstrates its limitations under conditions of sustained and indeterminate strain. A new construct is introduced and formalized through a set of theoretical propositions.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Findings</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The analysis shows that individuals may sustain cognitive engagement without reducing demands, achieving interpretive coherence or disengaging. To account for this pattern, the paper introduces cognitive flexibility under prolonged organizational strain, defined as a mode of functioning characterized by interpretive openness, non-directional engagement and ongoing meaning adjustment without convergence.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Originality/value</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The paper contributes by identifying prolonged organizational strain as a distinct condition and re-specifying adaptation as sustained cognitive functioning without directional progression. It extends organizational behavior theory by explaining how cognition operates when resolution, coherence and disengagement do not structure activity.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Cognitive styles and resource orchestration capability: pathways to innovation and competitive advantage under environmental dynamism in hotels
container-title: Journal of Hospitality and Tourism Insights
01822006967d988fa49d250e9e8c6efe4d862551.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Purpose</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The study examines how hotel management uses cognitive styles to optimize resource allocation and gain competitive advantage amid rapid technological advances, changing customer needs, and intensified market competition. The study focuses on how the three cognitive styles-creating, planning, and knowing-influence organizational agility and resource orchestration capability.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Design/methodology/approach</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The research used a quantitative survey design. The researchers collected survey data from 325 hotel managers and used structural equation modelling to test the proposed theoretical framework.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Findings</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The results are in line with the framework suggested. The three cognitive styles have positive effects on both organizational agility and resource orchestration capability. The relationship between these capabilities and competitive advantage as well as organizational growth is mediated by organizational innovation. Environmental dynamism reinforces the effects of organizational agility and resource orchestration capability on innovation.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Practical implications</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The results give hotel leaders practical information about innovation that suggests that workforce development strategies and managerial practices should be in line with the latest market trends. It shows that managerial cognitive styles are central to developing dynamic capabilities, and that leadership training, recruitment, and strategic planning have implications to develop the creating, planning, and knowing styles to increase the agility of the organization, its resource management, and ability to innovate.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Originality/value</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The paper combines the Dynamic Capabilities Theory and the Resource Orchestration Theory in explaining how hotels gain competitive advantage as a result of innovation in an environment of market instability. It also determines managerial cognitive styles to be the core microfoundations of dynamic capability development and provides a new understanding of how organizations develop strategic flexibility and economic value in the hospitality industry.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Green HRM and sustainability outcomes: the roles of employee engagement, servant leadership and green innovation practices in Vietnam
container-title: Employee Relations: The International Journal
d02eb35ac777cba382866823c4137702af90e4a0.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Purpose</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study examines how green human resource management (GHRM) is associated with sustainability outcomes through green work engagement (GWE) and whether servant leadership (SER) and Green Innovation Practices (GIP) strengthen different relationships within this pathway.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Design/methodology/approach</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>A cross-sectional survey was conducted among employees across industries in Vietnam. Of 385 questionnaires received, 364 complete responses were analyzed using confirmatory factor analysis and structural equation modeling. Indirect and interaction effects were examined using bootstrapping.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Findings</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>GHRM was positively associated with GWE, which mediated its relationships with green innovative work behavior (GIWB) and perceived green performance (PGP). SER strengthened the GHRM–GWE relationship, whereas GIP strengthened the relationships between GWE and both outcomes.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Practical implications</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Organizations may benefit from aligning green HR practices with supportive supervisory leadership and concrete green innovation practices. HR managers can embed environmental objectives into core HR practices, while supervisors and operational leaders can support employee engagement and opportunities for environmental improvement.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Originality/value</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The study provides a boundary-condition refinement of the GHRM–engagement–outcome pathway by distinguishing relational and organizational conditions at different relationships within the model. Specifically, servant leadership strengthens the GHRM–GWE relationship, whereas GIP strengthens the GWE–outcome relationships, extending understanding of sustainable employment relationships in Vietnam.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Ambivalent close ties and cognitive functioning: Does coping play a role?
container-title: Innovation in Aging
419f0d405dbcdc84839382b903d619de51c8a365.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Background and Objectives</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Close relationships that are characterized by both positive and negative qualities (i.e., ambivalent ties) are common in later life and often give rise to interpersonal tensions with deleterious consequences for well-being. However, little is known about their effect on cognitive health. These effects may depend on seldom-studied interpersonal coping strategies that may either stimulate or deplete cognitive resources. This study tested whether ambivalent ties relate to lower cognitive functioning among older adults, and whether interpersonal coping strategies moderate these associations.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Research Design and Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>As part of the Daily Experiences and Well-being Study (DEWS), participants (N = 271, ages 65-89) completed an in-person baseline interview assessing positive and negative qualities of their close social relationships and overall cognitive functioning (composite of four tests), followed by a self-administered questionnaire assessing three interpersonal coping strategies (engaged, avoidant, destructive).</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Linear regression models revealed that a greater proportion of ambivalent ties was associated with worse overall cognitive functioning, but this association was not moderated by any interpersonal coping strategy. Sensitivity analyses of the separate cognitive tests revealed, unexpectedly, that greater use of engaged coping strengthened the association between ambivalent ties and worse executive functioning performance.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Discussion and Implications</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>A greater proportion of ambivalent ties in one’s social network is associated with lower cognitive functioning among older adults, a link that may not easily be buffered through coping. Results suggest that ambivalent ties are an understudied important potential risk factor for adverse cognitive outcomes in later life.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Drinking-Water 4,4′-Methylenedianiline Establishes a Longitudinally Tractable Mouse Model of Cholestatic Liver Injury
container-title: Toxicological Sciences
443b48a811c5bde614e8b42d548b037c795de9b5.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Longitudinal studies of liver injury require models that can be maintained with simple administration, low procedure-related stress, and acceptable survival. Drinking-water thioacetamide (TAA-DW) is useful for this purpose, but it mainly produces centrilobular hepatocellular injury. Few drinking-water models are available for cholestatic liver injury. Here, we tested whether 4,4′-methylenedianiline (MDA), a known bile-duct-damaging hepatotoxicant, can be used to build a practical drinking-water model of cholestatic liver injury in mice. Male C57BL/6JJcl mice received MDA in drinking water for up to 28 days. A route- and administration-schedule-matched TAA-DW model was used as a reference. Drinking-water MDA (MDA-DW) caused sustained ALT elevation without observed mortality under the tested regimen. Compared with TAA-DW, MDA-DW produced stronger cholestatic biochemical features, including increased ALP, TBIL, and TCHO. Histology showed bile duct hyperplasia with degeneration, periportal/peribiliary fibrosis, and scattered focal hepatocellular necrosis. Whole-slide image analysis supported the distinct lesion distribution between MDA-DW and TAA-DW. Early time-resolved multimodal profiling showed model-specific responses: MDA-DW showed ALT elevation around Days 2–3, increased CD8-positive T cells on Day 8, and enrichment of fibrinolysis-related gene sets, whereas TAA-DW showed a sharp early injury peak and transient eosinophil increase. Impact Statement: This study expands the range of drinking-water liver injury models by providing a low-mortality MDA-DW model with cholestatic liver injury. The model offers a simple platform for time-resolved studies of liver injury progression, tissue remodeling, and model-specific inflammatory responses.</jats:p>

title: Elite basketball athletes at rest: enhanced sensorimotor activity and reduced cognitive load
container-title: Brain Communications
a867f1111467f16d2068d87c0420c2f94da66236.abstract:
<jats:p>Long-term sports training is associated with experience-dependent brain plasticity, but the core functional architecture of open-skill athletes remains unclear. As a representative open-skill sport, basketball requires rapid sensorimotor integration in dynamic settings. This study examined resting-state functional characteristics in elite basketball athletes, focusing on interactions between sensorimotor and advanced cognitive systems. Fifty-seven national first-class basketball athletes (mean age 20.17 ± 1.87 years, twenty-three males) and sixty-one healthy controls (mean age 20.33 ± 1.89 years, twenty-five males) underwent resting-state functional MRI. Fractional amplitude of low-frequency fluctuations (fALFF) and degree centrality (DC) were used to evaluate regional spontaneous activity and overall brain network integration, respectively. Group comparisons controlled for age, sex and head motion. Athletes showed a dual pattern of functional differences. First, athletes showed changed sensorimotor processing: significantly higher fALFF and DC in the superior temporal gyrus, cerebellum (anterior and posterior), parahippocampal gyrus, cuneus, and lingual gyrus, indicating stronger neural substrates for visuospatial integration and motor coordination. Second, athletes showed greater neural efficiency: lower fALFF and DC in the middle frontal gyrus, cingulate cortex, medial prefrontal cortex, and precuneus (parts of the default mode network), which may reflect enhanced cognitive control and reduced cognitive load. Notably, the insula and midbrain showed a distinct pattern (increased fALFF but decreased DC), indicating a specialized "high-readiness and low-redundancy" state for salience monitoring. Long-term basketball training is associated with distinct patterns of functional brain characteristics, marked by improved sensorimotor processing and greater neural efficiency within cognitive control networks. These training-related neural patterns may serve as biomarkers for athlete evaluation and selection.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>Abbreviated summary</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>Wang et al. report that elite basketball athletes exhibit distinct resting-state functional brain characteristics, including enhanced sensorimotor-related activity and altered cognitive control network organization. These findings suggest that basketball expertise is associated with specialized neural organization supporting the demands of open-skill sports.</jats:p>

title: Water footprint of large AI models: risks to global water security and sustainable optimization strategies
container-title: Water Policy
7bc4d996ef1e8d7d275c67c8a8741273c4f6cf4e.abstract:
<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Diagram linking AI model training and inference to lifecycle water use, estimated at 4.2–6.6 billion m³ annually by 2027, and showing water reuse, efficient cooling, smarter workloads, and standardized reporting as strategies to protect global water security.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>The rapid proliferation of large-scale artificial intelligence (AI) models has introduced a significant yet underexamined environmental challenge: freshwater consumption. This narrative review synthesizes scientific literature, industry sustainability reports, and case studies to quantify the water footprint of AI systems across their full lifecycle, from semiconductor fabrication and data center operations to electricity generation and supply chains. Direct water use occurs primarily through evaporative and liquid cooling in data centers, where a single large facility can consume 11,000–19,000m3/day. Indirect water use is embedded in electricity generation and chip manufacturing, with advanced fabrication plants drawing 10,000–37,000m3/day. Major technology companies, including Google, Microsoft, and Meta, collectively consume billions of cubic meters in 2022–2024, with consumption rising alongside accelerating AI deployment. Critically, over 52% of the world's top 100 data centers are projected to be located in high water stress regions by 2030, where AI infrastructure increasingly competes with agricultural, municipal, and ecological needs. Sustainable alternatives, including immersion cooling, nonpotable water reuse, and AI-driven workload optimization, offer measurable reductions but remain inconsistently adopted. The direct and indirect water footprints of AI models during their entire lifecycle are reviewed. Two of the main direct water usage sources are semiconductor manufacturing and data center cooling. Clip manufacturing and electricity generation significantly increase the indirect water footprint of AI. In areas with scarce freshwater supplies, the growth of AI technology may worsen water stress. Standardized reporting frameworks and lifecycle-based water accounting are urgently needed to safeguard global water security.</jats:p>

title: Joint associations of handgrip strength and chair-stand performance with motoric cognitive risk syndrome in older adults
container-title: The Journals of Gerontology, Series A: Biological Sciences and Medical Sciences
7a38c90b286ffa04131bcbafb5ff6cbfb6a0faf0.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Motor dysfunction is associated with cognitive vulnerability, but whether impairments across body regions jointly contribute to motoric cognitive risk syndrome (MCR) remains unclear. We examined the independent and joint associations of handgrip strength and chair-stand test (CST) with MCR.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This cross-sectional study included 6258 dementia-free older adults (mean age 71.5 ± 6.6 years; 63.1% women) from a community-based cohort. Handgrip strength and CST performance were used to define upper- and lower-extremity motor impairment. Participants were classified as normal, handgrip weakness only, CST impairment only, or combined motor impairment. Multivariable logistic regression was performed with adjustment for demographic, socioeconomic, lifestyle, and clinical factors. Additive and multiplicative interactions were assessed.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>MCR was present in 10.4% of participants. Using the A/B CST cutoff as the primary definition, adjusted odds ratios (95% confidence intervals) for MCR, compared with normal function, were 1.84 (1.14–2.97) for handgrip weakness only, 4.17 (2.97–5.85) for CST impairment only, and 9.17 (6.56–12.81) for combined motor impairment. Associations were directionally consistent across alternative CST cutoffs. A positive additive interaction was observed at the A/B CST cutoff (relative excess risk due to interaction = 3.48; attributable proportion = 0.40; and synergy index = 1.83), whereas multiplicative interaction was not positive.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Combined handgrip weakness and poorer CST performance were strongly associated with prevalent MCR. A positive additive interaction at the primary CST cutoff suggests that joint motor impairment may help characterize MCR-related vulnerability in older adults.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Health, Fiscal, and Societal Economic Consequences of Traditional Tobacco Control Policies and Generation-Based Sales Bans in Türkiye: A Dynamic Cohort Simulation Model
container-title: Nicotine & Tobacco Research
265c5f69ea3406a353a3bf813095bb8b880a9462.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Introduction</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Tobacco use remains a cause of avoidable disease and economic loss in Türkiye. Evidence is limited on the consequences of generation-based sales restrictions compared with conventional tobacco control.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>We developed a dynamic open-cohort state-transition model of Türkiye's population aged ≥15 years. Over 50 annual cycles, baseline smoking was compared with enhanced cessation, stronger prevention, and a fully effective generation-based sales ban. Outcomes included smoking prevalence, disease cases and deaths, life-years, disability-adjusted life years (DALYs), healthcare savings, tobacco tax revenue, productivity, and household cigarette expenditure. Monetary outcomes were expressed in 2025 international dollars; uncertainty was assessed using 1,000 Monte Carlo simulations.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>By year 50, smoking prevalence was 30.4% under baseline, 27.5% with enhanced cessation, 24.2% with stronger prevention, and 5.6% under the generation-based sales ban. The ban prevented 8.45 million disease cases and 1.87 million disease-specific deaths and generated 10.48 million discounted life-years and 18.26 million discounted DALYs. Discounted healthcare savings were 3.64, 7.39, and 13.40 billion 2025 international dollars for cessation, prevention, and the ban; corresponding societal gains were 11.37, 27.55, and 61.85 billion. All policies reduced tobacco tax receipts, producing negative net fiscal effects.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>A fully effective generation-based sales ban produced the largest health and societal gains. It should complement cessation support and conventional tobacco control, with planning for declining tobacco tax revenue.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Business Ukrainian in the Age of Artificial Intelligence: Transformation of Language Norms, Professional Etiquette, and Communicative Culture
container-title: Revista Cultura Científica
413bbafc3d26779772004cb1cebd79962c05dd94.abstract: <jats:p>The article develops a psycholinguistic account of how generative artificial intelligence changes professional Ukrainian-language writing, with particular attention to language norms, professional speech etiquette, communicative culture, and the educational workplace. A structured theoretical synthesis was conducted on a corpus of 29 peer-reviewed journal articles from 2022–2026. The corpus was organised into four evidence blocks: artificial intelligence in business and workplace communication; pragmatic behaviour of large language models; politeness and email communication in academic and workplace settings; and Ukrainian psycholinguistic and speech-etiquette contexts. Studies were coded for communication domain, speech act or genre, role of artificial intelligence, normative and pragmatic outcomes, relational perceptions, and contextual limitations. Because research designs and outcome measures were heterogeneous, the analysis used qualitative comparative synthesis rather than meta-analysis. The synthesis reveals three recurrent transformations. First, generative systems often strengthen formal correctness, structural coherence, and explicit politeness. Second, these gains can be accompanied by communicative conventionalisation: increased formality, formulaic organisation, reduced lexical or strategic variability, and weaker adjustment to the local interpersonal context. Third, artificial-intelligence mediation changes attributional and relational judgements: perceived authorship, authenticity, sincerity, trust, and willingness to maintain interaction may diverge from ratings of professionalism or clarity. These transformations are not uniform; their magnitude depends on communicative risk, status relations, degree of imposition, genre conventionality, source disclosure, and the extent of human revision. On this basis, a three-component model of normative optimisation, communicative conventionalisation, and attributional-relational shift is proposed. For Ukrainian professional communication, especially in higher education, generative artificial intelligence should be treated as a mediator of linguistic choice rather than a neutral editing device. The key research gap is the lack of direct empirical evidence on Ukrainian-language AI-mediated professional writing, which limits straightforward transfer of findings from English-dominant studies.</jats:p>

title: A Novel Well-Test-Based and ESO-Driven Fracture Model Calibration Method for Dual-Porosity/Dual-Permeability Models in Naturally Fractured Carbonate Reservoirs Using Embedded Discrete Fracture Modeling (EDFM)
container-title: ADIPEC
5eb1ec6a7a9b1b92f77e0c59e861d769de0a088a.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>This study presents a new workflow for well test-driven fracture model calibration using the Embedded Discrete Fracture Model (EDFM) available in a high-fidelity reservoir simulator. EDFM explicitly models fractures as embedded conductive features within the matrix, allowing fracture flow behavior to be governed by their distinct attributes. By integrating well test interpretation with EDFM-based simulations and optimizing it with an Evolution Strategy Optimization (ESO) workflow, while modelling fracture dip and azimuth as they observed to keep geological reliability; aperture, and permeability are constrained based on their respective effects on the pressure derivative response of the well test. The resulting calibrated fracture properties are upscaled to dual-porosity/dual-permeability models, resulting in a more reliable fracture grid representation and significantly improved matching of well test-derived production behavior.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>EDFM represents fractures as lower-dimensional elements embedded in the matrix grid without grid remeshing, with matrix-fracture and fracture-fracture flow modeled through non-neighbor connections. In contrast, dual-porosity/dual-permeability (DP/DK) models employ effective fracture properties defined at the grid scale. In this novel approach for well test calibration, a discrete fracture network is constructed by integrating geological and petrophysical data and distributed along the well trajectory. Fracture properties are calibrated through ESO-driven history matching of well-test pressure and pressure-derivative data. The calibrated fracture permeability tensor, fracture porosity, and matrix-fracture transfer coefficient are upscaled and applied as grid properties in a field-scale dual porosity/dual permeability model.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>Following history matching of the well-test pressure and pressure-derivative responses, the estimated fracture attributes—including fracture aperture, permeability, dip azimuth, and dip angle—are upscaled to 3D grid properties for the fracture grids. These upscaled properties are then inserted into the field-scale history-matching workflow. The well test-calibrated fracture representation yields a consistent match to bottom hole pressure, water production rate, and liquid production rate for the specified well. Furthermore, alignment of fracture-set dip azimuth, dip angle, and the aperture with the well-test response ensures calibration of the fracture permeability tensor, thereby constraining the dominant flow directions toward the wellbore.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>This paper presents a novel workflow for three-dimensional well test-based and ESO-driven fracture calibration using a sector-scale, high-fidelity reservoir simulator. The flexible modeling capabilities of the simulator enable a consistent transition from well-level history matching to field-scale history matching by integrating geological interpretation, well-log measurements, and well-test data. The proposed methodology introduces a data-driven, optimization-based, static-to-dynamic three-dimensional fracture characterization workflow for naturally fractured carbonate reservoirs, ensuring consistency between fracture geometry, petrophysical properties, and dynamic flow responses.</jats:p>

title: AI-Assisted Automated Compositional PVT Modeling: Model Construction, EOS Tuning, and Validation Using Laboratory and Field Data
container-title: ADIPEC
2103dc6c37be56fd0371a901225e70c00847fa13.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Accurate PVT models are essential for predicting the phase behavior of reservoir fluids in digital twins, reservoir simulation models, and integrated asset models. Conventional tuning is usually based on manual adjustment or mathematical regression of equation-of-state (EOS) parameters against laboratory experiments performed near reservoir temperature. Although manual adjustment can reproduce experimental curves with high accuracy, the resulting model may still show significant deviations under actual field operating conditions or for other tests from the same formation. Mathematical regression can also provide acceptable numerical accuracy, but it often produces physically inconsistent trends in PVT-model parameters with molecular weight.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>This study presents an automatic tuning algorithm for gas-condensate PVT models that combines a step-by-step tuning approach with optimization objective functions and uses both laboratory measurements and field data. Field low-temperature separation data are included because they represent operating conditions that differ substantially from standard PVT experiments and therefore provide an important test of model reliability.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>The workflow also incorporates AI-assisted data preparation, using large language models to extract and structure component compositions, PVT experiments, and separation data from laboratory reports. The extraction workflow was validated on 6 laboratory reports. The average field-level extraction accuracy was 90 %, while the time required for preparing one PVT dataset was reduced from approximately 5-8 hours of manual entry to 10 minutes of engineering review and correction. The AI layer therefore reduces routine data-entry effort while retaining engineering control before EOS initialization and tuning.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>The algorithm is based on a staged constrained optimization approach combining physically guided parameter tuning, best-state selection with guard constraints, and local numerical refinement. It tunes the main thermodynamic parameters controlling phase behavior, including the critical properties of heavy fractions, binary interaction coefficients (BICs), acentric factors, and shift parameters. The procedure aims to reproduce laboratory PVT data and field predictions of separator-fluid density and condensate-gas factor under production conditions.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>The approach can be applied to individual reservoir-fluid systems or to several systems simultaneously. Global tuning produces a consistent set of model parameters and prevents improvement for one fluid composition from causing unacceptable errors for others. The model was tested using fluid data from a Russian gas-condensate field and demonstrated good agreement with laboratory and field measurements.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>The practical relevance of the study lies in automated PVT-model tuning for real gas-condensate reservoir fluids and in extending model validation beyond laboratory experiments. In this study, the algorithm was tested using six fluid compositions from different Russian fields. The tuned models can be used for separator calculations, production forecasting, field-development studies, monitoring, and integration into digital field-management and production-simulation systems.</jats:p>

title: Advanced Gas Lift Production and Network Solutions for Large-Scale Operations: Enabling Sustainable Flaring Reduction and Net Zero Objectives
container-title: ADIPEC
1e077d322e1d209b81cc5716fd7de35b95a1c706.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Conventional tie-ins and brownfield upgrades on high-pressure gas lift networks may require complete header depressurization, creating routine flaring, loss of valuable lean gas, and exposure to production interruption. This paper presents a field-proven alternative that uses existing gas lift wellhead bullheading or rocking lines to route isolated header inventory through oil production flowlines to the processing facility. The work combined piping-integrity verification, wellhead configuration screening, hydraulic and process-safety review, operating procedure development, and controlled field execution. The reported campaign avoided up to 46.0 MMscf of lean-gas flaring and 3,266 metric tons of CO2 equivalent, while preserving operational continuity. Additional reported value included 268,000 bbl of production gain, approximately USD 13.4 million in production value, USD 72,000 of avoided lean-gas buyback, and avoidance of an estimated USD 52 million annulus bleed-off piping modification. The solution required no major capital project and created a scalable framework for future greenfield and brownfield gas lift tie-ins. The principal contribution is the conversion of underused wellhead connectivity into a controlled gas-recovery pathway, aligning commissioning execution with flaring reduction and net-zero objectives.</jats:p>

title: A Novel Early Production Facility (EPF) Concept for Multi-Operator Field Tie-In Using Full-Range Multiphase Flow Metering and Model-Driven Optimization: Chadar–Faragh Fields, Libya
container-title: ADIPEC
c18ba76b8404e16f1f8dd239c143053d9b028890.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>The development of marginal and early-stage oil fields in the MENA region is often constrained by high capital expenditures (CAPEX), extended project schedules, and the need for dedicated surface processing and custody metering infrastructure. This paper presents a novel concept implemented in the Chadar Field (Libya), which instead of Early Production Facility (EPF) enables direct tie-in of untreated multiphase production to a third-party processing facility operated by Waha Oil Company (WOC) at the Faragh Field. The proposed architecture eliminates upstream separation and dedicated processing trains, achieving CAPEX savings of 51–67% and reducing project execution time by 40–50%, while significantly accelerating first oil. The concept integrates allocation-grade full-range multiphase flow metering (FR MPFM), real-time digital optimization in modern software, and a multi-operator governance framework in concession. Field implementation achieved additional production rates of 4,500 BOEPD and 15 MMSCFD, with cumulative oil production exceeding 1.2 million barrels during the initial operational phase. This work represents the first documented deployment of a fully integrated EPF that enables cross-operator production integration without physical phase segregation, while maintaining accurate production allocation through model-driven surveillance (AlfaFlow platform). The approach provides a scalable, low-CAPEX template for marginal field developments and introduces a new paradigm for multi-operator production coordination in complex and remote onshore environments using Integrated Production Optimisation Service (IPOS).</jats:p>

title: Transforming Carbonates Well Performance: Large-Scale Deployment of SRP in Horizontal Wells in North Oman
container-title: ADIPEC
3c72affd9157a0ae92f07506c0d3f90847150535.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Daleel Petroleum is one of the leading operators in the Sultanate of Oman, developing mainly horizontal wells in carbonate reservoirs. While these wells typically demonstrate strong initial production rates, they often experience rapid early-life decline driven by insufficient water injection support, high gas interference, and unstable production behavior. This paper presents a comprehensive review of artificial lift strategy evolution in Block-5, highlighting the transition from conventional systems including natural flow, electrical submersible pumps (ESP), and progressive cavity pumps (PCP) to sucker rod pumps (SRP) as a primary lift method. Despite being relatively uncommon in carbonate applications within North Oman, SRP deployment has proven to be a transformative solution when combined with tailored design and optimized operational practices.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>A comprehensive, data-driven evaluation was conducted across more than 600 wells in Block-5, analyzing production performance, failure rates, and operational efficiency of various artificial lift systems. The study involved systematic well screening, candidate selection, and phased implementation of SRP systems in deviated and horizontal wells. These installations have been significantly enhanced over time with continuous optimization including the pump design and control automation system along with maintaining suitable well flowing pressure of individual wells. Additionally, integrated solutions implemented including deploying the pumps deep in the deviated and horizontal sections. Comparative analysis against ESP system was performed using key performance indicators such as run life, production rates, deferment, and intervention frequency.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>Field-wide deployment of SRP systems demonstrated significant performance improvements over ESP installations. Oil production increased by approximately 28%, primarily due to improved drawdown control and reduced gas interference effects. Failure rates decreased by 86%, and oil deferment was reduced by 78% as a result of improved runtime and operational stability. Additionally, workover frequency and associated costs were reduced by more than 50%, driven by fewer equipment failures and much smaller number of trips. The study highlights that SRP systems, when properly designed and optimized, can effectively handle high gas liquid ratios and unstable inflow conditions typical of carbonate reservoirs. These findings confirm that SRP can outperform ESP systems in specific operating environments especially in high GOR and low inflow performance areas.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>This paper offers a comprehensive review of a large-scale, unconventional application of SRP systems in horizontal carbonate wells, a practice rarely implemented in Northern Oman. It introduces a data driven artificial lift selection framework and demonstrates how tailored SRP design and deployment can outperform ESP systems under high gas interference conditions, offering a scalable and cost-effective solution for similar reservoirs.</jats:p>

title: A Novel Model for Predicting Carbon Sequestration and Gas Recovery of CCUS-EGR in Gas Reservoirs
container-title: ADIPEC
24e4f8659d119070640e97062621bbc71eabd75e.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Under the background of net-zero emissions, CCUS-EGR (carbon capture, utilization and storage & enhanced gas recovery) has become an important technology to enhance gas recovery and reduce greenhouse gas emissions. However, it's still unclear how much gas recovery can be improved and how much CO2 (carbon dioxide) can be sequestered in gas reservoirs through CCUS-EGR. Therefore, it's neccesary to establish a theoretical model to quantitatively evaluate the stimulation performance and carbon sequestration capacity of CCUS-EGR. Firstly, a novel model for predicting gas recovery and carbon sequestration of CCUS-EGR was proposed. In this model, a key parameter, CO2 sweep area, could be analytically and efficiently determined by establishing material balance equations and simplifying the distribution characteristics of gas components, which was usually calculated through time-consuming numerical simulation in previous research. Then, the new model was applied to the X pilot area in Ordos Basin to evaluate the stimulation performance and carbon sequestration capacity of CCUS-EGR. Finally, sensitivity analysis was conducted to evaluate how key parameters influence recovery factor and CO2 storage of CCUS-EGR. The following conclusions were drawn: (a) The recovery increment of CCUS-EGR was comprehensively influenced by four key factors, including sweep efficiency of pressure drop, depletion efficiency in depletion development stage, CO2 sweep efficiency and CO2 displacement efficiency; (b) Carbon sequestration capacity of CCUS-EGR was jointly determined by reservoir pore volume, gas recovery and formation pressure after CO2 injection; (c) In the tight gas reservoir at the X pilot area, sweep efficiency of pressure drop, depletion efficiency in depletion development stage, CO2 sweep efficiency and CO2 displacement efficiency would reach 51.4%, 70.3%, 61.6% and 87.3% respectively, and the recovery increment of CCUS-EGR was estimated to be 5.4%; (d) CCUS-EGR was expected to approximately increase natural gas production by 7.5×107 cubic meters and storage CO2 by 4.82×105 tons in the pilot area. This research innovatively constructed a new model for predicting gas recovery and carbon sequestration of CCUS-EGR in gas reservoirs. It could quantitatively evaluate the potential of production stimulation and carbon sequestration of CCUS-EGR in the X pilot area. The research outcomes provide a solid theoretical and practical reference for a large-scale application of CCUS-EGR technology in gas reservoirs in China.</jats:p>

title: Mobile Solar-Diesel Hybrid Power Solution for Jet Pumps in Abu Dhabi: Field Deployment of a Containerized Energy-As-A-Service Model for Off-Grid Oilfield Production
container-title: ADIPEC
de31d7b58b4f1721617ba6d3670e8c4db4b1c054.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>This paper presents the design, field deployment, and operational evaluation of a mobile solar-diesel hybrid power system used to supply electricity to temporary jet pumps in off-grid wellsite locations in Abu Dhabi, UAE deployed by an onshore oil and gas operator in the United Arab Emirates (UAE). The pilot was developed to demonstrate whether a containerized renewable-power solution could reduce diesel dependence while maintaining the continuity, power quality, and operational flexibility required by artificial-lift applications that were previously powered by traditional diesel generators. The deployed architecture combined a mobile solar container with inverters, integrated power electronics, a hybrid control system, diesel generation sized to the pump load with prime and backup configurations, fuel monitoring, and a remote monitoring platform. The solution was delivered under an energy-as-a-service model, allowing the operator to obtain a complete power-generation service without assuming responsibility for the hybrid plant's day-to-day operation and maintenance.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>The pilot covered several well locations in the UAE with different deployment and approval conditions. One unit achieved sustained hybrid operation with 16% solar contribution and 100% availability during its operating period using the original unchanged diesel generator setup, while the second unit achieved a 21% solar contribution with availability of at least 99.9% over more than twelve months of continuous operation, also with the original diesel generator setup. A third location operated initially with a correctly sized diesel generator achieved a 21% solar contribution with availability of at least 99.9% over more than six months of continuous operation. Based on the well-level energy data available through 31st July 2026, the three locations delivered approximately 961 MWh in aggregate, with approximately 140 MWh attributable to solar generation at the two sites where photovoltaic was deployed and no solar-attributable outage was recorded, which is equivalent to approximately 63,000 liters of diesel saved.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>The field experience demonstrates that the technical integration of mobile solar with diesel generation can provide reliable power to artificial-lift loads while reducing fuel consumption, generator operating hours, acoustic impact, and maintenance burden. The principal limitation on higher solar penetration during the pilot was not the hybrid technology itself, but operational administration complexity. The pilot also identified the importance of correctly sizing diesel generators before mobilization, resolving electrical interfaces with variable-speed-drive equipment, and establishing documentation and permit requirements before equipment reaches site. The results support further deployment of containerized solar-diesel systems for temporary wellsite power, with battery energy storage and power-conversion equipment offering a pathway toward substantially higher renewable penetration.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>This project marks one of the region's most pioneering mobile solar-diesel hybrid integrations for powering active jet pumps and offers practical insights for scaling sustainable solutions in upstream operations. It provides valuable operational insights into the potential for hybrid power systems to support decarbonization targets in high-demand upstream environments. The successful operation over the pilot period underscores the feasibility of scaling this solution to multiple locations across the operator's portfolio while adding battery storage capabilities to increase diesel savings. The project highlights the operator's proactive approach toward sustainable energy practices, aligned with the operator's target of net zero by 2045 and the national target of net zero by 2050.</jats:p>

title: Offshore Sustainable Operating Model (SOM): Pioneering a One-To-Two-Week No-Touch Concept on a Producing Offshore Complex
container-title: ADIPEC
ba906fc11b6747575558235ffdf9cb170b808088.abstract:
<jats:p>ADNOC Offshore is demonstrating an outcome not yet achieved by any producing offshore operator in the GCC: a producing, brownfield offshore complex sustaining safe, reliable operation for two-week periods with no operations or maintenance personnel on board. The Sustainable Operating Model (SOM) is the vehicle for that ambition, rebuilding the entire operating model across one greenfield & one brownfield assets around this single, unifying objective. Central to that rebuild is a further distinction: SOM does only overlay artificial intelligence onto existing workflows but redesigns operations, decision rights, and organizational structure around AI from the outset. The difference between an operation that is merely AI-enabled and one that is genuinely AI-native, applied here at the scale of an entire producing complex, and the foundation of ADNOC's ambition to become the world's most AI-enabled energy company.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>That ambition translates into three measurable commitments: a two-week no-touch cycle marking a direct step toward Normally Unattended Facility status; an optimization in combined unit operating cost, delivered through leaner operations rather than one-off cuts; and investment payback within two years, with value continuing to compound thereafter. These are not three separate targets; an asset that no longer requires a permanent crew is, by construction, one that costs less to run and pays back faster.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>Delivering this requires six focus areas working as a single system: control, orchestration, workforce, maintenance, well intervention, and logistics. Coordinated through a Collaborative Working Environment that turns continuous AI-generated insight into real-time decisions across every discipline it touches. None of these levers deliver value in isolation; the evidence so far confirms it only appears once they move together. Behind them sits a substantial physical re-engineering of the assets themselves, converting control infrastructure from observation to action, and a workforce brought along deliberately, through structured upskilling, on-the-job development, piloting, and staged communication, rather than assumed to adapt on its own.</jats:p>

title: Assessment Method and Influencing Factors Analysis of Unconventional Hydrocarbon Recoverable Reserves Based on Coupled Fracture Flow Model
container-title: ADIPEC
adb43fdbb0afed98677df2f058ecdcce211009a1.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Addressing the unique geological characteristics of unconventional resources—such as low porosity and permeability—requires specialized development techniques, notably horizontal drilling and hydraulic fracturing, which differ significantly from conventional reservoir approaches. Consequently, conventional recoverable reserves evaluation methods are not directly applicable. Developing accurate and reliable assessment techniques for unconventional reserves under existing technological constraints remains a critical challenge for global operators. The assessment of recoverable reserves in unconventional oil and gas resources using integrated geo-engineering modeling involves four key steps: First, iterative refinement of the model is conducted based on geological data from existing wells, integrating well log attributes and seismic inversion results. Using kriging variogram interpolation constrained by seismic inversion data, detailed attribute models are built at a small-layer scale to enhance the accuracy of reservoir properties, gas content, and mechanical models. Second, multi-disciplinary data—including geological, engineering, and production data—are utilized to perform full 3D coupled simulation of hydraulic fractures. This incorporates 3D geomechanical and discrete fracture network (DFN) models, accounting for stress shadow effects, natural fracture distribution, and proppant transport and settling, with validation through microseismic data to accurately characterize post-fracture geometry. Third, a mathematical and numerical model is established that couples nonlinear oil-gas-water flow in micro-nano pores with stress-sensitive effects in the reservoir and fractures, integrating multiple flow mechanisms and complex fracture morphology. Finally, embedded fully coupled fracture modeling enables numerical simulation preprocessing for complex fracture networks in horizontal wells. Combined with actual production data, 4D geomechanical and production history matching is performed to evaluate post-fracturing productivity, providing technical support for recoverable reserves assessment and optimization of development strategies. The recoverable reserves of unconventional resources are not a fixed value but vary with horizontal section length and stimulation scale, directly impacting both recoverable volume and economic viability. Key operational factors include the number of horizontal wells, lateral length, stage length, cluster count, proppant and fluid volumes, and injection rate. Through multi-factor data analysis, 28 parameters were normalized to minimize absolute value errors and enhance the accuracy of controlling factor identification. Combined with recoverable reserves evaluation, cross-variable analysis revealed the following order of influence: Among geological parameters, reservoir contact length demonstrates the highest significance, followed by total organic carbon and then gas saturation; for engineering parameters, proppant intensity shows the greatest influence, ahead of total fluid volume and injection rate. Building on integrated geological-reservoir studies, a high-resolution 3D model incorporating multi-scale, multi-disciplinary data was developed to collaboratively optimize engineering designs, enabling precise and economically viable reserves assessment.</jats:p>

title: Uncertainty Reduction of Hydraulic Fracture Simulation Using 3D DFN Coupled Model for Production Enhancement in Unconventional Resources
container-title: ADIPEC
af568f6d24dea8ced17ea52f06791a62ffd47794.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Hydraulic fracturing in shale reservoirs is significantly different from conventional formation due to the interactions between the created hydraulic fracture and the pre-existing natural fractures. The propagation of hydraulic fractures in the fractured rock mass is achieved by breaking the predefined fracture plane in either tensile opening or slip. Therefore, natural fracture modeling is one of the most important factors that affect the geometry of hydraulic fractures. The hydraulic fractures propagation behavior is simulated in a fully coupled with 3D DFN (Discrete fracture network) modeling, which means that the fluid exists in the natural fractures results in pore pressure on the blocks while the deformation of blocks also affects the fluid flow in the fractures by changing the aperture size. Furthermore, the dynamic hydraulic fractures propagation can be assessed enabling a direct prediction of the occurrence of micro-seismicity, including the timing, location, magnitude and source mechanism/moment tensor. The technique for hydraulic fracture propagation simulation fully-coupled 3D natural fracture modeling was applied in 5 horizontal wells of the shale oil reservoir. The successful hydraulic fracture treatments enlarged the fracture geometry including length and height, improved the well conductivity, re-stimulated the natural fractures and subsequently greatly increased the well productivity. Compared with homogenous modeling used for hydraulic fracture propagation simulation, the uncertainty of the fracture modeling geometry can be greatly reduced verified by micro-seismic patterns, the cross-over analysis among research results, the actual micro-seismic patterns and production data. The uncertainty of hydraulic fracture geometries reduced by 35.2%，the consistency of numerical simulation and productivity prediction increased by 22.5%.The case study shows that hydraulic fracture path reorientation or block when intersect with 3D DFN modeling in propagation process, the coupled model is used to identify the characteristic pressure signature and micro-seismic patterns associated with different hydraulic fracture geometries. This research results provides insight for the diagnostic of hydraulic fracture propagation and suggestions for treatment optimization.</jats:p>

title: Objective Pre-Shift Cognitive Readiness as a Human Factors Barrier: Field Evidence from Offshore Operations
container-title: ADIPEC
cd7a65cb092fe5f60c57cfac271e71bc3cf677e2.abstract:
<jats:p>Offshore operations depend on reliable performance in safety-critical functions, and the industry's human performance framework treats that performance as shaped by the conditions under which work is done, among them workload, sleep opportunity, rotation design, and supervision (IOGP 2026). When these conditions degrade, the effect reaches the operation as well as the safety record: in the deployments described in this paper, events whose investigations recorded reduced human performance among the contributing factors also carried production cost, in interrupted operations and deferred output. The controls that address these conditions, from fatigue risk management to competence assurance, primarily operate at the level of the schedule and the job category, and do not ordinarily provide a standardized, individual-referenced signal before the shift. In current practice, that space is covered by the supervisor's judgment and the pre-shift conversation. A standardized signal would give that judgment an instrument: an indication of when to offer support, and when to review the day's risk controls before critical work begins.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>The barrier literature offers a test for what a daily process built around such a signal would need to do. Sklet (2006) describes active safety barriers as realizing a sequence of functions: detect a deviation, decide on a response, and carry the response out. In the barrier models the industry applies across many domains, bowtie analysis among them, degraded human performance appears as one of several escalation factors that can erode the performance of other barriers, together with technical and organizational degradation. The controls that address the contributing conditions are set in advance and calibrated for groups: rosters, hours-of-service limits, training cycles. The growing use of leading indicators in operational safety follows a logic that applies here as well: monitor conditions relevant to barrier performance before the barrier is called on, instead of counting the events it failed to stop (IOGP 2023). A daily, individual-referenced readiness signal has not been routinely integrated with this set of controls, a gap discussed at greater length in the field study that precedes this paper.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>That field study showed the signal can be produced under routine offshore conditions. Before the shift, each operator in a safety-critical function completes a short cognitive task of under three minutes, delivered as a standardized digital application with the format of a game and the function of an instrument: the result is derived from measured performance on the task, not from a questionnaire. The task is calibrated to each function through an onboard neuroergonomic assessment, the application of neuroscience methods to the study of work (Parasuraman and Wilson 2008), which characterizes the cognitive demands the activity places on whoever performs it. The result is read against the operator's own accumulated baseline together with the cognitive demands of the function, so a deviation records a change in test performance relative to that combined reference, and it enters the day's risk assessment as an individual-referenced input, read much as a wind limit is read before work at height: the value is compared with a reference range, and an out-of-range reading changes how the task is conducted and which controls apply. A green result, within the operator's normal range, requires no further step. A yellow result opens a support conversation between operator and supervisor and activates predefined, graded, non-punitive risk controls, co-designed with the asset team, before critical work begins; the result is not a diagnosis and is not used for appraisal or discipline, and activation is used in this sense throughout the paper. Over a 22-month evaluation at one asset, the program was associated with a sustained reduction in events whose investigations recorded reduced human performance among the contributing factors, and in the production downtime attributed to those events (Baldassim et al. 2026, in press).</jats:p>

title: Numerical Model for Calculating Human-Factor Risk in Well Integrity for HSE Performance Enhancement Using a 5×6 Lifecycle Maturity Matrix
container-title: ADIPEC
bf0e2e9e419990bf7bcb1c65cb738cdb7f92a99f.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Effective HSE performance requires measurable control of human and organizational risk. Human and organizational weaknesses can progressively erode well barrier reliability, yet they are rarely measured in a structured or auditable manner within well integrity assurance. This paper presents a quantitative human‑reliability framework that converts human‑factor controls into measurable, risk‑informed maturity indices directly applicable to lifecycle well integrity management.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>The framework integrates five human‑factor control layers—governance, competence, execution, assurance, and learning—across six ISO‑aligned well lifecycle phases: basis of design, design, construction, operations, intervention, and abandonment. The resulting 5×6 lifecycle matrix defines 30 phase–layer control cells, each assessed using a five‑level maturity scale ranging from reactive to resilient, enabling qualitative organizational behaviors to be translated into auditable maturity evidence.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>To quantify system performance, three indices are introduced: Phase Maturity Index (PMI), Layer Maturity Index (LMI), and Well Integrity System Maturity (WISM). These indices transform ordinal maturity levels into percentage‑based scores using an exponential maturity function with configurable phase and layer weightings. The exponential form increases sensitivity to low‑maturity conditions, where human‑factor weaknesses pose the greatest risk to barrier reliability, while a safety factor (S) represents residual risk consistent with ALARP principles.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>Across 30 assessment cells and five maturity states, the framework represents approximately 9.3×1020 possible maturity configurations, providing high diagnostic resolution to distinguish localized control weaknesses from system‑level governance and assurance gaps. The configurable weighting structure allows adaptation to different asset types, risk profiles, and regulatory environments while preserving a consistent calculation basis for transparent benchmarking and improvement planning.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>The proposed model delivers a scalable numerical method for embedding human and organizational controls into lifecycle well integrity governance, assurance prioritization, and continuous improvement. By quantifying human‑factor maturity and linking it directly to assurance focus and decision‑making, the framework supports stronger barrier reliability, risk‑based assurance prioritization, and measurable progression toward resilient well integrity performance.</jats:p>

title: Large-Scale Temporary Associated-Gas Reinjection to Recycle Methane and Enhance Deliverability in a Mature Depletion-Driven Gas Reservoir Under Integrated Surface and Subsurface Constraints
container-title: ADIPEC
5f57170f4af823c4c593770be5961b83539d78fa.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Managing associated-gas volumes during periods of infrastructure limitation is a recurring challenge for mature gas-producing assets, particularly where multiple reservoirs are connected to a common facility and may later receive shared compression support. This paper evaluates an alternative strategy in which Reservoir X, the largest reservoir within a group of mature gas reservoirs undergoing depletion, is used for temporary methane storage and recovery through large-scale associated-gas reinjection. The objective is to quantify how injection duration, rate, and injector configuration affect methane recycling, post-injection deliverability, condensate revaporization, pressure support, and long-term production timing while honoring wellhead injection pressure, injectivity, trunkline, and compression constraints.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>A full-field EOS-based compositional reservoir simulation model was coupled with surface-network operating limits to evaluate temporary associated-gas reinjection in Reservoir X. The sensitivity analysis covered short-, intermediate-, and extended-duration injection periods; lower-, intermediate-, and upper-count injector configurations; field injection rates ranging from constrained operating cases to a high field-scale rate envelope; and asset-approved conservative and upper WHIP envelopes. The workflow incorporated injector screening, fault-communication risk assessment, gas-composition compatibility, pressure diagnostics, post-injection blowdown forecasting, and alignment with the prospective compression-assisted operating phase. The extended-duration, intermediate-count injector case was selected as the reference development option because it provided the best balance among methane-recycling performance, implementation practicality, compression readiness, and subsurface containment-risk management.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>Across the evaluated forecast period, the principal value of temporary reinjection was not a large increase in ultimate recovery, but a substantial improvement in post-injection deliverability, methane-value preservation, and sustainable production-plateau timing. Following injection cessation, gas and condensate rates were materially higher than in the depletion-only case, with uplift in the approximate 20% range during blowdown. When aligned with the prospective compression-assisted operating phase for the integrated multi-reservoir system, the selected intermediate-count reference configuration extended the sustainable plateau by approximately two to three years. Injected methane was progressively produced back after blowdown initiation, with roughly three-quarters to nine-tenths recovered within several years, depending on injection volume, duration, and pressure support. Repressurization also reduced condensate dropout in highly depleted regions of Reservoir X and supported partial condensate revaporization through dilution/displacement, enrichment, and compositional redistribution.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>Routing associated gas to reinjection instead of flaring can reduce flared volumes and associated emissions, subject to facility and safe-operating constraints. This field-scale case study combines temporary associated-gas reinjection with integrated surface-subsurface constraints, conversion of existing producers to injection service, reconversion to production during blowdown, and compositional diagnostics. The study quantifies the trade-off between modest ultimate-recovery gains and substantial post-injection rate uplift, while explicitly tracking methane recycling, condensate revaporization, and compression-phasing mechanisms to support practical reinjection design.</jats:p>

title: Development of a Moodle LMS-Assisted Blended Learning Model in the Information Systems Study Program at Institut Hasan Sulur
container-title: Journal of Multidisciplinary Science: MIKAILALSYS
4d2f662834acdbebc3f22646483bc592ea4a0502.abstract: <jats:p>Integrating face-to-face and online learning in higher education requires coherent instructional design and appropriate digital support. This study evaluated the feasibility, practicality, and effectiveness of a Moodle-assisted blended learning model in the Information Systems Study Program. A research and development (R&D) approach was employed, with data collected through expert validation, student responses, classroom activity observations, and pretest and posttest assessments. Evaluation scores were 90% for learning materials, 91% for media presentation, 90% for practicality, 88% for pedagogical aspects, 93% for instructional devices, and 89% for the user guidebook. Individual, small-group, and field trials yielded scores of 84.76%, 89%, and approximately 96%, respectively. The student learning activity assessment yielded 87%. Mean test scores increased from 31.53 before implementation to 45.93 afterward, out of a maximum of 54. These descriptive findings support the model’s feasibility and practicality, while the observed score increase provides preliminary evidence of potential learning benefits. The study contributes a technology-supported instructional model for systematically integrating face-to-face and online activities in higher education, with practical implications for lecturers and institutions implementing blended learning. Further evaluation involving a control group and inferential statistical analysis is recommended to establish the model’s effectiveness more rigorously.</jats:p>

title: From Data to Decisions: A Structured Execution Model for Reducing Production Deferment in Brownfield Onshore Assets
container-title: ADIPEC
fa3d7cc0f18627b3358c726bb4fb0ccfa2c145e4.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Production deferment remains a persistent challenge in mature onshore oil and gas assets despite significant investment in production surveillance, digital monitoring, and integrated operational workflows. While organizations have improved their ability to detect production losses, converting production information into timely, coordinated execution actions remains inconsistent, resulting in delayed interventions and prolonged production losses.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>This paper presents a Structured Execution Model (SEM) that improves production recovery by systematically transforming production data into prioritized operational interventions. The framework comprises five sequential stages, Detect, Diagnose, Decide, Execute, and Track, integrating Reservoir, Operations, and Maintenance functions into a unified recovery process. Embedded within the decision stage is the Production Exposure Prioritization Matrix (PEPM), a quantitative decision model that prioritizes competing production constraints using a value-to-effort approach, combining deferred production volume, execution complexity, intervention lead time, and recurrence risk into a single, repeatable score.</jats:p>
