title:
Air-Stable Nickel
Oxide Nanosheets as a Model Platform
for Decoupling Structure–Activity Relation in Oxygen Evolving
Electrocatalysts
container-title: ACS Nano
74cc8bd3987e34202951fdf83bcce42d3b39308f.abstract: Abstract Nickel oxides are among the most active electrocatalysts for the alkaline oxygen evolution reaction (OER), a key process in green hydrogen production. However, the fundamental reaction mechanism remains unclear, limiting the rational design of electrocatalysts capable of reducing the cost of sustainable hydrogen generation. Herein, we develop an air-stable model electrocatalyst system of submonolayer nickel oxide (NiO) nanosheets with controlled coverages and morphologies on atomically flat Au(111), enabling atomic-scale investigation of structure–activity relationships under ambient conditions. Atomic force microscopy (AFM), scanning tunneling microscopy (STM) in ultrahigh vacuum (UHV), X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), and electrochemical measurements were combined to correlate nanosheet structure and composition with electrocatalytic performance. We reveal OER activity scales with nanosheet edge density, identifying edge sites as the dominant active sites of the reaction. XPS measurements demonstrate the formation of nickel hydroxide on the nanosheet surfaces and edges following OER testing, consistent with the generation of a catalytically active nickel oxyhydroxide phase during operation. These findings provide insight into the structure–activity relationships governing NiO electrocatalysts and demonstrate a strategy for resolving atomic-scale structure–activity relationships without the need to maintain samples under UHV. We propose that future NiO-based OER electrocatalysts are designed to maximize the number density of accessible edge sites, hence maximizing the electrocatalytic activity.

title: A Hybrid Convolutional Recurrent Neural Model for Noise Detection and Automated Calibration of Medical Devices via Molecular Vibration Analysis
518557eedb6ff36ea9b47c24553d6afd51c850c8.abstract: Abstract Accurate noise detection and calibration are essential for maintaining the measurement reliability of medical devices. This study proposes a hybrid convolutional recurrent neural network (CRNN) framework for noise detection and automated calibration of ventilators and electrocardiogram (ECG) machines using molecular vibration analysis. A molecular vibration model was developed to characterize mechanical vibration, electromagnetic interference, and environmental conduction noise, achieving an average noise classification accuracy of 96.2%. The proposed CRNN with hybrid attention maintained 91.5% accuracy under low signal-to-noise conditions. A deep deterministic policy gradient-based calibration strategy was subsequently employed to optimize calibration parameters automatically, reducing calibration time by 72.5% and improving calibration accuracy by 78.5% compared with conventional methods. After calibration, the average relative errors were 1.9% for ventilator tidal-volume measurements and 0.92% for QRS-complex amplitude measurements in ECG devices. Cross-device validation achieved 94.3% accuracy across different equipment brands. The results demonstrate that integrating molecular vibration analysis, hybrid deep learning, and automated calibration provides an effective approach for reliable noise detection and precision calibration of medical devices.

title: Beyond dissolution: a lifecycle model of supplier relationship management
container-title: Journal of Business & Industrial Marketing
2722837947789beb8f26e20ab78fbbfe7fcc588f.abstract: Purpose Supplier relationship management (SRM) remains insufficiently understood from a lifecycle perspective. While existing research provides valuable insights into individual SRM activities, it offers limited understanding of how supplier relationships evolve over time and how digitalization supports their management. This study aims to address these gaps by extending the supplier relationship framework of Möller et al. (2006). Design/methodology/approach The study is based on 43 semi-structured interviews with practitioners across multiple industries. This qualitative approach provides in-depth insights into how companies design, manage and digitalize supplier relationships across different phases. Findings The analysis confirms the three established SRM phases – out-supplier management, in-supplier management and in-supplier dissolution management – and extends the framework by identifying two additional phases: sleeping and reactivation. The findings show that SRM is a dynamic and iterative lifecycle characterized by recurring transitions between phases. Furthermore, digital technologies are embedded throughout the lifecycle, supporting information continuity, coordination and more consistent decision-making. Originality/value This study extends Möller et al. (2006) SRM framework by developing an empirically grounded lifecycle model that incorporates sleeping and reactivation phases. It further advances SRM theory by conceptualizing recurring relational and digital touchpoints as mechanisms that support transitions across the supplier relationship lifecycle. Finally, the study contributes to the digitalization literature by demonstrating that digital technologies function as integral governance mechanisms throughout the lifecycle rather than as isolated support tools.

title: Post-occupancy environmental performance of a household-model residential aged care facility: a same-site sequential evaluation (Phase 2)
container-title: Facilities
f59b1690af0c7d13d9f600a5034d9cc66aa83d23.abstract: Purpose Built residential aged care (RAC) facilities adopting household models are widely promoted as assets that improve environmental quality and resident comfort. However, post-occupancy evidence verifying whether these facilities deliver measurable improvements against health-relevant acoustic, lighting and thermal benchmarks remains limited. This study aims to report a Phase 2 post-occupancy evaluation of a newly constructed household-model RAC facility, comparing realised indoor environmental quality (IEQ) performance and occupant perceptions with established benchmarks and a pre-relocation baseline evaluation (PrBE) from the legacy facility it replaced. Design/methodology/approach Environmental monitoring was undertaken over two consecutive 14-day deployments in March 2025 across private bedrooms, communal lounges and dining areas and transitional spaces. Minute-resolution acoustic, lighting and temperature data were collected using industry-grade IC-NSRT and HOBO MX2202 loggers. Performance was evaluated against World Health Organization (WHO) and AS/NZS 2107:2016 acoustic criteria, pragmatic circadian-supportive lighting thresholds (=1,000 lux daytime; =10 lux night) and thermal guidance emphasising diurnal variation (=2°C) and avoidance of prolonged operation above 22°C. Parallel surveys of residents, proxies and staff captured perceived environmental conditions and operational influences. Findings Compared with the legacy facility, the household model building demonstrated improvements in night-time acoustic conditions in bedrooms, enhanced daylight availability in communal spaces and modest reductions in nocturnal light intrusion. Daytime illuminance in bedrooms improved but remained variable, influenced by orientation, shading and resident use. Thermal conditions were generally cooler and widely perceived as comfortable, with increased diurnal variation evident in some spaces. Survey responses indicated improved satisfaction with acoustic and lighting conditions, while perceptions of thermal comfort remained consistently positive across phases. Practical implications Findings indicate that architectural change can deliver measurable IEQ gains but that full alignment with health-relevant benchmarks depends on post-handover operational tuning, staff awareness and adaptive use of environmental controls. Residual performance gaps are best understood as opportunities for optimisation rather than design shortcomings. Originality/value The study contributes longitudinal same-site sequential post-occupancy evidence from an RAC redevelopment, integrating objective environmental monitoring with occupant perceptions to support evidence-informed facilities management and post-occupancy optimisation.

title: Enacting effectuation in scarcity: a symbiotic model driven by bricolage and socio-cultural networks in Moroccan SME entrepreneurship
container-title: Asia Pacific Journal of Innovation and Entrepreneurship
362d4dce0274c4e44a5f366ed1da155f3cedb083.abstract: Purpose Effectuation theory (Sarasvathy, 2001) posits a control-oriented logic for entrepreneurial decision-making under uncertainty, yet its enactment in resource-scarce emerging economies remains underexplored, particularly through cultural and recombinative lenses. This study aims to address this gap by examining how Moroccan SME entrepreneurs in artisanal, agricultural and digital sectors navigate Knightian uncertainty via effectuation, moderated by socio-cultural networks and mediated by bricolage, to achieve hybrid effectuation-causation logics and sustained performance. Design/methodology/approach Drawing on a qualitative multiple-case study of five established SMEs, the authors develop a symbiotic model exploring four theoretical propositions. These propositions examine how: (P1) effectuation enables adaptive decision-making through controllable means-based action in volatile contexts; (P2) collectivist networks (el-maârifa) shape the adoption and enactment of effectual principles; (P3) bricolage serves as the operational mechanism transforming bird-in-hand means into value; and (P4) entrepreneurs navigate venture lifecycles through dynamic hybrid logics blending effectual discovery with causal execution. Findings Thematic analysis reveals pervasive effectual principles – affordable loss and crazy quilt – enacted through trust-based recombinations (e.g. waste-to-innovation in ceramics and honey) and context-adaptive ambidexterity. This yields resilience amid pandemics, regulations and climatic risks. Research limitations/implications While the deep contextual insights are a core contribution, future research could test the transferability of this framework in other emerging economies. Practical implications Practically, it offers a roadmap for emerging-market entrepreneurs – “build on roots, recombine creatively” – legitimizing adaptive bootstrapping. Social implications The study highlights the role of collectivist networks (el-maârifa) in fostering trust-based recombinations and ethical hybridity, promoting collective stewardship and resilience in resource-scarce communities facing socio-economic and environmental challenges. Originality/value The authors contribute a context-specific theoretical framework: a symbiotic model integrating socio-cultural network embeddedness and ethical hybridity. This elaborates effectuation beyond individualism to collective stewardship in scarcity-driven settings.

title: Indigenous Language Media and Women Social Empowerment in Rivers State, Nigeria
container-title: RESEARCH JOURNAL OF MASS COMMUNICATION AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY
9ab9d8057236b9dd14e0c34677ecaf6c387bdc57.abstract: This study is an examination of indigenous language media and women social empowerment in Rivers State, Nigeria. This study adopted a qualitative research method. The population of the study consisted of women in Rivers State who actively consume indigenous language media, including radio, television, and digital platforms. A sample size of 20 participants were selected using purposive sampling technique. The primary method of data collection was email interviews, allowing participants to provide detailed, reflective responses at their convenience. Participants were receive structured, open-ended questions designed to elicit in-depth insights on how indigenous language media influences women's awareness, agency, and participation in socio-economic and political activities. For data analysis, the study employed thematic analysis, where interview responses were transcribed, coded, and categorised into themes that reflect key patterns and emerging insights. This method ensures a systematic interpretation of qualitative data, allowing for a nuanced understanding of how indigenous language media fosters women’s empowerment, the barriers they face, and possible policy recommendations for improving gender-inclusive communication. Findings from the study revealed that, indigenous language media plays a crucial role in enhancing women’s access to vital information, particularly in health, agriculture, and governance, by breaking down language barriers and providing content that is culturally relevant and accessible, although infrastructural challenges such as poor network coverage and limited access to devices hinder its full reach. The study concluded that indigenous language media plays a pivotal role in enhancing women’s access to critical information, providing them with the tools to make informed decisions about their health, economic, and social lives, but its full potential is constrained by infrastructural limitations, requiring targeted investments to improve accessibility and reach. The study recommended that government and private sector stakeholders should invest in expanding media infrastructure and providing affordable technology to ensure broader access to indigenous language media for women.

title: From awe to emotional brand attachment: a cognitive appraisal perspective on VR brand experiences
container-title: Journal of Product & Brand Management
2a02739e2da8b57381342589a61ac9c76d3c74b0.abstract: Purpose Prior research on awe in relation to virtual reality (VR) has treated awe as a response to technological stimuli, leaving the consumer appraisals through which awe arises underexplored. Drawing on cognitive appraisal theory, this paper aims to address this gap by investigating whether aesthetic, sensory and content appraisals of a VR brand experience predict awe and whether awe mediates the relationships between these appraisals and emotional brand attachment. Design/methodology/approach Data were collected via a survey of 334 Generation Z participants who experienced an in-person brand encounter via a VR headset and were analysed using covariance-based structural equation modelling in LISREL. Findings Aesthetic, sensory and content appraisals positively predict awe, which, in turn, predicts emotional brand attachment. Awe also mediates the relationships between each of the three appraisal and emotional brand attachment. Originality/value At the intersection of the cognitive psychology of VR and emotional branding, this paper reframes the origins of awe in VR brand experiences, shifting from a stimulus-centred to an appraisal-centred account. It also identifies aesthetic, sensory and content appraisals as the experiential predictors of awe and extends emotional branding to self-transcendent emotions by showing how awe translates experiential appraisals into emotional brand attachment.

title: Exploring the formation mechanism of new energy vehicle technology innovation network: a stimulus–response model analysis
container-title: Journal of Business & Industrial Marketing
5b10f935faa3e10a63c459cf610989a6e20b4d34.abstract: Purpose This paper aims to explore the formation mechanism of technology innovation network in new energy automobile industry based on the stimulus-response model and to analyze the dynamic interaction process among innovation subjects, platform and government under the market mechanism, platform participation and government regulation. Design/methodology/approach This paper adopts static regression analysis to study the formation mechanism of technology innovation network in new energy automobile industry. Multiagent simulation model is used to explore the dynamic evolution mechanism of innovation network formation. Findings The research findings indicate that the innovation behavior of technology receivers is significantly influenced by their own technology cross-border search and technology internalization capability, and technology ecological niche of technology senders, information stimulation intensity, the level of platform participation and government regulation. The simulation results show that in the interaction among innovation subjects under the market mechanism, a greater number of enterprises choose technology-restructuring innovation. However, in the interaction between innovation subjects and the environment, a higher number of technology-distributed innovation subjects is observed. Originality/value This paper reveals the “black box” of technological innovation network formation in new energy automobile industry based on the stimulus–response model. This paper also enriches the research framework of technological innovation networks by exploring the attributes of innovation subjects as well as exploring the dynamic interactions of subjects, platform and government.

title: The Functional-Vertical and Horizontal Model of the Rustvelian Classification of Shairoba
რუსთველური შაირობის ფუნქციურ-ვერტიკალური  და ჰორიზონტალური კლასიფიკაციის მოდელი
container-title: სჯანი
04dbf5c3f351b38ce3b0d74e539945903e21df6b.abstract: This article analyzes the classification of shairoba (poetry) presented by Shota Rustaveli in the Prologue of The Knight in the Panther's Skin and proposes a new interpretive model for its comprehension. Drawing upon generic, textual, culturo­lo­gical, and comparative-theoretical approaches, the study reviews the foundational discourses within Rustavelology (including the scholarship of K. Kekelidze, A. Bara­midze, G. Imedashvili, A. Bakradze, Z. Gamsakhurdia, R. Siradze, and I. Ratiani). Con­se­quently, it demonstrates that Rustaveli's conceptualization of poetry extends far beyond mere genre differentiation. According to the authors, Rustaveli views po­etry as a form of wisdom, cognition, and spiritual experience that harmoniously uni­fies aesthetic and ethical functions. The central thesis of this study argues that Rustaveli posits a dual functional-vertical and horizontal classification of poetry. The vertical axis divides poetry into "divine" (saghmrt'o) and "earthly" (saak'ao) shairoba. "Divine" poetry is intrinsically lin­ked to the cognition of God, spiritual elevation, and a gnoseological function, which the authors elucidate through a textual and philosophical analysis of the terms "divine" (saghmrt'o) and "divinely perceived" (saghmrt'od gasagoni). Within this con­text, the study examines the interpretations of Ioane Petritzi, the hymnographic tra­dition of Gregory of Nazianzus, and the overarching influence of Christian Neoplato­nism. The authors conclude that for Rustaveli, the primary purpose of poetry is sac­red and cog­nitive, and its ultimate goal is to bestow a "spiritual benefit" (marghi) upon the listener. The horizontal classification pertains to genre differentiation. Rustaveli distin­guishes between epic and lyric poetry, further dividing the lyric sphere into several subgenres: festive (sanimado), amorous (saashiko), playful (salaghobo), melodic (sam­ghereli), and colloquial (amkhanagta satreveli) poetry. Special emphasis is placed on specific textual instances within The Knight in the Panther's Skin, particularly the letters of Avtandil, Patman, and Nestan-Darejan. Patman's letter is analyzed as a mani­festation of mundane, erotic, and situational lyricism, while Nestan's letter rep­re­sents an elevated expression of Neoplatonic and ontological devotion. A compa­ra­tive analysis of these letters clearly elucidates the interconnectedness of style, func­tion, and content. Finally, the article demonstrates that Rustaveli's poetic framework is deeply intertwined with Classical antiquity and Hellenistic aesthetic theories. It explores the perspectives of Plato, Aristotle, Horace, and various Neoplatonists regarding the na­ture and function of poetry. The authors conclude that Rustaveli successfully har­monizes Platonic idealism, Aristotelian functionalism, and the Christian worldview into a unified system, thereby synthesizing a highly original, multi-layered concep­tion of poetry that encapsulates spiritual, aesthetic, and social dimensions. Rustaveli’s poetic conception may be understood as a synthesis of Platonic idealism and Aristotelian poetics, mediated by the Christian intellectual tradition. His characterization of shairoba (poetry) as “divine” suggests a Platonic under­stan­ding of poetry as connected with a higher, transcendent order of truth. At the same time, his emphasis on poetry’s “great benefit” to its audience and the pleasure it pro­vides introduces a distinctly functional dimension, which resonates with Aris­totle’s understanding of poetry as both cognitively and affectively significant. Within Rustaveli’s poetic system, therefore, the transcendent origin of poetry is complemented by its human-oriented function: poetry is expected to provide both benefit and pleasure. This synthesis allows The Knight in the Panther’s Skin to be interpreted simultaneously as a text of philosophical and spiritual significance and as a work grounded in human experience and emotional life. Rustaveli’s conception may consequently be viewed not as a simple reproduction of classical aesthetic doct­rines, but as an original reconfiguration of several intellectual traditions. In particu­lar, Aristotelian conceptions of poetic form and function, the Horatian principle of utile dulci, and a Christianized Neoplatonic understanding of spiritual hierarchy converge within a unified poetic and aesthetic framework.

title: Dissident Literature: Model and Contradictions
დისიდენტური მწერლობა. მოდელი და წინააღმდეგობანი
container-title: სჯანი
85be1ce9c98d60d21ce1c7d1e63c9967e7bab35e.abstract: Dissident literature is a specific form of literary narrative that emerged in the 1960s and 1970s in the Soviet Union, as well as in the countries of the socialist bloc of Central and Eastern Europe. Driven by the ideological pressure in these coun­tries – which limited not only creative freedom but also violated fundamental human freedoms such as freedom of speech, thought, and belief – writers assumed a number of social responsibilities alongside their creative ones, directly linked to the protec­tion of international human rights standards. In this regard, a significant con­tribution was made by writers from the socialist bloc and Soviet countries, including Georgian dissident authors such as Merab Kostava, Zviad Gamsakhurdia, and Petre Gruzinsky. Dissident literature is defined as a specific form of literary narrative that oppo­ses dominant political, social, and cultural clichés, repressive regimes, and censorship norms. It represents a non-violent model of resistance aimed at protecting human rights. Formed under conditions of political repression, dissident literature aims to con­front the regime and construct alternative modes of thought using all available stylistic devices. Furthermore, facing persecution by state censorship, dissident lite­rature was forced to disseminate through "underground" means. The article examines the political and cultural precursors of dissident literature, such as the death of Joseph Stalin – a materialized symbol of the country – in 1953, the high-profile 20th Congress of the Communist Party, the speech by then-leader Nikita Khrushchev, as well as the "Thaw" era and its cultural trends: the libe­ra­lization of literary discourse, the emergence of Soviet neo-realism, and the inten­sification of existential discourse. It is noted that the Thaw period was soon replaced by the "Period of Stagna­tion." From the 1970s onward, the Soviet regime's aggression toward any innovation intensified, becoming extremely artificial on the one hand and disrupting elementary norms of communication on the other. Consequently, the writer, as one of the most qualified consumers of information, suffered from an information deficit. Bound by political shackles, this epoch rightfully earned its status as an era of "stagnation" or immobility. It was precisely during this era that dissident literature developed in full force. The article notes that although Georgian dissident literature was somewhat weaker in terms of artistic quality, it nonetheless maintained a significant influence on Geor­gian society (e.g., the poetry of Zviad Gamsakhurdia and Merab Kostava, and Petre Gruzinsky's "Raised in Fear," "I Feel Sorry for My Castrated Generation...", among others). The article introduces and defines terms such as literature beyond bars, isolation, internal emigration, psychiatric discourse, and forced repentance. Drawing from its own experience, dissident literature helped society overcome complex psy­cho­logical and moral obstacles through its distinctive thematic freedom and radical socio-political narratives. According to the author, dissident writers openly faced physical persecution, and their texts were subject to harsh censorship methods. Accordingly, the article in­troduces concepts such as killer censorship and corrupted censorship. Finally, it dis­cu­sses the mechanisms for disseminating dissident texts, which strictly followed un­derground rules: ideas were heavily veiled using various stylistic techniques, while the texts themselves were circulated in manuscript form or through self-publishing (Samizdat).

title: How Can a Body Under Surveillance Rediscover Its Own Himalaya?  Transcendence, Language, and Sensory Liberation in Johanna Sinisalo’s  The Core of the Sun

ff7e4852cb8d4b0897444f210ea70c669c8c9b35.abstract: This article examines Johanna Sinisalo’s Finnish dystopian novel The Core of the Sun (Finnish original: Auringon ydin, 2013; English translation by Lola Rogers, 2016) through the intersecting lenses of Foucauldian biopolitics, feminist body the­ory, and South Asian epistemologies of inner transcendence. Set in a fictional “Eusis­tocratic Republic of Finland,” the novel imagines a technocratic welfare state that po­lices women’s bodies, suppresses autonomous language, and criminalizes sensory ple­asure – most notably the consumption of chili peppers – in the name of collective health and social stability. Drawing on Michel Foucault’s theorizations of disciplina­ry power and biopower, the analysis demonstrates how the state apparatus in Sini­salo’s text constructs the surveilled female body as a primary site of governance, re­ducing it to a classifiable, optimizable instrument. The Eusistocracy divides women into two legally enforced biological categories – eloi (submissive, sexually available bree­ders) and morlocks (intelligent women condemned to sterilization and menial labor) – thereby literalizing what Foucault describes as the production of “docile bodies”: subjects who have so thoroughly internalized regulatory norms that survei­llan­ce becomes self-sustaining. The article then pivots toward a comparative philosophical reading. It argues that the protagonist Vanna’s (also known as Vera) escalating addiction to increasing­ly potent chili peppers, culminating in hallucinations and out-of-body experiences induced by the legendary “Core of the Sun” pepper, bears a striking structural resem­blance to the South Asian philosophical concepts of tejas and samadhi as articulated in Ayurvedic, Samkhya, and Yoga traditions. Tejas – derived from Sanskrit and mea­ning inner luminous fire or radiance – refers in Ayurvedic philosophy to the trans­for­mative energy that underlies digestion, cognition, and spiritual perception; at its highest refinement, it is associated with liberation, clarity, and the capacity to over­come oppressive forces. Samadhi, as described in the Yoga Sutras of Patanjali and in broader Indian meditative traditions, designates a state of absorbed, undivided cons­ciousness in which the ordinary boundaries between self and world dissolve, enab­ling a mode of awareness that transcends the surveilling, classifying ego. The article argues that capsaicin’s physiological mechanism – activating the same receptor that responds to thermal heat, causing the body to register chili literally as fire – gives Sinisalo’s conceit an unexpected material literalism: the protagonist’s experiences are, at the level of bodily chemistry, an encounter with inner fire in the most direct sense. Situating the novel within the thematic orbit of literature in exile – broadly understood as writing that negotiates belonging, displacement, and the desire to rec­laim a self that power structures have tried to erase – the article proposes that Sini­salo’s text stages the body as a site of counter-knowledge that no surveillance appara­tus can fully colonize. The exile Vanna endures is not primarily geographical but corporeal: she is a self evicted from its own body by a biopolitical order that claims ownership of life itself. Her chili addiction becomes a project of return – each cap­saicin experience a brief restoration of somatic sovereignty that enacts what South Asian philosophy would recognize as a movement toward moksha (liberation). The Himalaya invoked in this article’s title names not a geographic destination but an interior altitude: the luminous, high, and uncharted territory of consciousness that the body can reach when freed from the demand that it be only what power decrees. The article also attends to the novel’s formal architecture – its collage of fic­tional government documents, health bulletins, propaganda pamphlets, and Vanna’s fragmented trance-prose – arguing that this formal opposition between institutional discourse and somatic illegibility enacts the epistemological argument the novel ma­kes thematically, and connects Sinisalo’s project to Hélène Cixous’s concept of écri­ture féminine. By bridging Nordic speculative fiction and South Asian philosophical frameworks through the shared medium of bodily fire, this study contributes to com­parative literary studies and opens new pathways for reading dystopian fiction as a literature of internal exile and embodied resistance. It further suggests that the most searching forms of counter-surveillance do not require political manifestos; they require only a body willing to burn.

title: From intimacy to consumption: an exploration into the role of consumer engagement and self-esteem in second-hand luxury consumption

6ec3ec9f9baaff345707050cc533bfc7302a98ae.abstract: Purpose This study combines the concept of parasocial relationships (PSRs) with social exchange theory (SET) in the situation of second-hand luxury (SHL) consumption on social media. It examines not only how PSRs drive SHL consumption through consumer engagement and attitudes, but also consumers' self-esteem and how it moderates the above relationship. Design/methodology/approach A total of 740 valid responses were gathered through an online questionnaire, and the proposed model was examined using partial least squares structural equation modeling. Findings The results indicate that PSRs directly and positively affect SHL consumption. The sequential mediation testing results demonstrate that consumer engagement and attitudes serially mediate the above relationship. In addition, PSRs do not translate uniformly into consumer engagement and mainly exert an influence on consumers with low self-esteem. Originality/value This study extends the applicability of SET to SHL consumption. Additionally, it reveals not only how PSRs influence consumer behaviors but also the reason by highlighting the psychological exchange process and the boundary role of self-esteem.

title: Antioxidant capacity, cytotoxicity and post-treatment effect of Myrtus communis L. leaf extract in a 6-hydroxydopamine-induced SH-SY5Y cell model
container-title: Biological Diversity and Conservation
6df21c673ef0a619114f98952c5c9cf8c6722994.abstract: Purpose: Oxidative stress drives the loss of dopaminergic neurons in Parkinson's disease, which is usually diagnosed after many of these neurons are lost. Agents acting after injury are therefore of interest. This study measured the phenolic content and antioxidant capacity of an ethanolic Myrtus communis L. leaf extract, defined its non-cytotoxic concentration range, and tested whether the extract, applied after 6-hydroxydopamine (6-OHDA) injury, improves the viability of human SH-SY5Y neuroblastoma cells.Method: Leaves of M. communis were collected in Hatay Province (Türkiye), dried, powdered and macerated in ethanol for 3 days. Total phenolic (Folin–Ciocalteu) and total flavonoid (aluminum chloride) contents, DPPH and ABTS radical scavenging, and ferric reducing antioxidant power (FRAP) were measured. Cytotoxicity was assessed in L929 fibroblasts and SH-SY5Y cells by the MTT assay after 24 and 48 h. SH-SY5Y cells were exposed to 200 µM 6-OHDA for 24 h and then treated with the extract (10–1000 µg/mL) for 24 h. Groups were compared by ANOVA and Dunnett's test.Findings: The extract (yield 16.87%) contained 256.00 ± 6.16 mg GAE/g total phenolics and 48.00 ± 11.41 mg QE/g total flavonoids, and its FRAP value was 285.66 ± 21.92 mg GAE/g extract. DPPH and ABTS IC50 values were 75.97 and 106.7 µg/mL (gallic acid: 45.25 and 64.41 µg/mL). By the ISO 10993-5 criterion (≥70% viability), L929 cells tolerated up to 31.25 µg/mL for 48 h. SH-SY5Y cells were about five times more sensitive than L929 cells (48-h IC50 31.16 vs 158.4 µg/mL). 6-OHDA reduced SH-SY5Y viability slightly at 24 h (87.5% at 200 µM) and by about half at 48 h (IC50 227.7 µM). Post-treatment increased the MTT signal only at 75 µg/mL (116.0% of 6-OHDA-only cells, p = 0.016), whereas concentrations ≥200 µg/mL lowered it to 54.0–73.1%.Conclusion: The extract showed moderate radical-scavenging activity but was tolerated only in a narrow range, and SH-SY5Y cells were more sensitive to it than fibroblasts. Evidence for a post-injury benefit was limited to a higher MTT signal at a single concentration. This exploratory finding needs confirmation with independent viability assays, appropriate controls, stronger injury and mechanistic endpoints.

title: A critical discourse analysis of TikTok on parliamentary processes: Unpacking language ideologies in South Africa
container-title: Inkanyiso
a3a0ea1a6af23698c73038c4705939714d651152.abstract: There is no doubt that South African parliamentarians have embodied English, even though 12 languages are spoken in South Africa and are constitutionally protected. This insidious embodiment of English speaks to language ideologies that set it above other African languages, and it is important to highlight this on the African continent, where languages of colonisers remain more dominant. The article sets out to analyse language ideologies as reflected in TikTok discourses responding to South African parliamentary processes, particularly following a few notable incidents that occurred in Parliament in July 2024. Furthermore, the dominance of English in public discourse is examined as realised and reflected on social media platforms such as TikTok. We argue that, based on parliamentary discourses in South Africa, the TikTok comments analysed show a complex interplay of language ideologies that reflect broader societal debates about language, power and identity. We conclude that there is still a need to highlight the importance of recognising and valuing linguistic diversity as a key component of social justice and access. Contribution: The article extends language ideology scholarship into the South African digital context, using TikTok discourse to show how ordinary citizens interpret and contest the dominance of English within a formal political institution such as Parliament. In doing so, it demonstrates the value of social media as an underused site for tracking public sentiment on multilingual policy tensions that often remain hidden in official parliamentary discourse.

title: A hybrid model–data framework for elastoplasticity with kinematic and isotropic hardening
container-title: Computational Mechanics
3333a1bd78e1c3a1770a5b4c1ca3dc38c324c886.abstract: Abstract Data-driven computational mechanics offers an alternative solution methodology to conventional methods by replacing constitutive models with data spaces defining admissible material states. Originally proposed for linear elasticity, its application to plasticity remains challenging. Purely data-driven plasticity schemes are usually restricted to one-dimensional problems due to the excessively large data space required as a result of path dependence. Hybrid frameworks combining constitutive assumptions with data have shown promise but are often limited by their underlying assumptions such as isotropic hardening or their inability to capture strain-path changes. In this work, a new hybrid model–data plasticity framework is proposed that incorporates kinematic and isotropic hardening via data spaces derived from discrete datasets, while adopting Prager’s law for back stress evolution without explicitly defining its functional form. The approach preserves the standard computational plasticity algorithmic procedures, while an implicit return-mapping procedure and a search direction calculation akin to the elastoplastic tangent are performed through the data spaces. Numerical examples in one and three-dimensional problems demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework in more general plasticity problems.

title: Behavioural lifestyle profiles among students in public higher education: health behaviours, digital engagement, leisure and sociability
a32ad9c84549fec7374a4423ac2b295f3f0f7e5e.abstract: Abstract Background Student lifestyles encompass a wide range of interrelated behaviours, yet research has rarely examined conventional health behaviours alongside digital engagement and sociocultural activities. We identified lifestyle profiles among students in Portuguese public higher education and examined their sociodemographic correlates and health, psychosocial, and academic outcomes. Methods Data were drawn from the probabilistic ES + Saúde survey of 9611 students in Portuguese public higher education. Latent profile analysis included 8840 students and 27 behavioural indicators spanning sleep, physical activity, sedentary behaviour, diet, leisure, digital use, gaming, and substance use. Multinomial logistic regression assessed sociodemographic correlates; adjusted linear models compared 17 distal outcomes. Results Four profiles emerged: Low-risk and low digital/recreational engagement (46.5%), Social alcohol and risk consumption (19.9%), Sedentary recreational digital/gaming (19.2%), and Active sociocultural and digitally engaged (14.3%). Profile membership varied by age, gender, residential relocation, field of study, institution type, and subjective social class. All 17 outcomes differed significantly across profiles after adjustment ( p < .001), although effects were generally modest (partial η² = .008–.062). The sedentary digital/gaming profile showed the least favourable overall health, psychological, social, and academic outcomes. Conversely, the active sociocultural profile combined the highest digital engagement with the highest physical activity and sociocultural participation and generally favourable outcomes. The low-risk profile also showed favourable outcomes. Conclusions Student lifestyles reflect distinct behavioural configurations rather than a simple healthy–unhealthy continuum. Digital engagement was not inherently associated with adverse outcomes; its relevance depended on accompanying behaviours. Health promotion may benefit from addressing co-occurring behavioural patterns rather than isolated risks.

title: Hybrid U-Net Model with Transformer-Enhanced Skip Connections for Abdominal Organ Segmentation in Laparoscopic Images
34e8247e98b81e33d79ce10c277474aa0691c912.abstract: Abstract The organ Segmentation in surgical images plays a crucial role in computer-assisted diagnosis and robotic surgeries, yet it faces challenges like class imbalance, occlusions, and computational constraints. In order to overcome these challenges, we propose an architecture which uses asymmetric multi-scale transformer along with the attention-gated skip connections in U-Net Model to efficiently segment abdominal organs. Our proposed architecture allows efficient extraction of local features and modelling of global contexts. We also propose a hybrid loss function by combining Lovasz-Softmax loss and sparse categorical cross-entropy loss, which helps in overcoming class imbalance in the training process and improving performance on the minor classes. Our proposed method attains a mean precision of 0.9667, mean recall of 0.9432, mean dice of 0.9522, mean IoU of 0.9150, and mean HD95 of 0.4704 on all 13 classes of the CholecSeg8k dataset, which makes it better than the state-of-the-art techniques.

title: Effect of Fuel Injection Spray Angle on NOx and Soot Emission in CI Engine Using Unsteady Flamelet Model

10f02fc8901bee213642d5146ee3006b2b614572.abstract: Effect of piston wall wetting due to misalignment in fuel injection on NOx and soot emissions were estimated using 3D CFD modelling in a CI engine with compression ratio of 18. Eulerian- Lagrangian approach was used in this study where the time history of fuel spray and atomization was modeled in the Lagrangian framework whereas in-cylinder aerodynamics was modeled by solving the 3D Navier Stokes equation in the Eulerian framework. Turbulence was modeled using k-ɛ model. A 6-hole fuel injector was used in this work and only 1/6th sector of the engine volume was modeled assuming uniform fuel injection. Combustion was modelled using by using 246 species and 1062 reactions containing skeletal n-dodecane/n-butanol/NOx/Polycyclic Aromatic Hydrocarbon (PAH) combustion mechanism that was previously developed and reported in open literature (Wakale, Banerjee and Banerjee, 2020). Two fuel injection pressures of 800 bars and 1500 bars and three different fuel spray cone angles of 800, 1200 and 1590 were modeled. It was found that lower spray cone angle increases the propensity of soot formation at lower injection pressure. However, it was found that soot formation is not significantly affected by wall wetting and higher injection pressure.

title: Hodges–Lehmann and Vision‐Language Model Based Intelligent Fire Detection in Complex Environments
container-title: Expert Systems
9e7059706e0d2e3f647f3294037bcdd36f6ac0b0.abstract: ABSTRACT Fires in industrial and environmental settings pose threats to process safety. Current vision‐based fire detection models face challenges in balancing high accuracy with lightweight deployment, suffer from high false alarm rates, and lack a closed‐loop inspection workflow. To enhance fire prevention capabilities and practical applicability, it is necessary to develop a methodology encompassing robust detection models and intelligent agents for fire safety inspection. Therefore, this study proposes a two‐stage robust fire detection methodology. Particularly, a novel Hodges–Lehmann‐based Robust Attention (HLRA) module is developed, utilising statistical estimators to achieve parameter‐free spatial and channel attention. Based on this, a real‐time detection model named RobustFireDet is proposed, integrating a triangular masked convolution and a robust HL‐IoU loss to improve accuracy while reducing parameters. Subsequently, a classification model named RobustFireNet is designed to mitigate false alarms by focusing on small‐target flames using the CoAlign Loss function. Experiments compare the proposed models with mainstream counterparts. RobustFireDet attains a detection mAP@0.5 of 74.3%, surpassing the second‐best YOLOv11 by 2.2 percentage points with 22.7% fewer parameters. RobustFireNet achieves a small‐flame classification accuracy of 96.9%, surpassing the second‐best EfficientNetV2‐S by 2.5 percentage points. The two‐stage pipeline further suppresses spurious fire boxes by 29.2% and false‐alarm images by 25.4% in an end‐to‐end evaluation. On top of the two‐stage detection results, a Vision‐Language Model‐based intelligent agent called FirePatrolAgent is further developed for scene analysis and recommendation generation, forming a closed‐loop inspection system that completes detection, verification, analysis, and response within 25.43 s per risk event.

title: Genome-scale metabolic model analysis of Korean Campylobacter jejuni isolates reveals lineage-level metabolic structure
container-title: Genomics & Informatics
69611897de3bfc38a3e48864b33041fec356c074.abstract: Abstract Genome-scale metabolic models (GSMMs) of Campylobacter jejuni ( C. jejuni ) have been studied mainly for reference strains, and their characteristics at the lineage level remain poorly understood. We reconstructed GSMMs for 86 C. jejuni isolates collected in Korea using gapseq and analyzed them together with in vitro substrate utilization data for seven substrates measured on the same isolates. Strain-specific GSMMs clustered by clonal complex (CC): in all nine CCs with ≥ 2 isolates the mean within-CC Jaccard distance was smaller than the mean between-CC distance; across all strain pairs the median distance was 0.082 within CCs and 0.130 between CCs ( P < 0.001). In the in vitro phenotypes, only five of the nine CCs showed smaller within- than between-CC distances, and the GSMM and in vitro distances were only weakly correlated (Mantel r = 0.13, P = 0.03). In an exploratory comparison of two lineages with contrasting profiles, CC-443 ( n = 7) showed negative mean z -scores for all seven substrates, whereas CC-658 ( n = 4) showed positive mean z -scores for all seven, the highest being sulfite (z = + 0.95). In GSMMs, CC-443 lacked reactions for the monoamine/polyamine oxidase family and pantothenate/CoA biosynthesis, whereas CC-658 was enriched in fatty acid/phospholipid biosynthesis, sialic acid metabolism, and anaerobic sulfur respiration. Anaerobic sulfur respiration-related reactions were more prevalent in CC-658 (75%) than in the other CCs (11%), consistent with its high in vitro sulfite utilization; this difference was retained when the comparison was restricted to chicken isolates (0% in CC-443 vs. 100% in CC-658). In silico growth simulations under two gut-mimicking diets (Western and high-fiber) showed consistently lower predicted growth for CC-443 than for CC-658 under both conditions (exact permutation test, P = 0.048), although the eleven models yielded only four distinct predicted values under each diet, which limits the strength of this comparison. These results indicate that metabolic modeling of C. jejuni benefits from considering lineage-level diversity rather than relying on a single reference-strain GSMM.

title: Generative artificial intelligence drives large model generation algorithm for enhancing Chinese modern traditional cultural knowledge
container-title: Discover Artificial Intelligence
f48c63c87e8ab5a4802a0daf6c6d06f0de6ee24c.abstract: Abstract To address outdated knowledge, cultural-context mismatch, weak evidence linkage, and unsupported expansion in general-purpose large language model generation of traditional-cultural content, this study proposes a generative AI-driven knowledge-enhanced generation algorithm. The method decouples a frozen Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct generator from an external dynamic knowledge base and uses a four-field semantic tag scheme covering cultural category, historical stage, regional origin, and application scenario. Candidate evidence is ranked by vector similarity, graph relations, tag consistency, source credibility, and conflict penalties, then assembled into a constrained prompt without modifying the internal attention layers of the frozen model. An incremental update mechanism combines source verification, conflict detection, and expert review, while factual consistency, cultural-context adaptability, and evidence coverage are used for post-generation verification. Experiments cover classical texts, cultural heritage objects, intangible cultural heritage crafts, traditional Chinese opera, and folk culture, with 1,080 factual question-answering samples and 360 contextual generation tasks. The proposed system achieves 88.61% factual accuracy, 95.28% answer relevance, 94.17% evidence faithfulness, and 92.50% cultural-context adaptability. After knowledge updating, accuracy on update-dependent questions rises from 58.67% to 91.33%. These results indicate that the proposed framework provides a traceable, context-sensitive generation pipeline while retaining a frozen generation model; between-system differences are interpreted descriptively because complete paired baseline predictions were not retained.

title: Eye gaze as a window into good-enough processing: Sentence comprehension by Mandarin-Chinese-speaking learners of Korean
container-title: Second Language Research
111b5714b2c690a6f8f9a86f3a41b732de9b6dd5.abstract: The present study examines how Mandarin-Chinese-speaking learners of Korean comprehend clausal constructions expressing transitivity within a good-enough processing framework. Using picture selection with webcam eye-tracking, we compare learners with native Korean speakers in two studies. Study 1 crosses voice (active vs passive), word order (canonical vs scrambled), and verb position (verb-final vs verb-initial). Learners are accurate for canonical actives but perform below chance on passives and show temporally divergent gaze trajectories in critical regions, consistent with a persistent Agent-First bias and limited use of case-marking and passive morphology. Study 2 obscures case markers to isolate verbal morphology; learners again favour agent-first interpretations and show only weak sensitivity to passive morphology. Across the two studies, proficiency predicts more target-like reanalysis, especially in non-canonical configurations. These findings highlight the role of cue alignment and (re)weighting in L2-acquisition pathways and a proficiency-mediated shift towards algorithmic parsing, suggesting the dynamic and adaptive nature of L2 good-enough processing.

title: The Impact of Artificial Intelligence Adoption on Corporate Default Risk: Empirical Evidence Based on Large Language Models
container-title: Innovation in Science and Technology
63702179c1297b4221b67f2229489d8c255713b3.abstract: Against the backdrop of rapid advances in digital technologies and growing uncertainty in the business environment, artificial intelligence (AI) offers firms new opportunities to strengthen risk identification, improve managerial decision-making, and mitigate default risk. Using firm-level data from Chinese A-share listed companies over the period 2009–2024, this study empirically examines the relationship between AI adoption and corporate default risk. The results indicate that AI adoption is associated with a significant reduction in corporate default risk. This finding remains robust to alternative fixed-effects specifications, different levels of standard-error clustering, and the exclusion of observations from periods affected by major external shocks. Heterogeneity analyses further reveal that the negative association is particularly pronounced among firms in non-high-tech industries and those located in eastern and central China. By examining AI adoption from a corporate risk management perspective, this study extends the literature on the economic consequences of AI adoption and provides firm-level empirical evidence on the role of digital technologies in mitigating financial risk. The findings also offer policy implications for integrating AI into corporate management practices and strengthening firms’ risk governance capabilities.

db7c9e84b1582ab85de9311144e98dcd752c562c.abstract: Abstract. We consider a phase-field system modeling solid tumor growth. This system consists of a Cahn–Hilliard equation coupled with a nutrient equation. The former is characterized by a degenerate mobility and a singular potential. Both equations are subject to suitable reaction terms which model proliferation and nutrient consumption. Chemotactic effects are also taken into account. Adding an elliptic regularization, depending on a relaxation parameter [Formula: see text], in the equation for the chemical potential, we prove the existence of a weak solution to an initial and boundary value problem for the relaxed system. Then, we let [Formula: see text] go to zero, and we recover the existence of a weak solution to the original system.

title:

Identification of a Candidate
α-Synuclein Aggregation Inhibitor under Secondary-Nucleation-Dominated
Conditions
container-title:

e0cf17694d119c0dc306df6586e545e58794ae80.abstract: Abstract The process of α-synuclein aggregation results in the formation of amyloid deposits that accumulate in the brain of patients affected by Parkinson’s disease and related synucleinopathies. Among possible therapeutic strategies for these conditions, one approach is based on the development of compounds capable of inhibiting α-synuclein aggregation. An effective inhibition could be achieved by blocking the nucleation sites on the surface of the amyloid fibrils that are responsible for their autocatalytic proliferation. Here, we use an E(3)-equivariant conditional diffusion model to identify candidate inhibitors of this type. With this approach, we generated pocket-conditioned molecules, identified purchasable analogues, and experimentally tested selected compounds. We thus identified a compound that delays α-synuclein aggregation under conditions in which secondary nucleation is the dominant process. These results illustrate the use of conditional diffusion models to identify candidate aggregation inhibitors.

ef47d4c0a77eb0d586acd6cade98d5f282a6038d.abstract: Abstract All-dielectric metasurfaces have been extensively applied to three-dimensional displays, vortex beam generation, beam steering, and luminescence enhancement. However, studies on all-dielectric metasurfaces for enhancing biofluorescence imaging remain relatively scarce. In this study, an anodic aluminum oxide (AAO) template is employed to fabricate a large-area silicon metasurface embedded in PDMS to serve as a fluorescence imaging slide. Under the excitation of the electromagnetic dipole resonance of metasurface, the cells stained with iFluor 555-phalloidin on the metasurface film exhibit a fluorescence enhancement potentially arising from the combined contributions of Purcell-related radiative decay-rate modification, local excitation-field enhancement, and changes in fluorescence collection efficiency, substantially improving the fluorescence imaging quality. The experimental results demonstrate that when the silicon metasurface embedded in PDMS serves as a fluorescence imaging slide, the fluorescence imaging intensity is enhanced by a factor of approximately 3.38. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first demonstration of large-area all-dielectric metasurfaces fabricated via the AAO template method for enhanced fluorescence imaging. This finding broadens the scope of all-dielectric metasurfaces with large area for biomedical fluorescence imaging.

title: The cyclin-G associated kinase (GAK) is a clinically actionable drug target required for mitosis in diffuse large B-cell lymphoma
container-title: Leukemia
a9cb62378e04d30bbb6b908ea14a6e79cf849be6.abstract: Abstract Though 100 kinase inhibitors are approved for clinical use, most kinases in the genome remain poorly characterized. Moreover, though kinase inhibitors have revolutionized the care of selected cancers, most others respond transiently or not at all to these drugs, typically directed against signal-transduction pathways. Given cellular regulation at every step by phosphorylation events, we hypothesized that phenotypic screening and machine-learning analysis can reveal novel kinase targets. Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL), the most common lymphoma, responds poorly to signal transduction-directed kinase inhibitors. We applied a library of probes to DLBCL systems broadly representing its pathogenic heterogeneity and subjected results to iterative target-deconvolution analysis aimed at tumor selectivity (idTRAX). These efforts identified the cyclin G-associated kinase (GAK) as a tumor-selective target. Mechanistic studies showed GAK kinase activity is required for mitotic progression, with inhibition leading to G2/M arrest and cell death and increased efficacy in the absence of the retinoblastoma (RB) tumor suppressor. GAK-directed kinase inhibitors, including repurposed clinical compounds, showed promising single-agent anti-DLBCL activity in vivo. GAK kinase function is therefore a targetable dependency, opening novel treatment strategies suitable for rapid clinical translation. Moreover, we establish phenotypic screening with target deconvolution as a generalizable strategy to reveal tumor-selective kinase dependencies.

title: Reliability and validity of an online auditory aptitude testing platform: A validation study of formant discrimination tasks
container-title: Second Language Research
b374cea3426c06cd735f89db61e59c21636c9ffb.abstract: Individual differences in auditory processing abilities constrain second language (L2) speech learning outcomes. This study developed and validated three versions of an auditory discrimination test designed to measure formant perception acuity, a domain-general auditory ability relevant to L2 learning. We compared Standard (adaptive staircase method), Gamified (staircase with game components), and QUEST (Bayesian adaptive method) versions in terms of threshold estimation, test–retest reliability, and their predictive validity for L2 vowel discrimination. In 2 sessions, 114 Mandarin speakers completed all 3 test versions and an English vowel perception task. All versions yielded comparable thresholds. The Gamified version demonstrated the highest test–retest reliability, followed by the Standard version; the QUEST version showed the least consistency. The relationship between formant acuity and L2 vowel discrimination was statistically indistinguishable across versions. The results indicate that gamification elements can enhance measurement consistency without compromising validity. This open-access platform offers researchers a validated, accessible tool for measuring formant discrimination acuity, a key component of auditory processing in L2 acquisition.

title: The Paradox of Algorithmic Sycophancy: Sycophancy in Large Language Models and the Limits of AI-Mediated Knowledge Reconstruction in the Metacognitive Creative Destruction Model
f31f456f51b7580c96613027043ba5bcb62c702c.abstract: The Metacognitive Creative Destruction (MCD) model approaches educational innovation as a perpetual spiral process. Contradiction (accumulated cognitive conflicts that resist interpretation), activates Metacognitive Capacity, enabling Destructive Unlearning Propensity, the conscious abandonment of outdated mental schemas, which in turn enables Creative Reconstruction Ability, and ultimately, new knowledge. In the model’s empirical validation with 1,498 teachers, a critical finding emerged: AI Augmentation Intensity (AIA) predicted Metacognitive Capacity (MC) and Creative Reconstruction Ability (CRA), but not Destructive Unlearning Propensity (DUP).This article argues that this finding is not accidental, but reflects an inherent weakness of modern AI systems, and more specifically, the tendency toward AI Sycophancy. Models trained with reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) tend to avoid disagreements and be likable to the user, preventing the individual from experiencing cognitive conflicts, perpetuating their already formed beliefs at the expense of scientific accuracy.Therefore, in an environment of “algorithmic flattery”, the necessary contradictions that trigger unlearning are not produced. Based on the MCD model, it is concluded that the absence of unlearning, that is, the deliberate and conscious abandonment of outdated beliefs, mental models and practices, makes the reconstruction of knowledge absolutely superficial and thus, algorithmically condescending interaction does not produce deep and authentic knowledge, regardless of AI Augmentation Intensity.

title: Iterated Hypernode Model, Iterated UberGraph, and Iterated Relational MetaHyperGraph
77113c83960847de8040ee6367b105b3ffe4454b.abstract: The Hypernode Model and UberGraph represent nested vertices and recursive hyperedge membership, respectively, while Meta-HyperGraphs describe relations among hypergraphs. We study three finite, typed extensions of these models. An Iterated Hypernode Model is equipped with explicit cross-level links between vertex occurrences; an Iterated UberGraph treats an entire UberGraph as a fundamental vertex at the next outer level; and an Iterated Relational MetaHyperGraph uses an edge-witnessed lifting of admissible relations. We establish well-definedness, canonical injective representations, and basic properties of nesting depth and relation lifting. Examples illustrate the constructions and clarify the distinction between an incidence-preserving embedding and a recoverable higher-level encoding.

title: The SDI Model: Stabilization, Disconfirmation, Integration. Contact × Safety × Time as a Common Mechanism of Change in Anxiety Disorders, Phobias, and OCD
cfad96cf8f478f2fe036e3de8edb684b6307eb70.abstract: Psychotherapy for anxiety-related conditions is described in the vocabulary of many schools: exposure, habituation, extinction, inhibitory learning, emotional processing, and memory reconsolidation. This paper proposes the SDI Model (Stabilization–Disconfirmation–Integration), a conceptual framework that treats these descriptions as accounts of a single process: the nervous system learns to respond differently to a stimulus that previously triggered fear, avoidance, or rituals. The model specifies three necessary conditions for this change: contact with the stimulus, a framework of safety, and sufficient time (summarized as Contact × Safety × Time). Under these conditions, threat expectancies are disconfirmed, new learning occurs, and the experience is integrated. The model further proposes a clinical principle of the precise stimulus: change is accelerated when contact targets the specific image, thought, phrase, or scene that actually triggers the response, rather than the general label of the fear. The framework is grounded in the inhibitory learning and expectancy violation literature and is offered as a clinically oriented integrative model. Its applications to phobias, panic, and obsessive-compulsive disorder are outlined, and directions for empirical testing are proposed.

title: Understanding Virtual Gifting Behavior on UGC Video Platforms: The Roles of Mukbang Content Values and Danmaku Engagement
98d2a1836986af9b6707bf40c15bb75635c80150.abstract: Virtual gifting has become a crucial mechanism for digital content platforms to achieve commercialization. However, existing research has largely approached gifting behavior through creator-centric frameworks and treated user interactions as homogeneous signals, leaving the inherent value of digital content and the multi-dimensional nature of danmaku engagement underexplored. To fill this gap, this study examines the impact of different dimensions of mukbang UGC consumption values and danmaku engagement on virtual gifting amounts in non-real-time content consumption scenarios, and further analyzes the mediating role of video popularity. We collected panel data from the Bilibili platform, and used panel fixed-effects models and bootstrap methods for hypothesis testing. The results show that different dimensions of UGC consumption values and danmaku engagement have heterogeneous impacts on content dissemination performance and economic performance, while video popularity plays a selective mediating role. This study refines the Theory of Consumption Values by revealing its differentiated behavioral conversion in digital content settings, advances the decoupling perspective between content virality and monetization, conceptualizes danmaku as heterogeneous social signals, and extends virtual gifting research to asynchronous environments where content-centered mechanisms take precedence over creator-driven dynamics.

title: Laya-Med: Efficient Clinical Decision Support with a Compact Language Model
536100ee508f16bc00a6ed917064744e0a816f1c.abstract: Clinical decision support requires models that can interpret patient records with short response times and modest computational demands. We present Laya-Med, a clinical adaptation of a 322-million-parameter bidirectional language model that assigns probabilities to predefined outcomes in a single forward pass. We evaluated the approach in two retrospective studies. For acute abdominal diagnosis, we fine-tuned the model on 1,680 MIMIC-IV-Ext Clinical Decision-Making admissions and compared it with three zero-shot large language models and a term frequency–inverse document frequency (TF-IDF) classifier on 360 held-out admissions. Laya-Med achieved macro-F1 of 81.1% (95% confidence interval 76.1–85.7) and accuracy of 85.6%, compared with 84.6% and 86.9% for Qwen3.8-27B. Mean processing time under batched inference was 10.8 ms per case, versus 0.60 s for Qwen3.8-27B on the same GPU. In a second study, we independently fine-tuned Laya-Dengue on Portuguese narratives generated from dengue surveillance records. On 2,157 test cases, its macro-averaged area under the receiver operating characteristic curve was 95.2%, compared with 94.0% for TF-IDF and 91.1% for MedGemma 27B. For non-fatal severe dengue versus death, the corresponding values were 73.9%, 67.7% and 54.7%. Local interfaces updated predictions in approximately 50 ms. These results support compact, task-adapted encoders as a computationally efficient approach to clinical decision support. Prospective evaluation is needed to establish their performance on clinical workflows and outcomes.

title: Cognitive Computing at the Edge: Lag Analysis and Neural Network Forecasting for Fishery Landings in the Colombian Caribbean
104069ce56d5a7b920f01172ca80aacf17057ffc.abstract: Fishery-dependent indices in data-limited fisheries are short and incomplete, which raises the question of when adaptive learned models, including cognitively inspired ones deployed at the edge, are justified. We analysed monthly landings per unit effort (LPUE) of pink shrimp (Penaeus notialis) in the Gulf of Morrosquillo, Colombian Caribbean: 65.7% of values are missing and the longest continuous segment has 28 months. Naive, trend, autoregressive (AR), echo state network (ESN), LightGBM and LSTM models were compared in rolling-origin experiments with training-only preprocessing, and their cost was measured on an NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano. One-step-ahead errors were 5.1–5.7 kg per trip for the trend, the AR(2) and the learned models, against 7.6 for persistence; no learned model showed a robust out-of-sample improvement over a linear trend or an AR(2). An exploratory model incorporating river flow at a data-selected lag achieved the lowest RMSE (4.2 kg per trip), but its improvement over the statistical baselines was not statistically conclusive and was not consistently reproduced when lag selection was restricted to the training data at each origin. Backcasting was worse than persistence. A fit took 8 ms (AR) to 3–9 s (LSTM); the double-precision ESN execution process showed the largest peak memory footprint (1.7–4.1 GB of 8 GB). The limit is the information in the series, not the platform; under these conditions a linear trend or an AR(2) is a sufficient reference.

title: AI Model Energy and Carbon Disclosure: A Source-Audited Study of 103 Releases (2024-2026)
59d3047d593bdd3064939431188715f273b686fc.abstract: AI model cards and release documents are supposed to help people assess models. For energy and carbon, they often leave out the number a reader needs, or print figures that cannot be compared directly. I built the Release Energy Ledger, a source-traceable record of 161 distinct developer releases, and audited a selected set of 103 dated 2024-2026 releases that passed a page check. On the designated release document, 85 (82.5 percent) print no energy, carbon or compute figure, 1 prints compute only, and 17 (16.5 percent) print an energy or carbon-related figure: 16 training-specific and 1 life-cycle footprint. None prints release-specific inference energy. Meta accounts for 10 of the 17; without Meta, the count is 7 of 93. The figures differ in method, unit, equipment boundary and emissions accounting, and only 8 of the 17 state a basis, a boundary and a method together. Changing the unit of analysis gives 11 of 80 documents, 10 of 59 model families and 7 of 23 developers. The strict-quote subset (5 of 74) is a different evidence frame, not a lower bound. A page re-read confirmed the printed figures for all 17; blinded AI coding agreed with the ledger on 91.9 to 100 percent of fields, and a separately instructed AI adjudicator agreed on 42 of 42 selected cells. These results describe the documents in this selected set, not actual emissions, the universe of releases or legal compliance. No human has validated any label. The ledger and counting script are released with the paper as a versioned data record (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23808341).

title: Shared logical representations with asymmetric access: Evidence from cross-quantifier scope priming across languages
container-title: Second Language Research
fa5432494d65f6dbe8b25cf65b8a204c17919437.abstract: The current study explores whether logical (form) representations underlying doubly-quantified ambiguous sentences are quantifier- and language-general or constrained by quantifier- and language-specific features. We examined cross-quantifier and cross-linguistic priming in Chinese-English bilinguals using sentences with contrasting scope preferences: Mandarin Chinese “ měi / suǒyǒu . . . yī ” and English “ every / all . . . a ” constructions. Three sentence-picture matching experiments involving 249 participants tested priming effects across three contexts: within L1 Chinese (L1-L1), from L1 Chinese to L2 English (L1-L2), and within L2 English (L2-L2). Results revealed a language-of-prime asymmetry: robust priming emerged across both within- and cross-quantifier conditions in L1-L1 and L1-L2 contexts when L1 served as the priming language; whereas priming was restricted to the within-quantifier condition in L2-L2 when L2 served as the priming language, providing evidence for L1-L2 asymmetry in bilingual scope priming. This asymmetry may be mediated by Mandarin’s obligatory overt dōu-mediated scope-making configuration, which externalizes the scope computation and renders abstract logical (form) representations structurally explicit and cognitively accessible. The current study is the first to demonstrate robust cross-quantifier, cross-language scope priming with quantifiers exhibiting opposite baseline preference, revealing that shared logical representations exist across languages; yet their cross-quantifier generalizations are modulated by language-specific properties, with L1 serving as a foundation for L2 quantifier interpretation in bilingual processing.

title: Linguistic Ambiguity and Hallucination in Large Language Models: A Cross-Linguistic and Cultural Analysis of Output Accuracy
container-title: Frontiers in International Humanities & Social Sciences
72cd722d157a03c8e092eb1866946be7830e980e.abstract: An inaccurate response to an ambiguous prompt can reflect a mistaken interpretation, an unsupported factual assertion or a translation problem. These outcomes require different explanations and evaluation criteria. This paper examines their relationship through a structured literature analysis and a proposed Chinese-English evaluation of GPT and Claude models. It distinguishes ambiguity in meaning and reference from factual support, translation fidelity and the adequacy of available evidence. Existing studies inform a comparative framework, while their different models, languages and tasks limit direct comparisons. The proposed evaluation pairs ambiguous prompts with disambiguated versions and contrasts implicit cultural context with explicit context. Bilingual reviewers validate the materials before generation. Exact model versions, prompting conditions and output records are retained, and blinded human annotation separates supported claims, confirmed contradictions, unsupported additions and unresolved cases. Evaluation reports factual outcomes alongside answer coverage, clarification and abstention, with repeated outputs analysed at the item level. Mitigation involves clarifying consequential uncertainty, supplying relevant context and checking claims against appropriate sources. The paper contains no new model outputs, measured hallucination rates or model rankings. Its contribution is a design for examining how language and context affect interpretation and factual reporting without treating every incorrect or unscorable response as hallucination.

title: Pathways for Teaching Model Reform Driven by the Interaction between New Quality Productive Forces and Vocational Education: The Case of Electrical Automation Technology
container-title: Frontiers in International Humanities & Social Sciences
14d63151b73b468ada88e96f57debf86e7cecb59.abstract: Electrical automation teaching must prepare students to commission interconnected equipment, diagnose faults and judge technical changes against operating requirements. These tasks bring the relationship between new quality productive forces and vocational education into the classroom: industrial change reshapes competence requirements, while skilled graduates and college technical services can support the adoption and improvement of production technologies. This paper develops a teaching reform proposal for the three-year higher vocational Electrical Automation Technology programme. It combines policy and document analysis, conceptual comparison and instructional design, using the national professional teaching standard and research on project-based learning, workplace learning and authentic assessment. The analysis identifies coordination problems involving curriculum sequencing, practical training, enterprise participation, assessment and resource provision. A proposed project, upgrading a conveying and sorting cell while examining its energy use, connects programmable logic controller programming, variable-frequency drives, human-machine interfaces and industrial networking. Students move from requirement analysis and simulation to supervised commissioning, fault diagnosis and evidence-based review. Assessment combines project documentation and operating records with individual explanation and transfer tasks. The proposed reciprocal mechanism depends on translating workplace requirements into assessable learning tasks and returning reviewed teaching outcomes to enterprise discussion, staff training or technical service. These routes require sustained teacher coordination and explicit responsibility for accepting changes. The paper presents a design for subsequent piloting; it reports no institutional intervention or measured learning gains. A future evaluation should examine competence transfer separately from any claim about enterprise productivity, because a functioning classroom prototype provides insufficient evidence of industrial impact.

title: Enhancing Communicative Competence in English through Play-Based Language Activities: Implications for English Language Teaching in Basic Schools
container-title: British Journal of Contemporary Education
c1a2bf4e85e807c6ca502d39a68d240752bb3346.abstract: This study examined the extent to which play-based language activities improve learners’ communicative competence in English and explored teachers’ and learners’ perceptions of their contribution to English language learning in basic schools. The study adopted an explanatory sequential mixed-methods design guided by the pragmatist paradigm. The quantitative phase employed a one-group pre-test–post-test quasi-experimental design involving 45 Basic Seven learners selected through census sampling. The qualitative phase involved semi-structured interviews with two English language teachers and 10 purposively selected learners. Data were collected through a communicative competence achievement test and interview guides. Quantitative data were analysed using descriptive statistics and paired-samples t-test, while qualitative data were analysed thematically. The findings revealed that participation in play-based language activities improved learners’ communicative competence in English. Teachers and learners perceived the activities as enhancing vocabulary development, oral communication, pronunciation, confidence, classroom participation, collaboration, and motivation to use English in authentic communicative situations. The study concludes that play-based language activities are a valuable pedagogical approach for developing communicative competence in English. It recommends that English language teachers integrate structured play-based activities into classroom instruction and that teacher education programmes strengthen teachers’ capacity to implement play-based pedagogies effectively.

title: An Application of the Self-Determination Theory Model for AI-Enhanced, Digital Psychosocial Interventions for Pediatric Disabilities
container-title: Western Journal of Nursing Research
6a353330c39f733eb7e369612f893bac2e52174c.abstract: Background: Youth with developmental disabilities (DDs) experience elevated psychosocial challenges, including difficulties with emotion regulation, self-concept, and access to timely mental health support. Pediatric nurses are well-positioned to address these needs; however, time constraints, limited training, and restricted access to specialty services often impede the provision of consistent psychosocial care. Digitally delivered psychosocial interventions enhanced by artificial intelligence (AI) offer new opportunities for individualized, accessible support, but these approaches frequently lack a clear theoretical foundation. Purpose: This paper applied Self-Determination Theory (SDT), specifically Basic Psychological Needs Theory, to guide pediatric nurses’ use of AI-enhanced, digital psychosocial interventions for DDs in practice. Methods: A theory-driven synthesis mapped SDT needs (autonomy, competence, and relatedness) to AI-enabled intervention features: conversational agents, neuro/adaptive feedback, and emotion-recognition tailoring. Results: The framework specifies how these features can promote volitional engagement, optimal challenge with timely feedback, and supportive interactions for youth with DDs. It also notes evidence gaps (small, heterogeneous samples; limited comparisons and follow-up) and barriers involving payment/workload, equity and access, and data protection, transparency, and bias. Conclusions/Implications: SDT offers a coherent, testable foundation for designing, evaluating, and integrating AI-enhanced psychosocial supports for pediatric DDs. Nurses can screen for support, coach families, monitor risks, and advocate for ethical deployment and rigorous research.
