title: Adaptive optimization of large-margin learning for physics-informed time–frequency maps for the diagnosis of rotating components
container-title: Structural Health Monitoring
054ff56cd7bc0512b0025c9a721179018133bf56.abstract: This article introduces a novel physics-informed large-margin learning framework for diagnosing rotating component faults, addressing the limitations of traditional methods and “black-box” artificial intelligence models in handling complex, noisy vibration data. The methodology integrates feature mode decomposition and short-time Fourier transform to generate physics-informed time–frequency maps, from which interpretable features are extracted. A large-margin learning model then utilizes these features, with its five critical hyperparameters adaptively optimized using the slime mould algorithm to ensure robustness and optimal performance. Evaluated on the Case Western Reserve University (CWRU) and intelligent maintenance systems (IMS) bearing datasets, the proposed framework achieves a diagnostic accuracy of 88.75% on CWRU and 96.67% on IMS, outperforming seven state-of-the-art classification baselines implemented under identical experimental conditions. This approach enhances interpretability, diagnostic accuracy, and generalization, offering a more reliable solution for machine health monitoring.

title: A CONCEPTUAL MODEL OF ADAPTIVE MECHANISMS IN INNOVATION-ORIENTED AGRICULTURAL ENTREPRENEURSHIP
container-title: Baltic Journal of Economic Studies
7b84fefbaca664a28306eee312949b0c9f8af8ea.abstract: The war in Ukraine has presented the agricultural sector with an unprecedented combination of risks, including the loss of production assets, climate volatility, supply chain disruption and institutional instability. In such circumstances, traditional models of entrepreneurial resilience, which are primarily designed for peacetime or isolated natural or economic shocks, lose their adaptive capacity. Meanwhile, there is virtually no comprehensive theoretical synthesis of the mechanisms by which agribusiness adapts to multiple simultaneous threats. This article aims to substantiate a conceptual model of adaptive management mechanisms for innovative agribusiness by integrating the theories of dynamic capabilities and adaptive management with institutional economics. The subject of this study is the processes through which agro-industrial enterprises adapt to conditions of institutional instability and armed conflict. The study is based on the systematic organisation and critical analysis of scientific literature on dynamic capabilities theory, classical adaptive management, and institutional economics. It also draws on a synthesis of empirical studies on agribusiness adaptability under various types of shock. As a result, a four-level conceptual model has been developed. This model sequentially combines an exogenous shock in the form of armed conflict with a reinterpreted triad of dynamic capabilities—sensing, seizing and transforming—for wartime conditions. It also incorporates an institutional moderator and the final outcome of 'bounce forward' adaptive resilience. The practical value of the model lies in its potential use as an analytical tool for assessing the preparedness of agricultural enterprises for multiple crises, developing state policy to support the agricultural sector during wartime and the post-war period, and for formulating enterprise management strategies that take into account the quality of the institutional environment.

title: Novel Mathematical Model for Natural Dispersion of Oil Spill on Dyanmic Sea
545746b45d1ca96a7c85b2ed79bb6830dd8d4181.abstract: Abstract Natural dispersion is an important weathering process that controls the transfer of oil from the sea surface into the water column. However, conventional dispersion models have limited capability to represent the combined effects of dynamic wave breaking, whitecap coverage, turbulence, oil properties, and droplet formation. The present study develops an energy-constrained natural-dispersion model in which whitecap coverage defines the dynamically active slick area and a wave-breaking energy-transfer efficiency determines the fraction of turbulent energy available for creation of new oil–water interfacial area. The proposed framework introduces whitecap coverage to represent the dynamically active fraction of the oil slick and an energy-transfer efficiency factor to account for the portion of wave-breaking energy available for droplet generation. The model also explicitly considers the interfacial energy required to create new oil–water surface area and couples turbulent energy dissipation with oil viscosity, interfacial tension, and droplet size. This provides a mechanistic relationship between sea-state forcing, wave breaking, useful dispersion energy, droplet generation, water-column entrainment, and subsequent resurfacing. The proposed approach provides an improved physical representation of natural oil dispersion under variable sea conditions and offers a basis for more realistic prediction of oil behavior during marine spill events.

title: Blood-brain barrier model architecture shapes peripheral immune cell trafficking in Parkinson’s disease
container-title: Acta Neuropathologica Communications
f1b9f57262a350c5821399b3df5c0d441fde2d36.abstract: Abstract Parkinson’s disease (PD) is a neurodegenerative disorder traditionally characterized by dopaminergic neuron loss in the substantia nigra pars compacta , but peripheral immune dysregulation and blood-brain barrier (BBB) dysfunction have been increasingly implicated in disease pathophysiology. However, how circulating immune cells interact with the human BBB and how these interactions are captured across experimental models remains poorly understood. In particular, human BBB models offer multiple platforms to interrogate these biological questions, with organ-on-chip approaches attracting significant interest. In this context, it is essential to determine whether model architecture influences the assessment of immune-endothelial interactions in PD, and if it may lead to fundamentally different interpretations of immune cell trafficking at the human BBB. Here, we compared peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) from control donors or individuals with PD in human induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC)-derived BBB models to determine how static and dynamic BBB systems influence immune cell behavior. To do so, we leveraged our brain chip platform to establish a model based on expression of the PD-associated SNCA triplication mutation. Using two-dimensional permeable membrane inserts and a three-dimensional (3D) microfluidic BBB chip, we evaluated PBMC attachment and transmigration according to PBMC disease status, endothelial cellular background (control or SNCA triplication), and exposure to α-synuclein (α-Syn) monomers or preformed fibrils (PFFs). PBMCs from PD donors showed increased baseline reactivity and altered endothelial interactions compared with controls. In insert-based models, greater PBMC attachment and selectively increased transmigration of PD PBMCs were associated with SNCA triplication vs. control endothelial cells, while PFF exposure increased attachment without affecting transmigration. In contrast, in the microfluidic BBB chip, attachment was largely unchanged by endothelial background or α-Syn exposure, whereas transmigration increased following α-Syn monomer pre-treatment. Together, PBMC-BBB interactions in PD appear to be shaped by immune cell status, endothelial background, and α-Syn exposure, but are strongly influenced by the architecture of the BBB model. This study underscores the importance of physiologically relevant multicellular and flow-based BBB systems and provides a human-focused framework for studying peripheral immune cell trafficking across the diseased BBB. These findings also emphasize that biological insights into BBB function are inherently shaped by the experimental model used, underscoring the need for complementary human BBB platforms.

title: Post-Training on the Clock: Specializing a Small Language Model on a Consumer GPU
30fd5261958157f23f1937e99eb7454cba3d53c6.abstract: Abstract How should a language model be specialized for a target task when training is limited to one consumer GPU and a few hours? We study the allocation of a nominal three-hour training budget, with up to 0.3 additional hours, between supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO). We use tool calling as a case study because of its practical relevance to language-model agents and its verifiable outputs. Using Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct with low-rank adaptation on an RTX 5060 Ti with 16 GB of memory, we compare SFT, GRPO, and six sequential SFT-to-GRPO allocations. Training uses a filtered mixture of xLAM function-calling examples and Hammer irrelevance examples, covering both call construction and abstention when no offered tool is suitable. Evaluation reports xLAM exact tool-call and function-name accuracies for local call construction, BFCL-v3 Single-turn FC (agg) for external function calling, BFCL-v3 Irrelevance (agg) for abstention, and MMLU, MATH-500, and IFEval for selected general capabilities. The suffix (agg) denotes study-specific averages of selected subset accuracies weighted by subset size. At the last evaluated checkpoints within 3.3 reported hours, SFT achieves the highest xLAM exact tool-call accuracy (82.82%), compared with 69.13% for GRPO alone. Selected hybrid allocations improve external function-calling accuracy over SFT, with different abstention trade-offs. Most sampled GRPO groups have constant rewards and provide no relative task-reward signal. We release the prepared mixed dataset, all allocation-study checkpoints, and Post-Training Lab, an editable training and evaluation codebase with CUDA and MLX implementations.

title: PAANN-ProAct Autoencoder Neural Network Model for Energy Efficient and Robust Anomaly Detection in WSN
container-title: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
ef4d97535b1cc4ff06c8b8ec05f36f44f9c922fb.abstract: Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs) are extensively employed in environmental monitoring, healthcare, industrial automation, military surveillance, and security applications. However, the limited energy, computational capacity, and communication resources of sensor nodes make efficient anomaly detection a challenging task. Malicious attacks, sensor faults, communication failures, and abnormal measurements can further degrade network reliability and reduce its operational lifetime. To overcome these challenges, this research proposes a ProAct Autoencoder Neural Network (PAANN) for energy-efficient and robust anomaly detection in WSNs. The proposed approach employs a cluster-based architecture in which sensor nodes perform local data processing and anomaly detection, while cluster heads aggregate the relevant information and forward significant anomaly events to the base station. The PAANN model utilizes an autoencoder to learn normal sensor-data patterns and detect abnormal observations based on reconstruction errors. Spatial correlation among neighboring sensor nodes is incorporated to improve anomaly identification and localization. An erroneous-decision abstainer mechanism is also introduced to reduce false-positive alerts and unnecessary computational operations. Furthermore, the Ascendable Energy Coherent Array-based Anomaly Detection (AECAAD) mechanism is incorporated to improve energy efficiency and identify potential Denial-of-Service (DoS) attacks from abnormal communication patterns. Huffman and Arithmetic Coding techniques are employed to compress data before transmission, thereby reducing communication overhead, bandwidth consumption, and energy expenditure. The proposed framework is designed to provide accurate and timely anomaly detection while extending network lifetime and improving the reliability, security, and robustness of WSNs.

title:
Large-scale frequency-domain elastic wave modeling with
column-norm-weighted CARP-CG
42b821a62d2c31c9b270b48a14882a9f1538c24c.abstract: Abstract Frequency-domain elastic wave modeling requires solving a large-scale sparse linear system. To avoid unaffordable memory costs when direct solvers are used, we resort to iterative methods. An attractive choice is the component-averaged row projections method with conjugate-gradient acceleration (CARP-CG), which has been shown to be robust in complicated physical settings. To avoid its slow convergence, we develop the Weighted CARP-CG (WCARP-CG) method, in which squared column norms of row-scaled local matrices, a positive shift, and an exponent 𝛽 define fixed positive weights. These weights determine local row updates and component averaging in the 𝑊 -inner product and induce the 𝑀-inner product for CG on original variables. For consistent systems, the CG system and the original equations have the same solutions, and CG converges in exact arithmetic. At 𝛽 = 0.5, weighting decreases condition numbers computed from positive eigenvalues by factors of 2.77–3.38 in small-scale tests, relative to equal weights. We verify the accuracy of the WCARP-CG solutions by comparisons with direct solver solutions. Across six three-dimensional tests combining frequencies of 0.5–3 Hz with different grid spacings and two further tests at different Poisson’s ratios, the number of iterations decreases by 51.8–65.5% and iteration-loop time decreases by 45.1–61.7% relative to CARP-CG at a relative residual of 10−4 for the row-scaled system. We also use an improved CSR storage strategy that reduces coefficient and column-index storage to 5% of the conventional explicit format.

title: Recruitment, Retention, and Patient Engagement of Adolescents and Young Adult Cancer Survivors in Psycho-Oncology Research: A Qualitative Study
container-title: Journal of Adolescent and Young Adult Oncology
62a391227dba3c6b0be1d3418ad255264ab33023.abstract: Background: Adolescent and young adult (AYA) cancer patients/survivors are underrepresented in psycho-oncology, limiting research generalizability. This study identified strategies to improve AYA recruitment and retention by consulting survivors and health care professionals (HCPs). Methods: Fourteen online sessions were conducted, comprising eight individual interviews and six small group discussions (2–4 participants), with 15 AYAs (18–25 years; 47% culturally and linguistically diverse [CALD]) and 9 HCPs (33% clinical; 67% researchers). Data were analyzed using inductive content analysis. Results: AYAs and HCPs considered research participation through an implicit “value proposition” shaped by three interrelated domains: trust, respect for time, and ease of engagement. Trust acted as a gatekeeper, with AYAs preferring studies introduced by trusted clinicians. CALD survivors valued rapport with culturally matched researchers. Financial incentives signaled respect for time and legitimacy, with most survivors favoring guaranteed, staggered payments over lotteries, although preferences varied. Ease of engagement supported recruitment and retention through low-burden designs, digital communication, procedural flexibility, and clear materials. Reduced burden appeared to reinforce trust, and trusted relationships appeared to make participation easier. Conclusion: Findings suggest that recruitment and retention of AYAs may benefit from HCP-led recruitment, guaranteed financial incentives, and low-burden digital study designs, delivered through integrated, survivor-centered and culturally tailored approaches that build relational trust and reduce structural barriers to participation. Future studies should evaluate and report on the effectiveness of recruitment strategies and further test the preliminary framework proposed here to strengthen the evidence base for AYA research engagement.

title: ddmtorch: A Differentiable, MPS-Accelerated Toolbox for Drift-Diffusion Model Estimation on Apple Silicon
de8c36ae78d2310a43931b21cc60da51d21b9a6e.abstract: Abstract The drift-diffusion model (DDM) explains choice probabilities and response-time (RT) dis- tributions through a small set of interpretable parameters, but fitting it requires repeated eval- uation of the Wiener first-passage time (WFPT) density. Existing tools are predominantly CPU-bound, rely on compiled code, or are embedded in Bayesian sampling frameworks. We present ddmtorch, an open-source PyTorch (Paszke et al., 2019) implementation that vectorizes the WFPT likelihood across trials and subjects, supports automatic differentiation, and runs on CPU and Apple Silicon Metal Performance Shaders (MPS). It provides batched maximum- likelihood estimation, a hybrid large-time/small-time density following Navarro and Fuss (2009), synthetic data generators, and a fixed-proportion contaminant mixture. On an Apple M5 Mac- Book Air, MPS evaluates a forward–backward pass over one million trials in 0.62 s, versus 1.22 s for CPU float32 and 3.21 s for CPU float64; a 50,000-trial, 20-subject MLE fit takes 2.32 s ver- sus 4.10 s and 7.30 s. In 100 synthetic datasets with 500 trials each, parameter correlations ranged from 0.981 to 0.998. On a public motion-discrimination dataset, ddmtorch and PyDDM recovered nearly identical parameters; on a 14-subject dataset, ddmtorch MLE and a PyMC 5 HDDM-style hierarchical fit correlated at r = 0.996–0.9995, with the expected shrinkage. The WFPT math is inherited from the literature; the contribution is a differentiable, MPS- ready implementation and a transparent evaluation. We document limitations, including the absence of inter-trial variability and hierarchical priors. Because MPS does not support float64, precision-sensitive workflows should use the CPU float64 path.

title: A dual‐boundary model for gas‐like/liquid‐like crossovers from subcritical to supercritical states
container-title: AIChE Journal
9894e3a659b6a78953e5245c3e897a93e51826f7.abstract: Abstract Supercritical fluids do not behave as a featureless single phase; instead, they retain gas‐like and liquid‐like characteristics. Existing descriptions usually emphasize a single Widom‐type line, whereas the finite width of the crossover remains insufficiently defined. Here we propose a dual‐boundary thermodynamic map that combines a critical‐tangent inner boundary with a hierarchy of reduced density‐pressure response contours. The inner boundary is defined by the tangent to the vapor–liquid coexistence curve at the critical point and represents the near‐critical central trend shared by several Widom‐line candidates. The outer response envelopes are described by the dimensionless response [ T r ( dρ r / dp r ) Tr ], which provides comparable response‐level contours for diverse pure fluids and selected refrigerant mixtures. Comparisons with experimental crossover observations for water, methane, and carbon dioxide, together with thermodynamic calculations for pure fluids and selected refrigerant mixtures, demonstrate the practical applicability and reproducibility of the proposed framework.

title: Immediate and Long‐Term Effects of Prejudice Control Instructions to Reduce Accent Discrimination Against Second‐Language Speakers of English
container-title: International Journal of Applied Linguistics
c9dda8207565abcb90095bb1b7c8c67974a4a5cf.abstract: ABSTRACT Previous research has shown that non‐native accents can negatively affect listeners’ perceptions of lecturers’ competence, teaching quality, and hirability. Listener‐focused interventions, such as awareness‐raising instructions in the form of brief texts encouraging awareness and fairness have been shown to mitigate such biases immediately after the intervention, yet their long‐term impact remains unclear. This longitudinal study examined the immediate and long‐term effects of awareness‐raising instructions on evaluations of moderately Dutch‐accented English lecturers. A total of 349 highly proficient L2 English listeners with various nationalities were randomly assigned to intervention or control groups and evaluated lecturers at two time points, 12 weeks apart. Participants who received awareness‐raising instructions rated lecturers more positively on status, likeability, dynamism, teaching quality, and hirability at the first time point. However, these effects did not last after 12 weeks and did not transfer to a novel speaker at the second time point. These findings suggest that brief awareness raising instructions can temporarily reduce accent‐related bias but may be insufficient to produce lasting or generalized changes in evaluations.

title: Exploring AI as a reading companion: L2 learners' approaches to literary comprehension
container-title: Foreign Language Annals
29d85c7100d4beb2a558fa842c9a1f66727182f2.abstract: Abstract Generative AI tools are increasingly present in language learning, yet their role in second language (L2) reading remains underexplored. This study investigates how intermediate German learners engaged with ChatGPT during interpretive reading using a three‐condition design with a Grimm fairytale. The study examines the relationship between AI access and reading performance, patterns of use or resistance, and students' ethical and motivational interpretations of AI‐mediated reading. Generative AI emerged as a negotiated presence that learners approached with curiosity, caution, or resistance. Required AI use was associated with reduced differences in comprehension outcomes across proficiency levels, whereas optional use revealed diverse strategic, reluctant, and value‐driven stances rooted in ethical concerns, discipline‐specific norms, and a desire to maintain interpretive autonomy. Students who routinely used AI in other courses engaged more selectively in German, suggesting AI practices may be shaped by disciplinary contexts. The findings support guided, reflective AI integration while valuing learner resistance.

title: Reduced-Order Model for Multijet Supersonic Retropropulsion
container-title: Journal of Spacecraft and Rockets
bab0f4ae75959bc924197574b0769efd5c9ce47a.abstract: Supersonic retropropulsion enables human-scale Mars entry, but predicting multijet aerodynamic interference forces and moments remains a challenge. Existing high-fidelity models are computationally prohibitive for trajectory analysis, while prior reduced-order models assume a single unified plume and therefore miss the topological transition between isolated and merged plumes. This work presents a topology-adaptive reduced-order model that removes this limitation, predicting heatshield forces during multijet operation at zero degrees angle of attack. The framework employs a shared-cap control volume coupled to an annular throat, using an axisymmetric method of characteristics solver to resolve individual plume boundaries. A blockage model adjusts according to whether plumes act as separate jets or merge into a single structure, resolving the ambiguity in identifying the contact surface for noninteracting nozzles, particularly in annular configurations. Comparisons against NASA wind-tunnel data for single-, three-, four-, and eight-jet configurations across a range of freestream Mach numbers and mass flow rates demonstrate that the model reproduces shielding onset and high-thrust force plateaus, reducing the mean squared error by more than 50% relative to a single-jet baseline. At approximately 1 s per prediction on one CPU, the model facilitates rapid design trade studies and characterizes the coupling between nozzle canting and control-volume topology.

title: Analisis Peramalan Produksi Gambir di Sumatera Barat Menggunakan Model ARIMA
container-title: JURNAL AGRIBISNIS
670c442710dc17035c38e1f156c5bdd2148d8d96.abstract: Tanaman gambir adalah salah satu tanaman yang memiliki potensi ekspor yang tinggi di Indonesia dan sebagian besar berasal di Sumatera Barat. Tanaman gambir memiliki banyak manfaat yaitu diantaranya sebagai bahan campuran menyirih, buah gambir juga dapat dimanfaatkan sebagai bahan baku obat-obatan, bahan kosmetik, pewarna tekstil, dan sebagai bahan baku perekat kayu lapis dan papan. Namun tanaman gambir memiliki kendala dalam hal produksi yang masih dilakukan secara sederhana sehingga jumlah produksi gambir mengalami fluktuasi sepanjang tahun. Tujuan penelitian ini untuk meramalkan produksi selama 5 periode. Metode penelitian merupakan penelitian kuantitatif dengan pendekatan forecasting menggunakan model ARIMA. Teknik pemodelan ARIMA merupakan salah satu indikator yang banyak digunakan untuk peramalan dan merupakan metode yang menghasilkan prediksi berdasarkan sintesis pola data historis. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa model forecasting yang cocok ialah dengan model ARIMA atau Box Jenkins (1, 1, 2) dengan jumlah peramalan selama 5 tahun sebanyak 70.539,69 Ton. Hasil peramalan menunjukkan produksi gambir meningkat selama periode tahun 2023-2027. ARIMA merupakan pemodelan deret waktu yang hanya akurat untuk prediksi jangka pendek, sehingga perlu mempertimbangkan faktor-faktor lain yang terkait untuk investasi jangka panjang. Gambier is one of the plants that has high export potential in Indonesia and mostly comes from West Sumatra. The gambier plant has many benefits, including as a mixture of stirring, gambier fruit can also be used as a raw material for medicines, cosmetic materials, textile dyes, and as raw materials for plywood and board adhesives. However, gambier plants have obstacles in terms of production that are still carried out simply so that the amount of gambier production fluctuates throughout the year. The purpose of this study is to forecast production for 5 periods. The research method is a quantitative research with a forecasting approach using the ARIMA model. The ARIMA modeling technique is one of the indicators that is widely used for forecasting and is a method that produces predictions based on the synthesis of historical data patterns. The results of the study show that the forecasting model is suitable for the ARIMA or Box Jenkins model (1, 1, 2) with a 5-year forecast of 70,539.69 tons. The forecast results show that gambier production will increase for 5 periods of 2023-2027. ARIMA is a time series modeling that is only accurate for short-term predictions, so it is necessary to consider other factors related to long-term investments.

title: A comprehensive mapping review of participatory autism research over a 22-year period
container-title: Research Involvement and Engagement
785f9bbc9dbe30a1841780ff07bf27faa9604d5b.abstract: Abstract Background Participatory research, which involves community members as partners rather than merely research subjects, has gained prominence in autism research. However, the extent and nature of participatory approaches across the field remain unclear. Methods We conducted a mapping review of autism research reporting community involvement, searching six databases. We coded who was involved, at what level, and in which research activities, and examined factors associated with participation. Results We identified 382 studies published between 2001 and 2023, with 95% published in the past decade. Two-thirds (67%) involved Autistic people, though one-third claiming to be “participatory” excluded them entirely. The most common participation level was consulting (31%), with community-led (5%) and community-controlled (1%) research remaining rare. Community involvement concentrated in study design (73%) rather than analysis (33%) or dissemination (29%). Participatory research was heavily concentrated in Western countries (USA, UK, Australia, Canada: 86%), applied research areas, and qualitative studies. Deeper participation was associated with identity-first language use and publication in journals with clear community-centered agendas. Conclusions While participatory language is increasingly becoming the norm in autism research, genuine power-sharing between researchers and community members is still a rare occurrence. Most participatory research operates at consultative levels, with academic researchers retaining primary decision-making authority. Moving toward authentic participation requires systemic changes to funding structures, institutional policies, and epistemic hierarchies that determine whose knowledge counts.

title: Primary stability of dental implants placed by novice surgeons: an ex vivo study across two implant systems in a porcine mandible model
container-title: International Journal of Implant Dentistry
7d161f1a4222d13651e84d8282bbae01ed7546e4.abstract: Abstract Purpose Dental implant placement is a technically demanding procedure in which surgical experience is considered a key determinant of outcome. Primary stability, as measured by the implant stability quotient (ISQ) via resonance frequency analysis (RFA), is a critical predictor of successful osseointegration. This study aimed to quantify the influence of surgical experience on primary implant stability in a standardized porcine mandible model. Methods Dental students with no prior implant experience and experienced oral surgeons placed implants using two commercially available systems (Straumann Standard Plus and Astra Tech EV). Primary stability was assessed by RFA immediately after insertion at four standardized measurement positions. ISQ values were analyzed using a linear mixed-effects model with surgical experience, implant system, and measurement position as fixed factors and a random intercept for implant to account for the non-independence of the four measurements obtained per implant. Results A total of 760 ISQ measurements were included in the analysis. Experienced surgeons achieved significantly higher ISQ values (M = 75.72, SD = 5.22) than students (M = 68.68, SD = 11.61; p < 0.001), with an overall mean difference of approximately 7 ISQ points. Within the Straumann Standard Plus, the difference was 8.14 ISQ points ( p = 0.028); within the Astra Tech EV, the difference was 5.42 ISQ points ( p < 0.001). Variability was markedly greater in the student group across both systems. Conclusions Surgical experience significantly influences primary implant stability within both implant systems investigated. Novice operators achieve lower and less consistent ISQ values, which may have clinical implications for the selection of loading protocols. These findings suggest that structured training may help improve primary stability among less-experienced operators, a hypothesis that warrants prospective clinical evaluation. Clinical trial number Not applicable.

title: Construction and Case Study of a Quality Evaluation Model for Intelligent Information Systems in a Generative Artificial Intelligence Environment: The Case of Bilibili
container-title: Computers and Artificial Intelligence
ae0c9b8f351889f3b45fc54a1fff53fb8eabc8be.abstract: After generative artificial intelligence (AI) was embedded in search, content generation, and user interaction, traditional information system quality evaluation faced new boundaries. Based on the DeLone and McLean (D&M) Information Systems Success Model, this study adopts literature research and a single-case study, takes Bilibili as the case, and constructs and applies a six-dimensional evaluation framework based on public materials, observations of platform functions, and publicly available user feedback. The findings show that system quality, information quality, and service quality can still explain basic platform operation, information output, and service support, but they cannot fully cover AI’s semantic understanding and task completion, the trustworthiness of generated results, and continuous human-computer interaction. Therefore, this study introduces AI intelligence quality, trustworthiness quality, and interaction quality on the basis of the three traditional dimensions and clarifies the boundary of each dimension. The Bilibili case shows that the framework can identify both basic capabilities and AI-specific quality, thereby helping to avoid conflating technical performance, content quality, intelligent capability, and trust issues. The study provides a structured analytical framework for evaluating the quality of intelligent information systems in a generative AI environment and a reference for platforms to optimize AI functions and governance mechanisms.

title: AAV8-PDE6B with 3’UTR provides rescue of photoreceptor structure and function in the rd10 mouse model of retinitis pigmentosa
container-title: Gene Therapy
f86d722952ac40f91bd41cf2cd24f5e919851cf6.abstract: Abstract Retinitis pigmentosa (RP), a leading cause of inherited blindness, results in a subset of cases from phosphodiesterase 6 (PDE6) deficiency. We evaluated a novel gene therapy construct, AAV8-RK- PDE6B -3′UTR, in the rd10 mouse model which has a homozygous missense variant that disrupts the function of the β-subunit of PDE6. The construct utilises a rhodopsin-kinase promoter, human PDE6B cDNA, and a PDE6B 3′ untranslated region (3′UTR), which was delivered subretinally at postnatal day 12 (P12). Treated mice showed sustained preservation of retinal function and structure for up to 15 months, as confirmed by visual acuity (VA), electroretinography (ERG), optical coherence tomography (OCT), and immunohistochemistry. This represents the longest functional and structural follow-up reported for AAV-mediated PDE6B gene supplementation in the rd10 model. Inclusion of the PDE6B 3′UTR increased PDE6B expression in vitro and improved functional rescue in four week post-therapy testing. These data indicate that the combination described here of vector capsid type and promoter specific to photoreceptors, along with PDE6B 3′UTR sequence may provide benefit in therapeutic effect in PDE6B gene therapy.

title: Additive manufacturing-aware topology optimization of cooling channels using a reduced-order cold plate model for electric machine water jackets
container-title: Proceedings of the Estonian Academy of Sciences
a89048784a7118c8f2c6363ad8c35041d8d40569.abstract: Integrated liquid cooling jackets are widely used in the thermal management of high-power-density motors, but traditional designs rely on parametric channel layouts, failing to fully utilize the geometric degrees of freedom offered by additive manufacturing (AM). This paper proposes an AM-aware topology optimization framework based on a reduced-order cold plate model. A two-dimensional case study systematically investigates the effects of manufacturability-oriented regularization on channel topology and thermo-hydraulic performance. Results show that stronger regularization substantially reduces interface complexity and fluid area fraction, while generally increasing hydraulic resistance and degrading thermal performance. A sharp-interface reanalysis further demonstrates good agreement in the global thermal response, while revealing the sensitivity of the local peak temperature and hydraulic conductance to the density-based representation.

title: Construction of a clinical model for early prediction of gestational diabetes mellitus based on women of increased maternal age singleton pregnant women
container-title: International Journal of Gynecology & Obstetrics
68054920138a0f4cfba78e62583b137a3c0b0921.abstract: Abstract Purpose This study develops and validates an early clinical prediction model for gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) specifically in women of increased maternal age with singleton pregnancies, thereby facilitating early identification of high‐risk individuals and timely targeted intervention. Methods This retrospective cohort study included 338 women of increased maternal age with singleton pregnancies (82 diagnosed with GDM) who received prenatal care at the First People's Hospital of Changde between January 2023 and June 2024, comprising the training set. An additional 232 women (70 with GDM) seen between July 2024 and June 2025 comprised the validation set. Clinical data were collected and risk factors for GDM were identified using logistic regression analysis. A prediction model was constructed using R software. Model performance was assessed using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves, with internal validation performed via K ‐fold cross‐validation, and external validation carried out in the independent validation set. Results A significant between‐group difference was observed in assisted reproductive technology history between the training and validation sets ( Z = 8.631, P = 0.003). In the training set, pre‐pregnancy body mass index (BMI, calculated as weight in kilograms divided by the square of height in meters), fasting plasma glucose, uric acid, and triglyceride levels differed significantly between the GDM and non‐GDM groups ( P < 0.05 for all). Multivariate logistic regression identified all four parameters as independent risk factors for GDM ( P < 0.05). The ROC curve analysis yielded an area under the curve of 0.773 for the training set and 0.808 for the validation set, indicating good predictive performance. Conclusion We established a GDM prediction model for women of increased maternal age with singleton pregnancies, incorporating four readily available clinical indicators. The model demonstrated satisfactory discrimination and generalizability upon both internal and external validation.

title: Stakeholder Engagement Practices and Performance of Climate-Smart Agriculture Projects in Marsabit County, Kenya.
container-title: International Journal of Social Science and Humanities Research (IJSSHR) ISSN 2959-7056 (o); 2959-7048 (p)
3fda63cfaf738d49c14a5ec9a8998b86e096f3f6.abstract: Stakeholder engagement is the process through which project implementers involve the individuals, groups and institutions that affect or are affected by a project in planning, implementation and evaluation decisions, so that project outcomes reflect their needs and priorities. It is increasingly regarded as a critical determinant of project performance, particularly in development interventions implemented in climate-vulnerable and resource-constrained settings. Empirical evidence suggests that projects with strong stakeholder engagement frameworks achieve up to 30% higher adoption rates and better sustainability outcomes than those with limited participation. However, the performance of climate-smart agriculture (CSA) projects in Marsabit County remains below expectations, with recurrent droughts, food insecurity affecting over 60% of households and uneven uptake of climate-resilient practices. Therefore, the purpose of this study was to establish the influence of stakeholder engagement practices on the performance of climate-smart agriculture projects in Marsabit County, Kenya. It examined four dimensions of stakeholder engagement, namely stakeholder communication, participation in decision making, stakeholder empowerment and stakeholder co-creation practices, and how they influence project performance. The study was anchored on Stakeholder Theory and supported by Participatory Development Theory, Empowerment Theory and Social Exchange Theory. The study adopted a descriptive survey research design and targeted 45 active CSA sub-projects implemented under the FSRP, DRSLP, FLLoCA and NGO-led programmes in Marsabit County, involving 740 stakeholders. The unit of observation comprised project managers, county government officials, NGO representatives, extension officers, community leaders and beneficiary farmer representatives. A sample size of 129 respondents was determined using the Nassiuma (2000) formula and selected through census, purposive and stratified random sampling. Structured questionnaires were used to collect data. Both descriptive and inferential statistical methods were used to analyse the data, which were presented in tables and discussed. The findings revealed that stakeholder communication was the strongest determinant of the performance of CSA projects in Marsabit County. The study also found that participation in decision making significantly enhanced project performance, although stakeholders’ attendance at meetings exceeded their actual influence over decisions. The study further found that stakeholder co-creation practices had a significant positive influence on project performance. Finally, the study established that stakeholder empowerment was a significant but comparatively weaker determinant of performance. Jointly, the four practices explained 53.5% of the variation in project performance. The study, therefore, recommends that project managers establish predictable two-way communication schedules that reach all stakeholder groups, including farmers. Project implementers should move beyond meeting attendance and give stakeholders demonstrable influence over project priorities and resource allocation. Project managers, the county government and partner NGOs should formalize accessible grievance procedures, maintain visible complaint registers and set defined response times. Project managers should pair long-term capacity building with a dependable supply of tools and materials and clearly delegate authority to trained stakeholders.

title: Implementation Challenges of Artificial Intelligence-Empowered Project-Based Learning in Compulsory Education
container-title: Journal of Language, Culture and Education
9528dc8f306ff8c3fc5267c18f89fec4d4a030b8.abstract: With the rapid development of generative artificial intelligence, new possibilities have emerged for addressing problems in project-based learning at the compulsory education stage, such as insufficient teacher guidance resources and inadequate personalized support for students. Based on literature research, this paper analyzes the implementation challenges faced by artificial intelligence-empowered project-based learning from the dual perspectives of teachers and students. The study finds that, at the teacher level, there are three types of problems: superficial AI application, generalized technology embedding, and fragmented instructional design. At the student level, there are difficulties such as the substitution of the inquiry process, interference with learning engagement, and compression of the space for collaborative construction. In response to these problems, this paper proposes optimization strategies, including promoting subject-differentiated technical support, designing structured collaborative learning sheets, improving the formative evaluation system, and enhancing teachers’ AI literacy, with a view to providing references for the deep integration of artificial intelligence and project-based learning in compulsory education.

title:
Pre‐service teachers' descriptions of
                    <scp>UDL</scp>
                    engagement guidelines that supported asynchronous professional experience coursework
container-title: Journal of Research in Special Educational Needs
0db04951badde0d2393a876a044c403b28d60b90.abstract: Abstract The growth of asynchronous delivery in higher education has made it increasingly important to examine the conditions that support meaningful student engagement. This article reports on a qualitative case study of five pre‐service teachers (PSTs) enrolled in fully asynchronous professional experience (PEx) coursework at a large Australian university. PEx is the work‐integrated learning component of initial teacher education (ITE), where university coursework connects with supervised practice in schools and early childhood settings. The study draws on Universal Design for Learning (UDL) to examine which guidelines PSTs identified as supporting engagement. Data were generated through semi‐structured interviews and analysed thematically. The findings show that in asynchronous PEx, engagement was supported by the two UDL engagement guidelines, including welcoming interests and identities and sustaining effort and persistence. The study shows that asynchronous PEx coursework can be a way of modelling differentiated practice for PSTs through multiple means of engagement that respond to learner differences. By experiencing this design as learners, PSTs can see how to enact differentiation in their own future practice.

title: Understanding the Pattern of Cognitive Decline in GBA1 ‐Related Parkinson's Disease: An Exploratory Longitudinal Multi‐Cohort Study
container-title: Annals of Neurology
8f39665691e6b88120e2dafbc26116e179cad79b.abstract: Objective People with Parkinson's disease (PD) who carry a pathogenic GBA1 variant (PD GBA1 ) are at higher risk of cognitive impairment than those without the variant (PD GBA1_wildtype ). To date, little is known about the pattern and evolution of cognitive decline in PD GBA1 . This multicenter study characterized the cognitive profile of PD GBA , focusing on the longitudinal trajectories and the group‐specific onset times among cognitive functions, as well as their clinical relevance. Methods In this exploratory longitudinal multicohort‐study (Parkinson's Precision Medicine Initiative [PPMI], Amyloid‐Beta in cerebrospinal spinal fluid as a risk factor for cognitive dysfunction in Parkinson's Disease [ABC‐PD], and National Centre for Excellence in Research on Parkinson's disease [NCER‐PD]), comprehensive neuropsychological assessments were standardized across 546 healthy controls (follow‐up years = 2.9 ± 4.3), 903 PD GBA1_wildtype (follow‐up years = 4.4 ± 4.2), and 211 PD GBA1 (follow‐up years = 4.8 ± 3.4). We evaluated performance across age and disease duration using generalized linear mixed effects models (GLMMs) within each cognitive domain. An exploratory latent trajectory analysis was computed to identify potential cognitive subgroups. Time‐to‐first‐event models, assessing risks of clinically relevant performance impairment (test score z ≤ −1.5, Montreal Cognitive Assessment [MoCA] < 26), and an expanding time‐window approach identified the course of cognitive impairment. Results PD GBA1 performed worse in executive function, attention, visuocognitive skills, and memory than PD GBA1_wildtype at baseline and exhibited a more rapid and widespread decline across these domains. The risk of developing clinically relevant cognitive impairment during the disease course was increased in PD GBA1 . Processing speed and visuoperceptual showed the earliest performance impairments in PD GBA1 , preceding PD GBA1_wildtype by 1.2 and 2.5 disease years, respectively. Within the PD GBA1 group, we identified a subgroup with rapidly declining cognition, who were more likely to be male patients, report depressive symptoms, and carry a severe GBA1 mutation. Interpretation PD GBA1 exhibits accelerated domain‐generalized and more severe cognitive decline compared to PD GBA1_wildtype . ANN NEUROL 2026

title: A Convergence Result for a Planning Problem for Mean Field Games and Rigorous Proof of a Ventcel–Freidlin-Type Large Deviations Principle for the $$1+1$$ KPZ Equation
container-title: Archive for Rational Mechanics and Analysis
a5ac760a98c8a79aaecfbb0805aa094fd8c13bb3.abstract: Abstract We study an innovative connection between a very singular optimal transport variational problem with a congestion term connecting two Dirac measures, which is related to the planning problem in mean field games or gases with negative pressure, and a large deviation principle for the KPZ equation. The main result proves a limit of a singular approximate problem with vanishing diffusive flux and a relaxed initial condition. The paper also provides a rigorous justification for the informal analysis of the ad hoc large deviation principle for the KPZ equation appearing in the physics literature.

title: Spectral invariants and spectral calibration in the ZEBTS model: zeta-determinant, topological index, and mass gap
bf369bba2d1aa0d45d26eaa8c36fcafcf6f5805d.abstract: This paper presents the ZEBTS (Law of the Unity of the Triune Substance) framework as a unified spectral‑topological approach to fundamental physics, where key invariants are derived from the arithmetic properties of the Riemann xi‑function ξ(s)\xi(s)ξ(s). We establish a direct link between the spectral data of a specially constructed operator HχH_\chiHχ​ and the imaginary parts of the nontrivial zeros of ξ(s)\xi(s)ξ(s) via the Spectral Calibration Postulate (SP‑1). Within this setup, we rigorously demonstrate the equivalence of several conditions (SB ⇔ G4‑QF ⇔ TC‑Gap ⇔ HP‑Amp) that guarantee the existence of a spectral gap. This spectral gap is then identified with the physical Yang–Mills mass gap, yielding a parameter‑free determination of Δ\DeltaΔ. Furthermore, we show that the Atiyah–Patodi–Singer (APS) index becomes a computable arithmetic‑spectral quantity, expressed through a regularized trace tied to the logarithmic derivative of ξ(1/2+it)\xi(1/2+it)ξ(1/2+it). The model’s defining feature is the absence of free parameters: all fundamental quantities are fixed by the spectrum determined through SP‑1 and the known asymptotics of the zeros of ξ(s)\xi(s)ξ(s). The paper outlines numerical verification strategies, generalizations to other gauge groups and dimensions, and the relationship between the consistency of ZEBTS and the Riemann Hypothesis.

title: Love Takes Time: Faster Romantic Onset, Lower Closeness, and Similarity Benefits in Human-AI Relationships
container-title: Journal of Language and Social Psychology
0dfcaccfe33e6f40a134f0287b4cf4245a067bff.abstract: As human–artificial intelligence (AI) romantic relationships become increasingly prevalent, understanding how they develop is important. Such relationships differ from human–human relationships in how AI partners accommodate user needs and preferences, potentially influencing relationship development and closeness. In this survey ( N = 167), individuals who reported falling in love more quickly with human partners also tended to do so with AI partners. However, paired within-subject analyses ( n = 110) revealed that participants perceived a faster overall pace of falling in love with AI than human partners, driven primarily by shorter conversation lengths rather than fewer days or total conversations. Despite this expediency, participants reported greater current relational closeness with human partners than AI partners. Perceived similarity with AI partners was positively associated with relational closeness and relationship quality with AI. These findings suggest that human–AI romantic relationships may develop rapidly through familiar interpersonal processes such as similarity attraction, yet involve lower relational closeness.

title: Former versus current smoking among older adults living with Alzheimer's disease, related dementias, and cognitive impairment
container-title: Journal of Alzheimer’s Disease
d4f5985c1784cabacf8eca2e1d79b729df2bab5e.abstract: Smoking is a major modifiable risk factor for Alzheimer's disease and related dementias (ADRD), yet smoking status among older adults with ADRD or cognitive impairment, not dementia (CIND), remains poorly characterized. Using pooled 2010–2020 Health and Retirement Study data, we examined former versus current smoking among US adults aged ≥55 years with lifetime cigarette smoking. In weighted analyses of 13,595 participants, adults with CIND (AOR = 0.83, 95% CI: 0.74, 0.92) and ADRD (AOR = 0.80, 95% CI: 0.65, 0.99) had lower odds of former smoking than cognitively normal adults. Findings highlight the importance of understanding smoking cessation needs in cognitively impaired populations.

title: Adaptive gain sliding mode observer based on recursive least square for ultra-local model estimation in model-free predictive control of brushless DC motor drives
container-title: Electrical Engineering & Electromechanics
34d886b8de4214b3ae17172968ce60d65f221002.abstract: Introduction. Accurate current estimation is essential for high-performance brushless DC (BLDC) motor drives, especially in finite control set model predictive control (FCSMPC), where prediction accuracy directly affects control quality. Problem. Sliding mode observers (SMOs) are widely adopted for this purpose due to their robustness against modeling uncertainties. However, the performance of conventional SMO strongly depends on proper gain tuning, which is typically fixed and may lead to degraded performance under parameter variations and changing operating conditions. Goal. To develop an adaptive SMO gain strategy that automatically adjusts the observer gain online using recursive least squares (RLS) approach to improve robustness and estimation accuracy of the ultra local model without manual tuning. Methodology. The proposed method proposes the SMO gain adaptation as an online regression problem, where the RLS algorithm is used to recursively update the observer gain at each sampling instant. The adaptive SMO is integrated into an FCSMPC scheme. Its performance is evaluated through simulations under nominal conditions and parameter mismatches and compared with static-gain and PI-based adaptive SMO approaches using dynamic and steady-state performance metrics. Results. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed RLS-based adaptive gain SMO achieves faster convergence, reduced chattering, and improved robustness against parameter variations. Scientific novelty. The main contribution of this work is the use of RLS to adapt the SMO gain rather than directly estimating system parameters, providing a stable and statistically grounded gain adaptation mechanism. Practical value. The method reduces the integral of time-weighted absolute error (ITAE) of the sliding variable by 5.8 % compared to the static-gain approach and provides faster settling time and lower steady-state error in speed response. The settling time is reduced by 33 % and decreasing steady-state error by 58 % compared to the conventional static-gain approach. In addition, the adaptive mechanism enhances robustness under parameter mismatch and load disturbance conditions. References 34, tables 3, figures 6.

title: IntentSpider - The Fluid Language Web for Textual Tension and Prediction
a2503c5b2aa4eaa0a69b1ab38b0febe546345052.abstract: IntentSpider is an on-device, privacy-first predictive text engine built in C++ STL, modeled as a human's intent graph. Prediction and graph updates operate on-device. Each edge carries a coefficient and transmission fidelity value deciding whether it is TF or capture type, sending signal toward the human's next selection. Roles are reversible. IntentSpider uses personalized PageRank through local push, initialized from recent words using fan dispersion rather than equal initialization values. IntentSpider addresses blindness to the valency by Valence Gated Signed Diffusion using typing interval patterns. The Necessity Gating Algorithm controls whether the ranked word is displayed. Hexarousal measures how much typing rate differs from that human's ordinary rate. Others include shared reinforcement, increasing diffusion radius, sudden suppression, settling, typing substate search, and combined behavioral values, motivated by the Orb Spider, Wandering Spider, and struggling isopod prey. A 2D process converts sentence diffusion outputs into paths. Across 500 events, IntentSpider achieved 14.40% first rank and 27.80% Top 3 accuracy. Every shared event set had greater measured first rank and Top 3 accuracy, outperforming Google Gboard, Samsung Keyboard, Microsoft SwiftKey, and OpenBoard. Against Gboard on 187 events, IntentSpider reached 17.65% vs 7.49% first rank and 33.16% vs 14.44% Top 3 accuracy. Prediction produced 2.4 ms median time and 3.66 ms 95th percentile. Largest changes appeared when the recent word seed was reduced to 1 and the Necessity Gating algorithm removed. This depicts uncertainty in text prediction, potentially altering, simplifying, or negatively influencing human communication. IntentSpider Webnet is one approach to this issue.

title: A curing-dependent hybrid Popovics–Thorenfeldt constitutive model for geopolymer-stabilized lateritic soil under uniaxial compression
container-title: Proceedings of the Institution of Mechanical Engineers, Part L: Journal of Materials: Design and Applications
0cdd987de09c953a3966f2f4bd396971db53182c.abstract: Constitutive models are useful for describing the stress–strain response of stabilized soils in geotechnical analysis. However, existing models for geopolymer-stabilized soils often have difficulty reproducing brittle post-peak behavior or require specimen-specific calibration. This study develops a curing-dependent hybrid Popovics–Thorenfeldt model for geopolymer-stabilized lateritic soil under uniaxial compression. The model uses the Popovics equation for the ascending branch and a Thorenfeldt-type function for post-peak softening. Calibration and internal cross-validation were based on 18 stress–strain curves covering three fly ash contents (20%, 30%, and 40%), three curing regimes (open-air, sealed, and saturated), and two curing ages (28 and 91 days). A hierarchical procedure was used to relate the curvature parameter β to compressive strength. Compared with the constant-β Popovics model, the proposed formulation reduced the average Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE) from 0.525 to 0.464 MPa (11.5%) and increased the mean coefficient of determination (R 2 ) from 0.748 to 0.803. The normalized ascending branch followed β(y)=3.42 + 2.20y, with comparable coefficients across curing regimes. Cross-validation indicated that the shared parameters were transferable within the tested experimental domain, although independent validation using other materials and curing histories is still needed. The current formulation addresses only uniaxial compression and does not explicitly account for confinement effects, strain-rate dependence, or cyclic loading behavior. Extension toward triaxial stress states would likely require incorporating pressure-dependent modifications to peak strain and softening parameters.

title: Engagement-Zone-Aware Input-Constrained Guidance for Safe Target Interception
container-title: Journal of Guidance, Control, and Dynamics
71ccc93487d234cb8314ae26222074ae1d9a241e.abstract: This paper addresses target interception in contested, GPS-denied environments with multiple finite-range, moving defenders. Conventional methods impose conservative stand-off constraints based on maximum engagement distance and neglect actuator limitations, while safety-critical designs typically rely on online optimization. Instead, we formulate safety constraints using defender-induced engagement zones (regions of the attacker’s state space from which capture becomes inevitable under the defenders’ current capability). To account for actuator limits, the nonholonomic vehicle model is augmented with input saturation dynamics, and a time-varying safe-set tightening parameter is proposed to handle transient constraint violations by adaptively contracting the admissible safe region. To ensure scalable safety enforcement, a log-sum-exp operator combines individual defender threat measures. The proposed safety framework yields an explicit feedback guidance law that coordinates interception and safety objectives without online optimization. Additionally, the guidance law relies only on relative information and supports distributed implementation without knowledge of the defender’s control inputs. Lyapunov-based analysis provides sufficient conditions guaranteeing target interception, practical safety across all defender engagement zones, and satisfaction of actuator bounds. An input-constrained guidance law based on conservative maximum engagement range is also developed. Simulation studies demonstrate reduced interception time and shorter trajectories compared to conventional methods while maintaining safety.

title: Real-time geometric complexity of language is associated with global functioning across psychosis and major depression
container-title: NPP—Digital Psychiatry and Neuroscience
ee08bfc20a1e8522bf808ddfca0c5483a2a2c406.abstract: Abstract Language disturbances are prominent across psychiatric disorders, yet their underlying organization and relationship to clinical functioning remain poorly understood. We conceptualized spontaneous speech as a temporally evolving sequence of contextual representations through semantic space, in which successive concepts define transitions between large-language-model embeddings. We characterized the local dynamics of these representations using Lyapunov-inspired measures of sensitivity to perturbation and anisotropy—the extent to which nearby neighboring contextual representations diverge differently depending on direction in representational space. We applied this approach to picture descriptions from 129 German-speaking participants with major depressive disorder (n = 43), schizophrenia spectrum disorders (n = 42), or no psychiatric diagnosis (n = 44). Individual differences in local geometric dynamics predicted multiple clinical dimensions, with the strongest association observed for global functioning, for which the geometric measures explained 51% of the variance. Clinically informative geometric structure was already detectable within the first three sentences of speech, where distinct dynamical profiles were associated with differences in negative and positive symptoms, anxiety, depression, and global functioning. These associations suggest that the dynamics of local representational divergence and contraction during speech reflect broad variation in cognitive and social functioning rather than diagnosis alone. Together, these findings suggest that psychiatric variation is reflected not simply in what people say, but in the dynamics by which semantic representations evolve during ongoing language production. A dynamical-geometric analysis of language may provide a compact, transdiagnostic marker of clinically meaningful variation in psychopathology.

title: Redundant attention fails to replicate as sustained engagement: Information quality in early review cohorts and long‐run popularity of books
container-title: Journal of the Association for Information Science and Technology
29df535d6eda70428b375dc2ca2def53f85d92de.abstract: Abstract Early reviews on social reading platforms are an important clue for book buyers. However, research has so far focused on their volume and average rating rather than their informational content. To address this gap, we scraped nearly one million reviews of 25,000 books across five genres from lubimyczytac.pl, Poland's largest social reading platform. We modeled the long‐run accumulation of reviews attracted after a book's 30‐day initial launch window. Conditional on early review volume and book characteristics, reviews with greater semantic similarity and stronger solicitation cues predict less subsequent engagement. In contrast, early reviews with more linguistic perplexity and more diverse reviewer portfolios predict more engagement in the future. Furthermore, a text sentiment classifier we fine‐tuned to this specific domain added predictive signal beyond the raw star ratings, consistent with ratings being a coarsely discretized projection of the evaluative signal carried by review text. We frame these results within information quality theory: the informational profile of an early review cohort contributes to the prediction of sustained platform engagement beyond review volume and rating.

title: Chemical threat detection from open-source intelligence using a large language model: a zero-shot feasibility evaluation, with radiological assessment precluded by data sparsity
container-title: International Journal of Data Science and Analytics
15ecccb8e6b6a354beb90090d3bc437bf7252417.abstract: Abstract Timely detection of chemical and radiological incidents is crucial for public health surveillance; however, no global event-based surveillance system currently exists. Open-source intelligence (OSINT) and large language models (LLMs) present new opportunities for early detection; however, their application in these domains remains largely unexplored. This study evaluated GPT-4o’s performance for named entity recognition (NER) of chemical and radiological incidents from OSINT sources, assessing its potential to support global threat detection and early warning systems. Radiological entities were retained in the extraction schema throughout, but proved too sparse in the retrieved corpus to permit any evaluation of radiological performance; the evaluation reported here is therefore effectively confined to the chemical domain. A lexicon of 45 lay-accessible search terms, derived from 6646 technical chemical and radiological terms, was used to query the Bing News Application Programming Interface (API) from August 2024 to January 2025. Retrieved articles were scraped, translated when necessary, summarised by GPT-4o, and the summaries were and processed by GPT-4o using structured zero-shot prompts to extract entities, including event occurrences, substances, case numbers, fatalities, locations, and temporal features. Two annotators manually labelled a ground-truth dataset of 200 articles to evaluate performance using precision, recall, and F 1 Scores. Performance was compared against four baselines evaluated on the same corpus: a rule-based lexicon extractor, an off-the-shelf pretrained NER pipeline, a domain-pretrained biomedical NER model, and a supervised TF-IDF classifier. Of 37,618 retrieved articles, 8077 were parsed by GPT-4o. Event identification (F 1 = 0.96) and chemical substance recognition (F 1 = 0.94) were highly accurate. Geographic entities performed well at the state (F 1 = 0.98) and city (F 1 = 0.92) levels and remained strong at the country (F 1 = 0.93) and county (F 1 = 0.91) levels. Temporal (Date and Timeframe: F 1 = 0.74; Temporal expressions: F 1 = 0.81) and numerical extraction were moderate-to-strong (case numbers F 1 = 0.83; fatalities F 1 = 0.82). Only four positive radiological entity instances were identified within the annotated dataset, precluding meaningful evaluation of radiological extraction performance. Against a cross-validated supervised classifier, event identification improved from F 1 = 0.87 to F 1 = 0.96, and GPT-4o higher F 1 than the rule-based, pretrained NER, and domain-pretrained comparators across the entity types for which direct comparison was possible.Within the constraints of this limited evaluation, GPT-4o demonstrated feasibility for extracting several core public health entities from OSINT sources; however, while performance exceeded rule-based, pretrained-NER, and supervised classical baselines on a common corpus, comparison against transformer-based and fine-tuned biomedical NER architectures remains outstanding. Performance was weaker for Date and Timeframe precision. Radiological extraction could not be evaluated at all, because the corpus yielded too few positive radiological instances to support any performance estimate. This study, therefore, demonstrates chemical-domain feasibility under the conditions tested and documents radiological sparsity within this retrieval pipeline as a barrier to evaluation, rather than demonstrating radiological detection capability.

title: IMPROVING PANCASILA EDUCATION LEARNING OUTCOMES ON REGIONAL CHARACTERISTICS TOPIC THROUGH CONTEXTUAL TEACHING AND LEARNING MODEL USING VISUAL MEDIA
container-title: JURNAL PENDIDIKAN GLASSER
4d9618e2782b3b7298f6a92f5d348ad5b35623d0.abstract: This study aims to improve learning outcomes in Pancasila Education on the subject of Regional Characteristics through the implementation of the Contextual Teaching and Learning (CTL) model assisted by visual media. This research is a Classroom Action Research (CAR) conducted in two cycles in grade V of SD Islam Sultan Agung 4 Semarang with 20 students as subjects. The data collection instrument used learning achievement tests. The results showed a significant improvement. In the pre-cycle, classical completeness only reached 20% with an average score of 58.2. After implementing the CTL model with visual media (pictures) in Cycle I, classical completeness increased to 62.5% with an average of 69.45. In Cycle II, researchers optimized visual media using contextual videos, which resulted in an increase in classical completeness to 87.5% with an average of 82.05. In the final post-test evaluation, completeness reached 85% with an average of 85.5, meeting the established success indicator of 85%. In conclusion, the collaboration between a meaningful CTL approach and the use of environment-based video media successfully resolves the abstract nature of spatial geography material and significantly stimulates elementary student learning outcomes.

title: Data‐driven or structure‐driven: Toward a process model of data behavior in humanities research
container-title: Journal of the Association for Information Science and Technology
428513158771482ab6391ba9470ea02df9b0b900.abstract: Abstract The emergence of digital humanities has transformed how scholars engage with research materials, yet data behaviors of humanities scholars remain underexplored compared to those in science and social science fields. This study develops a comprehensive process model of data behavior in humanities research and examines contextual factors shaping these behaviors. Through in‐depth interviews with 27 humanities scholars across multiple disciplines, we identified two distinct research approaches—data‐driven and structure‐driven—that fundamentally shape how scholars interact with data throughout their research processes. Data‐driven scholars aim to discover patterns from comprehensive data collection, while structure‐driven scholars engage in iterative interpretation and re‐structuring informed by selective data. Our findings reveal diverse data behaviors including processing, analysis, and sharing practices that vary significantly between these approaches. We identified three categories of contextual factors influencing these behaviors, including internal factors, social and organizational factors, and infrastructural factors. The study contributes a comprehensive model and reveals that humanities scholars' data behaviors are embedded in their ways of sensemaking. The study offers implications for research infrastructure development, tool design, and academic reward systems that can better support evolving scholarly practices in the age of AI.

title: Hierarchical Cloud-Edge Cooperative Control Framework for Multi-Vehicle Autonomous Driving Using Reinforcement Learning and Model Predictive Control
container-title: Transportation Research Record: Journal of the Transportation Research Board
3106e008d3d07fe231d2b6af0a474cf8d70d7f72.abstract: This study presents a hierarchical cooperative control framework for hybrid electric vehicles in intelligent transportation systems, termed “cloud-coordinated cooperative driving with deep reinforcement learning.” The framework integrates reinforcement learning with model predictive control (MPC) to balance adaptability and stability. A cloud-level coordinator utilizes the multi-agent deep deterministic policy gradient (MADDPG) algorithm for global policy optimization, while each vehicle executes a local Soft Actor–Critic (SAC) controller for real-time adaptive control. A predecessor–leader–follower-based cooperative economic MPC module is incorporated to ensure stable spacing and energy-efficient trajectory tracking. Furthermore, a hybrid offline–online learning mechanism with state synchronization and experience replay enhances convergence speed and generalization capability. Under three representative driving cycles: highway fuel economy test, US06 (a high-speed, high-acceleration cycle), and China light-duty vehicle test cycle with an initial state-of-charge (SOC) of 0.60, the proposed MADDPG-SAC algorithm consistently outperforms deep deterministic policy gradient (DDPG) and MADDPG. This method attains lower fuel consumption (17.93–20.62 L/100 km), higher minimum SOC (0.33–0.35), reduced speed tracking error (0.22–0.26 m/s) and spacing error (0.29–0.35 m), smoother control (mean jerk of 0.041–0.049 m/s 3 ), and faster convergence (11–13 episodes compared with 12–29 episodes for DDPG and MADDPG). Overall, the framework exhibits strong cooperative capability, energy efficiency, and driving stability, demonstrating its potential for large-scale energy-aware autonomous driving applications.

title: Pengaruh Model Kooperatif Tipe <i>Numbered Heads Together</i> (NHT) Terhadap Kemampuan Berpikir Kritis Siswa Pada Materi Rantai Makanan
container-title: Punggawa Global Research: Jurnal Multidisiplin
440cc7f544d7e398fa976d5112b6589ad825d109.abstract: Kemampuan berpikir kritis merupakan keterampilan penting dalam pembelajaran Ilmu Pengetahuan Alam (IPA), khususnya pada materi rantai makanan yang menuntut siswa menganalisis hubungan antar makhluk hidup dalam suatu ekosistem. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mengetahui pengaruh model pembelajaran kooperatif tipe Numbered Heads Together (NHT) terhadap kemampuan berpikir kritis siswa pada materi rantai makanan. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif dengan metode pre-eksperimental dan desain One-Group Pretest–Posttest. Subjek penelitian berjumlah 35 siswa dalam satu kelas. Data dikumpulkan melalui tes yang diberikan sebelum dan sesudah penerapan model pembelajaran NHT, kemudian dianalisis menggunakan uji normalitas, paired-samples t-test, dan N-gain. Hasil uji paired-samples t-test menunjukkan adanya perbedaan yang signifikan antara skor pretest dan posttest, dengan nilai t = −11,466, df = 34, dan p < 0,001. Rata-rata N-gain sebesar 0,3745 atau 37,45%, yang termasuk dalam kategori sedang. Temuan ini menunjukkan bahwa kemampuan berpikir kritis siswa meningkat setelah mengikuti pembelajaran dengan model NHT, karena siswa terlibat aktif dalam berdiskusi, bertukar pendapat, dan bertanggung jawab atas jawaban kelompok. Meskipun demikian, penelitian ini hanya melibatkan satu kelompok tanpa kelas kontrol, sehingga hasilnya perlu ditafsirkan dengan mempertimbangkan keterbatasan desain penelitian.

763b3ba0d6d5f87fb9fdbf31e8526c16767dec3b.abstract: This article provides a comprehensive analysis of the international legal foundations of the right to return, its doctrinal evolution, and the mechanisms for its implementation in post-conflict contexts. It argues that the right to return should not be understood merely as a classical individual human right, but rather as a complex, multi-level, and functional legal institution shaped by the interaction of normative frameworks, institutional mechanisms, and practical enforcement processes. Using a comparative legal approach, the study systematically examines post-conflict models of return in Bosnia and Herzegovina, Kosovo, and Cyprus. Their normative, institutional, and procedural characteristics are analyzed, highlighting both similarities and differences in the implementation of the right to return. Particular emphasis is placed on the role of property rights as a central element of this right, as well as on the primacy of restitution as the principal mechanism for restoring violated rights. The article also addresses the limitations of compensation as a subsidiary mechanism, applicable only when restitution is not feasible. Drawing on the case-law of the European Court of Human Rights, the study explores the doctrine of “continuing violation” and its implications for the temporal and legal scope of the right to return.
