title: Large language model–based simplification of breast imaging reports: a prospective multicentre study with 2965 patient-based evaluations
container-title: Insights into Imaging
fd4f6c6ee7d37482dc068258b9156701527de9c1.abstract: Abstract Objective To compare patient perceptions of radiologist-written and artificial intelligence (AI)-generated simplifications of breast imaging reports in terms of simplicity, comprehensibility, empathy, and overall preference. Materials and methods In this prospective multicentre survey-based study, 10 anonymized breast imaging reports (5 ultrasound, 5 mammography; one BI-RADS category 1–5 per modality) were simplified by ChatGPT-4 within a 50-word limit. After assessment by a panel of 20 physicians, paired radiologist-written and AI-generated reports were evaluated by 314 patients (2965 evaluations) who rated simplicity, comprehensibility, and empathy on a 5-point Likert scale and indicated their preferred report. The origin of each report was concealed, and each pair was presented in randomized order. Univariable and multivariable mixed-effects logistic regression analyses were performed to identify factors associated with preferring AI-generated reports. Results AI-generated reports were preferred in 63.3% (1876/2965) of evaluations. High simplicity and comprehensibility scores (4–5) were more frequently assigned to AI reports than to radiologist-written reports (70.0% vs 43.4% and 68.1% vs 40.4%, respectively). In multivariable analysis, higher comprehensibility was the strongest predictor in both directions: higher comprehensibility of AI-generated reports increased the odds of preferring AI (score 4: adjusted OR 1.87, 95% CI 1.08–3.23, p = 0.025), while higher comprehensibility of radiologist-written reports reduced them (score 4: adjusted OR 0.45, 95% CI 0.29–0.69, p < 0.001). Preference for AI-generated reports showed a non-significant trend toward increase with educational level. Conclusion AI-generated breast imaging reports were preferred by most patients and perceived as clearer, supporting a complementary and supervised use of AI-generated summaries. Key Points Question Patients increasingly access their own radiology reports, yet standard radiologist-written reports are often difficult to understand, highlighting the need for patient-friendly alternatives. Findings In this study, AI-generated breast imaging reports were preferred by patients in 63.3% of evaluations, with comprehensibility emerging as the strongest predictor of preference. Critical relevance statement AI-generated breast imaging reports were preferred by most patients and received higher ratings for simplicity and comprehensibility than radiologist-written reports, supporting a supervised and complementary use of AI-generated summaries in clinical breast imaging.

title: Differences in Translators' Cognitive Load under Generative-AI Post-Editing: An Eye-Tracking Study of English-Chinese Scientific Texts
container-title: Future of Social Sciences
7c7fe2b629e6642e4941218c5d737a4c99000526.abstract: {'en': 'Generative artificial intelligence has entered the translation workflow faster than evidence about its effect on the translator has accumulated. This study asks whether working from a large language model draft lowers cognitive load or merely redistributes it. Thirty-six translators, twenty translation trainees and sixteen practising professionals, rendered nine English popular-science and technical passages into Chinese under three within-subject conditions. These were unaided human translation (HT), post-editing of a static neural machine translation draft (NMT-PE), and post-editing of a GPT-4o draft with an interactive prompt pane (GAI-PE). Pupil diameter change, fixation duration, gaze distribution, keystroke logs, NASA-TLX ratings and MQM scores were recorded. GAI-PE cut task time by 44.2 per cent against HT and by 17.1 per cent against NMT-PE. Its MQM scores were higher than those of NMT-PE, while the difference from HT did not reach significance. Pupil diameter change was nevertheless largest in GAI-PE at 0.095 mm, against 0.083 mm in HT and 0.064 mm in NMT-PE, while gaze on the source text fell to 38.3 per cent, the lowest of the three. Subjective ratings moved the other way and ranked HT as the most demanding condition. In an exploratory analysis, self-reported AI-use frequency was associated with a smaller pupil response in GAI-PE, whereas English proficiency showed no such association. These observations are consistent with an increased demand for verification, though the generative condition also gave access to an interactive prompt pane, so the differences cannot be attributed to the model alone.'}

title: Illumination and the Emergence of Creative Ideas: A Dual-Route Model
2d2afc81fdfe1a0910e62a76233375ba3eed386e.abstract: Illumination has occupied a central position in theories of creativity since Wallas identified itas one of the four phases of the creative process. Although subsequent models have continuedto recognize illumination as the moment at which new ideas emerge into awareness, relativelylittle attention has been devoted to the cognitive processes underlying this transition. At thesame time, a parallel literature on insight problem solving has generated extensive evidencedescribing the processes that precede and accompany the sudden emergence of new ideas, yetthese findings have rarely been integrated into broader theories of creativity. This chapter bringstogether these traditions to reconsider illumination within the broader process of creative ideageneration. Building on classical and contemporary theories of creativity, a Dual-Route Modelof Creative Idea Generation is proposed. In the continuous route, intermediate states remainaccessible to conscious awareness as an idea develops. By contrast, in the discontinuous route,an idea becomes abruptly available to conscious awareness, following processing that is not fullyaccessible to introspection. Behavioral, metacognitive, and neurocognitive evidence relevant tothese different modes of idea emergence is reviewed, alongside their potential relationships withthe quality and subsequent memory of the ideas generated. Finally, the broader implicationsof the framework are considered by examining insight as a possible form of model updating,outlining the main empirical predictions of the Dual-Route Model, and discussing its relevanceto creative problem solving in engineering and design.

title: Can solutions journalism counter news avoidance? A choice experiment examining effects on emotions, self-efficacy, and news engagement
container-title: Journalism
4f70377531fe078f2458ffe8cfc712ab3cdd641c.abstract: Solutions journalism has been proposed as a potential remedy to the negativity bias in news coverage, which is often blamed for emotional exhaustion and disengagement among audiences, eventually leading to news avoidance. However, it remains unclear who is drawn to such content and what effects it produces. This study presents a large-scale choice experiment ( N = 4622) examining preferences for solution-focused versus problem-focused journalism on antibiotic resistance, and the effects on emotions, self-efficacy, and news engagement. Participants were presented with one of four news stories focused on either problems or solutions at either an individual level or societal level. Some participants were assigned to watch a specific news story, and others were free to choose themselves. The results show a clear preference for solutions journalism, particularly when stories are framed at the individual level, though not more strongly among news avoiders. Exposure to solutions journalism increases positive emotions, reduces negative ones, and enhances self-efficacy, but does not boost news engagement (e.g., sharing, searching, or discussion). Together, the findings suggest that solutions journalism can to some extent counter news avoidance, yet it is not a definitive remedy.

title: THE LANGUAGE OF FEAR: ANALYSIS OF SUSPENSE IN THOMAS HARRIS’S FICTION
container-title: Litterae Novae: Journal of Contemporary Literary Research
caeaed71906a582c078fe5a960cdcaf45b5baf82.abstract: This article examines how Thomas Harris creates suspense through language and the way information is presented. It focuses mainly on Red Dragon and The Silence of the Lambs. The analysis looks at changes in narrative viewpoint, descriptions of characters’ thoughts, word choice, sentence structure, and dialogue. Particular attention is paid to scenes in which readers know that danger is near, but do not know exactly what will happen. The article also considers how ordinary conversations can become tense when one speaker has more knowledge or control than the other. Using close textual analysis and ideas from cognitive stylistics, the study argues that suspense develops through the relationship between language, narrative information, and readers’ interpretation.

title: From automation to authorship: Computational reasoning and design agency in architectural AI tools
container-title: Journal of Information Technology in Construction
f459ddbe10d9229aeff00984e777729be2bb0281.abstract: The increasing presence of AI in architectural practice is renegotiating who, or what, holds creative authority over a project. This paper introduces a novel two-construct framework, AI Logic (AL) and Architectural Value (AV), to operationalise this shift. AL captures a tool's computational reasoning across automation, optimisation, and predictive capability, while AV captures design agency support, contextual sensitivity, and exploratory capacity. Positioning fifty AI-driven tools within this AL-AV construct via tension map analysis identifies stage-specific patterns within the selected dataset. It shows that design agency is redistributed unevenly across the project lifecycle, expanding in early design stages where tools act as creative collaborators, and contracting under efficiency-driven logics in later stages where automation prioritises monitoring and compliance over qualitative judgement. Cross-referencing against secondary parameters such as building typology, user group, tool maturity, and regulatory context surfaces fundamental gaps in current AI provision. The selected tools predominantly support residential and commercial applications. Documented regional orientations include North American and European standards, while coverage of other regions and typologies is less evident within the sample. To assess scoring consistency, ten AEC professionals and the author independently evaluated a subset of five tools, with one tool representing each of RIBA Stages 1–5. Intraclass correlation analysis demonstrated strong panel-level inter-rater reliability for both constructs, while comparison of the author's scores with the expert consensus indicated close alignment. Following this calibration, the author independently applied the same evaluation framework to the remaining forty-five tools. Beyond its analytical application, the framework offers a practical means of informing future AI development and adoption. It gives toolmakers a vocabulary for embedding stakeholder values in development decisions, and architects a means of recognising embedded biases before adoption, so that increasing automation extends rather than erodes the disciplinary and cultural values of architecture as a whole.

title: ‘It doesn’t bother me anymore’: The Becoming Model of narrative victimology and (non-)narrative making
container-title: The British Journal of Criminology
de85ae8a0c838e83dd8f1710112f4e22b9bb7dcd.abstract: Abstract This paper contributes to narrative victimology by theorizing how victims/survivors may create a narrative that is not centred on victimization. As proposed by Kelly and her colleagues, the paper aims to debunk the victim/survivor dichotomy to appreciate the wholeness of victims’/survivors’ lives, which constantly evolve beyond the victimization or survival. To this end, the paper presents the ‘Becoming Model’ of narrative generation, drawing on Deleuze and Guattari’s notion of the rhizome, and uses a romance fraud victim’s/survivor’s case to illustrate the Model’s applicability. The current study contributes to narrative victimology by criticizing the idealization of active and decisive agency as a desirable feature for victims/survivors and the negative connotation attached to passivity.

title: PERSONALITY AND PROBLEM-SOLVING NEXUS: EXAMINING THE RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN FIVE FACTOR MODEL OF PERSONALITY TRAITS AND PROBLEM-SOLVING ABILITY AMONG SECONDARY STAGE STUDENTS
container-title: Interdisciplinary Perspectives of Education
c14956d46986ff00e44d3237bbe7e7644b414eea.abstract: Background: Personality traits are the significant factors influencing the problem-solving ability among the students. The Five-factor model (FFM) of personality includes Openness, conscientiousness, extroversion, agreeableness and the last neuroticism acronymed as OCEAN, also known as Personality’s big five factors. Objectives: The objectives were to find the relationship among the big five factors of personality and problem-solving ability among secondary stage students. Methodology: The study adopted a descriptive survey method with a quantitative approach. The study consists of 200 students of 9th class of secondary stage school of Agra, U.P. Data were collected using two standardised two tools of Five Personality Traits Inventory (FPTI-MKS) and Problem-Solving Ability Test (PSAT-D). The data were analysed by calculating mean, standard deviation (SD) and Pearson correlation coefficient. Result: The study found that the big five factors of personality as openness, conscientiousness, extroversion, agreeableness were positively correlated with problem solving ability and neuroticism is negatively correlated with the problem-solving ability of secondary stage students.

title: AVATARS AS EXTENSIONS OF THE SELF: A SELF-CONGRUITY PERSPECTIVE ON BRAND ENGAGEMENT IN METAVERSE ENVIRONMENTS
container-title: Interdisciplinary Perspectives of Education
98bb790b518db5cd118eb3e9f67fe05e916c6fe7.abstract: The fast development of avatar-mediated interaction has shifted the consumer-brand interaction process from traditional screen-based and physical environment to immersive metaverse environment. In this regard, the current paper aims to provide an overview of the theory and empirics on the topic of self-congruity in avatar-mediated consumer-brand interaction in metaverse environment. The Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) framework was used to select peer-reviewed literature on this topic from Scopus, Web of Science, and the Korean Citation Index. Of 347 papers screened, 28 papers met inclusion and exclusion criteria. This paper reviews four dominant theories that guide consumer behavior in the context of avatars: the digital doppelgänger theory, embodied self-extension theory, dual congruity integration theory, and cross-reality transference theory. As per the findings, it is found that the configurational features of avatars, such as similarity in appearance, anthropomorphism, customization, and avatar intimacy, have an impact on avatar-self congruence, which in turn affects flow and affective responses, which are psychological mechanisms connected with virtual purchase intention, real purchase intention, and brand loyalty. Avatar-self congruence is also different from the conventional brand-self congruence on account of digital embodiment, mutual identity influence, cross-reality spill-over, and ambiguity contingent process. In light of the synthesis, the proposed study develops a structural model comprising of eight latent variables and ten hypotheses using structural equation modeling. This study provides the research gaps both in methodology and theories along with a research agenda comprising longitudinal designs, experimental designs, cross-culture studies, multidimensional measures, social coexperience, and behavioral measures.

title: EFFECTIVENESS OF MULTIMEDIA BASED TEACHING IN IMPROVING STUDENTS’ ENGAGEMENT, PARTICIPATION AND ACADEMIC PERFORMANCE
container-title: Interdisciplinary Perspectives of Education
0216c955deb73b5f67ac586757ec5f407d98c44b.abstract: Introduction: Today is an era of technology, and the field of education is no exception. From primary to higher education, from arts to science, from engineering to medicine, every field is covered in technology. Objectives: To analyse the impact of multimedia and AV aids on students’ retention power, motivation level, and academic achievement across different subjects and educational levels. To compare the effectiveness of multimedia-based teaching (Online teaching) with traditional method. Hypotheses: There is no significant effect of multimedia in classroom teaching. There is no significant difference between in academic achievement of student in both online and traditional classroom teaching.

title: SOCRATIVE-BASED DIGITAL FORMATIVE ASSESSMENT WITH IMMEDIATE FEEDBACK AND LEARNING ENGAGEMENT AMONG B.ED. STUDENTS: A MIXED-METHOD STUDY
container-title: Interdisciplinary Perspectives of Education
df42f8954c29f112df7e7a3a03dc036cfc2bbb32.abstract: Digital formative assessment provides opportunities for teachers to obtain information about students' learning during instruction and to respond with timely feedback. This mixed-method classroom study examined changes in learning-engagement and feedback-related perceptions and formative-assessment knowledge among B.Ed. students following the use of Socrative-based digital formative assessment with immediate feedback. The study employed a one-group pretest-posttest design involving 46 B.Ed. students enrolled in an Assessment for Learning course. Two Socrative-based assessment sessions were conducted during the intervention period. Each session contained 10 questions, and approximately 15 minutes were provided for completion. Students accessed the activities using mobile phones. Socrative supplied immediate information about correct and incorrect responses, after which the teacher provided explanations and clarification of misconceptions. Quantitative data were collected through pretest and posttest responses while Qualitative data was obtained from open-ended responses and classroom observations. The Likert scale consists of eight items showed high internal consistency at both administrations (pretest α = .924; posttest α = .933). Among the 45 students who completed both test. Learning-engagement and feedback-related scores increased from M = 32.73 (SD = 6.36) at pretest to M = 33.54 (SD = 5.90) at posttest. However, this difference was not statistically significant, t (44) = 0.91, p = .367, d = .14. Formative-assessment knowledge scores also showed a small increase, from M = 2.30 (SD = 0.96) to M = 2.46 (SD = 0.98), with no statistically significant difference, t (45) = −0.87, p = .391, d = .13. Qualitative findings shows that students were perceived feedback was very useful for identifying their strengths and weaknesses, understanding mistakes and planning for further steps and strategies to improve their learning. Classroom observations further indicated that the learner has interest in the digital formative assessment format and appreciated the information about whether their response is correct or incorrect. The results reveal that Socrative was feasible for conducting formative assessment in the classroom. The short period of intervention, absence of a comparison group, one-institution sample, and limited platform data makes it difficult to interpret data normally.

title: DISCOURSE MARKERS IN HAUSA WRITING: RULES OF WORD COMBINATION AND SEPARATION IN MODERN HAUSA LANGUAGE
container-title: International Journal of Humanities, Literature and Art Research
ada34512a2f1305fc6dd21d4ac2877e2739f20db.abstract: This study examines discourse markers in contemporary Hausa writing, focusing on the orthographic rules governing their combination (hadewa) and separation (rabewa). It aims to document the structural types of markers in use, quantify combined and separated forms, compare usage with codified conventions, and derive evidence-based standardization guidelines. The study is descriptive and qualitative, supported by quantitative frequency analysis, and draws on Schiffrin’s (1987) and Fraser’s (1999) frameworks for identifying discourse markers and Haugen’s (1966) model of language standardization. It plans a purposive sample of twenty to thirty texts across educational, print/broadcast media, literary, and digital domains. This article reports a preliminary corpus of nine texts (two novels, six newspaper articles, and one linguistics textbook) containing 33 coded occurrences. Of 24 occurrences with a determinate orthographic status, 19 (79.2%) are written separated and five (20.8%) combined. Only five occurrences could be checked against a directly verified rule (Sa’id, 2019): three conform and two deviate (both ko da yaushe written fused, in one novel). The remainder await page-level checks against other authorities. The four Educational occurrences are author-constructed examples from a single textbook. The findings are preliminary and do not characterize Hausa writing generally. Separated forms predominate in this small, unbalanced sample. Completing the corpus, especially digital material and educational texts with running prose, and checking the remaining authorities are necessary before standardization guidelines can be proposed.

title: The Development and Initial Validation of the Mentoring Engagement Scale
container-title: Journal of Counseling & Development
e0f940ea4cb741d9c2e23c38b8389da9293c63c0.abstract: ABSTRACT Professional mentoring is a potential protective factor against burnout and stress in school counselors. However, existing mentoring measures are limited by weak development procedures, inconsistent psychometric support, and limited practical use. We sought to develop and evaluate the Mentoring Engagement Scale (MES), a self‐report instrument designed to measure a person's level of engagement in receiving professional mentoring, among a sample of US school counselors. The research was conducted in two studies. In the first study, content validity was assessed using Lawshe's quantitative approach to capture expert evaluation of item essentialness. The refined scale was then administered to a sample of 324 practicing US school counselors. Exploratory factor analyses revealed a two‐factor structure— Investment and Impact —accounting for 64.2% of variance. MES scores demonstrated strong internal consistency and evidence of response validity. These findings provide initial support for the MES as a measure of school counselors’ mentoring engagement.

title: Student-Rated Teacher TPACK and Perceptions of Technology-Enhanced English Language Learning as Predictors of Perceived Learning Outcomes: Evidence from the University of Sargodha, Pakistan
container-title: Journal of Language, Literature & Social Affairs
c06413c305db6faf663546512b4047c7ee14dc9c.abstract: Technology-enhanced English language learning (TEELL) is spreading across university classrooms, yet its benefits depend on how teachers combine technology with pedagogy and content. This cross-sectional survey examined how students’ ratings of their teachers’ Technological Pedagogical Content Knowledge (TPACK) and students’ perceptions of TEELL relate to perceived English language learning outcomes. Data came from 303 undergraduates at the University of Sargodha, who completed a questionnaire built on a five-point Likert scale. The TPACK (24 items, α = .937), TEELL (13 items, α = .912) and learning-outcome (10 items, α = .881) scales showed good internal consistency. Pearson correlation and multiple linear regression were used for analysis. All three variables correlated positively and significantly (r = .536 to .774, p < .001). In the final model, TEELL perceptions (β = .642, p < .001) and TPACK (β = .246, p < .001) both predicted perceived outcomes and together explained 64.2% of the variance (R² = .642, F(2, 300) = 268.899, p < .001). TEELL perceptions alone explained 59.9%, and adding TPACK raised this by 4.3% (ΔR² = .043). Teachers’ knowledge matters, but students’ perceived outcomes track their own experience of technology in class more closely. Because every measure was self-reported by the same students at one time point, the findings describe associations and not effects. The results bear on teacher education and institutional support in resource-limited universities.

title: Thermomechanical Phase-Field Model for Electrothermal Wing Deicing Systems
container-title: AIAA Journal
474926a5dbdae9e54133e2185043fb2df7a2ade7.abstract: This paper addresses the challenge of ice accumulation on aircraft wings and focuses on the modeling of electrothermal deicing. Ice buildup on aircraft not only adds weight but also hampers aerodynamic performance, posing a threat to flight safety. Thus, understanding ice shedding under the effect of an electrothermal deicer is necessary. However, its modeling remains particularly challenging. This study introduces a novel model employing phase-field methods. This model incorporates phase change, liquid–solid interaction, and fracture initiation and propagation, allowing for an enriched multiphysical simulation of the complex electrothermal ice-shedding process. The paper provides an overview of existing models, details the chosen modeling of individual phenomena, discusses their coupling, outlines numerical techniques, presents benchmark tests, and concludes with a discussion of results and future prospects.

title: Cultural buffering in entrepreneurial city diplomacy: Wuxi’s economic engagement abroad
container-title: Urban Studies
4d844cb84d50f3c6c58e0248fb32357255cac40d.abstract: Why do investment-oriented municipal delegations begin with culture? This article develops cultural buffering to explain how municipal actors use cultural forms and assets when development-oriented diplomacy brings together organisations with different authority, timetables and commitments. The analysis draws on multi-sited ethnography of 5 Wuxi delegation circuits across Japan, the United Kingdom and continental Europe, followed by tracing of 21 initiatives to July 2026. It identifies two recurrent problems: municipal schedules can outrun partner learning and due diligence, while demands for visible outputs can exceed commitment and post-event ownership. Municipal actors respond to these temporal and accountability mismatches through naming, sequencing, coalition broadening and managed ambiguity. These moves can change who participates, what becomes discussable, which organisations enter the relationship and how provisional alignment is recorded. Subsequent project implementation depends on authority, resources, delivery capacity and an organisation willing to own the next step. Cultural buffering therefore identifies the encounter-level work through which an unsettled proposal becomes discussable and revisitable before its implementation is determined.

title: Two-state resonance narrowing model and verification of organic molecule emission spectra
container-title: The Journal of Chemical Physics
2790b64ac52eb47d970964be40ba7e7255bba703.abstract: Electron–vibrational coupling theory quantitatively describes organic molecular spectra and is key to understanding spectral broadening. However, organic molecular vibrational modes are discrete, high-frequency, and multimode-coupled; a unified framework that condenses mode-resolved information into a single, physically meaningful descriptor remains lacking. To this end, we employ the two-state resonance (TSR) model to construct a unified framework in which the resonance coefficient c2 is a core descriptor for the charge-reorganization response of a molecule along the neutral–zwitterionic coordinate; in the presence of an external polarizing field such as a solvent field, it also reflects sensitivity to solvation perturbations. For typical heteroatom narrowband emitters, fitting FWHM against TSR parameters enables estimation of the limit and guides the design of high-color-purity emitters.

title: The contribution of population genetics to the epidemiological tracing of pathogenic bacteria: the predominant clonal evolution model
container-title: Frontiers in Bacteriology
0c7d42aa743ed8b1c64f5a635e72d1e091c42436.abstract: This article aims to present the specific contribution of population genetics and evolutionary genetics to the molecular tracing of epidemiological routes in bacteria pathogenic to humans and animals. More specifically, the “predominant clonal evolution” (PCE) model is exposed in details. It suggests that bacterial lineages are stable in space and time, from the macroevolutionary scale down to the level of microevolution (a time and space scale of a few years and kilometers, i. e., “measurably evolving pathogens”). This stability is a “si ne qua non” to make epidemiological tracing reliable. The PCE model does not state that genetic recombination is absent in bacteria, but merely that its impact is insufficient to break the pattern of predominant clonal evolution (clonal frame, multilocus bifurcating trees, linkage disequilibrium, stable multilocus genotypes). A few illustrative examples are drawn from major species: Escherichia coli , Mycobacterium tuberculosis , Neisseria meningitidis and Staphylococcus aureus .

title: Cognitive and Computational Mechanisms of Multi-Agent Task Allocation in Digital Environments
container-title: Zamonaviy dunyoda ilm-fan va texnologiya, Vol. 5, No. 32 (2026)
88311ab5879695c66cef064bee8f1ffe9c71873e.abstract: Digital environments transform multi-agent task allocation in terms of computational load, utility optimization, and allocation of attention. Based on distributed systems theory and reinforcement learning, this study will combine empirical evidence in artificial intelligence, software engineering, and information systems studies to determine the impact of digital stimuli (prompt complexity, resource constraints, and algorithmic task routing) on agent cognition and neural-inspired valuation processes. The paper constructs a conceptual Multi-Agent Task Allocation Model (MATAM) based on bounded rationality and multi-agent reinforcement learning theories using secondary data synthesis. The effects of computational overload, the activation of reward circuitry, and dynamic personalization in multi-agent environments are summarized in three integrative tables of documented empirical evidence. The results indicate that online agent frameworks reinforce decentralized processing, reward optimization, and dynamically restructure preference formation. The paper enriches software engineering theory because it incorporates computational and cognitive-inspired processes in adaptive multi-agent systems.

title: A moderated mediation model: depressive symptom, loneliness and social support among immigrant and Portuguese population
container-title: Journal of Public Mental Health
6629bed429a1462e515338c4901f1e2aefe2dbd8.abstract: Purpose The purpose of this study is to analyse the mediating effect of loneliness in the relationship between social support and depressive symptoms among Portuguese and immigrants residing in Portugal. Moreover, the study aims to explore the moderating effect of population group, Portuguese sample and immigrant sample, in this mediation model. Design/methodology/approach Survey data were collected from a diverse sample of employed Portuguese and immigrant from May 2023 to January 2024. Participants completed the UCLA loneliness scales, Multidimensional Scale of Perceived Social Support and Depression, Anxiety and Stress Scale (DASS-21). The SPSS programme with PROCESS macro (Models 4 and 15) was used to test the hypothesis regarding the mediation and moderation effect. Findings The bootstrap analysis found that loneliness played a significant mediation role in the relationship between social support and depressive symptoms among Portuguese and immigrant populations. Moreover, the study found that the population groups played a significant moderating effect on the negative indirect effect of social support on depressive symptoms through loneliness. This effect was significantly higher in magnitude among the Portuguese sample. Originality/value This research advances the authors’ understanding of social support among Portuguese and immigrant populations while providing suggestions for interventions tackling loneliness and depressive symptoms.

title: Performance Architecture and Competitive Phenotypes in HYROX: A Large-Scale Analysis of Official Race Performances
container-title: Applied Sciences
e24f33db150ddd18376021d85270907d156ca2fa.abstract: Previous studies of HYROX have described its physiological demands and pacing, but the organization of race-segment performance and the existence of distinct performance profiles among high-performing athletes remain unclear. This retrospective observational study analyzed official results of 11,592 male HYROX Pro athletes (one performance per athlete; 143 events; 2018–2025). Event-related differences were accounted for by centering race-segment times within each event (venue × year). Segment contributions were quantified using partial correlations controlling for event, part–rest correlations, and an additive decomposition of between-athlete variance. In the fastest within-event quartile (n = 2847), K-means clustering was applied to level-independent residual segment profiles, and exploratory classification trees examined whether these profiles discriminated faster from slower athletes. All segments correlated with total race time (partial r = 0.55–0.78). Running plus Roxzone time and workout-station time each accounted for about half of the between-athlete variance; Wallballs, Sled Pull, and Roxzone were the largest single components, whereas mid-race running segments were most strongly associated with the rest of the race. Two reproducible profiles emerged, characterized by relatively faster workout stations or relatively faster running, with equivalent total times in the primary residual-profile analysis; given their low separation (silhouette = 0.18), they represent positions along a continuum rather than distinct athlete types. In exploratory analyses with training and test data fully separated, profiles discriminated poorly between faster and slower high performers (AUC ≈ 0.54). These findings provide a descriptive basis for Performance Architecture and Competitive Phenotypes in HYROX.

title: Mitigating Data Imbalance in Head Pose Estimation Through Diffusion Model Generated Synthetic Data with Pose Reference
container-title: Applied Sciences
81ef666901d829b82d6d6243c3910800e5127155.abstract: Many head pose estimation approaches are limited by the scarcity of diverse, accurately annotated datasets, especially for skewed facial orientations. Such extreme angles occur far less frequently in real-world data collection, leaving them severely underrepresented. This weakens trained models exactly at the extreme angles they had few chances to learn. Rather than perturbing existing samples, we generate genuinely new ones where data is sparse: a synthetic data framework using the SDXL diffusion model conditioned on OpenPose-derived keypoint maps, with InstantID for identity preservation. Because the produced pose can differ from the request, every image is reannotated by an independent 3D estimator (DAD-3DNet) rather than labeled by its target angle, yielding a more balanced pose distribution. We evaluate cross-dataset generalization using the Geodesic Error across two backbones, 6DRepNet and Hopenet. Adding the synthetic data to real training lowers cross-dataset error for both backbones, most clearly on unseen subjects, showing it is an effective complement to real data at rare orientations.

title: Effects of Cognitive Behavioral Interventions on Core Symptom Dimensions of Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder in Children and Adolescents: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
container-title: Brain Sciences
6a8f61df667a2aec7602c5e57ab62b23c88523ba.abstract: Background: Previous research on psychosocial interventions for children and adolescents with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) has primarily focused on overall symptom severity, with less attention to treatment effects across core symptom dimensions. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the effects of cognitive behavioral interventions on overall ADHD symptoms, inattention, and hyperactivity/impulsivity and explored the influence of intervention type, treatment duration, and weekly session frequency. Methods: PubMed, Web of Science Core Collection, Embase, and CENTRAL were searched from inception to 30 June 2026 for randomized controlled trials. Risk of bias was assessed using RoB 2. Effect sizes were calculated as Hedges’ g and pooled using random-effects models, with sensitivity and exploratory subgroup analyses conducted. The review was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261376097). Results: Ten randomized controlled trials involving 849 participants were included. Cognitive behavioral interventions significantly reduced overall ADHD symptoms (g = −0.389, 95% CI −0.773 to −0.005), inattention (g = −0.415, 95% CI −0.749 to −0.082), and hyperactivity/impulsivity (g = −0.366, 95% CI −0.658 to −0.075). Inattention showed the numerically largest pooled effect. Exploratory subgroup analyses showed numerical differences across intervention type, treatment duration, and weekly session frequency, but formal moderator tests found no statistically significant between-subgroup differences. Conclusions: These findings support the potential benefits of cognitive behavioral interventions for ADHD symptom management, with the most consistent results observed for inattention. Future randomized controlled trials should compare intervention components and treatment schedules while assessing actual treatment exposure, including home practice, to inform more targeted cognitive behavioral interventions.

title: Assessing Joint Media Engagement During Screen Time in Early Childhood: A Scoping Review of Parent–Child Interaction Measures
container-title: Multimodal Technologies and Interaction
0e53dc27841beb392f7a3ccf4842510499b0ec9c.abstract: Background: Joint media engagement (JME) is recognized as a relational process involving shared participation, media context, and parent–child interaction. This scoping review aimed to identify methods used to evaluate JME and examine the extent to which questionnaire-based measures capture its joint, media, and engagement characteristics. Methods: A search of 6 databases up to May 2025 was conducted following PRISMA-ScR guidelines. Fifty included studies were synthesized to identify evaluation methods, questionnaire characteristics, and reported psychometric properties. Results: JME was evaluated using questionnaires, observations, interviews, diaries, and qualitative methods, with questionnaires being the predominant approach. Questionnaires varied considerably in conceptual coverage. Most captured only one or two JME characteristics, while few integrated all three. Joint characteristics commonly emphasized co-presence or co-viewing frequency; media characteristics addressed devices, activities, or content; and engagement characteristics included cognitive, affective, and technical or physical scaffolding. Many Questionnaires originated from parental-mediation literature and emphasized active or restrictive mediation. Psychometric evaluation was limited and inconsistently reported. Conclusions: Existing Questionnaires capture important JME-related practices but rarely represent JME as an integrated relational process. The findings support developing a psychometrically robust, multidimensional measure that connects participants, media context, and engagement quality and is validated across developmental, cultural, and digital contexts.

title: Passive Multi-View 3D Reconstruction for Immersive Foreign-Language Interpreting Training Assessment in Intelligent Education: Balancing Cross-Scale Symmetry and Observation Asymmetry Under Non-Ideal Consumer-Camera Acquisition
container-title: Photonics
773ee6f92b26390bda6b142bcc1fa9764f713b3c.abstract: In intelligent education, reusable immersive scenes can provide consistent visual contexts for foreign-language interpreting practice and structured assessment activities. This work focuses on the optical and geometric stage of such scene preparation: passive multi-view 3D reconstruction from non-ideal consumer-camera imagery. The PatchMatchNet pipeline incorporates PANet-style bidirectional cross-scale feature exchange and CBAM weighting of aggregated matching evidence to balance reciprocal geometric information with spatially variable observation reliability. The reported allocation comprises 99 DTU scenes and 44 assigned self-collected scenes, with 5 additional self-collected scenes listed outside the allocation. In the joint-module comparison, the reported reconstruction-to-reference, reference-to-reconstruction, and symmetric-mean point-set distances change from 0.483, 0.321, and 0.402 to 0.350, 0.222, and 0.286, respectively (nominal mm). These values characterize the custom mixed evaluation and its within-table architectural comparison. The reconstruction, point-cloud export, and Unity3D (version 2022.3 LTS) visualization workflow is illustrated on the PICO 4 Pro, supporting the preparation of visual assets for immersive language-learning environments.

title: Adaptive Deep Learning Model with Anatomical Priors for 3D Segmentation of Fine Hepatic Vasculature on CT
container-title: Radiology Advances
86467c6926c30e65e94b3c0b7ae02cc5507850a9.abstract: Abstract BACKGROUND Accurate segmentation of fine hepatic vessels on CT remains challenging because peripheral branches are small and low contrast. PURPOSE To develop and test PriM Fusion Net, a deep learning model that adaptively integrates an optimized anatomical prior to improve 3D CT segmentation of portal and hepatic veins, emphasizing fine peripheral branches for preoperative 3D modeling. MATERIALS AND METHODS This retrospective study used the public MSD Task08-HepaticVessel dataset of 303 abdominal CT volumes. PriM Fusion Net uses a dual-encoder architecture: a Swin Transformer processes CT images and a parallel convolutional pathway processes a dataset-optimized Frangi vesselness prior. Gated multimodal units act as spatially varying voxel-wise gates that fuse the two feature streams at multiple scales. A rule-based SimpleMind post-processing module refined anatomical plausibility. Performance was evaluated with five-fold cross-validation and zero-shot external inference on 3DIRCADb. RESULTS PriM Fusion Net achieved a mean Dice similarity coefficient (DSC) of 77.68% (95% confidence interval [CI]: 77.11, 78.25) and 95th percentile Hausdorff distance (HD95) of 11.55 mm (95% CI: 9.94, 13.16), outperforming all baselines (all adjusted P &lt; .02). For vessels with radius ≤ 1.5 mm, DSC improved by 13.5% versus SwinUNETR (59.2% [95% CI: 54.48, 63.92] vs 45.7% [95% CI: 40.49, 50.91]). In ablation, replacing rigid concatenation with gated fusion improved DSC from 75.86% [95% CI: 75.31, 76.41] to 77.65% [95% CI: 76.92, 78.38], and SimpleMind post-processing reduced HD95 from 14.98 mm [95% CI: 10.91, 19.05] to 11.55 mm [95% CI: 9.94, 13.16]. On 3DIRCADb, zero-shot inference yielded DSC of 68.42% [95% CI: 65.82, 71.02] and HD95 of 11.78 mm [95% CI: 8.50, 15.06]. CONCLUSION Adaptive deep fusion of an optimized anatomical prior improved CT segmentation of portal and hepatic veins, especially fine peripheral branches, supporting further evaluation in 3D vascular modeling workflows for liver surgery and intervention.

title: Performance of Free Web-Based Multimodal Large Language Models on Turkish and English Image-Based Dental Examination Questions
container-title: Dentomaxillofacial Radiology
3ad38630551bfb130165750c7cb870669a5321fd.abstract: Abstract Objectives To compare final-answer accuracy of web-based large language models (LLMs) on Turkish and English image-based dental examination multiple-choice questions (deMCQs), and to describe explanation quality, reference quality, output volume, and an exploratory word-normalized water-use scenario. Methods Fifty-two image-based deMCQs (2012–2025) were evaluated in Turkish and English using ChatGPT, Gemini, and Claude, yielding 312 responses. Accuracy was coded as correct or incorrect. Explanation and reference quality were assessed using a 5-point Likert scale and treated as exploratory descriptive outcomes. Accuracy was analyzed using question-clustered binomial generalized estimating equations (GEE) with model, language, and model×language interaction terms. Output word counts were summarized, and a study-specific exploratory word-normalized water-use scenario was derived from a published exchange-level estimate. Results Overall accuracy was 56.7% (177/312). Accuracy was 59.0% in Turkish and 54.5% in English. GEE analysis showed no significant effects of model, language, or model×language interaction (p &gt; 0.05). Descriptively, Gemini had the highest accuracy (61.5%), whereas Claude had the highest mean explanation (3.95±1.31) and reference quality (4.85±0.38) scores. Across 312 prompt–response exchanges, the models generated 34,534 words, corresponding to an exploratory word-normalized water-use proxy of 3.12–7.80 L. Conclusions Freely accessible web-based LLMs demonstrated moderate accuracy on image-based deMCQs. The water-use proxy was derived from published exchange-level assumptions and should not be interpreted as a direct measurement or validated model-specific estimate of water consumption. Descriptive differences between models and languages should not be interpreted as evidence of superiority or equivalence. These systems may support dental education; however, outputs require expert verification before educational or clinical use. Advances in knowledge This study evaluates three widely accessible web-based multimodal LLMs using an entirely image-based dental examination question set, accounts for repeated observations through question-clustered GEE, compares Turkish and English performance without equating non-significance with equivalence, and presents a transparent word-normalized environmental scenario with explicit assumptions and limitations.

title: Visual search as a cognitive marker to discriminate progressive supranuclear palsy from Parkinson’s disease
container-title: Brain Communications
abda63e481849a88d2097be19b78ee960e6d5e9f.abstract: Abstract Early and accurate diagnosis of Progressive Supranuclear Palsy is a high priority for both patients and clinicians. Nearly half of individuals with Progressive Supranuclear Palsy are initially given an alternative diagnosis—most commonly Parkinson’s disease—and the correct diagnosis of Progressive Supranuclear Palsy is delayed by an average of three years compared with Parkinson’s disease. Problems with cognition arise early in the progression of Progressive Supranuclear Palsy, including profoundly disturbed visual search. This search deficit is likely caused by a combination of oculomotor, visuospatial, attentional and executive dysfunction, which is not observed in Parkinson’s. Since assessment of visual search is not routinely included in clinical testing for Progressive Supranuclear Palsy, it may represent a promising method for differentiating these movement disorders. However, few studies have systematically compared visual search in Progressive Supranuclear Palsy and Parkinson’s disease, so the extent to which search deficits can reliably differentiate the two diseases is unknown. To address this issue, patients with Progressive Supranuclear Palsy (N = 28), Parkinson’s disease (N=28) and age matched controls (N=27) completed four tests of visuospatial attention: an easy feature search task, a difficult feature search task, a conjunction search task and a paper-and-pencil cancellation task (the Bells test). We measured perceptual sensitivity (d prime), search time and detection accuracy. Search efficiency in the Bells test was also modelled using Quality of Search score. In addition, patients completed tests of oculomotor system integrity, the Montreal Cognitive Assessment and the National Eye Institute Visual Function Questionnaire 25. As predicted, Progressive Supranuclear Palsy was associated with a profound search deficit: search was slow and highly disorganised on all tests. Furthermore, reflexive orienting along the vertical axis was impaired on the easy feature search. Critically, Receiver Operator Characteristic analyses revealed that the Quality of Search score derived from the Bells test classified Progressive Supranuclear Palsy with a sensitivity of 82%, a specificity of 96%, and Area under the Curve of .90. Given the Bells test is fast to administer (∼5 mins), free, relatively simple to score and already widely used in neuropsychology assessment, it has the potential to be a highly effective addition to the battery of tests used in the differential diagnosis of Progressive Supranuclear Palsy

title: Optimizing HIV pre-exposure prophylaxis among transgender women in the United States: a conceptual framework of engagement in prevention-effective adherence
c46c7f940f5331a71b5e11ae68bd15a26eda8feb.abstract: Abstract Transgender women in the United States experience a disproportionate burden of HIV driven by multi-level social and structural vulnerabilities. Although oral PrEP, injectable cabotegravir, and twice-yearly lenacapavir are now available, PrEP use remains suboptimal. We conducted a qualitative analysis of 18 semi-structured life history calendar interviews conducted between February and June 2022 with transgender women in the eastern and southern United States who were indicated for PrEP and had varied PrEP histories. We generated a conceptual framework of prevention-effective adherence based on findings. Two bidirectional domains, capacity to safely engage with the healthcare system and compatibility between PrEP and individual values and preferences, shaped prevention-effective adherence. Influencing both domains were distal factors, including stigmas, identity-based oppression and marginalization, and sociostructural context. Unlike models that categorize barriers using existing frameworks, our inductively derived framework specifies how factors relate to each other, centers prevention-effective adherence rather than discrete cascade steps, and situates PrEP engagement in the life course. Our findings illuminate modifiable factors, including cost, availability of gender-affirming care, and access to evidence-based HIV/STI information, to improve and optimize PrEP engagement among transgender women in the United States.

title: Occupational Types, Working Hours, and Cognitive Trajectories
container-title: Work, Aging and Retirement
ffb9730bc26d334ee9d4a045cd264d4e1fd4ff60.abstract: Abstract The relationship between work and cognitive function in later years has gained attention recently. However, information on occupational types, working hours, and cognitive function based on longitudinal cohort studies from developing countries remains limited. This study utilizes data from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study and employs group-based trajectory modeling to depict the heterogeneous changes in cognitive function over time among middle-aged and older adults and specifically examines the associations between occupational types (agricultural work, non-agricultural employment, non-agricultural self-employed or family business), working hours, and cognitive trajectories. Our findings indicate that agricultural work is associated with poorer cognitive trajectories compared to non-agricultural employment and non-agricultural self-employed or family business. Compared to individuals working 40 hours or less per week, those working 41–55 hours had a higher likelihood of experiencing a “rapid decline” cognitive trajectory. Furthermore, working over 55 hours per week was associated with an increased likelihood of belonging to both the “rapid decline” and “persistently moderate” trajectory groups. We did not observe a significant multiplicative interaction between occupational types and working hours on the cognitive trajectories. These results enhance our understanding of the relationship between work-related factors and cognitive function, providing a scientific basis for developing targeted intervention measures in the context of developing countries.

title: Large Peritoneal Macrophages influence CD8+ T cell activation and parasite control during acute Trypanosoma cruzi infection
container-title: Journal of Leukocyte Biology
895f79e9f242cf3a38d572212758036b221227ea.abstract: Abstract Resident peritoneal macrophages consist of two subpopulations with distinct origin, sizes and phenotype named Large Peritoneal Macrophages (LPMs) and Small Peritoneal Macrophages (SPMs). While LPMs are long-live cells that origin in embryonic yolk sac and can self-replenish after mild loss, SPMs are short-live cells that derive from blood monocytes and are in continuous replenishment. Under homeostasis, LPMs constitute more than 70% of total CD11b+ cells, but during infection or inflammation drastically dampen. As LPMs have been reported to be essential for CD8+ T cell priming and replication control in parasite infections, we aimed to study their role in the context of Chagas’ disease. We observed a reduction in LPMs during acute phase of T. cruzi infection in BALB/c mice that did not restore in chronic phase. Instead, this subset was replaced by a population with intermediate expression of F4/80, previously described as ‘inflammatory macrophages’, but with a mixed phenotype activation in this case. Besides, this F4/80int population could also be associated with truncated maturation of monocytes to resident macrophages. In this work, LPMs showed higher CD80+ and lower PD-L1+ cells frequencies and produced more IL-12 and TNF than SPMs. This profile may favor CD8+ T-cell activation, reflected by increased CD69 expression and Perforin/Granzyme B production. Replenishment of LPMs by adoptive transfer of PEMs was associated with reduced parasitemia and enhanced splenic CD8+ T-cell activation. Thus, LPMs may contribute to CD8+ T-cell responses and parasite control during acute T. cruzi infection.

title: PROGNOSTIC VALUE OF RED BLOOD CELL DISTRIBUTION WIDTH IN PATIENTS WITH DIFFUSE LARGE B-CELL LYMPHOMA

2843965134f1b4aa61e021428d2ee0e4928c6e0c.abstract: Mục tiêu: Đánh giá giá trị tiên lượng của RDW đối với kết cục lâm sàng ở bệnh nhân (BN) DLBCL. Đối tượng và phương pháp: Nghiên cứu được thực hiện trên 134 BN được chẩn đoán và điều trị tại Bệnh viện Quân y 103 trong giai đoạn 01/2016 -01/2026. BN được phân thành hai nhóm theo ngưỡng RDW 14%. Kết quả: Nhóm RDW >14% có tỷ lệ ECOG ≥2, giai đoạn Ann Arbor III/IV, nồng độ β₂-microglobulin tăng và nhóm nguy cơ cao theo R-IPI cao hơn có ý nghĩa so với nhóm RDW ≤14% (p < 0,05). Tỷ lệ không đáp ứng điều trị ở nhóm RDW >14% cao hơn so với nhóm RDW ≤14% (24,2% so với 9,7%; p = 0,023). RDW trung vị giảm có ý nghĩa sau hóa trị ở nhóm đạt đáp ứng hoàn toàn (p =0,041). RDW >14% làm tăng nguy cơ tiến triển bệnh 1,695 lần và nguy cơ tử vong 1,876 lần. Tỷ lệ PFS và OS sau 3 năm ở nhóm RDW >14% lần lượt là 46,8% và 54,8%, thấp hơn rõ rệt so với nhóm RDW ≤14% (63,9% và 75,0%; p <0,01).

title: Systematic Evaluation of Mixture-Design for Multi-Oxide Magnesium Aluminosilicate Glass Development: Model Comparison, Modifier Interactions, and Predictive Limitations
2c0aa1a866ecbeccfd660fd63586c5b03525e699.abstract: A constrained ternary mixture design (Design of Experiments, DoE) was applied to four magnesium aluminosilicate (MAS) glass series to evaluate the predictive capability of Scheffé mixture polynomials for the specific Young’s modulus (spE = E/ρ), the key figure of merit for lightweight glass-fibre reinforcements. Two base compositions (V, Al2O3-rich; T, MgO-rich) were each modified with a 14 wt.% Y2O3–ZnO–CeO2 or La2O3–ZnO–CeO2 block. Linear, quadratic and special-cubic models were fitted to ten design points per series and ranked by R2, R2(adj) and the leave-one-out coefficient R2(pred). Three distinct regimes emerge: the V-series requires a special-cubic model with a dominant ternary Y2O3·ZnO·CeO2 term (β = −47.2, p = 0.001; R2(pred) = 97 %); the T-series is strictly linear (R2(pred) = 55 %), higher orders overfitting; and both La-series show a significant La2O3·CeO2 interaction absent in their Y-analogues. Three additive property models (Makishima–Mackenzie, an extended variant, and Yamane–Sakaino) deviate systematically from measured spE (absolute errors 6.9–12.2 × 106 N·m·kg-1, negative R2), most strongly where DoE detects interactions. The study delineates where additive approaches suffice, where binary synergy dominates, and where genuinely ternary cooperative effects must be resolved.

title: A Cellular Sheaf Model for Aromaticity in Discrete Molecular Systems
fe5e3994f9b89c7fa7a2e29a43542bbad0c61bdb.abstract: Aromaticity underpins molecular stability in fields ranging from pharmaceuticals to organic semiconductors, yet existing prediction methods are either too computationally costly for large-scale screening or too empirically restricted for broad applicability. This work introduces the molecular sheaf, a cellular sheaf model free of empirical parameters for chemical bonding that generalizes standard molecular graph theory. From this the frontier eigengap Δ_F is derived as a spectral approximation of the HOMO-LUMO gap requiring only molecular topology and electron count. Δ_F correctly classifies the aromaticity and antiaromaticity of the full annulene series, including benzene and cyclobutadiene, exactly recovering Hückel theory for regular hydrocarbon systems. At scale, it accounts for 62.5% of the variance in DFT HOMO-LUMO gaps across 17,523 structurally diverse polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons and 21.7% across 52,000 heteroaromatic systems, with the reduction reflecting the deliberate cost of parameter freedom. This confirms that aromatic character can be approximated from molecular connectivity and electron count alone, suggesting that cellular sheaves offer a largely unexplored mathematical framework for the modeling of chemical bonding and structure. All calculations run at under 1 ms per molecule, over seven orders of magnitude faster than corresponding DFT calculations. The molecular sheaf thus also enables rapid, parameter-free pre-screening of aromatic character from structural data alone.

title: CITIZEN-MAJORITY TOKENIZED OWNERSHIP FOR MSME REVIVAL IN INDIA: THE G-CMTO MODEL INTEGRATING BLOCKCHAIN, THE E-RUPEE AND THE MICROSME–BLOCKCHAIN INDEX
container-title: EPRA International Journal of Economics Business and Management Studies
5767b292d8b7543fded6ed3f276960d4d626c798.abstract: India's micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) produce about 31.1% of GDP and nearly half of the country's exports (48.58%), yet they work against an addressable credit gap of roughly ₹30 lakh crore. Meanwhile, India's trade deficit with China touched a record US$112.6 billion in FY2025-26. The policy conversation has no shortage of diagnoses; what it lacks is a mechanism someone could actually implement. This paper offers one: the Gujar Citizen-Majority Tokenized Ownership (G-CMTO) Model, designed for new micro and small manufacturing units of ₹50 lakh to ₹10 crore in product categories exposed to imports. In a G-CMTO unit, resident citizens and non-resident Indians together own 50–55% of the equity through tokenized shares that can be bought for as little as ₹100. An accountable operator holds 30–35%, the government contributes a 5% subordinated first-loss stake, and bank debt covers the remaining 10%. Three layers hold the model together: the e-Rupee as programmable money, a depository-run permissioned ledger for ownership, and a new MicroSME–Blockchain Index (MBI) for intelligence. Sixty per cent of the MBI's weight comes from verified money flows, and its grades decide how much GST is reimbursed, whether the operator's bonus equity vests and when new issuance is paused. Following a design-science approach, the paper sets out the capital structure, governance, index, fiscal incentive and legal pathway, and works them through three illustrative cases: a ₹50 lakh toy unit, a ₹1 crore series LED unit and a ₹10 crore BLDC fan plant. The argument is simple. India can build citizen-owned industrial capacity on infrastructure its regulators are already piloting, and the more people take part, the stronger the index becomes.

title: Student Engagement with Digital Library Resources through Learning Analytics in Adamawa State University, Mubi
container-title: RESEARCH JOURNAL OF MASS COMMUNICATION AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY
bac75cd498df9d6c565016912780cdd9c210ab5e.abstract: This study investigates student engagement with digital library resources at Adamawa State University, Mubi, using learning analytics and survey data. A stratified sample approach was designed to obtain responses from 1,800 students across faculties. Measures included frequency of use, session duration, resource diversity, perceived usefulness, accessibility, digital literacy, and institutional use of learning analytics. Descriptive and inferential analyses — including ttests, ANOVA, and regression models — were employed. Results indicate that overall engagement with digital library resources is lower than neutral (mean engagement = 2.52/5), with no statistically significant differences across faculties. Awareness of learning analytics alone did not correspond to higher engagement; rather, infrastructural and user-related challenges (poor connectivity, limited digital skills, and usability issues) were significant negative predictors of engagement. The study concludes that implementing robust learning-analytics dashboards, improving digital infrastructure, and incorporating digital literacy training are key to increasing students’ meaningful engagement with digital resources. Recommendations include investment in reliable connectivity, targeted training programs, and dashboard-driven interventions to personalize resource recommendations and promote deeper use.

title: Responsible entrepreneurship, safety involvement, prohibitive safety voice and employee safety participation in a developing economy: a serial model
container-title: Social Responsibility Journal
46493c520a4ece91f11f204a39f89ae1efb24446.abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine how owner-managers’ responsible entrepreneurship influences employee safety participation through the serial mediation of safety involvement and prohibitive safety voice. Design/methodology/approach Data were collected from 417 owner-managers of manufacturing SMEs in Ghana. The hypotheses were tested using partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM). Findings The results show that responsible entrepreneurship positively influences employee safety participation. While safety involvement does not moderate this relationship, it significantly mediates the link between responsible entrepreneurship and both prohibitive safety voice and employee safety participation. The serial mediation analysis further indicates that responsible entrepreneurship enhances safety involvement, which fosters prohibitive safety voice and, in turn, increases employee safety participation. Practical implications Owner-managers should involve employees in identifying workplace hazards, discuss safety concerns during routine meetings and provide simple channels for reporting unsafe practices. Policymakers can support SMEs through practical safety guidelines, short training programmes and advisory services that help businesses implement affordable employee-centred safety practices. Originality/value This study develops a process-oriented framework explaining the employee-level behavioural mechanisms through which responsible entrepreneurship fosters proactive safety practices in SMEs, particularly under the resource and structural constraints common in developing economies.

title: Source Expertise, Argument Strength, and Multidimensional Source Sensitivity in Large Language Model Evaluation
c9ea8d973bfe8358f2d405cd3fe83905b3b9ef4a.abstract: Abstract Large language models are increasingly used to evaluate arguments, responses, and decisions, yet their judgments may be influenced by contextual information about who produced the content. This study examined how source expertise relevance and argument strength affect LLM evaluation and whether source effects differ across judgment dimensions. Twenty arguments spanning 10 topics were constructed as strong–weak pairs and presented under four source conditions: relevant expert, irrelevant expert, non-expert, and no source. Four large language models evaluated each argument on logical quality, credibility, persuasiveness, and agreement. Five repetitions were collected for each model-by-argument-by-source-by-dimension combination and averaged before inferential testing. Human validation assessed the intended argument-strength manipulation but showed negligible overall strong–weak separation in the second validation round, including two reversed topic pairs. Separate manipulation checks indicated that the models rated topic-relevant expertise and general professional expertise differently across source conditions. Source attribution most consistently affected credibility. Topic-level robustness analyses showed significant source-condition effects on credibility across all four models, while persuasiveness remained significant only for GPT-5.6 Sol. Relevant-expert attribution did not produce a universal advantage: credibility was significantly higher for relevant than irrelevant experts for Claude Opus 5.5 and DeepSeek Flash, and Claude Opus 5.5 also showed significantly higher persuasiveness for relevant than irrelevant experts. Exploratory analyses suggested that this pattern may reflect an irrelevant-expertise penalty more than a universal bonus for relevant expertise. No robust evidence showed that relevant expertise disproportionately improved weak arguments. Credibility was descriptively more source-sensitive than logical quality, but corrected direct contrasts were not statistically significant. Overall, LLM evaluation was neither fully source-neutral nor characterized by simple deference to experts. Source expertise produced dimension-specific and model-dependent effects, with credibility showing the clearest sensitivity.

title: Programmer expertise classification using cognitive load and transfer learning
container-title: Discover Computing
f504c1239bb13fa73a7b7735bc8c27cc18f7e8e5.abstract: Abstract Context Evaluating a programmer’s performance by considering both technical and cognitive skills is indispensable in many software development tasks. Problem Technical skills are relatively easy to assess, whereas non-technical skills, such as long-term memory, critical thinking, and emotional intelligence, are often overlooked while measuring the performance of a programmer. Aim The primary objective of this work is to propose a reliable framework for classifying programmers into five framework-derived proficiency ranks. Methods Participants are given an assignment with both technical and non-technical questions. A cognitive load index that combines technical and non-technical skills is used to analyze performance and stratify it into five ranks. The proposed framework was evaluated using CatBoost and TabNet classifiers in a transfer-learning setup. It used the source dataset (Another researcher’s dataset) for pre-training and the proposed programmer dataset for fine-tuning. Extensive experiments, including confusion matrix analysis, 5-fold cross-validation, sensitivity analysis, and ablation studies, confirm the framework’s effectiveness and robustness. Results The fine-tuned CatBoost model outperformed the TabNet model, achieving an impressive 87% accuracy, a significant improvement over the pre-trained model’s 31%. The findings demonstrate that combining technical skills with non-technical aspects greatly enhances the accuracy of classifying programmer expertise. This offers a dependable method for assessing programmers in software engineering education. The study develops a robust framework for evaluating programming performance that incorporates both technical and non-technical skills, and it can be adapted for other cognitive and skill-based evaluations across different fields.

title:
Phosphide-Mediated
Hydrogen Evolution by a Well-Defined
Molecular Model for Amorphous Cobalt Phosphide Surfaces
container-title: Inorganic Chemistry
5bf648002a3feb3a7b785e77fb321f0eed4f4a28.abstract: Abstract Cobalt phosphide is a promising non-noble metal electrocatalyst for the electrocatalytic production of hydrogen gas, although the mechanism by which it operates at its amorphized surfaces is not well understood. In this work, we report a highly stable cobalt phosphide cluster, Co3(μ3-P)(CO)6(CNArDipp2)3 (ArDipp2 = 2,6-(2,6-(iPr)2C6H3)2C6H3), which is a competent catalyst for electrocatalytic hydrogen evolution (HER) under acidic conditions and serves as a functional model system for amorphous cobalt phosphide surfaces. The active catalyst was identified as being the protonated cluster [Co3(μ3-PH)(CO)6(CNArDipp2)3]+, which was isolated and fully characterized. Additionally, P-functionalized derivatives were found to have impeded or absent catalytic activity, implicating the phosphide atom as playing a crucial role in the catalytic mechanism. This work suggests that the phosphide anions on heterogeneous cobalt phosphide surfaces serve as important mediators of proton delivery, analogous to the well-established importance of Lewis basic moieties in molecular and biological hydrogen evolution catalysts.

title: Minimal Intervention: Function Isolation via AST before Language-Model Patching
b04497c58d74fc85af7560256e86c10b84cb8e4c.abstract: Automatic code-repair agents such as SWE-agent operate at the repository level, generating patches that touch multiple files and functions. This granularity increases token cost and complicates verification: a correct fix inside one function can be masked by unrelated changes. We formulate the scope control problem as separate from verification and propose MINIMAL-INTERVENTION REPAIR, a pipeline that isolates the faulty function through AST analysis, passes only that function to the language model, and verifies the candidate by executing tests before commit. The language model is treated as a black-box oracle. The architecture requires no fine-tuning and is compatible with any API. This is a position paper: we define the pipeline stages, pseudocode for localization and isolation, classes of functions that cannot be isolated, and an evaluation protocol on QuixBugs with ablations and a green-but-wrong patch metric.

title: LACHESIS: Robust stellar parameters through Bayesian model averaging of isochrone grids
container-title: Astronomy & Astrophysics
cc4a816515a21040b08aff20f93c3d38749aa802.abstract: Accurate stellar parameters underpin much of modern astrophysics, from the characterisation of exoplanetary systems to Galactic archaeology. For isolated field stars, masses and especially ages are most often inferred by comparing observed properties against stellar evolution models, yet these inferences depend on the chosen model grid, and the systematic differences between grids can rival the statistical uncertainties of any single pipeline. We present , a package that determines stellar masses, radii, and ages from photometry and spectroscopy while explicitly accounting for the systematic uncertainties introduced by the choice of stellar evolution model grid. lachesis python We interpolated five independent isochrone grids in Fe/H , log age, and equivalent evolutionary phase conditioned on the data; sampled each grid using nested sampling; and combined the resulting per-grid posteriors using Bayesian model averaging, with weights proportional to the Bayesian evidence of each grid. We validated against a benchmark of Kepler asteroseismic dwarfs and subgiants. Masses were recovered with a robust scatter of sim4% and radii to sim2%, with the radius negligibly biased by $<1%$ and the masses carrying a small ∼-3% systematic. Stellar age was recovered with a robust scatter of 30% that depends strongly on the evolutionary state. The grid-to-grid systematic contributes a sim9% floor, a subdominant but real term that a single-grid fit omits. Model averaging is better calibrated than when selecting a single grid, its credible intervals approach nominal coverage once the reference uncertainty is included, and the intervals cover near the nominal rate in injection tests even when the generating model lies outside the ensemble. lachesis By marginalising over an ensemble of stellar model grids, folds the choice-of-grid systematic directly into the posterior, so the reported uncertainties reflect the choice-of-grid systematic rather than only within-grid data noise and stay near a nominal value in injection tests even when the generating model lies outside the ensemble. This delivers homogeneous, well-characterised masses, radii, and ages for exoplanet host characterisation and stellar population studies. lachesis

63ebda269aaea21d19ae4f6a5bb6fcc50cde34f4.abstract: Zusammenfassung Große untertägige Forschungsinfrastrukturen erzeugen innerhalb weniger Jahre Aushubmengen im Millionen-Kubikmeter-Bereich. Am Beispiel des Einstein Teleskops (ET) wird ein Rahmen für eine Aushubmaterial-Strategie in der frühen Planungs- und Entwurfsphase entwickelt. Risikomanagement wird dabei als Leitlogik mit einem durchgängigen Qualitätsmanagement verknüpft, die Verwertungsplanung als Portfolio- und Matching-Aufgabe gefasst. Für die drei Kandidatenregionen Euregio Maas-Rhein, Lausitz und Sos Enattos werden Geologie, Rechtsrahmen und Verwertungspfade gegenübergestellt. Die Auswertung zeigt, dass die untersuchten Rechtsordnungen eine hochwertige Kreislaufführung grundsätzlich zulassen und die maßgeblichen Restriktionen geowissenschaftlicher Natur sind. Als Ergebnis werden die Grundlagen eines integrierten Qualitätsmanagementplans sowie ein Erhebungskonzept vorgestellt, das sensorgestützte Mess- und Klassifikationsansätze in realitätsnaher Umgebung erprobt.

container-title: Journal of Digital Health
8c2b2b92dc34c507f5536f1e76215cac1a12b795.abstract: Prompt engineering shapes large language model (LLM) output, but practicing clinicians have little guidance on which prompting style suits a given clinical task. A single publicly available, de-identified pediatric psychiatric case report was submitted to a base, unauthenticated ChatGPT-5.5 session under four prompt conditions: zero-shot, chain-of-thought, role/persona, and structured/constrained output. Each output was scored from 0 (feature absent) to 2 (complete) on four criteria: diagnostic accuracy, causative agent recognition, safety completeness, and calibration. Output was compared against the published clinical course. Total scores were zero-shot 7/8, chain-of-thought 6/8, role-persona 7/8, and structured 7/8. All four conditions ranked bipolar I disorder above substance-induced psychotic disorder, whereas the treating team's documented differential favored unspecified and substance-induced categories without a confirmed bipolar diagnosis. All four conditions recommended neuroimaging, electroencephalography, and lumbar puncture, exceeding the workup the treating team actually performed. Across four prompt styles, core diagnostic content was materially the same; the styles differed in the precision of probability quantification and in reasoning transparency, not in the underlying differential generated.

title: PERBEDAAN ANTARA  MODEL PEMBELAJARAN PENYELIDIKAN DAN PENEMUAN  PEMAHAMAN SISWA TENTANG KONSEP MATEMATIKA DALAM MATERI PYTHAGOREAN
