d2e1061ed2876f1917109b9647f72e9f9c33b47a.abstract: Students' understanding of mathematical concepts in the Pythagorean Theorem at SMP Negeri 13 Kupang remains low due to teacher-centered learning and formula memorization. This study aims to examine the significant difference in mathematical concept understanding between students taught using Inquiry Learning and Discovery Learning models. A quantitative approach with a quasi-experimental nonequivalent control group design was employed. The sample was selected through purposive sampling, consisting of class VIII G (30 students) as experimental class I utilizing Inquiry Learning and class VIII H (30 students) as experimental class II utilizing Discovery Learning. The instrument was an objective test of mathematical concept understanding comprising 15 validated multiple-choice items. Data were analyzed inferentially using an independent sample t-test via IBM SPSS Statistics 22. The results demonstrated that the post-test mean of the Inquiry Learning class was 69.53, while the Discovery Learning class achieved 60.47. Hypothesis testing yielded a significance value of 0.035 (p<0.05), confirming a statistically significant difference in mathematical concept understanding between both learning models. Consequently, the Inquiry Learning model yields superior conceptual understanding compared to Discovery Learning by systematically engaging students in problem formulation, scientific investigation, hypothesis testing, and conclusion drawing. ABSTRAK Pemahaman konsep matematika peserta didik pada materi Teorema Pythagoras di SMP Negeri 13 Kupang masih tergolong rendah karena pembelajaran cenderung berpusat pada guru dan berorientasi pada hafalan rumus. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menguji perbedaan yang signifikan pada pemahaman konsep matematis antara siswa yang diajar menggunakan model Inquiry Learning dan Discovery Learning. Pendekatan penelitian yang digunakan adalah kuantitatif dengan desain quasi-experimental tipe nonequivalent control group design. Sampel dipilih secara purposive sampling, yaitu kelas VIII G (30 siswa) sebagai kelas eksperimen I dengan model Inquiry Learning dan kelas VIII H (30 siswa) sebagai kelas eksperimen II dengan model Discovery Learning. Instrumen pengumpulan data berupa tes objektif pemahaman konsep sebanyak 15 butir soal pilihan ganda yang telah divalidasi oleh ahli. Data dianalisis secara inferensial menggunakan independent sample t-test dengan bantuan IBM SPSS Statistics 22. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan rata-rata nilai post-test kelas Inquiry Learning sebesar 69,53, sedangkan kelas Discovery Learning sebesar 60,47. Uji hipotesis menghasilkan nilai signifikansi sebesar 0,035 (p<0,05), yang membuktikan adanya perbedaan pemahaman konsep matematis yang signifikan antara kedua kelas tersebut. Dengan demikian, penerapan model Inquiry Learning memberikan capaian pemahaman konsep yang lebih baik dibandingkan Discovery Learning karena melibatkan siswa secara intensif dalam tahapan perumusan masalah, penyelidikan ilmiah, pengujian hipotesis, dan penarikan kesimpulan.

title: PENINGKATAN KEMAMPUAN NUMERASI MELALUI PENERAPAN MODEL CONTEXTUAL TEACHING AND LEARNING (CTL) BERBANTUAN WORDWALL PADA MATERI BILANGAN CACAH  DI KELAS V UPTD SD NEGERI 070999 TARAKHAINI
container-title: SCIENCE : Jurnal Inovasi Pendidikan Matematika dan IPA
6392ab2457692469b3ac35032a1a506749343ebf.abstract: The numeracy skills of fifth-grade students at UPTD SD Negeri 070999 Tarakhaini in whole numbers up to 1,000,000 were initially low. This condition was evidenced by pre-cycle test results indicating that only 5 out of 20 students (25%) achieved mastery learning with a class average score of 48.5. This study aims to describe the implementation of the Contextual Teaching and Learning (CTL) model assisted by Wordwall and to analyze the improvement of students' numeracy skills in learning whole numbers up to 1,000,000. The methodology employed was Classroom Action Research (CAR) following the Kemmis and McTaggart model across two cycles, comprising planning, action, observation, and reflection stages. The findings revealed that teacher activity increased from 76.39% in Cycle I to 92.13% in Cycle II, while student activity improved from 59.20% to 80.36%. Furthermore, students' average numeracy score improved from 48.5 in the pre-cycle to 65 in Cycle I and reached 76 in Cycle II, with classical mastery increasing significantly from 25% to 70% and ultimately to 90%. Consequently, the implementation of the Contextual Teaching and Learning model assisted by interactive Wordwall media effectively enhances elementary school students' numeracy skills. ABSTRAK Kemampuan numerasi peserta didik kelas V UPTD SD Negeri 070999 Tarakhaini pada materi bilangan cacah sampai 1.000.000 masih tergolong rendah. Kondisi tersebut terbukti dari hasil tes awal pra-siklus yang mencatat hanya 5 dari 20 peserta didik (25%) yang mencapai kriteria ketuntasan dengan nilai rata-rata kelas sebesar 48,5. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mendeskripsikan keterlaksanaan model Contextual Teaching and Learning (CTL) berbantuan Wordwall serta menganalisis peningkatan kemampuan numerasi peserta didik pada materi bilangan cacah sampai 1.000.000. Metode penelitian menggunakan Penelitian Tindakan Kelas (PTK) model Kemmis dan McTaggart yang dilaksanakan dalam dua siklus, dengan tahapan perencanaan, pelaksanaan tindakan, observasi, dan refleksi. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa keterlaksanaan aktivitas guru meningkat dari 76,39% pada Siklus I menjadi 92,13% pada Siklus II, sedangkan aktivitas peserta didik meningkat dari 59,20% menjadi 80,36%. Nilai rata-rata numerasi peserta didik juga meningkat dari 48,5 pada pra-siklus menjadi 65 pada Siklus I dan mencapai 76 pada Siklus II, dengan persentase ketuntasan belajar melonjak dari 25% menjadi 70% lalu mencapai 90%. Berdasarkan hasil tersebut, penerapan model Contextual Teaching and Learning berbantuan media interaktif Wordwall terbukti efektif dalam meningkatkan kemampuan numerasi peserta didik sekolah dasar.

title: PENERAPAN MODEL PEMBELAJARAN QUANTUM TEACHING UNTUK MENINGKATKAN HASIL BELAJAR IPAS PADA PESERTA DIDIK KELAS IV SD NEGERI 074049 TELUK BELUKAR
container-title: SCIENCE : Jurnal Inovasi Pendidikan Matematika dan IPA
1cc484181ebd48ad08af1e0cc9d7a5529cc54e05.abstract: This study was prompted by the low learning outcomes of fourth-grade students at SD Negeri 074049 Teluk Belukar in Natural and Social Sciences (IPAS), specifically regarding the topic of Indonesia's Rich Culture. This low performance was primarily caused by passive student engagement in teacher-centered instruction that provided limited direct learning experiences. This research aims to improve students' learning outcomes by implementing the Quantum Teaching model utilizing the TANDUR framework (Grow, Experience, Label, Demonstrate, Review, and Celebrate). A Classroom Action Research (CAR) design based on Kurt Lewin's model was conducted across two cycles, comprising planning, action, observation, and reflection. The subjects were 20 fourth-grade students during the 2025/2026 academic year. Data were gathered through instructional observations, written learning achievement tests, and field notes, then examined through comparative descriptive analysis. The findings revealed that teacher activity rose from 60.00% in Cycle I to 88.00% in Cycle II, while student activity improved from 66.70% to 91.70%. Academic achievement also advanced, indicated by the increase in the class average score from 61.25 in Cycle I to 77.85 in Cycle II, with classical learning mastery increasing from 70.00% (14 students) to 85.00% (17 students). In conclusion, the implementation of the Quantum Teaching model effectively enhances student learning outcomes in fourth-grade elementary science and social studies. ABSTRAK Rendahnya hasil belajar IPAS materi Indonesia Kaya Budaya di kelas IV SD Negeri 074049 Teluk Belukar dilatarbelakangi oleh kurangnya keaktifan peserta didik akibat pembelajaran yang masih berpusat pada guru (teacher-centered). Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk meningkatkan hasil belajar peserta didik melalui penerapan model pembelajaran quantum teaching berkerangka TANDUR (Tumbuhkan, Alami, Namai, Demonstrasikan, Ulangi, dan Rayakan). Metode yang digunakan adalah Penelitian Tindakan Kelas (PTK) model Kurt Lewin yang dilaksanakan dalam dua siklus, dengan tahapan perencanaan, tindakan, observasi, dan refleksi. Subjek penelitian terdiri atas 20 peserta didik kelas IV tahun ajaran 2025/2026. Data dikumpulkan melalui observasi keterlaksanaan aktivitas, tes hasil belajar uraian, dan catatan lapangan, kemudian dianalisis menggunakan teknik deskriptif komparatif. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan peningkatan aktivitas guru dari 60,00% pada Siklus I menjadi 88,00% pada Siklus II, serta aktivitas peserta didik dari 66,70% menjadi 91,70%. Peningkatan hasil belajar ditunjukkan oleh kenaikan nilai rata-rata kelas dari 61,25 pada Siklus I menjadi 77,85 pada Siklus II, dengan ketuntasan klasikal meningkat dari 70,00% (14 peserta didik) menjadi 85,00% (17 peserta didik). Dengan demikian, penerapan model pembelajaran quantum teaching terbukti efektif dalam meningkatkan hasil belajar IPAS materi Indonesia Kaya Budaya.

title: PENGARUH MODEL PEMBELAJARAN INKUIRI TERBIMBING DENGAN KONTEKS KEARIFAN LOKAL GAMELAN TERHADAP KEMAMPUAN BERPIKIR KRITIS
container-title: SCIENCE : Jurnal Inovasi Pendidikan Matematika dan IPA
12665ee8de5cde498ec1b64504a66456eece13e9.abstract: This study was initiated by the low mathematical critical thinking skills of fourth-grade students at SD 2 Gondangmanis. This condition was evidenced by preliminary data showing that 55% of the students had not achieved the minimum passing grade. In addition to the insufficient scores, the students also appeared passive during the classroom learning process. They generally only memorized problem-solving steps without truly understanding the core concepts required to solve the problems. This study implemented the guided inquiry learning model. This learning model was integrated with local wisdom, specifically the traditional gamelan art, to make it more engaging for the students. The primary objective was to determine whether there was a significant effect of this new learning approach on student progress. Additionally, this study aimed to measure the extent of the learning model's influence on the critical thinking skills of fourth-grade students at SD 2 Gondangmanis. This study utilized a quantitative experimental method by testing a single group within a class before and after the lessons were conducted. Since the total number of fourth-grade students at the school was only 22, all students were included as research subjects. Data were collected through interviews, written tests in the form of higher-order problem-solving questions, and documentation. Data processing was conducted using simple linear regression analysis. The results of the study indicate that the implementation of the guided inquiry learning model contextualized with the local wisdom of gamelan arts has a significant effect on the critical thinking skills of fourth-grade students at SD 2 Gondangmanis. Based on the hypothesis testing analysis using the partial t-test, a significance value of 0.031 (Sig. < 0.05) was obtained, proving a tangible impact of the learning model's implementation on the students' cognitive abilities. Furthermore, the coefficient of determination (R Square) analysis revealed that student activities during the learning process contributed 21.1% to the variance in their critical thinking skills ABSTRAK Penelitian ini didasari oleh rendahnya kemampuan berpikir kritis matematika pada peserta didik kelas IV di SD 2 Gondangmanis. Kondisi tersebut dibuktikan oleh data awal yang menunjukkan bahwa 55% murid belum mencapai batas nilai kelulusan. Selain nilainya masih kurang, peserta didik juga terlihat pasif saat mengikuti proses belajar di dalam kelas. Mereka biasanya hanya menghafalkan langkah-langkah pengerjaan soal tanpa benar-benar memahami konsep dasar untuk memecahkan masalah tersebut. Penelitian ini akan menerapkan model pembelajaran inkuiri terbimbing. Model pembelajaran tersebut akan dikaitkan dengan unsur kearifan lokal berupa kearifan lokal gamelan agar lebih menarik bagi peserta didik. Tujuan utamanya adalah untuk melihat apakah ada pengaruh yang nyata dari cara belajar baru ini terhadap kemajuan peserta didik. Selain itu, penelitian ini juga bertujuan untuk mengukur seberapa besar pengaruh pembelajaran tersebut terhadap kemampuan berpikir kritis peserta didik kelas IV SD 2 Gondangmanis. Penelitian ini menggunakan metode kuantitatif eksperimen dengan menguji satu kelompok dalam satu kelas sebelum dan sesudah diberikan pelajaran. Karena jumlah peserta didik kelas IV di sekolah tersebut hanya 22 orang, maka seluruh peserta didik diikutsertakan sebagai subjek penelitian. Data penelitian akan dikumpulkan melalui proses wawancara, tes tertulis berupa soal pemecahan masalah tingkat tinggi, dan dokumentasi. Pengolahan data menggunakan uji linieritas regresi sederhana. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa penerapan model pembelajaran inkuiri terbimbing berkonteks kearifan lokal kesenian gamelan memberikan pengaruh yang signifikan terhadap kemampuan berpikir kritis siswa kelas IV di SD 2 Gondangmanis. Berdasarkan analisis pengujian hipotesis melalui uji t-parsial, diperoleh nilai signifikansi sebesar 0,031 (Sig. < 0,05) yang membuktikan adanya pengaruh nyata dari implementasi model pembelajaran tersebut terhadap kognitif siswa. Analisis koefisien determinasi (R Square) lebih lanjut mengungkapkan bahwa aktivitas siswa selama pembelajaran memberikan kontribusi sebesar 21,1% terhadap variasi kemampuan berpikir kritis mereka.

title: One source, two targets
container-title: Studies in Language
feba0b193f9f5d4af385a83fd9a31d2d97e473bf.abstract: Abstract The paper addresses the phenomenon of polygrammaticalization based on data from Udi, a lesser-studied language of the Nakh-Daghestanian family. In Udi, two function words sal and saal share the same source structure and represent combinations of the numeral ‘one’ with the additive clitic ‘also, even’. Synchronically, the two words are both formally and functionally distinct: whereas sal is an emphatic negative polarity item ‘(not) a single one’, ‘(not) at all’, saal can be used with the meaning ‘again, one more time’, but is more often found as a coordinating conjunction ‘and’. Considering both modern and diachronic data, I discuss the uses of sal and saal , and the structural and functional parallels of the two Udi words in other languages of the Eastern Caucasus and adjacent areas. The findings highlight the importance of a constructional perspective on grammaticalization, and stress the need to take into account both genealogical and areal factors.

title: Beyond social facilitation and inhibition: Experimenter presence regulates executive function engagement in children
container-title: Child Development
b3fd4a4bc1bcd35ed1b9e8e76a7067f679836118.abstract: Abstract Executive function (EF) performance, which is often treated as an index of children's endogenous self-regulatory capacity, is assumed to be independent of immediate context. However, EF is typically assessed in the presence of an experimenter, and little is known about how this presence shapes performance. We examined the developmental trajectory of experimenter presence effects on children's EF and their modulation by working memory demands. French children aged 4–8 years (N = 54, 17 boys, 37 girls, majority White and upper-middle SES) completed a Go/no-Go task in which working memory load was orthogonally manipulated, both in the presence and absence of the experimenter. Children were slower and made fewer errors when the experimenter was present. Exploratory order analyses showed that these effects were stronger when the experimenter presence condition was completed first, particularly among younger children. Subsequent drift diffusion modeling indicated that the order-dependent effects of experimenter presence were associated with increased nondecision time, with modest evidence and little evidence for changes in evidence accumulation and response caution, respectively. Together, these findings demonstrate that children's EF performance in a canonical task is shaped by their immediate social context.

title: Management of Certain Goods and Services Tax Collection (PBJT) by the Regional Tax and Retribution Management Agency of Bungo District in Increase Regional Original Revenue
container-title: Jurnal Riset Akuntansi
6352e0b4113a81a7e84f61b73476719c79dc619f.abstract: This study aims to analyze the management of Certain Goods and Services Tax (PBJT) collection by the Regional Tax and Retribution Management Agency of Bungo Regency, specifically for hotel services and arts and entertainment services, in increasing Regional Original Income (PAD). The research approach uses a qualitative case study method with data collection through observation, in-depth interviews, and documentation, as well as analysis using Nvivo 15 software. The results of the study indicate that the management of PBJT collection has not been running optimally, as seen from the low contribution of revenue to PAD, the continued use of conventional collection methods, incomplete data collection of taxpayer objects, and weak supervision that opens up opportunities for tax avoidance and fraud. The study also found a number of inhibiting factors, such as minimal use of technology, lack of internal coordination, and limited resources. Meanwhile, supporting factors include clear regulations, local government commitment, and the availability of basic tax data. This study provides strategic recommendations to improve the effectiveness of PBJT collection in order to strengthen Bungo Regency's PAD in a sustainable manner.

title: Assessing industrial process innovation: development and application of a multidimensional composite model
container-title: International Journal of Innovation Science
56d2bbc0ad6b40d339515f4504cd0c93ffc9c0a1.abstract: Purpose This study aims to develop and apply the multidimensional industrial process innovation composite model (MIPICM) as a reproducible formative composite and examines what can be validly inferred from public project metadata. Design/methodology/approach The CORDIS Industrial Process Innovation Database comprises official Horizon 2020 and Horizon Europe projects. From 56,591 parsed projects, 16,094 met transparent eligibility criteria and 10,000 were selected by deterministic SHA-256 ordering. Frozen dictionaries transform auditable metadata into seven documentary-evidence dimensions. Evaluation includes a blinded 250-record human audit, missingness diagnostics, PCA, VIFs, 10,000-draw Monte Carlo weight sensitivity and cluster robustness. Findings Two independent evaluators achieved 98.76% agreement (κ = 0.963). Against exact human consensus, dictionary precision was 71.67%, recall 33.28% and F1 45.45%, indicating two independent evaluators achieved 98.76% agreement (κ = 0.963). Against exact human consensus, dictionary precision was 71.67%, recall 33.28% and F1 45.45%, indicating conservative retrieval. Weight sensitivity remained high (median rank correlation = 0.984; within-one-quintile agreement = 99.99%). D3 missingness was program- and time-structured, and clustering remained weakly separated and algorithm-dependent. Research limitations/implications Scores measure the intensity of documentary evidence, not realized productivity, overall equipment effectiveness, lead-time or carbon outcomes. External outcome validation and longitudinal evidence remain necessary. Practical implications MIPICM can support transparent screening and portfolio comparison when users retain links to the underlying records and avoid treating the index as a performance league table. Originality/value This study contributes an auditable, missingness-aware formative composite and demonstrates a conservative evaluation strategy for large public innovation-project databases.

title: Extending the developmental niche model to studies of intergenerational co-parenting in China
container-title: Child Development Perspectives
bdcc2d533b4beb2d342f66be8dfed156a01f6dd0.abstract: Abstract Despite the global prevalence of grandparents' involvement in child care, research findings linking specific dimensions of involvement to children's outcomes remain inconsistent. Increasingly, studies on intergenerational co-parenting recognize the coordination between parents and grandparents but often assess the quality of relationships broadly rather than examining the specific settings, practices, and beliefs through which co-parenting unfolds. In this article, the author proposed extending the developmental niche model developed by Super and Harkness as an integrative framework for studying Chinese intergenerational co-parenting families. The model highlights how parents and grandparents jointly construct three interconnected subsystems of children's developmental ecology: physical and social settings, customs of care, and caretakers' psychology. Examining these subsystems and their transactions may clarify how sociocultural change and intergenerational negotiation shape caregiving and children's development.

title: Tracing the semantic development of Hebrew clicks
container-title: Studies in Language
996919577bef2f9ee7c039ecf258f77a6ce764ce.abstract: Abstract This paper describes six functions of clicks in Hebrew interaction, some of which have also been identified in other languages: frame-shifting at discourse unit boundaries; signaling word searches; expressing negative affect; negating statements or implications thereof. Two new functional categories are introduced: marking other-repair (only clicks involving self-repair have been described so far), and indicating ‘oblique responses’, a type of dispreferred response. Clicks in different functions exhibit different degrees of liminality/conventionalization. This, and the considerable overlap between functions, is proposed as evidence for diachronic development over a semantic map, explaining why clicks perform a similar range of functions in unrelated languages around the world.

title: Navigating job demands and resources: a process model of workplace learning and engagement among early career teachers
container-title: Journal of Workplace Learning
9aad5e49cd971a5fd75436056349fa00e5e4f785.abstract: Purpose This study aims to adopt a processual perspective to examine how early career teachers manage job demands and use organisational resources in a learning-intensive environment, exploring how work, learning and engagement manifest in their daily activities. Design/methodology/approach A qualitative, abductive design was used based on 15 semi-structured interviews with early career teachers in a UK Academy Trust. Data were analysed using an iterative thematic approach, combining data-led coding with later-stage theoretical engagement with the job demands–resources (JD–R) framework and workplace-learning perspectives. Findings The analysis identified recurring patterns through which the teachers’ interpreted demands, engaged with organisational cues and reworked the available sources of guidance. Participants consistently understood the demands, and organisational resources were used based on their specific features and their availability. When feedback and organisational signals were limited, teachers engaged in resource substitution, a set of situated practices in which they assembled provisional reference points from alternative guidance sources, including peer interactions, task-related cues and reflections. Originality/value This study contributes a processual account of how demands and resources are used in practice, complementing the established variance-oriented approaches in JD–R literature. By bringing JD–R into dialogue with workplace learning research, this study proposes resource substitution as a contextually situated practice in early career settings.

title: Ombudsman On the Spot as a Proactive Service Model for Expanding Access to Public Service Complaint Mechanisms in Central Java
container-title: Jurnal Pengabdian Hukum Indonesia (Indonesian Journal of Legal Community Engagement) JPHI
e107deb1000f07026c0dbc44875509f94464fddd.abstract: Unequal access to complaint mechanisms may prevent members of the public from obtaining remedies for maladministration when distance, limited information, digital barriers, disability, age, or confidentiality concerns restrict contact with oversight institutions. This article examines Ombudsman On the Spot, implemented by the Central Java Representative Office of the Ombudsman of the Republic of Indonesia, as a proactive complaint access service. Using a descriptive evaluative community engagement approach, the study analyses five internal activity reports covering seven service points from April to September 2025, supported by institutional records, SIMPeL 4.0 administrative data, programme guidelines, and legislation. Across the seven service points, eight non-report consultations and six registered complaints were directly recorded through OTS, together with one recommendation for service improvement. The six registered complaints subsequently received institutional follow-up through examination and/or coordination with the reported institutions and were administratively closed. These are administrative outputs, not evidence of user satisfaction or causal effects. The findings identify three complementary modalities: facility-based service booths, community education and consultation, and targeted visits for users requiring accessibility or confidentiality adjustments. They also identify four dimensions of access: physical, informational, procedural, and relational. The article develops a six-stage framework consisting of access mapping, targeted outreach, rights education, consultation and preliminary verification, registration, referral or coordination, and monitoring and evaluation. Four stages are practice-derived, while two are normatively completed by the 2025 programme guideline. The framework offers a replicable structure for proactive complaint access while retaining privacy safeguards and cautious limits on claims of effectiveness.

title: Emotional Roller Coaster: Phenomenological Lived Experiences of EFL Students’ Emotional Reminiscence and Trajectory in Writing Class
container-title: IJELTAL (Indonesian Journal of English Language Teaching and Applied Linguistics)
2a8b12b5d9f9e4e8a56b436517db2f39b95b790a.abstract: Indonesian EFL university students experiencing as well as regulating emotions in EFL writing tasks are the topic of this phenomenological study. Although language education traditionally highlights cognitive and linguistic aspects, the emotional struggle in EFL writing e.g., anxiety, frustration, and burnout, has received less attention, partly because this work might not translate in non-Western contexts and because cultural attitudes to emotion expression or emotion regulation might vary. Using reflective journals, which consisted of two stages, i.e., pre- or before writing and during or drafting process, seven Indonesian students from different academic levels reported negative emotional reactions at the beginning of writing, emotional fluctuation from negative to positive, positive to negative, negative to positive like an emotional roller coaster, and direct emotional alteration from negative to positive during the drafting process. Furthermore, there were efforts done by students to solve their negative emotional experiences indicated after the students expressed their emotional experiences. Therefore, this implies that further research on students’ emotion regulation strategies has potential to be explored in the future. Sequential instructions, from the simple to complex task is recommended to by apply in the teaching and learning of writing since it will also have direct effect on the students’ emotions.

title: From Punitive to Supportive: Exploring the Role of Positive Reinforcement in Student Engagement among Junior High School Students
container-title: IJELTAL (Indonesian Journal of English Language Teaching and Applied Linguistics)
9d3aef5440a656abc88eab3dd9ee3bd90d5306f7.abstract: In many educational contexts, classroom disciplinary practices are often dominated by punitive approaches, in which mistakes are responded to criticism or punishment in the name of maintaining order and discipline. Such practices may discourage participation, reduce students’ confidence, and limit meaningful engagement, particularly in English as a Foreign Language (EFL) learning where students are already vulnerable to anxiety and fear of making mistakes. However, alternative approaches that emphasize support rather than punishment remain underexplored, especially in relation to their broader impact on classroom dynamics. Grounded in Behaviourist theory by Skinner, this study investigates whether and how Positive Reinforcement enhances student engagement in EFL classrooms. A sequential explanatory mixed-method design was employed involving 105 junior high school students in Indonesia. Quantitative data were collected through pre- and post-surveys, followed by qualitative interviews with five students to further explain the statistical findings. The quantitative results showed a statistically significant improvement in students’ engagement (p < .001) after the implementation of Positive Reinforcement, with a large effect size (r = 0.86), indicating a strong practical impact. The qualitative findings further revealed improvements in five major areas: (1) behavioural engagement, (2) cognitive engagement, (3) emotional safety and confidence, (4) peer interaction and communication, and (5) student-teacher relationships. These findings suggest that shifting from punitive to supportive practices not only enhances individual student engagement but also contributes to the development of more positive and supportive classroom dynamics in EFL learning environments.

title: Use my language, use my pronouns: Queer approaches to linguistic justice for inclusive language policies
container-title: Ethnicities
2c91a285c3c566f537fc92fe24cdf8f75a4f2ffa.abstract: The linguistic environment of any given country, region, or city is fluid: minoritised, migrant, heritage and Indigenous languages defeat the dichotomy of ‘one nation, one language’ and challenge the hierarchies of power behind monolingualism. At the same time, gender identity also refuses binarity: similarly to language, the way people experience and express their gender identity is much more diverse, with new linguistic avenues being opened to represent the lived experience of genderqueer and trans people. This article adopts nonbinarity as an intrasemantic approach, grounded in postcolonial and queer theory, to reflect on the complexity of linguistic and gender identity. Drawing from trans linguistics, I argue that gender-fair and trans language is a quintessential part of linguistic justice as a practice of social justice and thus that “queer linguistic justice” advocates for an inclusive avenue for language policies incorporating a holistic view of the languagers.

title: Expertise modifies neural responses to causal inference during language comprehension
84c0ad5dd47f83758b91f143be5e8b50743682ac.abstract: Abstract Linguistic communication relies on shared common ground, yet different individuals in a community have specialized semantic knowledge. As a key example, physicians acquire rich knowledge about the causes of illness. An open question is whether such “causal expertise” influences the neural basis of language comprehension. Here we tested the hypothesis that when understanding everyday language like, “Holly used a grimy faucet during her overseas plane ride. Now she has the stomach flu,” medical experts retrieve richer representations in semantic networks of the brain. Physicians (n=16) and age- and education-matched controls (n=16) undergoing fMRI read two-sentence vignettes that elicited implicit causal inferences about illness or object mechanics as well as control vignettes that did not elicit causal inferences. Vignettes were linguistically matched across conditions and were accessible to experts and non-experts alike. Across both groups, causal vignettes about illness engaged a temporoparietal semantic network previously implicated in thinking about animates, i.e., people and animals (precuneus and left temporoparietal junction), whereas causal vignettes about object mechanics engaged a semantic network associated with places and objects. Critically, physicians’ responses in the animacy network were more robust and self-similar, suggesting the activation of richer semantic knowledge. Medical expertise effects were specific to biological inferences rather than mechanical or mental state inferences. By contrast, individually localized frontotemporal language and frontoparietal reasoning networks did not respond preferentially to causally connected sentences or show effects of expertise. Our findings suggest that causal expertise alters neural responses to causal inferences that unfold automatically during language comprehension. Significance statement Shared knowledge is necessary for communication, but what we know about the world varies significantly across individuals. Medical expertise offers a classic example. Relative to other people, medical experts develop a richer understanding of what causes illness. Here we asked whether becoming a “causal expert” alters neural responses during language comprehension. We find that physicians show enhanced responses to causal inferences about illness elicited by language. This expertise effect is specific to semantic networks of the brain that represent knowledge about animate entities, such as people and animals. Our findings suggest that content-specific semantic networks enable causal inferences during language comprehension and are modified by causal expertise, offering new insight into how conceptual variation shapes the neural basis of language.

title: Technical note: Benefits of Bayesian estimation of model parameters in a large hydrological model ensemble
container-title: Hydrology and Earth System Sciences
d65e939c30b234a6031fbdbd492a3983c2f0da1c.abstract: Quantifying and mitigating parametric and structural uncertainties in hydrological models are crucial to accurately understand and predict the rainfall-runoff process. Despite recent advances in Bayesian approaches for quantifying structural uncertainty using very large hydrological model ensembles, the simultaneous quantification of both parametric and structural uncertainties has yet to be implemented since previous works on large model ensembles have relied on deterministic optimization of parameters. Here we present the potential benefits of Bayesian estimation of parametric uncertainty within a large hydrological model ensemble. We find that Bayesian estimation of model parameters (more generally, change in calibration methods) potentially influences the interpretation of model comparisons. Specifically, Bayesian parametric uncertainty quantification greatly benefits complex models with many parameters, thereby affecting discussions of the appropriate level of model complexity. We also find that Bayesian parametric uncertainty quantification does not substantially improve multi-model hydrological predictions. The adverse effects of parameter misspecification in individual models are effectively mitigated by combining models with diverse structures. Thus, the high computational cost of Bayesian parameter estimation is not paid for to improve rainfall-runoff analysis in a large hydrological model ensemble.

title: Model Pedagogi Al-Fatihah: Karakteristik Pendidik dan Peserta Didik Perspektif Al-Qur'an dalam Pendidikan Nasional Indonesia
container-title: Continuous Education: Journal of Science and Research
cd4bb1125610a688daa407f091a26f3a7c77d99d.abstract: Indonesian national education continues to face challenges in strengthening students' character, moral integrity, and spirituality, highlighting the need for an educational paradigm rooted in Qur'anic values. This study aims to analyze the characteristics of educators and learners from the Qur'anic perspective through a pedagogical interpretation of Surah Al-Fatihah and to examine its relevance to Indonesian national education. The study employed a qualitative approach using library research and the tafsir tarbawi method. Data were collected from the Qur'an, classical and contemporary Qur'anic commentaries, Islamic education literature, scholarly articles, and national education policy documents. Data were analyzed through reduction, categorization, interpretation, and conceptual synthesis. The findings reveal that Surah Al-Fatihah presents the ideal characteristics of educators as murabbi, humanistic, empathetic, and just and accountable, while learners are characterized as spiritual learners, humble learners, lifelong learners, and reflective learners. Based on these findings, this study proposes the Al-Fatihah Pedagogical Model, which integrates the characteristics of educators and learners into a Qur'anic pedagogical framework. The model is relevant to the goals of Indonesian national education and provides a conceptual contribution to the development of character education grounded in Qur'anic values.

title: Initial Placement for Fruchterman--Reingold Force Model With Coordinate Newton Direction
container-title: Journal of Graph Algorithms and Applications
05249485ae1fb691cc362a32286ea4145f81eceb.abstract: The Fruchterman--Reingold (FR) force model is widely used in force-directed graph drawing, and multilevel approaches such as sfdp in Graphviz scale these methods effectively. A crucial step in multilevel schemes is refinement, which improves the graph layout typically performed with the FR algorithm. For this refinement, optimization-based methods, such as L-BFGS, often yield better layouts by exploiting past gradient information. However, they suffer from high per-iteration costs for large graphs and difficulty in handling highly twisted graphs. In this research, we propose a new initial placement based on the stochastic coordinate descent to accelerate the optimization process. We first reformulate the problem as a discrete optimization problem using a hexagonal lattice and then iteratively update a randomly selected vertex along the coordinate Newton direction with low per-iteration costs. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our method through numerical experiments, showing that our initial placement leads to faster convergence and higher-quality layouts compared to naive optimization approaches. We also discuss how the coordinate Newton direction can be applied to other graph-related problems from an optimization perspective.

title: Eco-anxiety as a public health imperative: from individual resilience to culturally informed holistic engagement
container-title: Frontiers in Public Health
09af3166959fd55233b95173cffbaf62e6f0c7b9.abstract: Eco-anxiety has increasingly drawn public health attention. Although often conceptualized as an individual psychological burden, eco-anxiety may also serve as a catalyst for collective action. However, prevailing coping strategies largely center on individual resilience, with insufficient focus on social connectedness and the human-nature bond. This narrative review critically examines the limitations of individual resilience as a coping mechanism for eco-anxiety and advocates for a paradigm shift toward holistic engagement informed by Indigenous knowledge systems and traditional Chinese philosophy. Evidence indicates that eco-anxiety disproportionately affects vulnerable populations, including Indigenous groups, women, and youth; yet most research remains Western-centric and individually oriented. While beneficial for personal mental health, individual resilience often overlooks the systemic and sociopolitical drivers of ecological distress, potentially intensifying feelings of isolation and helplessness. In contrast, holistic engagement emphasizes reciprocal human-nature relationships, social connectivity, and collective action, offering more enduring coping mechanisms. Addressing eco-anxiety as a public health issue requires moving beyond individual resilience toward culturally attuned, holistic, and collective strategies. Integrating Indigenous and Chinese philosophical insights into mental health interventions may promote environmental stewardship, social cohesion, and emotional wellbeing, particularly for vulnerable populations disproportionately affected by ecological crises.

title: Pengaruh Model Pembelajaran Discovery Learning Menggunakan Padlet terhadap Literasi Digital pada Mata Pelajaran Informatika Kelas VIII SMP Negeri 19 Padang
container-title: Jurnal QOSIM : Jurnal Pendidikan Sosial & Humaniora
14c03194d70b6c4a0abe0c9b55cff10dd48541fa.abstract: Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mengetahui pengaruh model pembelajaran Discovery Learning menggunakan Padlet terhadap literasi digital peserta didik pada mata pelajaran Informatika, khususnya pada materi Dampak Sosial Informatika, di SMPN 19 Padang. Penelitian ini dilatarbelakangi oleh hasil observasi awal yang menunjukkan bahwa pembelajaran masih berpusat pada guru, peserta didik cenderung pasif dan jarang bertanya atau menyampaikan pendapat, serta modul ajar mencantumkan media digital yang tidak dioperasikan dalam pembelajaran. Penelitian ini menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif dengan kuasi-eksperimen desain Nonequivalent Control Group Design, yang membandingkan kelas eksperimen yang belajar menggunakan model Discovery Learning berbantuan Padlet dengan kelas kontrol yang belajar menggunakan model Direct Instruction. Sampel ditentukan melalui teknik purposive sampling, sehingga diperoleh kelas VIII-5 sebagai kelas eksperimen (32 peserta didik) dan kelas VIII-4 sebagai kelas kontrol (32 peserta didik). Pengumpulan data dilakukan melalui angket literasi digital berskala Likert sebanyak 10 butir yang mencakup dimensi teknis, kognitif, dan sosial-emosional (Ng, 2012), dengan reliabilitas yang mengacu pada penelitian terdahulu (α = 0,869–0,898), diberikan sebelum dan sesudah perlakuan, lalu dianalisis menggunakan uji normalitas Shapiro-Wilk, uji homogenitas Levene, dan Independent Samples t-Test. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa kelas eksperimen memperoleh rata-rata skor posttest 39,47 (tertinggi 46, terendah 33), lebih tinggi dibandingkan kelas kontrol dengan rata-rata 36,03 (tertinggi 41, terendah 31). Kedua data berdistribusi normal (Sig. 0,261–0,686) dan homogen (Sig. 0,560 dan 0,719), serta uji t menghasilkan t hitung sebesar 4,708 yang lebih besar dari t tabel sebesar 1,999 dengan Sig. (2-tailed) < 0,001 < 0,05 dan ukuran efek besar (Cohen’s d = 1,18). Peningkatan terutama terjadi pada dimensi teknis dan kognitif, sedangkan dimensi sosial-emosional meningkat tipis pada kedua kelas. Dengan demikian, model Discovery Learning menggunakan Padlet berpengaruh signifikan terhadap literasi digital peserta didik pada pembelajaran Informatika dan dapat dijadikan alternatif strategi pembelajaran yang berpusat pada peserta didik dengan dukungan media digital interaktif.

title: Pengaruh Knowledge Sharing terhadap Innovative Work Behavior pada Santri Pengabdian di MA Al Irsyad Tengaran dengan Employee Engagement Sebagai Variabel Mediasi
container-title: Jurnal QOSIM : Jurnal Pendidikan Sosial & Humaniora
7243ea6bdf0e5caa1cc728447aa5367bd56b2a61.abstract: Penelitian ini menguji pengaruh Knowledge Sharing terhadap Innovative Work Behavior santri pengabdian di MA Al Irsyad Tengaran, baik secara langsung maupun melalui Employee Engagement sebagai variabel mediasi. Kerangka analisis bertumpu pada Job Demands-Resources Theory dan Social Exchange Theory. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif eksplanatori dengan teknik sampling jenuh terhadap seluruh populasi sebanyak 50 santri pengabdian, yang seluruhnya laki-laki, berusia di bawah 25 tahun, berpendidikan lulusan SMA, dan memiliki masa pengabdian kurang dari satu tahun. Data dianalisis menggunakan Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) melalui evaluasi model pengukuran, evaluasi model struktural, pengujian hipotesis dengan bootstrapping, dan pengujian efek mediasi. Hipotesis yang diuji meliputi pengaruh knowledge sharing terhadap employee engagement, pengaruh employee engagement terhadap IWB, pengaruh langsung knowledge sharing terhadap IWB, serta peran mediasi employee engagement. Hasil penelitian diharapkan memberikan kontribusi teoretis pada kajian manajemen sumber daya manusia dan implikasi praktis bagi pimpinan dalam membangun budaya berbagi pengetahuan untuk mendorong perilaku inovatif.

title: Training-corpus overlap and evaluation protocol constrain measured gains in a fine-tuned clinical language model
container-title: Scientific Reports
694d39eafb8ce1c284f275436f36a9f758f74d35.abstract: Abstract Fine-tuned medical language models are frequently assessed using public question-answering benchmarks, which may overlap with their training data. We re-evaluated an 8.2-billion-parameter QLoRA fine-tune of Qwen3-8B under a fixed generative chain-of-thought harness and compared eight benchmarks against its 97,041-item fine-tuning corpus using 13-gram, exact-stem and longest-common-subsequence matching. Exact-stem overlap exceeded 70% for PubMedQA, MedQA and MMLU Professional Medicine, making those scores unsuitable for capability claims, while MedMCQA, evaluated on a held-out split, was effectively unflagged. On several overlapping benchmarks the unmodified parent checkpoint matched or exceeded the fine-tune, significantly so on MedQA. On the 1,838 MedXpertQA items not flagged by exact-stem matching, the fine-tune scored 20.8% against 15.6% for its parent, a paired gain of 5.2 percentage points (McNemar exact P = 7.9 × 10⁻⁷), against an originally reported 7.1. A bundled ablation, in which reasoning traces, sampling weights, curriculum staging, token exposure and output-format supervision differed simultaneously, preserved approximately 70% of the observed improvement. The remaining 1.6-point difference was not statistically significant ( P = 0.175) and cannot be attributed to any single component. The evaluation protocol and the overlap of the training corpus limit the scope of measurable outcomes in these benchmarks.

title: Exploring the Relationships Between Auditory Processing, Language, Cognitive, and Speech-in-Noise Abilities in School-Aged Children
container-title: Ear & Hearing
b2bbc5e2c8343f5ecda5c388fc13eada6672f977.abstract: Objectives: Understanding speech in noise and reverberation requires the integration of auditory, language, and cognitive abilities. Many children experience listening difficulties in such environments which, if persistent, can affect long-term academic outcomes. However, relative contributions of underlying processes remain poorly understood. This study investigated how nonspeech auditory processing, language and cognitive abilities contribute to phoneme identification and sentence understanding in noise in a representative sample of school-aged children. Design: The study included 221 primary school children aged 6 to 11 yr (88 boys, 133 girls), all with normal peripheral hearing. Participants completed measures of nonspeech auditory processing, phoneme identification, and sentence understanding in noise and reverberation, as well as language ability, attention, nonverbal intelligence, and memory. Using structural equation modeling enabled us to consider the influence of multiple predictors simultaneously. Results: A complex pattern of relationships emerged. Bottom-up nonspeech auditory processing supported phoneme identification, which in turn supported sentence understanding in noise. Language ability had a direct top-down influence on sentence understanding. Memory and intelligence contributed indirectly through their influence on language. Minimal associations were observed between cognition and nonspeech auditory processing, supporting a conceptual distinction between auditory and higher-level processes. Conclusions: The results show that bottom-up and top-down abilities make distinct contributions to listening and identify direct and indirect pathways underlying children’s listening in adverse conditions. Auditory processing contributed to phoneme perception, which in turn supported sentence understanding in noise. Language abilities exerted a strong independent influence to sentence understanding in noise, while nonverbal intelligence and memory affected performance only indirectly through language.

title: Bearing Remaining Useful Life Prediction and Maintenance Decision Support Using a Large Language Model
container-title: Applied Sciences
e090ff2403da079aeeb7af46459bc990896b2bb0.abstract: Bearing remaining useful life (RUL) estimates require causal inputs and temporal consistency before supporting maintenance. This study develops a large language model (LLM)-assisted pipeline connecting online degradation evidence, prediction applicability, structured state output, and maintenance rules. Historical vibration evidence is used to construct a health indicator and determine the domain in which RUL prediction is applicable. The LLM then generates health stages and RUL predictions, with direct token and regression head methods compared for numerical RUL prediction. A causal median filter and monotonic temporal projection are subsequently applied, and deterministic risk rules are used to generate maintenance recommendations. Direct token and regression head readouts are evaluated separately; only the regression head path supplies nonincreasing temporal processing and the frozen risk mapping. Five bearing disjoint folds cover 15 XJTU-SY bearings and 9216 observations. Seven numerical baselines are evaluated on validation and test data. In the seed-42 test, long short-term memory achieves the lowest sample-pooled mean absolute error (MAE), 0.134, while direct token achieves the lowest bearing-equal MAE, 0.174. The regression head’s validation advantage over direct token is not retained. Across three LLM seeds, temporal processing reduces mean overestimation proportions by 35.762% and 55.666%. The primary rule reaches high on 12 bearings. Complete LLM inference takes a median 10.744 s per observation at batch one on an RTX 3090. The framework makes prediction and rule trade-offs traceable through a common structured interface. Its cross-bearing evidence supports conservative temporal processing and explicit inspection rules, while compact models retain important accuracy and computational advantages.

title: Effects of Intermittent Theta-Burst Stimulation over the Left Dorsolateral Prefrontal Cortex on Executive Function During Sustained Simulated Flight Operations: A Randomized Crossover Study Using a Flight–Cognitive Dual-Task Paradigm
container-title: Bioengineering
650e5a5940124e8eb202662f1b08dd2cb3a024fd.abstract: Sustained flight operation load may compromise executive control in complex human–machine interaction environments. Intermittent theta-burst stimulation (iTBS) over the left dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (DLPFC) holds potential for modulating executive function, yet its effects on different executive components under sustained operational load remain unclear. This study employed a randomized, balanced, within-subject crossover design, enrolling 25 healthy male participants. Each participant completed three intervention conditions: Active iTBS, Sham iTBS, and No-stimulation. Each experimental session consisted of stimulation delivery, a 60-min cruising simulated flight, and a 30-min flight–cognitive dual-task phase. Primary outcomes were behavioral performance on the Go/No-Go, 3-back, and number-rule switching tasks; EEG microstates and prefrontal relative oxygenated hemoglobin (HbO) changes during the dual-task phase served as exploratory neurophysiological indices. Results showed that condition differences were concentrated in working memory updating and rule switching: compared with No-stimulation, Active iTBS shortened 3-back reaction time and reduced switch cost; compared with both No-stimulation and Sham iTBS, Active iTBS improved 3-back accuracy and number-rule switching accuracy; the switch-cost difference between Active and Sham iTBS did not reach significance (pBonferroni = 0.055). No significant condition effect was observed for the Go/No-Go task. EEG microstate analysis revealed task-specific changes: under the Active iTBS condition, the occurrence rate and temporal coverage of microstate D increased during the 3-back task; temporal coverage of microstate D increased during the number-rule switching task; no significant microstate changes were observed during the Go/No-Go task. Exploratory fNIRS analysis indicated that left-hemisphere and all-channel prefrontal HbO under Active iTBS was higher than under Sham iTBS in planned pairwise comparisons (pBonferroni < 0.03), but the corresponding condition main effects (p ≥ 0.065) and condition × hemisphere interaction (p = 0.919) were non-significant, and channel-level effects did not survive multiple-comparison correction. These findings suggest that, within the flight–cognitive dual-task paradigm, Active iTBS over the left DLPFC is associated with improvements in working memory and rule switching performance, accompanied by changes in microstate temporal organization during certain tasks. The microstate and fNIRS results provide exploratory neurophysiological observations and cannot establish causal relationships with the behavioral improvements.

title: A Verifiable Agentic Framework for Sequential Multimodal Prediction of Mild Cognitive Impairment Progression
container-title: Bioengineering
8d08380a0ed180432ed111d94da0148d50eb7ea4.abstract: Multimodal models can predict progression from mild cognitive impairment (MCI) to Alzheimer’s disease (AD), but most evaluations assume that every modality is immediately available. We developed a retrospective framework using only the Alzheimer’s Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI) that separates statistical risk estimation, sequential evidence acquisition, language-model explanation, and deterministic verification. Participants with baseline MCI were assigned state-specific landmarks using information visible within a +/−90-day window. The primary simulation cohort included 425 participants with clinical/cognitive, magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-derived, and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) evidence; 153 converted to AD within 36 months after the landmark. Calibrated elastic-net models were evaluated with 10 repeated nested five-fold cross-validation. In the common-landmark cohort, adding MRI-derived and CSF features improved the Brier score from 0.158 (95% confidence interval (CI) 0.141–0.175) to 0.138 (0.122–0.155) and the area under the receiver-operating characteristic curve (AUROC) from 0.837 (0.802–0.871) to 0.878 (0.847–0.908). A sequential policy used cross-fitted estimates of individual Brier-score gain to decide whether to request MRI or CSF. The fixed-threshold exploratory analysis requested 40.6% fewer simulated tests than an all-tests policy while meeting the prespecified Brier and AUROC noninferiority margins. Under fully nested threshold selection, the policy requested 46.9% fewer tests and met the AUROC criterion, while narrowly missing the Brier criterion (difference 0.00546, 95% CI 0.00090–0.01003; margin +0.01). In a 40-card-per-model engineering audit, local Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-8B models copied probabilities and cited supplied evidence correctly in 40/40 cards but matched the deterministic action in 16/40 and 15/40 cards, respectively. Execution authority therefore remained with the deterministic policy. Here, agentic refers to the orchestration of modular evidence states, policy checks, verification, and explanation; it does not imply autonomous language-model control. As a retrospective simulation, the framework does not establish prospective clinical utility, real-world cost savings, or external computational reproducibility.

title: Electrophysiological Evidence of Cognitive Dysfunction After tSAH: An ERP Study Based on Three Different Stimulation Paradigms
container-title: Brain Sciences
9c1f28aac38dfb37542d762505b948d39fe676e9.abstract: Objectives: This study aims to investigate the characteristics of event-related potentials (ERP) in patients with traumatic subarachnoid hemorrhage (tSAH) during the clinical stable phase, with the aim of obtaining neuroelectrophysiological indicators that can objectively assess cognitive dysfunction caused by this injury. Methods: A total of 16 healthy volunteers and 33 tSAH patients in the stable phase were recruited. Demographic and clinical data were collected, MMSE assessments were completed, and EEG data for P300, mismatch negativity (MMN), and contingent negative variation (CNV) were recorded using a 32-lead ERP system. ERP analysis was performed by comparing the tSAH group with the healthy control (HC) group and by further dividing the tSAH group into a cognitive impairment subgroup (CI, n = 18) and a normal cognition subgroup (NC, n = 15) based on MMSE scores, with a focus on the mean amplitude and peak latency within specific time windows and their correlation with cognitive behavioral measures. Results: The results showed no significant differences in demographic characteristics between the two groups, while the MMSE scores of the tSAH group were significantly lower than those of the HC group. Compared with HC, the mean amplitude of P300 in response to the target stimuli was significantly reduced in multiple brain regions in the tSAH group and attenuated the negativity of mean CNV amplitudes across multiple brain regions, while no significant differences in mean MMN amplitudes were detected across electrodes and no significant differences were observed in peak latencies of P300 and MMN. The CI group was slightly older than the NC group; after controlling for the effect of age, the Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) scores of the CI group were significantly lower than those of the NC group, but no significant differences were found between the two groups in mean amplitudes and peak latencies of P300 and MMN or in mean CNV amplitudes. Conclusions: This study indicates that tSAH may be one of the relevant risk factors for post-traumatic cognitive dysfunction. ERP findings suggest that the allocation of relevant cognitive resources is attenuated in this population, but no differences were detected in the temporal sequence of neural processing. No significant abnormalities were observed during auditory deviance detection corresponding to the MMN time window, and no significant differences in ERP characteristics were found among the subgroups. This study found that tSAH can cause selective cognitive electrophysiological impairment, but ERP electrophysiological changes do not fully match cognitive impairment classified based on clinical scales.

title: Objective Ground Motion Model Selection and Ranking Using Likelihood and Bayesian Criteria: A Case Study for Türkiye
container-title: GeoHazards
37c4c169e68d8c37d02c9d67287651595ee6978c.abstract: Ground motion models (GMMs) constitute a fundamental component of the probabilistic seismic hazard analysis (PSHA) framework and represent one of the primary sources of epistemic uncertainty in seismic hazard estimates. This uncertainty largely stems from the availability of multiple candidate GMMs, with varying performance across different ground motion databases. The logic-tree framework is a well-established method for addressing this uncertainty by incorporating multiple GMMs with logic-tree branch weights. However, selecting an appropriate suite of GMMs is a non-trivial task. While often determined by expert judgment, the inherent subjectivity of this process has motivated the development of data-driven ranking methods. This study evaluates parametric and machine-learning-based GMMs for Türkiye using two information-theoretic ranking methods: the log-likelihood (LLH) and the deviance information criterion (DIC). The analysis uses an updated Turkish strong-motion database comprising 12,160 recordings from 1976 to 2023, including observations from the 2023 earthquakes. The DIC framework employs Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) sampling to estimate the posterior distribution of the total residual standard deviation while keeping the median prediction functions and regression coefficients fixed. Ranking stability is further investigated across magnitude ranges and event-based subsets, alongside sensitivity of DIC to prior distributions.

title: Characterization of Pathogenic Features of Dengue Virus Serotypes 1–4 in the AG129 Mouse Model
container-title: Viruses
2374eba11600ec2d3712ff727789833cb533fe10.abstract: An AG129 mouse infection model with four DENV isolates was established to systematically characterize the early pathogenic phenotypes of these strains. DENV-1 caused 100% mortality by 15 dpi, with sustained viremia, widespread multi-organ injury, and persistent leukopenia. DENV-4 exhibited peak viremia at 4 dpi and unique neurovirulence, presenting exclusive hind-limb paralysis, severe pulmonary hemorrhage, and characteristic cerebral parenchymal lesions. DENV-2 and DENV-3 induced only transient mild viremia and focal tissue alterations without mortality. Hematological and biochemical alterations, as well as occasional splenic hemosiderin deposition, were noted among infected animals. This preclinical dataset offers insights into serotype-specific DENV pathogenesis and may aid future evaluation of broad-spectrum antivirals and tetravalent vaccine candidates.

title: From post-editing to prompting
container-title: Translation and Translanguaging in Multilingual Contexts
d424fcf44502667e6a60fc58c426437d6562f9b9.abstract: Abstract This study compares traditional translation and post-editing with generative-AI-assisted translation in Arabic–English translation education. Drawing on 68 task records completed by 58 undergraduate students through EduApp, it examines observable effort, textual intervention, and implications for translation competence. The findings indicate that AI-assisted tasks involved significantly more written or entered characters and a higher length ratio, but no statistically significant difference in task completion time. Qualitative analysis suggests a shift from local correction to broader reformulation, including more formal institutional phrasing and syntactic restructuring. The study concludes that AI-assisted translation redistributes rather than eliminates student effort and requires evaluative and interactive skills alongside established translation abilities.

title: Why does dialogue matter in writing studies?
container-title: Language and Dialogue
75e53535bcb5deb4cbfd2f46cc15268aa2a9a1c3.abstract: Abstract This contribution argues that dialogue is not merely a feature of writing but its constitutive condition, and that this dialogic nature is most visible in academic citational practices. Academic writing is seen as an ongoing negotiation among textual voices, in which writers present ideas by positioning themselves within a field of prior utterances. From this perspective, citation functions as a key site where authors converse with prior scholarship, address potential audience reactions, and navigate complex relationships of alignment and critique. The argument is supported by an analysis of expert writing in the field of medicine, showing how writers negotiate, inhabit, and transform the voices of others in the production of knowledge.

title: Navigating policy and practice
container-title: Translation and Translanguaging in Multilingual Contexts
00e1ea42553edfcb1aabfed6f50a699af5ae163b.abstract: Abstract This article delves into how institutional and cultural factors influence translanguaging in Chinese classes at Mali’s Confucius Institute, using Hornberger’s (2002) ecological approach, Bourdieu’s (1991) linguistic capital, and García & Li’s (2014) translanguaging theory. Data from interviews with 20 teachers, document reviews, classroom observations, and a learner questionnaire ( N = 56) reveal a tension: policies favour Chinese-only instruction, yet teachers use informal translanguaging to connect with students. Cultural hierarchies complicate this: French as a “code for cognition,” Bamanankan as a “code for connection,” and local languages remain marginalised. Drawing on systematic observation coding (187 translanguaging events across three classroom sessions) and conversation analysis of representative episodes, the study proposes a Hierarchical Translanguaging Model for CFL to address layered postcolonial hierarchies and design graded language scaffolding, balancing immersion and multilingual support without abandoning core Chinese practice. These insights emphasise the need for policy reforms, improved teacher training, and culturally responsive resources to legitimise translanguaging in CFL.

container-title: RESEARCH JOURNAL OF MASS COMMUNICATION AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY
df6ad02455ba1edb5b534884c2221350b22dd61a.abstract: This study explored the influence of digital literacy skills on the academic engagement of secondary school students in Rivers State, Nigeria. In the Information Age, where digital technologies permeate everyday life, the ability to effectively use these tools is essential for meaningful learning. While students frequently engage with digital devices for communication and entertainment, their capacity to leverage these tools for academic purposes remains a concern. Descriptive survey design was adopted. The population of the study was all public senior secondary school students in Rivers State consisting of 193,436 admitted in 2024/2025 academic session. Sample was 560 public senior secondary students selected using multi-stage sampling. Instruments were Digital Literacy Skills Scale (DLSS) and Academic Engagement Questionnaire (AEQ). Both instruments were validated and showed reliability coefficients of 0.82 and 0.85. Questionnaires were administered with the help of trained assistants and data were collected. Research questions were analyzed using mean, standard deviation while the null hypotheses were tested using simple linear regression and t-tests at 0.05 significance level No significant gender differences were observed in digital literacy, whereas urban students demonstrated significantly higher academic engagement than their rural peers. Regression analysis further showed that digital literacy accounted for 38% of the variance in academic engagement. The findings highlight digital literacy as a key driver of student involvement, motivation, and participation in learning. The study recommends enhanced digital literacy training, improved ICT infrastructure, strategic integration of digital tools into teaching, and targeted support for rural schools to address engagement disparities.

title: Human mitochondrial DNA variants influence telomere length: evidence from a transmitochondrial cybrid model
73284a61817bc53b43b45e94ab9ef773c06c2332.abstract: Telomere shortening is a hallmark of aging, yet telomere length (TL) varies considerably among individuals and is strongly influenced by inheritance. In mice, efficient mitochondrial function-characterized by low reactive oxygen species (ROS) production-is critical for telomere elongation during early embryogenesis. Since mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) encodes several subunits of the electron transport chain, it may influence TL at birth by regulating mitochondrial function in utero. To explore the relationship between mtDNA and TL in human, we used a transmitochondrial cybrid approach, introducing mitochondria from donor platelets with varying telomere lengths into mtDNA-depleted cells. This revealed an inverse correlation between donor blood TL and mitochondrial ROS levels measured in the resulting cybrids, suggesting that specific mtDNA variants may contribute to the maintenance of long telomeres in humans by enhancing mitochondrial fitness. During in vitro cybrid formation, a transient phase of oxidative stress precedes cellular adaptation. In this specific window, mtDNA variants associated with reduced complex I (CI) activity induced rapid telomere shortening—an effect rescued by antioxidant and NAD⁺ precursor supplementation. While these variants occur naturally in certain individuals with long telomeres, our data suggest that, at least under in vitro conditions of acute oxidative stress, CI is critical to support PARP1 activity by maintaining the NAD⁺/NADH balance, thereby preserving telomere integrity. Collectively, these findings solidify the link between mtDNA variants and human TL regulation, highlighting potential therapeutic opportunities for mitochondrial replacement strategies.

title: The scientisation of literacy education and the fantasy of governable literacy
container-title: The Australian Journal of Language and Literacy
ea9d6901fd13b2a9ffd66837ebe190abdc846e21.abstract: Abstract Across contemporary education policy, science and evidence are increasingly invoked as authoritative grounds for educational reform. This article examines how scientific authority is constructed and mobilised within literacy policy through a comparative analysis of three Swedish Government Official Reports underpinning reforms of compulsory schooling, teacher education, and the national curriculum. Drawing on discourse-theoretical policy analysis, the study traces how references to science and related forms of scientific rationality are connected to particular understandings of literacy development, teaching, assessment, and professional practice. The analysis identifies three distinct but complementary patterns. In the compulsory school reform, literacy development is made increasingly visible through systematic mapping, assessment, and early intervention. In the teacher education reform, scientific authority is linked more directly to evidence-based instructional methods and professional competence. In the curriculum reform, this logic extends into the organisation of knowledge, teaching strategies, and assessment. Across the three cases, these developments accumulate into a broader policy formation in which literacy is increasingly constructed as an object that can be identified, monitored, predicted, and directed through scientifically authorised forms of knowledge and intervention. We conceptualise the promise that literacy development can thereby be rendered increasingly knowable, predictable, and amenable to intervention as a fantasy of governable literacy . The article argues that this development concerns not simply the growing authority of science in literacy education, but a particular construction of literacy itself as an increasingly knowable and governable educational object. The study contributes to research on the scientisation of education by showing how scientific authority can operate across different reform arenas without relying on a single, stable definition of what counts as science.

Stepped-Care Internet Cognitive Behaviour Therapy for Childhood and Adolescent Anxiety: Parent Perspectives
container-title: Clinical Child Psychology and Psychiatry
ce2db54e7ae5b390b78d7fa0a535a4714acf6b33.abstract: Objective By exploring parental views, we can better understand how stepped-care models with internet cognitive behavioural therapy (ICBT) interventions are experienced by young people and their families. A qualitative approach was used to understand parents’ perceptions of the acceptability and appropriateness of a stepped-care ICBT intervention. Specifically, what elements were effective, what barriers existed and how treatment expectations could inform adjustments to enhance overall outcomes for young people. Methods Twenty parents of children and adolescents (aged 9-16 years) who completed the BRAVE Stepped-Care randomised controlled trials for anxiety participated in semi-structured interviews informed by Proctor et al.’s implementation science framework. Data were analysed using deductive reflexive thematic analysis. Results Four overarching themes were identified, (1) comfort with stepped-care approach, (2) desire for support that feels personalised, (3) parental involvement perceived as helpful and (4) importance of family flexibility. Conclusions The self-directed component of ICBT was well received, particularly with parental involvement. Parents valued personalised support, especially via videoconferencing, and the flexible stepped-care ICBT approach suited busy family schedules. Finding suggest that stepped-care ICBT can be effectively implemented in routine care when parental engagement and flexible, personalised support are prioritised, potentially improving adherence, outcomes and scalability.
