title: Visual and Linguistic Cues of Gender: A Semiotic Analysis of Costume, Locale, and Language in Select Nigerian Television Commercials
container-title: RESEARCH JOURNAL OF MASS COMMUNICATION AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY
1149e20260b76de2b64ac793fa1e24f3f28b7095.abstract: This study examined gender stereotypes in select Nigerian television commercials, focusing on how costume, locale, and language perpetuate gendered representations across Africa Independent Television (AIT), Nigerian Television Authority (NTA), and Channels Television. Specifically, the research analyzed how costume is used to reinforce gender roles, the ways locale shapes gender narratives, how verbal and non-verbal language sustain stereotypes, and the broader societal implications of these portrayals. Anchored on the Social Cognitive Theory and Framing Theory, the study employed qualitative content analysis to critically interpret recurring patterns of gender representation in selected commercials across various product categories such as Maggi, Indomie, GTBank, Lux, and Guinness. The findings revealed that women were predominantly portrayed in domestic or beauty-centered roles through the use of aprons, wrappers, and glamorous attire, while men were dressed in corporate, sporty, or professional outfits symbolizing authority and control. Similarly, locales such as kitchens, dining rooms, and bathrooms confined women to caregiving and private spaces, whereas men were situated in offices, cars, and outdoor environments that emphasized leadership and productivity. Verbal and non-verbal cues further entrenched these stereotypes, as women were associated with soft, nurturing speech and submissive gestures, while men employed assertive tones and dominant body language. The study concluded that these portrayals normalize patriarchal ideologies and perpetuate gender inequality by valorizing men as providers and leaders and relegating women to subordinate or decorative roles. The study recommends that Nigerian media producers and advertising agencies adopt gender-sensitive approaches that promote inclusivity, challenge stereotypes, and align with the United Nations Sustainable Development Goal 5 on gender equality.

title: A machine learning model for identifying heart failure in patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease based on routine laboratory indicators
container-title: BMC Cardiovascular Disorders
1dd98d1c47202b193c638e5a2faaba82086763a9.abstract: Abstract Background Heart failure (HF) is a frequent and prognostically important comorbidity of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), yet it is often documented late. We developed and temporally validated an interpretable machine learning model that identifies clinically documented comorbid HF in patients with COPD using routinely collected laboratory indicators. Methods In this retrospective study, 1,087 patients with COPD (292 with clinically documented HF) hospitalised between January 2023 and December 2025 formed the development cohort, and 268 patients hospitalised between January and September 2026 (63 with HF) formed a temporal external validation cohort. Twenty-five candidate predictors were screened by least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression and the Boruta algorithm; nine algorithms were trained without class-imbalance correction, and the final model was selected on cross-validated discrimination and out-of-fold calibration. Internal validity was quantified by bootstrap optimism correction with the entire pipeline nested (1,000 resamples). The model was benchmarked against NT-proBNP. Results The elastic net model, built on 12 routine predictors, achieved an apparent development AUC of 0.817, an optimism-corrected AUC of 0.799 and an external validation AUC of 0.759 (95% CI 0.683–0.835), with near-ideal external calibration (intercept − 0.133, slope 0.958). At a development-derived threshold targeting 90% sensitivity, 98 of the 268 patients in the external cohort (36.6%) were classified as negative and could potentially have been spared echocardiography, at the cost of missing 11 of the 63 patients with HF (17.5%). NT-proBNP alone achieved an external AUC of 0.983; the model adds no discrimination where natriuretic peptide testing is already available. SHAP variable rankings were preserved across cohorts. Conclusion An elastic net model built exclusively on routine laboratory indicators identified clinically documented comorbid HF in patients with COPD, with discrimination and calibration preserved across a temporal external cohort. Because NT-proBNP outperformed the model, its intended role is a zero-marginal-cost pre-screening layer applied to blood tests that already exist, to prioritise which patients with COPD warrant natriuretic peptide testing and echocardiography. External validation in independent centres is required before clinical use.

title: Retrieval-augmented large language models for bank complaint prioritization: accuracy, bias transfer and fairness-aware retrieval
299733b1cdf32e067dba8ac798ce3c35af2df69e.abstract: Abstract Banks must decide which customer complaints to escalate, and large language models (LLMs) now offer to automate this decision. Zero-shot LLMs rank complaints that end in monetary relief close to chance, because the outcome depends on institutional history that the complaint text does not contain. This study tests whether retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), which supplies similar past complaints and their outcomes, closes that gap, and whether it transfers historical disparities between consumer groups. Using 309{,}348 complaints from 2021--2024 as retrieval memory and complaints from 2025--2026 as queries, drawn from the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau archive, we evaluate Qwen3-8B and Claude Haiku~4.5 under six context conditions against three non-LLM baselines. On a pilot set, similar cases with their outcomes raise ROC AUC from 0.61 to 0.76--0.77 for both models; similar cases without outcomes, or random cases with outcomes, give no gain. On the 3{,}000-complaint test set, Qwen3-8B rises from 0.56 to 0.81, matching supervised models (0.80--0.82) but not the historical relief rate used directly as a score (0.84). Institutional memory also widens the recall gap between servicemembers and other consumers, from +0.6 percentage points without context to -4.1 with full context, approaching the -6.0 to -8.1 points of the base rate and supervised models, because servicemembers' meritorious complaints retrieve neighbours with lower historical relief rates. For complaint prioritization, what the model is shown matters more than which model is used, and retrieval memory requires a fairness audit before deployment.

title: Effects of Model-Lead-Test Strategy on Interest and Performance in Ecology Concept among Secondary School Biology Students in Tudun Wada Local Government Area, Kano State, Nigeria
container-title: Federal University Gusau Faculty of Education Journal
07434da88c792d1f0c954c63038cc13437adca93.abstract: This study examined the difference in interest and academic performance between senior secondary school students taught selected Ecology concepts through the Model-Lead-Test (MLT) instructional strategy and students taught the same concepts through the conventional lecture method in Tudun Wada Local Government Area, Kano State, Nigeria. A quasi-experimental pretest–posttest control-group design was adopted. The study involved 128 Senior Secondary II Biology students: 65 in the MLT group and 63 in the control group. Data were collected using a Biology Performance Test (BPT) and a Biology Students’ Interest Questionnaire (BSIQ). Descriptive statistics and independent-samples t-tests were used for data principal analyses. The descriptive results show a higher mean interest score for the MLT group (M = 3.92, SD = 0.42) than the control group (M = 3.25, SD = 0.51), and a higher mean performance score for the MLT group (M = 68.25, SD = 8.50) than the control group (M = 61.10, SD = 7.90). Data collected were analyzed using mean, standard deviation, and t-test statistics to answer the research questions and tested the hypotheses at the 0.05 level of significance. Findings revealed that students taught using the MLT instructional strategy shows higher interest level and performed significantly better in Biology concepts than those taught using lecture method. The study concludes that the MLT approach enhances learning and students’ interest. The study recommends that teachers, curriculum planners, and professional bodies such as STAN should adopt the strategy to improve Biology teaching and learning.

title: MELAS Associated With a Large-Scale MT-ND2 Deletion
container-title: The Neurologist
60f3a21761317780538a60c423e895e61e57081c.abstract: Introduction: Mitochondrial encephalomyopathy, lactic acidosis, and stroke-like episodes (MELAS) is a clinically and genetically heterogeneous mitochondrial disorder. Although the m.3243A>G variant in MT-TL1 is the most common molecular cause, atypical cases with negative routine genetic testing and nondiagnostic muscle biopsy may pose a substantial diagnostic challenge. Here, we report a clinically diagnosed MELAS case with supportive neuropathological findings and a large-scale deletion involving MT-ND2. Case Report: A 20-year-old man presented with recurrent seizures and encephalopathic episodes over 1.5 years. His clinical course was characterized by episodic visual disturbance, hearing impairment, hemiparesis, and progressive encephalopathic deterioration. Serial magnetic resonance imaging revealed recurrent migratory cortical lesions involving the occipital, temporal, and frontal lobes, and magnetic resonance spectroscopy demonstrated a lactate peak. Cerebrospinal fluid analysis and autoimmune and infectious investigations were unremarkable. Electromyography, muscle biopsy, and initial next-generation sequencing, including testing for the common m.3243A>G variant, were nondiagnostic. Subsequent brain biopsy demonstrated laminar cortical necrosis, supporting a mitochondrial encephalopathic process. Multiplex ligation-dependent probe amplification further identified a large-scale pathogenic deletion involving MT-ND2. Based on the characteristic clinical course, neuroimaging pattern, neuropathological findings, and complementary genetic analysis, a diagnosis of MELAS was established. Conclusion: This case expands the diagnostic spectrum of MELAS and highlights that typical clinical and radiologic features may still be present even when routine lactate testing, muscle biopsy, and standard genetic screening are nondiagnostic. In highly suspected cases, brain biopsy and complementary methods for mitochondrial structural variation analysis, such as MLPA, may provide crucial diagnostic evidence.

title: Delirium and Long-Term Cognitive Trajectories in Cognitively Unimpaired Adults
container-title: JAMA Neurology
decd909bc02f644cbdd6f9a7a856ce27ff3de930.abstract: Importance Delirium is a state of acute confusion characterized by deficits in attention that occurs commonly during hospitalization and is associated with adverse outcomes; however, the association of delirium with longitudinal cognitive trajectories is not fully understood. Objective To evaluate the association of delirium during hospitalization with subsequent development of mild cognitive impairment (MCI), dementia, and longitudinal cognitive trajectories. Design, Setting, and Participants This cohort study used data from participants with hospitalizations in the Mayo Clinic Study of Aging (MCSA) from October 2004 to December 2023. The MCSA is a prospective, population-based longitudinal study of cognitive aging among residents of Olmsted County, Minnesota. Of participants enrolled in the MCSA between 2004 and 2023, individuals who experienced 1 or more hospitalization prior to their last MCSA encounter were included in this study. Participants with dementia at MCSA enrollment or prior to first hospitalization were excluded. Follow-up continued until development of MCI or dementia, last MCSA visit, or the end of the study. Exposure Delirium was identified using a validated natural language processing algorithm applied to clinical notes from hospitalizations, associated emergency department visits, and follow-up within 30 days after hospitalization. Delirium status was modeled as a time-dependent exposure. Main Outcomes and Measures Incident MCI and dementia were assigned through MCSA expert consensus evaluations, including neuropsychological testing performed every 15 months. Association between delirium and development of MCI or dementia was assessed using Cox proportional hazards regression, adjusted for patient age, sex, level of education, and apolipoprotein E (APOE) ε4 allele carrier status; cognitive trajectories were assessed with linear mixed-effects models. Results Of 7030 participants enrolled in the MCSA, 3542 individuals experienced 1 or more hospitalization prior to their last MCSA encounter and were included, and 41 participants with dementia at enrollment or prior to first hospitalization were excluded. The cohort included 3501 participants with at least 1 hospitalization. Median (IQR) age was 74.1 (66.6-80.9) years, 1676 participants (47.9%) were female, median (IQR) level of education was 14 (12-16) years, and 910 participants (26.0%) were APOE ε4 carriers. During a median (IQR) follow-up of 7.2 (4.1-10.4) years, 75 participants (2.1%) had delirium documented within 30 days of hospitalization. Delirium was associated with increased risk of MCI (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR], 3.67; 95% CI, 2.19-6.15) and dementia (aHR, 5.39; 95% CI, 2.94-9.85) and with accelerated decline in longitudinal cognitive testing. Conclusions and Relevance In this cohort study among adults in the MCSA, including those with unimpaired cognition at baseline, delirium during hospitalization was strongly associated with increased risk of MCI and dementia and accelerated cognitive decline in subsequent years.

title:
Quantifying
and Managing the Structural Lifetimes
of Nanocrystalline Model Catalysts in CO
container-title: Nano Letters
ca3244dcbe1c0171e151ec2c3daeb1d815595910.abstract: Abstract Dynamic restructuring of metal nanocrystals (MNCs) in reactive gas atmospheres challenges the static paradigm of shape-controlled model catalysis. Quantifying their structural lifetimes under operating conditions is essential, yet predicting atomistic kinetics over macroscopic time scales remains a fundamental challenge. Here, we transform unpredictable structural lifetimes into a manageable variable using an improved environmental kinetic Monte Carlo (iEKMC) method. It overcomes traditional time scale limits and predicts Pt NC reshaping kinetics across macroscopic time domains under CO atmospheres. By resolving the combined effects of initial morphology, particle size, and temperature, we establish a quantitative framework that determines the reshaping time of MNCs under reaction conditions, showing consistency with benchmarking experiments. We demonstrate that selected combinations of particle size and reaction conditions can effectively mitigate restructuring, preserving predesigned MNC morphologies over day-scale observation windows. This work evaluates and manages operando shape stability in a predictive strategy, restoring the core validity of shape-controlled model catalysis.

title: Empathy-driven remote pedagogy in accounting education − a bilingual model for student engagement and digital resilience
container-title: Information and Learning Sciences
0d74c15ca76677cb5f8a41797811042843685f77.abstract: Purpose This paper presents the empathy-based bilingual digital pedagogy (EBBDP) model, a practice-informed framework developed through the author’s experience in remote teaching of accounting and taxation during and after the COVID-19 pandemic. It aims to show how pedagogical empathy can be translated into bilingual and digitally supported teaching practices intended to strengthen engagement, accessibility and emotional safety in virtual learning environments, particularly within technical education. Design/methodology/approach This study adopts a reflective-practice methodology grounded in lived teaching experience within Portuguese vocational and professional training. It draws on pedagogical documentation, autoethnographic reflection and iterative adaptation of instructional strategies. The model integrates empathy, bilingual inclusivity and digital co-creation as central pedagogical pillars, illustrated through concrete examples using tools such as Google Workspace, Canva, Padlet and ChatGPT to support collaborative learning and formative assessment. Findings The reflective analysis identifies structured emotional check-ins, bilingual scaffolding, digital co-creation and multimodal assessment as practices through which pedagogical empathy may support accessibility, belonging and sustained participation. These practice-based interpretations are presented as conceptual propositions for future empirical testing rather than as measured effects. Originality/value This paper contributes to post-pandemic digital pedagogy by positioning empathy as a core teaching competence rather than a soft skill. It offers a conceptually grounded yet practice-driven model that translates pedagogical empathy into a structured set of bilingual, relational and digitally supported teaching practices, thereby bridging theory and classroom experience in technical education.

title: Effects of mind-body exercise on cognitive function in patients with mild cognitive impairment: A systematic review and network meta-analysis
container-title: Aging Clinical and Experimental Research
5b05d6a64bd0c6e2cd23823b3dc1488ed254c4c6.abstract: Abstract Objective This investigation carried out a systematic review and network meta-analysis to assess how different forms of mind–body exercise influence overall cognitive performance in patients with MCI. Methods A systematic search was conducted across eight Chinese and English databases (up to April 2026). A frequency-based network meta-analysis was performed to estimate the standardized mean differences and 95% confidence intervals, with interventions ranked by SUCRA values. Results A total of 44 RCTs (3,189 patients with MCI) were included. The network meta-analysis showed that, for the MoCA outcome, Baduanjin, Tai Chi, Qigong, and dance were all significantly superior to the control group ( p < 0.05). For the MMSE outcome, all three exercise types except Qigong were significantly superior to the control group. SUCRA rankings indicated that Baduanjin ranked first for both the MoCA (91.6%) and MMSE (88.3%). Subgroup analyses suggested that Baduanjin was most effective for short-term (≤ 12 weeks), high-frequency (> 3 times/week), or short-duration (< 60 min) interventions, while Tai Chi was more effective for long-term (> 12 weeks), low-frequency (≤ 3 times/week), or long-duration (≥ 60 min) interventions. The sensitivity analysis results were robust, and the risk of publication bias was low; however, the certainty of the evidence was generally low. Conclusion Baduanjin, Tai Chi, dance, and Qigong may be beneficial for global cognition in individuals with MCI. Baduanjin ranked highest in the SUCRA analysis. Tai Chi showed a potential advantage in longer-duration interventions. Given the low certainty of evidence and reliance on indirect comparisons, these findings should be interpreted cautiously.

title: Modelo de Análisis de Documentos Curriculares Institucionales
Model for Analysing Institutional Curriculum Documents
container-title: Avances de Investigación en Educación Matemática
5859402743b7808dd1cd492374dadb689edab51c.abstract: Adapting national education regulations to the characteristics of each educational institution in contexts of curricular autonomy gives rise to interpretations that may affect the quality of the area plans developed by schools to operationalize the curriculum. In this article, we propose a model for analysing an area plan from three perspectives: its pedagogical usefulness for teachers, its alignment with national regulations, and its internal consistency. The model comprises five attributes: the pedagogical treatment of topics, alignment with standards, topic coverage, topic specificity, and coherence. We provide guidelines for measuring these attributes and comparing them with a reference area plan. We illustrate the application of the model using a Colombian secondary-school mathematics area plan. The results obtained with this model make it possible to identify areas for improvement in the area plans produced by schools.

title: Essential but vulnerable: a model for understanding how macro–meso–micro-level factors combine to impede the sustainability of female health providers
container-title: International Journal of Ethics and Systems
0ead857020b7d81582930cf5af8d3ee55e46b14b.abstract: Purpose Global health discourse has increasingly focused on achieving universal health coverage, yet the occupational health needs of the workforce delivering these services remain systematically neglected. This paper aims to address the systematic neglect of the occupational health needs of female health-care providers – principally nurses and midwives – in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs). The paper makes particular reference to Sub-Saharan Africa. It develops an integrative multilevel conceptual model that explains how this neglect is produced, transmitted and amplified and proposes implementable multilevel responses. Design/methodology/approach The study uses a structured integrative literature review, reported in line with the PRISMA 2020 statement, and conducted for the purpose of conceptual model development. Eighty-six sources retained from six databases and grey literature repositories were synthesised through a codebook-style thematic analysis. It draws on the Social Determinants of Health (SDH) framework, Moral Injury Theory, the Job Demands–Resources (JD-R) model and the Health Equity Framework. Findings The synthesis suggests that macro-level structural determinants are proposed to produce the foundational architecture of provider neglect. Meso-level organisational factors are proposed to transmit macro-structural neglect into the lived realities of individual providers. Micro-level clinical stressors appear to amplify the intermediate consequences experienced by individual providers beyond what structural and organisational factors alone imply. Gendered structures operate as a cross-cutting context conditioning every level of the model. Feedback loops link deteriorating health system outcomes back to macro- and meso-level conditions. Dismantling provider neglect is therefore proposed to require simultaneous interventions at all three levels of the model. Research limitations/implications As a conceptual paper, the proposed model is not empirically tested. It requires empirical validation through quantitative and qualitative studies across different health-care settings, particularly in LMICs. Cross-national comparative studies across Sub-Saharan African, South Asian and Latin American contexts would test the model’s generalisability. Longitudinal studies tracking the same provider cohorts over time would help examine the proposed sequence and feedback loops. Practical implications The paper emphasises the necessity for national governments, health ministries and institutions and policymakers to establish comprehensive occupational health programmes, dedicated health insurance schemes for providers, workplace wellness initiatives, mental health services and financial protection mechanisms. It specifies responsible actors, implementation priorities and measurable outcomes for each recommendation. International development partners, global health donors and multilateral organisations should integrate health-care workforce welfare into health systems-strengthening investments. Social implications The study reframes health-care providers as a vulnerable population whose health needs are often overlooked within health-care systems. It contributes to sustainable development goals 1 (end poverty in all its forms everywhere), 3 (ensure healthy lives and promote well-being for all), 8 (productive employment and decent work and economic development for all), 10 (reduce inequality) and 16 (provide access to justice for all). Originality/value To the best of the authors’ knowledge, this is the first study to integrate macro-, meso- and micro-level explanations of health-care provider neglect within a single conceptual model that embeds gender-specific mechanisms and feedback loops in its connecting structure. It reframes this neglect as an equity and social justice issue rather than a management problem. It extends Moral Injury Theory into the domain of occupational health exclusion. It repositions the SDH framework as a tool for analysing occupational health inequalities among the health workforce itself.

title: Decreasing Reviewer Engagement Trends at Two STFM Journals
container-title: Family Medicine
f4875ede8d33bbb6396b457a61a91bcca860bb77.abstract: Background and Objectives: Securing peer reviewers for scholarly manuscripts is essential to journal operations but has become increasingly challenging. We sought to describe trends in acceptance of reviewer invitations and review completion at two journals sponsored by the Society of Teachers of Family Medicine: PRiMER and Family Medicine.Methods: We conducted retrospective quality assurance of reviewer invitation outcomes for research manuscripts submitted to either journal from January 2010 to April 2026. Data were extracted from ScholarOne. We calculated odds ratios (ORs) for agreement to review and for review completion for each year via binary logistic regression, employing the generalized estimating equation to control for individual reviewer behavior, journal, and article type.Results: We included 16,905 discrete invitations to review 2,574 manuscripts. Agreement rates at Family Medicine ranged from 70.99% in 2010, to a low of 41.80% in 2025, and 37.99% through April 2026; PRiMER agreement ranged from 74.36% in 2016, to 42.79% in 2025, and 20.23% in partial 2026. Combined completion rates dropped from 89.90% in 2010, to 82.20% in 2025, and to 73.90% in partial 2026. Using 2010 as the reference year, ORs for agreement to review dropped markedly, with the odds of accepting a review invitation in 2026 only 15.9% of the 2010 (2026: OR = 0.159, P&lt;0.001) and the odds of review completion in 2026 falling to 32.9% of 2010 (OR = 0.329, P&lt;0.001).Conclusions: Reviewer engagement is declining across both journals. New, innovative strategies to recruit, engage, and incentivize reviewers will be necessary to sustain peer review.

title: Teachers’ basic psychological need satisfactions and their intentions to use generative artificial intelligence: the mediating role of engagement in professional development
container-title: Frontiers in Psychology
21f4814308b95f9a8b6d35b1286fd353e5f5bb75.abstract: Introduction Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) offers new opportunities for instructional innovation, yet the psychological mechanisms underlying teachers’ intentions to adopt it remain unclear. Intrinsic motivation is an important internal factor shaping teachers’ intentions to use GenAI and is closely linked to the satisfaction of their basic psychological needs. Drawing on self-determination theory (SDT), this study develops and tests a theoretical framework linking teachers’ basic psychological need satisfaction to their intention to use GenAI through intrinsic motivation and engagement in professional development. Such engagement may foster innovation in GenAI-supported teaching practices. Methods Survey data were collected from 146 teachers participating in a GenAI learning program. Structural equation modeling was used to examine the hypothesized relationships among basic psychological need satisfaction, intrinsic motivation, engagement in professional development, and intention to use GenAI. Results Perceived competence in using GenAI was significantly and positively associated with intrinsic motivation, whereas perceived autonomy and relatedness were not significantly associated with intrinsic motivation. Engagement in professional development mediated the relationship between intrinsic motivation and intention to use GenAI. Discussion These findings provide a nuanced understanding of the psychological mechanisms underlying teachers’ intentions to adopt GenAI, highlighting the roles of perceived competence, intrinsic motivation, and engagement in professional development. They also offer practical implications for supporting the integration of GenAI into teaching.

title: Quantum Chemical Calculations, Molecular Docking, ADMET and Unveiling Therapeutic Potential of Marine Alkaloid Petrosamine: Shows Promise for Anxiolytic, Anticonvulsant, and Memory-Preserving Effects in Zebrafish Model
d44e83bc7ebf3679c55c76f98b6e7d476c5cc6c4.abstract: Abstract Research into natural products of marine origin has experienced a rapid advance during the 21st century due to the discovery of the various pharmacological potentialities reported in the literature of exclusively marine bioactives with mechanisms of action involving important biological activities found in various species of marine organisms. The pyridoacridine alkaloid petrosamine, extracted from species of sea sponges of the genus Petrosia sp ., which occur on the coast of the state of Ceará, is a natural marine compound with experimentally proven neuroprotective pharmacological properties. The aim of this article is to evaluate the anxiolytic, sedative, anticonvulsant and memory-preventing effects of the marine alkaloid extract petrosamine in adult zebrafish . Thus, the findings confirm the pharmacological potential of petrosamine as an anxiolytic and memory-suppressing agent, supporting its investigation in new therapeutic strategies. Moreover, petrosamine exhibits intermediate chemical reactivity, characterized by a moderate HOMO–LUMO energy gap and high electrophilicity. The MEP and Fukui function analyses consistently highlight the cationic nitrogen atoms as electrophilic centers, while the oxygen and bromine atoms represent the main nucleophilic regions. Petrosamine had a sedative and anxiolytic effect and prevented memory in adult zebrafish via GABAergic neurotransmission. The studies evaluated indicate that compounds of marine origin are emerging as a promising source of bioactive compounds, revealing an important therapeutic potential for the treatment of neurodegenerative diseases.

title: Developing Civility Agency in Academic Nursing: A Developmental Conceptual Framework
container-title: Journal of Nursing Education
5c0d57c862c03b0b331e118ad59969e251cd9d41.abstract: Background: The importance of fostering civility in academic nursing is well established; however, research has focused primarily on describing civility and evaluating interventions rather than explaining how civility develops. Consequently, nursing education lacks a developmental framework explaining how civility is intentionally cultivated and translated into consistent professional action. Method: Grounded in Bandura's social cognitive theory, the Civility Agency Framework was systematically derived from the Middle-Range Theory of Civility in Academic Nursing through theoretical synthesis. Results: The Civility Agency Framework conceptualizes civility agency as eight interdependent dimensions organized within three developmental phases that collectively explain how individuals intentionally develop and sustain civility in academic nursing. Conclusion: The Civility Agency Framework advances nursing education by providing a theoretically grounded foundation for intentionally cultivating civility throughout nursing education.

title: Building a pre-trained model for single-cell multi-omics analysis beyond highly variable feature selection
container-title: Nature Communications
cba2b8d854d21b19b15f1711fe8758daf81ceb2a.abstract: Abstract Single-cell multi-omics technologies enable simultaneous measurement of transcriptomic, epigenomic, and proteomic modalities in individual cells, offering a unique opportunity to dissect cellular identity and regulation. The heterogeneity of multi-omics data, together with the wide range of downstream analytical tasks, underscores the need for a versatile computational framework for integrative analysis. However, current multi-omics analysis approaches typically rely on task-specific training and highly variable feature selection, which can hinder effective knowledge transfer across datasets and discard biologically informative signals. Here, we present scPMMI, a pre-trained multimodal model for integrative analysis of single-cell multi-omics data. By grouping features into patches according to genomic coordinates, scPMMI processes tens of thousands of features per cell with reduced reliance on prior feature selection, thereby preserving more complete biological information. Our results demonstrate that scPMMI learns biologically coherent cell representations by jointly modeling multi-omics data. Through further transfer learning, the model can be readily adapted to achieve superior performance across diverse downstream tasks, including multi-omics integration, cell type annotation, protein abundance prediction, transcriptomic enhancement, and trajectory reconstruction.

title: Technical note: Evaluation of snow water equivalent from large-scale land-surface products over Italy
container-title: Hydrology and Earth System Sciences
b7f6be89ac5955ef46927a00dc869e434e4867f7.abstract: Snow water equivalent (SWE) is a critical hydrological variable for water resource management in mountainous regions, where seasonal snowpacks function as natural reservoirs regulating streamflow and water supply. While high-resolution, observation-constrained regional or national snow products provide reliable daily SWE estimates at fine spatial resolution (less than 1 km), their limited temporal coverage often restricts their use for long-term hydro-climatological studies. Large-scale land-surface products, in which SWE is derived from land-surface model simulations driven by atmospheric reanalyses or regional dynamical downscaling systems, provide multi-decadal coverage, but their reliability may be affected by biases in meteorological forcing, limited topographic representation, and simplified snow process parameterisation, requiring rigorous regional evaluation. This study evaluates the SWE estimates of three large-scale land-surface products, i.e., the global ERA5-Land, the European CERRA-Land, and the Italian VHR-REA_IT, against the national reference dataset IT-SNOW across Italy. The analysis combines grid-scale bias assessment of mean annual SWE and snow cover duration with temporal correlation analysis of daily SWE series, and is complemented by an evaluation of precipitation and temperature biases in each product, providing insight into how each product represents the atmospheric conditions governing snow accumulation and ablation and thereby supporting the interpretation of the identified SWE discrepancies. The results show clear regional differences in product performance, with no single product performing best across all metrics. ERA5-Land shows the strongest temporal correlation with IT-SNOW, but tends to overestimate mean annual SWE and snow cover duration in the Alps. CERRA-Land shows more moderate biases than ERA5-Land in the Italian Alps, but generally underestimates mean annual SWE across most subregions, where autumn and winter precipitation deficits in the forcing limit snow accumulation. Across the Apennines, both ERA5-Land and CERRA-Land tend to underestimate SWE and snow cover duration, particularly in the northern sectors. VHR-REA_IT shows widespread underestimation and the weakest temporal correspondence with IT-SNOW despite its finer grid spacing, which may be due to its fully coupled atmosphere–land architecture with no assimilation of meteorological observations. Overall, the results suggest that forcing biases explain a substantial part of the observed SWE discrepancies, although not all of them. This study provides useful insights for the use of SWE estimates from large-scale land-surface products in long-term hydro-climatological assessments over Italy and helps to understand whether the products can be used to evaluate snow dynamics in mountainous regions lacking high-quality benchmark estimates.

title: Leakage-Controlled Benchmarking of Variant Effect Predictors and Development of Gradient-Boosting Consensus Model
b61c623578dfe10cb93e4a5095c23182c8c6eca0.abstract: Abstract Single amino acid mutations are among the most common forms of genetic variation, with effects ranging from negligible to severe disruption of protein function. Accurate quantitative evaluation of protein variants therefore represents a key challenge in medicine and protein engineering. Computational variant effect predictors (VEPs) are widely used to prioritize missense variants, yet their fair comparison is hindered by data circularity, benchmarks restricted to human clinical annotations, and limited availability of code and training data, all of which can inflate apparent performance. Here, we reviewed 18 recent and 3 older, widely adopted variant effect predictors for reproducible benchmarking and assembled a rigorously curated, leakage-controlled Benchmark dataset by integrating clinically annotated human variants from ClinVar and Humsavar as well as cross-species variants with functional annotations. The evaluation on this dataset revealed a narrow overall performance range for the benchmarked tools (AUC 0.631–0.758) and a consistent drop from clinical to functional data. Surprisingly, several tools published two decades ago demonstrated comparable performance to mid-ranked modern predictors. Building on these results, we developed a gradient-boosting consensus model, PredictSNP prot , which achieved an AUC of 0.82 on a held-out test set, outperforming the original PredictSNP meta-predictor and the best individual state-of-the-art tool by 13.6 and 5.7 percentage points, respectively. The Benchmark dataset , including the predictions from the evaluated tools, is available at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23597130 and PredictSNP prot consensus predictor is available at https://github.com/loschmidt/PredictSNPprot . Key Points We constructed a leakage-controlled benchmark dataset of 10,385 clinical and cross-species functional variants, thoroughly filtered to exclude overlap with training data of benchmarked tools. The benchmarking of 14 sequence-based variant effect predictors on this dataset yielded narrow AUC range (0.631–0.758) and most performed markedly worse on functional than on clinical variants. We developed PredictSNP prot , a gradient boosting consensus model, integrating 9 constituent tools and reaching an AUC of 0.818 on a held-out test set, compared with 0.761 for the best single tool. The benchmark dataset including all in-house generated tool predictions as well as the PredictSNP prot code are openly available at Zenodo and GitHub, respectively.

title: a-справедливая оптимизационная модель и численные алгоритмы выбора общей лексической нормы тюркских языков
An a-Fair Optimization Model and Numerical Algorithms for Selecting a Common Lexical Norm of Turkic Languages
container-title: Problems of Computational and Applied Mathematics
cd528884ac15d8a6bd618743ea5e06a34243a3e9.abstract: The selection of a common lexical norm for Turkic languages is formulated as a discrete optimization problem that ensures fair intelligibility for speakers of all languages. For each concept, one form is chosen from a set of candidates; intelligibility for speakers of each language is estimated by a feature-weighted edit distance, and the choice is governed by an a-fair objective function together with phonological consistency constraints. We prove that the weighted averaging model is the special case a = 0, while the max-min criterion is the limit a → ∞. An exact mixed-integer linear programming formulation and an approximate algorithm based on relaxation, mirror ascent, rounding and local search are developed. A computational experiment on 1016 concepts of five Turkic languages from the NorthEuraLex database shows that under weighted averaging the intelligibility for the worst-off language (Kazakh) is 0.528, whereas the max-min solution raises it to 0.704 (by 33.2%) while reducing the population-weighted average by only 6.0%. The proposed algorithm deviates from the exact solution by less than 0.03% and is up to 49 times faster for a = 1.

title: Towards Intersectional Justice
container-title: Amicus Curiae
5294bff7780d4623f1145c176f87cf12960e5bdc.abstract: This article analyses the first-level refugee appeal cases in New Zealand by queer women through utilizing an intersectional feminist lens. While New Zealand is often seen as welcoming towards individuals who claim asylum on the grounds of sexual orientation, it has been argued that tribunal judges set high thresholds for establishing the credibility of queer women’s asylum applications compared to queer men. An analysis of the decisions of the New Zealand Immigration and Protection Tribunal highlights the judiciary’s increasingly progressive understanding of the challenges faced by queer women, contributing to critical analysis challenging intersectional discrimination impacting queer women. Keywords: gender; sexuality; intersectionality; asylum; New Zealand.

title: Use of Large Language Models for Automated Short-Answer Question Grading in Second-Cycle Medical Education: Performance and Consistency Evaluation Study
container-title: JMIR Medical Education
11a8d18764103471cba8b13e6d1a563b7564307c.abstract: Background Short-answer questions (SAQs) effectively assess higher-order reasoning skills in medical education but face challenges in scalability due to time-intensive manual grading and concerns about interrater reliability. Recent advances in large language models (LLMs) may offer a solution through automated assessment. Objective This study evaluated the performance and consistency of LLMs—ChatGPT, Claude Sonnet 4, and Mistral Pro—compared with those of human graders for SAQ grading in hepatology and gastroenterology. Methods We retrospectively analyzed SAQs from hepatology and gastroenterology examinations at Sorbonne University, Paris, France (2023-2025). Three human evaluators (2 hepatogastroenterologists and 1 radiologist) independently graded all responses twice, with the majority consensus score serving as the reference standard. Six LLMs were evaluated: ChatGPT (GPT-4o, GPT-4.5, GPT-4o3, and GPT-5), Claude Sonnet 4, and Mistral Pro. Each LLM graded all responses twice using standardized prompts, including questions, model answers, grading guidelines, and scoring rubrics. Agreement was assessed using quadratic weighted kappa (QWK), Cohen κ, the intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC), and the mean absolute error (MAE) for interhuman, intrahuman, LLM-versus-human, and intramodel comparisons. Results A total of 902 student responses from 12 SAQs were included and analyzed. Interhuman grader agreement was almost perfect (QWK 0.90-0.92; ICC 0.90-0.92; MAE 0.05-0.07). Claude Sonnet 4 and GPT-4o3 demonstrated near-human–level performance when compared with the majority vote of human evaluators (Claude Sonnet 4: QWK 0.88-0.90; ICC 0.88-0.90; MAE 0.06-0.07 and GPT-4o3: QWK 0.82-0.89; ICC 0.82-0.89; MAE 0.07-0.09). GPT-5 showed substantial agreement (QWK 0.77-0.79). Mistral Pro and older ChatGPT versions performed poorly (QWK <0.63). Intramodel consistency was the highest for Claude Sonnet 4 (QWK 0.93), approaching the best human intrarater reliability. Agreement did not correlate with prompt design choices (number of examples or minimum word count). Conclusions Advanced LLMs, particularly Claude Sonnet 4 and GPT-4o3, demonstrated near-human–level grading performance, supporting their potential use as assistive tools in SAQ grading. However, performance varied by model, and agreement alone does not ensure educational validity. Until broader multicenter validation is conducted across diverse domains, stakes, and question formats—along with safeguards for bias, privacy, and model drift—LLMs should augment rather than replace human faculty graders.

title: Assessment of clinker phases in cement production with multivariate model based on X-ray diffraction and X-ray fluorescence
container-title: Advances in Cement Research
0b996e44e2f8be1abe183d22f9ed5e409b5dac6f.abstract: A method for the assessment of the relative abundance and composition of clinker phases is presented. The tested population consists of 269 clinker samples from industrial facilities. Data from X-ray diffraction (XRD) and X-ray fluorescence (XRF) techniques are correlated with multivariate modelling. An empirical algorithm is presented to fit the XRD phase relative abundance (R2 of 0.84 for C3S; 0.89 for C2S; 0.92 for C3A; 0.93 for C4AF). A semi-empirical algorithm is also presented to assess the composition of clinker phases. The validation strategy includes a comparative assessment with traditional models based on random data. The model shows better fitting (e.g. R2 of 0.84 for C3S) to the experimental XRD data than traditional models (e.g. R2 of 0.59 and 0.54 for C3S with the Bogue and Taylor model, respectively) and values closer to the bisector (e.g. R2 of 0.78 for C3S with the present model, compared against −0.01 and −5.85 with the Bogue and Taylor model, respectively). Thus, starting from the relative abundance of oxides, the relative abundance and composition of the silicate and aluminate phases could be accurately determined. Factors affecting phase abundance and composition could be distinguished and independently controlled, enabling the delivery of improved technical and sustainability-related performance of cement.

title: Strength distribution for mudstone absorbing water and its softened statistical damage constitution model
container-title: Proceedings of the Institution of Civil Engineers - Geotechnical Engineering
21cae562df3447e8256307471ea1d89c44d833d3.abstract: The mechanical strength of mudstone after absorbing water significantly decreases, seriously affecting the stability of tunnel projects. It is very important to study the laws and mechanism of this strength deterioration of mudstone. In this study, the main causes of the diseases in mudstone tunnels were determined. Through a series of the uniaxial compression and scanning electron microscopy tests, the strength deterioration mechanisms were studied and a statistical damage constitutive model was established. The results show that softening and expansion of mudstone after absorbing water were the main causes for the mudstone tunnel diseases. The probability of disease occurrence in mudstone tunnels from high to low was the inverted arch, vault, side wall and haunch. The softening and expansion of the mudstone were mutually reinforcing, and their mutual interaction formed a vicious cycle of water erosion. The stress–strain curve of mudstone showed a plastic–elastic–plastic curve. As the water content increased, the failure mode shifted from splitting failure to shear failure, while the degree of plastic deformation increased. Based on the Weibull distribution model and the Mohr–Coulomb failure criterion, a statistical damage constitutive model for mudstone absorbing water was established; the model can depict the failure process of softening mudstone.

title: An Integrated Experimental and Informatics Strategy Enables Large Proteoform Identification in Top-Down Proteomics
670a65716f09f0ec6fa82daa361d1bd13249d292.abstract: Abstract Top-down proteomics enables identification and characterization of intact proteoforms, preserving information on co-occurring sequence variations and post-translational modifications. However, identifying large proteoforms remains challenging due to an exponential decrease in signal-to-noise ratio with increasing molecular weight, interference from coeluting smaller species, unresolved precursor isotopic envelopes, difficulty obtaining informative MS/MS spectra, and limitations of current informatics tools. To address these challenges, here we present an integrated experimental and informatics strategy combining protein separation, data acquisition, precursor mass assignment, and MS/MS interpretation. First, we demonstrate that online two-dimensional liquid chromatography coupling size-exclusion and reversed-phase separations enables facile detection of large proteoforms. We then utilize a precursor mass correction strategy to enable conventional database searching of data-dependent acquisition (DDA) data containing isotopically unresolved precursors. Finally, we use data-independent acquisition (DIA) optimized for large proteins to enhance fragment signal and enable identification through intact-mass-guided candidate discovery and MS/MS validation. Applied to human heart tissue, the integrated strategy identified 703 nonredundant proteoforms from 236 unique proteins, including 65 proteins >30 kDa and 22 proteins >50 kDa, with identifications extending to 223 kDa. This integrated strategy bridges the detection-to-identification gap for large proteins and expands the accessible mass range of discovery top-down proteomics.

title: Laparoscopic resection of a large primary retroperitoneal mucinous cystadenoma assisted by controlled decompression with a SAND balloon catheter: a case report
container-title: International Journal of Surgery Case Reports
b0c6eb51adfa60c6444055a9ba537537b789f3e5.abstract: Introduction and importance: Primary retroperitoneal mucinous cystadenoma (PRMC) is a rare epithelial neoplasm that is challenging to diagnose preoperatively because of nonspecific imaging findings. Laparoscopic resection of large retroperitoneal cystic tumors can be technically demanding because of limited working space and the risk of cyst rupture and fluid spillage. Case presentation: A 43-year-old woman presented with a gradually enlarging palpable mass in the left lower abdomen. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography revealed a well-defined, unilocular cystic lesion measuring 12 × 10 × 7 cm, without enhancing solid components or adjacent organ invasion. Laparoscopic resection was performed with controlled decompression using a SAND balloon catheter. Approximately 450 mL of cyst fluid was aspirated, thereby facilitating operative visualization. Complete resection was achieved without intraoperative spillage. Histopathological examination confirmed a benign PRMC. The postoperative course was uneventful, and the patient was discharged on postoperative day 5. At 7 months, she remained well, without recurrence. Clinical discussion: In this case, the absence of radiological features strongly suggestive of malignancy supported a laparoscopic approach, while the large cyst markedly restricted the working space and made intact manipulation difficult. Although intact excision is preferable, controlled decompression may be considered a selective technical adjunct in such circumstances. Conclusion: PRMC is a rare cystic neoplasm, and laparoscopic resection of large lesions can be technically challenging. In the present case, controlled decompression using a SAND balloon catheter facilitated laparoscopic resection and may represent a useful technical option when intact excision is difficult.

title: Beyond cognitive ability, investigating the symmetrical and asymmetrical pathways of emotional and spiritual intelligence on academic achievement in higher education
container-title: Discover Education
8bd2627003c378bdc46f5dc2fbf48213ed81dfe3.abstract: Abstract Higher education is typically explained in terms of cognitive ability (IQ) when linked to academic achievement. However, despite evidence of non-cognitive intelligence, specifically emotional and spiritual intelligence, its association with academic achievement remains underexplored. In Ghana, where spiritual orientation is strong, research on the relationship between emotional and spiritual intelligence and academic achievement among higher education students remains limited. This study used Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling (PLS-SEM) and Fuzzy-set Qualitative Comparative Analysis (FsQCA) to assess symmetrical and asymmetrical pathways. The study used a quantitative cross-sectional correlation design, drawing on data from 339 students across six colleges at Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KNUST). PLS-SEM shows that emotional intelligence is significantly related to academic achievement (β = 0.344, p < .001) and spiritual intelligence (β = 0.661, p < .001). Spiritual intelligence is associated with academic achievement (β = 0.371, p < .001). The model explains 43. 4% of the variance in academic achievement. The FsQCA results showed that a single configuration was consistently associated with high academic achievement. The combined presence of both high emotional intelligence and spiritual intelligence had a consistency of 0.825 and a coverage of 0.766. Configurations in which one intelligence was high showed high consistency but low PRI consistency, so they were associated with both high and low achievement. The same findings appear in the robustness analysis. Therefore, emotional intelligence and spiritual intelligence appear to relate to achievement conjecturally, as co-occurring resources rather than independent or compensatory routes. The findings call for Ghanaian evidence on the multidimensionality of intelligence and show the value of integrating PLS-SEM and FsQCA to inform educational research.

title: A quantitative model for the meridional drift of mesoscale eddies: β-dipole advection and eddy interaction
container-title: Journal of Physical Oceanography
19c9e41eaa73db9c4b36a9d959180db8dc93249e.abstract: Abstract This study develops a quantitative model for the meridional drift of nonlinear mesoscale eddies in a reduced-gravity, quasi-geostrophic framework. The metric is the drift velocity of an eddy centroid defined and tracked by a closed height-anomaly contour. The analysis considers both single-eddy evolution and eddy interaction. As nonlinearity increases, the evolution of an isolated, axisymmetric eddy transitions from Rossby-wave dispersion with minimal meridional deflection to movement as a compact entity with persistent meridional drift. Using the difference between centroid and height-extremum trajectories as a measure of dispersiveness, a practical criterion for the compact-eddy regime is established. For eddies in this regime, a central result is a quantitative relationship that connects the meridional drift to meridional advection of the eddy boundary. When applied to isolated eddies, this relationship accurately captures the temporal variability of the drift velocity in numerical simulations. Decomposition of eddy circulation reveals a well-known secondary, tilted β -dipole (” β -gyres”) structure. The dipole dominates the boundary advection, thereby leading to a direct and validated relationship in which the temporal variability of centroid drift is controlled by the boundary-averaged meridional dipole velocity, with a proportionality factor depending on eddy size. The size dependence also implies that smaller eddies drift more rapidly. Because the boundary-advection formulation is general and could account for mutual advection, the quantitative relationship remains applicable when eddies interact. This general utility is demonstrated by testing against simulations where realistic eddy interaction is permitted.

title: A Data-Driven Tropical Cyclone Model Based on Lagrangian Limited-Area Transformers: Investigating Physical Fidelity through Real-Case Simulations and Idealized Experiments
container-title: Journal of the Atmospheric Sciences
5a0d6f2c85ad9fadb3ae1a5435340f1b9f26acf1.abstract: Abstract Data-driven weather prediction (DWP) offers advantages in computational efficiency and demonstrates superior synoptic-scale performance compared with numerical weather prediction. However, global DWP models typically operate at coarser resolutions and remain limited in their ability to accurately predict tropical cyclone (TC) wind structure and rainfall. Therefore, the Lagrangian Limited-Area Transformer for typhoon (LLAT.ty) is developed for TC-following DWP; it is specifically designed to learn TC evolution with 3-hourly intervals and is trained using TC-centered ERA5 reanalysis. Notably, LLAT.ty explicitly predicts the TC center location for the next time step. Therefore, LLAT.ty can generate three-dimensional forecasts on continuous time steps, provided that boundary conditions from the global DWP are used via one-way boundary updating or two-way domain interactions. LLAT.ty also provides additional predicted variables essential for TC forecasting, including rainfall and vertical motion. This study subsequently uses LLAT.ty as a scientific testbed to examine whether a purely data-driven prediction system reproduces the established dynamical behavior of TCs. Simulations of all 2024 typhoons show that LLAT.ty improves TC track predictions by approximately 30% relative to the baseline FourCastNETv2 global DWP. Moreover, idealized experiments demonstrate that LLAT.ty produces realistic TC responses to variations in sea surface temperature, latitude-dependent Earth’s rotation, and vertical wind shear governing the convective asymmetry. Also, LLAT.ty successfully simulates the evolution of beta gyres, which exert a physically reasonable influence on TC motion. Overall, this study suggests that DWP models can better represent TC-specific dynamics by adjusting the learning framework to the scales and weather systems of interest.

title: Development of a novel empirical model for optimization of sludge discharge in drinking water treatment clarifiers
container-title: Water Supply
4b82b7ba4c34cbfbd179ad0b278dcb9448d01f51.abstract: ABSTRACT Optimization of sludge discharge operation in sedimentation clarifiers is important for maintaining treatment efficiency and minimizing unnecessary water losses in drinking water treatment plants. The present study aimed to develop a novel practical operational model for estimating sludge valve opening duration based on hydraulic and sludge generation characteristics under full-scale operating conditions. Field investigations were conducted in seven surface water treatment plants in Sohag Governorate, Egypt, including P1, P2, P3, P4, P5, P6, and P7 coded treatment plants. The proposed methodology combined jar-test measurements, sludge sampling, and hydraulic measurements for determination of theoretical and actual sludge generation rates. The developed model was based on the relationship between hydraulic-operational parameters and sludge generation characteristics for calculation of sludge valve opening duration. Results indicated that the hydraulic-operational constant (C) remained relatively stable for most treatment plants and ranged from approximately 2.1 to 3.2 despite differences in plant dimensions and operating conditions. In contrast, the sludge generation ratio factor (F) showed greater variability, with values ranging from 0.009 to 0.032 under normal operating conditions. calculated valve opening duration ranged from 21 to 71 s for most investigated plants. The developed model demonstrated sensitivity to sludge discharge configuration and operating conditions and may provide a practical tool for improving sludge management efficiency and optimizing sludge discharge operation in drinking water treatment plants.

title: Advancing healing in large hard-to-heal wounds: the ripple effect of autologous whole blood clot therapy: a case series
container-title: Journal of Wound Care
ab817f1f1c030749779f311b3bb4df361e3124fa.abstract: Objective: Hard-to-heal (chronic) wounds of the lower extremity, particularly large-area wounds, present significant challenges due to their usually prolonged healing time and complications that might lead to surgical interventions, adding to the high burden on the healthcare system. This study aimed to evaluate the efficacy of autologous whole blood clot (AWBC) therapy in promoting healing in large (>28cm 2 ), hard-to-heal wounds. Method: Patients with a mean wound size of 63.4±31.6cm 2 were treated weekly with AWBC therapy. AWBC was created from a small blood sample of the patient and applied weekly onto the wound, covering only part of it (the clot size is 28cm 2 , and only one was used). The patients were followed until complete wound closure or satisfactory healing was achieved. Results: This case series comprised 27 patients (55.5% female, mean age: 69.7±15.8 years). The results showed that 78% of the treated wounds progressed toward healing, with an overall mean percent area reduction of 74% at the final follow-up. AWBC therapy demonstrated a high level of efficacy across all wound types, showing effectiveness even when the clot did not fully cover the wound area. Conclusion: In this case series AWBC therapy offered a promising solution for large, hard-to-heal wounds by creating a favourable microenvironment that promoted tissue repair. The therapeutic effect extended beyond the area directly covered by the clot, suggesting a ripple effect mediated by bioactive factors from the clot. AWBC therapy represents an innovative and effective treatment option for large, hard-to-heal wounds. While additional studies are needed to optimise protocols and further investigate the underlying mechanisms, these findings demonstrate AWBC therapy's ability to address the limitations of existing wound care strategies.

738ea4e749ccdac5bf207a2ab0443b7dc9cae2cf.abstract: Em 13 de janeiro de 2025, o Brasil sancionou a Lei nº 15.100, que proíbe o uso de aparelhos eletrônicos portáteis pessoais por estudantes durante aulas, recreio e intervalos em toda a educação básica, declarando como objetivo salvaguardar a saúde mental, física e psíquica de crianças e adolescentes. O artigo examina a natureza da evidência disponível sobre os três domínios de desenvolvimento invocados por essa premissa. A pesquisa foi conduzida na base Europe PMC, restrita a título e resumo, sobre registros indexados até 26 de setembro de 2026, com classificação de delineamento por tipo de publicação indexado. Foram identificados 4.934 registros que associam exposição a telas e infância. O domínio emocional reúne 931 registros, o cognitivo 792 e o comportamental 287. A assimetria entre delineamentos é acentuada e desigual entre os domínios: a razão entre estudos transversais e ensaios randomizados é de 5,5 para 1 no domínio cognitivo, de 17,5 para 1 no comportamental e de 20,2 para 1 no emocional, domínio que reúne apenas 13 ensaios randomizados em toda a literatura indexada. A participação dos ensaios randomizados caiu de 10,8% dos registros de 2015 para 2,4% em 2025, enquanto o volume anual quadruplicou. Conclui-se que a premissa legislada apoia-se em um corpo de evidência predominantemente observacional, escassez que decorre em parte de limitações éticas intrínsecas ao objeto.

title: Decision-Making Amid Information-Based Threats in Sociotechnical Systems: A Review
container-title: Journal of Cognitive Engineering and Decision Making
f7e372db0709368f0b1565c58d708c269d3a00b0.abstract: Technological systems increasingly mediate human information exchange, spanning interactions among humans as well as between humans and artificial agents. The unprecedented scale of, and reliance on, information disseminated through these systems substantially expand the scope of information-based influence that can both enable and undermine sound decision-making. Consequently, understanding and protecting decision-making today faces growing challenges, as individuals and organizations must navigate evolving opportunities and information-based threats across domains and information environments. While these risks are widely recognized, research remains fragmented: work evaluating information-based threat phenomena has progressed largely in isolation from foundational studies of human information processing. In this review, we synthesize insights from both domains to identify shared cognitive mechanisms that mediate vulnerability to information-based threats and shape behavioral outcomes. We then present a multilevel conceptual framework and outline directions for future research aimed at integrating these perspectives, emphasizing the importance of mitigating human vulnerabilities and aligning human-machine representations.
