title: Hydraulic Cylinder Loads in an Automated Orchard Post-Driving Machine Determined from a Solid Model: A Basis for Selecting Control System Settings
container-title: Applied Sciences
7a231374abb610322bdb71a7f50fd8b14aef2173.abstract: In automated hydraulically driven agricultural machines, valve settings and motion limits are usually selected empirically, without knowing cylinder loads. These loads were predicted for the Horty AutoHammer orchard post-driving machine from its solid model, manufacturing drawings and operating manual. Forces in four hydraulic cylinders were derived using the principle of virtual work; the derivation was checked by numerical differentiation, link equilibrium and energy balance. The parallelogram linkage makes lifting force independent of tower inclination and hammer position. With the mast horizontal, the predicted tilting pressure increases linearly with hammer position from 27 to 189 bar, exceeding the 140 bar working limit above approximately 4.0 m, so mast lowering requires a hammer-position interlock. A Lagrangian model with oil compressibility yields hydraulic natural frequencies of 2.2–31 Hz. The classical ramp dynamic amplification factor, confirmed by nonlinear simulation, shows that at the full flow of one pump (56.1 L/min), tilting (hammer below mid-mast) and post lifting would require valve ramps of 3.8 and 5.2–7.4 s, exceeding the stroke times; limiting the flow to 15 and 8 L/min allows 1 s ramps. The predicted lifting pressure sensitivity of 11–58 mbar/kg indicates potential for pressure-based post detection. A validation test with predicted values is specified.

title: Zebrafish as a Model Organism in Space Biology Research
container-title: Biology
4c5fa3b6523469ae6836330144451d1aa4802091.abstract: As deep-space exploration advances, the health effects of the space environment have become a critical concern. Zebrafish (Danio rerio) have emerged as a valuable vertebrate model for space biology owing to their genetic tractability, optical transparency, and conserved organ systems. This review summarizes recent advances in using zebrafish to study spaceflight-associated health risks, focusing on ionizing radiation and altered gravity. We examine effects across the cardiovascular, nervous, musculoskeletal, sensory, reproductive, and other systems. Radiation induces cardiac dysfunction, neurobehavioral deficits, skeletal deformation, ocular damage, and reproductive toxicity, often through oxidative stress, apoptosis, and dysregulated signaling pathways. Microgravity and hypergravity primarily affect the musculoskeletal and vestibular systems, with microgravity reducing bone ossification and impairing otolith development. We also discuss current limitations, including the gap between ground-based simulations and actual space conditions, and the lack of combined-stressor studies. Finally, we highlight future directions, such as in-orbit live imaging, CRISPR/Cas9-based validation, and high-throughput countermeasure screening. This review aims to provide a theoretical framework for using zebrafish to assess space-environment-associated health risks and to inform research on health risks relevant to long-duration spaceflight.

title: Applying the Transcreation Framework to Design the Recovery Coach Doula Role and Delivery Model to Support Individuals with Substance Use Disorder in the Perinatal Period
container-title: Behavioral Sciences
cec4970dd7311c8ad19ce01443b71404f51a51cb.abstract: Background: Treating perinatal substance use disorder is a public health priority. Social support is associated with better substance use and perinatal outcomes. Doula care and recovery coaching from peers who are in recovery themselves are two evidence-based interventions designed to provide social support. The aim was to braid doula care and peer recovery coaching into a novel healthcare personnel role and develop a delivery model for implementation in community settings. Methods: A team led by community members from the recovery and birth justice communities and perinatal clinicians, with a policy analysts, and an implementation scientist applied the Transcreation Framework guided by extant literature, theory, formative research, and existing community infrastructure in weekly or biweekly sessions over three years. Results: The team identified a strong evidentiary foundation for Recovery Coach Doula care and supportive community infrastructure. Through theory analysis and formative research, the team identified 15 core functions of the Recovery Coach Doula role and developed a delivery model. The core functions were intentionally designed to be adaptable to allow Recovery Coach Doulas to meet the needs of their clients. To deliver Recovery Coach Doula care in community settings, the team created a hub and spoke model delivery program to accommodate varying healthcare models and center the needs of the Recovery Coach Doulas, as well as the clients. The transcreation process provided structure required for rigorous co-design over an extended period time with iteration. Conclusions: Systematic application of the Transcreation Framework with community laid the foundation for implementation of Recovery Coach Doula care. Next steps include rigorously testing the effectiveness of Recovery Coach Doula care and developing implementation strategies and outcomes.

title: The Impact of Entrepreneurial Team Relational Governance on Opportunity Pivoting and New Venture Performance: A Moderated Mediation Model
container-title: Behavioral Sciences
d3e92fd5963bb9ba15b26870223328701df01972.abstract: Strategic adaptation in highly dynamic environments is a central focus of entrepreneurship research. However, existing studies lack a rigorous analysis of the mechanisms linking relational governance to opportunity pivoting (OP). Consequently, the effectiveness of OP remains inconclusive. Based on dynamic capabilities theory, this study uses two-wave survey data from 471 new ventures to examine the associations among entrepreneurial team relational governance (ETRG), opportunity pivoting, new venture performance, and AI-environmental dynamism (AIED), focusing on the indirect (mediating) association of OP between ETRG and new venture performance and the moderating association of AIED. The results show that ETRG is positively associated with OP, that OP is positively associated with new venture performance (a significant indirect association). In addition, AIED positively moderates the relationship between ETRG and OP. The theoretical contributions of this study are threefold. First, it highlights the role of relational governance in relating to entrepreneurial team opportunity pivoting. Second, it clarifies the indirect pathway—relational governance → opportunity pivoting → new venture performance—as an associational mechanism. Third, it identifies the boundary conditions for effective governance in the AI era, providing practical implications for optimizing governance mechanisms to navigate technological turbulence.

title: Disaster Exposure and Early Self-Reported Posttraumatic Growth: Indirect Associations Through Cognitive Emotion Regulation and Moderation by Dark Triad Traits
container-title: Behavioral Sciences
7553839e402798acbe66405d35048d85716a9ff7.abstract: Associations between disaster exposure and posttraumatic growth (PTG) are inconsistent, highlighting the potential relevance of cognitive processing and personality differences. This study surveyed 1498 individuals within one week of the July 2021 Henan floods to examine the associations among disaster exposure, early self-reported PTG, cognitive emotion regulation (CER), and Dark Triad traits. Disaster exposure showed a small positive association with PTG in the unadjusted model (b = 0.324, p < 0.001), which became nonsignificant after adjusting for gender, age, and current location (b = 0.146, p = 0.139). In the unadjusted parallel indirect-association model, disaster exposure showed positive indirect associations with PTG through both adaptive CER (estimate = 0.079, 95% CI [0.031, 0.144]) and maladaptive CER (estimate = 0.166, 95% CI [0.083, 0.256]), whereas the direct association was nonsignificant. After adjustment, only the indirect association through maladaptive CER remained distinguishable from zero. Dark Triad traits moderated several component associations, but only the conditional indirect association through adaptive CER differed across Dark Triad levels. Early perceived PTG was more closely associated with patterns of cognitive emotion regulation and personality differences than with disaster exposure severity alone. However, the cross-sectional design precludes temporal or causal interpretations, underscoring the need to distinguish early perceptions of growth from enduring psychological adaptation.

title: From Intention to Action: The Functional Motivation Model for Goal-Directed Learning
container-title: Education Sciences
2666d95afb82a821ca4b17cdc769aa643d632ad2.abstract: Students often express motivation to learn yet struggle to translate intention into sustained academic action. Although existing motivational theories explain important aspects of learning engagement, few provide a neurocognitively grounded account of how motivation becomes action. The Functional Motivation Model (FMM) proposes that goal-directed learning behavior emerges through the interaction of motivational drive, self-referential evaluation, and executive control processes. This study proposes a neuroeducational framework explaining how intention is translated into action and operationalizes the model through a questionnaire assessing its core components. Participants were 118 seventh- and eighth-grade students. The questionnaire assessed three dimensions of functional motivation: Initial Motivation, Self-Referential Evaluation and Executive Control. Confirmatory factor analysis, reliability analyses, inter-factor correlations, and associations with mathematics achievement were conducted. Findings provided preliminary support for the refined three-factor structure and indicated promising psychometric properties. Self-referential evaluation and executive control showed stronger associations with achievement than initial motivation. The findings provide preliminary empirical support for the proposed FMM framework and its questionnaire-based operationalization. The model suggests that academic difficulties may arise from breakdowns in different functional conditions involved in translating intention into action and provides a framework for examining three functional conditions underlying goal-directed learning: Do I want this? Can I do this? How do I do it? By integrating perspectives from educational psychology and neuroscience, the FMM offers both a theoretical framework and a practical tool for understanding students’ learning behavior.

title: Exploring Language and Literacy Instruction for Deaf and Hard of Hearing Students with Disabilities: Practices, Considerations, and Suggestions from Educational Professionals
container-title: Education Sciences
3fbdba9a1ec95a0be65fc7039c8e2257e2ad3b59.abstract: Students who are deaf or hard of hearing with disabilities (DWD) represent a diverse population whose language and communication development is shaped by access to language, learner characteristics, and educational contexts. Despite the importance of language and communication as foundations for literacy learning, little is known about how educational professionals implement and adapt instructional strategies to support DWD in school settings. This mixed-methods study explored current practices, considerations, and suggestions related to language and literacy instruction for DWD from the perspectives of educational professionals in British Columbia, Canada. Data were collected through an online survey completed by 123 educational professionals and six focus groups involving 15 participants, including teachers of the deaf and hard of hearing, classroom teachers, special education teachers, district specialists, and administrators. Findings indicated that educators employed a range of instructional strategies primarily focused on developing learners’ language and literacy skills, with comparatively less emphasis on strengthening communication partners’ capacity and adapting educational environments. Approximately one-third of respondents perceived that DWD’s needs were adequately met in each of the language and communication, social–behavioral, and literacy domains. Participants identified concerns related to language and communication access, shortages of trained personnel and professional learning opportunities, and insufficient collaboration. The findings highlight the need for strengths-based, student-centered approaches that promote learners’ active participation, build the capacity of communication partners (e.g., teachers, educational assistants, peers, family members), and enhance the accessibility of learning environments, alongside system-level supports that promote equitable and sustainable language and communication access for DWD.

title: Benchmarking Security and Reliability of Open-Source and Commercial Large Language Models in Financial-Domain Scenarios
container-title: FinTech
f9f52cb5979f9169d1e10c587fc7038eb5d8bb08.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are adopted in financial services, yet existing benchmarks provide limited insight into financial-domain capability, regulatory compliance-action performance, and security robustness. This study proposes a unified multidimensional evaluation framework for evaluating open-source and commercial LLMs in regulated financial environments. The framework comprises three complementary benchmark components: the Integrated Financial Benchmark (IFB), which integrates financial-domain benchmarks for capability evaluation; the newly developed RegBench for context-grounded regulatory compliance-action performance; and the newly developed FinSec-Eval-1000 for adversarial robustness. Eight LLMs, including five open-source and three commercial models, were evaluated using an inference pipeline, task-specific metrics, statistical testing, and a Composite Security Score (SS). Claude Sonnet 4.6 achieved the highest IFB performance (68.72%) and four-judge mean security robustness (97.43%), while GPT-5.1 achieved the highest RegBench performance (50.28%). Among open-source models, Gemma 3 12B led on IFB (63.50%), whereas Phi-3-small achieved the strongest open-source RegBench (49.22%) and four-judge mean security (92.78%) results, demonstrating that model rankings vary across evaluation dimensions. No detectable monotonic association was observed between financial capability and security robustness (Spearman’s ρ = 0.095, p = 0.823). The benchmarking framework provides a transparent and reproducible methodology for multidimensional LLM evaluation and supports informed model selection in regulated financial environments.

title: BioMetaHarmonizer: An Integrated Pipeline for Retrieval, Harmonization and Standardization of NCBI BioSample Metadata for Large-Scale Bacterial Genomic Epidemiological Analysis
container-title: Informatics
d3f7aa963715244b66d5a197b3e2ef2ccf03b4de.abstract: Large-scale comparative genomics and antimicrobial resistance surveillance depend on structured, machine-readable sample metadata, yet NCBI BioSample, the primary repository for microbial genomic provenance, contains heterogeneous submitter-supplied metadata despite field-specific validation. Attribute names can vary across submitters, date representations may require normalization, and geographic fields combine country, region, and locality information. Without harmonization and structured extraction, phylogeographic analysis, cross-sector AMR surveillance, and One Health source attribution at the scale of tens to hundreds of thousands of genomes can be labor-intensive and require manual preprocessing that does not scale. We designed BioMetaHarmonizer, an open-source Python package that directly fetches BioSample records from the NCBI Entrez API and transforms them into a standardized 53-column output in CSV, TSV, Excel, Parquet, or JSONL format through a modular harmonization pipeline covering attribute synonym resolution, ISO 8601 date normalization, geospatial parsing with ISO 3166-1 country-code assignment, and automated One Health category inference. Performance of BioMetaHarmonizer was evaluated using 17,573 Bacillus cereus group and 217,226 Klebsiella pneumoniae BioSample records. On a modest cloud virtual machine, the pipeline exhibited end-to-end processing in under 5 and 27 min, respectively, with One Health classification accuracies of 0.9488 and 0.9945. Source code is freely available under the MIT license.

title: Deferasirox, an Oral Iron Chelator, Confers Antidepressant and Procognitive Effects in a Rat Model of Depression: Hippocampal Ferroptosis, Synaptopathy, and Neurodegeneration
container-title: Pharmaceuticals
446baba147320f9cf28021101a775cf4b5215572.abstract: Background: Disrupted iron homeostasis is increasingly perceived as a key driver of major depressive disorder pathogenesis; hence, targeting ferroptotic cascades may reveal novel therapeutic targets. This study evaluated the neuroprotective potential of the oral iron chelator deferasirox (DEF) against chronic unpredictable mild stress (CUMS)-induced depressive-like behaviors and cognitive deficits in Wistar rats. Methods: We specifically explored whether DEF could provide neuroprotection by targeting ferroptotic and oxidative stress pathways. Male Wistar rats were exposed to a 6-week CUMS protocol and treated with DEF (10, 20, or 40 mg/kg). Results: CUMS-exposed rats exhibited significant anhedonia, behavioral despair, and impaired spatial and recognition memory. Further analyses revealed a reduction in colonic and choroid plexus occludin, reflecting compromised structural integrity of both the intestinal and blood-CSF barriers, accompanied by enhanced hippocampal iron accumulation with increased Acyl-CoA synthetase long-chain family member 4 (ACSL4), Acyl-CoA synthetase family member 2 (ACSF2), and citrate synthase expression, alongside exaggerated oxidative stress and deficient neuroprotective mediators, specifically BDNF and synaptophysin, and increased neurofibrillary tangle (NFT) deposition, collectively exacerbating neurodegenerative pathology. DEF treatment ameliorated most of these effects, significantly reducing iron deposition, attenuating ferroptosis-related signaling, reducing oxidative stress, diminishing the ongoing neurodegeneration, and replenishing the depleted pool of BDNF and synaptophysin, which was accompanied by a reduction in depressive-like symptoms and improved cognitive functions. Conclusions: These findings support a link between ferroptosis-related signaling and depression-like phenotypes, reinforcing the concept of a metal-driven component in depression pathophysiology and offering a mechanistic rationale for further exploring targeting ferroptotic pathways and central iron regulation as potential targeted strategies in depression management.

title: Threshold-Crossing Limits and Model-Fidelity Assessment of Supervised NLM Error Shaping for MMC Circulating-Current Control
container-title: Symmetry
db8fae7944cf6ea5ab3c44afb4fbcaa75e631b1a.abstract: Finite-level nearest-level modulation (NLM) couples modular multilevel converter (MMC) internal dynamics to a discontinuous arm-voltage execution error. Building on an established proportional reduced-order quasi-resonant (P-ROQR) circulating-current regulator and a Fourier-based NLM error-correction concept, this study investigates the interaction between harmonic pre-distortion and circulating-current control under discrete NLM execution. A unified energy/error model and an exact threshold-crossing representation show that sub-level pre-distortion can affect the converter only when an integer insertion command changes. However, threshold opportunity alone does not guarantee closed-loop improvement. A causal cycle-wise quantization-error shaping (QES) layer is therefore combined with a threshold-aware efficacy supervisor that rejects candidate shaping actions when they do not alter the discrete actuator or are predicted to increase the circulating-current response. During large operating-point changes, the QES path is temporarily blocked and is reactivated after coefficient reacquisition and smooth recovery. The fixed QES implementation is first examined in mean-arm and individual-submodule models, where its performance is shown to depend strongly on numerical and model fidelity. In the individual-submodule model, fixed QES reduces the selected high-order component but increases the total circulating-current rms and peak. In the ten-submodule-per-arm model, supervised QES reduces circulating-current rms relative to both fixed QES and the P-ROQR baseline, although its steady-state current peak and switching-transition count remain above the baseline values. During the tested power step, transient blocking keeps the peak circulating-current deviation close to the P-ROQR result while reducing the additional excursion introduced by fixed QES. These results support the use of local prediction to screen candidate shaping actions within the investigated simulation conditions; performance in larger MMC systems and hardware implementations remains to be established.

title: SAF-Net: Stage-Aware Semantic Allocation with Frequency-Refined Vision-Language Decoding for Medical Lesion Segmentation
container-title: Symmetry
9730c918d97a29c36de7858ce5027dd05bc65108.abstract: Medical lesion segmentation remains challenging due to ambiguous boundaries, heterogeneous appearances, and the limited ability of visual features alone to capture clinically meaningful semantics. Existing vision-language segmentation methods have demonstrated the value of textual guidance, but they often rely on fixed or shared textual representations across different decoder stages, despite the fact that visual features progressively evolve from coarse semantic representations to finer spatial details. To address this stage-wise representation mismatch, we propose SAF-Net, a stage-aware vision-language segmentation framework that couples stage-specific semantic allocation with frequency-refined progressive decoding. Specifically, Adaptive Hierarchical Text Allocation (AHTA) retains the hidden representations from all layers of a frozen medical language encoder and learns independent layer-mixing distributions for different text-guided decoder stages, enabling stage-specific semantic guidance without manually predefined layer-to-stage correspondence. Meanwhile, Frequency-Gated Spatial-aware Channel Attention (FGSCA) refines the incoming decoder features through complementary frequency-aware spatial-channel modeling before cross-modal interaction. By coordinating hierarchical textual semantics with frequency-aware visual refinement across progressive decoding stages, SAF-Net allows the representations participating in multimodal interaction to better adapt to the changing requirements of hierarchical decoding. Extensive experiments on QaTa-COV19 and MosMedData+ demonstrate the effectiveness and competitiveness of the proposed framework.

title: Interpretable machine learning model based on intratumoral and peritumoral MRI for predicting tumor budding grade in breast cancer
container-title: BMC Medical Imaging
fd809418d1a1f91f7f7bb1dc33dc53945a35b73d.abstract: Abstract Objective Tumor budding (TB) is a histopathological indicator associated with aggressive tumor behavior and poor prognosis in breast cancer. However, TB assessment is mainly dependent on postoperative pathological examination, limiting its availability for preoperative risk stratification and treatment decision-making. This study aimed to develop a non-invasive nomogram integrating intratumoral and peritumoral radiomic features with clinicopathological variables to predict the tumor budding grade of breast cancer. Methods Clinicopathological data of patients with pathologically confirmed invasive breast cancer were retrospectively analyzed, and their preoperative magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scans were collected. Volume of interests (VOIs) of the tumors were manually delineated on the dynamic contrast-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging (DCE-MRI) and diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) sequences. Peritumoral VOIs were obtained by expanding the intratumoral VOIs outward by 3 mm. Radiomic features were extracted and screened from the intratumoral, peritumoral VOIs separately, and six prediction models were established. A nomogram was further constructed by incorporating clinicopathological variables. The performance of all models was assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) with 95% confidence interval (95% CI). Calibration curves and decision curve analysis (DCA) were applied to evaluate the clinical applicability of the predictive models, and SHAP plots were used for further visual interpretation of the model results. Results A total of 281 patients with breast cancer were enrolled in this study, including 175 cases in the training set, 76 cases in the internal validation set and 30 cases in the external validation set. Among the clinicopathological variables, Ki-67 expression and enhancement pattern were significantly correlated with tumor budding grade, and the established clinicopathological model exhibited good predictive performance. The combined intratumoral-peritumoral model based on fused DCE-MRI and DWI features outperformed all other single models, with AUC values of 0.854, 0.760 and 0.755 in the training, internal validation and external validation sets, respectively. The nomogram model achieved even better predictive efficacy, with AUC values of 0.906, 0.845 and 0.825 in the training, internal validation and external validation sets, respectively. Conclusion The proposed MRI-based nomogram provides a reliable and interpretable approach for non-invasive preoperative prediction of tumor budding grade in breast cancer. By enabling early identification of patients with aggressive tumor characteristics before surgery, this model may facilitate individualized risk stratification and treatment planning, and represents a potential complementary tool to conventional pathological assessment. Further multicenter studies are warranted to validate its clinical applicability and promote its integration into personalized breast cancer management.

title: Task-Specific Impacts of Cognitive Fatigue on Subjective Experience and Psychomotor Performance
container-title: Human Factors: The Journal of the Human Factors and Ergonomics Society
522c0265a8e374ae7e4e7c27de993e0dcbdc142a.abstract: Objective To determine how cognitive fatigue (CF) affects subjective experience and reaction time (RT) performance across tasks with different processing demands (simple, go/no-go, choice), and whether these effects depend on the type of fatigue-inducing mental work. Background CF is a psychobiological state of subjective exhaustion from mental effort that can compromise workplace productivity and safety. Although slowed RT is an often-observed consequence of CF, it is unclear how this compares across RT paradigms and fatigue-inducing tasks. Method Using a remotely administered experiment, 402 participants completed a 60-minute CF (Math-Memory, Stroop, Time Load Dual-Back) or control (documentary) intervention. Subjective ratings (mental fatigue, motivation) and RT performance (simple, go/no-go, choice) were assessed pre- and post-intervention. Results Relative to control, all CF tasks increased subjective fatigue ( p < .001), while motivation declined following Dual-Back and Stroop ( p ≤ .030) but not Math-Memory. Simple and choice RT slowed significantly following all CF interventions vs control ( p < .010), with the greatest choice RT slowing after Stroop ( p ≤ .032). Only Stroop produced significant go/no-go RT slowing ( p = .004). Conclusion Subjective fatigue and simple RT were broadly sensitive to CF, indicating general psychomotor slowing. Conversely, motivation and higher-complexity RT measures showed task-specific effects, perhaps reflecting overlap between fatigue-inducing and RT task demands. Application Task type is important when considering RT as a fatigue assessment tool. These findings support multidimensional (subjective and RT) CF assessments and indicate that simple RT may be effective for rapid, broad fatigue monitoring, whereas complex RT metrics may be useful when exploring task-specific executive processing effects.

title: An Exploratory Study of Image-Guided Cochlear Implant Intervention on Articulation and Phonological Processing in Children With Speech Sound Disorders
container-title: American Journal of Speech-Language Pathology
90e2772f0c659288fc6e9f950066d0c1f1c71068.abstract: Purpose: Poor spectral clarity from cochlear implants (CIs) has been hypothesized to contribute to articulation and phonological processing deficits among children with CIs. Therefore, CI programming techniques that aim to improve spectral resolution may lead to improvements in articulation and phonological processing skills (i.e., phonological awareness as well as phonological and phonetic recoding). Method: We analyzed the articulation and phonological skills of 21 children with CIs (4.7–13.1 years old) with articulation and phonological processing deficits who were enrolled in a 2-year waitlist-deferred randomized controlled trial examining image-guided cochlear implant programming (IGCIP). In the clinical trial, participants were randomly assigned to receive IGCIP at varying time points throughout the study. Change over time in articulation and phonological processing was assessed in the subset of 21 children. Additionally, an exploratory analysis of the effect of IGCIP on articulation and phonological processing skills was completed. Results: Only articulation, not phonological processing, improved relative to age norms. IGCIP did not have a statistically significant effect on articulation or phonological processing in the first year of the study. However, participants who received IGCIP within the first year of the study did exhibit larger and clinically meaningful improvements in articulation scores compared with those who did not receive IGCIP. Conclusions: Articulation deficits, but not phonological processing deficits, improved over time among children with CIs. Future studies should assess the impact of IGCIP on articulation within a larger sample of CI users with articulation deficits to clarify its role in such improvements.

title: Toward Artificial Intelligence–Supported Development of Image-Based Tasks in Aphasia
container-title: American Journal of Speech-Language Pathology
ba6ad144f098a157b9ae0b01ca2b72c45041b0a8.abstract: Purpose: Images play a central role in language assessment and therapy for people with aphasia, yet the development of psychometrically robust image stimuli is often time consuming, costly, and difficult to tailor to specific research questions or individual patient needs. Recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI), particularly text-to-image generation models, offer new opportunities to rapidly produce high-quality, customizable visual stimuli. Despite this potential, methodological guidance for integrating AI-generated images into aphasia research and clinical practice remains limited. This tutorial aimed to provide practical recommendations for the use of AI text-to-image tools in developing image-based tasks for people with aphasia. Method: Using a case study framework, we demonstrate the development of a semantic judgment task with images generated with the help of the DALL-E 3 model. We outline key decision points that went into this process and provide recommendations across the major stages of task development: task conceptualization, stimulus design, image ideation, prompt engineering, and image quality evaluation by AI models. Results: We demonstrate that structured prompt engineering combined with systematic validation can yield high-quality, interpretable image stimuli suitable for aphasia tasks. The approach allows for flexible control over stimulus characteristics while maintaining consistency across experimental conditions. Conclusions: AI text-to-image generation offers a promising, scalable approach to developing customized image stimuli for aphasia research and clinical practice. We discuss methodological considerations, limitations, and future directions for the responsible integration of generative AI technologies into aphasia-related research and clinical applications.

title: Cognitive Digital Ocean: integration of quantum hybrid computing, digital twins and graph neural networks for bioresource and fleet management. Part 2
container-title: Fisheries
c40dddc14b2325b2b65698c06f7464e21fbbec8c.abstract: The paper presents the concept of the Cognitive Digital Ocean (CDO) – a multi level cyber physical system for managing the fishery complex, integrating quantum hybrid computing, physics informed neural networks (PINN), graph neural networks (GNN), a hierarchy of digital twins (from genome to global ocean), and fractal analysis of the spatial distribution of bioresources. Special attention is paid to the shipbuilding aspect: mathematical models of the ship power plant (SPP), controllable pitch propeller (CPP), propulsion complex, and hull hydrodynamics are presented. It is shown that solving the fundamental Millennium Problem – the Navier Stokes equations – on quantum computers opens up fundamental possibilities for hydrodynamic forecasting with a horizon of up to 30 days. The system is aimed at solving the strategic tasks of the Russian Federal Agency for Fisheries (Rosrybolovstvo) until 2030: increasing production by 25%, digital transformation, and technological sovereignty. The limitations of the applicability of quantum methods are considered and engineering workarounds are proposed.

title: AI-Assisted Analysis of Spontaneous Affective Facial Responses for Cognitive Status Assessment in Older Adults: Exploratory Feasibility Study
container-title: JMIR Formative Research
6543568e570b9512b4946b58992f226b2f1a3be5.abstract: Background As Taiwan enters a super-aged society, the prevalence of dementia continues to rise, highlighting the need for scalable, noninvasive approaches to identify behavioral alterations associated with cognitive decline. AI-based analysis of spontaneous affective facial responses has emerged as a potential digital phenotyping tool, but its feasibility for assessing cognitive performance remains underexplored. Objective This study aimed to examine the feasibility of using AI-derived spontaneous affective facial response metrics, including affective expression congruency and onset latency, to characterize differences across cognitive performance levels in older adults with healthy cognition (HC), mild cognitive impairment (MCI), or dementia. Methods A total of 60 participants (HC, MCI, and dementia; 20 per group) were presented with positive and negative emotion-eliciting videos and completed Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) recall and calculation tasks. Facial expressions were video-recorded and analyzed using a convolutional neural network–based AI system. AI-derived metrics included affective expression congruency, categorized as congruent, neutral, or incongruent according to the detected facial response, and affective expression onset latency, defined as the time from stimulus presentation to the emergence of a nonneutral facial expression detected by the AI model. Group differences were analyzed using 1-way ANOVA, Pearson chi-square or Fisher-Freeman-Halton exact tests, Bonferroni-adjusted pairwise post hoc comparisons, analysis of covariance adjusting for age and education, and exploratory receiver operating characteristic analyses. Results Affectively congruent responses were generally less frequent among participants with lower cognitive performance. During the 14-second positive stimulus, congruent positive expressions were observed in 65% (13/20) of HC participants, 20% (4/20) of MCI participants, and 0% (0/20) of participants with dementia. During the 48-second negative stimulus, congruent negative expressions were observed in 60% (12/20) of HC participants compared with 5% (1/20) of both MCI and dementia participants. Onset latency differed significantly across groups for the 14-second positive stimulus (F2,57=19.63; P<.001; η2=0.41), 52-second positive stimulus (F2,57=4.25; P=.02; η2=0.13), 48-second negative stimulus (F2,57=15.61; P<.001; η2=0.35), and MMSE-based cognitive-task condition (F2,57=11.28; P<.001; η2=0.28). After adjustment for age and education, the group effect remained significant for all latency outcomes (F2,55=3.89-10.68; all P≤.03; partial η2=0.12-0.28). Exploratory receiver operating characteristic analyses showed stronger separation in several HC vs MCI and HC vs dementia comparisons, whereas MCI vs dementia comparisons showed limited separability. Conclusions AI-assisted analysis of spontaneous affective facial responses revealed differences in expression congruency and onset latency across cognitive performance levels. These preliminary findings suggest that AI-derived facial behavioral metrics may serve as noninvasive adjunctive features for observational cognitive assessment. However, the findings should be interpreted cautiously because of the exploratory design, modest sample size, and absence of internal or external validation.

title: Cognitive frailty typologies and subsequent dementia in a large representative sample of the English population
container-title: Communications Medicine
bff347764d292b0f23527266b128282b945e49b8.abstract: Abstract Background Cognitive Frailty (CF), the coexistence of mild cognitive impairment with physical frailty, may represent an intermediate state between functional vulnerability and preclinical dementia. Its potential reversibility makes it an important target for prevention. Distinguishing patterns of CF that are more and less likely to lead to dementia, and associated factors, is important for developing interventions. Methods Using data from the English Longitudinal Study of Ageing (Waves 4-9), we examined different typologies of CF based on specific cognitive impairments demonstrated. We compared longitudinal outcomes of incident dementia over 10 years for the different typologies. We also examined the impact of inequalities (Index of Multiple Deprivation (IMD) and household wealth), cognitive reserve (low education), and psychosocial factors (depression and loneliness) on the longitudinal models. Results CF groups with executive function (using verbal fluency) and/or processing speed impairment (Group 1) are distinguished from those with memory impairment only (Group 2) or impaired memory and executive function and/or processing speed (Group 3). Inequalities, cognitive reserve and psychosocial factors all show association with CF likelihood, but education (odds ratio (OR) of no qualifications compared to degree/higher education = 1.632 (Group 1) and 3.436 (Group 3)), IMD (OR 1.656 (Group 1 quintile 5), 2.083 (Group 3 quintile 4) compared to quintile 1) and loneliness (OR 1.208 (Group 1), 1.185 (Group 3)) are only associated with CF where executive function/processing speed are key characteristics. Longitudinally, only CF groupings with memory impairment (OR 2.024, Group 2; 2.733, Group 3) are predictive of dementia. Conclusions Distinguishing typologies of CF and associated risk factors is important for estimating future dementia risk, and for targeted design of interventions.

title: Ethnoracial and Linguistic Diversity in Treatment Research for Primary Progressive Aphasia: A Systematic Review
container-title: American Journal of Speech-Language Pathology
b2219cacbe69270a6e4d693c59eaee017b9bb352.abstract: Purpose: This systematic review article sought to characterize the ethnoracial and linguistic representation of participants in the nonpharmacological intervention literature for primary progressive aphasia (PPA) and primary progressive apraxia of speech (PPAOS). In addition, we aimed to identify which social determinants of health (SDOH) factors are most frequently reported across studies. Method: We performed a comprehensive search across six electronic databases: OVID Medline, OVID PsycINFO, EBSCO Medline, EBSCO CINAHL Plus, Embase, and Web of Science, as well as additional published literature not indexed in these databases. We identified 149 original studies that administered neuromodulation and/or speech-language interventions to individuals with PPA or PPAOS and reported communication outcomes relative to a baseline or control group. From these studies, we extracted data on participants' race, ethnicity, spoken languages, occupation, years of education, and other relevant sociodemographic variables. Results: Ethnoracial and linguistic diversity in the current PPA literature is limited and underrepresented. Among studies that reported the extracted variables, the majority of participants were identified as non-Hispanic White, and most studies were conducted in the United States. English was the most commonly reported spoken language and was frequently used as an inclusion criterion. Regarding SDOH, participants tend to have medium–high education and hold higher skill-level occupations. Very few studies reported retirement status and whether retirement was due to symptom onset. Conclusions: Current intervention research for PPA and PPAOS lacks ethnoracial and linguistic diversity. This underrepresentation is further compounded by limited reporting of factors related to SDOH. The concentration of research in homogenous populations limits the generalizability of current findings and restricts their relevance for managing PPA and PPAOS across diverse demographic, cultural, linguistic, and socioeconomic contexts. Future research on treatment should not only ensure comprehensive reporting of participant characteristics but also actively expand the inclusivity of recruitment practices.

title: The Influence of Narrative Intervention on Mandarin-Speaking Children at Risk for Developmental Language Disorder: A Pilot Study
container-title: Language, Speech, and Hearing Services in Schools
09a1e8343d2d990c72a222426c59ccb4f05467b0.abstract: Purpose: The purpose of this pilot study was to investigate narrative interventions for Mandarin-speaking children at risk (AR) for developmental language disorders and compare the effectiveness of one-on-one intervention (OI) versus group intervention (GI). Method: Twenty-eight AR children ( M age = 6 years and 4 months) were divided into OI ( n = 9), GI ( n = 9), and control ( n = 10) groups. We conducted a 4-week narrative intervention using the STEPS-STORY narrative therapy. We compared macrostructure (story structure, structural complexity), general microstructure (productivity, diversity, complexity, grammaticality), and fine-grained microstructure ( ba / bei , negation, classifiers, aspect markers). Results: The pilot study demonstrates that both OI and GI enhance the narrative abilities of AR children. The similarities lie in the fact that, in the posttest, both the OI and GI demonstrated score gains on the ba of the fine-grained microstructure, with large effect sizes observed in the OI group and small effect sizes in the GI group, relative to the control group. The differences are as follows: Compared to the control group, the OI outperformed the GI in several areas. In the posttest, the OI group showed score gains with medium effect sizes for total number of utterances, large effect sizes for total number of words, and small effect sizes for grammatically well-formed utterances within the general microstructure, as well as medium effect sizes for perfective aspect markers and progressive aspect markers within the fine-grained microstructure, all compared to the control group. In the follow-up test, the OI group demonstrated a small effect size in score gains for negation within the fine-grained microstructure relative to the control group. Conversely, compared to the control group, the GI group performed better in other areas. In the posttest, the GI group showed a small effect size in score gains for the number of different words (NDW) within the general microstructure compared to the control group. In the follow-up test, the GI group exhibited small effect sizes for structural complexity of the macrostructure and NDW of the general microstructure, as well as a large effect size for percentage of complex utterances of the general microstructure, relative to the control group. Conclusions: Narrative intervention has a positive impact on the narrative abilities of Mandarin-speaking AR children. The different modes of intervention service delivery (one-on-one vs. group) explored in this study have both similarities and differences in their effects on AR children. Supplemental Material: https://doi.org/10.23641/asha.34818273

title: Enhancing Health Literacy in Communication Sciences and Disorders
container-title: American Journal of Speech-Language Pathology
44be26248aed7bf2d2d653fe6be54bf067420640.abstract: Purpose: This review article provides an integrated synthesis of health literacy within communication sciences and disorders (CSD), with emphasis on conceptual frameworks, clinical applications, and educational considerations relevant to speech-language pathology and audiology. Method: This narrative review synthesizes current literature and evidence-based practices to connect health literacy frameworks with clinical communication, patient education, and professional training in CSD. Results: Limited health literacy is prevalent among individuals with communication disorders and is associated with poorer health outcomes and reduced engagement in care. Key strategies include the use of plain language, multimodal communication supports, and health literacy–informed assessment and intervention approaches to improve clinician–patient interactions. Conclusions: Integrating health literacy into routine clinical practice and CSD education is essential for improving patient understanding, supporting shared decision making, and enhancing health outcomes. Coordinated efforts across clinical, educational, and organizational contexts are needed to reduce communication barriers and advance equitable, patient-centered care.

title: Does Participation in a Story Retell Affect Performance on Comprehension Questions for Kindergartners?
container-title: Journal of Speech, Language, and Hearing Research
4a2d54b3ee22c2b54ed11d53b3026625b920cc82.abstract: Purpose: The purpose of this research note is to contribute to the literature on language comprehension screening by examining kindergarteners' performance on two subtests included in the Virginia Language and Literacy Screening System: a narrative retell and comprehension questions. Method: A three-level hierarchical linear model with students nested within classrooms within schools was used to examine whether participation in the narrative retell affected performance on the comprehension questions related to the narrative. A total of 7,557 students participated in the narrative retell and the comprehension questions, and 9,859 participated in only the comprehension questions. Results: Students who participated in the retell and the comprehension questions outperformed those who participated in only the comprehension questions. The difference was statistically significant in a multilevel model controlling for demographic variables, b = 0.229, SE = 0.062, t (16, 432) = 3.68, p < .001, Cohen's d = 0.1. Conclusions: The difference in scores is minimal; however, the significant results suggest that participation in the retell may contribute to scores on the comprehension questions. Possible explanations for the positive effect and implications for instruction are discussed.

title: Formulation, In Vitro and In Vivo Evaluation of Lutein–Myo-Inositol Microspheres in a Letrozole-Induced Rat Model of PCOS
container-title: ASSAY and Drug Development Technologies
582be50a1fca86ffea0c8c191d2fa84cf23cfe4e.abstract: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) is a prevalent and complex hormone-metabolic condition that impacts females of reproductive age. Current pharmacological treatments often address limited symptoms, may involve long-term use of synthetic drugs, and are frequently associated with adverse effects and limited patient adherence. In recent years, natural therapeutic agents such as Lutein and Myo-inositol have acquired increasing interest due to their promising biological properties and minimal side effects. Strong antioxidant lutein aids in lowering inflammation and oxidative stress, while Myo-inositol, a naturally occurring sugar alcohol, has insulin-sensitizing and ovulation-inducing effects, making them ideal candidates for addressing the multifaceted pathophysiology of PCOS. Nevertheless, the application of these compounds in therapy is restricted by their limited solubility, reduced bioavailability, and brief half-life. To overcome these challenges, the present research focused on the development and assessment of sustained-release poly-herbal microspheres incorporating Lutein and Myo-inositol using the emulsification method. Nine different formulations (F1 to F9) were prepared and characterized for in vitro parameters. Among the nine formulations developed, one optimized formulation demonstrated high encapsulation efficiency (>90%), satisfactory production yield (>85%), and sustained drug release of approximately 90% over 8 h. In the letrozole-induced PCOS rat model, treatment significantly reduced malondialdehyde (MDA) levels and increased glutathione (GSH) levels compared with the disease control group ( p < 0.001). Histopathological evaluation showed a marked reduction in cystic follicles and restoration of normal ovarian morphology in the treated group. Furthermore, in vivo efficacy was confirmed through histopathological examination of ovarian tissues in animal models, where treated groups, especially T3, receiving the highest concentration demonstrated restoration of normal ovarian architecture, reduction in cystic follicles, and improved follicular development. These outcomes support the hypothesis that a combination of Lutein and Myo-inositol, when delivered through a sustained-release microsphere system, can effectively target oxidative stress, insulin resistance, hormonal imbalance, and ovarian dysfunction, which are central to PCOS pathogenesis.

title: Comparative Accuracy and Safety of Large Language Models in Glaucoma Knowledge Assessment
container-title: Journal of Glaucoma
a283f6d33ddcb2465c7a1011cdc00a5179e11659.abstract: Précis: Across glaucoma MCQs, GPT-5.2, Gemini 3 Pro, and Claude Opus 4.5 were highly accurate, whereas DeepSeek-V3.2 underperformed; potentially harmful wrong answers were uncommon. Purpose: To compare the accuracy and potential patient-safety risk of four large language models (LLMs) on glaucoma multiple-choice questions (MCQs). Methods: DeepSeek-V3.2, GPT-5.2 (via ChatGPT), Gemini 3 Pro, and Claude Opus 4.5 were tested on two American Academy of Ophthalmology datasets: 129 text-only AAO ONE Network glaucoma self-assessment questions and 32 text-only Basic and Clinical Science Course (BCSC) glaucoma study questions. Each item was queried once per model using a standardized prompt in a fresh session. Accuracy was compared using Cochran’s Q and pairwise exact McNemar tests with Holm adjustment. Potentially harmful wrong answers (HW2) were coded using a prespecified rubric. Results: In AAO ONE, accuracy was 69.0% for DeepSeek-V3.2, 93.0% for GPT-5.2, 92.2% for Gemini 3 Pro, and 96.1% for Claude Opus 4.5 (Q=65.17, P <0.0001). DeepSeek-V3.2 was significantly less accurate than the other three models; differences among the other models were not significant. In BCSC, accuracy was 65.6%, 93.8%, 84.4%, and 87.5%, respectively (Q=18.00, P =0.0004); GPT-5.2 outperformed DeepSeek-V3.2 after correction. A post hoc item-level screen classified 38/161 questions (23.6%) as directly HW2-eligible; four HW2 events occurred and did not differ significantly across models. Conclusions: GPT-5.2, Gemini 3 Pro and Claude Opus 4.5 achieved high accuracy on text-only glaucoma MCQs, whereas DeepSeek-V3.2 underperformed. Harmful errors were uncommon but present, underscoring the need for clinician oversight.

title: Differential Accuracy of Semantic Versus Phonological Speech Error Transcription in Aphasia: Comparing Large Language Model (Whisper) to Clinician (Speech-Language Pathologist) Performance
container-title: Journal of Speech, Language, and Hearing Research
537426d0a7a0d28e1c795fb11984c36b511437ba.abstract: Purpose: Patient speech samples provide insights into cognitive and linguistic status, yet their utilization has been limited by labor-intensive manual transcription. Advances in automated speech recognition (ASR) with large language models (LLMs) potentially save time, but performance on impaired speech, such as due to poststroke aphasia, remains understudied. Method: We transcribed 4,535 trials of the Philadelphia Naming Test (PNT) administered to 26 people with aphasia (PWA) using OpenAI's Whisper speech-to-text LLM. These ASR transcripts were compared with gold-standard transcriptions by an experienced speech-language pathologist (SLP). Clinician–LLM match or mismatch in transcription was analyzed across speech-error types (semantic vs. phonemic), patient severities, and word frequency. Results: For each 175-trial PNT, transcriptions by SLP required 180 ± 40 min versus 2.3 ± 0.5 min by Whisper. Compared to > 95% match rate with SLP transcripts for trained humans, Whisper achieved an overall match rate of 75.52%, subdivided as 88.83% match on correct PNT trials, 92.22% on semantic errors, and 23.05% for trials with phonemic errors by PWA. Western Aphasia Battery–Aphasia Quotient scores correlated with match rate ( R 2 = .196, p = .023) and hallucination rate ( R 2 = .291, p = .0048). Low-frequency words showed higher mismatch than medium- or high-frequency words (analysis of variance F = 14.26, p < .001). Conclusions: Whisper reliably transcribed semantic but not phonological errors, suggesting automation is best for fluent aphasia types with less phonemic distortions. This study benchmarks LLM transcription for impaired speech, offering a scalable alternative to manual transcription that may streamline clinical and research workflows. Supplemental Material: https://doi.org/10.23641/asha.34790292

title: Addressing threats to validity in large dataset research
container-title: PLOS Medicine
f22373d1ffafbb3c4ca546bceacb22f54fa635cd.abstract: Summary points Large dataset research offers new opportunities across biomedicine, but it also faces major threats to validity. These threats are underappreciated and often not recognized or managed appropriately. We dissect here 4 major types of validity threats: (1) P -value inflation and trivial effects; (2) residual and differential confounding across multiple sites; (3) issues surrounding harmonization and measurement error; and (4) causal identification in the presence of rich covariates. For each of them we provide their theoretical background, empirical evidence, and simulations that showcase how they operate. We make recommendations that may offer guidance for analyses and inferences from large datasets across biomedicine. These include: deciding on the placement in a continuum of exploration versus targeted causation; evaluating both statistical significance and effect sizes; modeling site heterogeneity; treating harmonization as measurement modeling; considering causal diagrams to guide adjustment; checking covariate balance; embedding sensitivity analysis and exploration of robustness; reporting limitations structurally; considering falsification calibration of performance; considering multi-analyst approaches; enhancing sharing, openness, transparency, and documentation; and considering encompassing analyses rather than least publishable units. Improving large dataset research and adequately addressing these threats is essential for the integrity of the scientific record and eventually also for informing policy and clinical practice.

title: Salivary microbiome, socioeconomic status, and cognitive performance: Triangulating the relationship
container-title: PLOS One
900c75d87c6cc3c60af6305c71352c54ace522bf.abstract: Research increasingly demonstrates that endogenous bacterial communities (microbiomes) are associated with both cognitive functioning and socioeconomic status (SES). In this study, we used a metagenomics approach to characterize oral microbiome diversity in Hispanic and African American children aged 6–16 years. We examined how microbiome composition and SES were related to cognitive performance, as assessed by the Wechsler Intelligence Scale for Children (WISC). Our findings indicate that SES and the microbiome contributed complementary, comparably sized influences on cognitive functioning. Together, variability in conventional SES indicators and microbiome composition accounted for approximately 10% of the variability in WISC scores. These results highlight the importance of integrating both social and biological determinants of health when studying cognitive performance and other psychological outcomes.

title: Predicting Public Engagement with Tourism Videos Across Unseen YouTube Channels Using Text-Informed Ensembles
6b8f9fff9365123f354b2a969a1f3187f808f177.abstract: Abstract Public engagement counters for tourism videos reflect both content and exposure-related conditions. We analysed 4,231 public YouTube tourism videos, including 3,271 no longer than 60 s, and modelled contemporaneous views, likes and comments. A leakage-controlled neural branch combined train-fitted text, thumbnail and structured inputs; its predictions were blended with a validation-selected XGBoost metadata expert using validation-only convex weights. Across five randomized channel-grouped splits, the hybrid achieved mean R² values of 0.538, 0.516 and 0.495 for views, likes and comments, improving on XGBoost by 0.078, 0.063 and 0.064. Corresponding strict-short-video R² values were 0.529, 0.481 and 0.504. Removing text from training and evaluation reduced rebuilt-hybrid R² by 0.057–0.072 across outcomes. Cultural supervision and diffusion did not improve prediction, while removing the sparsely available visual branch improved the neural branch. Chronological transport was substantially weaker, particularly for comments. The results support a text-informed ensemble for channel-held-out contemporaneous engagement prediction and delimit the conditions under which its performance transfers.

title: Learning-based multi-criteria decision-making model for sawmill location problems
container-title: Journal of Transport and Land Use
23230e4605741016365d1e73d2e93e24240ca22e.abstract: Strategically locating a sawmill is vital for enhancing the efficiency, profitability, and sustainability of timber supply chains. Our study proposes a Learning-Based Multi-Criteria Decision-Making (LB-MCDM) framework that integrates machine learning (ML) with GIS-based spatial location analysis via MCDM. The proposed framework provides a data-driven, unbiased, and replicable approach to assessing site suitability. We demonstrate the utility of the proposed model through a case study in Mississippi (MS). We apply five ML algorithms (Random Forest Classifier, Support Vector Classifier, XGBoost Classifier, Logistic Regression, and K-Nearest Neighbors Classifier) to identify the most suitable sawmill locations in MS. Among these models, the Random Forest Classifier achieves the highest performance. We use the SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) technique to determine the relative importance of each criterion, revealing the Supply-Demand Ratio, a composite feature that reflects local market competition dynamics, as the most influential factor, followed by Road, Rail Line and Urban Area Distance. The validation of suitability maps generated by our LB-MCDM model suggests that 10%-11% of the MS landscape is highly suitable for sawmill location.

title: Surrogate-assisted multi-objective topology optimization design method for prefabricated large-span Suspen-Dome based on structural-mapping-method and improved-PGSA
container-title: PLOS One
ac9820a8c32c2ade118ddb61ca487ac385a4f891.abstract: Existing optimization studies on large-span Suspen-Dome structures have mainly focused on either size optimization of the upper reticulated shell or topology optimization of the lower cable-strut system. Such a separated strategy prevents the integrated optimization of the whole structure, restricts the design space, and limits further improvement in structural performance. This study investigates the integrated optimization of prefabricated large-span Suspen-Dome structures by simultaneously considering the size, geometric configuration, and topology of the upper reticulated shell, together with the topology and cable forces of the lower cable-strut system. To ensure practical applicability, the design variables are classified into topological and size variables. The former define the structural configuration and connectivity, while the latter determine material-related properties. The optimization aims to maximize stiffness and minimize weight, subject to member slenderness, material strength, local stability, and overall structural stability constraints. An Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP)-based candidate screening model is introduced to accelerate the optimization algorithm and reduce unnecessary ANSYS analyses. A partial full-stress design (PFSD) concept is proposed, in which the reticulated shell serves as a structural safety reserve. The proposed structural mapping method-improved plant growth algorithm (SMM-iPGSA) is validated through two examples. Results show that the optimized structures exhibit improved stability, more uniform stress distribution, and displacements well below the allowable limits.

title: Cohort Profile: The Adolescent and Young Adult Tracking Engagement and Management Skills (AYA TEAMS) longitudinal cohort of childhood cancer survivors in the United States
container-title: PLOS One
1109d6759a922020e4ac0677b5451cb011f39131.abstract: Purpose To describe the rationale, methods, and baseline sample descriptives of the Adolescent and Young Adult Tracking Engagement and Management Skills (AYA TEAMS) cohort. The AYA TEAMS study is a longitudinal observational cohort study that aims to identify determinants and patterns of self-management and engagement in cancer-related long-term follow-up (LTFU) care and validate a novel transition readiness assessment among adolescent and young adult (AYA) survivors of childhood cancer. Participants AYA survivors of childhood cancer (ages 16–25) and their caregivers were enrolled from 3 large pediatric oncology centers across the United States from 2020–2022 and followed for 2 years (minimum) to 3 years and 3 months (if transferred to adult care). AYA inclusion criteria were: past childhood cancer diagnosis (treated in a pediatric oncology setting), at least 2 years off-treatment, 5 years since diagnosis, engaged with the participating pediatric health care system (any department/specialty) within the last 18 months, cognitively able to complete study procedures, and English speaking. AYA completed a comprehensive battery of measures including assessments of self-management and transition readiness at baseline and annually for 2 years. For AYA transferred to adult care, separate measures were administered at the time of transfer (following last pediatric visit) and 15 months post transfer. Caregivers (English or Spanish-speaking) completed a single survey at baseline to capture family functioning, psychosocial risk, and transition readiness. Cancer diagnosis, treatment modalities, treatment-related late effects, and engagement in LTFU care were captured via electronic medical record review. In total, 709 AYA were enrolled and 587 were included in the final cohort [Mean age = 19.7 years, 52.5% female, 38.2% from racial and/or ethnic minoritized groups (REMG)]. The cohort was on average 7.3 years old at the time of diagnosis and 10.5 years off treatment. Half (52.5%) were survivors of leukemia/lymphoma, 38.0% solid tumors, and 9.5% central nervous system tumors. Three hundred and ninety-nine caregivers participated (90% mothers). Findings to date Enrolled AYA excluded from the baseline cohort were more likely to be male, from REMG, and/or to enroll without a caregiver. Baseline cohort differences between study sites emerged for age, race and ethnicity, socioeconomic status, and treatment modalities and intensity. Future plans Data collection was completed in April 2025. Findings from this cohort will elucidate important predictors of self-management and engagement in recommended annual LTFU and inform the design of interventions to reduce disengagement in LTFU.

title: A quantitative assessment of Chinese county high school policies using the PMC index model
container-title: PLOS One
afba73f7bf58341a21e14fbca0d64f556f9ce764.abstract: The county high school policies (CHSPs) is crucial for improving the quality of basic education in China’s counties and promoting rural social development. As policy documents are the foundational elements of policy systems, it is crucial to evaluate current policy texts, identify their shortcomings, and provide empirical evidence for future policy development. This study collected 55 policy texts from provincial and municipal governments, utilizing the Policy Modeling Consistency index model to evaluate 14 representative policies. The results indicate that all the assessed policies fall within the“pass”,“good”,or“with distinction” score category, with no substandard policies identified and none achieving a “perfect” score.A detailed analysis identifies critical policy shortcomings, including the prioritization of short-to-medium-term strategies over long-term planning, fragmented enrollment systems, insufficient campus culture development, as well as limited career guidance, mental health support,and policy guidance for home-school-community joint education. Local governments adopt a conservative stance on educational policy evaluation and systemic institutional reforms.To address these issues, this study recommends that local governments integrate the enrollment systems of public and private high schools within their jurisdictions, strengthen the prohibition of on cross-regional enrollment, increase investment in students’ career guidance and mental health education, and launch more programs to encourage parents and communities to participate in school education. Moreover, the central government should urge local authorities to accelerate reforms in the high school education system.

title: SpatioCAD: Context-aware graph diffusion model for pinpointing spatially variable genes in heterogeneous tissues
container-title: PLOS Computational Biology
b31f489578062efbaa32486cbe3d38e357ae743c.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics enables comprehensive characterization of tissue architecture, and the identification of spatially variable genes (SVGs) is a critical step for defining region-specific molecular markers and uncovering spatially regulated mechanisms across diverse biological contexts. However, most existing methods for SVG detection overlook cell density variations, a major confounding factor in complex tissues such as tumors, where heterogeneous cellularity frequently introduces false-positive calls. Here we present SpatioCAD, a computational framework that explicitly decouples genuine spatial expression patterns from confounding effects driven by cellularity. SpatioCAD introduces a graph diffusion model that inherently incorporates cell-density-aware conditions to simulate expression propagation, supporting the identification of SVGs across a broad range of expression levels. Systematic evaluations on simulated datasets demonstrate its superior statistical power and specificity. Applied to breast cancer, lung cancer, and glioma datasets, SpatioCAD identifies functionally diverse SVGs, including low‑abundance transcripts with established roles in tumor progression, while also recapitulates biologically meaningful tissue architecture features. Importantly, SpatioCAD is fast and scalable to large tissues.

title: Bi-Mamba-Load: A bidirectional structured state space model with sequence relationship adaptive perception for electricity load forecasting
container-title: PLOS One
24e6f29992c4c050cb67307763c6a6fac495daad.abstract: The accurate prediction of electricity load is a critical component for smart-grid management, energy allocation, and grid stability. Traditional statistical methods and Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) often struggle with nonlinear relationships or long-range temporal dependencies, whereas Transformer architectures incur quadratic complexity in the sequence length. The Structured State Space Model Mamba provides linear sequence modeling but uses a unidirectional scan and a fixed treatment of multivariate dependencies. To address these limitations, we propose Bi-Mamba-Load, which combines a bidirectional Mamba encoder, a custom forget gate, and a Sequence Relationship Adaptive Perception (SRAP) module. Both encoder branches operate exclusively on the observed historical window, so no observations from the forecasting horizon are used as inputs. SRAP computes Spearman correlation statistics from the training split and performs dataset-level selection between channel-independent and channel-mixing tokenization; the selected route remains fixed for all samples in that dataset. Experiments across eight benchmark datasets indicate competitive or superior forecasting accuracy against the evaluated baselines while retaining linear scaling with the input length, subject to the constant-factor overhead of bidirectional scanning.

title: Implementation of The Smart Environment Concept in Waste Bank-Based Waste Management in The Mandalika SEZ:  A Narrative Literature Review and  Prescriptive Conceptual Model
container-title: Indonesian Journal of Applied Science and Technology
e1bff3fea3a83b873e64d94799f360a8e4450a82.abstract: The Mandalika Special Economic Zone (SEZ) has experienced rapid growth driven by tourism and international sporting events, leading to a surge in waste generation. This article synthesizes literature from 2016 to 2026 on applying the Smart Environment concept to waste bank-based management and, on that basis, proposes a prescriptive conceptual model for Mandalika; it does not evaluate the effectiveness of any program already in operation. A narrative review of 17 documents (16 journal or proceedings articles and one preprint) reveals four key findings: (1) smart environment integrates digital technology with community participation; (2) waste banks offer economic and environmental benefits, though success depends on public knowledge, social norms, and operator capacity; (3) Mandalika’s waste, according to one field measurement and to secondary media and program reports kept outside the review corpus, is dominated by organic matter, with sharp volume spikes during major events; and (4) empirical data on the Putri Nyale Waste Bank remain limited to descriptive accounts. Consequently, this study proposes a prescriptive model combining waste banks for inorganic waste, composting or biodigestion for organic waste, and a layered digital architecture that links waste bank records, waste-generation monitoring, SEZ management dashboards, and the Go Mandalika tourism platform, supported by youth environmental cadres. The model has not been empirically validated.

title: Whose Judgement Counts? An Appraisal-Informed Critical Discourse Analysis of Educational AI Communications
container-title: International Journal of Language and Literary Studies
ca7cc3247b2bab2b1cb7f34026579cd3052ba99d.abstract: Public guidance on generative AI asks students to exercise judgement while institutions and platforms define the conditions of use. This study examines how these texts distribute authority over writing, evidence and assessment. The purposively selected corpus comprises eight official webpages from three UK universities and Google and captions from three educational videos, retrieved in October 2026. Appraisal-informed critical discourse analysis examines 30 decision-focused units: passages addressing a particular choice or responsibility. Analysis also considers modality and legitimation, meaning the reasons offered to justify a practice. The main finding is boundary maintenance: texts distinguish what fluent writing, technical capability or disclosure can establish about learning, reliability and permission. University guidance and Gemini promotion both value learner participation, although they serve different purposes. Staff guidance also encourages discussion of assessment criteria. These findings suggest that teachers should explain acceptable assistance, student responsibilities and opportunities to question criteria. The small documentary corpus supports interpretation of published communications, not conclusions about classroom practice or AI effectiveness.
