title: Role of Speech-Language Pathologists Working With Individuals With Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder: A Scoping Review of Countries Within the Mutual Recognition Agreement
container-title: Perspectives of the ASHA Special Interest Groups
be626ff04804cc195b52caf8ee7d4af16c8dd274.abstract: Background: Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) is a prevalent neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by inattention, hyperactivity, and impulsivity, which can have a significant impact on an individual's functioning. Speech-language pathologists (SLPs) within the United Kingdom, the United States, Canada, New Zealand, Australia, and Ireland, with their expertise in communication disorders, could play a crucial role in the assessment, intervention, and management of ADHD-related communication. The authors explored the current role of SLPs in the assessment and management of individuals with ADHD within multidisciplinary teams across six countries. Specifically, how do the policies and practices of Mutual Recognition Agreement (MRA) countries define and support the role of SLPs in ADHD management, and what lessons can be applied to the Australian context? Method: This study performed a scoping review of literature from MRA countries plus research published in peer-reviewed journals in English within the past 20 years that references ADHD and the role of the SLP. Content analysis categorized the data into seven themes. Results: The search found 17 articles relevant to the research question and five guidelines from MRA countries. Of the MRA countries, all had a practice guideline; New Zealand shares a practice guideline with Australia. Conclusions: Contemporary research indicates that SLPs are rarely included explicitly in the management of ADHD across the lifespan. Recommendations are made for the potential role and scope of practice of the SLP when working with these individuals.

title: Professional identity of a foreign language teacher in a multicultural classroom: from disorientation to axiological certainty
container-title: The Education and science journal
8b130b9f7ccea9dc8dfeb340c8d6cc2d0739b49c.abstract: Introduction. The internationalisation of higher education in Russia has resulted in a consistent increase in multicultural cohorts within universities. This development has significantly altered the working conditions for teachers of foreign languages and Russian as a foreign language. Nevertheless, the role of the teacher has remained marginal in scholarly inquiry, and the transformation of their professional identity in response to engagement with cultural diversity has been inadequately explored. Aim. The present study aims to elucidate the process of professional identity formation among foreign language teachers within multicultural groups by analysing disorienting events, perceptions of fairness, language policies, and self-definitions in the role of mediator. Methodology and research methods. The methodological foundation of this study is a synthesis of J. Mezirow’s concept of transformative learning and the processual approach to professional identity. The empirical research was conducted within the qualitative paradigm. The primary data collection method comprised semi-structured interviews with 87 teachers from five Russian universities. Results. The findings facilitated the identification of a typology of disorienting events, alongside strategies of fairness characterised by equality and equity. Moreover, various types of language policy were delineated, including monolingualism, pragmatic multilingualism, and translanguaging, as well as forms of professional self-definition, such as the rejection of the mediator role, its acceptance, and the emergence of a hybrid identity. A five-phase model of identity transformation, progressing from a technical to an expert axiological stage, was also elucidated. Furthermore, factors within the institutional context were identified that either facilitate or impede the effective processing of dissonance. Scientific novelty. The scientific novelty of this study lies in the integration of international concepts of transformative learning, translanguaging, and culturally relevant pedagogy with the Russian tradition of pedagogical axiology and institutional analysis. In addition, a processual model of teacher identity within a multicultural environment is developed and rigorously substantiated. Prac tical significance. The practical significance of the study resides in the development of recommendations designed to support teachers through the various stages of identity transformation. These recommendations include creating opportunities for collegial reflection, mentoring, and the formal institutional recognition of the role of the intercultural mediator.

title: An Isogenic iPSC Model of LMNA p.R482W Recapitulates Adipocyte Dysfunction in Familial Partial Lipodystrophy Type 2
538cf543f42ca3478572dc129d4c97e056fadc65.abstract: Abstract Familial partial lipodystrophy type 2 (FPLD2) is a rare autosomal dominant disorder caused by pathogenic variants in LMNA , most commonly p.R482W, and is characterized by selective loss of subcutaneous adipose tissue, severe insulin resistance, and dyslipidemia. The cellular mechanisms underlying adipocyte dysfunction in FPLD2 remain incompletely understood, in part because existing in vitro models rely on patient-derived, non-isogenic cell lines or require non-physiologic transgene overexpression to achieve adipogenic differentiation. Here, we describe a CRISPR/Cas9-edited isogenic iPSC model of FPLD2 in which the heterozygous LMNA c.1444C>T (p.R482W) variant was introduced into a healthy donor-derived iPSC line. Using a transgene-free mesenchymal progenitor differentiation protocol, we generated LMNA p.R482W and isogenic control adipocytes and characterized their transcriptomic and functional phenotypes. Bulk RNA-sequencing demonstrated strong concordance in adipogenesis gene expression between genotypes during differentiation (Pearson ρ = 0.968), yet LMNA p.R482W adipocytes exhibited significant downregulation of key adipogenic, lipid-handling, and extracellular matrix genes compared to isogenic controls. Functionally, LMNA p.R482W adipocytes showed markedly impaired glucose uptake under both basal and insulin-stimulated conditions, consistent with severe insulin resistance. Seahorse extracellular flux analysis revealed a globally quiescent metabolic state with significantly reduced oxygen consumption rate (126.5 vs. 261.5 pmol/min, p < 0.0001) and extracellular acidification rate (27.6 vs. 46.7 mpH/min, p < 0.0001). To validate these findings in human tissue, gene set enrichment analysis results from the iPSC model were compared to single-nucleus RNA-sequencing data from subcutaneous white adipose tissue biopsies of individuals with FPLD2 carrying the LMNA p.R482W variant. Across 37 mutually significant pathways, 59.5% were concordant between the iPSC model and human adipose tissue, including the pathways most central to FPLD2 pathophysiology: adipogenesis, fatty acid metabolism, oxidative phosphorylation, and inflammatory response. These findings establish this isogenic iPSC system as a faithful cellular model of FPLD2 adipocyte biology and a platform for functional characterization of LMNA variants of uncertain significance. title: A foundation model for three-dimensional anatomical reconstruction from sparse X-ray projections
c38e55481f53bc13d6ab511dcab9eee4f2e8ac87.abstract: Abstract Computed tomography (CT) provides three-dimensional anatomical information but requires costly scanners and exposes patients to higher radiation doses than conventional X-ray imaging. Reconstructing three-dimensional anatomy from a few X-ray projections could extend widely available X-ray systems beyond two-dimensional imaging. We present SPARC, a foundation model pretrained once on 47,149 chest scans across diverse acquisition settings, enabling a single model to be adapted to different X-ray imaging configurations and anatomical regions. Across eight datasets covering five body regions, seven mainly outside the chest, SPARC reconstructed volumes with greater fidelity than five existing methods, exceeding the strongest in peak signal-to-noise ratio by 0.8-2.6 dB with eight projections and 1.4-2.7 dB with four. CT-based tools for abnormality classification and organ segmentation retained most of their performance when applied directly to SPARC's reconstructions from eight projections, fewer than 3% of the hundreds recorded by a CT scanner. They reached 98% of their area under the receiver operating characteristic curve on CT for 18 chest abnormalities, and 86% and 93% of their Dice score on CT for abdominal organs and lung lobes, with Dice scores 8.8% and 4.4% higher, in relative terms, than with the best competing method. Pretraining considerably increased the adaptation data efficiency. With ten patients, SPARC reconstructed chest CT more accurately than the same architecture trained from scratch on 100 patients. With the models and code released, SPARC could support the clinical translation of sparse-view reconstruction and expand access to three-dimensional imaging where CT scanners are unavailable.

title: Testing Group Differences in Network Models using Bayesian Model Selection: A Tutorial
20b36b318f3d81376460484f9eddeca399ecbb1a.abstract: Network models are increasingly used to model multivariate data and many research questions are about whether networks differ across groups. This tutorial provides an accessible introduction to Bayesian model-selection for testing group differences in networks, as implemented in the R package bgms. This approach provides posterior inclusion probabilities and Bayes factors for each group difference, allowing researchers to distinguish evidence for a difference from evidence for equality. We focus the tutorial on group differences in ordinal network models, since the vast majority of data in cross-sectional research are measured on ordinal scales. We explain the model parameters, prior choices, missing-data handling, convergence checks, checks of model fit, and the interpretation of posterior summaries of group differences. The workflow is illustrated with a reproducible comparison of problematic pornography use symptom networks in women and men.

title: Kinetic Multi-reaction Model of Platinum Nanoparticle Oxidation and Cathodic Dissolution in a Wide Potential Window
container-title: ACS Catalysis
3be0b324aaeaba4b002cb2763cfa08d3cf6a9b72.abstract: Abstract Mathematical modeling provides a powerful framework for understanding and mitigating degradation in catalyst materials such as platinum nanoparticles. A hallmark of platinum degradation during voltage cycling is the appearance of two distinct maxima in the dissolved Pt concentration: a smaller peak upon increasing potential and a larger peak upon decreasing potential. To explain this observation, we propose a kinetic multi-reaction model of Pt nanoparticle oxidation and dissolution, which describes dissolution as an interplay between direct electrochemical dissolution, passivation of the Pt surface, and the electrochemical dissolution of Pt oxides. The model is calibrated using cyclic voltammograms and time traces of Pt ion concentrations measured for two Pt catalyst samples with different nanoparticle sizes and different supports (carbon-supported 3 nm and unsupported 30 nm particles). The model results show very good agreement with the experimental data and indicate that the dissolution dynamics are indeed governed by oxide surface passivation and dissolution. Furthermore, comparison of results for different catalysts shows that the observed differences in Pt dissolution arise not only from variations in reaction rates on particles of different sizes but also from differences in the catalysts’ microscopic structure, which significantly influence Pt loss through diffusion.

title: A MODEL FOR MEASURING EFFECTS OF ENVIRONMENTAL FEATURES’ ON RENTAL VALUES OF RESIDENTIAL PROPERTIES IN KADUNA METROPOLIS, NIGERIA
container-title: Journal of Biodiversity and Environmental Research
098777f54f234c59b94dc6e64f5e459a855c3706.abstract: Environmental features, has potentially significant effects on environments and their populations, thus it is important to understand its drivers and how to measure them. The aim of this study is to develop a model for measuring the effects of environmental features on rental values of residential properties in Kaduna Metropolis with a view to establish the most sustainable attributes that significantly contribute to change in rental values in order to guide in making the best real estate investment decisions. To achieve this aim, five objectives were developed to determine the environmental features' quality provided in rented residential properties, assess the average rental values of residential properties, examine the condition of property features provided in the rented residential properties, and assess the effect of environmental features and property features in determining variation in rental values of residential property in Kaduna metropolis. The population of the study is 9,545. The study adopted quantitative research approaches and survey strategy. Structured questionnaires were distributed to 382 respondents. The data was analysed using mean ranking, frequency distribution tables and multiple regression analysis. The result revealed that, the average (Mean) rent paid in different types of rented residential properties in Kaduna metropolis, Nigeria, stands for flat ₦436,093, bungalow ₦547,043 and tenement ₦116,083. Meanwhile, the overall result of the conditions of physical features (tangibles) provided in the rented residential properties, indicate a good result in Kaduna metropolis. Also the overall result of conditions of non-physical features (intangibles) provided in the rented residential properties in Kaduna metropolis indicates a good condition. The study found that only two independent variables (Housing Non Physical Characteristics and Environmental Locational Proximity) were statistically significant, while the other two (HCPS and LPS) were statistically insignificant. The overall model performance showed an R-squared of approximately 69.91%, indicating that the independent variables collectively account for a proportion of the total variation observed in the (rent). The study recommends that property owners/developers should continue to prioritize regular maintenance and timely repairs of fundamental property elements, as this ensures tenant satisfaction, and increases turnover.

title: Mitochondrial DNA-cGAS-STING-CISD1 axis mediates hypoxia-induced cognitive impairment by driving hippocampal neuronal ferroptosis
cc81e6e2b1c76d35d0698ecacec2effda553e0d8.abstract: Abstract High-altitude hypoxic cognitive impairment severely compromises the physical and mental health of individuals who rapidly ascend to or reside long-term at high altitude; however, its initiating mechanisms, pathological cascades, and molecular regulatory network remain incompletely understood, leaving a paucity of effective therapeutic targets and preventive strategies. Using a mouse model of simulated 6000 m hypobaric hypoxia and a primary hippocampal neuron hypoxia model, we integrated behavioral testing, transmission electron microscopy, Seahorse metabolic analysis, transcriptomic profiling, co-immunoprecipitation-coupled proteomics, structural prediction, pharmacological intervention, and clinical validation in human cohorts to systematically delineate the molecular mechanisms and core regulatory pathways underlying hypoxia-induced neuronal ferroptosis. Hypoxic exposure time-dependently impaired object recognition and spatial memory in mice and caused hippocampal neuron loss. Mechanistically, mitochondrial damage emerged as a critical initiating event during hypoxic stress, triggering mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) release and subsequent activation of the cGAS-STING signaling pathway. Hypoxic hippocampal neurons exhibited canonical features of ferroptosis, including elevated Fe²⁺ and malondialdehyde (MDA) levels, decreased GPX4 expression, and enhanced ACSL4 expression and increased mitochondrial C11-BODIPY oxidation. Pharmacological inhibition of STING with C-176 significantly alleviated these ferroptosis phenotypes, neuronal loss, and cognitive impairment. Co-immunoprecipitation combined with proteomics identified CISD1 (mitoNEET), a mitochondrial outer membrane protein, as a STING-interacting partner, and their binding was enhanced under hypoxia and localized to mitochondria-endoplasmic reticulum contact sites. Moreover, the ferroptosis inhibitor Liproxstatin-1 rescued hypoxic cognitive impairment and partially restored mitochondrial morphology and respiratory function without reversing STING phosphorylation, indicating that ferroptosis functions downstream of STING and constitutes a feed-forward amplification loop by aggravating mitochondrial damage. In human cohorts, levels of serum iron and oxidative damage markers correlated positively with residential altitude. Collectively, these findings establish a self-amplifying pathological axis of mitochondrial damage-mtDNA-cGAS-STING-CISD1-ferroptosis, and targeting this axis may provide novel strategies for the prevention and treatment of high-altitude hypoxic cognitive impairment.

title: Ophthalmic AI With Just Ten Examples: Comparing Multimodal Large Language Models, Vision Foundation Models, and Vision-Language Models
39e75df2cc86efffe98ece2f5801fc9170ca9006.abstract: ABSTRACT Purpose To compare multimodal large language models (MLLMs), vision foundation models (VFMs), and contrastive vision-language models (VLMs) for ophthalmic image interpretation with no labeled examples (zero-shot) or as few as 10 labeled examples per class (10-shot). Design Retrospective benchmarking study. Subjects 4 public datasets (UCSD, IDRiD, REFUGE, ASOCT-MSDC) and 3 private datasets (OHTS, BPEI-DLS, WashU-OCT) of anterior-and posterior-segment ophthalmic imaging. Methods Nine AI models were evaluated across 3 architectural families: MLLMs (Qwen3.8-27B, GLM-5.3-Flash, Gemma-4-31B-it), VFMs (DINOv3, RETFound, VisionFM), and VLMs (CLIP, EyeCLIP, SigLIP2). Models were assessed on disease classification, disease risk and severity grading, anatomical assessment, and lesion localization in fundus and OCT imaging. MLLMs were also compared with a 3D VFM (OCTCube-M) for whole-volume OCT classification. MLLMs were evaluated zero-shot and 10-shot, without additional training. Vision models (VFMs and VLMs) were adapted by linear probing and fine-tuning on the same 10-shot set and on the full training dataset (FD). Main Outcome Measures Disease classification performance (macro-averaged F1, AUROC, quadratic weighted kappa [QWK]), anatomical localization accuracy, and cross-dataset generalization. Results For retinal OCT disease classification, 10-shot MLLMs achieved a macro-F1 of 0.94, versus 0.59 (10-shot) and 0.96 (FD) for vision models. For diabetic retinopathy and macular edema grading, 10-shot MLLMs achieved QWKs of 0.69 and 0.73, versus 0.48 and 0.57 (10-shot) and 0.72 and 0.79 (FD) for vision models. For lesion localization, 10-shot MLLMs achieved an F1 of 0.75, versus 0.70 (10-shot) and 0.86 (FD) for vision models. For vertical cup-to-disc ratio estimation (OHTS), zero-shot MLLMs achieved a mean absolute error of 0.14, versus 0.21 (10-shot) for vision models. For whole-volume OCT classification (WashU-OCT), zero-shot MLLMs achieved a macro-F1 of 0.71, versus 0.50 (10-shot) and 0.82 (FD) for vision models. Conclusions Open-weight MLLMs given 10 labeled examples per class outperformed VFMs and VLMs trained on the same examples in most tasks and approached the performance of fully trained VFMs and VLMs in selected disease classification and grading tasks. MLLMs also demonstrated promising zero-shot performance on non-public clinical datasets without task-specific training. By reducing the need for large labeled datasets and task-specific model adaptation, MLLMs could broaden who can develop and validate ophthalmic AI.

title: Triage Advice From General-Purpose Language Models in Health and Everyday Situations
880d1dd4ca04d222b6a435037ac3eea170872fe0.abstract: Importance One adult in 10 has consulted a chatbot for health information within 6 months, and nearly half of users do so to decide whether they need care. Referral regardless of need could add demand on stretched services. Objective To compare referral to a professional by general-purpose language models in health and non-health situations against the level of contact that human raters judged necessary. Design, Setting, and Participants Cross-sectional study of 4,346 responses generated in September 2026 by 53 general-purpose model configurations, released between March 2023 and September 2026 and accessed through APIs or run locally, to 82 investigator-written messages (41 health and 41 non-health). No patients were involved. Exposures Health vs non-health scenario. Main Outcomes and Measures Professional referral, unconditional or conditional on a future change or on doubt, coded by 3 language models and compared with the level of contact that physicians, pharmacists and 2 technically trained raters judged necessary. Results Referral occurred in 74.7% of health and 46.3% of non-health responses, more often for health in every configuration (standardized difference, 28.3 percentage points; 95% CI, 18.3-37.0). Where raters judged contact unnecessary, 64.5% of health vs 27.6% of non-health responses recommended a professional (odds ratio, 17.08; 95% CI, 6.14-47.54); most of the health excess was conditional referral (46.3% vs 21.0%), and unconditional referral was 18.1% vs 6.6% (odds ratio, 4.66; 95% CI, 1.43-15.19). Where an in-person assessment was judged necessary, referral was similar (89.6% vs 84.5%). In medicines and physical health, referral was not associated with rated severity (odds ratio per point, 1.16; 95% CI, 0.53-2.55), unlike outside health (3.86; 95% CI, 1.79-8.33). The referral gap was 20.5 percentage points among configurations released in 2023 and 32.2 and 32.3 in 2025 and 2026 (4.8 percentage points per year; 95% CI, 2.3-7.2). Conclusions and Relevance General-purpose language models referred people to a professional where a visit was needed, in health as outside it, but in health also in 2 in 3 situations that physicians and pharmacists judged manageable without contact, a pattern stronger in newer models. Evaluations of these systems should include whether their advice distinguishes situations that can be deferred or managed at a distance, alongside the referral of serious cases.

title: Peningkatan Kemampuan Literasi Matematis Murid Kelas X Melalui Model Pembelajaran Problem Based Learning (PBL) Terintegrasi Growth Mindset
container-title: Jurnal Ilmiah Profesi Pendidikan
eb8ba23a0eba5a058eedd680320a511f29a2fa4f.abstract: Kemampuan literasi matematis merupakan salah satu kompetensi penting yang perlu dikuasai murid agar mampu menerapkan konsep matematika dalam menyelesaikan permasalahan kontekstual. Namun, dalam pembelajaran matematika, murid masih mengalami kesulitan dalam merumuskan permasalahan, menerapkan konsep matematika, serta menafsirkan hasil penyelesaian sesuai dengan konteks permasalahan. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk meningkatkan kemampuan literasi matematis murid kelas X.E SMA Muhammadiyah 3 Jember tahun pelajaran 2025/2026 melalui penerapan model pembelajaran Problem Based Learning (PBL) terintegrasi growth mindset. Penelitian ini merupakan Penelitian Tindakan Kelas (PTK) yang dilaksanakan dalam dua siklus dengan mengacu pada tahapan perencanaan, tindakan, observasi, dan refleksi. Subjek penelitian adalah murid kelas X.E SMA Muhammadiyah 3 Jember. Data kemampuan literasi matematis diperoleh melalui tes uraian pada setiap siklus yang mencakup tiga indikator, yaitu formulate, employ, dan interpret. Data dianalisis secara deskriptif kuantitatif dengan menghitung persentase ketercapaian setiap indikator. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan adanya peningkatan ketercapaian pada seluruh indikator. Pada Siklus I, indikator formulate mencapai 93%, employ 60%, dan interpret 33%. Pada Siklus II, ketercapaian meningkat menjadi 100% pada indikator formulate, 87% pada indikator employ, dan 60% pada indikator interpret. Dengan demikian, indikator employ dan interpret masing-masing mengalami peningkatan sebesar 27 poin persentase. Penerapan model pembelajaran PBL terintegrasi growth mindset dapat meningkatkan kemampuan literasi matematis murid, terutama dalam menerapkan konsep matematika dan menafsirkan hasil penyelesaian permasalahan kontekstual.

title: Clinically Meaningful Cognitive Improvement from Intermittent Neurostimulation of the Nucleus Basalis of Meynert in Parkinson’s Disease
87c7670ad172788159ae620b9d3fce90c3f08286.abstract: Abstract Cognitive decline begins in early stages of Parkinson’s disease (PD) for many individuals and remains largely untreated. The nucleus basalis of Meynert (NBM), the brain’s cortical cholinergic hub, and its lateral efferent fiber bundle degenerate early in PD and are linked to cognitive and cognitive-motor impairment. Pre-clinical evidence indicates intermittent stimulation of the NBM improves cognition. The objective of this study is to establish the feasibility of combined continuous subthalamic nucleus (STN) and intermittent NBM DBS for cognitive impairment in people with PD. Five patients with PD and cognitive impairment approved for STN DBS were enrolled as part of an ongoing clinical trial for combined STN and NBM DBS under an Investigational Device Exemption. Three participants received a ‘vertical’ trajectory in which two leads were placed in the STN, and two additional leads were placed in the anterior portion of the NBM, both using the same burr hole for each hemisphere. The two other participants received a novel ‘lateral trajectory’ in which the NBM leads were placed along the NBM lateral efferent bundle via a small twist craniostomy behind the ear. An automated programming algorithm DBS Illumina 3D™ (Boston Scientific) was used to program the NBM leads based on volume of tissue activated modeling. The investigational Chronos software (Boston Scientific) was used to deliver continuous high frequency DBS to the STN 24 hours/day and intermittent patterned DBS to the NBM for 1 hour/day. The two leads placed in the NBM (‘Vertical’ target) or its lateral efferent bundle (‘Lateral’ target) were successfully and accurately placed as part of the usual STN DBS procedure. All participants were successfully programmed using the Illumina 3D™ algorithm without adverse effects. Following 6 months of combined continuous STN and intermittent NBM DBS, all five participants saw clinically meaningful improvements in cognition as part of a neuropsychological assessment battery, as well as the expected motoric benefit from STN DBS. The current study demonstrated that intermittent stimulation of the NBM to target cortical cholinergic deficits may provide clinically meaningful improvements in cognitive symptoms in Parkinson’s disease. ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT05968703

title: Mapping Linguistic Errors in English Writing: A Quantitative Study of Ninth-Grade Students
container-title: Journal of English Language Teaching
cea6ee14295fd088eb834b208daa3ae521709b48.abstract: This study presents empirical evidence on linguistic errors among secondary school learners in India, using a validated error-classification framework. The study aimed to determine the frequency and distribution of linguistic errors in English writing, compare errors across school type and gender, and test the reliability of the error-coding rubric. A quantitative descriptive research design was adopted, with data collected from a stratified random sample of 185 students drawn from two secondary schools, one government and one private, in Bhadohi district, Uttar Pradesh. Students completed a standardised dictation task, and their written responses were analysed using a validated rubric classifying errors as orthographic, morphological, syntactic, lexical, and punctuation-related. Inter-rater reliability was estimated using Fleiss’ Kappa (0.534–0.678) and intraclass correlation coefficients (0.756–0.845). The findings reveal a high error density (40.29%), with orthographic errors occurring most frequently, followed by syntactic and morphological errors. A Mann-Whitney U test showed no significant difference in error density by school type (U = 3870.5, p = .449) or gender (U = 4092.50, p = .639), suggesting that writing challenges are more closely linked to instructional factors than to demographic characteristics. The validated coding rubric demonstrated satisfactory reliability for structured linguistic error analysis. These findings provide empirical evidence for English language teaching in the Indian ESL context and underline the need for explicit instruction in spelling, grammar, and sentence construction, alongside diagnostic assessment practices and teacher professional development to strengthen writing proficiency.

title: Analysing Reading-Focused Activities in a Grade VIII English Textbook: Evidence from Government Schools in Assam
container-title: Journal of English Language Teaching
8661484bf0545488ad1056c2fd92266f623d6672.abstract: Textbooks serve as primary instructional resources in contexts with limited teaching materials and play a central role in achieving curriculum goals (Li & Wang, 2024; Stara et al., 2017). Given this central role, the design and quality of literacy activities included in a textbook become crucial for supporting learners’ literacy development. This study examines reading-focused activities in the Grade VIII SCERT English textbook used in government schools in Assam, evaluating how effectively they promote essential reading skills aligned with the NCERT Learning Outcomes (2017). The analysis focuses on three key skills: fluent reading, reading for vocabulary development, and reading for comprehension of main ideas and specific information. A researcher-developed and expert-evaluated checklist (S-CVI/Ave = 1.00) was used for systematic analysis. Findings reveal strong representation of comprehension-focused activities, while activities supporting fluency and vocabulary appear comparatively limited, indicating the need for a more balanced distribution of activities to foster holistic reading development.

title: Prompting Metacognition: Using Prompt Writing as a Language Task and Metacognitive Tool in ELT
container-title: Journal of English Language Teaching
d9efcec3e3b2dcd11603001b11c1fb4829caafbc.abstract: Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) tools have made their way into English Language Teaching (ELT) contexts, yet their pedagogical value remains contested. While many learners engage with GenAI primarily as a quick hack for producing answers, fewer use it as a resource for reflective language learning. This study explores prompt writing as a language learning task that supports both language development and metacognitive awareness. The study was conducted with a target group of pre-seminary, tertiary-level learners with mixed linguistic proficiency. Over the course of four instructional sessions, the study used a classroom-based action research design. Learners engaged in cycles of prompt drafting, GenAI-generated responses, peer discussion, and prompt refinement. Classroom observations, learner reflections, and group discussions were used to gather qualitative insights. The findings indicate measurable improvement in learners’ autonomy, as learners became aware of how lexical choices shape meaning, along with increased engagement, teamwork, and reflective thinking. The study argues that prompt writing, when treated as a language task rather than a technical skill, can function as a practical tool for fostering metacognition in ELT classrooms.

title: Role of Reading Strategies in Improving English Academic Performance Among Secondary Schools in Edo State, Nigeria
container-title: Journal of English Language Teaching
f19373975f33fc6ad3de9429ab23e30cd6c285a4.abstract: This study investigated the role of reading strategies in improving English academic performance among secondary school students in Esan West Local Government Area, Edo State. Using a descriptive survey design, data were collected from 400 students selected through stratified random sampling and 25 purposively selected teachers via a Student Questionnaire on Reading Strategies (SQRS) and a Teachers’ Interview Guide (TIG), respectively. Descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation, and multiple regression were used for quantitative analysis, while qualitative data were thematically analysed. Findings revealed that students predominantly employed cognitive and metacognitive strategies, including underlining, note-taking, summarising, re-reading, and self-questioning, while affective and social strategies were less frequently adopted. English academic performance was generally moderate, and a strong positive relationship existed between reading strategy use and performance. Cognitive and metacognitive strategies emerged as the strongest performance predictors. The study recommends explicit strategy instruction, guided collaborative reading, and motivational classroom support.

title: OPEN: A Benchmark Dataset and Baseline for Older Adult Patient Engagement Recognition in Virtual Rehabilitation Learning Environments
container-title: ACM Transactions on Computing for Healthcare
15da22bbb1e361fbb587282abf4d63fc478211b7.abstract: Engagement in virtual rehabilitation programs is crucial for participant satisfaction, adherence, and successful program delivery. Measuring engagement in virtual group settings remains a significant challenge. There is growing interest in applying artificial intelligence (AI) for large-scale, automated engagement recognition. While engagement has been extensively studied among young learners in academic contexts, research methods and datasets focusing on older adults in virtual and telehealth environments are limited. Many existing approaches overlook the contextual relevance of learning materials and the longitudinal nature of engagement. This paper introduces OPEN (Older adult Patient ENgagement), a novel dataset created to support the development of AI models for engagement recognition. Data were collected from eleven older adults over six weeks of virtual cardiac rehabilitation sessions, totaling nearly 35 hours, making it one of the largest datasets of its kind. To protect privacy, raw video is withheld, but released data include facial, hand, and body joint landmarks, along with behavioral and affective features. Annotations provide second-level binary engagement states, emotional and behavioral labels, and contextual details. Machine-learning and deep-learning models trained on the dataset achieved up to 81% accuracy. OPEN provides a scalable foundation for advancing AI-driven engagement recognition in aging populations and broader research contexts.

title: Designing and Evaluating a Clinical Decision Support System to Assess Mild Cognitive Impairment
container-title: ACM Transactions on Computing for Healthcare
763e62297c3779a364c1110e9de905b0814b78e4.abstract: Explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) is increasingly used in clinical decision support systems (CDSS) to improve the interpretability and trustworthiness of machine learning (ML) predictions in healthcare. While prior work has examined how healthcare professionals (HCPs) interpret various explanation methods, limited research has investigated how these explanations function in systems that incorporate novel data sources like game-based digital biomarkers. This paper extends our previous work by presenting an improved, interactive web-based CDSS designed to support HCPs in assessing the risk of Mild Cognitive Impairment (MCI). The system integrates ML predictions from gameplay data with data-centric, feature-importance, and counterfactual explanations to assist diagnosis and case-finding. We conducted a mixed-methods study with 51 HCPs to evaluate the system's understandability (objective and perceived), perceived usefulness, perceived ease of use, and trust. Participants gave consistently positive ratings across the self-reported perceived constructs, which were found to be strongly correlated. HCPs generally perceived the explanations as useful for clinical reasoning and reported that they understood and trusted the system, while acknowledging an initial learning curve. However, the evaluation of objective understanding was more mixed and correlated only weakly with the perceived constructs. In particular, participants encountered challenges in understanding game-based digital biomarkers, interpreting feature importances, combining local and global explanations, and understanding details of the underlying ML models. These findings highlight the importance of explanation designs that foster both positive user perceptions and accurate comprehension.

title: A decision-only model as a low-cost judge of medical AI answers
34bbfe5df770a427e9785cd56dd0d877bfc93809.abstract: Abstract Background Testing and deploying medical AI systems at scale already results in more outputs than clinicians can review, and the use of large language models (LLMs) as judges is growing rapidly. Decision-only models, cheap and fast models that return structured probabilities rather than text, offer a potentially scalable option for that goal. Methods In an OSF pre-registered evaluation, we tested TypeSafe Jev 1.13 as a judge on tasks from five validated clinical benchmarks: rubric grading (HealthBench), planted clinical errors (When Rubrics Fail), risk in AI-written clinical documents (MedVAL), counseling ratings and failures (CounselBench) and physicians’ preferences between answers (Real-POCQi). Comparators were expert raters’ agreement with each other, OpenAI Decisions, GPT-6 Luna, a proposed hybrid team combining decision models and a cheap LLM and, as frontier comparators, GPT-6.1 Sol and Claude Opus 5.5. The main outcome was plain agreement with the expert label. Results The test comprised 25,091 units and 213,913 model calls. Jev’s agreement with expert labels averaged 64.7% over six tasks. On 3,614 matched units it averaged 66.1%, against 65.0% for Opus and 60.7% for Sol, and it was non-inferior to both on four of six tasks. Jev judged the whole pool in 17 minutes for US$1.46; per judgment, it cost 1/34 of Sol’s price and 1/152 of Opus’s. A preset cutoff held its false-alarm rate on fresh planted-error answers, and in simulation, reviewing Jev’s least-sure answers first found 1.4 times the errors of a random audit. Still, omissions were hard for both: at the same false-alarm rate, Jev missed 55.6% of planted omissions and Opus 48.1%, and Opus caught 8.8 points more planted errors overall. Conclusions Across more than 200,000 model calls, a decision-only model was non-inferior to two frontier judges on most tasks at a small fraction of their cost and time, while reporting how sure it was of every call. With local cutoffs and expert oversight of omissions and clinical documents, judging every output of a deployed medical AI system becomes more affordable.

title: DRHL: Cross-Language Detection and Repair of Access Control Vulnerabilities via Hybrid Analysis and LLMs
container-title: ACM Transactions on Software Engineering and Methodology
c33ccf782117c242e524421daa0aa4edae1c4204.abstract: Broken Access Control (BAC) enables unauthorized resource access, posing critical risks. Traditional detection suffers from inefficiency and high false positives, while existing repairs are largely manual, PHP-centric, and low success rates. To address this, we propose DRHL, a cross-language framework for automated BAC detection and repair grounded in the Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) model. DRHL constructs a Hybrid Site Navigation Graph (HSNG) via dynamic-static analysis to map roles, permissions, and pages, enabling precise inference and targeted payload generation that curbs redundancy and false positives. For repair, it extracts access control snippets from multilingual applications under syntactic-semantic constraints and encodes them with detection results into prompts, guiding a Large Language Model (LLM) to generate context-aware, style-consistent patches across languages. Evaluations on 16 web applications across PHP, Java, Python, and Go show that DRHL detects all 50 independently established ground-truth vulnerabilities with only 1 FP and 0 FNs, and repairs 48 of them within three attempts. It also improves average code coverage over ZAP and Burp Suite by 3.89 and 9.77 percentage points, respectively, at comparable runtime, while 94.68% of expert patch-quality ratings are positive across Access-Control Correctness, Functionality Preservation, and Code Quality.

title: Media -Based Interventions for Enhancing English Writing Skills in ESL Classrooms
container-title: Journal of English Language Teaching
efd21d3eac2b5394d04cad4963f5a6778a64a3b1.abstract: This paper investigates the effectiveness of media-based interventions, particularly English songs and movies, in enhancing the writing skills of English as a Second Language (ESL) learners. Using a mixed-methods research design, the study was conducted with Bachelor of Business Administration (BBA) undergraduate students. Data were obtained through a structured questionnaire, semi-structured interviews, and analysis of students’ writing samples to evaluate improvements in the use of vocabulary, coherence, organisation, and overall writing proficiency. The findings indicate that students who engaged regularly with carefully selected English media demonstrated better vocabulary use, greater paragraph coherence, and more effective written expression than those with limited media exposure. The study identifies three essential factors contributing to improved writing performance: meaningful exposure to authentic media content, guided reflection and writing activities, and the use of AI tools such as Grammarly for feedback and revision.

title: An Analysis of the Writing Module Taught to the MA FL Students at EFLU Hyderabad
container-title: Journal of English Language Teaching
950dabf41b48123e074e659d2e48073769340550.abstract: NEP 2020 highlights the importance of integrating employability skills into the University curriculum to make education more relevant and adequate for facing the challenges of the 21st century. In line with this, the EFL University, Hyderabad, introduced a new course on Communicative English for its postgraduate students of various Foreign Languages (FL) in the academic year 2022-2023. Spread across two semesters, this course contained a writing skills module dedicated to enhancing students’ employability skills by helping them develop e-portfolios showcasing their strengths and potential to perform in a given job role. This study analyses the efficacy of the writing module by using classroom observation, survey responses and teacher and student interviews as primary tools of data collection. A group of 20 students from Semester 1 of the course participated in the study along with the two co-instructors of the writing module. The study found that learners perceived e-portfolios to be a challenging yet motivating and rewarding approach to assess and improve their English writing skills, which are needed to enhance their employability skills to tackle the nuances of professional communication.

title: Reading for Autonomy: Literature Circles in the Secondary English Classroom<!--a=1-->
container-title: Journal of English Language Teaching
ef9a220907f90a0663477072fcabab7d07712518.abstract: Literature instruction in many secondary school contexts remains shaped by examination-orientated pedagogy that offers limited scope for independent interpretation or reflective engagement with texts. This study examines literature circles - small, student-led discussion groups organised around rotating roles - as a pedagogical alternative capable of fostering learner autonomy and reflective thinking. Drawing on a four-week qualitative case study conducted with 44 Grade 9 students at a CBSE-affiliated school in India, the study analysed students’ reflective journals and semi-structured interviews using thematic analysis. Findings reveal two key themes: literature circles fostered a gradual but observable shift toward greater student ownership of the reading process through structured, accountable roles; and collaborative, peer-driven discussion consistently prompted students to reconsider and articulate their own interpretive reasoning, generating both immediate and longer-arc reflective thinking. These findings suggest that autonomy and reflection are conditions built into the design of literature circles, offering practical implications for teachers seeking learner-centred approaches to literature pedagogy.

title: Towards Sustainable Hydrogen Systems: Supply Chain Optimization with Model Predictive Control and Reinforcement Learning
be4b3aee75dc455c8abbc8fba089830fbb83d01a.abstract: Hydrogen supply chains are expected to play a central role in future low-carbon energy systems. However, the operation of such systems is inherently challenged by factors such as uncertainty in renewable availability, electricity prices, and hydrogen demand, as well as by practical engineering constraints associated with electrolyzers, energy storage, and grid interaction. Effective control strategies must therefore balance economic performance, operational feasibility, and sustainability objectives under time-varying and uncertain conditions, especially as hydrogen infrastructure scales beyond pilot deployments. This paper investigates and compares four operational control approaches for a renewable-powered hydrogen supply chain: a rule-based controller (RBC), model predictive control (MPC), reinforcement learning without forecasts (RL-NF), and reinforcement learning with forecast-augmented observations (RL-F). All methods are evaluated within a unified, physically realistic framework that incorporates electrolyzer minimum load and ramping constraints, battery and hydrogen storage dynamics, grid import limits, renewable curtailment, and consistent economic assumptions. This unified formulation ensures methodological consistency, enabling a fair and rigorous comparison of predictive and adaptive control paradigms under identical system conditions and uncertainty realizations. Simulation results show that MPC achieves the highest economic performance by effectively exploiting short-term forecasts to reduce grid dependence and optimize storage utilization, highlighting the value of predictive optimization when reliable forecasts are available. RL-NF demonstrates robust and competitive performance despite operating without future information, while RL-F does not consistently outperform its no-forecast counterpart, illustrating the challenges of learning from noisy forecasts in complex energy systems. These findings illustrate the relative strengths and limitations of predictive and learning-based control approaches for hydrogen supply chains under uncertainty and motivate further investigation into their roles in large-scale hydrogen system operation.

title: Governing Cybersecurity in Digital Business Ecosystems: A Maturity Model Integrating Enforceable Minimum Security Baselines
800df12976465e15f866d6976bac4cee64a496d7.abstract: Abstract Maturity models are widely used instruments for assessing and guiding organizational capability, yet they assume a single organization advancing along a single-stage path. That assumption is difficult to reconcile with cybersecurity governance in digital business ecosystems, where capabilities develop unevenly across autonomous organizations, and an enforceable baseline of protection must coexist with progressive capability growth. Drawing on design science research, we present a maturity model that integrates Minimum Security Baselines (MSBs) as binding, measurable requirements that every participant must meet, directly into a multi-dimensional maturity structure. We evaluate the model in a seaport ecosystem pilot of 35 transport and logistics partners, combining a six-week field assessment with an expert evaluation using an adapted System Usability Scale. Practitioners judged the model usable, learnable, and adaptable. We position the model against established cybersecurity maturity models and recent maturity-and-resilience frameworks, and show that none couples an enforceable participation baseline with a configurable, multi-dimensional progression at ecosystem scale. The contribution is a governance mechanism that pairs an enforceable participation baseline with configurable, non-linear improvement trajectories across heterogeneous ecosystem members.

title: Benchmarking single-subject detectability of cognitive event-related potentials in healthy controls and minimally conscious state patients
e3b47e6137797db11cda8e0c85daf5667bb8be05.abstract: Abstract Event-related potentials (ERP) may reveal residual cognitive processing in disorders of consciousness, but clinical translation is limited because group-level effects do not guarantee reliable single-subject detection. Few ERP paradigms have been benchmarked in healthy participants and compared directly with patients in disorders of consciousness. We tested a hierarchical ERP battery in healthy controls and patients in minimally conscious state (MCS) to (1) estimate upper-bound single-subject detectability in healthy participants, (2) compare detection rates with those of MCS patients, and (3) evaluate prognostic value for recovery of consciousness. Forty-eight healthy controls and 26 patients in MCS completed six auditory paradigms: multifeature mismatch negativity (MMN), passive and active oddball P300, the subject’s own name, semantic oddball, and sentence N400. Effects were classified using blinded expert visual scoring, region-of-interest ANOVA, cluster-based permutation tests, and support vector machine decoding. Associations between binary ERP classifications and recovery were tested in 22 surviving patients at follow-up. In healthy controls, visual scoring identified MMN to at least one deviant and P300 in both oddball tasks in all 48 participants. Command following as demonstrated by task-related P300 enhancement between active and passive oddball conditions was detected in 81%. Command following was detected in 92% in the semantic oddball task. Sentence-congruity effects (N400 and/or P600) were identified in 69%, despite a strong group-level response, while the own-name effect was detected in only 35%. In patients, detection rates were lower: MMN was found in 27% for the short-duration deviant and 65% when any of five deviant types counted as positive; passive oddball P300 in 35% and active oddball P300 in 31%; sentence-congruity effects in 12%; active-versus-passive oddball modulation in 12%; and semantic oddball effects in 8%. Visual scoring and machine learning generally detected more effects than ANOVA and cluster-based testing, and agreement varied substantially across paradigms. Binary ERP classifications were not significantly associated with recovery (14 recovered, eight did not), although prognostic analyses were limited by sample size. Group-level ERP effects overstated single-subject detectability in healthy controls, whereas the absence of group-level effects in MCS obscured reliable ERP responses resembling those of healthy controls in a few individual patients. In MCS, ERP effects associated with semantic processing and command following were generally uncommon, and binary ERP indicators did not predict recovery in this sample. Our findings establish a benchmark for selecting and refining ERP paradigms and detection methods to assess residual cognition after severe brain injury.

title: A continuum-based analytical model for the design of floating energy piles in generalised inhomogeneous soils
a2160706cd68d57438c18fb6c27933c6de859763.abstract: This study presents a novel continuum-based semi-analytical framework for the analysis of floating energy piles embedded in generalised inhomogeneous soils. The soil is modelled as an approximate Tajimi-type continuum. Vertical soil inhomogeneity is incorporated into the model by formulating a generalised eigenvalue problem for the evaluation of the soil modes, which are approximated through a series expansion in terms of simple trigonometric functions. The pile and the soil column beneath its tip are represented as a single axially deforming rod, and the restraint effect provided by thermally inactive piles connected to the same cap is accounted for through a concentrated spring at the pile head. In this way, a unified framework in which continuous and piecewise functions, or arbitrary combinations thereof, are used to describe the variation of soil stiffness with depth, is developed to derive the axial force along energy piles. The proposed solution is also extended to include mechanical loads. The predictive capability of the proposed model is assessed through comparisons with established analytical solutions, complex fully coupled numerical analyses and data from full scale field tests on energy piles supporting a real structure. The very close agreement confirms the reliability of the proposed framework as an efficient alternative to computationally demanding numerical approaches, which can serve as a simple tool for pile design.
