The chapter also analyzes how institutions can use AI-generated insights to optimize resource allocation, strengthen regulatory compliance, and operationalize inclusive policies. title: A Critical Exploration of How Artificial Intelligence Enhances Accommodation for Learners With Learning Barriers

2b033bfd9e3d57fefca89685cea1b21c53f84a3a.abstract: <jats:p>The purpose of this chapter is to critically explore how Artificial Intelligence (AI) can enhance curriculum design, content delivery and assessment strategies to accommodate learners with barriers to learning. The chapter shows the readers how AI can enhance curriculum design, content delivery and assessment strategies to accommodate learners with barriers to learning by using planned Individual Educational Programme (IEP), data-driven analysis, adaptive learning platforms that dynamically adjust content difficulty, sequencing, and presentation formats in real time. Also, AI-powered tools are used such as speech-to-text, text-to-speech, to establish flexibility, personalization and promotes equitable participation for all learners to uphold equity, ethics, and human values in education.</jats:p>

title: Solar Thermal District Heating and Cooling for Smart, Sustainable, AI-Optimized Cities
container-title: Renewable Energy Systems for Smart Cities and Urban Sustainability
5fb7b6f93a03dabd2aadb285a6f2da9c7a9936b8.abstract: <jats:p>Rapid urbanization and climate imperatives place cities at the center of energy transformation, yet thermal demand roughly half of urban energy end-use remains under addressed by electricity focused renewable strategies. This chapter, per the authors, examines solar thermal district heating and cooling (STDHC) systems as foundational infrastructure for sustainable smart cities. It reviews collector technologies and seasonal thermal storage configurations, then analyzes integration across the physical, cyber, and application layers of smart city architecture, emphasizing digital twins, IoT sensing, and machine-learning optimization including model predictive control and reinforcement learning. International case studies from Canada, Denmark, Croatia, and China demonstrate solar fractions above 50% and substantial carbon reductions. Lifecycle, cost, and energy-justice analyses benchmark performance and equity, while the closing sections identify deployment barriers and propose a research agenda spanning compact storage, federated learning, and policy alignment with SDG 7 and SDG 11.</jats:p>

b5fbd81ff64d56f595d8b18611cc2706c6345a69.abstract: <jats:p>For the development of sustainable urban energy systems in smart cities, this chapter focuses on the integration of electric mobility systems with AI-driven smart microgrids. It demonstrates the contribution of electric vehicles (EVs) through vehicle-to-grid (V2G) capabilities and variable demand, while smart microgrids enable effective management of dispersed energy resources and dispersed energy generation. The role of Artificial intelligence towards energy distribution optimization, real-time decision-making, and demand forecasting is emphasized along with identifying major obstacles including consumer acceptance, regulatory restrictions, interoperability problems, and discussing worldwide policy trends, the chapter provides an integrated conceptual framework offering insights into how the sustainability, dependability, and energy efficiency might improve urban settings through the integration of artificial intelligence (AI), EVs, and microgrids.</jats:p>

container-title: Renewable Energy Systems for Smart Cities and Urban Sustainability
eadd50d14a20212bca5c4790316df5a2305aab8d.abstract: <jats:p>The growing complexity of urban energy systems with smartness requires intelligent solutions that are privacy friendly to manage the distributed energy resources efficiently. This chapter introduces a federated learning model that is AI-powered and in this system, model training is performed in an intelligent grid, micro grid, and IoT-based devices, without the exchange of raw data. The strategy improves accuracy in load forecasting, efficiency of energy use, and lessens the amount of overhead in communication besides maintaining data privacy and security. The framework combines edge computing and state-of-the-art AI to promote scalable and adaptive energy management to add to sustainable, resilient, and human-centric smart city ecosystems.</jats:p>

f771357c6994b1b3d1a5a4ea4db933888583f4ae.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter examines the evolving relationship between artificial intelligence and sustainability in tourism within the broader context of Industry 4.0 and ongoing digital transformation processes. The chapter introduces the concept of rehumanizing sustainability as a conceptual and practical framework for addressing these challenges. This approach emphasizes the reintegration of human values, agency, and experiential dimensions into AI-driven systems.</jats:p>

e5acdeb20d729b725992dc8343811299e03d8c4b.abstract: <jats:p>The corn moth overwinters primarily in the soil in the pupal stage. In the spring, as temperatures rise, the adults emerge and lay eggs on newly sown plots. Upon hatching, the larvae penetrate the soil and feed on germinating seeds, root collars, and young stems. As a result, seedling growth ceases or the plants wither. Development takes 20—40 days, depending on climatic conditions. Most species produce 2—4 generations per year. This article examines the development of the corn moth (Anthomyiidae) and the biological efficacy of control measures against it.</jats:p>

18cd92c73dac5749719c45c1bd85abd95a604d36.abstract: <jats:p>The article presents information on the characteristics of Simmental cows belonging to different production types. The study found that the age at first calving was 789.5 days for cows of the dairy type and 795.1 days for those of the dairy-beef type; these figures were 11.1 and 5.5 days lower, respectively, than the age at first calving for cows of the beef-dairy type. Additionally, the service period lasted 78.3 days for dairy-type cows and 81.2 days for dairy-beef-type cows—4.2 and 1.3 days shorter, respectively, than the service period for beef-dairy-type cows. Research findings regarding the duration of the service period indicate that the cow itself is a primary factor determining reproductive performance; this highlights the importance of effectively utilizing cows of dairy and dual-purpose (dairy-beef) types for milk production.</jats:p>

372cb4c69dc68f61038297f6ed9d9f1ebba38b16.abstract: <jats:p>The article presents the results of a study of milk productivity in local goats and first-generation (F₁) crossbred goats obtained by crossing local does with purebred Murciano-Granadina breeding bucks imported from abroad, as well as with Murciano-Granadina breeding bucks produced through local selection. The study examined lactation performance indicators and the chemical composition of milk, including the contents of protein, fat, lactose, dry matter, and mineral substances. A comparative analysis of these indicators was conducted between local goats and F₁ crossbreds.</jats:p>

title: ТЎҒОНСИЗ СУВ ОЛИШ ШАРОИТИДА МАГИСТРАЛ КАНАЛ КИРИШ ҚИСМИДА ЛОЙҚА ЧЎКИНДИЛАРИ ДИНАМИКАСИНИ ТАҲЛИЛ ҚИЛИШ ВА ЗЕМСНАРЯДЛАР ИШЛАШ САМАРАДОРЛИГИНИ ОШИРИШ

5f254fc5f7b7f246b8ec58bd1d3b1fca692abe1d.abstract: <jats:p>The article examines the dynamics of sediment deposition at the intake section of the Qarshi Main Canal (QMC) under damless (free) water intake from the Amudarya River, together with the role of dredgers in the overall volume of cleaning works. Based on field monitoring data, the distribution of sediment along the canal length, as well as the technical condition and placement of the fleet of 17 dredgers along the canal, were analysed. It was found that the PK 0-40 segment of the canal intake accumulates more than 85% of the total sediment volume, making it the most heavily loaded section. Recommendations are proposed for the rational placement of dredgers along the canal and for adjusting the cleaning schedule to seasonal sediment inflow.</jats:p>

title: ШЎРЛАНМАГАН ТУПРОҚЛАР ШАРОИТИДА КУЗГИ БУҒДОЙНИ СУҒОРИШ МУДДАТЛАРИНИ БЕЛГИЛАШДА БАРГ ҲУЖАЙРА ШИРАСИ КОНЦЕНТРАЦИЯСИ ВА ТУПРОҚ НАМЛИГИ ДИНАМИКАСИ

f9b8de5eb1f617501ce4215003adb91c374cb193.abstract: <jats:p>The article evaluates the pre-irrigation soil moisture regimes (70-70-70, 75-75-75, and 80-80-80% of FC) and the dynamics of leaf cell sap concentration (CSC) in winter wheat grown on non-saline soils during 2020–2021. The results indicated that as pre-irrigation soil moisture increased, leaf CSC values proportionally decreased (13.82–16.31%), whereas toward the end of the growing season, values rose to 17.36–19.50% due to physiological tissue senescence. The study substantiates the high efficacy of using a refractometric method for rapid determination of irrigation timing based on CSC to enhance water-use efficiency. </jats:p>

379586c39b8fc86fe6bcbc1041c1fd88ba0b9658.abstract: <jats:p>This study evaluated sprinkler irrigation for carrot production on typical grey soils in the Tashkent region of Uzbekistan. Field experiments with the “Mirzoyi kizil” variety compared furrow irrigation with sprinkler intensities of 0.3, 0.4, and 0.5 mm min⁻¹. The highest yield, 29.2 t ha⁻¹, was obtained at 0.4 mm min⁻¹, compared with 22.7 t ha⁻¹ under furrow irrigation.</jats:p>

The final suitability class is determined by the most limiting factor. Separating current and potential suitability and using GIS zoning makes it possible to select irrigation technologies that better match local conditions.</jats:p>

title: SUGʻORILADIGAN BOʻZ - OʻTLOQI TUPROQLARNING AGROKIMYOVIY XOSSALARI VA SANOAT CHIQINDILARI TA’SIRIDA OGʻIR METALLAR BILAN IFLOSLANISHI

ba0ed90ab84fabb0583adc409521ff67536ed2c8.abstract: <jats:p>This article highlights the agrochemical properties of irrigated gray-earth meadow soils of Sharaf Rashidovsky district of the Jizzakh Free Economic Zone (JEZ), reserves of humus, total nitrogen, total phosphorus, and potassium. There is a high probability of heavy metal pollution in the region near industrial zones, free economic zones, and irrigation networks. Since these soils have a relatively humic layer, as well as a unique water-retaining structure, heavy metals can accumulate in the soil and negatively affect its agrochemical properties. Heavy metals adhere to soil colloids and retain their activity in the soil for a long time. In the soil under study, the lead content of Pb is 40-80 mg/kg (the norm is 32 mg/kg or more), cadmium CD is 0.5 - 2.0 mg/kg (the norm is 0.5 mg/kg or more), zinc Zn is 150-220 mg/kg (the norm is 100 mg/kg or more). This situation indicates an increase in the level of pollution combined with salinization and carbonate content of irrigated gray-earth meadow soils.</jats:p>

The effects of the number of ripper discs, vertical load, and travel speed on the degree of soil crumbling and draft resistance were studied. title: LEGUME CROP PRODUCTION IN UZBEKISTAN: AN EMPIRICAL ANALYSIS OF DETERMINANTS
container-title: Agro ilm
b7f635d6999751960d8ed769b449e51e02d7f0e9.abstract: <jats:p>This paper examines factors affecting legume production in Uzbekistan using cross-sectional data from 1,225 farmers across 12 districts in the UzFarmBarometer 2024 database. A probit model identifies factors associated with the probability of legume adoption. Results show that older farmers are less likely to cultivate legumes, while larger households and more experienced farmers are more likely to adopt them. Earlier-established farms also show lower adoption. Distance to input markets is positively associated with adoption, whereas distance to output markets is negatively associated with it, reflecting differences in input dependence and transaction costs. We suggest that improving rural market infrastructure, extension services, and stable labor arrangements could support legume cultivation.</jats:p>

title: AI adoption in purchasing and supply management: how institutional voids rewire the UTAUT framework
container-title: Modern Supply Chain Research and Applications
fd976dc156551128de71dc829f70972275c8141d.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Purpose</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study investigates how institutional voids and behavioral factors jointly drive artificial intelligence (AI) adoption in purchasing and supply management (PSM) within emerging economies.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Design/methodology/approach</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Survey data from 200 PSM professionals in Morocco were analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) to test an integrated UTAUT–institutional theory framework.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Findings</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Performance expectancy (PE) (ß = 0.530) and social influence (ß = 0.453) primarily drive behavioral intention (BI), while coercive pressure is non-significant (ß = 0.050, p = 0.260). Facilitating conditions (FC) (ß = 0.472) and (BI) (ß = 0.497) exert near-equal direct effects on actual use, confirming an “infrastructure imperative”. Post-hoc multi-group analysis reveals that PE dominates predictive AI adoption, whereas effort expectancy dominates Generative AI.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Practical implications</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Organizations in emerging economies must pair AI software procurement with dedicated infrastructure, data governance and peer-led change management rather than relying on unsupported mandates.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Originality/value</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study demonstrates that institutional voids modify the UTAUT nomological network by elevating FC to a primary co-determinant of technology use, proving infrastructure readiness equals user intention in driving adoption.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Future of work in the era of AI: how technology strategy shapes daily job roles
container-title: International Journal of Organizational Analysis
aafce7fbea450e0f9f9a750ed043c623a0abe324.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Purpose</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study aims to explore the impact of organizational technology strategies, particularly in the context of artificial intelligence (AI), on employees’ daily job activities. It also looks at the extent of the transformation and the role of leadership, supportive of innovation and cultural change, in reinforcing the transformation.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Design/methodology/approach</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The researcher adopted a quantitative research design based on the survey data collected from employees in various industries in Pakistan. The researcher used structural equation modeling to analyze the relationships among technology strategies, organizational facilitators and the transformation of job roles.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Findings</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The research shows that organizations that implement AI and automation alongside digitized processes and advanced data analysis capabilities will experience fundamental changes in their employees’ work functions, skills and job duties. The implementation of digital strategies enhances operational efficiency, but their impact extends beyond this benefit, as they completely transform how work is executed. The presence of an innovation-supportive culture together with strong leadership commitment creates an enhanced effect. The combination of encouragement of organizational experimentation and active leadership support for technological change results in more visible and positive changes in job responsibilities.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Practical implications</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The research findings demonstrate that organizations need to combine technology investments with operational changes to achieve successful digital transformation outcomes. Organizations must establish supportive cultures together with proactive leadership to assist employees throughout the process of organizational change. Organizations need to develop their employees’ skills and build adaptable workforces while maintaining open communication to implement meaningful job role changes that last over time.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Originality/value</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The research contributes to the future of work literature by examining how workers change their job functions at the individual-employee level rather than observing outcomes at the organizational level. The research describes how organizations use technology strategies and organizational enablers to create distinct work environments for the AI age by integrating Job Demands–Resources and Socio-Technical Systems perspectives.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: The copilot paradox: configurational pathways to human-AI symbiosis in knowledge work
container-title: International Journal of Organizational Analysis
10429646653846e10fef0781eea8935c49efcda2.abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine the “Copilot Paradox” in safety-critical operations, offering insights into how the chronic tension between the algorithm’s increased efficiency and operational vulnerability is subdued through socio-cognitive configurations across time. Design/methodology/approach With the use of a two-wave longitudinal fuzzy-set Qualitative Comparative Analysis (fsQCA), the paper explores the changing dynamics of human–artificial intelligence (AI) symbiosis in the oil and gas industry. Findings Analysis of necessity shows that there is no single condition required in all cases. Sufficiency analysis reveals three distinct, equifinal pathways: buffering, synergy and substitution. At early adoption, institutional re-skilling coupled with psychological safety acts as a buffering mechanism against job insecurity induced by AI. As integration progresses, synergy (fuelled by empowering leadership) and substitution (where team resources fill the gaps in leadership) come to dominate. Practical implications Team psychological safety and capability building are structural safeguards for managers in high-reliability sectors, not optional cultural flourishes. These lessons point to pathways for realising AI copilots while preserving human agency and operational resiliency. Originality/value This paper contributes to paradox theory by developing a socio-cognitive infrastructure that highlights its dynamic, temporal configuration and causal asymmetries. Methodologically, it showcases the new promise of longitudinal fsQCA to model dynamics in algorithms’ infusion by capturing their embeddedness through time.

title: From risk management to AI-enabled governance: five intellectual orientations in EPC and infrastructure project risk governance
container-title: Journal of Engineering, Design and Technology
262b73632bb16a2f06249b0dfe727ae37edc8674.abstract: Purpose This study aims to synthesise the intellectual development of engineering–procurement–construction and infrastructure project risk governance and examine whether bibliometric evidence supports five overlapping intellectual orientations. Design/methodology/approach The study combined bibliometric analysis with Bibliometrix/Biblioshiny, VOSviewer and a scripted workflow to examine 173 Scopus-indexed publications (1999–2026). The analytical corpus was derived through relevance validation of 678 candidate records, with provenance checked against an 801-row master ledger. Fifteen provisional 2026 records were excluded from temporal comparisons. Findings The analysis identified five orientations: risk analysis and control (53 documents), performance and overrun (80), governance and relational mechanisms (52), digital information integration (7) and artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled decision support (18). The share of period publications addressing performance and overrun increased from 34.7 % in 1999–2018 to 59.7 % in 2023–2025, whereas the digital and AI orientations remained comparatively limited. These patterns concern the published literature and do not establish organizational maturity or realised capability. Research limitations/implications Scopus coverage, title/abstract-based relevance validation, citation lag, analytical thresholds and interpretive coding delimit the findings. Project-level research is required to test the proposed relationships. Practical implications The orientations provide structured review prompts for risk processes, outcome linkage, decision rights, information integration and human oversight of predictive systems; they are not intended as a diagnostic maturity instrument. Originality/value The study connects construction risk, megaproject governance and construction AI through an auditable corpus and an evidence-bounded conceptual framework.

title: Digital and AI tools in informal care: understanding caregivers’ experiences in rural Nigeria
container-title: Working with Older People
3d95ea5e81a5dd3ac98c9f9e80e04a8c952edbad.abstract: Purpose Although informal caregiving for older adults is well-researched, a significant gap exists in understanding how informal caregivers navigate their caregiving roles with the help of digital technologies, especially in rural Nigeria, where internet connectivity is poor and access to digital devices is limited. This study aims to explore how informal caregivers in rural Nigeria use digital technology to support care for older adults. Design/methodology/approach The study adopted a qualitative descriptive approach, data were collected from 10 informal caregivers, using semi-structured interviews. The data were further analysed thematically using NVivo 14. Findings Results identified that caregivers use digital technology for communication and care coordination, learning and self-empowerment, responding to emergency situations, improving efficiency, reducing stress and maintaining contact between older adults and their diaspora family members. The study also found poor access and limited internet infrastructure as barriers to the use of digital technology to improve caregiving. Research limitations/implications Only caregivers in rural areas were interviewed. This excluded the experiences of caregivers in urban areas, who may face urban economic stressors that shape their overall caregiving experience and their use of digital technology for caregiving. Practical implications The findings highlight the potential of digital technology to support informal caregiving in rural Nigeria. Improving access to affordable digital devices, reliable internet connectivity and digital literacy can enhance care coordination, caregiver support, emergency response and communication with older adults and their families. Originality/value This study is important because it provides new insight into how informal caregivers in rural Nigeria use digital technology to support older adults despite limited connectivity and access to digital devices. It highlights both the potential of digital tools to strengthen caregiving and the infrastructural barriers that must be addressed.

title: Librarians' perspectives on AI for environmental sustainability in Ghanaian academic libraries
container-title: Library Hi Tech
931d99d9c196e1b88e58ba8390c4eca27c050aac.abstract: Purpose This study examined academic librarians' perspectives on the potential of artificial intelligence to advance environmental sustainability through sustainable library practices and efficient service delivery. Design/methodology/approach A qualitative approach was adopted, drawing on semi-structured interviews with 21 academic librarians and guided by the Technology Acceptance Model. Thematic analysis was used to identify key patterns and perspectives on AI adoption for environmental sustainability in academic libraries. Findings The study found that academic librarians recognize AI's potential to advance environmental sustainability through intelligent energy management, predictive maintenance, environmental monitoring, and sustainability planning, yet its practical implementation remains limited. Research limitations/implications The qualitative design and small sample limit generalizability; however, the findings provide contextual insights and a basis for broader research across diverse library settings. Practical implications The findings recommend that universities and library management integrate AI into sustainability planning through effective governance, improved digital infrastructure, and continuous AI literacy training, supported by national policies and investment in responsible AI innovation. Social implications The study highlights the value of AI in advancing environmental sustainability in libraries, emphasizing the need for educational initiatives, institutional policies, and responsible technology adoption. Originality/value This study provides timely empirical insight into AI-enabled environmental sustainability in Ghanaian academic libraries, highlighting the critical gap between librarians' awareness and perceived potential of AI and its limited practical implementation.

title: Efficacy of Stellate Ganglion Block for Preventing Postoperative Atrial Fibrillation After Cardiac Surgery: A Randomized, Double‐Blind, Placebo‐Controlled Trial
container-title: Journal of the American Heart Association
47d160a0277168adf9351a8df9bee14429b106b7.abstract: Background Stellate ganglion block (SGB) may reduce postoperative atrial fibrillation (POAF) by modulating the autonomic nervous system. This study evaluated the efficacy of preoperative SGB in preventing POAF following cardiac surgery. Methods In this single‐center, randomized, double‐blind, placebo‐controlled trial, 140 patients undergoing valve surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass were assigned (1:1) to ultrasound‐guided right SGB with 7 mL of 0.5% ropivacaine or 7 mL of normal saline. The primary outcome was the incidence of POAF from postoperative day 0 to day 7 or until discharge. Results A total of 132 patients completed the study and were included in the modified intention‐to‐treat population (SGB group: n=65; saline group: n=67). POAF occurred in 43% of the SGB group and 40% of the saline group (odds ratio [OR], 0.99 [95% CI, 0.46–2.15], adjusted P =0.989). The SGB group demonstrated a lower incidence of intraoperative ventricular fibrillation/ventricular tachycardia requiring defibrillation after aortic cross‐clamp release (6% versus 19%; OR, 0.21 [95% CI, 0.06–0.80]; adjusted P =0.022), lower postoperative high‐sensitivity troponin I levels (median difference: −2562 ng/L [95% CI, −4301 to −45]; P =0.045), and a reduced risk of postoperative acute kidney injury (5% versus 18%; OR, 0.24 [95% CI, 0.06–0.98]; adjusted P =0.046). Conclusions While preoperative SGB did not reduce the incidence of POAF, it was associated with potential benefits, including a lower requirement for intraoperative defibrillation attributable to ventricular arrhythmias, attenuated myocardial injury (as indicated by lower high‐sensitivity troponin I levels), and a decreased risk of postoperative acute kidney injury. Registration URL: https://www.chictr.org.cn ; URL Identifier: ChiCTR2300068572.

title: Capabilities shaping institutional adoption: modeling generative AI adoption in higher education
container-title: Journal of Knowledge Management
08a009fe077bc5af12d714b4d60c2ab8c6973296.abstract: Purpose Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is rapidly transforming higher education, yet its successful institutional adoption extends beyond technological capability to require effective knowledge governance, organizational readiness and coordinated decision-making. This study aims to structurally model the CSFs for GenAI adoption in education using an integrated interpretive structural modeling (ISM)–DEMATEL approach. The authors frame GenAI adoption explicitly as a knowledge management problem, analyzing how governance, infrastructure and privacy conditions enable or inhibit institutional capabilities for creating, sharing and governing GenAI-empowered knowledge. Design/methodology/approach The authors identified ten CSFs through a structured literature review and classified them as enablers, capabilities or outcomes across governance, infrastructure, data privacy, analytics, user experience and academic integrity. To analyze the causal and hierarchical relationships among CSFs, an expert validation was conducted through DEMATEL analysis by 20 experts, followed by ISM modeling, which involved 16 experts. Findings DEMATEL identifies technical infrastructure and scalability (CSF-V), data privacy and security (CSF-VII) and integration with LMS/SSO/enterprise systems (CSF-IX) as prominent causal factors. ISM further positions CSF-V at the deepest foundational level, followed by AI governance, policy and ethics (CSF-III), while assessment integrity and academic honesty (CSF-X) occupies the terminal dependent level. The findings identify assessment integrity (CSF-X), prompt literacy (CSF-IV) and user experience (CSF-VI) as dependent factors, confirming that they emerge from structural readiness rather than acting as independent adoption determinants. Research limitations/implications Results are restricted to expert judgment and defined CSFs, which can reduce generalizability across diverse educational settings. Future research must involve larger samples, validate empirically and use longitudinal designs to study changing relations while also testing the knowledge governance mechanisms revealed in this research. Practical implications The model enables phased prioritization of CSFs for optimal implementation of GenAI. Foundational readiness requires infrastructure, system integration and data governance, followed by governance policies and faculty capacity development, before addressing user experience and academic integrity as dependent outcomes. Originality/value The research provides a systems approach to GenAI adoption in education by presenting an integrated ISM–DEMATEL framework based on TOE and DOI, grounded in knowledge governance theory. It aids authors’ understanding of how technological, organizational and knowledge governance dimensions must be sequentially aligned to enable better implementation of GenAI.

title: Facilitating generative mentoring in higher education: a systematic review and measurement framework for mentoring, generativity, and the minority tax
container-title: International Journal of Mentoring and Coaching in Education
1c4576303f7dc7a655cd1b351ac0a3834966b1b5.abstract: Purpose The purpose of this study is to synthesise how faculty mentoring in higher education has been evaluated in relation to mentor generativity and equity-related pressures (including the minority tax) and to propose a minimum measurement framework for valid evaluation. Design/methodology/approach A Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses 2020-guided systematic review was registered on the International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews (CRD42025647836). The review question was developed using a Sample, Phenomenon of Interest, Design, Evaluation, Research-informed approach appropriate to the inclusion of both quantitative and qualitative evidence. Scopus, Web of Science, ScienceDirect and EBSCOhost were searched from database inception to June 2025. Two reviewers independently screened and extracted data, study quality was appraised using design-appropriate tools, and findings were narratively synthesised. Findings Eight studies met the inclusion criteria (six quantitative, two qualitative), with most of the evidence from the USA. No study directly measured mentor generativity using validated generativity instruments; instead, studies relied on proxy outcomes (e.g. satisfaction, productivity, promotion). This limits conclusions about the construct validity of generativity and may obscure costs when mentoring demands are high and recognition is low, especially for historically marginalised faculty. Research limitations/implications The evidence base was small (eight studies), predominantly U.S.-based, methodologically heterogeneous, and reliant on proxy outcomes rather than validated measures of mentor generativity. These limitations precluded meta-analysis and causal inference. Future research should directly measure generativity alongside mentoring load, institutional recognition, strain, and equity-related indicators across more diverse regions, disciplines, and institutional contexts. Practical implications The framework provides institutions and researchers with a concise set of indicators to evaluate mentoring programmes, inform workload crediting and promotion criteria, and monitor equity in the distribution and recognition of mentoring labour. Originality/value This review reframes the evaluation of faculty mentoring as a construct-measurement problem and proposes a minimum measurement framework that distinguishes direct generativity from commonly used proxy outcomes. By integrating mentoring load, institutional recognition, strain, and equity considerations, the framework also provides a basis for empirically testing the proposed “generativity paradox”, the conditions under which mentoring may be experienced as renewing, burdensome, or both.

title: The relationship between AI awareness and thriving at work: exploring the moderated mediation model
container-title: European Journal of Training and Development
cfd18b7156538271965b458c0a8e74dbffca959e.abstract: Purpose Drawing on the socially embedded model of thriving and the conservation of resources model, this study aims to investigate the relationship between artificial intelligence (AI) awareness, seen as a hindrance stressor, and thriving at work. In particular, it explores how AI anxiety mediates this relationship and how self-efficacy moderates the mediating effect. Design/methodology/approach To securitize the study hypotheses, data were obtained from banking employees via an electronic questionnaire, yielding 320 valid responses. The proposed model relationships were assessed through partial least squares structural equation modeling and process analysis. Findings The results uncover that while AI awareness is not significantly linked to vitality, it is negatively correlated with learning. Furthermore, AI anxiety mediates the direct influence that AI awareness has on dimensions of thriving at work. In addition, self-efficacy acts as a buffer, mitigating the adverse indirect influence of AI awareness on thriving at work through AI anxiety. Practical implications This study highlights the need for organizations adopting AI-driven systems to execute‎ initiatives that mitigate AI-induced stress, thereby fostering employee thriving. It is recommended that organizations offer targeted training and digital literacy programs, alongside interventions designed to enhance self-efficacy, to bolster employee well-being amid rapid technological change. Originality/value This study highlights the need for organizations adopting AI-driven systems to execute‎ initiatives that mitigate AI-induced stress, thereby fostering employee thriving. It is recommended that organizations offer targeted training and revise their role descriptions, alongside interventions designed to enhance self-efficacy, to bolster employee well-being amid rapid technological change.

title: Demystifying generative AI adoption in higher education: an integrated GRAI–AKM framework
container-title: Journal of Knowledge Management
2d81d35ddbb0a163d25a04512796c4f2fe000a1d.abstract: Purpose Generative Artificial Intelligence (Gen AI) is rapidly transforming higher education, yet successful institutional adoption requires effective knowledge governance, organizational readiness and coordinated decision-making. Existing studies have predominantly relied on individual-level technology acceptance models, providing limited insight into organizational and knowledge management capabilities for sustainable implementation. Design/methodology/approach A qualitative research design was employed using open-ended written responses from 20 academic professionals recruited through Prolific. The qualitative responses were analyzed using thematic analysis, and the resulting themes were mapped onto the proposed graphs with results and actions interconnected (GRAI) and active knowledge models (AKM) framework (GRAI–AKM). Findings Six themes were identified: (1) professional training and AI literacy, (2) ethical governance and academic integrity, (3) structural capital flexibility and knowledge processes, (4) trust, transparency and relational capital, (5) platform maturity and technological infrastructure and (6) human–AI complementarity. Professional training and AI literacy emerged as the most-discussed themes. The findings suggest that Gen AI adoption depends on the interaction of human, structural, technological, and knowledge resources rather than technology acceptance alone. Research limitations/implications Although based on a qualitative sample and self-reported written responses, the study advances knowledge management research by integrating Intellectual Capital (IC) and the Knowledge-Based View (KBV) into a comprehensive framework. Practical implications The findings highlight the importance of AI literacy, ethical governance, organizational learning and human–AI collaboration for sustainable adoption of Gen AI in higher education. Originality/value The study provides qualitative empirical support for the GRAI–AKM framework, offering a multidimensional perspective on knowledge management for sustainable adoption of Gen AI.

title: Organizational AI orientation, AI self-efficacy and value co-creation: a human-AI collaboration perspective in healthcare
container-title: Journal of Health Organization and Management
6445e52cab7175f314892526d760c6e1d1251ed8.abstract: Purpose Artificial intelligence (AI) is vital to healthcare system transformation. Existing research mainly focuses on the macro-level technological empowerment of AI, yet insufficiently explores how healthcare organizations’ strategic commitment to AI translates into better medical service outcomes through individual psychological mechanisms. Design/methodology/approach From the perspective of human-AI collaboration, we utilize survey data collected from medical staff working in Chinese medical institutions to examine the mediating mechanisms and boundary conditions linking organizational AI orientation and AI value co-creation outcomes. Findings Drawing on social cognitive theory, the results reveal that healthcare organizations’ AI orientation is positively related to medical staff’s AI value co-creation outcomes, and AI self-efficacy mediates this relationship. Moreover, their creative self-efficacy positively moderates the relationship between AI self-efficacy and AI value co-creation. Originality/value This study clarifies the micro-level transmission paths between organizational AI orientation and medical staff’s value co-creation outcomes. It provides new insights for hospitals to enhance medical service quality and optimize human-AI collaboration during AI-driven healthcare organizational transformation.

title: Evolutionary dynamics of AI-driven enterprise digital transformation: a cybernetic perspective
container-title: Kybernetes
406b79671b63af881cd115f6a281bbe0560605cc.abstract: Purpose In the AI era, digital transformation has become essential for enterprises to adapt as complex systems to uncertain business environments. In this work, we aim to analyze the evolutionary dynamics of AI-driven enterprise digital transformation (EDT), focusing on its evolution and impact on enterprise performance from a system cybernetics perspective. Design/methodology/approach We employ evolutionary dynamics analysis grounded in game theory to model the EDT process, and perform an econometric and empirical analysis on a sample of Chinese A-share-listed enterprises from 2009 to 2023. The approach encompasses heterogeneity analysis, moderation effect models, such as testing enterprise environmental, social, and governance (ESG) factors and market concentration, and threshold effect analyses. Findings The evolutionary dynamics analysis finds that increasing the risk-averse benefits of traditional enterprises and reducing the additional benefit coefficient would hinder EDT. Increasing the investment of technology enterprises in internal resource restructuring accelerates the transformation process. Empirically, AI significantly contributes to EDT. ESG positively moderates the relationship between AI and EDT, while market concentration exerts a negative moderating effect. Furthermore, AI and EDT show an inverted U-shaped trend when R&D intensity exceeds a specific threshold, while a U-shaped trend is observed when enterprise performance exceeds a specific threshold. Originality/value In this work, we uncover the complex, non-linear cybernetic feedback loops, such as U-shaped and inverted U-shaped, and boundary conditions, such as ESG and market concentration for AI-driven EDT, offering systemic strategies for enterprises adapting to the digital ecosystem.

title: Neuro-symbolic AI for proactive risk forecasting: bridging large language models and dynamic Bayesian networks
container-title: Smart and Sustainable Built Environment
9a1bf248111e208571dfad68b70369f36fefa354.abstract: Purpose Periodic risk reports constitute a substantial repository of operational data for project management. Despite the inherent informational value, archived records remain largely unstructured and highly fragmented. This study proposes a fully local neuro-symbolic approach for dynamic risk forecasting by translating qualitative project narratives into a quantifiable predictive engine to support decision-making. Design/methodology/approach The proposed methodology adopts a mixed-methods architecture including four layers: (1) spatial morphology reconstruction using a Y-axis density clustering algorithm; (2) a hybrid pseudonymization filter; (3) a local large language model (LLM) with chain-of-thought reasoning; and (4) a symbolic causal engine powered by a dynamic Bayesian network (DBN) to quantify causal propagation into a dynamic risk index. Findings An empirical evaluation across 28 reporting cycles spanning a 33-month large-scale infrastructure project indicates that the symbolic layer provides a temporally coherent aggregation of the output of a zero-shot perception layer operating at a macro F1-score of 53.62%. By quantifying causal risk propagation, the DBN captured a 93.59% risk-saturation state, for which the retrieved evidence identifies chronic site-clearance bottlenecks. Notably, using an alert threshold selected by sensitivity analysis together with an analytic constraint on the posterior mass attributable to the critical state (talert = 70.0%), the model outputs Bayesian probabilities alongside LLM-extracted textual evidence, yielding an anticipation interval of 1.33 reporting cycles relative to the documented administrative response. Originality/value The neuro-symbolic framework bridges the gap between deep learning perception and causal inference in construction management. By coupling LLM-driven zero-shot ordinal extraction with DBN causal reasoning, the research establishes an auditable framework for risk documentation. The integrated framework transitions AI from an opaque prediction model into an accountable decision-support tool, providing stakeholders with transparent explainable AI diagnostics and supporting a shift from reactive mitigation to proactive, evidence-based risk prevention.

328c2811455766f15c52fe23724799c45e0d5bbc.abstract: The article investigates the effect of irrigation on the formation and accumulation of nodule bacteria in the root system of the chickpea varieties “Yulduz” and “Milyutin-6” under meadow sierozem soil conditions in the Samarkand region. title: Academic librarians' perceptions of new skills, competencies and professional development needs in the AI age
container-title: Library Hi Tech
3610c8c0f0d1c535e41c0b71849dce304d1c7a28.abstract: Purpose This study examined academic librarians' perceptions of new skills and competencies, use of AI tools and professional development needs. Design/methodology/approach An online survey was distributed via professional networks, and data were collected and analysed from 155 valid respondents across Australia, European countries and the USA. Findings The findings demonstrate that the highly ranked new skills needed by academic librarians included AI tools and output evaluation, application of data governance and management, AI literacy instruction and integration of AI into curricula. The new competencies consisted of ethical implementation and governance, critical analysis and evaluation of AI tools and AI literacy and conceptual understanding of AI. AI tools could be used to improve information service provisions through responsible and ethical information management and discovery. Key training and knowledge areas included critical evaluation of AI-generated content. Hands-on tutorials with case studies and in-person or hybrid workshops were the most suitable training formats. Practical implications The findings are helpful and practical for academic librarians to develop new skills and competencies and support professional development and curriculum renewal. Originality/value The new contribution of this study lies in the identification of important new skills and competencies that academic librarians need to utilise AI tools in a successful way, mitigate associated potential risks and adapt to changing professional roles.

title: Beyond the laggard myth: time-series analysis of AI job market dynamics in construction
container-title: Smart and Sustainable Built Environment
4e1908c31127b7c180069c373440c5cd8dc5cf0e.abstract: Purpose This study presents one of the first time-series, cross-industry analyses of the artificial intelligence (AI) job market for the construction sector. It benchmarks construction against both digital and traditional industries to interrogate prevailing assumptions of linear diffusion and temporal catch-up in AI workforce adoption. Design/methodology/approach Drawing on 51 months of Lightcast job postings (January 2021–March 2025), with construction defined as ANZSIC Division E, the study employs an interpretable analytical toolkit comprising Seasonal-Trend decomposition using Loess decomposition (period = 12), month-of-year bootstrap tests on detrended series, cross-correlation analysis with bootstrap confidence bands, Newey–West trend estimation on sectoral share ratios and conservative one-step Exponential Smoothing State-Space (ETS) forecasts. All results are re-estimated excluding the partial final month (March 2025) as a sensitivity check. Findings Construction's AI hiring is very sparse, accounting for under 1% of AI postings and is more volatile than hiring in peer sectors, but it grew fastest: annual construction postings rose more than fourfold between 2021 and 2024, against increases of 13% and 9% in the digital and traditional sectors, whose postings peaked in 2022. Construction's share of AI postings relative to both comparators therefore rises (converges) rather than falls. No delayed-follower pattern is detected: no lag at which the comparator sectors lead construction is statistically reliable, and the short-run associations that are detected are weak, near-contemporaneous and sensitive to the sample end. Unlike the comparator sectors, construction shows no statistically significant within-year seasonality and short-horizon ETS forecasts do not improve on a seasonal-naïve benchmark. These findings are robust to the exclusion of the partial final month of data. Construction thus appears as a low-base, fast-growing entrant with its own hiring dynamics, not a “laggard” following digital-sector cycles with a delay. Practical implications The findings suggest that construction firms should prioritise internal capability building and domain-specific AI skills where external hiring is thin, support flexible, year-round upskilling, and design policy and vendor strategies tailored to the sector's operational realities rather than importing digital-sector playbooks. Originality/value This study provides among the first data-driven, time-series evidence that qualifies the dominant “late adopter” narrative in construction. It shows that construction's low level of AI hiring coexists with the fastest growth and a rising share, without a delayed-follower timing pattern, distinguishing a low starting point from a lagging trajectory and offering an empirically grounded alternative to technologically deterministic accounts of cross-industry AI adoption.

title: Combined imaging of myocardial scar and fat using AI-guided dual bright- and black-blood late gadolinium enhancement
container-title: European Heart Journal - Imaging Methods and Practice
ae0982a8e8e213a8cea9fa3564d8cc1d02f304ce.abstract: Abstract Aims Characterization of myocardial scar and fat is clinically important for diagnosis, risk stratification, and procedural planning in cardiomyopathies. While black-blood late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) improves scar conspicuity, fat remains hyperintense and may confound interpretation. We aimed to develop and evaluate SPOT-DIXON, a dual bright- and black-blood LGE sequence with Dixon water-fat separation and artificial intelligence (AI)-guided analysis, enabling simultaneous and co-registered quantification of myocardial scar and intra- and extra-cardiac fat. Methods SPOT-DIXON alternates bright- and black-blood LGE preparations on consecutive heartbeats while acquiring dual-echo data for Dixon water-fat separation. Simulations, phantom experiments, and validations in a prospective cohort of 36 patients referred for cardiac MRI were performed. An AI model automatically segmented the left ventricular (LV) wall on bright-blood water images, with contours propagation to scar and fat images. Results Simulations and phantoms confirmed preserved bright- and black-blood contrast and accurate water-fat separation. In patients, AI-based LV wall segmentation showed excellent agreement with manual delineation (global DICE=84.4 ± 4.0%). SPOT-DIXON yielded higher scar volume, burden, and transmurality measurements than reference sequences, while LV wall volume was similar between sequences. Novel quantitative metrics, including intramyocardial fat burden expressed relative to scar mass, were feasible only with SPOT-DIXON. Acquisition times were comparable across sequences (5min55s ± 2min17 s), while AI-based analysis substantially reduced post-processing time to 2.1 ± 0.7 seconds. Conclusion AI-guided SPOT-DIXON enables simultaneous, co-registered assessment of myocardial scar and fat within a single LGE acquisition. This approach overcomes key limitations of current workflows and introduces novel quantitative markers of fibrofatty remodelling with potential clinical relevance in cardiomyopathies.

title: Water footprint of large AI models: risks to global water security and sustainable optimization strategies
container-title: Water Policy
71384b0b7ce71aeb82049c155da192ce552f67b9.abstract: ABSTRACT Diagram linking AI model training and inference to lifecycle water use, estimated at 4.2–6.6 billion m³ annually by 2027, and showing water reuse, efficient cooling, smarter workloads, and standardized reporting as strategies to protect global water security. The rapid proliferation of large-scale artificial intelligence (AI) models has introduced a significant yet underexamined environmental challenge: freshwater consumption. This narrative review synthesizes scientific literature, industry sustainability reports, and case studies to quantify the water footprint of AI systems across their full lifecycle, from semiconductor fabrication and data center operations to electricity generation and supply chains. Direct water use occurs primarily through evaporative and liquid cooling in data centers, where a single large facility can consume 11,000–19,000m3/day. Indirect water use is embedded in electricity generation and chip manufacturing, with advanced fabrication plants drawing 10,000–37,000m3/day. Major technology companies, including Google, Microsoft, and Meta, collectively consume billions of cubic meters in 2022–2024, with consumption rising alongside accelerating AI deployment. Critically, over 52% of the world's top 100 data centers are projected to be located in high water stress regions by 2030, where AI infrastructure increasingly competes with agricultural, municipal, and ecological needs. Sustainable alternatives, including immersion cooling, nonpotable water reuse, and AI-driven workload optimization, offer measurable reductions but remain inconsistently adopted. The direct and indirect water footprints of AI models during their entire lifecycle are reviewed. Two of the main direct water usage sources are semiconductor manufacturing and data center cooling. Clip manufacturing and electricity generation significantly increase the indirect water footprint of AI. In areas with scarce freshwater supplies, the growth of AI technology may worsen water stress. Standardized reporting frameworks and lifecycle-based water accounting are urgently needed to safeguard global water security.

title: University students' disciplinary perspectives on generative AI after two years of its widespread use
container-title: Journal of Applied Research in Higher Education
e5ed294fd6697fa9565e5119f14a79e5ae870103.abstract: Purpose This study explores how university students use generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) across various disciplines, including STEM, Business, Education Futures, Clinical & Health Sciences (CHS), Creative and Allied Health & Human Performance (AHHP). It aims to identify discipline-based perspectives, perceived benefits, ethical boundaries and the support needs required for responsible use of GenAI tools. Design/methodology/approach A survey was conducted approximately two years after the widespread use of GenAI, by which time participants were expected to be familiar with its use. Students were categorised based on their discipline, English fluency, mode of learning and level of study. Their responses were analysed to compare usage patterns, satisfaction levels and ethical considerations across disciplines. Findings The results highlight that student perspectives on GenAI tools are discipline-dependent. STEM and Education Futures showed the highest acceptance, while CHS and Business students were more cautious and sceptical about accuracy and ethical issues. Non-native English speakers rated GenAI tools more favourably as aids for writing and comprehension. Novice users expressed enthusiasm, while expert users showed dissatisfaction due to errors and false information. Research limitations/implications The study relied on self-reported perceptions and represents a single institutional context. Broader investigations are recommended, with a particular focus on equity groups such as students with disabilities, low-SES students and remote learners. Practical implications Different approaches were suggested for integrating GenAI into learning. STEM students favoured comparative tasks; CHS recommended support for diagnostic reasoning; Allied Health preferred role-playing simulations; Education Futures highlighted lesson planning; and Business students suggested case-based and productivity uses. Originality/value The study provides cross-disciplinary analyses of GenAI use by students and proposes approaches for ethical and discipline-specific integration into university curricula.

c2aefe7750439a7c6d21abaa77f9bc7919a3e53b.abstract: This study examined the extent to which senior high school teachers monitor AI-generated written outputs, focusing on the use of AI detectors, manual review, and cross-checking results. The study respondents were teachers from the Humanities and Social Sciences (HUMSS) strand of Philippine Christian University-Dasmariñas. The researchers collected data through a structured questionnaire and analyzed it using descriptive statistics, including mean and standard deviation. Results showed that teachers used AI detectors and cross-checking to a moderate extent, while they used manual review to a high extent and found it significant. Teachers faced challenges such as limitations in AI detection tools and time constraints in manual evaluation and cross-checking. title: AI-Based Customer Service and Brand Loyalty in Saudi Retail: An Empirical Investigation of the Service Quality–Emotional Attachment–Loyalty Pathway in 2025–2026
container-title: Revista Cultura Científica
7447b8bdae9fbb1f476fe7e2a877364778cb869e.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI)-powered customer service systems have expanded across Saudi Arabia’s retail sector during 2025–2026, with major retailers increasingly exploring chatbots, recommendation engines, and automated service technologies. Official Saudi digital-economy statistics document the wider shift towards digital commerce, although online-shopping participation should not be interpreted as a direct measure of AI adoption or retailer-specific investment. This study examines the relationship among AI service quality, emotional brand attachment, and brand loyalty using survey results reported for 512 retail customers in Riyadh, Jeddah, and Dammam, collected between May and September 2026. Using partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM) and bootstrap resampling, the analysis reports a positive direct association between AI service quality and loyalty (β = 0.421, p < 0.001), together with a positive indirect association through emotional brand attachment (reported indirect effect = 0.238, 95% CI [0.187, 0.289]). The study considers a possible “mechanical efficiency paradox”: functional improvements in AI service may be more strongly associated with loyalty than with emotional attachment. Importantly, this survey does not include a direct comparison with human-delivered service, and the reported positive attachment coefficient (β = 0.187) cannot establish that AI decreases attachment. The reported gender subgroup estimates differ: the AI quality–attachment association is positive for male respondents (β = 0.289, p = 0.001) and statistically nonsignificant for female respondents (β = −0.023, p = 0.811). Age-specific estimates also vary, with more positive reported coefficients in younger groups, although the statistical significance of the age differences requires further supporting output. The manuscript reports that the model accounts for 51.2% of the variance in loyalty (R2 = 0.512) and has positive predictive relevance (Q2 = 0.289). Because some path estimates, correlations, and variance-explained values are not mutually consistent, these results require rechecking against the original SmartPLS output before publication. Managerial implications include offering hybrid AI–human service, allowing customers to choose their preferred channel, and maintaining personal attention for complex or emotionally sensitive interactions. The findings provide a framework for assessing how technological service quality and relationship-building might jointly contribute to brand loyalty.

aa4faf4ac7e79634028cac55dc7ad5f3339f2b47.abstract: Abstract : This study aims to analyze the challenges of using Generative Artificial Intelligence (Generative AI) to understand the Qur’an and Hadith among undergraduate Islamic Education (PAI) students, their practices of information verification and academic integrity, and the application of Islamic ethics of seeking knowledge. title: From Routine Fixed Schedules to Signals: A Condition-Responsive, AI-Augmented Pigging Intelligence Framework for Localised Internal Corrosion Control in Crude Oil and Water Injection Pipelines
container-title: ADIPEC
bb102d5cbb0ad65fc316c638ad53cb6149af8dab.abstract: Abstract Pigging plans in most operating companies globally are scheduled by calendar days. Pipeline segments are pigged every 30, 60 or 90 days based on the historical fixed maintenance schedules set during commissioning, regardless of the real time corrosion dynamics of the pipeline when in service. However, in most crude oil and water injection lines where the corrosion environment shifts with well stream composition, throughput and bacteria activity, the fixed schedule methodology of pigging does not prevent escalation of corrosion events. A five-year trending of several pipeline ILI data shows why 63% of anomalies deeper than 18% wall thickness were found in segments fully compliant with their pigging schedule. A 24-month study across 312 km length of pipelines compared condition-responsive segments against fixed 30-day controls showed that the mean maximum pit depth growth fell by 54.5% with over 80% drop in reactive integrity actions. Furthermore, the chemical inhibitor wetting efficiency increased by 18 points with 22.5% reduction in pigging runs. More so, 78% of the anomaly's clusters were located at the 5 to 7 o'clock orientation and concentrated in pipelines where inhibitor wetting had dropped below 69%. Sulphate Reducing Bacteria (SRB) and Iron Oxidizing Bacteria (IOB) counts proved the strongest leading indicators in the corrosion index, which is what should be expected in MIC-susceptible water injection systems. This paper proposes and validates the Pigging Intelligence Framework (PIF), in which pig runs are triggered by corrosion signals rather than fixed maintenance schedules. The PIF has three layers namely: the Corrosion Signal Index (CSI), supervised machine learning model and a root cause framework. The CSI combines flow velocity, BS&W content, microbiological activity, inhibitor residuals and ILI pit depth progression into a continuously updated risk score for each segment. Furthermore, the supervised machine learning model, trained on five years of pigging records and post-pig debris analytics from the pipelines, identifies the leading indicators of accelerated pitting. A root cause investigation tool anchored in NACE SP0106 ensures every unacceptable corrosion event produces a traceable corrective action, with outputs mapped to SAP PM and the integrity database. The study posits that pigging should be timed, based on the state of the pipeline and integrity condition of the medium rather than pigging as a historical norm. Therefore, it put forwards an A.I augmented framework in which pigging frequency, chemical dosing and inspection strategy recalibrate continuously from model output, closing the loop between detection, diagnosis and action.

title: The Skills Intelligence Engine for an AI-Ready Energy Workforce
container-title: ADIPEC
8f4721afded7a4529d81dc5465a5e908e8a7d7fd.abstract: Abstract As digitalization and AI reshape the energy industry, operators must transform large technical workforces without eroding core domain expertise. The challenge goes beyond training digital specialists; it requires evolving domain professionals into domain-plus-AI, domain-plus-digital, and domain-plus-business practitioners. This paper presents a framework of energy organization's Skills Intelligence Infrastructure, a single engine linking learning activity, curated curricula, skills maps, HR data, and a conversational AI agent (beta) that bridges HR and business to support upskilling, mobility, promotion readiness, and strategic workforce planning. The infrastructure was developed through a four-layer architecture. First, a unified data foundation integrates employee learning activity with HR data, enabling segmentation by role, organization, geography, seniority, and business area. Second, curated curricula and skills maps are designed with business owners to align with enterprise priorities across AI, machine learning, data, operations, sustainability, project management, safety-critical training, sales, and domain competence. These resources support aspirational and promotion-linked roles while clarifying expectations, gaps, and priorities. Third, persona-driven experiences serve employees and managers: employees pursue pathways, identify gaps and future requirements, and build T-shaped capability—deep domain expertise broadened by AI, digital, project, and business skills—while managers monitor development, assess the regional distribution of skills, and identify talent opportunities for mobility, promotion, and hiring. Fourth, a conversational AI agent lets employees ask which skills target roles require and which pathways to prioritize, while managers evaluate talent against skills, learning records, pathway completion, and readiness indicators. Deployed across approximately 8,000 professionals, the platform delivers curated curricula for more than 60 aspirational roles, including 12 promotion-linked roles, and hundreds of pathways across digital, AI, data, project management, safety, sales, and domain expertise. As the enterprise system of record for capability, it provides end-to-end visibility into the AI upskilling funnel: more than 3,000 employees advancing their skills, more than 1,500 certified data science practitioners, and early identification of domain data scientist candidates. It surfaces more than 150 AI-powered innovation projects across the E&P lifecycle and tracks participation in an enterprise's strategic development program. For managers, it reveals skills trends across regions, business lines, and disciplines, exposing hidden capability gaps and talent opportunities. By favoring internal development over hiring, it has reduced recruitment costs for scarce digital talent and improved satisfaction with learning and career development. Unlike commercial talent-marketplace platforms, this skills-based workforce intelligence solution is purpose-built for a large technical energy workforce. It links HR and business through manager-owned skills maps, integrates siloed domain certifications and critical pathways, and operationalizes the domain-to-domain-plus-AI transformation at scale. It supports upskilling, talent conversion, mobility, promotion readiness, compliance tracking, and build-versus-hire decisions. Future enhancements will infer skills from roles, projects, and experience and extend the AI agent into talent management. This provides a foundation on which the energy workforce can build as AI reshapes the industry.

title: From Multi-Agent Models to Enterprise Intelligent Agents: An AI-Powered Knowledge Compilation and Production Optimisation Platform for Oil and Gas Field Development
container-title: ADIPEC
e7d8f78e3172f82ea9630dc2347efccce5549eed.abstract: Abstract Oil and gas field development planning remains a slow, expert-dependent workflow, with multi-year plans scattered across subsidiaries in heterogeneous formats and tacit knowledge locked in individual experts. This paper presents an enterprise scientific research agent that compiles development plans into a unified knowledge base and enables autonomous scheme generation, simulation and continuous optimisation at enterprise scale. The architecture fuses a 240-indicator standardised ontology, multi-modal LLM knowledge compilation, a lifecycle-aware knowledge graph (facts, states, events), a RAG-augmented three-tier memory, long-horizon multi-agent orchestration (Build and Optimize modes with frozen-evidence acceptance), a unified MCP tool bus, and a git-style model relation tree that makes every run traceable and reversible. The platform has compiled 2,924 development plans across 14 subsidiaries of a national oil company. In a black-oil case, the agent autonomously generated water-flooding well-pattern schemes in two hours without human intervention, raising the ten-year recovery factor from 18.9% to 34.6% against a 30% target, while planning-cycle latency was substantially reduced. The results confirm that progressing from multi-agent research models to unified enterprise intelligent agents is a scalable path toward knowledge-driven decision-making in large, multi-asset petroleum portfolios.

title: A deep learning-based method for enhanced prediction of long-term diaphragm wall deflections using multi-source data
container-title: AI in Civil Engineering
04ff52c9850c5be57a455789b03eadf78fd2ea9f.abstract: Abstract Machine learning-based autoregressive models are widely applied to deformation prediction of braced excavations, yet they often suffer from pronounced error accumulation and deteriorated accuracy in long-term forecasting. To address these limitations, this study proposes a multi-source information fusion framework for predicting diaphragm wall deformation that integrates construction information with historical wall-deflection data. By incorporating construction-related dynamic features as auxiliary inputs, the proposed model effectively strengthens long-term dependency learning and reduces the propagation of autoregressive errors. A depth-weighted loss coefficient is further introduced to prioritize accuracy in shallow regions where deformation is most critical, and a 1D U-Net decoder is employed to enhance profile-level reconstruction through multi-scale spatial feature extraction. The framework is validated using two deep excavation projects on Nanjing Metro Line 11. For excavation-induced deformation, the model demonstrates stable and accurate multi-step prediction performance for diaphragm wall deflection, even under long forecasting steps. Comparative analyses further confirm that the proposed fusion architecture provides superior long-term robustness under limited monitoring data. The results highlight the method’s potential as a practical tool for deformation forecasting and construction risk management in foundation pit engineering.

title: AI-Agent-Built Fiber-Sensing Interpretation Platform for Real Well Operations
container-title: ADIPEC
ccebed683e4632e963d6055547994a210645342a.abstract: Abstract Distributed acoustic sensing (DAS) and distributed temperature sensing (DTS) are fiber-optic technologies that turn an optical fiber into a distributed sensor array. Originally developed in the telecommunications and defense sectors, these methods were adopted by the oil and gas industry. DTS entered thermal-recovery surveillance in the mid-1990s (Brown and Hartog 2002), and DAS followed more widely after the first downhole trials in 2009 (Molenaar et al. 2012). They now expand the observational basis for well logging by providing distributed temperature and acoustic measurements over the instrumented interval at survey-specific spatial and temporal sampling. However, interpretation-tool development has lagged acquisition technology: multiple vendor formats, multiday survey volumes, and job-specific processing still leave much of the acquired data underused relative to acquisition cost. An engineer-directed development approach was evaluated in which a domain engineer used general-purpose artificial intelligence (AI) coding agents to construct a DAS/DTS and well-log interpretation software environment. Development was performed against field-surveillance data sets from multiple vendors and job types. As application scope increased, unstructured agent use was replaced by a documentation-driven operating framework comprising architecture rules, task-scoped guidance, decision ownership, plan-before-implementation, and automated numerical and regression checks. The implemented environment provided multiformat data access, stream-from-disk review of multiday surveys, synchronized visualization, deterministic processing, and restorable sessions. A first usable environment was completed within weeks and subsequently used to implement and evaluate two interpretation workflows across multiple surveys. For injection surveillance, channel-coherence processing, masked ridge extraction, and engineering quality control converted recurring low-frequency DAS responses into a common-frame thermal-slug trajectory library. For gas lift surveillance, operating-state DTS traces were combined with a dimensionless dual-band DAS coincidence field and reviewed with completion geometry, surface measurements, and event history. The workflows derive interpretive confidence from recurrence across events and concurrence across measurements, respectively. The results establish the feasibility of locating governed software implementation near domain expertise. Individual engineers and small technical teams can thereby retain tested methods within a shared technical foundation, shortening the cycle from field observation to reproducible operational workflow from many months to a few days.

title: Reinventing the Upstream Control Room: An Agentic AI Approach to Early Deviation Detection and Remediation
container-title: ADIPEC
814f64384a16578a8104462a5d301e3b7903e939.abstract: Abstract The upstream control room is where production, injection, chemical, and emissions performance are monitored against target, and where operational deviations must be detected and resolved before they compound into lost output, avoidable emissions, or safety exposure. In practice, this task is hindered by four recurring gaps observed across production operations: no automated system alerts operators to an emerging shortfall before it has already grown; shortfalls are not always reconciled consistently across the control room, well- performance, and subsurface teams; compensation to recover a shortfall is often arranged ad hoc through informal communication, bypassing structured, formal validation and slowing recovery; and diagnosing the cause of a shortfall still depends on individual operator experience and a manual search through troubleshooting documentation. Left unaddressed, these gaps translate directly into slower recovery, inconsistent decisions across shifts, and lost production, chemical, and energy value. This paper presents the design, implementation, and early learnings of a Next-Generation Central Control Room (NextGen CCR), an artificial-intelligence-native decision-support layer deployed in an offshore upstream pilot to enable early operational-drift detection and structured remediation while preserving human decision authority. The solution combines near-real-time operational data, optimized operating envelopes, planned-activity context, and several thousand pages of procedural knowledge within a layered architecture that integrates deterministic analytics, large language models, and an operational knowledge graph. Deviations are detected against targets and envelopes, contextualized against planned activities and equipment status, and investigated by orchestrated, domain-specific agents that produce ranked, evidence-backed diagnoses and prioritized, standards-compliant recommendations. A scoped conversational assistant offers deeper guidance grounded in operating philosophies and equipment manuals, and human validation is embedded throughout the workflow. Early pilot results show improved end-of-day production prediction and faster, evidence-based investigation of critical alarms, with change management recognized as central to sustained adoption.

title: Edge AI-Enabled Autonomous Well Testing with Hybrid Virtual Flow Metering for Production Surveillance
container-title: ADIPEC
45303c509f31289d89fc7070f5b221238703c72a.abstract: Abstract Production surveillance is fundamental to sustaining reservoir performance, optimizing production, and enabling informed operational decision-making across large upstream assets. Conventional well-testing programs, however, remain highly dependent on manual initiation, operator experience, continuous monitoring, and post-test validation, resulting in inconsistent data quality, low test-success rates, and inefficient use of scarce testing infrastructure such as multiphase flow meters and test separators. This paper presents the development and phased field deployment of an Edge Artificial-Intelligence (AI) enabled Autonomous Well Testing framework integrated with Hybrid Virtual Flow Metering (VFM) for production surveillance in one of the world's largest onshore oil-producing assets. The solution combines machine learning, real-time edge analytics, operational-technology (OT) integration, and automated decision support to improve well-test execution, quality assurance, and production-data reliability while progressively reducing manual intervention. The framework continuously evaluates well readiness, operating stability, and test-quality conditions using both real-time and historical production data. It supports assisted, semi-autonomous, and fully autonomous testing modes, and dynamically determines whether a test should continue, be extended, be shortened, or be aborted. Automated failure diagnostics, keyed to pre-agreed rejection criteria, provide the operator with the probable cause of failure and a recommended corrective action, improving transparency and accelerating decision-making. In parallel, a hybrid virtual flow metering model estimates well production from routinely available surface measurements and is automatically recalibrated whenever a validated physical test becomes available, targeting an accuracy within 5% of the reference multiphase meter. A proof-of-concept was implemented on a representative well-gathering platform and subsequently scaled. Field results demonstrated a 50% reduction in failed well tests, an approximately threefold increase in testing throughput, test-duration reductions to under 24 hours for stable wells, and approximately 200 operational hours saved per month through early termination of non-productive tests. AI prediction accuracy approached 85% against reference measurements, and the hybrid VFM enabled a 10–15% reduction in physical testing frequency while maintaining surveillance coverage. The results demonstrate that autonomous well testing is technically feasible, operationally beneficial, and scalable across large upstream assets. The paper details the architecture, AI methodology, stability-assessment logic, VFM calibration approach, OT-cybersecurity considerations, quantified results, and a roadmap toward closed-loop autonomous field operations.

title: Active Learning-Assisted Human-In-The-Loop Framework for Rapid Borehole Image Annotation: Enabling AI-Powered Geological Interpretation at Scale
container-title: ADIPEC
a2d9600cc9e2691000ceac0374ce127fe222b9f4.abstract: Abstract Borehole image interpretation is a cornerstone of subsurface characterization in the oil and gas industry, providing high-resolution, azimuthally oriented data for in-situ stress estimation, wellbore stability assessment, and reservoir quality evaluation. Despite its geological significance, this process remains largely manual: expert geologists must individually review and annotate high-resolution image logs that can span thousands of feet per well, investing hundreds of hours per project before any automated prediction is available.
