Methods, Procedures, Process X-ray fluorescence (XRF) geochemistry on cuttings is encoded through a multilayer perceptron; cuttings photographs through a ResNet-18 network; and drilling parameters (rate of penetration, weight on bit, rotary speed, and torque), together with total mud-gas records (component chromatography was not consistently available), through a one-dimensional convolutional neural network, alongside a depth/formation covariate branch. Late fusion concatenates the three sensor encoders into a 448-dimensional representation feeding a shared multi-task regression head that predicts DT, RHOB, and NPHI, with GR retained as an auxiliary training target; measured MWD GR is used for final curve-set assembly. Target-specific diagnostic heads were also evaluated; the headline DT result uses the target-specific DT ensemble. Modality dropout supports inference under missing streams. Training and evaluation use 17 Utsira High wells (14 training, 3 held-out blind-test wells) from Norwegian Offshore Directorate/DISKOS data. Results, Observations, Conclusions On Well 16/1-14, adding XRF to drilling features raised within-well DT R2 from 0.59 to 0.98 and cut RMSE from 9.0 to 2.2 µs/ft, identifying XRF as the dominant single-modality contributor in that benchmark. The feature-based multi-well model, trained on 14 wells, achieved R2 = 0.93 (RMSE = 9.97 µs/ft) on blind well 16/1-18. The within-well RHOB benchmark reached R2 = 0.96 (RMSE = 0.028 g/cm3), best of five models. The completed evaluation extends these benchmarks: blind three-well fusion DT reached R2 = 0.858 (RMSE = 11.1 µs/ft), statistically exceeding XRF-only and the equivalent feature-based model (95% confidence intervals excluding zero). RHOB interval backfill reached R2 = 0.646 versus 0.478 for the geological baseline and approximately 0.30 over interpolation. NPHI achieved moderate interval-backfill R2 but did not significantly outperform interpolation and did not transfer reliably across wells; measured MWD GR remained the more reliable final GR source. For preliminary CCS screening, reconstructed DT and RHOB—and, where locally validated, NPHI—together with measured GR could provide formation-evaluation inputs relevant to injectivity, storage-capacity, and seal-integrity assessment in unlogged intervals. Novel/Additive Information The contribution integrates four surface-acquired modalities—XRF cuttings geochemistry, cuttings imagery, drilling parameters, and total mud-gas records—in a late-fusion, multi-task neural model targeting the quad-combo suite. Unlike conventional missing-log workflows that use other logs as predictors, the framework does not require other wireline curves as inputs and can operate where target-log coverage is absent, provided depth/formation context and the surface modalities are available. The completed evaluation demonstrates blind-well DT transfer, RHOB interval backfill, and missing-stream operation, supporting a transparent progression toward deployable quad-combo formation evaluation in legacy, unlogged, or LWD-degraded intervals.

title: AI-Augmented SIL Engineering: Transforming Safety Integrity Level Assessments in Oil and Gas
container-title: ADIPEC
9f0329832aeb1cd6f77781d6f18f296804964855.abstract: Abstract Safety Integrity Level assessment is one of the most specialised and resource-intensive activities in oil and gas engineering. It covers SIL determination through Layer of Protection Analysis, SIL verification through probability of failure calculations, and the documentation needed to satisfy IEC 61511 and company functional safety requirements. In a typical mid-size processing facility, a SIL review can take 6 to 8 weeks, involve 5 to 6 engineers, and require 700 to 1,000 man-hours at an estimated cost of USD 100,000 to USD 150,000. With larger project portfolios and a limited pool of certified functional safety specialists, this traditional approach is becoming difficult to sustain. This paper presents a practical framework for applying artificial intelligence to the preparation, consistency checking and workflow integration parts of SIL engineering while keeping qualified engineers and approved IEC 61511-compliant SIL software as the controlling elements of the calculation process. The proposed AI layer extracts SIF data from project documents, prepares LOPA inputs, checks data consistency, structures assumptions, and interfaces with company-approved IEC 61511-compliant SIL software. The AI layer does not replace these calculation engines. PFDavg, Risk Reduction Factor, architectural constraint and achieved SIL calculations remain within authorised SIL software and are reviewed by competent functional safety personnel. Based on workflow analysis and benchmarking against conventional SIL review practices, the expected benefits include reducing review duration from 6-8 weeks to 2-3 weeks, reducing effort from 700-1,000 man-hours to approximately 350-500 man-hours, and reducing review cost by approximately 50%. These figures are preliminary validation targets derived from workflow analysis. They are not results from a completed pilot and must be confirmed through a controlled pilot before being used as performance claims. The paper also discusses limitations, including incomplete input data, unusual failure modes, software integration boundaries, plant-specific conditions and the need for independent human verification before use.

title: Autonomous LNG Plant Startup Pre-Cooldown: Scaling Secure AI Closed-Loop Automation for Enhanced Production and Carbon Emission Reduction
container-title: ADIPEC
430a33c429116024daa9f813702561b4bf1c2eba.abstract: Abstract The objective of this work is to demonstrate the successful deployment of a secure, AI-driven closed-loop automation system for LNG plant pre-cooldown. The scope encompasses the transition from a data-driven advisory model to a fully autonomous system that executes real-time valve adjustments. It focuses on achieving critical outcomes in enabling autonomous, real-time adjustments through AI-driven recommendations, minimizing startup duration variability, maximizing additional production hours and reducing greenhouse gas emissions through optimized thermodynamic control. The methodology utilized twenty-five years of historical startup data, which was cleaned and profiled to train supervised machine learning models that predict Main Cryogenic Heat Exchanger (MCHE) temperature profiles and valve responses. These predictive models were integrated with an advanced optimization layer to define precise control sequences that satisfy safe operating envelopes. A cyber-resilient IT-OT architecture was engineered, employing network segmentation and protocol gateways to bridge the plant network and the AI engine securely. The process followed a phased validation: initial deployment as a "live advisory" to calibrate model accuracy, followed by the activation of a closed-loop controller that executes autonomous valve adjustments with human-in-the-loop safeguards. The system was successfully deployed across eight LNG train startups at Malaysia LNG plant. Quantitative results confirm a 16% average reduction in pre-cooldown duration compared to the live-advisory baseline. This acceleration directly translates into increased production availability and the reduction of operators' workloads, which allows operators to focus on strategic overview and process safety —enhancing both safety and efficiency. Observations revealed that the closed-loop implementation successfully standardized the pre-cooldown sequence across all eight production runs, delivering near-identical, optimized cooling trajectories. Critically, the tighter control of the Main Cryogenic Heat Exchanger (MCHE) cooling curve led to a 22% reduction in greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions by minimizing flaring events during the transition to stable operations. The study concludes that autonomous closed-loop systems are superior in achieving repeatable, high-efficiency startups. Furthermore, the integration of a secure IT-OT framework addresses the industry's primary barrier to AI adoption: cybersecurity in critical infrastructure. This paper provides a documented case study of an AI system moving beyond "recommendations" into "autonomous execution" in a critical energy facility. It introduces a novel, hybrid methodology combining Supervised Machine Learning with prescriptive optimization logic. This innovation highlights the transformative power of closed-loop, AI-driven automation, reinforcing the organization's leadership in operational excellence and its commitment to setting new standards for industrial processes.

title: From Fragmented Interpretations to an Automated Unified Full-Column Subsurface Framework: Enabling High-Fidelity Subsurface Model and Reliable Horizontal Well Placement, and Agentic AI–Driven Structural Quality Control
container-title: ADIPEC
6bb4ad23235fa2ea3d10f8955280c6cdb168c109.abstract: Abstract Mature carbonate assets with dense well control and stacked reservoir architecture commonly evolve through multiple generations of reservoir-specific structural interpretations. Although each local model may be technically valid within its own reservoir interval, the combination of fragmented interpretations across the full stratigraphic column can introduce structural aliasing, inconsistent fault geometries, horizon overlaps, vertical contradictions, and uncertainty propagation into field-development decisions. These inconsistencies have direct operational consequences: reduced confidence in horizontal well landing, greater uncertainty in target depth, repeated model rework, weaker linkage between static and dynamic models, and avoidable risk during drilling execution. (Salib et al. 2024). Traditional structural modeling methods struggle with time-consuming updates and imprecise well placements within reservoir models. In fact, they are nothing but workarounds to overcome the shortfalls of structure framework algorithms by introducing fake or dummy wells with fake well tops to constrain the structure, resulting in neglected models and potential financial losses and/or missed opportunities. It's crucial to overcome these obstacles for a more reliable reservoir modeling and well placement strategy in the subsurface industry. This paper presents an automated, unified full-column subsurface framework that integrates overburden, faults, horizons, formation tops, well trajectories, reservoir-specific interpretations, uncertainty propagation, and model-governance logic into a single authoritative structural model without using any dummy wells or well tops. The framework combines Bayesian-based Horizon Uncertainty Modeling, referred to in this work as COHIBA, Automated Structural Modeling (ASM), automated surface stacking, embedded validation rules, evergreen model-regeneration practices, and an Agentic AI Structural Quality Control (QC) Assistant. The AI assistant continuously reviews structural surfaces, verifies stratigraphic ordering, detects truncated surfaces, screens well-top mismatches, and provides explainable recommendations to geomodelers within a human-in-the-loop governance process. (Salib et al. 2024; Abrahamsen 2005; Abrahamsen and Benth 2001). Application of the workflow in a congested carbonate field-development setting demonstrated measurable improvements in structural integrity and model-governance efficiency. Automated surface stacking, validation, and reconciliation eliminated 15 identified cross-reservoir structural conflicts and horizon-stacking violations, resulting in a structurally consistent full-column framework. The Agentic AI QC Assistant evaluated 293 wells across 57 modeled reservoir zones within minutes, reducing structural quality-control effort by more than 95% compared with approximately one week of manual review per iteration. In addition, the AI-driven workflow identified and prioritized 25 well-top mismatches requiring expert review, enabling faster model updates, improved structural consistency, and increased confidence in horizontal well planning and multidisciplinary development decisions.

title: AI-Assisted Marine Logistics Digital Twin for Optimizing Dredger, Barge, and Support Vessel Coordination
container-title: ADIPEC
b09a80821043991c06e043a04fda032638702974.abstract: Abstract Marine construction projects may combine several material-transfer methods that must operate as one coordinated production system. In the studied configuration, a self-propelled hopper dredger transports material in its own hopper, a cutter suction dredger delivers slurry through a pipeline, and sand barges handle approximately 20% of the modeled sand volume. These operations also depend on tugboats, a multicat, a fuel barge, a survey boat, rock barges, receiving-area availability, and onshore equipment. Poor coordination between these resources can increase waiting time, interrupt production, and raise fuel consumption. This paper proposes an AI-assisted marine logistics digital twin that maintains an updated virtual representation of vessel status, dredging progress, pipeline condition, weather restrictions, support-resource availability, and island receiving capacity. The AI component consists of two supervised XGBoost models trained, validated, and tested using a physics-informed synthetic dataset developed within published equipment operating ranges and explicit engineering assumptions. A regression model predicts hopper-dredger cycle duration and discharge waiting, while a classification model estimates the probability of a pipeline interruption during the following operating period. These predictions are incorporated into a rolling-horizon decision method that evaluates discharge timing, vessel assignments, sailing speeds, pipeline operating conditions, and support-service windows as the operational state changes. The framework was evaluated through a representative 14-day island-reclamation scenario using paired simulations of predefined rule-based and ML-assisted rolling-horizon coordination. The ML-assisted strategy increased modeled placed sand by approximately 6%, reduced mean hopper-dredger discharge waiting by approximately 83%, and lowered fuel intensity by approximately 10%. It also reduced CSD and pipeline downtime and improved the reliability of meeting the daily production target. These values are simulation-based proof-of-concept results generated under defined engineering assumptions and should be interpreted as a validation pathway for future project-data deployment rather than as measured field performance. The results show that the main value of the digital twin lies in using ML predictions to coordinate dredging, transport, pipeline, support, and receiving activities as one connected operation rather than optimizing individual assets separately.

title: From Broker Calls to Autonomous Chartering: How AI and Real-Time Market Intelligence are Reshaping Offshore Vessel Logistics
container-title: ADIPEC
df6a5f2e9db916cc0ed56d54fcca63a7da33ffa8.abstract: Abstract This paper explores how AI-powered vessel intelligence platforms and agentic systems are reshaping the way offshore energy operators and project managers identify, evaluate and engage with vessel owners. The objective is to demonstrate how consolidating real-time AIS tracking, vessel specifications, market availability and owner contact workflows into a single platform compresses the vessel sourcing cycle and reduces operational uncertainty in offshore logistics planning. The paper draws on the development and deployment of an offshore vessel intelligence platform aggregating data from 30,000+ vessels across 25+ countries, covering vessel specifications, live AIS positioning, ownership data and market availability signals. The methodology documents how agentic AI layers applied to this dataset enable project teams to move from initial vessel search to direct owner engagement within minutes rather than days. Case studies from European offshore wind and EPCI markets illustrate how consolidated market intelligence replaces fragmented, network-dependent sourcing processes with structured, data-driven workflows accessible to any operator regardless of existing broker relationships. The platform approach demonstrates measurable improvements across three dimensions of offshore vessel sourcing. Vessel identification cycles, traditionally dependent on broker networks and manual market canvassing, are reduced from days to minutes when real-time availability, technical specifications and ownership data are consolidated in a single searchable environment. Agentic AI systems enable operators to initiate contact with relevant vessel owners and receive preliminary availability confirmation within the same session, eliminating the sequential delays inherent to conventional brokerage. At the market intelligence level, aggregated fixture data and fleet movement analytics provide project teams with pricing benchmarks and availability forecasts previously accessible only to established brokers. These capabilities are particularly relevant for Gulf-based operators managing complex multi-vessel EPCI campaigns, where sourcing speed and market transparency directly impact project schedules and cost outcomes. This paper presents the first structured analysis of agentic AI applied specifically to offshore vessel sourcing workflows, demonstrating how real-time vessel intelligence and accelerated owner engagement compress commercial timelines without reliance on traditional brokerage intermediaries. This addresses a documented gap in digital transformation literature for offshore marine logistics.

title: Bridging Reservoir Characterization and Production Performance Using AI-Driven Permeability in Carbonate Systems
container-title: ADIPEC
51a7cca7fa82602602a570aa0d40792288b6b0c3.abstract: Abstract This paper presents field-based examples from structurally complex Cretaceous carbonate reservoirs in an onshore Abu Dhabi marginal field, illustrating how AI-enabled borehole image interpretation can deliver value beyond interpretation speed and automation. The study aims to demonstrate that high-resolution, AI-derived permeability provides a more realistic representation of reservoir flow capacity than conventional petrophysical permeability. By exhibiting stronger agreement with measured production and injection responses, the AI-derived permeability output offers a more reliable input for dynamic reservoir modelling, production forecasting, and history matching. The workflow combines borehole image logs with triple-combo data, drilling and mud logs, core information, and dynamic datasets from horizontal wells completed in heterogeneous, structurally complex Cretaceous carbonate intervals. Deep learning and computer vision techniques are used to segment borehole images, characterize diagenetic heterogeneity, detect fractures and faults, and generate a continuous, high-resolution permeability index. Finite element modelling and Darcy-based simulation are then applied to translate image-derived heterogeneity into permeability behaviour. The resulting AI-derived rock-property outputs are integrated with production and injection performance data to evaluate their applicability in completion design, flow interpretation, and reservoir modelling workflows. The case examples indicate that the higher-resolution AI-derived permeability index demonstrates a stronger and more consistent relationship with actual production and injection behaviour than conventional petrophysical permeability, which typically follows porosity trends and tends to average out fine-scale reservoir heterogeneity. Its positive correlation with PLT and injectivity profiles confirms its relevance as a more representative indicator of effective flow contribution. From a reservoir engineering standpoint, improved permeability definition is fundamental because dynamic models are highly sensitive to the spatial distribution of flow capacity. A high-resolution and geologically consistent permeability input reduces uncertainty, strengthens the physical basis for model calibration, and provides a more robust foundation for production forecasting and history matching compared with conventional lower-resolution permeability logs. The AI-derived permeability product also supports enhanced completion segmentation, stimulation planning, and water-control strategy by resolving heterogeneity that may otherwise remain obscured in conventional interpretations. In parallel, the workflow shortens interpretation turnaround from days or weeks to hours, enabling faster and better-informed decisions in structurally complex marginal-field developments. Overall, this study presents a field-validated AI-driven workflow that establishes a direct link between high-resolution, image-based permeability estimation and observed production performance in structurally complex carbonate reservoirs. The approach moves beyond conventional interpretation by capturing fine-scale geological heterogeneity and integrating it with dynamic flow response. The resulting permeability output offers a scalable and more dependable input for production forecasting, history matching, and reservoir development planning, representing an important advancement in the characterization and management of marginal carbonate fields.

title: First Global Deployment of a Closed-Loop AI Drilling Optimizer Integrated with Rig Control Systems
container-title: ADIPEC
936f251409ba4e437d9b0337f77a1efe7819a334.abstract: Abstract The rapid advancement of drilling automation is accelerating the industry's transition toward autonomous drilling systems capable of continuously optimizing performance with minimal operator intervention. AI-based drilling optimization has already demonstrated measurable improvements in drilling efficiency through closed-loop control. However, successful deployment still depends on reliable integration with rig control systems. Variations in control architecture, communication protocols, cybersecurity requirements, and operating philosophy across equipment manufacturers remain significant barriers to implementation across global drilling fleets. To the authors' knowledge, this paper presents the first documented integration of an AI Drilling Optimizer with a Chinese rig control system, enabling fully closed-loop optimization of drilling parameters while preserving the rig's existing control philosophy and equipment safety systems. The project demonstrates how a modular integration architecture can connect two independent control environments without fundamentally modifying either the optimization software or the underlying drilling control logic. The integration architecture used a layered communication framework that separates optimization algorithms from control system interfaces. Real-time drilling measurements were acquired from the rig control network and processed by the AI optimization engine. The engine continuously evaluated drilling performance and generated optimized weight on bit (WOB) and rotary speed (RPM) setpoints. These recommendations were transmitted back to the rig control system through a secure communication interface. Command validation, operating limits, and existing safety interlocks remained under the authority of the rig control system. This approach allowed the optimizer to enhance drilling performance while ensuring the driller could immediately resume manual control whenever required. A structured engineering methodology was applied throughout the project, covering communication mapping, interface verification, simulator testing, hardware-in-the-loop validation, factory acceptance testing, site commissioning, and phased operational deployment. Particular emphasis was placed on: deterministic communications;clear transfer of control ownership between automation systems and the driller;fail-safe behavior during communication loss; andverification that automated commands could not exceed predefined operational limits. Field deployment demonstrated stable closed-loop operation during drilling activities. The optimizer continuously adapted drilling parameters to changing downhole conditions, while the rig control system retained full authority over equipment protection and operational safety. The implementation confirmed that differences in controller architecture, software organization, and human-machine interface (HMI) design can be accommodated through standardized communication interfaces without compromising system reliability or operator confidence. The project establishes a repeatable methodology for integrating AI-based drilling optimization with heterogeneous rig control systems and represents an important milestone toward vendor independent autonomous drilling. The engineering lessons presented provide practical guidance for future cross platform automation projects and support ongoing industry efforts to improve interoperability between drilling automation applications and rig control systems.

title: Predictive Analytics for Reliability-Centered Maintenance: Leveraging AI for Optimization
container-title: ADIPEC
2a46968d34eb09e23ae80747d6503cd8dae3734f.abstract: Abstract This study introduces a next-generation AI-driven framework that transforms Reliability-Centered Maintenance (RCM) from static, time-based scheduling into a dynamic, risk-optimized decision system. In industrial environments, limited failure history often forces conservative preventive maintenance (PM), resulting in inefficiencies—simultaneously over-maintaining healthy components while failing to prevent critical breakdowns. This work addresses that structural gap by deploying an agentic AI architecture that continuously fuses condition monitoring, probabilistic risk analytics, and degradation forecasting into a closed-loop optimization workflow. The objective is to enable real-time, failure-mode–specific PM decisions that balance reliability, cost, and operational constraints—delivering a step-change from periodic maintenance to adaptive, evidence-based execution. The framework integrates three autonomous layers: (1) data source and data conditioning, (2) AI-driven health scoring and prioritization, and (3) probabilistic forecasting and cost-optimized interval. Multi-source data—including PI historian streams, vibration signatures, lubricant analysis, and asset criticality—are harmonized and filtered to isolate true degradation signals. For each failure mode, an AI agent computes a normalized health score (0–100) based on degradation severity, persistence, trend dynamics, and data confidence. Failure modes breaching risk thresholds are escalated to specialized sub-agents that generate ensemble degradation forecasts (linear, polynomial, exponential), producing probabilistic remaining useful life (RUL) estimates (P10/P50/P90). These are translated into time-to-failure distributions and fitted using Weibull modeling, where β characterizes failure behavior and η defines characteristic life. The framework has been deployed to GE LM2500+G4 compressor package which is a gas turbine compressor package locating on Offshore Processing facility in the Gulf of Thailand. Results reveal a critical insight: nearly 57% of modeled failure modes exhibited non-aging (β &lt; 1) behavior, indicating that traditional PM is inherently ineffective for these mechanisms. These modes were reclassified to run-to-failure or extended intervals, eliminating unnecessary maintenance. For aging-related modes (β &gt; 1), optimization delivered substantial value. PM intervals were extended beyond the standard 8,000-hour cycle, with a representative wear-out case (β ≈ 5.4) achieving an optimal interval of ~18,300 hours—more than 2× extension without increased risk. Cost-risk curves clearly demonstrate the nonlinear trade-off between excessive maintenance and escalating failure probability, while sensitivity analysis highlights that interval decisions can vary by &gt;30% depending on cost assumptions—reinforcing the importance of economic calibration.

title: AI-Driven Well Reactivation in Mature Omani Fields: Part I – Candidate Selection and Workflow Architecture
container-title: ADIPEC
c03b62d00e9da9bab74492b49c8996aa2b800817.abstract: Abstract Under current market conditions, operators are compelled to minimize capital expenditure on new drilling projects. However, production decline in mature assets necessitates effective strategies to sustain output and optimize recovery. Conventional approaches such as drilling infill wells are cost-prohibitive, driving the need for alternative solutions. Reactivating shut-in wells has emerged as a practical method to restore production without significant additional investment. The challenge lies in scale: with a large inventory of inactive wells, manual candidate screening is labor-intensive, prone to subjectivity, and time-consuming. To address this, an AI-driven candidate selection methodology has been developed to automate the evaluation process. The automated workflow leverages an AI-powered decision support system while preserving the rigor of standard evaluation methodologies. Unlike traditional manual and well-centric approaches, this AI-driven process automates candidate screening and assesses shut-in well potential from a broader, field-level perspective. This transformation enables faster, more consistent decision-making and significantly reduces the time and resources required for analysis. The workflow incorporates advanced analytical techniques to deliver comprehensive evaluations. Logistic regression is applied for pattern classification, such as Chan and Hall Plot diagnostics, followed by trend detection for heterogeneity analysis. Time-series forecasting automates decline curve analysis, including outlier filtering, event-based segmentation, and weighted curve fitting. Neural networks and random forest models evaluate behind-casing opportunities, while Bayesian networks estimate intervention success probabilities. Finally, multi-criteria decision-making algorithms rank opportunities based on technical and economic parameters. The system consolidates data from multiple sources—including production history and well information—into a unified dataset for automated processing and visualization. The workflow successfully evaluated nearly one hundred wells in Area-1, operated by MEDCO LLC Oman, a mature asset within the Sultanate of Oman. The system identified multiple candidates for interventions such as stimulation, water shut-off, reperforation, and hydraulic fracturing, while also flagging underperforming wells for further review. Economic analysis incorporated both pre- and post-intervention forecasts, along with key financial parameters including intervention costs, discount rates, inflation, and operational expenses. These inputs were used to calculate incremental oil production and project Net Present Value (NPV), forming the basis for systematic prioritization of opportunities. This paper introduces a fully automated workflow for well reactivation and prioritization in mature fields. It also highlights the challenges encountered during data QA/QC and shares lessons learned in automating data capture from existing operator systems. While additional details on intervention recommendations using the Intervention Advisor module will be presented in future publications, the methodology outlined here provides a practical roadmap for operators aiming to optimize production by systematically selecting shut-in well candidates and automating the evaluation process.

title: AI-Optimized Offshore Supply Vessel Operations for Fuel Efficiency, Emissions Reduction, and Operational Sustainability
container-title: ADIPEC
c913a00bef757ab191068df68edc5475e89a525d.abstract: Abstract This paper investigates the application of AI-driven optimisation to offshore supply vessel (OSV) operations in order to reduce fuel consumption, minimise emissions, and improve logistical efficiency in offshore oil and gas activities. The objective is to develop an intelligent operational framework capable of dynamically optimising vessel routing, speed profiles, and load distribution based on real-time environmental and operational conditions. An integrated optimisation framework was developed using operational vessel data, meteorological conditions, wave parameters, fuel consumption profiles, and offshore scheduling requirements. Machine learning and predictive routing algorithms were applied to continuously evaluate optimal navigation paths, vessel speeds, and cargo allocation strategies under varying offshore conditions. A real-time optimisation model was designed to dynamically respond to weather fluctuations, operational delays, and changing supply demands. Simulation studies were conducted using representative offshore logistics scenarios to evaluate fuel efficiency, emissions reduction, voyage reliability, and operational responsiveness. Comparative benchmarking was performed against conventional fixed-route offshore supply operations. Simulation studies indicate that the proposed AI-optimised framework has the potential to reduce offshore vessel fuel consumption by approximately 16% compared to conventional operations. These results, while promising, are derived from discrete-event simulation and require validation through real-world deployment. The framework demonstrates pathway viability for achieving measurable efficiency gains, with simulation suggesting proportional CO2 emissions reductions and improved voyage scheduling performance. Dynamic route optimisation enabled vessels to avoid high-resistance sea conditions, reducing unnecessary engine loading and improving overall energy efficiency. Adaptive speed control further contributed to fuel savings while maintaining operational delivery requirements.The system also demonstrated improved responsiveness to operational disruptions, including weather-related delays and fluctuating offshore demand schedules. AI-assisted cargo allocation reduced inefficient load distribution and minimised unnecessary vessel movements between offshore facilities. Comparative analysis indicates that the proposed framework outperforms traditional fixed-routing strategies in both environmental and operational performance metrics.In addition to reducing operating costs, the framework supports offshore sustainability objectives by lowering fuel usage and enhancing logistical coordination across offshore assets. The findings demonstrate strong potential for integrating AI-driven optimisation into offshore marine operations as part of broader digital transformation and decarbonization initiatives within the upstream energy sector. This work introduces a real-time, AI-assisted optimisation framework specifically designed for offshore supply vessel operations in the upstream sector. Unlike conventional marine logistics approaches based on static routing and scheduling, the proposed system integrates environmental data, operational demand, and predictive optimisation to simultaneously enhance fuel efficiency, reduce emissions, and improve offshore logistical performance within a scalable digital operations framework.

title: Beyond the Fracture: AI-Driven Subsurface Analytics Solve a Shallow-Aquifer Fluid-Invasion Mystery, Onshore Abu Dhabi
container-title: ADIPEC
7057e6d7bb6ca5f454f36cd4e898e5a2e060c6f4.abstract: Abstract Drilling through the shallow Dammam, Umm Er Radhuma and Simsima aquifer complex in a giant onshore Abu Dhabi field presents challenges due to the limited understanding of these water-bearing intervals. In one cluster, a dark, solids-laden fluid surfaced from a water-supply well following drilling activity at a nearby offset well. The well was idled, and the injection cluster it supplied had to be taken offline, which reduced the field water-injection capacity. The study aimed to identify the root cause of the fluid invasion, characterize the structural, sedimentological and geomechanical heterogeneity of the shallow aquifer, and optimize drilling practices in future wells. A multidisciplinary, AI-assisted workflow was utilized, with 3D seismic as the spatial framework. Gradient Coherence Cube (GCC) and spectral decomposition attributes, co-rendered on Relative Geological Time (RGT) slices, were employed to detect structure below conventional seismic resolution. An automated, depth-matched correlation engine was then used to compare 113 time-indexed mud-loss events against borehole-image (BHI) interpretations of fractures, conductive seams and bedding. Rock-physics templates, wireline pressures and aquifer fluid samples were integrated to test the competing invasion mechanisms. The analysis showed that 57% of the losses fell outside the imaged interval and only eight lay within 25 ft of an interpreted fracture, while the most severe losses were the least fracture associated. Loss severity therefore did not track fracture density. Instead, a friable shale at the boundary between the Umm Er Radhuma basal shale and the Simsima, identified in cores and on rock-physics templates, was found to be geomechanically weak. Fluid samples showed high total suspended solids that decreased with flushing, and localized aquifer-pressure depletion indicated a lateral gradient towards the affected wells. The integrated diagnosis attributes the incident to drilling-induced wellbore breakout in the friable shale rather than natural-fracture leakage and redirects mitigation towards managed drilling parameters and mud-window optimization.

title: AI-Powered Smart Port Operations: A Digital Transformation Roadmap for Marine Safety, Efficiency, and Compliance
container-title: ADIPEC
c7569faf5c20f7f2f31559ae303fa236ab236848.abstract: Abstract Marine jetty and port operations within onshore oil-field environments require continuous safety compliance, controlled access, reliable vessel visibility, asset availability, environmental awareness, and disciplined response to abnormal conditions. Manual supervision remains essential, but it can be limited when activities are distributed across jetties, gates, contractor areas, mooring zones, navigation channels, and control-room interfaces. This paper presents an AI-powered Smart Port Operations roadmap for ADNOC Onshore NEB Marine Operations. The roadmap expands the immediate smart-gate, AI CCTV, and Marine Control Room concept into a full digital ecosystem that integrates people, processes, infrastructure, vessels, and data. The model includes vessel traffic information, berth and jetty management, smart gate access, digital permit-to-work, predictive maintenance, smart navigation aids, drone inspections, smart dredging management, environmental monitoring, digital marine logistics, AI-based analytics, smart security, and a live digital twin. The paper describes the current operational challenge, the transformation framework, the fourteen initiatives, the technical application of priority systems, governance requirements, implementation assurance, limitations, and a phased five-year roadmap. It also aligns the concept with recognized maritime guidance, including IMO e-navigation principles, ISPS security objectives, IALA navigation-aid guidance, and port sustainability themes. The main conclusion is that smart-port value is created when surveillance, access control, asset monitoring, vessel traffic data, dashboards, alerts, and response workflows operate as one integrated management system. AI and automation should assist authorized personnel, improve consistency, and increase the quality of evidence, while accountable marine decision-making remains with trained operators and supervisors. The proposed roadmap therefore provides a practical path toward safer, more efficient, more resilient, and more sustainable marine operations at NEB.

title: AI Reservoir Characterization in Geologically Complex Fields
container-title: ADIPEC
e0a270840325907ed5c42c82b4d7e144658c4934.abstract: Abstract Reservoir characterization in structurally and stratigraphically complex settings is often limited by the turnaround time and assumptions of conventional seismic inversion. Low-frequency model construction, wavelet estimation, phase uncertainty, and smoothing can materially influence the resulting elastic volumes, particularly where reservoir intervals are thin or laterally variable. This study evaluates a stratigraphy-guided artificial intelligence workflow for estimating elastic and petrophysical properties in the Poseidon field of the Browse Basin, offshore northwestern Australia. The workflow combines migrated 3D seismic data, well logs, interpreted horizons, stratigraphic units, and Relative Geologic Time within a temporal convolutional network. Acoustic impedance, porosity, and gamma ray were modeled, with acoustic impedance used for the principal quantitative comparison. Generalization was assessed by withholding wells from training and validation, and the predictions were compared with published simultaneous-inversion and other benchmark results from the same field. Across the evaluated wells, acoustic-impedance correlations exceeded 90% on average, while blind-well correlations were above 80%. The corresponding published simultaneous-inversion benchmark reported average correlations of approximately 60%. Adding stratigraphic context improved the blind Poseidon-1 correlation from approximately 70% to 81% and reduced mean absolute percentage error from approximately 10% to 5%. The predicted volumes delineated low-impedance intervals in the Plover Formation and preserved greater vertical detail than the comparison inversion. The results show that stratigraphic constraints can improve the accuracy and geological coherence of AI and data-driven property estimation. The approach is complementary to physics-based inversion and provides a rapid method for testing reservoir interpretations where conventional assumptions are uncertain.

title: Agentic AI in the Air-Gap: Hybrid ML and LLM Reconciliation of Combined-Frequency Drilling KPIs at ADNOC Offshore
container-title: ADIPEC
35406c918641afd0db00bdf95315e507450edf50.abstract: Abstract Invisible lost time, or ILT, is the gap between the time an operation actually consumes and the technical limit it could reach under ideal conditions. Earlier work showed that pairing low-frequency daily drilling reports with high-frequency rig-sensor data brings sub-activity contributors to ILT into view — contributors that daily reporting on its own keeps hidden (Landaeta Rivas et al. 2022). What that approach did not solve was the reconciliation itself. Aligning parallel descriptions of the same operation — sensor-derived rig states, coded daily reports, the planned well timeline, and technical-limit benchmarks — stayed a manual exercise, inconsistent in its definitions and heavy on engineering time. This paper describes a way to bridge that gap by using a hybrid setup. Deterministic machine-learning classifiers turn high-frequency surface-sensor streams into rig-state sequences, and large-language-model reasoning agents; then harmonize those states with low-frequency activity codes, the planned operations, and technical-limit benchmarks, producing a single operational timeline in which every interval carries its provenance. The whole system runs inside an air-gapped operator tenant, within the data-residency and cybersecurity limits in compliance with national and offshore operators' framework. The design is additive where the low-frequency report stays the auditable record, high-frequency data sharpens resolution wherever the instrumentation supports it, and the agentic layer reasons across the sources while every published figure passes a human-review gate. We evaluated the framework in a pilot spanning five wells and two rigs in an offshore field during 2026. The paper is candid about where the agentic layer over-flagged, where a reviewer had to override it, and where it added nothing. Its contribution is twofold: a reproducible way to deploy reasoning agents under air-gap constraints, and an extension of the combined-frequency ILT principle toward supervised, near-real-time performance diagnosis. Closed-loop autonomous optimization is left explicitly to future work.

title: From Barrier Assurance to Cumulative Risk: A Knowledge Graph-Based AI Framework for Major Accident Hazard Risk Management
container-title: ADIPEC
8a4581877e5a38c5b0eae6f83353593dd4296027.abstract: Abstract Major Accident Hazard (MAH) risk in oil and gas assets rarely arises from the failure of a single component, equipment item or barrier. Instead, risk emerges cumulatively when maintenance deferrals, operational constraints, inspection findings, integrity anomalies, temporary repairs and project activities interact with degraded asset conditions and weakened safety barriers across complex systems (Reason, 1997, Kletz, 2009). Conventional work prioritization methods typically evaluate these activities using static, discipline-specific or equipment-level criteria. Although effective for local decision-making, such methods can obscure the aggregate effect of multiple individually tolerable impairments on a shared MAH scenario. Prior work at a GCC onshore COMAH site demonstrated that artificial intelligence (AI), retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) and large language models (LLMs) can automate identification and verification of Safety Critical Elements (SCEs), generate performance standards, verify assurance tasks in the computerized maintenance management system (CMMS), and reduce engineering effort by more than 90% (Stewart et al., 2025). This paper extends that framework from static barrier assurance to dynamic cumulative risk prioritization. The proposed method combines a Semantic Asset Knowledge Graph with a GraphRAG retrieval layer (Edge et al., 2024) and an agentic AI risk reasoning engine. Structured asset, maintenance, integrity and operational datasets are integrated with unstructured safety cases, bow tie studies, performance standards, inspection reports and maintenance data. These datasets are normalized and linked to represent physical, functional, safety-critical and causal dependencies between equipment, barriers, protection layers and MAH escalation pathways. The architecture enables specialised AI agents to identify affected barriers, assess degradation states, detect common dependencies, evaluate escalation pathways and rank competing work. In the current implementation, barrier mapping and cumulative risk clustering were demonstrated, with additional agent capabilities defined for future deployment. Application of the method demonstrated improved visibility of cumulative risk clusters and demonstrated the use of graph-based reasoning to support MAH-focused prioritisation. The system identified clusters of cumulative risk in which individually low-priority work items combined to create credible MAH precursors, consistent with the Swiss Cheese model of accident causation. The approach reduced manual engineering screening effort by approximately 40% and identified more than USD 100 million of production value at risk associated with suboptimal prioritization. The work demonstrates a practical and scalable method for moving from barrier assurance to dynamic, asset-level MAH risk management.

title: Validation-Gated Agentic AI for Comparative LDSM Shale-Reactivity Assessment and Drilling-Fluid Decision Support
container-title: ADIPEC
65a2e92a8ad94de8ea43cc6b28303a8bc0f2fd0f.abstract: Abstract Reactive shale can swell during contact with water-based drilling fluid, and the resulting LDSM curve is often used to compare models or support drilling decisions. However, many readings from one pellet are still one physical experiment, so a model can look accurate when it is only reconstructing points inside a known curve. This study developed a validation-gated agentic AI workflow and applied it to three source-controlled LDSM records from Talhar, Ranikot, and Khadro shales exposed to the same salt-polymer-glycol Mud A. Each record contained 41 ordered observations over 18 h from a 15 g pellet compacted at 6000 psi for 30 min. Four nonredundant response families and three tree regressors were evaluated. Complete-curve fitting, within-curve interpolation, prediction of the unseen remainder, and 0.5 to 4 h forecasts were tested as separate tasks. Final observed swelling was 4.35% for Talhar, 17.62% for Ranikot, and 5.70% for Khadro. Their average rates at 0.5 h were 6.63, 9.22, and 4.57%/h. Hyperbolic gave the lowest Talhar complete-curve MAE at 0.0750 percentage point, while Weibull gave the lowest Ranikot and Khadro MAEs at 0.0952 and 0.0436 percentage point. Linear interpolation produced lower leave-one-observation-out error than every tree model. The lowest chronological future-block error was still 5.7 to 32.2 times the corresponding interpolation error, showing that accurate reconstruction inside a known curve is not the same as future prediction. The rule-governed agent kept early rate, directly measured swelling, and endpoint-model agreement as separate evidence states. Ranikot reached a high-reactivity screening output at 0.5033 h, Talhar at 5 h, and Khadro reached an elevated-magnitude output at 1.85 h because its initial rate remained below the study-defined 5%/h gate. The workflow completed analytical screening for all three records and routed final fluid selection to matched comparative testing and engineering review. The main contribution is a simple and traceable workflow that separates curve description, interpolation, forecasting, screening, and engineering action.

title: Autonomous Wellbore Execution Monitoring and Predictive Derisking via AI-Driven Real-Time Anomaly Detection
container-title: ADIPEC
6ac2327a111b0becf94b7b6453b0827275d567a1.abstract: Abstract This study introduces an AI-powered autonomous agent designed to transform well execution from a reactive process to a proactive, data-driven operation. The objective is to continuously monitor drilling activities against planned baselines using real-time telemetry and historical data. By detecting early precursors to operational risks, the system aims to provide predictive alerts and decision support, significantly reducing Non-Productive Time (NPT) and improving overall wellbore quality. The methodology employs a three-module architecture. First, a Markov-based transition model was trained on over 60,000 Daily Drilling Reports (DDR) to establish activity dependencies and duration baselines. Second, an autonomous engine ingests real-time WITSML telemetry and narrative reports to detect rate-based and time-based deviations. Finally, a knowledge-augmented reasoning engine utilizes an Incident-Precursor Knowledge Graph, containing over 50 risk scenarios, to map detected anomalies to historical incident patterns and provide specific mitigation recommendations through a collaborative chat interface. Preliminary simulator validation demonstrates high performance, with activity forecast accuracy exceeding 95%. The deviation detection logic identified activity delays with precision ranging from 68% to 85%. Historical analysis confirmed that the system's precursor signatures effectively cover major incident types: stuck pipe (83%), total loss (89%), wellbore instability (83%), and equipment failures (88%). The study codifies a master list of approximately 330 unique activity-level KPIs, providing a statistically robust foundation for real-time monitoring. Conclusions indicate that precursor signals are often present in data hours before an event, and systematic pattern recognition can make these "invisible" signals actionable. While currently in the simulator phase, the roadmap includes pilot field deployments in late 2026. This shift toward autonomous monitoring allows operational teams to focus on high-consequence decision-making while delegating routine oversight to AI agents. This research introduces a unique combination of Markov-based sequential modeling and a structured Incident-Precursor Knowledge Graph. It moves beyond simple threshold alerts by implementing "memory-aware" reasoning, allowing engineers to interact with the AI agent to update well-specific assumptions. This approach codifies over 330 industry KPIs and 50 risk scenarios into a production-grade autonomous agent, bridging the gap between historical DDR analysis and real-time WITSML data streams.

title: The Human Factor: Safeguarding Oil & Gas Jobs in an AI Dominated Future
container-title: ADIPEC
b18814bbb54eb39a750ce94bb35a4222e38a5eab.abstract: Abstract Objectives/Scope This study investigates how Learning and Development (L&D) participation shapes employee resilience and reduces AI-related job anxiety within the oil and gas industry (O&G). The scope covers the transition from routine, automatable tasks to higher-value roles requiring human judgment. It examines how targeted upskilling and reskilling interventions can reduce employees' perceived threat of job loss across various organizational departments. Research Methodology Adopting a quantitative design, the study engaged participants from diverse professional backgrounds and organizational levels within the O&G industry (N = 30). Data was collected using a questionnaire comprising survey items adapted from previously validated instruments (Wang and Wang, 2019; Connor and Davidson, 2003), assessing AI-induced job loss anxiety, L&D participation, and employee resilience. Relationships between variables were tested using Pearson and Spearman correlation analysis. Results & Conclusions All four hypothesized relationships were in the expected direction. AI-related L&D was associated with lower job loss anxiety and higher employee resilience, while job loss anxiety was associated with lower resilience. The relationship between L&D and resilience was the strongest and most consistent finding, the L&D engagement measure, incorporating training hours and perceived training effectiveness, was significantly positively correlated with resilience (p = .388, p = .034), while a simpler binary participation measure showed a similar but non-significant pattern (r = .324, p = .081). L&D was also negatively associated with the Learning- specific subfactor of AI anxiety (p = -.301, p = .106), suggesting its effect may be concentrated on anxiety related to the learning process itself. The remaining associations did not reach statistical significance. These findings suggest a meaningful link between structured AI-related L&D and employees' psychological readiness for AI- driven change, though most results should be interpreted as preliminary given the sample size. The findings suggest that while AI adoption is essential for operational efficiency, its success may also depend on the workforce's psychological readiness and that unaddressed job-loss anxiety could contribute to employee withdrawal and reduced organizational commitment (Castro-Castaneda et al., 2023). The study suggests that strategic L&D investment may help employees view AI as a tool that enhances their work rather than threatens their jobs, potentially supporting productivity and retention in an increasingly automated industry. Research Gap While existing literature focuses heavily on the technical efficiency gains of AI, limited research has examined how AI-related L&D may influence employees' job-loss anxiety and resilience in the energy sector. This study addresses this gap and finds that all four hypothesized relationships were in the expected direction, with L&D significantly correlated with resilience (p = .388, p = .034). These findings offer preliminary evidence that structured L&D may support psychological readiness for AI-driven workforce change.

title: Generative AI for Integrity Anomaly Risk Assessment: A Human-In-The-Loop Approach to Probability and Consequence of Failure Characterization at Scale
container-title: ADIPEC
94b30d352190b51ef7f8a605dba518a0d0eb91b9.abstract: Abstract Integrity-management systems should connect anomaly findings to consistent assessment, prioritization and action. In practice, large populations of short, inconsistent and abbreviation-rich anomaly narratives and linked tasks can exceed the capacity available for prompt, consistent interpretation. The resulting data fog can obscure material integrity evidence and consume specialist effort in repetitive record handling. The objective is not to remove the engineer from integrity management. It is to give engineers a clearer population view, an auditable evidence trail and a more focused basis for applying professional judgment. This paper presents a human-in-the-loop architecture in which a large language model structures source-grounded evidence from anomaly narratives and linked task records. Controlled deterministic rules then assign ordinal Probability of Failure, calculate production-loss Economic Consequence of Failure, place each record on a risk matrix, determine evidence confidence and route records for proportionate human assurance. Traceability is maintained from the original wording through the extracted evidence, applied definitions and calculations to the resulting classification and review route. The proof of concept used a synthetic population of 5,000 anomaly records and associated tasks designed to represent common characteristics of integrity-management data, including short narratives, local terminology, missing information, ambiguous abbreviations and linked follow-up activities. A random sample of 100 anomalies and 207 associated tasks formed the completed dataset used to test the end-to-end architecture. Given the proof-of-concept scope, the study used a deliberately bounded set of engineering inputs and controlled assumptions. The asset context, terminology, production-loss assumptions, ordinal PoF mappings and five-band risk matrix were established using relevant engineering good practices and representative engineering requirements. The selected matrix defines Very Low, Low, Medium, High and Very High risk bands and was used consistently throughout the proof of concept. These inputs provided a transparent and reproducible basis for testing the architecture but are not presented as universal engineering rules. Each deployment requires the terminology, assumptions, category mappings, consequence criteria and risk-matrix definitions to be reviewed and approved against the organization's asset-specific requirements. The completed analysis classified 90 records as Very Low risk, five as Low, four as Medium and one as High, with no Very High records. A completed preliminary human comparison of 26 records produced exact agreement of 92% for PoF, 85% for Economic CoF and 85% for risk band, with quadratically weighted kappa values of 0.94, 0.82 and 0.83, respectively. Expansion to the full synthetic population and broader independent engineering validation are identified as future work.

title: Production Enhancement Through the Development of an AI-Based Gas Lift Virtual Metering in Rich Gas Environments. Case Study from a Smart Field
container-title: ADIPEC
c137657228735376d1039f5b4277eee970647e6f.abstract: Abstract Gas lift flow control and rate measurement are critical to gas lift operations, particularly under rich-gas conditions where condensate formation and phase changes introduce additional challenges to accurate measurement. Meter selection directly affects project economics, energy efficiency, and production optimization. This technical study examines field experience from a major smart field with complex gas lift dynamics and compares the performance of differential-pressure, ultrasonic, tracer and orifice-plate meters against physics-AI-based virtual meters in real field applications. The deployment of AI meters enabled real-time production optimization, delivering a 7% uplift while improving gas lift efficiency. Injecting rich gas as a form of lifted gas can be very challenging, impacting the efficiency of gas-lift systems and well test quality. Understanding these phenomena is crucial for designing, operating, and measuring flow rates accurately. Following commissioning of the gas lift facilities, the field experienced a marked decline in well-test acceptance, with many tests rejected because of erroneous or negative formation of GOR values. Analysis using hybrid physics-AI-based gas lift virtual meters showed that differential-pressure and orifice-plate meters were under or overpredicting the gas volume, with absolute deviations ranging from 15-100%. The findings were further validated using clamp-on ultrasonic and tracer technologies, confirming the model's ability to identify faulty measurements. This study evaluates the performance of multiple flow-measurement technologies under complex and variable gas compositions and provides practical insights into operational challenges, installation issues, corrective actions, and best practices for gas lift rate measurement in rich-gas environments. The AI gas lift virtual meter was developed to consume real-time historian data consumed by an hybrid full-physics, reduced-order, proxy and data-driven machine-learning models. The calculated values are compared with field-measured gas lift rates and integrated into an expert system to support visualization, exception detection, and identification of underperforming or faulty meters. Subsequently, the gas lift verification results were embedded into the real-time system to correct gas lift rates and enable more meaningful gas lift optimization. This was achieved by integrating real-time virtual-meter validation, expert-system diagnosis, and independent field verification into a practical measurement-assurance workflow. The study demonstrates that an AI gas lift virtual meter can improve well-test data quality, support meter troubleshooting, assess wet-gas effects, diagnose control-valve issues and optimize gas lift performance under challenging rich-gas operating conditions.

title: Rigless Remediation of Sustained Annulus Pressure in Sensitive Residential Areas Using Advanced Epoxy Resin Systems
container-title: ADIPEC
70e4338031b161d4b75a347c696baff429e6a420.abstract: Abstract Sustained annulus pressure (SAP) presents a significant well-integrity challenge and may pose environmental and safety risks, particularly in mature assets located near residential developments. This paper presents the successful rigless remediation of SAP in a plugged and abandoned (P&A) well using an advanced epoxy-resin system after conventional intervention methods failed to establish sufficient injectivity. The objective was to achieve stable annular conditions while avoiding the operational complexity associated with a workover-rig intervention. The candidate well exhibited SAP within the production-casing annulus and contained hydrogen sulfide (H2S), requiring stringent HSE controls throughout execution. Injectivity testing indicated extremely limited fluid acceptance, rendering conventional squeeze-cementing techniques impractical. Following annulus preparation and fluid removal, a dual-sided injection system was installed, and a staged epoxy-resin treatment was performed. Resin returns observed from the opposite annulus outlet confirmed annular communication and treatment coverage. Progressive improvement in pressure containment was observed during the treatment campaign. Following the final injection stage and curing period, post-treatment monitoring confirmed stable annular conditions with no pressure rebuild. The remediation was validated against the required well-integrity acceptance criteria. The results demonstrate that advanced epoxy-resin systems can provide an effective alternative to rig-based remediation methods for managing SAP in low-injectivity wells. The methodology offers a repeatable approach for restoring annular integrity while reducing operational footprint and environmental impact.

title: Predicting Tomorrow's Failure Today: AI-Driven Time-To-Failure and Multivariable Deviation Analytics for Advancing Reliability and Production Excellence
container-title: ADIPEC
c770d6261637f29451005773beae129d13900075.abstract: Abstract Oil and gas facilities operate as interconnected systems. A change in one part of the plant can affect equipment reliability, process stability, production, energy use, and emissions elsewhere. Conventional surveillance relies on alarms, operating limits, inspections, and subject matter expertise. These safeguards remain essential, but they may not reveal the weak, multivariable patterns that develop before equipment degradation, process instability, production deferment, or increased flaring. This paper presents an integrated industrial artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) framework that combines time-to-failure (TTF) estimation, multivariable deviation detection, and process forecasting. The framework uses historical and real-time operati.ng data to characterize normal operation, degradation, and known failure events. It then compares current plant behavior with these learned patterns to identify emerging risk, show the variables associated with the change, and provide lead time for intervention. TTF modeling estimates the time remaining before a defined undesirable event. For suitable and validated failure models, the prediction horizon can extend to 7 days. Multivariable deviation analytics complements TTF by detecting abnormal relationships among process, mechanical, utility, and environmental variables. This method is particularly useful when few repeat failures are available. Forecasting can also be applied to continuous process measurements when a future value has operational value. Used together, the three methods provide a system-level view rather than a series of isolated tag assessments. The paper draws on deployments in oil and gas processing, gas compression, utilities, and production optimization. It then describes the extension of this approach to the Gas Treatment Plant and Onshore Gas Terminal (GTPOGT). The implementation links the Operation Process Playbook to a web-based, real-time analytics platform. For the high-pressure (HP), low-pressure (LP), and tank flare systems, the platform combines TTF, deviation analytics, and flare rate forecasting. Selected flare rates are forecast up to 4 hours ahead to support earlier investigation and intervention. The main finding is that a predictive model creates lasting value only when it is part of a disciplined operating workflow. Data readiness, clear event definitions, technical ownership, alert governance, engineering validation, response protocols, and model maintenance are as important as the algorithm. The proposed framework moves plant surveillance from alarm-driven response toward predictive, and eventually governed prescriptive, decision support. This shift can improve reliability, reduce exposure to unplanned deferment, increase production efficiency, and support lower carbon operations.

title: Autonomous Well Startup and Control with AI-Based Decisioning for Measurable Production Outcomes and Operational Excellence Using Real-Time Wellhead Intelligence
container-title: ADIPEC
8db35cd131842310f9d5d4faf2dbfb30ea10108c.abstract: Abstract This paper details an innovative practice and adapted initiative implemented by Company Asset to ensure continuous measurement, monitoring, and control of oil flow from oil-producing well leveraging Artificial Intelligence. In addition to maintaining the specified oil flow target, autonomous gas flow control was also effectively managed to ensure comprehensive well control. This arrangement proved advantageous in achieving the well testing key performance indicators (KPIs) and eliminating the need for manual intervention, thereby saving man-hours. The need for real-time flow monitoring & control at individual wellheads led to evaluating various solutions. A Multiphase Flow Meter (MPFM) was installed, enhancing flow measurement and allowing configuration of oil flow rate signals to control valve. This setup enabled autonomous control of the well, managing both natural oil flow and artificial lift gas flow when needed. The design allows easy relocation based on well-activated needs. Steps taken included: Implementing management of change for new solutionsConducting risk assessmentsEvaluating vital GL well surface and subsurface parameters Developing safe operating procedures, scenarios, schematics, and a user-friendly control scheme The autonomous control of the well enabled comprehensive management of the lift gas well. It also significantly reduced the manual labor required for diverting the well into testing facilities. Additionally, it facilitated the optimization of the gas flow rate and ensured the continuous production of oil through the oil-producing wells. The observed well control behavior was smooth and adhered to the stipulated setpoints. By leveraging the capability to connect the MPFM with the piping connections available at the wellhead, the following benefits were achieved and will continue to be advantageous in the future: Optimization of manhours approximately 87 hours for 10 wells / 1,200 hours for 140 wellsProduction gain of 1,850,000 barrels of oil by preventing production loss from gas lift wellsOptimization of GL flow rate, leading to savings of lean gas (9,000 MMscf for 50 wells) valued at 133 MMUSDAchievement of 100% well testing KPIsEffective and timely dual-string well testing resulting in a 10 MMUSD production gainEnsuring compliance with subsurface parameter restrictions, thereby preserving reservoir healthEnhancement of well digitalizationFacilitation of autonomous well controlReal-time well testingAccurate representation of the well's behaviorAI-based decision-making ensuring adherence to restrictions and WH/reservoir guidelines The implemented solution is highly effective in ensuring continuous production, timely well testing, and reducing manhours by leveraging autonomous control integrated with artificial intelligence. This methodology can be replicated across other existing facilities within the company and globally for the following reasons: Real-time flow monitoring and controlWell testing complianceEffective reservoir management This implementation will enhance well availability with continuous production while ensuring the health of the reservoir and surface facilities.

title: Reference Implementation and Verification Procedure for Deployment of AI Components in OT Systems Adjacent to Safety-Related Systems, Deployment Sovereignty Through Independent Deployment Verification Under UAE and Saudi Arabia Data Regulation
container-title: ADIPEC
78412239afbb794fc3ff4abe3ea5d48460be2654.abstract: Abstract This paper addresses operators of critical energy infrastructure in the UAE and Saudi Arabia integrating AI components into control loops that govern irreversible physical actions—emergency shutdowns, pipeline isolation, autonomous well control. For Critical Information Infrastructure, regional regulation requires classified operational data to remain within the applicable jurisdiction and geographical boundaries (UAE IA Standard v2.1, T1.3.3; NCA CSCC-1), alongside personal-data regimes (UAE Federal Decree-Law 45/2021; Saudi PDPL). Standard compliance demonstrations—configuration checks, procedural audits, post-factum reviews—are insufficient here, since they occur after an irreversible event. Verification must therefore precede deployment and be executed independently by the operator, not the vendor or a third-party auditor. We term this property deployment sovereignty. We propose a methodology of three elements: an operational test distinguishing systems that require strict data confinement and irreversible actions; an architecture for these systems defined by four interdependent properties (continuous integrity attestation, fail-closed behavior under uncertainty, a hardware root of trust, a verifiable supply chain); and a public reference implementation with an SPDX SBOM, Sigstore Rekor transparency-log entries, and per-file reproducible builds, verified by two independent cold rebuilds on separate infrastructure (Section 5.3), letting the operator compile the source and verify per-file hashes against the vendor's shipped SBOM. As AI models are routinely retrained and replaced, this verifiable update path matters more than in conventional OT software. The distinction the paper draws is between compliance achieved by construction and compliance asserted by configuration: only the former survives a compromised vendor build pipeline. The architecture maps directly to mandatory UAE IA v2.1 controls: continuous attestation to T3.1.1 (Configuration Management), the hardware root to T3.4.1/T3.4.3 (Cryptography and Key Management), the verifiable supply chain to T6.2.3 (ICT Supply Chain Security), and the composition to T1.3.3 (Data Handling). Applicable oil-and-gas scope includes autonomous drilling loops, pipeline monitoring with automatic isolation, setpoint optimization, and decision-support systems executing emergency shutdowns. This is an architectural position supported by a public reference implementation, not a report on a production deployment; performance under load and validation on target equipment are out of scope.

title: From AI Prototype to Agentic AI: Scaling Intelligent Well Placement for Field Development Planning
container-title: ADIPEC
4032215a85683589a46e0b5cb84197135af286b6.abstract: Abstract Well placement decisions are central to field development planning because they require simultaneous consideration of reservoir quality, remaining hydrocarbon potential, subsurface uncertainty, well deliverability, drilling constraints, and development economics. Conventional workflows rely on sequential interpretation and repeated manual screening, which restricts the number of alternatives that multidisciplinary teams can evaluate within a study cycle. Earlier work demonstrated an artificial-intelligence-assisted workflow that combined probabilistic opportunity maps, machine-learning-based target classification, drilling-risk information, completion-quality indicators, and optimization of reservoir targets, well trajectories, and drilling centers. This paper describes the next stage of that work: transformation of the pilot workflow into a scalable, on-premises application integrated with the established subsurface modeling and simulation environment, together with an agentic orchestration layer for broader field-development studies. The productized workflow accepts map-based quality indicators from a deterministic model or an ensemble, enables configurable construction of an opportunity index, excludes existing wells and constrained regions, and uses a development-concept generation engine to place reservoir targets and create drillable trajectories subject to surface no-go areas, existing facilities capacities, and well design constraints. New wells are transferred into simulation cases for performance evaluation with two widely used reservoir simulators. A probabilistic analysis window then compares well-level and development-level outcomes across realizations. At the orchestration level, specialized agents coordinate target identification, trajectory generation, simulation-case preparation, uncertainty evaluation, and scenario ranking while retaining engineer-defined objectives, constraints, review gates, and final approval. Validation across three customer projects demonstrates a progression from pilot to repeatable deployment. In a giant onshore oil reservoir, the workflow reduced the planned well count by 18, extended the production plateau by up to two years, and reduced well-placement and assessment time by up to 80%. In a complex deep gas-condensate field, machine-learning proxies and high-performance simulation enabled more than 6,500 realization runs in three months and supported identification of more than 20 infill locations. A third, unpublished application continued the product-improvement cycle by introducing AI-assisted risk-reward optimization. These examples show that the standard product provides the automation and optimization backbone, while project-specific AI augments model calibration, opportunity screening, scenario ranking, and decision support. The value is controlled expansion of the decision space—not autonomous selection of a single answer.

title: Enabling Resilient and Adaptive Production Operations Through AI-Enabled Production System Optimization at Scale
container-title: ADIPEC
df316736063baaf91859d79d24c2bef4d58801cc.abstract: Abstract ADNOC has deployed an AI-enabled Production System Optimization (AiPSO) solution to strengthen the resilience, flexibility, and responsiveness of production operations under increasing global supply demand uncertainty. This paper presents the value outcomes from the Phase-1 implementation across eight producing fields, demonstrating how real-time production intelligence and rapid scenario planning enable proactive, compliant, and value-driven production operations at scale. AiPSO is implemented as an integrated Production System Digital Twin spanning reservoirs, wells, and surface production systems, combining physics-based engineering models with AI-driven analytics. A scalable Industrial Data and AI Foundation automates real-time data ingestion, validation, contextualization, and model orchestration through a centralized DataOps pipeline. Core workflows include exception-based surveillance, automated diagnostics, scenario-aware production optimization, and execution tracking. Generative AI capabilities evolve from an engineering copilot to domain-specific advisory services and AiPSO Agents, accelerating scenario evaluation and shortening the decision-to-action cycle. Real-time engineering operating envelopes enable safe, constraint-aware execution and controlled autonomy. The Phase-1 deployment of AiPSO across eight producing fields during 2025–2026 delivered measurable business value by enhancing ADNOC's ability to anticipate, evaluate, and respond to production variability and operational uncertainty. More than 25 advanced digital workflows were operationalized, enabling real-time surveillance, automated diagnostics, and intelligent optimization, resulting in a sustained 1–2% production uplift with no incremental CAPEX. Key workflows, including exception-based well surveillance, artificial-lift diagnostics, multiphase flowmeter validation, and integrated production monitoring, significantly improved data confidence, asset visibility, and decision quality. The integrated digital twin enabled earlier identification of reservoir, well, and surface constraints, reducing time-to-intervention and improving production stability. Operations shifted from reactive issue resolution to proactive, scenario-driven constraint management. GenAI-enabled workflows accelerated root-cause analysis and response planning, while real-time operating envelopes supported safe closed-loop adjustments, strengthening operational resilience and supply reliability. This paper presents a multi-field, enterprise-scale application of AI-driven production system digital twins focused on operational resilience and rapid scenario planning. The integration of Generative AI evolving from engineering copilots to action-ready AiPSO Agents represents a novel advancement beyond traditional digital oilfield practices, enabling proactive, adaptive, and increasingly autonomous production operations across large, complex upstream assets.
