title: AI-Driven Integration of Seismic, Geological, and Dynamic Data to Delineate Sub-Seismic Lineaments Controlling Pressure-Sink Behavior and Waterflood Performance in a Mature Offshore Carbonate Reservoir – A Case Study (ADNOC Offshore Abu Dhabi)
container-title: ADIPEC
e034caf2958a52636a241f0c860ce03b5b8c04ba.abstract: Abstract Reservoir development in mature carbonates is often challenged by localized low-pressure anomalies not supported by conventional models. In the studied offshore Abu Dhabi field, a persistent pressure sink in Sector B of the "XYZ" Reservoir exhibits weak aquifer and injection support, resulting in non-uniform pressure distribution and inefficient waterflood sweep. This study aims to identify causes of this behavior and investigate partial transmissibility barriers by characterizing sub-seismic structural features due to tectono-stratigraphic evolution and present-day compartment behavior, integrating them into a predictive reservoir framework to improve development planning and injector placement. A multidisciplinary workflow integrated pressure-regime mapping and Pressure While Drilling (PWD) data with AI-assisted seismic fault and horizon interpretation. Pressure surveillance and PWD trends reveal localized gradients (hundreds of psi over short distances) and delayed pressure transfer from injection corridors toward the sink, inconsistent with a homogeneous response. The AI-driven approach enhanced detection of subtle faults and discontinuities, enabling extraction of a refined lineament network beyond conventional seismic resolution. These features were validated using seismic attributes, structural dip variations, and multidirectional sections. Open-hole logs, saturation logs, and production data identified saturation contrasts across interpreted lineaments. Pressure transient analysis (PTA) served as a tool to evaluate boundary conditions, revealing sealing to partially sealing faults and anisotropic transmissibility behavior. Drilling observations, including mud losses, kicks, and stuck-pipe events, provided additional evidence of heterogeneity. New data, including cores, logs, high-resolution seismic images, and PWD measurements, are being integrated to further validate interpretations and refine transmissibility characterization for optimizing injector placement and improving pressure support and sweep efficiency. Sector B exhibits injection corridors with elevated pressure yet slow pressure transfer into a sink area, with steep gradients (including approximately 500 psi/km changes), indicating restricted communication inconsistent with uniform connectivity. The analysis demonstrates that the pressure sink is controlled by sub-seismic lineaments, fractures, and low-permeability features acting as partial transmissibility barriers, restricting pressure communication from injectors and aquifer support. AI-enhanced seismic interpretation improves confidence in these features, which align with observed pressure gradients, PTA flow regimes, and well-log signatures. Incorporating these lineaments into the reservoir model improves prediction of pressure distribution and waterflood performance, reducing mismatch between modeled and observed behavior. This work presents a scalable workflow integrating AI-driven seismic interpretation with geological and dynamic datasets, where pressure data and PTA are primary tools for validating sub-seismic structures. The approach reduces structural uncertainty and directly links lineament behavior to waterflood effectiveness and well-placement decisions in mature carbonate reservoirs

title: Generative 3d Asset Reconstruction from Few Images for Scalable Industrial Digital Twins in Turbomachinery Assembly
container-title: ADIPEC
29a392fa11ba6ee9266bb6e5bd4eda94a6784189.abstract: Abstract Digital twin initiatives are frequently constrained by the limited availability of three-dimensional asset models. This work presents an industrial adaptation of a structured-latent, flow-matching generative 3D reconstruction model for rapid reconstruction of industrial assets from one to four photographs. The proposed modification augments the original image-conditioned flow-matching pipeline with a multi-image conditioning mechanism that appends multiple image embeddings to the conditioning sequence. The method was developed to support creation of a manufacturing digital twin for turbomachinery assembly environments. Generated assets are integrated into workflows supporting layout validation, ergonomics assessment, logistics planning, material-flow analysis and scenario simulation. Preliminary industrial evaluation indicates that multi-image conditioning improves reconstruction completeness for assets containing significant self-occlusion while preserving workflow simplicity. The paper discusses architecture, deployment pipeline, qualitative results, limitations and future research directions.

title: AI-Driven Facility Inspection Using Vision-Language Models and Image Classification: Model Selection and Prompt Design
container-title: ADIPEC
f46140850ebf72b4e0b337f5199fb8e3dca783dc.abstract: Abstract Visual inspection remains essential at dispersed oil and gas facilities because many operating conditions cannot be inferred from instruments alone. Routine site visits provide this visual evidence, but they become difficult to scale when facilities are numerous and most inspections find nothing actionable. FieldView addresses this challenge through scheduled photography, automated image assessment, and human review. In the studied deployment, 200 cameras across 100 facilities produce about 2,000 images per day. This paper considers two practical decisions in designing image-based inspections. The first is whether a task is better suited to an object detector, which locates and classifies a defined target, or a vision-language model (VLM), which can interpret evidence across a wider scene. The second is how much instruction a VLM prompt should contain. Rain-cap, flare, smoke, and spill inspections are used to examine how the visual evidence required by an engineering decision can guide model and prompt selection. The study evaluates fixed detector and VLM configurations on expert-labeled field images for rain-cap, flare, smoke, and spill inspections. Matched-image comparisons are used where possible, with class-level metrics, statistical analysis, and error review used to interpret overall performance. The rain-cap detector achieved 97.72% mAP@0.5 on its validation set, demonstrating strong performance for a localized and consistently labeled target. For flare-state classification, the full-image VLM achieved 91.2% accuracy on the 227-image benchmark, compared with 69.2% for the fine-tuned detector workflow. The smoke configuration achieved 96.2% accuracy, while the selected spill configuration achieved 77.0% accuracy and a macro F1 of 0.756. Controlled prompt comparisons also showed that additional instructions, response fields, and decision procedures did not consistently improve accuracy. Together, the evaluations provide quantitative evidence across both localized targets and scene-level inspection decisions. These results are used to support engineering selection and validation of complete inspection configurations rather than to claim that one model family is universally superior. The results indicate that model choice should follow the structure of the inspection rather than a preference for one model family. A detector performed well for the localized rain-cap task, while a full-image VLM was more effective for flare-state classification on the studied benchmark. Across flare and spill evaluations, additional prompt detail did not consistently improve accuracy. These findings support a measured workflow: define the visual evidence needed for the decision, test complete configurations on representative images, retain prompt additions only when they demonstrate value, and preserve human review for operational disposition.

title: A Continuous Satellite-Based Quantification of Associated Gas Flaring Using a Novel AI-Driven Framework
container-title: ADIPEC
4d816be7d0d956348b010336afe7a63b2005bf3c.abstract: Summary This study presents a novel AI-driven framework for quantifying associated gas flaring using satellite imagery, addressing critical measurement gaps in fields where key reservoir gas contributions are not directly metered. Reliable flaring quantification is essential for accurate gas balance, regulatory compliance, and emissions mitigation, yet conventional vendor-based approaches remain costly, infrequent, and operationally limited. The proposed methodology integrates nighttime VIIRS satellite data with advanced Artificial Neural Network (ANN) models to detect flaring sites and predict flare temperature, radiant heat, and daily flared gas volumes. By leveraging multispectral infrared inputs—including radiance, viewing geometry, and cloud masking—the model delivers high-resolution, continuous monitoring. The model derives flared volumes using a machine learning model calibrated against in-situ measurements, enabling robust validation and extension to previously unmonitored sites. CO2 emissions are simultaneously quantified as part of the workflow. The framework delivers strong predictive performance and improved accuracy over conventional methods while capturing dynamic operational changes across six flaring locations. It enables enhanced gas balance reconstruction, indirect estimation of unmeasured reservoir contributions, and near real-time reporting through automated dashboards. This work establishes a scalable, cost-effective, and independent solution for flare monitoring, with direct applications in emission reduction, operational optimization, and deployment in infrastructure-constrained environments.

title: From Reactive to Predictive: Deploying AI Computer Vision for Real-Time Safety Monitoring Across Oxy Oman Operations
container-title: ADIPEC
e5115df726c795ea12d87b54660a34437d402768.abstract: Abstract This paper describes the deployment of an AI-enabled computer vision platform across drilling rigs, hoists, and workshop facilities in Oxy Oman to support proactive HSE monitoring through continuous, automated safety observation. The objective is to demonstrate how real-time AI detection of unsafe behaviors — including PPE non-compliance, red zone management, line-of-fire exposure, and housekeeping deficiencies — can support a shift in safety management from reactive incident response toward more proactive hazard identification and prevention. A centralized, on-premise server architecture was configured to process up to 40 concurrent camera streams and was made accessible across facilities through a secure browser-based interface. The deployment leveraged existing closed-circuit television (CCTV) infrastructure, minimizing incremental field hardware requirements. Safety scenarios were validated through a structured User Acceptance Testing (UAT) process using datasets collected across varied lighting and environmental conditions. Each AI-generated observation was reviewed by trained end-users and classified as True, False, or No Decision, creating a continuous feedback loop to refine scenario logic, improve model performance, and reduce false positives. During the monitoring period, the system generated close to 1,500 safety observations across day and night shifts, with 25 active scenarios deployed across 23 cameras. Model performance varied by use case, with PPE-related detections showing stronger true-observation rather than more context-dependent scenarios. A key advancement was the implementation of conditional rig-floor use cases in which AI visual detection was integrated with real-time drilling data to enable context-aware scenario triggering. In this approach, scenarios such as red zone management during drilling operations was activated only when predicted operational thresholds were met, such as rotary rpm. This integration of visual AI with live drilling telemetry reduced false positives and improved the operational relevance of alerts. False alarm analysis identified recurring causes-including area-definition errors, camera perspective limitations, and scenario-logic mismatches — which were addressed through iterative configuration updates. The results indicate that a structured, feedback-driven deployment combining visual AI, operational data, and human review can support more proactive safety monitoring in upstream drilling environments. This paper presents a phased implementation framework for AI-enabled HSE monitoring in upstream oil and gas operations, combining human-in-the-loop (HITL) validation with structured false-alarm analysis. It also introduces a context-aware deployment model in which computer vision scenarios are triggered by live drilling telemetry thresholds, improving alert relevance and supporting scalable adoption through existing site infrastructure.

title: From Tender to Total Depth: Artificial Intelligence and Generative AI Agents Deployed Across Well Construction Planning and Execution
container-title: ADIPEC
d3e85950220b86d6b794d2c08b01b4de2c16e93a.abstract: Abstract Well construction projects face data and decision challenges across two distinct phases: pre-well planning and tender preparation, where manual offset analysis limits coverage and introduces bias; and active drilling execution, where non-productive time (NPT) events demand rapid, data-backed decisions. This paper describes an AI-driven platform that serves the full well lifecycle — automating time and risk estimation during tender preparation, and providing real-time generative AI agent support during drilling execution. The platform integrates 13+ AI and machine learning engines applied to Daily Drilling Reports (DDRs) across two workflow phases. For tender and planning: a transformer-based model classifying drilling activities from operational text in English and Spanish; Monte Carlo simulation for probabilistic time forecasting; a genetic algorithm adapted from multiple sequence alignment techniques to predict operational sequences from historical patterns; a Well Risk Index (WRI) for quantitative, data-driven risk scoring; and hierarchical aggregation from section to campaign level, enabling AFE and P&L scenario construction at tender scale. For drilling execution: a suite of generative AI agents that mine offset cases, rank hypotheses, and deliver remediation recommendations for NPT events including stuck pipe and loss circulation; a location-specific Optimum Fishing Time (OFT) model that replaces global cost rules of thumb with field-calibrated economic thresholds; and a generative AI agent that automates end-of-well report generation from DDR data. The platform is actively used by more than 250 engineers with 38% annual growth, supporting assessment of well construction tenders valued at $10-17 billion annually. Well classification time has been reduced from 8 hours to 20 minutes per well; offset coverage has expanded from the 10-20 wells an engineer can manually review to the full available dataset; data preparation effort has been reduced by 56%; risk assessment is 26 times faster than manual evaluation; and a MENA region tender involving 56 well architectures and 158 sections was completed in at least half the previously required time while evaluating all available offset wells. End-of-well report generation has been reduced from four days to two days. Automated technology identification has been estimated to recover approximately $34.7 million in value per year. P10 well time targets — previously aspirational — are now consistently achievable with actionable steps across the Integrated Well Construction (IWC) portfolio. This paper presents a field-validated, multi-component AI architecture structured around three operational phases — winning work, planning wells, and executing well construction programs — that links time estimation, AFE optimization by constructing scenarios, risk quantification, NPT classification, technology identification, local fishing economics, and real-time drilling event support within a single, data-driven ecosystem. Finally, this solution enables engineers to spend their time in high value activities than in manual excel intensive tasks.

title: Hydrogen Fuel Switching in Refining Assets: Technical Integration and Economic Barriers to Large-Scale Deployment
container-title: ADIPEC
44666aa46b51766f868be5b2015cd0823de16db7.abstract: Abstract The increased risks of climate change are becoming increasingly prevalent worldwide. Many refiners and operators have therefore made ambitious pledges to meet net zero emissions. This has led to growing interest in decarbonization opportunities to reduce Scope 1 greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions. While hydrogen firing has been demonstrated on individual refinery assets, refinery-wide deployment remains largely unexplored. This paper presents one of the first published refinery-scale assessments of hydrogen fuel switching, evaluating the technical integration requirements, economic performance, and decarbonization potential of large-scale deployment across a representative Middle Eastern refinery. A structured methodology was developed using experience from multiple refinery concept studies to assess hydrogen production, distribution, combustion equipment modifications, refinery fuel gas (RFG) management, and site integration requirements. Four fuelswitching pathways were evaluated: Existing Hydrogen Capacity - Partial Fuel Switching,Existing Hydrogen Capacity - Full Fuel Switching of Selected Consumers,Additional Blue Hydrogen Capacity - Full Fuel Switching,Additional Green Hydrogen Capacity - Full Fuel Switching. Economic performance was assessed using the levelized cost of abatement (LCOA) over a 25-year project life. The assessment identified fuel gas network limitations, hydrogen distribution infrastructure, management of displaced RFG, and plot space availability as the principal factors governing refinery-scale implementation. Results show that large-scale blue hydrogen production with integrated carbon capture emerged as the most economically attractive hydrogen fuel-switching option. The process proved to be more energy efficient for hydrogen production and carbon capture compared to the case using existing hydrogen capacity. This meant that over the 25 years operation it was much more economically attractive, as the fuel gas requirements make up a large proportion of overall project costs. Compared to the green hydrogen case the CAPEX costs are substantially lower. Green hydrogen production requires significant infrastructure for electricity production, electrolysis and energy storage. Comparison with a representative refinery Carbon Capture, and Storage concept demonstrated that under the baseline pricing conditions the CCS concept returns slightly better economics for carbon abatement. However, sensitivity analysis showed that hydrogen fuel switching becomes increasingly competitive under conditions of high fuel gas prices, low electricity prices, and refinery layouts that constrain CCS deployment. The study demonstrates that no single decarbonization pathway is universally optimal and highlights the importance of refinery-wide techno-economic assessments to identify the most effective site-specific decarbonization strategy and support long-term investment decisions.

title: Agentic AI Control Tower for Offshore EPCI Marine Logistics Optimisation in Multi-Contractor Island Projects
container-title: ADIPEC
5d44c0528017712697411348f4c13e53d242d191.abstract: Abstract Offshore engineering, procurement, construction, and installation work depends on a marine logistics chain capable of balancing urgent construction demand against limited vessel capacity, field-entry and towage approvals, crew compliance, berth congestion, weather windows, fuel and freshwater availability, and cost responsibility across several projects operating on the same island. In many projects, the information needed to make these decisions is scattered across cargo manifests, vessel schedules, permit trackers, daily reports, emails, and spreadsheets. This paper sets out a practical agentic artificial-intelligence control-tower model that brings those fragmented inputs into one predictive and auditable decision environment. Deterministic safety and compliance gates are combined with bounded AI agents covering cargo prioritisation, voyage consolidation, vessel and tug assignment, permit and crew monitoring, weather and berth risk, bunkering forecasts, and project-level cost attribution. The prototype dashboard and workflow were assessed against an anonymised 12-week operating dataset from concurrent offshore construction projects on an ADNOC-operated island in Abu Dhabi. Performance under the observed baseline was compared with a model-assisted re-planning scenario. Average deck-space utilisation rose from 31% to 89%; combined landing-craft productivity increased from about one to 3.2 sailings per week; and completed cargo-barge towage cycles increased from about one to 3.8 cycles per active barge per month. Cargo readiness confirmed before berth booking improved from 57% to 93%, while average berth-related waiting fell from 11.2 to 3.1 hours for each affected voyage. Fuel-allocation completeness increased from 68% to 97%, and daily fuel-forecast error declined from 19.5% to 3.5%. The model also surfaced towage-approval, crew-rotation, weather, berth, and regional-disruption risks before mobilisation. Its main contribution is an integrated control-tower architecture that evaluates operational constraints and commercial ownership together, while preserving human authority over every safety-critical decision.

title: From Real-Time Integrated Formation Evaluation and Geosteering to ICD Optimization: A Case Study for Sustained Oil Production in a Mature Offshore Carbonate Field
container-title: ADIPEC
26112abef211d0be0545fcd85d4eb3909d939c7d.abstract: Abstract This paper presents an integrated formation evaluation workflow developed to drill and complete horizontal producer Well X in a mature offshore carbonate field in Abu Dhabi. Historical dump flooding within the oil pool, followed by decades of peripheral water injection and later crestal gas injection, has resulted in complex fluid distributions within the reservoir, characterized by localized gas-cap expansion and irregular injected-water distribution. Several offset producers near Well X experienced unexpected rapid increases in water cut and subsequent loss of natural flow, highlighting the challenges associated with accurately predicting fluid distribution. To mitigate the risk of premature water breakthrough, a pilot hole was drilled prior to the horizontal section of Well X. In addition, this well incorporated advanced data acquisition technologies, including Logging-While-Drilling (LWD) triple-combo, Ultra-Deep Azimuthal Resistivity (UDAR), Formation Testing While Drilling (FTWD), and Advanced Mud Logging (AML). The acquired data were integrated in real time to evaluate fluid distribution and optimize geosteering decisions during drilling. Pilot-hole LWD data showed no water indication within the proposed landing interval in the upper part of Sub-layer 2 and indicated gas influence near the top of Sub-layer 3. The gas indication was observed again from LWD and AML data while drilling the horizontal landing section. Based on these results, the horizontal drain was landed within the oil-bearing zone of Sub-layer 2. However, although pilot-hole evaluation suggested oil-bearing conditions within the proposed landing interval, conventional propagation resistivity and UDAR identified a conductive interval within Sub-layer 2 approximately 1,200 ft from the reservoir entry. The historical injector distribution, high-water-cut behavior observed in nearby producers, and the absence of any significant porosity or lithological change supported the interpretation that the interval represented slumped injected water. Following several hundred feet of further evaluation, the well trajectory was adjusted upward by approximately 12 ft TVD into the oil-bearing portion of Sub-layer 3. The adjustment repositioned the wellbore away from the interpreted water-affected interval and established an estimated TVD separation of 6 to 7 ft from the conductive interval remaining within Sub-layer 2, while staying below the gas-affected upper part of Sub-layer 3. The lower-completion design was subsequently revised from the planned conventional Limited-Entry Liner (LEL) to a NETool-modeled 10-compartment ICD completion. High, Medium, and Low relative nozzle restrictions were assigned based on the interpreted reservoir risk profile along the wellbore and installed nozzle geometry. The design was intended to limit excessive compartment inflow, moderate localized reservoir drawdown, and lower water-coning risk while maintaining deliverability from lower-risk intervals. The resulting well placement and completion design were followed by sustained production performance, with 0% measured surface water cut over more than two years of monitoring.

title: AI-Enabled Maritime Operations: Transforming Safety, Efficiency, and Decarbonization Through Real-Time Fleet Intelligence
container-title: ADIPEC
60f309ca54c33ce36234da56369dd71b92dc0693.abstract: Abstract This paper presents a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) framework for improving safety, efficiency, compliance visibility, and decarbonization decision support in offshore maritime operations. Vessel daily reports, fuel and lube oil records, machinery hours, HSE observations, defects, inspections, certificates, crew and training data, and emissions indicators are often dispersed across applications, spreadsheets, emails, and document stores. The resulting problem is not lack of data, but difficulty retrieving and interpreting the right evidence when a decision is required. The framework converts verified vessel and company records into an access-controlled maritime knowledge base. For each natural-language question, the system applies validation, metadata filters, hybrid retrieval, reranking, deterministic calculations, grounded generation, source citation, and human verification. Representative questions include abnormal consumption, machinery hours inconsistent with activity, recurring defects, overdue or unverified compliance items, HSE themes, training gaps, and emissions variance. The demonstration indicates that RAG is valuable when it connects records that are normally reviewed separately. Consumption becomes meaningful when combined with activity, weather, machinery configuration, and comparable periods; safety observations become more useful when linked to actions, inspections, and training; and compliance queries can distinguish expiry from an approaching due date or superseded document. The process also reveals inconsistent units, duplicate entries, missing activity codes, and stale records. RAG can therefore provide traceable fleet decision support when it uses approved data, preserves lineage, enforces vessel- and role-based access, and permits a no-answer response where evidence is insufficient. It should reduce manual searching and support earlier intervention, while operational authority remains with competent maritime personnel. The evaluation approach therefore specifies quantitative measures—retrieval precision, citation coverage, calculation accuracy, end-to-end investigation and verification time, manual workflow steps, source-system switches, human correction rate, and user adoption—benchmarked against the same questions completed through existing reports and dashboards. Deployment success also depends on governed source quality, scalable indexing, integration controls, and maintained maritime metadata and taxonomies. Cross-industry controlled and field studies report AI-related productivity or task-time improvements ranging from approximately 15% to 55.8% [11–14]. Given the higher consequence of maritime decisions and mandatory human verification, this paper proposes benchmark-informed initial targets of 25-35% lower end-to-end investigation time and 25-30% lower manual workflow effort, with at least 90% retrieval precision and at least 95% citation coverage. These are acceptance targets for paired trials, not measured fleet outcomes.

title: From Reactive to Predictive Offshore Operations an AI – Enabled Integrated Framework for Vessel Reliability Enhancement and NPT Reduction
container-title: ADIPEC
3a9092cf379d2df075f4bd689bf039d3960fbb62.abstract: Abstract Offshore project execution is increasingly challenged by rising operational complexity, tighter project schedules, and growing expectations for reliability, safety, and cost efficiency. Despite technological advancements in the offshore sector, Non-Productive Time (NPT) continues to significantly affect project delivery due to equipment failures, vessel downtime, maintenance inefficiencies, logistical constraints, and fragmented operational decision-making. Traditional reactive maintenance approaches often address failures after operational disruption has occurred, resulting in increased costs, schedule delays, and reduced asset utilization. This paper proposes an integrated framework that combines vessel operational data, maintenance history, equipment condition monitoring, offshore logistics information, and project execution parameters within a centralized digital platform. The methodology integrates predictive maintenance principles, reliability engineering analysis, and AI-enabled anomaly detection to identify operational risks and early indicators of equipment degradation. The framework further connects vessel scheduling, maintenance planning, resource coordination, logistics, and offshore execution tracking within a unified operational decision-support model. Key performance indicators, including Mean Time Between Failures (MTBF), Mean Time to Repair (MTTR), vessel utilization, project schedule adherence, maintenance response efficiency, and NPT trends, are incorporated to support predictive operational decision-making and project risk prioritization. A simulation-based evaluation was conducted using a representative offshore construction support vessel operating over a 12-month campaign. The simulated baseline represented a reactive-preventive maintenance environment with an MTBF of 620 operating hours, MTTR of 18 hours, vessel utilization of 78%, and annual NPT of 11.4%. Under the proposed framework scenario, the model projected an increase in MTBF to 860 operating hours, a reduction in MTTR to 8 hours, an increase in vessel utilization to 87%, and a 54% reduction in equipment-related NPT. Schedule adherence was also projected to improve by 18% under the defined simulation assumptions. The results indicate that the proposed framework has the potential to improve offshore reliability and execution performance by integrating equipment condition information with maintenance planning, logistics coordination, and project execution requirements. By providing a common decision-support architecture, the framework is designed to support earlier maintenance intervention, improved resource coordination, and more proactive management of vessel-related operational risks. The simulation therefore provides an indicative assessment of the potential benefits of integrating reliability analytics with offshore project execution planning. Unlike conventional offshore operational studies focused primarily on project optimization or standalone maintenance systems, this work introduces a cross-functional framework integrating vessel reliability engineering, predictive maintenance analytics, offshore logistics, and project execution intelligence into a unified operational ecosystem. The proposed model provides a scalable architecture for supporting the transition from reactive offshore management toward more predictive, data-driven operational planning. The reported performance improvements are simulation-based outcomes generated under the defined modelling assumptions and have not yet been validated through live vessel deployment or field trials. Operational validation using vessel-specific historical data and controlled pilot implementation is identified as the next stage for assessing predictive accuracy, failure prediction performance, and the realized impact on reliability, NPT, and project execution.

title: Field-Validated AI-Enabled Advanced Process Control for Operating Efficiency in Large-Scale Oil and Gas Separation Trains
container-title: ADIPEC
149e77286c029a31359d3646c03fa90db748fc39.abstract: Abstract Conventional oil and gas separation facilities operate under highly variable conditions caused by changing well contributions, gas-oil ratio, water cut, production routing, slugging, and strong interactions among separation, desalting, stabilization, and export systems. These conditions have historically limited the application of Advanced Process Control in upstream production facilities, where optimization commonly depends on independent regulatory control loops, conservative operating targets, delayed laboratory measurements, and frequent operator intervention. This paper presents the full-scale deployment and field validation of an AI-enabled Advanced Process Control (Ai-APC) architecture across five conventional oil and gas separation trains and associated facilities within one of the world's largest onshore oil fields. The Gas Oil Separation Plant, designed for 780,000 BOPD and processing commingled production from more than 600 wells, was optimized using next-generation Dynamic Matrix Control (DMC3™), adaptive process models, and real-time soft sensors for Reid Vapor Pressure and salt prediction. The deployment methodology included site assessment, data conditioning, live-plant dynamic testing, model development and validation, Distributed Control System integration, operator training, closed-loop commissioning, and digital performance auditing using real-time KPI dashboards. Performance was evaluated from 17 February to 30 March 2026 against a validated pre-APC baseline. The Ai-APC application achieved 99.35% availability and improved oil recovery by 0.31 vol%, equivalent to 2,208 BOPD of incremental production. Lean-gas consumption per barrel of oil decreased by 55%, fresh wash-water consumption decreased by 3%, and the frequency and variability of manual operator intervention decreased by 20%. The deployment also reduced CO2 emissions by 11,666 metric tons and delivered approximately USD 43 million/year in annualized realized value. The results demonstrate that highly variable conventional separation facilities can be transformed from reactive, laboratory-dependent operation into predictive, quality-aware, and continuously optimized assets. The work establishes a transferable AI-enabled brownfield separation optimization framework integrating adaptive multivariable control, real-time quality inferential, operator decision support, and digital performance assurance. This framework provides a scalable foundation for improving operating efficiency and advancing progressively autonomous upstream production operations.

title: Diagnosing Sustained Annulus Pressure with Fiber Based Downhole Leak Detection: Pinpointing Leak Depth & Flow Communication Beyond Bleed Off Limitations in an ADNOC Offshore Well
container-title: ADIPEC
6b956df20cedaf1a01819772b2174403a4ff889f.abstract: Abstract High sustained annulus pressure (SAP) represents a critical well integrity risk and often necessitates immediate intervention. This paper presents a case study describing the application of a fibre based downhole leak detection technology to diagnose the source and behaviour of SAP in a single oil producing well experiencing elevated annulus pressure which could not be reduced through conventional bleed off practices. The primary objective was to accurately determine the leak depth and flow communication in a time critical operation. The bare optical fibre was deployed to acquire distributed acoustic sensing (DAS), distributed temperature sensing (DTS) across a sequence of operational stages, including baseline monitoring, controlled annulus fluid injection and pressure build up. Survey parameters were carefully selected to manage high leak rates and elevated flow velocities, enabling clear discrimination between tubing and annular flow regimes. The integrated dataset supported interpretation of fluid movement and pressure response throughout the surveyed interval. The combined DAS/DTS, and surface pressure data delivered a clear and consistent identification of a single tubing leak. Closely matched pressure trends between the tubing and annulus confirmed active communication, while localised acoustic and thermal anomalies precisely identified the leak location during the activation operations. Fluid velocity analysis further validated the flow path, confirming annular flow above the leak and tubing flow below it, and eliminating evidence of additional leak sources. High-quality data were maintained throughout the survey, enabling confident interpretation for the challenging operating conditions. This case study demonstrates bare fibre optic sensing can deliver high confidence SAP diagnostics within a short operational window. The complete leak detection workflow, from deployment through multi-stage pressure manipulation was completed over a brief survey duration (&lt;4 hours) while the leak remained dynamically active. The results highlight the value of short duration distributed sensing surveys as an effective and timely tool for urgent well integrity assessment and decision making.

title: AI-Driven Video Analytics and Behavioral Safety Intelligence: Enhancing Human-Centered Operational Adaptation in Offshore Support Vessels
container-title: ADIPEC
156e6d6192a3d2679989b73fff7135b74a8cfd47.abstract: Computer vision and artificial intelligence (AI) are increasingly used in industrial Health, Safety, and Environment (HSE) management to detect missing personal protective equipment (PPE), restricted-zone entries, and line-of-fire exposure. Early offshore and industrial deployments established the technical feasibility of real-time edge processing and automated safety monitoring (Almadhoun et al. 2020; Tamaazousti et al. 2022). A practical challenge emerges when these systems are scaled across multiple assets: large volumes of detections must be converted into operationally meaningful information. Real-time alerts can support immediate intervention, but isolated detections do not necessarily explain why a behavior recurses or whether the underlying procedure, equipment, or task design contributes to the observed deviation (Corallo and Spingardi 2024; Vukicevic et al. 2024). Traditional HSE responses may treat behavioral deviations primarily as individual compliance failures. Human Factors engineering instead recognizes that task demands, equipment interfaces, and environmental constraints shape worker behavior (Reason 1997). Safety-II similarly emphasizes the difference between prescribed work and operational practice, commonly described as Work-as-Imagined and Work-as-Done (Hollnagel 2014).

title: AI Digital Rock Typing (AIDRT): A No-Code Physics-Augmented Machine-Learning Workflow for Carbonate Rock Typing and Static-To-Dynamic Property Prediction
container-title: ADIPEC
727c7415ff84c95106f61fe038cce60407a1ef65.abstract: Abstract Carbonate rock typing requires connecting the pore-throat network (PorThN) and geological lithofacies description with porosity, permeability, capillary pressure, wettability, and relative permeability across multiple scales, from nano-, micro-, and macro-scales with core image and plug scales to log scale in feet, and finally to reservoir-model scales. This paper presents AI Digital Rock Typing (AIDRT), a no-code, physics-augmented workflow that builds that connection while keeping observations, predictions, calibrations, uncertainty, validation evidence, and expert approval distinct. AIDRT organizes image and tabular evidence through Machine Learning Image Processing and Recognition (MLIR), which identifies Controllable Measurable Volume (CMV) with descriptors as part of the Morphology Decoder process, and integrates 3D Carbonate Heterogeneous Permeability (kHeC), Permeability-linked Capillary Pressure Function (P-Function), wettability-sensitive relative-permeability analysis with pore-throat Deformation Factor (df), and the digital Rock Typing Carbonate Morphology chart (DRT-CAMO). The workflow registers sample scale and provenance, derives pore- and mineral-related evidence, evaluates the pore-throat network, estimates local and aggregated permeability, constructs capillary-pressure and flow-function hypotheses, and transfers candidate rock types toward core–log correlation. The AIDRT implementation completed all software tests and demonstrates traceable project artifacts, validation, and uncertainty views. These results verify the tested workflow behavior with the bundled synthetic table and image. Eqs. (1) - (9) remain the dependable AIDRT workflow formulation. AIDRT's principal contribution is therefore a reviewable evidence-to-reservoir-model chain in which petrophysicists, geologists, and reservoir engineers can examine the same rock-type decision, preserve its applicability limits, and retain accountable interconnectivity among porosity, permeability, lithology, lithofacies, capillary pressure, wettability, and relative permeability, to produce carbonate rock types and their reservoir static and dynamic petrophysical properties, all in one place.

title: RANCANG BANGUN SISTEM INFORMASI MANAJEMEN TOKO RITEL BERBASIS AI UNTUK PREDIKSI PERMINTAAN DAN REKOMENDASI PEMESANAN BARANG
container-title: Simtek : jurnal sistem informasi dan teknik komputer
b1a24950e0848616c9845895e41f1733b3098d24.abstract: Ketidakpastian permintaan dalam pengelolaan persediaan toko ritel dapat menyebabkan stockout maupun overstock. Penelitian ini membangun sistem informasi manajemen toko ritel yang mengintegrasikan pengelolaan transaksi dan stok dengan prediksi permintaan serta rekomendasi pemesanan barang. Sistem dikembangkan dengan metode Waterfall, sedangkan modul prediksi menggunakan kerangka CRISP-DM untuk membandingkan XGBoost dan Holt-Winters, lalu memilih model dengan MAE terendah pada setiap produk. Safety stock dan reorder point dihitung dari data historis penjualan, sedangkan jumlah saran pesanan berasal dari prediksi 14 hari. Dataset sintetis periode September 2025–Agustus 2026 mencakup 20 produk, 5 pemasok, dan 10.886 transaksi. Rata-rata MAPE XGBoost sebesar 36,07% dan Holt-Winters 35,56%, sehingga kinerja keduanya relatif setara. Black Box Testing terhadap 35 skenario menunjukkan seluruh fungsi berjalan sesuai rancangan. Pengujian pada data transaksi riil diperlukan pada penelitian selanjutnya.

title: A Critical Analysis of AI from the Perspective of the Philosophy of Science among Grade X Students at SMA Don Bosco Padang
container-title: Journal of Multidisciplinary Science: MIKAILALSYS
78e1e5475c4f3b6cf9f26befe44e5548f4ddcce2.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) facilitates access to information in education, increasing the importance of critically evaluating claims and their underlying assumptions. This study examined Grade 10 students’ ability to distinguish facts, opinions, and values in AI-related information at SMA Don Bosco Padang from a philosophy of science perspective. A descriptive quantitative approach was employed involving 33 students. Data were collected through a 15-item written test comprising five items each for fact, opinion, and value identification. Descriptive analysis examined frequencies, percentages of correct responses, score distributions, and classification error patterns. Across 495 responses, 337 were correct and 158 were incorrect, yielding an overall accuracy of 68.08%. Accuracy was highest for opinion identification (76.36%), followed by fact identification (67.88%) and value identification (60.00%). Value identification presented the greatest difficulty, with an error rate of 40.00%. These findings reveal descriptive differences in students’ classification performance, particularly their greater difficulty recognizing values within AI-related information. From a philosophy of science perspective, the results underscore the relevance of epistemology for evaluating evidence and the justification of claims, alongside axiology for recognizing ethical considerations. The study provides contextual evidence to inform AI literacy instruction that integrates information verification, critical reasoning, and ethical reflection to support responsible technology use.

title: INTEGRASI GENERATIVE VIDEO DALAM WORKFLOW PRODUKSI VFX FILM PENDEK “SPLIT//SECOND”
container-title: VOCATIONAL: Jurnal Inovasi Pendidikan Kejuruan
0ec57bf51ada7f1be718f5b1197573476a30b8e0.abstract: The rapid advancement of generative video technology presents novel opportunities for visual effects (VFX) asset generation, yet full reliance on artificial intelligence often creates visual inconsistencies, reduced artistic control, and integration barriers with live-action footage. This article aims to analyze the integration of generative video into the VFX post-production workflow of the short film “SPLIT//SECOND” and evaluate its effectiveness relative to conventional computer-generated imagery (CGI) practices. Employing a practice-based research methodology, the production applied a hybrid workflow where live-action footage serves as the physical reality anchor while artificial intelligence assets construct surreal virtual reality (VR) elements. Empirical results demonstrate that generative video substantially accelerates visual asset acquisition with up to 95% time efficiency, reducing manual tasks from 60–90 minutes to approximately 30 seconds to 3 minutes. Although it eliminates manual modeling labor, this method does not remove the essential requirements of digital compositing, rotoscoping, tracking, and color matching, while also introducing variable operating costs driven by platform credit consumption. ABSTRAK Perkembangan teknologi generative video membuka peluang baru dalam penyediaan aset visual effects (VFX), namun penggunaannya secara mandiri kerap memicu kendala konsistensi visual, penurunan kontrol artistik, dan hambatan integrasi dengan rekaman live-action. Artikel ini bertujuan menganalisis integrasi generative video dalam workflow produksi VFX pada film pendek “SPLIT//SECOND” serta membandingkan efektivitasnya dengan pendekatan computer-generated imagery (CGI) konvensional. Penciptaan karya menerapkan metode practice-based research melalui hybrid workflow yang menempatkan rekaman live-action sebagai jangkar realitas fisik dan elemen berbasis kecerdasan buatan (artificial intelligence / AI) sebagai pembangun dunia virtual reality (VR). Pengujian empiris membuktikan bahwa pemanfaatan generative video mampu mempercepat penyediaan aset visual secara signifikan dengan efisiensi waktu mencapai 95%, yakni dari durasi manual sekitar 60–90 menit menjadi hanya 30 detik hingga 3 menit. Kendati memangkas tahapan teknis permodelan manual, pendekatan ini tidak mengeliminasi kebutuhan digital compositing, rotoscoping, tracking, dan color matching, serta menimbulkan konsekuensi beban biaya variabel berbasis konsumsi credits.

title: AI translation sounds convincing, but it can be riddled with hidden errors
A Smart Insole-Based Explainable AI Framework for Non-Invasive Sciatica Diagnosis Using Optimally Selected Plantar Force Sensors
44867e825acf1cdcc9b18ad253e5851e1983b666.abstract: Abstract Sciatica is a neuropathic disorder that can cause significant alterations in lower-limb biomechanics, including gait asymmetry and abnormal plantar force distribution. This study proposes a wearable, explainable artificial intelligence (XAI)-based framework for automated sciatica diagnosis using optimally selected force-sensitive resistor (FSR) sensors integrated into a smart insole. A dataset of 37 subjects, comprising 20 patients with Sciatica and 17 healthy subjects, was acquired using 16 FSR sensors, with eight sensors positioned on each foot, along with concurrent electromyography (EMG) and inertial measurement unit (IMU) data. From the bilateral plantar force signals, 601 biomechanical features were extracted, incorporating statistical, temporal, magnitude, and inter-limb asymmetry characteristics. A K-fold combinatorial sensor-selection strategy identified the optimal sensor configuration, with K = 5 providing the most stable performance. The optimal configurations, L2, L5, L8 for the left foot and R2, R5, R8 for the right foot, reduced the number of sensors from 16 to 6, representing a 62.5% reduction in sensing hardware. The selected left-foot sensors achieved 96% accuracy, 96% precision, 93% recall, 94% F1-score, and 0.93 AUC, while the right-foot sensors achieved 87% accuracy, 83% precision, 76% recall, 79% F1-score, and 0.91 AUC. Using the six optimally selected sensors, the proposed one-dimensional convolutional neural network (1D-CNN) achieved 90.3% classification accuracy, 89.9% sensitivity, 90.3% specificity, and a ROC-AUC of 0.911. Furthermore, XAI-based plantar heatmaps confirmed the contribution of the selected biomechanical regions to the classification decision. Cross-validation against the concurrent EMG/IMU modality achieved 85.2% accuracy, with approximately 81.5% diagnostic agreement between the force-sensor and EMG/IMU models. The quantitative results demonstrate that a substantially reduced FSR sensor configuration can preserve diagnostically relevant biomechanical information while providing accurate, interpretable, and portable sciatica screening. The proposed framework offers potential for low-cost wearable gait assessment and automated clinical decision support.

title: Human-AI Collaboration in Urban Digital Transformation: Balancing Efficiency and Human Values in Shanghai’s AI-Enabled Talent Recruitment
container-title: Digital Technologies Research and Applications
99b2a4d2edc2dc8df689bff6b515848affbe723a.abstract: In the context of the urban digital revolution, recruitment through AI technologies has become common practice to address competition in the labor market. However, it is still unclear how the effectiveness of such recruitment is connected with humanistic values. For this research, an exploratory qualitative research design was used, involving semi-structured interviews with eight human resource professionals in Shanghai. Based on the results, the use of AI in recruitment led to increased efficiency mainly when screening candidates through high-volume, standardized processes, although the promised efficiency was not delivered in practice because the introduction of the AI system increased the workload. Patterns of human-machine cooperation were observed in different companies: tech companies and foreign companies are inclined to adopt interactive adjustment approaches, while state-owned enterprises retain human-dominated decision-making. Transparency of algorithms was still lacking in numerous instances, and there was an asymmetry in the accountability framework of algorithms, wherein disobeying algorithms carries more personal consequences than obeying them. The more experienced professionals became more autonomous in their work, while the less experienced professionals depended more on the algorithm. Issues like management support, information accuracy, and departmental integration have a major impact on implementation. This study contributes to the theory of human-machine collaboration by proposing the concept of asymmetric algorithmic accountability, which captures the uneven distribution of organizational consequences for following versus overriding AI recommendations and shapes practitioner behavior in ways that extend beyond individual trust or algorithmic transparency.

title: Interfacial Schottky-barrier-assisted optoelectronic resistive switching and synaptic plasticity in ITO/BiFeO3/ZnO/BiFeO3/Ag heterostructure memristors
container-title: Applied Physics Letters
4343ceeed4e89b2d5df01c8755ddf0cf98f49e3c.abstract: An ITO/BiFeO3/ZnO/BiFeO3/Ag heterostructure memristor was fabricated by magnetron sputtering and post-annealing to investigate Schottky-barrier-assisted resistive switching and synaptic plasticity. Structural characterization confirms the formation of a compact BiFeO3/ZnO/BiFeO3 multilayer film with nanocrystalline morphology and distinct ZnO and BiFeO3 phases. The device exhibits stable bipolar resistive switching, and illumination enhances the resistance-state separation by modulating carrier concentration and oxygen-vacancy-related defect states. Transport analysis indicates Ohmic conduction at low bias, while Schottky emission dominates the higher-bias region, revealing the important role of BiFeO3/ZnO interfacial barriers. The switching behavior is primarily associated with oxygen-vacancy-assisted conductive pathway formation and rupture, while reversible Schottky barrier modulation at the heterointerfaces further regulates carrier transport. Furthermore, illumination- and pulse-interval-dependent long-term potentiation and depression are demonstrated, revealing optically tunable synaptic plasticity. These results suggest that the BiFeO3/ZnO/BiFeO3 heterostructure provides an effective platform for optoelectronic memristors and artificial synaptic devices.

title: From AI readiness to regenerative tourism orientation: a tourist-centric model of smart tourism villages
container-title: ABAC Journal
600067ed573dc780c1bd155c47ed81d59d2f7b38.abstract: Purpose This study develops and validates a tourist-centric model of AI-driven smart tourism villages (AI-DSTV), explaining how perceived digital infrastructure and smart governance relate to tourist acceptance and perceived regenerative tourism orientation (PRTO) through rural authenticity, value co-creation, AI trust, and perceived service value. Design/methodology/approach A cross-sectional survey involved 686 domestic tourists who had experienced an AI-supported tourism touchpoint in rural tourism settings in Indonesia. The sample was predominantly young and digitally engaged, with 75.1% aged 18–24 and 68.4% students. The model was tested using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) with 10,000 bootstrap resamples and importance-performance map analysis (IPMA). Findings All 12 hypothesized relationships were significant. Rural authenticity strongly enhanced perceived AI service value, while tourist value co-creation strengthened AI trust and ethical acceptance. Digital infrastructure and smart governance also showed significant downstream effects through authenticity–service-value and co-creation–trust pathways. The model explained 56.3% of PRTO variance. IPMA identified AI trust and ethical acceptance as the most important antecedent of PRTO and the lowest-performing construct, indicating a key managerial priority. Practical implications Rural destinations should prioritize transparent, culturally grounded, participatory and locally accountable AI systems. Strengthening ethical trust, co-creation, and culturally appropriate personalization may offer greater managerial leverage than technological sophistication alone. Originality/value The study extends technology-adoption research beyond behavioral acceptance by introducing PRTO as a tourist-level psychological outcome. It conceptualizes AI-DSTV as a socio-technical ecosystem linking destination readiness with authenticity, co-creation, trust and service evaluation while distinguishing regenerative orientation from verified destination regeneration.

title: Generative Inverse Design of Shell Metamaterials through Continuous-Latent Conditional Flow Matching
29d4141b48d61843e953cf6048d027f8417e5f4f.abstract: Abstract Mechanical metamaterials derive programmable properties from a repeated unit cell’s geometry. A stress–strain curve summarizesa three-dimensional shell geometry in a few numbers, so distinct geometries can share a curve and the inversemap from curve to geometry is one-to-many. We develop a continuous-latent conditional flow-matching framework thatdesigns periodic shell unit cells for prescribed compressive responses. Each shell geometry is a continuous periodic function,and a function encoder learns a basis that compresses it into 32 coefficients. Conditional flow matching learns theresponse-conditioned coefficient distribution and generates many candidate geometries. On 200 held-out targets, our 5.9-million-parameter model reaches a mean best-of-20 NRMSE of 0.074 at 73% validity, against 0.118 and 48% for a 40-million-parameter tokenized-diffusion baseline. Sampling requires 26.8 ms per candidate versus 2.03 s for the baseline.Finite-element analysis of 981 shortlisted candidates yields a mean best-design NRMSE of 0.092, compared with a simulationto-simulation reproducibility of 0.016–0.063.

title: Prolonged visual-motor dual-task effects on dynamic stability in children with ADHD subtypes
container-title: Scientific Reports
9762eafa8c68e4750d2b0d37344fa16ffb0895ee.abstract: Abstract Research on dynamic stability in children with Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) has predominantly relied on short-term laboratory paradigms, limiting understanding of how prolonged task demands affect gait stability. This study investigated the effects of prolonged visual-motor dual-task walking on gait stability across ADHD subtypes. Fifty-seven children (7–10 years) participated: 19 with the combined subtype (ADHD-C), 17 with the predominantly inattentive (ADHD-I), and 21 typically developing peers. Participants walked on a treadmill at self-selected speeds for three minutes under four visual conditions (no target, fixation, saccade, and smooth pursuit). Group-by-visual condition effects on Margin of Stability (MOS) and its coefficient of variation (CV) were analyzed via mixed-model ANOVA (α = 0.05). Typically developing children exhibited larger MOS and lower CV than both ADHD groups across most conditions. However, children with ADHD-C achieved stability levels comparable to typically developing children during fixation, whereas children with ADHD-I remained less stable across conditions. Smooth pursuit was associated with the lowest stability in both ADHD subtypes. Saccades and fixation conditions were associated with greater stability consistency, with saccades showing the lowest variability. Distinct patterns of stability were observed across ADHD subtypes and visual-task conditions. Prolonged visual-motor dual-task walking revealed subtype-specific patterns of gait stability in children with ADHD. These findings suggest that visual-task demands may differentially influence gait stability across ADHD subtypes and highlight the importance of considering visual-attentional demands when examining locomotor control in this population.

title: High Use, Low Preparation
container-title: American Journal of Physical Medicine & Rehabilitation
cd596e36835769e8c758e2939412febb985e5034.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (Gen-AI) has rapidly entered clinical environments, posing a risk of “cognitive offloading” that may impede the development of independent clinical judgment. This study conducted a cross-sectional survey of residents, fellows, and faculty at a large academic medical center in January 2026 to quantify Gen-AI utilization and perceptions in physical medicine and rehabilitation (PM&R) to inform curriculum development. Thirty-six trainees (95% response rate) and 11 faculty members (30% response rate) completed the survey; 43 (91.5%) reported any Gen-AI use and formed the analytic sample. Among users, 72.1% used Gen-AI daily for clinical learning and 51.2% during patient encounters, yet 67.4% were self-taught and only 7.0% always requested citations. Trainees requested citations more often than faculty ( P =.048), while faculty more often relied on clinical judgment without additional verification (62.5% vs. 25.7%, P =.089). Gen-AI-derived evidence was rarely surfaced in teaching: 60.5% discussed it during case presentations rarely or never, and only 16.2% always disclosed its origin. Residents are integrating Gen-AI into clinical workflows at rates that outpace faculty familiarity, while verification remains largely undiscussed and untaught. These gaps highlight an urgent need for structured Gen-AI curricula in PM&R residency.
