title: Trust in artificial intelligence and AI-assisted social and civic decision-making among Arab youth: evidence from Egypt, Kuwait, and the UAE
container-title: Frontiers in Sociology
9c22c48dec77add12e18981832964c2f183e35aa.abstract: Introduction Trust in artificial intelligence (AI) increasingly shapes how young people evaluate information and public issues, yet evidence from Arab contexts remains limited. This study examined the socio-technical correlates of trust in AI and its association with AI-assisted social and civic decision-making among digitally engaged youth in Egypt, Kuwait, and the United Arab Emirates. Methods A cross-sectional online survey was conducted with 1,023 respondents aged 18–35 recruited through purposive, non-probability sampling. Confirmatory factor analysis (CFA), structural equation modeling (SEM), multi-group CFA, and competing full- versus partial-mediation models evaluated measurement and structural relationships. Results The partially mediated model fit significantly better than the fully mediated model, Δχ2(5) = 55.66, p &lt; 0.001. Institutional confidence (β = 0.303), AI literacy (β = 0.281), perceived usefulness (β = 0.242), and social influence (β = 0.107) were positively associated with trust in AI, and perceived risk was negatively associated (β = −0.106; all p &lt; 0.001). Trust was positively associated with AI-assisted decision-making (β = 0.412, p &lt; 0.001). Significant indirect associations through trust were observed for all five antecedents, while the direct perceived-risk path to AI-assisted decision-making was nonsignificant. Multi-group CFA supported metric and practical scalar measurement invariance across the three countries. Discussion The findings support a socio-technical account of AI trust in which technological, cognitive, institutional, and social conditions jointly relate to AI-assisted decision-making, with trust functioning as a central but not exclusive pathway. Given the cross-sectional, purposive design, findings are interpreted as associations rather than causal or nationally representative effects.

title: A preliminary design framework for human-friendly AI interaction: grounded in anthropomorphism
container-title: Frontiers in Computer Science
46e7d698557d6ad9c8af0e26c30db1eac6a6fb1b.abstract: People converse with AI as they would with friends in daily life, collaborate with it, and form personalized relationships. In response to these emerging forms of interaction, this study clarifies the concept of Human-Friendly Interaction with conversational AI and develops the Human-Friendly AI Interaction Design Framework (HFAI-DF). This study positions anthropomorphism, a foundational phenomenon in human–AI interaction, as a theoretical bridge and reviews literature on anthropomorphism theory and related research on human cognition. On this basis, this study interpretively derives and organizes how anthropomorphism-inducing stimuli can be applied to AI agents, systematizing them into 30 AI behavioral items that enable human-friendly interaction. Subsequently, a survey was conducted and exploratory factor analysis performed to identify six dimensions as a preliminary structure for a design framework for AI’s human-friendly interaction. These dimensions are: Self-Aware Interaction, User-Adaptive Responsiveness Interaction, Context-Aware Reasoning Interaction, Socio-Emotional Interaction, Creative Collaboration Interaction, and Proactive Assistance Interaction. Within the evolving AI research landscape focused on interaction, this study extends the human-centered AI concept toward human-friendly interaction that operates in an organic manner comparable to human–human conversation, grounded in an understanding of human cognitive functioning. The proposed framework provides both AI providers and designers with an initial structure for shaping and improving the quality of human-friendly interaction.

title: Perceptions of AI in veterinary medicine: insights from students, faculty, and practicing veterinarians in Hong Kong
container-title: Frontiers in Veterinary Science
d5c0bfa269240bf48c6ea87f212741cd8f464ca1.abstract: Introduction As artificial intelligence (AI) transforms veterinary medicine, understanding stakeholder perceptions is crucial for its effective and responsible integration. To support the development of targeted educational and policy initiatives, this study aimed to evaluate the knowledge, attitudes, and practices regarding AI among Bachelor of Veterinary Medicine (BVM) students, PhD students, faculty, and practicing veterinarians in Hong Kong. Methods A cross-sectional online survey was conducted between December 2023 and March 2024 among BVM students, PhD students, and faculty members at City University of Hong Kong, and practicing veterinarians in Hong Kong who are members of the Hong Kong Veterinary Association. The survey assessed participants’ familiarity with AI, prior training, perceived benefits, concerns, and willingness to adopt AI in education and clinical practice. Descriptive and comparative analyses were performed to examine differences across stakeholder groups. Results Of 79 complete responses, nearly half (46.8%) reported unfamiliarity with AI concepts. Only 17.7% had received formal AI training, although 78.5% expressed interest in future AI education. Most respondents agreed that AI could enhance veterinary teaching and practice (83.5%) and 81.0% indicated they would likely incorporate AI tools into their work. Key perceived benefits included support for case-based learning (83.5%), virtual animal models for teaching (77.2%), and improved diagnostic accuracy (74.7%). However, 41.8% felt inadequately prepared to use AI. Major concerns included veterinarian accountability for AI-related harms (79.7%), lack of system flexibility (75.9%), and potential clinical inaccuracies (70.9%). Descriptively, practicing veterinarians reported the lowest AI tool use (66.7% had never used AI tools), the lowest preparedness (66.7% felt unprepared), and lower agreement with AI’s clinical benefits, although attitude differences were not statistically significant. Conclusion These exploratory findings suggest gaps in self-reported AI knowledge and differing perceptions of AI across veterinary stakeholder groups in Hong Kong, with AI use already widespread at the time of the survey despite limited formal training. While enthusiasm for AI integration is high, concerns about preparedness, accuracy, and ethical responsibility remain. Larger, multi-institutional studies are needed to confirm these patterns and to inform targeted training programs and ethical frameworks for safe and effective AI adoption in veterinary medicine.

title: Global classrooms: a tri-national study on AI integration by higher education students
container-title: Frontiers in Computer Science
4ce5be4917c40263b11f6c7ca8eabe77dd89211a.abstract: Collaborative cross-cultural learning expands higher education students’ (HES’) intercultural and language awareness, enhances their intercultural competence, has an impact on attitudes towards technology and AI as well as towards the course design and general satisfaction with the collaborative experience in the course. Furthermore, their self-perceived role in a digital setting and their self-perceived English proficiency were measured. The CoGIH Project encourages HES to explore the educational potential of artificial intelligence (AI) for learning and teaching in the school setting. A special focus is on the impact AI might have on the language learning process in English as a lingua franca in a multilingual setting. N = 113 HES, including both pre-service and in-service teachers as well as students preparing for educational administration, from five institutions in Israel, Germany, and Hungary collaborated in 14 international groups, representing five higher education institutions; n = 91 answered the questionnaires. Each group investigated the educational potential of a specific AI application and developed an AI-supported, results-based webpage. The study employed a multi-method research design. Questionnaires were administered to the HES to investigate their experiences at the beginning and at the end of the course. While quantitative data were used to investigate the research through the lens of descriptive statistics and correlations between factors, qualitative data from the open questions were analysed to enable a deeper understanding of HES’ perceptions, experiences and meanings, as well as their critical thinking. The study highlighted strengths and challenges in using AI for educational purposes. The HES valued clear structures, logical navigation, and creative, motivating tasks. Simultaneously, recurring issues included incomplete translations, limited depth of critical reflection, and weaknesses in visual design. In sum, even though AI can support creativity and language learning and teaching, individual learners’ reflections and authentic teacher guidance remain indispensable for meaningful learning.

title: P2-VGAN: a lightweight velocity-weighted graph attention network for privacy-conscious edge anomaly detection
container-title: Frontiers in Artificial Intelligence
76c7345c8fd139e3ac90e2e10cd36d5a162fde2d.abstract: Introduction Two persistent challenges hinder intelligent video surveillance in public spaces: dense pixel-based models incur heavy computational costs on edge infrastructure, and continuous capture of identifiable imagery creates substantial visual privacy liabilities. Skeleton-based pipelines, which abstract each video frame into articulated landmark coordinates, support visual data minimization by discarding appearance information. However, conventional graph backbones weight joint trajectories uniformly across time, frequently confusing benign high-speed locomotion (such as sprinting for transit) with violent anomalies. Methods This paper presents the Privacy-Conscious Velocity-Weighted Graph Attention Network (P2-VGAN; the prefix “P2” is retained as a legacy identifier designating privacy-conscious representation rather than a cryptographic guarantee), an efficient framework engineered for desktop-class CPU edge gateways. The pipeline decouples motion analysis from visual appearance by extracting 33 planar body landmarks via a single-shot pose estimator; the application does not intentionally store or transmit decoded RGB frames after pose extraction, ensuring downstream processing operates strictly on appearance-reduced pose coordinates. The primary contribution is the Velocity-Weighted Attention Mechanism (VW-AM), an ultra-lightweight gating module requiring only two shared parameters that converts inter-frame coordinate displacements into a bounded squared-displacement motion proxy. This proxy modulates node features prior to multi-head graph attention, directing message passing toward rapidly moving limbs while damping near-stationary joints. Trained under a weakly supervised Multiple Instance Learning objective with temporal smoothness and sparsity regularizers, P2-VGAN is evaluated across five random seeds on the ShanghaiTech Campus and a human-centric subset of UCF-Crime. Results On ShanghaiTech, the model achieves a frame-level AUC of 84.72 ± 0.28% with 1.81 M downstream trainable parameters (pose-extractor parameters excluded) and sustains 34.01 frames per second (FPS) on an Intel Core i7-10700 CPU without hardware acceleration. When compared directly with an identical Vanilla GAT backbone without gating (83.14 ± 0.39%), VW-AM provides an unconfounded +1.58% absolute AUC gain ( p = 0.00096). On the human-centric UCF-Crime subset (215 test videos), it attains 77.88 ± 0.35% micro-average AUC, with high-motion categories (Fighting, Assault) exceeding 82% AUC. Stepwise ablations document an incremental +2.52% gain from VW-AM over an adaptive ST-GCN baseline. Discussion We position P2-VGAN as a Pareto-efficient framework for lightweight CPU surveillance, acknowledging that coordinate streams reduce visual surface exposure but do not eliminate biometric gait re-identification.

title: AI-generated advertising in agricultural livestreaming and the auditability of disclosure regulation: a three-layer audit of public Douyin data from China
container-title: Frontiers in Sustainable Food Systems
c177ed750eb610123bd142c9d637834496b25555.abstract: Agricultural products are credence goods, and in livestreaming, the grower’s visible presence signals the price. China has required labeling of deep-synthesis content since January 2023 and, since 1 September 2025, of AI-generated synthetic content. Whether public platform data can verify compliance in a market where the authenticity premium is especially salient remains unclear, given that growers themselves sell produce. We audited three layers of public Chinese platform data: 189 policy snippets, 19 accounts retrieved by AI technical terms, and 455 unique authors retrieved by crop names. In the one policy coding field with complete intercoder agreement ( κ = 1.000), only 6 of 189 snippets name authenticity as a farmer asset. Retrieval by technical terms returns intermediaries: 13 of 19 accounts sell AI tools or tutorials, and none discloses using AI to sell its own produce. Among AI-announcing cases retrieved by crop-name queries, an expanded text-field detector validated at 94.7% recall flags 10 of 455 authors: seven supply-side or service-provider accounts, one incidental non-agricultural mention, and two product-query artifacts; none discloses grower own-use of AI livestreaming. Checks of API-exposed platform metadata for all 575 video records and cover images for 472 records found no platform-side AI label or visible AI/AIGC/statutory AI-generated notice. AI was announced primarily by accounts that sell, service, or discuss AI, rather than by produce-selling grower accounts. No grower own-use disclosure appears in either audited slice: 0 of 19 technical-keyword accounts and 0 of 455 transaction-query authors. The zero admits two readings that the audited surface cannot separate: smallholders do not use these tools, making the requirement inert for them, or they use them without disclosure. No label-reading instrument applied to the audited surface can decide between them, because such inspection observes announcement rather than use. Platforms and regulators may hold backend data unavailable to an external audit. If the theoretically derived authenticity-penalty mechanism holds, disclosure would impose an uneven cost, falling more heavily on growers than on intermediaries. The observed pattern is consistent with this hypothesis but does not establish it.

title: A Deepfake Detection Framework for Securing Facial Biometrics Using Attention-Based Deep Learning and Blockchain
container-title: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
a0074b87d1d6c79dcfbe609a01fe5bc5a247f1d2.abstract: Facial biometric authentication is widely deployed for identity verification, yet it is increasingly exposed to deepfakebased presentation and injection attacks and to large-scale breaches of centrally stored biometric templates. This paper proposes a deepfake-resilient facial biometric security framework that combines attention-based deep learning with blockchain technology. At registration, face images are pre-processed, augmented with a generative adversarial network (GAN), encoded by a convolutional neural network (CNN) with self-attention, and classified as real or fake by an artificial neural network (ANN). Only images classified as real are encrypted, bound to a unique user identifier and committed to a private blockchain through a cryptographic hash, whereas fake attempts are written to an immutable event log. At authentication, a fresh probe passes through the same pipeline and is verified by smart contracts that check the integrity of the registered commitment and the template similarity using zero-knowledge proofs (ZKPs), so that raw biometric features are never disclosed. We formalise the threat model, specify the architecture, the smart-contract interface and the security properties, and define an evaluation protocol based on the CIPLAB Real and Fake Face Detection and UTKFace datasets that covers detection accuracy, authentication error rates, adversarial robustness, demographic fairness and system overhead. The framework provides a basis for privacy-preserving, auditable and scalable facial authentication in digital identity management, financial services, healthcare and e-governance.

title: STUDY ON FORMULATION, CHARACTERIZATION AND MODIFICATION OF SUSTAINED RELEASE BILAYER MATRIX TABLETS OF PROPRANOLOL HCl AND NIFEDIPINE FOR ANTIHYPERTENSIVE THERAPY
container-title: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
3612c18670ab14e392ce35fe3133554843250140.abstract: Background: Sustained-release (SR) bilayer matrix tablets allow two release segments, or two drugs, to be combined in one dosage unit. Propranolol hydrochloride (BCS class I) and nifedipine (BCS class II) are complementary antihypertensives, but their contrasting solubility makes the design of a shared SR system challenging. Objective: To critically analyse published formulation, characterization and modification data on SR bilayer/matrix tablets of propranolol HCl and SR hydroxypropyl methylcellulose (HPMC) tablets of nifedipine, and to derive an evidence-based design framework for a combined bilayer tablet. Methods: Quantitative data on composition, micromeritics, tablet quality, drug release, swelling, release kinetics, particle size, similarity factor (f2) and bioequivalence were extracted from five key studies. Published dissolution data (HPMC K15M and Kollidon® SR matrices, 1–4 h) were re-analysed using zero-order, first-order, Higuchi, HixsonCrowell and Korsmeyer–Peppas models, and Hausner ratios were derived from reported compressibility indices. Results: In the bilayer propranolol tablet, 20 mg sodium starch glycolate released 99.72% of the loading dose in 10 min, while the SR layer containing 40% HPMC K15M (F9) released 98.41% over 12 h (f2 = 60.5; Peppas n = 0.622; anomalous transport). Re-analysis showed that release from low-polymer matrices was best described by the Higuchi model (R2 ≥ 0.989), whereas higher Kollidon® SR levels gave near-linear release (zero-order R2 = 0.998–0.999). For nifedipine, raw-drug particle size governed release similarity: the batch whose in-tablet D90 (147 µm) matched the reference (150 µm) gave f2 = 78.2 and was bioequivalent under fasting and fed conditions. Conclusion: Polymer grade and level control the propranolol layer, while particle size and solubilisation control the nifedipine layer. A proposed propranolol–nifedipine bilayer composition and a characterization protocol are presented for experimental verification.

title: A TiVCrMoC3 MXene-Based Sustained-Release Vancomycin Nanoplatform Mitigates Septic Arthritis through Modulation of Bacterial Acetate Metabolism
container-title: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces
8c2c9a0eab8536d613f1a5ae3c8532450e3fff90.abstract: Abstract Acute septic arthritis caused by bacterial infection is a common and serious orthopedic disease. The formation of bacterial biofilms severely limits antibiotic penetration, rendering conventional therapy ineffective and short‑acting. In this study, we developed a novel nanodrug delivery system by loading vancomycin onto high‑entropy TiVCrMoC3 MXene (VCM@NPs). Featuring a sheet‑like porous structure, this material enables efficient drug loading via electrostatic interactions and sustains release in the weakly acidic infection microenvironment, achieving a cumulative release of 67% over 20 days. In vitro, VCM@NPs exhibited potent bactericidal activity against Staphylococcus aureus, with complete colony eradication by day 5, and markedly disrupted biofilm architecture, as shown by electron and confocal microscopy. In a rat septic arthritis model, a single intra‑articular injection of VCM@NPs effectively inhibited bacterial growth, alleviated joint inflammation, and improved cartilage and bone damage. By day 10, OARSI scores in the VCM@NPs group were significantly lower than those in the free vancomycin group, and micro‑CT analysis revealed increased bone volume and trabecular thickness, confirming sustained therapeutic efficacy. Notably, mass spectrometry imaging demonstrated that VCM@NPs reprogrammed the joint metabolic microenvironment by suppressing the bacterial acetate metabolic pathway, thereby destabilizing biofilms—a mechanism that, to the best of our knowledge, has not been previously reported in the context of nanoparticle-mediated modulation of this pathway. Collectively, this study offers a new nanodrug delivery strategy that integrates sustained release with biofilm disruption, holding promise for clinical translation in septic arthritis.

title: Human-Governed Multi-Agent AI for Biological Hypothesis Generation: An Evidence-Grounded Framework Using JUMP Cell Painting Profiles
7a2bcb64973bd56bae183bb619c26a0d3a9a5a47.abstract: Abstract High-dimensional cellular phenotypes can motivate biological hypotheses, but similarity alone cannot establish mechanism or causal validity. DISCOVERY-AGENT links exploratory JUMP Cell Painting evidence with evidence-grounded hypothesis generation, independent critique and bounded human-review routing. An initial 65-record CRISPR/ORF analysis across nine gene–modality tests found four FDR-significant CRISPR plate-level associations (AKT1, BRCA1, MTOR and TP53), none among evaluated ORF genes. A distinct later cross-source compound-identity benchmark used 614 morphological features and achieved AUROC 0.6142 on 1,250 held-out compounds with training-only preprocessing; this is identity discrimination, not mechanism-of-action classification. Three structured hypotheses underwent LLM critique and revision, while eleven gene-pair evidence assessments yielded no FDR-significant mechanistic finding (minimum q = 0.2037). Archived governance checks passed 1,021/1,021 predefined tests; nevertheless, the initial live-agent run contained two execution errors among five cases, with both cases responding on fresh retest. These findings demonstrate feasibility of auditable evidence processing and modest cross-source morphology signal, not validated autonomous discovery, prospective safety, or completed expert review. The work delineates practical requirements for independent biological validation and reproducible scientific agents.

title: An attention-enhanced CNN-BiLSTM framework with confidence-gated inference for arrhythmia detection using ECG signals
container-title: Discover Computing
44feadb188256eccd1812c299d06ca2b1bdc38f0.abstract: Abstract Automated arrhythmia detection from electrocardiogram (ECG) signals is essential for early diagnosis and continuous cardiac monitoring. However, accurate classification remains challenging due to complex temporal dependencies in ECG waveforms and severe class imbalance, where clinically significant arrhythmias are underrepresented. To address these challenges, we propose an Attention-Enhanced CNN–BiLSTM framework with a Confidence-Gated Inference mechanism for ECG-based arrhythmia detection. The proposed model integrates a one-dimensional convolutional neural network (1D-CNN) to capture local morphological features with a Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (BiLSTM) network to model long-range temporal dependencies in ECG signals. A temporal attention mechanism is employed to focus on diagnostically relevant segments of the signal. Additionally, a confidence-gated inference strategy is introduced to improve prediction reliability, particularly for minority classes. An extensive ablation study across 18 configurations is conducted to evaluate the contribution of temporal modeling, attention, and inference strategies. On the MIT-BIH Arrhythmia Database, the proposed model achieves an accuracy of 96.58% and a macro-F1 score of 86.05%. To ensure an unbiased evaluation free of test-set leakage, we further adopt a strict protocol in which all hyperparameters ( $$\gamma$$ , $$\tau$$ ) are selected exclusively on a held-out validation set; under this leakage-free protocol the model attains an accuracy of 96.74% and a macro-F1 score of 86.54% on the untouched test set. These findings demonstrate that integrating attention-driven temporal modeling with calibrated inference yields efficient arrhythmia classification on the MIT-BIH benchmark.

title: Teachers’ attitudes and behavioural intentions towards AI integration in Chinese higher education: a qualitative interview study
container-title: Frontiers in Psychology
c6fe4330bbf5fd4fe3ac0771cb768c511236b747.abstract: Introduction The rapid expansion of generative AI has intensified scholarly and policy debate over its role in higher education, yet university teachers’ attitudes towards its integration remain complex and context-dependent. This study explores how university teachers perceive, experience, and respond to AI integration in their teaching. Guided primarily by the three-component attitude model and informed by the technology acceptance model and the theory of planned behaviour, the study examines cognitive appraisals, affective responses, behavioural intentions, and perceived support needs. Methods The study draws on semi-structured interviews with 14 university teachers from four higher education institutions in China. The interview data were analysed using codebook-informed thematic analysis combining deductive and inductive coding. Results The findings indicate that teachers generally perceive AI as a supportive rather than substitutive educational tool, valuing it for improving efficiency, supporting lesson preparation, and enriching pedagogical design. Emotional responses varied from enthusiasm and a sense of accomplishment to caution, neutrality, and, in some cases, declining satisfaction. Across the interviews, teachers’ primary concerns centred less on their own replacement than on the perceived risks of inappropriate AI use for students’ independent thinking, reasoning, originality, and authentic understanding. Teachers’ intentions to adopt AI were therefore conditional and bounded, shaped by pedagogical purpose, disciplinary context, student readiness, and the need to maintain teacher control. Teachers also emphasised that sustainable AI integration requires more than general encouragement, calling instead for AI literacy development, discipline-sensitive support, specialised tools, and enabling institutional infrastructure. Discussion Overall, these findings extend contextual understandings of teachers’ AI acceptance by showing how adoption intentions are pedagogically negotiated and highlight the importance of supporting professional judgement and students’ independent thinking in higher education.

title: Automated assessment of healthcare de-escalation communication skills in a conversational AI virtual reality simulation
container-title: Frontiers in Digital Health
9bc424b8b0ee6bc350b4296b68f692e3f29c8284.abstract: Introduction Digital health training environments increasingly require scalable methods for assessing communication skills in realistic, interactive scenarios. This paper presents a comparative study of automated assessment approaches within a conversational AI virtual reality simulation designed for verbal de-escalation training. Methods A total of 20 nursing students completed the simulation, where their spoken responses were captured and converted to text through a speech-to-text system, and were evaluated across 11 de-escalation competencies. The evaluation compared three fine-tuned deep learning models (BERT, RoBERTa, and XLNet) with a modified RATAS, a rubric-driven framework that leverages large language models. Two experiments were conducted: one using controlled 100-item validation datasets for each section, and another using the real-world responses collected during the user study. Results On the validation datasets, the deep learning models achieved the highest performance, with RoBERTa obtaining an average accuracy of 0.9927, followed by BERT at 0.9900 and XLNet at 0.9790, while RATAS achieved 0.8554. On the student-response dataset, performance decreased for all approaches, with RoBERTa obtaining 0.8590 accuracy, RATAS 0.8181, BERT 0.8000, and XLNet 0.7681. Discussion These results suggest that transformer-based models perform best under controlled conditions, whereas RATAS demonstrated stability in grading across different dataset types. These preliminary findings support the feasibility of integrating deep learning and rubric-driven LLM-based automated assessment approaches for communication and de-escalation training in nursing education.

title: Uneven automation: comparing authorship anxiety and generative AI use among art and design undergraduate students
container-title: Frontiers in Psychology
8942b2ac014d5d2bac7e05011f209f96a5fce870.abstract: Art and design education expects students to develop a sense of authorship over original work, but generative AI (GenAI) complicates how students understand and claim that authorship. This study examined whether these experiences differ across creative fields through a mixed-methods design. The survey included 2,441 GenAI-using students from seven field categories at 33 art and design institutions in China and assessed authorship anxiety, creative agency, perceived usefulness, dependence on GenAI, and frequency of use. The quantitative analysis first examined variation across all seven categories and then compared fine art with the five applied design fields. Interview data from 22 survey participants were also examined thematically. The main findings include that (1) authorship anxiety did not differ significantly across the seven categories or between fine art and pooled design; the latter comparison met the equivalence criterion at ±d = 0.20, but not at tighter bounds; (2) clearer differences emerged in how students used GenAI. Compared with fine-art students, design students considered GenAI more useful and used it more frequently; (3) across the interviews, most students described authorship as retaining control over the creative idea while delegating parts of its execution to GenAI. Specifically, fine-art students often grounded authorship in embodied making and human imperfection, whereas design students placed greater emphasis on judgement, selection, and control. We call this pattern uneven automation: concern about authorship was broadly shared, but students in different fields responded to GenAI in different ways, potentially reflecting the varying labour-market pressures surrounding their disciplines.

title: Digital transformation, traceability, and supply chain resilience in food manufacturing SMEs: a review of AI, blockchain-IoT, and institutional mechanisms
container-title: Frontiers in Sustainable Food Systems
c0821ee379eb16d2e0252633d6030dd152fbd833.abstract: Food supply chains in China face persistent challenges of food safety risks, inadequate transparency, and supply disruptions, with food manufacturing small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) disproportionately vulnerable due to limited resources and non-standardized internal processes. Digital transformation encompassing artificial intelligence (AI), blockchain, Internet of Things (IoT), and digital twin technologies is increasingly regarded as a strategic solution to strengthen supply chain resilience, yet the organizational and institutional conditions under which these digital investments translate into tangible resilience improvements for food manufacturing SMEs remain poorly understood. This review conducts a PRISMA 2020-compliant systematic review and thematic synthesis of 40 multidisciplinary sources spanning the food safety, supply chain management, and information systems literatures. Drawing on Dynamic Capabilities Theory and Institutional Theory, we propose an integrative conceptual framework comprising six research propositions, in which traceability capability acts as a food-safety-specific mediating mechanism linking digital transformation to supply chain resilience, while regulatory stringency moderates the strength of this indirect pathway. A central argument of this framework is that deploying blockchain, IoT, or AI hardware does not itself constitute traceability capability the institutional and organisational conditions under which digital tools are adopted determine whether firms build substantive traceability capability or engage in symbolic compliance without genuine food safety governance improvement. Three key contributions distinguish this framework: conceptualizing traceability capability as a distinct dynamic capability rather than a generic digitalization mechanism; directing analytical focus explicitly toward food manufacturing SMEs, a population largely overlooked in existing large-firm panel studies; and introducing regulatory stringency as a first-stage moderator within a moderated mediation structure. Critical research gaps are identified, including the absence of SME-calibrated digital transformation measurement instruments, the lack of a validated multi-item traceability capability scale, and a complete empirical vacuum for testing the proposed moderated mediation model in food manufacturing SME contexts. This review provides a structured future research agenda for scholars and delivers actionable insights for practitioners and policymakers seeking to direct digital technology investments toward improved food safety governance in China’s food manufacturing sector.

title: Human-in-the-loop semantic learning analytics for assessing moral-value reasoning in university AI ethics education
container-title: Frontiers in Psychology
4c153cd19693204269d4536c8e62024e2ea30575.abstract: Introduction University AI ethics education addresses fairness, privacy, accountability, transparency, human autonomy, and academic integrity, but the semantic structure of students' moral-value reasoning and its connection to responsible solutions remain insufficiently characterized. This study examined a human-in-the-loop semantic learning analytics framework for task-specific moral-value reasoning. Methods Ninety science and engineering graduate students completed an online explicit-reflective AI ethics module in a one-group pre–post multimethod study without a control group. Assessments comprised an AI ethics knowledge test, a perceived-awareness scale, and open-ended ethical reasoning tasks. Expert annotations informed transformer-based multi-label coding, descriptive value coverage and balance metrics, problem–solution coupling, and baseline-only nested cross-validated prediction of subsequent raw problem-solving change. Results Within-participant pre–post increases were observed in ethical knowledge, perceived moral-value awareness, actual ethical awareness, problem–solving skills, value coverage, value balance, and problem–solution coupling. Automated semantic coding achieved participant-grouped cross-validated macro-F1 = 0.83 (95% CI [0.78, 0.87]; micro-F1 = 0.86; macro-AUPRC = 0.82). The baseline-only prediction model yielded cross-validated R 2 = 0.30 (95% CI [0.11, 0.45]) for subsequent raw problem-solving change. Discussion Expert-supervised semantic analytics can characterize value representation and issue–solution reasoning in AI ethics assessments. Coverage and balance describe response structure rather than moral quality. The absence of a control group, repeated use of one scenario, and modest sample size preclude causal and broad trait-level conclusions.

title: Perceived AI literacy and TPACK in pre-service teacher education: mediating roles of perceived usefulness, ease of use, and value in blended learning
container-title: Frontiers in Psychology
1bad51d2ab1c081fcbf1788c8c81f98f9ce0044c.abstract: Background The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into blended learning requires pre-service teachers to develop AI-related competencies and the ability to integrate technology into pedagogy. This study examines how perceived AI literacy and technological pedagogical content knowledge (TPACK) are associated with deep learning through perceived usefulness, perceived ease of use, and perceived value of AI use. Methods A cross-sectional survey was completed by 423 pre-service teachers enrolled in blended learning courses at a university in China. Data were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM), with covariance-based structural equation modeling and fuzzy-set qualitative comparative analysis (fsQCA) used as complementary robustness and configurational analyses. Results Perceived usefulness, perceived ease of use, and perceived value of AI use significantly mediated the relationships between the two competencies and deep learning. All six indirect pathways were significant in both the PLS-SEM and covariance-based SEM analyses. The fsQCA revealed an equifinal and asymmetric structure: multiple, partly substitutable conditions were sufficient for high deep learning, and no single condition was necessary for either high or low deep learning. Conclusions The findings integrate the technology acceptance model and expectancy-value theory to explain how pre-service teachers' competencies and perceptions relate to deep learning in AI-enhanced blended environments. Teacher education should support technical competence alongside positive perceptions of AI's utility, usability, and value. Because the measures were self-reported and collected cross-sectionally at one university, the findings are interpreted as associational and configurational rather than causal.

title: Effectiveness of an AI-Based Educational Video Generator in Enhancing Oral Health Knowledge and Behavior Among Children: A Randomized Controlled Trial
container-title: Al-Rafidain Journal of Medical Sciences ( ISSN 2789-3219 )
025217a90eae33a9efbb4f3e4378042549e3202e.abstract: Background: Artificial intelligence (AI) is a new innovation that presents an opportunity for oral health education in children. Objective: To evaluate the effectiveness of an AI-assisted educational video versus standardized in-person oral health education for children regarding oral health knowledge and behaviors. Methods: This randomized controlled trial included 300 children aged 10-12 years (n=150 per group), both boys and girls, who were divided into AI video and standardized face-to-face oral health education groups. Baseline and 2-week follow-up evaluations were conducted for knowledge scores, four behavioral items, and the Silness and Löe Plaque Index. The internal consistency of the knowledge scale was checked (Cronbach's α=0.79). Wilcoxon signed-rank and Mann–Whitney U tests were the primary non-parametric tests used for statistical evaluations, with a median, (IQR), and effect size r provided. Chi-square tests with a Bonferroni adjustment at α=0.0125 were used to evaluate behavioral items. Results: There were significant enhancements in intra-group knowledge (p<0.0001 for both groups; r=0.663 for AI; r=0.345 for Control). The clinical efficacy was similar for both strategies with significant reduction of intra-group plaque (AI: p< 0.001, r= 0.425; Control: p< 0.001, r= 0.331), but no inter-group difference at the end of the intervention (p= 0.608; r= 0.030). In the conventional group, the utilization of dental floss was significantly improved (p=0.0056), and no other behaviors showed significant improvement across groups. Conclusions: The AI-assisted educational video demonstrated better knowledge retention than the standardized face-to-face oral health education, achieved similar clinical plaque reduction, and can be easily scaled for pediatric preventive dentistry.

title: Analog Spin–Orbit Torque Switching in Vertically Graded Pt/Co–Re Heterostructures for Neuromorphic Computing
container-title: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces
c0f744ce051750bdd55778c9f4dbdc3b3a09ab49.abstract: Abstract Achieving gradual, analog magnetization switching in spin–orbit torque (SOT) devices is essential for neuromorphic computing. In perpendicular magnetic anisotropy (PMA)-based SOT devices, gradual switching can arise from domain nucleation, domain-wall propagation, and pinning, and controlling it through materials design remains a key goal. This study demonstrates that a vertically graded cobalt (Co)–rhenium (Re) alloy region, formed through a simple Co/Re multilayer design, enables analog SOT switching in Pt/Co–Re heterostructures. Microstructural and compositional analyses confirm that annealing transforms the discrete multilayer into a depth-dependent alloy with tunable gradient direction and magnitude, controlled by adjusting the Re layer thickness distribution. Increasing the Co/Re bilayer repetition number up to 3 yields a pronounced sigmoid-like transfer characteristic plausibly explained by the sequential reversal of sub-regions with distributed local switching thresholds, with only a small change in the effective PMA energy. We demonstrate stable, bidirectional long-term potentiation and depression under repeated pulse stimulation across Re compositions of 30–70%. System-level validation using a multilayer perceptron on MNIST (modified National Institute of Standards and Technology) Digits, Fashion-MNIST, and MNIST Characters datasets shows test accuracies within 1.21 percentage points of the ideal sigmoid baseline, with MNIST Digits accuracy varying by 0.24 percentage points across the full compositional range.

title: Improving Learner Performance Through Score Based Analysis on a Gamified AI Driven Cybersecurity Learning Platform
d2b1981b0d01f6ee261a12a86c8c602586119c26.abstract: Abstract This study examines whether structured engagement with instructional content improves learner performance on Cyber Security Academy, an AI-driven, gamified cybersecurity learning platform. Activity logs covering 1,500 completed assessments from users in ten Anglophone and Francophone countries were analyzed by comparing learners who consulted the lessons and completed the full learning pathway (n = 900) with those who engaged only partially with the platform (n = 600). Group differences were tested with Welch's t-test, the Mann Whitney U test, one-way ANOVA, Spearman correlations, and Cohen's d as a measure of effect size. Learners who read the lessons before assessment obtained a mean score of 71.27 % versus 60.41 % for non-readers (Δ = +10.86 points; t(1192) = 12.21; p < 0.001; d = 0.650; 95 % CI [9.12, 12.60]), committed fewer errors (2.50 vs. 4.85; d = -1.069), and responded faster (9.85 vs. 12.69 minutes; d = -0.807), indicating greater fluency of cognitive processing. The effect decreased monotonically with age (d = 1.205 for learners aged 13 and under; d = 0.387 for those 22 and over) and with digital literacy (d = 1.434 for beginners; d = 0.524 for experts), while remaining positive in all ten countries. These findings indicate that structured, AI-personalized, and gamified learning environments substantially enhance cybersecurity learning outcomes, particularly for younger and less experienced users.

title: AI Labour Rights Awareness and Career Adaptation Confidence among Respondents in Bangladesh
4bebd9cda335afcb1b14dbb90e41e4c4857a6c33.abstract: Abstract Artificial intelligence changes both the skills used at work and the conditions under which employment decisions are made. Awareness of these changes does not necessarily coincide with confidence in adapting a career. This study examines that distinction in 385 adult, AI-aware survey records from Bangladesh, including 238 law students and 61 respondents classified as law graduates. Five statements separately assess awareness of workplace rights and responsibilities, recognition of protection from unfair automated decisions, reported complementary skill development, adaptation confidence and the perceived preparedness benefit of understanding labour issues. Analyses combine full response distributions, joint endorsement patterns, paired comparisons, ordinal correlations and an exploratory proportional-odds model. Recognition of the need for protection was endorsed by 79.2%, compared with 48.8% endorsing adaptation confidence, a paired difference of 30.4 percentage points (95% bootstrap interval 23.9–36.6). General rights awareness and skill development had small positive ordinal associations with confidence. In the adjusted ordinal model, their odds ratios were 1.30 (95% interval 1.04–1.61; Holm p = 0.038) and 1.40 (1.09–1.79; Holm p = 0.024) respectively. The protection-recognition estimate was less certain, although the two awareness coefficients were not demonstrably different. The findings distinguish rights recognition, reported action and confidence rather than establish a causal awareness-to-adaptability pathway. They support evaluating legal-literacy education alongside practical career tasks and institutional safeguards. The mixed sample, study-specific single items, undocumented recruitment and fieldwork dates, and source-documentation limitations constrain inference. A subsequent study should use verified graduate eligibility, independent legal-knowledge assessments and longitudinal career outcomes.

title: Mode Switching in Two Blue Large-amplitude Pulsators Observed by OGLE, KMTNet, and DREAMS
container-title: The Astrophysical Journal
b67d0469422dbb66fcc676d1faae8a6d42e57d8a.abstract: Abstract Blue large-amplitude pulsators (BLAPs) are rare, hot, short-period pulsating stars whose rapid oscillations provide a unique probe of stellar interiors and atmospheres. In this paper, we study two short-period BLAPs in the Galactic bulge, Optical Gravitational Lensing Experiment (OGLE)-BLAP-142 ( P ≈ 6.6 minutes) and OGLE-BLAP-148 ( P ≈ 7.5 minutes), by combining light curves from the OGLE, KMTNet, and DREAMS surveys, spanning 17 yr with cadences ranging from minutes to hours to days. We perform generalized Lomb–Scargle periodogram analyses of their light curves and identify, for each BLAP, three closely spaced pulsation modes separated by ∼1%. The dominant mode can switch within timescales of order a year, accompanied by a likely blueward color shift (∼0.1–0.2 mag). The yearly period excursions of the resolved mode families imply apparent ∣ P ̇ / P ∣ values of order 10 −6 –10 −4 yr −1 , large enough to mimic or exceed smooth evolutionary period changes. One mode family in OGLE-BLAP-148 shows a coherent decade-long drift at the ∼10 −5 yr −1 level, but its failure to extrapolate to the earliest and latest epochs suggests a transient mode-family drift rather than secular evolution. Such close-spaced multiple pulsations and mode switching may be common among BLAPs with periods shorter than 10 minutes, and their physical origin remains unclear.

title: Regulating AI-Generated Inventions in Tanzania: A Comparative Analysis of BRELA and South Africa’s CIPC
container-title: East African Journal of Law and Ethics
97d91fe2e65b9b432b752d3e2552b57b2f5ca94f.abstract: Artificial intelligence systems now produce technical solutions with little or no human contribution to the inventive step, and the DABUS applications filed by Dr Stephen Thaler have tested whether patent law can accommodate an inventor that is not a person. Courts and offices in the United Kingdom, the United States, Europe, Australia and Germany have refused, while South Africa’s Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC) published the grant of a patent naming DABUS as inventor in July 2021. This article asks whether Tanzania’s Business Registrations and Licensing Agency (BRELA) could follow that example under the Patents (Registration) Act, Cap 217, and, if not, what reform is required. Using doctrinal analysis and functional comparison, it finds that the two statutes are closer than is usually assumed: neither defines ‘inventor’, and both require an applicant who is not the inventor to show a right derived from the inventor. The decisive difference is administrative. The South African grant followed a formalities-only check in which, on the published record, the applicant’s entitlement was not tested, leaving validity to revocation proceedings. Section 25(7) and (8) of Cap 217, by contrast, require the Registrar to examine every request for compliance with section 18(3) and (4) and to reject one that is not corrected. An application naming DABUS would therefore fail at the formal stage, and one naming a human who did not devise the invention would be open to invalidation under section 64(2)(d). BRELA cannot reproduce the CIPC outcome by discretion. The article recommends, in order of priority, statements of practice on AI-assisted inventions, revised forms, a statutory definition of inventor and, after regional consultation through ARIPO and the East African Community, a deliberate legislative choice on whether AI-generated inventions should be protected.

title: A Hybrid Convolutional Recurrent Neural Model for Noise Detection and Automated Calibration of Medical Devices via Molecular Vibration Analysis
518557eedb6ff36ea9b47c24553d6afd51c850c8.abstract: Abstract Accurate noise detection and calibration are essential for maintaining the measurement reliability of medical devices. This study proposes a hybrid convolutional recurrent neural network (CRNN) framework for noise detection and automated calibration of ventilators and electrocardiogram (ECG) machines using molecular vibration analysis. A molecular vibration model was developed to characterize mechanical vibration, electromagnetic interference, and environmental conduction noise, achieving an average noise classification accuracy of 96.2%. The proposed CRNN with hybrid attention maintained 91.5% accuracy under low signal-to-noise conditions. A deep deterministic policy gradient-based calibration strategy was subsequently employed to optimize calibration parameters automatically, reducing calibration time by 72.5% and improving calibration accuracy by 78.5% compared with conventional methods. After calibration, the average relative errors were 1.9% for ventilator tidal-volume measurements and 0.92% for QRS-complex amplitude measurements in ECG devices. Cross-device validation achieved 94.3% accuracy across different equipment brands. The results demonstrate that integrating molecular vibration analysis, hybrid deep learning, and automated calibration provides an effective approach for reliable noise detection and precision calibration of medical devices.

title: Editorial: generative AI and the small business frontier – charting pathways toward meaningful social impact
container-title: Journal of Social Impact in Business Research
c4b06f07519c890d4aa7881d2f5de009595df712.abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine how small and medium-sized enterprises can leverage generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) to create social impact, by developing a multidimensional framework linking GenAI adoption with social-value creation. Design/methodology/approach This editorial adopts a conceptual synthesis approach, that integrates insights from the special-issue papers with emerging research and identifies principal domains of social impact. Findings Social impact is not a property of GenAI but a contingent outcome of how it is applied and adopted. While firms may have similar GenAI potentialities across various impact domains, success is dependent on human, organisational, sectoral and institutional contexts. Practical implications This editorial provides a framework for assessing where GenAI can support social-value creation whilst managing ethical, organisational and workforce risks. Impact accrues through organisational processes rather than through adoption itself. Originality/value The social impact of GenAI is extended beyond productivity and efficiency and positioned as a multidimensional and contingent outcome of technology adoption. A four-element framework links GenAI capability, organisational mechanisms, enabling and constraining conditions and stakeholder outcomes, which then informs a research agenda.

title: Radial Kernel Attention for Long-Range Modeling in Polymer Machine Learning Force Fields
569d9c0f37ae1ad406ec120b61cd9e579ab007dc.abstract: We introduce Radial Kernel Attention (RKA) for long-range modeling in polymer machine learning force fields. Local neighbor graphs constrain communication across polymer chains and their surrounding environments, while explicit all-pair attention incurs quadratic cost. RKA maps atomic distances from the cluster centroid to learned radial features and combines their overlap with content-dependent queries and keys. Factorized aggregation and readout enable global feature exchange at linear cost in atom count for fixed feature dimensions. We insert the invariant scalar update between EquiformerV3 local blocks and obtain conservative forces by differentiating the total energy, including its radial coordinate dependence. We evaluate energy and force prediction for finite polymer-derived clusters in OPoly26. Our models are trained on the official training split for 12 epochs and evaluated directly after training on the complete official validation split. A matched 5M comparison shows that RKA reduces per-atom energy and force MAEs by 67.4% and 36.3%, respectively. The 20M RKA model is compared with UMA-S-1.2 and UMA-S-1.2.1 on the same validation structures. The 20M model attains a total-energy MAE of 15.81 meV and a force MAE of 2.619 meV/Å; its per-atom energy MAE is 0.1182 meV/atom. RKA provides a compact global communication pathway that improves energy and force prediction on the evaluated polymer-derived clusters.

title: Trustworthy Federated Clinical Intelligence with Homomorphic Encryption and  Explainable AI
container-title: International Journal on Advanced Computer Engineering and Communication Technology
e9efaf7e4de70a4bb9a5e76e1dc2d37a457ecb6d.abstract: Cross-institutional clinical artificial intelligence is constrained by fragmented patient data, non-identically distributed (non-IID) populations, leakage from shared model updates, and limited interpretability. Federated learning (FL) preserves data locality, but ordinary FL neither makes model updates confidential nor guarantees stable optimization under heterogeneous clients. This paper proposes a defense-in-depth framework that coordinates Federated Proximal (FedProx) optimization, record-level differential privacy (DP), Cheon–Kim–Kim–Song (CKKS) approximate homomorphic encryption, and explainable artificial intelligence (XAI). FedProx limits local model drift; DP-SGD bounds the influence of an individual training record; and CKKS permits weighted aggregation while client updates remain encrypted. A key-separated design keeps the aggregation server from being provisioned with the secret key used to reveal individual contributions; only the aggregate is released for global-model construction. Grad-CAM and SHAP/LIME provide clinician-facing explanations, while an audit dashboard reports convergence, privacy-accounting inputs, encryption status, and systems overhead. We formalize the learning objective, privacy mechanism, encrypted aggregation, threat model, numerical approximation error, communication footprint, and an evaluation protocol spanning IID and controlled non-IID partitions. The contribution is a reproducible system-level co-design and evaluation framework rather than a new cryptographic primitive or optimization algorithm.

title: AI-Driven Predictive Maintenance for Institutional Electrical Systems
container-title: Journal of Technology and System Information
743e0632b4637f415786ff15de8256d3f95412a3.abstract: High-voltage power distribution networks in institutional settings are increasingly vulnerable to age-related degradation, operational volatility, and unexpected service disruptions. Conventional maintenance practices—dominated by reactive repairs and static time-based servicing—impose significant financial burdens and risk over-servicing intact assets. To address these operational constraints, this study employs a thematic literature synthesis of smart grid prognostics and IIoT asset telemetry (2015–2025) to formulate an end-to-end four-layer predictive maintenance (PdM) framework. The architectural continuum is established by systematically mapping physical multi-sensor acquisition to edge-cloud analytics (GRU and Bi-LSTM engines), dynamic Asset Health Index (AHI) tracking, and automated, cyber-secure Computerized Maintenance Management System (CMMS) dispatch. Synthesizing literature performance baselines reveals that deep bidirectional recurrent networks—notably Bi-LSTM models—achieve superior degradation tracking for Remaining Useful Life (RUL) estimation, attaining an F1-score of 91.0%, a Mean Absolute Error of 4.3%, and a Root Mean Squared Error of 4.2. Furthermore, multi-modal feature fusion significantly sharpens Asset Health Index (AHI) modeling, driving prediction errors down to an RMSE of 0.052, lengthening warning lead times to 37 days, and maintaining false alarm rates at 6.2%. The transition to an AI-enabled prognostic strategy yields up to a 50.0% decrease in overall operational and maintenance costs while extending high-voltage asset longevity by 40%. The inclusion of Explainable AI (SHAP and LRP) alongside robust Operational Technology cybersecurity measures guarantees operational transparency and cyber resilience.

title: TECHNOLOGICAL EMPOWERMENT AND VALUE BALANCE: DUAL PATHWAYS IN CHINA’S TECHNOLOGY GOVERNANCE POLICIES FOR THE AI ERA
container-title: Trends in Social Sciences and Humanities Research
046a4b825efe15b9ca51cb520c373729b94ebde6.abstract: The deep embedding of artificial intelligence (AI) technology is reshaping global governance. The tension between “technological empowerment” and “value balance” has become a common governance challenge for countries worldwide. Based on a dual-pathway framework of “technology-driven modernization of state governance” and “technology-embedded multi-actor social co-governance,” this paper systematically analyzes the internal logic and operational mechanisms of technology governance in China in the AI era. The study finds that China’s technology governance is not a single efficiency-oriented application of technology; rather, through the coordinated operation of dual pathways, it comprehensively achieves four major governance functions: efficiency improvement, equity promotion, security assurance, and institutional reconstruction. In terms of model characteristics, China has developed a distinctive paradigm centered on “enabling governance”-one that takes state capacity as its foundation, institutional flexibility as its safeguard, and plural public values as its goals. This paradigm transcends the single efficiency-oriented governance logic of the West and offers a non-Western pathway with both theoretical inspiration and practical reference for global digital governance. This paper argues that the core of “enabling governance” lies in resolving the tension between technological empowerment and value balance through institutional design, and that the transferability of its experience depends on the conditions of fit in specific institutional contexts.

title: Generative artificial intelligence drives large model generation algorithm for enhancing Chinese modern traditional cultural knowledge
container-title: Discover Artificial Intelligence
f48c63c87e8ab5a4802a0daf6c6d06f0de6ee24c.abstract: Abstract To address outdated knowledge, cultural-context mismatch, weak evidence linkage, and unsupported expansion in general-purpose large language model generation of traditional-cultural content, this study proposes a generative AI-driven knowledge-enhanced generation algorithm. The method decouples a frozen Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct generator from an external dynamic knowledge base and uses a four-field semantic tag scheme covering cultural category, historical stage, regional origin, and application scenario. Candidate evidence is ranked by vector similarity, graph relations, tag consistency, source credibility, and conflict penalties, then assembled into a constrained prompt without modifying the internal attention layers of the frozen model. An incremental update mechanism combines source verification, conflict detection, and expert review, while factual consistency, cultural-context adaptability, and evidence coverage are used for post-generation verification. Experiments cover classical texts, cultural heritage objects, intangible cultural heritage crafts, traditional Chinese opera, and folk culture, with 1,080 factual question-answering samples and 360 contextual generation tasks. The proposed system achieves 88.61% factual accuracy, 95.28% answer relevance, 94.17% evidence faithfulness, and 92.50% cultural-context adaptability. After knowledge updating, accuracy on update-dependent questions rises from 58.67% to 91.33%. These results indicate that the proposed framework provides a traceable, context-sensitive generation pipeline while retaining a frozen generation model; between-system differences are interpreted descriptively because complete paired baseline predictions were not retained.
