title: Teachers’ attitudes and behavioural intentions towards AI integration in Chinese higher education: a qualitative interview study
container-title: Frontiers in Psychology
c6fe4330bbf5fd4fe3ac0771cb768c511236b747.abstract: Introduction The rapid expansion of generative AI has intensified scholarly and policy debate over its role in higher education, yet university teachers’ attitudes towards its integration remain complex and context-dependent. This study explores how university teachers perceive, experience, and respond to AI integration in their teaching. Guided primarily by the three-component attitude model and informed by the technology acceptance model and the theory of planned behaviour, the study examines cognitive appraisals, affective responses, behavioural intentions, and perceived support needs. Methods The study draws on semi-structured interviews with 14 university teachers from four higher education institutions in China. The interview data were analysed using codebook-informed thematic analysis combining deductive and inductive coding. Results The findings indicate that teachers generally perceive AI as a supportive rather than substitutive educational tool, valuing it for improving efficiency, supporting lesson preparation, and enriching pedagogical design. Emotional responses varied from enthusiasm and a sense of accomplishment to caution, neutrality, and, in some cases, declining satisfaction. Across the interviews, teachers’ primary concerns centred less on their own replacement than on the perceived risks of inappropriate AI use for students’ independent thinking, reasoning, originality, and authentic understanding. Teachers’ intentions to adopt AI were therefore conditional and bounded, shaped by pedagogical purpose, disciplinary context, student readiness, and the need to maintain teacher control. Teachers also emphasised that sustainable AI integration requires more than general encouragement, calling instead for AI literacy development, discipline-sensitive support, specialised tools, and enabling institutional infrastructure. Discussion Overall, these findings extend contextual understandings of teachers’ AI acceptance by showing how adoption intentions are pedagogically negotiated and highlight the importance of supporting professional judgement and students’ independent thinking in higher education.

title: Automated assessment of healthcare de-escalation communication skills in a conversational AI virtual reality simulation
container-title: Frontiers in Digital Health
9bc424b8b0ee6bc350b4296b68f692e3f29c8284.abstract: Introduction Digital health training environments increasingly require scalable methods for assessing communication skills in realistic, interactive scenarios. This paper presents a comparative study of automated assessment approaches within a conversational AI virtual reality simulation designed for verbal de-escalation training. Methods A total of 20 nursing students completed the simulation, where their spoken responses were captured and converted to text through a speech-to-text system, and were evaluated across 11 de-escalation competencies. The evaluation compared three fine-tuned deep learning models (BERT, RoBERTa, and XLNet) with a modified RATAS, a rubric-driven framework that leverages large language models. Two experiments were conducted: one using controlled 100-item validation datasets for each section, and another using the real-world responses collected during the user study. Results On the validation datasets, the deep learning models achieved the highest performance, with RoBERTa obtaining an average accuracy of 0.9927, followed by BERT at 0.9900 and XLNet at 0.9790, while RATAS achieved 0.8554. On the student-response dataset, performance decreased for all approaches, with RoBERTa obtaining 0.8590 accuracy, RATAS 0.8181, BERT 0.8000, and XLNet 0.7681. Discussion These results suggest that transformer-based models perform best under controlled conditions, whereas RATAS demonstrated stability in grading across different dataset types. These preliminary findings support the feasibility of integrating deep learning and rubric-driven LLM-based automated assessment approaches for communication and de-escalation training in nursing education.

title: Uneven automation: comparing authorship anxiety and generative AI use among art and design undergraduate students
container-title: Frontiers in Psychology
8942b2ac014d5d2bac7e05011f209f96a5fce870.abstract: Art and design education expects students to develop a sense of authorship over original work, but generative AI (GenAI) complicates how students understand and claim that authorship. This study examined whether these experiences differ across creative fields through a mixed-methods design. The survey included 2,441 GenAI-using students from seven field categories at 33 art and design institutions in China and assessed authorship anxiety, creative agency, perceived usefulness, dependence on GenAI, and frequency of use. The quantitative analysis first examined variation across all seven categories and then compared fine art with the five applied design fields. Interview data from 22 survey participants were also examined thematically. The main findings include that (1) authorship anxiety did not differ significantly across the seven categories or between fine art and pooled design; the latter comparison met the equivalence criterion at ±d = 0.20, but not at tighter bounds; (2) clearer differences emerged in how students used GenAI. Compared with fine-art students, design students considered GenAI more useful and used it more frequently; (3) across the interviews, most students described authorship as retaining control over the creative idea while delegating parts of its execution to GenAI. Specifically, fine-art students often grounded authorship in embodied making and human imperfection, whereas design students placed greater emphasis on judgement, selection, and control. We call this pattern uneven automation: concern about authorship was broadly shared, but students in different fields responded to GenAI in different ways, potentially reflecting the varying labour-market pressures surrounding their disciplines.

title: Digital transformation, traceability, and supply chain resilience in food manufacturing SMEs: a review of AI, blockchain-IoT, and institutional mechanisms
container-title: Frontiers in Sustainable Food Systems
c0821ee379eb16d2e0252633d6030dd152fbd833.abstract: Food supply chains in China face persistent challenges of food safety risks, inadequate transparency, and supply disruptions, with food manufacturing small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) disproportionately vulnerable due to limited resources and non-standardized internal processes. Digital transformation encompassing artificial intelligence (AI), blockchain, Internet of Things (IoT), and digital twin technologies is increasingly regarded as a strategic solution to strengthen supply chain resilience, yet the organizational and institutional conditions under which these digital investments translate into tangible resilience improvements for food manufacturing SMEs remain poorly understood. This review conducts a PRISMA 2020-compliant systematic review and thematic synthesis of 40 multidisciplinary sources spanning the food safety, supply chain management, and information systems literatures. Drawing on Dynamic Capabilities Theory and Institutional Theory, we propose an integrative conceptual framework comprising six research propositions, in which traceability capability acts as a food-safety-specific mediating mechanism linking digital transformation to supply chain resilience, while regulatory stringency moderates the strength of this indirect pathway. A central argument of this framework is that deploying blockchain, IoT, or AI hardware does not itself constitute traceability capability the institutional and organisational conditions under which digital tools are adopted determine whether firms build substantive traceability capability or engage in symbolic compliance without genuine food safety governance improvement. Three key contributions distinguish this framework: conceptualizing traceability capability as a distinct dynamic capability rather than a generic digitalization mechanism; directing analytical focus explicitly toward food manufacturing SMEs, a population largely overlooked in existing large-firm panel studies; and introducing regulatory stringency as a first-stage moderator within a moderated mediation structure. Critical research gaps are identified, including the absence of SME-calibrated digital transformation measurement instruments, the lack of a validated multi-item traceability capability scale, and a complete empirical vacuum for testing the proposed moderated mediation model in food manufacturing SME contexts. This review provides a structured future research agenda for scholars and delivers actionable insights for practitioners and policymakers seeking to direct digital technology investments toward improved food safety governance in China’s food manufacturing sector.

title: Human-in-the-loop semantic learning analytics for assessing moral-value reasoning in university AI ethics education
container-title: Frontiers in Psychology
4c153cd19693204269d4536c8e62024e2ea30575.abstract: Introduction University AI ethics education addresses fairness, privacy, accountability, transparency, human autonomy, and academic integrity, but the semantic structure of students' moral-value reasoning and its connection to responsible solutions remain insufficiently characterized. This study examined a human-in-the-loop semantic learning analytics framework for task-specific moral-value reasoning. Methods Ninety science and engineering graduate students completed an online explicit-reflective AI ethics module in a one-group pre–post multimethod study without a control group. Assessments comprised an AI ethics knowledge test, a perceived-awareness scale, and open-ended ethical reasoning tasks. Expert annotations informed transformer-based multi-label coding, descriptive value coverage and balance metrics, problem–solution coupling, and baseline-only nested cross-validated prediction of subsequent raw problem-solving change. Results Within-participant pre–post increases were observed in ethical knowledge, perceived moral-value awareness, actual ethical awareness, problem–solving skills, value coverage, value balance, and problem–solution coupling. Automated semantic coding achieved participant-grouped cross-validated macro-F1 = 0.83 (95% CI [0.78, 0.87]; micro-F1 = 0.86; macro-AUPRC = 0.82). The baseline-only prediction model yielded cross-validated R 2 = 0.30 (95% CI [0.11, 0.45]) for subsequent raw problem-solving change. Discussion Expert-supervised semantic analytics can characterize value representation and issue–solution reasoning in AI ethics assessments. Coverage and balance describe response structure rather than moral quality. The absence of a control group, repeated use of one scenario, and modest sample size preclude causal and broad trait-level conclusions.

title: Perceived AI literacy and TPACK in pre-service teacher education: mediating roles of perceived usefulness, ease of use, and value in blended learning
container-title: Frontiers in Psychology
1bad51d2ab1c081fcbf1788c8c81f98f9ce0044c.abstract: Background The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into blended learning requires pre-service teachers to develop AI-related competencies and the ability to integrate technology into pedagogy. This study examines how perceived AI literacy and technological pedagogical content knowledge (TPACK) are associated with deep learning through perceived usefulness, perceived ease of use, and perceived value of AI use. Methods A cross-sectional survey was completed by 423 pre-service teachers enrolled in blended learning courses at a university in China. Data were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM), with covariance-based structural equation modeling and fuzzy-set qualitative comparative analysis (fsQCA) used as complementary robustness and configurational analyses. Results Perceived usefulness, perceived ease of use, and perceived value of AI use significantly mediated the relationships between the two competencies and deep learning. All six indirect pathways were significant in both the PLS-SEM and covariance-based SEM analyses. The fsQCA revealed an equifinal and asymmetric structure: multiple, partly substitutable conditions were sufficient for high deep learning, and no single condition was necessary for either high or low deep learning. Conclusions The findings integrate the technology acceptance model and expectancy-value theory to explain how pre-service teachers' competencies and perceptions relate to deep learning in AI-enhanced blended environments. Teacher education should support technical competence alongside positive perceptions of AI's utility, usability, and value. Because the measures were self-reported and collected cross-sectionally at one university, the findings are interpreted as associational and configurational rather than causal.

title: Effectiveness of an AI-Based Educational Video Generator in Enhancing Oral Health Knowledge and Behavior Among Children: A Randomized Controlled Trial
container-title: Al-Rafidain Journal of Medical Sciences ( ISSN 2789-3219 )
025217a90eae33a9efbb4f3e4378042549e3202e.abstract: Background: Artificial intelligence (AI) is a new innovation that presents an opportunity for oral health education in children. Objective: To evaluate the effectiveness of an AI-assisted educational video versus standardized in-person oral health education for children regarding oral health knowledge and behaviors. Methods: This randomized controlled trial included 300 children aged 10-12 years (n=150 per group), both boys and girls, who were divided into AI video and standardized face-to-face oral health education groups. Baseline and 2-week follow-up evaluations were conducted for knowledge scores, four behavioral items, and the Silness and Löe Plaque Index. The internal consistency of the knowledge scale was checked (Cronbach's α=0.79). Wilcoxon signed-rank and Mann–Whitney U tests were the primary non-parametric tests used for statistical evaluations, with a median, (IQR), and effect size r provided. Chi-square tests with a Bonferroni adjustment at α=0.0125 were used to evaluate behavioral items. Results: There were significant enhancements in intra-group knowledge (p<0.0001 for both groups; r=0.663 for AI; r=0.345 for Control). The clinical efficacy was similar for both strategies with significant reduction of intra-group plaque (AI: p< 0.001, r= 0.425; Control: p< 0.001, r= 0.331), but no inter-group difference at the end of the intervention (p= 0.608; r= 0.030). In the conventional group, the utilization of dental floss was significantly improved (p=0.0056), and no other behaviors showed significant improvement across groups. Conclusions: The AI-assisted educational video demonstrated better knowledge retention than the standardized face-to-face oral health education, achieved similar clinical plaque reduction, and can be easily scaled for pediatric preventive dentistry.

title: Improving Learner Performance Through Score Based Analysis on a Gamified AI Driven Cybersecurity Learning Platform
d2b1981b0d01f6ee261a12a86c8c602586119c26.abstract: Abstract This study examines whether structured engagement with instructional content improves learner performance on Cyber Security Academy, an AI-driven, gamified cybersecurity learning platform. Activity logs covering 1,500 completed assessments from users in ten Anglophone and Francophone countries were analyzed by comparing learners who consulted the lessons and completed the full learning pathway (n = 900) with those who engaged only partially with the platform (n = 600). Group differences were tested with Welch's t-test, the Mann Whitney U test, one-way ANOVA, Spearman correlations, and Cohen's d as a measure of effect size. Learners who read the lessons before assessment obtained a mean score of 71.27 % versus 60.41 % for non-readers (Δ = +10.86 points; t(1192) = 12.21; p < 0.001; d = 0.650; 95 % CI [9.12, 12.60]), committed fewer errors (2.50 vs. 4.85; d = -1.069), and responded faster (9.85 vs. 12.69 minutes; d = -0.807), indicating greater fluency of cognitive processing. The effect decreased monotonically with age (d = 1.205 for learners aged 13 and under; d = 0.387 for those 22 and over) and with digital literacy (d = 1.434 for beginners; d = 0.524 for experts), while remaining positive in all ten countries. These findings indicate that structured, AI-personalized, and gamified learning environments substantially enhance cybersecurity learning outcomes, particularly for younger and less experienced users.

title: AI Labour Rights Awareness and Career Adaptation Confidence among Respondents in Bangladesh
4bebd9cda335afcb1b14dbb90e41e4c4857a6c33.abstract: Abstract Artificial intelligence changes both the skills used at work and the conditions under which employment decisions are made. Awareness of these changes does not necessarily coincide with confidence in adapting a career. This study examines that distinction in 385 adult, AI-aware survey records from Bangladesh, including 238 law students and 61 respondents classified as law graduates. Five statements separately assess awareness of workplace rights and responsibilities, recognition of protection from unfair automated decisions, reported complementary skill development, adaptation confidence and the perceived preparedness benefit of understanding labour issues. Analyses combine full response distributions, joint endorsement patterns, paired comparisons, ordinal correlations and an exploratory proportional-odds model. Recognition of the need for protection was endorsed by 79.2%, compared with 48.8% endorsing adaptation confidence, a paired difference of 30.4 percentage points (95% bootstrap interval 23.9–36.6). General rights awareness and skill development had small positive ordinal associations with confidence. In the adjusted ordinal model, their odds ratios were 1.30 (95% interval 1.04–1.61; Holm p = 0.038) and 1.40 (1.09–1.79; Holm p = 0.024) respectively. The protection-recognition estimate was less certain, although the two awareness coefficients were not demonstrably different. The findings distinguish rights recognition, reported action and confidence rather than establish a causal awareness-to-adaptability pathway. They support evaluating legal-literacy education alongside practical career tasks and institutional safeguards. The mixed sample, study-specific single items, undocumented recruitment and fieldwork dates, and source-documentation limitations constrain inference. A subsequent study should use verified graduate eligibility, independent legal-knowledge assessments and longitudinal career outcomes.

title: Regulating AI-Generated Inventions in Tanzania: A Comparative Analysis of BRELA and South Africa’s CIPC
container-title: East African Journal of Law and Ethics
97d91fe2e65b9b432b752d3e2552b57b2f5ca94f.abstract: Artificial intelligence systems now produce technical solutions with little or no human contribution to the inventive step, and the DABUS applications filed by Dr Stephen Thaler have tested whether patent law can accommodate an inventor that is not a person. Courts and offices in the United Kingdom, the United States, Europe, Australia and Germany have refused, while South Africa’s Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC) published the grant of a patent naming DABUS as inventor in July 2021. This article asks whether Tanzania’s Business Registrations and Licensing Agency (BRELA) could follow that example under the Patents (Registration) Act, Cap 217, and, if not, what reform is required. Using doctrinal analysis and functional comparison, it finds that the two statutes are closer than is usually assumed: neither defines ‘inventor’, and both require an applicant who is not the inventor to show a right derived from the inventor. The decisive difference is administrative. The South African grant followed a formalities-only check in which, on the published record, the applicant’s entitlement was not tested, leaving validity to revocation proceedings. Section 25(7) and (8) of Cap 217, by contrast, require the Registrar to examine every request for compliance with section 18(3) and (4) and to reject one that is not corrected. An application naming DABUS would therefore fail at the formal stage, and one naming a human who did not devise the invention would be open to invalidation under section 64(2)(d). BRELA cannot reproduce the CIPC outcome by discretion. The article recommends, in order of priority, statements of practice on AI-assisted inventions, revised forms, a statutory definition of inventor and, after regional consultation through ARIPO and the East African Community, a deliberate legislative choice on whether AI-generated inventions should be protected.

title: A Hybrid Convolutional Recurrent Neural Model for Noise Detection and Automated Calibration of Medical Devices via Molecular Vibration Analysis
518557eedb6ff36ea9b47c24553d6afd51c850c8.abstract: Abstract Accurate noise detection and calibration are essential for maintaining the measurement reliability of medical devices. This study proposes a hybrid convolutional recurrent neural network (CRNN) framework for noise detection and automated calibration of ventilators and electrocardiogram (ECG) machines using molecular vibration analysis. A molecular vibration model was developed to characterize mechanical vibration, electromagnetic interference, and environmental conduction noise, achieving an average noise classification accuracy of 96.2%. The proposed CRNN with hybrid attention maintained 91.5% accuracy under low signal-to-noise conditions. A deep deterministic policy gradient-based calibration strategy was subsequently employed to optimize calibration parameters automatically, reducing calibration time by 72.5% and improving calibration accuracy by 78.5% compared with conventional methods. After calibration, the average relative errors were 1.9% for ventilator tidal-volume measurements and 0.92% for QRS-complex amplitude measurements in ECG devices. Cross-device validation achieved 94.3% accuracy across different equipment brands. The results demonstrate that integrating molecular vibration analysis, hybrid deep learning, and automated calibration provides an effective approach for reliable noise detection and precision calibration of medical devices.

title: Editorial: generative AI and the small business frontier – charting pathways toward meaningful social impact
container-title: Journal of Social Impact in Business Research
c4b06f07519c890d4aa7881d2f5de009595df712.abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine how small and medium-sized enterprises can leverage generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) to create social impact, by developing a multidimensional framework linking GenAI adoption with social-value creation. Design/methodology/approach This editorial adopts a conceptual synthesis approach, that integrates insights from the special-issue papers with emerging research and identifies principal domains of social impact. Findings Social impact is not a property of GenAI but a contingent outcome of how it is applied and adopted. While firms may have similar GenAI potentialities across various impact domains, success is dependent on human, organisational, sectoral and institutional contexts. Practical implications This editorial provides a framework for assessing where GenAI can support social-value creation whilst managing ethical, organisational and workforce risks. Impact accrues through organisational processes rather than through adoption itself. Originality/value The social impact of GenAI is extended beyond productivity and efficiency and positioned as a multidimensional and contingent outcome of technology adoption. A four-element framework links GenAI capability, organisational mechanisms, enabling and constraining conditions and stakeholder outcomes, which then informs a research agenda.

title: Trustworthy Federated Clinical Intelligence with Homomorphic Encryption and  Explainable AI
container-title: International Journal on Advanced Computer Engineering and Communication Technology
e9efaf7e4de70a4bb9a5e76e1dc2d37a457ecb6d.abstract: Cross-institutional clinical artificial intelligence is constrained by fragmented patient data, non-identically distributed (non-IID) populations, leakage from shared model updates, and limited interpretability. Federated learning (FL) preserves data locality, but ordinary FL neither makes model updates confidential nor guarantees stable optimization under heterogeneous clients. This paper proposes a defense-in-depth framework that coordinates Federated Proximal (FedProx) optimization, record-level differential privacy (DP), Cheon–Kim–Kim–Song (CKKS) approximate homomorphic encryption, and explainable artificial intelligence (XAI). FedProx limits local model drift; DP-SGD bounds the influence of an individual training record; and CKKS permits weighted aggregation while client updates remain encrypted. A key-separated design keeps the aggregation server from being provisioned with the secret key used to reveal individual contributions; only the aggregate is released for global-model construction. Grad-CAM and SHAP/LIME provide clinician-facing explanations, while an audit dashboard reports convergence, privacy-accounting inputs, encryption status, and systems overhead. We formalize the learning objective, privacy mechanism, encrypted aggregation, threat model, numerical approximation error, communication footprint, and an evaluation protocol spanning IID and controlled non-IID partitions. The contribution is a reproducible system-level co-design and evaluation framework rather than a new cryptographic primitive or optimization algorithm.

title: AI-Driven Predictive Maintenance for Institutional Electrical Systems
container-title: Journal of Technology and System Information
743e0632b4637f415786ff15de8256d3f95412a3.abstract: High-voltage power distribution networks in institutional settings are increasingly vulnerable to age-related degradation, operational volatility, and unexpected service disruptions. Conventional maintenance practices—dominated by reactive repairs and static time-based servicing—impose significant financial burdens and risk over-servicing intact assets. To address these operational constraints, this study employs a thematic literature synthesis of smart grid prognostics and IIoT asset telemetry (2015–2025) to formulate an end-to-end four-layer predictive maintenance (PdM) framework. The architectural continuum is established by systematically mapping physical multi-sensor acquisition to edge-cloud analytics (GRU and Bi-LSTM engines), dynamic Asset Health Index (AHI) tracking, and automated, cyber-secure Computerized Maintenance Management System (CMMS) dispatch. Synthesizing literature performance baselines reveals that deep bidirectional recurrent networks—notably Bi-LSTM models—achieve superior degradation tracking for Remaining Useful Life (RUL) estimation, attaining an F1-score of 91.0%, a Mean Absolute Error of 4.3%, and a Root Mean Squared Error of 4.2. Furthermore, multi-modal feature fusion significantly sharpens Asset Health Index (AHI) modeling, driving prediction errors down to an RMSE of 0.052, lengthening warning lead times to 37 days, and maintaining false alarm rates at 6.2%. The transition to an AI-enabled prognostic strategy yields up to a 50.0% decrease in overall operational and maintenance costs while extending high-voltage asset longevity by 40%. The inclusion of Explainable AI (SHAP and LRP) alongside robust Operational Technology cybersecurity measures guarantees operational transparency and cyber resilience.

title: TECHNOLOGICAL EMPOWERMENT AND VALUE BALANCE: DUAL PATHWAYS IN CHINA’S TECHNOLOGY GOVERNANCE POLICIES FOR THE AI ERA
container-title: Trends in Social Sciences and Humanities Research
046a4b825efe15b9ca51cb520c373729b94ebde6.abstract: The deep embedding of artificial intelligence (AI) technology is reshaping global governance. The tension between “technological empowerment” and “value balance” has become a common governance challenge for countries worldwide. Based on a dual-pathway framework of “technology-driven modernization of state governance” and “technology-embedded multi-actor social co-governance,” this paper systematically analyzes the internal logic and operational mechanisms of technology governance in China in the AI era. The study finds that China’s technology governance is not a single efficiency-oriented application of technology; rather, through the coordinated operation of dual pathways, it comprehensively achieves four major governance functions: efficiency improvement, equity promotion, security assurance, and institutional reconstruction. In terms of model characteristics, China has developed a distinctive paradigm centered on “enabling governance”-one that takes state capacity as its foundation, institutional flexibility as its safeguard, and plural public values as its goals. This paradigm transcends the single efficiency-oriented governance logic of the West and offers a non-Western pathway with both theoretical inspiration and practical reference for global digital governance. This paper argues that the core of “enabling governance” lies in resolving the tension between technological empowerment and value balance through institutional design, and that the transferability of its experience depends on the conditions of fit in specific institutional contexts.

title: tModBase v2.0: an expanded database of tRNA modifications with an AI-powered assistant
container-title: Nucleic Acids Research
6dc27bcf3717dbf61b825aaa6a0d910a0b11a2a6.abstract: Abstract Chemical modifications of transfer RNAs (tRNAs) are crucial for tRNA stability, codon decoding, translational fidelity, and tRNA-derived small RNA (tsRNA) biogenesis. Changes in these modifications are associated with stress responses, physiological regulation, and human disease, underscoring the need to integrate modification information with experimental evidence and biological context. We previously established tModBase, a web resource to organize and explore tRNA modification-related data. Its first release integrated modification sites, high-throughput sequencing-derived signals, and condition-dependent changes. Since then, tRNA profiling has expanded through modification-specific and direct RNA sequencing strategies, with rapidly growing datasets across species and conditions. Here, we present tModBase v2.0 (http://www.tmodbase2.com/), containing 528 datasets across 23 species, 40 sequencing and library-preparation methods, and 42 modification types. It includes 68 third-generation and 210 modification-specific sequencing datasets, extending coverage of direct-RNA and modification-specific approaches. tModBase v2.0 further integrates sequencing-derived signals, condition-dependent information, and biological annotations linking modifications with enzymes, genetic variants, tsRNAs, diseases, and expression profiles. The LLM- and retrieval-augmented generation-powered assistant tModBot enables natural-language exploration across database modules while grounding responses in retrieved tModBase evidence. tModBase v2.0 therefore provides an expanded resource for investigating the diversity, dynamics, and biological context of tRNA modifications.

title: The mediating role of self-efficacy in the relationships of technophilia and positive emotional experience with perceived learning effectiveness in AI-supported EFL education
container-title: Discover Artificial Intelligence
1e046e91cd43fe005cca1d83a4437e55e4d42551.abstract: Abstract Despite the increasing integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into English as a Foreign Language (EFL) education, the psychological mechanisms linking learners’ technological dispositions and emotional experiences to perceived learning effectiveness remain undertheorized and empirically underexplored. This study examined whether self-efficacy served as a statistical mediator in the relationships of technophilia and positive emotional experience with perceived learning effectiveness in AI-supported EFL education. A cross-sectional survey was conducted involving 234 students enrolled in English-language courses at a private college of health sciences. Adapted multi-item scales on technophilia, positive emotional experience, self-efficacy, and perceived learning effectiveness were administered. Structural equation modeling with bootstrapping (5000 resamples) was used to examine direct and indirect associations. Self-efficacy demonstrated the strongest direct association with perceived learning effectiveness (β = 0.375, p = 0.001). Positive emotional experience was strongly associated with self-efficacy (β = 0.624, p < 0.001), and its indirect association with perceived learning effectiveness through self-efficacy was significant (β = 0.234, 95% CI [0.128, 0.351]). Technophilia was also positively associated with self-efficacy (β = 0.307, p = 0.002), and its indirect association with perceived learning effectiveness through self-efficacy was significant. The findings were consistent with self-efficacy partially mediating both relationships. These findings suggest that learners’ confidence in managing AI-supported tasks plays an important role in linking affective dispositions to perceived effectiveness appraisals. The study contributes to computer-assisted language learning (CALL) research by clarifying how positive orientation toward AI-supported technologies, emotional experience, and efficacy beliefs jointly relate to learners’ perceptions of effective AI-supported language learning. Pedagogically, the findings suggest that progressively scaffolded practice and mastery-oriented AI tasks may strengthen self-efficacy and improve learners’ perceived effectiveness in AI-supported EFL environments.

title: Generative AI and Employment Concerns Among AI Aware Respondents in Bangladesh
2175796b9a04ec3e661e8e64d03823c1cc031301.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) may change professional tasks, but the implications for workers depend on how technology is introduced and how people adapt. This study examines stated perceptions of task change, concern about routine work and AI-related learning in 385 adult, AI-aware questionnaire records from Bangladesh. Most respondents were recorded as law students, and the dataset does not establish that all participants were employed or young professionals. The questions do not directly measure current job security or the effects of AI exposure on employment. Individual items are therefore analysed separately using response distributions, paired endorsement comparisons and exploratory rank correlations. Of 385 respondents, 232 (60.3%) agreed that AI may reduce demand for some routine professional tasks; 307 (79.7%) agreed that learning to work effectively with AI could reduce their future job-security concerns; and 211 (54.8%) anticipated new tasks requiring human judgement and oversight. A total of 184 respondents endorsed both the routine-task concern and the potential reassurance of learning. These statements differ in meaning and do not establish whether training actually reduces insecurity. Exploratory correlations were small and should not be interpreted causally. Job demands-resources theory, psychological contract theory and career construction provide complementary lenses rather than validated models. The study distinguishes concern about tasks from concern about losing a job and identifies the need for independently verified employment status, recruitment documentation and direct measures of perceived job security in future research.

title: The Paradox of Algorithmic Sycophancy: Sycophancy in Large Language Models and the Limits of AI-Mediated Knowledge Reconstruction in the Metacognitive Creative Destruction Model
f31f456f51b7580c96613027043ba5bcb62c702c.abstract: The Metacognitive Creative Destruction (MCD) model approaches educational innovation as a perpetual spiral process. Contradiction (accumulated cognitive conflicts that resist interpretation), activates Metacognitive Capacity, enabling Destructive Unlearning Propensity, the conscious abandonment of outdated mental schemas, which in turn enables Creative Reconstruction Ability, and ultimately, new knowledge. In the model’s empirical validation with 1,498 teachers, a critical finding emerged: AI Augmentation Intensity (AIA) predicted Metacognitive Capacity (MC) and Creative Reconstruction Ability (CRA), but not Destructive Unlearning Propensity (DUP).This article argues that this finding is not accidental, but reflects an inherent weakness of modern AI systems, and more specifically, the tendency toward AI Sycophancy. Models trained with reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) tend to avoid disagreements and be likable to the user, preventing the individual from experiencing cognitive conflicts, perpetuating their already formed beliefs at the expense of scientific accuracy.Therefore, in an environment of “algorithmic flattery”, the necessary contradictions that trigger unlearning are not produced. Based on the MCD model, it is concluded that the absence of unlearning, that is, the deliberate and conscious abandonment of outdated beliefs, mental models and practices, makes the reconstruction of knowledge absolutely superficial and thus, algorithmically condescending interaction does not produce deep and authentic knowledge, regardless of AI Augmentation Intensity.

title: SAGE-AIP: A Scale-Adaptive Gated Ensemble Framework for Predicting AI Adoption and Productivity Across Multiple Data Scales
5358271a89a3a9d9de2f5155abb8bccaa93cc9ce.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is frequently associated with productivity improvement, yet empirical conclusions depend on where AI exposure is measured, how productivity is defined, and which model is used. This study develops a multi-scale comparative framework using three datasets: 145,000 AI-adoption records from 10 countries and eight industries; 2,074 observed country-year records from 233 country or regional units (2015–2023); and 150 employee-level observations. Robust regression, country fixed effects, dynamic fixed effects, and difference-GMM sensitivity analysis are combined with a proposed Scale-Adaptive Gated Ensemble Framework for AI Adoption and Productivity (SAGE-AIP), which is benchmarked against six established regressors using temporal holdouts for the two longitudinal datasets and a train–test split for the employee data. The adoption dataset shows almost no systematic structure (R2 = 0.00018), and SAGE-AIP does not improve on simpler models there (test RMSE 28.976 vs. 28.900 for Elastic Net). In the global panel, automation intensity is strongly associated with AI-attributed productivity (β = 19.882, SE = 0.434), and SAGE-AIP attains the lowest test RMSE (4.448; R2 = 0.544). At the employee level, recorded AI-tool information remains positively associated with productivity (β = 0.905, SE = 0.220), but Random Forest outperforms SAGE-AIP (test RMSE 0.435 vs. 0.583). SAGE-AIP is therefore not uniformly superior; its value is scale-specific, which supports evaluating models across data scales rather than relying on a single dataset or model class.

title: Tidal City Intelligence: A Conceptual Framework for AI-Enabled Service Governance in Cities with Fluctuating Populations
9125839bb912dfa67489dd5a63f2a2fd021e86f5.abstract: Many cities serve far more people than their civil register counts, and the gap rises and falls with tourist seasons, holidays, pilgrimages and festivals. Municipal budgets, staffing and data systems are nonetheless sized to the register. This conceptual paper introduces the Tidal City, a city whose population present swings in recurring, largely predictable cycles that change how public services must be planned. We distinguish the concept from the service population, tourism seasonality and overtourism; propose a two-part Tidal Index measuring the swing’s amplitude and regularity; and offer a typology of seasonal, day-visitor and event-driven tidal cities. Drawing on dynamic capabilities and adaptive governance theory, we set out Tidal City Intelligence, a four-layer framework (Sense, Anticipate, Adapt, Govern) describing the data and AI capabilities a local government needs, and derive testable propositions for each layer. Published data from Pattaya, Thailand, put the average population present at roughly two to three times the registered population and show annual waste moving with guest arrivals while the register barely changed. With only annual guest data, the case illustrates load and demand regularity rather than the full index. The paper offers cities a common measure of the problem and researchers an empirical agenda.

title: AI Model Energy and Carbon Disclosure: A Source-Audited Study of 103 Releases (2024-2026)
59d3047d593bdd3064939431188715f273b686fc.abstract: AI model cards and release documents are supposed to help people assess models. For energy and carbon, they often leave out the number a reader needs, or print figures that cannot be compared directly. I built the Release Energy Ledger, a source-traceable record of 161 distinct developer releases, and audited a selected set of 103 dated 2024-2026 releases that passed a page check. On the designated release document, 85 (82.5 percent) print no energy, carbon or compute figure, 1 prints compute only, and 17 (16.5 percent) print an energy or carbon-related figure: 16 training-specific and 1 life-cycle footprint. None prints release-specific inference energy. Meta accounts for 10 of the 17; without Meta, the count is 7 of 93. The figures differ in method, unit, equipment boundary and emissions accounting, and only 8 of the 17 state a basis, a boundary and a method together. Changing the unit of analysis gives 11 of 80 documents, 10 of 59 model families and 7 of 23 developers. The strict-quote subset (5 of 74) is a different evidence frame, not a lower bound. A page re-read confirmed the printed figures for all 17; blinded AI coding agreed with the ledger on 91.9 to 100 percent of fields, and a separately instructed AI adjudicator agreed on 42 of 42 selected cells. These results describe the documents in this selected set, not actual emissions, the universe of releases or legal compliance. No human has validated any label. The ledger and counting script are released with the paper as a versioned data record (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23808341).

title: Compression‐Resilient, Resolution‐Vulnerable: A Statistical Robustness Analysis of EfficientNet‐B2 for AI‐Generated Image Detection
40c90e02b219b35a0c83b43f046473f558552e91.abstract: Reliable classification of AI-generated images requires more than high accuracy on unmodified test examples: media files may be compressed or downsampled before forensic analysis. This paper presents a controlled, paired robustness evaluation of a previously developed EfficientNet-B2 detector using RGB, fast Fourier transform (FFT), and artifact-oriented image features. The existing checkpoint, validation-selected classification threshold, and fixed set of 6,000 held-out images were reused without training or test-time threshold adjustment. Six transformed conditions were evaluated against original inputs: JPEG qualities 90, 70, and 50, and bicubic downsampling to maximum dimensions of 256, 128, and 64 pixels followed by reconstruction to the original dimensions. The baseline achieved 94.53% accuracy and 0.9857 area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC). JPEG variants produced accuracies between 94.38% and 94.63%, with paired 95% bootstrap intervals of accuracy change spanning zero. By contrast, downsampling to 256, 128, and 64 pixels yielded accuracies of 93.15%, 91.73%, and 74.40%, respectively. At 64 pixels, the accuracy difference was −20.13 percentage points (95% paired bootstrap interval approximately −21.12 to −19.12), and AUROC fell to 0.8967. The evidence indicates substantially greater sensitivity to severe spatial resolution loss than to the tested JPEG compression settings. Because the existing training procedure incorporates JPEG augmentation, these findings characterize this detector and evaluation protocol rather than establish universal robustness across detectors or unseen transformations.

title: An Application of the Self-Determination Theory Model for AI-Enhanced, Digital Psychosocial Interventions for Pediatric Disabilities
container-title: Western Journal of Nursing Research
6a353330c39f733eb7e369612f893bac2e52174c.abstract: Background: Youth with developmental disabilities (DDs) experience elevated psychosocial challenges, including difficulties with emotion regulation, self-concept, and access to timely mental health support. Pediatric nurses are well-positioned to address these needs; however, time constraints, limited training, and restricted access to specialty services often impede the provision of consistent psychosocial care. Digitally delivered psychosocial interventions enhanced by artificial intelligence (AI) offer new opportunities for individualized, accessible support, but these approaches frequently lack a clear theoretical foundation. Purpose: This paper applied Self-Determination Theory (SDT), specifically Basic Psychological Needs Theory, to guide pediatric nurses’ use of AI-enhanced, digital psychosocial interventions for DDs in practice. Methods: A theory-driven synthesis mapped SDT needs (autonomy, competence, and relatedness) to AI-enabled intervention features: conversational agents, neuro/adaptive feedback, and emotion-recognition tailoring. Results: The framework specifies how these features can promote volitional engagement, optimal challenge with timely feedback, and supportive interactions for youth with DDs. It also notes evidence gaps (small, heterogeneous samples; limited comparisons and follow-up) and barriers involving payment/workload, equity and access, and data protection, transparency, and bias. Conclusions/Implications: SDT offers a coherent, testable foundation for designing, evaluating, and integrating AI-enhanced psychosocial supports for pediatric DDs. Nurses can screen for support, coach families, monitor risks, and advocate for ethical deployment and rigorous research.

title: INTEGRATION OF GENERATIVE AI SKILLS IN JOB REQUIREMENTS: EVIDENCE FROM JOB ADVERTISEMENTS IN GEORGIA
container-title: Baltic Journal of Economic Studies
2e932bf664680814b7e5be137f1e6f4677cfcbee.abstract: The rapid diffusion of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) tools has created a demand for new skills in labour markets. However, research into how employers articulate GenAI competencies in job advertisements has focused almost exclusively on large, technologically advanced economies. This study examines how employers in Georgia, a small upper-middle-income transitional economy, indicate GenAI skill requirements in job advertisements, considering four dimensions: skill visibility, linguistic framing, organisational readiness and skill depth. Deductive content analysis was applied to 94 job advertisements collected in January 2026 from three major Georgian labour market platforms (LinkedIn, Jobs.ge and HR.ge). Each advertisement was coded using a structured 20-indicator codebook derived from established theoretical frameworks. The results show that employers articulate GenAI skills in two ways: by explicitly naming the tool, which is present in 38.3 per cent of advertisements, and by using implicit task language, which is present in 61.7 per cent of advertisements and constitutes the dominant form of signalling. Regardless of occupation or skill depth, employers frame GenAI requirements as mandatory in 81.9 per cent of advertisements, indicating the rapid institutionalisation of GenAI literacy as a baseline labour market expectation. Signals of organisational readiness remain weak: only 21.3 per cent of job advertisements acknowledge any organisational role in enabling AI adoption, while the remaining 78.7 per cent present GenAI competence purely as a prerequisite for candidates. Skill complexity is almost evenly divided between basic and advanced requirements, and occupation strongly predicts this division, creating a clear distinction between a technically advanced group and a large group adopting AI on a more general operational level. Signals of organisational readiness remain weak: only 21.3 per cent of job advertisements acknowledge any organisational role in enabling AI adoption, while the remaining 78.7 per cent present GenAI competence purely as a prerequisite for candidates. Skill complexity is almost evenly divided between basic and advanced requirements, and occupation strongly predicts this division, creating a clear distinction between a technically advanced group and a large group adopting AI on a more general operational level.

title: From Adoption to Human-AI Leadership: A Scoping Review of Artificial Intelligence in Educational Leadership and Management
container-title: Social Scientific Centered Issues
1e0569103ec369b6f75ff1186f587acf5a4f67a0.abstract: This scoping review maps how artificial intelligence is conceptualized and used in educational leadership and management and examines the transition from technology adoption toward human-AI leadership. Following established scoping-review guidance and PRISMA-ScR, records from Scopus, Web of Science, and PubMed published or officially available online from 2022 to the final search date in 2026 were screened; items assigned a 2027 bibliographic year were eligible only if already available online before the cutoff. Of 747 records identified, 183 duplicates were removed and 323 records underwent title-and-abstract screening. Full texts were sought for 81 reports; two could not be retrieved, 79 were assessed for eligibility, and 50 studies were included. Four themes emerged: leadership readiness and capability; AI-augmented leadership practice; organizational conditions and institutional transformation; and human-AI agency, governance, and ethical boundaries. The evidence favors augmentation rather than autonomous substitution, with human judgment remaining central to accountability. The review proposes a five-stage Human-AI Educational Leadership Continuum integrating individual capability, organizational readiness, governance, and decision authority. The review was limited to three databases and English-language articles, and the evidence base remains methodologically heterogeneous and largely cross-sectional or context-specific.

title: From Communication Anxiety to Psychological Reliance
container-title: Journal of Media Psychology
bfda88b1644227e14d7f234fea59df6cb5059730.abstract: Abstract: Grounded in self-determination theory (SDT), this study investigates how communication anxiety and psychological need satisfaction relate to the use of Large Language Model (LLM)-based chatbots, specifically ChatGPT, for communication tasks (e.g., writing emails, drafting messages, and preparing scripts). Using a three-wave panel survey of participants from the United States and South Korea, we examined both between- and within-person dynamics. Results showed that individuals with higher trait-level communication anxiety tended to use ChatGPT more frequently for communication tasks, whereas within-person fluctuations in anxiety did not predict greater use. ChatGPT use was positively associated with the satisfaction of basic psychological needs – autonomy, competence, and relatedness – and this need satisfaction, in turn, was associated with greater psychological reliance on ChatGPT. Importantly, need satisfaction further mediated the relationship between ChatGPT use and psychological reliance at both within- and between-person levels. Cultural comparisons revealed that US participants exhibited stronger momentary effects, while Korean participants showed more stable, trait-based patterns. These findings highlight the role of LLM-based chatbots as need-supportive communication tools that may become integrated into users’ communication practices over time, with implications for theories of AI-mediated communication, cross-cultural research, and the design of human-AI communication systems.

title: Regulatory and scientific frameworks for AI-driven biosensor technologies in antimicrobial resistance monitoring
container-title: Frontiers in Medical Technology
ca04b8070cfb7b9f722852afe28eb10e6fa25a73.abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) diagnostics require evidence matched to the intended clinical or surveillance use. This narrative review synthesizes biosensor research, artificial intelligence (AI) analytics, and device oversight through a regulatory-scientific lifecycle perspective. Electrochemical and optical transduction are distinguished from microfluidic sample handling and nanomaterial enhancement. Pathogen identification, resistance-gene detection, phenotypic antimicrobial susceptibility testing (AST), minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) prediction, and population surveillance are compared by output, reference standard, and validation requirement. Representative Raman-machine-learning and microfluidic studies illustrate both analytical promise and limitations in independent clinical validation. The review maps these findings to US and European device pathways, software controls, interoperability, cybersecurity, and data governance. Its proposed five-phase framework adapts established total-product-lifecycle, quality-management, and risk-management principles to AMR-specific challenges, including emerging resistance mechanisms, breakpoint revisions, specimen shifts, and algorithm changes. The framework is a conceptual implementation tool, not a new regulatory pathway or an empirically validated model. Safe translation requires claim-specific validation and controlled updates rather than extrapolation from isolated prototype performance.

title: Exploring AI as a reading companion: L2 learners' approaches to literary comprehension
container-title: Foreign Language Annals
29d85c7100d4beb2a558fa842c9a1f66727182f2.abstract: Abstract Generative AI tools are increasingly present in language learning, yet their role in second language (L2) reading remains underexplored. This study investigates how intermediate German learners engaged with ChatGPT during interpretive reading using a three‐condition design with a Grimm fairytale. The study examines the relationship between AI access and reading performance, patterns of use or resistance, and students' ethical and motivational interpretations of AI‐mediated reading. Generative AI emerged as a negotiated presence that learners approached with curiosity, caution, or resistance. Required AI use was associated with reduced differences in comprehension outcomes across proficiency levels, whereas optional use revealed diverse strategic, reluctant, and value‐driven stances rooted in ethical concerns, discipline‐specific norms, and a desire to maintain interpretive autonomy. Students who routinely used AI in other courses engaged more selectively in German, suggesting AI practices may be shaped by disciplinary contexts. The findings support guided, reflective AI integration while valuing learner resistance.

title: AI-Powered Global Expansion: The Impact of Artificial Intelligence Adoption on Firms’ Outward Foreign Direct Investment
container-title: Journal of Academic Research and Advances
637d8e42c2f43232a8a9f9a4df0bdbd08128534a.abstract: Against the backdrop of profound shifts in the global economic landscape and rapid advances in digital technologies, artificial intelligence (AI) offers firms new opportunities to expand into international markets and improve the allocation of resources across borders. Drawing on a sample of Chinese A-share listed firms from 2009 to 2024, this study empirically examines the relationship between AI adoption and outward foreign direct investment (OFDI), with particular attention to the mechanisms underlying this relationship. The findings indicate that AI adoption is positively and significantly associated with firms’ OFDI activities. This result remains robust across a range of alternative specifications, including different measures of AI adoption, adjustments to fixed effects and standard-error clustering, and the exclusion of selected observations. Heterogeneity analyses suggest that the positive relationship is more pronounced among technology-intensive firms and larger enterprises. Further analysis identifies two potential channels through which AI adoption may facilitate OFDI: technological innovation and the alleviation of financial constraints. Together, these mechanisms may strengthen firms’ technological capabilities and improve their access to the financial resources required for international expansion. By examining OFDI through the lens of firm-level AI adoption, this study extends the literature on the determinants of international investment and provides further insight into how AI may shape firms’ internationalization strategies. The findings also offer empirical evidence relevant to the integration of AI into the real economy, the enhancement of firms’ international competitiveness, and China’s efforts to pursue higher-standard economic opening-up.

title: Predicting East Africa’s rainfall extremes with calibrated AI post-processing systems
container-title: npj Natural Hazards
ec9141399a544d08ca24ab587ea2340b91490af5.abstract: Abstract Accurate and reliable rainfall forecasts are crucial for Early Warning Systems (EWS). Artificial Intelligence approaches, which post-process global physical forecasts, enable low-cost ensemble generation, extending skill to medium-range lead times and offering scalable systems to inform EWS, particularly under resource-constrained settings. However, assessing their practical value in representing user-relevant rainfall extremes and guiding decisions for EWS remains critical. We present a low-cost, uncertainty quantification method that calibrates ensemble forecasts to probabilities of exceedances for rainfall extremes. Applied to raw and post-processed rainfall forecasts over East Africa, sub-regional analysis shows the threshold-calibrated, post-processed forecasts better reflecting the observed chances of extremes at higher rainfall thresholds. Case-study results show encouraging added value from post-processed forecasts at longer lead times. Forecast skill decomposed across rainfall and probability thresholds highlights the ranges of rainfall and risk tolerances where most actionable improvement arises, whether using satellite or rain-gauge data as reference. This tailored evaluation helps guide forecast adoption for EWS.

title: Measuring the geometric parameters of woven fabrics with AI chatbots: a benchmark and three paths to higher accuracy
container-title: Research Journal of Textile and Apparel
4d55cae7f658133b1c2ac11d6e85d0ac844e8650.abstract: Purpose Publicly available multimodal chatbots could make fabric geometry measurement accessible in low-resource settings, yet their accuracy for this task has never been systematically evaluated. This study aims to benchmark six such chatbots and investigates whether protocol-level improvements can raise measurement accuracy without model fine-tuning, unavailable to end users. Design/methodology/approach One hundred woven fabrics were scanned and their ground-truth values – weave type, thread count, cover factor, twist direction and twist angle – were measured according to ISO/ASTM. Six chatbots were tested with five runs per fabric, yielding 3,000 tests. Three improvement paths were examined: intra-system averaging, prompt enrichment with known fabric data and inter-system aggregation. Errors were quantified via misclassification rate (MCR) and mean absolute percentage error (MAPE). Findings Baseline accuracy was far below metrological requirements (MCR = 15–46%, MAPE = 9–34%). Three repeated runs indicated variability of ± 2–4 percentage points. Intra-system averaging and prompt refinement produced small, heterogeneous changes within this variability. Inter-system aggregation reduced five errors: weave MCR 32% to 21%, thread count MAPE 14% to 7%, cover factor MAPE 12% to 7%, twist direction MCR 32% to 20% and twist angle MAPE 28% to 18%. Paired tests showed significant differences between Path 3 and matched conditions after correction. Originality/value Aggregating heterogeneous, non-specialised chatbot outputs reduced fabric-geometry measurement error without model training. The resulting applicability matrices illustrate the potential operational range of each parameter, providing a parameter-by-parameter framework for interpreting the trade-off between accuracy and accessibility in low-infrastructure textile screening.

title: Governing work delegated to AI through dynamic control fit
b4bcf2ad069df09c25a6ca3a7753fd577733549c.abstract: Abstract When organizations delegate work to artificial intelligence (AI), controls that remain formally in place may no longer achieve their purposes. We combine systematic identification and selection with integrative analysis of 171 papers across five research streams and 26 supplementary sources. The synthesis develops dynamic control fit: an arrangement's ability to achieve a specified control function while sustaining or restoring the conditions on which that function depends. We explain this ability through a framework of three interconnected requirements: Deliver, Renew and Adapt. Deliver concerns whether coverage, information, expertise and opportunities to intervene support effective control in current work. Renew concerns the practice, feedback and maintenance through which these capabilities persist. Adapt concerns recognizing deficiencies, obtaining authorized changes and verifying restored performance. The framework explains how AI may improve immediate enforcement while reducing experiences through which people develop judgment for future oversight, although other activities may compensate. Coverage, reviewer capacity and revision authority impose distinct constraints requiring different responses. Continued reliance must also be assessed separately from performance because beliefs, external expectations and practical constraints can sustain or limit use. By following a specified function across changes in control arrangements, the review develops testable explanations of improvement, erosion, compensation and recovery.

title: When Is Something Alive? Integrating Bottom-Up and Top-Down Perspectives on Aliveness
container-title: Journal of Artificial Intelligence and Consciousness
76ca802569b2f2b00a5220af8d5f5cb05960cc03.abstract: What it means for an individual entity to be alive remains conceptually unresolved, particularly for artificial systems that display increasingly life-like behavior. This paper distinguishes life as an evolutionary, population-level process from aliveness as an individual property, and develops a candidate condition for assessing when an entity, biological or artificial, should be considered alive. A bottom-up heuristic identifies structural and functional characteristics commonly associated with biological organisms, but applying this heuristic to an embodied artificial agent shows that such characteristics are not by themselves sufficiently discriminative. A complementary top-down perspective introduces self-referential regulation, understood as the capacity of an entity to internally represent and regulate its own continued existence through embodied causal processes. Integrating both perspectives yields a unified candidate condition for aliveness, proposed primarily for complex entities while leaving open how aliveness should be characterized in simpler ones.

title: Does it matter if agentic AI is an author? effort and Nigerian Copyright Law
container-title: The Journal of World Intellectual Property
ec516169dbb7c13b285128fc4a3660775ca0e2a9.abstract: Abstract Agentic AI complicates copyright by unsettling the basis on which authorship is attributed, particularly where effort bears on originality and protection. This article asks what makes effort legally authorial, examining Nigerian copyright law, whose originality threshold requires effort to give a work original character, alongside comparative doctrine. That formulation reflects a common‐law tradition attentive to labour, skill and judgment, distinct from the European emphasis on the author's own intellectual creation and free and creative choices. The article argues that neither the quantity of labour involved in production nor the operational agency attributed to an AI system establishes authorship by itself. What matters is the relation between the claimed effort and the determination of copyright‐relevant expression. This difficulty is especially apparent where systems generate music with limited human intervention. Agentic production thus exposes a broader problem of legal attribution. Copyright may continue to seek an author even where production no longer coheres around one. The article describes the unsettled condition surrounding this shift as nescience, arguing that it counsels legal restraint rather than inaction. Where no qualifying human authorial contribution to the resulting expression can be established, copyright protection should be withheld, leaving fully AI‐generated expression in the public domain.

title: Love Takes Time: Faster Romantic Onset, Lower Closeness, and Similarity Benefits in Human-AI Relationships
container-title: Journal of Language and Social Psychology
0dfcaccfe33e6f40a134f0287b4cf4245a067bff.abstract: As human–artificial intelligence (AI) romantic relationships become increasingly prevalent, understanding how they develop is important. Such relationships differ from human–human relationships in how AI partners accommodate user needs and preferences, potentially influencing relationship development and closeness. In this survey ( N = 167), individuals who reported falling in love more quickly with human partners also tended to do so with AI partners. However, paired within-subject analyses ( n = 110) revealed that participants perceived a faster overall pace of falling in love with AI than human partners, driven primarily by shorter conversation lengths rather than fewer days or total conversations. Despite this expediency, participants reported greater current relational closeness with human partners than AI partners. Perceived similarity with AI partners was positively associated with relational closeness and relationship quality with AI. These findings suggest that human–AI romantic relationships may develop rapidly through familiar interpersonal processes such as similarity attraction, yet involve lower relational closeness.

title: Healthsync-AI: Health Monitoring and AI-Driven Emergency System
1f6d853a3e4994c47c22e6f1ddda21f5145442f8.abstract: Abstract HealthSync AI (HSAI) is an intelligent health monitoring system designed to make personal healthcare more accessible, convenient, and proactive through the integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI), the Internet of Things (IoT), and software technology. In today's busy lifestyle, people may overlook changes in their health until they become serious, highlighting the need for continuous monitoring and timely awareness. HealthSync AI addresses this need by providing a desktop application where users can manage their health profiles, monitor vital signs and physical activity through compatible Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) devices, and store their health information securely in a user-specific database. The system uses AI-based analysis to examine available health readings, identify unusual patterns, and provide personalized health insights and general wellness recommendations. It also incorporates features such as nearby hospital discovery, emergency contact support, and outbreak-related information to help users make more informed decisions. By combining wearable sensor data, intelligent analysis, and an easy-to-use interface, HealthSync AI aims to encourage healthier habits and support early awareness of potential health concerns. The system is intended to complement, rather than replace, professional medical advice and diagnosis. Right now, our healthcare system is fundamentally reactive, meaning people usually only end up in a hospital after their symptoms have already become severe. Most healthcare apps available today are pretty limited, functioning mostly as digital filing cabinets for storing medical records or simple tools for booking appointments. On a broader scale, public health authorities are constantly fighting an uphill battle. Because medical data is scattered across different systems and reporting is often delayed, officials struggle to spot disease outbreaks at an early stage when intervention could actually save lives. To move far beyond the single-metric limitations of typical open-source projects, HealthSync AI is designed to ingest and process eleven distinct telemetry streams simultaneously, offering a complete and continuous window into a user's physiological state. This multi-parameter data doesn't just sit in a silo; it is securely managed through local SQLite persistence and channeled into an intelligent backend framework that processes structured health observations rather than relying on superficial, generic API wrapper chatbots. The platform also tackles the broader systemic issues of delayed reporting and fragmented medical data by introducing integrated outbreak analysis. While traditional systems leave public health authorities struggling to spot community-level risks in time, HealthSync AI bridges individual continuous monitoring with aggregated insights to help track potential health threats at an early stage. Combined with built-in emergency response features and a clean separation of responsibilities across its BLE, database, and UI layers, HealthSync AI transforms personal wellness tracking and community health intelligence into a single, cohesive, and future-ready solution.

title: AI Leaderboard Governance: A 56-Board Audit of Submission, Retesting, and Score Removal Rules
c27b6f460ac94333e25f77bc6599cd976c1f6fdd.abstract: Background. A leaderboard gives a score, but not necessarily the rules behind it: who could submit a model, whether variants were tested privately, how uncertainty was reported, or when a score could be removed or corrected. Methods. I built a source-traced registry of 56 public AI leaderboards from the operators' own pages (source rows checked 2026-10-20, probes 2026-10-24). I coded five procedural disclosure dimensions and three further cells as stated or not found in the material searched. Results. A submission route or rule was stated on 32 boards and a contamination mechanism on 24. A repeat requirement was stated on 7 and uncertainty reporting on 20 (21 in all). Removal or correction rules appeared on 6 (4 prospective removal rules, 1 correction rule, 1 discretionary disqualification). Some private-testing, exposure, publication or submission-frequency disclosure appeared on 7, including 4 that describe private pre-release variants. In the searched material, 9 boards stated none of the five dimensions. Validation. I checked quotations verbatim against saved pages; every one of the 90 stated cells across the five dimensions has a cell-specific passage. The classifications remain provisional. AI quote-window agreement, measured against pre-adjudication labels, varied by dimension. An independent AI adjudicator reading excerpts agreed with 43 of 50 sampled labels (5 undecidable; the two disagreements were recoded). Human and whole-page validation are not complete. Contribution. The Leaderboard Governance Registry makes these disclosures, their sources and the search boundaries available as a versioned, machine-readable record. It does not measure policy enforcement or ranking integrity.

title: Gender Differences in Conditional Willingness and Trust Expectations for AI Legal Services in Bangladesh
56f8c5fec9ddf79eb9ed6216c0f81d8b151bfe65.abstract: Abstract Artificial intelligence may widen access to legal information while reproducing inequalities in who can use, evaluate and challenge its outputs. Research on gender and legal AI therefore needs to distinguish conditional willingness to use a service from confidence that its design supports trustworthy operation. This study examines that distinction in the supplied Group 10 Law-SDG database, linking gender and technology, procedural justice and digital inclusion perspectives. All 385 records inform descriptive analysis; comparisons between respondents recorded as female and male use 364 records, with the remaining gender responses retained descriptively. Item-level analysis combines distributional comparisons, stratified bootstrap intervals, paired contrasts and covariate-adjusted logistic models. Conditional willingness was endorsed by 307 records (79.7%), whereas 198 (51.4%) endorsed the proposition that inclusive design can improve trust. Their paired difference was 28.3 percentage points (95% bootstrap interval 21.8–34.8). The female-minus-male willingness difference was − 0.7 points (-9.0-7.5); the adjusted difference was 1.0 point (-7.4-9.4). Inclusive-design trust expectations and discrimination salience likewise showed small estimated gender contrasts with substantial uncertainty. Low block reliability precluded latent-scale modelling. The findings support neither a gender-deficit explanation nor a claim of established equality: similar reported willingness can coexist with unequal access and unmeasured exposure to harm. The contribution is a measurement-conscious distinction between conditional acceptance, trust expectations and substantive inclusion. Interpretation remains bounded by undocumented recruitment and by codebook labels identifying respondent sequences and comments as synthetic; numeric response provenance requires verification before these records can support claims about a human population.

title: Magnetic Microfluidics with AI-Based Cell Level Quantification of Nanoparticle Delivery
container-title: ACS Applied Engineering Materials
b7f2c8feb2b9378c6236def81ee8325c748b72aa.abstract: Abstract Targeted therapeutic delivery to sites of nerve injury remains a major challenge in regenerative medicine, where efficient treatment requires maximizing local drug concentration while minimizing off-target effects. Recently, microfluidic platforms have proven to be powerful tools for modeling physiological flow and drug delivery. Here, we used iron oxide nanoparticles conjugated to nerve growth factor (NGF-MNPs) and applied an external magnetic field to defined target regions within a microfluidic device. Using live imaging, we first visualize the flow of fluorescent MNPs within the device to track particle displacement under magnetic stimulation. The resulting shift in particle trajectories, designed to mimic physiological flow conditions, was quantified to assess the influence of the magnetic field on nanoparticle behavior. We next quantified the accumulation of MNP-associated fluorescent puncta at a single-cell resolution utilizing state-of-the-art artificial intelligence and image processing approaches for segmentation, enabling optimization of nanoparticle internalization per cell as a function of external magnetic field application and nanoparticle size. We also demonstrated that PC12 cells exposed to NGF-MNPs within the microfluidic device exhibited efficient growth and differentiation. Finally, our results showed that a strong magnetic field increased MNP internalization by 116% relative to conditions without external magnetic stimulation, highlighting the efficiency of magnetically guided drug delivery. In all, these findings establish a magnetic microfluidic delivery platform approach for guiding therapeutic nanoparticles under physiologically relevant flow conditions. This integrated platform approach provides a quantitative foundation for future neurorepair systems and supports the development of magnetically guided regenerative drug delivery technologies.
