title: The cicada genus Albanycada Villet, 1989 (Hemiptera, Cicadidae): systematic revision
container-title: African Invertebrates
91d539f1e77cc488143e368c149620a27925ad73.abstract: Phylogenetic analysis of the nucleotide sequences of the cytochrome oxidase I gene of specimens of Albanycada Villet, 1989 supported the hypothesis that the genus includes more than one species-level lineage. Comparison of the syntype of Platypleura albigera Walker, 1850, the type species of Albanycada , with the syntypes of Platypleura membranacea Karsch, 1890 confirmed that the two species are synonyms, so the other lineage is described under the name Albanycada bellinganorum Villet & Price, sp. nov . Lectotypes are designated for P. albigera Walker, 1850 and P. membranacea Karsch, 1890 to reflect these comparisons. Its morphology, geographical distribution, and calling song are illustrated. Ecological and conservation notes are summarised for both species, and their phylogenetic origins are discussed.

title: Green AI for Telehealth
container-title: Healthcare Management Forum
7b0a606b53c98d3d725366c54edc67aca709604e.abstract: Telehealth is increasingly supported by connected devices, remote monitoring, Artificial Intelligence (AI), and distributed computing. These tools can extend access and support more responsive care, but their computational and environmental demands are rarely considered alongside clinical and organizational needs. We describe the current Canadian telehealth landscape, including remote care management, virtual visits, patient portals, and remote monitoring, and identify opportunities and gaps for AI integration. We then define Green AI in healthcare and explain how an IoT–fog–cloud architecture can support resource-aware telehealth. For health leaders, Green AI is not only an engineering issue. It affects procurement, infrastructure planning, workforce capacity, clinical workflow, environmental responsibility, and equity. Evaluation should consider clinical performance, resource use, organizational fit, and sustainability. Responsible AI-enabled telehealth requires more than technical performance. A Green AI perspective can help health organizations improve computational efficiency while maintaining patient safety, usable workflows, resilience, and equitable access.

title: Explainable AI-Based Pulmonary Nodule Classification from Computed Tomography Images with an End-to-End Clinical Decision Support Interface
88c30d289bf1b961035f9e444a0fba8d0eecea5a.abstract: Abstract Early and accurate detection of pulmonary nodules in computed tomography (CT) imaging is critical for reducing lung cancer mortality. Although deep learning-based computer-aided detection (CAD) systems have demonstrated promis-ing diagnostic performance, their widespread clinical adoption has been impeded by two persistent limitations: the absence of visual explainability and the lack of deployable end-to-end interfaces that integrate prediction, explanation, and clinical workflow. This paper presents an explainable, end-to-end CAD system for pulmonary nodule classification that addresses both shortcomings. The proposed system employs a transfer-learned ResNet-50 architecture, fine-tuned on 2,372 balanced CT patches extracted from the publicly available LUNA16 dataset. Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping (Grad-CAM) is integrated into the inference pipeline to generate per-prediction heatmaps that visually localize the discriminative regions driv-ing each classification decision. The complete system is deployed as a production-grade web application featuring a FastAPI backend and a React frontend, complete with authentication and database persistence. On a held-out test set of 356 samples, the proposed system achieves an accuracy of 90.45%, precision of 90.91%, recall of 89.89%, F1 score of 90.40%, and an AUC-ROC of 0.9615. A confidence-based abstention mechanism returns an “Inconclusive” verdict for predictions below a 60% probability threshold, reducing the risk of unreliable automated decisions. Rather than claiming state-of-the-art raw accuracy, this work’s principal contribution is demonstrating that competitive classification performance, real-time visual explainability, and a fully deployed, browser-accessible clinical interface can be integrated into a single reproducible, open-source system, contributing a practical baseline for future hospital validation studies.

title: Should there be a teacher in-the-loop? A study of generative AI-personalized tasks middle school
container-title: Educational technology research and development
71e2c405c203835b767e5e282172a8a2716b2168.abstract: Abstract Large language models can be used to design instructional tasks to align to students’ needs. These generative AI models can create tasks that correspond to students’ out-of-school interests in areas like sports or music, which may enhance students’ interest in learning. However, little is known about teachers’ processes for creating or modifying tasks with generative AI, despite commercial AI companies’ claims that they will save teachers time. In the present study, 7 middle school mathematics teachers used ChatGPT to create personalized versions of problems in their curriculum to correspond to their students’ interests. The prompting moves teachers made and their students’ open-ended feedback on personalized problems were examined through thematic analysis. Teachers’ efficiency when creating problems and the ratings of their 7th grade students who received personalized assignments were examined. Results from this sample suggest that having a teacher-in-the-loop may result in generative AI-enhanced personalization being enacted at a broad grain size, whereas students often expressed preference for a smaller grain-size where they receive specific popular culture references that interest them. Teachers used prompting to adjust popular culture references and address issues with the depth, ethics, or realism of the problems generated, in some cases showing epistemic agency. The article closes with an exploratory, design-focused look at scalability trade-offs with teacher-facing personalization, patterns of teacher prompting practices, and opportunities for teachers to exercise epistemic and ethical monitoring of personalization outputs.

title: The association between interpersonal alienation and problematic use of conversational AI among adolescents: A mediated network analysis of perceived anthropomorphism and AI attachment
container-title: Journal of Behavioral Addictions
ff534d5ad54fc3950fd718f5f9991e0436ac0790.abstract: Abstract Background and aims With the rapid development of conversational artificial intelligence (CAI), problematic use of conversational AI (PUCAI) among adolescents has attracted increasing attention. However, the underlying psychological factors associated with PUCAI remain unclear. Guided by the Interaction of Person-Affect-Cognition-Execution (I-PACE) model, this study explored the associations between interpersonal alienation, perceived anthropomorphism, AI attachment, and PUCAI. Methods Data were collected from 1,124 Chinese high school students (516 males, 608 females; M age = 16.59). Serial mediation analysis and network analysis were conducted. Results Interpersonal alienation was positively associated with PUCAI. It also had indirect associations through both parallel and serial mediation involving perceived anthropomorphism and AI attachment. Network analysis further revealed that perceived anthropomorphism exhibited the highest bridge expected influence, and emotional trust showed the highest centrality. Conclusion These findings suggest that adolescent PUCAI is associated not only with general psychological risk factors but also with social-cognitive perceptions and emotional bonding experiences during human–AI interactions. This study provides a novel perspective for understanding problematic use behaviors in emerging human–AI interaction contexts and offers implications for future risk assessment and research on healthy AI use.

title: Where Do We Look? Visual Attention Competition Between Hyper-Salient Objects and AI-Generated Virtual Endorsers in Generative Artificial Intelligence Advertising
container-title: Journal of Eye Movement Research
36fc050f60ce8845ba8db20a6617fcac6439e5ea.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) advertising, defined as advertising content created or substantially assisted by generative AI systems (AIGC), has introduced new visual features that combine algorithmically generated objects with human-like representations. Hyper-salient objects, defined by exaggerated perceptual prominence and semantic incongruity, and AI-generated virtual endorsers, represented by human-like AI-created figures, have become increasingly common in such advertisements. However, little is known about how these distinct visual cues compete for consumers’ limited attentional resources when presented together. Drawing on visual attention and scene perception perspectives, this study investigated how hyper-salient objects and AI-generated virtual endorsers influence visual attention allocation in AI-generated advertising. A 2 (hyper-salient object: present vs. absent) × 2 (AI endorser: present vs. absent) between-subjects eye-tracking experiment was conducted with 160 participants in a controlled laboratory setting using static AI-generated advertisements. Eye movements were recorded, and memory was assessed using signal detection measures (d′) from a recognition task involving target and distractor advertisements. Advertising attitude and product trust were measured using established scales. Results from linear and generalized linear mixed-effects models showed that hyper-salient objects increased early fixation probability and attracted a larger dwell time proportion, demonstrating strong attentional capture. AI-generated endorsers also attracted attention when presented alone, but their proportional attention share decreased when hyper-salient objects were simultaneously present. The effects of these visual elements on memory and product trust were conditional on their co-occurrence rather than uniform across conditions. Within the specific set of experimentally constructed stimuli and four sampled product categories, this research contributes to AIGC advertising literature by developing a visual competition perspective on how multiple AI-generated visual cues interact under limited attentional capacity, offering implications for designing effective generative AI advertisements.

title: Unlocking Radical Innovation Through AI Orientation: The Roles of Knowledge Search, Knowledge Recombination Creation, and CEO Openness
container-title: Systems
590a10f8f90535ff916d657c2ad8b0aecb63dbd7.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is crucial for driving radical innovation, which is key for firms to gain and maintain long-term competitive advantage. However, relatively little is known about how radical innovation is shaped by strategic direction regarding AI, and the perspective from when this innovation takes place. Drawing on the knowledge-based view and the upper echelons theory, this study delves into how and when AI orientation impacts radical innovation. Based on data from 510 Chinese manufacturing listed firms over the period 2013–2023, our study demonstrates a significant positive effect of AI orientation on radical innovation, and provides evidence consistent with positive indirect associations through knowledge search and knowledge recombination creation. Our findings also provide evidence that CEO openness may strengthen the positive relationships of AI orientation with radical innovation and knowledge search. Further, our findings make contributions to strategic orientation and technological innovation literature, and offer implications for practice in AI-innovation research by stressing the influence of knowledge and CEO personality in radical innovation domains.

title: From post-editing to prompting
container-title: Translation and Translanguaging in Multilingual Contexts
d424fcf44502667e6a60fc58c426437d6562f9b9.abstract: Abstract This study compares traditional translation and post-editing with generative-AI-assisted translation in Arabic–English translation education. Drawing on 68 task records completed by 58 undergraduate students through EduApp, it examines observable effort, textual intervention, and implications for translation competence. The findings indicate that AI-assisted tasks involved significantly more written or entered characters and a higher length ratio, but no statistically significant difference in task completion time. Qualitative analysis suggests a shift from local correction to broader reformulation, including more formal institutional phrasing and syntactic restructuring. The study concludes that AI-assisted translation redistributes rather than eliminates student effort and requires evaluative and interactive skills alongside established translation abilities.

title: Health Data that Follows the Patient: The European Health Data Space and its Perspectives for Clinical Practice, Clinical Studies, and AI
container-title: EMJ Innovation
ffa9144b4752eb9d5236581f307c7373e15cf413.abstract: Health data are generated across Europe in great volume, yet remain distributed across institutions, registries, and national systems that do not communicate. For clinicians, relevant information is hard to assemble, and eligible patients remain invisible to research. The European Health Data Space (EHDS) Regulation is the EU’s response. Its primary use is setting common interoperability requirements and individual rights, so that records can be exchanged and accessed by citizens and HCPs across systems and borders. Its secondary use is to establish a governance framework in which national Health Data Access Bodies (HDAB) grant controlled access for research, innovation, and policy-making. Most obligations will apply in stages from 2029. This article considers the implications for clinical practice, clinical studies, and AI, with examples from two European projects. REpresentative Clinical Research – ADvancing Inclusivity in Europe (READI) addresses the representativeness of clinical studies, in part by helping study sites and patients find each other. The Supporting Health Data Access Bodies to establish AI pathways enabling Deployment of AI as medical device tools (SHAIPED) project examines HDAB pathways for AI-based medical devices, including the transportability of a chronic kidney disease risk model to other European countries. The EHDS offers a foundation, not a guarantee: legacy systems, uneven digital maturity, partly paper-based documentation, governance, and patient trust will shape whether better access translates into more equitable care and research. Whether implementation narrows or widens existing gaps between member states remains open.

title: Evaluating the AI-predictive potential of the PIC database for pediatric ICU mortality
container-title: Pediatric Research
a1027cf94e9d7475764d0cee5472fd585fd57344.abstract: Abstract Background Reliable Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools in healthcare depend on both data quality and model design. However, the predictive integrity of datasets is rarely assessed. Publicly available resources for critically ill children remain scarce. The Pediatric Intensive Care (PIC) database remains, to the best of current knowledge, the only open-access resource focused on pediatric critical care research. Methods This study evaluates the predictive potential of the PIC database. After applying strict cohort selection and data preprocessing, mortality risk was analyzed using statistical analysis through univariate Odds Ratio (OR) to measure associations, and machine learning (ML) models interpreted through SHAP values to assess feature importance and model behavior. Results ML experiments showed moderate but limited predictive performance for mortality. CatBoost performed best, with an AUC of 0.8521 (0.8414–0.8627) on the hold-out test set, but low sensitivity (42%) limited its ability to identify non-survivors. These findings suggest dataset-related constraints that reduce clinical reliability. Most relevant variables were minimum lactate, maximum lactate, mean respiratory rate, maximum hematocrit, and minimum urea. Conclusion Analysis showed that PIC lacks essential physiological data, highlighting the limits of current pediatric databases and the need for richer multicenter datasets to enable more robust, clinically applicable AI models. Impact Provides the first comprehensive evaluation of the PIC database, assessing its suitability for machine learning-based predictive modeling. Identifies key clinical variables and data gaps that influence the reliability of AI–based mortality prediction and model performance. Underscores the need for richer, multicenter pediatric ICU databases for research that incorporate essential physiological and neurological indicators. Demonstrates the value of combining statistical association and AI interpretability methods to assess the predictive integrity of clinical datasets.

title: Staged sternal distraction for early thoracic expansion in Shwachman–Diamond syndrome
container-title: The Annals of The Royal College of Surgeons of England
65c78afe9e5445c1df3281d2904c83c9f0252f28.abstract: Shwachman–Diamond syndrome (SDS) is a rare inherited multisystem disorder with variable skeletal involvement; severe neonatal thoracic dystrophy is uncommon but can cause thoracic insufficiency and mimic Jeune syndrome. We report staged sternal distraction in a 5-month-old infant with a severely constricted thorax, pulmonary hypoplasia, refractory pulmonary hypertension, tracheostomy-dependent respiratory failure and an iatrogenic posterior tracheal wall injury. Subsequent trio long-read genome sequencing identified compound heterozygous pathogenic variants in SBDS, c.183_184delinsCT (p.Lys62Ter), inherited paternally, and c.258+2T>C, inherited maternally, establishing a molecular diagnosis of SDS. At presentation, the chest circumference measured 36cm, compared with an age-expected value of 41cm. The patient underwent staged median sternotomy distraction followed by stabilisation with custom fibular allograft struts. At approximately 3 months, chest circumference had increased to 41cm, peak inspiratory pressures had decreased from 40–50cm H 2 O to the mid-20cm H 2 O range, pulmonary hypertension was no longer evident on echocardiography, and the tracheal injury had healed. At 6 months, he remained on home mechanical ventilation, with peak inspiratory pressures in the upper 20cm H 2 O range. To our knowledge, operative thoracic expansion specifically for SDS-associated thoracic insufficiency has not previously been described. In carefully selected infants with severe thoracic insufficiency who are not yet candidates for conventional thoracic reconstruction, staged sternal distraction may serve as an interim strategy to achieve meaningful thoracic expansion.

title: Ethical Implications of Generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) Use Among Library and Information Science (LIS) Students: A Narrative Review
container-title: Education for Information
cfb0b4301f1f8befc86d8ba35dd13d0f98160b83.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence is increasingly being used by students and is reshaping the way information is accessed, processed, and utilised for academic work and everyday purposes. As the use of AI technologies continues to expand, there is a growing need to discuss the ethical implications associated with the use of generative AI among LIS students. This study employed a narrative review method to analyse and synthesise evidence from existing scholarly literature obtained through various library resources and online databases on the Internet. The study identified several ethical implications regarding the use of generative AI among LIS students, which include breaches of academic integrity, plagiarism risks, misinformation, output bias, privacy and security concerns, reduced critical engagement with learning materials, overdependence on AI systems, fabricated references, and so on. The findings revealed that ethical use of generative AI requires LIS students to critically evaluate AI-generated content, acknowledge AI assistance where necessary, and maintain responsibility for the accuracy and originality of their academic work. The study showed areas for future research directions in ethical concerns of generative AI use among LIS students for responsible AI use in academic practices.

title: Artificial intelligence in radiology education: from AI-supported learning to clinical innovation—a narrative review
container-title: Frontiers in Medicine
14bc18448b3e1dd017f9fcc36decfc4878a507b1.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is changing diagnostic radiology, but education and training have not kept pace. This narrative review brings together current evidence on AI-supported learning in radiology education and how such learning can move into clinical innovation. Surveys from different countries point to the same gap: in a 25-country international survey of radiographers, radiologists, and students, only 10.3% had received formal AI training; in one national survey of Turkish residents, 84.5% had received none. The review maps competency frameworks and curriculum models that define AI literacy and support staged integration into residency. It also assesses AI as a teaching tool, including AI-assisted case-based learning, computer-aided diagnosis training, precision-education knowledge recommenders, and virtual, augmented, and extended reality. Controlled and randomized studies show measurable gains: computer-aided diagnosis training raised resident scores above self-study controls (mean score 52 vs. 38 on a 100-point scale), while an AI-based knowledge recommender shortened reporting time by 162 s per case and relative improvement in graded reporting accuracy scores of 14% (95% CI 8.1–19.8%). Large language models are promising but limited: GPT-4 approaches board-style examination performance (80.6%) yet remains poor at image-based reasoning (47.8%). The review closes by considering how education can feed clinical innovation, along with algorithmic and automation bias, ethical governance, and future research needs. AI education should therefore span the full continuum-from undergraduate training to continuing professional development-if radiology is to innovate safely, effectively, and equitably.

title: Technical Evaluations in the Field of AI Music Composition
container-title: International Journal of Advanced Research in Science Communication and Technology
5df941c743a153546d43a193ffb4af5972b864dd.abstract: AI-based music composition has progressed from symbolic melody generation to systems that produce audio from natural-language prompts, melodic references, or combinations of both. However, the perceived usefulness of a generated track cannot be captured by audio realism alone. A system may sound convincing yet ignore the requested mood, lose musical structure over time, offer little editing control, or provide insufficient information about the provenance of its training data. This paper develops a practical, multidimensional framework for evaluating AI music composition systems. The framework organizes evaluation into five dimensions: audio and musical quality, prompt and structure alignment, controllability and editability, workflow usefulness, and responsible-use transparency. It proposes a staged evaluation protocol combining listening tests, task-based assessment, technical checks, and documentation review. The framework is a conceptual synthesis informed by published work on text-to-music generation, controllable music models, synthetic-music detection, and the supplied systematic review of AI music composition. No new experimental dataset or performance results are claimed. The paper's contribution is an evaluation blueprint that researchers, developers, educators, and music practitioners can adapt before conducting empirical validation

title: Qualitative Study on the Role of AI-Driven Problem Based Learning in Transforming Biology Classroom for Dual Mandate System in Nigeria
container-title: Federal University Gusau Faculty of Education Journal
25866bb3a5bedda7128257900d82074e053dfedd.abstract: Dual mandate - the federal College of Education act 2023 signed by President Bola Ahmed Tinubu legally and officially empowered these institutions to award education degrees while the NCE programmes continues. The Nigerian curriculum for biology at the senior secondary school level is designed to help students develop a range of skills which include understanding biological concepts and principles, application of the knowledge to solve real-life situations, problem solving skills and ability to communicate biological ideas and concepts effectively. Problem based learning is a pedagogical approach that involves students learning through the experience of solving real world problems. It is a student centered approach that encourages critical and creative thinking, collaboration, active learning and application of skills to solve real world problems. Problem based learning can be effectively integrated with STEM subjects; science, technology, education and mathematics. Problem based learning is grounded in several theories like constructivist, social constructivism posits by Vygotsky 1978. Artificial Intelligence has the potential to make up for the shortcomings of traditional problem based learning by giving full account of students reports in the project, timely feedback and helps teachers to monitor students learning outcome. AI tools used in education/science include machine learning algorithms; natural language processing techniques which are used to create personalized learning; AI powered VR or AR are also used. AI driven PBL used include Khammigo or custom GPT, Google Docs, Padlet AI, Gradescope, Google sheets etc. The global AI in education market size was estimated at USD 5.88 billion in 2024 is projected to grow at Compound Annual Growth Rate (CAGR) of 31.2% from 2025 to 2030. However, with PBL, the teachers have to provide students with necessary resources e.g. learning materials, tools and technological support as well as guidance. One of the opportunities of integrating AI in education include personalized learning, creating more interactive and immersive learning experiences, games and simulations that boost students confidence, motivation and persistence leading to improved academic achievement.

title: Public Awareness of Artificial Intelligence (AI) Utilisation in Healthcare Institutions in Anambra State
container-title: RESEARCH JOURNAL OF MASS COMMUNICATION AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY
62381fb047bb10071282679fbff11b561b408c75.abstract: Given the growing adoption of AI-driven diagnostic and treatment tools across health systems, understanding community awareness is crucial for effective integration and health communication. Applying the survey design, data were collected from 384 adult residents selected from across six Local Government Areas of Anambra State, Nigeria, using multistage and proportionate sampling techniques. Findings revealed a moderately high level of awareness of AI utilisation, with respondents expressing the strongest familiarity with AI-powered tools such as automated diagnostics and virtual assistants. Social media emerged as the dominant source of AI information, followed by traditional media, while healthcare providers contributed minimally to public knowledge. Respondents also recognised significant benefits of AI, including improved diagnostic accuracy, enhanced service delivery, and overall healthcare quality. However, concerns were evident regarding potential medical errors, privacy concerns, and job displacement of healthcare workers. These findings align with national and international studies showing high exposure but limited depth of understanding among the public and health workers. Guided by the Diffusion of Innovations and Agenda-Setting theories, the study concludes that public awareness is largely media-driven and remains at an early diffusion stage, underscoring the need for deliberate institutional communication, ethical safeguards, and structured public sensitisation. The study recommends strengthening health communication strategies, promoting data protection frameworks, and enhancing healthcare worker involvement in public AI education.

title:
Nanotechnology-Integrated
Diagnostic Platforms toward
Decentralized Infectious Disease Management
container-title: ACS Nano
66a5821c95bf68c4608967740f2e3e4a6671a5b2.abstract: Abstract Nanotechnology-integrated diagnostic platforms are increasingly being developed across infectious disease management, from screening and diagnosis to potentially treatment-guiding assessment and monitoring. Yet current progress has rarely been synthesized from a clinical management perspective, making it difficult to determine which technologies are ready for decentralized use, where progress remains fragmented, and which clinical needs remain unmet. This review examines nanotechnology-enabled strategies according to how they enable the sample-to-answer workflow, rather than classifying them by material type. Major diagnostic platform architectures are then assessed in terms of practical implementation, with emphasis on platform-specific limitations and emerging solutions. Current applications are further mapped across the infectious disease management continuum to identify established capabilities, missing links, and disconnects from clinical workflows. The broader changes needed to close these gaps are also discussed. This review aims to clarify how nanotechnology-integrated diagnostic platforms can be better developed toward decentralized, reliable, and clinically actionable infectious disease management.

title: Why Do University Students Use AI: Drivers and Barriers?
container-title: Journal of Higher Education Theory and Practice
a7ba4434497a8206487ea5dc62f7c019c23b0ffb.abstract: As generative artificial intelligence becomes integrated into academic life, understanding what drives student adoption is essential for informed institutional policy. This study examines AI engagement among 672 students at a public midsize southern university, integrating the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) and Social Cognitive Theory (SCT) to evaluate eight constructs: perceived usefulness, perceived ease of use, perceived trust, perceived risk, social influence, self-efficacy, anxiousness, and affection. Survey data show students frequently use AI for information retrieval and writing assistance, while specialized applications such as graphic and video generation remain underutilized. Regression analysis shows perceived usefulness, affection, and trust are the primary positive predictors of adoption, whereas anxiety and perceived risk are significant deterrents. Notably, affection, the emotional enjoyment of technology, emerged as one of the most consistent motivators across academic tasks, from research to creative ideation. These results suggest emotional and trust-based factors are as critical as functional utility in shaping student behavior. Universities should prioritize emotional comfort and ethical trust alongside technical training to foster responsible, confident AI integration..

title:
High-Efficiency Multistimuli Responsive Carbon Dots
with Near-100% Photoluminescence Quantum Yield for Anticounterfeiting
Technologies
container-title: ACS Central Science
e696e350ea70172c78e11663353959951592cc5e.abstract: Abstract With the rising demand for information security and anticounterfeiting, developing intelligent luminescent materials responsive to external stimuli is crucial for enhancing encryption and anticounterfeiting technologies. Herein, a facile one-pot solvothermal strategy was developed to prepare multistimuli responsive carbon dots (CDs), which exhibit solvent-responsive, concentration-responsive, and pH-responsive properties, along with a photoluminescence quantum yield (PLQY) approaching 100% in aqueous dispersion. Systematic investigations reveal that the high PLQY of the CDs originates from the cross-arranged nonextended conjugation of perylene-based backbones in the CDs core, which prevent further π–π stacking. In addition, surface functional groups regulate solvent-dependent luminescence behavior through polar interactions and hydrogen bonding. As the concentration increased, enhanced intermolecular interactions induce the emission from monomer-dominated to aggregate-dominated states. Furthermore, under different pH conditions, reversible protonation and deprotonation of surface functional groups enable dynamic modulation of the electronic structure, thereby regulating the fluorescence emission. By combining with polymers, multicolor high-brightness polymer powders with PLQY approaching 100% were successfully prepared. These composite materials demonstrate excellent performance in handicraft decoration and anticounterfeiting systems. This work not only provides a theoretical basis for the design of highly efficient luminescent CDs but also expands their potential in intelligent materials and photonic applications.

title: Designing a Human–AI Collaborative Blended Learning Framework for EFL Speaking Development
container-title: Jurnal Arbitrer
4135691faa6a06a94879c23def856361f75264c6.abstract: While artificial intelligence (AI) technologies such as conversational chatbots and speech recognition systems are increasingly adopted in language education, existing research focuses predominantly on isolated tools rather than integrated instructional models. This study proposes and evaluates a Human–AI Collaborative Blended Learning Framework for the development of English as a Foreign Language (EFL) speaking skills. Using a two-phase research design, the study first synthesizes contemporary literature to establish a 7-layer conceptual framework that connects stakeholder participation, learner profiling, a Human–AI collaboration engine, blended activities, adaptive speaking services, teacher facilitation, and continuous learning analytics. Second, the framework was evaluated through an expert validation survey involving 52 specialists in language education, applied linguistics, and educational technology (40.4% PhDs, 57.7% Master’s). Quantitative findings revealed strong endorsement for actionable teacher support dashboards (80.8% agreement), visual pronunciation feedback (78.8%), and private AI speaking practice for anxiety reduction (75.0%; M = 2.98/4.00). However, experts expressed reservations regarding automated prompts for language elaboration (53.8% agreement), fixed 14-meeting schedules (57.7%), and automated grading weights (57.7%). Qualitative analysis highlighted that acceptance remains conditional upon accent fairness, data privacy, and active teacher oversight. Implications: Theoretically, the study advances AI-assisted language learning by establishing a human-centered collaborative model that prioritizes teacher-AI shared regulation over technological substitution. Pedagogically and practically, the findings imply that institutions and EdTech developers should deploy AI primarily for scalable, low-stakes rehearsal and actionable lesson planning, while preserving teacher authority over social communication, pragmatic competence, and high-stakes assessment.

title: The Ambient AI Era and Medical Student Education: Insights From Family Medicine Clerkship Directors
container-title: Family Medicine
b4e2d0fe06cca1696478c8fecf236a903aad34ab.abstract: Background and Objective: Artificial intelligence (AI) adoption in medicine is rapidly expanding, including ambient AI (AAI), which converts clinician-patient conversations into documentation. Despite growing use among practicing physicians, little is known about student access to AAI or barriers to implementation during medical student clerkships.Methods: We surveyed 174 family medicine clerkship directors (CDs) through the Council of Academic Family Medicine Educational Research Alliance network regarding AAI availability, permissibility, and opinions on student use. We analyzed responses using descriptive statistics and Fisher’s exact tests.Results: Ninety-four CDs responded to AAI-related questions. Student AAI use was permitted for only 3% of core family medicine clerkships. CDs cited missing technology (38.3%) or institutional restrictions (42.5%) as barriers. Opinions on student use were divided: 42.6% opposed any use, 41.5% supported some use, and 16% were unsure. Among those who opposed use, major concerns included potential negative effects on clinical reasoning (82.5%) and communication skills (85%). Supporters of student use were significantly more likely to believe AI will improve training and become commonplace in students’ careers than those who did not support student use of AAI (P&lt;0.0001).Conclusions: Access to AAI for medical students during core family medicine clerkships is rare, and CDs expressed substantial concerns regarding its impact on clinical reasoning and communication skills. Given the expeditious integration of AI into clinical practice, medical educators must be prepared to teach with technology, proactively design curricula that assume AAI availability, and consider modalities in addition to clinical documentation to assess student clinical reasoning.

title: Generative AI dependency and perceived learning outcomes among university students: an indirect association involving effort regulation
container-title: Frontiers in Psychology
4c672fa254b25b8a16adf60aab3a3ca16a55554e.abstract: Objective Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is increasingly integrated into university learning, raising questions about dependency-oriented reliance and self-regulation. Drawing on a self-regulated learning perspective, this study examined associations among GenAI dependency, effort regulation, and multidimensional perceived learning outcomes, including the statistical indirect association involving effort regulation. Methods Cross-sectional survey data were collected from 982 students at three higher education institutions in Guangdong Province, China. Confirmatory factor analysis and covariance-based structural equation modeling were conducted, with indirect associations tested using 5,000 bias-corrected bootstrap resamples. Sensitivity analyses adjusted for GenAI use frequency. Results The measurement model showed acceptable fit (CFI = 0.953, TLI = 0.944, RMSEA = 0.043, SRMR = 0.041). GenAI dependency showed a small negative total association with perceived learning outcomes ( β = −0.087) and was negatively associated with effort regulation ( β = −0.257). Effort regulation was positively associated with perceived learning outcomes ( β = 0.497). The residual direct association was nonsignificant ( β = 0.041), whereas the indirect association was negative and significant ( β = −0.128). After adjustment for GenAI use frequency, the indirect association remained significant, but the small total association was no longer significant. Conclusion The findings highlight effort regulation as a relevant learner-controlled process in the association between GenAI dependency and perceived learning outcomes. They also distinguish dependency-oriented reliance from frequency of GenAI use. The cross-sectional design and potential classroom clustering warrant cautious interpretation.

title: Generative AI and the Transformation of Elite Valuations in Photography
692259e21e260da069e4add3a5164afe88bbbaba.abstract: Abstract This study examines how mainstream English-language newspapers evaluated entries in AI photography competitions compared to those in traditional photography competitions between 2015 and 2025. Drawing on Bourdieu’s field theory, symbolic capital and boundary construction, the study treats photography competitions as institutional fields where legitimacy is publicly negotiated and views newspapers as cultural intermediaries that translate these negotiations into broader public discourse. Employing a comparative longitudinal qualitative content analysis approach, the study analyzed three corpora constructed using Factiva, comprising traditional competitions, AI competitions, and AI rule controversies, to examine shifts in the evaluation criteria, tone, and timing of newspaper coverage. In traditional competition coverage, newspapers primarily evaluate entries based on established criteria such as technical quality, composition, impact, and social significance. However, in AI-related reporting, the focus shifts to the authorship, information disclosure, fairness, category relevance, authenticity, and public trust. The tone of the reports also varies across different corpora: traditional reports are mostly neutral or supportive, while those in the AI field tend to be more skeptical. Later, as the debate intensified, reports increasingly focused on procedural issues, emphasizing rule changes, disclosure requirements, and institutional oversight. Eventually, the evaluative paradigm shifted from photographic quality to boundary conflicts and formal governance.

title: Enhancing Students' Critical Evaluation of AI Versus Human-Generated Literature Reviews: Deliberative Pedagogy
container-title: Journal of Nursing Education
ac644a3e053032e14a709217de485df2fea700f7.abstract: Background: AI misuse in literature reviews has emerged as an issue for educators. The goal of this teaching innovation was to foster learners' critical thinking about AI use in literature reviews. Method: A four-step deliberative pedagogical process was applied: (a) announcing literature review battles between AI and humans, (b) presenting review results generated by both sides, (c) using a poll to ask learners to choose their preferred review results for policy decision-making, and (d) debriefing on the speed and accuracy of both reviews. Results: Sixty-one learners responded to the poll: 51% ( n = 31) chose human-generated reviews, 36% ( n = 22) chose AI-generated reviews, while 13% ( n = 8) expressed their surprise at AI's performance. Debriefing showed that AI spent only 0.5 hours completing the review, but with low search accuracy, whereas humans achieved high accuracy but took more than 6 months. Conclusion: Deliberative pedagogy encourages learners to recalibrate their AI knowledge and reconsider the importance of human decision-making in literature reviews.

title: From entrepreneurship education and AI literacy to AI-enabled entrepreneurial action: the role of technology readiness under resource constraints
container-title: Journal of Entrepreneurship in Emerging Economies
86b6715dcb56f1f4e0030c7323977abfb02f8ad1.abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine how entrepreneurship education, AI literacy, Technology Readiness and perceived resource scarcity are associated with university students’ AI-enabled micro-entrepreneurial opportunity enactment in a resource-constrained emerging-economy setting. Design/methodology/approach Drawing on Entrepreneurial Action Theory and Technology Readiness research, the study analysed survey data from 450 university students in Nigeria. Partial least squares structural equation modelling was used to assess the proposed relationships and fuzzy-set qualitative comparative analysis examined alternative configurations associated with high and low levels of AI-enabled micro-entrepreneurial opportunity enactment. Findings Entrepreneurship education and AI literacy were positively associated with Technology Readiness. Technology Readiness was positively associated with AI-enabled micro-entrepreneurial opportunity enactment and mediated the associations of entrepreneurship education and AI literacy with that outcome. Perceived resource scarcity was negatively associated with opportunity enactment but strengthened the positive association between Technology Readiness and opportunity enactment. The configurational analysis further indicated that high opportunity enactment can emerge through multiple combinations of educational, technological and contextual conditions, whereas configurations associated with low opportunity enactment were not simple inverses of high-outcome pathways. Originality/value The study extends Entrepreneurial Action Theory by identifying Technology Readiness as a digitally mediated mechanism that enables entrepreneurial and AI-related capabilities to become practically consequential. It also shows that AI-enabled entrepreneurial participation depends on more than access to intelligent tools: students require entrepreneurial capability, AI literacy, practical readiness to engage with technology and conditions that reduce resource-related barriers to action.

title: Med Intel: An AI-Based Healthcare Pharmacy Management System with Intelligent Prescription Recognition and Drug Safety Verification
container-title: International Journal of Scientific Research in Engineering & Technology
fe7618ba67e18fca61775afa33f8cf09dc039336.abstract: The manual processing of handwritten prescriptions and the lack of automated drug safety verification in pharmacy management systems pose significant risks to patient safety and operational efficiency. This paper presents MedIntel, an AI-based healthcare pharmacy management system that integrates intelligent prescription recognition and comprehensive drug interaction detection. The prescription recognition module employs a dual-engine optical character recognition (OCR) pipeline combining EasyOCR with Tesseract as a fallback, enhanced by four image preprocessing strategies: grayscale conversion, contrast-limited adaptive histogram equalization (CLAHE), median filtering denoising, and Otsu binary thresholding. Extracted text undergoes a multi-stage natural language processing pipeline that splits recognized text into individual word candidates, filters noise using stop-word elimination and alphabetic character ratio thresholds, and matches each candidate against the medicine database using prefix-based SQL ILIKE queries augmented by RapidFuzz token-based fuzzy matching. The drug interaction detection system performs real-time pairwise checking of all cart items against a pre-populated DrugInteraction database using bidirectional ILIKE fuzzy matching, presenting warnings categorized by four severity levels: critical, severe, moderate, and mild, each accompanied by clinical descriptions and actionable recommendations. The system is developed using Python with Flask framework on the backend and Bootstrap 5.3 on the frontend, with SQLite for persistent storage. Evaluation of the medicine name recognition module achieves a token-level accuracy of 99.19% with an entity-level F1-score of 0.971 across 140 annotated prescription sentences, and the drug interaction database covers 15 clinically validated interaction pairs across four severity categories. The system demonstrates the feasibility of deploying lightweight, database-driven AI approaches for enhancing pharmacy safety in resource-constrained healthcare environments.

title: AI-Based Smart Traffic Monitoring System
container-title: International Journal of Scientific Research in Engineering & Technology
b1e70c247f77577319cf074a9e10d3caa0356b79.abstract: Manual enforcement of traffic rules in Indian cities is slow, inconsistent and difficult to scale, and most automated systems treat every offence identically regardless of the offender’s history. This paper presents the design and prototype implementation of the AI-Based Smart Traffic Monitoring System, built with Flask and OpenCV. The system registers five classes of camera-detectable violations (illegal parking, red-light jumping, riding without a helmet, wrong-way driving and triple riding) from simulated multi-camera feeds, uploaded images or video, and browser camera snapshots; stores evidence with each complaint; resolves owner details through a simulated RTO lookup; and uses a rule-based Violation Predictor to compute a Rule Breach Rate (15–98%) from prior violations and violation severity. The predictor then decides automatically between an official Warning for first-time offenders and a Direct E-Challan whose fine is escalated by 25% (third offence) and 50% (fourth and later offences), removing operator ambiguity at the review stage. A browser-side offline queue with idempotent retry prevents loss of evidence during server outages. Testing of the prototype showed that the decision logic behaves deterministically across all nine supported violation types, that image analysis takes 3–30 ms per 800×420 image on a CPU, and that the live scene renderer sustains the 45 ms stream interval comfortably. The detection layer is simulated and has not been validated on real CCTV data; this limitation, together with a weakness we found in the thumbnail-based demo matcher, is discussed along with the steps required for real deployment.

title: Global AI Impact in the Era of Intelligent Paradigm: A Perspective from Research Papers
container-title: Journal of Scholarly Publishing
854d0c813c992c06e0d2d0b6dee6f67272ba9a4d.abstract: This study conducts an in-depth exploration of the formation process behind the global impact of artificial intelligence research papers (AI papers). At the macro level, it conducts a cross-national comparison of AI papers from the perspectives of publication volume and policy citations. At the meso level, the Criteria Importance Through Intercriteria Correlation method is employed to conduct separate single-dimensional evaluations of the global impact of AI papers across four key dimensions: academic impact, perceived impact, societal impact, and policy impact. At the micro level, a comprehensive evaluation of the global impact of AI papers is carried out using the Projection Pursuit Classification Model, with the results subsequently validated using convolutional neural networks and correlation analysis. This study reveals the formation mechanisms of the global impact of AI papers, develops an evaluation framework based on four impact dimensions, and empirically validates its reliability and validity.

title: SHIELD-Net: A Sperm Halo Image Classification Framework via Hybrid ROI Extraction and ROI-Guided Dual-View Learning
container-title: AI Chemistry
e5750030231ded7d3e59283d131be7a566188cac.abstract: The sperm chromatin dispersion (SCD) test is widely used to assess sperm DNA fragmentation by observing the halo structure around the sperm head. However, manual halo interpretation is labor-intensive and subjective, which limits its consistency and throughput in clinical practice. To address these limitations, we propose SHIELD-Net, an image-level single-sperm halo morphology classification framework for four halo categories: large halo, medium halo, small halo, and without halo. SHIELD-Net includes two modules, i.e., a hybrid ROI extraction (HyREx) module and dual-view learning with ROI-guided gate fusion (RGF). The HyREx module converts the traditional direct classification pipeline into a segmentation-classification pipeline. It uses the cell segmentation foundation model, i.e., Cellpose, to segment halo-centered regions of interest (ROIs) and proposes a fallback mechanism to ensure segmentation effectiveness. In this way, HyREx can construct a head–halo-centered ROI and reduce interference from tail and background regions. Based on the original image and the extracted ROI, SHIELD-Net performs dual-view ConvNeXt encoding. RGF further uses the ROI representation to generate a spatial gate that recalibrates the original-view feature map toward halo-morphology-related responses. Experiments were conducted on a public expert-annotated sperm microscopy dataset containing 403 individual sperm halo images using stratified five-fold cross-validation. SHIELD-Net achieved a Macro F1 of 0.9290 ± 0.0161. Compared with the original-image ConvNeXt-Small baseline, SHIELD-Net improved Macro F1 by 0.1755. These results indicate that combining head–halo-centered ROI construction with ROI-guided feature recalibration improves image-level sperm halo morphology classification.

title: Repeatability and Agreement of CephX AI-Driven Cephalometric Analysis in Patients with Cleft Palate Only: A Comparative Study with Non-Cleft Controls
container-title: Applied Sciences
a342d32c9c6842cbefd98af7e362e17c9c84599c.abstract: Cephalometric analysis is essential in patients with cleft palate only (CPO) for the assessment of craniofacial morphology and treatment planning. This study evaluated the test–retest repeatability of CephX AI-driven cephalometric analysis and its agreement with expert manual measurements in patients with CPO versus non-cleft controls. Cephalometric radiographs of 50 patients with CPO (25 males and 25 females; aged 14–23 years) and 50 non-cleft controls matched for sex and ethnic origin were traced manually by two experienced orthodontists using CephX. All analyses were repeated after a two-week interval. Repeatability was assessed using Lin’s concordance correlation coefficient (CCC), and agreement between AI and manual measurements was evaluated using Bland–Altman analysis. CephX showed high test–retest repeatability for both groups, with CCC values of 0.97 or higher for all cephalometric variables evaluated. However, the agreement with expert manual measurements varied among cephalometric variables. In the CPO group, 34 of 50 radiographs required manual scale calibration and 31 of 50 generated a landmark-review warning; nevertheless, no skeletal or dental landmarks included in the analysis were manually repositioned by the investigators. CephX provided highly reproducible measurements, but the need for calibration and landmark review indicates that clinician supervision remains important, particularly in patients with altered craniofacial anatomy.

title: The Effects of Corporate AI Environment Factors on Employees’ Technology Acceptance Attitude and Continuous Intention to Use
container-title: Behavioral Sciences
e8078cb4da48844d192f23ccde505fac90f4b925.abstract: As artificial intelligence (AI) becomes an imperative survival strategy for modern enterprises, numerous organizations continue to face implementation failures stemming from employees’ psychological resistance. To address the scarcity of empirical research regarding the practical and psychological acceptance of AI in workflows, this study investigates the structural relationships between technological maturity and users’ cognitive adoption. Grounded in an integrated framework utilizing the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM), this research conceptualizes the “AI Environment Factor” as a higher-order construct comprising four foundational sub-dimensions: AI System Quality, AI Information Quality, AI Data Quality, and AI Infrastructure. A quantitative survey was administered to 189 corporate practitioners who have utilized enterprise-wide AI systems for at least one year, and the empirical data were analyzed using Structural Equation Modeling (SEM). The analytical results indicate that the AI Environment Factor exerts a statistically significant positive effect on both Perceived Ease of Use and Perceived Usefulness. Furthermore, Perceived Ease of Use was found to positively influence Perceived Usefulness. Ultimately, both Perceived Ease of Use and Perceived Usefulness are significantly associated with the employees’ continuous AI Intention to Use. These findings theoretically contribute to the literature by providing a measurable structural model for the continuance intention phase of organizational AI adoption. Practically, this study offers actionable guidelines for corporate executives, emphasizing that securing rigorous data accuracy and a stable system infrastructure is indispensable for mitigating cognitive load, fostering innovative corporate cultures, and maximizing the efficacy of AI utilization.

title: A CDIO-Based Reform of Advanced Separation Engineering: AI-Supported Curriculum Innovation and Practice
container-title: Education Sciences
6f70cdc82ec1b030d44e7be968d9d8de6d2a1fab.abstract: Advanced Separation Engineering requires graduate students to connect separation principles with process design and engineering decision-making. Using action research, this study developed and refined a reform based on the Conceive–Design–Implement–Operate (CDIO) framework across four annual offerings from 2022 to 2025. The reform integrated authentic engineering projects, AI-supported learning resources, digital process simulation, collaborative inquiry, and continuous assessment. Course evaluations from the 2021 pre-reform historical cohort (n = 46) were compared with those from the pooled reform cohorts (n = 254), supplemented by open-ended responses and interviews. The reform cohorts reported higher ratings on all five common course-evaluation items, with differences remaining statistically significant after Holm adjustment and Hedges’ g ranging from 1.29 to 2.11. Overall satisfaction averaged 3.41 in the historical cohort and 4.58 in the reform cohorts. On supplementary single-item self-report questions, 91.7% considered the CDIO reform helpful for developing comprehensive engineering competence, and 76.4% reported that AI-supported resources and digital simulation helped them understand complex separation processes. Student feedback identified software learning demands, group coordination, verification of AI outputs, and inconsistent industry-expert participation as continuing challenges. This four-year action research study provides a practice-informed reference for integrating CDIO projects and technological support in graduate engineering courses, based on students’ reported experiences.

title: AI Adoption at Higher Education Institutions: A Call for Designated AI Management
container-title: Education Sciences
893344e55b7a2d336456df016fc437e8ea34d6f6.abstract: Artificial intelligence is transforming teaching, learning and administration in higher education institutions (HEIs), yet responsibility for its governance is rarely assigned. This article develops and empirically tests the profile of an AI Manager for HEIs proposed by the Erasmus+ project FORCE AI. A literature-based definition and nine-area competence profile were examined in a sequential mixed-methods study, a survey of 387 students and staff from 13 countries and five nominal-group focus groups in Germany, Latvia, the Netherlands, and Türkiye in 2025, which tested the elements stakeholders can rate: competences, responsibilities, placement, and qualifications. Only 17% of respondents knew of a designated AI-management responsibility at their institution; of the remainder, 71% considered one necessary and 76% expected an AI Manager to improve their experience. The expected mandate comprised training, ethical oversight, data security and strategy; preferences were split between a dedicated position and a shared cross-functional function. Survey respondents portrayed the role as a compliance-oriented technical specialist, whereas staff-dominated focus groups, rating the same competencies, prioritised leadership, change and project management, and communication alongside AI expertise and ethics; this contrast between methods and samples persists for staff respondents alone. The revised definition and profile position designated AI management, a dedicated AI Manager or a team with an accountable lead, as change leadership with technical credibility and give HEIs a tested basis for establishing this role.

title:
Physics‐Based
                    <scp>AI</scp>
                    ‐Augmented Workflows Discovering Candidate Graphene Quantum Dot Near‐Infrared Chromophores
container-title: Journal of Computational Chemistry
9015055fc9241d12559eb385dd3eabeb43c352b9.abstract: ABSTRACT Graphene quantum dots (GQDs) exhibit optical properties that depend strongly on their size, edge structure, and surface functionalization, but identifying the molecular structures responsible for near‐infrared (NIR) emission remains challenging because of their structural complexity and disorder. In this work, we developed a computational framework combining rule‐based molecular generation, semi‐empirical quantum chemistry calculations, machine learning, and time‐dependent density functional theory (TD‐DFT) to predict possible chemically realistic candidate GQDs with NIR‐emitting optical properties. A fusion‐based hexagonal lattice growth approach was used to generate 100,000 candidate graphitic structures. A random subset of 5000 structures was selected for semiempirical calculations. Computed band gaps were used to train and evaluate five machine learning models (Random Forest, XGBoost, LightGBM, CatBoost, and Neural Network). LightGBM predicted bandgaps were used to pre‐screen the remaining 95,000 structures. 11,000 structures with low predicted gaps were selected for semiempirical calculations, and 50 top candidates with low gap and low SA score were selected for TD‐DFT calculations employing LC‐ ω PBE functional. All 50 structures were predicted to exhibit NIR emission, offering a computed database of candidate NIR‐emitting GQDs for future validation against experiment.

title: AI-Assisted Analysis of Spontaneous Affective Facial Responses for Cognitive Status Assessment in Older Adults: Exploratory Feasibility Study
container-title: JMIR Formative Research
6543568e570b9512b4946b58992f226b2f1a3be5.abstract: Background As Taiwan enters a super-aged society, the prevalence of dementia continues to rise, highlighting the need for scalable, noninvasive approaches to identify behavioral alterations associated with cognitive decline. AI-based analysis of spontaneous affective facial responses has emerged as a potential digital phenotyping tool, but its feasibility for assessing cognitive performance remains underexplored. Objective This study aimed to examine the feasibility of using AI-derived spontaneous affective facial response metrics, including affective expression congruency and onset latency, to characterize differences across cognitive performance levels in older adults with healthy cognition (HC), mild cognitive impairment (MCI), or dementia. Methods A total of 60 participants (HC, MCI, and dementia; 20 per group) were presented with positive and negative emotion-eliciting videos and completed Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) recall and calculation tasks. Facial expressions were video-recorded and analyzed using a convolutional neural network–based AI system. AI-derived metrics included affective expression congruency, categorized as congruent, neutral, or incongruent according to the detected facial response, and affective expression onset latency, defined as the time from stimulus presentation to the emergence of a nonneutral facial expression detected by the AI model. Group differences were analyzed using 1-way ANOVA, Pearson chi-square or Fisher-Freeman-Halton exact tests, Bonferroni-adjusted pairwise post hoc comparisons, analysis of covariance adjusting for age and education, and exploratory receiver operating characteristic analyses. Results Affectively congruent responses were generally less frequent among participants with lower cognitive performance. During the 14-second positive stimulus, congruent positive expressions were observed in 65% (13/20) of HC participants, 20% (4/20) of MCI participants, and 0% (0/20) of participants with dementia. During the 48-second negative stimulus, congruent negative expressions were observed in 60% (12/20) of HC participants compared with 5% (1/20) of both MCI and dementia participants. Onset latency differed significantly across groups for the 14-second positive stimulus (F2,57=19.63; P<.001; η2=0.41), 52-second positive stimulus (F2,57=4.25; P=.02; η2=0.13), 48-second negative stimulus (F2,57=15.61; P<.001; η2=0.35), and MMSE-based cognitive-task condition (F2,57=11.28; P<.001; η2=0.28). After adjustment for age and education, the group effect remained significant for all latency outcomes (F2,55=3.89-10.68; all P≤.03; partial η2=0.12-0.28). Exploratory receiver operating characteristic analyses showed stronger separation in several HC vs MCI and HC vs dementia comparisons, whereas MCI vs dementia comparisons showed limited separability. Conclusions AI-assisted analysis of spontaneous affective facial responses revealed differences in expression congruency and onset latency across cognitive performance levels. These preliminary findings suggest that AI-derived facial behavioral metrics may serve as noninvasive adjunctive features for observational cognitive assessment. However, the findings should be interpreted cautiously because of the exploratory design, modest sample size, and absence of internal or external validation.

title: How do PhD Students Use Generative AI? Reflections on Practice and Ethics
container-title: Journal of Teaching and Learning
1658044309243f3c79c66e0ba28f754f3714ac51.abstract: Generative AI (GenAI) has rapidly moved from novelty to ubiquity, reshaping how doctoral students approach learning, research, and career preparation. Yet while universities and the public often frame debates around undergraduate use, comparatively little attention has been given to PhD students despite their dual role as learners and future scholars. In this paper, we reflect on our experiences as PhD students using GenAI across coursework, qualifying exams, thesis research, teaching, and the job market. Drawing on these experiences, we highlight both the opportunities GenAI provides—for efficiency, conceptual clarity, and skill development—and the ethical challenges it raises, including concerns about academic integrity, cognitive outsourcing, disclosure, and employability beyond academia. Our reflections emphasize that GenAI use is not uniform: it varies with disciplinary context, institutional policies, and students’ levels of development. We argue that GenAI is no longer peripheral to doctoral education but central to its practice, and the challenge ahead is how it can be integrated responsibly to support learning, uphold integrity, and prepare graduates for an evolving academic and professional landscape.

title: Extracorporeal Spinal Orthosis-Fixation With Progressive Distraction for Severe Spinal Tuberculosis Kyphosis: A Technical Case Series With Long-Term Follow-Up
container-title: Spine Open
272e2a2624f1f749d7f97d423bc11d44a6f4311d.abstract: Study Design: Retrospective technical case series. Objective: To describe the technical feasibility and long-term outcomes and radiographic experience of an extracorporeal spinal orthosis-fixation (ESOF) device combined with a progressive-adaptive distraction in highly selected patients with severe multilevel spinal tuberculosis (TB) kyphosis. Summary of Background Data: Severe spinal TB with extensive vertebral destruction may result in marked kyphosis, spinal shortening, and substantial bone loss. Conventional reconstruction can be technically challenging when multiple contiguous vertebral segments(≥3) and a Cobb Angle of ≥70° are involved. The feasibility of gradual deformity correction combined with progressive spinal lengthening in this severe setting has not been well described. Materials and Methods: Three patients with severe multilevel spinal TB deformity were retrospectively reviewed. They had extensive vertebral destruction involving three to seven vertebral segments and a preoperative Cobb Angle of ≥70°. Treatment consisted of anterior debridement and bone grafting, posterior placement of extra-long pedicle screws with an ESOF device, and postoperative progressive-adaptive distraction. Simultaneously, anti-TB drug treatment was administered for one and a half years before, during, and after surgery, including at the lesion site and during postoperative traction. Clinical and radiographic observations included Cobb Angle, spinal-pelvic tilt, standing height, erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR), C-reactive protein (CRP), Oswestry Disability Index (ODI), neurological status, and complications during three phases: distraction orthopedic phase, distraction osteogenesis phase, and long-term follow-up, respectively. Results: The mean preoperative Cobb Angle was 80.3°. During the initial distraction phase, lasting a mean of 71.3 days, the mean Cobb Angle decreased to 21.7°, and the mean standing height increased by 5.3 cm. During the subsequent distraction osteogenesis phase, lasting a mean of 2 years 4 months, the mean Cobb Angle was 12.7° and the mean height gain reached 7.0 cm, with radiographic evidence of new bone formation. At a mean follow-up of 12.3 years, the mean Cobb Angle was 17.0°, the mean height gain was 6.7 cm, and the mean ODI was 3.0. One patient developed a mild screw-hole infection that resolved with local wound care; two patients reported painless lumbar popping. No neurological deterioration or other major adverse event was observed. Conclusions: In this small, highly selected retrospective technical series, ESOF combined with progressive-adaptive distraction was technically feasible and was associated with substantial deformity correction and long-term maintenance of spinal alignment. These observations should be considered preliminary proof-of-concept findings rather than evidence establishing the safety or efficacy of the technique. Further studies are required to determine reproducibility, complication rates, and clinical effectiveness.

title: Institutional Approval Is Not Public Authorization: Legitimacy as a Governance Requirement for Clinical AI
container-title: Journal of Medical Internet Research
8c7db9301128a840c604aa65210fef008480b1f9.abstract: Clinical AI governance has advanced rapidly in technical validation, regulatory compliance, risk management, human oversight, and postdeployment monitoring. Yet a more fundamental question often remains implicit: under what conditions are health institutions justified in exercising consequential authority through AI over patients, clinicians, and communities? In this Viewpoint, we argue that legitimacy should be recognized as an independent governance requirement, distinct from technical assurance, legal and ethical compliance, trust, acceptance, and institutional approval. Our aim is to distinguish institutional approval from public authorization and to propose a normative framework for authorizing consequential clinical AI deployments. We address health system leaders, clinical AI governance and procurement teams, frontline clinicians, and patient and community representatives. Drawing on theories of legitimacy and public value and published clinical AI governance research, we make the following contributions: (1) the concept of the unclaimed decision, defined as a consequential choice about purpose, threshold, population, or priority for which no actor clearly assumes responsibility for public justification; (2) a tripartite framework comprising procedural authorization, substantive justification, and relational renewal; and (3) practical governance tools to support public justification, contestation, and renewal. These tools include 3 minimum auditable conditions: visibility of deployment; affected-party input before governing conditions are fixed; and conditional reviewability, which requires a predefined trigger that can be invoked by a named actor outside the deploying team. A 5-question public authorization test examines purpose, distribution, exclusion, meaningful choice and contestability, and renewal. Governance intensity should increase with clinical consequence; distributive reach; difficulty of reversal; and the absence of genuine, informed choice. For smaller health care organizations, we propose ways to perform the same core governance functions through existing advisory bodies, targeted interviews, shared regional resources, and standardized documentation. We also outline a heuristic for identifying affected publics, procedures for specifying participation authority and resolving disagreement, and procurement provisions that preserve reviewability across vendor boundaries. These are normative proposals requiring evaluation. Public authorization requires continuing substantive justification; it cannot be inferred from compliance, popularity, or completion of an audit checklist.

title: On the Exculpatory Moral Economy of AI-DSS
container-title: Oxford Intersections: AI in Society
5567540863c712aeb6643ebd1c45f7594c6c03d6.abstract: Abstract This article analyzes the foundational concepts underpinning the European Union’s governance of artificial intelligence decision support systems (AI-DSSs): “trustworthy AI” and “human oversight.” Evidence from behavioral psychology, computer science, and ethics and legal scholarship demonstrates that automation bias, selective adherence, and AI hypersuasion systematically undermine meaningful human agency (MHA). Furthermore, the anthropomorphic discourse of trustworthiness obscures moral responsibility rather than ensuring accountability. This situation raises a significant question left unresolved in the literature: why does the oversight paradigm persist and even expand despite its well-documented insufficiency? To address this, the article applies the moral economy framework, as developed by E. P. Thompson and further elaborated by Bonini and Treré, to the context of AI-DSS deployment. It delineates four key positions: deployers, subjects, resistors, and the conscripted human-in-the-loop. The analysis identifies the dominant value system in this field as an exculpatory moral economy, in which protective norms are fulfilled through performance rather than genuine protection, resulting in the receipt of trust and the granting of absolution. From this perspective, the failure of oversight is not a flaw to be corrected but an intended outcome of the arrangement. The article advocates for a strong presumption against deploying AI-DSSs in sensitive areas of societal governance. Where deployment continues, it proposes two legally grounded avenues for organized societal resistance to uncritical AI-DSS deployment: promoting moral economy-aware critical AI literacy, which furthers skepticism rather than trust, and establishing collective MHA councils, rooted in the AI Act and the precautionary principle.

title: AI, Epistemic Relations, and Testimonial Outsourcing
container-title: Oxford Intersections: AI in Society
446cfa55911f505e21152883c74d3747ae487879.abstract: Abstract Generative AI “companions” are increasingly integrated into higher education as always-available interlocutors that offer feedback, explanation, and encouragement. This article examines how such systems reshape the epistemic relations through which students speak, are heard, and come to count as knowers, and argues that companion-style AIs can disrespect epistemic relations in systematic ways. Students may become less able, and less willing, to testify on their own in genuinely reciprocal spaces (such as class discussions, office hours, and peer groups), habitually relying on their AI companions instead. Call this phenomenon testimonial outsourcing: a structural tendency to outsource one’s testimonial activity, which functions as a self-imposed, technologically mediated analogue of gaslighting. Students come to treat the AI’s outputs as more reliable than their own judgment and expressive capacities, thereby eroding their epistemic self-trust and cultivating a distorted conception of legitimate epistemic expectations. This article concludes by drawing implications for AI design and educational policy, placing constraints that preserve “non-mediated” spaces of speech, require explicit AI transparency, and build frictions that redirect students back toward interpersonal relations.
