title: Multi-color space image enhancement with weighted fusion and lightweight deep learning framework for AI-based breast cancer histopathology image classification
container-title: Frontiers in Bioinformatics
81667f64e8a02a616d7fa09a49a1bd1ce28e3da1.abstract: Introduction Variations in Hematoxylin and Eosin (H&amp;E) staining, illumination, tissue preparation, and image acquisition affect breast histopathology image analysis, altering nuclear contrast, color consistency, and downstream feature extraction. Separately, prior BreakHis studies have often used image-wise splitting, which can place a patient’s images in both training and test sets and inflate performance estimates. Methods To address these two issues, this study introduced a Multi-color Space Image Enhancement (MSIE) approach and evaluates it under strict, leakage-controlled, patient-wise five-fold cross-validation on the BreakHis dataset. MSIE combines H&amp;E color deconvolution, stain normalization, hematoxylin contrast processing with Contrast Limited Adaptive Histogram Equalization (CLAHE), Hue-Saturation-Value (HSV) space processing, eosin reconstruction, and H&amp;E-weighted fusion. Before model training, the dataset underwent a decoded-pixel Secure Hash Algorithm 256-bit (SHA-256) integrity check, and 125 duplicate images were removed, reducing the dataset from 7,909 to 7,784. The Lightweight Convolutional Neural Network (LCNN) model is trained and tested on MSIE and original RGB images using an identical architecture and patient partitions, and MobileNetV2, ResNet50, DenseNet169, and EfficientNetB0 are evaluated under the same protocol to assess efficiency-accuracy trade-offs across model capacities. Results Performance is assessed at the image and patient levels using accuracy, precision, recall, F1 Score, Receiver Operating Characteristic Area Under the Curve (ROC AUC), and Precision-Recall Area Under the Curve (PR AUC), alongside Fusion-coefficient sensitivity, magnification-specific performance, computational efficiency, Grad-CAM visualization, and independent BACH testing. At the patient level, original RGB achieved an accuracy of 0.8397 ± 0.0325 and F1-score of 0.8789 ± 0.0326, versus a mean accuracy of 0.7522 ± 0.2218 and F1-score of 0.7632 ± 0.2734 for MSIE. MSIE, however, produced a slightly higher mean ROC-AUC (0.9024 ± 0.1274 versus 0.8952 ± 0.1023). Higher-capacity ImageNet-pretrained architectures performed better on MSIE inputs, with EfficientNetB0 achieving the highest mean patient-level accuracy (0.9007 ± 0.0718) and ROC-AUC (0.9707 ± 0.0354). Independent evaluation on the BACH dataset using frozen BreaKHis-trained MSIE-LCNN models yielded an accuracy of 0.7056 and an ROC-AUC of 0.7012, indicating substantial cross-dataset domain shift. Discussion Overall, MSIE provides a stain-aware representation whose downstream benefits are not universal and depend on the classifier architecture, fusion balance, operating point, and dataset domain, thereby supporting leakage-controlled and externally validated assessment of histopathology processing methods rather than claims of immediate clinical translation.

title: Association between cardiovascular disease risk and cognitive function in older adults based on the China-PAR model: a cross-sectional study
container-title: Frontiers in Public Health
e0f98251d06684be6269a16df0a97bbca90c6c74.abstract: Objective To investigate the association between cardiovascular disease (CVD) risk and cognitive function in older adults using the China-PAR model. Methods This study adopted stratified random sampling. A total of 570 older adults were selected from 3,750 health examinations at a community health service station, with sample size calculated by the cross-sectional study formula. We collected questionnaire and physical examination data including demographics, blood pressure and metabolic indicators. Cognitive function was measured by the Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA), and cardiovascular risk was assessed via the China-PAR model. All analyses were performed with SPSS 27.0 using Spearman's rank correlation analysis and multiple linear regression analysis. Results The mean MoCA score was 25.94 ± 2.71. MoCA scores differed significantly across CVD risk groups and were negatively correlated with CVD risk level (r = −0.56, p &lt; 0.001). In the primary adjusted Model 2, both the high-risk (B = −0.68, p &lt; 0.001) and moderate-risk groups (B = −0.31, p = 0.02) had significantly lower MoCA scores than the low-risk group. In the sensitivity analysis (Model 3) additionally adjusting for age and gender, the results were similar (high risk: B = −0.65, p &lt; 0.001; moderate risk: B = −0.30, p = 0.03). Compared with the college group, all lower education groups showed significantly lower MoCA scores. Sensitivity analyses restricted to participants aged ≤ 74 years yielded a similar pattern of findings. Conclusion Higher CVD risk was associated with poorer cognitive function in this study population, with lower MoCA scores observed particularly among participants in the high-risk group. Given the cross-sectional design, longitudinal studies are needed to clarify the temporal relationship between CVD risk and cognitive function.

title: A near-real-time UAV-based computer vision framework for fire and smoke detection and localization using YOLO object detection and visible light communication
container-title: Frontiers in Robotics and AI
c30acc0f112184d52c32549aa1253e6669759ca9.abstract: Introduction Early and reliable fire and smoke detection is essential for effective emergency monitoring, particularly in UAV-based environments characterized by variable illumination, changing object scales, and smoke-related visual disturbances. This study proposes a near-real-time UAV-based computer vision framework integrating YOLO-based object detection, geometric fire-source localization, and visible light communication (VLC). Methods A dataset of 4,200 manually annotated fire and smoke images was divided into training, validation, and test subsets using an 80:10:10 ratio. YOLOv10, YOLOv11, and YOLOv12 architectures were compared using Precision, Recall, mAP50, mAP50-95, inference time, and frames per second. Fire-source localization was modeled using camera-ray projection and ground-plane intersection based on UAV position and camera geometry. RF and VLC communication were evaluated through analytical modeling and simulation. Results YOLOv10l demonstrated a favorable balance between detection accuracy and computational efficiency, achieving Precision of 0.962, Recall of 0.968, mAP50 of 0.980, and mAP50-95 of 0.676. Under the modeled communication conditions, VLC-assisted transmission showed signal loss of 5–10%, compared with 15–25% for RF communication, with estimated latency below 40 ms. Simulated fire-source localization errors ranged from 0.5 to 1.2 m and decreased to 0.3–0.5 m under multi-view triangulation assumptions. Discussion The findings demonstrate the potential of integrating YOLO-based fire and smoke detection with geometric localization and VLC-assisted communication for near-real-time UAV monitoring. The detection experiments were conducted using workstation hardware, while communication and localization results were obtained through modeling and simulation. Further onboard UAV testing and independent validation are required to assess real-world performance and generalizability.

title: SoniNet: an AI framework for enhancing voice features in speech-based health monitoring
container-title: Frontiers in Aging Neuroscience
df058c0d47df5c575310bd3736829d80323f0898.abstract: Deep learning based speech embeddings learned from large-scale speech corpora have achieved strong performance across a range of speech analysis tasks. However, handcrafted acoustic features, such as prosodic, spectral, and voice-quality descriptors, remain widely used in clinical speech analysis because of their established role in characterizing vocal behavior. Despite this, these features often struggle to generalize across variations in speech dynamics, recording duration, and recording conditions. This paper introduces SoniNet , a framework that enhances the discriminative power of handcrafted acoustic features by learning data-driven temporal representations from large-scale speech data. SoniNet captures the temporal evolution of acoustic descriptors across speech recordings of variable length while maintaining compatibility with established acoustic feature sets used in clinical speech analysis. We evaluate SoniNet on benchmark speech data sets and demonstrate consistent improvements in classification performance across clinical speech assessment tasks, outperforming conventional acoustic modeling approaches in 22 out of 24 feature-task combinations. These findings highlight the potential of SoniNet as a robust framework for speech-based health monitoring, affect recognition, and computational behavioral analysis.

title: Negotiating epistemic authority in AI-assisted lesson planning: a multiple-case study of preservice mathematics teachers
container-title: Frontiers in Psychology
70b1eff9b5e330f7c9820a2235ea43bbf0d67f31.abstract: Introduction Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) can provide preservice teachers with a complete lesson plan before they have articulated the reasoning the plan is intended to develop, creating conditions for automation bias and cognitive offloading. This multiple-case study examined how five preservice mathematics teachers in China negotiated epistemic authority while planning using GenAI. Methods Cases were selected from 42 preservice teachers through preliminary quantitative screening. Screen-recording-derived event logs, concurrent verbalizations, video-stimulated recall interviews, and written reflections were integrated into an evidence matrix comprising 34 decision episodes. Authority was interpreted as retained, shared, or ceded based on the relationship among the source of a proposal, the participant’s action, the warrant invoked, and whether that warrant was enacted in the lesson plan. Results Authority was retained in 16 episodes, shared in 12, and ceded in 6, with variation across cases. Visible actions did not map onto authority positions in a fixed way, and professional warrants were sometimes not enacted. Two vulnerabilities emerged. A closed verification loop, observed in four episodes across two cases, occurred when participants recognized uncertainty about AI output yet asked the same AI to validate it. An insight–action gap, illustrated by three episodes in a single case, occurred when recognized pedagogica problems were not translated into planned teacher responses. Discussion The findings support the proposition that the educative value of AI-assisted planning depends less on how much novices edit AI output than on whether tasks require independent verification and warranted, enacted decisions.

title: From Emotional Impulse to Recurring Revenue: Consumer Psychology, Unit Economics, and VC Investment Evaluation of AI Companion Hardware for Gen Z
container-title: Advances in Economics, Management and Political Sciences
0cf49e0249f0e620ecc8cb9e38c8e4a036773ef2.abstract: With the rapid convergence of Large Language Models (LLMs) and embodied intelligence, AI companion hardware targeted at Generation Z (e.g., desktop AI pets and smart emotional robots) has emerged as a premier track for venture capital (VC) investment. However, these conceptual devices frequently face severe Unit Economics crises characterized by high customer acquisition costs (CAC), elevated initial product returns, and steep user churn rates. This paper examines the psychological drivers behind Gen Z's willingness to pay (WTP) high emotional premiums for feature-incomplete AI hardware, and investigates how hardware enterprises can leverage proactive retention mechanisms to optimize LTV/CAC ratios and valuation multiples . This paper conducts a literature review that synthesizes theoretical frameworks from behavioral finance, consumer psychology, human-computer interaction (HCI), and venture capital valuation models. The study reveals that Gen Z's demand for loneliness compensation and social status validation provides firms with strong initial pricing power and gross margins. However, sustaining long-term commercial viability requires overcoming the "novelty decay trap" through proactive AgentOS interactions and dynamic memory graphs. Transforming hardware from a one-off transaction into an Annual Recurring Revenue (ARR) subscription model substantially improves capital efficiency, expanding valuation multiples from 1.0x–2.0x P/S to 8.0x–12.0x P/S.

title: The Impact Mechanism of Generative AI Marketing Content on Consumer Purchase Intention
container-title: Advances in Economics, Management and Political Sciences
a88b594da4229c4372724aa7ce209f50a21e80ab.abstract: Generative Artificial Intelligence (GAI) technology is rapidly becoming popular, and more and more companies are using it for marketing content creation. GAI marketing content is changing consumers' information reception experience and influencing their purchase decisions. To address the question of how generative AI marketing content affects consumer purchase intention, this article uses a literature review to examine relevant research on brand image and brand equity, generative AI marketing content, and marketing psychology. Based on the existing literature, a theoretical analysis is conducted to develop a dual-path framework. The study focuses on two paths: the brand image path and the marketing psychology path, and discusses how factors such as AI content quality, AI disclosure and consumer trust, brand type, and FOMO sensitivity may influence these paths. This paper proposes a conceptual dual-path framework based on existing research, summarizes the limitations of current research, and suggests directions for future research. The study provides a theoretical reference for enterprises seeking to apply generative AI in marketing practices.

title: From “usefulness” to “dependence”: the dynamic evolution mechanism of generative AI use behaviors
container-title: Frontiers in Psychology
3539493dde1068e3e61ed22c9b87cdd05b24a87e.abstract: Background As generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) rapidly permeates Chinese higher education, university students’ AI use behaviors have come to be characterized by “high frequency, wide penetration, and rapid iteration.” Yet, a systematic understanding of the dynamic evolution mechanism from initial cognition to deep dependence remains lacking. Methods Employing a four-wave longitudinal design spanning 18 months (the first week of June 2024 to the first week of December 2025, with one wave every 6 months) and drawing on 524 valid responses to the 600 distributed questionnaires, retained in full across all four waves, this study systematically investigates the dynamic trajectories and mediating mechanisms of 12 core constructs, including perceived usefulness, trust, technology concerns, ethical concerns, use behavior, technology integration, usage habits, academic dependence, and moral disengagement. Results Repeated-measures ANOVA and mediation model testing reveal the following: (1) Perceived usefulness exhibits an asymmetric U-shaped trajectory of “sharp initial decline, stabilization, and rebound,” which does not support the hypothesized inverted U-shaped pattern. (2) Trust shows a trajectory of “adjusted decline, low-level stabilization, and internalized overshooting,” with an “overshooting” phenomenon in the later stage that surpasses the initial level. (3) Technology concerns decrease in a strictly monotonic fashion, whereas ethical concerns follow an asymmetric U-shaped trajectory of “precipitous decline, stabilization, and sharp rebound,” revealing a differentiated pattern of technological desensitization and ethical re-sensitization. (4) Technology integration partially mediates the transformation from actual use behavior to usage habits (indirect effect proportion = 23.39%), with the cognitive pathway accounting for only about one-quarter of the total association. (5) Early trust significantly and positively predicts continuance intention 18 months later (β = 0.400), and this effect is partially mediated by user satisfaction. (6) Exploratory analyses show that perceived usefulness negatively predicts academic dependence and moral disengagement through the sequential mediation of “actual use behavior → technology integration → usage habits,” suggesting that “high usefulness” may lead to benign autonomous use rather than problematic dependence. Conclusion This study is among the first to adopt a longitudinal design to reveal the nonlinear dynamic evolution patterns of GenAI use behaviors among Chinese university students. It provides crucial empirical evidence for extending technology acceptance theories along the temporal dimension, for understanding the stratified evolution of risk perception, and for informing AI education interventions. The sample was recruited by convenience sampling and consists almost entirely of female students in the humanities and social sciences; the findings describe this sample, and no claim of generalization to all Chinese university students is made.

title: Pathological complete response and major pathological response as surrogate endpoints for recurrence-free survival in perioperative immunotherapy for hepatocellular carcinoma: a systematic review and meta-analysis
container-title: Frontiers in Pharmacology
c5e67b2f10363f109b2d3bb3e75df03fe6d5bc53.abstract: Background High post-resection recurrence of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) limits long-term survival. Perioperative immunotherapy, including neoadjuvant therapy for resectable HCC and conversion therapy for unresectable HCC, has become a research hotspot. Whether pathological complete response (pCR) and major pathological response (MPR) can serve as surrogate endpoints for recurrence-free survival (RFS) remains unclear, with important implications for accelerating trial design. Objective To systematically evaluate the correlation between pCR/MPR and RFS following HCC perioperative immunotherapy, quantitatively synthesize hazard ratios (HRs) of pCR/MPR versus non-pCR/non-MPR for RFS (and overall survival, OS) across studies, and assess their reliability as surrogate endpoints. Methods We systematically searched PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, Web of Science, China National Knowledge Infrastructure (CNKI) and Wanfang Data databases (from inception to June 2026), supplemented by manual searching and citation tracking. The DerSimonian-Laird random-effects model was used to pool effect sizes. Heterogeneity was assessed using I 2 statistic and Q test. Sensitivity analysis was performed using leave-one-out method. Subgroup analyses were conducted by treatment stage (neoadjuvant vs. conversion), treatment regimen (ICI mono/dual vs. ICI + TKI vs. triple therapy), study design (prospective vs. retrospective), and MPR definition (≥70% vs. ≥ 90% necrosis). Publication bias was evaluated using Egger’s regression test. Results The systematic review included 21 studies for descriptive analysis. The meta-analysis included 10 studies reporting HR values: 5 pCR studies (n = 720) and 6 MPR studies (n = 785), one of which (NeoHCC, D’Alessio 2024) (D'Alessio et al., Lancet Oncol, 2024, 25(12), 1465–1475) encompassed both. The pCR vs. non-pCR → RFS/DFS: Pooled HR = 0.342 (95% CI: 0.248–0.472), p &lt; 0.000001, heterogeneity I 2 = 0.0%. In sensitivity analysis, pooled HR remained stable at 0.244–0.354. MPR vs. non-MPR → RFS/PFS: Pooled HR = 0.291 (95% CI: 0.155–0.548), p = 0.000132, I 2 = 66.6%. Heterogeneity was primarily driven by one study containing non-immunotherapy cohorts (Zhang 2024, n = 481) (Zhang et al., Hepatobiliary Pancreat Dis Int, 2025, 24(2), 157–163); after exclusion, I 2 decreased to 0.0%, HR = 0.215. Conclusion The pCR and MPR after perioperative immunotherapy are strongly associated with improved RFS in HCC, corresponding to approximately 66% and 70% reductions in recurrence risk, respectively. These findings support pCR/MPR as promising surrogate endpoints, although prospective randomized validation remains necessary.

title: Roxadustat ameliorates bone microarchitectural deterioration in CKD-MBD rats in association with mitigated systemic micro-inflammation and restored FGF23–Wnt/β-catenin signaling
container-title: Frontiers in Pharmacology
964d2a2696481dfacc7edb15d60682a22777ba77.abstract: Elevated FGF23 is associated with bone microarchitectural deterioration in chronic kidney dis-ease-mineral and bone disorder (CKD-MBD). While roxadustat (a HIF-PHI) is established for the treatment of renal anemia, its potential bone-protective effects in CKD-MBD remain unclear. We investigated whether roxadustat ameliorates femoral microarchitectural deterioration in CKD-MBD rats in association with FGF23 downregulation and restoration of Wnt/β-catenin signaling. A CKD-MBD rat model was established by unilateral nephrectomy and adenine gavage, and animals were randomized into sham, model, and roxadustat (50 or 100 mg/kg, three times weekly) groups for 8 weeks. Renal function, hematological indices, calcium-phosphate parame-ters, and femoral microarchitecture were evaluated, and target protein levels (FGF23, FGFR1, DKK1, β-catenin) were assessed by Western blotting and immunohistochemistry. Roxadustat improved renal function, ameliorated the reduction in erythroid parameters, and restored calcium-phosphate homeostasis. Systemically, it mitigated micro-inflammation by reducing serum CRP and hepcidin, and downregulated serum FGF23 levels as well as tissue FGF23 expression in kidney and bone. In conclusion, the bone-protective effect of roxadustat occurs synchronously with systemic micro-inflammation mitigation, FGF23 downregulation, and Wnt/β-catenin signaling restoration. These findings highlight its pleiotropic therapeutic potential in CKD-MBD management, suggesting a synergistic benefit associated with both systemic metabolic recovery and local skeletal regulation.

title: Embedded Edge Ai-Based Smart Dam and Bridge Structural Health Monitoring with Predictive Flood Analytics and Iot System
container-title: International Research Journal on Advanced Engineering Hub (IRJAEH)
0a180d0b6b9f88661eeeb2f309429c4d2a30ff3d.abstract: Dams and bridges require continuous monitoring to ensure safety and long-term performance, yet conventional inspection relies on periodic manual measurements that can delay the detection of abnormal behavior. This paper presents an embedded Edge AI-based smart dam and bridge structural health monitoring system with predictive flood analytics and IoT connectivity. ESP32-based monitoring units acquire temperature, humidity, rainfall, water level, load, vibration, acceleration, gyroscope, strain and tilt-related parameters from prototype dam and bridge models, while an ESP32-CAM provides live visual surveillance. Feed-forward artificial neural networks developed with TensorFlow/Keras, using 17 input features for the dam and 15 for the bridge with StandardScaler normalization, classify each structure as NORMAL, WARNING or CRITICAL; the dam model is converted to TensorFlow Lite for edge deployment. A Flask backend connects the units to a web dashboard, and critical conditions trigger LED, buzzer and siren alerts, an automated motor/gate response and e-mail notification. Dashboard outputs, logged sensor records and time-wise event analyses from the prototype demonstrate continuous, low-cost and real-time condition assessment that reduces dependence on manual inspection.

title: Implementation of API-based library services at IIT Delhi: research analytics and conversational AI
container-title: Library Hi Tech News
3f39a4843baa933f94e72c6518e921f1dc6a537c.abstract: Purpose Academic libraries need to connect library systems with external platforms to automate workflows, enrich metadata and develop intelligent user services. Application Programming Interfaces (APIs) provide an effective mechanism for such integration and seamless exchange of data between different systems. This study aims to describe the potential applications and practical use of APIs to develop research analytics and conversational library services. Design/methodology/approach The article presents practical implementations using the Scopus and OpenAlex APIs for research analytics and the Koha and DSpace REST APIs for developing a conversational library interface. Findings The implementations demonstrate how APIs can extend existing library systems without replacing them, enabling automated research analytics, integrated discovery and conversational access to library resources. Practical implications The paper can help librarians, systems developers and library administrators to explore API-based services using their existing library management systems, repositories and scholarly information sources. Originality/value The article presents practical experiences of using different APIs to develop research analytics and conversational services in an academic library environment.

title: Who Shapes AI? Technology, Institutions, and Power in the Development of Artificial Intelligence
container-title: Communications in Humanities Research
356ffd8026b5a395cd32477e24147cc7f57bfb2f.abstract: Artificial intelligence is usually mainly explained through technological breakthroughs, such as larger models, improved algorithms, stronger computing power and expanded datasets. This article challenges this interpretation by viewing artificial intelligence as a sociotechnical system whose development and consequences are constantly influenced by social institutions. Based on research of the history of the Internet and human-computer interaction, institutional development, automated responsibility, and algorithmic labor, this paper compares early computing systems with contemporary artificial intelligence. Analysis shows that technical capabilities themselves cannot determine how a technology develops or how it affects society. Governments, universities, companies, markets, legal systems, workers and users all influence the way artificial intelligence is funded, deployed, regulated and understood. Meanwhile, these actors do not have equal power. Cases such as moral collapse zones and algorithmic wage discrimination demonstrate how automation unevenly redistributes responsibility, information and economic benefits. Therefore, this article holds that the future of artificial intelligence is not determined by the technology itself, but rather by the institutional structure and power relations in which the technology is developed and utilized.

title: Technological Empowerment and Subject Integrity: Fostering Originality and Constructing Ethical Norms in AI-Assisted Dance Choreography Pedagogy
container-title: Communications in Humanities Research
904b0335d698bba3850c59ef604cf595cb0c0245.abstract: Artificial intelligence is deeply involved in dance choreography, and it has impacted the traditional logic of creation and brought about problems such as the dissolution of student subjectivity, originality problems, and ethical anomie. This study aims to explore how to hold on to creative subjectivity under technological empowerment, to cultivate original ability, and to construct ethical norms. The study uses a method that combines literature review, classroom observation, and action research; it defines the boundaries of concepts, diagnoses the typical problems of AI involvement in teaching, and revises the teaching plan through pilot iteration. The results show that although AI has expanded the boundaries of creation, it has also led to "prompt-first," the homogenization of works, and integrity risks. On this basis, this study proposes three results: first, reconstructing the "three-stage progressive" teaching model and establishing the order of bodily experience first, AI placed later, and reverse verification; second, designing a "four-node" embedded ethics module that covers the key links of the whole creation process; third, building a process-based evaluation system in which the human-machine division of labor is visible, and bringing the personal character of body vocabulary and the critical handling of AI output into scoring. The conclusion holds that the core issue lies in "how to use" rather than "whether to use." Only when technology and the subject constrain each other can compound choreography talents be cultivated. The course system proposed in this paper can provide a promotable model for the "AI+" teaching reform of the dance major.

title: Visualizing Subculture: Symbolism, Storytelling and Media Behavior in AI Videos — A Case Study of The Era of Smart Guardian?
container-title: Communications in Humanities Research
5f0a858d2b53000e66de15477b37fae5539d6781.abstract: In the era of rapid development in the AI industry, AI can accurately answer the meanings and connotations of many concepts, including subcultures. However, some people question whether AI generated videos can fully reflect its understanding of the subcultures being represented. This study examines how subcultural elements are represented in AI-generated advertising videos, using the case study of a Chinese commercial The Era of Smart Guardian. The investigation analyzes from three dimensions, which are visual symbols, storytelling and media behaviors. The advertisement mainly incorporates three subcultural elements: "cyberpunk", "pop art", and "surrealism". The overall research has found that the synergistic effect of these three dimensions forms a phenomenon, which is "hollowed representation", where subcultures retain high visual recognizability, whereas they lost their contextual meaning and critical potential, becoming mere aesthetic commodities for commercial consumption.

title: Ethical Controversies in AI-Driven Risk Control and Content Moderation on Social Platforms—A Case Study of Xiaohongshu
container-title: Communications in Humanities Research
e1a340d0b698a6c9bcd1496f036d89c468b89652.abstract: The use of artificial intelligence (AI) to identify and manage content risks on social platforms is growing. It raises ethical questions about uncertain classifications, proportionate intervention and opportunities to challenge decisions. This paper examines Xiaohongshu through a qualitative documentary case study comprising a technical publication, a regulatory document and three original news reports. The analysis distinguishes source identification, harmfulness assessment and moderation action, and examines the relationship between internal explanations and user-facing remedies. The selected documents separately describe evidence for reviewers, information for audiences and appeal access, leaving their integration unevaluated. This study argues that technical explanations alone do not establish user-facing procedural protection, understandable reasons and accessible correction are also necessary. Source labels can provide transparency without establishing harm, while stronger restrictions require an additional justification appropriate to their consequences. Differentiated review, bounded disclosure and traceable appeals are proposed as design requirements whose effectiveness remains to be evaluated. The contribution emphasizes linking content-safety objectives with user protections in platform governance.

title: Language-Mediated Frenchness: Cultural Representation and Distributed Authorship in Multilingual Generative AI Narratives
container-title: Communications in Humanities Research
2ccdf9485ce3fab9eaa51b491acd7a84295e1295.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence is gradually expanding beyond information retrieval and text-assistance tools into storytelling, literary production, and cultural expression. For multilingual AI, language not only serves an informational function but may also be associated with different training data, forms of cultural knowledge, and narrative conventions. Consequently, the same narrative task may yield cultural expressions that are not entirely identical when generated in different linguistic contexts. Taking "a French child leaving home for the first time" as a common narrative theme, this study compares three stories generated by ChatGPT from equivalent prompts in French, English, and Chinese. Using comparative textual analysis, the three texts are coded across multiple dimensions. The findings show that although the texts share a common narrative structure, they differ markedly in their cultural expressions and representational choices. These linguistic differences should not be interpreted as evidence that language directly determines culture. Rather, language can be understood as a cultural interface and cue that prompts the model to activate different language–culture associations, which in turn shape the characters, spaces, values, and narrative forms of the stories.

title: Low Cost Wearable AI Knee Rehabilitation System: Real-Time Motion Correction and Adaptive Training Based on Multimodal Sensing Fusion
container-title: Theoretical and Natural Science
fd2e3c704ef12833fbf0c69ebce86dcf944b53d6.abstract: The success of knee rehabilitation depends heavily on the correct execution of exercises. Currently, most treatments require supervision by physical therapists, which can be expensive. When exercises are performed without a therapist, incorrect movements are often used, increasing the risk of re-injury. To address this, a low-cost, wearable smart knee rehabilitation system is introduced in this study. A combination of multimodal sensors is employed to provide real-time motion correction and adaptive training. By integrating IMU data, visual pose estimation, and muscle signals (EMG), three-dimensional knee angles are accurately measured. Common mistakes such as knee collapse, twisting, or insufficient bending can be detected. Instant feedback is delivered through a display interface, guiding users to correct their posture and thereby improving exercise quality while reducing injury risk. Additionally, the system incorporates a smart training feature. Surface EMG (sEMG) is used to monitor muscle fatigue and movement accuracy. When fatigue is detected, the workout is automatically adjusted—by reducing speed or decreasing the number of repetitions. This approach reduces the dependence on expensive clinical equipment. The integration of multimodal sensor data with an adaptive system makes home rehabilitation more scientific, accurate, and user-friendly. Finally, this research provides a low-cost, high-precision real-time tracking prototype for smart home monitoring.

title: Native-to-fibril structural remodelling reveals an amyloid-selective transthyretin epitope for AI-guided binder design
0f4beab0194266f85aa8a93aa74c4ccf134164d3.abstract: Abstract Transthyretin (TTR) amyloidosis involves conversion of the native tetramer into cross-$\beta$ fibrils, creating potential targets for conformation-selective binders. Full-assembly solvent-accessibility analysis of 30 patient-derived fibril structures, spanning wild-type TTR and ten hereditary variants, identifies increased exposure of an N-terminal region adjacent to Cys10. Using a common normalisation reference, mean relative solvent accessibility for residues 11--15 is 0.089 in native TTR and at least 0.168 in fibrils. Modification mapping, saturation-mutagenesis stability predictions and steric PTM models provide molecular context. BoltzGen and RFAntibody generate candidate binders, and sequence-only Boltz-2 counter-predictions place selected nanobodies at the Pro11/Met13/Lys15 region in fibril-derived constructs but at distal surfaces in native-state constructs. Vitreous-fibril designs also engage cardiac-fibril constructs, suggesting cross-tissue epitope recognition. These results support structure-guided candidate prioritisation, while fibril geometry, binding affinity and disease-state selectivity require experimental validation.

title: AI for Everything: Opportunities, Challenges, and Responsible Use of Artificial Intelligence in School Education
container-title: Saudi Journal of Engineering and Technology
7dfe9b4d0f5210bb02b154f05d865035753032c9.abstract: AI assistance can improve a pupil’s immediate output without improving independent learning. This targeted, structured review examines school education at approximately ages 6–18, synthesizing 25 cited sources and extracting comparable design and outcome information from eight studies or reviews. Logged revision searches, DOI metadata, source decisions, and extraction records support auditability without claiming a comprehensive systematic search. Domain-specific intelligent tutoring systems and general-purpose generative AI have different evidence bases. Effects depend on comparators, outcome measures, implementation, and assessment conditions; confidence intervals and reported uncertainty are retained rather than combining incompatible results. A school evidence table distinguishes pupils from repeated observations and immediate assisted performance from verified unaided outcomes. Self-regulated learning, cognitive offloading, and scaffolding inform a proposed attempt–consult–verify–explain–fade–transfer routine. An unvalidated decision aid links developmental context, tool eligibility, supervision, and local unaided-learning evidence, complementing existing competency, child-rights, and assessment-regime frameworks. Schools should prioritize learning, inclusion, safety, and teacher responsibility, and revise or stop uses that do not meet those goals.

title: Explainable AI Driven Frameworks for Real Time Cyber Threat Detection and Response: A Systematic Review
f477932434f4ad5794064f13c1c53610bb3f41a6.abstract: The digitization of an ever-developing network of cybersecurity threats has weighted traditional packet filter rule-based firewalls and signature based intrusion detection systems towards being less effective against zero day vulnerabilities, ransomware, polymorphic malware, and Advanced Persistent Threat (APTs) attacks. Emerging technologies like Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) have potential to be game changers for proactive and adaptive defence of cyberspace. This review investigates AI powered cybersecurity systems: machine learning algorithms, deep learning architectures, Reinforcement Learning, and Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI). Also investigated will be applications within Cloud Computing, Healthcare, Maritime Systems and National Critical Infrastructure. Further discussions will include feature engineering, Transformer based Zero Shot Learning (ZSL), SOAR integration, blockchain-based forensic integrity, adversarial AI and quantum computing concerns. The results demonstrated positive trends through AI powered cybersecurity systems improving detection Accuracy, lowering False Positives, reducing incident response time and enhancing Autonomous Defence capabilities. However, challenges around Explainability, Ethical Governance, Scalability of Computation, and Adversarial Resistance are expressed as possible major concerns. A conclusion point will outlining future research directions to develop, build and maintain resilient, transparent and quantum resistant Cybersecurity Ecosystems.

title: Employee Privacy and Human Review in AI Workplace Monitoring in Bangladesh
800395b5755d17a4eab6ab1e93201406111fcac9.abstract: Artificial intelligence can expand the ability of employers to collect and analyse information about work. Whether such monitoring is acceptable depends on both informational safeguards and the procedures through which monitoring data affect employees. This study examines expectations of notice, proportionate purpose, data disclosure and human review in Bangladesh. It analyses 385 adult respondents who reported awareness of AI, using item-level distributions, paired endorsement comparisons and an exploratory proportional-odds model. The sample includes 238 law students and is not presented as representative of employed workers or the national workforce. Notice that AI monitors workplace activity was endorsed by 292 respondents (75.8%), while review before serious employment consequences was endorsed by 205 (53.2%). Their within-person difference was 22.6 percentage points (95% bootstrap interval 16.4-28.8; Holm-adjusted p < .001). Sixty-one respondents (15.8%) endorsed all four procedural safeguards. Privacy safeguards were said to affect acceptance of monitoring by 301 respondents (78.2%). In the adjusted model, the notice expectation showed a pointwise odds ratio of 1.35 (95% confidence interval 1.04-1.75), but its Holm-adjusted p-value was .102; the four focal associations therefore provide limited evidence after multiplicity adjustment. These findings describe distinctions between stated expectations, not the effect of actual monitoring, privacy violations or psychological-contract breach. Integrating legal safeguards with job demands-resources and psychological-contract perspectives, the article proposes a sequence connecting notice, purpose limitation, usable information and meaningful review. Longitudinal and experimental studies of employees and implemented systems are needed to examine whether these safeguards change perceived privacy and workplace outcomes.

title: Former Third Molar Sockets Often Remain Histopathologically Altered: A Retrospective Study of Covered Socket Residua with AI-Based Cell Quantification
80d78eec3ac54be2bbf2fd98f7197bc28b24850b.abstract: Background/Objectives: After tooth removal the crest may close before the socket has mineralised, leaving a covered socket residuum (CSR). Third molars are usually removed in young patients, often prophylactically. We examined what former third molar sites contain years later. Methods: Retrospective single-centre study of bone removed at revision of a radiologically diagnosed CSR at former third molar sites, consisting of the bone lid covering the residuum and, where labelled separately, tissue from its depth. For every section the routine pathology report was coded for a leading finding, and the cells were classified independently by whole-slide AI analysis without knowledge of the report. Results: Eighty-three sections from 28 patients (median age 54 years) were analysed. Fifty-one (61.4%) carried a distinguishing finding (53.0% without haematopoietically active marrow), most often marrow fibrosis (14.5%), granulocytic inflammation or osteomyelitis (13.3%) and lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate (10.8%). Of 24 patients with more than one section, 13 showed different findings in different sections. Fibroblasts and inflammatory cells were inversely related (r = −0.979), and the diagnoses formed a gradient from fibroblast-rich avital bone and unremarkable marrow to lymphocyte-rich inflammation (Holm-adjusted p ≤ 0.0065 for fibroblasts, lymphocytes and neutrophils). Conclusions: In this cohort, more than half of the sections from former third molar sites were histopathologically altered, with findings that varied within the same patient. Third molar removal is bone surgery requiring asepsis, removal of the follicle and debridement of the socket, and filling the socket to prevent a residuum deserves controlled evaluation.

title: AI Driven Recommendations and Consumer Awareness of Transparency and Misleading Claims in Bangladesh
9b2c7f6bf51d9f894e8210377d960f5c8c6437cd.abstract: Automated recommendations organise commercial visibility, yet consumers’ support for transparency should not be equated with demonstrated knowledge of recommendation practices or legal remedies. This study examines that distinction using the supplied Group 7 database of 385 adult, consenting, AI-aware respondents in Bangladesh. Law students account for 232 observations; recent online-shopping experience is not independently established. Rather than combine heterogeneous questionnaire blocks into latent constructs, the analysis uses item distributions, paired endorsement contrasts, joint response patterns, rank correlations and adjusted binary and ordinal models. Agreement that misleading AI-generated claims create consumer-protection concerns reaches 81.0%, compared with 56.1% for understanding recommendation influence. Personalisation disclosure receives 69.4% endorsement, while 60.5% endorse clear information about sponsored or manipulated recommendations. Transparency’s perceived decision value exceeds self-reported manipulation recognition by 13.8 percentage points. The four questionnaire blocks have low internal consistency, with alpha between 0.158 and 0.201. No focal predictor survives multiplicity correction in the primary binary model of misleading-claims awareness. Influence awareness is positively associated with the outcome in an ordinal sensitivity model, indicating dependence on outcome coding. These findings distinguish broad protection preferences from narrower self-reported capabilities without establishing a causal literacy pathway, objective legal competence or actual complaint behaviour. The contribution is a consumer-autonomy framework linking recommendation visibility to information usability and contestability. Platform recommendations prioritise intelligible sponsorship labels, accessible explanations and practical evidence preservation. The findings concern a legally oriented sample and should inform targeted behavioural research rather than estimates of national consumer competence.

title: Evaluating Human–AI Decision Architectures Under Varying Risk and Readiness: A Monte Carlo Simulation in Industrial Quality Control
e56e2aa7650aca247b7f1501b9b96478885b3fe9.abstract: Artificial Intelligence is increasingly involved in industrial decision-making, but its valuedepends not only on predictive accuracy but on how information and decision power areshared between humans and AI. This study assesses six Human–AI decision architectures forindustrial quality control through a controlled Monte Carlo simulation: Human-only,calibrated cost-aware AI-only automation, Black-box Human–AI, Explainable Human–AI,Actionable Human–AI, and a normative expected-cost benchmark. The analysis combines abaseline experiment, a full-factorial sensitivity analysis over 27 combinations of AIreadiness, human readiness, and false-accept cost, and a 60-month dynamic simulationincorporating human learning, AI performance degradation, and periodic retraining. Nosingle deployable architecture is uniformly best across all conditions and performancecriteria. At baseline, AI-only automation achieves the lowest Cost of Quality amongdeployable architectures, while Actionable Human–AI clearly outperforms Human-only,Black-box, and Explainable designs. However, Actionable Human–AI beats AI-onlyautomation in cost terms in only three of the 27 static scenarios, all involving low AIreadiness with sufficiently capable humans. In dynamic weak-AI conditions, ActionableHuman–AI cuts false-accept rates by over 24 percentage points and improves normativedecision alignment at only modest extra cost. The findings show that explainability alonedoes not improve operational decisions, that human control adds value only under specificcapability and risk conditions, and that AI's role should be treated as a context-dependentdesign factor. The study offers a computational framework for evaluating Human–AIdecision architectures beyond model accuracy alone.

title: Teachers’ self-reported AI literacy across educational levels in Greece: Awareness without conceptual depth?
container-title: International Journal of Research Studies in Education
0d54666a57e2d19673e62dcf1e5f982df429e5a3.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) literacy is increasingly recognized as an essential teacher competence, yet evidence concerning its dimensional structure and variation across educational sectors remains limited. This study investigated self-reported AI literacy among 1,173 in-service teachers in primary, secondary, and higher education in Greece, examining its empirical structure, overall levels, and associations with prior AI-related training and teaching level, while accounting for academic qualifications. Data were collected through a researcher-developed questionnaire and analyzed using exploratory factor analysis, descriptive statistics, and general linear models. Two dimensions emerged: Conceptual–Technical AI Literacy and Critical–Ethical AI Literacy, while Practical AI Use was retained as a separate indicator. Overall self-reported AI literacy was relatively low, with substantially higher scores on critical–ethical indicators than on conceptual–technical indicators, suggesting a profile of perceived awareness without corresponding conceptual depth. Prior AI-related training was positively associated with all AI-literacy outcomes across educational sectors. However, significant teaching-level × training interactions revealed particularly strong associations in higher education, especially for Conceptual–Technical AI Literacy. These findings highlight the multidimensional and context-sensitive nature of teachers’ self-reported AI literacy and the importance of distinguishing perceived confidence from demonstrated competence. They underscore the need for differentiated, pedagogically grounded professional development that integrates conceptual understanding, practical AI applications, critical evaluation, and ethical judgment across educational sectors.

title: Enforcing the AI Act at the national level: Germany’s KI-MIG as a blueprint for AI market surveillance in Europe?
container-title: International Cybersecurity Law Review
dae4e116ca0ea4a6fcb9e2c1d5e6b30cdd3bc86b.abstract: Abstract The EU Artificial Intelligence Act is directly applicable in all Member States, yet its practical effectiveness hinges on national enforcement structures that the Regulation itself only sketches in outline. Member States were required to designate notifying and market surveillance authorities by 2 August 2025—a deadline most of them, including Germany, missed. With the entry into force of the KI-Marktüberwachungs- und Innovationsförderungsgesetz (KI-MIG) on 29 July 2026, Germany has now settled its national enforcement architecture: a hybrid model that concentrates residual market surveillance, coordination, single-point-of-contact and complaint-handling functions in the Bundesnetzagentur, preserves the sectoral competences of existing regulators at federal and Länder level, creates an independent chamber for fundamental-rights-sensitive high-risk AI systems, and ties the supervision of the cybersecurity dimension of high-risk AI to the market surveillance authority of the Cyber Resilience Act—a role performed in the interim by the Federal Office for Information Security. This article analyses the KI-MIG against the requirements of Chapter VII of the AI Act, situates it within the timelines recalibrated by the Digital Omnibus on AI (Regulation (EU) 2026/1744), and compares the German approach with the enforcement models emerging in Spain, Italy, Cyprus and other Member States. It argues that the German hybrid model offers instructive answers to the coordination problems of decentralised AI oversight, but that its ‘blueprint’ quality will ultimately depend on operational capacity, on the resolution of federal frictions that have already brought the law to the brink of a mediation procedure, and on whether the Union succeeds in containing the fragmentation of AI market surveillance across 27 national systems.

title: A multi-reader multi-case study comparing Breast Cancer Reading Efficiency and Accuracy in Screening with Tomosynthesis versus AI-assisted mammography
container-title: British Journal of Radiology
99047a82d2afcff90eea4ff1243855ccabcd968b.abstract: Abstract Objectives Full-field digital mammography (FFDM) is the standard for breast cancer screening but has reduced sensitivity in dense breasts. Digital breast tomosynthesis (DBT) improves cancer detection compared to 2D mammography but is limited by cost and longer reading times. Artificial intelligence (AI)–enhanced mammography has demonstrated improved sensitivity compared to 2D mammography. This study compares AI-enhanced 2D mammography (DM+AI) with DBT in recalling interval breast cancers (IBCs). Methods : A multi-reader, multi-case crossover study was conducted using the Emory BrEast Imaging Dataset, which includes paired FFDM and DBT images with biopsy-proven outcomes. Six radiologists reviewed 53 IBC and 53 screen-detected cancer (SDC) cases, with random assignment to DM+AI or DBT, followed by crossover after a washout period. Primary outcomes included recall rate of IBCs. Secondary outcomes included recall rate of SDCs, interpretation time, and subgroup analysis by breast density. Results : For IBCs, DM+AI and DBT demonstrated similar recall rates (41.5% vs 40.9%) and detection rates (14.8% vs 11.9%). DM+AI identified more non-invasive (31.5% vs 13.0%) and mass-forming (61.0% vs 21.8%) cancers. For SDCs, recall and detection rates were comparable across modalities. In fatty breasts, recall was higher with DM+AI (91.7% vs 50.0%), while DBT performed better in extremely dense breasts. DM+AI enabled faster interpretation, averaging 24.1 seconds less per case. Conclusion : AI-enhanced 2D mammography demonstrated comparable performance to DBT with shorter interpretation times, supporting a stratified screening approach. Advances in Knowledge This study is the first direct comparison of AI-enhanced mammography and digital breast tomosynthesis for IBC detection.

title: From conventional monitoring to agentic AI: integration of data streams and computational tools for real-time microalgal surveillance
container-title: Frontiers in Systems Biology
4db3ab5d7cf530a92142b474b34e50977109bfc0.abstract: Microalgal cultivation generates continuous and diverse data streams, including physicochemical sensor measurements, optical and spectroscopic signals, and episodic molecular tests. Together, these data characterize cultivation conditions at different biological scales. Existing AI/ML frameworks can interpret these streams independently; however, human intervention is required to translate predictions into cultivation decisions, adding delays and limiting adaptability across strains, reactors, and environmental conditions. This mini-review describes the transition from conventional monitoring to agentic AI as the progressive integration of sensing, interpretation, and action. The real-time sensing modalities that constitute an agent’s perceptual field include AI/ML models and genome-scale metabolic models, which serve as callable tools in the proposed agentic architecture for coordinated data-model integration in algal systems biology. Emerging evidence from agentic systems in microbiome research and precision oncology supports the conceptual and technical plausibility of a multi-agent, tool-enabled framework for autonomous microalgal cultivation and management. However, the proposed integrated architecture holds significant potential for microalgal cultivation systems, it has not yet been implemented and requires experimental validation.

title: <b>Understanding the Relationship Between Generative AI Dependence and Students’ Problem-Solving Ability: The Roles of Cognitive Offloading and AI Literacy</b>
container-title: International journal of interdisciplinary knowledge (IJIK)
5adbd2c658c88307c120c73ec371e4ffa9afcdb5.abstract: Today, Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) is quickly becoming a staple of university students' work, as it can provide instant answers to information search, writing, explanation and problem solving. While GenAI can aid in learning, overreliance can lessen students' independent thinking. This study explores the ties between generative AI reliance and students' problem-solving skills, focusing on cognitive offloading as a mediation factor and AI literacy as a moderation factor. A quantitative, cross-sectional research design is suggested with a sample of 100 University students. The data will be analyzed using descriptive statistics, reliability analysis, Pearson correlation, regression, mediation and moderation analysis through SPSS. The conceptual model suggests that students' problem-solving ability may be linked to their degree of cognitive offloading, which could be further linked to their reliance on GenAI. The authors suggest AI literacy as a boundary condition that could affect the relationship between GenAI dependence and problem solving ability. New studies suggest that students' use of GenAI in problem-solving is multi-layered and constructive, as well as thoughtless, and that there are four aspects of AI literacy: knowledge, application, evaluation, and understanding of ethical issues. Thus, the present study is centered on not only students' usage of GenAI, but also how reliance on GenAI can impact their thinking processes when addressing academic challenges.

title: AI-Enabled Experience Orchestration: Coordinating Physical, Digital & Human Resources across Situational Customer Journeys
container-title: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
479827cd30030c3a07bb272e1365d49fd6349d5b.abstract: Purpose: The study creates AI-enabled experience orchestration (AIEO) to describe how service systems can orchestrate digital, physical and human resources as customer requirements vary through a journey. Design/methodology/approach: The study incorporates customer-journey, service-system, omni-channel and AIenabled service lenses. In a doctoral survey of 578 complete eligible herbal-cosmetics consumers, bounded phenomenon motivation has been administered instead of a test of AIEO; the survey did not include any AI measures. Findings: AIEO consists of situational sensing, matching of resources, sequencing and continuity journey. The relevance, coherence, confidence, reducing uncertainty and perceived control, subject to the complexity of journey, situational changeability, resource complementary features, readiness of AI and responsible governance theories these capabilities should function. Originality: The framework goes beyond channel connectivity and discrete points of contact with the AI system by imagining adaptive, journey-level coordination of heterogeneous services resources and keeping customer agency. Practical implications: Service managers ought to diagnose the existing customer need, activate the most appropriate resource, and maintain only authorized context and present meaningful override and human escalation.

title: Evaluating AI agents on the IUCN Red List assessor exam: Tradeoffs and opportunities for AI assistants in extinction risk assessments
344ed78469f05367014df1a39f361b0d892e725a.abstract: The IUCN Red List of Threatened Species is the world's most widely used system for assessing the global extinction risk of species, underpinning conservation policy and action worldwide. However, due to funding constraints and limited assessor capacity, the Red List faces significant gaps in species coverage (less than 20% of plant species have been assessed) and challenges in keeping assessments up to date (over 30% are 10+ years old). Recent advances in AI open new opportunities for helping assessors increase assessment throughput and quality, but also raise concerns about trust and reliability, data security, cost, and environmental impact. As a starting point for considering these tradeoffs, this paper evaluates the performance of AI agents on the official IUCN Red List assessor training exam. On a benchmark of 101 exam questions, we show that several frontier models from Anthropic and OpenAI reliably clear the exam's 75% pass mark. The top-performing model, Anthropic's Claude Opus 5, reaches 96% mean accuracy, increasing to 99% with majority vote over five attempts. Notably, the pass mark is now also reached by open-weight models running on local hardware: Alibaba's Qwen3.8 Flash, self-hosted on a single desktop Mac Studio, attains 81% mean accuracy (87% majority vote). This points to viable hosting alternatives where data security or sustainability concerns preclude sending data through external providers' data centres. Whilst the exam serves only as a capability floor, these results strengthen the case for thoughtful use of AI assistants in assessors' workflows, such as quality and consistency checks on draft assessments.

title: From Execution to Discovery : Physical Verification as the Key Gap in AI Agents for Science
f0e6da5eaeddda2939ea63a91dcd65c87a21b744.abstract: Why can AI agents operate reliably in digital environments such as software development yet still struggle to achieve autonomous scientific discovery? We argue that this gap reflects not only limitations in model capability but also differences in how agent capabilities are externalized and how reliably environments can verify the consequences of agent actions. In this survey, we trace the technical evolution of AI agents and propose a three-stage framework of capability externalization: reasoning externalization makes knowledge, memory, and intermediate inferences inspectable; execution externalization makes tool use and long-horizon workflows governable; and world-interaction externalization integrates environmental evidence into hypothesis revision and action selection. Materials discovery provides a demanding testbed for all three stages, spanning literature-grounded hypothesis generation, computational design, automated experimentation, and iterative knowledge updating. Although agents can increasingly complete predefined research workflows, workflow automation alone does not constitute scientific discovery. Sustained autonomy requires agents to assess whether new observations support or challenge a hypothesis and to select subsequent experiments accordingly. We therefore identify environmental verifiability as a central systems constraint on agent autonomy: the extent to which an environment can translate actions into timely, attributable, reproducible, and affordable evidence. This perspective positions physical verification capacity as a key scaling dimension for autonomous scientific discovery.

title: Accommodation Made Cheap: AI Impacts on Replies to Online Reviews and the Signal Value of Tailoring
a0980e060282ae3be0051462bc8d9c53432624a8.abstract: Accommodating a message to its recipient takes effort, and that effort is part of what accommodation signals. AI language models now reduce this effort. We study a masspersonal setting, restaurant replies to diners’ reviews on OpenTable, in six U.S. metropolitan areas from 2019 to mid-2026, with an interrupted time-series design around the introduction of ChatGPT. The detected AI likelihood of replies rose to 44% by mid-2026, compared with 1.2% for customer reviews. Replies became more tailored to the reviews they answered, most in quarters when AI likely wrote at least half of a restaurant’s replies. They also became more similar across restaurants but less similar within each restaurant. Before 2023, more tailored replies were followed by more reviews over the next year; from 2023, they no longer were, although this decline cannot yet be attributed to AI authorship. The form of accommodation may spread while the effort behind it falls.

title: Pemanfaatan Fitur AI Text-to-Image pada Canva untuk Meningkatkan Kreativitas Desain Antarmuka Siswa SMP
container-title: Journal of Authentic Research
af64dd54c6ea2efc8bd1e0bb0249f9385e3608f0.abstract: Kreativitas siswa dalam merancang antarmuka digital dapat terhambat ketika pembelajaran terlalu bergantung pada template siap pakai. Penelitian ini bertujuan membandingkan kreativitas desain antarmuka siswa yang belajar dengan fitur AI Text-to-Image pada Canva dan siswa yang menggunakan fitur standar Canva, mengukur peningkatan kreativitas, serta menjelaskan pengalaman siswa selama ko-kreasi dengan AI. Penelitian menggunakan metode campuran dengan desain sekuensial eksplanatori. Tahap kuantitatif menerapkan kuasi-eksperimen nonequivalent control group pada 61 siswa kelas VIII SMP Negeri 2 Sijunjung, terdiri atas 30 siswa kelompok eksperimen dan 31 siswa kelompok kontrol. Kreativitas dinilai melalui tes unjuk kerja berdasarkan kelancaran, keluwesan, orisinalitas, dan elaborasi; tahap kualitatif menggunakan wawancara reflektif terhadap enam siswa kelompok eksperimen. Analisis tanpa penyesuaian skor awal menunjukkan rata-rata posttest kelompok eksperimen (12,80) lebih tinggi daripada kelompok kontrol (9,20), t(59) = 8,712, p < 0,001, Cohen’s d = 2,23, 95% CI [1,58, 2,87]. Secara deskriptif, N-Gain kelompok eksperimen sebesar 0,66 dan kelompok kontrol 0,29, dengan selisih indikator terbesar pada orisinalitas. Wawancara menunjukkan bahwa siswa terbantu memunculkan ide visual, merevisi prompt secara iteratif, dan merefleksikan tanggung jawab etis. Temuan ini menunjukkan hasil yang menjanjikan bagi integrasi AI Text-to-Image melalui prompt engineering terstruktur, tetapi interpretasi kausal perlu dibatasi karena penugasan kelas tidak dilakukan secara acak. Students’ creativity in digital interface design can be constrained when learning relies heavily on ready-made templates. This study compared interface-design creativity between students learning with Canva’s AI Text-to-Image feature and those using standard Canva features, quantified improvement, and explored students’ experiences during human–AI co-creation. An explanatory sequential mixed-methods design was employed. The quantitative phase used a nonequivalent control group quasi-experiment involving 61 eighth-grade students at SMP Negeri 2 Sijunjung, with 30 students in the experimental group and 31 in the control group. Creativity was assessed through a performance task covering fluency, flexibility, originality, and elaboration; the qualitative phase used reflective interviews with six experimental-group students. The unadjusted posttest comparison showed a higher mean for the experimental group (12.80) than the control group (9.20), t(59) = 8.712, p < .001, Cohen’s d = 2.23, 95% CI [1.58, 2.87]. Descriptively, normalized gain was 0.66 in the experimental group and 0.29 in the control group, with the largest indicator-level difference in originality. Interviews indicated that students generated visual ideas more easily, revised prompts iteratively, and reflected on ethical responsibility. These findings suggest promising educational value for structured prompt-engineering activities with text-to-image AI, while causal claims should remain cautious because class assignment was nonrandom.

title: One product, two rulebooks: the cybersecurity of high-risk AI systems between article 15 AI act and the cyber resilience act after the digital omnibus
container-title: International Cybersecurity Law Review
959eb7b5c5ca4aa295e6151af6cd673982e3233c.abstract: Abstract High-risk AI systems distributed as software or embedded in connected hardware are simultaneously subject to two horizontal security rulebooks: the accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity requirements of Art. 15 of the AI Act and the essential cybersecurity requirements of the Cyber Resilience Act (CRA). The Union legislature anticipated this overlap and built a bridge: under Art. 12 CRA—since July 2026 mirrored in Art. 42(3) AI Act, as inserted by the Digital Omnibus on AI (Regulation (EU) 2026/1744)—products with digital elements that are classified as high-risk AI systems are deemed to comply with the cybersecurity requirements of Art. 15 AI Act if they satisfy the CRA’s essential requirements and the achievement of the Art. 15 protection level is demonstrated in the CRA declaration of conformity, with the conformity assessment, as a rule, integrated into the AI Act procedure. The Omnibus has re-sequenced the two regimes: the high-risk obligations for stand-alone Annex III systems, deferred to 2 December 2027, now become applicable nine days before the CRA’s main obligations on 11 December 2027, whereas high-risk AI embedded in Annex I products follows on 2 August 2028, and the CRA’s reporting duties have bound manufacturers—including of AI products already on the market—since 11 September 2026. Drawing on the consolidated legislative texts, the Commission’s CRA guidance of July 2026 and the standardisation work of CEN-CENELEC JTC 13 and JTC 21, this article maps the scope overlap, analyses the mechanics and limits of the bridge—the accuracy and robustness carve-out, the narrowly drawn derogation for important and critical products in Art. 12(3) CRA, and the gap between AI-specific attack vectors and the CRA’s generic essentials—and argues that the bridge is coherent on a reading, anchored in the recitals of both acts, under which the adversarial-machine-learning threat model enters the CRA’s risk-based essentials. It translates the analysis into an integrated compliance architecture with a structured requirement-to-evidence mapping and formulates recommendations addressed separately to the Commission and the standardisation bodies, and to providers and manufacturers.

title: Regulatory Science: A Condition of Innovation for AI as a Medical Device
container-title: EMJ Innovation
deb5207c6a8ffea2ba10ac6ec6ab818b32b7381c.abstract: AI systems are increasingly being introduced into healthcare, many of them meeting the threshold for regulation as medical devices. However, the regulatory frameworks built to evaluate their safety and performance were designed for stable, tangible products rather than the highly context-dependent, frequently updating software systems whose risks emerge in real-world use. This creates a dilemma for health systems: the pressure to adopt AI at pace sits uneasily alongside the need to validate, monitor, and govern it vigilantly. This piece will describe how regulatory science offers a route through this tension to realise the benefits of innovation safely. Drawing on national infrastructure and case studies from the Centre of Excellence for Regulatory Science and Innovation in AI and Digital Health (CERSI-AI), this article sets out what regulatory science looks like in practice, and why building the governance and capability to deploy AI responsibly may prove harder than building the technology itself.

title: Silent methodological failures in AI-assisted science: benchmarking large language model agents for virtual gene knockout analysis
7806bc591bff0cc653dde9473f1875b7c740b9d4.abstract: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed as autonomous agents in computational biology, yet their reliability in executing complex scientific workflows remains poorly characterized. Here, we benchmarked five LLM agents (DeepSeek V4 Pro, GLM 5.1, HY3 Preview, Kimi K2.6, and Minimax M2.7) on virtual gene knockout analyses using four computational frameworks across two single-cell RNA-sequencing datasets. All agents successfully completed the assigned workflows, but their quantitative outputs varied substantially: execution times spanned a 31fold range (61 − 1,920 s), while cross-model coefficients of variation reached 142.1%. Notably, four of five agents (80%) exhibited “silent methodological failures,” generating computationally valid, error-free code that produced biologically implausible results. Among the evaluated agents, GLM 5.1 showed the most balanced performance across computational efficiency and biological plausibility. These findings demonstrate that successful code execution alone does not ensure scientific validity and highlight cross-model concordance and biological validation as important quality-control strategies for Artificial Intelligence (AI)-assisted computational biology workflows.

3304231ea0d6e9259b8785884fbd7581e74971ca.abstract: Technological progress is a continuous process that changes perceptions and approaches to the implementation of various types of activities. This is how artificial intelligence (AI) appears and is applied in most areas of our lives. Its spread in school environments is increasing and developing in different directions which suggests that higher education also needs to build application standards. Its establishment as a method of training is an important component for the incorporation of students in the business environment. The integration of AI into everyday economic activities is constantly growing. Building models for the use of artificial intelligence is becoming a major component in the formation of work competencies. Management accounting is among the fastest-growing economic sciences, which also implies the development of relevant training. It is significant to develop an approach to the use of AI in management accounting training, since lack of familiarity with the system creates undesirable effects from its application.

title: Rhetorical Effects of AI Paraphrasing on Argumentation and Authorial Stance in Arab EFL Literature Reviews
container-title: World Journal of English Language
3ef92b12a02e1e6e76bb26a3194e86a266fd06a2.abstract: Recent research has identified systematic differences between AI-generated and human-authored academic writing. However, most studies focus on argumentative essays, leaving the rhetorical effects of AI use on literature reviews underexplored. This paper addresses this gap through a controlled analysis of how AI paraphrasing reshapes argumentation and authorial stance in Arab EFL postgraduate literature reviews under content-preserving conditions.Using a paired corpus design, this study compares ten human-authored literature reviews produced in 2020, prior to the widespread use of large language models, with ChatGPT-paraphrased versions produced using a controlled prompt. This design isolates core AI transformation patterns. Analysis draws on Toulmin’s model of argumentation and Hyland’s stance framework, supported by corpus-based validation.Results indicated systematic rhetorical transformation. While ChatGPT preserved structural coherence and improved surface fluency, the AI-generated texts showed reduced rhetorical complexity and weakened authorial stance. Self-mention and reader inclusion were sharply reduced, hedging became more formulaic, warrants shifted from situated reasoning to generic principles, and contrastive and causal connectives occurred less frequently. These findings clarify which rhetorical features are most vulnerable under controlled AI paraphrasing and position AI paraphrasing as a concern for EFL academic writing pedagogy.

title: AI vs. Human Communication: A Pragmatic Analysis of Implicature and Gricean Maxims in EFL Contexts
container-title: World Journal of English Language
4501246acd3bafaee3e600660bedf69fb64d9f66.abstract: The importance of Gricean maxims in online text communication stems from the lack of prosodic features and non-verbal cues in AI tools that may lead to digital misunderstanding. As AI tools like ChatGPT continue to be integrated into English as a Foreign Language (EFL) classrooms, learners increasingly interact with AI interlocutors whose pragmatic abilities, patterns of adherence to Gricean maxims, and implicature generation may differ fundamentally from those of human speakers. This mixed-methods explanatory study compares AI-generated and human EFL learner communication with respect to adherence to Gricean maxims and the generation and interpretation of conversational implicature. The study sample comprised 84 intermediate-to-advanced EFL undergraduates at a Saudi university who completed a Discourse Completion Task (DCT), an Implicature Interpretation Task (IIT), and a 32-item questionnaire. A standardized prompting protocol was used to prompt ChatGPT to deliver responses to the same DCT scenarios as human participants. Analysis of quantitative data indicated that the AI responses complied with Grice’s maxims of quantity and manner but exhibited productive flouting, reflecting a diminished capacity to engage in the contextually sensitive maxim flouting necessary to generate conversational implicatures. Meanwhile, EFL learners flouted the maxims more intuitively - particularly in relation and quality - generating richer implicature, but their comprehension of AI-generated implicit meaning was poorer than that of human-generated implicature. The study concludes with theoretically informed suggestions for pragmatics-integrated EFL teaching and AI tool development, and proposes adopting generative AI systems tuned to pragmatic depth in language.

title: Rethinking Intellectual Property in the Age of Generative AI: Ethics, Rights and Accountability
9123672b7cf31cde0882046971aee32bb6bae394.abstract: Abstract The rapid commercialisation of generative artificial intelligence (AI) has converted long-standing philosophical debates about authorship, property and fairness into live disputes before courts and legislatures. This article examines the ethical dimensions of AI and intellectual property rights (IPR) through a mixed doctrinal–empirical design. It develops a four-axis analytical framework (Consent, Compensation, Credit and Accountability) and tests it against secondary data drawn exclusively from verifiable public sources: the World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO) patent landscape on generative AI, the Stanford AI Index 2025, curated litigation trackers, court judgments and settlement orders from the United States, the United Kingdom, Germany and India, creator surveys by the Society of Authors, an economic study commissioned by CISAC, and the foundational algorithmic-bias audit by Buolamwini and Gebru. The findings show that (i) generative-AI patenting is highly concentrated, with China-based inventors accounting for roughly 71 per cent of 54,000 patent families filed in 2014–2023, while India accounts for about 2.5 per cent; (ii) United States copyright suits against AI developers more than doubled, from 46 to 101, between June 2025 and May 2026; (iii) the US$1.5 billion Bartz v. Anthropic settlement, at about US$3,100 per work, equals roughly 2 per cent of the statutory ceiling yet is four times the statutory minimum; (iv) harm to creators is concentrated in readily substitutable segments, with 36 per cent of surveyed translators and 26 per cent of illustrators reporting lost work; and (v) the leading global AI-ethics guidelines, although convergent on transparency (73 of 84 documents), do not treat creator consent or remuneration as a distinct principle. Comparative analysis of seven jurisdictions reveals divergent judicial answers to the same ethical question, most recently illustrated by the Delhi High Court's interim refusal in ANI v. OpenAI (24 July 2026) and the Munich Regional Court's contrary reasoning in GEMA v. OpenAI (11 November 2025). The article concludes by proposing a layered governance model that combines training-data transparency, statutory remuneration with collective management, calibrated human-contribution thresholds for authorship, and shared accountability for outputs, with specific attention to the equity interests of emerging economies.
