db8d68d7e357fe011d20da94380d8d01ed24566b.abstract: FAIR principles make scientific data more reusable. But who pays for the work, maintains the infrastructure, and sustains the people who make reuse possible? The FAIR principles (Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, and Reusable) have shaped how researchers think about data stewardship. Yet data does not become reusable simply because it is deposited in a repository. It must be documented, cleaned, standardised, and maintained.

title: Generative AI in Software Engineering Education: A Study on Competency and Perception
container-title: Jurnal Sistem Informasi
8c187fd3aecb19ad3d0caa47b5a2ab2b15c81b6f.abstract: Software Engineering (SE) education struggles to align graduate competencies with industry needs, a challenge compounded by Generative AI (GenAI). This study’s purpose is to explore how structured GenAI utilization can enhance student competencies and learning perceptions. This exploratory case study used a mixed-method design involving four students in a controlled experiment. Data was collected via quantitative (SWEBOK-based artifact assessments, questionnaires) and qualitative narrative reflections. Results show the group using AI produced higher-quality artifacts and reported a more efficient, positive experience. A key finding is the transformation of work processes, shifting the primary challenge from manual execution to the critical evaluation of AI outputs. Due to its small scale, the findings are preliminary but suggest GenAI can enhance competencies. This requires an educational shift toward human-AI collaboration skills like critical evaluation and prompt engineering. Further validation with larger, more comprehensive studies is essential to generalize these initial insights.

title: Cognitive Engagement as a Key Mechanism of Cognitive Sustainability in the Age of Generative AI: An Interdisciplinary Framework
container-title: Applied Sciences
213defa629d7a7d5fddd05f2c3b388e73859993a.abstract: Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) systems can improve productivity, yet their long-term implications for human cognition remain contested. This article develops an interdisciplinary framework for explaining how different patterns in the distribution and support of cognitive operations between humans and GenAI may shape cognitive engagement and cognitive outcomes over time. The framework draws upon a Neuro-Information-Systems (NeuroIS)-informed approach by integrating cognitive, behavioral, self-report, and neurophysiological perspectives into a multilevel account of how GenAI use shapes human cognition. We argue that cognitive engagement—the depth, persistence, and strategic quality of human processing during AI-supported tasks—is a proposed central mechanism linking the distribution and support of cognitive operations between humans and GenAI to cognitive outcomes. Direct effects on outcomes may coexist with engagement-mediated effects on outcomes. The cognitive consequences depend particularly on whether cognitively consequential operations related to understanding, learning, critical evaluation, and independent judgment continue to involve meaningful human engagement. Specifically, the framework integrates five elements: (1) antecedent conditions (user, task, and GenAI/system characteristics); (2) regulatory processes (metacognition, trust calibration, and motivational/goal regulation); (3) human–AI cognitive work configuration and cognitive engagement (i.e., how cognitive operations are distributed between the user and the AI system and how cognitively engaged the user remains); (4) short- and intermediate-term outcomes (performance, understanding, retention, and agency); and (5) long-term outcomes of cognitive sustainability and cognitive dependence. The article derives design principles for engagement-preserving AI and contributes to an interdisciplinary research agenda for examining these relationships through convergent behavioral, self-report, neurophysiological, and longitudinal evidence.

title: A SIRS-Type Dynamical Model for Generative-AI Data Pollution with Synthetic Seeding and Real-Data Preservation
container-title: Applied System Innovation
a9361b4beffb85396bed9b90944a8cf343b0b265.abstract: Generative-AI systems are increasingly trained on datasets containing AI-generated content, creating recursive feedback that may cause progressive losses of tail mass, diversity, and effective variance in learned distributions–a phenomenon commonly associated with model collapse. Existing analyses are primarily empirical or based on discrete-generation mixture models, motivating the development of a continuous-time dynamical framework. We develop a SIRS-type compartmental model, in which a normalized training-data pool is divided into clean, AI-polluted, and flagged/recovered fractions, with synthetic seeding (σ) and real-data preservation (ρ). We establish well-posedness, positivity, boundedness, and positive invariance; derive the equilibria and an explicit contamination threshold governing the clean equilibrium in the unseeded system; and analyze local stability and global convergence using planar dynamical-systems methods. Numerical simulations and parameter sweeps illustrate the resulting dynamics. In addition, a proof-of-concept fit of the reduced contamination–seeding subsystem to independently reported web-content prevalence data reproduces the observed post-2022 growth trend (R2=0.977). Contamination (β) and synthetic seeding (σ) increase equilibrium pollution, whereas detection (γ) and real-data preservation (ρ) reduce it. Within the parameter ranges investigated, increasing the cleaning rate (α) can indirectly increase equilibrium pollution by returning more data to the clean compartment, where it is again exposed to contamination. These results identify continuous real-data preservation and effective detection as key mechanisms for limiting synthetic-data pollution in generative-AI training ecosystems.

title: Behavioral and Neural Measures of Auditory Distraction Are Not Associated with Tinnitus Severity
container-title: Brain Sciences
45fb63df91697aaa88e59656378653af115103d6.abstract: Background/Objectives: Individuals with chronic tinnitus perceive a phantom sound that imposes either a bothersome and irrepressible distraction throughout waking hours or a relatively mild nuisance that often fades into subliminal awareness. The difference in tinnitus salience may reflect a general difference in inhibitory control over any distracting sound, whether externally or internally generated. In this exploratory study, we tested whether tinnitus burden, assessed using the Tinnitus Handicap Inventory (THI), was associated with behavioral and neural responses to external auditory distraction. Methods: Thirty adults with chronic tinnitus completed behavioral and electroencephalographic (EEG) testing. Participants with lower and higher THI scores were similar in age and hearing thresholds. Data from twenty-three neurotypical adults provided an additional reference cohort. Participants classified sequences of amplitude-modulated tones as random or repeating during behavioral testing or combined behavioral and EEG recording sessions. Competing noise or melodic distractors imposed lower and higher levels of distraction, respectively. Results: Melodic distractors reduced response accuracy more than noise distractors, with comparable effects in the lower- and higher-THI groups. Neural synchronization to changes in the target sequence also decreased more with melodic distractors, but this effect did not differ between groups. Other measures of synchronization to target and distractor features showed no significant group differences. Conclusions: Behavioral and neural measures were sensitive to external auditory distraction but did not distinguish participants with lower and higher tinnitus burden. These findings do not support a general deficit in suppressing external auditory distractors as an explanation for greater tinnitus burden under the conditions tested.

title: The Hidden Psychological Cost of Educational AI: Associations Between AI Involvement, Teachers’ Pride, and Meaningfulness at Work
container-title: Behavioral Sciences
7f74963f7875d989bebd75000054e0c08467fd5e.abstract: The proliferation of generative AI tools in educational settings raises a fundamental but underexplored question: does delegating creative teaching tasks to AI erode the psychological rewards that make teaching meaningful? In the current research, we advance a dual-level framework distinguishing the immediate emotional costs of AI involvement at the task level from its broader costs at the career level. We tested this framework across two complementary studies. Study 1 was a randomized experiment (N = 101 high school teachers) where participants either designed a classroom activity independently or revised an AI-generated draft. Teachers who revised the AI-generated draft reported lower psychological ownership of the product, which partially accounted for their lower state pride; this indirect effect was stronger among teachers with stronger callings. Study 2 was a two-wave time-lagged field survey (N = 231 university teachers) examining habitual AI involvement and career calling at Time 1 and psychological ownership and work meaningfulness one month later. AI involvement was indirectly associated with lower work meaningfulness through lower psychological ownership, with the indirect effect stronger among teachers with stronger callings. Together, the two studies provide experimental (Study 1) and time-lagged correlational (Study 2) evidence that AI involvement is associated with lower psychological ownership, which in turn is linked to lower pride in a specific task and lower meaningfulness of work as a whole. These associations were stronger among teachers with stronger callings, suggesting an ironic vulnerability that warrants attention in educational AI policy, teacher professional development, and AI system design.

title: Employee–AI Collaboration and Work Well-Being: The Roles of AI-Related Perceived Organizational Support, Workload, and Leader AI Symbolization
container-title: Behavioral Sciences
57f2b53b6ef012fc6741a056c3caff1ffd2ea813.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly embedded in organizational work, yet its implications for employee work well-being remain unclear. Integrating Job Demands–Resources (JD–R) theory with organizational support theory, cognitive appraisal theory, and social information processing theory, this study used a two-wave, single-source questionnaire design to examine two pathways linking employee–AI collaboration to work well-being and the moderating role of leader AI symbolization (LAIS). Data from 335 employees in China showed a positive total association between employee–AI collaboration and work well-being. Employee–AI collaboration was positively associated with both AI-related perceived organizational support (AI-related POS) and workload: AI-related POS carried a positive indirect effect, whereas workload carried a negative indirect effect. Because these pathways operated in opposite directions, their summed indirect effect was not statistically significant. LAIS strengthened the AI-related POS pathway and attenuated the workload pathway. Simultaneous path analysis and bootstrap robustness tests yielded the same pattern. These findings characterize employee–AI collaboration as a work arrangement that may be appraised through both resource-gain and demand-related pathways; the two-wave design does not establish causal ordering.

title: AI Literacy and Innovative Behavior in AI-Assisted Learning: Cognitive and Affective Trust in AI and Creative Self-Efficacy as Sequential Pathways
container-title: Behavioral Sciences
7a1575dc6e48a5d7d18de55d9f384ea3155029aa.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GAI) is increasingly embedded in higher education, yet how AI literacy relates to AI-assisted innovative behavior in learning (IBL) remains unclear. This cross-sectional study examined whether cognitive and affective trust in AI, together with creative self-efficacy (CSE), sequentially linked AI literacy to IBL. A sample of 1173 Chinese college students completed an online survey; gender, age, and AI use frequency were controlled. AI literacy was associated with IBL in total (β = 0.211, 95% CI [0.155, 0.267]), but the direct association was no longer significant once the mediators were included (β = 0.057, p = 0.056); the total indirect effect accounted for 73.2% of the total association. When both trust dimensions were modeled simultaneously, all seven specific indirect pathways were significant. The pathway through cognitive trust (0.093) exceeded that through affective trust (0.057; Δ = 0.036). Re-estimation under a symmetric covariate specification confirmed a modest antecedent asymmetry (Δ = 0.086), whereas the two trust dimensions did not differ reliably downstream. Cognitive trust thus appears to be the more readily mobilized gateway to IBL, whereas affective trust may require relationally supportive design. Single-wave self-reports preclude causal inference.

title: Declared, Not Detected: A Blockchain-Anchored, Agentic Framework for Academic Integrity in the Generative AI Era
container-title: Information
bde050b22ae6aa1dab8684cb1f49a8e806797ea5.abstract: Integrity enforcement in higher education increasingly rests on detectors of machine-written text, yet these detectors are defeated by paraphrase and trivial edits and disproportionately misclassify students who write in English as an additional language. This article proposes SCRIBE, a framework in which the reportable offence is a declaration that misdescribes how the work was produced. Students declare an assistance level and attest to their own authorship, while an instrumented editor commits process digests to a permissioned ledger. Seven smart contracts bind these commitments to the governing policy and encode a due-process procedure that no software agent can complete; four agents prepare each case, a human panel decides it, and abstention is always available. We evaluate the framework as a mechanism-verification exercise on 60,000 synthetic submissions whose behaviour classes, generator parameters and oral-probe response rates are stated assumptions, so the figures below describe that specified model rather than expected real-world performance. Within a false accusation budget of 0.5%, SCRIBE refers 30.6% of misdeclarations at 97.1% precision, wrongly referring 73 of 22,131 truthful submissions, whereas a simulated detector refers 0.3% at the same budget. Recall ranges from 5.0% to 52.3% across plausible oral-probe parameters. Process evidence alone cannot exceed a posterior of 0.604, and a replayed writing trace cuts referral to 7.2%. For a single institution, a witnessed append-only log provides four of the six procedural guarantees; the ledger’s distinctive value lies in multi-institution settings where no party is trusted to operate the log.

d3c3cd8fcf8d9e3bcfd02b26384ddf1ce5d7bbe9.abstract: General education-a critical arena for cultivating interdisciplinary and innovative talents in higher education-faces structural dilemmas such as outdated content, undiversified pathways, and disconnection from industry demands. Taking tourism colleges as the empirical setting, this study draws on the theories of competency-based education (CBE) and outcome-based education (OBE) to explore educational pathways for AI-empowered general education courses. A three-tier progressive competency map spanning cognition, application, and creation was constructed; a modular curriculum system driven by the dual engines of OBE and project-based learning (PBL) was designed; and a spiral action research mechanism was introduced for empirical validation in teaching practice. Empirical results demonstrate that the proposed pathway effectively addresses such challenges as the lack of vehicles for cultivating AI literacy among non-computer-science students and the mismatch between curriculum provision and industry demands, thereby achieving a value leap of general education from "inward talent cultivation" to "outward empowerment." The closed-loop paradigm of "demand insight–curriculum reconstruction–practical validation–outcome transformation" proposed in this study offers a replicable model for the digital-intelligent reform of general education in application-oriented universities.

title: Influence of dominant sequence artifacts on generative AI for virtual contrast-enhancement in breast MRI
container-title: BMC Medical Imaging
e0cef0cf5be77f4dda6ed7f2bbd19c44a70f8179.abstract: Abstract Background Virtual contrast-enhanced (vCE) breast MRI is a deep learning approach for generating contrast-like images from non-contrast acquisitions. As diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) has emerged as a major contributor to enhancement synthesis, understanding the influence of DWI-related image artifacts is important for the robustness and potential clinical implementation of AI-based contrast-free imaging approaches. We evaluated the robustness of a pix2pix-based vCE synthesis model to artifact-contaminated DWI during training and inference. Materials and methods This IRB-approved, retrospective study included 1,974 multiparametric breast MRI examinations (mean age: 49 years) acquired with two clinical routine 3T MRI scanners (2017–2022). High b-value (b = 1500 s/mm 2 ) DWI images were automatically classified for high-intensity (HI) and low-intensity (LI) artifacts using a pretrained neural network. A pix2pix 2D-GAN was trained either after excluding artifact-affected slices (vCE-clean) or using all available slices (vCE-all). Performance was evaluated using image similarity metrics, lesion-based analysis, reader assessment, and correlation of artifact scores with reconstruction errors. Results Excluding artifact-affected slices during training resulted in a small but statistically significant increase in whole-image structural similarity index (SSIM) with small effect size ( vCE-all 0.843 ± 0.034; vCE-clean 0.849 ± 0.031, p < 0.001, d av = 0.20). However, lesion-based metrics and qualitative ratings of lesion enhancement and image quality were comparable between models. During Inference, strong LI DWI artifacts were associated with higher lesion-based errors. Conclusion Controlling for artifacts on diffusion weighted imaging (DWI) during vCE training only minorly influenced technical metrics but not perceived image quality/lesion enhancement. In contrast, severe signal-loss artifacts during inference impaired local performance, highlighting the importance of image quality control during potential deployment.

title: Green AI-Driven Synthetic Data Generation for Improved Industrial Metal Surface Defect Detection
container-title: INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF COMPUTERS  COMMUNICATIONS & CONTROL
a0f8723b760555cb36c36065854e75622e1ff570.abstract: Defect detection of industrial metal surfaces is often limited by the scarcity of annotated data and the high cost of manual labeling, which limits the performance of data-driven inspection systems. This paper presents a Green AI-driven framework for synthetic data generation that efficiently augments industrial defect datasets while minimizing computational and annotation costs. The proposed approach employs a deterministic procedural pipeline to generate synthetic defect images together with aligned segmentation masks at the pixel-level, providing accurate supervision without the computational overhead of deep generative models. The framework is evaluated on the Kolektor Surface-Defect Dataset 2 (KSDD2), which is extended into a hybrid dataset through synthetic augmentation followed by human-in-the-loop validation, to ensure the realism and reliability of the generated samples and annotations. A lightweight state-of-the-art anomaly detection model, SuperSimpleNet, is trained under controlled ablation settings on both the original and hybrid datasets using identical test splits for fair comparison. Performance is evaluated using both image-level and pixel-level metrics, including AUROC and average precision. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed hybrid dataset consistently improves defect detection and localization performance while substantially reducing the need for costly data acquisition and manual annotation. Unlike computationally intensive generative approaches based on GANs or diffusion models, the proposed procedural framework synthesizes defects directly within predefined regions, enabling automatic generation of pixel-accurate ground-truth annotations without human intervention. The resulting hybrid dataset improves all evaluation metrics, achieving the largest gain in anomaly localization performance, with AP-loc increasing by 5.3%, while image-level AUROC increases from 0.9840 to 0.9907. By combining efficient synthetic data generation with precise automatic annotation, the proposed approach provides a resource-efficient solution that aligns with Green AI principles.

title: Application of Fourth-Order Cybernetics in Digital Twin-Enabled Adaptive Systems of Systems Operating in High-Stakes Environments

41a036c7fbbda972f124e6931af287df58c0e266.abstract: Modern systems of systems (SoS) operating in high-stakes environments like Distributed Operational System (DOS) are characterized by tightly coupled interactions among human operators, autonomous agents, and heterogeneous technological subsystems. Conventional reliability engineering approaches, which primarily focus on component level failure probabilities and static models are often insufficient for capturing emergent behaviors and nonlinear failure propagation across interconnected sociotechnical systems. This study proposes a cybernetically informed framework that integrates digital twin technology, the Viable System Model (VSM) and an extended Failure Modes and Effects Criticality Analysis (FMECA) methodology to reconceptualise reliability as a dynamic and emergent system property. Digital twins function as continuously updated virtual representations that synchronise real time data, simulation models, and predictive analytics, enabling recursive observation and anticipatory regulation. Their integration with FMECA supports scenario based reliability analysis, allowing the modelling of cascading failures, coordination disruptions and adaptive system responses. The findings demonstrate that reliability emerges from system interactions rather than isolated components, advancing the design of adaptive, resilient, and self-regulating systems operating in complex and uncertain environments. Although applicable to systems of systems related contexts, the framework is intentionally generalised to support broader applications across critical infrastructure, healthcare coordination systems, industrial automation, autonomous transportation, emergency response networks and distributed cyber physical systems. Simulation experiments across distributed systems of systems networks demonstrate how local disturbances propagate through interconnected nodes and are mitigated through cybernetic feedback mechanisms. Simulation experiments across distributed systems of systems networks and demonstrate how local disturbances propagate through interconnected nodes and are mitigated through cybernetic feedback mechanisms. Monte Carlo analysis (n = 1000) indicates high robustness, with operational effectiveness (ζ = 0.929 ± 0.021) and system availability (A = 0.98 ± 0.015). Monte Carlo analysis indicates high robustness, with strong operational continuity and system availability across varying disruption scenarios.

title: AI-Driven Performance Optimization of NB-IoT for Real-Time Industrial Monitoring in Industry 4.0: A Critical Review
container-title: Journal of Future Artificial Intelligence and Technologies
6a0d77e656e2b24d5c928bf6ef6b11169d360848.abstract: Narrowband Internet of Things (NB-IoT) is an important cellular low-power wide-area network (LPWAN) technology for industrial sensing, offering wide-area coverage, licensed-spectrum operation, low device complexity, and long battery life. However, real-time industrial monitoring requires simultaneous consideration of latency, reliability, coverage, energy efficiency, security, and scalability. Although artificial intelligence (AI) has been proposed to adapt NB-IoT operation to changing channel and traffic conditions, the practical benefits and limitations of these approaches remain insufficiently consolidated. This paper presents a critical, PRISMA-inspired review of AI-driven NB-IoT performance optimization for industrial monitoring in Industry 4.0. Following the screening of literature from IEEE Xplore, SpringerLink, ScienceDirect, MDPI, ACM, Wiley, Scopus, and relevant 3GPP documents, 43 sources were retained and classified as core AI-driven NB-IoT studies, non-AI comparator studies, or supporting literature. The review maps AI paradigms to six performance objectives and examines their potential deployment across device, edge, and cloud layers. The synthesis reveals three key insights. First, direct evidence remains limited, with core studies relying predominantly on reinforcement-learning-related methods and simulation-based evaluation. Second, the available evidence does not establish a single AI paradigm as suitable for the entire monitoring pipeline; a layered combination of device-level TinyML, edge-level prediction and constrained control, and cloud-level training represents a promising direction, although end-to-end validation remains lacking. Third, AI overhead—including training, inference, model updates, memory, energy, and communication costs—must be evaluated alongside network performance because it may offset optimization gains. The review links six research gaps to seven future research directions and identifies reproducible testbeds, open datasets, overhead-aware multi-KPI benchmarking, and safe, explainable control as priorities for credible industrial deployment.

title: Decentralized Finance and Digital Assets: A New Perspective on Financial Management and Risk
container-title: Lex localis - Journal of Local Self-Government
13b14090a5c64d7c3224b43ae85f72408e707dbf.abstract: <jats:p>Financial services are being transformed, how they are designed, accessed, and managed, by the rise of decentralized finance (DeFi) and digital assets. These innovations via blockchain networks, smart contracts, and tokenization offer alternatives to existing models for payments, lending, investment, and asset exchange. But the economic, institutional and operating risks of financial intermediation are not eroded when transactions are automated. In this conceptual study, the impact of DeFi and digital assets on financial management is explored, including capital allocation, treasury operations, risk management, and the governance of digital assets. It assesses what could be gained from this technology, alongside its potential technological vulnerabilities, market instability, regulatory uncertainty and inability to provide meaningful financial inclusion. An analysis approach is built to present a managerial perspective, which considers digital financial arrangements from an economic function, dependency and accountability standpoint. It points out that sustainable adoption requires coordination of technology with financial management, strong rights, organizational efficiency and appropriate governance. DeFi is therefore a reorganization of financial management and not the automatic replacement of existing financial institutions.</jats:p>

title: Expectation-driven gain modulation of preparatory spatial attention
container-title: eLife
42e0bff514a13e990dde6d5376170bcb87804ae4.abstract: <jats:p>The visual system can flexibly adjust attentional deployment to match task demands, but whether observers can proactively modulate the spatial scope of attention based on expectations about upcoming search difficulty remains unclear. According to the zoom lens model, attention can narrow or broaden its spatial extent, with narrower focus enhancing processing efficiency, a mechanism that would benefit target discrimination in crowded displays. We tested whether observers adjust attentional scope when expecting sparse versus dense search arrays by combining spatial cueing with block-wise manipulations of display density expectations. Participants performed a visual search task in which endogenous cues predicted target location, while blocks predominantly contained either sparse (1 target, 3 distractors) or dense (1 target, 7 distractors) displays. We applied inverted encoding models to broadband EEG data to reconstruct spatial channel tuning functions, enabling precise characterization of both the locus and breadth of attentional deployment. Behaviorally, expecting difficult searches selectively improved accuracy at cued locations without costs elsewhere. Consistent with this selective benefit, neural measurements revealed that expectancy enhanced the amplitude of spatially selective responses at the attended location but did not alter tuning width. These findings demonstrate that expectations about search difficulty modulate attention through gain-based signal enhancement rather than adjustments to spatial scope, revealing that preparatory attentional control operates via amplitude modulation within a stable spatial focus. This mechanism complements reactive attentional adjustments and provides an efficient means for the visual system to optimize processing under predictable task demands.</jats:p>
