title: Enhancing the accessibility of population-based cancer screening: insights from co-creation on a screening portal and a combined screening programme
container-title: Frontiers in Digital Health
a43a2500d29e7dba760ebc778702335f6ae2eaa9.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Introduction</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Population-based cancer screening programmes facilitate early cancer detection, thereby contributing to reduced cancer-related morbidity and mortality. However, participation rates have declined in recent years, with lower uptake particularly evident among invitees in vulnerable positions. This decline can be partly attributed to information that is insufficiently tailored to individual needs and literacy levels, and to the fragmented nature of the screening offer. To address these barriers, this study explored two strategies: (1) developing a personalised screening portal presenting information in an accessible and tailored manner, and (2) improving the alignment and potential integration of screening programmes.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Four co-creation sessions were conducted with 13 screening invitees and eight experts in cancer screening and human factors engineering. Two sessions focused on prototyping a screening portal and two explored the potential for combined screening. Sessions were audio-recorded, transcribed verbatim, and analysed thematically using inductive coding.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Invitees and experts emphasised the need for a digital portal offering concise, empathetic, personalised, and phase-specific information. Invitees perceived added value in combined screening, whereas experts considered organising all screenings at a single location and time to be infeasible in the current context. Both groups agreed that integrating information provision across programmes would be valuable and feasible.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Discussion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>These findings suggest that integrating information across screening programmes is a meaningful and achievable step towards improving accessibility and supporting informed decision-making, particularly for invitees in vulnerable positions.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Exploring clinician preferences for visualizing wearable health data: insights from UK anesthesiologists and Mexican general practitioners
container-title: Frontiers in Digital Health
bb08ca27eb503044fb6ad8b6b695a2b52c877c4f.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Wearable Health Monitoring Systems (WHMS) have the potential to transform clinical decision-making by providing real-time physiological, behavioral, and environmental data. However, the complexity and volume of these multi-source, multi-variable datasets present challenges for clinical interpretation.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Objective</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study examined clinicians' perspectives on how multi-source wearable health data could be summarized and visualized to support clinical interpretation, drawing on the views of anesthesiologists in an acute-care setting and general practitioners involved in primary care.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>A custom WHMS prototype, PatientSense, was used to collect data from participants over multiple days and nights. We developed and presented scatterplots, histograms, heatmaps, and icon-based behavioral summaries derived from the prototype developed and evaluated them through one-on-one semi-structured interviews with four anesthesiologists in the UK and focus groups with twenty-three general practitioners (GPs) in Mexico.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Clinicians expressed a preference for a hierarchical visualization strategy that begins with summarized trends and supports drill-down into finer temporal detail. Preferences for granularity differed between the two clinician groups: anesthesiologists favored higher-frequency views for interpreting rapid physiological changes, whereas GPs preferred broader summaries for longitudinal monitoring. Clinicians also highlighted the need for validation across diverse populations and clinical settings.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Clinician feedback indicated that context-aware, adaptable visualization approaches were perceived as useful for interpreting multimodal wearable health data. Integrating behavioral and physiological signals and providing flexible temporal granularity were identified as important design requirements for supporting clinical interpretation. Further evaluation in real clinical settings is required to determine their effects on clinical decision-making and patient care.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Martabat Manusia di Era Digital: Interpretasi Ajaran Sosial Gereja terhadap Dampak Kecerdasan Buatan dalam Pendidikan
container-title: Sinar Kasih: Jurnal Pendidikan Agama dan Filsafat
0127a312751901f8a5b9e567a73d31da484fe7b0.abstract: <jats:p>Artificial Intelligence (AI) has transformed the educational landscape through personalized learning, automated assessment, and expanded access to information; however, it has simultaneously raised ethical issues such as cognitive dependency, the erosion of academic integrity, algorithmic bias, digital attachment, and the weakening of pedagogical relationships. This study aims to analyze the impact of AI on human dignity in education and to outline the direction of its application based on the perspective of Catholic Social Teaching. A qualitative library research method was employed, utilizing content analysis and a critical-hermeneutic approach to examine documents from the Catholic Church's Magisterium and reputable scholarly journals. The findings indicate that the application of AI risks reducing learners to mere computational data and eroding their moral autonomy. The principles of human dignity (Imago Dei), the common good (bonum commune), subsidiarity, solidarity, and social justice prove relevant as an interpretive framework for positioning AI as an instrumental tool that serves integral human development.</jats:p>

title: Digital assets structure and liquidity position of ICT firms in Nigeria
container-title: Radiant Journal of Business & Sustainability
21bb33f2530dadca299e60735710beb96365d8f4.abstract:
<jats:p>This study examined the effect of digital asset structure on the liquidity position of listed ICT firms in Nigeria. Specifically, it investigated the effects of digital infrastructure assets and digital human capital on firm liquidity. An ex-post facto research design was adopted. The population comprised nine ICT firms listed on the Nigerian Exchange, from which seven firms were purposively selected based on data availability and continuous reporting over 2016–2025, producing 70 firm-year observations. Secondary data were obtained from annual reports and Nigerian Exchange publications. Liquidity was measured using the current ratio, while digital infrastructure assets were measured by total investment in information technology infrastructure and digital human capital by the number of IT-certified staff. Descriptive statistics, Spearman correlation and panel regression were employed. The Hausman test supported the random-effects specification. The random-effects estimates show that digital infrastructure assets have a positive and statistically significant association with liquidity (β = 0.5095, p = 0.0003), while digital human capital also has a positive and statistically significant association with liquidity (β = 0.6002, p = 0.0122). The model explains approximately 71.2% of the variation in liquidity (R² = 0.7116). The findings suggest that investments in digital infrastructure and digitally skilled human capital are associated with stronger liquidity positions among the sampled Nigerian ICT firms. The study contributes firm-level evidence from a relatively under-researched non-financial ICT sector in Nigeria.
Keywords: Digital Assets Structure, Digital Infrastructure Assets, Digital Human Capital, Liquidity, ICT Firms, Nigeria.</jats:p>

title: Beyond technological mandates: Innovation capacity, bureaucratic resistance, and digital governance transformation in local communities
container-title: Sustainable Social Development
b16086da3558230a1aaf18dd7358df6ede7f3d0d.abstract: <jats:p><p>Digital governance can improve public service delivery, but meaningful transformation requires more than adopting new technologies. This study examines how local government innovation capacity shapes organizational adaptation and public service change in Makassar City, Indonesia. Using an exploratory qualitative case-study design, the study draws on in-depth interviews, field observations, and document analysis across regional apparatus organizations. The findings show a persistent gap between digital policy ambitions and the institutional readiness required for implementation. Dedicated coordination units have strengthened data governance, yet fragmented information systems, uneven frontline digital competencies, hierarchical routines, and weak cross-agency integration continue to constrain reform. Frontline reluctance to use new systems is interpreted not as simple opposition to technology, but as an adaptive response to fragmented procedures, limited training, and increased administrative workload. The analysis shows that durable digital reform depends on adaptive leadership, cross-unit integration, workforce development, and institutional arrangements that can survive political and organizational change. To reduce the risk of widening the digital divide, local governments should shift from fragmented, project-based initiatives to inclusive institutional capabilities that align technology with service needs and public value.</p></jats:p>

DARA-PROBA3 features three cavities that perform TotalSolar Irradiance (TSI) measurements based on their component-level calibra-tion. First light was established on 25 February 2025, the three cavities record-ing 1362.15, 1362.02 and 1361.97 W m−2 at their respective first-measurementepochs. Averaged over their individual observation windows, DARA-PROBA3gives a mean TSI of 1361.96 ± 0.09 W m−2 across the three cavities, in agreementwith the value recorded by the VIRGO/PMO6 radiometer over the same interval(i.e. 1361.94 W m−2). title: Attractor computation in continuous-time digital networks
cdf969649460c02767dba9e2d877094db8262c3f.abstract: Attractor dynamics underlie the collective computation of neural networks. Recurrent connections between biological neurons can give rise to stable states towards which network activity relaxes, allowing parallel operation without global coordination while preserving robustness. Implementing physical systems with reliable attractor dynamics is therefore important both for understanding biological intelligence and for developing bio-inspired computing systems. However, parallel physical evolution introduces dynamical challenges. Concurrent evolution of artificial neurons can support rapid collective relaxation, but can also prevent the network from settling. Here, we realise a continuous-time digital Hopfield neural network (CTD-HNN) that combines digitally programmable energy landscapes with state evolution in physical time. Across ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic Ising models, associative memory tasks, and Max-Cut problems up to 1,000 vertices, we show that this system can be tuned to exhibit stable relaxation, persistent instability, or transient exploration of state space before convergence. By regulating feedback, activation and propagation delays, we control the intrinsic instability as a dynamical degree of freedom, thereby balancing exploration and convergence while preserving the task-defining interactions. This work combines the configurability and precision of digital hardware with continuous-time dynamics, establishing a programmable framework for attractor computation in which energy landscapes are digitally defined but physically explored.

title: Modern Approaches to Teaching Mathematics to Primary School Students in a Digital Learning Environment
container-title: The Journal of Interdisciplinary Human Studies
f950b8456239fcd2bbafb9d86e9e963c91e97c7f.abstract: <jats:p>This article examines modern approaches to teaching mathematics to primary school students in a digital learning environment, focusing on interdisciplinary integration. The study uses theoretical analysis, comparative analysis, and generalization of pedagogical literature to explore how digital resources can support mathematics instruction. The analysis suggests that interactive exercises, electronic textbooks, visual materials, and educational software offer opportunities to explain mathematical concepts, support independent practice, and provide feedback. Connecting mathematics with language, natural sciences, technology, and everyday situations may help students apply mathematical knowledge in practical contexts. Effective implementation requires teachers to align digital resources with lesson objectives, students’ developmental characteristics, and available technical facilities. The article concludes that combining digital tools with integrated teaching offers pedagogical opportunities for primary mathematics education, while empirical research is needed to assess its effects on students’ learning outcomes.</jats:p>

Determinants of Digital Marketing Adoption and MSME Performance in Indonesia’s Halal Food Sector
container-title: F1000Research
05a61f31587fb12ccd3bfa05e07791516e024196.abstract: <ns3:p>Background Digital transformation is a key driver of Indonesia’s economy, contributing an estimated USD 130 billion by 2025. Halal MSMEs in the food and beverage sector contribute approximately USD 180 billion annually, account for 60% of GDP, and employ nearly 97% of the workforce. However, digital marketing adoption remains constrained by digital literacy, infrastructure, financial, and sharia-related challenges. This study examines the determinants of digital marketing adoption and its impact on halal MSME performance. Methods This study employed an explanatory quantitative research design based on the Technology–Organization–Environment–Personal (TOEP) framework. Data were collected from 500 halal-certified MSMEs operating in the food and beverage sector across Indonesia using a structured questionnaire. Structural Equation Modeling–Partial Least Squares (SEM-PLS) with SmartPLS 4.0 was used to evaluate the relationships among technological, organizational, environmental, and personal factors, digital marketing adoption, and business performance. Results The findings indicate that technological, organizational, environmental, and personal factors significantly influence digital marketing adoption among halal MSMEs. All four dimensions showed positive and statistically significant relationships with adoption; however, complexity had a positive coefficient (β = 0.128, p = 0.010), contrary to the negative relationship hypothesized in H3. Furthermore, digital marketing adoption has a positive and significant effect on business performance by improving operational efficiency, increasing customer loyalty, strengthening halal brand visibility, and enhancing overall business competitiveness. Conclusions Digital marketing adoption is a key strategic driver for improving the competitiveness and sustainability of halal MSMEs in Indonesia. Strengthening digital capabilities through technological readiness, organizational support, favorable business environments, and personal competencies is essential to accelerate digital transformation and maximize the contribution of halal MSMEs to the national digital economy. The findings also highlight the importance of examining personal factors alongside technological, organizational, and environmental conditions when understanding digital marketing adoption among halal MSMEs.</ns3:p>

title: Digital Visual Learning Materials and Their Impact on Students' English Language Skills: A Guided Inquiry Approach
container-title: Architecture  Image Studies
f8551196af88780426ad7f681ba5db231968978e.abstract: <jats:p>This study investigates the effect of the Guided Inquiry model assisted by Digital Student Worksheets (LKPD) on eleventh-grade students' English language skills, specifically writing creativity, reading comprehension, speaking proficiency, and learning independence. Employing a quasi-experimental design with a Nonequivalent Control Group, the study involved 187 students from SMA Negeri 1 Woha, Bima, West Nusa Tenggara, selected through proportional random sampling and assigned to either an experimental group (Digital LKPD-supported Guided Inquiry) or a control group (conventional instruction). Pre- and post-tests were administered across all four outcome variables, and data were analyzed using Multivariate Analysis of Covariance (MANCOVA) and N-Gain tests. Results demonstrated statistically significant improvements in the experimental group across all four variables: writing creativity (t = 3.542; p = 0.001), reading comprehension (t = 3.215; p = 0.002), speaking skills (t = 3.611; p = 0.001), and learning independence (t = 3.214; p = 0.002). The MANCOVA revealed a simultaneous significant effect of the instructional model on all dependent variables (Pillai's Trace = 0.913; p < 0.001). N-Gain scores indicated moderate-to-high improvement in the experimental group (M = 0.65) compared to the control group (M = 0.35). These findings suggest that integrating digital visual learning materials within a Guided Inquiry framework functions not merely as a content delivery mechanism, but as a strategic instructional design component that promotes self-regulated learning, cognitive engagement, and holistic English language literacy development in 21st-century educational contexts.</jats:p>

title: QuickLeaf-LWA high-throughput software: automated digital image analysis for accurate measurement of leaf shape and size
container-title: Journal of Environmental Biology
e085f3c06cce32c4851f309e37554af7e94db74d.abstract:
<jats:p>Aim: Leaf size and shape are key character for assessing photosynthesis, growth, genetic diversity, and plant health. Manual measurement is labor-intensive, time-consuming, and error-prone, particularly in large-scale phenotyping studies. This study aimed to develop QuickLeaf-LWA, a software tool for rapid, precise, and automated estimation of leaf size (length and width) and shape (aspect ratio) from digital images.

Methodology: QuickLeaf-LWA integrates high-throughput automation (HTA) with comprehensive trait management and morphological analysis workflows. The software employs a robust image-processing pipeline using adaptive threshold for accurate leaf segmentation from complex backgrounds, followed by morphological operations to reduce noise. Leaf dimensions and aspect ratio are calculated using a rectangular-bounded, radially rotated image approach.

Results: Accuracy assessment showed low mean error rates (0.584–3.283%) and high accuracy (96.717–99.416%). Root mean square error (RMSE) and mean absolute error (MAE) values were low (0.150–0.564 and 0.082–0.476, respectively), with strong correlations to manual measurements (R2 ≥ 0.96).

Interpretation: QuickLeaf-LWA enables rapid analysis of hundreds of leaves within minutes offers an intuitive interface with batch-processing capability, making it a practical tool for plant physiology, genetics, agriculture, horticulture, and leaf phenotyping research.

Key words: Aspect ratio, Digital image analysis, Leaf phenotyping, QuickLeaf-(LWA)</jats:p>

title: Digital Technology Use, Cognitive Engagement and Perceived Learning Effectiveness Among Adult Learners in Non-Formal Education in Uzbekistan
8ceeae83917828c5b1e08cdb8fa3ca811cbe8ee6.abstract: Although digital technologies are increasingly embedded in adult education policy, evidence from post-Soviet Central Asia remains scarce. This sequential explanatory mixed-methods study examined how digital technology use relates to two proximal indicators of learning processes – cognitive engagement and perceived learning effectiveness – among adults in non-formal education programmes in Uzbekistan. Survey data from 312 learners nested in 26 programmes across three provinces were analysed with two-level random-intercept models, followed by semi-structured interviews with 22 learners and two facilitators, analysed through reflexive thematic analysis. After adjustment for age, gender, educational attainment, urban–rural location and programme type, digital technology use was positively associated with cognitive engagement (β = .38, 95% CI [.27, .49]) and perceived learning effectiveness (β = .35, 95% CI [.24, .46]). Between 17% and 18% of the variance in each outcome lay at the programme level. Four qualitative themes – socially produced digital self-efficacy, peer-mediated learning, institutional culture and structural barriers – helped to explain these patterns. Interpreted through self-directed learning theory and the capability approach, the findings suggest that the educational value of digital tools depends on the social and institutional conditions in which adults use them. The cross-sectional design and reliance on self-report preclude causal inference.

title: Early prediction of post-dialysis systolic and diastolic blood pressure using intradialytic data in Senegalese hemodialysis patients: a single-center retrospective cohort study
container-title: Frontiers in Digital Health
2a344cecaf92866f4c344d91c054506e2a92a09b.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Intradialytic blood pressure variability poses a major challenge in chronic hemodialysis, especially in resource-limited settings, contributing to cardiovascular complications and session interruptions. This study aimed to develop and evaluate supervised machine learning models to predict post-dialysis systolic blood pressure (SBP) and diastolic blood pressure (DBP) using only data available up to the third hour of the session.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>In this retrospective, single-center cohort study at Hôpital Militaire Ouakam (Dakar, Senegal; February 2023 to November 2024), we analyzed 7,600 hemodialysis sessions from 124 chronic patients after quality-based exclusions. Predictors included intradialytic hemodynamics, dialysis machine parameters, and demographic and contextual factors recorded up to hour 3, while end-of-session data were excluded to prevent leakage. Four models were retained after initial screening of six candidates (Ridge Regression, Random Forest, LightGBM, and XGBoost) and evaluated using patient-level 5-fold cross-validation, with mean absolute error across SBP and DBP as the primary performance metric.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Tree-based models outperformed linear and kernel-based methods, with the optimized Random Forest model achieving the best performance, with an MAE of 12.67 ± 0.80 mmHg for SBP and 8.93 ± 0.35 mmHg for DBP, a root mean square error of 14.68 ± 0.75 mmHg, and R² of 0.553 ± 0.033. Diastolic blood pressure predictions were more stable than systolic predictions, with no systematic bias observed in Bland-Altman analyses (bias = 0.015 mmHg for SBP and 0.395 mmHg for DBP). Subgroup performance showed moderate heterogeneity related to age, sex, and body mass index, with the best results observed in younger male patients.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>These findings demonstrate the feasibility of supervised machine learning for unbiased prediction of post-dialysis blood pressure in Senegalese chronic hemodialysis patients, supporting the potential development of proactive interventions during hemodialysis sessions. Prospective and multicenter studies are needed to validate and measure the clinical impact of artificial intelligence use in the management of dialysis patients in resource-limited settings.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: A Narrative Methodological Review of Discordance Between Statistical and Clinical Significance in Research on Digital Interventions for Adolescent Depression
c191d272099e0367162c2893d38bd819a00b9826.abstract: Background and Objective : Across trials of digital intervention for adolescent depression, statistically significant findings often coexist with only marginal clinical improvement whereas underpowered studies may fail to detect clinically meaningful benefits. This study aimed to apply the Multidimensional Clinical Interpretation Framework (MCIF), a seven-domain sequential framework for evaluate the clinical relevance of evidence from adolescent's Digital depression interventions trials. Methods : A narrative methodological review with conceptual framework development was conducted. PubMed, PsycINFO, Scopus and Web of science were searched from January 2005 to March 2026, with targeted citation tracking of key methodological publications. Two independent reviewers screened titles and abstracts, with disagreements resolved by consensus. Of 3,847 identified records, 42 studies met eligibility criteria. Results: Review of the 42 included trials showed that clinically meaningful outcomes were inconsistently reported with statistical significance frequently prioritized over interpretable effect magnitudes. To address these shortcomings, the Multidimensional Clinical Interpretation Framework (MCIF) was developed. It integrates seven interpretive domains (statistical outcome, effect size, measurement reliability, clinical meaningfulness, functional improvement, implementation feasibility, and reporting transparency) into a single sequential evaluative structure. The MCIF provides a practical and step-by-step approach to evaluating the real-world relevance of digital depression interventions for adolescents. Conclusion: reliance of statistical significance alone is insufficient for interpreting effectiveness. The MCIF is a tool that provides a structured, multidimensional approach to improve interpretation, strengthen reporting, and facilitate translation of research evidence into clinical practice.

title: Tectonic and A-Tectonic in Digital Documentation: A Model for Analyzing the Built Environment
container-title: Research into the Built Environment in Architectural Sciences
54dd1af850c749d9930377ab9f103911ad5c2d96.abstract: <jats:p>This study examines two distinct construction logics tectonic and a-tectonic that are superimposed within an architectural complex located around Nevşehir Castle in Cappadocia. The study addresses the a-tectonic spatial configuration of the subterranean troglodytic space formed by carving the existing rock mass into a void, as well as the tectonic configuration of the above-ground masonry structure. The research shows that three-dimensional documentation reveals the spatial continuity between the uper and lower levels a continuity that remains invisible in traditional two-dimensional representations by connecting these two spatial configurations. In this study, the tectonic aproaches of Bötticher, Semper, and Frampton are reevaluated in light of the a-tectonic conceptualization of troglodytic spaces. The case study focuses on an ancient structure at Nevşehir Castle that contains both underground and aboveground spaces. The study area is identified using point cloud analysis. By making the troglodytic layer visible, digital documentation also contributes to reassessing the cultural heritage value of the superstructure and the registration process. The study argues that digital documentation is not merely a record but a tool that generates architectural value.</jats:p>

<jats:p>This study aims to examine the role of financial inclusion as a mediating variable in the relationship between QRIS digital payments and MSME performance. A quantitative approach was adopted, involving 50 MSME owners in rural Central Java selected through purposive sampling. Data were collected using a 1–5 Likert scale questionnaire and analyzed using the Structural Equation Modeling-Partial Least Squares (SEM-PLS) method with SmartPLS software (version 4.1.1.8). This study enriches the literature on the digital transformation of rural MSMEs, an area that remains under-researched, while offering practical implications for business owners, digital payment service providers, and policymakers in designing strategies to strengthen financial inclusion and boost the performance of rural MSMEs.

ff0bfa74686305240986db51f7374ecbda57f4d4.abstract: <jats:p>This study aims to determine the priority of digital marketing strategies for Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) in Deli Serdang Regency using the Analytical Network Process (ANP). The study adopted a mixed-method design by intergrating qualitative and quantitative data collected through observations, interviews, and questionnaires involving 100 MSME owners selected using purposive sampling from five districts with the highest number of MSMEs implementing digital marketing. Data were analyzed using the ANP method with Super Decisions software to identify the key driving and inhibiting factors, analyze the interrelationships among the criteria, and establish the appropriate priority order for digital marketing strategies for MSMEs in Deli Serdang Regency. The findings indicate that target market is the most influential criterion (0.013613), followed by marketing cost (0.011748), customer satisfaction (0.011657), ease of platform use (0.009996), digital literacy and technology (0.009919), and response speed (0.009734). Furthermore, the analysis of alternative strategies shows that social media is the highest-priority digital marketing strategy (0.216037), followed by content marketing (0.095736), Search Engine Optimization (SEO) (0.060390), website and e-commerce (0.060366), and digital advertising (0.034137). These findings demonstrate that effective digital marketing for MSMEs depends on the integration of marketing budget allocation, target markets, the ease of use of digital platforms, customer satisfaction levels, response speed, and limitations in digital and technological literacy.</jats:p>

292f8b7b8ef02958a019ef2b1fb8965ec0d17003.abstract: <jats:p>This study aims to examine the impact of financial literacy and digital payments on the performance of MSMEs in urban areas. A quantitative approach was adopted as the methodological framework, involving 50 MSME owners in urban areas of Central Java Province selected through purposive sampling. Data were collected using a 1–5 Likert scale questionnaire and analyzed via multiple linear regression using SmartPLS version 4.1.1.8. The study yielded two key findings. First, financial literacy and digital payments each have a significant impact on MSME performance. Second, both factors were found to have a significant simultaneous impact on MSME performance. These findings confirm that enhancing financial literacy and adopting digital payments are crucial factors in boosting the performance of urban MSMEs. This study contributes to the limited body of research on urban MSMEs and offers practical implications for business owners and policymakers in designing strategies to strengthen MSME capacity. Consequently, improving financial literacy and utilizing digital payments emerge as two key strategies that should be promoted to enhance MSME performance in urban areas.</jats:p>

title: Radial Kernel Attention for Long-Range Modeling in Polymer Machine Learning Force Fields
0e9999db551e680dab8a3726c033f7250bf474ee.abstract: <jats:p>We introduce Radial Kernel Attention (RKA) for long-range modeling in polymer machine learning force fields. Local neighbor graphs constrain communication across polymer chains and their surrounding environments, while explicit all-pair attention incurs quadratic cost. RKA maps atomic distances from the cluster centroid to learned radial features and combines their overlap with content-dependent queries and keys. Factorized aggregation and readout enable global feature exchange at linear cost in atom count for fixed feature dimensions. We insert the invariant scalar update between EquiformerV3 local blocks and obtain conservative forces by differentiating the total energy, including its radial coordinate dependence. We evaluate energy and force prediction for finite polymer-derived clusters in OPoly26. Our models are trained on the official training split for 12 epochs and evaluated directly after training on the complete official validation split. A matched 5M comparison shows that RKA reduces per-atom energy and force MAEs by 67.4% and 36.3%, respectively. The 20M RKA model is compared with UMA-S-1.2 and UMA-S-1.2.1 on the same validation structures. The 20M model attains a total-energy MAE of 15.81 meV and a force MAE of 2.619 meV/Å; its per-atom energy MAE is 0.1182 meV/atom. RKA provides a compact global communication pathway that improves energy and force prediction on the evaluated polymer-derived clusters.</jats:p>

title: Behavioural lifestyle profiles among students in public higher education: health behaviours, digital engagement, leisure and sociability
1e5248308aa67c1d05f787c1d952e0a38ca28b0c.abstract: Background Student lifestyles encompass a wide range of interrelated behaviours, yet research has rarely examined conventional health behaviours alongside digital engagement and sociocultural activities. We identified lifestyle profiles among students in Portuguese public higher education and examined their sociodemographic correlates and health, psychosocial, and academic outcomes. Methods Data were drawn from the probabilistic ES + Saúde survey of 9611 students in Portuguese public higher education. Latent profile analysis included 8840 students and 27 behavioural indicators spanning sleep, physical activity, sedentary behaviour, diet, leisure, digital use, gaming, and substance use. Multinomial logistic regression assessed sociodemographic correlates; adjusted linear models compared 17 distal outcomes. Results Four profiles emerged: Low-risk and low digital/recreational engagement (46.5%), Social alcohol and risk consumption (19.9%), Sedentary recreational digital/gaming (19.2%), and Active sociocultural and digitally engaged (14.3%). Profile membership varied by age, gender, residential relocation, field of study, institution type, and subjective social class. All 17 outcomes differed significantly across profiles after adjustment ( p < .001), although effects were generally modest (partial η² = .008–.062). The sedentary digital/gaming profile showed the least favourable overall health, psychological, social, and academic outcomes. Conversely, the active sociocultural profile combined the highest digital engagement with the highest physical activity and sociocultural participation and generally favourable outcomes. The low-risk profile also showed favourable outcomes. Conclusions Student lifestyles reflect distinct behavioural configurations rather than a simple healthy–unhealthy continuum. Digital engagement was not inherently associated with adverse outcomes; its relevance depended on accompanying behaviours. Health promotion may benefit from addressing co-occurring behavioural patterns rather than isolated risks.

653308332c4faef092f45b4c3ad7b8cbeb387405.abstract: <jats:p>En complément des travaux statistiques qui mesurent le poids des facteurs sociodémo- graphiques d’exclusion numérique, l’article s’appuie sur une enquête qualitative menée entre 2021 et 2023 à l’échelle d’un département et visant à rendre compte de l’expérience que font de leur parcours d’accès aux droits les publics de ce point de vue vulnérables. Cette analyse confirme les caractéristiques des profils d’usagers que la littérature dispo- nible décrit comme particulièrement exposés. Elle souligne en outre les difficultés que rencontre une population a priori équipée pour faire face aux exigences de la transformation numérique mais qui se heurte à la complexité persistante des démarches administratives. title: The Use of Digital Technology in Christian Education
container-title: Aletheia Christian Educators Journal
f700f3d23c460a1c671913202c9aecb1fab9ddc7.abstract: <jats:p>Digital technology offers opportunities to expand access, engagement, and flexibility in Christian education. However, its contribution to academic learning and Christian formation requires critical examination. This systematic literature review synthesizes research on digital technology in Christian education, focusing on technological applications, reported educational outcomes, teachers’ roles, and implementation challenges. Searches of Google Scholar, GARUDA, and relevant educational journals identified ten articles published between 2020 and 2026 that met the inclusion criteria. Empirical and literature-based studies were analyzed using descriptive thematic synthesis. The reviewed literature reported benefits associated with e-learning platforms, Moodle, interactive media, audiovisual resources, and gamification, particularly for student motivation, participation, and access to learning materials. Nevertheless, differences in research designs and outcomes limit conclusions about effectiveness, especially regarding sustained academic achievement, character development, and spiritual formation. Successful integration depends on teacher competence, student readiness, infrastructure, and alignment with educational objectives. The synthesis highlights teachers’ complementary responsibilities as academic and spiritual leaders. Technological pedagogical content knowledge provides a useful perspective for interpreting instructional integration, while Christian educational purposes require additional attention to faith, ethical reflection, and community. The distinctive emphasis lies in the purposes guiding technology use rather than the tools themselves. Digital technology should therefore support purposeful teaching and meaningful relationships, with further empirical research needed to evaluate its long-term academic and formative contributions.</jats:p>

title: Fenomena Digital Pacifier pada Keluarga Pedesaan
container-title: Aletheia Christian Educators Journal
b6263c49ab3e4203ad1978d165c4ba64664f7d20.abstract: <jats:p>Penetrasi gawai di wilayah pedesaan memunculkan dinamika baru dalam pengasuhan anak. Literasi digital orang tua tidak selalu sejalan dengan praktik pengasuhan. Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis tingkat literasi digital orang tua dan disonansi antara literasi digital dengan praktik penggunaan gawai sebagai digital pacifier pada keluarga pedesaan. Penelitian menggunakan desain kuantitatif deskriptif dengan survei cross-sectional terhadap 25 orang tua di dua desa Kabupaten Mojokerto, Jawa Timur, dengan rata-rata usia anak terkecil 5,48 tahun. Data dikumpulkan melalui kuesioner skala Likert yang mengukur literasi digital dan praktik pengasuhan, kemudian dianalisis secara deskriptif dan inferensial menggunakan uji Wilcoxon, Spearman’s Rho, dan Fisher’s Exact. Hasil menunjukkan tingkat literasi digital teknis tinggi (>80%), tetapi kesadaran keamanan siber dan pemahaman kritis terhadap informasi masih terbatas. Tidak terdapat korelasi maupun perbedaan signifikan antara literasi digital dan status pekerjaan orang tua dengan praktik pembatasan akses gawai (p>0,05). Temuan menunjukkan paradoks antara pemahaman normatif dan praktik pengasuhan, ketika kelelahan pengasuhan (parenting burnout) mendorong penggunaan gawai sebagai digital pacifier. Intervensi digital parenting perlu menekankan mediasi aktif yang aplikatif dan peka budaya, bukan sekadar pembatasan waktu layar.</jats:p>

title: Hybrid TensorRT–PyTorch Inference Acceleration for Attention-Based CNNs with Dynamic ROI Sampling: A Case Study on Jetson Nano
9f2c09616dd1f8c5aadecd090f9c72559d64f057.abstract: <jats:p>Edge AI deployment requires low-latency inference on devices with tight constraints in size, weight, power, and cost. NVIDIA TensorRT accelerates inference through layer fusion, precision reduction, and kernel auto-tuning, but a model containing even one unsupported operator cannot be compiled into a single engine. This paper presents a hybrid TensorRT–PyTorch deployment in which the supported subnetworks run as TensorRT engines while the unsupported operations fall back to native PyTorch, and applies it to an attention-based convolutional neural network (ACNN) whose region-of-interest sampling operators are unsupported. On an NVIDIA Jetson Nano, the hybrid approach reduced the end-to-end latency of ACNN-dsc, the fastest native PyTorch model, from 38.37 ms to 20.40 ms (1.88×) under FP32. Under FP16, the hybrid ACNN-k3 achieved the lowest latency of 17.78 ms, a 2.23× speedup over its PyTorch FP32 counterpart and 2.16× over the fastest PyTorch model. Stepwise profiling of the image preprocessing pipeline showed that transferring raw images and performing most conversions on the GPU more than halves preprocessing latency. Further analyses across devices, precisions, and frameworks show that practical latency on edge AI accelerators depends on hardware and runtime factors beyond FLOPs and model size.</jats:p>

title: Deep Looking in Digital Pathology: An Explainable Federated Learning Framework for Lung Cancer Classification
8bd44e6ddd5021b8c2f6d413a841b0f937795d74.abstract: <jats:p>Background/Objectives: Lung cancer is the leading cause of cancer death worldwide, and growing slide volumes add to pathologists’ cognitive load. Deep learning can assist histopathological diagnosis, but two obstacles limit its clinical use: privacy regulations keep patient images in institutional “data silos”, and the “black-box” behavior of neural networks undermines clinical trust. Inspired by Topol’s Deep Medicine, we aimed to build a diagnostic platform that preserves privacy and explains its decisions. Methods: We developed the Lung Cancer Analysis System (LCAS), which combines federated learning (FL), explainable artificial intelligence (XAI), and a locally deployed medical large language model (LLM). Three public H&E datasets (LC25000, HistoSet-5×14, and CLID; 18,000 images; adenocarcinoma, squamous cell carcinoma, benign tissue) acted as three hospital nodes with source-induced non-independent and identically distributed (non-IID) data. DenseNet121, EfficientNet-B3, and MobileNetV3-Small were trained centrally and with FedAvg/FedProx for 20 rounds. Grad-CAM produced visual evidence, and MedGemma 1.5, served offline through LM Studio, converted predictions and heatmap descriptors into structured reports. Results: Centralized training reached 99.50% ± 0.21% accuracy with DenseNet121. Under non-IID federated training with FedProx, DenseNet121 and EfficientNet-B3 achieved 96.97% and 97.49% accuracy on an independent external blind test set of 958 images, whereas MobileNetV3-Small reached 91.23%. Accuracy remained 99.78% under Gaussian blur. t-SNE showed that global features clustered by tissue class rather than by hospital, and Grad-CAM highlighted glandular and tumor-nest regions consistent with histopathological criteria. Conclusions: FL, XAI, and on-premise LLM reporting can be integrated into a single workflow that keeps raw images within each institution while giving pathologists numerical, visual, and textual explanations, providing a practical path toward trustworthy cross-institutional computational pathology.</jats:p>

title: A Critical Analysis of the Legal and Ethical Challenges of Digital Lending Applications in Tanzania: A Doctrinal Analysis with Comparative Reference to Nigeria
container-title: East African Journal of Law and Ethics
fbc5debd264ec0ad7e2cc871a7d2c10303fba402.abstract: <jats:p>App-based digital lending has changed how Tanzanians borrow: a loan can be applied for, scored and disbursed on a handset within minutes, with an algorithm in place of the loan officer and the borrower’s phone data in place of collateral. This article asks whether Tanzanian law has kept pace with that change. Using doctrinal legal research, it examines the Microfinance Act, Cap 407, its 2019 Non-Deposit Taking Regulations, the Bank of Tanzania’s 2024 Guidance Note on Digital Lenders, the Financial Consumer Protection Regulations as amended in 2025, the 2025 Complaints Guidelines and the Personal Data Protection Act, Cap 44. The analysis draws on information asymmetry theory, the vulnerability theory of the consumer, informational self-determination and contextual integrity, and algorithmic accountability. It finds that the reforms of 2019 to 2025 have filled most literal silences in the law, but that the framework retains one legal gap, the absence of any standard for authenticating a guarantor’s consent on a mobile interface; four normative gaps, concerning informed guarantor consent, a flat penalty ceiling, the timing and comparability of cost disclosure, and weak explanation and reconsideration rights for automated decisions; two implementation gaps, in unaudited debt recovery and in-app redress; and one coordination gap among the Bank of Tanzania, the Personal Data Protection Commission and the newly designated self-regulatory associations. Nigeria’s move from interim guidelines to binding regulations, upheld by its Federal High Court in 2026, shows that converting guidance into enforceable rules is achievable. The article recommends a binding guarantor-verification standard, scaled penalties, pre-application cost disclosure, specified algorithmic disclosure, joint sampled audits and a formal inter-agency memorandum of understanding.</jats:p>

title: An Application of the Self-Determination Theory Model for AI-Enhanced, Digital Psychosocial Interventions for Pediatric Disabilities
container-title: Western Journal of Nursing Research
c620cf1b4f812518b0ef9e1f32165cf0b13e2621.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Background:</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Youth with developmental disabilities (DDs) experience elevated psychosocial challenges, including difficulties with emotion regulation, self-concept, and access to timely mental health support. Pediatric nurses are well-positioned to address these needs; however, time constraints, limited training, and restricted access to specialty services often impede the provision of consistent psychosocial care. Digitally delivered psychosocial interventions enhanced by artificial intelligence (AI) offer new opportunities for individualized, accessible support, but these approaches frequently lack a clear theoretical foundation.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Purpose:</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This paper applied Self-Determination Theory (SDT), specifically Basic Psychological Needs Theory, to guide pediatric nurses’ use of AI-enhanced, digital psychosocial interventions for DDs in practice.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods:</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>A theory-driven synthesis mapped SDT needs (autonomy, competence, and relatedness) to AI-enabled intervention features: conversational agents, neuro/adaptive feedback, and emotion-recognition tailoring.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results:</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The framework specifies how these features can promote volitional engagement, optimal challenge with timely feedback, and supportive interactions for youth with DDs. It also notes evidence gaps (small, heterogeneous samples; limited comparisons and follow-up) and barriers involving payment/workload, equity and access, and data protection, transparency, and bias.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusions/Implications:</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>SDT offers a coherent, testable foundation for designing, evaluating, and integrating AI-enhanced psychosocial supports for pediatric DDs. Nurses can screen for support, coach families, monitor risks, and advocate for ethical deployment and rigorous research.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: CRYPTOASSETS, MONEY LAUNDERING AND CRIMINAL LIABILITY: ECONOMIC AND LEGAL CHALLENGES OF THE DIGITAL FINANCIAL SYSTEM
container-title: Baltic Journal of Economic Studies
48114789291156faf82af99d185f1818a06eec98.abstract: <jats:p>The present article provides a comprehensive economic and legal analysis of the use of cryptoassets in mechanisms for the legalisation (laundering) of proceeds of crime. In addition, it examines the specific features of criminal-law responses to such practices within the digital financial system. The study's relevance is determined by the rapid expansion of the global cryptoasset market, the growth in the volume of illicit cryptocurrency transactions, and the increasing use of stablecoins, P2P and OTC channels, cryptocurrency mixers, and other technologies in schemes designed to transfer and conceal criminal proceeds. It is also determined by the need to adapt national financial monitoring and criminal justice systems to the technological transformation of financial relations. The purpose of the study is fourfold: to identify the economic mechanisms through which cryptoassets are used for money laundering; to assess the applicability of Article 209 of the Criminal Code of Ukraine to digital forms of economic value; to pinpoint the primary challenges of criminal law qualification and evidentiary assessment; and to provide recommendations for enhancing the national economic and legal mechanisms for combating illicit financial flows in the digital environment. The study establishes that, while cryptoassets do not alter the economic essence of money laundering, they do significantly transform the architecture of the financial trail. This is achieved by increasing transactional complexity, fragmenting financial flows, enabling the repeated conversion of digital value and combining decentralised and traditional financial infrastructures. It is argued that the current wording of Article 209 of the Criminal Code of Ukraine is sufficiently technology-neutral to encompass transactions involving cryptoassets. However, the main challenges lie in establishing the link between a digital asset and a predicate criminal offence, identifying the beneficial or actual controller of the asset, proving that the individual is aware of its criminal origin, and ensuring effective procedural control over virtual assets. The study also shows that the FATF's standards and the European Union's regulatory framework provide the conceptual basis for integrating crypto assets into the wider system of risk-based AML/CFT regulation. The study's scientific novelty lies in substantiating an integrated model of economic and legal counteraction to money laundering involving cryptoassets. This model incorporates technology-neutral criminal law, specialised criminal procedural mechanisms for dealing with digital assets, risk-based financial monitoring, blockchain analytics and international co-operation. The findings have the potential to improve law enforcement practice under Article 209 of the Criminal Code of Ukraine by developing procedures for the detection, seizure, custody, valuation and confiscation of cryptoassets. They could also strengthen the analytical capacity of financial intelligence and criminal justice authorities and harmonise national regulation with FATF standards and European Union law.</jats:p>

title: THE IMPACT OF DIGITAL BANKING AND ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE ON PRIVATE BANKING IN SWITZERLAND: ARE CHANGES AHEAD?
container-title: Baltic Journal of Economic Studies
fc0200543deeb6a741483b724d64137597441910.abstract: <jats:p>Subject of Research. This study focuses on the digital banking landscape and the integration of artificial intelligence (AI) in private banking and wealth management in Switzerland. More specifically, it examines how technological innovations – ranging from process automation and generative AI to advanced data analytics – alter the operational dynamics, customer relations, and structural competitiveness of Swiss private banks in the context of shifting client expectations and rigorous regulatory environments. Methodology. The research employs a qualitative analytical research design that uses triangulation of secondary evidence. It systematically integrates and cross-checks academic literature on digital finance, fintech adoption and robo-advisory trust, alongside empirical data, regulatory frameworks and market insights from reputable Swiss and international organisations. The primary data sources analysed were supervisory guides from the Swiss Financial Market Supervisory Authority (FINMA), reports from the Swiss Bankers Association, digital maturity benchmarks from Deloitte Switzerland and private banking market profitability assessments from KPMG and PwC Switzerland. Purpose. The main objective of this paper is to provide a comprehensive assessment of the impact of digital transformation and the deployment of AI on the traditional Swiss private banking model. By analysing seven key dimensions – technological progress, customer expectations, process optimization, data analytics, risk and security, regulation/compliance, and market trajectories – the study aims to clarify the economic mechanisms driving digital adaptation, identify the structural barriers preventing rapid technology adoption, and evaluate the strategic options available to Swiss banks facing intense global competition and margin compression. Findings and Conclusion. The study reveals a significant discrepancy between Switzerland's position as a global leader in asset management, with CHF 9.3 trillion under management, and its digital banking maturity score of 39 out of 60. Although private banking clients continue to establish relationships based on traditional factors such as reputation, trust and personal referrals, they are also demanding friction-free digital execution, personalised dashboards and virtual investment simulations. AI has been proven to have high economic value when acting as a productivity layer centred around advisors, optimising processes such as client onboarding, document extraction, compliance screening and portfolio monitoring. However, it is not as effective when acting as an autonomous replacement for human relationship managers. Ultimately, the integration of digital banking and AI is causing a clear market polarisation. Large-scale institutions are successfully absorbing the substantial fixed costs associated with technology, data governance and regulatory compliance under the frameworks of FINMA and the European Union (such as DORA and the EU AI Act). Conversely, smaller Swiss private banks are under severe pressure to increase their profitability and consolidate, unless they adopt highly focused niche advisory models. The paper therefore concludes that urgent regulatory attention and strategic repositioning are necessary to preserve the overall image and international attractiveness of the Swiss private banking ecosystem.</jats:p>

title: Impact of Video-Based Educational Content on Middle School Students’ Earthquake Knowledge and Attitudes
container-title: Journal of Learning and Teaching in Digital Age
cfe053e5496bb020e135a0ea7859edb6780f41de.abstract: <jats:p xml:lang="en">This study aimed to evaluate the impact of video-based educational content developed within the scope of earthquake education on middle school students’ earthquake-related knowledge and attitudes. The study employed a one-group pretest–posttest pre-experimental design and was conducted during the 2024–2025 academic year with 481 students enrolled in public middle schools. The video-based instructional materials were designed to enhance students’ cognitive understanding and affective responses to earthquakes. Data were collected using the Let’s Understand Earthquakes Test and the Attitude Toward Earthquakes Scale. Paired-samples t-tests and one-way ANOVA were used for data analysis. The findings of this study indicated that the intervention did not produce a statistically significant improvement in students’ overall earthquake knowledge, although a significant gain was observed in the protective behaviors dimension. In contrast, students’ attitudes toward earthquakes improved significantly with a large effect size. The results suggest that video-based educational materials developed within the scope of earthquake education are particularly effective in influencing affective outcomes such as attitudes, risk perception, and value-oriented motivation, while being less effective in fostering abstract conceptual knowledge. The study provides design implications for developing more cognitively supportive digital disaster-education materials.</jats:p>

title: Single-sensor acoustic emission source localization in blade local region based on an interpretable wavelet attention network
container-title: Structural Health Monitoring
92ef473a520b33a0e686c5dcb18c19961b4402ba.abstract: <jats:p>Acoustic emission (AE) technology is suitable for monitoring wind turbine blades because of its high-frequency response and sensitivity. However, existing damage localization approaches rely on multi-sensor arrays, which limit their engineering applicability. Moreover, deep learning models for single-sensor localization remain constrained by insufficient time-frequency representation and limited interpretability. To address these issues, a novel single-sensor AE source localization model, the Large-kernel dual wavelet attention network, was proposed. First, pencil lead break tests on real blade structures were conducted to investigate AE signal propagation, revealing strong nonlinear behavior and multi-scale attenuation characteristics. On this basis, a Large-kernel dual wavelet convolution layer was developed using Morlet and Mexican hat wavelets. With a mechanism-guided large wavelet kernel design, the arbitrariness in hyperparameter selection and the Gibbs phenomenon associated with incomplete truncation were mitigated, enabling the effective extraction of multi-scale time-frequency features. A time-grouped frequency attention mechanism module was introduced to adaptively recalibrate convolutional kernel weights through the fine-grained perception of localized time-frequency features, thereby improving the discrimination of critical features. Experiments on a real blade specimen demonstrated that the proposed method outperformed existing models in localization accuracy, achieving a minimum mean distance error of 20.29 mm. Furthermore, the model exhibited advantages in terms of feature interpretability and noise robustness. These results provide a promising and interpretable framework, laying the foundation for single-sensor damage localization in structural health monitoring of wind turbine blades.</jats:p>

title: Film Criticism and Analysis in the Digital Era: Role of Online Platforms
container-title: RESEARCH JOURNAL OF MASS COMMUNICATION AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY
b4652e251602ad62e5f4ef62ae1f31282fab57ac.abstract:
<jats:p>The digital era has revolutionized numerous facets of contemporary life, and film criticism is no
exception. Traditionally confined to the pages of newspapers and specialized journals, film
criticism has found new life on the internet, where online platforms have democratized and
diversified the field. Today, anyone with a keen eye for cinema and an internet connection can
publish reviews and analyses, challenging the dominance of established critics and broadening
the discourse around film. This shift has not only expanded the audience for film criticism but also
transformed the ways in which films are analyzed and discussed. The advent of the digital era has
profoundly transformed film criticism, shifting the landscape from traditional print media to
dynamic online platforms. Anchored on the technological determinism theory, this paper explores
the role of these platforms in reshaping film criticism and analysis. Online platforms such as blogs,
social media, and dedicated film websites have democratized the field, allowing a diverse array of
voices to participate in the discourse. These platforms provide immediacy and interactivity,
enabling rapid responses to new releases and fostering vibrant discussions. Furthermore, the
integration of multimedia elements like video essays and podcasts offers a more immersive
critique, enhancing traditional written reviews. However, this democratization also presents
challenges, including the proliferation of content, the difficulty of discerning credible voices, and
the polarization of online discourse. Despite these issues, the influence of online platforms is
undeniable, representing a significant evolution in film criticism. This paper examines the  opportunities and challenges presented by these digital mediums, highlighting their impact on how
films are reviewed, interpreted, and appreciated in the contemporary era.</jats:p>

title: Continuous glucose monitoring, automated insulin delivery, and remote care in adolescents with type 1 diabetes: advances toward integrated digital management
container-title: Frontiers in Endocrinology
3015c41314f48b63889f0cceb82e35af14ad39f4.abstract: <jats:p>Type 1 diabetes management in adolescents remains challenging due to physiological and behavioral factors. This review summarizes recent advances in three interconnected technologies: continuous glucose monitoring (CGM), automated insulin delivery (AID), and remote care. CGM provides real-time glycemic data with time in range (TIR) as the core metric, improving glycemic outcomes when implemented with structured education. AID systems, particularly hybrid closed-loop devices, consistently increase TIR, reduce glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c), and lower risks of severe hypoglycemia and diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA) across randomized trials and real-world studies, with validated efficacy in children as young as 1-year-old. Remote care models leverage continuous data streams to enable individualized follow-up, showing glycemic outcomes approaching those of traditional visits in comparative studies while improving access and psychosocial support. Despite proven benefits, barriers remain, including socioeconomic inequities in technology access, alarm fatigue, and implementation gaps across healthcare systems. Future priorities include fully closed-loop systems, dual-hormone approaches, algorithm optimization for exercise and illness, long-term psychosocial outcomes, and equitable implementation strategies. Clinical practice should integrate these technologies through multidisciplinary teams, early initiation, and patient-centered support to transform adolescent diabetes care from intermittent visits to continuous digital management.</jats:p>

title:
Etiquette in the Malay Archipelago Digital: A Comparative Study of Digital Media Self-Regulation and Cultural Values in
Indonesia and Malaysia
75e7598342906111c4c01abf6584612a7ef1292d.abstract: This study explores the ethical frameworks, cultural values, and self regulation mechanisms that underpin social media governance in Indonesia and Malaysia. Each country operates within distinct legal, political, and socio-cultural contexts, resulting in varied approaches to regulating digital communication. Utilizing document analysis and in-depth interviews, this research examines how ethics, normative values, and foundational principles of media freedom are operationalized in accordance with the 1984 Universal Declaration of Human Rights, which upholds freedom of speech and expression as fundamental rights. Findings reveal that while both countries recognize the importance of media freedom, they also emphasize the need for responsibility and regulation. Self regulation has emerged as a strategic model for aligning state laws, community norms, and platform standards. In particular, the study highlights how religious values, cultural traditions, and institutional frameworks shape ethical media practices in each nation. This research underscores the importance of fostering digital literacy that is deeply rooted in local ethical and cultural values. It recommends a participatory approach that strengthens collaboration among governments, digital communities, and platform providers to ensure a balanced and responsible digital ecosystem in Southeast Asia.

title: Efektivitas Sistem Informasi Haji dan Umrah (SIHU) sebagai Media Dakwah Digital dalam Pembinaan Jamaah Haji dan Umrah di Aceh
container-title: Khulasah : Islamic Studies Journal
1068bbce08759fbc323f5f57f70c5ead062fb3e8.abstract: <jats:p>Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis efektivitas Sistem Informasi Haji dan Umrah (SIHU) sebagai media dakwah dalam pembinaan jamaah haji dan umrah di Provinsi Aceh. Perkembangan teknologi informasi telah mendorong transformasi metode dakwah dari pendekatan konvensional menuju dakwah digital yang lebih interaktif, efektif, dan mudah diakses oleh masyarakat. Penelitian ini menggunakan pendekatan mixed methods dengan desain sequential explanatory, yaitu mengombinasikan metode kuantitatif dan kualitatif secara bertahap. Data kuantitatif diperoleh melalui survei terhadap 120 responden calon jamaah haji dan umrah, sedangkan data kualitatif diperoleh melalui wawancara mendalam terhadap 15 informan yang terdiri atas pengelola SIHU, pembimbing ibadah haji dan umrah, serta ulama Aceh. Teknik pengumpulan data dilakukan melalui observasi, wawancara, angket, dan dokumentasi. Analisis data kuantitatif menggunakan statistik deskriptif, sedangkan data kualitatif dianalisis menggunakan model Miles, Huberman, dan Saldaña yang meliputi reduksi data, penyajian data, dan penarikan kesimpulan. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa SIHU berperan efektif sebagai media dakwah modern yang mampu meningkatkan kualitas pelayanan administrasi, pembinaan keagamaan, komunikasi, dan pengawasan jamaah secara terintegrasi. Tingkat pemahaman jamaah meningkat dari 60% menjadi 85%, retensi pesan mencapai 70%, dan tingkat keterlibatan (engagement) jamaah mencapai 65%. Namun, perubahan perilaku keagamaan jangka panjang masih berada pada kategori sedang dengan persentase 45%. Hambatan utama yang ditemukan meliputi keterbatasan akses internet di beberapa daerah, rendahnya literasi digital, serta dominasi jamaah lanjut usia yang membutuhkan pendampingan khusus. Penelitian ini menyimpulkan bahwa efektivitas SIHU tidak hanya ditentukan oleh kecanggihan teknologi, tetapi juga oleh kemampuan sistem dalam mengintegrasikan nilai-nilai lokal, memperkuat pendampi-ngan, dan mengembangkan personalisasi konten yang sesuai dengan karakteristik jamaah Aceh. Oleh karena itu, optimalisasi SIHU dapat menjadi strategi dakwah digital yang berkelanjutan dalam meningkatkan kualitas pembinaan jamaah haji dan umrah di Aceh.</jats:p>

title: Students' Interest in Mathematics during the Digital Age: Impact of Online Learning, Self-efficacy, and Self-regulated Learning Using Structural Equation Modeling
container-title: Asian Journal of Education and Social Studies
6bf9fa7cb638cfdffbebb309e9b9db9014d7d325.abstract:
<jats:p>Background: The rapid digital transformation of higher education, accelerated by the COVID-19 pandemic, has increased students' engagement with mathematics through online learning platforms. While online learning offers flexibility and broader access to educational resources, its influence on students’ interest in mathematics remains unclear. Self-efficacy and self-regulated learning are considered important factors that may explain how online learning shapes students’ motivation and interest in mathematics.
Purpose: This study examined the mediating role of self-efficacy and self-regulated learning in the relationship between online learning and students’ interest in mathematics.
Methodology/Design/Approach: This study adopted a cross-sectional survey design. The study was conducted at a public university in Ghana. Data were collected using a structured questionnaire with a sample of 350 students. Participants were selected through stratified random sampling. Data were analysed using structural equation modelling (SEM) in Amos (version 23).
Findings: The analysis indicated that online learning significantly predicted students’ interest in mathematics, self-regulated learning, and self-efficacy. Additionally, self-efficacy and self-regulated learning also predicted students’ interest in mathematics. Furthermore, self-efficacy partially mediated the relationship between online learning and students' interest in mathematics. Finally, self-regulated learning partially and significantly mediated the link between online learning and students’ mathematics interest.
Research Limitations: This study focused on the mediating role of self-efficacy and self-regulated learning without examining moderating effects. However, these factors might be crucial in analysing the moderating influence of perceived digital literacy on the relationship between online learning and students’ interest in mathematics.
Originality: The principal contribution of this study is the examination of the mediating roles of self-efficacy and self-regulated learning in the relationship between online learning and students’ interest in mathematics.</jats:p>

title: Translation as pedagogy: strategic hybridization and multimodal equivalence in Indonesian–English digital storybooks for character education
container-title: Qualitative Research Journal
d65692294bdcd5c4a730ecd5f816539c73d3a00f.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Purpose</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study examines how translation strategies, equivalence, and multimodal resources interact to construct cultural, moral, and pedagogical meanings in an Indonesian–English bilingual digital storybook for character education.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Design/methodology/approach</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Adopting a qualitative descriptive approach, the study analyses 112 purposively selected translation units from an interactive digital storybook. Translation strategies are examined using Molina and Hurtado Albir's framework, while equivalence is analyzed at functional, linguistic and pragmatic levels. Multimodal analysis explores the alignment of verbal, visual and auditory elements.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Findings</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Three patterns emerge: strategic hybridization combines literal translation with pragmatic adaptation to maintain narrative clarity and pedagogical relevance; dynamic equivalence involves cultural and ideological reframing to make culture-specific expressions and moral values accessible to young readers; and multimodal reinforcement distributes moral and educational meanings across verbal, visual and auditory resources. These patterns demonstrate that translation involves negotiating linguistic accuracy, cultural specificity and pedagogical purpose rather than simply transferring meaning between languages.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Originality/value</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The study integrates translation strategies, equivalence and multimodal discourse analysis to conceptualize translation as a pedagogical and trans-semiotic practice. It extends text-centered approaches to equivalence by demonstrating how linguistic choices interact with multimodal resources in representing cultural knowledge and character-education values in digital children's literature.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Corporate Asset Allocation under Economic Policy Uncertainty: Avoidance Behaviour and the Conditional Value of Digital Economic Assets
container-title: Financial Economics Research
9ac435c50429ddfe4463124706d9c32c246764ba.abstract: <jats:p>Economic policy uncertainty has become an important factor affecting firms’ investment decisions in recent years. When uncertainty increases, firms may become more cautious about long-term investment and prefer to hold safer assets with higher liquidity. This paper studies how economic policy uncertainty influences firms' allocation between traditional safe assets and digital economic assets. It also examines whether this allocation affects firms' short-term performance differently under uncertain conditions. Using panel data from Chinese A-share listed companies between 2014 and 2023, this study applies fixed-effects regression models for empirical analysis. The results suggest that firms tend to increase traditional safe asset holdings and reduce digital asset investment when economic policy uncertainty rises. In addition, digital economic assets are negatively related to short-term return on assets (ROA) on average. However, the interaction results show that the negative effect becomes weaker under higher levels of uncertainty. These results may indicate that firms become more conservative during uncertain periods, but reducing digital investment too much could also weaken firms' ability to adapt to changing environments in the long run.</jats:p>

title: Technology-push risk screening for sustainable digital health adoption at the Uganda Cancer Institute: a design-stage research note aligned with SDG 3.8
46cbf1334f0a8068bf6d9e452a31c6c828c73472.abstract: Objective Digital health can contribute to stronger and more equitable health services, yet technologies introduced because they are externally funded, vendor-promoted or administratively driven may be poorly aligned with local need, user participation and institutional readiness. This research note describes a design-stage Technology Push Mitigation Framework for pre-deployment digital-health decision-making at the Uganda Cancer Institute (UCI) and positions its intended contribution against Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) 3, particularly target 3.8 on universal health coverage. Results Evidence was triangulated from global digital-health guidance, Uganda policy and standards, UCI-specific studies, and recent LMIC implementation literature. The resulting artefact has three layers: a technology-push risk screen, a four-domain readiness assessment, and a decision/escalation pathway. Six technology-push indicators and four readiness domains are operationalised, leading to three provisional decisions: proceed, revise/mitigate, or defer/escalate. The framework has not yet been empirically validated and does not demonstrate improved adoption or SDG outcomes. A staged validation pathway is specified for future empirical research.
