title: Digital Technology and Market Share of Selected Micro Enterprises Firms in Nigeria
container-title: RESEARCH JOURNAL OF MASS COMMUNICATION AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY
7318802c7475ce7d1a6df15371b4c4e8ea0daa97.abstract: The study examined the effect of digital technology on market share of selected micro enterprises firms in Nigeria. The specific objective was to determine the effect of e-commerce platform usage and social media marketing on market share of selected micro enterprises firms in Nigeria. Descriptive survey research design was adopted on a population of 41,469,947 operators of micro enterprises in Nigeria. A sample size of 400 was calculated using Taro Yamane formula while the respondents were recruited using purposive sampling approach. Primary data were collected using questionnaire based on five-point Likert-scale system. The hypotheses were tested using multiple regression analysis at 5% significance level. The study found the following: E-commerce platform usage has a significant and positive effect on market share of selected micro enterprises firms in Nigeria (β = 0.199, p = 0.000); Social media marketing has a significant and positive effect on market share of selected micro enterprises firms in Nigeria (β = 0.557, p = 0.000). In conclusion, micro enterprises that embrace digital technologies are better positioned to attract a larger customer base, compete more effectively, and grow their presence in the market. The study recommended that operators of micro enterprises should partner with technology solution providers to offer customized, subsidized e-commerce infrastructure and training programs tailored specifically for micro enterprise firms.

title: What Is a Digital Chemistry Lab?
container-title: Building a Digital Chemistry Lab
fcf44029228af378b81405988dd4bea90e8b74be.abstract: This opening chapter frames the concept of the digital chemistry lab by moving beyond imagery of robots and instead defining digitisation as the integration of automation, live data capture and algorithmic decision-making into experimental practice. It traces the historical roots of laboratory automation and explains why recent advances in hardware accessibility, data infrastructure and machine learning have lowered barriers to adoption. It also examines when digitisation is strategically advantageous, from hazardous and air-sensitive chemistry to ultrafast, long-duration and spatially complex systems. Readers are encouraged to assess what digitisation could mean for their own laboratory and why now is a pivotal moment to engage.

title: Automation and Robotics in the Modern Chemistry Lab
container-title: Building a Digital Chemistry Lab
12132c919241030d2f9b040bc0f267ce885bcde2.abstract: This chapter surveys the hardware and software foundations of the digital chemistry laboratory, guiding the reader from first principles of automation to the realities of closed-loop experimentation. It frames automation as a spectrum spanning manual workflows to fully autonomous self-driving laboratories, with trade-offs to be expected at each level. A comparative overview of physical implementations follows, including robotic arms, gantry systems, fluidic batch platforms, flow and microfluidic reactors, with attention to their respective strengths, bottlenecks and domains of applicability. We discuss commercially available digital labware and analytical instrumentation, including the practical challenges of interfacing with vendor software and legacy equipment. Finally, the chapter examines control architecture ranging from Python scripts to chemical programming languages and laboratory operating systems in order to acquaint the reader with automation strategies that may align with their scientific goals and available resources.

title: Designing and Implementing Custom Labware
container-title: Building a Digital Chemistry Lab
0045f858b4392024fc770627598a047e6bd96673.abstract: This chapter provides a practical guide to designing and implementing custom labware for the digital chemistry laboratory. It begins by looking at when bespoke hardware is justified and the balance between flexibility, time investment and scientific reproducibility. Core electronics concepts are introduced, including digital communication standards, analog signals, and pulse width modulation PWM control. Wireless options, power sources and strategies for safe voltage management are examined next. We then survey common sensors and actuators before outlining microcontroller ecosystems, concluding with prototyping workflows using CAD, 3D printing, laser cutting and aluminium extrusions.

title: Data Acquisition, Processing, and Interpretation
container-title: Building a Digital Chemistry Lab
4070d9765e56222d7bd875c107940855153bdab0.abstract: This chapter sets out practical foundations for handling experimental data in a digital laboratory, from capture to interpretation. It starts by outlining common routes to data acquisition, including direct instrument communication, file-based workflows and camera systems. We weigh options for organising and storing results using different file formats and databases. Core analytical ideas such as sampling, aliasing, Fourier transforms, filtering and dimensionality reduction are introduced with an emphasis on when and why they matter. The chapter closes with image-based data extraction and Bayesian modelling as tools for drawing quantitative conclusions under uncertainty.

title: Examples and Case Studies
container-title: Building a Digital Chemistry Lab
9db9f0ba73a0e30ac7924fc7edcec4f99174dee2.abstract: This chapter presents case studies that illustrate how digitisation can be implemented in real laboratory settings. What unique advantages do purpose-built digital laboratory spaces offer? How can legacy instruments be integrated into a modern experimental closed loop? And how can you accelerate your science via creative use of low-cost commodity hardware? A final case study demonstrates how to augment a closed robotic platform with external machine vision and hybrid control.

title: Summary and Further Learning
container-title: Building a Digital Chemistry Lab
8abe404efc3c171555c1035a6b29f6f2e08a8f10.abstract: This chapter concludes the book with closing thoughts and pointers to resources for learning more about some of the topics discussed in previous chapters.

title: Unlocking Europe’s Data Potential
9e100746d35b8070b98ffd24167df3289890c03f.abstract: The European Commission has outlined a comprehensive vision, ambition and strategy for its data economy. The goal is to unlock Europe’s data potential for innovation and societal value, while safeguarding digital autonomy and data sovereignty. The Common European Data Spaces are developed as the means to do so. As the architectures, standards and building blocks are rapidly maturing, the main challenges for their large-scale deployment and adoption are shifting towards governance, business and innovation management. In this inaugural lecture, Harrie Bastiaansen presents his vision and research agenda to address these challenges. The goals are to improve value creation, to decrease complexity and to stimulate adoption of the overarching data sharing ecosystem. A combined community-driven and participant-driven approach for trusted and interoperable data sharing across sectors, borders and data spaces is presented as the means to do so.

9bbaf6411e4d17f9b4d0ac6b9e47460a5ea24d33.abstract: Pemanfaatan kecerdasan buatan (artificial intelligence/AI) berpotensi membantu guru menyusun media presentasi pembelajaran secara lebih efisien, sistematis, dan menarik. Kegiatan pengabdian kepada masyarakat ini bertujuan memperkenalkan dan melatih penggunaan aplikasi berbasis AI untuk penyusunan slide presentasi bagi guru sekolah menengah atas. Pelatihan diselenggarakan oleh tim Program Studi Teknik Informatika Universitas Islam Riau pada 13 November 2025 di SMA Qurnat Internat Ibadurrahman, Belading, Duri. Metode kegiatan mencakup pengenalan konsep AI, demonstrasi pemanfaatan platform AI untuk mengolah materi menjadi rancangan slide, praktik langsung, diskusi, serta pendampingan peserta. Berdasarkan dokumentasi kegiatan, guru mengikuti sesi praktik dan terlibat aktif dalam diskusi penggunaan aplikasi AI. Kegiatan menghasilkan pengalaman awal pemanfaatan AI dalam perancangan presentasi pembelajaran; namun, besaran peningkatan kompetensi belum dapat dihitung karena data prates, pascates, dan penilaian produk belum tersedia pada dokumen sumber. Pelatihan ini menunjukkan peluang penguatan literasi AI guru melalui pendekatan praktik langsung dan menegaskan pentingnya tindak lanjut berupa evaluasi produk, verifikasi akurasi konten, dan pendampingan penggunaan AI secara bertanggung jawab.

title: Illicit drug marketing on social media in Thailand: a mixed-methods netnography and implications for drug policy
container-title: Frontiers in Digital Health
e4742faa9cbcbe591d04e4bb1a9c1999e451720d.abstract: Background Digital technologies have transformed illicit drug markets, with social media increasingly used for distribution and promotion. Our study aimed to characterize illicit drug marketing practices across multiple social media platforms in Thailand using a mixed-methods netnographic approach and to examine their implications for digital surveillance, prevention, and drug policy. Methods We conducted a mixed-methods netnographic study combining quantitative descriptive content analysis with qualitative coding of publicly accessible posts collected across multiple social media platforms in Thailand between January and December 2025. Posts were identified through targeted keyword searches and algorithmically recommended content, followed by manual screening. A curated Thai-language lexicon incorporating drug names, slang terms, euphemisms, coded expressions, and emoji-based representations was used to identify relevant content. Data were processed using Python-based tools, and marketing characteristics were coded across four domains: operational, psychological, conversion, and obfuscation. Descriptive analyses were conducted to summarize patterns across platforms, substance categories, communication features, and posting times. Results A total of 6,446 posts were analyzed. X accounted for 84.7% of posts. Stimulants were the most frequently identified substances (70.7%), followed by new psychoactive substances (22.2%). Indicators of convenience and accessibility were present in 68.7% of posts, while urgency and scarcity cues were observed in 25.9%. Cross-platform transition cues were identified in 41.8% of posts. Coded communication was widespread, including slang substitutions (74.2%) and emoji-based representations (28.6%). The largest proportion of posts (28.3%) by time period was observed during evening hours. Conclusion Illicit drug marketing on social media in Thailand occurs within a multi-platform environment characterized by accessibility-related marketing, coded communication, and cross-platform transition cues. By characterizing these features within the same multi-platform dataset, our study contributes evidence on social media drug markets within the Thai context. These findings support consideration of interaction across platforms in public health surveillance, drug abuse prevention, and drug policy responses.

title: Transformación Digital y Empleabilidad en Neiva: Habilidades Laborales y Necesidades Empresariales Percibidas Durante 2015–2025
container-title: Ciencia Latina Revista Científica Multidisciplinar
73e633fad509c0e22d5ef8b8d3747d6c915e3590.abstract: El objetivo fue analizar los cambios percibidos en las habilidades laborales asociados con la transformación digital y su relación con las necesidades empresariales y la empleabilidad en Neiva durante 2015–2025. Se realizó una síntesis cuantitativa descriptiva de una encuesta transversal de doce preguntas cerradas, organizada en tres dimensiones: cambios y aprendizaje, habilidades requeridas y oportunidades laborales. Esta versión utiliza provisionalmente las distribuciones de 35 respuestas presentadas en las gráficas del informe, cuya discrepancia con los 31 registros mencionados en la metodología debe resolverse. El 91,4 % declaró cambios en su forma de trabajar; el manejo de Excel, Word u otros programas fue el conocimiento más señalado en selección (68,6 %). El 82,9 % reportó beneficios laborales del aprendizaje tecnológico y el 42,9 % indicó dificultades de acceso al empleo por conocimientos insuficientes. El 91,4 % valoró como importante o muy importante continuar aprendiendo. Los hallazgos sugieren una complementariedad percibida entre herramientas digitales, adaptación y actualización. No permiten establecer causalidad, comprobar hipótesis ni generalizar a toda Neiva. Se propone orientar la formación hacia tareas concretas y contrastar las percepciones con información empresarial y registros individuales depurados.

title: Transformación Digital desde la Mirada del Talento Humano en IPS: Un Estudio Multicéntrico
container-title: Ciencia Latina Revista Científica Multidisciplinar
f27c640f4a3b4186df150a37b3f4a90d921fdc11.abstract: Objetivo: Explorar la transformación digital en las Instituciones Prestadoras de Servicios de Salud (IPS) desde la mirada del talento humano en un entorno digital. Metodología: Se empleó una metodología de revisión sistemática; la búsqueda de literatura científica se llevó a cabo entre enero y mayo de 2026, centrada en estudios publicados entre 2015 y 2025. Para ello, se realizaron exploraciones manuales y electrónicas en cinco bases de datos reconocidas por su relevancia académica en el ámbito de la salud: PubMed, Scopus, ScienceDirect, SciELO y Google Scholar. Resultados esperados: Los resultados revelan una implementación progresiva pero desigual de soluciones tecnológicas avanzadas, con mayor aplicación en áreas administrativas que clínicas. La inteligencia artificial es bien valorada como apoyo al diagnóstico médico, pero su uso clínico aún es limitado por resistencias culturales, falta de formación y ausencia de normativas específicas. En el ámbito de la innovación tecnológica, la investigación destaca la necesidad urgente de fortalecer el dominio de herramientas digitales por parte del personal de salud, promover la integración interdisciplinaria y avanzar hacia modelos de gobernanza digital que contemplen transparencia algorítmica, interoperabilidad y protección de datos. En conclusión, no es únicamente la tecnología disponible lo que impulsa la transformación digital en salud, sino que las capacidades organizacionales, humanas y éticas son necesarias para apropiarla. El camino hacia una administración en salud más inteligente, segura y predictiva exige esfuerzos coordinados entre actores institucionales, gubernamentales y académicos, con estrategias adaptadas a condiciones particulares de cada región.

title: Unterstützende Interventionen bei Aufmerksamkeitsdefizit‑/Hyperaktivitätsstörung (ADHS) im schulischen Kontext: Ein Scoping Review
Supportive interventions for attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) in the school context: a scoping review
container-title: Prävention und Gesundheitsförderung
e662bbbc6224c0d8996300acafe3f5375656c0f6.abstract: Zusammenfassung Hintergrund und Ziel Der schulische Alltag stellt für Schüler*innen mit Aufmerksamkeitsdefizit‑/Hyperaktivitätsstörung (ADHS), ihre Eltern und Lehrkräfte eine zentrale Belastungsquelle dar. Ziel des Scoping Reviews war es zu untersuchen, inwieweit Interventionen bei ADHS im schulischen Kontext Unterstützung bieten können. Methode Es wurde ein Scoping Review durchgeführt und gemäß PRISMA-ScR (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews) berichtet. Die systematische Recherche erfolgte in MEDLINE (via PubMed). Eingeschlossen wurden multimodale Interventionen für Schüler*innen mit ADHS im Alter von 6 bis 18 Jahren. Die Auswertung erfolgte mittels thematischer Analyse nach Braun und Clarke. Ergebnisse Zwölf Publikationen wurden eingeschlossen. Die Interventionen adressierten Schüler*innen, Eltern und Lehrkräfte insbesondere durch organisatorische und verhaltensbezogene Interventionsinhalte. Verbesserungen wurden v. a. bei der ADHS-Symptomatik und bei organisatorischen Leistungen berichtet. Die Befunde zu akademischen Leistungen und zum Sozialverhalten waren weniger einheitlich. Die Stichproben waren überwiegend männlich geprägt, und Interventionseffekte wurden nicht differenziert nach ADHS-Subtypen ausgewertet. Zudem lagen kaum Erkenntnisse zur fachlich-didaktischen und interaktionalen Gestaltung konkreter schulischer Lehr-Lern-Prozesse vor. Schlussfolgerung Forschungsbedarf besteht insbesondere hinsichtlich Mädchen mit ADHS, einer differenzierten Betrachtung unterschiedlicher ADHS-Erscheinungsbilder und Behandlungsbedingungen sowie der evidenzbasierten Gestaltung fachlich-didaktischer und interaktionaler Lehr-Lern-Prozesse im inklusiven Unterricht.

title: Pengaruh Model Pembelajaran Discovery Learning Menggunakan Padlet terhadap Literasi Digital pada Mata Pelajaran Informatika Kelas VIII SMP Negeri 19 Padang
container-title: Jurnal QOSIM : Jurnal Pendidikan Sosial & Humaniora
14c03194d70b6c4a0abe0c9b55cff10dd48541fa.abstract: Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mengetahui pengaruh model pembelajaran Discovery Learning menggunakan Padlet terhadap literasi digital peserta didik pada mata pelajaran Informatika, khususnya pada materi Dampak Sosial Informatika, di SMPN 19 Padang. Penelitian ini dilatarbelakangi oleh hasil observasi awal yang menunjukkan bahwa pembelajaran masih berpusat pada guru, peserta didik cenderung pasif dan jarang bertanya atau menyampaikan pendapat, serta modul ajar mencantumkan media digital yang tidak dioperasikan dalam pembelajaran. Penelitian ini menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif dengan kuasi-eksperimen desain Nonequivalent Control Group Design, yang membandingkan kelas eksperimen yang belajar menggunakan model Discovery Learning berbantuan Padlet dengan kelas kontrol yang belajar menggunakan model Direct Instruction. Sampel ditentukan melalui teknik purposive sampling, sehingga diperoleh kelas VIII-5 sebagai kelas eksperimen (32 peserta didik) dan kelas VIII-4 sebagai kelas kontrol (32 peserta didik). Pengumpulan data dilakukan melalui angket literasi digital berskala Likert sebanyak 10 butir yang mencakup dimensi teknis, kognitif, dan sosial-emosional (Ng, 2012), dengan reliabilitas yang mengacu pada penelitian terdahulu (α = 0,869–0,898), diberikan sebelum dan sesudah perlakuan, lalu dianalisis menggunakan uji normalitas Shapiro-Wilk, uji homogenitas Levene, dan Independent Samples t-Test. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa kelas eksperimen memperoleh rata-rata skor posttest 39,47 (tertinggi 46, terendah 33), lebih tinggi dibandingkan kelas kontrol dengan rata-rata 36,03 (tertinggi 41, terendah 31). Kedua data berdistribusi normal (Sig. 0,261–0,686) dan homogen (Sig. 0,560 dan 0,719), serta uji t menghasilkan t hitung sebesar 4,708 yang lebih besar dari t tabel sebesar 1,999 dengan Sig. (2-tailed) < 0,001 < 0,05 dan ukuran efek besar (Cohen’s d = 1,18). Peningkatan terutama terjadi pada dimensi teknis dan kognitif, sedangkan dimensi sosial-emosional meningkat tipis pada kedua kelas. Dengan demikian, model Discovery Learning menggunakan Padlet berpengaruh signifikan terhadap literasi digital peserta didik pada pembelajaran Informatika dan dapat dijadikan alternatif strategi pembelajaran yang berpusat pada peserta didik dengan dukungan media digital interaktif.

title: Perlindungan Hukum Bagi Pencipta Terhadap Pelanggaran Hak Cipta Konten Digital di Media Sosial Berdasarkan Hukum Positif di Indonesia
container-title: Jurnal QOSIM : Jurnal Pendidikan Sosial & Humaniora
c8b272b0fc6bb4b977729b27fffa8a602845f579.abstract: Studi ini memiliki tujuan untuk menguji serta menelaah ragam bentuk perlindungan hukum bagi para pemilik karya terhadap praktik pelanggaran hak cipta atas konten digital berupa video, foto, serta tulisan yang disebarluaskan secara tidak sah melalui berbagai platform media sosial. Rumusan masalah meliputi: (1) bagaimana pengaturan dan bentuk perlindungan hak cipta terhadap karya digital di media sosial; dan (2) bagaimana mekanisme penegakan hukum dan penyelesaian sengketa terhadap pembajakan konten digital di Indonesia. Kajian ini digolongkan sebagai penelitian yuridis normatif dengan menggunakan metode pendekatan perundang-undangan serta pendekatan konseptual. Sumber-sumber hukum yang dimanfaatkan mencakup bahan hukum primer, sekunder, dan tersier, yang dikumpulkan lewat teknik studi pustaka melalui pencatatan literatur yang berkaitan, untuk kemudian dievaluasi menggunakan metode kualitatif-deskriptif serta ditarik kesimpulan secara deduktif. Temuan studi ini mengindikasikan adanya dua poin utama. Pertama, pengamanan hukum atas karya digital di media sosial telah dipayungi oleh Undang-Undang Nomor 28 Tahun 2014 tentang Hak Cipta juncto Undang-Undang Nomor 1 Tahun 2024 mengenai Informasi dan Transaksi Elektronik (UU ITE). Hak cipta tersebut timbul secara deklaratif semenjak sebuah karya diwujudkan dalam wujud konkrit, yang sekaligus menganugerahkan hak moral serta hak finansial kepada sang pembuatnya. Namun, karakteristik media sosial yang mudah direkam, diunggah ulang (reposting), dan disebarluaskan tanpa izin menimbulkan kerentanan pembajakan massal. Kedua, penegakan hukum terhadap pelanggaran hak cipta digital mencakup perlindungan preventif melalui fitur pelaporan konten (takedown notice) dan pendaftaran hak cipta, serta perlindungan represif melalui gugatan perdata ganti rugi di Pengadilan Niaga maupun penuntutan pidana berdasarkan delik aduan. Kendati demikian, penegakan hukum masih menghadapi kendala anonimitas akun pelanggar dan lambatnya respons moderasi platform global.

title: Digital technologies for crop water stress detection, prediction and water-management decision-making in smallholder rainfed systems: a review
container-title: Plant Growth Regulation
a983720aabe77c2bb08a2d9228569e2032efbc69.abstract: Abstract Drought remains the single largest climatic threat to crop production in rainfed and smallholder farming systems, where irrigation infrastructure is limited and crop failure translates directly into food insecurity. Over the past decade, a rapid expansion of digital technologies has transformed our capacity to detect and anticipate crop water stress. This review examines how these technologies are being connected, or fail to be connected, to water-management decisions and agronomic interventions that improve outcomes for farmers. We reviewed relevant evidence across five dimensions: (i) sensing and prediction technologies; (ii) water-stress indicators; (iii) digital decision-support and advisory systems; (iv) intervention and adoption pathways in smallholder contexts; and (v) measured effects on yield, water-use efficiency (WUE) and drought resilience. Key findings include: detection accuracy has outpaced decision integration, with machine-learning models routinely achieving R² of 0.75–0.90 under controlled conditions but rarely feeding operational decisions; a marked lab-to-field transfer gap, with accuracies falling by up to ~ 22% points in farmer fields; a systematic WUE-yield trade-off under deficit irrigation; and consistent evidence that frugal tools outperform sophisticated systems in smallholder cost-benefit terms. Digital tools deliver their largest gains when they amplify proven agronomy (deficit and supplemental irrigation, rainwater harvesting, drought-tolerant cultivars) and when they are institutionally embedded in extension and water-governance systems. This evidence was integrated into a framework that identifies the “missing middle” between sensing and action as the field’s critical bottleneck, and derive research priorities for transferable, decision-centred, smallholder-appropriate digital water management.

title: Digital Twins for Decision Support in Production Planning and Control: A Conceptual Framework and Research Directions
container-title: Applied Sciences
940a6142a37a4e0681ce705249b33ad04c4674b6.abstract: With the advent of Industry 4.0, manufacturing is being reshaped by the adoption of digital technologies, which can support and enhance design and management activities in production systems. Within this context, the concept of the Digital Twin emerged as a new paradigm which enriches simulation modeling capabilities to forecast and analyze impacts related to production management decisions. In this context, the paper analyzes the state of the art of Digital Twins and their decision support through a systematic literature review. The novelty introduced in this work consists of a conceptual framework for the roles of Digital Twins with respect to decision support in Production Planning and Control. The framework first builds on the functional characterization of Digital Twins, which provides a set of use cases to describe how a Digital Twin can work to support decisions; then, the target applications are further analyzed, including process planning, production planning, scheduling, production control and dynamic scheduling. Finally, in light of Digital Twin capabilities extending traditional simulation modeling, this work outlines major characteristics and research directions in terms of the adoption of Digital Twins.

title: Multi-Scale Attention-Enhanced YOLO26 for Wind Power Equipment Surface Defect Detection
container-title: Applied Sciences
f3e3d977ada41c835585767e11bd2d4919f9b406.abstract: Surface defects in wind power equipment exhibit substantial variations in scale, morphology, texture, and orientation and are frequently affected by complex backgrounds, illumination changes, and surface contamination, posing challenges to reliable visual inspection. This study proposes a YOLO26-based surface defect detection framework that integrates multi-scale contextual modeling, spatial–channel collaborative attention, and directional feature recalibration. Specifically, the original SPPF module is replaced with SPPSCCAP to combine multi-scale pooling, spatial–channel reconstruction, and global contextual information. CADP-SCSA is subsequently introduced to jointly model directional spatial information and inter-channel dependencies, while ELA-B modules are embedded before the P3, P4, and P5 detection heads to preserve horizontal and vertical positional information. Experiments were conducted on a public wind power equipment dataset containing 9583 images and 22,856 annotated instances across seven defect categories. Under a unified training and testing protocol, comprehensive ablation experiments demonstrate that the effects of the three enhancement mechanisms are not simply additive. Among the evaluated configurations, the three-module Model H achieved the highest values across the four reported detection metrics, with a precision of 0.9120, a recall of 0.8860, an mAP50 of 0.9060, and an mAP50–95 of 0.6660. Compared with the baseline model, these results represent improvements of 5.57, 8.99, 8.63, and 9.44 percentage points, respectively. These findings demonstrate the importance of layer-specific feature enhancement and module coupling in multi-class defect detection and provide a practical basis for vision-based inspection and condition assessment of wind power equipment.

title: Digital Media Use Patterns and Correlates of Heavy Use Among Children in Türkiye: A Nationally Representative Cross-Sectional Analysis
container-title: Children
48971878edd1e6611848fdc87dda69d4a42ae1b9.abstract: Background/Objectives: Digital-media use is widespread among children, but nationally representative evidence on heavy use across media domains in Türkiye remains limited. We examined use patterns, associated characteristics, and profiles of heavy use. Methods: This cross-sectional study analyzed microdata from the 2024 Survey on Information and Communication Technology Usage by Children conducted by the Turkish Statistical Institute (n = 7072; ages 6–15 years). Heavy use was defined as ≥4 h/day within a media domain. Survey-weighted modified Poisson regression with household-clustered robust standard errors estimated adjusted prevalence ratios (aPRs). Classification and Regression Tree (CART) analysis identified profiles of heavy use in any domain on weekdays or weekends. Results: Internet use was reported by 91.3% of children. Among at-least-weekly users of each domain, heavy weekday use ranged from 6.9% for gaming to 17.4% for smartphones. In the full sample (n = 7072), 30.4% met the heavy-use criterion in at least one domain on weekdays or weekends. Boys had a higher adjusted prevalence of heavy weekday gaming (aPR 3.33, 95% CI 2.44–4.55). Among at-least-weekly smartphone users, 58.6% reported at least one contextual use behavior; 63.5% of at-least-weekly gamers reported at least one gaming-related difficulty. Perceived reductions in reading (34.4%) and studying (33.3%) were most common. CART identified the highest prevalence among smartphone-owning adolescents aged 14–15 years who did not read regularly. Conclusions: Heavy use varied by media domain and child characteristics. Considering media domains, use contexts, and perceived everyday impact may complement duration-based assessment; combined total screen time was not measured.

title: Convolutional LSTM and Self-Attention Networks in PyTorch for Decade-Ahead Forecasting of Land-Cover Time Series
container-title: Geomatics
5bcd22ac46f796abeff6f2bec51d576b5b6cad32.abstract: Forest cover in Vietnam has changed profoundly since 1990 under agricultural expansion, urbanization and plantation programs. This study used the 31 annual JAXA High-Resolution Land-Use and Land-Cover maps of Vietnam (v21.09, 1990–2020) to quantify the dynamics of natural forest and plantations and to forecast land cover to 2030 with two deep learning models implemented in PyTorch: a convolutional long short-term memory network (ConvLSTM) and a Temporal Vision Transformer (ViT). The 250 m Level-2 maps were grouped into seven classes, and their area bias relative to the 30 m maps was quantified. The models were trained on data up to 2010 and validated by hindcasting the 2020 map against persistence, CA–Markov and Random Forest baselines. Natural forest covered 139,100 km2 in 1990 and 136,800 km2 in 2020, and plantations covered 66,600 and 49,400 km2, respectively, with the largest net forest losses in the Central Highlands and the northern uplands. In the hindcast, the ViT predicted change best (figure of merit 0.203, against 0.182 for the ConvLSTM and 0.165 for the Random Forest), whereas the Random Forest reached the highest overall accuracy (0.746); all trained models predicted about 79,000 km2 of plantation for 2020, against 49,400 km2 observed after the sharp plantation decrease in 2017–2018. Having learned the dynamics of 1990–2010, the models forecast for 2030 a further forest loss of 4–5%, with natural forest declining by 11–14% to 117,200–122,100 km2 and plantations expanding by 13–21% to 56,000–59,700 km2, a scenario in which the plantation expansion of the 2000s resumes.

title: Where Do We Look? Visual Attention Competition Between Hyper-Salient Objects and AI-Generated Virtual Endorsers in Generative Artificial Intelligence Advertising
container-title: Journal of Eye Movement Research
36fc050f60ce8845ba8db20a6617fcac6439e5ea.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) advertising, defined as advertising content created or substantially assisted by generative AI systems (AIGC), has introduced new visual features that combine algorithmically generated objects with human-like representations. Hyper-salient objects, defined by exaggerated perceptual prominence and semantic incongruity, and AI-generated virtual endorsers, represented by human-like AI-created figures, have become increasingly common in such advertisements. However, little is known about how these distinct visual cues compete for consumers’ limited attentional resources when presented together. Drawing on visual attention and scene perception perspectives, this study investigated how hyper-salient objects and AI-generated virtual endorsers influence visual attention allocation in AI-generated advertising. A 2 (hyper-salient object: present vs. absent) × 2 (AI endorser: present vs. absent) between-subjects eye-tracking experiment was conducted with 160 participants in a controlled laboratory setting using static AI-generated advertisements. Eye movements were recorded, and memory was assessed using signal detection measures (d′) from a recognition task involving target and distractor advertisements. Advertising attitude and product trust were measured using established scales. Results from linear and generalized linear mixed-effects models showed that hyper-salient objects increased early fixation probability and attracted a larger dwell time proportion, demonstrating strong attentional capture. AI-generated endorsers also attracted attention when presented alone, but their proportional attention share decreased when hyper-salient objects were simultaneously present. The effects of these visual elements on memory and product trust were conditional on their co-occurrence rather than uniform across conditions. Within the specific set of experimentally constructed stimuli and four sampled product categories, this research contributes to AIGC advertising literature by developing a visual competition perspective on how multiple AI-generated visual cues interact under limited attentional capacity, offering implications for designing effective generative AI advertisements.

title: From Co-Evolution to Conversion: Reassessing the Digital–Green Nexus for Urban Sustainability in Major Chinese Cities
container-title: Sustainability
a1f7d0d61261ddda1baddeeb3fd0b3b6b6f9e9ab.abstract: Digitalization and green development have advanced together across major Chinese cities, but aggregate co-movement does not necessarily imply a robust positive association within cities. Using a balanced panel of 100 major Chinese cities (2012–2023), we construct multidimensional digitalization (DIG) and green development (GDI) indices and combine spatial and distributional analysis with a common five-specification comparison, covariance decomposition, and robustness checks. Both index means increase, while DIG dispersion widens and GDI dispersion narrows. The correlation between the annual mean DIG and GDI is 0.991 but falls to 0.517 after linear detrending, and to 0.130 for annual changes. Persistent city differences and common-year movement account for 48.04% and 51.67% of pooled covariance, respectively, whereas the two-way residual accounts for 0.30%. The two-way fixed-effects estimate is negative but statistically imprecise (β = −0.181, p = 0.150). Dimension-specific and alternative weight estimates are not uniform, cautioning against interpreting the composite result as evidence that every environmental outcome responds identically. We describe this pattern as a co-evolution–conversion gap: strong system-level co-movement coexists with weak or uncertain average within-city alignment. The findings support assessing energy, pollution, and ecological outcomes directly rather than inferring green performance from digital capability alone. Urban policymakers should evaluate digital investment alongside direct measures of energy use, emissions, pollution, and ecological amenities, while tailoring complementary actions to local industrial and energy conditions.

title: From Green Digital Transformation to Hotel Performance: The Roles of Dynamic Capabilities, Innovation Capabilities, and Organizational Resilience
container-title: Sustainability
47f59047ef5e155956022933c0d28a4e336389e0.abstract: The hotel industry has acknowledged the growing environmental concern and recognized the significance of adopting sustainable practices. The existing literature on the hotel industry reflects a discernible gap between green digital transformation and green dynamic capabilities, green innovation capabilities, and organizational resilience. Therefore, this study aims to examine the relationships between green digital transformation, green dynamic capabilities, green innovation capabilities, organizational resilience, and organizational performance. Using purposive sampling, data were gathered from 329 managers working in four Chinese cities and analyzed through partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM). The findings highlight the significant positive association between green digital transformation, green dynamic capabilities and green innovation capabilities, which, in turn, are positively associated with hotel resilience. Furthermore, organizational resilience is significantly associated with process innovation, service innovation, and organizational performance. Practically, the study’s findings help encourage hotel managers to implement digital technologies to improve hotels’ efficiency and organizational performance. Moreover, the study encourages regulatory authorities to support green digitalization initiatives and improve hotels’ performances.

title: Staged sternal distraction for early thoracic expansion in Shwachman–Diamond syndrome
container-title: The Annals of The Royal College of Surgeons of England
65c78afe9e5445c1df3281d2904c83c9f0252f28.abstract: Shwachman–Diamond syndrome (SDS) is a rare inherited multisystem disorder with variable skeletal involvement; severe neonatal thoracic dystrophy is uncommon but can cause thoracic insufficiency and mimic Jeune syndrome. We report staged sternal distraction in a 5-month-old infant with a severely constricted thorax, pulmonary hypoplasia, refractory pulmonary hypertension, tracheostomy-dependent respiratory failure and an iatrogenic posterior tracheal wall injury. Subsequent trio long-read genome sequencing identified compound heterozygous pathogenic variants in SBDS, c.183_184delinsCT (p.Lys62Ter), inherited paternally, and c.258+2T>C, inherited maternally, establishing a molecular diagnosis of SDS. At presentation, the chest circumference measured 36cm, compared with an age-expected value of 41cm. The patient underwent staged median sternotomy distraction followed by stabilisation with custom fibular allograft struts. At approximately 3 months, chest circumference had increased to 41cm, peak inspiratory pressures had decreased from 40–50cm H 2 O to the mid-20cm H 2 O range, pulmonary hypertension was no longer evident on echocardiography, and the tracheal injury had healed. At 6 months, he remained on home mechanical ventilation, with peak inspiratory pressures in the upper 20cm H 2 O range. To our knowledge, operative thoracic expansion specifically for SDS-associated thoracic insufficiency has not previously been described. In carefully selected infants with severe thoracic insufficiency who are not yet candidates for conventional thoracic reconstruction, staged sternal distraction may serve as an interim strategy to achieve meaningful thoracic expansion.

title: Technology and Digital Platforms: Commutative Resilience Towards Flood Mitigation in Jalingo Metropolis
container-title: RESEARCH JOURNAL OF MASS COMMUNICATION AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY
e9df76839075ea21d3c0cd627fdee01504d4fca4.abstract: Flooding being a recurring environmental challenge, the study Explores the role of development communication and digital platforms in enhancing flood risk perception, response, and mitigation in Jalingo metropolis which significantly affect livelihood, effective communication is crucial for building community resilience. Anchored on the Extended Parallel Process Model (EPPM), the study examines how fear based messages on digital media influence public awareness and motivate protective actions against flooding. Employing a qualitative approach, the study found that digital platforms like Facebook and Twitter has transformative capacity in mobilizing urban populations for flood preparedness and response. The discussion emphasizes the need for inclusive, multi-channel communication strategies combining digital innovation with communitybased approaches to effectively mitigate flood impacts and foster sustainable development. Gaps were also identified: such as digital literacy barriers, misinformation, and limited rural engagement of digital platforms. The study concludes that integration of digital platforms with community based communication will improve community preparedness.

title: Digital Literacy Skills and Their Influence on Students’ Academic Engagement in The Information Age in Rivers State, Nigeria
container-title: RESEARCH JOURNAL OF MASS COMMUNICATION AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY
df6ad02455ba1edb5b534884c2221350b22dd61a.abstract: This study explored the influence of digital literacy skills on the academic engagement of secondary school students in Rivers State, Nigeria. In the Information Age, where digital technologies permeate everyday life, the ability to effectively use these tools is essential for meaningful learning. While students frequently engage with digital devices for communication and entertainment, their capacity to leverage these tools for academic purposes remains a concern. Descriptive survey design was adopted. The population of the study was all public senior secondary school students in Rivers State consisting of 193,436 admitted in 2024/2025 academic session. Sample was 560 public senior secondary students selected using multi-stage sampling. Instruments were Digital Literacy Skills Scale (DLSS) and Academic Engagement Questionnaire (AEQ). Both instruments were validated and showed reliability coefficients of 0.82 and 0.85. Questionnaires were administered with the help of trained assistants and data were collected. Research questions were analyzed using mean, standard deviation while the null hypotheses were tested using simple linear regression and t-tests at 0.05 significance level No significant gender differences were observed in digital literacy, whereas urban students demonstrated significantly higher academic engagement than their rural peers. Regression analysis further showed that digital literacy accounted for 38% of the variance in academic engagement. The findings highlight digital literacy as a key driver of student involvement, motivation, and participation in learning. The study recommends enhanced digital literacy training, improved ICT infrastructure, strategic integration of digital tools into teaching, and targeted support for rural schools to address engagement disparities.

title: Teacher and Education Leader Perceptions of Digital Competences and Barriers to Digital Transformation of Education
29a80daf12a554f3695a218a24649cfd18663c77.abstract: Abstract Digital transformation is reshaping teaching and learning worldwide, yet its benefits remain unevenly distributed and the competences it demands of educators are still contested. This article asks how different educational stakeholders conceptualise the competences required for effective digitalisation of teaching and learning, and what they identify as the principal obstacles to it. The study forms part of an international Erasmus+ Teacher Academy project using a shared interview protocol across partner countries; this article reports the Latvian data. Thirty-two participants - pre-service teachers, in-service teachers and educational leaders, took part in semi-structured interviews, analysed using reflexive thematic analysis. Four findings stand out. First, the competences participants named varied systematically with their position in the system: pre-service teachers emphasised operational skills, in-service teachers pedagogical integration, and leaders strategic change management; strikingly few future-oriented competences were technological. Second, language operated as a double constraint, with English proficiency governing access to tools and professional learning while a scarcity of high-quality Latvian-language resources limited classroom use. Third, artificial intelligence was experienced primarily as a challenge to assessment rather than to teaching. Fourth, barriers internal to teachers fear of error and a perceived generational divide, persisted even in well-resourced schools, and change was carried largely by early-adopting colleagues rather than institutional mandate. Together these findings indicate that investment in equipment alone will not deliver digital transformation, and that professional development, resource policy and assessment design need to be addressed as a single problem rather than three separate ones.

title: Digital Activism, Citizens’ Journalism, and Public Sphere Discourse: Patterns and Approaches of the Obidient Movement in Nigeria
container-title: RESEARCH JOURNAL OF MASS COMMUNICATION AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY
9f09cb0d7353d4da08ebcb60377e64ab56c8f510.abstract: This study examines how digital activism, citizen journalism, and public-sphere interactions shaped the communicative behaviour of the Obidient Movement between September 2022 and February 2023. Anchored in an interpretivist and constructivist qualitative framework, the study treats digital texts as the primary population through which political meanings are produced, contested, and circulated. A total of 500 texts from social media platforms and mainstream newspapers formed the dataset, from which 20 texts were purposively selected based on ideological depth, narrative richness, and symbolic relevance. Supplementary documentary sources and semi-structured interviews enhanced triangulation. The analysis revealed four major thematic patterns: mobilisation and visibility, media framing and narrative construction, forms of resistance and state repression, and the emergence of civic identity and political consciousness. Findings demonstrate that digital platforms served as powerful arenas for mass mobilisation and informal civic education, while citizen journalism functioned as a counter-hegemonic tool for challenging biased reportage and amplifying grassroots perspectives. Despite experiencing multiple forms of repression—legal, symbolic, and digital—the movement sustained resilience through strong counter-discursive strategies. The study concludes that the Obidient Movement signifies a major transformation in Nigeria’s democratic culture by expanding the digital public sphere, redefining civic identity, and illustrating how networked citizens can challenge elite power. It recommends strengthening digital rights, promoting ethical journalism, improving civic education, and institutionalising youth political participation

title: Digital rectal examination as a standalone trigger for urgent prostate cancer investigation
container-title: The Annals of The Royal College of Surgeons of England
784c65f6e39bf895768c4f13474ffc121fb7a584.abstract: Introduction The contemporary value of digital rectal examination (DRE) as a standalone trigger for urgent prostate cancer investigation remains a subject of intense debate. Increasing scepticism regarding its diagnostic sensitivity, coupled with patient reluctance, has led to declining uptake of DRE in primary care. This study evaluates the outcomes of patients referred solely based on an abnormal DRE to determine its role in identifying clinically significant disease that might otherwise be overlooked by prostate-specific antigen (PSA) screening. Methods A retrospective analysis was conducted on 2,700 patients referred via the rapid prostate cancer pathway over a 33-month period. A specific cohort of 288 patients referred primarily because of an abnormal DRE finding – with PSA levels within the age-specific reference range – was identified. Results The mean patient age was 69 years and median PSA was 2.7ng/mL. Following secondary care assessment, 56.6% (163 of 288) of patients underwent biparametric magnetic resonance imaging. Of these, 35.5% had suspicious findings (Prostate Imaging–Reporting and Data System score ≥3). Ultimately, 14.2% (41 of 288) of patients underwent transperineal biopsy. Clinically significant prostate cancer was diagnosed in 16 patients (cancer detection rate: 5.6%); all 16 underwent radical treatment. Conclusions DRE should not be superseded by PSA testing alone. Rather, it should be offered as part of a comprehensive primary care assessment, with its use determined through shared decision making that balances clinical benefit against patient acceptability. An abnormal DRE, regardless of the PSA level, necessitates urgent referral to a rapid access urology pathway.

title: Media Convergence Influence on the Behaviour and Attention Span of Adolescents in Select Secondary Schools in Rivers State
container-title: RESEARCH JOURNAL OF MASS COMMUNICATION AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY
2824e66b073446102846e9703370d3d1335ea910.abstract: The evolution of digital media and the convergence of multiple platforms have profoundly influenced adolescent behaviour and cognitive functioning. This study examined the impact of media convergence on the behaviour and attention span of adolescents in selected secondary schools in Rivers State, Nigeria. Employing a survey research design, data were collected from 330 students across three secondary schools using structured questionnaires and teacher interviews. Findings indicate that 60% of respondents reported high daily exposure to online media, with the majority acknowledging that media use affects focus, reduces study time, and influences classroom behaviour. The results highlight a significant relationship between prolonged media exposure and decreased attention span, increased distractibility, and altered behavioural patterns. The study concludes that while digital media can enhance learning opportunities, excessive exposure poses risks to adolescents’ cognitive development and academic performance. Recommendations include strengthening digital literacy education, implementing screen-time regulations, and promoting balanced media use in schools. The findings provide valuable insights for educators, parents, and policymakers seeking to mitigate the adverse effects of media convergence on adolescents.

title: Generation Z Consumers’ Balance Between Online Shopping and Basic Needs in the Era of Digital Discounts
container-title: Journal of Management, Entrepreneurship, and Tourism
378e8d4cf40c626a8ba9f2194036c6f41a2a774e.abstract: The expansion of e-commerce and digital promotions has increased purchasing opportunities for Generation Z while raising concerns about balancing online shopping with essential needs. This study synthesized six empirical studies conducted in Indonesia to examine promotional purchasing influences, financial management factors, and implications for essential expenditure. A narrative literature review employed thematic synthesis of reported quantitative and qualitative findings without collecting primary data. Flash sales showed consistent positive associations with impulsive buying and purchase intention, while customer reviews were associated with purchase intention. Findings concerning fear of missing out and live shopping were less consistent across the reviewed studies. Qualitative evidence suggested that buy-now-pay-later facilities reduced the perceived immediate burden of payment and could obscure future obligations. Digital financial literacy was negatively associated with consumptive online shopping, while financial literacy and attitudes were positively associated with personal financial management. Financial socialization was linked to management indirectly through literacy rather than through a significant direct association. A conceptual framework and six propositions were developed to connect promotional stimuli, payment mechanisms, behavioral regulation, and essential-needs prioritization. Because none of the included studies directly measured essential-needs budget protection, the proposed relationships require future empirical testing using actual expenditure allocation, savings, and deferred-payment indicators.

title: Research on the Home and Community-Based Elderly Care Service Ecosystem Driven by Digital-Intelligence Empowerment
container-title: EAI Endorsed Transactions on Pervasive Health and Technology
704bfc1033491a719612352f1a08e9b4ac65ac06.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Fragmented demand records, invisible provider capacity, and weak closure verification reduce the responsiveness of home and community-based elderly care. OBJECTIVES: This paper specifies and evaluates a lightweight digital-intelligence workflow system rather than a predictive medical-diagnosis tool. The system links multi-channel demand intake, rule-based priority scoring, provider eligibility filtering, work-order state tracking, delivery verification, exception logging, and feedback closure. The architecture retains a core-provider layer, a beneficiary layer, and a four-module support system, but implements them through minimum data fields, explicit state transitions, and auditable scoring rules. METHODS: An eight-week AB/BA pilot was conducted at two community centers with 42 adults aged 65–82 and 386 valid service requests. RESULTS: Compared with the routine workflow, the supported workflow reduced mean demand-to-confirmation time from 58.4 to 36.9 min and staff coordination time from 8.9 to 6.2 min per request. On-time completion increased from 79.2% to 89.1%, while matching accuracy increased from 83.8% to 91.6%. CONCLUSION: The configuration uses ordinary tablets, office computers, spreadsheet-compatible records, role-based access, and human fallback channels, providing an implementable coordination mechanism for community elderly care.

title: Impact of Digital Media Consumption on the Emotional Well-Being of Secondary School Students in Rivers State
container-title: RESEARCH JOURNAL OF MASS COMMUNICATION AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY
d1d1b85ae2a1cd3f6aeeb07e2358e0599bea8e89.abstract: The rapid proliferation of digital media has profoundly influenced adolescents’ social and emotional experiences, raising concerns about their mental well-being. This study investigates the impact of digital media consumption on the emotional well-being of secondary school students in Rivers State, Nigeria. A survey research design was employed, collecting data from 330 students across three secondary schools using structured questionnaires, complemented by interviews with teachers. Findings reveal that a majority of students engage in high levels of digital media use, with prolonged exposure linked to mood swings, heightened anxiety, and reduced self-esteem. Teacher observations corroborate these results, highlighting social withdrawal, emotional dysregulation, and dependency on online validation. The study establishes a significant relationship between excessive digital media use and decreased emotional resilience among adolescents. While digital media can offer social connection and emotional support, unregulated engagement may negatively affect mental health. The study recommends promoting digital well-being education, parental guidance, school-based mental health resources, and offline social activities to foster balanced media consumption and enhance emotional resilience. These findings provide actionable insights for educators, parents, and policymakers seeking to support adolescents in navigating the digital environment safely.

title: Relationships Between Bladder Dysfunction, Fatigue, Quality of Life, and Mobility in People With Parkinson Disease
container-title: Journal of Women's & Pelvic Health Physical Therapy
e70d6afaeade39dc42c684c6c15744f850bbfb57.abstract: Purpose: Examine the relationship between bladder dysfunction, fatigue, quality of life (QoL), and mobility in people with Parkinson Disease (PD). Methods: In this cross-sectional secondary analysis, bladder dysfunction was measured by the Unified Parkinson’s Disease Rating Scale bladder function score (UPDRS bladder function scores, item 1.10). The Parkinson’s Fatigue Scale-16 measured fatigue. The Parkinson’s Disease Questionnaire measured physical and nonphysical QoL. The 10-M Walk Test and timed up and go (TUG) measured functional mobility, and average step-count measured real-world mobility. Associations of the UPDRS bladder function scores with fatigue, QoL, and mobility were determined using Spearman-rank correlations. Differences between UPDRS bladder function scores 0 to 1 (normal-to-slight) and 2 to 4 (mild-to-severe) groups were determined using independent t tests. Results: Twenty-nine people with PD with mild-to-moderate disability (Hoehn and Yahr 2-4) were included. The sample was 66% male (69.4 ± 9.4 years old, Hoehn and Yahr of 2.2 ± 0.7). UPDRS bladder function scores were mild-to-severe in 44.8%. Fair-to-moderate correlations were present between UPDRS bladder function scores and fatigue (ρ = 0.48, P = .009), overall QoL (ρ = 0.50, P = .008), physical QoL (ρ = 0.56, P < .001), nonphysical QoL (ρ = 0.39, P = .038), 10-M Walk Test (ρ = 0.42, P = .023), and the TUG (ρ = 0.42, P = .023). Fatigue and QoL were worse in the mild-to-severe bladder dysfunction group than in the normal-to-slight group ( P ≤ .05), but mobility did not differ significantly between groups. Discussion: Self-reported bladder dysfunction was correlated with fatigue, QoL, and functional mobility, but not real-world mobility, in people with PD. These relationships emphasize the role of rehabilitation clinicians in addressing interconnected symptoms and support further research into the implications for bladder screening in clinical care.

title: “Saying ‘I Love you’ With Icons”: Imagined Communication and the Relational Production of Digital Offerings
container-title: OMEGA - Journal of Death and Dying
8c5c02f82ff08536ec0b46ccb3d564cee134b16d.abstract: This paper explores the motivations, ritual practices, and cultural meanings of digital offerings on Chinese virtual memorials. Drawing on four years of online observation, auto-ethnography, and in-depth interviews, it finds digital offerings feature distinctive persistence, traceability, networked circulation and personalization. These affordances reshape mourning into an individualized, frequent, and flexible mediated practice, foregrounding mourner ’ s agency. Their circulation transforms private grief into a networked relational practice that challenges the utilitarian logic of traditional rituals. In this process, digital offerings and virtual memorials function as collective coping mechanisms, enabling bereaved parents to form affective communities grounded in shared trauma. Meanwhile, they are embedded in the digital economy of symbolic goods, producing intersections between emotional expression, affective labor, and commercial logics. Overall, as a mediated relational practice, digital offerings facilitate self-healing and filial piety while fostering connective mourning and social support networks, offering new possibilities for emotional communication and relationship building in China.

title: Microbial contamination and decontamination of reusable digital intraoral imaging equipment: a narrative review
container-title: Frontiers in Oral Health
a4f9861c3eee1fe1a457c4e473a1eda16cca4d01.abstract: Digital intraoral radiography relies on reusable solid-state sensors and photostimulable phosphor (PSP) plates that cannot be heat-sterilized, so infection control depends largely on single-use barriers and on disinfectants the equipment can tolerate. This narrative review synthesizes laboratory and clinical evidence on microbial contamination of reusable digital intraoral imaging equipment, the mechanisms by which barriers fail, and the balance between antimicrobial efficacy and device compatibility. Across the available clinical studies of barrier-protected PSP plates, contamination was reported in roughly 17% to 73% of plates and was frequently associated with handling-related factors, including perforation, incomplete sealing and non-aseptic removal, rather than with the barrier material alone. The exterior of intact envelopes becomes heavily contaminated during brief intraoral use, identifying removal technique as a distinct contamination route; these findings are integrated into a proposed six-stage contamination pathway. Evidence for solid-state sensors is largely limited to barrier-perforation testing, and data on cables, scanner internals and computer peripherals remain sparse. Studies of lead aprons and thyroid shields, mostly from non-dental settings and therefore contextual, report frequent contamination, now alongside 2023–2024 guidance recommending against routine shielding. Laboratory studies indicate that antimicrobial efficacy and plate compatibility vary independently across agents and plate brands, so the two must be evaluated together. Contamination indicates a plausible transmission pathway but does not demonstrate patient infection, and no study identified in this review has linked imaging equipment to a documented infection. The review concludes with an evidence-gap matrix and outlines emerging approaches to objective contamination surveillance.

title: Design and Application of an IDSS for Physical Education Evaluation in the Digital Era
container-title: International Journal of Decision Support System Technology
3c1b39694603652c0120b9cc63607178b6b9b01c.abstract: In the digital era, traditional physical education evaluation methods—often paper-based, subjective, and delayed—fail to support timely and evidence-based instructional decisions. To address this gap, an intelligent decision support system (IDSS) tailored for physical education evaluation in smart educational environments was proposed. The system integrated a neural network for data processing, an expert system for rule-based reasoning, and a multi-criteria autonomous advantage model to identify individual strengths and improvement areas. It integrated multisource student performance and behavioral signals collected from digital educational environments to generate dynamic and personalized evaluation results. Through system analysis and empirical testing, the proposed IDSS is shown to have the potential to enhance objectivity, reduce evaluator bias, and support teaching and learning decisions. This work contributes a practical IDSS framework for educational applications, aligning with the evolving needs of intelligent, data-driven decision support.

title: From E-Government to Algorithmic Governance
container-title: International Journal of Public Administration in the Digital Age
0eae7149493e7d69288710ba95f9b1b3dd17024d.abstract: Digital governance and digital-era governance mark a major paradigm shift in how the state and local administration function, driven by the growing role of digital technologies in government organization, state operations, and state-citizen relations. Although the literature has addressed e-government, digital transformation, and technology-enabled public management comprehensively, gaps remain in conceptual foundations, theoretical synthesis, and methodological approaches. This paper presents a bibliometric and science-mapping overview of digital governance studies from 2011 to 2025 to identify the field's intellectual development, collaborative structure, topical directions, and emerging research areas. By doing so, the study aims to move beyond descriptive evaluations and provide a theoretically informed account of governance transformation in the digital and algorithmic age.

title: Empathy-driven remote pedagogy in accounting education − a bilingual model for student engagement and digital resilience
container-title: Information and Learning Sciences
0d74c15ca76677cb5f8a41797811042843685f77.abstract: Purpose This paper presents the empathy-based bilingual digital pedagogy (EBBDP) model, a practice-informed framework developed through the author’s experience in remote teaching of accounting and taxation during and after the COVID-19 pandemic. It aims to show how pedagogical empathy can be translated into bilingual and digitally supported teaching practices intended to strengthen engagement, accessibility and emotional safety in virtual learning environments, particularly within technical education. Design/methodology/approach This study adopts a reflective-practice methodology grounded in lived teaching experience within Portuguese vocational and professional training. It draws on pedagogical documentation, autoethnographic reflection and iterative adaptation of instructional strategies. The model integrates empathy, bilingual inclusivity and digital co-creation as central pedagogical pillars, illustrated through concrete examples using tools such as Google Workspace, Canva, Padlet and ChatGPT to support collaborative learning and formative assessment. Findings The reflective analysis identifies structured emotional check-ins, bilingual scaffolding, digital co-creation and multimodal assessment as practices through which pedagogical empathy may support accessibility, belonging and sustained participation. These practice-based interpretations are presented as conceptual propositions for future empirical testing rather than as measured effects. Originality/value This paper contributes to post-pandemic digital pedagogy by positioning empathy as a core teaching competence rather than a soft skill. It offers a conceptually grounded yet practice-driven model that translates pedagogical empathy into a structured set of bilingual, relational and digitally supported teaching practices, thereby bridging theory and classroom experience in technical education.

title: Emotional polyphony in Milan Kundera’s The Joke : a computational analysis of narrative voices through SenticNet
container-title: Digital Scholarship in the Humanities
616a8df0e6d6145d5b6d0c4736c874740f55ad5d.abstract: Abstract This article investigates the affective architecture underlying narrative polyphony in Milan Kundera’s The Joke through a computational analysis of emotion dynamics. The study addresses a central narratological question: how distinct narrative voices construct differentiated emotional domains within a polyphonic framework. To explore this issue, the text is segmented according to Kundera’s four first-person narrators, and each segment is examined through SenticNet-based emotion modeling. For every narrative voice, the four core affective dimensions of the Hourglass of Emotion (attitude, introspection, sensitivity, temper) are computed together with a polarity-based sentiment index. The resulting trajectories are visualized across the novel, and key turning points—such as Ludvik’s deportation to the labor camp—are marked to assess how major events shape affective modulation. Radar charts and comparative boxplots reveal clear divergences among the emotional profiles of the narrators, indicating that Kundera’s polyphony operates not only on stylistic or ideological levels but also through the distribution of distinct affective regions. These results demonstrate that computational emotion analysis can operationalize interpretive intuitions commonly addressed through qualitative close reading, offering an empirically grounded perspective on the internal architecture of polyphonic fiction. The study highlights the interpretive potential of affective computing in literary analysis and suggests possible extensions to broader corpora of Central European narrative.

title: Headedness, overlap, and salience: the multi-dimensional tension in English blends
container-title: Digital Scholarship in the Humanities
cb7dcc4bf0a6c32ea1e9c657f57c8b8b7bd4bf5c.abstract: Abstract A recent contribution to Digital Scholarship in the Humanities by Meng and Hilpert (‘Measuring the Semantic Headedness of English Blends with Token-Based Semantic Vector Space Modelling: A Corpus-Based Study’, 2024, 39 (4), 1075–1091) applied distributional semantics to English lexical blends but conflated three conceptually independent dimensions: semantic headedness, semantic overlap, and semantic salience, while relying on static word embeddings that cannot adequately handle polysemy. To address these gaps, the present study distinguishes the three metrics and quantifies them using the contextualized language model BERT on a dataset of eighty-seven English blends. The research findings are threefold: (1) semantic headedness is right-headed in 52.9% and left-headed in 47.1% of the eighty-seven blends; semantic overlap is left‑oriented in 43.7% and right‑oriented in 56.3% of the eighty-seven blends; (2) in terms of semantic salience, 56.3% of the eighty-seven blends are left-oriented and 43.7% are right-oriented; (3) the three metrics exhibit systematic directional inconsistency, revealing that English blends function as multi-dimensional semantic objects in which categorical inheritance, distributional similarity, and contextual prominence need not converge, which calls for a more empirically grounded and multi-faceted account of blend semantics. Theoretically, our findings corroborate the gradient view of Meng and Hilpert, moving blend research beyond taxonomic classification towards a usage-grounded, multi-dimensional model that requires a multivariate approach. Methodologically, the study demonstrates the necessity of cross-validating conclusions using multiple metrics in morphological research, illustrating how digital methods can address longstanding problems in word formation.

title: The Relationship Between Fatigue and Quality of Life for Patients Participating in a Cancer Survivor Program
container-title: Oncology Rehabilitation in Practice
2154c40688bb7cf95991c5eb9c7510d37020cf5e.abstract: Introduction: The purpose of this chart review was to examine differences in fatigue and quality of life following cancer treatment based on gender, race, age, cancer type, and referral for rehabilitation services. Methods: Ninety-one patient charts were reviewed for demographic variables, cancer type, rehabilitation referral, and baseline scores on the Brief Fatigue Inventory (BFI) and Reintegration to Normal Life Index (RNLI). Group differences were analyzed using the Mann–Whitney U test, and correlations between fatigue and quality of life were assessed using Pearson’s correlation (p < 0.05). Results: Participants included 65 females (71%) and 26 males (29%), with 73% identifying as Black, 26% White, and 1% Asian. Most participants were ≥55 years (72%). Breast cancer was the most common diagnosis (44%). Forty percent required rehabilitation referral at enrollment. A significant negative correlation was observed between BFI and RNLI scores (r = –0.584, p < 0.05). Significant differences in fatigue and quality of life were found based on rehabilitation referral and age, with younger participants reporting greater fatigue and lower quality of life. No significant differences were identified based on gender, race, or cancer type. Discussion: Fatigue is strongly associated with reduced quality of life in cancer survivors. Functional limitations appear to contribute to this relationship, particularly among younger participants. The high proportion of minority participants provides important insight into an underrepresented population. Conclusion: Addressing fatigue and functional limitations is critical to improving quality of life outcomes in cancer survivorship programs.

title: DWSA: Dynamic-Weighting and Self-Attention Intelligent Framework Enables High-Sensitivity SERS Discrimination of Ultratrace Volatile Organic Compounds
container-title: Analytical Chemistry
26c3afe71d69c9e34655832cc31d09b5f4e8833a.abstract: Abstract Real-time on-site discrimination of ultratrace volatile organic compounds (VOCs) via surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) is fundamentally challenged by spectral complexity and the limited generalization of single models. Here, we develop a high-performance 3D porous material (PM) based on biopolymer-silver nanocomposites, providing a reliable platform for trace gas enrichment and signal enhancement. Moving beyond material optimization, we pioneer a novel dynamic-weighting and self-attention intelligent framework (DWSA) to integrate convolutional neural network (CNN)-based global feature extraction with k-nearest neighbors (KNN)-based local similarity reasoning. The hybrid algorithm overcomes the bottlenecks of traditional static ensemble methods; its core innovation lies in a confidence-driven dynamic weighting strategy, which adaptively balances the contributions of both models based on prediction reliability rather than fixed ratios. This underlying mechanism is augmented by a self-attention module that adaptively recalibrates feature weights to focus on key molecular vibrational fingerprints, effectively filtering noise and enhancing interpretability. Based on this hybrid framework, we propose a detection strategy with potential for portable SERS applications, featuring rapid spectral acquisition, intelligent identification, and QR-code-based traceability. This study promotes the practical application of SERS technology in on-site environmental monitoring by integrating ultra-high gas adsorption efficiency with the development of a novel intelligent algorithm.

title: Platform governance and digital property rights in virtual real estate: volatility, user entitlements and regulatory accountability
container-title: Journal of Information, Communication and Ethics in Society
c0442f68df21a1e431c072344c8b3b7e8d75cdcf.abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine how platform governance shapes the content and durability of user entitlements in virtual real estate. It defines virtual real estate narrowly as spatially delimited, platform-mediated parcels in persistent virtual worlds, whether recorded in a proprietary database or linked to a blockchain token. This study asks how access, exclusion, transfer, persistence and redress are distributed among users and platform operators and how uncertainty in those entitlements can contribute to market fragility and regulatory risk. Design/methodology/approach This study combines a targeted interdisciplinary review with comparative legal analysis of disputes and legal developments directly relevant to virtual land and digital property. Bragg v Linden Research and Evans v Linden Research are treated as core virtual-land cases; AA v Persons Unknown, Ruscoe v Cryptopia and the Property (Digital Assets etc) Act 2025 are used as broader digital-property comparators. Platform materials and descriptive post-boom market indicators are used for context. This study does not claim a causal econometric estimate of governance effects on prices. Findings Virtual real estate is governed through layered entitlements rather than a single ownership rule. Technical control, platform contract terms and external legal remedies may diverge, and transfers can occur through platform databases, in-game mechanisms, blockchain transactions or informal account and credential transfers. The 2021 NFT/metaverse boom is therefore treated as a historically exceptional episode rather than a representative market baseline. Post-boom evidence shows that leading platforms remain operational and retain user or creator activity, while land prices have fallen sharply; these observations support caution about market stability but do not by themselves identify governance uncertainty as the cause of price movements. Originality/value This study contributes a governance-centred account of virtual real estate that separates virtual land from virtual assets generally and distinguishes property-like expectations from legally enforceable entitlements. Its regulatory contribution is correspondingly narrower: it identifies entitlement disclosure, notice of material rule changes, transfer and portability safeguards, dispute resolution and platform accountability as mechanisms that can reduce avoidable uncertainty without assuming that virtual land is legally equivalent to physical real estate.
