title: FREELANCING SERVICES AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP DEVELOPMENT IN THE DIGITAL ERA: EVIDENCE FROM FREELANCE TECHNICIANS IN KARU, NASARAWA STATE, NIGERIA
container-title: International Journal of Entrepreneurship and Forensic Management Research
ecac2efef55f186306c65175696bd4e1d3230d56.abstract: The rapid growth of digital technology is creating new opportunities for individuals to transform technical skills into sustainable entrepreneurial ventures. Against this background, this study examined the effect of freelancing services on entrepreneurship development in the digital era among freelance technicians in Karu Local Government Area, Nasarawa State, Nigeria. Specifically, it examined the effects of digital technical services and online freelance market participation on entrepreneurship development. The study was anchored on Effectuation Theory and adopted a survey research design. A population of 120 freelance technicians was used for the analysis, with census sampling specified. Data were collected through a structured questionnaire and analysed using descriptive statistics and multiple regression analysis with SPSS Version 28. The results showed that digital technical services recorded a mean of 4.18 and a standard deviation of 0.61, while online freelance market participation recorded a mean of 3.94 and a standard deviation of 0.67. Entrepreneurship development had a mean of 4.06 and a standard deviation of 0.63. The regression model reported an R² of 0.679, indicating that the two independent variables jointly explained 67.9% of the variation in entrepreneurship development. Digital technical services (B = 0.514, t = 7.139, p < .001) and online freelance market participation (B = 0.356, t = 4.944, p < .001) were reported as positive and statistically significant predictors. The study recommends integrating freelancing into entrepreneurship education, improving digital infrastructure, and expanding business support for freelance technicians.

title: Revisiting Load-Stepping in Digital Photoelasticity: A Comparative Framework Bridging Hardware, Computation, and Emerging Paradigms
container-title: Applied Sciences
6969b11022565952948f671189104dfebc11239b.abstract: This work presents a comprehensive analysis of the load stepping method in digital photoelasticity, examined through four complementary perspectives: the classical formulation of load stepping, its extension using polarized-camera technology, a computational hybrid strategy, and exploratory deep learning approaches. Motivation arises from the need to quantify stress fields with greater robustness in contexts where experiments produce multiple fringe map displacements, as occurs under increasing load conditions. This approach aims to overcome the limitations of conventional phase-shifting techniques and lookup-table-based strategies while paving the way for new methodologies capable of generating multiple fringe displacements within a single-shot acquisition framework. The methodology combines synthetic simulations, experimental acquisitions with polarized array and color cameras, and a recent high-sensitivity technique for generating reference fringe-order maps. Demodulated stress fields are compared against these references using standard performance metrics such as MSE, PSNR, SSIM, and the maximum reliably recovered fringe order. The results demonstrate that while the classical approach remains theoretically sound, the polarized-camera update simplifies acquisition, the hybrid strategy reduces optical requirements through computational reconstruction, and deep learning shows promising adaptability to complex and irregular fringe patterns.

title: Exploring How Authenticity Is Constructed in Digital Technology-Supported Pre-Service Teacher Education: A Scoping Review
container-title: Education Sciences
5aace7b453303a8ce6ec9a66c34c681320e9ee3e.abstract: Digital technologies are increasingly used to create practice-oriented learning experiences in pre-service teacher education, yet authenticity is often treated as a presumed feature of technology-supported practice and receives limited analysis as a pedagogical construct. This scoping review examines how authenticity is constructed in digital technology-supported pre-service teacher education and considers its potential contribution to sustainable digital teaching. Following the PRISMA-ScR guidelines, 43 empirical studies published between 2018 and 2026 were selected from Web of Science, Scopus, and ERIC and analysed using Herrington and Oliver’s nine principles of authentic learning. The findings show that digital technologies were used mainly to connect university-based preparation with professional teaching practice. Authentic contexts and activities were consistently represented, while authentic assessment, collaboration, and expert modelling were less systematically embedded. Three contribution pathways were identified: connecting digital technologies with professional practice, supporting reflective and adaptive pedagogical judgement, and strengthening transfer-oriented teacher learning. Overall, authenticity was constructed unevenly across the reviewed digital learning designs. By synthesising evidence across different technologies through a common authentic-learning framework, the review clarifies how authenticity is pedagogically constructed and identifies design areas that require greater attention in relation to sustainable digital teaching.

title: Real-Time Instance Segmentation of Deep-Sea Polymetallic Nodules with Wavelet Statistical Cross-Attention and Reverse Convolution Upsampling
container-title: Journal of Marine Science and Engineering
fe4a4341c1b3a3d1d20721c28254fedb09a3f7a3.abstract: Deep-sea polymetallic nodules are vital strategic mineral resources. However, residual low-contrast features from complex seabed conditions, densely overlapped targets and severe seabed clutter greatly degrade the accuracy and real-time performance of automatic segmentation. This paper proposes a lightweight instance segmentation model, PWC-YOLO. Firstly, a partial convolution-based C3k2-PConv module is constructed to reduce computational cost. Secondly, Wavelet Statistical Cross-Attention (WSCA) replaces the built-in self-attention of C2PSA to suppress underwater noise and enhance the feature expression of tiny nodules. Thirdly, Converse2D reverse convolution upsampling recovers lost contour details of nodules. A manually annotated dataset of Clarion–Clipperton Zone nodules is established for evaluation. Ablation experiments validate that the PWC-YOLO model reaches 95.2% BBox mAP50 and 95.8% Mask mAP50, with only 2.47 M parameters and 9.3 GFLOPs at an inference speed of 88 FPS. Comparative experiments indicate that PWC-YOLO achieves competitive mask segmentation accuracy with fewer parameters and lower computational overhead, yielding a favorable accuracy–complexity trade-off against mainstream segmentation models. Visual results verify favorable robustness within the tested deep-sea scenes, showing favorable lightweight properties with only 2.47 M parameters and 9.3 GFLOPs, which provides potential prerequisites for future lightweight deployment on underwater edge computing devices.

title: Digital Transformation and ESG Synergy in Enhancing Enterprise Market Value
container-title: Sustainability
26d2a19d3f703ea0ac7ca63b7d5c41b3225e4813.abstract: Coordinating digital transformation with environmental, social, and governance (ESG) practices is essential for corporate sustainability. Examining how this coordination affects enterprise market value clarifies the value implications of integrating the two strategies. Drawing on 26,486 firm–year observations for Chinese A-share firms during 2011–2024, this study constructs a digital transformation–ESG synergy (DESG) index using a coupling coordination degree (CCD) model that integrates annual-report digital transformation frequency and Huazheng ESG performance scores. A two-way fixed-effects model is used for estimation. The reported baseline shows a significant positive association between DESG and enterprise market value after controlling for firm characteristics and firm and year fixed effects. First-link mechanism analysis indicates that DESG is positively associated with firms’ internal conversion capacities (absorptive, innovation, and adaptive capabilities), operational green transformation, and external corporate reputation. Moderation analysis further shows that all five internal and external moderators positively shift the marginal DESG–market value slope: media coverage and green governance recognition amplify the positive association across all quartiles, whereas entrepreneurial spirit, new quality productive forces, and analyst attention exhibit threshold effects in which the marginal slope shifts from negative or null in the lowest quartile to significantly positive at the median and upper quartiles. Heterogeneity analysis further reveals that this association is more pronounced in eastern and central China and among high-technology, state-owned, and large firms. The findings provide firm-level evidence on the market value implications of digital–ESG synergy and offer theoretical and managerial implications for coordinating the two strategies.

title: Teachers’ Digital Competence and Perceived Teaching Effectiveness in Jordan: A Structure–Configuration–Enactment Perspective
container-title: Sustainability
6e00f5bd59ea1ade54c5af55c0585fb40bc132f8.abstract: Teachers’ digital competence is central to inclusive, high-quality education, yet little is known about how its dimensions relate to one another and to teachers’ perceived teaching effectiveness (PTE). Drawing on the European Framework for the Digital Competence of Educators (DigCompEdu), this study examined these relationships among public-school teachers in Jordan through a Structure–Configuration–Enactment perspective. Survey data from 729 teachers were analysed using partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM) and fuzzy-set qualitative comparative analysis (fsQCA), and semi-structured interviews with 21 teachers were analysed using reflexive thematic analysis informed by cultural–historical activity theory (CHAT). Professional engagement was positively associated with digital pedagogical competence (β = 0.711), which was associated with facilitating learners’ digital competence (β = 0.784), which in turn was associated with PTE (β = 0.468); the sequential indirect association was significant (β = 0.261), alongside a direct association between professional engagement and PTE (β = 0.412). The fsQCA identified one sufficient configuration for high PTE, combining professional engagement, digital resources, teaching and learning, digital assessment, and facilitating learners’ digital competence; no condition was necessary, and no sufficient configuration emerged for low PTE. Interviews described infrastructural, institutional, pedagogical, and systemic tensions that constrained enactment. Although cross-sectional and self-reported, the findings can inform sustainable teacher professional development aligned with Sustainable Development Goal 4.

title: Task-Specific Impacts of Cognitive Fatigue on Subjective Experience and Psychomotor Performance
container-title: Human Factors: The Journal of the Human Factors and Ergonomics Society
522c0265a8e374ae7e4e7c27de993e0dcbdc142a.abstract: Objective To determine how cognitive fatigue (CF) affects subjective experience and reaction time (RT) performance across tasks with different processing demands (simple, go/no-go, choice), and whether these effects depend on the type of fatigue-inducing mental work. Background CF is a psychobiological state of subjective exhaustion from mental effort that can compromise workplace productivity and safety. Although slowed RT is an often-observed consequence of CF, it is unclear how this compares across RT paradigms and fatigue-inducing tasks. Method Using a remotely administered experiment, 402 participants completed a 60-minute CF (Math-Memory, Stroop, Time Load Dual-Back) or control (documentary) intervention. Subjective ratings (mental fatigue, motivation) and RT performance (simple, go/no-go, choice) were assessed pre- and post-intervention. Results Relative to control, all CF tasks increased subjective fatigue ( p < .001), while motivation declined following Dual-Back and Stroop ( p ≤ .030) but not Math-Memory. Simple and choice RT slowed significantly following all CF interventions vs control ( p < .010), with the greatest choice RT slowing after Stroop ( p ≤ .032). Only Stroop produced significant go/no-go RT slowing ( p = .004). Conclusion Subjective fatigue and simple RT were broadly sensitive to CF, indicating general psychomotor slowing. Conversely, motivation and higher-complexity RT measures showed task-specific effects, perhaps reflecting overlap between fatigue-inducing and RT task demands. Application Task type is important when considering RT as a fatigue assessment tool. These findings support multidimensional (subjective and RT) CF assessments and indicate that simple RT may be effective for rapid, broad fatigue monitoring, whereas complex RT metrics may be useful when exploring task-specific executive processing effects.

title: Cognitive Digital Ocean: integration of quantum hybrid computing, digital twins and graph neural networks for bioresource and fleet management. Part 2
container-title: Fisheries
c40dddc14b2325b2b65698c06f7464e21fbbec8c.abstract: The paper presents the concept of the Cognitive Digital Ocean (CDO) – a multi level cyber physical system for managing the fishery complex, integrating quantum hybrid computing, physics informed neural networks (PINN), graph neural networks (GNN), a hierarchy of digital twins (from genome to global ocean), and fractal analysis of the spatial distribution of bioresources. Special attention is paid to the shipbuilding aspect: mathematical models of the ship power plant (SPP), controllable pitch propeller (CPP), propulsion complex, and hull hydrodynamics are presented. It is shown that solving the fundamental Millennium Problem – the Navier Stokes equations – on quantum computers opens up fundamental possibilities for hydrodynamic forecasting with a horizon of up to 30 days. The system is aimed at solving the strategic tasks of the Russian Federal Agency for Fisheries (Rosrybolovstvo) until 2030: increasing production by 25%, digital transformation, and technological sovereignty. The limitations of the applicability of quantum methods are considered and engineering workarounds are proposed.

title: An Ensemble of Small Convolutional Neural Networks for Identifying Monogeneans of the Order Dactylogyridea from Digital Photographs
container-title: Fisheries
7eeaad2074a7a0b668e812a9b036983b76ce50bf.abstract: Fish diseases pose a serious obstacle to the economic stability of aquaculture. Correct and timely identification of the causative agent is a necessary condition for carrying out veterinary and sanitary measures, making it possible to prevent mass fish mortality. However, many fish farms lack the laboratory infrastructure and specialists required for detailed analysis. This paper proposes an ensemble of three compact convolutional neural networks for identifying monogeneans of the order Dactylogyridea in photographs obtained through the eyepiece of a light microscope using a smartphone camera. The biological material used to train the neural networks was collected during studies conducted by the Southern Scientific Centre of the Russian Academy of Sciences (SSC RAS) in southern Russia in 2019-2026.

title: Digital Transformation, Teaching Strategies, Critical Thinking, and Mathematics and Science Education
container-title: Journal of Teaching and Learning
2de17da4f602c26e28f1cac36a0fd1f6ec4d9dde.abstract: This issue focuses on digital transformation, teaching strategies, critical thinking, mathematics education, science education, and several additional topics. We begin with four articles on digital transformation. The articles examine Xuexitong for English learning, a component-based model of students' readiness to engage with digital platforms, the use of educational technology to enhance student performance in an English for Academic Purposes course, and the effectiveness of a distance teaching practicum program. Then, we present three articles on teaching strategies. The articles explore feminist pedagogy, the flipped classroom model, integration of humour into the classroom, and teacher effectiveness. We then share three articles on critical thinking. They investigate the Critical Thinking Assessment Scale-Short Form, embedding fiction in case studies within a non-literature course, and critical thinking skills. We continue with three articles on mathematics education. The articles examine integration of digital manipulatives in early childhood mathematics, Indonesia’s Pancasila Learner Profile Strengthening Project, and student achievement. Then we present three articles on science education. They include articles on the effectiveness of guided inquiry, the impact of augmented reality learning, and the links between ethnoscience, science literacy, and digital literacy. We also present articles on race and racism, entrepreneurship education, professional learning communities, and academic calling. This issue includes two dialogue and commentary articles on Generative AI and large language models, concluding with four book reviews.

title: Improving Entrepreneurship Education through a HOTS-Based Digital Assessment Tool Infused with Prophetic Values
container-title: Journal of Teaching and Learning
1e18332e731e014381507659634e2c25de5e8b44.abstract: Entrepreneurship education requires assessments that develop higher-order thinking while encouraging ethical reflection. This study developed and evaluated a learning-oriented digital assessment tool integrating Higher-Order Thinking Skills (HOTS) with prophetic values of honesty, responsibility, transparency, and wisdom, operationalized as culturally situated expressions of virtue ethics within authentic entrepreneurship tasks and rubrics. Guided by the Analysis, Design, Development, Implementation, and Evaluation (ADDIE) model, the study used a multiphase, mixed-methods research-and-development design involving 131 undergraduates: 30 pilot participants, 71 intervention participants, and 30 comparison participants. Quantitative data were examined using descriptive statistics, reliability analysis, significance testing, and effect-size estimation; student reflections were analyzed thematically. Four experts produced an average content-validity score of 81.67%, and the instrument demonstrated strong internal consistency (Cronbach’s α = .874). Pilot usability yielded a mean score of 82.33 (SD = 12.56). Among 30 students with matched pretest and posttest data, mean HOTS performance increased from 68.20% to 83.33% (p < .05, d = .86). Reflections suggested increased attention to ethical trade-offs, but the study did not establish improvement in entrepreneurial competence or long-term ethical behaviour. Findings provide preliminary evidence of the tool’s validity, usability, and potential to support cognitively demanding, ethically reflective learning. This context-sensitive framework contributes to learning-oriented digital assessment research in values-based higher education broadly.

title: Extracorporeal Spinal Orthosis-Fixation With Progressive Distraction for Severe Spinal Tuberculosis Kyphosis: A Technical Case Series With Long-Term Follow-Up
container-title: Spine Open
272e2a2624f1f749d7f97d423bc11d44a6f4311d.abstract: Study Design: Retrospective technical case series. Objective: To describe the technical feasibility and long-term outcomes and radiographic experience of an extracorporeal spinal orthosis-fixation (ESOF) device combined with a progressive-adaptive distraction in highly selected patients with severe multilevel spinal tuberculosis (TB) kyphosis. Summary of Background Data: Severe spinal TB with extensive vertebral destruction may result in marked kyphosis, spinal shortening, and substantial bone loss. Conventional reconstruction can be technically challenging when multiple contiguous vertebral segments(≥3) and a Cobb Angle of ≥70° are involved. The feasibility of gradual deformity correction combined with progressive spinal lengthening in this severe setting has not been well described. Materials and Methods: Three patients with severe multilevel spinal TB deformity were retrospectively reviewed. They had extensive vertebral destruction involving three to seven vertebral segments and a preoperative Cobb Angle of ≥70°. Treatment consisted of anterior debridement and bone grafting, posterior placement of extra-long pedicle screws with an ESOF device, and postoperative progressive-adaptive distraction. Simultaneously, anti-TB drug treatment was administered for one and a half years before, during, and after surgery, including at the lesion site and during postoperative traction. Clinical and radiographic observations included Cobb Angle, spinal-pelvic tilt, standing height, erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR), C-reactive protein (CRP), Oswestry Disability Index (ODI), neurological status, and complications during three phases: distraction orthopedic phase, distraction osteogenesis phase, and long-term follow-up, respectively. Results: The mean preoperative Cobb Angle was 80.3°. During the initial distraction phase, lasting a mean of 71.3 days, the mean Cobb Angle decreased to 21.7°, and the mean standing height increased by 5.3 cm. During the subsequent distraction osteogenesis phase, lasting a mean of 2 years 4 months, the mean Cobb Angle was 12.7° and the mean height gain reached 7.0 cm, with radiographic evidence of new bone formation. At a mean follow-up of 12.3 years, the mean Cobb Angle was 17.0°, the mean height gain was 6.7 cm, and the mean ODI was 3.0. One patient developed a mild screw-hole infection that resolved with local wound care; two patients reported painless lumbar popping. No neurological deterioration or other major adverse event was observed. Conclusions: In this small, highly selected retrospective technical series, ESOF combined with progressive-adaptive distraction was technically feasible and was associated with substantial deformity correction and long-term maintenance of spinal alignment. These observations should be considered preliminary proof-of-concept findings rather than evidence establishing the safety or efficacy of the technique. Further studies are required to determine reproducibility, complication rates, and clinical effectiveness.

title:
Digital-Assisted
Workflow for Organic Solvent Nanofiltration:
Accelerating Process Development in Pharmaceutical Manufacturing
container-title:
Organic Process Research
& Development
8bcc4943048f4f24c69d3effbe3896cd24a258e9.abstract: Abstract Organic solvents contribute more than 80% of total process mass intensity (PMI) in pharmaceutical manufacturing. Although organic solvent nanofiltration (OSN) diafiltration processes can improve sustainability, achieving high product yield typically requires large solvent volume to operate. Here, we present a digital-assisted workflow, built on the OSN Designer framework, that enables rapid screening of OSN process configurations to identify architectures that minimize solvent consumption while maintaining API recovery. The framework integrates a solution-diffusion transport model, film theory for concentration polarization, and non-steady-state mass balances, calibrated from crossflow experiments with compound A on the Borsig oNF-3 membrane in 2-methyltetrahydrofuran. Validated with average concordance correlation coefficient (ccc) of 0.72 across steady-state and dynamic operating regimes, the model was applied without recalibration to evaluate four process configurations. A two-stage membrane cascade with closed-loop permeate recycling achieved a process mass intensity (PMI) of 7.76─a 92.4% reduction relative to the single-stage constant-volume diafiltration baseline (PMI 101.5). The formalized four-phase workflow reduces experimental effort to approximately 3 weeks from more than 6–8 months and is directly transferable to other pharmaceutical OSN systems.

title: Behind the Digital Border of Anonymity
container-title: Oxford Intersections: Borders
de7b042b65ba397c2363e6019631a5fa0ff84e45.abstract: Abstract This article was inspired by the fact that most studies on immigrants in South Korea are designed, conducted, and written by non-immigrant South Korean citizens. Such a research ecosystem could lead to under-representation and misrepresentation of immigrants’ authentic voices, as the presence of a Korean researcher could prompt immigrant research participants to conform to mainstream narratives about immigrants. This article turns to anonymous cultural expressions in online spaces as an alternative research strategy that bypasses this bias and allows a more authentic representation of immigrants in South Korean migration studies. Using a borders perspective, the article conceptualizes the process of building online immigrant communities as a process of constructing digital borders that ward off unwanted voyeurs and visitors. Based on a visual discourse analysis of memes posted on Grumpy Aliens Korea, a Facebook page run by non-Koreans, the article examines how digital borders emerge through the posting and sharing of memes, all sourced from non-Korean residents of South Korea and offering humorous but critical commentary on immigrant life. The findings highlight the irony that digital borders are needed for immigrants to materialize their own discourses within the host society.

title: Museum visitors’ acceptance of digital services in China and Russia: Extending UTAUT2 with individual-level cultural values
container-title: PLOS One
c59afbe5a0135a74ebd60d630406d58bd715a624.abstract: Museum digital services have become an important means of supporting visitors’ access to information, understanding of exhibition content, and broader museum experiences. However, the mechanisms underlying visitors’ acceptance of these services may vary across visitor groups. Drawing on a context-adapted Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology model (UTAUT2), this study incorporates three individual-level cultural values—collectivism orientation, uncertainty avoidance, and long-term orientation—to examine acceptance intention toward museum digital services in China and Russia. The model was tested using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) with survey data from China (n = 316) and Russia (n = 307). Measurement invariance of composites (MICOM) and PLS multigroup analysis (PLS-MGA) were conducted to assess between-sample differences. Performance expectancy, effort expectancy, social influence, facilitating conditions, and hedonic motivation all had significant positive effects on acceptance intention in both samples. The PLS-MGA results showed no significant between-sample differences in the effects of performance expectancy or social influence. Hedonic motivation had a significantly stronger effect in the Chinese sample, whereas effort expectancy and facilitating conditions had stronger effects in the Russian sample. The latter two differences should nevertheless be interpreted cautiously because compositional invariance was not established for these constructs. Collectivism strengthened the effect of social influence, uncertainty avoidance strengthened the effects of effort expectancy and facilitating conditions, and long-term orientation strengthened the effects of performance expectancy and hedonic motivation. None of the five moderating effects differed significantly between the two samples. These findings show that acceptance intention toward museum digital services is jointly shaped by functional benefits, ease of use, social cues, available support, experiential value, and visitors’ individual cultural value orientations. The study provides evidence of both shared acceptance mechanisms and sample-specific path differences and offers a basis for visitor segmentation and the refinement of museum digital services.

title: Paying for clinical AI: The bill is not the cost
container-title: PLOS Digital Health
9315e1ba4c01711ff5c284649736bf81b882f421.abstract: Clinical AI is increasingly integrated into electronic health record workflows, but its cost is difficult to define. Health systems may pay through usage-based services, subscription or enterprise licenses, local hosting, or combinations of these approaches. Usage-based pricing introduces a distinct problem because billing units such as tokens or billable sessions are vendor-defined and may vary across data types, languages, and over time. Fixed licensing agreements can make vendor charges more predictable, while locally hosted AI models shift spending toward infrastructure and personnel. Regardless of the payment structure, the full resources required to use and maintain AI, including engineering, validation, oversight, and rights to clinical data, are difficult to capture. As the complexity of multimodal and agentic systems increases, so will that of the payment structures. Health systems will need to proactively develop ways to accurately measure the cost of AI use, evaluate its clinical value, and negotiate agreements with AI vendors that allow for regular reassessment of prices and terms. Doing so will help ensure that AI does not become yet another driver of healthcare spending detached from value delivered.

title: Role of Speech-Language Pathologists Working With Individuals With Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder: A Scoping Review of Countries Within the Mutual Recognition Agreement
container-title: Perspectives of the ASHA Special Interest Groups
be626ff04804cc195b52caf8ee7d4af16c8dd274.abstract: Background: Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) is a prevalent neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by inattention, hyperactivity, and impulsivity, which can have a significant impact on an individual's functioning. Speech-language pathologists (SLPs) within the United Kingdom, the United States, Canada, New Zealand, Australia, and Ireland, with their expertise in communication disorders, could play a crucial role in the assessment, intervention, and management of ADHD-related communication. The authors explored the current role of SLPs in the assessment and management of individuals with ADHD within multidisciplinary teams across six countries. Specifically, how do the policies and practices of Mutual Recognition Agreement (MRA) countries define and support the role of SLPs in ADHD management, and what lessons can be applied to the Australian context? Method: This study performed a scoping review of literature from MRA countries plus research published in peer-reviewed journals in English within the past 20 years that references ADHD and the role of the SLP. Content analysis categorized the data into seven themes. Results: The search found 17 articles relevant to the research question and five guidelines from MRA countries. Of the MRA countries, all had a practice guideline; New Zealand shares a practice guideline with Australia. Conclusions: Contemporary research indicates that SLPs are rarely included explicitly in the management of ADHD across the lifespan. Recommendations are made for the potential role and scope of practice of the SLP when working with these individuals.

title: COMPETENCIA DIGITAL DOCENTE Y APOYO AL APRENDIZAJE EN EDUCACIÓN SUPERIOR DEL SURESTE DE MÉXICO
container-title: FEGLININ
3b64de81fefa25584f8e458cb9be28314344abb7.abstract: University teacher preparation determines the quality of higher education, yet it lacks systematic empirical characterization in southeastern Mexico. This study examined the relationship between four dimensions of teacher preparation: perceived emotional intelligence (TMMS-24), self-efficacy (TSES), well-being and burnout (MBI-GS) and digital competence (DigCompEdu), and learning-support practices. An integrated questionnaire was administered to 21 lecturers from six higher-education institutions in Campeche and Yucatán, using nonparametric analysis and Bonferroni correction. Teacher digital competence was the most robust predictor of learning support (ρ = .641 to .719), together with personal accomplishment (ρ = .649). No differences were found between states. The findings, exploratory given the sample size, indicate that strengthening teachers' digital competence influences the quality of support offered to students.

title: A causal account of the neural origins of mental fatigue
container-title: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
2fd859fe3107277162db219db9e9ae7416ed1247.abstract: Successful goal-directed behavior often requires the exertion of effortful cognitive control processes, but it remains unclear why engaging in cognitive control is experienced as effortful and induces fatigue. Here, we tested the hypothesis that sustained activation in the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (DLPFC)—a neural substrate of cognitive control—causally induces motivational fatigue via the accumulation of prefrontal glutamate metabolites. For this purpose, we combined brain stimulation with spectroscopy imaging to assess how increasing DLPFC excitability during an effortful mental task changes the motivation for mental effort and glutamate concentrations. We found that stimulating the DLPFC during mental effort exertion improved mental performance at the cost of increased posteffort motivational fatigue, suggesting a causal role of DLPFC activation for inducing fatigue. On the neural level, DLPFC activation during effortful cognition also increased prefrontal concentrations of glutamate, which statistically explained the fatigue-induced lower motivation for mental effort. A corresponding analysis of combined glutamate–glutamine (Glx) concentrations revealed converging effects. Together, these findings provide causal evidence that enhanced DLPFC activation contributes to fatigue via neurochemical changes, supporting neuro-metabolic accounts of fatigue and offering new insights into why demanding cognitive tasks are perceived as effortful.

title: Digital Follow‐Up After Total Knee Arthroplasty: An Interview Study Among Orthopaedic Surgeons
container-title: Musculoskeletal Care
d46121443703ebfec300235edacae0469f68b017.abstract: ABSTRACT Background Traditionally, patients who undergo total knee arthroplasty (TKA) are scheduled for an in‐person routine follow‐up (RFU) regimen. Increasing pressure on orthopaedic services and growing acceptance of digital health technologies urge clinics to adopt more efficient RFU strategies. However, limited insight exists into how RFU after TKA is organised in clinical practice and under which conditions digital follow‐up is acceptable to orthopaedic surgeons. This study explored current RFU practices after TKA and examined surgeons’ perspectives on digital follow‐up. Methods A qualitative study using semi‐structured interviews was conducted with 21 orthopaedic surgeons from different healthcare institutions. Interviews were conducted digitally, transcribed verbatim, and analysed using qualitative analysis software. Two researchers independently coded the transcripts, after which the codes were compared, refined, and grouped into overarching themes. Results Four main themes emerged. (1) RFU after TKA was highly fragmented across institutions, with variation in timing, contact modality, responsible healthcare provider, and use of radiographic assessment. (2) Follow‐up visits were primarily perceived as a means to confirm uncomplicated recovery and detect complications early. (3) Digital follow‐up was viewed not as a replacement for in‐person visits but as an additional triage strategy to support decisions on physical consultation. (4) Acceptance of digital follow‐up depended on clear patient selection, predefined clinical recovery indicators, and preservation of professional and patient autonomy. Conclusion RFU after TKA is poorly standardized and institution dependent. Digital follow‐up is considered acceptable mainly as a triage mechanism if patient safety, professional autonomy, and the surgeon–patient relationship are maintained.

title: Streamlining Exploitation of Digital Archaeological Sites: A Scalable Authoring Platform to Build Digital Twins of Cultural Heritage for Research and Dissemination
container-title: Journal on Computing and Cultural Heritage
c666f4dbb34623fa94c69a2fd04a1af22e8b1112.abstract: Archaeological sites and artifacts are critical for understanding historical contexts, and maintaining their integrity is a vital undertaking. At the same time, ensuring their accessibility to enable direct study and exploration is essential for both researchers and the general public. To this aim, various works have explored the use of Digital Twins (DTs) for Cultural Heritage (CH) preservation and dissemination. However, the current state of the art remains fragmented and heterogeneous, with most approaches relying on ad hoc, case-specific solutions that are rarely reusable. In particular, existing research is often centered on individual digitization projects rather than on scalable frameworks that support the systematic creation and reuse of multiple DTs. Building on these considerations, this paper presents a scalable platform designed to streamline the construction and exploitation of archaeological DTs, enabling the rapid creation of case studies for both research and dissemination purposes. Specifically, we propose a no-code authoring environment that integrates 3D reconstructions of sites and artifacts with associated semantic information (e.g., annotations and points of interest), allowing users with limited technical expertise to create and manage DT-based experiences. The resulting case studies can be edited, organized, shared, and explored through both desktop and Virtual Reality interfaces. The platform positioning with respect to existing solutions has been explicitly investigated through a comparative analysis against representative state-of-the-art systems. In addition, the proposed approach has been evaluated through quantitative performance measurements, a comparative study, and two user studies targeting the Research and Dissemination modes, respectively. The platform was co-designed with curators from the Egyptian Museum in Turin, Italy, and validated through case studies based on two archaeological sites from Deir el-Medina, Egypt.

title: ARIP: An Interactive Framework for Digital Dissemination of Yangzhou Paper-Cutting
container-title: Journal on Computing and Cultural Heritage
fc43844f2d5709c0a3d1c561c79293d3b1e99dbf.abstract: Intangible cultural heritage (ICH) embodies collective memory and creative practices, yet many traditions rooted in manual skills and oral transmission face increasing risk under globalization. Conventional digital documentation—such as images, videos, and static visualizations—provides archival value but offers limited support for computational style analysis and lacks real-time interactivity, particularly for engaging younger audiences. To address these limitations, this paper proposes ARIP, an integrative design framework for the AI-assisted interactive dissemination of pattern-based ICH. Using Yangzhou paper-cutting as a case study, ARIP organizes four complementary design functions—AI-mediated style modeling, real-time response, interactive participation, and pattern-oriented visual constraints—within a unified implementation process. A user study with secondary school students assessed self-reported engagement using the User Engagement Scale (UES). Participants in the interactive condition reported higher engagement across the measured UES dimensions than those in the conventional digital-material condition. Qualitative feedback further suggests that the interactive experience encouraged participants to attend to the visual characteristics and culturally associated motifs of paper-cutting. These findings provide preliminary evidence for the feasibility of ARIP in the Yangzhou paper-cutting case and suggest its potential as a design reference for future AI-assisted interactive heritage applications.

title: Governing Cybersecurity in Digital Business Ecosystems: A Maturity Model Integrating Enforceable Minimum Security Baselines
800df12976465e15f866d6976bac4cee64a496d7.abstract: Abstract Maturity models are widely used instruments for assessing and guiding organizational capability, yet they assume a single organization advancing along a single-stage path. That assumption is difficult to reconcile with cybersecurity governance in digital business ecosystems, where capabilities develop unevenly across autonomous organizations, and an enforceable baseline of protection must coexist with progressive capability growth. Drawing on design science research, we present a maturity model that integrates Minimum Security Baselines (MSBs) as binding, measurable requirements that every participant must meet, directly into a multi-dimensional maturity structure. We evaluate the model in a seaport ecosystem pilot of 35 transport and logistics partners, combining a six-week field assessment with an expert evaluation using an adapted System Usability Scale. Practitioners judged the model usable, learnable, and adaptable. We position the model against established cybersecurity maturity models and recent maturity-and-resilience frameworks, and show that none couples an enforceable participation baseline with a configurable, multi-dimensional progression at ecosystem scale. The contribution is a governance mechanism that pairs an enforceable participation baseline with configurable, non-linear improvement trajectories across heterogeneous ecosystem members.

title: Dinámica de la Información Digital en español ante un riesgo emergente de salud pública: análisis exploratorio del caso hantavirus
container-title: Ciencia Latina Revista Científica Multidisciplinar
b275ec97698cae138e0cbbb79eceda5e92a9a8f1.abstract: Este artículo analiza la dinámica temporal de la información digital en español relacionada con el hantavirus como caso de un riesgo emergente de salud pública. Se realizó un estudio observacional, retrospectivo, descriptivo y exploratorio a partir de publicaciones digitales recuperadas mediante un canal de monitoreo orientado a México. De las 1,054 publicaciones en español recuperadas, 899 conformaron el corpus final, correspondiente al periodo del 7 de mayo al 8 de agosto de 2026. La delimitación temporal y la exclusión de registros sin fecha válida definieron esta selección. El volumen de publicaciones se analizó por día y los periodos de mayor actividad se identificaron a partir de la media y la desviación estándar. Se observaron tres episodios principales, con máximos de 78, 139 y 169 publicaciones. Los seis días clasificados como de alta actividad reunieron el 71.5% del corpus. El mayor volumen se registró el 19 de mayo, fecha en la que predominaron los contenidos relacionados con vigilancia o investigación epidemiológica (41.4%). La actividad informativa mostró una clara concentración temporal y una composición distinta entre episodios. Estos patrones permiten caracterizar cómo evolucionó el entorno informativo ante acontecimientos de interés para la salud pública. El volumen de publicaciones, sin embargo, no representa una medida de intensidad epidemiológica.

title: TRANSHUMANISM IN THE AGE OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE:THE SOCIO-PHILOSOPHICAL DIMENSIONS OF THE DIGITAL SOCIETY
container-title: Perspectives. Socio-political journal
b56f49cbde0e7b28ef4b717ea1f5c133a47c28c7.abstract: The relevance of the study. The rapid advancement of artificial intelligence, biotechnology, and neural interfaces underscores the need for a socio-philosophical analysis of transhumanism as a philosophical movement that advocates the possibility and desirability of technologically enhancing human nature. As digital society takes shape, transhumanist ideas are moving beyond academic discourse to become a driving force behind real-world social transformations, raising fundamentally new questions about the nature of human agency, the boundaries between the natural and the artificial, and the future social order. This article aims to examine the socio-philosophical dimensions of transhumanism in the age of artificial intelligence through an analysis of the movement’s key conceptual foundations, its interconnection with the processes of digitalisation, and a critical reflection on the associated risks and prospects. The study’s methodological framework is based on its stated aim and research objectives and adopts an interdisciplinary approach drawing on social philosophy, technology ethics, the social sciences, and media studies. The study employs comparative- historical analysis, the phenomenological method, critical discourse analysis, and a systems approach to investigating the social consequences of technological development. Research findings. The intellectual origins of transhumanism have been traced, from FM-2030’s futurist manifestos to contemporary concepts of the technological singularity and superintelligence. The analysis shows that digital society creates a distinct socio-technical environment in which transhumanist transformations assume concrete forms and give rise to new social tensions. Three key tensions within the transhumanist project have been identified: between individual freedom of self-improvement and its systemic social consequences; between techno-optimistic predictions and the real risks of humanity losing control over powerful technological systems; and between the pursuit of boundless self-improvement and the threat posed by the erosion of essential human qualities as the foundation of moral and legal equality. It is emphasised that a socio-philosophical understanding of transhumanism requires moving beyond the binary opposition between techno-optimism and technophobia in favour of a balanced, critical, and humanistically oriented approach that combines recognition of the genuine possibilities of technological progress with responsible consideration of its limits and risks.

title:
Spatially Decoupled
Donor and Acceptor Gradient Brush
Particle Blends for Mechanically Robust, Fatigue-Resistant, and Recyclable
Elastomers
container-title: ACS Nano
5afd1f7494f37d52c78cd9bbf298b087a281f489.abstract: Abstract Combining high mechanical strength, fatigue resistance, and reprocessability in a single soft material remains a fundamental challenge. Here, we report a strategy based on spatially decoupled interparticle hydrogen bonding in architecturally controlled brush particle blends. Complementary hydrogen-bonding motifs, namely poly(acrylic acid) (PAA) as donor and poly(dimethylaminoethyl methacrylate) (PDMAEMA) as acceptor, were incorporated into poly(n-butyl acrylate) (PnBA)-based gradient brush particles via surface-initiated atom transfer radical polymerization (SI-ATRP). Upon blending, reversible interparticle hydrogen bonds were formed, functioning as dynamic physical cross-links. The resulting materials exhibited tensile strengths up to 18 MPa, Young’s modulus of 95 MPa, and fracture strains exceeding 150–200%, a combination rarely achieved in physically cross-linked polymer networks. Hierarchical viscoelastic analysis revealed that the synergy between reversible interparticle bonding and architectural heterogeneity generates broad relaxation spectra and multiscale energy dissipation pathways. These features collectively underpin outstanding fatigue resistance, crack-propagation suppression, reprocessability, and thermally assisted self-healing, with annealing at 50 °C restoring approximately 90% of the original modulus and near-complete tensile strength. This work establishes spatial decoupling of hydrogen-bond donors and acceptors as a transferable design principle for durable, recyclable structural soft materials.

title: Digital Resilience-Based Course-Game Sequential Intervention for Social Participation in Stroke Survivors: Development and Usability Study
container-title: JMIR Serious Games
6e7042fe5bd2c62590b74923a404982c720c23f4.abstract: Abstract Background Social participation is a key goal of stroke rehabilitation, yet effective interventions remain limited. Existing approaches focus largely on functional training or general psychological support, rarely targeting resilience as a modifiable mechanism for enhancing social participation. Most interventions are delivered face-to-face, limiting accessibility and scalability. A theory-driven digital intervention that integrates resilience training with contextualized practice may offer a promising pathway to support social reintegration in stroke survivors. Objective This study aimed to develop a theory-driven, digital resilience-based course-game sequential intervention for improving social participation in stroke survivors and to evaluate its usability among the target population. Methods This was an intervention development and usability study. Following the first 4 steps of intervention mapping, we completed the following steps: (1) conducted a needs assessment based on prior empirical evidence identifying psychological resilience as a key determinant of social participation; (2) defined performance and change objectives grounded in the Kumpfer resilience framework, which delineates 5 protective factors (cognitive, emotional, spiritual, behavioral, and physical); (3) selected theory-based methods and practical applications; and (4) developed an intervention prototype through 4 phases: initial design integrating course learning and gamified experiential modules, expert review and refinement by an 8-member panel, development of the digital system via a WeChat mini-program, and finalization of comprehensive intervention scripts. Participants were recruited using convenience sampling from a rehabilitation hospital in Shanghai, China. Usability was evaluated with 14 stroke survivors through 5 representative tasks, the System Usability Scale (SUS), and semistructured qualitative interviews. Quantitative data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, and qualitative data were analyzed using conventional content analysis. Results The intervention comprised 2 sequential modules: a 7-session course learning module targeting 5 resilience factors, delivered weekly via narrative audio and multimodal content, and a gamified experiential module featuring a supermarket shopping scenario that enabled contextualized skill application. Each weekly course session was designed to last approximately 60 minutes. The duration of a single game session was 20 minutes. Participants had a mean age of 65.4 (SD 9.75) years, and 78.6% (11/14) had experienced an ischemic stroke. All participants completed the usability tasks successfully. The mean SUS score was 73.6 (SD 12.2, 95% CI 66.5-80.6; median 77.5, IQR 61.3-80.6), indicating good usability. Qualitative feedback revealed 3 themes: perceived ease of use and accessibility, perceived usefulness and engagement, and suggestions for improvement. Conclusions This study systematically developed a theory-driven, digital course-game sequential intervention that is innovative in targeting psychological resilience as a core mechanism for social participation, distinguishing it from conventional function-focused or generic resilience approaches. By integrating systematic course learning with contextualized gamified practice, it offers a scalable, low-burden tool that addresses key gaps in stroke rehabilitation. These findings support progression to feasibility and efficacy testing through randomized controlled trials in real-world settings.

title: Sociocultural Correlates of Infant Visual Attention
8473a031b71f412db61a7f2575838edd7fc38aae.abstract: Infant visual attention—most often operationalized through looking behavior—is a foundational method and explanatory construct in the study of early cognition. Cultural psychology has established that attention is organized by culturally structured practices and localized meanings, but this work has focused largely on children and adults, and the extent to which culturally patterned experience shapes the endogenous attentional processes that looking measures are used to index in infancy remains under-specified. This review focuses on the first two years of life and on four components of endogenous attention that are routinely inferred from looking behavior: focal versus contextual allocation, orienting speed versus accuracy, novelty versus familiarity orientation, and persistence versus flexibility. We distinguish culture—shared meanings, practices, and organized forms of everyday activity—from demographic indicators such as nationality, language background, race, and socioeconomic status, which are coarse proxies for proximal experience. Synthesizing cross-national studies alongside research on multilingual, interracial, and socioeconomic experience, we show that components of infant attention vary with experience and task context in ways that do not map cleanly onto reified group categories. We identify a gap between research documenting effects of specific experiences and research examining culture directly, and we propose a culturally situated model in which endogenous attentional mechanisms are calibrated through culturally patterned input across development. This approach preserves the value of looking-time and eye-tracking methods while strengthening their construct validity, measurement invariance, and generalizability.

title: INTERGENERATIONAL SHIFT BETWEEN TRADITIONAL ROMANIPEN AND DIGITAL HYPERMODERNITY
container-title: Наукові праці Міжрегіональної Академії управління персоналом. Політичні науки та публічне управління
9ab3121920cb020d31c11c3bc677e24d28ca3026.abstract: lobal social changes – accelerated digitalization, socioeconomic insecurity, and individualization – are also affecting more closed communities. In the environment of marginalized Roma communities (MRK) in Slovakia, the traditional unwritten code of values (romanipen) is confronted with the norms and patterns of Western hypermodernity. The main objective of the study is to examine the transformation of the value orientations of the Roma minority in Slovakia under the influence of modernization and digital processes. The study focuses on intergenerational shifts, the transformation of family structures, the authority of elders, and the influence of social networks on the identity of Roma youth. The research was designed as a qualitative ethnographic study using in-depth interviews (n = 18) and focus groups (n = 4; N = 24) with three groups of actors: traditional authorities and seniors in settlements, Roma youth (Generation Z) and field social workers in selected locations in eastern and central Slovakia (Ntotal = 42). The findings show that while the older generation of Roma strictly adheres to the traditional values of family solidarity, respect for elders and the informal code of Romanipen, the youngest generation is subject to massive digital acculturation. Among Roma youth, there is a shift from collective norms to individual success, a consumer lifestyle and self-representation on social networks. However, this shift creates value uncertainty (anomie), as youth encounter a double barrier: rejection of traditional rules in the settlement and at the same time persistent ethnic discrimination in the majority society. The transformation of values in Roma communities requires sensitive bridging of the intergenerational gap. Social policies and inclusive education must reflect the specifics of Roma identity in the digital age and support projects that combine respect for the positive elements of Romanipen with the development of critical thinking and digital literacy.

title: DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION OF PARLIAMENTARY TELEVISION BROADCASTING IN UKRAINE: EUROPEAN STANDARDS AND INSTITUTIONAL MODELS OF A MULTIMEDIA SERVICE
container-title: Наукові праці Міжрегіональної Академії управління персоналом. Політичні науки та публічне управління
45fc628955bcfca0b9a77a7cae8a86f5e80b0dc2.abstract: У статті досліджуються проблеми реформування парламентського телемовлення в Україні в контексті європейських стандартів свободи слова, незалежності медіа та суспільного мовлення. Основну увагу зосереджено на інституційно-правовому статусі парламентського телеканалу «Рада», особливостях його фінансування та управління, а також на законодавчих підходах до визначення його функцій. Проаналізовано юридичну експертизу Ради Європи щодо запропонованих у 2023 році змін до законодавства України про парламентське мовлення, зокрема двох концептуально різних моделей: обмеження діяльності парламентського каналу трансляцією роботи Верховної Ради та її комітетів і розширення його функцій до повноцінного виробництва редакційного медіа-контенту. Розглянуто європейський досвід організації парламентських аудіовізуальних служб, серед яких моделі, засновані на діяльності суспільних мовників, парламентських служб або їх поєднанні. Обґрунтовано необхідність розмежування функцій парламентського інформаційного сервісу та редакційного медіа. Запропоновано розглядати реформу парламентського телемовлення в Україні в ширшому контексті переходу від традиційного телевізійного каналу до мультимедійного парламентського медіа-сервісу. Визначено основні інституційні передумови такої реформи: редакційна незалежність, прозорість управління та фінансування, чітке визначення суспільної функції, відкритість парламентського контенту та адаптація до цифрового медіа-середовища. Актуальність теми трансформації парламентського мовника України з державного то суспільного медіа обумовлена викликами, що постають у зв’язку з переходом суспільних медіа від державної до громадської служби, а також від традиційного аналогового мовлення до цифрової дистрибуції контенту

title: Digital Transformation of Work-Integrated Learning in Vocational Education: Microcredential Technology, Collaboration, and Industry Engagement
container-title: International Journal of Engineering, Science and Information Technology
c2c7b1d564ca4b716ea2e2ed02822cdfd4ce285d.abstract: Work-Integrated Learning (WIL) is a strategic approach bridging vocational education and industry requirements. This study investigates digitalized WIL implementation in Indonesian vocational schools, focusing on microcredential technology utilization, interdisciplinary collaboration, and industry engagement. A descriptive survey was conducted with 146 respondents from West Java vocational schools, predominantly mechanical engineering programs. Data were collected June-July 2025 using validated Likert-scale questionnaires covering microcredential technology utilization, collaboration, digital portfolio development, and credential-based assessment mechanisms. Most respondents had less than three years WIL experience, reflecting early adoption stages. Findings reveal 71.9% of respondents rated the use of digital and microcredential-enabling technology as Good to Excellent, particularly in documentation and portfolio development. Infrastructure assessment shows 78.1% achieving good to excellent equipment quality, with 84.2% demonstrating adequate laboratory conditions. Interdisciplinary collaboration was rated effective by 69.8% of respondents, demonstrating progress toward integrated project-based learning. Industry mentor engagement reached 67.8%, with active participation through Learning Management Systems (87.7% usage), video conferencing (91.8%), and digital portfolios (73.3%). Digital portfolio quality achieved 59.6% good to excellent ratings, while documentation systems showed 61.6% effectiveness; these two dimensions form the evidence layer on which microcredential issuance depends, indicating that the technological pre-conditions for badge-based credentialing are present but not yet consolidated. Comparative analysis revealed significant improvements in digital versus traditional WIL, with 27.3% average enhancement across learning outcomes (p 0.001), particularly portfolio quality (+42.9%) and industry readiness (+32.0%). Results highlight that microcredential-oriented digital transformation enhances WIL effectiveness through improved collaboration, transparency, and school-industry alignment. However, challenges include uneven adoption, limited infrastructure, and varying digital literacy levels. The study recommends expanding microcredential platforms and their issuance-verification infrastructure, comprehensive educator training, and strengthened industry partnerships while developing standardized frameworks for microcredential recognition, issuance, and quality assurance

title: A Digital Ergonomics Framework for Preventive Workstation and Work-Process Optimization Using OWAS-Based Risk Assessment
container-title: International Journal of Engineering, Science and Information Technology
bde93ad8934bc0cea236552e293003165fed282c.abstract: Ergonomic workstation design is essential for improving the fit between workers, tasks, and the work environment while reducing the risk of work-related musculoskeletal disorders. The Ovako Working Posture Analysis System (OWAS) is widely used for ergonomic risk assessment; however, its conventional application to dynamic work can be inefficient because numerous working postures must be observed and evaluated. Moreover, conventional ergonomic design often requires multiple physical mock-ups, while motion-capture technologies such as Kinect are generally applied to existing work conditions, limiting their use for preventive evaluation during the design stage. This study proposes a digital ergonomics framework integrating workstation modeling, work-process simulation, and OWAS-based risk assessment for preventive ergonomic optimization. Digital models of the workstation and work activities were developed to simulate worker postures and identify potentially hazardous conditions before physical implementation. OWAS was used to classify postural risks and determine the required corrective actions. Workstation configurations and work procedures associated with higher risk levels were iteratively modified and reassessed in the digital environment. The results demonstrate that the proposed framework can identify and reduce ergonomic risks during the design stage without extensive physical prototyping. Higher-risk postures were mitigated through iterative modifications of workstation configurations and work procedures. This framework provides a systematic preventive approach for integrating ergonomic assessment into workstation and work-process design, supporting safer working conditions while improving the efficiency of the ergonomic design process

title: GBAS: A Hybrid GRU–BiLSTM–Attention–SVM Framework for Multiclass Stunting-Status Classification in Riau Province, Indonesia
container-title: International Journal of Engineering, Science and Information Technology
e4ae3d541e91cfa6c9448045cc7642b8d78cf788.abstract: Stunting-status classification using structured anthropometric data presents several challenges, including class imbalance, heterogeneous predictor characteristics, limited sample size, and the risk of target-derived information artificially inflating model performance. This study proposes GRU–BiLSTM–Attention–SVM (GBAS), a hybrid framework that combines recurrent deep representation learning, bidirectional processing, attention-based representation weighting, and margin-based classification for multiclass stunting-status classification. The study used 569 cross-sectional child-growth records from Riau Province, Indonesia, comprising Normal, Stunted, and Severely Stunted classes. Before model development, data-quality and leakage controls were applied, including measurement-unit standardization, exclusion of variables with substantial unavailable information, control of repeated feature combinations during partitioning, and removal of target-derived nutritional indicators. The remaining predictors were numerically encoded and standardized using parameters estimated from the training data, while class weighting was applied to address class imbalance without synthetic oversampling. In GBAS, GRU and BiLSTM operate as representation-learning components over a consistently ordered structured-feature representation, attention weights the resulting latent representations, and SVM performs final classification. On the held-out test set of 114 observations, GBAS correctly classified 113 observations, achieving 99.12% accuracy, 99.13% weighted precision, 99.12% weighted recall, and 99.12% weighted F1-score. Under the same experimental setting, GBAS outperformed the evaluated SVM, GRU, and BiLSTM baselines, which achieved accuracies of 89.46%, 95.78%, and 97.30%, respectively. These findings support the feasibility of the integrated GBAS framework for structured stunting-status classification. However, the results remain specific to the Riau dataset, feature ordering, and experimental configuration and require further validation through larger datasets, stronger tabular baselines, feature-order sensitivity analysis, component-level ablation, and external evaluation

title: Attention in model-based cognitive neuroscience: Mechanisms for optimization under constraint
3aaee46f4b8c0020acd131b68eb24d9ea7ccfb1a.abstract: Two major criticisms of attention research are: 1) verbal theories lack the specificity to make falsifiable predictions about how the various mechanisms of attention operate; and 2) the term ``attention’’ is frequently ascribed to conceptually similar phenomena despite dissociable neural underpinnings. The field of model-based cognitive neuroscience is well-positioned to address (1) through mathematical formalization of hypothesized processes, but may perpetuate (2) insofar as similar algorithms and parameters may recur across modeling traditions without necessarily drawing upon a shared neuro-mechanistic basis. This review provides a function-first organization of the algorithms that have been hypothesized to implement or give rise to ``attention'' at various levels of processing: perception, decision-making, and learning. We ground mathematically-formalized processes in the performance-relevant objectives they serve and the processing constraints that limit them. In doing so, we provide a road map of the broader computational-level solutions that ``attention'' mechanisms have been invoked to provide.

title: Revisiting Attention Modules for Still-Image Human Action Recognition: A Multi-Seed Evaluation on Stanford-40
container-title: International Journal of Engineering, Science and Information Technology
c52f55837f63d489cc4d73a1f2db1542e97d105c.abstract: Attention modules such as Squeeze-and-Excitation are often reported to improve convolutional neural networks for human action recognition in still images. Most of these reports, however, rely on a single training run, and published scores on the same benchmark are frequently obtained under different train–test splits. This study examines whether the reported benefit remains under a controlled evaluation. Four modules, namely Squeeze-and-Excitation (SE), the Convolutional Block Attention Module (CBAM), Efficient Channel Attention (ECA), and the parameter-free SimAM, were inserted into ResNet-34 at four positions and trained on the Stanford-40 Actions dataset under its official split with one fixed training recipe, giving 44 trained models. The four all-stage configurations were repeated with six random seeds and compared using a paired Wilcoxon signed-rank test and an exact McNemar test. Replacing the official split with a random 80/20 split increased test accuracy by 3.19 to 4.52 percentage points across four backbones, a larger change than any module produced. Across six seeds, SE changed macro-F1 by +0.06 points, within the seed-to-seed range of the unmodified baseline, whereas ECA and SimAM reduced it by 1.56 and 0.74 points. No module improved on the baseline by a statistically supported margin, yet every module increased single-image CPU latency by 4.3% to 18.3% while adding less than 0.02% in floating-point operations. The findings show that the evaluation protocol and run-to-run variance affect reported scores more than the modules themselves, and a reporting checklist is proposed for future evaluations of such modules

title: Assessing Digital Resilience in Primary Health Care: A Structural Framework
container-title: International Journal of Engineering, Science and Information Technology
9438321dc16f619e51335073026af168bd82528c.abstract: Digital transformation has significantly changed healthcare delivery, particularly in primary care settings such as Puskesmas (Community Health Centers) in Indonesia. Although digital technologies offer opportunities to improve accessibility, efficiency, and service quality, the capacity of healthcare institutions to adapt to digital disruptions remains insufficiently understood. This study aims to examine digital resilience in primary healthcare through a systematic literature review, focusing on research trends, key influencing factors, thematic developments, and knowledge gaps relevant to Puskesmas. The review analyzes scholarly articles, conference papers, and other academic publications retrieved from Scopus, PubMed, and Google Scholar. The analysis considers publication trends, influential authors, geographical distribution, and major research themes concerning digital resilience in healthcare. The findings indicate growing research interest in digital resilience, particularly regarding the challenges faced by healthcare systems operating under resource constraints. Four major factors emerge as relevant to digital adaptation: technological infrastructure, digital literacy, policy support, and community engagement. However, existing research predominantly emphasizes the technical dimensions of digital technologies, while organizational capacity and sociocultural factors receive comparatively limited attention. Research addressing digital resilience in Southeast Asia, particularly in Indonesian primary healthcare settings, also remains underrepresented. These gaps limit the contextual understanding of how digital resilience develops within community-based healthcare institutions. The review concludes that strengthening digital resilience in Puskesmas requires an integrated approach that combines technological readiness, organizational preparedness, workforce development, and community participation. Future research should investigate the organizational and sociocultural dimensions of digital adaptation and develop context-specific strategies for improving digital literacy among healthcare workers and communities. Policymakers should also prioritize sustainable digital infrastructure and continuous training to support resilient, accessible, and effective primary healthcare services in Indonesia

title: TECNOLOGIA DIGITAL COMO RECURSO DE INCLUSÃO NO ENSINO FUNDAMENTAL
container-title: Revista Ilustração
c4cae270d69a06c8da0c8309f6077d8fcfec0b5d.abstract: A utilização de recursos tecnológicos na educação inclusiva ampliou as possibilidades de participação de estudantes com deficiência nas atividades escolares, especialmente no Ensino Fundamental. Nesse contexto, o estudo teve como objetivo geral analisar as possibilidades de utilização de ferramentas digitais acessíveis para favorecer a participação e a aprendizagem de estudantes com deficiência no Ensino Fundamental. Especificamente, buscou-se compreender a relação entre tecnologias digitais e inclusão escolar, identificar recursos acessíveis e suas aplicações pedagógicas e examinar os desafios relacionados à utilização dessas ferramentas. A investigação foi desenvolvida por meio de pesquisa bibliográfica, de abordagem qualitativa e natureza descritiva, fundamentada na análise de cinco artigos científicos publicados entre 2024 e 2025. Os resultados identificaram aplicações de recursos digitais em atividades de alfabetização, letramento e comunicação, incluindo aplicativos educacionais, leitores de tela, materiais adaptados e dispositivos de comunicação alternativa. Também foram constatadas dificuldades relacionadas à infraestrutura escolar, às limitações de acessibilidade dos aplicativos e à adequação das atividades às necessidades educacionais dos estudantes. Concluiu-se que as ferramentas digitais acessíveis apresentaram possibilidades de contribuição para a inclusão escolar, desde que sua utilização estivesse associada aos objetivos curriculares, às características dos estudantes e às condições institucionais disponíveis. Entretanto, as diferenças metodológicas entre os estudos analisados limitaram a generalização dos resultados sobre a aprendizagem.

title: <b>Studi Implementasi Model Pembelajaran PAI Berbasis Kajian Kitab Klasik Dan Digital Learning Dalam Penguatan Pemahaman Keagamaan Peserta Didik</b>
container-title: Nusantara Journal Of Islamic Studies
d9bad89e4110e96e13e5ec4093cf0517cbaccff0.abstract: Penelitian ini berfokus pada implementasi model pembelajaran Pendidikan Agama Islam (PAI) berbasis kajian kitab klasik dan digital learning dalam upaya memperkuat pemahaman keagamaan peserta didik di SMP Ihyauddiniyah, Desa Kecik, Kecamatan Besuk, Kabupaten Probolinggo. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis proses pelaksanaan pembelajaran melalui kajian kitab klasik dan pemanfaatan media digital, mengungkap bentuk integrasi kedua pendekatan tersebut, serta memahami kontribusinya terhadap penguatan pemahaman keagamaan peserta didik. Penelitian menggunakan metode kualitatif dengan desain studi kasus. Data dikumpulkan melalui observasi, wawancara mendalam, dan dokumentasi, kemudian dianalisis menggunakan model interaktif Miles, Huberman, dan Saldaña yang meliputi kondensasi data, penyajian data, serta penarikan dan verifikasi kesimpulan. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa integrasi kajian kitab klasik dan digital learning dapat dipahami sebagai pendekatan komplementer yang menghubungkan pendalaman materi keislaman melalui literatur klasik dengan kemudahan akses dan variasi sumber belajar digital. Kajian kitab klasik memberikan landasan pemahaman keagamaan, sedangkan media digital mendukung penyampaian materi secara lebih interaktif dan kontekstual. Implikasi penelitian ini menegaskan pentingnya peran guru dalam mengintegrasikan sumber belajar klasik dan digital secara selektif, kritis, serta sesuai dengan kebutuhan peserta didik agar pembelajaran PAI tidak hanya berorientasi pada penguasaan materi, tetapi juga pada pemahaman dan penerapan nilai-nilai keislaman dalam kehidupan sehari-hari.

title: Trust in AI: A Decision-Theoretic framework for Human–AI Interactions in the Digital Society
cd2e1c34af9387fd565d30e964dce709b38b5e7f.abstract: Trust in artificial intelligence (AI) is crucial for ensuring productive human–AI interactions across domains ranging from medicine to finance. As AI systems become central in the digital society, understanding how people decide when to rely on algorithmic advice becomes increasingly important. This paper proposes that a decision-theoretic perspective is needed to explain how well-calibrated trust in AI can be achieved. We conceptualize trust in AI as a decision to delegate control to an artificial agent, balancing potential rewards and risks of following AI advice versus relying on one’s own judgment. Framed this way, established decision-making theories such as Prospect Theory, Evidence Accumulation Models, and Reinforcement Learning offer valuable insights into the cognitive processes that underlie trust in AI. These theories offer formal, computational models to explain how individuals evaluate AI-generated advice, weigh risks and rewards, form biases, and update trust based on feedback, enabling precise hypotheses about when and why people accept or reject AI advice. By grounding trust in cognitive theory, we offer a roadmap for empirical research that moves beyond surface-level behaviors and toward mechanistic understanding. We conclude that a decision-theoretic approach can enhance psychological insight and guide the responsible design of AI systems within the digital society that are better aligned with human cognition.

title: A phase-calibrated combined electrical-sensory neuromodulation platform for short-Term frontoparietal network modulation and cognitive fatigue resistance
container-title: Journal of Neural Engineering
a676847d59b7b8ff3eeaa396e9bedcbab7ac075d.abstract: Abstract Non-invasive multimodal neuromodulation is often limited by cross-modal temporal misalignment caused by modality-specific conduction delays. To address this challenge, we developed a microcontroller-based multiphysics stimulation platform integrating transcranial alternating current stimulation (tACS) with visual and auditory rhythmic inputs. A feedforward delaycompensation strategy using individualized ERP latencies (visual P1 and auditory N1) was implemented to reduce intermodal timing discrepancies.The system was evaluated in a randomized, sham-controlled crossover study with 15 participants providing complete EEG datasets. Compared with sensory-only stimulation, the phase-coordinated multiphysics condition increased resting-state frontoparietal theta power and enhanced functional connectivity (wPLI). During a subsequent high-load cognitive task, it was also associated with reduced accumulation of fatigue-related parietal alpha power.Exploratory analysis revealed a moderate association between parietal alpha stability and behavioral performance (r = 0.577, p = 0.024). These findings suggest that temporally coordinated cross-modal stimulation may support more stable large-scale neural dynamics and improved cognitive performance under sustained load, providing a technical framework for precision multimodal neuromodulation.
