title: Ramadan and the Timing of Scheduled Sessions on an Arabic Digital Mental Health Platform: A Three-Cycle Interrupted Time-Series Analysis (2023–2026)
container-title: Psychiatry International
9135433cbeb9a4eca65281d4271aea9c0fea204a.abstract: Background: Ramadan shifts sleep timing and daily routines, but, to our knowledge, its association with the timing of mental health care has not been measured across repeated cycles. Methods: We analysed de-identified records from an Arabic-language digital mental health platform in Saudi Arabia (30 September 2023–29 April 2026; 33,738 adults; 43,190 scheduled sessions). Ramadan 1445, 1446 and 1447 AH were compared with the 30 days before and after each month, using session-level logistic regression for session timing and negative-binomial regression for daily volume, adjusted for a flexible growth trend, day of week and holidays. Mood labels and PHQ-9 and GAD-7 scores were secondary outcomes. Results: During Ramadan, the share of sessions scheduled between 22:00 and 05:59 rose by 19.2 percentage points (95% CI 16.9–21.7; odds ratio 2.69), with increases in each cycle (26.6, 14.7 and 20.0 points) and in every sensitivity analysis; the gain came mainly from midday hours (12:00–17:59; −12.9 points) rather than the evening (−5.8). Daily volume did not change significantly (rate ratio 0.91, 0.81–1.02), although estimates depended on the trend specification and on where the series ended. Raw post-Ramadan increases in volume could not be separated from platform growth. Symptom scores did not differ, and mood shifts were inconsistent. Conclusions: On this platform, Ramadan was associated with a large, recurring shift in scheduled sessions into late-night hours, without a consistent change in volume or self-reported symptoms.

title: Roles of Artificial Intelligence in Urban Digital Twins and Governance
container-title: Smart Cities
f6f776daec0984758f82fb78da119f082a76cc5c.abstract: Artificial intelligence is becoming an increasingly used component in municipal operations, with applications spanning administrative automation, decision support, citizen interfaces, and predictive analytics across domains such as mobility, health and social services, and environmental management. While the literature documents benefits in operational efficiency and decision quality, most concrete evidence focuses primarily on internal efficiency. Urban digital twins have become commonplace in most European cities and smart cities globally. However, the role of AI within urban digital twins remains comparatively underexplored. This article addresses these gaps through a qualitative analysis of AI in Helsinki’s Experimentation Accelerator platform experiments and by comparing them against a DT framework based on the literature. Through this, we analyze how AI is piloted in municipal applications and how the identified use cases of AI align with the components of urban digital twins, identifying potential roles for AI in the urban digital twin as well as directions for future development.

title: Comparative Effects of a Cow Hoof Cover® and Bandaging as Dressing Materials for the Treatment of Digital Dermatitis in Dairy Cows
container-title: Animals
1ff5892b0f9a51b27d9b0f6d077c117017a5b102.abstract: Digital dermatitis (DD) contributes to lameness, posing major animal welfare and economic concerns. Corrective trimming, topical antibiotics, and bandaging are widely practised in managing DD. However, the challenges associated with conventional bandaging include water retention and a moist environment, which affect the healing process. This study evaluated the effectiveness of a Cow Hoof Cover® (CHC) for the treatment of DD in dairy cows. A quasi-experimental study was conducted, involving cows affected with active stages of DD (M1 and M2), allocated to CHC (n = 29) and conventional bandaging (n = 27) groups. The standard treatment entailed a Dutch five-step hoof trimming, wound management, application of topical antibiotic containing oxytetracycline (Engemycin 25 mg/mL), and wrapping of the digit using either the CHC or conventional bandaging. All cows received an intramuscular injection of flunixin meglumine (2.2 mg/kg) for pain relief. Primary outcomes were healing of DD lesions (transition from active stages to M0) and restoration of normal gait (locomotion score of 1). All cows were observed weekly until Week 4 after treatment. While alterations in locomotion score were not significantly different between the groups (p = 0.23) during the study period, the CHC group had significantly higher (p < 0.01) proportions of cured cows at week 3 (n = 6, 20.6%) and week 4 (n = 17; 58.6%) compared to the control. None of the CHC-wrapped lesions progressed into the chronic hyperkeratotic or proliferative stage (M4), but such transitions were recorded in four cows in the control group. Overall, the CHC had significantly higher probability of cure (HR = 2.79; 95% CI 1.30–5.97) than the control group. Excluding the treatment group, none of the tested animal characteristics and treatment-related variables influenced the probability of cure. Overall, the CHC offers practical advantages over conventional bandaging; it is quick to apply, durable, and water-resistant, supporting its use for field application and large-scale herd management. However, histological investigation and robust clinical trials are recommended to ascertain whether the CHC promotes a complete cure of active DD lesions.

title: The Impact of Digital Economy and Industrial Agglomeration on Green Total Factor Productivity: An Analysis of Mechanisms and Regulatory Conditions
container-title: International Journal of Financial Studies
27e813fc77c40967bc4469a8418e38681af20902.abstract: This paper examines the relationship between digital economy development, manufacturing agglomeration, and urban green total factor productivity (GTFP). Using an unbalanced panel of 283 Chinese prefecture-level cities over 2007–2022, we estimate a two-way fixed-effects model that includes digital development, manufacturing agglomeration, and their interaction. The interaction coefficient is positive and statistically significant, indicating that the association between manufacturing agglomeration and GTFP becomes more favorable as digital development increases. Sequential regressions link this relationship to lower capital misallocation, better labor allocation, and greater green patent activity, with stronger statistical support for the green-innovation channel. The lagged specification and environmental-performance outcome provide further supporting evidence. Subsample estimates provide suggestive evidence of a larger interaction coefficient in cities with higher environmental-regulation intensity. These findings connect digital development and manufacturing concentration with urban green productivity and highlight the relevance of factor allocation, green innovation, and regulatory conditions to the green transformation of industrial clusters.

title: Digital Financial Ecosystems and Trade-Related Working Capital Finance: Firm-Level Evidence from 39 Economies
container-title: International Journal of Financial Studies
3de372c992cbce7a3af0e4ce4b6acef8e8d9da67.abstract: How firms finance purchases and inventories may depend increasingly on the digital financial environment in which they operate, but cross-economy evidence on trade credit and customer advances remains limited. We merge firm-level Enterprise Survey records with digital finance, insurance, digital infrastructure, and macroeconomic indicators. The complete-case sample comprises 32,049 firms across 39 economies surveyed during 2014–2020. Conventional digital finance and insurance capacity are positively associated with percentage, fractional share, and adoption outcomes across OLS, fractional logit, and logit specifications. The interaction between mobile money and digital infrastructure is negative but only marginally significant for adoption, supporting a diminishing adoption association at the 10% level; it is nonsignificant for percentage and fractional outcomes and is absent among existing users. Nonlife digital readiness negatively moderates the fractional share at the 5% level and adoption at the 10% level, but not the OLS percentage outcome. Alternative received and granted trade credit outcomes yield positive interaction signs, indicating that the estimated relationships are sensitive to the specific working capital outcome examined. Overall, the findings support a disaggregated ecosystem perspective but remain associational because national exposures are not randomly assigned and the data are repeated across sections.

title: Digital Objective Lens: A Lightweight Neural Network for Super-Resolution of SEM Images
container-title: Processes
afaa3be7646d2fb3d1e2ce8a0329f9aa5258692a.abstract: Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) is a crucial and frequently employed tool for material characterization. However, owing to the hardware limitations of SEM, researchers often face a trade-off when observing materials: they must either use the fast scanning mode to acquire real-time images with poor details or wait 20 to 160 s for the slow scanning mode to obtain a high-resolution (HR) image with rich details. This significantly reduces observation efficiency and prevents process-level observations. In this study, we propose a wavelet-based lightweight super-resolution (SR) network (WLSR), which serves as a “digital objective lens”: by performing rapid SR on fast-scan SEM images, 2× or 4× digital magnification of the field of view with slow-scan image quality can be obtained while large-scale observation of the sample is conducted. A channel–spatial attention block and a wavelet-based upscaling module are introduced into the network structure, and a novel loss function combining a wavelet distillation loss and a perceptual loss is proposed for network training. WLSR was trained and evaluated on paired fast-/slow-scan SEM images of AgCl@Ag specimens, in which all LR inputs are genuine fast-scan images that are jointly denoised and super-resolved. Compared with existing lightweight SR networks, WLSR generates SEM SR images with richer details, superior subjective visual quality, and competitive objective evaluation metrics at an exceptionally fast inference speed of 3.7 ms per image on an NVIDIA GV100 GPU, indicating the feasibility of real-time deployment during live SEM observation. Through WLSR, the quality of fast-scan SEM images is significantly improved, which can enhance the efficiency and accuracy of sample observation.

title: Overcoming Dengue Underreporting: A Machine Learning Framework for Automated Dengue Notification Based on Electronic Medical Records
container-title: Tropical Medicine and Infectious Disease
9af697993d89b64a9f3999a0cdbda92068412686.abstract: Hospital notification of dengue cases is frequently delayed, contributing to underreporting. At Thai provincial hospitals the bottleneck is administrative, not diagnostic: delayed discharge coding and clerical steps mean notifications are submitted late or omitted. Existing machine learning (ML) studies require clinician-annotated features absent in passive electronic medical records (EMRs). We propose a dual-pathway EMR framework for ML-based pre-population of surveillance reports. We analyzed 1031 dengue-suspected encounters (508 notifiable) from Surin Hospital, Thailand (2019–2022). Pathway A combines EMR data with manually documented clinical features; Pathway B uses only passive EMR data. Using an 80/20 stratified split, we tested 7 ML methods across 11 feature sets (77 combinations) with SHAP-guided feature elimination and 10-fold cross-validation. On the primary split, Pathway A (CatBoost) achieved an F1 score of 96.62%, 95.10% sensitivity, and 98.10% specificity (10-seed mean F1 95.7% ± 1.4%). Pathway B (LightGBM) achieved an F1 score of 84.42%, 94.12% sensitivity, 75.24% specificity, and a projected negative predictive value of 99.1% at 10% prevalence; 10-seed performance was lower (F1 78.5% ± 4.3%; sensitivity 89.1%). An exploratory LSTM-16 stacking model (F1 83.99%; precision 79.49%) performed best in precision and specificity among Pathway B. Test F1 SD across 10 seeds was ≤5.0% in 75 of 77 combinations. Within this cohort, passive EMR modeling achieved 91–94% sensitivity on the primary split (85–89% across seeds) without additional data collection, supporting the feasibility of ML-based notification in resource-constrained hospitals. Whether this reduces dengue underreporting must be established in prospective, multi-center studies.

title: LMF-FD2M: Fatigue Driving Detection with Fusion of Millimeter-Wave Radar and Physiological Bracelet
container-title: Vehicles
62b82b625aeb879f4a47d7e817012e88713dbc7f.abstract: Fatigued driving is an important cause of traffic accidents, and the current fatigued driving detection methods based on a single modality have poor adaptability, weak anti-interference and difficulty in balancing the requirements of accuracy and real-time performance. To solve these limitations, this paper proposes a lightweight fatigue driving detection model, LMF-FD2M, based on Multi-sensor Fusion, which uses multi-dimensional physiological signals from millimeter-wave radar and a physiological bracelet. LMF-FD2M adopts an asymmetric two-branch architecture, where the Mamba branch is designed to capture long-term global patterns. In particular, a Fourier Analysis Module with Attention (FAMA) is designed for this branch in order to capture global periodic patterns and effective characteristics of physiological signals in the frequency domain. The CNN-BiLSTM branch acts as a high-precision detector for short-term dynamic changes. Specially, a Focused Linear Attention (FLA) is introduced for this branch in order to focus on local instantaneous variations in temporal domain and suppress noises. Moreover, an adaptive fusion method based on sample characteristics is designed to dynamically modulate the contributions of each modality and integrate the global pattern and local dynamics features. The experimental results on two public datasets (FatigueSet, DROZY) and a self-built dataset (M2FDD) show that our LMF-FD2M model is superior to other state-of-the-art models, and the numbers of parameters and FLOPs are only 7–28% of the baselines, which can meet the needs of in-vehicle deployment.

title: From urban digital embeddedness to management decisions: understanding innovative SMEs' digital orientation
container-title: Management Decision
946f0fd164210555a0afae10ae81bce43d4f0545.abstract: Purpose Developed for management decision's “The Practice of Making Decisions” section, this study examines a concrete managerial dilemma: what can managers learn by considering how deeply digital technologies are embedded in the urban environment alongside their availability? We examine how urban digital embeddedness is associated with innovative small and medium-sized enterprise (SMEs') digital orientation (DO) and its four dimensions. Design/methodology/approach The study combines city- and firm-level information for 24 Italian cities and 243 innovative SMEs observed over 13 years. Urban digital embeddedness captures citizens' use of home banking, municipal applications and broadband services. SMEs' DO is derived from annual mission statements and assessed across digital technology scope, digital capabilities, digital ecosystem coordination and digital architecture configuration. Relationships are estimated using a two-way fixed-effects Spatial Durbin Panel Model. Findings The findings show that urban digital embeddedness is most consistently associated with firms' stated digital capabilities and digital ecosystem coordination, followed by digital architecture configuration, while evidence for digital technology scope is comparatively weak. Practical implications Managers should look beyond digital technologies when making digital-strategy decisions and consider how technologies are actually embedded in the surrounding environment. Urban digital embeddedness can provide decision-relevant signals when evaluating locations, setting investment priorities, assessing external ecosystems and planning firms' digital transformation. Originality/value The study reframes the smart city as a managerial decision environment rather than a technological backdrop. It positions urban digital embeddedness as a source of contextual signals and DO as the organisational expression of strategic digital choices made by managers.

title: Effect of Digital Library Resources on Information Literacy Skills  of Undergraduate Students in Nigerian Higher Institutions
container-title: WORLD JOURNAL OF INNOVATION AND MODERN TECHNOLOGY
c5fb337d9599268533aca01c6f5f03ca4f5de158.abstract: The proliferation of digital library resources in Nigerian higher institutions has repositioned the university library from a passive repository of print materials to an active hub for electronic information access. This article examines the effect of digital library resources on the information literacy skills of undergraduate students in Nigerian higher institutions. Adopting a desk-review methodology, the study synthesises empirical and conceptual literature published mainly between 2017 and 2024 to interrogate the extent to which electronic databases, institutional repositories, e-journals and online public access catalogues (OPACs) shape students' ability to locate, evaluate, and ethically use information. The review shows that digital library resources have a generally positive effect on information literacy, particularly in search formulation and information retrieval, but that gains are uneven and are frequently constrained by epileptic power supply, poor internet connectivity, inadequate funding, and a shortage of structured digital-skills training. A synthesis table and a summary chart drawn from nine reviewed studies illustrate the recurring pattern of challenges across Nigerian university libraries. The article recommends the institutionalisation of credit-bearing information literacy courses, sustained investment in ICT infrastructure, and continuous digital-skills training for both students and librarians as strategies for optimising the benefits of digital library resources in Nigerian higher education.

title: From Cell Block to Cash Book: Entrepreneurial and Digital Accounting Literacy for Incarcerated Adults Preparing for Reintegration in Jakarta
container-title: Journal of Economics, Finance And Management Studies
59c89ce9b03494351eaaaf7791f96241d3f10f07.abstract: Prison-based entrepreneurship and financial education is increasingly promoted as a pathway to reintegration, yet evidence from Southeast Asian correctional settings is thin, and short community-engagement programs rarely disclose what their evaluations can and cannot show. This paper reports a lecturer–student program delivered to 31 inmates of the Class II A Salemba Correctional Institution in Jakarta on 15 July 2026. A 45-minute session on digital marketing and opportunity identification was followed by a 45-minute session on simple digital bookkeeping built around a worked cash-book case. Two insession instruments were collected, a business-idea worksheet (n = 21) and a cash-book task (n = 13); the planned post-test could not be administered. Ideas concentrated in trade (38.1%) and culinary ventures (19.0%), but 42.9% were anchored in a craft, repair, production, or technical skill, and only two of 21 were technology-based. Twelve of 13 returned cash-book sheets (92.3%; Wilson 95% CI 66.7–98.6) reached the correct closing balance of IDR 390,000. Because only 41.9% of attendees returned a sheet, the share of all attendees verifiably correct lies between 38.7% and 96.8%. We argue that the result evidences comprehension of a worked example, not a learning gain, and that the binding constraints on post-release practice lie elsewhere: a digital-access paradox, a capital and licensing gap, and a time lag that invites skill decay. We propose a staged design (parallel-form pre/post testing, practice on real transactions, booster sessions, and hand-over to community-corrections officers) and an evidence ladder that states which claims programs of this kind can support.

title: Hybrid Temporal-Spatial Attention Network for Rainfall Prediction in Urban Microclimates
container-title: Journal of Innovative Image Processing
f5ecef645613974b923f2b7cb8fbb62e6d818c63.abstract: Climate change has led to more frequent occurrences of extreme weather conditions and irregular rainfall patterns, making accurate prediction of rainfall amounts essential. In this paper, the performance of a Hybrid Temporal-Spatial Attention Network (HTSAN) model in predicting rainfall for the next day is evaluated using 12 meteorological predictors from the ERA5 reanalysis dataset. The geographical area covered by this research spans a 17 × 17 grid with 0.25° × 0.25° nominal resolution around Bangalore. HTSAN’s architecture involved a convolutional feature extractor, recurrent temporal representation, a transformer encoder, and a regression layer. HTSAN's performance was benchmarked against recurrent, convolutional-recurrent, and attention-based approaches using chronological test data. In this, benchmarking, the TFT approach resulted in the best RMSE value of 7.1474, while HTSAN had an RMSE of 7.5911, an MAE of 3.6779, and an R² of 0.4259. Extreme-rainfall benchmarking also revealed that HTSAN’s critical success index values were lower than those of the comparison approaches at the selected grid-cell rainfall thresholds. Thus, it can be inferred that the current version of HTSAN did not perform better than the selected benchmarks.

title: Development of digital educational media on the risks of illegal herbal medicines sold through e-commerce platforms: a qualitative study
container-title: Frontiers in Digital Health
0850c0eda58471340c9dee24a4da6b66f26ba2b3.abstract: Background Illegal herbal medicines sold through e-commerce platforms pose public health risks, particularly for people with chronic diseases. Objective This study aimed to develop digital educational media, comprising an e-module, educational video, and website, to address the risks associated with illegal herbal medicines sold through online platforms. Methods This qualitative descriptive study involved semi-structured interviews with 17 participants, comprising 11 professional informants and six patients with chronic diseases. Thematic analysis informed the development of an e-module, educational video, and website. Two academic reviewers subsequently provided preliminary feedback on the developed media using structured four-point assessment forms. Both reviewers had also participated in the qualitative interviews that informed the development of the materials. Results Ten themes informed the development of the digital educational media, addressing product legality, online marketing, health and digital literacy, cultural beliefs, regulatory supervision, professional involvement, and digital education needs. Preliminary expert feedback yielded descriptive ratings of 93.75% for the e-module, 98.75% for the educational video, and 95.00% for the website. These ratings reflect the assessments of two academic reviewers, both of whom had participated in the qualitative phase. Accordingly, the results should be interpreted as preliminary feedback rather than independent confirmation of content validity or evidence of educational effectiveness. Conclusion The study resulted in the development of three digital educational media addressing the risks associated with illegal herbal medicines sold through e-commerce platforms. The preliminary expert feedback provided initial academic input on the content and presentation of the materials. Further assessment involving independent experts and intended users is needed to examine content relevance, usability, acceptability, and educational effectiveness.

Impact of Digital Financial Services on the Growth of Small and  Medium Enterprises (SMES) in Lafia, Nasarawa State, Nigeria
container-title: INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF ECONOMICS AND FINANCIAL MANAGEMENT
e89c2e24aaea86dfb0aedc368518d405f717a1ae.abstract: The diffusion of digital technology into the financial sector has reshaped how small and medium enterprises (SMEs) in Nigeria access, manage, and deploy financial resources. This article presents a theoretical analysis of the impact of digital financial services (DFS) on the growth of SMEs in Lafia, Nasarawa State. Anchored on the Technology Acceptance Model, the Diffusion of Innovation Theory, Financial Intermediation Theory, and the Schumpeterian finance-growth perspective, the article examines how mobile money, agency banking, point-of-sale platforms, and mobile/internet banking shape SME performance in a semi-urban Nigerian setting. A qualitative, desk-based theoretical design is adopted, complemented by an illustrative sampling exercise in which respondents were randomly drawn from one polytechnic in each of Nigeria's six geo political zones, to assess the wider plausibility of the study's conceptual claims. The analysis suggests that DFS enhance SME growth by lowering transaction costs, widening access to credit, improving record-keeping, and extending market reach, but that infrastructural deficits, low digital literacy, cost sensitivity, and trust concerns constrain the full realization of these benefits in Lafia. The article concludes that DFS hold substantial promise for SME growth in Lafia and similar towns, and recommends targeted infrastructure investment, digital and financial literacy programmes, cost moderation, and trust-building measures.

title: Digital Climate Diplomacy on X: Perceived Outcomes, Opportunities and Challenges in Kenya and the United States
container-title: Editon Consortium Journal of Arts, Humanities and Social Studies
2556f5d58bbdbd2361dd2106ff72c345adbde0a5.abstract: This study examined how platform visibility and engagement by themselves, demonstrate no diplomatic influence. It examined the perceived outcomes, opportunities and structural challenges associated with Kenya’s and the United States’ use of X for climate diplomacy during the Africa Climate Summit (ACS) and COP28. The study employed a qualitative, interpretivist comparative case study research design that drew on 16 semi-structured interviews with diplomatic and senior government actors (eight from each country) and a documentary corpus of 284 posts from four official government X accounts, supplemented by summit documents. Analysis was informed by Strategic Narrative Theory, Framing Theory, the Dialogic Communication Model and Critical Discourse Analysis (CDA). Participants associated Kenya’s communication with equity, historical responsibility, African leadership and climate justice, while United States communication was described as more continuous and solution-oriented. Across both cases, interviewees identified diplomatic presence, narrative projection and access to policy conversations as potential benefits. Still, they stressed that these were conditioned by staffing, approval procedures, coordination, media systems and geopolitical position. Participants also cautioned that visible engagement cannot establish changes in public perception, media uptake or negotiation outcomes without independent evidence. The study recommends an outcome-oriented, platform-specific framework for analysing how communication mechanisms interact with institutional and geopolitical conditions. It also recommends closer coordination between negotiators and communicators, stronger capacity for responsive and multilingual communication, and evaluation beyond vanity metrics. The study’s significance lies in an outcomes-oriented, platform-specific framework for evaluating diplomatic communication without conflating visibility with influence.

title: MedClassNet: a novel NLP framework for automated disease classification from clinical text using transformer and graph attention networks
container-title: Scientific Reports
e2da6b2b299de52f46e75a96710a8fe3ba4bde01.abstract: Abstract A combination of complex vocabulary, acronyms, and relationships in clinical narratives makes automatic disease classification from clinical narratives challenging. The study proposes the MedClassNet framework that combines Graph Attention Network (GAT) and BioBERT-based contextual embeddings for disease classification in clinical narratives. The MedClassNet framework uses BioBERT embeddings of admission and progress notes and generates a similarity graph for patients by using the cosine similarity between patient contextual embeddings. To classify diseases, the BioBERT framework is combined with the relational embedding learned by the GAT framework for clinically similar patients. An annotated corpus of 1,748 clinical narratives from MIMIC-III dataset containing single-label ICD-9 disease categories is used for experimentation. To avoid label leakage, discharge summaries, final diagnosis, explicit ICD-9 codes, and other post-diagnosis data are excluded from the input for model training. According to the experimental protocol, MedClassNet framework yields an accuracy of 94.2%, a precision of 94.6%, and F1-score of 0.93. Clinically relevant textual features responsible for predictions of the model are discovered by using SHAP-based analysis. The results indicate that combining patient-level relational information with clinical language contextual embeddings can improve disease classification performance as compared with baseline models.

title: Digital Decision Support for Smallholder Farmers using Explainable Multi Criteria Agricultural Intelligence
container-title: Journal of Smart and Sustainable Farming
f627ba7649e6b8c05ba26b157356e25158419e55.abstract: Under uncertain weather, fluctuating prices, constrained liquidity and limited access to advice, smallholder farmers have to make decisions on what to grow, but many digital advisory services provide a single, black-box answer that can't be questioned by farmers and extension agents. This article introduces an explainable multi-criteria decision support system which ranks candidate crops for each plot, explains in simple language the reasons for choosing a particular crop and provides confidence in the rank. A fuzzy agro-ecological suitability is combined with a water-stress yield model which incorporates Monte Carlo rainfall and price shocks, together with seven benefit and cost criteria, Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) weights and TOPSIS ranking. The closeness margin between the recommended crop and the runner-up crop is distributed in a pie chart across individual criteria and Dirichlet perturbation of the weights measures recommendation stability. All data are simulated: 20 synthetic landscapes of 40×40 plots (2.5 km cells), six crops with indicative parameters, and a hypothetical expert panel (AHP consistency ratio 0.013). The recommended crop for each landscape was groundnut on 37.5%, sorghum on 31.0% and pearl millet on 17.4%. It produced a mean net return of 210 USD/ha and has a loss probability of 18.7% under out-of-sample seasons with 25% fatter rainfall and price shocks than assumed during the design process, while a traditional rule of thumb has a mean net return of 67 USD/ha and a loss probability of 38.9%. The Shapley attributions summed exactly to the closeness margin (maximum error 5.6e-16), and the mean stability was 0.84, with 53.3% of plots above 0.9. These results demonstrate the mechanics and behaviour of the framework in a controlled setting; they are not field evidence.

title: ECONOMIC NATURE OF MULTINATIONAL COMPANIES:  FROM CLASSICAL THEORIES TO DIGITAL INTERNATIONALISATION
container-title: State and Regions. Series: Economics and Business
b722651041bb4a23582f988caf9209dde4820cb0.abstract: The article examines the economic nature of multinational companies (MNCs) and traces the evolution of theoretical concepts explaining their emergence, from the classical theories of the 1960s to contemporary approaches to digital internationalisation. The evolution of terminology applied to international firms is considered, together with the reasons behind the UNCTAD transition from the notion of transnational corporation to that of multinational enterprise in 2022. It is noted that the choice of the term transnational in United Nations documents of 1974 was driven largely by political and terminological considerations, whereas the official documents of the World Trade Organization and the European Union consistently employ the latter term. The definitions of MNCs proposed by leading foreign and Ukrainian scholars are analysed, and the criteria that distinguish such a company from other forms of international business are identified, namely control over assets located abroad, an equity threshold of ten per cent, and the coordination of production at the highest level of the decision-making hierarchy. The principal theories of MNCs are systematised in a summary table covering monopolistic advantage theory, product life cycle theory, the macroeconomic approach, internalisation theory, transaction cost theory, the Uppsala model, the eclectic OLI paradigm, regional theory, the theory of heterogeneous firms, the springboard perspective on emerging market companies, and microfoundational theory. A common idea uniting these approaches is identified: MNCs emerge and develop where the internal organisation of production and knowledge proves more efficient than market coordination mechanisms, and where firm-specific advantages are sufficient to offset the costs of internationalisation. It is substantiated that digital MNCs scale globally without foreign direct investment or physical assets, which calls into question the explanatory capacity of classical theories. Four channels through which MNCs affect the well-being of host regions are distinguished: economic, social, environmental and institutional.

title: Membangun Budaya Sadar Hukum Sejak Dini Melalui Pendidikan Nilai Keadilan, Kejujuran, dan Toleransi Bagi Anak di Kota Jayapura
container-title: Journal of Digital Community Services
b1b4015e69e8c72eb4ffcc4349daaa2d6a10143c.abstract: Budaya sadar hukum perlu ditumbuhkan sejak masa kanak-kanak melalui pendidikan nilai yang membimbing anak untuk menghargai hak orang lain, bersikap bertanggung jawab, dan mematuhi aturan yang disepakati bersama. Kegiatan pengabdian kepada masyarakat ini bertujuan memberikan edukasi tentang nilai keadilan, kejujuran, dan toleransi sebagai pijakan awal pembentukan kesadaran hukum pada anak-anak di Kelurahan Kota Baru, Kecamatan Abepura, Kota Jayapura. Kegiatan berlangsung pada 10 Oktober 2026 dan diikuti oleh 25 anak berusia 8 hingga 12 tahun. Pelaksanaannya memadukan ceramah dengan permainan edukatif, sedangkan penilaian dilakukan melalui sesi tanya jawab selama kegiatan berlangsung. Hasil observasi memperlihatkan bahwa anak-anak mengikuti rangkaian acara dengan penuh antusias, terlibat aktif dalam permainan edukatif, serta mampu memahami contoh-contoh perilaku yang mencerminkan keadilan dan kejujuran. Kegiatan ini berfungsi sebagai sarana pengenalan nilai moral dan sosial yang berkaitan dengan penumbuhan budaya sadar hukum sejak dini. Meskipun demikian, capaian yang dilaporkan terbatas pada respons dan pemahaman yang teramati selama kegiatan, sehingga belum dapat dijadikan dasar untuk menyimpulkan adanya perubahan perilaku jangka panjang maupun peningkatan kesadaran hukum yang terukur. Pendidikan nilai yang berkesinambungan dengan dukungan keluarga dan masyarakat dibutuhkan untuk memperkuat penerapan nilai-nilai tersebut dalam keseharian anak.

title: A Complex-Valued Multiscale Feature Interaction Attention Vision Transformer for PolSAR Image Classification with Amplitude–Phase Decoupling
container-title: Remote Sensing
f13e49210f4d3150ec3c659afb2eca3e08fbaf06.abstract: Limited labeled data and class imbalance complicate polarimetric synthetic aperture radar (PolSAR) image classification. We propose a complex-valued multiscale feature interaction attention vision transformer (CV-MfIaViT) that combines spatial analytic-envelope preprocessing, complex-valued local feature extraction and global modeling. A two-dimensional Hilbert transform (2D HT) provides envelope features to the shallow pathway. The complex-valued amplitude–phase interaction attention (CV-APIA) module generates positive real gains through cross-modulation of pooled features; the final gating preserves the element-wise phase of non-zero input features. A complex-valued feature complementary mapper (CV-FCM), a complex-valued multiscale extractor (CV-MSE) and a complex-valued vision transformer (CV-ViT) complete the architecture. Under random-pixel sampling, the reported average accuracy (AA) exceeds CV-MsAtViT by 1.83, 3.42 and 2.48 percentage points on Flevoland, San Francisco and Nanjing, respectively. The advantage is also retained under spatial-block partitioning with shared label-free scene-level normalization. Component ablations and comparisons with two simple learned front ends characterize the combined design. The results support the evaluated architecture without isolating phase preservation as the cause of its accuracy gains.

title: MoEMamba: Mixture-of-Scale-And-Attention-Experts Mamba Network for Remote Sensing Change Detection
container-title: Remote Sensing
1aed84ad26277d2d4842952d811ce6774ae79d55.abstract: The Mamba network has recently emerged as a powerful architecture for remote sensing change detection (RSCD). Notably, the fusion of multi-scale features and heterogeneous attention mechanisms has proven effective in enhancing the performance of Mamba network. However, existing methods fail to quantitatively evaluate the actual contribution weights of different components during feature fusion, thereby limiting the interpretability of their improvements. To address this issue, this paper proposes a novel mixture-of-scale-and-attention-experts Mamba Network (MoEMamba) for the RSCD task, which has the following innovations and contributions: (1) a Siamese Mamba architecture is employed to extract features from bi-temporal images; (2) a mixture-of-scale-experts module is designed to enhance the generalization ability across multi-scale objects, which quantitatively evaluates the contribution of multiple scale-specific experts; and (3) a mixture-of-attention-experts module is proposed to improve the accuracy, which adaptively fuses complementary responses of heterogeneous attention mechanisms based on the learned weights. Extensive experiments on the WHU-CD and LEVIR-CD datasets demonstrate that MoEMamba outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods. Specifically, it achieves F1 scores of 94.20% and 92.62%, and IoU values of 89.04% and 86.25%, respectively. Importantly, this study provides valuable insights into the interpretability of multi-scale feature fusion and heterogeneous attention fusion for RSCD research.

title: Forest Digital Terrain Model from Copernicus GLO-30 DEM and GEDI L2A Using an Explainable Boosting Machine
container-title: Remote Sensing
94b8e327035bb7886e29043aa94be3457b60c44a.abstract: Accurate ground elevation beneath forest canopies is important for terrain and forest-structure analysis, yet satellite-based elevation data can be affected by canopy and terrain conditions, while spaceborne light detection and ranging (LiDAR) provides ground elevations only at discrete locations. Here, the elevation offset between the Copernicus GLO-30 DEM (CopDEM) and Global Ecosystem Dynamics Investigation (GEDI) L2A ground elevation was estimated using an Explainable Boosting Machine (EBM) with topographic, canopy-structure, and CopDEM-uncertainty predictors to generate continuous forest digital terrain models (DTMs) for two regions in the Republic of Korea. Validation against independent airborne LiDAR data showed root mean square errors (RMSEs) of the proposed DTM of 4.10 m in the central-western region and 3.67 m in the eastern region. In the EBM, the CopDEM height error mask (HEM), canopy cover, and aspect contributed most to the estimated offset, and the magnitude and direction of their contributions varied across canopy–terrain conditions and between regions. Residual bias increased with canopy height and became more negative on steep slopes, where RMSE also increased. These results show that the proposed approach can generate continuous forest DTMs while quantifying the contributions of the main predictors to the offset, their variation across environmental conditions, and the conditions under which residual errors increase.

title: The Video Essay as a Practice of Audiovisual Literacy in the Digital Society: A Case Study of Generation Z in Ecuadorian Higher Education
container-title: Societies
861520796a958abd7b41a49d561ce968b621982c.abstract: The consolidation of digital society has transformed the communication practices of new generations, and with them, the literacy demands facing higher education. In this context, the video essay emerges as a practice situated at the intersection of technological innovation, social change, and university education: based on audiovisual analysis, it requires its creators to interpret, argue, and communicate through images. This study examines how Generation Z university students appropriate the video essay as a practice of audiovisual literacy and a communication strategy of their own. A qualitative case study was conducted on 24 sixth-semester students in the Communication program at Universidad Técnica del Norte (Ibarra, Ecuador), combining the production of video essays, classroom observation, and focus groups; the 15 highest-rated video essays were purposively selected for in-depth analysis through thematic coding. Within this high-performing corpus, students redefined the video essay as a language of their own: they incorporated visual codes from the platforms they used but oriented them toward critical and sustained argumentation, which nuances techno-deterministic readings of this generation. The study provides situated evidence from an underrepresented region and offers insights for rethinking digital literacy in the university education of media communicators.

title: Strategic Drama Marketing and Consumer Reactions in Digital Commerce: Evidence from Thailand
container-title: Societies
86fb63fa6e9a55e1ac6f143ffd929aefc3859e34.abstract: Drama-based marketing has emerged as a distinctive form of digital marketing in which emotionally engaging narratives are used to capture attention, foster audience connection, and encourage consumer responses. This study examines the impact of strategic drama marketing—emotionally intense, narrative-driven content—on consumer purchase intention in Thailand. A sequential explanatory mixed-methods design was employed, combining survey data from 1350 respondents with in-depth interviews from 20 participants. Quantitative results indicate that emotional involvement and emotional connection with content creators significantly influence purchase intention, whereas emotional arousal and perceived sincerity do not. Perceived reliability—particularly authenticity, trust, and credibility—emerges as a strong predictor, while perceived justification of selling is insignificant. Platform dynamics, including social engagement, livestream interaction, and features that encourage continued viewing, significantly enhance purchase intention, whereas repeated exposure has no direct effect. Notably, overall perceived effectiveness of drama-based marketing is the strongest predictor. Qualitative findings reinforce these results, highlighting the roles of empathy, authenticity, and platform amplification in shaping consumer responses. This study contributes to the literature by integrating emotional, cognitive, and platform-driven perspectives to explain consumer behavior in emerging digital commerce environments.

title: Explainable Spatio-Temporal Graph Neural Networks for Dengue Outbreak Prediction: Environmental Data Integration and Policy Recommendation Framework in Yogyakarta, Indonesia
container-title: Oxford Open Digital Health
544462294382ebee0bb9a6fd26b6bcc6f0f5d234.abstract: Abstract Background Dengue fever is among the most rapidly spreading vector-borne diseases globally and a critical public health challenge in Indonesia, requiring evidence-based decisions supported by interpretable artificial intelligence (AI) systems rather than black-box prediction models with limited practical utility. Objective To demonstrate how an explainable Spatio-Temporal Graph Neural Network (STGNN) can generate actionable policy recommendations for dengue control by integrating environmental and surveillance data through interpretable AI mechanisms. Methods We developed Explain Dengue, a web-based platform implementing an STGNN with multi-head temporal attention, a graph attention network (GAT), and bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks, trained on dengue surveillance data (2021–2025) from Yogyakarta Province, Indonesia, using a chronological 70/10/20 train/validation/test split and an explicit 4-week forecast horizon, validated on 1300 weekly observations across five regions. Results Across five independently trained models, the STGNN achieved a mean (SD) test MAE of 7.50 (±0.48) cases/week and R2 of 0.265 (±0.102), outperforming seasonal-naive, gradient-boosting, and LSTM-only baselines. Using a statistical endemic-channel risk classification method (binary alert/no alert), the system achieved 77.6% accuracy (84.6% recall, 45.2% precision for alerts). Learned spatial attention was highly reproducible across seeds (r = 0.95), but an ablation-based faithfulness check found it was not a reliable causal explanation of predictions (r = −0.11), a limitation we discuss transparently. Conclusion A strictly held-out STGNN can outperform baselines for weekly dengue forecasting, offering a more evidence-based foundation for deploying explainable AI in vector-borne disease control, while surfacing an important caveat about the causal interpretability of learned attention.

title: Artificial Intelligence-Assisted Semi-automated Personal Health Data Curation and Reuse for Myocardial Infarction
container-title: European Heart Journal - Digital Health
6aab4ca5044a1448285d8de89a180d760962ec58.abstract: Abstract Background and Aims Digital applications have high potential in myocardial infarction management. This study aims to harmonize personal health data using a workflow driven by an Artificial Intelligence-assisted virtual assistant prototype, then reuse the data to facilitate the creation of standardized patient summaries and risk assessment. Methods The required configurations for data documentation and curation were developed to drive the workflow execution. With consent and data transfer agreements, data of patients with myocardial infarction were extracted from multi-source medical records, structured and ingested into the workflow. After transformation, personal health data were mapped into concrete clinical concepts connected with specific relationships defined by the reference ontology, forming source health knowledge graphs as the basic structure of personal health knowledge graphs. Then the constructed graphs were validated by using Shapes Constraint Language-based constraints, triggering the human-in-the-loop process to enhance data quality. Information queries were conducted for data reuse. Results 38 out of 45 planned patients were recruited with a signed informed consent. Thirty patients finalized the study. Overall successful data ingestion rate is approximately 83%. The average data quality score is 95.45/100. Constructed personal health knowledge graphs can be reused to represent medical information as an international patient summary and evaluate individual risk of future cardiovascular events by calculating the Second Manifestations of Arterial Disease risk score. Conclusion Our proposed workflow is feasible for semi-automated personal health data curation and secondary use. It provides a potential solution to enhance medical data interoperability, thereby facilitating risk assessment in cardiovascular diseases.

title: Contextualizing Sexual and Reproductive Health (SRH) Information to Develop an AI-enabled Chatbot for Adolescents with Disabilities in Ghana: Challenges and Strategies
container-title: Oxford Open Digital Health
c386ecaedfac0c46ae1ce3a07eadaf5fdefae494.abstract: Abstract Although artificial intelligence (AI) has proven to increase access to information on virtually any issue of human interest, not all content generated by AI may be appropriate for all consumers since socio-cultural and policy contexts vary. This paper demonstrates processes undertaken to contextualize sexual and reproductive health (SRH) data for adolescents with disabilities in Ghana for the purposes of training a chatbot to respond to their SRH information needs. Using design science research (DSR), and participatory approaches, medical and health promotion officers from the Ghana Health Service, who work on adolescent sexual and reproductive health, vetted 6591 question-and-answer pairs on adolescent sexual and reproductive health generated from OpenAI’s ChatGPT and Google’s Gemini. Employing content analysis, our findings after the vetting indicated that 1652 {25%} answers were modified, deleted, or expanded. This implies that without the review and validation, a notable amount of the SRH information would not have been relevant to the targeted end users. It is recommended that efforts to design AI solutions in SRH and other issues in Africa, which require the use of LLMs, should be deliberate about contextualizing the data generated to suit the targeted end-users.

title: Distributed and relational leadership in teachers’ digital resources use: Evidence from Shanghai's high-accountability school context
container-title: Educational Management Administration & Leadership
4555b48199403b966e85e83b57d9f5702789d487.abstract: Educational digitalization requires schools to translate institutional reform into teachers’ practice. Drawing on Social Cognitive Theory, this study examined the associations of distributed leadership (DL) and relational leadership (RL) with teachers’ digital resources use (DRU), and the mediating roles of teacher autonomy (TA) and digital resources use self-efficacy (DRUSE). Weighted TALIS 2024 data from 1364 Shanghai secondary school teachers were analyzed using complex-survey structural equation modelling and bootstrapping. In separate models, both leadership approaches had significant direct and indirect relationships with DRU. In the integrated model, DL retained a significant direct effect, whereas RL's direct and total effects were nonsignificant, although its indirect effects through TA, DRUSE and the sequential pathway remained significant. DL and RL differed significantly in their direct and total effects but not in their indirect effects. In Shanghai's high-accountability context, DL may be more closely connected with organizing digital reform, while RL is related to DRU primarily through teacher-level mechanisms. The strong correlation between DL and RL indicates potential multicollinearity when estimating their unique relationships. Because the data are cross-sectional, the results cannot establish temporal or causal ordering.

title: “I can Be Responsible With Digital Technology”: What Children Want Adults to Know About Their Use of Digital Technologies for Learning and Play
container-title: Australasian Journal of Early Childhood
644be752a5e6d6fd7c188a0a70de69cdcacc8c1d.abstract: Children have a right to participate in decisions shaping their lives, including how digital technologies are integrated into learning and everyday practices. This research explores children’s perspectives on digital learning and play, foregrounding their voices as central to inclusive, rights-based pedagogies. Building on research with early childhood educators, we engaged children (aged 6–11) and three 12-year-old co-researchers in a deliberative World Café workshop. Through arts-based methods, embodied practices, and dialogic engagement, children discussed research data, voted on key issues, and collaboratively developed recommendations. Challenging dominant assumptions surrounding children’s technology use, children positioned themselves as aware and agentic; wanting adults to see them as responsible digital citizens. Children demonstrated nuanced understandings of opportunities and risks and envisaged digital futures where child-adult relationships are reconfigured and context-sensitive decision-making supported. This paper advances the field by situating children as co-constructors of knowledge, co-interpreters of data, and co-regulators of their digital lives.

title: The Impact of Digital Learning Tools on the Academic  Performance of Secondary School Students in Nigeria: An  Empirical Review
container-title: INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF EDUCATION AND EVALUATION
14d99b4e7b330b735e2ba6297fccb1e1754dbd57.abstract: Nigeria’s National Digital Learning Policy promises inclusive digital learning for all, yet it remains unclear what digital tools actually do for secondary school students’ academic performance. This study reviewed empirical evidence on the impact of digital learning tools on the academic performance of secondary school students in Nigeria. A narrative, thematic review design was adopted. Twelve Nigerian studies published between 2011 and 2024 and covering eight states, comprising five experiments, two meta-analyses, one programme evaluation, three surveys and one national panel survey, were identified through Google Scholar, DOAJ, RePEc/IDEAS and university repositories, and synthesised under six themes. The review found that teacher-led computer-assisted instruction and computer animation generally improved achievement in mathematics and the sciences, although the gains varied by subject, with a mean effect size of 0.52 across science subjects but only 0.05 in Chemistry, and were sometimes smaller than those of non-digital methods such as problem-solving. By contrast, Osun State’s Opon-imo tablet programme was associated with lower English Language performance, and findings on social media use were mixed. Limited ICT facilities, low teacher competence, poor connectivity and unstable electricity restricted the benefits of digital learning, while gender made no significant difference. The study concludes that the value of digital tools depends less on the devices themselves than on how teachers use them and whether students can access them. It recommends teacher-led integration rather than device distribution alone, continuous teacher training, investment in power and connectivity, and more rigorous research, particularly in Northern Nigeria.

title: Combining digital outcomes of mobility with mobile brain imaging to predict future Parkinson’s disease
container-title: Communications in Kinesiology
197d12a979e997dacc7d49cdcea087bfa9399bd9.abstract: Introduction: Neurodegeneration represents a major health and economic crisis worldwide. Yet, transitioning from healthy brain aging to neurodegeneration is a prolonged process, including subtle pre-clinical features that, if identified, could lead to earlier diagnostic certainty. Individuals with isolated REM sleep Behaviour Disorder (iRBD) (i.e., those who enact their dreams) are 130 times more likely to eventually develop a synucleinopathy (i.e., approximately 50 % develop Parkinson’s disease (PD) versus dementia with Lewy bodies (DLB)) over a 10-15 year span, making iRBD the best current prodromal marker for predicting future neurodegeneration. However, iRBD alone does not reveal when a diagnosis can be made; individuals may be diagnosed in 5 or 15 years (Postuma et al., 2012). Whilst simple motor deficits in iRBD have been argued as one of the best predictors in iRBD for developing PD (Postuma et al., 2019), most of the evidence to date has evaluated walking speed, while neglecting more sensitive assessments such as postural stability, gait variability, gait asymmetry, and turning which are known to be impacted by pathology in brainstem regions. Recent work suggests that quantitative balance, gait and turning outcomes may be even more sensitive (Alibiglou et al., 2016; Ehgoetz Martens et al., 2019, 2020, 2022; MacKinnon et al., 2019; McDade et al., 2013). In fact, subtle balance and gait deficits can be exposed by challenging the motor system by manipulating sensory feedback or adding a concurrent cognitive task (dual task) (Ehgoetz Martens et al., 2019), which can interfere with compensation from prefrontal cognitive control networks often masking early motor signs due to declining motor automaticity. Quantitative, continuous monitoring with wearable technologies shows tremendous promise as well, however, the field is in its infancy since only a handful of studies have examined balance and gait deficits in iRBD using quantitative approaches beyond a stopwatch, and even fewer that have manipulated cognitive or sensory load or attempted to monitor individuals at home. Thus, a comprehensive set of sensitive and robust mobility assessments needs to be tested to reveal the optimal assessment that unmasks unique and subtle motor deficits in iRBD and determine their predictive utility for phenoconversion from iRBD to either PD or DLB. Only then can recommendations be made for the design of clinical trials to include sensitive motor assessments that best monitor and predict prodromal disease progression.Examining behaviour, however, does not always reveal the full picture, since the brain is well equipped to adapt and compensate as it undergoes progressive neurodegeneration. Several insights can be gained from examining the neural correlates of motor performance in early prodromal populations like iRBD. Functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS), an advanced technique to measure oxygenated hemoglobin levels (HbO2), can tolerate bodily movements, and is a non-invasive technique. This makes fNIRS suitable for both healthy and clinical populations to enable the assessment of changes in brain activation during gait to estimate cortical hemodynamic responses that occur in response to neural activity. While understanding the neural basis that underpins balance and gait deficits during the prodrome provides added insight into the neurodegenerative process, it is also instrumental for interpretating behaviour and making inferences for predictions for future disease progression.The objectives of this research are 1) to evaluate and optimize a comprehensive set of quantitative mobility assessments by comparing the performance outcomes in participants with iRBD to that of healthy control participants (HC); and 2) to understand early compensation related to prodromal neurodegeneration by evaluating cortical activation during motor performance using mobile neuroimaging in iRBD compared to PD and HCs.Methods: To evaluate objectives 1 and 2, 20 iRBD (67.8 years old), 27 age-matched HC participants (69.0 years old) were assessed in the clinic using wearable inertial measurement units (IMUs). After being outfitted with sensors, each participant underwent a motor and cognitive examination (UPDRS; MoCA). The participant was outfitted with a portable fNIRS system to measure HbO2 levels in the prefrontal cortex (PFC) while completing a comprehensive battery of validated balance and gait assessments. The clinical mobility assessment battery consisted of: (i) 30 second quiet stance with eyes open; (ii) 30 second quiet stance on a foam surface; (iii) 60 second alternating 360° turns test; (iv) 60 second alternating 360° turns test while performing the forward digit span (FDS, attention/working memory); (v) a self-paced 2 minute walk; (vi) a self-paced 2 minute walk while performing the forward digit span; (vii) a 2 minute dual-task walk while performing the oral Trail Making Test Part B (DT-TMB, executive function); (viii) a 2 minute dual-task walk while performing the auditory clock test (DT-AC, visuospatial); (ix) MiniBest test. A seated assessment of the forward digit span, Trail Making Test Part B, and auditory clock test were also completed to calculate dual-task interference. Participants also completed several questionnaires (Mayo sleep questionnaire, cognitive reserve index, life space assessment, movement specific reinvestment scale, hospital anxiety and depression scale, falls efficacy scale, activity-specific balance confidence scale). Different dual task walking trials were used to evaluate interference with attention, executive function, and visuospatial cognition. This cohort was also part of a larger sampler (23 iRBD, 61 HC) that completed remote continuous monitoring of gait over 7 days, where participants wore three IMUs (lumbar spine, bilateral feet) to collect measures of gait and turning during daily life. title: Impact of machine-based core muscle strengthening on back muscle function in chronic low back pain across age groups and sexes: Results of a prospective surface electromyographic fatigue study
container-title: Communications in Kinesiology
189589e9fe398125318d625953b15923f0f3c779.abstract: Introduction: The impact of aging on core muscle training outcomes on chronic low back pain (CLBP) remains poorly understood. This study investigated whether a 6-month machine-based core muscle strengthening (MB-CMS) program would produce differential surface electromyography (SEMG) fatigue-related responses in younger versus older males and females with CLBP. Methods: Four cohorts with CLBP (younger males [n= 53; mean age 35.3 ± 9.6], younger females [n= 43 mean age 32.9 ±10.4]; older males [n= 48; mean age: 64.8 ± 8.4]; older females [n= 48, mean age: 64.3 ± 7.2]) completed a 6-month rehabilitation program with 40 MB-CMS sessions. SEMG monitoring was performed during back extensions at 80% of maximum effort from the multifidus (L5), longissimus (L2), and iliolumbalis lumborum (L1). The primary outcome was median frequency fatigue slope (MDF-SEMG), normalized to onset, measured bilaterally. Secondary outcomes included MDF-SEMG and root mean square (RMS)-SEMG at fatigue-test onset. A mixed-effects model analyzed SEMG changes across recording sites. Results: At baseline, older individuals had significantly higher Body Mass Index scores than younger ones [2.2 (95%CI:1.1;3.4)]. Maximum back extension strength and trunk flexibility were comparable at baseline and improved significantly, without relevant differences between age- and sex-specific groups [younger vs older: 1.4 (95%CI:-11.2;14.0); younger vs older males: 1.8 (95%CI:-18.4;22.0), younger vs older females: 2.1 (95%CI:-12.6;16.8)]. Initial fear avoidance behavior and pain rating scores were similar across groups and improved after the intervention in all groups except older females(younger males: -0.4 (95%CI:-0.6;-0.2); older males: -0.4 (95%CI:-0.6;-0.2); younger females: -0.4 (95%CI:-0.5;-0.2); older females: -0.1 (95%CI:-0.3;+0.1). Baseline endurance behavior was similar across groups and remained unchanged after intervention. Roland Morris Disability Questionnaire scores were higher in older than in younger male and female participants and improved significantly within groups, without notable differences in age and sex. After intervention, MDF-SEMG fatigue changed toward steeper slopes in younger males (L5, L2) and older females (L5), without significant age- or sex-related between-group effects. Pooled sites showed greater changes in younger individuals. RMS-SEMG initial values showed a significant age-group effect (p<0.001), with increases in younger participants, except L2 in females, but not in older ones. MDF-SEMG fatigue changes correlated positively with enhanced spine sagittal flexibility (p<0.001). Changes in MB-CMS-related RMS-SEMG initial values indicate greater increases in back extensor muscle excitability in younger people with CLBP than in older ones. Conclusions: MDF-SEMG fatigue findings remain ambiguous. Because age-related disuse rather than hypertrophic muscle alterations may have increased MDF-SEMG fatigue in multifidi, particularly in older females with CLBP, MB-CMS protocols may require adaptation to prevent spinal degeneration during long-term training in these patients. Disclosure: *R.H. and G.E. contributed equally to the study.

title: Privacy-Aware Adaptive Mental State Intelligence for AI-Assisted Decision-Making in Digital Mental Health Systems: Architecture and Empirical Evaluation
container-title: Computer and Decision Making: An International Journal
2ddfc9058ffad2682f1b441344c6bcf16a00aa44.abstract: Opportunities to anticipate changes in depressive symptoms are provided by longitudinal digital mental-health records, but the usefulness of algorithmic recommendations and the preservation of model utility under privacy protections cannot be established from predictive accuracy alone. A Privacy-Aware Adaptive Mental State Intelligence (PA-AMSI) architecture was specified and evaluated using the Corona Health smartphone dataset. Historical Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9) assessments were used to predict five symptom-severity categories 14–30 days ahead. Following duplicate-origin correction and participant-disjoint partitioning, 6,314 forecasting samples from 903 participants were retained; 5,025 samples from 722 participants were allocated to development, and 1,289 samples from 181 participants were reserved for a single locked-test evaluation. Persistence, centralized classifiers, simulated federated averaging, and participant-clipped Gaussian-noised training were compared. On the locked test, the highest macro-F1 (0.6541) was obtained with persistence, whereas the highest accuracy (0.7168) was obtained with Random Forest. A macro-F1 of 0.2743 was obtained with the Gaussian-noised model, and none of the 46 severe-class assessments was detected. Under a predefined illustrative loss matrix, a lower mean simulated decision cost was obtained with the questionnaire-only policy (0.5531) than with Random Forest-assisted (0.6175) and privacy-noised (0.6594) policies. Higher costs for the AI-assisted policies were supported by participant-cluster bootstrap intervals. It is therefore shown that privacy assumptions, class-specific reliability, and decision consequences must be assessed together before digital mental-health prediction systems are considered for clinical evaluation.

title: Exploring Inquiry-Based Learning with Digital Portfolios: Preparing Teacher Candidates to Practice Multiliteracies
container-title: International Journal of Mass Communication
6a81ff9a402b64b51fbd998bc7d90c4db2706e98.abstract: Literacy instruction in today’s school settings should extend beyond print-based reading and writing by teaching students to read, write, synthesize, evaluate, and communicate in multimodal ways. Therefore, teachers need deep knowledge of technology, pedagogy, and content along with an understanding of the multimodal nature of digital texts and environments. Guided by theoretical frameworks of Multiliteracies and TPACK, this research explored how a graduate-level literacy course prepared teacher candidates to practice multiliteracies through engaging them with inquiry-based learning by making digital portfolios. The purpose of the study was to explore how educational scholars can respond to and re-envision teaching and learning for the technology-saturated educational landscape of the 21st century through integration of multimodal texts and practices.

title: Digital Literacy Education Through the Use of the Byond By BSI Application to Improve Understanding of Sharia Finance among the Sukabumi City Community
container-title: Escalate : Economics and Business Journal
19a13313f93fe7c7c57e58c6f4e1f4ad5a851d25.abstract: Low levels of Islamic financial literacy remain a challenge in supporting the optimization of digital banking services in Indonesia. This condition has prevented the public from optimally utilizing Islamic digital banking services, including the BYOND by BSI application. This community service activity aims to improve the understanding of Islamic financial literacy in Sukabumi City residents through digital education and assistance in using the BYOND by BSI application. The target group includes members of the healthcare worker group and micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs). The implementation method consisted of needs assessment, counseling, demonstrations of application features, practical assistance, and evaluation through discussions and observations of participant understanding. The results of the activity showed that participants had a better understanding of the basic principles of Islamic finance, were able to differentiate between Islamic and conventional banking products, understood the use of the main features of the BYOND by BSI application, and were more aware of the importance of security in digital transactions. The educational approach combined with hands-on practice has proven effective in improving Islamic financial literacy in the community and encouraging more optimal use of Islamic digital banking services.
