title: Digital Healthcare Pharmacovigilance in India: Adverse-Event Reporting, Data Interoperability, and AI-Assisted Safety Signal Detection
container-title: Indian Journal of Computer Science and Technology
801fdc9a829e67942ac6ae61e588afad8d3794df.abstract: The field of pharmacovigilance deals with timely data acquisition, coding, evaluation, and analysis of adverse drug reactions (ADRs) to medicines, vaccines, and medicinal products. The digital environment in India is evolving, and PvPI works through adverse reaction monitoring centers, while Indian Pharmacopoeia Commission has developed Adverse Drug Monitoring System (ADRMS) web portal in August 2024. While digital reporting can avoid bureaucratic hurdles, the worthiness of such platforms would be determined by the completeness of reports, consistency in language use, traceability, handling of duplicate reports, and the process that leads from the report to the evaluation stage by experts. This narrative review will cover the Indian reporting environment, the technical function of Individual Case Safety Reports (ICSRs) and E2B(R3), and possible contributions of machine-assisted technologies to case acquisition and safety signal prioritisation. It does not intend to compare AI models or provide a survey of clinical artificial intelligence. Rather, it reviews how the quality of digital reporting and data standards impact the safe implementation of such automation. The academic literature suggests that natural language processing and machine learning techniques can be used for extraction, coding, duplicate detection, and prioritization; however, the effectiveness of their performance depends on the quality of the source and context of use. Spontaneous report information continues to be hypothesis generating and does not prove causality on its own. A synthesis specific to the particular workflow process, where each automation step is coupled with validation needs, human responsibility, and metrics of process performance, is suggested. The analysis results in the conclusion that India’s best defense is to build structured data capturing and interoperability and only then consider automation.

title: Tantangan Redaksi BETV dalam Menghadapi Era Artificial Intelligence (AI) pada Produksi Pemberitaan Digital di BETV Disway.id
container-title: Jurnal Ragam Pengabdian
ffa07793fcc4b39b9d5fa6a27979ce637c9ccd2d.abstract: Perkembangan Artificial Intelligence (AI) telah membawa perubahan signifikan dalam industri media dan jurnalistik, khususnya pada proses produksi pemberitaan digital. Meskipun AI menawarkan efisiensi kerja, keberadaannya juga menghadirkan tantangan bagi redaksi media dalam menjaga akurasi, verifikasi, dan etika jurnalistik. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mengetahui dan mendeskripsikan tantangan yang dihadapi redaksi BETV.disway.id dalam menghadapi era Artificial Intelligence (AI) pada proses produksi pemberitaan digital. Penelitian ini menggunakan pendekatan kualitatif dengan jenis penelitian deskriptif. Data dikumpulkan melalui wawancara mendalam, observasi, dan dokumentasi, dengan tiga informan yang terdiri dari General Manager, wartawan, dan redaktur BETV Disway.id. Analisis data dilakukan melalui reduksi data, penyajian data, dan penarikan kesimpulan, serta dikaitkan dengan Teori Difusi Inovasi Everett M. Rogers (2003). Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa BETV Disway.id belum menjadikan AI sebagai alat utama dalam produksi pemberitaan. Proses produksi berita masih dilakukan secara langsung oleh wartawan melalui peliputan, pengumpulan data, wawancara, verifikasi, dan penulisan, kemudian diperiksa dan disunting oleh redaktur sebelum dipublikasikan. Tantangan utama yang dihadapi redaksi bukan hanya kemampuan teknis menggunakan AI, tetapi juga pengawasan terhadap kemungkinan penggunaannya, kesiapan sumber daya manusia, serta upaya mempertahankan kualitas, verifikasi, etika, dan peran manusia dalam proses produksi pemberitaan digital.

title: DIGITAL SUPPORT FOR THE PRIORITIZATION OF GREEN INVESTMENT PROJECTS IN UKRAINE’S POST-WAR RECONSTRUCTION
container-title: Economic Scope
609b971281a42e33b57366c579ca0ee7a90d3fd1.abstract: Ukraine’s post-war reconstruction requires substantial investment resources, making the transparent and well-grounded prioritization of investment projects particularly important. The purpose of this study is to develop a methodological approach to prioritizing green investment projects and to establish a functional model for the digital support of the corresponding assessment procedure.The study draws on a systematic analysis of approaches to public investment prioritization, sustainability assessment, and digitalization of public investment management. A three-stage procedure is proposed, distinguishing strategic alignment, compliance with green investment requirements, and comparative project ranking. Five groups of prioritization criteria are identified: economic performance, environmental benefits, resilience and social significance, financial capacity, and project feasibility. The proposed assessment procedure involves indicator normalization, weighted aggregation, and sensitivity analysis to examine the robustness of project rankings.A functional model of digital support is developed to link the stages of project assessment with the required information resources, digital processing operations, and evaluation outputs. The model comprises information, analytical, and control and documentation components. Its implementation may rely on existing categories of digital tools for standardized project data collection, automated calculations, verification, and traceability of assessment results.The proposed approach provides a methodological basis for transparent, comparable, and reproducible assessment of green investment alternatives within Ukraine’s public investment management system. Project rankings are regarded as analytical inputs to investment decisions rather than automatic funding allocations. Further research should focus on empirical testing of the proposed procedure and assessing the robustness of rankings under alternative weighting scenarios.

title: PUBLIC-PRIVATE PARTNERSHIP IN DIGITAL INFRASTRUCTURE AS A MECHANISM FOR ATTRACTING INVESTMENT IN HIGH-TECH DEVELOPMENT: INTERNATIONAL EXPERIENCE AND LESSONS FOR UKRAINE
container-title: Economic Scope
67011a30c8ef8abfc5fb6106deb5c90cfaa3555a.abstract: The article examines public-private partnership (PPP) in digital infrastructure as a mechanism for attracting investment, including international capital, for high-tech development. The aim of the article is to substantiate the role of PPP in digital infrastructure as an institutional mechanism for attracting investment to foster high-tech development; to identify the factors determining the effectiveness of various contractual arrangements for such partnerships; to propose a model of threshold conditions for transitioning from financing to technology transfer; and to outline the possibilities for its application in Ukraine. The concepts of international investment, foreign direct investment, PPP and technology transfer are distinguished. Based on a comparative analysis of four diverse broadband infrastructure cases – the KT Rwanda Networks joint venture (Rwanda), the planned BharatNet concession (India), the public initiative network concessions under the France Très Haut Débit plan (France), and the long-term lease of the Huntsville Utilities municipal fibre network to Google Fiber (USA) – the institutional, financial and managerial factors of partnership performance are identified. It is shown that high service coverage does not guarantee the financial sustainability of a partnership (Rwanda, where deteriorating financial results ended with the cancellation of exclusive terms), while approved budget co-financing does not guarantee even the emergence of a private partner (India, where the concession tender attracted no qualified bidders). A conceptual model of the PPP “performance corridor” is proposed. It is argued that PPP performance is determined not by the mere attraction of private capital but by the quality of risk allocation, contractual requirements for competence development and the state’s bargaining capacity. Public materials do not allow the scale of competence transfer to be assessed in any of the cases, nor whether the contracts contained relevant requirements and how they were fulfilled; this calls for analysis of the contracts themselves and for public reporting on competence development. Drawing on Law of Ukraine No. 4510-IX, the prerequisites and limitations of using PPP in digital infrastructure during post-war recovery are outlined.

title: DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION OF ENTERPRISE HUMAN RESOURCE AUDIT
container-title: Economic Scope
bf37807cabc7294fb60fcad04bac51258b8901d0.abstract: The mass transition to remote and hybrid employment formats has exposed the limitations of conventional retrospective human resource control. Relying on manual cross-referencing of timesheets after the reporting period generates delayed information, preventing management from effectively optimizing working time and labor costs. This article develops applied instruments for the digital transformation of enterprise human resource audits by implementing continuous auditing principles and cloud computing architecture. The methodology synthesizes structural-functional modeling with new institutional economics and data-driven decision-making. The research designs a practical four-tier continuous audit model. The primary tier executes automated data collection directly from corporate ERP databases, HRM platforms, task trackers, and physical access registers. Next, the extract, transform, load (ETL) pipeline unifies diverse data formats and enforces mandatory pseudonymization of personnel records, guaranteeing compliance with the GDPR and national privacy legislation. At the analytical core, the system utilizes deterministic control scripts to verify time-tracking data while applying machine learning algorithms to identify behavioral anomalies. This helps auditors detect simulated remote work activity and diagnose early symptoms of professional burnout. The visualization tier translates these findings into dynamic dashboards and immediate alerts. Transitioning personnel data to external cloud servers introduces regulatory, cybersecurity, technological, and behavioral vulnerabilities. To neutralize these threats, the study proposes evaluating objective key performance indicators and key results instead of tracking screen time. Technical protection is achieved through zero-trust architecture protocols and end-to-end encryption. The economic feasibility of this transformation is validated using a four-stage assessment procedure. This framework calculates the total cost of ownership by aggregating capital expenditures for software integration and operational expenditures for cloud subscriptions. The final audit opinion compares this cost against direct payroll savings achieved by eliminating unrecorded downtimes, incorporating the financial value of averting regulatory fines and minimizing turnover expenses.

d1489dedc0050f9d555295dd3a194ea811ae5e90.abstract: This community service program aims to enhance the capacity of Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) in utilizing live commerce. The program was held at the Cisayong District Hall and attended by 34 MSME owners. A participatory approach was employed, with participants engaging directly in discussions and hands-on practice using their own mobile devices. Initially, participants encountered various challenges, such as not having accounts, difficulties with synchronization, and technical hurdles in uploading products. Through intensive guidance and practical exercises, the results showed that approximately 80 percent of the participants successfully conducted live broadcasts and offered their products independently. These findings indicate that practice-based live commerce training is effective in improving the digital readiness of MSMEs and fostering a shift toward sales strategies that are more interactive and adaptive to the evolution of the digital marketplace.

title: Digital ethics – polscy konsumenci wobec wyzwań etycznych związanych z rozwojem technologii
bb54e283e567b03cfc8be71e9fa35119389a58a1.abstract: Tematyka etyki w świecie technologii jest szerokim zagadnieniem. Autorom zależało na zbadaniu zjawisk i technologii, które są wykorzystywane i znane przez grupę objętą badaniem. Projektując badanie mieli również na uwadze różnorodne obszary, w jakich technologia jest obecna i stosowana przez konsumentki i konsumentów, stąd próba poznania ich zachowań w życiu zawodowym i prywatnym.Raport podzielony został na kilka części, które ułatwiają poruszanie się po poszczególnych wymiarach. Osoby czytające przeprowadzone zostaną przez takie tematy jak:• autorytety i wartości,• sztuczna inteligencja,• konsument i technologie – wątpliwości etyczne,• obawy wobec technologii.Zbadano postrzeganie generatywnej sztucznej inteligencji oraz innych towarzyszących nam technologii w kontekście wyzwań etycznych, bezpieczeństwa użytkowania, odpowiedzialności podmiotów ale i świadomości z czym wiąże się zostawianie śladów cyfrowych. Badanie zrealizowane zostało przez firmę Minds and Roses na reprezentatywnej grupie 1000 dorosłych użytkowników internetu w maju 2026 roku metodą CAWI.

title: Association Between Digital Device use and Dry Eye Symptoms Among Students at Medical Colleges in Punjab, Pakistan
container-title: Journal of Global Social Transformation
b7aff176f986f08b3ecbd86cfa5cf6a434355d45.abstract: Background: Ocular discomfort is a concern among students who regularly use digital devices. We examined the association between digital-device use and dry-eye symptoms among students attending medical colleges in Punjab, Pakistan. Methods: This analytical cross-sectional study included 194 students recruited through non-probability consecutive sampling between 12 July and 25 October 2026. A self-administered Google Forms questionnaire assessed digital-device use, ocular health, and lifestyle characteristics. Symptoms were measured using the Ocular Surface Disease Index (OSDI). Primary symptom analyses included participants completing all 12 items. Multivariable linear regression with HC3 robust standard errors examined weekday screen-time categories, adjusting for age, sex, contact-lens use, and current ocular conditions. Results: Median participant age was 21 years (interquartile range: 19–23). Daily screen exposure of ≥6 hours was reported by 42.3% on weekdays and 64.9% on weekends. Among 114 participants completing the OSDI, the mean score was 39.3 ± 21.2; 103 screened positive (90.4%; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 83.5%–94.5%), including 62 (54.4%) with severe symptoms. In the adjusted analysis (n=113), weekday screen-time category was not significantly associated with symptom scores overall (p=0.214). Higher scores were associated with male sex (adjusted difference: 17.42 points; 95% CI: 8.81–26.02), regular contact-lens use (16.80; 3.47–30.13), and current ocular conditions (11.67; 2.76–20.59). Conclusion: Symptom burden was high among respondents completing the OSDI. Weekday screen duration showed no significant adjusted association with severity, although estimates were imprecise. The findings support attention to student ocular health and further investigation using clinical examinations and prospective exposure measurement.

title: <b>Digital Connectivity and Labor Productivity in Emerging Economies: The Moderating Roles of Human Capital and ICT Capability</b>
container-title: International Journal of Emerging Multidisciplinaries: Social Science
50b9202f9167a91dc78f21510b29ce5656fec2f2.abstract: The contribution of digital connectivity to productivity could also depend on the human and technological capacity to utilize the digital technological infrastructure, and this is a growing concern. The study explores the association between digital connectivity and labour productivity and assesses whether human capital and ICT capability strengthen this relationship in the six developing Asian economies in this study (namely Pakistan, India, Malaysia, the Philippines, Thailand and Indonesia) during 2005-2024. Labour productivity is calculated as GDP per labour, and digital connectivity is operationalized through using the number of fixed internet broadband subscriptions per 100 populations. Other factors that are also incorporate in the econometric framework are foreign direct investment, gross capital formation, and inflation. To control for the possibility of cross-country dependence and for the possible differential response of countries, the analysis is conducted using fixed-effects estimation with Driscoll–Kraay standard errors and a sensitivity assessment of the Common Correlated Effects Mean Group (CCE-MG) estimation. The baseline findings imply a positive and significant association between digital connectivity and worker productivity. Moreover, the interaction effects imply that this relationship is strengthened by higher levels of human capital and ICT capability, and that the productivity improvements from having broadband connectivity are higher the stronger the complementary levels of human and technological capabilities. The CCE-MG estimates, nevertheless, do not lead to statistically significant direct and interaction effects, suggesting that the base relations are affected by unobserved shared latent factors and inter-country heterogeneity. The conclusions are accordingly a warning against thinking of broadband expansion as a standalone solution for productivity improvements. Policies designed to enhance the productivity-enhancing outcomes of digital technological infrastructure for developing economies should involve investing in connectivity, along with improving education, digital skills, ICT capability, and technological development, allowing for variations in the country-specific economic conditions.

title: A comunicação de más notícias na perspectiva de familiares de pessoas com doenças neurodegenerativas
Communicating bad news from the perspective of family members of people with neurodegenerative diseases
container-title: Revista Saber Digital
73d9090b2600d6c18a329d4aad0426aa8579a479.abstract: Introdução: Uma boa comunicação é fundamental nos atendimentos médicos dado o seu potencial para fortalecer o vínculo e a confiança na relação dos profissionais com os pacientes e seus familiares. Porém, comunicar é uma ação complexa e desafiadora, sobretudo quando se trata de más notícias. Objetivo: O objetivo do presente estudo foi investigar a perspectiva de familiares sobre os desafios relacionados ao contexto de más notícias no acompanhamento médico de parentes diagnosticados com Doenças Neurodegenerativas, além de identificar formas consideradas mais ou menos adequadas pelos familiares de os profissionais transmitirem este tipo de notícias. Materiais e método: Participaram 14 familiares adultos de pessoas idosas com Doença de Alzheimer ou de Parkinson, que responderam a um questionário sociodemográfico autoadministrado e, posteriormente, participaram de entrevista semiestruturada, realizada de modo individual e online. Os dados obtidos foram submetidos a Análise de Conteúdo de Bardin. Resultados e discussão: A partir da análise dos dados foram criadas quatro categorias: modos de transmissão da notícia, participação ativa do familiar no processo de comunicação, atenção aos aspectos emocionais do familiar e familiar porta-voz de más notícias à família. Frente às más notícias recebidas, os familiares apontaram como desejáveis a objetividade, sinceridade e delicadeza na comunicação, além de uma resposta de atenção e escuta à família. Por outro lado, viram como inadequadas a insensibilidade no anúncio da má notícia e a falta de suporte posterior. Conclusão: Conclui-se que a comunicação de notícias difíceis demanda sensibilidade e preparo dos profissionais para o alcance de práticas comunicacionais mais humanizadas e capazes de reduzir o sofrimento dos familiares.

title: Women Engineers’ Occupational Safety in Iraq’s Construction Sector: Site Exposure, Gender-Responsive Working Conditions, and Digital Safety Reporting
container-title: Buildings
ce6c3eae785ed9ddeaf024ba86d7be0855df60c1.abstract: Safe and inclusive construction workplaces require more than conventional hazard control; they also depend on suitable welfare provision, personal protective equipment (PPE), reporting arrangements, and gender-responsive working conditions. This study examines women engineers’ occupational-safety experiences in Iraq’s construction sector through site exposure, welfare and privacy conditions, PPE suitability, gendered workplace interactions, reporting climate, and perceptions of digital and AI-enabled support. A survey-based design combining quantitative items with open-ended responses was used with 215 valid responses from women engineers in construction-related roles. Quantitative analysis included descriptive statistics, reliability analysis, ranked item means, Kruskal–Wallis tests, effect sizes, and Dunn post-hoc comparisons, while open-ended responses were analyzed thematically. Respondents strongly supported sanitary facilities, safe transportation, suitable PPE, contractor obligations, rest areas, managerial training, confidential reporting, women’s participation in safety committees, and anonymous digital reporting. Significant unadjusted differences were found across site-exposure groups for several safety, reporting, gender-related, and improvement dimensions. After adjustment, the associations remained significant for preparedness, safety concern, reporting barriers, and improvement priorities, but not for gender barriers. Open-ended responses emphasized male-dominated workplace culture, weak safety enforcement, welfare and privacy gaps, management practices, and transportation constraints. Digital and AI-enabled reporting options were viewed positively, alongside concerns about privacy, confidentiality, and organizational response. The findings suggest that safer and more inclusive construction workplaces should address site-exposure-sensitive arrangements, gender-responsive safety provisions, trusted reporting mechanisms, and carefully governed digital support.

title: Community Environment-Health Pathways from a Behavioural Perspective: A Study of Preschool Visual Acuity Using Digital Environmental Representation
container-title: Buildings
cdc5e708470c0f4952737c8a4f2f620f8d0ac43e.abstract: Health and wellbeing form a core dimension of urban resilience. Addressing this dimension requires attention to the everyday environments that support healthy living. To explore how daily activity may connect community environments with health, this study uses preschool visual acuity as a specific health outcome. A cross-sectional analysis examined environment-activity-visual acuity associations among 195 children aged 3–6 years in Shanghai. Path analysis used a structured digital representation comprising 13 parent-perceived indicators and five mapped measures in the contextual model. The clearest pattern centred on perceived greenery, which was consistently associated with longer outdoor duration in the primary and contextual models. Both associations met the pointwise and hypothesis-specific Holm criteria, although neither met the main analysis-based criterion. Other environmental attributes showed weaker, activity-specific associations. Outdoor-acuity and corresponding greenery-outdoor activity-visual acuity indirect estimates were positive, but their confidence intervals included zero, and neither met the Holm-adjusted criterion. The findings suggest outdoor activity as a potential behavioural link between perceived neighbourhood greenery and reported visual acuity. The digital representation brings parental assessments and physical conditions into a common framework for examining how community environments relate to activity and health. This approach can inform the health and wellbeing priorities of urban resilience planning and their application in child-friendly communities.

title: The Structure of Digital Brand Engagement: Multidimensional Item-Response Evidence Across Consumption, Contribution and Creation
container-title: Journal of Theoretical and Applied Electronic Commerce Research
33c52006dda7499c2c07cd5a3633071a6128f9db.abstract: Digital brand engagement scores can obscure the participation they summarise. This study examines consumers’ online brand-related activities (COBRAs) using 17 indicators from 384 technology-start-up users in Guayaquil, Ecuador. Five graded response models, paired ordinal contrasts, conditional information, exact-score comparisons and firm-held-out payment models evaluate structure, ordering and scoring consequences. Three correlated domains outperformed one dimension (BIC reduction = 650.43) and every pairwise merger; correlations ranged from 0.575 to 0.710. Consumption, contribution and creation followed the expected order at all four empirical response cutoffs, preserving that aggregate order under every common increasing category recoding. All eight simultaneous participant-bootstrap contrasts were positive; seven remained conclusive in the nine-firm cluster sensitivity analysis. Only 33.6% of users had strictly descending domain scores. Exact overall-score groups containing descending and inverted profiles covered 91.4% of users, with 24.1–29.5% of domain-score variability unresolved within score groups. Separate domains yielded a payment-classification AUC of 0.614 versus 0.606 for the overall score, with nearly identical held-out log loss. The contribution specifies the hierarchy’s aggregate meaning and quantifies the behavioural detail obscured by scoring. Domain profiles support participation diagnosis; their additional commercial classification value requires separate validation. Cross-sectional evidence cannot identify individual transitions or causal commercial effects.

title: The Impact of Online Review Information Overload on Platform Churn Intention: The Serial Mediating Role of Cognitive Fatigue and Decision Postponement
container-title: Journal of Theoretical and Applied Electronic Commerce Research
3ac6d9cd7a89309f4dedaae7559de137982d56ab.abstract: This study investigates how online review information overload is associated with platform churn intention through the serial mediating roles of cognitive fatigue and decision postponement. Drawing on Cognitive Load Theory and Ego Depletion Theory, the study proposes that excessive volume and complexity of online reviews are associated with cognitive fatigue, which is in turn associated with decision postponement and, ultimately, with review-engaged consumers’ intention to direct future purchases away from the platform. Survey data were collected from 350 consumers of an online cosmetics shopping platform and analyzed using OLS regression and bootstrap-based serial mediation analysis (PROCESS Model 6, 5000 resamples), controlling for user interface complexity. Results show that information overload was positively associated with cognitive fatigue (beta = 0.482, p < 0.001), cognitive fatigue with decision postponement (beta = 0.534, p < 0.001), and decision postponement with platform churn intention (beta = 0.512, p < 0.001). The serial indirect effect of information overload on churn intention through cognitive fatigue and decision postponement was significant (effect = 0.132, 95% CI [0.075, 0.210]), while the direct effect was not significant (beta = 0.031, p = 0.540). Because all constructs were measured concurrently in a single cross-sectional survey, these results indicate that the data are consistent with the proposed sequence rather than that the sequence is causal or temporally ordered. These findings extend information overload research by identifying a serial indirect association between review overload and provider-level exit intention through cognitive fatigue and decision postponement, after accounting for user interface complexity. Implications for review interface design are offered as recommendations that require further validation. These estimates describe review-engaged consumers in a high-density product category and should not be generalized to platform users who do not consult the review corpus before purchase.

title: Threshold Topologies and Separation Polynomials of Digital Images
container-title: Mathematics
96a31a5fca56f2398aa58967e07405f8a61dcf3c.abstract: A digital image is modeled as a finite metric space by equipping its pixel set with a color distance induced by a norm on R3. For a threshold δ, we study the threshold topology Tδ, generated by δ-chain connectedness, and the separation polynomial CΨ(z;δ), which enumerates δ-separated pixel sets. We prove that each Tδ is a partition topology and classify these spaces up to homeomorphism by component cardinalities. The filtration Tδ is shown to be equivalent to the maximal subdominant pseudo-ultrametric of the color metric, with δ-components precisely its closed balls. Its change points coincide with the distinct nonzero weights of a minimum spanning tree; we state explicitly which of these facts are reformulations of classical results on single-linkage clustering, and we treat the spatially constrained variant through a graph-restricted ultrametric. We establish a sharp Lipschitz stability estimate and derive filtration interleavings under uniform color perturbations, together with exact invariance under suitable margin conditions. Algebraically, CΨ(z;δ) is identified with the independence polynomial of the similarity graph and the face enumerator of its independence complex. A packing bound yields an efficient computation method. Finally, explicit greyscale examples establish the logical independence of the topological and algebraic invariants. The framework is illustrated on a 4×4 digital image through exact computations of filtrations, entropy, separation polynomials, and Euler characteristics.

title: Implementation and real-world feasibility of a digital psoriasis self-management app: a 12-month prospective observational study
container-title: Frontiers in Digital Health
980c25fd090776b3b5378d55c8bc37d56a086fa6.abstract: Background Psoriasis impairs physical and mental health. Evidence for real-world digital disease-management interventions remains limited. Objective This exploratory, single-arm feasibility study assessed real-world feasibility and usage patterns of a digital self-management app for psoriasis over 12 months and explored associations between app engagement and clinical and patient-reported outcomes in two German university dermatology outpatient settings. Methods 182 participants with psoriasis were enrolled and given access to a study app for continuous disease monitoring and weekly patient-reported outcomes. Assessments were conducted at baseline (V0), 6 months (V1) and 12 months (V2). Primary outcomes were feasibility measures: installation, activation (≥1 app login after installation), 12-month retention and sustained engagement (≥10 logins over 12 month, corresponding to ≈20% of study weeks). Changes in the Psoriasis Area and Severity Index (PASI), Dermatology Life Quality Index (DLQI) and Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale (HADS) were analysed as exploratory outcomes. Results All 182 participants installed the app, a condition of enrolment. Activation was achieved by 70.3% (128/182), sustained engagement 66.5% (121/182), photo upload 61.5% (112/182) an 12 month retention 58.2% (106/182). In paired complete-case analyses, PASI (median 3.0 → 1.0, n = 104; p &lt; 0.001), DLQI (7.0 → 3.0, n = 91; p &lt; 0.001), and HADS-A (7.0 → 5.0, n = 93; p = 0.002) declined significantly after Bonferroni correction ( α = 0.00625); HADS-D (5.0 → 4.0, n = 93; p = 0.033) did not survive correction. The HADS-A baseline median of 7 was already below the borderline-caseness threshold of 8, so this reduction does not represent threshold crossing. In a sensitivity analysis of 75 patients with stable therapy (54, 72.0%, with sustained engagement), within-person PASI change was −0.75 points ( n = 56; 95% CI −1.2 to −0.05; p &lt; 0.001); the DLQI change was smaller (median 0.0, mean −2.5; n = 52; p = 0.012). Higher app use frequency was not associated with greater changes in any outcome. Conclusion Integrating a digital self-management app into routine psoriasis care is feasible in a real-world setting, with 70.3% activation and 58.2% twelve-month retention. Clinical and patient-reported measures declined over the study period, but given the uncontrolled, single-arm design, attrition-related selection toward milder disease, and the absence of a dose-response relationship with app use, these changes cannot be attributed to the app and should be regarded as hypothesis-generating for a future randomised controlled trial. Clinical Trial Registration https://www.drks.de/search/de/trial/DRKS00037907/details , Deutsches Register Klinischer Studien DRKS00037907.

title: Digital Battlegrounds: Media, Behavior, and the Influence of Free Fire and Battlegrounds
daaecc6c5f1f01af0c95653a8330c9a99815d850.abstract: The rapid proliferation of smartphones and high-speed internet in India has transformed digital gaminginto a dominant leisure activity among youngsters. While gaming offers interactive entertainment, theexcessive and uncontrolled use of specific mobile titles, notably Battlegrounds Mobile India (BGMI)and Garena Free Fire, has sparked significant concerns regarding digital game addiction. Moving awayfrom traditional quantitative metrics and external qualitative observations, this study employs a rigorousautoethnographic methodology to deeply investigate the lived, internal experience of mobile gameaddiction. By utilizing self-generated data—including retrospective memory logs, reflective journalentries, and historical screen-time analysis—the researcher systematically documents their personalpsychological trajectory from casual engagement to compulsive dependency.Grounded in the Uses and Gratifications Theory, the thematic analysis deconstructs how thesophisticated behavioral designs of these battle royale games, such as competitive rank-pushing, squad-based social dynamics, and continuous reward systems, hyper-efficiently satisfy fundamentalpsychological needs. The study illustrates how these virtual environments frequently act as amaladaptive coping mechanism to escape real-world academic pressures and insecurities. The self-analysis reveals that excessive immersion severely disrupts daily life, resulting in profound behavioralshifts including heightened irritability, verbal aggression, and extreme emotional volatility directly tiedto in-game outcomes. Furthermore, the findings explicitly document significant academic displacement,physical and mental health consequences such as severe sleep disruption and underlying anxiety, and atragic psychosocial substitution where real-world family bonds are neglected in favor of virtual squadloyalties.Ultimately, this autoethnographic research highlights that while digital games provide temporaryescapism and a synthetic sense of status, uncontrolled addiction fundamentally destabilizes youthdevelopment. By documenting the visceral, real-world realities of mobile game addiction from theinside out, this study concludes by advocating for cognitive reframing, structured digital detoxification,and the active rebuilding of physical-world coping mechanisms to combat youth digital dependency.

title: Data Breach Notification under Tanzania’s Personal Data Protection Act: Empirical Evidence and Lessons from European Standards
container-title: East African Journal of Law and Ethics
aba13a4b4a051d651f564c29b22215c6c215657a.abstract: Section 27(5) of Tanzania’s Personal Data Protection Act, Cap 44 R.E. 2023, obliges a data controller to notify the Personal Data Protection Commission ‘without undue delay’ of any security breach affecting personal data, but does not say how long that is, sets no risk threshold for telling the people whose data has been exposed, and is silent on what a controller must do while the facts of an incident are still emerging. The objective of this article is to examine how effectively that duty operates in practice and to identify the lessons that European standards offer for its reform. Adopting an exploratory, qualitative socio-legal design, the study combines a doctrinal reading of the Act and its 2023 Regulations with semi-structured interviews, analysed thematically, with seven purposively selected key informants: four officers of data controller organisations, an official of the Commission, a legal practitioner and a data protection expert. The findings are read against Articles 33 and 34 of the General Data Protection Regulation, Article 7(2) of Convention 108+ and the guidelines of the European Data Protection Board. Organisations follow a consistent but undocumented sequence of technical, legal and management assessment before notifying; every respondent named the undefined timeframe as the main difficulty; direct notification of data subjects is left to case-by-case discretion; and the Commission escalates from guidance to sanction under clear capacity limits. Respondents also warned, independently, against copying the GDPR’s seventy-two-hour rule without the institutional support that makes it workable. The article proposes a defined notification period with phased disclosure, a statutory high-risk threshold for notifying data subjects, scenario-based guidance and published breach statistics, and argues that resourcing the Commission should precede any tighter deadline.

title: InlandVessel-2K-Sim: A Reproducible Multi-Source Testbed and Evaluation Protocol for Inland Vessel Trajectory Prediction, with a Spatiotemporal Graph Attention Reference Model
c30caac6bd24a8fb737233a86cc27d02bca93831.abstract: Abstract We release InlandVessel-2K-Sim , a configurable simulator generating synchronised AIS-radar-vision scenes for two inland channel geometries in the field-recording data layout, with an evaluation protocol anchoring absolute error on constant-velocity extrapolation, averaging three seeds on a fixed split, and scene-level bootstrap and paired tests. The testbed is demonstrated with ST-GAT-Fusion , a spatiotemporal graph attention reference model coupling three modality-specific encoders through dynamic-time-warping alignment, with explicit vessel-to-vessel and vessel-to-shore edges. On the released 160-scene split the four fusion-and-graph configurations sit at 19.2–19.5 m ADE — roughly half the 40.20 m of constant-velocity extrapolation — with differences inside seed variability (0.62–0.89 m for fused models, 0.04–0.11 m for AIS-only baselines). We therefore report, as a primary finding, that multi-source fusion yields no resolvable accuracy advantage: a capacity-matched AIS-only Transformer matches the fused model, a fixed-budget data-scale control shows the fusion edge eroding rather than growing with training scenes, and a larger AIS-only Transformer reaches 17.3 m, below all fused configurations. What it delivers is robustness: under AIS outage the fused model loses less than half a metre where the AIS-only baseline loses ten, and with no AIS it still predicts while the baseline cannot. The half-width model sustains 179 vessels/s on CPU.

title: Validación psicométrica de un instrumento digital de screening JEL-K para la detección temprana de riesgo lector en nivel inicial
Psychometric Validation of the Digital JEL-K Screening Tool for the Early Identification of Reading Risk in Kindergarten
Validação psicométrica de um instrumento digital de rastreamento JEL-K para a detecção precoce do risco de dificuldades de leitura na educação infantil
container-title: Ciencias Psicológicas
b9c4d680f4b56a5e598f1454495e0ff62ca8f6c7.abstract: The aim of this study was to analyze the psychometric properties of the digital version of the JEL-K battery, a screening instrument designed for the early identification of reading risk in kindergarten. A total of 2,154 children (52 % girls) enrolled in the last year of kindergarten or in first grade at private and public schools in Argentina participated in the study (M = 5.29; SD = 0.49). Separate samples and subsamples were used for each analysis: Group A (n = 684) for reliability and exploratory factor analyses; Group B (n = 1,349) for confirmatory factor analysis; Group C (n = 600) for test–retest stability (four- to five-week interval); Group D (n = 152) to compare digital and paper administration (three- to six-month interval); and Group E (n = 121) to evaluate discriminative capacity through receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis using reading fluency at the end of first grade as the criterion. Results showed adequate internal consistency for the total battery (α = .79; ω = .80) and high temporal stability (r = .98, p < .001). The correlated multifactor model showed good fit. No significant differences were found between digital and paper formats. ROC analysis showed adequate discriminative capacity, with a sensitivity of 83 % and a specificity of 74 %. Overall, the results support the validity and usefulness of the digital JEL-K as a screening tool in educational contexts.

title: Fungsi Pengawasan (Controlling) dan Evaluasi Lembaga Dakwah Muhammadiyah sebagai Penopang Akuntabilitas di Era Digital:  Model Siklus Empat Tahap Berbasis Nilai

18d4cd5873ab43fb757f0e378d54497451b0bd15.abstract: Dakwah Muhammadiyah dijalankan oleh perangkat persyarikatan yang tersusun berjenjang, terutama Majelis Tabligh. Perluasan dakwah ke media digital menambah tuntutan atas mutu program, keterbukaan, dan pengelolaan konten. Penelitian ini bertujuan menjelaskan fungsi pengawasan (controlling) dan evaluasi pada lembaga dakwah Muhammadiyah serta kontribusinya terhadap akuntabilitas. Penelitian memakai pendekatan kualitatif dengan tinjauan pustaka, yang sebagian besar berupa artikel jurnal ilmiah Indonesia tentang manajemen dakwah Muhammadiyah, pengawasan dan evaluasi dakwah, serta dakwah digital, ditambah buku teori dan peraturan perundang-undangan. Analisis memakai analisis tematik. Hasil kajian menunjukkan empat temuan. Pertama, pengawasan berjalan melalui laporan kepada pimpinan, rapat kerja, dan teguran langsung, tetapi standar capaian yang terukur dan catatan koreksi tertulis perlu diperkuat. Kedua, evaluasi cenderung menilai terlaksananya kegiatan dan perlu bergeser ke penilaian perubahan perilaku dan hasil bagi jamaah. Ketiga, dakwah digital menambah objek pengawasan, yaitu akurasi informasi, etika bermedia, dan keamanan data. Keempat, nilai amanah, musyawarah, keadilan, dan muhasabah bekerja melalui mekanisme pengawasan dan evaluasi, bukan di luarnya. Penelitian ini mengusulkan siklus pengawasan dan evaluasi empat tahap yang ditopang empat tuas kendali, dipetakan pada lima dimensi akuntabilitas, dan diterapkan dengan pembagian peran antartingkat pimpinan, disertai ilustrasi penerapan, rancangan uji lapangan, dan tiga format kerja.

title: Multi-Stage State-of-Health Estimation for Lithium-Ion Batteries Based on an Adaptive SHAP-Guided Dual-Attention LSTM
container-title: Batteries
37076663de9d091b6562ce8f0ace9ced5af5ac27.abstract: Accurate state-of-health (SOH) estimation across nonlinear battery aging is challenged by condition-dependent feature relevance. This study combines aging data up to a defined 80% SOH operational end-of-life threshold with an adaptive SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP)-guided dual-attention long short-term memory (LSTM) network. Current, voltage, state of charge (SOC), and a pulse-derived short-time resistance indicator from hybrid pulse power characterization (HPPC) are used as inputs. Training-set SHAP importance supplies a weak global feature prior, whose influence is adjusted for each input sequence by an adaptive gate. Residual feature attention recalibrates the inputs, while temporal attention aggregates representations from a shared LSTM encoder. Stage windows and labels are permuted synchronously during training to avoid fixed-position shortcuts. Under held-out SOC conditions, the complete model achieves MAE = 0.3418 percentage points (pp), RMSE = 0.5652 pp, MAPE = 0.3825%, and R2 = 0.9945, reducing MAE and RMSE by 14.1% and 12.4% relative to the Plain Shared LSTM. The results support the coordinated architecture within the tested SOC-holdout protocol; cross-cell performance is assessed separately under a different UDDS setting.

title: Intersectionality in Digital Health Literacy and Digital Health Application Use in Germany: A MAIHDA Study by Gender, Educational Attainment, and Generation
container-title: Healthcare
221ed47faa696470fc674383446a11999c8a0ce2.abstract: Background/Objectives: Social determinants of health (SDOHs) are linked to inequities in digital health application (DHA) use and digital health literacy (DHL), a predictor of DHA use, but few studies have examined these inequities intersectionally. This study examined intersectional differences by gender, educational attainment, and generation. Methods: Data were obtained from an online cross-sectional survey (STELLAR; N = 1200) in Germany. Intersectionality was assessed using Multilevel Analysis of Individual Heterogeneity and Discriminatory Accuracy (MAIHDA), with the intersections of gender, educational attainment, and generation defining strata for both outcomes. Results: Educational attainment was the strongest predictor of DHL and was associated with DHA use; gender was not significant for either. Generation was associated with DHA use, with higher odds for Generation Y and Z than for Traditionalists, but was not associated with DHL. Predicted DHL was highest among women with higher education from the Traditionalist or Generation Y group and lowest among men with basic education from Generation Z. Predicted DHA use was highest among women with higher education from Generation Z and lowest among men with basic education from the Baby Boomer generation. Additive main effects explained a greater share of the between-stratum variance for DHA use than for DHL, while the proportion of total variance attributable to strata remained limited for both outcomes. Conclusions: MAIHDA can identify population groups at greater risk of second-level digital divide-related inequities in DHL and DHA use, informing population-level measures to strengthen DHL and improve DHA use. Further research should clarify the underlying mechanisms.

title: Resistance Training for Hypertrophy in Trained Populations: A Narrative Review and Fatigue-Management Framework (2020–2026)
container-title: Journal of Functional Morphology and Kinesiology
f2095f7691ec02542dcfbf10eaa07ac856139c58.abstract: The prescription of resistance training for muscle hypertrophy in trained populations has shifted from static models requiring failure toward dynamic frameworks centered on fatigue management. This narrative review synthesizes evidence from 2020 to 2026 across five key programming variables, including weekly set volume, proximity to failure, exercise selection and order, range of motion, and autoregulation, to develop an integrated programming framework. A structured search of PubMed, MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, and SPORTDiscus identified published studies from January 2020 to September 2026 involving adults trained with resistance and hypertrophic outcomes. Systematic reviews and pooled analyses were prioritized over individual trials. The synthesis centers on the stimulus to fatigue ratio, defined as mechanical tension versus fatigue generated. Pooled analyses reveal a non-linear relationship between volume and hypertrophy, with 12 to 20 weekly sets per muscle group as a defensible starting range. Failure is unnecessary when volume is adequate; proximity to failure targets of 1 to 3 repetitions in reserve or velocity loss thresholds of 25% to 40% preserve hypertrophic stimulus while limiting disproportionate fatigue. Exercise selection and ordering distribute fatigue; mechanical tension at long muscle lengths drives hypertrophy, with lengthened partials offering regional lower body growth. These variables are integrated into a sequential decision tree algorithm guiding volume titration, exercise selection, effort regulation, and biomechanical optimization. Unlike prior reviews, this work provides a unified framework primarily developed for resistance-trained populations, with potential applicability to clinical and aging populations pending appropriate individual adaptations and further empirical validation. Future research should examine longitudinal periodization and empirically validate the algorithm in applied settings.

title: Can Standardized Small-Sided Games Be Used as a Tool to Monitor Post-Match Fatigue in Male Academy Soccer Players?
container-title: Sports
fb3102a37f4daa503bb28315512f97c4ea0bb4af.abstract: This study aimed to analyze residual post-match fatigue using time-motion analysis across small-sided games (SSGs), fitness performance, and heart rate variability (HRV) in academy soccer players. Fifteen male academy players (18.3 ± 0.6 years) performed four SSG formats: 3 vs. 3 and 3 vs. 3 + 2 goalkeepers, played on small (25 × 18 m; 75 m2 per player) and large (36 × 25 m; 150 m2 per player) areas in a four-week experimental design. Two non-match weeks served as baseline weeks, and two weeks followed an official match. Time-motion during SSGs was monitored via GNSS. Before each training session (24, 72, and 120 h post-match), HRV, countermovement jump (CMJ) height, and maximum isometric force (MIF) of the hamstrings were measured. External load metrics were generally lower in post-match sessions than in non-match weeks; however, their low reliability limited the interpretability of SSG outputs. CMJ height was reduced, MIF was elevated post-match, whereas HRV showed distinct mid-week responses, decreasing in starters but increasing in non-starters. Post-match fatigue was evident in neuromuscular performance but was inconsistently reflected in SSG outputs. CMJ height reliably reflects post-match fatigue in male academy soccer players and should be prioritized when monitoring neuromuscular recovery.

title: Informing Digital Career Transition and Mental Health Support Services Implementation: Perspectives of Active and Retired European Elite Athletes
container-title: Sports
5a2270e6318eb6c469fbe7a283963ee66e6cdbb0.abstract: This cross-sectional study explored the perceived challenges and needs of a convenience sample of European elite athletes regarding multilevel support services (dual career, mental health, and career retirement). Athletes recruited through the networks of the EU-funded “PORTAL” project partners in five European countries completed a 50-item semi-structured electronic questionnaire. Information relative to career path, career challenges and needs, and the perceived relevance, availability, satisfaction, frequency of provision, and possible digital implementation of 12 potential career support services were considered for analysis. Respondents (n = 136; 46% female; 44% retired; 75% Olympic/World) highlighted difficulties during their athletic and dual career paths, with limited formal recognition from sport (41%) and academic/vocational environments (43%), and inadequate preparation for retirement (48%). For retirement preparation, career transitions and mental health support services were considered crucial (5 pts/6), although the perceived effectiveness of currently available services was low (3 pts/6). Among the 12 evaluated services, workshops, career development/networking, financial planning, and mental health counselling were rated as the most relevant (4 pts/5). Most services (10/12) were reported as available by fewer than half of respondents (range: 20–44%), with a generally perceived low satisfaction (range: 2.5–3.2 pts/5). Positive perceptions emerged for possible digital implementation of all 12 services (range: 3.8–4.2 pts/5), with a service-dependent preferred frequency of provision varying from weekly to occasional. Considering the importance of multidimensional support systems for addressing practical, psychological, and emotional retirement-related challenges, although descriptive of the present sample and not generalizable to all European elite athletes, these end-user-informed findings may guide the development and implementation of a digital platform supporting athletes throughout their dual-career and retirement pathways and life beyond sport.

title: Corporate Green Investment and Debt Financing Costs: The Moderating Role of Green Institutional Investor Attention in China
container-title: Sustainability
bcc65a5470c7cefe07624beacc576bddc6330ace.abstract: This study examines the association between corporate green investment and subsequent debt financing cost and the moderating role of prior green institutional investor attention. Using 40,060 firm-year observations from 4633 non-financial Chinese A-share firms over investment years 2011–2024, firm and year fixed-effects models relate investment in year t to financing cost in year t + 1, with attention and pre-investment financing cost measured in year t − 1. Green investment is associated with lower subsequent financing cost, and this association becomes more negative as prior attention increases. At the 25th and 75th percentiles of attention, a one-percentage-point increase in green investment relative to total assets is associated with financing-cost reductions of 2.75 and 3.62 basis points, respectively. The negative interaction persists after ownership and selected liability-composition controls, within positive-investment observations, and under alternative clustered and wild-cluster bootstrap inference. Evidence is stronger for financing-cost measures scaled by total liabilities than for the measure based on average core interest-bearing debt. Period comparisons indicate a stronger negative investment association but weaker attention moderation after 2019, including when 2020 is excluded. Differences across firm characteristics and environmental-exposure groups are less conclusive after multiple-testing adjustment. The findings associate the financing relevance of environmental expenditure with prior specialized investor attention, with the strength of the evidence varying across accounting measures and periods.

title: Transformasi Ekonomi Digital dan Daya Saing UMKM
container-title: Jurnal QOSIM : Jurnal Pendidikan Sosial & Humaniora
20633dc9f6c866b778dfd84e9ff542bf6caa8905.abstract: Transformasi ekonomi digital telah mengubah cara Usaha Mikro, Kecil, dan Menengah (UMKM) menjalankan aktivitas bisnis, termasuk pemasaran, penjualan, transaksi, komunikasi dengan konsumen, dan pengelolaan usaha. Kondisi ini memberikan peluang bagi UMKM untuk memperluas pasar dan meningkatkan daya saing, sekaligus menuntut kemampuan untuk beradaptasi dengan perkembangan teknologi. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis transformasi ekonomi digital dan keterkaitannya dengan daya saing UMKM dengan menempatkan adaptasi usaha sebagai aspek penting dalam proses tersebut. Penelitian ini menggunakan pendekatan kualitatif dengan metode Systematic Literature Review (SLR). Literatur diperoleh melalui penelusuran Google Scholar, GARUDA, dan portal jurnal terindeks SINTA, dengan kriteria yang berfokus pada penelitian terkait digitalisasi, teknologi, adaptasi, inovasi, kinerja, dan daya saing UMKM. Analisis dilakukan menggunakan analisis isi (content analysis) dan analisis tematik (thematic analysis) dengan mengelompokkan temuan ke dalam tiga tema utama, yaitu transformasi ekonomi digital, adaptasi usaha, dan daya saing UMKM. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa transformasi digital UMKM tidak hanya diwujudkan melalui penggunaan media sosial, pemasaran digital, perdagangan elektronik (e-commerce), lokapasar (marketplace), dan pembayaran digital, tetapi juga melalui integrasi teknologi ke dalam proses bisnis. Adaptasi usaha merupakan proses penting yang mencakup perubahan strategi pemasaran, proses operasional, inovasi produk dan layanan, peningkatan literasi digital dan kualitas sumber daya manusia, serta penyesuaian terhadap kebutuhan pasar. Transformasi digital yang didukung oleh kemampuan adaptif dapat memperluas jangkauan pasar, meningkatkan efisiensi, mendorong inovasi, memperkuat kualitas pelayanan, dan meningkatkan kemampuan UMKM dalam menghadapi persaingan. Namun, keterbatasan literasi digital, sumber daya manusia, modal, kesiapan organisasi, dan manajemen perubahan masih menjadi hambatan dalam proses transformasi tersebut. Oleh karena itu, keberhasilan digitalisasi UMKM tidak hanya ditentukan oleh adopsi teknologi, tetapi juga oleh kemampuan pelaku usaha dalam mengintegrasikan teknologi dengan strategi, sumber daya, dan kebutuhan pasar.

title: La brecha digital como efecto postpandemia en el alumnado de la secundaria técnica no. 140 de Atlixco, Puebla
container-title: LATAM Revista Latinoamericana de Ciencias Sociales y Humanidades
26410a75f794d16d644ed646853df0f3e761efa6.abstract: La idea central de la brecha digital ya no se focaliza únicamente en la disposición de recursos tecnológicos, sino que se ha trasladado a la forma en que estos se integran en la enseñanza. Dicho cambio conceptual se interpreta mediante el modelo de Van Dijk de los cuatro tipos de acceso, que nos enseña que una vez cubierta la disponibilidad de dispositivos, la brecha se desplaza al aprovechamiento sustantivo de la tecnología y al desarrollo de habilidades. En este estudio se buscó evaluar las desigualdades tecnológicas en el acceso real que guardan los alumnos de la Secundaria Técnica 140 de Atlixco, Puebla al cumplirse seis años de la contingencia sanitaria por COVID-19, para lo cual se adoptó un diseño cuantitativo, no experimental, transversal y descriptivo. Se realizó un levantamiento de información entre 86% del universo estudiantil inscrito al ciclo escolar 2025-2026. La evidencia empírica muestra que el 94.1% de los encuestados que reporta una conectividad fija a internet en sus viviendas y el 86.7% que dispone de un dispositivo exclusivo para sus actividades académicas. Sin embargo, apenas un 13.3% de los estudiantes señala que sus profesores aprovechan las herramientas digitales en la mayoría de sus asignaturas. El contraste entre la disponibilidad de recursos tecnológicos y el uso educativo que perciben los estudiantes lleva a concluir que las políticas orientadas a reducir la brecha digital deberían concentrar sus esfuerzos ya no solo en el acceso, sino en la integración pedagógica de estos recursos digitales para así aprovechar los dispositivos con los que los estudiantes ya cuentan. Este trabajo contribuye directamente al marco del Objetivo de Desarrollo Sostenible 4 mediante la atención puntual en el desarrollo de competencias digitales, equidad en el acceso y la profesionalización de la planta docente.

title: Land use efficiency in the era of digital transformations: experience of China’s land resource management
container-title: Actual problems of innovative economy and law
18dfda213696fb928c306a1535f98aae19f932c4.abstract: The article presents a comprehensive institutional, spatial, and econometric analysis of land resource management transformation driven by digitalization, focusing on the experience of the People’s Republic of China, and outlines conceptual directions for adapting these practices to Ukraine’s post-war recovery. The study substantiates Green Land Use Efficiency (GLUE) as an advanced paradigm that integrates economic productivity with environmental risk minimization, resource saving, and carbon footprint reduction in the context of sustainable spatial development. The research thoroughly investigates China’s pivotal 2018 institutional reform, which eliminated interagency fragmentation by establishing the Ministry of Natural Resources and implementing the “multi-plan integration” (Duogui Heyi) framework. The engineering and technological foundations of the National Territorial Spatial Planning “One Map” platform are revealed alongside the “Tiandi Wang” dynamic monitoring system (RS + AI + Beidou) and the “three zones and three lines” spatial control framework. The paper systematizes the mathematical apparatus for measuring GLUE based on non-radial Super-SBM models (accounting for undesirable outputs) and Spatial Durbin Models (SDM), and empirically verifies initial spatial siphoning and subsequent green spillover effects across neighboring regions. Furthermore, the paper highlights sectoral and spatial specificities of land digitalization: the deployment of 3D/4D cadastral modeling, BIM, and Digital Twin Cities in densely populated urban agglomerations, versus electronic farmland circulation platforms (Sanquan Fengli) and satellite-driven precision agriculture in rural regions. The analysis also identifies key structural risks, including regional digital divides, local fiscal dependencies on land finance, and data security vulnerabilities. Finally, the study proposes practical directions for modernizing Ukraine’s spatial management. These include creating a unified National GIS Superplatform compliant with EU INSPIRE standards, deploying AI-driven satellite monitoring for war-damage auditing and mine-clearance prioritization, and legally establishing a digital spatial framework for recovery and ecological-protection lines. Keywords: Green Land Use Efficiency (GLUE), digital transformation, GIS platforms, One Map system, “three zones and three lines”, Super-SBM model, Spatial Durbin Model, post-war recovery of Ukraine, Beidou, State Land Cadastre.

title: Digital accounting implementation and perceived operational performance in Vietnamese commercial banks: Empirical evidence from accountants and managers
container-title: Banks and Bank Systems
04d6aac043a5ad3d39eb9cc374663cc4afd6d9fc.abstract: Type of the article: Research ArticleAbstractThis study examines the relationships among digital accounting implementation, financial reporting quality, usefulness of accounting information, top management support, and perceived operational performance in commercial banks. Data were collected from 562 accountants and managers working at 27 commercial banks in Vietnam, an emerging Asian economy. The study evaluated the proposed model using a two-stage Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling approach. The findings indicate that digital accounting implementation is positively associated with perceived operational performance. In addition, digital accounting implementation is indirectly associated with perceived operational performance through statistically significant indirect paths involving financial reporting quality and usefulness of accounting information. Financial reporting quality is also positively associated with the usefulness of accounting information. Furthermore, the positive associations between digital accounting implementation and both financial reporting quality and usefulness of accounting information were stronger at higher levels of perceived top management support, whereas the interaction between digital accounting implementation and perceived operational performance was not statistically significant. Collectively, the findings suggest that perceptions of digital accounting implementation are closely related to perceptions of information quality, information usefulness, managerial support, and perceived operational performance. This study contributes empirical evidence on the interrelationships among these perceived organizational constructs in the context of banking digital transformation in an emerging economy.

title: Research on a FOGG-GNS-Based User Engagement Mechanism for Lightweight Digital Art Games Supporting Well-being
container-title: EAI Endorsed Transactions on Pervasive Health and Technology
4773b2883eafe8ed5bfa7afb483e37a9055f00e9.abstract: Research Background and Gap (Why): Amidst the trend towards fragmented digital entertainment, lightweight games have emerged as an important form of mobile interaction, offering convenient “instant play” experiences through low barriers, short interaction cycles, and social integration. Although these characteristics provide new possibilities for digital art-based well-being experiences, current research lacks an integrated framework that systematically connects lightweight game design, user behavioral psychology, and well-being engagement mechanisms. Research Method (How): This study proposes the “FOGG-GNS” framework by integrating the Fogg Behavior Model (FBM) with Gamism-Narrativism-Simulationism (GNS) theory. The framework is used to analyze how game design structures and behavioral factors influence user engagement in lightweight digital art games. This study adopts a theory-driven empirical approach, combining qualitative analysis of lightweight game design with quantitative validation through a questionnaire survey (N = 450). Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) and Hierarchical Regression Analysis were employed to examine the proposed framework. Practical Implementation (With what): The FOGG-GNS framework was applied to the analysis of representative lightweight games and empirically validated through questionnaire data to examine the relationships among Motivation, Ability, Prompt, GNS dimensions, and well-being engagement. Core Conclusion (What): The results reveal that Prompt and Gamism-oriented design elements are associated with stronger initial engagement, whereas Motivation, supported by Narrativism and Simulationism, plays an important role in deeper and more sustained well-being engagement. Excessive reliance on Gamism mechanisms weakens the positive relationship between Motivation and well-being engagement, indicating a potential “Motivational Monopolisation” phenomenon. Significance and Value (So what): This study contributes to active-health-oriented digital design by explaining how lightweight digital art games may support everyday emotional awareness, self-expression, and self-management through accessible and meaningful interactions. The FOGG-GNS framework offers design implications for developing accessible digital experiences that may support everyday psychological self-management. However, this study measures self-reported well-being engagement rather than actual health behaviors or clinical outcomes. Whether such engagement translates into sustained health-supportive behaviors remains to be examined in future research.

title: NeuroLG-Seg: Attention-Guided Local–Global Feature Learning for Brain Tumor Segmentation in Super-Resolved MRI
container-title: International Journal of Innovative Research in Information Security
48e19ce529fa5fb3a9d11b6ddfc092b5e730b785.abstract: Accurate delineation of brain tumor sub-regions on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) underpins surgical planning, radiotherapy targeting and response assessment, yet manual segmentation is slow and varies between raters. This study presents NeuroLG-Seg, an attention-guided network that jointly learns local and global tumor features from super resolved MRI. Recurrent residual convolutional blocks and UNet++-style dense nested skip pathways capture local boundary detail across scales, a multi-head self-attention bottleneck models global context, and attention gates guide the fusion of the two in the decoder. Input volumes are up-sampled from 1.0 mm to 0.5 mm isotropic resolution with a pretrained enhanced deep super-resolution (EDSR) network, and six hyperparameters are selected by a Hybrid Tuatara Numbat Algorithm (HTNA). On a 187-case held-out test split of the BraTS 2021 cohort (1,251 cases), NeuroLG-Seg achieved Dice similarity coefficients of 0.924, 0.891 and 0.873 for the whole tumor (WT), tumor core (TC) and enhancing tumor (ET), compared with 0.896, 0.855 and 0.827 for TransUNet, the strongest of five baselines trained under the same protocol. It also reduced the ET 95th-percentile Hausdorff distance from 4.83 mm to 3.21 mm (Wilcoxon signed-rank test with Bonferroni correction, p < 0.01). In a cumulative ablation, the local components accounted for about half of the 0.068 WT Dice gain over a U-Net baseline, while the global transformer bottleneck gave the largest single gain for the enhancing tumor. On 262 TCGA-GBM cases, evaluated as an additional cross-dataset test, the model retained 97.5–98.3% of its BraTS Dice scores. Comparison with self-configuring 3D pipelines and an explicit super-resolution ablation remain necessary next steps.
