title: Entre o controle e a exposição da intimidade
Between control and the exposure of intimacy
Entre el control y la exposición de la intimidad
container-title: Revista de Estudos Universitários - REU
9ac0822e25abb9a15d209ae91cf6a4a9b4b37b89.abstract: This article analyzes the dynamics of virtual rape, focusing on contemporary forms of sexual violence mediated by digital technologies. Drawing from a communication-based approach and digital sociology, it investigates how platforms and technological artifacts function as agents of surveillance, coercion, and exposure, enhancing practices of domination and control over the bodies of girls and women. The study mobilizes concepts such as technobiopower (HARAWAY, 1991), aggressive voyeurism (CONTRERA, 2010), and pornotopia (PRECIADO, 2018) to understand how the threat of public exposure becomes a mechanism of submission and humiliation, naturalizing the violation of victims' privacy and dignity. Through the analysis of 35 cases reported by the Brazilian press between 2017 and 2023, it becomes evident that virtual rape is not a deviation, but rather an update of historical gender-based violence, now amplified and automated by the digital ecosystem. The empirical analysis shows that men are responsible for the majority of the crimes (94.12%), while most of the victims are girls and women (74.36%), reinforcing the central role of gender inequality in these contexts.

title: Sustainability data traceability in enterprise digital reporting
container-title: Actual problems of innovative economy and law
c58ee2603215495c3f1bd0634bd87a08c90ac1b6.abstract: The article develops an organizational and methodological approach to ensuring sustainability data traceability in enterprise digital reporting. Drawing on academic research and institutional guidance, it distinguishes traceability from data accuracy and identifies three interrelated dimensions: informational, procedural, and control-managerial. Traceability is defined as the capacity to identify the source of an ESG indicator, reconstruct its transformations, establish accountability, and verify the approved disclosure. The approach integrates data governance and risk-based internal control through a sequence linking sources, data operations, risks, controls, evidence, and reported indicators. A risk-control matrix covers five reporting stages: collection, transfer, processing, verification and approval, and disclosure. An electronic indicator passport records reporting boundaries, calculation methods, source versions, corrections, responsible persons, and evidence of approval. Direct and reverse tracing are proposed to test the completeness of data flows and the reproducibility of disclosed indicators. Implementation follows five stages: indicator identification, mapping information flows, risk assessment and control design, introducing indicator passports and procedures, and performance evaluation. Evaluation criteria comprise information coverage, independent reproducibility, change control, and timely resolution of discrepancies. The approach can be adapted for enterprises with varying levels of digital maturity, including those with controlled electronic registers. Its methodological contribution lies in combining data provenance, organizational accountability, and verifiable controls within a coherent reporting process. The approach awaits empirical validation; its effects on reporting quality, preparation time, and control costs require further investigation. Keywords: ESG data, data traceability, digital reporting, enterprise sustainability, data governance, risk-based control, internal control, electronic indicator passport.

title: Women's digital financial inclusion along the agrifood value chains in the NENA region
The Interplay Between Artificial Intelligence-Enabled Ac-counting, Digital Leadership, and Sustainable Competitive Performance
container-title: Administrative Sciences
83568391bd5540cde348b9a3e3e86e6a54102f33.abstract: This paper explores the impact of Artificial Intelligence in Accounting (AIIA) on Sustainable Competitive Performance (SCP). It also examines how digital leadership (DL) moderates the AIIA-SCP relationship. Data were gathered from accountants, finance managers, CFOs, and internal auditors working at firms listed on the Egyptian Stock Exchange (ESE), with a sample size of 417. The analysis was conducted using Smart-PLS software. Results show that all elements of AIIA positively and significantly influence SCP. Moreover, DL enhances the connection between AIIA and SCP, strengthening their relationship. The model explains 76.2% of SCP’s variance. These findings serve as a useful benchmark for corporate policy and provide key insights for improving competitive advantage and performance. This research also has important managerial implications, highlighting AIIA and DL’s potential to boost SCP. As one of the first studies to examine DL’s moderating role in the AIIA-SCP link, it offers valuable insights for emerging markets.

title: Digital–Green Twin Transformation and Economic Growth: The Asymmetric Moderating Role of Industrial Competitiveness in Transition Economies
container-title: Economies
1e6aeb91557db655742cb9d564ec2892bbec6230.abstract: Post-socialist economies in Central and Eastern Europe, the Western Balkans, the Eastern Partnership, and Central Asia inherited energy-intensive industrial structures and now diverge widely in digital adoption and decarbonisation, which makes them a revealing setting for the twin transition. This study examines how the digital and green transitions relate to real GDP per capita growth in 24 transition economies over 1996–2023 and whether industrial competitiveness conditions these relationships. Composite indices are constructed through principal component analysis. Following first- and second-generation diagnostic tests, the analysis employs fixed effects with Driscoll–Kraay standard errors, panel-corrected standard errors, system GMM, common correlated effects, and cross-sectionally augmented ARDL estimators, together with panel Granger non-causality tests robust to cross-sectional dependence. The digital transition, the green transition, and industrial competitiveness are each positively associated with growth. The central finding is an asymmetric moderation pattern. Industrial competitiveness strengthens the growth association of digitalisation but weakens that of greening, so that the green growth association appears concentrated in less industrialised economies. Granger predictive relationships run in both directions between each transition and growth and from industrial competitiveness to the green transition. The pattern is robust across subregions, EU and non-EU groups, the 2005–2023 period, alternative index constructions, and alternative treatments of missing data, although the green coefficient and its interaction with industrial competitiveness are not statistically significant in the 1997–2004 subsample. The system GMM and CS-ARDL estimates are treated as supplementary evidence. The evidence, which consists of conditional associations rather than causal effects, suggests that twin transition support may be more effective when it takes the industrial conditions of each economy into account rather than being applied as a uniform package.

title: Responsible FinTech and the Future of Digital Finance: The Moderating Role of Financial Inclusion in the FinTech–Environmental Sustainability Nexus in Africa
container-title: Economies
49dfe9fdf874d94533784f85bbc82c47b86cd06c.abstract: This study examines the effect of financial technology (FinTech) on environmental sustainability, emphasising the moderating role of financial inclusion in Africa. While existing studies focus on the relationship between financial inclusion and FinTech, the moderating mechanism through which financial inclusion influences the FinTech–environmental sustainability nexus remains underexplored. To address this gap, the study explores the interrelationships among FinTech, financial inclusion and environmental sustainability across 20 African countries from 2010 to 2025. Anchored in Rogers’ Diffusion of Innovation Theory, the study employs advanced panel econometric techniques, including the Hadri LM test, System Generalised Method of Moments (SGMM), the Dumitrescu–Hurlin panel causality test, the Difference-in-Hansen test, and Wald tests. Institutional quality, economic growth and foreign direct investment are included as control variables. The findings show that financial inclusion significantly moderates the impact of FinTech on environmental sustainability, providing strong empirical and theoretical support for the study’s central proposition. When considered independently, financial inclusion contributes negatively while FinTech contributes positively to environmental sustainability. However, their interaction/moderation yields a complementary effect that strengthens environmental sustainability by reducing carbon emissions. Furthermore, the study establishes a bidirectional causal relationship among FinTech, financial inclusion, and environmental sustainability. The study concludes that the African continent should systematically expand financial inclusion to amplify the environmental benefits of FinTech innovations by leveraging sustainable digital finance.

title: FingerAlphaNet: Static Sign Language Alphabet Recognition with Attention-Enhanced Convolutional Neural Networks for Inclusive Human–Computer Interaction
container-title: Electronics
4439804782f5bed93c0b0aff2f7ffcd694a1fc2b.abstract: Sign Language Alphabet Recognition (SLAR) is a critical component of inclusive Human–Computer Interaction (HCI), particularly for facilitating communication with Deaf and Hard-of-Hearing (DHH) individuals. The paper at hand proposes an attention-enhanced lightweight Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) architecture for interpretable SLR, exploiting the Convolutional Block Attention Module (CBAM) to improve both classification performance and model transparency. The introduced method is assessed on the Sign Language MNIST dataset, where the integration of attention mechanisms improves classification accuracy compared with the corresponding attention-free CNN configurations. Additionally, qualitative attention maps are presented to visualize the spatial regions emphasized by the model during classification, complemented by a quantitative attention-perturbation analysis assessing the functional relevance of these regions. Furthermore, a comprehensive analysis is conducted regarding the computational cost introduced by the CBAM integration, demonstrating a favorable trade-off between accuracy, interpretability, and model complexity. A comparative analysis with representative methods evaluated on the same dataset is also presented, contextualizing the proposed architectures in terms of recognition performance and computational efficiency. This study underscores the potential of attention mechanisms for developing more transparent and inclusive AI systems using static SLAR, providing a foundation for future real-world HCI and assistive communication applications. From an assistive technology and occupational therapy perspective, such recognition systems may support the development of accessible Augmentative and Alternative Communication (AAC) interfaces aimed at reducing communication barriers and facilitating participation of DHH individuals in everyday activities.

title: Towards Trustworthy Autonomy in Advanced Nuclear Systems: A Review of Advanced Control, Digital Twins, and Generative AI
container-title: Energies
efb86b06de620e2872f90a1e721925e2b43eb9d6.abstract: Advanced nuclear systems are expected to operate across a wider range of missions, plant configurations, staffing models, and external couplings than the existing light-water reactor fleet. The operating practices of that fleet were developed for large single units at steady baseload and cannot be assumed to transfer unchanged to flexible, multi-module, remotely supervised, or multi-product plants. This review examines how advanced control, digital twins, and generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) can extend those practices toward trustworthy autonomy. Model-based and predictive control, learning-enabled control, control-oriented digital twins, supervisory operation, and GenAI grounded in validated engineering tools are synthesized within a single framework organized by level of automation. The framework considers plant layer, degree of autonomy, and evidence maturity from conceptual proposals to operating-plant experience. The review finds that higher autonomy is most credible within a layered architecture. Independent protection and qualified regulatory control remain the safety foundation that every advanced layer must defer to. Predictive and supervisory control coordinate constrain plant-wide operation, and reinforcement learning is best confined to offline-trained supervisory decisions screened by verified filters. Digital twins supply state estimation, prediction, and controller-development infrastructure whose role narrows from action to advice as uncertainty grows. GenAI is best introduced as a grounded interface that retrieves controlled information, invokes validated tools, and prepares recommendations for human approval. The principal gap is integrated demonstration, and a staged roadmap in which the level of automation rises only with accumulated evidence is offered from the author’s perspective.

title: DCLCA-UNet: Dynamic Cross-Level Contextual Attention for 3D Medical Image Segmentation
container-title: Journal of Imaging
9965566c8cf5dfa9c0c84a78a359357accb1a834.abstract: Accurate 3D medical image segmentation requires effective integration of encoder details and decoder semantics. However, their relative contributions vary across decoding stages and spatial locations, and attention based only on the current feature pair may provide limited guidance in ambiguous regions. To address these challenges, we propose Dynamic Cross-Level Contextual Attention U-Net (DCLCA-UNet), which reconstructs cross-level context at each decoding stage from the incoming decoder feature and encoder features at the corresponding and shallower levels. The Cross-Level Contextual Attention Fusion (CLCAF) module uses this context to adaptively weight encoder and decoder features before fusion. The Context-Guided Feature Modulation (CGFM) module then reuses the context to refine the fused representation through scaling and additive correction. Experiments on Synapse, BTCV, and BraTS2023 yield average Dice scores of 88.70%, 84.13%, and 92.34%, respectively, with the lowest corresponding average Hausdorff distance (HD) or 95th-percentile Hausdorff distance (HD95) among the compared methods. These improvements are accompanied by increased computational cost. Repeated experiments and evaluation on AMOS22 provide additional evidence of stability and cross-dataset generalization. Ablation studies further assess the contributions of contextual fusion, modulation, and stage-specific context reconstruction. Together, these results support the effectiveness of contextual guidance in volumetric segmentation.

title: Characterizing KV-Cache Performance in Large Language Model Inference: Context Length, Attention Architecture, and GPU Memory Residency
container-title: Journal of Low Power Electronics and Applications
f1eabf55a2a75875b0c6f8eec7052df3f2f3dbd9.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) commonly employ key–value (KV) caching to avoid recomputing previous attention states during autoregressive inference. However, its measured performance benefit depends on workload characteristics and the memory environment. This study presents a controlled systems characterization across input context length, model-specific grouped-query attention configurations, and GPU-memory residency. Experiments use Qwen2.5-3B and SmolLM3-3B under verified fully resident conditions with fixed 128-token generation, prompt lengths from 128 to 2048 tokens, randomized cache-enabled/cache-disabled execution, GPU telemetry, and repeated paired validation. End-to-end generation speedup increases from 1.34× to 8.31× for Qwen2.5-3B and from 1.28× to 8.62× for SmolLM3-3B. At 2048 prompt tokens, 30 randomized paired trials confirm mean speedups of 8.10× and 8.51×, corresponding to runtime reductions of 87.65% and 88.25%, while physical GPU-memory utilization remains below 61%. SmolLM3-3B requires twice the theoretical KV-cache storage per token, yet both models show comparable context-dependent scaling in the fully resident regime. Because the models differ in characteristics beyond KV-head count, this cross-model comparison is descriptive and does not attribute the observed performance difference causally to GQA configuration. A separate Mistral-7B case study shows that apparent end-to-end speedup changes substantially under memory pressure; the underlying memory-system mechanism is not isolated. These results establish cache-related end-to-end generation speedup as workload- and system-dependent and demonstrate that meaningful benchmarking requires reporting context length, cache configuration, model and cache footprints, physical accelerator-memory residency, runtime, throughput, and relevant GPU-memory conditions during each inference experiment.

title: Optimized Thin-Layer Chromatography Coupled with Digital Image Analysis for Semi-Quantitative Screening of Salidroside in Rhodiola crenulata
container-title: Separations
e93035b52432c5d5a438155cd696889f6c0af137.abstract: Rhodiola crenulata (Hook. f. et Thoms.) H. Ohba is widely used in traditional Chinese and Tibetan medicine. Salidroside, its principal bioactive component, must not be less than 0.50% on a dry weight basis according to the 2025 Chinese Pharmacopoeia, which specifies high-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC) for quantitative determination. HPLC is a reliable but requires specialized equipment and trained personnel, restricting its use for rapid screening in resource-limited settings. This study presents an optimized thin-layer chromatography (TLC) method coupled with digital image analysis for the semi-quantitative screening of salidroside in R. crenulata. Mobile phase composition and development distance were adjusted to improve practical throughput while retaining usable spot appearance. Under the final conditions, a chloroform–methanol–acetone–water (5.5:3.5:1:1, v/v/v/v) mobile phase and 12 cm development distance were used with iodine visualization and ImageJ densitometry. The recommended working range was 0.20–0.70 mg/mL, supported by plate-specific calibration, residual analysis, and within-plate precision. Process recovery and matrix effect experiments indicated acceptable accuracy for a screening method. Application to three independent batches of root material gave results consistent with HPLC within a predefined relative window of ±10%, and the complete workflow could be completed in less than two hours. This approach provides a practical alternative for preliminary screening and quality control of salidroside content in R. crenulata under limited-resource conditions.

title: From AI Decision Support to Sustainable Digital Innovation: The Mediating Role of Decision-Making Quality and the Moderating Role of Digital Leadership in Libya’s Oil and Gas Sector
container-title: Sustainability
3ea021d3f8ef0f42e1f8f26a377259fa423ecc95.abstract: The accelerating integration of artificial intelligence (AI) technologies has profoundly reshaped the decision-making environment of resource-intensive industries, yet the mechanisms through which AI-driven decision support systems (AIDSS) are associated with sustainable digital innovation (SDI) remain underexplored, particularly in emerging economy contexts. Drawing on the Dynamic Capability View and the Digital Leadership Perspective, this study develops and tests an integrated model examining the direct association of AIDSS with SDI, the mediating role of decision-making quality (DMQ), and the moderating role of digital leadership (DL) in Libya’s oil and gas sector. Survey data were collected from 326 managers and decision-makers across major oil and gas companies operating in Libya between June and August 2025 and analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) via SmartPLS 4. Results indicate that AIDSS are significantly and positively associated with both SDI and DMQ, and that DMQ partially mediates the AIDSS–SDI association, identifying decision quality as the organizational mechanism through which AI capabilities translate into sustainable innovation. Furthermore, digital leadership significantly moderates the AIDSS-DMQ association, and moderated mediation analysis reveals that the indirect innovation pathway through decision quality is substantially stronger under high digital leadership conditions. These findings extend theoretical understanding of AI-enabled dynamic capabilities, establish decision-making quality as a pivotal intermediary in the AI-to-innovation pathway, and confirm that digitally competent leadership is an indispensable organizational amplifier of AI’s strategic value. Practical implications are discussed for oil and gas managers, digital leaders, and policymakers in Libya and comparable energy sector contexts.

title: Digital Accessibility in Tourism and the Limitations of Technical Assessment Indicators: A Source-Critical Airline Case Analysis
container-title: Tourism and Hospitality
83c887859527c8330c8c3fe02264ea58cc790b39.abstract: Whether technical accessibility findings justify conclusions about tourism participation depends on what they establish about travelers’ opportunities for action, a relationship examined here through the interpretation of heterogeneous evidence. Methodologically, the study combines a critical narrative evidence synthesis with bounded bibliometric mapping and an exploratory secondary analysis of published airline audits. A Crossref rerun on 24 October 2026 yielded 700 export positions and 593 unique digital object identifiers (DOIs); applying the reported selection rules recovered the same 34-title bibliometric corpus. Technical audit and digital booking journey scores were reconstructed for 11 airlines assessed between March and June 2023. Spearman’s rho was 0.440, with substantial resampling uncertainty. Four conflicts between the summary tables and airline profiles, along with a potentially related arithmetic discrepancy, were explicitly retained. Across 16 component-based source variants, rho ranged from 0.418 to 0.521. A machine-readable statement schema links reconstructed values to their measurement dimensions, scales, temporal context, and sources. Divergent rankings illustrate non-identical orderings within the audited cases; they do not constitute a validated test of practical non-interchangeability. The contribution lies in linking source reconstruction, provenance-preserving statements, and sensitivity analysis within one documented tourism case. Population-level equivalence, current legal compliance, and individual participation outcomes cannot be inferred.

title: Ageing, Digital Literacy, and Interaction Modality in Immersive Virtual Reality: Psychomotor Performance, Cognitive Flexibility, and Their Associations with Processing Speed
container-title: Virtual Worlds
936f8fb2cec8592e1d8977415d999c972a47c1a4.abstract: Extended reality (XR) increasingly supports training and cognitive assessment, yet the age sensitivity of its interaction techniques is unclear. This study examined age, digital literacy, and interaction modality as correlates of psychomotor and cognitive-flexibility performance in immersive virtual reality (VR). Two hundred and two adults (19–90 years) completed a five-mode Fitts’ law task (eye gaze, head gaze, controller ray-casting, virtual finger, and controller direct touch), the Trail Making Test in VR (TMT-VR), and a digital-literacy questionnaire. Age was associated with slower task times across modes, but controller direct touch carried the steepest relative age gradient while remaining among the fastest in absolute terms; technique altered relative age sensitivity without determining absolute efficiency. Higher digital literacy was associated with faster TMT-VR completion but not Fitts’ law task times. In the planned analyses, a Fitts’ law derived speed score predicted TMT-VR performance beyond age and, in a statistical decomposition, partly accounted for its age association, consistent with shared processing-speed variance. A post hoc exploratory full-battery extension confined the Fitts’ law score association with completion-time and error-adjusted-time indices and the digital-literacy association to error-adjusted-time indices, not wrong-target errors, mean selection distance, or relative Part B indices. Age-inclusive XR assessment should standardise interaction modality, evaluate rather than exclude mid-air direct selection, and interpret cognitive scores alongside digital literacy and psychomotor speed.

title: The Evidentiary Value of Commercial Books - Between Legal Requirements and Digital Transformation in the Saudi Legal System: A Critical Analytical Study
container-title: International Journal of Law Research and Studies
f111583dbe6b72a3b9f157134d262217daded3b7.abstract: This research examines commercial books under the Saudi legal system through an analytical and critical study of their statutory regulation and evidentiary value. It aims to clarify the concept of commercial books, the scope of the obligation to maintain them, their types, and the requirements governing their regularity and preservation. The study also addresses the legal regulation of electronic commercial books and the extent to which it keeps pace with the digital transformation taking place in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia. The research further discusses the evidentiary value of commercial books in favor of and against merchants under the Saudi Law of Evidence, with particular attention to the statutory conditions for relying on such books, the effect of their regularity or irregularity, and the role of the court in examining them and assessing their probative value. The study adopts analytical and critical approaches by examining the relevant statutory provisions and evaluating their suitability for the contemporary commercial environment. The research concludes that the Saudi legal framework provides, in general, a clear system governing commercial books and their evidentiary value, while also recognizing the use of electronic means for recording and preserving commercial data. Nevertheless, the study identifies a need to further develop certain provisions, particularly those relating to the criteria for the obligation to maintain commercial books, the regulation of electronic books, the integrity of digital data, and the traceability of any amendments made to such data. The study recommends updating certain provisions of the Commercial Books Law, strengthening coordination between it, the Law of Evidence, and the Electronic Transactions Law, and adopting more detailed rules governing digital commercial books in a manner that keeps pace with modern technological developments, enhances the stability of commercial transactions, and strengthens the evidentiary value of commercial books before the courts.

title: Advancing digital competence among prospective educational psychologists during educational transformation
container-title: Frontiers in Education
1cf6f4a132ae34b77d5b5837802b8f0555801157.abstract: Introduction Digital transformation is reshaping higher education and increasing the importance of professionally relevant digital skills among future educational psychologists. This cross-sectional study examined undergraduate students' perceptions of digital transformation, their readiness to engage with changes in the educational process, and selected characteristics of the educational environment associated with digital readiness. Methods The sample comprised 100 first- to fourth-year undergraduate students in educational psychology programs. Data were collected using an author-developed questionnaire and analyzed descriptively. An exploratory binary logistic regression was conducted using gender and age as predictors of readiness. Results Most students expressed positive attitudes toward digital transformation and the perceived role of digital competence in education. The use of modern technologies received a mean rating of 6.8/10, while teacher support received a lower mean rating of 5.2/10. The revised logistic model was not statistically significant, and neither gender nor age was associated with the readiness indicator. Discussion Because the questionnaire did not provide a validated composite measure of digital competence, the findings should be interpreted as indicators of perceptions and readiness rather than direct measures of competence. The study emphasizes the need for professionally integrated digital training, stronger pedagogical support, and validated multidimensional instruments in future research.

title: Enjoyment in Digital Play: Exploring Young Children’s Social Interactions
container-title: Australasian Journal of Early Childhood
c37be1a7258197dd6a1f49f431203c9b2d0120ae.abstract: This paper presents findings from a study that explored young children’s verbal and non-verbal expressions of enjoyment in social interactions when engaged in play with an augmented reality (AR) application. Data was collected from 34 children, aged five to eight years, from an indoor laboratory playground setting located in Western Australia. Transcripts of children’s social interactions in situ when engaged in play with the AR app were deductively coded for expressions of enjoyment using Eberle’s (2014) basic elements of play. Findings showed the children’s verbal and non-verbal expressions of anticipation, surprise, and pleasure using selected transcripts of their interactions. This paper argues that by analysing children’s social interactions through the talk-in-interaction, children’s enjoyment is realised through both the words they use and their actions – expressions not evident in broader measures of enjoyment. This exploration enhances our understanding about the aspects of digital play that the children enjoy.

title: Digital Twin Construction and Hierarchical 3D Visualization of Regional Traditional Ceramics
container-title: International Journal of Knowledge Management
cfb2796c1ad695b0fb40b9d11acecbfb1c6d6637.abstract: Existing digital projects for regional ceramic culture suffer from fragmented knowledge, static storage and insufficient iterative capacity, as most 3D reconstruction works merely realize geometric visualization without semantic linkage of kiln sites, firing crafts and user data. This paper constructs a lifecycle-oriented digital twin 3D visualization system for ceramic cultural knowledge assets. Taking ceramic ontology, glaze texture, firing process, kiln space and user behavior as core carriers, we establish unified quantitative data specifications, modeling quality thresholds and a dual closed-loop knowledge iteration mechanism supported by user feedback backflow. By converting user interaction data into knowledge base optimization basis, this study builds an evolvable digital asset framework for ceramic intangible heritage, offering standardized knowledge management solutions for cultural heritage digitization.

title: Digital Accounting, Talent Curriculum Reconstruction, and Evidence From Chinese Higher Vocational Education
container-title: International Journal of Mobile and Blended Learning
afb87dda6739de35f6359f656e1c3381ec8a5263.abstract: Digital-economy-driven industrial transformation has redefined accounting job competencies and caused a prominent industry-education mismatch in vocational talent supply. Conventional higher-vocational accounting training prioritizes manual-accounting knowledge yet lacks systematic digital competency development, leaving graduates poorly adapted to intelligent-finance scenarios. Using post-competency mapping, this study reconstructs a four-dimensional curriculum system, alongside a dynamic content-update mechanism and multi-dimensional evaluation framework, to align training with digital-industry requirements. A two-year controlled empirical investigation involving 870 students from ten higher vocational colleges reveals that the reconstructed curriculum substantially enhances students' digital-related capabilities (Cohen's d = 0.78–1.45). Graduates obtain greater corporate satisfaction, higher starting salaries and higher digital-finance-position employment ratios.

title: Foundry Operations in Unified Supply Chain Digital Twins: A Cross-Industry Literature Review
container-title: International Journal of Metalcasting
1c5d03938333ba64be6cf980bf75f71ff1e32dc3.abstract: Abstract The foundry industry is among the industries with the highest potential for digitalization, and occupies a critical, intermediate position in the industrial value chain, supplying cast components to the automotive, machinery, infrastructure, and energy sectors. To unlock this potential and enable cross-industry interoperability, digital twins (DTs) offer a promising approach for minimizing time, costs, and environmental impacts. This exploratory scoping review maps the existing literature on each pillar of the idea and calls for further research on this topic. The aim of this paper is to explore the existing literature, identify the problems, and discuss what research is necessary to address them from a holistic perspective. The methods are explained in three main topics: (i) scope of existing research, (ii) literature-based maturity assessment models for DTs, and (iii) specific methods employed in current studies. This review identifies key themes in the results, including methods for measuring digital twin maturity, current initiatives, and reference frameworks, interoperable data spaces, and available modeling software. The subsequent discussion addresses the challenges of advancing DT maturity and achieving cross-sector interoperability, the semantic, technical, and governance requirements that follow for foundry DTs, and the challenges that interoperable DTs can address, drawing on the reviewed initiatives, maturity models, and application cases from the foundry industry and from neighboring industries such as mining. The review answers four research questions on the challenges of the foundry industry, on DT maturity models, on interoperability initiatives and applications, and on the requirements for foundry digital twins. It collects the evidence from the literature for the view that the foundry industry is a digital bottleneck in the supply chains of cast products without testing it, and highlights the resulting research gaps. Ultimately, this work provides a structured review and a research agenda that reduces ambiguity and outlines future standardization efforts and research directions toward sustainable, digitalized foundry operations.

title: Versorgungskosten bei psychischen Erkrankungen nach Einführung Digitaler Gesundheitsanwendungen (PsyDiGA): Eine Sekundärdatenanalyse gesetzlich Versicherter
Healthcare costs for mental disorders following the introduction of digital health applications (PsyDiGA): a secondary data analysis of statutory health insurance beneficiaries
container-title: Bundesgesundheitsblatt - Gesundheitsforschung - Gesundheitsschutz
3307bac1ba3c53263883159c25842b259907abd4.abstract: Zusammenfassung Einleitung Seit 2020 können gesetzlich Versicherten Digitale Gesundheitsanwendungen für psychische Erkrankungen (PsyDiGA) verordnet werden. Um diese nutzen zu können, müssen Versicherte einen von der Krankenkasse bereitgestellten Freischaltcode einlösen. Untersucht wurde, wie häufig PsyDiGA verordnet und freigeschaltet werden und wie sich die nachfolgenden Versorgungskosten zwischen Personen mit und ohne eingelösten Freischaltcode unterscheiden. Methoden Analysiert wurden Abrechnungsdaten von Versicherten mit psychischen Erkrankungen der AOK Rheinland-Pfalz/Saarland aus den Jahren 2020–2022. Personen mit und ohne eingelösten Freischaltcode für eine PsyDiGA wurden hinsichtlich ihrer Versorgungskosten verglichen. Die durchschnittlichen Mehrkosten bei eingelöster PsyDiGA wurden für Alter, Geschlecht und Anzahl psychischer Erkrankungen adjustiert. Ergebnisse Insgesamt erhielten 671 Versicherte (0,11 %) einen Freischaltcode, von denen 75 % diesen einlösten. Bei Personen mit ambulanter Behandlungshistorie und eingelöstem Code zeigten sich im adjustierten Vergleich höhere Kosten für ambulante (+160,70 €/Quartal) und stationäre psychotherapeutische Leistungen (+262,10 €/Quartal). Bei Personen mit stationärer Behandlungshistorie und eingelöstem Code waren die adjustierten Kosten für ambulante psychotherapeutische Leistungen ebenfalls höher (+274,30 €/Quartal); für die übrigen Kostenkategorien zeigte sich keine eindeutige Tendenz. Diskussion Der Einsatz von PsyDiGA scheint insbesondere im ambulanten Bereich nicht mit einer Reduktion der Versorgungskosten einherzugehen. Die Ergebnisse deuten darauf hin, dass PsyDiGA eher ergänzend zu bestehenden Versorgungsleistungen als an deren Stelle eingesetzt werden.

title: Strategic Gaze: Attention Allocation and Transition Patterns Across Functional Areas of Interest by Gameplay Outcome
container-title: Proceedings of the ACM on Human-Computer Interaction
fdac82e503d98c86ead27b192a3322c44e4e2dc0.abstract: Video games present players with complex, spatially distributed information across interface elements, with attention shaped by visual features and task goals. Eye tracking provides a useful method for examining player attention through gaze behaviour during gameplay. Yet empirical game research has relied on accumulated fixation measures that capture where attention is directed and how long it is maintained within regions, leaving less known about how gaze moves between regions to coordinate distributed information. We address this gap by integrating distribution-, duration-, and transition-based gaze measures across functionally organised interface regions in relation to gameplay outcomes. We conducted a within-subject study with 32 participants using a deck-building game, defining six functional Areas of Interest (AOIs) within the turn-based combat interface, spanning enemy, player, action, and auxiliary elements. We computed AOI hit, dwell time, transition probabilities, and entropy to compare gaze behaviour across outcome groups. Players in the win group showed more selective attention allocation extending to peripheral auxiliary resources, with more frequent action-oriented gaze transitions, a wider range of AOI pairs, and a more even distribution across AOIs. Within a strategic game setting, our findings show that gameplay outcomes are reflected in how players distribute, sustain, and shift visual attention across functional interface elements, offering a more comprehensive account of attention organisation in gameplay.

title: Dress to Impress Digitally: Social Anxiety And Status Motivation Are Associated With Higher Spending on Digital Cosmetics Among Cosmetic Purchasers
container-title: Proceedings of the ACM on Human-Computer Interaction
b9902c4157cacb613e3283ce62640cfdedd1d076.abstract: Cosmetic items have become one of the most profitable monetization strategies in games. Like fashion in the physical world, their value is socially constructed and tied to visibility, prestige, and identity signalling. This raises questions about whether psychological factors influence cosmetic spending behaviour. Therefore, we conducted a cross-sectional survey with 199 in-game cosmetic purchasers. We assessed trait social anxiety, avatar and self-perception, actual spending for cosmetics, Big Five personality traits, and cosmetic purchase motivation. Through structural equation modelling, we found that, among cosmetic purchasers, trait social anxiety and status motivation showed the strongest association with spending amounts, with reward motives playing a secondary role. However, qualitative findings focused more on aesthetic appeal and economic considerations as primary stated motives, while social and community influences were less central. These findings suggest that individual psychological differences may warrant important design consideration for in-game cosmetics highlighting the multi-layered influences on previous purchase decisions.

title: SAVEstate: A Method for Documenting Player Reflection in Digital Games
container-title: Proceedings of the ACM on Human-Computer Interaction
81714ec3da12706404fcea673745507437e9e18c.abstract: In recent years, interest in eudaimonic player experiences (PX) - concerning reflection, meaning-making, and personal growth - has increased. However, most games user research methods are not well-suited to study eudaimonic PX, as they have been developed to evaluate features of hedonic PX, such as flow, immersion, and playability. To more deeply explore eudaimonic PX, we require methods that can 1) investigate how moment-to-moment PX shapes player reflection and 2) explore how players reengage and reinterpret their experiences longitudinally. In this paper, we present SAVEstate , a method that uses documentation as a means of studying player reflection. SAVEstate consists of two phases: reflection-in-action and reflection-on-action, which allow researchers to probe players’ in-situ reflections and how they reengage with their gameplay, respectively. Using SAVEstate, we were able to observe in-situ meaning-making and connect it to post-game reflection-on-action, and view synchronous sensemaking across multiple participants. We also developed an open-source desktop application for researchers to adapt in their own SAVEstate deployments. We discuss implications for how researchers might use SAVEstate to conduct future research in meaningful PX.

title: Transforming Digital Romance: How Women Otome Game Players Re-Interpret and Re-Construct Their Gaming Experiences Through Retrospective Imaginative Involvement
container-title: Proceedings of the ACM on Human-Computer Interaction
c36d8c1463815e6f00b5e7429ce8815ef6e027eb.abstract: How players develop intimate experiences through gameplay has been extensively studied in HCI and game research. Yet, while existing work largely focuses on intimacy within gameplay, how players may also intentionally extend game-mediated intimacy beyond the game itself is much less understood. Through an interview study (N=25), we aim to advance this research agenda by leveraging the lens of Retrospective Imaginative Involvement (RII), a framework defined as imaginative revisiting and extension of media experiences after exposure, to examine how Asian women players of otome games (single-player digital games that offer fictional romantic relationships with male characters) re-interpret and re-construct their gaming experiences outside the game, and how these post-game practices reshape their digital romantic experiences. This work provides initial empirical insights for expanding existing understandings of game-mediated intimate experiences by highlighting players’ engagement and disengagement spectrum that contributes to nuanced motivations in RIIs as a new form of play, how otome game-mediated intimacy toward virtual characters can also extend offline meanings, and post-game engagement as a unique space for understanding women players’ vulnerabilities. We then propose three high-level design principles to inform future game design that sustains immersive, emotionally fulfilling experiences beyond the gameplay, while mitigating risks we identified.

title: Leveraging Digital Technology on Teaching Basic Science and  Technology for The Transformation of Secondary School Education  in Rivers State
container-title: WORLD JOURNAL OF INNOVATION AND MODERN TECHNOLOGY
3e51c4142f4a7ae1393c0ccfcc9ed8c67adb8956.abstract: The research was on leveraging digital technology on teaching basic science and technology for the trans formation of secondary school education in Rivers State. The study adopted descriptive survey design and guided by two research questions were answered and one hypothesis tested with a population of 80 secondary school teachers of basic science and technology in Obio/Akpor Local Government Area, Rivers State. A sample size of 80 lecturers was drawn using purposive random sampling technique. The instrument for data collection was a 15-item questionnaire validated by three experts and it gave a reliability coefficient of 0.75 that was obtained using Cronbach Alpha method. The data collected were analyzed with mean and standard deviation, and z-test for the hypothesis. The findings showed that there is low extent of availability of digital technology tools for teaching basic science and technology and that there is low extent of utilization of digital tools in teaching basic science and technology for transformation of secondary school in Rivers State. It was then recommended that education stakeholders at all levels should provide digital technology tools for secondary schools in Rivers state., basic science and technology teachers should be given regular training on how to utilize digital tools for teaching in the present changing world, basic science and technology teachers should seek extra opportunities like symposiums, workshops and conferences to be better at the utilization of digital tools for teaching,

title: Digital tools for assessing and managing the innovation and investment potential of food industry enterprises
container-title: Actual problems of innovative economy and law
ae642a8fb5bbbd47129a92927917c9355c28bef5.abstract: This article examines how digital tools assess and manage the innovation and investment potential of food industry enterprises, particularly in the context of the economy’s digital transformation. It underscores the importance of innovation and investment potential as a foundation for modernizing production, enhancing competitiveness, and ensuring enterprises’ sustainable development. The study reviews key digital tools, including Business Intelligence (BI) systems, ERP systems, Big Data technologies, artificial intelligence, cloud computing, and financial modeling platforms. It identifies key indicators for assessing enterprises’ innovation and investment capacity, such as return on investment (ROI), innovation expenditures, production automation levels, labor productivity, and resource utilization efficiency. It also outlines ways to apply digital technologies to automate analysis of enterprise operations, forecast investment risks, optimize financial resource allocation, and monitor the implementation of innovation projects. Finally, it highlights the primary obstacles to digitalization, including high implementation costs, insufficient digital competencies among personnel, and cybersecurity risks. The study proposes practical recommendations for phased implementation of digital solutions, establishing a system of key performance indicators, and strengthening information and analytical management support. The study concludes that the comprehensive use of digital tools supports better-substantiated management decisions, increases efficiency in investment activities, and improves competitiveness for enterprises in the food industry. Future research directions include developing a comprehensive methodology for digitally assessing innovation and investment potential, as well as quantifying the economic impact of implementing digital technologies. Keywords: digital tools, digital transformation, innovation and investment potential, food industry enterprises, potential assessment, investment management, innovation-driven development, investment risks.

title: The Influence of Digital Marketing Strategies on Consumer  Purchase Decisions Among Small and Medium Enterprises in  Nigeria: A Conceptual Review and Framework
container-title: IIARD INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF ECONOMICS AND BUSINESS MANAGEMENT
e6aab266137a3509df7138b424bd004d3265ff4e.abstract: The advent of digital technologies has fundamentally transformed marketing practices and consumer engagement worldwide. Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs), which constitute a significant component of Nigeria's economic structure, increasingly rely on digital marketing strategies to improve brand visibility, engage customers, and encourage purchasing behaviour. Despite the growing acceptance of digital marketing channels such as social media, content marketing, email marketing, and online advertising, there remains a need for a comprehensive conceptual understanding of how these strategies influence consumer purchase decisions within the Nigerian SME context. This paper delivers a conceptual review of the relationship between digital marketing strategies and consumer purchase decisions among SMEs in Nigeria. It hinges on the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM), the AIDA (Awareness, Interest, Desire, Action) model, and the Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB). The study adopts a conceptual/narrative review approach and synthesizes relevant literature together with four recent Nigerian empirical studies, with particular attention to Adeoye et al. (2022), the study most closely aligned with the present outcome variable. The reviewed evidence consistently reports positive and statistically significant relationships between digital marketing dimensions and SME or consumer outcomes. For example, Adeoye et al. (2022) reported R² = 0.428 (Adjusted R² = 0.424) for social media marketing, content marketing, and online advertising in predicting consumer purchase decision,while other reviewed studies reported R² values ranging from 0.155 to 0.787 for related outcomes. The synthesis indicates that direct-effect evidence is substantial but fragmented and does not adequately explain the mechanisms connecting digital marketing exposure with final purchase decisions. The paper therefore proposes a mediated Digital Marketing Consumer Decision (DMCD) framework and a set of research propositions that can be empirically tested in future studies. The framework contributes a mechanism-oriented perspective for understanding digital marketing effectiveness among SMEs in Nigeria and provides practical implications for managers, policymakers, and researchers.

title: Digital twins for robot-assisted nuclear decommissioning: a review of perception, radiological mapping, and model interoperability, with the DORADO project as a case study
container-title: Frontiers in Nuclear Engineering
f1f5dec6fe2b47b2421767db3b43c2c9f58644eb.abstract: Nuclear decommissioning increasingly relies on digital technologies to support characterisation, planning, monitoring, and decision-making in environments where access is limited by radiation, contamination, or other operational constraints. Digital twins provide a framework for integrating geometric, radiological, and operational information, while robotic systems acquire data and perform tasks with reduced human exposure. Although often treated separately, the two are coupled through a continuous exchange of information: robotic observations update the digital representation of the facility, and the twin provides the context for mission planning and execution. This review examines that coupling from the perspective of information representation and information flow. Based on a structured search of the peer-reviewed literature, standards, and public technical reports, it covers geometric and radiological sensing, radiation-field estimation, geometric and semantic representations and their interoperability, geometry for radiation-transport calculation, localisation, change detection, mission planning, and data governance. Comparative tables summarise sensing technologies, radiological instruments, exchange formats, localisation approaches, international programmes, and the evidence obtained in real facilities to date. A dedicated section synthesises uncertainty propagation and verification and validation requirements for safety-relevant use. The EURATOM DORADO project is then presented separately as a case study, showing how the requirements identified in the review are addressed in an ongoing engineering programme and distinguishing published results from implementation and ongoing development. The review concludes that the main barriers are not the performance of individual sensors or algorithms but interoperability, end-to-end uncertainty management, validation under representative radiological conditions, and long-term data governance, and that most current systems operate at the level of digital shadows rather than fully bidirectional digital twins.

title: From ecosystem conditions to sustainable performance: role of dynamic capability and digital transformation in MSMEs
container-title: Competitiveness Review: An International Business Journal
7139b0344bf5c67c182d75449fbdfad370dc3e34.abstract: Purpose Despite entrepreneurial ecosystems (EE) being viewed as enablers of competitiveness and performance, the firm-level mechanism through which EE conditions translate into sustainable outcomes remains ambiguous, particularly in manufacturing micro, small and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs). This study aims to examine the effect of EE conditions on sustainable performance (SP), and effect of dynamic capability (DC) as a mediating mechanism and digital transformation (DT) as a boundary condition moderator. Design/methodology/approach This study uses cross-sectional survey data from 257 manufacturing MSMEs in an emerging market such as India. EE conditions are modelled as a second-order formative construct, estimated using the disjoint two-stage approach. The hypothesized relationships were analysed using partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM), with predictive relevance assessed using PLSpredict. Findings The findings show that EE conditions exert a significant positive effect on both DC and SP. DC significantly influences SP and partially mediates the EE−SP relationship. The interactions between DT and EE significantly strengthen the EE−SP relationship, confirming DT’s role as a boundary condition. Practical implications MSMEs aiming for sustainable outcomes should focus on developing DC alongside ecosystem engagement. Digital preparedness should be viewed as an enhancement of overall capabilities rather than a separate performance driver. Furthermore, policy interventions should integrate digital readiness into broader ecosystems, rather than treating the two separately. Originality/value This study contributes to the research on EE and DC capability theory by examining the EE−SP relationship in the MSME context, which is jointly controlled by an internal capability mechanism and a digital contingency condition.

title: Inertial−Digital Microfluidics Platform for High-Recovery, High-Purity Circulating Tumor Cell Isolation toward Single-Cell Genomic Analysis
container-title: Analytical Chemistry
7da4fce8f0721886ef7df0baa8b9a61cb05e1517.abstract: Abstract Isolating circulating tumor cells (CTCs) remains challenging owing to their rarity and the abundant background of white blood cells (WBCs). To overcome the traditional trade-off between the recovery rate and purity, we developed an orthogonal decoupling microfluidic platform consisting of two integrated modules. The integrated modules achieved an overall recovery of ∼87.3% and an overall WBCs depletion of 99.97%, reducing background WBCs contamination to a level that permitted direct microscopic visualization and single-cell isolation. Specifically, the first spiral inertial microfluidic module achieved an approximately 90% recovery rate for MCF-7 and HeLa cells (at a flow speed of 3 mL/min) while depleting 99.4% of WBCs. Second, a downstream digital microfluidic module removed &gt;95% of residual WBCs using immunomagnetic depletion and isolated single MCF-7 cells via electrowetting-on-dielectric actuation combined with hydrophilic microstructures. Subsequent whole-genome sequencing of single MCF-7 cells from spiked samples successfully detected expected copy number variations (1q/8q amplifications) and a PIK3CA mutation, confirming the integrated platform’s reliability. In preliminary clinical testing of blood samples obtained from patients with cancer, the platform successfully identified and isolated EpCAM/PanCK-positive and CD45-negative CTCs. Overall, this integrated approach resolves the CTC recovery−purity bottleneck, enabling precision single-cell genomics from spiked samples and providing a robust foundation for clinical translation.

title: Integration of an FDA-Authorized Digital Autism Diagnostic Tool Into an Outpatient Developmental Pediatrics Workflow: Preliminary Quality Improvement Study
container-title: JMIR Formative Research
b42a8355c78cb1388e8199b819806b84930ec66c.abstract: Background Long wait times and specialist shortages delay autism spectrum disorder (ASD) diagnosis, often beyond the period when early intervention is most effective. Digital diagnostic tools may help increase diagnostic capacity by supporting clinicians in delivering timely autism evaluations within routine outpatient care. Objective This study aimed to conduct a preliminary assessment of the integration of a digital autism diagnostic device (Canvas Dx) into an outpatient developmental pediatrics workflow, including a descriptive evaluation of agreement between device outputs and specialist clinical diagnoses and an exploration of clinician and caregiver experience. Methods A single-center, prospective quality improvement study evaluated the implementation and performance of Canvas Dx in a specialty developmental pediatrics clinic. Canvas Dx is a Food and Drug Administration (FDA)–authorized digital ASD diagnostic device approved for use in children aged 18 to 72 months with caregiver or health care provider concern for developmental delay. Eligible children were consecutively prescribed Canvas Dx during the study period and completed the assessment as part of routine clinical care. Device diagnostic outputs were compared with the final specialist clinical diagnoses. Clinician and caregiver feedback was collected to explore their experience with the assessment process and perceived workflow impact via poststudy surveys that captured both structured quantitative questions and open-ended qualitative questions. Results A total of 28 children were included (mean age 52.2, SD 13.8 months; 7/28, 25% female), with an autism prevalence of 67.9% (19/28) based on specialist diagnosis. The device generated a determinate result for 22 (78.6%) participants. Among participants with determinate device results, sensitivity was 94.1% (95% CI 73%-99%) and specificity was 80% (95% CI 37.6%-96.4%). Positive predictive value was 94.1% (95% CI 73%-99%), and negative predictive value was 80% (95% CI 37.6-96.4%) when compared with specialist diagnosis. These estimates were imprecise, particularly for specificity and negative predictive value, because of the small number of participants without an ASD diagnosis. Clinicians reported improved insights and ease of use during evaluation visits, and caregivers reported high satisfaction with the assessment process. Conclusions This preliminary quality improvement assessment demonstrates the feasibility of integrating Canvas Dx into a routine outpatient developmental pediatrics workflow and provides initial descriptive data on agreement with specialist diagnostic determinations and clinician and caregiver experience. Given the small sample size and resulting imprecision of diagnostic performance estimates, these findings should be interpreted as preliminary and used to inform larger prospective evaluations of diagnostic performance and workflow impact.

title: Mobile Medical Education Apps as Digital Health Information Resources in China and the United States: Longitudinal App Store Metadata Analysis and Topic Modeling of User Review Narratives
container-title: JMIR Medical Education
7e47a1ef3d0e5a0c6e3d1a6f8d731c7a846526f3.abstract: Background Mobile learning apps are increasingly used in medical education, but cross-national evidence on their longitudinal development and rating-based satisfaction patterns remains limited. Objective This study aimed to examine the longitudinal evolution of medical education apps in China and the United States and identify app-related factors associated with positive and negative rating deviations among app store reviewers. Methods We conducted a longitudinal app store analysis of 467 medical education apps and 232,598 user reviews from major Chinese and US app stores. Joinpoint regression was used to characterize temporal trends in app development. Latent Dirichlet allocation (LDA) topic modeling, with large language model–assisted topic labeling, was used to identify themes in user reviews. Tobit regression, Wald tests, and Kano model classification were used to examine asymmetric associations with positive and negative rating deviations and to classify review topics into functional attributes. Results Among the 232,598 analyzed reviews, 219,105 were rated 4 stars or higher, corresponding to an overall rating-based satisfaction proxy rate of 94.20%. This rating-based satisfaction proxy rate was lower in China than in the United States (128,018/139,416, 91.82% vs 91,087/93,182, 97.75%). Within the 2025-observable analytic cohort, cumulative observable app counts increased significantly in both countries, with average annual percentage changes of 41.69% in China and 41.17% in the United States. The joinpoint analysis identified temporal inflection points within this observable cohort around 2017 and 2021-2022. User concerns also shifted over time. In China, the dominant review theme changed from “Clinical practicality” in 2009-2017 (2735/7385 reviews, 37.03%) to “Practice test function” in 2018-2025 (53,929/132,031 reviews, 40.85%). In the United States, user attention shifted from “Functional availability” in 2009-2017 (20,736/26,118 reviews, 79.39%) to “Cost” in 2018-2025 (27,401/67,064 reviews, 40.86%). Tobit regression and Kano classification showed that factors associated with positive and negative rating deviations differed by country and developmental stage, with essential and charm factors varying across temporal phases. Conclusions This longitudinal app store analysis revealed distinct but partially converging patterns of observable app development and rating-based satisfaction among app store reviewers in China and the United States. These findings suggest that future medical education apps should prioritize reliable content, technical stability, affordable exam preparation, and personalized learning support. They may also inform the design of future AI-supported medical education platforms while requiring further validation with learning process and outcome data.

title: Educação digital e currículo contemporâneo: letramento crítico, inovação e gestão da aprendizagem
3bef438175b05d356b3758d962709de73d8c242a.abstract: Este estudo investiga como a integração do letramento crítico e tecnologias digitais pode ser efetivamente implementada no currículo de Língua Portuguesa. O problema central explorado é a necessidade de promover habilidades de pensamento crítico em estudantes de Língua Portuguesa, utilizando tecnologias digitais como ferramentas pedagógicas essenciais.

title: Repurposing, redefining, and reimagining: A paradigm shift towards person-driven neuroscience in the digital age
eb7c604398eea4a56a0483cacdb15b8710cc8e55.abstract: The focus of neuroscience has traditionally hinged on collecting quantifiable physiological data that are often distanced from the lived experiences of people. In contrast, qualitative, subjective, and situational information provides rich context, but lacks the empirical precision needed to map to neural processes. To reconcile this gap, we established ‘The Lαβ’ as an interdisciplinary initiative that fuses person-driven experiences, personal reflection, and empirical neuroscience. People engage with their chosen experiences in their chosen settings while wearing a portable EEG headset. Timestamped information is then collected from a variety of sources. We introduce our novel neurotriangulation approach: A person‑driven synthesis of quantitative electrophysiological signals, qualitative observations, and subjective and situational information into a single analytic stream. Our aim is to provide people with opportunities for neuro-self-reflection. We use an ethics-first approach to preserve data sovereignty, privacy, autonomy, and agency for the individual. In this paper, we present real-world case studies to demonstrate our data collection, real-time field analysis, and co-interpretation methodologies. These case studies also underscore the neurotriangulation model as an approach to move beyond reductive, data-centric models toward a person‑driven paradigm. This shift allows neurodata to be more accessible, inclusive, and personally meaningful, while prioritising safety and subjectivity. This has the potential to reshape how we think about neuroscientific applications in fields such as education and training, anthropology, creative arts, wellbeing, and mental health. By repurposing and redefining the use of extant neurotechnology, we are reimagining a future in which our understanding of ourselves is person-driven, reality-based, and ethically sound.

title: Endogenous spatial attention in far-peripheral vision:  Effects of eccentricity and cortical magnification scaling
9a9159b102781e51baaa53cf2a10fea90c176e21.abstract: Endogenous spatial attention allows observers to prioritize behaviorally relevant locations, but whether it remains effective in far-peripheral vision, where the cortical representation of a given stimulus is markedly reduced, is not fully understood. The present study examined whether endogenous spatial attention produces reaction-time facilitation at 40° eccentricity and whether the magnitude of this facilitation varies with eccentricity and stimulus scaling based on cortical magnification. Fifteen participants completed two experiments using a spatial-cuing task in which central arrow cues predicted the side on which targets would appear at 3°, 10°, and 40° eccentricity, with double-headed arrows serving as neutral cues. In Experiment 1, target stimuli were identical in physical size across eccentricities. In Experiment 2, stimulus size was adjusted according to the cortical magnification factor to partially reduce eccentricity-dependent differences in cortical representation. In both experiments, responses were fastest in the valid condition, intermediate in the neutral condition, and slowest in the invalid condition. A reliable cuing effect was observed at 40° eccentricity in both experiments. The magnitude of the cuing effect did not reliably differ across eccentricities in either experiment, nor between the unscaled and M-scaled conditions at 40°. These findings indicate that endogenous spatial attention remains behaviorally effective in far-peripheral vision at 40° eccentricity.

title: Smart Egg Processing in the Digital Food Era, Part II: AI-Optimized Non-Thermal Processing, Functional Preservation, and Industrial Implementation
container-title: Foods
08c440d804cf9720e538d08e8758d45f56bd879a.abstract: This is Part II of a two-part critical review of smart egg processing: the integration of sensing, artificial intelligence (AI), and processing technologies into one connected system. Building on Part I (non-destructive sensing and AI-based quality prediction), it reviews non-thermal egg processing technologies (high-pressure processing, pulsed electric fields, ultrasound, cold plasma, and ultraviolet treatments), AI-based parameter optimization, and effects on nutritional and functional quality. It then examines requirements for an integrated architecture: closed-loop control, digital twins and traceability, food safety, sustainability, scale-up, and standardization. Each technology is a mechanistically distinct but individually limited route to microbial inactivation. In the laboratory-scale egg studies reviewed, hurdle combinations at moderate intensity generally outperformed single technologies, although differences in matrices, organisms, and conditions preclude direct comparison. One laboratory study applied AI-driven multi-objective optimization to ultrasound–mild-heat co-sterilization of liquid whole egg, improving microbial safety and foaming retention together. In the literature searched, no study linked real-time sensing to automated non-thermal process control for eggs beyond the conceptual stage, and measured egg-specific energy, life cycle, and economic data were largely absent. A knowledge gap analysis, research agenda, and evidence-tiered conceptual framework (Smart Egg Processing 4.0) are presented.

title: From Multi-Sensor Survey to a Multi-Scale Geospatial Digital Twin Foundation of a Historic Hill Town: Fiumefreddo Bruzio, Southern Italy
container-title: Remote Sensing
513b520ce2401b90e888fb1a366a87453b954a7c.abstract: Historic hill towns require geometric information capable of relating urban morphology, construction features, and structural details within a common spatial and semantic framework. This paper presents a multi-sensor, multi-scale geomatics workflow for establishing an integrated geospatial information framework for the historic centre of Fiumefreddo Bruzio in Calabria, southern Italy. A control network of 38 points provided the spatial reference for UAV and terrestrial photogrammetry, six SLAM trajectories, and 270 static laser scans covering five buildings. Point clouds generated by Structure from Motion and range-based sensors were co-registered in the RDN2008/UTM zone 33N coordinate reference system and used to produce orthophotos, digital terrain and surface models, contour lines, textured meshes, and building-scale drawings. These products were organised within an interoperable geospatial information system based on persistent links between settlement-, aggregate-, building-, façade-, space-, and macroelement-level entities. The framework also supported structural characterisation and seismic vulnerability assessment at building and urban scales, linking building screening and potential local mechanisms to their spatial interpretation. The resulting survey-based digital model supports conservation documentation, seismic screening, and street-network analysis, while providing the foundation for future digital twin development rather than an operational implementation. The study offers a transferable acquisition-to-information workflow, preserving data provenance and metric quality for risk-informed management of historic settlements.

title: Digital Twin-Based Virtual Simulation Method for Visualization Monitoring of Flexible Production Lines Towards Intelligent Manufacturing
container-title: Sensors
7addbbc3be18c5c81d73c68d76aedeb69c194234.abstract: With the in-depth development of intelligent manufacturing worldwide, flexible production modes and corresponding production lines for personalized, customized, small-batch, and multi-variety products have become the dominant force in today’s manufacturing industry. To address the challenges of real-time information interaction and visualization monitoring in the flexible production lines (FPLs), this paper conducts in-depth research on the 3D visualization simulation of FPLs based on digital twin (DT) according to the characteristics of FPLs and the demand for intelligent development. Firstly, a five-layer DT framework for 3D visualization monitoring of FPLs is proposed, which is divided into the physical entity layer, twin model layer, twin data layer, application service layer, and connection transport layer. The corresponding DT models of the twin model layer are then organized at the atomic, unit, and system levels and described from four dimensions: geometric physical, attribute information, behavioral logic, and constraint rules. On this basis, the data interconnection mechanism, real-time data-driven twin model mapping, and twin data management methods of the above DT framework are further studied. Finally, a representative machining FPL for mechanical processing is selected as a case study, a virtual simulation system of FPLs for 3D visualization monitoring based on DT is developed and implemented. Through the implementation and application in the field operation, the effectiveness and feasibility of the proposed method and developed system are verified.

title: A Lightweight Hybrid-Attention Conformer for Affective State Recognition from Wearable EEG
container-title: Sensors
7151f5c06706d1f1a22ba53b83f94dc997422dce.abstract: Recognizing affective states from electroencephalography (EEG) is a core task in affective computing, with applications in mental health monitoring and public safety. Most existing approaches rely on handcrafted features or image-based transformations of EEG, while transformer models capture global context at high computational cost. This study proposes KimiFormer, an end-to-end hybrid-attention Conformer that classifies raw EEG directly. A hierarchical Spatio-Temporal Stemming (STS) module tokenizes the multichannel signal and learns inter-electrode relationships. Stacked Conformer blocks combine linear and full attention in a 3:1 ratio, reducing computational cost while preserving long-range modeling. The model was evaluated on the public EEG Violence Dataset, recorded with a 14-channel wearable headset from 14 participants viewing violent and neutral videos. Under record-wise leave-one-record-out cross-validation with nested selection of the training hyperparameters, KimiFormer achieved 95.5% accuracy (97.0% under 10-fold cross-validation). On the external DREAMER dataset, its subject-independent performance remained close to chance (balanced accuracy 52.7% for valence and 50.2% for arousal), as did that of two established raw-EEG models. Ablation showed the STS module to be essential (65% accuracy without it). With 3.2 M parameters, 1.51 GFLOPs and an inference latency of 15.64 ms per sample, KimiFormer is suited to real-time, on-device processing of low-channel wearable EEG.

title: Participating in Socioscientific Issue-Oriented Citizen Science Investigations: Mapping the Digital Terrain
container-title: in education
c0699d095124b0e9109c1a3a2510b16da63e03cd.abstract: Participation in Citizen Science (CitSci) projects can deepen understandings of science and the socially embedded nature of its practices, thereby better understanding science and scientists and better contextualizing science claims and knowledge. This paper draws attention to the reciprocal relationship between a socioscientific issues (SSI) framework and CitSci projects. As part of a broader study of CitSci projects within and across Canada, we developed an SSI analysis framework to understand and interpret how online text resources describing Canadian CitiSci projects integrate SSI perspectives. Our analysis suggests that selected SSI components are underdeveloped in online resources on project websites, and that participant engagement in most projects focus mainly on data collection. This analysis highlights opportunities to further understand and overcome challenges that influence whether such projects are implemented in K–12 and to explore how they might contribute to society and science overall. Keywords: Citizen Science (CitSci), scoping, socioscientific issues (SSI), SSI framework, public science literacy

title: Digital health interventions for psoriasis management: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
container-title: Frontiers in Medicine
3257c0b4f50447f88be585bd6f0ca0e9aa570d7d.abstract: Objective To systematically evaluate the effects of digital health interventions on disease severity and dermatology-specific quality of life in patients with psoriasis. Methods We searched PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL) through the Cochrane Library, and four Chinese databases (CNKI, Wanfang, VIP, and SinoMed) from inception to April 2026. Randomized controlled trials of psoriasis management interventions in which digital technology was the core component or a major component were eligible. The primary outcome was a PASI-family disease severity score. The secondary outcome was the Dermatology Life Quality Index (DLQI). Standardized mean differences were pooled as Hedges' g using random-effects models. Sensitivity analyses and structured narrative synthesis were also performed. Results Eleven randomized controlled trials involving 1,195 patients with psoriasis were included. Six studies contributed data to at least one prespecified quantitative synthesis. Digital health interventions did not significantly improve PASI-family scores (Hedges’ g : −0.07; 95% CI: −0.28 to 0.14; I 2 = 0.0%) or DLQI scores (Hedges’ g : −0.12; 95% CI: −0.46 to 0.21; I 2 = 59.8%). Sensitivity analyses did not materially change the findings. Narrative synthesis suggested that digital health interventions may improve process-related outcomes, including treatment adherence, disease knowledge, self-management, and access to follow-up care. Conclusions Current randomized evidence does not show that digital health interventions significantly improve skin lesion or symptom severity or dermatology-specific quality of life in patients with psoriasis. Nonsignificant differences should be interpreted as evidence of clinical equivalency rather than treatment failure, given that digital health interventions may maintain standard-of-care results while reducing travel burden, costs, and waiting times. Digital health interventions are better viewed as an adjunct to usual psoriasis care than as a replacement for face-to-face care or pharmacological treatment.
