945d92687c6d7953d19a14cadf41191d142af600.abstract: <jats:p>Morphometric and reproductive-biological traits of grass carp (Ctenopharyngodon idella Valenciennes, 1844) aged 3-5 years (n=540; 270 females, 270 males) reared in 2023-2025 at three farms (one monoculture, two polyculture) were studied. No significant differences in body size were found among farms (p>0.05), whereas gonadosomatic index (GSI) differed significantly among all three farms (Welch ANOVA, F=838.15; p<0.001; Games-Howell post-hoc). Compliance with the GSI≥12% criterion showed an absolute association with farm (100%, 0% and 100%; χ²=226.0; p<0.001). Most importantly, females selected by the GSI criterion significantly outperformed a traditional unselected control group on every reproductive measure ‒ relative fecundity (141.4 vs 111.8 thousand eggs/kg; p=0.023), fertilization rate (86.6% vs 78.0%; p<0.001), hatching rate (80.5% vs 74.1%; p<0.001), and survival to active feeding (75.7% vs 65.0%; p<0.001). These findings experimentally validate the practical effectiveness of GSI-based selection as a scientifically grounded method for forming a high-productivity broodstock.</jats:p>

title: Measure what you manage? Comparing urban forest composition metrics used in research assessing carbon and avian outcomes of urban forest management
container-title: Environmental Research: Ecology
7a32747428f857bdfc391ab3b8103f206e7c29f1.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    Urban forests are multifunctional social-ecological systems that can contribute to both climate change mitigation and biodiversity conservation. However, management of urban forests for these objectives are often studied independently. Knowing which measures can be used to assess multiple objectives could enable integrated monitoring efforts and subsequently increase potentials for synergies in management. We compared the use of forest composition metrics in studies focused on carbon storage (
                    <jats:italic>n</jats:italic>
                    = 109) and avian diversity (
                    <jats:italic>n</jats:italic>
                    = 158) extracted from a published systematic literature map. Through qualitative content analysis, we developed a standardized set of 24 urban forest composition metrics spanning size, taxonomy, structure, tree characteristics, and presence of vegetation layer types. Analysis assessed frequency and co-occurrence of metrics for research assessing carbon or avian outcomes. Carbon-focused studies were dominated by a smaller and more restricted set of variables, with tree species composition and diameter measured in over 90% of studies. In contrast, avian studies used a broader and specialized suite of metrics, emphasizing different types of vegetation layers and diverse habitat features such as shrubs, cavities, and fruit resources. Co-occurrence analysis revealed tightly clustered measurement frameworks in carbon studies and somewhat more diffuse patterns in avian research. These results highlight how the same measures of urban forest composition have been and can be used to assess both avian and carbon management outcomes. Overlaps and gaps identified places where alignment in urban forest monitoring could improve the capacity to manage for multiple outcomes.
                  </jats:p>

title: Between Artifice and Enlightenment: Queer Critique, Insecurity, and the AI Large Language Model
container-title: Insecurity and the Eclipse of Enlightenment
eb93d5dc2a9e17c6e89c89b29ec656faaa8e39e1.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Over several decades, machine learning systems—often described with the double metaphor “artificial intelligence”—have become indispensable computational tools in the flow and mediation of economic and social capital. These systems can, on the surface, appear to deepen the dialectic of enlightenment identified by Horkheimer and Adorno by enabling ever greater domination over natural systems and human agency. They therefore generate widespread concern that computational advances endanger the security and autonomy of human subjects, especially in the sphere of production and exchange. Contemporary social theory offers conceptual tools that go beyond received categories of domination and autonomy, however, to provide a reanalysis of machine learning systems and their implication in social dynamics and economic relations. This chapter focuses on the ways large language model (LLM) systems demonstrate complex affinities with theories of mimesis and simulacrum, and therefore how such systems and require a rethinking of performativity and artifice. Recent queer critique—in which reflection on computational systems and simulacra is proliferating—and contemporary social theory, when read together, thus reveal how rhetoric about LLMs demonstrates slippages between agency, performance, reproduction, representation, and meaning that must be unpacked historically and conceptually before metaphors of the “artificial” and “intelligence” can carry analytical weight in addressing today’s socioeconomic relations. Ultimately, this theoretical-conceptual reading highlights the stakes of the problem of truth in systems where artifice manifests both socially and computationally.</jats:p>

title: Exploring Leadership and Management Principles Through the Bhagavad Gita
container-title: Negotiating Faith, Fact, and the Future of Higher Education
c5487c95d6fec2cf75eaa336c1c7bb7f09f584e4.abstract: <jats:p>Leadership affects ethics, decision-making, and management. Transformational, servant, and situational leadership are popular today, but ancient Indian wisdom offers a unique perspective. The Bhagavad Gita teaches leadership, decision-making, and self-mastery. This research compares Bhagavad Gita leadership ideals to modern management. The study examines Dharma, Karma Yoga, resilience in decision-making, ethical leadership, and imaginative thinking. These ideas mirror transformational, ethical, and aware leadership. By studying Krishna's instruction to Arjuna, corporate leaders may achieve inner stability, strategic decision-making, and ethical responsibility. Motivation and sustainable leadership study Nishkama Karma—acting without outcomes.</jats:p>

title: Enhancing Virtual Education
container-title: Negotiating Faith, Fact, and the Future of Higher Education
29e1f9bbee2e7b9ef6f5798250cde760a1254465.abstract: <jats:p>Applications of artificial intelligence (AI) are shaping new ways of teaching, including the creation of virtual teachers who can automate the teaching process. AI can combine text-to-image, text-to-speech, lip sync and gesture animation for the creation of virtual avatars who can present and teach. However, despite advancements in technology, there are still issues with the realism of avatars and the ability to synchronize all of these processes in real-time. This chapter discusses the main artificial intelligence technologies that have been used to build automated virtual instructors, including advancements, challenges, and applications. In addition, the author discusses the educational value of these technologies and the need for better algorithms and system designs to foster the reliable, safe, and effective use of artificial intelligence in virtual education.</jats:p>

title: Reassessing Faith and Facts in AI-Augmented Modern Higher Education
container-title: Negotiating Faith, Fact, and the Future of Higher Education
7acbc3cc08e83ccb86f74983a4af53870891720e.abstract: <jats:p>The rapid integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) into modern higher education has produced a dual impact: while AI has opened new opportunities for innovation in teaching, learning, and research, it has also introduced significant challenges for academic practice. This paper explores how AI reshapes epistemic boundaries by challenging traditional notions and examines how confidence in institutional traditions and technological promise intersects with empirical data and algorithmic reasoning, and the ethical implications for transparent decision-making frameworks. By combining theoretical perspectives with practical examples, this paper highlights how AI is redefining epistemological foundations by the need to strengthen the relationship between faith and facts. The paper argues for a human-centred approach that promotes adaptive learning cultures. It concludes by proposing a forward-looking framework to help modern universities remain grounded in an AI-intensive future.</jats:p>

title: Regulation of the Use of AI in the Health Sector From a Human Rights Perspective
container-title: Innovation, Governance, and Resilience in Global Health Systems
1a2713af22e11b09e9095d4390eda378d5709e78.abstract: <jats:p>The discussion for the use and regulation of Artificial Intelligence in the healthcare sector from a human rights perspective is much needed due to its intrinsic ethical, social, legal and non-jurisdictional implications. The fourth generation human rights core discourse is focused on the technological advancements, its impact on human lives. Though the fourth-generation human rights are not yet enlisted and explicitly codified through domestic or international legislative body, nevertheless; this is one of the socio-legal discourse after invention of AI. The European Commission has criticized AI systems for not adequately addressing patients' rights health-related risks such as discrimination, privacy concerns, and opaque decision-making processes, etc.</jats:p>

title: Education Management as a Strategic Tool for Strengthening Health Systems in Georgia
container-title: Innovation, Governance, and Resilience in Global Health Systems
19c593837e1a9255bceca63c8ecf25c96a6170dc.abstract: <jats:p>This study examines education management as a strategic tool for strengthening Georgia's health system from a sociological perspective. It argues that workforce challenges such as regional disparities, professional imbalances, and migration are not only due to numerical shortages but reflect deeper structural links between education, institutions, and global labor markets. Drawing on qualitative analysis and sociological theory, the study shows that centralized and specialization-oriented medical education reinforces unequal workforce distribution and weak retention, particularly outside urban areas. At the same time, internationalization increases professional mobility, further intensifying these challenges. The study concludes that aligning education with health system needs through curriculum reform, decentralization, and inclusive policies can reduce inequalities and support a more resilient and sustainable healthcare system in Georgia.</jats:p>

The growing period, seed cotton weight per boll, plant productivity, fiber length, and fiber yield were evaluated in comparison with the Andijan-36 standard cultivar. The Bukhara-6 × 010888 combination achieved a plant productivity of 81.5 g and a fiber yield of 40.4%. The S-6524 × 011592 combination had the shortest growing period (114 days) and the greatest fiber length (34.5 mm). The Sulton × 011482 combination showed a plant productivity of 80.0 g and a fiber yield of 39.9%. 69d9be549364767eb4cd15be7d3c8e10711b9280.abstract: <jats:p>The paper analyzes grate constructions used in cotton cleaners for removing large impurities. 36d6b77407653d455c80e2f500634a6232d7a5a9.abstract: <jats:p>The increase in the demand for energy across the world coupled with environmental issues has heightened the importance of developing sustainable and intelligent energy systems. Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) represent some of the key technologies that can be employed to optimize the efficiency, reliability, and sustainability of the current energy systems. These technologies have become important due to the capacity of the systems based on such technologies to make data-driven decisions using predictive algorithms, automated control processes, as well as real-time decision-making processes. Some common applications of AI and ML include renewable energy forecasting, energy storage systems, predictive maintenance of energy systems, smart grids, and smart energy management in demand side. AI-based approaches for sustainable energy hold a lot of benefits for the environment as well as the economy. AI/ML technologies within the scope of sustainable energy engineering will be critical in realizing goals of energy efficiency and reduced emissions.</jats:p>

title: Deep Learning for Adaptive Management of Renewable Hybrid Power Systems

Optimizing Sustainable Energy Engineering With AI and Machine Learning
8dbc26d9167ed7772f47b06f9aa8d0293cf7c8ac.abstract: <jats:p>This study examines the problem of adaptive control for hybrid renewable energy systems combining photovoltaic panels, wind turbines, and battery storage under conditions of generation uncertainty and price volatility. A control strategy based on deep reinforcement learning is proposed, which does not require an explicit mathematical model and accounts for long-term consequences, including battery degradation. The control task is formalized as a markov decision process with an integral discounted reward combining economic costs, penalties for energy curtailment, and storage aging losses. Computational experiments on real meteorological data demonstrate that the trained regulator reduces operating costs by 12–15% compared to heuristic strategies, increases the share of renewable energy used by 18–22%, and extends estimated battery life by 15–20%. The results confirm the advantages of the proposed approach over classical methods, particularly under high uncertainty. Limitations and prospects for practical implementation are discussed.</jats:p>

5f910b7c7ff3cc7a08791e8c37c348d51a9d359d.abstract: <jats:p>The rapid growth of distributed energy resources and renewable technologies has increased the need for intelligent management of modern power systems. Microgrids offer a reliable, flexible, and sustainable solution by integrating local generation, storage, and controllable loads. However, their planning and control are complex due to uncertainties in renewable generation, varying load demand, and dynamic conditions. Artificial Intelligence (AI) has emerged as an effective tool to address these challenges. Techniques such as machine learning, deep learning, and optimization enable accurate forecasting of energy demand, renewable output, and system behavior.AI also enhances real-time control through adaptive decision-making and efficient energy management. This improves reliability, reduces costs, and increases resilience to disturbances. Overall, AI integration enables efficient resource use, minimizes losses, and supports the transition to smart, sustainable, and decentralized power systems.</jats:p>

96ab7ef154dc58376a40cf75f589dc662f80d0d9.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter reviews conventional optimization methods and AI-assisted approaches for hybrid renewable energy microgrids, highlighting their roles in system planning, sizing, operation, and control. It also explores emerging technologies, including reinforcement learning, explainable AI, digital twins, and edge AI, that are shaping the next generation of intelligent energy systems. To illustrate the practical application of these concepts, the chapter presents a case study of a hybrid renewable energy microgrid in Muanda, Democratic Republic of the Congo, featuring solar photovoltaic generation, battery energy storage, and blue-carbon bioenergy resources. The case study shows how optimization techniques can enhance techno-economic and environmental performance and discusses the potential of AI-based forecasting, intelligent battery management, and reinforcement learning to further improve system reliability, renewable energy utilization, and long-term sustainability.</jats:p>

title: Digital Intelligence and AI-Based System Optimization in Waste-to-Energy Infrastructure for Net-Zero Cities
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Optimizing Sustainable Energy Engineering With AI and Machine Learning
ff36013178296736d6e2747d2c7e1830b32bd841.abstract: <jats:p>The integration of digital intelligence and artificial intelligence in waste-to-energy (WtE) infrastructure optimization to achieve net-zero cities is presented in this chapter. The rapid urbanization and the growing amount of waste demand efficient and sustainable solutions. Municipal waste is turned into energy in WtE systems, and traditional operations lack flexibility and efficiency. The chapter uses systematic literature review as a method on the topic indexed in more than 200 articles and summarizing main conclusions of the quality research. It discusses monitoring with IoT, digital twins, and real-time optimization based on AI and predictive maintenance and energy recovery that is better. Case studies show the changes in the operational efficiency, emission control, and stability of systems. A conceptual AI-enabled framework is presented to find a solution to combine WtE systems with smart grids and urban energy networks. The results conclude on how smart WtE infrastructure contributes to the use of the circular economy and sustainable, low-carbon urban development.</jats:p>

title: AI-Driven Optimization of Solar Thermal Systems
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Optimizing Sustainable Energy Engineering With AI and Machine Learning
0860e093417810bedf80a8a8c80f3dec419bac99.abstract: <jats:p>Solar thermal systems encounter distinct operational challenges, which hinder their applicability. Artificial intelligence (AI) has the potential to solve them. The AI is more flexible and adaptable than traditional methods, which cannot deal with unpredictable factors, including changing weather and fluctuating energy demands. In this chapter, we introduced the solar thermal systems, and then the fundamentals of AI techniques used in solar thermal systems were provided. Subsequently, the application of AI in solar thermal systems was discussed. The advantages of the optimization process of the solar thermal systems were identified, supported by case studies from the real world. Then we identified the limitations and constraints that hinder the integration of AI into the solar thermal system. Finally, the economic benefits of using AI for the optimization of solar thermal systems were explained.</jats:p>

Optimizing Sustainable Energy Engineering With AI and Machine Learning
92ef05c8e2ba0949c3bf8f69974d39c51dc39e56.abstract: This chapter analyses the strategic incorporation of artificial intelligence technology into renewable energy systems to enhance energy security, operational efficiency, and long-term sustainability. This chapter aims to examine how intelligent energy management systems, machine learning algorithms, smart grids, decentralized microgrids, and Internet of Things (IoT) networks can enhance the performance and resilience of renewable energy systems. This chapter places emphasis on predictive analytics, battery management, solar forecasting, digital twins, and autonomous energy optimization. The chapter examines the economic, environmental, and technological ramifications of intelligent energy systems, emphasizing their capacity to minimize energy losses, improve system reliability, facilitate decentralized electrification, and expedite sustainable energy transitions towards enhanced national energy independence.

title: Machine Learning for Solar Thermal Energy Optimization and Smart Control
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Optimizing Sustainable Energy Engineering With AI and Machine Learning
974378bf655d4595a7410253b21e0ad381c1a368.abstract: This chapter presents a systematic examination of how Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning techniques are transforming the design, operation, diagnosis, and control of solar thermal energy systems, including flat-plate collectors, evacuated tube collectors, and concentrating solar power plants. Principal ML methodologies surveyed include Artificial Neural Networks, Support Vector Regression, Gradient Boosting, Long Short-Term Memory networks, Transformer architectures, Physics-Informed Neural Networks, and Deep Reinforcement Learning. Applications are reviewed across four domains data-driven surrogate models for thermal performance prediction, ML-based irradiance and thermal output forecasting, intelligent fault detection and predictive maintenance frameworks, and AI-driven control strategies shown to improve annual useful heat delivery by 8 to 15 percent. Research challenges including data scarcity, model interpretability, and cross-site generalization are identified, with future directions proposed in federated learning, physics-informed architectures, and explainable AI.

title: Energy Audits in Tanzanian Industrial SMEs for Methods, Barriers, and M&V-Linked Savings Prioritization
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics

a35056ead95e6546af494efa6e34c4e7ce0284ba.abstract: This chapter develops a conceptual and methodological framework for artificial-intelligence- and machine-learning-enabled energy audits in Tanzanian industrial small and medium-sized enterprises. Industrial SMEs often face energy-efficiency barriers related to limited capital, weak information systems, incomplete metering, and constrained managerial capacity. The chapter positions the energy audit as the organizing mechanism for sustainable energy engineering and shows how AI/ML can strengthen load profiling, benchmarking, anomaly detection, forecasting, measure prioritization, and measurement and verification. Drawing on peer-reviewed evidence from SME audit programs, ISO 50001 research, African industrial energy studies, and applied AI/ML energy literature, the chapter proposes a staged implementation roadmap for Tanzanian SMEs. The contribution is a practical pathway for moving from one-off audits toward data-informed, explainable, and financially grounded energy management.

title: Biogas Production Optimisation

2488e9ed487b4765c71f38c4edb94b5b6290f2ae.abstract: Anaerobic co-digestion is an effective approach for biogas production, but optimizing operating parameters remains challenging due to the interaction of multiple variables. This study integrates ultrasonic pretreatment with Response Surface Methodology (RSM) to enhance biogas yield from a mixture of dormitory food waste and pet animal dung. Batch digesters were operated at 37 °C, and daily biogas production was monitored. RSM evaluated the combined effects of ultrasonic temperature (25–65 °C), power (500–1,500 W), and treatment time (35–75 min). Biogas yield ranged from 35% to nearly 68%, with optimum conditions of 53.35 °C, 1,490.83 W, and 57.15 min, producing a predicted yield of 66.47%. The quadratic model showed excellent predictive performance (R2 = 0.9707; F = 110.33), confirming the importance of simultaneous optimization. The integrated ultrasonic–RSM approach provides a reliable and efficient strategy for maximizing biogas production in anaerobic co-digestion systems.

title: Application of Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning Methods to Optimize Energy System Stability
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Optimizing Sustainable Energy Engineering With AI and Machine Learning
af88092a3405a3484f3caf6617dee2099625164e.abstract: This article presents a systematic analysis of artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) methods applied to the optimization of energy system stability. Deep learning architectures for forecasting electricity demand and renewable energy generation, reinforcement learning algorithms for microgrid control, the concept of digital twins, and explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) methods are examined. The application of hybrid models reduces forecasting errors by 20–35% over ultra-short-term forecasting horizons ranging from several minutes to several hours. The transition to probabilistic forecasting reduces balancing costs by 8–15%, while the use of digital twins decreases operating costs by 15–25%. Current challenges limiting the implementation of intelligent technologies in the energy sector are identified, and priority areas for further research are outlined. The results are systematized in comparative tables suitable for practical use when selecting appropriate methodological tools.

title: Forecasting Electrical Load and Renewable Energy Generation Using Machine Learning Methods

b326566af7bfa615ecca304269db8b978877aabc.abstract: This chapter per the authors examines machine learning for forecasting electrical load and renewable generation under energy transition and grid digitalization. The purpose is to show why power systems need models handling nonlinear, non-stationary, and heterogeneous data. The chapter reviews LSTM, BiLSTM, GRU, CNN, TCN, hybrid architectures, ensembles, SVR, and GPR. Solar and wind forecasting depend on weather uncertainty, spatial relationships, and telemetry quality. The chapter compares facility types with forecasting methods and discusses digital twins, adaptive forecasting, and closed-loop control. Key problems: data drift, limited transferability, interpretability, computational complexity, and SCADA cybersecurity. Development requires integrating forecasting with digital twins, XAI, reinforcement learning, anomaly detection, and cybersecurity. Machine learning becomes a foundation for proactive and resilient power system management.

title: Integrating Transformer Neural Processes and Deep Kernel Learning for High-Throughput Screening and Uncertainty Quantification for Water-Splitting Electrocatalysts Across Perovskites and Metal Alloys
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Optimizing Sustainable Energy Engineering With AI and Machine Learning
bcafa941c82b95b48c33f91be24df91543e346ce.abstract: Years of experimentation have failed to enable the prediction of an efficient electrocatalyst from either a perovskite or an alloy without weeks of experimentation. There are more than a million perovskites, more exponential number of alloys but fewer than 0.1% of them have been studied. The traditional approach has failed. Density Functional Theory is impractical because of costs. Gaussian Process Regression struggles with scalability and lacks transfer between families. Its uncertainty calibration is off by miles. More importantly, the literature is not homogenous. Any framework that ignores that problem learns procedures, not physics. We gather Transformer Neural Processes (meta-learning across families) with Deep Kernel Learning (statistical uncertainty). This neural architecture can scale and model overpotential, stability, and activity with correlated uncertainties. Standardization of overpotential is done through Tafel correction. Prediction errors in the range of 50 millivolts and two- to three-fold reduction of experiments through Bayesian Optimization are our goals.

title: Integrasi AI dalam Kurikulum Akuntansi Pendidikan Pesantren: Tinjauan Literatur Sistematis tentang Kesiapan Teknologi, Pemahaman AI, dan Karakteristik Siswa
container-title: Business and Accounting Education Journal
9db92d2d3af48ff40caacdc975fdcbe142bb7929.abstract: Perkembangan Artificial Intelligence (AI) telah mendorong transformasi pendidikan akuntansi dan menuntut penyesuaian kurikulum agar sesuai dengan kebutuhan dunia kerja digital. Namun, adopsi AI dalam kurikulum akuntansi masih dipengaruhi oleh berbagai faktor, khususnya pada konteks pendidikan pesantren yang memiliki karakteristik unik. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis pengaruh kesiapan teknologi, pemahaman AI, dan karakteristik siswa terhadap adopsi AI dalam kurikulum akuntansi serta mengidentifikasi faktor yang paling dominan. Penelitian menggunakan metode Systematic Literature Review (SLR) dengan pedoman PRISMA 2020. Data diperoleh dari 38 artikel ilmiah terindeks Scopus yang dipublikasikan pada periode 2015-2026 dan dianalisis menggunakan sintesis tematik. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa kesiapan teknologi merupakan faktor yang paling dominan dalam mendorong adopsi AI, diikuti oleh pemahaman AI dan karakteristik siswa. Ketiga faktor tersebut saling melengkapi dalam meningkatkan penerimaan dan pemanfaatan AI dalam pembelajaran akuntansi. Temuan ini berkontribusi pada pengembangan model adopsi teknologi pendidikan serta menjadi dasar pengembangan kurikulum akuntansi berbasis AI di lingkungan pesantren.

fdd79e12d4dc98c72a7ea30e9bb3a464401f1cbe.abstract: The study investigated the inheritance of important morphological traits, including plant height and the number of lateral branches, in simple and backcross F₁ sesame hybrids involving the local varieties “Onimdar”, “Qora Shahzoda”, “Tashkent-122”, and “Sadaf”. The experiments were conducted under field and laboratory conditions. The patterns of trait formation and the degree of heterosis in the hybrids were analyzed. The number of lateral branches ranged from 5.8 to 6.2 per plant in the local varieties, from 5.7 to 8.7 in simple F₁ hybrids, and from 5.6 to 9.2 in backcross hybrids. Positive heterosis for the number of lateral branches was observed in most of the simple hybrids. Positive inheritance of this trait was also recorded in several backcross combinations. Promising hybrid combinations with high values of plant height and the number of lateral branches were identified. The results indicate that the selected hybrid combinations can be used in sesame breeding to develop valuable initial breeding material with high productivity, stability, and adaptability to local environmental conditions.

5ceb721e66711f7ae20303275a9a4626549b0abb.abstract: The article presents the results of research aimed at identifying valuable initial breeding material for barley breeding on irrigated lands. The studies were conducted in 2023–2026 at the experimental field of the “Farboma selekt” scientific seed-growing farm located in Jomboy district of Samarkand region. A total of 200 barley collection accessions obtained from the international centers ICARDA and CIMMYT, as well as the Institute of Plant Science and the Gallaorol Research and Experimental Station of the Research Institute of Grain and Legume Crops, were studied. The accessions were evaluated for productive tillering, number and weight of grains per spike, 1000-grain weight, yield, earliness, and resistance to diseases, winter conditions and lodging. The study identified valuable barley accessions with high productivity and yield potential. In particular, the Mirzacho‘l, K-22845, K-19985, Temur and K-566244 accessions demonstrated high yield performance. The selected accessions are recommended as valuable initial breeding material for developing new high-yielding, early-maturing and environmentally stress-resistant barley varieties for irrigated lands.

5a3db10baab032456fbf63d4deeb470fcfec6be3.abstract: This article evaluates the seasonal growth dynamics of low-stem fodder mulberry plantations under the climatic conditions of Uzbekistan in 2025-2026 based on phenological and biometric indicators. The highest morphological and economically valuable traits were recorded during the summer period. The average shoot length was 136 cm in 2025 and 143.0 cm in 2026. title: Caesarean section wound management: shared care approaches for midwifery practice

2932392ca757952725c21baf7acb3b59b6a0c1f0.abstract: Caesarean section rates in England continue to rise, accounting for 45% of the 542 235 births recorded in 2024–25. Surgical site infection represents a common and significant complication that carries a substantial burden for women and health services. National guidance on postoperative wound management is inconsistent, and evidence suggests that midwives often feel underprepared to provide adequate wound care education at discharge. This article examines the prevalence and impact of caesarean section wound infection, explores key inconsistencies in current national guidelines and presents a shared care approach to support women in recognising early signs of infection and managing their wounds at home. Practical approaches are presented to support midwives providing shared care, alongside a call for greater standardisation of guidance and investment in midwifery wound care education.

title: Tau hadronic decay channel reconstruction with a Lorentz-covariant graph attention network
container-title: Physica Scripta
7d7360eebe4f1102dd8fb23bb166025e3ac64c60.abstract: Abstract The reconstruction of hadronic decay modes of the τ lepton is a key task in high-energy physics experiments, directly impacting precision measurements and new physics searches. Conventional reconstruction approaches rely on handcrafted features and rule-based algorithms, which face challenges in handling complex decay topologies and detector effects. In this work, we propose LCGA-Net, a physics-informed deep learning framework for τ decay channel classification and four-momentum reconstruction. The method represents decay products as particle graphs and employs a multi-head attention mechanism to capture inter-particle correlations. To ensure physical consistency, Lorentz-invariant constraints are explicitly incorporated into the model architecture. A dedicated single- τ dataset is constructed from the simulation data of the Circular Electron Positron Collider, covering six major hadronic decay modes. The proposed model achieves an accuracy of 89.2% on the validation set, matching or slightly exceeding baseline models. More importantly, full physics constraints substantially improve the physical plausibility of reconstructed four-momenta—particularly the energy–momentum relation—without degrading classification performance. These results demonstrate that integrating physics priors with attention-based deep learning on particle clouds provides an effective approach for τ decay reconstruction, with potential applications in future high-energy physics analyses.

36ede77f584724c16c6df8d872616165c6726651.abstract: This article investigates the effectiveness of biological fertilizers and resource-saving agrotechnologies for potato (Solanum tuberosum L.) cultivation under the natural, climatic, and soil conditions of the Republic of Karakalpakstan. Based on field experiments, the effects of biological fertilizers on potato plant growth and development, tuber formation, yield, and product quality were evaluated. The results showed that, compared with the control, the application of biofertilizers increased plant height by 8-12% and the number of stems by 10-15%, while the number of tubers per plant increased from 7-8 to 9-11 tubers. Yield increased from 22-24 t/ha to 27-32 t/ha, corresponding to an approximately 21-36% increase compared with the control. The starch content of the tubers was 1,5-2,5 percentage points higher than in the control. In addition, the application of biological fertilizers enhanced soil biological activity and improved the uptake of nutrients by plants. The findings demonstrate that integrating biological fertilizers with resource-saving agrotechnologies is a promising agroecological approach for improving the efficiency of potato production under the conditions of Karakalpakstan.

title: Efficacy of a Validated Yoga-Breath Linked Intervention (Y-BLISS) for smoking cessation: A Randomized Controlled Trial

f4fd28ecb4c683c253f96e44b8e5c3512a01eddb.abstract: Abstract Introduction Tobacco use disorder remains a global health concern, and safe complementary interventions are needed. We evaluated a validated Yoga-Breath Linked Intervention to Stop Smoking (Y-BLISS). Methods In this randomized controlled trial, 139 smokers meeting DSM-5 criteria for tobacco use disorder with moderate to severe nicotine dependence (Fagerström Test for Nicotine Dependence, FTND ≥4) were randomized to Y-BLISS (n = 70) or desktop exercise control (n = 69). Y-BLISS comprised a 12-minute yoga-breath protocol with single-session yoga philosophy-based psychotherapy, delivered online under live supervision 5 days/week for 8 weeks. Controls received attention-matched desktop exercise with health education. The primary outcome was cigarettes per day (CPD). Secondary outcomes included 7-day point-prevalence abstinence, FTND, Tobacco Craving Questionnaire Short Form (TCQ-SF), peak expiratory flow rate (PEFR), and exhaled carbon monoxide (eCO). Assessments occurred at baseline, 4 and 8 weeks; analysis was intention-to-treat with linear mixed-effects models. Results Baseline characteristics were broadly comparable, with slightly higher dependence and craving in Y-BLISS (mean age 38.7 ± 8.6 years; 95% male; FTND 5.2 ± 1.2). At 8 weeks, Group × Time effects (β, 95% CI) favored Y-BLISS for CPD, FTND, TCQ-SF and PEFR, all p &lt; 0.001, and eCO (p = .04). Seven-day point-prevalence abstinence was 25.7% versus 11.6% (odds ratio 2.64, 1.06 to 6.57; p = 0.037). Differences were already present at 4 weeks for CPD, FTND, TCQ-SF and PEFR. Conclusions These findings support Y-BLISS as a promising adjunct to standard cessation care and justify longer-term, multicenter effectiveness and implementation trials.

title: Empowering people through diet and lifestyle in type 2 diabetes management

d545936a93095e0b623ff0ee19f9a2fd10f368c7.abstract: Dietary change, physical activity, weight management and self-management education are fundamental components of type 2 diabetes care. Medicines remain essential for many people, but outcomes are strengthened when pharmacological treatment is combined with person-centred support that reflects the individual's priorities, circumstances and readiness to change. This article outlines practical, evidence-informed approaches that practice nurses can use to explain insulin resistance, develop carbohydrate awareness, promote physical activity, support weight management and use glucose data appropriately. It also considers the psychological, social, cultural and economic barriers that may affect self-management. A case study illustrates how exploring the person's life context before escalating treatment can identify modifiable factors and support shared decision making.

title: Implementation strategies for integration of evidence-based caries management approach in dental education: a scoping review
container-title: Caries Research
742b8ba1781e73c57ec54fd70039950550d931bc.abstract: Abstract Introduction: The adoption of Evidence-Based Caries Management (EBCM) approach, introduced over two decades ago, has been slow and inconsistent in dental education and practice. There is a need for enhancing the implementation of EBCM in dental educational settings. This scoping review aims to map and summarizing evidence on EBCM implementation strategies and implementation outcomes in undergraduate dental schools. Methods: A comprehensive search strategy was conducted using MEDLINE, Scopus, Embase, and ERIC databases along with gray literature, and hand searches. Studies looking at implementation strategies for the EBCM approach in dental education were included. Data were screened, selected, and extracted by two independent reviewers. Qualitative content analysis was performed. Findings were reported following PRISMA-ScR guidelines. Results: One webinar and 25 studies, published between 2007 and 2023 across dental faculties in America, Europe, and Asia were included in the scoping review. Seven studies focused on developing comprehensive cariology curricula tailored to specific contexts, corresponding to the exploration/preparation phase. In the implementation phase, caries detection was the most frequently reported component of EBCM (n=7), followed by caries risk assessment (n=3), caries risk assessment and management (n=4) or multiple components of EBCM (n=4). According to ERIC classification, 22 out of 73 implementation strategies grouped in seven clusters were identified. The most frequent ERIC strategies were “make training dynamic” and “promote adaptability”, and the most frequent ERIC strategies’ cluster was “train and educate stakeholders”. Among the most frequent implementation outcomes identified were “acceptability”, “appropriateness”, “fidelity” and “adoption”. Less frequent outcomes were “sustainability” and “implementation cost”. Only three evidence sources reported about the implementation of the whole EBCM approach withing all graduate years of the undergraduate dental education. Conclusion: Overall, the findings underscore the need for more comprehensive and coordinated approaches to effectively integrate EBCM into dental curricula. The EBCM approach in undergraduate dental education remains in its early implementation stages and characterised by inconsistent adoption, as many institutions focus on isolated components rather than the entire framework within all Cariology curriculum. More studies focusing on the implementation of the whole EBCM approach in dental education using implementation science methodology are needed.

47c83c8edddcf3f80554e658fd45b7249b6122ed.abstract: This paper presents the findings of a multi-year study evaluating the effects of convective drying temperatures and processing durations on the dried product yield of six promising fig cultivars — Uzbekskiy zheltiy, Krym 9, Krym 29, Krym 43, Karshinskiy cherniy, and Dalmatskiy, grown under the subtropical conditions of Surkhandarya region. The experimental data revealed that increasing both drying temperature and exposure duration led to a consistent and substantial reduction in fruit yield due to intensive moisture evaporation, ranging from 68.7–77.9% at 40°C after 20 hours down to 8.7–13.7% following profound dehydration at 60°C after 80 hours. Distinct cultivar-specific dehydration kinetics were observed, governed by pericarp thickness, tissue density, and initial dry matter content. Uzbekskiy zheltiy (average yield of 42.04%) and Dalmatskiy (39.17%) exhibited notable technological stability and uniform moisture release, whereas Krym 29 and Krym 43 demonstrated rapid desiccation, achieving target moisture levels 10–15 hours earlier than the other cultivars. While drying at 40–45°C required excessive processing times (>70–80 hours) accompanied by high energy expenditure, exposure to 60°C provoked rapid surface hardening (case-hardening) and sensory degradation.

title: When traditional culture meets digital games: pathways and boundary conditions linking cultural identity to purchase intention
container-title: Journal of Product & Brand Management
b737bf9f158dd7fe1115790c35d9a3290a8b2095.abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine how cultural identity is associated with purchase intention for paid digital games featuring local cultural elements. In the context of Black Myth: Wukong, it further investigates whether perceived value and immersive experience explain this relationship and whether price sensitivity conditions these associations. Design/methodology/approach Survey data from 1,167 mainland Chinese and international gamers were analysed using covariance-based structural equation modelling. Analysis of variance (ANOVA) and cross-sample model comparisons were used to examine group differences. Findings Cultural identity was positively associated with purchase intention, with significant indirect effects through perceived value and immersive experience. In the full sample, price sensitivity weakened the links between cultural identity and both mediators and their indirect effects. Mainland Chinese gamers showed higher cultural identity and perceived value, and stronger direct and indirect effects of cultural identity, than international gamers. The moderating effect of price sensitivity was not significant in the international subsample. Practical implications Managers can strengthen culturally grounded digital products by embedding culturally resonant narratives, symbols and aesthetics into product design, communicating their relevance to target consumers and adopting differentiated value-framing and pricing strategies for consumers with varying levels of price sensitivity. Originality/value This study applies cultural identity theory to paid digital game consumption by integrating perceived value and immersive experience as two distinct mechanisms linking cultural identity to purchase intention and examining price sensitivity as a boundary condition of these relationships.

58666eea94c350bdfa7261dba276440be363cb70.abstract: The work is devoted to the study of the legal regulation of public administration of tertiary education in branch systems using the example of the Russian Ministry of Internal Affairs. The researches conclude that the existing regulatory framework for state sectoral management in this area does not fully meet the goals of developing higher education in general and providing law enforcement personnel in particular. The article identifies the issues of legal regulation of the administrative-legal status of the Russian Ministry of Internal Affairs as a departmental governing body for higher education, and substantiates the expediency of expanding the ministry's competence in the field of higher education in law enforcement-related specialties to universities implementing these programs, regardless of departmental affiliation. The researchers have developed proposals to improve legislation in the field of education and regulatory legal acts defining the legal status of the Russian Ministry of Internal Affairs.

title: Self-attention-aided multi-layer CNN-LSTM for non-uniform 4-level differential amplitude modulation and detection with atmospheric turbulence for OWANs
container-title: Optics Express
1922c9e0cb34b13e5ea74df3c48f83317a5531ed.abstract: This paper proposes an environment-aware four-level non-uniform differential amplitude modulation and detection scheme assisted by self-attentive multi-layer CNN-LSTM (SA-CNN-LSTM) for optical wireless access networks (OWANs) under atmospheric turbulence, to mitigate severe distortions induced by atmospheric turbulence in optical wireless communication (OWC) systems. Relying on four-level non-uniform differential amplitude modulation (NUADM-4) and a self-attention-aided detection algorithm at the receiving terminal, the proposed scheme can effectively suppress both multiplicative turbulence fading and additive Gaussian noise simultaneously. Numerical results reveal that the proposed scheme achieves remarkable bit error rate (BER) improvements compared with conventional detection frameworks for NUADM-4, and it substantially outperforms the classical uniform four-level pulse amplitude modulation (PAM-4) across diverse turbulence strength regimes. Moreover, the tailored architecture integrating self-attention with multi-layer CNN-LSTM maintains high transmission efficiency, reduces the dimension of the fully-connected layer at the receiver to a certain extent, and accelerates the computation speed compared with the CNN-based algorithm. In comparison with conventional detection-aided algorithms such as vanilla CNN, LSTM, and MLP, the presented scheme delivers a universal BER performance gain. Furthermore, the machine-learning-aided design philosophy for different modulation systems offers a practical design paradigm and implementable solution for the engineering deployment of high-speed OWC systems serving OWANs operating in volatile atmospheric turbulence environments.

title: Social Justice in Education
Bridging or Widening the Gap? AI Policies and Social Justice in Education
container-title: Social Justice in Education
9e13e6e7f3a42906186f831be85e28f41f88c8fe.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is widely promoted as a means to improve educational quality, efficiency, and equity. However, when introduced into systems already shaped by inequality, AI risks reproducing rather than reducing social injustice. This chapter examines whether AI policies in education bridge or widen existing gaps, drawing on Nancy Fraser's framework of redistribution, recognition, and representation. Through a comparative analysis of supranational frameworks and national strategies in the United States, China, India, and Türkiye, the chapter identifies persistent tensions between innovation-driven agendas and justice-oriented goals. The findings suggest that equity is often framed in technocratic terms, while issues of power, participation, and accountability remain marginal. The chapter concludes by proposing a justice-centered policy evaluation framework that emphasizes democratic governance, cultural responsiveness, and the right to contest or refuse harmful AI systems.

title: Cultivating Pre-Service EFL Teachers' Social Justice
container-title: Social Justice in Education
a002f3a0d9d2e35aa4b5b72098861ea596ef4433.abstract: This autoethnographic study investigates the mystories of three English as Foreign Language (EFL) teacher educators' respective implementation of social justice-oriented procedures in their teacher education programs with a distributed leadership lens. Data for this study came from autoethnographic reflections and autoethnographic conversations. Together with these, we built our own mystories that capture our total experiences in our attempts to cultivate pre-service EFL teachers' social justice awareness and practices. Findings indicated that we acted based on a sense of distributed leadership and highlighted the importance of preparing teachers to navigate the emotional and social aspects of learning while promoting critical and socially aware pedagogies.

title: Factories of Sadness
container-title: Social Justice in Education
e81bdafb57e30a783e40155efcfda801bb30326f.abstract: Authoritarian leadership in South African higher education institutions (HEIs) has reshaped collegial academic spaces into compliance-driven environments, described here as factories of sadness. Line managers often exercise control through micromanagement, manipulation, and opaque decision-making, a governance regime conceptualised as darkocracy. These practices erode academic freedom, undermine morale, and replace collaboration with fear and conformity. Drawing on literature and autoethnographic insights, this chapter examines toxic leadership as a systemic outcome of neoliberal and managerial governance rather than isolated managerial failure. It highlights the emotional and professional consequences for faculty, including burnout, disengagement, and loss of academic identity, and calls for ethical, transparent, and participatory leadership models that restore academic autonomy, psychological safety, and democratic engagement.

title: Inequality and Discrimination in Education
container-title: Social Justice in Education
83e3576767390bf5240a404bb35dc18dbc4a13ec.abstract: The multifaceted dynamics of discrimination and inequality in education have attracted growing academic interest in recent years, leading to the development of an increasingly interdisciplinary and conceptually diverse research field. Despite this expanding body of literature, there is still a limited number of studies that systematically map the evolution, major trends, leading research networks, and intellectual structures of this field. The present study aims to map the position, intellectual structure, and direction of development trends in discussions of inequality and discrimination in education by conducting a comprehensive bibliometric analysis. To provide a comprehensive map of the research field focusing on inequality and discrimination in education between 2000 and 2025, academic publications indexed in international databases (Web of Science, Scopus, etc.) are analyzed in temporal, geographical, and thematic dimensions. This study provides a systematic perspective on the fundamental research orientations of this field, the themes that emerge, and the future trends.

title: Leading with Inclusion
container-title: Social Justice in Education
1a7cfbf684b92ec753491daad36e2097fb76e2a6.abstract: This chapter views neurodiversity as a social justice issue in English language education from the leadership perspective. Despite a growing emphasis on diversity, equity, and inclusion, neurodivergent learners continue to encounter institutional practices restricting their meaningful participation and access. Drawing on narrative accounts from four English language educators in K-12 and higher education contexts, the chapter explores how leadership practices shape inclusivity. The educators' reflections reveal tensions between institutional policies and teachers' efforts to support neurodivergent learners in the face of curriculum and assessment-related restrictions. These narratives highlight the importance of teachers' role as informal leaders and advocates. From a social justice lens, the chapter argues for an inclusive leadership beyond policy statements to foster flexible, collaborative, and dignity-affirming practices. It displays the pivotal role of neurodiversity in equitable educational leadership and underscores lived experiences for inclusive institutional change.

title: Mapping Inclusive Practices in English Language Teacher Education
container-title: Social Justice in Education
6033410d4a72f78561e790674716af4e46de64e6.abstract: Teachers are not only facilitators of learning but also agents of change, capable of shaping educational systems to become more equitable and responsive to learner diversity. Their preparation within teacher education programs is therefore critical in ensuring that inclusivity moves from being a stated value to a lived reality. This study examines how inclusive education is represented in an English Language Teacher Education Program (ELTEP) and ELT department's artifacts. Data were collected through systematic document analysis of the program framework, mission, vision and goal statements, and program competency framework of the department. Analysis revealed that inclusivity is acknowledged but unevenly embedded, primarily through a single compulsory course and several electives of limited reach. These findings suggest that while inclusivity has some fragmented curricular presence, there is a need for structural revisions to embed it as a systematic, ELT-specific competency.

title: Polycentric Leadership for Justice and Epistemic Inclusion as Institutional Design in Education
container-title: Social Justice in Education
c3bded076c6ad636a7bd0da039f3919e672fde7c.abstract: This chapter proposes a polycentric institutional design that turns equity into routine educational practice. It integrates reflexive coaching, affective leadership, arts-infused curriculum and governance, epistemic inclusion, emotional sustainability, and semiotic pluralism. A systems map links micro-level instruction, meso-level governance, and macro-level accountability to outcomes in access, fairness, belonging, and staff vitality. The framework combines improvement science, realist evaluation, arts-based inquiry, calibrated moderation, and mixed-method scorecards with clear thresholds, review cycles, reciprocal accountability, and retire-to-add rules. It offers a portable operating grammar that distributes authority with coherence, broadens legitimate forms of knowledge without weakening rigor, and supports equitable practices that can survive leadership transitions and adapt to changing institutional conditions.

title: Social Justice Leadership in Practice
container-title: Social Justice in Education
db419fbd1fb801d6c3234298fc7483a39d22530a.abstract: This chapter presents a practitioner-scholar playbook for institutionalizing equity in the management systems that shape higher education: staffing, budgeting, promotion and tenure, safety/care, and accountability. Using a Social Justice Leadership lens informed by cross-sector accountability practice, we translate equity commitments into governance-ready tools that administrators can implement and evaluate. We present workload-equity bylaws and crediting schemas, need-weighted budgeting and transparent trade-off protocols, promotion and tenure criteria that recognize community-engaged and public scholarship, a student-facing support protocol, employee-facing restorative supervision scripts and coordinated referral procedures, and an equity accountability dashboard with KPIs and a review cadence. The chapter clarifies how Social Justice Leadership shifts equity from aspiration to measurable practice while strengthening institutional performance.

title: Teacher Educators as Justice-Oriented Leaders in Multilingual Higher Education
container-title: Social Justice in Education
61825cf85bcbfa9cbc588fef55660f73c241628a.abstract: This chapter explores the enactment of social justice-oriented leadership within English Language Teacher Education (ELTE). Adopting a critical collaborative dialogic autoethnographic approach, the authors examine how leadership for justice manifests through pedagogical rather than administrative means. The text analyzes how teacher educators navigate institutional and linguistic exclusions, such as native-speakerism and cultural misrecognition, which persist beneath celebratory discourses of internationalization. Through reflexive dialogue, the study theorizes leadership as a relational, ethical, and political practice across micro, meso, and macro levels. Findings suggest that justice-oriented leadership is realized through micro-level decisions; such as reframing student contributions or interrupting exclusionary norms, which carry significant emotional labor. The chapter argues for a grounded understanding of leadership that prioritizes sustained ethical attentiveness and the refusal of quiet erasures in multilingual spaces.

title: Trauma Sensitive Schools Creating Conditions for Resilience and Post Traumatic Growth
container-title: Social Justice in Education
22aaa6edbf54398f5ded8815364ce37f57e94a73.abstract: This chapter examines how schools can integrate trauma-informed principles with support for resilience and posttraumatic growth while addressing structural inequities. It clarifies the distinctions among adversity, trauma-related responses, and clinical diagnoses, and considers their developmental, relational, and educational implications. Critical and intersectional perspectives inform an analysis of how school practices can reproduce harm or support safety, belonging, and participation. A multilevel framework identifies universal, targeted, intensive, and organizational responsibilities. A student scenario illustrates observation, support, qualified assessment when needed, and follow-up. The chapter argues that schools can support recovery and learning without diagnosing students, requiring trauma disclosure, or treating growth as a required outcome.

title: Women Leading Social Justice Movements in an Era of Backlash
container-title: Social Justice in Education
2f7e50667971a4eb2a67e60157b77209758b2513.abstract: This chapter examines how women leaders sustain moral integrity and transformative vision amid escalating backlash against social justice movements. Drawing from global empirical research across educational, healthcare, and community contexts, it advances a moral-ecological framework linking fortitude, resilience, and justice. The analysis integrates intersectional, feminist, and decolonial perspectives—highlighting Latina superintendents' pláticas, African Ubuntu leadership, Arab women's contextual resilience, and Appalachian educators' relational fortitude. Findings reveal that resilience is relational rather than individual, and rooted in networks of care, mentorship, and collective healing. The chapter proposes a five-pillar framework emphasizing moral clarity, relational infrastructure, institutional reciprocity, collective healing, and joyful sustainability. Implications extend to leadership education, policy, and organizational design, urging systems that reward empathy and reflection as strategic assets.

title: The impact of the demise of department stores on the geography of UK retailing
container-title: Property Management
03f928301f0ff786416b6651b79fad4b14373eaf.abstract: Purpose The article examines the impact of the closures of department stores on the geography of retailing in the United Kingdom and the supply of shops in different types of shopping centres. Design/methodology/approach A three-step process was adopted to address the task. First, a list of closed department stores was identified. Second, the analysis draws on the CoStar database that provides information on real estate transactions from property agents. For each of the closed stores information was collected on what had happened since the store ceased trading, so whether the unit had been relet, sub-divided, use changed or remained vacant or a combination of these. A third step was the supplementation of this information with searches of news outlets such as the BBC and local newspapers to provide more detail. Findings The findings from the empirical analysis show that large regional centres have coped reasonably well with the demise of department stores, as have retail parks and large out-of-town centres. Nevertheless, there have been some changes of use for these vacant stores, notably to residential and leisure in city centres. Offices have also offered an alternative use. The long-term decline of small centres over decades has been amplified by the closure of their department stores that were probably the largest store in the locality. A high percentage remain empty while others have been converted to other uses, so that a significant majority of former department stores have been lost to retailing in these localities. Given that these stores acted as core attractions to shoppers in these small towns who then also visited other retail businesses, there is an existential crisis of local retail function unfolding for small centres. Originality/value This is the first article that assesses the impact of the widespread closure of department stores on the retail hierarchy. While the research is based on the United Kingdom, the findings almost certainly have a resonance for other countries.

title: Integrated risk management framework for international civil engineering projects
container-title: Proceedings of the Institution of Civil Engineers - Management, Procurement and Law
23cfd10aee7cfbf019a3f36dfcb937ee06bea5f8.abstract: International civil engineering projects are exposed to political, financial, technical, environmental, and organisational risks that frequently interact and evolve throughout the project lifecycle. Existing risk-management approaches, including the Integrated Project Risk Assessment (IPRA) tool, fuzzy logic, structural equation modelling (SEM), and resilience engineering, are typically applied independently, limiting their ability to support integrated decision making. This study develops an integrated conceptual framework that combines these complementary approaches within a unified risk-management process. A structured literature review guided by PRISMA 2020 covered publications from January 2000 to March 2024, supplemented by a targeted literature update through August 2026. The review identified and synthesised studies addressing structured risk identification, uncertainty modelling, risk interdependencies, and resilience-based management. Within the evidence identified through these searches, no publication explicitly integrated IPRA, fuzzy logic, SEM, and resilience engineering within a single framework for international civil engineering projects. The proposed framework links structured risk identification, uncertainty-aware risk evaluation, interdependency analysis, and adaptive management through iterative information flows and feedback mechanisms. The framework provides a structured basis for supporting risk-informed decision making and establishes a foundation for future empirical validation and implementation in the management of complex international civil engineering projects.

title: Family bricolage in family-managed agribusinesses
container-title: Management Decision
bb39fc6b075a2b7080a68b49bce0fab6782e335c.abstract: Purpose This study explores bricolage in mature, multigenerational family-managed agribusinesses and develops family bricolage to explain how family managers reproduce, regulate or reject inherited ways of making do. Design/methodology/approach The study uses a qualitative, abductive design based on 42 interviews with 29 participants from 26 family-managed agribusinesses, and one with a farming support organisation, in England, analysed iteratively alongside secondary evidence. Findings Family bricolage is a family-embedded process in which accumulated stories, knowledge, experience and intergenerational relationships shape how family managers recognize, mobilize and recombine resources at hand. It comprises family symbolic resources, family resourcefulness and family tinkering. Senior members regulate successors' tinkering, and negative cases show that inherited bricolage may be rejected when it inhibits renewal or professionalization. Research limitations/implications The context-specific findings are not statistically generalizable. Future research should compare industries and resource conditions and develop and validate measures of the three dimensions. Practical implications Family managers can use narratives, tacit knowledge and existing resources to address constraints, but should reassess inherited practices when self-reliance discourages external expertise or tinkering consumes resources without producing dependable, scalable solutions. Succession offers a natural point for this reassessment. Social implications Family bricolage may support continuity and adaptation in resource-constrained rural settings while enabling successors to reconsider inherited practices that inhibit renewal. Originality/value The study challenges the view that firms outgrow bricolage by showing how it is reproduced, regulated or rejected across generations in mature family firms. Family bricolage is conceptualized as an enabling and constraining process rather than a uniformly beneficial resource.

Monty's Liquid Carbon applied at R1 alone or in combination with generic azoxystrobin + propiconazole (10.5 fl. oz.) reduced the incidence of Physoderma brown spot. The findings provide corn producers with valuable guidance for implementing humic acid, chitosan additives, and fungicide treatments and determining the most effective application timing for disease management.

title: ШЎРЛАНМАГАН ТУПРОҚЛАР ШАРОИТИДА КУЗГИ БУҒДОЙНИ СУҒОРИШ МУДДАТЛАРИНИ БЕЛГИЛАШДА БАРГ ҲУЖАЙРА ШИРАСИ КОНЦЕНТРАЦИЯСИ ВА ТУПРОҚ НАМЛИГИ ДИНАМИКАСИ
container-title: Agro ilm
0cba3c6a2b51e67e9600d4233ff865069da94d2c.abstract: The article evaluates the pre-irrigation soil moisture regimes (70-70-70, 75-75-75, and 80-80-80% of FC) and the dynamics of leaf cell sap concentration (CSC) in winter wheat grown on non-saline soils during 2020–2021. The results indicated that as pre-irrigation soil moisture increased, leaf CSC values proportionally decreased (13.82–16.31%), whereas toward the end of the growing season, values rose to 17.36–19.50% due to physiological tissue senescence. The study substantiates the high efficacy of using a refractometric method for rapid determination of irrigation timing based on CSC to enhance water-use efficiency.

title: EFFICIENCY OF SPRINKLER IRRIGATION FOR CARROT PRODUCTION ON TYPICAL GREY SOILS OF THE TASHKENT REGION
container-title: Agro ilm
5ef2906a01d9b6f753d2c05ea1e7a3e09a50f2cb.abstract: This study evaluated sprinkler irrigation for carrot production on typical grey soils in the Tashkent region of Uzbekistan. Field experiments with the “Mirzoyi kizil” variety compared furrow irrigation with sprinkler intensities of 0.3, 0.4, and 0.5 mm min⁻¹. The highest yield, 29.2 t ha⁻¹, was obtained at 0.4 mm min⁻¹, compared with 22.7 t ha⁻¹ under furrow irrigation.

title: СУҒОРИШ УСУЛЛАРИНИ ТАНЛАШ ВА РАЙОНЛАШТИРИШНИНГ ТАКОМИЛЛАШТИРИЛГАН УСУЛИ
container-title: Agro ilm
9222642ac419326a3aa55f7ef99a614d0d0ebbf1.abstract: The paper proposes an improved approach for selecting irrigation methods by jointly assessing relief, reclamation conditions, soil and hydrophysical properties, agroclimatic conditions, and water source and quality. The final suitability class is determined by the most limiting factor. Separating current and potential suitability and using GIS zoning makes it possible to select irrigation technologies that better match local conditions.

title: ТОМЧИЛАТИБ СУҒОРИШ УСУЛИГА МОСЛАБ ТУПРОҚҚА ИШЛОВ БЕРИШ
container-title: Agro ilm
60fa4f677d111404afcd1ba1fd923ae03a930562.abstract: This article presents analytical data on non-inversion tillage, schematic representations of the new technology and the sequence of its implementation, the technological parameters of the agrotechnical operation, and its main advantages.

title: SUGʻORILADIGAN BOʻZ - OʻTLOQI TUPROQLARNING AGROKIMYOVIY XOSSALARI VA SANOAT CHIQINDILARI TA’SIRIDA OGʻIR METALLAR BILAN IFLOSLANISHI
container-title: Agro ilm
de5c8f6b87e3fd2e38c05b7f6f98a1efc6421451.abstract: This article highlights the agrochemical properties of irrigated gray-earth meadow soils of Sharaf Rashidovsky district of the Jizzakh Free Economic Zone (JEZ), reserves of humus, total nitrogen, total phosphorus, and potassium. There is a high probability of heavy metal pollution in the region near industrial zones, free economic zones, and irrigation networks. Since these soils have a relatively humic layer, as well as a unique water-retaining structure, heavy metals can accumulate in the soil and negatively affect its agrochemical properties. Heavy metals adhere to soil colloids and retain their activity in the soil for a long time. In the soil under study, the lead content of Pb is 40-80 mg/kg (the norm is 32 mg/kg or more), cadmium CD is 0.5 - 2.0 mg/kg (the norm is 0.5 mg/kg or more), zinc Zn is 150-220 mg/kg (the norm is 100 mg/kg or more). This situation indicates an increase in the level of pollution combined with salinization and carbonate content of irrigated gray-earth meadow soils.

title: BUXORO VILOYATI SUG‘ORILADIGAN TAQIR-O‘TLOQI TUPROQLARIDA SHO‘RLANISH TIPI VA DARAJASINING FERMENTATIV FAOLLIKKA TA’SIRI

c13b158dd0b3726a33eb3a3c6957adc4ea16c576.abstract: This study investigated the effects of soil salinity, soil depth, and seasonal conditions on catalase and dehydrogenase activities in irrigated takyr-meadow soils. The research was conducted in non-saline, slightly saline, moderately saline, and strongly saline soil variants at depths of 0–25, 25–50, and 50–80 cm. Enzymatic activity was determined during spring, summer, and autumn, and seasonal dynamics were comparatively assessed.

title: BUXORO VILOYATI SUG‘ORILADIGAN TAQIR-O‘TLOQI TUPROQLARDA SHO‘RLANISH TIPI VA DARAJASIGA BOG‘LIQ HOLDA BAKTERIYALAR SONINING O‘ZGARISHI
