title: B Corp certification and investment-cash flow sensitivity: evidence from unlisted European firms
container-title: European Journal of Management and Business Economics
80cf03788fea7a4c3dc77b02778ebe23c87f4219.abstract: Purpose This study examines whether B Corp certified firms present lower investment-cash flow sensitivity than non-certified firms, and whether this differential varies with B Impact Assessment scores or firm size. Design/methodology/approach A fixed-effects panel data analysis is conducted on 2,945 unlisted firms from five European countries over 2014–2022, of which 407 were certified during the period. Control firms were matched by size, sector, and country. Findings Certified firms exhibit significantly lower investment-cash flow sensitivity than non-certified firms, a pattern consistent with lower information asymmetries and agency conflicts. No significant differences are detected between firms scoring above and below the country-year mean on the B Impact Assessment, and size-related differences in sensitivity are of a similar magnitude in both groups. This lower sensitivity is already observable before certification. Research limitations/implications Certification is not random, so the findings should be interpreted as associations consistent with the proposed mechanisms rather than as strictly causal effects. Practical implications B Corp status identifies firms whose investment depends less on internally generated funds, which is informative for investors and lenders that assess certified firms. Social implications The findings support policy efforts to promote social enterprise models as instruments of sustainable and inclusive economic development. Originality/value This is the first study to relate B Corp certification to investment-cash flow sensitivity, in a sample of unlisted European firms, separating certification status from performance within the process.

title: Demystifying generative AI adoption in higher education: an integrated GRAI–AKM framework
container-title: Journal of Knowledge Management
2d81d35ddbb0a163d25a04512796c4f2fe000a1d.abstract: Purpose Generative Artificial Intelligence (Gen AI) is rapidly transforming higher education, yet successful institutional adoption requires effective knowledge governance, organizational readiness and coordinated decision-making. Existing studies have predominantly relied on individual-level technology acceptance models, providing limited insight into organizational and knowledge management capabilities for sustainable implementation. Design/methodology/approach A qualitative research design was employed using open-ended written responses from 20 academic professionals recruited through Prolific. The qualitative responses were analyzed using thematic analysis, and the resulting themes were mapped onto the proposed graphs with results and actions interconnected (GRAI) and active knowledge models (AKM) framework (GRAI–AKM). Findings Six themes were identified: (1) professional training and AI literacy, (2) ethical governance and academic integrity, (3) structural capital flexibility and knowledge processes, (4) trust, transparency and relational capital, (5) platform maturity and technological infrastructure and (6) human–AI complementarity. Professional training and AI literacy emerged as the most-discussed themes. The findings suggest that Gen AI adoption depends on the interaction of human, structural, technological, and knowledge resources rather than technology acceptance alone. Research limitations/implications Although based on a qualitative sample and self-reported written responses, the study advances knowledge management research by integrating Intellectual Capital (IC) and the Knowledge-Based View (KBV) into a comprehensive framework. Practical implications The findings highlight the importance of AI literacy, ethical governance, organizational learning and human–AI collaboration for sustainable adoption of Gen AI in higher education. Originality/value The study provides qualitative empirical support for the GRAI–AKM framework, offering a multidimensional perspective on knowledge management for sustainable adoption of Gen AI.

title: Transthyretin Amyloid Cardiomyopathy: Contemporary Pharmacological Management
container-title: European Cardiology Review
5505d232b22ea8d722b83d8b4914f6fabbacae44.abstract: Transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy (ATTR-CM) is a progressive infiltrative cardiomyopathy increasingly recognised as a cause of heart failure. Advances in the understanding of its pathophysiology have enabled the development of targeted therapies, making ATTR-CM a paradigm of precision medicine in cardiology. Currently approved disease-modifying therapies, including two stabilisers (tafamidis and acoramidis) and one gene-silencing agent (vutrisiran), slow disease progression and reduce hospitalisations and mortality, particularly when initiated early. Because these therapies do not reverse established amyloid deposition, supportive management remains a critical component of care and presents distinct challenges. These include universal anticoagulation in AF, careful diuretic management, the benefits of sodium–glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors and mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists, and limited tolerance to other foundational heart failure therapies. On-going intensive research is expanding the therapeutic landscape, with several Phase III trials evaluating next-generation silencers, gene-editing strategies and amyloid-removal therapies. While these advances hold promise for disease reversal and prevention, important unresolved issues arise, including optimal treatment selection, monitoring strategies and economic sustainability.

title: Organizational AI orientation, AI self-efficacy and value co-creation: a human-AI collaboration perspective in healthcare
container-title: Journal of Health Organization and Management
6445e52cab7175f314892526d760c6e1d1251ed8.abstract: Purpose Artificial intelligence (AI) is vital to healthcare system transformation. Existing research mainly focuses on the macro-level technological empowerment of AI, yet insufficiently explores how healthcare organizations’ strategic commitment to AI translates into better medical service outcomes through individual psychological mechanisms. Design/methodology/approach From the perspective of human-AI collaboration, we utilize survey data collected from medical staff working in Chinese medical institutions to examine the mediating mechanisms and boundary conditions linking organizational AI orientation and AI value co-creation outcomes. Findings Drawing on social cognitive theory, the results reveal that healthcare organizations’ AI orientation is positively related to medical staff’s AI value co-creation outcomes, and AI self-efficacy mediates this relationship. Moreover, their creative self-efficacy positively moderates the relationship between AI self-efficacy and AI value co-creation. Originality/value This study clarifies the micro-level transmission paths between organizational AI orientation and medical staff’s value co-creation outcomes. It provides new insights for hospitals to enhance medical service quality and optimize human-AI collaboration during AI-driven healthcare organizational transformation.

title: Evolutionary dynamics of AI-driven enterprise digital transformation: a cybernetic perspective
container-title: Kybernetes
406b79671b63af881cd115f6a281bbe0560605cc.abstract: Purpose In the AI era, digital transformation has become essential for enterprises to adapt as complex systems to uncertain business environments. In this work, we aim to analyze the evolutionary dynamics of AI-driven enterprise digital transformation (EDT), focusing on its evolution and impact on enterprise performance from a system cybernetics perspective. Design/methodology/approach We employ evolutionary dynamics analysis grounded in game theory to model the EDT process, and perform an econometric and empirical analysis on a sample of Chinese A-share-listed enterprises from 2009 to 2023. The approach encompasses heterogeneity analysis, moderation effect models, such as testing enterprise environmental, social, and governance (ESG) factors and market concentration, and threshold effect analyses. Findings The evolutionary dynamics analysis finds that increasing the risk-averse benefits of traditional enterprises and reducing the additional benefit coefficient would hinder EDT. Increasing the investment of technology enterprises in internal resource restructuring accelerates the transformation process. Empirically, AI significantly contributes to EDT. ESG positively moderates the relationship between AI and EDT, while market concentration exerts a negative moderating effect. Furthermore, AI and EDT show an inverted U-shaped trend when R&D intensity exceeds a specific threshold, while a U-shaped trend is observed when enterprise performance exceeds a specific threshold. Originality/value In this work, we uncover the complex, non-linear cybernetic feedback loops, such as U-shaped and inverted U-shaped, and boundary conditions, such as ESG and market concentration for AI-driven EDT, offering systemic strategies for enterprises adapting to the digital ecosystem.

title: Neuro-symbolic AI for proactive risk forecasting: bridging large language models and dynamic Bayesian networks
container-title: Smart and Sustainable Built Environment
9a1bf248111e208571dfad68b70369f36fefa354.abstract: Purpose Periodic risk reports constitute a substantial repository of operational data for project management. Despite the inherent informational value, archived records remain largely unstructured and highly fragmented. This study proposes a fully local neuro-symbolic approach for dynamic risk forecasting by translating qualitative project narratives into a quantifiable predictive engine to support decision-making. Design/methodology/approach The proposed methodology adopts a mixed-methods architecture including four layers: (1) spatial morphology reconstruction using a Y-axis density clustering algorithm; (2) a hybrid pseudonymization filter; (3) a local large language model (LLM) with chain-of-thought reasoning; and (4) a symbolic causal engine powered by a dynamic Bayesian network (DBN) to quantify causal propagation into a dynamic risk index. Findings An empirical evaluation across 28 reporting cycles spanning a 33-month large-scale infrastructure project indicates that the symbolic layer provides a temporally coherent aggregation of the output of a zero-shot perception layer operating at a macro F1-score of 53.62%. By quantifying causal risk propagation, the DBN captured a 93.59% risk-saturation state, for which the retrieved evidence identifies chronic site-clearance bottlenecks. Notably, using an alert threshold selected by sensitivity analysis together with an analytic constraint on the posterior mass attributable to the critical state (talert = 70.0%), the model outputs Bayesian probabilities alongside LLM-extracted textual evidence, yielding an anticipation interval of 1.33 reporting cycles relative to the documented administrative response. Originality/value The neuro-symbolic framework bridges the gap between deep learning perception and causal inference in construction management. By coupling LLM-driven zero-shot ordinal extraction with DBN causal reasoning, the research establishes an auditable framework for risk documentation. The integrated framework transitions AI from an opaque prediction model into an accountable decision-support tool, providing stakeholders with transparent explainable AI diagnostics and supporting a shift from reactive mitigation to proactive, evidence-based risk prevention.

title: NO‘XATNI SUG‘ORISHNING ILDIZ TIZIMIDAGI TUGANAK BAKTERIYALARI SHAKLLANISHIGA TA’SIRI
container-title: Agro ilm
328c2811455766f15c52fe23724799c45e0d5bbc.abstract: The article investigates the effect of irrigation on the formation and accumulation of nodule bacteria in the root system of the chickpea varieties “Yulduz” and “Milyutin-6” under meadow sierozem soil conditions in the Samarkand region. Field experiments were conducted using non-irrigated control and irrigated treatments. In the irrigated treatment, three irrigations were applied during the growing season at rates of 700, 1200, and 1200 m³/ha, respectively. The results showed that irrigation had a positive effect on the formation and accumulation of nodule bacteria in the chickpea root system. In the “Yulduz” variety, the mass of nodules on the roots of 10 plants was 3.2 g in the non-irrigated treatment and 10.3 g in the irrigated treatment, while in the “Milyutin-6” variety, the corresponding values were 3.2 and 10.1 g. Irrigation maintained an optimal soil moisture level, contributing to better root system development and increased activity of nodule bacteria. It was also established that a soil temperature of approximately 18 °C is favorable for active nodule development.

title: JANUBIY CHEGARA HUDUDLARINING ATROF-MUHIT OBYEKTLARI VA OZIQ-OVQAT MAHSULOTLARI  TARKIBIDAGI PESTITSIDLAR QOLDIQ MIQDORINI GIGIYENIK TAHLILI
container-title: Agro ilm
8ccb89ea325892c326bce90450f85ae81d2fa37a.abstract: An analysis of samples from 18 types of food products collected in 2020, 2021, and 2022 showed that in 2020, out of 1,859 samples, pesticides were detected in 30 fruit and vegetable samples, with concentrations remaining within permissible limits. In 2021, out of 6,825 samples, pesticides were detected in 5,707 food samples; of these, 56 were fruits and vegetables (with 32—or 57.1%—being potatoes), and 9 (47.3%) were potatoes. In 2022, out of 3,226 samples, pesticides were detected in 18 (47.3%) fruit and vegetable samples, but concentrations did not exceed permissible limits.

title: IPAK QURTI ZOT, LINIYA VA DURAGAYLARIDA BIOLOGIK KO‘RSATKICHLAR HAMDA TUXUM QO‘YMALARINING MIKROSKOPIK TAHLILI
container-title: Agro ilm
905bc87a5e41fa59c09045e84504aa164095a6ca.abstract: The article presents a comprehensive scientific analysis of the viability dynamics and the proportion of defective cocoons across various silkworm breeds, lines, and their inter-family hybrid combinations. The study confirmed the complete absence (0%) of pathogens causing highly dangerous diseases—such as nosemosis and nuclear polyhedrosis—in all samples. Hybrids belonging to the Line 31 group, as well as certain reciprocal combinations (13x57, 30x46, 314x191, 165x74, 5x155), demonstrated an absolute result: 100% healthy silkworm egg batches. The data obtained constitute a valuable practical and theoretical resource for selecting highly resistant genotypes and establishing breeding stock in sericulture.

title: ОСАЖДЕНИЕ НЕОДНОРОДНЫХ ПО КРУПНОСТИ НАНОСОВ ПРИ ДЕЙСТВИИ ВЕТРОВЫХ ВОЛН
container-title: Agro ilm
c962443678f7a1c69c2acae52901d1b4024d9f8e.abstract: A mathematical model of the settling of non-uniform sediment particles in water under wind-wave action is considered. Using the momentum and continuity equations for the solid and liquid phases, relationships are obtained for the variation of particle concentration with depth and time. Accounting for wave action makes it possible to refine the sequential settling behavior of sediment fractions. The resulting relationships can be applied to hydraulic calculations of settling basins and reservoirs by jointly considering flow parameters, wind velocity, and wave characteristics.

title: ЗАРАРЛАНГАН ТУПРОҚДА Pb(II) ИОНЛАРИНИ МОДИФИКАЦИЯЛАНГАН БЕНТОНИТ–САПРОПЕЛ КОМПОЗИТЛАРИ БИЛАН ИММОБИЛИЗАЦИЯЛАШ
container-title: Agro ilm
e8e7fffabfcb5dc5b6a429ba8a7278312e06d35f.abstract: The paper reports the Pb immobilization efficiency of composites prepared from Navbahor bentonite and Tashkent sapropel by mechanical and thermal activation, in a soil spiked with 1500 mg/kg of lead. Two mobile Pb fractions were determined at seven B:S ratios, five doses and three incubation times; the results were compared with three commercial humic sorbents and the advantage of the thermally activated composite is shown quantitatively.

title: TЕХНОЛОГИЯ И МАШИНА ДЛЯ УЛУЧШЕНИЯ АРИДНЫХ ПАСТБИЩ
container-title: Agro ilm
0e7368076f7d3fd009a01fba87bf4951ef28822e.abstract: This article presents information on the development of an environmentally friendly and energy-saving technology for improving arid pastures, as well as the design of a machine for its implementation. Certain specific features of sowing seeds of desert forage plants, which were taken into account during the machine's development, are presented.

title: KARTOSHKA YETISHTIRISHDA URUG‘–TUPROQ–O‘SIMLIK MAJMUIGA ULTRABINAFSHA NURLANISH BILAN ISHLOV BERISHNING SAMARADORLIGI
container-title: Agro ilm
b836279870e98a6986e89e7d12b58dc4a5615095.abstract: The paper examines the effect of combined pre-sowing ultraviolet (UV) irradiation of soil and seed tubers on potato emergence. Five irradiation variants at 10–50 cm from the source (0.42–0.76 mJ/cm²) and an untreated control were tested on cv. Santa in three replications. On day 15 after planting, emergence in all UV variants exceeded the control (56.7 %), reaching 63.3–83.3 %. The best result was obtained at 30 cm and 0.56 mJ/cm² (83.3 %; +26.6 percentage points over control, p = 0.047). Treated plots showed little Colorado potato beetle infestation; the trial used no fertilizers or chemical protection.

title: MONITORING OF SOURCES OF INDUSTRIAL TECHNOGENIC HAZARDS IN THE SAMARKAND REGION, ASSESSMENT OF THEIR TERRITORIAL DISTRIBUTION AND IDENTIFICATION OF HAZARDOUS OBJECTS BASED ON GIS
container-title: Agro ilm
eca09e7672449a9e53a6a065f219da9165f3cb10.abstract: This study is devoted to monitoring the sources of industrial techno genic risks in the Samarkand region, assessing the features of their territorial distribution and identifying dangerous objects based on geographic information technology (GIS). As part of the research, information about industrial enterprises and facilities that pose a potential anthropogenic hazard in the region is being collected, systematized and entered into a geoformation database. A comprehensive analysis of the spatial location of sources of danger, their technical condition, the likelihood of accidents, population density, environmentally sensitive areas and other factors is carried out. GIS technologies are used to map man-made risk zones and identify objects with a high level of potential danger. The results obtained can be used to assess territorial risks, prevent emergencies, ensure environmental safety and improve the management of sources of anthropogenic hazards.

title: O‘ZBEKISTON RESPUBLIKASI IQTISODIYOTI VA AGRAR SEKTORINI KLASTERLI MODERNIZATSIYA QILISH
container-title: Agro ilm
a4389bf32c3ec182fb2c7e4083888340ece3ad94.abstract: This article analyzes the economic content, institutional dynamics, and efficiency of cluster modernization processes in the agrarian sector of the Republic of Uzbekistan. The purpose of the study is to theoretically and econometrically substantiate the impact of agro-clustering on agricultural productivity, export potential, and the value-added chain, as well as to develop an analytical tool adapted to the conditions of Uzbekistan — the Cluster Modernization Index (CMI). The methodological framework includes a comparative-analytical method, index evaluation, and panel data-based econometric modeling (OLS, Fixed Effects, Random Effects, and Dynamic Panel/System GMM where necessary).

title: Academic librarians' perceptions of new skills, competencies and professional development needs in the AI age
container-title: Library Hi Tech
3610c8c0f0d1c535e41c0b71849dce304d1c7a28.abstract: Purpose This study examined academic librarians' perceptions of new skills and competencies, use of AI tools and professional development needs. Design/methodology/approach An online survey was distributed via professional networks, and data were collected and analysed from 155 valid respondents across Australia, European countries and the USA. Findings The findings demonstrate that the highly ranked new skills needed by academic librarians included AI tools and output evaluation, application of data governance and management, AI literacy instruction and integration of AI into curricula. The new competencies consisted of ethical implementation and governance, critical analysis and evaluation of AI tools and AI literacy and conceptual understanding of AI. AI tools could be used to improve information service provisions through responsible and ethical information management and discovery. Key training and knowledge areas included critical evaluation of AI-generated content. Hands-on tutorials with case studies and in-person or hybrid workshops were the most suitable training formats. Practical implications The findings are helpful and practical for academic librarians to develop new skills and competencies and support professional development and curriculum renewal. Originality/value The new contribution of this study lies in the identification of important new skills and competencies that academic librarians need to utilise AI tools in a successful way, mitigate associated potential risks and adapt to changing professional roles.

title: Enabling large language models for automated compliance checking of BIM models in architectural engineering through semantic modelling and linking
container-title: Engineering, Construction and Architectural Management
023ddb456a70738b9f768099f73b92556e042ba2.abstract: Purpose This study examines how standardised Building Information Modelling (BIM) data modelling can support large language models (LLMs) in automated compliance checking of architectural project information requirements. The focus is the Level of Information Need (LOIN) for design deliverables. The study addresses the disconnect between LLM reasoning and standardised project information. Design/methodology/approach A constructive research approach is adopted to develop and evaluate an LLM-based compliance checking framework. BIM resources and LOIN-based requirements are transformed into semantic data through information modelling and linking. An Information Container for Linked Document Delivery (ICDD) organises project documents and semantic links. The Model Context Protocol (MCP) connects LLM interaction with graph querying, compliance checking and issue reporting services. The prototype uses data from a single architectural project. A controlled benchmark compares direct review, Graph Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) and MCP review. Findings Direct review based on raw Turtle snippets showed limited performance because compliance evidence was often interpreted conservatively. Graph RAG achieved higher checking performance through structured graph retrieval, while MCP review achieved the best overall result by combining LLM-based task interpretation with tool-mediated checking. Performance varied across rule types. Explicit-data and derived-value rules were checked more reliably than extended data-structure rules, which were sensitive to alternative relation patterns. Originality/value This study presents a prototype approach to BIM–LLM integration for compliance-oriented project information management. Project resources, information requirements and checking rules are organised through ICDD and semantic graph data. MCP-mediated interaction links requirement interpretation with executable checking services, evidence retrieval and issue reporting, enabling traceable compliance review in project delivery.

title: Understanding CRM–service quality relationships through a multi-theoretical contingency framework: evidence from emerging economy banking
container-title: International Journal of Quality & Reliability Management
a12fc012e60aa1a13cd3cfb8b0ae4b3f9fbc7fe2.abstract: Purpose Although Customer Relationship Management (CRM) is widely regarded as a strategic mechanism for enhancing service quality in retail banking, empirical findings remain inconsistent, particularly within emerging economy contexts. This conceptual paper addresses the persistent CRM–service quality paradox by arguing that the relationship between CRM and service quality is neither universally positive nor linear, but contingent upon customer-level relational conditions, specifically Customer Commitment. The study develops an integrated multi-theoretical framework explaining how distinct CRM dimensions differentially influence perceived service quality and proposes Customer Commitment as a critical moderating mechanism. Design/methodology/approach The paper synthesises insights from Expectancy Disconfirmation Theory, Customer Engagement Theory, and Commitment-Trust Theory within the IDIC (Identify, Differentiate, Interact, Customize) CRM architecture. Building on this integration, the study advances six theoretically grounded propositions linking CRM dimensions to service quality outcomes. To facilitate future empirical validation, a mixed-methods sequential research design is proposed, comprising qualitative interviews with Nigerian retail banking customers, a large-scale survey analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling (PLS-SEM), and a longitudinal panel design to establish temporal relationships. Findings The paper advances a contingency-based reconceptualization of CRM effectiveness by demonstrating that identical CRM practices may produce divergent service quality outcomes depending on customers' commitment levels. The framework further distinguishes between volitional customer engagement, which enhances service experiences, and forced customer involvement, which may undermine perceived service quality. In doing so, the study extends Commitment-Trust Theory by repositioning Customer Commitment from a relational outcome to a perceptual moderator shaping customers' interpretations of CRM practices. Research limitations/implications As a conceptual study, the framework requires empirical validation across diverse institutional and cultural settings. Nevertheless, the propositions are theoretically grounded, falsifiable, and intended to provide a robust foundation for future doctoral and scholarly investigations into CRM effectiveness in emerging markets. Practical implications The study suggests that retail banks in emerging economies should calibrate CRM strategies according to customer commitment profiles rather than applying uniform relationship-management practices. For low-commitment customers, trust-building and relational assurance should precede intensive engagement initiatives. Social implications This study has important social implications for how retail banks in emerging economies manage customer relationships in a more equitable and trust-sensitive manner. By highlighting Customer Commitment as a key moderating factor, it shows that customers experience CRM practices differently depending on their relational readiness and trust levels. This reduces the risk of over-engagement or perceived intrusion, which can negatively affect vulnerable or low-commitment customers. The framework encourages banks to adopt more inclusive, ethical, and customer-sensitive relationship strategies that build trust gradually. Ultimately, this supports stronger financial inclusion, improved customer dignity, and more balanced digital banking relationships in sub-Saharan Africa. Originality/value This paper contributes to CRM and service management scholarship in four important ways. First, it reconceptualizes Customer Commitment as a moderating rather than outcome variable. Second, it distinguishes customer engagement from customer involvement, highlighting the potentially detrimental consequences of excessive participation demands. Third, it advances a contingency perspective of CRM effectiveness by demonstrating that CRM practices may generate both positive and negative service quality outcomes. Finally, the study contextualizes CRM theory within sub-Saharan African banking environments, a significantly underexplored setting in the relationship marketing literature.

title: Beyond the laggard myth: time-series analysis of AI job market dynamics in construction
container-title: Smart and Sustainable Built Environment
4e1908c31127b7c180069c373440c5cd8dc5cf0e.abstract: Purpose This study presents one of the first time-series, cross-industry analyses of the artificial intelligence (AI) job market for the construction sector. It benchmarks construction against both digital and traditional industries to interrogate prevailing assumptions of linear diffusion and temporal catch-up in AI workforce adoption. Design/methodology/approach Drawing on 51 months of Lightcast job postings (January 2021–March 2025), with construction defined as ANZSIC Division E, the study employs an interpretable analytical toolkit comprising Seasonal-Trend decomposition using Loess decomposition (period = 12), month-of-year bootstrap tests on detrended series, cross-correlation analysis with bootstrap confidence bands, Newey–West trend estimation on sectoral share ratios and conservative one-step Exponential Smoothing State-Space (ETS) forecasts. All results are re-estimated excluding the partial final month (March 2025) as a sensitivity check. Findings Construction's AI hiring is very sparse, accounting for under 1% of AI postings and is more volatile than hiring in peer sectors, but it grew fastest: annual construction postings rose more than fourfold between 2021 and 2024, against increases of 13% and 9% in the digital and traditional sectors, whose postings peaked in 2022. Construction's share of AI postings relative to both comparators therefore rises (converges) rather than falls. No delayed-follower pattern is detected: no lag at which the comparator sectors lead construction is statistically reliable, and the short-run associations that are detected are weak, near-contemporaneous and sensitive to the sample end. Unlike the comparator sectors, construction shows no statistically significant within-year seasonality and short-horizon ETS forecasts do not improve on a seasonal-naïve benchmark. These findings are robust to the exclusion of the partial final month of data. Construction thus appears as a low-base, fast-growing entrant with its own hiring dynamics, not a “laggard” following digital-sector cycles with a delay. Practical implications The findings suggest that construction firms should prioritise internal capability building and domain-specific AI skills where external hiring is thin, support flexible, year-round upskilling, and design policy and vendor strategies tailored to the sector's operational realities rather than importing digital-sector playbooks. Originality/value This study provides among the first data-driven, time-series evidence that qualifies the dominant “late adopter” narrative in construction. It shows that construction's low level of AI hiring coexists with the fastest growth and a rising share, without a delayed-follower timing pattern, distinguishing a low starting point from a lagging trajectory and offering an empirically grounded alternative to technologically deterministic accounts of cross-industry AI adoption.

title: Kidney-Sparing Percutaneous Management of High-Grade Upper Tract Urothelial Carcinoma in a Functionally Solitary Kidney: A 24-Month Follow-Up
container-title: Journal of Education, Health and Sport
f490cb03275bbda55f30c8e65abb231caa09244e.abstract: Introduction: High-grade upper tract urothelial carcinoma (UTUC) is generally treated with radical nephroureterectomy. Kidney-sparing treatment may be considered in selected patients with imperative indications.Aim: To present the clinical course and 24-month outcome of percutaneous nephroscopic ablation of high-grade UTUC in a patient with a functionally solitary kidney and Lynch syndrome.Materials and Methods: We describe a case of high-grade non-invasive papillary UTUC in a woman in her late seventies who declined radical surgery because it would have resulted in permanent dialysis dependence. Following unsuccessful ureteroscopic management, percutaneous holmium:YAG laser ablation and adjuvant mitomycin C instillation were performed.Results and Discussion: The renal pelvic tumor was macroscopically ablated without major perioperative complications. During intensive surveillance with computed tomography urography, ureterorenoscopy, and selective urinary cytology, no recurrence or progression was detected over 24 months, and renal function remained stable.Conclusion: Percutaneous kidney-sparing treatment may be a feasible option in highly selected imperative cases of high-grade UTUC when radical surgery would result in dialysis dependence. This approach requires multidisciplinary decision-making, careful counseling, and strict long-term surveillance.

title: De-risking from China: how US firms reconfigure sourcing through decoupling, diversification and friendshoring across geopolitical disruptions
container-title: International Journal of Operations & Production Management
3bb0fa9586297a5003f51185d95155c391b6558b.abstract: Purpose We examine whether US firms use three location strategies—decoupling, diversification, and friendshoring—to de-risk their sourcing portfolios. We investigate how the use of these strategies varies across bilateral (2018 US–China trade war), systemic (COVID-19 pandemic) and alliance-based (Russia–Ukraine war) shocks. We also test whether firms operating in high-tech industries de-risk more aggressively. Design/methodology/approach Using Panjiva US seaborne import records, we build firm-year measures of the three strategies for 1,565 US firms over 2011–2024. We then estimate fixed-effects models that interact firm's pre-disruption China exposure with the three disruption periods and a high-tech indicator. Findings Highly China-exposed firms decouple during all three disruptions, with decoupling switching on sharply at the trade war. Diversification activates specifically at the COVID-19 pandemic. Friendshoring peaks during the COVID-19 pandemic and reverses once the war begins. Sourcing portfolios appear more diversified and politically aligned, but these gains vanish once the China sourcing share is excluded, revealing them as mechanical by-products of decoupling. High-tech firms generally do not de-risk more than their peers. Originality/value We move the study of de-risking from perception-based case evidence to large-scale observed sourcing behavior. We conceptualize decoupling, diversification, and friendshoring as three sourcing location strategies and match each to its most salient disruption type, laying the groundwork for a contingency theory of strategy–shock fit. We further show that portfolio-wide indices of diversification and political alignment may overstate genuine de-risking because they incorporate the effects of decoupling. Moreover, policymakers' ambitions to de-risk high-tech industries and promote friendshoring have generated only a limited corporate response.

title: Risk-taking orientation and entrepreneurial strategy as drivers of business performance: evidence from private childcare centres in Indonesia
container-title: Journal of Knowledge, Risk, and Sustainable Management
38d7216433616db1678c490d4dc9681255881292.abstract: Purpose Entrepreneurial orientation (EO) is a recognised driver of firm performance, yet findings remain inconsistent and the mechanisms linking entrepreneurial behaviour to performance are underexplored in socially sensitive service sectors. This study examines whether risk-taking orientation affects business performance in private childcare centres in Indonesia via entrepreneurial strategy as a mediator. Design/methodology/approach A quantitative survey of 338 owners and managers of registered private childcare centres was conducted via cluster sampling from a population of 2,775 centres. 315 valid responses (93.2%) were analysed using partial least squares–structural equation Modelling with 5,000-resample bootstrapping. Findings Risk-taking orientation is positively associated with business performance, although this direct effect is comparatively modest. Entrepreneurial strategy shows a substantially stronger association with performance and partially mediates the risk-taking–performance relationship, suggesting that formalised strategic action represents a crucial structural path through which risk-taking orientation is associated with performance gains. Together, the two constructs account for a large share of the variance in business performance, and the measurement model demonstrates adequate discriminant validity and predictive relevance. Originality/value This study extends strategic entrepreneurship theory to a regulated, trust-based service sector, highlighting that strategic formalisation appears to play a more prominent role than risk appetite alone in accounting for performance variations. It guides childcare entrepreneurs on balancing risk-taking with strategic structuring, and informs policymakers on strategic capability development in early childhood services.

title: Case-based learning for facilities management education in a developing country context: bridging theory, practice and local realities
container-title: Education Innovations: Systems and Future Learning
fb5703d2038e44f130f78f61c971fe0407142d5c.abstract: Purpose Although case-based learning (CBL) has gained considerable attention as an active learning strategy in higher education, empirical evidence regarding its effectiveness in facilities management (FM) education, particularly within developing-country contexts, remains limited. This study examines the students' perceptions of CBL in relation to knowledge application, soft skills, learning preferences, and employability among FM undergraduates at a state university in Sri Lanka. Design/methodology/approach A quantitative survey generated 268 responses, of which 221 complete responses were retained for analysis. Descriptive statistics and Friedman tests were used to examine students' perceptions, learning preferences and differences across academic levels, with effect-size measures used to assess practical significance. Findings Students generally perceived CBL as contributing positively to knowledge application, critical thinking, self-directed learning, teamwork, engagement, and professional preparedness. They also associated CBL with greater confidence in problem-solving, decision-making under uncertainty, and handling industry-related responsibilities. Collaborative and application-oriented approaches, particularly group discussions and action-based activities, were preferred over more complex methods such as role-play and integrated project-based tasks. Overall, these findings are consistent with the principles of Experiential Learning Theory and Work-Integrated Learning, suggesting that CBL may provide a useful means of connecting academic learning with authentic professional contexts. Originality/value The study extends existing case-based learning research by providing discipline-specific empirical evidence from Facilities Management education in Sri Lanka, a developing-country context that remains underrepresented in the CBL literature. By examining students across multiple academic levels and comparing their perceptions of different CBL activities, the study provides context-sensitive insights for the design of practice-oriented FM curricula.

title: Building capacity in institutional voids: carbon competency development among quantity surveyors in Nigeria’s weak institutional environment
container-title: Journal of Knowledge, Risk, and Sustainable Management
ec171ee8a56bf81a78423f25df67dae41923a344.abstract: Purpose This study assesses the training needs and competency strategies that quantity surveyors (QSs) perceive as important for enhancing embodied carbon estimation (ECE) in Nigeria’s weak institutional environment. It addresses gap in understanding how global sustainability norms may be taken up by a profession traditionally focused on cost management, in a setting where institutional pressures remain limited. Design/methodology/approach This organization-based study collected data from 132 quantity surveying firms (QSFs) in Lagos, Nigeria, using a structured questionnaire covering 21 training needs and competency strategies. The data were analysed using descriptive statistics and exploratory factor analysis (EFA) to rank the perceived importance of these items and to identify the underlying competency clusters. Findings The factor analysis identified two clusters of perceived training needs and competency strategies: (1) technical and operational capacity building comprising skills for lifecycle assessment and the use of carbon digital tools; and (2) knowledge infrastructure and strategic integration, comprising systemic support such as carbon databases and online resources and industry guidelines. All 21 competency strategies were rated as highly important, suggesting that respondents did not strongly differentiate among them and regarded all of them as priorities for improving ECE. Practical implications The findings offer insights for academia, policymakers and professional bodies in the Nigerian built environment. Suggested priorities include a local embodied carbon database, industry guidelines, collaborative knowledge-sharing platforms, continuing professional development accreditation for ECE and phased, scalable multi-stakeholder implementation roadmaps. As the findings are specific to Lagos, Nigeria, implications for other developing countries and weak institutional environments should be drawn with caution. Originality/value The study offers three contributions. First, by showing that respondents attach high importance to ECE competencies in a context where formal requirements for ECE are limited, it provides a basis for further examining whether institutional pressures are the only route to competency development. Second, it proposes distributed competency as a conceptual lens, suggesting that sustainable construction competence may be better understood as drawing on socio-technical systems rather than on individual skills and knowledge alone. Third, it provides a data-driven structured categorization of perceived priorities for ECE competency development among construction cost professionals in Nigeria’s weak institutional context.

title: When technologies transform: a consideration of open innovation's contributions to operations management
container-title: International Journal of Operations & Production Management
cc71c98e657b1d40d9cdf1d88adc968f8cd8ef56.abstract: Purpose This paper examines what an open innovation (OI) perspective contributes to operations and supply chain management when a technology transition reshapes an industry. Earlier operations management research implicitly defined OI as a small set of isolated practices. This paper recovers its fuller depth as bidirectional knowledge flows and a mindset anchored in the business model. Design/methodology/approach The study traces innovation in the global automotive industry across three phases, then develops illustrative case studies of four Chinese electric vehicle (EV) entrants, Kandi, BYD, Xiaomi and Chery, analyzed through outside-in flows, inside-out flows and business model innovation. The cases build on a structured review of Chinese-language academic and industry literature, corroborated against company reports, trade press and industry data. Findings Chinese EVs have attained industry leadership, yet no dominant EV innovation strategy has emerged. All four firms drew heavily, but differently, on external knowledge, much of it from consumer electronics and smartphones, outside the automotive supply chain and each treated the vehicle as a platform. BYD and Chery also pursued inside-out flows, BYD through divisionalization and an open vehicle architecture, Chery through technology exports and internal suppliers. The contribution runs both ways: OI extends operations management research from project-and dyad-level openness to firm-level strategy, while operations management research helps explain organizational configuration and governance in innovation. Research limitations/implications The findings rest on a single industry. Future work should test them in other transforming sectors: pharmaceuticals, financial services and defense. Originality/value The paper reframes OI for operations management scholarship and uses the Chinese EV phenomenon to show how it complements operations management when industry architectures are disrupted.

title: Gendered Barriers and Adaptive Strategies in Sustainable Ecosystem Management in Lupanda, Zimbabwe: A Feminist Political Ecology Analysis
container-title: Gender and Sustainability in the Global South
096febd6d6ba249f8dba51e7a3ec904e783b5461.abstract: Abstract This article examines the gendered barriers constraining rural women’s participation in sustainable ecosystem management (SEM) in Lupanda, Zimbabwe. It integrates Social Exclusion Theory (SET), Feminist Political Ecology (FPE), and intersectionality to explain how institutional arrangements, gendered ecological labour, and intersecting inequalities shape women’s access to resources and decision-making authority. The study draws on semi-structured interviews with 30 women, dialogues with 15 key informants, and documentary analysis. Interview and dialogue data were thematically analysed using NVivo, with documentary materials providing additional contextual evidence. The findings show that patriarchal governance, economic marginalisation, information exclusion, and time poverty reinforce one another, concentrating environmental responsibilities among women without corresponding governance authority. Women respond through cooperative networks, livelihood diversification, and the transmission of indigenous ecological knowledge, demonstrating substantial adaptive capacity that does not necessarily translate into institutional influence. Building on these findings, the article proposes the Gender-Ecosystem Governance Model (GEGM), comprising four interrelated pillars: empowerment and capacity building, institutional reform, economic inclusion and resource access, and knowledge integration and co-production. The study’s distinctive contribution is its demonstration that ecological responsibility does not necessarily translate into governance authority, together with a contextually grounded framework for addressing the relationship between ecological labour, resource access, and decision-making power. As a qualitative single-case study, it offers analytical insights rather than statistical generalisations; the proposed model requires further evaluation across different contexts.

title: The supply-side consequences of popularity signals: evidence from a natural experiment
container-title: Industrial Management & Data Systems
e81a551d6124056cb692be14bb057da8cfab3c80.abstract: Purpose This study investigates the supply-side consequences of disclosing popularity information on digital content platforms, focusing on how public disclosure of popularity metrics shapes creators’ production strategies along both the intensive margin (output volume) and extensive margin (thematic diversity). Design/methodology/approach We exploit a two-sided, platform-wide natural experiment on a major Chinese blogging platform that publicly displayed article view counts on December 7, 2020, and reversed the policy on February 5, 2021. Using a uniform random sample of 10,000 creators, we estimate the causal effect of disclosure with a DID-in-time design grounded in feedback intervention theory (FIT). We use the policy reversal as a reverse-shock test, conduct heterogeneity analyses by creator rank and niche density to examine FIT’s task-motivation and task-learning channels and construct a platform-level HHI to assess whether creator-level diversification is accompanied by aggregate topical concentration. Findings The public disclosure of popularity information significantly increases creators’ weekly output and thematic diversity. Notably, the increase in output volume is modest, whereas the expansion in thematic diversity is substantial, suggesting creators primarily respond by diversifying their content. These effects are robust across multiple empirical checks, including the reverse-shock analysis. Heterogeneity analyses reveal a cross-pattern consistent with FIT’s dual-channel architecture: the volume response is concentrated among low-rank creators (task-motivation channel), while the diversity response is concentrated among thin-niche creators (task-learning channel). Platform-level HHI shows no detectable increase during the disclosure period, indicating creator-level broadening does not translate into aggregate homogenization in our window. Originality/value This study uncovers a supply-side mechanism through which popularity signals influence creator behavior and extends FIT to the context of the creator economy. The findings demonstrate that popularity information functions as dual-purpose feedback by motivating higher output while guiding diversification, thus offering important implications for platform governance and the design of feedback systems.

title: Organizational ambidexterity and green performance in emerging markets: examining the role of environmental dynamism in sustainability-oriented performance management
container-title: International Journal of Productivity and Performance Management
d0143a3600420c6a8540894603ebdd3e7eb96135.abstract: Purpose This study examines how organizational ambidexterity influences green performance in emerging market firms and investigates the role of environmental dynamism as a contextual condition shaping this relationship. Responding to growing calls within productivity and performance management research for sustainability-oriented performance frameworks, the study explores how firms integrate exploratory innovation and exploitative efficiency to achieve environmental performance outcomes. Design/methodology/approach A quantitative cross-sectional survey design was employed using data collected from 249 firms operating in the Greater Kumasi Metropolitan Area of Ghana. Structural equation modeling using Analysis of Moment Structure was applied to test the direct effects of organizational ambidexterity and environmental dynamism on green performance, as well as the moderating influence of environmental dynamism. Findings The results show that organizational ambidexterity significantly enhances green performance, demonstrating that firms capable of balancing exploratory innovation with exploitative efficiency achieve superior environmental outcomes. Environmental dynamism also exhibits a strong positive direct effect on green performance. However, contrary to contingency expectations, environmental dynamism does not significantly moderate the relationship between ambidexterity and green performance, suggesting that internal strategic capabilities play a more decisive role than external turbulence in shaping sustainability performance in emerging market contexts. Research limitations/implications The study relies on cross-sectional and perceptual data from firms operating within a single emerging economy. Future research could adopt longitudinal designs, incorporate objective environmental performance indicators, and explore antecedents of organizational ambidexterity to deepen understanding of sustainability-driven performance management. Practical implications The findings highlight the importance for managers to develop ambidextrous capabilities that integrate innovation with operational efficiency. Firms seeking to improve sustainability outcomes should embed environmental initiatives within performance management systems while simultaneously encouraging experimentation and process optimization. Originality/value This study contributes to productivity and performance management literature by demonstrating that organizational ambidexterity functions as a critical capability for achieving green performance in emerging markets. By providing empirical evidence from sub-Saharan Africa and revealing that environmental dynamism acts as an independent driver rather than a boundary condition of sustainability performance, the study advances understanding of the sustainability–performance nexus in volatile institutional environments.

title: Understanding the effect of professional and social signals on physician performance on online health platforms
container-title: Industrial Management & Data Systems
a42db6a8f30b18ad7941ab39973000540c506b40.abstract: Purpose Drawing on signaling theory, this study investigates the interaction between professional signals (professional capital) and social signals (peer and patient recognition) in shaping physician performance on online health platforms (OHPs). Design/methodology/approach The research model is tested using panel data from a leading OHP. We employed the correlated random-effects model to test the research hypotheses. Findings Results confirm that professional capital, peer recognition and patient recognition each positively associate with physician performance. Both peer recognition and patient recognition, as online-generated social signals, substitute for professional capital, a signal generated and certified offline but displayed online. Crucially, the three-way interaction effect confirms that social signals jointly substitute for professional signal. Originality/value This study contributes to the online health platform and digital platform signaling literature by theorizing and empirically testing how institutionally generated professional signals interact with peer- and patient-generated social signals. Its primary contribution is the identification and testing of a joint substitution mechanism: peer and patient recognition together reduce the marginal value of professional capital. The study also highlights an alternative platform-supported career path, especially for junior physicians, and offers implications for platform governance, physician reputation management and equitable online health ecosystem design.

title: Combined imaging of myocardial scar and fat using AI-guided dual bright- and black-blood late gadolinium enhancement
container-title: European Heart Journal - Imaging Methods and Practice
ae0982a8e8e213a8cea9fa3564d8cc1d02f304ce.abstract: Abstract Aims Characterization of myocardial scar and fat is clinically important for diagnosis, risk stratification, and procedural planning in cardiomyopathies. While black-blood late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) improves scar conspicuity, fat remains hyperintense and may confound interpretation. We aimed to develop and evaluate SPOT-DIXON, a dual bright- and black-blood LGE sequence with Dixon water-fat separation and artificial intelligence (AI)-guided analysis, enabling simultaneous and co-registered quantification of myocardial scar and intra- and extra-cardiac fat. Methods SPOT-DIXON alternates bright- and black-blood LGE preparations on consecutive heartbeats while acquiring dual-echo data for Dixon water-fat separation. Simulations, phantom experiments, and validations in a prospective cohort of 36 patients referred for cardiac MRI were performed. An AI model automatically segmented the left ventricular (LV) wall on bright-blood water images, with contours propagation to scar and fat images. Results Simulations and phantoms confirmed preserved bright- and black-blood contrast and accurate water-fat separation. In patients, AI-based LV wall segmentation showed excellent agreement with manual delineation (global DICE=84.4 ± 4.0%). SPOT-DIXON yielded higher scar volume, burden, and transmurality measurements than reference sequences, while LV wall volume was similar between sequences. Novel quantitative metrics, including intramyocardial fat burden expressed relative to scar mass, were feasible only with SPOT-DIXON. Acquisition times were comparable across sequences (5min55s ± 2min17 s), while AI-based analysis substantially reduced post-processing time to 2.1 ± 0.7 seconds. Conclusion AI-guided SPOT-DIXON enables simultaneous, co-registered assessment of myocardial scar and fat within a single LGE acquisition. This approach overcomes key limitations of current workflows and introduces novel quantitative markers of fibrofatty remodelling with potential clinical relevance in cardiomyopathies.

title: Optimal Interest Rates and Repayment Penalties under Strategic Delay in Microfinance Lending
container-title: IMA Journal of Management Mathematics
d7dfc994bf3a27450dcfe9251a30373eae940ae2.abstract: Abstract Strategic repayment delay is a major concern for microfinance institutions because it affects loan recovery and financial sustainability. This paper develops a discrete-time Markov chain model of individual repayment dynamics using data from a Ghanaian microfinance institution (MFI) to examine how interest rates and late-repayment penalties affect borrower incentives and lender sustainability. Borrowers transition among applicant, beneficiary, delay, permanent exclusion, and reapplication states. We derive expected discounted wealth across these states and formulate a constrained optimization problem that maximizes borrower wealth subject to MFI sustainability and an incentive-compatibility condition that prevents strategic delay. The model yields explicit expressions for the optimal interest rate and penalty and establishes a feasibility condition linking timely repayment probability, borrower revenue, and lending cost. Results show that, without penalties, delaying repayment can generate greater expected wealth than timely repayment, while higher interest rates further weaken repayment incentives. A feasible interest-rate–penalty combination exists only when timely repayment exceeds 52.5%, given borrower revenue equal to twice the capital lent and a lending cost of 5% of the amount lent. As this probability increases from $55\%$ to $85\%$, the optimal interest rate falls from $90.91\%$ to $23.53\%$, while the optimal penalty is non-monotonic. Using the data-based permanent-exclusion rate of $\alpha _{2}=0.3020$, the observed repayment rate of $46.08\%$ falls below the feasibility threshold, making individual lending infeasible under the present assumptions.

title: Supplier-Led or Retailer-Led Supply Chains: Emergency Supplies Pre-positioning under Option Contracts and Corporate Social Responsibility
container-title: IMA Journal of Management Mathematics
ad0a99429e6d56a3838f1994bed4368fe65acf33.abstract: Abstract Effective emergency supplies pre-positioning is critical for mitigating disaster losses, but government-managed reserves face persistent shortages and waste. Public-private collaboration offers a practical solution, yet its sustainability is constrained by firms’ trade-offs between commercial operations and emergency obligations, and the role of corporate social responsibility (CSR) in driving participation remains underexplored. This study evaluates two public-private emergency collaboration modes with supplier-led and retailer-led supply chains respectively, and identifies their applicable conditions. Unlike existing bilateral government-firm research, it innovatively integrates vertical supply chain competition and heterogeneous CSR signaling into a unified framework. We construct a three-stage Stackelberg game model under option contracts, derive equilibria via rigorous backward induction, and complement theory with numerical analysis. Four key findings emerge. First, rising consumer CSR sensitivity consistently boosts overall supply chain profits but raises emergency reserves in supplier-led modes and reduces them in retailer-led modes. This stems from distinct CSR signal transmission paths across the two structures. Second, option contracts do not always ensure effective collaboration, with two distinct incentive failure types across the modes: supplier underproduction and government zero procurement respectively. Third, the two modes yield identical government procurement cost and total reserve capacity, so cost minimization alone cannot reliably guide mode selection. Fourth, the supplier-led mode outperforms under low disaster risk, production cost and CSR sensitivity, while the reverse holds otherwise. These findings offer scenario-based guidance for policymakers to select partners, design incentive-compatible contracts, and leverage CSR as a lever to build sustainable public-private emergency reserve systems.

title: Water footprint of large AI models: risks to global water security and sustainable optimization strategies
container-title: Water Policy
71384b0b7ce71aeb82049c155da192ce552f67b9.abstract: ABSTRACT Diagram linking AI model training and inference to lifecycle water use, estimated at 4.2–6.6 billion m³ annually by 2027, and showing water reuse, efficient cooling, smarter workloads, and standardized reporting as strategies to protect global water security. The rapid proliferation of large-scale artificial intelligence (AI) models has introduced a significant yet underexamined environmental challenge: freshwater consumption. This narrative review synthesizes scientific literature, industry sustainability reports, and case studies to quantify the water footprint of AI systems across their full lifecycle, from semiconductor fabrication and data center operations to electricity generation and supply chains. Direct water use occurs primarily through evaporative and liquid cooling in data centers, where a single large facility can consume 11,000–19,000m3/day. Indirect water use is embedded in electricity generation and chip manufacturing, with advanced fabrication plants drawing 10,000–37,000m3/day. Major technology companies, including Google, Microsoft, and Meta, collectively consume billions of cubic meters in 2022–2024, with consumption rising alongside accelerating AI deployment. Critically, over 52% of the world's top 100 data centers are projected to be located in high water stress regions by 2030, where AI infrastructure increasingly competes with agricultural, municipal, and ecological needs. Sustainable alternatives, including immersion cooling, nonpotable water reuse, and AI-driven workload optimization, offer measurable reductions but remain inconsistently adopted. The direct and indirect water footprints of AI models during their entire lifecycle are reviewed. Two of the main direct water usage sources are semiconductor manufacturing and data center cooling. Clip manufacturing and electricity generation significantly increase the indirect water footprint of AI. In areas with scarce freshwater supplies, the growth of AI technology may worsen water stress. Standardized reporting frameworks and lifecycle-based water accounting are urgently needed to safeguard global water security.

title: Ownership structure and the exploration–exploitation tradeoff: evidence from Chinese advanced manufacturing firms
container-title: Baltic Journal of Management
9fafaafcf064b19bcb04108970fdbb8555b42c10.abstract: Purpose Although the ambidexterity literature emphasizes the importance of balancing exploration and exploitation, less is known about whether the innovation–performance implications of relative exploration vary across corporate governance conditions. This study examines whether executive and institutional shareholding are associated with differences in the estimated exploration–exploitation turning point. Design/methodology/approach Using an unbalanced panel of 254 Chinese advanced manufacturing firms from 2010 to 2020, this study estimates two-way fixed-effects models of the relationship between relative exploration (RE) and innovation performance. The sample firms are identified from companies included in the SSE Made in China (2025) Index and the CSI Made in China (2025) Index during 2015–2020. We further examine whether executive shareholding and two types of institutional shareholding – pressure-sensitive and pressure-resistant – are associated with the location of the estimated conditional turning point. Findings RE is associated with innovation performance in an inverted U-shaped pattern. Higher executive shareholding is associated with a more exploration-oriented estimated conditional turning point, whereas higher pressure-resistant institutional shareholding is associated with a more exploitation-oriented turning point. By contrast, the interaction between RE and pressure-sensitive institutional shareholding is statistically insignificant and is treated as inconclusive rather than as evidence of an absent or substantively negligible moderating association. All estimates represent conditional associations and should not be interpreted as causal effects. Originality/value Building on the established inverted U-shaped association between RE and innovation performance, this study offers an empirical extension of ambidexterity research by showing that the estimated conditional turning point varies across ownership arrangements. It identifies heterogeneous ownership structures as boundary conditions of the established RE–innovation performance relationship.

title: University students' disciplinary perspectives on generative AI after two years of its widespread use
container-title: Journal of Applied Research in Higher Education
e5ed294fd6697fa9565e5119f14a79e5ae870103.abstract: Purpose This study explores how university students use generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) across various disciplines, including STEM, Business, Education Futures, Clinical & Health Sciences (CHS), Creative and Allied Health & Human Performance (AHHP). It aims to identify discipline-based perspectives, perceived benefits, ethical boundaries and the support needs required for responsible use of GenAI tools. Design/methodology/approach A survey was conducted approximately two years after the widespread use of GenAI, by which time participants were expected to be familiar with its use. Students were categorised based on their discipline, English fluency, mode of learning and level of study. Their responses were analysed to compare usage patterns, satisfaction levels and ethical considerations across disciplines. Findings The results highlight that student perspectives on GenAI tools are discipline-dependent. STEM and Education Futures showed the highest acceptance, while CHS and Business students were more cautious and sceptical about accuracy and ethical issues. Non-native English speakers rated GenAI tools more favourably as aids for writing and comprehension. Novice users expressed enthusiasm, while expert users showed dissatisfaction due to errors and false information. Research limitations/implications The study relied on self-reported perceptions and represents a single institutional context. Broader investigations are recommended, with a particular focus on equity groups such as students with disabilities, low-SES students and remote learners. Practical implications Different approaches were suggested for integrating GenAI into learning. STEM students favoured comparative tasks; CHS recommended support for diagnostic reasoning; Allied Health preferred role-playing simulations; Education Futures highlighted lesson planning; and Business students suggested case-based and productivity uses. Originality/value The study provides cross-disciplinary analyses of GenAI use by students and proposes approaches for ethical and discipline-specific integration into university curricula.

title: Teacher Monitoring Strategies for AI-Aided Student Writing Outputs Toward Policy Guidelines
container-title: GEO Academic Journal
c2aefe7750439a7c6d21abaa77f9bc7919a3e53b.abstract: This study examined the extent to which senior high school teachers monitor AI-generated written outputs, focusing on the use of AI detectors, manual review, and cross-checking results. The study respondents were teachers from the Humanities and Social Sciences (HUMSS) strand of Philippine Christian University-Dasmariñas. The researchers collected data through a structured questionnaire and analyzed it using descriptive statistics, including mean and standard deviation. Results showed that teachers used AI detectors and cross-checking to a moderate extent, while they used manual review to a high extent and found it significant. Teachers faced challenges such as limitations in AI detection tools and time constraints in manual evaluation and cross-checking. These findings highlight the importance of a layered monitoring approach, where teacher judgment remains central, and AI tools serve as supplementary aids. The study provides evidence for developing clear guidelines and practices that balance ethical assessment, professional discretion, and responsible integration of AI in student writing evaluation. Keywords: Artificial intelligence, AI-generated text, teacher monitoring strategies, manual review, cross-checking

title: AI-Based Customer Service and Brand Loyalty in Saudi Retail: An Empirical Investigation of the Service Quality–Emotional Attachment–Loyalty Pathway in 2025–2026
container-title: Revista Cultura Científica
7447b8bdae9fbb1f476fe7e2a877364778cb869e.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI)-powered customer service systems have expanded across Saudi Arabia’s retail sector during 2025–2026, with major retailers increasingly exploring chatbots, recommendation engines, and automated service technologies. Official Saudi digital-economy statistics document the wider shift towards digital commerce, although online-shopping participation should not be interpreted as a direct measure of AI adoption or retailer-specific investment. This study examines the relationship among AI service quality, emotional brand attachment, and brand loyalty using survey results reported for 512 retail customers in Riyadh, Jeddah, and Dammam, collected between May and September 2026. Using partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM) and bootstrap resampling, the analysis reports a positive direct association between AI service quality and loyalty (β = 0.421, p < 0.001), together with a positive indirect association through emotional brand attachment (reported indirect effect = 0.238, 95% CI [0.187, 0.289]). The study considers a possible “mechanical efficiency paradox”: functional improvements in AI service may be more strongly associated with loyalty than with emotional attachment. Importantly, this survey does not include a direct comparison with human-delivered service, and the reported positive attachment coefficient (β = 0.187) cannot establish that AI decreases attachment. The reported gender subgroup estimates differ: the AI quality–attachment association is positive for male respondents (β = 0.289, p = 0.001) and statistically nonsignificant for female respondents (β = −0.023, p = 0.811). Age-specific estimates also vary, with more positive reported coefficients in younger groups, although the statistical significance of the age differences requires further supporting output. The manuscript reports that the model accounts for 51.2% of the variance in loyalty (R2 = 0.512) and has positive predictive relevance (Q2 = 0.289). Because some path estimates, correlations, and variance-explained values are not mutually consistent, these results require rechecking against the original SmartPLS output before publication. Managerial implications include offering hybrid AI–human service, allowing customers to choose their preferred channel, and maintaining personal attention for complex or emotionally sensitive interactions. The findings provide a framework for assessing how technological service quality and relationship-building might jointly contribute to brand loyalty.

title: UAV multispectral imagery for assessing tree health in tart cherry orchards with a focus on powdery mildew detection
container-title: Journal of the American Pomological Society
5760705ede1b04402dfc22e2a15af35dc1337418.abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-based multispectral imagery could provide a more efficient approach to pest scouting in tart cherry, a relatively low-input orchard crop. We evaluated whether vegetation indices derived from UAV-mounted multispectral imagery could detect powdery mildew (PM) in three commercial tart cherry orchard blocks in Utah during 2022 and 2023. Powdery mildew severity was surveyed repeatedly and compared with vegetation indices calculated from multispectral imagery collected during the same period. The optimized chlorophyll vegetation index (OCVI) showed the strongest overall relationship with PM severity, but correlations were only moderate when data were pooled across orchards and dates. Within individual orchards and sampling dates, vegetation indices were not consistently related to PM severity. Relationships were especially weak when analyses were restricted to observations below an estimated economic threshold of 20% severity, where early detection would be most useful for management decisions. Although UAV multispectral imagery was not reliable for early PM detection, it was useful for identifying broader spatial variability in tree health. Tree health, assessed using red-edge normalized difference vegetation index as an indicator of canopy chlorosis and vigor, varied substantially among orchards and was associated with canopy density and apparent soil electrical conductivity (ECa). In the most variable orchard, poorer tree health and greater chlorosis were concentrated in areas of lower canopy density and higher ECa, corresponding to finer-textured soils. These findings indicate that UAV multispectral imagery was not reliable for early detection of PM in tart cherry under commercial orchard conditions but was useful for characterizing orchard-scale variability in tree health related to canopy structure and soil properties.

title: Artificial Intelligence and Religious Policy: Ethical Governance  in the Digital Public Sphere
container-title: AMUYA: INDONESIAN JOURNAL OF MANAGEMENT REVIEWS
3e92be76556d313607d793a0624ba717c1fa41bd.abstract: Artificial intelligence increasingly mediates religious communication, knowledge, and participation in the digital public sphere, yet research remains fragmented across digital religion, human rights, and AI governance. This study examines how AI-mediated religious communication shapes authority, visibility, and participation; identifies associated ethical and rights-based concerns; and analyzes the institutional conditions relevant to its governance. Using a qualitative, non-experimental, exploratory-analytical design, the study draws on academic publications, policy documents, regulatory instruments, institutional guidelines, human-rights reports, and documented analyses of digital religious practices. Materials were purposively selected for substantive relevance and examined through structured reading and extraction, open and focused coding, thematic synthesis, source triangulation, and iterative cross-source comparison. The analysis identified three interconnected domains: access, visibility, and religious authority; religious freedom, inclusion, and algorithmic risks; and accountability, contestability, and institutional responsibility. AI-mediated technologies can broaden access to religious resources while simultaneously shaping the visibility and perceived authority of religious actors and interpretations. Expanded access can coexist with unequal representation, privacy risks, profiling, and constraints on meaningful participation, while distributed responsibility can create accountability gaps when consequential outcomes are difficult to explain or challenge. These relationships are context-dependent rather than predetermined effects of AI. By integrating sociotechnical and algorithmic-governance perspectives, the study provides an analytical framework for understanding ethical governance as the intersection of technological mediation, religious pluralism, fundamental rights, participation, and identifiable institutional responsibility.

title: <b>Problematika Generative AI Dalam Memahami Al-Qur’an Dan Hadis: Perspektif Etika Menuntut Ilmu</b>
container-title: Nusantara Journal Of Islamic Studies
aa4faf4ac7e79634028cac55dc7ad5f3339f2b47.abstract: Abstract : This study aims to analyze the challenges of using Generative Artificial Intelligence (Generative AI) to understand the Qur’an and Hadith among undergraduate Islamic Education (PAI) students, their practices of information verification and academic integrity, and the application of Islamic ethics of seeking knowledge. This qualitative study employed a case study design. Data were collected through an online questionnaire comprising open-ended and closed-ended questions administered to 13 informants and analyzed using thematic analysis. The findings indicate that Generative AI helps students understand learning materials and access information efficiently. However, its use presents risks, including inaccurate information, unclear sources, and reduced learning independence. Students reported verifying AI-generated information through Qur’anic commentaries, Hadith collections, scholarly literature, and consultations with lecturers or teachers, although verification practices varied. Ethical AI use requires honesty, trustworthiness, diligence, discipline, and responsibility to ensure that technology remains a learning aid rather than a substitute for independent thinking and engagement with authoritative Islamic sources.

title: From Routine Fixed Schedules to Signals: A Condition-Responsive, AI-Augmented Pigging Intelligence Framework for Localised Internal Corrosion Control in Crude Oil and Water Injection Pipelines
container-title: ADIPEC
bb102d5cbb0ad65fc316c638ad53cb6149af8dab.abstract: Abstract Pigging plans in most operating companies globally are scheduled by calendar days. Pipeline segments are pigged every 30, 60 or 90 days based on the historical fixed maintenance schedules set during commissioning, regardless of the real time corrosion dynamics of the pipeline when in service. However, in most crude oil and water injection lines where the corrosion environment shifts with well stream composition, throughput and bacteria activity, the fixed schedule methodology of pigging does not prevent escalation of corrosion events. A five-year trending of several pipeline ILI data shows why 63% of anomalies deeper than 18% wall thickness were found in segments fully compliant with their pigging schedule. A 24-month study across 312 km length of pipelines compared condition-responsive segments against fixed 30-day controls showed that the mean maximum pit depth growth fell by 54.5% with over 80% drop in reactive integrity actions. Furthermore, the chemical inhibitor wetting efficiency increased by 18 points with 22.5% reduction in pigging runs. More so, 78% of the anomaly's clusters were located at the 5 to 7 o'clock orientation and concentrated in pipelines where inhibitor wetting had dropped below 69%. Sulphate Reducing Bacteria (SRB) and Iron Oxidizing Bacteria (IOB) counts proved the strongest leading indicators in the corrosion index, which is what should be expected in MIC-susceptible water injection systems. This paper proposes and validates the Pigging Intelligence Framework (PIF), in which pig runs are triggered by corrosion signals rather than fixed maintenance schedules. The PIF has three layers namely: the Corrosion Signal Index (CSI), supervised machine learning model and a root cause framework. The CSI combines flow velocity, BS&W content, microbiological activity, inhibitor residuals and ILI pit depth progression into a continuously updated risk score for each segment.
