The result was calibrated and validated against core data (CT scan and thin section) and wells with full PLT/ILT coverage before being applied to wells with partial or no PLT/ILT data. In validation wells, the image-derived FZI flow profiles showed good agreement with measured PLT inflow distributions and core-based flow unit definitions, confirming that AI-segmented borehole images capture flow-relevant heterogeneity in this tight carbonate system. When applied to horizontal wells with restricted PLT accessibility, the workflow produced physically consistent zonal contribution estimates that aligned with geological zonation and offset well performance. The approach also reveals lateral reservoir heterogeneity that conventional logs may be overlooked. Applied to long horizontal wells in a green field tight carbonate development, it provides a practical and transparent alternative for estimating zonal contribution where PLT coverage is incomplete or unavailable, as well as providing additional data required for static and dynamic simulations.

title: 31% Lateral ROP Uplift Through Remotely Automated Surface Pressure Management: Field Results from U.S. Unconventional Drilling
container-title: ADIPEC
49f0c644841fd0b385b870c2d3bfb0dee3d42995.abstract: Abstract Unconventional drilling programs continue to push hydraulic performance toward technical limits in pursuit of reducing days on well and AFE costs. However, conventional manual surface pressure management introduces operational variability, limits utilization of the available hydraulic operating window, and requires personnel to work in close proximity to high-pressure equipment. This paper presents the field deployment and performance evaluation of an automated surface pressure management system designed to enhance drilling operations. The system combines high-frequency redundant pressure sensing with automated pressure relief and programmable bleed-down sequences within a closed-loop control architecture. By continuously monitoring standpipe pressure (SPP) and autonomously controlling pressure release, the system maintains a defined operating window with a level of precision, consistency, and repeatability unattainable through conventional systems. Performance was evaluated across a five-well pad equipped with the automated system and compared against offset wells drilled on the same rig under similar geological and operational conditions. Key performance indicators included rate of penetration, flow rate, differential pressure, standpipe pressure utilization, connection-time performance, and system response to abnormal pressure events. Relative to the offset wells, the automated system achieved a 31% increase in lateral ROP, a 4% increase in flow rate, a 20% increase in usable differential pressure, and a 7% increase in standpipe pressure utilization. Automated connection management reduced average bleed-down time by approximately 20 seconds per connection while maintaining precise pressure control throughout the process. During an unplanned internal blowout preventer (IBOP) mechanical malfunction, the system detected two consecutive overpressure events and automatically limited peak surface pressure, mitigating loss of pressure containment and allowing drilling operations to continue without significant downtime associated without equipment integrity evaluation. These results show that automated surface pressure management allows operators to safely use more of the available hydraulic envelope while improving drilling efficiency, reducing operational variability, and limiting personnel exposure to high-pressure equipment. The technology provides a practical advancement in drilling automation by enhancing hydraulic performance without requiring changes to rig infrastructure or drilling practices.

title: Integrated MMV Baseline Deployment for Co2 Storage in the UAE: Enabling Site Certification, Risk Management and Carbon Crediting
container-title: ADIPEC
0bceb1999768cccdd8ea7b9f17432741dd6cc2c9.abstract: Abstract The deployment of Carbon Capture and Storage (CCS) at commercial scale requires robust Measurement, Monitoring, and Verification (MMV) programs to establish pre-injection conditions, support storage assurance, and demonstrate the long-term containment of injected CO2. This paper presents the development and implementation of a comprehensive MMV baseline program for a geological CO2 storage site in Abu Dhabi, UAE. The baseline program was designed using a risk-based approach and integrated atmospheric, groundwater, and passive seismic monitoring systems to characterize environmental and subsurface conditions prior to CO2 injection. The monitoring network was deployed across a remote desert environment and supported by a vendor digital platform for data acquisition, quality assurance, traceability, and long-term data management. Initial baseline datasets were generated to establish reference conditions and capture natural variability, providing the foundation for future anomaly detection, storage performance assessment, and containment verification throughout the storage lifecycle. A key component of the program was the consolidation of diverse monitoring datasets into a unified digital ecosystem, enabling standardized workflows, metadata management, cross-disciplinary data integration, and audit-ready traceability. By integrating environmental, geophysical, and operational datasets within a single framework, the platform supports efficient data traceability and auditability, facilitates regulatory reporting, and provides a transparent basis for independent verification and certification activities. The project demonstrated that effective MMV implementation requires more than the deployment of monitoring technologies alone. Successful delivery depended on risk-based monitoring design, proactive stakeholder engagement, close coordination with technology vendors, and operational flexibility to address deployment challenges associated with a remote desert operating environment. The experience confirms that MMV baseline acquisition should commence during the early stages of CCS project development to ensure adequate characterization of natural conditions prior to injection. The integrated monitoring and digital traceability framework established through this program provides a scalable and auditable model for future CCS projects, supporting storage assurance, regulatory compliance, certification readiness, and emerging carbon market requirements across the UAE and wider region.

title: AI-Enabled Well Inactivity Prediction for Proactive Production Target Protection in Upstream Operations
container-title: ADIPEC
f24c0fdd822b3cdc5ba7128622e59310095284fb.abstract: Abstract Unplanned well string inactivity is one of the biggest sources of production deferral, unstable short term forecasts, and missed annual targets in upstream operations. Most surveillance today is reactive. An asset team usually confirms that a string has gone inactive from the monthly report, once the barrels have already been lost, and then works out the cause well by well. This paper describes an AI based predictive framework that runs the other way round. It looks ahead and estimates which active strings are likely to become inactive, what is most probably driving them, and roughly when, so that reservoir, well and operations teams can step in before the deferment happens. The framework brings together three analytical layers that support one another. Time series forecasting provides the portfolio inactivity outlook. Supervised machine learning gives each string a level of risk and names its most likely cause. Survival analysis estimates the remaining active time before an expected event. Threshold exceedance and degradation trend features feed all three and act as early warning signals. The prediction is scoped deliberately to well and reservoir related problems rather than facility driven downtime, because that is where advance warning changes the outcome. We developed and tested the framework on a mature onshore assets with thousands of wells, covering oil producers, water injectors and gas injectors. On blind, out of time data it gives useful advance visibility of inactivity risk months before the loss shows up in the numbers, and it lets teams intervene earlier and concentrate effort on the wells that matter most.

title: AI-Enabled Integrated Talent Platforms: Accelerating Readiness for Critical Roles in Energy Operations
container-title: ADIPEC
616e76f02a6087071688234d837ceb0458f0edc6.abstract: Summary The energy industry continues to face increasing workforce complexity driven by digital transformation, changing demographics, evolving competency requirements, and the need to maintain operational continuity across critical business functions. While organizations have invested heavily in digital technologies for operational excellence, succession planning and workforce readiness management remain areas where decision making is frequently influenced by fragmented information, limited visibility of workforce capabilities, and subjective assessments. These challenges become increasingly significant in large organizations where talent mobility, cross functional experience, and diverse competency profiles make successor identification more complex. A major downstream energy company identified several challenges in its talent management and succession processes. Historically, succession planning activities relied heavily on management discussions, performance records, current job assignments, and managerial recommendations. This approach often created limitations in identifying hidden talent, recognizing cross functional experiences, and objectively evaluating workforce readiness for critical positions. The organization required a more comprehensive system capable of capturing broader dimensions of employee capability while providing greater transparency, consistency, and governance throughout the succession planning process. To address these challenges, the organization implemented an integrated talent ecosystem consisting of a Career Management Platform (CMP) and Capability Development Platform (CDP). CMP centralized succession planning activities using a meritocracy based point system incorporating capability, experience, aspiration, and achievement dimensions, while CDP connected competency assessments, capability gap identification, and structured development interventions. Together, the platforms established a closed loop talent management process that improved visibility into workforce capability and readiness. Although the implementation significantly improved governance, transparency, and workforce visibility, several limitations remained. Successor rankings continued to rely on predefined weighting mechanisms and rule based logic, making it difficult to evaluate the relative importance of different experiences, identify hidden talent across functions, and anticipate future succession risks. To address these limitations, the organization identified an AI-enabled Workforce Intelligence Layer as the next stage of maturity aligned with its Human Capital 5.0 transformation roadmap. The proposed AI capabilities include successor readiness prediction, intelligent talent discovery, dynamic successor evaluation, development path recommendations, and succession risk forecasting. This paper presents the implementation of CMP and CDP as the current state of workforce readiness management while proposing an AI-enabled evolution toward predictive workforce intelligence.

title: A Closed-Loop Architecture for Intelligent Reservoir Management: Framework, Building Blocks, and Field Evidence
container-title: ADIPEC
6fe1659ee2653fd1560f6adfea6c8ade7c80f4eb.abstract: Abstract Integrated Reservoir Management (IRM) brought subsurface, well, facility, and economic disciplines into a common workflow, yet many reservoir decisions are still made in periodic cycles. By the time a surveillance signal is validated, interpreted, modeled, approved, and executed, the operating opportunity may have changed. We propose Intelligent Reservoir Management (i-RM) as an engineering-supervised architecture for shortening that cycle. i-RM links continuous observation, governed data, a living representation of reservoir-well-facility behavior, automated diagnostics, and decision support. These elements are coordinated through a shared state and explicit rules for authority, escalation, and post-action learning. The framework was developed from a structured literature review and its feasibility examined against a mixed evidence base of operational deployments, proofs of concept, and public benchmarks. The evidence does not yet demonstrate a complete autonomous loop in field operation. It does, however, show that the required components are technically mature enough to be assembled: governed data workflows reduce reconciliation effort; machine-learning and physics-informed models accelerate interpretation and forecasting; anomaly and candidate-screening tools improve prioritization; and bounded control policies can approach high-fidelity optimization at lower computational cost. The practical implication is that i-RM should not be treated as an AI replacement for reservoir engineering. It is an operating model that connects existing engineering tools, preserves uncertainty, and makes the path from observation to action explicit and auditable. Field-scale adoption will depend on clear observed/measured data and model ownership, calibrated decision limits, coordinated agent behavior, and disciplined comparison of predicted and realized outcomes.

title: Detection of Work-Related Musculoskeletal Disorder Risk Factors Using AI-Enabled 3D Motion Capture: Implementation Experience in a UAE Oil and Gas Company
container-title: ADIPEC
f0555612019991345b10c490715aed0516346d72.abstract: Abstract Objectives/Scope Oil and gas operations involve repetitive manual handling, forceful exertions, awkward postures, and prolonged static positions that contribute to work-related musculoskeletal disorders (WMSDs). Traditional observational tools such as RULA and REBA remain prone to observer subjectivity and imprecise scoring of individual body segments. This descriptive, cross-sectional implementation study evaluated the practical application of an AI-enabled three-dimensional motion capture (3D MOCAP) assessment tool in a UAE oil and gas company to identify and prioritize ergonomic risks by work activity, worker group, and affected body region, and to define appropriate control measures. Methods, Procedures, Process Site HSE and Occupational Health SMEs were trained over an online course and a two-day workshop, then recorded task videos (minimum 1080p, 30 fps) using CICPA-approved intrinsically safe devices. Hand force was captured by force gauge, dynamometer, or Borg perceived exertion. Videos were uploaded to an industrial ergonomics platform where AI compared detected joint angles against thresholds benchmarked to REBA, OCRA, the Strain Index, and the ACGIH Hand Activity TLV. The software returned a skeleton-overlay video, a Risk Priority Score (RPS, 0–100) aggregating posture, force, frequency, and duration, and body area scores for six body segments. Results for 625 assessments across seven business units were logged in an Industrial Ergonomics Assessment Register between March 2023 and August 2024. Results, Observations, Conclusions Historical data (2020–2022) showed low back pain accounted for 84–85% of WMSD cases. Across the 625 assessments the median RPS was 22 and the mean 26, indicating a Moderate overall risk profile, with Operators and Maintenance groups representing 95% of assessments. Repetitive manual handling was the leading risk factor (41.9%), followed by excessive force (16.6%) and frequent hand tool use (8.72%). Aircraft refuelers, civil projects/kerbstone installers, and chemical offloaders recorded the highest RPS and body area scores, particularly at the right elbow, right shoulder, neck, and back. Of 836 recommendations, 58.4% were administrative — work instruction and coaching alone accounted for 43.7% — and 62% have been approved, completed, or are in progress. Novel/Additive Information The study demonstrates a scalable, bias-reduced, field-deployable AI ergonomics method and identifies the training, device, and governance conditions required for successful rollout.

title: The Whole Worker: Integrating Occupational Health Risk Management and Mental Wellbeing in the Middle East Energy Sector
container-title: ADIPEC
865b91cdf23eb89f4a0208f68481b0070a5c30a1.abstract: Abstract Energy sector workers in the Middle East face a dual burden that conventional health, safety, and environment (HSE) frameworks have historically addressed in isolation: physical occupational health risks, including non-communicable diseases (NCDs) and chronic conditions, and mental health challenges, including burnout, psychosocial stress, and rotational isolation. This paper presents an integrated Occupational Health and Mental Wellbeing (OHMW) model developed by a global health and security risk management organisation and field-validated across Gulf energy operations between 2021 and 2025. The methodology integrates operational data, electronic medical record (EMR)-derived health surveillance, and workforce wellbeing programme outputs from energy sector clients across the region, applying a dual-track analytical approach within a governance framework aligned to ISO 45003:2021. The OHMW model comprises four interconnected elements: workplace health risk assessments covering physical hazards and psychosocial stressors; structured pre-deployment medical screening addressing NCD burden and psychological vulnerability; integrated digital health surveillance monitoring physical and psychosocial key performance indicators (KPIs); and continuous remote clinical and psychological support services. Results demonstrate that the integrated model produces outcomes exceeding those achieved through siloed programmes: a 38% reduction (relative to pre-programme baselines within the same operations) in medical evacuations driven by early NCD detection and structured chronic disease management; a 28% reduction (against the same pre-programme baselines) in sick leave and absenteeism among cohorts receiving integrated wellbeing support; and clear evidence of convergence effects, whereby workers with unmanaged chronic physical conditions exhibit elevated psychosocial risk and workers with poor mental health show higher rates of NCD complications and occupational injury. These findings confirm that the conventional separation of occupational health and mental health management represents a critical governance gap in the energy sector, and that a unified, clinically co-governed model is more effective, more efficient, and directly supportive of Duty of Care obligations in the region's most demanding operational environments.

title: Challenges and Risk Management while Drilling the 8½-in. Horizontal Section in Unconventional Oil Wells with Overpressured Reservoir Zones Influenced by Offset Fractured Wells
container-title: ADIPEC
392b92d188c2db38fdf23daefd3ee1f69e3ebb36.abstract: Abstract In closely spaced, multi-well pad development of unconventional carbonate reservoirs, drilling and hydraulic fracturing are carried out within a few hundred metres of one another and often on overlapping schedules. This paper examines the drilling challenges and associated risk controls when an 8½-in. horizontal section is drilled through an overpressured interval whose pressure is locally elevated by an adjacent, recently fractured well. The regional pore-pressure model, calibrated to the static formation, cannot capture this transient anomaly. Consequently, a mud weight selected above the predicted pore pressure can still be several pounds per gallon underbalanced against the interval actually drilled. The analysis draws on field experience from the unconventional development, where two independent influxes, in wells WELL #1 and WELL #2, occurred while drilling the unconventional source rock. In both, post-event 3D seismic places the influx interval within roughly 100 to 150 m of an interpreted sub-seismic fault and its associated natural fractures, consistent with pressure communication from offset stimulation rather than with the regional trend. The better-instrumented WELL #1 event serves as the primary case study. A practical risk-management framework is proposed for this class of well: treating offset-frac status as a formal drilling gate, evaluating safe standoff and flowback state before the lateral is entered, integrating geosteering and ant-tracked fault interpretation into the drilling risk picture, dimensioning barriers, monitoring and surface equipment for a high-underbalance kick, and sequencing drilling and fracturing so the two activities do not compete for the same rock at the same time. The framework gives drilling and completion teams a repeatable method to recognise, rank, and control a hazard that conventional pore-pressure prediction alone cannot anticipate.

title: World Scale Application of Glass Disc Intervention Less Plugs Technology: Data Driven Operational Improvements from UAE Onshore Completions
container-title: ADIPEC
9abdb4fa9e886f503e077119d6ee03a86a6344a5.abstract: Abstract The drilling and completion industry's increasing demand for higher standards requirement to have completion installation safer, low risk, efficient, cost effective and provide longer well life cycle for further intervention activity. Slickline plug deployment has long been the industry standard intervention in completion and offers reliable method downhole plug placement. The intervention activities basically require operational time incorporated with surface unit preparation, intervention activity, cost, and well exposure. The potential for operational issues during intervention activities can result in additional remedial operations, driving the adoption of interventionless plug technologies to reduce risk, complexity, and well delivery time. The interventionless plug application enhances completion efficiency while reducing operational risk and maintaining compliance with standard well integrity verification practices, including inflow test safety valve and completion testing. Multiple interventionless plug technologies have been initiated, field trial and implemented with advantages and disadvantages for each technology to fit with the application and requirements. The glass disc as one of intervention less plug introduced, trial and applied into operation from few years ago and the improvement continuously conducted to meet with the requirements and increase success ratio. The increasing demand for higher standards has positioned and transformed glass discs as one of the effective solutions for interventionless plug and barrier application. This paper presents insights from one of the largest glass discs plug deployment campaigns in UAE onshore completion operations. Based on extensive historical data, field trials, and performance validation, the study identifies key success factors, operational risks, and improvement opportunities to enhance deployment reliability, operational efficiency, and process standardization. The glass disc is indeed beneficial for completion installation operation as intervention less plug, it provides assurance for process of packer setting and completion integrity testing. The development of glass disc technology has scaled up to massive levels and intrinsically single use due to material properties as its function compared with other completion accessories. Given its role and single-use nature, glass disc reliability and performance are critical to successful application. The success of installation has been discussed in several papers as functional of plug prior to packer setting and completion integrity test such as improvement of the design, best practice and lesson learn. The well completion is designed with consideration to maintain life of the well, efficient production and minimizing intervention during full lifecycle. The glass disc acts as a temporary isolation barrier during completion operations and should not contribute to production phase. The well shall be completed with full accessibility, which is essential for further activities in production phase. The assessment must verify that glass disc deployment does not adversely affect production performance. The assessment must verify that glass disc deployment does not adversely affect production performance. The production team as key stakeholder contributes operational expertise and historical field data to the evaluation process. Statistical analyses, field case studies, and stakeholder feedback support continuous improvement, capture lessons learned and establish best practices. The glass disc plugs have been widely deployed in UAE onshore completion operations, with approximately more than 200 data samples annually, becoming a standard component in completion strings. The feedback from production teams indicates a minor impact with less than 3% of data samples experiencing accessibility issues, it remains important and critical to understand these cases in detail. The Failure Modes and Effects Analysis (FMEA) was conducted to identify and prioritize potential failure modes associated with glass disc deployment, including non-rupture, premature rupture, and post-completion accessibility restrictions. System Integration Testing (SIT) validated failure mechanisms and mitigation measures under simulated field conditions prior to field implementation. Continuous field evaluation drive technology refinement and maximizes the value of the interventionless plug through best completion practices and operations.

title: From Predictive Analytics to Decision Governance: An AI-Enabled Framework for Condition-Based Maintenance of Industrial Gas Turbines
container-title: ADIPEC
489046c3b998f38a12f19559840cab0fa3dfbf5b.abstract: Abstract The objective of this paper is to reframe AI-enabled predictive maintenance from a failure prediction activity into a structured decision support capability. It describes how artificial intelligence, combined with physics-based models and real operating data, supports faster interpretation of asset behavior when systems operate close to technical limits. Rather than replacing engineering expertise, AI enables more disciplined, traceable, and defensible maintenance and operational decisions within a Condition-Based Maintenance (CBM) framework. The proposed method integrates AI-based analytics within a structured Condition-Based Maintenance (CBM) decision process. Physics-based models, OEM domain knowledge, and real-time operating data are combined through AI-enabled pre-processing to identify anomalies, characterize degradation behavior, and continuously update asset condition assessments. Decisions related to inspection interval extensions, temporary operating limit exceedances, and deferral of non-critical work are governed through a formal decision process based on departure records. These records document underlying assumptions, residual risk, agreed mitigation actions, and clearly defined re-entry conditions, ensuring accountability, technical traceability, and shared risk ownership across the asset operating lifecycle. Scenario-based "what if" analyses are used to assess decision robustness and reversibility before the implementation, with final decision authority retained by human experts. Application of the proposed approach has enabled customers to extend maintenance intervals in a controlled and risk-based manner across a broad range of assets. Evidence from 104 documented departure records issued in 2025 shows that condition-based decisions have been implemented at fleet scale, with 54% of departures related to aeroderivative units and 46% to heavy duty gas turbines. The industrial revance of these results is illustrated by large LNG applications, including implementations with ExxonMobil where condition-based interval extensions were formally adopted following OEM analytics, engineering validation, and structured risk assessment. In these applications, inspection intervals for critical gas turbines were extended from standard semi-annual Level 1 cycles (4,000 fired hours) to condition-based intervals exceeding 15,000 fired hours, avoiding multiple days of production downtime per train while maintaining asset integrity. These results support the transition toward Performance-Based Contract (PBC) models, where CBM-driven decisions, digital insights, and engineering governance are directly linked to shared performance outcomes such as availability, reliability, and production continuity rather than prescriptive maintenance schedules. This paper adds to the existing literature by demonstrating that the adoption of an AI-enabled CBM decision process, grounded in formal risk assessment and decision governance, enables new collaborative operating and contractual models, including Performance-Based Contracts (PBC). The approach shifts OEM–operator relationships from transactional service delivery to partnership-based models, where priorities, risk acceptance, and operational flexibility are jointly defined. This enables operators to sustain production under constrained conditions while maintaining traceable, accountable decision-making.

title: Systems of Surrogates: A Method for Physics-Informed AI in Surface Network Optimization at Full-Field Scale
container-title: ADIPEC
cdab351641a95582cce46d68bc8ac708ca1d057f.abstract: Oil and gas well-network systems are inherently complex hydraulically, thermodynamically, and operationally. Even the smallest network will typically demonstrate well-to-well hydraulic pressure interference, co-mingling fluids and gasses, down-hole constraints and capacity constraints once the multiphase mixtures reach their processing destination. A suite of mature commercial simulation offerings exist which have throughout the years shown to be quite capable in accurately predicting the steady state behavior of such systems given adequate well design, flowline, and fluid PVT data (Schlumberger 2023; Petroleum Experts 2023). Unfortunately, the simulation-driven optimization of such systems faces a multiplicative computational burden as a target network increases in size with respect to well count: the cost per forward solution increases and the dimensionality of the inverse problem itself (number of control variables) increases; proportionally demanding additional forward evaluations to find feasible optimums (Bieker et al. 2007). For example, a co-mingled network of 200 ESP wells undergoing choke opening and ESP frequency optimization will require 401 (1 baseline + 400 control variable perturbations) forward solves for the construction of a single two-point finite difference estimated Jacobian matrix. When operating networks of these scales, the time-horizon for decision making is the critical constraint. While combining a high-fidelity simulator with optimization algorithms can technically support a wide array of inverse problems, it may take so long to produce an answer from such an approach that the chance to apply a decision based on that answer has passed. There are many classical and novel approaches to accelerating optimization tasks including probabilistic methods, gradient free schemes, and linearization (Camponogara and Nakashima 2006), all with varying compatibility and utility for problems of this high dimensionality. In this work we focus on a proxy/surrogate model approach (Forrester et al. 2008) which leverages a computationally expensive yet robust gradient based optimizer algorithm, while compressing the forward solve time itself via assemblages of non-linear physics-informed deep neural network regressors.

title: From Data to Decision: A Field-Validated AI-Assisted Production Intelligence Framework for Opportunity Identification, Artificial Lift Optimization, and Surveillance in the Indus Basin
container-title: ADIPEC
682401dea7bf98f4681e69f40979ea43326f1efc.abstract: Abstract Objectives/Scope The increasing complexity of mature oil, gas, and condensate assets has expanded surveillance data volumes while making rapid identification of high-value production opportunities increasingly difficult. Conventional workflows rely on fragmented datasets, manual interpretation, and reactive assessments resulting in delayed intervention planning, suboptimal artificial lift performance, and inconsistent prioritization across large portfolios. This study presents a field-validated AI-assisted production intelligence framework to enhance opportunity identification, artificial lift optimization, and surveillance efficiency across a multi-well oil, gas, and condensate portfolio in the Indus Basin, Pakistan. Methods, Procedures, Process The framework integrates production, pressure, temperature, choke, gas lift injection, well testing, downtime, and intervention datasets from production databases into a centralized Python-based environment connected to business intelligence dashboards. Isolation Forest and gradient boosting-based anomaly detection algorithms were combined with petroleum engineering workflows including nodal analysis, liquid loading diagnostics using Turner and Coleman critical velocity models, gas lift performance diagnostics, and operating envelope validation to establish a physics-guided decision intelligence system. The framework screens wells across natural flow and artificial lift modes, diagnosing liquid loading, gas lift inefficiency, skin buildup, and choke instability, ranking opportunities by uplift potential and operational feasibility. Results, Observations, Conclusions Field deployment across 41 active wells including 4 gas lift producers reduced manual well review cycles from bi-weekly to daily automated anomaly alerts. Within 6 months, 29 anomaly flags were reduced to 16 physics-validated opportunities across four categories: 5 liquid loading remediation candidates drawn from 8 wells confirmed below Turner critical rate with deficits ranging from 12% to 78%, 2 gas lift optimization candidates, 4 choke and operating envelope deviations, and 5 rigless intervention candidates. Gas lift optimization contributed an incremental ~80 BOED, while aggregate uplift reached approximately 650 BOED (~3.9 MMSCFD) representing an ~18% improvement over the 12-month pre-deployment baseline. Decision cycle time was reduced by an estimated 55%, with full portfolio coverage achieved without additional engineering headcount. Novel/Additive Information This methodology demonstrates how AI-assisted surveillance integrates with petroleum engineering domain knowledge to create scalable production decision intelligence systems for mature assets. Unlike purely data-driven approaches, the framework combines machine learning with physics-based validation at every decision node preserving auditability, operational trust, and engineering accountability. This scalable, low-infrastructure model confirms that AI-assisted production intelligence is deployable without enterprise-scale investment across the Indus Basin and similar producing regions globally.

title: Physics-Guided AI–Numerical Simulation for Sand Production Prediction and Completion Optimization
container-title: ADIPEC
6faae9cc1216c5f7bd2de1d415c2ac2ff3fe5cc3.abstract: Abstract Sand production is a nonlinear, path-dependent, and strongly coupled process controlled by reservoir depletion, effective-stress redistribution, near-wellbore stress concentration, elastoplastic failure, damage accumulation, grain debonding, hydraulic detachment, erosion, and particulate transport. Its occurrence and severity depend on rock-strength variability, stress regime, well trajectory, completion type, perforation orientation, production drawdown, transient rate history, water weakening, and evolving cavity geometry. Conventional sanding workflows typically combine empirical screening, analytical failure criteria, and detailed numerical simulation, but each method has limitations when used independently. Empirical correlations may not extrapolate reliably; analytical methods simplify geometry and constitutive behavior; and high-fidelity finite-element or discrete-element models are computationally expensive for field-scale optimization and real-time control. This paper develops a unified physics-guided artificial-intelligence and numerical-simulation framework for predicting sanding onset, critical drawdown, transient sand rate, cumulative sand production, cavity evolution, and completion-dependent operating envelopes. The workflow integrates quality-controlled petrophysical logs, drilling and production records, depletion history, laboratory measurements from unconfined compression, triaxial compression, thick-wall-cylinder and advanced thick-wall-cylinder tests, calibrated one-dimensional geomechanical models, and three-dimensional poroelastoplastic finite-element simulations. Sanding initiation is constrained by an analytical effective-strength-factor load criterion and a laboratory-calibrated critical-strain-limit criterion. Mechanical failure is coupled to hydraulic mobilization through drag, lift, seepage, and retention forces, while an erosion law governs sand generation and transport. The AI layer combines gradient-boosted trees, random forests, deep neural networks, temporal models, graph neural networks, neural operators, residual learning, and physics-informed neural networks. A multi-task, multi-fidelity loss function enforces data agreement, finite-element consistency, equilibrium, mass conservation, yield admissibility, Critical state line (CSL) consistency, nonnegative sand rate, physically valid bounds, and regime-dependent monotonicity. Bayesian and ensemble uncertainty quantification provides conservative safe-drawdown limits and out-of-distribution detection. Completion optimization is posed as a constrained multi-objective problem over well trajectory, perforation orientation, phasing, penetration, sand-control selection, and drawdown schedule. The supplied field-study basis indicates that representative depletion scenarios up to 3,000 psi, a stress-path coefficient near 0.6, TWC variability, and open-hole versus cased-and-perforated geometry materially alter the sanding envelope. Laboratory-calibrated TWC/perforation-scale CSL values range approximately from 30 to 68 millistrain in the documented cases, and open-hole CSL may be 20–60% lower because of hole-size and unsupported-boundary effects. The proposed framework converts high-fidelity numerical simulations into rapid probabilistic operating envelopes without inventing unsupported AI performance statistics. It supports pre-drill completion screening, uncertainty-aware production design, adaptive choke control, and continuously updated sand-management digital twins.

title: Preventing Major Road Transportation Incidents Through ADAS and AI-Enabled Fleet Intelligence: A Framework for Safer and More Resilient Energy Supply Chains
container-title: ADIPEC
9f5cdc164fe04e1f1f074f71895b4ac13038b5b4.abstract: Abstract Objectives/Scope Road traffic crashes cause approx. 1.19 million fatalities and 20-50 million injuries globally each year (WHO 2023), while imposing economic losses approaching 3% of GDP in many countries. Transportation of fuels, chemicals, LNG, industrial gases, and other hazardous materials represents one of the most critical and risk-intensive links in global energy supply chains. Human factors—including fatigue, distraction, speeding, impaired judgement, and blind-spot errors—contribute to nearly 80-90%of severe transportation incidents. While telematics-based fleet monitoring has improved operational visibility, they remain largely reactive. This paper evaluates how Advanced Driver Assistance Systems (ADAS) with AI-enabled fleet intelligence and Driver Monitoring System (DMS) can transform commercial fleet safety by shifting risk management from reactive monitoring to proactive accident prevention Methods, Procedures, Process This study utilizes a multi-evidence triangulation methodology integrating four streams: (1) forensic reconstruction of 60 severe tanker crashes (including 25 internal accident investigation); (2) physiological survey of 500 active drivers; (3) a 90-day pilot of 155 tankers using AI telematics and infrared DMS; and (4) Level 0–2 ADAS testing via an LCV-to-HCV validation bridge. The Safety Cocoon fuses forward 77 GHz radar, forward optical camera, and 24 GHz side radars with an in-cab DMS to continuously assess risk. Results, Observations, and Conclusions Forensic analysis identified rollovers (35%), rear-end impacts (28%), and sideswipes (18%) as dominant crash typologies, driven primarily by fatigue and distraction. The 155-tanker pilot revealed a 12-to-1 Detection Gap where DMS captured behavioral precursors invisible to passive GPS. Triangulated findings indicate the Safety Cocoon is projected to prevent 70–75% of forward and lateral collisions. Economic modelling projects a 17.12-month payback period on an upfront CapEx of ₹285.90 Lakh, generating ₹17.19 Crore in 10-year fleet lifecycle net returns. Novel Approach This paper presents an integrated Accident-to-ADAS Risk Mitigation Framework developed from real-world crash forensics, driver behavioural analytics, operational AI-enabled Fleet Intelligence pilot data, and an LCV-to-HCV ADAS Validation Framework. Rather than positioning ADAS as an optional vehicle feature, the research establishes an engineering and economic blueprint for integrating AI-enabled Fleet Intelligence, active ADAS, and Journey Risk Management 2.0 into a multi-layered Safety Cocoon for hazardous-material transportation. The proposed framework bridges the gap between passive behavioural monitoring and active physical intervention, providing energy executives, fleet operators, and regulators with a technically rigorous and economically justified pathway for strengthening the safety and resilience of global energy logistics

title: AI-Based Optimization for LNG Sustainable and Efficient Production
container-title: ADIPEC
db84223af7bad433721ea6d2e836439e1a64b9f3.abstract: Abstract Asset optimization has become increasingly important in recent years, particularly in the Oil & Gas industry, where improving process efficiency is essential to address both economic and environmental challenges. As the global energy sector moves toward a lower-carbon future, natural gas is expected to play a key role as a transition fuel thanks to its lower emissions compared to other fossil fuel sources. Within this framework, Liquefied Natural Gas (LNG) represents a valuable source to enhance energy security and supply diversification due to its intrinsic flexibility in transportation and trading. This work presents one of the first applications of a Differential Evolution (DE) algorithm to the optimization of an offshore Dual Mixed Refrigerant (DMR) natural gas liquefaction process modelled and validated with real plant data. The process is first modeled using a commercial simulation software and, after validation, it is integrated with a Differential Evolution-based (DE) optimization tool to identify the operating conditions that maximize process performance while respecting relevant operational constraints. Different optimization scenarios are investigated by progressively expanding the set of decision variables, including refrigerant compositions, pressure drops across Joule-Thomson valves of the refrigeration cycles, and refrigerant mass flow rates. The results highlight the ability of the Differential Evolution-based approach to effectively explore the solution space and identify operating configurations capable of significantly increasing LNG production while maintaining acceptable energy consumption levels.

title: Augmenting Petroleum Engineers with Agentic AI: A ReAct Agent Framework for Automated Well Diagnostics and Candidate Screening
container-title: ADIPEC
9bc6b07335ff5537c9111977aedb5e3ddced754a.abstract: Abstract Mature onshore oil fields carry thousands of wells that all need watching. Rates drift, water cuts creep up, injectors quietly lose conformance, and somewhere in that population sit the handful of candidates that would pay back an intervention. In day-to-day practice, petroleum engineers spend a large share of their time pulling data, hopping between tools such as OFM and spreadsheets, and repeating the same diagnostic steps well after well. The work is necessary but slow, and because everyone does it slightly differently, interpretations vary from engineer to engineer and from asset to asset. This paper describes an Agentic Petroleum Engineering Assistant that turns a plain-language question into a standardized, multi-step production analysis, so the engineer spends the time on judgement rather than on data wrangling. The assistant is built on a custom ReAct (Reasoning + Acting) agent organized as five layers: an interaction layer where engineers ask in domain language; a reasoning layer that breaks the request into ordered diagnostic steps and routes to tools using domain rules under a transparent plan-execute-summarize loop; a domain-tools layer holding a validated library (decline-curve analysis, type-well benchmarking, Chan water diagnostics, Hall-plot injector checks, a heterogeneity index, and controlled read-only queries); a data and integration layer that conditions and quality-checks a unified data foundation so results are comparable across wells; and a governance layer that enforces read-only access, blocks unsafe instructions, and sanity-checks outputs. The system runs on the Dataiku LLM Mesh, which gives enterprise tracing, prompt and version governance, and reproducibility. It was developed and tested across more than 1,500 wells in a matured onshore field. Engineers now ask for complex diagnostics "rank workover candidates by uplift" or "flag injectors with Hall-plot damage signatures" and get plots plus a concise interpretation in minutes. The larger gain is consistency: the agent triangulates evidence across diagnostics, applies the same analytical sequence every time, and states the driver behind each underperformance call, with a full trace log that a peer can review.

title: From Saturation Surveillance to Time-Critical Intervention: An Integrated Pulsed Neutron Logging, Well Test, and Trajectory Analytics Framework for Water-Drive Fields
container-title: ADIPEC
f7d03f2d3e86904d5de5d8dbcd9619755c4c4706.abstract: Abstract Mature natural water-drive fields sustaining high water cut (WC) face compounding challenges including locating remaining oil, diagnosing production impairment, and assessing shrinking intervention windows. This paper introduces a concurrent diagnostic workflow integrating memory-mode pulsed neutron logging (PNL), well test production analytics, and trajectory modeling, applied to a mature field where surveillance coverage is partial. The objective is to demonstrate how cross-dataset integration can reverse PNL-derived intervention priorities and produce a time-sequenced recommendation roadmap. The studied field is a mature shallow-water small field offshore Asia, producing from stacked sandstone reservoirs under natural bottom-water drive with sustained WC exceeding 80%. A memory-mode, multi-detector PN (MDPN) campaign deploying Gas and Carbon/Oxygen (C/O) modes was run on slickline across Well A and D, covering two reservoir intervals. The PNL results were cross-referenced against twenty-four well test records from four producers between 2023 to 2026 using a hypothesis-exclusion diagnostic method. Trajectory analytics, applied as a relative timing tool for intervention urgency assessment, were modeled using four different methods anchored to contact—rise rate, single-tank volumetric depletion, direct WC rates, and gas influx trend. PNL confirmed water encroachment in both reservoir intervals. In the lower reservoir, a consistent Gas-Oil contact (GOC) was identified across Well D with 17 ft of remaining oil column. Post-survey production in Well D confirms active oil contribution with 81% WC. In the upper reservoir, inconsistent saturation profiles between adjacent wells indicated partial sweep and compartmentalization, supporting additional perforation into un-swept intervals. Trajectory results of reservoir B span 2.4 to 11 years, with the tightest window coming from the gas influx trend method focusing on Well D. At constant choke, gas rate rose 148% and Gas-Oil ratio (GOR) 123% against a WC rise of 3%. Besides, well test from non-PN-surveyed Well C revealed a 27% oil rate decline over 11 months. With a choke-verified rise in flowing tubing head pressure (FTHP) and a declining oil rate, this is inconsistent with water breakthrough or classical skin. This reversed the PNL-derived recommendation - Well C's behaviors shall be diagnosed first, ahead of any further perforation additions based on PNL results. The constructed intervention sequencing decision tree helped produce a time-sequenced intervention roadmap: (1) diagnosing any well restriction; (2) proactive artificial lift feasibility evaluation; (3) zonal isolation to protect the narrowing oil column. In small-field campaigns where PNL coverage is partial and active producers co-exist outside the logging program, concurrent integration of PNL saturation and dynamic well test trends have not been systematically demonstrated as a priority-reversing diagnostic tool. This paper addresses the gap, elevating the PNL output from static volumetric input to a time-sensitive production decision component. Memory-mode slickline deployment demonstrates a cost-accessible surveillance pathway for mature fields with restricted wireline access and constrained intervention budgets.

title: A Domain-Intelligent Multi-Agent AI Framework for Upstream Subsurface Data Querying
container-title: ADIPEC
1eb4e2ef000deadd72c0847803594fb4bb0e6bd7.abstract: Abstract Objectives/Scope In upstream operations, professionals must make rapid decisions, yet critical data is often fragmented across complex schemas, causing delays or errors. This paper presents a GPT-5-based multi-agent AI framework that enables engineers to query enterprise data in natural language and receive validated, contextualized answers with supporting evidence in under one minute. The objective is to reduce decision latency and improve reliability in subsurface workflows by providing consistent, accurate, and immediately actionable data access. Methods, Procedures, Process The framework operates through four agents. The Domain Intelligence Agent (DIA) contextualizes queries using operator-specific naming conventions, business rules, and schema relationships, enabling accurate schema linking. Retrieval follows a two-stage approach: semantic table selection, then column refinement. Controlled experiments (N&gt;300) showed table-first retrieval significantly improves SQL quality (p=0.031) versus column-level indexing. A SQL agent generates and self-corrects queries with validation against schema constraints and join paths. Finally, dual verification agents assess schema consistency, semantic correctness, and the plausibility of the generated results, ensuring output reliability before returning validated outputs or reports. Results, Observations, Conclusions The framework achieved &gt;85% execution accuracy across 300 subsurface queries spanning 50+ tables. Accuracy is defined as successful execution producing semantically correct results, validated through Abstract Syntax Tree (AST)-based comparison, LLM-as-judge scoring, and SME review. These complementary methods capture distinct failure modes. Error analysis shows primary failure drivers include ambiguous queries (21% of incorrect outputs), database inconsistencies (17%), complex join-path errors (9%), and aggregation or unit misinterpretation (6%). Notably, over 30% of initially incorrect outputs were reclassified as external issues (prompt ambiguity or data quality), suggesting a lower intrinsic model error rate. A subsequent two-week field validation, in which 40 practicing SMEs posed more than 700 of their own daily-work questions and rated responses against a formal correctness rubric, corroborated this result with an independently assessed accuracy exceeding 93%. Standard benchmarks such as Spider and BIRD were not directly applied due to limited alignment with upstream schema complexity. Instead, a domain-specific benchmark dataset was developed, reflecting realistic subsurface workflows. Operationally, the system reduces reliance on manual data extraction, enabling users to obtain validated answers within minutes. Early adoption shows improved efficiency and a shift from reactive reporting to proactive data exploration. The framework has been validated through internal pilots, live demonstrations, and use in real operational tasks. Novel/Additive Information This work introduces a portable Domain Intelligence Agent that encodes domain knowledge for scalable deployment. It demonstrates, with statistical evidence (p=0.031), that table-first retrieval improves NL-to-SQL performance in complex industrial schemas with overlapping semantics. The study also proposes an error-aware evaluation framework that separates model performance from data and ambiguity issues. By enabling reliable data access at scale, the framework provides a foundation for future upstream AI agents and autonomous analytical workflows.

title: Fatigue Life Assessment and Integrity Management of Deaerator System in Hydrogen Unit
container-title: ADIPEC
3e2aafc5bc0cb6b27c667d0a9e25c8f4c2554910.abstract: Abstract Process water deaerators remove dissolved oxygen and carbon dioxide from boiler feed water by counter current contact with low pressure stripping steam. The duty combines a relatively cool water feed with a substantially hotter steam feed inside a single welded envelope, which makes the equipment intrinsically exposed to thermal gradients and, where operating conditions fluctuate, to thermal fatigue. Cracking is investigated for a process water deaerator within a hydrogen reformer unit. A water leak was reported in service and, following removal of the external insulation, leakage was confirmed at the water inlet nozzle reinforcement-pad telltale hole and at a circumferential crack in the shell. Internal inspection identified a total of six crack areas within the vertical stripping section, together with localised corrosion damage in the horizontal surge tank. Testing aimed to establish the credible damage mechanism and to quantify the remaining fatigue life. Laboratory examination of a section removed from the leaking shell to nozzle weld confirmed that the SS316L material complied with its specification and was free of metallurgical anomaly, and that the crack origin carried no pitting or mechanical damage. Corrosion, corrosion fatigue and vibrational fatigue were excluded on that basis, while beach marks and adjacent fatigue striations confirmed progressive fatigue crack growth. Thermal modelling of five operating conditions and subsequent structural analysis established the driving force. The design case represents the original full-throughput duty, with 8.7 kg/s of condensate at 102 °C and stripping steam at 140 °C. The operational case represents current running since withdrawal of the upstream condensate preheater, with reduced flow of 3.1 kg/s entering at 50 °C. Two upset cases were modelled: an extreme start up, in which 110 °C water enters an ambient vessel, and an extreme cool-down, in which 30 °C water enters an already warm vessel. Withdrawal of the preheater increased the steam-to-condensate temperature deviation at the vessel inlet from 48 °C by design to approximately 93 °C in operation. Linearised stresses reached 271 MPa in the design case and 231 MPa in the extreme cool down case against a 205 MPa allowable, compared with 76 MPa in normal running. The predicted high stress locations coincided with the surveyed crack positions. A significant finding is that the vessel is noncompliant at its own design condition, not only in upset. The original design basis had not evaluated the stripping column for cyclic thermal duty, so the equipment carries insufficient fatigue margin independently of how it is operated. Redesign of the stripping column to ASME Section VIII Division 2, explicitly assessing fatigue, is therefore required alongside any operational measure. The redesign should reduce stress concentration at the inlet nozzle, its reinforcement pad and the internal attachment welds, and should adopt worst case thermal transients rather than steady-state conditions as the design basis. The fatigue screening showed limited fatigue life under design and upset conditions, with only 10,000 to 30,000 allowable cycles, compared with more than one million cycles during normal operation. Because the material environmental interaction was found not driving the damage, the only variable the operator controls is the temperature difference between the two streams. Reinstating the preheater raises the condensate temperature and closes that gap at source. Until it is restored, the vessel should be held within the operating envelope shown to be compliant, and warmed and cooled slowly, since the damage is done during transitions rather than during steady running. Inspection strategy is equally critical. The vessel carried a thirty year risk based interval and had never been internally inspected since commissioning, which is why progressive fatigue damage developed undetected. Where the credible threat is cyclic rather than progressive metal loss, inspection intervals should be derived from the fatigue assessment rather than from corrosion rate models alone.

title: Cased Hole Tractor Conveyance RestoresSurveillance and Intervention Access in Long, Deep Horizontal Wells: A 20-Well Middle EastCampaign
container-title: ADIPEC
b3e71ebbc8eea2ff53628b6302f03ebab5580ca7.abstract: Abstract Long, deep horizontal wells completed with inflow control devices, swell packers, and slotted liner limit surveillance and intervention over the life of the field. Gravity wireline reaches lockup before total depth, and coiled tubing stalls in tortuous laterals with restrictive completion inside diameter. Reservoir contact stays unsurveyed, and planned remedial work is deferred. This paper reports a Middle East field campaign in which a latest-generation wheel-driven cased hole tractor extended conveyance beyond conventional limits and restored diagnostic and intervention access across the producing interval. Twenty tractor runs were executed in extended-reach horizontal wells with lateral lengths of 8,000 to 14,000 ft. Pre-job torque and drag modeling set the access envelope against pull capacity, dogleg severity, and minimum-restriction inside diameter. Toolstrings combined multiphase production logging, pulsed-neutron saturation, and casing integrity measurement. Each run was benchmarked against offset coiled tubing attempts, and the outcomes were written into a candidate-screening and execution standard with built-in risk controls. Tractor conveyance reached 61 to 99 percent depth coverage of the producing interval, against less than 50 percent for coiled tubing on comparable offset wells. Wells at the low end were held back by debris and scale, not by tractor capability, so pre-job wellbore cleanup can extend accessibility further. The acquired data resolved three-phase flow, sigma-derived saturation, and completion integrity along the surveyed interval, and fed water and gas shut-off ranking, integrity assessment, and inflow uncertainty in the reservoir model. Runs met their planned envelopes with no downhole losses, and used fewer rig days and less fluid handling than the coiled tubing alternative. The work adds a regional performance dataset for cased hole tractor conveyance in Middle East extended-reach horizontals, an area thinly covered in the published record, and positions the tractor as an enabling technology for life-of-field surveillance rather than a recovery tool alone. A pipeline of 66 further wells has been identified for the next surveillance cycle.

title: From Three Interventions to One: An Integrated Well Intervention Framework Delivering 50% Production Deferment Reduction and 24% Cost Savings in Mature Oil Fields
container-title: ADIPEC
d6a92ae6632927c49a8860cd307f42ae3e5d9d2d.abstract: Abstract Mature oil fields frequently require stimulation, cleanout, and well restoration activities to sustain production. Traditionally, these operations are executed through three separate intervention campaigns: an initial workover unit intervention to retrieve the completion, a standalone coiled tubing intervention to perform stimulation or cleanout activities, followed by a second workover intervention to reinstall the completion and return the well to production. While technically effective, this conventional approach results in extended production deferment, multiple mobilizations, increased HSE exposure, and significant operational costs. To address these challenges, an integrated well intervention framework was developed and implemented in South Oman, combining workover and coiled tubing operations within a single coordinated intervention campaign. The primary innovation was not the intervention technology itself; it was the operator-led redesign of the entire delivery model through one schedule, one barrier and interface-control strategy, and one end-to-end performance system. The framework enabled completion retrieval, stimulation or cleanout execution, and well reinstatement under one integrated operational strategy, eliminating unnecessary mobilizations and reducing operational interfaces between service providers and stakeholders. The implementation required extensive planning, multidisciplinary alignment, revised operating procedures, lifting studies, well control assessments, logistics optimization, and integrated execution workflows. The methodology was successfully deployed across eight field applications involving cleanout and stimulation activities in mature oil-producing wells characterized by ultra-low reservoir pressure and complex completion configurations. The results demonstrated significant operational and economic benefits. Average production deferment was reduced from approximately 25-30 days under the conventional intervention model to nearly 13 days using the integrated framework, representing approximately 50% improvement in restoration time. In addition, average CT intervention charges were reduced by 24%, while an average of three workover rig days per well were released. The reduction in mobilizations and joined-pipe operations also contributed to lowering overall HSE exposure and operational risk. Beyond the direct cost and time savings, the framework established a repeatable intervention model that improves resource utilization, accelerates production recovery, and enhances operational reliability. The methodology has demonstrated scalability across multiple wells and provides a practical blueprint for operators seeking to maximize asset value while reducing intervention complexity in mature oil fields. This paper presents the planning philosophy, implementation methodology, operational challenges, lessons learned, and performance outcomes associated with transitioning from a conventional three-intervention model to a fully integrated well intervention framework.

title: From Diagnosis to Digital Execution: AI-Enabled Materials Management for High-Intensity Operations
container-title: ADIPEC
c7e3ab01e28b2440de95c71f949d78f3b4b53488.abstract: Abstract In high-intensity energy operations, material availability depends on more than the accuracy of an enterprise resource planning inventory balance. A component may be recorded as available and still be unusable because its location, condition, certification or readiness for the work cannot be confirmed. The resulting searches, expediting, emergency purchasing and workarounds create a form of operational friction that is often managed locally until the cumulative effect appears in maintenance delay, lost productivity, excess working capital or avoidable logistics activity. A diagnostic-led transformation method is presented using practitioner evidence from energy and other asset-intensive operations. The method combines site engagement, benchmarking, value stream mapping, direct process observation and data analysis to identify where material flow is breaking down. Critical-to-quality requirements are then translated into a future-state operating model before the digital architecture is selected. Typical execution controls include master-data remediation, barcode or Radio Frequency Identification (RFID) identification, mobile warehouse tasks, two-way Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) integration, automated exception workflows, supplier-performance visibility, risk-based inventory policy and AI-enabled optimisation where the data and decision are suitable for probabilistic modelling. Across the case evidence, digitally controlled execution produced material improvements in processing speed, traceability, training burden, inventory performance and logistics flow. The strongest results did not come from technology deployed in isolation. They came from removing process variation, clarifying ownership and decision rights, improving data quality and then using digital tools to enforce the redesigned flow. The approach is particularly applicable to Middle Eastern operations, where large-scale energy investment, complex contractor ecosystems, remote and offshore logistics, localisation objectives and high expectations for uptime increase the cost of material uncertainty. Materials management is therefore treated here as an operational assurance discipline supported by digital and AI capability, rather than as a transactional warehouse function.

title: Enhancing Oil Production Resilience Through Integrated and Flexible Gas Network Management
container-title: ADIPEC
2761b4531fd3bb92ce4e7a62244f90aca0fa1a75.abstract: ABSTRACT Sustaining oil production in a large, mature onshore field depends on the robustness and flexibility of the gas systems that support gas lift, reservoir injection, fuel supply, and safe disposal. This paper describes an operations-led framework developed for the Bu Hasa field to manage these interconnected services as one production-enabling network. The approach combines system-wide visibility, standardized operating philosophies, dynamic gas allocation, flexible operating envelopes, scenario-based procedures, and close alignment among operations, subsurface, maintenance, and facilities teams. It is designed to accommodate evolving reservoir demand, production ramp-up, brownfield tie-ins, planned maintenance, equipment unavailability, and unplanned disturbances without losing sight of the Field Sustainable Oil Production Rate. Implementation improved coordination of gas consumers, strengthened response to constraints, reduced avoidable recycling and flaring, and supported production stability during outages and network disturbances. Automation also removed selected manual interventions, providing an estimated reduction of 384 person-hours per year and avoiding remote-station vehicle movements associated with approximately 183 kg CO2-equivalent emissions. The case demonstrates that gas-network flexibility should be treated as a strategic production-sustainability lever rather than a reactive facilities function. The framework is transferable to mature assets where interconnected gas systems, brownfield limitations, energy efficiency, and emissions performance must be managed simultaneously.

title: From Pilot to Enterprise Scale: Lessons Learned from Delivering Ai Solutions Across Diverse Industries and Stakeholder Ecosystems
container-title: ADIPEC
651cf7f2da6c313e194e18642e298b762030e033.abstract: Abstract Artificial Intelligence (AI) has rapidly evolved from experimental proof-of-concepts to a strategic enabler of business transformation across industries. Despite significant investments in AI technologies, many organizations continue to struggle with moving successful pilots into scalable enterprise-wide deployments. While technical feasibility is often demonstrated during pilot phases, challenges related to stakeholder alignment, governance, change management, user adoption, data readiness, and operational integration frequently limit the realization of sustainable business value. As AI solutions become increasingly embedded within critical business processes, organizations require structured approaches to bridge the gap between innovation and large-scale implementation. This paper presents practical lessons learned from coordinating and delivering AI solutions across diverse industries, organizational structures, and stakeholder ecosystems. The objective is to identify key success factors that enable organizations to transition from isolated AI pilots to enterprise-scale deployments while maximizing adoption, business impact, and long-term sustainability. The study examines a portfolio of AI initiatives involving multiple stakeholders, including business leaders, domain experts, technical teams, governance functions, and end users operating across different sectors and geographic regions. The approach focuses on the end-to-end AI delivery lifecycle, from opportunity identification and pilot development to enterprise deployment and operationalization. A structured delivery framework was established incorporating stakeholder engagement, governance alignment, business value definition, agile execution, user enablement, and adoption monitoring. Special attention was given to managing diverse stakeholder expectations, facilitating collaboration between technical and non-technical teams, and ensuring alignment between AI capabilities and business objectives. The framework also emphasizes iterative value realization through continuous feedback loops, performance measurement, and scalable operating models that support expansion across business units and functions. Lessons learned from deployment challenges, adoption barriers, and organizational readiness assessments were systematically analyzed to identify recurring patterns and critical success factors. The findings demonstrate that successful AI scaling is driven less by technological sophistication and more by organizational readiness, stakeholder engagement, and governance maturity. Projects that established clear business outcomes, executive sponsorship, and cross-functional collaboration achieved significantly higher adoption rates and sustained business value compared with technology-centric implementations. The study further highlights the importance of early user involvement, transparent communication, and continuous capability development in building trust and accelerating adoption. Organizations that embedded AI solutions into existing operational workflows experienced smoother transitions from pilot to production and stronger long-term performance outcomes. Across diverse deployment environments, scalability was found to depend on repeatable delivery methodologies, robust governance structures, and the ability to balance innovation with operational requirements. These factors collectively contributed to improved project outcomes, increased organizational confidence in AI technologies, and accelerated digital transformation efforts. The novelty of this work lies in its focus on the often-overlooked transition between AI experimentation and enterprise-scale operationalization. While existing literature primarily emphasizes model development and technical performance, this paper presents a practical delivery-centric perspective based on real-world implementation experiences. The proposed framework integrates governance, stakeholder management, adoption strategies, value realization, and organizational readiness into a unified methodology for scaling AI solutions. The lessons learned provide actionable guidance for organizations seeking to transform AI from isolated innovation initiatives into sustainable enterprise capabilities capable of delivering measurable business

title: AI-Driven Predictive Modeling for Real-Time Drilling Optimization in Extended-Reach Wells: Enabling First Trend-Setting Mile-A-Day Performance for a UAE Operator
container-title: ADIPEC
14482a2060752f3a346cc45bfde99dcc09840f3f.abstract: Abstract Extended-reach wells in onshore fields of Abu Dhabi combine long lateral exposure, thin reservoir targets, and dense interbedded formations, making the selection of drilling parameters a continuous compromise between rate of penetration (ROP), trajectory delivery, and downhole tool reliability. This paper presents the field execution of a machine learning (ML)-driven ROP optimization solution and real-time monitoring workflow deployed in advisory mode on two wells, referred to as Well A and Well B. The objective was to quantify on-bottom ROP gains, drilling time reduction, and economic value under live conditions. ML ROP models were trained on high- and low-frequency historical data from well-specific offset groups. Separate models were developed for rotary steerable system (RSS) and positive displacement motor (PDM) bottomhole assemblies (BHAs) and validated before field use during the proof of concept (PoC) phase. During drilling, the system continuously ingested real-time wellsite information transfer standard markup language (WITSML) data, computed optimum drilling parameter setpoints by depth and formation within limits agreed with the drilling team, and issued targeted adjustments. Across the two wells, more than 59 hours of on-bottom drilling time were saved—a 20% reduction relative to the top-quartile (P75) plan—representing more than USD 208,000 in operational savings. Seven of eight sections exceeded the P75 benchmark, and the 6-in. reservoir section of Well B delivered 5,280 ft in 24 hours, a mile-a-day performance in a thin reservoir target and a first for the operator. The results establish condition-based, data-driven parameter management as a validated bridge from advisory optimization toward end-to-end, closed-loop drilling automation.

title: End-To-End Petrophysical Operations with Agentic AI: A Horizontal Carbonate Reservoir Well Case Study from a Mature Onshore Field, Abu Dhabi
container-title: ADIPEC
726f6f024204d3baddaa0dccb00e7a3076e9f472.abstract: Abstract Petrophysical work follows a well from planning through drilling and into completion, and at each step it usually passes between different specialists, vendor software, and email threads. This paper describes an in-house agentic artificial-intelligence assistant that brings those steps together behind one interface driven by text and voice. The system was validated end to end on a horizontal development well, denoted Well A here for confidentiality, drilled through a heterogeneous carbonate reservoir in a mature onshore field in Abu Dhabi. The assistant runs a fleet of nine configuration-driven skills grouped into two co-equal suites. A planning suite covers a well-data registry, document compilation, logging-program generation, cement-bond evaluation, and a logging-activity dashboard. An operations suite covers a vendor-aware quick-look interpretation pipeline, a production-log checklist automator, a drilling-correspondence router, and an inbox-triage dashboard. The skills chain deterministically: the daily geosteering report is parsed automatically, and the picked subzone tops seed per-zone Archie parameters straight into the log computation. On the case-study well, the planning package was assembled in about five minutes against a typical half-day of manual effort. During drilling, the cycle from a raw real-time log email to a delivered evaluation deck fell from roughly ninety minutes to under four minutes on a cached, scheduled run; the cold-start cycle on a log arriving from the rig for the first time, which is the one that governs how quickly the steering team sees an answer, ran between five and ten minutes. Automated subzone tagging let porosity and saturation cutoffs track a lithology change across adjacent subzones within the same shift, which supported steering decisions. Cement-bond and production-log preparation were completed within the shift the source data arrived. Reliability came from deterministic engineering beneath the language model: the evaluated interval was assembled from separate logging runs across two contractors, and porosity was computed per sample through a two-tier cascade of density-neutron porosity with a sonic fallback. The pipeline output was checked against an independent computer-based interpretation built in commercial petrophysical software on the same well. The petrophysical result is reported as computed, with the well name, reservoir zonation, and depths withheld for confidentiality.

title: AI-Driven Risk-Based Inspection of Offshore Well Conductors
container-title: ADIPEC
dc8a67be598474088f3179417f8dc88f94b7f7f5.abstract: Abstract Offshore well conductors are the outermost structural members of a well. They provide secondary structural support to the surface casing, which remains the primary load-bearing member. In mature fields, conductors are also among the oldest well components still in service. For many years, conductor re-inspection was planned on a fixed calendar basis, mainly linked to age. That approach is simple, but in a mature field it can lead to inefficient inspection planning. This paper describes a condition-based risk-based inspection (RBI) framework developed for one of ADNOC Offshore's mature fields with a large conductor population. The framework uses AI to support the engineering assessment, while remaining aligned with the company's Well Integrity Management System (WIMS) standard for conductor integrity. The framework combines multi-year ultrasonic thickness (UT) survey data with an explainable AI integrity agent. The agent reads the survey files, extracts the governing Minimum Mean Thickness (MMT), and calculates two corrosion rates: one based on total life and one based on the latest inspection interval. It then estimates remaining life against the structurally derived Minimum Required Thickness (MRT) and proposes a revised inspection priority. The priority logic gives proper weight to splash-zone metal loss and to containment indicators such as effluent dripping or an open cement top window. Inspection intervals are then set by condition rather than age. The output remains transparent and is reviewed by an integrity engineer before it is accepted into the register. The framework was applied to just over 500 conductors. The results showed that risk was controlled by actual corrosion condition rather than age alone. Most of the conductors are several decades old, but sound external coating, effective cathodic protection and cemented annuli have kept corrosion rates low. These conductors could therefore be placed on extended inspection intervals. The higher risk was concentrated in a much smaller group, mainly where splash-zone coating had failed or where a containment pathway had opened. The agent output was benchmarked against conventional engineering assessment and against the field's own repair history, and the two agreed closely: the wells the agent ranked highest were, in the main, wells the integrity team had already repaired on its own judgement.
