title: Human-AI Collaboration in Urban Digital Transformation: Balancing Efficiency and Human Values in Shanghai’s AI-Enabled Talent Recruitment
container-title: Digital Technologies Research and Applications
99b2a4d2edc2dc8df689bff6b515848affbe723a.abstract: In the context of the urban digital revolution, recruitment through AI technologies has become common practice to address competition in the labor market. However, it is still unclear how the effectiveness of such recruitment is connected with humanistic values. For this research, an exploratory qualitative research design was used, involving semi-structured interviews with eight human resource professionals in Shanghai. Based on the results, the use of AI in recruitment led to increased efficiency mainly when screening candidates through high-volume, standardized processes, although the promised efficiency was not delivered in practice because the introduction of the AI system increased the workload. Patterns of human-machine cooperation were observed in different companies: tech companies and foreign companies are inclined to adopt interactive adjustment approaches, while state-owned enterprises retain human-dominated decision-making. Transparency of algorithms was still lacking in numerous instances, and there was an asymmetry in the accountability framework of algorithms, wherein disobeying algorithms carries more personal consequences than obeying them. The more experienced professionals became more autonomous in their work, while the less experienced professionals depended more on the algorithm. Issues like management support, information accuracy, and departmental integration have a major impact on implementation. This study contributes to the theory of human-machine collaboration by proposing the concept of asymmetric algorithmic accountability, which captures the uneven distribution of organizational consequences for following versus overriding AI recommendations and shapes practitioner behavior in ways that extend beyond individual trust or algorithmic transparency.

title: Functional reproduction of living heritage in a tea harvest event
container-title: International Journal of Event and Festival Management
101388b7aa513ab07ced05a4b8e31fe1555a83f9.abstract: Purpose This study examines how the Tea Harvest Welcoming Event is interpreted in stakeholder narratives in relation to tea culture, cultural heritage, local identity and future potential. It evaluates a harvest-based local event in terms of the selection, representation, transmission and functional interpretation of cultural heritage. Design/methodology/approach The research was designed as a qualitative case study. Data were collected from stakeholder representatives involved in planning, implementing or evaluating the event through a semi-structured written interview form consisting of open-ended questions. The data were analysed through a theory-driven abductive framework analysis informed by the cultural heritage approach and Malinowski's functional theory of culture. Findings The findings show that the cultural meaning of the event is constructed through the first harvest ritual, meci/imece, producer labour, tea tasting, local music, shared emotions and belonging. In stakeholder narratives, the event is considered a setting that supports the intergenerational transmission of tea culture, the continuity of local identity and renewed engagement with tea. The future of the event is also associated with experiential tea tourism, local economic contribution, institutionalization, stakeholder collaboration and the safeguarding of cultural content. Research limitations/implications This research is based on written interview form responses from stakeholder representatives involved in the planning, implementation or evaluation of the Tea Harvest Welcoming Event. Therefore, the findings reflect the evaluations of stakeholders who were directly connected to the event, rather than the general visitor experience. The collection of data during the post-event evaluation meeting may have increased participants' tendency to provide positive evaluations. In addition, the focus of the research on a single event case requires the findings to be interpreted contextually. Future studies may comparatively examine the experiences of visitors, producers, different segments of residents, tourism businesses and public institutions. The development of the event over time, its contribution to the local economy, its effects on younger generations and the long-term outcomes of tea culture transmission may be evaluated through mixed-method research. Comparisons with different harvest festivals may open a broader discussion on the relationship between programme design, local participation and tourism development in cultural heritage-based events. Originality/value The study combines the selection, representation and transmission processes of the critical heritage approach with Malinowski's functional theory of culture to examine tea culture within a harvest-based organized event. Its original contribution lies in showing how programme elements are associated in stakeholder narratives with functions related to cultural transmission, belonging, experience and tourism value.

title: How artificial intelligence adoption relates to women’s entrepreneurial success in Tunisia
container-title: International Journal of Business and Management (IJBM)
240839ff6fd82ea246285db461aade71b83f333c.abstract: This study examines whether adopting artificial intelligence tools is associated with entrepreneurial success among women entrepreneurs in Tunisia, which business capabilities carry that association, and under what conditions it is stronger. The study uses a cross-sectional survey of 350 women who own, jointly own or principally manage a business that uses at least one AI tool. Respondents were recruited through women’s business associations, incubators and entrepreneurial networks, with quotas by region and sector. The data were analysed with partial least squares structural equation modelling. Four capabilities (operational efficiency, market and customer capability, innovation capacity, and financial readiness) are tested as mediators. Digital skills and institutional support are tested as moderators. AI adoption has a positive direct association with entrepreneurial success (β = 0.200, p < .001). The four specific indirect effects are all positive and sum to 0.330, giving a total effect of 0.530 at mean moderator levels and indicating complementary partial mediation. Market and customer capability is the largest pathway (0.120). Digital skills (interaction β = 0.120, p = .003) and institutional support (interaction β = 0.100, p = .004) both strengthen the direct association. The model explains 62.0% of the variance in entrepreneurial success. Entrepreneurs should start with clearly defined tasks, especially marketing and customer service, and pair adoption with hands-on training. Support organisations can combine tool access with mentoring, practical skills programmes and guidance on responsible data use. The study offers gender-focused evidence on AI and business outcomes in Tunisia, a setting where earlier SME studies do not report results by owner gender. The findings are associations within a sample of AI users and need longitudinal testing before causal claims are made.

title: Digital inventory management systems and the growth of agro farms in Cross River State, Nigeria
container-title: International Journal of Business and Management (IJBM)
429d8bd01c584e4dc82bf9b5a77fd72733534c2a.abstract: Digital technologies are increasingly promoted as a way to improve stock handling and coordination on farms, yet evidence from Nigerian agro farms is limited. This study examines how digital tools, mobile applications, and software systems for inventory control relate to the productivity, profitability, and market expansion of agro farms in Cross River State, Nigeria. A cross sectional survey was conducted between February and August 2025 under a positivist, hypothetico deductive approach. A structured questionnaire with five point Likert items was administered to owners and managers of registered crop, livestock, and mixed farms selected through stratified random sampling, yielding 364 valid responses from 450 distributed. Reliability and construct validity were assessed, and hypotheses were tested using multiple regression at the 5 percent level of significance. The results show that IoT systems and digital monitoring systems are positively associated with productivity, with a reported indirect effect through inventory accuracy. Mobile stock tracking applications, cloud based farm inventory systems, and barcode and QR code applications are positively associated with profitability. Web based inventory platforms and enterprise level digital supply chain software are positively associated with market expansion. The study concludes that digital inventory control systems can support agro farm growth and recommends regular staff training and reliable internet connectivity at farm locations. Because the design is cross sectional and relies on self reported measures, the findings indicate association rather than causation.

title: Rockfall risk management on transportation corridors: coupling risk assessment with terrestrial mobile LiDAR survey on the A22 motorway (South Tyrol, Italy)
container-title: Natural Hazards
180815f0d163a6cac5e4405dd2e94080b9ff9d34.abstract: Abstract This study presents an integrated approach, coupling rockfall risk assessment with a vehicle-based surveying for the large-scale management of slope assets along transportation corridors. Rockfall risk was assessed qualitatively using relative rating scales. To reduce the subjectivity inherent in expert judgment, susceptibility was estimated through probabilistic methods, while vulnerability was informed by conventional runout simulations. Despite the associated uncertainties, the occurrence of a January 2024 rockfall within an area classified as high risk provides independent qualitative support for the consistency of the first-level screening results. Terrestrial Mobile LiDAR (TML) survey conducted from a car was designed to maximise effectiveness and efficiency in capturing rockfall-prone slopes and establishing a baseline for long-term monitoring. Its actual effectiveness, efficiency, potential and limitations were evaluated through a survey conducted in April 2023. Approximately 3.5 km of the A22 motorway, representing more than one-quarter of the analysed section, were found to be potentially exposed to rockfall risk, originating from 27 of the 55 identified potential detachment zones. The TML survey successfully detected over 70% of these zones, achieving a point density potentially sufficient to identify volumes greater than approximately 10 dm 3 . The scanning was constrained by morphological conditions, such as vertical slopes adjacent to the motorway, structural obstacles, such as tunnel portals, and the instrument’s maximum range of 475 m. Despite these limitations, the quality and accuracy of the acquired data indicate that the TML can effectively support the motorway operators in large-scale rockfall risk management.

title: From AI readiness to regenerative tourism orientation: a tourist-centric model of smart tourism villages
container-title: ABAC Journal
600067ed573dc780c1bd155c47ed81d59d2f7b38.abstract: Purpose This study develops and validates a tourist-centric model of AI-driven smart tourism villages (AI-DSTV), explaining how perceived digital infrastructure and smart governance relate to tourist acceptance and perceived regenerative tourism orientation (PRTO) through rural authenticity, value co-creation, AI trust, and perceived service value. Design/methodology/approach A cross-sectional survey involved 686 domestic tourists who had experienced an AI-supported tourism touchpoint in rural tourism settings in Indonesia. The sample was predominantly young and digitally engaged, with 75.1% aged 18–24 and 68.4% students. The model was tested using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) with 10,000 bootstrap resamples and importance-performance map analysis (IPMA). Findings All 12 hypothesized relationships were significant. Rural authenticity strongly enhanced perceived AI service value, while tourist value co-creation strengthened AI trust and ethical acceptance. Digital infrastructure and smart governance also showed significant downstream effects through authenticity–service-value and co-creation–trust pathways. The model explained 56.3% of PRTO variance. IPMA identified AI trust and ethical acceptance as the most important antecedent of PRTO and the lowest-performing construct, indicating a key managerial priority. Practical implications Rural destinations should prioritize transparent, culturally grounded, participatory and locally accountable AI systems. Strengthening ethical trust, co-creation, and culturally appropriate personalization may offer greater managerial leverage than technological sophistication alone. Originality/value The study extends technology-adoption research beyond behavioral acceptance by introducing PRTO as a tourist-level psychological outcome. It conceptualizes AI-DSTV as a socio-technical ecosystem linking destination readiness with authenticity, co-creation, trust and service evaluation while distinguishing regenerative orientation from verified destination regeneration.

title: Linking green entrepreneurship to green innovation: the mediating role of green entrepreneurial self-efficacy
container-title: African Journal of Economic and Management Studies
56d99d620c7bd84d2c10aab08611ed68af39c4be.abstract: Purpose In line with the United Nations 2030 Agenda, environmental sustainability has become a prominent concept in academic discourse. Due to its vast natural resources, Africa is well-positioned to become a global leader in green business. However, with a growing small and medium-sized enterprise (SME)population in Africa, empirical evidence on SME sustainability efforts remains limited. For this reason, this research examined the mediation effect of green entrepreneurial self-efficacy on the relationship between green entrepreneurship and green innovation in Zimbabwean manufacturing SMEs. Design/methodology/approach The data were analysed using SmartPLS 4 from a randomly selected sample of 370 managers. Findings The results showed that while green entrepreneurship strongly influenced green innovation, green entrepreneurial self-efficacy partially mediated the relationship between the two variables. Originality/value The study contributes context-specific evidence from an African economy, addressing the limited representation of developing markets in green innovation research. In environments characterised by institutional constraints and resource scarcity, identifying self-efficacy as an enabling mechanism provides novel insight into how firms can stimulate green innovation despite structural limitations. The findings, therefore, enrich both theory and practice by integrating strategic and psychological perspectives within the African economic context.

title: How scene features activate customer behaviour transformation in metaverse retailing
container-title: International Journal of Retail & Distribution Management
1248ff41cb9b7bcd09ed8e17927ea7c23d1e315a.abstract: Purpose As a crucial nexus between technological innovation and customer experience within the metaverse, effectively designed scene features represent a vital source of competitive advantage in retail. However, current research focuses narrowly on either technology or consumer perceptions, overlooking the integration between the two and resulting in limited effectiveness in consumer retention. To bridge this gap, this study develops and tests an integrated model of metaverse retail scene features. Design/methodology/approach Grounding in the Stimulus-Organism-Response (S-O-R) framework, the model integrates the Design-Ambient-Social-Trialability (DAST) dimensions, to specify the environmental Stimulus. It incorporates the customer inspiration mechanism (Organism) and the variable of immersive time to explicate the psychological process leading to behavioural Responses. The proposed relationships are examined through two experiments. Findings The results demonstrate that: (1) six scene features, i.e. Visual appeal, Navigability, Informativeness, Novelty, Embodied co-presence and Trialability, significantly enhance purchase intention, pleasure and loyalty; (2) the customer inspiration process, sequentially moving from inspired-by to inspired-to, fully mediates these effects; (3) the immersive time positively moderates the impact of Informativeness, Embodied Co-presence and Trialability on the initial inspired-by stage. Originality/value This study contributes a novel, time-adaptive strategy for metaverse retail. It reveals that scene features exert differential influence based on exposure duration, suggesting prioritizing visual appeal and novelty for initial engagement, then leveraging deeper informational and social features for sustained immersion. By deconstructing multidimensional scenes, it offers actionable design principles for virtual retail spaces.

title: White coats in the news feed: the effects of content features on physicians' engagement behaviors in online academic medical communities
container-title: Aslib Journal of Information Management
7353f574ac1fb297470e88c542e86cf0e544ddfd.abstract: Purpose Online academic medical communities (OAMCs) have become central channels for physicians to exchange medical knowledge. Yet a substantial share of physician-generated medical content on these platforms fails to elicit meaningful peer engagement, constraining the dissemination of medical knowledge. Given that the intrinsic features of content in OAMCs are likely key drivers of peer engagement, understanding what makes content appealing is essential. However, the relationship remains unclear. This study aims to address this gap by examining how distinct content features influence different forms of peer engagement in OAMCs. Design/methodology/approach Leveraging data from a leading Chinese OAMC, we operationalize six content features (complexity, subjectivity, professionalism, completeness, informativeness, multimodal information presentation) via natural language processing and examine their effects on physicians' collecting and interacting behaviors and the moderating role of disease severity. Findings Peer physicians prioritize information-rich content for collecting, while favoring discussion-oriented content for interacting. Multimodal, comprehensive content is welcomed, whereas overly sophisticated, highly specialized content is less effective. Disease severity moderates these relationships, with physicians exhibiting greater selectivity in collecting but more interactive under high-severity conditions. Originality/value This study is among the first to uncover the impact of content features on physicians' engagement behaviors while considering disease severity as the moderating variable. By incorporating natural language processing techniques, it extends the information adoption model to online physician platforms and offers actionable guidance for optimizing physician online engagement.

title: CryptoBooks: next-generation library management with NFTs and blockchain technology
container-title: Library Management
fadd109a47b88039ffeefbd5430efab42ad18e5e.abstract: Purpose This study proposes CryptoBooks, a novel framework integrating cryptographic hashing and blockchain-based non-fungible tokens (NFTs) to ensure document authenticity, ownership and integrity in digital library environments. Design/methodology/approach A design science research approach is adopted to develop and demonstrate a prototype system combining SHA-512 hashing, InterPlanetary File System storage and Ethereum-based NFT minting. The workflow is implemented using Python scripting, decentralized storage and smart contract deployment via Remix Integrated Development Environment (IDE). Findings The prototype demonstrates that digital documents can be transformed into immutable, verifiable assets with embedded cryptographic fingerprints and decentralized ownership records. The system ensures tamper-evident verification, transparent provenance tracking and independent authentication without reliance on centralized authorities. Mapping the framework against established authenticity criteria shows that its three components correspond to the content, agent and time of creation of a record. Practical implications The framework supports digital preservation, forgery prevention and verifiable credentialing in academic libraries. Seven applications are identified, including provenance for special collections, priority claims in academic integrity disputes and mitigation of reference rot. A staged adoption roadmap is proposed whose first stage requires no distributed ledger and no expenditure. Originality/value While cryptographic hashing combined with token-based ownership is established in other sectors, this study is among the first to adapt the approach to document-level authentication in libraries and to map its components onto the conditions of authenticity codified in archival science.

title: Exploring the capability–experience–satisfaction (CES) pathway in omnichannel retailing
container-title: International Journal of Retail & Distribution Management
a5a3277b617e80101dad04844933aac95e8e18f5.abstract: Purpose This study proposes that fulfilment, fluency and flexibility represent the consequences of omnichannel capability and act as key drivers of journey satisfaction. The study also examines whether journey satisfaction affects broader retailer-level customer satisfaction over time. Design/methodology/approach This study utilised a multi-method design combining survey and experimental data. Structural equation modelling and PROCESS analyses were based on survey data from 420 customers with omnichannel shopping experience. To provide supplementary evidence for the proposed pathway, an additional experimental study was conducted with 80 participants, and the results were analysed using logistic regression. Findings Results showed that omnichannel capability had positive effects on fulfilment, fluency and flexibility, which, in turn, had positive effects on journey satisfaction. Longitudinal analysis showed that journey satisfaction at T0 had a positive effect on broader retailer-level customer satisfaction at T1 one year later. Originality/value This study emphasises the importance of omnichannel capability in understanding customer satisfaction over time. It develops and examines the capability–experience–satisfaction pathway. Findings suggest that omnichannel capability should be managed as an integrated organisational capability supporting journey experiences, satisfaction and broader customer satisfaction over time.

title: Effect of Peer Support on Resilience and Emotional Regulation among University Students: Mediating Role of Stress Management
container-title: Pakistan Journal of Positive Psychology
53ce23fed5f142af05f503c93a58c00782a943b3.abstract: This current study was carried out to analyze the impact of peer support on resilience and emotional regulation in university students considering the mediating influence of stress management. Quantitative correlational research approach with a convenient sampling technique was used for the current study. Information was gathered from 150 university students of Pakistan (n = 81 males and n = 69 females) with ages between 18-27 years using standardized measures: Friend subscale of the multidimensional scale of perceived social support (MSPSS), perceived stress scale (PSS-10), brief resilience scale (BRS), and emotional regulation questionnaire (ERQ). Pearson correlation, regression analysis and mediation analysis using bootstrapping approach was performed. It was found that peer support had a significant positive effect on emotional regulation (B = .34, p < .001), however, its direct effect on resilience was not significant. Most importantly, stress management partially mediated the link between peer support and resilience (B = .39, p < .05) as well as emotional regulation (B = .32, p < .05). The current study underscores the important significance of peer support network along with stress management interventions in enhancing psychological well-being of university students.

title: Running sustainably: how ESG practices at non-mega sport events foster residents' value co-creation and support for sustainable development
container-title: International Journal of Event and Festival Management
1633fabf3780be7cf5f34861e3c2aaf60ed42de0.abstract: Purpose This study examines how residents' event-related environmental, social and governance (ESG) perceptions at a recurring non-mega sport event influence their value co-creation intentions and support for sustainable destination and event development, and the moderating role of place attachment in this process. Design/methodology/approach A structured questionnaire survey was conducted with 417 residents two weeks prior to the 2026 Wuhan Marathon. Partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) in SmartPLS 4.1 was used to test the hypothesised direct, mediating and moderating relationships. Social embeddedness theory and the value-belief-norm (VBN) perspective served as the theoretical foundation. Findings Event-related ESG perceptions significantly and positively predicted both value co-creation intentions (β = 0.606) and support for sustainable destination and event development (β = 0.720). In the main model, value co-creation intentions positively predicted support (β = 0.213) and partially mediated the ESG-support relationship. Place attachment significantly but negatively moderated the ESG-value co-creation relationship, indicating a weaker link among highly attached residents, consistent with a place-based norm saturation pattern. The moderation of ESG on support was non-significant. Originality/value This study is among the first to conceptualise and empirically test event-related ESG perceptions from a resident standpoint in a non-mega sport event context. By integrating social embeddedness theory with the VBN perspective, it positions resident co-creation as a potential social licence mechanism through which ESG-oriented events gain community legitimacy, and offers a tentative, exploratory interpretation of place-based norm saturation as a possible explanation for the unexpected negative moderating role of place attachment.

title: Management of a Shared-Meal Culture in the Free Nutritious Meal Program Based on Islamic Values to Strengthen Students’ Empathy and Solidarity
container-title: Journal of General Education and Humanities
f5395a41cac6d664c5f85dc1548bc5615bb55b0f.abstract: This study aims to analyze the management of a shared-meal culture within the Free Nutritious Meal Program (Program Makan Bergizi Gratis/MBG) based on Islamic values and its contribution to strengthening students’ empathy and solidarity. The study employed a qualitative method with an exploratory analytical approach. The research was conducted at SDN 1 Bodak, Central Lombok Regency, involving 20 fifth- and seventh-grade students selected purposively as informants. Data were collected through participant observation, in-depth interviews with the principal, homeroom teachers, and students, as well as documentation. Data were analyzed using the Miles and Huberman interactive model, comprising data collection, data condensation, data display, and conclusion drawing and verification. The findings indicate that the management of the shared-meal culture was implemented in a structured and organized manner through scheduled activities, food inspection, meal distribution, collective prayer, shared meals, practices of sharing, and habituation of cleanliness and responsibility. These practices integrated Islamic values of religiosity, ta’awun (mutual assistance), ukhuwah (brotherhood), care, and togetherness into students’ daily activities. The shared-meal culture also created a social interaction space that encouraged students to help one another, pay attention to their peers’ conditions, share food, and develop closer interpersonal relationships. The findings suggest that the shared-meal culture within the MBG Program has the potential to serve as an Islamic educational management practice that integrates nutritional fulfillment with social character development, particularly the strengthening of students’ empathy and solidarity.

title: Preventive Health and Health Services Block Grant Flexible Funding Mechanism Is Associated With Improved Population Outcomes
container-title: Journal of Public Health Management & Practice
ca9aa732d02416dce45613faa7492f4401754f32.abstract: ABSTRACT Objectives: To investigate the association between Preventive Health and Health Services (PHHS) Block Grant (BG) funding and population health outcomes. Design: A state-level panel data set (2000–2019) for 50 US states was compiled from USA Spending, PHHS BG administrative system, US Census Bureau, and America's Health Rankings. The long-term population health outcome was years of life lost (YLL), measured as deaths before age 75 years per 100 000 population. We used a generalized method of moments (GMM), along with a Koyck distributed lag model and a 2-way fixed-effects approach, to assess the impact of PHHS BG funding on YLL. We also provided several sensitivity analyses. Setting: This study examines the effects of PHHS Block Grant flexible funding on the population health outcomes during the period of 2000–2019. Participants: Fifty US States were included in the study. Main Outcome Measure: YLL before age 75, per 100 000 population. Results: During 2000–2019, a $1 per capita increase in PHHS BG funding was associated with a 1.5%–11% reduction in YLL (110–832 fewer years lost per 100 000 population). Conclusions: Increasing use of PHHS BG funds is associated with substantial years of life savings.

title: High Use, Low Preparation
container-title: American Journal of Physical Medicine & Rehabilitation
cd596e36835769e8c758e2939412febb985e5034.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (Gen-AI) has rapidly entered clinical environments, posing a risk of “cognitive offloading” that may impede the development of independent clinical judgment. This study conducted a cross-sectional survey of residents, fellows, and faculty at a large academic medical center in January 2026 to quantify Gen-AI utilization and perceptions in physical medicine and rehabilitation (PM&R) to inform curriculum development. Thirty-six trainees (95% response rate) and 11 faculty members (30% response rate) completed the survey; 43 (91.5%) reported any Gen-AI use and formed the analytic sample. Among users, 72.1% used Gen-AI daily for clinical learning and 51.2% during patient encounters, yet 67.4% were self-taught and only 7.0% always requested citations. Trainees requested citations more often than faculty ( P =.048), while faculty more often relied on clinical judgment without additional verification (62.5% vs. 25.7%, P =.089). Gen-AI-derived evidence was rarely surfaced in teaching: 60.5% discussed it during case presentations rarely or never, and only 16.2% always disclosed its origin. Residents are integrating Gen-AI into clinical workflows at rates that outpace faculty familiarity, while verification remains largely undiscussed and untaught. These gaps highlight an urgent need for structured Gen-AI curricula in PM&R residency.

title: Orchestrating inter-organizational technology networks to build data analytics capability: the case of a professional service firm
container-title: International Journal of Operations & Production Management
c4350ce1bf2699b1f1cb84ae4e32a8f2c2e74169.abstract: Purpose This study examines how professional service firms (PSFs) orchestrate inter-organizational technology networks to develop data analytics capability. Adopting an organizational information processing perspective, we examine how PSFs vary orchestration modes across networks to mobilize distributed resources and increase their information-processing capacity. Design/methodology/approach We conducted a longitudinal single-case study of a global PSF in the UK construction sector, triangulating 37 interviews with observations and project documentation. Using an abductive theory-elaboration approach, we explain how the PSF accessed, bundled and leveraged network-embedded resources to build analytics capability. Findings We identify three interrelated components of analytics capability: data capture, data transformation and processing, and data visualization and interpretation. Closed-mode orchestration enabled standardized data capture across the supply network; hybrid orchestration combined broad open engagement with selective closure to integrate technological expertise from SMEs; and open-mode orchestration within the client network fostered use-case elicitation, sensemaking and interpretive alignment. We theorize how inter-organizational network orchestration enables PSFs to assemble information-processing capacity from distributed data, technical expertise and interpretive requirements, thereby improving fit between information-processing needs and capacity. Originality/value We conceptualize analytics capability as a composite inter-organizational capability assembled across organizational boundaries. We extend Organizational information processing theory by showing how information-processing capacity can be assembled across networks of external actors through inter-organizational network orchestration, and advance network orchestration research by identifying a contingency logic linking orchestration mode to the coordination conditions surrounding distributed resources.

title: Ecocentric approach for knowledge management and eco-conscious open innovation for a circular economy: leveraging intellectual capital
container-title: Journal of Enterprise Information Management
686c261491946be26d24c79772bd44511d29dc4d.abstract: Purpose The transition toward a circular economy (CE) requires organizations to develop environmentally responsible innovation practices; however, limited research has explained how knowledge management (KM) practices facilitate eco-conscious open innovation (EOI), particularly within small and medium-sized manufacturing enterprises (SMEs) in emerging economies. Furthermore, the role of intellectual capital (IC) as an underlying mechanism linking the ecocentric approach to KM with EOI remains underexplored. Therefore, this study examines the mediating role of IC dimensions in the relationship between the ecocentric approach to KM and EOI among manufacturing SMEs in Pakistan. Drawing on the resource-based view (RBV), knowledge-based view (KBV), and intellectual capital-based view (ICBV), the study explains how environmentally oriented knowledge practices are transformed into sustainable innovation outcomes. Design/methodology/approach Data were collected from 398 respondents employed in manufacturing SMEs in Pakistan. PLS-SEM using SmartPLS 4.0.9 was employed to test the proposed relationships and examine the mediating role of IC dimensions in the ecocentric KM–EOI relationship. Findings The findings reveal that IC dimensions fully mediate the relationship between the ecocentric approach to KM and EOI. The results further indicate that the ecocentric approach to KM enhances human, structural, and relational capital, which subsequently promote inbound and outbound EOI. The direct effects of the ecocentric approach to KM on EOI became insignificant when IC dimensions were included, whereas the corresponding indirect effects remained significant, confirming full mediation. Originality/value This study contributes to the literature by extending understanding of the ecocentric approach to KM within the CE context and by identifying IC as a critical mechanism through which environmentally oriented knowledge practices contribute to EOI. By integrating RBV, KBV and ICBV, the study offers a comprehensive theoretical explanation of the KM–EOI relationship. Moreover, evidence from Pakistani manufacturing SMEs provides insights from an underexplored emerging-economy context and offers practical implications for organizations seeking to strengthen intellectual capital and advance eco-conscious innovation for circular economy objectives.

title: Development of an Integrated Aided Language Stimulation (ALS) Intervention Model to Improve Expressive Communication in Autistic Children at UPTD Disability Services Sidoarjo
container-title: Journal of General Education and Humanities
b7b0d11d53ab60f86fec6738c0cba48871fcc2a1.abstract: Children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) often experience difficulties in expressive communication, including requesting, responding, expressing needs, initiating interaction, and maintaining communication. This study aimed to develop an Intervention Model Integrated Aided Language Stimulation (ALS) with Augmentative and Alternative Communication (AAC) to support expressive communication among autistic children at UPTD Services Disability Sidoarjo, Indonesia. The study employed a Research and Development approach using the Four-D model comprising Define, Design, Develop, and Disseminate stages. The developed model integrated AAC media, ALS language modeling, functional communication activities, communication opportunities, partner responsiveness, reinforcement, generalization, and evaluation. Expert validation involved four validators representing four areas of expertise: subject matter, special education/autism, communication/AAC, and media. The validation percentage was calculated by dividing the obtained score by the maximum possible score and multiplying by 100%, resulting in 90.5% (very valid). Practicality was assessed through responses from teachers, therapists, and/or companions using the same percentage formula, resulting in 90% (very practical), while implementation was assessed through structured observation and reached 91% (very good). A one-group pretest-posttest limited trial involving five autistic children showed an increase in expressive communication scores from 42/100 (mean = 4.2) to 76/100 (mean = 7.6). The mean N-Gain was 0.65, categorized as moderate improvement according to the study criteria. Because the limited trial involved only five children and did not include a control group, the observed improvement should not be interpreted as definitive evidence of intervention effectiveness. Overall, the findings support the model’s feasibility for further investigation with larger samples and more rigorous comparative designs.

title: Strategic integration of business intelligence tools to enhance business management efficiency
container-title: Journal of Innovative Digital Transformation
15aaaabce800370f4d4f3fa8c96a859b42098edb.abstract: Purpose This study examines how data and business intelligence (BI) systems support procurement decisions and strategic execution. It aims to improve the efficiency of business management. Design/methodology/approach A five-stage implementation framework is proposed for integrating BI into strategic business execution. The methodology includes technical validation and a case study that assesses the impact of digital transformation and BI adoption on tracking strategic execution and key performance indicators (KPIs). We frame BI adoption within the broader digital transformation (DT) agenda, aligning data, processes and governance to strategic objectives. Findings Research shows that aligning digital transformation initiatives with an organization’s specific operational needs is the most cost-effective path to achieving efficiency. Analysis suggests that a successful digital transformation must be closely linked to the management requirements. Selecting appropriate BI tools is critical to delivering substantial business value. Research limitations/implications The proposed framework offers managers a structured approach to implementing BI systems aligned with strategic goals. The case study provides actionable insights for professionals aiming to improve operational and management performance through data-driven strategies and digital transformation. Originality/value The research contributes to the literature on digital transformation by presenting a structured, stage-gated framework for integrating BI tools into strategic management. It offers practical guidance for organizations seeking to enhance performance through data-informed decision-making, differentiating itself through a detailed implementation model developed and illustrated in a procurement context.

title: Sales growth conditions the relationship between cost management and business liquidity
container-title: F1000Research
bd05ec969105682ef37608ac53b4705a257797ee.abstract: Background Cost management and business liquidity are determinants of the stability of industrial firms, but little is known about how it depends on the commercial context. It was determined whether cost management influences the liquidity of an industrial firm in Pomalca, Peru (2011–2025), under the moderating effect of inventory turnover and sales growth. Methods An applied, quantitative, non-experimental, longitudinal and correlational-explanatory study with the financial statements of the firm (2011–2025, census sampling, n = 15), analyzed by means of a documentary file and linear regression with robust HAC/Newey-West errors in R 4.6.1. Results Cost management did not show a direct effect on current liquidity (β = 0.072; p = 0.146), but its interaction with sales growth was significant (β = 0.001; p = 0.009). Current liquidity, acid test, and net working capital significantly influenced cost management (p = 0.043; 0.040; 0.003), moderated by sales growth (adjusted R 2 64.0%–68.9%). Conclusions Cost management does not directly influence liquidity; its effect only appears with sales growth, while liquidity does directly influence cost management, which functions as a limiting condition of this relationship.

title: Effectiveness of Behavioural Intervention Regarding Anaemia and Its Prevention among Postnatal Mothers: An Interventional Study
12fe6a2e92fb5e2910df896caf3494d377c35d3c.abstract: Abstract Anaemia is a public-health concern that may persist after childbirth and affect maternal recovery and well-being. This study assessed the effectiveness of a behavioural intervention regarding anaemia and its prevention among postnatal mothers. A quantitative approach and quasi-experimental one-group pre-test–post-test design were used in the postnatal unit of Jalpaiguri Government Medical College and Hospital, West Bengal. Of 83 mothers initially enrolled/interviewed, 55 postnatal mothers with haemoglobin below 11 g/dL were included in the final analysis. Knowledge was assessed before and after structured teaching, and haemoglobin was reassessed 30–42 days after delivery. The mean knowledge score increased from 15.45 (SD 3.37) to 19.69 (SD 1.76), with a statistically significant difference (paired t=8.27, df=54, p<0.001). Mean haemoglobin increased from 9.55 (SD 0.98) g/dL at first contact to 10.72 (SD 0.75) g/dL at follow-up (paired t=10.444, df=54, p<0.001). At follow-up, 25 mothers (45.45%) had haemoglobin levels of at least 11 g/dL. The findings indicate improved knowledge and haemoglobin levels between baseline and follow-up. Because the study had no control group, the haemoglobin change cannot be attributed to the intervention alone. Structured teaching may support postnatal care alongside appropriate treatment, nutrition and follow-up.

title: Digital health misinformation in Southeast Asia: a systematic review of susceptibility, public health consequences, and intervention evidence
container-title: Frontiers in Public Health
1c958c1db51f20b8c7d600471373d90ab013a16b.abstract: Background Digital health misinformation forms part of the information environment in which people assess health risks and act on health advice. We systematically reviewed participant-level studies from Southeast Asia addressing susceptibility, public-health consequences, and intervention evidence. Methods We searched PubMed, Europe PMC, Web of Science Core Collection, and Scopus, supplemented by known reports from the original manuscript and publication-version checks. Prespecified eligibility criteria required primary empirical research involving Southeast Asian populations, an explicit health-misinformation focus, a documented digital connection, and participant-level outcomes. The search and selection process was reported according to PRISMA 2020. Methodological quality was assessed using the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool (MMAT 2018). Heterogeneity in study designs, measures, and outcomes precluded meta-analysis; findings were synthesized narratively. Results The searches identified 2,210 database records; 1,142 remained after deduplication. Including supplementary identification, 282 reports were sought, 147 were assessed in full text, and 77 reports were included, representing 74 conservatively grouped study populations. Country-attributable evidence came from Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, the Philippines, Thailand, Vietnam, and Lao PDR; two further reports provided regional findings. Fifty-four reports concerned COVID-19. Appraisal and belief were associated with cognition, literacy, trust, identity, emotion, and social context, although measures and sampling differed considerably. Findings linked misinformation-related constructs with sharing, vaccine attitudes, preventive behavior, distress, and accounts of delayed care. Correction, inoculation, digital education, chatbots, and community responses produced heterogeneous findings; most interventions did not isolate a misinformation-specific behavioral effect. Discussion Interpretation is limited by 135 unretrieved reports, a single assessment workflow without independent duplicate human screening, and predominantly observational evidence. The regional literature supports context-sensitive interpretation of exposure, appraisal, belief, and action; it does not establish a uniform causal pathway or a preferred intervention transferable across all settings.

title: Trust in artificial intelligence and AI-assisted social and civic decision-making among Arab youth: evidence from Egypt, Kuwait, and the UAE
container-title: Frontiers in Sociology
9c22c48dec77add12e18981832964c2f183e35aa.abstract: Introduction Trust in artificial intelligence (AI) increasingly shapes how young people evaluate information and public issues, yet evidence from Arab contexts remains limited. This study examined the socio-technical correlates of trust in AI and its association with AI-assisted social and civic decision-making among digitally engaged youth in Egypt, Kuwait, and the United Arab Emirates. Methods A cross-sectional online survey was conducted with 1,023 respondents aged 18–35 recruited through purposive, non-probability sampling. Confirmatory factor analysis (CFA), structural equation modeling (SEM), multi-group CFA, and competing full- versus partial-mediation models evaluated measurement and structural relationships. Results The partially mediated model fit significantly better than the fully mediated model, Δχ2(5) = 55.66, p &lt; 0.001. Institutional confidence (β = 0.303), AI literacy (β = 0.281), perceived usefulness (β = 0.242), and social influence (β = 0.107) were positively associated with trust in AI, and perceived risk was negatively associated (β = −0.106; all p &lt; 0.001). Trust was positively associated with AI-assisted decision-making (β = 0.412, p &lt; 0.001). Significant indirect associations through trust were observed for all five antecedents, while the direct perceived-risk path to AI-assisted decision-making was nonsignificant. Multi-group CFA supported metric and practical scalar measurement invariance across the three countries. Discussion The findings support a socio-technical account of AI trust in which technological, cognitive, institutional, and social conditions jointly relate to AI-assisted decision-making, with trust functioning as a central but not exclusive pathway. Given the cross-sectional, purposive design, findings are interpreted as associations rather than causal or nationally representative effects.

title: Recommendations for the primary care management of post COVID and post acute infectious syndrome: a comparative analysis of international guidelines
container-title: Frontiers in Medicine
db7227e9bdc1cf159fd5b323f796188d8e34dd14.abstract: The medical care of people with post COVID syndrome (PCS) and other post-acute infectious syndromes (PAIS) remains a major challenge as dedicated care structures are scarce, diagnostic evaluation is often complex, and curative therapies are largely lacking. General practitioners play an essential role in initial assessment and the coordination of care and treatment. However, standardized and evidence-based recommendations specifically tailored to primary care are scarce. This study aimed to analyze and compare diagnostic and therapeutic recommendations for primary care of PCS from international guidelines. Six guidelines and recommendations were included, originating from Germany, Switzerland, the United Kingdom, the United States, the WHO, and a European scientific society. The analysis revealed considerable variation in scope, level of detail and practical applicability. Most guidelines recommend symptom-based or exclusionary diagnostic approaches. Non-pharmacological interventions such as rehabilitation, self-management and psychological support are commonly addressed. In contrast, pharmacological options are rarely specified due to limited evidence. While the importance of general practitioners is acknowledged across documents, specific support structures and implementation strategies vary. To date, structured care recommendations for patients with Long COVID and other PAIS in primary care remain limited.

title: A preliminary design framework for human-friendly AI interaction: grounded in anthropomorphism
container-title: Frontiers in Computer Science
46e7d698557d6ad9c8af0e26c30db1eac6a6fb1b.abstract: People converse with AI as they would with friends in daily life, collaborate with it, and form personalized relationships. In response to these emerging forms of interaction, this study clarifies the concept of Human-Friendly Interaction with conversational AI and develops the Human-Friendly AI Interaction Design Framework (HFAI-DF). This study positions anthropomorphism, a foundational phenomenon in human–AI interaction, as a theoretical bridge and reviews literature on anthropomorphism theory and related research on human cognition. On this basis, this study interpretively derives and organizes how anthropomorphism-inducing stimuli can be applied to AI agents, systematizing them into 30 AI behavioral items that enable human-friendly interaction. Subsequently, a survey was conducted and exploratory factor analysis performed to identify six dimensions as a preliminary structure for a design framework for AI’s human-friendly interaction. These dimensions are: Self-Aware Interaction, User-Adaptive Responsiveness Interaction, Context-Aware Reasoning Interaction, Socio-Emotional Interaction, Creative Collaboration Interaction, and Proactive Assistance Interaction. Within the evolving AI research landscape focused on interaction, this study extends the human-centered AI concept toward human-friendly interaction that operates in an organic manner comparable to human–human conversation, grounded in an understanding of human cognitive functioning. The proposed framework provides both AI providers and designers with an initial structure for shaping and improving the quality of human-friendly interaction.

title: Perceptions of AI in veterinary medicine: insights from students, faculty, and practicing veterinarians in Hong Kong
container-title: Frontiers in Veterinary Science
d5c0bfa269240bf48c6ea87f212741cd8f464ca1.abstract: Introduction As artificial intelligence (AI) transforms veterinary medicine, understanding stakeholder perceptions is crucial for its effective and responsible integration. To support the development of targeted educational and policy initiatives, this study aimed to evaluate the knowledge, attitudes, and practices regarding AI among Bachelor of Veterinary Medicine (BVM) students, PhD students, faculty, and practicing veterinarians in Hong Kong. Methods A cross-sectional online survey was conducted between December 2023 and March 2024 among BVM students, PhD students, and faculty members at City University of Hong Kong, and practicing veterinarians in Hong Kong who are members of the Hong Kong Veterinary Association. The survey assessed participants’ familiarity with AI, prior training, perceived benefits, concerns, and willingness to adopt AI in education and clinical practice. Descriptive and comparative analyses were performed to examine differences across stakeholder groups. Results Of 79 complete responses, nearly half (46.8%) reported unfamiliarity with AI concepts. Only 17.7% had received formal AI training, although 78.5% expressed interest in future AI education. Most respondents agreed that AI could enhance veterinary teaching and practice (83.5%) and 81.0% indicated they would likely incorporate AI tools into their work. Key perceived benefits included support for case-based learning (83.5%), virtual animal models for teaching (77.2%), and improved diagnostic accuracy (74.7%). However, 41.8% felt inadequately prepared to use AI. Major concerns included veterinarian accountability for AI-related harms (79.7%), lack of system flexibility (75.9%), and potential clinical inaccuracies (70.9%). Descriptively, practicing veterinarians reported the lowest AI tool use (66.7% had never used AI tools), the lowest preparedness (66.7% felt unprepared), and lower agreement with AI’s clinical benefits, although attitude differences were not statistically significant. Conclusion These exploratory findings suggest gaps in self-reported AI knowledge and differing perceptions of AI across veterinary stakeholder groups in Hong Kong, with AI use already widespread at the time of the survey despite limited formal training. While enthusiasm for AI integration is high, concerns about preparedness, accuracy, and ethical responsibility remain. Larger, multi-institutional studies are needed to confirm these patterns and to inform targeted training programs and ethical frameworks for safe and effective AI adoption in veterinary medicine.

title: Multilevel needs and perceived implementation challenges of mHealth for community frailty management: a qualitative study guided by the Fogg Behavior Model
container-title: Frontiers in Public Health
1bb8627d4c51dcc514b6d3fc4038460198138666.abstract: Background Frailty is an important public health challenge in ageing populations and increasingly requires community-based approaches to prevention and management. Mobile health (mHealth) technologies may support health education, self-management, monitoring, and continuity of care among older adults with pre-frailty or frailty. However, successful implementation depends not only on technological usability but also on behavioral, interpersonal, and health-system factors. Evidence regarding these factors from the perspectives of both older adults and community healthcare professionals remains limited. Objective This study aimed to explore the needs and perceived implementation challenges associated with mHealth for community frailty management from the perspectives of older adults with pre-frailty or frailty and community healthcare professionals, and to interpret these factors using the Fogg Behavior Model (FBM). Methods An exploratory qualitative study was conducted using semi-structured face-to-face interviews with 15 community-dwelling older adults with pre-frailty or frailty and 10 community HCPs. Data were analyzed using a hybrid inductive–deductive thematic analysis approach. Results Seven empirically derived subthemes were developed inductively and subsequently organized into three higher-order interpretive domains corresponding to the FBM dimensions of motivation, ability, and prompts. (1) health-oriented motivation was constrained by limited awareness of frailty and insufficient trust in digital health information; (2) individuals and the primary healthcare system jointly constituted multilevel ability barriers; and (3) mHealth engagement was perceived to depend on complementary action cues and social support. Conclusion Participants perceived the implementation of mHealth in community frailty management as being shaped by interacting factors related to motivation, ability, and prompts. To optimize implementation, attention should be paid to age-friendly design, trustworthy digital health information, frailty and digital health competencies among community HCPs, and coordinated support from family members and healthcare professionals.

title: Global classrooms: a tri-national study on AI integration by higher education students
container-title: Frontiers in Computer Science
4ce5be4917c40263b11f6c7ca8eabe77dd89211a.abstract: Collaborative cross-cultural learning expands higher education students’ (HES’) intercultural and language awareness, enhances their intercultural competence, has an impact on attitudes towards technology and AI as well as towards the course design and general satisfaction with the collaborative experience in the course. Furthermore, their self-perceived role in a digital setting and their self-perceived English proficiency were measured. The CoGIH Project encourages HES to explore the educational potential of artificial intelligence (AI) for learning and teaching in the school setting. A special focus is on the impact AI might have on the language learning process in English as a lingua franca in a multilingual setting. N = 113 HES, including both pre-service and in-service teachers as well as students preparing for educational administration, from five institutions in Israel, Germany, and Hungary collaborated in 14 international groups, representing five higher education institutions; n = 91 answered the questionnaires. Each group investigated the educational potential of a specific AI application and developed an AI-supported, results-based webpage. The study employed a multi-method research design. Questionnaires were administered to the HES to investigate their experiences at the beginning and at the end of the course. While quantitative data were used to investigate the research through the lens of descriptive statistics and correlations between factors, qualitative data from the open questions were analysed to enable a deeper understanding of HES’ perceptions, experiences and meanings, as well as their critical thinking. The study highlighted strengths and challenges in using AI for educational purposes. The HES valued clear structures, logical navigation, and creative, motivating tasks. Simultaneously, recurring issues included incomplete translations, limited depth of critical reflection, and weaknesses in visual design. In sum, even though AI can support creativity and language learning and teaching, individual learners’ reflections and authentic teacher guidance remain indispensable for meaningful learning.

title: P2-VGAN: a lightweight velocity-weighted graph attention network for privacy-conscious edge anomaly detection
container-title: Frontiers in Artificial Intelligence
76c7345c8fd139e3ac90e2e10cd36d5a162fde2d.abstract: Introduction Two persistent challenges hinder intelligent video surveillance in public spaces: dense pixel-based models incur heavy computational costs on edge infrastructure, and continuous capture of identifiable imagery creates substantial visual privacy liabilities. Skeleton-based pipelines, which abstract each video frame into articulated landmark coordinates, support visual data minimization by discarding appearance information. However, conventional graph backbones weight joint trajectories uniformly across time, frequently confusing benign high-speed locomotion (such as sprinting for transit) with violent anomalies. Methods This paper presents the Privacy-Conscious Velocity-Weighted Graph Attention Network (P2-VGAN; the prefix “P2” is retained as a legacy identifier designating privacy-conscious representation rather than a cryptographic guarantee), an efficient framework engineered for desktop-class CPU edge gateways. The pipeline decouples motion analysis from visual appearance by extracting 33 planar body landmarks via a single-shot pose estimator; the application does not intentionally store or transmit decoded RGB frames after pose extraction, ensuring downstream processing operates strictly on appearance-reduced pose coordinates. The primary contribution is the Velocity-Weighted Attention Mechanism (VW-AM), an ultra-lightweight gating module requiring only two shared parameters that converts inter-frame coordinate displacements into a bounded squared-displacement motion proxy. This proxy modulates node features prior to multi-head graph attention, directing message passing toward rapidly moving limbs while damping near-stationary joints. Trained under a weakly supervised Multiple Instance Learning objective with temporal smoothness and sparsity regularizers, P2-VGAN is evaluated across five random seeds on the ShanghaiTech Campus and a human-centric subset of UCF-Crime. Results On ShanghaiTech, the model achieves a frame-level AUC of 84.72 ± 0.28% with 1.81 M downstream trainable parameters (pose-extractor parameters excluded) and sustains 34.01 frames per second (FPS) on an Intel Core i7-10700 CPU without hardware acceleration. When compared directly with an identical Vanilla GAT backbone without gating (83.14 ± 0.39%), VW-AM provides an unconfounded +1.58% absolute AUC gain ( p = 0.00096). On the human-centric UCF-Crime subset (215 test videos), it attains 77.88 ± 0.35% micro-average AUC, with high-motion categories (Fighting, Assault) exceeding 82% AUC. Stepwise ablations document an incremental +2.52% gain from VW-AM over an adaptive ST-GCN baseline. Discussion We position P2-VGAN as a Pareto-efficient framework for lightweight CPU surveillance, acknowledging that coordinate streams reduce visual surface exposure but do not eliminate biometric gait re-identification.

title: AI-generated advertising in agricultural livestreaming and the auditability of disclosure regulation: a three-layer audit of public Douyin data from China
container-title: Frontiers in Sustainable Food Systems
c177ed750eb610123bd142c9d637834496b25555.abstract: Agricultural products are credence goods, and in livestreaming, the grower’s visible presence signals the price. China has required labeling of deep-synthesis content since January 2023 and, since 1 September 2025, of AI-generated synthetic content. Whether public platform data can verify compliance in a market where the authenticity premium is especially salient remains unclear, given that growers themselves sell produce. We audited three layers of public Chinese platform data: 189 policy snippets, 19 accounts retrieved by AI technical terms, and 455 unique authors retrieved by crop names. In the one policy coding field with complete intercoder agreement ( κ = 1.000), only 6 of 189 snippets name authenticity as a farmer asset. Retrieval by technical terms returns intermediaries: 13 of 19 accounts sell AI tools or tutorials, and none discloses using AI to sell its own produce. Among AI-announcing cases retrieved by crop-name queries, an expanded text-field detector validated at 94.7% recall flags 10 of 455 authors: seven supply-side or service-provider accounts, one incidental non-agricultural mention, and two product-query artifacts; none discloses grower own-use of AI livestreaming. Checks of API-exposed platform metadata for all 575 video records and cover images for 472 records found no platform-side AI label or visible AI/AIGC/statutory AI-generated notice. AI was announced primarily by accounts that sell, service, or discuss AI, rather than by produce-selling grower accounts. No grower own-use disclosure appears in either audited slice: 0 of 19 technical-keyword accounts and 0 of 455 transaction-query authors. The zero admits two readings that the audited surface cannot separate: smallholders do not use these tools, making the requirement inert for them, or they use them without disclosure. No label-reading instrument applied to the audited surface can decide between them, because such inspection observes announcement rather than use. Platforms and regulators may hold backend data unavailable to an external audit. If the theoretically derived authenticity-penalty mechanism holds, disclosure would impose an uneven cost, falling more heavily on growers than on intermediaries. The observed pattern is consistent with this hypothesis but does not establish it.

title: Short-term clinical outcomes of feline maxillofacial trauma management
container-title: Frontiers in Veterinary Science
2dadfd844153864b20984b8065f993a31d956940.abstract: Introduction Maxillary and mandibular fractures frequently occur in cats presenting with maxillofacial trauma, and prompt evaluation and management are essential for soft and hard tissue healing. Objective The aim of this retrospective descriptive study was to evaluate the immediate outcomes and complications associated with emergent maxillofacial trauma management in cats. Methods The study included 42 cats that presented to a tertiary animal hospital for maxillofacial trauma. All medical records and imaging were reviewed for etiology, concurrent trauma, fracture location, treatment, treatment revisions, complications, and management of complications. Results The most common location for trauma was the mandibular ramus (23%) and the mandibular symphysis (22%), followed by the temporomandibular joint (Fracture: 11%, Luxation: 7%). Trauma associated with the maxilla (26%) and mandible (67%) were disproportionate. The most utilized management techniques were symphyseal fixation (29%), tape muzzle (15%), rigid maxillomandibular fixation (RMMF) (15%), and modified maxillomandibular fixation (BMMF) (15%). Thirty-nine of 42 (93%) cases had satisfactory outcomes with a complication rate of 54% (21/39), the most common complication being malocclusion (20/21; 95%). Three of 42 patients had unsatisfactory recoveries with 2 dying of unrelated causes prior to bony healing and 1 lost to follow-up following temporomandibular joint (TMJ) ankylosis. Conclusion Acute diagnosis and management of feline maxillofacial trauma can have satisfactory healing and good outcomes if complications can be managed effectively. Trauma management and technique selection depends heavily on fracture location, available dentition, patient factors, and owner ability to manage postoperative care.

title: Three years of RCVS and PRES cases at a single comprehensive stroke center: observations on clinical presentation, headache features, triggers, and management
container-title: Frontiers in Neurology
318d4b9d4391022f61a366b6d26894a99a4c18aa.abstract: Introduction Reversible cerebral vasoconstriction syndrome (RCVS) and posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome (PRES) are rare neurovascular disorders requiring further investigation into their characteristics. Methods We retrospectively reviewed and compared inpatient RCVS and PRES cases over a 3-year period, collecting data on demographics, medical history (including migraine), clinical presentation, diagnostics (urine drug screening and imaging), length of stay, time to diagnosis, suspected triggers (including substances), complications, and treatment. Results The sample consisted of 21 PRES and 9 RCVS cases ( n = 30). Migraine ( n = 5/9, 56%) and chronic pain ( n = 4/9, 44%) were the predominant comorbidities in the RCVS group, whereas hypertension ( n = 17/21, 81%) and chronic kidney disease ( n = 8/21, 38%) were the predominant comorbidities in the PRES group. All individuals with RCVS presented with headache ( n = 9/9, 100%), specifically thunderclap headache ( n = 8/9, 89%), followed by headache that was different from their usual migraine, positional headache, and new migraine. PRES commonly presented with altered mental status ( n = 15/21, 71%) and focal neurologic deficits ( n = 10/21, 48%). Initial neurologic examination findings demonstrated a similar pattern, with altered mental status ( n = 18/21, 86%) being common in PRES. Urine drug screening was completed for the majority of the RCVS group ( n = 6/9, 67%) and half of the PRES group ( n = 11/21, 52%). Of those tested in the RCVS group, n = 4/6 (67%) were positive for THC. The primary imaging modality was a CT angiogram (CTA) for RCVS ( n = 9/9, 100%) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) for PRES ( n = 18/21, 86%). Patients with PRES had a shorter median time to diagnosis (1 day [IQR 1–2] vs. 3 days [IQR 2–4] for RCVS) and a longer median length of stay (5 days [IQR 3–9] vs. 1 day [IQR 1–2] for RCVS). The most common physician-identified triggers were THC for RCVS ( n = 7/9, 78%) and hypertension for PRES ( n = 15/21, 71%). For PRES, the most common complications were seizures ( n = 10/21, 48%) and respiratory failure ( n = 4/21, 19%), while there were no complications in the RCVS group. The majority of patients with RCVS were treated with verapamil ( n = 8/9, 89% of the RCVS group). For PRES, treatment with blood pressure control ( n = 20/21, 95%) and antiseizure medication ( n = 7/21, 33%) was most common. Discussion RCVS cases were more frequent in individuals with migraine presenting with thunderclap headache, with THC as the primary identified trigger. PRES cases were characterized by altered mental status, a hypertension trigger, faster diagnosis, longer lengths of stay, and more complications.

title: A Deepfake Detection Framework for Securing Facial Biometrics Using Attention-Based Deep Learning and Blockchain
container-title: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
a0074b87d1d6c79dcfbe609a01fe5bc5a247f1d2.abstract: Facial biometric authentication is widely deployed for identity verification, yet it is increasingly exposed to deepfakebased presentation and injection attacks and to large-scale breaches of centrally stored biometric templates. This paper proposes a deepfake-resilient facial biometric security framework that combines attention-based deep learning with blockchain technology. At registration, face images are pre-processed, augmented with a generative adversarial network (GAN), encoded by a convolutional neural network (CNN) with self-attention, and classified as real or fake by an artificial neural network (ANN). Only images classified as real are encrypted, bound to a unique user identifier and committed to a private blockchain through a cryptographic hash, whereas fake attempts are written to an immutable event log. At authentication, a fresh probe passes through the same pipeline and is verified by smart contracts that check the integrity of the registered commitment and the template similarity using zero-knowledge proofs (ZKPs), so that raw biometric features are never disclosed. We formalise the threat model, specify the architecture, the smart-contract interface and the security properties, and define an evaluation protocol based on the CIPLAB Real and Fake Face Detection and UTKFace datasets that covers detection accuracy, authentication error rates, adversarial robustness, demographic fairness and system overhead. The framework provides a basis for privacy-preserving, auditable and scalable facial authentication in digital identity management, financial services, healthcare and e-governance.

title: Opportunity or Uncertainty? Understanding Pre-IPO Information Environment, Investor Preferences, and Early Market Dynamics
container-title: Business Management Journal
1c718ab277349484e4bab356d60aa533e79d50a7.abstract: Research on Initial Public Offerings (IPOs) has predominantly focused on post-listing outcomes, such as underpricing, stock returns, and long-term market performance. Comparatively, the relationships among the pre-IPO information environment, prospective investor preferences, investor participation, and early market dynamics warrant more integrated examination. This study examines the relationships among these dimensions in the Indonesian capital market. It employs a qualitative descriptive approach with a multiple-case study design involving six IPOs in the July 2026 issuance wave on the Indonesia Stock Exchange. Secondary data were obtained from IPO prospectuses, official exchange disclosures, investor preference polls conducted during the offering period, oversubscription statistics, and stock prices during the first seven trading days. The analysis uses a four-stage framework informed by Organizational Information Processing Theory (OIPT) as a descriptive analytical device to compare information characteristics, investor preferences, subscription participation, and early price movements. The findings reveal substantial variation across cases, with oversubscription ranging from 14 times for EMMI to 709.93 times for PRDL. PRDL's share price increased from IDR 120 at the IPO to IDR 386 on the seventh trading day, whereas EMMI closed at IDR 460 against an IPO price of IDR 470. These differences indicate heterogeneity in stated investor preferences, subscription demand, and early price movements. However, the available aggregate and documentary data are insufficient to establish individual information-processing mechanisms or causal relationships among disclosure, preferences, subscription demand, and stock prices. This study contributes an OIPT-informed descriptive analytical framework for comparing these dimensions in an integrated manner and identifying directions for further research in emerging capital markets.

title: Corporate reputation in India: unveiling the role of board dimensions
container-title: Rajagiri Management Journal
fa0dda5b49ca9ee9dd32caaf9edda09d872537d7.abstract: Purpose The primary motive of this research is to quantify corporate reputation by developing a reputation index along with investigating the influence of governance mechanisms, specifically board characteristics, on the reputation of Indian firms. Design/methodology/approach Reputation of 249 manufacturing firms listed in the National Stock Exchange (NSE) 500 index has been analysed over the period 2015–2024 using a reputation index, and to further investigate its association with board dynamics, panel data analysis has been employed. Findings Results reveal that board dimensions at firms in India have a huge contribution in impacting their reputation. Specifically, larger boards negatively affect corporate reputation, adding credence to agency theory, while board independence enhances it. Research limitations/implications This study enriches the corporate governance literature by empirically linking board attributes with corporate reputation in the Indian context. Practical implications The findings suggest that firms should prioritise the appointment of independent directors while maintaining optimal board size to improve their reputational standing. Furthermore, the reputation index developed in this study offers investors an additional tool to evaluate potential investments by providing firms' reputation scores. Social implications The article contains valuable insights for shareholders who must be aware of how effective governance mechanisms help to build corporate reputation. Originality/value The present study is novel in examining the association between board dynamics and corporate reputation in India in the post-Companies Act, 2013 context. It further develops a reputation index using several proxies for measuring firms' reputation quantitatively, offering a distinctive contribution to the literature.
