title: Mobile Health in Pancreatic Cancer Management
container-title: Gastroenterology Nursing
1d9fccf27b13356d2cf7c4d0bfa86324238922ad.abstract: Due to its specific disease characteristics, the diagnosis and treatment of pancreatic cancer often requires patients to repeatedly travel between their home and medical institutions due to the ineffective management of symptoms, cachexia, and other issues, thus incurring significant time, costs, and financial investment in their quest for medical treatment. The use of mobile health (mHealth) technology has alleviated this predicament, at least to a certain extent. The aim of this article is to discuss the current status and issues faced when using mHealth in the disease management of patients with pancreatic cancer. We summarize the current new advances in mHealth in the field of pancreatic cancer disease management and analyze barriers to the widespread adoption of mHealth technologies. mHealth technology makes the various stages of disease management more convenient and efficient for pancreatic cancer patients. It is hoped that relevant legislation and regulations will be developed and that narrowing the “digital divide” will be more conducive to the development of mHealth models in pancreatic cancer patients.

title: Capital Market Development and Economic Transformation in Nigeria
container-title: London Journal of Research in Management and Business
15270c563342c86c54ff1d9f2706d3e6ce655881.abstract: The study determined the nature of the relationship capital market development and economic growth in Nigeria during 1990 – 2024. The data for the period under consideration were sourced from the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) Statistical Bulletin for annual time-series analysis; the economic growth indicator used was real GDP growth while total market capitalization was used as the measure of the capital market development. Control variables included money supply, private sector credit and inflation. The Autoregressive Distributed Lag (ARDL) method was used to analyse the short and long run relationships between the variables. A long run relationship was confirmed with the bounds test. In the long run, the impact of market capitalization and money supply are positive for economic growth while the impact of private sector credit and inflation are negative. In the short run, the capitalization of a market has positive and significant impact on both the contemporaneous and lagged changes in the economic growth, while the money supply has negative and significant impact on the economic growth. Inflation has a negative contemporaneous effect but positive and significant effects at its first and second lags; private sector credit has no significant short-run effect. The disequilibration correction coefficient is negative and significant, which means there is a high rate of correction of about 91.8% or more of the disequilibrium in one year. The study found that capital market development has relevance to Nigeria’s economic development but its impact is moderated by the general state of the monetary and macro economic conditions. It suggests policies to increase market depth, build investor confidence, increase long-term capital inflows and to optimize monetary and credit management to boost the contribution of the capital market to economic growth.

title: Human-Governed Multi-Agent AI for Biological Hypothesis Generation: An Evidence-Grounded Framework Using JUMP Cell Painting Profiles
7a2bcb64973bd56bae183bb619c26a0d3a9a5a47.abstract: Abstract High-dimensional cellular phenotypes can motivate biological hypotheses, but similarity alone cannot establish mechanism or causal validity. DISCOVERY-AGENT links exploratory JUMP Cell Painting evidence with evidence-grounded hypothesis generation, independent critique and bounded human-review routing. An initial 65-record CRISPR/ORF analysis across nine gene–modality tests found four FDR-significant CRISPR plate-level associations (AKT1, BRCA1, MTOR and TP53), none among evaluated ORF genes. A distinct later cross-source compound-identity benchmark used 614 morphological features and achieved AUROC 0.6142 on 1,250 held-out compounds with training-only preprocessing; this is identity discrimination, not mechanism-of-action classification. Three structured hypotheses underwent LLM critique and revision, while eleven gene-pair evidence assessments yielded no FDR-significant mechanistic finding (minimum q = 0.2037). Archived governance checks passed 1,021/1,021 predefined tests; nevertheless, the initial live-agent run contained two execution errors among five cases, with both cases responding on fresh retest. These findings demonstrate feasibility of auditable evidence processing and modest cross-source morphology signal, not validated autonomous discovery, prospective safety, or completed expert review. The work delineates practical requirements for independent biological validation and reproducible scientific agents.

title: Sustainable postharvest management of fruits: Bridging biology, technology and policy
container-title: Journal of Environmental Biology
e9f03af1ea715cad1f7441edccc158f118471f6f.abstract: Postharvest loss remains a major barrier to agricultural productivity, yet proven technologies and interventions exist to reduce it. Globally, an estimated 14% of food is lost between harvest and retail (FAO, 2019), while a further 19% of the food available to consumers is wasted in retail, food service, and households (UNEP, 2024). Fruits and vegetables are among the most perishable agricultural commodities, and their high-water content, fragile tissues, and vulnerability to mechanical injury and decay lead to value-chain losses of 20% - 50%, depending on the crop and region (Khan et al., 2024). Where fruit is lost depends on where it is grown. In developing regions, losses occur early, on farms and during handling, because cold storage facility is scarce and produce passes through thousands of unconnected smallholders. In developed economies, losses occur later, at retail and household levels, driven by overproduction, strict cosmetic standards and consumer behavior (Khan et al., 2024). Globally, these losses cost hundreds of billions of dollars annually. Due to this, growers earn less, consumers pay more, and the land, water and energy used to produce the fruit gets wasted. Although logistics plays pivotal role in post-harvest loss reduction, however, it explains only part of the problem. Understanding quick fruit deterioration needs looking at biology. Physiological and biochemical processes going on within fruit are important in fruit spoilage. Senescence is not a simple decay, but a firmly regulated process in which ethylene plays a central role. In climacteric fruits, ethylene biosynthesis and signalling trigger a burst of respiration that drives ripening, while non-climacteric species follow quieter, ethylene-independent cues feeding into much the same genetic machinery (Tipu and Sherif, 2024). As senescence proceeds, reactive oxygen species accumulate faster than the fruit's antioxidant enzymes can neutralise them, causing lipid peroxidation and membrane damage. Simultaneously, enzymes such as polygalacturonase and cellulase break down the pectin and hemicellulose that give tissue its structure, explaining why ripe fruit softens. Chlorophyll degrades, other pigments accumulate, water is lost through transpiration, and starch converts into sugar, rewriting colour, texture, and flavour within days. Ethylene and abscisic acid pathways, alongside carbohydrate and ROS metabolism, remain the principal molecular drivers of this decline across both fruit classes (Storch et al., 2025). Every serious postharvest intervention such as cold chain, packaging, coating, or biocontrol agent, works by interrupting one of these triggers rather than masking its effects. Conventional refrigeration is the obvious starting point, but it is energy intensive, still largely dependent on hydrofluorocarbons, and out of reach for smallholders without reliable grid access. Low carbon alternatives are beginning to close this gap. Solar photovoltaic cold storage, paired with cold thermal energy storage using ice, chilled water, or phase change materials, keeps cooling running through cloudy days and after dark, making it more dependable in weak-grid settings and considerably lower carbon than diesel backed refrigeration over its lifetime (Mehtab et al., 2026). Passive evaporative systems achieve much the same result with no electricity at all such as charcoal coolers, clay pot devices, and cooling blankets exploit evaporative cooling to lower produce temperature by 3–10°C and raise relative humidity to 70–100%, buying several extra days of shelf life (Defraeye et al., 2023). Field trials in tropical value chains report postharvest loss reduction of up to 45% from these passive systems, rivalling far costlier mechanical options. Where cold chains manage the environment fruit sits in, modified and controlled atmosphere packaging (MAP/CAP) manages the microclimate around each piece, adjusting oxygen, carbon dioxide, and nitrogen levels to slow respiration, delay ripening, and hold microbial growth in check. It is among the most commercially proven postharvest tools, yet its dependence on petroleum based films has pushed research toward starch, chitosan, and cellulose based alternatives that now match synthetic films for barrier performance while breaking down naturally once discarded. Edible coatings extend this idea further, forming a semipermeable layer directly on the fruit's surface that regulates respiration, water loss, and gas exchange while carrying active compounds where they are needed. Chitosan, alginate, and gum arabic dominate this space for their antimicrobial properties, film forming stability, and compatibility with plant derived actives such as essential oils, which additionally slowdown enzymatic browning and limit lipid peroxidation restraining senescence on several fronts at once. Because these materials are renewable, non-toxic and compostable, they align with both circular economy goals and clean label consumer preferences. Non-thermal physical treatments offer a chemical free complement to these methods without sacrificing sensory quality or nutrition. Cold plasma, produced by ionising gas at room temperature, generates reactive oxygen and nitrogen species, UV photons, and charged particles that eliminate surface pathogens while pushing the fruit's own metabolism. Reported microbial log reductions of 2.0–5.0 across fruit types match or exceed conventional sanitisers without heat damage (Shill and Sit, 2025), while also stimulating antioxidant enzyme activity that helps preserve phenolic and flavonoid content. Pulsed light, UV-C, ozone, and electrolysed water work through related mechanisms, suppressing spoilage organisms with little effect on firmness, colour, or vitamin content, a natural complement to cold chains and packaging rather than a replacement. A different, biological line of defence targets pathogens directly. Botrytis cinerea, Penicillium, and Alternaria species collectively ac

title: Fusarium sugarcane pathosystem: Etiology, diversity, host-pathogen interactions, epidemiology, diagnosis and management of Pokkah Boeng disease of sugarcane
container-title: Journal of Environmental Biology
d36c898f884558bec4c0d9d471662d8077d985f3.abstract: Pokkah Boeng is an emerging and economically significant disease of sugarcane (Saccharum spp.), causing yield losses of 10-15% in India and posing an increasing threat to sustainable cane production worldwide. This review provides a comprehensive synthesis of current knowledge on the Fusarium Sugarcane Pathosystem, encompassing disease etiology, pathogen diversity, host-pathogen interactions, epidemiology, diagnostics and integrated management strategies. Particular emphasis is laid on the taxonomic complexity, phylogenetic relationships and pathogenic variability of the Fusarium species complex associated with Pokkah Boeng disease of sugarcane. The review further explores the influence of climatic drivers, crop production practices, inoculum dynamics and pathogen dissemination mechanisms in shaping disease outbreaks, with particular relevance to Indian agro-ecosystems. Recent advances in understanding molecular interactions between Fusarium and sugarcane are discussed including fungal effectors, virulence-associated factors, host defence responses and emerging biotechnological approaches. Current disease management practices, including resistant cultivar deployment, cultural measures, biological control, fungicide application and RNA based technologies are critically evaluated. Finally, key knowledge gaps and future research priorities are highlighted, emphasising the integration of precision diagnostics, genomics-assisted resistance breeding, climate based disease forecasting and sustainable agro-ecological approaches for durable management of Pokkah Boeng disease of sugarcane. Key words: Epidemiology, Fusarium spp., Host Pathogen interaction, Pokkah Boeng, Sugarcane

title: Autologous Platelet-Rich Plasma Penile Injection After Failed Oral Medical Management of Erectile Dysfunction
container-title: NATIONAL BOARD OF EXAMINATIONS JOURNAL OF MEDICAL SCIENCES
ad1922425109e74499ef23a8596e2424a5628cd2.abstract: Objective: Platelet-rich plasma (PRP) injection is an evolving regenerative therapy in the management of erectile dysfunction (ED). This study aimed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of autologous intracavernosal PRP injections in patients with ED who failed oral medical management. Methods: The single-arm prospective interventional study included men with all grades of ED who received two PRP injections (prepared using the TriCell TriPReP TUBEX system) one month apart. The primary endpoint was the percentage of men who achieved the minimum clinically important difference (MCID). Secondary endpoints included change in International Index of Erectile Function-Erectile Function (IIEF-EF) domain scores from baseline to 1- and 3-month post-treatment, adverse events, and overall treatment satisfaction. Results: Thirty out of 32 enrolled patients completed the study protocol (mean age 36.53 years). Mean IIEF-EF scores significantly improved (p < 0.001) from baseline (13.01) to 1 month (15.9) and 3 months (18.03) post-treatment. MCID was achieved by 30% of patients at 1 month and 53.3% at 3 months, across all grades of ED. More importantly, patients with mild and mild-to-moderate ED showed superior response rates in achieving MCID (90% at 1 month, 100% at 3 months) compared to moderate and severe ED patients (0% at 1 month, 30% at 3 months). No adverse events were reported, and patients reported moderate satisfaction with overall treatment (mean score of 2.2 on a Likert scale of 1-4). Conclusion: PRP is safe across all grades of ED but efficacious in mild and mild-moderate grades of ED. Future, larger, placebo-controlled studies are warranted to further validate these findings.

title: Comparative Study of Lateral Internal Sphincterotomy and Medical Management in Chronic Anal Fissure
container-title: NATIONAL BOARD OF EXAMINATIONS JOURNAL OF MEDICAL SCIENCES
24183e511e6a138bbbc9f001a28a912b88c417ab.abstract: Background: Chronic anal fissure is a common condition that affects the anorectal region and causes considerable pain and reduced quality of life for the patient. LIS surgery and medical therapy are standard treatments. The present study sought to assess the outcomes of LIS surgery and medical therapy among patients with chronic anal fissure. Methods: A Comparative observation study was carried out at the Department of General Surgery of a tertiary care hospital from March to August 2026. The total number of 260 patients having chronic anal fissure was selected and equally distributed in two groups (LIS = 130, Medical management = 130). The outcome measures include fissure healing, pain score, time required for fissure healing, recurrence, hospitalization period, resuming regular activities, need for further treatment, and patient satisfaction. Results: There was a high proportion of healing after 1 month with LIS compared to medical treatment (90.8% compared to 65.4%; p<0.001), and after 3 months 95.4% vs 77.7% (p<0.001). The mean healing time was shorter with LIS. There was a significant difference in pain scores at 1 week, 1 month, and 3 months with LIS (p<0.001). There was a low proportion of recurrence after 6 months with LIS (3.1%) compared to medical treatment (10.8%), (p=0.028). Conclusion: LIS was found to have better healing rate, more pain reduction, less recurrence and earlier recovery than the medical therapy. Treatment should be individualized depending on the clinical features and the patients’ preference.

title: Efficacy and Safety of Eltrombopag 25 Mg for the Management of Chemotherapy-Induced Thrombocytopenia in Patients with Solid Tumours: A Retrospective Comparative Study
container-title: NATIONAL BOARD OF EXAMINATIONS JOURNAL OF MEDICAL SCIENCES
18d45831de7e5ad6ceaacf49747bb855c79b4fa8.abstract: Background: Chemotherapy-induced thrombocytopenia (CIT) can compromise chemotherapy delivery in patients with solid tumours. This study evaluated the efficacy and safety of eltrombopag 25 mg compared with standard supportive care. Methods: This retrospective comparative analysis involved 200 adult patients suffering from solid tumours and experiencing CIT where 100 patients received eltrombopag 25 mg while the other 100 were under conventional supportive treatment. The outcomes of platelet recovery, platelet kinetics, changes in chemotherapy regimen, transfusions, bleeding, thromboembolic events, hepatotoxicity and adverse events were analysed using multivariable logistic regression. Results: There was adequate platelet recovery for administration of planned chemotherapy in 64.0% patients in eltrombopag group compared to 33.0% patients in control arm (OR 3.61, 95% CI 2.01-6.47; p<0.001). The eltrombopag was associated with increased platelet nadir, increased platelet count on day 7 and 14 and reduced time to recovery (9.1±2.8 versus 13.0±3.7 days; p<0.001). The incidence of chemotherapy delay and dose reduction was less common in eltrombopag group (20.0% versus 38.0%, p=0.005; 18.0% versus 36.0%, p=0.004, respectively). Conclusions: Low-dose eltrombopag 25 mg was associated with improved platelet recovery and fewer chemotherapy modifications without a statistically significant increase in adverse outcomes. Prospective randomized studies are warranted to confirm efficacy, define optimal treatment strategies and establish safety.

title: An attention-enhanced CNN-BiLSTM framework with confidence-gated inference for arrhythmia detection using ECG signals
container-title: Discover Computing
44feadb188256eccd1812c299d06ca2b1bdc38f0.abstract: Abstract Automated arrhythmia detection from electrocardiogram (ECG) signals is essential for early diagnosis and continuous cardiac monitoring. However, accurate classification remains challenging due to complex temporal dependencies in ECG waveforms and severe class imbalance, where clinically significant arrhythmias are underrepresented. To address these challenges, we propose an Attention-Enhanced CNN–BiLSTM framework with a Confidence-Gated Inference mechanism for ECG-based arrhythmia detection. The proposed model integrates a one-dimensional convolutional neural network (1D-CNN) to capture local morphological features with a Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (BiLSTM) network to model long-range temporal dependencies in ECG signals. A temporal attention mechanism is employed to focus on diagnostically relevant segments of the signal. Additionally, a confidence-gated inference strategy is introduced to improve prediction reliability, particularly for minority classes. An extensive ablation study across 18 configurations is conducted to evaluate the contribution of temporal modeling, attention, and inference strategies. On the MIT-BIH Arrhythmia Database, the proposed model achieves an accuracy of 96.58% and a macro-F1 score of 86.05%. To ensure an unbiased evaluation free of test-set leakage, we further adopt a strict protocol in which all hyperparameters ( $$\gamma$$ , $$\tau$$ ) are selected exclusively on a held-out validation set; under this leakage-free protocol the model attains an accuracy of 96.74% and a macro-F1 score of 86.54% on the untouched test set. These findings demonstrate that integrating attention-driven temporal modeling with calibrated inference yields efficient arrhythmia classification on the MIT-BIH benchmark.

title: Tendinopathy: Current Concepts in Pathophysiology, Clinical Presentation, and Management – An Updated Review
container-title: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
dfd8440130a852226a93fd6f46681b75f88fa543.abstract: Tendinopathy is a common musculoskeletal disorder characterized by tendon pain, impaired function, and reduced loadbearing capacity. It affects both athletic and non-athletic populations and represents a significant cause of disability and healthcare burden worldwide. Traditionally regarded as an inflammatory condition, current evidence suggests that tendinopathy is a multifactorial disorder involving mechanical overload, extracellular matrix degradation, collagen disorganization, cellular dysfunction, oxidative stress, neurovascular ingrowth, and a failed healing response. Commonly affected tendons include the Achilles tendon, patellar tendon, rotator cuff tendons, and lateral elbow extensor tendons. Several intrinsic and extrinsic risk factors, including aging, obesity, diabetes mellitus, repetitive occupational activities, and sports-related overuse, contribute to disease development and progression. Advances in imaging modalities such as ultrasonography and magnetic resonance imaging have improved the diagnosis and monitoring of tendon pathology. Management strategies include exercise-based rehabilitation, physiotherapy, extracorporeal shockwave therapy, pharmacological interventions, platelet-rich plasma therapy, regenerative medicine approaches, and surgical treatment in refractory cases. Emerging therapies such as stem cell therapy, growth factor delivery, gene therapy, and tissue-engineered scaffolds offer promising future directions for tendon regeneration. This review provides a comprehensive overview of the epidemiology, pathophysiology, clinical manifestations, diagnosis, and current as well as emerging treatment strategies for tendinopathy, highlighting recent advances and future perspectives in tendon research and clinical practice

title: Efektivitas Penggunaan E-Layanan Bebas Temuan pada Inspektorat Daerah Provinsi Sulawesi Barat: Analisis Berdasarkan Dimensi Campbell
container-title: Journal of Management and Social Sciences
3d03928763f8fecaa1f4535ada60bc40fe4a3b2a.abstract: Digitalizing personnel administration services is part of bureaucratic reform, yet studies on digital services developed independently by regional inspectorates remain scarce. This study measures the effectiveness of the E-Layanan Bebas Temuan, an online service for issuing the Surat Keterangan Bebas Temuan (SKBT, a certificate of no outstanding audit findings) to civil servants at the Regional Inspectorate of West Sulawesi Province, using Campbell’s five measures of effectiveness. A descriptive quantitative approach was applied to 100 civil servants selected by simple random sampling, with the sample size determined by the Slovin formula. Data were collected through a 27-item Likert-scale questionnaire that proved valid and reliable (Cronbach’s Alpha = 0.851), complemented by interviews with three informants, observation, and documentation. Overall effectiveness reached 89.58% (Very Effective), with dimension scores between 88.65% and 90.07%. Input efficiency scored highest (92.00%), whereas accessibility scored lowest (87.00%). Interviews indicated that processing time fell from 3-7 working days to 1-3 working days. Improvements are still needed in user assistance, administrator capacity during peak periods, automatic status notifications, and database integration. The findings imply that the success of internal digital services in local governments depends on user readiness and system integration, not merely on the availability of an application.

title: Pengaruh Citra Merek, Pemasaran Media Sosial, dan Kepercayaan Merek terhadap Niat Pembelian
container-title: Journal of Management and Social Sciences
0b473081293576e7101f0c24b20d72a133a4d70e.abstract: This study aims to examine the effect of brand image, social media marketing, and brand trust on the purchase intention of consumers of Camille Beauty products in Semarang City. This study employed a quantitative approach. The population consisted of all consumers of Camille Beauty products in Semarang City; however, the exact number of the population was unknown. The sample size was determined based on Roscoe's theory, resulting in 126 respondents. The sampling technique used was purposive sampling, with the criteria that respondents were residents of Semarang City and had used Camille Beauty products for at least one month. Data were collected through questionnaires and analyzed using SPSS version 22. The data analysis techniques included respondent descriptive analysis, variable descriptive analysis, validity testing, reliability testing, the F-test, the coefficient of determination (R²) test, and the t-test. The results indicate that brand image, social media marketing, and brand trust have a positive and significant effect on the purchase intention of consumers of Camille Beauty products in Semarang City.

title: Face Recognition Based Attendance System
container-title: International Scientific Journal of Engineering and Management
29cb3222ef9e0631f07975b9e1641aa82463183c.abstract: Attendance recording is a routine academic task, yet manual roll calls, paper registers and card-based methods are time-consuming, error-prone and open to proxy attendance. This paper presents a Face Recognition Based Attendance System that automates attendance using facial biometrics on low-cost, locally hosted infrastructure. The system is built with Python and Flask, uses the face_recognition library, based on a pretrained deep-learning face-embedding model from dlib, for 128-dimensional face encodings, OpenCV for camera processing and SQLite for local storage. It provides two workflows: administrator-controlled enrollment, in which front, left and right facial references are stored for each student and duplicate identities are rejected, and continuous webcam-based verification, in which each detected face is compared with the enrolled encodings using Euclidean distance. A face within a predefined threshold is marked present once per day, while an unmatched face is labelled unrecognized rather than assigned to a student. An administrator dashboard supports viewing, manual correction and reporting. The prototype is aimed at classroom entrances and small institutions. Dedicated liveness detection and large-scale quantitative evaluation are not yet included and are identified as future work. Key Words: Face Recognition, Facial Embedding, Automated Attendance, OpenCV, Flask, Biometric Authentication.

title: Effectiveness of dynamic epidemic intelligence networks for early detection and intervention in infectious diseases: a systematic review and meta-analysis
container-title: Frontiers in Public Health
90382af3734d9426b22d92982c3bfbbd157280ad.abstract: Background The increasing frequency of global health emergencies highlights the critical need for surveillance systems that transcend the limitations of traditional laboratory confirmation. Dynamic epidemic intelligence systems and syndromic surveillance networks have emerged as vital tools for early detection, yet their operational effectiveness remains characterized by significant variability across geographic and clinical contexts. Objective This study aimed to provide a comprehensive meta-analytical evaluation of the effectiveness of dynamic epidemic intelligence systems, focusing on diagnostic classification accuracy, outbreak detection sensitivity, signal precision (Positive Predictive Value), and temporal forecasting reliability. Methods A systematic review and meta-analysis were conducted, synthesizing data from original research articles searched across multiple databases (PubMed, Ovid/MEDLINE, and Embase) Methodological quality was appraised using structured six-domain quality assessment framework adapted from CASP principles and surveillance-system evaluation criteria. Diagnostic validity was synthesized using a bivariate random-effects (Reitsma) model to account for the correlation between sensitivity and specificity. Outbreak detection and alert precision were pooled using random-effects model, MSE was synthesized using inverse-variance random-effects meta-analysis on the log-transformed scale and back-transformed for interpretation. MAPE was summarized descriptively because only two estimates from a single study were available. Results Thirty-four articles were included for analysis. The pooled diagnostic analysis demonstrated high specificity (0.97; 95% CI: 0.94–0.99) but moderate sensitivity (0.64; 95% CI: 0.37–0.85), with a Summary Receiver Operating Characteristic (SROC) Area Under the Curve of 0.96. While systems were highly effective at detecting established outbreaks (pooled rate: 0.91; 95% CI: 0.73–0.97), performance was markedly lower for rare pathogens such as Ebola (0.30) compared to international health threats (0.97). Alert precision was a significant challenge, with a pooled Positive Predictive Value of 0.36 (95% CI: 0.14–0.66), indicating that approximately 64% of system-triggered signals were “noise”. Conclusions Epidemic intelligence systems are powerful instruments for excluding non-events and capturing large-scale outbreaks, yet their reliability for daily operational alerts is highly context dependent. To minimize investigative burden, future implementations must prioritize pathogen-specific optimization and the integration of diverse data streams to enhance sensitivity in humanitarian and low-resource settings.

title: Teachers’ attitudes and behavioural intentions towards AI integration in Chinese higher education: a qualitative interview study
container-title: Frontiers in Psychology
c6fe4330bbf5fd4fe3ac0771cb768c511236b747.abstract: Introduction The rapid expansion of generative AI has intensified scholarly and policy debate over its role in higher education, yet university teachers’ attitudes towards its integration remain complex and context-dependent. This study explores how university teachers perceive, experience, and respond to AI integration in their teaching. Guided primarily by the three-component attitude model and informed by the technology acceptance model and the theory of planned behaviour, the study examines cognitive appraisals, affective responses, behavioural intentions, and perceived support needs. Methods The study draws on semi-structured interviews with 14 university teachers from four higher education institutions in China. The interview data were analysed using codebook-informed thematic analysis combining deductive and inductive coding. Results The findings indicate that teachers generally perceive AI as a supportive rather than substitutive educational tool, valuing it for improving efficiency, supporting lesson preparation, and enriching pedagogical design. Emotional responses varied from enthusiasm and a sense of accomplishment to caution, neutrality, and, in some cases, declining satisfaction. Across the interviews, teachers’ primary concerns centred less on their own replacement than on the perceived risks of inappropriate AI use for students’ independent thinking, reasoning, originality, and authentic understanding. Teachers’ intentions to adopt AI were therefore conditional and bounded, shaped by pedagogical purpose, disciplinary context, student readiness, and the need to maintain teacher control. Teachers also emphasised that sustainable AI integration requires more than general encouragement, calling instead for AI literacy development, discipline-sensitive support, specialised tools, and enabling institutional infrastructure. Discussion Overall, these findings extend contextual understandings of teachers’ AI acceptance by showing how adoption intentions are pedagogically negotiated and highlight the importance of supporting professional judgement and students’ independent thinking in higher education.

title: Case Report: Long-term nutritional and surgical management of short bowel syndrome in a child with Strømme syndrome
container-title: Frontiers in Pediatrics
60a60a5f295a33227fd7fbf5b139db9a42da9a39.abstract: Strømme syndrome is an extremely rare autosomal recessive ciliopathy caused by biallelic mutations in CENPF , characterized by microcephaly, ocular abnormalities, and intestinal atresia; intestinal involvement can evolve into short bowel syndrome (SBS), a recognized but infrequently documented complication. We report the case of an infant with genetically confirmed Strømme syndrome, complicated by severe apple-peel jejunoileal atresia that progressed to SBS. After an initial phase of total dependence on parenteral nutrition (PN) and recurrent catheter-related infectious complications, a coordinated, individually tailored care plan combining personalized nutritional strategies with intensive follow-up allowed a gradual transition to partial oral feeding combined with cyclical home PN. Despite the severity of the condition and the prolonged duration of PN, the child achieved catch-up growth (from an initial nadir to the 50th percentile by the latest follow-up) and preserved liver function. To our knowledge, this is the first detailed report of the long-term nutritional rehabilitation and PN-weaning trajectory in a child with genetically confirmed Strømme syndrome complicated by SBS, showing how well-structured, personalized, and integrated home nutritional management can lead to positive outcomes even in this complex and rare setting.

title: Long-term management of relapsing anti-GPIHBP1 (Glycosylphosphatidylinositol-anchored high-density lipoprotein-binding protein 1) associated hypertriglyceridaemia: a case report and literature review
container-title: Frontiers in Immunology
828dd6381804e0674b904b9807b41ba4abf3a84d.abstract: Anti-GPIHBP1 syndrome is a rare, acquired cause of hypertriglyceridaemia, characterized by severe elevation of triglyceride that is refractory to standard lipid-lowering therapies. It is autoimmune in nature and demonstrates a significant response to immunosuppressive treatment. However, it has a chronic relapsing course and the role of maintenance immunosuppression in this syndrome remains unclear. We report a 46-year-old woman diagnosed with anti-GPIHBP1 syndrome following an initial presentation of acute pancreatitis. While her initial presentation and short-term induction response were previously reported, we would like to present her longitudinal follow-up, highlighting the long-term relapsing nature of the syndrome. She showed a good therapeutic response to intravenous rituximab infusions. Due to recurrent episodes of pancreatitis, maintenance immunosuppression with rituximab was commenced. Serial monitoring of CD19+ B-cell repopulation was used to guide the subsequent dosing timing as a hypothesis-generating strategy to aid in relapse prevention. During the latest follow-up, she remained in clinical and biochemical remission with proactive rituximab maintenance infusions. This single case observation suggests that patients with relapsing anti-GPIHBP1 syndrome might benefit from maintenance treatment with rituximab. Furthermore, regular monitoring of CD19+ B-cell repopulation may serve as a potential biomarker to guide retreatment, though it warrants further evaluation in more patients.

title: Automated assessment of healthcare de-escalation communication skills in a conversational AI virtual reality simulation
container-title: Frontiers in Digital Health
9bc424b8b0ee6bc350b4296b68f692e3f29c8284.abstract: Introduction Digital health training environments increasingly require scalable methods for assessing communication skills in realistic, interactive scenarios. This paper presents a comparative study of automated assessment approaches within a conversational AI virtual reality simulation designed for verbal de-escalation training. Methods A total of 20 nursing students completed the simulation, where their spoken responses were captured and converted to text through a speech-to-text system, and were evaluated across 11 de-escalation competencies. The evaluation compared three fine-tuned deep learning models (BERT, RoBERTa, and XLNet) with a modified RATAS, a rubric-driven framework that leverages large language models. Two experiments were conducted: one using controlled 100-item validation datasets for each section, and another using the real-world responses collected during the user study. Results On the validation datasets, the deep learning models achieved the highest performance, with RoBERTa obtaining an average accuracy of 0.9927, followed by BERT at 0.9900 and XLNet at 0.9790, while RATAS achieved 0.8554. On the student-response dataset, performance decreased for all approaches, with RoBERTa obtaining 0.8590 accuracy, RATAS 0.8181, BERT 0.8000, and XLNet 0.7681. Discussion These results suggest that transformer-based models perform best under controlled conditions, whereas RATAS demonstrated stability in grading across different dataset types. These preliminary findings support the feasibility of integrating deep learning and rubric-driven LLM-based automated assessment approaches for communication and de-escalation training in nursing education.

title: Uneven automation: comparing authorship anxiety and generative AI use among art and design undergraduate students
container-title: Frontiers in Psychology
8942b2ac014d5d2bac7e05011f209f96a5fce870.abstract: Art and design education expects students to develop a sense of authorship over original work, but generative AI (GenAI) complicates how students understand and claim that authorship. This study examined whether these experiences differ across creative fields through a mixed-methods design. The survey included 2,441 GenAI-using students from seven field categories at 33 art and design institutions in China and assessed authorship anxiety, creative agency, perceived usefulness, dependence on GenAI, and frequency of use. The quantitative analysis first examined variation across all seven categories and then compared fine art with the five applied design fields. Interview data from 22 survey participants were also examined thematically. The main findings include that (1) authorship anxiety did not differ significantly across the seven categories or between fine art and pooled design; the latter comparison met the equivalence criterion at ±d = 0.20, but not at tighter bounds; (2) clearer differences emerged in how students used GenAI. Compared with fine-art students, design students considered GenAI more useful and used it more frequently; (3) across the interviews, most students described authorship as retaining control over the creative idea while delegating parts of its execution to GenAI. Specifically, fine-art students often grounded authorship in embodied making and human imperfection, whereas design students placed greater emphasis on judgement, selection, and control. We call this pattern uneven automation: concern about authorship was broadly shared, but students in different fields responded to GenAI in different ways, potentially reflecting the varying labour-market pressures surrounding their disciplines.

title: Invasive Candida viswanathii infections in critically ill neonates: clinical challenges and management insights from a case series
container-title: Frontiers in Pediatrics
b7bc26d306e62326f955c03cc0182b2f26f48ab3.abstract: Background Candida species continue to be a major cause of invasive fungal infections in neonatal intensive care units, with a growing awareness of new non-Albicans Candida species that pose diagnostic and therapeutic problems in critically ill neonates. Candida viswanathii is an uncommon pathogen with poor clinical evidence, particularly in neonatal critical care units. Methods From April to August 2025, we conducted a case series of five newborns admitted to the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) of Bambino Gesù Children's Hospital in Rome, Italy, who had bloodstream infections caused by C. viswanathii . Whole-genome sequencing (WGS), chromogenic agar evaluation, MALDI-TOF mass spectrometry, and traditional culture were all used in microbiological identification. Broth microdilution was used to test for antifungal susceptibility. Retrospective clinical data on risk factors, treatment, and results were collected. Results Six cases of candidemia were reported in five critically unwell newborns, the majority of whom were premature or had severe congenital comorbidities. All of the patients had central venous catheters and had been in intensive care for an extended period of time. Initial identification methods misidentified isolates as Candida tropicalis , however molecular research revealed a clonal cluster of C. viswanathii . The BCID2 panel failed to detect the organism. All isolates had higher fluconazole minimum inhibitory concentrations, but echinocandins and amphotericin B had lower MIC values. Systemic echinocandin therapy was the primary treatment, with liposomal amphotericin B added in severe instances, as well as rigorous source control measures such as catheter removal and antifungal lock therapy. Microbiological clearance was documented in all six candidemia episodes. Three patients were discharged, whereas two died because of their underlying cardiopulmonary disease. Conclusions Invasive C. viswanathii infection represents a diagnostic and therapeutic challenge in the NICU. Advanced microbiological techniques, prompt source control, and targeted antifungal therapy are essential for effective management of this emerging pathogen.

title: Digital transformation, traceability, and supply chain resilience in food manufacturing SMEs: a review of AI, blockchain-IoT, and institutional mechanisms
container-title: Frontiers in Sustainable Food Systems
c0821ee379eb16d2e0252633d6030dd152fbd833.abstract: Food supply chains in China face persistent challenges of food safety risks, inadequate transparency, and supply disruptions, with food manufacturing small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) disproportionately vulnerable due to limited resources and non-standardized internal processes. Digital transformation encompassing artificial intelligence (AI), blockchain, Internet of Things (IoT), and digital twin technologies is increasingly regarded as a strategic solution to strengthen supply chain resilience, yet the organizational and institutional conditions under which these digital investments translate into tangible resilience improvements for food manufacturing SMEs remain poorly understood. This review conducts a PRISMA 2020-compliant systematic review and thematic synthesis of 40 multidisciplinary sources spanning the food safety, supply chain management, and information systems literatures. Drawing on Dynamic Capabilities Theory and Institutional Theory, we propose an integrative conceptual framework comprising six research propositions, in which traceability capability acts as a food-safety-specific mediating mechanism linking digital transformation to supply chain resilience, while regulatory stringency moderates the strength of this indirect pathway. A central argument of this framework is that deploying blockchain, IoT, or AI hardware does not itself constitute traceability capability the institutional and organisational conditions under which digital tools are adopted determine whether firms build substantive traceability capability or engage in symbolic compliance without genuine food safety governance improvement. Three key contributions distinguish this framework: conceptualizing traceability capability as a distinct dynamic capability rather than a generic digitalization mechanism; directing analytical focus explicitly toward food manufacturing SMEs, a population largely overlooked in existing large-firm panel studies; and introducing regulatory stringency as a first-stage moderator within a moderated mediation structure. Critical research gaps are identified, including the absence of SME-calibrated digital transformation measurement instruments, the lack of a validated multi-item traceability capability scale, and a complete empirical vacuum for testing the proposed moderated mediation model in food manufacturing SME contexts. This review provides a structured future research agenda for scholars and delivers actionable insights for practitioners and policymakers seeking to direct digital technology investments toward improved food safety governance in China’s food manufacturing sector.

title: Human-in-the-loop semantic learning analytics for assessing moral-value reasoning in university AI ethics education
container-title: Frontiers in Psychology
4c153cd19693204269d4536c8e62024e2ea30575.abstract: Introduction University AI ethics education addresses fairness, privacy, accountability, transparency, human autonomy, and academic integrity, but the semantic structure of students' moral-value reasoning and its connection to responsible solutions remain insufficiently characterized. This study examined a human-in-the-loop semantic learning analytics framework for task-specific moral-value reasoning. Methods Ninety science and engineering graduate students completed an online explicit-reflective AI ethics module in a one-group pre–post multimethod study without a control group. Assessments comprised an AI ethics knowledge test, a perceived-awareness scale, and open-ended ethical reasoning tasks. Expert annotations informed transformer-based multi-label coding, descriptive value coverage and balance metrics, problem–solution coupling, and baseline-only nested cross-validated prediction of subsequent raw problem-solving change. Results Within-participant pre–post increases were observed in ethical knowledge, perceived moral-value awareness, actual ethical awareness, problem–solving skills, value coverage, value balance, and problem–solution coupling. Automated semantic coding achieved participant-grouped cross-validated macro-F1 = 0.83 (95% CI [0.78, 0.87]; micro-F1 = 0.86; macro-AUPRC = 0.82). The baseline-only prediction model yielded cross-validated R 2 = 0.30 (95% CI [0.11, 0.45]) for subsequent raw problem-solving change. Discussion Expert-supervised semantic analytics can characterize value representation and issue–solution reasoning in AI ethics assessments. Coverage and balance describe response structure rather than moral quality. The absence of a control group, repeated use of one scenario, and modest sample size preclude causal and broad trait-level conclusions.

title: Perceived AI literacy and TPACK in pre-service teacher education: mediating roles of perceived usefulness, ease of use, and value in blended learning
container-title: Frontiers in Psychology
1bad51d2ab1c081fcbf1788c8c81f98f9ce0044c.abstract: Background The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into blended learning requires pre-service teachers to develop AI-related competencies and the ability to integrate technology into pedagogy. This study examines how perceived AI literacy and technological pedagogical content knowledge (TPACK) are associated with deep learning through perceived usefulness, perceived ease of use, and perceived value of AI use. Methods A cross-sectional survey was completed by 423 pre-service teachers enrolled in blended learning courses at a university in China. Data were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM), with covariance-based structural equation modeling and fuzzy-set qualitative comparative analysis (fsQCA) used as complementary robustness and configurational analyses. Results Perceived usefulness, perceived ease of use, and perceived value of AI use significantly mediated the relationships between the two competencies and deep learning. All six indirect pathways were significant in both the PLS-SEM and covariance-based SEM analyses. The fsQCA revealed an equifinal and asymmetric structure: multiple, partly substitutable conditions were sufficient for high deep learning, and no single condition was necessary for either high or low deep learning. Conclusions The findings integrate the technology acceptance model and expectancy-value theory to explain how pre-service teachers' competencies and perceptions relate to deep learning in AI-enhanced blended environments. Teacher education should support technical competence alongside positive perceptions of AI's utility, usability, and value. Because the measures were self-reported and collected cross-sectionally at one university, the findings are interpreted as associational and configurational rather than causal.

title: Management of a giant rectal prolapse with bowel evisceration in a low-resource setting
container-title: Adesh University Journal of Medical Sciences & Research
66e631704b758aa3cfc8bfadf8cc104b135eebc4.abstract: Rectal prolapse (RP) involves full-thickness rectal protrusion through the anus, often associated with anatomical changes such as a deep pouch of Douglas. Delay in treatment can lead to giant prolapse (>10 cm) and, rarely, necrosis with bowel evisceration. We report a 36-year-old male with giant RP complicated by evisceration of bowel. An exploratory laparotomy was performed. The intraoperative findings included a 15 cm prolapsed rectum with an anterior wall tear through which loops of bowel herniated. Only 93 cm of jejunum and 10 cm of terminal ileum remained viable. Additional findings included a deep pouch of Douglas and an edematous pelvic floor. We performed an enterectomy of the gangrenous small bowel loops with divided stoma (end jejunostomy and mucus fistula). The prolapsed rectum was repaired with a three-point fixation to the anterior abdominal wall and the iliopsoas fasciae on either side of the rectum, after an upward traction. He died 30 h after surgery from septic shock. Eviscerated bowel, a rare complication of neglected RP, is associated with challenges and increased mortality in a resource-poor setting. There is a need for health education to promote early presentation among individuals with RP.

title: Observation of the beneficial effects of nasal saline irrigation combined with inhaled budesonide on acute asthma exacerbations in children: a retrospective study
container-title: World Economy and Management research
42b2d494767bb3f284f52ee492e82ebcc224b8fe.abstract: Background Acute asthma exacerbations remain a major cause of morbidity in children. While inhaled budesonide is a cornerstone of acute management, concurrent upper-airway inflammation may limit treatment efficacy. This study aimed to evaluate the clinical effects of nasal saline irrigation combined with inhaled budesonide in children with acute asthma exacerbations. Methods This retrospective study was conducted at Beijing Chaoyang Hospital, Capital Medical University. Children aged 1–14 years who were treated for acute asthma exacerbations were divided into a control group (inhaled budesonide alone) and a combination group (inhaled budesonide plus nasal saline irrigation). Clinical symptom scores, peripheral oxygen saturation (SpO₂), respiratory rate, length of hospital stay, and adverse events were compared between the two groups. The study was approved by the institutional ethics committee (BJCY-26-371). Results A total of 186 children were included (control group, n = 92; combination group, n = 94). Baseline characteristics were comparable between groups. The combination group showed significantly faster reductions in total and nasal symptom scores, more rapid improvement in SpO₂ and respiratory rate at 24–72 h, and a shorter median length of hospital stay (4.0 vs. 5.0 days, P = 0.003) compared with the control group. The requirement for additional systemic corticosteroids was also lower in the combination group. Nasal saline irrigation was well tolerated, with only mild, self-limiting adverse events reported. Conclusions Nasal saline irrigation combined with inhaled budesonide was associated with faster clinical improvement and a shorter hospital stay in children with acute asthma exacerbations compared with inhaled budesonide alone, without increasing adverse events. These findings support the potential value of nasal saline irrigation as a simple adjunctive therapy in this setting.

title: Effectiveness of an AI-Based Educational Video Generator in Enhancing Oral Health Knowledge and Behavior Among Children: A Randomized Controlled Trial
container-title: Al-Rafidain Journal of Medical Sciences ( ISSN 2789-3219 )
025217a90eae33a9efbb4f3e4378042549e3202e.abstract: Background: Artificial intelligence (AI) is a new innovation that presents an opportunity for oral health education in children. Objective: To evaluate the effectiveness of an AI-assisted educational video versus standardized in-person oral health education for children regarding oral health knowledge and behaviors. Methods: This randomized controlled trial included 300 children aged 10-12 years (n=150 per group), both boys and girls, who were divided into AI video and standardized face-to-face oral health education groups. Baseline and 2-week follow-up evaluations were conducted for knowledge scores, four behavioral items, and the Silness and Löe Plaque Index. The internal consistency of the knowledge scale was checked (Cronbach's α=0.79). Wilcoxon signed-rank and Mann–Whitney U tests were the primary non-parametric tests used for statistical evaluations, with a median, (IQR), and effect size r provided. Chi-square tests with a Bonferroni adjustment at α=0.0125 were used to evaluate behavioral items. Results: There were significant enhancements in intra-group knowledge (p<0.0001 for both groups; r=0.663 for AI; r=0.345 for Control). The clinical efficacy was similar for both strategies with significant reduction of intra-group plaque (AI: p< 0.001, r= 0.425; Control: p< 0.001, r= 0.331), but no inter-group difference at the end of the intervention (p= 0.608; r= 0.030). In the conventional group, the utilization of dental floss was significantly improved (p=0.0056), and no other behaviors showed significant improvement across groups. Conclusions: The AI-assisted educational video demonstrated better knowledge retention than the standardized face-to-face oral health education, achieved similar clinical plaque reduction, and can be easily scaled for pediatric preventive dentistry.

title: Earnings management practices and financial performance   of listed insurance firms in Nigeria
container-title: Radiant Journal of Business & Sustainability
48c3c5c6fa32103c5e89dd3523017c922ecd125b.abstract: This study examines the effect of earnings management practices on the financial performance of listed insurance firms in Nigeria. The study focuses on three dimensions: real activities earnings management (RAEM), small profit earnings management (SPEM), and timely loss recognition earnings management (TLREM). An ex-post facto research design was adopted, using secondary data obtained from Nigerian Exchange Group fact books and the annual reports of 20 listed insurance firms over the 2015–2024 period, producing 200 firm-year observations. Financial performance was measured by return on total assets, while the explanatory variables were operationalized using the Roychowdhury real activities earnings management model and threshold-based indicators for small profit reporting and timely loss recognition. Descriptive statistics, correlation analysis, diagnostic tests, and panel regression were employed. The Hausman specification test supported the fixed-effects model, while the presence of groupwise heteroskedasticity motivated the use of cluster-robust standard errors. The results show that RAEM has a negative but statistically insignificant effect on financial performance (β = −0.814, p = 0.090). SPEM has a positive but statistically insignificant effect (β = 0.228, p = 0.500). TLREM has a negative and statistically significant effect on financial performance (β = −3.003, p < 0.001). The findings indicate that the three earnings-management dimensions do not have uniform effects on financial performance. The study highlights the importance of reporting quality, monitoring, and regulatory attention to practices associated with timely loss recognition in the Nigerian insurance sector. Keywords: Earnings Management, Real Activities Earnings Management, Small Profit Earnings Management, Timely Loss Recognition, Financial Performance, Insurance Firms, Nigeria.

title: Utility-Gated Personalized Federated Forecasting for Peak-Constrained Building Energy Management
39bf8ad3166fac823170674ba2f29c0a542360c2.abstract: Abstract Distributed building energy management depends on forecasts, yet federated forecasting is commonly evaluated without testing the decisions that those forecasts support. This study examines whether selective, communication-efficient collaboration improves both load prediction and battery operation. The proposed UtilityGossipmethod maintains separate private and collaborative low-rank adapters at each node. A peer adapter is incorporated only when randomized cross-fitting on local held-out data indicates a meaningful reduction in forecast error. Evaluation on public electricity and solar benchmarks covers longer horizons, alternative network topologies, node failures, and transmit-time noise. At the 96-step horizon, the method reduces Solar-Energy mean squared error by 1.59% relative to local training and avoids the greater than 3% degradation caused by unconditional federation on Electricity, using half the communication of federated averaging. Operational value is assessed by replaying every forecast source through the same frozen battery policy for a held-out week. An external projection prevents coordinated charging from increasing the running no-storage district peak. The proposed forecast supports a 19.34% cost reduction relative to no storage, and diagnostic replays confirm that forecast timing affects dispatch. Its additional control gain over a strong local forecast is not statistically resolved. The results support selective federation for distributed forecasting but show that lower prediction error does not necessarily yield proportional energy savings.

title: HESS Opinions: Operationalizing sociohydrology from systems thinking to systems doing for sustainable and resilient water management
container-title: Hydrology and Earth System Sciences
248d074c40030f917c8ac78c5d9716bce693e541.abstract: Sociohydrology has advanced explanations of coupled human-water systems, but its translation into decision support remains uneven. We propose two complementary approaches to move from systems thinking to systems doing: (i) canonical feedback structures, which describe the main components of human-water systems and how they interact and enable comparison across cases while accounting for important local differences; and (ii) critical pathways, which trace how management actions propagate through these components to produce outcomes, including unintended consequences. Drawing on cases such as the levee effect and reservoir effect, these approaches connect system understanding with intervention design, monitoring, and adaptive learning. We then propose a minimal “systems-doing loop” that links the decision setting, feedback mapping, pathway tracing, indicator selection, and iteration, with equity and legitimacy treated as explicit constraints on useful knowledge and acceptable action. This framing complements predictive modelling and integrated water resources management by accounting for potential unintended consequences in decision-making and clarifying what to monitor and revisit as systems change.

title: Improving Learner Performance Through Score Based Analysis on a Gamified AI Driven Cybersecurity Learning Platform
d2b1981b0d01f6ee261a12a86c8c602586119c26.abstract: Abstract This study examines whether structured engagement with instructional content improves learner performance on Cyber Security Academy, an AI-driven, gamified cybersecurity learning platform. Activity logs covering 1,500 completed assessments from users in ten Anglophone and Francophone countries were analyzed by comparing learners who consulted the lessons and completed the full learning pathway (n = 900) with those who engaged only partially with the platform (n = 600). Group differences were tested with Welch's t-test, the Mann Whitney U test, one-way ANOVA, Spearman correlations, and Cohen's d as a measure of effect size. Learners who read the lessons before assessment obtained a mean score of 71.27 % versus 60.41 % for non-readers (Δ = +10.86 points; t(1192) = 12.21; p < 0.001; d = 0.650; 95 % CI [9.12, 12.60]), committed fewer errors (2.50 vs. 4.85; d = -1.069), and responded faster (9.85 vs. 12.69 minutes; d = -0.807), indicating greater fluency of cognitive processing. The effect decreased monotonically with age (d = 1.205 for learners aged 13 and under; d = 0.387 for those 22 and over) and with digital literacy (d = 1.434 for beginners; d = 0.524 for experts), while remaining positive in all ten countries. These findings indicate that structured, AI-personalized, and gamified learning environments substantially enhance cybersecurity learning outcomes, particularly for younger and less experienced users.

title: Outpatient Management of Complicated Polysubstance Use Disorder with Kratom Dominance Using the MATRIX Program: A Case Series from Thailand
b2bf72272b256b5c5acb43c2482d018c05940feb.abstract: Abstract Background Kratom ( Mitragyna speciosa ) was decriminalised in Thailand in August 2021, followed by the Kratom Plant Act 2022. Despite growing accessibility, clinical data on the outpatient management of kratom use disorder with co-occurring psychiatric comorbidities remain scarce. Objective To describe the clinical presentations, treatment approaches, and outcomes of three patients with kratom use disorder managed in an outpatient addiction psychiatry setting. Methods A retrospective case series of three male patients presenting to an outpatient psychiatric clinic between July and November 2023. All received structured biopsychosocial treatment using the MATRIX Intensive Outpatient Program, combined with brief interventions, motivational interviewing, cognitive-behavioural therapy (CBT), and relapse prevention. Pharmacotherapy was individualised according to comorbidity. Results All three patients (ages 19–24) with complex psychiatric comorbidities reported six-month kratom abstinence using the MATRIX Intensive Outpatient Program and individualised pharmacotherapy. Abstinence was based on self-report and clinical evaluations, as standard immunoassay panels do not detect kratom alkaloids and no mitragynine-specific testing was performed. Conclusions A structured outpatient biopsychosocial program, combined with targeted pharmacotherapy, may facilitate kratom abstinence in patients with complex psychiatric comorbidities. Clinicians should remain alert to emerging primary psychiatric disorders that may be masked or precipitated by kratom and polysubstance use.

title: AI Labour Rights Awareness and Career Adaptation Confidence among Respondents in Bangladesh
4bebd9cda335afcb1b14dbb90e41e4c4857a6c33.abstract: Abstract Artificial intelligence changes both the skills used at work and the conditions under which employment decisions are made. Awareness of these changes does not necessarily coincide with confidence in adapting a career. This study examines that distinction in 385 adult, AI-aware survey records from Bangladesh, including 238 law students and 61 respondents classified as law graduates. Five statements separately assess awareness of workplace rights and responsibilities, recognition of protection from unfair automated decisions, reported complementary skill development, adaptation confidence and the perceived preparedness benefit of understanding labour issues. Analyses combine full response distributions, joint endorsement patterns, paired comparisons, ordinal correlations and an exploratory proportional-odds model. Recognition of the need for protection was endorsed by 79.2%, compared with 48.8% endorsing adaptation confidence, a paired difference of 30.4 percentage points (95% bootstrap interval 23.9–36.6). General rights awareness and skill development had small positive ordinal associations with confidence. In the adjusted ordinal model, their odds ratios were 1.30 (95% interval 1.04–1.61; Holm p = 0.038) and 1.40 (1.09–1.79; Holm p = 0.024) respectively. The protection-recognition estimate was less certain, although the two awareness coefficients were not demonstrably different. The findings distinguish rights recognition, reported action and confidence rather than establish a causal awareness-to-adaptability pathway. They support evaluating legal-literacy education alongside practical career tasks and institutional safeguards. The mixed sample, study-specific single items, undocumented recruitment and fieldwork dates, and source-documentation limitations constrain inference. A subsequent study should use verified graduate eligibility, independent legal-knowledge assessments and longitudinal career outcomes.

title: Developing and Evaluating a Real-World Calculus Pedagogy for Sustainable Business Management Students
container-title: Educational Journal of Technology and Innovation
81fe0c98b10581b67937d28e82c1c36ede65757d.abstract: This study developed and evaluated a real-world calculus pedagogy for Sustainable Business Management students. The purpose was to determine whether contextualized calculus instruction, built around sustainable business problems such as marginal cost, revenue optimization, carbon-cost trade-offs, inventory control and break-even analysis, improves students' conceptual understanding, engagement and perceived ability to apply calculus in sustainability-oriented managerial decisions. A quasi-experimental mixed-methods design was adopted. The population comprised 320 undergraduate Business Management students enrolled in a business mathematics course at a higher learning institution. From this population, 180 students were selected through stratified random sampling and assigned to a control group (n = 90) and an experimental group (n = 90). Quantitative data were collected through a calculus achievement test, a learning engagement scale, a perceived business applicability scale and a sustainability decision-making confidence scale. Qualitative data were collected through short reflective responses from 24 purposively selected students in the experimental group. The intervention lasted eight teaching weeks. The results showed that the experimental group improved from a pre-test mean of 49.76 to a post-test mean of 70.21, while the control group improved from 47.46 to 55.96. The difference in learning gain was statistically significant, with a large effect size. The experimental group also reported higher engagement, perceived applicability and sustainability decision-making confidence. The study concludes that a real-world calculus pedagogy can make calculus more meaningful for business students by connecting abstract mathematical ideas to practical sustainability decisions. It recommends that business mathematics courses should be redesigned around authentic managerial cases, technology-supported modelling and reflective decision-making tasks.

title: Factors Influencing In-Hospital and Long-Term Mortality in Patients with Acute ST-Elevation Myocardial Infarction Undergoing Primary Percutaneous Intervention
container-title: Journal of the Medical Association of Thailand
d443e240b78d3e721616d91ea55a707954e529a0.abstract: Objective: To identify factors associated with in-hospital and long-term mortality among patients with ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) undergoing primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) in a regional hospital in Thailand. Materials and Methods: This retrospective cohort study analyzed patients with STEMI who received primary PCI from January 2014 to December 2022. Demographic characteristics, clinical presentation, angiographic findings, procedural details, and clinical outcomes were extracted from medical records. The primary outcome was long-term all-cause mortality during a 3-year follow-up period. Survival probabilities were estimated using the Kaplan-Meier method, and Cox proportional hazards regression assessed factors associated with long-term mortality. Statistically significant defined as p<0.05. Results: The 283 patients with STEMI undergoing primary PCI were analyzed, with 12 (4.2%) dying during hospitalization. Long-term survival data included 270 patients. 3-year and 5-year survival rates were 81.0% and 78.4%, respectively. Non-survivors were older and presented with greater clinical severity. Kaplan-Meier analysis showed significantly lower survival among patients with Killip class III-IV and those who achieved a myocardial blush grade (MBG) ≤2 after PCI (log-rank p<0.001). Multivariable Cox regression, age >65 years, left ventricular dysfunction, mechanical ventilation, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, a greater number of stents, and severe coronary calcification on angiography were independently associated with increased long-term mortality. In contrast, achievement of MBG 3 (adjusted HR 0.28, 95% CI 0.13-0.64, p=0.002), longer duration of dual antiplatelet therapy (adjusted HR 0.07, 95% CI 0.02-0.28, p<0.001), and eGFR 60-89 mL/minute/1.73 m² (adjusted HR 0.24, 95% CI 0.09-0.65, p=0.005) were independently associated with lower long-term mortality. Conclusion: Long-term mortality remained substantial. Older age and greater clinical severity were associated with poorer outcomes, whereas achievement of MBG 3 was associated with improved long-term survival, highlighting the importance of early risk stratification and optimized reperfusion strategies

title: Orthopedic Patient Characteristics, Management Patterns, and Clinical Outcomes in a Disaster-Prone Region
container-title: Antigen : Jurnal Kesehatan Masyarakat dan Ilmu Gizi
77760b990617b11cf586bcfe6107dbe58fe9f06f.abstract: Datu Beru Hospital serves a geographically challenging, disaster-prone region of Central Aceh, where evidence on orthopedic case characteristics and referral practices remains limited. This study aimed to describe orthopedic patient characteristics, injury patterns, management indicators, and referral-based disposition between 2023 and 2025. A retrospective descriptive study analyzed medical records of 766 orthopedic cases using total sampling. Variables included presentation year, sex, anatomical injury location, long-bone involvement, injury mechanism, open or closed classification, and referral status. Frequencies, percentages, and descriptive cross-tabulations were used. The highest number of cases occurred in 2024 (339; 44.3%), and 482 patients (62.9%) were male. Hand injuries were most common (206; 26.9%), followed by leg (119; 15.5%) and foot injuries (89; 11.6%). Tibia-fibula injuries predominated among cases with documented long-bone involvement (116; 31.6%). Road traffic accidents were the leading documented mechanism (394; 57.4%), while closed injuries accounted for 314 cases (76.0%) with available classification data. Overall, 576 patients (75.2%) were managed without interfacility referral, whereas 190 (24.8%) were referred. Referral proportions were highest for spinal (90.9%), wrist (85.7%), and hip injuries (67.9%). These findings highlight the hospital's role in local orthopedic care and identify anatomical presentations requiring more frequent referral. However, incomplete medical records and the use of referral status rather than direct recovery measures limit conclusions about clinical outcomes. The findings support stronger trauma triage, specialized assessment, referral coordination, and disaster-responsive orthopedic preparedness in Central Aceh. Improved documentation of injury severity, treatment interventions, complications, and functional recovery would strengthen future regional evaluations of orthopedic service effectiveness.
