title: CLASSIFICATION OF PUBLIC OPINION ON FOREST MANAGEMENT IN SOUTHEAST SULAWESI PROVINCE BASED ON SOCIAL MEDIA COMMENTS USING AN LSTM-BASED DEEP LEARNING MODEL
container-title: Simtek : jurnal sistem informasi dan teknik komputer
e175f0a942c8b79fe961770e698ff3a2be91fc3f.abstract: Forest management requires information support capable of rapidly capturing public responses. However, social media opinions are unstructured and difficult to analyze manually on a large scale. This study developed an opinion classification model based on Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (BiLSTM) to categorize YouTube comments related to forest management in Southeast Sulawesi Province into positive, negative, and neutral sentiment classes. A total of 1,875 comments were collected from 40 public videos across 30 YouTube channels using the YouTube Data API v3. Following initial labeling and preprocessing, 1,838 comments were retained for model development. The dataset was stratified into 1,286 training samples, 184 validation samples, and 368 testing samples. The model architecture consisted of a 128-dimensional embedding layer, 128 bidirectional LSTM units, dropout regularization, and a three-class softmax output layer. On the test dataset, the model achieved an accuracy of 89.40%, weighted precision of 89.49%, weighted recall of 89.40%, and weighted F1-score of 88.83%. The neutral class achieved an F1-score of 94.01%, outperforming the positive and negative classes, which obtained F1-scores of 64.71% and 58.82%, respectively. These findings indicate that the model is effective for overall sentiment classification; however, class imbalance limits its ability to consistently identify minority classes. Therefore, the classification results are more appropriately utilized as preliminary analytical support for understanding public opinion, while further improvements in labeling quality and data balancing are necessary to enhance classification performance.

title: WEB-BASED EMPLOYEE PAYROLL MANAGEMENT INFORMATION SYSTEM WITH MANAGERIAL APPROVAL FEATURES AT BANG AWAL RESTAURANT
container-title: Simtek : jurnal sistem informasi dan teknik komputer
ac9ebe2ac389f9b3a40619d0a41e90cf8ed1bbd9.abstract: Managing attendance and payroll manually carries the risk of delayed data consolidation, calculation errors regarding salary components, and inadequate control over the validity of employee attendance records. This study aims to design and implement a web-based employee payroll management system for Rumah Makan Bang Awal, featuring managerial approval workflows and geolocation-based attendance verification. The system was developed using PHP and MySQL, employing an object-oriented design approach. System modeling utilized the Unified Modeling Language (UML)—including use case, sequence, and activity diagrams—alongside database relationship designs. The system integrates the management of data regarding employees, branches, positions, shifts, attendance, leave (including sick leave), loans, overtime components and deductions, salary submissions, managerial approvals, and payroll history. Implementation results demonstrate that previously fragmented payroll administration processes have been consolidated into a single web-based application, while geolocation features facilitate location verification during attendance logging. This research has produced an integrated system that supports the entire payroll workflow, from attendance recording to salary approval. Further research involving structured functional testing and user acceptance evaluation is required to quantitatively assess the system's reliability.

title: Proposal of Stratified Framework for Dental Management of Children with Special Health Care Needs: A Technical Report
container-title: Journal of Advances in Medicine and Medical Research
8b4a4d708a02cffadd66fae59daedc619fbb2e37.abstract: Background: Managing paediatric patients with special health care needs (SHCN) presents significant behavioural and operational challenges in clinical dentistry. Although medical and functional classification systems are available, they may not directly reflect the adaptations and care settings required for dental treatment. Aim: To introduce a four-category stratified clinical framework for classifying children with SHCN according to anticipated dental management requirements. Technical Design: The proposed framework comprises four categories: Category I (Routine Dental Care), for children who can receive care in routine dental settings with minor support; Category II (Modified Dental Care), for children requiring additional behavioural, environmental, communication or accessibility adaptations; Category III (Advanced Dental Care), for children requiring specialised techniques, multidisciplinary coordination or referral to hospital-based dental services; and Category IV (Comprehensive/Complex Dental Care), for children with profound disabilities or life-threatening systemic conditions requiring complex hospital-based dental management. Classification is based on anticipated treatment complexity and necessary modifications to dental care rather than diagnosis alone. Conclusion and Clinical Significance: The proposed four-category framework may support individualised treatment planning, clinical adaptations, referral decisions and communication among dental teams, caregivers and other healthcare professionals. As a conceptual proposal, the framework requires formal validation before its reliability and clinical utility can be established.

title: Longitudinal perspective on the buffering effect of Tai Chi intervention against accumulated perceived stress and its sleep-improving effects among late adolescence
container-title: Frontiers in Pediatrics
d996d64eb821f2c368083e9209de2558fbe15247.abstract: Purpose First-year university students stand at the close of WHO-defined adolescence (10–19 years), in mid-transition: leaving family, entering a new institution, and assuming adult academic and social roles. Stress during adolescence can have consequences that persist into adulthood. Most mental disorders begin by the mid-twenties, while higher levels of adolescent stress predict greater risks of adult anxiety and depression, academic dropout, and lower workforce participation and productivity. The 16-form simplified Tai Chi routine is easy to learn, but direct evidence of its effect in late adolescents is limited. This randomized controlled trial examined its effect on perceived stress and sleep quality. Participants and methods A total of 176 first-year undergraduates, all aged 18 years at baseline, at a university in Hangzhou, China, were randomly allocated 1:1 to a Tai Chi group ( n = 88) or a no-intervention control group ( n = 88). The Tai Chi group practiced the 16-form simplified routine three times weekly for 12 weeks (90 min per session: 30 min of warm-up and 60 min of guided practice); controls maintained their usual lifestyle. Perceived stress (Perceived Stress Scale, PSS-14) and sleep quality (Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index, PSQI) were assessed before and after the intervention. The primary outcomes (PSS-14 and PSQI global scores at week 12) were analyzed by baseline-adjusted analysis of covariance. Results The groups had similar baseline characteristics. All 176 participants completed the PSS-14 and 168 had complete PSQI data. Within groups, both measures improved under Tai Chi (PSS-14 −3.28; PSQI −1.00; both P &lt; 0.01), whereas perceived stress rose in controls (+4.47, P &lt; 0.001) and sleep quality was unchanged. After baseline adjustment, PSS-14 scores were lower in the Tai Chi group (adjusted mean difference −7.48, 95% CI −8.80 to −6.17; P &lt; 0.001), as were PSQI global scores (−1.17, 95% CI −1.87 to −0.46; P = 0.001). Exploratory component analyses gave nominal P &lt; 0.05 for four PSQI components, none of which remained significant after correction for multiple comparisons. Conclusion Compared with no intervention, a 12-week 16-form Tai Chi program lowered perceived stress and improved sleep quality in late adolescents starting university, buffering the stress escalation of the academic semester, and merits multicenter testing against an active comparator.

title: Regulating AI-Generated Inventions in Tanzania: A Comparative Analysis of BRELA and South Africa’s CIPC
container-title: East African Journal of Law and Ethics
97d91fe2e65b9b432b752d3e2552b57b2f5ca94f.abstract: Artificial intelligence systems now produce technical solutions with little or no human contribution to the inventive step, and the DABUS applications filed by Dr Stephen Thaler have tested whether patent law can accommodate an inventor that is not a person. Courts and offices in the United Kingdom, the United States, Europe, Australia and Germany have refused, while South Africa’s Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC) published the grant of a patent naming DABUS as inventor in July 2021. This article asks whether Tanzania’s Business Registrations and Licensing Agency (BRELA) could follow that example under the Patents (Registration) Act, Cap 217, and, if not, what reform is required. Using doctrinal analysis and functional comparison, it finds that the two statutes are closer than is usually assumed: neither defines ‘inventor’, and both require an applicant who is not the inventor to show a right derived from the inventor. The decisive difference is administrative. The South African grant followed a formalities-only check in which, on the published record, the applicant’s entitlement was not tested, leaving validity to revocation proceedings. Section 25(7) and (8) of Cap 217, by contrast, require the Registrar to examine every request for compliance with section 18(3) and (4) and to reject one that is not corrected. An application naming DABUS would therefore fail at the formal stage, and one naming a human who did not devise the invention would be open to invalidation under section 64(2)(d). BRELA cannot reproduce the CIPC outcome by discretion. The article recommends, in order of priority, statements of practice on AI-assisted inventions, revised forms, a statutory definition of inventor and, after regional consultation through ARIPO and the East African Community, a deliberate legislative choice on whether AI-generated inventions should be protected.

title: A Hybrid Convolutional Recurrent Neural Model for Noise Detection and Automated Calibration of Medical Devices via Molecular Vibration Analysis
518557eedb6ff36ea9b47c24553d6afd51c850c8.abstract: Abstract Accurate noise detection and calibration are essential for maintaining the measurement reliability of medical devices. This study proposes a hybrid convolutional recurrent neural network (CRNN) framework for noise detection and automated calibration of ventilators and electrocardiogram (ECG) machines using molecular vibration analysis. A molecular vibration model was developed to characterize mechanical vibration, electromagnetic interference, and environmental conduction noise, achieving an average noise classification accuracy of 96.2%. The proposed CRNN with hybrid attention maintained 91.5% accuracy under low signal-to-noise conditions. A deep deterministic policy gradient-based calibration strategy was subsequently employed to optimize calibration parameters automatically, reducing calibration time by 72.5% and improving calibration accuracy by 78.5% compared with conventional methods. After calibration, the average relative errors were 1.9% for ventilator tidal-volume measurements and 0.92% for QRS-complex amplitude measurements in ECG devices. Cross-device validation achieved 94.3% accuracy across different equipment brands. The results demonstrate that integrating molecular vibration analysis, hybrid deep learning, and automated calibration provides an effective approach for reliable noise detection and precision calibration of medical devices.

title: Artificially influential: examining the impact of virtual influencers on non-followers’ behavior
container-title: Journal of Product & Brand Management
4da0c4c0bae5cfec2fc39e0134174647e2f5faae.abstract: Purpose This study aims to address the limited understanding of how unfamiliar non-followers respond to virtual versus human influencers encountered through algorithmically curated feeds. This study tests whether disclosure that a seemingly human influencer is AI-generated lowers perceived authenticity, producing negative expectation disconfirmation that reduces engagement and purchase intentions. Design/methodology/approach Two between-subjects online experiments with US non-followers (n = 303 and n = 316) were conducted through CloudResearch Connect. Measurement validity was assessed using confirmatory factor analysis in SmartPLS 4, and hypotheses were tested using PROCESS serial mediation analyses with bootstrapping. Findings Across both studies, virtual influencer disclosure significantly lowered perceived authenticity, which generated more negative expectation disconfirmation and reduced engagement intentions. In Study 2, this serial process extended to lower purchase intentions. The hypothesized serial indirect effects were significant. Practical implications Brands using human-presenting virtual influencers with unfamiliar audiences should treat disclosure as expectation management by clearly identifying the influencer as AI-generated or virtual from initial exposure. Managers should also recognize that disclosure may lower perceived authenticity, engagement and purchase intentions. Originality/value This study examines an underexplored stage of virtual influencer exposure involving unfamiliar non-followers. This study broadens the expectation–performance comparison process of expectation disconfirmation theory by showing that, during initial encounters, the comparison standard can derive from category-based expectations formed without prior experience with the focal influencer. Perceived authenticity serves as the evaluative mechanism linking newly revealed information to disconfirmation.

title: Editorial: generative AI and the small business frontier – charting pathways toward meaningful social impact
container-title: Journal of Social Impact in Business Research
c4b06f07519c890d4aa7881d2f5de009595df712.abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine how small and medium-sized enterprises can leverage generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) to create social impact, by developing a multidimensional framework linking GenAI adoption with social-value creation. Design/methodology/approach This editorial adopts a conceptual synthesis approach, that integrates insights from the special-issue papers with emerging research and identifies principal domains of social impact. Findings Social impact is not a property of GenAI but a contingent outcome of how it is applied and adopted. While firms may have similar GenAI potentialities across various impact domains, success is dependent on human, organisational, sectoral and institutional contexts. Practical implications This editorial provides a framework for assessing where GenAI can support social-value creation whilst managing ethical, organisational and workforce risks. Impact accrues through organisational processes rather than through adoption itself. Originality/value The social impact of GenAI is extended beyond productivity and efficiency and positioned as a multidimensional and contingent outcome of technology adoption. A four-element framework links GenAI capability, organisational mechanisms, enabling and constraining conditions and stakeholder outcomes, which then informs a research agenda.

title: Closing the resilience gap: technology adoption and performance challenges in facility management in the USA
container-title: Facilities
5e890a9865ca9ce43afee05896411ba1bee42286.abstract: Purpose Climate change imposes significant stress on the physical and built environment. Facility managers (FMs) are vital to maintaining optimal facility performance, particularly amid the increasing frequency and intensity of natural disasters. Resilient technology can be one of the ways to mitigate the impacts of natural disasters. Therefore, this study aims to investigate adoption trends and analyze the barriers influencing the adoption of resilient technologies among FMs in the USA. This study also examines relationships among organizational characteristics, workforce preparedness indicators and resilient technology adoption and utilization. Design/methodology/approach This research used a cross-sectional research design with a population consisting of FM professionals working in the USA. Data were collected using an online survey, and 45 complete responses from in-house FMs in the USA were analyzed. Findings Resilient technology adoption among FM organizations was predominantly characterized by partial integration, despite high levels of resilience awareness and preparedness. Emergency response systems, energy management systems and advanced HVAC control systems were the most widely adopted technologies. Funding availability and implementation cost emerged as the most influential factors affecting adoption, serving as both key drivers and major barriers. Correlation analysis further indicated that higher levels of technology adoption were associated with longer adoption histories and more frequent technology utilization, while organizational size and annual FM budget were not significantly related to adoption levels. Research limitations/implications This study emphasizes the need to shift resilience research from purely technology-centered evaluations toward socio-technical approaches that integrate facility management processes, organizational context and operational realities. Combining qualitative insights from FMs with quantitative performance data can better explain why resilience technologies succeed or fail in practice. Practical implications From a practical standpoint, strengthening building resilience requires embedding facility management expertise throughout the entire life cycle, supported by cross-disciplinary collaboration, targeted training and governance structures that enable effective data-driven decision-making and accountability. Originality/value Closing the resilience gap in the built environment requires aligning technological innovation with the realities of FM practices. By placing FMs in the center of both research and implementation efforts, the industry can move toward more resilient, adaptive and performance-driven building operations.

title: Beyond dissolution: a lifecycle model of supplier relationship management
container-title: Journal of Business & Industrial Marketing
2722837947789beb8f26e20ab78fbbfe7fcc588f.abstract: Purpose Supplier relationship management (SRM) remains insufficiently understood from a lifecycle perspective. While existing research provides valuable insights into individual SRM activities, it offers limited understanding of how supplier relationships evolve over time and how digitalization supports their management. This study aims to address these gaps by extending the supplier relationship framework of Möller et al. (2006). Design/methodology/approach The study is based on 43 semi-structured interviews with practitioners across multiple industries. This qualitative approach provides in-depth insights into how companies design, manage and digitalize supplier relationships across different phases. Findings The analysis confirms the three established SRM phases – out-supplier management, in-supplier management and in-supplier dissolution management – and extends the framework by identifying two additional phases: sleeping and reactivation. The findings show that SRM is a dynamic and iterative lifecycle characterized by recurring transitions between phases. Furthermore, digital technologies are embedded throughout the lifecycle, supporting information continuity, coordination and more consistent decision-making. Originality/value This study extends Möller et al. (2006) SRM framework by developing an empirically grounded lifecycle model that incorporates sleeping and reactivation phases. It further advances SRM theory by conceptualizing recurring relational and digital touchpoints as mechanisms that support transitions across the supplier relationship lifecycle. Finally, the study contributes to the digitalization literature by demonstrating that digital technologies function as integral governance mechanisms throughout the lifecycle rather than as isolated support tools.

title: When processing feels smooth: brand placement mode and contextual influences on purchase intentions
container-title: Journal of Product & Brand Management
f92c4a79cd2617f0fbe118aa4ebabbbd8f4b19f2.abstract: Purpose This study aims to use processing fluency as an integrative lens to examine why placement prominence does not yield a stable persuasive advantage and how contextual influences shape explicit and implicit placement effectiveness in narrative media. Design/methodology/approach Four between-subjects experiments (2 × 2 factorial designs) were conducted using authentic Korean drama clips. Each study examined one potential disruption source: product category, brand familiarity, endorser image valence or parasocial interaction, comparing explicit and implicit placement with purchase intention as the dependent variable (n = 616). Findings Results were consistent with a processing-fluency explanation. Product category and parasocial interaction (PSI) each interacted with placement mode (ps &lt; 0.001): explicit placement favored search goods and low-PSI characters, whereas implicit placement favored experience goods and high-PSI characters. Brand familiarity moderated effects (p = 0.039), with a larger implicit-placement advantage for unfamiliar brands. The endorser-valence study showed main effects only. Practical implications Managers should tailor placement modes to contextual conditions rather than maximize visibility, reducing potential disruption to viewing experiences and enhancing purchase intentions. Originality/value This research uses contextual processing demands to interpret crossover, asymmetric and additive placement effects beyond specific forms of fit and congruence. The framework complements persuasion-knowledge accounts by considering narrative disruption alongside resistance to persuasive intent. This integrative explanation of prominence’s variable persuasive value requires direct tests of the underlying processes.

title: ESG Performance and Its Disclosures: Evidence on Corporate Profitability from ASEAN-5 Manufacturing Firms
container-title: MARGINAL JOURNAL OF MANAGEMENT ACCOUNTING GENERAL FINANCE AND INTERNATIONAL ECONOMIC ISSUES
a17828e64a1148c81ce9037b57bba8eaf6e28a49.abstract: Growing pressure on firms to demonstrate sustainability has made ESG a central corporate concern, yet evidence on its financial consequences remains mixed, particularly in emerging ASEAN markets. Listed manufacturers across the ASEAN-5 countries are the subject here, with attention to whether ESG performance links to their financial results. The relationship examined in the study is how ROA is affected by ESG performance and its three subcomponents including Environmental, Social, and Governance Disclosure Scores. Using a quantitative approach to explanatory research design, the study uses panel data collected from 744 firm-year observations of manufacturing firms in Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Philippines, and Thailand in the period 2023-2025. Regarding the overall ESG Score, the study finds no support for the hypothesis, as its effect on ROA is negative and statistically significant. Each of the three disclosure scores, namely Environmental, Social, and Governance, behaves differently, producing a positive and statistically significant effect on ROA. What this suggests is that high ESG performance may not necessarily yield high financial performance, while every individual ESG dimension can still affect ROA positively.

title: Allodynia in migraine patients with fibromyalgia comorbidity: focus on small fiber pathology
container-title: Confinia Cephalalgica
51426227d71eff876befe446cf87eb2c2bda1b58.abstract: Background: Cutaneous allodynia is a clinical marker of central sensitization in migraine and is associated with greater migraine severity and poorer outcomes. Fibromyalgia (FM) is a frequent comorbidity of migraine that may further enhance central sensitization, whereas small fibre pathology (SFP) has been identified in a substantial proportion of FM patients. Whether FM comorbidity and peripheral small-fibre abnormalities contribute to cutaneous allodynia in patients with migraine remains unclear. We investigated cutaneous allodynia and migraine characteristics in patients with migraine with and without FM and, within the FM cohort, according to skin biopsy findings. Methods: In this retrospective cross-sectional study, 212 patients with migraine were included: 106 patients with FM who had undergone skin biopsy (65 with pathological and 41 with normal biopsy findings) and 106 patients without FM with the same sex distribution and comparable age. FM and migraine were diagnosed according to current clinical criteria. Cutaneous allodynia was assessed using a standardized clinical checklist. Skin biopsy was performed at the proximal thigh and distal leg, and SFP was defined by reduced intraepidermal nerve fibre density (IENFD). The comparison between patients with and without FM was the primary analysis; comparisons according to skin biopsy findings and correlations with IENFD were secondary analyses. Migraine characteristics, allodynia, and migraine-related disability were compared across groups. Results: The proportion of chronic migraine (CM) was similar in patients with and without FM (19.8% vs. 21.7%; p=0.866). Cutaneous allodynia was more frequent in patients with FM than in those without FM (82.1% vs. 64.2%; p=0.005), and moderate-to-severe allodynia affected 50.9% vs. 16.0% of patients, respectively (p<0.001). Median allodynia scores were 6 (interquartile range [IQR] 4-8) in patients with FM and pathological biopsy findings, 6 (3-7) in those with normal biopsy findings, and 3 (2-5) in patients without FM (p<0.001; ε2=0.133), with no difference between the two FM subgroups; allodynia scores were not associated with proximal or distal IENFD. Greater allodynia was associated with greater migraine-related disability among participants with available Migraine Disability Assessment (MIDAS) data, including after adjustment for age, headache frequency, and FM status (partial ρ=0.267, p=0.002). Conclusions: FM comorbidity identifies patients with migraine with a greater burden of cutaneous allodynia, independently of migraine chronification. This sensory hypersensitivity was not clearly related to the presence or extent of structural small-fibre loss, supporting a predominant contribution of central sensitization. Structural and functional assessments of small fibres, including trigeminal territories, may further clarify the contribution of peripheral abnormalities to migraine-related allodynia in FM.

title: Reconsidering green logistics adoption: the role of perceived behavioral control and ESG information in shippers' selection of logistics service providers
container-title: The International Journal of Logistics Management
f14faa48b238a1f97a4c3ba15c173bb7d87770e2.abstract: Purpose The purpose of this study is to examine how perceived behavioral control and environmental, social and governance (ESG) information shape shippers' adoption of green logistics service providers. Specifically, the study aims to (1) investigate the presence of an intention–behavior gap in green logistics adoption and (2) assess whether ESG information enhances perceived behavioral control, thereby facilitating actual adoption behavior within an extended theory of planned behavior (TPB) framework. Design/methodology/approach The study adopts a quantitative survey-based research design. Data were collected from shippers involved in logistics service provider selection and analyzed using structural equation modeling. The research framework integrates the Theory of Planned Behavior with persuasion theory, incorporating ESG information as an external antecedent influencing perceived behavioral control, behavioral intention and actual adoption behavior. Findings The results show that environmental attitudes significantly influence behavioral intention, while subjective norms do not. Behavioral intention does not directly translate into actual green logistics adoption, indicating a clear intention–behavior gap. Perceived behavioral control has a strong and direct effect on actual adoption behavior. ESG information significantly enhances perceived behavioral control, indirectly strengthening both intention and behavior. Research limitations/implications This study is based on cross-sectional survey data, which limits causal inference. The empirical context focuses on shippers within a specific institutional and regulatory environment, which may affect generalizability. Future research could employ longitudinal designs, cross-country comparisons or experimental approaches to further examine the dynamic role of ESG information in sustainable logistics decision-making. Practical implications The findings suggest that promoting green logistics requires more than fostering pro-environmental intentions. Logistics service providers and policymakers should focus on enhancing shippers' perceived control by improving information transparency, reducing decision uncertainty and strengthening ESG disclosure credibility. ESG ratings can serve as practical decision-support tools that legitimize green logistics choices within organizational governance structures. Originality/value This study contributes original value by reconceptualization green logistics adoption as a control-driven rather than intention-driven process. It extends TPB by identifying perceived behavioral control as the central mechanism in organizational logistics decisions and positions ESG information as a control-enabling governance instrument. This integrated perspective offers a novel theoretical explanation for the persistent intention–behavior gap in sustainable logistics adoption.

title: From reactive to proactive: how artificial intelligence is transforming organizational crisis management
container-title: Journal of Ethics in Entrepreneurship and Technology
db1de318fec5c17ca66a9f918e647042eb8e41f2.abstract: Purpose This paper examines how artificial intelligence (AI) can improve organizational crisis management as firms increasingly operate in a polycrisis marked by overlapping pandemics, geopolitical conflict and rapid technological change. It maps AI capabilities to the before, during and after phases of the crisis lifecycle. Design/methodology/approach This narrative/conceptual review synthesizes empirical and theoretical scholarship on AI in crisis management across management, information systems and crisis communication journals. It integrates evidence on early warning, anticipation, social media analytics, crisis communication and resilience into a lifecycle framework. Findings Before a crisis, AI-driven early warning systems can predict disruptions weeks in advance and help mitigate losses. During a crisis, natural language processing supports situational awareness, and generative AI accelerates communication. After a crisis, social listening and simulation support learning, while deepfake defense protects reputation. Benefits are conditional on governance maturity and complement, rather than replace, human judgment. Practical implications Firms should adopt AI proactively but judiciously for sensing, triage and rehearsal, guided by governance readiness rather than novelty. They should also invest in data governance and interoperability. Organizations should keep accountability and ethical judgment visibly human where trust and empathy matter most. SMEs benefit from modular, centrally supported adoption pathways. Originality/value This paper integrates AI and crisis management into a lifecycle framework centered on the governance conditions that enable AI to improve outcomes. It advances two propositions: (1) AI’s value shifts from augmenting anticipation to substituting risk as authorship becomes visible, and (2) governance maturity moderates, rather than predicts, AI’s crisis-management payoff.

title: From awe to emotional brand attachment: a cognitive appraisal perspective on VR brand experiences
container-title: Journal of Product & Brand Management
2a02739e2da8b57381342589a61ac9c76d3c74b0.abstract: Purpose Prior research on awe in relation to virtual reality (VR) has treated awe as a response to technological stimuli, leaving the consumer appraisals through which awe arises underexplored. Drawing on cognitive appraisal theory, this paper aims to address this gap by investigating whether aesthetic, sensory and content appraisals of a VR brand experience predict awe and whether awe mediates the relationships between these appraisals and emotional brand attachment. Design/methodology/approach Data were collected via a survey of 334 Generation Z participants who experienced an in-person brand encounter via a VR headset and were analysed using covariance-based structural equation modelling in LISREL. Findings Aesthetic, sensory and content appraisals positively predict awe, which, in turn, predicts emotional brand attachment. Awe also mediates the relationships between each of the three appraisal and emotional brand attachment. Originality/value At the intersection of the cognitive psychology of VR and emotional branding, this paper reframes the origins of awe in VR brand experiences, shifting from a stimulus-centred to an appraisal-centred account. It also identifies aesthetic, sensory and content appraisals as the experiential predictors of awe and extends emotional branding to self-transcendent emotions by showing how awe translates experiential appraisals into emotional brand attachment.

title: Radial Kernel Attention for Long-Range Modeling in Polymer Machine Learning Force Fields
569d9c0f37ae1ad406ec120b61cd9e579ab007dc.abstract: We introduce Radial Kernel Attention (RKA) for long-range modeling in polymer machine learning force fields. Local neighbor graphs constrain communication across polymer chains and their surrounding environments, while explicit all-pair attention incurs quadratic cost. RKA maps atomic distances from the cluster centroid to learned radial features and combines their overlap with content-dependent queries and keys. Factorized aggregation and readout enable global feature exchange at linear cost in atom count for fixed feature dimensions. We insert the invariant scalar update between EquiformerV3 local blocks and obtain conservative forces by differentiating the total energy, including its radial coordinate dependence. We evaluate energy and force prediction for finite polymer-derived clusters in OPoly26. Our models are trained on the official training split for 12 epochs and evaluated directly after training on the complete official validation split. A matched 5M comparison shows that RKA reduces per-atom energy and force MAEs by 67.4% and 36.3%, respectively. The 20M RKA model is compared with UMA-S-1.2 and UMA-S-1.2.1 on the same validation structures. The 20M model attains a total-energy MAE of 15.81 meV and a force MAE of 2.619 meV/Å; its per-atom energy MAE is 0.1182 meV/atom. RKA provides a compact global communication pathway that improves energy and force prediction on the evaluated polymer-derived clusters.

title: Board monitoring and the informational content of ESG performance
container-title: Sustainability Accounting, Management and Policy Journal
52844a0dce623244afb7f91364d8fafeb85385d9.abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine whether improvements in environmental, social and governance (ESG) performance are associated with subsequent realised firm outcomes and whether board monitoring conditions these relationships. Using UK FTSE 350 firms, the study evaluates whether year-on-year ESG improvements predict ESG controversies, environmental incidents, investment inefficiency and future operating performance. It further investigates whether stronger board monitoring increases the extent to which ESG improvements are associated with favourable subsequent outcomes. Design/methodology/approach The study uses an unbalanced panel of 314 FTSE 350 firms, comprising 4,396 firm-year observations from 2010 to 2024, with ESG, governance and financial data from LSEG. Panel regressions include industry and year fixed effects with firm-clustered standard errors. Board monitoring is measured using a composite index based on board independence, CEO-chair role separation and board ESG expertise. Robustness tests include disaggregated governance components, an ESG measure excluding the governance pillar, firm fixed effects, lagged specifications and multicollinearity diagnostics. Findings ESG improvements are not consistently associated with subsequent ESG controversies, investment inefficiency or future operating performance. For environmental incidents, however, the interaction between ESG improvement and board monitoring is negative and statistically significant, indicating that the association becomes more favourable as monitoring strengthens. Component-level analyses show similar negative moderation for board independence, CEO-chair separation and ESG expertise, although statistical strength varies. The result also remains when the governance pillar is excluded from the ESG measure. Lagged specifications provide more limited evidence, indicating that the relationship is outcome-specific and not persistent across all time horizons. Research limitations/implications The study focuses on UK listed firms operating within a relatively strong governance environment, which may limit generalisability to weaker institutional settings. The board monitoring index uses equal weighting, although component-level tests reduce concerns regarding this construction. The outcome measures capture specific dimensions of realised firm behaviour and do not directly measure greenwashing, managerial intent or board detection processes. Future research could examine alternative governance measures, weighting schemes, outcome intensity, other institutional settings and additional mechanisms such as ownership structure, executive incentives and external assurance. Practical implications The findings suggest that ESG score improvements should not be interpreted in isolation as evidence of substantive operational change. For boards, the results highlight the importance of effective oversight in linking ESG initiatives to underlying business practices, particularly in environmentally sensitive areas. For investors, ESG changes may be more informative when considered alongside governance characteristics. For regulators and standard setters, the evidence suggests that enhanced ESG disclosure alone may be insufficient unless supported by governance structures that promote accountability and substantive implementation. Social implications The study has broader implications for corporate accountability and stakeholder confidence in ESG information. By showing that ESG improvements are not uniformly associated with realised outcomes, the findings reinforce the need for stronger governance and scrutiny over how sustainability claims relate to actual corporate behaviour. More credible alignment between ESG performance and operational conduct may improve the usefulness of sustainability information for employees, communities, investors and other stakeholders and may help reduce the risk that symbolic improvements are interpreted as evidence of substantive social or environmental progress. Originality/value The study contributes by shifting attention from ESG levels to the informational content of ESG improvements and their association with subsequent realised outcomes. It further shows that this relationship is conditional on board monitoring and differs across outcome types. Unlike studies focused mainly on ESG disclosure or contemporaneous firm value, this study links changes in ESG performance to future adverse events, investment efficiency and operating performance. It also provides new evidence that the environmental-outcome relationship is not solely driven by the construction of the composite monitoring index or mechanical overlap with the ESG governance pillar.

title: Unveiling ESG ratings: corporate perspectives and institutionalisation dynamics
container-title: Sustainability Accounting, Management and Policy Journal
a09cc151f1c0bec0cd6eabb3d0ae1d8201fbc1ba.abstract: Purpose Environmental, social and governance (ESG) ratings have become a central mechanism for assessing, benchmarking and signalling corporate sustainability performance to financial investors. Yet, their widespread use persists despite ongoing criticism of their capacity to accurately reflect firms’ social and environmental contributions. This paper aims to examine this paradox from the perspective of rated companies, exploring why firms continue to engage with ESG ratings despite criticism of their effectiveness, even as investors remain their primary users. Drawing on institutional theory, the authors adopt this underexplored perspective and investigate how ESG ratings become institutionalised within organisations. Design/methodology/approach Based on abductive thematic analysis of 45 semi-structured interviews with sustainability executives from listed European firms, the authors develop a framework distinguishing between substantive and symbolic forms of ESG rating institutionalisation. Findings ESG rating adoption is shaped by institutional pressures and unfolds along a continuum. At one end, firms substantively integrate sustainability considerations into core operations; at the other, ESG ratings are used symbolically to secure external recognition and legitimacy. This study also highlights the risk of deinstitutionalisation if the limitations of ESG ratings remain unaddressed. Practical implications This study offers managers, investors and policymakers insights into navigating ESG pressures and strengthening the credibility of ESG frameworks while providing a diagnostic lens to distinguish symbolic compliance from substantive integration. Social implications While the potential deinstitutionalisation of ESG ratings could erode credibility, accountability and investor trust, substantive adoption could benefit transparency, stakeholder oversight and the diffusion of sustainability norms. Addressing their limitations is therefore crucial for maintaining credibility in the financial sector and directing capital towards companies with meaningful sustainability practices. Originality/value This study extends research on corporate responses to ESG ratings by drawing on institutional theory and developing a conceptual framework of symbolic and substantive institutionalisation from the perspective of rated companies. Specifically, it shifts the explanatory focus beyond firms’ strategic orientations by showing that corporate responses are also shaped by the institutional characteristics and structural limitations of ESG rating systems, thereby advancing the concept of ESG ratings’ deinstitutionalisation.

title: Migrant Culture in Sweden with Focus  on Georgian-Swedish Literary Contacts
მიგრანტული კულტურა შვედეთში: ქართულ-შვედური ლიტერტურული ურთიერთობების მაგალითზე
container-title: სჯანი
f743ecc7bcfba5e6d9fbc4d6d6103305afbae2ba.abstract: The paper takes as its point of departure approaches to the maintenance of language and culture in immigrant communities in Sweden and how members of these communities are encouraged to preserve their home language and cultural iden­tity while also acquiring Swedish. This includes the opportunity for children of Georgian immigrants in Sweden to study Georgian as their home language at school, including the teaching of Georgian culture. Sweden today is a country that has received large groups of immigrants, mos­tly after World War II. The Georgian community in Sweden is relati­vely small and primarily formed during the post-Soviet period. However, Sweden is not only a country of immigration. In earlier periods, from the mid-nineteenth century to the beginning of the twentieth century, Sweden was cha­rac­­terized by extensive emigration from its rural population, primarily to the United States. The paper briefly introduces the Swedish emigrant literature with its most prominent representative, the author Vilhelm Moberg (1898-1973). He has become internationally renowned for his four “Emigrant novels”: (Utvandrarna (The Emig­rants), Invandrarna (The Immigrants), Nybyggarna (The New Land), and Sista brevet till Sverige (The Last Letter Home). The paper notes that the Georgian-Scandinavian literary contacts date back to the end of the nineteenth century. Amid increased Scandinavian interest in the Caucasus during this period, the Danish explorer Olaf Lange included an introduc­tion to Georgian literature and translations of Georgian poetry in his travelogue from the Caucasus (1891), intended to introduce a Danish and broadly Scadinavian audi­ence to the classics of Georgian literature. Despite its relatively small numbers, today’s Georgian community in Sweden actively promotes Georgian-Swedish literary con­tacts. This involves original literary production, with Georgian poet Zurab Rtveliashvili as its best-known representative. He lived in emigration in Sweden from 2010 to 2020. Members of the Georgian community in Sweden are also actively working on translating Georgian literature into Swedish and Swedish literature into Georgian. The catalogues of the central libraries in both countries – Kungliga biblioteket (The National Library of Sweden) and Sakartvelos erovnuli bibliotek’a (The National Library of Georgia) – have been explored to make an inventory of literature trans­lated from Swedish to Georgian and from Georgian to Swedish. More translations have appeared in recent decades, based on translations directly from Swedish and Georgian, the languages of the originals. Some works translated in the Soviet period, used Russian as the mediating language. An important hub for presenting Georgian literature in Sweden is the Malmö-based publishing house Smockadoll, founded by poet and translator Kristian Carl­sson. It has published thirteen Geor­gian titles in Swedish, partly in collaboration with Georgian partners. Smockadoll’s Georgian publications include two books by the emigrant poet Zurab Rtveliashvili, Poesins diktatur (2015) and 150.000 Mega­hertz (2016). Another central publication is a collection of translations of works by 28 modern Georgian poets, Den kaukasiska fallenheten (2018). Swedish literature is well represented in translation to Georgian. Many of the Swedish books in translation have been issued by Sulakauri Publishing in Tbilisi, founded by Bakur Sulakauri, a translator and Swedish specialist. Sulakauri Publishing has a special focus on children’s literature in Swedish, with authors such as Astrid Lindgren, Tove Jansson, and Sven Nordqvist.

title: Trustworthy Federated Clinical Intelligence with Homomorphic Encryption and  Explainable AI
container-title: International Journal on Advanced Computer Engineering and Communication Technology
e9efaf7e4de70a4bb9a5e76e1dc2d37a457ecb6d.abstract: Cross-institutional clinical artificial intelligence is constrained by fragmented patient data, non-identically distributed (non-IID) populations, leakage from shared model updates, and limited interpretability. Federated learning (FL) preserves data locality, but ordinary FL neither makes model updates confidential nor guarantees stable optimization under heterogeneous clients. This paper proposes a defense-in-depth framework that coordinates Federated Proximal (FedProx) optimization, record-level differential privacy (DP), Cheon–Kim–Kim–Song (CKKS) approximate homomorphic encryption, and explainable artificial intelligence (XAI). FedProx limits local model drift; DP-SGD bounds the influence of an individual training record; and CKKS permits weighted aggregation while client updates remain encrypted. A key-separated design keeps the aggregation server from being provisioned with the secret key used to reveal individual contributions; only the aggregate is released for global-model construction. Grad-CAM and SHAP/LIME provide clinician-facing explanations, while an audit dashboard reports convergence, privacy-accounting inputs, encryption status, and systems overhead. We formalize the learning objective, privacy mechanism, encrypted aggregation, threat model, numerical approximation error, communication footprint, and an evaluation protocol spanning IID and controlled non-IID partitions. The contribution is a reproducible system-level co-design and evaluation framework rather than a new cryptographic primitive or optimization algorithm.

title: Forecasting the Feasibility of a Sales Budget Expansion Target in Shipping Logistics: Evidence from PT XYZ
container-title: Journal of Economics and Management Scienties
ef1dae0b8571536b406721c26d2e241ddb417e4a.abstract: Annual sales budgets in shipping logistics are often set by managerial ambition rather than evidence. This study tests whether a 100% incremental sales target is quantitatively feasible, using 36 months of revenue and operational data (June 2023 to May 2026) from PT XYZ, an Indonesian freight forwarding provider. Ten forecasting models in three groups (baseline, statistical and decomposition-based, including Prophet-type and empirical wavelet transform hybrids) were compared on a 12-month hold-out year. The chosen model was re-evaluated to predict revenue for FY2027, and a bootstrap simulation was used to determine the likelihood of achieving the USD 21.99 million target. The simple model performed best, with a MAPE of 9.62%, and none of the decomposition models surpassed the basic benchmarks. It was found that the length of the forecasting period had a greater impact on accuracy than the complexity of the model. The forecast for FY2027 revenue is USD 12.57 million, which is an increase of 14.3%, but this only meets 57% of the target. None of 30,000 simulated outcomes reached the target, which would require operational volumes to grow by 100% to 184%, against a record of 82.7%. An evidence-based committed budget of USD 12.74 million and a stretch budget of USD 13.10 million are proposed. The study links forecasting research with budget target-setting theory by measuring target difficulty before the budget year and offers a transparent procedure that firms with short data histories can replicate.

title:
Readability of German Sustainability Reports: The Role of
                    <scp>ESG</scp>
                    Performance and Audit Committee Characteristics
container-title: Corporate Social Responsibility and Environmental Management
c48a63ebd45ed76089d2d3aa54c6e1dfee2879ae.abstract: ABSTRACT This paper examines whether firms' environmental, social and governance (ESG) performance and audit committee (AC) characteristics—size, number of meetings, attendance rate at meetings, and gender diversity—are associated with the readability of sustainability reports. We measure readability by the German adaptation of the Flesch Reading Ease Score. Drawing on a sample of 524 firm‐year observations of German CDAX firms from 2017 to 2022 obliged to prepare a sustainability report (i.e., large PIEs with more than 500 employees), we estimate multivariate OLS regression models and conduct split‐sample analyses based on whether firms obtain voluntary external assurance. We find that higher ESG performance is associated with greater readability, driven by the social pillar. On average, larger ACs are associated with lower readability, whereas more AC meetings are positively associated with readability. The assurance context matters: among firms that engage an external assurance provider, larger ACs are linked to lower readability, while greater AC gender diversity is positively associated with readability. Among firms without external assurance, where reports are subject to supervisory board review, AC size remains negatively associated, and gender diversity remains positively associated with readability. In contrast, the number of meetings and attendance are each positively associated with readability in this context.

title: AI-Driven Predictive Maintenance for Institutional Electrical Systems
container-title: Journal of Technology and System Information
743e0632b4637f415786ff15de8256d3f95412a3.abstract: High-voltage power distribution networks in institutional settings are increasingly vulnerable to age-related degradation, operational volatility, and unexpected service disruptions. Conventional maintenance practices—dominated by reactive repairs and static time-based servicing—impose significant financial burdens and risk over-servicing intact assets. To address these operational constraints, this study employs a thematic literature synthesis of smart grid prognostics and IIoT asset telemetry (2015–2025) to formulate an end-to-end four-layer predictive maintenance (PdM) framework. The architectural continuum is established by systematically mapping physical multi-sensor acquisition to edge-cloud analytics (GRU and Bi-LSTM engines), dynamic Asset Health Index (AHI) tracking, and automated, cyber-secure Computerized Maintenance Management System (CMMS) dispatch. Synthesizing literature performance baselines reveals that deep bidirectional recurrent networks—notably Bi-LSTM models—achieve superior degradation tracking for Remaining Useful Life (RUL) estimation, attaining an F1-score of 91.0%, a Mean Absolute Error of 4.3%, and a Root Mean Squared Error of 4.2. Furthermore, multi-modal feature fusion significantly sharpens Asset Health Index (AHI) modeling, driving prediction errors down to an RMSE of 0.052, lengthening warning lead times to 37 days, and maintaining false alarm rates at 6.2%. The transition to an AI-enabled prognostic strategy yields up to a 50.0% decrease in overall operational and maintenance costs while extending high-voltage asset longevity by 40%. The inclusion of Explainable AI (SHAP and LRP) alongside robust Operational Technology cybersecurity measures guarantees operational transparency and cyber resilience.

title: The Effects of Proactive Personality, Work–Life Balance, And Perceived Organizational Support On Teachers’ Adaptive Performance: The  Mediating Role of Role Breadth Self-Efficacy  and Job Satisfaction
container-title: International Journal of Science, Technology & Management
e47ce5437561fa863c4febf0cc90b1e56a85299a.abstract: This study examines the effects of Proactive Personality, Work-Life Balance (WLB), and Perceived Organizational Support (POS) on teachers’ Adaptive Performance by investigating the mediating roles of Role Breadth Self-Efficacy (RBSE) and Job Satisfaction. A quantitative approach based on the positivist paradigm was employed. Data were collected from 262 senior high school and vocational high school teachers in Tangerang Regency using purposive sampling and a validated questionnaire. The data were analyzed using Partial Least Squares–Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) with SmartPLS 4.0. The findings indicate that Proactive Personality, Work-Life Balance, and Perceived Organizational Support have positive and significant effects on Role Breadth Self-Efficacy and Job Satisfaction. Furthermore, Role Breadth Self-Efficacy and Job Satisfaction significantly enhance teachers’ Adaptive Performance, supporting the proposed structural model. The study highlights the importance of integrating individual characteristics, work-life balance, and organizational support in strengthening teachers’ adaptability to changing work demands. These findings contribute to the human resource management literature in the education sector by providing empirical evidence on the mechanisms through which psychological and organizational factors improve Adaptive Performance.

title: Sclerotinia sclerotiorum : a dual‐purpose biological control agent for weed and disease management in pastures and cereal crops
container-title: Pest Management Science
745c4b989e8c03387e904e9cf6b8ee8d0263df6f.abstract: Abstract The cosmopolitan phytopathogenic fungus Sclerotinia sclerotiorum (Lib.) de Bary infects many dicotyledonous species, including major crops and weeds. Its virulence toward key pasture weeds and the innate immunity of grasses has motivated research in North America and New Zealand into its potential as a microbial bioherbicide for pastures. Independently, discovery in China that S. sclerotiorum adopts a symptomless endophytic lifestyle in grasses protecting them against fungal diseases has stimulated research into its potential as a cereal crop vaccine. Together, these findings raise the prospect of deploying a single fungal strain as a broad‐spectrum biological tool for integrated weed and disease control in pastures and cereals, challenging long‐held assumptions about the ecological roles and applied value of this pathogen. We evaluate S. sclerotiorum as the active ingredient of such a dual‐purpose biocontrol product using four foundational pillars for success—hypervirulence (efficacy), low production cost, formulation suitability and biosafety. Wild‐type strains are sufficiently virulent and competent endophytic mutualists, whereas microsclerotia offer a cost‐effective scalable active ingredient alternative to mycelium. Further innovation is needed to optimize industrial‐scale production and formulation. To meet biosafety requirements, we propose developing a non‐sclerotia‐forming strain retaining hypervirulence and endophytic competence. © 2026 The Author(s). title: TECHNOLOGICAL EMPOWERMENT AND VALUE BALANCE: DUAL PATHWAYS IN CHINA’S TECHNOLOGY GOVERNANCE POLICIES FOR THE AI ERA
container-title: Trends in Social Sciences and Humanities Research
046a4b825efe15b9ca51cb520c373729b94ebde6.abstract: The deep embedding of artificial intelligence (AI) technology is reshaping global governance. The tension between “technological empowerment” and “value balance” has become a common governance challenge for countries worldwide. Based on a dual-pathway framework of “technology-driven modernization of state governance” and “technology-embedded multi-actor social co-governance,” this paper systematically analyzes the internal logic and operational mechanisms of technology governance in China in the AI era. The study finds that China’s technology governance is not a single efficiency-oriented application of technology; rather, through the coordinated operation of dual pathways, it comprehensively achieves four major governance functions: efficiency improvement, equity promotion, security assurance, and institutional reconstruction. In terms of model characteristics, China has developed a distinctive paradigm centered on “enabling governance”-one that takes state capacity as its foundation, institutional flexibility as its safeguard, and plural public values as its goals. This paradigm transcends the single efficiency-oriented governance logic of the West and offers a non-Western pathway with both theoretical inspiration and practical reference for global digital governance. This paper argues that the core of “enabling governance” lies in resolving the tension between technological empowerment and value balance through institutional design, and that the transferability of its experience depends on the conditions of fit in specific institutional contexts.

title: Recognising patterns of vulnerability in a seagrass-dependent social-ecological system to support place-based management
b994a6259e14985d113cffb75312e1221d6c5705.abstract: Seagrass social-ecological systems are increasingly demonstrated to contribute to the well-being, livelihood opportunities and local economies of millions of people across coastlines globally. Seagrasses are also recognised for supporting endangered, culturally significant biodiversity and fisheries species. In the Palk Bay, Tamil Nadu region of southern India, we use a vulnerability framework to explore household and village scale sensitivity, exposure and adaptive capacity to social-ecological shocks. Through village consultations and household and key informant interviews with seagrass-dependent fishers, we reveal household- and village- scale vulnerabilities which can be grouped to present potential pathways towards social-ecological resilience. We found that fishing was the primary livelihood of most surveyed households and limited other livelihood options were reported. Households where fishing was the primary livelihood were found to be more sensitive to change than households with alternate primary livelihoods. At a village scale, exposure, sensitivity and adaptive capacity varied independently. Trends in adaptive capacity and exposure were used to inform categorisation of villages into a four-part management complex: priority support sites, co-management opportunity sites, preventative support sites, and stewardship or learning sites. In doing so, this work provides tailored approaches to bottom-up, place-based management in a data-poor small-scale fishery system.

title: Farm practice typologies as a strategy for management-relevant land use and land cover mapping in the Great Lakes Region
container-title: Scientific Reports
4708aba7e9d3ea3bd12d3730292d27a787832e9d.abstract: Abstract The Great Lakes region (GLR) is dominated by agricultural land use, characterized by diverse land use and land cover (LULC), land management practices (LMPs), and, in turn, diverse land processes. Conventional LULC classification systems often rely on coarse categorizations, summarized into spatial units that are either unmeaningful to management or lack the fidelity to capture human-driven heterogeneity relevant to environmental outcomes. Furthermore, most LULC systems are temporal snapshots, agnostic to the spatial dependencies of temporal land-use transitions and fail to provide an inventory of the diversity of land use and management within regions. Hence, we developed a multi-year integrated typology framework by combining LULC class transitions (2008–2023) with trends in LMPs, to characterize these differences in the landscape, using inductively developed, threshold-based classification rules at the farm-parcel level.​ Our multi-year integrated typology combined LULC and LMP classes to yield a total of 135 unique land types for the GLR, capturing sufficient variation in agricultural management and landscape heterogeneity that is not reflected in conventional LULC products. Staple Crop Rotation – Tile Drained (StRot-TD) and Staple Crop Rotation – Conventional (StRot-Con) emerged as the dominant multi-year integrated typologies across the GLR. Across three threshold scenarios in sensitivity analysis, 84.27%, 99.01% and 83.43% of parcels retained LULC transition, LMPs trend and multi-year integrated typology classes respectively. The diversity of annual integrated typology increased over time due to the complexity of land use and management practices, even though it decreased for conventional LULC. To demonstrate the practicality of our approach, we used linear mixed-effects models, which compare the performance of our annual integrated typology relative to conventional LULC classifications in predicting water-quality parameters (phosphorus, nitrite, and Kjeldahl nitrogen) in streams draining agricultural watersheds. The annual integrated typology models achieved lower RMSE and higher R 2 than conventional LULC models in the validation for phosphorus, nitrite, and Kjeldahl nitrogen, supporting the predictive value of combining the management attributes in the case study. The framework offers a flexible, interpretable tool for landscape characterization, agricultural planning, conservation implementation, and informed decision-making, and is replicable across regions.

title: From Contested Endogenization to Regulatory Unravelling of Mandatory Human Rights Due Diligence: Extending the Endogeneity of Law Framework
container-title: Journal of Management Studies
d381e7503f63d03046c06e7f0bec55419f948c55.abstract: Abstract Drawing on the endogeneity of law framework, this study examines how business, legal, public, and civil society actors constructed the meaning and practice of mandatory human rights due diligence in the context of the German garment industry and the German Supply Chain Act. Using interview, document, and observation data spanning the period 2019 to 2026, our findings reveal a two‐stage process: an initial phase of contested endogenization in which actors experienced with private regulation prevented convergence on a managerialized interpretation of the law, followed by regulatory unravelling in which changes in the political‐economic climate provided avenues for substantively weakening the law and preventing its implementation. We discuss how the dual processes of managerializing a law and legalizing of organizations is complicated by three boundary conditions: the complexity of the regulatory issue, the field's regulatory maturity, and the degree of regulatory uncertainty. Connecting the endogeneity of law framework with research on the public and private governance of global supply chains allows us to theorize refinements to this framework when applied to contested, complex governance fields, and to derive a set of theoretical and practical implications for public supply chain regulation.
