title: tModBase v2.0: an expanded database of tRNA modifications with an AI-powered assistant
container-title: Nucleic Acids Research
6dc27bcf3717dbf61b825aaa6a0d910a0b11a2a6.abstract: Abstract Chemical modifications of transfer RNAs (tRNAs) are crucial for tRNA stability, codon decoding, translational fidelity, and tRNA-derived small RNA (tsRNA) biogenesis. Changes in these modifications are associated with stress responses, physiological regulation, and human disease, underscoring the need to integrate modification information with experimental evidence and biological context. We previously established tModBase, a web resource to organize and explore tRNA modification-related data. Its first release integrated modification sites, high-throughput sequencing-derived signals, and condition-dependent changes. Since then, tRNA profiling has expanded through modification-specific and direct RNA sequencing strategies, with rapidly growing datasets across species and conditions. Here, we present tModBase v2.0 (http://www.tmodbase2.com/), containing 528 datasets across 23 species, 40 sequencing and library-preparation methods, and 42 modification types. It includes 68 third-generation and 210 modification-specific sequencing datasets, extending coverage of direct-RNA and modification-specific approaches. tModBase v2.0 further integrates sequencing-derived signals, condition-dependent information, and biological annotations linking modifications with enzymes, genetic variants, tsRNAs, diseases, and expression profiles. The LLM- and retrieval-augmented generation-powered assistant tModBot enables natural-language exploration across database modules while grounding responses in retrieved tModBase evidence. tModBase v2.0 therefore provides an expanded resource for investigating the diversity, dynamics, and biological context of tRNA modifications.

title: The mediating role of self-efficacy in the relationships of technophilia and positive emotional experience with perceived learning effectiveness in AI-supported EFL education
container-title: Discover Artificial Intelligence
1e046e91cd43fe005cca1d83a4437e55e4d42551.abstract: Abstract Despite the increasing integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into English as a Foreign Language (EFL) education, the psychological mechanisms linking learners’ technological dispositions and emotional experiences to perceived learning effectiveness remain undertheorized and empirically underexplored. This study examined whether self-efficacy served as a statistical mediator in the relationships of technophilia and positive emotional experience with perceived learning effectiveness in AI-supported EFL education. A cross-sectional survey was conducted involving 234 students enrolled in English-language courses at a private college of health sciences. Adapted multi-item scales on technophilia, positive emotional experience, self-efficacy, and perceived learning effectiveness were administered. Structural equation modeling with bootstrapping (5000 resamples) was used to examine direct and indirect associations. Self-efficacy demonstrated the strongest direct association with perceived learning effectiveness (β = 0.375, p = 0.001). Positive emotional experience was strongly associated with self-efficacy (β = 0.624, p < 0.001), and its indirect association with perceived learning effectiveness through self-efficacy was significant (β = 0.234, 95% CI [0.128, 0.351]). Technophilia was also positively associated with self-efficacy (β = 0.307, p = 0.002), and its indirect association with perceived learning effectiveness through self-efficacy was significant. The findings were consistent with self-efficacy partially mediating both relationships. These findings suggest that learners’ confidence in managing AI-supported tasks plays an important role in linking affective dispositions to perceived effectiveness appraisals. The study contributes to computer-assisted language learning (CALL) research by clarifying how positive orientation toward AI-supported technologies, emotional experience, and efficacy beliefs jointly relate to learners’ perceptions of effective AI-supported language learning. Pedagogically, the findings suggest that progressively scaffolded practice and mastery-oriented AI tasks may strengthen self-efficacy and improve learners’ perceived effectiveness in AI-supported EFL environments.

title: Role of Artificial Intelligence in Disease and Pest Management in Cauliflower: A Review
container-title: International Journal of Plant & Soil Science
f6d9a7d2865720ba3912565ea2b876139ac95423.abstract: Cauliflower (Brassica oleracea var. botrytis L.) is a nutritionally important cole vegetable and a high-value component of intensive vegetable production. Its yield and market quality are frequently reduced by bacterial, fungal and oomycete diseases and by insect pests that cause direct feeding injury or facilitate secondary infections. Conventional disease and pest surveillance is largely dependent on visual scouting, expert diagnosis and periodic field observations. These approaches remain indispensable, but they can be labour-intensive, subjective and difficult to scale over large production areas. Artificial intelligence (AI), including machine learning, deep learning, computer vision, image segmentation, object detection, remote sensing and predictive analytics, offers a complementary approach for rapid and repeatable crop-health assessment. This review examines the potential role of AI in cauliflower disease and pest management, covering image acquisition, disease classification, lesion localisation, severity estimation, insect identification, automated counting, forecasting, smartphone applications, UAV-based surveillance and AI-enabled integrated pest management. Cauliflower-specific research has demonstrated promising performance of deep-learning models. The Cauli-Det modified YOLOv8 system reported precision of 93.2%, recall of 82.6% and mean average precision of 91.1% for bacterial soft rot, downy mildew and black rot in its experimental dataset (Uddin et al., 2024). Another recent cauliflower study reported 99.85% classification accuracy using EfficientNet-B3 under its experimental conditions (Malik et al., 2025). Broader plant-disease research also demonstrates strong potential for CNNs and transfer learning (Mohanty et al., 2016; Ferentinos, 2018), while pest-detection research supports automated insect recognition and monitoring (Thenmozhi & Reddy, 2019; Chakrabarty et al., 2026). However, field variability, limited crop-specific datasets, class imbalance, symptom similarity, model explainability, computational requirements and inadequate independent validation remain major constraints. Future research should integrate AI predictions with weather, crop stage, pest abundance, disease severity and economic thresholds so that the technology supports practical, affordable and environmentally responsible IPM in cauliflower.

title: Rethinking B‐BBEE Policy Implementation: A Systematic Review of Regulatory Frameworks and Inclusive MSME Development in South Africa
28a541d0da6cadcc9d6730e91e5eaed4be476bbc.abstract: Introduction: Broad-Based Black Economic Empowerment (BBBEE) is intended to address apartheid-era exclusion through ownership, skills development, preferential procurement, enterprise development and wider economic participation. Its relationship with inclusive Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprise (MSME) development, growth and sustainability remains contested because access to benefits is uneven and implementation may privilege formal compliance over substantive transformation.Methods: The researcher-selected databases and information sources were Google Scholar, ERIC. The eligibility protocol restricted publication years to 2015–2026. The exact calendar date of search execution was not recorded in the verified identification provenance; this is distinct from the publication-year eligibility range. Google Scholar and ERIC were the researcher-selected information sources. The eligibility period was 2015–2026.Results: B-BBEE provides an inclusion-oriented policy route and can support finance, women’s empowerment, enterprise development and procurement access. However, benefits are conditional and uneven. Compliance burdens, regulatory instability, weak institutional capacity, fronting, corruption, elite capture and symbolic compliance constrain inclusive outcomes. Enterprise and supplier development are most promising when linked to capability building, meaningful operational participation, transparent procurement, finance, quality systems, long-term relationships and coordinated stakeholder support. Direct evidence on long-term MSME survival and micro-enterprise outcomes remains limited.Discussion/Conclusion: BBBEE is neither uniformly ineffective nor consistently developmental. Its contribution to inclusive MSME growth depends on whether regulatory compliance is connected to measurable, broad-based and sustainable productive outcomes. A reoriented framework should reduce navigational burdens, strengthen accountability and monitor enterprise-level outcomes rather than relying primarily on scorecard attainment.

title: Generative AI and Employment Concerns Among AI Aware Respondents in Bangladesh
2175796b9a04ec3e661e8e64d03823c1cc031301.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) may change professional tasks, but the implications for workers depend on how technology is introduced and how people adapt. This study examines stated perceptions of task change, concern about routine work and AI-related learning in 385 adult, AI-aware questionnaire records from Bangladesh. Most respondents were recorded as law students, and the dataset does not establish that all participants were employed or young professionals. The questions do not directly measure current job security or the effects of AI exposure on employment. Individual items are therefore analysed separately using response distributions, paired endorsement comparisons and exploratory rank correlations. Of 385 respondents, 232 (60.3%) agreed that AI may reduce demand for some routine professional tasks; 307 (79.7%) agreed that learning to work effectively with AI could reduce their future job-security concerns; and 211 (54.8%) anticipated new tasks requiring human judgement and oversight. A total of 184 respondents endorsed both the routine-task concern and the potential reassurance of learning. These statements differ in meaning and do not establish whether training actually reduces insecurity. Exploratory correlations were small and should not be interpreted causally. Job demands-resources theory, psychological contract theory and career construction provide complementary lenses rather than validated models. The study distinguishes concern about tasks from concern about losing a job and identifies the need for independently verified employment status, recruitment documentation and direct measures of perceived job security in future research.

title: The Paradox of Algorithmic Sycophancy: Sycophancy in Large Language Models and the Limits of AI-Mediated Knowledge Reconstruction in the Metacognitive Creative Destruction Model
f31f456f51b7580c96613027043ba5bcb62c702c.abstract: The Metacognitive Creative Destruction (MCD) model approaches educational innovation as a perpetual spiral process. Contradiction (accumulated cognitive conflicts that resist interpretation), activates Metacognitive Capacity, enabling Destructive Unlearning Propensity, the conscious abandonment of outdated mental schemas, which in turn enables Creative Reconstruction Ability, and ultimately, new knowledge. In the model’s empirical validation with 1,498 teachers, a critical finding emerged: AI Augmentation Intensity (AIA) predicted Metacognitive Capacity (MC) and Creative Reconstruction Ability (CRA), but not Destructive Unlearning Propensity (DUP).This article argues that this finding is not accidental, but reflects an inherent weakness of modern AI systems, and more specifically, the tendency toward AI Sycophancy. Models trained with reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) tend to avoid disagreements and be likable to the user, preventing the individual from experiencing cognitive conflicts, perpetuating their already formed beliefs at the expense of scientific accuracy.Therefore, in an environment of “algorithmic flattery”, the necessary contradictions that trigger unlearning are not produced. Based on the MCD model, it is concluded that the absence of unlearning, that is, the deliberate and conscious abandonment of outdated beliefs, mental models and practices, makes the reconstruction of knowledge absolutely superficial and thus, algorithmically condescending interaction does not produce deep and authentic knowledge, regardless of AI Augmentation Intensity.

title: SAGE-AIP: A Scale-Adaptive Gated Ensemble Framework for Predicting AI Adoption and Productivity Across Multiple Data Scales
5358271a89a3a9d9de2f5155abb8bccaa93cc9ce.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is frequently associated with productivity improvement, yet empirical conclusions depend on where AI exposure is measured, how productivity is defined, and which model is used. This study develops a multi-scale comparative framework using three datasets: 145,000 AI-adoption records from 10 countries and eight industries; 2,074 observed country-year records from 233 country or regional units (2015–2023); and 150 employee-level observations. Robust regression, country fixed effects, dynamic fixed effects, and difference-GMM sensitivity analysis are combined with a proposed Scale-Adaptive Gated Ensemble Framework for AI Adoption and Productivity (SAGE-AIP), which is benchmarked against six established regressors using temporal holdouts for the two longitudinal datasets and a train–test split for the employee data. The adoption dataset shows almost no systematic structure (R2 = 0.00018), and SAGE-AIP does not improve on simpler models there (test RMSE 28.976 vs. 28.900 for Elastic Net). In the global panel, automation intensity is strongly associated with AI-attributed productivity (β = 19.882, SE = 0.434), and SAGE-AIP attains the lowest test RMSE (4.448; R2 = 0.544). At the employee level, recorded AI-tool information remains positively associated with productivity (β = 0.905, SE = 0.220), but Random Forest outperforms SAGE-AIP (test RMSE 0.435 vs. 0.583). SAGE-AIP is therefore not uniformly superior; its value is scale-specific, which supports evaluating models across data scales rather than relying on a single dataset or model class.

title: Regulatory Compliance Requirements, Administrative Burden, Operational Costs and Compliance Efficiency Among SMEs: A Systematic Review
2d721a9226b6db6fdcb746e3960c69fca287b5cf.abstract: Introduction: Small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) may experience regulatory compliance requirements as relatively high fixed costs because managerial time, documentation, specialist expertise and financial resources are limited. The supplied literature also suggests that simplification, digitalisation and proportionate regulation may improve compliance efficiency, although deregulation can create risks for oversight and public-interest protection.Methods: The researcher-selected databases and information sources were Google Scholar, ERIC. The eligibility protocol restricted publication years to 2015–2026. The exact calendar date of search execution was not recorded in the verified identification provenance; this is distinct from the publication-year eligibility range. Google Scholar and ERIC were the researcher-selected information sources for English-language peer-reviewed publications dated 2015–2026.Results: The synthesis generated seven codes, three categories, two descriptive themes and four analytical themes. Compliance was commonly associated with disproportionate administrative and financial burden, particularly where requirements were complex, fragmented, frequently changing or inconsistently enforced. Digital services, interoperable registers, automation, training and institutional support could reduce manual work and improve transparency, but their benefits depended on implementation capacity and system fit. Simplification and deregulation supported access and innovation in some contexts but required safeguards. Compliance could also improve formalisation, reporting accuracy, legitimacy and stakeholder assurance.Discussion/Conclusion: The evidence supports proportionate, risk-sensitive and coordinated compliance rather than deregulation alone. Policy effectiveness depends on regulatory coherence, institutional capability, SME knowledge, digital infrastructure, accessible guidance and meaningful consultation.

title: Tidal City Intelligence: A Conceptual Framework for AI-Enabled Service Governance in Cities with Fluctuating Populations
9125839bb912dfa67489dd5a63f2a2fd021e86f5.abstract: Many cities serve far more people than their civil register counts, and the gap rises and falls with tourist seasons, holidays, pilgrimages and festivals. Municipal budgets, staffing and data systems are nonetheless sized to the register. This conceptual paper introduces the Tidal City, a city whose population present swings in recurring, largely predictable cycles that change how public services must be planned. We distinguish the concept from the service population, tourism seasonality and overtourism; propose a two-part Tidal Index measuring the swing’s amplitude and regularity; and offer a typology of seasonal, day-visitor and event-driven tidal cities. Drawing on dynamic capabilities and adaptive governance theory, we set out Tidal City Intelligence, a four-layer framework (Sense, Anticipate, Adapt, Govern) describing the data and AI capabilities a local government needs, and derive testable propositions for each layer. Published data from Pattaya, Thailand, put the average population present at roughly two to three times the registered population and show annual waste moving with guest arrivals while the register barely changed. With only annual guest data, the case illustrates load and demand regularity rather than the full index. The paper offers cities a common measure of the problem and researchers an empirical agenda.

title: Forward-Looking Information Disclosure: A Prisma-Based Systematic Literature Review
4d423273bb89e379c0fb7de8afcb49915878307e.abstract: The purpose of this systematic literature review (SLR) was to use the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) framework to systematically evaluate the literature on FLID and identify emerging research gaps. A systematic search was conducted in two major academic databases (Scopus & Web of Science) using predefined inclusion or exclusion criteria. The dominant theoretical frameworks identified are the Agency Theory and Impression Management Theory to explain the board's dual role to monitor and control agent behaviour while controlling and managing strategic representation through dissemination of future-oriented information and management of agency cost and information asymmetry. Other relevant theoretical frameworks include the Resource-Based View theory which provides insight into how internal resources affect FLID, Legitimacy theory which explains how stakeholder expectations affect FLID and Signalling theory which informs how information asymmetries influence FLID. The majority of previous studies on FLID were conducted in developed countries specifically in the United States. Research on this topic in developing countries such as Malaysia appears to be underrepresented. This study has identified several avenues for the potential use of alternative communication methods with respect to the examination of FLID in a post COVID-19 world that may include increased levels of uncertainty.

title: Hybrid TensorRT–PyTorch Inference Acceleration for Attention-Based CNNs with Dynamic ROI Sampling: A Case Study on Jetson Nano
2356aca907e0d5b1b6084ccaae24703cb4766568.abstract: Edge AI deployment requires low-latency inference on devices with tight constraints in size, weight, power, and cost. NVIDIA TensorRT accelerates inference through layer fusion, precision reduction, and kernel auto-tuning, but a model containing even one unsupported operator cannot be compiled into a single engine. This paper presents a hybrid TensorRT–PyTorch deployment in which the supported subnetworks run as TensorRT engines while the unsupported operations fall back to native PyTorch, and applies it to an attention-based convolutional neural network (ACNN) whose region-of-interest sampling operators are unsupported. On an NVIDIA Jetson Nano, the hybrid approach reduced the end-to-end latency of ACNN-dsc, the fastest native PyTorch model, from 38.37 ms to 20.40 ms (1.88×) under FP32. Under FP16, the hybrid ACNN-k3 achieved the lowest latency of 17.78 ms, a 2.23× speedup over its PyTorch FP32 counterpart and 2.16× over the fastest PyTorch model. Stepwise profiling of the image preprocessing pipeline showed that transferring raw images and performing most conversions on the GPU more than halves preprocessing latency. Further analyses across devices, precisions, and frameworks show that practical latency on edge AI accelerators depends on hardware and runtime factors beyond FLOPs and model size.

title: Understanding Virtual Gifting Behavior on UGC Video Platforms: The Roles of Mukbang Content Values and Danmaku Engagement
98d2a1836986af9b6707bf40c15bb75635c80150.abstract: Virtual gifting has become a crucial mechanism for digital content platforms to achieve commercialization. However, existing research has largely approached gifting behavior through creator-centric frameworks and treated user interactions as homogeneous signals, leaving the inherent value of digital content and the multi-dimensional nature of danmaku engagement underexplored. To fill this gap, this study examines the impact of different dimensions of mukbang UGC consumption values and danmaku engagement on virtual gifting amounts in non-real-time content consumption scenarios, and further analyzes the mediating role of video popularity. We collected panel data from the Bilibili platform, and used panel fixed-effects models and bootstrap methods for hypothesis testing. The results show that different dimensions of UGC consumption values and danmaku engagement have heterogeneous impacts on content dissemination performance and economic performance, while video popularity plays a selective mediating role. This study refines the Theory of Consumption Values by revealing its differentiated behavioral conversion in digital content settings, advances the decoupling perspective between content virality and monetization, conceptualizes danmaku as heterogeneous social signals, and extends virtual gifting research to asynchronous environments where content-centered mechanisms take precedence over creator-driven dynamics.

title: AI Model Energy and Carbon Disclosure: A Source-Audited Study of 103 Releases (2024-2026)
59d3047d593bdd3064939431188715f273b686fc.abstract: AI model cards and release documents are supposed to help people assess models. For energy and carbon, they often leave out the number a reader needs, or print figures that cannot be compared directly. I built the Release Energy Ledger, a source-traceable record of 161 distinct developer releases, and audited a selected set of 103 dated 2024-2026 releases that passed a page check. On the designated release document, 85 (82.5 percent) print no energy, carbon or compute figure, 1 prints compute only, and 17 (16.5 percent) print an energy or carbon-related figure: 16 training-specific and 1 life-cycle footprint. None prints release-specific inference energy. Meta accounts for 10 of the 17; without Meta, the count is 7 of 93. The figures differ in method, unit, equipment boundary and emissions accounting, and only 8 of the 17 state a basis, a boundary and a method together. Changing the unit of analysis gives 11 of 80 documents, 10 of 59 model families and 7 of 23 developers. The strict-quote subset (5 of 74) is a different evidence frame, not a lower bound. A page re-read confirmed the printed figures for all 17; blinded AI coding agreed with the ledger on 91.9 to 100 percent of fields, and a separately instructed AI adjudicator agreed on 42 of 42 selected cells. These results describe the documents in this selected set, not actual emissions, the universe of releases or legal compliance. No human has validated any label. The ledger and counting script are released with the paper as a versioned data record (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23808341).

title: Compression‐Resilient, Resolution‐Vulnerable: A Statistical Robustness Analysis of EfficientNet‐B2 for AI‐Generated Image Detection
40c90e02b219b35a0c83b43f046473f558552e91.abstract: Reliable classification of AI-generated images requires more than high accuracy on unmodified test examples: media files may be compressed or downsampled before forensic analysis. This paper presents a controlled, paired robustness evaluation of a previously developed EfficientNet-B2 detector using RGB, fast Fourier transform (FFT), and artifact-oriented image features. The existing checkpoint, validation-selected classification threshold, and fixed set of 6,000 held-out images were reused without training or test-time threshold adjustment. Six transformed conditions were evaluated against original inputs: JPEG qualities 90, 70, and 50, and bicubic downsampling to maximum dimensions of 256, 128, and 64 pixels followed by reconstruction to the original dimensions. The baseline achieved 94.53% accuracy and 0.9857 area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC). JPEG variants produced accuracies between 94.38% and 94.63%, with paired 95% bootstrap intervals of accuracy change spanning zero. By contrast, downsampling to 256, 128, and 64 pixels yielded accuracies of 93.15%, 91.73%, and 74.40%, respectively. At 64 pixels, the accuracy difference was −20.13 percentage points (95% paired bootstrap interval approximately −21.12 to −19.12), and AUROC fell to 0.8967. The evidence indicates substantially greater sensitivity to severe spatial resolution loss than to the tested JPEG compression settings. Because the existing training procedure incorporates JPEG augmentation, these findings characterize this detector and evaluation protocol rather than establish universal robustness across detectors or unseen transformations.

title: The Effect of Internal Integration on Operational Performance with Supply Chain Capability Mediation
container-title: MARGINAL JOURNAL OF MANAGEMENT ACCOUNTING GENERAL FINANCE AND INTERNATIONAL ECONOMIC ISSUES
7c5e4fb3fcf218b8ec2f8734f02aefcc77a4ec41.abstract: The rapid growth of the coffee shop industry in the Special Region of Yogyakarta has increased competition and requires MSMEs to have efficient and adaptive operational performance. This situation calls for integrated internal process management and supply chain capabilities that are responsive. The setting of this inquiry is coffee shop micro, small, and medium enterprises in the Special Region of Yogyakarta, and it investigates the manner in which internal integration shapes operational performance, positioning supply chain capability as an intervening (mediating) variable. An explanatory quantitative design was adopted, executed through a cross-sectional survey. Two hundred respondents were handpicked via purposive sampling, comprising proprietors, supervisors, and staff members who are personally engaged in operational and supply chain undertakings. Information was gleaned by means of a structured questionnaire and then processed with Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (SEM-PLS) through the SmartPLS application. The evaluation began with the measurement model, appraised via convergent validity, discriminant validity, and construct reliability, and proceeded to the structural model, which was examined through R-square coefficients and a bootstrapping procedure. According to the empirical findings, internal integration favorably and significantly affects both supply chain capability and operational performance. Supply chain capability, in turn, positively and significantly impacts operational performance and simultaneously functions as a partial mediator connecting internal integration to operational performance. Such outcomes corroborate that fortifying internal integration, buttressed by adaptable supply chain capability, constitutes an indispensable strategy for durably elevating the operational performance of coffee shop MSMEs.

1d8c4bd46dcdf5e5ffd22feec73804a9a5d99426.abstract: Patent foramen ovale (PFO) is present in some people, and PFO may lead to cryptogenic stroke. How to identify the causal relationship between PFO and cryptogenic stroke and how to assess the risk of stroke recurrence remain clinical challenges. We reviewed the related mechanisms, diagnosis, relevant biomarkers and the risk assessment of PFO-associated stroke. We also discussed recent advances in PFO closure and its potential indications. Further researches are needed on post-closure medical management and the use of PFO closure in patients over 60 years of age.

title: Can a Brief Online Intervention Raise Adolescents’ STEM Expectancy and Values? A Four-Arm Randomized Trial of Goal Setting and Role Modeling
bbacfc137394830b388aa3535de2fa8b0f4ae8a0.abstract: Adolescents’ expectancies and subjective task value beliefs for STEM decline across secondary school, yet few trials have compared different intervention components for enhancing these beliefs within the same trial. This four-arm randomized trial, framed by situated expectancy-value theory, compared brief online interventions focused around goal setting, role modeling, their combination, and an active control. Participants were 855 Year 9 students (401 female, 454 male; M age = 14.68) across six Australian schools (3 urban, 3 rural). Outcomes were expectancy, intrinsic value, utility value, and perceived cost for STEM overall and, in exploratory analyses, for biology, chemistry, and physics. Compared to the control condition, the goal-setting-only condition produced higher post-intervention expectancy (Δ = 0.17, q = .034) and intrinsic value (Δ = 0.18, q = .034) but not utility value. Role modeling alone produced no significant benefit after statistical correction. The combined condition raised expectancy but also perceived cost. No gender interaction was significant. In rural (compared to urban) schools, exploratory analyses showed that, relative to the active control, goal setting alone raised utility value (Δ = 0.46, q &lt; .001) and role modeling alone raised expectancy (Δ = 0.11, q &lt; .001). Exploratory subject-specific analyses showed similar goal-setting gains. Results suggest that a brief, structured online goal-setting sequence can raise adolescents’ immediate STEM expectancy and intrinsic value, warranting longer-term follow-up.

title: Kimchi as Korean fermented-food heritage in everyday meal practices: a qualitative focus group study in the USA and the UK
container-title: Journal of Ethnic Foods
e966c3cca7da793799a6d584765fd505176e09b1.abstract: Abstract Kimchi is a Korean lactic acid-fermented vegetable food and cultural tradition shaped by seasonal preservation, regional diversity, and kimjang . This exploratory qualitative study examined how consumers in the US and the UK interpreted kimchi and described incorporating or not incorporating it into everyday meals. Four online focus groups conducted in August 2023 comprised 14 participants: six US consumers stratified by current consumption status and frequency, four UK consumers, and four UK non-consumers. The small groups, structured differently in each country, were designed for analytic contrast rather than national comparison. Transcripts were analyzed thematically using sensitizing concepts from food choice and practice theory; inductively derived negative and ambivalent cases were retained. Participants initially classified kimchi through relational categories such as side dish, pickle, salad, or ingredient. Sensory uncertainty concerned unfamiliar aroma, sourness, texture, and fermentation-related variation. Four analytic positions—routine use, partial incorporation, selective incorporation, and pre-trial uncertainty—differed in the practical competence available to support use. According to participants, ways to make kimchi easier to serve and eat in everyday meals included familiar food pairing, routine building, portion and sensory adjustment, and guided exposure. Cultural authenticity could motivate learning but also increase uncertainty. Within this small purposive sample, the findings suggest that incorporating an ethnic fermented food into everyday meals involves practical competence as well as sensory acceptance. Consumer education may benefit from pairing heritage context with concrete guidance on selection, storage, portioning, and meal use. Such guidance might also support the continuity of a seasonally grounded, plant-forward fermented-food tradition.

title: An Application of the Self-Determination Theory Model for AI-Enhanced, Digital Psychosocial Interventions for Pediatric Disabilities
container-title: Western Journal of Nursing Research
6a353330c39f733eb7e369612f893bac2e52174c.abstract: Background: Youth with developmental disabilities (DDs) experience elevated psychosocial challenges, including difficulties with emotion regulation, self-concept, and access to timely mental health support. Pediatric nurses are well-positioned to address these needs; however, time constraints, limited training, and restricted access to specialty services often impede the provision of consistent psychosocial care. Digitally delivered psychosocial interventions enhanced by artificial intelligence (AI) offer new opportunities for individualized, accessible support, but these approaches frequently lack a clear theoretical foundation. Purpose: This paper applied Self-Determination Theory (SDT), specifically Basic Psychological Needs Theory, to guide pediatric nurses’ use of AI-enhanced, digital psychosocial interventions for DDs in practice. Methods: A theory-driven synthesis mapped SDT needs (autonomy, competence, and relatedness) to AI-enabled intervention features: conversational agents, neuro/adaptive feedback, and emotion-recognition tailoring. Results: The framework specifies how these features can promote volitional engagement, optimal challenge with timely feedback, and supportive interactions for youth with DDs. It also notes evidence gaps (small, heterogeneous samples; limited comparisons and follow-up) and barriers involving payment/workload, equity and access, and data protection, transparency, and bias. Conclusions/Implications: SDT offers a coherent, testable foundation for designing, evaluating, and integrating AI-enhanced psychosocial supports for pediatric DDs. Nurses can screen for support, coach families, monitor risks, and advocate for ethical deployment and rigorous research.

title: MIGRATION PROCESSES AND HUMAN CAPITAL MANAGEMENT IN THE CONTEXT OF UKRAINE’S POST-WAR ECONOMIC RECONSTRUCTION
container-title: Baltic Journal of Economic Studies
b5a51a0d5a9c754314dffe505e6e15033905868d.abstract: The subject of the study is to analyse key trends in global migration processes, including the opportunities available to Ukrainian refugees and their role within these processes. The study will also examine ways to preserve domestic human capital through the development of strategic directions for Ukraine's post-war economic recovery, specifically with regard to migration policy. The study's methodological framework is based on general scientific research methods. The analytical method made it possible to demonstrate the impact of migration on the size, state and quality of domestic human capital. Statistical methods and comparative analysis revealed the nature of migration processes in EU countries and showed how Ukrainian refugees are distributed unevenly across Europe, depending on various factors including minimum wage levels. The synthesis method facilitated the organisation of the research, determined the feasibility of developing a state migration policy strategy and helped to draw conclusions and suggest future research on this topic. The research results revealed the dynamics of migration processes and the influx of new labour into the European labour market. Meanwhile, Ukraine experienced a labour shortage as refugees sought safety during the full-scale war. This necessitates changes to Ukraine's existing migration policy, in order to reflect current realities and encourage Ukrainians to return home to participate in post-war reconstruction. This would be driven by positive shifts across multiple economic sectors, which highlights the practical value of this study. Practical implications. The study's practical significance lies in establishing a scientifically grounded framework for optimising state migration policy and developing effective human capital management strategies amidst global crises. By analysing the specific characteristics of Ukrainian refugees, viable mechanisms can be created to preserve the nation's intellectual and labour potential. This can transform the experience of forced migration into an opportunity to capitalise on new knowledge and skills. The findings of this study are of strategic importance for demographic modelling, labour market forecasting and leveraging the investment and intellectual potential of the diaspora. This is essential for comprehensive post-war reconstruction project planning and execution in Ukraine. Value/Originality. The study provides a comprehensive understanding of migration processes, their current state and development trends. It emphasises the role of migration in shaping human capital amidst contemporary global challenges, as well as the specific characteristics of the domestic labour market. These characteristics create the prerequisites for economic competitiveness, macro-security, a favourable investment climate and the formulation of a state migration policy strategy. This strategy is part of the strategic direction for Ukraine's post-war economic reconstruction.

title: INTEGRATION OF GENERATIVE AI SKILLS IN JOB REQUIREMENTS: EVIDENCE FROM JOB ADVERTISEMENTS IN GEORGIA
container-title: Baltic Journal of Economic Studies
2e932bf664680814b7e5be137f1e6f4677cfcbee.abstract: The rapid diffusion of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) tools has created a demand for new skills in labour markets. However, research into how employers articulate GenAI competencies in job advertisements has focused almost exclusively on large, technologically advanced economies. This study examines how employers in Georgia, a small upper-middle-income transitional economy, indicate GenAI skill requirements in job advertisements, considering four dimensions: skill visibility, linguistic framing, organisational readiness and skill depth. Deductive content analysis was applied to 94 job advertisements collected in January 2026 from three major Georgian labour market platforms (LinkedIn, Jobs.ge and HR.ge). Each advertisement was coded using a structured 20-indicator codebook derived from established theoretical frameworks. The results show that employers articulate GenAI skills in two ways: by explicitly naming the tool, which is present in 38.3 per cent of advertisements, and by using implicit task language, which is present in 61.7 per cent of advertisements and constitutes the dominant form of signalling. Regardless of occupation or skill depth, employers frame GenAI requirements as mandatory in 81.9 per cent of advertisements, indicating the rapid institutionalisation of GenAI literacy as a baseline labour market expectation. Signals of organisational readiness remain weak: only 21.3 per cent of job advertisements acknowledge any organisational role in enabling AI adoption, while the remaining 78.7 per cent present GenAI competence purely as a prerequisite for candidates. Skill complexity is almost evenly divided between basic and advanced requirements, and occupation strongly predicts this division, creating a clear distinction between a technically advanced group and a large group adopting AI on a more general operational level. Signals of organisational readiness remain weak: only 21.3 per cent of job advertisements acknowledge any organisational role in enabling AI adoption, while the remaining 78.7 per cent present GenAI competence purely as a prerequisite for candidates. Skill complexity is almost evenly divided between basic and advanced requirements, and occupation strongly predicts this division, creating a clear distinction between a technically advanced group and a large group adopting AI on a more general operational level.

title: ORGANISATIONAL CHANGE MANAGEMENT AND IMPACT OF LEADERSHIP ON EMPLOYEE PERCEPTIONS
container-title: Baltic Journal of Economic Studies
4d54d99a7aa9aafdf5fc45566b7ef0ea6c67c817.abstract: In today's dynamic business environment, organisational change is a key management issue, without which it is impossible for organisations to maintain and develop their competitive position. This study focuses on the psychological and cultural factors that cause resistance to change, including cognitive, emotional, and behavioural aspects, which can hinder the success of change initiatives. During an organisational change, the head plays a decisive leadership role. Their strategic vision and ability to motivate employees and communicate the ongoing process transparently determine the effectiveness of the changes. A total of 520 representatives from 'LTD Batumis Tskal', 'LTD Kobuleti Tskal' and other similar entities participated in the aforementioned study. This number enables a generalisation of the study results to the research object. The paper analyses the reasons for and needs of implementing changes, the skills required of managers to manage changes, and the factors that lead to employee satisfaction in the change process. Hypotheses have been put forward to study these issues, and the verification and justification of these hypotheses reveal the necessary conclusions and recommendations for the effective management of organisational changes. Verifying the presented hypotheses enabled conclusions to be drawn about the factors that determine effective management of organisational changes, the role of managers, employee satisfaction and trust in changes. The study aimed to evaluate employees' attitudes towards organisational changes and to identify the factors influencing their trust in management, satisfaction with the organisation, and willingness to change supervisors. The study was conducted using a quantitative method. Data were collected via questionnaires designed to assess employee satisfaction and awareness, as well as the manager's change management skills. The data obtained were processed using the statistical software package SPSS. The study found that a manager's ability to manage change is the most influential factor in determining employee attitudes. High levels of satisfaction with the organisation significantly reduce the desire to change supervisors. Being aware of the results of changes increases both trust and overall satisfaction. Transparent communication from management simultaneously strengthens trust and loyalty. A lack of information and communication gaps increases employee resistance and dissatisfaction.

title: From the Gangyan System to the Ticket-Based (Piaoyan) Salt System: Salt Administration Reform in Northern Huai during the Qing Dynasty and Its Contemporary Implications
container-title: Journal of Economics, Management and Trade
012a7433443d9b39075546d9d814d2ab995ee9ea.abstract: Aims: To analyse the transition from the gangyan (designated-merchant) arrangement to ticket-based (piaoyan) salt distribution in Northern Huai and to consider carefully delimited implications for tax administration. Study Design: Qualitative historical and institutional analysis of published primary documents and scholarly interpretations. Place and Duration: Northern Huai in the Qing Dynasty, especially the Jiaqing and Daoguang reigns, with emphasis on the ticket reform of 1832 and the assessment decision of 1837. Methods: Reform memorials and salt-administration compilations were examined for changes in trading eligibility, tax and fee arrangements, transport inspections and official accountability. Documentary claims were compared across sources and assessed for their evidentiary limitations. Results: The reform allowed tax-paying ticket holders to transport salt in specified territories while preserving the state monopoly and inspection requirements. A retrospective account gives an aggregate exceeding 7.7 million taels for accumulated arrears, deficiencies in transport capital and associated liabilities. An imperial record reports a previous quota above 90,000 permits for stagnant territories and more than 100,000 ticket applications during lunar months seven to nine of 1832. These represent different accounting categories, not observed shipment or revenue totals. Contemporary records further describe improvements in tax remittance, but do not permit causal estimation. Conclusion: The experience illustrates how distribution rights, regulatory procedures and administrative accountability could be jointly adjusted in response to institutional strain. Its relevance to current tax administration is conceptual rather than evidence of policy transfer or causal continuity.

title: From Adoption to Human-AI Leadership: A Scoping Review of Artificial Intelligence in Educational Leadership and Management
container-title: Social Scientific Centered Issues
1e0569103ec369b6f75ff1186f587acf5a4f67a0.abstract: This scoping review maps how artificial intelligence is conceptualized and used in educational leadership and management and examines the transition from technology adoption toward human-AI leadership. Following established scoping-review guidance and PRISMA-ScR, records from Scopus, Web of Science, and PubMed published or officially available online from 2022 to the final search date in 2026 were screened; items assigned a 2027 bibliographic year were eligible only if already available online before the cutoff. Of 747 records identified, 183 duplicates were removed and 323 records underwent title-and-abstract screening. Full texts were sought for 81 reports; two could not be retrieved, 79 were assessed for eligibility, and 50 studies were included. Four themes emerged: leadership readiness and capability; AI-augmented leadership practice; organizational conditions and institutional transformation; and human-AI agency, governance, and ethical boundaries. The evidence favors augmentation rather than autonomous substitution, with human judgment remaining central to accountability. The review proposes a five-stage Human-AI Educational Leadership Continuum integrating individual capability, organizational readiness, governance, and decision authority. The review was limited to three databases and English-language articles, and the evidence base remains methodologically heterogeneous and largely cross-sectional or context-specific.

title: Single-sensor acoustic emission source localization in blade local region based on an interpretable wavelet attention network
container-title: Structural Health Monitoring
ede9793d57cf20866e46b892aa7f92f49bbf6016.abstract: Acoustic emission (AE) technology is suitable for monitoring wind turbine blades because of its high-frequency response and sensitivity. However, existing damage localization approaches rely on multi-sensor arrays, which limit their engineering applicability. Moreover, deep learning models for single-sensor localization remain constrained by insufficient time-frequency representation and limited interpretability. To address these issues, a novel single-sensor AE source localization model, the Large-kernel dual wavelet attention network, was proposed. First, pencil lead break tests on real blade structures were conducted to investigate AE signal propagation, revealing strong nonlinear behavior and multi-scale attenuation characteristics. On this basis, a Large-kernel dual wavelet convolution layer was developed using Morlet and Mexican hat wavelets. With a mechanism-guided large wavelet kernel design, the arbitrariness in hyperparameter selection and the Gibbs phenomenon associated with incomplete truncation were mitigated, enabling the effective extraction of multi-scale time-frequency features. A time-grouped frequency attention mechanism module was introduced to adaptively recalibrate convolutional kernel weights through the fine-grained perception of localized time-frequency features, thereby improving the discrimination of critical features. Experiments on a real blade specimen demonstrated that the proposed method outperformed existing models in localization accuracy, achieving a minimum mean distance error of 20.29 mm. Furthermore, the model exhibited advantages in terms of feature interpretability and noise robustness. These results provide a promising and interpretable framework, laying the foundation for single-sensor damage localization in structural health monitoring of wind turbine blades.

title: Exploring Factors Impacting the Self-Management of Type 2 Diabetes in Older Black African and Afro-Caribbean People (BAACP): A Qualitative Evidence Synthesis
container-title: The Science of Diabetes Self-Management and Care
33726a17fed8527cdae6a873f445b93de12dbb2f.abstract: Purpose: The purpose of this qualitative evidence synthesis (QES) was to synthesize qualitative evidence on perceived barriers and facilitators influencing self-management of type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) among older Black African and Afro-Caribbean adults. Methods: A QES of qualitative and mixed-methods studies with extractable qualitative findings was conducted using the PICO (Population, Phenomena of Interest, Context) framework and PRISMA (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses) guidance. Searches were undertaken in MEDLINE, PubMed, CINAHL, PsycINFO, African Journals Online, and Worldviews on Evidence-Based Nursing for studies published between January 2010 and June 2025. Studies were screened against predefined eligibility criteria. Methodological quality was assessed using the Critical Appraisal Skills Program checklist, and findings were synthesized thematically. Results: From 5092 records, 12 studies met the inclusion criteria. Five overarching themes were identified. Key facilitators included spirituality, culturally responsive health care, and strong family or community support networks. Major barriers included limited health literacy, mistrust of health care systems, cultural conflicts with biomedical advice, and structural barriers such as financial constraints, limited access to health care services, and racial discrimination. Conclusion: Self-management of T2DM in older Black African and Afro-Caribbean adults is shaped by interconnected cultural, relational, and structural influences. Diabetes services should prioritize culturally tailored education, trust-building clinical relationships, family and community-engaged interventions, and addressing social determinants and racial inequalities to improve self-management outcomes in this population.

title: Intelligent Machine Learning Framework for Advanced Cyber Threat Detection: A Focus on Ransomware Attacks
container-title: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
0622ec2b35da577e505d6043bbabfd8258fa572b.abstract: Ransomware has evolved into one of the most sophisticated cyber threats, causing severe financial and operational disruptions across healthcare, banking, education, government, and critical infrastructure sectors. Traditional signaturebased antivirus systems and rule-based intrusion detection mechanisms struggle to identify novel ransomware variants due to their rapidly evolving attack strategies. This paper proposes an Intelligent Machine Learning Framework (IMLF) for advanced ransomware detection that integrates supervised machine learning, feature engineering, behavioral analytics, and ensemble learning techniques to achieve real-time threat detection. The framework utilizes network traffic features, file system activities, registry modifications, process execution patterns, and API call sequences to distinguish ransomware from benign software. Multiple machine learning algorithms including Logistic Regression, Decision Tree, Random Forest, Support Vector Machine (SVM), Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), and Deep Neural Networks (DNN) are evaluated using benchmark cybersecurity datasets. Experimental results demonstrate that ensemble-based approaches significantly outperform conventional methods, achieving detection accuracy above 99%, reduced false positives, and lower detection latency. The proposed framework provides an adaptive, scalable, and intelligent solution capable of detecting both known and zero-day ransomware attacks.

title: Effects of air pollution on corporate charitable donations: evidence from China
container-title: Chinese Management Studies
2cbbdd4a96d033b740588046874b9941fbbbcf9b.abstract: Purpose This paper aims to examine the impact of air pollution on corporate charitable giving by combining listing data from the China Stock Market and Accounting Research Database (CSMAR) and data on air pollution in Chinese cities. Using the instrumental variable method and regression discontinuity design, it explores the impact of air pollution on corporate charitable donations and further explores the impact of air pollution on state-owned enterprises and enterprises in high-pollution industries. Design/methodology/approach Using 2013–2019 data from Chinese listed firms and air quality indices, this study examines air pollution as a new influence factor. To address omitted variable bias, regressions include industry/year fixed effects, regional economic controls and corporate governance variables. Endogeneity concerns are mitigated via three tests: an instrumental variable (thermal inversion) for reverse causality, a regression discontinuity test and a Huai River policy placebo test – all yielding robust results. Findings Empirical results show air pollution significantly reduces corporate charitable donations: a 10% pollution increase correlates with an approximately 30% decrease in corporate charitable donations. These findings hold after robustness checks (excluding air quality index (AQI) manipulation, alternative measures and first-tier cities). Effects are heterogeneous: SOEs and firms in highly polluting industries exhibit greater donation reductions under severe pollution. Originality/value This paper adds to the literature by examining the influence of air pollution – a natural factor – on corporate charitable donations, an area that has been largely overlooked in favor of social factors like strategy, politics, altruism and managerial self-interest. It is possibly the first to explore this connection, offering a more holistic view of what drives corporate giving. Given the severity of air pollution in China and its potential to affect firm behaviors and reputation, this study is particularly timely, providing insights into whether and how air pollution might reduce corporate donations, which are critical for enhancing a firm’s image and value.

title: Integrating Customer Profitability Analysis into Retail Banking Strategic Planning: A Case Study of Bank Syariah Indonesia in Makassar
container-title: Journal of Economics, Management, and Accounting
f532beb78ddcecfe9aafbf07740764cfefddc49d.abstract: Digital transformation has increased the strategic relevance of customer-level financial information in retail banking, although its managerial application within Islamic banking remains insufficiently understood. This study examined how Customer Profitability Analysis (CPA) was interpreted and incorporated into strategic planning at Bank Syariah Indonesia, Makassar Area. A qualitative case study employed an in-depth, semi-structured interview with the Retail and Transaction Business Manager, supported by corporate reports and institutional documents. Thematic analysis identified three interrelated dimensions: the construction of customer profitability, its application to relationship management, and adaptation to local and Sharia-related considerations. Profitability assessments encompassed account balances, fee-based income, digital transactions, financing characteristics, collectibility risks, and service costs. These considerations informed customer segmentation, differentiated services, retention, cross-selling, up-selling, and marketing resource allocation. Managerial interpretations also reflected local interest in gold-related banking products and the financing needs of micro, small, and medium enterprises, alongside principles of justice and public benefit. CPA consequently functioned as a context-sensitive decision-support framework rather than a verified calculation of customer-level net profitability. Evidence from one managerial informant and secondary documents limits transferability and prevents claims of measured financial improvement. The findings clarify how accounting information can inform strategic choices while accommodating financial inclusion objectives within local markets.

title: Short-Run Production Theory and Labor Efficiency in Purbalingga’s False-Eyelash Industry
container-title: Journal of Economics, Management, and Accounting
60023f66a35bdcc8ba359fba17a46be84182b9f0.abstract: The false-eyelash industry in Purbalingga Regency represents a labor-intensive manufacturing sector in which productivity depends on workforce utilization and production capacity. This study aimed to examine the application of short-run production theory to labor efficiency and productivity, emphasizing the relationships among Total Product (TP), Average Product (AP), Marginal Product (MP), and diminishing marginal returns. A descriptive qualitative literature review was conducted using journal articles and academic conference proceedings addressing production theory, technical efficiency, labor productivity, manufacturing operations, and employment conditions. Sources were selected according to topical relevance, identifiable publication information, and verifiable academic content. The literature was analyzed through thematic classification, methodological comparison, and conceptual synthesis. The findings established that labor productivity and technical efficiency represent distinct performance dimensions and cannot be interpreted interchangeably. Workforce expansion may increase aggregate output, but its marginal contribution depends on equipment capacity, raw-material availability, employee capabilities, working conditions, and production coordination. The synthesis also identified limitations in existing evidence concerning firm-level marginal productivity and optimal workforce allocation. The study contributes an integrated conceptual framework for interpreting labor utilization under short-run production constraints. Empirical assessment requires comparable observations of output, labor input, working hours, equipment utilization, and material consumption.

title: Improving HPV Vaccine Uptake Among Girls Aged 9–14 Years in Akwa Ibom State, Nigeria: A Community-Participatory Pre/Post-Intervention Study
7470369898295f3c268432a97673b88ed9323f0c.abstract: Abstract Background Cervical cancer remains a leading cause of cancer-related mortality among women in Nigeria, where Human Papillomavirus (HPV) vaccine uptake has historically been among the lowest in sub-Saharan Africa. Despite the introduction of the HPV vaccine into Nigeria's National Immunisation Programme in 2023, uptake remains suboptimal. This study evaluated the effect of a community-participatory, multi-channel sensitisation intervention on HPV vaccine uptake, awareness, and knowledge among caregivers of girls aged 9–14 years in Akwa Ibom State, Nigeria. Methods A pre/post-intervention study was conducted across six communities in three local government areas representing urban, semi-urban, and rural settings. Independent cross-sectional surveys were administered to caregivers of eligible girls before (n = 331, January 2025) and after (n = 355, June 2025) a fourteen-week community sensitisation intervention delivered through five channels: churches, schools, primary healthcare facilities, community sound announcers, and physical materials. All materials were co-designed with community stakeholders. Descriptive statistics, chi-square and Mann-Whitney U tests, and multivariable logistic regression were used for analysis. Statistical significance was set at p < 0.05. Results HPV vaccine uptake increased from 7.3% (95% CI: 4.5%–10.0%) to 50.4% (95% CI: 45.2%–55.6%), an absolute increase of 43.1 percentage points. HPV vaccine awareness rose from 15.1% to 65.4% (p < 0.001). Among HPV-aware respondents, good HPV knowledge increased from 63.9% to 84.3% (p = 0.019), though vaccine-specific knowledge remained predominantly poor across both phases (4.0% vs. 6.9%, p = 0.749). Willingness to vaccinate among unvaccinated caregivers was high and unchanged (87.0% vs. 87.5%, p = 0.979). Routine facility records corroborated survey findings, showing a 276% increase in mean monthly doses administered. HPV vaccine awareness was the strongest independent predictor of uptake in both phases (pre-intervention aOR 9.88, 95% CI: 2.07–47.46; post-intervention aOR 16.59, 95% CI: 6.98–39.46). Conclusions A community co-designed, multi-channel sensitisation intervention was associated with a substantial increase in HPV vaccine uptake within six months. Limited awareness rather than vaccine hesitancy was the primary barrier in this setting. Sustaining these gains requires parallel investment in vaccine supply-chain resilience alongside community sensitisation, and future interventions should prioritise strengthening vaccine-specific knowledge to support informed and durable vaccination uptake. Trial registration Pan African Clinical Trials Registry (PACTR), PACTR202609683563072, [07 September, 2026]. Retrospectively registered.

title: An Analysis of the Factors Influencing Consumer Behavior in the Purchase of Food Products
container-title: Journal of Economics, Management, and Accounting
591fa2e95417f8c89ec016c6dc7dc1c453654b10.abstract: Food purchasing behavior reflects interactions among consumer characteristics, psychological evaluations, marketing stimuli, and purchasing circumstances. This study aimed to identify, classify, and synthesize factors influencing consumer behavior in purchasing food products. A descriptive qualitative literature review was conducted using secondary data from journal articles, academic books, and previous research reports. The original review covered literature published between 1991 and 2023, with findings analyzed through thematic synthesis and comparative interpretation. Six determinant categories were identified: cultural, social, personal, psychological, marketing-mix, and situational factors. Comparative evidence revealed differences in the dominant factors across food categories and purchasing environments. Price was dominant in instant noodle purchasing, with a reported influence of 12.15%, while psychological factors were most influential in steamed layer cake purchasing. Product attributes were most decisive in a selected food outlet, whereas purchasing time was the strongest factor in a fast-food restaurant setting. These differences indicated that purchasing behavior depended on product characteristics, consumer evaluations, and transaction circumstances rather than a universally dominant determinant. The study contributes an integrated conceptual framework for interpreting heterogeneous purchasing influences and supports context-sensitive marketing strategies. Differences in research designs and measurements limit direct statistical comparisons and causal generalization.

title:
Sex Hormones as Regulators of the Age‐ and Sex‐Dependent Benefits of Caloric Restriction: An Emerging Research Protocol of a Controlled Dietary Intervention (The
                    <scp>GendAge</scp>
                    Weight Loss Study)
container-title: Nutrition Bulletin
f4d2c07873ba68cfb76b55db600fb75f2f21a844.abstract: ABSTRACT With nearly two‐thirds of the UK population living with overweight or obesity, there is an urgent necessity for evidence‐based public health guidance to promote a healthy weight. Current weight management advice centres on lifestyle modification. However, existing dieting recommendations fail to consider sex or age. This is a surprising oversight, as it is well established that health outcomes vary significantly between men and women across the lifespan. Our preliminary work in mice and humans suggests young females are more resistant than males to calorie‐restriction (CR)‐induced fat loss and reductions in energy expenditure, and that this resistance diminishes in older, post‐menopausal participants—implicating oestrogen as a possible modulator of CR response. Further, the menopause may have an impact on fat storage linked to changes in sex hormones. This article describes emerging research being done through a controlled feeding study in 75 younger and older men and women. This study will directly test whether CR's effects on fat mass, energy expenditure and glucose homeostasis are age‐ and sex‐dependent, and whether HRT use in post‐menopausal women restores a CR response more similar to that of younger women. Energy expenditure and body composition will be assessed using gold‐standard techniques, including doubly labelled water, alongside blood and abdominal adipose tissue sampling to investigate underlying hormonal mechanisms. The findings of this new study will clarify whether dietary weight‐management advice should be tailored by sex, age, or menopausal/HRT status, informing more precise, evidence‐based obesity guidance and supporting women's health and healthy ageing.

title: Mapping Campus Crises: An Updated Taxonomy for Higher Education
container-title: Journal of Contingencies and Crisis Management
c8806484b5ca0c2f769e205a7f8c8408e04bd540.abstract: ABSTRACT Increasingly, higher education leaders must lead from a presumption that they may encounter some type of institutional, national, and/or international crisis, and seek to be as ready as possible for the wide range of crisis types that can befall their institution. Adequate preparation involves having access to updated crisis taxonomies that are relevant to institutions of higher education. Therefore, in this paper, we conduct a literature review and a media analysis, replicating methods from Gigliotti (2020) to review previous categories of crisis types in higher education and identify potential shifts in the intervening years. We also assert that polycrisis—a compendium of crises where one contributes to a domino effect and causes or amplifies other crises—is itself a type of crisis that higher education leaders and practitioners need to understand and contend with. Our findings resulted in an updated 14‐category crisis taxonomy for institutions of higher education, which can be used to shape institutional preparation and response.

title: From Communication Anxiety to Psychological Reliance
container-title: Journal of Media Psychology
bfda88b1644227e14d7f234fea59df6cb5059730.abstract: Abstract: Grounded in self-determination theory (SDT), this study investigates how communication anxiety and psychological need satisfaction relate to the use of Large Language Model (LLM)-based chatbots, specifically ChatGPT, for communication tasks (e.g., writing emails, drafting messages, and preparing scripts). Using a three-wave panel survey of participants from the United States and South Korea, we examined both between- and within-person dynamics. Results showed that individuals with higher trait-level communication anxiety tended to use ChatGPT more frequently for communication tasks, whereas within-person fluctuations in anxiety did not predict greater use. ChatGPT use was positively associated with the satisfaction of basic psychological needs – autonomy, competence, and relatedness – and this need satisfaction, in turn, was associated with greater psychological reliance on ChatGPT. Importantly, need satisfaction further mediated the relationship between ChatGPT use and psychological reliance at both within- and between-person levels. Cultural comparisons revealed that US participants exhibited stronger momentary effects, while Korean participants showed more stable, trait-based patterns. These findings highlight the role of LLM-based chatbots as need-supportive communication tools that may become integrated into users’ communication practices over time, with implications for theories of AI-mediated communication, cross-cultural research, and the design of human-AI communication systems.

title: Continuous glucose monitoring, automated insulin delivery, and remote care in adolescents with type 1 diabetes: advances toward integrated digital management
container-title: Frontiers in Endocrinology
58f95259b2343193e59a2556b35816e8cb201993.abstract: Type 1 diabetes management in adolescents remains challenging due to physiological and behavioral factors. This review summarizes recent advances in three interconnected technologies: continuous glucose monitoring (CGM), automated insulin delivery (AID), and remote care. CGM provides real-time glycemic data with time in range (TIR) as the core metric, improving glycemic outcomes when implemented with structured education. AID systems, particularly hybrid closed-loop devices, consistently increase TIR, reduce glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c), and lower risks of severe hypoglycemia and diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA) across randomized trials and real-world studies, with validated efficacy in children as young as 1-year-old. Remote care models leverage continuous data streams to enable individualized follow-up, showing glycemic outcomes approaching those of traditional visits in comparative studies while improving access and psychosocial support. Despite proven benefits, barriers remain, including socioeconomic inequities in technology access, alarm fatigue, and implementation gaps across healthcare systems. Future priorities include fully closed-loop systems, dual-hormone approaches, algorithm optimization for exercise and illness, long-term psychosocial outcomes, and equitable implementation strategies. Clinical practice should integrate these technologies through multidisciplinary teams, early initiation, and patient-centered support to transform adolescent diabetes care from intermittent visits to continuous digital management.

title: Relationship Between Utilisation of Funds from Income-Generating Activities and Delivery of Classroom Teaching Services in Public Secondary Schools in Uasin Gishu County, Kenya
container-title: Journal of Education Management and Leadership (JEML)
70670e514bcaae695f7fddee5e6afddc29d5f3ce.abstract: This study examined the relationship between the utilisation of income-generating activity (IGA) funds and the delivery of classroom teaching services in public secondary schools in Uasin Gishu County, Kenya. Despite increased government capitation, schools often receive insufficient funding, prompting reliance on IGAs to sustain operations. Guided by the Innovation Theory of Necessity and the Problem-Solving Theory, and grounded in pragmatism, the study adopted a correlational design within a convergent parallel mixed-methods framework. Multi-stage sampling was used to select 80 public secondary schools (40 boarding and 40 day) and 240 respondents comprising 80 headteachers, 80 senior teachers of academics and 80 bursars. Data were collected through questionnaires and interviews and analysed using Pearson and Spearman correlations and thematic analysis. Findings revealed that IGA fund utilisation was significantly related to seven of the nine teaching services examined, including textbook acquisition, employment of Board of Management teachers and continuous professional development. However, no significant relationships were established with hiring part-time teachers or financing teacher motivation. Overall, IGA fund utilisation had a strong, positive and statistically significant relationship with classroom teaching service delivery (r = .707, p < .001). The study recommends that the Ministry of Education establish guidelines requiring schools to allocate a minimum proportion of IGA profits towards improving teaching quality and digital integration. Additionally, Boards of Management should incorporate IGA-to-pedagogy objectives into school strategic plans to strengthen the contribution of alternative funding to classroom teaching services.

title: The Roadmap and Manufacturing Challenges of EMLs and CW Lasers for 800G, 1.6T, and 3.2T Super Intelligence (SI) and Artificial Intelligence (AI) Computing Applications
container-title: Applied Science and Innovative Research
d5376656dc40dab08c79bb68c51e743c519d0fbf.abstract: This paper presents the roadmap and manufacturing challenges of electroabsorption-modulated lasers (EMLs) and continuous-wave (CW) lasers for 800G, 1.6T, and 3.2T super intelligence (SI) and artificial intelligence (AI) optical transmission and computing applications. We highlight the roadmap for EMLs and CW lasers across different generations of optical switching technologies and discuss key manufacturing challenges, including (1) technical complexity, (2) substrate constraints, and (3) process equipment requirements.

title: Regulatory and scientific frameworks for AI-driven biosensor technologies in antimicrobial resistance monitoring
container-title: Frontiers in Medical Technology
ca04b8070cfb7b9f722852afe28eb10e6fa25a73.abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) diagnostics require evidence matched to the intended clinical or surveillance use. This narrative review synthesizes biosensor research, artificial intelligence (AI) analytics, and device oversight through a regulatory-scientific lifecycle perspective. Electrochemical and optical transduction are distinguished from microfluidic sample handling and nanomaterial enhancement. Pathogen identification, resistance-gene detection, phenotypic antimicrobial susceptibility testing (AST), minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) prediction, and population surveillance are compared by output, reference standard, and validation requirement. Representative Raman-machine-learning and microfluidic studies illustrate both analytical promise and limitations in independent clinical validation. The review maps these findings to US and European device pathways, software controls, interoperability, cybersecurity, and data governance. Its proposed five-phase framework adapts established total-product-lifecycle, quality-management, and risk-management principles to AMR-specific challenges, including emerging resistance mechanisms, breakpoint revisions, specimen shifts, and algorithm changes. The framework is a conceptual implementation tool, not a new regulatory pathway or an empirically validated model. Safe translation requires claim-specific validation and controlled updates rather than extrapolation from isolated prototype performance.

title: Exploring AI as a reading companion: L2 learners' approaches to literary comprehension
container-title: Foreign Language Annals
29d85c7100d4beb2a558fa842c9a1f66727182f2.abstract: Abstract Generative AI tools are increasingly present in language learning, yet their role in second language (L2) reading remains underexplored. This study investigates how intermediate German learners engaged with ChatGPT during interpretive reading using a three‐condition design with a Grimm fairytale. The study examines the relationship between AI access and reading performance, patterns of use or resistance, and students' ethical and motivational interpretations of AI‐mediated reading. Generative AI emerged as a negotiated presence that learners approached with curiosity, caution, or resistance. Required AI use was associated with reduced differences in comprehension outcomes across proficiency levels, whereas optional use revealed diverse strategic, reluctant, and value‐driven stances rooted in ethical concerns, discipline‐specific norms, and a desire to maintain interpretive autonomy. Students who routinely used AI in other courses engaged more selectively in German, suggesting AI practices may be shaped by disciplinary contexts. The findings support guided, reflective AI integration while valuing learner resistance.
