title: Between Artifice and Enlightenment: Queer Critique, Insecurity, and the AI Large Language Model
container-title: Insecurity and the Eclipse of Enlightenment
5ea4098d32b460e0385913aad6336e3634f5a5d9.abstract: Abstract Over several decades, machine learning systems—often described with the double metaphor “artificial intelligence”—have become indispensable computational tools in the flow and mediation of economic and social capital. These systems can, on the surface, appear to deepen the dialectic of enlightenment identified by Horkheimer and Adorno by enabling ever greater domination over natural systems and human agency. They therefore generate widespread concern that computational advances endanger the security and autonomy of human subjects, especially in the sphere of production and exchange. Contemporary social theory offers conceptual tools that go beyond received categories of domination and autonomy, however, to provide a reanalysis of machine learning systems and their implication in social dynamics and economic relations. This chapter focuses on the ways large language model (LLM) systems demonstrate complex affinities with theories of mimesis and simulacrum, and therefore how such systems and require a rethinking of performativity and artifice. Recent queer critique—in which reflection on computational systems and simulacra is proliferating—and contemporary social theory, when read together, thus reveal how rhetoric about LLMs demonstrates slippages between agency, performance, reproduction, representation, and meaning that must be unpacked historically and conceptually before metaphors of the “artificial” and “intelligence” can carry analytical weight in addressing today’s socioeconomic relations. Ultimately, this theoretical-conceptual reading highlights the stakes of the problem of truth in systems where artifice manifests both socially and computationally.

title: Climate Change, Reason, and American Higher Education: Inculcating the Self-Deception of Capitalist Society
container-title: Insecurity and the Eclipse of Enlightenment
7c58025ad2c210f503bb6dd24bf7f1b417d06d0c.abstract: Abstract Climate change is among the greatest sources of insecurity in the 21st century. The university is an important institutional curator of instrumental reason and, especially in applied research, is crucial to addressing related issues of insecurity across various domains. Yet, as this chapter demonstrates, the neoliberal university, and the capitalist economy in which it is embedded, is antithetical to what is needed to foster the knowledge, values, dispositions, and relationships required for tackling the climate crisis in meaningful ways. This chapter begins by interrogating the Boyer Commission’s (2022) report on American higher education, sponsored by the US-based Carnegie Foundation for the Advancement of Teaching, and its idea of world-readiness, which provokes students and educators to think differently by moving away from workforce skills and training to better understand the complexity of the world we live in. Interweaving examples from the American societal context with insights drawn from critical theory, this chapter discusses ways in which the American higher education system, mediated by the accumulation logic of capital, reproduces the economic growth imperative, diminishes the prospects for rational solutions to climate change, and exacerbates the uneven relationship between the technological mastery of nature and the mastery of human irrationality. This analysis furthermore examines how the transformation of education into a market-driven commodity not only reconfigures the institutional culture of the university but also cultivates modes of selfhood that are fundamentally misaligned with, and often detrimental to, the values and practices of ecological responsibility and care.

title: Enhancing Virtual Education
container-title: Negotiating Faith, Fact, and the Future of Higher Education
ef4f0aaa09ae551d9c3e068f71a492e2fd205170.abstract: Applications of artificial intelligence (AI) are shaping new ways of teaching, including the creation of virtual teachers who can automate the teaching process. AI can combine text-to-image, text-to-speech, lip sync and gesture animation for the creation of virtual avatars who can present and teach. However, despite advancements in technology, there are still issues with the realism of avatars and the ability to synchronize all of these processes in real-time. This chapter discusses the main artificial intelligence technologies that have been used to build automated virtual instructors, including advancements, challenges, and applications. In addition, the author discusses the educational value of these technologies and the need for better algorithms and system designs to foster the reliable, safe, and effective use of artificial intelligence in virtual education.

title: Reassessing Faith and Facts in AI-Augmented Modern Higher Education
container-title: Negotiating Faith, Fact, and the Future of Higher Education
3098ae300a50b242ae5b282892b8c9c0aa1b6ebc.abstract: The rapid integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) into modern higher education has produced a dual impact: while AI has opened new opportunities for innovation in teaching, learning, and research, it has also introduced significant challenges for academic practice. This paper explores how AI reshapes epistemic boundaries by challenging traditional notions and examines how confidence in institutional traditions and technological promise intersects with empirical data and algorithmic reasoning, and the ethical implications for transparent decision-making frameworks. By combining theoretical perspectives with practical examples, this paper highlights how AI is redefining epistemological foundations by the need to strengthen the relationship between faith and facts. The paper argues for a human-centred approach that promotes adaptive learning cultures. It concludes by proposing a forward-looking framework to help modern universities remain grounded in an AI-intensive future.

title: The Learning Loop in Entrepreneurship Education
container-title: Negotiating Faith, Fact, and the Future of Higher Education
27e5afdd0d25ab2bee720e21617025713eee16ce.abstract: This study introduces the Learning Loop, an experiential learning framework designed to bridge the gap between theoretical instruction and practical application in entrepreneurship education. Grounded in Kolb's Experiential Learning Theory, the model engages students in real-world case studies from technology-based ventures. The project begins with the identification of industry entrepreneurs and the development of real-world case studies based on unresolved business challenges. These cases are introduced through live webinars, providing students with concrete experiential exposure. Students then engage in reflective observation by analysing entrepreneurial decisions, questioning assumptions, and exploring alternative strategies. This is followed by abstract conceptualisation, where students apply entrepreneurial theories and tools such as feasibility analysis, opportunity mapping, and business model frameworks to structure viable solutions. In the active experimentation stage, students conduct feasibility studies, develop conceptual prototypes, and propose actionable business strategies, which are presented and defended before industry professionals in a simulated pitching environment. A dedicated digital case platform supports all stages by hosting case materials, webinar recordings, and analytical resources. The learning process concludes with structured reflection and feedback to reinforce entrepreneurial mindset development. Each stage aligns with course learning outcomes, ensuring both academic rigour and practical relevance. Student feedback highlights improved engagement, confidence, and decision-making under uncertainty. The model also nurtures adaptability, resilience, and reflective thinking, traits vital for the innovation-driven economy. As Malaysia advances its digital agenda, the Learning Loop presents a scalable, future-focused strategy to strengthen entrepreneurship education across higher education institutions and disciplines.

title: Use of Digital Transformation to Create an Inclusive Learning Environment in Tourism by Mediation of Artificial Intelligence in Africa
container-title: Inclusion and Diversity in Business and Tourism Education
0a4f3a883acafff5f6a87917158607f1dafa1a58.abstract: Inspecting the connection among digital transformation, artificial intelligence (AI), as well as the synthesis of inclusive environment of learning in the awareness among tourists sector is the article's primary goal. It tackles the issue of how this technological synthesis can augment educational accessibility and participation for a range of scholar demographics. The investigation employs a mixed-methods approach, combining quantitative surveys and qualitative interviews to gather data from educators and scholars. Key outcomes demonstrate that digital transformation considerably promotes inclusivity in learning experiences, while AI plays a critical mediating function in personalizing education and catering to expert scholar requirements. In order to incubate more equitable environment of learning s, educational institutions should strategically incorporate digital tools along with artificial intelligence (AI) into their curricula, as per to the outcomes. Future initiatives assimilate comparative investigations across various educational contexts.

title: Developing an Anti-Ableist Framework for Teaching and Learning With Pre-Service Teachers
container-title: Preparing Pre-Service Educators for Diverse Learners and Communities
b2424298c3a2e344f41eec21184e7335c100b5dd.abstract: Full inclusion and active participation of students with disabilities in K-12 education is imperative in a move toward universal culturally sustaining practice in the United States education system. This chapter presents the Anti-Ableist Framework for Teaching and Learning and its six components: reframe the deficit mindset; shift your language; support self-determination; center anti-racist, equity-based practices; collaborate over demanding compliance; and avoid assumptions. The goal in using this Framework is to provide teacher educators with a concrete set of mind shifts and actions they can take to develop an anti-ableist frame through which they could develop their praxis.

title: A Deep Learning Advancement in Early Diagnosis Using Chest X-Rays

ddb081025fda0034ba0faecc68a837bd1bbcdf0a.abstract: TRegarding the world health agenda, it is still very important to do early and precise diagnosis of tuberculosis (TB). The current method achieves good diagnosis accuracy and resilience by using chest x-ray (CXR) images and an autonomous TB detection system based on deep learning. The framework integrates enhanced preprocessing methods for effective feature extraction, contrast augmentation, and noise reduction, leading to high efficiency in learning. CNNs, ViTs, and hybrid models are some typical deep learning architectures used to systematically assess their effectiveness in identifying and categorizing damaged lung regions due to tuberculosis. Validation is performed using large-scale, publicly available datasets, while performance evaluation metrics include specificity, sensitivity, and accuracy. The findings demonstrate that the suggested system works better than the cutting edge models, making it a dependable and expandable option for automated TB diagnosis and early clinical intervention in environments with limited resources.

title: Universal machine learning force fields for materials simulation: from model construction to complex-system applications
container-title: Physica Scripta
208fd721fe2470535bc6387a6d792eb1c617a7ec.abstract: Abstract Machine learning force fields (MLFFs) can reproduce reference electronic-structure energies and forces with high accuracy within validated chemical and configurational domains while substantially reducing the computational cost relative to direct first-principles calculations. Currently, MLFFs are evolving from system-specific models toward universal MLFFs. This review summarizes recent progress in universal MLFFs from data construction, model architecture, fine-tuning strategy, physical priors, and complex-system applications. We focus on three reliability bottlenecks: potential energy surface softening due to biased near-equilibrium pretraining data, catastrophic forgetting during downstream fine-tuning, and insufficient treatment of long-range electrostatics, dispersion, and polarization. Representative datasets and published benchmarks are assessed alongside graph, equivariant, basis-expansion and descriptor-based model families, with attention to model size, inference cost and task-specific validation. We further review forgetting-aware fine-tuning strategies, physics-enhanced frameworks and polarizable long-range models, as well as representative applications in battery electrolytes, solid-state interfaces, ferroelectric phase transitions, phonons, defects and thermal transport. Finally, future directions are discussed toward multifidelity data fusion, task-oriented benchmarks, uncertainty quantification, interpretability and integrated simulation toolchains.

c3e35dc9cc6d6c3db481ba0234b0a9903939fd49.abstract: The article presents a comparative assessment of valuable agronomic traits in F₄ cotton hybrids studied in a first-year breeding nursery. The growing period, seed cotton weight per boll, plant productivity, fiber length, and fiber yield were evaluated in comparison with the Andijan-36 standard cultivar. The Bukhara-6 × 010888 combination achieved a plant productivity of 81.5 g and a fiber yield of 40.4%. bdc53edec3b08e5979205cd7592596da45af6845.abstract: This article presents data on the yield of cotton varieties from research conducted at the experimental fields of the Syrdarya scientific-experimental station. The study involved the regionalized “Guliston” variety and the promising "S-5727" variety, which were irrigated one to two times. Irrigation was applied at soil moisture levels of 70-70-60% and 75-75-60% relative to field capacity, with plant densities maintained at 100, 150, and 200 thousand plants per hectare. Taking the boll opening rate into account, it was determined that the cotton yield across the experimental variants averaged between 41.1 and 49.1 centners per hectare.

a30f93e414b36964ab066ff1dffbf8f328a97663.abstract: The study investigated the phenological development and duration of the growing season of 11 perennial wheat collection samples. The growing season, calculated from emergence to full maturity, ranged from 225 to 232 days. Among the perennial samples, the earliest-maturing WHEAT-AGROPYRON INTERMEDIUM PARTIAL AMPHIPLOID6 had a growing season of 225 days, while the latest-maturing MADSEN//CHINESE SPRING/PI531718 had 232 days. These differences indicate phenological diversity in the development of perennial wheat genotypes.

b39a782935211bc85d4c9cb2bcbc690694c75c7a.abstract: The paper analyzes grate constructions used in cotton cleaners for removing large impurities. The aim is to systematize the advantages and limitations of stationary round, triangular and trapezoidal grate bars and to analyze the influence of grate design parameters on the cleaning process. The source material reports triangular grate dimensions of 19, 25 and 12 mm, a 1570 mm placement radius relative to the saw drum and a 40 mm spacing as an effective configuration. For the CHX-3 cleaner, trapezoidal grate bars with dimensions of 25, 16, 12 and 10 mm are reported, while a low efficiency is noted for the 12 mm working edge configuration in CHX-ZM. A grate with different grate-bar diameters and solutions aimed at increasing the degrees of freedom of grate bars are also considered. Since the source material does not contain sufficient quantitative results of a new experiment, numerical efficiency values were not fabricated; the analysis is based on the parameters and conclusions available in the source material.

0107d93e0c6265c326136b831716e2b85322e18a.abstract: The article investigates the effect of different rates of mineral fertilizers and the Moddus retardant on the photosynthetic activity of winter wheat varieties Krasnodarskaya-99 and Chillaki. The results showed that the application of mineral fertilizers in combination with the retardant had a positive effect on leaf area formation and the photosynthetic potential of plants. The highest values of photosynthetic activity were recorded when mineral fertilizers were applied at a rate of N210P105K70 in combination with Moddus at a rate of 0.4 L/ha. Among the studied varieties, Chillaki demonstrated higher leaf area and photosynthetic potential compared with Krasnodarskaya-99. The obtained results indicate that an optimal combination of mineral nutrition and Moddus retardant application can contribute to improving the photosynthetic activity of winter wheat plants.

title: Self-supervised scene-adaptive spectral imaging via implicit mask evolution
container-title: Optics Express
89bd583fbe8b1d1f31b7b86e8b1b7f7ab382a8c3.abstract: The performance of snapshot coded aperture spectral imaging (CASSI) is fundamentally constrained by the reliance on scene-agnostic static masks or computationally heavy data-driven optimizations that require extensive spectral ground truth. We propose a self-supervised, scene-adaptive CASSI framework that refines the physical coded aperture without requiring labeled spectral data. By integrating a dual-branch architecture with an efficient, implicit model-driven reconstruction engine, the system establishes a self-supervised consistency loop that tailors the mask morphology to the spatial-frequency characteristics of the incident scene. Numerical benchmarks and physical prototype validation demonstrate the framework’s ability to adapt to structural boundaries, effectively mitigating high-frequency aliasing artifacts while demonstrating robust generalization across disparate scene distributions without offline training. Operating at an algorithmic latency of ∼55ms per iteration and enabling low-latency closed-loop modulation, this approach demonstrates the feasibility of hardware-integrated physical adaptation for static scenes and establishes the theoretical potential for continuous spatiotemporal evolution in high-throughput sensing pipelines.

title: Unsupervised detection of overshooting defects using hybrid generative and boundary classification models
container-title: Journal of Logic and Computation
5bd5611f5a7b62192ff0e5e55cf8165aac10e28e.abstract: Abstract Quality control in modern manufacturing increasingly relies on unsupervised anomaly detection to identify structural defects when abnormal samples are critically scarce. This study presents an evaluation of hybrid generative architectures designed to detect complex overshooting anomalies in industrial simple sub-assemblies base plates. We analysed eight distinct model combinations by pairing four advanced generative backbones, including a latent space resampling autoencoder and a denoising diffusion model, with two boundary classification strategies: the one class support vector machine and the deep support vector data description. The experimental results demonstrate that the configuration pairing the latent space resampling autoencoder with the one class support vector machine achieves superior detection capabilities, securing the highest mean area under the curve of 0.7870 alongside absolute statistical dominance. However, our findings reveal a critical architectural vulnerability, as pairing heavily regularized generative latent spaces with the rigid hyperspherical boundaries of the deep data description model invariably degrades detection, driving in the most strongly regularized configuration a systematic inversion of the anomaly score rather than a loss of discriminative power. Ultimately, this research establishes that flexible margin optimization is required to preserve anomaly detection accuracy in complex industrial topologies, providing a framework for deploying reliable automated quality assurance systems.

2c82404e59061d43e26831844193b6893fbcf292.abstract: The increase in the demand for energy across the world coupled with environmental issues has heightened the importance of developing sustainable and intelligent energy systems. Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) represent some of the key technologies that can be employed to optimize the efficiency, reliability, and sustainability of the current energy systems. These technologies have become important due to the capacity of the systems based on such technologies to make data-driven decisions using predictive algorithms, automated control processes, as well as real-time decision-making processes. Some common applications of AI and ML include renewable energy forecasting, energy storage systems, predictive maintenance of energy systems, smart grids, and smart energy management in demand side. AI-based approaches for sustainable energy hold a lot of benefits for the environment as well as the economy. AI/ML technologies within the scope of sustainable energy engineering will be critical in realizing goals of energy efficiency and reduced emissions.

title: Deep Learning for Adaptive Management of Renewable Hybrid Power Systems

Optimizing Sustainable Energy Engineering With AI and Machine Learning
d578d62f03821803d57f6e8a397facef71850f2b.abstract: This study examines the problem of adaptive control for hybrid renewable energy systems combining photovoltaic panels, wind turbines, and battery storage under conditions of generation uncertainty and price volatility. A control strategy based on deep reinforcement learning is proposed, which does not require an explicit mathematical model and accounts for long-term consequences, including battery degradation. The control task is formalized as a markov decision process with an integral discounted reward combining economic costs, penalties for energy curtailment, and storage aging losses. Computational experiments on real meteorological data demonstrate that the trained regulator reduces operating costs by 12–15% compared to heuristic strategies, increases the share of renewable energy used by 18–22%, and extends estimated battery life by 15–20%. The results confirm the advantages of the proposed approach over classical methods, particularly under high uncertainty. Limitations and prospects for practical implementation are discussed.

63395033ead6c334c44934c0c842fb3ccadf45ea.abstract: The rapid growth of distributed energy resources and renewable technologies has increased the need for intelligent management of modern power systems. Microgrids offer a reliable, flexible, and sustainable solution by integrating local generation, storage, and controllable loads. However, their planning and control are complex due to uncertainties in renewable generation, varying load demand, and dynamic conditions. Artificial Intelligence (AI) has emerged as an effective tool to address these challenges. Techniques such as machine learning, deep learning, and optimization enable accurate forecasting of energy demand, renewable output, and system behavior.AI also enhances real-time control through adaptive decision-making and efficient energy management. This improves reliability, reduces costs, and increases resilience to disturbances. Overall, AI integration enables efficient resource use, minimizes losses, and supports the transition to smart, sustainable, and decentralized power systems.

title: AI-Assisted Optimization of Hybrid Renewable Energy Microgrids for Sustainable Rural Electrification

ea5cb44704ea7f5ca67dc3a9d789f030592a4484.abstract: This chapter reviews conventional optimization methods and AI-assisted approaches for hybrid renewable energy microgrids, highlighting their roles in system planning, sizing, operation, and control. It also explores emerging technologies, including reinforcement learning, explainable AI, digital twins, and edge AI, that are shaping the next generation of intelligent energy systems. To illustrate the practical application of these concepts, the chapter presents a case study of a hybrid renewable energy microgrid in Muanda, Democratic Republic of the Congo, featuring solar photovoltaic generation, battery energy storage, and blue-carbon bioenergy resources. The case study shows how optimization techniques can enhance techno-economic and environmental performance and discusses the potential of AI-based forecasting, intelligent battery management, and reinforcement learning to further improve system reliability, renewable energy utilization, and long-term sustainability.

a481d5d2ec22f7c57987bf6fb1f4d55e7e848167.abstract: The integration of digital intelligence and artificial intelligence in waste-to-energy (WtE) infrastructure optimization to achieve net-zero cities is presented in this chapter. The rapid urbanization and the growing amount of waste demand efficient and sustainable solutions. Municipal waste is turned into energy in WtE systems, and traditional operations lack flexibility and efficiency. The chapter uses systematic literature review as a method on the topic indexed in more than 200 articles and summarizing main conclusions of the quality research. It discusses monitoring with IoT, digital twins, and real-time optimization based on AI and predictive maintenance and energy recovery that is better. Case studies show the changes in the operational efficiency, emission control, and stability of systems. A conceptual AI-enabled framework is presented to find a solution to combine WtE systems with smart grids and urban energy networks. The results conclude on how smart WtE infrastructure contributes to the use of the circular economy and sustainable, low-carbon urban development.

dc3def60d826262ab21f0eea8c2fef98b5d58e72.abstract: Solar thermal systems encounter distinct operational challenges, which hinder their applicability. Artificial intelligence (AI) has the potential to solve them. The AI is more flexible and adaptable than traditional methods, which cannot deal with unpredictable factors, including changing weather and fluctuating energy demands. In this chapter, we introduced the solar thermal systems, and then the fundamentals of AI techniques used in solar thermal systems were provided. Subsequently, the application of AI in solar thermal systems was discussed. The advantages of the optimization process of the solar thermal systems were identified, supported by case studies from the real world. Then we identified the limitations and constraints that hinder the integration of AI into the solar thermal system. Finally, the economic benefits of using AI for the optimization of solar thermal systems were explained.

92ef05c8e2ba0949c3bf8f69974d39c51dc39e56.abstract: This chapter analyses the strategic incorporation of artificial intelligence technology into renewable energy systems to enhance energy security, operational efficiency, and long-term sustainability. This chapter aims to examine how intelligent energy management systems, machine learning algorithms, smart grids, decentralized microgrids, and Internet of Things (IoT) networks can enhance the performance and resilience of renewable energy systems. This chapter places emphasis on predictive analytics, battery management, solar forecasting, digital twins, and autonomous energy optimization. The chapter examines the economic, environmental, and technological ramifications of intelligent energy systems, emphasizing their capacity to minimize energy losses, improve system reliability, facilitate decentralized electrification, and expedite sustainable energy transitions towards enhanced national energy independence.

974378bf655d4595a7410253b21e0ad381c1a368.abstract: This chapter presents a systematic examination of how Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning techniques are transforming the design, operation, diagnosis, and control of solar thermal energy systems, including flat-plate collectors, evacuated tube collectors, and concentrating solar power plants. Principal ML methodologies surveyed include Artificial Neural Networks, Support Vector Regression, Gradient Boosting, Long Short-Term Memory networks, Transformer architectures, Physics-Informed Neural Networks, and Deep Reinforcement Learning. Applications are reviewed across four domains data-driven surrogate models for thermal performance prediction, ML-based irradiance and thermal output forecasting, intelligent fault detection and predictive maintenance frameworks, and AI-driven control strategies shown to improve annual useful heat delivery by 8 to 15 percent. Research challenges including data scarcity, model interpretability, and cross-site generalization are identified, with future directions proposed in federated learning, physics-informed architectures, and explainable AI.

a35056ead95e6546af494efa6e34c4e7ce0284ba.abstract: This chapter develops a conceptual and methodological framework for artificial-intelligence- and machine-learning-enabled energy audits in Tanzanian industrial small and medium-sized enterprises. Industrial SMEs often face energy-efficiency barriers related to limited capital, weak information systems, incomplete metering, and constrained managerial capacity. The chapter positions the energy audit as the organizing mechanism for sustainable energy engineering and shows how AI/ML can strengthen load profiling, benchmarking, anomaly detection, forecasting, measure prioritization, and measurement and verification. Drawing on peer-reviewed evidence from SME audit programs, ISO 50001 research, African industrial energy studies, and applied AI/ML energy literature, the chapter proposes a staged implementation roadmap for Tanzanian SMEs. The contribution is a practical pathway for moving from one-off audits toward data-informed, explainable, and financially grounded energy management.

2488e9ed487b4765c71f38c4edb94b5b6290f2ae.abstract: Anaerobic co-digestion is an effective approach for biogas production, but optimizing operating parameters remains challenging due to the interaction of multiple variables. This study integrates ultrasonic pretreatment with Response Surface Methodology (RSM) to enhance biogas yield from a mixture of dormitory food waste and pet animal dung. Batch digesters were operated at 37 °C, and daily biogas production was monitored. RSM evaluated the combined effects of ultrasonic temperature (25–65 °C), power (500–1,500 W), and treatment time (35–75 min). Biogas yield ranged from 35% to nearly 68%, with optimum conditions of 53.35 °C, 1,490.83 W, and 57.15 min, producing a predicted yield of 66.47%. The quadratic model showed excellent predictive performance (R2 = 0.9707; F = 110.33), confirming the importance of simultaneous optimization. The integrated ultrasonic–RSM approach provides a reliable and efficient strategy for maximizing biogas production in anaerobic co-digestion systems.

title: Application of Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning Methods to Optimize Energy System Stability

af88092a3405a3484f3caf6617dee2099625164e.abstract: This article presents a systematic analysis of artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) methods applied to the optimization of energy system stability. Deep learning architectures for forecasting electricity demand and renewable energy generation, reinforcement learning algorithms for microgrid control, the concept of digital twins, and explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) methods are examined. The application of hybrid models reduces forecasting errors by 20–35% over ultra-short-term forecasting horizons ranging from several minutes to several hours. The transition to probabilistic forecasting reduces balancing costs by 8–15%, while the use of digital twins decreases operating costs by 15–25%. Current challenges limiting the implementation of intelligent technologies in the energy sector are identified, and priority areas for further research are outlined. The results are systematized in comparative tables suitable for practical use when selecting appropriate methodological tools.

b326566af7bfa615ecca304269db8b978877aabc.abstract: This chapter per the authors examines machine learning for forecasting electrical load and renewable generation under energy transition and grid digitalization. The purpose is to show why power systems need models handling nonlinear, non-stationary, and heterogeneous data. The chapter reviews LSTM, BiLSTM, GRU, CNN, TCN, hybrid architectures, ensembles, SVR, and GPR. Solar and wind forecasting depend on weather uncertainty, spatial relationships, and telemetry quality. The chapter compares facility types with forecasting methods and discusses digital twins, adaptive forecasting, and closed-loop control. Key problems: data drift, limited transferability, interpretability, computational complexity, and SCADA cybersecurity. Development requires integrating forecasting with digital twins, XAI, reinforcement learning, anomaly detection, and cybersecurity. Machine learning becomes a foundation for proactive and resilient power system management.

title: Integrating Transformer Neural Processes and Deep Kernel Learning for High-Throughput Screening and Uncertainty Quantification for Water-Splitting Electrocatalysts Across Perovskites and Metal Alloys

bcafa941c82b95b48c33f91be24df91543e346ce.abstract: Years of experimentation have failed to enable the prediction of an efficient electrocatalyst from either a perovskite or an alloy without weeks of experimentation. There are more than a million perovskites, more exponential number of alloys but fewer than 0.1% of them have been studied. The traditional approach has failed. Density Functional Theory is impractical because of costs. Gaussian Process Regression struggles with scalability and lacks transfer between families. Its uncertainty calibration is off by miles. More importantly, the literature is not homogenous. Any framework that ignores that problem learns procedures, not physics. We gather Transformer Neural Processes (meta-learning across families) with Deep Kernel Learning (statistical uncertainty). This neural architecture can scale and model overpotential, stability, and activity with correlated uncertainties. Standardization of overpotential is done through Tafel correction. Prediction errors in the range of 50 millivolts and two- to three-fold reduction of experiments through Bayesian Optimization are our goals.

title: Quantum machine learning for quantitative finance

724fa6d98bd76a667b62a4a9ef37642267472d2d.abstract: Abstract Machine learning (ML) and quantum ML (QML) have gained significant importance, as they offer powerful tools for tackling complex computational problems across various domains. An overview of QML’s uses in quantitative finance is presented here. The connection between quantum computing and ML in financial applications, spanning a range of use cases including portfolio optimization, market prediction and trading, pricing and risk management is examined. The different applications from the literature review are categorized based on specific use cases, ML approaches, optimization methods, and the types of quantum hardware utilized. To facilitate this examination, we employ a morphological box, which allows us to analyze different combinations of these elements across financial use cases.

title: Integrasi AI dalam Kurikulum Akuntansi Pendidikan Pesantren: Tinjauan Literatur Sistematis tentang Kesiapan Teknologi, Pemahaman AI, dan Karakteristik Siswa
container-title: Business and Accounting Education Journal
9db92d2d3af48ff40caacdc975fdcbe142bb7929.abstract: Perkembangan Artificial Intelligence (AI) telah mendorong transformasi pendidikan akuntansi dan menuntut penyesuaian kurikulum agar sesuai dengan kebutuhan dunia kerja digital. Namun, adopsi AI dalam kurikulum akuntansi masih dipengaruhi oleh berbagai faktor, khususnya pada konteks pendidikan pesantren yang memiliki karakteristik unik. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis pengaruh kesiapan teknologi, pemahaman AI, dan karakteristik siswa terhadap adopsi AI dalam kurikulum akuntansi serta mengidentifikasi faktor yang paling dominan. Penelitian menggunakan metode Systematic Literature Review (SLR) dengan pedoman PRISMA 2020. Data diperoleh dari 38 artikel ilmiah terindeks Scopus yang dipublikasikan pada periode 2015-2026 dan dianalisis menggunakan sintesis tematik. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa kesiapan teknologi merupakan faktor yang paling dominan dalam mendorong adopsi AI, diikuti oleh pemahaman AI dan karakteristik siswa. Ketiga faktor tersebut saling melengkapi dalam meningkatkan penerimaan dan pemanfaatan AI dalam pembelajaran akuntansi. Temuan ini berkontribusi pada pengembangan model adopsi teknologi pendidikan serta menjadi dasar pengembangan kurikulum akuntansi berbasis AI di lingkungan pesantren.

title: Reduced desaturation-based detection of sleep apnea events in self-identified Black individuals across two cohorts
container-title: American Journal of Respiratory and Critical Care Medicine
ed4970d6b47ded144161ae130827ea3845a200e6.abstract: Abstract Rationale Pulse oximetry may overestimate oxygen saturation in individuals with darker skin pigmentation, potentially reducing detection of desaturation during sleep-disordered breathing. Objectives To assess racial/ethnic differences in desaturation-based obstructive event detection and cardiovascular risk, and evaluate heart-rate response as an oximetry-independent marker for risk stratification. Methods We analyzed participants without cardiovascular disease in the Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis(MESA) and Sleep Heart Health Study(SHHS). We modeled desaturation-based AHI relative to airflow-defined AHI and examined AHI-ΔHR6, defined by respiratory events with a heart-rate increase ≥6 beats/min. Adjusted Cox models evaluated associations with a composite outcome, major adverse cardiovascular events or all-cause mortality(MACE/mortality). Measurements and Main Results Black participants had 21% and 20% lower proportions of airflow-defined events meeting the ≥4% desaturation criterion than White participants in MESA (ratio 0.79[95% CI,0.68–0.93]; p = 0.003) and SHHS (0.80[0.68–0.94]; p = 0.008), respectively. No other racial/ethnic group showed a lower proportion of airflow-defined events meeting desaturation criteria than White participants. AHI-ΔHR6 event detection was similar between Black and White participants in both cohorts. In Whites participants, desaturation-based events were associated with MACE/mortality in MESA but not in SHHS, while desaturation-based AHI measures were not significantly associated with MACE/mortality in Black individuals in either cohort. In contrast, AHI-ΔHR6 was associated with MACE/mortality in MESA (HR 1.33[1.09–1.63];p=0.006) and SHHS (1.26[1.02–1.55]; p = 0.033). Conclusions Desaturation-based scoring identified a lower proportion of reduced flow events in Black than White participants, whereas heart-rate-response-based event detection was similar across groups, suggesting oximetry-related under-detection in individuals with darker pigment.

title: MOSQMIXERNET: A CUSTOM DEEP LEARNING ARCHITECTURE FOR EARLY-STAGE MOSQUITO CLASSIFICATION AND GENUS-LEVEL IDENTIFICATION
container-title: Oxford Open Digital Health
b19eb599996384d4293e8b42a9b81d7a6a708b27.abstract: Abstract Mosquito-borne diseases such as malaria, dengue, zika, and chikungunya impose a disproportionate heavy public health burden on Africa. While artificial intelligence (AI) tools have been applied in species identification on the adult mosquitoes, the early aquatic stages have been largely ignored. Yet, these early stages are critical since vector control strategies often target larvae and pupae to break the transmission cycle before mosquitoes mature into biting adults. Moreover, the identification of these specimens is prone to human error by experts due to the striking similarity in morphological features between larval and pupal stages across species. This limitation delays surveillance and increases the risk of misclassification, potentially compromising vector control efforts. In response, an Africa-based curated dataset is introduced, encompassing the larval and pupal stages of Aedes, Anopheles, and Culex species, along with non-mosquito specimens of similar morphology. This dataset helps address the underrepresentation of African samples in global repositories and provides a rare contribution to pupal-stage classification, a category largely overlooked in most classification tasks. MosqMixerNet is introduced as a lightweight deep learning model designed for image-based classification of mosquito early stages. The proposed MosqMixerNet balances compactness and accuracy with only 169 666 trainable parameters and was benchmarked against MobileNetV2, DenseNet121, and NASNetMobile. For genus-level identification, it achieved 99.37% accuracy, surpassing NASNetMobile (97.30%), MobileNetV2 (97.26%), and DenseNet121 (80.39%). The work advances computer vision for public health and tropical disease control, and provides a foundation for integration into digital vector monitoring platforms in endemic settings.

title: KUNJUTNING ODDIY VA BEKROSS CHATISHTIRISH NATIJASIDA OLINGAN F1  DURAGAYLARIDA O‘SIMLIK BO‘YI VA YON SHOXLARI SONI BELGILARINING IRSIYLANISHI
container-title: Agro ilm
fdd79e12d4dc98c72a7ea30e9bb3a464401f1cbe.abstract: The study investigated the inheritance of important morphological traits, including plant height and the number of lateral branches, in simple and backcross F₁ sesame hybrids involving the local varieties “Onimdar”, “Qora Shahzoda”, “Tashkent-122”, and “Sadaf”. The experiments were conducted under field and laboratory conditions. The patterns of trait formation and the degree of heterosis in the hybrids were analyzed. The number of lateral branches ranged from 5.8 to 6.2 per plant in the local varieties, from 5.7 to 8.7 in simple F₁ hybrids, and from 5.6 to 9.2 in backcross hybrids. Positive heterosis for the number of lateral branches was observed in most of the simple hybrids. Positive inheritance of this trait was also recorded in several backcross combinations. Promising hybrid combinations with high values of plant height and the number of lateral branches were identified. The results indicate that the selected hybrid combinations can be used in sesame breeding to develop valuable initial breeding material with high productivity, stability, and adaptability to local environmental conditions.

title: SUG‘ORILADIGAN YERLAR UCHUN ARPA SELEKSIYASIDA OLIB BORILAYOTGAN TADQIQOTLAR
container-title: Agro ilm
5ceb721e66711f7ae20303275a9a4626549b0abb.abstract: The article presents the results of research aimed at identifying valuable initial breeding material for barley breeding on irrigated lands. The studies were conducted in 2023–2026 at the experimental field of the “Farboma selekt” scientific seed-growing farm located in Jomboy district of Samarkand region. A total of 200 barley collection accessions obtained from the international centers ICARDA and CIMMYT, as well as the Institute of Plant Science and the Gallaorol Research and Experimental Station of the Research Institute of Grain and Legume Crops, were studied. The accessions were evaluated for productive tillering, number and weight of grains per spike, 1000-grain weight, yield, earliness, and resistance to diseases, winter conditions and lodging. The study identified valuable barley accessions with high productivity and yield potential. In particular, the Mirzacho‘l, K-22845, K-19985, Temur and K-566244 accessions demonstrated high yield performance. The selected accessions are recommended as valuable initial breeding material for developing new high-yielding, early-maturing and environmentally stress-resistant barley varieties for irrigated lands.

711b3b23f900ba8e064c6c874bedbee457db7997.abstract: The article examines the impact of sowing methods, timing, and rates on the yield and grain quality of chickpea varieties in irrigated lands (under the conditions of the Kashkadarya region). The research results demonstrate the extent of this influence on the productivity and grain quality of chickpea varieties in the irrigated soils of the Kashkadarya region.

title: NO’XATNI SUG’ORISHNING TUP SONIGA TA’SIRI

082f36c736e87ce9716851e175549fbf531e9f4b.abstract: The article studies the formation of plant density in chickpea varieties under different irrigation methods and irrigation regimes. The study examined the effects of furrow, drip and sprinkler irrigation, as well as irrigation regimes of 65–70–60%, 70–75–65% and 75–80–70% of field capacity. The results showed that plant density of the Zumrad and Malhotra chickpea varieties varied depending on the irrigation method and soil moisture regime. The highest plant density was recorded under drip irrigation with an irrigation regime of 75–80–70% of field capacity in the Malhotra variety, reaching 282.7 plants/m² at the beginning of the growing period and 275.3 plants/m² at the end. The obtained results demonstrate the importance of selecting an appropriate irrigation method and soil moisture regime for chickpea cultivation.

title: MUTTASIL SHOLI VA QISQA NAVBATLI ALMASHLAB EKISH TIZIMLARINING BARG SATHI VA QURUQ MODDA TO‘PLANISHIGA TA’SIRI

59460cc3f998f0cb6fd2a2c8fc98b6ddf4dd81eb.abstract: This article examines issues related to continuous rice cropping and the rice–barley–rice and rice–green manure–rice crop rotation systems. title: Feature Interaction-Driven Machine Learning for Hotel Cancellation Prediction: Integrating Bayesian Networks and Gradient Boosting
container-title: International Journal of Information Technology & Decision Making
2eb6ba098c04fc796d8c90763a87e74e47bd74ac.abstract: Online travel platforms such as Trip.com and Agoda have made it easier to modify or cancel hotel reservations, increasing uncertainty for hotel revenue management. Cancellations can increase room vacancy, destabilize revenue, and raise operating costs. To address these challenges, this study proposes a feature-interaction-enhancement framework that enriches reservation data with interpretable cross-dimensional features designed to capture nonlinear relationships between booking behavior and cancellation risk. Unlike hybrid prediction models that jointly optimize a Bayesian network (BN) and a classifier, the proposed framework uses the BN solely as an auxiliary feature extractor. It generates two meta-features — the posterior cancellation probability and its entropy — which are concatenated with the original and interaction features for downstream prediction. We systematically compare several optimized machine-learning models, including Decision Tree, Random Forest, Gradient Boosting, and XGBoost, and apply SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) to the best-performing model to quantify feature contributions and derive operational insights. The experimental results show that the feature-enhanced framework outperforms baselines that rely solely on the original predictors. The resulting risk estimates can help hotels identify high-risk bookings and design targeted interventions, provided they are appropriately calibrated and operationally validated.

title: Does Portable Voice Amplification Improve Vocal Outcomes in Elementary School Teachers? Evidence From Aerodynamic, Acoustic, and Self-Reported Measures
container-title: American Journal of Speech-Language Pathology
0ab54f51f121d8c34e36c0f89336b670debb8790.abstract: Purpose: The present study aimed at evaluating the impact of a voice amplification system plus vocal hygiene on aerodynamic, acoustic, and self-reported outcomes in elementary school teachers with and without voice problems. Method: A total of 217 elementary school teachers were initially recruited: 108 normal-voiced participants and 109 participants with voice complaints. Participants from both groups were assessed before and after voice intervention, with aerodynamic, acoustic, and self-reported outcomes being observed. Participants were randomly assigned to one of two treatments before starting voice intervention procedures: (a) use of amplification system in their classroom setting plus vocal hygiene program (experimental condition) and (b) vocal hygiene program only (control condition). Thus, four groups were generated for this study. Data were analyzed by implementing mixed-effects models for all dependent variables. Results: For dysphonic teachers, significant interactions were observed on Vocal Fatigue Index, Voice Handicap Index, and Vocal Tract Discomfort Scale values, reflecting greater improvement for the experimental group as compared to the control group once the intervention was completed. In contrast, no differential effects were observed for smoothed cepstral peak prominence, airflow rate, subglottal pressure, or phonation threshold pressure. Only one significant interaction was detected in participants with normal voices, suggesting that treatment is more effective for teachers already suffering from dysphonia. Conclusions: Portable amplification system plus vocal hygiene seems to positively impact dysphonic school teachers' voice, especially in terms of self-reported improvements in functional, physical, and emotional voice-related dimensions; throat discomfort; and vocal fatigue symptoms. No statistically significant changes were observed for aerodynamic or acoustic outcomes. These findings, along with prior evidence, suggest that voice amplification may be most beneficial when implemented as one component of a broader approach to occupational vocal health, combined with other strategies such as voice training and classroom acoustic interventions.

title: From prediction to design rules: explainable machine learning analysis of cryoprotectant effects in GelMA-based cryobioprinting bioinks
container-title: Biomedical Physics & Engineering Express
cba1d2360d45f4f2da517a4c0ec4ef34475e0fff.abstract: Abstract Machine learning has been used to predict cryoprotective-agent (CPA) effects in cryobioprinting, but prediction accuracy alone does not yield experimentally usable formulation rules. Here, we performed a secondary explainable analysis of Qiao et al ’s GelMA-HUVEC dataset using formulation-grouped validation, SHAP interpretation, stability metrics, and multi-objective ranking. A compact Random Forest model using permeable CPA identity, sugar CPA identity, permeable CPA concentration, sugar concentration, and storage day achieved MAE = 4.842%, RMSE = 6.106%, and R 2 = 0.649, with bootstrap 95% confidence intervals of 4.418–5.274% for MAE and 0.585–0.710 for R 2 . SHAP analysis identified permeable CPA concentration and storage day as the strongest viability drivers, with directional patterns favoring balanced 15% permeable CPA and 15% sugar CPA rather than simple concentration maximization. Multi-objective ranking identified GL_15_RA_15 as the strongest individual formulation, whereas EG + trehalose showed the highest average CPA-family performance. Cross-domain tests showed limited transfer between EG and GL formulations, indicating that the extracted rules should be treated as local, data-supported design hypotheses rather than universal cryoprotectant principles. Together, these results show that explainable secondary analysis can convert small cryobioprinting datasets into experimentally testable CPA hypotheses while explicitly defining their transferability limits.

title: Physics-inspired semi-supervised multi-loss learning for internal defect monitoring in laser directed energy deposition
container-title: Measurement Science and Technology
217f787146f8579923b134a94b5579cae5fe3536.abstract: Abstract In laser directed energy deposition (LDED) additive manufacturing, monitoring internal defects based on melt pool features is critical for ensuring product quality, process efficiency, and operational safety. However, existing monitoring approaches remain constrained by two key limitations: (i) the scarcity of defect-labelled data, since defect characterization typically requires destructive testing; and (ii) the dominance of purely data-driven models, which often neglect the intrinsic connection between melt pool features and internal defects, consequently lack interpretability. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a physics-inspired semi-supervised defect monitoring framework that integrates melt pool features with defect-related physical information within a multi-loss learning paradigm. Specifically, image processing extracts melt-pool width, length, area, perimeter and intensity. Correlation-derived feature weights define a class-specific consistency criterion for accepting high-confidence pseudo-labels, while crack and porosity penalties and a structural complexity term guide the selection of random-forest models. The forests are constructed using standard CART induction; the physics-inspired information acts through candidate-model selection and the composition of the augmented training set. Ablation and comparative studies on LDED data report an accuracy of 0.94, a support-weighted F 1-score of 0.94 and a macro- F 1 score of 0.87. The framework provides a means of incorporating defect-related knowledge into monitoring with limited annotations.

title: Charge collection efficiency in air-vented plane-parallel ionisation chambers at ultra-high dose rates: a self-consistent Garfield++ Monte Carlo model including space-charge effects and ion recombination
container-title: Physics in Medicine & Biology
4821ad7e99d838bfdb7f094f0aa12de65a149d58.abstract: Abstract Objective. Ultra-high dose rate (UHDR) irradiation used in FLASH radiotherapy can lead to significant reductions in charge collection efficiency (CCE) in plane-parallel ionisation chambers due to enhanced ion recombination, while the high charge densities involved can also induce strong space-charge-induced electric-field distortions. This work aims to develop a Monte Carlo framework for investigating these coupled effects. Approach. We extended the Garfield++ Monte Carlo particle-transport framework by implementing ion–ion recombination and self-consistent space-charge electric field calculations. The resulting model couples particle transport, electron attachment, recombination processes, and dynamic electric-field distortions. The implementation was validated against analytical and numerical models from the literature. Main results. Excellent agreement was obtained for the free electron fraction (FEF), CCE, induced current, and electric field evolution under UHDR conditions. The simulations show that space charge can locally increase the electric field by more than a factor of four or reduce it to nearly zero in some regions of the chamber. The results further suggest that the decrease in the FEF caused by electric-field-dependent electron attachment plays a major role in the reduction of the CCE under UHDR conditions. Significance. These findings highlight the importance of accurately describing the evolution of the FEF for modelling recombination under UHDR conditions, opening up prospects for improved analytical models and real-time correction methods for ionisation chamber dosimetry. More broadly, this work provides a flexible and self-consistent Monte Carlo framework for investigating recombination phenomena and improving dosimetry models for FLASH radiotherapy.

title: Rising to the challenges: Teaching and learning grand challenges through the vertical BCom core
e183ff03a65f541eb459c4cd14b6557272c8283c.abstract: Businesses, governments and societies around the world face significant challenges that demand ambitious ideas, diverse perspectives, expertise and coordinated effort: Grand Challenges. Rising to the Challenges is an Open Educational Resource (e-text) for anyone curious about studying commerce and public policy, as well as for students already enrolled in the Bachelor of Commerce (BCom) at Te Herenga Waka—Victoria University of Wellington. It reveals what working on these challenges requires and how the vertically integrated BCom degree develops those capabilities. More than a course text, Rising to the Challenges shows the pieces of the jigsaw and how they fit together, helping a student to understand what’s coming before they need it, rather than only making sense of it afterwards. The resource follows students from identifying and framing Grand Challenges in BCOM 101, through structured analysis in BCOM 201, to developing and justifying practical responses in BCOM 301. It shows how BCOM 102’s tools, skills and mindsets support this progression alongside subject expertise developed through students’ majors. Used alongside detailed course resources, the e-text helps students look ahead, revisit earlier learning and connect experiences to deepen understanding. It supports increasing ownership of learning, evidence-based articulation of capability, and preparation for professional work and continuing development. It also shares the educational approach with colleagues and other educators. The aim is to help you make more of your BCom: connect what you learn, recognise what you can do, and carry it into work and life so you can rise to the challenges ahead.

36ede77f584724c16c6df8d872616165c6726651.abstract: This article investigates the effectiveness of biological fertilizers and resource-saving agrotechnologies for potato (Solanum tuberosum L.) cultivation under the natural, climatic, and soil conditions of the Republic of Karakalpakstan. title: Efficacy of a Validated Yoga-Breath Linked Intervention (Y-BLISS) for smoking cessation: A Randomized Controlled Trial
container-title: Nicotine & Tobacco Research
f4fd28ecb4c683c253f96e44b8e5c3512a01eddb.abstract: Abstract Introduction Tobacco use disorder remains a global health concern, and safe complementary interventions are needed. We evaluated a validated Yoga-Breath Linked Intervention to Stop Smoking (Y-BLISS). Methods In this randomized controlled trial, 139 smokers meeting DSM-5 criteria for tobacco use disorder with moderate to severe nicotine dependence (Fagerström Test for Nicotine Dependence, FTND ≥4) were randomized to Y-BLISS (n = 70) or desktop exercise control (n = 69). Y-BLISS comprised a 12-minute yoga-breath protocol with single-session yoga philosophy-based psychotherapy, delivered online under live supervision 5 days/week for 8 weeks. Controls received attention-matched desktop exercise with health education. The primary outcome was cigarettes per day (CPD). Secondary outcomes included 7-day point-prevalence abstinence, FTND, Tobacco Craving Questionnaire Short Form (TCQ-SF), peak expiratory flow rate (PEFR), and exhaled carbon monoxide (eCO). Assessments occurred at baseline, 4 and 8 weeks; analysis was intention-to-treat with linear mixed-effects models. Results Baseline characteristics were broadly comparable, with slightly higher dependence and craving in Y-BLISS (mean age 38.7 ± 8.6 years; 95% male; FTND 5.2 ± 1.2). At 8 weeks, Group × Time effects (β, 95% CI) favored Y-BLISS for CPD, FTND, TCQ-SF and PEFR, all p &lt; 0.001, and eCO (p = .04). Seven-day point-prevalence abstinence was 25.7% versus 11.6% (odds ratio 2.64, 1.06 to 6.57; p = 0.037). Differences were already present at 4 weeks for CPD, FTND, TCQ-SF and PEFR. Conclusions These findings support Y-BLISS as a promising adjunct to standard cessation care and justify longer-term, multicenter effectiveness and implementation trials.

title: Physics-guided deep residual learning for sound absorption prediction of micro-perforated panels
container-title: Physica Scripta
57d8592455e90409349a066b271cdd1c0d3d8c0c.abstract: Abstract To address the limited accuracy of analytical models, the high computational cost of finite element method (FEM) simulations, and the sample dependence of purely data-driven approaches for micro-perforated panel (MPP) sound absorption prediction, this study proposes a physics-guided deep residual network (PGDRN). A paired analytical-FEM dataset is constructed under identical structural parameters and frequency sampling points. Instead of directly fitting the complete FEM absorption curve, the FEM response is decomposed into an analytical baseline and an analytical-FEM residual correction. The network is trained to learn this residual discrepancy, while the analytical absorption coefficient and resonance mismatch are introduced as physics-guided features to enhance the representation of resonance-related frequency regions. Experiments on 1000 paired analytical-FEM samples show that PGDRN achieves an MAE of 0.0012, an RMSE of 0.0021, an R 2 of 0.9999, and a mean peak absorption coefficient error of 0.0022 on the test set. Compared with Mambular, the strongest data-driven baseline, PGDRN reduces MAE, RMSE, and peak error by 94.76%, 95.14%, and 95.53%, respectively. Ablation and limited-sample analyses confirm the contributions of residual learning and physics-guided features to prediction accuracy, peak-region stability, and sample efficiency. FEM sound-field visualization further supports the physical consistency of the predicted absorption behavior. The proposed method provides an accurate and interpretable surrogate model for rapid MPP sound absorption prediction under limited FEM samples.

title: Frequency, clinical course, and determinants of self-reported skin events during travel: a prospective mHealth cohort study
container-title: Journal of Travel Medicine
e74779da1d7ed85913ec2c6144dfef7d2227d532.abstract: Abstract Background Skin problems are frequently reported among international travelers. However, most existing evidence is from post-travel data, which overrepresent severe or healthcare-seeking disease. The broader daily spectrum of skin events that travelers experience remains poorly characterized. We aimed to quantify the frequency, clinical course, and determinants of self-reported skin-health events during travel using prospective data. Methods Real-time data were collected through the TOURIST2 prospective mHealth cohort study, in which travelers from Switzerland to Thailand, China, India, Tanzania, Brazil, or Peru reported daily symptoms via a smartphone application before, during, and after travel. Seven skin symptoms, signs, and skin injuries were recorded: rash, sunburn, insect bite–related itch, non–insect-related itch, wounds/cuts, animal-related injury, and marine animal injury. We described overall clinical burden (proportion of travelers with ≥1 event and with ≥2 distinct event types), incidence rates (IR) per 1,000 travel-days, and the clinical course of events (timing of onset, duration, severity on a 4-point Likert scale, and care-seeking). Negative binomial regression models were applied to estimate incidence rate ratios (IRRs) for demographic, behavioral, environmental, and destination-related determinants, using each participant’s pre- and post-travel data from Switzerland as comparison. Results Among 793 travelers, 68% reported at least one skin-health event during the first 16 days of travel and 48% experienced more than one skin health event during travel. Insect bite–related itch had the highest incidence (156.1 per 1,000 travel-days), followed by sunburn (103.0), non–insect-related itch (39.0) and rash (37.8). Most reports appeared after 7-11 days of travel, were mild and short-lived (median duration 1.0-2.5 days), and formal healthcare-seeking was uncommon; when treatment was sought, pharmacy use predominated over physician care. Insect-related itch and sunburn tended to occur early in travel, whereas rashes and other skin events showed distinct temporal patterns. A history of pre-existing skin-health conditions was the strongest predictor of skin events, increasing the risk of rash (IR = 8.64, 95% CI 4.31–19.03) and non-insect-related itch (IR = 4.41, 95% CI 2.50–8.27). Allergies were associated with a higher risk of itch (IR = 1.40, 95% CI 1.16–1.70) but a lower incidence of sunburn (IR = 0.76, 95% CI 0.62–0.92). Older age was consistently protective. Female sex was associated with greater risk of rash and animal-related injuries, whereas males reported more sunburn. Conclusions Skin-health events were common during international travel, but were predominantly short-lived, mild and rarely required medical care. Their timing and risk profiles differed by symptom type, supporting tailored pre-travel counseling on insect protection, sun exposure, allergy management, and care for travelers with pre-existing skin conditions. Smartphone-based monitoring complements traditional travel medicine surveillance by capturing the broader spectrum and clinical course of non-care-seeking travel-related morbidity.

title: Light Regulation of Phototropin Promoter Activity in Arabidopsis thaliana
container-title: Plant and Cell Physiology
eef9afd53eb47a4daee3251a5a2e7271ffbfa24c.abstract: Abstract Light regulates the expression of phototropins by decreasing PHOT1 mRNA levels and increasing PHOT2 mRNA levels. In Arabidopsis thaliana, the light-regulated activity of phototropin promoters paralleled the levels of PHOT1 and PHOT2 transcripts. The activity of phototropin promoters in different organs and at various developmental stages reflected the physiological need for those receptors. The PHOT1 promoter was predominantly active in the above-ground parts of etiolated seedlings, which depend on the ability of phototropin1 to sense low light levels. The PHOT2 promoter activity was high in light-grown mature plants, with substantial expression found in inflorescence, rosette, and cauline leaves. The PHOT2 promoter was strongly activated by light also in N. benthamiana leaves. Y1H assay revealed transcription factors that might be responsible for the light regulation of phototropin promoters. Transcription factors from the homeobox (HB) family (ATHB12) were identified as interacting with the PHOT1 promoter, while ANAC102, ARF19, TCP2, and A-PTF-1 were found to interact with the PHOT2 promoter. Using cEMSA, interactions between the DNA-binding domains of TCP2 and ANAC102 with the PHOT2 promoter and the interaction between the ATHB12 domain and the PHOT1 promoter were demonstrated in vitro. The role of ATHB12 in the control of PHOT1 expression was further confirmed at the mRNA level in Arabidopsis seedlings. Our results point to transcription factor families that may be important for the control of phototropin promoter activity.

title: Learning discriminative time-frequency representations for EEG segment-level seizure-state classification with channel selection
container-title: Biomedical Physics & Engineering Express
1ed17958fb1f2a16077b144e070f680132ef71bf.abstract: Abstract Electroencephalography (EEG)-based seizure monitoring supports the diagnosis and management of epilepsy; however, high-dimensional multichannel EEG recordings impose substantial computational burden and limit suitability for portable monitoring systems. This paper proposes a reduced-channel framework for segment-level classification of EEG into ictal, preictal and interictal states. It integrates attention-guided EEG channel selection, high-resolution time-frequency analysis via the time reassigned multisynchrosqueezing Transform and concentration of frequency and time, and a hybrid CNN-BiLSTM classifier. The framework is evaluated on the CHB-MIT and Siena Scalp EEG databases under two complementary protocols: a stratified 70/30 holdout split and rigorous leave-one-subject-out (LOSO) cross-validation to assess subject independent generalization. Under holdout evaluation using a single EEG channel, the proposed framework achieves an accuracy of 99.28 ± 0.63 % , sensitivity of 99.18 % , specificity of 99.64 % , and Matthews correlation coefficient (MCC) of 0.97 on CHB-MIT, and an accuracy of 98.75 ± 0.74 % , sensitivity of 98.77 % , specificity of 99.38 % , and MCCs of 0.97 on Siena. LOSO cross-validation demonstrates subject independent generalization, exceeding 91 % accuracy on both databases. These results demonstrate that the framework achieves an effective balance among segment-level classification accuracy, computational efficiency and reduced-channel operation. Moreover, applicability for portable and wearable EEG-based seizure-state monitoring applications is investigated.

title: Deep learning reveals severe shelterbelt degradation in eastern Ukraine due to the war
container-title: Environmental Research Letters
bd8226c397bea6376a1edce594afb06704e9ea1b.abstract: Abstract Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022 has caused extensive damage to forests, particularly in eastern and southern regions with sustained combat, where field shelterbelts have often been used as cover and subsequently heavily destroyed. This study presents a systematic region-scale assessment of pre-war shelterbelt area and war-related loss between 2021 and 2025 using 3 m PlanetScope imagery and deep learning. We evaluated three input datasets—monthly PlanetScope RGB mosaics, multiseasonal PlanetScope RGB stacks, and surface reflectance (SR) PlanetScope imagery—in combination with two semantic segmentation architectures: a convolutional U-Net with a ResNet-34 encoder and a transformer-based SegFormer with a MiT-B0 backbone. Across all input configurations, the U-Net consistently outperformed SegFormer, achieving the highest F 1 scores. Monthly RGB mosaics delivered accuracy comparable to more complex multiseasonal and SR inputs in pixel-based evaluation and are a cost-efficient option for mapping narrow shelterbelts. The RGB-based model trained on July 2021 mosaics reached an F 1 score of 0.71 and retained values of 0.58–0.67 for other months of the same leaf-on season. Temporal transfer to 2025 resulted in lower but still reasonable performance with F 1 scores of 0.53–0.63. Error-adjusted mapping estimated the shelterbelt area in 2021 at 254 ± 14.5 thousand ha, equivalent to a mean density of 2.6 ha km −2 . By 2025, this area had been reduced by approximately 41 thousand ha, or 16% of the pre-war area. Losses were strongly concentrated along frontlines where local losses exceeded 1.5 ha km −2 compared to an average loss of 0.5 ha km −2 across the entire study area. The resulting maps complement the existing forest monitoring framework in Ukraine and provide a spatially explicit basis for prioritizing post-war remediation and assessing losses in protective functions and carbon accumulation.

title: Cochlea-inspired spectral representation with bi-branch ensemble learning for single-source domain generalization motor fault diagnosis
container-title: Measurement Science and Technology
3d0c0504d94dc928cfb2b7304a776651ae0e7a45.abstract: Abstract Single-source motor fault diagnosis often degrades under unseen speed and load conditions because a single operating condition provides limited spectral diversity, whereas unconstrained augmentation may introduce non-fault-related artifacts. To address both limitations, we propose CoMel-Brain, which couple fault-sensitive spectral representation with controlled pseudo-domain learning. The CoMel representation maps cochlear-decomposed vibration components onto the Mel scale to emphasize low-frequency fault patterns. Based on this representation, a phase-preserving magnitude-spectrum perturbation expands spectral diversity while maintaining structural information. A guidance-exploration architecture further aligns augmented representations with the fault-related semantics of the original samples and stabilizes knowledge integration through periodic parameter averaging. Experiments on a seven-class induction-motor dataset covering 15 speed–load conditions yield average target-domain accuracies of 93.60%, 95.38%, and 84.87% for source domains A, H, and O, respectively, outperforming the strongest competing methods by 7.23, 3.66, and 6.47 percentage points.

title: Gcn5 and mTORC1 mediated regulation of autophagy controls Drosophila blood cell homeostasis
container-title: eLife
9c550981cef0b3b83e44bac93a32a92a87838e3c.abstract: Blood progenitors are regulated by a variety of systemic and nutritional cues from their environment. In the Drosophila lymph gland (LG), the Posterior Signaling Center acts as a stem cell niche striking a balance between progenitors and differentiated blood cells. Autophagy is a vital cellular process that maintains homeostasis by removing unnecessary or dysfunctional cell components through autophagic degradation and recycling. Here, using genetic perturbation analysis, we show that autophagy plays a critical role in regulating LG blood cell homeostasis. General control non-derepressible 5 (Gcn5), a histone acetyltransferase, is expressed in the primary LG lobe, and modulation of Gcn5 levels perturbs LG homeostasis. Our results show that hemocyte-specific Gcn5 modulation controls autophagic flux in the hemocytes. Furthermore, we show that modulation of mTORC1 activity can perturb hematopoiesis. Our results indicate that organismal Gcn5 levels respond to dietary shifts and are modulated by mTORC1 signaling. Chemical intervention shows that mTORC1 overrides the effect exerted by Gcn5 in regulating LG hematopoiesis. Taken together, our findings demonstrate that Gcn5 and mTORC1 regulate autophagy to maintain blood cell homeostasis in Drosophila .

title: MeO-2PACz-mediated interfacial engineering for strain regulation in efficient narrow-bandgap Sn–Pb perovskite solar cells
container-title: Nanotechnology
2d1e611a12be6185e6d392eaf732d4a83650e3cc.abstract: Abstract Compositional engineered narrow-bandgap (NBG) Sn–Pb perovskites with an intrinsic bandgap of 1.2–1.3 eV have emerged as promising photovoltaic materials, holding tremendous application prospects in tandem solar cells, near-infrared photodetection and imaging, as well as building-integrated photovoltaics. However, their practical applications are severely hampered by severe Sn 2+ oxidation, mismatched crystallization and large interfacial compressive strain between perovskite and hole transport layer. Herein, we adopt co-additives to fundamentally suppress Sn 2+ oxidation, and further construct a MeO-2PACz self-assembled monolayer (SAM) buried interface to relieve bottom interfacial compressive strain of perovskite films. The SAM buffer layer mitigates lattice and thermal expansion mismatch-induced strain, reduces lattice distortion and interfacial defects, and optimizes interfacial energy level alignment simultaneously. Benefiting from the above interfacial engineering, the oxidation of Sn 2+ in NBG Sn–Pb perovskite absorbers is remarkably inhibited. As a result, the optimized Sn–Pb perovskite devices deliver a power conversion efficiency of 20.50%. In addition, the unencapsulated devices with synergistic modification of additive engineering and MeO-2PACz interfacial treatment exhibit exceptional long-term durability. Specifically, the devices maintain 95% of the original efficiency after 1000 h of ambient exposure, and retain 93% of their initial efficiency after 20 h thermal aging at 85 °C in a nitrogen atmosphere.

title: Self-attention-aided multi-layer CNN-LSTM for non-uniform 4-level differential amplitude modulation and detection with atmospheric turbulence for OWANs
container-title: Optics Express
1922c9e0cb34b13e5ea74df3c48f83317a5531ed.abstract: This paper proposes an environment-aware four-level non-uniform differential amplitude modulation and detection scheme assisted by self-attentive multi-layer CNN-LSTM (SA-CNN-LSTM) for optical wireless access networks (OWANs) under atmospheric turbulence, to mitigate severe distortions induced by atmospheric turbulence in optical wireless communication (OWC) systems. Relying on four-level non-uniform differential amplitude modulation (NUADM-4) and a self-attention-aided detection algorithm at the receiving terminal, the proposed scheme can effectively suppress both multiplicative turbulence fading and additive Gaussian noise simultaneously. Numerical results reveal that the proposed scheme achieves remarkable bit error rate (BER) improvements compared with conventional detection frameworks for NUADM-4, and it substantially outperforms the classical uniform four-level pulse amplitude modulation (PAM-4) across diverse turbulence strength regimes. Moreover, the tailored architecture integrating self-attention with multi-layer CNN-LSTM maintains high transmission efficiency, reduces the dimension of the fully-connected layer at the receiver to a certain extent, and accelerates the computation speed compared with the CNN-based algorithm. In comparison with conventional detection-aided algorithms such as vanilla CNN, LSTM, and MLP, the presented scheme delivers a universal BER performance gain. Furthermore, the machine-learning-aided design philosophy for different modulation systems offers a practical design paradigm and implementable solution for the engineering deployment of high-speed OWC systems serving OWANs operating in volatile atmospheric turbulence environments.

title: Bridging or Widening the Gap? AI Policies and Social Justice in Education
