Every output follows the corporate documentation standard, which removes the variation between engineers, and every value can be traced back to the source file it came from. The framework recovers an estimated four or more engineering hours per well event, needs no new infrastructure or software licences, and works with any logging service provider active on the field. It offers a practical and immediately replicable route to AI adoption for operations-intensive subsurface teams.

title: Clean Firm Power for the AI Age: Geothermal Pathways to Data Center Decarbonization Across the Energy Trilemma
container-title: ADIPEC
cc6d8e58073e31067a91b019c40b86fd18b9b127.abstract: Abstract The evolving development and deployment of Artificial Intelligence (‘AI’) is driving unprecedented 24/7 data center energy demand. A single generative AI query consumes roughly ten times the electricity of a conventional internet search, and one planned US data center has requested 1.4 GW of continuous power. This will exceed the total demand of some small states. These loads reframe the energy trilemma, highlighting the need to simultaneously deliver reliability, low carbon impact, and cost-effective energy, and expose the limitations of intermittent renewables for mission-critical digital infrastructure. Geothermal energy, with capacity factors exceeding 70–90% and very low lifecycle emissions, offers a reliable "clean firm" power and thermal management solutions. This study examines how the United States, UAE, and Saudi Arabia deploy geothermal solutions to decarbonize data centers while advancing all three trilemma pillars. The methodology adopts a three-case comparative analysis. In the United States, we assess Utah's Operation Gigawatt, aiming to double capacity from ∼4 GW, and Ormat Technologies’ long-term Power Purchase Agreements (‘PPAs’), including contracts supplying up to 150 MW of geothermal electricity to hyperscale operators. In the UAE, we evaluated ADNOC's G2COOL geothermal district cooling pilot at Masdar City, using ∼90°C water from ∼2.6 km depth to provide ∼10% of cooling demand with ∼50% lower electricity consumption. In Saudi Arabia, we analyzed KAPSARC resource mapping (Alsuwailem et. al, 2024) and KAUST's 2024 pilot at Thuwal targeting geothermal cooling applications. Each case is systematically assessed against trilemma metrics of reliability, carbon impact, and cost-effectiveness. This study evaluates geothermal applications for power generation and thermal management across three stages of market maturity. The United States case demonstrates reliability through baseload geothermal electricity for hyperscale computing; the UAE delivers carbon impact reduction through operational district cooling in extreme climates; and Saudi Arabia explores cost-effectiveness through early-stage geothermal-exchange systems optimizing cooling-intensive demand. The assessment identifies distinct contributions to reliability, carbon impact, and cost-effectiveness. For reliability, geothermal provides continuous baseload power and long-term PPAs that reduce supply volatility. For carbon impact, geothermal systems emit approximately 90% lower lifecycle CO2 than combined-cycle gas (≈40 against ≈500 gCO2e/kWh) and up to ∼99% lower operational CO2 against the same baseline while materially reducing cooling-related emissions in high-demand regions (IPCC 2011). For cost-effectiveness, for the right application, geothermal cooling and geo-exchange solutions can reduce electricity consumption by up to ∼50%, particularly in markets where cooling accounts for 65–70% of power demand. Across all three jurisdictions, geothermal solutions reconcile accelerating AI-driven electricity demand with system resilience, decarbonization objectives, and cost optimization. By positioning geothermal within the energy trilemma framework, this study demonstrates its strategic role in supporting sustainable large scale digital infrastructure.

title: Interdisciplinary Agentic AI Deployment: A Success Story from the Malay Basin, Malaysia
container-title: ADIPEC
b47c293a97591dffd00ec3af985e81ae3731d271.abstract: Subsurface professionals working in the oil and gas exploration and production industry are routinely exposed to a wide and diverse array of specialized software packages, digital tools, and sophisticated applications. These have been developed by various international technology companies, service organizations, and independent software vendors from around the world to help geoscientists, engineers, and technical analysts conduct their complex geological studies, detailed reservoir interpretations, and comprehensive data analysis tasks with greater efficiency and accuracy. The selection of one particular software solution over another competing alternative in the marketplace is primarily driven by several key factors. These include the software's comprehensive technical capabilities, its specific functional features, and perhaps most importantly, the individual user's personal proficiency, accumulated hands-on experience, and overall comfort level with the tool developed over months or years of regular use. When the technical capabilities and available features appear to be roughly equivalent or comparable between different software options, professionals naturally and instinctively gravitate toward the software platform with which they are most familiar and have the greatest operational experience using in their daily work activities. This well-established and understandable preference for familiar and well-understood tools, however, inevitably introduces significant operational friction across different workflows. This is particularly problematic when technical teams need to transition between various disconnected tools from different software vendors, which frequently results in operational delays, increased inefficiencies, potential data loss or corruption, and considerable frustration among team members who must constantly adapt to new interfaces and workflows.

title: Supramolecular Self-Assembled Sulfonated Polymers for Chemical EOR: Bulk Viscosity and Viscoelastic Properties Evaluation
container-title: ADIPEC
1054c6d3fd65dc0b6c8cedea40a3ac24e1a8decf.abstract: Abstract Effective chemical enhanced oil recovery (EOR) in mature reservoirs requires chemical additives that are able to retain their functionality under reservoir conditions. However, conventional chemical additives are often affected by retention, mechanical degradation, and injectivity limitations. These issues considerably restrict their field application. In view of this, the present study evaluates a supramolecular self-assembled polymer (SAP) system. This system is designed to overcome the aforementioned limitations through dynamic, reversible, noncovalent interactions. Such interactions result in the formation of a self-healing polymolecular network. SAP formulations were prepared using an ATBS-containing polymer, alpha-olefin sulfonate (AOS), and β-cyclodextrin (β-CD), and their performance was compared under high-salinity conditions. The bulk rheological behavior was characterized by using steady- and oscillatory-shear measurements conducted with a modular compact rheometer. Viscosity was measured at both constant and varying shear rates, and the effect of temperature on the rheological response was also investigated. Furthermore, oscillatory measurements were carried out to determine the storage and loss moduli, which were used to assess the viscoelastic structure of the system. It was observed that the prepared SAP formulation exhibited a notable improvement in rheological performance compared with the baseline polymer-surfactant systems. Its higher viscosity was attributed to the combined interactions among the polymer, surfactant, and β-CD, which generated a more robust associative structure. Compared with the polymer-surfactant system, both the storage and loss moduli increased upon introducing β-CD to encapsulate the surfactant, indicating that host-guest inclusion between the hydrophobic portion of AOS and the β-CD cavity, together with hydrogen bonding, produces a more stable polymolecular network. The novelty of this work lies in the bulk rheological evaluation of an ATBS-based polymer/AOS/β-CD formulation under offshore reservoir conditions. The ongoing work will extend the evaluation to the system's interfacial properties and coreflooding experiments, and quantify the improvement in oil recovery arising from the synergistic interaction among the polymer, surfactant, and β-CD host-guest network.

title: Real-Time AI-Based Prediction of Stuck Pipe Events to Minimize Non-Productive Time in Drilling Operations
container-title: ADIPEC
6beab8a0dac09b280b7359b0333fbcf9e5ee0548.abstract: Abstract Stuck pipe remains a major drilling challenge, causing significant non-productive time (NPT), increased costs, and operational risks. This paper presents an artificial intelligence (AI)-based framework for early prediction of stuck pipe events using real-time drilling data to enable proactive risk mitigation. The solution utilizes a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network trained on refined WITSML data from multiple wells. Key drilling parameters, including hookload, torque, standpipe pressure, flow rate, rotary speed, and rate of penetration, were combined with engineered features to identify precursor patterns associated with stuck pipe incidents. Real-time inference workflows were developed to support field deployment. The model achieved 96.1% accuracy, 0.991 ROC-AUC, 83.3% precision, 87.5% recall, and an F1-score of 85.4%. It successfully predicted 7 of 8 confirmed stuck pipe events while maintaining a false alarm rate of only 2.1%. An average Early Warning Time of 2.9 minutes allowed drilling crews to implement preventive actions before conditions became irreversible. Deployment analysis indicated the potential to reduce stuck pipe-related NPT from 142.5 hours to 31hours, representing a 78.2% reduction. The results demonstrate that AI-driven prediction can improve drilling efficiency, reduce operational costs, and support digital transformation through reliable, actionable early-warning alerts.

title: Propose-Validate-Correct Shadow-Plant Architecture for Safe AI Agents in Process Operations
container-title: ADIPEC
0c41a406387415d7bed6a516d78d35033d6a7bf3.abstract: Abstract Large-language-model (LLM) agents are increasingly explored for autonomous process-plant operations, yet they can propose physically unsafe control actions due to hallucination and imprecise numerical reasoning. We introduce the Propose-Validate-Correct (PVC) architecture, a framework-agnostic safety layer in which every agent-proposed action is first simulated in a shadow plant, a lightweight physics-grounded process simulator, before reaching the real process. When the shadow simulation detects constraint violations, the proposal is rejected and the agent receives structured feedback for correction. PVC is an advisory safety layer and does not replace certified safety instrumented systems (SIS). Experiments are conducted on OpsEnv, an open-source continuous stirred-tank reactor (CSTR) benchmark featuring mass and energy balance ordinary differential equations (ODEs), Arrhenius reaction kinetics, and proportional-integral cooling control. Four agent configurations (ReAct and Plan-and-Execute, each with and without PVC) are evaluated on four LLMs: Google Gemini 2.5 Flash (cloud), Alibaba Qwen 2.5 32B, Meta Llama 3.1 8B, and Mistral 7B (all three local via Ollama). The evaluation spans 440 experiment cells organized in four tiers covering eleven scenarios, with three feedback granularity levels (binary, descriptive, suggested fix) for shadow-equipped agents. Both shadow-equipped setups record zero actual violations in all 282 PVC cells, while react_direct accumulates 10.4 mean violations per episode (Tiers 1–3) and plan_exec_direct incurs 0.2. Across all tiers, PVC intercepts 1,552 proposals that would have violated safety constraints, predominantly in upset scenarios where every agent proposal at every timestep triggers a constraint violation. In optimization scenarios (A-series), the correction loop salvages 40.3% of rejected proposals (Self-Correction Success Rate, SCSR), with descriptive per-variable feedback improving SCSR 3.0× over binary reject/accept for matched Gemini Flash cells (50.9% vs. 16.7%). In upset scenarios (B-series), SCSR is 0% under the current stability threshold; PVC acts as a conservative safety gate during disturbed states. Completion scores show a negligible trade-off (Cohen's d = −0.053, 95% CI [−0.283, 0.174]): no statistically significant performance cost is observed, though formal equivalence remains undemonstrated at the current sample size. Plan-and-Execute with PVC runs 31× faster than ReAct with PVC (60 s vs. 1,835 s for Gemini Flash). Shadow-plant validation is a viable safety mechanism for deploying LLM agents in safety-critical process environments; structured physics-based feedback markedly improves self-correction in optimization scenarios. AI-assisted tools were used in the experimental evaluation; all outputs were reviewed and validated by the authors.

title: Real Time Optimization of Gas Separation Cynara Membrane Through AI & ML for Adaptive CO2 Removal and Maximum CH4 Recovery Under Variable Feed Conditions
container-title: ADIPEC
c6cfd536b349f3833ba9d2761dcd4e1414008326.abstract: Abstract Gas processing facility that processes sour feeds, CO2 removal is required to meet pipeline specifications for the natural gas transmission pipeline. The separation is particularly challenging when high CO2 streams must be to processed. The present study does not consider alternative separation technologies, but rather systematically optimizes an existing membrane type process to optimize the removal of CO2 so as to avoid the production of off specification gas, which is costly to be generated. It is based on the commercially available hollow fiber membrane commercial cellulosic triacetate (CTA) modules, nominal capacity of 12T 0.72 MMCFD/membrane module as per Simulation. Deployments and optimizations to these modules will be explained in real time thus pressure of about 600 psi is applied to the membrane feed for optimum separation, furthermore it is mandatory to maintain a minimum CO2 concentration of the Nonpermeate within regulatory requirements (3 mol % set by Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority, OGRA Pakistan) for feeds containing approximately 22 mol % CO2. In line pressure, flow rate and temperature data are measured, while composition data are measured simultaneously from an online gas chromatograph sampling the feed, Nonpermeate and permeate streams. This data is fed to a supervisory machine learning layer which predict the behavior of the Nonpermeate CO2 concentration and provide appropriate set point values for required feed pressure, flow rate and temperature. If an excess of CO2 is detected, the controller provides predictive value for the CO2 rich stream thus decreasing the CO2 concentration in the stream prior to exceeding the Nonpermeate specification by controlling the flowrate. On the other hand, a decrease CO2 in the feed provide an operational slack that will allow a safe increase in throughput. This has resulted in a closed-loop, human in the loop configuration with significant improvements in process stability, hydrocarbon recovery, and significant reduction in off specification events using Artificial Intelligence. The study thereby presents a feasibility of real time sweetening of natural gas by machine learning & Artificial Intelligence in an industrially viable way.

title: A Case Study of Seismic Geomorphology Analysis of Post-MMU Carbonate-Clastic Systems in Central Luconia Using Seismic Attributes and AI-Assisted Relative Geological Time (RGT)
container-title: ADIPEC
0b0205ecc5b667dca5f7cb6450e3e04af649301d.abstract: Abstract Seismic geomorphology has become a powerful geophysical approach for resolving complex depositional architectures and reservoir heterogeneity in mixed carbonate-clastic systems. In Central Luconia, post-Middle Miocene Unconformity (post-MMU) stratigraphy is characterized by the interplay of carbonate development and clastic sedimentation; however, significant uncertainties remain regarding their depositional architecture and the resulting impacts on reservoir presence and quality, as well as seal integrity. This study applies advanced seismic attribute analysis, integrated with the Relative Geological Time (RGT) approach, to enhance the imaging and interpretation of post MMU depositional systems and their impact on reservoir architecture and seal integrity. High quality 3D seismic data were interpreted using a suite of geometric and amplitude-based attributes, including variance, RMS amplitude, sweetness, and spectral decomposition. Attribute driven horizon and time slice analyses above the MMU surface were employed to extract geomorphological features and delineate seismic facies associated with post-MMU carbonate and clastic deposition. The integration of RGT improves stratigraphic continuity and chronostratigraphic interpretation, enabling clearer visualization of subtle depositional elements that are poorly resolved on conventional seismic sections. Seismic geomorphological mapping reveals spatially heterogeneous post-MMU depositional patterns, including localized carbonate build ups, irregular platform margins, slope deposits, and basinward clastic drapes and infill. Distinct seismic attribute responses allow discrimination between carbonate dominated and clastic dominated facies, reflecting contrasts in internal architecture, depositional energy, and acoustic properties. Post-MMU carbonate development is strongly influenced by antecedent relief inherited from pre-MMU structures, whereas clastic systems preferentially occupy inter build up lows and basinward settings, locally onlapping carbonate flanks. From a geophysical reservoir characterization and containment perspective, the juxtaposition of post- MMU carbonates and clastics introduces pronounced seismic scale heterogeneity with implications for reservoir connectivity, compartmentalization, and seal integrity. In particular, the juxtaposition of uppermost carbonate units with overlying fluvial deposits is interpreted to locally form high permeability pathways that may act as potential thief zones, increasing the risk of vertical fluid migration and seal bypass. This study demonstrates the effectiveness of seismic geomorphology, supported by attribute-based imaging and RGT assisted interpretation, in resolving mixed depositional systems and provides a robust geophysical framework for reducing subsurface uncertainty in mature carbonate provinces such as Central Luconia Traditionally, detailed characterization of carbonate-clastic interactions such as differentiating talus deposits and identifying potential thief sands relies heavily on manual interpretation, which can be time-intensive and subject to uncertainty, ultimately impacting exploration risking. The proposed methodology offers a more systematic and data-driven approach, enabling improved discrimination of depositional elements land delivering enhanced insights into subsurface architecture and associated risks.

title: First Autonomous Curve Construction in Middle East Carbonate Fields with AI-Powered Downhole Steering Control
container-title: ADIPEC
ab1c7c8df2a1c9dbc493b585057c2f69019dce95.abstract: Abstract This paper presents a deployment of a solution that replaces surface driven control during curve construction with a downhole closed loop steering ratio controller embedded within the rotary steerable systems. This controller represents an AI-enabled, objective driven autonomous control system, continuously evaluating tool response and trajectory deviation relative to plan and autonomously adjusting curvature commands in real time. The system was deployed without modification to rig site workflows and evaluated through multiple field trials, including complex 3D curve profiles in high-performance drilling environments. Field results demonstrated that autonomous downhole curve control enables reliable construction of complex three-dimensional curve sections with minimal surface intervention. The closed loop controller reacted faster to formation and drilling condition changes than manual steering workflows, demonstrating adaptive, real-time decision making at the downhole execution level, resulting in improved well trajectory adherence and optimal execution. Across multiple wells, automated downhole steering control delivered measurable performance improvements. The reduction in downlinking frequency also contributed to improved wellbore quality through a corresponding decrease in excess tortuosity. The deployment confirms that downhole automation can extend autonomous drilling capability beyond vertical and tangent sections into curve construction, traditionally considered the most challenging phase of trajectory execution. The results demonstrate that closed loop downhole control improves drilling efficiency, consistency, and robustness, particularly in high performance and unconventional drilling environments.

title: AI-Assisted Borehole Image Analysis to Diagnose Reservoir Heterogeneity and Flow Behavior: A Tight Carbonate Case Study
container-title: ADIPEC
78ac76b3917716c8a834c898498288d310ef6aa6.abstract: Abstract Understanding reservoir heterogeneity and identifying zonal flow distribution are critical for reservoir management, well targeting, and depletion control. However, Production or Injection Logging Tool (PLT/ILT) data are often incomplete or unavailable due to well accessibility issues. This study addresses the challenge in characterizing reservoir heterogeneity and identifying zonal flow distribution in a relatively green field tight carbonate development by integrating all available data. High-resolution borehole image logs acquired along the horizontal wellbores were analyzed using an AI/ML-based segmentation workflow that differentiates matrix from secondary (vuggy and fracture-related) features at image scale. Matrix and secondary porosity and permeability were estimated independently and combined to generate continuous image-derived total porosity and permeability logs. These properties were used to compute a Flow Zone Indicator (FZI) along the wellbore, which was integrated to generate a synthetic flow profile. The result was calibrated and validated against core data (CT scan and thin section) and wells with full PLT/ILT coverage before being applied to wells with partial or no PLT/ILT data. In validation wells, the image-derived FZI flow profiles showed good agreement with measured PLT inflow distributions and core-based flow unit definitions, confirming that AI-segmented borehole images capture flow-relevant heterogeneity in this tight carbonate system. When applied to horizontal wells with restricted PLT accessibility, the workflow produced physically consistent zonal contribution estimates that aligned with geological zonation and offset well performance. The approach also reveals lateral reservoir heterogeneity that conventional logs may be overlooked. Applied to long horizontal wells in a green field tight carbonate development, it provides a practical and transparent alternative for estimating zonal contribution where PLT coverage is incomplete or unavailable, as well as providing additional data required for static and dynamic simulations.

title: AI-Enabled Well Inactivity Prediction for Proactive Production Target Protection in Upstream Operations
container-title: ADIPEC
f24c0fdd822b3cdc5ba7128622e59310095284fb.abstract: Abstract Unplanned well string inactivity is one of the biggest sources of production deferral, unstable short term forecasts, and missed annual targets in upstream operations. Most surveillance today is reactive. An asset team usually confirms that a string has gone inactive from the monthly report, once the barrels have already been lost, and then works out the cause well by well. This paper describes an AI based predictive framework that runs the other way round. It looks ahead and estimates which active strings are likely to become inactive, what is most probably driving them, and roughly when, so that reservoir, well and operations teams can step in before the deferment happens. The framework brings together three analytical layers that support one another. Time series forecasting provides the portfolio inactivity outlook. Supervised machine learning gives each string a level of risk and names its most likely cause. Survival analysis estimates the remaining active time before an expected event. Threshold exceedance and degradation trend features feed all three and act as early warning signals. The prediction is scoped deliberately to well and reservoir related problems rather than facility driven downtime, because that is where advance warning changes the outcome. We developed and tested the framework on a mature onshore assets with thousands of wells, covering oil producers, water injectors and gas injectors. On blind, out of time data it gives useful advance visibility of inactivity risk months before the loss shows up in the numbers, and it lets teams intervene earlier and concentrate effort on the wells that matter most.

title: AI-Enabled Integrated Talent Platforms: Accelerating Readiness for Critical Roles in Energy Operations
container-title: ADIPEC
616e76f02a6087071688234d837ceb0458f0edc6.abstract: Summary The energy industry continues to face increasing workforce complexity driven by digital transformation, changing demographics, evolving competency requirements, and the need to maintain operational continuity across critical business functions. While organizations have invested heavily in digital technologies for operational excellence, succession planning and workforce readiness management remain areas where decision making is frequently influenced by fragmented information, limited visibility of workforce capabilities, and subjective assessments. These challenges become increasingly significant in large organizations where talent mobility, cross functional experience, and diverse competency profiles make successor identification more complex. A major downstream energy company identified several challenges in its talent management and succession processes. Historically, succession planning activities relied heavily on management discussions, performance records, current job assignments, and managerial recommendations. This approach often created limitations in identifying hidden talent, recognizing cross functional experiences, and objectively evaluating workforce readiness for critical positions. The organization required a more comprehensive system capable of capturing broader dimensions of employee capability while providing greater transparency, consistency, and governance throughout the succession planning process. To address these challenges, the organization implemented an integrated talent ecosystem consisting of a Career Management Platform (CMP) and Capability Development Platform (CDP). CMP centralized succession planning activities using a meritocracy based point system incorporating capability, experience, aspiration, and achievement dimensions, while CDP connected competency assessments, capability gap identification, and structured development interventions. Together, the platforms established a closed loop talent management process that improved visibility into workforce capability and readiness. Although the implementation significantly improved governance, transparency, and workforce visibility, several limitations remained. Successor rankings continued to rely on predefined weighting mechanisms and rule based logic, making it difficult to evaluate the relative importance of different experiences, identify hidden talent across functions, and anticipate future succession risks. To address these limitations, the organization identified an AI-enabled Workforce Intelligence Layer as the next stage of maturity aligned with its Human Capital 5.0 transformation roadmap. The proposed AI capabilities include successor readiness prediction, intelligent talent discovery, dynamic successor evaluation, development path recommendations, and succession risk forecasting. This paper presents the implementation of CMP and CDP as the current state of workforce readiness management while proposing an AI-enabled evolution toward predictive workforce intelligence.

title: Enhancing Fault Interpretation in Complex Structures Using Customized Data Driven Machine Learning Networks: An Offshore Case Study, Offshore Abu Dhabi, UAE
container-title: ADIPEC
02450cb512e9303d9ed3a8e5a83b70e6a7d10a76.abstract: Abstract Fault interpretation in salt-influenced offshore settings is challenging due to complex deformation styles, fault segmentation, imaging limitations, and variable seismic quality. While foundation machine-learning (ML) fault-detection networks enable rapid identification of major fault systems, their generalized training can limit structural consistency and geological reliability when applied to complex regional settings. This study demonstrates the value of customized, data-driven ML training networks for enhancing fault interpretation through an offshore salt-related anticline case study from Abu Dhabi. Several foundation ML fault networks were initially applied to a high-quality 3D seismic dataset to establish a baseline structural framework. Although these networks successfully delineated primary fault trends, limitations were observed in fault continuity, detection of subordinate fault populations, and consistency across stratigraphic levels—particularly in deeper intervals characterized by low seismic reflectivity and salt-related deformation. To address these challenges, bespoke ML fault networks were trained using interpreter-generated fault sticks extracted from selected inline and crossline seismic sections. The training interpretation was guided by seismic attributes, including multi-attribute color blends derived from tensor attributes, structure-oriented semblance, dip information, and frequency decomposition. Iterative training and quality-control cycles were applied to progressively refine fault detectability, orientation fidelity, and structural coherence. Application of the customized networks to the full seismic volume demonstrates a clear improvement over foundation models. Results show enhanced fault continuity, improved delineation of minor faults, and more geologically consistent fault geometries in both time slices and vertical sections. Importantly, the refined fault framework exhibits improved agreement with well data, bringing the interpreted structure a step closer to geological reality and increasing confidence in fault positioning and connectivity. This case study highlights how customized ML training, grounded in local seismic expression and geological understanding, delivers tangible value beyond generic AI solutions, supporting improved subsurface characterization, development planning, and risk reduction in salt-influenced offshore environments.

title: An Integrated Physics-Machine Learning Framework for Time-Dependent Injectivity Decline and Fracture Growth in Horizontal Water-Injection Wells
container-title: ADIPEC
bb17b977c5acbe15a346ebfc3696bacd85df33a5.abstract: Summary A hybrid physics-machine learning framework is presented to predict time-dependent injectivity decline and fracture half-length evolution in horizontal water injection wells subjected to particulate-laden injection. The framework couples mechanistic formation damage and filtration models with machine learning surrogates trained on over 30000 CMG-IMEX reservoir simulations, enabling rapid, physically consistent evaluation of fracture-initiation risk and injection performance across a wide range of reservoir and operating conditions. The framework integrates physics-based filtration models for near-wellbore and near-fracture damage covering internal pore plugging and external filter-cake buildup with machine learning (ML) surrogates (CatBoost, LightGBM, and XGBoost) trained on 30000 high-fidelity CMG-IMEX simulations. Surrogates predict bottom-hole pressure, fracture-tip pressure, and flow partitioning for static well-fracture states. A sequential operator-split time-marching scheme couples damage evolution with quasi-static fracture growth governed by a minimum horizontal stress admissibility criterion. Simulation scenarios are organised into throughput-based injection systems to ensure physically interpretable sensitivity analysis across constrained, moderate, and high-injectivity reservoir-well configurations. Three representative throughput systems (B1-B3) spanning constrained to high injectivity were analysed under base particulate concentration (20 ppmv). Base injection rates were designed to suppress fracture initiation under clean-water conditions, ensuring all observed fracture growth was attributable solely to particulate-induced pressure buildup. Fracture initiation and progressive half-length growth were observed in all systems, with final fracture half-lengths of 14, 40 and 86 ft for B1, B2 and B3 at 1000 days, respectively. Bottom-hole pressure and fracture-tip pressure rose sharply at early time due to near-wellbore and fracture-face damage before stabilising slightly above the minimum horizontal stress. Well skin increased monotonically, with final values of 51, 76, and 148 across the three systems. Sensitivity analysis identified minimum horizontal stress gradient, reservoir thickness, horizontal permeability, water viscosity, injected solids concentration, and injection duration as the dominant controlling parameters across all throughput systems. The framework reproduces coupled injectivity-fracture behaviour at computational costs orders of magnitude lower than fully implicit numerical simulators, enabling practical uncertainty analysis and fracture-risk assessment. The throughput-system design methodology provides a rigorous and operationally meaningful basis for injection-well optimisation and water-quality specification. This framework is among the first to couple physics-based filtration damage models for horizontal wells and fractures with ML surrogates trained on 30000 CMG-IMEX simulations for rapid, time-resolved prediction of injectivity decline and fracture growth. The throughput-system scenario design methodology enables physically interpretable uncertainty analysis, offering practising engineers a computationally efficient tool for injection-well optimisation, water-quality specification, fracture-risk assessment, and evaluation of remedial treatment timing.

title: Detection of Work-Related Musculoskeletal Disorder Risk Factors Using AI-Enabled 3D Motion Capture: Implementation Experience in a UAE Oil and Gas Company
container-title: ADIPEC
f0555612019991345b10c490715aed0516346d72.abstract: Abstract Objectives/Scope Oil and gas operations involve repetitive manual handling, forceful exertions, awkward postures, and prolonged static positions that contribute to work-related musculoskeletal disorders (WMSDs). Traditional observational tools such as RULA and REBA remain prone to observer subjectivity and imprecise scoring of individual body segments. This descriptive, cross-sectional implementation study evaluated the practical application of an AI-enabled three-dimensional motion capture (3D MOCAP) assessment tool in a UAE oil and gas company to identify and prioritize ergonomic risks by work activity, worker group, and affected body region, and to define appropriate control measures. Methods, Procedures, Process Site HSE and Occupational Health SMEs were trained over an online course and a two-day workshop, then recorded task videos (minimum 1080p, 30 fps) using CICPA-approved intrinsically safe devices. Hand force was captured by force gauge, dynamometer, or Borg perceived exertion. Videos were uploaded to an industrial ergonomics platform where AI compared detected joint angles against thresholds benchmarked to REBA, OCRA, the Strain Index, and the ACGIH Hand Activity TLV. The software returned a skeleton-overlay video, a Risk Priority Score (RPS, 0–100) aggregating posture, force, frequency, and duration, and body area scores for six body segments. Results for 625 assessments across seven business units were logged in an Industrial Ergonomics Assessment Register between March 2023 and August 2024. Results, Observations, Conclusions Historical data (2020–2022) showed low back pain accounted for 84–85% of WMSD cases. Across the 625 assessments the median RPS was 22 and the mean 26, indicating a Moderate overall risk profile, with Operators and Maintenance groups representing 95% of assessments. Repetitive manual handling was the leading risk factor (41.9%), followed by excessive force (16.6%) and frequent hand tool use (8.72%). Aircraft refuelers, civil projects/kerbstone installers, and chemical offloaders recorded the highest RPS and body area scores, particularly at the right elbow, right shoulder, neck, and back. Of 836 recommendations, 58.4% were administrative — work instruction and coaching alone accounted for 43.7% — and 62% have been approved, completed, or are in progress. Novel/Additive Information The study demonstrates a scalable, bias-reduced, field-deployable AI ergonomics method and identifies the training, device, and governance conditions required for successful rollout.

title: Machine Learning Assisted Rock Physics Workflow for Greenfield Hydrocarbon Prospect Evaluation
container-title: ADIPEC
07060458abec97e35f379851298511ec5d4b7106.abstract: Abstract Accurate reservoir characterization in greenfield hydrocarbon exploration remains challenging because sparse well control, seismic inversion non-uniqueness, and geological heterogeneity introduce significant uncertainty in predicting reservoir properties beyond existing wells. Conventional machine learning workflows commonly employ single-stage models that neglect the hierarchical dependency among petrophysical properties and rarely integrate rock physics calibration and geological constraints into the prediction process. This study presents an integrated machine learning-assisted rock physics workflow that combines petrophysical interpretation, rock physics modelling, seismic calibration, geological constraints, and supervised machine learning within a unified framework for field-scale reservoir characterization. Five exploration wells were used to construct a calibrated rock physics database incorporating acoustic impedance, reflection coefficients, synthetic seismograms, seismic inversion, and interpreted petrophysical properties. A physics-guided Sequential Random Forest workflow was developed to emulate the conventional petrophysical interpretation sequence by sequentially predicting porosity, lithology-related properties, shale volume, sand volume, water saturation, and bulk volume water. The workflow was benchmarked against Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) using blind-well validation. Cumulative hydrocarbon pore volume analysis established an optimum shale-volume cut-off of 0.65–0.70 v/v, while calibrated AI–Vp/Vs rock physics templates demonstrated that reservoir and non-reservoir intervals should be interpreted probabilistically because of the combined influence of multiple geological factors on elastic properties. Blind-well validation showed that both machine learning approaches produced reliable reservoir-property predictions; however, the Sequential Random Forest workflow achieved comparable predictive performance with lower model-development complexity, reduced hyperparameter optimization, and greater physical interpretability. The proposed workflow extends well-based reservoir characterization into the interwell seismic domain by integrating rock physics, geological constraints, and sequential machine learning within a physically consistent predictive framework. This methodology provides a scalable approach for reducing exploration uncertainty and supporting more reliable hydrocarbon prospect evaluation and well-placement decisions.

title: World Scale Application of Glass Disc Intervention Less Plugs Technology: Data Driven Operational Improvements from UAE Onshore Completions
container-title: ADIPEC
9abdb4fa9e886f503e077119d6ee03a86a6344a5.abstract: Abstract The drilling and completion industry's increasing demand for higher standards requirement to have completion installation safer, low risk, efficient, cost effective and provide longer well life cycle for further intervention activity. Slickline plug deployment has long been the industry standard intervention in completion and offers reliable method downhole plug placement. The intervention activities basically require operational time incorporated with surface unit preparation, intervention activity, cost, and well exposure. The potential for operational issues during intervention activities can result in additional remedial operations, driving the adoption of interventionless plug technologies to reduce risk, complexity, and well delivery time. The interventionless plug application enhances completion efficiency while reducing operational risk and maintaining compliance with standard well integrity verification practices, including inflow test safety valve and completion testing. Multiple interventionless plug technologies have been initiated, field trial and implemented with advantages and disadvantages for each technology to fit with the application and requirements. The glass disc as one of intervention less plug introduced, trial and applied into operation from few years ago and the improvement continuously conducted to meet with the requirements and increase success ratio. The increasing demand for higher standards has positioned and transformed glass discs as one of the effective solutions for interventionless plug and barrier application. This paper presents insights from one of the largest glass discs plug deployment campaigns in UAE onshore completion operations. Based on extensive historical data, field trials, and performance validation, the study identifies key success factors, operational risks, and improvement opportunities to enhance deployment reliability, operational efficiency, and process standardization. The glass disc is indeed beneficial for completion installation operation as intervention less plug, it provides assurance for process of packer setting and completion integrity testing. The development of glass disc technology has scaled up to massive levels and intrinsically single use due to material properties as its function compared with other completion accessories. Given its role and single-use nature, glass disc reliability and performance are critical to successful application. The success of installation has been discussed in several papers as functional of plug prior to packer setting and completion integrity test such as improvement of the design, best practice and lesson learn. The well completion is designed with consideration to maintain life of the well, efficient production and minimizing intervention during full lifecycle. The glass disc acts as a temporary isolation barrier during completion operations and should not contribute to production phase. The well shall be completed with full accessibility, which is essential for further activities in production phase. The assessment must verify that glass disc deployment does not adversely affect production performance. The assessment must verify that glass disc deployment does not adversely affect production performance. The production team as key stakeholder contributes operational expertise and historical field data to the evaluation process. Statistical analyses, field case studies, and stakeholder feedback support continuous improvement, capture lessons learned and establish best practices. The glass disc plugs have been widely deployed in UAE onshore completion operations, with approximately more than 200 data samples annually, becoming a standard component in completion strings. The feedback from production teams indicates a minor impact with less than 3% of data samples experiencing accessibility issues, it remains important and critical to understand these cases in detail. The Failure Modes and Effects Analysis (FMEA) was conducted to identify and prioritize potential failure modes associated with glass disc deployment, including non-rupture, premature rupture, and post-completion accessibility restrictions. System Integration Testing (SIT) validated failure mechanisms and mitigation measures under simulated field conditions prior to field implementation. Continuous field evaluation drive technology refinement and maximizes the value of the interventionless plug through best completion practices and operations.

title: Synergetic Dispatch Optimization of Natural Gas Transmission Networks and Underground Storage Clusters Using Optimal Transport Theory and Deep Learning
container-title: ADIPEC
e5515f51612f658a9d32db6a88c34a09f29f6f0e.abstract: Abstract Objectives/Scope The increasing complexity of regional natural gas infrastructures requires dispatch strategies that can simultaneously maintain supply security, reduce operating cost, and preserve system flexibility. In integrated source-network-load-storage systems, coordinated operation between transmission pipelines and underground gas storage (UGS) clusters remains difficult because linepack dynamics, compressor energy consumption, and storage injection/withdrawal scheduling are strongly coupled. This paper develops a multi-objective synergetic dispatch framework for coordinated day-ahead operation of natural gas transmission networks and UGS clusters, aiming to optimize the tradeoff between operating economy and system stability under practical hydraulic and equipment constraints. Methods, Procedures, Process A coupled source-network-load-storage optimization framework was established for the Chongqing regional gas transmission system. Optimal transport (OT) theory was introduced to describe gas redistribution among source nodes, demand nodes, storage facilities, and linepack adjustment segments, improving the physical interpretability of resource reallocation. Two objective functions were formulated: minimization of total operating expenditure and minimization of linepack deviation from target operating bands. The model included explicit constraints on pipeline throughput, nodal pressure, linepack limits, compressor operating envelopes, gas-source delivery capacity, and UGS injection/withdrawal rates. To improve computational efficiency and equipment-level fidelity, a deep-learning proxy model based on a multi-layer perceptron was trained to characterize nonlinear compressor power response using SCADA data, while semi-empirical power models were adopted for data-sparse facilities. The multi-objective problem was solved using NSGA-II, and TOPSIS was applied to select executable operating schemes from the Pareto set. Results, Observations, Conclusions The proposed framework demonstrated clear economic and operational benefits. For compressor energy modeling, the deep-learning proxy reduced prediction error to below 4.8%, compared with 12.4% for the conventional mechanical model. In the coordinated dispatch case, the synergetic strategy reduced total compressor power consumption by 4.65% and yielded an estimated 6.11% saving in annual energy costs, equivalent to approximately CNY 3.2 million. Relative to empirical dispatching, the framework reduced the mean absolute deviation of pipeline linepack by 61.3% and improved the safety margin of critical pipeline segments to 18.4%. At the storage-facility scale, the Pareto front reduced formation-pressure deviation from 26.3 MPa2 to a theoretical minimum of 1.4 MPa2, while the selected compromise used for subsequent analysis achieved 7.5 MPa2 at an injection pressure of 20 MPa. The average computational time for a 24-hour dispatch cycle was approximately 345 s, supporting day-ahead operational application. Novel/Additive Information Unlike workflows that schedule the transmission network and storage facilities separately, the proposed procedure carries one source-receiver allocation through hydraulic screening, compressor-power prediction, Pareto search, and final ranking. Linepack, storage duty, and compressor energy are therefore resolved as parts of the same day-ahead operating decision.

title: Uncertainty-Aware Graph Temporal Surrogate with Preference-Conditioned Reinforcement Learning for Multi-Objective CO2 Flooding and Storage Optimization
container-title: ADIPEC
e0ebf140a4c5b0e3688e09db109b72c8d438e2be.abstract: Abstract Multi-objective optimization of CO2 flooding requires repeated evaluation of long-term oil production and CO2 storage responses, whereas compositional reservoir simulation is computationally expensive for large-scale schedule search. This study develops an uncertainty-aware graph temporal surrogate-assisted optimization workflow for CO2 flooding and geological storage. The reservoir well pattern is represented as a multi-layer graph, where interwell connectivity describes spatial coupling among injectors and producers, and injection-production controls are encoded as time-dependent inputs. The surrogate couples topology-adaptive graph convolution with recurrent temporal modeling to predict gas, oil, water, and produced CO2 responses. A heteroscedastic variance head estimates data-dependent predictive uncertainty, and engineering-inspired regularization improves temporal plausibility and control-response consistency. The trained surrogate is embedded into a preference-conditioned reinforcement learning framework to generate schedules under different storage-oil trade-off preferences. Experiments on a conceptual low-permeability compositional simulation model show that the proposed surrogate achieves lower MAE and RMSE than GRU, LSTM, TCN, and GNN-GRU baselines. Under the same surrogate-based evaluation setting, the reinforcement learning optimizer generates a denser Pareto set than NSGA-II and improves the high-oil-production region, while NSGA-II remains competitive at the high-storage extreme. A representative optimized schedule is further re-simulated in Eclipse, showing generally consistent production trends. The workflow provides an efficient decision-support tool for simulation-based CO2 flooding optimization within the tested conceptual reservoir model.

title: From Predictive Analytics to Decision Governance: An AI-Enabled Framework for Condition-Based Maintenance of Industrial Gas Turbines
container-title: ADIPEC
489046c3b998f38a12f19559840cab0fa3dfbf5b.abstract: Abstract The objective of this paper is to reframe AI-enabled predictive maintenance from a failure prediction activity into a structured decision support capability. It describes how artificial intelligence, combined with physics-based models and real operating data, supports faster interpretation of asset behavior when systems operate close to technical limits. Rather than replacing engineering expertise, AI enables more disciplined, traceable, and defensible maintenance and operational decisions within a Condition-Based Maintenance (CBM) framework. The proposed method integrates AI-based analytics within a structured Condition-Based Maintenance (CBM) decision process. Physics-based models, OEM domain knowledge, and real-time operating data are combined through AI-enabled pre-processing to identify anomalies, characterize degradation behavior, and continuously update asset condition assessments. Decisions related to inspection interval extensions, temporary operating limit exceedances, and deferral of non-critical work are governed through a formal decision process based on departure records. These records document underlying assumptions, residual risk, agreed mitigation actions, and clearly defined re-entry conditions, ensuring accountability, technical traceability, and shared risk ownership across the asset operating lifecycle. Scenario-based "what if" analyses are used to assess decision robustness and reversibility before the implementation, with final decision authority retained by human experts. Application of the proposed approach has enabled customers to extend maintenance intervals in a controlled and risk-based manner across a broad range of assets. Evidence from 104 documented departure records issued in 2025 shows that condition-based decisions have been implemented at fleet scale, with 54% of departures related to aeroderivative units and 46% to heavy duty gas turbines. The industrial revance of these results is illustrated by large LNG applications, including implementations with ExxonMobil where condition-based interval extensions were formally adopted following OEM analytics, engineering validation, and structured risk assessment. In these applications, inspection intervals for critical gas turbines were extended from standard semi-annual Level 1 cycles (4,000 fired hours) to condition-based intervals exceeding 15,000 fired hours, avoiding multiple days of production downtime per train while maintaining asset integrity. These results support the transition toward Performance-Based Contract (PBC) models, where CBM-driven decisions, digital insights, and engineering governance are directly linked to shared performance outcomes such as availability, reliability, and production continuity rather than prescriptive maintenance schedules. This paper adds to the existing literature by demonstrating that the adoption of an AI-enabled CBM decision process, grounded in formal risk assessment and decision governance, enables new collaborative operating and contractual models, including Performance-Based Contracts (PBC). The approach shifts OEM–operator relationships from transactional service delivery to partnership-based models, where priorities, risk acceptance, and operational flexibility are jointly defined. This enables operators to sustain production under constrained conditions while maintaining traceable, accountable decision-making.

title: Systems of Surrogates: A Method for Physics-Informed AI in Surface Network Optimization at Full-Field Scale
container-title: ADIPEC
cdab351641a95582cce46d68bc8ac708ca1d057f.abstract: Oil and gas well-network systems are inherently complex hydraulically, thermodynamically, and operationally. Even the smallest network will typically demonstrate well-to-well hydraulic pressure interference, co-mingling fluids and gasses, down-hole constraints and capacity constraints once the multiphase mixtures reach their processing destination. A suite of mature commercial simulation offerings exist which have throughout the years shown to be quite capable in accurately predicting the steady state behavior of such systems given adequate well design, flowline, and fluid PVT data (Schlumberger 2023; Petroleum Experts 2023). Unfortunately, the simulation-driven optimization of such systems faces a multiplicative computational burden as a target network increases in size with respect to well count: the cost per forward solution increases and the dimensionality of the inverse problem itself (number of control variables) increases; proportionally demanding additional forward evaluations to find feasible optimums (Bieker et al. 2007). For example, a co-mingled network of 200 ESP wells undergoing choke opening and ESP frequency optimization will require 401 (1 baseline + 400 control variable perturbations) forward solves for the construction of a single two-point finite difference estimated Jacobian matrix. When operating networks of these scales, the time-horizon for decision making is the critical constraint. While combining a high-fidelity simulator with optimization algorithms can technically support a wide array of inverse problems, it may take so long to produce an answer from such an approach that the chance to apply a decision based on that answer has passed. There are many classical and novel approaches to accelerating optimization tasks including probabilistic methods, gradient free schemes, and linearization (Camponogara and Nakashima 2006), all with varying compatibility and utility for problems of this high dimensionality. In this work we focus on a proxy/surrogate model approach (Forrester et al. 2008) which leverages a computationally expensive yet robust gradient based optimizer algorithm, while compressing the forward solve time itself via assemblages of non-linear physics-informed deep neural network regressors.

title: Machine Learning-Based Detection of Stealthy Fraudulent Data Injection Attacks in Modern Digital Energy Systems
container-title: ADIPEC
91ca006a8e602c604123391dcaf90cd2468ab9a2.abstract: Abstract The increasing digitalization of modern energy systems through Advanced Metering Infrastructure (AMI), Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT), and smart metering technologies has significantly enhanced operational efficiency, monitoring capabilities, and system automation. However, the widespread adoption of interconnected digital devices has also expanded the cybersecurity attack surface, exposing energy systems to sophisticated cyber threats, including Fraudulent Data Injection Attacks (FDIAs). These attacks manipulate energy measurement data in transit, compromising data integrity and potentially leading to incorrect operational decisions and fraudulent billing. Traditional detection techniques, including Bad Data Detection (BDD), have proven ineffective against stealthy FDIAs that can evade conventional validation mechanisms. This paper presents a machine-learning-based framework for detecting stealthy fraudulent data-injection attacks in digital energy systems. A realistic AMI simulation testbed was developed using virtualized digital energy meters, communication protocol simulators, and a controlled attack environment to generate both benign and malicious datasets. Network traffic was captured using Wireshark, and a dataset comprising selected communication and protocol features was constructed through preprocessing, feature selection, encoding, and normalization procedures. A total of 33 network- and application-layer features were used to develop the FDIA detection model. Four unsupervised machine learning algorithms, namely Isolation Forest (IF), One- Class Support Vector Machine (OC-SVM), Local Outlier Factor (LOF), and Elliptic Envelope (EE), were trained exclusively on benign operational data and evaluated using a test dataset containing both normal and FDIA-generated malicious samples. Comparative performance analysis was conducted using confusion matrices, accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, Matthews Correlation Coefficient (MCC), balanced accuracy, and Area Under the Receiver Operating Characteristic Curve (AUROC). Experimental results demonstrate that the Local Outlier Factor algorithm achieved the best overall performance, achieving 95.8% accuracy, 97.2% balanced accuracy, 92.2% F1-score, an MCC of 0.899, and perfect recall and AUROC of 1.000, successfully detecting all fraudulent data-injection attacks without any false negatives. The findings confirm that density-based anomaly detection techniques provide superior capability for identifying stealthy FDIAs in digital energy communication networks. The proposed framework offers an effective and scalable approach for strengthening cybersecurity, preserving data integrity, and enhancing the resilience of modern smart energy infrastructures

title: Physically Constrained Data Augmentation and Machine Learning for Pressure and Production Forecasting in Data-Restricted Mature Gas Fields: A Balochistan Case Study
container-title: ADIPEC
b77a39d3a397d7c6af14e6ea8c3e1d437d370bad.abstract: Abstract Balochistan is home to a strategically important mature gas field currently facing an abrupt decline in reservoir pressure that threatens long-term deliverability and regional energy security; this study develops a forecasting framework that transforms sparse annual field records into high-resolution daily datasets to support pressure and production forecasting, with the objective of providing a data-driven foundation for a reservoir decision-support system that enables operators to evaluate production redistribution and selective well shut-in strategies to mitigate depletion while sustaining field deliverability. The methodology applies Piecewise Cubic Hermite Interpolating Polynomial (PCHIP) interpolation to transform 21 years of annual well-level data (2000–2020) into high-resolution daily augmented datasets, with a mass-balance-preserving correction layer ensuring physical consistency: gas and water production are treated as cumulative quantities with annual volume-balance correction, while reservoir pressure and water-gas ratio are treated as state variables; these augmented datasets are then used to train and compare Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks and eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) models, which are validated against actual 2026 field data to assess long-term predictive robustness. Results show that physically consistent data augmentation significantly enhances the utility of sparse reservoir records for machine learning, and external validation against 2026 field data reveals that model performance is target-specific—XGBoost achieves better accuracy for reservoir pressure decline and water-gas ratio (WGR) prediction, while LSTM shows stronger resilience in capturing gas and water production trends—and incorporating reservoir-informed feature engineering, such as time-lagged variables and rolling averages, further optimizes performance, reducing the Mean Absolute Error (MAE) for gas production to 2.78; a key observation is that standard mathematical interpolation can introduce non-physical oscillations, whereas the PCHIP-based mass-balance approach preserves the physical interpretation of reservoir depletion, leading to the conclusion that reliable forecasting in mature fields requires a hybrid, target-specific approach—tree-based models for state-variable trends and recurrent networks for production sequences—and demonstrating that practical deliverability forecasting can be achieved without high-cost operational variables such as choke sizes or bottom-hole temperatures, provided that data augmentation respects production-volume balance constraints. This paper introduces a novel integration of reservoir-engineering constraints with data augmentation that, unlike black-box machine learning, distinguishes between cumulative and state variables to preserve annual mass balance, offering the industry a cost-effective workflow for transforming legacy annual records into high-resolution predictive tools and bridging the gap between sparse historical reporting and modern requirements for data-driven reservoir management.

title: From Data to Decision: A Field-Validated AI-Assisted Production Intelligence Framework for Opportunity Identification, Artificial Lift Optimization, and Surveillance in the Indus Basin
container-title: ADIPEC
682401dea7bf98f4681e69f40979ea43326f1efc.abstract: Abstract Objectives/Scope The increasing complexity of mature oil, gas, and condensate assets has expanded surveillance data volumes while making rapid identification of high-value production opportunities increasingly difficult. Conventional workflows rely on fragmented datasets, manual interpretation, and reactive assessments resulting in delayed intervention planning, suboptimal artificial lift performance, and inconsistent prioritization across large portfolios. This study presents a field-validated AI-assisted production intelligence framework to enhance opportunity identification, artificial lift optimization, and surveillance efficiency across a multi-well oil, gas, and condensate portfolio in the Indus Basin, Pakistan. Methods, Procedures, Process The framework integrates production, pressure, temperature, choke, gas lift injection, well testing, downtime, and intervention datasets from production databases into a centralized Python-based environment connected to business intelligence dashboards. Isolation Forest and gradient boosting-based anomaly detection algorithms were combined with petroleum engineering workflows including nodal analysis, liquid loading diagnostics using Turner and Coleman critical velocity models, gas lift performance diagnostics, and operating envelope validation to establish a physics-guided decision intelligence system. The framework screens wells across natural flow and artificial lift modes, diagnosing liquid loading, gas lift inefficiency, skin buildup, and choke instability, ranking opportunities by uplift potential and operational feasibility. Results, Observations, Conclusions Field deployment across 41 active wells including 4 gas lift producers reduced manual well review cycles from bi-weekly to daily automated anomaly alerts. Within 6 months, 29 anomaly flags were reduced to 16 physics-validated opportunities across four categories: 5 liquid loading remediation candidates drawn from 8 wells confirmed below Turner critical rate with deficits ranging from 12% to 78%, 2 gas lift optimization candidates, 4 choke and operating envelope deviations, and 5 rigless intervention candidates. Gas lift optimization contributed an incremental ~80 BOED, while aggregate uplift reached approximately 650 BOED (~3.9 MMSCFD) representing an ~18% improvement over the 12-month pre-deployment baseline. Decision cycle time was reduced by an estimated 55%, with full portfolio coverage achieved without additional engineering headcount. Novel/Additive Information This methodology demonstrates how AI-assisted surveillance integrates with petroleum engineering domain knowledge to create scalable production decision intelligence systems for mature assets. Unlike purely data-driven approaches, the framework combines machine learning with physics-based validation at every decision node preserving auditability, operational trust, and engineering accountability. This scalable, low-infrastructure model confirms that AI-assisted production intelligence is deployable without enterprise-scale investment across the Indus Basin and similar producing regions globally.

title: Physics-Guided AI–Numerical Simulation for Sand Production Prediction and Completion Optimization
container-title: ADIPEC
6faae9cc1216c5f7bd2de1d415c2ac2ff3fe5cc3.abstract: Abstract Sand production is a nonlinear, path-dependent, and strongly coupled process controlled by reservoir depletion, effective-stress redistribution, near-wellbore stress concentration, elastoplastic failure, damage accumulation, grain debonding, hydraulic detachment, erosion, and particulate transport. Its occurrence and severity depend on rock-strength variability, stress regime, well trajectory, completion type, perforation orientation, production drawdown, transient rate history, water weakening, and evolving cavity geometry. Conventional sanding workflows typically combine empirical screening, analytical failure criteria, and detailed numerical simulation, but each method has limitations when used independently. Empirical correlations may not extrapolate reliably; analytical methods simplify geometry and constitutive behavior; and high-fidelity finite-element or discrete-element models are computationally expensive for field-scale optimization and real-time control. This paper develops a unified physics-guided artificial-intelligence and numerical-simulation framework for predicting sanding onset, critical drawdown, transient sand rate, cumulative sand production, cavity evolution, and completion-dependent operating envelopes. The workflow integrates quality-controlled petrophysical logs, drilling and production records, depletion history, laboratory measurements from unconfined compression, triaxial compression, thick-wall-cylinder and advanced thick-wall-cylinder tests, calibrated one-dimensional geomechanical models, and three-dimensional poroelastoplastic finite-element simulations. Sanding initiation is constrained by an analytical effective-strength-factor load criterion and a laboratory-calibrated critical-strain-limit criterion. Mechanical failure is coupled to hydraulic mobilization through drag, lift, seepage, and retention forces, while an erosion law governs sand generation and transport. The AI layer combines gradient-boosted trees, random forests, deep neural networks, temporal models, graph neural networks, neural operators, residual learning, and physics-informed neural networks. A multi-task, multi-fidelity loss function enforces data agreement, finite-element consistency, equilibrium, mass conservation, yield admissibility, Critical state line (CSL) consistency, nonnegative sand rate, physically valid bounds, and regime-dependent monotonicity. Bayesian and ensemble uncertainty quantification provides conservative safe-drawdown limits and out-of-distribution detection. Completion optimization is posed as a constrained multi-objective problem over well trajectory, perforation orientation, phasing, penetration, sand-control selection, and drawdown schedule. The supplied field-study basis indicates that representative depletion scenarios up to 3,000 psi, a stress-path coefficient near 0.6, TWC variability, and open-hole versus cased-and-perforated geometry materially alter the sanding envelope. Laboratory-calibrated TWC/perforation-scale CSL values range approximately from 30 to 68 millistrain in the documented cases, and open-hole CSL may be 20–60% lower because of hole-size and unsupported-boundary effects. The proposed framework converts high-fidelity numerical simulations into rapid probabilistic operating envelopes without inventing unsupported AI performance statistics. It supports pre-drill completion screening, uncertainty-aware production design, adaptive choke control, and continuously updated sand-management digital twins.

title: Pore-Scale Prediction of Apparent and Relative Permeability in Continental Shale Using Deep-Learning-Enhanced Digital Rocks
container-title: ADIPEC
85b086f922ac82b5613423e3fa9c3dd52c010e12.abstract: Abstract Accurate characterization of multiphase flow in continental shale remains challenging because of ultra-low permeability, nanoscale confinement effects, and the difficulty of conducting representative core-flooding experiments. This study presents a pore-scale simulation framework that integrates deep-learning-enhanced digital rock reconstruction with pore network modeling (PNM). The framework is applied to investigate nonlinear single- and two-phase flow behaviors and to quantify the effects of boundary-layer phenomena, wettability, and fluid properties on apparent and relative permeability. A three-dimensional digital rock model was reconstructed from focused ion beam scanning electron microscopy (FIB-SEM) images with an initial resolution of 9.4 nm. To overcome the tradeoff between field of view and imaging resolution, a deep-learning-based super-resolution algorithm was employed to enhance the image resolution to 4.7 nm prior to PNM extraction. To simulate nonlinear flow behavior, an open-source PNM simulator was modified by incorporating upscaled molecular-simulation results to capture nanoscale boundary-layer effects. The enhanced model dynamically evaluates apparent permeability and two-phase relative permeability under varying pressure gradients, fluid viscosities, interfacial tensions (IFT), and mixed-wettability conditions. The extracted pore network exhibits a highly compact structure dominated by pores ranging from 5 to 25 nm and throats ranging from 15 to 40 nm, with limited connectivity. Single-phase flow simulations demonstrate pronounced nonlinear flow behavior, where apparent permeability increases with pressure gradient because of the progressive weakening of boundary-layer effects. In addition, fluids with higher viscosity require disproportionately larger pressure gradients to achieve effective transport. For two-phase flow, incorporation of boundary-layer effects slightly increases oil relative permeability while decreasing water relative permeability, primarily because water adsorption along pore walls reduces the effective flow volume available to the aqueous phase. Mixed wettability also strongly influences displacement behavior, and a lower oil-wet fraction preferentially distributed in larger pores is found to enhance shale oil recovery. Furthermore, increasing oil viscosity shifts the crossover point of the relative permeability curves toward the lower-left region, indicating greater resistance during waterflooding. In contrast, higher IFT shifts the crossover point toward the upper-right region, suggesting enhanced capillary-driven displacement during imbibition. This study establishes a multiscale workflow that links molecular-scale boundary-layer effects with pore-scale flow evaluation in continental shale reservoirs. By enabling dynamic prediction of apparent and relative permeability without reliance on costly and time-consuming physical core-flooding experiments, the proposed method provides a practical and physics-informed foundation for optimizing shale oil development and evaluating displacement efficiency.

title: Preventing Major Road Transportation Incidents Through ADAS and AI-Enabled Fleet Intelligence: A Framework for Safer and More Resilient Energy Supply Chains
container-title: ADIPEC
9f5cdc164fe04e1f1f074f71895b4ac13038b5b4.abstract: Abstract Objectives/Scope Road traffic crashes cause approx. 1.19 million fatalities and 20-50 million injuries globally each year (WHO 2023), while imposing economic losses approaching 3% of GDP in many countries. Transportation of fuels, chemicals, LNG, industrial gases, and other hazardous materials represents one of the most critical and risk-intensive links in global energy supply chains. Human factors—including fatigue, distraction, speeding, impaired judgement, and blind-spot errors—contribute to nearly 80-90%of severe transportation incidents. While telematics-based fleet monitoring has improved operational visibility, they remain largely reactive. This paper evaluates how Advanced Driver Assistance Systems (ADAS) with AI-enabled fleet intelligence and Driver Monitoring System (DMS) can transform commercial fleet safety by shifting risk management from reactive monitoring to proactive accident prevention Methods, Procedures, Process This study utilizes a multi-evidence triangulation methodology integrating four streams: (1) forensic reconstruction of 60 severe tanker crashes (including 25 internal accident investigation); (2) physiological survey of 500 active drivers; (3) a 90-day pilot of 155 tankers using AI telematics and infrared DMS; and (4) Level 0–2 ADAS testing via an LCV-to-HCV validation bridge. The Safety Cocoon fuses forward 77 GHz radar, forward optical camera, and 24 GHz side radars with an in-cab DMS to continuously assess risk. Results, Observations, and Conclusions Forensic analysis identified rollovers (35%), rear-end impacts (28%), and sideswipes (18%) as dominant crash typologies, driven primarily by fatigue and distraction. The 155-tanker pilot revealed a 12-to-1 Detection Gap where DMS captured behavioral precursors invisible to passive GPS. Triangulated findings indicate the Safety Cocoon is projected to prevent 70–75% of forward and lateral collisions. Economic modelling projects a 17.12-month payback period on an upfront CapEx of ₹285.90 Lakh, generating ₹17.19 Crore in 10-year fleet lifecycle net returns. Novel Approach This paper presents an integrated Accident-to-ADAS Risk Mitigation Framework developed from real-world crash forensics, driver behavioural analytics, operational AI-enabled Fleet Intelligence pilot data, and an LCV-to-HCV ADAS Validation Framework. Rather than positioning ADAS as an optional vehicle feature, the research establishes an engineering and economic blueprint for integrating AI-enabled Fleet Intelligence, active ADAS, and Journey Risk Management 2.0 into a multi-layered Safety Cocoon for hazardous-material transportation. The proposed framework bridges the gap between passive behavioural monitoring and active physical intervention, providing energy executives, fleet operators, and regulators with a technically rigorous and economically justified pathway for strengthening the safety and resilience of global energy logistics

title: AI-Based Optimization for LNG Sustainable and Efficient Production
container-title: ADIPEC
db84223af7bad433721ea6d2e836439e1a64b9f3.abstract: Abstract Asset optimization has become increasingly important in recent years, particularly in the Oil & Gas industry, where improving process efficiency is essential to address both economic and environmental challenges. As the global energy sector moves toward a lower-carbon future, natural gas is expected to play a key role as a transition fuel thanks to its lower emissions compared to other fossil fuel sources. Within this framework, Liquefied Natural Gas (LNG) represents a valuable source to enhance energy security and supply diversification due to its intrinsic flexibility in transportation and trading. This work presents one of the first applications of a Differential Evolution (DE) algorithm to the optimization of an offshore Dual Mixed Refrigerant (DMR) natural gas liquefaction process modelled and validated with real plant data. The process is first modeled using a commercial simulation software and, after validation, it is integrated with a Differential Evolution-based (DE) optimization tool to identify the operating conditions that maximize process performance while respecting relevant operational constraints. Different optimization scenarios are investigated by progressively expanding the set of decision variables, including refrigerant compositions, pressure drops across Joule-Thomson valves of the refrigeration cycles, and refrigerant mass flow rates. The results highlight the ability of the Differential Evolution-based approach to effectively explore the solution space and identify operating configurations capable of significantly increasing LNG production while maintaining acceptable energy consumption levels.

title: Augmenting Petroleum Engineers with Agentic AI: A ReAct Agent Framework for Automated Well Diagnostics and Candidate Screening
container-title: ADIPEC
9bc6b07335ff5537c9111977aedb5e3ddced754a.abstract: Abstract Mature onshore oil fields carry thousands of wells that all need watching. Rates drift, water cuts creep up, injectors quietly lose conformance, and somewhere in that population sit the handful of candidates that would pay back an intervention. In day-to-day practice, petroleum engineers spend a large share of their time pulling data, hopping between tools such as OFM and spreadsheets, and repeating the same diagnostic steps well after well. The work is necessary but slow, and because everyone does it slightly differently, interpretations vary from engineer to engineer and from asset to asset. This paper describes an Agentic Petroleum Engineering Assistant that turns a plain-language question into a standardized, multi-step production analysis, so the engineer spends the time on judgement rather than on data wrangling.
