The framework also demonstrates how validated reports and recurring risk themes can be converted into task-specific learning content, including microlearning, toolbox-talk material, scenario-based quizzes, and AI-generated safety podcasts. Connecting reporting, classification, corrective action, learning, feedback, and recurrence monitoring creates a closed safety-learning loop and helps reduce the likelihood that repeated unsafe acts or conditions develop into more serious incidents. The paper concludes that human-centered AI can help offshore marine operators move from isolated and reactive record handling toward earlier recognition of recurring risks and more focused preventive action. The technology can support seafarers, vessel managers, and shore-based HSE teams by making frontline information easier to interpret and connect with corrective actions, inspections, operational exposure, and targeted learning. It should not assign blame, determine disciplinary outcomes, establish root cause autonomously, or replace the authority of competent maritime professionals.

title: Evaluating AI for Speed, Consistency, and Traceability in Energy Regulatory Decision Support
container-title: ADIPEC
e02c303b92aa19e5fc04918698846dd4235a86a3.abstract: Abstract This paper evaluates select Artificial Intelligence (AI) setups designed to audit anonymised safety case submissions of petroleum operators for regulatory compliance. We compared a Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) Pipeline (using gpt-4o-mini) against a One-Shot Baseline (direct gpt-4o-mini processing) and an Agentic AI (using gemini-2.5-flash, and Antigravity as harness). We demonstrated that automated reviews achieve notable speedups over manual reviews, up to 240.8x for RAG and 634.8x for the Agentic AI. While the One-Shot Baseline is the fastest overall (2 to 6 minutes), RAG and the Agentic AI showed higher recall in discovering compliance omissions on large documents (e.g., the 564-page SUB-002). We also identified a self-evaluation bias, where gpt-4o-mini rates its own faithfulness much higher (4.13/5.0) than the judge (2.21/5.0).

title: A Master Well, Multilayer Artificial Intelligence / Machine Learning (AI/ML) Framework for Scalable Porosity Permeability Prediction and Log Reconstruction in Carbonate Reservoirs
container-title: ADIPEC
dfaac0c94fde56ef5a3e7aa3ea031a204d0361e0.abstract: Abstract Carbonate reservoirs exhibit complex petrophysical behavior arising from heterogeneity, uneven core coverage and variable log data quality. These challenges significantly limit the scalability and repeatability of conventional petrophysical workflows, particularly when extended to large well populations. To address these limitations, this study presents a Master Well centric artificial intelligence and machine learning (AI/ML) framework for scalable prediction of porosity and permeability and log reconstruction with a focus on improving model generalization, validation robustness and operational efficiency across the field. Conventional petrophysical machine learning is bound to the well in which it was calibrated. This study shifts the unit of training from the well to the field by constructing a Master Well, a single core calibrated reference population assembled by randomized sampling across nine wells. Two advances underpin the approach. Pore aspect ratio is estimated from the fractional lithology curves of the multimineral solution, so the elastic properties follow the local calcite and dolomite volumes and stay consistent with theoretical endmember values. The soft and stiff pore endmembers defined by Kumar and Han (2005) and Xu and Payne (2009) provide the envelope within which each sample is placed, and the aspect ratio contours between those limits separate the pore classes. Each pore system is normalized within its class to decompose total porosity into comparable fractions, which enter the models as engineered features alongside the pore classes carried through training and testing as categorical classifiers. The secondary porosity index and the pore aspect ratio emerge as the strongest permeability indicators of those tested, and both outrank porosity alone. Seventy two models were developed across multiple algorithm families, with the best realization of each retained for comparison. Held out testing returns R2 between 0.71 and 0.95, the wireline responses being reconstructed most accurately and the rock properties limited by genuine reservoir heterogeneity rather than by model capability. Because the reference population spans the full multilayer succession rather than a single interval, the models carry that layered behavior into every well to which they are applied. Deployment to a new well requires only environmental correction and normalization to the Master Well reference distributions, with no additional core. Accuracy is expected to hold within the calibration envelope of approximately 20 km lateral extent defined by the present dataset, beyond which predictions should be treated as indicative until confirmed against local core.

title: Integrating Machine Learning with Lean Six Sigma for Pre-Emptive Waste Elimination in Marine Logistics
container-title: ADIPEC
bc98c450fc3b4cefde06f13820dc30c1a0e5a19f.abstract: Abstract Traditional Lean and Six Sigma waste-elimination methods are generally activated after inefficiency, deviation, or non-conformance has already appeared in the process. This paper presents a pre-emptive waste-elimination framework that uses artificial intelligence and process telemetry to detect early signals of waste formation before measurable operational loss occurs. The scope covers asset performance, process flow, decision latency, quality variation, and behavioral indicators in operational environments. The study develops an AI-enabled waste lifecycle model that extends the conventional define-measure-analyze-improve-control cycle. The framework classifies waste into three stages: latent waste, emerging waste, and realized waste. Latent waste is identified through weak signals in process data, including small deviations in cycle time, asset behavior, quality variance, queue accumulation, and repeated decision delays. Machine learning models are applied to historical and live process data to detect patterns associated with waste formation. Human validation is then used to confirm operational relevance and convert predicted waste signals into preventive improvement actions. The framework changes the role of operational excellence from retrospective correction to predictive intervention. In conventional Lean systems, waste is normally identified after it has affected cost, time, quality, safety, or resource utilization. The proposed model allows waste to be detected earlier by monitoring precursor conditions that may not breach conventional thresholds but indicate process degradation. The key result is the introduction of a staged waste lifecycle that separates latent, emerging, and realized waste. This distinction enables improvement teams to act before waste becomes visible in standard KPIs or value stream maps. For example, recurring approval delays, minor equipment performance drift, unstable handover timing, or early quality variation can be treated as predictive waste signals rather than isolated process noise. The paper concludes that AI does not replace Lean problem solving. Instead, it expands the observation boundary of Lean by identifying where waste is likely to form, allowing practitioners to prioritize investigation, reduce response time, and prevent avoidable loss before it is fully realized. The paper introduces a pre-emptive waste-elimination model that extends traditional Lean and Six Sigma practice beyond observed defects and process losses. Its novelty lies in defining waste as a lifecycle that can be detected before it becomes measurable. This provides practicing engineers and operational excellence leaders with a structured method to integrate AI into continuous improvement without abandoning established Lean principles.

title: Reliability AI: A Production LLM System for Converting Maintenance Data into ISO 14224-Compliant Reliability Information
container-title: ADIPEC
7193d7a0bfbd5be3af262f515776bbae2bf8ae11.abstract: Abstract Reliability engineering in the oil and gas industry depends on accurate, standardized failure data, yet the raw material for that data—free-text maintenance work orders—is inherently unstructured, inconsistent, and expensive to interpret. This paper describes the design, production deployment, and iterative accuracy improvement of an artificial-intelligence system that converts unstructured maintenance work-order text into ISO 14224-compliant reliability classifications without requiring supervised model training. The system combines a hierarchical retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) pipeline built on a vector database of labeled work-order examples with a three-run large-language-model (LLM) consensus mechanism that scores candidate failure codes using a weighted combination of voting agreement, average model confidence, and cross-run consensus strength. A two-stage human-in-the-loop override-and-approval workflow allows reliability engineers to correct AI-generated classifications; approved corrections are written back into the vector store as provenance-tagged examples, closing the feedback loop without retraining the underlying models. Beyond classification, agentic conversational analytics layer adaptively draws on a governed SQL tool over the structured work-order mart, a retrieval-augmented tool over the ISO 14224 standard itself, or both together within a single session, giving engineers direct, auditable access to failure trends and taxonomy guidance. In an initial blind evaluation against 300 historical work orders, the system achieved approximately 70% classification accuracy with no labeled training data. Following a structured improvement phase that incorporated approximately 1,000 additional work orders and their associated engineer corrections through the override-approval feedback loop, accuracy on an expanded validation set increased to approximately 88%, with continued refinement targeted at a 95% operating threshold. Beyond accuracy, on the system's current production hardware footprint, the effort required to prepare ISO 14224-compliant data for 10,000 work orders is reduced from roughly six months of manual engineering time to two weeks, while enabling reliability queries that previously took days to be answered in seconds. This paper presents the system architecture, the consensus-based classification methodology, the feedback-driven improvement pathway, and production deployment lessons relevant to safety-critical, air-gapped industrial environments.

title: Leadership Development – Building Enterprise-Wide Capability and Accelerating Diverse Leadership Impact with Cohort-Based Learning
container-title: ADIPEC
6a92bd1db1b92a023c59ca1dce0557346b3e7c21.abstract: Abstract This paper examines how Occidental Petroleum Corporation uses cohort-based leadership development to build enterprise-wide leadership capability and accelerate leadership impact across career stages. Grounded in research on experiential learning and learning retention, the paper first identifies several barriers that can prevent leadership learning from translating into sustained behavior change, including rapid forgetting, limited practice opportunities, low perceived relevance, insufficient leader reinforcement, and limited psychological safety or protected learning time. The paper then describes how the company's leadership development portfolio, including training and development for the company's high potential employees, new leaders, seasoned leaders, and leaders of leaders, addresses these barriers through interactive learning, immediate application, cross-functional projects, guided coaching, senior-leader engagement, and ongoing reinforcement. The paper also summarizes a needs analysis that used Korn Ferry Leadership Architect behavioral competencies to identify priority skill gaps for individual contributors, front-line leaders, and managers of managers, and to align program content to career-level needs. In addition, each development program involves participants from diverse functions, disciplines, and backgrounds to ensure cross-functional exposure and robust networking. Participation, satisfaction, career-movement, and skill-development data suggest that the programs are associated with strong learner satisfaction, expanded leadership capability, promotions, lateral movement, retention, and improved readiness for broader responsibilities. Collectively, these results provide compelling evidence that a focused, experiential, senior leader supported, and business-relevant approach can meaningfully strengthen leadership capability and accelerate career growth. Lessons learned from implementation suggest that cohort-based programs are most effective when they are manageable in duration, highly interactive, reinforced over time, and directly connected to real organizational challenges.

title: Strategy and Crisis Monitor: An AI-Enabled Autonomous Maritime Monitor for Disruption Intelligence and Operational Resilience
container-title: ADIPEC
58cade6d0892c7942bcb9842e0ff73b921a3b017.abstract: Abstract This paper presents the Strategy and Crisis Monitor, an agentic artificial-intelligence (AI) enabled executive dashboard conceived, built, and deployed end-to-end in days to track regional events, incidents, transport disruption, and energy-market signals during a live crisis. The work pursues three objectives: to demonstrate that autonomous AI agents can convert public maritime, energy, and trade data into always-on disruption intelligence; to replace the analyst-curated executive briefing with a live, evidence-linked signal layer operating under human oversight; and to compress executive decision latency from days to minutes. The architecture comprises three operational layers. An ingestion layer of autonomous agents continuously normalizes heterogeneous public sources, including multilateral chokepoint transit data, vessel-tracking feeds derived from the Automatic Identification System (AIS), international oil and gas statistics, and maritime trade and connectivity indicators, supplemented by market context as evidence layers. A classification layer maps incoming data against a rules-based event taxonomy covering chokepoint disruption, export-route stress, gas exposure, port-connectivity deterioration, and regional trade impact. A prioritization layer scores signals using a weighted composite risk index with exponentially weighted moving average (EWMA) and cumulative sum (CUSUM) anomaly detection, and surfaces them through a 60-second executive scan pattern with full drill-down to underlying sources. Deployed live during the March 2026 Strait of Hormuz disruption, when average daily transits collapsed by approximately 95% against the February baseline and the benchmark very large crude carrier (VLCC) rate reached an all-time high, the platform was used to brief senior leadership of a major national maritime and energy logistics operator in near real time. It reduced executive decision latency from a typical 24- to 72-hour analyst cycle to under five minutes per signal, a compression factor of roughly 290 to 860, while integrating more than 40 public indicators. The same detection logic was subsequently applied retrospectively to four historical chokepoint crises, in the Red Sea (2023 to 2024), the Suez Canal (2021), the Strait of Hormuz (2019), and the Panama Canal (2023 to 2024), confirming that the monitored public signals were available weeks to months ahead of official statistics in every case. Those case studies were reconstructed with knowledge of how each episode unfolded and therefore document signal availability and design generality rather than prospective detection performance. The contribution is twofold and is, to the authors’ knowledge, the first implementation of its kind in the maritime-resilience and energy-logistics literature. First, a decision-method contribution: passive public reporting feeds are converted into a structured, always-on resilience instrument fusing maritime, energy, and trade signals in a single operating view. Second, an operating-model contribution: the architecture is public-data-native, lightweight to sustain, and reproducible across operating companies, corridors, and risk domains, and is presented together with the governance, oversight, and control mechanisms required before agentic AI is admitted to a critical operational environment. Both are directly actionable for practicing engineers and planners in operations, strategy, and resilience roles.

title: Integrating Downhole Corrosion Evaluation with Metallurgical Analysis for AI-Driven Well Failure Prediction Model
container-title: ADIPEC
b3ec944994b27ae3cf154a5cef754319b5619408.abstract: Abstract Objectives/Scope Recurring tubing failures driven by aggressive downhole corrosion represent a critical operational and economic challenge in ESP-lifted production wells of the EKI field, East Kuwait 1. With an average corrosion rate of 4 mm/year and 325 documented tubing failures across the South East Kuwait (SEK) portfolio, the lack of a mechanistic corrosion management framework has sustained a reactive workover cycle with production deferment and integrity risk. This paper presents the first deployment of a 64-element fixed-array advanced ultrasonic cement and corrosion tool within 3½-inch production tubing, enabling simultaneous 360° azimuthal corrosion evaluation in a single rigless pass. The objective is to integrate high-resolution corrosion mapping with laboratory metallurgical analysis, establish the corrosion mechanism for the study well, and translate the findings into the foundation of an AI-driven Corrosion Management System (CMS) and well failure prediction model. Methods, Procedures, Process A two-run rigless wireline evaluation was executed. The first run deployed a 24-arm multi-finger caliper and electromagnetic multi-string tool to assess inner surface morphology and average wall thickness across four nested casing strings. The second run deployed the 64-element fixed-array ultrasonic tool, commercially known as Reveal Barrier (SLB), in its first deployment within 3½-inch production tubing, acquiring simultaneous 360° azimuthal inner wall and thickness maps in a single monocable pass. Six tubing samples, selected using the corrosion map, underwent laboratory investigation comprising X-ray diffraction, X-ray fluorescence, ion chromatography, optical emission spectroscopy, tensile testing, electrochemical corrosion modeling, and quantitative PCR microbiological analysis. An operational SOP was established to enable safe and repeatable deployment across the portfolio. Results, Observations, Conclusions The deployment enabled a proactive, data-driven workover decision that achieved zero non-productive time (NPT) during tubing retrieval. Laboratory analysis confirmed two distinct corrosion mechanisms: internal chloride-induced CO2/H2S pitting above the ESP, where mechanical scale disruption initiates deep anodic pits; and external crevice corrosion below the ESP, driven by clamp contact geometry in a stagnant H2S-enriched annulus. CO2 and H2S were identified as likely byproducts of excess water production, enabling targeted mitigation. Microbiologically influenced corrosion was ruled out. The integrated dataset supports an AI predictive model trained on 133 wells in the EKI/SEK portfolio, demonstrating promising first-pass corrosion-rate predictions and ongoing refinement using time-lapse data. Chemical injection has been identified as the preferred mitigation strategy targeting a reduction from 4 mm/year to below 1 mm/year. Novel/Additive Information This work establishes three original contributions to well integrity and corrosion management: (1) the first deployment of a 64-element fixed-array ultrasonic tool in 3½-inch production tubing, enabling combined corrosion and cement evaluation in a previously inaccessible completion size; (2) the first use of full 360° azimuthal pre-workover corrosion mapping to support a zero-NPT, data-driven workover decision for tubing retrieval in this completion size; and (3) the integration of downhole ultrasonic thickness mapping with laboratory metallurgical analysis to derive a spatially resolved corrosion mechanism, forming the foundation of an AI-driven field-wide CMS and well failure prediction model scalable across the KOC's portfolio.

title: A Geology-Led, Physics-Informed, ML-AI Driven Architecture for Real-Time Drilling Hazard Prediction
container-title: ADIPEC
250fc79740d4e0eb603a3943f325d506107535b5.abstract: Abstract Drilling hazards, including wellbore influxes, mud losses, overpressure, shale instability, and bit balling, account for up to 35% of global non-productive time (NPT). Traditional telemetry alarms remain largely reactive, while pure "black-box" ML models often generate high false-positives by misclassifying standard operational transients. To address these limitations, this paper presents the Geology-led, Physics-informed ML-AI Early Warning System (GeoMLAI-EWS), an edge-ready framework that combines ML-AI, drilling physics, and geology within a unified prediction pipeline. The methodology transforms real-time telemetry into 15 continuous physical and geological indices. These features are evaluated using a multi-model framework comprising Isolation Forest (IF), Local Outlier Factor (LOF), Temporal Convolutional Networks (TCN), spatial accumulators, and a Gradient Boosted Tree (GBT) ensemble. The architecture also incorporates a deterministic Physics Veto, governed by multivariable logic gates, to suppress ML-AI anomalies that are inconsistent with established geomechanical behaviour (e.g., predicting a kick/influx while standpipe pressure is increasing), thereby reducing physically unrealistic alarms. Case studies using five historical well data across three Indian Basins, achieved 95.0% recall, 90.5% precision, and an F1-score of 0.927. The framework successfully predicted drilling hazards up to 6m before the recorded event. The results indicate that integrating ML-AI with physics and geology provides a practical approach for reducing HSE risk, minimizing NPT, and improving wellbore integrity.

title: An Open-Source, AI-Powered Simulator for Automated Pressure-Transient Interpretation in Dry-Gas Reservoirs: Application to Wireline Formation Testing and Underground Gas Storage
container-title: ADIPEC
5eb429ea0c9547c622ebed29d6a976f409e63cc3.abstract: Abstract Underground gas storage (UGS) wells and wireline formation tester (WFT) interval pressure-transient tests (IPTT) share a common interpretation need: fast, reliable single-well pressure-transient analysis of dry-gas reservoirs under production, injection, and shut-in conditions. In practice, both workflows depend on closed commercial software and expert-driven manual analysis, which limits accessibility, transparency, and reproducibility. This paper presents an open-source Python simulator and automated interpretation framework that addresses this gap. The framework builds on a previously published and commercially validated numerical foundation for real-gas pressure-transient simulation (SPE-215576-MS): a fully implicit 2-D (r-z) single-phase real-gas model with wellbore storage, skin, and non-Darcy (Forchheimer) flow. The present work re-implements that formulation in Python, extends it to full 3-D cylindrical (r-θ-z) flow, and embeds three artificial-intelligence components: exact-gradient Jacobians by automatic differentiation, a machine-learning surrogate for pressure-dependent gas properties, and gradient-based automated history matching with Monte Carlo uncertainty quantification. The Python implementation reproduces analytical radial-flow, limited-entry, buildup, skin, wellbore-storage, and non-Darcy signatures, with back-calculated permeability within 0.1% of the model input. In 3-D, a point source at one azimuthal sector produces physically ordered multi-probe responses that no 2-D radial model can represent. Automated history matching with exact automatic-differentiation gradients recovers radial permeability, vertical permeability, mechanical skin, and the non-Darcy coefficient to four significant figures in 52 function evaluations from a deliberately poor initial guess, whereas identically configured finite-difference gradients plateau at a noise floor after 435 evaluations. Monte Carlo uncertainty quantification of a simulated flow-after-flow test delivers probabilistic absolute open flow in minutes on a standard laptop, propagating a ±35% permeability uncertainty to a P90/P10 deliverability ratio of 1.8, and an injection–falloff cycle demonstrates that the identical workflow characterizes storage wells under injection conditions. The complete workflow is delivered through an interactive browser dashboard requiring no programming from the user. The framework lowers the barrier to high-fidelity single-well gas analysis and provides an extensible open platform for the energy-transition applications of gas storage surveillance and formation testing.

title: Automated Identification of Underperforming Wells and Intervention Prioritization in a Mature Oilfield Using Unsupervised Machine Learning on Production Data: A Case Study from a Mature Oil Field in Russia
container-title: ADIPEC
3018754b14565de07d5347d6701855cd91968ea3.abstract: Abstract Mature oilfield surveillance requires rapid conversion of routine production records into reliable intervention decisions. Manual review of water cut, gas oil ratio (GOR) and rate trends, which can delay intervention and obscure failure modes. This study aims to develop a production driven, unsupervised workflow that classifies wells into performance groups and ranking intervention candidates from monthly production data of oil, gas, liquid, water cut and GOR. The workflow starts from the wells with production start dates from 2020 onward. After minimum-history requirement of more than six valid monthly oil-production points, 250 wells were used for clustering. Cumulative oil, water, and gas production were calculated for each well, and cubic curves constrained to pass through the origin were fitted to the cumulative profiles. Curve coefficients for oil, water, and gas, together with average GOR and water cut, were computed to generate 11 input features for clustering. K-means, Gaussian Mixture Model, Fuzzy C-Means, and Ward Agglomerative clustering were evaluated using the elbow method and silhouette score. Cross-algorithm comparisons provided an independent robustness check using cross-tabulation, Adjusted Rand Index (ARI), and Normalized Mutual Information (NMI). K-means was retained as the operational model because it produced interpretable surveillance classes and showed the strongest agreement with Ward Agglomerative clustering. A composite intervention score integrating cluster severity, high water-cut risk, high-GOR risk, and low oil-productivity risk was then used to rank wells for operational action. This approach isolated a small group of high-priority intervention candidates for focused engineering review.

title: Closing the Gap Between Planned and Performed Work: Learning from Normal Work Through Visual Job Design and Reflective Review
container-title: ADIPEC
9bb9b94b0deb95a20b825bb31494d8abbbdde043.abstract: Abstract Historically, safety-critical industries have relied on procedures, job safety analyses, toolbox talks, and incident investigations to improve work execution. These controls are still important, but they provide limited insight into how work is performed in the real operating environment. This paper reports on a field application of the visual Job by Design (JBD 2.0) storyboard methodology combined with reflective self-assessment video reviews to improve learning from normal work and reinforce operational consistency. The approach was performed on an offshore jack-up unit supporting drilling, wireline, coiled tubing, well testing, and coring, and lifting operations from July 2024 to July 2026. The work activities were planned with visual storyboards (JBD 2.0) and subsequently recorded with fixed cameras during routine execution. The footage was reviewed by the same frontline teams who performed the work through structured reflective learning sessions aimed at comparing planned versus performed work. Over the 24-month period, 55 task recordings were conducted over nine activity families with reflective sessions after each recording. Thirty-four sessions were structured learning records and produced 208 positive practice observations and 153 improvement observations. The most frequent learning themes involved line-of-fire exposure, body positioning, working hands free, and red zone discipline. Video reviews uncovered work plan deviations from actual execution, highlighted transition points in tasks that require additional controls, and produced engineering improvements that would not normally arise from traditional behavioral observation programs. The results indicate that combining visual work design with reflective learning offers a workable means of surfacing operational variability. Two effects stand out: crews took greater ownership of the learning process, and planned work aligned more closely with work as performed. Since the method draws on routine operations rather than rare events, it appears scalable — though sustaining front-line engagement over longer deployments remains untested.

title: AI-Driven Production Diagnostics for Complex Reservoirs: A Physics-Informed Workflow to Optimize Tight-Gas Carbonate Management
container-title: ADIPEC
c9f942d693539882dd649e01cf008d5dc8f044ac.abstract: Abstract The naturally fractured carbonate reservoirs in North Kuwait Jurassic (NKJ) fields present significant challenges for decline management and production diagnostics. Tight reservoir behavior, high-pressure/high-temperature (HPHT) conditions, frequent operational interventions, and prevalent production data noise complicate traditional decline curve analysis (DCA) and reservoir diagnostics. These factors often lead to misinterpretation of reservoir behavior, suboptimal decision-making, and value erosion. To address these challenges, a novel workflow has been developed to integrate empirical production data, numerical simulation forecasts, and dynamic economic modeling into a unified, physics-informed platform. This workflow enables proactive asset management by rapidly triangulating historical telemetry, simulation outputs, and economic reality, ensuring that decisions are data-driven, consistent, and value-optimized. This study presents a physics-informed workflow for autonomous diagnostics in complex, high-stakes reservoir environments. The objective is to standardize remaining reserves estimation, enhance operational surveillance, and enable proactive, physics-based asset management. The scope includes the integration of empirical production data, numerical simulation forecasts, and dynamic economic modeling into a unified digital platform tailored to the unique challenges of tight-gas decline in the NKJ field and deep, naturally fractured carbonates. The workflow is built on a Python-based open-architecture stack with three core analytical engines: Hybrid Forecasting Engine: Uses competitive algorithms to select between Arps and Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average model (ARIMA) model, filtering operational noise from reservoir data.Physics-Based Reconciliation Module: Integrates numerical simulations with empirical data to detect model discrepanciesActive Surveillance System: Monitors decline rates via log-linear regression, triggering alerts only when decline acceleration correlates with reservoir diagnostics (e.g., water cut, GOR).Generative AI Layer: Translates engineering data into natural-language insights, supporting decision-making without performing mathematical computations. The implementation of this workflow has demonstrated a significant reduction in engineering man-hours required for monthly production decline reviews, with a reported decrease of up to 80%. Key features such as the "Forecast Snapshot" and "Intervention What-If" scenarios provide quantitative insights into the potential value of workovers, identifying candidates where rate uplift could improve net present value (NPV), even in the face of high intervention costs. Alarm-triggered alerts have shown a notable improvement in diagnostic accuracy, with a reduction in false positives by approximately 60%, enhancing the system's reliability in distinguishing between operational and reservoir-driven performance changes. The novelty of this workflow lies in its "Grey Box" approach, uniquely combining rigorous physics reconciliation with a generative AI that translates engineering metrics into actionable narratives. Unlike "Black Box" conventional tools, this system ingests calculated engineering metrics such as b-factors, water cut trends, and forecast deltas, to generate context-aware explanations for underperformance. This hybrid framework addresses the unique challenges of managing tight-gas carbonates decline in the NKJ field, offering a level of interpretability and economic integration rarely found in existing solutions. This workflow represents a transformative step in the digitalization of subsurface workflows. By automating the triangulation of DCA, simulation, and economics, it frees engineers to focus on complex problem-solving, ensuring that asset management decisions are data-driven, consistent, and value-optimized.

title: Identification and Localization of Remaining Mobile Oil in Mature Fields Using Integrated Physics-Based and AI/ML Workflow: A Case Study
container-title: ADIPEC
6d717080f2d06e307423d86c4505addf52db4420.abstract: Abstract Identification and localization of remaining mobile oil are fundamental components of mature-field reservoir management. This task becomes increasingly challenging when large portfolios contain numerous fields, reservoirs, fault blocks, and producing intervals with varying levels of data completeness and subsurface understanding. Conventional field-by-field studies based on detailed static and dynamic reservoir modelling can provide reliable results but require substantial time, data preparation, and technical resources. Consequently, a rapid and consistent screening methodology is required to identify the fields, reservoirs, and well locations that should be prioritized for more detailed subsurface maturation. This paper presents an integrated physics-based and artificial intelligence/machine learning workflow developed for portfolio-scale screening and localization of remaining mobile oil. The methodology follows a sequential two-step approach in which analytical reservoir-engineering methods are applied first to rank fields and reservoirs, followed by production-data-driven AI/ML analysis to identify underperforming wells and localize potential opportunity areas. The automated workflow consists of two main stages: (1) Analytical models: zone/block level Buckley Leverett and recovery factor benchmark screening: each field zone / block production, reservoir, and fluid data are consolidated, quality controlled, and corrected for missing or non-physical values using regional correlations, field averages, and analogue. Remaining mobile oil is then estimated using two independent analytical approaches. The first applies Buckley–Leverett fractional-flow calculations to estimate movable oil after water displacement. The second compares the planned recovery factor, derived from production and booked resources, with a benchmark recovery factor calculated from displacement and sweep-efficiency relationships. The combined results are adjusted for existing production and booked volumes, filtered using a minimum opportunity-volume threshold, and used to rank fields and reservoir zones. (2) AI/ML models: producer-level remaining oil localization: Production histories from the highest-ranked fields are utilized to calculate &gt; 50 well performance indicators such as early-time production, cumulative oil, decline behaviour, water cut, gas-oil ratio, production duration and uptime, etc. Multiple regression-based machine-learning models are trained to predict expected ultimate recovery from well performance indicators. Underperforming wells are identified from the positive difference between ML-predicted and actual well EUR. The calculated gap between predicted by ML and actual well EUR, remaining-production potential, is normalized to the historical performance distribution of infill wells in the field drilled for last years. Each well estimated potential is integrated in bubble maps to evaluate today high water cut, high GOR, and low pressure risks to define and rank remaining-mobile-oil opportunity areas. The methodology was applied to a large mature-field portfolio comprising &gt; 150 fields, &gt; 5000 field–zone–block evaluation areas, and &gt; 3000 well-completion intervals. The analytical screening identified nine fields with the highest additional 2C potential for detailed well-level evaluation. The AI/ML stage subsequently identified high-potential underperforming producers, grouped the well-level potential into reservoir-scale opportunity areas, and supported the identification of "low hanging fruits" (well-reopening, well reactivation) and infill-drilling candidates. Opportunities were further ranked with today high water cut, high GOR, ow reservoir pressure risks, minimum economic-volume thresholds, and wells accessibility. The workflow was validated through comparison with calibrated, history-matched dynamic reservoir models and ongoing field studies remaining mobile oil interpretations. Validation included comparison of the remaining mobile oil location in identified opportunity areas and ranking of the most potential reservoir zones and blocks today. Thus the paper introduces a scalable workflow that combines classical reservoir engineering analytics with AI/ML well-performance screening to accelerate mature-field 2C opportunity maturation and shorten the identification to maturation to execution cycle.

title: Compositional-Data Representations for AI-Enabled Flash Surrogates in Integrated Asset Modeling Workflows
container-title: ADIPEC
c25310f5df2381b845974e03f65986f498aecca6.abstract: Abstract Compositional flash calculations supply phase fractions and liquid and vapor compositions to reservoir, well, separator, and surface-network models. These outputs are closed vectors: their nonnegative parts sum to one. We compare a conventional RAW CatBoost surrogate with a centered log-ratio (CoDA-CLR) formulation for phase-composition prediction. The dataset contains 157,849 states from 500 interpolated feed groups derived from 71 measured fluids. Feed-disjoint partitions contained 350 training, 75 validation, and 75 blind-test groups; no state from a blind feed appeared during fitting. On the blind test, selected CLR reduced mean Aitchison distance from 2.2601 ± 0.0326 to 0.1249 ± 0.0015 for liquid and from 2.4419 ± 0.0472 to 0.1516 ± 0.0018 for vapor relative to projected RAW. The paired feed-group difference was -2.4008, with a 95% interval from -2.9915 to -1.8281, effect size -0.93, and all three seeds agreeing. Projected RAW retained lower component RMSE and Kullback-Leibler divergence. Direct RAW returned a negative part in 17.9% of liquid rows and 23.9% of vapor rows, whereas inverse CLR predictions were positive and closed. CLR is preferred when downstream work depends on component ratios and a valid closed vector; RAW remains stronger for absolute component error.

title: Real-Time Operator Fatigue Detection Using Physics-Informed AI and Standard Camera Infrastructure
container-title: ADIPEC
3d666a8c688f624e211bf1cb3c013af6376ca993.abstract: Abstract This paper presents a real-time physiological fatigue monitoring system for energy facility operators using standard camera hardware. The system applies remote photoplethysmography to extract heart rate and heart rate variability from facial video without wearable sensors. It targets control room personnel, drilling supervisors, and offshore operators. A key objective is equitable detection performance across all skin tones present in multinational energy workforces. A seven-stage Physics-Informed Synthetic Dataset generation pipeline (PISD-rPPG) was developed. Photorealistic operator faces were generated using StyleGAN3 and animated using SadTalker. Physiological signals were synthesized with NeuroKit2 and refined using a diffusion model. Forward Plane-Orthogonal-to-Skin (POS) validation confirmed signal integrity before reverse-POS embedding injected signals at melanin-dependent amplitudes derived from Beer-Lambert absorption physics, producing skin-tone-accurate training data across all six Fitzpatrick classifications. A Temporal Shift Convolutional Attention Network (TSCAN) was pre-trained on the synthetic dataset and evaluated on subjects from the MMPD dataset that were unseen during training. The prototype targets a capture rate of 30 Hz and scores operator fatigue using three personalized physiological thresholds calibrated against individual baselines. The study employed a controlled comparison protocol. TSCAN was pre-trained on 793 synthetic videos generated through the PISD-rPPG pipeline and evaluated against the full MMPD real-world dataset as a cross-domain transfer test, achieving a mean absolute error of 15.7 BPM. This result confirms that physics-informed synthetic data produces signal representations that transfer to real camera footage without any exposure to real training subjects. Under the same protocol, an unrefined physics-based baseline of 80 synthetic videos reached 17.2 BPM. The published SCAMPS reference of 2,800 synthetic videos (McDuff et al., 2022) reports 19.05 BPM under a separately published test configuration. Because dataset size and refinement differ together, that gap is reported as a combined effect and not as the contribution of the diffusion stage alone. Demographic fairness across Fitzpatrick Types III-IV and Types V-VI is an objective of the pipeline design rather than a result of this study, and no per-group figures are claimed, since that evaluation is still under replication. The prototype classifies operator fatigue into three graded states: Normal, Mild Fatigue, and Severe Fatigue, each triggering a corresponding supervisor alert. Status descriptions are generated by a rule-based condition engine requiring no language model. Face detection and cropping occur on the operator device, and no full-frame video is transmitted or stored. No hardware beyond existing facility cameras is required. This paper presents the first application of a physics-informed synthetic training strategy for rPPG-based operator fatigue monitoring in energy facilities. The synthetic pre-training stage addresses demographic bias without requiring real subject data, while the diffusion refinement stage demonstrates that effective domain adaptation requires no real subjects at all. This combination is directly relevant to energy industry deployment contexts where diverse workforces and limited data collection opportunities are practical constraints. One boundary should be read carefully. The accuracy reported here is for heart-rate estimation on benchmark data. Fatigue detection itself has not been validated against a fatigue reference in any operator, and a controlled operator pilot is the next stage of this work.

title: Operational Risks and AI Bias in LLM-Based Agentic Systems for a Process Plant: Electric Motor Operations Case Study (Oil & Gas)
container-title: ADIPEC
d288aab208920da33ee86182452f26d1ab5c51ca.abstract: Abstract The rapid development of Large Language Models (LLMs) has encouraged many industries to explore Agentic AI. Earlier AI tools were used mainly for data analysis and information retrieval. Newer systems can carry out a sequence of related tasks, combine information from several engineering sources and prepare recommendations with relatively limited user input. These capabilities can support document review, procurement quality, maintenance planning, commissioning and operational troubleshooting. However, they also bring risks that are not normally associated with conventional engineering software. Because the output is probabilistic, a recommendation may be influenced by missing technical information, incomplete operating context, biased source material or incorrect interpretation of safety-critical requirements. It may still appear convincing even when its engineering basis is weak. Electric motors are used throughout oil and gas facilities and are essential to the operation of pumps, compressors, fans, cooling systems and other plant equipment. A motor failure can interrupt production and, in some cases, affect the safety or reliability of the wider process. Decisions relating to motor protection, alarms, equipment condition, commissioning, fault diagnosis and maintenance therefore require sound engineering judgement, supported by approved protection settings, operating history, OEM guidance and relevant international standards. This makes electric motors a practical case for examining the use of LLM-based Agentic AI in a safety-critical engineering environment. The paper considers a series of representative motor scenarios covering design review, Factory Acceptance Testing (FAT), commissioning, operational troubleshooting, predictive maintenance, alarm assessment and root cause analysis. The findings show that prediction accuracy and model confidence alone do not establish whether an AI recommendation is safe or technically reliable. That judgement depends on the quality of the available evidence, the completeness of the operating context, compliance with applicable standards and protection philosophy, and verification by a qualified engineer. To manage these risks, the paper introduces the Engineering Trustworthiness Assurance Framework (ETAF). It brings the main checks into one process, starting with the quality of the available engineering information and ending with the approval of the final recommendation. ETAF includes the Engineering AI Assurance Pyramid (EAAP), the Operational AI Risk Propagation Model (OARPM) and the AI Engineering Governance Matrix (AEGM). It also uses three assessment measures: the Engineering Trustworthiness Score (ETS), AI Recommendation Criticality Level (ARCL) and Engineering Confidence Index (ECI). These are proposed as practical, illustrative tools that organisations can adapt when introducing LLM-assisted decision support in safety-critical engineering work. Although the representative scenarios are based on electric motor operations, the proposed framework is applicable to other classes of rotating equipment deployed throughout upstream, midstream, and downstream oil and gas facilities. The paper contributes a practical engineering governance approach that complements existing AI assurance initiatives by emphasizing engineering trustworthiness, protection philosophy, operational accountability, and responsible human oversight during the deployment of Agentic AI systems.

title: Bounded Autonomy: A Budget-Constrained Framework for AI Agent Operations Toward Safety-Critical Process Environments
container-title: ADIPEC
218b63ba23b1023922dbb33dc33f93956e9f5161.abstract: Abstract Tight autonomy budgets improve safety for AI agents in process control with bounded completion cost: the pooled 95% CI for retention is 90.9 to 111.5%, admitting up to 9.1% loss in the worst case but centering on 100.8% (no net cost). For reactive architectures, safety-check rejections drop by 89% and token cost by 85% while completion change is negligible (Cohen's |d| &lt; 0.01). We introduce Bounded Autonomy, a framework that constrains AI agent autonomy along four coordinated dimensions (tool calls, cumulative process perturbation, simulation timesteps, and checkpoint intervals), all calibrated from a single tightness parameter derived from each scenario's estimated optimal action count. Pre-execution middleware, implemented as a LangGraph StateGraph, rejects over-budget actions before they reach the process. Four agent architectures (ReAct, Reflexion, Plan-and-Execute, Hybrid) are evaluated under four budget levels across 20 Continuous Stirred-Tank Reactor (CSTR) scenarios in the OpsEnv benchmark. The evaluation totals over 7,100 experiment cells: 1,680 core Tier 1 cells, 2,800 extended-seed cells, 1,260 cross-model cells, and 1,452 supplementary cells (sensitivity, ablation, rollback, and decoupled experiments). Under tight budgets (1.2× optimal), reactive architectures retain completion (Cohen's |d| &lt; 0.01; Bonferroni-corrected p &gt; 0.05; 95% CI for pooled retention: 90.9 to 111.5%) with 7× wall-time reduction for ReAct and 6.7× for Reflexion. Unconstrained agents take ∼5× more actions than necessary, and these excess actions are counterproductive: in the most pronounced case (scenario B04), a ReAct agent improves from 0.041 to 0.950 completion under budget constraints. Conversely, multi-step optimization tasks (e.g., A04 under ReAct) can lose up to 73 percentage points. Cross-model validation with Qwen 2.5 32B and Llama 3.1 8B (1,260 cells across up to 20 scenarios) confirms the directional violation-reduction effect at reduced magnitude (25% vs. 89% for Tier 1). AI-assisted tools were used in the experimental evaluation; all outputs were reviewed and validated by the authors.

title: Petroleum Target Explorer (PTX-AIM): A Rigorously Validated Machine Learning Framework for TOC Prediction in Frontier Basins, a Case Study from the Kolmani River-2 Well, Gongola Basin, Upper Benue Trough, Nigeria
container-title: ADIPEC
aa9dac26fdfd2770fad5d7469f299436eb7c2c82.abstract: Abstract Objectives/Scope The Kolmani River discovery confirmed a working petroleum system in Nigeria's Gongola Basin (Upper Benue Trough), but too few wells and sampled intervals exist for conventional Total Organic Carbon (TOC) prediction to be reliable. We present PTX-AIM (Petroleum Target Explorer – Artificial Intelligence Machine), an open-source framework that predicts TOC from standard wireline logs and compares machine learning models under leakage-free validation. The objective is to test whether machine learning can outperform the industry-standard Passey ΔlogR method where data are scarce. Methods, Procedures, Process The workflow runs end-to-end: LAS/CSV ingest, IQR cleaning, user-selectable feature selection, scaling, and model selection across five algorithms, with an automated machine learning (AutoML) search over the same library. Evaluation uses spatially blocked validation: contiguous 50-ft depth blocks are held out entirely, so no test interval shares a depth neighbour with the training data. This removes the depth-adjacency leakage that inflates reported ML accuracies on single-well data. Results, Observations, Conclusions Under blocked validation on KR-2, a manually tuned Random Forest performed best (R2 = 0.288, RMSE = 0.261 wt%, MAE = 0.182 wt%). Calibrated Passey ΔlogR returned R2 = 0.138, RMSE = 0.287 wt%, MAE = 0.216 wt%. SHAP attribution identified neutron porosity as the dominant predictor. These figures are deliberately conservative: the skill remaining once leakage is removed, not the inflated R2 a random split yields on 0.25-ft data. For a basin with two to three wells, ML extracts more usable TOC signal from existing logs than ΔlogR. Novel/Additive Information This is a first leakage-controlled ML study of TOC prediction on Nigerian frontier-basin data, treating depth-adjacency leakage as a methodological contribution rather than reporting inflated accuracies. It couples user-driven model selection with a natural-language chatbot, making interpretable analysis accessible without ML expertise, and transfers to other frontier basins.

title: An Integrated Machine Learning and Time-Series Forecasting Framework for Predicting Hydrate Blockage Dynamics in Pipelines
container-title: ADIPEC
bdaa23074346e02c7af0b91019c5b1dd99fa46db.abstract: Abstract Hydrate formation in subsea and multiphase pipeline systems can lead to severe flow restrictions, unstable operating conditions, and complete blockage events, creating significant flow assurance challenges and associated economic risk. Predicting blockage evolution remains difficult because hydrate growth behavior is governed by multiple mechanisms, highly non-linear temporal dynamics, and changing operating conditions. This work presents a physics-guided hybrid machine learning and multivariate time-series forecasting framework for predicting pressure-drop evolution, hydrate progression, and blockage proximity using real field-trial data. The methodology integrates operational metadata with multivariate differential-pressure time-series measurements in a multi-stage predictive workflow. An automated signal-processing approach first identifies sloughing events from differential-pressure behavior and extracts moving-window features representing hydrodynamic and thermodynamic operating conditions. A classification model distinguishes sloughing from non-sloughing cases, while ridge regression estimates blockage-related pressure scaling and expected blockage differential pressure from early-stage pressure signatures and operating conditions. The resulting pressure profiles are normalized to provide a unified representation across different hydrate growth mechanisms. These outputs, together with operating-condition features and pressure history, are incorporated into a conditional Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network to forecast future pressure-drop evolution and blockage timing. The framework effectively captures both gradual monotonic pressure increases and oscillatory trends associated with sloughing behavior. Evaluation on previously unseen field-trial scenarios achieved sloughing-state classification accuracy above 90% and provided reliable blockage differential-pressure estimates while accurately reproducing hydrate growth trajectories and blockage timing. The normalization strategy improves generalization across operating conditions and offers an interpretable indicator of blockage proximity. Overall, the proposed framework combines probabilistic classification, regression-based blockage scaling, and deep sequence learning within a unified, scalable hydrate monitoring system, enabling risk-informed operational decision-making and early warning of hydrate blockage risk.

title: A Novel Self-Breaking Emulsion Diverter for Matrix Acidizing: Lab Experiments, Field Trial, and 1000+ bbl/d Production Lift
container-title: ADIPEC
51ce658406064ccf7a0151b555298f53bae52702.abstract: Abstract Conventional acidizing often worsens water cut due to preferential entry into high-water-saturation zones. Existing diverters such as viscoelastic surfactants, N2, CO2, and foam are costly or require extra equipment. We propose a self-breaking W/O emulsion diverter that temporarily blocks high-permeability zones and automatically cleans up upon acid contact. A novel alkyl polyene polyamine oil-soluble surfactant was developed as emulsifier. The emulsion features a low oil/water ratio ranging from 1:9 to 4:6 and a high viscosity of hundreds of centipoise at a shear rate of 70 s-1. Its viscosity increases exponentially with water cut but drops sharply when meeting crude oil. Most importantly, acid triggers amine-to-ammonium reaction, causing HLB reversal and emulsion breakdown, which ensures easy flowback without formation damage. Parallel dual-core flooding experiments demonstrated the selective plugging capability: for a 27.42–108.48 mD core pair, the high-permeability core experienced a 92.7% permeability reduction while the low-permeability core was reduced by only 14.5%. In an integrated plugging–acidizing experiment (3.4–15.7 mD core pair), the high-permeability core lost 74.5% permeability, whereas the low-permeability core gained 23.5%.Droplet size of 2-4 μm prevents entry into low-permeability zones and ensures stability according to Stokes' law. In a field trial in a 4000 m-deep matrix porous limestone reservoir in Iraq, a new ESP well failed to produce after two acid and solvent treatments, with water cut of 90-100% and highly viscous emulsified produced fluids. After stimulating the lowpermeability oil zone with our emulsion diverter and solvent, the well achieved 1088-1375 bbl/d with water cut reduced to 71-91%. This is a laboratory and field demonstration of a self-breaking oilexternal emulsion diverter for matrix acidizing. The fluid selectively plugs highperm zones, reverses upon acid, and delivers over 1,000 bbl/d production lift in a previously noncommercial well. Detailed application guidelines are provided.

title: AI-Assisted Workover in Mature Oilfields: Enhancing Post-Workover Evaluation Accuracy
container-title: ADIPEC
26fa5a320803e22d4a572912548dade7945c2338.abstract: Abstract Mature oilfields face accelerating production decline, increasing water breakthrough, and escalating mechanical failure frequency. Conventional workover decision-making relies predominantly on empirical judgment and static geological models, resulting in suboptimal candidate selection, elevated re-intervention rates, and marginal economic returns. Workover success rates and return on investment have emerged as critical bottlenecks for economically sustainable production. The paper presents an AI assisted closed-loop solution from reservoir characterization to operational optimization for workover decision-making in mature fields. The methodology combines ensemble-based data assimilation with machine learning diagnostics and multi-objective optimization. Production history and well log data are assimilated using an Ensemble Kalman Filter to update reservoir property distributions and construct a high-fidelity dynamic geological model. A hybrid XGBoost-convolutional neural network architecture processes over 700,000 dynacard images from rod-pumped wells, achieving automated anomaly detection with 95% classification accuracy. Reservoir simulation outputs together with key workover parameters including perforation density and fracture stage length are fed into a multi-objective optimization framework. Validation was conducted in a mature onshore field with over 30 years of production history. Bypassed pay zones identified by the method matched testing data with 86% consistency. After implementing the optimized workover plans, average daily oil production per target well increased by 23% and water cut decreased by 7% points. The proportion of wells requiring no re-intervention within the first post-workover year improved by 17%. The contribution of each module to the overall improvement is analyzed individually: the EnKF update accounts for the majority of the oil-rate gain through more accurate bypassed-pay identification, the dynacard diagnosis drives the improvement in re-intervention-free share by eliminating mechanically unfit candidates, and the NSGA-II optimization is the main driver of the superior return ratio. A feedback loop that returns post-workover evaluation errors to the upstream models reduced rate-prediction error from 16% to 8% in the second cycle, demonstrating that using evaluation accuracy as the feedback variable is the core innovation enabling compounding gains. Compared with purely data-driven models, the physics-guided approach reduced root-mean-square error in reservoir property prediction by 34%.

title: Automating Well-Centric Geomechanics Workflows: AI-Driven Breakout Detection with Domain-Informed Processing for Field Development
container-title: ADIPEC
b1b0b2570f0d7c55a889d58fd8e2a3af463f09cd.abstract: Abstract Borehole breakout interpretation is essential for geological analysis and wellbore stability assessment. Conventional workflows are manual, time-consuming, and difficult to scale across large field development programs. This paper presents an automated breakout detection workflow that combines semantic segmentation with domain-informed post-processing, integrated directly into standard wellbore interpretation software. The workflow was trained on expert interpretations from wells spanning multiple geological settings, acquisition tools, and borehole conditions. Physics-guided post-processing enforces geological constraints including azimuthal symmetry and depth continuity to improve detection reliability and reduce false positives. A dedicated algorithm resolves breakouts that cross image boundaries due to cylindrical flattening, correctly treating split features as single continuous structures. Validation against expert interpretations confirms consistent detection across diverse lithologies and borehole environments. Automated outputs include breakout azimuth, angular width, vertical continuity, and quality indicators, all suitable for direct use in stress analysis and geological modeling. Beyond automated detection, the workflow enables consistent multi-well stress characterization and supports identification of stress orientation variations, mechanically active intervals, and geological domains across field development programs. By reducing interpretation time from hours to minutes while ensuring uniform interpretation criteria across entire well portfolios, the proposed approach provides a scalable and reliable solution for geomechanical analysis, drilling optimization, and development decision-making.

title: Multimodal AI Reconstruction of Petrophysical-Scale Logs from Drill Cuttings and Drilling Data: A Sonic- And Density-Validated Framework Toward Quad-Combo Formation Evaluation
container-title: ADIPEC
93422630040f0d827bae45b7a2d25683c8b5a1d0.abstract: Abstract Objectives/Scope Continuous formation evaluation depends on wireline or logging-while-drilling (LWD) measurements, yet complete suites are often absent due to tool failure, cost, or hole instability. Cuttings, photographs, drilling parameters, and mud-gas are acquired throughout drilling but isolated from logging. This work presents a multimodal AI framework converting these surface measurements into log-scale predictions toward the quad-combo suite—gamma ray (GR), compressional sonic (DT), bulk density (RHOB), and neutron porosity (NPHI)—anchored on validated DT and RHOB benchmarks and completed here with held-out-well, interval-backfill, and missing-modality evaluation. Methods, Procedures, Process X-ray fluorescence (XRF) geochemistry on cuttings is encoded through a multilayer perceptron; cuttings photographs through a ResNet-18 network; and drilling parameters (rate of penetration, weight on bit, rotary speed, and torque), together with total mud-gas records (component chromatography was not consistently available), through a one-dimensional convolutional neural network, alongside a depth/formation covariate branch. Late fusion concatenates the three sensor encoders into a 448-dimensional representation feeding a shared multi-task regression head that predicts DT, RHOB, and NPHI, with GR retained as an auxiliary training target; measured MWD GR is used for final curve-set assembly. Target-specific diagnostic heads were also evaluated; the headline DT result uses the target-specific DT ensemble. Modality dropout supports inference under missing streams. Training and evaluation use 17 Utsira High wells (14 training, 3 held-out blind-test wells) from Norwegian Offshore Directorate/DISKOS data. Results, Observations, Conclusions On Well 16/1-14, adding XRF to drilling features raised within-well DT R2 from 0.59 to 0.98 and cut RMSE from 9.0 to 2.2 µs/ft, identifying XRF as the dominant single-modality contributor in that benchmark. The feature-based multi-well model, trained on 14 wells, achieved R2 = 0.93 (RMSE = 9.97 µs/ft) on blind well 16/1-18. The within-well RHOB benchmark reached R2 = 0.96 (RMSE = 0.028 g/cm3), best of five models. The completed evaluation extends these benchmarks: blind three-well fusion DT reached R2 = 0.858 (RMSE = 11.1 µs/ft), statistically exceeding XRF-only and the equivalent feature-based model (95% confidence intervals excluding zero). RHOB interval backfill reached R2 = 0.646 versus 0.478 for the geological baseline and approximately 0.30 over interpolation. NPHI achieved moderate interval-backfill R2 but did not significantly outperform interpolation and did not transfer reliably across wells; measured MWD GR remained the more reliable final GR source. For preliminary CCS screening, reconstructed DT and RHOB—and, where locally validated, NPHI—together with measured GR could provide formation-evaluation inputs relevant to injectivity, storage-capacity, and seal-integrity assessment in unlogged intervals. Novel/Additive Information The contribution integrates four surface-acquired modalities—XRF cuttings geochemistry, cuttings imagery, drilling parameters, and total mud-gas records—in a late-fusion, multi-task neural model targeting the quad-combo suite. Unlike conventional missing-log workflows that use other logs as predictors, the framework does not require other wireline curves as inputs and can operate where target-log coverage is absent, provided depth/formation context and the surface modalities are available. The completed evaluation demonstrates blind-well DT transfer, RHOB interval backfill, and missing-stream operation, supporting a transparent progression toward deployable quad-combo formation evaluation in legacy, unlogged, or LWD-degraded intervals.

title: AI-Augmented SIL Engineering: Transforming Safety Integrity Level Assessments in Oil and Gas
container-title: ADIPEC
9f0329832aeb1cd6f77781d6f18f296804964855.abstract: Abstract Safety Integrity Level assessment is one of the most specialised and resource-intensive activities in oil and gas engineering. It covers SIL determination through Layer of Protection Analysis, SIL verification through probability of failure calculations, and the documentation needed to satisfy IEC 61511 and company functional safety requirements. In a typical mid-size processing facility, a SIL review can take 6 to 8 weeks, involve 5 to 6 engineers, and require 700 to 1,000 man-hours at an estimated cost of USD 100,000 to USD 150,000. With larger project portfolios and a limited pool of certified functional safety specialists, this traditional approach is becoming difficult to sustain. This paper presents a practical framework for applying artificial intelligence to the preparation, consistency checking and workflow integration parts of SIL engineering while keeping qualified engineers and approved IEC 61511-compliant SIL software as the controlling elements of the calculation process. The proposed AI layer extracts SIF data from project documents, prepares LOPA inputs, checks data consistency, structures assumptions, and interfaces with company-approved IEC 61511-compliant SIL software. The AI layer does not replace these calculation engines. PFDavg, Risk Reduction Factor, architectural constraint and achieved SIL calculations remain within authorised SIL software and are reviewed by competent functional safety personnel. Based on workflow analysis and benchmarking against conventional SIL review practices, the expected benefits include reducing review duration from 6-8 weeks to 2-3 weeks, reducing effort from 700-1,000 man-hours to approximately 350-500 man-hours, and reducing review cost by approximately 50%. These figures are preliminary validation targets derived from workflow analysis. They are not results from a completed pilot and must be confirmed through a controlled pilot before being used as performance claims. The paper also discusses limitations, including incomplete input data, unusual failure modes, software integration boundaries, plant-specific conditions and the need for independent human verification before use.

title: Autonomous LNG Plant Startup Pre-Cooldown: Scaling Secure AI Closed-Loop Automation for Enhanced Production and Carbon Emission Reduction
container-title: ADIPEC
430a33c429116024daa9f813702561b4bf1c2eba.abstract: Abstract The objective of this work is to demonstrate the successful deployment of a secure, AI-driven closed-loop automation system for LNG plant pre-cooldown. The scope encompasses the transition from a data-driven advisory model to a fully autonomous system that executes real-time valve adjustments. It focuses on achieving critical outcomes in enabling autonomous, real-time adjustments through AI-driven recommendations, minimizing startup duration variability, maximizing additional production hours and reducing greenhouse gas emissions through optimized thermodynamic control. The methodology utilized twenty-five years of historical startup data, which was cleaned and profiled to train supervised machine learning models that predict Main Cryogenic Heat Exchanger (MCHE) temperature profiles and valve responses. These predictive models were integrated with an advanced optimization layer to define precise control sequences that satisfy safe operating envelopes. A cyber-resilient IT-OT architecture was engineered, employing network segmentation and protocol gateways to bridge the plant network and the AI engine securely. The process followed a phased validation: initial deployment as a "live advisory" to calibrate model accuracy, followed by the activation of a closed-loop controller that executes autonomous valve adjustments with human-in-the-loop safeguards. The system was successfully deployed across eight LNG train startups at Malaysia LNG plant. Quantitative results confirm a 16% average reduction in pre-cooldown duration compared to the live-advisory baseline. This acceleration directly translates into increased production availability and the reduction of operators' workloads, which allows operators to focus on strategic overview and process safety —enhancing both safety and efficiency. Observations revealed that the closed-loop implementation successfully standardized the pre-cooldown sequence across all eight production runs, delivering near-identical, optimized cooling trajectories. Critically, the tighter control of the Main Cryogenic Heat Exchanger (MCHE) cooling curve led to a 22% reduction in greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions by minimizing flaring events during the transition to stable operations. The study concludes that autonomous closed-loop systems are superior in achieving repeatable, high-efficiency startups. Furthermore, the integration of a secure IT-OT framework addresses the industry's primary barrier to AI adoption: cybersecurity in critical infrastructure. This paper provides a documented case study of an AI system moving beyond "recommendations" into "autonomous execution" in a critical energy facility. It introduces a novel, hybrid methodology combining Supervised Machine Learning with prescriptive optimization logic. This innovation highlights the transformative power of closed-loop, AI-driven automation, reinforcing the organization's leadership in operational excellence and its commitment to setting new standards for industrial processes.

title: From Fragmented Interpretations to an Automated Unified Full-Column Subsurface Framework: Enabling High-Fidelity Subsurface Model and Reliable Horizontal Well Placement, and Agentic AI–Driven Structural Quality Control
container-title: ADIPEC
6bb4ad23235fa2ea3d10f8955280c6cdb168c109.abstract: Abstract Mature carbonate assets with dense well control and stacked reservoir architecture commonly evolve through multiple generations of reservoir-specific structural interpretations. Although each local model may be technically valid within its own reservoir interval, the combination of fragmented interpretations across the full stratigraphic column can introduce structural aliasing, inconsistent fault geometries, horizon overlaps, vertical contradictions, and uncertainty propagation into field-development decisions. These inconsistencies have direct operational consequences: reduced confidence in horizontal well landing, greater uncertainty in target depth, repeated model rework, weaker linkage between static and dynamic models, and avoidable risk during drilling execution. (Salib et al. 2024). Traditional structural modeling methods struggle with time-consuming updates and imprecise well placements within reservoir models. In fact, they are nothing but workarounds to overcome the shortfalls of structure framework algorithms by introducing fake or dummy wells with fake well tops to constrain the structure, resulting in neglected models and potential financial losses and/or missed opportunities. It's crucial to overcome these obstacles for a more reliable reservoir modeling and well placement strategy in the subsurface industry. This paper presents an automated, unified full-column subsurface framework that integrates overburden, faults, horizons, formation tops, well trajectories, reservoir-specific interpretations, uncertainty propagation, and model-governance logic into a single authoritative structural model without using any dummy wells or well tops. The framework combines Bayesian-based Horizon Uncertainty Modeling, referred to in this work as COHIBA, Automated Structural Modeling (ASM), automated surface stacking, embedded validation rules, evergreen model-regeneration practices, and an Agentic AI Structural Quality Control (QC) Assistant. The AI assistant continuously reviews structural surfaces, verifies stratigraphic ordering, detects truncated surfaces, screens well-top mismatches, and provides explainable recommendations to geomodelers within a human-in-the-loop governance process. (Salib et al. 2024; Abrahamsen 2005; Abrahamsen and Benth 2001). Application of the workflow in a congested carbonate field-development setting demonstrated measurable improvements in structural integrity and model-governance efficiency. Automated surface stacking, validation, and reconciliation eliminated 15 identified cross-reservoir structural conflicts and horizon-stacking violations, resulting in a structurally consistent full-column framework. The Agentic AI QC Assistant evaluated 293 wells across 57 modeled reservoir zones within minutes, reducing structural quality-control effort by more than 95% compared with approximately one week of manual review per iteration. In addition, the AI-driven workflow identified and prioritized 25 well-top mismatches requiring expert review, enabling faster model updates, improved structural consistency, and increased confidence in horizontal well planning and multidisciplinary development decisions.

title: AI-Assisted Marine Logistics Digital Twin for Optimizing Dredger, Barge, and Support Vessel Coordination
container-title: ADIPEC
b09a80821043991c06e043a04fda032638702974.abstract: Abstract Marine construction projects may combine several material-transfer methods that must operate as one coordinated production system. In the studied configuration, a self-propelled hopper dredger transports material in its own hopper, a cutter suction dredger delivers slurry through a pipeline, and sand barges handle approximately 20% of the modeled sand volume. These operations also depend on tugboats, a multicat, a fuel barge, a survey boat, rock barges, receiving-area availability, and onshore equipment. Poor coordination between these resources can increase waiting time, interrupt production, and raise fuel consumption. This paper proposes an AI-assisted marine logistics digital twin that maintains an updated virtual representation of vessel status, dredging progress, pipeline condition, weather restrictions, support-resource availability, and island receiving capacity. The AI component consists of two supervised XGBoost models trained, validated, and tested using a physics-informed synthetic dataset developed within published equipment operating ranges and explicit engineering assumptions. A regression model predicts hopper-dredger cycle duration and discharge waiting, while a classification model estimates the probability of a pipeline interruption during the following operating period. These predictions are incorporated into a rolling-horizon decision method that evaluates discharge timing, vessel assignments, sailing speeds, pipeline operating conditions, and support-service windows as the operational state changes. The framework was evaluated through a representative 14-day island-reclamation scenario using paired simulations of predefined rule-based and ML-assisted rolling-horizon coordination. The ML-assisted strategy increased modeled placed sand by approximately 6%, reduced mean hopper-dredger discharge waiting by approximately 83%, and lowered fuel intensity by approximately 10%. It also reduced CSD and pipeline downtime and improved the reliability of meeting the daily production target. These values are simulation-based proof-of-concept results generated under defined engineering assumptions and should be interpreted as a validation pathway for future project-data deployment rather than as measured field performance. The results show that the main value of the digital twin lies in using ML predictions to coordinate dredging, transport, pipeline, support, and receiving activities as one connected operation rather than optimizing individual assets separately.

title: From Broker Calls to Autonomous Chartering: How AI and Real-Time Market Intelligence are Reshaping Offshore Vessel Logistics
container-title: ADIPEC
df6a5f2e9db916cc0ed56d54fcca63a7da33ffa8.abstract: Abstract This paper explores how AI-powered vessel intelligence platforms and agentic systems are reshaping the way offshore energy operators and project managers identify, evaluate and engage with vessel owners. The objective is to demonstrate how consolidating real-time AIS tracking, vessel specifications, market availability and owner contact workflows into a single platform compresses the vessel sourcing cycle and reduces operational uncertainty in offshore logistics planning. The paper draws on the development and deployment of an offshore vessel intelligence platform aggregating data from 30,000+ vessels across 25+ countries, covering vessel specifications, live AIS positioning, ownership data and market availability signals. The methodology documents how agentic AI layers applied to this dataset enable project teams to move from initial vessel search to direct owner engagement within minutes rather than days. Case studies from European offshore wind and EPCI markets illustrate how consolidated market intelligence replaces fragmented, network-dependent sourcing processes with structured, data-driven workflows accessible to any operator regardless of existing broker relationships. The platform approach demonstrates measurable improvements across three dimensions of offshore vessel sourcing. Vessel identification cycles, traditionally dependent on broker networks and manual market canvassing, are reduced from days to minutes when real-time availability, technical specifications and ownership data are consolidated in a single searchable environment. Agentic AI systems enable operators to initiate contact with relevant vessel owners and receive preliminary availability confirmation within the same session, eliminating the sequential delays inherent to conventional brokerage. At the market intelligence level, aggregated fixture data and fleet movement analytics provide project teams with pricing benchmarks and availability forecasts previously accessible only to established brokers.
