title: Prevalence and factors associated with self-medication in Pabna, Bangladesh: An interpretable statistical and machine learning approach
d46a37b50cb393c72af6bd8fd12205034cb33c21.abstract: Abstract Background : Self-medication (SM), the use of medicines without a doctor’s supervision, is common in Bangladesh and other low- and middle-income countries and may cause adverse effects and contribute to antibiotic resistance. Factors associated with SM have mostly been identified with a single analytical method, leaving their consistency across methods underexplored. This study aimed to estimate the prevalence of SM and identify associated factors by comparing several methods within one interpretable framework. Methods : A cross-sectional survey of 421 adults was conducted in Pabna Sadar, Bangladesh. Four methods were applied in parallel to 13 variables and compared at the variable level: chi-square tests, multivariable logistic regression, LASSO stability selection, and SHAP-based importance from machine learning. Nine models were compared by nested cross-validation (CV) and evaluated on a held-out test set. Factors supported by at least two methods were considered associated. Antibiotic SM was examined with multivariable logistic regression. Results : The prevalence of SM in the previous month was 54.2%, and pharmacies were the main source of medicine information (55.7%). Among self-medicators, 39.0% took antibiotics, more often those aged 48 to 58 years than those aged 18 to 28 years. A chronic condition, gender, and education were supported by all four methods, and occupation and awareness of the antibiotic-dairy interaction by two. Respondents with a chronic condition had over four times the adjusted odds of SM (adjusted odds ratio [AOR] 4.36; 95% confidence interval [CI] 2.61 to 7.27), and males had about twice the odds of females (AOR 2.13; 95% CI 1.17 to 3.87). Random forest achieved the highest discrimination (CV AUC 0.818 ± 0.052; test AUC 0.827). Conclusions : SM was common in this setting. The identified factors depended partly on the analytical method, and agreement across methods distinguished robust from method-dependent factors. People with chronic conditions may need particular attention, and the pharmacy counter may be a practical point for intervention, including antibiotic sales. The framework may be applied to other survey-based health studies.

title: A Critical Analysis of AI from the Perspective of the Philosophy of Science among Grade X Students at SMA Don Bosco Padang
container-title: Journal of Multidisciplinary Science: MIKAILALSYS
78e1e5475c4f3b6cf9f26befe44e5548f4ddcce2.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) facilitates access to information in education, increasing the importance of critically evaluating claims and their underlying assumptions. This study examined Grade 10 students’ ability to distinguish facts, opinions, and values in AI-related information at SMA Don Bosco Padang from a philosophy of science perspective. A descriptive quantitative approach was employed involving 33 students. Data were collected through a 15-item written test comprising five items each for fact, opinion, and value identification. Descriptive analysis examined frequencies, percentages of correct responses, score distributions, and classification error patterns. Across 495 responses, 337 were correct and 158 were incorrect, yielding an overall accuracy of 68.08%. Accuracy was highest for opinion identification (76.36%), followed by fact identification (67.88%) and value identification (60.00%). Value identification presented the greatest difficulty, with an error rate of 40.00%. These findings reveal descriptive differences in students’ classification performance, particularly their greater difficulty recognizing values within AI-related information. From a philosophy of science perspective, the results underscore the relevance of epistemology for evaluating evidence and the justification of claims, alongside axiology for recognizing ethical considerations. The study provides contextual evidence to inform AI literacy instruction that integrates information verification, critical reasoning, and ethical reflection to support responsible technology use.

title: INTEGRASI GENERATIVE VIDEO DALAM WORKFLOW PRODUKSI VFX FILM PENDEK “SPLIT//SECOND”
container-title: VOCATIONAL: Jurnal Inovasi Pendidikan Kejuruan
0ec57bf51ada7f1be718f5b1197573476a30b8e0.abstract: The rapid advancement of generative video technology presents novel opportunities for visual effects (VFX) asset generation, yet full reliance on artificial intelligence often creates visual inconsistencies, reduced artistic control, and integration barriers with live-action footage. This article aims to analyze the integration of generative video into the VFX post-production workflow of the short film “SPLIT//SECOND” and evaluate its effectiveness relative to conventional computer-generated imagery (CGI) practices. Employing a practice-based research methodology, the production applied a hybrid workflow where live-action footage serves as the physical reality anchor while artificial intelligence assets construct surreal virtual reality (VR) elements. Empirical results demonstrate that generative video substantially accelerates visual asset acquisition with up to 95% time efficiency, reducing manual tasks from 60–90 minutes to approximately 30 seconds to 3 minutes. Although it eliminates manual modeling labor, this method does not remove the essential requirements of digital compositing, rotoscoping, tracking, and color matching, while also introducing variable operating costs driven by platform credit consumption. ABSTRAK Perkembangan teknologi generative video membuka peluang baru dalam penyediaan aset visual effects (VFX), namun penggunaannya secara mandiri kerap memicu kendala konsistensi visual, penurunan kontrol artistik, dan hambatan integrasi dengan rekaman live-action. Artikel ini bertujuan menganalisis integrasi generative video dalam workflow produksi VFX pada film pendek “SPLIT//SECOND” serta membandingkan efektivitasnya dengan pendekatan computer-generated imagery (CGI) konvensional. Penciptaan karya menerapkan metode practice-based research melalui hybrid workflow yang menempatkan rekaman live-action sebagai jangkar realitas fisik dan elemen berbasis kecerdasan buatan (artificial intelligence / AI) sebagai pembangun dunia virtual reality (VR). Pengujian empiris membuktikan bahwa pemanfaatan generative video mampu mempercepat penyediaan aset visual secara signifikan dengan efisiensi waktu mencapai 95%, yakni dari durasi manual sekitar 60–90 menit menjadi hanya 30 detik hingga 3 menit. Kendati memangkas tahapan teknis permodelan manual, pendekatan ini tidak mengeliminasi kebutuhan digital compositing, rotoscoping, tracking, dan color matching, serta menimbulkan konsekuensi beban biaya variabel berbasis konsumsi credits.

title: Machine learning prediction of hydrogen sorption properties of zirconium-titanium based C14 Laves phase AB 2 alloy from chemical composition
10a682166303ee1182d27d9fa09b4fbca145e9b4.abstract: Abstract Machine learning (ML) models were developed to predict the hydrogen sorp-tion properties of Zr–Ti-based C14 Laves phase AB 2 alloys—unit cell volume (V14), enthalpy of hydrogen absorption (∆H), entropy of hydrogen absorption (∆S), and equilibrium plateau pressure (P eq)—from chemical composition and calculated physical properties. A curated dataset of 244 alloys was compiled from the literature, with two feature categories compared: element atomic percent and properties-based variables (molar mass, bulk density, molar volume, atomic radius ratio, bulk modulus, electron density, B/A ratio). Five ML algorithms (linear regression, random forest, ridge regression, KNN, XGBoost) were trained with 80/20 train–test split, 5-fold cross-validation, and forward feature selection. Element atomic percent features outperformed properties-based features for all target variables. V14 was predicted with the highest accuracy (R 2 up to 0.955 on the test set), while P eq showed moderate accuracy (R 2 up to 0.741) and a notable linear correlation with V14. Prediction of ∆H and ∆S yielded moderate and low accuracies, respectively, highlighting opportunities for more advanced feature engineering. These results demonstrate the potential of ML to accelerate the design of AB 2 hydrogen storage alloys.

title: Deep Reinforcement Learning for Adaptive Temperature Control in Greenhouses: A DQN-Based Framework and Experimental Evaluation
d73b7a5f4b2b57295e6a5e71df3ac19551934c4e.abstract: Abstract The integration of artificial intelligence into controlled environment agriculture represents a transformative opportunity for addressing global food security challenges while promoting sustainable resource utilisation. This paper presents a comprehensive Reinforcement Learning (RL) framework for optimizing greenhouse temperature management, leveraging data from the second edition of the Autonomous Greenhouse Challenge. We formulate the climate control problem as a Markov Decision Process (MDP) and implement a Deep Q-Network (DQN) agent that learns to regulate temperature through discrete actions: heating, cooling, or maintaining the current state. Our methodology incorporates a sophisticated reward function that balances multiple objectives, including maintaining optimal growing conditions, minimizing energy consumption, and ensuring temperature stability. The agent is trained and evaluated on a subset of the 2019 challenge dataset, specifically utilizing measurements from the Reference team's compartment to ensure data consistency and reliability. Experimental results demonstrate that the RL agent effectively learns an adaptive control policy, achieving an average comfort zone occupancy of 40.1\% across diverse starting conditions while demonstrating appropriate action selection based on environmental state. The agent exhibits particularly strong performance when initialised within the optimal temperature range, achieving 100\% comfort zone occupancy in multiple evaluation episodes. This research contributes to the growing body of knowledge on AI-driven agricultural automation by providing a reproducible methodology, comprehensive performance analysis, and insights into the practical challenges of implementing RL systems in real-world greenhouse environments. The findings suggest that RL approaches offer a viable path toward autonomous greenhouse management with potential benefits for crop yield optimization and energy efficiency.

title: AI translation sounds convincing, but it can be riddled with hidden errors
A A Comparative Study of Multimodal Discourse in Micro-Learning Videos via Intersemiotic Complementarity Theory
container-title: English Language Teaching and Linguistics Studies
76a318cbe0fe51eab76a091b29b6d9d03d7fc425.abstract: With the increasing popularity of online educational videos, how to teach and disseminate these videos has become a challenge for many creators. But few of the current studies discussed the intersemiotic complementarity of micro-learning videos and how to promote their effectiveness through this angle. Based on the intersemiotic complementarity theory, this research explores how the collaborative interaction between micro-learning videos’ image and text affects the effectiveness of teaching and dissemination. This study compares and analyzes the image-text relationship of the two videos, Crash Course (CC) and Home Revise (HR) from ideational, interpersonal and compositional intersemiotic complementarity (IC). The study finds that: (1) For ideational IC, both videos use synonymy, collocation and hyponymy, and repetition is often combined with other relationship types to form a composite type. (2) For interpersonal IC, CC uses a lot of demand shots, and the text mood is diverse, so as to build a sense of interaction. (3) For compositional IC, the layout of CC is more flexible. In contrast, the layout of HR is relatively fixed and monotonous. The results of this study show that good ideational IC can reduce the cognitive burden and promote the teaching effectiveness; highly interactive interpersonal IC can improve audience participation; good compositional IC can balance teaching and fun. This study expands the application of intersemiotic complementarity in video analysis, and also provides inspirations for the design and evaluation of micro-learning videos.

title: Consumer Protection in the Digital Economy Era: A Literature Analysis of E-Commerce Regulation in Indonesia
container-title: SKYHAWK : Jurnal Aviasi Indonesia
937ec062869aad0cc56986605e5cdb5b726f0a4b.abstract: The growth of Indonesia’s digital economy has driven a significant transformation in transaction patterns while posing new challenges regarding consumer protection. Although the Consumer Protection Law and Personal Data Protection Law have been passed, they are not considered optimal in responding to the complexity of the digital ecosystem. This research uses a descriptive qualitative approach based on a structured literature review combined with doctrinal legal analysis and thematic synthesis. This study aims to evaluate the effectiveness of consumer protection regulations in e-commerce transactions in Indonesia by examining legal studies, consumer behavior, and international regulatory comparisons through a literature review approach. The study’s results show that regulatory implementation weaknesses, low digital literacy, insufficiently standardized online dispute resolution mechanisms, and institutional enforcement and supervisory gaps remain important obstacles. Additionally, an overly rigid ex-ante regulatory approach has the potential to stifle digital innovation. Therefore, adaptive, participatory policy reformulation based on the principle of equitable consumer protection is needed.

title: GAMES BASED LEARNING DETECTIVE CONFLICT DALAM BIMBINGAN KELOMPOK UNTUK MENINGKATKAN KETERAMPILAN MENGELOLA KONFLIK SISWA SMP
container-title: SECONDARY: Jurnal Inovasi Pendidikan Menengah
47a8059d1f5c7c5be16f215926fe3faa382054b0.abstract: Peer conflict represents a natural facet of adolescent social dynamics that can impair interpersonal relationships if left unmanaged. This study aimed to describe the implementation of group guidance utilizing a games-based learning approach through the Detective Conflict game and to identify differences in conflict management skill scores among seventh-grade students before and after the intervention. A quantitative approach with a pre-experimental one-group pretest-posttest design was employed with eight students of class VII C at SMP Negeri 11 Malang, selected via purposive sampling based on student needs assessment data. Data were gathered through a 40-item conflict management skill scale administered at pre-test and post-test sessions and analyzed using the Wilcoxon signed rank test. The results demonstrated a statistically significant increase in mean scores from 131.75 (SD = 7.03) to 138.88 (SD = 5.38) with Z = −2.457 and p = 0.014, indicating a significant difference in student scores following the intervention. In conclusion, active student participation in the Detective Conflict game exhibits viable potential as an alternative group guidance medium, although the limitations of a single-group pre-experimental design preclude definitive causal claims. ABSTRAK Konflik dengan teman sebaya merupakan bagian wajar dari dinamika interaksi sosial remaja yang dapat memicu kerenggangan relasi sosial apabila tidak dikelola secara konstruktif. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mendeskripsikan keterlaksanaan bimbingan kelompok dengan metode games-based learning melalui permainan Detective Conflict serta mengetahui perbedaan skor keterampilan mengelola konflik siswa kelas VII sebelum dan sesudah perlakuan. Pendekatan kuantitatif dengan desain pre-experimental one-group pretest-posttest diterapkan pada delapan siswa kelas VII C SMP Negeri 11 Malang yang dipilih melalui teknik purposive sampling berdasarkan hasil asesmen kebutuhan. Pengumpulan data menggunakan skala keterampilan mengelola konflik 40 butir pada sesi pre-test dan post-test, kemudian dianalisis menggunakan Wilcoxon signed rank test. Hasil analisis menunjukkan adanya peningkatan skor rata-rata dari 131,75 (SD = 7,03) menjadi 138,88 (SD = 5,38) dengan nilai Z = −2,457 dan signifikansi p = 0,014, yang membuktikan terdapat perbedaan skor yang signifikan setelah pelaksanaan layanan. Simpulannya, keterlibatan aktif siswa dalam permainan Detective Conflict berpotensi menjadi media alternatif bimbingan kelompok, meskipun keterbatasan desain tanpa kelompok kontrol menuntut kehati-hatian dalam menarik kesimpulan kausal langsung.

title: GAMBARAN SELF-EFFICACY PADA PESERTA DIDIK SLOW LEARNER DI SEKOLAH PENYELENGGARA PENDIDIKAN INKLUSIF
container-title: SECONDARY: Jurnal Inovasi Pendidikan Menengah
8921a46be7be87bf00285fe4cac1a9cfc4a6f743.abstract: Slow learner students face distinctive academic challenges requiring extended processing time, instructional repetition, and individualized learning accommodations. These cognitive dynamics are closely related to the development of self-efficacy, specifically students' confidence in their capabilities to accomplish educational demands. This study aims to describe the self-efficacy of slow learner students in an inclusive junior high school based on three dimensions and four primary sources. A qualitative case study design was employed involving two slow learner students in Surabaya identified through official psychological assessments, alongside a school guidance and counseling teacher as a secondary informant. Data were gathered through semi-structured interviews supported by corroborative academic progress reports from the school counselor, followed by interactive data condensation and cross-case analysis. The findings reveal that students' self-efficacy is contextually reflected in task difficulty levels, persistence strength, and subject-matter generality. Furthermore, self-efficacy construction is closely linked to incremental mastery experiences, divergent interpretations of peer performance, perceived meaningfulness of verbal praise, and affective states such as nervousness and embarrassment. ABSTRAK Peserta didik slow learner menghadapi tantangan belajar unik yang menuntut waktu penyerapan materi lebih panjang, repetisi instruksional, serta akomodasi pembelajaran individual. Dinamika kognitif tersebut berkaitan erat dengan pembentukan self-efficacy atau keyakinan peserta didik terhadap kapasitas dirinya dalam menuntaskan tuntutan akademik. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mendeskripsikan self-efficacy peserta didik slow learner di sekolah penyelenggara pendidikan inklusif berdasarkan tiga dimensi dan empat sumber pembentuknya. Pendekatan kualitatif dengan desain studi kasus melibatkan dua peserta didik slow learner jenjang SMP di Kota Surabaya yang diidentifikasi melalui asesmen psikologis resmi, serta satu guru bimbingan dan konseling (BK) sebagai informan sekunder. Pengumpulan data dilakukan melalui wawancara semi-terstruktur mendalam yang didukung oleh verifikasi laporan perkembangan belajar siswa dari guru BK, kemudian dianalisis menggunakan kondensasi data dan analisis lintas kasus. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa keyakinan diri kedua subjek tercermin secara kontekstual pada tingkat kesulitan tugas (level), daya tahan usaha (strength), dan keberagaman mata pelajaran (generality). Selain itu, pembentukan keyakinan tersebut berkaitan dengan pengalaman keberhasilan bertahap, interpretasi terhadap capaian teman sebaya, kebermaknaan pujian guru, serta kecemasan afektif seperti rasa malu dan gugup.

title: HelloTalk as a Digital Communication Space for Korean Language Learning among Indonesian Users: A Qualitative Study
container-title: Jurnal Komunikasi dan Bisnis
42ca5a4036d2f6825577df977fab14b21d30729d.abstract: Digital media have become important communication spaces in which people learn foreign languages beyond formal classrooms. However, research on HelloTalk has largely concentrated on English learners and on pedagogical outcomes such as speaking skills and learner autonomy, and limited attention has been given to how Indonesian users experience HelloTalk as a communication space for learning Korean. This study examines how Indonesian users experience HelloTalk as a digital communication space for Korean language learning, using New Media Theory and Computer-Mediated Communication (CMC) as its analytical framework. A qualitative approach with a post-positivist paradigm was applied. Five Indonesian HelloTalk users who actively learn Korean were selected through purposive sampling. Data were collected through in-depth interviews, observation, and documentation, and analyzed through data reduction, data display, and conclusion drawing, with source and technique triangulation. The findings show that informants experience HelloTalk as an interconnected, accessible, interactive, and open-ended space that enables them to communicate with native speakers, receive peer correction, share content, and learn flexibly across time and place. Within the CMC dimensions, informants emphasized wide access to information, fast message exchange, varied learning input, and motivation, while the perceived usefulness of the application depended on the intensity and purpose of use. Informants also reported constraints related to VIP features, time differences, and device limitations. The study argues that HelloTalk functions as a participatory digital communication space in which Korean language learning takes place through interpersonal interaction, peer correction, and user-generated content. The study does not measure language proficiency.

title: The Application of the Inquiry Learning Model to Enhance Critical Thinking Skills in Science and Social Studies (IPAS) Instruction for Grade III  Students at SD Negeri 3 Kota Mobagu
container-title: International Journal of Educational Research & Social Sciences
070178c4c71681ca5f659e42c59b3321cd362642.abstract: This classroom action research aimed to improve students' critical thinking skills through the Inquiry Learning model in Natural and Social Sciences (IPAS) lessons on heat energy sources in Grade III at SD Negeri 3 Kotamobagu. The study was conducted in two cycles with 29 students, each cycle consisting of planning, action, observation, and reflection. Data were collected through an essay test based on five of Ennis' critical thinking indicators (Focus, Reason, Inference, Situation, Clarity) and through observation of teacher and student activities. In Cycle I, the mean critical thinking score was 58.10, with classical mastery (minimum category Good, score ≥ 60) of 51.72%; student activity was 66.25% and teacher activity was 71.43%, both in the Good category. After improvements in Cycle II, namely stronger teacher guidance, guiding questions, and greater student involvement in inquiry activities, the mean score rose to 77.76 with classical mastery of 93.10%; student activity increased to 88.75% and teacher activity to 91.96%, both in the Very Good category. Based on the school's learning objective achievement criterion (score ≥ 75), classical mastery rose from 24.14% to 72.41%, which is still below the 75% target. These results indicate an improvement in students' critical thinking after the implementation of the Inquiry Learning model.

title: A Smart Insole-Based Explainable AI Framework for Non-Invasive Sciatica Diagnosis Using Optimally Selected Plantar Force Sensors
44867e825acf1cdcc9b18ad253e5851e1983b666.abstract: Abstract Sciatica is a neuropathic disorder that can cause significant alterations in lower-limb biomechanics, including gait asymmetry and abnormal plantar force distribution. This study proposes a wearable, explainable artificial intelligence (XAI)-based framework for automated sciatica diagnosis using optimally selected force-sensitive resistor (FSR) sensors integrated into a smart insole. A dataset of 37 subjects, comprising 20 patients with Sciatica and 17 healthy subjects, was acquired using 16 FSR sensors, with eight sensors positioned on each foot, along with concurrent electromyography (EMG) and inertial measurement unit (IMU) data. From the bilateral plantar force signals, 601 biomechanical features were extracted, incorporating statistical, temporal, magnitude, and inter-limb asymmetry characteristics. A K-fold combinatorial sensor-selection strategy identified the optimal sensor configuration, with K = 5 providing the most stable performance. The optimal configurations, L2, L5, L8 for the left foot and R2, R5, R8 for the right foot, reduced the number of sensors from 16 to 6, representing a 62.5% reduction in sensing hardware. The selected left-foot sensors achieved 96% accuracy, 96% precision, 93% recall, 94% F1-score, and 0.93 AUC, while the right-foot sensors achieved 87% accuracy, 83% precision, 76% recall, 79% F1-score, and 0.91 AUC. Using the six optimally selected sensors, the proposed one-dimensional convolutional neural network (1D-CNN) achieved 90.3% classification accuracy, 89.9% sensitivity, 90.3% specificity, and a ROC-AUC of 0.911. Furthermore, XAI-based plantar heatmaps confirmed the contribution of the selected biomechanical regions to the classification decision. Cross-validation against the concurrent EMG/IMU modality achieved 85.2% accuracy, with approximately 81.5% diagnostic agreement between the force-sensor and EMG/IMU models. The quantitative results demonstrate that a substantially reduced FSR sensor configuration can preserve diagnostically relevant biomechanical information while providing accurate, interpretable, and portable sciatica screening. The proposed framework offers potential for low-cost wearable gait assessment and automated clinical decision support.

title: Arbitrary-Scale Light Field Super-Resolution via Spatio-Angular Consistent Neural Epipolar Geometry Learning
944eef59fbee9a2711198609e7bf93f5bddbde89.abstract: Abstract Light field imaging, a promising technology in computer vision, captures both spatial and angular information of light rays. However, the inherent trade-off between spatial and angular resolution limits its applications. This paper introduces a novel spatio-angular consistent local neural epipolar geometry learning framework for arbitrary-scale light field super-resolution. By modelling light field epipolar plane images (EPIs) as continuous local implicit geometry functions, our approach enables simultaneous super-resolution across both angular and spatial domains. Experimental results on synthetic and real-world datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our model, achieving high geometric structure fidelity under arbitrary upscaling factors.

title: PENERAPAN MODEL PROJECT BASED LEARNING (PjBL)  UNTUK MENINGKATKAN HASIL BELAJAR IPAS  SISWA KELAS III UPTD SDN 071030 AFIA
container-title: STRATEGY : Jurnal Inovasi Strategi dan Model Pembelajaran
823691802aa3e64c0bbfa43ba95bf7589e8c387b.abstract: Learning outcomes are one of the indicators of the success of the learning process. However, the IPAS learning outcomes of third-grade students at UPTD SDN 071030 Afia are still relatively low, necessitating a learning model that can improve student learning outcomes. This study aims to improve the IPAS learning outcomes of third-grade students at UPTD SDN 071030 Afia through the implementation of the Project-Based Learning (PjBL) model. The research design used was Classroom Action Research (CAR), conducted in two cycles. Each cycle consisted of the planning, implementation, observation, and reflection stages. The research subjects were 20 third-grade students at UPTD SDN 071030 Afia. Data collection techniques included tests, observations, and documentation. The data were analyzed both quantitatively and qualitatively. The results showed that students’ IPAS learning outcomes in the pre-cycle stage were 30%, then increased to 60% in Cycle I, and rose further to 85% in Cycle II. Based on the research results, it can be concluded that the Project-Based Learning (PjBL) model is effective in improving the IPAS learning outcomes of third-grade students at UPTD SDN 071030 Afia.

title: Human-AI Collaboration in Urban Digital Transformation: Balancing Efficiency and Human Values in Shanghai’s AI-Enabled Talent Recruitment
container-title: Digital Technologies Research and Applications
99b2a4d2edc2dc8df689bff6b515848affbe723a.abstract: In the context of the urban digital revolution, recruitment through AI technologies has become common practice to address competition in the labor market. However, it is still unclear how the effectiveness of such recruitment is connected with humanistic values. For this research, an exploratory qualitative research design was used, involving semi-structured interviews with eight human resource professionals in Shanghai. Based on the results, the use of AI in recruitment led to increased efficiency mainly when screening candidates through high-volume, standardized processes, although the promised efficiency was not delivered in practice because the introduction of the AI system increased the workload. Patterns of human-machine cooperation were observed in different companies: tech companies and foreign companies are inclined to adopt interactive adjustment approaches, while state-owned enterprises retain human-dominated decision-making. Transparency of algorithms was still lacking in numerous instances, and there was an asymmetry in the accountability framework of algorithms, wherein disobeying algorithms carries more personal consequences than obeying them. The more experienced professionals became more autonomous in their work, while the less experienced professionals depended more on the algorithm. Issues like management support, information accuracy, and departmental integration have a major impact on implementation. This study contributes to the theory of human-machine collaboration by proposing the concept of asymmetric algorithmic accountability, which captures the uneven distribution of organizational consequences for following versus overriding AI recommendations and shapes practitioner behavior in ways that extend beyond individual trust or algorithmic transparency.

title: Project Cost Estimation Based on BIM and Deep Learning
8cfbc1ee91ed917b9d8704ac92ac09a29f2ca60a.abstract: Abstract The accuracy of project cost estimation directly affects the effectiveness of construction management, and the nonlinear fluctuation of material prices is a major source of estimation bias. To address this issue, this paper proposes a dynamic cost estimation framework that couples 5D quantities extracted from building information modeling (BIM) with a grey BP neural network optimised by the sparrow search algorithm (SSA‑PGNN) for material price forecasting. Unlike traditional static approaches, the framework introduces a bidirectional event‑driven data interface and a dual‑threshold feedback mechanism that support dynamic updating of cost estimates and proactive risk immunisation. Using data from 62 real construction projects in Liaoning Province, China (2016–2021), material quantities are extracted from BIM models and monthly material prices are forecast by the SSA‑PGNN model. The proposed model achieves a mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) of 2.43%–4.04% for material prices and 2.9% for total project cost under leave‑one‑project‑out cross‑validation, outperforming the PGNN, SSA‑BP, XGBoost, random forest and LSTM benchmarks (p < 0.05) within the present dataset. Time‑series rolling validation, a synthetic extreme‑shock stress test and statistical hypothesis testing support the stability and robustness of the proposed method; however, as the evidence derives from a single regional dataset, external validation beyond the study region remains an essential next step.

title: From AI readiness to regenerative tourism orientation: a tourist-centric model of smart tourism villages
container-title: ABAC Journal
600067ed573dc780c1bd155c47ed81d59d2f7b38.abstract: Purpose This study develops and validates a tourist-centric model of AI-driven smart tourism villages (AI-DSTV), explaining how perceived digital infrastructure and smart governance relate to tourist acceptance and perceived regenerative tourism orientation (PRTO) through rural authenticity, value co-creation, AI trust, and perceived service value. Design/methodology/approach A cross-sectional survey involved 686 domestic tourists who had experienced an AI-supported tourism touchpoint in rural tourism settings in Indonesia. The sample was predominantly young and digitally engaged, with 75.1% aged 18–24 and 68.4% students. The model was tested using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) with 10,000 bootstrap resamples and importance-performance map analysis (IPMA). Findings All 12 hypothesized relationships were significant. Rural authenticity strongly enhanced perceived AI service value, while tourist value co-creation strengthened AI trust and ethical acceptance. Digital infrastructure and smart governance also showed significant downstream effects through authenticity–service-value and co-creation–trust pathways. The model explained 56.3% of PRTO variance. IPMA identified AI trust and ethical acceptance as the most important antecedent of PRTO and the lowest-performing construct, indicating a key managerial priority. Practical implications Rural destinations should prioritize transparent, culturally grounded, participatory and locally accountable AI systems. Strengthening ethical trust, co-creation, and culturally appropriate personalization may offer greater managerial leverage than technological sophistication alone. Originality/value The study extends technology-adoption research beyond behavioral acceptance by introducing PRTO as a tourist-level psychological outcome. It conceptualizes AI-DSTV as a socio-technical ecosystem linking destination readiness with authenticity, co-creation, trust and service evaluation while distinguishing regenerative orientation from verified destination regeneration.

title: Linking green entrepreneurship to green innovation: the mediating role of green entrepreneurial self-efficacy
container-title: African Journal of Economic and Management Studies
56d99d620c7bd84d2c10aab08611ed68af39c4be.abstract: Purpose In line with the United Nations 2030 Agenda, environmental sustainability has become a prominent concept in academic discourse. Due to its vast natural resources, Africa is well-positioned to become a global leader in green business. However, with a growing small and medium-sized enterprise (SME)population in Africa, empirical evidence on SME sustainability efforts remains limited. For this reason, this research examined the mediation effect of green entrepreneurial self-efficacy on the relationship between green entrepreneurship and green innovation in Zimbabwean manufacturing SMEs. Design/methodology/approach The data were analysed using SmartPLS 4 from a randomly selected sample of 370 managers. Findings The results showed that while green entrepreneurship strongly influenced green innovation, green entrepreneurial self-efficacy partially mediated the relationship between the two variables. Originality/value The study contributes context-specific evidence from an African economy, addressing the limited representation of developing markets in green innovation research. In environments characterised by institutional constraints and resource scarcity, identifying self-efficacy as an enabling mechanism provides novel insight into how firms can stimulate green innovation despite structural limitations. The findings, therefore, enrich both theory and practice by integrating strategic and psychological perspectives within the African economic context.

title: Learning from Abroad? Citizen Preferences for International Policy Models
56d07bb1a27aec15e81eaf94b515d82b2abe418d.abstract: Politicians and policy professionals frequently refer to successful examples abroad to justify and promote policy reforms, making international comparisons central to policy debates. Yet we know little about which countries citizens prefer their own country to learn from, and whether information about policy performance changes those preferences. We study these questions using a cross-national survey in six countries in which respondents repeatedly choose between pairs of countries as policy models for the economy, immigration, and climate change. To identify the causal effect of performance information, we embed a randomized experiment in which half see country names only, while the other half also see issue-specific performance rankings. Citizens favor well-governed and affluent countries as policy models. Performance information shifts preferences toward better-performing countries, especially for the economy, with smaller effects for immigration and climate change. These findings contribute to understanding the micro-foundations of international policy learning.

title: Effect of Peer Support on Resilience and Emotional Regulation among University Students: Mediating Role of Stress Management
container-title: Pakistan Journal of Positive Psychology
53ce23fed5f142af05f503c93a58c00782a943b3.abstract: This current study was carried out to analyze the impact of peer support on resilience and emotional regulation in university students considering the mediating influence of stress management. Quantitative correlational research approach with a convenient sampling technique was used for the current study. Information was gathered from 150 university students of Pakistan (n = 81 males and n = 69 females) with ages between 18-27 years using standardized measures: Friend subscale of the multidimensional scale of perceived social support (MSPSS), perceived stress scale (PSS-10), brief resilience scale (BRS), and emotional regulation questionnaire (ERQ). Pearson correlation, regression analysis and mediation analysis using bootstrapping approach was performed. It was found that peer support had a significant positive effect on emotional regulation (B = .34, p < .001), however, its direct effect on resilience was not significant. Most importantly, stress management partially mediated the link between peer support and resilience (B = .39, p < .05) as well as emotional regulation (B = .32, p < .05). The current study underscores the important significance of peer support network along with stress management interventions in enhancing psychological well-being of university students.

title: Generative Inverse Design of Shell Metamaterials through Continuous-Latent Conditional Flow Matching
29d4141b48d61843e953cf6048d027f8417e5f4f.abstract: Abstract Mechanical metamaterials derive programmable properties from a repeated unit cell’s geometry. A stress–strain curve summarizesa three-dimensional shell geometry in a few numbers, so distinct geometries can share a curve and the inversemap from curve to geometry is one-to-many. We develop a continuous-latent conditional flow-matching framework thatdesigns periodic shell unit cells for prescribed compressive responses. Each shell geometry is a continuous periodic function,and a function encoder learns a basis that compresses it into 32 coefficients. Conditional flow matching learns theresponse-conditioned coefficient distribution and generates many candidate geometries. On 200 held-out targets, our 5.9-million-parameter model reaches a mean best-of-20 NRMSE of 0.074 at 73% validity, against 0.118 and 48% for a 40-million-parameter tokenized-diffusion baseline. Sampling requires 26.8 ms per candidate versus 2.03 s for the baseline.Finite-element analysis of 981 shortlisted candidates yields a mean best-design NRMSE of 0.092, compared with a simulationto-simulation reproducibility of 0.016–0.063.

title: Group Counseling Using Symbolic Modeling Techniques to Enhance Students’ Self-Efficacy in  Continuing Their Education
container-title: Berkala Ilmiah Pendidikan
a820e65ff2860c704b9f134305cc1ce09c076c25.abstract: Low self-efficacy in continuing education to higher education requires appropriate guidance and counseling services. This study examined the effectiveness of group guidance using the symbolic modeling technique in improving students' self-efficacy in continuing education. A quantitative quasi-experimental pretest-posttest control group design was used. The sample consisted of 24 twelfth-grade students of SMA Negeri 2 Sutera Padang, Indonesia, prioritizing those with low self-efficacy, selected through purposive sampling and divided into experimental (n = 12) and control (n = 12) groups. Data were collected with a Likert-scale self-efficacy questionnaire and analyzed using the Wilcoxon Signed Ranks Test, Mann-Whitney U test, and N-Gain with SPSS 25.0. The experimental group's average score increased from 93.8 (moderate) to 133 (very high) with Asymp. Sig. 0.002, while the control group increased from 95.3 to 106 with Asymp. Sig. 0.003. The Mann-Whitney U test showed a significant posttest difference between groups (Asymp. Sig. 0.002), with an average N-Gain of 70% (moderately effective) for the experimental group, far higher than the control group's 13% (ineffective). Group guidance using the symbolic modeling technique is effective in improving students' self-efficacy in continuing education. The findings imply that vicarious experience through symbolic media can strengthen students' confidence in planning further education. Guidance and counseling teachers are advised to apply this technique in a programmed manner, particularly for students with low self-efficacy, and schools are encouraged to include it in guidance programs for final-year students.

title: HUBUNGAN SELF EFFICACY DENGAN KEPATUHAN MINUM OBAT PADA PASIEN HIPERTENSI DI RSUD KABUPATEN TANGERANG
container-title: JHN: Journal of Health and Nursing
d21b09f4464d67d976375a0b3ced7b997a8f8aaa.abstract: Hypertension is a non-communicable disease that remains a major global health issue. Successful blood pressure control in hypertensive patients largely depends on medication adherence, and one of the psychological factors influencing this adherence is self efficacy. This study aimed to determine the relationship between self efficacy and medication adherence among hypertensive patients at the Tangerang District Regional General Hospital (RSUD Kabupaten Tangerang). A quantitative, analytical, correlational research design with a cross-sectional approach was employed. The sample consisted of 207 respondents selected using a purposive sampling technique. Self efficacy was measured using the Medication Adherence Self Efficacy Scale – Revised (MASES-R), while medication adherence was assessed using the 8-item Morisky Medication Adherence Scale (MMAS-8). Data were analyzed using the chi-square test. The results showed that the majority of respondents possessed high self efficacy (79.7%) and were adherent to their medication (63.8%). The chi-square test revealed a significant relationship between self efficacy and medication adherence (p < 0.001), with an Odds Ratio (OR) of 7.750 (95% CI: 3.590–16.731). This indicates that patients with high self efficacy are 7.75 times more likely to be adherent to their medication compared to those with low self efficacy. Therefore, this study demonstrates a significant association between self efficacy and medication adherence among hypertensive patients at the Tangerang District Regional General Hospital.

container-title: Journal for Nurses in Professional Development
6060236358d8ef690ce890cac6d34968314533a7.abstract: New graduate pediatric direct care registered nurses (PDCRNs) may be at risk for unsuccessful transition to practice because of fewer pediatric educational experiences as students. In this cross-sectional observational study, perceptions of transition to practice among new graduate PDCRNs ( N =50) were examined. Findings indicate that supporting PDCRNs in transition to practice after graduation may help increase successful transition to practice of new graduate acute care pediatric RNs.

title: Discrete Memoryless Channel Capacity Estimation using Deep Learning and 256QAM
b38c357b495251d1b341dce82be672f81bc1f82e.abstract: Abstract Channel capacity should be accurately estimated to design effective communication systems particularly in high-order modulation settings. In this paper, a deep learning-trained structure of the capacity estimation of discrete memoryless channels (DMCs) in the context of 256-Quadrature Amplitude Modulation (256QAM) is introduced. The presented approach is built upon Deep neural networks (DNNs) to train capacity directly based on input-output information, which is contrary to the classical methods like the Blahut-Arimoto algorithm which are both computationally intensive and depend on channel complexity. The simulation findings indicate that the CNN model has the capacity estimates that are close to the theoretical ones with low root mean square error (RMSE) and mean absolute error (MAE) at different signal-to-noise ratios (SNRs). The DNN-based capacity estimator takes 0.043 s (76% fast) to execute a test sample, which is much lower than the average execution time of the Blahut Arimoto algorithm of 0.184 s per SNR point, showing that the proposed approach is computationally efficient. The model is also more scalable and converges faster and hence can be used in real time applications. The article fits into the intersectional area of information theory and artificial intelligence, providing a viable and scalable capacity estimation methodology in next-generation wireless networks.

title: High Use, Low Preparation
container-title: American Journal of Physical Medicine & Rehabilitation
cd596e36835769e8c758e2939412febb985e5034.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (Gen-AI) has rapidly entered clinical environments, posing a risk of “cognitive offloading” that may impede the development of independent clinical judgment. This study conducted a cross-sectional survey of residents, fellows, and faculty at a large academic medical center in January 2026 to quantify Gen-AI utilization and perceptions in physical medicine and rehabilitation (PM&R) to inform curriculum development. Thirty-six trainees (95% response rate) and 11 faculty members (30% response rate) completed the survey; 43 (91.5%) reported any Gen-AI use and formed the analytic sample. Among users, 72.1% used Gen-AI daily for clinical learning and 51.2% during patient encounters, yet 67.4% were self-taught and only 7.0% always requested citations. Trainees requested citations more often than faculty ( P =.048), while faculty more often relied on clinical judgment without additional verification (62.5% vs. 25.7%, P =.089). Gen-AI-derived evidence was rarely surfaced in teaching: 60.5% discussed it during case presentations rarely or never, and only 16.2% always disclosed its origin. Residents are integrating Gen-AI into clinical workflows at rates that outpace faculty familiarity, while verification remains largely undiscussed and untaught. These gaps highlight an urgent need for structured Gen-AI curricula in PM&R residency.

title: Does the Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation Self-Assessment Examination for Residents Predict the Chances of Passing the Part 1 Board Certification Examination? An Update
container-title: American Journal of Physical Medicine & Rehabilitation
b899f73e35a32558c5a77b1fe1389909320e56de.abstract: Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation (PM&R) residents take the Self-Assessment Exam for Residents (SAE-R) offered by the American Academy of Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation (AAPM&R). The SAE-R is used by residency programs to assess resident knowledge and by residents in preparation for the American Board of Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation Certification Examination (ABPMR-CE) Part I. In 2017, Massagli’s, “Does the Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation Self-Assessment Examination for Residents Predict the Chances of Passing the Part I Board Certification Examination?”, provided data linking performance on the SAE-R with ABPMR-CE Part I passage rate. The objective of this study was to reinvestigate the predictive value of the SAE-R performance on ABPMR-CE Part I with an increased data set from 2015 to 2024. Probability models were developed that predicted passing for PGY-4 SAE-R test takers, in three criterion-referenced score groups: Failing, Just Passing, and Comfortably Passing. The highest Youden Index indicated SAE-R score of 105 as the optimal cut-point and was associated with a 9.2% (95% CI 0.370, 0.465) chance of failing the ABPMR-CE Part I. The SAE-R remains a useful tool in assessing likelihood of passing ABPMR-CE Part I; however, correlations between SAE-R and ABPMR-CE Part I scores were lower than reported previously.

title: Perceived environmental responsibility, green brand image, and green trust: asymmetric moderating roles of green self-concept consistency and green skepticism among electric-motorcycle users
container-title: F1000Research
798347fd4cdb8b8a4c49ff160a4e9f0b24394598.abstract: Background Perceived Environmental Corporate Social Responsibility (ECSR) signals environmental priorities, but consumers may interpret this signal differently when judging brand image and trust. We examine how green skepticism and green self-concept consistency (GSCC) moderate these associations among electric-motorcycle users. Methods A cross-sectional survey was conducted from 29/06/2026 to 28/07/2026, following the institutional ethical clearance issued on 25 June 2026, among 502 consenting adult electric-motorcycle owners or active users in Greater Jakarta, Indonesia, recruited through purposive sampling. Six focal associations specified in the broader research framework were reported from SmartPLS 4 estimates using 5,000 bootstrap subsamples, two-tailed tests, and a 5% significance level. Separate composite-score analyses served as robustness checks. Results Perceived ECSR was positively associated with green brand image (β = 0.353, t = 9.363, p < 0.001) and green trust (β = 0.287, t = 7.030, p < 0.001); green brand image was associated with green trust (β = 0.319, t = 6.959, p < 0.001). Green skepticism weakened the ECSR–trust association (β = −0.125, p = 0.011). GSCC weakened the direct ECSR–trust association (β = −0.118, p = 0.002) but strengthened the ECSR–image association (β = 0.141, p < 0.001). The supplementary indirect ECSR → green brand image → green trust association was positive (β = 0.113, p < 0.001). Conclusions Perceived ECSR is associated with two distinguishable outcomes: environmental brand meaning and relational credibility. Identity fit shows opposing moderation patterns for image and direct trust, while skepticism weakens the direct trust association. The cross-sectional design does not establish causal or temporal effects.

title: Development of an Integrated Aided Language Stimulation (ALS) Intervention Model to Improve Expressive Communication in Autistic Children at UPTD Disability Services Sidoarjo
container-title: Journal of General Education and Humanities
b7b0d11d53ab60f86fec6738c0cba48871fcc2a1.abstract: Children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) often experience difficulties in expressive communication, including requesting, responding, expressing needs, initiating interaction, and maintaining communication. This study aimed to develop an Intervention Model Integrated Aided Language Stimulation (ALS) with Augmentative and Alternative Communication (AAC) to support expressive communication among autistic children at UPTD Services Disability Sidoarjo, Indonesia. The study employed a Research and Development approach using the Four-D model comprising Define, Design, Develop, and Disseminate stages. The developed model integrated AAC media, ALS language modeling, functional communication activities, communication opportunities, partner responsiveness, reinforcement, generalization, and evaluation. Expert validation involved four validators representing four areas of expertise: subject matter, special education/autism, communication/AAC, and media. The validation percentage was calculated by dividing the obtained score by the maximum possible score and multiplying by 100%, resulting in 90.5% (very valid). Practicality was assessed through responses from teachers, therapists, and/or companions using the same percentage formula, resulting in 90% (very practical), while implementation was assessed through structured observation and reached 91% (very good). A one-group pretest-posttest limited trial involving five autistic children showed an increase in expressive communication scores from 42/100 (mean = 4.2) to 76/100 (mean = 7.6). The mean N-Gain was 0.65, categorized as moderate improvement according to the study criteria. Because the limited trial involved only five children and did not include a control group, the observed improvement should not be interpreted as definitive evidence of intervention effectiveness. Overall, the findings support the model’s feasibility for further investigation with larger samples and more rigorous comparative designs.

title: Effectiveness of Behavioural Intervention Regarding Anaemia and Its Prevention among Postnatal Mothers: An Interventional Study
12fe6a2e92fb5e2910df896caf3494d377c35d3c.abstract: Abstract Anaemia is a public-health concern that may persist after childbirth and affect maternal recovery and well-being. This study assessed the effectiveness of a behavioural intervention regarding anaemia and its prevention among postnatal mothers. A quantitative approach and quasi-experimental one-group pre-test–post-test design were used in the postnatal unit of Jalpaiguri Government Medical College and Hospital, West Bengal. Of 83 mothers initially enrolled/interviewed, 55 postnatal mothers with haemoglobin below 11 g/dL were included in the final analysis. Knowledge was assessed before and after structured teaching, and haemoglobin was reassessed 30–42 days after delivery. The mean knowledge score increased from 15.45 (SD 3.37) to 19.69 (SD 1.76), with a statistically significant difference (paired t=8.27, df=54, p<0.001). Mean haemoglobin increased from 9.55 (SD 0.98) g/dL at first contact to 10.72 (SD 0.75) g/dL at follow-up (paired t=10.444, df=54, p<0.001). At follow-up, 25 mothers (45.45%) had haemoglobin levels of at least 11 g/dL. The findings indicate improved knowledge and haemoglobin levels between baseline and follow-up. Because the study had no control group, the haemoglobin change cannot be attributed to the intervention alone. Structured teaching may support postnatal care alongside appropriate treatment, nutrition and follow-up.

title: Implementing lesson study as teacher professional development in English schools: exploring the role of the leader through an implementation science lens
container-title: International Journal for Lesson & Learning Studies
9aef26d4cc20c3343f26dc0562529063a658efd0.abstract: Purpose Lesson study (LS) is a Japanese teacher professional development (PD) approach which has been adopted globally to emulate Japan's high student achievement. In Japan, three leadership roles ensure the high-quality implementation of LS: a school Research Steering Committee, in-school facilitators and external experts. Teachers can develop leadership expertise through their participation in LS. This study uses implementation science as a framework to investigate leadership functions that enabled and hindered LS implementation in English schools that voluntarily adopted LS, frequently without funding, policy guidance or systemic opportunities for LS leadership development. Design/methodology/approach This study uses a case study methodology, exploring data from six purposefully recruited schools that implemented and used LS for at least two years, four of which subsequently abandoned it. We analysed interview data from LS leaders and participants, alongside documents detailing LS policy and practice, to assess the extent to which leaders fulfilled the three Japanese leadership roles and to reveal the characteristics and behaviours of implementation leaders. Findings What distinguishes sustained from abandoned cases is the propensity of LS leaders to “champion” LS. These knowledgeable yet humble leaders led implementation with passion, solved problems, allocated funding and resources, developed other champions and ensured that the responsibilities of the three Japanese roles were undertaken. Originality/value Despite the considerable use of LS beyond Japan, this study is one of only a few that provide an overview of leadership functions supporting school-based LS implementation in international contexts.
