Digital health misinformation in Southeast Asia: a systematic review of susceptibility, public health consequences, and intervention evidence
container-title: Frontiers in Public Health
1c958c1db51f20b8c7d600471373d90ab013a16b.abstract: Background Digital health misinformation forms part of the information environment in which people assess health risks and act on health advice. We systematically reviewed participant-level studies from Southeast Asia addressing susceptibility, public-health consequences, and intervention evidence. Methods We searched PubMed, Europe PMC, Web of Science Core Collection, and Scopus, supplemented by known reports from the original manuscript and publication-version checks. Prespecified eligibility criteria required primary empirical research involving Southeast Asian populations, an explicit health-misinformation focus, a documented digital connection, and participant-level outcomes. The search and selection process was reported according to PRISMA 2020. Methodological quality was assessed using the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool (MMAT 2018). Heterogeneity in study designs, measures, and outcomes precluded meta-analysis; findings were synthesized narratively. Results The searches identified 2,210 database records; 1,142 remained after deduplication. Including supplementary identification, 282 reports were sought, 147 were assessed in full text, and 77 reports were included, representing 74 conservatively grouped study populations. Country-attributable evidence came from Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, the Philippines, Thailand, Vietnam, and Lao PDR; two further reports provided regional findings. Fifty-four reports concerned COVID-19. Appraisal and belief were associated with cognition, literacy, trust, identity, emotion, and social context, although measures and sampling differed considerably. Findings linked misinformation-related constructs with sharing, vaccine attitudes, preventive behavior, distress, and accounts of delayed care. Correction, inoculation, digital education, chatbots, and community responses produced heterogeneous findings; most interventions did not isolate a misinformation-specific behavioral effect. Discussion Interpretation is limited by 135 unretrieved reports, a single assessment workflow without independent duplicate human screening, and predominantly observational evidence. The regional literature supports context-sensitive interpretation of exposure, appraisal, belief, and action; it does not establish a uniform causal pathway or a preferred intervention transferable across all settings.

title: Network analysis of hope, medical coping, and self-deficiency in patients with port-wine stain
container-title: Frontiers in Public Health
76041914ba44a62b41f97795dae1e0d8d414164a.abstract: Background Port-wine stain (PWS) is a chronic congenital vascular malformation that often causes substantial psychosocial burden due to visible skin lesions. However, the complex interrelationships among hope, medical coping, and self-deficiency in patients with PWS remain unclear. Objective This study aimed to explore the network structure of hope, medical coping styles, and self-deficiency in patients with PWS, identify core and bridge psychological nodes, and examine subgroup differences by socioeconomic status (SES), gender, and treatment experience. Methods A cross-sectional study was conducted among 227 patients with PWS. Hope was assessed using the Herth Hope Index (HHI), coping styles using the Medical Coping Modes Questionnaire (MCMQ), and self-deficiency using the Feeling of Inadequacy Scale (FIS). Network analysis was performed to estimate the psychological interaction structure, evaluate centrality and bridge centrality, identify community structures, and assess network stability. Subgroup network comparisons were further conducted based on gender, SES, and treatment experience. Results The network analysis identified learning ability as the most central node and the most important bridge node. Confrontation and appearance also showed high centrality. The strongest edge was observed between learning ability and confrontation, suggesting a close interaction between perceived competence and active coping. Bridge centrality analysis further highlighted social confidence as an important connector across psychological domains. Community detection identified three interconnected psychological subsystems. Subgroup analyses revealed substantial heterogeneity: males showed stronger associations between hope and self-deficiency, females demonstrated tighter connections among self-esteem, appearance, and social confidence, and patients without treatment experience exhibited denser psychological networks. In addition, low-SES patients had significantly higher network density than high-SES patients, indicating stronger mutual reinforcement among psychological factors. Conclusion The psychological adaptation of patients with PWS exhibits a complex network structure, with learning ability, confrontation, and social confidence serving as key intervention targets. Patients with lower SES may be more psychologically vulnerable due to denser network connectivity. These findings provide a theoretical basis for precision psychological interventions in PWS from a network perspective. Notably, patients with low SES exhibited denser network connectivity, suggesting heightened psychological vulnerability, so future public health strategies should prioritize both node-specific interventions and resources for disadvantaged populations.

title: Trust in artificial intelligence and AI-assisted social and civic decision-making among Arab youth: evidence from Egypt, Kuwait, and the UAE
container-title: Frontiers in Sociology
9c22c48dec77add12e18981832964c2f183e35aa.abstract: Introduction Trust in artificial intelligence (AI) increasingly shapes how young people evaluate information and public issues, yet evidence from Arab contexts remains limited. This study examined the socio-technical correlates of trust in AI and its association with AI-assisted social and civic decision-making among digitally engaged youth in Egypt, Kuwait, and the United Arab Emirates. Methods A cross-sectional online survey was conducted with 1,023 respondents aged 18–35 recruited through purposive, non-probability sampling. Confirmatory factor analysis (CFA), structural equation modeling (SEM), multi-group CFA, and competing full- versus partial-mediation models evaluated measurement and structural relationships. Results The partially mediated model fit significantly better than the fully mediated model, Δχ2(5) = 55.66, p &lt; 0.001. Institutional confidence (β = 0.303), AI literacy (β = 0.281), perceived usefulness (β = 0.242), and social influence (β = 0.107) were positively associated with trust in AI, and perceived risk was negatively associated (β = −0.106; all p &lt; 0.001). Trust was positively associated with AI-assisted decision-making (β = 0.412, p &lt; 0.001). Significant indirect associations through trust were observed for all five antecedents, while the direct perceived-risk path to AI-assisted decision-making was nonsignificant. Multi-group CFA supported metric and practical scalar measurement invariance across the three countries. Discussion The findings support a socio-technical account of AI trust in which technological, cognitive, institutional, and social conditions jointly relate to AI-assisted decision-making, with trust functioning as a central but not exclusive pathway. Given the cross-sectional, purposive design, findings are interpreted as associations rather than causal or nationally representative effects.

title: Organizational trust in the workplace: explainable machine learning evidence from Ecuadorian workers
container-title: Frontiers in Psychology
c7ded733576fec6b9909491fade0467fab2973a5.abstract: Organizational trust reflects employees' willingness to accept vulnerability on the basis of positive expectations about supervisors and the organization. This study examined whether organizational cynicism, organizational climate, job satisfaction, and worker characteristics contain reproducible information for distinguishing high organizational trust among workers in Ecuador. A quantitative, non-experimental, cross-sectional design was applied to 899 valid survey records obtained through non-probability availability sampling. The focal construct was the 12-item Organizational Trust Inventory, comprising trust in the immediate supervisor and trust in the organization. High trust was defined a priori as a mean score of at least 5.0, the first response anchor labeled “High,” yielding 555 high-trust and 344 non-high-trust cases. Ordinal confirmatory factor analysis supported the proposed measurement structures; composite reliability ranged from 0.833 to 0.965, and the four-construct measurement model showed good fit ( CFI = 0.991, TLI = 0.991, RMSEA = 0.036). Logistic regression, Random Forest, XGBoost, LightGBM, and CatBoost were compared through nested cross-validation, training-only hyperparameter tuning, a held-out test set, and bootstrap uncertainty intervals. Logistic regression achieved the highest nested cross-validated ROC-AUC (0.865), while CatBoost obtained the highest test ROC-AUC (0.855); paired bootstrap intervals indicated that these differences were not statistically distinguishable. Satisfaction, cognitive cynicism, and organizational climate were the most informative predictor groups. A stability-validated two-profile solution separated a favorable profile with 84.4% high trust from a critical profile with 34.1%. The results support cautious organizational diagnosis and hypothesis generation, not employee-level automated decisions. An incremental benchmark compared demographic, satisfaction-only, cynicism-only, climate-only, and combined predictor sets under the same repeated nested cross-validation protocol; job satisfaction alone reached a mean nested ROC-AUC of 0.843, and adding cynicism and climate raised it to 0.875, so the integrated framework yields a modest rather than transformative increment. High trust is an analytically defined category, not a diagnostic threshold, and the held-out set is drawn from the same convenience sample, so the evidence constitutes internal out-of-sample validation rather than external validation.

title: Hybrid one-shot and vertical federated learning framework for privacy-preserving brain tumor classification and segmentation using the BRISC2025 dataset
container-title: Frontiers in Artificial Intelligence
4e6e7bc5f7fb16414f2671c35b84aa06ef98beba.abstract: Introduction From MRI images, diagnosis of brain tumors may have limitations due to restriction over patient privacy and lack of annotated datasets so that models cannot be trained across multiple institutions. Methods HOS-VFL: A Hybrid One-Shot and Vertical Federated Learning framework with a two-round protocol that jointly enjoys the advantages of prototype-based one-shot aggregation and encrypted vertical feature space augmentation. Tested on BRISC2025 MRimages of glioma, meningioma, pituitary and non-tumor, with T1-weighted images, expert-annotated, at five simulated institutions, with simulated IID and Dirichlet setups. Results HOS-VFL obtained values of 98.73% on accuracy and 35–50 for conventional federated learning, with a 94.3% reduction compared to the best baseline valued. HOS-VFL performed 98.73% accuracy and 35–50 for the conventional federated learning with an improvement of 94.3% when compared with its best baseline accuracy. The mean Dice and IoU of Segmentation was 0.9147, 0.8423 respectively. Performance did not wane differently in terms of competitive levels and number of institutions, and was able to withstand gradient inference attacks. Discussion HOS-VFL philosophy is centralised performance with minimum communication with retention of raw data local. The method needs to be validated on larger real multi-center datasets before their clinical use.

title: Development and internal validation of an interpretable machine learning-based risk stratification model for sarcopenic obesity in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus
container-title: Frontiers in Medicine
6dc60ab5481f90f36f0a7911b58344657b56f308.abstract: Objective To analyze the factors associated with sarcopenic obesity (SO) in patients with type 2 diabetes (T2DM), and to develop and internally validate an SO risk stratification model based on interpretable machine learning, thereby providing guidance for the clinical screening of high-risk patients and the implementation of personalized risk assessment. Methods A single-center cross-sectional study design was adopted, enrolling 378 patients with T2DM, who were divided into an SO group and a non-SO group based on SO diagnostic results. Demographic characteristics, disease-related data, anthropometric measurements, and laboratory test results were collected. The cohort was randomly divided into a training set ( n = 265) and a validation set ( n = 113) in a 7:3 ratio. Univariate analysis, LASSO regression, and multivariate logistic regression were used to identify factors associated with SO, and based on these results, five risk-stratification models were constructed: logistic regression, random forest, SVM, LightGBM, and XGBoost. Model performance was evaluated using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), area under the precision-recall curve (AUPRC), accuracy, sensitivity, recall, precision, F1 score, and Brier score. Model calibration performance and clinical applicability were assessed using calibration curves, calibration slope, calibration intercept, calibration-in-the-large (CITL), and decision curve analysis (DCA). Supplementary internal validation of the LightGBM model was performed using 1,000 bootstrap resamples, and interpretability analysis was conducted using the SHAP method. Results In this study, the detection rate of SO in patients with T2DM was 36.2%, age, ADL, waist circumference, HDL, and 25(OH)D were the primary factors influencing SO. The AUC values of the five models on the validation set ranged from 0.806 to 0.821. Among them, LightGBM achieved the numerically highest AUC in this sample, at 0.821 (95% CI: 0.744–0.897), with an AUPRC of 0.712; however, the DeLong test indicated that the differences in AUC among the models were not statistically significant (all P &gt; 0.05). Overall, the models demonstrated good calibration performance and potential clinical net benefit; however, bootstrap internal validation indicated that LightGBM still exhibited a certain degree of optimism bias and under-calibration. SHAP analysis revealed that age, ADL, waist circumference, HDL, and 25(OH)D contributed significantly to model predictions, with age being the most important predictive feature. Conclusion The SO risk stratification models developed using machine learning methods demonstrated good performance and potential clinical utility, with LightGBM achieving the highest numerical performance. SHAP-based interpretability analysis enhanced model transparency and clinical credibility, providing a reference for assisted screening, risk stratification, and individualized assessment of SO in patients with T2DM.

title: A preliminary design framework for human-friendly AI interaction: grounded in anthropomorphism
container-title: Frontiers in Computer Science
46e7d698557d6ad9c8af0e26c30db1eac6a6fb1b.abstract: People converse with AI as they would with friends in daily life, collaborate with it, and form personalized relationships. In response to these emerging forms of interaction, this study clarifies the concept of Human-Friendly Interaction with conversational AI and develops the Human-Friendly AI Interaction Design Framework (HFAI-DF). This study positions anthropomorphism, a foundational phenomenon in human–AI interaction, as a theoretical bridge and reviews literature on anthropomorphism theory and related research on human cognition. On this basis, this study interpretively derives and organizes how anthropomorphism-inducing stimuli can be applied to AI agents, systematizing them into 30 AI behavioral items that enable human-friendly interaction. Subsequently, a survey was conducted and exploratory factor analysis performed to identify six dimensions as a preliminary structure for a design framework for AI’s human-friendly interaction. These dimensions are: Self-Aware Interaction, User-Adaptive Responsiveness Interaction, Context-Aware Reasoning Interaction, Socio-Emotional Interaction, Creative Collaboration Interaction, and Proactive Assistance Interaction. Within the evolving AI research landscape focused on interaction, this study extends the human-centered AI concept toward human-friendly interaction that operates in an organic manner comparable to human–human conversation, grounded in an understanding of human cognitive functioning. The proposed framework provides both AI providers and designers with an initial structure for shaping and improving the quality of human-friendly interaction.

title: Perceptions of AI in veterinary medicine: insights from students, faculty, and practicing veterinarians in Hong Kong
container-title: Frontiers in Veterinary Science
d5c0bfa269240bf48c6ea87f212741cd8f464ca1.abstract: Introduction As artificial intelligence (AI) transforms veterinary medicine, understanding stakeholder perceptions is crucial for its effective and responsible integration. To support the development of targeted educational and policy initiatives, this study aimed to evaluate the knowledge, attitudes, and practices regarding AI among Bachelor of Veterinary Medicine (BVM) students, PhD students, faculty, and practicing veterinarians in Hong Kong. Methods A cross-sectional online survey was conducted between December 2023 and March 2024 among BVM students, PhD students, and faculty members at City University of Hong Kong, and practicing veterinarians in Hong Kong who are members of the Hong Kong Veterinary Association. The survey assessed participants’ familiarity with AI, prior training, perceived benefits, concerns, and willingness to adopt AI in education and clinical practice. Descriptive and comparative analyses were performed to examine differences across stakeholder groups. Results Of 79 complete responses, nearly half (46.8%) reported unfamiliarity with AI concepts. Only 17.7% had received formal AI training, although 78.5% expressed interest in future AI education. Most respondents agreed that AI could enhance veterinary teaching and practice (83.5%) and 81.0% indicated they would likely incorporate AI tools into their work. Key perceived benefits included support for case-based learning (83.5%), virtual animal models for teaching (77.2%), and improved diagnostic accuracy (74.7%). However, 41.8% felt inadequately prepared to use AI. Major concerns included veterinarian accountability for AI-related harms (79.7%), lack of system flexibility (75.9%), and potential clinical inaccuracies (70.9%). Descriptively, practicing veterinarians reported the lowest AI tool use (66.7% had never used AI tools), the lowest preparedness (66.7% felt unprepared), and lower agreement with AI’s clinical benefits, although attitude differences were not statistically significant. Conclusion These exploratory findings suggest gaps in self-reported AI knowledge and differing perceptions of AI across veterinary stakeholder groups in Hong Kong, with AI use already widespread at the time of the survey despite limited formal training. While enthusiasm for AI integration is high, concerns about preparedness, accuracy, and ethical responsibility remain. Larger, multi-institutional studies are needed to confirm these patterns and to inform targeted training programs and ethical frameworks for safe and effective AI adoption in veterinary medicine.

title: Global classrooms: a tri-national study on AI integration by higher education students
container-title: Frontiers in Computer Science
4ce5be4917c40263b11f6c7ca8eabe77dd89211a.abstract: Collaborative cross-cultural learning expands higher education students’ (HES’) intercultural and language awareness, enhances their intercultural competence, has an impact on attitudes towards technology and AI as well as towards the course design and general satisfaction with the collaborative experience in the course. Furthermore, their self-perceived role in a digital setting and their self-perceived English proficiency were measured. The CoGIH Project encourages HES to explore the educational potential of artificial intelligence (AI) for learning and teaching in the school setting. A special focus is on the impact AI might have on the language learning process in English as a lingua franca in a multilingual setting. N = 113 HES, including both pre-service and in-service teachers as well as students preparing for educational administration, from five institutions in Israel, Germany, and Hungary collaborated in 14 international groups, representing five higher education institutions; n = 91 answered the questionnaires. Each group investigated the educational potential of a specific AI application and developed an AI-supported, results-based webpage. The study employed a multi-method research design. Questionnaires were administered to the HES to investigate their experiences at the beginning and at the end of the course. While quantitative data were used to investigate the research through the lens of descriptive statistics and correlations between factors, qualitative data from the open questions were analysed to enable a deeper understanding of HES’ perceptions, experiences and meanings, as well as their critical thinking. The study highlighted strengths and challenges in using AI for educational purposes. The HES valued clear structures, logical navigation, and creative, motivating tasks. Simultaneously, recurring issues included incomplete translations, limited depth of critical reflection, and weaknesses in visual design. In sum, even though AI can support creativity and language learning and teaching, individual learners’ reflections and authentic teacher guidance remain indispensable for meaningful learning.

title: An explainable data-local federated learning framework for intrusion detection in connected healthcare systems
container-title: Frontiers in Medicine
373cf0d2af24d89f3e439b438c579dad5177fc38.abstract: Introduction Connected healthcare networks link medical sensors, gateways, electronic health record systems and cloud services, which enlarges their exposure to cyberattacks. Centralized intrusion detection systems (IDSs) require traffic from all sites to be pooled in one repository, which conflicts with data-residency constraints and creates a single high-value target, and their alerts are often not interpretable. Methods This paper proposes an explainable, privacy-aware federated learning (FL) framework for intrusion detection in which privacy is limited to data locality: clients exchange trained models and summary statistics instead of raw records, but model updates are not encrypted, securely aggregated or differentially private. The framework combines (i) federated training, (ii) client-side SHAP-guided feature ranking reconciled at the server into a common global feature set, and (iii) SHAP and LIME explanations of the aggregated model that are evaluated quantitatively. The framework was evaluated on the WUSTL-EHMS-2020 healthcare dataset, which combines network-flow and patient biometric features, partitioned into five simulated clients under IID and non-IID settings, using a leakage-controlled protocol in which host identifiers and record indices were excluded and all preprocessing was fitted on training data only. Results Under non-IID partitioning, the federated gradient-boosting model reached an accuracy of 0.935 ± 0.009, a Matthews correlation coefficient (MCC) of 0.673 ± 0.045 and a ROC-AUC of 0.895 ± 0.020, compared with an MCC of 0.700 ± 0.013 for centralized training and 0.540 ± 0.036 for local-only training. All data-alteration attacks were detected, whereas most spoofing attacks were missed. SHAP-guided feature selection and reliability-weighted aggregation did not improve detection and are therefore presented as design options; LIME explanations had low local fidelity ( R² = 0.332), and the usefulness of the explanations for security analysts was not evaluated. Discussion All results come from a single laboratory dataset partitioned into simulated clients; they demonstrate experimental feasibility only and do not establish generalizability to other healthcare networks or readiness for clinical deployment.

title: AI-generated advertising in agricultural livestreaming and the auditability of disclosure regulation: a three-layer audit of public Douyin data from China
container-title: Frontiers in Sustainable Food Systems
c177ed750eb610123bd142c9d637834496b25555.abstract: Agricultural products are credence goods, and in livestreaming, the grower’s visible presence signals the price. China has required labeling of deep-synthesis content since January 2023 and, since 1 September 2025, of AI-generated synthetic content. Whether public platform data can verify compliance in a market where the authenticity premium is especially salient remains unclear, given that growers themselves sell produce. We audited three layers of public Chinese platform data: 189 policy snippets, 19 accounts retrieved by AI technical terms, and 455 unique authors retrieved by crop names. In the one policy coding field with complete intercoder agreement ( κ = 1.000), only 6 of 189 snippets name authenticity as a farmer asset. Retrieval by technical terms returns intermediaries: 13 of 19 accounts sell AI tools or tutorials, and none discloses using AI to sell its own produce. Among AI-announcing cases retrieved by crop-name queries, an expanded text-field detector validated at 94.7% recall flags 10 of 455 authors: seven supply-side or service-provider accounts, one incidental non-agricultural mention, and two product-query artifacts; none discloses grower own-use of AI livestreaming. Checks of API-exposed platform metadata for all 575 video records and cover images for 472 records found no platform-side AI label or visible AI/AIGC/statutory AI-generated notice. AI was announced primarily by accounts that sell, service, or discuss AI, rather than by produce-selling grower accounts. No grower own-use disclosure appears in either audited slice: 0 of 19 technical-keyword accounts and 0 of 455 transaction-query authors. The zero admits two readings that the audited surface cannot separate: smallholders do not use these tools, making the requirement inert for them, or they use them without disclosure. No label-reading instrument applied to the audited surface can decide between them, because such inspection observes announcement rather than use. Platforms and regulators may hold backend data unavailable to an external audit. If the theoretically derived authenticity-penalty mechanism holds, disclosure would impose an uneven cost, falling more heavily on growers than on intermediaries. The observed pattern is consistent with this hypothesis but does not establish it.

title: Self-efficacy and job burnout among early childhood physical education teachers: exploratory indirect associations through the negative compassion-fatigue domain and professional identity moderation
container-title: Frontiers in Psychology
ac2fc6818417a373a604c8067f2108889f30c412.abstract: Background Early childhood physical education teachers work at the intersection of early childhood education and physical education, yet psychological factors associated with job burnout in this group remain underexamined. Guided by the Job Demands–Resources model, this study examined associations among self-efficacy, an exploratory negative-domain composite, professional identity, and job burnout, including an indirect association and moderation of the direct association. Methods A cross-sectional online survey using snowball sampling included 588 early childhood physical education teachers in Chengdu, China (555 women, 33 men; mean age = 26.12 years, SD = 5.77). Participants completed the Chinese short-form Teachers’ Sense of Efficacy Scale, an adapted 15-item Chinese compassion-fatigue questionnaire, the Chinese Maslach Burnout Inventory-Education Survey, and the Teacher Professional Identity Scale. An exploratory 10-item negative-domain composite was constructed from five burnout-related and five secondary traumatic stress (STS) items, excluding the five compassion-satisfaction items. Pearson correlations and PROCESS Models 4 and 5 were estimated, adjusting for age and gender. Indirect associations were evaluated using 5,000 bootstrap resamples. Results Self-efficacy was negatively correlated with job burnout (r = −0.38, p &lt; 0.001) and positively correlated with the negative-domain composite (r = 0.16, p &lt; 0.001), which was also positively correlated with job burnout (r = 0.19, p &lt; 0.001). The adjusted indirect association through the composite was positive (ab = 0.081, 95% CI [0.034, 0.143]) and opposed the negative direct association (B = −0.778, p &lt; 0.001). Professional identity moderated the direct association (interaction B = −0.263, p &lt; 0.001; ΔR 2 = 0.018), which was nonsignificant at low professional identity (B = −0.086, 95% CI [−0.260, 0.088]) and strongest at high professional identity (B = −0.422, 95% CI [−0.610, −0.234]). Conclusion Higher self-efficacy was associated with lower job burnout, and this negative association was stronger at higher levels of professional identity. The positive indirect association through the exploratory negative-domain composite was small and sensitive to its operationalization. Given the cross-sectional design and measurement limitations, these findings should be interpreted as exploratory statistical associations rather than evidence of causal mechanisms.

title: Evaluation of transfer learning in hydrological forecasting using ensemble LSTM models: a statistical approach to uncertainty and accuracy
container-title: Frontiers in Water
b1b3dbfa7c4ead80ded6ed0113ebb7ed4e38c302.abstract: Global change poses significant challenges to water resource management. Water Table Depth (WTD) is a critical variable linking subsurface dynamics to land-surface processes; however, real-world observations remain sparse. Transfer learning can support WTD monitoring, but assessing prediction quality in locations without observations is challenging. This contribution explores a method using an assessment tool to estimate prediction quality in such locations. We implement an ensemble of 100 Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks to predict WTD using the physically-based Terrestrial Systems Modeling Platform Groundwater to Atmosphere (TSMP-G2A) simulation dataset, spatially split into training and transfer subsets. The training subset is temporally split into training and testing time periods, while the transfer subset evaluates transferability to unseen locations within the TSMP-G2A dataset during the testing period. Each ensemble LSTM member was trained on a spatial sample of the training subset, randomly sampled based on geographic location. By leveraging the ensemble spread, we develop spread-skill relationships to assess prediction quality in the transfer subset. Results indicate good generalization and transfer abilities on the TSMP-G2A dataset within the study domain. Additionally, expanding each ensemble member's training subset from 100 to 400 grid cells improves global transfer prediction accuracy by 11.52 and 17.42% in root mean square error (RMSE) and Pearson correlation, respectively. The spread-skill relationships show a strong correlation between ensemble spread and both RMSE and absolute mean bias, suggesting that spread can effectively estimate prediction quality for these metrics without observations, whereas the relationship with Pearson correlation is weak. This study highlights transfer learning's potential to improve hydrological modeling and provides an assessment tool for prediction quality in regions lacking observations. Future research could extend this framework to evaluate its global-scale transferability and validate it against real-world observational data.

title: Sustainable Federated Continual Learning for environmental monitoring: a systematic review
container-title: Frontiers in Artificial Intelligence
b389fbb5ad33979bef8f6f3c3429ad0c8cd7c880.abstract: Introduction The use of distributed sensing infrastructures is increasingly becoming a key approach to environmental monitoring that is required to be mobile, flexible and adaptable to non-stationary conditions, preserve data privacy and consume as few resources as possible. The decentralized training paradigm provided by Federated Learning together with the ability of adapting sequentially over time without forgetting from Continual Learning has resulted in a concept of Federated Continual Learning (FCL) which offers a promising approach for privacy preserving environmental sensing systems that are capable of learning over time without forgetting. This systematic review provides an in-depth synthesis of the latest research, progress, environmental applications, sustainability, trustworthiness and future directions of Federated Continual Learning (FCL) for environmental monitoring. Methods A total of 90 peer-reviewed publications were identified by conducting a systematic literature search using pre-defined inclusion/exclusion criteria, quality assessment, bibliometric analysis and qualitative evidence synthesis with the framework of PRISMA 2020. Results The synthesized evidence suggests that Federated Learning has come of age in terms of optimization, communication complexity, robustness, and personalization, but Federated Continual Learning is still in its infancy with few applications in the real world. Typically, sustainability, trustworthiness, privacy, fairness, personalization and explainability are explored separately and not in parallel. Although most applications have been single-shot Federated Learning systems, without genuine continual adaptation, isolated examples include some applications from air quality to water quality, agriculture to disaster monitoring and remote sensing. Seven cross-cutting research gaps are identified: disjointed integration of research directions, few deployments in the real world, absence of standardized evaluation, unsolved multi-objective optimization, poor scaling in the long term, weak sustainability-trustworthiness coupling, and poor cross-domain generalization. Discussion It is not just about the evolution of single algorithmic breakthroughs anymore, but actual realization of Federated Continual Learning systems that can effectively assist in continual adaptation while ensuring communication efficiency, sustainability, trustworthiness, scalability and long-term deployment under real environmental conditions.

title: Coarse-to-fine-grained insulator defect detection using two-stage deep learning framework
container-title: Frontiers in Artificial Intelligence
a7263f4cd77959700086b801b46c1fa720140817.abstract: Introduction In power transmission and power distribution systems, insulators are the fundamental components which provide mechanical support and electrical isolation between conductors and supporting towers. However, these insulators are continuously exposed to extreme weather conditions, mechanical stress, pollution and dust, which can lead to surface damage and abnormal operation. Method Conventionally, manual on-site inspection is performed to identify faulty insulators. However, this method is labor intensive, risky, and reactive. With the advancement in unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) technology and deep learning method, automatic visual inspection has replaced the conventional methods. However, automatic visual inspection from UAV images is challenging task due to complex background and small size of the insulators. To address these challenges, we proposed a framework that consists of two stages. In the first stage, you only look once (YOLO)-based is used for extracting candidate region of insulator to get coarse class prediction. During the second stage, the candidate regions are then cropped from the image into image patches and fed to a lightweight patch-level classifier. In order to enhance inter-class separability, hard-pair contrastive classification loss is proposed by adding hard-pair contrastive term to the cross-entropy loss in the embedding space. Discussion The proposed technique is evaluated using an open-source insulator defect image dataset. The experiment results demonstrate the superior performance of the proposed framework compared with the YOLO variants and representative two-stage detectors.

title: Predicting microvascular invasion in hepatocellular carcinoma using contrast-enhanced CT-based deep learning models: a comparative study of transformer, CNN, and MIL
container-title: Frontiers in Oncology
2345b9acd146da8379c6a34c2f49c98c59383a82.abstract: Objective Microvascular invasion (MVI) predicts postoperative recurrence in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), yet preoperative prediction remains challenging. This study compared a Transformer, a convolutional neural network (CNN), and a multiple instance learning (MIL) framework for predicting MVI from contrast-enhanced CT. Methods We retrospectively enrolled 236 patients with pathologically confirmed HCC. Tumor regions of interest were semi-automatically delineated on arterial-phase CT images, and slices centered on the largest tumor cross-section were sampled to build a 2.5D dataset. Four models—Transformer, MIL, CNN, and a clinical baseline—were trained. Models were compared using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) with the DeLong test; bootstrap resampling assessed the stability of AUC estimates. Results The Transformer achieved the highest AUC of 0.827 (95% CI 0.7585–0.8962), with an accuracy of 0.775, sensitivity of 0.577, and specificity of 0.889, followed by MIL (0.766; 95% CI 0.6875–0.8441), CNN (0.723), and the clinical model (0.715). Bootstrap validation confirmed stable AUC estimates for all models, with the Transformer ranking first (mean 0.827; SD 0.034). The Transformer significantly outperformed the CNN (adjusted P = 0.001) and the clinical model (adjusted P = 0.039); after correction for multiple comparisons, its difference from MIL was of borderline significance (adjusted P = 0.097). No significant differences were observed among the CNN, MIL, and clinical models. Conclusion Among the four models evaluated, the contrast-enhanced CT-based Transformer predicted MVI most accurately, and its advantage persisted after bootstrap internal validation. These findings concern the ranking of discriminative performance only; the clinical utility of the model is not established, and prospective validation in larger cohorts is required before any clinical application.

title: A Deepfake Detection Framework for Securing Facial Biometrics Using Attention-Based Deep Learning and Blockchain
container-title: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
a0074b87d1d6c79dcfbe609a01fe5bc5a247f1d2.abstract: Facial biometric authentication is widely deployed for identity verification, yet it is increasingly exposed to deepfakebased presentation and injection attacks and to large-scale breaches of centrally stored biometric templates. This paper proposes a deepfake-resilient facial biometric security framework that combines attention-based deep learning with blockchain technology. At registration, face images are pre-processed, augmented with a generative adversarial network (GAN), encoded by a convolutional neural network (CNN) with self-attention, and classified as real or fake by an artificial neural network (ANN). Only images classified as real are encrypted, bound to a unique user identifier and committed to a private blockchain through a cryptographic hash, whereas fake attempts are written to an immutable event log. At authentication, a fresh probe passes through the same pipeline and is verified by smart contracts that check the integrity of the registered commitment and the template similarity using zero-knowledge proofs (ZKPs), so that raw biometric features are never disclosed. We formalise the threat model, specify the architecture, the smart-contract interface and the security properties, and define an evaluation protocol based on the CIPLAB Real and Fake Face Detection and UTKFace datasets that covers detection accuracy, authentication error rates, adversarial robustness, demographic fairness and system overhead. The framework provides a basis for privacy-preserving, auditable and scalable facial authentication in digital identity management, financial services, healthcare and e-governance.

title: Multi-Agent Learning for Adaptive Prompt Optimization in Heterogeneous Clinical Narratives
574b8475460e337279d0ff4020d499b0632f38d4.abstract: Abstract Free-text narratives within electronic health records, particularly echocardiography reports, contain vital physiological parameters that are frequently absent from structured flowsheet tables. While modern foundation language models offer strong textual comprehension, manual prompt engineering remains an empirical and non-robust procedure. Small prompt changes can cause formatting errors, missed unit conversions, and numerical hallucinations. To address these issues, we formulate prompt optimization as a discrete-action Markov Decision Process and evaluate it on 120,555 echocardiography notes from 38,022 adult ICU patients in the MIMIC-IV database. Unlike conventional rule-based parsers and naive prompts, the proposed reinforcement learning agents optimize extraction using a numeric reward with a strict \pm 2.5% relative tolerance. Both the off-policy Dueling Double Deep Q-Network (D3QN) and on-policy Deep SARSA agents converged within 15 training episodes, achieving a 7.24% relative improvement in extraction accuracy over conventional NLP methods.

title: Developmental trajectories of neural modules underlying emotion generation and regulation across childhood and adolescence
a200b51e591e0b19099c4e72cb6360c3a375678f.abstract: Abstract Emotional maturation involves a fundamental shift from the raw, somatic reactions during childhood to the precise, cognitively elaborated processes during adulthood. However, the neural dynamics that drive this developmental transition, especially the changing contributions of distributed neural modules, remain unclear. Leveraging principal component analysis of a large-scale fMRI dataset in conjunction with a sliding-window regression approach, we quantified age-varying contributions of neural modules to emotion generation and emotion regulation. During emotion generation, while frontotemporal modules are the predominant sources of activation, the limbic-salience module remains the core substrate contributing to negative affect across the entire age range. For emotion regulation via reappraisal, the lateral temporal module emerged as the sole positive contributor to regulatory success. Conversely, activation of the frontotemporal regions around age 8 and the occipital activation across the entire age range contributed to poorer regulation. Such modules further showed distinct linear and quadratic links to real-world emotion measures and cross-process coupling. Together, the work delineates a dynamic, non-linear reorganization of emotional architecture and underscores the need for stage-matched interventions.

title: Enhancing Cyber Security Through Machine Learning: A Comprehensive Approach to Intelligent Threat Detection and Prevention
container-title: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
b4c21c61ea2f649900321093ca392951b47dfa1b.abstract: The rapid growth of digital technologies and interconnected systems has significantly increased cyber security risks worldwide. Traditional security mechanisms often struggle to detect sophisticated cyber threats due to the evolving nature of attacks. Machine Learning (ML) has emerged as a powerful solution for enhancing cyber security by enabling automated threat detection, anomaly identification, malware classification, and intrusion prevention. This paper examines the role of machine learning in strengthening cyber security frameworks, evaluates different ML algorithms used in cyber defense, and presents a comparative analysis of their effectiveness. The findings suggest that machine learning-based approaches significantly improve detection accuracy while reducing response times compared to conventional security methods.

title: Human-Governed Multi-Agent AI for Biological Hypothesis Generation: An Evidence-Grounded Framework Using JUMP Cell Painting Profiles
7a2bcb64973bd56bae183bb619c26a0d3a9a5a47.abstract: Abstract High-dimensional cellular phenotypes can motivate biological hypotheses, but similarity alone cannot establish mechanism or causal validity. DISCOVERY-AGENT links exploratory JUMP Cell Painting evidence with evidence-grounded hypothesis generation, independent critique and bounded human-review routing. An initial 65-record CRISPR/ORF analysis across nine gene–modality tests found four FDR-significant CRISPR plate-level associations (AKT1, BRCA1, MTOR and TP53), none among evaluated ORF genes. A distinct later cross-source compound-identity benchmark used 614 morphological features and achieved AUROC 0.6142 on 1,250 held-out compounds with training-only preprocessing; this is identity discrimination, not mechanism-of-action classification. Three structured hypotheses underwent LLM critique and revision, while eleven gene-pair evidence assessments yielded no FDR-significant mechanistic finding (minimum q = 0.2037). Archived governance checks passed 1,021/1,021 predefined tests; nevertheless, the initial live-agent run contained two execution errors among five cases, with both cases responding on fresh retest. These findings demonstrate feasibility of auditable evidence processing and modest cross-source morphology signal, not validated autonomous discovery, prospective safety, or completed expert review. The work delineates practical requirements for independent biological validation and reproducible scientific agents.

title: Explainable Machine Learning for Next-Hour Prediction Using Three Meteorological Variables and Historical PM2.5 Data
container-title: International Journal of Mathematics, Statistics, and Computing
a2f008b323003bd67ebcfb5ab45b3f96c0c7d94c.abstract: Ambient fine particulate matter (PM2.5) remains one of the most consequential urban air-quality hazards, yet forecasting its next-hour concentration accurately and transparently remains challenging owing to the non-linear, multivariate nature of pollutant-meteorology interactions and the black-box character of high-performing ensemble models. This study proposes an explainable machine learning framework for next-hour PM2.5 concentration prediction that integrates Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) with a parsimonious set of predictors comprising three meteorological variables (air temperature, relative humidity, and wind speed) together with historical PM2.5 concentrations. Using 43,824 hourly observations from the Beijing PM2.5 dataset (2010–2014), lag, rolling-statistic, and cyclical calendar features were engineered, and model hyperparameters were systematically tuned through Bayesian optimization using the Optuna framework with the Tree-structured Parzen Estimator over 30 trials under a strictly chronological training validation testing split. Model interpretability was achieved through SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis. The tuned XGBoost model achieved a root mean squared error of 16.50 µg/m³, a mean absolute error of 9.89 µg/m³, a mean absolute percentage error of 21.75%, and a coefficient of determination of 0.9478 on the test set, corresponding to reductions of approximately 4.4%, 10.5%, and 12.4% in RMSE, MAE, and MAPE, respectively, relative to a non-optimized baseline model. SHAP analysis revealed that the one-hour PM2.5 lag feature overwhelmingly dominated the model's predictions, far surpassing the combined contribution of all meteorological variables, while wind speed and temperature retained secondary but physically meaningful influence. These findings demonstrate that a minimal, readily obtainable feature set can support highly accurate and interpretable next-hour PM2.5 forecasting, offering a practical and scientifically transparent tool to support early-warning air-quality systems and evidence-based environmental health policy.

title: Comparative Analysis of Statistical, Machine Learning, and Deep Learning Models for USD/IDR Prediction Using Macroeconomic Indicators and Explainable Artificial Intelligence
container-title: International Journal of Mathematics, Statistics, and Computing
563b51be889d2953f9d8bd3c5be637544cabc3c2.abstract: The USD/IDR exchange rate is a key daily barometer of Indonesia's economic health. Accurate forecasting is vital for trade, inflation, and monetary stability. However, its volatile and nonlinear dynamics pose challenges. While research has applied statistical models, machine learning, and deep learning, few studies offer a comprehensive comparison integrating predictive accuracy with model interpretability, particularly using banking stock prices as exogenous predictors. This study addresses this gap by developing and evaluating eight forecasting approaches—a naive random-walk baseline, two statistical models (ARIMA, SARIMAX), three tree-based ensembles (Random Forest, XGBoost, LightGBM), and two recurrent neural networks (LSTM, GRU) using daily data from January 2015 to July 2026 (3,005 observations). Five major banking stocks (BBCA, BBRI, BMRI, BBNI, BDMN) are included as one-day-lagged exogenous features. Models are assessed via hold-out testing and five-fold walk-forward cross-validation using RMSE, MAE, MAPE, and R². Contrary to expectations, the naive random-walk consistently achieves the lowest error (RMSE=115.24, MAE=63.80, MAPE=0.39%) and the most stable performance, with LSTM as the best-performing complex model (RMSE=269.59, R²=0.785). Diebold-Mariano tests confirm statistical significance (p<0.001). To enhance transparency, SHAP-based Explainable AI is applied to Random Forest, revealing that the lagged USD/IDR value overwhelmingly dominates predictions (mean |SHAP|=1,509.01), while banking stock contributions are negligible. These findings also empirically confirm the well-known Meese-Rogoff puzzle and weak-form market efficiency for USD/IDR, clearly proving that simple baselines remain formidable benchmarks for short-horizon forecasts. This study ultimately underscores the critical importance of combining rigorous benchmarking with XAI to deliver accurate and interpretable predictions for economic policymakers and financial practitioners.
