title: PENGARUH ENTREPRENEUR EDUCATION, FAMILY ENVIRONMENT, DAN ENTREPRENEURIAL PASSION TERHADAP ENTREPRENEUR INTENTION MELALUI SELF-EFFICACY PADA PESERTA PELATIHAN YAYASAN KARANG WIDYA (THE LEARNING FARM)
Pengaruh Entrepreneur Education, Family Environment, Dan Entrepreneurial Passion Terhadap Entrepreneur Intention Melalui Self-Efficacy Pada Peserta Pelatihan Yayasan Karang Widya (The Learning Farm)
container-title: Jurnal Riset Ilmu EKONOMI (JRIE)
bf24955a8f89920fc83370b05d621ad430c65a97.abstract: Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis pengaruh pendidikan kewirausahaan, lingkungan keluarga, dan gairah kewirausahaan terhadap niat berwirausaha melalui efikasi diri sebagai variabel intervening pada peserta pelatihan Yayasan Karang Widya (The Learning Farm). Pendekatan kuantitatif digunakan dalam penelitian ini dengan metode survei menggunakan kuesioner yang disebarkan kepada 100 responden, yang terdiri dari peserta dan alumni pelatihan kewirausahaan. Teknik analisis data menggunakan Partial Least Square Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) dengan bantuan perangkat lunak SmartPLS. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa pendidikan kewirausahaan, lingkungan keluarga, dan gairah kewirausahaan berpengaruh signifikan terhadap efikasi diri dan niat berwirausaha. Selain itu, efikasi diri terbukti sebagai variabel mediasi yang memperkuat hubungan antara ketiga variabel independen dengan niat berwirausaha. Penelitian ini memberikan kontribusi teoritis bagi pengembangan literatur kewirausahaan dan implikasi praktis bagi lembaga pelatihan untuk meningkatkan efektivitas program kewirausahaan berbasis efikasi diri.

title: The Rise of the Academic Precariat in Indonesia: A Tripartite Analysis of Wage Injustice through Islamic Corporate Finance, Legal Gaps, and Sharia Ethics
container-title: AL-IMAM: Journal on Islamic Studies, Civilization and Learning Societies
d303c26b14fbf8b9dd7e9d1fab4b31e5eeefcbe4.abstract: This study aims to analyse the structural factors underlying the economic vulnerability and wage inequality experienced by lecturers at private higher education institutions (PHEIs) in Indonesia, examining the relationship between financial governance, legal protection and ethical responsibility. It employs normative legal research using statutory, conceptual and philosophical approaches. Primary, secondary and tertiary legal materials were collected through a literature review and analysed qualitatively using descriptive-analytical and prescriptive methods. The findings indicate that the academic precariat is caused not merely by low wages, but also by limited transparency in remuneration policies, insecure employment relationships and the gap between legal norms and their implementation. From the perspective of Sharia ethics, the principles of al-'adl (justice), kafalah (guarantee and responsibility) and maqasid al-shari'ah (the objectives of Islamic law) provide a normative foundation for evaluating remuneration fairness, institutional accountability and lecturers' welfare. The novelty of this study lies in developing an integrated analytical framework that connects Islamic Corporate Finance, positive law and Sharia ethics to understand the academic precariat as a structural issue rather than merely a matter of individual income. The study concludes that addressing lecturers' economic vulnerability requires stronger remuneration standards, better protection of employment relationships and greater institutional financial accountability, ensuring that the financial sustainability of PHEIs is aligned with the fulfilment of lecturers' economic rights and respect for their professional dignity.

title: Effectiveness of dynamic epidemic intelligence networks for early detection and intervention in infectious diseases: a systematic review and meta-analysis
container-title: Frontiers in Public Health
90382af3734d9426b22d92982c3bfbbd157280ad.abstract: Background The increasing frequency of global health emergencies highlights the critical need for surveillance systems that transcend the limitations of traditional laboratory confirmation. Dynamic epidemic intelligence systems and syndromic surveillance networks have emerged as vital tools for early detection, yet their operational effectiveness remains characterized by significant variability across geographic and clinical contexts. Objective This study aimed to provide a comprehensive meta-analytical evaluation of the effectiveness of dynamic epidemic intelligence systems, focusing on diagnostic classification accuracy, outbreak detection sensitivity, signal precision (Positive Predictive Value), and temporal forecasting reliability. Methods A systematic review and meta-analysis were conducted, synthesizing data from original research articles searched across multiple databases (PubMed, Ovid/MEDLINE, and Embase) Methodological quality was appraised using structured six-domain quality assessment framework adapted from CASP principles and surveillance-system evaluation criteria. Diagnostic validity was synthesized using a bivariate random-effects (Reitsma) model to account for the correlation between sensitivity and specificity. Outbreak detection and alert precision were pooled using random-effects model, MSE was synthesized using inverse-variance random-effects meta-analysis on the log-transformed scale and back-transformed for interpretation. MAPE was summarized descriptively because only two estimates from a single study were available. Results Thirty-four articles were included for analysis. The pooled diagnostic analysis demonstrated high specificity (0.97; 95% CI: 0.94–0.99) but moderate sensitivity (0.64; 95% CI: 0.37–0.85), with a Summary Receiver Operating Characteristic (SROC) Area Under the Curve of 0.96. While systems were highly effective at detecting established outbreaks (pooled rate: 0.91; 95% CI: 0.73–0.97), performance was markedly lower for rare pathogens such as Ebola (0.30) compared to international health threats (0.97). Alert precision was a significant challenge, with a pooled Positive Predictive Value of 0.36 (95% CI: 0.14–0.66), indicating that approximately 64% of system-triggered signals were “noise”. Conclusions Epidemic intelligence systems are powerful instruments for excluding non-events and capturing large-scale outbreaks, yet their reliability for daily operational alerts is highly context dependent. To minimize investigative burden, future implementations must prioritize pathogen-specific optimization and the integration of diverse data streams to enhance sensitivity in humanitarian and low-resource settings.

title: From generation to judgment: the multidimensional structure of design thinking mindset and differences across learning stages in AIGC-supported fashion film design learning
container-title: Frontiers in Psychology
e6e79bc6cb105e45a63939887b04adcfcbb9b1ae.abstract: Introduction Artificial intelligence-generated content (AIGC) is changing how design alternatives are generated in fashion film design learning, enabling students to obtain large numbers of comparable and iteratively refinable visual outcomes within a short period. However, expanded generative capacity does not, by itself, determine how learners interpret, evaluate, experiment with, and select among uncertain outcomes. In this human–AI collaborative creative environment, empirical evidence remains limited on whether learners’ design-related psychological tendencies form a distinguishable multidimensional structure that is comparable across learning stages. Design Thinking Mindset (DTM) provides a multidimensional psychological framework for addressing this issue. Methods Drawing on Vignoli et al.’s DTM framework, this study examined five dimensions—Uncertainty and Risk, Empathy, Experimentation, Abductive Reasoning, and Creative Confidence—through a cross-sectional survey of 409 first-year and third-year students from three Chinese universities who had experience with AIGC fashion film design projects. Confirmatory factor analysis and measurement invariance testing across year groups were used to examine the five-dimensional structure and its measurement comparability, followed by latent mean comparisons. Results The five DTM dimensions formed a correlated yet distinguishable structure and demonstrated measurement comparability across year groups. Third-year students had significantly higher latent means on all five dimensions, with the largest descriptive standardized difference point estimates observed for Abductive Reasoning and Creative Confidence. Discussion These findings provide empirical support for the applicability of five selected DTM dimensions in AIGC-supported fashion film design learning and reveal distinct patterns of self-reported psychological tendencies across year groups. From an educational perspective, the results suggest that AIGC-supported design education should attend not only to the generation of creative alternatives but also to learners’ psychological orientations toward uncertainty, experimentation, audience understanding, creative reasoning, and confidence in creative work.

title: Beyond instruction: exstruction and the dialectics of experience in outdoor learning
container-title: Frontiers in Sports and Active Living
2de3f1b53ddce4afdd707dfdbce0d66d123ffb69.abstract: This article introduces exstruction as a new conceptual lens for understanding experiential learning processes in contexts characterized by uncertainty, risk, and direct engagement with the natural environment. In this article exstruction is defined as the intentional withholding of instructions or learning content in order to foster learner driven and inductive learning processes. Exstruction enables educators to deliberately withhold instruction, allowing learners to discover their own solutions and develop deeper, internalized understanding through experience. It may create conditions for creativity, improvisation, and learner-driven exploration, while requiring careful planning to manage and minimize didactic risk (DidRex). Overall, it enriches learning depth and transferability, making it a valuable approach in sports, adventure, tourism, and guiding education. The concept is situated within experiential learning theory and dialectical philosophy of education, particularly drawing on Litt’s (1923) notion of polar tensions between experience (Erlebnis) and recognition (Erkenntnis). Rather than presenting a formal empirical study, the article uses a practice-derived snow-cave example as an illustrative vignette to explore how varying degrees of instructional intervention shape learning processes. The vignette highlights how instruction tends to support functional task completion, whereas exstruction invites variability, uncertainty, and increased learner engagement with problem-solving and experiential reflection. The article argues that instruction and exstruction should not be understood as opposing categories, but as positions on a continuum of pedagogical intervention. This perspective enables a more nuanced understanding of how educators may balance guidance, autonomy, and risk in experiential learning environments. Finally, the paper introduces the concept of didactic risk as a framework for calibrating the level of instructor intervention in contexts characterized by uncertainty and potential failure. The contribution of the article lies in clarifying exstruction as a distinct pedagogical mechanism and providing a conceptual vocabulary for teaching in emergent and unpredictable learning situations.

title: Self-regulatory moderators of the intention–behavior gap in physical activity: an ecological momentary assessment study among young adults
container-title: Frontiers in Digital Health
462fb1794824a8b3a28486939b424d3c4cae8f69.abstract: Physical activity (PA) intentions do not always translate into behavior, particularly at the momentary level, producing a well-documented intention–behavior gap; yet it remains unclear whether self-regulatory factors explain for whom and when intention–PA coupling is stronger or weaker. This study examined whether time-invariant self-regulatory traits (behavioral inhibition system/behavioral activation system sensitivity, trait self-control, and PA self-regulatory strategies) and time-varying momentary states (feeling focused, feeling in control, procrastinating) moderate the within-day association between momentary PA intentions and subsequent accelerometer-measured PA among young adults. Participants ( N = 228; ages 18–29) completed hourly, signal-contingent mobile ecological momentary assessment (EMA) surveys assessing intentions for PA in the next 60 min across 4-day monitoring periods repeated over 12 months, paired with wrist-worn accelerometer measuring movement intensity (20,491 observations). Multilevel Gamma models decomposed intention and moderator variables into between-person (BP) and within-person (WP) components. Within-person intention consistently predicted greater subsequent movement in the 60 min following each EMA prompt ( p ≤ 0.002) in 13 of 14 models. Seven of 14 moderators produced a significant interaction at p &lt; 0.01, one term from each of seven moderator constructs. Trait behavioral inhibition, PA self-monitoring, and time management moderated the BP intention–PA association, indicating for whom a higher overall rate of intending translated into greater activity. Social support and self-reinforcement moderated the WP intention–PA association, indicating for whom momentary intentions more strongly predicted subsequent activity. Momentary focus moderated the WP association at the occasion level, indicating when within a person intentions were more predictive, and momentary procrastination moderated the BP association. All seven effects were compensatory rather than augmenting: The intention–PA association was strongest among individuals lower in self-regulatory capacity and, for the momentary states, on occasions when a person's capacity was lower than usual. These findings suggest that momentary intentions may serve as an alternative route to activity when self-regulatory capacity is low. Just-in-time intervention strategies that support the formation of momentary intentions among individuals and moments of greatest self-regulatory vulnerability may be useful for improving PA.

title: Teachers’ attitudes and behavioural intentions towards AI integration in Chinese higher education: a qualitative interview study
container-title: Frontiers in Psychology
c6fe4330bbf5fd4fe3ac0771cb768c511236b747.abstract: Introduction The rapid expansion of generative AI has intensified scholarly and policy debate over its role in higher education, yet university teachers’ attitudes towards its integration remain complex and context-dependent. This study explores how university teachers perceive, experience, and respond to AI integration in their teaching. Guided primarily by the three-component attitude model and informed by the technology acceptance model and the theory of planned behaviour, the study examines cognitive appraisals, affective responses, behavioural intentions, and perceived support needs. Methods The study draws on semi-structured interviews with 14 university teachers from four higher education institutions in China. The interview data were analysed using codebook-informed thematic analysis combining deductive and inductive coding. Results The findings indicate that teachers generally perceive AI as a supportive rather than substitutive educational tool, valuing it for improving efficiency, supporting lesson preparation, and enriching pedagogical design. Emotional responses varied from enthusiasm and a sense of accomplishment to caution, neutrality, and, in some cases, declining satisfaction. Across the interviews, teachers’ primary concerns centred less on their own replacement than on the perceived risks of inappropriate AI use for students’ independent thinking, reasoning, originality, and authentic understanding. Teachers’ intentions to adopt AI were therefore conditional and bounded, shaped by pedagogical purpose, disciplinary context, student readiness, and the need to maintain teacher control. Teachers also emphasised that sustainable AI integration requires more than general encouragement, calling instead for AI literacy development, discipline-sensitive support, specialised tools, and enabling institutional infrastructure. Discussion Overall, these findings extend contextual understandings of teachers’ AI acceptance by showing how adoption intentions are pedagogically negotiated and highlight the importance of supporting professional judgement and students’ independent thinking in higher education.

title: Constructing the Self Data Atlas ontology: a crisp-fuzzy ontology for quality of life representation in children with neurodevelopmental and learning disabilities
container-title: Frontiers in Public Health
5bf2a2317c8b790b370e68fa02d4598cebe2f53e.abstract: The lived experiences of children with neurodevelopmental and learning disabilities are documented through diverse forms of personal data, including identity, medical, mental health, accomplishments, social relationships, financial resources, and personal ecology. However, these records rarely integrate quality of life (QoL) information represented through validated multidimensional frameworks. Building on the gap identified in a companion narrative review, this paper presents a reproducible ontology engineering methodology for representing QoL in children with neurodevelopmental and learning disabilities. The paper presents a design-science methodology for constructing an ontology from the Self Research Institute's Self Data Atlas (SDA), a seven-category taxonomy for organizing longitudinal personal data. Derived from Wieringa's design-science framework, the methodology follows a seven-step protocol comprising: (1) competency-question-based requirements specification; (2) ontology reuse and re-engineering; (3) conceptualization; (4) crisp formalization in OWL 2 DL; (5) fuzzy formalization in Fuzzy OWL 2; (6) alignment with the Common Core Ontology (CCO) as a Basic Formal Ontology (BFO)-conformant mid-level scaffold; and (7) iterative evaluation and refinement. The methodology incorporates two complementary design features. First, it separates factual and classificatory information, including demographics, SNOMED CT diagnostic codes, and clinical observations, represented in classical description logic, from graded and context-dependent QoL concepts, including social inclusion, severity, intensity, and wellbeing, represented using fuzzy datatypes, fuzzy linguistic variables, and graded class membership. Second, it embeds tritemporal reasoning by assigning three temporal qualifiers to each SDA event, state, or information artifact: (1) absolute time, representing when the fact existed in reality; (2) ingestion time, representing when the record entered the system; and (3) assignment time, representing when an interpretative classification was applied. These temporal qualifiers are represented as ontology entities rather than opaque metadata. This tritemporal structure supports longitudinal queries, retrospective recording, and event-history replay. Each stage is illustrated using examples from the seven SDA categories. The paper illustrates how CCO classes provide stable upper-level abstractions for SDA components and interoperability with ICF, SNOMED CT, HL7 FHIR, and the Schalock–Verdugo QoL model. This paper makes a methodological rather than an empirical contribution. It provides a reproducible ontology engineering methodology for future SDA ontology development and related personal-data ontologies.

title: Automated assessment of healthcare de-escalation communication skills in a conversational AI virtual reality simulation
container-title: Frontiers in Digital Health
9bc424b8b0ee6bc350b4296b68f692e3f29c8284.abstract: Introduction Digital health training environments increasingly require scalable methods for assessing communication skills in realistic, interactive scenarios. This paper presents a comparative study of automated assessment approaches within a conversational AI virtual reality simulation designed for verbal de-escalation training. Methods A total of 20 nursing students completed the simulation, where their spoken responses were captured and converted to text through a speech-to-text system, and were evaluated across 11 de-escalation competencies. The evaluation compared three fine-tuned deep learning models (BERT, RoBERTa, and XLNet) with a modified RATAS, a rubric-driven framework that leverages large language models. Two experiments were conducted: one using controlled 100-item validation datasets for each section, and another using the real-world responses collected during the user study. Results On the validation datasets, the deep learning models achieved the highest performance, with RoBERTa obtaining an average accuracy of 0.9927, followed by BERT at 0.9900 and XLNet at 0.9790, while RATAS achieved 0.8554. On the student-response dataset, performance decreased for all approaches, with RoBERTa obtaining 0.8590 accuracy, RATAS 0.8181, BERT 0.8000, and XLNet 0.7681. Discussion These results suggest that transformer-based models perform best under controlled conditions, whereas RATAS demonstrated stability in grading across different dataset types. These preliminary findings support the feasibility of integrating deep learning and rubric-driven LLM-based automated assessment approaches for communication and de-escalation training in nursing education.

title: CT-based clinical deep learning radiomics nomogram for preoperative differentiation of pyelocaliceal upper tract urothelial carcinoma and xanthogranulomatous pyelonephritis
container-title: Frontiers in Oncology
e1ad172428dafa2eebafee98a0b304e956e03582.abstract: Objective This study sought to create a CT-based clinical deep learning radiomics (CDLR) model to noninvasively differentiate between pyelocaliceal upper tract urothelial carcinoma (UTUC) and xanthogranulomatous pyelonephritis (XGP) preoperatively, aiding in personalized treatment decisions. Methods A retrospective analysis included 161 patients with pathologically confirmed pyelocaliceal UTUC or XGP following surgery. Patients were randomly divided into a training cohort (n=112) and a validation cohort (n=49). Radiomics (Rad) features and deep learning (DL) features were extracted from the corticomedullary phase CT images. Combined with clinical features, and after feature selection, a logistic regression (LR) classifier was employed to construct the clinical model, the deep learning radiomics (DLR) model, and the clinical deep learning radiomics (CDLR) model. Model performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves and decision curve analysis (DCA), with interpretability assessed by the shapley additive explanations (SHAP) method. In addition, the diagnostic performance of the models was compared with that of a radiologist with 5 years of experience in abdominal CT diagnosis. Results The CDLR model achieved AUCs of 0.955 in the training cohort and 0.930 in the validation cohort. In the validation cohort, the CDLR model significantly outperformed the radiologist’s assessment (AUC: 0.930 vs. 0.695, P = 0.0006) and yielded numerically higher AUCs than the clinical model (0.823) and the DLR model (0.882). DCA indicated that the CDLR model provided the highest net clinical benefit. SHAP analysis demonstrated good model interpretability. Conclusion The CDLR model integrating clinical, Rad, and DL features serves as an effective noninvasive tool for preoperative differentiation of pyelocaliceal UTUC and XGP, offering valuable reference for clinical decision-making.

title: Uneven automation: comparing authorship anxiety and generative AI use among art and design undergraduate students
container-title: Frontiers in Psychology
8942b2ac014d5d2bac7e05011f209f96a5fce870.abstract: Art and design education expects students to develop a sense of authorship over original work, but generative AI (GenAI) complicates how students understand and claim that authorship. This study examined whether these experiences differ across creative fields through a mixed-methods design. The survey included 2,441 GenAI-using students from seven field categories at 33 art and design institutions in China and assessed authorship anxiety, creative agency, perceived usefulness, dependence on GenAI, and frequency of use. The quantitative analysis first examined variation across all seven categories and then compared fine art with the five applied design fields. Interview data from 22 survey participants were also examined thematically. The main findings include that (1) authorship anxiety did not differ significantly across the seven categories or between fine art and pooled design; the latter comparison met the equivalence criterion at ±d = 0.20, but not at tighter bounds; (2) clearer differences emerged in how students used GenAI. Compared with fine-art students, design students considered GenAI more useful and used it more frequently; (3) across the interviews, most students described authorship as retaining control over the creative idea while delegating parts of its execution to GenAI. Specifically, fine-art students often grounded authorship in embodied making and human imperfection, whereas design students placed greater emphasis on judgement, selection, and control. We call this pattern uneven automation: concern about authorship was broadly shared, but students in different fields responded to GenAI in different ways, potentially reflecting the varying labour-market pressures surrounding their disciplines.

title: Normative messages and students’ intentions to engage in collaborative learning: evidence from an experimental study
container-title: Frontiers in Psychology
fe8046e0511f99c9a176779159ad5d1accefe165.abstract: Introduction Despite the recognized benefits of collaborative learning, students’ voluntary participation in activities such as group reading remains limited. This study examined students’ intentions to engage in collaborative learning and explored whether a brief normative-message intervention varied as a function of norm framing and message source. Methods In a 2 × 2 between-subjects online experiment, 183 students at the University of Tehran were randomly assigned to one of four conditions combining dynamic versus static descriptive norms with identity-proximal versus identity-distal message sources. Subjective behavioral intention and anticipated participation frequency were analyzed as separate outcomes. Attitudes, injunctive and descriptive norms, perceived behavioral control, behavior-related student identity linkage, and previous-semester participation frequency were also assessed. Data were analyzed using multiple regression, two-way multivariate analysis of variance, and exploratory moderation analyses. Results Attitudes, perceived behavioral control, previous-semester participation frequency, and behavior-related student identity linkage were significant correlates of anticipated participation frequency, whereas demographic characteristics, injunctive norms, and descriptive norms were not significant predictors. However, the experimental manipulation was unsuccessful: participants receiving dynamic and static messages did not differ significantly in perceived past-to-present norm change or expected future norm growth. Consistent with the failed manipulation, neither assigned norm type nor assigned message source, nor their interaction, significantly affected either outcome, and effect sizes were negligible. An exploratory interaction between assigned norm condition and behavior-related student identity linkage reached statistical significance, but no conditional effect was significant and no region of significance was identified; therefore, this finding should not be interpreted as evidence of a substantive moderation effect. Discussion Because perceived source proximity was not assessed following the manipulation, the null source effect cannot be interpreted as evidence that source proximity is ineffective. Overall, the study documents an unsuccessful single-exposure normative-message manipulation while identifying attitudinal, perceived-control, prior-participation, and identity-related variables as correlates of participation intentions. The findings underscore the importance of verifying normative perceptions and source identification before drawing conclusions about the downstream effects of normative interventions.

title: Mapping abortion regulation in US states: a subnational application of a global framework
container-title: Frontiers in Reproductive Health
843858e99d5166bfbea763697615b03fb3f55943.abstract: Background Following the overturning of Roe v. Wade by Dobbs v. Jackson Women's Health Organization , abortion regulation in the United States (US) is now regulated by individual states, producing a fragmented legal landscape that complicates efforts to assess how state laws align with human rights standards and public health guidance. A recently developed global framework classifies abortion regulation into several models grounded in human rights standards and public health guidance. When adapted, this framework can classify US states, situate them within a global context, and support comparison of state law against these standards. Methods A state-level comparative legal and policy analysis was conducted using data from four organizations that track US abortion law (Bloomberg Law, Center for Reproductive Rights, Guttmacher Institute, and Kaiser Family Foundation), extracted between June 22 and July 4, 2026. The framework was adapted into six models, each representing a different abortion legal environment. States were categorized through a sequential coding process based on four pre-specified criteria: legal status, exceptions, criminal penalties, and healthcare integration. Results No state fell within the criminalization or decriminalization-without-legalization models. 13 states were classified under the restrictive model, 23 under abortion-specific laws and policies with partial decriminalization, ten under abortion-specific laws and policies with full decriminalization, and four (California, Massachusetts, New Jersey, and New York) under legalization as healthcare. Conclusion The distribution of states supports the framework's central claim that decriminalization and legalization are distinct processes that do not necessarily advance together. Most states fall in the middle of the spectrum, with only four integrating abortion into healthcare, consistent with the literature on abortion exceptionalism. The adapted framework offers a replicable, updatable method for situating US states within a global context and monitoring where their abortion laws sit relative to human rights standards and public health guidance, which current international mechanisms, focused on the national level, do not fully capture.

title: Digital transformation, traceability, and supply chain resilience in food manufacturing SMEs: a review of AI, blockchain-IoT, and institutional mechanisms
container-title: Frontiers in Sustainable Food Systems
c0821ee379eb16d2e0252633d6030dd152fbd833.abstract: Food supply chains in China face persistent challenges of food safety risks, inadequate transparency, and supply disruptions, with food manufacturing small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) disproportionately vulnerable due to limited resources and non-standardized internal processes. Digital transformation encompassing artificial intelligence (AI), blockchain, Internet of Things (IoT), and digital twin technologies is increasingly regarded as a strategic solution to strengthen supply chain resilience, yet the organizational and institutional conditions under which these digital investments translate into tangible resilience improvements for food manufacturing SMEs remain poorly understood. This review conducts a PRISMA 2020-compliant systematic review and thematic synthesis of 40 multidisciplinary sources spanning the food safety, supply chain management, and information systems literatures. Drawing on Dynamic Capabilities Theory and Institutional Theory, we propose an integrative conceptual framework comprising six research propositions, in which traceability capability acts as a food-safety-specific mediating mechanism linking digital transformation to supply chain resilience, while regulatory stringency moderates the strength of this indirect pathway. A central argument of this framework is that deploying blockchain, IoT, or AI hardware does not itself constitute traceability capability the institutional and organisational conditions under which digital tools are adopted determine whether firms build substantive traceability capability or engage in symbolic compliance without genuine food safety governance improvement. Three key contributions distinguish this framework: conceptualizing traceability capability as a distinct dynamic capability rather than a generic digitalization mechanism; directing analytical focus explicitly toward food manufacturing SMEs, a population largely overlooked in existing large-firm panel studies; and introducing regulatory stringency as a first-stage moderator within a moderated mediation structure. Critical research gaps are identified, including the absence of SME-calibrated digital transformation measurement instruments, the lack of a validated multi-item traceability capability scale, and a complete empirical vacuum for testing the proposed moderated mediation model in food manufacturing SME contexts. This review provides a structured future research agenda for scholars and delivers actionable insights for practitioners and policymakers seeking to direct digital technology investments toward improved food safety governance in China’s food manufacturing sector.

title: Opportunities for creative thinking in an out-of-school learning environment: perceptions and experiences of children attending the Discovery Campus
container-title: Frontiers in Psychology
5b061da5aee0a14356de53f31c3b9eaea1527678.abstract: Creative thinking emerges as a critical skill that adds meaning to individuals’ lives in today’s competitive world. One of the learning environments aimed at developing this skill is the Discovery Campus, which serves as a children’s university. This qualitative study aimed to investigate the perceptions and experiences regarding creative thinking of 32 children aged 11–13 who regularly attend the Discovery Campus in Gaziantep, Türkiye. The participants were selected through criterion sampling, a purposive sampling method. Data were collected via written interview forms and analysed using the content analysis method. The findings indicated that participants perceive the Discovery Campus as a learning environment where, in addition to acquiring new knowledge, they can apply what they have learned, discover their own potential, and develop original ideas. It was determined that creative project ideas aim to develop solutions to problems based on the needs of humans, society, and living organisms; and that experiences at the Discovery Campus are associated with an approach based on hands-on learning, material use, enquiry, observation, and imagination, which differs from formal school environments. Furthermore, in the children’s narratives, it was observed that opportunities for creative thinking are shaped by the processes of conducting research, focusing on areas of interest, participating in workshop activities, transforming ideas into projects, and sharing the developed designs. Accordingly, in order to support children’s creative thinking processes, it is recommended to expand science centres that bring together different disciplines and provide opportunities for practical application and project production.

title: Human-in-the-loop semantic learning analytics for assessing moral-value reasoning in university AI ethics education
container-title: Frontiers in Psychology
4c153cd19693204269d4536c8e62024e2ea30575.abstract: Introduction University AI ethics education addresses fairness, privacy, accountability, transparency, human autonomy, and academic integrity, but the semantic structure of students' moral-value reasoning and its connection to responsible solutions remain insufficiently characterized. This study examined a human-in-the-loop semantic learning analytics framework for task-specific moral-value reasoning. Methods Ninety science and engineering graduate students completed an online explicit-reflective AI ethics module in a one-group pre–post multimethod study without a control group. Assessments comprised an AI ethics knowledge test, a perceived-awareness scale, and open-ended ethical reasoning tasks. Expert annotations informed transformer-based multi-label coding, descriptive value coverage and balance metrics, problem–solution coupling, and baseline-only nested cross-validated prediction of subsequent raw problem-solving change. Results Within-participant pre–post increases were observed in ethical knowledge, perceived moral-value awareness, actual ethical awareness, problem–solving skills, value coverage, value balance, and problem–solution coupling. Automated semantic coding achieved participant-grouped cross-validated macro-F1 = 0.83 (95% CI [0.78, 0.87]; micro-F1 = 0.86; macro-AUPRC = 0.82). The baseline-only prediction model yielded cross-validated R 2 = 0.30 (95% CI [0.11, 0.45]) for subsequent raw problem-solving change. Discussion Expert-supervised semantic analytics can characterize value representation and issue–solution reasoning in AI ethics assessments. Coverage and balance describe response structure rather than moral quality. The absence of a control group, repeated use of one scenario, and modest sample size preclude causal and broad trait-level conclusions.

title: Deciphering natural alkaline water-induced human molecular homeostatic regulation via non-invasive sweat metabolic profiling
container-title: Frontiers in Bioengineering and Biotechnology
fd3e3562b80aa5aeb05a0d20f6412c0ba0f64eb1.abstract: Natural alkaline water, a weakly alkaline NaHCO 3 ‐enriched solution, has been postulated to modulate systemic metabolic homeostasis, but its clinical metabolic effects remain poorly characterized due to the scarcity of non-invasive, longitudinal molecular evidence. Conventional flexible microneedles for sweat analysis are limited to single‐analyte detection, failing to meet the need for simultaneous profiling of multiple biomarkers required to assess systemic homeostasis. To address these challenges, we engineered a hierarchical metal‐carbide (MXene)‐based flexible microneedle array integrated with high‐performance mass spectrometry, establishing a non‐invasive, high‐throughput sweat metabolic profiling platform. Here, we show that the hierarchical architecture, featuring a petal‐like AgNWs@MXene heterostructure, creates synergistic hotspots that enhance laser desorption/ionization mass spectrometry (LDI‐MS) signal intensity by more than twofold compared with pristine MXene, allowing robust detection of 77 ± 8 metabolic features from a single sweat‐patch sample. In a cohort study (n = 107), this platform enabled simultaneous dynamic monitoring of key metabolic features associated with uric acid, lactate, and glutamine (p &lt; 0.001). Overall, this work reveals the regulatory effects of natural alkaline water on metabolic homeostasis and provides a scalable, high‐throughput strategy for non‐invasive multi‐feature sweat metabolic profiling.

title: Physiological markers of low-altitude exercise load for predicting acute mountain sickness: development of an interpretable machine learning model and research web calculator
container-title: Frontiers in Public Health
ebb10a5d0b2d2954c1d608ffb7d6d6db97a9b27c.abstract: Acute mountain sickness (AMS) poses a significant threat to individuals ascending to high-altitude regions, yet early identification of susceptible populations remains challenging. This study aimed to develop an interpretable machine learning model for estimating AMS risk from exercise-induced physiological responses measured at low altitude. A total of 171 healthy participants were included, with 111 participants (51 AMS events) comprising the development cohort and 60 participants (27 AMS events) forming an external validation cohort. Model development was repeated within a nested cross-validation framework, including LASSO feature selection and algorithm selection within the resampling process. The final locked five-feature model included changes in post-exercise pulse oxygen saturation (ΔSpO 2 ) and cardiac output (ΔCO), sex, smoking history, and drinking history, and combined logistic regression, support vector machine, and random forest by equal-weight soft voting. In the development cohort, pooled outer-fold predictions yielded an AUC of 0.866 (95% CI, 0.791–0.929), an AUPRC of 0.842 (95% CI, 0.748–0.932), and a Brier score of 0.148. The calibration intercept was −0.033 (95% CI, −0.504 to 0.527), the calibration slope was 0.931 (95% CI, 0.664–1.351) and the positive net benefit range was 0.078–0.840. In the external validation cohort, the locked model yielded an AUC of 0.834 (95% CI, 0.723–0.929), an AUPRC of 0.867 (95% CI, 0.758–0.946), and a Brier score of 0.152; the calibration intercept was −0.103 (95% CI, −0.834 to 0.531), the calibration slope was 1.013 (95% CI, 0.655–1.666) and a positive net benefit range of 0.200–0.953. Post-hoc SHAP analysis identified ΔSpO 2 and ΔCO as the two most influential predictors. These findings support an association between low-altitude exercise responses and subsequent AMS. However, the prediction model requires further development and validation in substantially larger cohorts before clinical deployment.

title: LncRNA‑AK158273 suppresses lipopolysaccharide‑triggered autophagy by up‑regulation of Mst1 expression in microglia
container-title: Frontiers in Molecular Neuroscience
49cbe717ae3b7bdddb0818cf3f36dfdeb6702de8.abstract: Introduction The aim of the present study was to investigate the mechanism by which lncR-AK158273 regulates autophagy in lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-induced neuroinflammation cognitive impairment (LPS-NCI). Methods LPS was used to establish a mouse of neuroinflammation‑mediated cognitive dysfunction. Cognitive deficits in the LPS‑NCI model were assessed using the new-object recognition test and Y maze test. Immunohistochemistry and immunofluorescence were performed to evaluate neuronal injury and the expression of CD11b, phosphorylated (p)-tau, and total tau. ELISA was used to quantify the levels of TNF-α and IL-6. RT-qPCR and western blotting were applied to measure the mRNA expression of STK4 and lncR-AK158273, as well as the protein levels of Mst1 and autophagy-related proteins. In addition, si-lncR-AK158273 or pcDNA-lncRNA-AK158273 was transfected into LPS‑stimulated BV2 cells to explore the function of this lncRNA in autophagy. Autophagosomes were visualized by transmission electron microscopy. Autophagic flux was determined using mRFP-GFP-LC3 fluorescence tracing with chloroquine (CQ) treatment to block lysosomal degradation. Results The results showed that LPS markedly elevated the protein levels of CD11b, TNF-α, IL-6, p-tau, Aβ 1–42, and P62, while reduing Beclin-1 expression and the LC3II/LC3I ratio, thereby suppressing autophagy in both LPS‑NCI mice and LPS-stimulated BV2 cells ( P &lt; 0.05). Futhermore, lncR-AK158273 and STK4(Mst1) were significantly upregulated in LPS‑NCI mice and LPS-treated BV2 cells. Follow-up experiments verified that lncR-AK158273 upregulates Mst1 expression upon LPS stimulation. Moreover, lncR-AK158273 suppressed LPS‑triggered microglial autophagy by increasing Mst1 level. Discussion lncR-AK158273 may inhibit microglial autograph via upregulation of Mst1 expression during LPS-induced neuroinflammation.

title: Perceived AI literacy and TPACK in pre-service teacher education: mediating roles of perceived usefulness, ease of use, and value in blended learning
container-title: Frontiers in Psychology
1bad51d2ab1c081fcbf1788c8c81f98f9ce0044c.abstract: Background The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into blended learning requires pre-service teachers to develop AI-related competencies and the ability to integrate technology into pedagogy. This study examines how perceived AI literacy and technological pedagogical content knowledge (TPACK) are associated with deep learning through perceived usefulness, perceived ease of use, and perceived value of AI use. Methods A cross-sectional survey was completed by 423 pre-service teachers enrolled in blended learning courses at a university in China. Data were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM), with covariance-based structural equation modeling and fuzzy-set qualitative comparative analysis (fsQCA) used as complementary robustness and configurational analyses. Results Perceived usefulness, perceived ease of use, and perceived value of AI use significantly mediated the relationships between the two competencies and deep learning. All six indirect pathways were significant in both the PLS-SEM and covariance-based SEM analyses. The fsQCA revealed an equifinal and asymmetric structure: multiple, partly substitutable conditions were sufficient for high deep learning, and no single condition was necessary for either high or low deep learning. Conclusions The findings integrate the technology acceptance model and expectancy-value theory to explain how pre-service teachers' competencies and perceptions relate to deep learning in AI-enhanced blended environments. Teacher education should support technical competence alongside positive perceptions of AI's utility, usability, and value. Because the measures were self-reported and collected cross-sectionally at one university, the findings are interpreted as associational and configurational rather than causal.

title: Effectiveness of an AI-Based Educational Video Generator in Enhancing Oral Health Knowledge and Behavior Among Children: A Randomized Controlled Trial
container-title: Al-Rafidain Journal of Medical Sciences ( ISSN 2789-3219 )
025217a90eae33a9efbb4f3e4378042549e3202e.abstract: Background: Artificial intelligence (AI) is a new innovation that presents an opportunity for oral health education in children. Objective: To evaluate the effectiveness of an AI-assisted educational video versus standardized in-person oral health education for children regarding oral health knowledge and behaviors. Methods: This randomized controlled trial included 300 children aged 10-12 years (n=150 per group), both boys and girls, who were divided into AI video and standardized face-to-face oral health education groups. Baseline and 2-week follow-up evaluations were conducted for knowledge scores, four behavioral items, and the Silness and Löe Plaque Index. The internal consistency of the knowledge scale was checked (Cronbach's α=0.79). Wilcoxon signed-rank and Mann–Whitney U tests were the primary non-parametric tests used for statistical evaluations, with a median, (IQR), and effect size r provided. Chi-square tests with a Bonferroni adjustment at α=0.0125 were used to evaluate behavioral items. Results: There were significant enhancements in intra-group knowledge (p<0.0001 for both groups; r=0.663 for AI; r=0.345 for Control). The clinical efficacy was similar for both strategies with significant reduction of intra-group plaque (AI: p< 0.001, r= 0.425; Control: p< 0.001, r= 0.331), but no inter-group difference at the end of the intervention (p= 0.608; r= 0.030). In the conventional group, the utilization of dental floss was significantly improved (p=0.0056), and no other behaviors showed significant improvement across groups. Conclusions: The AI-assisted educational video demonstrated better knowledge retention than the standardized face-to-face oral health education, achieved similar clinical plaque reduction, and can be easily scaled for pediatric preventive dentistry.

title: Eco-social pedagogy through outdoor learning in early childhood education: Teachers' outdoor practices in northern Spain
container-title: Journal of Childhood, Education & Society
494f3af76073e962037909467ce7943c47c05565.abstract: Early childhood education is increasingly recognised as a critical space for cultivating climate awareness, care, and agency through embodied and relational learning, with outdoor education emerging as a particularly powerful context for this development. This mixed-methods study examines how educators in regular schools in the Basque Country (Northern Spain) describe the role of sustained engagement with nearby ecosystems in supporting eco-social pedagogies and education for sustainability in early childhood settings. Data were collected through questionnaires completed by educators representing schools participating in the Forest School Network (n = 28 schools), complemented by 21 semi-structured interviews with teachers who regularly engage in outdoor learning in nearby ecosystems. Findings indicate that outdoor environments function as emotionally secure and pedagogically generative spaces where children engage in place-based practices such as tree planting, litter collection, habitat creation, monitoring invasive species, measuring water and air temperature, participating in citizen science initiatives, and using local ecological knowledge, including Basque species names. Educators described these everyday practices as fostering eco-social dispositions grounded in care, relational ethics, agency, and shared environmental responsibility. Teachers described a professional shift from transmitting environmental knowledge toward facilitating inquiry, empathy, and collective forms of environmental care. At the same time, many educators identify gaps in institutional support and climate-related training within teacher education programmes. By situating these insights within current debates on early childhood climate education, the study contributes grounded empirical evidence on how educators perceive the relationship between eco-social pedagogy, outdoor learning and environmental education in early childhood settings. It suggests that outdoor education, when framed as emotional, agential, ethical, and community-oriented engagement, is perceived by educators as creating opportunities to encourage dispositions associated with environmental responsibility, care, and sustainability.

title: Modern Approaches to Teaching Mathematics to Primary School Students in a Digital Learning Environment
container-title: The Journal of Interdisciplinary Human Studies
a96be798bb994247daa8f325fdb8751fbd140856.abstract: This article examines modern approaches to teaching mathematics to primary school students in a digital learning environment, focusing on interdisciplinary integration. The study uses theoretical analysis, comparative analysis, and generalization of pedagogical literature to explore how digital resources can support mathematics instruction. The analysis suggests that interactive exercises, electronic textbooks, visual materials, and educational software offer opportunities to explain mathematical concepts, support independent practice, and provide feedback. Connecting mathematics with language, natural sciences, technology, and everyday situations may help students apply mathematical knowledge in practical contexts. Effective implementation requires teachers to align digital resources with lesson objectives, students’ developmental characteristics, and available technical facilities. The article concludes that combining digital tools with integrated teaching offers pedagogical opportunities for primary mathematics education, while empirical research is needed to assess its effects on students’ learning outcomes.

title:
Interpretable
Machine-Learning Prediction of Pollutant
Adsorption and Degradation by MnO2 in Aqueous Systems
container-title: ACS ES&T Water
b75399c1a421e5298761a198776cccae82d42d1e.abstract: Abstract Manganese dioxide (MnO2) is a key redox-active mineral governing pollutant migration and transformation, making quantitative prediction of MnO2–pollutant interactions essential for evaluating contaminant fate. Here, we compiled two data sets covering MnO2 adsorption and abiotic degradation across 7 MnO2 structural categories, 48 organic pollutants, and 27 inorganic pollutants. By integrating molecular descriptors, separate machine learning models were developed for predicting log qmax and log kobs. Random forest achieved a mean test R2 of 0.69 for adsorption, whereas CatBoost reached 0.82 and 0.83 for degradation using PaDEL and RDKit descriptors, respectively. Permutation importance and SHAP analysis showed that adsorption was weighted primarily toward environmental conditions, whereas degradation predictions depended jointly on environmental conditions and pollutant properties. SHAP dependence and PDP analyses further clarified feature–prediction relationships, identifying pollutant concentration as the dominant adsorption predictor, likely reflecting concentration-dependent site saturation and isotherm design, while reaction pH and molecular descriptors were the dominant predictors of degradation. The models were integrated into a graphical user interface to enable rapid prediction of MnO2 reactivity. By integrating contaminant retention and transformation into a unified, interpretable framework, this study provides predictions and testable mechanistic hypotheses for contaminant fate in Mn-bearing aquatic systems.

title: Deep learning versus conventional risk scores for postoperative mortality prediction in adult cardiac surgery: a systematic review
container-title: The Cardiothoracic Surgeon
87de45a40c7853e884326e69cad353574c5553a1.abstract: Abstract Background Earlier reviews of machine learning for mortality after cardiac surgery pooled deep learning (DL) with shallow and non-neural methods. We asked whether models meeting an explicit definition of DL discriminate short-term mortality better than EuroSCORE II, the Society of Thoracic Surgeons Predicted Risk of Mortality (STS-PROM) or logistic regression in the same patients. Methods This re-conducted review (PROSPERO CRD420261354546) supersedes an earlier preprint. MEDLINE, Europe PMC, Lens.org and IEEE Xplore were searched on 27–28 September 2026, with backward citation searching; Embase, CINAHL and CENTRAL were not searched, and forward citation searching was not performed. DL required at least two hidden layers, or a named architecture of established depth, shown in the source. A large language model pre-screened records and extracted data; two reviewers verified every decision and value. Risk of bias was assessed with PROBAST + AI, and results were synthesised without meta-analysis as within-cohort differences in the area under the curve (AUC). Results Of 1,845 records identified, 515 duplicates were removed and 1,330 were screened; of 76 reports sought, 54 were assessed in full and 22 could not be retrieved. Four studies (five cohort-level comparisons) met all criteria. A chest-radiograph convolutional network had lower AUCs than STS-PROM in temporal (0.829 vs. 0.884) and external (0.738 vs. 0.803) cohorts with about two dozen deaths each; two-hidden-layer perceptrons did not outperform logistic regression (0.761 vs. 0.762; 0.77 vs. 0.80); one study reported AUCs only graphically. All four studies had high or unclear risk of bias. Fifteen reports described networks of undetermined depth, including a tabular transformer that outperformed EuroSCORE II internally (0.834 vs. 0.807); in the 12 with extractable comparisons, the network had a higher AUC than the best comparator in 4 and lower in 8 (median difference − 0.004). Conclusions Evidence that DL improves on established scores for short-term mortality after adult cardiac surgery is sparse, inconsistent and at high or unclear risk of bias, and the search was incomplete relative to the registered protocol. Differences in discrimination were small or absent, and calibration and clinical utility were rarely evaluated. Superiority cannot be established. PROSPERO registration This review was registered on PROSPERO, the International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews, on 29 March 2026 (CRD420261354546; https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/prospero/). At registration, the record stated that searching and screening for an earlier version of the review had been completed and that data extraction had not started. That earlier version was posted as a preprint on 31 March 2026 (Preprints.org, doi:10.20944/preprints202603.2465.v1); it is superseded by this report. Its withdrawal was requested from Preprints.org on 18 October 2026 and had not been confirmed at the time of resubmission. The review reported here was re-conducted in full after registration: the searches were run on 27–28 September 2026, and screening, data extraction and risk-of-bias assessment followed. The registered eligibility criteria were not changed in substance; the registered deep-learning criterion was operationalised before full-text assessment and, after peer review, applied more strictly (a post hoc change reported in the manuscript). The search sources, risk-of-bias tool and synthesis method differ from the registered protocol. Every difference, with its timing and reason, is reported in Table 1 of the manuscript, and an amendment describing them has been submitted to PROSPERO.

title: Improving Learner Performance Through Score Based Analysis on a Gamified AI Driven Cybersecurity Learning Platform
d2b1981b0d01f6ee261a12a86c8c602586119c26.abstract: Abstract This study examines whether structured engagement with instructional content improves learner performance on Cyber Security Academy, an AI-driven, gamified cybersecurity learning platform. Activity logs covering 1,500 completed assessments from users in ten Anglophone and Francophone countries were analyzed by comparing learners who consulted the lessons and completed the full learning pathway (n = 900) with those who engaged only partially with the platform (n = 600). Group differences were tested with Welch's t-test, the Mann Whitney U test, one-way ANOVA, Spearman correlations, and Cohen's d as a measure of effect size. Learners who read the lessons before assessment obtained a mean score of 71.27 % versus 60.41 % for non-readers (Δ = +10.86 points; t(1192) = 12.21; p < 0.001; d = 0.650; 95 % CI [9.12, 12.60]), committed fewer errors (2.50 vs. 4.85; d = -1.069), and responded faster (9.85 vs. 12.69 minutes; d = -0.807), indicating greater fluency of cognitive processing. The effect decreased monotonically with age (d = 1.205 for learners aged 13 and under; d = 0.387 for those 22 and over) and with digital literacy (d = 1.434 for beginners; d = 0.524 for experts), while remaining positive in all ten countries. These findings indicate that structured, AI-personalized, and gamified learning environments substantially enhance cybersecurity learning outcomes, particularly for younger and less experienced users.

title: Design of a compact rotational compliant stage with self-compensation for rotation center offset
container-title: Mechanical Sciences
fa9b231cfbfa1c69919419c826b4c3662743d899.abstract: Compliant rotational stages are widely used for the fine angular positioning of optical components, where rotation center stability is critical to positioning accuracy. However, conventional designs often suffer from rotation center offset. A rotational compliant mechanism with self-compensation for rotation center offset is proposed based on a two-stage lever amplification system incorporating a non-vertical connecting beam and a double-ended fixed flexure hinge. The input force transmitted to the second-stage lever is decomposed into two orthogonal components. The y direction component drives the secondary lever to generate rotational motion, whereas the x direction component produces a negative x direction displacement through the double-ended fixed flexure hinge, thereby compensating for the rotation center offset. A kinematic analysis and a compliance model are established, based on which multi-objective dimensional optimization is performed to balance the rotational output and the center-offset indicator. The optimized design is subsequently evaluated using COMSOL finite element simulations. Under a prescribed relative input displacement of 28 µm, the mechanism produces an output rotation of 3.12 mrad, with a first natural frequency of 572 Hz and a maximum center offset of 0.42 µm. The stage has overall dimensions of 51 mm × 78 mm. These numerical results indicate that the proposed configuration can reduce rotation center offset and parasitic translational coupling under the adopted idealized simulation conditions.

title: Search-based agents outperform reinforcement learning in Dahal Jeet, a Nepaliimperfect-information card game
3f9f3d6a8996de2c0c8dd95436138f4cc9bcab48.abstract: Abstract Dahal Jeet is a four-player partnership card game played daily across the Terai- Madhesh region of Nepal, in which only the four tens score. Its objective is lexicographic rather than additive: a majority of tens decides most hands, trick count the rest. The game belongs to the documented Mendikot branch of the Court Piece family, matching Mendikot on 21 of 26 compared features, but the Nepali variant has no published rule description, and the indexed literature returns one paper on the entire family. We contribute a formal specification of the ruleset, drawn from the first author’s own play across seven districts, and a computational study built on it. 26 agents spanning hand-written heuristics, metaheuristic tuning, determinized search and seven learning families are compared across 325 pairings under duplicate-deal protocols with bootstrap intervals and family-wise error control. Search dominates: information-set Monte Carlo tree search leads and no learner reaches a tuned heuristic. An exact doubledummy solver shows search converts 0.923 of theoretically won endgames against 0.810 for the best heuristic. A minimal state encoding outperforms a rich handdesigned one, every deterministic heuristic is exploitable by a search that knows its policy, and the deal alone explains up to 0.391 of outcome variance.

title: Development of A Diagnostic Assessment Instrument For Mathematics Learning For Grade II Elementary School
container-title: International Journal of Educational Research & Social Sciences
8f20a5f7eeb26cf3ebda572e880bd34d2fe1baa2.abstract: This study aims to develop a valid diagnostic assessment instrument for second-grade elementary school mathematics (addition and subtraction of whole numbers). Existing diagnostic instruments mostly target other grade levels or focus on misconceptions, while lower-grade teachers still need a ready-to-use instrument that links students’ answers to coding, interpretation, and follow-up actions. This research and development study used a 3D model (Define, Design, Develop) modified from Thiagarajan’s 4D model. The product is a 12-item instrument (5 multiple-choice and 7 short-answer items; maximum score 19) with a test blueprint, answer keys, coding guidelines, interpretation, and follow-up plans. Validation by two expert lecturers and one classroom teacher yielded an average validity of 86.67% (very valid). A small-group trial with five students produced a mean score of 83.16; two students were in the “full understanding” category and three in the “partial understanding” category. The least mastered indicators were addition with regrouping and subtraction with borrowing (two of five students each). The instrument is valid and feasible as a teacher’s tool for mapping students’ initial understanding; its effectiveness and psychometric properties need to be tested with larger samples.

title: AI Labour Rights Awareness and Career Adaptation Confidence among Respondents in Bangladesh
4bebd9cda335afcb1b14dbb90e41e4c4857a6c33.abstract: Abstract Artificial intelligence changes both the skills used at work and the conditions under which employment decisions are made. Awareness of these changes does not necessarily coincide with confidence in adapting a career. This study examines that distinction in 385 adult, AI-aware survey records from Bangladesh, including 238 law students and 61 respondents classified as law graduates. Five statements separately assess awareness of workplace rights and responsibilities, recognition of protection from unfair automated decisions, reported complementary skill development, adaptation confidence and the perceived preparedness benefit of understanding labour issues. Analyses combine full response distributions, joint endorsement patterns, paired comparisons, ordinal correlations and an exploratory proportional-odds model. Recognition of the need for protection was endorsed by 79.2%, compared with 48.8% endorsing adaptation confidence, a paired difference of 30.4 percentage points (95% bootstrap interval 23.9–36.6). General rights awareness and skill development had small positive ordinal associations with confidence. In the adjusted ordinal model, their odds ratios were 1.30 (95% interval 1.04–1.61; Holm p = 0.038) and 1.40 (1.09–1.79; Holm p = 0.024) respectively. The protection-recognition estimate was less certain, although the two awareness coefficients were not demonstrably different. The findings distinguish rights recognition, reported action and confidence rather than establish a causal awareness-to-adaptability pathway. They support evaluating legal-literacy education alongside practical career tasks and institutional safeguards. The mixed sample, study-specific single items, undocumented recruitment and fieldwork dates, and source-documentation limitations constrain inference. A subsequent study should use verified graduate eligibility, independent legal-knowledge assessments and longitudinal career outcomes.

title: Factors Influencing In-Hospital and Long-Term Mortality in Patients with Acute ST-Elevation Myocardial Infarction Undergoing Primary Percutaneous Intervention
container-title: Journal of the Medical Association of Thailand
d443e240b78d3e721616d91ea55a707954e529a0.abstract: Objective: To identify factors associated with in-hospital and long-term mortality among patients with ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) undergoing primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) in a regional hospital in Thailand. Materials and Methods: This retrospective cohort study analyzed patients with STEMI who received primary PCI from January 2014 to December 2022. Demographic characteristics, clinical presentation, angiographic findings, procedural details, and clinical outcomes were extracted from medical records. The primary outcome was long-term all-cause mortality during a 3-year follow-up period. Survival probabilities were estimated using the Kaplan-Meier method, and Cox proportional hazards regression assessed factors associated with long-term mortality. Statistically significant defined as p<0.05. Results: The 283 patients with STEMI undergoing primary PCI were analyzed, with 12 (4.2%) dying during hospitalization. Long-term survival data included 270 patients. 3-year and 5-year survival rates were 81.0% and 78.4%, respectively. Non-survivors were older and presented with greater clinical severity. Kaplan-Meier analysis showed significantly lower survival among patients with Killip class III-IV and those who achieved a myocardial blush grade (MBG) ≤2 after PCI (log-rank p<0.001). Multivariable Cox regression, age >65 years, left ventricular dysfunction, mechanical ventilation, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, a greater number of stents, and severe coronary calcification on angiography were independently associated with increased long-term mortality. In contrast, achievement of MBG 3 (adjusted HR 0.28, 95% CI 0.13-0.64, p=0.002), longer duration of dual antiplatelet therapy (adjusted HR 0.07, 95% CI 0.02-0.28, p<0.001), and eGFR 60-89 mL/minute/1.73 m² (adjusted HR 0.24, 95% CI 0.09-0.65, p=0.005) were independently associated with lower long-term mortality. Conclusion: Long-term mortality remained substantial. Older age and greater clinical severity were associated with poorer outcomes, whereas achievement of MBG 3 was associated with improved long-term survival, highlighting the importance of early risk stratification and optimized reperfusion strategies

title: Efektivitas Penggunaan Model Cooperative Learning Berbantuan Media Konkret Takalintar Terhadap Pemahaman Konsep Perkalian Bersusun
container-title: Master Journal of Future Education
b41b69bc91eb0f3fc0f2d7c75a35b9f1102d5fd0.abstract: Penelitian ini dilatarbelakangi oleh rendahnya pemahaman siswa kelas III SDN 101/II Muara Bungo terhadap konsep perkalian bersusun, khususnya pada tahap penyimpanan angka dan penempatan nilai tempat. Kondisi tersebut ditemukan melalui observasi awal yang menunjukkan pembelajaran matematika masih berpusat pada guru dan belum memanfaatkan media konkret secara optimal. Penelitian ini bertujuan mengetahui pengaruh dan efektivitas model Cooperative Learning berbantuan media konkret Takalintar terhadap pemahaman konsep perkalian bersusun siswa kelas III. Metode yang digunakan adalah eksperimen dengan desain nonequivalent control group design. Sampel ditentukan melalui cluster random sampling sehingga diperoleh kelas III.A sebagai kelas eksperimen (33 siswa) dan kelas III.B sebagai kelas kontrol (33 siswa). Data dikumpulkan melalui tes uraian pada tahap pre-test dan post-test, kemudian dianalisis menggunakan uji Wilcoxon, uji Mann-Whitney, dan uji N-Gain. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan rata-rata nilai kelas eksperimen meningkat dari 45,88 menjadi 88,70, jauh lebih tinggi dibandingkan kelas kontrol yang meningkat dari 37,39 menjadi 62,33. Uji Wilcoxon dan Mann-Whitney menunjukkan nilai signifikansi di bawah 0,05, sedangkan uji N-Gain kelas eksperimen sebesar 0,70 (kategori sedang, cukup efektif) dan kelas kontrol sebesar 0,37 (tidak efektif). Dapat disimpulkan bahwa model Cooperative Learning berbantuan media konkret Takalintar berpengaruh dan cukup efektif dalam meningkatkan pemahaman konsep perkalian bersusun siswa kelas III.

title: Metabolic regulation of oocyte developmental competence: cellular cooperation, developmental transitions, and human evidence
container-title: Frontiers in Cell and Developmental Biology
9e9f05703b4b08c0bc781f4efa32f02f1e12e0b9.abstract: Oocyte metabolism supports meiotic maturation and prepares the cytoplasm for fertilization and early cleavage. These functions depend on the exchange of substrates with cumulus cells, mitochondrial activity and organization, redox balance, and the use of metabolites in biosynthesis and chromatin regulation. This narrative review examines how these processes contribute to developmental competence, drawing on mammalian perturbation studies and human oocyte, cumulus-cell, follicular-fluid and embryo studies. Animal experiments show that disturbed substrate use or organelle organization can impair development despite meiotic progression or little change in total adenosine triphosphate (ATP) content. They also reveal dose- and stage-dependent responses to metabolic supplementation. Human studies identify related molecular and optical changes, particularly during reproductive aging, but the biological meaning of a measurement depends on the sampled cell, developmental stage and experimental conditions. Direct oocyte profiling, associated follicular samples and embryo measurements therefore address different questions. The Goldilocks concept helps frame the possibility that both insufficient activity and excessive demand can accompany developmental failure; it does not establish a common metabolic threshold for clinical selection. We discuss metabolic interventions as tests of mechanism and distinguish developmental rescue in experimental systems from benefit in vitro fertilization. The central challenge is to determine which metabolic changes contribute to loss of competence and which arise as responses to aging, culture or developmental arrest.

title: Digital Visual Learning Materials and Their Impact on Students' English Language Skills: A Guided Inquiry Approach
container-title: Architecture  Image Studies
1038c780f28dc5e4d0947f9a7bd13f7b8af43fcc.abstract: This study investigates the effect of the Guided Inquiry model assisted by Digital Student Worksheets (LKPD) on eleventh-grade students' English language skills, specifically writing creativity, reading comprehension, speaking proficiency, and learning independence. Employing a quasi-experimental design with a Nonequivalent Control Group, the study involved 187 students from SMA Negeri 1 Woha, Bima, West Nusa Tenggara, selected through proportional random sampling and assigned to either an experimental group (Digital LKPD-supported Guided Inquiry) or a control group (conventional instruction). Pre- and post-tests were administered across all four outcome variables, and data were analyzed using Multivariate Analysis of Covariance (MANCOVA) and N-Gain tests. Results demonstrated statistically significant improvements in the experimental group across all four variables: writing creativity (t = 3.542; p = 0.001), reading comprehension (t = 3.215; p = 0.002), speaking skills (t = 3.611; p = 0.001), and learning independence (t = 3.214; p = 0.002). The MANCOVA revealed a simultaneous significant effect of the instructional model on all dependent variables (Pillai's Trace = 0.913; p < 0.001). N-Gain scores indicated moderate-to-high improvement in the experimental group (M = 0.65) compared to the control group (M = 0.35). These findings suggest that integrating digital visual learning materials within a Guided Inquiry framework functions not merely as a content delivery mechanism, but as a strategic instructional design component that promotes self-regulated learning, cognitive engagement, and holistic English language literacy development in 21st-century educational contexts.

title: Decentralized Finance and Digital Assets: A New Perspective on Financial Management and Risk
container-title: Lex localis - Journal of Local Self-Government
13b14090a5c64d7c3224b43ae85f72408e707dbf.abstract: <jats:p>Financial services are being transformed, how they are designed, accessed, and managed, by the rise of decentralized finance (DeFi) and digital assets. These innovations via blockchain networks, smart contracts, and tokenization offer alternatives to existing models for payments, lending, investment, and asset exchange. But the economic, institutional and operating risks of financial intermediation are not eroded when transactions are automated. In this conceptual study, the impact of DeFi and digital assets on financial management is explored, including capital allocation, treasury operations, risk management, and the governance of digital assets. It assesses what could be gained from this technology, alongside its potential technological vulnerabilities, market instability, regulatory uncertainty and inability to provide meaningful financial inclusion. An analysis approach is built to present a managerial perspective, which considers digital financial arrangements from an economic function, dependency and accountability standpoint. It points out that sustainable adoption requires coordination of technology with financial management, strong rights, organizational efficiency and appropriate governance. DeFi is therefore a reorganization of financial management and not the automatic replacement of existing financial institutions.</jats:p>

title: Expectation-driven gain modulation of preparatory spatial attention
container-title: eLife
42e0bff514a13e990dde6d5376170bcb87804ae4.abstract: <jats:p>The visual system can flexibly adjust attentional deployment to match task demands, but whether observers can proactively modulate the spatial scope of attention based on expectations about upcoming search difficulty remains unclear. According to the zoom lens model, attention can narrow or broaden its spatial extent, with narrower focus enhancing processing efficiency, a mechanism that would benefit target discrimination in crowded displays. We tested whether observers adjust attentional scope when expecting sparse versus dense search arrays by combining spatial cueing with block-wise manipulations of display density expectations. Participants performed a visual search task in which endogenous cues predicted target location, while blocks predominantly contained either sparse (1 target, 3 distractors) or dense (1 target, 7 distractors) displays. We applied inverted encoding models to broadband EEG data to reconstruct spatial channel tuning functions, enabling precise characterization of both the locus and breadth of attentional deployment. Behaviorally, expecting difficult searches selectively improved accuracy at cued locations without costs elsewhere. Consistent with this selective benefit, neural measurements revealed that expectancy enhanced the amplitude of spatially selective responses at the attended location but did not alter tuning width. These findings demonstrate that expectations about search difficulty modulate attention through gain-based signal enhancement rather than adjustments to spatial scope, revealing that preparatory attentional control operates via amplitude modulation within a stable spatial focus. This mechanism complements reactive attentional adjustments and provides an efficient means for the visual system to optimize processing under predictable task demands.</jats:p>
