title: Self-supervised scene-adaptive spectral imaging via implicit mask evolution
container-title: Optics Express
22be55733956f9e4e64dc68e4a0666d9b0815351.abstract: <jats:p>The performance of snapshot coded aperture spectral imaging (CASSI) is fundamentally constrained by the reliance on scene-agnostic static masks or computationally heavy data-driven optimizations that require extensive spectral ground truth. We propose a self-supervised, scene-adaptive CASSI framework that refines the physical coded aperture without requiring labeled spectral data. By integrating a dual-branch architecture with an efficient, implicit model-driven reconstruction engine, the system establishes a self-supervised consistency loop that tailors the mask morphology to the spatial-frequency characteristics of the incident scene. Numerical benchmarks and physical prototype validation demonstrate the framework’s ability to adapt to structural boundaries, effectively mitigating high-frequency aliasing artifacts while demonstrating robust generalization across disparate scene distributions without offline training. Operating at an algorithmic latency of ∼55ms per iteration and enabling low-latency closed-loop modulation, this approach demonstrates the feasibility of hardware-integrated physical adaptation for static scenes and establishes the theoretical potential for continuous spatiotemporal evolution in high-throughput sensing pipelines.</jats:p>

title: Deep Learning for Adaptive Management of Renewable Hybrid Power Systems
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Optimizing Sustainable Energy Engineering With AI and Machine Learning
8dbc26d9167ed7772f47b06f9aa8d0293cf7c8ac.abstract: <jats:p>This study examines the problem of adaptive control for hybrid renewable energy systems combining photovoltaic panels, wind turbines, and battery storage under conditions of generation uncertainty and price volatility. A control strategy based on deep reinforcement learning is proposed, which does not require an explicit mathematical model and accounts for long-term consequences, including battery degradation. The control task is formalized as a markov decision process with an integral discounted reward combining economic costs, penalties for energy curtailment, and storage aging losses. Computational experiments on real meteorological data demonstrate that the trained regulator reduces operating costs by 12–15% compared to heuristic strategies, increases the share of renewable energy used by 18–22%, and extends estimated battery life by 15–20%. The results confirm the advantages of the proposed approach over classical methods, particularly under high uncertainty. Limitations and prospects for practical implementation are discussed.</jats:p>

title: Digital Intelligence and AI-Based System Optimization in Waste-to-Energy Infrastructure for Net-Zero Cities
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Optimizing Sustainable Energy Engineering With AI and Machine Learning
ff36013178296736d6e2747d2c7e1830b32bd841.abstract: <jats:p>The integration of digital intelligence and artificial intelligence in waste-to-energy (WtE) infrastructure optimization to achieve net-zero cities is presented in this chapter. The rapid urbanization and the growing amount of waste demand efficient and sustainable solutions. Municipal waste is turned into energy in WtE systems, and traditional operations lack flexibility and efficiency. The chapter uses systematic literature review as a method on the topic indexed in more than 200 articles and summarizing main conclusions of the quality research. It discusses monitoring with IoT, digital twins, and real-time optimization based on AI and predictive maintenance and energy recovery that is better. Case studies show the changes in the operational efficiency, emission control, and stability of systems. A conceptual AI-enabled framework is presented to find a solution to combine WtE systems with smart grids and urban energy networks. The results conclude on how smart WtE infrastructure contributes to the use of the circular economy and sustainable, low-carbon urban development.</jats:p>

title: Digital Constitutionalism and the Protection of Customary Law People’s Rights in Indonesia
container-title: Verdict: Journal of Law Science
1550186a7789202fdb696659dd9f4104a7a42a91.abstract: <jats:p>Digital revolution has altered the manner in which public authority is administered and how citizens engage with public services, partake in democratic activities, and assert their constitutional rights. This research examines the effects of digital transformation on the constitutional rights of customary law communities and delineates Indigenous Data Sovereignty within the Indonesian legal system. Contemporary studies on digital constitutionalism mostly emphasise individual rights, state power, and the governance of digital platforms, but Indigenous Data Sovereignty discourse specifically underscores collective management of Indigenous data. However, the relationship between these two fields remains insufficiently developed in Indonesia, particularly with communal data, indigenous wisdom, and cultural identity. This research employs a normative legal approach utilising statutory and conceptual frameworks. Primary and secondary legal texts were collected through library research and analysed qualitatively. The findings suggest that digital transformation improves cultural preservation, information availability, civic participation, and public service provision. Concurrently, it fosters unequal digital accessibility, administrative exclusion, diminishment of community control over collective data, and the unauthorised utilisation of indigenous knowledge without authorisation or fair benefit-sharing. Indonesia’s personal data protection framework primarily emphasises identifiable individuals and is deficient in explicit restrictions concerning communal data or collective detriment. This research contends that Indigenous Data Sovereignty should be founded on recognising communal data and customary law communities as collective rights-holders, employing consent based on traditional practices, guaranteeing community governance over data access and use, instituting benefit-sharing, performing collective impact assessments, ensuring institutional oversight, and delivering effective remedies.</jats:p>

title: MOSQMIXERNET: A CUSTOM DEEP LEARNING ARCHITECTURE FOR EARLY-STAGE MOSQUITO CLASSIFICATION AND GENUS-LEVEL IDENTIFICATION
container-title: Oxford Open Digital Health
3f9de5f6c7ac23f07c42f175676e294f0e8b124c.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Mosquito-borne diseases such as malaria, dengue, zika, and chikungunya impose a disproportionate heavy public health burden on Africa. While artificial intelligence (AI) tools have been applied in species identification on the adult mosquitoes, the early aquatic stages have been largely ignored. Yet, these early stages are critical since vector control strategies often target larvae and pupae to break the transmission cycle before mosquitoes mature into biting adults. Moreover, the identification of these specimens is prone to human error by experts due to the striking similarity in morphological features between larval and pupal stages across species. This limitation delays surveillance and increases the risk of misclassification, potentially compromising vector control efforts. In response, an Africa-based curated dataset is introduced, encompassing the larval and pupal stages of Aedes, Anopheles, and Culex species, along with non-mosquito specimens of similar morphology. This dataset helps address the underrepresentation of African samples in global repositories and provides a rare contribution to pupal-stage classification, a category largely overlooked in most classification tasks. MosqMixerNet is introduced as a lightweight deep learning model designed for image-based classification of mosquito early stages. The proposed MosqMixerNet balances compactness and accuracy with only 169 666 trainable parameters and was benchmarked against MobileNetV2, DenseNet121, and NASNetMobile. For genus-level identification, it achieved 99.37% accuracy, surpassing NASNetMobile (97.30%), MobileNetV2 (97.26%), and DenseNet121 (80.39%). The work advances computer vision for public health and tropical disease control, and provides a foundation for integration into digital vector monitoring platforms in endemic settings.</jats:p>

title: Adjustable memristive multi-scroll hyperchaotic systems and their synchronization via adaptive super-twisting sliding mode control
container-title: Physica Scripta
75da4afdac2538d2fff4e0e4e49df96a4a57f6fa.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>This paper proposes a novel system construction method based on introducing memristors into a four-dimensional hyperchaotic conservative system. By leveraging the nonlinear characteristics of memristors to disrupt system conservatism, the transition from conservative systems to dissipative systems is achieved. On this basis, novel nonlinear functions are introduced to construct a one-dimensional memristive multi-scroll hyperchaotic system (1D-MMSHCS) and a two-dimensional memristive multi-scroll hyperchaotic system (2D-MMSHCS), respectively. Through equilibrium points analysis, coexisting attractors, bifurcation diagrams, and Lyapunov exponents, the complex dynamic behaviors of the memristive multi-scroll hyperchaotic systems are systematically revealed. To verify the hardware realizability of the memristive multi-scroll hyperchaotic systems, a digital hardware platform based on field-programmable gate array is developed, successfully implementing the 1D-MMSHCS and the 2D-MMSHCS. Addressing the synchronization problem of the more complex 2D-MMSHCS, unknown parameters can be estimated in real time through parameter adaptive mechanisms and dynamically adjust controller parameters, proposing an improved adaptive super-twisting sliding mode control method. Simulation results demonstrate that this method can achieve rapid system synchronization. The method also exhibits excellent robustness against time-varying bounded disturbances.</jats:p>

title: Tau hadronic decay channel reconstruction with a Lorentz-covariant graph attention network
container-title: Physica Scripta
48dd6af93c13d027dd2a5b2312100fb17c5e3a52.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    The reconstruction of hadronic decay modes of the
                    <jats:italic>τ</jats:italic>
                    lepton is a key task in high-energy physics experiments, directly impacting precision measurements and new physics searches. Conventional reconstruction approaches rely on handcrafted features and rule-based algorithms, which face challenges in handling complex decay topologies and detector effects. In this work, we propose LCGA-Net, a physics-informed deep learning framework for
                    <jats:italic>τ</jats:italic>
                    decay channel classification and four-momentum reconstruction. The method represents decay products as particle graphs and employs a multi-head attention mechanism to capture inter-particle correlations. To ensure physical consistency, Lorentz-invariant constraints are explicitly incorporated into the model architecture. A dedicated single-
                    <jats:italic>τ</jats:italic>
                    dataset is constructed from the simulation data of the Circular Electron Positron Collider, covering six major hadronic decay modes. The proposed model achieves an accuracy of 89.2% on the validation set, matching or slightly exceeding baseline models. More importantly, full physics constraints substantially improve the physical plausibility of reconstructed four-momenta—particularly the energy–momentum relation—without degrading classification performance. These results demonstrate that integrating physics priors with attention-based deep learning on particle clouds provides an effective approach for
                    <jats:italic>τ</jats:italic>
                    decay reconstruction, with potential applications in future high-energy physics analyses.
                  </jats:p>

title: DAPNet: a decoupled adaptive prototyping network for few-shot medical image segmentation
container-title: Biomedical Physics & Engineering Express
9308dbebee4a292fa6ee544f37320a82b7307e53.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Few-shot medical image segmentation (FSMIS) holds immense potential in medical scenarios where annotations are expensive and scarce. However, the majority of existing methods perform queries under the guidance of a foreground prototype, which causes them to struggle, as this single representation fails to effectively model both the target and its complex anatomical surroundings. To address this limitation, we propose the decoupled adaptive prototype network (DAPNet), explicitly disentangling the representation of foreground and background through a dual-path dynamic feature enhancement and feedback framework. The deformable anatomical prototype sampling (DAPS) module, which innovatively combines coordinate-aware and deformable convolutions to achieve adaptive anatomical alignment, resulting in a robust set of background prototypes derived from support features; and the dual attention-boosted prototyping module, which generates a highly discriminative foreground prototype by fusing semantic attention with a boundary-aware mechanism to effectively mitigate feature bias and enhance the structural integrity of the target. By jointly optimizing these distinct but complementary prototypes, DAPNet forms a powerful and comprehensive representation for classification. Extensive experiments on multiple public datasets demonstrate that our method consistently outperforms state-of-the-art approaches. Ablation studies and visualizations further validate the effectiveness and synergy of our proposed modules, establishing a new and robust paradigm for FSMIS.</jats:p>

title: Pembuktian Digital dan Pertanggungjawaban Pidana Pelaku Penjualan Akun Streaming Premium Ilegal: Perspektif Hak Cipta serta Batasnya terhadap <i>Terms of Service</i> dan UU ITE
container-title: Verdict: Journal of Law Science
bf1a4c4bf1b308dc3fd22ddd77000c616dfcf57a.abstract: <jats:p>The rise of subscription-based streaming services has been accompanied by the unofficial sale of premium accounts through social media and digital marketplaces in Indonesia. Although such practices are commonly labelled illegal, the label does not automatically establish criminal liability. This study addresses two issues: first, how difficulties in digital evidence and offender anonymity constrain criminal enforcement, and the standing of electronic evidence in linking offenders, accounts, transactions, and copyright-related objects; second, how criminal liability of sellers of illegal premium streaming accounts is constructed under the Copyright Law, and where its limits lie in relation to Terms of Service violations and offences under the Electronic Information and Transactions Law. Using normative legal research with statutory and conceptual approaches, the study analyses primary legal materials and secondary literature through descriptive-analytical qualitative analysis. The findings show that digital infringement leaves no physical trace, so proof depends on authentic, intact, and relevant electronic evidence supported by digital forensics. Criminal liability under the Copyright Law arises only when the act is committed without right or permission, relates to economic rights over protected works, including computer programs, is carried out for commercial use, involves fault and capacity to be held accountable, and is proven by valid electronic evidence. Violations of Terms of Service remain contractual, while the Electronic Information and Transactions Law applies only when its prohibited elements are met. The study contributes a framework linking digital proof with criminal liability in digital copyright enforcement.</jats:p>

title: When traditional culture meets digital games: pathways and boundary conditions linking cultural identity to purchase intention
container-title: Journal of Product & Brand Management
f4411bb0ddc28ff8c7ca11de384db891845accaf.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Purpose</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study aims to examine how cultural identity is associated with purchase intention for paid digital games featuring local cultural elements. In the context of Black Myth: Wukong, it further investigates whether perceived value and immersive experience explain this relationship and whether price sensitivity conditions these associations.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Design/methodology/approach</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Survey data from 1,167 mainland Chinese and international gamers were analysed using covariance-based structural equation modelling. Analysis of variance (ANOVA) and cross-sample model comparisons were used to examine group differences.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Findings</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Cultural identity was positively associated with purchase intention, with significant indirect effects through perceived value and immersive experience. In the full sample, price sensitivity weakened the links between cultural identity and both mediators and their indirect effects. Mainland Chinese gamers showed higher cultural identity and perceived value, and stronger direct and indirect effects of cultural identity, than international gamers. The moderating effect of price sensitivity was not significant in the international subsample.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Practical implications</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Managers can strengthen culturally grounded digital products by embedding culturally resonant narratives, symbols and aesthetics into product design, communicating their relevance to target consumers and adopting differentiated value-framing and pricing strategies for consumers with varying levels of price sensitivity.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Originality/value</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study applies cultural identity theory to paid digital game consumption by integrating perceived value and immersive experience as two distinct mechanisms linking cultural identity to purchase intention and examining price sensitivity as a boundary condition of these relationships.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Adoption potential, timeline and implementation measures for bio-digital integration in South African construction: a modified Delphi study
container-title: Journal of Engineering, Design and Technology
09260d9d2b1e62bf4440faed69464f113c4b9415.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Purpose</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Limited empirical evidence exists on the adoption potential, expected implementation timeline and measures required to support bio-digital integration in developing-country construction contexts. This study aims to examine expert perspectives on these dimensions within the South African construction industry.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Design/methodology/approach</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>An exploratory modified Delphi approach was adopted with 12 built environment experts. Adoption potential and expected timelines were assessed using categorical scales and descriptive statistics. Fifteen implementation measures were evaluated using a ten-point Likert scale and reassessed in a second round following controlled feedback. Consensus was assessed using median, interquartile deviation and percentage agreement, with mean and standard deviation additionally reported for Round 2.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Findings</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The expert panel indicated moderate adoption potential and predominantly anticipated adoption within 6–10 years and beyond. Regulatory frameworks, circular economy principles and workforce training were among the most highly rated implementation measures. However, consistently high ratings across all measures indicate limited differentiation between their relative importance. A structured adoption pathway is proposed to support implementation.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Research limitations/implications</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The findings reflect the perspectives of a small, predominantly academically affiliated expert panel and should not be interpreted as representative of the South African construction industry.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Practical implications</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The findings provide context-specific guidance for policymakers, industry stakeholders and researchers on policy development, capacity building and innovation investment.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Originality/value</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The study provides context-specific empirical evidence on expert assessments of bio-digital integration in South Africa by jointly examining adoption potential, anticipated timelines and highly rated implementation measures within a single framework.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: The Digital Evolution of Migration Management in the Russian Federation: Stages, Tools, and Legal Risks
container-title: ADMINISTRATIVE LAW AND PROCEDURE
d4468aef69f6d0153d066280ec14e7aa52225f7d.abstract:
<jats:p>The article examines the stages of the digitalization process of migration management in the Russian Federation.
The article analyzes innovations based on the State Migration Registration Information System created in 2007, including
the Register of Controlled Persons and the Digital Profile of a Foreign Citizen. Experiments based on the use of digital
technologies to improve the rules and conditions of entry into the Russian Federation, to introduce additional mechanisms
for accounting for migrant workers, as well as the automatic termination of a patent are considered. The shortcomings
of legal regulation have been identified, measures have been proposed to eliminate them, as well as to improve the
management of migration processes using modern digital technologies.</jats:p>

title: Administrative Liability for Violations in the Sphere of Digital Currency Circulation: Issues of Defining Offense Elements and Prospects for Legislative Development
container-title: ADMINISTRATIVE LAW AND PROCEDURE
09d9b7697e26bf7eb33286344f2bb9a8cf46316c.abstract:
<jats:p>The article examines the theoretical and practical issues of establishing the institution of administrative liability
for violations in the sphere of digital currency circulation in the Russian Federation. Based on the analysis of federal laws
of 2020–2026, legislative initiatives including Draft Federal Law No. 1194944-8, as well as doctrinal approaches to defining
the legal nature of digital currency, the author identifies systemic shortcomings in the legislative construction of new
administrative offence compositions. It is substantiated that the fragmentary nature of legislative activity, the absence
of a unified conceptual framework and a procedural mechanism for bringing to liability create risks of regulatory
inconsistency and reduce the effectiveness of legal regulation. An author’s classification of offences in the field under
study is proposed according to the subject composition, the nature of the act, and the degree of public danger, and specific
proposals are formulated for the systematisation of the compositions within a new chapter of the Code of Administrative
Offences of the Russian Federation.</jats:p>

title: Self-attention-aided multi-layer CNN-LSTM for non-uniform 4-level differential amplitude modulation and detection with atmospheric turbulence for OWANs
container-title: Optics Express
fedd060d0254eff3eb9ce0c2cc0964613783fd42.abstract: <jats:p>This paper proposes an environment-aware four-level non-uniform differential amplitude modulation and detection scheme assisted by self-attentive multi-layer CNN-LSTM (SA-CNN-LSTM) for optical wireless access networks (OWANs) under atmospheric turbulence, to mitigate severe distortions induced by atmospheric turbulence in optical wireless communication (OWC) systems. Relying on four-level non-uniform differential amplitude modulation (NUADM-4) and a self-attention-aided detection algorithm at the receiving terminal, the proposed scheme can effectively suppress both multiplicative turbulence fading and additive Gaussian noise simultaneously. Numerical results reveal that the proposed scheme achieves remarkable bit error rate (BER) improvements compared with conventional detection frameworks for NUADM-4, and it substantially outperforms the classical uniform four-level pulse amplitude modulation (PAM-4) across diverse turbulence strength regimes. Moreover, the tailored architecture integrating self-attention with multi-layer CNN-LSTM maintains high transmission efficiency, reduces the dimension of the fully-connected layer at the receiver to a certain extent, and accelerates the computation speed compared with the CNN-based algorithm. In comparison with conventional detection-aided algorithms such as vanilla CNN, LSTM, and MLP, the presented scheme delivers a universal BER performance gain. Furthermore, the machine-learning-aided design philosophy for different modulation systems offers a practical design paradigm and implementable solution for the engineering deployment of high-speed OWC systems serving OWANs operating in volatile atmospheric turbulence environments.</jats:p>

title: Artificial Intelligence-Enabled Early Warning Systems for the Psychosocial Wellbeing of Students With Hearing Loss in Inclusive Educational Settings
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Improving Disability Support and Institutional Performance With AI
129abc45062d56b3fbb0027ea16533ce2776036a.abstract: <jats:p>Students with hearing loss in inclusive settings frequently face psychosocial challenges including social isolation, communication fatigue, and emotional disengagement that develop gradually and evade conventional monitoring systems focused solely on academic metrics. This chapter proposes an AI-enabled early warning system (EWS) to proactively identify emotional distress and social withdrawal among deaf or hard of hearing (DHH) students. Integrating multimodal data streams, machine learning, transformer-based NLP, and explainable AI (XAI), the system generates actionable risk indicators for educators and counselors. Grounded in Social Inclusion Theory, Universal Design for Learning, Ecological Systems Theory, and Affective Computing Theory, it functions as a human-centered decision-support platform rather than a surveillance tool. Ethical dimensions including data privacy, algorithmic bias, transparency, and informed consent are critically examined alongside a roadmap for evidence-based implementation.</jats:p>

title: The Antecedents of Trust and Its Effects on Credibility Within Digital Infrastructure
container-title: Enabling Human Transformation Through Socio-Technical Systems in Industry 4.0
a60dd27e017c4b64f6840b661e9f7bbbd2753353.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter examines the antecedents of digital trust and their influence on brand credibility within digital infrastructure, encompassing websites, e-commerce platforms, the Internet of Things (IoT), and chatbots. The chapter concludes by identifying gaps in the literature around competence and benevolence in emerging and AI-driven digital technologies, and proposes a future research agenda focused on cross-cultural and empirical investigation of these antecedents, intended to support students, researchers, policymakers, and brand managers engaging with questions of trust in digital environments.</jats:p>

title: Blockchain-Enabled Supply Chain Transparency
container-title: Enabling Human Transformation Through Socio-Technical Systems in Industry 4.0
86065cac2611a56130774f5b230d0727cdc835e3.abstract: <jats:p>The blockchain has emerged as a new technology that is revolutionizing the transparency of the supply chain, allowing for the decentralization, security, and protection of data in Industry 4.0 environments. Often the traditional supply chains lack real-time visibility and have traceability problems, fraud, and counterfeiting. Smart contracts, decentralized identity management, and cryptographic security mechanisms are just a few of the ways that blockchain increases trust, automation, and accountability. The chapter offers insights into evolving innovations like blockchain-based digital twins, NFT product authentication, and AI-powered predictive analytics for intelligent supply chain management. In addition, the chapter outlines future trends like quantum-resistant cryptography, cross-chain interoperability, and autonomous supply chains powered by Web3 to enhance transparency, efficiency, and security in the global supply chain.</jats:p>

title: Bridging the Digital Divide
container-title: Enabling Human Transformation Through Socio-Technical Systems in Industry 4.0
9ee41e2d5686c557723f6c732c26a61e168620d6.abstract: <jats:p>The rapid rise of digital technologies has been a game-changer in global communication, commerce and governance, but it has also created the spread of digital inequality and complex cybersecurity challenges. The chapter provides an overview of the relationships of digital inequality and cybersecurity risks with evolving global governance system. Digital inequality manifests as uneven access to digital infrastructure, digital literacy and online economies and is disproportionately prevalent among disadvantaged populations and nations. Meanwhile, the expansion of digital network exposes people, organizations,nations to cybersecurity threats, including cyber-crime, systemic insecurity, data breaches, which can undermine trust and socioeconomic systems. The chapter explores the role of international governance arrangements, and partnerships in minimizing the risks and promoting equitable access to technology. The case studies indicate the success stories and failures of multilateral treaties, cybersecurity policies and public-private partnerships in solving access and security problems.</jats:p>

title: Data Sovereignty and Algorithmic Governance in Developing Economies
container-title: Enabling Human Transformation Through Socio-Technical Systems in Industry 4.0
6fdbeb58e96e829a460768ed1eba7412a41afc2e.abstract: <jats:p>Data is among the most contested resources of the twenty-first century. Citizens in developing and middle-income economies generate it constantly through mobile transactions, health services, and social platforms. Yet, the infrastructure that processes it and the governance frameworks that regulate it have largely been designed elsewhere. This chapter examines data sovereignty and algorithmic governance as twin pillars of an equitable digital transformation agenda, using South Africa as its primary lens. It argues that three connected interventions are essential: sovereign infrastructure architecture, algorithmic transparency and accountability, and genuine community participation in governance design. Drawing on socio-technical systems theory and institutional economics, the chapter demonstrates that data sovereignty cannot be achieved through any single instrument but requires deliberate alignment between technical architecture, governance institutions, and participatory process to produce inclusive Fourth Industrial Revolution outcomes in structurally unequal economies.</jats:p>

title: Digital and AI tools in informal care: understanding caregivers’ experiences in rural Nigeria
container-title: Working with Older People
9193766175c91a5d0c22308aaadf2db77e3cb6ef.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Purpose</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Although informal caregiving for older adults is well-researched, a significant gap exists in understanding how informal caregivers navigate their caregiving roles with the help of digital technologies, especially in rural Nigeria, where internet connectivity is poor and access to digital devices is limited. This study aims to explore how informal caregivers in rural Nigeria use digital technology to support care for older adults.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Design/methodology/approach</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The study adopted a qualitative descriptive approach, data were collected from 10 informal caregivers, using semi-structured interviews. The data were further analysed thematically using NVivo 14.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Findings</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Results identified that caregivers use digital technology for communication and care coordination, learning and self-empowerment, responding to emergency situations, improving efficiency, reducing stress and maintaining contact between older adults and their diaspora family members. The study also found poor access and limited internet infrastructure as barriers to the use of digital technology to improve caregiving.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Research limitations/implications</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Only caregivers in rural areas were interviewed. This excluded the experiences of caregivers in urban areas, who may face urban economic stressors that shape their overall caregiving experience and their use of digital technology for caregiving.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Practical implications</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The findings highlight the potential of digital technology to support informal caregiving in rural Nigeria. Improving access to affordable digital devices, reliable internet connectivity and digital literacy can enhance care coordination, caregiver support, emergency response and communication with older adults and their families.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Originality/value</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study is important because it provides new insight into how informal caregivers in rural Nigeria use digital technology to support older adults despite limited connectivity and access to digital devices. It highlights both the potential of digital tools to strengthen caregiving and the infrastructural barriers that must be addressed.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Digital literacy competencies among library professionals: a systematic literature review
container-title: Global Knowledge, Memory and Communication
dbcbc3e8a445c7ba8f3b2a1c5fbdf1881528cedb.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Purpose</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study aims to assess the digital literacy proficiency, identify gaps in digital literacy and challenges encountered by library professionals in acquisition and application of digital literacy skills.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Design/methodology/approach</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>A systematic literature review was carried out by using PRISMA 2020 guidelines. The databases used in this study includes Scopus, Web of Science, Emerald, Taylor and Francis. Articles published from 2020 to 2024 were included in this study. Initially, a total of 561 articles were identified from the selected databases, and after applying the criteria of inclusion and exclusion, 18 articles were selected for detailed analysis. The included studies were conducted across various countries, which indicates a broad geographical coverage of this study.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Findings</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The findings of this study indicated that most of the library professionals were well-versed in basic digital literacy skills, while a gap was observed in advanced level of digital literacy skills. The major challenges faced by them were lack of funds or budget allocation, followed by lack of digital infrastructure and lack of support from the authorities.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Originality/value</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This systematic review examines digital literacy competencies among library professionals to identify key competency areas, gaps and challenges faced by them. Existing literature lacks a comprehensive review focusing on current level of digital literacy competencies among library professionals. Therefore, this research work contributes to better understanding of digital literacy competencies among library professionals. The findings will also help inform future strategies, training programmes and initiatives aimed at strengthening digital literacy within the library profession.</jats:p>

title: Depth-adaptive suppression of subject-dependent interference for robust cross-subject EEG emotion recognition
container-title: Biomedical Engineering / Biomedizinische Technik
e29afc0025a958d32e6bbab8bcd5a4cfbf8867f3.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec id="j_bmt-2026-0393_abs_001">
                    <jats:title>Objectives</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Cross-subject electroencephalography (EEG) emotion recognition is limited by inter-subject variability, which embeds subject-specific nuisance information in learned representations and reduces generalization to unseen individuals.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec id="j_bmt-2026-0393_abs_002">
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>We propose a two-stage layer-adaptive subject-interference suppression framework built on EEG Conformer. In the search stage, differentiable gates and adversarial subject classifiers are attached to hierarchical representations from the patch embedding layer and Transformer blocks to estimate where subject information is most strongly encoded. The top-ranked layers are then fixed and the model is retrained for final emotion classification. A subject-aware supervised contrastive regularizer is further used to improve label-consistent cross-subject representation learning.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec id="j_bmt-2026-0393_abs_003">
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Experiments on SEED under strict leave-one-subject-out evaluation show improved performance over representative machine-learning, domain-adaptation, and deep-learning baselines. Auxiliary experiments on SEED-IV indicate adaptability under a more challenging label setting. Layer-wise probing shows that subject-specific information remains decodable across depths but is relatively stronger in shallow and early intermediate representations.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec id="j_bmt-2026-0393_abs_004">
                    <jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Selective depth-aware suppression provides a practical and interpretable strategy for robust EEG-based affective brain–computer interfaces.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Leadership agility in UAE public health care: enabling an agile mindset during digital transformation

<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Purpose</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study aims to examine how leadership agility shapes the development of an agile mindset within public health care organizations in the United Arab Emirates (UAE) during periods of digital and organizational transformation. It investigates how leaders at different levels of agility influence adaptability, collaboration and learning in highly regulated, hierarchical health-care environments.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Design/methodology/approach</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>A qualitative, multiple case study design was used. Data were collected through semistructured interviews with senior and middle managers, clinical leaders and document analysis across three UAE public health-care organizations. Thematic analysis was conducted using leadership agility theory to guide coding, interpretation and cross-case comparison.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Findings</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Leadership agility operates along a developmental continuum. Expert- and achiever-level behaviors ensured operational stability, regulatory compliance and strategic alignment with national agendas, while catalyst, cocreator and synergist practices fostered adaptability, collaboration, innovation and learning. Organizational culture, learning orientation and strategies for managing resistance to change were identified as critical enablers or constraints in cultivating an agile mindset.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Practical implications</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The study provides actionable insights for leaders and policymakers, emphasizing the need for context-sensitive, culturally informed leadership.                   <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Originality/value</jats:title>

title: From corporate digital responsibility to responsible cybersecurity: unpacking the role of substantive digital transformation

<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Purpose</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>As digital-related threats affect organizations and stakeholders, understanding how firms develop responsible cybersecurity has become essential. This study aims to examine the role of corporate digital responsibility dimensions in promoting responsible cybersecurity through substantive digital transformation, addressing the limited empirical evidence on the pathways linking digital responsibility to cybersecurity practices.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Design/methodology/approach</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>A cross-sectional survey of 382 firms in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam, was conducted using snowball sampling. The proposed model was tested using partial least squares structural equation modeling and necessary condition analysis.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Findings</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Ethical digital responsibility is positively associated with the economic, legal and philanthropic dimensions of corporate digital responsibility. Digital responsibilities are positively associated with substantive digital transformation, which statistically mediates the relationship between corporate digital responsibility and responsible cybersecurity. The results also show that legal and ethical dimensions of corporate digital responsibility are necessary conditions for achieving higher levels of substantive digital transformation.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Originality/value</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Drawing on institutional theory, resource-based view and dynamic capabilities theory, this study contributes to the corporate digital responsibility literature by providing empirical evidence on the links between its dimensions, substantive digital transformation and responsible cybersecurity. By combining partial least squares structural equation modeling with necessary condition analysis, the study provides complementary evidence on both sufficiency and necessity relationships, offering an integrated empirical perspective on the conditions associated with responsible cybersecurity.</jats:p>

title: Evolutionary dynamics of AI-driven enterprise digital transformation: a cybernetic perspective
container-title: Kybernetes
2b2a2584eeba12477d60849925f24bde6a805644.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Purpose</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>In the AI era, digital transformation has become essential for enterprises to adapt as complex systems to uncertain business environments. In this work, we aim to analyze the evolutionary dynamics of AI-driven enterprise digital transformation (EDT), focusing on its evolution and impact on enterprise performance from a system cybernetics perspective.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Design/methodology/approach</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>We employ evolutionary dynamics analysis grounded in game theory to model the EDT process, and perform an econometric and empirical analysis on a sample of Chinese A-share-listed enterprises from 2009 to 2023. The approach encompasses heterogeneity analysis, moderation effect models, such as testing enterprise environmental, social, and governance (ESG) factors and market concentration, and threshold effect analyses.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Findings</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The evolutionary dynamics analysis finds that increasing the risk-averse benefits of traditional enterprises and reducing the additional benefit coefficient would hinder EDT. Increasing the investment of technology enterprises in internal resource restructuring accelerates the transformation process. Empirically, AI significantly contributes to EDT. ESG positively moderates the relationship between AI and EDT, while market concentration exerts a negative moderating effect. Furthermore, AI and EDT show an inverted U-shaped trend when R&D intensity exceeds a specific threshold, while a U-shaped trend is observed when enterprise performance exceeds a specific threshold.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Originality/value</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>In this work, we uncover the complex, non-linear cybernetic feedback loops, such as U-shaped and inverted U-shaped, and boundary conditions, such as ESG and market concentration for AI-driven EDT, offering systemic strategies for enterprises adapting to the digital ecosystem.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Studies of media, religion, and society have often connected religion and celebrity culture in ways that apply religious concepts and terminology to secular celebrities. This article reverses this trend and calls attention to the importance of religious celebrities, or celebrities who specifically emerge within and contribute to specific religious contexts. After reviewing recent literature at the intersections of celebrity, influencer, and religious cultures, this article offers a basic classificatory schema that describes distinct types of religious celebrities within the evangelical Christian context in the United States. title: Between policy and practice: a scoping review of the literature on national strategies for digital cultural heritage in the GLAM sector
container-title: Journal of Documentation
cd0d2b2938e27926663505f0bd2ba13575fa92cf.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Purpose</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study examines how national strategies for digital cultural heritage are conceptualised and implemented across the GLAM sector, and whether European policy ambitions concerning access, interoperability, shared infrastructures and coordinated governance are reflected in academic research and institutional practice.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Design/methodology/approach</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The study combines a qualitative documentary analysis of key European policy documents published between 2005 and 2025 with a scoping review conducted according to PRISMA-ScR guidelines. Searches in Scopus and Web of Science identified 501 records, of which 44 publications were included.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Findings</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>European policy frameworks converge around four strategic axes, namely cultural rights and people-centred access, digitisation, access and reuse, interoperability and metadata quality, and coordinated governance. However, the literature lacks a stable definition of national strategy. Two governance approaches are identified, ranging from top-down regulation to participatory and community-oriented governance, alongside an aggregation-based infrastructural model through which national coordination is translated into shared access. These dimensions are not mutually exclusive, since aggregation infrastructures may operate under centralised, participatory or hybrid arrangements. Implementation is constrained by legal barriers, unstable funding, limited organisational capacity and digital skills, fragmentation across GLAM sectors and technical and interoperability challenges. Standards, linked data and emerging technologies are widely promoted, but their practical adoption remains uneven.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Originality/value</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>By integrating policy analysis with a scoping review, the study provides an integrated analytical synthesis of national digital cultural heritage strategies. It connects governance, infrastructures, standards and institutional capacity and explains why technological progress alone has not produced coherent, sustainable and inclusive national digital heritage ecosystems.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Adaptive conformal finite-blocklength link adaptation for burst-mode coherent passive optical networks
container-title: Journal of Optical Communications
109c291816c9bdc09c9264c4d9378c37b32d551c.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>In upstream coherent passive optical networks (PONs), the challenge of coping with short bursts arises due to variations in received powers, carrier offsets, phase states, and digital signal processing residuals. While point-estimate adaptation may not provide calibrated reliability, fixed margins have the drawback of imposing constraints on power and spectral efficiency. To address this problem, the paper presents an approach called adaptive conformal finite block length (AC-FBLA), which consists of an optical line terminal controller that transforms recent signed residual estimates into the context-dependent and recency-weighted one-sided lower bound for burst SNR. Adaptive miscoverage feedback helps handle the issues of undercover, while the scheme uses a finite block length feasibility sieve for selecting the levels of launch power, modulation formats, and coding rates for each grant effectively. Using Monte Carlo simulations with 32 ONUs, 25 GBd transmissions, 1,024 symbol payload cases, six coded modes, four powers of launch, and four regimes of channel estimation enabled the teams to reach a high 97.67–97.77 % coverage compared to the target of 98 %. Therefore, one can see that the offered solution can improve the block error rate by 87.3–97.8 % compared to point estimate adaptation and reach improvements in spectral efficiency of 45.3–79.6 %.</jats:p>

title: Gendered Barriers and Adaptive Strategies in Sustainable Ecosystem Management in Lupanda, Zimbabwe: A Feminist Political Ecology Analysis
container-title: Gender and Sustainability in the Global South
865953afb82ec1047e86b386f183492627725ce3.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>This article examines the gendered barriers constraining rural women’s participation in sustainable ecosystem management (SEM) in Lupanda, Zimbabwe. It integrates Social Exclusion Theory (SET), Feminist Political Ecology (FPE), and intersectionality to explain how institutional arrangements, gendered ecological labour, and intersecting inequalities shape women’s access to resources and decision-making authority. The study draws on semi-structured interviews with 30 women, dialogues with 15 key informants, and documentary analysis. Interview and dialogue data were thematically analysed using NVivo, with documentary materials providing additional contextual evidence. The findings show that patriarchal governance, economic marginalisation, information exclusion, and time poverty reinforce one another, concentrating environmental responsibilities among women without corresponding governance authority. Women respond through cooperative networks, livelihood diversification, and the transmission of indigenous ecological knowledge, demonstrating substantial adaptive capacity that does not necessarily translate into institutional influence. Building on these findings, the article proposes the Gender-Ecosystem Governance Model (GEGM), comprising four interrelated pillars: empowerment and capacity building, institutional reform, economic inclusion and resource access, and knowledge integration and co-production. The study’s distinctive contribution is its demonstration that ecological responsibility does not necessarily translate into governance authority, together with a contextually grounded framework for addressing the relationship between ecological labour, resource access, and decision-making power. As a qualitative single-case study, it offers analytical insights rather than statistical generalisations; the proposed model requires further evaluation across different contexts.</jats:p>

title: Hybrid Machine Learning Framework for Proactive Fault Detection and Classification in Synchronous Digital Hierarchy (SDH) Networks Using KPI-Based Analysis
container-title: Journal of Engineering Research and Reports
91f8376b86f3591f2eec58cb4f10dc7d9b0bf050.abstract: <jats:p>Reliable monitoring of Synchronous Digital Hierarchy (SDH) networks remains important in settings where legacy telecommunications infrastructure is still in operation. This study evaluated a key performance indicator (KPI)-based hybrid machine learning framework for detecting anomalies and classifying faults in SDH network observations collected from a Network Monitoring System in Uyo, Nigeria, between January and June 2026. The indicators examined were Bit Error Rate (BER), Errored Seconds (ES), Severely Errored Seconds (SES), Background Block Errors (BBE), and Unavailable Seconds (UAS). Isolation Forest was used for unsupervised anomaly detection, while Random Forest was used for supervised fault classification. Temporal features, including lagged and rolling statistics, were incorporated to represent changing KPI patterns. The Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE) was used to address class imbalance, and Optuna was applied for hyperparameter optimisation. The reported evaluation indicated an overall classification accuracy of 98% and a macro F1-score of 0.90. Reported fault-class precision and recall were 0.81 and 0.80, respectively. The confusion matrix contained 519 true positives, 137 false negatives, 113 false positives, and 9,657 true negatives. The area under the receiver operating characteristic curve was 0.991, while average precision was 0.887. Lagged BBE features and BER were identified as influential predictors. These findings suggest that combining anomaly detection with supervised classification can support KPI-based fault monitoring in the SDH network context examined.</jats:p>

title: OECD Digital Economy and Society Outlook 2026
Artificial Intelligence and Religious Policy: Ethical Governance  in the Digital Public Sphere
container-title: AMUYA: INDONESIAN JOURNAL OF MANAGEMENT REVIEWS
9ea48f78d4d9703acd338209364519f5b6587504.abstract: <jats:p>Artificial intelligence increasingly mediates religious communication, knowledge, and participation in the digital public sphere, yet research remains fragmented across digital religion, human rights, and AI governance. This study examines how AI-mediated religious communication shapes authority, visibility, and participation; identifies associated ethical and rights-based concerns; and analyzes the institutional conditions relevant to its governance. Using a qualitative, non-experimental, exploratory-analytical design, the study draws on academic publications, policy documents, regulatory instruments, institutional guidelines, human-rights reports, and documented analyses of digital religious practices. Materials were purposively selected for substantive relevance and examined through structured reading and extraction, open and focused coding, thematic synthesis, source triangulation, and iterative cross-source comparison. The analysis identified three interconnected domains: access, visibility, and religious authority; religious freedom, inclusion, and algorithmic risks; and accountability, contestability, and institutional responsibility. AI-mediated technologies can broaden access to religious resources while simultaneously shaping the visibility and perceived authority of religious actors and interpretations. Expanded access can coexist with unequal representation, privacy risks, profiling, and constraints on meaningful participation, while distributed responsibility can create accountability gaps when consequential outcomes are difficult to explain or challenge. These relationships are context-dependent rather than predetermined effects of AI. By integrating sociotechnical and algorithmic-governance perspectives, the study provides an analytical framework for understanding ethical governance as the intersection of technological mediation, religious pluralism, fundamental rights, participation, and identifiable institutional responsibility.</jats:p>

title: Regulatory risk perception and corporate financialization: evidence from China
container-title: Digital Economy and Sustainable Development
f4ad279036c45899d4c10e8b62eb0f6d62a242be.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>This paper investigates the effect of regulatory risk perception on corporate financialization in China. Using the method of keyword search, we quantify regulatory risk perception in China based on the text data of listed companies’ annual reports. With the sample of Chinese A-share companies from 2011 to 2024, we find robust evidence that regulatory risk perception significantly curbs corporate financialization. Meanwhile, our results also indicate that this effect is stronger in non-SOEs (non-state-owned enterprises), firms at the maturity and decline stages, and firms with lower risk preference and lower market position. Finally, we propose that easing financing constraints, reducing corporate tax avoidance and alleviating corporate credit mismatches are plausible channels through which regulatory risk perception decreases corporate financialization. Overall, we shed light on the real effects of regulatory risk perception and the determinants of corporate financialization.</jats:p>

title: A Physics-Based Digital Twin for Real-Time Steel Catenary Riser Fatigue from Existing FPSO Motion-Reference-Unit Data, with Generalization to Fixed Jacket Structures
container-title: ADIPEC
5429cb35a42f0e10ee34775bb9b788f9c6907481.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>This paper establishes a physics-based digital twin that converts existing FPSO motion reference unit (MRU) data that is continuously recorded but never applied to structural integrity into real-time steel catenary riser (SCR) fatigue records. The core objectives are to derive and validate the MRU-to-touchdown-point transfer function, develop an Arabian Gulf corrected fatigue accumulation model, and to demonstrate condition-based optimized inspection for probabilistic remaining life estimation. The digital twin operates through two layers. Layer 1 uses the MRU-to-touchdown-point bending moment transfer function using lazy-wave catenary mechanics and linearized Morison loading, validated against Quéau et al. (2015, Ocean Engineering) across the frequency range 0.05 to 0.30 Hz. In Layer 2, rainflow cycles are computed and accumulated using Miner's rule on Arabian Gulf-corrected DNV S-N curves, taking a temperature factor of 0.72–0.78 (Vosikovsky 1975) and a salinity factor of 0.85–0.90 (combined factor 0.61–0.70). 10,000-member Monte Carlo ensemble maps uncertainties into a continuous remaining fatigue life probability distribution.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>Applied to typical SCR configurations subject to Arabian Gulf wave climate conditions, with North Sea reanalysis incorporated as a reference operating environment, the digital twin generates three findings. Firstly, realistic interannual wave climate variability leads to an observed discrepancy in accumulated fatigue damage fraction prediction between design and simulation of 5% at the 10th ensemble percentile and 28% at the 90th percentile by year 15, indicating that static design calculations are inherently unreliable for each asset individually. Secondly, the 90% credible interval for remaining fatigue life narrows proportionately to 1/√T, where T is the monitoring period, consistent with Bayesian posterior contraction, and is halved after four years of continuous MRU monitoring. Thirdly, the Arabian Gulf environmental correction reduces effective SCR fatigue life by 30–39% compared to standard DNV seawater curves, indicating a non-conservative allowance that will be systematically underestimated using North Atlantic calibrated design calculations for Arabian Gulf assets. Condition-based inspection scheduling guided by digital twin output projects a 20-year net inspection cost reduction of $6.6M to $36.5M for a 20-unit floating production fleet, with sensor network investment recovered within one to six years</jats:p>

title: A Digital Approach for Visualization of Cause-And-Effect Logic and Interlock Sequences in Process Plants
container-title: ADIPEC
c08d25751fa615f73137cc0db156ad435f2b5566.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Objectives/Scope</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This paper presents a low-cost digital initiative developed using Microsoft Excel VBA to improve understanding of Cause and Effect logic and compressor interlock philosophy in process plants. The platform replicates conventional Cause-and-Effect diagrams in a DCS style environment, enabling process engineers and operators to visualize interlock activation, alarm annunciation, and equipment response in real time. By transforming static theoretical diagrams into an interactive learning tool, the system enhances understanding of interlock operation, equipment protection philosophy, and process safety requirements, thereby improving operator awareness and competency.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods, Procedures, Process</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The platform was developed using Microsoft Excel VBA, macros, graphical animations, and event-driven programming. Interactive buttons allow users to activate process, MMS, lubrication oil, cooling water, and capacity control interlocks. The simulator executes corresponding Cause and Effect logic, alarms, automatic actions, and shutdown sequences. Audible alarm annunciation, acknowledge and reset functions, and a dynamic explanation section are incorporated to replicate DCS operation. The system visually demonstrates process parameter changes and explains the purpose and safety significance of each interlock.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results, Observations, Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The developed Excel VBA-based DCS simulator successfully demonstrated dynamic visualization of Cause and Effect logic, interlock actions, alarms, and annunciation systems. The platform improved operator understanding by enabling users to trigger individual interlocks and observe equipment response in real time. Compared with conventional static Cause and Effect diagrams, the simulator provided better understanding of compressor protection philosophy, process safety limits, and emergency shutdown procedures. The inclusion of alarm annunciation, acknowledge and reset functions, and dynamic explanations created a realistic training environment that enhanced operator competency, troubleshooting capability, emergency preparedness, and process safety awareness. The methodology can be expanded to other refinery units and industrial process applications.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Novel/Additive Information</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This paper presents a unique and cost-effective approach for transforming conventional static Cause-and-Effect diagrams into an interactive DCS style visualization and operator training platform using Microsoft Excel VBA and Macros. Unlike traditional training methods, the developed simulator dynamically demonstrates compressor interlocks, alarm annunciation behavior, auto-start logic, shutdown sequences, timer operations, cooling water and lubrication protection systems, and compressor capacity control behavior. A key innovative feature of the platform is its operator-interactive interlock visualization capability, which allows users to manually select interlocks through graphical buttons and immediately observe process responses, alarm generation, and equipment protection actions. The integration of dynamic explanation sections, audible alarm annunciation, and reset-based repeat simulation creates a realistic training environment that enhances operator understanding of process safety, troubleshooting, and compressor protection philosophy while utilizing a widely available and low-cost software platform</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Smart Field Automation in Marginal Assets: A Field Proven Digital Retrofit for Legacy ICSS
container-title: ADIPEC
9b7e9c9caff4475b06baecd54aca1e3447855a14.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Marginal oil and gas assets are increasingly required to deliver dependable production under tight economics, limited modernization budgets, aging automation infrastructure, and stronger expectations for safety, efficiency, and environmental performance. Many such assets rely on legacy Integrated Control and Safety Systems (ICSS), periodic manual well testing, fragmented production reconciliation workflows, and operator-dependent well start-up practices. Complete control-system replacement is often impractical to justify because of capital constraints, brownfield execution risk, and potential production interruption.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>This paper presents a field-proven digital retrofit approach that transforms ESP-driven and naturally flowing marginal wells into smart, remotely managed assets by embedding targeted automation, control logic, and digital surveillance capability within the existing ICSS environment. The solution integrates ESP and VSD operating data, choke and wellhead signals, historian information, OEM operating envelopes, virtual flow estimation, automated well testing, hydrocarbon accounting, production allocation, and Safety Instrumented System alignment into a controlled brownfield execution model.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>The approach supports single push-button start-up, stable steady-state operation, exception-based monitoring, equipment protection, and real-time operational visibility without major infrastructure replacement thus minimal additional CAPEX. Field deployment demonstrated improved production transparency, reduced manual intervention, better ESP operating discipline, enhanced production reconciliation, lower routine field exposure, and a scalable pathway for asset-wide smart operation. It demonstrates that digital transformation in marginal fields can be achieved pragmatically: by maximizing the value of installed systems, preserving safety barriers, and targeting high-value automation functions that directly improve operating economics.</jats:p>

title: Cross-Resolution Surrogate Modeling for CCUS-EOR Digital Twins Using 4DFNO Coupled with a Denoising Hamiltonian Network
container-title: ADIPEC
0096cb793a5ed91d42abaa4fe8b9fb282e88d97b.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Repeated compositional simulation is costly when Carbon Dioxide-Enhanced Oil Recovery (CO2-EOR) is deployed within carbon capture, utilization, and storage (CCUS) workflows that evaluate many geological realizations, assimilate production data, or compare grid resolutions. The proposed framework, termed DHN-4DFNO, couples a four-dimensional Fourier neural operator (4DFNO) with a Denoising Hamiltonian Network (DHN) to predict pressure, oil saturation, and CO2 molar fraction over (t,z,x,y). The 4DFNO provides the global spatiotemporal state fields, while DHN encodes the 4DFNO feature-field response into time-indexed latent variables q and p, applies block-wise denoising Hamiltonian relations conditioned by a trajectory code z, and uses the scaled latent refinement in a 4DFNO-feature residual branch. The training objective combines supervised prediction and coarse-field losses with a Hamiltonian block loss. An optional simulator-exported component residual-label branch is retained in the implementation, but its particle swarm optimization (PSO)-selected weight is zero in the reported model. It therefore contributes neither loss nor gradient during final training. Tests use 1,500 compact compositional CO2-EOR numerical simulations with latent permeability-field variance parameter 0.2. The fixed random split gives 1,350 final-training cases and a 150-case evaluation partition reserved from final model fitting. For representative evaluation case 214, field-specific structural similarity index (SSIM) values are 0.9228-0.9994 over 370 reporting records, and DHN-4DFNO reduces pressure mean squared error (MSE) from 0.6322 to 0.3632 and CO2 molar-fraction MSE from 7.56E−3 to 2.45E−3. The trained framework is also evaluated from the native 40 × 40 × 3 setting to an 80 × 80 × 3 target grid without retraining, where the target-grid reference states are generated by rerunning the compositional simulator after horizontal interpolation of the rock-property fields. The surrogate supports rapid state forecasting, response screening, permeability data assimilation, CO2 storage-accounting post-processing, and net present value (NPV) evaluation.</jats:p>

title: From Trial-And-Error to Structured Digital Engineering: A Closed-Loop Optimization Workflow for HPHT Unconventional Gas Wells
container-title: ADIPEC
bf691a80df2e353d8c8ce9e66f58cabc49a29b53.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>The Middle East unconventional gas development includes three technically demanding hole sections drilled through multiple formation tops with significant lithological and rock strength variation, chert and hard stringer intervals, high temperature conditions, complex directional profiles associated with batch drilled pad wells, and severe drilling dysfunction leading to increased downhole tool failure and flat time, resulting in inconsistent drilling performance across offset wells despite repeated field trials and traditional optimization approaches. The objective of this work was to develop an integrated drilling optimization workflow to improve drilling performance consistency and accelerate implementation efficiency.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>Traditional benchmarking and field trial approaches were insufficient to address the drilling complexity observed. A structured closed loop optimization workflow was developed integrating calibrated simulation and field validation. The workflow integrated offset well evaluation, machine learning based dull cutter analysis, rock strength characterization, and detailed surface and downhole drilling parameter analysis to identify drilling dysfunction and cutter failure mechanisms across all sections. The integrated dataset was used to develop calibrated digital rock models within a 4D finite element analysis environment to evaluate multiple bit and bottomhole assembly design iterations prior to implementation. Final drilling recommendations were field validated using surface drilling data and available high-frequency downhole measurements, where such measurements were available.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>The initial workflow validation was performed across multiple individual wells using baseline bit and bottomhole assembly designs combined with high-frequency downhole measurements. The findings were used to calibrate subsequent digital rock files, drilling-system models, and simulation workflows. The calibrated digital workflow was then used to develop fit-for-purpose bit designs, bottomhole assembly configurations, and drilling parameter roadmaps based on the drilling dysfunction and formation responses identified in each section. The optimized drilling systems were deployed across eight batch-drilled wells and delivered consistent performance improvement across the project population. Compared with the defined historical offset baseline, average ROP increased from 33 to 69 ft/h in the 16-in. section (+109%), from 27 to 41.5 ft/h in the 12.25-in. section (+54%), and from 24.5 to 45.3 ft/h in the 8.5-in. extended high-temperature lateral section (+85%), with the latter drilled over intervals 45–60% longer than the historical baseline. At the project level, average well-delivery time decreased from 71 days for the historical offsets to 49 days across the project wells, representing an average reduction of 31%; the best-performing well reached 41 days, corresponding to a 42% reduction relative to the historical baseline.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>This study demonstrates a scalable digital drilling ecosystem designed to accelerate optimization turnaround in unconventional drilling campaigns where rapid implementation cycles are critical for efficient well delivery. The workflow integrates machine-learning-based cutter analytics, digital rock modelling, calibrated 4D finite element simulation, and field validation using surface and available high-frequency downhole measurements to enable rapid fit-for-purpose drilling-system recommendations while reducing dependency on repeated field-trial iterations.</jats:p>

title: Adaptive Diffusivity LBM Modeling for Hydrogen Leakage Risk Assessment in Nanoporous Caprock of Depleted Gas Reservoirs
container-title: ADIPEC
857a8dc2fd0ad27966d205caa15e430303720258.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Depleted gas reservoirs are important targets for underground hydrogen storage (UHS), but their sealing reliability depends on hydrogen diffusion through nanoporous caprock occupied by methane. Existing leakage assessments commonly use constant diffusivity or sample-averaged effective diffusivity, which cannot capture local diffusivity variations induced by nanopore confinement and hydrogen enrichment. A multicomponent Shan-Chen LBM was extended with a regression-based adaptive diffusivity scheme for H2-CH4 diffusion in nanoporous caprock occupied by methane. Reference diffusion cases covering nanopore diameter and methane saturation were used to infer the gas interaction parameter G by fitting LBM concentration transients to the numerical solution of Fick's second law. An explicit diameter-saturation-G correlation was embedded into the LBM solver. During simulation, local pore diameter and methane saturation were evaluated node by node, allowing diffusivity to update with pore geometry and hydrogen enrichment. We simulated hydrogen diffusion into caprock containing methane with three pore-scale cases: unequal-diameter channels, regular porous media, and irregular porous media. The adaptive diffusivity model captured diffusion suppression caused by nanoconfinement and enhanced spreading near the source. In regular porous media, increasing characteristic pore diameter from 1 to 10 nm raised effective diffusivity from 1.88×10−8 to 5.85×10−8 m2/s and increased centroid migration distance by a factor of 6.01. In irregular structures, nanopore diameter set the baseline diffusivity, while saturation-dependent enhancement became evident mainly in hydrogen-enriched regions. Early spreading preferentially followed large pores connected to the source, while distant large pores contributed little before hydrogen arrival. The effective diffusivity of the irregular structure was 5.254×10−8 m2/s. By contrast, a constant-diffusivity case using the coefficient at the average pore diameter of 5.22 nm gave a 33% lower effective diffusivity, indicating that constant-diffusivity assumptions may underestimate diffusion-controlled hydrogen migration potential in heterogeneous nanoporous caprock. By explicitly incorporating the effects of nanopore diameter and methane saturation on H2-CH4 diffusivity, this study proposes a correlation-based adaptive diffusivity LBM model for caprock in depleted gas reservoirs.</jats:p>

title: Automated Digital Twin Workflow for ESP Surveillance - Enhancing Reliability, Reducing Failures, and Enabling Real-Time Predictive Monitoring in High-Solid Environments
container-title: ADIPEC
d35ac602006a8b8fde528baf90c9187e0b5acaa6.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Electrical Submersible Pumps (ESPs) are widely used in mature oil fields; however, their reliability is significantly impacted in solid-laden environments characterized by scale, sand, and polymer flooding. High solids influx leads to pump choking, increased hydraulic resistance, shaft failures, and rapid performance decline, ultimately reducing ESP run life. Furthermore, conventional ESP surveillance and performance modeling using tools like PROSPER are manual, time-intensive, and impractical for large-scale field applications. To address these challenges, this study details the development and implementation of a fully automated digital workflow at Vedanta Oil & Gas. The system utilizes Python-based automation to extract real-time ESP sensor data and production parameters from field SQL databases.
