Overall, the approach reduced drilling time by up to 17% and well cost by approximately 6%. In addition, fewer tripping operations and more efficient drilling contributed to lower rig energy consumption, improved operational performance, and better well delivery outcomes across multiple field applications.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>This work introduces a digital twin-based drilling decision framework that extends conventional MSE analysis into real-time operational intelligence. Its novelty lies in integrating MSE with structured decision logic to classify drilling states and enable proactive interventions, supporting more autonomous, efficient, and lower-carbon drilling operations in complex field environments.</jats:p>

title: From Data to Decisions: A Closed Loop Digital Reliability Ecosystem for Predictive Maintenance in Stimulation and Coiled Tubing Operations
container-title: ADIPEC
3c7612bc39bb7b36086da4284505d97548df7876.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Hydraulic fracturing and coiled tubing operations rely on mechanically intensive equipment operating under highly variable loads across global environments. Conventional maintenance strategies are often constrained by fragmented data, delayed diagnostics, and reactive interventions, limiting asset utilization and spare parts planning.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>This paper presents the deployment of an integrated digital ecosystem enabling the transition from reactive to condition-based maintenance. By integrating real-time surveillance, Prognostics and Health Management Models (PHMs), and advanced analytics, the ecosystem improves equipment reliability, maximizes asset availability, and reduces operating costs.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>A closed-loop reliability framework was implemented to continuously monitor equipment health, detect degradation, assess risk, and trigger proactive maintenance actions. IoT-enabled instrumentation was deployed across global fracturing and coiled tubing fleets to stream real-time equipment health parameters into a centralized monitoring platform, enabling remote surveillance and fleet-wide visibility. PHMs were developed using historical failure datasets, multivariate parameter correlations, and condition signatures to characterize degradation behavior and predict failure onset. An integrated analytics architecture fused real-time operational data, prognostic model outputs, and condition signatures to continuously assess equipment health, prioritize maintenance actions, and support fleet-level decision making.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>The deployed ecosystem demonstrated the capability to identify emerging fault conditions in critical equipment components, including fracturing pump engines, transmissions, coiled tubing engines, and injector heads, through deviations from normal operating envelopes and evolving fault signatures. These early-warning capabilities enabled condition-based interventions before functional failure and supported improved maintenance planning, equipment availability, and fleet reliability.</jats:p>

title: Transforming Gas Plant Performance Through First-Principle Digital Twin Integration: Enhanced Visualization with Intelligent Engineering Deployment at GTPOGT, Turkmenistan
container-title: ADIPEC
3b3347e34bc3978308e4f2af295c82506e32fb2e.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>As the global energy sector intensifies its focus on efficiency, reliability, and lower carbon operations, industrial digital twins are becoming critical enablers for operational optimization and GHG emissions reduction. Enhanced Visualization with Intelligent Engineering is a new generation, first-principle-based digital twin designed to provide continuous performance insights for complex processing facilities. This paper presents the first deployment of digital twin integration at an international asset, specifically the Gas Treatment Plant and Onshore Gas Terminal (GTPOGT), in Turkmenistan. The deployment demonstrates how process-engineering-led digitalization can translate plant data into operationally relevant insights and measurable value across an integrated gas processing value chain.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>Digital twin integration was developed using a fully integrated steady-state process simulation software model representing the major gas and condensate processing systems in GTPOGT. Its scope encompasses feed gas and condensate reception, feed gas separation, acid gas removal, gas dehydration, hydrocarbon dewpoint control, propane refrigeration, flash gas compression, and condensate stabilization. The solution integrates process simulation with plant historian data, Plant Information Asset Framework, Plant Information Visualization Platform dashboards, automated data conditioning, model-informed key performance indicators, and virtual measurements. This architecture establishes continuous mass balance visibility and enables equipment-level performance diagnostics using a unified engineering model.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>Process studies covering October 2024 to June 2025 identified optimization opportunities in the hydrocarbon dewpointing, propane refrigeration, and flash gas compression systems. Simulation results indicated that achieving the intended temperature profile could increase condensate recovery by up to 28%, representing an estimated margin opportunity of USD 10,000 to USD 30,000 per day on the basis of the stated economic assumptions. Post-cleaning observations showed a 2 to 3°C improvement in performance.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>Flash gas compressor analysis showed that the antisurge valves were frequently open by more than 25% in the first-stage and more than 50% in the second-stage. Simulation estimated that rerouting approximately 2.9 MMscf/D of triethylene glycol (TEG)-treated gas to the compressor suction could reduce dependence on internal gas recycling and improve compressor loading. The value assessment associated compressor trip avoidance and approximately 8 MMscf/D of flaring with a cost avoidance potential of USD 593.75/hour.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>The digital twin integration deployment demonstrates how a first-principle digital twin can transform gas plant performance management from retrospective data review toward model-informed engineering oversight. By combining process fundamentals, operational data, interactive visualization, and targeted scenario analysis, digital twin integration provides a scalable framework for enhancing visibility, identifying optimization opportunities, improving reliability, and supporting GHG emissions reduction initiatives across gas processing plants.</jats:p>

title: IDEAL: A Digital Auditing Platform for Level 2 and Level 3 Audits in Petroleum Development Oman
container-title: ADIPEC
4800f7c9582470abdeb0bc2add296a76b38d72e9.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>This paper presents the development, enhancement, and operational deployment of IDEAL—the platform to Identify, Discuss, Enhance, Assure and Learn—Petroleum Development Oman's digital auditing platform for Level 2 and Level 3 audits. Introduced in 2022, IDEAL was developed to transform conventional auditing practices into a centralized and data-driven assurance process that improves audit execution, corrective action management, service-provider collaboration, and organizational learning across drilling and well engineering operations.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>The platform evolved through continuous user feedback and operational experience, with enhancements focused on workflow simplification, user experience, and centralized action management. Major developments introduced in 2025 included offline mobile functionality for remote field locations, Strength of Controls (SoC) mapping, centralized contractor documentation, and integration of SAIL lists and Corrective Action Requests (CARs). Service providers can participate digitally in audit preparation through document submission and self-assessment and subsequently manage assigned corrective actions and submit supporting evidence for closeout within the same workflow.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>Implementation of IDEAL has improved the visibility, consistency, and accountability of assurance activities by centralizing historical audit records, standardizing audit execution, strengthening action-closeout governance, and enabling recurring findings and control weaknesses to be identified across audits. The reuse of contractor documentation reduces repetitive submissions, while offline functionality enables field personnel to capture audit information in locations with limited connectivity and synchronize the information when network access becomes available.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>The IDEAL journey demonstrates how an integrated digital approach can extend auditing beyond individual compliance assessments toward a collaborative operational assurance process supporting continuous improvement and knowledge sharing. The paper also discusses the future expansion of the platform and potential application of artificial intelligence to support trend identification, evidence assessment, and more proactive, data-driven assurance within the petroleum industry.</jats:p>

title: ADNOC Pre-Retirement Program: A Strategic Workforce Transition Model Advancing Employee Wellbeing, Readiness, Through Sustainable Culture Approach
container-title: ADIPEC
d1fcb4956be5124a8a81aec6b991034da23cae8c.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Organizations worldwide are experiencing a major demographic shift driven by longer life expectancy, changing retirement expectations, evolving economic conditions, and rapid technological advancement. As a result, retirement is increasingly viewed as a structured workforce transition rather than the end of employment. Effective preparation supports employees in maintaining financial security, psychological resilience, social connection, and physical wellbeing after active service.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>Historically, retirement planning in many organizations focused on pension administration, end-of-service benefits, and procedural compliance. These processes remain essential; however, they do not fully address the practical and personal challenges employees may face when transitioning from employment to retirement.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>Modern organizations increasingly recognize that support across the full employment lifecycle strengthens organizational culture, employee trust, employer reputation, and long-term workforce sustainability. Retirement preparation is therefore better positioned as a strategic human capital investment than as a purely administrative activity.</jats:p>

title: Magnetic Field–Enhanced Digital Twin for Battery SoC/SoH Estimation
container-title: ADIPEC
04c49a89d66c2e80c95d925dcca80e9a253ad42f.abstract:
<jats:title>Summary</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>This study adopts a two-step approach for battery state estimation in commercial large-format NMC pouch cells. First, a validated baseline for state of charge (SoC), state of health (SoH), and remaining useful life (RUL) is established using physics-based modeling, conventional electrical and thermal measurements, electrochemical characterization, and machine-learning techniques. Second, spatially resolved magnetic-field measurements are introduced as an additional sensing modality to investigate whether they improve observability of internal current-distribution heterogeneity and reduce estimation uncertainty. A physics-constrained recurrent neural network is used for SoH estimation from cycle-level electrical, thermal, and electrochemical health indicators and is evaluated using leave-one-cell-out cross-validation across 15 cells. The validated baseline achieves a per-cell SoH mean absolute percentage error of 0.94%, compared with 1.83% for a non-physics-informed recurrent baseline. A recurrent SoC estimator using time-resolved voltage, current, and temperature measurements achieves a mean absolute error of 1.12 percentage points of SoC. RUL estimation remains less mature because only five cells have reached the defined end-of-life threshold, with the current point-RUL model achieving 26.97% mean absolute percentage error. In parallel, a spatial magnetic-sensor array provides time-synchronized magnetic-field measurements that are incorporated as additional input features. Ongoing analysis compares the established electrical, thermal, and electrochemical baseline with the same estimators augmented by magnetic-field descriptors under an equivalent validation protocol. The work therefore establishes a rigorously validated baseline and an integrated magnetic-field feature pathway, against which the incremental diagnostic value of magnetic sensing is being assessed through a controlled ablation study.</jats:p>

title: Casing Design Evolution for Geothermal and CCUS Applications: Beyond the Envelope in the Era of Digital and Automated Workflows
container-title: ADIPEC
a37830670f27704ad7650c89c299fa726513505f.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Casing design has historically evolved in response to increasingly complex well environments, advances in modelling capability, and lessons learned from field failures. This paper examines the next phase of that evolution, where Geothermal and Carbon Capture, Utilisation and Storage (CCUS) applications introduce load scenarios, regulatory requirements, and integrity challenges beyond the scope of conventional oil and gas practice. In parallel, the industry is undergoing a broader transition toward digitalisation and automation of design workflows, impacting existing casing design practices.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>The objective of this paper is to assess how geothermal conditions, CO2 containment requirements, and the increasing adoption of automated methodologies for annular pressure variation and management in challenging wells, including subsea developments, together with Open Subsurface Data Universe (OSDU)-based data integration, are reshaping casing design methodology and challenging established approaches.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>The paper reviews emerging casing design challenges across geothermal and CCUS applications and evaluates their compatibility with traditional design frameworks. For hot and superhot geothermal wells, the analysis focuses on environments where plastic deformation, post-yield tubular behaviour, thermal cycling, connection fatigue, and time-dependent material effects become significant. For CCUS wells, the study considers API and Class VI regulatory requirements, together with subsea operating conditions, including trapped annuli, annular pressure reduction, and potential annular vacuum conditions associated with cold CO2 injection.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>In parallel, the role of automated design workflows to address modern well architectures is assessed, particularly for subsea developments where annular pressure behaviour has long been a critical design driver. These workflows include annular pressure variation (APV) and annular pressure envelope (APE) methodologies and are evaluated as part of a broader shift towards scalable, repeatable, and auditable casing design processes, supported by OSDU-based data integration and data sharing.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>The analysis indicates that some next-generation wells introduce conditions that extend beyond the assumptions of conventional elastic, deterministic casing design approaches. Superhot geothermal wells may require intentional design into the post-yield regime, while CCUS wells introduce long-term integrity requirements, complex thermodynamic behaviour, and annular pressure responses not fully captured by traditional load cases. At the same time, automated annular pressure methodologies enable more systematic evaluation of multi-scenario loading conditions across a wide range of well types, extending beyond CCUS-specific applications.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>Existing API standards and regulatory frameworks, including Class VI, provide an essential foundation but do not fully address all of the emerging design considerations associated with these applications. Digital workflows and integrated data platforms improve the ability to manage complexity but introduce new challenges related to model transparency and preservation of engineering judgement.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>This paper positions geothermal and CCUS applications as part of the next stage in the evolution of casing design, while also identifying automation and digital integration as independent drivers of change across the industry. It integrates post-yield geothermal design, CCUS annular behaviour including pressure reduction and vacuum conditions, regulatory considerations, and automated annular pressure methodologies within a unified framework.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>The work highlights a transition toward system-level, lifecycle-based casing design, supported by digital data environments such as OSDU, providing a forward-looking perspective on well integrity in increasingly complex and long-duration operating conditions.</jats:p>

title: AI-Assisted Marine Logistics Digital Twin for Optimizing Dredger, Barge, and Support Vessel Coordination
container-title: ADIPEC
68fc7a4d1626eeb58edea0e9dd7b9251fe008f77.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Marine construction projects may combine several material-transfer methods that must operate as one coordinated production system. In the studied configuration, a self-propelled hopper dredger transports material in its own hopper, a cutter suction dredger delivers slurry through a pipeline, and sand barges handle approximately 20% of the modeled sand volume. These operations also depend on tugboats, a multicat, a fuel barge, a survey boat, rock barges, receiving-area availability, and onshore equipment. Poor coordination between these resources can increase waiting time, interrupt production, and raise fuel consumption. This paper proposes an AI-assisted marine logistics digital twin that maintains an updated virtual representation of vessel status, dredging progress, pipeline condition, weather restrictions, support-resource availability, and island receiving capacity. The AI component consists of two supervised XGBoost models trained, validated, and tested using a physics-informed synthetic dataset developed within published equipment operating ranges and explicit engineering assumptions. A regression model predicts hopper-dredger cycle duration and discharge waiting, while a classification model estimates the probability of a pipeline interruption during the following operating period. These predictions are incorporated into a rolling-horizon decision method that evaluates discharge timing, vessel assignments, sailing speeds, pipeline operating conditions, and support-service windows as the operational state changes. The framework was evaluated through a representative 14-day island-reclamation scenario using paired simulations of predefined rule-based and ML-assisted rolling-horizon coordination. The ML-assisted strategy increased modeled placed sand by approximately 6%, reduced mean hopper-dredger discharge waiting by approximately 83%, and lowered fuel intensity by approximately 10%. It also reduced CSD and pipeline downtime and improved the reliability of meeting the daily production target. These values are simulation-based proof-of-concept results generated under defined engineering assumptions and should be interpreted as a validation pathway for future project-data deployment rather than as measured field performance. The results show that the main value of the digital twin lies in using ML predictions to coordinate dredging, transport, pipeline, support, and receiving activities as one connected operation rather than optimizing individual assets separately.</jats:p>

title: Virtual Wellbore Strengthening Deployment Using Predictive Modeling, Real-Time Fluid Monitoring, and Digital Advisory Integration
container-title: ADIPEC
37f5abc1dbe6791c798166e244a26634a78ed3c4.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Lost circulation and wellbore instability remain among the most significant contributors to non-productive time (NPT), increased well construction costs, and well integrity risks in drilling operations. Formations such as porous carbonate and shale present a particularly challenging environment where drilling operations must remain within a narrow mud-weight (MW) and equivalent-circulating-density (ECD) operating window. In carbonate formations, naturally fractured intervals and thief zones can initiate partial-to-total losses once ECD approaches the fracture limit, while Shales typically requires higher mud weights to maintain wellbore stability. This creates a narrow margin between the stability floor and fracture ceiling, increasing operational risk and limiting drilling flexibility. Conventional lost-circulation management practices generally rely on reactive treatments using generic lost circulation material (LCM) formulations that are frequently unable to account for formation-specific fracture geometries and uncertainty in subsurface conditions.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>This paper presents an integrated workflow that combines probabilistic geomechanics, Virtual wellbore strengthening (VWBS), Fracture-Bridging Simulator, laboratory validation, and real-time drilling surveillance into a unified framework for proactive loss prevention. A geomechanics pilot was conducted for the interval to calibrate pore pressure, fracture gradient, in-situ stresses, and rock mechanical properties. The calibrated model was subsequently implemented within VWBS Plan to generate P10, P50, and P90 wellbore stability envelopes that defined depth-dependent MW and ECD operating limits. Predicted fracture-opening widths were then utilized within the Fracture-Bridging Simulator module to engineer customized stress-cage and bridging-material formulations based on formation-specific fracture characteristics.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>The engineered formulations were validated through laboratory slot-plugging and pressure-holding tests prior to field implementation. During drilling operations, real-time measurements and VWBS Wellsite were integrated into a closed-loop advisory workflow capable of continuously comparing planned and actual drilling conditions. The system identified deviations in ECD, rheology, hydraulics, and PSD requirements, allowing adaptive mitigation measures to be implemented before significant losses occurred. Key performance indicators included drilling-fluid losses, pill success rate, percentage drilling time within the designed fracture-opening envelope, and NPT associated with losses and wellbore stability events (Whitfill 2008).</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>The study demonstrates how integration of geomechanics, drilling-fluid engineering, laboratory validation, and digital drilling technologies can transform wellbore strengthening from a reactive lost-circulation treatment into a predictive and preventative workflow. The proposed methodology establishes a scalable framework for the application of Well Bore Strengthening in fractured formations and narrow drilling-window environments.</jats:p>

title: AI-Powered Smart Port Operations: A Digital Transformation Roadmap for Marine Safety, Efficiency, and Compliance
container-title: ADIPEC
38f318a8a716a132758b3022e52073a221e38348.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Marine jetty and port operations within onshore oil-field environments require continuous safety compliance, controlled access, reliable vessel visibility, asset availability, environmental awareness, and disciplined response to abnormal conditions. Manual supervision remains essential, but it can be limited when activities are distributed across jetties, gates, contractor areas, mooring zones, navigation channels, and control-room interfaces. This paper presents an AI-powered Smart Port Operations roadmap for ADNOC Onshore NEB Marine Operations. The roadmap expands the immediate smart-gate, AI CCTV, and Marine Control Room concept into a full digital ecosystem that integrates people, processes, infrastructure, vessels, and data. The model includes vessel traffic information, berth and jetty management, smart gate access, digital permit-to-work, predictive maintenance, smart navigation aids, drone inspections, smart dredging management, environmental monitoring, digital marine logistics, AI-based analytics, smart security, and a live digital twin. The paper describes the current operational challenge, the transformation framework, the fourteen initiatives, the technical application of priority systems, governance requirements, implementation assurance, limitations, and a phased five-year roadmap. It also aligns the concept with recognized maritime guidance, including IMO e-navigation principles, ISPS security objectives, IALA navigation-aid guidance, and port sustainability themes. The main conclusion is that smart-port value is created when surveillance, access control, asset monitoring, vessel traffic data, dashboards, alerts, and response workflows operate as one integrated management system. AI and automation should assist authorized personnel, improve consistency, and increase the quality of evidence, while accountable marine decision-making remains with trained operators and supervisors. The proposed roadmap therefore provides a practical path toward safer, more efficient, more resilient, and more sustainable marine operations at NEB.</jats:p>

title: Intelligent Cross-Well Static Rock-Type Identification from Sparse Geological and Petrophysical Evidence Using Adaptive Geo-Wavelet Networks with Masked Heterogeneous Supervision
container-title: ADIPEC
7892538560faf1ecdf3027d39d52dff7e257529a.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Static rock-type identification in heterogeneous carbonate reservoirs has to reflect both depositional and diagenetic fabric and the pore-throat system. In practice, the supporting evidence is sparse: thin-section descriptions, mercury-injection capillary-pressure tests, and expert SRT labels are rarely recorded at the same depth. We present the Adaptive Geo-Wavelet Network with Masked Heterogeneous Supervision (AGW-MHS). It uses these partially paired observations only during training, combining an adaptive geowavelet encoder with dynamic domain alignment (AGW-DDA). Auxiliary CRT1 to CRT5 and PG1 to PG5 heads are activated only for records that carry the corresponding label, while Gaussian soft depth-window pooling links each physical sample to a short interval of log data. The auxiliary heads are removed before inference, so an uncored well is interpreted from six conventional logs and the formation boundaries alone. In an anonymized Upper Cretaceous carbonate interval, 232 records from 10 wells were available, but only 45 had all three labels. Under transductive 10-fold leave-one-well-out validation, AGW-MHS reached a mean per-well macro-F1 of 0.772 versus 0.731 for the matched AGW-DDA baseline without auxiliary supervision. The paired gain was 0.041 (95% bootstrap CI 0.029 to 0.053; exact sign-flip p=0.0039), with improvements in 9 of 10 wells. Retaining half of the auxiliary labels gave 0.755 macro- F1. With synthetic plus or minus 1 m depth perturbations, soft-window association scored 0.761, compared with 0.728 for nearest-depth matching. The results indicate that sparse physical evidence can strengthen cross-well log interpretation without becoming a deployment input, provided the model remains within the same field-scale stratigraphic framework.</jats:p>

title: A Model-Based Digital Thread Approach for Managing the Complexity of Next-Generation Offshore Support Vessels Design, Build, Delivery and Beyond
container-title: ADIPEC
aeabdfc9fa4ab5128a3847814ba06bbeaa3786ce.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Objectives and Scope</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Growth in offshore wind, subsea construction, and carbon capture and storage is reshaping the missions OSVs are built to support. Traditionally designed to provide logistics, transportation, and operational support to offshore oil and gas installations, modern OSVs are now expected to support a much wider range of missions. These include offshore wind farm installation and maintenance, subsea construction and inspection activities, carbon capture and storage (CCS), low-carbon energy infrastructure remote and autonomous operations, environmental monitoring and operations involving increasingly sophisticated power and propulsion systems. At the same time, vessel owners and operators face growing pressure to improve sustainability, reduce emissions, enhance operational efficiency, and maintain compliance with increasingly demanding regulatory and classification requirements.</jats:p>
                    <jats:p>As a result, the design, construction, operation, and maintenance of OSVs have become substantially more complex than in previous generations of vessels. Modern vessels contain a greater number of integrated systems, including hybrid and electric propulsion architectures, advanced automation and control systems, dynamic positioning technologies, sensor networks, communication platforms, and mission-specific equipment. These interconnected systems generate large volumes of engineering, operational, maintenance, and regulatory information throughout the vessel lifecycle all the way from preliminary and initial designs to construction and further to operations and eventual refit.</jats:p>
                    <jats:p>Managing this information effectively has emerged as one of the primary challenges facing both shipbuilders and vessel operators. In many organizations, critical lifecycle information remains fragmented across multiple disconnected systems, databases, spreadsheets, documents, and departmental processes. This fragmentation often results in inconsistent information, duplicated effort, reduced traceability, delayed decision-making, and increased lifecycle costs. It also creates challenges when managing vessel modifications, upgrades, certification activities, and maintenance programs throughout decades of operation.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: First Field Application of a Novel Digital Semi-Automated Ion Measurement Technology for Water-Based Drilling Fluids
container-title: ADIPEC
1e04cb394e4787a540d2ee621d74cd32d07d7d80.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Conventional drilling-fluid testing provides essential field information for water-based mud (WBM) management, but it provides limited visibility of concentrations of many mud components, specially chemically active species that influence mud performance during drilling. This limitation is particularly important when WBM systems are used to drill reactive shale formations, where shale inhibitors concentration in the system may fluctuate during drilling due to system dilution, treatment additions, and fluid-formation interactions.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>This paper presents the first field deployment of a novel digital, semi-automated chemical-analyzing technology capable of providing rapid measurement of ionic species and selected shale-inhibitor concentrations in a WBM system under rig-site conditions.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>The objective of this study is to evaluate the capability of a novel continuous chemical analyzing technology to quantify depletion of key shale inhibitors, specifically potassium ion and polyamine-based additives, and to assess its value in improving drilling-fluid monitoring and management across reactive shale formations. The technology was deployed across three offshore wells in the UAE to monitor potassium, sodium, chloride, polyamine, and other drilling-fluid ionic components during drilling. Time- and depth-based paired active-pit and flowline samples were used to evaluate apparent chemical depletion after circulation through the wellbore and exposure to reactive shale intervals.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>The study demonstrated that semi-automated, analytical chemical monitoring workflow can identify chemical depletion trends across reactive shale intervals, which can be correlated and supported by mineralogical and CEC analyses. Compared with conventional testing, the technology provides improved visibility of fluid–formation interaction, inhibitor depletion, treatment response, and chemical variability.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>The multi-well deployments validated the technology and support more predictive, depletion-based chemical management. This may expand HPWBM applications into intervals traditionally drilled with non-aqueous fluids (NAF), with potential benefits in NAF usage reduction and associated waste management, environmental impact, and drilling economics.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>Future work will extend the technology application to other aqueous fluid systems and additives and will incorporate predictive analytics for proactive chemical optimization.</jats:p>

title: Probabilistic Fatigue Digital Twin for Offshore Jackets: Ensemble Kalman Filtering with a Tidal Calibration Signal — A Simulation-Based Feasibility Study
container-title: ADIPEC
eecf3f551070b1e656c48655b163ee9b706cdaf8.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Objectives/Scope</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>To replace the current practice of managing fatigue in ageing offshore jackets through periodic inspection with a continuous digital twin that uses sensor readings to give operators updated information on each joint after every tidal cycle. The current approach is limited to a pre-installation fatigue calculation and ROV inspection every three to five years, which fails to detect damage developing between intervals. This paper presents a monitoring framework that addresses this gap using freely available environmental loading signals.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods, Procedures, Process</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>FBG optical strain sensors, with long-term drift below 0.05 µstrain per year and resolution of 0.1 µstrain, together with acoustic-emission detectors, are installed on fatigue-critical joints by ROV clamp retrofit, with no alteration to existing production infrastructure. A log-transformed Ensemble Kalman Filter with multiplicative covariance inflation continuously updates the probability distribution of remaining fatigue life using DNV-RP-C203 seawater S-N curves with Arabian Gulf corrosion-fatigue corrections and BS 7910 fracture mechanics. The tidal loading and diurnal thermal cycle serve as free structural calibration signals, each separated from wave loading by three to four orders of magnitude in frequency and extracted by narrow-band spectral filtering and coherent phase-averaging over multiple cycles.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results, Observations, Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>For a representative K-joint (chord OD = 762 mm, wall = 25 mm, brace angle = 45°, spring tidal current = 0.8 m/s), elastic frame analysis gives an intact excess strain ratio of 0.200 at the bracketing sensor pair. A 20% through-wall crack producing a 10% local stiffness reduction raises this ratio by 11.1%; the underlying crack-to-stiffness relation is a modelling assumption that requires experimental validation and is not a measured result. The detection threshold (an SNR of 3) is reached in about 1.4 days under spring tides, while during neap periods the diurnal thermal signal maintains detection coverage, confirming that the dual-signal architecture is necessary rather than optional. Across a synthetic five-year validation parameterised on Abu Dhabi metocean data, the log-EnKF converges to within 8% of the true remaining fatigue life within about 13 months, narrows the 90% credible interval from ±2.2 to ±0.4 years by month 36, and flags a crack that the conventional S-N model leaves undetected over the same period. For a representative fleet of 30 fixed steel jackets, a lifecycle-cost scenario indicates that condition-based monitoring reaches break-even only if it reduces the annual unplanned-intervention probability by about 0.5 percentage points; no net saving is demonstrated. All results are simulation-based, and field validation is required before any operational or economic claim.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Metering Digital Twin: A Game Changer to Monitor MPFM Health and Sustain Accuracy in Well Testing and Custody Meter Transfer
container-title: ADIPEC
60f586fe777e22e93ffc260b56fdd0866d2dd328.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Metering is fundamental to well testing, gas-lift surveillance, custody transfer, back-allocation, and reservoir simulation workflows. However, critical metering technologies, particularly multiphase flow meters (MPFMs), often operate as "black boxes," limiting visibility into meter health, calibration validity, and measurement uncertainty. In many installations, limited access to raw sensor measurements and insufficient transparency of flow-computer calculations make it difficult to detect drift, verify performance, and sustain long-term measurement accuracy.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>To address these challenges, a metering digital twin is developed for each field meter to replicate its operating modes, response characteristics, and flow-computer calculations from raw sensor signals to reported flow rates. The twin continuously ingests live measurements to monitor operating envelopes, infer fluid-property behavior, assess meter condition, and detect parameter drift or abnormal responses. It then supports corrective actions, including profile updates, computation tuning, and calibration verification, to maintain measurement accuracy during routine operations. In addition, what-if simulations are performed within the twin environment to evaluate proposed changes and operating scenarios before field implementation.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>A Remote Metering Monitoring (RMM) solution was piloted in a Middle East onshore asset to develop and validate the metering digital twin concept. The pilot scope included multi-vendor MPFMs, multi-vendor gas-lift meters, a fixed test separator, and field custody-transfer meters. Raw measurement tags from each meter were configured in the platform, and the digital twin reproduced flow- computer logic to calculate flow rates at line and standard conditions. Thermodynamic PVT models were applied to convert line measurements to standard conditions and diagnose sensitivity to fluid-property assumptions. Following deployment, the twin recommended targeted corrections to well-fluid properties and PVT profiles prior to updating the respective meters. The impact was verified during MPFM well testing by comparing results before and after property updates, demonstrating improved oil-rate estimates and enhanced measurement consistency. This paper presents the pilot architecture, configuration and testing methodology, user acceptance results, implementation limitations, and roadmap for full-field deployment.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>The principal contribution of this work is a vendor-agnostic metering digital twin that exposes raw measurements and reproduces flow-computer calculations to enable continuous, traceable meter-health surveillance. By integrating physics-based PVT conversion, real-time diagnostics, and what-if simulation, the solution identifies measurement drift, recommends calibration and profile updates, and de-risks operational changes before field execution. The approach provides a scalable framework to sustain well-test, allocation, gas-lift, and custody-transfer measurement accuracy across large and diverse meter populations.</jats:p>

title: Non-Intrusive Assessment of PVT and MPFM Configuration Parameter Impacts on Multiphase Flow Meter Performance Using a Proprietary Digital Twin Framework
container-title: ADIPEC
309aaed391c4cbb5d175ded1d0dd1c5266949ebc.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Multiphase Flow Meters (MPFMs) play a critical role in modern oil and gas operations by providing continuous measurements of oil, water, and gas production without the need for conventional test separators. However, MPFM performance is influenced not only by meter hardware but also by the fluid-property data and configuration parameters used within the meter calculation models. Depending on the meter technology and measurement principles employed, these inputs may include Pressure-Volume-Temperature (PVT) data, fluid-characterization properties, calibration settings, and other configuration parameters. Operators routinely update such inputs to improve measurement performance; however, understanding the impact of these changes before implementation remains challenging. Conventional validation typically relies on well testing, making it difficult to isolate the effect of individual updates from normal variations in production and operating conditions</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>This paper presents a practical methodology that uses a proprietary MPFM Digital Twin to evaluate the impact of fluid-property (PVT) updates and key meter configuration parameters. After calibration against trusted well-test data, the MPFM Digital Twin was used to assess proposed changes, perform sensitivity analyses, and investigate measurement deviations while maintaining the same operating conditions. This approach allows the effect of individual changes to be evaluated before implementation, helping reduce uncertainty and supporting more effective deployment planning, troubleshooting, and measurement-assurance activities.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>The methodology was applied to various field case studies, two are demonstrated in paper. In a deepwater asset, the MPFM Digital Twin was used to evaluate the transition from a field-wide PVT model to well-specific PVT data across multiple producing wells. The analysis showed that sensitivity to PVT updates varied considerably between wells, ranging from negligible effects to more than 10% changes in calculated oil and gas rates. These results enabled the asset team to identify the wells most affected by the PVT update and prioritize validation efforts accordingly. In a mature brownfield asset, the MPFM Digital Twin was used to evaluate MPFM configuration parameters, assess vendor-recommended updates, and investigate measurement discrepancies. The analysis identified key parameter sensitivities and isolated configuration-related causes of measurement deviations. In one application, the resulting configuration changes helped in reducing the MPFM water-cut from approximately 70% to 45%, demonstrating the value of Digital Twin-assisted troubleshooting and optimization</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>The results showed that sensitivity to PVT and configuration changes varied considerably across wells and operating conditions. The MPFM Digital Twin quantified these effects, identified key drivers of measurement deviations, and enabled informed evaluation of proposed updates before deployment.</jats:p>

title: Closed-Loop Remote Optimization of ESP Systems Using Real-Time Voltage/Frequency Control: A Field-Proven Digital Method to Reduce Energy, Emissions, and Failure Risk
container-title: ADIPEC
921e9d52a689519fa6eca9911c05d9e113f19c01.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>This paper presents a closed-loop, fully remote optimization framework for Electrical Submersible Pump (ESP) systems, validated across 9 wells in a mature field in Ecuador, that dynamically adjusts motor operating conditions. Unlike conventional ESP tuning practices relying on periodic manual interventions or static design assumptions, this approach continuously optimizes the voltage/frequency (V/f) ratio based on real-time electrical readings. The objective is to reduce energy consumption, emissions, and equipment failures without interrupting production or requiring field intervention.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>The methodology integrates high-frequency telemetry with a real-time decision workflow that continuously evaluates motor loading, power consumption, and thermal behavior. Variable Speed Drive (VSD) parameters are remotely modified through dynamic adjustment of the Frequency Base (FBase), enabling continuous optimization of the Voltage/Frequency ratio. A data-driven diagnostic classifies operating regimes as over-magnetized or under-magnetized, and corrective actions are applied accordingly. Underloaded systems receive voltage reductions to eliminate excess magnetizing current; overloaded systems receive controlled voltage increases to restore torque capability. All adjustments are executed online, forming a closed-loop cycle with no well shutdowns, site visits, or production deferral.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>Field deployment across 9 pilot ESP units demonstrated average real power reductions of 2.5% for over-magnetized systems, with savings up to 4.9 kW per well. Annual CO2 emission reductions were estimated between 9.6 and 28.8 metric tons per ESP. Thermal stabilization was observed across several optimized systems, with motor temperature reductions of up to 3.7°F—directly contributing to insulation integrity and extended run life. Systems operating beyond nominal load (101%) exhibited measurable efficiency improvements following voltage correction, confirming that conventional derating strategies overlook optimization opportunities in under-magnetized cases. Average economic savings reached $225 USD per month per well, while eliminating deferred production and reducing exposure to start-up-related mechanical and electrical stresses—key contributors to premature ESP failure.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>This work redefines ESP optimization as a continuous digital process rather than a discrete field intervention. The demonstrated ability to simultaneously reduce energy consumption, lower carbon emissions, and extend equipment run life—while operating 100% remotely with zero HSE exposure—establishes a scalable pathway toward autonomous artificial lift management in mature fields. The finding that controlled voltage increases in under-magnetized motors yield measurable energy savings challenges established derating conventions and introduces a new optimization paradigm.</jats:p>

title: Enabling Resilient and Adaptive Production Operations Through AI-Enabled Production System Optimization at Scale
container-title: ADIPEC
3cfb0f97f5e944fb74e1155b11eff77411fb1196.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>ADNOC has deployed an AI-enabled Production System Optimization (AiPSO) solution to strengthen the resilience, flexibility, and responsiveness of production operations under increasing global supply demand uncertainty. This paper presents the value outcomes from the Phase-1 implementation across eight producing fields, demonstrating how real-time production intelligence and rapid scenario planning enable proactive, compliant, and value-driven production operations at scale.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>AiPSO is implemented as an integrated Production System Digital Twin spanning reservoirs, wells, and surface production systems, combining physics-based engineering models with AI-driven analytics. A scalable Industrial Data and AI Foundation automates real-time data ingestion, validation, contextualization, and model orchestration through a centralized DataOps pipeline. Core workflows include exception-based surveillance, automated diagnostics, scenario-aware production optimization, and execution tracking. Generative AI capabilities evolve from an engineering copilot to domain-specific advisory services and AiPSO Agents, accelerating scenario evaluation and shortening the decision-to-action cycle. Real-time engineering operating envelopes enable safe, constraint-aware execution and controlled autonomy.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>The Phase-1 deployment of AiPSO across eight producing fields during 2025–2026 delivered measurable business value by enhancing ADNOC's ability to anticipate, evaluate, and respond to production variability and operational uncertainty. More than 25 advanced digital workflows were operationalized, enabling real-time surveillance, automated diagnostics, and intelligent optimization, resulting in a sustained 1–2% production uplift with no incremental CAPEX.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>Key workflows, including exception-based well surveillance, artificial-lift diagnostics, multiphase flowmeter validation, and integrated production monitoring, significantly improved data confidence, asset visibility, and decision quality. The integrated digital twin enabled earlier identification of reservoir, well, and surface constraints, reducing time-to-intervention and improving production stability. Operations shifted from reactive issue resolution to proactive, scenario-driven constraint management. GenAI-enabled workflows accelerated root-cause analysis and response planning, while real-time operating envelopes supported safe closed-loop adjustments, strengthening operational resilience and supply reliability.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>This paper presents a multi-field, enterprise-scale application of AI-driven production system digital twins focused on operational resilience and rapid scenario planning. The integration of Generative AI evolving from engineering copilots to action-ready AiPSO Agents represents a novel advancement beyond traditional digital oilfield practices, enabling proactive, adaptive, and increasingly autonomous production operations across large, complex upstream assets.</jats:p>

title: Revolutionising Asset Performance Management Through Autonomous Robotics and Integrated Digital Platform Intelligence: First Deployment of an ATEX/IECEX-Rated Quadruped Robot in Kuwait
container-title: ADIPEC
062966d13bfb17389c860995870dff7a02dd0f5f.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Reliability engineers in operating facilities are increasingly burdened by the manual aggregation of asset health data from disparate sources — process historians, ERP systems, and periodic inspection records — leaving limited capacity for higher-value analysis and decision-making. This paper presents the design and first deployment of an integrated autonomous inspection and asset performance management solution at a Kuwait Oil Company (KOC) facility, delivered through a tripartite collaboration between KOC, SLB and ANYbotics. The core objective was to demonstrate that continuous, robot-acquired inspection data — fused with existing ERP and DCS data on SLB's platform — could enable AI and physics-based models to autonomously generate asset health and maintenance actions, fundamentally augmenting the role of the reliability engineer.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>The solution architecture comprises three integrated layers. First, the ANYmal X quadruped robot — certified for Zone 1 and Zone 2 explosive atmospheres — was deployed to conduct autonomous inspection rounds across the KOC facility. The quadruped's terrain mobility across stairs, gratings, elevated structures, and confined walkways enabled coverage of approximately 70–80% of total inspection routes, including persistent monitoring of identified bad actor assets responsible for disproportionate unplanned downtime. The robot's multi-modal payload captures thermal anomalies, acoustic signatures, visual data with AI-based interpretation, and gas leak detection at frequencies unachievable through manual rounds. Due to the applicable explosive-atmosphere standards were written for fixed installations and manned mobile plants rather than for autonomous legged machines, the paper also sets the challenges in the design and realization of an Ex-product for such applications.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>Second, this continuous stream of inspection data is ingested into SLB's asset performance management platform; OptiSite - alongside existing asset health data — real-time process values from the DCS and equipment history and work orders from the ERP — creating a unified, continuously enriched data foundation for each asset.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>Third, SLB's AI models and physics-based models operate on this fused dataset to automatically generate prioritised maintenance recommendations, failure risk assessments, and asset health scores. The system was designed to take on a significant portion of the routine analytical workload traditionally performed by KOC's reliability engineers, allowing them to focus on complex exception handling and strategic decision-making.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>The deployment demonstrated that fusing autonomous robotic inspection data with ERP and DCS sources on a single intelligent platform produces a qualitative shift in asset performance management capability. Coverage of 70–80% of inspection rounds — with targeted monitoring of bad actor assets — provided reliability teams with a continuous, objective view of asset condition that manual inspection cycles cannot sustain. AI and physical model outputs translated this enriched data into actionable maintenance recommendations, measurably reducing the analytical burden on reliability engineers and shortening the time from anomaly detection to intervention. Personnel exposure in hazardous zones was also substantially reduced, improving HSE performance at the KOC facility.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>This paper presents the first deployment of the ATEX/IECEx-rated quadruped in an Ex-rated operational environment in Kuwait and the first documented implementation of a fully integrated solution combining quadruped robotic inspection — thermal, acoustic, visual interpretation, and gas detection — with ERP, DCS and AI-driven asset performance models on a single platform. The novelty lies not in any individual component, but in the end-to-end architecture: robot-acquired field data continuously enriching a digital asset health foundation, with AI and physical models closing the loop from data to action. This model represents a scalable blueprint for augmenting reliability engineering workflows across GCC operating facilities. The paper closes with a discussion of the deployment's limitations, challenges, and future work as the programme moves into its Expand and Commit phases.</jats:p>

title: Coupled Experimental Rock Deformation and Digital Rock Physics Based Investigation Into the Poro-Mechanical Evolution of Carbonate Reservoir Rocks
container-title: ADIPEC
2840f8dfe5d715d1db2f7d4f964fddbe1cb01f62.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Whilst stress-induced elasticity is known to offer controls over fluid flow in carbonate reservoirs, both during recoverable loading-unloading, and as a precursor to irrecoverable failure and occlusion of the pore system, standard bulk geomechanical tests alone miss the pore-scale damage that drive permeability collapse. Permeability can remain nearly quasi-stable during elastic loading prior to dropping sharply once yielding and pore collapse initiates. Microscopic damage induced by poro-elastic loading, as well as its role in the localization of irrecoverable failure within the porous framework remains irresolvable by core plug scale bulk triaxial loading tests alone. This study addresses this gap by coupling triaxial loading of carbonate rocks (Indiana Limestone) with high-resolution micro-computed tomography, digital volume correlation (DVC), and image-based computational fluid dynamics. Measured plug porosities were moderate, and liquid-permeability testing prioritized brine over distilled water to mitigate mobilization of fines promoted by the ingress of low salinity fluids. Considerable sample-to-sample variability in petrophysical properties was observed, with brine permeability ranging from 39 to 136 mD and distilled-water permeability from 45 to 265 mD. Unconfined compression gave a peak strength of 35.6 MPa and a Young's modulus of 17.8 GPa, with brittle failure typical of porous granular carbonates. Subsequently, triaxial loading of another sample (S3) was performed until just before reaching its yield point, followed by post-deformation imaging, which captured the change in pore structure, while DVC mapped the full-field displacement and strain, resolving diffuse, dilation-dominated non-elastic deformation. The deformed pore geometry was meshed and used for two-phase, oil-brine drainage simulation. Comparison of the pre- and post-compression cases showed that loading altered the connected pore geometry and the displacement response at the pore scale: the post-compression case reached breakthrough earlier, showed a more fluctuating inlet-pressure response, and had a lower measured permeability, decreasing from 265.04 mD to 164.44 mD. These results tie the loss of flow capacity to specific pore-scale changes: the connected pathways rerouted, the inlet pressure became less stable, and breakthrough came earlier, none of which is observable using conventional rock mechanical testing in isolation. Linking experimentally deformed rock directly to pore-scale simulation in this way gives a physically meaningful workflow for predicting reservoir performance and subsurface storage behavior in carbonate formations.</jats:p>

title: Generative 3d Asset Reconstruction from Few Images for Scalable Industrial Digital Twins in Turbomachinery Assembly
container-title: ADIPEC
2680fe8bb792c3bdd17045ac2a40d7e212680ad4.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Digital twin initiatives are frequently constrained by the limited availability of three-dimensional asset models. This work presents an industrial adaptation of a structured-latent, flow-matching generative 3D reconstruction model for rapid reconstruction of industrial assets from one to four photographs. The proposed modification augments the original image-conditioned flow-matching pipeline with a multi-image conditioning mechanism that appends multiple image embeddings to the conditioning sequence. The method was developed to support creation of a manufacturing digital twin for turbomachinery assembly environments. Generated assets are integrated into workflows supporting layout validation, ergonomics assessment, logistics planning, material-flow analysis and scenario simulation. Preliminary industrial evaluation indicates that multi-image conditioning improves reconstruction completeness for assets containing significant self-occlusion while preserving workflow simplicity. The paper discusses architecture, deployment pipeline, qualitative results, limitations and future research directions.</jats:p>

title: From Flaring to Value: A Scalable and Digital Enabled Multi Well Pad Green Completion Model Delivering 94% Emissions Reduction in Oman
container-title: ADIPEC
2896e50a42d196c6b42bb4333256e788f4518459.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Hydraulically fractured gas wells commonly require extended cleanup and testing periods during which significant volumes of hydrocarbons may be flared. Strategies to reduce emissions by capturing and exporting hydrocarbons during well flowback, commonly called "Green Completions", have been deployed in several producing basins in the middle east, however widespread implementation remains challenged by facility interfaces, solids and water management requirements, process safety considerations, and operational complexity. The need for scalable solutions is increasing as operators seek to simultaneously reduce emissions and improve project value.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>Shell Development Oman is advancing Green Completions as a component of its low carbon strategy by deploying reduced emission completion frameworks with a focus on enhancing asset performance during post-frac flowback operations. This addresses the dual challenge of maintaining production excellence while meeting stringent decarbonization targets.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>This paper presents a novel case study of the design, planning, and execution of Green Completions in a tight gas condensate asset in Oman, constituting a next-generation model integrating multi-well pad operations, direct tie-in to production facilities, advanced four-phase separation and solids management, digital real-time surveillance, and simultaneous operations framework into a low-carbon value stream. The case study presents a roadmap for operators to reduce flaring while improving operational efficiency and value.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>The case study highlights the successful integration of decarbonization objectives, process safety, and digital operational excellence, positioning Green Completions as a scalable and commercially viable solution for sustainable upstream development.</jats:p>

title: Hybrid Digital Twin for Sensor Mapping, Realtime Leak Source Detection and Dispersion Forecasting
container-title: ADIPEC
fa8d92d18a1de88b56bc357ff0bddd83deefde9a.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Industrial emergency response to accidental releases of toxic or flammable substances requires a rapid estimate of where a release is occurring, how the released cloud will move through the installation, and which areas may be affected in the immediate future. In congested process facilities, these tasks are difficult because buildings, process equipment, storage facilities, terrain, vegetation, low wind conditions, and local turbulence can strongly alter the wind field and plume trajectory. This paper presents a hybrid digital twin architecture in which a site-specific three-dimensional computational fluid dynamics (CFD) model provides the physical basis for gas- flow and dispersion prediction, while inverse CFD and reduced-order modelling provide the speed required for real-time operation. The digital twin continuously receives detector and weather information. When detector levels indicate a possible release, an inverse source-mapping stage estimates the most likely source location, effective release intensity, and release start time from measured concentration patterns. The resulting source estimate is then passed to a real-time dispersion forecasting stage to generate three-dimensional concentration fields and near-term impact information. A CFD-based sensor-mapping methodology is used during system configuration to evaluate sensor visibility under representative source and wind conditions, thereby improving the probability that the detector network can observe relevant plume trajectories. The numerical approach builds three-dimensional atmospheric flow was solved with mass, momentum, and energy conservation, a k-epsilon turbulence model, Monin-Obukhov based micrometeorological treatment, and Eulerian-Lagrangian treatment of flow and species transport. The source-identification formulation uses Bayesian inference and Markov Chain Monte Carlo sampling to handle sparse and noisy measurements. Earlier field work at a complex industrial site included SF6 tracer-release campaigns and comparison of measured and numerical concentration distributions, with the CFD approach reproducing important plume trends in congested geometry. The resulting architecture has also been demonstrated in operational real-time installations and has reported source-location error below 30 m in a representative application. The paper discusses the digital twin architecture, sensor mapping, inverse source localization, accelerated forecasting, validation evidence, and the requirements for deployment in refinery and process-industry emergency response applications.</jats:p>

title: Digital Revolution in Coiled Tubing Operations: Pioneering a Remote Operations Center Framework that Redefines Intervention Efficiency, Asset Reliability, and Sustainability Across a Large-Scale CT Fleet
container-title: ADIPEC
41f76fd9cd9c133d5eddd6c981bdc5b9dc53e0c1.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Coiled tubing (CT) interventions have traditionally required significant field presence, intensive personnel deployment, and reactive decision-making. A Remote Operations Center (ROC) framework, integrating real-time asset health monitoring, live operational parameter surveillance, and remote expert engagement, fundamentally challenges this model. Deployed across a long fleet of CT units and validated in more than 100 jobs, this framework redefines how interventions are monitored, managed, and optimized by reducing well-site personnel dependency.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>The framework operates through two integrated digital layers and three synchronized pillars. An asset health and monitoring platform delivers real-time visibility across injector head performance, pressure control equipment supply pressures, hydraulic readings, engine diagnostics, maintenance status, and operational parameters for each CT unit. A remote screen access and communication interface enables live data viewing, direct supervisor engagement, and real-time technical intervention without physical presence. Three pillars govern execution: a Field Team responsible for on-location job execution, a ROC Team providing live monitoring, engineering oversight, and technical decision support, and a Reliability Team managing equipment anomaly detection, alarm generation, and notification workflows.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>Deployed across a fully digitalized fleet of CT units, the ROC framework consistently demonstrated its ability to detect and resolve critical deviations before escalation—including job design, treatment execution, equipment performance, tubing force verification, injector head chain behavior, and BOP supply conditions—interventions that conventional field-only execution models would have missed or delayed.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>Operational efficiency increased by 80% year-on-year. Pipe failures were eliminated entirely in the first full deployment year. CT pipe life extension reached 39% in underbalanced operations and 78% in conventional operations, delivering combined maintenance savings exceeding 20% of the annual cost in supplies. Injector head chain twist incidents dropped 64% year-on-year. Sustainability outcomes proved equally transformative: diesel consumption fell 45% year-on-year, saving over 2.6 million liters, with reductions of 27 metric tons CO2e in Scope 1 and 545 metric tons CO2e in Scope 3 emissions. These combined results establish remote operations not as a support function, but as a core enabler of safer, smarter, and more sustainable coiled tubing intervention delivery.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>Remote monitoring concepts exist broadly across oil and gas, yet a purpose-built ROC governing an entire CT fleet through integrated asset health surveillance, live parameter monitoring, and synchronized three-pillar expert engagement represents a step change in how coiled tubing interventions are managed. This framework establishes a new operational benchmark for the industry, offering a scalable and replicable blueprint to elevate CT intervention performance, asset reliability, and sustainability through structured digital transformation</jats:p>

title: Comprehensive Monitoring of a Macro Grid Through Digital Tools in a Secondary Recovery Process
container-title: ADIPEC
d13cd9f9dc85cdac40992acf99233a36ee43d86c.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>After more than 40 years of production, Field A faced reservoir energy depletion in Reservoir B, as evidenced by declining pressure and low recovery. This work addresses the implementation of secondary recovery through water injection, based on a large-scale grid of horizontal producer and injector wells. The objective is to increase ultimate recovery and sweep efficiency, focusing on the evolution of the strategy, the monitoring of injection distribution, and well performance from 2017 to 2026.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>The methodology combined workover and strategic conversion of wells, drilling of new horizontal producers and injectors, and the implementation of a multiscale monitoring system for the Macro-grid (field, sector, pattern, well, flow unit) that evaluates pressures, production, and incremental oil. Dynamic simulation models and advanced digital analytical tools were employed, calibrated with real data and comparative analysis of pressure and production before and after water injection. Flow unit correlations and pattern adjustments allowed for optimized efficiency considering the heterogeneity and dynamic behavior of the reservoir.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>The original reservoir pressure (3,600 psi) decreased to approximately 900 to 1,100 psi before injection, very close to the bubble point pressure (874.7 psi). Upon implementation of the project, the current average pressure increased to 1,524 psi in the optimized areas. Between January 2017 and April 2026, 12 injection wells and 37 active producers were completed in the B sandstone. The average daily injection rate in April 2026 was 57,395 BWIPD, generating an average production increase of 10,506 BOPD associated with secondary recovery, with a total fluid production of 47,445 BFPD. The incremental reserves by waterflooding developed at December 2025 are estimated at 27.64 MMSTB. The response time was short (1–3 months), with water breakthrough occurring 90–180 days after each injection, and the voidage replacement ratio is 1.1. Continuous monitoring has allowed for pattern adjustments and maximized sweep efficiency, keeping field production above 18,000 BOPD even with increasing water cut, and maintaining it above the bubble point pressure.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>This work introduces an innovative methodology for the monitoring and optimization of secondary recovery in mature fields, integrating a macro-grid composed of multiple injection patterns and horizontal wells, along with multiscale monitoring systems and advanced digital tools. Unlike traditional approaches based on simple injection patterns, this strategy enables adaptive, continuous control tailored to real reservoir complexity. It demonstrates not only the technical effectiveness of secondary recovery through water injection, but also continuous optimization based on data and analytical/dynamic simulation, highlighting an adaptable approach to maximize reserves and efficiency.</jats:p>

title: Integrated Flare Energy Reduction and Emissions Mitigation at Oman LNG: Low-Capital Operational and Digital Solutions
container-title: ADIPEC
56aba0650cb8375e1d092dfc54a624378fb7b647.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Liquefied natural gas (LNG) facilities are under increasing pressure to lower greenhouse gas emissions while preserving the safety margins required for continuous, high-reliability operation. Flaring will remain necessary for process protection during abnormal or emergency conditions; however, routine or avoidable flaring represents lost hydrocarbon value, unnecessary fuel consumption, and additional carbon emissions. Within the Oman LNG complex, flare management was therefore treated not as a single environmental project, but as an operating discipline linked to energy efficiency, production planning, marine coordination, and Oman LNG's broader Net Zero Emissions roadmap.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>This paper describes an integrated flare energy-reduction program built around practical changes that could be implemented with existing assets and internal technical capability. Implemented or operationally established initiatives include fuel-gas-to-nitrogen flare purge optimization, comprehensive flare quantification, nitrogen monitoring and consumption, warm ship handling improvements, and Cold Gas Recovery. The Direct Cooldown Method is presented as a trial-demonstrated concept with optimization ongoing.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>Engineering calculations based on restriction-orifice design flows estimated that substitution of continuous fuel-gas flare purging with nitrogen reduced fuel-gas consumption by approximately 7.05 t/d, equivalent to more than 2,500 t/year of avoided hydrocarbon consumption. Digital quantification improved identification of individual flare contributors, event duration, cause classification and emissions reporting. Warm ship handling improvements delivered an observed operational result: zero cooldown-related flare events in 2022 and 2023 despite 20 cooldown activities in 2023 compared with 17 in 2019.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>The Direct Cooldown Method eliminated the conventional gas-up stage, corresponding to approximately 12,000 MMBtu of avoided gas-up energy and a calculated gross emissions-reduction potential of approximately 793 tCO2e per applicable operation. The trial also identified an important limitation: elevated nitrogen concentration in the ship vapor return prevented the intended fuel-gas-system recycling and resulted in approximately 500 t of flaring. Further optimization is therefore required before the gross emissions-reduction potential can be considered a net achieved benefit. Cold Gas Recovery has been completed and implemented, with an estimated annual reduction potential of approximately 3,303 tCO2e/year based on the recovery of shutdown-related cold gas through the BOG/fuel-gas system. Overall, the case study shows that low-capital engineering, operational and digital interventions can materially reduce routine and avoidable flaring while preserving the safety function and availability of the flare system.</jats:p>

title: Adaptive Criticality-Based Maintenance (ABC): A Dynamic Strategy Fit-For-Remaining Life Offshore Platform
container-title: ADIPEC
6bd955883a29c23b655c4f685b7fed9449425718.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Late-life offshore assets face escalating challenges in sustaining reliability under declining production, evolving risk profiles, and increasingly constrained logistics. Traditional time-based maintenance, although effective during peak-production years, frequently drives inefficient resource allocation and unnecessary interventions that are misaligned with an asset's actual value or remaining economic life.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>This paper presents an Adaptive Criticality-Based Maintenance (ABC) framework applied to more than 200 offshore wellhead platforms (WHPs) in the Gulf of Thailand. The approach dynamically aligns maintenance and inspection strategies with production potential, remaining life, risk exposure, and offshore logistics constraints across multiple asset types of production, hub, and water injection facilities and a broad equipment population spanning mechanical systems, cranes, booster compressors, electrical and instrumentation (E&I) systems, pressure vessel, piping and safety-critical equipment (SCE).</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>The ABC framework integrates production forecasting, risk-based analysis, and equipment criticality into a unified decision model. Platforms are categorized using Field Development Plan (FDP) data into three tiers "No" production (&lt; P1 MMSCFD), "Low" production (P1–P2 MMSCFD), and "High" production (&gt;P2 MMSCFD) providing a value-based basis for prioritization.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>Criticality is assessed on safety impact, production consequence, and failure likelihood, consistent with As Low as Reasonably Practicable (ALARP) principles, and strategies are optimized through a blend of preventive maintenance (PM), condition-based maintenance (CBM), and risk-based inspection (RBI).</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>Implementation proceeded through cross-functional workshops, structured stakeholder engagement, and integration into the Computerized Maintenance Management System (CMMS), establishing a closed-loop link between planning, risk assessment, and execution.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>The portfolio was classified into high-production (14%), low-production (51%), and no-production (11%) WHPs, enabling differentiated strategies. The optimization reduced logistics demand including a decrease in the active crew-boat vessel fleet 10% while lowering maintenance workload and offshore personnel exposure through the elimination of low-value activities.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>CBM principles were extended to crane and booster compressor components alongside continued inspection optimization. By mid of 2026, the year end 2026 forecast compares with the 2025 baseline show 13% reduction in Maintenance and Inspection (M&I) cost per platform across the combined preventive, corrective, and modification workload. Collectively, these results demonstrate improved resource efficiency, operational flexibility, and cost-effectiveness while preserving asset integrity, offering a scalable and replicable model for "fit-for-remaining-life" management of mature offshore assets.</jats:p>

title: Lightweight Digital Twin Fabric: Scaling Asset Intelligence via Progressive Fidelity and Reduced-Order Intelligence
container-title: ADIPEC
7f51899ef5bbc9f1801580afe67bc6db3aa9d8f8.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Objectives/Scope</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Despite significant capital investment, industrial digital twin initiatives frequently fail to scale across large brownfield portfolios due to unsustainable modeling costs and lifecycle overhead. This paper introduces the Lightweight Digital Twin Fabric(LwDT-Fabric)—a decision-centric architecture that decouples actionable insight from full-physics model dependency. By prioritizing decision relevance over exhaustive fidelity, the framework enables enterprise-scale deployment aligned with ISO 55000 and API 580/581. The objective is a "Right-Sized" digital transformation delivering maximum asset integrity with minimum computational and human overhead.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods, Procedures, Process</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The LwDT-Fabric utilizes a progressive, event-driven architecture built on open-standard schemas, including CFIHOS and ISO 15926, to ensure cross-platform interoperability and long-term data sustainability.
