Perioperative Digital Glycaemic Management in Gastrointestinal Surgery
container-title: The International Journal of Medical Robotics and Computer Assisted Surgery
bcb8895f8f9bd751dcf4a1c2152a3a0bb1d818ea.abstract: ABSTRACT Background Perioperative dysglycemia in gastrointestinal surgery is driven by fasting, surgical stress, inflammation, medications, nutritional transitions, and enhanced recovery pathways. Conventional glycaemic management based on intermittent testing and reactive insulin adjustment may not adequately capture these rapid metabolic changes. Methods Recent guidelines, expert consensus statements, randomized trials, systematic reviews, and implementation studies addressing perioperative digital glycaemic management were narratively reviewed. Results Perioperative digital glycaemic management can be conceptualised as a workflow‐integrated control loop that encompasses glucose sensing, contextual clinical data analysis, algorithm‐assisted interpretation, insulin‐nutrition coordination, and multidisciplinary governance. Emerging technologies, including continuous glucose monitoring (CGM), electronic health record (EHR)‐based alerts, and closed‐loop insulin systems, may improve the continuity and responsiveness of perioperative metabolic care. Conclusions Digital glycaemic pathways offer a more adaptive approach to perioperative management in gastrointestinal surgery. Future studies should determine whether these strategies improve clinically meaningful surgical outcomes beyond glucose metrics alone.

title: Consumer Consciousness
42ce2e4239a5bb821fcadb9bc56901f624ec30b5.abstract: Abstract This book aims to introduce a new approach to understanding the consumer—as a conscioumer—by redefining the role of the consumer in today’s experience-driven context. It situates the consumer not simply as a purchaser but as a conscious experiencer whose sensory reality is reshaped by emerging technologies. Focusing on the evolving relationship between sensory perception and consciousness, the work highlights how multisensory experiences and technological integration are transforming consumer awareness into a new form of digital consciousness. By exploring how technologies such as artificial intelligence, augmented reality, and multisensory interfaces alter the sensory input that shapes conscious experience, the book questions the implications of this shift for consumer well-being and broader societal outcomes. It argues that conscious awareness is essential to understanding modern consumption beyond automatic or habitual behaviour, emphasizing the importance of reflective engagement with experience. Ultimately, the book challenges traditional consumer models by proposing that consciousness—shaped by the senses and technology—is central to how consumers make meaning and decisions today. It invites further reflection on the ethical, social, and environmental impacts of this new digital consumer consciousness, advocating for practices that promote well-being and responsibility within the rapidly changing landscape of consumption.

title: DIGITAL LABOUR AND EPISTEMIC ERASURE: A SEMIOTIC ANALYSIS OF INDIGENOUS KNOWLEDGE AND AI INFRASTRUCTURES IN HUMANS IN THE LOOP
container-title: Interdisciplinary Perspectives of Education
f3d3fff8613295115b19afeda98d7e4193beb31e.abstract: This paper explores how artificial intelligence (AI) and digital labour affect marginalised identities, using the 2025 Netflix film Humans in the Loop (directed by Aranya Sahay). Research follows the female protagonist of the film, named Nehma, an Indigenous (Adivasi) woman who works as a data labeller. Her deep, traditional knowledge about nature is ignored because of the way AI categorisation systems use a rigid, one-size-fits-all sorting method and act as epistemic hierarchies that erase Indigenous ways of living and thinking. Using a social semiotic approach, the research identifies a disconnection between local ecological knowledge and the rigid binary logic of machine-learning infrastructures. The article argues that digital frameworks mirror power dynamics inside educational institutions, where underrepresented students often have their cultural identity and cultural expressions erased or misrepresented. By analysing the lived experiences of marginalised communities, the study critiques techno-solutionist solutions and proposes solutions grounded in epistemic justice, cultural agency and equity and recommends that equitable AI systems require moving away from extractive labour practices to recognise the intellectual and cultural contributions of the Global South.

title: FROM DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION TO AI-ENABLED EDUCATION: A CRITICAL REVIEW OF EMERGING TRENDS, OPPORTUNITIES, AND CHALLENGES
container-title: Interdisciplinary Perspectives of Education
a30e8b5e4e056b3879ef048a09f681d3adc86be6.abstract: The higher education sector has seen the emergence of several technological advancements over the past two decades. These include learning management systems, massive open online courses, and the latest on the market: Generative Artificial Intelligence (AI). This paper aims to make a critical review of the shift from Digital Transformation to AI-driven education as a whole. The paper particularly emphasizes the shift of the digital transformation from being an administrative phenomenon to being more of a central feature in education. The paper summarises the literature on the concepts of digital transformation, the implementation of generative AI, and adaptive learning and AI ethics in the teaching and learning process, based on peer-reviewed papers that were mainly published in Scopus and Web of Science from 2019 to 2026. There are three themes that are repeated in the literature. First, AI in education is a further step towards digital transformation in which capacity building processes are substituted with independent decision making. Second, personalisation, accessibility and efficiency are opportunities, not equally accessible or equally taken up, nor equally realised; and these opportunities go first to the best resourced institutions.

title: SOCRATIVE-BASED DIGITAL FORMATIVE ASSESSMENT WITH IMMEDIATE FEEDBACK AND LEARNING ENGAGEMENT AMONG B.ED. STUDENTS: A MIXED-METHOD STUDY
container-title: Interdisciplinary Perspectives of Education
df42f8954c29f112df7e7a3a03dc036cfc2bbb32.abstract: Digital formative assessment provides opportunities for teachers to obtain information about students' learning during instruction and to respond with timely feedback. This mixed-method classroom study examined changes in learning-engagement and feedback-related perceptions and formative-assessment knowledge among B.Ed. students following the use of Socrative-based digital formative assessment with immediate feedback. The study employed a one-group pretest-posttest design involving 46 B.Ed. students enrolled in an Assessment for Learning course. Two Socrative-based assessment sessions were conducted during the intervention period. Each session contained 10 questions, and approximately 15 minutes were provided for completion. Students accessed the activities using mobile phones. Socrative supplied immediate information about correct and incorrect responses, after which the teacher provided explanations and clarification of misconceptions. Quantitative data were collected through pretest and posttest responses while Qualitative data was obtained from open-ended responses and classroom observations. The Likert scale consists of eight items showed high internal consistency at both administrations (pretest α = .924; posttest α = .933). Among the 45 students who completed both test. Learning-engagement and feedback-related scores increased from M = 32.73 (SD = 6.36) at pretest to M = 33.54 (SD = 5.90) at posttest. However, this difference was not statistically significant, t (44) = 0.91, p = .367, d = .14. Formative-assessment knowledge scores also showed a small increase, from M = 2.30 (SD = 0.96) to M = 2.46 (SD = 0.98), with no statistically significant difference, t (45) = −0.87, p = .391, d = .13. Qualitative findings shows that students were perceived feedback was very useful for identifying their strengths and weaknesses, understanding mistakes and planning for further steps and strategies to improve their learning. Classroom observations further indicated that the learner has interest in the digital formative assessment format and appreciated the information about whether their response is correct or incorrect. The results reveal that Socrative was feasible for conducting formative assessment in the classroom. The short period of intervention, absence of a comparison group, one-institution sample, and limited platform data makes it difficult to interpret data normally.

title: BIM–digital twin integration for construction safety: Mechanisms, maturity pathways, and socio-technical progression
container-title: Journal of Information Technology in Construction
b650139a647d3fa0043c741b3798d65a029ce8d3.abstract: The construction industry continues to experience high rates of serious injury and fatality worldwide, motivating an increasing interest in advanced digitalization strategies that combine building information modeling (BIM) with digital twin (DT) capabilities. By linking static semantic site models with continuous field data, these systems offer a powerful approach to proactive risk management. However, while individual remote sensing and predictive analytics components are well researched, a unified understanding of how these BIM and DT safety systems are integrated remains critically limited. Specifically, there is a clear need to understand how system capabilities evolve across different maturity stages and what underlying factors drive this progression across the construction lifecycle. This paper presents a comprehensive scoping review of BIM and DT integration for construction safety management across the entire project lifecycle. Using a tiered evidence strategy and structured thematic coding, the existing literature is synthesized through three main analytical lenses: integration mechanisms and data exchange patterns, maturity characteristics and capability horizons, and the socio-technical factors that systematically influence maturity transitions. This review clarifies the dominant architectural integration approaches and maps current proof-of-concept efforts against the requirements for more predictive and governance-ready safety twins. The findings indicate that most implementations remain at the interactive monitoring stage, with predictive capability emerging mainly in data-rich contexts and autonomous adaptation not yet realized. Furthermore, it identifies persistent bottlenecks in data interoperability and real-time processing that currently hinder widespread industry adoption. Finally, the study proposes a focused research agenda designed to help transition these intelligent monitoring systems from isolated prototypes to robust, scalable applications suitable for safety-critical construction environments.

title: Evaluating the Use of Digital Technology Tools by Instructors at Veritas University Abuja for Instruction and Learning
container-title: RESEARCH JOURNAL OF MASS COMMUNICATION AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY
6c8964bba5fe22443fe1b0e59d6d271082000c3f.abstract: The study looked into how instructors at Veritas University Abuja used both traditional and digital pedagogical approaches and methods in their teaching and learning. The primary goal was to determine the number of university arts and social science faculties that have embraced the use of digital technologies for lecturers' classroom instruction and learning, as well as whether or not this use of technology is properly documented. A descriptive survey was the approach taken. 240 instructors from 12 faculties at Veritas University in Abuja were selected at random using a standardized questionnaire. According to the study's findings, only the education faculty has successfully embraced the use of technology in the teaching-learning process; the other faculty members have not yet done so because of a number of issues, including erratic power supplies and poor internet connectivity, among others. Based on the results, it was suggested that the university administration supply sufficient digital technology equipment for teaching and learning in order to improve the proper use of digital technology for university instruction.

title: ANALISIS PENGARUH KEPERCAYAAN TERHADAP PENINGKATAN KEPUTUSAN PRODUK HALAL BERBASIS DIGITAL TRACEABILITY
container-title: Jurnal Manajemen dan Bisnis
b22850b9ebfb460e756568045a8ec2a0d7e3d5c7.abstract: Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis pengaruh digital traceability dan kepercayaan konsumen terhadap keputusan pembelian produk halal. Digital traceability memungkinkan konsumen menelusuri asal bahan baku, proses produksi, dan status sertifikasi halal suatu produk melalui platform digital. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif dengan metode survei terhadap 30 konsumen Muslim di Pekalongan yang pernah menggunakan fitur pelacakan digital, seperti memindai kode QR pada kemasan produk halal. Data dianalisis dengan regresi linear berganda menggunakan EViews. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa digital traceability (t = 1,322; p = 0,197) dan kepercayaan konsumen (t = −0,111; p = 0,911) tidak berpengaruh signifikan terhadap keputusan pembelian, baik secara parsial maupun simultan (p = 0,132), dengan R² sebesar 0,13. Reliabilitas instrumen tergolong rendah (Cronbach’s Alpha 0,419–0,592), sehingga temuan ini bersifat eksploratif dan perlu ditafsirkan secara hati-hati. Hasil ini mengindikasikan bahwa konsumen masih lebih mengandalkan label halal resmi dan reputasi merek daripada informasi pelacakan digital.

title: Artificial Intelligence and Digital Innovation in Smart Tourism Destination Management: An Integrative Review and the AI-SDM Framework
container-title: Inkubis : Jurnal Ekonomi dan Bisnis
b9b2afe723164bea6e7be350837363abda6c2fe3.abstract: Background: Artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming tourism destinations through personalized services, conversational and generative interfaces, predictive analytics, and data-driven decision-making. Yet technology adoption alone does not explain how destinations convert AI-generated information into coordinated managerial action. Objective: This study addresses that organizational problem through a conceptual integrative review of research on AI-enabled tourism services, smart destination management, destination governance, visitor experience, organizational capabilities, workforce readiness, and responsible data practices. Methods: The synthesis identifies four interconnected application domains: AI-driven personalization, conversational and generative visitor interaction, predictive visitor-flow analytics, and data-driven destination governance. These domains are abstracted into the AI-Enabled Smart Destination Management (AI-SDM) framework, which connects AI-Enabled Service Capability, Smart Destination Governance Capability, and Visitor Experience Outcomes. Results: Visitor and operational intelligence functions as the principal conversion input, while visitor-generated behavioral and experiential feedback supports subsequent organizational learning and AI adaptation. Workforce AI Readiness and Responsible Data Governance are positioned as enabling conditions. The framework contributes to destination-management theory by shifting attention from AI adoption toward the organizational capability required to sense relevant visitor information, interpret and coordinate responses, and responsibly convert intelligence into destination action and visitor value. It complements broad smart-tourism and emerging cognitive-destination architectures by specifying the organizational intelligence-to-action mechanism that links AI-enabled interactions with destination governance and learning. Conclusion: The paper concludes with propositions and an empirical research agenda for measurement development and validation.

title: INTEGRASI NILAI PEDULI LINGKUNGAN DALAM E-MODUL IPAS: PENGEMBANGAN BAHAN AJAR DIGITAL BAGI SISWA SEKOLAH DASAR
container-title: LEARNING : Jurnal Inovasi Penelitian Pendidikan dan Pembelajaran
e35bcc4c1c956632065dbdec372918143bb619d3.abstract: IPAS learning in primary schools requires teaching materials that are engaging, easy to understand, and can support the formation of students’ character, especially an environmentally caring character. This research focuses on the development of an IPAS learning e-module oriented toward environmental care character values for fourth-grade elementary school students. This research aims to produce an e-module that is valid and practical for use in the learning process. The method used is research and development (Research and Development) with the ADDIE model, which consists of five stages: Analysis, Design, Development, Implementation, and Evaluation. The product developed is an e-module on the topic “My Role in the School and Community Environment,” which includes materials, learning activities, images or illustrations, exercises, evaluations, and activities that incorporate environmental care character values. The research subjects were 27 fourth-grade students from SDN 4 Labuhan Haji. Data collection was carried out using validation sheets from display experts, material experts, language experts, student response questionnaires, and practicality questionnaires, and then analyzed descriptively quantitatively. The research results showed that the e-module received a validation percentage of 93% from display experts, 93% from material experts, and 82.66% from language experts, all of which fall into the very good category. Student responses received a percentage of 87.04% in the very good category, while the practicality results reached 89.87%. Thus, the IPAS learning e-module oriented toward environmental care character values is declared valid, practical, and suitable to be used as an alternative teaching material in IPAS learning at elementary schools. ABSTRAK Pembelajaran IPAS di sekolah dasar membutuhkan bahan ajar yang menarik, mudah dipahami, serta dapat mendukung pembentukan karakter siswa, khususnya karakter peduli lingkungan. Penelitian ini berfokus pada pengembangan e-modul pembelajaran IPAS berorientasi nilai-nilai karakter peduli lingkungan untuk siswa kelas IV sekolah dasar. Penelitian ini bertujuan menghasilkan e-modul yang valid dan praktis, digunakan dalam proses pembelajaran. Metode yang digunakan adalah penelitian dan pengembangan (Research and Development) dengan model ADDIE yang terdiri atas lima tahap, yaitu Analysis, Design, Development, Implementation, dan Evaluation. Produk yang dikembangkan berupa e-modul pada materi “Peranku di Lingkungan Sekolah dan Masyarakat”, yang dilengkapi materi, kegiatan pembelajaran, gambar atau ilustrasi, latihan, evaluasi, serta aktivitas yang memuat nilai-nilai karakter peduli lingkungan. Pengumpulan data dilakukan menggunakan lembar validasi ahli tampilan, ahli materi, ahli bahasa, angket respons siswa, dan angket kepraktisan, kemudian dianalisis secara deskriptif kuantitatif. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa e-modul memperoleh persentase validasi ahli tampilan sebesar 93%, ahli materi sebesar 93%, dan ahli bahasa sebesar 82,66%, yang termasuk kategori sangat baik. Respons siswa memperoleh persentase 87,04% dengan kategori sangat baik, sedangkan hasil kepraktisan mencapai 89,87%. Dengan demikian, e-modul pembelajaran IPAS berorientasi nilai-nilai karakter peduli lingkungan dinyatakan valid, praktis, dan layak digunakan sebagai salah satu alternatif bahan ajar dalam pembelajaran IPAS di sekolah dasar.

title: Digital Health Literacy in Adults With Heart Failure: Cross-Sectional Study
container-title: Nursing Research
f8afae3f115c44d5a8c05d4ac7911fd2cd38076c.abstract: Background: Digital technology is increasingly used in heart failure (HF) management. Deficiencies in digital health literacy (DHL) may hinder the delivery of digitally mediated nursing care. Investigating sociodemographic and clinical factors associated with DHL in middle-income countries could inform targeted interventions to reduce disparities in HF management. Objective: To examine associations between DHL and sociodemographic and clinical factors in adults with HF. Methods: Descriptive, cross-sectional, and correlational study. The sample consisted of adult outpatients with HF from a cardiology clinic in João Pessoa, Brazil. Individuals with a clinical diagnosis of HF confirmed in the medical record, regardless of left ventricular ejection fraction, aged ≥18 years, were included. We obtained sociodemographic and clinical data through self-report. We assessed DHL using the eHealth Literacy Scale . We examined associations between sociodemographic and clinical variables and the digital literacy score using the Mann–Whitney or Kruskal–Wallis test and Spearman’s correlation. Results: The study included 109 participants (mean age, 59.1 years; 60% female). DHL was predominantly low. Age, education, and number of comorbidities were significantly associated with DHL. Discussion: Age, education, and comorbidity burden may affect patients’ ability to engage with digital technologies used in HF management in middle-income countries. Supporting patients’ technological competencies may expand opportunities for digitally mediated caring relationships, enabling nurses to better understand and support individuals with HF in increasingly digital health care environments.

title: Cognitive and Computational Mechanisms of Multi-Agent Task Allocation in Digital Environments
container-title: Zamonaviy dunyoda ilm-fan va texnologiya, Vol. 5, No. 32 (2026)
88311ab5879695c66cef064bee8f1ffe9c71873e.abstract: Digital environments transform multi-agent task allocation in terms of computational load, utility optimization, and allocation of attention. Based on distributed systems theory and reinforcement learning, this study will combine empirical evidence in artificial intelligence, software engineering, and information systems studies to determine the impact of digital stimuli (prompt complexity, resource constraints, and algorithmic task routing) on agent cognition and neural-inspired valuation processes. The paper constructs a conceptual Multi-Agent Task Allocation Model (MATAM) based on bounded rationality and multi-agent reinforcement learning theories using secondary data synthesis. The effects of computational overload, the activation of reward circuitry, and dynamic personalization in multi-agent environments are summarized in three integrative tables of documented empirical evidence. The results indicate that online agent frameworks reinforce decentralized processing, reward optimization, and dynamically restructure preference formation. The paper enriches software engineering theory because it incorporates computational and cognitive-inspired processes in adaptive multi-agent systems.

title: Happiness in Action (Hia): From Conceptual Framework to Systemic Wellbeing Practice
01b3b91840b60715dae9d8af7122dd5591a41760.abstract: Abstract The theoretical analysis conducted in this study indicates that existing models of subjective well-being remain largely fragmented and do not fully capture the dynamic interplay between an individual’s internal psychological state, external socio-environmental conditions, and purposeful activity through which well-being is developed and sustained over time. The study proposes a systems-based approach to subjective well-being, conceptualising happiness as a dynamic outcome of the continuous interaction between an individual’s internal state, socio-environmental context, and purposeful activity. Based on the findings, a two-component structure of subjective well-being was proposed, comprising internal harmony and external harmony, operationalised through 14 interrelated components. The analysis also identified a phenomenon of “selective perception”, whereby individuals tend to attach greater importance to those well-being factors they perceive as most personally relevant, while paying comparatively less attention to other important components. These findings suggest that educational approaches aimed at developing a more holistic understanding of well-being and increasing awareness of the interrelationships among its components may help reduce this effect. The findings further indicate the potential importance of combining long-term goals related to meaning and personal values with short-term positive emotional states in the development and maintenance of sustainable well-being. Drawing on the theoretical and empirical findings, the Happiness in Action (HIA) model was developed based on a two-component structure of subjective well-being. A distinctive feature of HIA is the Value Flow mechanism, conceptualised as a process through which individuals systematically assess their current state, identify priority areas for development, and undertake purposeful actions. This approach enables well-being to be understood as an evolving process rather than solely as a collection of discrete states or determinants. Importantly, the HIA model may support the identification of needs, the establishment of priorities, and the development of systematic approaches to maintaining and enhancing well-being at both individual and collective levels.

title: Entropy-Guided Adaptive Confidence-Weighted Complementary Deep Ensemble for osteopenia and osteoporosis classification from knee radiographs
container-title: Scientific Reports
5b51cdbd79e70c4abda21fb49fdbf403bf61fb13.abstract: Abstract Automated osteoporosis assessment from knee radiographs remains a challenging computer-aided diagnosis task due to subtle structural differences among normal, osteopenic, and osteoporotic bone patterns, together with the limited availability of transparent and reproducible evaluation frameworks based on publicly accessible datasets. Existing studies predominantly rely on standalone deep learning models or conventional ensemble methods that assume fixed classifier reliability and rarely incorporate predictive uncertainty into decision-level fusion. To address this limitation, this study proposes an Entropy-Guided Adaptive Confidence-Weighted Complementary Deep Ensemble (E-ACW Ensemble) for uncertainty-aware osteoporosis-related knee radiograph classification in both binary and multi-class settings. The proposed framework integrates standardized radiographic preprocessing, fold-specific data augmentation, complementary deep feature learning, and an entropy-guided adaptive fusion strategy. Predictive uncertainty is estimated using Shannon entropy to enable sample-specific confidence weighting during decision-level fusion. The framework was evaluated on publicly available knee radiograph datasets using a rigorous five-fold stratified cross-validation protocol. Comprehensive experimental evaluation, including comparative benchmarking, ablation studies, fold-wise stability analysis, statistical significance testing, and computational efficiency assessment, was conducted to validate predictive performance, robustness, and reproducibility. Among the investigated configurations, the proposed EfficientNetB0 + MobileNetV2 + E-ACW Ensemble achieved the best overall performance, reaching 99.2% accuracy and 99.1% F1-score for binary classification and 98.7% accuracy and 98.5% F1-score for multi-class classification while requiring substantially lower computational cost than the corresponding high-capacity ensemble. These findings demonstrate that entropy-guided adaptive confidence weighting provides an effective and computationally efficient decision-level fusion strategy for osteoporosis-related knee radiograph classification. The proposed E-ACW Ensemble establishes a reproducible framework that can be readily extended to future computer-aided musculoskeletal image analysis and uncertainty-aware medical imaging applications.

title: A systematic review of research issues with Levels of Automation (LOA)
container-title: Journal of Digital Educational Technology
a19171cb1916c18b47d40caf7cd9d48b59ad2e38.abstract: This systematic review critically analyzes the contexts and challenges of Levels of Automation (LOA), particularly in light of advancements by Artificial Intelligence (AI). Human–automation interaction (HAI) seeks to understand how humans interact with automated systems, particularly as increasing automation places operators increasingly out of the loop. A foundational framework within this field is the Levels of Automation (LOA) framework, which characterizes the respective roles and capabilities of human operators and automated systems. As AI becomes increasingly integrated into traditional HAI applications, a renewed examination of the current state of LOA is warranted. This systematic review examines the following research question: What research demographics, contexts, and challenges associated with LOA are reported in the literature? Data analysis, extraction, and open and axial coding were employed, and consensus was reached by iterative discussion between the authors. The review ultimately included 118 studies. The review identified six contextual categories and 26 challenge codes. The findings provide a comprehensive analysis of the evolving landscape of human–automation interaction. The contribution of this work is to outline weaknesses embedded in research with LOA and suggest a reform with prospects of enhanced HAI with AI.

title: Digital Microfluidic System with Dual Half-Moon Electrodes
container-title: Applied Sciences
922bbf12cc649307de840b243f405a3e32d1d79a.abstract: With the rapid advancement of digital microfluidic technology, this study presents the design and fabrication of a PCB-based digital microfluidic system aimed at reducing chip driving voltage and manufacturing costs while enhancing droplet manipulation performance. The system integrates peripheral modules to establish a complete digital microfluidic platform. A novel double half-moon serrated electrode is proposed, which provides enhanced droplet driving force and enables multidirectional droplet movement through flexible electrode arrangement. Three electrode configurations with different scaling parameters were designed and experimentally evaluated. The results demonstrate that the electrode with a scaling parameter of A = 1 exhibits the best driving performance. At an applied voltage of 120 V, the average droplet velocities in the transverse and longitudinal directions reached 1.18 mm/s and 0.98 mm/s, respectively, while at 200 V they increased to 2.57 mm/s and 1.88 mm/s. Compared with conventional rectangular and serrated electrodes, the proposed electrode structure effectively improves droplet driving capability. This work provides a low-cost and high-performance solution for the development of portable and integrated digital microfluidic systems.

title: Identification of Fracture-Related Acoustic Emission Signals in Mine-Site Monitoring Using Multi-Domain Features and a 1D-CNN with Local-Window Self-Attention
container-title: Applied Sciences
468361152740737b2ff83a8a56ab244e2affbe33.abstract: Acoustic emission (AE) monitoring captures transient elastic waves generated by rock fracturing. Reliable identification of fracture-related AE signals supports rock-mass damage monitoring and subsequent early-warning analysis of mining-induced geohazards. However, AE signals are often corrupted by operational noise, hindering accurate detection. To improve AE signal identification under complex field conditions, raw binary AE data from a mine site were parsed, segmented, and manually labeled, and a binary dataset of fracture-related AE signals and industrial noise was constructed. Seven time-domain statistical features and three frequency-band energy-ratio features were extracted from each segment and combined into a 10-dimensional multi-domain feature vector. A hybrid model integrating a 1D convolutional neural network (1D-CNN) with a local-window self-attention mechanism was developed. The proposed model was compared with eight models: a standalone 1D-CNN, a 1D-CNN with global self-attention, a BPNN, an SVM, logistic regression, k-nearest neighbors, random forest, and XGBoost. On an independent test set comprising 400 samples, the proposed model achieved mean accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score values of 96.75 ± 0.71%, 93.99 ± 1.20%, 99.90 ± 0.22%, and 96.85 ± 0.67%, respectively, across five repeated runs. It achieved the highest mean accuracy and F1-score among the nine models. Across five fixed feature permutations, recall remained stable, whereas precision, accuracy, and F1-score showed greater variation. These findings indicate the potential of the proposed model for front-end classification of fracture-related AE signals in mine-site monitoring.

title: Intelligent High-Resolution Marine Seismic Survey Using Machine Learning and Adaptive Acquisition Optimization
container-title: Applied Sciences
c58944d6ad93c9cbda6151d2e7eb79aa13c7dc23.abstract: Conventional high-resolution marine seismic surveys often face challenges in detecting small features in the shallow subsurface because acquisition parameters involve trade-offs among spatial resolution, penetration, signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), and operational efficiency. This study presents an intelligent marine seismic acquisition framework that integrates selectable acquisition hardware with modified ML Real domain adaptation, deep learning reconstruction, quantitative quality-control (QC) evaluation, and a human-supervised adaptive agent. Rather than directly predicting acquisition parameters with the neural network, the deep learning model reconstructs high-resolution seismic images from degraded acquisitions, which are subsequently evaluated using QC metrics including reflector continuity, spectral bandwidth, SNR, and depth penetration. The adaptive agent uses these metrics to rank discrete, hardware-feasible configurations of source type, source energy, dominant frequency, and shot interval and recommends the configuration for the subsequent acquisition cycle. Synthetic benchmark tests demonstrate improved imaging of thin layers and localized subsurface features under the tested conditions. A two-cycle nearshore field experiment further demonstrates the operational feasibility of the workflow, in which QC evaluation of the initial acquisition guided the subsequent acquisition configuration and resulted in improved reflector continuity, penetration, and SNR. The results show that integrating AI-assisted numerical modeling and evaluation can guide acquisition-parameter refinement and reduce reliance on repeated offshore trial-and-error surveys. The proposed framework provides a proof-of-concept for integrating configurable high-resolution seismic hardware with AI-assisted, QC-guided acquisition optimization for marine shallow-subsurface imaging.

title: Effects of Cognitive Behavioral Interventions on Core Symptom Dimensions of Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder in Children and Adolescents: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
container-title: Brain Sciences
6a8f61df667a2aec7602c5e57ab62b23c88523ba.abstract: Background: Previous research on psychosocial interventions for children and adolescents with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) has primarily focused on overall symptom severity, with less attention to treatment effects across core symptom dimensions. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the effects of cognitive behavioral interventions on overall ADHD symptoms, inattention, and hyperactivity/impulsivity and explored the influence of intervention type, treatment duration, and weekly session frequency. Methods: PubMed, Web of Science Core Collection, Embase, and CENTRAL were searched from inception to 30 June 2026 for randomized controlled trials. Risk of bias was assessed using RoB 2. Effect sizes were calculated as Hedges’ g and pooled using random-effects models, with sensitivity and exploratory subgroup analyses conducted. The review was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261376097). Results: Ten randomized controlled trials involving 849 participants were included. Cognitive behavioral interventions significantly reduced overall ADHD symptoms (g = −0.389, 95% CI −0.773 to −0.005), inattention (g = −0.415, 95% CI −0.749 to −0.082), and hyperactivity/impulsivity (g = −0.366, 95% CI −0.658 to −0.075). Inattention showed the numerically largest pooled effect. Exploratory subgroup analyses showed numerical differences across intervention type, treatment duration, and weekly session frequency, but formal moderator tests found no statistically significant between-subgroup differences. Conclusions: These findings support the potential benefits of cognitive behavioral interventions for ADHD symptom management, with the most consistent results observed for inattention. Future randomized controlled trials should compare intervention components and treatment schedules while assessing actual treatment exposure, including home practice, to inform more targeted cognitive behavioral interventions.

title: Omni-Flex GraphFormer: Parallel Fusion of Local Graph Aggregation and Global Attention Across Image Resolutions
container-title: Information
486564d19a14112ee291281e74085d1c8c166091.abstract: Graph neural networks (GNNs) capture local image structure with few parameters, whereas Vision Transformers (ViTs) model global context at a higher computational cost. We propose the Omni-Flex GraphFormer, which applies a graph branch (OMNIVIG: max-relative aggregation over a fixed 3×3 pixel neighbourhood) and a Transformer branch (FLEXIVIT: global multi-head self-attention) in parallel and sums their outputs. Because each baseline is the hybrid with one branch removed, comparing the three models on eight datasets from 8×8 to 96×96 pixels, under equal training budgets and over three seeds, is a controlled branch ablation. Global attention is decisive: the hybrid exceeds OMNIVIG in test macro-F1 on every dataset and in all 24 runs, by 3.7 to 15.1 points (Wilcoxon test, p=0.0078). Against FLEXIVIT, the hybrid has the best mean F1 on six datasets and a 40–62% smaller seed-to-seed spread on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100, but the difference is not significant (p=0.38). The graph branch adds only 0.5–3.1% to the number of multiply–accumulate operations, and under warmed-up timing, both models run at the same speed, whereas unwarmed timing overstates latency by up to 15×. Under Gaussian noise, the summed hybrid degrades like the graph branch, which motivates gated or attention-guiding fusion.

title: Endocrine Metabolic Crosstalk of Insect Growth Regulators: Mechanisms, Resistance, and Climate-Adaptive Pest Management
container-title: Insects
05b82c1d389356a35131d4f46771a9c475ff4729.abstract: Insect growth regulators (IGRs), including chitin synthesis inhibitors (CSIs), juvenile hormone analogues (JHAs), and ecdysteroid agonists, have become important components of sustainable pest management because they can selectively disrupt insect-specific developmental, endocrine, or structural processes that differ from those in vertebrates. Rather than treating all IGR classes as operating through one common pathway, this review proposes an integrative framework in which class-specific primary modes of action interact with endocrine regulation, metabolism, stress responses, and ecological context. Across the literature, IGR exposure is associated with changes in carbohydrate, lipid, and protein metabolism, altered detoxification and digestive enzyme activities, and changes in reproductive physiology that can reduce insect fitness. However, these metabolic responses vary substantially with compound class, species, developmental stage, dose, and exposure duration. Their occurrence does not by itself establish active resource reallocation, a common metabolic crisis, or a causal role in mortality. Endocrine–metabolic crosstalk is therefore considered here as a mechanistic framework and testable hypothesis rather than an established universal mechanism of IGR toxicity or resistance evolution. Field-evolved resistance to IGRs is mechanistically diverse and can involve target-site changes, altered detoxification, reduced penetration, transport processes, and regulatory mechanisms, with the strength of evidence varying among compounds and pest species from functionally supported mechanisms to candidate pathways. The review also evaluates integration of IGRs with conventional insecticides and biological control agents and examines how climate warming may alter pest phenology, developmental timing, and temperature-dependent IGR performance, while acknowledging that direct empirical evidence linking climate warming specifically to IGR endocrine or metabolic sensitivity remains limited. Future progress will require stronger functional validation of proposed endocrine–metabolic links, climate-informed deployment strategies, and resistance management based on validated mechanisms and multiple control tactics.

title: Digital Traffic and Guest Profile Analysis of a Rural Accommodation: An Exploratory Case Study from Győr–Moson–Sopron County
container-title: Sustainability
cf6a820585aa850dfbade5b737e4f99dec7037d1.abstract: The digital transformation of the tourism sector, coupled with the proliferation of automated data reporting systems, has rendered precise, data-driven guest analysis accessible even to small, rural lodging businesses. The present study examines visitor behaviour and consumer habits through an embedded case study in Győr–Moson–Sopron County. The objective of the research is to explore the demographic characteristics, the purpose of travel, and stay habits of rural tourism consumers, with a view to laying the groundwork for a more effective, segment-specific marketing strategy. The research also highlights aspects of sustainable tourism management and sustainable consumer behaviour. The methodological framework of the study was provided by primary data from the National Tourism Data Centre (NTAK) for the year 2025. The empirical research employed a quantitative, cross-sectional approach; the analysis was based on a sample of 250 valid cases, representing the total annual revenue of a small rural business. In the statistical analysis, descriptive methods, cross-tabulation, and the chi-square test were utilised. The findings underscore substantial intercorrelations among the indicators examined, with a pronounced correlation evident between guests’ gender and the purpose of their trip. Furthermore, a moderate correlation was identified between the guests’ purpose of travel and their length of stay, as well as between the guests’ region of origin and the purpose of their trip. In addition, a fourth hypothesis was subjected to testing using binary logistic regression, which revealed a highly significant predictive relationship between the age of guests, the purpose of their travel, and the length of their stay (1–2 vs. 3+ nights). Concurrently, cross-tabulation revealed that there was no association between trip purpose and weekend arrivals, thereby establishing a clear temporal distinction between weekday-dominated business trips and weekend-concentrated leisure visits. The study’s findings offer direct, practical guidance for the development of communication strategies tailored to specific target groups. These recommendations facilitate the optimisation of capacity utilisation and the enhancement of the competitiveness of rural accommodation providers in the digital market. In doing so, this paper provides a rigorous framework for analysing sustainable tourism outcomes from an operational and economic perspective. It also establishes methods through which data-driven segment management can be used to mitigate rural seasonality, maximise capacity optimisation, and strengthen local economic resilience. This can be achieved by securing steady tourism cash flow during the traditional business off-season.

title: Adaptive Deep Learning Model with Anatomical Priors for 3D Segmentation of Fine Hepatic Vasculature on CT
container-title: Radiology Advances
86467c6926c30e65e94b3c0b7ae02cc5507850a9.abstract: Abstract BACKGROUND Accurate segmentation of fine hepatic vessels on CT remains challenging because peripheral branches are small and low contrast. PURPOSE To develop and test PriM Fusion Net, a deep learning model that adaptively integrates an optimized anatomical prior to improve 3D CT segmentation of portal and hepatic veins, emphasizing fine peripheral branches for preoperative 3D modeling. MATERIALS AND METHODS This retrospective study used the public MSD Task08-HepaticVessel dataset of 303 abdominal CT volumes. PriM Fusion Net uses a dual-encoder architecture: a Swin Transformer processes CT images and a parallel convolutional pathway processes a dataset-optimized Frangi vesselness prior. Gated multimodal units act as spatially varying voxel-wise gates that fuse the two feature streams at multiple scales. A rule-based SimpleMind post-processing module refined anatomical plausibility. Performance was evaluated with five-fold cross-validation and zero-shot external inference on 3DIRCADb. RESULTS PriM Fusion Net achieved a mean Dice similarity coefficient (DSC) of 77.68% (95% confidence interval [CI]: 77.11, 78.25) and 95th percentile Hausdorff distance (HD95) of 11.55 mm (95% CI: 9.94, 13.16), outperforming all baselines (all adjusted P &lt; .02). For vessels with radius ≤ 1.5 mm, DSC improved by 13.5% versus SwinUNETR (59.2% [95% CI: 54.48, 63.92] vs 45.7% [95% CI: 40.49, 50.91]). In ablation, replacing rigid concatenation with gated fusion improved DSC from 75.86% [95% CI: 75.31, 76.41] to 77.65% [95% CI: 76.92, 78.38], and SimpleMind post-processing reduced HD95 from 14.98 mm [95% CI: 10.91, 19.05] to 11.55 mm [95% CI: 9.94, 13.16]. On 3DIRCADb, zero-shot inference yielded DSC of 68.42% [95% CI: 65.82, 71.02] and HD95 of 11.78 mm [95% CI: 8.50, 15.06]. CONCLUSION Adaptive deep fusion of an optimized anatomical prior improved CT segmentation of portal and hepatic veins, especially fine peripheral branches, supporting further evaluation in 3D vascular modeling workflows for liver surgery and intervention.

title: Factors Hindering Digital Tool Integration into Construction
container-title: Vestnik Tomskogo gosudarstvennogo arkhitekturno-stroitel'nogo universiteta. JOURNAL of Construction and Architecture
4469ecc062a043fee6736261d71e5206711669b4.abstract: The development of the construction industry leads to an increasing use of digital tools at all stages of the object lifecycle. The digital tool implementation involves not only assessing their effectiveness but also considering factors hindering this process. Assessing their impact and identifying the most pressing factors is an important task that will optimize the implementation of digital tools in the construction. Purpose: The aim of the work is to identify factors having the greatest impact digitalization of the development and verification of documentation in the construction company activity, using the expert survey. Research findings: A list of the main factors hindering digitalization is compiled based on the literature review. The expert survey of construction engineers with the experience ranging from 6 months to 27 years and the data analysis shows the most significant factors, and a system of assessing the importance of expert responses based on experience is developed. Value: The results allow identifying the factors most significantly hindering the digitalization of construction. Difficulties in obtaining licensed software and the insufficient education level of graduates are the most significant among the factors identified. The relationships between the most influential factors are also formulated, and the most significant factors by the main groups of the expert survey is assessed.

title: COMPARATIVE ANALYSIS OF DIGITAL LENDING PLATFORMS AND DEPOSIT MONEY BANKS LENDING IN NIGERIA
container-title: International Journal of Financial Research and Business Development
8685ad43ed3f0f0f7df6fea3fc7ca6d56579a9cb.abstract: Nigeria’s Deposit Money Banks (DMBs) and credit market is increasingly characterized by the coexistence of technology-driven digital lending platforms (DLPs). This study examined the two lending channels with emphasis on credit accessibility, cost of lending, loan quality and financial inclusion. A descriptive survey design was adopted, and structured questionnaires were administered to borrowers in Jos North Local Government Area of Plateau State who had obtained credit from DLPs, DMBs, or both. 384 questionnaires administered, 247 usable responses were received, representing 64.32%, Data collected were analyzed using descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation and simple regression in SPSS version 30. The results indicate that lending type significantly explains differences in all four outcomes. DLPs demonstrated superior credit accessibility (B = 0.804, β = 0.749, p < .001) and stronger contribution to financial inclusion (B = 0.921, β = 0.763, p < .001). However, DLPs were associated with higher lending costs (B = 0.769, β = 0.724, p < .001) and with weaker loan quality (B = −0.836, β = −0.737, p < .001), relative to DMBs. The findings suggest a balancing relationship between speed and inclusion on one hand and affordability and credit quality on the other. The study recommends proportionate regulation, transparent pricing, responsible digital credit assessment, interoperable credit information systems and stronger digital capabilities among DMBs. Rather than treating DLPs and DMBs as mutually exclusive alternatives, therefore policymakers should encourage complementary strengths while protecting borrowers from excessive costs, over-indebtedness and abusive recovery practices.

title: Strategi Promosi Berbasis Etika Bisnis Islam pada Industri Genteng Tradisional di Era Digital

d0354b6e955411879e7bb9aed424875b93cb1f80.abstract: This study aims to describe the promotional strategies of traditional roof tile businesses in Wringinanom Village, Sambit Subdistrict, Ponorogo Regency in the digital era, analyze the application of Islamic business ethics in promotional activities, and formulate directions for developing promotion based on Islamic business ethics. The study employs a qualitative approach with a descriptive design. Data were collected through interviews with five informants (roof tile business owners and the village head) and documentation, then analyzed using the Miles et al. interactive model, comprising data reduction, data display, and conclusion drawing. The results show that promotion combines Word of Mouth (WOM) with digital media (Facebook, WhatsApp, Instagram, and TikTok). According to the informants, WOM remains the main strategy, while digital media are used in a simple way to extend reach, forming a hybrid promotional pattern. The values of sidq (honesty), amanah, responsibility, courtesy, and healthy competition were expressed by the informants and are visible in promotional practices, including production-process content and customer testimonials. However, their application remains individual and has not become a shared standard, and some business owners reported that price undercutting on social media reduces their profits. The proposed directions for developing promotion include strengthening digital content, testimonial-based electronic Word of Mouth (e-WOM), improving business owners' digital skills, and reinforcing an ethics-based sharia marketing identity. This study proposes a conceptual model linking product quality, Islamic business ethics, WOM/e-WOM, and digital promotion to customer trust as perceived by the informants. These relationships require further testing in future research.

title: Digital Scaffolding Strategies in Instructional Design: Enhancing Independent Learning Among Pre-University Students in Kota Samarahan, Malaysia
f1bdd545abc79dd8e46327af91d641ea758ffc01.abstract: Abstract This study investigates the role of digital scaffolding strategies in instructional design and their effectiveness in enhancing independent learning among pre-university students in Kota Samarahan, Malaysia. The research employed a quantitative survey method, incorporating both a pilot test and a full-scale study. The instrument measured three constructs: digital scaffolding strategies, independent learning skills, and perceived effectiveness of scaffolds. Reliability analysis demonstrated excellent internal consistency for all constructs, with Cronbach’s alpha values exceeding 0.93. Based on responses from 112 students, the findings revealed consistently high mean scores across the 30 items, indicating strong agreement regarding the positive role of scaffolding in facilitating independent learning. Furthermore, findings suggest that digital scaffolding strategies not only support learner autonomy but also strengthen motivation, time management, and confidence in self-directed learning. The study contributes to instructional design research by demonstrating how structured scaffolding mechanisms can be effectively integrated into pre-university curricula to foster independent learners. Implications for practice, policy, and future research are discussed.

title: Student Engagement with Digital Library Resources through Learning Analytics in Adamawa State University, Mubi
container-title: RESEARCH JOURNAL OF MASS COMMUNICATION AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY
bac75cd498df9d6c565016912780cdd9c210ab5e.abstract: This study investigates student engagement with digital library resources at Adamawa State University, Mubi, using learning analytics and survey data. A stratified sample approach was designed to obtain responses from 1,800 students across faculties. Measures included frequency of use, session duration, resource diversity, perceived usefulness, accessibility, digital literacy, and institutional use of learning analytics. Descriptive and inferential analyses — including ttests, ANOVA, and regression models — were employed. Results indicate that overall engagement with digital library resources is lower than neutral (mean engagement = 2.52/5), with no statistically significant differences across faculties. Awareness of learning analytics alone did not correspond to higher engagement; rather, infrastructural and user-related challenges (poor connectivity, limited digital skills, and usability issues) were significant negative predictors of engagement. The study concludes that implementing robust learning-analytics dashboards, improving digital infrastructure, and incorporating digital literacy training are key to increasing students’ meaningful engagement with digital resources. Recommendations include investment in reliable connectivity, targeted training programs, and dashboard-driven interventions to personalize resource recommendations and promote deeper use.

title: Evaluation of Digital Literacy Skills for Effective Library Service Delivery among Library Staff in Adamawa State University, Mubi
container-title: RESEARCH JOURNAL OF MASS COMMUNICATION AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY
892add480af4c341cc5e25764e4a78c1e9e3b508.abstract: This study evaluated digital literacy skills and their influence on effective library service delivery among staff of Adamawa State University, Mubi. With the growing demand for digital information services, the research aimed to assess staff competencies, identify skill gaps, and examine challenges affecting digital performance. A descriptive survey design was employed, and data were gathered through a structured questionnaire and interviews with library personnel. Descriptive and inferential statistics, including correlation and ANOVA, were used to analyze the data 0.05. Findings revealed that library staff possessed moderate to high proficiency in basic digital skills such as word processing and internet use but exhibited limited competence in advanced areas like digital preservation and database management. Results further showed a significant positive relationship between digital literacy and the quality of library service delivery. Major challenges identified included unstable power supply, poor internet connectivity, and inadequate training opportunities. The study recommends continuous capacity-building programs, improved ICT infrastructure, and institutional support to enhance staff digital competencies and ensure efficient, technology-driven library services.

title: Challenges and Prospects of Digital Technology Utilization among Library Personnel in Adamawa State University, Mubi
container-title: RESEARCH JOURNAL OF MASS COMMUNICATION AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY
be56ee9cd7b56deb937c4dd5278e58d2ece200ae.abstract: This study investigates the challenges and prospects of digital technology utilization among library personnel at Adamawa State University, Mubi. A descriptive survey design was adopted, with a population of 46 library staff. Data collected through structured questionnaires were analyzed using SPSS version 25. Findings revealed that major challenges affecting digital technology use include frequent power outages (mean = 4.44), poor internet connectivity (mean = 4.30), inadequate ICT training (mean = 4.28), and insufficient funding (mean = 4.16). Despite these challenges, utilization levels were moderate to high, particularly in the use of OPAC and automation software. Prospects for improving digital utilization were strongly identified, such as regular digital literacy training, improved ICT infrastructure, and increased funding. Inferential analysis indicated significant relationships between technology availability, staff competence, and utilization (p < 0.05). The study concludes that addressing infrastructural and skill gaps through continuous training and improved digital support systems will enhance service efficiency and promote sustainable digital transformation in academic libraries.

title: “Bridging the Digital Divide in Academic Libraries: Strategies for Promoting Equitable Access to Digital Information Resources at the Federal Polytechnic, Mubi”
container-title: RESEARCH JOURNAL OF MASS COMMUNICATION AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY
7b8359e2ec9accc2f4b7e5d0d8b274ba9b92300f.abstract: This study examined strategies for promoting equitable access to digital information resources in the Federal Polytechnic, Mubi library, focusing on bridging the digital divide among users. The study adopted a descriptive survey design, involving 120 respondents comprising 20 library staff and 100 students across levels. Data were collected using structured questionnaires and analyzed using descriptive and inferential statistics, including mean, standard deviation, and one-way ANOVA. The findings revealed that while digital resources such as e-journals, databases, and online catalogues were available, access was hindered by inadequate infrastructure, limited bandwidth, and insufficient user training. The ANOVA test indicated a significant relationship between digital infrastructure availability and access to digital information resources (p < 0.05). The study concluded that bridging the digital divide requires both infrastructural development and digital literacy initiatives. It recommended continuous investment in ICT facilities, regular digital skills training for both staff and students, and collaborative partnerships with information technology organizations to ensure inclusive access to digital resources.

title: Digital Media, Citizen Journalism, Ethics and Self-Censorship
container-title: RESEARCH JOURNAL OF MASS COMMUNICATION AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY
b1b3a6c7787499a1aa4f10f270337b931845d929.abstract: This article looks at the impact of digital media on citizen journalism, ethics of journalism and self-censorship. There is no doubt that citizens have played a greater role in the advancement of the journalism profession, through on the spot collection and dissemination of news worthy events and pictures. This was made possible with the help of digital technology. Since these citizen journalists lack training in the profession, it seems that the core ethics of journalism have not been adhered to, in the course of their practice and the task of censorship remains daunting. Given the contributions of these invaders to the advancement of the work associated with journalism, citizens should be more involved, through a collaborative effort by media houses, who should encourage the citizenry, through training and the publication of their stories in their medium. This article assesses the effect of digital technology on citizen journalism, and made suggestions and contributions that encourage citizen journalism, stressed the importance of adherence to ethical codes and self-censorship, to establish a robust and sustainable relationship between the media and its publics.

title: Legitimasi Yuridis Partisipasi Masyarakat Digital sebagai Instrumen Pengawasan terhadap Akuntabilitas Aparat Penegak Hukum dalam Fenomena No Viral No Justice di Indonesia
container-title: Jurnal Ragam Pengabdian
6666bec9dbab9b17b00e997bb0734df8faf7e2ea.abstract: Fenomena No Viral No Justice mencerminkan pemanfaatan media sosial sebagai sarana pengawasan terhadap aparat penegak hukum yang dinilai lamban dan kurang transparan, sementara aturan yang mengatur peran dan perlindungan hukumnya belum jelas. Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis legitimasi yuridis partisipasi masyarakat digital sebagai instrumen pengawasan akuntabilitas aparat penegak hukum, batas yuridisnya, dan harmonisasinya dengan due process of law. Metode yang digunakan adalah hukum normatif dengan pendekatan perundang-undangan dan konseptual, melalui studi kepustakaan dan analisis kualitatif. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa partisipasi digital memiliki legitimasi yuridis yang kuat karena berlandaskan kedaulatan rakyat, kebebasan berpendapat, dan hak atas informasi dalam UUD NRI 1945 serta Undang-Undang Keterbukaan Informasi Publik. Pengawasan ini dibatasi oleh Pasal 28J ayat (2) UUD NRI 1945, ketentuan pencemaran nama baik dan berita bohong dalam UU ITE, serta asas praduga tak bersalah. Putusan Mahkamah Konstitusi Nomor 105/PUU-XXII/2024 menegaskan bahwa kritik terhadap institusi tidak termasuk pencemaran nama baik. Partisipasi digital dapat mendorong responsivitas dan transparansi aparat, tetapi tekanan viralitas berisiko menimbulkan penghakiman massa dan mengganggu peradilan yang adil. Harmonisasi memerlukan literasi digital, saluran pengaduan yang responsif dan mudah diakses, serta penguatan regulasi.

title: The Effect of AI Absorptive Capacity of Organizations on Workers’ Perceptions About Smart Work Environment Perception Towards Digital Innovation Behavior.
container-title: WSEAS Transactions on Information Science and Applications
743b00c8552a137b4c5e81a5f74226040cc68957.abstract: This study investigates the effect of organizational artificial intelligence (AI) absorptive capacity on employees’ perceptions of the smart work environment and how these perceptions influence their digital innovative behavior in the telecommunications industry, with Digital Transformational Leadership as a moderating variable. In this study, two important theoretical perspectives were utilized: Absorptive Capacity Theory, which highlights how organizations acquire, assimilate, and apply their knowledge related to AI, and Socio-Technical Systems Theory, which addresses the connection between technology and the social aspect of the working environment. A quantitative research design was used through partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM). The data were gathered from 279 respondents working in the telecommunication industry in Jordan. These respondents worked for internet service providers, network operators, and mobile network operators. The findings show that organizational AI absorptive capacity has a strong positive effect on Smart Work Environment Perception (β = 0.742), which in turn enhances Digital Innovative Behavior (β = 0.681). Smart Work Environment Perception partially mediates the relationship between AI absorptive capacity and Digital Innovative Behavior (indirect effect β = 0.506), while Digital Transformational Leadership positively moderates the relationship between AI absorptive capacity and the smart work environment (β = 0.276) and between the smart work environment and Digital Innovative Behavior (β = 0.241). The current research adds value to the literature surrounding AI adoption within organizations by examining how technical capabilities and organizational leadership help foster Digital Innovative Behavior in the telecommunications industry.

title: Prompt style effects on large language model differential diagnosis output in adolescent catatonia and psychosis
container-title: Journal of Digital Health
8c2b2b92dc34c507f5536f1e76215cac1a12b795.abstract: Prompt engineering shapes large language model (LLM) output, but practicing clinicians have little guidance on which prompting style suits a given clinical task. A single publicly available, de-identified pediatric psychiatric case report was submitted to a base, unauthenticated ChatGPT-5.5 session under four prompt conditions: zero-shot, chain-of-thought, role/persona, and structured/constrained output. Each output was scored from 0 (feature absent) to 2 (complete) on four criteria: diagnostic accuracy, causative agent recognition, safety completeness, and calibration. Output was compared against the published clinical course. Total scores were zero-shot 7/8, chain-of-thought 6/8, role-persona 7/8, and structured 7/8. All four conditions ranked bipolar I disorder above substance-induced psychotic disorder, whereas the treating team's documented differential favored unspecified and substance-induced categories without a confirmed bipolar diagnosis. All four conditions recommended neuroimaging, electroencephalography, and lumbar puncture, exceeding the workup the treating team actually performed. Across four prompt styles, core diagnostic content was materially the same; the styles differed in the precision of probability quantification and in reasoning transparency, not in the underlying differential generated.

title: Digital Technology and Market Share of Selected Micro Enterprises Firms in Nigeria
container-title: RESEARCH JOURNAL OF MASS COMMUNICATION AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY
7318802c7475ce7d1a6df15371b4c4e8ea0daa97.abstract: The study examined the effect of digital technology on market share of selected micro enterprises firms in Nigeria. The specific objective was to determine the effect of e-commerce platform usage and social media marketing on market share of selected micro enterprises firms in Nigeria. Descriptive survey research design was adopted on a population of 41,469,947 operators of micro enterprises in Nigeria. A sample size of 400 was calculated using Taro Yamane formula while the respondents were recruited using purposive sampling approach. Primary data were collected using questionnaire based on five-point Likert-scale system. The hypotheses were tested using multiple regression analysis at 5% significance level. The study found the following: E-commerce platform usage has a significant and positive effect on market share of selected micro enterprises firms in Nigeria (β = 0.199, p = 0.000); Social media marketing has a significant and positive effect on market share of selected micro enterprises firms in Nigeria (β = 0.557, p = 0.000). In conclusion, micro enterprises that embrace digital technologies are better positioned to attract a larger customer base, compete more effectively, and grow their presence in the market. The study recommended that operators of micro enterprises should partner with technology solution providers to offer customized, subsidized e-commerce infrastructure and training programs tailored specifically for micro enterprise firms.

title: What Is a Digital Chemistry Lab?
container-title: Building a Digital Chemistry Lab
fcf44029228af378b81405988dd4bea90e8b74be.abstract: This opening chapter frames the concept of the digital chemistry lab by moving beyond imagery of robots and instead defining digitisation as the integration of automation, live data capture and algorithmic decision-making into experimental practice. It traces the historical roots of laboratory automation and explains why recent advances in hardware accessibility, data infrastructure and machine learning have lowered barriers to adoption. It also examines when digitisation is strategically advantageous, from hazardous and air-sensitive chemistry to ultrafast, long-duration and spatially complex systems. Readers are encouraged to assess what digitisation could mean for their own laboratory and why now is a pivotal moment to engage.

title: Automation and Robotics in the Modern Chemistry Lab
container-title: Building a Digital Chemistry Lab
12132c919241030d2f9b040bc0f267ce885bcde2.abstract: This chapter surveys the hardware and software foundations of the digital chemistry laboratory, guiding the reader from first principles of automation to the realities of closed-loop experimentation. It frames automation as a spectrum spanning manual workflows to fully autonomous self-driving laboratories, with trade-offs to be expected at each level. A comparative overview of physical implementations follows, including robotic arms, gantry systems, fluidic batch platforms, flow and microfluidic reactors, with attention to their respective strengths, bottlenecks and domains of applicability. We discuss commercially available digital labware and analytical instrumentation, including the practical challenges of interfacing with vendor software and legacy equipment. Finally, the chapter examines control architecture ranging from Python scripts to chemical programming languages and laboratory operating systems in order to acquaint the reader with automation strategies that may align with their scientific goals and available resources.

title: Designing and Implementing Custom Labware
container-title: Building a Digital Chemistry Lab
0045f858b4392024fc770627598a047e6bd96673.abstract: This chapter provides a practical guide to designing and implementing custom labware for the digital chemistry laboratory. It begins by looking at when bespoke hardware is justified and the balance between flexibility, time investment and scientific reproducibility. Core electronics concepts are introduced, including digital communication standards, analog signals, and pulse width modulation PWM control. Wireless options, power sources and strategies for safe voltage management are examined next. We then survey common sensors and actuators before outlining microcontroller ecosystems, concluding with prototyping workflows using CAD, 3D printing, laser cutting and aluminium extrusions.

title: Data Acquisition, Processing, and Interpretation
container-title: Building a Digital Chemistry Lab
4070d9765e56222d7bd875c107940855153bdab0.abstract: This chapter sets out practical foundations for handling experimental data in a digital laboratory, from capture to interpretation. It starts by outlining common routes to data acquisition, including direct instrument communication, file-based workflows and camera systems. We weigh options for organising and storing results using different file formats and databases. Core analytical ideas such as sampling, aliasing, Fourier transforms, filtering and dimensionality reduction are introduced with an emphasis on when and why they matter. The chapter closes with image-based data extraction and Bayesian modelling as tools for drawing quantitative conclusions under uncertainty.

title: Examples and Case Studies
container-title: Building a Digital Chemistry Lab
9db9f0ba73a0e30ac7924fc7edcec4f99174dee2.abstract: This chapter presents case studies that illustrate how digitisation can be implemented in real laboratory settings. What unique advantages do purpose-built digital laboratory spaces offer? How can legacy instruments be integrated into a modern experimental closed loop? And how can you accelerate your science via creative use of low-cost commodity hardware? A final case study demonstrates how to augment a closed robotic platform with external machine vision and hybrid control.

8abe404efc3c171555c1035a6b29f6f2e08a8f10.abstract: This chapter concludes the book with closing thoughts and pointers to resources for learning more about some of the topics discussed in previous chapters.
