title: Adaptive auditory stimulation sustains auditory-respiratory coordination and promotes slowing of spontaneous breathing
2c17cca13e85e4210c5acfb04f280a9c0d6f0a30.abstract: Auditory feedback may influence breathing without explicit instructions to regulate it, but its precise impact remains unclear. We examined responses to adaptive and nonadaptive breath-like sounds during passive listening. Thirty-nine young adults completed four counterbalanced conditions: nonrhythmic filtered noise (Static), rhythmic sounds progressively slowing or speeding relative to initial breathing rate (Slowing and Speeding respectively), and sound adapting continuously to respiratory frequency and phase with a prescribed phase delay relative to respiration (Adaptive). Each condition included 4 min of nominal silence followed by 4 min of stimulation. Primary outcomes were breathing rate slopes, auditory–respiratory phase locking as a measure of auditory-respiratory coordination, respiratory sinus arrhythmia, and subjective relaxation. Breathing-rate trajectories differed across conditions; Adaptive showed a more negative slope than Static, although average rates were similar. Phase locking was higher and more sustained during Adaptive than during the nonadaptive rhythmic conditions. Respiratory sinus arrhythmia trajectories differed, but planned contrasts did not survive multiplicity correction. A relaxation composite score did not differ by condition, but an item-level analysis indicated less physical relaxation after Adaptive than Static. Secondary outcomes provided no evidence of increased cardiorespiratory coupling or reduced upper-trapezius muscle activity. Interestingly, the negative breathing-rate trajectories remained significantly different in Adaptive compared to Static after retaining only the 25 respondents that did not notice the sound’s adaptation to their breathing. These findings support adaptive auditory stimulation as a means of supporting auditory-respiratory coordination during uninstructed listening, with a modest and relative change in breathing rate. Clinical benefits and independence from intentional breathing control remain to be tested.

title: Trust in AI: A Decision-Theoretic framework for Human–AI Interactions in the Digital Society
cd2e1c34af9387fd565d30e964dce709b38b5e7f.abstract: Trust in artificial intelligence (AI) is crucial for ensuring productive human–AI interactions across domains ranging from medicine to finance. As AI systems become central in the digital society, understanding how people decide when to rely on algorithmic advice becomes increasingly important. This paper proposes that a decision-theoretic perspective is needed to explain how well-calibrated trust in AI can be achieved. We conceptualize trust in AI as a decision to delegate control to an artificial agent, balancing potential rewards and risks of following AI advice versus relying on one’s own judgment. Framed this way, established decision-making theories such as Prospect Theory, Evidence Accumulation Models, and Reinforcement Learning offer valuable insights into the cognitive processes that underlie trust in AI. These theories offer formal, computational models to explain how individuals evaluate AI-generated advice, weigh risks and rewards, form biases, and update trust based on feedback, enabling precise hypotheses about when and why people accept or reject AI advice. By grounding trust in cognitive theory, we offer a roadmap for empirical research that moves beyond surface-level behaviors and toward mechanistic understanding. We conclude that a decision-theoretic approach can enhance psychological insight and guide the responsible design of AI systems within the digital society that are better aligned with human cognition.

title: PARTNERSHIPS BETWEEN FASHION BRANDS AND DIGITAL INFLUENCERS: PERCEPTIONS OF CREDIBILITY AND AUTHENTICITY
container-title: Revista e-TECH: Tecnologias para Competitividade Industrial - ISSN - 1983-1838
5b3f4b4751567b3d5e2aa254d2d5bfba9cb32a87.abstract: Influencer marketing has expanded its presence in the fashion industry, establishing new forms of interaction between brands, content creators, and consumers in digital environments. Within this context, this study aims to analyse how female fashion influencers perceive and manage credibility and authenticity in advertising partnerships with brands. This applied research adopts a qualitative, descriptive approach, combining a literature review with field research. Data were collected through a questionnaire comprising five open-ended questions, answered by four female digital influencers operating in the Brazilian fashion market, with distinct professional profiles, audiences, and follower counts ranging from approximately 50,000 to 8 million. Participants were selected through purposive key-informant sampling based on their practical experience in developing commercial partnerships with brands. The responses were analysed qualitatively and interpreted in relation to theoretical perspectives on consumer behaviour, influencer marketing, and digital communication. The perceptions identified in the participants’ responses highlighted the alignment between influencer and brand values, transparency in advertising communication, autonomy in content creation, and responsibility in product recommendations as aspects associated with maintaining credibility and authenticity in commercial partnerships.

container-title: Sustainable Development
97dbe42e10f8e04e8790bc873ae37a368d004476.abstract: ABSTRACT Water scarcity has become a multidimensional sustainability challenge driven by climate change, demographic growth, governance quality and technological adaptation. Although desalination is increasingly recognised as a strategic response to water stress, existing assessment approaches remain fragmented and fail to evaluate its adaptive resilience comprehensively. This study develops the Desalination Resilience Dynamic Index (DRDI), a multidimensional framework integrating technological, economic, institutional and distributive dimensions to assess desalination resilience. The framework is developed through a structured literature review supported by a descriptive bibliometric analysis and operationalised as a transparent composite indicator based on five complementary resilience dimensions. Rather than predicting system performance, the DRDI provides a replicable methodology for comparative assessment and evidence‐based policy analysis. By integrating previously disconnected research streams, the proposed framework advances resilience assessment and offers a practical tool to support sustainable water governance under increasing environmental uncertainty.

title: AFSAF-Net: Adaptive Frequency-Spatial Attention Fusion Network with IMU Guidance for Robust Indoor Localization under Low-Light and Texture-Degraded Environments
8d1e2827b2f7782a467743b281ca63833a28e0d7.abstract: Abstract Indoor localization under low-light and texture-degraded environments remains challenging because insufficient visual information leads to unstable feature extraction, while inertial measurements are inevitably affected by accumulated drift. Previous MC4L-IMU-based studies demonstrated the effectiveness of handcrafted texture descriptors, frequency-domain enhancement, deep visual representation learning, and visual-inertial fusion for improving localization performance in dark indoor scenarios. However, these approaches mainly rely on manually designed frequency representations and fixed fusion strategies, limiting their adaptability to dynamically changing sensor reliability. To address these limitations, this paper proposes an Adaptive Frequency-Spatial Attention Fusion Network with IMU Guidance (AFSAF-Net) for robust indoor localization. The proposed framework introduces an adaptive frequency learning branch to capture spectral information beyond handcrafted transformations, an attention-driven frequency-spatial fusion module to dynamically integrate complementary visual representations, and an IMU reliability gate to adjust the contribution of inertial information according to sensor confidence. By jointly modeling frequency characteristics, spatial semantics, and inertial reliability, AFSAF-Net enables adaptive multimodal perception under challenging indoor conditions. Experiments conducted on the MC4L-IMU indoor localization platform demonstrate that AFSAF-Net achieves a mean localization error of 0.85 cm and the highest coefficient of determination (R 2 = 0.9986) among the evaluated methods. Furthermore, the proposed framework maintains more stable localization performance under low-light conditions compared with conventional visual and visual-inertial approaches. These results indicate that adaptive spectral representation learning and reliability-aware sensor fusion can effectively improve localization robustness without relying on fixed feature extraction or predefined fusion rules.

title: PROGRAMA DE TRANSFORMACIÓN DIGITAL DE SABOREÉ ROSARIO
container-title: Informes de Investigacion. IIATA.
35c7cdc632423d6f879ab9ac4f5ae9f35f06d7d0.abstract: Este artículo presenta una propuesta de transformación digital para Saboreé Rosario, microempresa local dedicada a la elaboración artesanal de alfajores, conitos, espumitas de limón y budines. El trabajo parte de un diagnóstico de la organización, su contexto competitivo, sus segmentos de clientes y sus principales procesos, para identificar oportunidades de digitalización. Se propone un modelo gradual que combina comercio electrónico, WhatsApp Business, herramientas de gestión, sistemas de relación con clientes, analítica y digitalización de los procesos administrativos, productivos y comerciales. El plan se estructura en objetivos de corto, mediano y largo plazo, acompañados por resultados clave e indicadores de desempeño que permiten realizar seguimiento. Asimismo, se analizan riesgos vinculados con la inversión inicial, la capacitación, la resistencia al cambio, las fallas técnicas y la seguridad de la información. La propuesta busca ampliar el alcance comercial, mejorar la eficiencia operativa, fortalecer la fidelización y facilitar la toma de decisiones basada en información, preservando al mismo tiempo la identidad artesanal de la empresa. En este sentido, la transformación digital se plantea como un proceso progresivo de integración entre tradición e innovación.

title: TRANSFORMACIÓN DIGITAL DE LOS ESTUDIOS CONTABLES
container-title: Informes de Investigacion. IIATA.
a2cccb4732cf721d657ba266b1f9735d02b6a7b2.abstract: Este trabajo se centra en analizar los estudios contables de la ciudad de Rosario y su proceso de transformación digital. El objetivo es evaluar la implementación de nuevas tecnologías en los estudios contables y su implementación (o no) dentro de un marco estratégico. En este análisis se aborda este proceso desde cinco dominios clave: relaciones con clientes, competencia, gestión de datos, procesos de innovación y propuesta de valor. Se emiten al final una serie de recomendaciones a partir de la implementación del modelo E-A-T desarrollado por Leo Piccioli para la optimización del trabajo profesional y el logro de la deseada transformación digital de la gestión de la profesión.

title: COMPETENCIA DIGITAL EN LA ENSEÑANZA Y EL APRENDIZAJE DE HABILIDADES DE INVESTIGACIÓN EN LA UNIVERSIDAD 21
container-title: Informes de Investigacion. IIATA.
7ef1aa218ae5a17d1a89e8a6faaadcdb56b9443e.abstract: Este artículo explora la integración de la competencia digital en la enseñanza y el aprendizaje de habilidades de investigación dentro del paradigma de la Universidad 4.0, haciendo hincapié en su aplicabilidad en contextos educativos ajenos a las disciplinas técnicas. La Universidad 4.0, alineada con la Educación 4.0, sitúa a la investigación como elemento central, fomentando la creatividad, la innovación y el aprendizaje continuo. El estudio evalúa las autopercepciones de las competencias digitales entre estudiantes de carrera de grado y posgrado en educación en Argentina, centrándose en su capacidad para utilizar herramientas digitales esenciales para la investigación en el ámbito humanístico. A través de una encuesta en línea, se recopilaron datos para examinar la competencia digital autopercibida y en qué medida se ajusta a los requerimientos de las prácticas de investigación actuales. Los resultados revelan brechas en la competencia digital, incluso en comandos informáticos básicos, más notoriamente en el nivel de grado que en el de posgrado. Estos hallazgos subrayan los desafíos que implica adoptar las herramientas digitales en carreras educativas en las antípodas de las ingenierías, y resaltan la necesidad de intervenciones específicas para alcanzar el modelo de Estudiante 4.0. El estudio contribuye a la comprensión del papel de las alfabetizaciones digitales en el fomento de las habilidades de investigación. Subraya la necesidad de que los programas universitarios ofrezcan oportunidades transformadoras que aborden las brechas digitales y se alineen con los paradigmas educativos actuales. Asimismo, destaca las implicancias críticas para el diseño curricular en el fomento de la competencia digital como piedra angular del futuro liderazgo e innovación educativos.

title: IMPLEMENTASI TEKNOLOGI DIGITAL DALAM PROSES PEMBELAJARAN KELAS VI DI SD NEGERI MARABAHAN 2
container-title: EDUCATIONAL : Jurnal Inovasi Pendidikan & Pengajaran
11b4bd45879181d7783c90ccf97f56df80216560.abstract: This study aimed to describe the implementation of digital technology in sixth-grade learning, analyze teachers’ strategies in its use, and identify supporting factors and challenges at SD Negeri Marabahan 2. Although various studies have examined the use of digital media in elementary schools, studies that simultaneously investigate forms of implementation, teacher strategies, supporting factors, and challenges in the context of sixth-grade learning remain limited. This study employed a descriptive qualitative approach. Data were collected through interviews with the principal and sixth-grade teacher, non-participant observations of the learning process and student activities, and documentation. Data analysis followed the stages of data reduction, data display, and conclusion drawing, while trustworthiness was strengthened through source and method triangulation. The findings showed that digital technology was used in almost every subject through LCD projectors, laptops, internet access, interactive display boards, Canva, Quizizz, learning videos, PowerPoint, and electronic worksheets. The teacher planned media use based on learning materials, objectives, student characteristics, and readiness, and combined it with lectures, discussions, question-and-answer sessions, idea sharing, and ice-breaking activities. Implementation was supported by digital facilities, school leadership policies, the Cemara Learning Community, teacher working groups, and professional training. The main challenge was the continuous need to improve teachers’ competence in response to rapid technological change, while students’ technical difficulties could be addressed through teacher guidance. During digital learning activities, students were perceived as more enthusiastic and showed more active engagement, participation, and learning responses. These findings indicate that successful digital learning depends on the integration of infrastructure, teachers’ digital-pedagogical competence, institutional support, and continuous professional development. ABSTRAKPenelitian ini bertujuan mendeskripsikan implementasi teknologi digital dalam proses pembelajaran kelas VI, menganalisis strategi guru dalam pemanfaatannya, serta mengidentifikasi faktor pendukung dan kendala yang dihadapi di SD Negeri Marabahan 2. Meskipun berbagai penelitian telah membahas penggunaan media digital di sekolah dasar, kajian yang secara bersamaan menelaah bentuk implementasi, strategi guru, faktor pendukung, dan kendala dalam konteks pembelajaran kelas VI masih terbatas. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan kualitatif deskriptif. Data diperoleh melalui wawancara dengan kepala sekolah dan guru kelas VI, observasi nonpartisipatif terhadap proses pembelajaran dan aktivitas peserta didik, serta dokumentasi. Analisis data mengikuti tahapan reduksi data, penyajian data, dan penarikan kesimpulan, sedangkan keabsahan data diperkuat melalui triangulasi sumber dan metode. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa teknologi digital telah digunakan hampir pada setiap mata pelajaran melalui LCD proyektor, laptop, jaringan internet, papan layar interaktif, Canva, Quizizz, video pembelajaran, PowerPoint, dan E-LKPD. Guru merencanakan penggunaan media berdasarkan materi, tujuan pembelajaran, karakteristik, dan kesiapan peserta didik, kemudian memadukannya dengan ceramah, diskusi, tanya jawab, berbagi gagasan, dan ice breaking. Implementasi didukung oleh sarana digital, kebijakan kepala sekolah, Komunitas Belajar Cemara, KKG, dan pelatihan profesional. Kendala utama berupa tuntutan peningkatan kompetensi guru untuk mengikuti perubahan teknologi yang cepat, sedangkan kendala teknis pada peserta didik dapat diatasi melalui bimbingan guru. Selama pembelajaran digital, peserta didik dipersepsikan lebih antusias dan menunjukkan keterlibatan, partisipasi, serta respons belajar yang lebih aktif. Temuan ini menegaskan bahwa keberhasilan pembelajaran digital ditentukan oleh keterpaduan fasilitas, kompetensi pedagogis digital guru, dukungan kelembagaan, dan pengembangan profesional berkelanjutan.

title: Learning Evidence and Assessment Design for Traditional Chinese Medicine Cultural Education within an Inheritance-Integration-Innovation Framework: Digital Learning Tasks Using Central Plains Resources
container-title: Journal of Education and Educational Research
ddb3dfd1490c197ed1969a0c50f752016250ce44.abstract: Assessing a digital exhibit in traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) culture requires more than judging the finished slides. Teachers also need to know how students selected sources, interpreted them, and responded to criticism. This paper proposes an assessment design for university general education based on the inheritance-integration-innovation framework, evidence-centered design, and formative assessment. Six indicators specify the evidence to collect across three 90-minute units using Yaofang Cave materials from the Longmen Grottoes. The units move from source verification and annotation to exhibit design and revision. Individual explanations accompany group submissions, and an analytic rubric addresses cultural interpretation, digital resource use, and justified design decisions. A separate Funiu Mountain task examines performance with unfamiliar materials before feedback is provided. Subsequent revision is assessed separately. Cultural understanding and reasoned value reflection remain distinct from cultural identification throughout the design. The proposal sets out a procedure for classroom assessment; its feasibility and measurement properties still require testing.

title: A Study on Brand Equity Dilution and Digital Marketing Adjustment Caused by Excessive Collaborations with Uniqlo UT
container-title: Academic Journal of Management and Social Sciences
a3167f482925a5d3aa39353baff8dd280543de14.abstract: Brand collaboration has become a key method in modern digital marketing to cater to the desire for individual expression among young people. However, the collaboration strategy of the Uniqlo UT series is showing a marked tendency toward excess. The rapid pace of new releases combined with simplistic "decal-style" IP replication not only depletes product scarcity and causes consumer aesthetic fatigue but also undermines the brand's original quality positioning of "LifeWear." Addressing this phenomenon, this paper conducts an in-depth analysis using a combination of web data mining, surveys, and interviews. The study indicates that the current model of heavy IP aggregation is unsustainable. Uniqlo needs to shift toward "two-way value co-creation," leveraging data feedback to drive innovation in product functionality and original graphic aesthetics, while constructing immersive online-to-offline (O2O) consumption scenarios, thereby providing a reliable path for realigning its brand marketing strategy.

title: Influence of Digital Resources and Information Sharing on Supply Chain Sustainability
container-title: Business Strategy and the Environment
b120a109871168f3198f44bfb649dc6aeaa62cf6.abstract: ABSTRACT Although supply chain digitalization has received considerable research attention, the mechanisms through which digital resources contribute to sustainability outcomes are not fully understood. This study examines how digital technologies, particularly big data analytics (BDA), support sustainability practices and performance in supply chains through information sharing. Building on the resource‐based view (RBV) and the dynamic capabilities perspective, a conceptual framework is developed and empirically tested using cross‐industry survey data from Finland and partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS‐SEM). The results show that digital resources and BDA indirectly contribute to supply chain sustainability by enhancing information sharing among supply chain partners. More effective information sharing improves transparency and coordination across the supply chain, thereby supporting the achievement of sustainability goals. This study makes two contributions. First, from an RBV perspective, it shows that information sharing is a key resource through which digitalization translates into sustainability outcomes. Second, from a dynamic capabilities perspective, it extends the emerging literature by showing how digitally enabled capabilities support sustainability transitions in supply chains.

Adaptive Substructure
Sampling for Molecules with
Flexible Alkyl Substituents
container-title:
Journal of Chemical Theory
and Computation
60b18a189881e5fc0de454344f8bd59cbd0a34fe.abstract: Abstract The exponential growth of conformational space in molecules with flexible side chains presents a fundamental bottleneck for atomistic sampling methods. A large fraction of this complexity arises from weakly coupled, quasi-degenerate torsional degrees of freedom that contribute little to chemically meaningful structural diversity while dramatically increasing computational cost. We present a substructure-based conformational sampling framework that separates flexible side chains from the molecular core at the graph level. Detached substituents are replaced by capped surrogate groups, enabling independent sampling of subsystems and systematic reconstruction of approximate full-molecule ensembles. A limiting variant neglects explicit sampling of the side chains and assumes extended reference conformations. This approximation is rationalized using high-level electronic-structure data for linear alkyl chains, which show that folded conformations become thermodynamically competitive only beyond well-defined lengths, particularly in solution. The approach is implemented within CREST and reduces the effective dimensionality of conformational sampling for molecules with extended flexible substituents.

title: Hierarchy-aware strategy recommendation for emotional support dialogues via hyperbolic representation and conservative offline learning
container-title: Exploration of Digital Health Technologies
db4c17578ba8411b2fd010d5dface4aa0a3742ef.abstract: Aim: Effective emotional support requires selecting support strategies appropriate to the seeker’s state and grounded in counselling theory. We present a computational proof-of-concept that combines hyperbolic representation learning with conservative offline reinforcement learning for support-strategy recommendation. Methods: Support strategies from Hill’s Helping Skills framework are embedded in the Poincaré ball to encode their three-level hierarchy. On this representation, we train Conservative Hyperbolic Implicit Q-Learning (CH-IQL) on the Emotional Support Conversation dataset (ESConv; 1,300 dialogues; 910/195/195 train/validation/test split). All results are reported as mean ± standard deviation over five training seeds. Policy value is measured by independent Fitted Q-Evaluation (FQE) with twin Q-networks, calibrated against the behavior policy’s Monte-Carlo ground truth and an analytic value ceiling, with dialogue-level bootstrap confidence intervals. Strategy appropriateness is additionally assessed by four blinded human raters over 120 stratified test states. Results: Under the stochastic (sampling) deployment, CH-IQL attains an FQE-estimated value of 4.79 ± 0.07 versus 3.66 for the estimated behavior policy—positive under every seed and under two alternative, feedback-anchored reward designs—while its strategy distribution matches the entropy of human supporters (1.98 vs. 1.99) and uses all eight strategies. In blinded pairwise comparison, raters preferred the model’s strategy in 43.9% of disputed cases (95% CI 32.6–55.9%), statistically indistinguishable from the observed supporter behavior. The heuristic reward shows no dialogue-level correlation with seeker-reported outcomes (Spearman ρ = 0.009), which we disclose and address through reward-robustness experiments. Conclusions: The framework improves the specified reward while remaining comparable to observed supporter behavior under expert judgment. These results support offline reinforcement learning with hierarchical representations as a viable strategy-recommendation mechanism, and identify outcome-correlated reward design as the key requirement for progress toward real-world utility. The system is a computational proof-of-concept and is not suitable for clinical deployment.

title: Readiness for digital case-based learning in Community Medicine: a multi- institutional cross-sectional needs assessment of undergraduate medical students in India
616279a19e4b441240fd5b573ec658ee2f0c692e.abstract: Abstract Background Community Medicine asks medical students to reason from an individual case to action at family, community and programme level, but teaching in India still relies heavily on lectures and field visits. Digital case-based learning (DCBL) could give students repeated, structured practice in this kind of reasoning. Learner needs are rarely assessed before such modules are built. We assessed students’ self-rated confidence in clinical reasoning, learning preferences, digital access, barriers and interest in DCBL, and identified factors associated with high interest. Methods We conducted a cross-sectional online survey between 10 July 2025 and 29 June 2026 among undergraduate medical students and interns at five medical colleges in four southern Indian states. The questionnaire combined 5-point ratings, multiple-response items and open questions. High interest (rating 4–5) was modelled using multivariable logistic regression, with an ordinal model as a sensitivity analysis. Free-text responses were analysed using content analysis. Results Of 906 responses, 860 were analysed. Of these, 28.0% rated their confidence in applying clinical reasoning to public-health problems as high; 53.4% chose the midpoint. Students learned best through clinical postings and field visits (64.7%), case-based learning (48.3%) and problem-based learning (43.6%); 30.0% chose classroom lectures. Most used a smartphone or tablet (91.9%). The commonest barriers were lack of motivation (35.1%), lack of internet access (34.5%) and limited time (31.9%). High interest in DCBL was reported by 47.4%, and 41.7% chose the midpoint. High interest was independently associated with higher confidence (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 1.51, 95% CI 1.26–1.81) and higher engagement with current teaching (aOR 1.54, 1.29–1.83). It was less likely with lack of internet access (aOR 0.56, 0.41–0.76) and prior learning with digital cases (aOR 0.71, 0.53–0.95). Students valued realism, interactivity, visuals and anytime access, and most wanted cases on communicable diseases, outbreak investigation and maternal and child health. Conclusions Interest in DCBL was moderate rather than enthusiastic. It followed students’ engagement and confidence rather than prior exposure. DCBL modules for Community Medicine should be realistic, decision-focused and interactive, work on mobile devices and low-bandwidth connections, and be linked to field and classroom teaching. Their design should specifically reach disengaged and less confident learners.

title: When a better future becomes visible: digital twins, normative authority, and care after refusal
1d9e1956886a9a27d498ac3e7667b0539923e8df.abstract: Abstract Simulation-oriented digital twins may enable comparisons of patient-specific health trajectories under alternative treatments or courses of action. Where these representations remain available after a decision, an alternative originally generated to inform choice may later become a reference point for evaluating refusal. This article examines what normative authority an unrealised but medically preferable simulated future should retain when an adverse outcome occurs and the patient requires further care. Through conceptual and normative analysis, it considers cases in which the simulation is sufficiently credible for deliberation and the patient has adequate understanding, decision-making capacity, and a reasonable opportunity to pursue the recommended option. Three connected limits are defended. Epistemic credibility does not by itself determine what the patient ought, all things considered, to choose. Medical preferability does not by itself establish a personal obligation to accept the associated option. Neither the occurrence of an adverse outcome nor the continued visibility of the alternative supplies the normative justification needed to convert refusal into moral failure. Independently justified reassessment remains possible, but retrospective salience cannot substitute for that justification. Continuing care also rests on the patient’s standing as a person entitled to respectful clinical consideration, which is not earned through compliance. Past choices may inform current treatment without alone justifying blame or diminished moral standing. Care should remain responsive to present need, support renewed deliberation, and preserve relevant context without requiring patients to justify themselves as a condition of respect. Digital twins thus illuminate a broader problem concerning how technologically represented futures can inform human agency without becoming authoritative verdicts on past choices or present claims to care.

title: OS IMPACTOS DO ESTELIONATO DIGITAL EM INVESTIMENTOS: A FRAUDE NA VENDA DE AÇÕES FALSAS
container-title: Revista Tópicos
6663316adbfbb099bdef695fe6f6830e5b362bca.abstract: O estelionato digital em investimentos constitui problema jurídico e social relacionado ao uso de tecnologias para induzir investidores em erro, obter vantagem ilícita e provocar prejuízo patrimonial. A expansão das plataformas digitais, redes sociais e aplicativos de mensagens ampliou o acesso ao mercado financeiro, mas também criou novas possibilidades de fraude, como a oferta de ações inexistentes, falsas corretoras e perfis fraudulentos. Este artigo analisa os impactos econômicos e sociais dessas práticas e os instrumentos jurídicos brasileiros aplicáveis ao seu enfrentamento. A pesquisa é qualitativa, exploratória e descritiva, com método dedutivo e procedimentos bibliográfico e documental, baseada em legislação, doutrina e documentos institucionais. Consideram-se o art. 171 do Código Penal, a Lei nº 14.155/2021 e a atuação da CVM e do Banco Central. A análise evidencia que os danos ultrapassam a perda financeira individual, alcançando a confiança dos investidores e a credibilidade das instituições. Conclui-se que a prevenção depende de proteção jurídica, fiscalização, preservação da prova digital, educação financeira e mecanismos de segurança.

title: Addressing the Cognitive Care Gap in Parkinson's Disease through Participatory Co-design of a Digital Neuropsychological Assessment Platform
62dbeb0f8367cfb5f7ba72fb4c63952bc62d52d6.abstract: Abstract Cognitive impairment is a prevalent and clinically significant feature of Parkinson’s disease (PD), although systematic neuropsychological assessment remains inconsistently integrated into movement disorder clinical care. Time constraints, limited neuropsychology workforce capacity, and fragmented data infrastructure impede early identification and longitudinal monitoring of cognitive decline in this population. The ‘PDCogniCare’ program aimed to address this gap by developing best-practice guidelines and a PD-specific neuropsychological toolkit. To implement this program in clinical settings, the PDCogniCare digital platform was co-designed and developed as a web-based tool to improve access to cognitive assessment, support clinician training, competence and confidence, and enable longitudinal tracking of neuropsychological outcomes across Movement disorders and psychology services. A participatory asynchronous co-design methodology was employed across three workshops and an interim system evaluation, across metropolitan health services in Queensland, Australia. Fifteen participants were involved, encompassing all interest holders in the neuropsychological assessment journey. Design activities included journey map refinement, MoSCoW feature prioritisation, low-fidelity prototype development, and iterative platform evaluation. Consumer and caregiver input was integrated throughout. The finalised platform received a mean System Usability Scale score of 82.5, placing it in the excellent range. Participants confirmed broad alignment between the platform and their clinical and lived experience priorities. Remaining concerns, including system integration, client enrolment, clinical pathway gaps, and data governance issues, were identified as priorities for future refinement prior to wider implementation. The findings support participatory co-design as an effective methodology for developing acceptable and clinically grounded digital health tools in neurodegenerative disease contexts.

title: MICROTRANSACTION PADA ROBLOX DAN POLA KONSUMSI DIGITAL GENERASI Z: RELEVANSINYA BAGI LITERASI KEUANGAN DIGITAL DALAM PEMBELAJARAN IPS
container-title: EDUTECH : Jurnal Inovasi Pendidikan Berbantuan Teknologi
a55be9317809d2eb3b49c4f71aa1d6c29efff7fb.abstract: The rapid advancement of digital gaming has established a novel economic sphere integrated into youth lifestyle. Within this gaming environment, users not only play and interact but also execute economic decisions using virtual currency. This study aims to describe microtransaction patterns among Generation Z Roblox users and analyze their relevance to strengthening digital financial literacy in Social Studies education. Employing a descriptive quantitative survey approach, this study involved 48 respondents aged 15–23 who actively play Roblox and have made real-money purchases. The findings reveal that all respondents had microtransaction experience, with 87.5% conducting transactions in the past month primarily to enhance avatar appearances (70.8%) and acquire desired virtual items (58.3%). These findings underscore the pedagogical necessity of embedding digital financial literacy within Social Studies to guide students in distinguishing needs from wants in digital consumption spaces. ABSTRAK Perkembangan permainan digital telah membentuk ruang ekonomi baru yang terintegrasi dengan keseharian generasi muda. Di dalam ekosistem permainan, pengguna tidak hanya berinteraksi dan bermain, tetapi juga mengambil keputusan ekonomi melalui transaksi mata uang virtual. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mendeskripsikan pola microtransaction pada pengguna Roblox dari kelompok Generasi Z serta menganalisis relevansinya bagi penguatan literasi keuangan digital dalam pembelajaran Ilmu Pengetahuan Sosial (IPS). Penelitian ini menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif deskriptif dengan metode survei terhadap 48 responden berusia 15–23 tahun yang aktif bermain Roblox dan pernah melakukan transaksi menggunakan uang riil. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa seluruh responden memiliki pengalaman bertransaksi, dengan 87,5% di antaranya bertransaksi dalam satu bulan terakhir untuk mempercantik avatar (70,8%) dan mengoleksi item virtual (58,3%). Temuan ini memperlihatkan adanya urgensi penguatan literasi keuangan digital dalam pembelajaran IPS guna membimbing peserta didik membedakan kebutuhan dan keinginan dalam ruang konsumsi digital.

title: PERAN ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE DAN INFRASTRUKTUR DIGITAL DALAM MENINGKATKAN KETERLIBATAN AKADEMIK DAN EFEKTIVITAS BELAJAR MAHASISWA
container-title: EDUTECH : Jurnal Inovasi Pendidikan Berbantuan Teknologi
5ea9bceb2f3180b84a5816dcbcff96e3b3f5aa5e.abstract: The increasing integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and digital technologies into higher education has created new opportunities to support the learning process. However, the effectiveness of technology utilization is not solely determined by technical availability, but also by students' active involvement in learning activities. This study aims to analyze the role of AI utilization and digital infrastructure in enhancing learning effectiveness, with student engagement serving as a mediating variable among students at Institut Teknologi Kalimantan. A quantitative survey approach was administered to 347 active students across faculties and cohorts selected through multistage stratified sampling. Data were gathered using a five-point Likert scale questionnaire and analyzed using Partial Least Squares–Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) with a second-order construct through the Hierarchical Component Model. The results demonstrate that AI usage and digital infrastructure exert positive and significant effects on student engagement and learning effectiveness. Furthermore, student engagement partially mediates the effects of AI usage and digital infrastructure on learning effectiveness, with AI usage exhibiting a more dominant total contribution. ABSTRAK Perkembangan Artificial Intelligence (AI) dan teknologi digital telah memberikan peluang baru dalam mendukung proses pembelajaran di perguruan tinggi. Namun, efektivitas pemanfaatan teknologi tidak hanya ditentukan oleh ketersediaan fasilitas semata, melainkan juga oleh keterlibatan aktif mahasiswa dalam proses akademik. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis peran pemanfaatan AI dan infrastruktur digital dalam meningkatkan efektivitas belajar dengan keterlibatan mahasiswa (student engagement) sebagai variabel mediasi pada mahasiswa Institut Teknologi Kalimantan. Pendekatan kuantitatif dengan metode survei diterapkan kepada 347 mahasiswa aktif dari berbagai fakultas dan angkatan yang dipilih melalui teknik multistage stratified sampling. Pengumpulan data menggunakan kuesioner skala Likert lima tingkat dan dianalisis menggunakan Partial Least Squares–Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) dengan model konstruk tingkat kedua melalui Hierarchical Component Model. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa penggunaan AI dan infrastruktur digital berpengaruh positif dan signifikan terhadap keterlibatan mahasiswa serta efektivitas belajar. Selain itu, keterlibatan mahasiswa terbukti memediasi secara parsial pengaruh penggunaan AI dan infrastruktur digital terhadap efektivitas belajar, dengan pemanfaatan AI memberikan kontribusi total yang lebih dominan.

title: Integrasi Teknologi Digital Dalam Pembelajaran Tematik Terpadu Model Webbed Untuk Mengatasi Kesulitan Belajar Siswa Di Sekolah Dasar: Kajian Sistematis
container-title: Citizen : Jurnal Ilmiah Multidisiplin Indonesia
773b16af54743d3b07ae6166c0a3b0ba1f793dd5.abstract: Tujuan – Penelitian ini mensintesis bukti mengenai kesulitan belajar dalam pembelajaran tematik terpadu di sekolah dasar, menelaah penggunaan teknologi digital, dan mengusulkan kerangka integrasinya dalam model Webbed. Desain/metodologi/pendekatan – Kajian literatur sistematis ini dilaporkan mengikuti PRISMA 2020 dan PRISMA-S. Penelusuran laman penerbit dan jurnal pada 25 Oktober 2026 mencakup publikasi periode 2021–2026. Satu penilai menyaring 70 rekaman unik dan menetapkan 13 studi inti: tiga mengenai kesulitan belajar, tujuh mengenai teknologi digital, dan tiga mengenai model Webbed. Penilaian menggunakan daftar periksa adaptasi lima butir, disertai sintesis naratif; 17 sumber tambahan mendukung metode dan teori. Temuan – Kesulitan mencakup pemahaman konsep lintas muatan, keterlibatan dan konsentrasi, serta keterampilan dasar membaca dan berhitung. Teknologi digital menunjukkan hasil menjanjikan terutama pada luaran proksi berupa capaian kognitif dan motivasi. Bukti langsung terbatas pada satu intervensi membaca; sebuah tinjauan mengenai peserta didik penyandang disabilitas menilai bukti yang dikajinya lemah. Tidak ada studi inti yang menguji pembelajaran Webbed berbantuan teknologi digital untuk menangani kesulitan belajar. Keterbatasan penelitian/implikasi – Penelusuran berbasis web, penyaringan oleh satu penilai, dan terbatasnya bukti langsung membatasi kesimpulan. Kerangka usulan memerlukan validasi melalui penelitian berbasis desain, kuasi-eksperimen, atau penelitian tindakan kelas. Implikasi praktis – Guru dapat menggunakan enam tahap, yaitu perencanaan, diagnosis, pembelajaran lintas muatan, penguatan, remedial, dan refleksi, sebagai panduan sementara untuk merancang dan mengevaluasi pembelajaran. Orisinalitas/nilai – Kajian menghubungkan tiga kelompok bukti untuk mengusulkan kerangka pembelajaran Webbed berbantuan teknologi digital yang belum divalidasi. Sintesis menunjukkan kelayakan konseptual tanpa membuktikan efektivitasnya.

title: Peningkatan Kompetensi Digital Guru Melalui Pelatihan Canva Pendidikan Untuk Pengembangan LKPD dan Desain Pembelajaran di SD Negeri 1 Oirata
container-title: Jurnal Masyarakat Madani Indonesia
b55753df5c5f58528343dcea012c7f46f350167a.abstract: Keterbatasan pengalaman guru dalam memanfaatkan teknologi digital menjadi salah satu permasalahan dalam pengembangan bahan ajar di SD Negeri 1 Oirata, Pulau Kisar, Kabupaten Maluku Barat Daya. Meskipun sebagian besar guru telah mengetahui Canva, pemanfaatannya untuk mengembangkan Lembar Kerja Peserta Didik masih terbatas. Kondisi tersebut diperkuat oleh keterbatasan jaringan internet, perangkat digital, dan kesempatan praktik. Kegiatan Pengabdian kepada Masyarakat ini bertujuan meningkatkan pengetahuan dan keterampilan guru dalam memanfaatkan Canva Pendidikan untuk mengembangkan Lembar Kerja Peserta Didik yang sesuai dengan kebutuhan pembelajaran. Kegiatan dilaksanakan menggunakan pendekatan Participatory Action atau Participatory Training melalui delapan tahapan, yaitu identifikasi kebutuhan, persiapan, penyampaian materi, demonstrasi, praktik terbimbing, pengembangan Lembar Kerja Peserta Didik, presentasi dan umpan balik, serta evaluasi. Hasil kegiatan menunjukkan bahwa dari 12 guru yang mengikuti kegiatan, 10 guru atau 83, 3 persen berhasil menghasilkan minimal satu rancangan Lembar Kerja Peserta Didik menggunakan Canva Pendidikan. Guru juga mulai mampu menghubungkan fitur desain dengan kebutuhan pedagogis pembelajaran. Dengan demikian, pelatihan berbasis praktik langsung dapat membangun kompetensi awal guru dalam mengembangkan bahan ajar digital dan perlu dilanjutkan melalui pendampingan serta praktik berkelanjutan.

title:
The Impact of
                    <scp>ESG</scp>
                    Activity on Employees' Psychological Wellbeing and Intention to Participate: The Mediating Effect of Authenticity, Organizational Trust, and Identification
container-title: Corporate Social Responsibility and Environmental Management
e23fd7225a6af7346f4aacf2308461e765cad0af.abstract: ABSTRACT This study examines how employees' recognition of environmental, social, and governance (ESG) activities affects their psychological well‐being and participation intention in ESG initiatives, focusing on the mediating roles of authenticity, organizational trust, and identification. Using survey data from 358 Korean employees in the financial industry, structural equation modeling was employed to test the hypotheses. The results revealed that ESG authenticity fully mediated the relationship between ESG recognition and organizational trust and identification, which subsequently enhanced employees' psychological well‐being and intention to engage in ESG programs. Organizational identification and trust were found to be key mechanisms through which authentic ESG initiatives contribute to positive employee outcomes. These findings underscore that employees' perceptions of the sincerity and integrity of ESG efforts are more influential than mere recognition of such activities. This study contributes to the literature on micro‐level ESG impacts by clarifying the psychological processes linking ESG perceptions to employee attitudes and behaviors.

title: Complex System Perspectives on Learning in Networked Digital Communities
container-title: Systems Research and Behavioral Science
05b6334ff70bc095c8e9882efeabb6906a6e4c93.abstract: ABSTRACT In the rapidly evolving digital landscape, learning is increasingly understood as a complex adaptive system shaped by nonlinear interactions among cognitive, social and technological agents. Despite the fact that data‐driven and AI‐enhanced approaches have led to an increase in the capacity to model this complexity, there remains a paucity of theoretical integration with the learning sciences, resulting in a fragmentation of interpretations of learning dynamics. The present study proposes a networked complex learning model that unites complex systems theory, the connectivity paradigm and digital learning ecologies to advance a systemic understanding of learning. The present study employs a bibliometric analysis of publications indexed in the Web of Science (2000–2025) to apply co‐word, co‐citation and thematic mapping techniques within the Bibliometrix (R‐Biblioshiny) framework, in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta‐Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines for transparency and methodological rigour. The results indicate an exponential increase in research activity after 2018, which is indicative of theoretical expansion towards systemic, emergent and connective models of learning. Thematic mapping reveals global clustering around AI‐mediated and network‐based approaches, while ethical and conceptual integration remains underdeveloped. The study concludes that combining complex systems theory with data‐intensive modelling offers a holistic, adaptive and ethically responsive framework for understanding learning as a dynamic behavioural system in digital environments.

title: User Engagement with Clinician-Developed Guided Meditations on a Global Digital Platform: A Multi-Method Study
container-title: Journal of Technology in Behavioral Science
31a91fde3e4c41a72dfd88c261ec113df9cc1df8.abstract: Abstract Digital meditation applications are increasingly used to support stress management, emotional balance, and everyday coping among individuals seeking accessible mental health and wellness resources. At the same time, less is known about how people engage with and experience clinician-developed guided meditation content on large global wellness platforms outside of formal research settings. This multi-method study examined user engagement and user-reported experiences associated with a series of clinician-developed guided meditations delivered through a single clinician-developed Insight Timer account. Quantitative descriptive analyses were conducted using platform analytics, including total plays (N = 6,688 since February 2025), follower activity, and available geographic information for followers and commenters. In addition, 59 publicly available user comments were extracted; 29 comments met the inclusion criteria and were analyzed using reflexive thematic analysis. Descriptive findings indicated ongoing listener interaction through plays, follows, and written commentary, while available geographic information for followers and commenters indicated engagement across multiple regions. Qualitative analysis identified four primary themes in commenters’ descriptions of their experiences with the recordings: emotional regulation and nervous system calming, perceived psychological safety, integration into daily coping routines, and the therapeutic qualities of the audio environment. Listener comments frequently described feelings of relaxation, reassurance, and emotional support while engaging with the meditation content. Grounded in a health psychology framework, this study provides practice-informed observational evidence regarding how a self-selected subset of users described experiencing clinician-developed guided meditations in a real-world digital environment. These findings contribute to the growing literature on digital mental health by providing insight into how clinician-developed digital mindfulness resources are voluntarily integrated into everyday coping and wellness practices outside formal clinical settings. As digital mental health continues to evolve, understanding naturally occurring patterns of user engagement may help guide future observational and intervention-based research and support the development of accessible, evidence-informed digital resources that complement traditional models of behavioral health care.

title: Adaptive Weighted Ensemble of CNN Models with Focal Loss and Grad-CAM Explainability for Skin Lesion Classification
e1ca9d2b5792a5d5e968c74110c26de09eac5886.abstract: Abstract Skin cancer is one of the oldest and most widespread forms of cancer globally, and discovering it early is crucial for improving patient outcomes. Traditional diagnosis heavily depends on experience, which may be time-consuming and human-scheduled. Recent developments in algorithms for deep learning, particularly convolutional neural networks (CNNs), provide promising platforms for independent image analysis, but individual models are prone to fail with unstable predictions and weak generalizability. In this research, we have worked with a weighted ensemble transfer learning framework that integrates ResNet34, ResNet50 and EfficientNet-B0 to enhance the utilization of the HAM10000 dataset to sort skin lesions. Each model is individually finetuned. And Ensemble weights are assigned according to validation performance. That ensures a stronger network and a stronger influence on the final prediction at the end. Additionally, Grad-CAM visualisation helps to show where lesions are located. It also confirms that the ensemble focuses on the area that matters clinically. Our tests show that the weighted ensemble method outperforms single CNNs in accuracy and F1 score. It also gives a better understanding and is more dependable. These results show that pairing adaptive weighting with visual details produces a more reliable and clear way of automatically detecting skin cancer for clinics.

title: TECHNOLOGY, REGULATION, AND THE DIVERGENT TRAJECTORIES OF RETAIL AND CROSS-BORDER CENTRAL BANK DIGITAL CURRENCY
container-title: DIVERSITY Logic Journal Multidisciplinary
ef739792b3e100b84efec8eaca6b5bf14607aae0.abstract: Background. Central bank digital currency (CBDC) sits where fast-moving cryptographic and ledger technology meets fast-moving regulation, yet the two are usually studied separately, and retail and cross-border uses are usually treated as one object. Between 2024 and 2026 major jurisdictions made sharply different regulatory choices. Research Purpose. This review examines how advanced cryptographic solutions and hybrid blockchain architectures interact with evolving regulatory frameworks to shape economic outcomes and user adoption, and how that interaction differs between retail and cross-border implementations. Research Method. We conduct a critical review. A Scopus search on 8 October 2026 (1,418 records, 1,045 retained) maps the field, and a purposive selection of peer-reviewed studies and official publications is synthesised around four research questions. Findings. Technology and regulation terms co-occur at about the level expected by chance, and evidence on cryptographic feasibility and on adoption comes largely from separate literatures. Hybrid, two-tier architectures dominate, and the tension between privacy and anti-money laundering is increasingly handled through cryptographic design. Retail adoption is weak in every live system reviewed, while wholesale cross-border arrangements show the clearest technological value but are limited by governance. Regulatory choices since 2024 now shape outcomes more than technical feasibility does. Conclusion. Technology and regulation co-evolve, and retail and cross-border CBDC face different binding constraints. We offer a co-evolution framework with four falsifiable propositions and argue that CBDC should be studied together with regulated stablecoins and tokenised deposits. Keywords: central bank digital currency, privacy-enhancing technologies, distributed ledger technology, cross-border payments, financial regulation.

title: Digital operational excellence in retail: a systematic review and dynamic causal framework
container-title: The TQM Journal
e0991833c2cbf27db04aaa0c679cccb54a595d69.abstract: Purpose This study examines how digital technologies integrate with Operational Excellence (OpEx) routines, including Lean Six Sigma, in retail, identifying responsive processes, benefits, evolving KPIs, enablers, barriers, and mitigation strategies, and developing a retail-specific dynamic causal framework. Design/methodology/approach A systematic literature review and bibliometric analysis of 58 peer-reviewed articles from Q1/Q2 journals (2016–2026), following PRISMA guidelines, combined publication mapping, full-text coding, and narrative synthesis to conceptualize Digital-OpEx integration in retail. Findings Digital-OpEx is most evident in inventory, warehousing, logistics, and e-commerce. Digital technologies provide visibility, prediction, and traceability, while OpEx routines provide standardization and continuous-improvement discipline, with implications for customer experience and revenue. KPIs shift from retrospective to real-time, predictive, system-integrated indicators. Adoption depends on digital infrastructure, leadership commitment, employee capabilities, data availability, and system integration; financial, technical, organizational, and ethical barriers persist, though phased rollout and pilot testing aid implementation. Practical implications The framework helps retail managers prioritize high-responsiveness processes, align OpEx routines with digital technologies, build implementation readiness, deploy real-time indicators, and apply barrier-mitigation strategies to sustain performance. Social implications Digital-OpEx also raises workforce, data-privacy, customer-trust, accessibility, and environmental considerations that should inform investment decisions from the outset. Originality/value To the authors' knowledge, this is the first study combining a systematic review and bibliometric analysis of Digital-OpEx specifically in retail, advancing a retail-specific framework and proposing testable propositions for future empirical research.

title:
Unpacking the Governance Innovation Nexus: How Board Characteristics Drive Sustainable Innovation Through Digital Capability in Emerging
                    <scp>BRI</scp>
                    Economies
container-title: Business Strategy & Development
6c05871b510ea05734befeed7681f1e2f9d7e686.abstract: ABSTRACT As global sustainability pressures intensify, firms in emerging economies, particularly those operating within Belt and Road Initiative (BRI) countries, face growing expectations to improve environmental responsibility while navigating complex and volatile institutional contexts. In this context, board‐level corporate governance plays a critical role in shaping firms' commitment to responsible innovation and environmental performance. This study examines how board‐level strategic governance influences sustainable innovation among manufacturing firms in BRI economies, with particular attention to the mediating role of digital innovation capacity and the moderating effect of board ability. Using a panel dataset of 496 firms covering 2013–2023, the study applies dynamic panel and instrumental‐variable estimation techniques to address potential endogeneity and strengthen the robustness of the empirical findings. The results indicate that governance mechanisms associated with inclusiveness and accountability, particularly gender‐diverse boards, performance‐based incentives, and board ownership, positively influence sustainable innovation. In contrast, larger boards and longer director tenures are associated with weaker sustainable innovation outcomes. Digital innovation capacity emerges as an important mediating mechanism through which board‐level governance contributes to sustainable innovation. At the same time, board ability directly enhances sustainable innovation and strengthens the effectiveness of governance mechanisms. By focusing on five MENA BRI economies, the study provides context‐specific evidence on governance and sustainability in emerging and transition economies. The findings contribute to the corporate governance, corporate social responsibility, and environmental management literature and offer practical implications for firms and policymakers seeking governance reforms that support innovation‐driven sustainability transitions.

title: Leveraging Digital Innovation for Entrepreneurial Resource Deployment: The Case of Sholapith Craft Artisans of Murshidabad, West Bengal
container-title: South Asian Journal of Business and Management Cases
c1808cab1d068e370ee2728f5fa0074560508909.abstract: The present qualitative single-case study investigates how the cultural resources inherited by the artisans of the Sholapith community in Kandi municipality, Murshidabad (West Bengal), are used in the context of new digital practices. The fieldwork was carried out from February 2025 to September 2025 and included two focus group discussions, ten semi-structured interviews, one key-informant interview, non-participant observation and a documentary and social-media review, with a total of twenty-one unique artisan participants. Gioia-inspired abductive coding was used to analyse the data, and the resource-based view and the VRIO (Value, Rarity, Imitability and Organization) framework were used as sensitizing analytical concepts. The results indicate that tacit craftsmanship, ritual symbolism and identity are valuable, relatively scarce and difficult-to-imitate resources because they depend on tacit learning, historical embeddedness and community legitimacy, while place-bound material knowledge and community-specific design provide qualified and context-dependent resource advantages. Notwithstanding, the lack of coordination, dependence, low digital literacy, infrastructure limitations and financial exclusion limit value capture. The organization dimension is partially reinforced by the development of rudimentary marketing, transaction and knowledge-sharing routines through social-media storytelling, direct-to-consumer selling and digital payments and peer-assisted learning, but these are not yet a source of sustained competitive advantage. The study builds on VRIO by conceptualizing organization as an emergent collective capability, not a formal structure, and draws implications for artisan communities, development practitioners and development policy.

title: Information Disclosure Transformation in the Digital Economy: The Role of Digital Infrastructure in Visual Disclosure
container-title: Accounting & Finance
cef22ac94baf1d427abf31c1c415d80f05b03bca.abstract: ABSTRACT We investigate how digital infrastructure development affects corporate visual disclosure, distinguishing between discretionary image‐based formats and structured table‐based formats. Using data on Chinese A‐share‐listed firms from 2009 to 2022, we find that improvements in digital infrastructure are associated with greater use of image‐based visual disclosure in annual reports, whereas we detect no statistically significant association with table‐based visual disclosure. Mechanism analyses show that this relationship is driven by both supply‐side enhancements in firms' organizational capabilities and demand‐side incentives to cater to external users' information‐processing demands, as evidenced by stronger effects among firms with more extensive explicit discussions of digital transformation in their MD&A and higher institutional ownership. We also find that this effect is more pronounced in regions with higher levels of AI computing power development, as well as among firms with a lower propensity for earnings manipulation and fewer financing constraints. This paper expands the theoretical framework for understanding changes in corporate disclosure formats in the digital economy and offers implications for policymakers, investors and firms.

title: PENERAPAN SISTEM AKUNTANSI DIGITAL TERHADAP EFISIENSI DAN KUALITAS LAPORAN KEUANGAN PADA UMKM MIE AYAM DAN BAKSO NGASINAN GRESIK
container-title: SOCIAL : Jurnal Inovasi Pendidikan IPS
b1bf58f60bec951d01ab49effb7ff79e7ca5665b.abstract: Micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs) serve as a strategic pillar supporting national economic resilience in Indonesia. The implementation of digital accounting systems has become an essential necessity to optimize operational performance through structured and automated transaction recording. This study aims to analyze the implementation of the SI APIK digital accounting application and its impact on operational efficiency and the quality of financial statements at Mie Ayam and Bakso Ngasinan MSME in Gresik Regency. The research employed a qualitative descriptive approach with a case study design, gathering data through participatory observation, documentation, and in-depth interviews with the business owner. Data were analyzed interactively through data reduction, data display, and conclusion drawing, validated via source and technique triangulation. The findings demonstrate that the implementation of SI APIK significantly shortens daily bookkeeping duration, eliminates manual calculation errors, and produces financial statements that are relevant, reliable, and compliant with SAK EMKM. Consequently, the digital accounting transformation effectively enhances financial information accountability for sound managerial decision-making. ABSTRAK Usaha mikro, kecil, dan menengah (UMKM) merupakan pilar strategis dalam menopang ketahanan ekonomi nasional di Indonesia. Penerapan sistem akuntansi digital menjadi kebutuhan esensial untuk mengoptimalkan kinerja operasional melalui pencatatan transaksi yang terstruktur dan terotomatisasi. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis penerapan sistem akuntansi digital berbasis aplikasi SI APIK serta dampaknya terhadap efisiensi kerja dan kualitas laporan keuangan pada UMKM Mie Ayam dan Bakso Ngasinan di Kabupaten Gresik. Metode penelitian menggunakan pendekatan kualitatif deskriptif dengan rancangan studi kasus (case study), di mana data dihimpun melalui observasi partisipatif, dokumentasi, dan wawancara mendalam bersama pemilik usaha. Analisis data dilakukan secara interaktif melalui reduksi data, penyajian data, dan penarikan kesimpulan dengan uji keabsahan melalui triangulasi sumber dan teknik. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa implementasi SI APIK memangkas durasi pembukuan harian, mengeliminasi risiko galat hitung manual, serta menghasilkan laporan keuangan yang relevan, andal, dan patuh terhadap SAK EMKM. Dengan demikian, transformasi pembukuan digital terbukti meningkatkan akuntabilitas informasi keuangan yang dapat diandalkan sebagai dasar pengambilan keputusan manajerial.

title:
<scp>Rep2Rep</scp>
                    ‐Shuffle: Shuffled Repetition‐to‐Repetition Learning for Noise‐Adaptive Self‐Supervised
                    <scp>MRI</scp>
                    Denoising
container-title: Magnetic Resonance in Medicine
4e85bfcc2f091be750db73ad20fa07636dfa23d2.abstract: ABSTRACT Purpose MRI applications with low SNR, such as non‐proton imaging and low‐field imaging, often require multiple signal averages to achieve adequate image quality at the cost of longer scan times. This work proposes Rep2Rep‐Shuffle, a self‐supervised learning framework that improves MRI denoising performance in repeated‐acquisition imaging with limited training datasets. Methods Rep2Rep‐Shuffle extends our previously proposed repetition‐to‐repetition learning (Rep2Rep)‐based self‐supervised denoising approach with a new shuffled repetition pairing strategy. Instead of using a fixed split between training input and target repetitions, different repetition combinations are randomly generated during training epochs for each dataset, which increases the effective training space when training datasets are limited. In addition, the framework also extends from slice‐wise 2D to 3D denoising by exploiting correlations across all spatial dimensions. The proposed method was tested in vivo using sodium MRI and further validated using synthetic noisy MRI datasets. Different training strategies for both 2D and 3D denoising were compared. Results In vivo sodium MRI results demonstrated improved denoising and better preservation of anatomical structures with 3D Rep2Rep‐Shuffle compared with fixed pairing (Rep2Rep) and 2D denoising. Reader evaluation further confirmed that 3D Rep2Rep‐Shuffle received higher scores for different assessment categories. In synthetic experiments, 3D Rep2Rep‐Shuffle achieved the best performance among self‐supervised methods and approached the performance of supervised learning. Conclusion Rep2Rep‐Shuffle outperforms Rep2Rep for MRI denoising by increasing training diversity through shuffled repetition pairing and by leveraging volumetric spatial correlations. The method is particularly suited for low‐SNR MRI applications that acquire multiple repetitions but have limited training datasets.

title: Digital Divide and Institutional Communication: Telecommunications Infrastructure Barriers to Transparency and Citizen Participation in Rural Areas of Ecuador
container-title: Studies in Media and Communication
2a678942fef1914b47fef24cb936508c972c009a.abstract: Government transparency and digital citizen participation in Latin America are conditioned by the available telecommunications infrastructure, particularly in rural areas of the region. This narrative review, with a systematic search, analyzes the telecommunications infrastructure barriers to providing broadband Internet access, which limit institutional communication aimed at transparency and citizen participation in rural areas of Ecuador, with a Latin American scope. A search was conducted in Scopus, Web of Science (WoS), SciELO, Redalyc, and Google Scholar (2020–2025) following the PRISMA 2020 guidelines for transparency in the selection process. From an initial 326 records, 20 studies that met the inclusion criteria were selected for this review. The results show a 36-percentage-point urban-rural gap in meaningful connectivity in the region; in Ecuador, only 20% of the rural population has access to effective broadband internet service, while 61% of national connections are concentrated in the provinces of Guayas and Pichincha. A regulatory paradox is identified: the Organic Law on Transparency and Access to Public Information (LOTAIP) requires digital transparency in territories lacking the infrastructure to support it. An interdisciplinary framework is proposed that articulates technical telecommunications parameters with dimensions of institutional communication as a tool to guide public policies for effective digital inclusion.

title: Peer Review Report For: Digital I&C System Modernization in the U.S.: Drivers, Barriers, Strategies, and Benefits [version 3; peer review: 1 approved, 1 approved with reservations]
Participation Without Adaptive Preferences
container-title: Journal of Social Philosophy
44244412542ee5db9554d65491b933899e66ac04.abstract: ABSTRACT Feminism opposes the unjust inequality and subjugation of women. Core feminist projects morally critique people, institutions, social practices, norms, and behaviors that contribute to or constitute the subordination of women. But such projects confront individual women and groups of women who participate in and endorse the practices being critiqued. A common response to this tension is to posit adaptive preferences in the form of “deformed desires” among participating women. But a standing alternative holds that participating women engage in trade‐offs among goods in nonideal situations. Here, I extend this “tradeoffs” alternative by arguing that simple ideas from game‐theoretic models support the possibility of trade‐off explanations that respect and illuminate the agency of participating women while allowing for feminist critique. And trade‐off accounts can avoid substantive assumptions regarding human flourishing or the nature of the good. Both features make trade‐off accounts normatively preferable to adaptive preference accounts of participation in unjust social arrangements.

title: Exploring the feasibility of evaluating workplace health and wellbeing initiatives that are free at the point of use for workplaces (WHISPAs)
764323f86c127012e70acf02c7310579d17773bd.abstract: Abstract Background Workplace health and wellbeing initiatives that are free at the point of use for employers (WHISPAs) are increasingly used to improve employee health and reduce health inequalities. Despite investment in workplace health programmes, evidence of effectiveness remains limited, and there is little consensus on how to evaluate these initiatives. This study explored stakeholder perspectives on the feasibility and design of future evaluations of WHISPAs across the UK. Methods A qualitative study used semi-structured online interviews with stakeholders involved in the development, delivery, commissioning and evaluation of WHISPAs. Participants were recruited through a national WHISPA network. Interviews were conducted between March and April 2024, transcribed verbatim and analysed using framework analysis informed by current guidance for evaluating complex interventions. Results Sixteen stakeholders participated. Five overarching themes were identified: support for evaluation; practical barriers to implementation and evaluation; outcomes for employers, employees and providers; workplace culture; and socio-economic inequalities. Participants supported mixed-methods evaluations and valued qualitative evidence alongside quantitative outcomes. Recruitment of employers and employees, particularly within small businesses and routine/manual occupations, was considered challenging. Standardised organisational outcomes, such as sickness absence and staff turnover, were viewed as important but difficult to measure consistently. Stakeholders highlighted workplace culture as a key determinant of intervention success and expressed concern that workplace health initiatives may inadvertently widen inequalities by preferentially engaging more advantaged organisations and workers. Conclusions Stakeholders considered evaluation of WHISPAs necessary but highlighted methodological and practical challenges. Future evaluations should use mixed-methods designs, equity-focused recruitment strategies, and account for organisational context and workplace culture. Developing robust evaluation frameworks is essential to strengthen the evidence base for workplace health interventions and support equitable implementation. These findings have informed the development of a new NIHR-funded workplace health evaluation, including outcome selection, evaluation methods and strategies to address equity and implementation challenges.

title: The cognitive–digital pathway to sustainable entrepreneurship: examining entrepreneurial mindfulness, digital adaptability and sustainable growth aspirations
container-title: Management & Sustainability: An Arab Review
d952b9a015248a60c1ea53a3e716529ca5d832bd.abstract: Purpose This study examines how entrepreneurial mindfulness and digital adaptability capability jointly influence opportunity recognition and sustainable growth aspirations. Grounded in Cognitive Appraisal Theory and Dynamic Capabilities Theory, it explores how entrepreneurs' cognitive awareness and adaptive digital capabilities interact to shape long-term growth aspirations in increasingly uncertain and digitally evolving business environments. Design/methodology/approach This study employed a quantitative cross-sectional design using survey data from 238 respondents (N = 238) engaged in digitally enabled entrepreneurial activities. Established measurement scales were used to measure the study constructs, and the hypothesized relationships were analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling. Findings The findings indicate that all hypotheses were supported. Entrepreneurial Mindfulness significantly influenced Opportunity Recognition (β = 0.566, t = 4.609, p &lt; 0.001) and Sustainable Growth Aspiration (β = 0.400, t = 5.363, p &lt; 0.001). Digital Adaptability Capability positively influenced Opportunity Recognition (β = 0.334, t = 2.560, p = 0.010) and Sustainable Growth Aspiration (β = 0.299, t = 3.689, p &lt; 0.001). Opportunity Recognition also positively affected Sustainable Growth Aspiration (β = 0.317, t = 4.744, p &lt; 0.001). Research limitations/implications The cross-sectional design limits causal inference, while the use of self-reported data and a sample of digitally active entrepreneurs in Indonesia may constrain generalizability. Future research should employ longitudinal or multi-source designs and examine the proposed relationships across diverse national and digital contexts. Practical implications The findings emphasize that sustainable entrepreneurial growth requires the simultaneous development of cognitive and digital capabilities. Entrepreneurship education, incubators, and business support programs should therefore integrate mindfulness-based decision-making with digital capability development to strengthen opportunity recognition, strategic adaptability, and long-term business sustainability. Originality/value This study provides a conceptually integrated perspective on sustainable entrepreneurial growth by examining the complementary roles of entrepreneurial mindfulness and digital adaptability capability through opportunity recognition. Rather than introducing a new theoretical model, it extends existing entrepreneurship literature by demonstrating how Cognitive Appraisal Theory and Dynamic Capabilities Theory can be jointly applied to explain the cognitive and technological foundations of entrepreneurs' sustainable growth aspirations in digitally transforming business contexts.

title: Self-Evolving Laboratories Through Persistent Digital and Physical Adaptation
721251dc9ea74a94f1d7d4cea797349a941a4398.abstract: Turning a scientific idea into an experiment often requires researchers to build, configure and repeatedly adapt the laboratory around it. This work demands resources and specialized expertise that can place ambitious experiments beyond reach. Here we introduce a self-evolving laboratory framework that connects computation, physical experiments and AI models through persistent cycles of observation and revision. GPT Astra uses camera observations and physical feedback to adapt robotic actions, digital twins and CAD designs. These changes are retained as reusable skills and infrastructure, allowing the laboratory to develop alongside its scientific tasks. In a fume-hood prototype, GPT Astra identified the need for a beaker holder and storage stand and generated successive designs for on-demand 3D printing. Four holder generations and two stand generations culminated in parts integrated into the robotic workflow with operator assistance. A photoresist campaign proposed by Raven connects this platform to materials fabrication. Exposure to a 405 nm continuous-wave laser in the two-photon polymerization setup produced circular features that survived development; optical microscopy and reduced acrylate-band absorbance in ATR–FTIR support polymerization and qualitative double-bond conversion. An accompanying evaluation protocol relates the retention and transfer of capabilities to the time, cost and expertise needed to establish them. By making laboratory capabilities reusable and adaptable, this approach offers a path towards broader participation in experimental science, empowering researchers to build and extend the tools their ideas require. Project website: https://ai4ssi.github.io/self-evolving-superintelligence-lab/.
