title: Performing to the void: Rock musicians’ experiences of digital liveness in online streaming concerts
container-title: Convergence: The International Journal of Research into New Media Technologies
7beb8bc27bbb74b14bcbbf483c13a5ed8ec526d6.abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic forced live music onto digital platforms, disrupting liveness – the shared, real-time experience between performers and audiences. While research on digitally mediated concerts has examined audience experience and platform affordances, the perspective of performers, who must actively produce liveness, remains comparatively underexamined in English-language media and performance scholarship. This study examines how rock musicians construct digital liveness in online streaming concerts, drawing on focus group and in-depth interviews with 30 Korean rock band performers (6–47 years of experience) and one concert producer. Focusing on the three components of liveness in which performer agency is most directly implicated – audience interaction, temporality, and role reversal – the study finds that digital liveness did not arise from technological affordance alone. Rather, it was produced through performer conscious participation : the deliberate perceptual and emotional work of constituting an absent audience as co-present. The liveness so produced remained partial, fragile, and materially distinct from venue-based liveness, yet it converted mere transmission into performance. These findings extend Auslander’s theory of digital liveness through a triangular model in which technological affordance, audience wilful participation, and performer conscious participation jointly constitute digital liveness. The forms this participation took reflect the resource constraints of independent music production under pandemic conditions.

title: Digital Phenotyping and Digital Interventions in Adolescent and Young Adult Cancer Survivors Long-Term Follow-up: A Scoping Review (Preprint)
e8ca6ff151fdcc09cd7be70c7a3f22d865de5ca9.abstract: BACKGROUND As survival after adolescent and young adult (AYA) cancer continues to improve, follow-up care needs to address late effects, psychosocial challenges, and quality-of-life impacts after treatment. Conventional follow-up models remain largely episodic and may miss fluctuations in symptoms, functioning, and everyday well-being. Digital phenotyping can capture real-world health-related patterns through smartphones, wearables, apps, sensors, and patient-generated health data, while digital interventions can translate these data into feedback, self-management support, behavioral or psychosocial intervention content. However, how these approaches are used in AYA survivorship follow-up, and which user-oriented factors facilitate or limit their adoption and sustained use, remains fragmented. OBJECTIVE This scoping review aimed to map user-oriented evidence on digital phenotyping and digital interventions in post-treatment AYA cancer survivorship follow-up, focusing on technologies, support strategies, and the facilitators and barriers influencing adoption and use. To our knowledge, this is the first review to examine digital phenotyping and digital interventions together in post-treatment AYA cancer follow-up from a user-oriented perspective. METHODS The review followed PRISMA-ScR guidance. Searches were conducted in PubMed, Web of Science, Scopus, and PsycNet, with SciSpace as a supplementary AI-assisted discovery tool. Peer-reviewed English-language publications from 2020 to early 2026 were eligible when they focused on AYA cancer survivors, digital phenotyping or digital interventions, and user-oriented outcomes. Data were extracted using structured tables and synthesized thematically. RESULTS Sixteen publications were included. Digital follow-up was organized through complementary support strategies: adaptive goal setting, tailored feedback, personalized coaching, peer or social connectivity, and clinical integration. No publication relied on passive sensing alone. Collected data were mainly used for self-monitoring, less often to adapt goals, feedback, or risk information, and rarely connected to clinical follow-up. Wearable data supported mainly physical activity, while psychosocial and sleep support relied more on self-report and human interaction. Seventy-seven facilitator examples were grouped into 11 themes, most frequently engagement, social support integration, personalization and adaptive design, user experience, and benefits. Barriers were most frequently related to personalization and adaptive design, engagement, timing of activities, and technical support or issues. CONCLUSIONS Digital follow-up in AYA cancer survivorship is developing from isolated monitoring or intervention components toward service processes that connect monitored information with feedback, self-management support, and follow-up care where available. Acceptable digital support depends on manageable engagement, personalization, relational support, visible benefit, usable and accessible interaction, technical reliability, and clear privacy and data-control conditions. These facilitators and barriers can be translated into requirement areas, specified through stakeholder elicitation and co-design, and used to evaluate digital follow-up systems in practice.

title: The dark side of digital distraction: supervisor phubbing and employee performance – the indirect roles of cyberloafing and social distance
container-title: Leadership & Organization Development Journal
cb3a0421c9f2f76f5b73dd0ceb8a9475f5953d1d.abstract: Purpose Supervisor phubbing occurs when supervisors use their mobile devices during face-to-face interactions with subordinates. Despite the increasing prevalence of smartphones in the workplace and the importance of supervisor–employee interactions, limited research has examined how supervisor phubbing is associated with key employee outcomes. This study examines the relationship between supervisor phubbing and employee performance and estimates two theoretically specified indirect associations, one through employee cyberloafing and the other through perceived social distance. Design/methodology/approach Data were collected from 965 employees working in Egyptian travel agencies and tour operators. The hypothesized associations were estimated using structural equation modeling. Findings The estimated coefficients linked higher supervisor phubbing with lower employee performance, greater employee cyberloafing and wider perceived social distance. Both proposed mediators yielded statistically significant negative indirect associations; the supervisor phubbing–employee performance coefficient remained significant after their simultaneous inclusion, a pattern consistent with complementary partial mediation in statistical terms. Originality/value This study is among the few to employ social exchange theory to interpret the relationships among supervisor phubbing, employee performance, employee cyberloafing and social distance. It extends the literature by bringing a behavioral response and a relational perception into a single empirical model while providing evidence from the Egyptian tourism industry. The resulting pattern offers theoretical and practical insight into the relationship between supervisory digital distraction and employee performance while underscoring the managerial relevance of attentive communication in service-oriented organizations.

title: Cancer Patients' Preferences for Home-Based Digital Health Services: A Scoping Review (Preprint)
86b4b917a0240e44378c93b927b46a8e0c51e298.abstract: BACKGROUND Advances in cancer treatment have steadily increased the number of people living with cancer, and home-based digital health services are increasingly proposed to deliver continuous, personalised support beyond the hospital. However, digital health products are iterating rapidly and proliferating in type, and many such services are designed around technological feasibility rather than patients’ own preferences, and the evidence on what cancer patients actually want from these services has not been systematically mapped. OBJECTIVE To synthesise the available evidence on cancer patients’ preferences for home-based digital health services, with particular attention to study characteristics, the methods used to elicit preferences, and facilitators of and barriers to acceptance. METHODS This scoping review was conducted in accordance with the PRISMA extension for Scoping Reviews. Eight databases (PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, Scopus, CINAHL, the Cochrane Library, Ovid including PsycINFO, and EBSCOhost) were searched from inception to October 10, 2026. Quantitative, qualitative, and mixed-methods studies reporting cancer patients’ preferences for home-based digital health services were eligible. Data were charted and synthesised narratively. RESULTS Thirteen studies published between 2022 and 2026 were included, conducted in China (n = 5), the United States (n = 3), the Netherlands (n = 2), and Iran, Canada, and Saudi Arabia (n = 1 each). Sample sizes ranged from 8 to 2,459 participants. Across the included studies, cancer patients consistently preferred services offering emotional support, convenience, personalisation, and immediate access; instructional videos were preferred over text-based messages, and personalised online support was preferred over generic supportive messages. The most frequently reported barriers were a preference for face-to-face care, privacy concerns, low eHealth literacy, technical difficulties, and constant illness reminders, whereas convenience, emotional support, personalisation, and time savings were the most frequently reported facilitators. Only two studies employed discrete choice experiments. CONCLUSIONS Current evidence is limited in volume and geographic scope and is dominated by descriptive qualitative designs. Future studies applying theory-grounded preference-elicitation methods—including, but not limited to, discrete choice experiments—in more diverse cancer populations are needed to quantify patients’ preferences for the attributes of home-based digital health services and to guide patient-centred service development. CLINICALTRIAL The review protocol was preregistered on the Open Science Framework (OSF; DOI: 10.17605/OSF.IO/J6XPY).

title: Digital behavioural data should inform mental health screening
container-title: BJPsych Bulletin
4e6f96174cdd42ec9dc779ea79744db452ec8187.abstract: Summary Digital behavioural data from smartphones, wearables and artificial intelligence-enabled systems are increasingly available alongside mental health screening questionnaires. However, there is limited guidance on when such signals are appropriate for mental health screening contexts and how they should be interpreted without overreach into diagnosis. We outline four principles (detectable change, context, informing timing and sustained utility) to guide how digital data can inform interpretation and follow-up while preserving the role of validated screening instruments.

title: Digital borders, algorithmic governance and civic digital literacy: examining the educational implications of AI-driven immigration management in post-apartheid South Africa
container-title: Frontiers in Education
59b10eecd73e3fe9d4e78423b54be93163ff24c2.abstract: Introduction South Africa is moving towards AI-based digital border management, including biometric screening, drone-supported aerial surveillance and the Electronic Travel Authorisation (ETA) system. This paper explores the educational consequences of that shift, with a special focus on the civic digital literacy that algorithmic immigration governance requires of citizens, policymakers and educators. Methods The study takes a qualitative, interpretive approach, drawing on critical digital pedagogy, algorithmic accountability theory and postcolonial education studies. It synthesises peer-reviewed scholarly works, policy documents and grey literature on the Border Management Authority's use of biometric surveillance, drone technology and the ETA system. A corpus of 53 sources was screened through an adapted PRISMA-style procedure and analysed through a three-phase thematic synthesis that produced five descriptive and three analytical themes. Results AI-based border governance exposes a pressing and largely ignored digital literacy gap. The communities most affected by algorithmic immigration decisions are those without the conceptual tools to engage with, debate or take part in the governance of the AI systems that regulate their lives and rights. Standard digital literacy programmes are not sufficient to equip learners with the knowledge to participate in the governance of algorithmically driven systems. Discussion Geography and social sciences education has a special role in equipping learners with the skills needed for critical AI citizenship. The study proposes that algorithmic governance be incorporated into the school curriculum, that community-facing digital civic education programmes be developed, and that participatory AI accountability structures be established in border management. The study advances digital learning innovation by theorising civic AI literacy as a new educational priority in the Global South and by showing that algorithmic governance necessitates a fundamental redefinition of digital citizenship education.

title: Mapping digital health intervention components to Bandura’s sources of self-efficacy in cancer care: a scoping review
container-title: Frontiers in Psychology
44d89f3d94caef5f5c8ecc054df1d492f10f6695.abstract: Background Digital health technologies are increasingly used for symptom management, patient education, and continuity of care among people with cancer. However, the relationship between intervention components and theoretical pathways of self-efficacy has not been systematically mapped. Objective This scoping review aimed to describe the types, functional components, implementation characteristics, and self-efficacy outcome directions of digital health technologies designed to support self-efficacy in adults with cancer, and to map these components to Bandura’s sources of self-efficacy information. Methods This scoping review was conducted in accordance with the JBI methodological guidance and reported according to PRISMA-ScR. PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, the Cochrane Library, and PsycINFO were searched from inception to January 9, 2026. Studies of digital health interventions for adult patients with cancer that reported self-efficacy outcomes were eligible. Two reviewers independently performed study selection, data extraction, and theory-based coding. Findings were synthesized using descriptive statistics, narrative synthesis, and evidence matrices. Results Twenty-one studies were included. Digital health technologies mainly included mobile applications, online platforms or websites, telehealth-supported care, and wearable devices; some studies integrated artificial intelligence, virtual simulation, text messaging, or other electronic communication tools. Intervention components included health education, self-monitoring, goal setting, task practice, feedback, professional support, peer interaction, reminders, and emotion regulation. Five studies reported significant improvement in overall self-efficacy, three reported improvement in specific dimensions, two reported improvement in high-engagement or subgroup analyses, three showed non-significant positive trends, and eight observed no significant change. In the descriptive comparison, moderate-to-strong mastery-experience coding was observed in all 10 studies reporting statistically significant improvement in overall, domain-specific, or high-engagement/subgroup self-efficacy, compared with 7 of 11 studies not reporting statistically significant improvement. Moderate-to-strong verbal-persuasion coding was observed in 10 of 10 and 6 of 11 studies, respectively. These patterns reflected co-occurrence rather than independent effects. Conclusion Digital health interventions varied substantially in functional components, theoretical operationalization, professional support, engagement, and outcomes. Moderate-to-strong mastery-experience and verbal-persuasion coding was more common among studies reporting statistically significant improvement. Future studies should report intervention components, theoretical pathways, engagement, professional support, and follow-up more consistently.

title: HyEff-UNet: an attention-driven Efficientnet U-Net with hybrid loss optimization for UAV-based marine oil spill detection and segmentation
container-title: Frontiers in Water
c492e363cd245facf297484c5696e738583492e4.abstract: Introduction Monitoring oil spills in the port area is very difficult and can spread rapidly, resulting in considerable damage to the environment. This study proposes HyEff-UNet, a deep learning-based semantic segmentation model for the detection of oil spills using drone-captured RGB images of port environments. Methods HyEff-UNet employs a modified version of the U-Net model with an EfficientNet-B4 model as an encoder is used as the model architecture to classify the pixels of the input image as oil, water, or other surface regions. A combined categorical cross-entropy and Dice loss function is used to jointly optimize pixel-wise classification and region overlap. Results The results show that the complete architecture achieves the highest performance among the internally evaluated models, while the sequential ablation indicates that the largest performance improvement is observed after the hybrid categorical cross-entropy and Dice loss is introduced following the EfficientNet-B4 and attention-based architecture. Conclusion These findings demonstrate the effectiveness of the complete architecture within the evaluated configurations. However, the sequential ablation study does not isolate the independent contribution of the hybrid loss. Furthermore, the measured inference latency indicates that further optimization and unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-specific benchmarking are required before real-time onboard deployment can be considered.

title: Physical exercise and sense of social responsibility among Chinese residents: potential explanatory roles of social capital and subjective wellbeing
container-title: Frontiers in Psychology
7717efc4b4b508f4e47ee2d08919e6cb82aab9e8.abstract: Introduction Physical exercise (PE) may have broader social implications beyond its established health benefits, but its association with residents’ sense of social responsibility (SSR) remains underexplored. This study examines the association between PE and SSR among Chinese residents and investigates the potential explanatory roles of social capital and subjective wellbeing, providing evidence on the broader social significance of everyday exercise behavior. Methods This cross-sectional observational study used data from the nationally representative China General Social Survey (CGSS) 2023. After sample screening, 5,290 valid observations were retained. Multiple linear regression, ordered probit models, subgroup analyses, stepwise regression, and bootstrap analysis with 5,000 resamples were used to examine the PE–SSR association, assess its robustness and heterogeneity, and test potential explanatory pathways involving social trust, social interaction, social support, and subjective wellbeing. Results PE was positively associated with SSR, and the association remained robust across alternative model specifications, different measures of PE, and additional covariate adjustments. Subgroup analyses showed variation across gender, household registration, and income groups, with relatively stronger associations among females, urban residents, and middle-income respondents. Further analyses indicated that social trust, social support, and subjective wellbeing statistically accounted for part of the association between PE and SSR, whereas social interaction did not. Bootstrap results were consistent with the stepwise regression findings. Conclusion PE was positively associated with SSR among Chinese residents, while social trust, social support, and subjective wellbeing may represent potential explanatory pathways in this association. These findings extend understanding of the social relevance of physical exercise beyond conventional health outcomes and suggest that PE may constitute an important everyday behavioral context for understanding social responsibility. Given the cross-sectional design, the findings should be interpreted as statistical associations rather than causal relationships.

title: Fairness and governance of dual-track scoring on digital competition platforms: evidence from 34 seasons of Dancing with the Stars
container-title: Asia Pacific Journal of Innovation and Entrepreneurship
e5f20a5a588be08773d2a75f531b238712c89615.abstract: Purpose Dual-track entrepreneurial platforms integrate expert and public scores, but confidential voting figures create a data black box when evaluations from these two sources conflict. This study aims to examine how alternative mechanisms for integrating scores from these different sources shape screening fairness and how governance design can balance fairness with platform vitality. Design/methodology/approach Using 34 seasons of Dancing with the Stars as a proxy sample that is structurally analogous to dual-track entrepreneurial platforms that integrate expert assessments and public evaluations in screening decisions, this study applies inverse optimization, ordinal logistic regression and cardinal convex optimization to reconstruct unobserved public-preference trajectories. A third-order information-entropy variation system is then used to compare the institutional efficiency of alternative score-aggregation mechanisms. Findings Changes in scoring rules alter the elimination outcomes in 35% of borderline and controversial cases, while extremely low expert scores trigger a sympathy-vote rebound in subsequent stages. The proposed dynamic-weighting and dual-track-elimination mechanism gives greater weight to public input in early stages and shifts toward expert input in later stages. Historical backtesting raises the fairness score from 0.620 to 0.712 while maintaining platform vitality. Research limitations/implications The use of entertainment data limits generalizability because entertainment competitions and entrepreneurial ventures employ different evaluation criteria. Future research should validate the findings using commercial crowdfunding data. Practical implications The proposed mechanism helps platform designers balance public participation with professional risk control when configuring scoring, screening and elimination rules. Originality/value This study combines inverse reconstruction with an entropy-based framework to evaluate algorithmic fairness when proprietary platform data are unavailable, offering a governance tool for dual-track entrepreneurial ecosystems.

title: The role of AI adoption in the relationship between digital self-efficacy and sustainable entrepreneurship intentions among university students in Jordan
container-title: Management & Sustainability: An Arab Review
31b71467d2d907fa638bb67cb3940cd9d9d934a0.abstract: Purpose This study investigates associations among digital self-efficacy (DSE), artificial intelligence (AI) adoption intention and sustainable entrepreneurship intentions (SEIs) among university students at a private university in Amman, Jordan – a context with high unemployment and national digital agendas. Design/methodology/approach A sequential exploratory mixed-methods design was employed. Phase 1 involved semi-structured interviews with seven entrepreneurship faculty and an incubator director at a private university in Amman. Phase 2 comprised a survey of 150 students from the same institution. The technology acceptance model (TAM) and social cognitive theory (SCT) were integrated in a mediated model tested using partial least squares structural equation modelling. Findings DSE was positively associated with perceived usefulness (PU) (β = 0.570, p &lt; 0.001) and perceived ease of use (PEOU) (β = 0.584, p &lt; 0.001) of AI tools. AI adoption intention (AIAI) mediated the relationship between DSE and SEI. The total indirect effect of DSE on SEI through both serial mediation paths was 0.247 (p &lt; 0.001). The specific serial indirect effects were 0.078 (DSE → PU → AIAI → SEI, p = 0.012) and 0.093 (DSE → PEOU → AIAI → SEI, p = 0.006). The model accounted for 42.8% and 25.3% of the variance in AIAI and SEI, respectively. These findings are limited to university students at one institution; replication with representative samples and longitudinal designs is needed before drawing broader conclusions. Practical implications Within university settings, educators might consider building DSE through experiential training that links AI to sustainability challenges. Universities could explore integrating AI literacy into entrepreneurship curricula. Originality/value This study positions AIAI as a potential mediating mechanism between DSE and SEIs, providing empirical evidence from a Middle Eastern university context. The contribution is incremental and context-specific, providing preliminary evidence consistent with the proposed theoretical mechanism.

title: Ethnic traditional sports participation, cultural identity, and psychological wellbeing among Chinese minority adolescents: a moderated mediation model
container-title: Frontiers in Psychology
243affc28e5ee7b8e32f281b3b1f9e8faadfc168.abstract: Ethnic traditional sports constitute a distinctive vehicle for cultural transmission and physical activity among ethnic minority youth, yet their psychological correlates remain underexplored. This study examined whether cultural identity statistically mediates the relationship between ethnic traditional sports participation and psychological wellbeing among Chinese minority adolescents, and whether this indirect pathway is moderated by perceived social support. A total of 1,086 secondary school students (522 boys, 564 girls, M age = 14.26 years, SD = 1.38) from six schools in Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region completed anonymous questionnaires measuring ethnic traditional sports participation, cultural identity, perceived social support, and psychological wellbeing. Moderated mediation analysis was conducted using the PROCESS macro (Model 14) with 5,000 bootstrap resamples. Participation in ethnic traditional sports was positively associated with cultural identity ( β = 0.46, p &lt; 0.001), which in turn was associated with psychological wellbeing ( β = 0.37, p &lt; 0.001). The participation–identity link and the identity–wellbeing link combined to form a significant indirect effect [ β = 0.168, 95% bootstrap CI (0.137, 0.200)]. Perceived social support moderated the second stage of the mediation, such that the association between cultural identity and psychological wellbeing was stronger among adolescents reporting higher social support ( β interaction = 0.08, p &lt; 0.001); the index of moderated mediation was significant [ β = 0.037, 95% bootstrap CI (0.014, 0.060)]. These findings suggest that participation in ethnic traditional sports is associated with minority adolescents’ wellbeing, partly through its association with cultural identity, and that this indirect association is stronger when supportive interpersonal environments are in place. The moderated mediation finding is preliminary rather than robust across all plausible clustering scenarios: class and school identifiers were not retained in the anonymized data set, so clustering could not be modeled directly, and the design-effect sensitivity analysis indicates that the interaction would lose significance at an intraclass correlation of about 0.06 or higher. As the design is cross-sectional, these associations may inform culturally grounded school-based programs for minority youth wellbeing pending verification in longitudinal and experimental designs.

title: Negotiating Digital Innovation and Pesantren Traditions: Teachers’, Administrators’, and Students’ Experiences of Digital Transformation in Islamic Religious Education
container-title: MODERATE: Journal of Religious, Education, and Social
3fa90d25d840352b1b228d1ca8c121d9acf58810.abstract: Transformasi digital di pondok pesantren bukan tentang memperkenalkan perangkat teknologi atau memindahkan pembelajaran ke platform online, melainkan negosiasi antara peluang teknologi, pengetahuan agama, otoritas guru, pedagogi tatap muka, dan nilai-nilai institusi. Makalah ini mengkaji pengalaman dan proses negosiasi pembelajaran PAI di sebuah pondok pesantren di Indonesia menggunakan desain studi kasus kualitatif (18 informan yang dipilih secara purposif: enam guru PAI, dua manajer pendidikan, dan 10 siswa). Data dikumpulkan melalui wawancara semi-terstruktur, delapan sesi observasi kelas non-partisipan, dan analisis dokumen pembelajaran institusi; dianalisis secara tematik menggunakan familiarisasi data, pengkodean awal, pengembangan kategori, dan interpretasi lintas sumber. Temuan diorganisir menjadi empat dimensi analitis yang saling terkait: adopsi teknologi digital, adaptasi pedagogis, mediasi guru, dan negosiasi berbasis nilai. Presentasi, materi audiovisual, dan smartphone memperluas akses ke materi pembelajaran dan mendiversifikasi aktivitas pembelajaran tetapi tidak menggantikan penjelasan langsung, diskusi, interaksi guru-siswa, dan praktik pembelajaran yang ada. Guru memediasi informasi agama digital dengan seleksi, pemeriksaan, penjelasan, dan kontekstualisasi sumber. Informan juga menyebutkan gangguan, kredibilitas informasi online, kompetensi digital guru, dan waktu persiapan tambahan. Penelitian ini menjelaskan transformasi digital sebagai negosiasi kontekstual (bukan pergeseran linear dari pembelajaran tradisional ke digital). Penelitian ini menawarkan lensa analitis empat dimensi untuk memahami interaksi antara penggunaan teknologi, keputusan pedagogis, mediasi pengetahuan keagamaan, dan nilai kelembagaan pesantren. Kerangka ini bersifat interpretatif dan berakar pada satu kasus sehingga perlu dikaji lebih lanjut dalam konteks kelembagaan yang berbeda. The rapid expansion of digital technology has transformed educational practices, including Islamic Religious Education (IRE) in Islamic boarding schools. However, the integration of technology into pesantren education presents a particular challenge because technological innovation must be negotiated with established pedagogical practices and religious values. This study aims to examine how technology-driven transformation occurs in IRE at Pondok Pesantren Al-Kifyah Riaty and how teachers and students negotiate the relationship between digital innovation and traditional Islamic educational practices. A qualitative case study was employed involving 18 participants, consisting of six IRE teachers, two educational administrators, and ten students. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews, classroom observations, and analysis of relevant institutional documents and were analyzed thematically through data reduction, coding, categorization, and cross-source triangulation. The findings reveal four interconnected dimensions of digital transformation: digital adoption, pedagogical adaptation, teacher mediation, and value-based negotiation. Digital technologies expanded access to learning resources, diversified teaching strategies, and supported student engagement; however, technology did not replace direct instruction, teacher–student interaction, or traditional Islamic learning practices. Teachers increasingly acted as selectors, evaluators, and mediators of digital religious information, while challenges emerged concerning teachers’ digital competence, student distraction, information credibility, and additional preparation time. The study contributes a context-sensitive understanding of digital transformation in Islamic education by demonstrating that meaningful digitalization in pesantren is not a linear transition from traditional to digital learning, but a negotiated process in which technological innovation is integrated with pedagogical, cultural, and religious values.

title: IMPLEMENTASI BROAD LEARNING SYSTEM (BLS)  UNTUK IDENTIFIKASI PENYAKIT DAUN TANAMAN TOMAT BERDASARKAN CITRA DIGITAL
container-title: INTECOMS: Journal of Information Technology and Computer Science
f06480076faf467d171c060d415676013c5e3f93.abstract: Penyakit daun pada tanaman tomat dapat menurunkan produktivitas sehingga diperlukan metode identifikasi berbasis karakteristik visual citra. Penelitian ini bertujuan menerapkan Broad Learning System (BLS) sebagai classifier untuk klasifikasi penyakit daun tomat dengan MobileNetV2 sebagai feature extractor. Dataset yang digunakan berasal dari PlantVillage dan terdiri atas 18.160 citra dalam 10 kelas. Tahapan penelitian meliputi preprocessing, augmentasi citra, ekstraksi fitur menggunakan MobileNetV2, L2 normalization, reduksi dimensi menggunakan Principal Component Analysis (PCA), klasifikasi menggunakan BLS, dan evaluasi model. Hasil pengujian terhadap data testing menunjukkan accuracy sebesar 78%, dengan macro precision 0,78, macro recall 0,78, dan macro F1-score 0,77. Confusion matrix menunjukkan bahwa sebagian besar data dapat diklasifikasikan dengan benar, meskipun masih terdapat kesalahan pada beberapa kelas dengan karakteristik visual yang serupa. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa kombinasi MobileNetV2 dan BLS dapat digunakan sebagai salah satu pendekatan untuk klasifikasi penyakit daun tomat berbasis citra digital. Kata kunci: Broad Learning System, MobileNetV2, penyakit daun tomat, PlantVillage.

title: Reconstruction of the Islamic Education Curriculum in Shaping Religious Digital Literacy Awareness in the Modern Era
container-title: Edusoshum : Journal of Islamic Education and Social Humanities
465a5b73888db063ab7e950bbf30d7b1598aa0d0.abstract: The rapid development of digital technology has changed how students access and engage with religious information, creating new challenges for Islamic Religious Education (IRE). The widespread circulation of unverified religious content highlights the need to strengthen students’ ability to evaluate and use digital religious information critically and responsibly. However, the integration of religious digital literacy into the IRE curriculum requires a more comprehensive framework. This study aims to identify the curriculum components that need to be reconstructed and formulate a framework for integrating religious digital literacy into IRE. It employs a qualitative approach through a literature review of scholarly books, journal articles, conference proceedings, and educational policy documents. The collected literature is analyzed using content analysis to identify recurring themes and synthesize relevant findings. The results identify five dimensions of religious digital literacy: technical competence, critical evaluation of digital religious content, Islamic digital ethics, religious communication in digital spaces, and the use of technology for spiritual development. The study also identifies four curriculum components requiring reconstruction: learning objectives, learning materials, instructional methods, and assessment. The proposed framework integrates Islamic values and digital competencies through technology-supported learning, authentic assessment, and the cultivation of ethical and responsible digital behavior. The study concludes that curriculum reconstruction should address both digital competence and Islamic values to prepare students to engage critically, ethically, and responsibly with religious information in the digital era.

title: PENINGKATAN KETERAMPILAN MENULIS PUISI MELALUI MEDIA POP UP BOOK DIGITAL BERBASIS ASSEMBLR EDU

219485c802f860f6e0fb11d9c1e4c25136b39d8c.abstract: The low level of poetry writing skills among elementary school students remains a challenge in Indonesian language learning, particularly in generating ideas, selecting appropriate diction, developing imagery, and composing meaningful poems. This study aimed to improve students' poetry writing skills and describe teacher and student activities through the implementation of a digital pop-up book based on Assemblr Edu. This study employed Classroom Action Research (CAR), conducted in two cycles consisting of planning, action, observation, and reflection. The participants were 35 fifth-grade students of SDN 2 Tambakrigadung. Data were collected through observation, performance tests, and documentation, then analyzed using quantitative descriptive techniques. The results showed that teacher activity increased from 55% in Cycle I to 88% in Cycle II, while student activity increased from 53% to 88%. The average poetry writing score also improved from 67 to 79, with learning mastery increasing from 40% to 83%. These improvements indicate that three-dimensional visualizations provided through the learning media helped students generate inspiration, develop imagination, and select appropriate diction. Therefore, implementing a digital pop-up book based on Assemblr Edu can serve as an alternative approach to improving elementary school students' poetry writing skills. ABSTRAK Rendahnya keterampilan menulis puisi siswa sekolah dasar menjadi permasalahan dalam pembelajaran Bahasa Indonesia, terutama dalam menemukan ide, memilih diksi, membangun imaji, dan mengembangkan gagasan menjadi puisi yang utuh. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk meningkatkan keterampilan menulis puisi serta mendeskripsikan aktivitas guru dan siswa melalui penerapan media Pop Up Book Digital berbasis Assemblr Edu. Penelitian ini menggunakan metode Penelitian Tindakan Kelas (PTK) yang dilaksanakan dalam dua siklus, meliputi perencanaan, pelaksanaan tindakan, observasi, dan refleksi. Subjek penelitian adalah 35 siswa kelas V SDN 2 Tambakrigadung. Data dikumpulkan melalui observasi, tes kinerja, dan dokumentasi, kemudian dianalisis menggunakan teknik deskriptif kuantitatif. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa aktivitas guru meningkat dari 55% pada siklus I menjadi 88% pada siklus II, sedangkan aktivitas siswa meningkat dari 53% menjadi 88%. Nilai rata-rata keterampilan menulis puisi juga meningkat dari 67 menjadi 79, dengan ketuntasan belajar dari 40% menjadi 83%. Peningkatan tersebut menunjukkan bahwa visualisasi tiga dimensi dalam media membantu siswa menemukan inspirasi, mengembangkan imajinasi, dan memilih diksi. Dengan demikian, penerapan media Pop Up Book Digital berbasis Assemblr Edu dapat menjadi alternatif untuk meningkatkan keterampilan menulis puisi siswa sekolah dasar.

title: Does open access strengthen the link between online attention and citations?
58fe5cd252b54e7fa9a09fb5d584bc2f3e562cba.abstract: Abstract Altmetric Attention Scores are often proposed as early signals of later citations. We test whether open access (OA) changes this relationship by comparing OA and non-OA articles within the same hybrid journals. Study 1 uses 60,565 articles published mainly in 2018 in 1,275 Springer hybrid journals, with attention recorded in 2021 and citations in 2022–2026. Attention predicted later citations more strongly for hybrid OA articles, made open at publication, than for other articles (Spearman ρ = 0.38 vs 0.19). After exact matching, a gap of 0.06 (95% CI 0.03–0.10) remained; it shrank further once early citations were controlled. Downloads accounted for most of the attention–citation link. A natural experiment, in which national agreements made hybrid OA the default in several European countries, points to causal effects of OA on attention, downloads and citations: in the same journals, articles from these countries received 29% more citations, while their non-hybrid articles were not cited more. The hybrid OA citation advantage declined as journal impact factor rose. In Study 2, covering 7,073 Nature articles, OA brought no citation advantage over closed articles. In Study 3, Altmetric data on Colombian research show that the gap lies in public attention (news, blogs, X), not in Mendeley readership. Hybrid OA was concentrated among authors in high-income countries and top-ranked universities. Altmetric scores are thus a somewhat better proxy for citations when articles are free to read, but a poor substitute for citations in assessment.

title: Delegating Digital Policing: The Evolution of China’s Security-Industrial Complex
container-title: The China Quarterly
484c679263da1b3e263c4d9e8d7d4068a7954357.abstract: Abstract How did China build its formidable digital policing apparatus so rapidly? While prevailing narratives emphasize top-down state direction, this statist perspective obscures critical local dynamics. This article argues that China’s security-industrial complex actually emerged from decentralized administrative pressures. Burdened by unfunded, time-sensitive central security mandates, resource-strapped local security agencies abandoned state-led technological development and outsourced to the private sector. Drawing on extensive field interviews (2017–2022) and policy analysis, this study traces the complex’s evolution through three interrelated mechanisms: the decentralization of internal security politics, the formation of hybrid public–private partnerships, and the varied transactional behaviour exhibited by capitalists, as well as between government and business, in a multi-layered system. By demonstrating how localized security projects inadvertently catalysed technological innovation, this research reveals the hidden market-driven roots of China’s security-industrial complex. It offers a novel framework for understanding how the party-state adaptively leverages capital for building a digital security state.

title: Is Your Phone Distracting You, Even If You’re Not Using It? How Do Notifications and Merely Having a Phone Nearby Affect How Well We Focus and Remember Things?
container-title: Advances in Social Sciences Research Journal
0d2190f86b083886fc77f8ef63df08d54743e877.abstract: This review examines whether a cell phone can negatively impact an individual’s ability to pay attention and recall information while the person is not actively using the device. Ward et al. (2017) indicated that simply having one’s own cell phone present resulted in less available working memory, with the greatest negative effects being among individuals who depend heavily upon their phones. Additionally, Thornton et al. (2014) discovered similar decreases in performance on challenging attention-demanding tasks. However, Ruiz Pardo and Minda (2022), in a pre-registered direct replication, and Hartmann et al. (2020), in a pre-registered conceptual replication, both failed to find a significant overall effect of phone presence. The results of the meta-analyses were also mixed. Some found evidence of effects on memory, while another found no significant overall effect of phone presence. Beyond the mere presence of a cell phone, receiving notifications has been shown to impair sustained attention (Stothart et al., 2015), and frequent media multitaskers showed poorer filtering abilities when dealing with extraneous information in Ophir et al.’s (2009) study. Overall, the evidence supporting a memory cost from phone presence remains limited and disputed.

title: Adaptive management under uncertainty: sustained participatory management of endemic species in Brazilian Cerrado
container-title: Environmental Conservation
cdee9e1f5b9eee69340b5377bedd6db41f4b33be.abstract: Summary Given land-use change threatening both biodiversity and traditional extractive livelihoods since 2004, an action research process in Minas Gerais (Brazil) has focused on the management of two endemic species: the giant earthworm Rhinodrilus alatus and the pequi tree Caryocar brasiliense . Socio-ecological assessments, ecological field surveys and market analyses generated the evidence that extractivists and public institutions used to negotiate management agreements. Despite more than a decade of institutional uncertainty and the absence of formal regulation, local actors maintained voluntary harvesting restrictions, including a closed season during the reproductive period. Ecological evidence supported reassessing the conservation status of R. alatus , enabling discussions on regulated sustainable use. To address seasonal income losses, we developed a community-based pequi processing initiative that aligns livelihood activities with ecological cycles. Over two decades, sustained collaboration, co-produced knowledge and livelihood diversification reduced conflict, strengthened local organization and supported adaptive management under legal uncertainty. This demonstrates that long-term participatory processes can sustain conservation outcomes and reconcile biodiversity conservation with rural livelihoods in socially and biologically diverse landscapes.

title: A Privacy-Aware Hierarchical Membership Information System with UUID-Based QR Verification of Digital Membership Cards for a Faith-Based Youth Organization in Indonesia
container-title: International Journal of Mathematics, Statistics, and Computing
9afc5293b42fb1b5c91d433bdc4f9b888272b8c3.abstract: Membership is the core asset of many faith-based youth organizations, yet in emerging economies it is often recorded on paper or in scattered spreadsheets, and printed membership cards cannot be verified or revoked once issued. Recent studies report that nonprofit digital transformation is under-theorized and that Indonesian evidence is scarce, while digital credential research favours blockchain or self-sovereign identity designs too costly for small volunteer organizations. This study designs and evaluates a web-based membership information system for the Regional Board of Pemuda Muhammadiyah in Sukabumi Regency, Indonesia. The system encodes the organization's region, branch and twig hierarchy and its bylaw age limit directly in the data model, derives membership status at read time, and issues digital membership cards whose QR code carries only an opaque version 4 UUID that is resolved against live server records, so that revocation requires no reissuance. A privacy-by-design audit aligned with Indonesian Law No. 27 of 2022 on Personal Data Protection is proposed together with a data exposure ratio for the public verification endpoint. Artefact analysis shows that the current verification page discloses 9 of 23 stored personal attributes, including date and place of birth, and identifies ten remediable privacy, access-control, functional and usability defects. A usability survey of 86 student participants gave a mean System Usability Scale score of 61.8 (95% CI 57.8 to 65.8) after excluding 25 straight-lined responses, below the benchmark of 68; open answers traced the main problems to entered data lost after a failed submission and a dashboard not adapted to small screens. All 150 automated verification trials returned the correct status, but pages of pending and rejected applicants still disclosed names and membership numbers. Median verification latency over 4G was 0.26 s. The study contributes a low-cost, regulation-aware reference design for membership digitalization in hierarchical nonprofit organizations.

title: Perilaku Phubbing Mahasiswa Muslim sebagai Gejala Anomie Durkheimian dalam Perubahan Sosial Digital Perguruan Tinggi Islam
container-title: Khulasah : Islamic Studies Journal
2069ff6ffad5982f0d4417032c95d91bfa769dc6.abstract: Ponsel pintar telah menjadi infrastruktur utama kehidupan akademik dan keagamaan mahasiswa, tetapi kehadirannya juga melahirkan phubbing, yakni sikap mengabaikan lawan bicara karena perhatian tertuju pada gawai. Kajian terdahulu didominasi pendekatan psikologis kuantitatif yang memandang phubbing sebagai gejala individual, sehingga dimensi struktural dan normatifnya di kalangan mahasiswa Muslim belum banyak diungkap. Artikel ini bertujuan menganalisis fungsi sosial ponsel pintar yang melatarbelakangi phubbing, pola phubbing sebagai gejala anomie, serta implikasinya terhadap relasi sosial-religius mahasiswa Muslim di perguruan tinggi Islam. Penelitian ini menggunakan metode kualitatif berjenis studi kepustakaan kritis dengan pendekatan sosiologis. Desain ini dipilih agar seluruh klaim empiris dapat ditelusuri pada sumber terpublikasi tanpa menghadirkan data lapangan primer. Data sekunder dihimpun dari artikel jurnal bereputasi terbitan 2021–2026, buku sosiologi klasik, serta kitab etika Islam, kemudian dianalisis dengan model interaktif reduksi, penyajian, dan penarikan kesimpulan melalui lensa teori anomie Émile Durkheim. Hasil kajian menunjukkan bahwa ponsel pintar berfungsi sebagai media komunikasi, informasi, aktualisasi diri, spiritualitas, dan hiburan yang saling bertumpang tindih. Phubbing terpola sebagai ritualisme notifikasi, normalisasi kebiasaan individualistik, dan pelarian sosial. Dampaknya ambivalen, yaitu memperluas akses belajar dan religiusitas digital, tetapi melemahkan perhatian, empati, dan adab majelis. Simpulannya, phubbing merupakan gejala anomie yang menuntut pelembagaan etika komunikasi Islam di perguruan tinggi.

title: Integrasi Layanan Antrean Digital dan Konsultasi Medis Berbasis Web Mobile menggunakan Pendekatan Telemedicine

58b75c11518ffd8c1b05e0a45e5a4737729cc41b.abstract: Registration and patient queueing at Mangunjaya Community Health Center have relied on in-person procedures, requiring patients to visit the facility to obtain queue numbers. This practice may contribute to crowded waiting areas and uncertainty regarding service times. This study aimed to develop an Android-based application for queue reservations and medical consultations, integrated with a Laravel backend and a web-based administration panel. The system incorporates online queue booking with dynamically displayed daily capacity, an information chatbot, real-time messaging, electronic medical record documentation with role-based access, and integrated notifications. Application development focused on connecting patient-facing services with administrative and clinical workflows within the health center. Implementation results showed that the application displayed current queue quotas and progress, supported doctors in recording clinical encounters, and facilitated communication between patients and health center personnel. Functional testing of the interface and system workflows indicated that the evaluated features operated according to the specified requirements. These findings demonstrate the functional feasibility of integrating reservation, communication, and documentation services within a single mobile platform. The application is expected to reduce the need for patients to visit the facility solely for queue registration and to support more organized service delivery. However, its actual effects on waiting times, patient satisfaction, and operational efficiency require further evaluation during routine use.

title: Explainable artificial intelligence for understanding digital technology sophistication and firm productivity in developing and emerging economies
container-title: Discover Artificial Intelligence
1c19e4ce2daa8d5ee9372abac76df5078c693b08.abstract: Abstract Digital technologies increasingly shape how firms coordinate internal processes, engage markets, and organise commercial transactions, yet evidence remains limited on whether technology sophistication across distinct business functions is consistently associated with firm productivity and generalises across heterogeneous developing and emerging economies. This study examines business administration, marketing, and sales technology sophistication in relation to relative firm labour productivity using harmonised data from 9664 establishments across Bangladesh, Brazil, Ethiopia, Georgia, Ghana, India, Kenya, Senegal, and Vietnam. Productivity was measured as within-country-wave standardised log sales per permanent full-time employee. The expanded specification accounted for managerial sector experience, foreign ownership, firm size, firm age, workforce tertiary education, export status, capital intensity, and country and sector heterogeneity. Fixed-effects econometric estimation was combined with Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), geographically grouped cross-validation, a linear predictive benchmark, out-of-fold SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP), and leave-one-country-out validation. All three technology dimensions exhibited positive conditional associations with productivity in the preferred specification, although business administration technology sophistication showed the most consistent relationship across robustness analyses, while marketing and sales technology associations were not statistically significant under survey weighting. Capital intensity emerged as the dominant XGBoost predictive feature, while business administration technology sophistication remained the most important technology-related feature. Under grouped country-wave validation, the fixed-configuration XGBoost model achieved an out-of-fold R 2 of 0.152 compared with 0.150 for the linear benchmark, indicating little aggregate predictive advantage from the evaluated nonlinear specification. Leave-one-country-out validation produced pooled R 2 values of 0.148 for XGBoost and 0.143 for the linear benchmark, while country-specific XGBoost performance ranged from − 0.027 to 0.379. The two geographically restrictive validation designs therefore indicate limited and heterogeneous geographic predictive transfer, with little overall predictive advantage from the more flexible learner. These findings show that function-specific technology sophistication contains predictive information about relative sales-based labour productivity but is embedded within a broader configuration of firm resources and does not transfer uniformly across national settings. By combining econometric estimation, predictive benchmarking, geographically restrictive validation, and out-of-fold explainability, the study distinguishes conditional association, predictive importance, and geographic transportability without treating explainable machine learning as evidence of causality.

title: Digital Twin-Based Risk Monitoring for Construction
container-title: Applied and Computational Engineering
a247f53bdf2b42e2586635b4914329fabd4e520a.abstract: Due to the continuous changes in the construction site, construction equipment and working environment, the traditional manual and periodic site inspections have difficulty controlling the risk in time. Therefore, it is necessary to adopt a more continuous monitoring approach. This article adopts the method of literature synthesis and analysis of representative studies, organizes the data and supporting technology of the digital twin for construction safety management and analyzes related studies in three aspects, namely personnel safety and dangerous area monitoring, equipment and construction environment risk monitoring, fire risk monitoring and emergency response. Existing research shows that the digital twin can associate information such as Building Information Modeling (BIM), personnel positioning, wearable devices, equipment operation and environmental monitoring with digital models, and provide more continuous on-site information for dangerous area identification, lifting equipment risk analysis and fire condition monitoring. However, its actual effect is still affected by factors such as data accuracy, model update speed, sensor stability, system integration and field conditions. At this stage, the digital twin is more suitable as an auxiliary tool for construction safety management, and related systems still need to be continuously verified in more real projects.

title: Dynamic Environmental Risk Identification for Historic Buildings Based on Multi-Source Sensing Digital Twins
container-title: Applied and Computational Engineering
3cb2a15c6451b420d691036586a898567c2e2d7f.abstract: Buildings with heritage suffer from various disturbances like hygrothermal disturbances, moisture, vibration, and crack problems which cannot be easily identified from sensor readings independently. In this research, a multi-source sensing-based digital twin is developed for identifying environmental risks dynamically in a monitored two-story building made of bricks and timber structure. Variables such as temperature, relative humidity, wall moisture, vibration, crack displacement, and weather data outside are synchronized every five minutes and mapped into IFC-based Heritage Building Information Model in Unity. With the Temporal Fusion Transformer, a multivariate history with 24 time steps is taken into account, and normal, hygrothermal instability, moisture infiltration, vibration abnormalities, and crack displacement risk predictions are done. The architecture includes class weights, adaptive temporal consistency, and spatial regularization of components. With temporal testing, macro-F1 of 0.891±0.012, AUROC of 0.962±0.006, and mean warning delay of 6.7±1.1 min were obtained which is better than LSTM and XGBoost models with p<0.001. Removal of moisture sensors yielded maximum drop of macro-F1 to 0.847±0.014. Digital twin localization error was 0.43±0.17 m.

title: Digital IIR Filter Design Methods and Filter Selection Trade-Offs in Hardware Implementation
container-title: Applied and Computational Engineering
0c4c6bd3c6c7b231725ef9ee38808fe9fe0f08fd.abstract: Digital IIR filters are widely used for signal denoising in signal processing systems. IIR filter implementation requires a lower order with the same design specifications when compared with FIR filters. Among typical IIR categories, Butterworth and Chebyshev filters are two commonly used filters. This paper introduces the fundamental theory of digital IIR filters, reviews two major indirect design approaches including, bilinear transformation and impulse invariance, and explains the different properties of Butterworth, Chebyshev type I and Chebyshev type II filters. Further qualitative comparison of different types of filters is conducted in hardware implementation scenarios. The analysis concludes that Butterworth filters have no ripple in the passband response and superior signal integrity at the cost of higher hardware complexity, whereas Chebyshev filters achieve sharper transition bands with reduced order at the expense of ripples. This work clarifies practical selection principles in scenarios with limited resources and points out that unified quantitative selection metrics for IIR filter hardware deployment remain insufficient for low-cost scenarios.

title: Future Faculty Development in the Age of AI: University Teachers’ Roles, Needs, and Institutional Support
container-title: Frontiers of Digital Education
505d8830ac9df419c1922aa596a0e1b98d3c9b8a.abstract: Abstract AI is reshaping higher education in ways that extend beyond the adoption of new tools, challenging established assumptions about assessment, curriculum, ethics, graduate preparation, and the work of university teachers. Drawing on insights from the Teacher Panel at the International Conference on GenAI and Pedagogical Innovations held in Hong Kong in May 2026, this commentary argues that faculty development in the AI era must move beyond generic technology training towards a more role-based, discipline-sensitive, future-oriented, and ecosystemic approach. The commentary identifies four key insights from the panel discussion: AI use is already widespread and assessment has become an immediate pressure point; AI literacy is necessary but insufficient without disciplinary, professional, ethical, and human-centred dimensions; universities must connect learning more explicitly with the authentic world beyond campus while renewing the role of the campus as a site of experimentation and futures literacy; and institutions need stronger capacity for evidence-informed, forward-looking AI governance. Building on these insights, the commentary proposes seven emerging roles for university teachers: human-centred educator; disciplinary and professional expert; learning architect and intellectual guide; assessment (re)designer; technically competent and critically informed professional; ethical steward; and educational experimenter and evidence-based practitioner. Corresponding faculty development needs are then discussed, including support for human-centred education, curriculum renewal, world-connected learning, assessment redesign, technical-pedagogical AI capability, ethical stewardship, AI policy literacy, and scholarship-informed educational improvement. The commentary concludes with a preliminary role-based framework for faculty development. It emphasises that these roles need not be performed by a single individual teacher. Rather, as educational design and delivery become more complex in the age of AI, university education should increasingly be understood as a collective endeavour involving academic staff, educational developers, technology specialists, professional staff, students, external partners, employers, and community organisations.
