title: RADIAN: Regime-Adaptive Dilated Inter-Attention Network for Non-Stationary Financial Time-Series Forecasting
6698e7c660e353c7e7b83678da42ad8013815e40.abstract: Financial forecasting is challenged by non-stationarity, volatility clustering, and regime transitions that induce distribution shifts. Conventional neural architectures often rely on shared decoder mappings that inadequately capture regime-dependent dynamics. We introduce RADIAN (Regime-Adaptive Dilated Inter-Attention Network), which preserves regime-agnostic temporal and cross-variable encoders while applying causal regime conditioning only in gated fusion and decoding. A deterministic four-dimensional regime vector computed from normalized one-step target returns guides a regime-aware gated mixture-of-experts directional head, path-based trajectory construction, and residual correction; SafeFeatureRevIN preserves sample-specific scale during normalization and reconstruction. We evaluate RADIAN on nine hourly financial datasets across asset classes against eight baselines under a fixed protocol with three seeds. RADIAN achieves the lowest mean test MAE, improving by 0.6704% on average over the strongest per-dataset baseline, and the lowest RMSE on all nine datasets and lowest MSE/MAE on eight. RMSE improvement averages 0.41% (median 0.36%), and mean directional accuracy reaches 51.279% versus 50.950% for the next-best model average. Paired tests show large effect sizes, with Benjamini-Hochberg-corrected significance on two datasets. Ablations confirm decoder-side regime conditioning: removing path decoding raises RMSE by up to 2.55%, and replacing gated fusion reduces directional accuracy by up to 1.15 percentage points. RADIAN attains an aggregated test RMSE of 94.1048 with 516,425 parameters and processes batches of 64 in 24.7172 ms versus 83.7451 ms for ModernTCN. These findings support decoder-centric causal regime conditioning for accurate, efficient financial forecasting under heterogeneous market conditions.

title: Trustworthy Multi-Agent Systems: A Human-in-the-Loop Framework for Monitoring, Governance, and Adaptive Correction
17dab29973a0729a7721707c5fe9d22b0afbcb9a.abstract: Autonomous multi-agent systems are increasingly being designed to perform complex tasks with limited human intervention. However, increasing autonomy introduces challenges related to trust, transparency, accountability, controllability, and safe decision-making. This paper presents a web-based control-room prototype for a Trustworthy Multi-Agent System designed to monitor and govern autonomous agents while maintaining human oversight. The proposed framework integrates trust monitoring, evidence-based decision-making, adaptive self-correction, auditability, explainability, runtime monitoring, and Safe Mode controls. The system provides a Trust Posture dashboard for monitoring overall system trust, agent activity, self-corrections, human interventions, and trust trajectories. An Agent Roster provides information about individual agents, including their roles, trust scores, operational status, run counts, and available operator controls. Recent audit events maintain a human-readable record of approvals, reviews, corrections, and evidence updates. A Safe Mode mechanism provides controlled autonomy by requiring human confirmation before new autonomous actions can proceed. The evaluation framework considers Trust Score, Confidence Level, Agent Activity, Self-Correction Count, Human Intervention Count, Agent Status, Audit Events, and Decision/Action Status as measurable variables. Purposive sampling is used to identify meaningful system activities for evaluation. The proto-type demonstrates how monitoring, human oversight, evidence-based decisions, and adaptive correction can be integrated into a unified governance framework for trustworthy autonomous multi-agent systems.

title: TAPE–TAFTE: Redefining Mental Health Detection Through Adaptive Temporal Fusion in 6G-Enabled Health Systems
bc4f69ae35b2cfc186aa9216c1a917bc85664387.abstract: Mental disorder identification has turned into a substantial element in the 6G-powered healthcare setup of tomorrow that makes use of the characteristics such as edge intelligence, ultra-low latency, and extensive data connectivity to render the mental health monitoring a smooth, uninterrupted, and customizable process. Nevertheless, these pieces of research in their present state encounter various obstacles like the restricted multimodal integration, lack of temporal and context-awareness, high computational overheads, and reduced interpretability of mental disorder classification. Moreover, the conventional deep learning models are not capable of generalizing across different datasets and might overlook even more minute behavioral and linguistic aspects that are highly instrumental in the early stage of diagnosis. This paper devises a smart mechanism with Tabular Adaptive Projection and Embedding (TAPE) and Tabular-Aware Field-Time Encoder (TAFTE) modules that help in a quick identification and accurate localization of mental disorders in clinical and social data at large scale. The TAPE module enables the feature mapping through the embedding of the multi-dimensional mental health metrics into one single latent representation, whereas TAFTE automatically captures the contextual and temporal relations thus facilitating self-learning and interpretability. The research framework utilized Reddit and Kaggle Mental Health datasets that are open sources of real and varied emotional, linguistic, and behavioral data distributions. The experimental results reveal that the proposed TAPE + TAFTE model achieves the topmost performance with the following measures: accuracy of 99.12%, precision of 98.97%, recall of 99.03%, F1-score of 98.99% and time of 1.5s.

title: Multi-Dimensional Attention for Small Object Detection in Airport Obstacle Limitation Airspace
3065f2ef7b67c06fce6ffba5179916887ccafdc9.abstract: In airport clearance airspace, illegally flown unmanned aerial vehicles and birds in long-range imagery occupy extremely small pixel proportions, suffer from texture scarcity, and are readily overwhelmed by background clutter; consequently, generic detectors struggle to achieve accurate detection. To this end, this paper proposes a multi-dimensional attention collaborative optimization method that improves small-object detection performance across three complementary dimensions, feature enhancement, convolution decoupling, and loss reweighting. Initially, a multi-semantic self-attention module is developed, which employs multi-scale depthwise separable convolutions and group normalization to extract multi-semantic spatial features while guiding channel attention learning, thereby enhancing small-object response intensity. Subsequently, a receptive-field decoupled attention module is introduced, which decouples positions within the receptive field of standard convolution and independently assigns attention weights, thereby breaking the parameter-sharing limitation of convolution kernels and improving boundary regression sensitivity. Finally, a unified intersection-over-union loss is proposed, which adjusts the focus on predicted boxes of different qualities through dynamic scaling and annealing strategies, thereby strengthening the fine-grained refinement of high-quality boxes. Furthermore, the effectiveness of these three components is validated on four datasets: TIB, UB-SOD, Drone, and Flying. Notably, on TIB, the proposed method achieves 87.4% mAP50 and 38.9% mAP50-95, improving the baseline by 4.7% and 3.2%, respectively; moreover, it exhibits significant advantages over other methods.

title: Smart Tech, Smart Tourists: A Systematic Review of Digital Technology and Sustainable Tourist Behaviour
c071543e414708673d0e90ea83d32673b74fb5c6.abstract: Tourists are increasingly using digital technologies to search for, book, stay and share about their experiences. Their environmental concern is generally not reflected in their actual travel behaviour. Digital technologies are increasingly influencing tourist decisions, but it is not clear whether they actually close the gap between pro-environmental attitudes and pro-environmental behaviour. This review looks at the mechanisms by which digital technologies can lead to changes in sustainable tourist behaviour, the strength of the evidence for each mechanism and when individual change results in net benefit at the system level. Following PRISMA 2020, we identify the digital mechanisms which lead to changes in sustainable tourist behaviour and assess the strength of the evidence for each. Scopus and Web of Science were searched for studies published between 2010 and 30 June 2026 with a supplementary citation search. A total of 156 studies were included and coded by touchpoint, design and outcome. They were graded for strength of evidence and synthesised thematically. The literature is very new with 95% of the studies published since 2020 and the vast majority (87%) reporting on stated intentions. Only 11 of the studies actually looked at a change in behaviour; these are largely field experiments in which the technology influenced behaviour at the moment of choice via real time feedback, digital defaults, recommenders, robot delivered prompts or app based rewards. Evidence for the use of social media, labels, immersive media and smart destinations is still emerging. AI agents can either promote or inhibit pro-environmental behaviour. Spillover, rebound and the technology’s own footprint are rarely measured. We propose a Technology-Mediated Sustainable Tourist Behaviour (TMSTB) model which links behavioural to system level outcomes and which sets six questions for future research.

title: THE FIELD RESONANCE MODEL (FRM)-FROM RNG COHERENCE TO ADAPTIVE FIELD ECOLOGY
container-title: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
82ab0806d746182b1ab050a3a4897c89dec8f235.abstract: Random Number Generator (RNG) coherence data has been widely used in collective consciousness and global coherence research. Such data can reveal departures from statistical randomness or increased coherence across RNG networks, but the inner dynamics of the observed field remain difficult to interpret from raw coherence values alone. This paper proposes the Field Resonance Model (FRM) as a threshold-based ecological interpretation framework that extends the concept of field coherence toward a more dynamic concept of field resonance. The FRM was developed through long-duration analysis of RNG coherence data from Device RNG, installed in the large Meditation Pyramid at Pyramid Valley International (PVI), Bengaluru, beginning April 2024. The PVI dataset was selected as the foundational developmental sample because it provided long-term continuity, repeated meditation events, a stable sacred-geometry environment, and rich lunar-cycle variability. The model evolved through several methodological refinements: moving from civil-day analysis to sunrise-to-sunrise segmentation, then to lunar-month and paksha-based stratification, and finally to nakshatra anchoring. RNG coherence values were interpreted through threshold zones: Elevated, High, Very High, and Extreme. These zones were then transformed into HRV-like field rhythm layers named Manas, Prana, and Buddhi, with Extreme events interpreted as transition-critical or quantum-leap-like field events. The analogy of Ayurvedic Nadi Pariksha was used as an interpretive framework for classifying layered field rhythms, not as a literal equivalence. The resulting FRM generates composite field parameters such as Coupling, Criticality, Integrated Field Index (IFI), Field Potential Index (FPI), and Field Evolution Index (FEI). The paper presents FRM as an exploratory but structured ecological signal interpretation framework for studying subtle energy fields, high-energy pyramids, sacred geometries, heart coherence work, and consciousness-field research.

title: Transcending the Beer–Lambert Limit with Full-Dimensional Digital Colorimetry
e162e87ec286861a54751bd4916d61351c0f3f96.abstract: Automated workflows are rapidly accelerating discovery across the chemical sciences, yet the throughput of such platforms remains bottlenecked by the high cost and slow operation of traditional analytical hardware. 1 While digital colorimetry offers a ubiquitous, low-cost alternative for reaction monitoring, current techniques rely on the linear approximations of the Beer–Lambert law. 2, 3 This constraint causes data degeneracy, severely limiting analytical accuracy. Here we present quantitative Colorimetric Analysis of Molecules (qCAM), a methodology that bypasses the Beer–Lambert law by retaining the full dimensionality of digital colorimetric data. When applied to the quantification of metals in solution, qCAM matches the accuracy of inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP-MS), the current gold-standard tool, while reducing equipment costs 100-fold and accelerating analysis time from hours to minutes. We demonstrate the versatility of qCAM as compatible with both high-throughput workflows and automated flow-synthesis platforms for chemical, environmental, and medical monitoring, producing results within 0.20 ppm of current analytical methods.

title: Adaptive and Resilient T-PBFT Consensus for Internet of Vehicles Using Multi-Objective Optimization and Reinforcement Learning
cfd93c6c8077667bb54e56f834f0add8fd3f2c78.abstract: Abstract The Internet of Vehicles (IoV) enables continuous communication among vehi-cles and roadside infrastructures, but its highly dynamic conditions, changing network density, resource constraints and exposure to attacks make efficient blockchain consensus challenging. This paper proposes an adaptive T-PBFT con-sensus framework that combines a trust evaluation mechanism inspired by the principles of EigenTrust, the NSGA-III multi-objective optimization algorithm and Deep Q-Network (DQN) reinforcement learning. The proposed approach jointly considers validator selection and T-PBFT configuration while optimiz-ing consensus latency, communication overhead, computational cost, security risk, validator trust and availability. NSGA-III generates candidate configura-tions representing different trade-offs among these objectives, while the DQN agent selects a suitable configuration according to the current network state. The framework is evaluated through a Python-based simulation under nor-mal, high-density, Sybil-attack, denial-of-service (DoS) and combined stress scenarios. Five independent random seeds are used for each scenario and the results are compared with a fixed T-PBFT configuration and an NSGA-III-only approach. The results show that adaptive approaches substantially improve consensus performance under non-DoS conditions, while the hybrid approach provides scenario-dependent benefits, particularly under Sybil attacks. How-ever, under severe DoS conditions, all evaluated methods experience complete consensus failure. These findings demonstrate the potential of combining multi-objective optimization and reinforcement learning for adaptive consensus, while highlighting the need for stronger attack-resilience mechanisms.

title: Eğitim Örgütlerinde Dijital Liderlik ve Teknostres: Kuramsal Çerçeve ve Alanyazın Değerlendirmesi
f979276fc54de9b635b7429c7545170b1827d31e.abstract: Dijital dönüşüm, eğitim örgütlerinin liderlik yapılarını ve çalışanların iş yapma biçimlerini köklü bir şekilde değiştirmektedir. Bu kitap, eğitim örgütlerinde dijital liderlik ve teknostres kavramlarını kuramsal bir çerçevede bir araya getirmeyi, her iki kavrama ilişkin ulusal ve uluslararası alanyazını sistematik biçimde sunmayı ve iki kavram arasındaki ilişkiyi tartışmayı amaçlamaktadır. Giriş bölümünün ardından yedi bölüm ve genel bir değerlendirmeden oluşan kitapta önce dijital dönüşüm kavramı ve eğitimde dijital dönüşüm ele alınmakta; ardından dijital liderlik, dijital liderlerin yeterlilik ve özellikleri ile karşılaştıkları zorluklar bağlamında incelenmektedir. Eğitim örgütlerinde dijital liderlik; Sheninger’in dijital liderlik rolleri, ISTE standartları, okul müdürünün dijital liderlik rolü ve yapay zekâ liderliği çerçevesinde tartışılmaktadır. Teknostres; boyutları, tetikleyicileri, başa çıkma yöntemleri ve bireysel-örgütsel sonuçlarıyla incelenmekte, okul yöneticileri, öğretmenler ve öğrenciler özelinde değerlendirilmekte; teknostresi azaltma ve önleme yolları da ortaya konmaktadır. Her iki kavram için Türkiye’de ve uluslararası alanda yapılan lisansüstü tezler, akademik çalışmalar ve geliştirilen ölçme araçları özetlenmektedir. Yedinci bölümde liderlik ve dijital liderliğin teknostresle ilişkisi, kavramsal bir model ve güncel araştırmalar ışığında tartışılmaktadır. Alanyazın, dijital liderliğin teknostresi kendiliğinden azaltan bir değişkenden çok, teknostresin olumsuz sonuçlarını hafifletebilen ve etkililiği teknostres tarafından sınırlanabilen bir örgütsel kaynak olarak işlev gördüğüne işaret etmektedir. Bir doktora tezine dayanan ve güncel çalışmalarla genişletilen kitap, eğitim yönetimi alanında çalışan araştırmacılar, lisansüstü öğrenciler, okul yöneticileri, öğretmenler ve eğitim politikalarına yön veren karar alıcılar için derli toplu bir başvuru kaynağı sunmaktadır.

title: Attention Renders Sensory Contents into Conscious State via Content-invariant Frontal-Posterior Coupling in Humans
d580ccdc347f467ac53816dbe4798316da62ec5a.abstract: Abstract Although attention promotes conscious perception, how it does so remains unclear. Human neuroimaging research has richly characterized attentional modulation upon visual processing, yet it remains unclear which of its components act as precursors of consciousness, which constitute consciousness itself, and which merely reflect post-perceptual, response-related operations. Combining a newly developed psychophysical paradigm with intracranial electroencephalography (iEEG), we addressed this issue in the human brain. Behavioral results from the psychophysical experiment and its replication showed that top-down attention plays a preparatory role: it promotes visual consciousness not directly, but by enabling attentional capture specific to salient stimuli. iEEG then revealed that early attentional preparation unfolds in a module-dependent manner, differing between the posterior brain (sensory module) and the frontal brain (attention module). We further dissociated two neural signals—one tracking the rapid rise and decay of visual consciousness, the other supporting post-perceptual responses through global late (>600 ms) content retrieval—thereby isolating a conscious window (~250–550 ms) from its preconscious and post-perceptual confounds. Finally, coherence analyses revealed the predicted frontal–posterior coupling (~4 Hz) restricted to this window. Critically, this coupling encoded only the binary on/off state of conscious awareness, whereas fine-grained contents were persistently encoded in the posterior brain. Together, these findings provide pioneering evidence that attention does not promote consciousness directly by itself; rather, it engages a content-invariant frontal–posterior coupling mechanism—not an earlier sensory enhancement mechanism or a later global content broadcast mechanism—to render sensory contents into an explicit conscious state.

title: Transformasi Edukasi Antenatal melalui Kelas Ibu Hamil Berbasis Digital untuk Penguatan Literasi Kesehatan Maternal dan Kapasitas Kader
container-title: Cakrawala: Jurnal Pengabdian Masyarakat Global
6b4a27e42374c99d118fb13c14451a9505b24d4a.abstract: Antenatal education plays a crucial role in helping pregnant women recognize pregnancy danger signs and make informed decisions regarding appropriate healthcare seeking. However, constraints related to time, accessibility, and flexibility in the implementation of pregnancy classes may hinder the continuity of education at the community level. This community engagement program aimed to improve maternal health literacy among pregnant women and strengthen community health worker capacity through the digital transformation of pregnancy classes. The program was conducted over one month in the working area of Tateli Primary Health Center and involved 40 participants, comprising 25 pregnant women and 15 community health workers. The intervention was delivered through a WhatsApp group and consisted of four educational sessions using e-booklets and videos. Evaluation was conducted using pretest and posttest assessments to measure changes in participants’ knowledge. The results demonstrated a substantial improvement in knowledge. Among pregnant women, the mean knowledge score increased from 49.60 to 89.68, representing an increase of 40.08 points (p<0.001). Among community health workers, the mean knowledge score increased from 51.30 to 88.93, representing an increase of 37.63 points (p<0.001). These findings indicate that digital pregnancy classes can serve as an effective educational approach to strengthen maternal health literacy and community health worker capacity at the community level.

title: Digital twins for health and safety management in construction: a systematic review
container-title: Journal of Engineering, Design and Technology
c83a0ad8535923ccebeb5fe11a49a7d3264a6902.abstract: Purpose Despite regulatory and technological advances, construction health and safety (H&S) management remains hindered by poor hazard visibility, fragmented information and reactive decision-making. Digital twins (DTs) offer a proactive, integrated and data-driven approach by connecting physical construction environments with continuously updated virtual representations. However, evidence remains fragmented regarding how DT applications, enabling conditions and implementation challenges interact to improve H&S outcomes. This study aims to systematically review and synthesise evidence on DT-enabled H&S management during the construction stage. Design/methodology/approach A systematic literature review was conducted following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses guidelines, identifying 26 peer-reviewed journal articles from the Scopus and Web of Science databases. Bibliometric analysis and qualitative content synthesis were used to examine research trends, DT applications, implementation enablers, challenges and future research directions. Findings DTs are mainly applied to workforce monitoring, hazard detection, safety training, risk prediction and decision support. Implementation success relies on technological, organisational, human and institutional enablers, but is hindered by interoperability issues, data governance gaps, skill shortages, high costs and regulatory ambiguity. Current research remains technology-oriented, underemphasising socio-technical integration, governance and scale-up. Originality/value This study develops an integrated, context-sensitive socio-technical framework, grounded in socio-technical systems theory and the technology–organisation–environment framework, explaining how technological capabilities, organisational readiness and governance conditions collectively shape DT-enabled H&S outcomes. The framework directs future research while informing policy and practice to support the effective and scalable adoption of DT-enabled construction safety systems.

title: Adaptive scrambling-based hadamard transform for peak-to-average power ratio reduction in sixth-generation orthogonal time-frequency space waveforms
container-title: PeerJ Computer Science
a3f52dcd0e95235459db9a2ef81cdadd7c5a4ee6.abstract: Orthogonal time-frequency space (OTFS) modulation is a promising waveform for sixth-generation (6G) wireless systems owing to its robustness in high-mobility and doubly selective channels. However, the inherent two-dimensional symbol spreading and multicarrier synthesis of OTFS generates a high peak-to-average power ratio (PAPR), severely constraining power amplifier efficiency and causing nonlinear distortion and spectral regrowth. This study proposes an Adaptive Scrambling-Based Hadamard Transform (ASB-HT) framework that enables distortionless and side-information-free PAPR reduction through intrinsic data-driven adaptivity. Unlike static transform precoding or probabilistic candidate generation schemes, the proposed method embeds row-wise energy balancing within an orthogonal Hadamard precoder, structurally reducing the likelihood of deterministic peak alignment prior to inverse symplectic finite Fourier transform (ISFFT) spreading. A theoretical analysis establishes the relationship between excess kurtosis and PAPR tail probability, demonstrating that the proposed precoder reduces the fourth-order signal statistics and systematically suppresses the complementary cumulative distribution function (CCDF) of the PAPR. The scheme preserves signal energy, maintains receiver transparency, and introduces only marginal computational overhead. Simulation results across multiple grid sizes (64--512 subcarriers) demonstrate consistent gains, achieving up to 6 dB PAPR reduction at CCDF = 10 −3 and up to 7 dB signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) improvement at bit error rate (BER) = 10 −3 compared to conventional OTFS, selective mapping (SLM), discrete Fourier transform (DFT)-spread OTFS, genetic algorithm (GA), and deep neural network (DNN)-based approaches. The power spectral density analysis further confirmed the significant suppression of out-of-band emissions, validating the proposed framework for energy-efficient 6G OTFS transceivers.

title: Adaptive Attention and Optimization-Based Feature Refinement for Transformer-Driven Sentiment Classification
container-title: Computer and Decision Making: An International Journal
0f3e0429bf8025b7881a7f2cd500cdc8492fd74b.abstract: Sentiment analysis has become a fundamental task in natural language processing to extract public opinions from social media and online review platforms at a large scale. Recent machine learning, deep learning and transformer-based approaches have been significantly improved for sentiment classification. However, these models are still suffering from high-dimensional feature representations, redundant contextual information and unstable feature learning, which limit the classification accuracy and model generalization. To solve these problems, this paper proposes an Optimization-Guided Feature Refinement and Adaptive Attention RoBERTa (OGFAA-RoBERTa). OGFAA-RoBERTa reduced the feature dimensionality by an optimization-based feature selection technique and improved the model stability by a deep contextual feature extraction strategy. The OGFAA-RoBERTa incorporates preprocessing of data, optimization-guided feature refinement, adaptive attention learning and enhanced RoBERTa classifier to learn highly discriminative semantic representation while suppressing redundant contextual features. Experimental evaluation was performed on Sentiment140 and SemEval-2014 datasets. The OGFAA-RoBERTa achieves 92.34% accuracy on Sentiment140 and 88.76%, 92.43% and 85.74% on the Laptop14, Restaurant14 and Twitter subsets of SemEval-2014, respectively. The results show that the optimization-guided feature refinement and the adaptive attention can significantly improve the performance of sentiment classification, model stability and cross-domain generalization over the existing state-of-the-art methods.

title: Interacting multiple-model-driven robust adaptive factor graph optimization for GNSS/SINS/ODO positioning
container-title: Measurement Science and Technology
272cbbfd2cf49ecf60d74af188116033c2e47d3b.abstract: Abstract Integrated navigation systems often have limited awareness of environmental changes in complex settings. When global navigation satellite system (GNSS) signals are disrupted, mismatch in the measurement-noise model can substantially degrade positioning accuracy and stability. To address this problem, we propose an interacting multiple-model-driven innovation-adaptive factor graph optimization method (IMM-IAFGO). First, the IMM framework runs multiple noise models in parallel and updates their posterior probabilities using measurement innovations and prior knowledge, thereby estimating the measurement-noise covariance. The resulting estimate is then used to adaptively reconstruct the observation-information weights of the GNSS factor nodes in the factor graph. Second, robust estimation is achieved through a dynamic adjustment mechanism based on inter-frame innovations. Under severe GNSS signal distortion, odometry (ODO) aided by inertial measurement unit attitude feedforward is introduced to constrain the inter-frame displacement increments. Real-world vehicle experiments demonstrate that the proposed method significantly outperforms error-state Kalman filter, factor graph optimization, and adaptive factor graph. Specifically, it reduces the horizontal positioning root mean square error by 87.92%, 82.85%, and 23.72%, and the mean absolute error by 90.68%, 82.33%, and 26.38%, respectively. This method provides an effective strategy for achieving continuous and high-precision positioning in vehicle integrated navigation systems operating in complex environments.

title: Network analysis of attention deficit hyperactivity disorder traits and mental health indicators in Brazilian adults
container-title: PeerJ
2baf81f7ca9af97c29c0d2f2cfd481b2d996e33b.abstract: Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD), a neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by behavioral traits such as inattention, hyperactivity, and impulsivity, has been widely associated with mental health impairments. However, the presence of these traits alone does not determine diagnosis, as they must also cause significant functional impairment for the individual to fulfill diagnostic criteria. Therefore, this study aimed at exploring how ADHD traits are associated with mental health indicators in general population adults regardless of whether participants met full diagnostic criteria for the disorder. The Adult ADHD Self-Report Scale (ASRS) was used to screen ADHD traits in an online survey that also addressed mental health indicators such as excessive preoccupation, lack of meaning in life and substance use. Invitations were distributed via social media platforms. The final sample consisted of 2,159 Brazilian adult participants. Data were analyzed using network analysis. An undirected network was modeled using the Gaussian Graphical Model based on partial polychoric correlations, and regularization was applied using EBICglasso. The main network analysis was conducted for individual ADHD traits. Additional analyses were performed for the summed inattention and hyperactivity/impulsivity scores, for the total ASRS summed score, and for subgroups of participants exhibiting extreme levels of trait presentation. Results indicate that, in an adult community sample, association between ADHD traits and mental health impairment is predominantly indirect. This indirect association was commonly interposed by younger age and feelings of insecurity. The results were consistent across all analyses. Overall, our results suggest that the presence of ADHD traits alone is not strongly associated with mental health impairment in the general population. We propose that both research and clinical practice may benefit from further exploring and addressing intervening factors—such as insecurity—that could underlie the association between ADHD traits and mental health impairment observed in previous studies.

title: AI-Enabled Experience Orchestration: Coordinating Physical, Digital & Human Resources across Situational Customer Journeys
container-title: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
479827cd30030c3a07bb272e1365d49fd6349d5b.abstract: Purpose: The study creates AI-enabled experience orchestration (AIEO) to describe how service systems can orchestrate digital, physical and human resources as customer requirements vary through a journey. Design/methodology/approach: The study incorporates customer-journey, service-system, omni-channel and AIenabled service lenses. In a doctoral survey of 578 complete eligible herbal-cosmetics consumers, bounded phenomenon motivation has been administered instead of a test of AIEO; the survey did not include any AI measures. Findings: AIEO consists of situational sensing, matching of resources, sequencing and continuity journey. The relevance, coherence, confidence, reducing uncertainty and perceived control, subject to the complexity of journey, situational changeability, resource complementary features, readiness of AI and responsible governance theories these capabilities should function. Originality: The framework goes beyond channel connectivity and discrete points of contact with the AI system by imagining adaptive, journey-level coordination of heterogeneous services resources and keeping customer agency. Practical implications: Service managers ought to diagnose the existing customer need, activate the most appropriate resource, and maintain only authorized context and present meaningful override and human escalation.

title: Peningkatan Kemampuan Problem Solving Anak Usia 5-6 Tahun melalui Game Digital Edukasi Keselamatan Diri “Area Privasiku”
container-title: Pepatudzu : Media Pendidikan dan Sosial Kemasyarakatan
01422396139f05eb0fca13db16a15bdbafb4e499.abstract: The alarmingly high prevalence of sexual violence against young children underscore the urgent need for preventive efforts that strengthen children’s problem-solving competencies in potentially dangerous situations. This research aims to evaluate the effectiveness of “Area Privasiku”, a digital self-safety educational game, in enhancing problem-solving skills among children aged 5-6 years. a quantitative, pre-experimental One Group Pretest-Posttest design was employed, involving a sample of 30 children. Data were collected through an observation checklist comprehension of basic concepts, problem identification, formulation of initial responses and solutions, and recognition of preventive strategies. As the pretest and posttest scores did not meet the assumption pf normal distribution, the data were analyzed using the nonparametric Wilcoxon Signed Ranks Test. Findings revealed a marked improvement in mean scores, from 4.83 at pretest to 6.83 in the posttest, with the Wilcoxon test producing in a Z-value of -4.501 and a significance level of 0.000 (p < 0.05). These findings indicate an improvement in the problem-solving skills of children aged 5–6 years through the digital self-safety educational game "Area Privasiku." The improvement was evident in the overall score as well as in all seven indicators, with the largest gains occurring in the early stages of problem solving, namely understanding basic concepts and determining initial responses.

title: <b>Kontekstualisasi Islam Berkemajuan Dalam Transformasi Pembelajaran PAI Digital</b>
container-title: At-Tahabbu
d85472ab501b0c3ec3994aa3b1a84ae3606c3dc2.abstract: Digital transformation presents both opportunities and challenges for Islamic Religious Education (IRE), particularly regarding religious knowledge authority, unequal access, character formation, and the use of artificial intelligence. This study aims to examine the characteristics of Progressive Islam (Islam Berkemajuan) and develop a conceptual framework for contextualizing them in digitally mediated IRE. Employing a qualitative library research design, the study examines the Risalah Islam Berkemajuan, Islamic education scholarship, and publications on educational technology. The materials are interpreted through thematic categorization, critical reading, and conceptual synthesis. The analysis proposes that five characteristics of Islam Berkemajuan—monotheism, commitment to the Qur’an and Sunnah, ijtihad and renewal, moderation, and mercy for all creation—can inform five educational orientations: spiritual integrity, religious source literacy, critical innovation, inclusive dialogue, and digital social responsibility. The proposed framework connects value-based learning outcomes, purposeful technology selection, digital-issue-based inquiry, ethical guidance on AI use, and authentic reflective assessment. Digital transformation in IRE should therefore be assessed not simply by platform adoption but by the quality of religious reasoning and ethical practice it enables. As a conceptual proposal, the framework requires empirical validation.

title: Enhancing neural automatic short answer grading with attention masking, WordNet-based semantic enrichment, and ordinal regression
container-title: PeerJ Computer Science
40bf101ebf4bb7c9d8fbd95c42b20a4c85687d39.abstract: Automatic Short Answer Grading (ASAG) is an important task in educational technology and natural language processing (NLP), enabling efficient and consistent evaluation of open-ended student responses. Although recent neural architectures have achieved strong performance, further improvements are possible in model focus, semantic understanding, and score consistency. This study builds upon the hybrid convolutional neural network–bidirectional long short-term memory (CNN-BiLSTM) Siamese model by Chen et al. (2023) and introduces three complementary extensions. First, an attention masking mechanism is applied to enhance focus on relevant tokens and reduce noise from padding or less informative text. Second, semantic enrichment is achieved through the integration of WordNet-based lexical similarity, enabling the model to capture deeper relationships between conceptually related terms. Third, rank-consistent ordinal regression replaces categorical prediction to better reflect the ordered nature of grading. Experiments on three datasets (Haidir, Mohler, and Rahutomo) demonstrate that each enhancement improves performance, with the combined model achieving the strongest overall results. On average across datasets, the proposed framework reduces normalized mean absolute error (NMAE) from 0.117 to 0.087 and normalized root mean squared error (NRMSE) from 0.205 to 0.159, while increasing Pearson correlation from 0.703 to 0.806 and Spearman correlation from 0.708 to 0.792. These findings show that integrating attention refinement, external semantic knowledge, and ordinal modelling substantially enhances ASAG accuracy and ranking reliability. This work contributes to the development of more robust, linguistically grounded, and educationally meaningful ASAG systems for diverse learning contexts.

title: Digital empowerment for ecological governance in South China Sea island villages: mechanism, efficiency, and stakeholder network analysis
container-title: Frontiers in Marine Science
3836714deba612f4f735d05952af66e8f1637afb.abstract: Introduction Against the backdrop of global digital transformation and United Nations Sustainable Development Goal 14 (SDG 14: Life Below Water), digital technologies may mitigate ecological degradation and strengthen governance capacity in geographically isolated island villages. South China Sea island villages face coral reef decline, coastal eutrophication, and fragmented multi-stakeholder collaboration, yet digital governance research lacks island-specific frameworks and integrated quantitative evidence. This study develops a mixed-methods framework linking the empowerment mechanism, measured efficiency, and stakeholder network. Methods We combined a qualitative mechanism analysis with a slack-based DEA model (DEA-SBM), a bootstrap-truncated second-stage regression of efficiency drivers, and social network analysis (SNA), using 30 semi-structured stakeholder interviews (2021–2023), field surveys, administrative and platform records, and panel data from ten representative island villages over 2019–2023. Results A three-dimensional mechanism—technical, collaborative, and regulatory empowerment—operates along a sky–sea–land perceptionintelligent decision-makingcoordinated execution chain. Mean comprehensive efficiency was 0.77, rising from 0.69 in 2019 to 0.81 in 2023. Collaboration intensity and technical–scenario matching were positively associated with efficiency, whereas resident participation capacity and island area were only marginally associated; all findings are correlational rather than causal. The government-dominated network was moderately dense. Discussion The framework extends digital marine governance theory to small-island contexts; given the ten-unit sample, associations are cautious rather than causal. Targeted measures—collaborative platforms, scenario-matched technology, resident digital capacity, and slack-input reallocation—support reef conservation and offer replicable insights for vulnerable island ecosystems worldwide.

title: Drift-Aware Dynamic Ensemble Learning for Adaptive Email Spam Detection
container-title: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
5c8fe7875cd4bd64e9dbaea835f3aaf6db34d9b0.abstract: Email spam evolves every day with disguised text, changing campaigns, dangerous links and quick changing message patterns. This research aims at proposing a different email spam detection ensemble-learning framework from the one proposed in the IEEE MENACOMM-2025 project which combines SVC, MLP, and ET. The proposed system uses character n-gram feature hashing and light-weight message statistics, and consists of three online linear base-learners: Ridge Classifier, SGD Classifier with modifiedHuber loss, Passive-Aggressive Classifier. DWM ensemble: an ensemble changes the weight of the learners over time and ADWIN detects changes in the distribution of emails and adapts the weight of the weak learners. The system is deployed with a Django based email client interface which takes the fields of sender, topic and message content and returns a Spam or Legitimate/NonSpam with confidence and key indicators. The comparison illustrates that the proposed DWM+ADWIN configuration has improved accuracy of 98.2%, precision of 97.7%, recall of 98.0% and F1-score of 97.8%, and recovers faster in a temporal distribution shift, compared to static classifiers. The focus of the framework is on adaptation, low memory text representation, operational false positive control, and practical web deployment.

title: Yapay Zekâ Çağında Hemşirelik: Dijital Dönüşüm ve Bakım Uygulamaları
ab6c38ade7217a9f984dc5186380d817ac824359.abstract: Bu kitap, yapay zekâ ve dijital sağlık teknolojilerinin hemşirelik mesleği üzerindeki etkilerini eğitim, klinik uygulama, yönetim ve araştırma alanları açısından ele almaktadır. Yapay zekâ okuryazarlığı ve dijital yetkinliklerden hemşirelik eğitimindeki dönüşüme, klinik kullanım alanlarından yapay zekâ destekli karar verme ve hasta güvenliğine kadar birbiriyle ilişkili konuları kapsamaktadır. Mahremiyet, algoritmik önyargı, insan denetimi, hukuki boyutlar ve sağlık politikaları, teknolojinin sorumlu kullanımını değerlendiren başlıca konular arasındadır. Kitapta ayrıca üretken yapay zekâ, yenilikçi uygulamalar, dijital sağlık ekosistemindeki dönüşüm ve bilimsel kanıtların klinik uygulamaya aktarılması incelenmektedir. Eser, teknolojik gelişmelerin sunduğu olanaklarla birlikte sınırlılıkları ve riskleri de değerlendirerek dijital dönüşüme bütüncül bir bakış sunmayı amaçlamaktadır. Yapay zekâ ve dijital teknolojiler, hemşirelik bilgisini, klinik muhakemeyi ve mesleki sorumluluğu destekleyen araçlar olarak ele alınmaktadır. İnsan odaklı bakım, etik ilkeler, bilimsel kanıtlar ve bireylerin gereksinimleri kitabın temel yaklaşımını oluşturmaktadır. Hemşirelik öğrencileri, akademisyenler, klinik hemşireler, hemşire yöneticiler ve diğer sağlık profesyonelleri için hazırlanan kitap, dijital yetkinliklerin geliştirilmesine ve sağlık teknolojilerinin etik ve güvenli kullanımına yönelik farkındalığa katkı sağlamayı hedeflemektedir.

title: Yapay Zekâ Çağında Hemşirelik: Dijital Dönüşüm ve İnsan Odaklı Bakım
container-title: Yapay Zekâ Çağında Hemşirelik: Dijital Dönüşüm ve Bakım Uygulamaları
e617c90c3620cf20f8912a5a59dc55c4b3b616fa.abstract: Sağlık alanında kullanılan yapay zekâ robotları, hemşirenin rutin görevlerini üstlenerek iş yükünü azaltmış, hemşirelerin hastalarıyla daha fazla zaman geçirmesini sağlamıştır. Özellikle sağlık alanında yapay zekâ kavramıyla yapay zekânın uygulama alanları, sık kullanılan yapay zekâ araçları, robotlar ve yapay zekânın avantaj ve dezavantajlarından bahsedilmiştir. Yapay zekâ çağında hemşirelik mesleği farklı bir bakış açısıyla ele alınmış ve hemşirelerin gelecekteki rollerini nasıl şekillendirdiğine odaklanılmıştır. Yapay zekânın hemşirelik uygulaması ile birleştirilmesi ile birlikte ortaya çıkacak etik ve mahremiyet ihlalleri konularına değinerek, teknolojiyi insan merkezli bakımla birleştirmenin yöntemlerini keşfetmeye çalışmıştır. Yapay zekânın insanlara sunduğu potansiyel fırsatları keşfederken, bu keşif sürecinde hemşirelik mesleğinin sahip olduğu değerleri nasıl koruyabileceğine dair konular da ele alınmıştır. Yapay zekânın hemşirelik mesleğine bir tehdit olarak değil, insan merkezli bakımı güçlendiren bir ortak olduğu üzerinde durulmuştur.

title: Hemşirelikte Yapay Zekâ Okuryazarlığı ve Dijital Yetkinlikler

9f5870dedb20d7e75d599df75522a38cd6876a71.abstract: Yapay zekânın (YZ) sağlık hizmetlerine entegre olması, hemşirelik mesleği açısından yalnızca teknolojik bir değişimi değil, klinik bilginin üretilme, yorumlanma ve bakım kararlarına dönüştürülme biçiminde köklü bir dönüşümü de beraberinde getirmektedir. Bu nedenle YZ kullanımının eleştirel düşünme ve klinik muhakemeyi zayıflatmayacak şekilde yapılandırılması gerekmektedir. Ancak teknolojinin eğitimde etkili kullanımı, yalnızca dijital araçların müfredata eklenmesini değil; YZ okuryazarlığı, dijital yetkinlik, etik farkındalık, eleştirel düşünme ve klinik muhakemenin bütünleştirildiği insan merkezli bir eğitim yaklaşımını gerektirmektedir. Geleceğin hemşirelerini dijital sağlık ekosistemine hazırlamak için hemşirelik müfredatlarının YZ ve dijital sağlık teknolojilerini kapsayacak biçimde güncellenmesi ve öğretim elemanlarının dijital pedagojik yeterliliklerinin güçlendirilmesi önem taşımaktadır.

title: Hemşirelikte Yapay Zekâ Uygulamaları: Klinik Kullanım Alanları ve Bakım Süreçleri

Hemşirelerin hastalarla doğrudan ve sürekli etkileşim içinde olması, YZ destekli sistemlerin klinik uygulamadaki fırsatlarının yanı sıra ortaya çıkabilecek risklerin yönetiminde de hemşireleri önemli bir konuma getirmektedir. YZ tabanlı erken uyarı ve klinik karar destek sistemleri; klinik kötüleşme, düşme ve diğer istenmeyen olayların öngörülmesi, hasta izleminin desteklenmesi, ilaç güvenliğinin artırılması ve klinik verilerin bütüncül biçimde değerlendirilmesi açısından önemli olanaklar sunmaktadır. Bununla birlikte, veri kalitesi ve güvenilirliği, algoritmik yanlılık, hasta mahremiyeti, veri güvenliği, açıklanabilirlik, otomasyon yanlılığı ve sorumluluğun belirlenmesi gibi önemli riskler bulunmaktadır. Özellikle eksik, hatalı veya farklı hasta gruplarını yeterince temsil etmeyen verilerle geliştirilen algoritmalar, klinik kararların doğruluğunu ve eşitliğini olumsuz etkileyebilmektedir. Bu bağlamda YZ sistemlerinin klinik uygulamalara entegrasyonu yalnızca teknolojik performans üzerinden değil, hasta güvenliği, bakım kalitesi, etik ilkeler ve mesleki sorumluluk çerçevesinde değerlendirilmelidir. YZ destekli karar süreçlerinde nihai klinik sorumluluk sağlık profesyonellerinin denetiminde kalmalı; hemşireler algoritmik çıktıları eleştirel biçimde değerlendirmeli, hasta verileri ve klinik bağlamla karşılaştırmalı ve gerektiğinde sistem önerisini reddedebilmelidir. Bu bölümde hemşirelikte YZ'nin başlıca klinik uygulama alanları, potansiyel riskleri ve risk yönetimi yaklaşımları ele alınmakta; güvenli, etik ve insan merkezli klinik karar verme açısından insan denetiminin önemi tartışılmaktadır.

title: Yapay Zekâ Destekli Klinik Karar Verme ve Hasta Güvenliği

Hemşirelik bakımında ise yapay zekâdan yararlanılırken klinik bilgi ve deneyimin yanı sıra insan merkezli bakım ve empati gibi temel unsurların korunması önem taşımaktadır. Sonuç olarak, yapay zeka hemşirelik alanına entegrasyonu, etik çerçeveler gözetildiği sürece hasta bakımında verimlilik ve kalite artışı sağlayacak önemli bir fırsat olarak değerlendirilebilir. Bu süreçte hasta haklarının korunması ve insani bakım anlayışının önceliklendirilmesi, teknolojinin insan odaklı kullanımı açısından vazgeçilmezdir.

title: Yapay Zekâ Hemşireliğinde Hukuki Düzenlemeler ve Sağlık Politikaları

Sonuç olarak YZ'nin hemşirelikte güvenilir ve sürdürülebilir biçimde kullanılabilmesi, teknolojik gelişmelerin hukuki güvenceler, etik ilkeler ve insan merkezli bakım anlayışıyla bütünleştirilmesine bağlıdır.

title: Kanıta Dayalı Hemşirelik ve Yapay Zeka: Kanıtın Klinik Uygulamaya Aktarılması ve Kullanımı

c822ba0ddbc24338660d1a768e14b8d4fe39ae10.abstract: Kanıta dayalı hemşirelik, en iyi bilimsel kanıtların klinik deneyim, bireyin değerleri ve tercihleri ile bakım koşulları doğrultusunda bütünleştirilmesini esas almaktadır. Yapay zekâ (YZ) teknolojilerindeki gelişmeler, klinik karar desteği, risk tahmini, hasta izlemi, hemşirelik dokümantasyonu ve hasta eğitimi gibi alanlarda yeni olanaklar sunmakla birlikte, bu teknolojilerin klinik uygulamaya aktarılması bilimsel geçerlilik, güvenlik, etik sorumluluk ve uygulanabilirlik açısından dikkatli değerlendirme gerektirmektedir. Bu çalışmanın amacı, kanıta dayalı hemşirelik ile yapay zekâ arasındaki ilişkiyi incelemek ve bilimsel kanıtın klinik uygulamaya güvenli, etkili ve sürdürülebilir biçimde entegrasyonuna yönelik temel ilkeleri ortaya koymaktır. Çalışma kapsamında YZ'nin hemşirelik bakımındaki kullanım alanları; klinik kanıtın değerlendirilmesi, klinik iş akışlarına ve elektronik sağlık kayıtlarına entegrasyon, hasta güvenliği, klinik kullanılabilirlik, alarm yorgunluğu, otomasyon yanlılığı, insan gözetimi, veri güvenliği ve uygulama sonrası performans izlemi çerçevesinde ele alınmaktadır. Ayrıca enfeksiyonların önlenmesi, onkoloji, kronik hastalık yönetimi, ruh sağlığı, toplum ve evde bakım, çocuk ve kadın sağlığı ile yaşlı bakımındaki uygulamalar değerlendirilmektedir. Kurgusal bir klinik vaka üzerinden, risk tahmin modelinin teknik performansı ile klinik yarar arasındaki ayrım açıklanmakta ve yapay zekâ çıktılarının hemşirelik değerlendirmesinin yerine geçmemesi gerektiği vurgulanmaktadır. Değerlendirme sonucunda, YZ sistemlerinin klinik kullanıma alınmasından önce uygun doğrulama çalışmalarının yapılması, yerel koşullarda performanslarının incelenmesi, hasta ve bakım veren gereksinimlerinin gözetilmesi ve insan gözetiminin güvence altına alınması gerektiği ortaya konulmaktadır. Sonuç olarak yapay zekâ, hemşirenin mesleki muhakemesini ve kişi merkezli bakım sorumluluğunu ikame eden bir araç olarak değil, bilimsel kanıtla desteklendiği ve sürekli denetlendiği koşullarda klinik kararları ve bakım süreçlerini geliştirebilecek tamamlayıcı bir teknoloji olarak değerlendirilmelidir.

title: One product, two rulebooks: the cybersecurity of high-risk AI systems between article 15 AI act and the cyber resilience act after the digital omnibus
container-title: International Cybersecurity Law Review
959eb7b5c5ca4aa295e6151af6cd673982e3233c.abstract: Abstract High-risk AI systems distributed as software or embedded in connected hardware are simultaneously subject to two horizontal security rulebooks: the accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity requirements of Art. 15 of the AI Act and the essential cybersecurity requirements of the Cyber Resilience Act (CRA). The Union legislature anticipated this overlap and built a bridge: under Art. 12 CRA—since July 2026 mirrored in Art. 42(3) AI Act, as inserted by the Digital Omnibus on AI (Regulation (EU) 2026/1744)—products with digital elements that are classified as high-risk AI systems are deemed to comply with the cybersecurity requirements of Art. 15 AI Act if they satisfy the CRA’s essential requirements and the achievement of the Art. 15 protection level is demonstrated in the CRA declaration of conformity, with the conformity assessment, as a rule, integrated into the AI Act procedure. The Omnibus has re-sequenced the two regimes: the high-risk obligations for stand-alone Annex III systems, deferred to 2 December 2027, now become applicable nine days before the CRA’s main obligations on 11 December 2027, whereas high-risk AI embedded in Annex I products follows on 2 August 2028, and the CRA’s reporting duties have bound manufacturers—including of AI products already on the market—since 11 September 2026. Drawing on the consolidated legislative texts, the Commission’s CRA guidance of July 2026 and the standardisation work of CEN-CENELEC JTC 13 and JTC 21, this article maps the scope overlap, analyses the mechanics and limits of the bridge—the accuracy and robustness carve-out, the narrowly drawn derogation for important and critical products in Art. 12(3) CRA, and the gap between AI-specific attack vectors and the CRA’s generic essentials—and argues that the bridge is coherent on a reading, anchored in the recitals of both acts, under which the adversarial-machine-learning threat model enters the CRA’s risk-based essentials. It translates the analysis into an integrated compliance architecture with a structured requirement-to-evidence mapping and formulates recommendations addressed separately to the Commission and the standardisation bodies, and to providers and manufacturers.

title: The 2C model: examining the synergy between institutions to improve digital literacy
container-title: Management Decision
e341ef896a5d38f086241a3973356b8ee15b9280.abstract: Purpose This research aimed to (1) analyze the ability of government and nongovernment institutions in coordinating and collaborating to form institutional synergy in empowering digital literacy in micro, small and medium enterprise (MSME) and (2) formulate a “2C” Model (coordination and collaboration) that facilitates effective institutional synergy Design/methodology/approach Qualitative and quantitative methods were used with informants from institutions within the city government and state-owned enterprises. Qualitatively, in-depth interviews were conducted to obtain information on the implementation of coordination and collaboration. Quantitatively, weaknesses, opportunities and threats from the implementation of coordination and cooperation were analyzed to obtain strengths Findings Public institutions underexamined coordination and collaboration despite shared objectives, leading to fragmented programs and underutilized resources. This research proposed 2C model, positioning coordination and collaboration as a foundational process and strategic mechanism to integrate cross-sector resources and build institutional synergy for enhancing digital literacy in a developing-country context. Originality/value The results connect two institutions under different leadership with the same goal of improving digital literacy in MSME. Therefore, the developed 2C model serves as a guide for institutions to synergize, coordinate and collaborate, combining various inputs and processes to increase the number of small and micro businesses.

title: A Moodle Lesson for Pre-Simulation Endodontic Training for Third-Year Dental Students: A Preliminary Satisfaction Study
container-title: Digital Educational Technologies
a0d355b7e4897dd599cb3fc590b07e779939f95e.abstract: Simulation-based education plays an increasingly important role in dental curricula, supporting the acquisition of psychomotor and cognitive skills in a controlled, low-risk environment. Learning management systems such as Moodle can further enhance this process by providing structured, interactive learning units that prepare students for hands-on training on high-fidelity simulators. This study describes the development and preliminary evaluation of an interactive Moodle lesson used as pre-simulation preparation in Endodontics for thirdyear dental students at the Medical University of Plovdiv. An interactive learning unit titled “Endodontic Access Cavity Preparation” was developed using the Lesson activity in Moodle. The learning unit included clearly defined objectives, nonlinear navigation paths, and multimodal content (text, images, and short video clips), and embedded formative questions to maintain interactivity. It was implemented in both Bulgarian- and English-taught groups of third-year dental students. Student satisfaction was assessed via an anonymous electronic questionnaire following lesson completion. Data was exported and analyzed quantitatively using IBM SPSS Statistics version 23. Results indicate high levels of student satisfaction across both language groups. Participants reported that the structure and multimodal presentation made the material interesting and engaging, and the nonlinear pathways supported a sense of personalization and choice in learning. Students also stated that the lesson was suitable for self-directed preparation before working with a high-technology dental simulator and helped them better understand key steps in endodontic access cavity preparation. No significant difference in satisfaction levels was observed between Bulgarian- and English-speaking cohorts Integrating interactive Moodle lessons as preparatory tools for simulation-based training in dental education positively influences student engagement and learning satisfaction. The approach supports personalized learning and serves as an effective bridge between theoretical instruction and practical application on high-fidelity simulators.

title: Integration of AI into Management Accounting Education
container-title: Digital Educational Technologies
3304231ea0d6e9259b8785884fbd7581e74971ca.abstract: Technological progress is a continuous process that changes perceptions and approaches to the implementation of various types of activities. This is how artificial intelligence (AI) appears and is applied in most areas of our lives. Its spread in school environments is increasing and developing in different directions which suggests that higher education also needs to build application standards. Its establishment as a method of training is an important component for the incorporation of students in the business environment. The integration of AI into everyday economic activities is constantly growing. Building models for the use of artificial intelligence is becoming a major component in the formation of work competencies. Management accounting is among the fastest-growing economic sciences, which also implies the development of relevant training. It is significant to develop an approach to the use of AI in management accounting training, since lack of familiarity with the system creates undesirable effects from its application.

title: Artificial Intelligence as a Tool for Supporting the Education of Students with Special Educational Needs
container-title: Digital Educational Technologies
639aa489cc349b7eab91605b3c79c1eaf332e160.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly recognized as a promising tool for supporting inclusive education and addressing the diverse learning needs of students with special educational needs (SEN). Its potential lies in facilitating content adaptation, personalized learning, differentiated instruction, multimodal access to information, and enhanced educational support. At the same time, international organizations emphasize that the implementation of AI should be guided by human-centered, ethical, and inclusive principles (UNESCO, 2021, 2023, 2024; OECD, 2024). This study explores educational professionals’ attitudes toward the use of AI in supporting students with SEN. The research involved 121 participants, including teachers, resource teachers, special educators, psychologists, speech and language therapists, and preschool teachers. Data were collected through a structured questionnaire examining digital readiness, previous experience with AI, perceived pedagogical opportunities, perceived risks, and readiness for implementation. The findings indicate generally positive attitudes toward AI. Participants identified content adaptation, individualized task design, differentiated instruction, and teacher support as the most valuable opportunities. A strong positive relationship was found between perceived pedagogical opportunities and readiness to implement AI, while perceived risks did not significantly reduce implementation readiness. Qualitative findings further revealed that participants view AI primarily as a tool for personalization and educational support rather than as a replacement for the teacher. The study concludes that the successful integration of AI in inclusive education depends on teacher preparedness, ethical governance, and the preservation of the teacher’s central role in the educational process.

title: A Model for the Digitalization of Administrative Processes in the Development and Monitoring of University Curricula
container-title: Digital Educational Technologies
d8f1a90ceae5ebf60c0c4485478d22f5fb92869c.abstract: This article presents a rule-based model and a prototype tool for the digitalization of administrative activities related to the development of university curricula. The research aims to overcome challenges associated with manual data entry, the calculation of teaching hours and ECTS credits, and similar tasks. The methodology employed includes a functional analysis of activities, modeling of the curriculum structure, formalization of regulatory and organizational rules, and practical validation. The curriculum is represented as a system of interconnected specialization blocks, semesters, compulsory, elective, and optional courses, as well as graduation requirements. Based on the developed model, a prototype tool (an intelligent e-template) was implemented. It provides automated calculations, controls permissible actions during curriculum creation and editing, performs final checks for structural, quantitative, and logical inconsistencies, and generates data on teaching staff allocation, part-time and distance learning formats, and a translation-ready copy. The results demonstrate that formalizing administrative rules as executable checks reduces the risk of technical errors, improves traceability, and enables the single entry and multiple use of data. The development holds both scientific and practical value as a viable model for the digitalization of university administrative processes.

title: The Vulnerability of Traditional Examination Forms in Distance Learning in the Era of Large Language Models (LLMs)
container-title: Digital Educational Technologies
060a695e0f7a0237b27eef5929f03d933fa22778.abstract: This study examines the impact of generative artificial intelligence (GAI) — specifically text-generating Large Language Models (LLMs) — on assessment methods in a digital learning environment, illustrated by a specific case from the field of finance. The widespread adoption of GAI in the educational environment calls into question the validity of established forms of remote assessment. The paper analyzes the vulnerability of a multi-component written assignment in a finance course through a benchmark experiment: reference answers generated by three text-generating systems are compared with real student works in a distance learning format. The results reveal moderate to high levels of similarity with LLM-generated reference answers among a significant proportion of participants. This trend is characterized by distinct stylistic markers, structural similarities across assignments, and indications of possible AI reliance. The findings are discussed in terms of their implications for the reliability of remote assessment and teaching practice, and practical recommendations for adapting assessment to the changing technological environment are proposed.

title: A Moodle Quiz for Pre-Simulation Endodontic Training for Third-Year Dental Students
container-title: Digital Educational Technologies
1ef88a4c10d6fb21a762a32de9943ec6757f5a12.abstract: Simulation-based training is central to contemporary conservative dentistry curricula. Embedding assessment-as-learning activities in a learning management system such as Moodle may further enhance self-regulation, metacognition, and preparedness for high-technology simulation. This study describes the design and preliminary evaluation of an interactive formative quiz on “Endodontic access cavity preparation” used as pre-simulation assessment-as-learning in third-year dental students at the Medical University of Plovdiv. A Moodle interactive quiz with multiple attempts on “Endodontic access cavity preparation” was developed. The quiz included different question types and allowed repeated attempts without penalty, with targeted hints for incorrect responses and explanatory feedback for correct answers. The activity was implemented in both Bulgarian- and English-taught cohorts of third-year dental students in Conservative dentistry. Students’ perceptions of the quiz as an assessment-as-learning tool were collected through an anonymous electronic questionnaire administered after quiz completion. Data were analysed using IBM SPSS Statistics v.23. Findings indicate high levels of satisfaction with the interactive quiz among both Bulgarian- and English-speaking students. Learners reported that the quiz helped them not only check and consolidate their knowledge but also monitor their progress over time by analysing their results across multiple attempts. Students ed the detailed feedback supported error analysis, guided correction of misconceptions, and informed adjustments in their learning strategies. Participants perceived the quiz as a suitable tool for self-directed preparation before practice on a high-technology dental simulator. The results suggest that an interactive Moodle quiz configured for assessment as learning is a feasible and well-received approach to support pre-simulation preparation in conservative dentistry. Further work will examine relationships between quiz engagement, changes in self-reported learning strategies, and performance in subsequent simulation sessions.

title: Pedagogical Capabilities of Generative Artificial Intelligence in Support of the Modern Teacher
container-title: Digital Educational Technologies
2422dabe29d98f3476027bb57ccfce7086787556.abstract: Amidst digitalization and globalization, the educational process is undergoing significant changes driven by the adoption of modern digital technologies and tools based on artificial intelligence. The development of generative artificial intelligence opens up new opportunities for education and places new demands on teachers’ professional competence. This paper analyzes the pedagogical potential of generative artificial intelligence as a means of supporting the teaching profession and highlights its capacity to enhance the quality of instruction.

title: The Myth of Mankurt and a Conceptual Framework for Digital Food Identity and Data Sovereignty in Kyrgyzstan
container-title: Agriculture Economics Review
000ff7e11d8dda8127b30beea74de748500b3067.abstract: This paper introduces the concept of digital food identity, in which Ch. Aitmatov’s rethought myth of mankurt serves as an analytical lens to criticise digital food regimes and processes of digital mankurtisation. Using Kyrgyzstan as an illustrative documentary case, the paper examines how policy, service, and media materials frame data governance, local knowledge, and food-cultural diversity in agrifood digitalisation. The analysis identifies a potential representational and governance gap: efficiency, traceability, registries, and administrative integration are more visible in the analysed corpus than farmer data rights, local knowledge, and food-cultural practices. This finding concerns documentary representation and institutional framing; it does not demonstrate the loss of local practices or the experiences of farmers and consumers. We developed a typology of digital mankurtisation levels (epistemological, regulatory, infrastructural, and political-economic). We introduced the “field scout of data” institute as an element of humanistic digital food policy, aimed at strengthening food sovereignty and the cultural diversity of food in the digital age.

title: Derechos civiles y políticos de los trabajadores migratorios en la era digital. Regularidad, irregularidad y efectividad
Civil and political rights of migrant workers in the digital age.  Regularity, Irregularity and Effectiveness
container-title: REVISTA ELECTRONICA IBEROAMERICANA
ef5e9c28dedeae82ea32281b01f8b060ba178ad6.abstract: El artículo examina los derechos civiles y políticos de los trabajadores migratorios a partir de la distinción entre situación regular e irregular en el sistema universal de Naciones Unidas. El análisis comparado entre el Pacto Internacional de Derechos Civiles y Políticos y la Convención de los Trabajadores Migratorios de 1990 muestra que la irregularidad no excluye a los trabajadores migratorios de un núcleo amplio de derechos, aunque ciertos ámbitos admiten diferencias vinculadas a la legalidad de la estancia, la regularidad o la ciudadanía. El estudio sostiene que la divergencia más intensa aparece en la efectividad. El riesgo de identificación, detención o expulsión puede inhibir el acceso a la justicia, la libertad de asociación y otros derechos formalmente universales. El Pacto Mundial para la Migración confirma esta tensión en el plano de la gobernanza y sus revisiones muestran una aplicación desigual, mientras que la digitalización y la inteligencia artificial incrementan la capacidad de detectar y utilizar el estatuto migratorio, con efectos sobre privacidad, no discriminación, debido proceso y libertades públicas.

title: Beyond the digital divide: Analyzing the influence of digital media literacy on political participation among Gen Z and Millennials
container-title: Perspectives in Social Sciences
32333249f7dfcd3911b865d6273569367133c929.abstract: Digital media literacy is crucial in understanding how people interact with political information and engage in digital spaces. Since Gen Z and Millennials use their digital skills in different ways, their relationship with online political engagement patterns also differ between these cohort. The current paper analyzed the influence of digital media literacy on online political participation of Gen Z and Millennials. Based on the idea of cognitive perspectives of digital literacy and digital inequality research, the paper considered technical competence, source identification, assessment of online data and critical evaluation skills as relevant factors for studying the influence on political participation. This paper adopted quantitative research design to analyze the influence of digital media literacy on online political participation of Gen Z and Millennials. A survey approach was used and survey questionnaire was distributed among students and staff of NUML Rawalpindi and Islamabad. A total of 191 respondents participated in the study, out of which 90 were Millennial, while 101 were Gen Z. Using hierarchal regression, the influence of digital media literacy on online political participation of both generations was investigated and results indicated a positive relationship between DML and online political participation across both cohorts. However, DML had a strong influence on political participation of Millennials more than Gen Z. Millennials strong critical evaluation skills and reflective awareness make them more capable of engaging in meaningful political activities on social media. These findings highlight why it is important to study DML and its relationship with online political participation.
