title: Examining Digital Egalitarianism through the Moderating Effect of Job Level on G2E Systems Adoption
container-title: Jurnal Sistem Informasi
5978097f6050b981d9d7f9038f1aa5ef0f4aedff.abstract: To support budget efficiency and bureaucratic reform, while embodying the ASN “Adaptive” Core Value regarding technology, it is essential to evaluate the existing Government-to-Employee (G2E) systems in the Deputy of Economic Cooperation and Investment, Coordinating Ministry of Economic Affairs, Republic of Indonesia. In this context, the Sipentakel platform was developed to digitally integrate program and governance services. This study aims to evaluate the performance of Sipentakel by employing a hybrid framework that integrates the DeLone & McLean IS Success Model, the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology (UTAUT), and the Human-Organization-Technology (HOT) Fit model. Additionally, this study assesses the moderating role of Job Level on the relationship between Human Factors and Behavioral Intention. The analysis was performed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) on data from 52 system users. The findings indicate that Behavioral Intention to use the system is significantly driven by Human and Technology factors, whereas Organization factors and User Satisfaction do not demonstrate a significant effect. Furthermore, Net Benefits are primarily determined by Behavioral Intention. The Technology factor emerged as the most critical driver, suggesting that enhancing system and information quality is the most effective strategy for optimizing Sipentakel implementation. Notably, the assessment reveals that Job Level does not significantly moderate the influence of Human Factors on Behavioral Intention. This finding highlights a phenomenon of digital egalitarianism, indicating that user acceptance is driven by system utility rather than hierarchical position.

title: A Suitable-Area Selection Method for Road Vector Map Matching Based on a Hypergraph-Enhanced Graph Attention Network
container-title: Automation
90dcf703a10e120f8576e5a43a7beb54a8d11353.abstract: Suitable-area selection reduces candidate-search costs and mismatch risk in road vector map matching. Existing image-based assessments primarily characterize grayscale, texture, and edge saliency, whereas the suitability of road vector maps depends on road continuity, intersection organization, and topological uniqueness. This study proposes a high-confidence suitable-area selection framework based on a Hypergraph-Enhanced Graph Attention Network (HG-GAT). A road-network suitability dataset is constructed using offline matching results. Candidate regions are represented as road graphs, with semantic hyperedges encoding road chains, intersection stars, and key-node neighborhoods. Hypergraph propagation and graph attention jointly learn high-order structural relations and pairwise road connections, while dual-channel readout integrates regional organization and salient local structures. On the Wuhan test data, HG-GAT achieves an accuracy of 0.8074, an F1-score of 0.8309, and a Precision@10% of 0.8980, the highest values for these metrics among the compared methods. It retains high-confidence candidates with a recall of 0.9467 while reducing false selections relative to the image-based and ordinary graph-learning baselines. The results support the value of semantic high-order topology for distinguishing structurally effective road regions and prioritizing candidates for subsequent matching.

title: Pain Sensitivity and Digital Hoarding as an Avoidance Behavior on Social Media: A Moderated Mediation Model Involving Fear of Pain and Dispositional Greed
container-title: Behavioral Sciences
d8a701336a7a0f376124447914e9f27a00fec46e.abstract: In the past decade, both the public health significance of pain and research interest in digital hoarding behavior have increased. The current research investigates whether these two increasingly studied phenomena are connected and, if so, their associated psychological processes and boundary conditions, with a specific focus on the context of social media as a form of popular media. We conducted a cross-sectional survey study with 1054 social media users. The results indicated that pain sensitivity is associated with digital hoarding behavior and that fear of pain mediates this association. Moreover, dispositional greed moderates the association between pain sensitivity and digital hoarding behavior such that this association is stronger for social media users with high dispositional greed. Dispositional greed also moderates the association between fear of pain and digital hoarding behavior such that the association is stronger for social media users with low dispositional greed. The psychological processes and differential moderating role of dispositional greed deepen the understanding of the associations between pain sensitivity and digital hoarding behavior within the realm of popular media use.

title: Climate Vulnerability and Adaptive Capacity in Selected Cyclone-Prone Communities of Southern Africa: A Comparative Gendered Analysis of Mozambique, Malawi, and Madagascar
container-title: Climate
aec54acfcd2c9588ba1b3a01eabb595b9d1b1167.abstract: This study comparatively assesses household climate vulnerability and adaptive capacity across cyclone-prone communities in Mozambique, Malawi, and Madagascar through a gendered lens. Drawing on 2618 primary household surveys, a Household Vulnerability Index (HVI) was constructed via Principal Component Analysis (PCA) within the IPCC exposure–sensitivity–adaptive capacity framework, with group differences evaluated using ANOVA and Bonferroni post hoc tests. The analysis tests three core hypotheses: cross-country differences in vulnerability (H1), gender as a determinant of vulnerability category membership (H2), and adaptive capacity as the primary driver of cross-country divergence (H3). Findings indicate that Mozambique’s study sites exhibit the highest vulnerability among the three countries, driven by compounding exposure, elevated sensitivity, and constrained adaptive capacity. Conversely, Malawi’s study sites present the lowest overall vulnerability as superior adaptive capacity offsets household vulnerability. Madagascar’s study sites occupy an intermediate position, with households concentrated in moderate vulnerability due to structural sensitivity and limited adaptive capacity. Although mean HVI scores are statistically indistinguishable across gender groups (F < 0.01; p = 0.980), category distributions reveal a gendered division of risk: male-headed households face higher direct occupational exposure, whereas female-headed households suffer structural deficits in adaptive capacity. These findings demonstrate that adaptive capacity, rather than physical exposure, is the primary driver of cross-country divergence in household vulnerability, and that gender restructures risk pathways rather than altering aggregate vulnerability levels. Targeted institutional investments in extension services, anticipatory action frameworks, and gender-responsive training are therefore critical pathways to vulnerability reduction in comparable low-income settings.

title: Supporting the EU Soil Monitoring Law Through Digital Soil Mapping: Evaluating Random Forest-Based Approaches in Tuscany (Italy)
container-title: Land
8fb0c691dec6e377294a850971ff1ac0fac63d87.abstract: Digital soil mapping (DSM) supports the implementation of the EU Soil Monitoring Law by providing spatially explicit information on key soil properties over large areas. Despite widespread use of machine learning techniques, the influence of modelling strategy and covariate quality on predictive performance remains unclear in heterogeneous regions. This study evaluated three Random Forest-based approaches, Random Forest (RF), Quantile Random Forest (QRF), and a regime-based model (RF-REGIME5), to predict topsoil properties (0–30 cm) across Tuscany (23,000 km2). Two predictor sets were tested: BASE (environmental covariates only) and AUGMENTED (with legacy soil data). Within the three RF-based approaches examined, the inclusion of legacy soil-derived predictors produced more consistent improvements in predictive performance than changes in modelling strategy. Soil-derived covariates improved predictive performance, while differences among modelling approaches were generally limited and property-dependent. QRF performed comparably and additionally quantified prediction uncertainty, especially for skewed variables like soil organic carbon. In contrast, the regime-based approach did not consistently outperform global models, as potential benefits from reduced environmental heterogeneity were offset by smaller sample sizes within individual domains. Overall, improving predictor datasets and expanding soil observation networks appear more effective than increasing model complexity for enhancing regional DSM applications and supporting future soil monitoring efforts.

title: Anisotropy in Images Varies with Spatial Frequency and Digital Category: Digital Images Present a Different World to the Viewer
container-title: Signals
1aa8220e66bc2bd11cf1dbe872ae20d8d2562fe6.abstract: Researchers have described the manner in which the low-level information from images varies with regard to orientation distribution, referred to as the level of anisotropy in an image. Prior work has described deviations from typical real-world (nature, suburban, urban) images in the content of various categories of digital images, including games, social media, and others. The present work extends prior findings by bandpass filtering images across nine categories, analyzing orientation content within each bandpass range and comparing anisotropy across spatial frequency. Anisotropy in this analysis was found to increase with spatial frequency; relatively isotropic orientation information was present in the low bandpass range across all image categories, while medium and high bandpass images show a pattern of increasing anisotropy in a category-dependent manner. In particular, deviations from the distribution defined by nature images characterize multiple categories of digital images; this finding is discussed in terms of potential implications for visual system plasticity and the potential for such changes to impact multiple facets of perception. Potential impacts of this finding on training sets for machine learning tools are also discussed.

title: Adaptive Behavior Challenges Increase Into Young Adulthood and Are Predicted by Parent‐Reported Executive Function in Autistic Youth
container-title: Autism Research
84529d208dbe2b1d8da8019104d2f9f73b609b9a.abstract: ABSTRACT Everyday adaptive behavior skills are a strong predictor of independence, mental health, and quality of life for autistic people. However, autistic individuals' adaptive skills are typically below expectation for their age and their intellectual abilities. Executive function is related to concurrent adaptive behavior, but few longitudinal studies have evaluated it as a predictor of adaptive behavior development over time. This study examines the trajectories of parent‐reported adaptive behavior skills in autistic youth from early childhood to young adulthood and their relationship to parent‐reported flexibility, working memory, and inhibition challenges. Leveraging a longitudinal sample of 313 participants (age range = 2–25 years; 64 females; Full Scale IQ: M = 103.3, range = 52–159; number of visits per participant: M = 3.01, range = 2–9) across a total of 941 visits, we examined trajectories of adaptive skills and their relationship to executive function challenges using multilevel growth curve modeling. Age‐related adaptive skills decline with age in autistic people from 2 to 25 years old, regardless of parent education level. Parent‐reported executive function challenges predict adaptive behavior scores across all adaptive skill domains. Adaptive behavior challenges endure across development for autistic people. Executive function is a key factor in adaptive outcomes, making it an important target for intervention and environmental supports.

title: CEPEX: Enhancing Corporate Event Prediction with Stock Price Dynamics and GRU-Attention Networks
container-title: INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF COMPUTERS  COMMUNICATIONS & CONTROL
371d163ba8874d3707b264fe6327481896cf2134.abstract: Accurate corporate event prediction (CEP) presents a significant challenge for decision-making in financial markets. In this work, we reframe the CEP task as a problem of forecasting the optimal next step in a corporate life-cycle sequence, and introduce CEPEX, a novel predictive framework that enhances a Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) attention-based model by uniquely incorporating quantified stock price dynamics alongside historical event sequences. Evaluated on the comprehensive Chinese Corporate Event Prediction (CCEP) dataset, CEPEX achieves a state-of-the-art accuracy of 84.28%. A key contribution of our work is the demonstration that stock market data provide notably stronger predictive power for future corporate actions than financial news. This framework improves decision-support systems in financial informatics and offers a new approach for predictive control in dynamic market environments.

title: Cross-Environment WiFi CSI Gesture Recognition Using a Domain-Generalized Multi-Scale Attention Residual Network with Robust Feature Learning
38a65505f6130cc5c844720fff816a2364fc9fc3.abstract: Abstract WiFi Channel State Information (CSI) records changes in wireless signals induced by hand and body motions, providing a practical and contact-free method of gesture recognition. Changes in the environment, multipath propagation, and signal circumstances might affect CSI patterns, making it tough to achieve consistent detection across varied indoor situations. In this paper, we provide a framework for WiFi CSI gesture recognition that works in any environment by using a robust feature-learning Domain-Generalized Multi-Scale Attention Residual Network. Meaningful patterns linked with various movements are identified by the framework via the use of CSI amplitude fluctuations throughout time and subcarriers. A Stable Field Various resolutions of the gesture are captured using multi-scale convolution, and the network is trained to concentrate on the most important features with the aid of channel and spatial attention. Stable model training and successful feature learning are both supported by residual connections. Evaluating performance in both learned and unknown situations, the trials take five gesture classes into account. The validation and training results for a robust domain demonstrate consistent recognition performance and continuous convergence. A Stable Field The framework’s recognition accuracy in the unseen test environment is 86%, while in the two training domains they are 94% and 91%, respectively. The t-SNE image further highlights the substantial differences across the gesture classes, suggesting that the learnt characteristics maintain their uniqueness even when exposed to different environments. A Stable Field According to the ablation research, each component contributes to the overall improvement in accuracy; for example, using multi-scale convolution increased accuracy from 72% to 79%, channel/spatial attention increased accuracy to 82%, and the full framework improved accuracy to 86%. A Stable Field The findings show that the suggested method can reliably and robustly recognize gestures based on WiFi CSI even when the interior environment is constantly changing.

title: Cloud-Native Digital Twin Architecture for Intelligent Microgrids: Real-Time Synchronization and Data-Driven Predictive Management
container-title: Green Energy and Environmental Technology
63575fdfd0841950c01e7efd1b6663b8a765e48f.abstract: Current electrical networks must be restructured to meet decarbonization targets and modern energy requirements, particularly due to the high integration of distributed resources, which complicates their management. In this context, this paper proposes a cloud-native digital twin architecture for real-time monitoring, predictive management, and decision support in a microgrid. The proposed model is based on an intelligent modular architecture implemented in a cloud environment. Each entity in the microgrid is modeled using the Digital Twins Definition Language, where updates are synchronized in real time. The architecture also integrates three machine learning models dedicated to prediction and diagnosis: (1) a multilayer perceptron (MLP) for predicting and real-time simulation of the microgrid behavior when a digital twin parameter is modified; (2) a temporal fusion transformer (TFT) model for sequential forecasting of power generation and demand; and (3) a Random Forest classifier for fault identification. The architecture was evaluated in a simulation-in-the-loop testbed comprising a MATLAB-Simulink microgrid model, a physical ESP32 communication interface, and a Node-RED dashboard. The results show consistent replication of the Simulink source telemetry in the cloud-based twin under the evaluated conditions. The MLP achieves mean absolute errors between 0.1 and 0.36 kW, while the TFT achieves an error of approximately 2 kW for Ppv. This integrated digital twin architecture, combining prediction and diagnosis in a cloud environment, provides a solid foundation for more efficient management of electrical microgrids.

41a036c7fbbda972f124e6931af287df58c0e266.abstract: Modern systems of systems (SoS) operating in high-stakes environments like Distributed Operational System (DOS) are characterized by tightly coupled interactions among human operators, autonomous agents, and heterogeneous technological subsystems. Conventional reliability engineering approaches, which primarily focus on component level failure probabilities and static models are often insufficient for capturing emergent behaviors and nonlinear failure propagation across interconnected sociotechnical systems. This study proposes a cybernetically informed framework that integrates digital twin technology, the Viable System Model (VSM) and an extended Failure Modes and Effects Criticality Analysis (FMECA) methodology to reconceptualise reliability as a dynamic and emergent system property. Digital twins function as continuously updated virtual representations that synchronise real time data, simulation models, and predictive analytics, enabling recursive observation and anticipatory regulation. Their integration with FMECA supports scenario based reliability analysis, allowing the modelling of cascading failures, coordination disruptions and adaptive system responses. The findings demonstrate that reliability emerges from system interactions rather than isolated components, advancing the design of adaptive, resilient, and self-regulating systems operating in complex and uncertain environments. Although applicable to systems of systems related contexts, the framework is intentionally generalised to support broader applications across critical infrastructure, healthcare coordination systems, industrial automation, autonomous transportation, emergency response networks and distributed cyber physical systems. Simulation experiments across distributed systems of systems networks demonstrate how local disturbances propagate through interconnected nodes and are mitigated through cybernetic feedback mechanisms. Simulation experiments across distributed systems of systems networks and demonstrate how local disturbances propagate through interconnected nodes and are mitigated through cybernetic feedback mechanisms. Monte Carlo analysis (n = 1000) indicates high robustness, with operational effectiveness (ζ = 0.929 ± 0.021) and system availability (A = 0.98 ± 0.015). Monte Carlo analysis indicates high robustness, with strong operational continuity and system availability across varying disruption scenarios.

title: Techno-Economic Optimization of a Hybrid PV-Wind-Battery Energy System for Adaptive Melon Greenhouse Using Priority-Based Load Management and HOMER Pro

64a895290e5722485011a7e8fdacd256c515c15a.abstract: Greenhouse automation requires reliable power; a load profile mismatched to available renewables inflates generation, storage and capital costs. This study assessed how priority-based load management affects demand, component sizing and initial cost of a hybrid renewable energy system for a 200 m² melon greenhouse in Trenggalek, East Java. HOMER Pro simulations, using Indonesian prices, compared three scenarios: PV-battery and PV-wind-battery at full load, and PV-wind-battery with priority-based load shedding. Loads were classed critical (pumps, sensors), semi-critical (fans) or flexible (night lighting). Load shedding cut daily consumption from 5.00 to 3.24 kWh (35.2%) and peak load from 1.06 to 0.76 kW (28.3%). Scenario three required 2.00 kW PV, three LiFePO4 batteries (3 kWh total), a 1.00 kW wind turbine and 1.00 kW converter, costing about $1,079.85. Relative to scenario one, PV and converter capacities halved and battery units fell 57.1%. Load prioritisation can therefore reduce demand, component size and capital cost.

title: Changes in Social Wellbeing Among Older Adults With Limited Prognosis: Results From a Nationally Representative Cohort
container-title: Journal of the American Geriatrics Society
bec32d345b34e8888fa28c32ccf70fca66e12f1f.abstract: ABSTRACT Background Physicians use clinical prognostic estimates to identify medical tests and treatments likely to benefit patients within their lifetime. Poor social wellbeing is associated with mortality, but it is unclear if prognostic indices can identify older adults at risk for worsening social well‐being. We examined associations between a mortality prognostic index and social wellbeing at baseline and over 2 years to inform care priorities in the context of a limited prognosis. Methods Data from the National Social Life, Health and Aging Project (NSHAP) Round 4 (2021–2023) and Round 4.2 (2024) included 1630 older adults. Social measures included loneliness, living alone, and at least monthly volunteering, socializing, and attending community groups and religious services. Scores of 8 or higher on the Lee Index (range: 0–26) indicated high mortality risk. Survey‐weighted logistic regressions adjusting for sociodemographic and health covariates were used to compare baseline and 2‐year changes in social wellbeing in the high versus low mortality risk group. Results Participants had a mean age of 70.3 years, and were 54% female, 62% White, 20% Black, and 14% non‐Black Hispanic. At baseline, higher mortality risk participants had poorer social wellbeing on all measures except socializing. Among those not lonely at baseline, 24.2% of higher versus 15.6% of lower risk participants became lonely at follow‐up (aOR 1.47; 95% CI: 1.01–2.14). Among those socializing at least monthly at baseline, 19.0% of higher versus 12.3% of lower risk participants transitioned to less‐than‐monthly socializing (aOR 1.60; 95% CI: 0.97–2.65). Higher risk participants had larger declines in all measures of social wellbeing at follow‐up. Conclusions Older adults with higher mortality risk had poorer social wellbeing at baseline and were more likely to become lonely and decrease social participation at follow‐up. Prognostic information may help clinicians avoid low‐value medical interventions while prioritizing interventions to support meaningful social connection.

title: DIGITAL TECHNOLOGIES IN PUBLIC FINANCE MANAGEMENT: GLOBAL TRENDS AND UKRAINIAN REALITIES
container-title: State and Regions. Series: Economics and Business
566bc774f254214199254d0865b4527899bea822.abstract: Digital transformation of public financial management has become a key factor in modernizing the public sector and strengthening state institutional capacity. This process is particularly relevant for Ukraine amid the full-scale war, the need to ensure transparency and accountability in the use of international financial assistance, European integration, and preparation for post-war economic recovery. The purpose of the article is to generalize global trends in the digitalization of public financial management and develop an integrated digital model of public financial management in Ukraine based on the principles of a unified information environment, interoperability, single source of truth, data-driven decision-making, digital by design, cybersecurity, transparency, and responsible use of artificial intelligence. The study systematizes contemporary approaches to digital public finance and examines international practices of using financial management information systems, Big Data, cloud technologies, artificial intelligence, digital identification, and integrated platforms. It is established that digital transformation is moving beyond the automation of individual financial operations toward comprehensive integration of public financial processes and information systems. Based on a comparative analysis of international practices and the Ukrainian experience, the need to integrate budgetary, treasury, tax, customs, procurement, accounting, and financial control systems into a unified digital environment is substantiated. An integrated digital model of public financial management in Ukraine is proposed, comprising six interconnected functional blocks: digital budget planning; electronic treasury services; digital accounting and reporting; electronic public procurement; open financial data and analytics; and digital financial control and risk management. The model is based on unified information infrastructure, data standardization, interoperability, cybersecurity, transparency, and responsible application of artificial intelligence. The major challenges of digitalizing public financial management in Ukraine are identified, including fragmentation of information systems, insufficient interoperability, increasing cybersecurity risks, limited adoption of advanced digital technologies, and the need to develop digital competencies in public administration.

title: Conservation-focused digital twins: the current landscape and lessons learned from the Dangermond Preserve
container-title: Frontiers in Environmental Science
21f545cc86f7b0ff0feb4435bbb35704f4fcd3dd.abstract: As conservation challenges intensify, digital twins—virtual models that integrate real-time data and simulations—offer a powerful new approach to understanding and managing natural systems. In this paper, we explore how digital twin technologies, widely used in industry, can be adapted to meet the unique needs of conservation. We introduce a technical maturity framework tailored to conservation contexts, outlining stages from foundational data collection to Artificial Intelligence (AI) augmented management. Drawing on global examples and a detailed case study from The Nature Conservancy’s Jack and Laura Dangermond Preserve, we illustrate how conservation-focused digital twins (CFDTs) can support biodiversity monitoring, scenario planning, decision-making, and stakeholder engagement. While the field is still emerging, early efforts show promise in transforming how we collect, interpret, and act on environmental data. We highlight key lessons learned, including the importance of modular design, data governance, and community involvement. Ultimately, CFDTs have the potential to reduce the divide between the physical and the digital world, and thus data and decision-making, enabling more adaptive, inclusive, and effective conservation strategies.

title: When hope is no longer enough: emotional ambivalence, digital exposure and the limits of the affective buffer against political polarisation
ea5dcc4c5a0038569b0e0188535be8d2a5243cca.abstract: Abstract Political emotions are central to democratic life, sustaining civic engagement but also fuelling social division. Research has shown that hope and pride sustain institutional participation, whereas anger and resentment drive non-institutional participation and affective polarisation, yet little is known about what happens when these emotions are experienced simultaneously, or under which conditions hope contains the divisive effect of anger. This study examines five discrete political emotions (hope, pride, anger, fear and resentment) as predictors of democratic participation and affective polarisation among Spanish university students. Data come from a computer-assisted web interviewing (CAWI) survey administered between 30 June and 24 July 2026 to 573 students. A moderated-moderation model tested whether hope buffers the polarising effect of anger and whether exposure to emotionally charged political content on social media erodes that buffer. The anger × hope × social media exposure interaction was positive and significant (b = 0.029; p = .006): under low digital exposure, hope almost entirely neutralised the translation of anger into polarisation (simple slope = -0.225), whereas under high exposure anger regained much of its polarising capacity even among the most hopeful respondents (simple slope = 0.279). A k-means cluster analysis identified an ambivalent profile (26.0% of the sample) combining high anger and high hope, whose affective polarisation did not differ significantly from that of the hopeful (p = .307) or angry (p = .113) profiles. The findings qualify the dual emotional pathway model and show that the civic value of hope depends on the media environment in which it is experienced. Framed within Sustainable Development Goals 10 (Reduced Inequalities) and 16 (Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions), the results carry implications for platform governance, media literacy and civic education aimed at fostering inclusive participation and reducing intergroup hostility.

title: Oscillatory Phase Coding Emerges in Adaptive RNNs for Flexible Working Memory
443e5e0f3156fe6a3ec21d6c7b08b3e5ba455e7f.abstract: A bstract Oscillatory phase coding (OPC) is widely observed in neural systems and has been implicated in cognitive functions such as memory and sequence processing. However, its computational role and neural substrates remain largely unclear. Here, we studied OPC by training recurrent neural networks (RNNs) with adaptation to perform sequence working memory tasks with variable delays. After training, we found that OPC emerges in the RNN spontaneously: the memorized items recur at distinct phases of a shared rhythm, with oscillation amplitude encoding item identity and phase encoding serial order. Ablation studies identified three key elements required for OPC: adaptation in neural dynamics, variable delay in memory retention, and flexibility in reading out information. Neuron-type analysis revealed the emergence of content and time cells in the trained RNN, and they process item identity and sequence order separately. Recurrent connectivity analysis revealed phase-organized connections among time cells and structured connections within digit-selective content-cell groups. Inspired by these findings, we proposed a neural circuit model which reproduces OPC through interactions between content units and an adaptive time ring. Together, this study reveals how OPC arises from network structures and task demands, offers insights into the implementation and computational mechanisms of OPC in biological systems, and inspires us to develop computational models for human-like cognitive functions.

title: Adaptive Multi-Modal Learning Framework for Streaming Big Data: A Dynamic Information- Theoretic and Distributed Optimization Approach
container-title: Mesopotamian Journal of Big Data
2cdc42eb5d8aab7eb1a14ec303dbe1a7456c5e8e.abstract: The massive increase in both heterogeneity and velocity of data streams has raised the need for learning systems with adaptivity to evolving distributions at scale. In this paper, we propose the Adaptive Multi-Modal Learning (AMML) framework to provide a one-stop solution for analyzing non-stationary multi-modal big data in real-time. The AMML combines modality-specific representation learning with modelling the drift by an information-theoretic measure based on KL divergence to track distributional changes. By combining a temporally regularized optimization framework with variational information constraints, the model can balance an optimal trade-off between stability and flexibility under continuous updates. The framework is deployed in a distributed Spark–Hadoop environment for large-scale deployment with scalability, low latency and resilient data recovery. For a convex online surrogate of AMML, the theoretical analysis provides a path-variation-dependent dynamic-regret bound. Vanishing average dynamic regret is obtained when the cumulative variation of the time-varying comparator grows sufficiently slowly, which implies it is capable of tracking the changing optimal predictors. Empirical results on simulated and synthetic multimodal streaming data demonstrate that AMML achieves higher accuracy, faster drift recovery, smoother parameter evolution, and near-linear scalability than existing streaming learning algorithms.

title: A INFLUÊNCIA DO MARKETING DIGITAL NAS DECISÕES DE COMPRA DE JOVENS UNIVERSITÁRIOS
container-title: Revista Tópicos
6f0e2ebc1e315eb2b9f749c5d2ce20a010e5dd18.abstract: O estudo analisa a influência do marketing digital e das redes sociais nas decisões de compra de jovens universitários, com ênfase no consumo impulsivo e não planejado. A pesquisa, de natureza aplicada, abordagem quantitativa e caráter descritivo, adotou o levantamento (survey) com estudantes de uma universidade estadual. A coleta de dados ocorreu entre 6 e 18 de outubro de 2026, por meio de questionário estruturado no Google Forms, respondido por 204 estudantes, e a análise utilizou frequências absolutas e relativas. Os resultados mostram que 190 participantes utilizam o Instagram semanalmente e que 162 acompanham ao menos alguns influenciadores. As avaliações de outros consumidores (165 participantes) e a descoberta de produtos nas redes sociais (152) obtiveram a maior concordância entre os fatores de influência. Ao todo, 147 participantes relataram ao menos uma compra on-line não planejada nos três meses anteriores à pesquisa, e a frequência dessas compras varia entre os estudantes. Como o estudo é descritivo e se baseia em autorrelato, os dados descrevem associações, e não relações de causa e efeito. Conclui-se que o marketing digital e as redes sociais integram o ambiente de consumo dos estudantes, principalmente como canais de descoberta de produtos e de circulação de avaliações e promoções.

title:
Analog Rules, Digital
Reality: Implementing Rules
as Code for Pesticide and Crop Biotechnology Safety Assessments
container-title:

2acb94de6c16c4c7703585cf3221e155f67d87e9.abstract: Abstract Agricultural and digital innovations are advancing rapidly, creating new opportunities to explore how regulatory review processes can become more efficient, transparent, and scalable while maintaining rigorous oversight. This perspective introduces Rules-as-Code (RaC), the practice of translating regulatory requirements into machine-executable logic as a mechanism to realize this transition. Two case studies illustrate how RaC can support automated compliance checks in pesticide and crop biotechnology risk assessments. By providing a standardized digital representation of regulatory requirements, RaC offers a framework to enhance consistency, efficiency, and regulatory preparedness in an increasingly data-rich scientific landscape.

title: Legal regulation of digital services in the EU: defining the material scope
container-title: Law and innovative society
39dd093dd2db47f53780c706378a0576738bb9a9.abstract: The article examines the challenges of defining the material scope of the legal regulation of digital services in the European Union by distinguishing between digital content and digital services and comparing related concepts established in EU law. Formal legal, comparative legal and systemic methods are applied. The relationships between digital services, information society services, intermediary services, electronic communications services and audiovisual media services are analysed. It is established that distinguishing digital content from digital services requires an examination of the substance of the provider’s obligations concerning the supply of content and the provision of functionalities for working with data. The possibility of combining these obligations within a single contract is demonstrated. The auxiliary role of the duration and periodicity of supply in distinguishing between content and services is substantiated. The consumer-contractual scope of the definition of a digital service in Directive (EU) 2019/770 is clarified. Different types of relationships between legal categories of digital services are identified. Certain concepts are related as general and specific categories. At the same time, a single service may fall within the scope of different legal acts governing distinct aspects of its provision. It is also shown that the extent of a provider’s obligations may depend on the scale of use of the service. The role of dissemination of information to the public in legal classification is examined using hosting services and online platforms as examples. A comparison of audiovisual media services and video-sharing platform services highlights the role of the provider’s editorial responsibility. The relationship between the general requirements of the DSA and the specific rules of Regulation (EU) 2021/784 concerning the removal of terrorist content is examined. It is substantiated that the classification of a single service under several legal categories reflects different aspects of its regulation. The applicability of the proposed criteria for the legal classification of digital services to determining the requirements governing their provision under Ukrainian legislation is demonstrated.

title: Application of virtual reality for developing a new format of student-teacher interaction in the digital era
container-title: Palestine Technical University Research Journal
8bda7ce40c80580a0d342b3e12c742cfb4016989.abstract: The aim of the study was to identify optimal directions for the application of Virtual Reality platforms in higher education and to determine their potential for supporting learning process organisation and instructional design and shaping innovative learning strategies. The methodology included an analysis of approaches to the use of virtual reality in the learning process: content analysis of international educational strategies, and comparative analysis of three Virtual Reality platforms – ENGAGE VR, Hyperskill, and OpenSim – according to the criteria of interactivity, accessibility, analytical capacity, and level of collaboration. The main findings indicated that the analysed platforms differ in accessibility, interactivity, analytical capacity, and suitability for specific educational scenarios, as well as its context-dependent effectiveness in enhancing student engagement. It was established that Hyperskill provides an integration of automated code evaluation, personalised feedback, and collaborative opportunities, which increase the effectiveness of both individual and group learning in programming and the acquisition of practical information technology cases. OpenSim demonstrated substantial potential for interdisciplinary projects due to its customisable environments and analytics. The practical significance of the study lies in providing recommendations for differentiated implementation of Virtual Reality in higher education: the choice of a specific platform should depend on educational objectives, technical capacities, and students’ accessibility requirements, disciplinary preparation, digital literacy, and preferred modes of interaction

title: Integration of Digital Tools into language Education as a Means of Developing Intercultural Competence in Future Teachers Within a Multicultural Environment
container-title: Palestine Technical University Research Journal
4b81bd8c7993466b34238d7ca32b50b2015898f4.abstract: The purpose of this study is to determine the effectiveness of integrating digital tools into language education for the development of intercultural competence among future teachers in a multicultural educational environment. The study was conducted over eight months at three pedagogical universities in the Kyrgyz Republic: I. Arabaev Kyrgyz State University, Osh State University, and Naryn State University, selected for their culturally diverse student populations. The methodology involved a questionnaire survey of 243 education students learning languages using digital platforms, such as Zoom, Moodle, Padlet, Canva, Google Classroom, YouTube, and Telegram. The findings demonstrate the following average scores (on a five-point scale) for the components of intercultural competence: cognitive – 3.68, affective – 3.75, behavioural – 3.64. Correlational analysis indicated a significant positive relationship between the frequency of digital platform use and the development level of each competence component. The cognitive component was most strongly influenced by video platforms, which expanded students’ knowledge of other cultures and traditions. The affective component was enhanced through the use of Padlet, which fostered empathy and tolerance in intercultural communication. The behavioural component, reflecting readiness for intercultural dialogue, correlated most strongly with the use of messaging applications for content exchange, which supported active interaction and practical application of knowledge. A statistically significant difference was observed between students with high and low digital engagement, underscoring the impact of the digital environment on the development of intercultural skills. The results hold practical value for designing language education curricula aimed at developing intercultural competence

title: Integration of Digital and Computer Technologies into Teaching Mathematical Analysis: Innovative Competence-Based Approaches and Prospects for Development
container-title: Palestine Technical University Research Journal
0bb44c8e22e899c4dac0f7b2b0dc20ca9de821de.abstract: The study aimed to explore correlations between digital activity, student satisfaction, and assimilation of mathematical analysis content in Kyrgyzstan. The theoretical and empirical study was conducted between January and April 2025 at Kyrgyz State University named after I. Arabaev and Jalal-Abad State University named after B. Osmonov. The sample included 130 respondents, including 112 undergraduate and graduate students majoring in mathematics and computer science, and 18 teachers of relevant disciplines who participated in the survey before and after completing a digital module implemented using the GeoGebra, Desmos, Moodle, and Wolfram Mathematica platforms. A theoretical analysis of educational programmes and regulatory documents governing digital integration was also conducted. The results showed an increase in the proportion of highly motivated students from 30% to 60%, a decrease in the proportion of low-motivation students from 25% to 10%, and an increase in satisfaction with digital solutions to 62.5%. Statistical analysis confirmed a significant positive correlation (ρ=0.47) between the regularity of digital tool use and self-assessment of learning outcomes. Institutional differences in approaches were identified: at Kyrgyz State University named after I. Arabaev, the emphasis was on visualisation and methodological support, while at Jalal-Abad State University named after B. Osmonov, the emphasis was on functionality and analytical accuracy. The data obtained confirm the didactic significance of digital solutions for adapting course content to the specifics of training, increasing learning motivation, and developing functional mathematical literacy. The results can be used to update educational standards, develop digital training modules, and improve the quality of training for mathematics teachers in the context of digitalisation

title: Learning Models Using Digital Technologies in the System of Higher Professional Education
container-title: Palestine Technical University Research Journal
931b9d86f21954070acbf34260bd1e72d54b2e98.abstract: The aim of this study was to examine the features of functioning and effectiveness of educational models using digital technologies in the higher professional education systems of the Kyrgyz Republic and China. The Delphi expert evaluation method with the participation of 42 specialists and the method of stratified randomisation in group formation were applied in this work. The testing of the model was carried out from September 2024 to March 2025 in four universities with the participation of 240 students (30 people in the experimental and control groups of each university), studying in the fields of information technology and economics. In the course of the study, five key groups of factors influencing the effectiveness of the implementation of digital educational models were identified: technological, economic, cultural, pedagogical, and institutional. Comparative analysis showed that in the Chinese educational system technological (8.7 points for Internet availability), economic (9.2 points for digitalisation funding), and institutional factors (9.0 points for educational policy) dominated. In the Kyrgyz Republic, cultural factors (8.4 points for traditional values) and technological limitations (5.6 points for Internet availability) prevailed. The results of the testing at Bishkek University showed a 42% increase in students’ motivation and a 0.8-point increase in academic performance. At Osh University an increase of 53% in students’ digital competences was recorded. At Peking University the implementation of the model reduced the time for mastering material by 21% and increased the proportion of independent assignments by 25%. At Xi’an Jiaotong University a 32% increase in students’ professional competence was observed. The practical significance of the study lay in the development of adaptive recommendations for optimising digital educational models, taking into account national and institutional specificities

title: A Quishing Detection Model via Global Attention-Based Adaptive Fusion of QR Code and URL Text
container-title: ACM Transactions on Internet Technology
d0b6e638903d4f038c0eb1cd1324010101d06d2d.abstract: Quishing (QR code phishing) represents an emerging cybersecurity threat characterized by its dual-modal nature. This attack simultaneously exploits the visual modality of QR code images and the semantic modality of embedded URLs to launch covert attacks. Such a dual-modal attack strategy renders existing single-modality detection methods (relying solely on either images or URLs) and traditional fusion approaches based on expert-driven feature engineering fundamentally inadequate for comprehensive defense. To address this gap, this study proposes QRURL-GAAFNet (QR Code and Associated URL Features Global Attention-Based Adaptive Feature Fusion Network), which, to the best of our knowledge, represents the first end-to-end deep learning framework that holistically addresses the unique cross-modal correlation patterns inherent in Quishing attacks. Within this framework, dedicated deep learning networks independently extract visual features from QR codes and semantic features from URLs. Unlike conventional multimodal fusion approaches that treat modalities independently or use fixed fusion strategies, our proposed Global Attention-based Adaptive Feature Fusion (GAAF) mechanism dynamically learns sample-specific cross-modal dependencies by computing adaptive fusion weights from joint representations. By emphasizing discriminative information based on learned cross-modal correlations, this adaptive weighting strategy enables the model to focus on attack-relevant signatures that emerge from the interaction between QR code visual artifacts and URL semantic obfuscation patterns. Experimental results on public dataset demonstrate that QRURL-GAAFNet outperforms state-of-the-art methods in Quishing detection. Moreover, comprehensive experiments on the effectiveness of the data increment mechanism and robustness analysis, including evaluations against QR code image perturbations and URL text obfuscation attacks, validate its strong practical applicability in real-world security scenarios.

title: LABMFA-MCC: A Lightweight, Risk-Adaptive, Biometric-Bound Multi-Factor Authentication Protocol for Mobile Cloud Computing
container-title: Computation
731b36a4077e4c3025b6a47fe61ac7c918fc666d.abstract: Mobile cloud computing enables resource-constrained devices to offload storage and computation to remote servers. It involves authentication over an unsecure wireless link, while meeting stringent energy and bandwidth constraints, often with different service providers. Often, the protocols that achieve security requirements are too heavy for mobile devices or are limited to a single server. However, the adaptive risk-aware processes required by mobile platforms typically run on the top of the cryptographic layer rather than within it. This paper presents LABMFA-MCC, a lightweight authentication and key-agreement protocol that binds the credential to a biometric during each login, builds an end-to-end session key between the device and the server using an edge proxy that is intentionally excluded from the key derivation, and permits access to multiple servers through a single offline registration. Contextual risk is scored at the edge and used to raise the authentication posture, demanding a fresh biometric; we present this as a tunable mechanism rather than a calibrated policy. We validated the protocol in ProVerif under three adversary models, complemented by a computational session-key security argument in the Real-or-Random model, and developed a prototype, tested on a standard mobile phone and an x86 host, requiring about 0.88 ms of total processing (including the measured fuzzy-extractor reproduction) and 1744 bits of communication per login, measured with one enrolled user, the server’s constant-time anonymous user search adds about 3.4 µs per enrolled user.

title: Ramadan and the Timing of Scheduled Sessions on an Arabic Digital Mental Health Platform: A Three-Cycle Interrupted Time-Series Analysis (2023–2026)
container-title: Psychiatry International
9135433cbeb9a4eca65281d4271aea9c0fea204a.abstract: Background: Ramadan shifts sleep timing and daily routines, but, to our knowledge, its association with the timing of mental health care has not been measured across repeated cycles. Methods: We analysed de-identified records from an Arabic-language digital mental health platform in Saudi Arabia (30 September 2023–29 April 2026; 33,738 adults; 43,190 scheduled sessions). Ramadan 1445, 1446 and 1447 AH were compared with the 30 days before and after each month, using session-level logistic regression for session timing and negative-binomial regression for daily volume, adjusted for a flexible growth trend, day of week and holidays. Mood labels and PHQ-9 and GAD-7 scores were secondary outcomes. Results: During Ramadan, the share of sessions scheduled between 22:00 and 05:59 rose by 19.2 percentage points (95% CI 16.9–21.7; odds ratio 2.69), with increases in each cycle (26.6, 14.7 and 20.0 points) and in every sensitivity analysis; the gain came mainly from midday hours (12:00–17:59; −12.9 points) rather than the evening (−5.8). Daily volume did not change significantly (rate ratio 0.91, 0.81–1.02), although estimates depended on the trend specification and on where the series ended. Raw post-Ramadan increases in volume could not be separated from platform growth. Symptom scores did not differ, and mood shifts were inconsistent. Conclusions: On this platform, Ramadan was associated with a large, recurring shift in scheduled sessions into late-night hours, without a consistent change in volume or self-reported symptoms.

title: Roles of Artificial Intelligence in Urban Digital Twins and Governance
container-title: Smart Cities
f6f776daec0984758f82fb78da119f082a76cc5c.abstract: Artificial intelligence is becoming an increasingly used component in municipal operations, with applications spanning administrative automation, decision support, citizen interfaces, and predictive analytics across domains such as mobility, health and social services, and environmental management. While the literature documents benefits in operational efficiency and decision quality, most concrete evidence focuses primarily on internal efficiency. Urban digital twins have become commonplace in most European cities and smart cities globally. However, the role of AI within urban digital twins remains comparatively underexplored. This article addresses these gaps through a qualitative analysis of AI in Helsinki’s Experimentation Accelerator platform experiments and by comparing them against a DT framework based on the literature. Through this, we analyze how AI is piloted in municipal applications and how the identified use cases of AI align with the components of urban digital twins, identifying potential roles for AI in the urban digital twin as well as directions for future development.

title: Sustainability-Oriented Time-Varying Optimal Scheduling of Household Appliances Using Adaptive Multi-Source Transfer Algorithm
container-title: Sustainability
91567530765dae2bc30b0e110095e682b5cb11d3.abstract: Under the “dual carbon” strategy, home energy management systems have emerged as a core demand-side management technology to enable sustainable residential energy consumption. Nevertheless, most existing research investigates appliance scheduling within static frameworks. This study develops a dynamic three-objective scheduling model that minimizes electricity cost, user dissatisfaction, and carbon emissions. An adaptive multi-source transfer learning-assisted dynamic multi-objective evolutionary algorithm (AMS-TL-RMMEDA) is proposed to track the time-varying Pareto-optimal sets. The algorithm assigns transfer weights using Hausdorff-based similarity metrics, transfers historical knee points via geodesic flow kernel subspace alignment, and adjusts its response strategy according to quantified change intensity. On DF1–DF14, AMS-TL-RMMEDA yields the best MIGD values for 8 out of 14 problems and attains the lowest Friedman rank of 1.98. In simulations with eight household appliances across three environmental drift patterns, its MIGD is 38.03–52.85% lower than that of the best competing algorithms. The obtained knee solutions reduce electricity cost by up to 16.6%, carbon emissions by up to 17.3%, and peak-to-average ratio by up to 12.5% at a modest comfort sacrifice. Accordingly, adaptive multi-source transfer learning guides residential energy use toward low-cost, low-carbon, and grid-friendly operation, offering a decision-support tool for sustainable home energy management.

title: Comparative Effects of a Cow Hoof Cover® and Bandaging as Dressing Materials for the Treatment of Digital Dermatitis in Dairy Cows
container-title: Animals
1ff5892b0f9a51b27d9b0f6d077c117017a5b102.abstract: Digital dermatitis (DD) contributes to lameness, posing major animal welfare and economic concerns. Corrective trimming, topical antibiotics, and bandaging are widely practised in managing DD. However, the challenges associated with conventional bandaging include water retention and a moist environment, which affect the healing process. This study evaluated the effectiveness of a Cow Hoof Cover® (CHC) for the treatment of DD in dairy cows. A quasi-experimental study was conducted, involving cows affected with active stages of DD (M1 and M2), allocated to CHC (n = 29) and conventional bandaging (n = 27) groups. The standard treatment entailed a Dutch five-step hoof trimming, wound management, application of topical antibiotic containing oxytetracycline (Engemycin 25 mg/mL), and wrapping of the digit using either the CHC or conventional bandaging. All cows received an intramuscular injection of flunixin meglumine (2.2 mg/kg) for pain relief. Primary outcomes were healing of DD lesions (transition from active stages to M0) and restoration of normal gait (locomotion score of 1). All cows were observed weekly until Week 4 after treatment. While alterations in locomotion score were not significantly different between the groups (p = 0.23) during the study period, the CHC group had significantly higher (p < 0.01) proportions of cured cows at week 3 (n = 6, 20.6%) and week 4 (n = 17; 58.6%) compared to the control. None of the CHC-wrapped lesions progressed into the chronic hyperkeratotic or proliferative stage (M4), but such transitions were recorded in four cows in the control group. Overall, the CHC had significantly higher probability of cure (HR = 2.79; 95% CI 1.30–5.97) than the control group. Excluding the treatment group, none of the tested animal characteristics and treatment-related variables influenced the probability of cure. Overall, the CHC offers practical advantages over conventional bandaging; it is quick to apply, durable, and water-resistant, supporting its use for field application and large-scale herd management. However, histological investigation and robust clinical trials are recommended to ascertain whether the CHC promotes a complete cure of active DD lesions.

title: The Impact of Digital Economy and Industrial Agglomeration on Green Total Factor Productivity: An Analysis of Mechanisms and Regulatory Conditions
container-title: International Journal of Financial Studies
27e813fc77c40967bc4469a8418e38681af20902.abstract: This paper examines the relationship between digital economy development, manufacturing agglomeration, and urban green total factor productivity (GTFP). Using an unbalanced panel of 283 Chinese prefecture-level cities over 2007–2022, we estimate a two-way fixed-effects model that includes digital development, manufacturing agglomeration, and their interaction. The interaction coefficient is positive and statistically significant, indicating that the association between manufacturing agglomeration and GTFP becomes more favorable as digital development increases. Sequential regressions link this relationship to lower capital misallocation, better labor allocation, and greater green patent activity, with stronger statistical support for the green-innovation channel. The lagged specification and environmental-performance outcome provide further supporting evidence. Subsample estimates provide suggestive evidence of a larger interaction coefficient in cities with higher environmental-regulation intensity. These findings connect digital development and manufacturing concentration with urban green productivity and highlight the relevance of factor allocation, green innovation, and regulatory conditions to the green transformation of industrial clusters.

title: Digital Financial Ecosystems and Trade-Related Working Capital Finance: Firm-Level Evidence from 39 Economies
container-title: International Journal of Financial Studies
3de372c992cbce7a3af0e4ce4b6acef8e8d9da67.abstract: How firms finance purchases and inventories may depend increasingly on the digital financial environment in which they operate, but cross-economy evidence on trade credit and customer advances remains limited. We merge firm-level Enterprise Survey records with digital finance, insurance, digital infrastructure, and macroeconomic indicators. The complete-case sample comprises 32,049 firms across 39 economies surveyed during 2014–2020. Conventional digital finance and insurance capacity are positively associated with percentage, fractional share, and adoption outcomes across OLS, fractional logit, and logit specifications. The interaction between mobile money and digital infrastructure is negative but only marginally significant for adoption, supporting a diminishing adoption association at the 10% level; it is nonsignificant for percentage and fractional outcomes and is absent among existing users. Nonlife digital readiness negatively moderates the fractional share at the 5% level and adoption at the 10% level, but not the OLS percentage outcome. Alternative received and granted trade credit outcomes yield positive interaction signs, indicating that the estimated relationships are sensitive to the specific working capital outcome examined. Overall, the findings support a disaggregated ecosystem perspective but remain associational because national exposures are not randomly assigned and the data are repeated across sections.

title: A Method for Pellet Feed Moisture Content Detection Based on Electrode Plate Structure Optimization and Temperature-Adaptive Compensation
container-title: Processes
11dc98ffbec49c29b41349bb11493e2e0294694d.abstract: Moisture content critically affects the stability, nutritional value, and shelf life of pellet feed during production and storage, yet conventional measurement methods are limited by slow response, poor accuracy, strong temperature sensitivity, and poor on-site applicability. To overcome these issues, this study proposes a dielectric-based detection method incorporating electrode geometry optimization and temperature-adaptive compensation, using sheep pellet feed as the test material. COMSOL Multiphysics simulations revealed the effects of electrode thickness, spacing, and overlap area on the fringe field; the optimal configuration of 1 mm thickness, 40 mm spacing, and 15,000 mm2 overlap area reduced fringe field width by 32.7% and improved field uniformity by 41.2%. A cubic polynomial coupling model relating temperature, moisture content, and relative permittivity was established via a two-factor, five-level full factorial design with polynomial response surface regression, yielding a coefficient of determination of 0.996, an adjusted R2 of 0.994, and a root-mean-square error of 0.123, thereby enabling temperature-adaptive compensation. An STM32F103VET6-based prototype with capacitance sensing, temperature acquisition, display, and storage was developed. Across moisture contents of 10% to 20% and temperatures of 15 to 35 °C, it achieves a mean absolute error of 0.350%, a mean relative error of 2.600%, a repeatability coefficient of variation of 1.120%, and a one-hour drift below 0.080%. The device offers a fast, low-cost, and interference-resistant solution for real-time feed quality monitoring.

title: Digital Objective Lens: A Lightweight Neural Network for Super-Resolution of SEM Images
container-title: Processes
afaa3be7646d2fb3d1e2ce8a0329f9aa5258692a.abstract: Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) is a crucial and frequently employed tool for material characterization. However, owing to the hardware limitations of SEM, researchers often face a trade-off when observing materials: they must either use the fast scanning mode to acquire real-time images with poor details or wait 20 to 160 s for the slow scanning mode to obtain a high-resolution (HR) image with rich details. This significantly reduces observation efficiency and prevents process-level observations. In this study, we propose a wavelet-based lightweight super-resolution (SR) network (WLSR), which serves as a “digital objective lens”: by performing rapid SR on fast-scan SEM images, 2× or 4× digital magnification of the field of view with slow-scan image quality can be obtained while large-scale observation of the sample is conducted. A channel–spatial attention block and a wavelet-based upscaling module are introduced into the network structure, and a novel loss function combining a wavelet distillation loss and a perceptual loss is proposed for network training. WLSR was trained and evaluated on paired fast-/slow-scan SEM images of AgCl@Ag specimens, in which all LR inputs are genuine fast-scan images that are jointly denoised and super-resolved. Compared with existing lightweight SR networks, WLSR generates SEM SR images with richer details, superior subjective visual quality, and competitive objective evaluation metrics at an exceptionally fast inference speed of 3.7 ms per image on an NVIDIA GV100 GPU, indicating the feasibility of real-time deployment during live SEM observation. Through WLSR, the quality of fast-scan SEM images is significantly improved, which can enhance the efficiency and accuracy of sample observation.

title: Moniliophthora roreri in Cacao: An Evidence-Calibrated Synthesis from Population Biology and Molecular Pathogenicity to Epidemiology and Adaptive Disease Management
container-title: Sci
ae3b622535002fd1bb45d6bdfbdd7bc1615b5431.abstract: Frosty pod rot (FPR), caused by the basidiomycete Moniliophthora roreri, remains a major constraint to cacao production in the Neotropics and a biosecurity concern where the pathogen is absent. This critical narrative review appraises 69 sources spanning reproductive biology, infection-stage transitions, population genomics, molecular pathogenicity, diagnostics, epidemiology, resistance and management, calibrating recurrent claims against the directness and reproducibility of their evidence. The evidence supports predominantly clonal reproduction, marked geographical structure, continued genome evolution and prolonged hidden colonisation. It does not support a uniquely resolved geographical origin, a correspondence between genetic structure and pathogenic phenotype, or the inference of epidemic risk from pathogen DNA alone, and extensive candidate secreted-protein and carbohydrate-active enzyme (CAZyme) repertoires remain largely without causal validation. We integrate these domains into an evidence-calibrated causal framework linking pathogen diversity, molecular processes, infection and transmission traits, epidemic behaviour and adaptive management and identify epidemiological resistance and dynamic sentinel-isolate panels as priorities for advancing predictive and durable FPR management.

title: From urban digital embeddedness to management decisions: understanding innovative SMEs' digital orientation
container-title: Management Decision
946f0fd164210555a0afae10ae81bce43d4f0545.abstract: Purpose Developed for management decision's “The Practice of Making Decisions” section, this study examines a concrete managerial dilemma: what can managers learn by considering how deeply digital technologies are embedded in the urban environment alongside their availability? We examine how urban digital embeddedness is associated with innovative small and medium-sized enterprise (SMEs') digital orientation (DO) and its four dimensions. Design/methodology/approach The study combines city- and firm-level information for 24 Italian cities and 243 innovative SMEs observed over 13 years. Urban digital embeddedness captures citizens' use of home banking, municipal applications and broadband services. SMEs' DO is derived from annual mission statements and assessed across digital technology scope, digital capabilities, digital ecosystem coordination and digital architecture configuration. Relationships are estimated using a two-way fixed-effects Spatial Durbin Panel Model. Findings The findings show that urban digital embeddedness is most consistently associated with firms' stated digital capabilities and digital ecosystem coordination, followed by digital architecture configuration, while evidence for digital technology scope is comparatively weak. Practical implications Managers should look beyond digital technologies when making digital-strategy decisions and consider how technologies are actually embedded in the surrounding environment. Urban digital embeddedness can provide decision-relevant signals when evaluating locations, setting investment priorities, assessing external ecosystems and planning firms' digital transformation. Originality/value The study reframes the smart city as a managerial decision environment rather than a technological backdrop. It positions urban digital embeddedness as a source of contextual signals and DO as the organisational expression of strategic digital choices made by managers.

title: Effect of Digital Library Resources on Information Literacy Skills  of Undergraduate Students in Nigerian Higher Institutions
container-title: WORLD JOURNAL OF INNOVATION AND MODERN TECHNOLOGY
c5fb337d9599268533aca01c6f5f03ca4f5de158.abstract: The proliferation of digital library resources in Nigerian higher institutions has repositioned the university library from a passive repository of print materials to an active hub for electronic information access. This article examines the effect of digital library resources on the information literacy skills of undergraduate students in Nigerian higher institutions. Adopting a desk-review methodology, the study synthesises empirical and conceptual literature published mainly between 2017 and 2024 to interrogate the extent to which electronic databases, institutional repositories, e-journals and online public access catalogues (OPACs) shape students' ability to locate, evaluate, and ethically use information. The review shows that digital library resources have a generally positive effect on information literacy, particularly in search formulation and information retrieval, but that gains are uneven and are frequently constrained by epileptic power supply, poor internet connectivity, inadequate funding, and a shortage of structured digital-skills training. A synthesis table and a summary chart drawn from nine reviewed studies illustrate the recurring pattern of challenges across Nigerian university libraries. The article recommends the institutionalisation of credit-bearing information literacy courses, sustained investment in ICT infrastructure, and continuous digital-skills training for both students and librarians as strategies for optimising the benefits of digital library resources in Nigerian higher education.

title: From Cell Block to Cash Book: Entrepreneurial and Digital Accounting Literacy for Incarcerated Adults Preparing for Reintegration in Jakarta
container-title: Journal of Economics, Finance And Management Studies
59c89ce9b03494351eaaaf7791f96241d3f10f07.abstract: Prison-based entrepreneurship and financial education is increasingly promoted as a pathway to reintegration, yet evidence from Southeast Asian correctional settings is thin, and short community-engagement programs rarely disclose what their evaluations can and cannot show. This paper reports a lecturer–student program delivered to 31 inmates of the Class II A Salemba Correctional Institution in Jakarta on 15 July 2026. A 45-minute session on digital marketing and opportunity identification was followed by a 45-minute session on simple digital bookkeeping built around a worked cash-book case. Two insession instruments were collected, a business-idea worksheet (n = 21) and a cash-book task (n = 13); the planned post-test could not be administered. Ideas concentrated in trade (38.1%) and culinary ventures (19.0%), but 42.9% were anchored in a craft, repair, production, or technical skill, and only two of 21 were technology-based. Twelve of 13 returned cash-book sheets (92.3%; Wilson 95% CI 66.7–98.6) reached the correct closing balance of IDR 390,000. Because only 41.9% of attendees returned a sheet, the share of all attendees verifiably correct lies between 38.7% and 96.8%. We argue that the result evidences comprehension of a worked example, not a learning gain, and that the binding constraints on post-release practice lie elsewhere: a digital-access paradox, a capital and licensing gap, and a time lag that invites skill decay. We propose a staged design (parallel-form pre/post testing, practice on real transactions, booster sessions, and hand-over to community-corrections officers) and an evidence ladder that states which claims programs of this kind can support.

title: Hybrid Temporal-Spatial Attention Network for Rainfall Prediction in Urban Microclimates
container-title: Journal of Innovative Image Processing
f5ecef645613974b923f2b7cb8fbb62e6d818c63.abstract: Climate change has led to more frequent occurrences of extreme weather conditions and irregular rainfall patterns, making accurate prediction of rainfall amounts essential. In this paper, the performance of a Hybrid Temporal-Spatial Attention Network (HTSAN) model in predicting rainfall for the next day is evaluated using 12 meteorological predictors from the ERA5 reanalysis dataset. The geographical area covered by this research spans a 17 × 17 grid with 0.25° × 0.25° nominal resolution around Bangalore. HTSAN’s architecture involved a convolutional feature extractor, recurrent temporal representation, a transformer encoder, and a regression layer. HTSAN's performance was benchmarked against recurrent, convolutional-recurrent, and attention-based approaches using chronological test data. In this, benchmarking, the TFT approach resulted in the best RMSE value of 7.1474, while HTSAN had an RMSE of 7.5911, an MAE of 3.6779, and an R² of 0.4259. Extreme-rainfall benchmarking also revealed that HTSAN’s critical success index values were lower than those of the comparison approaches at the selected grid-cell rainfall thresholds. Thus, it can be inferred that the current version of HTSAN did not perform better than the selected benchmarks.

title: Development of digital educational media on the risks of illegal herbal medicines sold through e-commerce platforms: a qualitative study
container-title: Frontiers in Digital Health
0850c0eda58471340c9dee24a4da6b66f26ba2b3.abstract: Background Illegal herbal medicines sold through e-commerce platforms pose public health risks, particularly for people with chronic diseases. Objective This study aimed to develop digital educational media, comprising an e-module, educational video, and website, to address the risks associated with illegal herbal medicines sold through online platforms. Methods This qualitative descriptive study involved semi-structured interviews with 17 participants, comprising 11 professional informants and six patients with chronic diseases. Thematic analysis informed the development of an e-module, educational video, and website. Two academic reviewers subsequently provided preliminary feedback on the developed media using structured four-point assessment forms. Both reviewers had also participated in the qualitative interviews that informed the development of the materials. Results Ten themes informed the development of the digital educational media, addressing product legality, online marketing, health and digital literacy, cultural beliefs, regulatory supervision, professional involvement, and digital education needs. Preliminary expert feedback yielded descriptive ratings of 93.75% for the e-module, 98.75% for the educational video, and 95.00% for the website. These ratings reflect the assessments of two academic reviewers, both of whom had participated in the qualitative phase. Accordingly, the results should be interpreted as preliminary feedback rather than independent confirmation of content validity or evidence of educational effectiveness. Conclusion The study resulted in the development of three digital educational media addressing the risks associated with illegal herbal medicines sold through e-commerce platforms. The preliminary expert feedback provided initial academic input on the content and presentation of the materials. Further assessment involving independent experts and intended users is needed to examine content relevance, usability, acceptability, and educational effectiveness.

title: Aspect‐Ratio Preserving Target‐Matrix Optimization With Linesweep Smoothing for Arbitrary Lagrangian–Eulerian Meshes With Adaptive Refinement
container-title: International Journal for Numerical Methods in Engineering
8102081b4a845812112247d7baf54cae347832dd.abstract: ABSTRACT We present a rezoning method for three‐dimensional arbitrary Lagrangian–Eulerian (ALE) and ALE with adaptive mesh refinement (ALE‐AMR) simulations. The method combines linesweep smoothing with an aspect‐ratio‐preserving target‐matrix optimization paradigm (TMOP) formulation. It is designed to preserve anisotropic mesh structures produced by the Lagrangian phase while maintaining mesh validity and reducing shear, sliver formation, and cell bunching in block‐structured, optionally nonconformal meshes. The approach combines a patch‐local TMOP objective and a convexity‐based disentanglement metric within an existing linesweep framework. The TMOP target matrix is built from local edge geometry and includes a prescribed aspect‐ratio cap, which provides an explicit control parameter for mesh relaxation. The metric is evaluated on an extended nodal patch, so that the objective couples the motion of a node to the quality of neighboring elements affected by that motion. Combined with sequential updates, this ensures that accepted steps are tested against the updated quality of the local coupled patch, rather than only against the elements directly incident on the node. When invalid configurations are detected, the TMOP objective is replaced by a convexity objective that drives signed volumes back to positive values. Parallelism is recovered through a distance‐1 coloring of the nodal graph, allowing independent node updates to be performed concurrently. Mesh‐only and hydrodynamic tests assess shear reduction, aspect‐ratio control, and mesh validity. Among the configurations examined, only the TMOP combined method consistently satisfies these requirements together while retaining anisotropic mesh structures, with no observed invalid post‐rezoning states. The prescribed target cap provides explicit control over excessive elongation without imposing an isotropic target. Strong and weak scaling measurements quantify the cost of the parallel optimization.
