Optimizing Sustainable Energy Engineering With AI and Machine Learning
36d6b77407653d455c80e2f500634a6232d7a5a9.abstract: <jats:p>The increase in the demand for energy across the world coupled with environmental issues has heightened the importance of developing sustainable and intelligent energy systems. Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) represent some of the key technologies that can be employed to optimize the efficiency, reliability, and sustainability of the current energy systems. These technologies have become important due to the capacity of the systems based on such technologies to make data-driven decisions using predictive algorithms, automated control processes, as well as real-time decision-making processes. Some common applications of AI and ML include renewable energy forecasting, energy storage systems, predictive maintenance of energy systems, smart grids, and smart energy management in demand side. AI-based approaches for sustainable energy hold a lot of benefits for the environment as well as the economy. AI/ML technologies within the scope of sustainable energy engineering will be critical in realizing goals of energy efficiency and reduced emissions.</jats:p>

title: Deep Learning for Adaptive Management of Renewable Hybrid Power Systems
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Optimizing Sustainable Energy Engineering With AI and Machine Learning
8dbc26d9167ed7772f47b06f9aa8d0293cf7c8ac.abstract: <jats:p>This study examines the problem of adaptive control for hybrid renewable energy systems combining photovoltaic panels, wind turbines, and battery storage under conditions of generation uncertainty and price volatility. A control strategy based on deep reinforcement learning is proposed, which does not require an explicit mathematical model and accounts for long-term consequences, including battery degradation. The control task is formalized as a markov decision process with an integral discounted reward combining economic costs, penalties for energy curtailment, and storage aging losses. Computational experiments on real meteorological data demonstrate that the trained regulator reduces operating costs by 12–15% compared to heuristic strategies, increases the share of renewable energy used by 18–22%, and extends estimated battery life by 15–20%. The results confirm the advantages of the proposed approach over classical methods, particularly under high uncertainty. Limitations and prospects for practical implementation are discussed.</jats:p>

title: Intelligent Energy Systems
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Optimizing Sustainable Energy Engineering With AI and Machine Learning
5f910b7c7ff3cc7a08791e8c37c348d51a9d359d.abstract: <jats:p>The rapid growth of distributed energy resources and renewable technologies has increased the need for intelligent management of modern power systems. Microgrids offer a reliable, flexible, and sustainable solution by integrating local generation, storage, and controllable loads. However, their planning and control are complex due to uncertainties in renewable generation, varying load demand, and dynamic conditions. Artificial Intelligence (AI) has emerged as an effective tool to address these challenges. Techniques such as machine learning, deep learning, and optimization enable accurate forecasting of energy demand, renewable output, and system behavior.AI also enhances real-time control through adaptive decision-making and efficient energy management. This improves reliability, reduces costs, and increases resilience to disturbances. Overall, AI integration enables efficient resource use, minimizes losses, and supports the transition to smart, sustainable, and decentralized power systems.</jats:p>

title: AI-Assisted Optimization of Hybrid Renewable Energy Microgrids for Sustainable Rural Electrification
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Optimizing Sustainable Energy Engineering With AI and Machine Learning
96ab7ef154dc58376a40cf75f589dc662f80d0d9.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter reviews conventional optimization methods and AI-assisted approaches for hybrid renewable energy microgrids, highlighting their roles in system planning, sizing, operation, and control. It also explores emerging technologies, including reinforcement learning, explainable AI, digital twins, and edge AI, that are shaping the next generation of intelligent energy systems. To illustrate the practical application of these concepts, the chapter presents a case study of a hybrid renewable energy microgrid in Muanda, Democratic Republic of the Congo, featuring solar photovoltaic generation, battery energy storage, and blue-carbon bioenergy resources. The case study shows how optimization techniques can enhance techno-economic and environmental performance and discusses the potential of AI-based forecasting, intelligent battery management, and reinforcement learning to further improve system reliability, renewable energy utilization, and long-term sustainability.</jats:p>

title: Digital Intelligence and AI-Based System Optimization in Waste-to-Energy Infrastructure for Net-Zero Cities
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Optimizing Sustainable Energy Engineering With AI and Machine Learning
ff36013178296736d6e2747d2c7e1830b32bd841.abstract: <jats:p>The integration of digital intelligence and artificial intelligence in waste-to-energy (WtE) infrastructure optimization to achieve net-zero cities is presented in this chapter. The rapid urbanization and the growing amount of waste demand efficient and sustainable solutions. Municipal waste is turned into energy in WtE systems, and traditional operations lack flexibility and efficiency. The chapter uses systematic literature review as a method on the topic indexed in more than 200 articles and summarizing main conclusions of the quality research. It discusses monitoring with IoT, digital twins, and real-time optimization based on AI and predictive maintenance and energy recovery that is better. Case studies show the changes in the operational efficiency, emission control, and stability of systems. A conceptual AI-enabled framework is presented to find a solution to combine WtE systems with smart grids and urban energy networks. The results conclude on how smart WtE infrastructure contributes to the use of the circular economy and sustainable, low-carbon urban development.</jats:p>

title: AI-Driven Optimization of Solar Thermal Systems
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Optimizing Sustainable Energy Engineering With AI and Machine Learning
0860e093417810bedf80a8a8c80f3dec419bac99.abstract: <jats:p>Solar thermal systems encounter distinct operational challenges, which hinder their applicability. Artificial intelligence (AI) has the potential to solve them. The AI is more flexible and adaptable than traditional methods, which cannot deal with unpredictable factors, including changing weather and fluctuating energy demands. In this chapter, we introduced the solar thermal systems, and then the fundamentals of AI techniques used in solar thermal systems were provided. Subsequently, the application of AI in solar thermal systems was discussed. The advantages of the optimization process of the solar thermal systems were identified, supported by case studies from the real world. Then we identified the limitations and constraints that hinder the integration of AI into the solar thermal system. Finally, the economic benefits of using AI for the optimization of solar thermal systems were explained.</jats:p>

81ed3d5ef17a5775f35361935d09bc66b4b5cc4e.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter analyses the strategic incorporation of artificial intelligence technology into renewable energy systems to enhance energy security, operational efficiency, and long-term sustainability. This chapter aims to examine how intelligent energy management systems, machine learning algorithms, smart grids, decentralized microgrids, and Internet of Things (IoT) networks can enhance the performance and resilience of renewable energy systems. This chapter places emphasis on predictive analytics, battery management, solar forecasting, digital twins, and autonomous energy optimization. The chapter examines the economic, environmental, and technological ramifications of intelligent energy systems, emphasizing their capacity to minimize energy losses, improve system reliability, facilitate decentralized electrification, and expedite sustainable energy transitions towards enhanced national energy independence.</jats:p>

title: Machine Learning for Solar Thermal Energy Optimization and Smart Control
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Optimizing Sustainable Energy Engineering With AI and Machine Learning
fb44f8ecb89dccb4a11eab978ce879fb41e44f26.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter presents a systematic examination of how Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning techniques are transforming the design, operation, diagnosis, and control of solar thermal energy systems, including flat-plate collectors, evacuated tube collectors, and concentrating solar power plants. Principal ML methodologies surveyed include Artificial Neural Networks, Support Vector Regression, Gradient Boosting, Long Short-Term Memory networks, Transformer architectures, Physics-Informed Neural Networks, and Deep Reinforcement Learning. Applications are reviewed across four domains data-driven surrogate models for thermal performance prediction, ML-based irradiance and thermal output forecasting, intelligent fault detection and predictive maintenance frameworks, and AI-driven control strategies shown to improve annual useful heat delivery by 8 to 15 percent. Research challenges including data scarcity, model interpretability, and cross-site generalization are identified, with future directions proposed in federated learning, physics-informed architectures, and explainable AI.</jats:p>

title: Energy Audits in Tanzanian Industrial SMEs for Methods, Barriers, and M&V-Linked Savings Prioritization
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Optimizing Sustainable Energy Engineering With AI and Machine Learning
b85063b2e64cb2adf03e3a6fd9c4b42f3f347e50.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter develops a conceptual and methodological framework for artificial-intelligence- and machine-learning-enabled energy audits in Tanzanian industrial small and medium-sized enterprises. Industrial SMEs often face energy-efficiency barriers related to limited capital, weak information systems, incomplete metering, and constrained managerial capacity. The chapter positions the energy audit as the organizing mechanism for sustainable energy engineering and shows how AI/ML can strengthen load profiling, benchmarking, anomaly detection, forecasting, measure prioritization, and measurement and verification. Drawing on peer-reviewed evidence from SME audit programs, ISO 50001 research, African industrial energy studies, and applied AI/ML energy literature, the chapter proposes a staged implementation roadmap for Tanzanian SMEs. The contribution is a practical pathway for moving from one-off audits toward data-informed, explainable, and financially grounded energy management.</jats:p>

title: Biogas Production Optimisation
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Optimizing Sustainable Energy Engineering With AI and Machine Learning
3a1fabea3f97fb97115f71a9b24c656748b30ad4.abstract: <jats:p>Anaerobic co-digestion is an effective approach for biogas production, but optimizing operating parameters remains challenging due to the interaction of multiple variables. This study integrates ultrasonic pretreatment with Response Surface Methodology (RSM) to enhance biogas yield from a mixture of dormitory food waste and pet animal dung. Batch digesters were operated at 37 °C, and daily biogas production was monitored. RSM evaluated the combined effects of ultrasonic temperature (25–65 °C), power (500–1,500 W), and treatment time (35–75 min). Biogas yield ranged from 35% to nearly 68%, with optimum conditions of 53.35 °C, 1,490.83 W, and 57.15 min, producing a predicted yield of 66.47%. The quadratic model showed excellent predictive performance (R2 = 0.9707; F = 110.33), confirming the importance of simultaneous optimization. The integrated ultrasonic–RSM approach provides a reliable and efficient strategy for maximizing biogas production in anaerobic co-digestion systems.</jats:p>

title: Application of Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning Methods to Optimize Energy System Stability
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Optimizing Sustainable Energy Engineering With AI and Machine Learning
638e43b89445c1c4efd078d51246af0e90e11d12.abstract: <jats:p>This article presents a systematic analysis of artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) methods applied to the optimization of energy system stability. Deep learning architectures for forecasting electricity demand and renewable energy generation, reinforcement learning algorithms for microgrid control, the concept of digital twins, and explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) methods are examined. The application of hybrid models reduces forecasting errors by 20–35% over ultra-short-term forecasting horizons ranging from several minutes to several hours. The transition to probabilistic forecasting reduces balancing costs by 8–15%, while the use of digital twins decreases operating costs by 15–25%. Current challenges limiting the implementation of intelligent technologies in the energy sector are identified, and priority areas for further research are outlined. The results are systematized in comparative tables suitable for practical use when selecting appropriate methodological tools.</jats:p>

title: Forecasting Electrical Load and Renewable Energy Generation Using Machine Learning Methods
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics

ea63ae340e55dcd23a21c92099270e55640a1e65.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter per the authors examines machine learning for forecasting electrical load and renewable generation under energy transition and grid digitalization. The purpose is to show why power systems need models handling nonlinear, non-stationary, and heterogeneous data. The chapter reviews LSTM, BiLSTM, GRU, CNN, TCN, hybrid architectures, ensembles, SVR, and GPR. Solar and wind forecasting depend on weather uncertainty, spatial relationships, and telemetry quality. The chapter compares facility types with forecasting methods and discusses digital twins, adaptive forecasting, and closed-loop control. Key problems: data drift, limited transferability, interpretability, computational complexity, and SCADA cybersecurity. Development requires integrating forecasting with digital twins, XAI, reinforcement learning, anomaly detection, and cybersecurity. Machine learning becomes a foundation for proactive and resilient power system management.</jats:p>

title: Integrating Transformer Neural Processes and Deep Kernel Learning for High-Throughput Screening and Uncertainty Quantification for Water-Splitting Electrocatalysts Across Perovskites and Metal Alloys
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Optimizing Sustainable Energy Engineering With AI and Machine Learning
db14ec7802b2943f0f932ee90ef99812da7cac80.abstract: <jats:p>Years of experimentation have failed to enable the prediction of an efficient electrocatalyst from either a perovskite or an alloy without weeks of experimentation. There are more than a million perovskites, more exponential number of alloys but fewer than 0.1% of them have been studied. The traditional approach has failed. Density Functional Theory is impractical because of costs. Gaussian Process Regression struggles with scalability and lacks transfer between families. Its uncertainty calibration is off by miles. More importantly, the literature is not homogenous. Any framework that ignores that problem learns procedures, not physics. We gather Transformer Neural Processes (meta-learning across families) with Deep Kernel Learning (statistical uncertainty). This neural architecture can scale and model overpotential, stability, and activity with correlated uncertainties. Standardization of overpotential is done through Tafel correction. Prediction errors in the range of 50 millivolts and two- to three-fold reduction of experiments through Bayesian Optimization are our goals.</jats:p>

title: Interpretable Finger Vein Identification: Analysis of Fine-tuned Models with Explainable Artificial Intelligence
container-title: International Journal of Information Technology & Decision Making
28fb2182955c16ae0e2b0018164db6f7aebf61bf.abstract: <jats:p>Although convolutional neural networks report near-perfect accuracy in public finger vein datasets, their operational trustworthiness remains a critical, unevaluated blind spot. This study challenges the conventional reliance on accuracy as the primary metric for model viability. It is hypothesized that state-of-the-art models often achieve high scores not by learning robust vascular patterns, but by overfitting to spurious, nonbiometric cues in the dataset background. To expose this vulnerability, an explainability-driven audit is conducted using Local Interpretable Model-Agnostic Explanations (LIME) on eight deep learning models across two benchmark datasets (SDUMLA and UTFVP). The results reveal a significant accuracy-reliability paradox. The highest-accuracy model, Densely Connected Convolutional Networks (DenseNet121-99.84%), is found to be functionally insecure, heavily relying on background artifacts for prediction. Conversely, Extreme Inception (Xception), despite lower raw accuracy, emerges as the most biometrically faithful architecture (Explainability Score: 89%), consistently targeting valid finger vein patterns. Unlike traditional performance-oriented studies, the primary novelty of this research lies in its explainability-driven audit approach, which systematically evaluates the trustworthiness of deep learning models in finger vein recognition, bridging the gap between high accuracy and model interpretability. This discovery demonstrates that high accuracy can mask significant security flaws, making models vulnerable to presentation attacks. Consequently, explainability is established not as a secondary feature, but as a mandatory security metric. It is proposed that future biometric evaluations must adopt interpretability analysis to ensure models characterize the biological trait rather than dataset noise.</jats:p>

title: Tau hadronic decay channel reconstruction with a Lorentz-covariant graph attention network
container-title: Physica Scripta
48dd6af93c13d027dd2a5b2312100fb17c5e3a52.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    The reconstruction of hadronic decay modes of the
                    <jats:italic>τ</jats:italic>
                    lepton is a key task in high-energy physics experiments, directly impacting precision measurements and new physics searches. Conventional reconstruction approaches rely on handcrafted features and rule-based algorithms, which face challenges in handling complex decay topologies and detector effects. In this work, we propose LCGA-Net, a physics-informed deep learning framework for
                    <jats:italic>τ</jats:italic>
                    decay channel classification and four-momentum reconstruction. The method represents decay products as particle graphs and employs a multi-head attention mechanism to capture inter-particle correlations. To ensure physical consistency, Lorentz-invariant constraints are explicitly incorporated into the model architecture. A dedicated single-
                    <jats:italic>τ</jats:italic>
                    dataset is constructed from the simulation data of the Circular Electron Positron Collider, covering six major hadronic decay modes. The proposed model achieves an accuracy of 89.2% on the validation set, matching or slightly exceeding baseline models. More importantly, full physics constraints substantially improve the physical plausibility of reconstructed four-momenta—particularly the energy–momentum relation—without degrading classification performance. These results demonstrate that integrating physics priors with attention-based deep learning on particle clouds provides an effective approach for
                    <jats:italic>τ</jats:italic>
                    decay reconstruction, with potential applications in future high-energy physics analyses.
                  </jats:p>

title: Parental scaffolding and cognitive development in early childhood: Insights from a dynamic systems perspective
container-title: Child Development
958b98b1626b048c7804b6008b090f93e5b57b23.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Grounded in dynamic systems theory, which conceptualizes parent–child interactions as evolving systems of reciprocal influence over time, the main objective of this study was to examine which patterns of parent–child scaffolding in a problem-solving situation were associated with children's early cognitive development and to explore whether these patterns were influenced by prior child characteristics. A total of 193 mother–child dyads (109 girls) were observed during a number–image association task at 48 months. Children were predominantly White (95%) and of Canadian or European ethnic background. Three scaffolding phases were examined using the State Space Grid (SSG): modeling (problem-solving strategies are demonstrated by parents), guidance (characterized by shared participation in task execution), and fading (support is gradually withdrawn and greater initiative is shown by children). Only the fading phase was found to be associated with higher complex executive functioning (β = 0.30) and number knowledge (β = 0.42) 1 year later, at 60 months, controlling for prior child cognitive abilities. Furthermore, higher socioeconomic status, receptive vocabulary, and cognitive flexibility at 42 months were positively associated with fading. These findings highlight the importance of interactional processes that promote children's active participation in problem- solving for subsequent cognitive development.</jats:p>

title: Role of artificial intelligence in irritable bowel syndrome: A narrative review
container-title: Artificial Intelligence in Gastroenterology
26e8e947a394393704e8925e510fa123555cf186.abstract: <jats:p>Irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) is a prevalent yet incompletely understood functional gastrointestinal disorder whose estimated prevalence depends heavily on the diagnostic criteria applied, falling from approximately 9% under Rome III to approximately 4% under Rome IV. Characterized by recurrent abdominal pain and altered bowel habits, it substantially impairs quality of life and imposes a considerable economic burden. Its pathophysiology is complex and multifactorial, involving visceral hypersensitivity, altered gastrointestinal motility, immune activation, gut-brain axis dysregulation, and intestinal dysbiosis. This narrative review examines the potential of artificial intelligence (AI) to refine the diagnosis, subclassification, and management of IBS and related functional gastrointestinal disorders. We discuss the principal AI methodologies - machine learning, deep learning, and natural language processing - and how they enable the integration of diverse data sources, including patient-reported outcomes, microbiome profiles, and multi-omics data. Early studies suggest AI can support the differentiation of IBS from organic disease, the identification of biologically distinct microbiota subgroups, and the prediction of response to the low-fermentable oligosaccharides, disaccharides, monosaccharides and polyols diet. These findings, however, derive largely from small, single-center cohorts with heterogeneous methods and without external validation; a 2025 systematic review identified only six eligible studies comprising 1366 participants and found the evidence too heterogeneous to permit meta-analysis. We further identify domains in which AI is frequently invoked but not yet evidenced in IBS, including machine-learning analysis of longitudinal patient-collected symptom data and of psychological comorbidity. Substantial challenges remain around data standardization, external and temporal validation, model interpretability, and ethical and regulatory considerations. Progress will depend less on the development of further models than on standardized data collection, multi-center validation, and reporting against AI-specific standards such as transparent reporting of a multivariable prediction model for individual prognosis or diagnosis + AI.</jats:p>

title: The mitigation of agricultural supply chain risks through cross-collaboration in implementing the circular economy using DEMATEL and ANP
container-title: British Food Journal
2f8b6512ff6a0f24f16d3def94a8423f6ce6b19b.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Purpose</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Supply chain (SC) disruption is a significant obstacle to implementing a circular economy (CE), due to its multi-layered and complex production chain, especially in the agricultural sector. However, there is an unexplored assessment of disruptions in supply chain risks (SCRs) that can provide solutions to the CE. In this study, we aim to identify and mitigate SCRs through cross-collaboration that involves elaboration between joint efforts and sharing activities.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Design/methodology/approach</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The study employed two methods that integrate the decision-making trial and evaluation laboratory (DEMATEL) and the analytical network process (ANP).</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Findings</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The results show that the top three highest risk levels – namely, climatic, perishable and seasonality – influence agricultural SCR. Then, cross-collaboration can mitigate these risks through a joint problem-solving strategy that is the best alternative strategy from joint effort in the development of circular SC management.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Practical implications</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This research offers recommendations to improve product distribution and inventory management in the agricultural sector. Farmers can collaborate with food processors through joint planning to determine the quantity and type of products to be processed, thereby reducing raw material waste. Such cross-party collaboration helps minimize risks, fostering a more resilient, efficient, and sustainable agribusiness system; in this model, risks are no longer borne by a single party but are shared, creating value from available resources.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Originality/value</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study contributes to the understanding that agricultural stakeholders collaborate to find innovative solutions that enable them to better prepare for climate risks by implementing the CE concept.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Self-attention-aided multi-layer CNN-LSTM for non-uniform 4-level differential amplitude modulation and detection with atmospheric turbulence for OWANs
container-title: Optics Express
fedd060d0254eff3eb9ce0c2cc0964613783fd42.abstract: <jats:p>This paper proposes an environment-aware four-level non-uniform differential amplitude modulation and detection scheme assisted by self-attentive multi-layer CNN-LSTM (SA-CNN-LSTM) for optical wireless access networks (OWANs) under atmospheric turbulence, to mitigate severe distortions induced by atmospheric turbulence in optical wireless communication (OWC) systems. Relying on four-level non-uniform differential amplitude modulation (NUADM-4) and a self-attention-aided detection algorithm at the receiving terminal, the proposed scheme can effectively suppress both multiplicative turbulence fading and additive Gaussian noise simultaneously. Numerical results reveal that the proposed scheme achieves remarkable bit error rate (BER) improvements compared with conventional detection frameworks for NUADM-4, and it substantially outperforms the classical uniform four-level pulse amplitude modulation (PAM-4) across diverse turbulence strength regimes. Moreover, the tailored architecture integrating self-attention with multi-layer CNN-LSTM maintains high transmission efficiency, reduces the dimension of the fully-connected layer at the receiver to a certain extent, and accelerates the computation speed compared with the CNN-based algorithm. In comparison with conventional detection-aided algorithms such as vanilla CNN, LSTM, and MLP, the presented scheme delivers a universal BER performance gain. Furthermore, the machine-learning-aided design philosophy for different modulation systems offers a practical design paradigm and implementable solution for the engineering deployment of high-speed OWC systems serving OWANs operating in volatile atmospheric turbulence environments.</jats:p>

title: Learning Activator-Inhibitor Dynamics at the Cell Cortex with Neural Likelihood Ratio Estimation
container-title: PRX Intelligence
7efe9f2f0aa0561c1191c4552f34c6805a3622cb.abstract: <jats:p>A key question in cell biology is how cell-scale organization emerges from a given set of molecular players and rules of interaction. Given its multiscale nature, addressing this question requires a combination of experimental perturbation, mathematical modeling, and parameter inference. We leverage recent advances in each of these fields, focusing, in particular, on neural-network methods for simulation-based inference, to study how cell-scale patterns of Rho guanosine triphosphatase (GTPase) activity are defined by molecular-scale activator-inhibitor interactions with filamentous actin. Using an existing model of this interaction, we demonstrate that an overexpressive, regularized classification neural network can approximate the likelihood of data arising from a particular parameter set. We show that variations in F-actin assembly dynamics can be inferred directly from experimental data, but only if the network is made less sensitive to model misspecification. We use our approach to interpret perturbation experiments in which increasing Rho GTPase-activating protein (RhoGAP) coexpression increases the frequency and coherence of Rho activity waves in frog eggs. After showing that the known functions of RhoGAP are insufficient to explain experimentally observed dynamics, we use neural methods to suggest an alternative pathway by which RhoGAP could decrease filament nucleation rates to sustain waves. Our work yields specific, experimentally testable predictions and illustrates how a combination of traditional forward simulation models and modern inference tools can aid in unraveling mechanisms of self-organization.</jats:p>

title: Machine-Learned Particle Flow as a Foundation Model for Collider Physics
container-title: PRX Intelligence
a7c1b0fda6c698ac6ecf5fb9195fb389dd37f5d8.abstract: <jats:p>The workflow from particle collision to physics analysis passes through a series of reconstruction steps that are traditionally modular and disconnected, with no shared representation linking low-level detector data to high-level analysis tasks. We show that casting event reconstruction as a machine learning problem naturally produces such a shared representation. We repurpose a machine learning model trained for particle-flow reconstruction (MLPF) to perform three distinct analysis tasks: jet flavor identification, jet energy regression, and missing momentum regression. By appending the per-particle latent representations learned during reconstruction as additional input features, we substantially improve over baselines that use conventional particle-level features alone. We further demonstrate that a single linear layer trained using only the latent representations achieves competitive performance against state-of-the-art baseline architectures, and outperforms the baseline for missing momentum regression with approximately 35 times fewer parameters. These results demonstrate that the latent representations learned during reconstruction encode essential physics information needed for downstream analysis, establishing MLPF as a foundation model and offering a concrete step toward an end-to-end pipeline from detector data to physics analysis.</jats:p>

96194347b26c0eee3dabcf71df528ca9f2951b64.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter explores the integration of artificial intelligence (AI), universal design for learning (UDL), and inclusive teaching practices in higher education to enhance institutional performance. It examines how AI supports personalised learning, accessibility, and differentiated instruction aligned with UDL principles. Using conceptual analysis, the chapter shows that inclusive teaching improves engagement, retention, and equitable outcomes. It also situates inclusive pedagogy within social justice frameworks. Findings indicate that AI strengthens flexibility and responsiveness, while UDL promotes proactive accessibility for diverse learners. However, challenges such as algorithmic bias, data privacy, and unequal access remain critical considerations.</jats:p>

title: Agentic AI for Inclusive Assistive Ecosystems
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics

64f993336be792d7c4b612d79a8d17390e1701fa.abstract: <jats:p>Artificial intelligence is transforming assistive technologies, yet many systems remain reactive, fragmented, and insufficiently personalized for individuals with disabilities and neurodivergent conditions. This chapter examines the architectural, design, and governance foundations of trustworthy agentic assistive systems. It synthesizes limitations of conventional approaches, including restricted adaptability, low interoperability, and weak support for user autonomy, and introduces a taxonomy of agentic architectures to guide scalable deployment. The chapter proposes a multi-agent framework integrating multimodal interaction, hybrid reasoning, explainable AI, and health-aware data to enable context-sensitive support. It further addresses privacy, ethical governance, and responsible institutional adoption while outlining future research directions. By bridging architectural innovation with human-centered design, this work advances a forward-looking vision for inclusive intelligent environments.</jats:p>

title: Empowering Visually Disabled Users Through Web Accessibility
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Improving Disability Support and Institutional Performance With AI
e7b77c9fed0598c385d0917aa449f2d031fae972.abstract: <jats:p>The Indian Institutes of Technology (IITs), often categorised as Institutions of Eminence (IoE) in India, are set as the standards of measurement for the rest of academia. In this regard, the purpose of this paper is to evaluate the accessibility standard of the IIT Library websites in terms of the perceivable guidelines of the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (v. 2.1) using the Siteimprove Accessibility Checker. To improve the level of analytical precision based on the policy, technological, and user layers' conceptual frameworks, the study employs an artificial intelligence (AI)-based evaluation. The results indicate that there are considerable accessibility barriers in the various success criteria, such as non-textual content, information organisation, colour use, contrast ratio, and text images. Functional and visually organised designs notwithstanding, there are still critical gaps in ensuring the inclusion of visually impaired users. It also suggests the use of evidence-supported measures to enhance digital inclusivity and fair access in academic library settings.</jats:p>

title: AI-Driven Mindfulness-Based Mental Health Support for Mothers of Children With Autism
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics

9d38710756c4d8e79d2247e02869d371d633cd4f.abstract: <jats:p>Mothers caring for children with Autism Spectrum Disorder often face ongoing stress, emotional challenges, and significant caregiving responsibilities. These factors can affect family dynamics and the quality of support services available for disabilities. Although traditional counselling can offer some psychological relief, it may lack personalization, scalability, or ongoing monitoring. This chapter presents a mindfulness-based intervention enhanced by artificial intelligence, utilizing established techniques like Mindfulness-Based Stress Reduction to provide flexible and accessible mental health resources. By combining AI with structured mindfulness practices, this approach seeks to improve emotional regulation, promote increased caregiver engagement, and foster better collaboration with disability service organizations. The chapter emphasizes that AI-enhanced mindfulness can serve as a valuable resource to bolster caregiver resilience and facilitate more efficient and responsive delivery of disability services.</jats:p>

title: Leveraging Artificial Intelligence for Financial Accountability and Disability-Inclusive Resource Management

0d7a80fdfad7d743e38ff0f3aa9123c3f7b1ecd3.abstract: <jats:p>Artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming institutional financial management by improving transparency, accountability, and evidence-based decision-making. This chapter examines how AI strengthens budgeting, financial reporting, fraud detection, procurement, and performance measurement while advancing disability-inclusive resource management. It discusses the conceptual foundations of AI adoption, relevant theoretical perspectives, and practical applications that support equitable resource allocation and accessibility investments. The chapter also addresses governance, ethical considerations, data privacy, implementation strategies, emerging technologies, and persistent challenges affecting AI adoption. It concludes that responsible AI implementation, supported by effective governance, skilled personnel, quality data, and inclusive policies, can enhance financial accountability, optimise institutional performance, and promote sustainable disability-inclusive financial management across educational and public institutions.</jats:p>

b83110c46123ad08d922ea8250e5266e1fe8dd02.abstract: <jats:p>Higher education institutions worldwide are increasingly prioritizing inclusive learning environments that accommodate the diverse needs of students with disabilities. Advances in artificial intelligence (AI) have introduced transformative opportunities for developing assistive ecosystems that support accessibility, personalized learning, and institutional efficiency. AI-enabled technologies—including intelligent tutoring systems, speech recognition, computer vision, and predictive analytics—can significantly enhance disability support services while improving educational outcomes and institutional performance. This chapter explores the concept of AI-enabled assistive ecosystems within higher education and examines how integrated AI technologies can support students with physical, sensory, cognitive, and learning disabilities. The chapter analyzes the potential benefits of AI-driven accessibility tools, institutional data analytics, and adaptive learning platforms for promoting inclusive education.</jats:p>

title: AI-Powered Predictive Analytics for Early Identification of Learning Disabilities
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics

043143cf4cb7b04ac142cd26e901f7ca8ddd2099.abstract: <jats:p>Learning disabilities (LDs) need to be identified at an early age so that they can be addressed promptly so that they can utilize their academic performance and inclusive learning. Conventional diagnostic procedures are mostly reactive, time-consuming and subjective and rely on the use of standardized tests, teacher observations, as well as, clinical evaluations. The development of artificial intelligence (AI) and predictive analytics allows active risk screening based on machine learning and deep learning, and explainable AI models. This chapter investigates predictive pipelines, benchmarking models (SVM) and random forests, (CNN and LSTM) and validation, ethics, privacy, and adaptive intervention frameworks in an attempt to encourage equitable, transparent, and scalable learning intervention systems.</jats:p>

title: AI-Supported Inclusive Teaching, Learning, and Assessment Practices

f7d5b07d3572f89cb66a9323a13e52d04b0ad451.abstract: <jats:p>Artificial Intelligence (AI) is rapidly transforming educational systems, offering innovative pathways for enhancing inclusive teaching, learning and assessment practices. In the context of disability support, AI-driven tools provide opportunities to personalize instruction, improve accessibility and strengthen institutional performance through data-informed decision-making. However, despite these potentials, some educational institutions face challenges in effectively integrating AI into inclusive education practices. This chapter therefore examines how AI-supported instructional strategies, adaptive learning systems and intelligent assessment tools can address diverse learner needs. It critically analyzes ethical concerns, implementation barriers and capacity gaps associated with AI adoption in education. The chapter proposes a conceptual framework linking AI integration, inclusive pedagogy and institutional outcomes. It further provides actionable suggestions for stakeholders seeking to leverage AI for sustainable disability support and improved institutional effectiveness.</jats:p>

title: Artificial Intelligence-Enabled Early Warning Systems for the Psychosocial Wellbeing of Students With Hearing Loss in Inclusive Educational Settings
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Improving Disability Support and Institutional Performance With AI
129abc45062d56b3fbb0027ea16533ce2776036a.abstract: <jats:p>Students with hearing loss in inclusive settings frequently face psychosocial challenges including social isolation, communication fatigue, and emotional disengagement that develop gradually and evade conventional monitoring systems focused solely on academic metrics. This chapter proposes an AI-enabled early warning system (EWS) to proactively identify emotional distress and social withdrawal among deaf or hard of hearing (DHH) students. Integrating multimodal data streams, machine learning, transformer-based NLP, and explainable AI (XAI), the system generates actionable risk indicators for educators and counselors. Grounded in Social Inclusion Theory, Universal Design for Learning, Ecological Systems Theory, and Affective Computing Theory, it functions as a human-centered decision-support platform rather than a surveillance tool. Ethical dimensions including data privacy, algorithmic bias, transparency, and informed consent are critically examined alongside a roadmap for evidence-based implementation.</jats:p>

title: Intelligent Assistive Technologies in Higher Education
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Improving Disability Support and Institutional Performance With AI
7510ca4a3f66341f01e483ae97917d37a915e525.abstract: <jats:p>Artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming higher education by enabling intelligent assistive technologies that enhance learning outcomes for students with disabilities. This chapter examines the landscape of AI-driven assistive tools—including speech recognition, adaptive learning platforms, natural language processing, and predictive analytics—and their role in advancing inclusive education. Drawing on recent systematic reviews and empirical studies, it critically evaluates opportunities such as personalized accommodation, improved accessibility, and universal design for learning (UDL) integration, alongside challenges including algorithmic bias, data privacy, and digital equity. Frameworks for ethical AI deployment and institutional policy recommendations are presented. The chapter concludes with future directions for sustainable, human-centered AI assistive ecosystems in higher education.</jats:p>

title: Assistive Tools to Intelligent Systems
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Improving Disability Support and Institutional Performance With AI
2d0c2eecb37bb3dc4dd370074acc4a5b42bfc597.abstract: <jats:p>Artificial intelligence is changing how disability assistance systems work by combining personalized institutional services with proactive, data-driven methods. This chapter reviews the old support systems that often react slowly and create extra work and looks at how AI tools like predictive analytics, natural language processing, and intelligent decision-support systems can improve how institutions operate and provide help for disabilities. It discusses applications including automated management of reasonable accommodations, AI-powered virtual assistants, and accessible learning environments that enable earlier identification of support needs. The chapter also analyzes how institutions can use AI-generated insights to optimize resource allocation, strengthen regulatory compliance, and operationalize inclusive policies. Finally, it addresses key ethical challenges, including algorithmic bias, data privacy, and disability-inclusive design, and outlines principles for responsible implementation of AI in disability assistance.</jats:p>

container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics

00ce053ee1c65f0ed357fb21fa1391ad7c7cc4f7.abstract: <jats:p>Artificial intelligence is transforming disability support in higher education by enabling personalization, predictive analytics, and systemic change. This chapter explores AI tools—such as adaptive learning platforms, NLP assistants, early-alert systems, and automated accommodations—used to address barriers faced by students with diverse disabilities. Grounded in Universal Design for Learning and the social model of disability, it reframes AI as a means to enhance student autonomy rather than just improve services. It also examines risks like algorithmic bias, surveillance, and data misuse. title: A Critical Exploration of How Artificial Intelligence Enhances Accommodation for Learners With Learning Barriers

2b033bfd9e3d57fefca89685cea1b21c53f84a3a.abstract: <jats:p>The purpose of this chapter is to critically explore how Artificial Intelligence (AI) can enhance curriculum design, content delivery and assessment strategies to accommodate learners with barriers to learning. 4bffbc9d3ce152f4180027ae5d08a50dd6eca207.abstract: <jats:p>Urbanization and climate challenges are increasing pressure on cities to adopt sustainable energy solutions. title: Revisiting the diffusion of innovations theory: artificial intelligence adoption in social media

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec id="j_omgc-2026-0013_abs_001">
                    <jats:title>Purpose</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The present study aims at revisiting the applicability of Rogers’ diffusion of innovations theory in the digital era, particularly in relation to recent advancements in Artificial Intelligence and their use in social media. It further explores the role of generational differences in shaping AI adoption patterns.</jats:p>

                  <jats:sec id="j_omgc-2026-0013_abs_002">

AI was itself used during qualitative data analysis following our AI-Assisted Data Analysis Procedure (ADAP), including generating and categorizing codes, themes, and excerpts.</jats:p>

                  <jats:sec id="j_omgc-2026-0013_abs_003">
                    <jats:title>Findings</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The findings provide updated insights into the elements of the diffusion process, establishing potential grounds for modernizing the theory in light of AI-driven innovations. Shifts in innovation attributes, decision-making processes, and generational influences are identified, revealing how AI adoption transforms communication practices within digitally networked environments that increasingly shape contemporary global communication. The study further highlights patterns of resistance and reasons for non-AI adoption.</jats:p>

                  <jats:sec id="j_omgc-2026-0013_abs_004">
                    <jats:title>Practical implications</jats:title>

title: Equivalent circuit of a 6–10 kV cable network for locating single-phase earth faults using an artificial neural network
container-title: Vestnik IGEU
a333ac2f6de8ae21bcc5d53ee036200bd8890983.abstract: <jats:p>Location of single-phase earth faults in 6–10 kV cable networks is a challenging task, especially in the presence of complex transient processes and various neutral grounding regimes. Traditional methods based on the analysis of zero-sequence currents and voltages often require complex and time-consuming calculations and do not always provide high fault location accuracy. The use of artificial neural networks improves the efficiency of single-phase earth fault location through automatic transient analysis and adaptation to changing network conditions and parameters. However, training and testing the neural network requires an accurate equivalent circuit for the 6–10 kV cable network. To study transient processes during earth faults, T-shaped and L-shaped equivalent circuits of a 6–10 kV cable line have been used. Modeling of ground faults has been performed in MATLAB/Simulink. Also, an artificial neural network has been developed to determine the location of damage based on transient parameters. A T-shaped equivalent circuit for a 6–10 kV cable network is proposed, taking into account the portion of the network beyond the earth fault location. The trained neural network has demonstrated high fault location accuracy under various neutral grounding conditions and transient resistances. The use of a T-shaped equivalent circuit for a 6–10 kV cable network in training and testing an artificial neural network as the basis of the method of locating single-phase earth faults allows increasing its selectivity and adaptability. It is especially important for networks with a voltage of 6–10 kV operating with different neutral grounding modes for different types of earth faults.</jats:p>

title: Artificial Intelligence‐Assisted Automated Optical Coherence Tomography Analysis for Percutaneous Coronary Intervention Planning: From Plaque Analysis to Precision Lesion Preparation and Stent Optimization
container-title: Journal of the American Heart Association
29f3e4c86954f0e6d47e4d87c84dc0f778078163.abstract: <jats:p xml:lang="en">Percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) remains the cornerstone of revascularization in coronary artery disease. However, despite advances in stent technology, adverse outcomes related to suboptimal stent placement including under‐expansion, malapposition, incomplete coverage, edge dissection, and neoatherosclerosis persist. Optical coherence tomography (OCT) is the highest resolution widely available intravascular imaging modality, allowing unparalleled visualization of stent‐vessel interactions and plaque morphology. However, there are significant barriers to large‐scale OCT adoption, including time‐consuming manual interpretation and dependence on the operator, resulting in significant variability between analysts. Artificial intelligence (AI)‐based automated OCT analysis promises to assist PCI by delivering rapid, reproducible, and standardized stent optimization, but current analysis systems lack important features to optimize stent placement. This review summarizes the principles of OCT in PCI, the evidence for OCT‐guided optimization, and recent advances in AI‐driven automated OCT analysis. We discuss plaque analysis and classification, highlighting how AI‐driven automated OCT analysis can identify fibrous, lipid‐rich, and calcified lesions and guide tailored lesion preparation using balloons, specialty balloons, drug‐coated balloons, intravascular lithotripsy, and atherectomy. We outline emerging AI‐enabled workflows for fully automated PCI optimization, evaluate clinical outcomes, interpretability, and workflow integration. Finally, we explore future directions including AI imaging‐physiology fusion, multiomics integration, and robotics. If successful, automated AI‐empowered OCT analysis could become a central imaging platform for precision PCI, enabling tailored lesion preparation, optimal stent deployment, and improved clinical outcomes in coronary artery disease management.</jats:p>

title: Optimising sleep regularity during shiftwork is important for cognitive performance, sleepiness and mood
container-title: SLEEP Advances
1feb0e7d2cb9f318c1cf9eac264b69994eea234b.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Sleep regularity is important for performance and wellbeing. Sleep regularity is underexplored in shiftworkers, a population that may struggle to maintain regular sleep timing due to unstable work hours. It is important to understand how sleep regularity relates to wellbeing and performance outcomes for shiftworkers. Using the sleep regularity index (SRI), we assessed the relationship of sleep regularity to performance and wellbeing in maritime watchstanding shiftworkers who worked two different schedules (known as “watchbills”). Active-duty sailors (N = 23, aged 25.96 ± 3.13 years, [mean ± standard deviation]) wore an actiwatch for ~14 days while underway on the 5-hrs on/10-hrs off watchbill, and four months later for ~10 days while on the 3-hrs on/9-hrs off watchbill. The psychomotor vigilance task (PVT) was administered 2 to 4 times daily during both underway periods; the Epworth Sleepiness Scale (ESS), Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI), and Profile of Mood States (POMS) were administered at the end of both data collection periods. High variability in SRI score was observed for shiftworkers on the same shift of the same schedule. Higher SRI scores were associated with faster reaction times (Spearman’s rho [ρ] = -0.73, p = .019) and better cognitive performance on seven other PVT metrics (all p &lt; .05), and reduced daytime sleepiness (ρ = -0.512, p = .013) and total mood disturbance (ρ = -0.634, p = .005). The study found that sleep regularity is an important dimension of sleep to optimise during shiftwork to improve cognitive performance and reduce daytime sleepiness and mood disturbance.</jats:p>

title: Unlocking creativity with artificial intelligence: field and experimental evidence on human resource management in the ready-made garments industry
container-title: International Journal of Manpower
8e39c3a582dc2aaffcade755af1b68c5294514ef.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Purpose</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study examines how human–AI collaboration influences human resource management (HRM) creativity in Bangladesh’s readymade garments (RMG) industry, a labor-intensive sector facing persistent manpower challenges related to skills mismatch, absenteeism, turnover, worker voice, compliance, women’s advancement and production continuity. The study develops a human-centered “Goldilocks” perspective, arguing that AI contributes most effectively to HRM innovation when collaboration is neither too limited nor excessive.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Design/methodology/approach</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Drawing on human-centered AI theory, creativity research and sector-specific HRM scholarship, the study adopts a three-study design. Study 1 examines AI collaboration in an RMG-focused HRM innovation task among business professionals. Study 2 extends the analysis to a larger working-adult sample with crowdsourced creativity ratings. Study 3 develops a field-oriented HRM model incorporating collaboration intensity, AI self-efficacy, knowledge diversity, problem restructuring, HR innovation climate, age and tenure.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Findings</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Across the studies, moderate human–AI collaboration produces stronger creative HRM outcomes than low or high collaboration. Knowledge diversity emerges as the strongest explanatory mechanism, suggesting that AI enhances HRM creativity mainly by broadening the range of ideas, comparisons and workforce-related solutions available to managers. Excessive AI reliance, however, risks generic recommendations, anchoring effects, reduced contextual judgement and surveillance-oriented HRM practices.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Originality/value</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The study contributes to manpower and HRM research by explaining how responsible AI collaboration can support creative workforce management in a labor-intensive emerging-economy industry. It advances a calibrated model of AI-enabled HRM in which technology strengthens, rather than replaces, human judgement, ethical interpretation and context-sensitive decision-making.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: The end of the end, the beginning of the end: architecture, artificial intelligence and the exhaustion of the post-classical
container-title: Archnet-IJAR: International Journal of Architectural Research
e6c140b46fd10ab301c9925bbd907d7814e51f19.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Purpose</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This article examines how artificial intelligence (AI) is reconstituting the figure of the architect – not as an external disruption but as the latest instance of a recurring pattern in which mediating tools rewrite the discipline from within. Situating the present moment as the third in a sequence of paradigmatic “ends” diagnosed by Tafuri (1969/1973) and Eisenman (1984), the article traces a genealogy of the architect from Vitruvius through Alberti to the modern professional, and argues that generative AI has mechanically realized the post-classical project Eisenman announced as avant-garde provocation, thereby exhausting its critical force and demanding a fundamental redefinition of architectural labor.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Design/methodology/approach</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The article employs a critical-theoretical methodology combining historical genealogy with contemporary empirical evidence. It constructs a genealogy of the architect-figure organized around successive mediating instruments (orthographic projection, notation, legal seal, computation, AI), drawing on Tafuri’s ideology critique, Eisenman’s post-classical theory and Carpo’s digital-turn thesis. This theoretical framework is grounded in recent empirical data, including RIBA’s 2024–2025 AI adoption surveys, Schneider et al.’s experimental study of client-AI co-design, Bernstein’s practice-based research and World Economic Forum labor projections.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Findings</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The article finds that generative AI has industrialized the formal operations Eisenman theorized as avant-garde in 1984 – architecture without origin, without telos, without representational meaning – rendering the post-classical paradigm the default rather than the transgression. This exhaustion produces an asymmetric absorption: AI enters practice fastest where authorial labor concentrates (ideation, visualization) and is resisted where liability concentrates (documentation, certification), splitting the legal author from the substantive author. Five emergent functions of the architect are identified – dataset curator, question framer, output evaluator, liability bearer and system critic – collectively relocating architectural authority from form-giving to judgment.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Originality/value</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The article offers the first sustained reading of architectural AI through the combined lens of Tafuri’s ideology critique and Eisenman’s post-classical theory, demonstrating that the diffusion model mechanically performs the very operations Eisenman demanded as deliberate aesthetic transgression. This reframing moves the discourse beyond the prevailing optimism/dystopia binary toward a structural analysis of how tools historically constitute the architect-figure rather than merely assist it. By identifying five emergent functions that relocate architectural authority from authorship to judgment, the article provides a theoretically grounded framework for rethinking professional identity and disciplinary self-understanding in the age of AI.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Artificial neural network–assisted comparative analysis of variable viscosity models in polymer wire coating
container-title: Multidiscipline Modeling in Materials and Structures
c445edaa367f8205d60d81487a68f16fc36cc854.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Purpose</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>An ANN-based computational framework is designed to examine the role of variable viscosity in the wire-coating process. For this, two well-known viscosity models, namely the Vogel and Arrhenius, are considered. Third-grade fluid flow in the presence of radiative heat, variable viscosity and a transverse magnetic field is measured. A comparative study is performed to understand the role of each model on the flow and thermal outlines in the coating region.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Design/methodology/approach</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The modeled nonlinear differential equations were numerically solved using the MATLAB bvp5c function, and the ANN–LMA concept was applied to analyze regression, mean-squared error, state transition dynamics and error histogram results.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Findings</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>A parametric analysis is performed to determine the significance of each parameter in fiber coating. The Vogel’s model predicts relatively stable flow behavior under varying parameters compared with the Arrhenius model. The artificial neural network (ANN) performance, training state, error histogram and regression analysis reveal fast convergence, low mean squared error and a perfect regression coefficient (R = 1), demonstrating the precision and reliability of the proposed model.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Originality/value</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Published works have not analyzed the role of variable viscosity in the wire-coating process. This study fills the above gap through a comparative analysis using ANNs, considering third-grade fluid. This study also aims to identify the optimal viscosity model from the Vogel and Arrhenius models.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Unpacking top management team judgment in ethical cybersecurity disclosure: navigating transparency and confidentiality in corporate reporting across an emerging economy
container-title: International Journal of Ethics and Systems
96c0e88eaa34aaa884db605d4938fffec232ec4d.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Purpose</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study aims to examine how Saudi executives make cybersecurity disclosure decisions in a rapidly changing digital environment. Ethical principles guide these decisions. Modern ethical frameworks combine with contextual values, including Islamic notions of responsibility and harm prevention, which support balanced judgment when leaders navigate transparency, protection and regulatory expectations.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Design/methodology/approach</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The research draws on 50 semistructured interviews with senior executives from finance, energy, industry, services, health care and technology. A thematic analysis supports the interpretation of ethical reasoning. Double coding, reflexive notes and sectoral comparison matrices strengthen analytical rigor.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Findings</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Executives view cybersecurity disclosure as an ethical act. Transparency matters. Nonmaleficence dominates when disclosure may expose vulnerabilities. Leaders rely on responsibility, fairness and harm prevention. Islamic ethical principles reinforce these choices across all sectors. The Chief Digital Officer plays a central mediating role between technical, regulatory and stakeholder demands.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Research limitations/implications</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The study focuses on one national context and one category of actors. Broader multistakeholder research is needed to deepen understanding.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Practical implications</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Organizations benefit from ethical disclosure frameworks, stronger governance structures and training on ethical risk communication. Integrating Islamic ethics enhances legitimacy, coherence and trust.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Originality/value</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The study provides one of the first empirical analyses showing how ethical and Islamic principles jointly guide cybersecurity disclosure in an emerging market undergoing rapid digital transformation.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Observations on Lean Office and artificial intelligence intricacies in the context of public administration scenarios using a systematic literature review
container-title: International Journal of Lean Six Sigma
7146107c537ac4336a5e1701dbdf47a500820ac1.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Purpose</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study aims to discuss the state of the art in Lean Office, its technological advancement through artificial intelligence (AI) and its application in the public sector, while proposing a way to unify these three areas.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Design/methodology/approach</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>A systematic literature review (SLR) following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses protocol identified literature published between 2020 and 2024. The final sample underwent bibliometric analysis (Bibliometrix and R language) to map the field’s conceptual and intellectual structures.</jats:p>

                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Findings</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>“Lean Principles” and “Public Sector” emerged as motor themes alongside “AI,” with “Lean Office” positioned as a transitional topic. The intellectual structure centers on Lean public sector adaptation. The analysis identifies two integration modes: AI for automating administrative tasks and AI as a support tool for Lean methods. However, tension exists between centralized AI development and the decentralized nature of Lean culture and principles.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Research limitations/implications</jats:title>

                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Practical implications</jats:title>

                    <jats:title>Originality/value</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This research bridges the knowledge gap by integrating three disparate themes: Lean Office, AI and public administration. title: Building organizational resilience in project-based SMEs through capability development: a process-based perspective
container-title: Journal of Enterprising Communities: People and Places in the Global Economy
1ef9fe4d5adb3b44db21b1887659658551a50578.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Purpose</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study examines how organizational resilience develops in project-based small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) through interconnected capability-building processes rather than isolated antecedents. Although prior research has identified numerous structural and strategic correlates of SME resilience, limited attention has been paid to how resilience emerges from learning, cultural embedding and adaptive capability development. Addressing this gap, the study develops and tests a process-based capability-development framework linking operational practices, organizational learning, organizational culture, dynamic capabilities and organizational resilience. The purpose of this study is to clarify the selective pathways through which SMEs build adaptive capacity under conditions of environmental uncertainty.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Design/methodology/approach</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The study uses survey data from 124 Canadian project-based SMEs and applies partial least squares structural equation modeling to examine the proposed capability-development relationships. The model tests the direct and indirect associations among operational practices, organizational learning, organizational culture, dynamic capabilities and resilience. Methodological rigor is ensured through reliability and validity assessments, non-response bias testing, marker-variable and common-latent-factor procedures and bootstrapped mediation analysis. The cross-sectional design supports the estimation of theoretically grounded associations while acknowledging limitations regarding temporal ordering.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Findings</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Dynamic capabilities emerge as the most immediate organizational mechanism associated with resilience. Organizational learning is positively associated with organizational culture, organizational culture is positively associated with dynamic capabilities and project management and risk management are positively associated with learning. Diversification is positively associated with dynamic capabilities and indirectly associated with resilience through dynamic capabilities. In contrast, longer sequential mediation pathways were not supported, indicating that capability development is selective rather than universal. The results highlight how adaptive capacity develops through specific organizational processes rather than through broad, multi-stage capability chains.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Research limitations/implications</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The cross-sectional design limits causal inference and prevents examination of how resilience unfolds over time. The sample is restricted to Canadian project-based SMEs, which may limit generalizability to other institutional contexts. Future research should use longitudinal or mixed-method designs to capture temporal dynamics, explore cross-country variation and examine how digital transformation and external shocks interact with internal capability-building processes. The findings refine process-based resilience theory by identifying which capability pathways matter most and which assumed sequential mechanisms do not hold empirically.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Practical implications</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The findings suggest that SME resilience is strengthened primarily through internal capability-building rather than through external support alone. Managers should invest in project management routines, risk management practices, organizational learning mechanisms and adaptive cultural norms that facilitate knowledge integration and capability development. Policymakers should prioritize interventions that enhance managerial training, learning infrastructures and collaborative knowledge-sharing platforms. Because diversification contributes indirectly through dynamic capabilities, strategic variety should be accompanied by deliberate capability development to ensure adaptive benefits.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Originality/value</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study reframes SME resilience as a process-based organizational outcome emerging from learning, cultural embedding and dynamic capability development rather than as a direct consequence of resources or external support. It advances dynamic capabilities theory by examining learning and culture as microfoundational processes in project-based, resource-constrained SMEs. The capability-development architecture provides a nuanced explanation of how SMEs sustain adaptive continuity within enterprising communities. By identifying both supported and unsupported pathways, the study offers a refined, empirically grounded perspective on how resilience develops through selective organizational processes.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Competition as a driver of democratization? Suffrage and migration in antebellum USA
container-title: Journal of Historical Political Economy
71182942987d913a660fba60a3e8af99cb202afe.abstract: <jats:p>In the early USA, suffrage was largely restricted to property owners. However, within a few decades, all states extended the franchise to poorer white men. A prominent theory argues that these reforms were driven by interstate competition for labor, as states broadened voting rights to attract workers. Yet, given the limited state capacity of the period, it is unclear whether workers indeed responded to changes in political rights. Using a contiguous-county, staggered difference-in-differences design, the author shows that franchise extensions causally increased local population growth. An analysis of local age structure suggests that the effect operated through migration rather than changes in fertility or mortality. These findings indicate that, in the antebellum USA, more inclusive political institutions attracted labor, lending support to the interstate-competition hypothesis.</jats:p>

title: System or self: the role of slaveholding on Congressional behavior in the US North, 1789−1861
container-title: Journal of Historical Political Economy
39c6994ccf2df075d06c31c912938096facbdabf.abstract: <jats:p>We use the 2022 Washington Post’s database of congressional enslavers to ask how much the direct interest of Northern politicians in slavery affected voting. Comparing systemic to self-interest parallels efforts to replace vocabulary, e.g., slaveholder with enslaver, which emphasizes individual agency (and culpability) over societal constraints. Northern slaveholders voted differently from their non-slaveholding Northern colleagues. But this gap was much smaller than the overall North−South divide. Slaveholding had minimal explanatory power over voting in both chambers, except for two periods in the Senate, notably in the 1850s with a slaveholding cluster. But the rise of the GOP diminished their power.</jats:p>

title: The study of intelligence in nature for an ecocentric perspective in education
container-title: Constellations of hope
e5922db9e5ce5f10c4af8eb8a418d81c612ec06b.abstract:
<jats:p>One of the greatest challenges of our time is establishing a new relationship with nature by adopting different knowledge, values, and attitudes. Currently, the anthropocentric worldview dominates social systems — from economics to education — and from this perspective nature and living beings are mere objects valued only for human benefit. To move forward, we must recognise the intrinsic value of all life, from microbes to entire landscapes, by adopting an ecocentric worldview. We can learn from Indigenous cultures that view humans and the natural world as a single community guided by reciprocity, respect and devotion. In these traditions, nature is alive, intelligent and a teacher. Simultaneously, scientific fields such as cognitive ecology, ethology and bioacoustics are providing compelling evidence that intelligence is an inherent characteristic of life. Furthermore, technologies like machine learning are now helping us decode non-human communication, a clear feature of intelligence.
            These insights offer a transformative opportunity to create educational content that supports an ecocentric perspective, awakening wonder, compassion and critical thinking. This article explores the philosophical foundations of ecocentric education and its relationship with intelligence in nature — examining capacities such as animal culture, communication and memory. Ultimately, it advocates for a paradigm shift: moving away from a mechanistic view of life towards a holistic, ecological perspective where nature is no longer an object, but a subject and a mentor.</jats:p>
