title: Artificial Intelligence and Youth Development: Assessing Negative Impacts in Cameroon
container-title: International Journal of Innovative Science and Research Technology
2787d554497107c82de9f013a70decc43b605759.abstract: This research evaluates the negative impacts of Artificial Intelligence dependency on the cognitive and academic development of students within the Cameroonian higher education landscape. Utilizing a multiple case study design to facilitate literal replication across diverse settings, this study analyzed data collected from students at the University of Yaoundé, the University of Bamenda, and Yaoundé International Business School. A total of 525 students were surveyed using a purposive sampling strategy to account for the unique dynamics of public university massification and private sector specialization in Cameroon. The findings indicate a high prevalence of AI utilization, with 85.3% of respondents reporting daily or weekly usage for academic tasks.

title: Digital Technology Use, Cognitive Engagement and Perceived Learning Effectiveness Among Adult Learners in Non-Formal Education in Uzbekistan
45a1f4b7c88044561b62fd4240d2f0ed18697212.abstract: Abstract Although digital technologies are increasingly embedded in adult education policy, evidence from post-Soviet Central Asia remains scarce. This sequential explanatory mixed-methods study examined how digital technology use relates to two proximal indicators of learning processes – cognitive engagement and perceived learning effectiveness – among adults in non-formal education programmes in Uzbekistan. Survey data from 312 learners nested in 26 programmes across three provinces were analysed with two-level random-intercept models, followed by semi-structured interviews with 22 learners and two facilitators, analysed through reflexive thematic analysis. After adjustment for age, gender, educational attainment, urban–rural location and programme type, digital technology use was positively associated with cognitive engagement (β = .38, 95% CI [.27, .49]) and perceived learning effectiveness (β = .35, 95% CI [.24, .46]). Between 17% and 18% of the variance in each outcome lay at the programme level. Four qualitative themes – socially produced digital self-efficacy, peer-mediated learning, institutional culture and structural barriers – helped to explain these patterns. Interpreted through self-directed learning theory and the capability approach, the findings suggest that the educational value of digital tools depends on the social and institutional conditions in which adults use them. The cross-sectional design and reliance on self-report preclude causal inference.

title: Artificial intelligence-based models for predicting bronchopulmonary dysplasia in preterm infants: a systematic review
container-title: Frontiers in Pediatrics
e41d772d879e787c32f509443b8895a263eec88c.abstract: Background Bronchopulmonary dysplasia (BPD) is one of the most common chronic respiratory complications in preterm infants. Early identification of high-risk patients is essential for individualizing preventive strategies and optimizing therapeutic decisions. Artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) models have emerged as promising tools to improve predictive performance in this population. Objective To evaluate and synthesize the predictive performance of AI-based models for BPD development in preterm infants and to assess their methodological quality. Methods A systematic review was conducted following PRISMA recommendations. We searched PubMed, Scopus and Cochrane Library up to February 2026. Studies developing or validating AI-based models for predicting BPD in preterm infants born at &lt;32 weeks of gestation and/or with a birth weight &lt; 1,500 g were included. Methodological quality and risk of bias were assessed using the PROBAST tool. Results Eighteen studies were included. Random Forest and XGBoost were the most frequently used algorithms. AUC values for the best-performing models ranged from 0.80 to 1.00, showing improved performance as postnatal variables were incorporated. However, the PROBAST assessment revealed a high overall risk of bias in 72.2% of the studies, primarily due to deficiencies in the analysis domain. Clinical applicability raised high concern in 38.9% of the studies due to a lack of external validation and heterogeneity in outcome definitions. Conclusions AI-based models show high discriminative capacity for BPD prediction; however, they have not yet demonstrated clear superiority over conventional statistical models in robust comparisons. Their routine clinical implementation is currently limited by poor methodological quality and scarce external validation. Systematic Review Registration https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261466494 , PROSPERO: CRD420261466494, registered retrospectively on August 4, 2026.

title: Attitudes towards artificial intelligence and their association with innovative behaviour among diploma nursing students in selected state nursing training schools in Sri Lanka: a cross-sectional study
ab39ed3c8cf24b5d9b2558fb1f43847651bef4c6.abstract: Abstract Background Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly embedded in healthcare and education. Nursing students will enter AI-enabled clinical environments, yet evidence from Sri Lanka on their attitudes towards AI and how these relate to innovative behaviour is limited. This study assessed AI attitudes and innovative behaviour and examined their association among diploma nursing students in selected state nursing training schools in Sri Lanka. Methods A descriptive cross-sectional study was conducted among 282 diploma nursing students from Kalutara and Galle Nursing Training Schools using systematic random sampling. Data were collected using an expert-reviewed and pretested self-administered questionnaire comprising sociodemographic items, the 13-item Artificial Intelligence Attitude Scale, and the 10-item Innovative Work Behaviour Scale. Descriptive statistics and tests of normality were performed in IBM SPSS Statistics version 27. Because the total scores were not normally distributed, Spearman's rank-order correlation was used to examine the association between AI attitudes and innovative behaviour. Statistical significance was set at p < 0.05. Results Among 282 participants, 228 (80.9%) were female and 260 (92.2%) were third-year students. The mean AI attitude score was 44.32 (SD 4.65), and the mean innovative behaviour score was 35.73 (SD 4.79). AI attitude scores showed a weak but statistically significant positive correlation with innovative behaviour scores (Spearman's rho = 0.203, p < 0.001). Conclusions More favourable AI attitudes were associated with slightly higher innovative behaviour among diploma nursing students, although the association was weak and does not establish causality. The findings support consideration of structured, responsible AI literacy and innovation-focused learning activities in nursing education. Larger multi-site and longitudinal studies are needed to identify additional factors that shape innovative behaviour.

title: Practical Bedside Tests for Assessing Postoperative Cognitive Dysfunction (POCD) in Anesthetized Patients
container-title: Journal of the Medical Association of Thailand
89bb02a8d8803dc56f0474315a1d0c943e80e694.abstract: Postoperative cognitive dysfunction (POCD)—characterized by deficits in memory, executive function, and processing speed—is a prevalent yet frequently underrecognized complication of surgery and anesthesia. POCD is associated with protracted recovery, diminished quality of life, and adverse long-term outcomes, particularly among elderly and high-risk populations. While early detection via bedside cognitive tests is vital for optimizing postoperative care, more comprehensive gold-standard neuropsychological batteries remain largely unfeasible in routine clinical practice due to significant time, cost, and resource constraints. This narrative review evaluates the clinical utility of practical bedside cognitive assessments for identifying POCD. Commonly employed tools—including the Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA), Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE), Trail Making Test (TMT), Digit Span, Clock Drawing Test (CDT), and Abbreviated Mental Test Score (AMTS)—are critically appraised regarding their sensitivity, limitations, and suitability for the perioperative environment. The review specifically addresses feasibility in acute postoperative settings, accounting for confounding factors such as age, literacy, and sensory or motor impairments. Furthermore, the necessity of establishing baseline cognitive status and the urgent need for tool validation within surgical cohorts are highlighted. No single bedside instrument offers a sufficiently comprehensive assessment for POCD. Rather, a multimodal approach—integrating high-sensitivity tools like the MoCA or TMT with rapid screening instruments—represents a more robust and clinically viable strategy for early detection. Future research must focus on standardizing assessment protocols and validating these tools across diverse surgical populations to ultimately enhance the quality of postoperative cognitive care.

title: The indirect association of emotional intelligence with self-reported performance-related outcomes through psychological resilience in athletes
container-title: Scientific Reports
277c425ae415c75b223f9f9b8319ceb0ed0849ff.abstract: Abstract The aim of this study is to examine the relationships between emotional intelligence and self-reported performance-related outcomes (psychological performance and subjective athletic performance satisfaction) in athletes, and to evaluate the indirect role of psychological resilience in these relationships. The research was conducted using a quantitative, cross-sectional design. A total of 403 national-team athletes aged between 18 and 38 years voluntarily participated. Data were collected through self-report measures of emotional intelligence, psychological resilience, psychological performance, and aggression, together with a visual analog scale assessing subjective athletic performance satisfaction. Direct and indirect associations were estimated using path analysis with observed composite scores. Statistical inference was based on 95% bias-corrected and accelerated (BCa) bootstrap confidence intervals obtained from 10,000 resamples, with aggression included as an auxiliary covariate. Emotional intelligence was positively associated with psychological resilience (β = 0.586, 95% BCa CI [0.495, 0.670]), and psychological resilience was positively associated with psychological performance (β = 0.469, 95% BCa CI [0.368, 0.559]) and subjective athletic performance satisfaction (β = 0.170, 95% BCa CI [0.054, 0.286]). The adjusted direct associations of emotional intelligence with psychological performance (β = 0.013, 95% BCa CI [-0.093, 0.121]) and subjective athletic performance satisfaction (β = 0.117, 95% BCa CI [-0.004, 0.231]) were not supported because their confidence intervals included zero. Significant indirect associations through psychological resilience were observed for psychological performance (β = 0.275, 95% BCa CI [0.205, 0.354]) and subjective athletic performance satisfaction (β = 0.100, 95% BCa CI [0.032, 0.176]). After accounting for aggression as an auxiliary covariate, the findings indicate that psychological resilience is an important statistical pathway linking emotional intelligence with self-reported performance-related outcomes. Because the study was cross-sectional, the results should be interpreted as directional associations rather than causal effects. Because all outcomes were self-reported with satisfaction assessed by a single item and the psychological performance measure showing mixed confirmatory factor analysis fit these associations should be interpreted with caution.

title: Effect of albumin on artificial membrane permeation of acidic drugs
container-title: ADMET and DMPK
2a377770c3bfd13aa15b57eff99c77a460287066.abstract: Background and purpose: The free fraction theory (FFT) plays a central role in pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics. However, for acidic drugs, deviations from FFT have been reported in cell‑based assays involving albumin binding. The purpose of the present study was to investigate the effect of albumin on the passive membrane permeation of acidic drugs in the parallel artificial membrane permeation assay (PAMPA). Experimental approach: Eight acidic drugs (atorvastatin, bosentan, entacapone, fluvastatin, meloxicam, pitavastatin, rosuvastatin, and tolbutamide) were used as model drugs. The PAMPA membrane consisted of phospholipids dissolved in decane. The effective permeation coefficient (Pe) was measured in the absence and presence of 4 % bovine serum albumin (BSA) in the donor solution. The unbound fraction (fu) was determined using equilibrium dialysis. Concentration dependence and phospholipid‑composition dependence of Pe were examined. Key results: Pe was substantially reduced by the addition of BSA, showing good consistency with FFT. The minor deviation from FFT was explained by a concentration‑dependent increase in the membrane permeability of unbound drug molecules, except for rosuvastatin. The effect of BSA on the permeability of rosuvastatin was influenced by phospholipid composition, possibly suggesting albumin-phospholipid interactions. Conclusion: PAMPA permeation showed good consistency with FFT. The slight deviations from FFT observed for the low‑permeability drugs can be explained by the concentration dependence of unbound drug permeability, except for rosuvastatin.

title: From Entrepreneurial Orientation to Environmental Performance: Dynamic Capabilities and Institutional Weaknesses in an Emerging Economy
container-title: Business Strategy and the Environment
ce7f3e93fa9af2c266d1592bdf2f88bfefa80e16.abstract: ABSTRACT This study examines how entrepreneurial orientation is associated with environmental performance in manufacturing firms, focusing on the mediating roles of dynamic managerial capabilities and dynamic technological capabilities and the conditioning role of institutional weaknesses. Drawing on dynamic capabilities theory and institutional theory, the study adopts a capability‐based and context‐sensitive perspective to explain how entrepreneurial strategies translate into environmental outcomes in an emerging economy. Survey data were collected from 320 manufacturing firms located predominantly within Ghana's Southern industrial zone and analysed using a two‐step approach involving confirmatory factor analysis and regression‐based bootstrapped estimation of direct, indirect and conditional indirect associations. The results show that entrepreneurial orientation is positively associated with environmental performance, primarily through dynamic managerial and technological capabilities. Moreover, the indirect associations are stronger under higher levels of institutional weakness, indicating that internal capabilities become more salient in challenging institutional environments. The study contributes to the entrepreneurship and sustainability literature by demonstrating that entrepreneurial orientation is associated with environmental performance mainly through capability‐based mechanisms and that institutional context shapes the strength of these mechanisms. The findings offer context‐specific insights for managers and policymakers seeking to enhance environmental performance among manufacturing firms operating in weak institutional settings, although the geographic concentration of the sample requires caution in generalising the results to less industrialized and resource‐constrained regions.

title: Bottom-up: utilising artificial intelligence to identify what successful leaders do, using an abductive approach
container-title: Strategy & Leadership
3cee68ff35b51f9a6b094eafc9705df4214c3916.abstract: Purpose Identifying exceptional leaders remains a top priority for organisations. Traditionally, leaders were selected using a battery of assessments measuring key personal attributes believed to make leaders successful. However, there has been a shift away from selecting leaders based on an a priori list of virtues, towards a focus on the actual behaviours linked to high performance. This abductive approach in competency framework development for leaders starts with the behaviours demonstrated in assessments and then constructs the competency framework in a bottom-up approach. Design/methodology/approach In the current study, a total of 15 411 leaders from 283 different companies and 38 countries completed a 3.5-hour online assessment centre simulation exercise. Natural language processing and machine learning were then utilised to identify 38 competencies by screening more than 30 million words. We then mapped this artificial intelligence-derived framework to prominent leadership models. Findings Despite strong congruence between frameworks, the abductive approach revealed three critical findings: 1) Not all competencies are equally distributed across the leader population; 2) Competencies are distributed across job levels, with some commonly observed in junior leadership roles and others primarily amongst senior leaders; and 3) the artefacts collected by the machine-learning algorithm enable a more granular view of the behaviours that constitute a competency compared to human assessors. Originality/value Using abductive methods to supplement deductive models capitalising on the strengths of both approaches, yield more nuanced leadership competency frameworks.

title: From reactive to proactive: how artificial intelligence is transforming organizational crisis management
container-title: Journal of Ethics in Entrepreneurship and Technology
db1de318fec5c17ca66a9f918e647042eb8e41f2.abstract: Purpose This paper examines how artificial intelligence (AI) can improve organizational crisis management as firms increasingly operate in a polycrisis marked by overlapping pandemics, geopolitical conflict and rapid technological change. It maps AI capabilities to the before, during and after phases of the crisis lifecycle. Design/methodology/approach This narrative/conceptual review synthesizes empirical and theoretical scholarship on AI in crisis management across management, information systems and crisis communication journals. It integrates evidence on early warning, anticipation, social media analytics, crisis communication and resilience into a lifecycle framework. Findings Before a crisis, AI-driven early warning systems can predict disruptions weeks in advance and help mitigate losses. During a crisis, natural language processing supports situational awareness, and generative AI accelerates communication. After a crisis, social listening and simulation support learning, while deepfake defense protects reputation. Benefits are conditional on governance maturity and complement, rather than replace, human judgment. Practical implications Firms should adopt AI proactively but judiciously for sensing, triage and rehearsal, guided by governance readiness rather than novelty. They should also invest in data governance and interoperability. Organizations should keep accountability and ethical judgment visibly human where trust and empathy matter most. SMEs benefit from modular, centrally supported adoption pathways. Originality/value This paper integrates AI and crisis management into a lifecycle framework centered on the governance conditions that enable AI to improve outcomes. It advances two propositions: (1) AI’s value shifts from augmenting anticipation to substituting risk as authorship becomes visible, and (2) governance maturity moderates, rather than predicts, AI’s crisis-management payoff.

title: From awe to emotional brand attachment: a cognitive appraisal perspective on VR brand experiences
container-title: Journal of Product & Brand Management
2a02739e2da8b57381342589a61ac9c76d3c74b0.abstract: Purpose Prior research on awe in relation to virtual reality (VR) has treated awe as a response to technological stimuli, leaving the consumer appraisals through which awe arises underexplored. Drawing on cognitive appraisal theory, this paper aims to address this gap by investigating whether aesthetic, sensory and content appraisals of a VR brand experience predict awe and whether awe mediates the relationships between these appraisals and emotional brand attachment. Design/methodology/approach Data were collected via a survey of 334 Generation Z participants who experienced an in-person brand encounter via a VR headset and were analysed using covariance-based structural equation modelling in LISREL. Findings Aesthetic, sensory and content appraisals positively predict awe, which, in turn, predicts emotional brand attachment. Awe also mediates the relationships between each of the three appraisal and emotional brand attachment. Originality/value At the intersection of the cognitive psychology of VR and emotional branding, this paper reframes the origins of awe in VR brand experiences, shifting from a stimulus-centred to an appraisal-centred account. It also identifies aesthetic, sensory and content appraisals as the experiential predictors of awe and extends emotional branding to self-transcendent emotions by showing how awe translates experiential appraisals into emotional brand attachment.

title: Radial Kernel Attention for Long-Range Modeling in Polymer Machine Learning Force Fields
569d9c0f37ae1ad406ec120b61cd9e579ab007dc.abstract: We introduce Radial Kernel Attention (RKA) for long-range modeling in polymer machine learning force fields. Local neighbor graphs constrain communication across polymer chains and their surrounding environments, while explicit all-pair attention incurs quadratic cost. RKA maps atomic distances from the cluster centroid to learned radial features and combines their overlap with content-dependent queries and keys. Factorized aggregation and readout enable global feature exchange at linear cost in atom count for fixed feature dimensions. We insert the invariant scalar update between EquiformerV3 local blocks and obtain conservative forces by differentiating the total energy, including its radial coordinate dependence. We evaluate energy and force prediction for finite polymer-derived clusters in OPoly26. Our models are trained on the official training split for 12 epochs and evaluated directly after training on the complete official validation split. A matched 5M comparison shows that RKA reduces per-atom energy and force MAEs by 67.4% and 36.3%, respectively. The 20M RKA model is compared with UMA-S-1.2 and UMA-S-1.2.1 on the same validation structures. The 20M model attains a total-energy MAE of 15.81 meV and a force MAE of 2.619 meV/Å; its per-atom energy MAE is 0.1182 meV/atom. RKA provides a compact global communication pathway that improves energy and force prediction on the evaluated polymer-derived clusters.

title: Trustworthy Federated Clinical Intelligence with Homomorphic Encryption and  Explainable AI
container-title: International Journal on Advanced Computer Engineering and Communication Technology
e9efaf7e4de70a4bb9a5e76e1dc2d37a457ecb6d.abstract: Cross-institutional clinical artificial intelligence is constrained by fragmented patient data, non-identically distributed (non-IID) populations, leakage from shared model updates, and limited interpretability. Federated learning (FL) preserves data locality, but ordinary FL neither makes model updates confidential nor guarantees stable optimization under heterogeneous clients. This paper proposes a defense-in-depth framework that coordinates Federated Proximal (FedProx) optimization, record-level differential privacy (DP), Cheon–Kim–Kim–Song (CKKS) approximate homomorphic encryption, and explainable artificial intelligence (XAI). FedProx limits local model drift; DP-SGD bounds the influence of an individual training record; and CKKS permits weighted aggregation while client updates remain encrypted. A key-separated design keeps the aggregation server from being provisioned with the secret key used to reveal individual contributions; only the aggregate is released for global-model construction. Grad-CAM and SHAP/LIME provide clinician-facing explanations, while an audit dashboard reports convergence, privacy-accounting inputs, encryption status, and systems overhead. We formalize the learning objective, privacy mechanism, encrypted aggregation, threat model, numerical approximation error, communication footprint, and an evaluation protocol spanning IID and controlled non-IID partitions. The contribution is a reproducible system-level co-design and evaluation framework rather than a new cryptographic primitive or optimization algorithm.

title: India's Energy Transition Towards Methanol and Ethanol Economy in Pursuit of Carbon Neutrality
container-title: Journal of Energy and Environmental Sustainability
3bf34d9ceb12152dcadfa272c9ccb48f68b482c2.abstract: In 2021, India committed to achieving Net Zero emissions by 2070. India announced this commitment at COP26. The Indian government is committed to focusing on transport, buildings, urban and power sectors to achieve Net Zero by lowering greenhouse gas emissions. India has already started investing in the "Ethanol Economy" by replacing a significant fraction of transport gasoline with ethanol. India has progressively increased ethanol use by enhancing ethanol production capacity. National Institution for Transforming India (NITI Ayog), a think tank of the government of India, has envisioned a "Methanol Economy" to support energy transition activities. Technology demonstrations for methanol production and vehicle field trials have been undertaken. This paper aims to summarise the role of the "Methanol Economy" and "Ethanol Economy" in India's quest for energy transition to achieve net zero. India's energy security and the approaches followed by other countries to achieving net zero are summarised as well. Various aspects of the "Methanol and Ethanol Economy", such as production capacity, emissions, and role for greenhouse gas emissions reductions, are discussed. Various steps taken by the government of India are summarised, which include setting up standards for the adaptation of methanol/ethanol, setting up production infrastructure, and technology development for end-user applications, etc.

title: An Ecocentric Assessment Framework for Artificial Intelligence and Computational Design in Architecture
container-title: Research into Ecological Transformation in Architectural Sciences: From Anthropocentric Design to Ecology-Focused Design
e88ddf4966a22876df09e503b06d3de0d3c14442.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) supports environmental performance prediction and the evaluation of alternatives in architectural design. However, improvements in energy or carbon indicators alone do not demonstrate that non-human life holds independent value in design decisions. This chapter examines AI and related computational design approaches in architecture from an ecocentric perspective through a focused narrative review and conceptual synthesis supported by a structured database search. The 375 raw records retrieved from Scopus and Web of Science were reduced to 256 unique records; following title and abstract screening, a final purposive selection of 19 studies was established. Together with one supplementary publication, the 20 documents were examined under the themes of performance and decision-making, life cycle boundaries, the representation of non-human life, habitat geometry and materials, time and maintenance, and visual generation and ecological validation. The synthesis informs a preliminary ecocentric assessment framework comprising three dimensions: stakeholder scope, integration of environmental and ecological impacts into decision-making, and ecological responsibility. By distinguishing computational success from ecological outcomes, the framework provides an analytical basis for examining who benefits from design decisions, how environmental and ecological requirements influence those decisions, and how responsibility for their outcomes is addressed.

title: From Vernacular Ecological Intelligence to Planetary Design: Life Cycle Thinking as a Framework for Ecological Transformation in Architecture
container-title: Research into Ecological Transformation in Architectural Sciences: From Anthropocentric Design to Ecology-Focused Design
8c713823c70f94c725f6482bb0c297b9e934319d.abstract: The ecological transformation of architecture requires reconsidering how architectural knowledge is produced, environmental consequences are evaluated, and responsibility is addressed across spatial, temporal, and ecological scales. This chapter brings vernacular ecological knowledge into dialogue with Life Cycle Thinking and Planetary Design. Vernacular architecture is approached as a dynamic socio-ecological knowledge system shaped by culture, climate, materiality, and collective practices. Maintenance, repair, adaptability, and intergenerational learning are examined as forms of situated ecological intelligence rather than historical models to be replicated. Life Cycle Thinking provides a framework for integrating place-based knowledge into contemporary architectural decisions, extending environmental assessment beyond carbon to circularity, biodiversity, regeneration, cultural continuity, and resilience. The relationship with Planetary Design is understood as a scalar and epistemic connection through which local knowledge informs decisions affecting broader ecological and material systems. Rather than prescribing a universal method, Planetary Design is presented as a boundary-aware, sufficiency-led, regenerative, justice-oriented, and adaptive approach. The chapter argues that ecological transformation depends on combining quantitative assessment with local knowledge, social needs, interconnected system boundaries, and long-term stewardship.

title: Generative artificial intelligence drives large model generation algorithm for enhancing Chinese modern traditional cultural knowledge
container-title: Discover Artificial Intelligence
f48c63c87e8ab5a4802a0daf6c6d06f0de6ee24c.abstract: Abstract To address outdated knowledge, cultural-context mismatch, weak evidence linkage, and unsupported expansion in general-purpose large language model generation of traditional-cultural content, this study proposes a generative AI-driven knowledge-enhanced generation algorithm. The method decouples a frozen Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct generator from an external dynamic knowledge base and uses a four-field semantic tag scheme covering cultural category, historical stage, regional origin, and application scenario. Candidate evidence is ranked by vector similarity, graph relations, tag consistency, source credibility, and conflict penalties, then assembled into a constrained prompt without modifying the internal attention layers of the frozen model. An incremental update mechanism combines source verification, conflict detection, and expert review, while factual consistency, cultural-context adaptability, and evidence coverage are used for post-generation verification. Experiments cover classical texts, cultural heritage objects, intangible cultural heritage crafts, traditional Chinese opera, and folk culture, with 1,080 factual question-answering samples and 360 contextual generation tasks. The proposed system achieves 88.61% factual accuracy, 95.28% answer relevance, 94.17% evidence faithfulness, and 92.50% cultural-context adaptability. After knowledge updating, accuracy on update-dependent questions rises from 58.67% to 91.33%. These results indicate that the proposed framework provides a traceable, context-sensitive generation pipeline while retaining a frozen generation model; between-system differences are interpreted descriptively because complete paired baseline predictions were not retained.

title: The Impact of Artificial Intelligence Adoption on Corporate Default Risk: Empirical Evidence Based on Large Language Models
container-title: Innovation in Science and Technology
63702179c1297b4221b67f2229489d8c255713b3.abstract: Against the backdrop of rapid advances in digital technologies and growing uncertainty in the business environment, artificial intelligence (AI) offers firms new opportunities to strengthen risk identification, improve managerial decision-making, and mitigate default risk. Using firm-level data from Chinese A-share listed companies over the period 2009–2024, this study empirically examines the relationship between AI adoption and corporate default risk. The results indicate that AI adoption is associated with a significant reduction in corporate default risk. This finding remains robust to alternative fixed-effects specifications, different levels of standard-error clustering, and the exclusion of observations from periods affected by major external shocks. Heterogeneity analyses further reveal that the negative association is particularly pronounced among firms in non-high-tech industries and those located in eastern and central China. By examining AI adoption from a corporate risk management perspective, this study extends the literature on the economic consequences of AI adoption and provides firm-level empirical evidence on the role of digital technologies in mitigating financial risk. The findings also offer policy implications for integrating AI into corporate management practices and strengthening firms’ risk governance capabilities.

title: Truthful, Wise, and Responsible
container-title: Aletheia Christian Educators Journal
9d21647987783075650a6ac214947b7e617fade7.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly entering dental education, and recent reviews report both its benefits and recurring concerns about factual inaccuracy, academic integrity, over-reliance, bias, and privacy. Existing responses are largely technical and regulatory; they specify what should be done but say little about the character of the educators and students who use AI. This critical integrative review proposes a Christian virtue framework, grounded in the doctrine of the imago Dei, to guide dental educators and students. Empirical literature on AI in dental and health-professions education was read alongside Catholic and evangelical documents on AI and Christian scholarship on education and personhood. Five virtues, identified from Christian virtue-ethics literature on AI, were mapped to the main AI issues: truthfulness (hallucinated content and academic integrity), practical wisdom (automation bias, overconfidence, and deskilling), responsibility (accountability for AI-supported decisions), justice (bias and unequal access), and love (empathy, the clinician–patient relationship, and privacy). For each virtue, implications for educators and students are outlined. The framework suggests that responsible AI use in dental education is a matter not only of policy but also of formation, and it offers Christian dental schools a basis for curricula and institutional guidance.

title: The mediating role of self-efficacy in the relationships of technophilia and positive emotional experience with perceived learning effectiveness in AI-supported EFL education
container-title: Discover Artificial Intelligence
1e046e91cd43fe005cca1d83a4437e55e4d42551.abstract: Abstract Despite the increasing integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into English as a Foreign Language (EFL) education, the psychological mechanisms linking learners’ technological dispositions and emotional experiences to perceived learning effectiveness remain undertheorized and empirically underexplored. This study examined whether self-efficacy served as a statistical mediator in the relationships of technophilia and positive emotional experience with perceived learning effectiveness in AI-supported EFL education. A cross-sectional survey was conducted involving 234 students enrolled in English-language courses at a private college of health sciences. Adapted multi-item scales on technophilia, positive emotional experience, self-efficacy, and perceived learning effectiveness were administered. Structural equation modeling with bootstrapping (5000 resamples) was used to examine direct and indirect associations. Self-efficacy demonstrated the strongest direct association with perceived learning effectiveness (β = 0.375, p = 0.001). Positive emotional experience was strongly associated with self-efficacy (β = 0.624, p < 0.001), and its indirect association with perceived learning effectiveness through self-efficacy was significant (β = 0.234, 95% CI [0.128, 0.351]). Technophilia was also positively associated with self-efficacy (β = 0.307, p = 0.002), and its indirect association with perceived learning effectiveness through self-efficacy was significant. The findings were consistent with self-efficacy partially mediating both relationships. These findings suggest that learners’ confidence in managing AI-supported tasks plays an important role in linking affective dispositions to perceived effectiveness appraisals. The study contributes to computer-assisted language learning (CALL) research by clarifying how positive orientation toward AI-supported technologies, emotional experience, and efficacy beliefs jointly relate to learners’ perceptions of effective AI-supported language learning. Pedagogically, the findings suggest that progressively scaffolded practice and mastery-oriented AI tasks may strengthen self-efficacy and improve learners’ perceived effectiveness in AI-supported EFL environments.

title: Role of Artificial Intelligence in Disease and Pest Management in Cauliflower: A Review
container-title: International Journal of Plant & Soil Science
f6d9a7d2865720ba3912565ea2b876139ac95423.abstract: Cauliflower (Brassica oleracea var. botrytis L.) is a nutritionally important cole vegetable and a high-value component of intensive vegetable production. Its yield and market quality are frequently reduced by bacterial, fungal and oomycete diseases and by insect pests that cause direct feeding injury or facilitate secondary infections. Conventional disease and pest surveillance is largely dependent on visual scouting, expert diagnosis and periodic field observations. These approaches remain indispensable, but they can be labour-intensive, subjective and difficult to scale over large production areas. Artificial intelligence (AI), including machine learning, deep learning, computer vision, image segmentation, object detection, remote sensing and predictive analytics, offers a complementary approach for rapid and repeatable crop-health assessment. This review examines the potential role of AI in cauliflower disease and pest management, covering image acquisition, disease classification, lesion localisation, severity estimation, insect identification, automated counting, forecasting, smartphone applications, UAV-based surveillance and AI-enabled integrated pest management. Cauliflower-specific research has demonstrated promising performance of deep-learning models. The Cauli-Det modified YOLOv8 system reported precision of 93.2%, recall of 82.6% and mean average precision of 91.1% for bacterial soft rot, downy mildew and black rot in its experimental dataset (Uddin et al., 2024). Another recent cauliflower study reported 99.85% classification accuracy using EfficientNet-B3 under its experimental conditions (Malik et al., 2025). Broader plant-disease research also demonstrates strong potential for CNNs and transfer learning (Mohanty et al., 2016; Ferentinos, 2018), while pest-detection research supports automated insect recognition and monitoring (Thenmozhi & Reddy, 2019; Chakrabarty et al., 2026). However, field variability, limited crop-specific datasets, class imbalance, symptom similarity, model explainability, computational requirements and inadequate independent validation remain major constraints. Future research should integrate AI predictions with weather, crop stage, pest abundance, disease severity and economic thresholds so that the technology supports practical, affordable and environmentally responsible IPM in cauliflower.

title: Generative Artificial Intelligence and the Reconstruction of Subjectivity in Literary Creation
container-title: Frontiers in International Humanities & Social Sciences
c16ed156eadd87151a511a77af2845f3b097e319.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence can participate in literary composition by proposing plots, producing passages and revising prose. Its participation raises questions about the position from which a work is imagined, judged and presented to readers. This paper examines the reconstruction of literary subjectivity through theoretical argument and analysis of research on assisted writing. It distinguishes subjectivity from observable interaction, the institutional attribution of authorship and evaluations of textual quality. Literary theories of authorship and dialogue are brought into conversation with accounts of writing processes and technological mediation, with attention to their different explanatory purposes. A comparative framework considers intention, lived experience, narrative form and responsibility across conception, drafting and revision. The analysis identifies tensions involving delegated intention, narrative anchoring, simulated experience, stylistic specificity and public attribution. It proposes that agency can be sustained through active reconsideration of creative aims, consequential aesthetic judgement, attention to experiential and cultural particularity, and accountable relations with readers. These are analytical proposals, not a validated measure of subjectivity. Existing studies concern specific interfaces and writing tasks and cannot establish a universal effect on literary identity. The paper reports no new experiment or interviews; its focus is short fiction and novel writing.

title: Artificial Intelligence and Sustainable  Entrepreneurship in Territorial Innovation  Ecosystems: A Scoping Review of Actors, Pathways and Gaps
eaa3387f2f9610a785c02e8a7d05fe6f5d7cf986.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly presented as a lever for sustainable entrepreneurship and the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), yet little is known about how its contribution unfolds within the territorial ecosystems where ventures emerge. This scoping review mapped how AI is conceptualised, its pathways, ecosystem actors, outcomes, risks and gaps. Following JBI guidance and PRISMA-ScR, we searched EBSCO Discovery Service, Lens.org and SciELO (2020–2026); AI-assisted screening and charting were fully verified, and two reviewers coded independently. Of 910 records, 26 studies were included. The evidence is recent (88% from 2025–2026) and concentrated in Europe and Asia; only three studies address Latin America. Of the 26 studies, 11 view AI through an instrumental lens, 10 through an infrastructural or orchestrating lens and 5 through an institutional lens. Sustainable business models (11), venture creation and ecosystem orchestration (10 each) were the most frequent pathways; governments and universities, the most frequent actors. Environmental effects were addressed in 15 studies but measured with an outcome indicator in only 2, and the SDGs cited were mainly economic and social (especially SDGs 8 and 9). We propose an integrative framework, research propositions and an agenda on causal designs, environmental measurement, AI governance and Latin America.

title: Tidal City Intelligence: A Conceptual Framework for AI-Enabled Service Governance in Cities with Fluctuating Populations
9125839bb912dfa67489dd5a63f2a2fd021e86f5.abstract: Many cities serve far more people than their civil register counts, and the gap rises and falls with tourist seasons, holidays, pilgrimages and festivals. Municipal budgets, staffing and data systems are nonetheless sized to the register. This conceptual paper introduces the Tidal City, a city whose population present swings in recurring, largely predictable cycles that change how public services must be planned. We distinguish the concept from the service population, tourism seasonality and overtourism; propose a two-part Tidal Index measuring the swing’s amplitude and regularity; and offer a typology of seasonal, day-visitor and event-driven tidal cities. Drawing on dynamic capabilities and adaptive governance theory, we set out Tidal City Intelligence, a four-layer framework (Sense, Anticipate, Adapt, Govern) describing the data and AI capabilities a local government needs, and derive testable propositions for each layer. Published data from Pattaya, Thailand, put the average population present at roughly two to three times the registered population and show annual waste moving with guest arrivals while the register barely changed. With only annual guest data, the case illustrates load and demand regularity rather than the full index. The paper offers cities a common measure of the problem and researchers an empirical agenda.

title: An Integrated Policy Framework for the Informal Economy: Based on Comparative Drivers and Dynamics Across ASEAN-5
4ec865564d651b8d9d77d390c1bf28f4500004ec.abstract: The informal economy remains an important source of employment across ASEAN-5 economies despite economic growth and formalization initiatives. This study examines informal economic activity in Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Thailand, and Vietnam through bibliometric mapping and comparative qualitative analysis, drawing on PLS-SEM findings reported by Ramdani Salim et al. (2026) for panel data covering 2015–2022. The reported results indicate a negative association between institutional quality and informality (β = −0.378; p = 0.015), alongside positive associations for social protection, labor market policies, and economic growth. These patterns are consistent with possible coverage gaps and regulatory constraints, but do not establish their causal mechanisms. The reported technological mediation result was not statistically significant (β = 0.011; p = 0.335), providing no sufficient evidence of mediation in that model. The comparative analysis identifies differences in institutional development, labor market structures, social protection systems, and digital governance across the five countries. Its contribution is to interpret these findings within national policy contexts and develop an integrated framework combining institutional strengthening, inclusive social protection, adaptive labor regulation, and digital governance. The framework offers policy directions for inclusive and sustainable development, rather than evidence of the effectiveness of individual interventions.

title: Hybrid TensorRT–PyTorch Inference Acceleration for Attention-Based CNNs with Dynamic ROI Sampling: A Case Study on Jetson Nano
2356aca907e0d5b1b6084ccaae24703cb4766568.abstract: Edge AI deployment requires low-latency inference on devices with tight constraints in size, weight, power, and cost. NVIDIA TensorRT accelerates inference through layer fusion, precision reduction, and kernel auto-tuning, but a model containing even one unsupported operator cannot be compiled into a single engine. This paper presents a hybrid TensorRT–PyTorch deployment in which the supported subnetworks run as TensorRT engines while the unsupported operations fall back to native PyTorch, and applies it to an attention-based convolutional neural network (ACNN) whose region-of-interest sampling operators are unsupported. On an NVIDIA Jetson Nano, the hybrid approach reduced the end-to-end latency of ACNN-dsc, the fastest native PyTorch model, from 38.37 ms to 20.40 ms (1.88×) under FP32. Under FP16, the hybrid ACNN-k3 achieved the lowest latency of 17.78 ms, a 2.23× speedup over its PyTorch FP32 counterpart and 2.16× over the fastest PyTorch model. Stepwise profiling of the image preprocessing pipeline showed that transferring raw images and performing most conversions on the GPU more than halves preprocessing latency. Further analyses across devices, precisions, and frameworks show that practical latency on edge AI accelerators depends on hardware and runtime factors beyond FLOPs and model size.

title: Cognitive Computing at the Edge: Lag Analysis and Neural Network Forecasting for Fishery Landings in the Colombian Caribbean
104069ce56d5a7b920f01172ca80aacf17057ffc.abstract: Fishery-dependent indices in data-limited fisheries are short and incomplete, which raises the question of when adaptive learned models, including cognitively inspired ones deployed at the edge, are justified. We analysed monthly landings per unit effort (LPUE) of pink shrimp (Penaeus notialis) in the Gulf of Morrosquillo, Colombian Caribbean: 65.7% of values are missing and the longest continuous segment has 28 months. Naive, trend, autoregressive (AR), echo state network (ESN), LightGBM and LSTM models were compared in rolling-origin experiments with training-only preprocessing, and their cost was measured on an NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano. One-step-ahead errors were 5.1–5.7 kg per trip for the trend, the AR(2) and the learned models, against 7.6 for persistence; no learned model showed a robust out-of-sample improvement over a linear trend or an AR(2). An exploratory model incorporating river flow at a data-selected lag achieved the lowest RMSE (4.2 kg per trip), but its improvement over the statistical baselines was not statistically conclusive and was not consistently reproduced when lag selection was restricted to the training data at each origin. Backcasting was worse than persistence. A fit took 8 ms (AR) to 3–9 s (LSTM); the double-precision ESN execution process showed the largest peak memory footprint (1.7–4.1 GB of 8 GB). The limit is the information in the series, not the platform; under these conditions a linear trend or an AR(2) is a sufficient reference.

title: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN HIGHER EDUCATION THROUGH THE FOUNDATIONS OF BASIC RESEARCH, ECOLOGY AND ACADEMIC CONSCIENCE: A REFLECTIVE COMMENTARY
container-title: ShodhSamajik: Journal of Social Studies
c2d6611c513c2513c1547f4e4f6ff0a0d5e4c39e.abstract: Artificial intelligence is increasingly discussed through frameworks of adoption, automation, and organisational reinvention. Their application to higher education requires careful consideration of what education is intended to achieve. This reflective commentary examines McKinsey's three horizons of AI transformation through my experiences in ecological research, university teaching, postgraduate supervision, and academic writing. It develops ten connected arguments concerning scientific foundations, independent learning, field experience, curiosity, institutional resilience, academic conscience, respectful leadership, educational relationships, environmental responsibility, and selective adoption. Selected empirical studies and foundational ecological literature support the discussion, while personal judgments are distinguished from established findings. I argue that faster production of academic material alone cannot demonstrate deeper understanding or stronger research competence. AI can help when its use aligns with learning objectives and is supported by verification, fair assessment, and accountable human decisions. Risks include dependence on generated explanations, weakening of observational skills, restriction of exploratory inquiry, unfair judgments about authorship, increased workload, unequal access, and environmental costs. An ecological perspective also encourages attention to relationships, feedback, and institutions' ability to function when technological services fail. I propose that universities assess AI by what students can explain independently, how reliably they engage with evidence, and the quality of educational relationships. The central responsibility is to preserve the conditions that enable people to become capable researchers and conscientious members of society.

title: Smart Democracy: Leveraging Artificial Intelligence to Combat Election  Misinformation in Nigeria
container-title: International Journal of Innovative Science and Research Technology
ceaf28012c87f425c86aaa40b8afe8b993f3262a.abstract: The increasing use of digital communication technologies has transformed democratic participation in Nigeria, but it has also accelerated the spread of election misinformation through social media and other online platforms. False political information, manipulated digital content, and coordinated disinformation campaigns have continued to undermine electoral credibility, public trust, and informed voter decision-making. Artificial Intelligence (AI) has emerged as a promising tool for detecting misinformation, verifying online content, identifying coordinated inauthentic behavior, and supporting evidence-based electoral communication. Despite these opportunities, there is limited empirical evidence on how AI can be effectively integrated into Nigeria's electoral communication system to strengthen democratic governance. This study examines the role of AI in combating election misinformation and promoting smart democracy in Nigeria. Specifically, it investigates the prevalence and patterns of election misinformation, assesses stakeholders' awareness and adoption of AI technologies for misinformation detection, examines the opportunities and challenges associated with AI deployment, and proposes communication strategies for responsible AI use during elections. The study adopts a mixed-methods research design, combining quantitative surveys with qualitative interviews involving electoral officials, journalists, fact-checkers, communication experts, and registered voters. Quantitative data will be analyzed using descriptive and inferential statistics, while qualitative data will be analyzed through thematic analysis. The findings are expected to provide practical recommendations for policymakers, the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), media organizations, technology developers, and civil society organizations on leveraging AI to enhance electoral transparency, improve information integrity, strengthen public trust, and promote democratic participation in Nigeria. The study contributes to the growing literature on artificial intelligence, development communication, digital governance, and democratic innovation in Africa.

title: Divergent research orientations of affective and emotion concepts in artificial intelligence education through a bibliometric analysis
container-title: Discover Artificial Intelligence
71d9530c40fb3216e3687cdf1569e621bad79cf4.abstract: Abstract This study adopted bibliometric analysis, employing a dual-track keyword search of the Scopus database and including 292 publications from 2020 to 2025 for keyword co-occurrence analysis and five-dimensional content analysis. Content coding followed a hybrid procedure in which two large language models produced initial codes and the researchers arbitrated disagreements, and reliability was examined by a second independent coder. Based on keyword analysis, four major categories were identified: technical recognition, pedagogical application, psychological and emotional response, and generative AI and emerging technologies. The technical-recognition category had a relatively earlier average publication year, whereas the other three have been concurrently active in recent years. The annual volume of publications grew steadily, reaching 151 articles in 2025, approximately 8.9 times that of 2022. Chi-square tests showed significant differences between the two groups in all five dimensions: research purpose, measurement channel, research subject, learning environment, and subject domain. The Affective group more often defined explicit learners in real classrooms, whereas the Emotion group more often left the research subject and learning environment unspecified and had a higher proportion of identification/diagnosis studies. In both groups, evaluating the impact of existing tools was the main research purpose, and questionnaire-based self-report was the most common measurement method. This study proposes the “Dual Knowledge Production Framework of Affective and Emotion AI Research,” reinterpreting the existing literature as systematic differences between two research orientations in research subjects and contexts, as a reference for future literature-search strategies and interdisciplinary research design.

title: THE IMPACT OF DIGITAL BANKING AND ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE ON PRIVATE BANKING IN SWITZERLAND: ARE CHANGES AHEAD?
container-title: Baltic Journal of Economic Studies
fbee2638caf8a4913086b40b3e787ce2544b774d.abstract: Subject of Research. This study focuses on the digital banking landscape and the integration of artificial intelligence (AI) in private banking and wealth management in Switzerland. More specifically, it examines how technological innovations – ranging from process automation and generative AI to advanced data analytics – alter the operational dynamics, customer relations, and structural competitiveness of Swiss private banks in the context of shifting client expectations and rigorous regulatory environments. Methodology. The research employs a qualitative analytical research design that uses triangulation of secondary evidence. It systematically integrates and cross-checks academic literature on digital finance, fintech adoption and robo-advisory trust, alongside empirical data, regulatory frameworks and market insights from reputable Swiss and international organisations. The primary data sources analysed were supervisory guides from the Swiss Financial Market Supervisory Authority (FINMA), reports from the Swiss Bankers Association, digital maturity benchmarks from Deloitte Switzerland and private banking market profitability assessments from KPMG and PwC Switzerland. Purpose. The main objective of this paper is to provide a comprehensive assessment of the impact of digital transformation and the deployment of AI on the traditional Swiss private banking model. By analysing seven key dimensions – technological progress, customer expectations, process optimization, data analytics, risk and security, regulation/compliance, and market trajectories – the study aims to clarify the economic mechanisms driving digital adaptation, identify the structural barriers preventing rapid technology adoption, and evaluate the strategic options available to Swiss banks facing intense global competition and margin compression. Findings and Conclusion. The study reveals a significant discrepancy between Switzerland's position as a global leader in asset management, with CHF 9.3 trillion under management, and its digital banking maturity score of 39 out of 60. Although private banking clients continue to establish relationships based on traditional factors such as reputation, trust and personal referrals, they are also demanding friction-free digital execution, personalised dashboards and virtual investment simulations. AI has been proven to have high economic value when acting as a productivity layer centred around advisors, optimising processes such as client onboarding, document extraction, compliance screening and portfolio monitoring. However, it is not as effective when acting as an autonomous replacement for human relationship managers. Ultimately, the integration of digital banking and AI is causing a clear market polarisation. Large-scale institutions are successfully absorbing the substantial fixed costs associated with technology, data governance and regulatory compliance under the frameworks of FINMA and the European Union (such as DORA and the EU AI Act). Conversely, smaller Swiss private banks are under severe pressure to increase their profitability and consolidate, unless they adopt highly focused niche advisory models. The paper therefore concludes that urgent regulatory attention and strategic repositioning are necessary to preserve the overall image and international attractiveness of the Swiss private banking ecosystem.

title: Visualizing use of generative artificial intelligence in higher education
container-title: Learning Futures and Emerging Technologies
3b755c7cb97fbc9e2515fdb87c420fac40b3db35.abstract: Purpose Higher education students are engaged with academic learning and research using generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) applications. A major shift in pedagogical approach surfaces many challenges to academic integrity that urging to redefining assessment model and ethical literacy. This study aims to investigate impact of the GenAI apps among the students using survey of technical and non-technical disciplines. Survey is mainly focused on: use of GenAI apps, variations in observed effectiveness and student’s usage pattern, level of adoption and acceptance of GenAI apps. Reviews of existing literature on the implications of GenAI and emerging need for systemic changes are discussed with reference to result. Design/methodology/approach Survey was developed to assess the integration of GenAI apps in the higher education. It was conducted with undergraduate and postgraduate students so as to find the adoption and acceptance rate of GenAI apps among the students; it has been partitioned into two categories: non-technical disciplines and technical disciplines. Students from the social science and pure sciences are in the non-technical disciplines, while students from computer science and engineering students are in the technical discipline. The questionnaire included a mix of multiple-choice questions, scale items and open-ended responses. Findings This research is classified for students into technical and non-technical disciplines, revealing notable differences in adoption patterns. First, students from non-technical disciplines are not entirely using GenAI applications. Second, effectiveness of the usage can be analyzed by the purpose of usage of GenAI apps which is shown by graphs. However, technical students show higher inclination for AI usages. Third, regarding adoption or acceptance, many rural students initially adopt it through classmates or roommates. In contrast, students in urban areas, especially in technical disciplines, spend higher hours; here, they accept the technology and update themselves with new technology. Research limitations/implications The survey did not assess the accuracy or effectiveness of GenAI outputs. This is a limitation for drawing conclusions about the performance quality of these apps across disciplines. Originality/value Students come from different parts of India, so it is also possible that the places where they previously studied lacked facilities such as internet connectivity and stable power supply. This influences the usage. Students from many disciplines participated in the survey, so their perspective to look at the GenAI apps is a unique feature. GenAI apps are accepted among technical students, and non-technical students are gradually adopting. Over-reliance may hinder the individual learning and creativity; it can be an aid to the learning but not as a supplement of human intelligence. Universities face challenges in formulating policies.

title: Advances on triply periodic hyperbolic surface structures: from biological inspiration to artificial self-assembly
container-title: Micro Nano Science
67034a036dc26f4c7bf546a12608936220fab5aa.abstract: Triply periodic hyperbolic surfaces (TPHSs) are a class of complex structures that extend periodically throughout three-dimensional space and possess smooth surfaces with non-positive Gaussian curvature. They appear in a wide range of natural systems, from cellular membranes to butterfly wing scales and beetle exoskeletons. Owing to their unique geometries and extraordinary properties, TPHSs have attracted extensive attention and research interest. Detailed structural characterizations of naturally occurring TPHSs have been performed, and a variety of artificial analogs have been fabricated by top-down physical methods and bottom-up chemical approaches. These efforts have deepened our understanding of TPHSs and broadened their application scope. This review discusses the progress on TPHSs in biological systems and their artificial synthesis, and it surveys current applications of these structures in fields such as photonics, energy storage and conversion, catalysis, sensing, thermal management and mechanical metamaterials. It thereby provides a new framework linking biological structures to artificial structures. Finally, this review concludes by outlining current challenges and proposing directions for future research.

title: From Adoption to Human-AI Leadership: A Scoping Review of Artificial Intelligence in Educational Leadership and Management
container-title: Social Scientific Centered Issues
1e0569103ec369b6f75ff1186f587acf5a4f67a0.abstract: This scoping review maps how artificial intelligence is conceptualized and used in educational leadership and management and examines the transition from technology adoption toward human-AI leadership. Following established scoping-review guidance and PRISMA-ScR, records from Scopus, Web of Science, and PubMed published or officially available online from 2022 to the final search date in 2026 were screened; items assigned a 2027 bibliographic year were eligible only if already available online before the cutoff. Of 747 records identified, 183 duplicates were removed and 323 records underwent title-and-abstract screening. Full texts were sought for 81 reports; two could not be retrieved, 79 were assessed for eligibility, and 50 studies were included. Four themes emerged: leadership readiness and capability; AI-augmented leadership practice; organizational conditions and institutional transformation; and human-AI agency, governance, and ethical boundaries. The evidence favors augmentation rather than autonomous substitution, with human judgment remaining central to accountability. The review proposes a five-stage Human-AI Educational Leadership Continuum integrating individual capability, organizational readiness, governance, and decision authority. The review was limited to three databases and English-language articles, and the evidence base remains methodologically heterogeneous and largely cross-sectional or context-specific.

title: Single-sensor acoustic emission source localization in blade local region based on an interpretable wavelet attention network
container-title: Structural Health Monitoring
ede9793d57cf20866e46b892aa7f92f49bbf6016.abstract: Acoustic emission (AE) technology is suitable for monitoring wind turbine blades because of its high-frequency response and sensitivity. However, existing damage localization approaches rely on multi-sensor arrays, which limit their engineering applicability. Moreover, deep learning models for single-sensor localization remain constrained by insufficient time-frequency representation and limited interpretability. To address these issues, a novel single-sensor AE source localization model, the Large-kernel dual wavelet attention network, was proposed. First, pencil lead break tests on real blade structures were conducted to investigate AE signal propagation, revealing strong nonlinear behavior and multi-scale attenuation characteristics. On this basis, a Large-kernel dual wavelet convolution layer was developed using Morlet and Mexican hat wavelets. With a mechanism-guided large wavelet kernel design, the arbitrariness in hyperparameter selection and the Gibbs phenomenon associated with incomplete truncation were mitigated, enabling the effective extraction of multi-scale time-frequency features. A time-grouped frequency attention mechanism module was introduced to adaptively recalibrate convolutional kernel weights through the fine-grained perception of localized time-frequency features, thereby improving the discrimination of critical features. Experiments on a real blade specimen demonstrated that the proposed method outperformed existing models in localization accuracy, achieving a minimum mean distance error of 20.29 mm. Furthermore, the model exhibited advantages in terms of feature interpretability and noise robustness. These results provide a promising and interpretable framework, laying the foundation for single-sensor damage localization in structural health monitoring of wind turbine blades.

title: Artificial Intelligence in Acute Stroke: Applications and Implications for the Portuguese National Healthcare System
container-title: Acta Médica Portuguesa
2a3eada78cd04ede50ea25d68e1ab6ed1357e21b.abstract: Introduction: Acute stroke is a leading cause of death and long-term disability in Portugal. Rapid and accurate imaging is critical to guide acute stroke management, and artificial intelligence has shown growing potential to support triage, quantification, and therapeutic decision-making. This study aimed to characterize the current use of artificial intelligence in acute stroke imaging workflow in Portuguese public hospital neuroradiology departments, and to identify perceived benefits, implementation barriers and prospects.Methods: A descriptive, cross-sectional study was conducted using an online questionnaire distributed between January and April 2026 to neuroradiology departments of Portuguese public hospitals with stroke intervention units. The questionnaire covered department characterization, current use of artificial intelligence, and perceptions regarding future applications. Responses were analyzed descriptively.Results: Ten hospitals from the North, Centre, Lisbon Metropolitan Area, South and insular regions were included. All operated under a stroke code protocol, used computed tomography as the first-line modality, and provided 24-hour neuroradiology coverage through a combined on-site and teleradiology model. Only two hospitals used dedicated artificial intelligence software, and one was in an implementation phase. Three additional centers used computational tools with artificial intelligence functionalities without identifying them as such. Prior contact with artificial intelligence was reported by 80% of respondents, and all anticipated its integration into routine practice. The most frequently cited applications were automated ASPECTS, core/penumbra quantification, large vessel occlusion identification and hemorrhage detection. Faster time-to-treatment and support for teleradiology workflows were the most perceived benefits. Opinions on funding were divided between the hospital institution and the state. Formal staff training was reported only by one center.Conclusion: Despite high awareness and a well-established organizational framework, adoption of artificial intelligence remains limited. Coordinated procurement strategies, structured training programs and shared operational definitions of artificial intelligence are needed to enable broader and more equitable integration into stroke care.

title: Artificial Intelligence, Auditor Trust, and Fraud Detection in FinTech Audits: Evidence from Iraq
container-title: Asian Journal of Economics, Business and Accounting
de1ee708fc5b6d618614b590374a9545b9846011.abstract: FinTech has shifted financial activity towards platforms that generate high-volume, high-velocity transaction data, creating new opportunities for fraud. This study examines the association between AI-enabled auditing and auditors' perceived fraud-detection effectiveness in FinTech environments, and whether this association varies with auditors' trust in AI tools. Drawing on trust-in-automation and technology acceptance research, we surveyed 214 auditors engaged with Iraqi banks and licensed electronic payment providers and tested the hypotheses using partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM) with bootstrapped moderation analysis. The results show a positive association between AI-enabled auditing and perceived fraud-detection effectiveness. Auditor trust in AI has no statistically significant direct association with detection effectiveness, but it positively moderates the association between AI-enabled auditing and fraud detection: the estimated association is approximately 2.6 times stronger among high-trust auditors than among low-trust auditors. Trust therefore appears to act as a moderating condition rather than an independent predictor of perceived detection effectiveness. The study extends the discussion of audit technology beyond adoption to consider how trust conditions its perceived effectiveness. It also provides evidence from an emerging FinTech market in which research remains limited. For regulators, audit firms and FinTech supervisors, the findings suggest the importance of calibrated rather than uncritical trust in AI, supported by explainable tools, targeted training and clear guidance on AI-generated audit evidence.

title: Realization and analysis of Artificial Intelligence appearance in Agricultural system
container-title: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
e7bd5e00c3a9e74090e7ff26b418fc962b8551f0.abstract: Agriculture is increasingly expected to produce more food while minimizing the usage of water, chemical-based fertilizers, energy, chemicals, and labor. Agricultural decision-making is further complicated by climate unpredictability, soil degradation, shortages of water, crop illnesses, pests, weeds, and yield uncertainties. An IEEE-style review and implementation methodology for AI in agriculture is presented in this research. Examined are a number of important applications, including as crop recommendations, crop-yield estimation, disease and pest recognition, weed identification, soil and nutrient administration, smart irrigating, weather forecasting, livestock monitoring, agricultural robots, and post-harvest management. A multilayer AI-enabled farming system is proposed in which a conventional sensor, image processing, and historical information are acquired through IoT, UAV, satellites, and field devices; processed information is provided to machine-learning(ML)/deep-learning models; and the ensuing decisions are transmitted to farmers or automated actuators. Conventional models such as Decision Tree(DT), Random Forest, K-Nearest Neighbor(KNN), Support Vector Machine(SVM), and Artificial Neural Network(ANN) are contrasted conceptually with CNN, LSTM, and Transformer-based techniques.Substantial research gaps in dataset variety, model generalization and explanation, efficiency of computation, cybersecurity, field validation,, and cost for small-scale farmers are also identified in the report. For sustainable intelligent agriculture, a future research path based on explainable AI, edge intelligence, hybrid AI, and multimodal data fusion is suggested.

title: AI-Powered Global Expansion: The Impact of Artificial Intelligence Adoption on Firms’ Outward Foreign Direct Investment
container-title: Journal of Academic Research and Advances
637d8e42c2f43232a8a9f9a4df0bdbd08128534a.abstract: Against the backdrop of profound shifts in the global economic landscape and rapid advances in digital technologies, artificial intelligence (AI) offers firms new opportunities to expand into international markets and improve the allocation of resources across borders. Drawing on a sample of Chinese A-share listed firms from 2009 to 2024, this study empirically examines the relationship between AI adoption and outward foreign direct investment (OFDI), with particular attention to the mechanisms underlying this relationship. The findings indicate that AI adoption is positively and significantly associated with firms’ OFDI activities. This result remains robust across a range of alternative specifications, including different measures of AI adoption, adjustments to fixed effects and standard-error clustering, and the exclusion of selected observations. Heterogeneity analyses suggest that the positive relationship is more pronounced among technology-intensive firms and larger enterprises. Further analysis identifies two potential channels through which AI adoption may facilitate OFDI: technological innovation and the alleviation of financial constraints. Together, these mechanisms may strengthen firms’ technological capabilities and improve their access to the financial resources required for international expansion. By examining OFDI through the lens of firm-level AI adoption, this study extends the literature on the determinants of international investment and provides further insight into how AI may shape firms’ internationalization strategies. The findings also offer empirical evidence relevant to the integration of AI into the real economy, the enhancement of firms’ international competitiveness, and China’s efforts to pursue higher-standard economic opening-up.

title: Controversies in Zero-Shot Forecasting with Time Series Foundation Models and a Three-Layer Framework for Trustworthy Evaluation
container-title: Computers and Artificial Intelligence
70e66cb1b102e478c16880234a262380523576f3.abstract: Time series foundation models (TSFMs) aim to forecast new datasets without target-specific parameter updates. Assessing this capability requires scrutiny of how evaluation evidence is generated and interpreted. We present a semi-systematic review of 80 core papers on the evaluation of TSFMs and large language model (LLM)-based forecasting methods. The review comprises 68 papers from the initial search and 12 from a targeted supplementary search within the same January 2022 to August 2026 publication window. We organize the evidence around benchmark integrity, ranking robustness, and domain transferability. In the reviewed literature, empirical audits of overlap between TSFM pretraining corpora and test benchmarks remain limited. Protocol choices, including normalization, forecast horizons, information availability, and metric aggregation, can alter model comparisons. Domain studies report both competitive performance and limitations, depending on task formulation, the relevance of pretraining data, sampling granularity, and data quality. These findings warrant conditional interpretations of zero-shot results rather than general claims of success or failure. We propose a five-part checklist for trustworthy evaluation and identify research priorities in corpus auditing, statistical comparison, domain-specific calibration, broader empirical coverage, and model selection. Reliable deployment requires evidence relevant to the intended task and operating conditions.
