title: Construction and Case Study of a Quality Evaluation Model for Intelligent Information Systems in a Generative Artificial Intelligence Environment: The Case of Bilibili
container-title: Computers and Artificial Intelligence
ae0c9b8f351889f3b45fc54a1fff53fb8eabc8be.abstract: After generative artificial intelligence (AI) was embedded in search, content generation, and user interaction, traditional information system quality evaluation faced new boundaries. Based on the DeLone and McLean (D&M) Information Systems Success Model, this study adopts literature research and a single-case study, takes Bilibili as the case, and constructs and applies a six-dimensional evaluation framework based on public materials, observations of platform functions, and publicly available user feedback. The findings show that system quality, information quality, and service quality can still explain basic platform operation, information output, and service support, but they cannot fully cover AI’s semantic understanding and task completion, the trustworthiness of generated results, and continuous human-computer interaction. Therefore, this study introduces AI intelligence quality, trustworthiness quality, and interaction quality on the basis of the three traditional dimensions and clarifies the boundary of each dimension. The Bilibili case shows that the framework can identify both basic capabilities and AI-specific quality, thereby helping to avoid conflating technical performance, content quality, intelligent capability, and trust issues. The study provides a structured analytical framework for evaluating the quality of intelligent information systems in a generative AI environment and a reference for platforms to optimize AI functions and governance mechanisms.

title: Research Evolution and Hotspot Detection of AIGC-Empowered Education in China, 2022–2025
container-title: Computers and Artificial Intelligence
7f01b19580053c1ec77fc5f72de4f2745f91e1f7.abstract: With the breakthrough advancement of Generative Artificial Intelligence (AIGC) technology, its integration into education has become a central issue in the global digital transformation of education. To systematically reveal the research status, hotspots, and evolutionary trends in the field of AIGC-empowered education in China, this study draws on the Web of Science (WoS) Core Collection. It combines bibliometric and content analyses to examine 1,505 English-language journal articles published by Chinese scholars between 2022 and 2025. The bibliometric results show that publication output in this field has grown explosively since 2022, forming a research landscape centered on highly cited educational-technology journals and characterized by multidisciplinary integration; research hotspots are concentrated on themes such as the educational applications of large language models, instructional innovation, learning outcomes, educational ethics, and intelligent tutoring systems; and the field's development has proceeded through three stages—technology introduction, application exploration, and deep integration—with the research frontier now shifting toward personalized learning, smart-education ecosystems, and digital transformation.

title: The Effect of Circular Economy Practices on Sustainable Tourism Development Among Tourism and Hospitality Enterprises Around Simien Mountains National Park in Ethiopia
e4ea2678b7ddf28f672d98dd70ee2cb374d466e0.abstract: Abstract Circular economy practices have become increasingly important for promoting sustainable tourism by reducing resource consumption, minimizing waste, strengthening local resource use, and encouraging innovative tourism products and services. However, tourism and hospitality enterprises in developing destinations often face challenges in adopting circular practices due to limited infrastructure, financial resources, technical capacity, and institutional support. This study examined the relationship between circular economy practices and sustainable tourism development among tourism and hospitality enterprises around Simien Mountains National Park, Ethiopia. A cross-sectional research design was employed, and data were collected from tourism and hospitality enterprises using a structured questionnaire. A total of 305 usable questionnaires were analyzed using descriptive statistics and multiple linear regression analysis. The study examined six dimensions of circular economy practices: resource reduction and efficiency, reuse practices, recycling and waste recovery, sustainable procurement, renewable energy and resource conservation, and circular product and service innovation. The findings revealed that the overall regression model was statistically significant, F(6, 298) = 68.236, p < .001, with the six circular economy practices jointly explaining 57.9% of the variation in sustainable tourism development. Circular product and service innovation (β = .552, p < .001), sustainable procurement (β = .303, p < .001), reuse practices (β = .261, p < .001), and resource reduction and efficiency (β = .102, p = .041) were positively and significantly associated with sustainable tourism development. In contrast, recycling and waste recovery (β = −.143, p = .032) and renewable energy and resource conservation (β = −.238, p = .001) showed statistically significant negative associations within the fitted model. These findings suggest that circular economy practices are important predictors of sustainable tourism development, although their relationships differ across dimensions and may reflect contextual implementation conditions. The study provides practical implications for tourism and hospitality enterprises, local government, park authorities, and other stakeholders to strengthen circular product and service innovation, sustainable procurement, resource efficiency, reuse systems, recycling infrastructure, and renewable-energy initiatives. The findings can contribute to the development of more resource-efficient, environmentally responsible, economically viable, and resilient tourism practices around Simien Mountains National Park..

title: The Transmission Mechanism Through Which the Platform Economy Promotes Integrated Urban-Rural Development—Based on the Meituan Platform in Yanyuan County, Sichuan
container-title: Environment, Social and Governance
979b7a69ba772d234eb67e01c4f267cc7b14453b.abstract: The urban-rural dual structure remains an issue in China’s development, and the platform economy offers possibilities for addressing it. Existing studies have mainly verified its role in promoting urban-rural integration, while the underlying transmission mechanism requires further examination. This study proposes a “four-element, three-stage transmission” framework that treats the platform economy as a composite actor of external driving forces and an internal capability system. Taking the Meituan platform in Yanyuan County, Sichuan, as a single case, the study examines how the platform economy promotes urban-rural integration. The findings show that the platform economy is not a simple empowerment tool but a “three-in-one” system comprising technological infrastructure, a capability system, and operational rules, all of which are indispensable. Platform expansion results from policy guidance, capital pressure, and platform capabilities, whereas urban-rural integration is the objective outcome of the transmission chain rather than an expression of platform intent. Platform expansion is also not one-way technological implantation. Algorithms and rules must be adapted and “translated” to local sociocultural conditions, and local elites play an irreplaceable coordinating role. This study integrates fragmented mechanism pathways into a coherent transmission sequence and provides a new theoretical perspective on the platform economy and urban-rural integration.

title: Implementation Challenges of Artificial Intelligence-Empowered Project-Based Learning in Compulsory Education
container-title: Journal of Language, Culture and Education
9528dc8f306ff8c3fc5267c18f89fec4d4a030b8.abstract: With the rapid development of generative artificial intelligence, new possibilities have emerged for addressing problems in project-based learning at the compulsory education stage, such as insufficient teacher guidance resources and inadequate personalized support for students. Based on literature research, this paper analyzes the implementation challenges faced by artificial intelligence-empowered project-based learning from the dual perspectives of teachers and students. The study finds that, at the teacher level, there are three types of problems: superficial AI application, generalized technology embedding, and fragmented instructional design. At the student level, there are difficulties such as the substitution of the inquiry process, interference with learning engagement, and compression of the space for collaborative construction. In response to these problems, this paper proposes optimization strategies, including promoting subject-differentiated technical support, designing structured collaborative learning sheets, improving the formative evaluation system, and enhancing teachers’ AI literacy, with a view to providing references for the deep integration of artificial intelligence and project-based learning in compulsory education.

title: Understanding the Pattern of Cognitive Decline in GBA1 ‐Related Parkinson's Disease: An Exploratory Longitudinal Multi‐Cohort Study
container-title: Annals of Neurology
8f39665691e6b88120e2dafbc26116e179cad79b.abstract: Objective People with Parkinson's disease (PD) who carry a pathogenic GBA1 variant (PD GBA1 ) are at higher risk of cognitive impairment than those without the variant (PD GBA1_wildtype ). To date, little is known about the pattern and evolution of cognitive decline in PD GBA1 . This multicenter study characterized the cognitive profile of PD GBA , focusing on the longitudinal trajectories and the group‐specific onset times among cognitive functions, as well as their clinical relevance. Methods In this exploratory longitudinal multicohort‐study (Parkinson's Precision Medicine Initiative [PPMI], Amyloid‐Beta in cerebrospinal spinal fluid as a risk factor for cognitive dysfunction in Parkinson's Disease [ABC‐PD], and National Centre for Excellence in Research on Parkinson's disease [NCER‐PD]), comprehensive neuropsychological assessments were standardized across 546 healthy controls (follow‐up years = 2.9 ± 4.3), 903 PD GBA1_wildtype (follow‐up years = 4.4 ± 4.2), and 211 PD GBA1 (follow‐up years = 4.8 ± 3.4). We evaluated performance across age and disease duration using generalized linear mixed effects models (GLMMs) within each cognitive domain. An exploratory latent trajectory analysis was computed to identify potential cognitive subgroups. Time‐to‐first‐event models, assessing risks of clinically relevant performance impairment (test score z ≤ −1.5, Montreal Cognitive Assessment [MoCA] < 26), and an expanding time‐window approach identified the course of cognitive impairment. Results PD GBA1 performed worse in executive function, attention, visuocognitive skills, and memory than PD GBA1_wildtype at baseline and exhibited a more rapid and widespread decline across these domains. The risk of developing clinically relevant cognitive impairment during the disease course was increased in PD GBA1 . Processing speed and visuoperceptual showed the earliest performance impairments in PD GBA1 , preceding PD GBA1_wildtype by 1.2 and 2.5 disease years, respectively. Within the PD GBA1 group, we identified a subgroup with rapidly declining cognition, who were more likely to be male patients, report depressive symptoms, and carry a severe GBA1 mutation. Interpretation PD GBA1 exhibits accelerated domain‐generalized and more severe cognitive decline compared to PD GBA1_wildtype . ANN NEUROL 2026

title: When Is Something Alive? Integrating Bottom-Up and Top-Down Perspectives on Aliveness
container-title: Journal of Artificial Intelligence and Consciousness
76ca802569b2f2b00a5220af8d5f5cb05960cc03.abstract: What it means for an individual entity to be alive remains conceptually unresolved, particularly for artificial systems that display increasingly life-like behavior. This paper distinguishes life as an evolutionary, population-level process from aliveness as an individual property, and develops a candidate condition for assessing when an entity, biological or artificial, should be considered alive. A bottom-up heuristic identifies structural and functional characteristics commonly associated with biological organisms, but applying this heuristic to an embodied artificial agent shows that such characteristics are not by themselves sufficiently discriminative. A complementary top-down perspective introduces self-referential regulation, understood as the capacity of an entity to internally represent and regulate its own continued existence through embodied causal processes. Integrating both perspectives yields a unified candidate condition for aliveness, proposed primarily for complex entities while leaving open how aliveness should be characterized in simpler ones.

title: Former versus current smoking among older adults living with Alzheimer's disease, related dementias, and cognitive impairment
container-title: Journal of Alzheimer’s Disease
d4f5985c1784cabacf8eca2e1d79b729df2bab5e.abstract: Smoking is a major modifiable risk factor for Alzheimer's disease and related dementias (ADRD), yet smoking status among older adults with ADRD or cognitive impairment, not dementia (CIND), remains poorly characterized. Using pooled 2010–2020 Health and Retirement Study data, we examined former versus current smoking among US adults aged ≥55 years with lifetime cigarette smoking. In weighted analyses of 13,595 participants, adults with CIND (AOR = 0.83, 95% CI: 0.74, 0.92) and ADRD (AOR = 0.80, 95% CI: 0.65, 0.99) had lower odds of former smoking than cognitively normal adults. Findings highlight the importance of understanding smoking cessation needs in cognitively impaired populations.

title: Artificial intelligence and the erosion of professional autonomy in clinical practice – a review and analysis
container-title: Clinical Ethics
0136a3db45cd1609e9bfcd4524d53476f9ee0b63.abstract: Professional autonomy is a foundational ethical principle in healthcare, underpinning healthcare professionals’ capacity to exercise independent clinical judgement in light of a patient's particular circumstances, preferences and needs. While ethical debate surrounding medical AI has focused extensively on safety, accuracy and bias, its implications for professional autonomy have received comparatively less attention, a notable omission given AI's growing role in shaping clinical decision-making. This article identifies three salient mechanisms through which AI integration may constrain professional autonomy: (1) algorithmic opacity and explainability, (2) automation bias and de-skilling and (3) institutional pressures. Whilst proposed safeguards such as explainable AI, professional training, system design and institutional governance represent important directions, they do not yet adequately protect professional autonomy. This article therefore calls for closer scrutiny of current approaches to AI integration and for governance frameworks that attend not only to the technical properties of AI systems, but to the organisational and institutional conditions in which they are deployed.

title: A maximum power point tracking control system leveraging artificial neural network for photovoltaic systems based on a Raspberry Pi embedded under various weather conditions
container-title: Electrical Engineering & Electromechanics
f75ca7a2819756cca5e87d2515da8fbbeda84d7e.abstract: Introduction. Maximum power point tracking (MPPT) is essential for maximizing the energy harvested from photovoltaic (PV) modules, especially under fast irradiance and temperature variations. Problem. Conventional MPPT methods like perturb and observe and incremental conductance suffer from slow convergence, steady-state oscillations, and reduced tracking accuracy when operating under fast and unpredictable environmental variations. Goal. To develop a fast, accurate, and robust MPPT strategy capable of improving power extraction efficiency and reducing power fluctuations under realistic and dynamic meteorological conditions. Methodology. This paper proposes an artificial neural network (ANN)-based MPPT scheme that uses two estimated reference inputs – reference current (Iref) and reference voltage (Vref) to directly update the duty cycle of a DC-DC boost converter. The algorithm is designed using LabVIEW for supervision and co-simulation and is implemented in real time on a Raspberry Pi 4 using Python to control the converter switch. Experimental validation is carried out using a laboratory prototype with measured meteorological data. Results. Experimental results show that the proposed ANN-based MPPT achieves superior performance compared to fuzzy logic control and particle swarm optimization techniques. The system reaches MPPT efficiencies of up to 99.5 %, exhibits faster transient response, and significantly reduces power oscillations around the MPP. Scientific novelty. The novelty of this work lies in the direct duty-cycle control using ANN with dual reference inputs (Iref and Vref), combined with real-time deployment on a low-cost embedded Raspberry Pi platform, bridging the gap between data-driven MPPT algorithms and practical hardware implementation. Practical value. The findings demonstrate that low-cost embedded platforms can deliver accurate and robust MPPT performance for PV energy conversion under realistic weather conditions, and confirm the efficacy of the recommended Raspberry Pi system, which is programmed with the proposed data-driven ANN-MPPT, in optimizing the power output from the panel across varying meteorological conditions. References 20, tables 4, figures 11.

title: From prediction to execution: a narrative review of artificial intelligence tactical models in badminton, player physiology and coaching use
container-title: Frontiers in Physiology
846ac884d08db9f6a6740d85200f39dad5588b9d.abstract: Machine learning models predict badminton strokes, but the practical value of tactical recommendations depends on whether players can execute them. Player capacity can change within matches and across successive tournament matches. Based on structured searches of eight bibliographic sources, this narrative review synthesizes tactical modelling and badminton physiology to examine the evidence needed for executable recommendations and coaching use. We distinguish five types of claim (description, prediction, prescription, adoption and outcome), each requiring a different form of validation. Most tactical studies focus on prediction or the development of coach-facing interfaces. Amongst tactical studies with assessable inputs, 30% included match-context variables, such as score, but no explicit measure of player state. Very few used explicit physiological variables, and none reported fitting or validating models using measured player state during match play. Beyond developer-led evaluations, our search identified no study in which practitioners received model-derived recommendations and an outcome was recorded. Physiological studies document metabolic demand, neuromuscular fatigue, perceptual changes under load and cumulative effects across successive matches. Several report maintained performance, so whether fatigue alters feasible or optimal tactics remains a testable hypothesis. We distinguish candidate inputs for use during play, principally video-derived estimates of player-specific movement load, from variables suited to research and post-match monitoring. We also propose a reporting checklist separating information studies can report now from requirements that need new data. This framework specifies the evidence needed to evaluate whether recommendations are executable, whether coaches adopt them and whether measurable outcomes follow.

title: Redundant attention fails to replicate as sustained engagement: Information quality in early review cohorts and long‐run popularity of books
container-title: Journal of the Association for Information Science and Technology
29df535d6eda70428b375dc2ca2def53f85d92de.abstract: Abstract Early reviews on social reading platforms are an important clue for book buyers. However, research has so far focused on their volume and average rating rather than their informational content. To address this gap, we scraped nearly one million reviews of 25,000 books across five genres from lubimyczytac.pl, Poland's largest social reading platform. We modeled the long‐run accumulation of reviews attracted after a book's 30‐day initial launch window. Conditional on early review volume and book characteristics, reviews with greater semantic similarity and stronger solicitation cues predict less subsequent engagement. In contrast, early reviews with more linguistic perplexity and more diverse reviewer portfolios predict more engagement in the future. Furthermore, a text sentiment classifier we fine‐tuned to this specific domain added predictive signal beyond the raw star ratings, consistent with ratings being a coarsely discretized projection of the evaluative signal carried by review text. We frame these results within information quality theory: the informational profile of an early review cohort contributes to the prediction of sustained platform engagement beyond review volume and rating.

title: Chemical threat detection from open-source intelligence using a large language model: a zero-shot feasibility evaluation, with radiological assessment precluded by data sparsity
container-title: International Journal of Data Science and Analytics
15ecccb8e6b6a354beb90090d3bc437bf7252417.abstract: Abstract Timely detection of chemical and radiological incidents is crucial for public health surveillance; however, no global event-based surveillance system currently exists. Open-source intelligence (OSINT) and large language models (LLMs) present new opportunities for early detection; however, their application in these domains remains largely unexplored. This study evaluated GPT-4o’s performance for named entity recognition (NER) of chemical and radiological incidents from OSINT sources, assessing its potential to support global threat detection and early warning systems. Radiological entities were retained in the extraction schema throughout, but proved too sparse in the retrieved corpus to permit any evaluation of radiological performance; the evaluation reported here is therefore effectively confined to the chemical domain. A lexicon of 45 lay-accessible search terms, derived from 6646 technical chemical and radiological terms, was used to query the Bing News Application Programming Interface (API) from August 2024 to January 2025. Retrieved articles were scraped, translated when necessary, summarised by GPT-4o, and the summaries were and processed by GPT-4o using structured zero-shot prompts to extract entities, including event occurrences, substances, case numbers, fatalities, locations, and temporal features. Two annotators manually labelled a ground-truth dataset of 200 articles to evaluate performance using precision, recall, and F 1 Scores. Performance was compared against four baselines evaluated on the same corpus: a rule-based lexicon extractor, an off-the-shelf pretrained NER pipeline, a domain-pretrained biomedical NER model, and a supervised TF-IDF classifier. Of 37,618 retrieved articles, 8077 were parsed by GPT-4o. Event identification (F 1 = 0.96) and chemical substance recognition (F 1 = 0.94) were highly accurate. Geographic entities performed well at the state (F 1 = 0.98) and city (F 1 = 0.92) levels and remained strong at the country (F 1 = 0.93) and county (F 1 = 0.91) levels. Temporal (Date and Timeframe: F 1 = 0.74; Temporal expressions: F 1 = 0.81) and numerical extraction were moderate-to-strong (case numbers F 1 = 0.83; fatalities F 1 = 0.82). Only four positive radiological entity instances were identified within the annotated dataset, precluding meaningful evaluation of radiological extraction performance. Against a cross-validated supervised classifier, event identification improved from F 1 = 0.87 to F 1 = 0.96, and GPT-4o higher F 1 than the rule-based, pretrained NER, and domain-pretrained comparators across the entity types for which direct comparison was possible.Within the constraints of this limited evaluation, GPT-4o demonstrated feasibility for extracting several core public health entities from OSINT sources; however, while performance exceeded rule-based, pretrained-NER, and supervised classical baselines on a common corpus, comparison against transformer-based and fine-tuned biomedical NER architectures remains outstanding. Performance was weaker for Date and Timeframe precision. Radiological extraction could not be evaluated at all, because the corpus yielded too few positive radiological instances to support any performance estimate. This study, therefore, demonstrates chemical-domain feasibility under the conditions tested and documents radiological sparsity within this retrieval pipeline as a barrier to evaluation, rather than demonstrating radiological detection capability.

title: Artificial intelligence in pediatric head and neck tumor imaging: a mini review of current applications and future directions
container-title: Frontiers in Oncology
977551aefb2d9e60cf93a6c507b7d100c422a1bd.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is creating new opportunities to enhance medical imaging in pediatric oncology through quantitative image analysis and clinical decision support. This mini review examines the emerging role of AI in pediatric head and neck tumor imaging, including applications in lesion detection and characterization, tumor segmentation and volumetric analysis, treatment planning, longitudinal surveillance, prognostication, and precision medicine. Particular attention is given to the challenges of translating these approaches to pediatric populations, where rare and heterogeneous tumors, limited datasets, variable imaging protocols, and insufficient multicenter validation remain important barriers. We also discuss emerging strategies that may facilitate clinical translation, including federated learning, multimodal data integration, explainable AI, and integration with existing radiology workflows. Although pediatric-specific evidence remains limited, continued multicenter collaboration and prospective validation may enable AI-based tools to provide more reproducible quantitative imaging assessment and increasingly personalized clinical decision support. Ultimately, the clinical value of these technologies will depend on their ability to augment radiologist expertise and improve patient care through responsible integration into routine practice.

title: DETERMINANTS OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE ADOPTION AMONG ACADEMIC AND NON-ACADEMIC STAFF OF AUCHI POLYTECHNIC, EDO STATE, NIGERIA
container-title: International Journal of African Innovation and Multidisciplinary Research
8d5e219fa57c4ff67651a119675249bb2d0558ef.abstract: This study examined the determinants of artificial intelligence (AI) adoption among academic and non-academic staff of Auchi Polytechnic, Edo State, Nigeria. Specifically, it investigated the relationships between perceived usefulness, AI literacy, institutional support and AI adoption. The study adopted a descriptive survey research design. The population comprised 3,150 academic and non-academic staff, from which a sample of 354 respondents was determined using the Taro Yamane formula. Data were collected through a structured questionnaire and analysed using descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation and multiple regression analysis with SPSS Version 26. The hypotheses were tested at the 5% level of significance. The descriptive results showed that perceived usefulness had a mean score of 4.18, AI literacy recorded 3.65, institutional support had 2.84, while AI adoption recorded 3.92. The multiple regression results indicated that perceived usefulness (β = 0.396, p < 0.001), AI literacy (β = 0.339, p < 0.001) and institutional support (β = 0.246, p < 0.001) had significant positive relationships with AI adoption. The overall regression model was statistically significant (F = 150.29, p < 0.001), with an R² of 0.545, indicating that the three explanatory variables jointly accounted for 54.5% of the variation in AI adoption. Perceived usefulness was the strongest predictor, followed by AI literacy and institutional support. The study concluded that AI adoption among staff of Auchi Polytechnic is associated with perceived work-related benefits, employees’ AI competencies and the availability of institutional resources and support. It recommended that the Polytechnic promote practical AI applications in academic and administrative activities, strengthen staff AI literacy through regular training, and improve digital infrastructure, technical assistance and institutional guidelines for responsible AI use.

title: Artificial intelligence in human resource management: A bibliometric analysis and literature mapping (2015–2025)
container-title: Problems and Perspectives in Management
84beea12ee0c7f96f38613f0e22b46b447068bc9.abstract: Type of the article: Research ArticleAbstractThe integration of artificial intelligence (AI) has profoundly transformed human resource management (HRM) from an administrative function into a strategic decision-making process, creating a critical need to balance algorithmic effectiveness with operational challenges. The purpose of this study is to explore the evolving integration of artificial intelligence within human resource management. This paper utilizes a bibliometric analysis using PRISMA reporting flow guidelines, analyzing data retrieved from the Scopus database for the period from 2015 to 2025. The results reveal an exponential expansion of scientific research over the decade. Out of an initial set of 2,949 publications, 622 relevant documents met the inclusion criteria and were analyzed using VOSviewer. Annual publications grew from nine articles in 2015 to 218 articles in 2025. The geographical distribution shows that India leads the field with 116 publications, followed by China (114) and the United States (98). Furthermore, the thematic mapping identifies nine distinct clusters, with AI and human resource management standing out as the primary domains experiencing transformation. The findings confirm that the field has become a consolidated, dynamic discipline, with strategic implications for organizations seeking to align technological efficiency with organizational justice, ethical considerations, and employee well-being.

title: Differences in Translators' Cognitive Load under Generative-AI Post-Editing: An Eye-Tracking Study of English-Chinese Scientific Texts
container-title: Future of Social Sciences
7c7fe2b629e6642e4941218c5d737a4c99000526.abstract: {'en': 'Generative artificial intelligence has entered the translation workflow faster than evidence about its effect on the translator has accumulated. This study asks whether working from a large language model draft lowers cognitive load or merely redistributes it. Thirty-six translators, twenty translation trainees and sixteen practising professionals, rendered nine English popular-science and technical passages into Chinese under three within-subject conditions. These were unaided human translation (HT), post-editing of a static neural machine translation draft (NMT-PE), and post-editing of a GPT-4o draft with an interactive prompt pane (GAI-PE). Pupil diameter change, fixation duration, gaze distribution, keystroke logs, NASA-TLX ratings and MQM scores were recorded. GAI-PE cut task time by 44.2 per cent against HT and by 17.1 per cent against NMT-PE. Its MQM scores were higher than those of NMT-PE, while the difference from HT did not reach significance. Pupil diameter change was nevertheless largest in GAI-PE at 0.095 mm, against 0.083 mm in HT and 0.064 mm in NMT-PE, while gaze on the source text fell to 38.3 per cent, the lowest of the three. Subjective ratings moved the other way and ranked HT as the most demanding condition. In an exploratory analysis, self-reported AI-use frequency was associated with a smaller pupil response in GAI-PE, whereas English proficiency showed no such association. These observations are consistent with an increased demand for verification, though the generative condition also gave access to an interactive prompt pane, so the differences cannot be attributed to the model alone.'}

title: Mapping multidimensional artificial intelligence anxiety among academic librarians in the United Arab Emirates: An exploratory survey
container-title: Journal of Information Science
3c01ea068af6fbf089f2134b3d74f524ade33ce0.abstract: This exploratory study examines artificial intelligence anxiety among academic librarians in the United Arab Emirates, a multilingual context undergoing rapid digital transformation. A cross-sectional online survey of 72 academic library professionals, recruited through purposive and snowball sampling, employed a newly developed 35-item instrument covering seven conceptually derived dimensions: job role evolution, ethical and bureaucratic concerns, patron resistance and social trust, governance and strategic alignment, infrastructure and digital divide, vendor and sustainability, and linguistic and cultural anxiety. Internal consistency ranged from acceptable to strong (α = 0.774–0.898). Overall, AI anxiety was moderate (M = 3.33 on a five-point scale), with ethical and bureaucratic concerns (M = 3.47), infrastructure and digital divide (M = 3.42), and vendor and sustainability concerns (M = 3.36) recording the highest means. However, the narrow range across construct means (0.23 points) warrants treating these differences as descriptive rather than substantive rankings. Concerns about storing patron data on foreign servers and shortages of skilled staff received the highest item-level ratings. Although women reported higher scores across all seven dimensions, no gender or other demographic differences remained statistically significant after correction for multiple comparisons. The findings highlight the institutional, infrastructural, ethical and governance conditions associated with AI anxiety in academic libraries. The proposed dimensions offer a context-specific framework for further investigation, subject to validation in larger samples. Practical implications include developing localized and multilingual AI tools, expanding inclusive professional development, and strengthening participatory governance of AI procurement and policy.

title: BIOLOGY TEACHERS’ READINESS AND ATTITUDES TOWARDS INTEGRATING ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN CONVENTIONAL TEACHING
container-title: Interdisciplinary Perspectives of Education
368bdcd532288d3efc2d5ea60c16449e3730bf7d.abstract: The fast-growing Artificial Intelligence has opened up the new possibilities for the improvement of the educational experience especially in the sciences. The successful integration of AI into traditional classrooms, to a great extent, depends on teachers’ readiness and attitudes toward its use. This quantitative study investigated the readiness and perceptions of biology teachers toward the use of artificial intelligence (AI) alongside traditional methods of teaching. This research employs a conceptual framework of AI readiness, concentrating on three essential aspects of teachers' preparedness: knowledge, skills, and attitude, as well as their correlations with various socio-demographic variables. A descriptive survey method was adopted and data were collected from 150 in-service Biology teachers (Botany & Zoology) of Uchch Madhyamik Vidyalaya of Darbhanga district of Bihar thru a standardized and pre-validated questionnaire. Statistical analysis was performed using descriptive statistics, Pearson’s correlation coefficient, independent samples t-tests and one-way ANOVA. Findings indicate that biology educators have a moderate level of knowledge and skills in using AI in the educational context and possess positive attitudes toward the use of AI in their teaching practices. There are large differences in teaching experience and availability of ICT resources for AI-readiness. These findings suggest that indeed occupational exposure and infrastructure assets are important. The results reveal a substantial difference between the positive attitudes of educators toward the use of AI and their actual preparedness for the integration of AI-enhanced instruction. Improved professional training of biology teachers, advances in ICT infrastructure and supportive policy frameworks will boost AI readiness. The results provide empirical evidence for the increasing discourse on the use of AI in education and discuss the implications for teacher education and training in terms of policy making.

title: QUALITY, EQUITY, AND AUTONOMY IN INDIAN HIGHER EDUCATION AFTER NEP 2020: A CRITICAL ASSESSMENT
container-title: Interdisciplinary Perspectives of Education
4e0d40f3ff2f376c2bb7231bc606708e77e61ca7.abstract: The National Education Policy of 2020 is often called the biggest shake-up of Indian higher education since 1986. It asks for a lot: multidisciplinary campuses in place of narrow single-subject colleges, credit-based movement between programmes, far more freedom for institutions to run themselves, and, at the same time, a real widening of access for groups who have historically been left out. This paper looks closely at three strands of that agenda - quality, equity, and institutional autonomy - using government reports, statutory documents, and the wider research literature as evidence. The argument is straightforward. NEP 2020's vision hangs together well on paper. Putting it into practice is another matter, given how unevenly resources and administrative capacity are spread across Indian states, and given inequalities that were there long before this policy existed. There is also a basic tension running through the reform: it wants institutions to be freer, yet the government still has to pay for most of what happens in this sector and still has to watch over it. What decides whether NEP 2020 succeeds, this paper suggests, will not be the elegance of the document itself but whether money, coordination between the Centre and the States, and careful, ground-level implementation actually follow.

title: EFFECTIVENESS AND PRACTICALITY OF LOCAL GOVERNMENT FISCAL AUTONOMY IN NIGERIA
container-title: International Journal of Humanities, Literature and Art Research
f079b76936887c216aef86709ab294da96e577ed.abstract: Local government is widely regarded as the level of government closest to the people and, therefore, a critical institution for grassroots development, service delivery and democratic participation in Nigeria. However, the effectiveness of local government administration has historically been constrained by inadequate financial resources, excessive dependence on statutory allocations and extensive control by state governments. This article examines the effectiveness and practicality of local government fiscal autonomy in Nigeria, with particular attention to the constitutional, institutional and practical challenges surrounding the financial independence of local governments. It evaluates whether granting local governments greater control over their statutory allocations and internally generated revenue can enhance accountability, service delivery, developmental outcomes and democratic governance at the grassroots level. The study adopts a doctrinal approach, examining relevant constitutional provisions, legislation, judicial decisions, governmental policies and scholarly literature on Nigerian federalism and local government administration. It argues that fiscal autonomy is both constitutionally desirable and practically necessary for meaningful local governance, but its success depends on complementary institutional reforms. These include transparent revenue-allocation mechanisms, strengthened internally generated revenue systems, effective financial controls, independent auditing, participatory budgeting and mechanisms for preventing corruption and political interference. The article further contends that fiscal autonomy without corresponding administrative capacity and accountability may merely transfer existing governance problems to the local level. It concludes that genuine local government fiscal autonomy is practicable in Nigeria if supported by constitutional safeguards, judicial enforcement, financial accountability and institutional capacity-building.

title: Artificial Intelligence and Digital Innovation in Smart Tourism Destination Management: An Integrative Review and the AI-SDM Framework
container-title: Inkubis : Jurnal Ekonomi dan Bisnis
b9b2afe723164bea6e7be350837363abda6c2fe3.abstract: Background: Artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming tourism destinations through personalized services, conversational and generative interfaces, predictive analytics, and data-driven decision-making. Yet technology adoption alone does not explain how destinations convert AI-generated information into coordinated managerial action. Objective: This study addresses that organizational problem through a conceptual integrative review of research on AI-enabled tourism services, smart destination management, destination governance, visitor experience, organizational capabilities, workforce readiness, and responsible data practices. Methods: The synthesis identifies four interconnected application domains: AI-driven personalization, conversational and generative visitor interaction, predictive visitor-flow analytics, and data-driven destination governance. These domains are abstracted into the AI-Enabled Smart Destination Management (AI-SDM) framework, which connects AI-Enabled Service Capability, Smart Destination Governance Capability, and Visitor Experience Outcomes. Results: Visitor and operational intelligence functions as the principal conversion input, while visitor-generated behavioral and experiential feedback supports subsequent organizational learning and AI adaptation. Workforce AI Readiness and Responsible Data Governance are positioned as enabling conditions. The framework contributes to destination-management theory by shifting attention from AI adoption toward the organizational capability required to sense relevant visitor information, interpret and coordinate responses, and responsibly convert intelligence into destination action and visitor value. It complements broad smart-tourism and emerging cognitive-destination architectures by specifying the organizational intelligence-to-action mechanism that links AI-enabled interactions with destination governance and learning. Conclusion: The paper concludes with propositions and an empirical research agenda for measurement development and validation.

title: Cognitive and Computational Mechanisms of Multi-Agent Task Allocation in Digital Environments
container-title: Zamonaviy dunyoda ilm-fan va texnologiya, Vol. 5, No. 32 (2026)
88311ab5879695c66cef064bee8f1ffe9c71873e.abstract: Digital environments transform multi-agent task allocation in terms of computational load, utility optimization, and allocation of attention. Based on distributed systems theory and reinforcement learning, this study will combine empirical evidence in artificial intelligence, software engineering, and information systems studies to determine the impact of digital stimuli (prompt complexity, resource constraints, and algorithmic task routing) on agent cognition and neural-inspired valuation processes. The paper constructs a conceptual Multi-Agent Task Allocation Model (MATAM) based on bounded rationality and multi-agent reinforcement learning theories using secondary data synthesis. The effects of computational overload, the activation of reward circuitry, and dynamic personalization in multi-agent environments are summarized in three integrative tables of documented empirical evidence. The results indicate that online agent frameworks reinforce decentralized processing, reward optimization, and dynamically restructure preference formation. The paper enriches software engineering theory because it incorporates computational and cognitive-inspired processes in adaptive multi-agent systems.

title: Winner or Loser? Opening to Export Markets and Gender‐Specific Labour Market Adjustments
container-title: The World Economy
156ef2dd802388d7e76f8931efcac7c96a7a99f0.abstract: ABSTRACT This paper examines the effects of a positive export shock on gender‐specific labour market outcomes using nationally representative household and firm‐level data from Vietnam. We exploit exogenous variation in provincial exposure to tariff reductions induced by the U.S.–Vietnam Bilateral Trade Agreement. We find that opening to export markets is associated with stronger wage growth for men than for women, widening the estimated gender wage gap, although we find little evidence of gender differences in working‐hour responses. Opening to export markets is also associated with workers' transitions out of unpaid family work and into formal employment. However, these responses do not differ significantly between women and men. By contrast, women are significantly more likely than men to transition into non‐manual occupations in provinces more exposed to U.S. tariff reductions. Moreover, a positive gender composition effect provides an additional channel through which trade shapes gender disparities. As complementary evidence, the firm‐level analysis shows stronger growth in female employment in trade‐exposed regions, while female workers are more concentrated in larger firms that experience lower wage growth. Our findings show that increased export market access can generate divergent effects along the employment and wage margins, helping reconcile conflicting results in the existing literature and highlighting the importance of heterogeneity in understanding the gendered consequences of global integration.

Artificial intelligence-driven governance threshold and sellers’ performance in cross-border e-commerce platforms
container-title: South African Journal of Economic and Management Sciences
664f73ae4926456ccdda8520bde27db844ed12f7.abstract: Background: Artificial intelligence (AI)-driven governance systems increasingly regulate seller decisions in cross-border e-commerce platforms. Mainstream research has treated AI-driven control intensity as a monotonically positive lever for platform coordination and seller outcomes. Aim: This study examines whether AI-driven governance intensity exhibits a non-linear performance boundary and identifies the mechanism under which governance expansion becomes counterproductive. Setting: The study was conducted among cross-border sellers on Amazon Global Selling, Alibaba International, and Shopee across China, Southeast Asia, and Eastern Europe. Method: Survey data from 207 cross-border sellers were analysed by using partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM) with 5000-resample bootstrapping. Nonlinearity was confirmed by using a dual-condition criterion and a one-sided monotonicity test. Results: An inverted-U relationship emerged between AI governance intensity and seller performance (b_linear = 0.28, p = 0.021; b_quadratic = −0.19, p = 0.038), with a performance-reversing threshold at x* = 4.16 (bias-corrected and accelerated [BCa] 95% confidence interval: [3.9, 4.5]). Excessive governance suppresses independent strategic learning (b = −0.34, p < 0.001), partially mediating the performance penalty (indirect = −0.16; direct = 0.14, p = 0.046). Market volatility amplifies the post-threshold effect (b = 0.19, p = 0.014), with 23% of sampled sellers in the substitution regime. Conclusion: Governance intensity must be calibrated relative to a structural threshold beyond which automation displaces the strategic-learning capability on which competitive performance depends. Contribution: This study contributes a regime-contingent threshold model showing that AI-driven governance intensity and seller performance follow an inverted-U relationship, with a performance-reversing threshold at x* = 4.16. Strategic-learning suppression is empirically confirmed as the erosion mechanism (partial mediation, indirect effect = −0.16), and market volatility amplifies the post-threshold penalty, grounded in dynamic capabilities theory and offering platform designers a calibration boundary rather than a general prescription.

title: Identification of Fracture-Related Acoustic Emission Signals in Mine-Site Monitoring Using Multi-Domain Features and a 1D-CNN with Local-Window Self-Attention
container-title: Applied Sciences
468361152740737b2ff83a8a56ab244e2affbe33.abstract: Acoustic emission (AE) monitoring captures transient elastic waves generated by rock fracturing. Reliable identification of fracture-related AE signals supports rock-mass damage monitoring and subsequent early-warning analysis of mining-induced geohazards. However, AE signals are often corrupted by operational noise, hindering accurate detection. To improve AE signal identification under complex field conditions, raw binary AE data from a mine site were parsed, segmented, and manually labeled, and a binary dataset of fracture-related AE signals and industrial noise was constructed. Seven time-domain statistical features and three frequency-band energy-ratio features were extracted from each segment and combined into a 10-dimensional multi-domain feature vector. A hybrid model integrating a 1D convolutional neural network (1D-CNN) with a local-window self-attention mechanism was developed. The proposed model was compared with eight models: a standalone 1D-CNN, a 1D-CNN with global self-attention, a BPNN, an SVM, logistic regression, k-nearest neighbors, random forest, and XGBoost. On an independent test set comprising 400 samples, the proposed model achieved mean accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score values of 96.75 ± 0.71%, 93.99 ± 1.20%, 99.90 ± 0.22%, and 96.85 ± 0.67%, respectively, across five repeated runs. It achieved the highest mean accuracy and F1-score among the nine models. Across five fixed feature permutations, recall remained stable, whereas precision, accuracy, and F1-score showed greater variation. These findings indicate the potential of the proposed model for front-end classification of fracture-related AE signals in mine-site monitoring.

title: BioExergoEconomics: A Unified Thermodynamic–Environmental Framework Integrating Exergy Analysis, Circular Economy, Life Cycle Assessment and Biological Resource Recovery
container-title: Biomass
5df44eb7438e1942555dc60843c1603664956622.abstract: The integration of thermodynamic efficiency, environmental mitigation, and circular resource recovery remains a fundamental challenge in the sustainability assessment of agro-industrial systems. Conventional methodologies—such as Exergoeconomics, Life Cycle Assessment (LCA), and Circular Economy (CE) indicators—typically operate in methodological isolation, limiting their ability to quantify trade-offs between energy-intensive biological recovery and environmental mitigation. To address this gap, this study proposes BioExergoEconomics, a novel unified framework that structurally integrates physical exergy analysis, Exergoeconomic cost allocation, carbon and water footprints, and biological resource recovery into a single F-P-R-I-B functional model. The principal contribution is the formulation of the BioExergoEconomics Index (BEC Index), a dimensionless metric that uniquely synthesizes exergy efficiency, circular resource recovery, biological recovery, carbon mitigation, water conservation, and economic performance. The framework is validated through a comparative case study of beef production (1 kg functional unit). Although biological processing increases electricity demand by 47.8%, this localized energy investment reduces upstream agricultural burdens, resulting in a 17.6% net reduction in energy and exergy demand, a 99.4% reduction in freshwater footprint, and a 51.1% decrease in carbon emissions. With a BEC Index of 0.55, the framework demonstrates that electrical exergy investments in biological nodes can drive systemic sustainability.

title: Effects of Cognitive Behavioral Interventions on Core Symptom Dimensions of Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder in Children and Adolescents: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
container-title: Brain Sciences
6a8f61df667a2aec7602c5e57ab62b23c88523ba.abstract: Background: Previous research on psychosocial interventions for children and adolescents with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) has primarily focused on overall symptom severity, with less attention to treatment effects across core symptom dimensions. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the effects of cognitive behavioral interventions on overall ADHD symptoms, inattention, and hyperactivity/impulsivity and explored the influence of intervention type, treatment duration, and weekly session frequency. Methods: PubMed, Web of Science Core Collection, Embase, and CENTRAL were searched from inception to 30 June 2026 for randomized controlled trials. Risk of bias was assessed using RoB 2. Effect sizes were calculated as Hedges’ g and pooled using random-effects models, with sensitivity and exploratory subgroup analyses conducted. The review was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261376097). Results: Ten randomized controlled trials involving 849 participants were included. Cognitive behavioral interventions significantly reduced overall ADHD symptoms (g = −0.389, 95% CI −0.773 to −0.005), inattention (g = −0.415, 95% CI −0.749 to −0.082), and hyperactivity/impulsivity (g = −0.366, 95% CI −0.658 to −0.075). Inattention showed the numerically largest pooled effect. Exploratory subgroup analyses showed numerical differences across intervention type, treatment duration, and weekly session frequency, but formal moderator tests found no statistically significant between-subgroup differences. Conclusions: These findings support the potential benefits of cognitive behavioral interventions for ADHD symptom management, with the most consistent results observed for inattention. Future randomized controlled trials should compare intervention components and treatment schedules while assessing actual treatment exposure, including home practice, to inform more targeted cognitive behavioral interventions.

title: Omni-Flex GraphFormer: Parallel Fusion of Local Graph Aggregation and Global Attention Across Image Resolutions
container-title: Information
486564d19a14112ee291281e74085d1c8c166091.abstract: Graph neural networks (GNNs) capture local image structure with few parameters, whereas Vision Transformers (ViTs) model global context at a higher computational cost. We propose the Omni-Flex GraphFormer, which applies a graph branch (OMNIVIG: max-relative aggregation over a fixed 3×3 pixel neighbourhood) and a Transformer branch (FLEXIVIT: global multi-head self-attention) in parallel and sums their outputs. Because each baseline is the hybrid with one branch removed, comparing the three models on eight datasets from 8×8 to 96×96 pixels, under equal training budgets and over three seeds, is a controlled branch ablation. Global attention is decisive: the hybrid exceeds OMNIVIG in test macro-F1 on every dataset and in all 24 runs, by 3.7 to 15.1 points (Wilcoxon test, p=0.0078). Against FLEXIVIT, the hybrid has the best mean F1 on six datasets and a 40–62% smaller seed-to-seed spread on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100, but the difference is not significant (p=0.38). The graph branch adds only 0.5–3.1% to the number of multiply–accumulate operations, and under warmed-up timing, both models run at the same speed, whereas unwarmed timing overstates latency by up to 15×. Under Gaussian noise, the summed hybrid degrades like the graph branch, which motivates gated or attention-guiding fusion.

title: Comparing Data-Derived and LLM-Elicited Indicator Weights for EU Circular Economy Assessment: An MCDA Study
container-title: Sustainability
c8c9ff9d8b3db25ab160f740a5369b87078ed967.abstract: Country rankings of circular economy (CE) performance depend on how indicators are weighted. This study compares data-derived and large language model (LLM)-elicited weights for 13 EU Circular Economy Monitoring Framework indicators across 27 EU countries in 2022. CRITIC, Entropy and MEREC provided data-derived weights, while Claude-sonnet-5 (Anthropic) and ChatGPT gpt-5.6-terra (OpenAI) generated pairwise comparisons using the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) and expert personas. Countries were ranked using TOPSIS and MARCOS. LLM weights were tested through additional repetitions and prompt variations and compared with two published human expert panels. Under TOPSIS, pooled LLM and CRITIC weights produced broadly similar country rankings (Spearman’s ρ = 0.78), despite different indicator priorities. The LLM panel gave greater weight to material and consumption footprints. Rankings varied with weighting and normalization choices. Claude and ChatGPT produced different TOPSIS rankings, although removing persona instructions barely changed pooled rankings (ρ = 0.995); ChatGPT showed greater sensitivity (ρ = 0.872). Both published expert panels prioritized Competitiveness and Innovation, unlike the LLM panel. Rankings under TOPSIS and MARCOS were generally similar. These findings show that similar rankings can conceal different indicator priorities. LLM-elicited weights offer an additional assessment scenario, not a substitute for human expert judgment.

title: Visual search as a cognitive marker to discriminate progressive supranuclear palsy from Parkinson’s disease
container-title: Brain Communications
abda63e481849a88d2097be19b78ee960e6d5e9f.abstract: Abstract Early and accurate diagnosis of Progressive Supranuclear Palsy is a high priority for both patients and clinicians. Nearly half of individuals with Progressive Supranuclear Palsy are initially given an alternative diagnosis—most commonly Parkinson’s disease—and the correct diagnosis of Progressive Supranuclear Palsy is delayed by an average of three years compared with Parkinson’s disease. Problems with cognition arise early in the progression of Progressive Supranuclear Palsy, including profoundly disturbed visual search. This search deficit is likely caused by a combination of oculomotor, visuospatial, attentional and executive dysfunction, which is not observed in Parkinson’s. Since assessment of visual search is not routinely included in clinical testing for Progressive Supranuclear Palsy, it may represent a promising method for differentiating these movement disorders. However, few studies have systematically compared visual search in Progressive Supranuclear Palsy and Parkinson’s disease, so the extent to which search deficits can reliably differentiate the two diseases is unknown. To address this issue, patients with Progressive Supranuclear Palsy (N = 28), Parkinson’s disease (N=28) and age matched controls (N=27) completed four tests of visuospatial attention: an easy feature search task, a difficult feature search task, a conjunction search task and a paper-and-pencil cancellation task (the Bells test). We measured perceptual sensitivity (d prime), search time and detection accuracy. Search efficiency in the Bells test was also modelled using Quality of Search score. In addition, patients completed tests of oculomotor system integrity, the Montreal Cognitive Assessment and the National Eye Institute Visual Function Questionnaire 25. As predicted, Progressive Supranuclear Palsy was associated with a profound search deficit: search was slow and highly disorganised on all tests. Furthermore, reflexive orienting along the vertical axis was impaired on the easy feature search. Critically, Receiver Operator Characteristic analyses revealed that the Quality of Search score derived from the Bells test classified Progressive Supranuclear Palsy with a sensitivity of 82%, a specificity of 96%, and Area under the Curve of .90. Given the Bells test is fast to administer (∼5 mins), free, relatively simple to score and already widely used in neuropsychology assessment, it has the potential to be a highly effective addition to the battery of tests used in the differential diagnosis of Progressive Supranuclear Palsy

title: Occupational Types, Working Hours, and Cognitive Trajectories
container-title: Work, Aging and Retirement
ffb9730bc26d334ee9d4a045cd264d4e1fd4ff60.abstract: Abstract The relationship between work and cognitive function in later years has gained attention recently. However, information on occupational types, working hours, and cognitive function based on longitudinal cohort studies from developing countries remains limited. This study utilizes data from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study and employs group-based trajectory modeling to depict the heterogeneous changes in cognitive function over time among middle-aged and older adults and specifically examines the associations between occupational types (agricultural work, non-agricultural employment, non-agricultural self-employed or family business), working hours, and cognitive trajectories. Our findings indicate that agricultural work is associated with poorer cognitive trajectories compared to non-agricultural employment and non-agricultural self-employed or family business. Compared to individuals working 40 hours or less per week, those working 41–55 hours had a higher likelihood of experiencing a “rapid decline” cognitive trajectory. Furthermore, working over 55 hours per week was associated with an increased likelihood of belonging to both the “rapid decline” and “persistently moderate” trajectory groups. We did not observe a significant multiplicative interaction between occupational types and working hours on the cognitive trajectories. These results enhance our understanding of the relationship between work-related factors and cognitive function, providing a scientific basis for developing targeted intervention measures in the context of developing countries.

title: Generative Artificial Intelligence in Architectural Research: Limits of Regulation
container-title: Vestnik Tomskogo gosudarstvennogo arkhitekturno-stroitel'nogo universiteta. JOURNAL of Construction and Architecture
c0d7722a36617cb6ecbf496cb086f01ec3037777.abstract: Purpose : The aim is to outline the problem area, define the boundaries of what is subject to regulation, distinguish ineffective regulatory strategies from promising ones, and identify likely trajectories as they apply to master’s and doctoral dissertations, primarily in architectural disciplines. Design/methodology/approach: A comparative analysis of Russian and international regulatory, publishing, and academic documents from 2023–2026 and empirical studies on detectors and the authenticity of generated text, experience in drafting regulations for a dissertation council in architectural disciplines. Research findings: Five areas of uncertainty are identified: authorship and responsibility, text as evidence of competence, reliability and plausibility, detectability and the flip side of metrics, and confidentiality and symmetry of expert evaluation. Three boundaries of regulation are defined, the ineffectiveness of a complete ban, total control, detectors as evidence, percentage quotas, regulation of specific products, and non-interference is demonstrated, transferable solutions from local legislation are described, i.e., functional classification, disclosure instead of prohibition, presumption of good faith and procedural safeguards, symmetry of requirements, industry standards, and technological neutrality. Practical implications : Transferable solutions of a local regulation include a function-based classification of use, disclosure instead of prohibition, a presumption of good faith with procedural guarantees, symmetrical requirements for candidates and reviewers, discipline-specific rules for images and reconstructions, and technological neutrality. Originality/value: The problem is shown to be epistemic and institutional rather than technological. The centre of gravity of assessment shifts from the manuscript to the oral defense of a thesis and verifiable artefacts. The restoration-theory principle of distinguishability of original and supplemented material is applied to the digital artefacts of a dissertation.

title: Assessment of Taraba Broadcast Journalists Knowledge, Adoption and Usage of Artificial Intelligence in Journalistic Practices
container-title: RESEARCH JOURNAL OF MASS COMMUNICATION AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY
97118f0bf859026cd214d2e2d60880a341ce2bbe.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has become an essential tool in various fields, including journalism. However, the extent to which broadcast journalists in Taraba State, Nigeria embraced and utilized AI in their practices remains a subject of debate. It is on the above premise that this research examined Taraba State broadcast journalists' knowledge and usage of AI in journalistic practices. The paper was built on the technology acceptance model, diffusion of innovation theory, and social learning theory. The study adopted a qualitative approach where in-depth interviews were used. The in-depth interviews were conducted until the results reached saturation point. Findings of the study revealed that in journalists in Taraba State, Nigeria are slowly beginning to embrace AI for journalistic practice. However, there knowledge of AI usage for journalistic practices is low hence there is a significant knowledge gap that needs to be bridged. Therefore, the study recommends among other things that journalists in Taraba State need to gain more knowledge about AI and its potential applications in journalistic practices. The paper concludes that with proper training and guidance, journalists in Taraba State can harness the power of this AI technology to improve their reporting practices while ensuring ethical standards are upheld.

title: Heterogeneity matters: cooling gains from artificial groundwater circulation in geothermal borehole fields
container-title: Geothermal Energy
315608efdc57b6c5ace19dbf454f03009e3c0cad.abstract: Abstract Artificial groundwater circulation using well doublets can substantially mitigate heat accumulation around borehole heat-exchanger (BHE) arrays, even in geologically heterogeneous settings. We develop a single-platform MODFLOW 6 model that couples the Groundwater Flow and Groundwater Energy packages to simulate a nine-BHE array within a five-layer aquifer system and quantify the cooling benefit of an engineered injection–extraction pair under both confined and unconfined conditions. After a vertical discretization analysis, we adopt a mesh that resolves interlayer temperature structure and use it to assess circulation rates from 0 to $$66~\mathrm {m^3\,d^{-1}}$$ . Forced circulation lowers 10-year temperatures near the BHE array by as much as $$8.7~^\circ \textrm{C}$$ , with unconfined cases remaining slightly warmer than confined cases at equal rates. Furthermore, we examine the effect of heterogeneity on the efficiency of the well doublet heat-mitigation strategy. Groundwater circulation consistently reduces subsurface temperatures. Unresolved hydraulic-conductivity heterogeneity introduces uncertainty in groundwater temperature predictions, resulting in temperature variations of up to $$4~^\circ \textrm{C}$$ among realizations, while the ensemble-mean temperature differs from that of the corresponding homogeneous aquifer by approximately $$1~^\circ \textrm{C}$$ . Shorter hydraulic-conductivity correlation lengths yield lower average temperatures. These results provide process-based guidance: (i) high-resolution characterization of the geothermal site is important for the efficient design of geothermal energy systems; (ii) deploy well doublets and tune pumping–injection rates $$Q$$ to advect heat away from the BHE array, recognizing diminishing returns at high rates; (iii) preferentially site BHE fields along high hydraulic conductivity pathways identified by site characterization; and (iv) account for partially saturated layers where relevant, as they modestly elevate groundwater temperatures.

title: Responsible entrepreneurship, safety involvement, prohibitive safety voice and employee safety participation in a developing economy: a serial model
container-title: Social Responsibility Journal
46493c520a4ece91f11f204a39f89ae1efb24446.abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine how owner-managers’ responsible entrepreneurship influences employee safety participation through the serial mediation of safety involvement and prohibitive safety voice. Design/methodology/approach Data were collected from 417 owner-managers of manufacturing SMEs in Ghana. The hypotheses were tested using partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM). Findings The results show that responsible entrepreneurship positively influences employee safety participation. While safety involvement does not moderate this relationship, it significantly mediates the link between responsible entrepreneurship and both prohibitive safety voice and employee safety participation. The serial mediation analysis further indicates that responsible entrepreneurship enhances safety involvement, which fosters prohibitive safety voice and, in turn, increases employee safety participation. Practical implications Owner-managers should involve employees in identifying workplace hazards, discuss safety concerns during routine meetings and provide simple channels for reporting unsafe practices. Policymakers can support SMEs through practical safety guidelines, short training programmes and advisory services that help businesses implement affordable employee-centred safety practices. Originality/value This study develops a process-oriented framework explaining the employee-level behavioural mechanisms through which responsible entrepreneurship fosters proactive safety practices in SMEs, particularly under the resource and structural constraints common in developing economies.

title: Does Green Brand Equity Buffer or Burn? Understanding Boundary Conditions in Justice Evaluations of Sharing Economy Service Failure
container-title: Review of Marketing Science
b5fb588585361e3bddd84feeaf43be49763a72e3.abstract: Abstract The authors investigate green brand equity as a representation of firm phenotype in terms of its impact on the relationship between perceived justice of service recovery and customer citizenship and behavioral loyalty behavior. The firm phenotype of GBE can perform different roles as a moral signal, a normative expectation or a value laden identity cue. The purpose of this study is to identify the role/s performed in the fair recovery of sharing economy service failure. Drawing on the tradeoff between expectation-disconfirmation versus judgment assimilation-categorization, this study seeks to understand the buffering/incendiary influence of green brand equity in the context of service recovery in a sustainable services context. The findings of the conceptual model are empirically verified through surveys distributed to 804 digitally engaged sharing economy consumers using Partial-Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling. The results reveal that while consumers demonstrate desirable citizenship towards the firm when it is perceived to be a high green brand equity firm that delivers fair service recovery, it does not extend the same leeway in terms of service re-patronage. The conclusion of the study is that sustainability signaling, though morally rewarded in the long-term through citizenship connoting judgment assimilation may not necessarily transform into a short-term financial reward through re-patronage since normative expectations are negatively disconfirmed. It establishes that boundary conditions within sustainable services context demonstrate a temporal dichotomy lending support to a contingency perspective of the branding buffer in service recovery.

title: Programmer expertise classification using cognitive load and transfer learning
container-title: Discover Computing
f504c1239bb13fa73a7b7735bc8c27cc18f7e8e5.abstract: Abstract Context Evaluating a programmer’s performance by considering both technical and cognitive skills is indispensable in many software development tasks. Problem Technical skills are relatively easy to assess, whereas non-technical skills, such as long-term memory, critical thinking, and emotional intelligence, are often overlooked while measuring the performance of a programmer. Aim The primary objective of this work is to propose a reliable framework for classifying programmers into five framework-derived proficiency ranks. Methods Participants are given an assignment with both technical and non-technical questions. A cognitive load index that combines technical and non-technical skills is used to analyze performance and stratify it into five ranks. The proposed framework was evaluated using CatBoost and TabNet classifiers in a transfer-learning setup. It used the source dataset (Another researcher’s dataset) for pre-training and the proposed programmer dataset for fine-tuning. Extensive experiments, including confusion matrix analysis, 5-fold cross-validation, sensitivity analysis, and ablation studies, confirm the framework’s effectiveness and robustness. Results The fine-tuned CatBoost model outperformed the TabNet model, achieving an impressive 87% accuracy, a significant improvement over the pre-trained model’s 31%. The findings demonstrate that combining technical skills with non-technical aspects greatly enhances the accuracy of classifying programmer expertise. This offers a dependable method for assessing programmers in software engineering education. The study develops a robust framework for evaluating programming performance that incorporates both technical and non-technical skills, and it can be adapted for other cognitive and skill-based evaluations across different fields.

title:
MALDI-TOF MS for
Next-Generation Food Adulteration
Screening: Combined Novel Matrices, Microfluidics, and Artificial
Intelligence for High-Throughput and Precise Detection
container-title:
Journal of Agricultural
and Food Chemistry
1f77015ea261c9dc668d21d254a9b7a9d1e2d24e.abstract: Abstract Matrix-assisted laser desorption/ionization time-of-flight mass spectrometry (MALDI-TOF MS) has emerged as a detection tool to ensure food safety and quality, especially for the rapid and accurate identification of adulterants. However, its application is challenged by limitations of commercial matrices, such as high background interference and low sensitivity. Complex sample preparation, labor-intensive data processing, and human errors further hinder its adoption in high-throughput workflows. Unlike previous reviews that primarily draw horizontal comparisons between MALDI-TOF MS and other conventional food detection methods, this review centers on complementary technical strategies to overcome the intrinsic analytical limitations of MALDI-TOF MS. It assesses innovative matrix materials for improved small-molecule detection performance. This work also provides a critical discussion of microfluidic-enabled automated sample preparation and machine learning-assisted spectral interpretation, which target current bottlenecks and expand practical applicability. The combination of MALDI-TOF MS with cutting-edge technologies provides promising new opportunities toward precise, automated, and high-throughput capabilities in food analysis.

title: A Lightweight Convolutional Neural Network for High-Accuracy Autism Spectrum Disorder Detection from Facial Images
container-title: Journal of Artificial Intelligence and Technology
64e8899b1e5752cd7dae086ad644aa2901c913fd.abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a neurodevelopmental disorder with diverse and complex manifestations. This condition requires early detection which is crucial in finding a cure. Traditional diagnostic procedures are biased and time-consuming. These create a pressing need for objective and accessible screening tools. The rapid development of artificial intelligence, particularly deep learning (DL) methods, offers promising resolutions for automating ASD detection. Such detection is done through analyzing behavioral and physical biomarkers. This study proposes a convenient but complex neural network to support early ASD screening through facial images. The model classifies facial images of children as autistic or non-autistic by using the publicly available Autistic Children Facial Dataset. Various experiments assess the model’s performance. The design is developed to be statistically efficient, which makes it suitable for mobile and embedded systems for real-time screening. Results show that our proposed model shows better performance than the existing approaches, especially in the levels of accuracy and area under curve (AUC). This further confirms its efficiency and prospects for autism screening applications. Achieving accuracy of 98.97%, the model delivers better performance than the evaluated benchmark models. These findings affirm that lightweight image-focused DL approaches are well suited to provide clinicians with a trustworthy and scalable method for early ASD screening. Thus, it is evident that the proposed model facilitates timely support for individuals and families.

title: Test-Time Adaptation and Domain Generalization in Multimodal Sentiment Analysis: From Laboratory to Real-World Deployment
container-title: Journal of Artificial Intelligence and Technology
5e4ecd83aef1b5b32370fdaa0350d6c5f45d009a.abstract: The deployment of multimodal sentiment analysis (MSA) systems in real-world environments is hindered by domain shift, where performance degrades significantly when test data diverges from the training distribution. This review paper provides a comprehensive survey of two pivotal strategies to address this challenge: domain generalization (DG) and test-time adaptation(TTA). We present a novel taxonomy of state-of-the-art methods, categorizing them into data manipulation, representation learning, meta-learning, and hybrid approaches. The review critically examines techniques specifically designed for multimodal data, including modality-specific adaptation and cross-modal consistency enforcement. Furthermore, we discuss the common benchmarks and evaluation metrics that are used to assess robustness to real-world challenges such as missing modalities, not independent and identically distributed (non-i.i.d.) data streams, and computational constraints. Finally, the paper outlines critical open challenges and future research directions, emphasizing the need to handle mixed and continual shifts, adapt large multimodal models efficiently, and improve explainability. This work assists researchers in building reliable MSA systems for real-world deployment.
