title: EVALUATING THE ACCURACY AND RELIABILITY OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE CHATBOTS IN ANSWERING DENTAL SPECIALTY EXAMINATION PERIODONTOLOGY QUESTIONS
container-title: Cumhuriyet Dental Journal
3b9c5a45c67ebce7e5c340566e0789cb4fbe6a5e.abstract: Background/Aim: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly utilized by dental students and specialty candidates as supplementary tools for examination preparation. However, their reliability in specialized clinical domains requiring analytical reasoning remains underexplored. This study aimed to comparatively evaluate the accuracy, reliability, and inter-model agreement of three contemporary reasoning-focused LLMs in answering Periodontology questions from the Turkish Dental Specialty Examination (DUS).Materials and Methods: In this cross-sectional in silico study, 100 multiple-choice Periodontology questions administered in past DUS sessions (2012–2026) were selected. The questions were presented in isolated sessions without prior contextual prompting to three models: OpenAI GPT-5.5 Thinking, Anthropic Claude Opus 4.7 (adaptive thinking), and Google Gemini 3.1 Pro. Responses were scored dichotomously against official answer keys. Overall accuracy rates were compared using Cochran's Q test, pairwise agreement was assessed via Cohen's Kappa (k) coefficient, and shared error distributions were analyzed using a two-tailed Binomial test (p 0.05), ChatGPT and Gemini selected the identical incorrect distractor in all 5 questions they mutually failed (100% shared error rate; p = 0.0625).Conclusion: Contemporary reasoning-capable LLMs demonstrate high accuracy and substantial inter-model consistency on specialty-level Periodontology questions. Nevertheless, the presence of concordant errors indicates shared algorithmic blind spots, underscoring that AI outputs must be supplemented by specialist oversight and evidence-based verification in dental education.

title: Robust power-law computing for edge intelligence using spin-orbit torque magnetic tunnel junctions
container-title: Applied Physics Reviews
1b0994b5b51419443b31c8e1fabba0db0c8b343c.abstract: Power-law transformations are widely used in edge perception, where compact implementations must balance numerical precision, circuit resources, and device variability. Here, we demonstrate a stochastic power-law architecture based on spin–orbit-torque magnetic tunnel junctions (SOT-MTJs). An event-driven feedback loop adjusts the write voltage to regulate the probability of an all-1 event in an n-bit block. Under the fixed-point sampling model, this establishes a switching probability p = b1/n, from which m-bit event statistics yield the power-law target bm/n. Online probability locking removes the need for offline per-device probability-voltage characterization or stored calibration tables. Measurements on W-based SOT-MTJs, combined with digital analysis of the acquired bitstreams, demonstrate representative power-law operations with absolute deviations of 0.003 or less at the reported precision, as well as parallel decoding of multiple exponents from one source. A 4-bit gamma-correction example preserves dark-region image detail and reaches approximately 35 dB peak signal-to-noise ratio relative to the theoretical gamma-domain reference near 1000 raw samples. A 5 Oe device-level field perturbation and a joint ±90% simulation centered on the measured parameter means of 25 devices examine adaptation and the safe voltage operating boundary under the tested conditions. These results establish a nonlinear computing primitive with accuracy controlled by sampling depth and an operating point maintained through feedback.

title: Artificial Intelligence-Supported Nutrition Guidance and Healthy Dietary Habits among University Students: The Mediating Role of Nutrition Literacy
container-title: Journal of Global Social Transformation
6f4e276d80bdf68506836dc1b84193d260077abf.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI)-supported nutrition guidance is increasingly becoming an accessible source of dietary information for university students; however, its relationship with healthy dietary habits and the potential mediating role of nutrition literacy require further investigation. This study examines the relationship between AI-supported nutrition guidance and healthy dietary habits among university students in Pakistan, with nutrition literacy as a potential mediator. A quantitative, cross-sectional research design was proposed, involving 327 undergraduate and postgraduate students recruited through non-probability convenience sampling. Primary data were planned to be collected through a self-administered structured questionnaire distributed using Google Forms. The questionnaire assessed AI-supported nutrition guidance, nutrition literacy, healthy dietary habits, and demographic characteristics. The proposed statistical analysis included descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation, regression analysis, and mediation analysis using Hayes’ PROCESS Macro Model 4 with 5,000 bootstrap samples and 95% confidence intervals. The illustrative results suggested a positive association between AI-supported nutrition guidance and nutrition literacy (β = 0.463, R² = 0.214), alongside a positive relationship between AI-supported nutrition guidance and healthy dietary habits (r = 0.542). The illustrative mediation analysis indicated an indirect effect through nutrition literacy of 0.246, with a 95% bootstrap confidence interval of [0.159, 0.343]. These numerical values are hypothetical and have not been calculated from actual participant responses. The study emphasizes that access to AI-generated nutrition information alone may not ensure healthier dietary decisions, as students must also be able to understand, evaluate, and apply the guidance they receive. Its proposed findings may inform university health education, digital nutrition literacy initiatives, and the development of more reliable AI-supported dietary resources. The research may also provide a foundation for future investigations into how digital nutrition guidance interacts with students’ knowledge, food choices, and everyday dietary practices. Longitudinal and experimental studies could further examine whether improvements in nutrition literacy are associated with sustained changes in healthy eating behaviors.

title: Unterstützende Interventionen bei Aufmerksamkeitsdefizit‑/Hyperaktivitätsstörung (ADHS) im schulischen Kontext: Ein Scoping Review
Supportive interventions for attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) in the school context: a scoping review
container-title: Prävention und Gesundheitsförderung
e662bbbc6224c0d8996300acafe3f5375656c0f6.abstract: Zusammenfassung Hintergrund und Ziel Der schulische Alltag stellt für Schüler*innen mit Aufmerksamkeitsdefizit‑/Hyperaktivitätsstörung (ADHS), ihre Eltern und Lehrkräfte eine zentrale Belastungsquelle dar. Ziel des Scoping Reviews war es zu untersuchen, inwieweit Interventionen bei ADHS im schulischen Kontext Unterstützung bieten können. Methode Es wurde ein Scoping Review durchgeführt und gemäß PRISMA-ScR (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews) berichtet. Die systematische Recherche erfolgte in MEDLINE (via PubMed). Eingeschlossen wurden multimodale Interventionen für Schüler*innen mit ADHS im Alter von 6 bis 18 Jahren. Die Auswertung erfolgte mittels thematischer Analyse nach Braun und Clarke. Ergebnisse Zwölf Publikationen wurden eingeschlossen. Die Interventionen adressierten Schüler*innen, Eltern und Lehrkräfte insbesondere durch organisatorische und verhaltensbezogene Interventionsinhalte. Verbesserungen wurden v. a. bei der ADHS-Symptomatik und bei organisatorischen Leistungen berichtet. Die Befunde zu akademischen Leistungen und zum Sozialverhalten waren weniger einheitlich. Die Stichproben waren überwiegend männlich geprägt, und Interventionseffekte wurden nicht differenziert nach ADHS-Subtypen ausgewertet. Zudem lagen kaum Erkenntnisse zur fachlich-didaktischen und interaktionalen Gestaltung konkreter schulischer Lehr-Lern-Prozesse vor. Schlussfolgerung Forschungsbedarf besteht insbesondere hinsichtlich Mädchen mit ADHS, einer differenzierten Betrachtung unterschiedlicher ADHS-Erscheinungsbilder und Behandlungsbedingungen sowie der evidenzbasierten Gestaltung fachlich-didaktischer und interaktionaler Lehr-Lern-Prozesse im inklusiven Unterricht.

title: Exploring Spatial Inequities and Livability: A Mixed-Methods Study Using Artificial Intelligence and Community Insights
container-title: Journal of Urban Health
b1ae7f00473b202c0bafa0519599bfb9ae112af0.abstract: Abstract Rapid urbanization has intensified health and social inequities through the uneven distribution of infrastructure, services, and public space. In St. Louis, Missouri (USA), these disparities remain geographically concentrated and rooted in long-standing patterns of racial segregation and disinvestment. This study examines how spatial inequities shape urban livability by integrating scalable artificial intelligence (AI) methods with community-based insights. We applied a vision–language model (VLM), supported by a large language model (LLM), to classify micro-scale built-environment features from 7848 Google Street View segments, and conducted semi-structured interviews with residents and stakeholders. The AI analysis revealed baseline infrastructure such as street lighting (84.9%) and continuous pavements (77%), but very low coverage of universal design features such as curb ramps (9.7%) and pedestrian crossings (7.1%). These deficits were significantly associated with lower median incomes and higher proportions of non-Hispanic Black residents. Qualitative findings confirmed and contextualized these patterns, linking them to historical redlining, fragmented governance, and everyday experiences of constrained mobility and safety. By combining scalable AI tools with community narratives, this study demonstrates that spatial inequities are both visible in the physical streetscape and embodied in daily life. Methodologically, it advances the use of VLM and LLM-enabled pipelines for urban audits; conceptually, it reframes livability metrics through the lens of spatial equity; and practically, it provides a replicable framework for equity-centered planning.

title: Temporal Evaluation of Hybrid Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning Models for Malware Detection using The EMBER Dataset
container-title: Journal of Global Social Transformation
bb47ef589a0980779729d7bb7314bba643dd951b.abstract: Malware detection remains a critical challenge in computer science and cybersecurity due to the continuous evolution of malicious software, concept drift, and the declining generalization capability of machine learning models over time. This study investigates the temporal performance of hybrid artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) models for static malware detection using the EMBER dataset. A quantitative experimental design is employed to compare Logistic Regression, Random Forest, LightGBM, and Multilayer Perceptron (MLP) classifiers with a hybrid ensemble approach. The methodology incorporates feature preprocessing, chronological data partitioning, supervised model training, and temporal performance evaluation using accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, and the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (ROC-AUC). Comparative analysis examined differences in classification performance and temporal degradation across the evaluated models. Confusion-matrix analysis and false-negative rates were also considered to assess classification reliability and identify potential detection errors. The hybrid framework combined tree-based learning and neural network predictions to investigate classification performance and detection consistency across temporally distinct malware samples. The significance of this research lies in addressing the limitations of conventional random-split evaluation and providing a more realistic framework for assessing the temporal generalization of intelligent malware detection systems. The findings are intended to inform the development of adaptive, scalable, and robust cybersecurity solutions capable of responding to evolving malware threats.

title: Exploring the Relationships Between Auditory Processing, Language, Cognitive, and Speech-in-Noise Abilities in School-Aged Children
container-title: Ear & Hearing
b2bbc5e2c8343f5ecda5c388fc13eada6672f977.abstract: Objectives: Understanding speech in noise and reverberation requires the integration of auditory, language, and cognitive abilities. Many children experience listening difficulties in such environments which, if persistent, can affect long-term academic outcomes. However, relative contributions of underlying processes remain poorly understood. This study investigated how nonspeech auditory processing, language and cognitive abilities contribute to phoneme identification and sentence understanding in noise in a representative sample of school-aged children. Design: The study included 221 primary school children aged 6 to 11 yr (88 boys, 133 girls), all with normal peripheral hearing. Participants completed measures of nonspeech auditory processing, phoneme identification, and sentence understanding in noise and reverberation, as well as language ability, attention, nonverbal intelligence, and memory. Using structural equation modeling enabled us to consider the influence of multiple predictors simultaneously. Results: A complex pattern of relationships emerged. Bottom-up nonspeech auditory processing supported phoneme identification, which in turn supported sentence understanding in noise. Language ability had a direct top-down influence on sentence understanding. Memory and intelligence contributed indirectly through their influence on language. Minimal associations were observed between cognition and nonspeech auditory processing, supporting a conceptual distinction between auditory and higher-level processes. Conclusions: The results show that bottom-up and top-down abilities make distinct contributions to listening and identify direct and indirect pathways underlying children’s listening in adverse conditions. Auditory processing contributed to phoneme perception, which in turn supported sentence understanding in noise. Language abilities exerted a strong independent influence to sentence understanding in noise, while nonverbal intelligence and memory affected performance only indirectly through language.

title:
Data Characterization
and Multi-Plant Data Integration
Strategies for Artificial Neural Network Modeling in Palm Oil Refining
container-title: ACS Omega
764ddf2a835029a5ceacb513bcddd293e1770973.abstract: Abstract Real-time quality monitoring in palm oil refining is often hindered by laboratory delays, which can be mitigated through the development of Artificial Neural Network (ANN) soft sensors. However, the effectiveness of these models is constrained by the characteristics of available process data. To address this, this study establishes a quantitative framework for assessing data set suitability by analyzing industrial data from three refineries using coefficient of variation (CV) statistics and self-organizing map (SOM) visualizations, with a feedforward neural network (FFN) used as a baseline model. Results show that process variables with CV exceeding 50% consistently yield better FFN performance than those below 50%. An integration strategy between different refineries was introduced to overcome the limitation of single-plant data and improve model performance to above 80% prediction accuracy for FFA content and Red Lovibond color. To test whether this improvement resulted from model capacity rather than data variability. The results further showed that data variability significantly affects model performance rather than model architecture. These findings establish CV as a practical criterion for data set suitability in ANN modeling for palm oil refining, offering an approach other chemical process industries facing similarly low-variation data may adapt.

title:
Ligand Design
for REE Recovery Using Artificial Intelligence
container-title: ACS ES&T Engineering
1727a3e30634b07118289bd35bd75e91359ce431.abstract: Abstract Rare earth elements (REEs) are designated as critical materials due to their urgent need and supply uncertainties. The scarcity of REE supply is exacerbated by environmentally damaging extraction practices, necessitating more efficient, sustainable extraction and separation methods. Traditional techniques such as solvent extraction are often constrained by their extensive organic solvent consumption and limited extraction efficiency, especially for e-waste feedstocks containing heterogeneous compositions. As an alternative to traditional methods, solid-phase extraction (SPE) technique streamlines REE extraction and separation by providing high chelating selectivity, fewer operational stages, and minimal secondary waste generation. This review explores recent advances in ligand design for REE recovery, especially carbonyl amide-based, phosphorus-containing, β-diketone- and acylpyrazolone-based, macrocyclic, and biologically derived ligands. Enhancing the surface density of more REE-selective ligands on solid-phase matrices provides a viable pathway to overcome the thermodynamic constraints of separating adjacent, chemically homologous REEs in urban mining processes. Direct applications of artificial intelligence (AI), particularly machine learning (ML), to experimentally validated REE recovery remain limited and are mainly focused on narrowly defined tasks, including metal–ligand stability-constant prediction, ligand ranking, extraction-equilibrium modeling, and process simulation. Rather than treating AI-assisted REE recovery as a mature field, this review critically distinguishes demonstrated REE-specific applications from transferable computational frameworks that remain to be validated. Particular attention is given to molecular descriptors, coordination geometry, thermodynamic properties, data quality, and validation requirements for predictive ligand design. By connecting established REE coordination chemistry with emerging AI methodologies, this review identifies current limitations and proposes a chemically grounded roadmap for future ligand discovery and process optimization.

title: Multi-Scale Attention-Enhanced YOLO26 for Wind Power Equipment Surface Defect Detection
container-title: Applied Sciences
f3e3d977ada41c835585767e11bd2d4919f9b406.abstract: Surface defects in wind power equipment exhibit substantial variations in scale, morphology, texture, and orientation and are frequently affected by complex backgrounds, illumination changes, and surface contamination, posing challenges to reliable visual inspection. This study proposes a YOLO26-based surface defect detection framework that integrates multi-scale contextual modeling, spatial–channel collaborative attention, and directional feature recalibration. Specifically, the original SPPF module is replaced with SPPSCCAP to combine multi-scale pooling, spatial–channel reconstruction, and global contextual information. CADP-SCSA is subsequently introduced to jointly model directional spatial information and inter-channel dependencies, while ELA-B modules are embedded before the P3, P4, and P5 detection heads to preserve horizontal and vertical positional information. Experiments were conducted on a public wind power equipment dataset containing 9583 images and 22,856 annotated instances across seven defect categories. Under a unified training and testing protocol, comprehensive ablation experiments demonstrate that the effects of the three enhancement mechanisms are not simply additive. Among the evaluated configurations, the three-module Model H achieved the highest values across the four reported detection metrics, with a precision of 0.9120, a recall of 0.8860, an mAP50 of 0.9060, and an mAP50–95 of 0.6660. Compared with the baseline model, these results represent improvements of 5.57, 8.99, 8.63, and 9.44 percentage points, respectively. These findings demonstrate the importance of layer-specific feature enhancement and module coupling in multi-class defect detection and provide a practical basis for vision-based inspection and condition assessment of wind power equipment.

title: Effects of Intermittent Theta-Burst Stimulation over the Left Dorsolateral Prefrontal Cortex on Executive Function During Sustained Simulated Flight Operations: A Randomized Crossover Study Using a Flight–Cognitive Dual-Task Paradigm
container-title: Bioengineering
650e5a5940124e8eb202662f1b08dd2cb3a024fd.abstract: Sustained flight operation load may compromise executive control in complex human–machine interaction environments. Intermittent theta-burst stimulation (iTBS) over the left dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (DLPFC) holds potential for modulating executive function, yet its effects on different executive components under sustained operational load remain unclear. This study employed a randomized, balanced, within-subject crossover design, enrolling 25 healthy male participants. Each participant completed three intervention conditions: Active iTBS, Sham iTBS, and No-stimulation. Each experimental session consisted of stimulation delivery, a 60-min cruising simulated flight, and a 30-min flight–cognitive dual-task phase. Primary outcomes were behavioral performance on the Go/No-Go, 3-back, and number-rule switching tasks; EEG microstates and prefrontal relative oxygenated hemoglobin (HbO) changes during the dual-task phase served as exploratory neurophysiological indices. Results showed that condition differences were concentrated in working memory updating and rule switching: compared with No-stimulation, Active iTBS shortened 3-back reaction time and reduced switch cost; compared with both No-stimulation and Sham iTBS, Active iTBS improved 3-back accuracy and number-rule switching accuracy; the switch-cost difference between Active and Sham iTBS did not reach significance (pBonferroni = 0.055). No significant condition effect was observed for the Go/No-Go task. EEG microstate analysis revealed task-specific changes: under the Active iTBS condition, the occurrence rate and temporal coverage of microstate D increased during the 3-back task; temporal coverage of microstate D increased during the number-rule switching task; no significant microstate changes were observed during the Go/No-Go task. Exploratory fNIRS analysis indicated that left-hemisphere and all-channel prefrontal HbO under Active iTBS was higher than under Sham iTBS in planned pairwise comparisons (pBonferroni < 0.03), but the corresponding condition main effects (p ≥ 0.065) and condition × hemisphere interaction (p = 0.919) were non-significant, and channel-level effects did not survive multiple-comparison correction. These findings suggest that, within the flight–cognitive dual-task paradigm, Active iTBS over the left DLPFC is associated with improvements in working memory and rule switching performance, accompanied by changes in microstate temporal organization during certain tasks. The microstate and fNIRS results provide exploratory neurophysiological observations and cannot establish causal relationships with the behavioral improvements.

title: A Verifiable Agentic Framework for Sequential Multimodal Prediction of Mild Cognitive Impairment Progression
container-title: Bioengineering
8d08380a0ed180432ed111d94da0148d50eb7ea4.abstract: Multimodal models can predict progression from mild cognitive impairment (MCI) to Alzheimer’s disease (AD), but most evaluations assume that every modality is immediately available. We developed a retrospective framework using only the Alzheimer’s Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI) that separates statistical risk estimation, sequential evidence acquisition, language-model explanation, and deterministic verification. Participants with baseline MCI were assigned state-specific landmarks using information visible within a +/−90-day window. The primary simulation cohort included 425 participants with clinical/cognitive, magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-derived, and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) evidence; 153 converted to AD within 36 months after the landmark. Calibrated elastic-net models were evaluated with 10 repeated nested five-fold cross-validation. In the common-landmark cohort, adding MRI-derived and CSF features improved the Brier score from 0.158 (95% confidence interval (CI) 0.141–0.175) to 0.138 (0.122–0.155) and the area under the receiver-operating characteristic curve (AUROC) from 0.837 (0.802–0.871) to 0.878 (0.847–0.908). A sequential policy used cross-fitted estimates of individual Brier-score gain to decide whether to request MRI or CSF. The fixed-threshold exploratory analysis requested 40.6% fewer simulated tests than an all-tests policy while meeting the prespecified Brier and AUROC noninferiority margins. Under fully nested threshold selection, the policy requested 46.9% fewer tests and met the AUROC criterion, while narrowly missing the Brier criterion (difference 0.00546, 95% CI 0.00090–0.01003; margin +0.01). In a 40-card-per-model engineering audit, local Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-8B models copied probabilities and cited supplied evidence correctly in 40/40 cards but matched the deterministic action in 16/40 and 15/40 cards, respectively. Execution authority therefore remained with the deterministic policy. Here, agentic refers to the orchestration of modular evidence states, policy checks, verification, and explanation; it does not imply autonomous language-model control. As a retrospective simulation, the framework does not establish prospective clinical utility, real-world cost savings, or external computational reproducibility.

title: Electrophysiological Evidence of Cognitive Dysfunction After tSAH: An ERP Study Based on Three Different Stimulation Paradigms
container-title: Brain Sciences
9c1f28aac38dfb37542d762505b948d39fe676e9.abstract: Objectives: This study aims to investigate the characteristics of event-related potentials (ERP) in patients with traumatic subarachnoid hemorrhage (tSAH) during the clinical stable phase, with the aim of obtaining neuroelectrophysiological indicators that can objectively assess cognitive dysfunction caused by this injury. Methods: A total of 16 healthy volunteers and 33 tSAH patients in the stable phase were recruited. Demographic and clinical data were collected, MMSE assessments were completed, and EEG data for P300, mismatch negativity (MMN), and contingent negative variation (CNV) were recorded using a 32-lead ERP system. ERP analysis was performed by comparing the tSAH group with the healthy control (HC) group and by further dividing the tSAH group into a cognitive impairment subgroup (CI, n = 18) and a normal cognition subgroup (NC, n = 15) based on MMSE scores, with a focus on the mean amplitude and peak latency within specific time windows and their correlation with cognitive behavioral measures. Results: The results showed no significant differences in demographic characteristics between the two groups, while the MMSE scores of the tSAH group were significantly lower than those of the HC group. Compared with HC, the mean amplitude of P300 in response to the target stimuli was significantly reduced in multiple brain regions in the tSAH group and attenuated the negativity of mean CNV amplitudes across multiple brain regions, while no significant differences in mean MMN amplitudes were detected across electrodes and no significant differences were observed in peak latencies of P300 and MMN. The CI group was slightly older than the NC group; after controlling for the effect of age, the Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) scores of the CI group were significantly lower than those of the NC group, but no significant differences were found between the two groups in mean amplitudes and peak latencies of P300 and MMN or in mean CNV amplitudes. Conclusions: This study indicates that tSAH may be one of the relevant risk factors for post-traumatic cognitive dysfunction. ERP findings suggest that the allocation of relevant cognitive resources is attenuated in this population, but no differences were detected in the temporal sequence of neural processing. No significant abnormalities were observed during auditory deviance detection corresponding to the MMN time window, and no significant differences in ERP characteristics were found among the subgroups. This study found that tSAH can cause selective cognitive electrophysiological impairment, but ERP electrophysiological changes do not fully match cognitive impairment classified based on clinical scales.

title: Convolutional LSTM and Self-Attention Networks in PyTorch for Decade-Ahead Forecasting of Land-Cover Time Series
container-title: Geomatics
5bcd22ac46f796abeff6f2bec51d576b5b6cad32.abstract: Forest cover in Vietnam has changed profoundly since 1990 under agricultural expansion, urbanization and plantation programs. This study used the 31 annual JAXA High-Resolution Land-Use and Land-Cover maps of Vietnam (v21.09, 1990–2020) to quantify the dynamics of natural forest and plantations and to forecast land cover to 2030 with two deep learning models implemented in PyTorch: a convolutional long short-term memory network (ConvLSTM) and a Temporal Vision Transformer (ViT). The 250 m Level-2 maps were grouped into seven classes, and their area bias relative to the 30 m maps was quantified. The models were trained on data up to 2010 and validated by hindcasting the 2020 map against persistence, CA–Markov and Random Forest baselines. Natural forest covered 139,100 km2 in 1990 and 136,800 km2 in 2020, and plantations covered 66,600 and 49,400 km2, respectively, with the largest net forest losses in the Central Highlands and the northern uplands. In the hindcast, the ViT predicted change best (figure of merit 0.203, against 0.182 for the ConvLSTM and 0.165 for the Random Forest), whereas the Random Forest reached the highest overall accuracy (0.746); all trained models predicted about 79,000 km2 of plantation for 2020, against 49,400 km2 observed after the sharp plantation decrease in 2017–2018. Having learned the dynamics of 1990–2010, the models forecast for 2030 a further forest loss of 4–5%, with natural forest declining by 11–14% to 117,200–122,100 km2 and plantations expanding by 13–21% to 56,000–59,700 km2, a scenario in which the plantation expansion of the 2000s resumes.

title: Where Do We Look? Visual Attention Competition Between Hyper-Salient Objects and AI-Generated Virtual Endorsers in Generative Artificial Intelligence Advertising
container-title: Journal of Eye Movement Research
36fc050f60ce8845ba8db20a6617fcac6439e5ea.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) advertising, defined as advertising content created or substantially assisted by generative AI systems (AIGC), has introduced new visual features that combine algorithmically generated objects with human-like representations. Hyper-salient objects, defined by exaggerated perceptual prominence and semantic incongruity, and AI-generated virtual endorsers, represented by human-like AI-created figures, have become increasingly common in such advertisements. However, little is known about how these distinct visual cues compete for consumers’ limited attentional resources when presented together. Drawing on visual attention and scene perception perspectives, this study investigated how hyper-salient objects and AI-generated virtual endorsers influence visual attention allocation in AI-generated advertising. A 2 (hyper-salient object: present vs. absent) × 2 (AI endorser: present vs. absent) between-subjects eye-tracking experiment was conducted with 160 participants in a controlled laboratory setting using static AI-generated advertisements. Eye movements were recorded, and memory was assessed using signal detection measures (d′) from a recognition task involving target and distractor advertisements. Advertising attitude and product trust were measured using established scales. Results from linear and generalized linear mixed-effects models showed that hyper-salient objects increased early fixation probability and attracted a larger dwell time proportion, demonstrating strong attentional capture. AI-generated endorsers also attracted attention when presented alone, but their proportional attention share decreased when hyper-salient objects were simultaneously present. The effects of these visual elements on memory and product trust were conditional on their co-occurrence rather than uniform across conditions. Within the specific set of experimentally constructed stimuli and four sampled product categories, this research contributes to AIGC advertising literature by developing a visual competition perspective on how multiple AI-generated visual cues interact under limited attentional capacity, offering implications for designing effective generative AI advertisements.

title: Artificial Intelligence-Assisted Design of High-Temperature High-Entropy Alloys: Progress, Challenges, and Perspectives
container-title: Metals
3eeb6a8290fac147198ffa536b62dff847ab1791.abstract: High-temperature high-entropy alloys (HTHEAs) provide a large compositional space for tuning phase constitution, microstructure, elevated-temperature strength, creep resistance, and oxidation behavior. Their design is difficult for the same reason: performance depends on processing history, microstructure, temperature, loading mode, exposure time, and environment as well as nominal chemistry. Artificial-intelligence (AI) and machine-learning (ML) methods are increasingly used to navigate this coupled space. This structured narrative review is organized around service-relevant high-temperature evidence rather than algorithm families, covering phase and microstructure stability, elevated-temperature strength, creep, oxidation, and the extent to which AI-selected alloys have been experimentally validated under the intended conditions. Evidence is assessed from internal statistical validation and physics-based filtering to alloy synthesis, direct high-temperature testing, extended service-relevant exposure, and iterative experiment–model feedback. Prospective studies now include tests of model-selected refractory high-entropy alloys (RHEAs) at 800–1200 °C, a 149 h creep-rupture validation of an ML-designed high-entropy superalloy (HESA) at 1023 K and 480 MPa, and active-learning campaigns coupled directly to 1000 °C oxidation experiments. Across these examples, the limiting factors are concrete: many records lack exposure time, atmosphere, loading mode, measured composition, or post-test microstructure; compression data still outweigh tensile and creep evidence; and few AI-selected alloys have been followed through long-duration service-relevant tests.

title: From post-editing to prompting
container-title: Translation and Translanguaging in Multilingual Contexts
d424fcf44502667e6a60fc58c426437d6562f9b9.abstract: Abstract This study compares traditional translation and post-editing with generative-AI-assisted translation in Arabic–English translation education. Drawing on 68 task records completed by 58 undergraduate students through EduApp, it examines observable effort, textual intervention, and implications for translation competence. The findings indicate that AI-assisted tasks involved significantly more written or entered characters and a higher length ratio, but no statistically significant difference in task completion time. Qualitative analysis suggests a shift from local correction to broader reformulation, including more formal institutional phrasing and syntactic restructuring. The study concludes that AI-assisted translation redistributes rather than eliminates student effort and requires evaluative and interactive skills alongside established translation abilities.

title: Ethical Implications of Generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) Use Among Library and Information Science (LIS) Students: A Narrative Review
container-title: Education for Information
cfb0b4301f1f8befc86d8ba35dd13d0f98160b83.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence is increasingly being used by students and is reshaping the way information is accessed, processed, and utilised for academic work and everyday purposes. As the use of AI technologies continues to expand, there is a growing need to discuss the ethical implications associated with the use of generative AI among LIS students. This study employed a narrative review method to analyse and synthesise evidence from existing scholarly literature obtained through various library resources and online databases on the Internet. The study identified several ethical implications regarding the use of generative AI among LIS students, which include breaches of academic integrity, plagiarism risks, misinformation, output bias, privacy and security concerns, reduced critical engagement with learning materials, overdependence on AI systems, fabricated references, and so on. The findings revealed that ethical use of generative AI requires LIS students to critically evaluate AI-generated content, acknowledge AI assistance where necessary, and maintain responsibility for the accuracy and originality of their academic work. The study showed areas for future research directions in ethical concerns of generative AI use among LIS students for responsible AI use in academic practices.

title: Application of artificial intelligence in predicting periodontal risks in orthodontic patients: a scoping review
container-title: Frontiers in Oral Health
9f6f3f11b99083169940b4e7af8d7627dbf4660d.abstract: Introduction This scoping review aims to evaluate artificial intelligence (AI), particularly deep learning, for predicting periodontal risks in orthodontic patients and to identify methodological gaps limiting clinical translation. Methods Reported in accordance with PRISMA-ScR and PRISMA-S guidelines, a systematic search was conducted across six electronic databases (PubMed, IEEE Xplore, Web of Science, Scopus, Embase, Cochrane Library), grey literature, and citation tracking (Jan 1, 2018–June 1, 2025). Out of 880 identified records (312 duplicates removed; 568 screened), 56 full texts were evaluated, yielding 3 core clinical CBCT studies meeting strict eligibility criteria (Xu et al., 2024; Pirayesh et al., 2024; Zheng et al., 2025). Methodological quality and risk of bias were appraised using QUADAS-2 and PROBAST. Results Reported performance for orthodontically induced inflammatory root resorption (OIIRR) ranged from 82.1% accuracy in small canine-induced resorption cohorts to &gt;94% accuracy in larger grading frameworks. However, critical appraisal revealed a high risk of bias across all studies due to single-center retrospective designs, lack of independent external validation, and missing calibration metrics. Direct clinical evidence for AI prediction of gingival recession or orthodontic alveolar bone loss was insufficient within strict pre-cutoff parameters. Discussion While AI demonstrates technical feasibility for assessing orthodontically related root resorption risk, robust individual-level risk prediction remains unestablished. Prospective multicenter external validation and adherence to standardized reporting guidelines are required prior to routine clinical adoption.

title: Stepped-Care Internet Cognitive Behaviour Therapy for Childhood and Adolescent Anxiety: Parent Perspectives
container-title: Clinical Child Psychology and Psychiatry
ce2db54e7ae5b390b78d7fa0a535a4714acf6b33.abstract: Objective By exploring parental views, we can better understand how stepped-care models with internet cognitive behavioural therapy (ICBT) interventions are experienced by young people and their families. A qualitative approach was used to understand parents’ perceptions of the acceptability and appropriateness of a stepped-care ICBT intervention. Specifically, what elements were effective, what barriers existed and how treatment expectations could inform adjustments to enhance overall outcomes for young people. Methods Twenty parents of children and adolescents (aged 9-16 years) who completed the BRAVE Stepped-Care randomised controlled trials for anxiety participated in semi-structured interviews informed by Proctor et al.’s implementation science framework. Data were analysed using deductive reflexive thematic analysis. Results Four overarching themes were identified, (1) comfort with stepped-care approach, (2) desire for support that feels personalised, (3) parental involvement perceived as helpful and (4) importance of family flexibility. Conclusions The self-directed component of ICBT was well received, particularly with parental involvement. Parents valued personalised support, especially via videoconferencing, and the flexible stepped-care ICBT approach suited busy family schedules. Finding suggest that stepped-care ICBT can be effectively implemented in routine care when parental engagement and flexible, personalised support are prioritised, potentially improving adherence, outcomes and scalability.

title: Borrowed Grief Projection, Mourning, and the Artificial Screen in Kazuo Ishiguro's Klara and the Sun
container-title: International Journal of Creative and Open Research in Engineering and Management
d71359ee82725c43c1aa39ef3fa176a807bba56f.abstract: Kazuo Ishiguro's Klara and the Sun (2021) has generally been read through the lens of posthumanism, with critics asking what the novel says about artificial minds, consciousness, and the ethical status of machines built to feel (Ajeesh and Rukmini; Sahu and Karmakar). Klara, the Artificial Friend (AF) who narrates the novel, is repeatedly framed by scholarship as a test case for whether a machine can possess genuine interiority, and whether human beings can ever truly know that interiority from the outside (Shang). This paper takes a different approach. Rather than asking what Klara is, it asks what Klara is used for. Read this way, Klara and the Sun is less a novel about artificial intelligence than a novel about human beings who cannot bear to look directly at loss, illness, and death, and who therefore route their most unbearable feelings through a listening, watching, uncomplaining object that will not look away, argue back, or die on its own schedule. Josie's mother, Chrissie, projects her anticipatory grief and her guilt over Josie's genetic "lifting" onto Klara by quietly preparing Klara to become a replacement daughter. Josie herself, isolated by illness from ordinary adolescent life, projects her need for an unthreatening companion onto Klara rather than risk further loss with human friends. Even Rick and the wider adult world around the Arthur family treat AFs as safe vessels for anxieties they will not name directly. Klara, in other words, functions across the novel as a screen: an entity human characters can fill with their own dread of mortality precisely because she seems not to have a mortality, or a claim, of her own.

title: Media Convergence Influence on the Behaviour and Attention Span of Adolescents in Select Secondary Schools in Rivers State
container-title: RESEARCH JOURNAL OF MASS COMMUNICATION AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY
2824e66b073446102846e9703370d3d1335ea910.abstract: The evolution of digital media and the convergence of multiple platforms have profoundly influenced adolescent behaviour and cognitive functioning. This study examined the impact of media convergence on the behaviour and attention span of adolescents in selected secondary schools in Rivers State, Nigeria. Employing a survey research design, data were collected from 330 students across three secondary schools using structured questionnaires and teacher interviews. Findings indicate that 60% of respondents reported high daily exposure to online media, with the majority acknowledging that media use affects focus, reduces study time, and influences classroom behaviour. The results highlight a significant relationship between prolonged media exposure and decreased attention span, increased distractibility, and altered behavioural patterns. The study concludes that while digital media can enhance learning opportunities, excessive exposure poses risks to adolescents’ cognitive development and academic performance. Recommendations include strengthening digital literacy education, implementing screen-time regulations, and promoting balanced media use in schools. The findings provide valuable insights for educators, parents, and policymakers seeking to mitigate the adverse effects of media convergence on adolescents.

title: Artificial intelligence in radiology education: from AI-supported learning to clinical innovation—a narrative review
container-title: Frontiers in Medicine
14bc18448b3e1dd017f9fcc36decfc4878a507b1.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is changing diagnostic radiology, but education and training have not kept pace. This narrative review brings together current evidence on AI-supported learning in radiology education and how such learning can move into clinical innovation. Surveys from different countries point to the same gap: in a 25-country international survey of radiographers, radiologists, and students, only 10.3% had received formal AI training; in one national survey of Turkish residents, 84.5% had received none. The review maps competency frameworks and curriculum models that define AI literacy and support staged integration into residency. It also assesses AI as a teaching tool, including AI-assisted case-based learning, computer-aided diagnosis training, precision-education knowledge recommenders, and virtual, augmented, and extended reality. Controlled and randomized studies show measurable gains: computer-aided diagnosis training raised resident scores above self-study controls (mean score 52 vs. 38 on a 100-point scale), while an AI-based knowledge recommender shortened reporting time by 162 s per case and relative improvement in graded reporting accuracy scores of 14% (95% CI 8.1–19.8%). Large language models are promising but limited: GPT-4 approaches board-style examination performance (80.6%) yet remains poor at image-based reasoning (47.8%). The review closes by considering how education can feed clinical innovation, along with algorithmic and automation bias, ethical governance, and future research needs. AI education should therefore span the full continuum-from undergraduate training to continuing professional development-if radiology is to innovate safely, effectively, and equitably.

title: Research on the Home and Community-Based Elderly Care Service Ecosystem Driven by Digital-Intelligence Empowerment
container-title: EAI Endorsed Transactions on Pervasive Health and Technology
704bfc1033491a719612352f1a08e9b4ac65ac06.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Fragmented demand records, invisible provider capacity, and weak closure verification reduce the responsiveness of home and community-based elderly care. OBJECTIVES: This paper specifies and evaluates a lightweight digital-intelligence workflow system rather than a predictive medical-diagnosis tool. The system links multi-channel demand intake, rule-based priority scoring, provider eligibility filtering, work-order state tracking, delivery verification, exception logging, and feedback closure. The architecture retains a core-provider layer, a beneficiary layer, and a four-module support system, but implements them through minimum data fields, explicit state transitions, and auditable scoring rules. METHODS: An eight-week AB/BA pilot was conducted at two community centers with 42 adults aged 65–82 and 386 valid service requests. RESULTS: Compared with the routine workflow, the supported workflow reduced mean demand-to-confirmation time from 58.4 to 36.9 min and staff coordination time from 8.9 to 6.2 min per request. On-time completion increased from 79.2% to 89.1%, while matching accuracy increased from 83.8% to 91.6%. CONCLUSION: The configuration uses ordinary tablets, office computers, spreadsheet-compatible records, role-based access, and human fallback channels, providing an implementable coordination mechanism for community elderly care.

title: IoT-enabled decision-aided system for remote monitoring of patients towards smart healthcare
container-title: Journal of Ambient Intelligence and Smart Environments
404363c9a693fc824ba15db370662b0c88301d4d.abstract: The rapid growth of Internet of Things (IoT) technologies has significantly transformed smart healthcare systems by enabling continuous monitoring of physiological parameters through wearable devices. However, many existing healthcare monitoring systems rely heavily on cloud-based architectures, which lead to increased network latency, high energy consumption, and limited real-time decision support. This study proposes an IoT-enabled Smart Healthcare Decision-aid System (ISHDS) that integrates a wearable physical sensor node (WPSN), mobile-based Edge AI computing, and cloud-assisted data analysis for efficient real-time health monitoring. The proposed system is designed as a four-layer architecture consisting of a wearable sensing layer, mobile edge processing layer, communication layer, and cloud analytics layer. A prototype WPSN device is developed to continuously monitor multiple physiological parameters, including blood pressure, body temperature, heart rate, blood oxygen saturation ( S p O 2 ) and respiration rate. A pilot experimental study was conducted for 5 consecutive days involving 27 participants aged between 11 and 77 years with a combination of healthy and patients having chronic conditions to evaluate system performance. The primary outcomes included measurement accuracy, system latency, and real-time decision support capability. The collected data were processed using an on-device data fusion approach through a mobile application (Healthy App), which reduces network latency and communication overhead while improving system responsiveness. Experimental results suggest that the proposed framework achieves high accuracy (up to 99.96%) in physiological data analysis; however, this result is preliminary and requires further validation on larger and more diverse populations. These findings indicate that the proposed ISHDS framework offers an efficient and scalable solution for smart healthcare applications by combining wearable sensing, Edge AI-based data processing, and intelligent data fusion. The system shows strong potential for deployment in remote healthcare monitoring and real-time medical decision support environments.

title: Evaluation of Tax Revenue Mobilization on Capital Allocation efficiency in Nigerian Economy: A Systematic Review of 2000 to 2025 Time-Series
container-title: Federal University Gusau Faculty of Education Journal
5de5f0cecf1d3f4826bb4ff6bb6162e9dc86e84e.abstract: This study investigates the empirical impact of tax revenue mobilization on capital allocation efficiency within the Nigerian economy. Against the backdrop of ongoing fiscal reforms and efforts to reduce heavy reliance on volatile oil revenues, understanding how public tax collection influences both public capital expenditure and private sector investment decisions is critical for sustainable national development. Utilizing an econometric framework based on time-series data spanning from 2000 to 2025, the research employs an autoregressive distributed lag (ARDL) technique to analyze the short-run and long-run relationships between disaggregated tax revenues—including petroleum profits tax, company income tax, and value-added tax—and key capital allocation indicators, such as infrastructural spending, gross fixed capital formation, and sectoral credit distribution. The empirical findings reveal that while aggregate tax revenue exerts a positive and statistically significant long-run effect on public capital expenditure, its transmission mechanism to private sector capital allocation is frequently encumbered by structural bottlenecks, high compliance costs, and sub-optimal revenue utilization. Furthermore, the results indicate a crowding-out effect in certain non-oil sectors when tax collection mechanisms become excessively burdensome without corresponding improvements in public infrastructure and the ease of doing business. The study concludes that increasing tax revenue alone is insufficient to drive optimal capital allocation in Nigeria; rather, the efficiency, transparency, and strategic deployment of tax proceeds into high-yielding public capital projects are paramount. Policy recommendations include streamlining tax administration to minimize distortions, expanding the tax net without discouraging productive investments, and strengthening institutional frameworks to ensure tax revenues are channeled transparently into productivity-enhancing infrastructure that crowds in private capital.

title: Health Information-Seeking Behaviour Using Artificial Intelligence Applications in Mobile Phones Among University Undergraduates in Anambra State
container-title: RESEARCH JOURNAL OF MASS COMMUNICATION AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY
f7db1723a347409eb9b88e7013e5f0e75471446a.abstract: Seeking health information is a common practice that helps individuals understand health conditions and manage illnesses. Among young people, this behaviour has increased due to the rapid growth of artificial intelligence (AI) technologies, improved mobile phone capabilities, and widespread internet access. However, despite the speed and convenience AI applications provide, there is a risk of inaccurate or misleading information, especially when users’ health conditions differ from the data on which the AI systems were trained. This study assessed the use of AI applications on mobile phones for health information-seeking among university undergraduates in Anambra State. The main objective was to examine undergraduates’ health information-seeking behaviour in relation to their utilization of AI mobile applications. The study was anchored on the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) and the Diffusion of Innovation theory. A quantitative survey design was adopted, using a structured Likert-scale questionnaire for data collection. From a population of 60,903 students, a sample size of 358 was determined using the Krejcie and Morgan formula. Data were analysed using mean scores, with 3.0 as the decision benchmark: items with mean scores below 3.0 were rejected, while those above 3.0 were accepted. Findings indicated that most respondents use AI applications on their mobile phones to seek health information, largely due to accessibility, convenience, and ease of interaction. The study concludes that although AI health information tools are useful, there is a need for greater caution and guidance regarding the quality of information accessed. It recommends the development and enforcement of stricter regulations on AI health information tools and the implementation of institutional educational programmes to improve students’ understanding of responsible AI use.

title: Artificial Intelligence Adoption and the Financial Performance of Commercial Banks in Kenya
container-title: Journal of Finance and Accounting
cf314b05e9c4ea930939b33d7abec62660e13e55.abstract: Commercial banks in Kenya have invested heavily in artificial intelligence (AI), yet sector profitability has weakened, with average return on assets (ROA) falling from 3.3 percent in 2021 to 2.6 percent in 2024. This research investigated the effect of AI adoption on the financial performance of commercial banks in Kenya. Specifically, it examined the effects of AI-enabled customer service, machine learning credit scoring, robotic process automation and AI-driven fraud detection on financial performance, measured by ROA, as well as the mediating effect of operational efficiency and the moderating effect of bank size. A census of all 38 commercial banks licensed by the Central Bank of Kenya was undertaken, using data from audited annual reports and Central Bank of Kenya supervisory returns. Data were analysed using random effects panel regression with cluster-robust standard errors, the causal steps approach supplemented by the Sobel test, and moderated regression. AI-enabled customer service had a positive and significant effect on ROA (β = 0.927, p = 0.003). Machine learning credit scoring (β = −0.046, p = 0.841), robotic process automation (β = −0.450, p = 0.098) and AI-driven fraud detection (β = 0.137, p = 0.459) had no significant effects. AI-enabled customer service lowered the cost-to-income ratio (β = −0.194, p < 0.001), but operational efficiency did not significantly mediate its relationship with ROA (Sobel z = 1.287, p = 0.198). The interaction between AI adoption and bank size was not significant (β = 0.154, p = 0.589). The study concluded that the effect of AI adoption on bank performance is application-specific. Only customer-facing AI translated into higher profitability, while the credit scoring, process automation and fraud detection applications did not. Operational efficiency did not mediate, and bank size did not moderate, the connection between AI adoption and performance.

title: Delirium and Long-Term Cognitive Trajectories in Cognitively Unimpaired Adults
container-title: JAMA Neurology
decd909bc02f644cbdd6f9a7a856ce27ff3de930.abstract: Importance Delirium is a state of acute confusion characterized by deficits in attention that occurs commonly during hospitalization and is associated with adverse outcomes; however, the association of delirium with longitudinal cognitive trajectories is not fully understood. Objective To evaluate the association of delirium during hospitalization with subsequent development of mild cognitive impairment (MCI), dementia, and longitudinal cognitive trajectories. Design, Setting, and Participants This cohort study used data from participants with hospitalizations in the Mayo Clinic Study of Aging (MCSA) from October 2004 to December 2023. The MCSA is a prospective, population-based longitudinal study of cognitive aging among residents of Olmsted County, Minnesota. Of participants enrolled in the MCSA between 2004 and 2023, individuals who experienced 1 or more hospitalization prior to their last MCSA encounter were included in this study. Participants with dementia at MCSA enrollment or prior to first hospitalization were excluded. Follow-up continued until development of MCI or dementia, last MCSA visit, or the end of the study. Exposure Delirium was identified using a validated natural language processing algorithm applied to clinical notes from hospitalizations, associated emergency department visits, and follow-up within 30 days after hospitalization. Delirium status was modeled as a time-dependent exposure. Main Outcomes and Measures Incident MCI and dementia were assigned through MCSA expert consensus evaluations, including neuropsychological testing performed every 15 months. Association between delirium and development of MCI or dementia was assessed using Cox proportional hazards regression, adjusted for patient age, sex, level of education, and apolipoprotein E (APOE) ε4 allele carrier status; cognitive trajectories were assessed with linear mixed-effects models. Results Of 7030 participants enrolled in the MCSA, 3542 individuals experienced 1 or more hospitalization prior to their last MCSA encounter and were included, and 41 participants with dementia at enrollment or prior to first hospitalization were excluded. The cohort included 3501 participants with at least 1 hospitalization. Median (IQR) age was 74.1 (66.6-80.9) years, 1676 participants (47.9%) were female, median (IQR) level of education was 14 (12-16) years, and 910 participants (26.0%) were APOE ε4 carriers. During a median (IQR) follow-up of 7.2 (4.1-10.4) years, 75 participants (2.1%) had delirium documented within 30 days of hospitalization. Delirium was associated with increased risk of MCI (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR], 3.67; 95% CI, 2.19-6.15) and dementia (aHR, 5.39; 95% CI, 2.94-9.85) and with accelerated decline in longitudinal cognitive testing. Conclusions and Relevance In this cohort study among adults in the MCSA, including those with unimpaired cognition at baseline, delirium during hospitalization was strongly associated with increased risk of MCI and dementia and accelerated cognitive decline in subsequent years.

title: Public Awareness of Artificial Intelligence (AI) Utilisation in Healthcare Institutions in Anambra State
container-title: RESEARCH JOURNAL OF MASS COMMUNICATION AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY
62381fb047bb10071282679fbff11b561b408c75.abstract: Given the growing adoption of AI-driven diagnostic and treatment tools across health systems, understanding community awareness is crucial for effective integration and health communication. Applying the survey design, data were collected from 384 adult residents selected from across six Local Government Areas of Anambra State, Nigeria, using multistage and proportionate sampling techniques. Findings revealed a moderately high level of awareness of AI utilisation, with respondents expressing the strongest familiarity with AI-powered tools such as automated diagnostics and virtual assistants. Social media emerged as the dominant source of AI information, followed by traditional media, while healthcare providers contributed minimally to public knowledge. Respondents also recognised significant benefits of AI, including improved diagnostic accuracy, enhanced service delivery, and overall healthcare quality. However, concerns were evident regarding potential medical errors, privacy concerns, and job displacement of healthcare workers. These findings align with national and international studies showing high exposure but limited depth of understanding among the public and health workers. Guided by the Diffusion of Innovations and Agenda-Setting theories, the study concludes that public awareness is largely media-driven and remains at an early diffusion stage, underscoring the need for deliberate institutional communication, ethical safeguards, and structured public sensitisation. The study recommends strengthening health communication strategies, promoting data protection frameworks, and enhancing healthcare worker involvement in public AI education.

title: Identification and control of potential occupational safety and health hazards of artificial intelligence: a scoping review
container-title: Frontiers in Public Health
0e5a2f0eaf36eb47e1f3757e1b397b070ab5440f.abstract: Introduction Artificial intelligence (AI) offers substantial societal benefits, but it also can pose significant hazards to workers. Methods A scoping literature review was conducted to identify materials published from 2010 to 2025 and indicative of artificial intelligence (AI) hazards to workers. The aim was to answer two research questions: What are the potential occupational safety and health hazards associated with exposure to AI? and What are the approaches that have been proposed to control these hazards in the workplace? Results Eight databases and grey literature were searched. These yielded 25,925 studies, which after screening resulted in 622 studies for full text review. Of these, 216 were eligible for data extraction. These studies substantiated 14 categories of potential hazards to workers from AI. These categories included: threats of physical trauma; dehumanization of workers; threats to human agency, autonomy, and workers’ voice; loss of human and workplace connection; threats to sense of self and identity; threats of increased stress, fatigue, and work-life imbalance from work intensification; dependence on AI, leading to deterioration of skills; potential exacerbation of OSH inequities in the workplace; threats of weakening the psychological contract, worker engagement, and trust; threats of job loss, unemployment, disruption of labor market, and reduced economic mobility; threats of underpaid, precarious, and hidden work; threats of cyberphysical attacks and bullying; inappropriate worker monitoring, surveillance, management, and selection; and threats of adverse consequences of worker cognitive and physical augmentation and enhancement. Control approaches also were identified for each hazard category. Discussion This study provides a comprehensive appraisal of AI-related potential OSH hazards and controls and offers a foundation for future research and practice.

title: Effects of mind-body exercise on cognitive function in patients with mild cognitive impairment: A systematic review and network meta-analysis
container-title: Aging Clinical and Experimental Research
5b05d6a64bd0c6e2cd23823b3dc1488ed254c4c6.abstract: Abstract Objective This investigation carried out a systematic review and network meta-analysis to assess how different forms of mind–body exercise influence overall cognitive performance in patients with MCI. Methods A systematic search was conducted across eight Chinese and English databases (up to April 2026). A frequency-based network meta-analysis was performed to estimate the standardized mean differences and 95% confidence intervals, with interventions ranked by SUCRA values. Results A total of 44 RCTs (3,189 patients with MCI) were included. The network meta-analysis showed that, for the MoCA outcome, Baduanjin, Tai Chi, Qigong, and dance were all significantly superior to the control group ( p < 0.05). For the MMSE outcome, all three exercise types except Qigong were significantly superior to the control group. SUCRA rankings indicated that Baduanjin ranked first for both the MoCA (91.6%) and MMSE (88.3%). Subgroup analyses suggested that Baduanjin was most effective for short-term (≤ 12 weeks), high-frequency (> 3 times/week), or short-duration (< 60 min) interventions, while Tai Chi was more effective for long-term (> 12 weeks), low-frequency (≤ 3 times/week), or long-duration (≥ 60 min) interventions. The sensitivity analysis results were robust, and the risk of publication bias was low; however, the certainty of the evidence was generally low. Conclusion Baduanjin, Tai Chi, dance, and Qigong may be beneficial for global cognition in individuals with MCI. Baduanjin ranked highest in the SUCRA analysis. Tai Chi showed a potential advantage in longer-duration interventions. Given the low certainty of evidence and reliance on indirect comparisons, these findings should be interpreted cautiously.

title: Sharia financial technology organizations and ethical responsibility for sustainable development: a moral economy perspective
container-title: International Journal of Ethics and Systems
7cac2d554e46b14a1112259e731e116bf16d9922.abstract: Purpose This paper aims to examine whether the ethical responsibility of Sharia financial technology (Sharia fintech) can be normatively justified rather than assumed on the basis of its religious identity or developmental claims. Design/methodology/approach This study uses a normative–conceptual ethical analysis that evaluates Sharia fintech as a morally accountable financial system using two normative benchmarks: the objectives of Sharia (maqasid al-Sharia) and the ethical vision embedded in the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). Findings The analysis develops a conceptual evaluation framework structured around four ethical tension fields: inclusion versus digital exclusion, social objectives versus profit orientation, technological efficiency versus data ethics and accountability and sustainability commitments versus symbolic alignment. These tensions show that ethical legitimacy in Sharia fintech is neither inherent nor guaranteed by formal compliance, but conditionally achieved through continuous moral negotiation between innovation, market pressures and social responsibility. Research limitations/implications This study is conceptual in nature and does not empirically assess specific fintech platforms or governance practices. Future research may operationalise the proposed framework through qualitative case studies or institutional analysis to examine how Sharia fintech organisations manage the identified ethical tensions in practice. Practical implications The proposed framework provides regulators, Sharia supervisory boards and fintech governance bodies with a structured ethical lens for evaluating Sharia fintech beyond formal compliance. It highlights the need to institutionalise accountability mechanisms in areas such as data governance, inclusion strategies and sustainability alignment within digitally mediated Sharia finance. Originality/value Rather than treating Sharia compliance or alignment with the SDGs as proxies for ethical legitimacy, this study develops a normative framework that evaluates where such claims become contested. The framework combines maqasid al-Sharia and the SDGs as complementary normative reference points and identifies four ethical tension fields through which the legitimacy of Sharia fintech can be critically assessed.

title: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE FOR STRATEGIC DECISION-MAKING: IMPLICATIONS FOR THE TRANSFORMATION OF BUSINESS MANAGEMENT
container-title: International Journal of African Development and Sustainable Research
eb30aafd0f6da9dd1f0e1fc259ee691e1dc8a240.abstract: In today’s rapidly evolving business environment, Artificial Intelligence (AI) has become a transformative technological capability with profound implications for strategic decision-making and modern business management. The growing ability of AI systems to analyse extensive volumes of structured and unstructured data, detect intricate patterns, produce predictive insights, and automate analytical activities is reshaping the processes through which organisations formulate and implement strategic decisions. Through the review of recent literature and real-world case studies, this paper critically argues that AI is fundamentally reshaping strategic decision-making and presents a reasoned perspective on how this shift is transforming business management practices and competitive strategies in contemporary organisations. This study also explores the challenges and risks of AI-driven strategic decision-making. The study concludes that the greatest value of AI lies in its capacity to augment rather than replace managerial intelligence. Hence, the study recommends that organisations should adopt hybrid decision-making by combining AI-generated insights with human expertise to enhance decision accuracy, critical thinking, and strategic judgement.

title: Teachers’ basic psychological need satisfactions and their intentions to use generative artificial intelligence: the mediating role of engagement in professional development
container-title: Frontiers in Psychology
21f4814308b95f9a8b6d35b1286fd353e5f5bb75.abstract: Introduction Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) offers new opportunities for instructional innovation, yet the psychological mechanisms underlying teachers’ intentions to adopt it remain unclear. Intrinsic motivation is an important internal factor shaping teachers’ intentions to use GenAI and is closely linked to the satisfaction of their basic psychological needs. Drawing on self-determination theory (SDT), this study develops and tests a theoretical framework linking teachers’ basic psychological need satisfaction to their intention to use GenAI through intrinsic motivation and engagement in professional development. Such engagement may foster innovation in GenAI-supported teaching practices. Methods Survey data were collected from 146 teachers participating in a GenAI learning program. Structural equation modeling was used to examine the hypothesized relationships among basic psychological need satisfaction, intrinsic motivation, engagement in professional development, and intention to use GenAI. Results Perceived competence in using GenAI was significantly and positively associated with intrinsic motivation, whereas perceived autonomy and relatedness were not significantly associated with intrinsic motivation. Engagement in professional development mediated the relationship between intrinsic motivation and intention to use GenAI. Discussion These findings provide a nuanced understanding of the psychological mechanisms underlying teachers’ intentions to adopt GenAI, highlighting the roles of perceived competence, intrinsic motivation, and engagement in professional development. They also offer practical implications for supporting the integration of GenAI into teaching.

title: Emerging Artificial Intelligence Applications in Capture Fisheries Monitoring and Assessment: A Bibliometric and Synthesis Review
container-title: New Zealand Journal of Marine and Freshwater Research
f56ce178a38e90dfdb4575d112e4423f7b321178.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly used to monitor and assess capture fisheries, addressing persistent limitations of conventional observation systems that are labor‐intensive, costly, and difficult to scale. Despite rapid technological expansion, AI development in this field remains fragmented, limiting a comprehensive understanding of its structure and direction. This study aimed to map the development, intellectual structure, and thematic evolution of AI research in capture fisheries monitoring and assessment through a bibliometric and synthesis‐based review of Scopus‐indexed literature (2015–2026). Following a documented, large language model‐assisted screening protocol with human verification, a final corpus of 495 journal articles was analyzed using an integrated bibliometric and science‐mapping workflow. Results showed a marked, near‐exponential increase in publication output after 2020. Rather than confirming a pre‐defined three‐domain structure, keyword co‐occurrence analysis revealed that the field's thematic organization follows technical task type (detection, classification, and operational/vessel management) more closely than application domain, with acoustic AI failing to form an independent thematic cluster and representing the smallest share of the corpus (8.1%), behind visual AI (44.0%) and vessel monitoring (28.9%). For synthesis, we nonetheless compare the field across three functional categories visual AI for fish detection and measurement, vessel monitoring using AIS/VMS data, and acoustic survey support finding that the field is methodologically converging around a shared AI/ML toolkit while remaining largely siloed at the technical‐application level. Although research productivity remains heavily concentrated in China (85.9% of records) and international collaboration is limited (23.64%), the field is moving beyond isolated proof‐of‐concept studies toward more operational, management‐relevant applications. Overall, this study provides an evidence‐grounded, rather than assumed, understanding of how AI research in capture fisheries is thematically structured, and identifies acoustic AI and cross‐domain integration as priority areas for future development toward fisheries‐oriented, evidence‐based management.

title: The origins and development of the National Flood Insurance Program
container-title: Journal of Political Institutions and Political Economy
5e22bb1af14205f045fe5401b40eaee2e10bc6bf.abstract: We explore the emergence and development of federal flood insurance over time. After a couple of false starts in the 1950s, Congress passed the National Flood Insurance Act of 1968, which established the National Flood Insurance Program (NFIP). The NFIP sought to provide federally subsidized flood insurance in high-risk flood zones, with premium inflows intended to cover claims-payment outflows. While the NFIP struggled financially through the early 21st century, its fragile administrative structure was laid bare by Hurricanes Katrina and Rita. Beginning in 2005, claims payments drove the NFIP deeply into the red. After several years of politicking, Congress acted to reform the NFIP by reducing the subsidization of premiums and making the program more actuarially sound. But members backpedaled quickly after homeowners organized and threatened electoral sanctions – and the reforms were largely undone. We find that the polarization inherent in today’s party system makes coordinating on flood insurance reform difficult, as Democrats and Republicans advocate for different things. That said, members from districts/states that have been hit hard by flooding, regardless of party, tend toward maintaining federally subsidized premiums rather than promoting actuarial soundness.

title: Autonomy and the Lawyer’s Role
container-title: Amicus Curiae
2dff32b19d56e127ad532c4abf656022687ae850.abstract: This note examines the tension between autonomy and protection in adult social care law and practice. Drawing on the authors’ experiences and the legal frameworks governing care, support and mental capacity, it explores how efforts to promote welfare and manage risk may restrict autonomy and liberty. Particular attention is given to the role of local government lawyers in advising social work professionals on the legality, necessity and proportionality of interventions, and in shaping applications before the Court of Protection and under the High Court’s inherent jurisdiction. It argues that meaningful person-centred practice requires critical reflection of the exercise of power when balancing risk, protection and individual choice. Keywords: adult social care; Mental Capacity Act 2005; Care Act 2014; Court of Protection; inherent jurisdiction; safeguarding; autonomy; deprivation of liberty; fluctuating capacity; local authority lawyers.

title: Law and Human Intelligence(s)
container-title: Amicus Curiae
8d7a2c14cafbfab2521b391a44680b812e84959c.abstract: This essay undertakes a comparison between human intelligence and artificial intelligence (AI) in the legal field, arguing that the first possesses cognitive, epistemological, emotional and affective abilities that are crucial for jurists and that the second could never learn. Taking Carrie Menkel-Meadow’s teachings as the polestar, the essay will identify those fundamental abilities, analyse the features and limits of AI that make this latter incapable of learning such abilities, and finally make some suggestions on how we should develop the abilities at issue to lay down the foundations of a possible “Human Intelligence Project”. Keywords: human intelligence; artificial intelligence; legal professions; legal education; negotiation studies; legal skills; legal culture; nature of the law; conflict; dispute resolution.
