title: Beyond cognitive ability, investigating the symmetrical and asymmetrical pathways of emotional and spiritual intelligence on academic achievement in higher education
container-title: Discover Education
8bd2627003c378bdc46f5dc2fbf48213ed81dfe3.abstract: Abstract Higher education is typically explained in terms of cognitive ability (IQ) when linked to academic achievement. However, despite evidence of non-cognitive intelligence, specifically emotional and spiritual intelligence, its association with academic achievement remains underexplored. In Ghana, where spiritual orientation is strong, research on the relationship between emotional and spiritual intelligence and academic achievement among higher education students remains limited. This study used Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling (PLS-SEM) and Fuzzy-set Qualitative Comparative Analysis (FsQCA) to assess symmetrical and asymmetrical pathways. The study used a quantitative cross-sectional correlation design, drawing on data from 339 students across six colleges at Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KNUST). PLS-SEM shows that emotional intelligence is significantly related to academic achievement (β = 0.344, p < .001) and spiritual intelligence (β = 0.661, p < .001). Spiritual intelligence is associated with academic achievement (β = 0.371, p < .001). The model explains 43. 4% of the variance in academic achievement. The FsQCA results showed that a single configuration was consistently associated with high academic achievement. The combined presence of both high emotional intelligence and spiritual intelligence had a consistency of 0.825 and a coverage of 0.766. Configurations in which one intelligence was high showed high consistency but low PRI consistency, so they were associated with both high and low achievement. The same findings appear in the robustness analysis. Therefore, emotional intelligence and spiritual intelligence appear to relate to achievement conjecturally, as co-occurring resources rather than independent or compensatory routes. The findings call for Ghanaian evidence on the multidimensionality of intelligence and show the value of integrating PLS-SEM and FsQCA to inform educational research.

title: DWSA: Dynamic-Weighting and Self-Attention Intelligent Framework Enables High-Sensitivity SERS Discrimination of Ultratrace Volatile Organic Compounds
container-title: Analytical Chemistry
26c3afe71d69c9e34655832cc31d09b5f4e8833a.abstract: Abstract Real-time on-site discrimination of ultratrace volatile organic compounds (VOCs) via surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) is fundamentally challenged by spectral complexity and the limited generalization of single models. Here, we develop a high-performance 3D porous material (PM) based on biopolymer-silver nanocomposites, providing a reliable platform for trace gas enrichment and signal enhancement. Moving beyond material optimization, we pioneer a novel dynamic-weighting and self-attention intelligent framework (DWSA) to integrate convolutional neural network (CNN)-based global feature extraction with k-nearest neighbors (KNN)-based local similarity reasoning. The hybrid algorithm overcomes the bottlenecks of traditional static ensemble methods; its core innovation lies in a confidence-driven dynamic weighting strategy, which adaptively balances the contributions of both models based on prediction reliability rather than fixed ratios. This underlying mechanism is augmented by a self-attention module that adaptively recalibrates feature weights to focus on key molecular vibrational fingerprints, effectively filtering noise and enhancing interpretability. Based on this hybrid framework, we propose a detection strategy with potential for portable SERS applications, featuring rapid spectral acquisition, intelligent identification, and QR-code-based traceability. This study promotes the practical application of SERS technology in on-site environmental monitoring by integrating ultra-high gas adsorption efficiency with the development of a novel intelligent algorithm.

ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE AS SUPPORT FOR TEACHING AND LEARNING IN EARLY YEARS OF ELEMENTARY SCHOOL
LA INTELIGENCIA ARTIFICIAL COMO APOYO A LA ENSEÑANZA Y EL APRENDIZAJE EN LA EDUCACIÓN PRIMARIA AÑOS INICIALES
container-title: Revista de Geopolítica
f5ea455241f5a833adb22237cbc67dbbd6ea5e58.abstract: Antes mesmo de dispor de diretrizes homologadas, a escola brasileira dos anos iniciais do ensino fundamental já convive com a inteligência artificial: em 2024, 35% dos professores dessa etapa utilizavam ferramentas de IA generativa na preparação de conteúdos didáticos, ante apenas 15% dos alunos de 4º e 5º ano, a única inversão desse tipo em toda a educação básica. Este artigo examina de que modo a inteligência artificial pode apoiar o ensino e a aprendizagem nos anos iniciais e sob quais condições pedagógicas e normativas esse apoio se legitima. Trata-se de pesquisa qualitativa, de caráter documental e bibliográfico, orientada pelos procedimentos da revisão integrativa, com fontes normativas oficiais, microdados e relatórios de pesquisas nacionais e internacionais (TIC Educação 2024, Censo Escolar, Indicador Criança Alfabetizada, TALIS 2024, Unesco) e literatura recente. Os resultados indicam convergência entre o dado empírico e o marco regulatório em consolidação: o Parecer CNE/CP nº 15/2026, aprovado em setembro de 2026 e pendente de homologação ministerial, admite a IA nos anos iniciais exclusivamente em atividades planejadas e mediadas por profissionais da educação, vedando o acesso autônomo das crianças e a interação com sistemas generativos ou conversacionais mesmo sob supervisão. Nessa etapa, portanto, a IA configura-se como tecnologia do professor: apoia diretamente o ensino (planejamento, diferenciação, materiais, avaliação formativa) e só apoia a aprendizagem de modo indireto, pela mediação docente. O estudo propõe uma matriz de aplicações mediadas com salvaguardas e identifica o gargalo decisivo: a formação docente, apontada como dificultador por 77% dos professores, em um cenário de desigualdade persistente de infraestrutura entre redes e territórios.

title: Effectiveness and Limitations of Machine Learning for Predicting Lower Atmosphere Temperature Profiles
container-title: Artificial Intelligence for the Earth Systems
71edbafe437f8b7658212cb81a705dd3146e4738.abstract: Abstract Temperature profiles in the lower atmosphere rapidly evolve during the morning transition, and predicting their details over complex urban environments is particularly important for pollutant dispersal. Temperature profiles can be predicted by operational weather models but are sensitive to model parameterizations. Machine learning models can be used, but require high-resolution profiles that are often unavailable. To overcome this, pre-dawn temperature and wind speed observations from aircraft over Dallas-Fort Worth, TX are used to predict the morning transition. Initially, only temperature is used as an input to assess several types and configurations of machine learning models. Each model’s prediction is evaluated based on various methods because standard metrics, such as mean square error (MSE), may be minimized but miss important features, such as strong temperature gradients. A long short-term memory network with an AdamW optimizer does not result in the lowest MSE but does better capturing the temperature structure. The model tends toward the annual mean by underestimating the onset of mixing and near-surface temperature in summer and overestimating these in the winter. Including wind speed does not have a statistically significant improvement in MSE but performs better sequentially and with the inversion at the top of the boundary layer. Further refinements are likely to improve rapidly updated short-term forecasts, which may provide an additional forecast tool, but large gradients, extreme means, and external forcing remain an inherent challenge. These results highlight the importance of holistic evaluation of machine learning techniques to ensure adequate representation of predicted temperature profiles.

title: EXPOSIÇÃO ÀS TELAS NA INFÂNCIA: REPERCUSSÕES NO DESENVOLVIMENTO COGNITIVO, EMOCIONAL E COMPORTAMENTAL

738ea4e749ccdac5bf207a2ab0443b7dc9cae2cf.abstract: Em 13 de janeiro de 2025, o Brasil sancionou a Lei nº 15.100, que proíbe o uso de aparelhos eletrônicos portáteis pessoais por estudantes durante aulas, recreio e intervalos em toda a educação básica, declarando como objetivo salvaguardar a saúde mental, física e psíquica de crianças e adolescentes. O artigo examina a natureza da evidência disponível sobre os três domínios de desenvolvimento invocados por essa premissa. A pesquisa foi conduzida na base Europe PMC, restrita a título e resumo, sobre registros indexados até 26 de setembro de 2026, com classificação de delineamento por tipo de publicação indexado. Foram identificados 4.934 registros que associam exposição a telas e infância. O domínio emocional reúne 931 registros, o cognitivo 792 e o comportamental 287. A assimetria entre delineamentos é acentuada e desigual entre os domínios: a razão entre estudos transversais e ensaios randomizados é de 5,5 para 1 no domínio cognitivo, de 17,5 para 1 no comportamental e de 20,2 para 1 no emocional, domínio que reúne apenas 13 ensaios randomizados em toda a literatura indexada. A participação dos ensaios randomizados caiu de 10,8% dos registros de 2015 para 2,4% em 2025, enquanto o volume anual quadruplicou. Conclui-se que a premissa legislada apoia-se em um corpo de evidência predominantemente observacional, escassez que decorre em parte de limitações éticas intrínsecas ao objeto.

title: Decision-Making Amid Information-Based Threats in Sociotechnical Systems: A Review
container-title: Journal of Cognitive Engineering and Decision Making
f7e372db0709368f0b1565c58d708c269d3a00b0.abstract: Technological systems increasingly mediate human information exchange, spanning interactions among humans as well as between humans and artificial agents. The unprecedented scale of, and reliance on, information disseminated through these systems substantially expand the scope of information-based influence that can both enable and undermine sound decision-making. Consequently, understanding and protecting decision-making today faces growing challenges, as individuals and organizations must navigate evolving opportunities and information-based threats across domains and information environments. While these risks are widely recognized, research remains fragmented: work evaluating information-based threat phenomena has progressed largely in isolation from foundational studies of human information processing. In this review, we synthesize insights from both domains to identify shared cognitive mechanisms that mediate vulnerability to information-based threats and shape behavioral outcomes. We then present a multilevel conceptual framework and outline directions for future research aimed at integrating these perspectives, emphasizing the importance of mitigating human vulnerabilities and aligning human-machine representations.

title: Reconstructing Core Competencies of Front-Office Employees in South Korean Professional Sports Organizations in the Era of Artificial Intelligence: A Delphi Study
container-title: Behavioral Sciences
a54fabd68a3b380334918c26f659d33b831babb9.abstract: As artificial intelligence (AI) increasingly reshapes organizational decision-making, fan engagement, and business operations, the competencies expected of front-office employees are also evolving. This study aimed to reconstruct the core competencies required of front-office employees in South Korean professional sports organizations in the AI era. To this end, a three-round Delphi study was conducted with 20 experts from academia, South Korean professional sports organizations, and research institutes. The Delphi process involved generating competency items, evaluating their relevance, and establishing expert consensus regarding the final competency framework. The findings identified 28 competency items grouped into the following five competency domains: Data & AI Utilization Competency, Human–AI Collaboration Competency, Marketing & Fan Engagement Competency, Communication & Execution Competency, and Ethics & Values Competency. These findings suggest that competencies in AI-enabled professional sports organizations extend beyond technical proficiency and warrant an integrated combination of technological, collaborative, organizational, relational, and ethical capabilities. This study refines the application of competency theory to AI-supported work by providing a context-specific framework for front-office employees in South Korean professional sports organizations. The proposed framework offers a foundation for understanding how South Korean professional sports organizations may reconstruct workforce competencies in response to the evolving demands of the AI era.

title: Disaster Exposure and Early Self-Reported Posttraumatic Growth: Indirect Associations Through Cognitive Emotion Regulation and Moderation by Dark Triad Traits
container-title: Behavioral Sciences
7553839e402798acbe66405d35048d85716a9ff7.abstract: Associations between disaster exposure and posttraumatic growth (PTG) are inconsistent, highlighting the potential relevance of cognitive processing and personality differences. This study surveyed 1498 individuals within one week of the July 2021 Henan floods to examine the associations among disaster exposure, early self-reported PTG, cognitive emotion regulation (CER), and Dark Triad traits. Disaster exposure showed a small positive association with PTG in the unadjusted model (b = 0.324, p < 0.001), which became nonsignificant after adjusting for gender, age, and current location (b = 0.146, p = 0.139). In the unadjusted parallel indirect-association model, disaster exposure showed positive indirect associations with PTG through both adaptive CER (estimate = 0.079, 95% CI [0.031, 0.144]) and maladaptive CER (estimate = 0.166, 95% CI [0.083, 0.256]), whereas the direct association was nonsignificant. After adjustment, only the indirect association through maladaptive CER remained distinguishable from zero. Dark Triad traits moderated several component associations, but only the conditional indirect association through adaptive CER differed across Dark Triad levels. Early perceived PTG was more closely associated with patterns of cognitive emotion regulation and personality differences than with disaster exposure severity alone. However, the cross-sectional design precludes temporal or causal interpretations, underscoring the need to distinguish early perceptions of growth from enduring psychological adaptation.

title: Bioactive Coatings and Engineered Settlement Interfaces for Artificial Coral Reefs: A Systematic Review of Advances, Challenges, and Future Perspectives
container-title: Journal of Marine Science and Engineering
3e1024e80f403c437cc89cd8de13a4c47f5d4fe2.abstract: The use of concrete in artificial reefs presents a “recruitment paradox”: its inherent hyperalkalinity and delayed natural neutralization severely impair coral larval settlement. Functional surface coatings can mitigate this cytotoxicity and actively provide biological settlement cues. Following PRISMA 2020 guidelines, this systematic review evaluates 16 years of experimental evidence on cementitious surface modifications across Web of Science, Scopus, and ScienceDirect up to September 2026. From 6436 screened records, 127 studies were assessed for full-text eligibility, with a strictly filtered subset of 12 experimental studies included for quantitative data extraction. To systematically categorize these technologies, we propose a novel dual classification framework mapping engineered interfaces by restoration approach (Classes I–IV) and Interfacial Activity Mode (A0–A4). The review evaluates relationships between coating architecture, bio-interfacial stability, and biological performance, identifying current technological bottlenecks. Addressing the need for scalable solutions, we propose a research roadmap integrating circular bioeconomy models and green biomaterials. Methodological quality was assessed by requiring biological validation of coatings in realistic larval settlement models, excluding purely theoretical material simulations. This systematic review was not prospectively registered. Ultimately, this materials-oriented framework clarifies bio-interfacial interactions and identifies research priorities for developing durable, biologically compatible substrates for coral reef restoration.

title: Real-Time Instance Segmentation of Deep-Sea Polymetallic Nodules with Wavelet Statistical Cross-Attention and Reverse Convolution Upsampling
container-title: Journal of Marine Science and Engineering
fe4a4341c1b3a3d1d20721c28254fedb09a3f7a3.abstract: Deep-sea polymetallic nodules are vital strategic mineral resources. However, residual low-contrast features from complex seabed conditions, densely overlapped targets and severe seabed clutter greatly degrade the accuracy and real-time performance of automatic segmentation. This paper proposes a lightweight instance segmentation model, PWC-YOLO. Firstly, a partial convolution-based C3k2-PConv module is constructed to reduce computational cost. Secondly, Wavelet Statistical Cross-Attention (WSCA) replaces the built-in self-attention of C2PSA to suppress underwater noise and enhance the feature expression of tiny nodules. Thirdly, Converse2D reverse convolution upsampling recovers lost contour details of nodules. A manually annotated dataset of Clarion–Clipperton Zone nodules is established for evaluation. Ablation experiments validate that the PWC-YOLO model reaches 95.2% BBox mAP50 and 95.8% Mask mAP50, with only 2.47 M parameters and 9.3 GFLOPs at an inference speed of 88 FPS. Comparative experiments indicate that PWC-YOLO achieves competitive mask segmentation accuracy with fewer parameters and lower computational overhead, yielding a favorable accuracy–complexity trade-off against mainstream segmentation models. Visual results verify favorable robustness within the tested deep-sea scenes, showing favorable lightweight properties with only 2.47 M parameters and 9.3 GFLOPs, which provides potential prerequisites for future lightweight deployment on underwater edge computing devices.

title: Artificial Intelligence and Green Water-Use Efficiency in China: Provincial Evidence from 2011–2024
container-title: Sustainability
a6b3bd62317fadf9761e8c3281d64ac53639f48b.abstract: Whether artificial intelligence (AI) alleviates or aggravates resource constraints is an open and increasingly consequential question: AI carries a substantial energy and water footprint, yet it may also raise resource-use efficiency through prediction, intelligent optimization, and better allocation. Using a balanced panel of 30 Chinese provinces over 2011–2024, this study measures green water-use efficiency (GWUE) with a Super-SBM model and estimates the association between AI development and GWUE using two-way fixed effects, complemented by an instrumental-variable strategy and interpretable machine learning. We find that AI development is associated with a significant improvement in GWUE: a one-standard-deviation increase in the AI index corresponds to a 3.8% rise in GWUE. The relationship is consistent with two channels—green technological innovation and environmental-governance capacity. The association is stronger where per-capita water use is higher, and differs across regions of differing industrial water dependence and computing infrastructure. XGBoost–SHAP analysis further suggests a nonlinear transition around an AI development level of approximately 0.12, beyond which AI’s marginal contribution to predicted GWUE becomes increasingly positive. These findings indicate that AI does not automatically become a green technology; its resource-efficiency dividend depends on the resource and technological environment in which it is deployed.

title: Task-Specific Impacts of Cognitive Fatigue on Subjective Experience and Psychomotor Performance
container-title: Human Factors: The Journal of the Human Factors and Ergonomics Society
522c0265a8e374ae7e4e7c27de993e0dcbdc142a.abstract: Objective To determine how cognitive fatigue (CF) affects subjective experience and reaction time (RT) performance across tasks with different processing demands (simple, go/no-go, choice), and whether these effects depend on the type of fatigue-inducing mental work. Background CF is a psychobiological state of subjective exhaustion from mental effort that can compromise workplace productivity and safety. Although slowed RT is an often-observed consequence of CF, it is unclear how this compares across RT paradigms and fatigue-inducing tasks. Method Using a remotely administered experiment, 402 participants completed a 60-minute CF (Math-Memory, Stroop, Time Load Dual-Back) or control (documentary) intervention. Subjective ratings (mental fatigue, motivation) and RT performance (simple, go/no-go, choice) were assessed pre- and post-intervention. Results Relative to control, all CF tasks increased subjective fatigue ( p < .001), while motivation declined following Dual-Back and Stroop ( p ≤ .030) but not Math-Memory. Simple and choice RT slowed significantly following all CF interventions vs control ( p < .010), with the greatest choice RT slowing after Stroop ( p ≤ .032). Only Stroop produced significant go/no-go RT slowing ( p = .004). Conclusion Subjective fatigue and simple RT were broadly sensitive to CF, indicating general psychomotor slowing. Conversely, motivation and higher-complexity RT measures showed task-specific effects, perhaps reflecting overlap between fatigue-inducing and RT task demands. Application Task type is important when considering RT as a fatigue assessment tool. These findings support multidimensional (subjective and RT) CF assessments and indicate that simple RT may be effective for rapid, broad fatigue monitoring, whereas complex RT metrics may be useful when exploring task-specific executive processing effects.

title: RECRUTAMENTO COM INTELIGÊNCIA ARTIFICIAL: CRITÉRIOS DE AUDITORIA PARA IDENTIFICAR EXCLUSÕES INDEVIDAS DE CANDIDATOS
ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE SYSTEMS SCREEN RESUMES AND ELIMINATE APPLICATIONS BEFORE ANY HUMAN CONTACT
RECLUTAMIENTO CON INTELIGENCIA ARTIFICIAL: CRITERIOS DE AUDITORÍA PARA IDENTIFICAR EXCLUSIONES INDEBIDAS DE CANDIDATOS
container-title: Revista de Geopolítica
4f6bb673cad690867b801e6d18a313e193647caf.abstract: Sistemas de inteligência artificial triam currículos e eliminam candidaturas antes de qualquer contato humano. O candidato excluído por esse mecanismo raramente sabe que foi avaliado por uma máquina e quase nunca dispõe de instrumento para contestar o resultado. Este artigo examina duas camadas do problema e propõe critérios operacionais de auditoria. A camada normativa consiste no exame do texto integral da Lei nº 13.709/2018 e da Lei nº 13.853/2019, obtidas no repositório oficial de legislação do Senado Federal, e na verificação da tramitação do projeto de marco legal da inteligência artificial junto à base de dados abertos da Câmara dos Deputados. A camada bibliométrica consiste no levantamento de dois corpora na base Europe PMC, com todas as consultas restritas aos campos de título e resumo. O exame normativo revela que a redação original garantia revisão de decisão automatizada por pessoa natural e que a expressão foi suprimida em 2019, que a palavra auditoria ocorre uma única vez na lei, em dispositivo condicionado à recusa de informação por segredo comercial e de exercício discricionário pela autoridade nacional, e que oito expressões do vocabulário do trabalho não ocorrem nenhuma vez. O exame bibliométrico revela que o corpus de auditoria algorítmica é majoritariamente médico, com 65,8% dos registros, e que os dois corpora compartilham um único registro. Propõem-se sete critérios de auditoria transpostos da prática médica para o recrutamento.

title: AgriEvoKG: Empirical Failure Modes and Remedies in LLM-Based Cross-Media Agricultural Knowledge Graph Construction
container-title: ICCK Transactions on Emerging Topics in Artificial Intelligence
5a42db703618703be95f83faa6cf423f8d92e735.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) make it possible to build knowledge graphs from professional literature at scale, but how such graphs fail at that scale is rarely measured. We built \sys{}, a cross-media knowledge graph of swine, aquaculture, tomato, maize and rice production, and analysed its 199,418 entities and 277,053 relations together with the web system that serves it. An LLM extracted typed triples from the professional literature of each sector; 74.9% of the relations carry an evidence record of document, page and excerpt, and a multimodal embedding model links 25,158 entities to images and 14,132 to video clips. We identified five failure modes of construction. First, the sector schemas diverged: the two sectors with free relation labels hold 23,727 and 19,139 distinct labels. Second, in three sectors most numeric facts lost the name of the measured quantity or object, because 85.4% to 98.0% of their value triples use a generic relation. Third, evidence anchoring was asymmetric: the LLM copied 87.5% of the values verbatim from their excerpts but only 38.7% of the head entities. Fourth, exact-name fusion merged 6,805 entity names across sectors but only 7 relations, and about half of the cross-sector relations touch value-like names. Fifth, media links concentrated on hub items: 104 of 15,314 media items held 71.6% of the links. On the deployed system, 62.5% of the relations added from 50 new passages used new relation types, and in a case study on 100 photographs graph context confirmed the model's initial identification rather than correcting it. We organise these findings into a taxonomy that pairs each failure mode with its root cause, a remedy and a test, and argue that most of them cannot be seen in the small samples on which construction methods are usually judged.

title: Toward Artificial Intelligence–Supported Development of Image-Based Tasks in Aphasia
container-title: American Journal of Speech-Language Pathology
ba6ad144f098a157b9ae0b01ca2b72c45041b0a8.abstract: Purpose: Images play a central role in language assessment and therapy for people with aphasia, yet the development of psychometrically robust image stimuli is often time consuming, costly, and difficult to tailor to specific research questions or individual patient needs. Recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI), particularly text-to-image generation models, offer new opportunities to rapidly produce high-quality, customizable visual stimuli. Despite this potential, methodological guidance for integrating AI-generated images into aphasia research and clinical practice remains limited. This tutorial aimed to provide practical recommendations for the use of AI text-to-image tools in developing image-based tasks for people with aphasia. Method: Using a case study framework, we demonstrate the development of a semantic judgment task with images generated with the help of the DALL-E 3 model. We outline key decision points that went into this process and provide recommendations across the major stages of task development: task conceptualization, stimulus design, image ideation, prompt engineering, and image quality evaluation by AI models. Results: We demonstrate that structured prompt engineering combined with systematic validation can yield high-quality, interpretable image stimuli suitable for aphasia tasks. The approach allows for flexible control over stimulus characteristics while maintaining consistency across experimental conditions. Conclusions: AI text-to-image generation offers a promising, scalable approach to developing customized image stimuli for aphasia research and clinical practice. We discuss methodological considerations, limitations, and future directions for the responsible integration of generative AI technologies into aphasia-related research and clinical applications.

title: Cognitive Digital Ocean: integration of quantum hybrid computing, digital twins and graph neural networks for bioresource and fleet management. Part 2
container-title: Fisheries
c40dddc14b2325b2b65698c06f7464e21fbbec8c.abstract: The paper presents the concept of the Cognitive Digital Ocean (CDO) – a multi level cyber physical system for managing the fishery complex, integrating quantum hybrid computing, physics informed neural networks (PINN), graph neural networks (GNN), a hierarchy of digital twins (from genome to global ocean), and fractal analysis of the spatial distribution of bioresources. Special attention is paid to the shipbuilding aspect: mathematical models of the ship power plant (SPP), controllable pitch propeller (CPP), propulsion complex, and hull hydrodynamics are presented. It is shown that solving the fundamental Millennium Problem – the Navier Stokes equations – on quantum computers opens up fundamental possibilities for hydrodynamic forecasting with a horizon of up to 30 days. The system is aimed at solving the strategic tasks of the Russian Federal Agency for Fisheries (Rosrybolovstvo) until 2030: increasing production by 25%, digital transformation, and technological sovereignty. The limitations of the applicability of quantum methods are considered and engineering workarounds are proposed.

title: AI-Assisted Analysis of Spontaneous Affective Facial Responses for Cognitive Status Assessment in Older Adults: Exploratory Feasibility Study
container-title: JMIR Formative Research
6543568e570b9512b4946b58992f226b2f1a3be5.abstract: Background As Taiwan enters a super-aged society, the prevalence of dementia continues to rise, highlighting the need for scalable, noninvasive approaches to identify behavioral alterations associated with cognitive decline. AI-based analysis of spontaneous affective facial responses has emerged as a potential digital phenotyping tool, but its feasibility for assessing cognitive performance remains underexplored. Objective This study aimed to examine the feasibility of using AI-derived spontaneous affective facial response metrics, including affective expression congruency and onset latency, to characterize differences across cognitive performance levels in older adults with healthy cognition (HC), mild cognitive impairment (MCI), or dementia. Methods A total of 60 participants (HC, MCI, and dementia; 20 per group) were presented with positive and negative emotion-eliciting videos and completed Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) recall and calculation tasks. Facial expressions were video-recorded and analyzed using a convolutional neural network–based AI system. AI-derived metrics included affective expression congruency, categorized as congruent, neutral, or incongruent according to the detected facial response, and affective expression onset latency, defined as the time from stimulus presentation to the emergence of a nonneutral facial expression detected by the AI model. Group differences were analyzed using 1-way ANOVA, Pearson chi-square or Fisher-Freeman-Halton exact tests, Bonferroni-adjusted pairwise post hoc comparisons, analysis of covariance adjusting for age and education, and exploratory receiver operating characteristic analyses. Results Affectively congruent responses were generally less frequent among participants with lower cognitive performance. During the 14-second positive stimulus, congruent positive expressions were observed in 65% (13/20) of HC participants, 20% (4/20) of MCI participants, and 0% (0/20) of participants with dementia. During the 48-second negative stimulus, congruent negative expressions were observed in 60% (12/20) of HC participants compared with 5% (1/20) of both MCI and dementia participants. Onset latency differed significantly across groups for the 14-second positive stimulus (F2,57=19.63; P<.001; η2=0.41), 52-second positive stimulus (F2,57=4.25; P=.02; η2=0.13), 48-second negative stimulus (F2,57=15.61; P<.001; η2=0.35), and MMSE-based cognitive-task condition (F2,57=11.28; P<.001; η2=0.28). After adjustment for age and education, the group effect remained significant for all latency outcomes (F2,55=3.89-10.68; all P≤.03; partial η2=0.12-0.28). Exploratory receiver operating characteristic analyses showed stronger separation in several HC vs MCI and HC vs dementia comparisons, whereas MCI vs dementia comparisons showed limited separability. Conclusions AI-assisted analysis of spontaneous affective facial responses revealed differences in expression congruency and onset latency across cognitive performance levels. These preliminary findings suggest that AI-derived facial behavioral metrics may serve as noninvasive adjunctive features for observational cognitive assessment. However, the findings should be interpreted cautiously because of the exploratory design, modest sample size, and absence of internal or external validation.

title: Cognitive frailty typologies and subsequent dementia in a large representative sample of the English population
container-title: Communications Medicine
bff347764d292b0f23527266b128282b945e49b8.abstract: Abstract Background Cognitive Frailty (CF), the coexistence of mild cognitive impairment with physical frailty, may represent an intermediate state between functional vulnerability and preclinical dementia. Its potential reversibility makes it an important target for prevention. Distinguishing patterns of CF that are more and less likely to lead to dementia, and associated factors, is important for developing interventions. Methods Using data from the English Longitudinal Study of Ageing (Waves 4-9), we examined different typologies of CF based on specific cognitive impairments demonstrated. We compared longitudinal outcomes of incident dementia over 10 years for the different typologies. We also examined the impact of inequalities (Index of Multiple Deprivation (IMD) and household wealth), cognitive reserve (low education), and psychosocial factors (depression and loneliness) on the longitudinal models. Results CF groups with executive function (using verbal fluency) and/or processing speed impairment (Group 1) are distinguished from those with memory impairment only (Group 2) or impaired memory and executive function and/or processing speed (Group 3). Inequalities, cognitive reserve and psychosocial factors all show association with CF likelihood, but education (odds ratio (OR) of no qualifications compared to degree/higher education = 1.632 (Group 1) and 3.436 (Group 3)), IMD (OR 1.656 (Group 1 quintile 5), 2.083 (Group 3 quintile 4) compared to quintile 1) and loneliness (OR 1.208 (Group 1), 1.185 (Group 3)) are only associated with CF where executive function/processing speed are key characteristics. Longitudinally, only CF groupings with memory impairment (OR 2.024, Group 2; 2.733, Group 3) are predictive of dementia. Conclusions Distinguishing typologies of CF and associated risk factors is important for estimating future dementia risk, and for targeted design of interventions.

title: INTELIGÊNCIA ARTIFICIAL NA PRODUÇÃO DE TRABALHOS ESCOLARES: CRITÉRIOS DE AVALIAÇÃO DA AUTORIA E DA APRENDIZAGEM NO ENSINO MÉDIO
ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN THE PRODUCTION OF SCHOOL ASSIGNMENTS: CRITERIA FOR EVALUATING AUTHORSHIP AND LEARNING IN SECONDARY EDUCATION
INTELIGENCIA ARTIFICIAL EN LA PRODUCCIÓN DE TRABAJOS ESCOLARES: CRITERIOS DE EVALUACIÓN DE LA AUTORÍA Y DEL APRENDIZAJE EN LA EDUCACIÓN MEDIA
container-title: Revista de Geopolítica
705935d97b13f3ef45b508cbbe9bd7db39352c8b.abstract: A disponibilidade de sistemas de inteligência artificial generativa colocou o professor do Ensino Médio diante de uma pergunta para a qual o seu instrumental de avaliação não foi desenhado: como atribuir autoria a um trabalho escolar quando o texto pode ter sido produzido por uma máquina. Este artigo examina duas camadas do problema. A primeira é normativa e consiste no mapeamento lexical da Base Nacional Comum Curricular do Ensino Médio, documento que organiza o currículo e orienta a avaliação na etapa. A segunda é bibliométrica e consiste no levantamento da literatura indexada sobre detecção de texto gerado por máquina e sobre avaliação na educação secundária, com todas as consultas restritas aos campos de título e resumo após um teste de contaminação. O mapeamento revela que a Base emprega autoria nove vezes, e que oito dessas ocorrências designam algo que o estudante exerce, não algo que o professor verifica. A única ocorrência em sentido de verificação integra uma habilidade de checagem de notícias falsas. Onze expressões do vocabulário da verificação de autoria não ocorrem uma única vez, entre elas plágio, originalidade, autenticidade, integridade acadêmica e inteligência artificial. No plano bibliométrico, o recorte que combina inteligência artificial generativa, educação secundária e avaliação retorna 25 registros, dos quais 12 são preprints sem revisão por pares, 9 pertencem a contexto clínico e apenas 1 trata de autoria na escrita do Ensino Médio, sendo também um preprint. Conclui-se que o professor opera sem amparo curricular e sem base de evidência consolidada.

title: Migration of a Cervical Artificial Disc Core: A Case Report of a Devastating Late-Occurring Complication
container-title: Spine Open
13058a57ae1e8a7c141bc6bdd1a49859cd087672.abstract: Study Design: Case report. Objective: Report a devastating cervical disc replacement complication underappreciated in the literature. Summary of Background Data: As many as 3000 patients receive single-level cervical disc replacements every year in the United States. Commonly acknowledged long-term complications may burden the patient ( e.g. , revision surgeries), but the potential for severe permanent neurological harm is not widely recognized. Differences in implant design impact this potential harm. Materials and Methods: We present a case report of a 28-year-old man, who had undergone cervical artificial disc replacement five years previously, thatpresented to our emergency department with sudden onset of quadriplegia after four days of worsening neck pain. Imaging revealed the artificial disc core displaced posteriorly into the spinal canal, confirmed during emergent surgical removal followed by anterior cervical fusion. Results: Despite successful removal of the migrated implant within 24 hours of his presentation with quadriplegia and revision with solid fusion, 14 months postrevision, the patient remains wheelchair-bound with complete C6-level quadriplegia. Physical therapy has improved his hand function, core strength, and range of motion. Conclusion: Core migration may cause catastrophic complications and occur years after implantation without a traumatic cause. This risk appears more likely with postoperative kyphotic device alignment and certain disc replacement implants. We found literature reporting similar incidents for two additional patients, although they had less drastic deficits. Our case report seeks to bring awareness to surgeons and patients of this long-term complication and shows the need for investigation into potential causes and prevention. Level of Evidence: Level V.

title: On the Exculpatory Moral Economy of AI-DSS
container-title: Oxford Intersections: AI in Society
5567540863c712aeb6643ebd1c45f7594c6c03d6.abstract: Abstract This article analyzes the foundational concepts underpinning the European Union’s governance of artificial intelligence decision support systems (AI-DSSs): “trustworthy AI” and “human oversight.” Evidence from behavioral psychology, computer science, and ethics and legal scholarship demonstrates that automation bias, selective adherence, and AI hypersuasion systematically undermine meaningful human agency (MHA). Furthermore, the anthropomorphic discourse of trustworthiness obscures moral responsibility rather than ensuring accountability. This situation raises a significant question left unresolved in the literature: why does the oversight paradigm persist and even expand despite its well-documented insufficiency? To address this, the article applies the moral economy framework, as developed by E. P. Thompson and further elaborated by Bonini and Treré, to the context of AI-DSS deployment. It delineates four key positions: deployers, subjects, resistors, and the conscripted human-in-the-loop. The analysis identifies the dominant value system in this field as an exculpatory moral economy, in which protective norms are fulfilled through performance rather than genuine protection, resulting in the receipt of trust and the granting of absolution. From this perspective, the failure of oversight is not a flaw to be corrected but an intended outcome of the arrangement. The article advocates for a strong presumption against deploying AI-DSSs in sensitive areas of societal governance. Where deployment continues, it proposes two legally grounded avenues for organized societal resistance to uncritical AI-DSS deployment: promoting moral economy-aware critical AI literacy, which furthers skepticism rather than trust, and establishing collective MHA councils, rooted in the AI Act and the precautionary principle.

title: Salivary microbiome, socioeconomic status, and cognitive performance: Triangulating the relationship
container-title: PLOS One
900c75d87c6cc3c60af6305c71352c54ace522bf.abstract: Research increasingly demonstrates that endogenous bacterial communities (microbiomes) are associated with both cognitive functioning and socioeconomic status (SES). In this study, we used a metagenomics approach to characterize oral microbiome diversity in Hispanic and African American children aged 6–16 years. We examined how microbiome composition and SES were related to cognitive performance, as assessed by the Wechsler Intelligence Scale for Children (WISC). Our findings indicate that SES and the microbiome contributed complementary, comparably sized influences on cognitive functioning. Together, variability in conventional SES indicators and microbiome composition accounted for approximately 10% of the variability in WISC scores. These results highlight the importance of integrating both social and biological determinants of health when studying cognitive performance and other psychological outcomes.

title: Role of Speech-Language Pathologists Working With Individuals With Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder: A Scoping Review of Countries Within the Mutual Recognition Agreement
container-title: Perspectives of the ASHA Special Interest Groups
be626ff04804cc195b52caf8ee7d4af16c8dd274.abstract: Background: Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) is a prevalent neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by inattention, hyperactivity, and impulsivity, which can have a significant impact on an individual's functioning. Speech-language pathologists (SLPs) within the United Kingdom, the United States, Canada, New Zealand, Australia, and Ireland, with their expertise in communication disorders, could play a crucial role in the assessment, intervention, and management of ADHD-related communication. The authors explored the current role of SLPs in the assessment and management of individuals with ADHD within multidisciplinary teams across six countries. Specifically, how do the policies and practices of Mutual Recognition Agreement (MRA) countries define and support the role of SLPs in ADHD management, and what lessons can be applied to the Australian context? Method: This study performed a scoping review of literature from MRA countries plus research published in peer-reviewed journals in English within the past 20 years that references ADHD and the role of the SLP. Content analysis categorized the data into seven themes. Results: The search found 17 articles relevant to the research question and five guidelines from MRA countries. Of the MRA countries, all had a practice guideline; New Zealand shares a practice guideline with Australia. Conclusions: Contemporary research indicates that SLPs are rarely included explicitly in the management of ADHD across the lifespan. Recommendations are made for the potential role and scope of practice of the SLP when working with these individuals.

title: Artificial Intelligence and Digitalization in Energy Markets: A Comprehensive Review of Optimization, Risk Management, Blockchain Integration, and the Electric Vehicle Landscape
container-title: Journal of Applied Sciences and Modelling
b08f85932bc5537d296ab3c28ac154e9b6e2f25b.abstract: This paper analyzes the considerable impact of artificial intelligence (AI) and digitalization on energy markets and trading systems, as well as the expanding electric vehicle (EV) industry and its challenges. As the complexity of energy systems increases due to the incorporation of renewable energy, distributed generation (DG), and evolving regulations, traditional market models struggle to adapt. This evaluation examines how AI and digital technologies can enhance energy generation, distribution, and consumption across various applications, including improved forecasting, grid management, market organization, risk assessment, and automated trading. The research integrates findings related to AI-driven market improvement, risk evaluation, and relationships with blockchain, the Internet of Things (IoT), and smart grids. The analysis also explores the potential effects of cryptocurrency mining on the energy industry, in both beneficial and detrimental ways. It examines global innovations in this field and specifically addresses the impacts of Monte Carlo simulation (MCS). Charts and factual investigations are examined, indicating potential avenues for future investigation. It emphasizes the opportunities and challenges that AI and digitalization present for the energy industry, highlighting the need to address information security, regulatory compliance, and ethical issues to advance a sustainable and resilient energy future.

cc2f5dc1a573a7041df48e5dd0885de0be216988.abstract: This research addresses the challenges SMEs in Santander face in adopting artificial intelligence, stemming from technological, organizational, and structural limitations that hinder its use as a tool for innovation and sustainable growth. The methodology focused on a comprehensive analysis of the benefits, barriers, and strategies associated with the responsible implementation of AI. Key findings revealed improvements in productivity, process optimization, cost reduction, enhanced decisionmaking, and greater business adaptability; however, obstacles persisted regarding inadequate technological infrastructure, a shortage of specialized talent, implementation costs, resistance to change, and a lack of trust in these technologies. The study concludes that AI can strengthen the innovation, competitiveness, and sustainability of SMEs, provided that its adoption integrates technological investment, workforce training, governance, and ethical principles

title: Mitochondrial DNA-cGAS-STING-CISD1 axis mediates hypoxia-induced cognitive impairment by driving hippocampal neuronal ferroptosis
cc81e6e2b1c76d35d0698ecacec2effda553e0d8.abstract: Abstract High-altitude hypoxic cognitive impairment severely compromises the physical and mental health of individuals who rapidly ascend to or reside long-term at high altitude; however, its initiating mechanisms, pathological cascades, and molecular regulatory network remain incompletely understood, leaving a paucity of effective therapeutic targets and preventive strategies. Using a mouse model of simulated 6000 m hypobaric hypoxia and a primary hippocampal neuron hypoxia model, we integrated behavioral testing, transmission electron microscopy, Seahorse metabolic analysis, transcriptomic profiling, co-immunoprecipitation-coupled proteomics, structural prediction, pharmacological intervention, and clinical validation in human cohorts to systematically delineate the molecular mechanisms and core regulatory pathways underlying hypoxia-induced neuronal ferroptosis. Hypoxic exposure time-dependently impaired object recognition and spatial memory in mice and caused hippocampal neuron loss. Mechanistically, mitochondrial damage emerged as a critical initiating event during hypoxic stress, triggering mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) release and subsequent activation of the cGAS-STING signaling pathway. Hypoxic hippocampal neurons exhibited canonical features of ferroptosis, including elevated Fe²⁺ and malondialdehyde (MDA) levels, decreased GPX4 expression, and enhanced ACSL4 expression and increased mitochondrial C11-BODIPY oxidation. Pharmacological inhibition of STING with C-176 significantly alleviated these ferroptosis phenotypes, neuronal loss, and cognitive impairment. Co-immunoprecipitation combined with proteomics identified CISD1 (mitoNEET), a mitochondrial outer membrane protein, as a STING-interacting partner, and their binding was enhanced under hypoxia and localized to mitochondria-endoplasmic reticulum contact sites. Moreover, the ferroptosis inhibitor Liproxstatin-1 rescued hypoxic cognitive impairment and partially restored mitochondrial morphology and respiratory function without reversing STING phosphorylation, indicating that ferroptosis functions downstream of STING and constitutes a feed-forward amplification loop by aggravating mitochondrial damage. In human cohorts, levels of serum iron and oxidative damage markers correlated positively with residential altitude. Collectively, these findings establish a self-amplifying pathological axis of mitochondrial damage-mtDNA-cGAS-STING-CISD1-ferroptosis, and targeting this axis may provide novel strategies for the prevention and treatment of high-altitude hypoxic cognitive impairment.

title: Clinically Meaningful Cognitive Improvement from Intermittent Neurostimulation of the Nucleus Basalis of Meynert in Parkinson’s Disease
87c7670ad172788159ae620b9d3fce90c3f08286.abstract: Abstract Cognitive decline begins in early stages of Parkinson’s disease (PD) for many individuals and remains largely untreated. The nucleus basalis of Meynert (NBM), the brain’s cortical cholinergic hub, and its lateral efferent fiber bundle degenerate early in PD and are linked to cognitive and cognitive-motor impairment. Pre-clinical evidence indicates intermittent stimulation of the NBM improves cognition. The objective of this study is to establish the feasibility of combined continuous subthalamic nucleus (STN) and intermittent NBM DBS for cognitive impairment in people with PD. Five patients with PD and cognitive impairment approved for STN DBS were enrolled as part of an ongoing clinical trial for combined STN and NBM DBS under an Investigational Device Exemption. Three participants received a ‘vertical’ trajectory in which two leads were placed in the STN, and two additional leads were placed in the anterior portion of the NBM, both using the same burr hole for each hemisphere. The two other participants received a novel ‘lateral trajectory’ in which the NBM leads were placed along the NBM lateral efferent bundle via a small twist craniostomy behind the ear. An automated programming algorithm DBS Illumina 3D™ (Boston Scientific) was used to program the NBM leads based on volume of tissue activated modeling. The investigational Chronos software (Boston Scientific) was used to deliver continuous high frequency DBS to the STN 24 hours/day and intermittent patterned DBS to the NBM for 1 hour/day. The two leads placed in the NBM (‘Vertical’ target) or its lateral efferent bundle (‘Lateral’ target) were successfully and accurately placed as part of the usual STN DBS procedure. All participants were successfully programmed using the Illumina 3D™ algorithm without adverse effects. Following 6 months of combined continuous STN and intermittent NBM DBS, all five participants saw clinically meaningful improvements in cognition as part of a neuropsychological assessment battery, as well as the expected motoric benefit from STN DBS. The current study demonstrated that intermittent stimulation of the NBM to target cortical cholinergic deficits may provide clinically meaningful improvements in cognitive symptoms in Parkinson’s disease. ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT05968703

title: Designing and Evaluating a Clinical Decision Support System to Assess Mild Cognitive Impairment
container-title: ACM Transactions on Computing for Healthcare
763e62297c3779a364c1110e9de905b0814b78e4.abstract: Explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) is increasingly used in clinical decision support systems (CDSS) to improve the interpretability and trustworthiness of machine learning (ML) predictions in healthcare. While prior work has examined how healthcare professionals (HCPs) interpret various explanation methods, limited research has investigated how these explanations function in systems that incorporate novel data sources like game-based digital biomarkers. This paper extends our previous work by presenting an improved, interactive web-based CDSS designed to support HCPs in assessing the risk of Mild Cognitive Impairment (MCI). The system integrates ML predictions from gameplay data with data-centric, feature-importance, and counterfactual explanations to assist diagnosis and case-finding. We conducted a mixed-methods study with 51 HCPs to evaluate the system's understandability (objective and perceived), perceived usefulness, perceived ease of use, and trust. Participants gave consistently positive ratings across the self-reported perceived constructs, which were found to be strongly correlated. HCPs generally perceived the explanations as useful for clinical reasoning and reported that they understood and trusted the system, while acknowledging an initial learning curve. However, the evaluation of objective understanding was more mixed and correlated only weakly with the perceived constructs. In particular, participants encountered challenges in understanding game-based digital biomarkers, interpreting feature importances, combining local and global explanations, and understanding details of the underlying ML models. These findings highlight the importance of explanation designs that foster both positive user perceptions and accurate comprehension.

title: Reading for Autonomy: Literature Circles in the Secondary English Classroom<!--a=1-->
container-title: Journal of English Language Teaching
ef9a220907f90a0663477072fcabab7d07712518.abstract: Literature instruction in many secondary school contexts remains shaped by examination-orientated pedagogy that offers limited scope for independent interpretation or reflective engagement with texts. This study examines literature circles - small, student-led discussion groups organised around rotating roles - as a pedagogical alternative capable of fostering learner autonomy and reflective thinking. Drawing on a four-week qualitative case study conducted with 44 Grade 9 students at a CBSE-affiliated school in India, the study analysed students’ reflective journals and semi-structured interviews using thematic analysis. Findings reveal two key themes: literature circles fostered a gradual but observable shift toward greater student ownership of the reading process through structured, accountable roles; and collaborative, peer-driven discussion consistently prompted students to reconsider and articulate their own interpretive reasoning, generating both immediate and longer-arc reflective thinking. These findings suggest that autonomy and reflection are conditions built into the design of literature circles, offering practical implications for teachers seeking learner-centred approaches to literature pedagogy.

title: Benchmarking single-subject detectability of cognitive event-related potentials in healthy controls and minimally conscious state patients
e3b47e6137797db11cda8e0c85daf5667bb8be05.abstract: Abstract Event-related potentials (ERP) may reveal residual cognitive processing in disorders of consciousness, but clinical translation is limited because group-level effects do not guarantee reliable single-subject detection. Few ERP paradigms have been benchmarked in healthy participants and compared directly with patients in disorders of consciousness. We tested a hierarchical ERP battery in healthy controls and patients in minimally conscious state (MCS) to (1) estimate upper-bound single-subject detectability in healthy participants, (2) compare detection rates with those of MCS patients, and (3) evaluate prognostic value for recovery of consciousness. Forty-eight healthy controls and 26 patients in MCS completed six auditory paradigms: multifeature mismatch negativity (MMN), passive and active oddball P300, the subject’s own name, semantic oddball, and sentence N400. Effects were classified using blinded expert visual scoring, region-of-interest ANOVA, cluster-based permutation tests, and support vector machine decoding. Associations between binary ERP classifications and recovery were tested in 22 surviving patients at follow-up. In healthy controls, visual scoring identified MMN to at least one deviant and P300 in both oddball tasks in all 48 participants. Command following as demonstrated by task-related P300 enhancement between active and passive oddball conditions was detected in 81%. Command following was detected in 92% in the semantic oddball task. Sentence-congruity effects (N400 and/or P600) were identified in 69%, despite a strong group-level response, while the own-name effect was detected in only 35%. In patients, detection rates were lower: MMN was found in 27% for the short-duration deviant and 65% when any of five deviant types counted as positive; passive oddball P300 in 35% and active oddball P300 in 31%; sentence-congruity effects in 12%; active-versus-passive oddball modulation in 12%; and semantic oddball effects in 8%. Visual scoring and machine learning generally detected more effects than ANOVA and cluster-based testing, and agreement varied substantially across paradigms. Binary ERP classifications were not significantly associated with recovery (14 recovered, eight did not), although prognostic analyses were limited by sample size. Group-level ERP effects overstated single-subject detectability in healthy controls, whereas the absence of group-level effects in MCS obscured reliable ERP responses resembling those of healthy controls in a few individual patients. In MCS, ERP effects associated with semantic processing and command following were generally uncommon, and binary ERP indicators did not predict recovery in this sample. Our findings establish a benchmark for selecting and refining ERP paradigms and detection methods to assess residual cognition after severe brain injury.
