title: TRANSHUMANISM IN THE AGE OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE:THE SOCIO-PHILOSOPHICAL DIMENSIONS OF THE DIGITAL SOCIETY
container-title: Perspectives. Socio-political journal
b56f49cbde0e7b28ef4b717ea1f5c133a47c28c7.abstract: The relevance of the study. The rapid advancement of artificial intelligence, biotechnology, and neural interfaces underscores the need for a socio-philosophical analysis of transhumanism as a philosophical movement that advocates the possibility and desirability of technologically enhancing human nature. As digital society takes shape, transhumanist ideas are moving beyond academic discourse to become a driving force behind real-world social transformations, raising fundamentally new questions about the nature of human agency, the boundaries between the natural and the artificial, and the future social order. This article aims to examine the socio-philosophical dimensions of transhumanism in the age of artificial intelligence through an analysis of the movement’s key conceptual foundations, its interconnection with the processes of digitalisation, and a critical reflection on the associated risks and prospects. The study’s methodological framework is based on its stated aim and research objectives and adopts an interdisciplinary approach drawing on social philosophy, technology ethics, the social sciences, and media studies. The study employs comparative- historical analysis, the phenomenological method, critical discourse analysis, and a systems approach to investigating the social consequences of technological development. Research findings. The intellectual origins of transhumanism have been traced, from FM-2030’s futurist manifestos to contemporary concepts of the technological singularity and superintelligence. The analysis shows that digital society creates a distinct socio-technical environment in which transhumanist transformations assume concrete forms and give rise to new social tensions. Three key tensions within the transhumanist project have been identified: between individual freedom of self-improvement and its systemic social consequences; between techno-optimistic predictions and the real risks of humanity losing control over powerful technological systems; and between the pursuit of boundless self-improvement and the threat posed by the erosion of essential human qualities as the foundation of moral and legal equality. It is emphasised that a socio-philosophical understanding of transhumanism requires moving beyond the binary opposition between techno-optimism and technophobia in favour of a balanced, critical, and humanistically oriented approach that combines recognition of the genuine possibilities of technological progress with responsible consideration of its limits and risks.

title: Serviço de referência de bibliotecas universitárias e inteligência artificial: usos e perspectivas
container-title: Revista Brasileira de Biblioteconomia e Documentação
5da0f8ee487d4e4cccf6b9c378cb2129a602f73e.abstract: Analisa as aplicações da inteligência artificial no serviço de referência de bibliotecas universitárias brasileiras, identificando desafios e percepções dos bibliotecários sobre essa inovação. Trata-se de pesquisa exploratória e descritiva, que combina pesquisa bibliográfica e de campo como métodos. Utiliza questionário como instrumento de coleta de dados e análise de conteúdo e estatística descritiva simples como técnica de análise. Adota abordagem qualiquantitativa para discutir os resultados. Contextualiza o serviço de referência, abordando sua evolução histórica e sua progressiva integração com tecnologias emergentes, além de apresentar os fundamentos teóricos da inteligência artificial e suas aplicações no campo biblioteconômico. Explica que a adoção de inteligência artificial em bibliotecas é uma tendência apresentada em relatórios de órgãos como a International Federation of Library Associations and Institutions e que deve crescer nos próximos anos. Informa que bibliotecários brasileiros já utilizam tecnologias de inteligência artificial, como sistemas de recomendação e assistentes virtuais, ainda que em escala reduzida em comparação ao cenário internacional. Contudo, especificamente no serviço de referência praticado essa adoção é ainda menor. Há interesse na adoção dessas tecnologias, mas há desafios como a ausência de formação específica e a falta de regramento institucional. Arrola que há escassez de estudos de caso e relatos de experiência sobre o uso de inteligência artificial no serviço de referência no Brasil e que a discussão deve ser ampliada. Conclui que a inteligência artificial pode desempenhar uma função importante na transformação dos serviços de referência, facilitando interações mais ágeis e adaptativas entre bibliotecários e usuários na era digital.

title: Cognitive Model Organism: The Unboxing of Thinking Process
b870d33e57aa206eb87c39c735b13a625d401a57.abstract: We establish the Hortus Regis Alti (HRA) Experimental and Observational Protocol for studying a frozen language model as a cognitive model organism. The preparation combines controlled input perturbations, complete native-token preservation, deterministic symbolic probes, contextual process coding, and explicit failure screening. One DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B implementation with INT8 linear layers and BF16 elsewhere produced 176 archived trajectories across four observation configurations of one Bayesian decision problem, containing 2,205,963 generated tokens. Eight baseline pairs regenerated identical overlapping prefixes across 93,016 token positions. Three empirical demonstrations organize the study. Symbolic closure separated from execution termination, including renewed processing after a closure marker. Aggregate consumption separated from item-specific response paths: 36 of 40 four-level item series changed direction. Correct local computation separated from maintenance of task representation: an auxiliary result could be calculated correctly and subsequently rebound as an operand. Complete contextual reading localized 1,926 evidence anchors, including successful repairs and recurrent failures. Measurement checks further showed that a short window could classify a long exact cycle as highly diverse. These findings motivate testable hypotheses of representational control competition, training-register capture, and content-specific effects of symbolic continuation. The contribution is a process-oriented experimental preparation, a reproducible trajectory collection, and a quality-control procedure that connects observable symbolic events to discriminating intervention sites. Precision specifications identify the model strain, execution conditions, measurement units, semantic coding decisions, and regeneration range supporting these claims.

title: Sociocultural Correlates of Infant Visual Attention
8473a031b71f412db61a7f2575838edd7fc38aae.abstract: Infant visual attention—most often operationalized through looking behavior—is a foundational method and explanatory construct in the study of early cognition. Cultural psychology has established that attention is organized by culturally structured practices and localized meanings, but this work has focused largely on children and adults, and the extent to which culturally patterned experience shapes the endogenous attentional processes that looking measures are used to index in infancy remains under-specified. This review focuses on the first two years of life and on four components of endogenous attention that are routinely inferred from looking behavior: focal versus contextual allocation, orienting speed versus accuracy, novelty versus familiarity orientation, and persistence versus flexibility. We distinguish culture—shared meanings, practices, and organized forms of everyday activity—from demographic indicators such as nationality, language background, race, and socioeconomic status, which are coarse proxies for proximal experience. Synthesizing cross-national studies alongside research on multilingual, interracial, and socioeconomic experience, we show that components of infant attention vary with experience and task context in ways that do not map cleanly onto reified group categories. We identify a gap between research documenting effects of specific experiences and research examining culture directly, and we propose a culturally situated model in which endogenous attentional mechanisms are calibrated through culturally patterned input across development. This approach preserves the value of looking-time and eye-tracking methods while strengthening their construct validity, measurement invariance, and generalizability.

title: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN THE MEDIA SPACE: BETWEEN TECHNOLOGICAL EFFICIENCY AND ETHICAL RESPONSIBILITY
container-title: Наукові праці Міжрегіональної Академії управління персоналом. Політичні науки та публічне управління
c9619f40106342c7e01f8f1ccf384b8bbc45bff5.abstract: Дослідження зосереджується на аналізі етичних викликах, що виникають при використанні штучного інтелекту (ШІ) у сучасній журналістиці. Основною метою статті є визначення ключових етичних проблем (точність, прозорість, відповідальність, приватність), аналіз їхнього впливу на медіапрактику та розробка рекомендацій щодо інтеграції ШІ без шкоди для журналістських стандартів. Дослідження ґрунтується на поєднанні теоретичного та емпіричного підходів. Виконано огляд наукових праць українських і міжнародних авторів, застосовано методи аналізу, синтезу та порівняльно-зіставний метод. Емпірична частина реалізована через метод кейс-стаді, що містить аналіз резонансних випадків 2023 року, пов’язаних із ШІ в журналістиці (автоматизоване створення новин, фейкові «ШІ-автори», підроблені інтерв’ю). Вибрані кейси (CNET, Sports Illustrated, Die Aktuelle, Microsoft Travel) дозволяють оцінити реальні наслідки порушення етичних норм. Встановлено, що використання ШІ у журналістиці супроводжується значними етичними ризиками, зокрема: неточність та алгоритмічна упередженість, непрозорість щодо ролі ШІ у створенні контенту, розмивання відповідальності між редакцією та алгоритмом, ризики порушення приватності через обробку персональних даних. Аналіз кейсів показав, що відсутність належного контролю за ШІ у медіа призводить до скандалів, втрати суспільної довіри та правових наслідків. Попри потенціал ШІ у підвищенні ефективності журналістики, він не може замінити журналіста – без людського контролю виникають серйозні етичні загрози. Для забезпечення етичного використання ШІ у журналістиці необхідно: запровадити політику прозорості щодо використання алгоритмів, впровадити людську перевірку AI-генерованого контенту, контролювати алгоритмічну упередженість шляхом етичних аудитів, захищати персональні дані та уникати порушень приватності. Наукова новизна дослідження полягає у комплексному аналізі впливу ШІ на журналістську етику та формулюванні практичних рекомендацій для медіаіндустрії щодо відповідального використання новітніх технологій.

title: GBAS: A Hybrid GRU–BiLSTM–Attention–SVM Framework for Multiclass Stunting-Status Classification in Riau Province, Indonesia
container-title: International Journal of Engineering, Science and Information Technology
e4ae3d541e91cfa6c9448045cc7642b8d78cf788.abstract: Stunting-status classification using structured anthropometric data presents several challenges, including class imbalance, heterogeneous predictor characteristics, limited sample size, and the risk of target-derived information artificially inflating model performance. This study proposes GRU–BiLSTM–Attention–SVM (GBAS), a hybrid framework that combines recurrent deep representation learning, bidirectional processing, attention-based representation weighting, and margin-based classification for multiclass stunting-status classification. The study used 569 cross-sectional child-growth records from Riau Province, Indonesia, comprising Normal, Stunted, and Severely Stunted classes. Before model development, data-quality and leakage controls were applied, including measurement-unit standardization, exclusion of variables with substantial unavailable information, control of repeated feature combinations during partitioning, and removal of target-derived nutritional indicators. The remaining predictors were numerically encoded and standardized using parameters estimated from the training data, while class weighting was applied to address class imbalance without synthetic oversampling. In GBAS, GRU and BiLSTM operate as representation-learning components over a consistently ordered structured-feature representation, attention weights the resulting latent representations, and SVM performs final classification. On the held-out test set of 114 observations, GBAS correctly classified 113 observations, achieving 99.12% accuracy, 99.13% weighted precision, 99.12% weighted recall, and 99.12% weighted F1-score. Under the same experimental setting, GBAS outperformed the evaluated SVM, GRU, and BiLSTM baselines, which achieved accuracies of 89.46%, 95.78%, and 97.30%, respectively. These findings support the feasibility of the integrated GBAS framework for structured stunting-status classification. However, the results remain specific to the Riau dataset, feature ordering, and experimental configuration and require further validation through larger datasets, stronger tabular baselines, feature-order sensitivity analysis, component-level ablation, and external evaluation

title: Attention in model-based cognitive neuroscience: Mechanisms for optimization under constraint
3aaee46f4b8c0020acd131b68eb24d9ea7ccfb1a.abstract: Two major criticisms of attention research are: 1) verbal theories lack the specificity to make falsifiable predictions about how the various mechanisms of attention operate; and 2) the term ``attention’’ is frequently ascribed to conceptually similar phenomena despite dissociable neural underpinnings. The field of model-based cognitive neuroscience is well-positioned to address (1) through mathematical formalization of hypothesized processes, but may perpetuate (2) insofar as similar algorithms and parameters may recur across modeling traditions without necessarily drawing upon a shared neuro-mechanistic basis. This review provides a function-first organization of the algorithms that have been hypothesized to implement or give rise to ``attention'' at various levels of processing: perception, decision-making, and learning. We ground mathematically-formalized processes in the performance-relevant objectives they serve and the processing constraints that limit them. In doing so, we provide a road map of the broader computational-level solutions that ``attention'' mechanisms have been invoked to provide.

title: Causal Geospatial Intelligence Framework for Identifying Environmental Drivers of Landslide Risk in Mountainous Regions
container-title: International Journal of Engineering, Science and Information Technology
c9dc1ee0508288613a4afb6efc2c29dfbef64449.abstract: Landslide susceptibility models can effectively predict areas prone to landslides but generally provide limited evidence on whether specific environmental exposures causally influence landslide occurrence. This research proposes an integrated causal-geospatial framework combining predictive modeling with causal effect estimation and spatial heterogeneity analysis for landslide occurrence in Desa Wih Pase, Bener Meriah, Indonesia. An analytical dataset comprising 18,450 30 m × 30 m grid cells from observations in 2025 was analyzed using Random Forest and Logistic Regression for occurrence probability modeling, followed by Causal Forest to derive average treatment effect estimates together with grid-level Conditional Average Treatment Effects (CATE). The Random Forest model reached a discrimination performance of 0.91 in AUC-ROC, exceeding the 0.79 achieved by the Logistic Regression baseline, demonstrating stronger predictive discrimination under the imbalanced landslide dataset. Causal analysis estimated a positive effect of cumulative rainfall, with a 100 mm increase associated with a 0.142 increase in landslide occurrence probability (95% CI: 0.089–0.195). A 10° increase in slope produced an estimated effect of 0.218 (95% CI: 0.161–0.275). Spatial CATE analysis revealed substantial heterogeneity, with rainfall effects ranging from ?0.039 to 0.302 and slope effects from ?0.024 to 0.490 across valid 30 m grid cells. Sensitivity analyses showed that the positive causal effects remained stable across alternative confounder sets, rainfall accumulation windows, and spatial resolutions. The framework distinguishes predictive susceptibility from causal environmental effects and provides a basis for spatially targeted landslide risk reduction and environmental engineering interventions

title: Revisiting Attention Modules for Still-Image Human Action Recognition: A Multi-Seed Evaluation on Stanford-40
container-title: International Journal of Engineering, Science and Information Technology
c52f55837f63d489cc4d73a1f2db1542e97d105c.abstract: Attention modules such as Squeeze-and-Excitation are often reported to improve convolutional neural networks for human action recognition in still images. Most of these reports, however, rely on a single training run, and published scores on the same benchmark are frequently obtained under different train–test splits. This study examines whether the reported benefit remains under a controlled evaluation. Four modules, namely Squeeze-and-Excitation (SE), the Convolutional Block Attention Module (CBAM), Efficient Channel Attention (ECA), and the parameter-free SimAM, were inserted into ResNet-34 at four positions and trained on the Stanford-40 Actions dataset under its official split with one fixed training recipe, giving 44 trained models. The four all-stage configurations were repeated with six random seeds and compared using a paired Wilcoxon signed-rank test and an exact McNemar test. Replacing the official split with a random 80/20 split increased test accuracy by 3.19 to 4.52 percentage points across four backbones, a larger change than any module produced. Across six seeds, SE changed macro-F1 by +0.06 points, within the seed-to-seed range of the unmodified baseline, whereas ECA and SimAM reduced it by 1.56 and 0.74 points. No module improved on the baseline by a statistically supported margin, yet every module increased single-image CPU latency by 4.3% to 18.3% while adding less than 0.02% in floating-point operations. The findings show that the evaluation protocol and run-to-run variance affect reported scores more than the modules themselves, and a reporting checklist is proposed for future evaluations of such modules

title: Inteligencia artificial en enfermería: Percepción de los estudiantes sobre sus beneficios, riesgos y utilidad para la práctica profesional. Búsqueda narrativa
Artificial intelligence in nursing: Students' perceptions of its benefits, risks, and utility for professional practice. A narrative review
container-title: Ibero Ciencias - Revista Científica y Académica - ISSN 3072-7197
168e2015328f00de2f4610ac0b3247b832d38811.abstract: This article analyzes nursing students' perceptions regarding the benefits, risks, and utility of artificial intelligence (AI) in their academic training and future professional practice. Through a narrative review of scientific literature published between 2020 and August 2026, the study examines AI's educational and clinical applications. The results reveal a generally favorable perception of AI, driven by its speed, accessibility, and ability to simplify complex concepts, summarize information, and facilitate autonomous learning. Furthermore, these tools can support clinical reasoning, case development, and the preparation of academic activities. However, risks are identified regarding incorrect information, algorithmic bias, privacy, academic integrity, technological dependence, and a potential decline in critical thinking. These concerns highlight the need to develop the digital, ethical, and professional competencies required to use these tools responsibly. The study concludes that the integration of AI into nursing must be planned, supervised, and person-centered. It is essential to verify information, protect data, and preserve clinical judgment, ensuring that technology complements but never replaces humanized care and the professional responsibility of nursing staff.

title: Inteligencia artificial: herramienta en el aprendizaje en estudiantes de enfermería de Uleam el Carmen-Manabi
container-title: Revista Científica de Innovación Educativa y Sociedad Actual "ALCON"
db716743d8f8b939aa9916b3cd5f80704747c0c6.abstract: La incorporación de la inteligencia artificial en la educación superior generó oportunidades para apoyar el aprendizaje, pero también planteó desafíos relacionados con la verificación de la información, el pensamiento crítico y la protección de datos. El estudio tuvo como objetivo analizar el uso de la inteligencia artificial como herramienta en el aprendizaje de los estudiantes de Enfermería de la Universidad Laica Eloy Alfaro de Manabí (ULEAM), Extensión El Carmen. Se desarrolló una investigación cuantitativa, no experimental, transversal y descriptivo-correlacional. Participaron 156 estudiantes de primero a séptimo semestre, quienes respondieron un cuestionario de 20 afirmaciones mediante una escala de cinco opciones. Los resultados mostraron una valoración global favorable de 3,90 sobre cinco puntos; además, el 57,0 % utilizó estas herramientas siempre o frecuentemente. ChatGPT fue la aplicación más empleada, con el 75,6 %, seguida de Gemini, con el 50,6 %. Se identificaron relaciones positivas fuertes entre el uso y la accesibilidad, el desarrollo de contenidos, el aprendizaje autónomo y la comprensión. El pensamiento crítico, la ética y el uso responsable obtuvieron la valoración más baja. La inteligencia artificial constituye una herramienta favorable para el aprendizaje, siempre que se integre con orientación docente, verificación de contenidos y protección de datos.

title: The potential for a wealth tax in South Africa: meritocracy as a ‘brake’ on political trust
container-title: Global Political Economy
8ca027858932f1d2ac7029e6eafddd7f4f2b1af7.abstract: The relationship between political trust and support for redistributive policies reveals a paradox: while political trust typically increases policy support, it may simultaneously strengthen meritocratic beliefs that legitimise wealth accumulation and suppress redistributive preferences. Drawing on survey data from 2,249 wealthier, predominantly secondary- and tertiary-educated South African adults collected in 2022, I test a mediation framework where political trust affects wealth tax preferences both directly and indirectly through meritocratic tendencies. The analysis reveals a ‘meritocratic brake effect’: while higher political trust increases support for wealth taxation, it also strengthens meritocratic beliefs about wealth accumulation, which in turn suppresses redistributive preferences. This creates a complex dynamic where the positive effect of trust on wealth tax support is partially offset by merit-based legitimisation of inequality. Given South Africa’s extreme inequality and historically low political trust levels (70 per cent of respondents expressing distrust), these findings reveal a potential vicious cycle where the institutional confidence needed to implement redistributive policies is undermined by the very ideologies that legitimise wealth concentration. The study contributes to understanding how trust-inequality-meritocracy dynamics shape attitudinal receptivity to wealth taxation in highly unequal societies, suggesting that successful wealth tax implementation may require simultaneous efforts to rebuild institutional trust and challenge meritocratic narratives about wealth accumulation.

title: The Cognitive Structure of the WPPSI-IV: What Can Network Analysis Tell Us?
fe7d653214c9983a2d6da39be54e06cd8953af19.abstract: The Wechsler Preschool and Primary Scale of Intelligence, Fourth Edition (WPPSI-IV), is widely used to assess young children’s cognitive abilities. Its indices describe performance in domains such as verbal comprehension and working memory, but evidence for interpreting these as distinct abilities remains limited. This study examined whether exploratory graph analysis (EGA), a network method, could recover the proposed index groupings from published normative correlations for ages 2:6 to 3:11 (n = 600) and 4:0 to 7:7 (n = 1,100). Simulations tested whether the same method could recover those groupings when separate, correlated factors generated the data. The main EGA procedure placed the primary subtests in one group. It also produced one group in 99.6% to 100% of samples generated from the index models, so it could not distinguish those models from simpler alternatives. In the older band, however, factor models fit better with several factors than with one. Recovery depended on factor correlations, the number of subtests per factor, and a built-in check for a single dimension. Groupings also changed with subtest coverage. For school psychologists, a one-group network result, however consistent, cannot by itself show whether WPPSI-IV index scores reflect distinct abilities.

title: REPOSITIONING NIGERIAN POLYTECHNIC CHEMISTRY PROGRAMMES FOR THE FOURTH INDUSTRIAL REVOLUTION: A CONCEPTUAL FRAMEWORK FOR EMBEDDING ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN THE CURRICULUM
container-title: Journal of Health Systems Research
bdb210daf2556908f1393514881e8801106ea0bf.abstract: The emergence of the Fourth Industrial Revolution (Industry 4.0) is fundamentally altering the landscape of the global chemical sector through automation, cyber-physical infrastructures, machine learning, and data-intensive approaches to discovery. These shifts have generated an acute need for professionals who can function effectively at the convergence of chemistry, computation, and digital technologies. In contrast, Nigerian polytechnics (institutions constitutionally tasked with cultivating mid-level technical expertise) continue to operate largely conventional, content-saturated chemistry curricula that show little correspondence with these evolving workforce expectations. This conceptual study set out to examine how artificial intelligence (AI) could be systematically woven into the chemistry curricula of Nigerian polytechnics as a means of equipping graduates for Industry 4.0. By triangulating scholarship on AI in education, chemistry pedagogy, technical and vocational education and training (TVET), and Industry 4.0 workforce requirements, the paper constructed a conceptual architecture for curriculum integration and evaluated four distinct integration pathways: the supplementary, embedded, dual-track, and fully reformed models. The analysis also interrogated the structural, human-capital, infrastructural, ethical, and policy-related obstacles that impede AI uptake within Nigerian polytechnics, while delineating the Industry 4.0 capabilities that chemistry graduates must command—namely data literacy, computational reasoning, digitally mediated laboratory competence, and AI-supported problem resolution. The study concludes that a staged, context-attuned integration approach—anchored in purposeful policy reform, lecturer capacity building, industry collaboration, and deliberate investment in digital infrastructure—is indispensable for sustaining the relevance of Nigerian polytechnics. Concrete recommendations are advanced for curriculum authorities, institutional managers, and industry stakeholders.

title: AFSAF-Net: Adaptive Frequency-Spatial Attention Fusion Network with IMU Guidance for Robust Indoor Localization under Low-Light and Texture-Degraded Environments
8d1e2827b2f7782a467743b281ca63833a28e0d7.abstract: Abstract Indoor localization under low-light and texture-degraded environments remains challenging because insufficient visual information leads to unstable feature extraction, while inertial measurements are inevitably affected by accumulated drift. Previous MC4L-IMU-based studies demonstrated the effectiveness of handcrafted texture descriptors, frequency-domain enhancement, deep visual representation learning, and visual-inertial fusion for improving localization performance in dark indoor scenarios. However, these approaches mainly rely on manually designed frequency representations and fixed fusion strategies, limiting their adaptability to dynamically changing sensor reliability. To address these limitations, this paper proposes an Adaptive Frequency-Spatial Attention Fusion Network with IMU Guidance (AFSAF-Net) for robust indoor localization. The proposed framework introduces an adaptive frequency learning branch to capture spectral information beyond handcrafted transformations, an attention-driven frequency-spatial fusion module to dynamically integrate complementary visual representations, and an IMU reliability gate to adjust the contribution of inertial information according to sensor confidence. By jointly modeling frequency characteristics, spatial semantics, and inertial reliability, AFSAF-Net enables adaptive multimodal perception under challenging indoor conditions. Experiments conducted on the MC4L-IMU indoor localization platform demonstrate that AFSAF-Net achieves a mean localization error of 0.85 cm and the highest coefficient of determination (R 2 = 0.9986) among the evaluated methods. Furthermore, the proposed framework maintains more stable localization performance under low-light conditions compared with conventional visual and visual-inertial approaches. These results indicate that adaptive spectral representation learning and reliability-aware sensor fusion can effectively improve localization robustness without relying on fixed feature extraction or predefined fusion rules.

title: <b>Pengaruh </b><b><i>User-Generated-Content</i></b><b> terhadap </b><b><i>Purchase Intention</i></b><b> melalui </b><b><i>Brand Image</i></b><b> Bedak Tabur Marcks Kota Depok </b>

d999e84ea7f4027941192a38c65fcd31ae0deccd.abstract: This study aims to analyze the influence of User Generated Content on Purchase Intention through Brand Image for Marcks Loose Powder in Depok. The research method used was a quantitative approach, with data collected via a questionnaire administered to 100 respondent individuals who had previously viewed reviews or user generated content related to Marcks Loose Powder. The sampling technique used was nonprobability sampling with an incidental sampling approach. Data analysis was conducted using SmartPLS 4.0 software via the Partial Least Squares – Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) approach. The analysis stages included testing the measurement model (outer model), the structural model (inner model), and hypothesis testing. The results of the study indicate that User Generated Content significant effect on Brand Image, and Brand Image significant effect on Purchase Intention. Furthermore, User Generated Content also significant effect on Purchase Intention through Brand Image as a mediating variable. These findings highlight the importance of user generated content strategies in enhancing brand image, which ultimately encourages consumers to purchase Marcks Loose Powder.

title: L’adoption et l’utilisation de l’IA dans l’économie sociale et l’action communautaire
The Adoption and Use of AI in the Social Economy and Community Action
container-title: Canadian Journal of Nonprofit and Social Economy Research
1557ba2729c3afa3ad2f2c6f5932df500c676083.abstract: Despite AI’s potential to significantly improve how organizations involved in the social economy and community action (ÉSAC, from the French économie sociale et action communautaire) use their limited resources to carry out their important mission, their adoption of AI has been slow because of the constraints they face. This article analyzes the use of AI in Quebec’s ÉSAC sector, which comprises cooperatives, membership organizations, nonprofits, and community action organizations. We conducted 27 semi-structured interviews with three distinct groups of professionals: managers, counsellors, and trainers. Of these participants, 25 work for ÉSAC organizations, and two are external IT trainers who intervened in ÉSAC entities. Drawing on a research framework based on the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology (UTAUT) adapted to AI, we used thematic analysis to identify the factors influencing the adoption and use of AI within the participating organizations. We grouped the identified factors under the four dimensions of the SWOT strategic analysis tool: strengths and weaknesses within the organization, opportunities for improvement, and potential threats to be mitigated.

title: A New Approach in Adolescent Health: Artificial Intelligence-Supported Mobile Applications in Supporting Nutrition, Exercise and Sleep

51111d0546efb6d99a7618a26855f8901db282e4.abstract: Adolescence is a critical developmental period in which health behaviors that will last a lifetime are established. Nutrition, physical activity and sleep emerge as three fundamental behavioral domains that directly determine adolescent health and are interconnected and mutually influence one another during this period. Global and national data indicate that the situation in these areas is extremely alarming; the majority of adolescents fail to meet physical activity recommendations, nutritional patterns remain inadequate, and sleep problems are widely prevalent. With the deep integration of smartphones into adolescent life, artificial intelligence (AI)-supported mobile applications emerge as a promising approach in this field with their capacity to provide personalized and real-time interventions. This review addresses the role of AI-supported mobile applications in supporting nutrition, physical activity and sleep behaviors in adolescents from a nursing perspective. Although digital health interventions may support improvements in health behaviors, evidence specifically demonstrating the effectiveness of AI-supported applications among adolescents remains limited. Considering potential limitations such as data privacy and algorithmic bias, the integration of these applications into school health services warrants further research.

title: Predicting Ground Granulated Blast-Furnace Slag (GGBS) Concrete Strength Based On PerformanceWith Interpretable Artificial Neural Networks (ANN)
container-title: Journal of the Civil Engineering Forum
4e8fa7e88dbcd439614fd29edd4c3845d4015ada.abstract: Accurate prediction of concrete strength is essential for effective mix proportioning, performance optimisation, and sustainable construction. Conventional empirical and regression–based approaches often have limited capability to capture the complex and nonlinear interactions among constituent materials, particularly in blended and geopolymer concrete systems. This study develops an Artificial Neural Network (ANN)–based machine learning framework for predicting the compressive and flexural strengths of GGBS–based concrete. A dataset comprising 150 concrete mixtures with varying binder compositions, material proportions, and curing periods was employed to develop and evaluate the predictive models. The modelling framework was assessed using k–fold cross–validation, statistical error indicators, \ and residual diagnostics to examine prediction accuracy, robustness, and generalisation capability. The ANN model demonstrated excellent predictive performance for compressive strength, achieving high coefficients of determination and low prediction errors across the training, validation, and testing datasets. In comparison, the prediction of flexural strength showed relatively lower generalisation performance, which may be attributed to greater experimental variability and the sensitivity of flexural behaviour to crack initiation, propagation, aggregate–matrix interaction, and material heterogeneity. To improve model interpretability, SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) analysis was employed to quantify the contribution of individual input variables. The results identified GGBS content and the alkali–to–binder ratio as the dominant factors influencing predicted strength, demonstrating consistency with the underlying chemical and mechanical behaviour of GGBS–based concrete. The integrated ANN–SHAP framework provides both accurate prediction and meaningful interpretation of strength development. Overall, the findings demonstrate that ANN based machine learning can serve as a reliable and efficient tool for strength prediction and performance–based optimisation of GGBS–based concrete, potentially reducing the need for extensive experimental trials while saving time, material consumption, and associated costs.

title: Efficacy of Mindfulness-Based Cognitive Therapy for Self-Esteem, Psychological Well-being, and Happiness in Substance Use Disorder: A Randomized Controlled Trial
7ff343eb5d6a06286b4da1324df537fd82f0c8a4.abstract: Abstract Substance use disorder (SUD), a major public health concern across the world, and also in India, is commonly associated with low self-esteem, reduced psychological well-being, and diminished happiness. Yet, rigorous trials of psychosocial interventions targeting these outcomes in rehabilitation settings remain scarce. This single-masked randomized controlled trial (RCT) examined the efficacy of an 8-week Mindfulness-Based Cognitive Therapy (MBCT) program, delivered alongside treatment as usual (TAU), in improving self-esteem, psychological well-being, and happiness among adults with SUD. Seventy-one men receiving inpatient rehabilitation at two centers in Bangalore, India, were block-randomized to an MBCT-plus-TAU group (n=36) or a TAU-only group (n=35); 30 participants per group completed all four assessments (baseline, post-intervention, and one- and three-month follow-up). Across the full sample, scores on all three outcomes improved significantly over time (all p<.001). A significant time x group interaction emerged for happiness (F(3,198)=5.51, p=.001, partial eta-squared=.087), with the MBCT group showing greater gains than the TAU group; interactions for psychological well-being and self-esteem were not significant. Mean gain scores indicated significantly greater improvements with MBCT than with TAU for happiness and self-esteem, but not for psychological well-being. These findings support MBCT as a valuable adjunctive intervention for SUD rehabilitation, with the most robust benefit observed for happiness. Trial registration: Clinical Trials Registry of India, CTRI/2025/09/094309 (Registered on 08/09/2025). Details are available at http://ctri.nic.in.

title: SegRef3D Lite: A browser-based workflow for artificial intelligence–assisted segmentation and quantitative three-dimensional morphological analysis
c5a756af6f408ee32edad7957d23a9851b975fe7.abstract: Abstract Segmentation is a major bottleneck in three-dimensional morphological analysis. Although artificial intelligence–assisted segmentation workflows can be used to address this issue, their implementations are constrained by dedicated software environments or local computing resources. To address these challenges, we developed SegRef3D Lite, a browser-based platform that integrates two complementary artificial intelligence–assisted segmentation approaches (namely, SegAnything and SegCT/MRI) within a common human-in-the-loop workflow. SegAnything provides general-purpose, prompt-based segmentation by using Segment Anything Model 2, and SegCT/MRI provides anatomy-specific segmentations of computed tomography and magnetic resonance imaging datasets by using TotalSegmentator. Both approaches generate segmentation masks that can be imported into the same browser-based workspace for visual review, manual correction, quantitative volume measurement, three-dimensional visualization, and surface-model export. In this workspace, routine image handling and refinement are performed locally in the browser, whereas artificial intelligence inference is executed through user-initiated Google Colaboratory workflows, thus eliminating the need for a compatible graphics processing unit on a local computer. We applied our platform to serial block-face photographs, volumetric computed tomography, serial light microscopy, serial electron microscopy, and human abdominal computed tomography. Across these diverse imaging modalities and spatial scales, our platform is able to process outputs from different segmentation approaches by using the same downstream workflow for review, refinement, quantitative analysis, and three-dimensional reconstruction. Therefore, SegRef3D Lite provides an accessible framework for integrating complementary artificial intelligence–assisted segmentation strategies with researcher-guided verification and quantitative morphological analysis. Mini-abstract : SegRef3D Lite integrates general-purpose and anatomy-specific artificial intelligence–assisted segmentation with browser-based human refinement, volume measurement, and three-dimensional reconstruction across diverse morphological imaging modalities.

title: Addressing the Cognitive Care Gap in Parkinson's Disease through Participatory Co-design of a Digital Neuropsychological Assessment Platform
62dbeb0f8367cfb5f7ba72fb4c63952bc62d52d6.abstract: Abstract Cognitive impairment is a prevalent and clinically significant feature of Parkinson’s disease (PD), although systematic neuropsychological assessment remains inconsistently integrated into movement disorder clinical care. Time constraints, limited neuropsychology workforce capacity, and fragmented data infrastructure impede early identification and longitudinal monitoring of cognitive decline in this population. The ‘PDCogniCare’ program aimed to address this gap by developing best-practice guidelines and a PD-specific neuropsychological toolkit. To implement this program in clinical settings, the PDCogniCare digital platform was co-designed and developed as a web-based tool to improve access to cognitive assessment, support clinician training, competence and confidence, and enable longitudinal tracking of neuropsychological outcomes across Movement disorders and psychology services. A participatory asynchronous co-design methodology was employed across three workshops and an interim system evaluation, across metropolitan health services in Queensland, Australia. Fifteen participants were involved, encompassing all interest holders in the neuropsychological assessment journey. Design activities included journey map refinement, MoSCoW feature prioritisation, low-fidelity prototype development, and iterative platform evaluation. Consumer and caregiver input was integrated throughout. The finalised platform received a mean System Usability Scale score of 82.5, placing it in the excellent range. Participants confirmed broad alignment between the platform and their clinical and lived experience priorities. Remaining concerns, including system integration, client enrolment, clinical pathway gaps, and data governance issues, were identified as priorities for future refinement prior to wider implementation. The findings support participatory co-design as an effective methodology for developing acceptable and clinically grounded digital health tools in neurodegenerative disease contexts.

title: Electric Vehicle Price Prediction Using Real-World Online Listings: An Explainable Machine Learning Approach
container-title: Journal of Computational and Cognitive Engineering
af09d5bbaffefa30e1f43ec5abbcb523f027c8b4.abstract: The recent gains in the adoption of electric vehicles (EVs) have triggered the emergence of secondary markets concerning EVs, where the determination of prices accurately and transparently is an extreme challenge. In the current study, we propose an explainable machine learning model to predict the advertised price (in Jordanian dinars) of used EVs, using actual online advertisements obtained in the Jordanian market. An EV-oriented and custom-made dataset of 2,165 listings was used that specifically includes battery capacity and driving range along with the typical vehicle features. The coefficient of determination (R²), mean absolute error, and root mean squared error were used to assess the performance of three tree-based regressors: CatBoost Regressor, Extreme Gradient Boosting Regressor, and Random Forest Regressor trained with a leakage-safe pipeline and evaluated using grouped, repeated cross-validation. SHapley Additive exPlanations were applied to the fitted models to quantify the global contribution of each feature to price predictions and to assess the stability of these contributions across validation folds, providing a transparent account of the price-determination mechanism. The empirical data indicate that battery capacity and driving range are the most dominant EV price determinants that continue to overshadow conventional predictors of price, including brand, mileage, and year. The soundness of such findings is supported by cross-model explainability analyses. As a result, the proposed framework enhances pricing transparency and enables informed decision-making in young EV markets. title: A GERAÇÃO QUE PESQUISA SEM LER: DEPENDÊNCIA DA INTELIGÊNCIA ARTIFICIAL, AUTONOMIA INTELECTUAL E O VÁCUO NA FORMAÇÃO DOCENTE NO BRASIL
container-title: Revista Tópicos
1958b2ee3f71eda8ac8021811c3cf85665ee5216.abstract: O uso de ferramentas de inteligência artificial generativa pelos estudantes brasileiros cresceu em ritmo superior ao da preparação das escolas e dos professores para orientá-lo, o que abriu espaço para práticas em que a ferramenta ocupa o lugar da leitura e do julgamento próprio do aluno. Este artigo analisa, por meio de revisão bibliográfica de abordagem qualitativa associada à análise documental, a relação entre o uso autônomo da inteligência artificial por estudantes e a lacuna na formação docente para mediá-lo, tomando como base levantamentos nacionais recentes, como o PISA 2025, a TIC Educação 2024 e a TALIS 2024, além de estudos experimentais e da produção teórica sobre autonomia, mediação e formação de professores. Os dados indicam que quase metade dos estudantes de 15 anos recorre semanalmente a chatbots para aprender e que a pesquisa rápida sobre temas novos é o uso em que o Brasil mais se distancia da média da OCDE, enquanto apenas cerca de um terço dos alunos relata ter recebido orientação da escola. Entre os docentes, a adesão às ferramentas é alta, porém concentrada no planejamento das aulas, e a falta de conhecimento aparece como principal motivo entre os que não as utilizam. Conclui-se que a dependência intelectual descrita na literatura guarda relação estreita com a ausência de mediação pedagógica, de modo que a formação continuada, situada na escola e voltada ao redesenho das tarefas e da avaliação, constitui a condição para que a inteligência artificial apoie a aprendizagem sem substituir o esforço cognitivo que a sustenta.

title: INOVASI E-MODUL KONSELING COGNITIVE BEHAVIORAL DENGAN TEKNIK COGNITIVE RESTRUCTURING UNTUK MENANGANI KECEMASAN SOSIAL SISWA KORBAN BULLYING
container-title: EDUTECH : Jurnal Inovasi Pendidikan Berbantuan Teknologi
3c4f3dd04b7fec69f7d8f645f546422f12282cb9.abstract: Bullying represents a critical psychosocial issue among adolescents that severely damages mental health, notably precipitating social anxiety among victims. Victimized students frequently manifest irrational fears of negative peer evaluations, socially withdraw from schooling activities, and experience sharp academic declines. Concurrently, school guidance and counseling services face severe structural constraints, including restricted session durations and a scarcity of validated digital intervention media. This research aimed to develop a cognitive behavioral counseling e-module utilizing cognitive restructuring techniques that is valid, practical, and effective in alleviating social anxiety among bullied junior high school students. The study employed a Research and Development (R&D) framework utilizing the five-phase ADDIE model (Analysis, Design, Development, Implementation, and Evaluation). Product efficacy was examined through a pre-experimental one-group pretest-posttest design involving eight eighth-grade students at SMP Negeri 1 Singaraja. The results established that the content validity of the e-module achieved an Aiken’s V coefficient between 0.875 and 1.00 from media and subject-matter experts, denoting very high validity. Practicality assessments yielded 87.33% from school counselors and 87.83% from students, placing both within the highly practical threshold. Inferential evaluation confirmed a statistically significant reduction in social anxiety scores (t=17.401;p=0.000<0.05) alongside an average score decline of 32.125 points. ABSTRAK Perilaku bullying merupakan salah satu persoalan krusial pada masa remaja yang berdampak destruktif terhadap kesehatan mental, khususnya memicu timbulnya kecemasan sosial pada korban. Korban bullying kerap mengalami ketakutan irasional terhadap evaluasi negatif, menarik diri dari pergaulan sebaya, serta mengalami penurunan keterlibatan akademik di sekolah. Di sisi lain, pelayanan bimbingan dan konseling di sekolah masih menghadapi keterbatasan alokasi waktu layanan serta minimnya ketersediaan media intervensi digital yang terstruktur. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mengembangkan e-modul konseling cognitive behavioral dengan teknik cognitive restructuring yang valid, praktis, dan efektif guna mereduksi kecemasan sosial siswa korban bullying di Sekolah Menengah Pertama. Metode penelitian menerapkan pendekatan Research and Development (R&D) menggunakan model ADDIE (Analysis, Design, Development, Implementation, dan Evaluation). Uji keefektifan produk menggunakan desain pre-experimental dengan bentuk one-group pretest-posttest design yang melibatkan 8 siswa kelas VIII SMP Negeri 1 Singaraja. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa validitas isi e-modul memperoleh koefisien Aiken’s V sebesar 0,875 hingga 1,00 pada uji ahli media dan materi dengan kriteria validitas sangat tinggi. Uji kepraktisan guru bimbingan dan konseling memperoleh persentase 87,33% serta kepraktisan siswa mencapai 87,83% dengan kategori sangat praktis. Uji efektivitas membuktikan adanya penurunan kecemasan sosial yang signifikan secara statistik (t=17,401;p=0,000<0,05) dengan selisih penurunan rata-rata sebesar 32,125 poin.

title: PERAN ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE DAN INFRASTRUKTUR DIGITAL DALAM MENINGKATKAN KETERLIBATAN AKADEMIK DAN EFEKTIVITAS BELAJAR MAHASISWA
container-title: EDUTECH : Jurnal Inovasi Pendidikan Berbantuan Teknologi
5ea9bceb2f3180b84a5816dcbcff96e3b3f5aa5e.abstract: The increasing integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and digital technologies into higher education has created new opportunities to support the learning process. However, the effectiveness of technology utilization is not solely determined by technical availability, but also by students' active involvement in learning activities. This study aims to analyze the role of AI utilization and digital infrastructure in enhancing learning effectiveness, with student engagement serving as a mediating variable among students at Institut Teknologi Kalimantan. A quantitative survey approach was administered to 347 active students across faculties and cohorts selected through multistage stratified sampling. Data were gathered using a five-point Likert scale questionnaire and analyzed using Partial Least Squares–Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) with a second-order construct through the Hierarchical Component Model. The results demonstrate that AI usage and digital infrastructure exert positive and significant effects on student engagement and learning effectiveness. Furthermore, student engagement partially mediates the effects of AI usage and digital infrastructure on learning effectiveness, with AI usage exhibiting a more dominant total contribution. ABSTRAK Perkembangan Artificial Intelligence (AI) dan teknologi digital telah memberikan peluang baru dalam mendukung proses pembelajaran di perguruan tinggi. Namun, efektivitas pemanfaatan teknologi tidak hanya ditentukan oleh ketersediaan fasilitas semata, melainkan juga oleh keterlibatan aktif mahasiswa dalam proses akademik. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis peran pemanfaatan AI dan infrastruktur digital dalam meningkatkan efektivitas belajar dengan keterlibatan mahasiswa (student engagement) sebagai variabel mediasi pada mahasiswa Institut Teknologi Kalimantan. Pendekatan kuantitatif dengan metode survei diterapkan kepada 347 mahasiswa aktif dari berbagai fakultas dan angkatan yang dipilih melalui teknik multistage stratified sampling. Pengumpulan data menggunakan kuesioner skala Likert lima tingkat dan dianalisis menggunakan Partial Least Squares–Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) dengan model konstruk tingkat kedua melalui Hierarchical Component Model. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa penggunaan AI dan infrastruktur digital berpengaruh positif dan signifikan terhadap keterlibatan mahasiswa serta efektivitas belajar. Selain itu, keterlibatan mahasiswa terbukti memediasi secara parsial pengaruh penggunaan AI dan infrastruktur digital terhadap efektivitas belajar, dengan pemanfaatan AI memberikan kontribusi total yang lebih dominan.

title: Drivers of supply chain resilience: the roles of artificial intelligence, knowledge sharing, blockchain adoption and radical innovation capabilities
container-title: International Journal of Productivity and Performance Management
5292c03a4c688f30746e4e5434e013cb5a5451ee.abstract: Purpose Global supply chain dynamics have undergone significant changes due to economic uncertainty, logistical disruptions and large-scale crises. Drawing on Dynamic Capabilities Theory, this study examines the relationships among artificial intelligence, knowledge sharing, radical innovation capabilities, blockchain adoption and supply chain resilience. Design/methodology/approach Survey data were collected from 208 firms operating in Türkiye's foreign trade sector and analyzed using structural equation modeling and moderation analysis. Findings The results indicate that artificial intelligence facilitates knowledge sharing, which is positively associated with supply chain resilience. While knowledge sharing is significantly related to radical innovation capabilities, radical innovation capabilities do not exhibit a direct association with supply chain resilience. In addition, blockchain adoption strengthens the relationship between knowledge sharing and supply chain resilience, suggesting that blockchain enhances the effectiveness of knowledge-sharing mechanisms in fostering resilience. Originality/value This study contributes to the productivity and performance management literature by integrating digital technologies and knowledge-based capabilities within a unified framework to explain supply chain resilience from a dynamic capabilities perspective. The findings also provide practical insights for managers and policymakers by demonstrating that digital technologies alone may not generate resilience unless they are aligned with complementary organizational capabilities, such as knowledge sharing and innovation-oriented structures.

title: Integrating Generative Artificial Intelligence into Financial Management Teaching: An Instructional Design for Finance Leasing
container-title: European Journal of Business, Economics & Management
6981d5022fb8e52d69b2b75160a632c60abcb9df.abstract: Financial Management courses often fall short in linking computational training with financing decision analysis. Taking finance leasing as a case, this paper explores how generative artificial intelligence (generative AI) can be brought into the classroom. The instructional design is built around a scenario in which a private hospital finances the purchase of medical equipment, and it connects rent calculation, comparison of financing alternatives, and scrutiny of decision conditions through a four-stage process: independent calculation, AI questioning, professional verification, and decision reconstruction. Students first carry out the calculations and form a preliminary financing judgment, then use generative AI to interrogate financing constraints and uncover the assumptions behind a plan, and finally verify the AI-generated content against financial principles to strengthen their argument. The design takes students' own judgments as the starting point of human-AI interaction and assigns AI the role of revealing and examining the conditions under which a financing plan holds, rather than making the decision for them. This approach offers a reference for bringing generative AI into accounting and finance courses.

title: Effects of sleep manipulation on athletic performance, cognitive function, and recovery: a systematic review of experimental studies
container-title: BMC Sports Science, Medicine and Rehabilitation
88a55b6138bb464352333f7d41ff100bcfd3da11.abstract: Abstract Sleep is important for recovery, cognitive and physical performance. Sleep manipulation (sleep extension, napping and sleep restriction) is a new way to enhance performance for athletes. This systematic review explored the effects of sleep manipulation on physical performance, cognitive performance and psychophysiological responses in the active and athletic population. The literature was searched in PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar for eligible studies published between 2011 and 2025, yielding 1,586 records. After removing duplicates and applying the exclusion and inclusion criteria, 15 intervention studies (randomized controlled trials and crossover) were identified. Data were extracted and the results synthesised in a structured narrative format due to variability in the designs and measures used. Sleep extension led to enhanced performance, including greater distance run in the shuttle run (+ 9.5 m), lower fatigue index (− 8.1%), shorter reaction time (− 43.6 ms), better sprint time (− 0.7 s) and improved accuracy ( ~ + 9%). Sleep extension led to a ~ 3% improvement in endurance, whereas sleep restriction led to a ~ 3% decrease in endurance, alongside higher fatigue and cognitive performance decrements. Daytime napping showed mixed results, with longer naps (60–90 min) enhancing maximum voluntary contraction (+ 74 N), distance (+ 89 m), and lowering perceived fatigue (− 1.9 units) and sleepiness (− 4.33 units). The effects of brief naps (20 min) were variable, with some minor performance deficits (+ 0.026 s in sprint time). Overall, sleep extension was generally associated with favourable physical, cognitive, and recovery-related outcomes, whereas sleep restriction was associated with adverse performance effects. The effects of daytime napping were more context-dependent and appeared to vary according to prior sleep status, nap duration, and subsequent performance demands.

title: Pengembangan pembelajaran di perguruan tinggi melalui pemanfaatan artificial intelligence (AI)
container-title: Prosiding Seminar Nasional Sanata Dharma Berbagi
41e60987f1aca9ee8c5b60224b34aeb80d11d79b.abstract: Perkembangan teknologi digital mendorong penggunaan artificial intelligence (AI) dalam pembelajaran di perguruan tinggi. AI dapat digunakan untuk membantu mahasiswa dan dosen dalam berbagai kegiatan pembelajaran. Kajian ini bertujuan untuk mengetahui pemanfaatan AI dalam mendukung pengembangan pembelajaran di perguruan tinggi. Penelitian ini menggunakan metode Systematic Literature Review (SLR) dengan mengumpulkan dan mengkaji artikel ilmiah yang relevan mengenai penggunaan AI dalam pembelajaran perguruan tinggi. Artikel yang dikaji merupakan publikasi tahun 2022–2026 yang membahas penggunaan AI dalam proses pembelajaran, pengalaman belajar mahasiswa, pembelajaran adaptif, pemberian umpan balik, pengembangan bahan ajar, evaluasi pembelajaran, serta kemandirian dan interaksi belajar. Data yang diperoleh kemudian dianalisis dan disusun untuk melihat berbagai bentuk pemanfaatan AI dalam pembelajaran. Hasil kajian menunjukkan bahwa AI dapat membantu mahasiswa dalam memahami materi, mencari informasi, mengembangkan ide, memperoleh penjelasan, dan mendapatkan umpan balik selama proses belajar. Bagi dosen, AI dapat membantu dalam menyusun bahan ajar, mengembangkan materi, merancang kegiatan pembelajaran, dan memberikan umpan balik kepada mahasiswa. Penggunaan AI juga dapat mendukung pembelajaran yang lebih personal, fleksibel, interaktif, dan efisien. Dengan demikian, AI dapat menjadi teknologi pendukung yang membantu mahasiswa dan dosen dalam mengembangkan proses pembelajaran di perguruan tinggi dan mencapai tujuan.

title: Smart Leaf Identification and Analysis using Artificial Intelligence
container-title: Journal of ICT Research and Applications
d174267717fd7402da76c473cb8a178f6425334b.abstract: This paper describes a leaf classification framework based on machine learning methodologies. The dataset included 36 leaf species with 340 instances and 16 features. Decision Tree, Logistic Regression, Support Vector Machine, XGBoost, AdaBoost, and Random Forest were applied initially on the raw dataset. It was found that Decision Tree, XGBoost and Random Forest performed well, with accuracy scores of 53%, 60% and 85% respectively. After feature reduction based on Information Gain and correlation matrix analysis, four highly correlated features were removed. This led to a marginal improvement in accuracy to 60% for Decision Tree and to 65% percentage for XG Boost, while the accuracy of Random Forest dropped to 74%. We also applied SMOTE (Synthetic Minority Oversampling Technique) to balance the raw dataset. This enhanced the accuracy of Random Forest and XGBoost to 91% and 81% respectively. With Computer Vision, we achieved an accuracy of 66% for SVM, 61% for Random Forest, 43% for K-NN and 37% for the Decision Tree classifier on the image dataset. The pre-trained VGG16 model achieved an impressive 90.47% accuracy, outperforming the custom CNN model and conventional models like Linear Discriminant Analysis (LDA) and KNN with various K-values from the literature

title: Terapia Ocupacional na terceira idade: Intervenções domiciliares inovadoras para promoção da autonomia, participação social e envelhecimento ativo
Terapia Ocupacional en la tercera edad: Intervenciones domiciliarias innovadoras para la promoción de la autonomía, la participación social y el envejecimiento activo
Occupational Therapy in later life: Innovative home-based interventions to promote autonomy, social participation and active ageing
container-title: Research, Society and Development
a8f31707a90d9744cbf96fed022e0cf6f152c701.abstract: El envejecimiento poblacional exige estrategias que preserven la autonomía y la participación social de las personas mayores en su domicilio. El objetivo fue sintetizar la evidencia publicada entre 2020 y 2026 sobre intervenciones domiciliarias de Terapia Ocupacional orientadas a la autonomía, la participación social y el envejecimiento activo de personas mayores. Revisión sistemática conducida según PRISMA 2020, con pregunta PICOS, riesgo de sesgo evaluado con RoB 2, ROBINS-I y JBI, síntesis sin metaanálisis guiada por SWiM y certeza de la evidencia según GRADE. Se realizaron 31 búsquedas el 17 de octubre de 2026; de 288 registros identificados, se incluyeron 12 estudios, nueve de ellos ensayos clínicos aleatorizados, con 3.214 participantes. Las intervenciones se agruparon en adaptación del contexto domiciliario, actividad integrada a la rutina, apoyo al cuidador y seguimiento híbrido. El programa de eliminación de riesgos domiciliarios redujo en un 38% la tasa de caídas, mientras que la evaluación ambiental aislada no redujo las caídas en una muestra de mayor riesgo. El programa de actividades personalizadas redujo la necesidad de asistencia en las actividades de la vida diaria de personas con demencia y mejoró el bienestar de los cuidadores, y la telerrehabilitación tras fractura de cadera mejoró las actividades instrumentales. Ocho ensayos presentaron algunas preocupaciones y uno, alto riesgo de sesgo, y la certeza de la evidencia fue baja o muy baja. Las intervenciones domiciliarias multicomponentes centradas en metas significativas son prometedoras, pero faltan ensayos con desenlaces de participación social, lo que fundamenta el modelo CASA-Ativa propuesto.

title: Being as cosmic processuality: Cognitive Psychiatry, a cosmogenetic theory of intelligibility and a critique of Heidegger’s ontology
El Ser como procesualidad cósmica: Psiquiatría Cognitiva, una teoría cosmogenética de la inteligibilidad y una crítica a la ontología de Heidegger
O Ser como processualidade cósmica: Psiquiatria Cognitiva, uma teoria cosmogenética da inteligibilidade e uma crítica à ontologia de Heidegger
container-title: Research, Society and Development
65fc29a8b47bef2162294197cb589f8b09fd2ce8.abstract: Heidegger’s ontological difference between Being and beings raises a question that remains open: does the manifestation and intelligibility of beings require an autonomous ontological problem, or can both be understood as dimensions of cosmic processuality itself? This article aims to propose, from the standpoint of Cognitive Psychiatry, a cosmogenetic and processual conception of Being and to examine its consequences for a critical reading of Heideggerian ontology. It is a theoretical proposition essay supported by a narrative review of literature published between 2021 and 2026. Intelligibility is neither an exclusively mental property nor an ontological dimension separate from the cosmos; it derives from the historical, causal, temporal and evolutionary organization of reality. Entities are relatively stable coagulations of processes, and the human organism, including its central nervous system, is a configuration of the same processuality that produces them. Cognition is co-praxization, an active participation of the organism in the processes of the world that involves Gestalt perception, conativity, causality, temporality, action, significance and valuation. Being is therefore cosmic processuality in its constitutive, manifestative and intelligible unity, and human understanding of Being is a reflexive perspectivization of that processuality. Heidegger recognizes pre-reflexive understanding and the temporal constitution of existence, but grants philosophical autonomy to a dimension that can be read as reflexively isolated. The phenomenological priority of an understanding does not demonstrate its cosmogenetic priority. Implications for Psychiatry and ten central propositions are presented.

title: A Tool, Not a Voice: Artificial Intelligence, Human Speech, and Christian Communicative Agency
container-title: Philosophia Reformata
fe8c930cf21c5318e08426d5a4ca0192fe72535d.abstract: Abstract This article asks what it means, from a Christian philosophical perspective, to say that artificial intelligence can mediate human speech but cannot possess voice. Language-generating systems and translation systems produce outputs that recipients use within religious, journalistic, and educational practices. The article distinguishes communicative uptake from voice, authorship, and responsible agency. Voice is not a property of output but the embodied, relational, and morally answerable act of a person; authorship names how a human or institution appropriates and answers for a text. While AI may extend, translate, and summarize human speech, it cannot supply its own accountability. Drawing on Reformational philosophy and Vatican materials, the article treats AI-assisted liturgical translation as a limit case, distinguishing translation and summarization from open-ended generation, whose outputs lack testimonial authority unless independently verified and responsibly adopted. It concludes with five criteria for Christian communication: accountability, transparency, dignity, embodied voice, and attention to linguistic inequality.

title: Reimagining adolescent education with ephegogy: generative AI and active learning in practice
container-title: Artificial Intelligence in Education
1d36e8829077dcd2cac6018973035fc5acb85d04.abstract: Purpose This paper introduces ephegogy, a theory addressing the gap between traditional educational models and adolescents' developmental needs in artificial intelligence (AI)-augmented societies. Blending constructivism, connectivism and generativism, it explores how integrating generative AI (GenAI) and active learning can scaffold motivation, autonomy, and relevance for adolescent learners. Design/methodology/approach A mixed-methods case study conducted in a single secondary-school geography course during 2024–2025. Quantitative data came from matched pre- and post-intervention surveys measuring motivation and self-efficacy (N = 17; N = 11 for the self-efficacy composite) and locus of control (N = 12), using instruments adapted for an under-14, predominantly English-as-an-additional-language cohort. A separate matched engagement survey (N = 24) and an end-of-course co-creation survey (N = 33) provided further data. Qualitative data comprised 74 individual student reflections analysed thematically using the cultural-historical activity theory (CHAT) framework, alongside open-text survey responses from 74 students. The study was designed using three frameworks (self-determination theory, ephegogy and CHAT). Findings Findings are associational and exploratory, specific to this pilot. Composite motivation increased significantly (p = 0.043, d = 0.53), led by a significant rise in school enjoyment (p = 0.028). On a separate instrument, confidence in using AI tools showed the largest single increase (p = 0.016) and motivation relative to traditional courses also rose (p = 0.040); as several items were examined, these are treated as exploratory. Self-efficacy and locus of control showed no reliable change. Qualitatively, choice, the learning contract, and resource autonomy were dominant themes; most students disclosed and reflected on their AI use, and the modal student experience was ambivalent, valuing autonomy while finding it demanding. Research limitations/implications As a single pilot case study with small, matched samples, no control group and a single teacher-researcher as sole coder, findings are context-specific and cannot support causal claims. Future research should evaluate the framework with larger samples, control conditions, and across diverse cultural contexts and disciplines. Practical implications Ephegogy provides actionable strategies for scaffolding student autonomy and ethical AI use within project-based learning. Tools such as the Student-Author Voice (SAV) rubric support metacognitive reflection and responsible co-creation, assessing authored voice rather than relying on AI detection. Social implications Ephegogy provides actionable strategies for scaffolding student autonomy and ethical AI use within project-based learning. Tools such as the SAV rubric support metacognitive reflection and responsible co-creation, assessing authored voice rather than relying on AI detection. Originality/value Ephegogy reconceptualises adolescent education for the AI era as a distinct developmental stage requiring its own framework, operationalised through gradual immersion and the assessment of authored voice. This paper reports an initial classroom pilot offering preliminary, transferable insights rather than confirmatory evidence.

title: From Promise to Peril: generative artificial intelligence's potential to deepen educational inequalities in geographically diverse contexts
container-title: Artificial Intelligence in Education
738cfd05a1ab75e74055fb96c77cb5f03ec65d3f.abstract: Purpose This study critically examines how van Dijk's Digital Divide Theory applies to generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) access in regional, remote and rural (RRR) educational contexts. It interrogates whether a framework designed for standardised digital tools adequately captures GenAI-specific barriers, while mapping where existing research concentrates and where significant gaps remain across van Dijk's four dimensions of access. Design/methodology/approach A scoping review was conducted using the Population, Concept, Context (PCC) framework across four academic databases, with AI-assisted Boolean search development validated through pilot testing and supervisory oversight. Strict inclusion criteria focused on peer-reviewed publications examining GenAI in RRR educational settings. Twenty-nine articles were analysed using van Dijk's four-dimensional framework: material access, skills access, usage access and motivational access. Findings Material and skills access emerged as the most researched dimensions, with material access representing a necessary but insufficient condition for equitable GenAI engagement and skills access requiring interventions across student, educator and policy levels simultaneously. Usage patterns cannot be assumed to follow naturally from material and skills access, requiring sustained time investment, pedagogical framing and institutional support. Motivational access remained critically under-researched, with only one study explicitly examining this dimension. The synthesis suggests sequential relationships across the four dimensions, where foundational precursors in material, skills and usage shape the conditions under which motivational engagement develops. This sequential pattern is presented as a provisional theoretical proposition warranting targeted empirical investigation. Research limitations/implications The interconnected nature of access barriers creates systemic constraints extending beyond van Dijk's original conceptualisation. The synthesis suggests that sequential relationships between dimensions help explain why motivational access remains under-researched, with GenAI lacking foundational precursors necessary for widespread motivational engagement in RRR communities. Evidence-based policy addressing material and skills dimensions becomes essential for preventing systematic exclusion from GenAI's transformative educational potential. Practical implications This research reveals that GenAI introduces a less visible form of digital exclusion in regional, remote and rural (RRR) educational contexts. Unlike previous digital divides characterised by observable access deficits, GenAI enables superficially sophisticated outputs from shallow engagement. This produces performative usage, defined here as the production of well-formed GenAI outputs that mask shallow understanding of subject content. Students in RRR communities may appear to use GenAI productively while developing neither subject mastery nor critical evaluation skills. Educational institutions serving RRR populations must therefore develop context-specific assessment frameworks capable of distinguishing between performative and meaningful GenAI engagement, ensuring that technology deployment addresses rather than obscures the educational disadvantages these communities already experience. Social implications This research highlights that motivational disengagement from GenAI in regional, remote and rural (RRR) communities emerges not from technology rejection but from cascading structural barriers. When infrastructure deficits create skills gaps and repeated failure diminishes perceived effort-to-benefit ratios, self-reinforcing cycles of technological disengagement develop that persist even when access improves. Motivational access remains the least researched dimension of GenAI's digital divide, despite being central to the conditions under which other access dimensions translate into sustained engagement. Policymakers and educational institutions serving RRR communities must recognise that addressing material and skills barriers alone proves insufficient without concurrent attention to how these compounding disadvantages shape willingness and aspiration to engage with GenAI technologies. Originality/value This study provides the first application of van Dijk's Digital Divide Theory as an analytical framework for examining generative artificial intelligence education research in regional, remote and rural (RRR) contexts. Theoretically, it proposes a provisional reconceptualisation of van Dijk's sequential dimensions, suggesting that material access supports skills development, which supports usage patterns, which subsequently shape motivational engagement. This proposition offers a coherent explanation for why motivational access remains critically under-researched in RRR communities, namely that foundational precursors necessary for motivational engagement are themselves absent. Practically, by exposing significant gaps in understanding how cascading access barriers shape GenAI engagement in geographically disadvantaged settings, this review establishes the empirical justification for targeted research into GenAI adoption and implementation within RRR educational institutions.
