title: Association between prenatal cannabis and tobacco co‐exposure and cognition in childhood: Insights from the US adolescent brain cognitive development study
container-title: Addiction
9eaf4dd773c9d8c14ef55e7892bc77894e0aa177.abstract: Abstract Background and aims While evidence on the individual effects of prenatal cannabis and tobacco exposure on offspring cognition is accumulating, their combined impact remains understudied. Therefore, we examined the interaction between prenatal cannabis and tobacco exposure on fluid (e.g. reasoning abilities) and crystallized (e.g. acquired knowledge) cognition in middle childhood. We also compared cognition in children with prenatal co‐exposure to those with cannabis‐only exposure, tobacco‐only exposure and no exposure. Design Cross‐sectional exploratory analysis of baseline data from an ongoing longitudinal cohort study. Setting Data collected between 2016 and 2018 from the United States‐based Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development study were extracted. Participants Children ( n = 8706), aged 9–11 years old, were parsed into four prenatal exposure groups: co‐exposure ( n = 236); cannabis only ( n = 195); tobacco only ( n = 803); and no exposure ( n = 7472). Measurements Prenatal co‐exposure was measured as a binary variable (yes/no) based on maternal/caregiver retrospective report. Fluid and crystallized scores were derived from the National Institutes of Health (NIH) Toolbox cognitive battery; scores ranged from 44 to 131 and 51115 for fluid and crystallized cognition, respectively. We employed linear mixed‐effects models to examine interactions between cannabis and tobacco exposure and group differences in fluid and crystallized scores, adjusting for covariates selected a priori using a Directed Acyclic Graph. Results For fluid cognition, a statistically significant interaction emerged between prenatal cannabis and tobacco exposure [beta coefficient (β) = −2.08, 95% confidence interval (CI) = −4.13 to −0.03]. Cannabis only (β = 2.13, 95% CI = 0.21–4.05) and unexposed children (β = 1.39, 95% CI = 0.03–2.76) had statistically significantly higher fluid scores than co‐exposed children, while the difference with tobacco‐only exposed children was not statistically significant (β = 1.34, 95% CI = −0.14 to 2.82). No statistically significant interaction was observed between prenatal co‐exposure and crystallized cognition (β = −0.62, 95% CI = −1.87 to 0.64), and crystallized scores did not statistically significantly differ between the co‐exposed group and the cannabis‐only (β = 0.66, 95% CI = −0.51 to 1.84), tobacco‐only (β = 0.19, 95% CI = −0.71 to 1.1) or unexposed groups (β = 0.24, 95% CI = −0.6 to 1.08). Summary Prenatal co‐exposure to cannabis and tobacco appears to be associated with poorer fluid cognition among children, but not poorer crystallized cognition, compared with cannabis‐only and unexposed groups. These findings should be interpreted with caution given the potential for residual confounding by shared genetic liability, substance exposure misclassification and selection bias. The cross‐sectional design of this study precludes causal inference.

title: Survey of Physician Attitudes on Artificial Intelligence
c48219bcd70c50c39491c08463a4308ed1cd4ac9.abstract: Abstract Objective To better understand how physicians view the potential use of artificial intelligence (AI) in their practices. Method We conducted an online cross-sectional survey of 1,258 physicians (MD, DO, MBBS or equivalent) in the United States (US) and Canada from December 2023 through February 2026. The survey contained 34 questions focused on 6 areas: (1) demographics, (2) training, (3) clinical benefits, (4) clinical concerns, (5) clinical AI prediction tools, and (6) generative AI. Results A total of 130 completed surveys were received (response rate, 10%). Top specialties included psychiatry (46.2%), internal medicine (14.6%) and pediatrics (13.8%). A total of 16.9% had training in computer science or information technology and 40.8% in statistics. Nearly half (46.9%) had no formal training in AI and were self-taught. Those with training in AI received it through vendors or at work. Sixty to seventy percent thought AI would provide diagnostic aid or treatment recommendations, but half did not feel adequately trained to safely use AI in practice. Over 70% thought it could help with administrative tasks. More than 80% were worried about errors, misinformation, or biases in the data. Conclusion There is a growing sense that AI in medicine could be helpful with specific tasks. Ongoing training, education, and study are needed to determine how AI will best integrate into clinical practice. Artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly being marketed for and integrated into clinical medicine. Previous physician surveys have shown that physicians are optimistic, yet cautious, about its implementation. This study utilizes a novel survey tool to assess physician attitudes toward the integration of AI in practice, highlighting the desire for ongoing education around and monitoring of AI among physicians in the United States and Canada. There is a growing recognition that AI, while a powerful tool, may harbor biases, promulgate misinformation, and lead to harm to patients, and requires ongoing training and oversight by humans.

title: Head-to-Head Comparison of Flortaucipir and MK6240 tau-PET to Detect Subtle Objective Cognitive Impairment in Clinically Unimpaired Individuals
c31d480a76a665c280032802bfa6a795b4b1f49d.abstract: Abstract Background and Objectives Tau-PET is associated with subtle objective cognitive impairment (SOCI) in clinically unimpaired (CU) individuals, but whether the spatial patterns and strengths of these associations differ across tracers remains unclear. We performed a head-to-head comparison of [¹□F]MK6240 and [¹□F]flortaucipir to investigate their associations with SOCI in CU individuals. Methods We cross-sectionally assessed CU participants from the HEAD study who underwent both tau-PET scans. Linear regressions examined associations between domain-specific cognition and tau burden using standardized uptake value ratios (SUVR) in regional and voxelwise analyses, alongside regional spatial extent of tauopathy (SEOT) measures. Tau burden was compared across groups representing different levels of SOCI. Models adjusted for age, sex, and education, with additional adjustment for amyloid-β burden. Centiloid-stratified analyses examined associations across amyloid-β burden levels. Results Among 297 participants (mean [SD] age, 67.0 [8.4] years; 179 [60.3%] female), higher [¹□F]MK6240 SUVR was associated with poorer memory performance. Greater SEOT with either tracer was associated with poorer memory and showed nominal associations with executive dysfunction. Regional association strengths did not differ significantly between tracers, while SEOT yielded comparable or stronger associations than SUVR. Centiloid-stratified analyses revealed tau– cognition associations primarily at intermediate and high amyloid-β burden. [¹□F]MK6240 showed more spatially extensive voxelwise associations with memory and across SOCI group comparisons. Regional analyses also yielded more statistically significant differences across SOCI groups with [¹□F]MK6240 than with flortaucipir. These differences were predominantly driven by participants meeting actuarial mild cognitive impairment criteria, who exhibited greater tau burden than groups with less pronounced psychometric impairment. Across tracers, SEOT yielded more consistently significant differences among SOCI groups than SUVR. Discussion Both tracers showed associations with SOCI in CU individuals, with broadly comparable regional association strengths despite differences in the spatial extent and statistical significance of their findings. SEOT complemented SUVR by identifying additional significant associations and group differences. These findings suggest that tracer choice and quantification approach may influence the spatial distribution and statistical significance of observed tau–cognition relationships without necessarily altering their overall strength.

title: A relational political economy of violence in education: An intersectional analysis of disability, gender, ethnicity, language and generation
container-title: European Educational Research Journal
a728bc6de6d4b3378112fc2bff0fa262ad2c1890.abstract: Violence against children with disabilities is a global concern, encompassing both physical and psychological violence. Corporal punishment, a key form of physical violence against children, is legally prohibited in many countries. However, it remains prevalent, including in parts of Europe. Despite growing attention to school violence, limited research has centred the experiences of students with disabilities from an intersectional perspective. This article draws on an exploratory qualitative study, focusing on the experiences of violence among students with visual impairments in a private school in Nepal. The findings show how judgements of ability differences are shaped not only by disability but also by expectations of obedience to school authorities, global and local language hierarchies, especially the high value placed on English as a global language and gendered restrictions, contributing to the reproduction of violence. The analysis suggests that an intersectional approach, which considers the entanglement of broader sociocultural, economic, political and global processes, is useful for understanding how violence against students with disabilities is reproduced through everyday relationships, by illustrating how pathologisation operates intersectionally. Building on this analysis, the article suggests a relational political economy of violence, highlighting how human relationships can mediate structural power and individual experiences.

title: Information Disclosure Transformation in the Digital Economy: The Role of Digital Infrastructure in Visual Disclosure
container-title: Accounting & Finance
cef22ac94baf1d427abf31c1c415d80f05b03bca.abstract: ABSTRACT We investigate how digital infrastructure development affects corporate visual disclosure, distinguishing between discretionary image‐based formats and structured table‐based formats. Using data on Chinese A‐share‐listed firms from 2009 to 2022, we find that improvements in digital infrastructure are associated with greater use of image‐based visual disclosure in annual reports, whereas we detect no statistically significant association with table‐based visual disclosure. Mechanism analyses show that this relationship is driven by both supply‐side enhancements in firms' organizational capabilities and demand‐side incentives to cater to external users' information‐processing demands, as evidenced by stronger effects among firms with more extensive explicit discussions of digital transformation in their MD&A and higher institutional ownership. We also find that this effect is more pronounced in regions with higher levels of AI computing power development, as well as among firms with a lower propensity for earnings manipulation and fewer financing constraints. This paper expands the theoretical framework for understanding changes in corporate disclosure formats in the digital economy and offers implications for policymakers, investors and firms.

title: Combating Crisis with Organizational Compassion Intelligence and Virtue Framing
container-title: South Asian Journal of Business and Management Cases
a89350bae1707f87a4ecef20c3e6ed575e14d656.abstract: When an unprecedented crisis strikes, neither individuals nor organizations are prepared. Hence, organizations must demonstrate agility in devising strategies to face the challenges posed by the unexpected crisis. An essential aspect of any crisis management plan is the compassion that organizations can show towards employees impacted by the crisis. In this research case, we focus on a single higher education institution to understand what enabled it to enact compassion initiatives over an extended period of collective crisis, overcoming bureaucratic hurdles, fears of personal safety and the paucity of helping hands. These initiatives were undertaken for its direct employees and several social communities impacted by the pandemic. Using an inductive process, we interviewed four focal actors who initiated, planned and executed several initiatives for internal and external stakeholders. The inductive analysis of the interview transcripts brought forward the concept of organizational compassion intelligence inculcated through a combination of individual actors’ personal traits and organizational practices that foster a culture of compassion.

title: Governing artificial intelligence in public services: accountability, transparency and democratic AI governance
container-title: Transforming Government: People, Process and Policy
251e48e292435e1d95249329194f0b7c4eb313d0.abstract: Purpose This paper aims to examine how democratic governments can regulate artificial intelligence (AI) in public services through accountable, transparent and institutionally governable frameworks. It addresses the governance gap between rapid AI adoption and limited democratic regulatory oversight by proposing the Transparent-Accountable-Governable (TAG) Framework. Design/methodology/approach This study adopts a qualitative conceptual research design using comparative policy analysis. It critically synthesises interdisciplinary literature in public administration, digital governance and AI ethics alongside the OECD AI Principles (2025), UNESCO Recommendation on the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence (2021), the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) AI Risk Management Framework (2023) and the European Union Artificial Intelligence Act (2024) to develop the TAG Framework. Findings The analysis argues that trustworthy AI depends upon the interaction of transparency, accountability and governability rather than ethical principles alone. The proposed TAG Framework provides an institutional governance model applicable across welfare administration, healthcare, taxation, policing and disaster management. Research limitations/implications This is a conceptual study and therefore does not empirically validate the TAG Framework. Future research should evaluate its applicability through comparative cross-country case studies and institutional assessments of AI implementation within public administration. Practical implications The framework offers policymakers practical guidance by recommending public AI registers, algorithmic impact assessments, meaningful human oversight, independent auditing and adaptive regulatory coordination to strengthen democratic governance and institutional accountability. Social implications By emphasising explainability, citizen participation and procedural justice, the TAG Framework provides a conceptual basis for examining how AI governance can contribute to inclusive and equitable public services. It also highlights the risks of algorithmic bias and opaque decision-making, both of which may undermine public trust. Originality/value This paper proposes the TAG Framework to examine AI governance in democratic public administration. It brings transparency and accountability together with governability, understood as the capacity of public institutions to coordinate their activities, monitor AI systems, learn from experience and adapt governance arrangements over time.

title: Research Ethics Committee and Community Engagement Readiness for Artificial Intelligence in African Clinical Trials: A Systematic Review (Preprint)
779f3983c25c92bc88110434cb73b92b8cd4f386.abstract: BACKGROUND Sub-Saharan Africa bears over 20% of the global burden of disease but hosts only 2% to 3% of global clinical trials. While artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly integrated into trial design, recruitment, safety monitoring, and data synthesis, the operational readiness of African Research Ethics Committees (RECs) and the alignment of community engagement (CE) models with AI paradigms remain insufficiently synthesized. OBJECTIVE To systematically appraise and synthesize empirical evidence and formal policy guidance on: (1) African REC capacity to evaluate AI-integrated clinical trials; (2) documented socio-technical oversight challenges; and (3) AI-adapted community engagement models across Africa. METHODS Conducted per PRISMA 2020 guidelines and registered on PROSPERO (PROSPERO ID: CRD420261530035). Eight databases (PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, CINAHL, Cochrane Library, Global Health, AJOL, and WHO Afro) and six grey repositories were searched from January 1, 2000, to September 30, 2026. The SPIDER framework guided selection. Editorials, commentaries, opinion pieces, news features, non-African studies, and non-clinical AI papers were strictly excluded. Methodological quality was appraised using MMAT (2018) for primary empirical studies and AACODS for policy frameworks. Synthesis followed Braun and Clarke’s Reflexive Thematic Analysis, with confidence assessed via GRADE-CERQual. RESULTS Of 1,912 records identified, 18 met strict inclusion criteria (12 primary empirical African studies and 6 formal policy frameworks). Although binding national guidance has emerged (e.g., South African NDoH 2024 Ethics Guidelines), operational REC readiness remains low. Key findings demonstrate severe technical literacy deficits among REC members, absence of specialized AI review SOPs in most institutions, algorithmic opacity, data extractivism risks, and liability voids. Community engagement remains largely conceptual, with traditional static consent models failing to address dynamic algorithms. GRADE-CERQual confidence in overall evidence was moderate. CONCLUSIONS African RECs face significant operational bottlenecks in overseeing AI trials. Priorities include institutionalizing competency-based AI training, establishing regional computational advisory panels under AVAREF, enforcing data sovereignty, and co-designing relational, Ubuntu-based community engagement frameworks. CLINICALTRIAL This was a systematic review and registered on the PROSPERO site (PROSPERO ID: CRD420261530035)

title: Artificial Intelligence Literacy and Educational Impact among Iraqi Nursing Students: A Cross-Sectional Survey
container-title: F1000Research
ac7bd1fea6400cc35ae538ce5bec4f94a68e2fad.abstract: Background and Objectives This study aimed to explore nursing students’ artificial intelligence literacy in terms of knowledge, attitudes, and practices and its impact on their educational input in Iraq. Methods A descriptive cross-sectional survey conducted across 100 nursing students from the College of Nursing, University of Baghdad, Iraq in 2025. The study utilized the Artificial Intelligence knowledge, attitudes, and practices scale. The Statistical Package for Social Sciences (SPSS), version 26 was used to examine the associations among the measured variables in the study. Results The majority of students (80.0%) had good knowledge level. More than half (59.0%) showed positive attitudes. Concerning practice, 34.0% often used AI, with 25.0% reporting most of the time/all the time, while 41.0% reported never/rarely. Age as a continuous variable showed a strong positive correlation with all KAP domains (p < 0.001). Academic year showed a highly significant association with all KAP scores (p < 0.01). Conclusion The study revealed that nursing students had a wavier level of artificial intelligence literacy of knowledge, attitude and practice and its application in nursing learning. Prioritize strategies should be applied in the nursing curricula to enhance students’ knowledge and translate positive attitudes into consistent practice, ultimately fostering effective integration of artificial intelligence in nursing education.

title: Conceptualizing the moral rebound effect–linking normative overload and stakeholder governance in circular economy transitions
container-title: Journal of Industrial Ecology
08c15cbd0aaa7e424a9669a610e59f3894d2ade7.abstract: Abstract Circular economy (CE) strategies are commonly promoted through morally charged narratives, yet they can still produce rebound effects, i.e., unintended consequences in resource use that offset anticipated benefits. Existing circular economy rebound (CER) research has largely explained such backfire through techno-economic mechanisms, while behavioral scholarship has highlighted moral licensing at the individual level. This article integrates these strands by conceptualizing moral rebound : a system-level deterioration of circular outcomes that can arise when morally saturated CE aspirations outpace the governance capacity required to operationalize them, thus promoting symbolic compliance or free-riding dynamics. Drawing on the ordonomic approach, this article conceptualizes moral rebound as a misalignment between normative semantics (ideas) and institutional incentives (governance). We develop a two-dimensional diagnostic space: normativity (realism vs. overload) and stakeholder governance (functional vs. dysfunctional), creating four heuristic regions within a continuous space capturing fluid real-world trajectories. We anchor this framework with illustrative cases, illuminating how selected backfire mechanisms documented in prior CER research may be interpreted through the lens of under-governed symbolic circularity. Finally, we derive three theoretically grounded propositions specifying conditions under which moral rebound may become more plausible, and propose possible governance levers for future empirical assessment, emphasizing verification and traceability, credible commitments across stakeholders, pacing of ambition, and intermediary coordination. This framework endogenizes moral discourse within rebound dynamics and offers a theoretical building block for systematic learning on moral rebound; one that calls for future empirical validation.

title: Flexible Artificial Neurons Based on NbO x for Robust Tactile Perception in a Wide Temperature Range
container-title: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces
642342862a53935903334e53b3da0839fd3c1974.abstract: Abstract Neuromorphic tactile sensing that emulates biological touch enables artificial systems to work with high efficiency and low energy consumption. As tactile-sensing scenarios may involve curved surfaces and different temperatures, artificial spiking afferent neurons require both flexibility and temperature robustness at the front end of artificial systems. Here, we report flexible artificial spiking neurons based on niobium oxide (NbOx) threshold-switching (TS) memristors prepared on polyimide (PI) substrates. Temperature-dependent transport analysis indicates that their temperature robustness is associated with a bulk switching pathway in the NbOx film. By integrating an oscillation circuit, the NbOx spiking afferent neurons convert analog inputs into frequency-modulated voltage spikes and retain oscillatory capability from –80 to 80 °C at a bending radius of 5 mm. Moreover, pressure sensors are coupled with the NbOx neurons to form mechanoreceptors that encode pressure as oscillation frequency. In the numerical tactile-recognition workflow, a convolutional neural network (CNN) classifies spatial frequency maps generated from the fitted pressure-to-frequency relations, achieving accuracies of 97.5% under the baseline condition and 93.2% at 80 °C at a bending radius of 5 mm. This work demonstrates that flexible NbOx neurons can serve as compact event-driven front ends for wide-temperature robotic tactile sensing.

title: Deliberate metaphor as a rhetorical strategy for corporate identity construction
container-title: Review of Cognitive Linguistics
a0cec37e204a09ee0e00d7644d9d36e141184b0e.abstract: Abstract Using Deliberate Metaphor Theory and metaphor scenario analysis, this study compares the corporate identities constructed by Huawei before and after the imposition of US sanctions. The results show both convergence and divergence in deliberate metaphors and corporate identities. Although Huawei has long been portrayed as partnership-focused, innovation-driven, talent-valued and law-abiding, the specific identities it has constructed change markedly. In the pre-sanction period, Huawei is portrayed as a confident navigator, a military-style agile organization, a discerning talent gardener, and a vigilant sentinel against organizational decay. In the post-sanction period, it is framed as a resilient and steadfast traveler, a forward-looking strategic force mobilizer in the intelligence era, a storm survivor, and a down-to-earth ecosystem cultivator, reorienting its communication focus from internal optimization to addressing external challenges and accomplishing digital-era missions. This study indicates that corporate identity is a dynamic, context-sensitive cognitive construct which enables corporations to build trust across diverse contexts.

title: Eye-tracking insights into cognitive mechanisms in L2 reading
container-title: Australian Review of Applied Linguistics
175aa67bc6416efa35cc78aae57b703a4d6373d4.abstract: Abstract This study investigates the differential roles of working memory (WM) and comprehension monitoring (CM) in predicting L2 reading comprehension among Persian EFL learners across beginner and advanced proficiency levels. Utilizing a sample of 80 participants, comprising 40 beginners and 40 advanced learners, various cognitive measures including a Reading Span Test (RST), an Eye-movement Inconsistency Detection Task (measuring gaze durations), and a reading test (RT) were employed to assess working memory capacity (WMC), comprehension monitoring, and reading performance. Group differences were examined using univariate and multivariate analyses, and a hierarchical multiple regression was conducted using the full sample to examine the predictive contributions of WMC and CM and their interactions with proficiency group. The results indicated that while both WM and CM are integral to L2 reading comprehension, their relative contributions differ significantly between beginner and advanced learners. While WM plays a crucial role in L2 reading comprehension among beginners, comprehension monitoring becomes more predictive for advanced learners. Specifically, beginner learners with higher WM capacity demonstrated better reading performance. In contrast, advanced learners benefited significantly from effective comprehension monitoring, as evidenced by longer gaze durations correlating with higher reading scores. The study offers insights into the cognitive mechanisms underlying L2 reading and highlights the need for proficiency-specific instructional approaches, with implications for theory, practice, and future research.

title: Culture or cognition?
container-title: Review of Cognitive Linguistics
bd05a49f19c9c16a4bf6c448f5bb16b750142bdb.abstract: Abstract Gender languages assign nouns to a category, such as masculine, feminine, neuter or common. Gender assignment is complicated and difficult to learn, as languages do not have specific rules for assigning a noun to one or the other gender. This study looks at gender assignment from the perspective of semantics and lexical semantic evolution, exemplified on the Indo-European family. Gender assignment has a semantic core, in which animate nouns are more likely to be masculine, inanimate nouns feminine and neuter, nature nouns masculine, and culture nouns feminine or neuter. To investigate how these patterns emerge, we study the evolutionary dynamics of these semantic properties on a gender-coded lexical data set for Indo-European. We find that masculine is a stable gender that remains in its semantic category and does not change. Feminine is also a stable category which may get lost or transfer to masculine. Neuter and common are unstable categories, which continuously alter or get lost in gender assignment. In sum, our result shows that the semantic core of gender — affected both by cognitive and cultural factors — remains stable and does not vacillate in evolution.

title: The cognitive–digital pathway to sustainable entrepreneurship: examining entrepreneurial mindfulness, digital adaptability and sustainable growth aspirations
container-title: Management & Sustainability: An Arab Review
d952b9a015248a60c1ea53a3e716529ca5d832bd.abstract: Purpose This study examines how entrepreneurial mindfulness and digital adaptability capability jointly influence opportunity recognition and sustainable growth aspirations. Grounded in Cognitive Appraisal Theory and Dynamic Capabilities Theory, it explores how entrepreneurs' cognitive awareness and adaptive digital capabilities interact to shape long-term growth aspirations in increasingly uncertain and digitally evolving business environments. Design/methodology/approach This study employed a quantitative cross-sectional design using survey data from 238 respondents (N = 238) engaged in digitally enabled entrepreneurial activities. Established measurement scales were used to measure the study constructs, and the hypothesized relationships were analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling. Findings The findings indicate that all hypotheses were supported. Entrepreneurial Mindfulness significantly influenced Opportunity Recognition (β = 0.566, t = 4.609, p &lt; 0.001) and Sustainable Growth Aspiration (β = 0.400, t = 5.363, p &lt; 0.001). Digital Adaptability Capability positively influenced Opportunity Recognition (β = 0.334, t = 2.560, p = 0.010) and Sustainable Growth Aspiration (β = 0.299, t = 3.689, p &lt; 0.001). Opportunity Recognition also positively affected Sustainable Growth Aspiration (β = 0.317, t = 4.744, p &lt; 0.001). Research limitations/implications The cross-sectional design limits causal inference, while the use of self-reported data and a sample of digitally active entrepreneurs in Indonesia may constrain generalizability. Future research should employ longitudinal or multi-source designs and examine the proposed relationships across diverse national and digital contexts. Practical implications The findings emphasize that sustainable entrepreneurial growth requires the simultaneous development of cognitive and digital capabilities. Entrepreneurship education, incubators, and business support programs should therefore integrate mindfulness-based decision-making with digital capability development to strengthen opportunity recognition, strategic adaptability, and long-term business sustainability. Originality/value This study provides a conceptually integrated perspective on sustainable entrepreneurial growth by examining the complementary roles of entrepreneurial mindfulness and digital adaptability capability through opportunity recognition. Rather than introducing a new theoretical model, it extends existing entrepreneurship literature by demonstrating how Cognitive Appraisal Theory and Dynamic Capabilities Theory can be jointly applied to explain the cognitive and technological foundations of entrepreneurs' sustainable growth aspirations in digitally transforming business contexts.

title: Mapping Women’s Contributions to Artificial Intelligence Using Large-Scale Text Analysis
4125b927acbe5f5970622d1172cc3ed4314324d3.abstract: Participation in AI research shapes which type of AI is built, whose societal needs it addresses, and how it is used in society. Despite increasing attention to gender diversity in AI, we lack systematic evidence on the research topics, methods used, and collaboration structures associated with female AI researchers. This paper addresses this significant gap by developing the first large-scale, validated mapping of women’s contributions to both generative and non-generative AI research across data science and the main social science disciplines (economics, political science, and sociology). Using a sample of over 500,000 papers published between 2023 and 2026, we document three key findings. First, women are under-represented among academic AI authors across all four disciplines and recent years, and least represented in data science. Second, conditional on participating, women’s AI research is thematically distinctive: it is more applied, social and purpose-driven, concentrated in health, education and fairness, and, in data science, oriented towards using rather than building AI. Third, this distinctive work is heard less: conditional on working on the same AI topic women and men are cited equally, but the topics women disproportionately work on are themselves cited less, so women’s ideas receive systematically fewer citations. This voice gap is therefore a topic-composition penalty rather than a same-topic penalty, and it reduces efficiency by giving a distinctive, society-oriented research agenda too little voice in how AI develops.

title: The Role of Artificial Intelligence in Reducing Maternal Mortality: A Systematic Review
container-title: F1000Research
09e66c57bbb1810145d28672bc4ac0eb634e17be.abstract: Abstract* Introduction Maternal mortality remains a critical global health issue, particularly in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), where the majority of deaths are preventable. Despite extensive efforts, progress in reducing maternal mortality has been slow and uneven. Recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) offer promising new strategies for addressing persistent gaps in maternal healthcare, particularly through early risk identification and optimized clinical decision-making. Materials and methods A comprehensive literature search was conducted across PubMed, Scopus, ScienceDirect, ProQuest, and Medline May 2020 to June 2025, following PRISMA guidelines. Registered in PROSPERO with CRD420251051696. Eligible studies included randomized controlled trials, cohort, or case-control studies investigating AI-based approaches to reduce maternal mortality among pregnant women. Data extracted included study characteristics, AI model details, and clinical outcomes. Study quality was assessed using the ROBINS-I tools. Results Eleven studies met the inclusion criteria, encompassing diverse settings and populations. AI and ML models, such as random forest, CatBoost, Naïve Bayes, and xgboost, were used to predict outcomes including obstetric complications, gestational diabetes, sepsis, hypertensive disorders, and postpartum hemorrhage. Many models demonstrated high predictive accuracy (AUC > 0.80), enabling early identification of high-risk pregnancies and supporting timely interventions. Integrating clinical, laboratory, and social determinants of health data improved model performance. However, challenges remain regarding data quality, infrastructure, ethical considerations, and model interpretability. Conclusion AI have significant potential to reduce maternal mortality by facilitating early risk stratification and personalized care. To realize this potential, future research should focus on prospective studies, integration of multimodal data, and development of explainable, equitable AI models. Collaborative efforts across disciplines and stakeholders are essential to address implementation barriers and achieve global maternal health targets.

title: Mechanisms of change in cognitive–behavioural therapy: implications for clinical practice
container-title: BJPsych Advances
48a932efcc92c9a842f94f70c5fa996187236cea.abstract: SUMMARY Cognitive–behavioural therapy (CBT) developed from two traditions: behavioural methods grounded in learning theory, and cognitive models that explain emotional distress through appraisals and beliefs. Contemporary practice integrates both at the level of formulation and technique: behavioural methods such as exposure and behavioural activation can change cognition, while cognitive strategies can support behavioural change. The empirical picture is more complex. Component studies suggest that behavioural interventions alone often produce outcomes comparable to full CBT, while the mediating role of cognitive change remains debated. This article reviews both traditions, describes how contemporary accounts of exposure (including inhibitory learning and expectancy violation) and behavioural experiments integrate them and considers what component and process research in social anxiety disorder and depression reveals about mechanisms of change. We argue for formulation-driven CBT, selecting cognitive strategies, behavioural strategies or both, according to the presentation, patient capacities and preferences, and treatment stage. Fictitious vignettes illustrate this approach, including adapted CBT for people with an intellectual disability.

title: Cognitive biases in nursing students' clinical decision-making: insights from high-fidelity simulation using think-aloud and observational methods
container-title: Frontiers in Medicine
939b27305964a06db43c5eb5dbea61e659cfa317.abstract: Background Cognitive biases are systematic errors in human reasoning that can compromise clinical decision-making (CDM) in healthcare. While extensively studied in medicine, nursing research on cognitive biases in CDM remains limited. Aim This study aimed to explore and identify cognitive biases and examine their relationship with nursing students' clinical decision-making during a high-fidelity simulation of a deteriorating patient scenario. Design A mixed-methods design was employed, incorporating concurrent and retrospective think-aloud (TA) protocols and observational data. Methods Twenty-three final-year Bachelor of Science nursing students participated in a high-fidelity, manikin-based simulation involving a clinically deteriorating patient scenario. A catalogue of 12 cognitive biases was developed from the literature and used to code statements from concurrent and retrospective think-aloud protocols and observational data using content analysis. Results A total of 166 bias occurrences were identified across all data sources (63 concurrent TA; 51 retrospective TA; 52 observation). Representativeness was the most frequently identified bias overall, particularly in retrospective think-aloud data. Order effect was the most common bias in concurrent think-aloud data, and representativeness and order effect were the most common in observational data. Premature closure and availability were also prominent across all sources of data. Biases occurred proportionally across both Type 1 (automated/pattern recognition) and Type 2 (hypothetico-deductive) decision-making, with notable differences between concurrent and retrospective think-aloud findings. The findings also suggest that simulation may support students' awareness of cognitive bias. Conclusion High-fidelity simulation, combined with think-aloud protocols and observation, provided a useful approach for identifying cognitive biases in nursing students' clinical decision-making. The findings have implications for simulation design, debriefing practice, and nursing education.

title: Selegiline prevents cognitive impairment and hippocampal CA1 excitability deficits induced by repeated isoflurane exposure
container-title: Frontiers in Cellular Neuroscience
f4522febc1fab1a0f93cd52f09ea158c866eed12.abstract: Postoperative cognitive dysfunction (POCD) is a common and clinically significant complication following anesthesia and surgery, affecting up to 40% of elderly patients, yet no established preventive therapy is currently available. Although neuroinflammation has been widely implicated in POCD, the electrophysiological mechanism linking anesthetic exposure to cognitive decline remains poorly understood, and pharmacological approaches to prevent this pathological cascade have not been established. To isolate the contribution of repeated anesthesia exposure itself, independent of surgical trauma, we used a repeated isoflurane-exposure mouse model, which we refer to as anesthesia-induced cognitive impairment (AICI). Using this model, we show that repeated anesthesia produces significant impairments in spatial working memory and recognition memory, accompanied by impaired hippocampal CA1 long-term potentiation (LTP). Whole-cell patch-clamp recordings further revealed intrinsic hypoexcitability of CA1 pyramidal neurons in isoflurane-exposed mice, characterized by reduced firing frequency, prolonged action potential half-width, slower repolarization, and diminished afterhyperpolarization. Reduced spontaneous excitatory postsynaptic current (sEPSC) frequency and amplitude further indicated impaired excitatory synaptic drive in CA1 neurons. Notably, pretreatment with selegiline, an FDA-approved selective monoamine oxidase-B (MAO-B) inhibitor, prevented isoflurane-induced cognitive deficits, preserved hippocampal LTP, preserved intrinsic neuronal excitability, and largely normalized action potential kinetics while maintaining sEPSC frequency, although the reduction in sEPSC amplitude was not significantly prevented by pretreatment. In contrast, direct application of high-concentration selegiline impaired LTP induction. Together, these findings identify impaired CA1 neuronal excitability and excitatory synaptic drive as key electrophysiological correlates of AICI and suggest selegiline as a promising pre-emptive candidate for mitigating anesthesia-related cognitive decline.

title: Design and Validation of a Novel Planar 2R1T Remote Center-of-Motion Mechanism Composing of Dual-Triangular and Straight-Line Linkages
container-title: Journal of Mechanisms and Robotics
caf43fb798aa694f48d6f5c32707dcb9a24ad400.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Benefiting from small incision and fast recovery, minimally invasive surgeries (MIS) exhibit great advantages in clinical operations. In such kind of surgeries, the remote center-of-motion (RCM) mechanisms play an important role owing to their special motion characteristics. This paper presents the design of a novel planar RCM mechanism of two rotational and one translational degrees-of-freedom (DOF). In the proposed design, the mobility of RCM mechanism is decomposed into one-DOF pure rotation and translation with a remote stationary point. The dual-triangular linkage and the Peaucellier–Lipkin straight-line linkage are introduced to achieve the remote rotation and translation, respectively. Inspired by the concept of virtual screw, a dual-helical differential-motion joint is particularly designed to generate the coaxial rotation and translation. A preliminary prototype is developed to validate the feasibility of the designed RCM mechanism. The experimental results show that the developed prototype is easy to control and of acceptable positioning accuracy, which manifests potential application in MIS.</jats:p>

title: Assessing the Quality of AI Explanations of Atrial Fibrillation: Comparative Analysis of ChatGPT and Google Gemini
container-title: JMIR Formative Research
598e2fa6d5c1d1ee8bb1eebc101a66353744cb13.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Atrial fibrillation (AF) is one of the most common arrhythmias and is associated with multiple risk factors, including stroke and heart failure. Therefore, it is important that accurate and comprehensive educational resources on AF are available. Artificial intelligence (AI) platforms such as Google Gemini and ChatGPT are emerging tools for medical education. To our knowledge, this is the first study to assess the quality of these platforms for AF education.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Objective</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This pilot study aimed to (1) assess the quality of ChatGPT and Google Gemini explanations of AF and its treatment, (2) compare responses from both platforms, and (3) analyze differences in interpretation between cardiologists and nonmedical professionals.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The prompt “Explain atrial fibrillation and how to treat it to a patient” was entered into both ChatGPT and Google Gemini. The responses, along with a survey created in Google Forms, were sent out to potential participants between September and October 2024. The survey questions were derived from the Patient Education Materials Assessment Tool for Printable Materials and DISCERN criteria. Each survey question was multiple choice and rated on a 5-point Likert scale, where 1 indicated strong disagreement and 5 indicated strong agreement. Averages of each answer from the survey were calculated and compared using the Wilcoxon signed-rank test.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The survey was completed by 28 participants, including cardiologists and cardiology fellows and 17 nonmedical professionals (college graduates not employed in the medical field). No significant overall quality differences were observed between ChatGPT and Google Gemini. When comparing participant groups, cardiologists rated AI-generated responses higher than nonmedical professionals for perceived bias (mean 3.82 vs mean 4.33; P=.04) and for explaining consequences of no treatment (mean 2.85 vs mean 1.86; P=.005). In contrast, nonmedical professionals rated structural and organizational features more favorably than cardiologists, including visual cues (mean 3.97 vs mean 2.48; P<.001), informative headers (mean 4.77 vs mean 3.95; P=.001), concise sections (mean 4.71 vs mean 4.29; P=.04), identifiable patient actions (mean 4.21 vs mean 3.19; P=.04), and references to additional resources (mean 2.65 vs mean 1.71; P=.006).</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The comparable quality of ChatGPT and Google Gemini suggests that both are viable for AF education. Differences in ratings of organizational features versus perceptions of bias and consequences of no treatment highlight a disconnect between cardiologists and nonmedical professionals. To optimize clinical application, cardiologists should evaluate both comprehensiveness and clarity of AI-generated responses. This serves as a pilot study, and future research should focus on longitudinal studies of AI-generated responses and their effects on clinical outcomes.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Expectation-driven gain modulation of preparatory spatial attention
container-title: eLife
42e0bff514a13e990dde6d5376170bcb87804ae4.abstract: <jats:p>The visual system can flexibly adjust attentional deployment to match task demands, but whether observers can proactively modulate the spatial scope of attention based on expectations about upcoming search difficulty remains unclear. According to the zoom lens model, attention can narrow or broaden its spatial extent, with narrower focus enhancing processing efficiency, a mechanism that would benefit target discrimination in crowded displays. We tested whether observers adjust attentional scope when expecting sparse versus dense search arrays by combining spatial cueing with block-wise manipulations of display density expectations. Participants performed a visual search task in which endogenous cues predicted target location, while blocks predominantly contained either sparse (1 target, 3 distractors) or dense (1 target, 7 distractors) displays. We applied inverted encoding models to broadband EEG data to reconstruct spatial channel tuning functions, enabling precise characterization of both the locus and breadth of attentional deployment. Behaviorally, expecting difficult searches selectively improved accuracy at cued locations without costs elsewhere. Consistent with this selective benefit, neural measurements revealed that expectancy enhanced the amplitude of spatially selective responses at the attended location but did not alter tuning width. These findings demonstrate that expectations about search difficulty modulate attention through gain-based signal enhancement rather than adjustments to spatial scope, revealing that preparatory attentional control operates via amplitude modulation within a stable spatial focus. This mechanism complements reactive attentional adjustments and provides an efficient means for the visual system to optimize processing under predictable task demands.</jats:p>

Entrepreneurial culture, social-emotional skills, and self-esteem in students participating in sports programmes in Colombia
container-title: Journal of Human Sport and Exercise
7487e0e532b00ca3a9d308c88e1fc9fc09e90f2f.abstract:
<jats:p>This research presents the results of a systematic review that analyses the relationship between entrepreneurial culture, social-emotional skills and self-esteem in students enrolled in sports programmes in Colombia, with the aim of identifying the factors that influence their positive attitude towards entrepreneurial capacity. In the literature review, 100 articles and academic research papers were selected between 2019 and 2025, prioritised from 42,958 results from different resources such as reference databases, multidisciplinary databases, academic repositories and academic journals. The databases with the highest number of results were Scopus, Web of Science, Wiley, Springer Nature, Science Direct, Ebsco Host, among others such as (COnnecting REpositories), Taylor & Francis, and Google Scholar. The results showed an interest in academia to research and reflect on the relationship between entrepreneurial culture, emotional skills, and young people. However, in most studies, entrepreneurial culture is associated with variables such as emotional intelligence and social skills in university contexts, leaving the field of the relationship between these variables and the field of sports somewhat lacking in studies. Studies that explore this relationship in depth conclude that athletes develop socio-emotional skills that make them strong candidates for entrepreneurship. However, there are limitations in the implementation of mechanisms that promote an entrepreneurial culture ( ) in university contexts for young people studying sports programmes.

title: VHMP: A High-efficacy and Parallel Processing Approach for CGRCA Supporting Virtual Heterogeneous Multi-core and Intra-core Multitask Pipeline
container-title: ACM Transactions on Design Automation of Electronic Systems
6069641410fbf34886a36b583f52e136660d22c8.abstract: <jats:p>The performance enhancements of coarse-grain reconfigurable cryptographic arrays (CGRCAs) through technology upgrades and increasing chip size are approaching limits. Enhancing parallel processing capabilities can relieve the computational burden on CGRCA in high-density computing scenarios. Specifically, a novel parallel processing approach is introduced in this article, named virtual heterogeneous multi-core pipelining (VHMP). VHMP supports virtual heterogeneous multi-core and intra-core multitask pipelining. Informed by hardware virtualization principles and analysis of CGRCA architectures, VHMP constructs virtual computing cores (VCCs) on CGRCA using multi-launch pipelines and implements multitask interleave pipelines within each VCC, enabling parallel processing at pipeline, task, and instruction levels. Furthermore, a hierarchical control mechanism is embedded within VHMP, integrating virtual computing path level and task-level management. This control mechanism allows diverse cryptographic algorithms to run concurrently without being bound to specific types or modes. Finally, applying VHMP to a 32 × 4 CGRCA, 32 heterogeneous VCCs are instantiated, with each core handling up to 16 interleaved tasks. Compared to treating CGRCA as a homogeneous multi-core processor, the VHMP approach achieves an average acceleration of 4.33 × (up to 6.34 ×) with quadrupled instruction execution capability. Additionally, the control mechanism reduces context volume to 18.7% and boosts configuration speed by 3 ×. Compared with related architectures, VHMP improves CGRCA throughput by an average of 5.3 ×.</jats:p>

title: Graphene-Based Interconnect Exploration for FPGA Design and Optimization Towards the End of the Roadmap
container-title: ACM Transactions on Design Automation of Electronic Systems
e4661457e8c7a67399488d41681b0b4a0b41cb22.abstract: <jats:p>The emerging graphene interconnect technology is expected to be a promising alternative to traditional interconnect technologies due to its superior conductivity. Because of the dominant impact of global routing on the overall performance of a widely used application, the Field-Programmable Gate Array (FPGA), this work investigates the potential advantage of using graphene-based interconnects to replace conventional copper (Cu) for global routing. Furthermore, a scalability analysis is performed, and the effects of technology node scaling from 7 nm to 1.5 nm are evaluated using lateral gate-all-around field-effect transistors (LGAAFETs) within the proposed system-technology co-design (STCO) framework. Key material-level parameters, including the mean free path (MFP), contact resistance, and the number of graphene layers, are systematically analyzed. Benchmark simulations demonstrate that a 32% improvement in the energy-delay product (EDP) is achieved with graphene-based interconnects compared to Cu counterparts at the 7 nm technology node, and an additional 46% reduction is observed at the 1.5 nm technology node. It is important to note that this work is an exploratory STCO study incorporating cross-layer design considerations, with a focus on long-term trends rather than short-term manufacturability.</jats:p>

title: LASM: Extensible Competitive Scheduling Framework for VLIW Assembly Optimization
container-title: ACM Transactions on Design Automation of Electronic Systems
d1804df4679dc580d7bd65e32240c18e9cb9fc7f.abstract: <jats:p>Very Long Instruction Word (VLIW) architectures deliver compelling performance-energy-cost advantages for automotive, AI, and high-performance computing. However, a persistent performance-productivity gap limits broader adoption: manual assembly optimization achieves superior performance but requires substantial expertise, while automated compilation underperforms. Existing assembly-level optimization tools commit to single scheduling strategies, unable to adapt to diverse program patterns. This article presents LASM, the first symbolic assembly framework enabling competitive multi-strategy orchestration for complete VLIW programs. Rather than committing to a single algorithm, multiple scheduling strategies simultaneously optimize identical code regions, with the framework automatically selecting the top solution through feasibility-driven ranking. LASM features standardized extension interfaces enabling plugin-style strategy integration and unified scheduling primitives eliminating algorithmic redundancy. We contribute two novel strategies: Longevity-Aware Expanded Modulo Scheduling (LAEMS) with dependency relaxation, proactive reordering, and parallel expansion search, and Front-Back Block Fusion (FBBF) for cross-boundary scheduling. Evaluation on 13 benchmarks across two production VLIW-SIMD processors demonstrates LASM achieves 103.6% and 101.6% of expert assembly performance while reducing manual code by 72.6%. A full YOLOv5 deployment validates production applicability at 95.9% of expert performance. Code is available at https://github.com/urays/lasm.</jats:p>

title: PolarGate: Breaking the Functionality Representation Bottleneck of And-Inverter Graph Neural Network
container-title: ACM Transactions on Design Automation of Electronic Systems
0aa9885c6dd1a82ee1b521ebf2ec7bff9bf19fb8.abstract: <jats:p>Understanding the functionality of Boolean networks is crucial for processes such as functional equivalence checking, logic synthesis, and malicious logic identification. With the proliferation of deep learning in electronic design automation (EDA), graph neural networks (GNNs) are widely used to embed and-inverter graphs (AIGs)—a standard form of Boolean networks—into vectorized representations. A key challenge in applying GNNs for Boolean representation is that although GNNs can effectively encapsulate the structural properties of AIGs, they struggle to efficiently capture Boolean logic functionality. In this work, we focus on breaking this bottleneck by enhancing the functional representation capability of GNNs, proposing PolarGate, an efficient solution that not only aligns message passing with AIG logical functionality but also effectively integrates global information. Leveraging the intrinsic ambipolar states (0 and 1) of AIG nodes, PolarGate maps gate behavior into an ambipolar state space, customizes differentiable logical operators, and designs a functionality-aware message passing strategy. To further capture global circuit information, PolarGate integrates a structure-aware preprocessing module and a global linear attention module, transcending the locality constraint of message passing. Experimental results on two functionality-related basic tasks (signal probability prediction and truth-table distance prediction) and a downstream task (logic equivalence prediction) show that PolarGate outperform state-of-the-art GNN-based methods.</jats:p>

title: ODCGate: Leveraging Observability Don’t Care Conditions for Enhanced Power Efficiency in Clock Gating
container-title: ACM Transactions on Design Automation of Electronic Systems
9cab47548290de0fcb0e5c4f5470bbe3c4f9a5e9.abstract:
<jats:p>
                    Clock gating reduces dynamic power by integrating activation functions and integrated clock gating (ICG) cells into the clock path, selectively disabling the clock signal to register when unnecessary. While conventional activation function extraction methods rely on manual design or register-transfer level analysis, a gate-level alternative exists: deriving activation functions through the extraction of observability don’t care (ODC) conditions from the underlying netlist. This article presents
                    <jats:bold>ODCGate</jats:bold>
                    , a framework designed to automatically detect ODC conditions as the activation functions and safely block clock transitions for unused registers, thereby further reducing dynamic power consumption during clock gating. The computation begins with cut boundary enumeration and simulation. To further minimize additional PPA overhead, we apply hybrid simplification techniques to the extracted logic, and enable sharing among registers through clustering. Experimental results show that, beyond the clock gating optimization of a commercial logic synthesis tool, our method achieves an average 33.46% additional reduction in dynamic power, with minimal impact on other PPA metrics.
                  </jats:p>

title: EnVector: Encoding using Pattern based Vectors for Energy Efficient Non-Volatile Main Memories
container-title: ACM Transactions on Design Automation of Electronic Systems
5243326e813a5b6c6c744dd3b22a5532319d4f01.abstract:
<jats:p>
                    Non-Volatile Memories (NVMs) provide new opportunities for scalable main memory due to their great scalability and other favorable attributes. However, considering their inherent write defects (long latency, high energy consumption), combined with their limited write endurance, their inclusion into the memory hierarchy requires careful handling. This not only shortens the lifespan of NVMs but also renders them as an expensive option. In this work, we propose a technique called
                    <jats:italic toggle="yes">EnVector</jats:italic>
                    that exploits the intrinsic uniformity in memory data to encode the cacheline data before the memory write takes place. By using well-designed fixed vectors, it minimizes the variation between the incoming and the stored data. This saves a lot of possible bit flips, reducing the likelihood of any memory failure from an excessive number of writes. Consequently, improving performance and lowering latency and energy requirements. We empirically demonstrated that
                    <jats:italic toggle="yes">EnVector</jats:italic>
                    upgrades the NVM lifetime by 37% and accelerates its performance by 15% over the baseline.
                  </jats:p>
                  <jats:p/>

title: Design and Implementation of a Vision Integrated Autonomous Research Rover
2e019a77a34534cace9acae8857fa40918f60895.abstract: <jats:p>This paper presents the design and implementation of a low-cost, vision-integrated autonomous rover for automated soil data collection. Traditional soil sampling methods are labor-intensive, and existing robotic solutions frequently depend on costly hardware and Global Positioning System (GPS) navigation, which can easily degrade in obstructed environments. To address these issues, a GPS-denied rover was developed using a Raspberry Pi 4B for high-level computer vision and a Robot Operating System 2 (ROS2) framework, paired with an Arduino Nano for real-time hardware control. The platform utilizes a linear actuator to autonomously deploy sensing probes for localized soil analysis. For stable navigation, an Extended Kalman Filter (EKF) is implemented to fuse wheel encoder odometry with inertial data. An OpenCV-based vision pipeline directs autonomous path following and marker detection. To mitigate tracking errors caused by processing and mechanical latency, a custom delay-compensation filter is introduced to actively reverse the rover and correct overshoot. This is paired with a history-dependent sweep prioritization algorithm that intelligently re-acquires lost paths based on prior trajectory data. The resulting system provides a reliable, accessible framework for independent environmental monitoring.</jats:p>

title: MLLM-Driven Autonomous Driving: Closed-Loop Decision-Making with Language-State Alignment and Human Instruction Integration
container-title: ACM Journal on Autonomous Transportation Systems
d800c7e114eb4db4826982c6e016151dc7d88ec1.abstract: <jats:p>The core challenge of autonomous driving is achieving real-time decision-making and safety control in complex, dynamic environments, especially in long-tail scenarios where conventional systems often fail due to limited adaptability, poor human-vehicle interaction, and low interpretability. This article introduces MLLM-CLAD, a closed-loop decision-making framework powered by a multimodal large language model, which addresses semantic gaps and feedback limitations through a co-optimization strategy that integrates behavior-state alignment and language instruction fusion. MLLM-CLAD integrates three core modules: (1) The Mapping-Enhanced Language-State Alignment Module employs a deterministic mapping pipeline from language instructions to control signals, which enables highly accurate mapping from LLM semantic outputs to executable control signals. (2) The Hierarchical Dynamic Instruction Integration Module robustly categorizes and dynamically prioritizes human language instructions into different semantic types. (3) The Multimodal Fusion Module leverages a lightweight spatiotemporal Q-Former to jointly encode images and LiDAR point clouds, aligned with language in latent space for improved temporal reasoning and cross-modal consistency. Evaluated in the CARLA Town05 Long, MLLM-CLAD achieves a 78.3% Driving Score and reduces collision rates by 35% in safety-critical scenarios. On the LangAuto benchmarks, MLLM-CLAD attains a 78.5% long-tail scenario pass rate. Furthermore, the end-to-end latency is reduced to 128 milliseconds. This work establishes a scalable path toward safe, low-latency, and interpretable autonomous driving in simulation, with a clear roadmap for real-world extension.</jats:p>

title: Study Design and Lessons Learned From Using Google Takeout Donations for Suicide Prevention Research: Prospective Cohort Study
container-title: Journal of Medical Internet Research
6610fc8dba7dec763399be61f0e967f4f50c2399.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="background">
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Social media and search engine tech companies, such as Google, use the wealth of data at their disposal to create algorithms to predict suicide risk and provide interventions based on company policies and outputs from these algorithms. Neither the details of these algorithms nor their accuracy in risk prediction are shared with the public; thus, research is needed to verify whether algorithms applied to search engine data can accurately predict suicide risk in a platform user. This paper provides new information about the methodological challenges in studying the value of search engine data for suicide prediction.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="objective">
                    <jats:title>Objective</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This paper describes the study methods and experiences regarding recruiting and retaining participants in a year-long, fully remote prospective cohort study of suicide prediction in people with variable risk of suicide, using Google Search data.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="methods">
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>We aimed to recruit 1000 United States–dwelling and English-speaking adults with current suicidal ideation who fell into 1 of 3 categories: participants with a suicide attempt in the past year, participants with a lifetime suicide attempt but not one in the past year, and participants with no suicide attempt in their lifetime. Recruitment sources included online advertisements hosted on various websites, to differing levels of success. Participants completed online surveys and an interview via Zoom to enroll in the study and then were sent follow-up surveys every 2 weeks for the year following initial enrollment. Recruitment was conducted from March 2022 to January 2024, with follow-up data being collected through February 2025.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="results">
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Of 15,120 records created in our Research Electronic Data Capture (REDCap) survey system, 485 participants were eligible to participate in the prospective year of the study. Recruitment challenges were mainly due to participant dropout across all enrollment time points, with 63.7% (9636/15,120) of the prescreening sample dropping out or refusing. Other issues included the difficulty of downloading Google Search data (446/3277, 13.6%) and not having enough data to meet the inclusion criteria among those who were able to successfully donate (252/3277, 7.7%). Lastly, the study encountered fraudulent behavior, with 489 of 15,120 records (3.2%) being identified as fraudulent over the course of the study.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="conclusions">
                    <jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Despite past success with remote clinical research methods, we found that recruitment can be significantly hampered by fraudulent participation, despite the use of state-of-the-art methods to mitigate this problem. Further, the ability to acquire useful Google Search data is extremely challenging and necessitates the use of technical assistance and continuous monitoring of Google Takeout data structure to ensure accurate and complete data donations. The solutions we provide for this type of research should be helpful for future endeavors. However, research is still limited by the barriers to obtaining data from technology companies. These limitations have significant implications in detecting the accuracy and utility of suicide prediction from search engine data.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Design optimization of Belleville washers made of shape memory alloys for advanced damping devices
container-title: International Review of Applied Sciences and Engineering
8b7bb47b9288de915570c928d3492949f6e6ceec.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Belleville washers made of Shape Memory Alloy (SMA) merge the unique properties of these materials with the advantages of conical disc spring geometry. Recent research has focused on characterizing these devices under cyclic compression. Key studies have involved numerical simulations and experimental testing. The findings confirm excellent recentering and energy dissipation capabilities of SMA Belleville washers, establishing them as prime candidates for next-generation seismic dampers for buildings and bridges. However, further investigation is required to optimize SMA Belleville washers by finding the cone angle and thickness that maximize energy dissipation. Considering damping devices fabricated by stacking Belleville washers, which rely on the pseudo-elastic effect, this work details an original methodology for systematic optimization of their design. This encompasses a preliminary elastic based sizing performed using adapted stress formulas, which is followed by a refinement stage employing Finite Element Analysis, via the 2020 R2 release of Ansys Mechanical solver. By generating a set of viable design alternatives, this novel methodology facilitates the efficient identification of the optimal configuration to maximize damping energy for given design constraints. The effectiveness of this approach was validated through case studies focused on optimizing SMA Belleville washers within advanced vibration suppression dampers.</jats:p>

title: CHARIOT: A Communication-Aware Exploration Framework for 2.5D/3D Silicon Interposer Design
container-title: ACM Transactions on Design Automation of Electronic Systems
fde248b576388e57d31ec8cfcc2323e389897a4a.abstract: <jats:p>Interposer design is crucial for optimizing inter-chiplet communication efficiency, performance, and energy consumption in 2.5D/3D integrated systems. To facilitate performance analysis and design space exploration (DSE) of interposers, this work presents CHARIOT, a fast, comprehensive exploration framework that establishes a systematic methodology for analyzing and exploring the design space of both passive and active interposers’ architecture. The design space of interposers is first developed to evaluate system performance. Then a roofline model-based methodology is introduced to analyze the bottleneck of performance. A multi-objective Bayesian optimization-based DSE framework, CHARIOT, is proposed, featuring a scheduling engine tailored to different interposer types and a communication-aware exploration engine for coordinated multi-objective exploration of the design space. Compared to the state-of-the-art (SOTA) chiplet system, the CHARIOT-generated optimal passive and active interposer designs achieve energy efficiency improvement up to 1.33× and 1.96×, as well as performance gains up to 1.49× and 1.75× speed-up. The Pareto frontiers of competitive design choices enable selecting the most suitable option based on the designers’ requirements.</jats:p>

title: SEC-CiM+: Selective and Reconfigurable Error Compensation for ReRAM-based Compute-in-Memory
container-title: ACM Transactions on Design Automation of Electronic Systems
11453691504ff8ab721724d52aa2fc6fce4b4ca2.abstract: <jats:p>ReRAM-based Compute-in-Memory (CiM) architectures provide a promising solution for accelerating Deep Neural Network (DNN) inference in edge computing environments. However, these architectures are susceptible to stuck-at faults (SAFs), including stuck-at intermediate states, which degrade inference accuracy. To address this challenge, we propose a reconfigurable error compensation (EC) mechanism that selectively mitigates errors while operating under memory constraints. By leveraging an indexed storage format, our approach efficiently compensates for errors without excessive overhead. We develop a theoretical framework to determine the minimum number of critical columns requiring compensation and analyze how EC transitions between three modes of operation across different models. The EC mechanism requires only 0.3874 mW of additional power for single operational-unit correction and introduces negligible latency overhead, while sustaining near-baseline accuracy for DenseNet121, VGG16, ResNet18, and SwinT under high fault densities (5–10%). Moreover, the overall energy overhead remains below 6% for ResNet18 and VGG16, and below 10% for DenseNet121.</jats:p>

title: DSETune: An Efficient Design Space Exploration Approach for Logic Synthesis
container-title: ACM Transactions on Design Automation of Electronic Systems
a855d3f0f9d5f837d27164f18752c0380dbbd423.abstract: <jats:p>As a critical step in the chip design flow, logic synthesis generates target circuits by iteratively applying various optimization algorithms. In practical applications, engineers must adjust the combination of optimization algorithms based on expert knowledge to meet diverse design requirements. However, existing approaches lack a multi-objective optimization perspective and exhibit poor solving efficiency. In light of this, we propose DSETune, the first synthesis flow search approach capable of thoroughly exploring the design space. First, a discrete particle swarm optimization algorithm incorporating genetic operators significantly improves search efficiency of design space. Second, a domain knowledge-driven initialization strategy of particles accelerates convergence and enhances solution quality. Finally, an update mechanism integrating a customized elite strategy enables more comprehensive solution space exploration, yielding superior Pareto-optimal solutions. Experimental results on the EPFL benchmark suite and four technology libraries demonstrate that DSETune outperforms existing methods: it reduces the area-delay product by 10.99%, improves the hypervolume metric by 109.80%, and achieves a 22.99% speedup, all on average.</jats:p>

title: Path Delay Faults Through Transition Faults with High Functional Switching Activities
container-title: ACM Transactions on Design Automation of Electronic Systems
d7c0604e26121ab930c68a14ad77f1a7756f99ac.abstract: <jats:p>Chip aging results in defects that are initially likely to appear as small delay defects. Path delay faults are used for detecting small delay defects. Because of the number of paths, path selection procedures are used for identifying a subset of path delay faults that are important to detect. A recent path selection procedure addresses small delay defects that are likely to occur because of chip aging. The procedure identifies a set of functionally possible path delay faults, from which it selects a subset based on an aging aware metric. This article studies this problem when the requirement for the path delay faults to be functionally possible is removed. The problem becomes that of selecting path delay faults through the largest numbers of transition faults with the highest susceptibilities to aging, and performing test generation for the selected path delay faults. Experimental results of path selection and test generation for benchmark circuits demonstrate the effectiveness of the procedures, and the differences from the case where the path delay faults are required to be functionally possible.</jats:p>

title: Quantifying Scalability-Performance Trade-offs: A Design Space Exploration of Compute-in-Memory based Ising Machines
container-title: ACM Transactions on Design Automation of Electronic Systems
314c1f4d98507cae1dbda9fa514e347fedc40048.abstract: <jats:p>Ising machines offer a promising paradigm for solving NP-hard combinatorial optimization problems (COPs). Among various approaches, Compute-in-Memory (CIM) based Ising machines show superior performance due to the reduced data transfer and efficient Multiply-and-Accumulate (MAC) operation. However, the scalability of CIM-based implementations remains limited due to challenges including restricted mapping size, circuit limitations and device non-idealities especially with emerging non-volatile memory (eNVM) technologies. This work presents a comprehensive design space exploration of three scalable CIM architectures for fully connected Ising models, analyzing their performance under constraints such as IR-drop, device variation, parasitic capacitance and analog to digital converter (ADC) precision loss across different memory technologies. According to our evaluation for randomized MAX-CUT benchmarks, the properly chosen design (Single array XNOR-based CIM mapping with Current Sense Amplifier) maintained over 95% solution quality while achieving nearly 2× higher energy efficiency and a 40% area reduction for 128-spins Ising model, while the optimal solution (Distributed subarray computation with 1-bit ADC precision loss) improves energy efficiency by 2.1× with small solution quality degradation (̴ 10%) for large-scale models (1,024 spins) compared to other designs options.</jats:p>

title: Toward Enhanced Hardware IP Security: Community Evaluation of Logic Locking, State Space Transformation, Redaction, and NoC Routing Table Configuration
container-title: ACM Transactions on Design Automation of Electronic Systems
274ba93baa637941a987ccfc15ebb7a42e0bfdac.abstract: <jats:p>As global hardware manufacturing expands and the need to meet time-to-market demands grows, companies increasingly depend on the zero-trust model to manage most of the design process for Integrated Circuits (ICs). Consequently, valuable hardware intellectual property (IP) becomes vulnerable to piracy, cloning, reverse engineering (RE), and unauthorized modifications throughout the global IC supply chain. Current security solutions are designed to safeguard the designs and protect sensitive information throughout the design flow. In this study, we present a thorough evaluation of various IP countermeasure techniques, including Logic Locking, State Space Transformation, Fine-grain Hardware Redaction, and NoC Routing Table Configuration, described in the existing literature. Inspired by cybersecurity competitions and community evaluation efforts, we designed a collaborative benchmarking initiative to evaluate these techniques on open-source benchmark designs, unveil the gaps and limitations of each technique, and discover crucial paths for future exploration. Through a retrospective analysis of this initiative, the insights we gained can significantly contribute to improving countermeasure techniques in the broad domain of hardware security and trust.</jats:p>

title: Fast TDDB Hotspot Detection of Large-Scale BEOL Circuits Using Physics-Informed Central Emphasized CNN
container-title: ACM Transactions on Design Automation of Electronic Systems
43ca2ee0c70088e2af9b1e91e0c2fd8f1b809f8c.abstract:
<jats:p>
                    Time-Dependent Dielectric Breakdown (TDDB) has emerged as a critical reliability concern in Back-End-of-Line (BEOL) interconnects. In Electric Path Generation (EPG) based TDDB analysis, the evolution of metal ion concentration is governed by a Partial Differential Equation (PDE). Traditional numerical methods for solving this equation are time-consuming and demand considerable computational resources, making them impractical for large-scale circuits analysis.
