63395033ead6c334c44934c0c842fb3ccadf45ea.abstract: The rapid growth of distributed energy resources and renewable technologies has increased the need for intelligent management of modern power systems. Microgrids offer a reliable, flexible, and sustainable solution by integrating local generation, storage, and controllable loads. However, their planning and control are complex due to uncertainties in renewable generation, varying load demand, and dynamic conditions. Artificial Intelligence (AI) has emerged as an effective tool to address these challenges. Techniques such as machine learning, deep learning, and optimization enable accurate forecasting of energy demand, renewable output, and system behavior.AI also enhances real-time control through adaptive decision-making and efficient energy management. This improves reliability, reduces costs, and increases resilience to disturbances. Overall, AI integration enables efficient resource use, minimizes losses, and supports the transition to smart, sustainable, and decentralized power systems.

title: AI-Assisted Optimization of Hybrid Renewable Energy Microgrids for Sustainable Rural Electrification
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Optimizing Sustainable Energy Engineering With AI and Machine Learning
ea5cb44704ea7f5ca67dc3a9d789f030592a4484.abstract: This chapter reviews conventional optimization methods and AI-assisted approaches for hybrid renewable energy microgrids, highlighting their roles in system planning, sizing, operation, and control. It also explores emerging technologies, including reinforcement learning, explainable AI, digital twins, and edge AI, that are shaping the next generation of intelligent energy systems. To illustrate the practical application of these concepts, the chapter presents a case study of a hybrid renewable energy microgrid in Muanda, Democratic Republic of the Congo, featuring solar photovoltaic generation, battery energy storage, and blue-carbon bioenergy resources. The case study shows how optimization techniques can enhance techno-economic and environmental performance and discusses the potential of AI-based forecasting, intelligent battery management, and reinforcement learning to further improve system reliability, renewable energy utilization, and long-term sustainability.

title: Digital Intelligence and AI-Based System Optimization in Waste-to-Energy Infrastructure for Net-Zero Cities
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Optimizing Sustainable Energy Engineering With AI and Machine Learning
a481d5d2ec22f7c57987bf6fb1f4d55e7e848167.abstract: The integration of digital intelligence and artificial intelligence in waste-to-energy (WtE) infrastructure optimization to achieve net-zero cities is presented in this chapter. The rapid urbanization and the growing amount of waste demand efficient and sustainable solutions. Municipal waste is turned into energy in WtE systems, and traditional operations lack flexibility and efficiency. The chapter uses systematic literature review as a method on the topic indexed in more than 200 articles and summarizing main conclusions of the quality research. It discusses monitoring with IoT, digital twins, and real-time optimization based on AI and predictive maintenance and energy recovery that is better. Case studies show the changes in the operational efficiency, emission control, and stability of systems. A conceptual AI-enabled framework is presented to find a solution to combine WtE systems with smart grids and urban energy networks. The results conclude on how smart WtE infrastructure contributes to the use of the circular economy and sustainable, low-carbon urban development.

title: AI-Driven Optimization of Solar Thermal Systems
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Optimizing Sustainable Energy Engineering With AI and Machine Learning
dc3def60d826262ab21f0eea8c2fef98b5d58e72.abstract: Solar thermal systems encounter distinct operational challenges, which hinder their applicability. Artificial intelligence (AI) has the potential to solve them. The AI is more flexible and adaptable than traditional methods, which cannot deal with unpredictable factors, including changing weather and fluctuating energy demands. In this chapter, we introduced the solar thermal systems, and then the fundamentals of AI techniques used in solar thermal systems were provided. Subsequently, the application of AI in solar thermal systems was discussed. The advantages of the optimization process of the solar thermal systems were identified, supported by case studies from the real world. Then we identified the limitations and constraints that hinder the integration of AI into the solar thermal system. Finally, the economic benefits of using AI for the optimization of solar thermal systems were explained.

92ef05c8e2ba0949c3bf8f69974d39c51dc39e56.abstract: This chapter analyses the strategic incorporation of artificial intelligence technology into renewable energy systems to enhance energy security, operational efficiency, and long-term sustainability. This chapter aims to examine how intelligent energy management systems, machine learning algorithms, smart grids, decentralized microgrids, and Internet of Things (IoT) networks can enhance the performance and resilience of renewable energy systems. This chapter places emphasis on predictive analytics, battery management, solar forecasting, digital twins, and autonomous energy optimization. The chapter examines the economic, environmental, and technological ramifications of intelligent energy systems, emphasizing their capacity to minimize energy losses, improve system reliability, facilitate decentralized electrification, and expedite sustainable energy transitions towards enhanced national energy independence.

title: Machine Learning for Solar Thermal Energy Optimization and Smart Control

974378bf655d4595a7410253b21e0ad381c1a368.abstract: This chapter presents a systematic examination of how Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning techniques are transforming the design, operation, diagnosis, and control of solar thermal energy systems, including flat-plate collectors, evacuated tube collectors, and concentrating solar power plants. Principal ML methodologies surveyed include Artificial Neural Networks, Support Vector Regression, Gradient Boosting, Long Short-Term Memory networks, Transformer architectures, Physics-Informed Neural Networks, and Deep Reinforcement Learning. Applications are reviewed across four domains data-driven surrogate models for thermal performance prediction, ML-based irradiance and thermal output forecasting, intelligent fault detection and predictive maintenance frameworks, and AI-driven control strategies shown to improve annual useful heat delivery by 8 to 15 percent. Research challenges including data scarcity, model interpretability, and cross-site generalization are identified, with future directions proposed in federated learning, physics-informed architectures, and explainable AI.

a35056ead95e6546af494efa6e34c4e7ce0284ba.abstract: This chapter develops a conceptual and methodological framework for artificial-intelligence- and machine-learning-enabled energy audits in Tanzanian industrial small and medium-sized enterprises. Industrial SMEs often face energy-efficiency barriers related to limited capital, weak information systems, incomplete metering, and constrained managerial capacity. The chapter positions the energy audit as the organizing mechanism for sustainable energy engineering and shows how AI/ML can strengthen load profiling, benchmarking, anomaly detection, forecasting, measure prioritization, and measurement and verification. Drawing on peer-reviewed evidence from SME audit programs, ISO 50001 research, African industrial energy studies, and applied AI/ML energy literature, the chapter proposes a staged implementation roadmap for Tanzanian SMEs. The contribution is a practical pathway for moving from one-off audits toward data-informed, explainable, and financially grounded energy management.

2488e9ed487b4765c71f38c4edb94b5b6290f2ae.abstract: Anaerobic co-digestion is an effective approach for biogas production, but optimizing operating parameters remains challenging due to the interaction of multiple variables. This study integrates ultrasonic pretreatment with Response Surface Methodology (RSM) to enhance biogas yield from a mixture of dormitory food waste and pet animal dung. Batch digesters were operated at 37 °C, and daily biogas production was monitored. RSM evaluated the combined effects of ultrasonic temperature (25–65 °C), power (500–1,500 W), and treatment time (35–75 min). Biogas yield ranged from 35% to nearly 68%, with optimum conditions of 53.35 °C, 1,490.83 W, and 57.15 min, producing a predicted yield of 66.47%. The quadratic model showed excellent predictive performance (R2 = 0.9707; F = 110.33), confirming the importance of simultaneous optimization. The integrated ultrasonic–RSM approach provides a reliable and efficient strategy for maximizing biogas production in anaerobic co-digestion systems.

title: Application of Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning Methods to Optimize Energy System Stability
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Optimizing Sustainable Energy Engineering With AI and Machine Learning
af88092a3405a3484f3caf6617dee2099625164e.abstract: This article presents a systematic analysis of artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) methods applied to the optimization of energy system stability. Deep learning architectures for forecasting electricity demand and renewable energy generation, reinforcement learning algorithms for microgrid control, the concept of digital twins, and explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) methods are examined. The application of hybrid models reduces forecasting errors by 20–35% over ultra-short-term forecasting horizons ranging from several minutes to several hours. The transition to probabilistic forecasting reduces balancing costs by 8–15%, while the use of digital twins decreases operating costs by 15–25%. Current challenges limiting the implementation of intelligent technologies in the energy sector are identified, and priority areas for further research are outlined. The results are systematized in comparative tables suitable for practical use when selecting appropriate methodological tools.

b326566af7bfa615ecca304269db8b978877aabc.abstract: This chapter per the authors examines machine learning for forecasting electrical load and renewable generation under energy transition and grid digitalization. The chapter reviews LSTM, BiLSTM, GRU, CNN, TCN, hybrid architectures, ensembles, SVR, and GPR. Solar and wind forecasting depend on weather uncertainty, spatial relationships, and telemetry quality. The chapter compares facility types with forecasting methods and discusses digital twins, adaptive forecasting, and closed-loop control. Key problems: data drift, limited transferability, interpretability, computational complexity, and SCADA cybersecurity. Development requires integrating forecasting with digital twins, XAI, reinforcement learning, anomaly detection, and cybersecurity. Machine learning becomes a foundation for proactive and resilient power system management.

title: Integrating Transformer Neural Processes and Deep Kernel Learning for High-Throughput Screening and Uncertainty Quantification for Water-Splitting Electrocatalysts Across Perovskites and Metal Alloys

bcafa941c82b95b48c33f91be24df91543e346ce.abstract: Years of experimentation have failed to enable the prediction of an efficient electrocatalyst from either a perovskite or an alloy without weeks of experimentation. There are more than a million perovskites, more exponential number of alloys but fewer than 0.1% of them have been studied. The traditional approach has failed. Density Functional Theory is impractical because of costs. Gaussian Process Regression struggles with scalability and lacks transfer between families. Its uncertainty calibration is off by miles. More importantly, the literature is not homogenous. Any framework that ignores that problem learns procedures, not physics. We gather Transformer Neural Processes (meta-learning across families) with Deep Kernel Learning (statistical uncertainty). This neural architecture can scale and model overpotential, stability, and activity with correlated uncertainties. Standardization of overpotential is done through Tafel correction. Prediction errors in the range of 50 millivolts and two- to three-fold reduction of experiments through Bayesian Optimization are our goals.

title: Towards theorising the normative agency of Central Europe: iterative identities and norms shaping from a Global East perspective
container-title: Pluriversal International Relations
2bab88b6b8efd5cb9648fabde86d60d4a0c7faa0.abstract: This article examines under what conditions actors operating through a semi-peripheral regional format can develop an emergent form of normative agency. It treats the Three Seas Initiative as an illustrative Central European case, viewed through the Global East as a relational and epistemic positionality rather than a fixed geography. The article introduces the constructivist model of iterative identities and norms shaping, a heuristic framework tracing how previously articulated norms, identity narratives and regional role claims re-enter later political and institutional contexts and are reinterpreted, contested, amplified or institutionalised. The model identifies identity alignment and norm localisation as the principal conditions of regional normative agency, distinguishing conditional norm co-creation from compliance, locally bounded autonomy and failed agency. Empirically, the article analyses Three Seas Initiative summit declarations from 2016 to 2025, supplemented by institutional documents and selected European Union and North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO) materials examining external recognition and convergence. The analysis reconstructs three phases of the initiative’s development: initial identity formation and the search for recognition; institutionalisation and the localisation of connectivity norms; and the post-2021 reinterpretation of infrastructure through resilience, security and eastern-flank vulnerability. The findings suggest that the initiative has generated limited and conditional normative agency through the regionally grounded reinterpretation of broader Euro-Atlantic normative templates. The case does not demonstrate autonomous norm creation but shows how historically norm-receiving actors may contribute to norm transformation when regional institutionalisation combines with wider recognition.

title: Dual-band beam-steering metasurface design and analysis based on transmission line theory
container-title: Physica Scripta
87fafcd321245e95abcb974a90a3d45a386a929a.abstract: Abstract This paper presents an advanced design methodology for dual-band, all-dielectric metasurfaces based on transmission line (TL) theory. The proposed structure integrates two single-band metasurfaces placed back-to-back, enabling highly versatile dual-band functionality. By leveraging the TL framework, the design parameters are analytically derived to provide independent control over the steering angles at two distinct operating frequencies. This flexibility allows the deflection angle at the second frequency to be configured as either larger or smaller than that at the first, depending on the application requirements. The effectiveness of this theoretical framework is validated through multiple design scenarios, including cases with diverse angular relationships and anomalous transmission in opposite directions. Full-wave electromagnetic simulation results demonstrate excellent agreement with theoretical predictions, confirming the precision and robustness of the proposed methodology in achieving selective and decoupled wavefront control in dual-band environments.

title: Design for dynamic fitness: archetypes of urban water systems
container-title: Environmental Research: Infrastructure and Sustainability
81188f34d9a13d7171ac9a63ae9b442ff8609543.abstract: Abstract Infrastructure systems were largely designed for a world of environmental stationarity, and the Anthropocene—characterized by accelerating change that often produces more dynamic and extreme stressors—challenges infrastructure robustness. Urban water supply systems (UWSs) epitomize the pressures of socio-environmental change on infrastructure as they increasingly operate outside their physical design conditions, putting new pressure on their institutional designs to weather emerging challenges. Water management institutions must therefore be designed for ‘dynamic fitness,’ defined by anticipatory capacity and responsiveness. However, we do not yet understand the specific institutional design features enabling dynamic fitness and their relation to infrastructure and environmental (i.e. biophysical) characteristics. We advance research on dynamic fitness in UWSs by synthesizing theory and analyzing 35-year data sets of stressors and responses for 16 U.S. urban water utilities using archetype analysis. We find that institutional archetypes capable of coping with higher biophysical complexity invest in information processing capacity and response diversity. While these features of dynamic fitness come at a cost, balancing these promotes efficiency, which can be expanded through polycentric regional governance structures. Institutional designs for dynamic fitness must weigh tradeoffs in flexibility across governance levels and between quick responses and slow transformative changes.

title: Integrasi AI dalam Kurikulum Akuntansi Pendidikan Pesantren: Tinjauan Literatur Sistematis tentang Kesiapan Teknologi, Pemahaman AI, dan Karakteristik Siswa

9db92d2d3af48ff40caacdc975fdcbe142bb7929.abstract: Perkembangan Artificial Intelligence (AI) telah mendorong transformasi pendidikan akuntansi dan menuntut penyesuaian kurikulum agar sesuai dengan kebutuhan dunia kerja digital. Namun, adopsi AI dalam kurikulum akuntansi masih dipengaruhi oleh berbagai faktor, khususnya pada konteks pendidikan pesantren yang memiliki karakteristik unik. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis pengaruh kesiapan teknologi, pemahaman AI, dan karakteristik siswa terhadap adopsi AI dalam kurikulum akuntansi serta mengidentifikasi faktor yang paling dominan. Penelitian menggunakan metode Systematic Literature Review (SLR) dengan pedoman PRISMA 2020. Data diperoleh dari 38 artikel ilmiah terindeks Scopus yang dipublikasikan pada periode 2015-2026 dan dianalisis menggunakan sintesis tematik. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa kesiapan teknologi merupakan faktor yang paling dominan dalam mendorong adopsi AI, diikuti oleh pemahaman AI dan karakteristik siswa. Ketiga faktor tersebut saling melengkapi dalam meningkatkan penerimaan dan pemanfaatan AI dalam pembelajaran akuntansi. Temuan ini berkontribusi pada pengembangan model adopsi teknologi pendidikan serta menjadi dasar pengembangan kurikulum akuntansi berbasis AI di lingkungan pesantren.

title: Fertility rates across generations in twins and singletons: a total population study in Finland
container-title: Human Reproduction
0f08f59259ab0674c77bfff27b139d628691813b.abstract: Abstract STUDY QUESTION Does twin status and zygosity (monozygotic vs dizygotic; same-sex vs opposite-sex) predict fertility outcomes and intergenerational reproductive patterns compared with singletons? SUMMARY ANSWER Dizygotic female twins had a modestly higher number of biological children than singletons and monozygotic twins and were more likely to have a twin birth, but we did not observe differences for males or intergenerational differences. WHAT IS KNOWN ALREADY Dizygotic twinning is associated with heritable hyperovulation and higher natural fertility but less is known about whether being a twin or zygosity influences reproductive outcomes across generations. STUDY DESIGN, SIZE, DURATION A population-based longitudinal cohort study using part of the Finnish Twin Cohort and national population registers. Participants included an Anchor Generation composed of monozygotic (MZ; N = 4068), same-sex dizygotic (SSDZ; N = 8890), opposite-sex dizygotic (OSDZ; N = 8474), unknown zygosity (XZ; N = 2320) twins, and singleton controls (N = 1 193 404) born between 1945 and 1957 (total N = 1 217 156; 49.1% female), their mothers, their children, and their grandchildren. PARTICIPANTS/MATERIALS, SETTING, METHODS Fertility outcomes (number of biological children, age at first birth, childlessness, multiple births) were derived from Finnish population registers. Analyses followed a preregistered plan (https://osf.io/qbwv3). MAIN RESULTS AND THE ROLE OF CHANCE Differences in fertility between singletons and twins were modest and varied by sex and zygosity. Differences were observed generally in the mothers of twins and female twins themselves, with limited differences in the offspring of twins as compared to the offspring of singletons. Twins were slightly older at first birth, had fewer total biological offspring, but were more likely to have a twin birth. Dizygotic twins in particular differed from monozygotic twins and singletons. LIMITATIONS, REASONS FOR CAUTION Findings are limited to individuals born in mid-20th-century Finland and thus generalizability to recent populations or non-Nordic contexts may be restricted. Further, analyses are observational, and causal inference is limited due to alternative motivation behind fertility rates like social or cultural reasons. WIDER IMPLICATIONS OF THE FINDINGS These findings suggest that zygosity and sex interact to shape reproductive outcomes, offering insight into genetic and environmental contributions to fertility. They highlight the value of large twin cohorts for studying intergenerational reproductive trends and the representativeness of twins in population-based fertility research. FUNDING As a supporting activity to ongoing research projects, funding for this project was provided by the Broad Trauma Initiative at the Broad Institute of MIT and Harvard. DISCLOSURES The authors declare no conflict of interest. TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER N/A.

title: KUNJUTNING ODDIY VA BEKROSS CHATISHTIRISH NATIJASIDA OLINGAN F1  DURAGAYLARIDA O‘SIMLIK BO‘YI VA YON SHOXLARI SONI BELGILARINING IRSIYLANISHI

fdd79e12d4dc98c72a7ea30e9bb3a464401f1cbe.abstract: The study investigated the inheritance of important morphological traits, including plant height and the number of lateral branches, in simple and backcross F₁ sesame hybrids involving the local varieties “Onimdar”, “Qora Shahzoda”, “Tashkent-122”, and “Sadaf”. The experiments were conducted under field and laboratory conditions. The patterns of trait formation and the degree of heterosis in the hybrids were analyzed. The number of lateral branches ranged from 5.8 to 6.2 per plant in the local varieties, from 5.7 to 8.7 in simple F₁ hybrids, and from 5.6 to 9.2 in backcross hybrids. Positive heterosis for the number of lateral branches was observed in most of the simple hybrids. Positive inheritance of this trait was also recorded in several backcross combinations. Promising hybrid combinations with high values of plant height and the number of lateral branches were identified. The results indicate that the selected hybrid combinations can be used in sesame breeding to develop valuable initial breeding material with high productivity, stability, and adaptability to local environmental conditions.

5ceb721e66711f7ae20303275a9a4626549b0abb.abstract: The article presents the results of research aimed at identifying valuable initial breeding material for barley breeding on irrigated lands. The studies were conducted in 2023–2026 at the experimental field of the “Farboma selekt” scientific seed-growing farm located in Jomboy district of Samarkand region. A total of 200 barley collection accessions obtained from the international centers ICARDA and CIMMYT, as well as the Institute of Plant Science and the Gallaorol Research and Experimental Station of the Research Institute of Grain and Legume Crops, were studied. The accessions were evaluated for productive tillering, number and weight of grains per spike, 1000-grain weight, yield, earliness, and resistance to diseases, winter conditions and lodging. The study identified valuable barley accessions with high productivity and yield potential. In particular, the Mirzacho‘l, K-22845, K-19985, Temur and K-566244 accessions demonstrated high yield performance. The selected accessions are recommended as valuable initial breeding material for developing new high-yielding, early-maturing and environmentally stress-resistant barley varieties for irrigated lands.

082f36c736e87ce9716851e175549fbf531e9f4b.abstract: The article studies the formation of plant density in chickpea varieties under different irrigation methods and irrigation regimes. The results showed that plant density of the Zumrad and Malhotra chickpea varieties varied depending on the irrigation method and soil moisture regime. The obtained results demonstrate the importance of selecting an appropriate irrigation method and soil moisture regime for chickpea cultivation.

5a3db10baab032456fbf63d4deeb470fcfec6be3.abstract: This article evaluates the seasonal growth dynamics of low-stem fodder mulberry plantations under the climatic conditions of Uzbekistan in 2025-2026 based on phenological and biometric indicators. The highest morphological and economically valuable traits were recorded during the summer period. The average shoot length was 136 cm in 2025 and 143.0 cm in 2026. 64c6d61b63e15cccc6046a9ac3e33de4bda278b4.abstract: The papain-like protease (PL pro ) of severe respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) is a promising therapeutic target owing to its vital role in viral polyprotein processing and modulation of host immune responses. Therefore, in the present work, a library of thiazole–benzamide analogues 8a-l incorporating ([Formula: see text]-1-(naphthalen-1-yl)ethyl amide moiety was designed, synthesized and evaluated for inhibitory activity against SARS-CoV-2. Among the synthesized compounds, the 4-chloropyridin-3-yl-based derivative 8f displayed the most potent PL pro inhibition with an IC[Formula: see text] value of [Formula: see text]M, followed by the derivative 8e (IC[Formula: see text]M) and 8g (IC[Formula: see text]M) possessing 6-methylpyridin-2-yl and isoquinolin-1-yl groups, respectively. All three compounds 8f showed lower IC[Formula: see text] values compared to the standard inhibitor GRL0617 (IC[Formula: see text]M). The observed weaker potency of several five-membered heteroaromatic analogues clearly demonstrated the dependence on the positioning of substituents and heteroaromatic ring selection for modulation of PL pro inhibition. Molecular docking against SARS-CoV-2 PL pro (PDB ID: 7CMD) revealed favorable predicted binding affinities for 8f (−8.337 kcal/mol), 8e (−8.099 kcal/mol), and 8g (−7.732 kcal/mol) compared with GRL0617 (−7.218 kcal/mol). Notably, compound 8f established three predicted hydrogen bonds with GLN269, ASP164, and TYR273, together with [Formula: see text]–[Formula: see text] and hydrophobic interactions involving TYR268, PRO247, and PRO248, supporting its favorable accommodation within the PL pro binding pocket. Density functional theory calculations at the B3LYP/6-311G(d,p) level demonstrated that 8f possessed the smallest highest occupied molecular orbital and lowest unoccupied molecular orbital (HOMO–LUMO) energy gap (3.80 eV) among the investigated derivatives, along with the highest global softness (0.263 eV[Formula: see text] and electrophilicity index (3.34 eV), indicating comparatively greater electronic polarizability and charge-transfer propensity. Molecular electrostatic potential analysis further identified electron-rich carbonyl and heterocyclic regions as potential sites for intermolecular interactions. ADMET predictions indicated that 8f exhibited the highest predicted PAMPA permeability (0.778) among the evaluated derivatives; however, high lipophilicity, limited aqueous solubility, and potential metabolic and toxicity liabilities highlighted the need for further structural optimization and experimental safety assessment. Collectively, the experimental and computational findings identify 8f as a promising lead compound and establish the thiazole–benzamide framework as a potential platform for developing novel SARS-CoV-2 PL pro inhibitors.

title: From prediction to design rules: explainable machine learning analysis of cryoprotectant effects in GelMA-based cryobioprinting bioinks
container-title: Biomedical Physics & Engineering Express
cba1d2360d45f4f2da517a4c0ec4ef34475e0fff.abstract: Abstract Machine learning has been used to predict cryoprotective-agent (CPA) effects in cryobioprinting, but prediction accuracy alone does not yield experimentally usable formulation rules. Here, we performed a secondary explainable analysis of Qiao et al ’s GelMA-HUVEC dataset using formulation-grouped validation, SHAP interpretation, stability metrics, and multi-objective ranking. A compact Random Forest model using permeable CPA identity, sugar CPA identity, permeable CPA concentration, sugar concentration, and storage day achieved MAE = 4.842%, RMSE = 6.106%, and R 2 = 0.649, with bootstrap 95% confidence intervals of 4.418–5.274% for MAE and 0.585–0.710 for R 2 . SHAP analysis identified permeable CPA concentration and storage day as the strongest viability drivers, with directional patterns favoring balanced 15% permeable CPA and 15% sugar CPA rather than simple concentration maximization. Multi-objective ranking identified GL_15_RA_15 as the strongest individual formulation, whereas EG + trehalose showed the highest average CPA-family performance. Cross-domain tests showed limited transfer between EG and GL formulations, indicating that the extracted rules should be treated as local, data-supported design hypotheses rather than universal cryoprotectant principles. Together, these results show that explainable secondary analysis can convert small cryobioprinting datasets into experimentally testable CPA hypotheses while explicitly defining their transferability limits.

title: Tau hadronic decay channel reconstruction with a Lorentz-covariant graph attention network
container-title: Physica Scripta
7d7360eebe4f1102dd8fb23bb166025e3ac64c60.abstract: Abstract The reconstruction of hadronic decay modes of the τ lepton is a key task in high-energy physics experiments, directly impacting precision measurements and new physics searches. Conventional reconstruction approaches rely on handcrafted features and rule-based algorithms, which face challenges in handling complex decay topologies and detector effects. In this work, we propose LCGA-Net, a physics-informed deep learning framework for τ decay channel classification and four-momentum reconstruction. The method represents decay products as particle graphs and employs a multi-head attention mechanism to capture inter-particle correlations. To ensure physical consistency, Lorentz-invariant constraints are explicitly incorporated into the model architecture. A dedicated single- τ dataset is constructed from the simulation data of the Circular Electron Positron Collider, covering six major hadronic decay modes. The proposed model achieves an accuracy of 89.2% on the validation set, matching or slightly exceeding baseline models. More importantly, full physics constraints substantially improve the physical plausibility of reconstructed four-momenta—particularly the energy–momentum relation—without degrading classification performance. These results demonstrate that integrating physics priors with attention-based deep learning on particle clouds provides an effective approach for τ decay reconstruction, with potential applications in future high-energy physics analyses.

36ede77f584724c16c6df8d872616165c6726651.abstract: This article investigates the effectiveness of biological fertilizers and resource-saving agrotechnologies for potato (Solanum tuberosum L.) cultivation under the natural, climatic, and soil conditions of the Republic of Karakalpakstan. title: Pulmonary hypertension and right ventricular dysfunction in hemodialysis: an overlooked cardiorenal interface and a target for dialysis prescription
container-title: Journal of Hypertension
1d71f073beb673d089fb4fa0a595fc7491f69a54.abstract: Pulmonary hypertension is an under-recognized cardiovascular complication of advanced chronic kidney disease, especially in maintenance hemodialysis. It links kidney failure, chronic volume stress, left-heart disease, pulmonary vascular remodeling, arteriovenous access flow, and right-ventricular dysfunction. This review frames pulmonary hypertension as central to the cardiorenal interface in hemodialysis and summarizes epidemiology, prognosis, mechanisms, diagnosis, and phenotyping. Echocardiography is the main screening tool, but pressure estimates should be interpreted according to dialysis timing and volume status. Right-heart catheterization remains essential to define phenotype and guide management. Treatment should target modifiable drivers: euvolemia without excessive ultrafiltration, optimized left-heart disease care, assessment of high-flow vascular access, and treatment of respiratory or hematologic contributors. Empirical pulmonary arterial hypertension-specific therapy should be avoided without hemodynamic confirmation. Pulmonary-artery denervation is promising in heart-failure pulmonary hypertension with mild to moderate CKD, but its role in hemodialysis remains unknown.

title: Design and manufacturing of a passive prosthetic knee joint
container-title: International Review of Applied Sciences and Engineering
196fcef93db33da231403970a046f1a68b7e8c5d.abstract: Abstract Passive prosthetic knee joints remain an attractive solution for transfemoral amputees in low-resource settings because of their low cost, mechanical simplicity, and ease of maintenance. But there are numerous commercial designs which are either relatively heavy or mechanically complex. In this work, the design, finite element analysis, material selection and fabrication of a lightweight passive prosthetic knee joint with a simple polycentric mechanism are proposed. Three candidate materials (AISI 4130 steel, Al2024-T4 and Al7075-T651) were selected and experimentally characterized by tensile testing and numerically compared in terms of stress distribution, deformation, weight and factor of safety and subjected to an extreme static loading of 1000 N. The maximum of von Mises stress obtained from the finite element calculations for all materials studied was 40.2 MPa, which was found to be below their respective yield strengths, thus providing sufficient structural integrity. Al7075-T651 was found to have the highest factor of safety (12.19), minimum structural deformation (0.0497 mm) and a good strength-to-weight ratio, thus showing the best overall performance among the materials evaluated, and the least prototype weight (198 g). The prototype weight was measured and compared with the CAD weight prediction (195 g), and good agreement was obtained with the fabricated prototype (198 g), with a deviation of 1.5%. This agreement indicates that the overall geometry, volume and assigned material density are consistent in the CAD model. The entire prototype was produced at an estimated cost of about USD 160, which is considerably less expensive than many passive prosthetic knee joints on the market. This proposed design is lightweight, has sufficient structural strength, a simple mechanical structure, and a low manufacturing cost, which make it a promising alternative for making transfemoral prostheses, especially in developing and resource-limited countries.

title: A novel application of definitive screening design: Co/Cu multilayer thin films
container-title: Physica Scripta
2ac342fbd84e25a8e8b32781f1d60c6b8e399294.abstract: Abstract This study aims to determine the optimal deposition parameters to achieve maximum saturation magnetisation of Co/Cu multilayer thin films. A novel statistical approach, DSD (DSD) was implemented to evaluate the simultaneous effects of five key process variables: Total Thickness, Co deposition rate, Cu deposition rate, Co layer thickness, and Substrate Rotation (SR). A 13-run DSD matrix was utilised for the film deposition, with magnetic characterisation performed via Vibrating Sample Magnetometry. Statistical analysis of the mean response characteristics and contour plots identified Co layer thickness as the most influential factor and the primary driver of interactive effects on the saturation magnetisation response. A regression model was developed to predict the optimal deposition recipe. The optimised conditions were identified as: Total Thickness = 144 nm, Co deposition rate = 0.08 nm s −1 , Cu deposition rate = 0.6 nm s −1 , Co layer thickness = 12 nm, and SR = 40 rpm. The regression model predicted a saturation magnetisation value of 1338.2 emu cm −3 under optimal conditions. Experimental validation confirmed these findings, yielding a saturation magnetisation of 1331.9 emu cm −3 , representing a 5.48% increase over the initial baseline (1262.7 emu cm -3 ). Structural characterisation via grazing incidence X-ray diffraction revealed that all synthesised films maintained a face-centred cubic structure with a predominant (111) preferential orientation. Overall, this study establishes DSD as a superior methodology for optimising magnetic multilayer films, providing a streamlined approach to developing next-generation spintronic devices and micro-electromechanical systems. It also presents an application of DSD to optimise magnetic multilayer thin films, demonstrating methodological innovation in experimental materials design. The work makes a valuable methodological contribution to condensed matter physics and materials science.

title: Drought responses in trees are context-dependent: the role of experimental design
container-title: Tree Physiology
8fc97c21662f483cf5fe3c7b0cbda9d6701b63f1.abstract: Abstract Drought is a major driver of vegetation change yet estimates of plant responses to drought are derived from experiments that vary widely in design. This raises an important question: to what extent do reported drought responses reflect biological processes rather than experimental context? We conducted a meta-analysis of drought experiments in Eucalyptus and Quercus, comprising 712 effect sizes from 160 studies and 106 species across photosynthesis, stomatal conductance, intrinsic water-use efficiency (iWUE), leaf water potential, soil water content and root-to-shoot ratio. We evaluated variation associated with growth environment, drought-imposition method, study duration and sample size, and tested whether experimental-design effects persisted after accounting for realised drought intensity, quantified from drought-induced changes in leaf water potential. Drought responses varied substantially among experimental contexts but realised drought intensity overlapped broadly among pot and field experiments and between binary and progressive dry-down treatments, demonstrating that these experimental categories did not correspond to fixed levels of water stress. Accounting for realised drought intensity substantially improved model fit and reduced the estimated difference between pot and field experiments, although experimental-design terms remained jointly significant, indicating that realised drought intensity did not fully account for variation associated with experimental context. Trait-specific responses also differed. Greater realised drought intensity was associated with increasingly negative photosynthetic responses, whereas the corresponding relationship for stomatal conductance was weaker, and no clear relationship was detected for iWUE. Sensitivity analyses identified the photosynthetic response to realised drought intensity as the most consistently supported trait-specific relationship. Our findings show that tree drought responses are context-dependent and that categorical experimental designs should be interpreted alongside the water stress experienced by plants. Incorporating realised drought intensity together with methodological context should improve cross-study comparisons and the interpretation of experimental drought responses.

title: Glass Bodies
On the feasibility of temporal interference stimulation of human brains using two arrays of electrodes
container-title: Biomedical Physics & Engineering Express
defa284f48483c3eda45d670f92d2b9377886a12.abstract: Abstract Background. Conventional temporal interference stimulation (TI, TIS, or tTIS) leverages two pairs of electrodes to induce an interfering electrical field in the brain. Both computational and experimental studies show that TI can stimulate deep brain regions without significantly affecting shallow areas. While promising, optimization of the locations and dosages on these two pairs of electrodes for maximal focal modulation remains computationally challenging. We are the first to propose two arrays of electrodes instead of two or multiple pairs of electrodes to boost modulation focality. However, the optimization algorithm outputs too many electrodes with overlaps across two frequencies, making it difficult to implement in practice. Objective. Based on recent progress in developing multi-channel TI devices and computational work on TI optimization, here we again advocate two-array TI with feasibility data. Methods & Results. We give a review on major algorithms for TI optimization, and compare these algorithms over 25 individual heads across six brain targets. We show that the latest optimization algorithm for two-pair TI innately works for two-array TI with the fastest speed (under 30 s) and a similar amount of electrodes as in multi-pair TI. At four of the six targets, this fastest algorithm for two-array TI achieves similar or even better focality than TI using up to 16 pairs of electrodes that takes days to optimize. We also show a hardware implementation of two-array TI using 10 electrodes on our 8-channel TI device. We argue that two-pair TI is only preferred for maximal modulation strength or when hardware is limited to only two current sources. We restate the focality-intensity tradeoff but in the context of TI and provide a first voxel-level map (at 4 mm resolution) of achievable focality and modulation strength by TI in the MNI-152 head template. Conclusions. Compared to two-pair or multi-pair TI, we promote two-array TI for its similar performance in focality and lower cost in terms of both optimization time and electrodes needed. We hope this work will pave the way for future adoptions of two-array TI for more focal non-invasive deep brain stimulation.

47c83c8edddcf3f80554e658fd45b7249b6122ed.abstract: This paper presents the findings of a multi-year study evaluating the effects of convective drying temperatures and processing durations on the dried product yield of six promising fig cultivars — Uzbekskiy zheltiy, Krym 9, Krym 29, Krym 43, Karshinskiy cherniy, and Dalmatskiy, grown under the subtropical conditions of Surkhandarya region. The experimental data revealed that increasing both drying temperature and exposure duration led to a consistent and substantial reduction in fruit yield due to intensive moisture evaporation, ranging from 68.7–77.9% at 40°C after 20 hours down to 8.7–13.7% following profound dehydration at 60°C after 80 hours. Distinct cultivar-specific dehydration kinetics were observed, governed by pericarp thickness, tissue density, and initial dry matter content. Uzbekskiy zheltiy (average yield of 42.04%) and Dalmatskiy (39.17%) exhibited notable technological stability and uniform moisture release, whereas Krym 29 and Krym 43 demonstrated rapid desiccation, achieving target moisture levels 10–15 hours earlier than the other cultivars. title: Adoption potential, timeline and implementation measures for bio-digital integration in South African construction: a modified Delphi study
container-title: Journal of Engineering, Design and Technology
7375bfa9af4a043c22a3a8c52792da2c8f1ab46e.abstract: Purpose Limited empirical evidence exists on the adoption potential, expected implementation timeline and measures required to support bio-digital integration in developing-country construction contexts. This study aims to examine expert perspectives on these dimensions within the South African construction industry. Design/methodology/approach An exploratory modified Delphi approach was adopted with 12 built environment experts. Adoption potential and expected timelines were assessed using categorical scales and descriptive statistics. Fifteen implementation measures were evaluated using a ten-point Likert scale and reassessed in a second round following controlled feedback. Consensus was assessed using median, interquartile deviation and percentage agreement, with mean and standard deviation additionally reported for Round 2. Findings The expert panel indicated moderate adoption potential and predominantly anticipated adoption within 6–10 years and beyond. Regulatory frameworks, circular economy principles and workforce training were among the most highly rated implementation measures. However, consistently high ratings across all measures indicate limited differentiation between their relative importance. A structured adoption pathway is proposed to support implementation. Research limitations/implications The findings reflect the perspectives of a small, predominantly academically affiliated expert panel and should not be interpreted as representative of the South African construction industry. Practical implications The findings provide context-specific guidance for policymakers, industry stakeholders and researchers on policy development, capacity building and innovation investment. Originality/value The study provides context-specific empirical evidence on expert assessments of bio-digital integration in South Africa by jointly examining adoption potential, anticipated timelines and highly rated implementation measures within a single framework.

title: A Phase 2 Trial of a Respiratory Syncytial Virus and Human Metapneumovirus Combination Virus-Like Particle Vaccine IVX-A12 in Adults ≥60 Years of Age
container-title: The Journal of Infectious Diseases
e2cc7b25eaee67a40c85ba950073c88388e44c18.abstract: Abstract Background Older adults (≥60 years) are susceptible to severe outcomes from infection with respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) or human metapneumovirus (hMPV). IVX-A12 is an investigational vaccine that uses virus-like particles (VLPs) to elicit an immune response against RSV and hMPV. Methods This Phase 2 trial (NCT06481579) randomized (1:1) adults ≥60 years of age to receive a single dose of IVX-A12 (150 µg RSV/150 µg hMPV) or the licensed RSV vaccine RSVPreF3 120 µg with AS01E adjuvant. Safety and immunogenicity were evaluated through 180 days post-vaccination. Results Overall, 143 participants received IVX-A12 (n = 71) or RSVPreF3 (n = 72). Solicited adverse reactions were reported through 7 days post-vaccination (IVX-A12, 25 [35.2%]; RSVPreF3, 36 [50.0%]). Unsolicited adverse events (AEs) were collected through Day 29 (IVX-A12, 5 [7.0%]; RSVPreF3, 11 [15.3%]). Serious AEs (IVX-A12, 2 [2.8%]; RSVPreF3, 1 [1.4%]) and medically attended AEs (IVX-A12, 1 [1.4%]; RSVPreF3, 9 [12.5%]) were documented through Day 181. There were no AEs of special interest and AEs leading to study discontinuation. At Day 29, IVX-A12 and RSVPreF3 administration increased RSV A neutralizing antibody (nAb) levels with geometric mean fold rise (GMFR) of 3.4 and 6.5, and RSV B nAb levels with GMFR of 2.9 and 5.4, respectively. IVX-A12, but not RSVPreF3, also increased hMPV A (GMFR 3.0) and hMPV B (GMFR 2.9) nAb levels. Conclusions IVX-A12 and RSVPreF3 were well tolerated and elicited nAb responses against their targeted pathogens. Given the neutralizing antibody response following IVX-A12, further investigation of an RSV-hMPV VLP combination vaccine is warranted.

title: Cascaded design for microstructured optical diffusers using a Gaussian scattering-kernel model
container-title: Optics Express
d7f500dc099f3a5e4c8406c4e0035581f5e4500d.abstract: A cascaded design method for surface-relief diffusers composed of concave ellipsoidal microstructures is presented. In this method, area-weighted Gaussian scattering kernels for broad parameter screening are combined with ray tracing for local refinement. In Stage I, a continuous surface is generated for each candidate parameter set. Local surface normals within the effective region of each microstructure are used to calculate output ray angles according to Snell’s law. Their mean and covariance define a two-dimensional Gaussian scattering kernel, while the effective-region area determines its weight. The superposition of all kernels is used for broad parameter search. In Stage II, the selected parameter region is refined by ray tracing. For a nearly circular 30 ∘ target, a final horizontal FWHM of 29.92 ∘ is obtained. For an anisotropic 30 ∘ /20 ∘ target, the final principal FWHMs are 30.01 ∘ and 20.05 ∘ . The same optimized surfaces are further evaluated for spatial coherence and polarization, with DoLP values of 0.9980 and 0.9991, respectively.

title: Self-attention-aided multi-layer CNN-LSTM for non-uniform 4-level differential amplitude modulation and detection with atmospheric turbulence for OWANs
container-title: Optics Express
1922c9e0cb34b13e5ea74df3c48f83317a5531ed.abstract: This paper proposes an environment-aware four-level non-uniform differential amplitude modulation and detection scheme assisted by self-attentive multi-layer CNN-LSTM (SA-CNN-LSTM) for optical wireless access networks (OWANs) under atmospheric turbulence, to mitigate severe distortions induced by atmospheric turbulence in optical wireless communication (OWC) systems. Relying on four-level non-uniform differential amplitude modulation (NUADM-4) and a self-attention-aided detection algorithm at the receiving terminal, the proposed scheme can effectively suppress both multiplicative turbulence fading and additive Gaussian noise simultaneously. Numerical results reveal that the proposed scheme achieves remarkable bit error rate (BER) improvements compared with conventional detection frameworks for NUADM-4, and it substantially outperforms the classical uniform four-level pulse amplitude modulation (PAM-4) across diverse turbulence strength regimes. Moreover, the tailored architecture integrating self-attention with multi-layer CNN-LSTM maintains high transmission efficiency, reduces the dimension of the fully-connected layer at the receiver to a certain extent, and accelerates the computation speed compared with the CNN-based algorithm. In comparison with conventional detection-aided algorithms such as vanilla CNN, LSTM, and MLP, the presented scheme delivers a universal BER performance gain. Furthermore, the machine-learning-aided design philosophy for different modulation systems offers a practical design paradigm and implementable solution for the engineering deployment of high-speed OWC systems serving OWANs operating in volatile atmospheric turbulence environments.

title: Bridging or Widening the Gap? AI Policies and Social Justice in Education
container-title: Social Justice in Education
9e13e6e7f3a42906186f831be85e28f41f88c8fe.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is widely promoted as a means to improve educational quality, efficiency, and equity. However, when introduced into systems already shaped by inequality, AI risks reproducing rather than reducing social injustice. This chapter examines whether AI policies in education bridge or widen existing gaps, drawing on Nancy Fraser's framework of redistribution, recognition, and representation. Through a comparative analysis of supranational frameworks and national strategies in the United States, China, India, and Türkiye, the chapter identifies persistent tensions between innovation-driven agendas and justice-oriented goals. The findings suggest that equity is often framed in technocratic terms, while issues of power, participation, and accountability remain marginal. The chapter concludes by proposing a justice-centered policy evaluation framework that emphasizes democratic governance, cultural responsiveness, and the right to contest or refuse harmful AI systems.

title: Mapping Inclusive Practices in English Language Teacher Education
container-title: Social Justice in Education
6033410d4a72f78561e790674716af4e46de64e6.abstract: Teachers are not only facilitators of learning but also agents of change, capable of shaping educational systems to become more equitable and responsive to learner diversity. Their preparation within teacher education programs is therefore critical in ensuring that inclusivity moves from being a stated value to a lived reality. This study examines how inclusive education is represented in an English Language Teacher Education Program (ELTEP) and ELT department's artifacts. Data were collected through systematic document analysis of the program framework, mission, vision and goal statements, and program competency framework of the department. Analysis revealed that inclusivity is acknowledged but unevenly embedded, primarily through a single compulsory course and several electives of limited reach. These findings suggest that while inclusivity has some fragmented curricular presence, there is a need for structural revisions to embed it as a systematic, ELT-specific competency.

title: Polycentric Leadership for Justice and Epistemic Inclusion as Institutional Design in Education

c3bded076c6ad636a7bd0da039f3919e672fde7c.abstract: This chapter proposes a polycentric institutional design that turns equity into routine educational practice. It integrates reflexive coaching, affective leadership, arts-infused curriculum and governance, epistemic inclusion, emotional sustainability, and semiotic pluralism. A systems map links micro-level instruction, meso-level governance, and macro-level accountability to outcomes in access, fairness, belonging, and staff vitality. The framework combines improvement science, realist evaluation, arts-based inquiry, calibrated moderation, and mixed-method scorecards with clear thresholds, review cycles, reciprocal accountability, and retire-to-add rules. It offers a portable operating grammar that distributes authority with coherence, broadens legitimate forms of knowledge without weakening rigor, and supports equitable practices that can survive leadership transitions and adapt to changing institutional conditions.

It synthesizes limitations of conventional approaches, including restricted adaptability, low interoperability, and weak support for user autonomy, and introduces a taxonomy of agentic architectures to guide scalable deployment. The chapter proposes a multi-agent framework integrating multimodal interaction, hybrid reasoning, explainable AI, and health-aware data to enable context-sensitive support. It further addresses privacy, ethical governance, and responsible institutional adoption while outlining future research directions. By bridging architectural innovation with human-centered design, this work advances a forward-looking vision for inclusive intelligent environments.

10df4f7f68f110e4f51b72d7d7994767a18827d5.abstract: Mothers caring for children with Autism Spectrum Disorder often face ongoing stress, emotional challenges, and significant caregiving responsibilities. These factors can affect family dynamics and the quality of support services available for disabilities. Although traditional counselling can offer some psychological relief, it may lack personalization, scalability, or ongoing monitoring. This chapter presents a mindfulness-based intervention enhanced by artificial intelligence, utilizing established techniques like Mindfulness-Based Stress Reduction to provide flexible and accessible mental health resources. By combining AI with structured mindfulness practices, this approach seeks to improve emotional regulation, promote increased caregiver engagement, and foster better collaboration with disability service organizations. The chapter emphasizes that AI-enhanced mindfulness can serve as a valuable resource to bolster caregiver resilience and facilitate more efficient and responsive delivery of disability services.

Advances in artificial intelligence (AI) have introduced transformative opportunities for developing assistive ecosystems that support accessibility, personalized learning, and institutional efficiency. This chapter explores the concept of AI-enabled assistive ecosystems within higher education and examines how integrated AI technologies can support students with physical, sensory, cognitive, and learning disabilities. The chapter analyzes the potential benefits of AI-driven accessibility tools, institutional data analytics, and adaptive learning platforms for promoting inclusive education.

Conventional diagnostic procedures are mostly reactive, time-consuming and subjective and rely on the use of standardized tests, teacher observations, as well as, clinical evaluations. It critically analyzes ethical concerns, implementation barriers and capacity gaps associated with AI adoption in education. Grounded in Social Inclusion Theory, Universal Design for Learning, Ecological Systems Theory, and Affective Computing Theory, it functions as a human-centered decision-support platform rather than a surveillance tool. Ethical dimensions including data privacy, algorithmic bias, transparency, and informed consent are critically examined alongside a roadmap for evidence-based implementation.

e1b09c035b4f62c4219b35e79df5a81dce545160.abstract: Rapid urbanization and climate imperatives place cities at the center of energy transformation, yet thermal demand roughly half of urban energy end-use remains under addressed by electricity focused renewable strategies. title: Enabling Human Transformation Through Socio-Technical Systems in Industry 4.0
Defining Industry 4.0 and the Fourth Industrial Revolution
container-title: Enabling Human Transformation Through Socio-Technical Systems in Industry 4.0
bcd6dbe581045e8a3bb74e904964895fd4eda3b3.abstract: Industry 4.0 is frequently described through its technologies: cyber-physical systems, the Internet of Things, artificial intelligence, advanced analytics, cloud and edge computing, robotics, digital twins and platform infrastructures. Such descriptions are useful, but incomplete. They explain what has become technically possible but do not adequately explain why the organisational and human consequences are so substantial. This chapter therefore defines Industry 4.0 and the wider Fourth Industrial Revolution through a socio-technical systems perspective. It distinguishes the industrial concept of Industry 4.0 from the broader societal idea of the Fourth Industrial Revolution, examines the convergence and interdependence that differentiate the present transition from earlier waves of digitisation, and considers the implications for work, knowledge, authority, identity and institutional arrangements. The central argument is that Industry 4.0 is best understood as a reconfiguration of relationships among people, technologies, organisations and institutions. Its significance lies not in the presence of intelligent technologies alone, but in the redistribution of sensing, interpretation and decision-making across human and machine actors. Human transformation is consequently not an adjunct to technological adoption. It is a constitutive element of the transformation itself.

title: Understanding Human Transformation in Industry 4.0
container-title: Enabling Human Transformation Through Socio-Technical Systems in Industry 4.0
a7b7b36045a25377c76d7aa0f3e2b2d423a8a01d.abstract: Every industrial revolution has altered the relationship between people, technology and work. Industry 4.0 intensifies this relationship because intelligent technologies do more than mechanise or automate predefined tasks: they increasingly sense, predict, recommend and participate in decisions. This introductory chapter therefore introduces the Fourth Industrial Revolution through a socio-technical systems perspective rather than through an extended catalogue of technologies. It briefly traces earlier industrial revolutions to show how industrial change repeatedly reorganised human work, authority and capability, before defining Industry 4.0 as a connected and intelligent socio-technical paradigm. The chapter then develops the Human Transformation through Socio-Technical Systems (HTSTS) Framework as an organising model for the book. The framework proposes that successful transformation depends on the alignment of digital technologies with leadership, culture, continuous learning, human capability, human-technology collaboration, ethical governance, socio-technical integration, organisational resilience and sustainable value creation. A developing-economy lens, with particular attention to South Africa, demonstrates why context matters. The chapter concludes by positioning Industry 5.0 as a human-centric, sustainable and resilient extension of Industry 4.0 and Industry 6.0 as an emerging, still-contested possibility centred on increasingly agentic and adaptive ecosystems. The central argument is straightforward: the defining challenge of Industry 4.0 is less about technological adoption than about human transformation within intelligent systems.

title: Employee Experience and the Future of Work

Comprising an insight into organizational behaviour, the science of human resources management and sustainability, the chapter offers a conceptual approach to the way in which the practices focused on the employees can help foster the creation of more adaptable, responsible, and human-intended organizations.

title: Reskilling and Upskilling in the Age of Intelligent Automation
container-title: Enabling Human Transformation Through Socio-Technical Systems in Industry 4.0
da477aafbddcb4d58d4f82cd117d6ab2f3e3535c.abstract: The rapid proliferation of intelligent automation technologies - encompassing artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning, and robotic process automation (RPA) - is fundamentally reshaping the global workforce landscape. This chapter examines the critical imperatives of reskilling and upskilling as strategic responses to technological displacement and the evolving demands of the labor market. Drawing on contemporary empirical research and theoretical frameworks, the chapter explores how organizations, educational institutions, and policymakers can collaboratively design and implement effective workforce development interventions. Special attention is given to the role of lifelong learning, digital literacy, and human-centric competencies in sustaining employability. The chapter also addresses equity dimensions, highlighting disparities in access to training opportunities across demographic and socioeconomic groups. Practical models and evidence-based recommendations are provided for building resilient, future-ready workforces capable of thriving alongside intelligent machines.

title: Safety Culture as a Socio-Technical Phenomenon
container-title: Enabling Human Transformation Through Socio-Technical Systems in Industry 4.0
cd909a42697fd40405bc679c2be9ba6ae4df241d.abstract: Safety culture is a determinant of organizational performance in high-reliability industries, yet research on it has stayed divided between technical and cultural traditions. This chapter conceptualizes safety culture as an irreducibly socio-technical phenomenon. It draws on socio-technical systems theory, James Reason's organizational accident model and Swiss Cheese Model, and the ICAO Safety Management System. The model positions safety culture at the intersection of human, process, technology, and structure, where it is both an outcome of system design and a mediating variable that regulates how systems respond to complexity and failure. The chapter transfers this to Industry 4.0, where cyber-physical systems, artificial intelligence and the Internet of Things restructure the human-machine relationship. Aviation's experience with cockpit automation, fly-by-wire systems, and Crew Resource Management is a longitudinal reference. The chapter closes with transferable principles: just culture, integration of human factors into system design, and continuous learning.

title: Enabling Platforms and Trust Infrastructures

b982957b20c7ad053d64027ef6ad391db935d848.abstract: The rapid convergence of digital, physical, and biological systems that characterizes Industry 4.0 has fundamentally altered the conditions under which human beings work, collaborate, and make decisions. At the heart of this transformation lies a question that is simultaneously technical and deeply human: on what basis can people reasonably trust the platforms and infrastructures that increasingly mediate their professional and personal lives? This chapter examines the architecture of enabling platforms and the trust infrastructures that must accompany them if Industry 4.0 technologies are to fulfill their transformative potential in human-centered ways. Drawing on socio-technical systems theory, platform economics, institutional design, and emerging scholarship on algorithmic governance, the chapter traces how trust is produced, maintained, and sometimes eroded within complex digital ecosystems. It argues that trust is not a byproduct of good engineering but a designed artifact requiring deliberate institutional, social, and technical effort.

474dc4312b293994049b37e3019b72b04cfc3411.abstract: This chapter examines the evolving relationship between artificial intelligence and sustainability in tourism within the broader context of Industry 4.0 and ongoing digital transformation processes. While AI-driven technologies are widely recognized for their capacity to enhance operational efficiency, optimize resource utilization, and support sustainable development goals, they simultaneously introduce significant conceptual, ethical, and governance-related challenges. Drawing on a socio-technical perspective, this study moves beyond purely technological or outcome-oriented approaches and explores how artificial intelligence reshapes not only the operationalization of sustainability but also its meaning, representation, and lived experience within tourism systems. The chapter introduces the concept of rehumanizing sustainability as a conceptual and practical framework for addressing these challenges. This approach emphasizes the reintegration of human values, agency, and experiential dimensions into AI-driven systems.

title: Smart Cities and Inclusive Development in South Africa

d7acb6b4786cd8f995f0818342ac7c095e9e2167.abstract: The chapter explores how smart objects form human-like social networks to exchange data, highlighting the relationship between individual social standing and internet use. The chapter evaluates the South African experience, focusing on the implementation of smart city initiatives and the risks of deepening exclusion where connectivity, digital literacy, and municipal capacity are unevenly distributed. The key argument is that smart city initiatives in South Africa have the potential to enhance service delivery and social inclusion. Still, their impact is limited by uneven access to digital infrastructure, low digital literacy, and insufficient municipal capacity, particularly in smaller towns and emerging settlements. The chapter's major contribution lies in offering a comprehensive assessment of South Africa's smart city initiatives, identifying opportunities and gaps, and linking them to strategies for promoting economic and social inclusion. The chapter concludes that smart cities, whether in large metros or smaller towns, can transform South Africa's development outcomes.

title: Modeling the Human Platform
container-title: Enabling Human Transformation Through Socio-Technical Systems in Industry 4.0
dc44a29b5998bc65c31bb59bb04ef292dd58e1ca.abstract: Industry 4.0 research still treats sustainability, inclusivity, and workforce capability as separate concerns. This chapter proposes the Human Platform, a higher order sociotechnical capability through which technological enablement, inclusivity practices, and sustainability orientation jointly shape human adaptability and organizational performance. Drawing on Sociotechnical Systems Theory, Human Capital Theory, Dynamic Capabilities Theory, the Capability Approach, and Stakeholder Theory, the chapter develops the Human Platform Model and eight theoretical propositions linking these constructs to sustainable organizational outcomes. A proposed explanatory sequential mixed methods design is offered for future empirical validation, illustrated through documented industry cases. The chapter closes with implications for theory, management practice, and workforce policy in digitally transforming organizations.

582c81d30ddfbf9e19997a9ac90076167e641264.abstract: The corn moth overwinters primarily in the soil in the pupal stage. In the spring, as temperatures rise, the adults emerge and lay eggs on newly sown plots. Upon hatching, the larvae penetrate the soil and feed on germinating seeds, root collars, and young stems. As a result, seedling growth ceases or the plants wither. Development takes 20—40 days, depending on climatic conditions. Most species produce 2—4 generations per year. This article examines the development of the corn moth (Anthomyiidae) and the biological efficacy of control measures against it.

de5c8f6b87e3fd2e38c05b7f6f98a1efc6421451.abstract: This article highlights the agrochemical properties of irrigated gray-earth meadow soils of Sharaf Rashidovsky district of the Jizzakh Free Economic Zone (JEZ), reserves of humus, total nitrogen, total phosphorus, and potassium. Heavy metals adhere to soil colloids and retain their activity in the soil for a long time. In the soil under study, the lead content of Pb is 40-80 mg/kg (the norm is 32 mg/kg or more), cadmium CD is 0.5 - 2.0 mg/kg (the norm is 0.5 mg/kg or more), zinc Zn is 150-220 mg/kg (the norm is 100 mg/kg or more). This situation indicates an increase in the level of pollution combined with salinization and carbonate content of irrigated gray-earth meadow soils.
