title: Human and Organizational Drivers in Marketing-Logistics Collaboration and Supply Chain Performance: Evidence from Moroccan Mass Retailing
container-title: Human Resources Management and Services
8253b628ded6ceb8a75fe8a83ab81eb200e0bb28.abstract: Effective collaboration between manufacturers and retailers depends not only on operational integration but also on the human and organizational conditions that facilitate cross-functional coordination, communication, and joint decision-making. This study examines the relationship between marketing-logistics collaboration and supply chain performance in Moroccan mass retailing, with particular attention to information sharing quality and retail format. Drawing on survey data from 142 organizational observations, the study employs structural equation modeling (SEM) to examine the relationships among marketing-logistics collaboration, information sharing quality, and supply chain performance. CPFR and VMI are examined as specific collaborative practices through supplementary regression analyses rather than as separate constructs in the principal structural model. The findings indicate that marketing-logistics collaboration is positively associated with supply chain performance (β = 0.312, p < 0.001). Information sharing quality significantly mediates this relationship, with a significant indirect effect (β = 0.301, 95% CI [0.182, 0.443]). A multi-group comparison further indicates that the collaboration-performance relationship is stronger among hypermarkets than among supermarkets. These findings support a socio-organizational interpretation of marketing-logistics collaboration, in which human and organizational conditions provide an important theoretical foundation for coordinating people, information, responsibilities, and processes. The study contributes to research on interfunctional collaboration by providing empirical evidence from an emerging-market retail context and offers managerial implications for strengthening organizational coordination and information-sharing quality.

title: Fiscal Forecasting to Support Public Sector Human Resource Planning in European Countries
container-title: Human Resources Management and Services
c1ca91f6357c181c363af1653147a0ee4b9eb119.abstract: Fiscal constraints can affect the affordability of public-sector workforce plans, but aggregate fiscal data do not identify staffing requirements. In this exploratory study, we examine whether historical revenue and expenditure shares jointly explain cross-country variation in their 2018 values and discuss a possible connection to personnel budgeting. We estimate two ordinary least-squares regressions using 28 countries belonging to the European Union in 2018 as observations, with nine annual fiscal shares from 2009–2017 as predictors. The data are percentages of GDP from a fixed Eurostat publication vintage, extracted by Eurostat on 12 May 2019. The revenue and expenditure specifications are jointly significant, with R² = 0.995248 and 0.976869, respectively. These results describe in-sample fit; we did not evaluate forecasting accuracy on independent data. Severe multicollinearity, the small sample, and influential expenditure observations constrain interpretation. In our proposed HRM framework, we link fiscal scenarios to approved personnel allocations and then to costed workforce options. We explain this connection through an illustrative example, but we do not empirically test the framework because the dataset contains no payroll, employment, vacancy, or service-demand indicators. Practical use therefore requires independent forecast validation and institution-specific financial and workforce information.

title: A Smart Insole-Based Explainable AI Framework for Non-Invasive Sciatica Diagnosis Using Optimally Selected Plantar Force Sensors
44867e825acf1cdcc9b18ad253e5851e1983b666.abstract: Abstract Sciatica is a neuropathic disorder that can cause significant alterations in lower-limb biomechanics, including gait asymmetry and abnormal plantar force distribution. This study proposes a wearable, explainable artificial intelligence (XAI)-based framework for automated sciatica diagnosis using optimally selected force-sensitive resistor (FSR) sensors integrated into a smart insole. A dataset of 37 subjects, comprising 20 patients with Sciatica and 17 healthy subjects, was acquired using 16 FSR sensors, with eight sensors positioned on each foot, along with concurrent electromyography (EMG) and inertial measurement unit (IMU) data. From the bilateral plantar force signals, 601 biomechanical features were extracted, incorporating statistical, temporal, magnitude, and inter-limb asymmetry characteristics. A K-fold combinatorial sensor-selection strategy identified the optimal sensor configuration, with K = 5 providing the most stable performance. The optimal configurations, L2, L5, L8 for the left foot and R2, R5, R8 for the right foot, reduced the number of sensors from 16 to 6, representing a 62.5% reduction in sensing hardware. The selected left-foot sensors achieved 96% accuracy, 96% precision, 93% recall, 94% F1-score, and 0.93 AUC, while the right-foot sensors achieved 87% accuracy, 83% precision, 76% recall, 79% F1-score, and 0.91 AUC. Using the six optimally selected sensors, the proposed one-dimensional convolutional neural network (1D-CNN) achieved 90.3% classification accuracy, 89.9% sensitivity, 90.3% specificity, and a ROC-AUC of 0.911. Furthermore, XAI-based plantar heatmaps confirmed the contribution of the selected biomechanical regions to the classification decision. Cross-validation against the concurrent EMG/IMU modality achieved 85.2% accuracy, with approximately 81.5% diagnostic agreement between the force-sensor and EMG/IMU models. The quantitative results demonstrate that a substantially reduced FSR sensor configuration can preserve diagnostically relevant biomechanical information while providing accurate, interpretable, and portable sciatica screening. The proposed framework offers potential for low-cost wearable gait assessment and automated clinical decision support.

title: A Bangla-language retrieval-augmented conversational agent for maternal health in a low-resource setting: design and formative evaluation
b7a713fa17d14289e6fb35f7ac651b94d58a8580.abstract: Abstract Maternal health information in Bangladesh is difficult to access for women with limited literacy and no English, and perinatal mental health remains under-supported. We designed and formatively evaluated Baby and Me, a Bangla-language conversational agent that retrieves from a curated, physician-reviewed corpus of 247 maternal health articles, segmented into 2,945 indexed passages, and generates responses grounded in the retrieved material. A survey of 72 pregnant and postpartum women established design requirements; Bangla-only language preference was universal among women with no formal or primary education, and a quarter of households reported annual income below one lakh Bangladeshi taka. Candidate model configurations were screened against physician-authored reference answers before deployment. Twenty-four respondents then rated the deployed system: ease of use was highest (mean 4.79 of 5) and clarity strong (4.54), while trust (4.29), concern alignment (4.04) and empathy (4.00) were lower and more dispersed. Interviews indicated that the interface showed users that retrieval had occurred but not whether guidance came from aclinically reviewed source, suggesting that process transparency and source attribution are not interchangeable. As a formative study with a modest sample, a single site and no controlled comparison, this work establishes feasibility rather than effectiveness.

title: Human-AI Collaboration in Urban Digital Transformation: Balancing Efficiency and Human Values in Shanghai’s AI-Enabled Talent Recruitment
container-title: Digital Technologies Research and Applications
99b2a4d2edc2dc8df689bff6b515848affbe723a.abstract: In the context of the urban digital revolution, recruitment through AI technologies has become common practice to address competition in the labor market. However, it is still unclear how the effectiveness of such recruitment is connected with humanistic values. For this research, an exploratory qualitative research design was used, involving semi-structured interviews with eight human resource professionals in Shanghai. Based on the results, the use of AI in recruitment led to increased efficiency mainly when screening candidates through high-volume, standardized processes, although the promised efficiency was not delivered in practice because the introduction of the AI system increased the workload. Patterns of human-machine cooperation were observed in different companies: tech companies and foreign companies are inclined to adopt interactive adjustment approaches, while state-owned enterprises retain human-dominated decision-making. Transparency of algorithms was still lacking in numerous instances, and there was an asymmetry in the accountability framework of algorithms, wherein disobeying algorithms carries more personal consequences than obeying them. The more experienced professionals became more autonomous in their work, while the less experienced professionals depended more on the algorithm. Issues like management support, information accuracy, and departmental integration have a major impact on implementation. This study contributes to the theory of human-machine collaboration by proposing the concept of asymmetric algorithmic accountability, which captures the uneven distribution of organizational consequences for following versus overriding AI recommendations and shapes practitioner behavior in ways that extend beyond individual trust or algorithmic transparency.

title: From AI readiness to regenerative tourism orientation: a tourist-centric model of smart tourism villages
container-title: ABAC Journal
600067ed573dc780c1bd155c47ed81d59d2f7b38.abstract: Purpose This study develops and validates a tourist-centric model of AI-driven smart tourism villages (AI-DSTV), explaining how perceived digital infrastructure and smart governance relate to tourist acceptance and perceived regenerative tourism orientation (PRTO) through rural authenticity, value co-creation, AI trust, and perceived service value. Design/methodology/approach A cross-sectional survey involved 686 domestic tourists who had experienced an AI-supported tourism touchpoint in rural tourism settings in Indonesia. The sample was predominantly young and digitally engaged, with 75.1% aged 18–24 and 68.4% students. The model was tested using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) with 10,000 bootstrap resamples and importance-performance map analysis (IPMA). Findings All 12 hypothesized relationships were significant. Rural authenticity strongly enhanced perceived AI service value, while tourist value co-creation strengthened AI trust and ethical acceptance. Digital infrastructure and smart governance also showed significant downstream effects through authenticity–service-value and co-creation–trust pathways. The model explained 56.3% of PRTO variance. IPMA identified AI trust and ethical acceptance as the most important antecedent of PRTO and the lowest-performing construct, indicating a key managerial priority. Practical implications Rural destinations should prioritize transparent, culturally grounded, participatory and locally accountable AI systems. Strengthening ethical trust, co-creation, and culturally appropriate personalization may offer greater managerial leverage than technological sophistication alone. Originality/value The study extends technology-adoption research beyond behavioral acceptance by introducing PRTO as a tourist-level psychological outcome. It conceptualizes AI-DSTV as a socio-technical ecosystem linking destination readiness with authenticity, co-creation, trust and service evaluation while distinguishing regenerative orientation from verified destination regeneration.

title: Generative Inverse Design of Shell Metamaterials through Continuous-Latent Conditional Flow Matching
29d4141b48d61843e953cf6048d027f8417e5f4f.abstract: Abstract Mechanical metamaterials derive programmable properties from a repeated unit cell’s geometry. A stress–strain curve summarizesa three-dimensional shell geometry in a few numbers, so distinct geometries can share a curve and the inversemap from curve to geometry is one-to-many. We develop a continuous-latent conditional flow-matching framework thatdesigns periodic shell unit cells for prescribed compressive responses. Each shell geometry is a continuous periodic function,and a function encoder learns a basis that compresses it into 32 coefficients. Conditional flow matching learns theresponse-conditioned coefficient distribution and generates many candidate geometries. On 200 held-out targets, our 5.9-million-parameter model reaches a mean best-of-20 NRMSE of 0.074 at 73% validity, against 0.118 and 48% for a 40-million-parameter tokenized-diffusion baseline. Sampling requires 26.8 ms per candidate versus 2.03 s for the baseline.Finite-element analysis of 981 shortlisted candidates yields a mean best-design NRMSE of 0.092, compared with a simulationto-simulation reproducibility of 0.016–0.063.

title: Lumbar Modic Changes Concentrate Stress at the Endplate–Vertebral Interface
b87f3df78e9104e01b7b79ae5a03b5d0bbf19b93.abstract: Abstract Background Modic changes occur where the lumbar disc transfers load to the vertebral body. Regional stress and segmental motion together describe their mechanical effects. We examined how material inputs for each Modic type changed local stress, with and without disc degeneration. Methods Paired computed tomography measurements from 24 patients with Modic changes provided stiffness multipliers for each type: seven type I, ten type II, and seven type III cases. Eight L4–L5 finite element models included normal anatomy, isolated disc degeneration, isolated Modic types I–III, and each type combined with disc degeneration. The models shared one base geometry, with a predefined reduction in disc height in degenerated models. Geometry and loading were matched to assess material effects. We applied 500 N compression and a 10 N·m moment in six directions and descriptively compared endplate and vertebral margin stress, disc stress, and range of motion. Results Models containing Modic changes showed focal stress concentration near the mapped region. Isolated Modic changes reduced range of motion by 0.5%–7.7%. Type III had the highest mean margin stress in every tested condition, and maximum stress rankings varied. Maximum L4 margin stress in isolated type III ranged from 13.97 to 36.28 MPa. Geometric mean stiffness multipliers were 2.05, 2.09, and 5.02 for types I, II, and III, respectively. With coexisting disc degeneration, margin stress redistribution depended on vertebral level and loading direction. Conclusions In the tested L4–L5 geometry, Modic-related material heterogeneity concentrated stress at the endplate and adjacent vertebral margin. Segmental motion changed relatively little. Local stress assessment complements segmental motion when studying Modic biomechanics.

title: Digital Agency and the Preservation of the Banggai Language Among the Younger Generation in Banggai City
container-title: Journal of General Education and Humanities
82dd679ddd2968dd144017e18e33b75be95f7aca.abstract: Regional languages are essential components of cultural identity, serving not only as means of communication but also as vehicles for transmitting values, knowledge, and local wisdom across generations. Banggai, spoken in Banggai Laut Regency, has shown signs of declining use among younger generations in family and educational settings. Meanwhile, digital technology offers new opportunities for regional language use and dissemination. This study examines the forms, functions, and factors influencing Banggai language maintenance among young people in Banggai City through the perspective of digital agency, which views youth as active and creative users of digital technology. This qualitative case study involved 29 respondents who completed open-ended questionnaires and three informants who participated in in-depth interviews. Participants aged 15–30 years were purposively selected. Data were analyzed using the interactive model of Miles, Huberman, and Saldaña, with source and methodological triangulation. The findings show that 19 respondents use Banggai on social media, primarily in informal conversations with fellow speakers. However, none reported producing Banggai-language content or collaborating on content creation, while digital resources, such as dictionaries, were rarely used. Digital spaces help maintain language use and strengthen linguistic identity and pride, although their contribution to broader language use, learning, and intergenerational transmission remains largely potential. Key supporting factors include preservation motivation and family and school support. Major barriers include limited language use in families and communities, the influence of Indonesian and other languages, restricted vocabulary, social stigma, and scarce digital content and learning resources. Limited device and internet access were not reported as barriers. This study refines digital agency by distinguishing language-use agency from content-production and collaborative agency, highlighting the need for youth-driven digital resources supported by families, schools, and local governments.

title: Developing a principles-based planning resource for the evaluation of public/consumer involvement in health service design
container-title: Australian Journal of Primary Health
35d625ee506678f224abc520ad0d366454ae08a1.abstract: Background Australian health services are required to incorporate public involvement in design and redesign; however, guidance on evaluating outcomes of public involvement is limited. Our aim was to develop public involvement planning resources to better support health services to evaluate outcomes. Methods Using a participatory research approach, the development of these resources involved small group workshops at an Australian regional health service, a web-based stakeholder survey, and a small process evaluation. Results Workshop activity resulted in five themes: evaluation purpose, parameters, partnership, practicalities and process. The themes informed the development of a draft infographic (the 5Ps) and accompanying material. Refinement of the 5Ps infographic and material occurred through a broader stakeholder survey that fed into the final workshop. A small evaluation of the workshop process was completed. Conclusion Through a participatory process, stakeholders supported the development of an evaluation resource for public involvement in health service design. Wider adoption of the 5Ps infographic and material will enable tailoring to the local context.

title: High Use, Low Preparation
container-title: American Journal of Physical Medicine & Rehabilitation
cd596e36835769e8c758e2939412febb985e5034.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (Gen-AI) has rapidly entered clinical environments, posing a risk of “cognitive offloading” that may impede the development of independent clinical judgment. This study conducted a cross-sectional survey of residents, fellows, and faculty at a large academic medical center in January 2026 to quantify Gen-AI utilization and perceptions in physical medicine and rehabilitation (PM&R) to inform curriculum development. Thirty-six trainees (95% response rate) and 11 faculty members (30% response rate) completed the survey; 43 (91.5%) reported any Gen-AI use and formed the analytic sample. Among users, 72.1% used Gen-AI daily for clinical learning and 51.2% during patient encounters, yet 67.4% were self-taught and only 7.0% always requested citations. Trainees requested citations more often than faculty ( P =.048), while faculty more often relied on clinical judgment without additional verification (62.5% vs. 25.7%, P =.089). Gen-AI-derived evidence was rarely surfaced in teaching: 60.5% discussed it during case presentations rarely or never, and only 16.2% always disclosed its origin. Residents are integrating Gen-AI into clinical workflows at rates that outpace faculty familiarity, while verification remains largely undiscussed and untaught. These gaps highlight an urgent need for structured Gen-AI curricula in PM&R residency.

title: The Genome Lab: designing a simpler interface for genome assembly and annotation
container-title: F1000Research
1dfab62eb2f26c63c18ec4774e4abab1c6d4748f.abstract: Background Galaxy is a web-based platform for analysing data, particularly biological data such as DNA. While genome assembly and annotation is a typical starting point for users, navigating this process can be challenging: many factors affect which tools and settings are appropriate, and researchers with genomes to analyse often have deep taxonomic expertise but less bioinformatics experience. Methods To better present relevant resources, we built the Genome Lab: a domain-specific interface for genome assembly and annotation. Informed by user experience considerations, the design targets discoverability and navigation, and is intended to reduce the effort required to find resources and to understand the genome assembly process. Applying six key design decisions, we gave the Lab a clear, simple layout showing an organised set of tools and workflows, so that new users can get started quickly and experienced users have their frequently required resources at hand. Results We present a worked example of genome assembly and annotation, carried out the way a researcher might use the Genome Lab. Working from Nanopore sequencing reads, the curated path produced a genome assembly, a completeness assessment and gene models, viewed in a genome browser. Conclusions The Genome Lab has been implemented as a generic framework that other communities have since used to build Labs for their own domains, on Galaxy Australia and elsewhere. A curated, domain-specific interface provides a simpler entry point for researchers new to the field. We describe the design decisions, the framework and a worked example, which may help other groups build a similar interface for their own domain.

title: Regional and Hormone-Associated Adaptations of Tissue-Resident Memory T cells across the Human Female Reproductive Tract.
4d43fd1b7467c891d8bdd902fada04b504a00d2e.abstract: Abstract Tissue-resident memory T cells (TRM) are essential components of mucosal immunity, yet their organization and regulation across the human female reproductive tract (FRT) remain poorly understood. Here, we investigated TRM across the FRT from donors with diverse hormonal profiles and identified regional and lineage-specific differences in phenotype, transcriptional programming, and abundance. CD8 T cells displayed greater enrichment of canonical TRM signatures and extensive T cell receptor clonal sharing across tissues, suggesting a common antigenic immune history. Despite these differences, resident CD4 and CD8 T cells shared CCR5 protein expression and TSC22D3 transcript enrichment, highlighting potentially distinctive features of FRT TRM. Single-cell transcriptomics revealed compartmental differences in metabolic, stress- and hormone-response pathways. Progesterone and testosterone levels were associated with differences in cervical T cell composition and CD8 TRM abundance. Together, these findings describe regional specialization by resident T cell immunity across the FRT and show that hormonal cues contribute to their homeostasis, offering new insight into factors that shape immune surveillance at mucosal sites of urogenital pathogen exposure.

title: A Multi-Agentic Digital Twin Framework for Human-in-the-loop Workflows
8533d3545a00a3ae0313b2e351dd9d6e1c2500ac.abstract: Abstract Traditional robot task planning struggles to recover from failures and changing requirements because it relies on predefined rules, labelled datasets, and limited state awareness. Digital twins provide real-time virtual representations of physical systems, while multi-agent systems support collaborative, stepwise reasoning. However, their integration for failure evaluation, requirement adaptation, and state-aware robot planning remains underexplored, particularly at the architectural level. This study proposes a multi-agentic digital twin framework for human-in-the-loop workflows, enabling bidirectional communication between machines, digital twins, and multi-agents. The framework is validated through robot task planning for an aerospace product-qualification metrology process. Results show that digital-twin integration adds 885-1,149 milliseconds to communication between robots and agents because continuous state updates are required. Multi-agent workflows need more human feedback than single-agent workflows to align outputs with predefined goals and mitigate hallucinations, highlighting the importance of human-in-the-loop orchestration. Datasets, logs, code, videos, results, and deployment instructions are available on GitHub 1 .

title: Genomic and ecological specialization of Methanobrevibacter species shape human methane emission and overall gut ecosystem function
1b329149b06aaef272aa3347af41f72466f1b589.abstract: Abstract Methane is a unique archaeal metabolite that links gut microbial ecology to host physiology. Although intestinal methane production varies by several orders of magnitude between individuals and has been associated with gastrointestinal transit and disease states, the ecological and functional determinants underlying this variation remain poorly understood. Here, we integrate breath methane phenotyping with shotgun metagenomics, metatranscriptomics, comparative genomics, cultivation and stable-isotope tracing in 80 deeply characterized individuals to determine the species-level and functional basis of human gut methanogenesis. Breath methane levels strongly reflected archaeal abundance but could not fully explain methane emission; species-resolved profiling revealed that methane emission represents distinct archaeome states rather than differences in methanogen quantity alone. High methane emitters were dominated by Methanobrevibacter smithii and M. intestini, whereas low emitters harbored a previously uncharacterized Methanobrevibacter lineage (M. sp900766745), for which we propose the name Candidatus Methanobrevibacter hominipaucus sp. nov. Comparative genomics revealed that M. sp900766745 represents a metabolically streamlined lineage lacking several methyl-compound utilization pathways and displaying reduced substrate acquisition capacity. Communities of low-emission individuals exhibited reduced microbial transcriptional activity and accumulated incompletely processed dietary metabolites, indicating lower fermentative turnover and altered hydrogen flux.

title: Serum context shapes macrophage baseline state and LPS responsiveness in human monocyte-derived macrophages
container-title: Frontiers in Immunology
a35c30c1620186587d52bac1de6627712debcfb1.abstract: Background Human monocyte-derived macrophages (MDMs) are central to translational immunology, yet most differentiation protocols rely on xenogeneic fetal calf serum (FCS), which may alter macrophage functional states. Autologous serum (AS) maintains the donor-specific immunometabolic milieu, but its impact on macrophage baseline programming and stimulus responsiveness has not been systematically evaluated. Methods Monocytes from 32 healthy donors were differentiated in parallel with 10% AS or FCS for five days with M-CSF, followed by 24-hour stimulation with LPS, IL-4/IL-10/TGF-β, or vehicle. Cytokine secretion was quantified by multiplex assay, activation markers by qPCR, and baseline transcriptional programs by bulk RNA sequencing. Results AS- versus FCS-differentiated MDMs showed significantly greater LPS-induced secretion of TNF-α, IL-6, IL-1β, IP-10, IL-23, TARC and IL-1RA together with higher CD86 and CCR7 expression, whereas these differences were not observed following IL-4/IL-10/TGF-β stimulation or in unstimulated cells. Transcriptomic analysis of unstimulated MDMs identified distinct serum-dependent baseline programs, with FCS associated with increased expression of inflammatory cytokines, chemokines, and innate immune activation genes, whereas AS was associated with genes involved in lipid metabolism, extracellular matrix remodeling, and immune surveillance. Conclusions Serum context is a major determinant of macrophage baseline state and inflammatory responsiveness. FCS is associated with a more inflammatory baseline and attenuated LPS-induced activation, while AS shows a metabolically and immunologically homeostatic baseline with greater LPS responsiveness. These findings demonstrate that serum composition shapes basal macrophage programs and differentially modulates responses to inflammatory versus alternative stimulation, supporting consideration of autologous serum when modeling donor-specific innate immune responses.

title: Bite-block effects on native s/ʃ and English r/l in child speakers of a language with/without this contrast
container-title: Frontiers in Human Neuroscience
d15c4702e6480bd35e07fb78dd49ffa982f77bdc.abstract: Learning to produce non-native speech contrasts requires developing new phonological categories as well as new articulatory-perceptual mappings for these new categories. However, within the same speakers, it remains unclear how these new categories compare to contrasts that are already fully established in the native language. To examine potential differences between native and non-native sounds, we recorded Japanese children’s (8–12 years) productions of a non-native contrast (English /ɹ/−/l/, indexed by F3–F2) and a native contrast (/s/−/ʃ/, indexed by Center of Gravity). Recordings were done both under normal speaking conditions and under articulatory perturbation induced by a temporary bite-block while listening to a model. Children acoustically differentiated both contrasts under normal speaking conditions, but the two contrasts showed different developmental profiles: differentiation of the native contrast did not vary with age, whereas differentiation of the non-native contrast was significant only in older children. As expected, the bite-block manipulation reduced acoustic distinctness for both contrasts; however, susceptibility to this disruption was age-invariant for the native contrast but increased with age for the non-native contrast.

title: Trust in artificial intelligence and AI-assisted social and civic decision-making among Arab youth: evidence from Egypt, Kuwait, and the UAE
container-title: Frontiers in Sociology
9c22c48dec77add12e18981832964c2f183e35aa.abstract: Introduction Trust in artificial intelligence (AI) increasingly shapes how young people evaluate information and public issues, yet evidence from Arab contexts remains limited. This study examined the socio-technical correlates of trust in AI and its association with AI-assisted social and civic decision-making among digitally engaged youth in Egypt, Kuwait, and the United Arab Emirates. Methods A cross-sectional online survey was conducted with 1,023 respondents aged 18–35 recruited through purposive, non-probability sampling. Confirmatory factor analysis (CFA), structural equation modeling (SEM), multi-group CFA, and competing full- versus partial-mediation models evaluated measurement and structural relationships. Results The partially mediated model fit significantly better than the fully mediated model, Δχ2(5) = 55.66, p &lt; 0.001. Institutional confidence (β = 0.303), AI literacy (β = 0.281), perceived usefulness (β = 0.242), and social influence (β = 0.107) were positively associated with trust in AI, and perceived risk was negatively associated (β = −0.106; all p &lt; 0.001). Trust was positively associated with AI-assisted decision-making (β = 0.412, p &lt; 0.001). Significant indirect associations through trust were observed for all five antecedents, while the direct perceived-risk path to AI-assisted decision-making was nonsignificant. Multi-group CFA supported metric and practical scalar measurement invariance across the three countries. Discussion The findings support a socio-technical account of AI trust in which technological, cognitive, institutional, and social conditions jointly relate to AI-assisted decision-making, with trust functioning as a central but not exclusive pathway. Given the cross-sectional, purposive design, findings are interpreted as associations rather than causal or nationally representative effects.

title: Integrating digital financial solutions into MSME business models: assessment of MSME readiness for digital financial integration
container-title: Frontiers in Human Dynamics
4660f01956871da463f0bc7d2c71e4952030eb95.abstract: The integration of digital financial solutions has become essential for enhancing the sustainability and competitiveness of Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs), especially in developing economies. This study examined MSME readiness in terms of digital capability, financial literacy, infrastructure readiness, and strategic orientation in relation to the integration of digital financial systems. Using a quantitative, cross-sectional research design, data were collected from 189 MSMEs in Surigao del Sur, Philippines, and analyzed using descriptive statistics, correlation, and regression techniques. The findings revealed a strong positive relationship between MSME readiness and the level of digital financial integration. MSMEs with higher levels of readiness demonstrated greater improvements in business performance, operational efficiency, and financial stability, whereas those with lower levels of readiness gained only limited benefits. The results also indicated that full and systematic integration produced better outcomes than partial adoption. Overall, the study highlights that readiness is a key driver of successful digital transformation among MSMEs and emphasizes the need for targeted interventions to strengthen their capabilities and support sustainable digital finance adoption.

title: A preliminary design framework for human-friendly AI interaction: grounded in anthropomorphism
container-title: Frontiers in Computer Science
46e7d698557d6ad9c8af0e26c30db1eac6a6fb1b.abstract: People converse with AI as they would with friends in daily life, collaborate with it, and form personalized relationships. In response to these emerging forms of interaction, this study clarifies the concept of Human-Friendly Interaction with conversational AI and develops the Human-Friendly AI Interaction Design Framework (HFAI-DF). This study positions anthropomorphism, a foundational phenomenon in human–AI interaction, as a theoretical bridge and reviews literature on anthropomorphism theory and related research on human cognition. On this basis, this study interpretively derives and organizes how anthropomorphism-inducing stimuli can be applied to AI agents, systematizing them into 30 AI behavioral items that enable human-friendly interaction. Subsequently, a survey was conducted and exploratory factor analysis performed to identify six dimensions as a preliminary structure for a design framework for AI’s human-friendly interaction. These dimensions are: Self-Aware Interaction, User-Adaptive Responsiveness Interaction, Context-Aware Reasoning Interaction, Socio-Emotional Interaction, Creative Collaboration Interaction, and Proactive Assistance Interaction. Within the evolving AI research landscape focused on interaction, this study extends the human-centered AI concept toward human-friendly interaction that operates in an organic manner comparable to human–human conversation, grounded in an understanding of human cognitive functioning. The proposed framework provides both AI providers and designers with an initial structure for shaping and improving the quality of human-friendly interaction.

title: Perceptions of AI in veterinary medicine: insights from students, faculty, and practicing veterinarians in Hong Kong
container-title: Frontiers in Veterinary Science
d5c0bfa269240bf48c6ea87f212741cd8f464ca1.abstract: Introduction As artificial intelligence (AI) transforms veterinary medicine, understanding stakeholder perceptions is crucial for its effective and responsible integration. To support the development of targeted educational and policy initiatives, this study aimed to evaluate the knowledge, attitudes, and practices regarding AI among Bachelor of Veterinary Medicine (BVM) students, PhD students, faculty, and practicing veterinarians in Hong Kong. Methods A cross-sectional online survey was conducted between December 2023 and March 2024 among BVM students, PhD students, and faculty members at City University of Hong Kong, and practicing veterinarians in Hong Kong who are members of the Hong Kong Veterinary Association. The survey assessed participants’ familiarity with AI, prior training, perceived benefits, concerns, and willingness to adopt AI in education and clinical practice. Descriptive and comparative analyses were performed to examine differences across stakeholder groups. Results Of 79 complete responses, nearly half (46.8%) reported unfamiliarity with AI concepts. Only 17.7% had received formal AI training, although 78.5% expressed interest in future AI education. Most respondents agreed that AI could enhance veterinary teaching and practice (83.5%) and 81.0% indicated they would likely incorporate AI tools into their work. Key perceived benefits included support for case-based learning (83.5%), virtual animal models for teaching (77.2%), and improved diagnostic accuracy (74.7%). However, 41.8% felt inadequately prepared to use AI. Major concerns included veterinarian accountability for AI-related harms (79.7%), lack of system flexibility (75.9%), and potential clinical inaccuracies (70.9%). Descriptively, practicing veterinarians reported the lowest AI tool use (66.7% had never used AI tools), the lowest preparedness (66.7% felt unprepared), and lower agreement with AI’s clinical benefits, although attitude differences were not statistically significant. Conclusion These exploratory findings suggest gaps in self-reported AI knowledge and differing perceptions of AI across veterinary stakeholder groups in Hong Kong, with AI use already widespread at the time of the survey despite limited formal training. While enthusiasm for AI integration is high, concerns about preparedness, accuracy, and ethical responsibility remain. Larger, multi-institutional studies are needed to confirm these patterns and to inform targeted training programs and ethical frameworks for safe and effective AI adoption in veterinary medicine.

title: Global classrooms: a tri-national study on AI integration by higher education students
container-title: Frontiers in Computer Science
4ce5be4917c40263b11f6c7ca8eabe77dd89211a.abstract: Collaborative cross-cultural learning expands higher education students’ (HES’) intercultural and language awareness, enhances their intercultural competence, has an impact on attitudes towards technology and AI as well as towards the course design and general satisfaction with the collaborative experience in the course. Furthermore, their self-perceived role in a digital setting and their self-perceived English proficiency were measured. The CoGIH Project encourages HES to explore the educational potential of artificial intelligence (AI) for learning and teaching in the school setting. A special focus is on the impact AI might have on the language learning process in English as a lingua franca in a multilingual setting. N = 113 HES, including both pre-service and in-service teachers as well as students preparing for educational administration, from five institutions in Israel, Germany, and Hungary collaborated in 14 international groups, representing five higher education institutions; n = 91 answered the questionnaires. Each group investigated the educational potential of a specific AI application and developed an AI-supported, results-based webpage. The study employed a multi-method research design. Questionnaires were administered to the HES to investigate their experiences at the beginning and at the end of the course. While quantitative data were used to investigate the research through the lens of descriptive statistics and correlations between factors, qualitative data from the open questions were analysed to enable a deeper understanding of HES’ perceptions, experiences and meanings, as well as their critical thinking. The study highlighted strengths and challenges in using AI for educational purposes. The HES valued clear structures, logical navigation, and creative, motivating tasks. Simultaneously, recurring issues included incomplete translations, limited depth of critical reflection, and weaknesses in visual design. In sum, even though AI can support creativity and language learning and teaching, individual learners’ reflections and authentic teacher guidance remain indispensable for meaningful learning.

title: P2-VGAN: a lightweight velocity-weighted graph attention network for privacy-conscious edge anomaly detection
container-title: Frontiers in Artificial Intelligence
76c7345c8fd139e3ac90e2e10cd36d5a162fde2d.abstract: Introduction Two persistent challenges hinder intelligent video surveillance in public spaces: dense pixel-based models incur heavy computational costs on edge infrastructure, and continuous capture of identifiable imagery creates substantial visual privacy liabilities. Skeleton-based pipelines, which abstract each video frame into articulated landmark coordinates, support visual data minimization by discarding appearance information. However, conventional graph backbones weight joint trajectories uniformly across time, frequently confusing benign high-speed locomotion (such as sprinting for transit) with violent anomalies. Methods This paper presents the Privacy-Conscious Velocity-Weighted Graph Attention Network (P2-VGAN; the prefix “P2” is retained as a legacy identifier designating privacy-conscious representation rather than a cryptographic guarantee), an efficient framework engineered for desktop-class CPU edge gateways. The pipeline decouples motion analysis from visual appearance by extracting 33 planar body landmarks via a single-shot pose estimator; the application does not intentionally store or transmit decoded RGB frames after pose extraction, ensuring downstream processing operates strictly on appearance-reduced pose coordinates. The primary contribution is the Velocity-Weighted Attention Mechanism (VW-AM), an ultra-lightweight gating module requiring only two shared parameters that converts inter-frame coordinate displacements into a bounded squared-displacement motion proxy. This proxy modulates node features prior to multi-head graph attention, directing message passing toward rapidly moving limbs while damping near-stationary joints. Trained under a weakly supervised Multiple Instance Learning objective with temporal smoothness and sparsity regularizers, P2-VGAN is evaluated across five random seeds on the ShanghaiTech Campus and a human-centric subset of UCF-Crime. Results On ShanghaiTech, the model achieves a frame-level AUC of 84.72 ± 0.28% with 1.81 M downstream trainable parameters (pose-extractor parameters excluded) and sustains 34.01 frames per second (FPS) on an Intel Core i7-10700 CPU without hardware acceleration. When compared directly with an identical Vanilla GAT backbone without gating (83.14 ± 0.39%), VW-AM provides an unconfounded +1.58% absolute AUC gain ( p = 0.00096). On the human-centric UCF-Crime subset (215 test videos), it attains 77.88 ± 0.35% micro-average AUC, with high-motion categories (Fighting, Assault) exceeding 82% AUC. Stepwise ablations document an incremental +2.52% gain from VW-AM over an adaptive ST-GCN baseline. Discussion We position P2-VGAN as a Pareto-efficient framework for lightweight CPU surveillance, acknowledging that coordinate streams reduce visual surface exposure but do not eliminate biometric gait re-identification.

title: Cell-free DNA in human ovarian follicular fluid as a potential biomarker of embryo quality in IVF cycles: a pilot study
container-title: Frontiers in Endocrinology
2f900190d87b40b49abd647d0e5af90b73d5ad7d.abstract: Introduction There is growing interest in evaluating cell-free DNA (cfDNA) in follicular fluid (FF) as a molecular feature of the follicular microenvironment and examining its association with subsequent embryo development. This exploratory pilot study aimed to investigate the association between FF cfDNA integrity, measured by the Arthrobacter luteus (ALU) 247/115 ratio, and morphology-based embryo quality in IVF cycles. Methods This observational study analyzed 106 follicular fluid samples from patients undergoing IVF with intracytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI) at a single fertility center. FF samples were collected during ovum pick-up, and cfDNA concentrations were quantified using ALU-quantitative PCR. To evaluate the ALU247/115 ratio in relation to age, participants were categorized into three age groups. Results The ALU247/115 ratio showed a significant but weak positive correlation with embryo quality score across all patients (n = 106, r = 0.23, p = 0.016). Subgroup analysis revealed stronger correlations in women under 35 years (n = 31, r = 0.38, p = 0.035) and those aged 35–39 years (n =40, r = 0.32, p = 0.044). No significant correlation was observed in women aged 40 or older (n = 35, r = 0.21, p = 0.225). Conclusions In women under 40, increased cfDNA fragmentation in FF was associated with lower morphology-based embryo quality. However, the observed correlations were modest, and the absence of preimplantation genetic testing for aneuploidy (PGT-A), implantation, clinical pregnancy, and live birth outcomes limits clinical interpretation. These exploratory findings do not establish FF cfDNA as a clinically validated predictive biomarker or demonstrate that it improves embryo selection. Larger prospective studies incorporating embryo ploidy and clinically relevant reproductive outcomes are warranted.

title: AI-generated advertising in agricultural livestreaming and the auditability of disclosure regulation: a three-layer audit of public Douyin data from China
container-title: Frontiers in Sustainable Food Systems
c177ed750eb610123bd142c9d637834496b25555.abstract: Agricultural products are credence goods, and in livestreaming, the grower’s visible presence signals the price. China has required labeling of deep-synthesis content since January 2023 and, since 1 September 2025, of AI-generated synthetic content. Whether public platform data can verify compliance in a market where the authenticity premium is especially salient remains unclear, given that growers themselves sell produce. We audited three layers of public Chinese platform data: 189 policy snippets, 19 accounts retrieved by AI technical terms, and 455 unique authors retrieved by crop names. In the one policy coding field with complete intercoder agreement ( κ = 1.000), only 6 of 189 snippets name authenticity as a farmer asset. Retrieval by technical terms returns intermediaries: 13 of 19 accounts sell AI tools or tutorials, and none discloses using AI to sell its own produce. Among AI-announcing cases retrieved by crop-name queries, an expanded text-field detector validated at 94.7% recall flags 10 of 455 authors: seven supply-side or service-provider accounts, one incidental non-agricultural mention, and two product-query artifacts; none discloses grower own-use of AI livestreaming. Checks of API-exposed platform metadata for all 575 video records and cover images for 472 records found no platform-side AI label or visible AI/AIGC/statutory AI-generated notice. AI was announced primarily by accounts that sell, service, or discuss AI, rather than by produce-selling grower accounts. No grower own-use disclosure appears in either audited slice: 0 of 19 technical-keyword accounts and 0 of 455 transaction-query authors. The zero admits two readings that the audited surface cannot separate: smallholders do not use these tools, making the requirement inert for them, or they use them without disclosure. No label-reading instrument applied to the audited surface can decide between them, because such inspection observes announcement rather than use. Platforms and regulators may hold backend data unavailable to an external audit. If the theoretically derived authenticity-penalty mechanism holds, disclosure would impose an uneven cost, falling more heavily on growers than on intermediaries. The observed pattern is consistent with this hypothesis but does not establish it.

title: Comparative bioinformatic analysis of human and swine MHC sequences: implications for xenotransplantation
container-title: Frontiers in Immunology
aeef155a7f59ccef74197ee7c41e940d1bbc1f0b.abstract: Introduction Xenotransplantation using genetically engineered pig organs has advanced toward clinical evaluation, but immune-mediated rejection remains a major barrier to durable graft survival. Deletion of dominant carbohydrate xenoantigens has reduced hyperacute antibody-mediated injury, increasing the relative importance of residual protein antigens, including swine leukocyte antigens (SLA). Because SLA and human leukocyte antigen (HLA) molecules share major histocompatibility complex functions and structural features, defining their molecular relationships may help prioritize mechanisms of human humoral and cellular xenoreactivity. Methods We compared HLA and SLA using protein sequence alignment, an HLA-trained classifier combining five models, analysis of positions contributing to potential HLA antibody-recognition sites (eplets), and structural modeling. The sequence dataset included 452 SLA proteins; classifier analysis included 260 class I and 152 class II β-chain proteins. Results Sequence identity supported corresponding DRB1 and DQB1 relationships between species, while class I relationships differed across loci. Class I SLA classifier predictions favored HLA-B, and 97 of 99 SLA-DRB1 proteins showed their strongest classifier relationship to HLA-DRB1. Individual SLA assignments varied across models. Among covered residues, mismatch was greater at HLA eplet-associated positions than elsewhere: 41.0% versus 21.8% in class I and 27.7% versus 16.3% in class II. This pattern depended on sequence coverage, particularly in class II, where counting gaps as mismatches reversed the comparison. Structural overlays showed conserved MHC-domain folds with local substitutions at HLA eplet-associated positions. Discussion Together, the sequence, classifier, eplet-position, and structural comparisons identify molecular relationships and candidate sites for investigating HLA/SLA cross-reactivity. These findings provide a basis for antibody-binding, peptide-presentation, and cellular studies to refine xenotransplant compatibility assessment.

title: A Deepfake Detection Framework for Securing Facial Biometrics Using Attention-Based Deep Learning and Blockchain
container-title: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
a0074b87d1d6c79dcfbe609a01fe5bc5a247f1d2.abstract: Facial biometric authentication is widely deployed for identity verification, yet it is increasingly exposed to deepfakebased presentation and injection attacks and to large-scale breaches of centrally stored biometric templates. This paper proposes a deepfake-resilient facial biometric security framework that combines attention-based deep learning with blockchain technology. At registration, face images are pre-processed, augmented with a generative adversarial network (GAN), encoded by a convolutional neural network (CNN) with self-attention, and classified as real or fake by an artificial neural network (ANN). Only images classified as real are encrypted, bound to a unique user identifier and committed to a private blockchain through a cryptographic hash, whereas fake attempts are written to an immutable event log. At authentication, a fresh probe passes through the same pipeline and is verified by smart contracts that check the integrity of the registered commitment and the template similarity using zero-knowledge proofs (ZKPs), so that raw biometric features are never disclosed. We formalise the threat model, specify the architecture, the smart-contract interface and the security properties, and define an evaluation protocol based on the CIPLAB Real and Fake Face Detection and UTKFace datasets that covers detection accuracy, authentication error rates, adversarial robustness, demographic fairness and system overhead. The framework provides a basis for privacy-preserving, auditable and scalable facial authentication in digital identity management, financial services, healthcare and e-governance.

title: Oral Utidelone Capsule, a First-in-Class Solid Microtubule Stabilizer, in Advanced Breast Cancer: A First-in-Human Phase I-II Trial
07c2ffcdd4ee5970844c1c0ba3b07ab42946f87b.abstract: Abstract Purpose: Chemotherapy options for advanced breast cancer (ABC), which are usually given intravenously, may have suboptimal tolerability and convenience for long‑term disease management. This first-in-human phase I-II study evaluated the efficacy, safety and pharmacokinetic (PK) profile of utidelone capsule (UTD2), the first oral solid microtubule stabilizer and an oral formulation of the approved microtubule inhibitor utidelone injection (UTD1), as monotherapy and in combination with capecitabine in ABC. Patients and Methods: This multicenter trial (NCT05700084) had three parts. In Part 1, dose-escalation of UTD2 in patients with advanced solid tumors was done to establish the maximum tolerated dose (MTD). Part 2 used a crossover design to compare PK profiles of UTD2 and UTD1 in patients with advanced solid tumors. In Part 3 patients with ABC received UTD2 plus capecitabine. Primary endpoints included the MTD of UTD2 and the objective response rate (ORR) of UTD2 plus capecitabine. Secondary endpoints included PK parameters, progression-free survival (PFS), disease control rate (DCR), and safety. Results: Between August 30, 2023 and May 9, 2025, 82 patients were enrolled. All 10 evaluable patients who received UTD2 monotherapy had ABC; the confirmed ORR was 20.0% and DCR was 70.0%. In the 44 evaluable patients treated with all-oral UTD2 plus capecitabine, the confirmed ORR was 52.3% (95% CI, 36.767.5), median PFS was 8.3 months (95% CI, 5.410.6) and DCR was 88.6% (95% CI, 75.496.2). No dose-limiting toxicities were observed. The absolute oral bioavailability of UTD2 was 31.8%. Grade ≥3 neutropenia occurred in 12% of patients and grade ≥3 peripheral neuropathy in 2%. Conclusion: UTD2 showed promising antitumor efficacy and was well-tolerated. UTD2 plus capecitabine provided clinical benefit in patients with ABC, offering an alternative to intravenous formulations of microtubule stabilizer.

title: Human-Governed Multi-Agent AI for Biological Hypothesis Generation: An Evidence-Grounded Framework Using JUMP Cell Painting Profiles
7a2bcb64973bd56bae183bb619c26a0d3a9a5a47.abstract: Abstract High-dimensional cellular phenotypes can motivate biological hypotheses, but similarity alone cannot establish mechanism or causal validity. DISCOVERY-AGENT links exploratory JUMP Cell Painting evidence with evidence-grounded hypothesis generation, independent critique and bounded human-review routing. An initial 65-record CRISPR/ORF analysis across nine gene–modality tests found four FDR-significant CRISPR plate-level associations (AKT1, BRCA1, MTOR and TP53), none among evaluated ORF genes. A distinct later cross-source compound-identity benchmark used 614 morphological features and achieved AUROC 0.6142 on 1,250 held-out compounds with training-only preprocessing; this is identity discrimination, not mechanism-of-action classification. Three structured hypotheses underwent LLM critique and revision, while eleven gene-pair evidence assessments yielded no FDR-significant mechanistic finding (minimum q = 0.2037). Archived governance checks passed 1,021/1,021 predefined tests; nevertheless, the initial live-agent run contained two execution errors among five cases, with both cases responding on fresh retest. These findings demonstrate feasibility of auditable evidence processing and modest cross-source morphology signal, not validated autonomous discovery, prospective safety, or completed expert review. The work delineates practical requirements for independent biological validation and reproducible scientific agents.
