title: An attention-enhanced CNN-BiLSTM framework with confidence-gated inference for arrhythmia detection using ECG signals
container-title: Discover Computing
44feadb188256eccd1812c299d06ca2b1bdc38f0.abstract: Abstract Automated arrhythmia detection from electrocardiogram (ECG) signals is essential for early diagnosis and continuous cardiac monitoring. However, accurate classification remains challenging due to complex temporal dependencies in ECG waveforms and severe class imbalance, where clinically significant arrhythmias are underrepresented. To address these challenges, we propose an Attention-Enhanced CNN–BiLSTM framework with a Confidence-Gated Inference mechanism for ECG-based arrhythmia detection. The proposed model integrates a one-dimensional convolutional neural network (1D-CNN) to capture local morphological features with a Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (BiLSTM) network to model long-range temporal dependencies in ECG signals. A temporal attention mechanism is employed to focus on diagnostically relevant segments of the signal. Additionally, a confidence-gated inference strategy is introduced to improve prediction reliability, particularly for minority classes. An extensive ablation study across 18 configurations is conducted to evaluate the contribution of temporal modeling, attention, and inference strategies. On the MIT-BIH Arrhythmia Database, the proposed model achieves an accuracy of 96.58% and a macro-F1 score of 86.05%. To ensure an unbiased evaluation free of test-set leakage, we further adopt a strict protocol in which all hyperparameters ( $$\gamma$$ , $$\tau$$ ) are selected exclusively on a held-out validation set; under this leakage-free protocol the model attains an accuracy of 96.74% and a macro-F1 score of 86.54% on the untouched test set. These findings demonstrate that integrating attention-driven temporal modeling with calibrated inference yields efficient arrhythmia classification on the MIT-BIH benchmark.

title: Design, Synthesis, and In Vitro Evaluation of Novel Saccharin Derivatives for Anticancer Activity Against Neuroblastoma (SH-SY5Y Cell Line) Through Targeting Anaplastic Lymphoma Kinase (ALK).
container-title: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
10e812625cd46cfd378585ea5b7e049bb15e60df.abstract: The study was designed, synthesised, characterized, and evaluated by using MTT Assay as a potential anticancer agent, new Saccharin-7-Sulphonamide derivatives will be tested on human Neuroblastoma SY5Y cancer cell lines. These are potential anticancer agents that target the Anaplastic Lymphoma Kinase receptor. As part of the computational design process, a variety of software tools were used to generate the structural models for the synthesized compounds, including Chemsketch, Swiss ADME, Molinspiration, OSIRIS property explorer, and PyRx. According to Lipinski rule predictions made using Swiss ADME, the properties of the Lipinski rule are not violated. As part of the assessment of the effectiveness of the synthesized compounds as anticancer agents, molecular docking studies were conducted with ALK, which demonstrated promising binding affinities between the synthesized compounds and ALK molecules. There was a determination and characterization of the percentage yield, molecular formula, solubility, melting point, appearance, and molecular formula of the compounds that were investigated. In order to confirm the purity, TLC was used and Rf values were calculated to determine the purity. It was further characterized by IR, NMR, and Mass spectroscopy in order to determine the nature of the compound. It has been demonstrated that all synthesized compounds exhibit anti-cancer activities, and at concentrations of 20, 40, and 50g/mol, SA2 exhibits significant efficacy against Neuroblastoma SY5Y cancer cell line. This study showed that CompoundSA2 exhibited the most potent activity with an IC50 value of 5.253±1.761 µ/mol, whereas SA 1, 3, 4, and 5 exhibited moderate activities with IC50 values ranging from 1 to 40µg/ml. This study suggests that synthesized Saacharin with Sulphanilamide derivatives, especially SA2, may prove to be promising candidates for further development as anticancer agents that target Neuroblastoma ALK receptors and are promising candidates for further development. Aim: To develop the novel and potent anti-cancer agents against neuroblastoma [SY5Y-cell line] Objective: To design molecules, synthesize, characterize and determine anti-cancer activity,acute toxicity and cytotoxicity.

title: Nutritional content of the African horned cucumber (Cucumis metuliferus E. May. Ex Naudin) fruit grown under varying fertiliser types and growing environments, and its potential role in human nutrition
container-title: Frontiers in Plant Science
6ea833bedc99a74ebb11f13aebcb76f13edb3ccf.abstract: The fruit sector is one of the key role players in food and nutritional security by supplying vital nutrients, increasing food availability, promoting dietary diversity, and contributing to economic stability. Currently, most fruit species that contribute to food and nutritional supply in the fruit industry are exotic varieties such as mangoes, oranges, grapes, and English cucumbers, owing to the established and reputable literature on their agronomic practices and protocols. To achieve food and nutritional security globally, the introduction of indigenous fruit crops, especially in regions where they are native, appear to be a promising strategy that could accelerate the attainment of Sustainable Development Goal 2 (Zero Hunger). Additionally, this inclusion may assist in complementing existing commercial crops to substantially boost communal nutrition and food diversity by offering phytochemicals, nutrients, and minerals, which are vital for sustained health and wellness. Among such crops is the African horned cucumber ( Cucumis metuliferus E. May. Ex Naudin), an indigenous fruit crop of Southern Africa claimed to be nutrient dense due to its abundance of vitamins and minerals, which human beings require in smaller and larger quantities daily. However, literature on the fruit’s biochemical content response when subjected to differing growing environments and the use of specific fertiliser types appears to be scanty. Therefore, the current study evaluated the impact of differing growing environments (greenhouse and shade net) and fertiliser types (organic and inorganic/chemical) on the biochemical constituents of African horned cucumber fruit. In addition, the fruit nutritional content was compared with the average recommended daily intake to determine its potential contribution to human health and nutrition. The results showed that a treatment combination of shade net and chemical fertilisers increased phosphorus (577.7 mg/100g DW) and potassium (1074 mg/100g DW) compared to other treatments. As a result, growers are encouraged to consider the greenhouse environment combined with chemical fertilisers for maximising phytochemicals such as total phenols and vitamin C, whereas the treatment combination of shade net and chemical fertiliser appeared to be the best for maximising minerals such as calcium, phosphorus, and iron.

title: From generation to judgment: the multidimensional structure of design thinking mindset and differences across learning stages in AIGC-supported fashion film design learning
container-title: Frontiers in Psychology
e6e79bc6cb105e45a63939887b04adcfcbb9b1ae.abstract: Introduction Artificial intelligence-generated content (AIGC) is changing how design alternatives are generated in fashion film design learning, enabling students to obtain large numbers of comparable and iteratively refinable visual outcomes within a short period. However, expanded generative capacity does not, by itself, determine how learners interpret, evaluate, experiment with, and select among uncertain outcomes. In this human–AI collaborative creative environment, empirical evidence remains limited on whether learners’ design-related psychological tendencies form a distinguishable multidimensional structure that is comparable across learning stages. Design Thinking Mindset (DTM) provides a multidimensional psychological framework for addressing this issue. Methods Drawing on Vignoli et al.’s DTM framework, this study examined five dimensions—Uncertainty and Risk, Empathy, Experimentation, Abductive Reasoning, and Creative Confidence—through a cross-sectional survey of 409 first-year and third-year students from three Chinese universities who had experience with AIGC fashion film design projects. Confirmatory factor analysis and measurement invariance testing across year groups were used to examine the five-dimensional structure and its measurement comparability, followed by latent mean comparisons. Results The five DTM dimensions formed a correlated yet distinguishable structure and demonstrated measurement comparability across year groups. Third-year students had significantly higher latent means on all five dimensions, with the largest descriptive standardized difference point estimates observed for Abductive Reasoning and Creative Confidence. Discussion These findings provide empirical support for the applicability of five selected DTM dimensions in AIGC-supported fashion film design learning and reveal distinct patterns of self-reported psychological tendencies across year groups. From an educational perspective, the results suggest that AIGC-supported design education should attend not only to the generation of creative alternatives but also to learners’ psychological orientations toward uncertainty, experimentation, audience understanding, creative reasoning, and confidence in creative work.

title: From biomechanical data to robotic execution: design and control of an intelligent Tuina system
container-title: Frontiers in Neurorobotics
d7a149825eb3d91eafa240f098cf5be8680c1a28.abstract: Introduction Traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) Tuina (massage) relies heavily on practitioners' physical stamina and subjective experience, leading to operational variability that hinders therapeutic standardization and scalable rehabilitation service delivery. To address this limitation, this study proposes an intelligent TCM Tuina robotic system integrating biomechanical data-driven design and hybrid control strategies. Methods A 6-DOF manipulator equipped with a biomimetic end-effector is developed, and a CMPGA-Corr neural network (Convolutional Multi-branch Prototype-Guided Architecture with a Channel-Correlation Branch) is constructed to decouple the spatiotemporal features of nine Tuina manipulations from 25-channel tactile data. Robotic execution is implemented within a Robot Operating System 2 (ROS 2)-based control framework. The framework combines RRT-Connect path planning, S-curve speed profiling, and RBF-compensated admittance control. PID, conventional Admittance, and RBF controllers were compared in complete-process simulations using five repetitions per manipulation. Results The RBF controller produced the lowest mean RMSE and MAE for all six evaluated manipulations. Physical experiments on a silicone back phantom further demonstrated bounded and repeatable force-tracking behavior under the tested conditions. Discussion The proposed framework bridges TCM practice with modern robotic engineering and provides a scalable and standardized solution for precision rehabilitation robotics.

title: Teachers’ attitudes and behavioural intentions towards AI integration in Chinese higher education: a qualitative interview study
container-title: Frontiers in Psychology
c6fe4330bbf5fd4fe3ac0771cb768c511236b747.abstract: Introduction The rapid expansion of generative AI has intensified scholarly and policy debate over its role in higher education, yet university teachers’ attitudes towards its integration remain complex and context-dependent. This study explores how university teachers perceive, experience, and respond to AI integration in their teaching. Guided primarily by the three-component attitude model and informed by the technology acceptance model and the theory of planned behaviour, the study examines cognitive appraisals, affective responses, behavioural intentions, and perceived support needs. Methods The study draws on semi-structured interviews with 14 university teachers from four higher education institutions in China. The interview data were analysed using codebook-informed thematic analysis combining deductive and inductive coding. Results The findings indicate that teachers generally perceive AI as a supportive rather than substitutive educational tool, valuing it for improving efficiency, supporting lesson preparation, and enriching pedagogical design. Emotional responses varied from enthusiasm and a sense of accomplishment to caution, neutrality, and, in some cases, declining satisfaction. Across the interviews, teachers’ primary concerns centred less on their own replacement than on the perceived risks of inappropriate AI use for students’ independent thinking, reasoning, originality, and authentic understanding. Teachers’ intentions to adopt AI were therefore conditional and bounded, shaped by pedagogical purpose, disciplinary context, student readiness, and the need to maintain teacher control. Teachers also emphasised that sustainable AI integration requires more than general encouragement, calling instead for AI literacy development, discipline-sensitive support, specialised tools, and enabling institutional infrastructure. Discussion Overall, these findings extend contextual understandings of teachers’ AI acceptance by showing how adoption intentions are pedagogically negotiated and highlight the importance of supporting professional judgement and students’ independent thinking in higher education.

title: Automated assessment of healthcare de-escalation communication skills in a conversational AI virtual reality simulation
container-title: Frontiers in Digital Health
9bc424b8b0ee6bc350b4296b68f692e3f29c8284.abstract: Introduction Digital health training environments increasingly require scalable methods for assessing communication skills in realistic, interactive scenarios. This paper presents a comparative study of automated assessment approaches within a conversational AI virtual reality simulation designed for verbal de-escalation training. Methods A total of 20 nursing students completed the simulation, where their spoken responses were captured and converted to text through a speech-to-text system, and were evaluated across 11 de-escalation competencies. The evaluation compared three fine-tuned deep learning models (BERT, RoBERTa, and XLNet) with a modified RATAS, a rubric-driven framework that leverages large language models. Two experiments were conducted: one using controlled 100-item validation datasets for each section, and another using the real-world responses collected during the user study. Results On the validation datasets, the deep learning models achieved the highest performance, with RoBERTa obtaining an average accuracy of 0.9927, followed by BERT at 0.9900 and XLNet at 0.9790, while RATAS achieved 0.8554. On the student-response dataset, performance decreased for all approaches, with RoBERTa obtaining 0.8590 accuracy, RATAS 0.8181, BERT 0.8000, and XLNet 0.7681. Discussion These results suggest that transformer-based models perform best under controlled conditions, whereas RATAS demonstrated stability in grading across different dataset types. These preliminary findings support the feasibility of integrating deep learning and rubric-driven LLM-based automated assessment approaches for communication and de-escalation training in nursing education.

title: Uneven automation: comparing authorship anxiety and generative AI use among art and design undergraduate students
container-title: Frontiers in Psychology
8942b2ac014d5d2bac7e05011f209f96a5fce870.abstract: Art and design education expects students to develop a sense of authorship over original work, but generative AI (GenAI) complicates how students understand and claim that authorship. This study examined whether these experiences differ across creative fields through a mixed-methods design. The survey included 2,441 GenAI-using students from seven field categories at 33 art and design institutions in China and assessed authorship anxiety, creative agency, perceived usefulness, dependence on GenAI, and frequency of use. The quantitative analysis first examined variation across all seven categories and then compared fine art with the five applied design fields. Interview data from 22 survey participants were also examined thematically. The main findings include that (1) authorship anxiety did not differ significantly across the seven categories or between fine art and pooled design; the latter comparison met the equivalence criterion at ±d = 0.20, but not at tighter bounds; (2) clearer differences emerged in how students used GenAI. Compared with fine-art students, design students considered GenAI more useful and used it more frequently; (3) across the interviews, most students described authorship as retaining control over the creative idea while delegating parts of its execution to GenAI. Specifically, fine-art students often grounded authorship in embodied making and human imperfection, whereas design students placed greater emphasis on judgement, selection, and control. We call this pattern uneven automation: concern about authorship was broadly shared, but students in different fields responded to GenAI in different ways, potentially reflecting the varying labour-market pressures surrounding their disciplines.

title: Digital transformation, traceability, and supply chain resilience in food manufacturing SMEs: a review of AI, blockchain-IoT, and institutional mechanisms
container-title: Frontiers in Sustainable Food Systems
c0821ee379eb16d2e0252633d6030dd152fbd833.abstract: Food supply chains in China face persistent challenges of food safety risks, inadequate transparency, and supply disruptions, with food manufacturing small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) disproportionately vulnerable due to limited resources and non-standardized internal processes. Digital transformation encompassing artificial intelligence (AI), blockchain, Internet of Things (IoT), and digital twin technologies is increasingly regarded as a strategic solution to strengthen supply chain resilience, yet the organizational and institutional conditions under which these digital investments translate into tangible resilience improvements for food manufacturing SMEs remain poorly understood. This review conducts a PRISMA 2020-compliant systematic review and thematic synthesis of 40 multidisciplinary sources spanning the food safety, supply chain management, and information systems literatures. Drawing on Dynamic Capabilities Theory and Institutional Theory, we propose an integrative conceptual framework comprising six research propositions, in which traceability capability acts as a food-safety-specific mediating mechanism linking digital transformation to supply chain resilience, while regulatory stringency moderates the strength of this indirect pathway. A central argument of this framework is that deploying blockchain, IoT, or AI hardware does not itself constitute traceability capability the institutional and organisational conditions under which digital tools are adopted determine whether firms build substantive traceability capability or engage in symbolic compliance without genuine food safety governance improvement. Three key contributions distinguish this framework: conceptualizing traceability capability as a distinct dynamic capability rather than a generic digitalization mechanism; directing analytical focus explicitly toward food manufacturing SMEs, a population largely overlooked in existing large-firm panel studies; and introducing regulatory stringency as a first-stage moderator within a moderated mediation structure. Critical research gaps are identified, including the absence of SME-calibrated digital transformation measurement instruments, the lack of a validated multi-item traceability capability scale, and a complete empirical vacuum for testing the proposed moderated mediation model in food manufacturing SME contexts. This review provides a structured future research agenda for scholars and delivers actionable insights for practitioners and policymakers seeking to direct digital technology investments toward improved food safety governance in China’s food manufacturing sector.

title: Human-in-the-loop semantic learning analytics for assessing moral-value reasoning in university AI ethics education
container-title: Frontiers in Psychology
4c153cd19693204269d4536c8e62024e2ea30575.abstract: Introduction University AI ethics education addresses fairness, privacy, accountability, transparency, human autonomy, and academic integrity, but the semantic structure of students' moral-value reasoning and its connection to responsible solutions remain insufficiently characterized. This study examined a human-in-the-loop semantic learning analytics framework for task-specific moral-value reasoning. Methods Ninety science and engineering graduate students completed an online explicit-reflective AI ethics module in a one-group pre–post multimethod study without a control group. Assessments comprised an AI ethics knowledge test, a perceived-awareness scale, and open-ended ethical reasoning tasks. Expert annotations informed transformer-based multi-label coding, descriptive value coverage and balance metrics, problem–solution coupling, and baseline-only nested cross-validated prediction of subsequent raw problem-solving change. Results Within-participant pre–post increases were observed in ethical knowledge, perceived moral-value awareness, actual ethical awareness, problem–solving skills, value coverage, value balance, and problem–solution coupling. Automated semantic coding achieved participant-grouped cross-validated macro-F1 = 0.83 (95% CI [0.78, 0.87]; micro-F1 = 0.86; macro-AUPRC = 0.82). The baseline-only prediction model yielded cross-validated R 2 = 0.30 (95% CI [0.11, 0.45]) for subsequent raw problem-solving change. Discussion Expert-supervised semantic analytics can characterize value representation and issue–solution reasoning in AI ethics assessments. Coverage and balance describe response structure rather than moral quality. The absence of a control group, repeated use of one scenario, and modest sample size preclude causal and broad trait-level conclusions.

title: Deciphering natural alkaline water-induced human molecular homeostatic regulation via non-invasive sweat metabolic profiling
container-title: Frontiers in Bioengineering and Biotechnology
fd3e3562b80aa5aeb05a0d20f6412c0ba0f64eb1.abstract: Natural alkaline water, a weakly alkaline NaHCO 3 ‐enriched solution, has been postulated to modulate systemic metabolic homeostasis, but its clinical metabolic effects remain poorly characterized due to the scarcity of non-invasive, longitudinal molecular evidence. Conventional flexible microneedles for sweat analysis are limited to single‐analyte detection, failing to meet the need for simultaneous profiling of multiple biomarkers required to assess systemic homeostasis. To address these challenges, we engineered a hierarchical metal‐carbide (MXene)‐based flexible microneedle array integrated with high‐performance mass spectrometry, establishing a non‐invasive, high‐throughput sweat metabolic profiling platform. Here, we show that the hierarchical architecture, featuring a petal‐like AgNWs@MXene heterostructure, creates synergistic hotspots that enhance laser desorption/ionization mass spectrometry (LDI‐MS) signal intensity by more than twofold compared with pristine MXene, allowing robust detection of 77 ± 8 metabolic features from a single sweat‐patch sample. In a cohort study (n = 107), this platform enabled simultaneous dynamic monitoring of key metabolic features associated with uric acid, lactate, and glutamine (p &lt; 0.001). Overall, this work reveals the regulatory effects of natural alkaline water on metabolic homeostasis and provides a scalable, high‐throughput strategy for non‐invasive multi‐feature sweat metabolic profiling.

title: Mapping ASR systems onto the human auditory spectrum: speech-in-noise recognition of Arabic in normal-sighted, blind, and hearing-impaired listeners
container-title: Frontiers in Psychology
95824f3a37393ce3776ba774ed6592156bac795a.abstract: Background/objectives This study examines how human listeners and automatic speech recognition (ASR) systems process speech under varying background noise levels. Methods Three groups of human participants—normal-sighted (NSLs), blind (BLs), and hearing-impaired listeners (HILs)—were compared with two state-of-the-art ASR systems, Whisper and TurboScribe. Forty Arabic sentences (20 imperative, 20 interrogative) were presented at four signal-to-noise ratios (SNRs: +10, +5, −5, −10 dB) using passenger boarding noise to simulate realistic acoustic environments. Results Accuracy declined with increasing noise for all groups, although rates varied substantially. BLs performed best, maintaining 85% accuracy even at −10 dB SNR, whereas HILs showed the steepest decline. The ASR systems achieved near-human performance in moderate noise but degraded sharply under severe masking, mirroring HIL trends. Statistical analysis confirmed significant group differences across SNRs ( p &lt; 0.05). A linear mixed-effects analysis further revealed a significant advantage for interrogative over imperative sentences in human listeners ( p &lt; 0.05), plausibly attributable to the rich prosodic cues of question intonation, but no comparable benefit was observed for ASR systems ( p = 0.30), which appear to weight segmental over prosodic information. Conclusion These findings highlight that, although contemporary ASR models approach human performance in favorable conditions, they lack the adaptive mechanisms that allow humans—especially BLs—to sustain intelligibility in complex acoustic scenes. By situating ASR performance within the spectrum of human auditory variability, this research underscores both the progress and the limitations of machine hearing and points toward neurobiologically inspired strategies for achieving noise-robust speech recognition. Clinically, this framework suggests that benchmarking ASR systems against the full spectrum of human auditory variability—including hearing-impaired and blind listeners—can inform the design of accessibility tools, hearing-aid signal processing, and supplementary diagnostic measures of speech-in-noise perception in audiology practice.

title: Perceived AI literacy and TPACK in pre-service teacher education: mediating roles of perceived usefulness, ease of use, and value in blended learning
container-title: Frontiers in Psychology
1bad51d2ab1c081fcbf1788c8c81f98f9ce0044c.abstract: Background The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into blended learning requires pre-service teachers to develop AI-related competencies and the ability to integrate technology into pedagogy. This study examines how perceived AI literacy and technological pedagogical content knowledge (TPACK) are associated with deep learning through perceived usefulness, perceived ease of use, and perceived value of AI use. Methods A cross-sectional survey was completed by 423 pre-service teachers enrolled in blended learning courses at a university in China. Data were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM), with covariance-based structural equation modeling and fuzzy-set qualitative comparative analysis (fsQCA) used as complementary robustness and configurational analyses. Results Perceived usefulness, perceived ease of use, and perceived value of AI use significantly mediated the relationships between the two competencies and deep learning. All six indirect pathways were significant in both the PLS-SEM and covariance-based SEM analyses. The fsQCA revealed an equifinal and asymmetric structure: multiple, partly substitutable conditions were sufficient for high deep learning, and no single condition was necessary for either high or low deep learning. Conclusions The findings integrate the technology acceptance model and expectancy-value theory to explain how pre-service teachers' competencies and perceptions relate to deep learning in AI-enhanced blended environments. Teacher education should support technical competence alongside positive perceptions of AI's utility, usability, and value. Because the measures were self-reported and collected cross-sectionally at one university, the findings are interpreted as associational and configurational rather than causal.

title: Effectiveness of an AI-Based Educational Video Generator in Enhancing Oral Health Knowledge and Behavior Among Children: A Randomized Controlled Trial
container-title: Al-Rafidain Journal of Medical Sciences ( ISSN 2789-3219 )
025217a90eae33a9efbb4f3e4378042549e3202e.abstract: Background: Artificial intelligence (AI) is a new innovation that presents an opportunity for oral health education in children. Objective: To evaluate the effectiveness of an AI-assisted educational video versus standardized in-person oral health education for children regarding oral health knowledge and behaviors. Methods: This randomized controlled trial included 300 children aged 10-12 years (n=150 per group), both boys and girls, who were divided into AI video and standardized face-to-face oral health education groups. Baseline and 2-week follow-up evaluations were conducted for knowledge scores, four behavioral items, and the Silness and Löe Plaque Index. The internal consistency of the knowledge scale was checked (Cronbach's α=0.79). Wilcoxon signed-rank and Mann–Whitney U tests were the primary non-parametric tests used for statistical evaluations, with a median, (IQR), and effect size r provided. Chi-square tests with a Bonferroni adjustment at α=0.0125 were used to evaluate behavioral items. Results: There were significant enhancements in intra-group knowledge (p<0.0001 for both groups; r=0.663 for AI; r=0.345 for Control). The clinical efficacy was similar for both strategies with significant reduction of intra-group plaque (AI: p< 0.001, r= 0.425; Control: p< 0.001, r= 0.331), but no inter-group difference at the end of the intervention (p= 0.608; r= 0.030). In the conventional group, the utilization of dental floss was significantly improved (p=0.0056), and no other behaviors showed significant improvement across groups. Conclusions: The AI-assisted educational video demonstrated better knowledge retention than the standardized face-to-face oral health education, achieved similar clinical plaque reduction, and can be easily scaled for pediatric preventive dentistry.

title: Mudscapes as a method: Co-creating climate pedagogies through muddy play and more-than-human relations
container-title: Journal of Childhood, Education & Society
be846feff07d1b1faac25721ac52aaa4337b4566.abstract: Current Euro-Western, developmentalist early childhood education frameworks prioritize individual, future-oriented, and measurable outcomes, limiting the relational engagements necessary for effective climate pedagogy. In response, this paper introduces Mudscapes, a practice-based workshop designed to engage pre-service teachers and educators in embodied, sensory encounters with mud. Drawing on Lowenfeld’s World Technique and Common Worlds pedagogies, this inquiry conceptualizes small-world muddy play as "worlding" - an ongoing relational becoming with human and more-than-human entities. Methodologically, this paper adopts an a/r/tographic and autotheoretical approach to reflect on facilitator practice, spatial curation, and material agency rather than human-subject empirical evaluations. Findings from autoethnographic journaling and spatial curation logs demonstrate how intentionally designing for uncertainty disrupts desires for control, cleanliness, and predetermined learning outcomes. By framing improvisation and material friction as core pedagogical practices, Mudscapes illustrates how practice-based educator workshops can cultivate the capacities required to navigate shared worlds in an era of climate crisis.

title: Minor moments of more-than-human encounters: Rethinking climate change education in early childhood
container-title: Journal of Childhood, Education & Society
de77146d54d5fd5adf499a13bf084d20e2fcc05e.abstract: In the context of intensifying climate crises, early childhood education is increasingly positioned as a site for cultivating the capacities, sensitivities, and solidarities needed for more sustainable futures (Spiteri & Pace, 2023; UNESCO & MECCE, 2024). Yet dominant approaches to climate change education continue to privilege cognitive, anthropocentric, and developmental framings, emphasizing knowledge transmission and individual responsibility while overlooking children’s relational and ecological entanglements. This paper offers a critical re-imagining of climate education in the early years through posthuman and feminist new materialist perspectives (Barad, 2007; Haraway, 2016; Lenz Taguchi, 2010; Taylor & Pacini-Ketchabaw, 2019). Drawing on ethnographic research into minor moments—everyday encounters between children and more-than-human entities such as wind and trees—the paper argues that ecological knowledge and climate resilience are already emergent within children’s ordinary play worlds. These moments of curiosity, care, loss, and response-ability (Haraway, 2016) often remain unnoticed within human-centered developmental frameworks. By foregrounding practices of noticing (Tsing, 2015) and orientation (Ahmed, 2006), the paper attends to how educators’ ways of looking, turning toward, and responding shape what counts as climate learning. The paper explores how posthuman and feminist new materialist approaches to play open new pedagogical orientations for climate education, shifting attention from what children should learn about climate change to how they already live, sense, and negotiate ecological conditions. This approach frames climate education as an ongoing practice of attunement, care, and “staying with the trouble” (Haraway, 2016), grounded in shared vulnerability and situated, more-than-human relations.

title: Modern Approaches to Teaching Mathematics to Primary School Students in a Digital Learning Environment
container-title: The Journal of Interdisciplinary Human Studies
a96be798bb994247daa8f325fdb8751fbd140856.abstract: This article examines modern approaches to teaching mathematics to primary school students in a digital learning environment, focusing on interdisciplinary integration. The study uses theoretical analysis, comparative analysis, and generalization of pedagogical literature to explore how digital resources can support mathematics instruction. The analysis suggests that interactive exercises, electronic textbooks, visual materials, and educational software offer opportunities to explain mathematical concepts, support independent practice, and provide feedback. Connecting mathematics with language, natural sciences, technology, and everyday situations may help students apply mathematical knowledge in practical contexts. Effective implementation requires teachers to align digital resources with lesson objectives, students’ developmental characteristics, and available technical facilities. The article concludes that combining digital tools with integrated teaching offers pedagogical opportunities for primary mathematics education, while empirical research is needed to assess its effects on students’ learning outcomes.

title:
Hydrophilic Nanoisland
Interface Engineering for Conquering
Activity–Stability Trade-Off in High-Efficiency Salt Lake Lithium
Extraction
container-title:

c0c55146db9da3ad67145d22a1a8302fc0e22824.abstract: Abstract The adsorption-based lithium extraction technology from ultralow-grade salt lake brine is severely restricted by the inherent activity–stability trade-off of traditional granular Li/Al-LDHs adsorbents (GLDHs). Herein, a nanoisland encapsulation strategy integrated with hydrophilic interface engineering is developed to fabricate Li/Al-LDHs composite granules with tailored hydrophilic interfaces (HILDHs), breaking the long-standing bottleneck of conventional aluminum-based lithium adsorbents used in the salt lake industry. Systematic experiments and multiscale simulations reveal that the strong water affinity of polyacrylonitrile cyano groups (−C≡N) creates a highly hydrated microenvironment for rapid Li+ transport, while the nanoisland-confined structure anchors Li/Al-LDHs nanosheets to preserve the layered framework under harsh deep desorption conditions, thus enabling excellent cycling stability. The optimized HILDHs deliver a 3.02-fold higher working adsorption capacity (7.25 mg g–1 vs 2.40 mg g–1 for GLDHs) in actual Qarhan old brine within 60 min, along with a 13.36-fold increase in adsorption rate constant, 40% lower rinsing water consumption, and excellent cycle stability. It is calculated the nanoisland encapsulation strategy can achieve a nearly 5-fold increase for the annual Li2CO3 production capacity from salt lake lithium industrial lines.

title: Improving Learner Performance Through Score Based Analysis on a Gamified AI Driven Cybersecurity Learning Platform
d2b1981b0d01f6ee261a12a86c8c602586119c26.abstract: Abstract This study examines whether structured engagement with instructional content improves learner performance on Cyber Security Academy, an AI-driven, gamified cybersecurity learning platform. Activity logs covering 1,500 completed assessments from users in ten Anglophone and Francophone countries were analyzed by comparing learners who consulted the lessons and completed the full learning pathway (n = 900) with those who engaged only partially with the platform (n = 600). Group differences were tested with Welch's t-test, the Mann Whitney U test, one-way ANOVA, Spearman correlations, and Cohen's d as a measure of effect size. Learners who read the lessons before assessment obtained a mean score of 71.27 % versus 60.41 % for non-readers (Δ = +10.86 points; t(1192) = 12.21; p < 0.001; d = 0.650; 95 % CI [9.12, 12.60]), committed fewer errors (2.50 vs. 4.85; d = -1.069), and responded faster (9.85 vs. 12.69 minutes; d = -0.807), indicating greater fluency of cognitive processing. The effect decreased monotonically with age (d = 1.205 for learners aged 13 and under; d = 0.387 for those 22 and over) and with digital literacy (d = 1.434 for beginners; d = 0.524 for experts), while remaining positive in all ten countries. These findings indicate that structured, AI-personalized, and gamified learning environments substantially enhance cybersecurity learning outcomes, particularly for younger and less experienced users.

title: Design of a compact rotational compliant stage with self-compensation for rotation center offset
container-title: Mechanical Sciences
fa9b231cfbfa1c69919419c826b4c3662743d899.abstract: Compliant rotational stages are widely used for the fine angular positioning of optical components, where rotation center stability is critical to positioning accuracy. However, conventional designs often suffer from rotation center offset. A rotational compliant mechanism with self-compensation for rotation center offset is proposed based on a two-stage lever amplification system incorporating a non-vertical connecting beam and a double-ended fixed flexure hinge. The input force transmitted to the second-stage lever is decomposed into two orthogonal components. The y direction component drives the secondary lever to generate rotational motion, whereas the x direction component produces a negative x direction displacement through the double-ended fixed flexure hinge, thereby compensating for the rotation center offset. A kinematic analysis and a compliance model are established, based on which multi-objective dimensional optimization is performed to balance the rotational output and the center-offset indicator. The optimized design is subsequently evaluated using COMSOL finite element simulations. Under a prescribed relative input displacement of 28 µm, the mechanism produces an output rotation of 3.12 mrad, with a first natural frequency of 572 Hz and a maximum center offset of 0.42 µm. The stage has overall dimensions of 51 mm × 78 mm. These numerical results indicate that the proposed configuration can reduce rotation center offset and parasitic translational coupling under the adopted idealized simulation conditions.

title: AI Labour Rights Awareness and Career Adaptation Confidence among Respondents in Bangladesh
4bebd9cda335afcb1b14dbb90e41e4c4857a6c33.abstract: Abstract Artificial intelligence changes both the skills used at work and the conditions under which employment decisions are made. Awareness of these changes does not necessarily coincide with confidence in adapting a career. This study examines that distinction in 385 adult, AI-aware survey records from Bangladesh, including 238 law students and 61 respondents classified as law graduates. Five statements separately assess awareness of workplace rights and responsibilities, recognition of protection from unfair automated decisions, reported complementary skill development, adaptation confidence and the perceived preparedness benefit of understanding labour issues. Analyses combine full response distributions, joint endorsement patterns, paired comparisons, ordinal correlations and an exploratory proportional-odds model. Recognition of the need for protection was endorsed by 79.2%, compared with 48.8% endorsing adaptation confidence, a paired difference of 30.4 percentage points (95% bootstrap interval 23.9–36.6). General rights awareness and skill development had small positive ordinal associations with confidence. In the adjusted ordinal model, their odds ratios were 1.30 (95% interval 1.04–1.61; Holm p = 0.038) and 1.40 (1.09–1.79; Holm p = 0.024) respectively. The protection-recognition estimate was less certain, although the two awareness coefficients were not demonstrably different. The findings distinguish rights recognition, reported action and confidence rather than establish a causal awareness-to-adaptability pathway. They support evaluating legal-literacy education alongside practical career tasks and institutional safeguards. The mixed sample, study-specific single items, undocumented recruitment and fieldwork dates, and source-documentation limitations constrain inference. A subsequent study should use verified graduate eligibility, independent legal-knowledge assessments and longitudinal career outcomes.

title: Metabolic regulation of oocyte developmental competence: cellular cooperation, developmental transitions, and human evidence
container-title: Frontiers in Cell and Developmental Biology
9e9f05703b4b08c0bc781f4efa32f02f1e12e0b9.abstract: Oocyte metabolism supports meiotic maturation and prepares the cytoplasm for fertilization and early cleavage. These functions depend on the exchange of substrates with cumulus cells, mitochondrial activity and organization, redox balance, and the use of metabolites in biosynthesis and chromatin regulation. This narrative review examines how these processes contribute to developmental competence, drawing on mammalian perturbation studies and human oocyte, cumulus-cell, follicular-fluid and embryo studies. Animal experiments show that disturbed substrate use or organelle organization can impair development despite meiotic progression or little change in total adenosine triphosphate (ATP) content. They also reveal dose- and stage-dependent responses to metabolic supplementation. Human studies identify related molecular and optical changes, particularly during reproductive aging, but the biological meaning of a measurement depends on the sampled cell, developmental stage and experimental conditions. Direct oocyte profiling, associated follicular samples and embryo measurements therefore address different questions. The Goldilocks concept helps frame the possibility that both insufficient activity and excessive demand can accompany developmental failure; it does not establish a common metabolic threshold for clinical selection. We discuss metabolic interventions as tests of mechanism and distinguish developmental rescue in experimental systems from benefit in vitro fertilization. The central challenge is to determine which metabolic changes contribute to loss of competence and which arise as responses to aging, culture or developmental arrest.

title: Spectrally efficient SCM-QPSK optical system: design and performance evaluation over long-haul fiber
container-title: Optical Engineering
f80c60f140824134e6ebba00dc9298db7962fbcd.abstract: The evolution toward 6G networks demands unprecedented data rates, spectral efficiency, and energy efficiency, motivating the integration of wireless and optical communication technologies to exploit the complementary advantages of both domains. Recently, subcarrier multiplexing (SCM) has received great attention because it allows sending multiple data streams over a single optical carrier. However, SCM is susceptible to impairments such as chromatic dispersion, nonlinearities, and accumulation of amplified spontaneous emission (ASE) noise in the amplifiers that adversely affect the performance of the SCM optical link. To address the need for spectrally efficient optical transmission, we numerically investigate a four-subcarrier system using quadrature phase shift keying (QPSK) over a 400-km multi-span optical fiber link. The four subcarriers are symmetrically positioned at ±5.5 and ±16.5 GHz and shaped using root-raised cosine filtering. The transmission link is modeled using the symmetric split-step Fourier method, including chromatic dispersion, Kerr nonlinearity, fiber attenuation, and ASE noise introduced after each 80-km erbium-doped fiber amplifier span. The individual subcarriers are recovered independently and evaluated using bit error rate (BER), error vector magnitude, signal-to-noise ratio, constellation diagrams, and eye diagrams. The results provide a numerical characterization of the impairment-induced degradation experienced by the individual SCM subcarriers after long-haul propagation. At the selected 400-km and 0-dBm operating point, substantial degradation is observed across all four subcarriers, with comparable performance among the symmetric subcarriers. A separate Additive White Gaussian Noise validation confirms the correct implementation of the QPSK modulation, demodulation, and BER calculation. The study provides a baseline for understanding subcarrier-level impairment behavior. However, nonlinear impairment mitigation is outside the scope of the present work.

title: The Concept of Biomimicry in the Form Determination Phase of Architectural Facade Design

06008fea714f593b1dfcc250b07cd22d229402a9.abstract: Throughout the history of architecture, nature has served as both a source of inspiration and a structural reference for designers. This reference has now entered the literature under the headings of biomimicry and biomimetic design, transforming into a systematic design methodology. Biomimicry is an approach that offers different opportunities in the design of facades, an architectural component. This study examines biomimicry in the form-determining process of architectural facade design through application examples and design methodologies. By investigating the inclusion of biomimicry in the form-determining phase of the conventional facade design process, the study addresses the question, "At what point does the biomimicry approach fit into the form-determining phase of architectural facade design?" The study concludes that biomimicry should be integrated into architectural practice not only as a formal aesthetic preference but also as a form-determining tool that optimizes parameters such as climate control, daylight management, energy efficiency, and user comfort.

title: Campus-City Interface: Key Components in the Integration of University Campuses with Urban Space
container-title: Research into the Built Environment in Architectural Sciences
9835a91ff60e2e86b0eadeb2a14f48019e1d1a39.abstract: University campuses are urban focal points that, beyond their educational functions, establish physical, functional, social, and environmental relationships with the city. This study examines the relationship between Recep Tayyip Erdoğan University’s Zihni Derin Campus and the city of Rize through these four dimensions of integration. The research evaluates campus boundaries, entrances, pedestrian and vehicular connections, surrounding urban functions, open and green spaces, the relationship with the coastline, topography, and user interactions. The findings indicate that the campus connects at various levels with the transportation network and with residential, commercial, healthcare, cultural, and recreational functions; however, transportation arteries, topography, and a fragmented open-space system limit physical and environmental continuity. Regarding social integration, the campus exhibits a multi-centered structure centered around the central square, sports and recreation areas, the cultural center, and shared-use spaces. The study concludes that campus-city integration should be addressed through uninterrupted, permeable, and mutually supportive spatial connections.

title: Regulating AI-Generated Inventions in Tanzania: A Comparative Analysis of BRELA and South Africa’s CIPC
container-title: East African Journal of Law and Ethics
97d91fe2e65b9b432b752d3e2552b57b2f5ca94f.abstract: Artificial intelligence systems now produce technical solutions with little or no human contribution to the inventive step, and the DABUS applications filed by Dr Stephen Thaler have tested whether patent law can accommodate an inventor that is not a person. Courts and offices in the United Kingdom, the United States, Europe, Australia and Germany have refused, while South Africa’s Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC) published the grant of a patent naming DABUS as inventor in July 2021. This article asks whether Tanzania’s Business Registrations and Licensing Agency (BRELA) could follow that example under the Patents (Registration) Act, Cap 217, and, if not, what reform is required. Using doctrinal analysis and functional comparison, it finds that the two statutes are closer than is usually assumed: neither defines ‘inventor’, and both require an applicant who is not the inventor to show a right derived from the inventor. The decisive difference is administrative. The South African grant followed a formalities-only check in which, on the published record, the applicant’s entitlement was not tested, leaving validity to revocation proceedings. Section 25(7) and (8) of Cap 217, by contrast, require the Registrar to examine every request for compliance with section 18(3) and (4) and to reject one that is not corrected. An application naming DABUS would therefore fail at the formal stage, and one naming a human who did not devise the invention would be open to invalidation under section 64(2)(d). BRELA cannot reproduce the CIPC outcome by discretion. The article recommends, in order of priority, statements of practice on AI-assisted inventions, revised forms, a statutory definition of inventor and, after regional consultation through ARIPO and the East African Community, a deliberate legislative choice on whether AI-generated inventions should be protected.

title:
Human Urine–Derived
Induced Pluripotent Stem
Cell Membranes Enable Personalized Transdermal Nanotherapy for Melanoma
container-title: ACS Nano
16aae0ac51e8ade33375b46694b03cde5a18d49d.abstract: Abstract Melanoma treatment remains limited by drug resistance, immune-related adverse effects, and inadequate tumor-specific drug delivery. Nanoparticle (NP)-based delivery platforms have shown promise, but their clinical translation is hindered by rapid immune clearance and suboptimal biocompatibility. Current membrane-coating strategies often depend on invasive cell sources and lack patient-specific applicability. This study introduces a personalized melanoma therapy platform that integrates MnO2 NPs (MNPs) coated with urine-derived induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC) membranes into a hydrogel-based transdermal patch. The patient-derived iPSC membrane enhances tumor targeting and immune evasion through the CXCR4/CXCL12 axis, while the MNPs facilitate pH-responsive release of cytotoxic drugs within the tumor microenvironment, maximizing therapeutic efficacy. The hydrogel transdermal patch enables direct, noninvasive delivery to skin lesions, promoting sustained drug exposure and potentially improving patient compliance. By combining autologous cell membrane coating, pH-responsive nanocarriers, and transdermal administration, this platform addresses key limitations of current melanoma therapies and supports the potential for clinical translation of personalized nanomedicine.

title: Noise in the process: Assessing the evidential value of mediation analyses in marketing and consumer psychology journals
9cd70974b7ad590ad3102271c770ce329a4b6146.abstract: Mediation analysis plays a central role in marketing research and consumer psychology by modeling the complex processes underlying total effects. Like other inferential methods, tests of indirect effects are susceptible to false-positive results when multiple defensible analytic decisions can lead to different conclusions (i.e. researcher degrees of freedom). To assess the collective evidential value of mediation analyses in marketing, we (1) measure the relative proximity (RP) of confidence intervals to zero and (2) aggregate a related set of RP scores into a single distribution. Study 1 demonstrates how researcher degrees of freedom in mediation analysis, such as trying many different mediators and outcomes or testing moderated mediation, can inflate false-positive rates to up to 20% in the scenarios we examined. This study also demonstrates the validity of the RP index by examining its correspondence with false-positive findings. In Study 2, we compare the RP distribution of mediation analyses published in top marketing journals (2018-2020) to simulations of null effects, low power, and adequate power. We find that mediation analyses in marketing substantially deviated from simulations with adequate power but were similar to simulated distributions with low power and null effects. We propose study preregistration, increased statistical power, and reduction of selection bias as solutions to increase evidential value of mediation analyses going forward.

title: Tecnología de la información para la atención de urgencias y emergencias: Revisión integrativa.
Information technology for urgent and emergency care: Integrative review
Tecnologia de informação para atendimento de urgência e emergência: Revisão integrativa.

6cd3e4463a530f6f5d3918b9a4b28155724559b0.abstract:
<jats:p>Objective: To identify in the scientific literature the technologies developed for the integration and optimization of urgent emergency services.
Method: This is an integrative literature review. To select the articles, the researchers accessed the online databases MedLine, PubMed, Lilacs, Scielo, BVS, Science Direct, Cochrane Library, Scopus, and the Google Academic search engine. The articles considered were the ones published from 2011 to 2019, and the data were collected from October to December 2019. Data analysis occurred throughout an exploratory, selective, analytical, and interpretive reading of the articles, and the results were presented in boxes.
Results: Eleven articles were selected, and among the technologies listed in them, those classified as “hard” are the ones that contain the most multiple functions; these include clinical data recording, medical service monitoring, programmed calculation of medications, teleradiology, among other services that optimize the services provided in the Urgent and Emergency Care Network.
Conclusion: Studies have shown that digital technologies are an adequate tool to support critical patient care practices within the urgent and emergency care services. Mobile applications can be effective as they were considered useful for pain monitoring, clinical management of specialties, drug preparation, mapping of critical areas, risk classification, reproduction of imaging tests as well as in helping clients to provide them information on the order and speed of service.</jats:p>

title: Assessing the Quality of AI Explanations of Atrial Fibrillation: Comparative Analysis of ChatGPT and Google Gemini
container-title: JMIR Formative Research
598e2fa6d5c1d1ee8bb1eebc101a66353744cb13.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Atrial fibrillation (AF) is one of the most common arrhythmias and is associated with multiple risk factors, including stroke and heart failure. Therefore, it is important that accurate and comprehensive educational resources on AF are available. Artificial intelligence (AI) platforms such as Google Gemini and ChatGPT are emerging tools for medical education. To our knowledge, this is the first study to assess the quality of these platforms for AF education.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Objective</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This pilot study aimed to (1) assess the quality of ChatGPT and Google Gemini explanations of AF and its treatment, (2) compare responses from both platforms, and (3) analyze differences in interpretation between cardiologists and nonmedical professionals.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The prompt “Explain atrial fibrillation and how to treat it to a patient” was entered into both ChatGPT and Google Gemini. The responses, along with a survey created in Google Forms, were sent out to potential participants between September and October 2024. The survey questions were derived from the Patient Education Materials Assessment Tool for Printable Materials and DISCERN criteria. Each survey question was multiple choice and rated on a 5-point Likert scale, where 1 indicated strong disagreement and 5 indicated strong agreement. Averages of each answer from the survey were calculated and compared using the Wilcoxon signed-rank test.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The survey was completed by 28 participants, including cardiologists and cardiology fellows and 17 nonmedical professionals (college graduates not employed in the medical field). No significant overall quality differences were observed between ChatGPT and Google Gemini. When comparing participant groups, cardiologists rated AI-generated responses higher than nonmedical professionals for perceived bias (mean 3.82 vs mean 4.33; P=.04) and for explaining consequences of no treatment (mean 2.85 vs mean 1.86; P=.005). In contrast, nonmedical professionals rated structural and organizational features more favorably than cardiologists, including visual cues (mean 3.97 vs mean 2.48; P<.001), informative headers (mean 4.77 vs mean 3.95; P=.001), concise sections (mean 4.71 vs mean 4.29; P=.04), identifiable patient actions (mean 4.21 vs mean 3.19; P=.04), and references to additional resources (mean 2.65 vs mean 1.71; P=.006).</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The comparable quality of ChatGPT and Google Gemini suggests that both are viable for AF education. Differences in ratings of organizational features versus perceptions of bias and consequences of no treatment highlight a disconnect between cardiologists and nonmedical professionals. To optimize clinical application, cardiologists should evaluate both comprehensiveness and clarity of AI-generated responses. This serves as a pilot study, and future research should focus on longitudinal studies of AI-generated responses and their effects on clinical outcomes.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

Towards Realistic Project-Level Code Generation via Multi-Agent Collaboration and Semantic Architecture Modeling

2e98affb75fe6b1c9fa0a80bf39cb6bb48af6b14.abstract:
<jats:p>
                    In recent years, Large Language Models (LLMs) have achieved remarkable progress in automated code generation. In real-world software engineering, the growing demand for rapid iteration and continuous delivery underscores the importance of project-level code generation, where LLMs are expected to generate complete software projects directly from complex user requirements. This task, however, presents greater challenges due to larger input scales, multi-modal information, and the need for holistic architectural reasoning. Although existing studies have made initial explorations, they still face key limitations, including unrealistic datasets and unreliable evaluation metrics that fail to reflect real-world complexity, the semantic gap between human-written requirements and machine-interpretable structures, and difficulties in managing hierarchical dependencies and maintaining quality throughout the generation process. To address these limitations, we first introduce
                    <jats:sc>CodeProjectEval</jats:sc>
                    , a project-level code generation dataset built from 18 real-world repositories with 12.7 files and 2,388.6 lines of code per task on average, supplemented with documentation and executable test cases for automatic evaluation. We further propose
                    <jats:sc>ProjectGen</jats:sc>
                    , a multi-agent framework that decomposes projects into architecture design, skeleton generation, and code filling stages with iterative refinement and memory-based context management. Within this framework, we introduce the Semantic Software Architecture Tree, a structured and semantically rich representation that effectively bridges user requirements and source code implementation. Experiments show that
                    <jats:sc>ProjectGen</jats:sc>
                    achieves state-of-the-art performance, passing 52/124 test cases on the small-scale project-level code generation dataset DevBench, a 57% improvement over the baseline approaches, and 310 test cases on
                    <jats:sc>CodeProjectEval</jats:sc>
                    , representing an improvement of roughly tenfold compared to the baselines.
                  </jats:p>

title: AI-Generated Exposure Hierarchies for Body Dysmorphic Disorder: Proof-of-Concept Study
container-title: JMIR Formative Research
475970c23de59b336f5f102fda0e80aa46b47e4e.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="background">
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Body dysmorphic disorder (BDD) is a chronic, impairing condition for which cognitive behavioral therapy, including exposure and response prevention (ERP), is the first-line treatment, but few clinicians are trained in BDD-specific ERP. Constructing personalized exposure hierarchies is time-intensive and requires clinical expertise, particularly for patients with absent insight who may hold appearance beliefs with delusional conviction. Generative AI (GenAI)–powered chatbots, such as ChatGPT, have shown utility for clinical content, but their capacity to produce safe, appropriate ERP hierarchies for BDD has not been examined.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="objective">
                    <jats:title>Objective</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study evaluated the feasibility of using ChatGPT (GPT-5) to generate ERP hierarchies for BDD, assessed the influence of clinical and demographic characteristics on output quality, benchmarked AI-generated hierarchies against those created by doctoral-level BDD specialists, and tested whether blinded experts could distinguish AI-generated from expert-generated hierarchies.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="methods">
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>GPT-5 generated 10-item graded exposure hierarchies for 72 simulated vignettes that varied by body area, insight level (good, limited, or absent), symptom specificity, age, and gender. Expert clinicians independently generated hierarchies for a subset of 18 vignettes. Two researchers rated all GPT-5 hierarchies for task completion and information integration. Three BDD expert clinicians, blinded to the hierarchy source (expert vs GPT-5), rated all 90 hierarchies for relevance, specificity, variability, safety, and overall quality. After unblinding, raters attempted to identify the AI-generated hierarchy in the 18 matched pairs.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="results">
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      GPT-5 generated complete hierarchies for 69 of 72 (95.8%) vignettes. Blinded experts rated GPT-5 hierarchies highly across all dimensions (mean scores ranging from 4.39, SD 0.26 to 4.90, SD 0.16 out of 5), with no significant differences from expert-generated hierarchies except for variability, where experts scored modestly higher (
                      <jats:italic>P</jats:italic>
                      =.02;
                      <jats:italic>r</jats:italic>
                      =0.24). After unblinding, raters correctly identified AI-generated hierarchies only 31.5% (17/54) of the time, significantly below chance (
                      <jats:italic>P</jats:italic>
                      =.009); this below-chance result was mostly due to one rater, and no rater performed above chance. Insight level was the most consistent predictor of quality: absent-insight hierarchies received significantly lower safety (
                      <jats:italic>P</jats:italic>
                      <.001;
                      <jats:italic>r</jats:italic>
                      =0.73) and overall quality ratings (
                      <jats:italic>P</jats:italic>
                      =.01;
                      <jats:italic>r</jats:italic>
                      =0.43). This pattern was not unique to GPT-5; safety ratings for expert-generated hierarchies also declined significantly by insight level (
                      <jats:italic>P</jats:italic>
                      =.03). Miscalibration of exposure difficulty, particularly for low- and absent-insight cases, was the most common rater concern (30/43, 69.8% comments), disproportionately directed at GPT-5 hierarchies.
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="conclusions">
                    <jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>GPT-5 generated ERP hierarchies for BDD that blinded experts rated as comparable to clinician-created hierarchies and could not reliably distinguish them from clinician-created hierarchies. However, hierarchies for patients with absent insight received lower safety and quality ratings from both AI and expert sources, and qualitative comments suggested AI-generated hierarchies were less well calibrated to delusional-level presentations. GenAI thus shows promise as a clinician-facing aid for ERP hierarchy generation, but these findings underscore the need for clinician oversight, especially for patients with delusional conviction.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: SAI: Virtualizing Shared Memory of GPU for AI workload acceleration
container-title: ACM Transactions on Design Automation of Electronic Systems
c8fa29b0323351e1659db262fc936958ed20d580.abstract:
<jats:p>
                    AI workloads increasingly demand high parallelism and efficient on-chip memory utilization on modern GPUs. However, the limited capacity of shared memory often constrains thread-level parallelism, while portions of the L2 cache remain underutilized. In this work, we propose
                    <jats:bold>SAI</jats:bold>
                    , a mechanism that virtualizes shared memory into the L2 cache to improve GPU performance for AI applications. SAI dynamically activates virtualization based on runtime resource usage, enabling additional CTAs with minimal architectural modifications. We further introduce an L2 cache management strategy that integrates associativity-based virtual page allocation and a replacement information table, reducing page-swapping overhead while preserving L2 cache performance. Experimental results demonstrate that SAI achieves an 18.6% performance improvement over the baseline design and outperforms SMILE-opt, our reproduced state-of-the-art baseline, by 8.8%. Moreover, SAI captures 60.2% of the performance gain delivered by the idealized Double SMEM design while reducing energy consumption to 87.7% of the baseline. These results highlight the effectiveness of SAI in enhancing thread-level parallelism and optimizing on-chip memory for AI workloads.
                  </jats:p>

title: AI-Enabled Early Detection of Epidemic Threats in a Resource-Constrained Health System: Implementation Research from Lebanon
container-title: Oxford Open Digital Health
94bf395e649f9c13344c021277ab854ad6c98be5.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Global South countries face heightened infectious disease risks compounded by fragmented surveillance systems and resource constraints. Lebanon’s health system crisis and recurrent outbreaks highlight the urgent need for new approaches to epidemic and pandemic preparedness.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Objective</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>To describe the design, implementation process, and early implementation findings of an artificial intelligence (AI)–enabled early warning system (AI-EWS) that automates detection of epidemiologically relevant events using laboratory data in Lebanon, with emphasis on feasibility, workflow integration, stakeholder engagement, and implementation learnings.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>We applied an implementation research approach to co-design and validate an AI-EWS prototype integrated within a university hospital laboratory. The system incorporates a hybrid statistical and machine learning analytic pipeline and a real-time dashboard for detecting epidemic events across multiple pathogens using routine laboratory information systems (LIS) data. The system was developed in collaboration with the Ministry of Public Health (MoPH) to support future national adoption.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Findings</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The project produced a structured framework for pathogen selection, rule development, dataset creation, and platform co-design with clinical and epidemiological experts, medical informatics professionals, MoPH experts, and technical specialists. Early implementation observations indicate operational feasibility within existing infrastructure, strong stakeholder engagement, and trust-building around AI-enabled surveillance through participatory design and responsible-AI governance.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>AI-enabled laboratory surveillance is a viable and scalable approach to strengthening epidemic preparedness in low-resource health systems when grounded in implementation science and responsible AI, and when explicitly aligned with local workflows and national policy priorities.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Bayesian Forecasting as the Analytical Core of an AI-Assisted Early Warning System for Dengue Outbreaks during the 2023 Epidemic: Implementation and Emergency Management in a Dominican Pediatric Hospital
container-title: Oxford Open Digital Health
056417fa3dbad64347775b6e5020ffb82cf01df1.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Dengue remains a major cause of pediatric morbidity in the Dominican Republic, with increasingly intense epidemic cycles. Advances in statistical modeling, probabilistic forecasting, and AI-assisted digital health systems offer new opportunities to enhance early warning capabilities and strengthen hospital preparedness. This study evaluated a Bayesian negative binomial regression forecasting model as the analytical core of an AI-assisted early warning system (EWS) for predicting weekly dengue cases nationwide, using strict out-of-sample validation during the 2023 epidemic and applying its outputs operationally in a high-demand pediatric hospital. National surveillance data (PLISA/PAHO), hospital records from the Dr. Hugo Mendoza Pediatric Hospital (HPHM), and climatic and satellite indicators (NOAA, MODIS) for 2014–2024 were integrated. The model incorporated climatically plausible lags, harmonic seasonality, two vegetation indices (NDVI_lag4 and EVI_lag4), a long-term spline trend, and weakly informative priors, achieving excellent convergence (Rhat = 1.00). Climatic and environmental predictors exhibited small and uncertain effects, whereas the temporal spline accounted for most long-term epidemic variability. In the 2023 national validation, the model captured the broad epidemic trajectory and improved RMSE and MAE compared with the historical seasonal baseline (RMSE = 783.3; MAE = 423.4; MAPE = 80.2%), although proportional accuracy remained limited during abrupt epidemic acceleration. The national model also captured ascending-phase signals that were temporally aligned with the HPHM hospital outbreak, including its sharp rise during epidemiological weeks 36–40. These outputs were used alongside routine surveillance and hospital indicators to support operational situational awareness, capacity planning, patient-flow reorganization, strengthened triage, and emergency preparedness during the epidemic. The model demonstrated temporal signal detection and operational relevance, positioning Bayesian probabilistic forecasting, embedded within an AI-assisted digital health workflow, as a useful analytical component for epidemic monitoring and hospital preparedness, subject to limitations in peak magnitude calibration and proportional accuracy.</jats:p>

title: Metastable Phase Separation and Information Retrieval in Multicomponent Liquids
container-title: Physical Review X
f02370894d54655c5f3a2f25a4c5c570dab5896a.abstract: <jats:p>Liquid mixtures can separate into phases with distinct composition. This phenomenon has recently come back to prominence due to its role in complex biological liquids, such as the cytoplasm, which contain thousands of components. For simple two-component mixtures phase-separated states are global free energy minima. However, local free energy minima, i.e., metastable states, are known to play a dominant role in complex systems with many components. For example, Hopfield neural networks can retrieve stored information from partial cues via relaxation to metastable states. Under what conditions can phase separated states be metastable, and what are the implications for information retrieval in multicomponent liquids? In this work we develop the general thermodynamic formalism of metastable phase separation. We then apply this formalism to an illustrative toy example inspired by recent experiments, binary mixtures with high-order interactions. Finally, as core application of the formalism, we study metastability in Hopfield liquids, a class of multicomponent mixtures capable of storing information on the composition of phases. We show that these phases can be nucleated from partial cues via metastable phase separation. Spatial simulations of liquids with a large number of components match our analytical solution. Our work suggests that complex biological mixtures can retrieve information through metastable phase separation.</jats:p>
