Vessel daily reports, fuel and lube oil records, machinery hours, HSE observations, defects, inspections, certificates, crew and training data, and emissions indicators are often dispersed across applications, spreadsheets, emails, and document stores. The resulting problem is not lack of data, but difficulty retrieving and interpreting the right evidence when a decision is required. The framework converts verified vessel and company records into an access-controlled maritime knowledge base. For each natural-language question, the system applies validation, metadata filters, hybrid retrieval, reranking, deterministic calculations, grounded generation, source citation, and human verification. Representative questions include abnormal consumption, machinery hours inconsistent with activity, recurring defects, overdue or unverified compliance items, HSE themes, training gaps, and emissions variance. The demonstration indicates that RAG is valuable when it connects records that are normally reviewed separately. Consumption becomes meaningful when combined with activity, weather, machinery configuration, and comparable periods; safety observations become more useful when linked to actions, inspections, and training; and compliance queries can distinguish expiry from an approaching due date or superseded document. The process also reveals inconsistent units, duplicate entries, missing activity codes, and stale records. RAG can therefore provide traceable fleet decision support when it uses approved data, preserves lineage, enforces vessel- and role-based access, and permits a no-answer response where evidence is insufficient. It should reduce manual searching and support earlier intervention, while operational authority remains with competent maritime personnel. The evaluation approach therefore specifies quantitative measures—retrieval precision, citation coverage, calculation accuracy, end-to-end investigation and verification time, manual workflow steps, source-system switches, human correction rate, and user adoption—benchmarked against the same questions completed through existing reports and dashboards. Deployment success also depends on governed source quality, scalable indexing, integration controls, and maintained maritime metadata and taxonomies. Cross-industry controlled and field studies report AI-related productivity or task-time improvements ranging from approximately 15% to 55.8% [11–14]. Given the higher consequence of maritime decisions and mandatory human verification, this paper proposes benchmark-informed initial targets of 25-35% lower end-to-end investigation time and 25-30% lower manual workflow effort, with at least 90% retrieval precision and at least 95% citation coverage. These are acceptance targets for paired trials, not measured fleet outcomes.

title: From Reactive to Predictive Offshore Operations an AI – Enabled Integrated Framework for Vessel Reliability Enhancement and NPT Reduction
container-title: ADIPEC
3a9092cf379d2df075f4bd689bf039d3960fbb62.abstract: Abstract Offshore project execution is increasingly challenged by rising operational complexity, tighter project schedules, and growing expectations for reliability, safety, and cost efficiency. Despite technological advancements in the offshore sector, Non-Productive Time (NPT) continues to significantly affect project delivery due to equipment failures, vessel downtime, maintenance inefficiencies, logistical constraints, and fragmented operational decision-making. Traditional reactive maintenance approaches often address failures after operational disruption has occurred, resulting in increased costs, schedule delays, and reduced asset utilization. This paper proposes an integrated framework that combines vessel operational data, maintenance history, equipment condition monitoring, offshore logistics information, and project execution parameters within a centralized digital platform. The methodology integrates predictive maintenance principles, reliability engineering analysis, and AI-enabled anomaly detection to identify operational risks and early indicators of equipment degradation. The framework further connects vessel scheduling, maintenance planning, resource coordination, logistics, and offshore execution tracking within a unified operational decision-support model. Key performance indicators, including Mean Time Between Failures (MTBF), Mean Time to Repair (MTTR), vessel utilization, project schedule adherence, maintenance response efficiency, and NPT trends, are incorporated to support predictive operational decision-making and project risk prioritization. A simulation-based evaluation was conducted using a representative offshore construction support vessel operating over a 12-month campaign. The simulated baseline represented a reactive-preventive maintenance environment with an MTBF of 620 operating hours, MTTR of 18 hours, vessel utilization of 78%, and annual NPT of 11.4%. Under the proposed framework scenario, the model projected an increase in MTBF to 860 operating hours, a reduction in MTTR to 8 hours, an increase in vessel utilization to 87%, and a 54% reduction in equipment-related NPT. Schedule adherence was also projected to improve by 18% under the defined simulation assumptions. The results indicate that the proposed framework has the potential to improve offshore reliability and execution performance by integrating equipment condition information with maintenance planning, logistics coordination, and project execution requirements. By providing a common decision-support architecture, the framework is designed to support earlier maintenance intervention, improved resource coordination, and more proactive management of vessel-related operational risks. The simulation therefore provides an indicative assessment of the potential benefits of integrating reliability analytics with offshore project execution planning. Unlike conventional offshore operational studies focused primarily on project optimization or standalone maintenance systems, this work introduces a cross-functional framework integrating vessel reliability engineering, predictive maintenance analytics, offshore logistics, and project execution intelligence into a unified operational ecosystem. The proposed model provides a scalable architecture for supporting the transition from reactive offshore management toward more predictive, data-driven operational planning. The reported performance improvements are simulation-based outcomes generated under the defined modelling assumptions and have not yet been validated through live vessel deployment or field trials. Operational validation using vessel-specific historical data and controlled pilot implementation is identified as the next stage for assessing predictive accuracy, failure prediction performance, and the realized impact on reliability, NPT, and project execution.

title: Field-Validated AI-Enabled Advanced Process Control for Operating Efficiency in Large-Scale Oil and Gas Separation Trains
container-title: ADIPEC
149e77286c029a31359d3646c03fa90db748fc39.abstract: Abstract Conventional oil and gas separation facilities operate under highly variable conditions caused by changing well contributions, gas-oil ratio, water cut, production routing, slugging, and strong interactions among separation, desalting, stabilization, and export systems. These conditions have historically limited the application of Advanced Process Control in upstream production facilities, where optimization commonly depends on independent regulatory control loops, conservative operating targets, delayed laboratory measurements, and frequent operator intervention. This paper presents the full-scale deployment and field validation of an AI-enabled Advanced Process Control (Ai-APC) architecture across five conventional oil and gas separation trains and associated facilities within one of the world's largest onshore oil fields. The Gas Oil Separation Plant, designed for 780,000 BOPD and processing commingled production from more than 600 wells, was optimized using next-generation Dynamic Matrix Control (DMC3™), adaptive process models, and real-time soft sensors for Reid Vapor Pressure and salt prediction. The deployment methodology included site assessment, data conditioning, live-plant dynamic testing, model development and validation, Distributed Control System integration, operator training, closed-loop commissioning, and digital performance auditing using real-time KPI dashboards. Performance was evaluated from 17 February to 30 March 2026 against a validated pre-APC baseline. The Ai-APC application achieved 99.35% availability and improved oil recovery by 0.31 vol%, equivalent to 2,208 BOPD of incremental production. Lean-gas consumption per barrel of oil decreased by 55%, fresh wash-water consumption decreased by 3%, and the frequency and variability of manual operator intervention decreased by 20%. The deployment also reduced CO2 emissions by 11,666 metric tons and delivered approximately USD 43 million/year in annualized realized value. The results demonstrate that highly variable conventional separation facilities can be transformed from reactive, laboratory-dependent operation into predictive, quality-aware, and continuously optimized assets. The work establishes a transferable AI-enabled brownfield separation optimization framework integrating adaptive multivariable control, real-time quality inferential, operator decision support, and digital performance assurance. This framework provides a scalable foundation for improving operating efficiency and advancing progressively autonomous upstream production operations.

title: AI-Driven Video Analytics and Behavioral Safety Intelligence: Enhancing Human-Centered Operational Adaptation in Offshore Support Vessels
container-title: ADIPEC
156e6d6192a3d2679989b73fff7135b74a8cfd47.abstract: Computer vision and artificial intelligence (AI) are increasingly used in industrial Health, Safety, and Environment (HSE) management to detect missing personal protective equipment (PPE), restricted-zone entries, and line-of-fire exposure. Early offshore and industrial deployments established the technical feasibility of real-time edge processing and automated safety monitoring (Almadhoun et al. 2020; Tamaazousti et al. 2022). A practical challenge emerges when these systems are scaled across multiple assets: large volumes of detections must be converted into operationally meaningful information. Real-time alerts can support immediate intervention, but isolated detections do not necessarily explain why a behavior recurses or whether the underlying procedure, equipment, or task design contributes to the observed deviation (Corallo and Spingardi 2024; Vukicevic et al. 2024). Traditional HSE responses may treat behavioral deviations primarily as individual compliance failures. Human Factors engineering instead recognizes that task demands, equipment interfaces, and environmental constraints shape worker behavior (Reason 1997). Safety-II similarly emphasizes the difference between prescribed work and operational practice, commonly described as Work-as-Imagined and Work-as-Done (Hollnagel 2014).

title: AI Digital Rock Typing (AIDRT): A No-Code Physics-Augmented Machine-Learning Workflow for Carbonate Rock Typing and Static-To-Dynamic Property Prediction
container-title: ADIPEC
727c7415ff84c95106f61fe038cce60407a1ef65.abstract: Abstract Carbonate rock typing requires connecting the pore-throat network (PorThN) and geological lithofacies description with porosity, permeability, capillary pressure, wettability, and relative permeability across multiple scales, from nano-, micro-, and macro-scales with core image and plug scales to log scale in feet, and finally to reservoir-model scales. This paper presents AI Digital Rock Typing (AIDRT), a no-code, physics-augmented workflow that builds that connection while keeping observations, predictions, calibrations, uncertainty, validation evidence, and expert approval distinct. AIDRT organizes image and tabular evidence through Machine Learning Image Processing and Recognition (MLIR), which identifies Controllable Measurable Volume (CMV) with descriptors as part of the Morphology Decoder process, and integrates 3D Carbonate Heterogeneous Permeability (kHeC), Permeability-linked Capillary Pressure Function (P-Function), wettability-sensitive relative-permeability analysis with pore-throat Deformation Factor (df), and the digital Rock Typing Carbonate Morphology chart (DRT-CAMO). The workflow registers sample scale and provenance, derives pore- and mineral-related evidence, evaluates the pore-throat network, estimates local and aggregated permeability, constructs capillary-pressure and flow-function hypotheses, and transfers candidate rock types toward core–log correlation. The AIDRT implementation completed all software tests and demonstrates traceable project artifacts, validation, and uncertainty views. These results verify the tested workflow behavior with the bundled synthetic table and image. Eqs. (1) - (9) remain the dependable AIDRT workflow formulation. AIDRT's principal contribution is therefore a reviewable evidence-to-reservoir-model chain in which petrophysicists, geologists, and reservoir engineers can examine the same rock-type decision, preserve its applicability limits, and retain accountable interconnectivity among porosity, permeability, lithology, lithofacies, capillary pressure, wettability, and relative permeability, to produce carbonate rock types and their reservoir static and dynamic petrophysical properties, all in one place.

title: RANCANG BANGUN SISTEM INFORMASI MANAJEMEN TOKO RITEL BERBASIS AI UNTUK PREDIKSI PERMINTAAN DAN REKOMENDASI PEMESANAN BARANG
container-title: Simtek : jurnal sistem informasi dan teknik komputer
b1a24950e0848616c9845895e41f1733b3098d24.abstract: Ketidakpastian permintaan dalam pengelolaan persediaan toko ritel dapat menyebabkan stockout maupun overstock. Penelitian ini membangun sistem informasi manajemen toko ritel yang mengintegrasikan pengelolaan transaksi dan stok dengan prediksi permintaan serta rekomendasi pemesanan barang. Sistem dikembangkan dengan metode Waterfall, sedangkan modul prediksi menggunakan kerangka CRISP-DM untuk membandingkan XGBoost dan Holt-Winters, lalu memilih model dengan MAE terendah pada setiap produk. Safety stock dan reorder point dihitung dari data historis penjualan, sedangkan jumlah saran pesanan berasal dari prediksi 14 hari. Dataset sintetis periode September 2025–Agustus 2026 mencakup 20 produk, 5 pemasok, dan 10.886 transaksi. Rata-rata MAPE XGBoost sebesar 36,07% dan Holt-Winters 35,56%, sehingga kinerja keduanya relatif setara. Black Box Testing terhadap 35 skenario menunjukkan seluruh fungsi berjalan sesuai rancangan. Pengujian pada data transaksi riil diperlukan pada penelitian selanjutnya.

title: A Critical Analysis of AI from the Perspective of the Philosophy of Science among Grade X Students at SMA Don Bosco Padang
container-title: Journal of Multidisciplinary Science: MIKAILALSYS
78e1e5475c4f3b6cf9f26befe44e5548f4ddcce2.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) facilitates access to information in education, increasing the importance of critically evaluating claims and their underlying assumptions. This study examined Grade 10 students’ ability to distinguish facts, opinions, and values in AI-related information at SMA Don Bosco Padang from a philosophy of science perspective. A descriptive quantitative approach was employed involving 33 students. Data were collected through a 15-item written test comprising five items each for fact, opinion, and value identification. Descriptive analysis examined frequencies, percentages of correct responses, score distributions, and classification error patterns. Across 495 responses, 337 were correct and 158 were incorrect, yielding an overall accuracy of 68.08%. Accuracy was highest for opinion identification (76.36%), followed by fact identification (67.88%) and value identification (60.00%). Value identification presented the greatest difficulty, with an error rate of 40.00%. These findings reveal descriptive differences in students’ classification performance, particularly their greater difficulty recognizing values within AI-related information. From a philosophy of science perspective, the results underscore the relevance of epistemology for evaluating evidence and the justification of claims, alongside axiology for recognizing ethical considerations. The study provides contextual evidence to inform AI literacy instruction that integrates information verification, critical reasoning, and ethical reflection to support responsible technology use.

title: AI translation sounds convincing, but it can be riddled with hidden errors
A Smart Insole-Based Explainable AI Framework for Non-Invasive Sciatica Diagnosis Using Optimally Selected Plantar Force Sensors
44867e825acf1cdcc9b18ad253e5851e1983b666.abstract: Abstract Sciatica is a neuropathic disorder that can cause significant alterations in lower-limb biomechanics, including gait asymmetry and abnormal plantar force distribution. This study proposes a wearable, explainable artificial intelligence (XAI)-based framework for automated sciatica diagnosis using optimally selected force-sensitive resistor (FSR) sensors integrated into a smart insole. A dataset of 37 subjects, comprising 20 patients with Sciatica and 17 healthy subjects, was acquired using 16 FSR sensors, with eight sensors positioned on each foot, along with concurrent electromyography (EMG) and inertial measurement unit (IMU) data. From the bilateral plantar force signals, 601 biomechanical features were extracted, incorporating statistical, temporal, magnitude, and inter-limb asymmetry characteristics. A K-fold combinatorial sensor-selection strategy identified the optimal sensor configuration, with K = 5 providing the most stable performance. The optimal configurations, L2, L5, L8 for the left foot and R2, R5, R8 for the right foot, reduced the number of sensors from 16 to 6, representing a 62.5% reduction in sensing hardware. The selected left-foot sensors achieved 96% accuracy, 96% precision, 93% recall, 94% F1-score, and 0.93 AUC, while the right-foot sensors achieved 87% accuracy, 83% precision, 76% recall, 79% F1-score, and 0.91 AUC. Using the six optimally selected sensors, the proposed one-dimensional convolutional neural network (1D-CNN) achieved 90.3% classification accuracy, 89.9% sensitivity, 90.3% specificity, and a ROC-AUC of 0.911. Furthermore, XAI-based plantar heatmaps confirmed the contribution of the selected biomechanical regions to the classification decision. Cross-validation against the concurrent EMG/IMU modality achieved 85.2% accuracy, with approximately 81.5% diagnostic agreement between the force-sensor and EMG/IMU models. The quantitative results demonstrate that a substantially reduced FSR sensor configuration can preserve diagnostically relevant biomechanical information while providing accurate, interpretable, and portable sciatica screening. The proposed framework offers potential for low-cost wearable gait assessment and automated clinical decision support.

title: Human-AI Collaboration in Urban Digital Transformation: Balancing Efficiency and Human Values in Shanghai’s AI-Enabled Talent Recruitment
container-title: Digital Technologies Research and Applications
99b2a4d2edc2dc8df689bff6b515848affbe723a.abstract: In the context of the urban digital revolution, recruitment through AI technologies has become common practice to address competition in the labor market. However, it is still unclear how the effectiveness of such recruitment is connected with humanistic values. For this research, an exploratory qualitative research design was used, involving semi-structured interviews with eight human resource professionals in Shanghai. Based on the results, the use of AI in recruitment led to increased efficiency mainly when screening candidates through high-volume, standardized processes, although the promised efficiency was not delivered in practice because the introduction of the AI system increased the workload. Patterns of human-machine cooperation were observed in different companies: tech companies and foreign companies are inclined to adopt interactive adjustment approaches, while state-owned enterprises retain human-dominated decision-making. Transparency of algorithms was still lacking in numerous instances, and there was an asymmetry in the accountability framework of algorithms, wherein disobeying algorithms carries more personal consequences than obeying them. The more experienced professionals became more autonomous in their work, while the less experienced professionals depended more on the algorithm. Issues like management support, information accuracy, and departmental integration have a major impact on implementation. This study contributes to the theory of human-machine collaboration by proposing the concept of asymmetric algorithmic accountability, which captures the uneven distribution of organizational consequences for following versus overriding AI recommendations and shapes practitioner behavior in ways that extend beyond individual trust or algorithmic transparency.

title: From AI readiness to regenerative tourism orientation: a tourist-centric model of smart tourism villages
container-title: ABAC Journal
600067ed573dc780c1bd155c47ed81d59d2f7b38.abstract: Purpose This study develops and validates a tourist-centric model of AI-driven smart tourism villages (AI-DSTV), explaining how perceived digital infrastructure and smart governance relate to tourist acceptance and perceived regenerative tourism orientation (PRTO) through rural authenticity, value co-creation, AI trust, and perceived service value. Design/methodology/approach A cross-sectional survey involved 686 domestic tourists who had experienced an AI-supported tourism touchpoint in rural tourism settings in Indonesia. The sample was predominantly young and digitally engaged, with 75.1% aged 18–24 and 68.4% students. The model was tested using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) with 10,000 bootstrap resamples and importance-performance map analysis (IPMA). Findings All 12 hypothesized relationships were significant. Rural authenticity strongly enhanced perceived AI service value, while tourist value co-creation strengthened AI trust and ethical acceptance. Digital infrastructure and smart governance also showed significant downstream effects through authenticity–service-value and co-creation–trust pathways. The model explained 56.3% of PRTO variance. IPMA identified AI trust and ethical acceptance as the most important antecedent of PRTO and the lowest-performing construct, indicating a key managerial priority. Practical implications Rural destinations should prioritize transparent, culturally grounded, participatory and locally accountable AI systems. Strengthening ethical trust, co-creation, and culturally appropriate personalization may offer greater managerial leverage than technological sophistication alone. Originality/value The study extends technology-adoption research beyond behavioral acceptance by introducing PRTO as a tourist-level psychological outcome. It conceptualizes AI-DSTV as a socio-technical ecosystem linking destination readiness with authenticity, co-creation, trust and service evaluation while distinguishing regenerative orientation from verified destination regeneration.

title: White coats in the news feed: the effects of content features on physicians' engagement behaviors in online academic medical communities
container-title: Aslib Journal of Information Management
7353f574ac1fb297470e88c542e86cf0e544ddfd.abstract: Purpose Online academic medical communities (OAMCs) have become central channels for physicians to exchange medical knowledge. Yet a substantial share of physician-generated medical content on these platforms fails to elicit meaningful peer engagement, constraining the dissemination of medical knowledge. Given that the intrinsic features of content in OAMCs are likely key drivers of peer engagement, understanding what makes content appealing is essential. However, the relationship remains unclear. This study aims to address this gap by examining how distinct content features influence different forms of peer engagement in OAMCs. Design/methodology/approach Leveraging data from a leading Chinese OAMC, we operationalize six content features (complexity, subjectivity, professionalism, completeness, informativeness, multimodal information presentation) via natural language processing and examine their effects on physicians' collecting and interacting behaviors and the moderating role of disease severity. Findings Peer physicians prioritize information-rich content for collecting, while favoring discussion-oriented content for interacting. Multimodal, comprehensive content is welcomed, whereas overly sophisticated, highly specialized content is less effective. Disease severity moderates these relationships, with physicians exhibiting greater selectivity in collecting but more interactive under high-severity conditions. Originality/value This study is among the first to uncover the impact of content features on physicians' engagement behaviors while considering disease severity as the moderating variable. By incorporating natural language processing techniques, it extends the information adoption model to online physician platforms and offers actionable guidance for optimizing physician online engagement.

title: High Use, Low Preparation
container-title: American Journal of Physical Medicine & Rehabilitation
cd596e36835769e8c758e2939412febb985e5034.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (Gen-AI) has rapidly entered clinical environments, posing a risk of “cognitive offloading” that may impede the development of independent clinical judgment. This study conducted a cross-sectional survey of residents, fellows, and faculty at a large academic medical center in January 2026 to quantify Gen-AI utilization and perceptions in physical medicine and rehabilitation (PM&R) to inform curriculum development. Thirty-six trainees (95% response rate) and 11 faculty members (30% response rate) completed the survey; 43 (91.5%) reported any Gen-AI use and formed the analytic sample. Among users, 72.1% used Gen-AI daily for clinical learning and 51.2% during patient encounters, yet 67.4% were self-taught and only 7.0% always requested citations. Trainees requested citations more often than faculty ( P =.048), while faculty more often relied on clinical judgment without additional verification (62.5% vs. 25.7%, P =.089). Gen-AI-derived evidence was rarely surfaced in teaching: 60.5% discussed it during case presentations rarely or never, and only 16.2% always disclosed its origin. Residents are integrating Gen-AI into clinical workflows at rates that outpace faculty familiarity, while verification remains largely undiscussed and untaught. These gaps highlight an urgent need for structured Gen-AI curricula in PM&R residency.

title: Ecocentric approach for knowledge management and eco-conscious open innovation for a circular economy: leveraging intellectual capital
container-title: Journal of Enterprise Information Management
686c261491946be26d24c79772bd44511d29dc4d.abstract: Purpose The transition toward a circular economy (CE) requires organizations to develop environmentally responsible innovation practices; however, limited research has explained how knowledge management (KM) practices facilitate eco-conscious open innovation (EOI), particularly within small and medium-sized manufacturing enterprises (SMEs) in emerging economies. Furthermore, the role of intellectual capital (IC) as an underlying mechanism linking the ecocentric approach to KM with EOI remains underexplored. Therefore, this study examines the mediating role of IC dimensions in the relationship between the ecocentric approach to KM and EOI among manufacturing SMEs in Pakistan. Drawing on the resource-based view (RBV), knowledge-based view (KBV), and intellectual capital-based view (ICBV), the study explains how environmentally oriented knowledge practices are transformed into sustainable innovation outcomes. Design/methodology/approach Data were collected from 398 respondents employed in manufacturing SMEs in Pakistan. PLS-SEM using SmartPLS 4.0.9 was employed to test the proposed relationships and examine the mediating role of IC dimensions in the ecocentric KM–EOI relationship. Findings The findings reveal that IC dimensions fully mediate the relationship between the ecocentric approach to KM and EOI. The results further indicate that the ecocentric approach to KM enhances human, structural, and relational capital, which subsequently promote inbound and outbound EOI. The direct effects of the ecocentric approach to KM on EOI became insignificant when IC dimensions were included, whereas the corresponding indirect effects remained significant, confirming full mediation. Originality/value This study contributes to the literature by extending understanding of the ecocentric approach to KM within the CE context and by identifying IC as a critical mechanism through which environmentally oriented knowledge practices contribute to EOI. By integrating RBV, KBV and ICBV, the study offers a comprehensive theoretical explanation of the KM–EOI relationship. Moreover, evidence from Pakistani manufacturing SMEs provides insights from an underexplored emerging-economy context and offers practical implications for organizations seeking to strengthen intellectual capital and advance eco-conscious innovation for circular economy objectives.

title: Beyond Alignment: The Retrieval Value of Offline Teacher Information
3cbd649a79ed1e354c7fe0052687439db175983a.abstract: Abstract A compressed retriever can gain substantial retrieval quality from teacher information that its alignment examples never constrain. We isolate this resource by changing only teacher-token responses outside the support of 2,048 fitting queries. Source features, cross-validation and fitted coefficients remain identical, while retrieval improves. Across two encoder settings and three tasks, the full teacher table exceeds the champion of a separate 30-configuration source-only affine, kernel and neighbor search in each encoder setting by .05165 ArguAna, .01334 NFCorpus and .08793 Android nDCG@10. The selected nonlinear completions improve source-coordinate reconstruction yet lose target relevance relative to the original affine rule. Revealing more exact teacher rows can likewise lower retrieval quality along a fixed acquisition order. These interventions separate information accuracy from retrieval value: a response matters through the query–document decisions it changes after pooling and readout. Retained priors provide a complementary source-null witness, and matched-readout comparisons show substantial remaining value in deep full-query computation above the offline table. The resulting account of query compression connects inherited information and offline teacher acquisition to the relevance earned by online computation. It motivates selecting teacher information for its effect on retrieval decisions.

title: Trust in artificial intelligence and AI-assisted social and civic decision-making among Arab youth: evidence from Egypt, Kuwait, and the UAE
container-title: Frontiers in Sociology
9c22c48dec77add12e18981832964c2f183e35aa.abstract: Introduction Trust in artificial intelligence (AI) increasingly shapes how young people evaluate information and public issues, yet evidence from Arab contexts remains limited. This study examined the socio-technical correlates of trust in AI and its association with AI-assisted social and civic decision-making among digitally engaged youth in Egypt, Kuwait, and the United Arab Emirates. Methods A cross-sectional online survey was conducted with 1,023 respondents aged 18–35 recruited through purposive, non-probability sampling. Confirmatory factor analysis (CFA), structural equation modeling (SEM), multi-group CFA, and competing full- versus partial-mediation models evaluated measurement and structural relationships. Results The partially mediated model fit significantly better than the fully mediated model, Δχ2(5) = 55.66, p &lt; 0.001. Institutional confidence (β = 0.303), AI literacy (β = 0.281), perceived usefulness (β = 0.242), and social influence (β = 0.107) were positively associated with trust in AI, and perceived risk was negatively associated (β = −0.106; all p &lt; 0.001). Trust was positively associated with AI-assisted decision-making (β = 0.412, p &lt; 0.001). Significant indirect associations through trust were observed for all five antecedents, while the direct perceived-risk path to AI-assisted decision-making was nonsignificant. Multi-group CFA supported metric and practical scalar measurement invariance across the three countries. Discussion The findings support a socio-technical account of AI trust in which technological, cognitive, institutional, and social conditions jointly relate to AI-assisted decision-making, with trust functioning as a central but not exclusive pathway. Given the cross-sectional, purposive design, findings are interpreted as associations rather than causal or nationally representative effects.

title: Lifestyle associations with hypertension and diabetes risk via metabolic function and physical indicators: a cross-sectional serial mediation model among community adults
container-title: Frontiers in Medicine
3f41b31659159fb1e18614bd7be034416f070ced.abstract: Objective To examine whether lifestyle is associated with hypertension and diabetes risk via sequential indirect pathways involving metabolic function and physical indicators among community adults. Methods A cross-sectional study was conducted among 6,178 community adults in Nanning, southern China. Structural equation modeling (SEM) was used to examine the direct and indirect associations among lifestyle, metabolic function, physical indicators, and disease risk. Bias-corrected bootstrap analyses with 5,000 resamples were performed to evaluate indirect associations. Results The model showed acceptable fit (CFI = 0.917, RMSEA = 0.048); the chi-square/df ratio (5.19) was elevated, as is common in samples of this size. Physical indicators exhibited the strongest direct association with disease risk ( β = 0.763, P &lt; 0.001), while metabolic function was also positively associated with disease risk ( β = 0.048, P = 0.010). Healthy lifestyle was associated with lower disease risk via indirect pathways involving physical indicators alone ( β = −0.360, P = 0.001) and via the sequential indirect pathway involving metabolic function and physical indicators ( β = −0.011, P = 0.021). For unhealthy lifestyle, indirect associations with higher disease risk were observed via metabolic function ( β = 0.003, P = 0.036) and physical indicators ( β = 0.092, P = 0.014), whereas the sequential indirect pathway was not statistically significant ( P = 0.104). Direct associations of lifestyle with disease risk were small in magnitude (| β | ≤ 0.035) and of limited clinical importance; only the direct association of unhealthy lifestyle reached statistical significance ( β = −0.035, P = 0.013). Conclusion In this cross-sectional sample, lifestyle was associated with hypertension and diabetes risk primarily via indirect pathways involving metabolic function and physical indicators. These findings should be interpreted as correlational and cannot establish causality. They highlight the importance of integrated lifestyle management and early metabolic risk assessment for the prevention of hypertension and diabetes in community settings.

title: A preliminary design framework for human-friendly AI interaction: grounded in anthropomorphism
container-title: Frontiers in Computer Science
46e7d698557d6ad9c8af0e26c30db1eac6a6fb1b.abstract: People converse with AI as they would with friends in daily life, collaborate with it, and form personalized relationships. In response to these emerging forms of interaction, this study clarifies the concept of Human-Friendly Interaction with conversational AI and develops the Human-Friendly AI Interaction Design Framework (HFAI-DF). This study positions anthropomorphism, a foundational phenomenon in human–AI interaction, as a theoretical bridge and reviews literature on anthropomorphism theory and related research on human cognition. On this basis, this study interpretively derives and organizes how anthropomorphism-inducing stimuli can be applied to AI agents, systematizing them into 30 AI behavioral items that enable human-friendly interaction. Subsequently, a survey was conducted and exploratory factor analysis performed to identify six dimensions as a preliminary structure for a design framework for AI’s human-friendly interaction. These dimensions are: Self-Aware Interaction, User-Adaptive Responsiveness Interaction, Context-Aware Reasoning Interaction, Socio-Emotional Interaction, Creative Collaboration Interaction, and Proactive Assistance Interaction. Within the evolving AI research landscape focused on interaction, this study extends the human-centered AI concept toward human-friendly interaction that operates in an organic manner comparable to human–human conversation, grounded in an understanding of human cognitive functioning. The proposed framework provides both AI providers and designers with an initial structure for shaping and improving the quality of human-friendly interaction.

title: Perceptions of AI in veterinary medicine: insights from students, faculty, and practicing veterinarians in Hong Kong
container-title: Frontiers in Veterinary Science
d5c0bfa269240bf48c6ea87f212741cd8f464ca1.abstract: Introduction As artificial intelligence (AI) transforms veterinary medicine, understanding stakeholder perceptions is crucial for its effective and responsible integration. To support the development of targeted educational and policy initiatives, this study aimed to evaluate the knowledge, attitudes, and practices regarding AI among Bachelor of Veterinary Medicine (BVM) students, PhD students, faculty, and practicing veterinarians in Hong Kong. Methods A cross-sectional online survey was conducted between December 2023 and March 2024 among BVM students, PhD students, and faculty members at City University of Hong Kong, and practicing veterinarians in Hong Kong who are members of the Hong Kong Veterinary Association. The survey assessed participants’ familiarity with AI, prior training, perceived benefits, concerns, and willingness to adopt AI in education and clinical practice. Descriptive and comparative analyses were performed to examine differences across stakeholder groups. Results Of 79 complete responses, nearly half (46.8%) reported unfamiliarity with AI concepts. Only 17.7% had received formal AI training, although 78.5% expressed interest in future AI education. Most respondents agreed that AI could enhance veterinary teaching and practice (83.5%) and 81.0% indicated they would likely incorporate AI tools into their work. Key perceived benefits included support for case-based learning (83.5%), virtual animal models for teaching (77.2%), and improved diagnostic accuracy (74.7%). However, 41.8% felt inadequately prepared to use AI. Major concerns included veterinarian accountability for AI-related harms (79.7%), lack of system flexibility (75.9%), and potential clinical inaccuracies (70.9%). Descriptively, practicing veterinarians reported the lowest AI tool use (66.7% had never used AI tools), the lowest preparedness (66.7% felt unprepared), and lower agreement with AI’s clinical benefits, although attitude differences were not statistically significant. Conclusion These exploratory findings suggest gaps in self-reported AI knowledge and differing perceptions of AI across veterinary stakeholder groups in Hong Kong, with AI use already widespread at the time of the survey despite limited formal training. While enthusiasm for AI integration is high, concerns about preparedness, accuracy, and ethical responsibility remain. Larger, multi-institutional studies are needed to confirm these patterns and to inform targeted training programs and ethical frameworks for safe and effective AI adoption in veterinary medicine.

title: Global classrooms: a tri-national study on AI integration by higher education students
container-title: Frontiers in Computer Science
4ce5be4917c40263b11f6c7ca8eabe77dd89211a.abstract: Collaborative cross-cultural learning expands higher education students’ (HES’) intercultural and language awareness, enhances their intercultural competence, has an impact on attitudes towards technology and AI as well as towards the course design and general satisfaction with the collaborative experience in the course. Furthermore, their self-perceived role in a digital setting and their self-perceived English proficiency were measured. The CoGIH Project encourages HES to explore the educational potential of artificial intelligence (AI) for learning and teaching in the school setting. A special focus is on the impact AI might have on the language learning process in English as a lingua franca in a multilingual setting. N = 113 HES, including both pre-service and in-service teachers as well as students preparing for educational administration, from five institutions in Israel, Germany, and Hungary collaborated in 14 international groups, representing five higher education institutions; n = 91 answered the questionnaires. Each group investigated the educational potential of a specific AI application and developed an AI-supported, results-based webpage. The study employed a multi-method research design. Questionnaires were administered to the HES to investigate their experiences at the beginning and at the end of the course. While quantitative data were used to investigate the research through the lens of descriptive statistics and correlations between factors, qualitative data from the open questions were analysed to enable a deeper understanding of HES’ perceptions, experiences and meanings, as well as their critical thinking. The study highlighted strengths and challenges in using AI for educational purposes. The HES valued clear structures, logical navigation, and creative, motivating tasks. Simultaneously, recurring issues included incomplete translations, limited depth of critical reflection, and weaknesses in visual design. In sum, even though AI can support creativity and language learning and teaching, individual learners’ reflections and authentic teacher guidance remain indispensable for meaningful learning.

title: AI-generated advertising in agricultural livestreaming and the auditability of disclosure regulation: a three-layer audit of public Douyin data from China
container-title: Frontiers in Sustainable Food Systems
c177ed750eb610123bd142c9d637834496b25555.abstract: Agricultural products are credence goods, and in livestreaming, the grower’s visible presence signals the price. China has required labeling of deep-synthesis content since January 2023 and, since 1 September 2025, of AI-generated synthetic content. Whether public platform data can verify compliance in a market where the authenticity premium is especially salient remains unclear, given that growers themselves sell produce. We audited three layers of public Chinese platform data: 189 policy snippets, 19 accounts retrieved by AI technical terms, and 455 unique authors retrieved by crop names. In the one policy coding field with complete intercoder agreement ( κ = 1.000), only 6 of 189 snippets name authenticity as a farmer asset. Retrieval by technical terms returns intermediaries: 13 of 19 accounts sell AI tools or tutorials, and none discloses using AI to sell its own produce. Among AI-announcing cases retrieved by crop-name queries, an expanded text-field detector validated at 94.7% recall flags 10 of 455 authors: seven supply-side or service-provider accounts, one incidental non-agricultural mention, and two product-query artifacts; none discloses grower own-use of AI livestreaming. Checks of API-exposed platform metadata for all 575 video records and cover images for 472 records found no platform-side AI label or visible AI/AIGC/statutory AI-generated notice. AI was announced primarily by accounts that sell, service, or discuss AI, rather than by produce-selling grower accounts. No grower own-use disclosure appears in either audited slice: 0 of 19 technical-keyword accounts and 0 of 455 transaction-query authors. The zero admits two readings that the audited surface cannot separate: smallholders do not use these tools, making the requirement inert for them, or they use them without disclosure. No label-reading instrument applied to the audited surface can decide between them, because such inspection observes announcement rather than use. Platforms and regulators may hold backend data unavailable to an external audit. If the theoretically derived authenticity-penalty mechanism holds, disclosure would impose an uneven cost, falling more heavily on growers than on intermediaries. The observed pattern is consistent with this hypothesis but does not establish it.

title: Mapping the knowledge domain of internal control and information technology: a bibliometric analysis using CiteSpace
container-title: Digital Transformation and Society
a772b98e74c00ef1071ae562e2fb8abebdfacc76.abstract: Purpose This study maps the knowledge domain of internal control and information technology (IC-IT) and traces how the intellectual foundations, thematic evolution and future research agenda of IC have evolved alongside digital technologies. The theoretical implications of these descriptive patterns are discussed for future theory development. Design/methodology/approach Using CiteSpace, the study analyses 1,222 publications and 43,092 cited references from the Web of Science Core Collection for 2005–2025. It conducts reference co-citation, author, country and institutional collaboration, cited journal, keyword co-occurrence and subject category analyses. Findings The findings show that IC-IT research has evolved from compliance-oriented IC, risk management and internal audit toward technology-enabled and intelligent control systems. The field is grounded in accounting, auditing, information systems and management, with emerging themes including artificial intelligence, machine learning, blockchain, cloud computing, access control, audit automation and real-time monitoring. Originality/value This study conceptualizes IC-IT as an integrated interdisciplinary domain and provides the first full-domain bibliometric mapping that crosses four traditionally isolated research streams. It identifies a three-stage evolution from compliance-oriented control toward technology-embedded and intelligent governance, showing how digital technologies are reorienting internal-control research toward new objectives, mechanisms, audit evidence and accountability systems.

title: Examining the digital divide for persons with aphasia: an evaluation of the accessibility of Australian health and government websites
container-title: Universal Access in the Information Society
4be13a3ee0740efc0d336a5df317ee9549f8f26c.abstract: Abstract Purpose The Internet has transformed the way we access healthcare and information, yet barriers to digital inclusion remain for persons with disabilities. Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) promote equitable digital access for persons with disabilities, however, guideline adherence is inconsistent, and standards do not fully address the needs of individuals with communication disabilities. This study aimed to investigate whether high-use Australian health and government websites meet: (1) minimum (WCAG 2.2 Level AA) and comprehensive (WCAG 2.2 Level AAA) web accessibility standards, and (2) Novel Level of Success Criteria for persons with aphasia (communication disability). Methods Eleven Australian healthcare and government websites were selected based on usage. The homepage and one internal webpage of each website were evaluated using Accessible Web RAMP™. Each website was assessed for: (1) compliance with WCAG 2.2 Level AA and Level AAA standards, and (2) performance against Novel Level of Success Criteria for persons with aphasia. Results At WCAG 2.2 Level AA, 7 (64%) homepages and 8 (73%) internal webpages were not fully compliant. At Level AAA, 10 (91%) homepages and 11 (100%) internal webpages demonstrated violations, presenting potential accessibility challenges for persons with aphasia. Performance on the Novel Criteria demonstrated a similar trend in non-conformance. However, some websites demonstrated a reduced total number of violations. The majority of issues were concentrated within the perceivable principle. Conclusion A high proportion of selected high-use Australian health and government websites presented accessibility non-compliances across all levels of criteria, including the Novel Criteria. Despite some websites demonstrating fewer violations against the Novel Criteria, accessibility barriers remain prevalent. This highlights the importance of improving inclusive practices, strengthening regulatory compliances, and integrating cognitive and communication disabilities into digital accessibility standards.

title: Opportunity or Uncertainty? Understanding Pre-IPO Information Environment, Investor Preferences, and Early Market Dynamics
container-title: Business Management Journal
1c718ab277349484e4bab356d60aa533e79d50a7.abstract: Research on Initial Public Offerings (IPOs) has predominantly focused on post-listing outcomes, such as underpricing, stock returns, and long-term market performance. Comparatively, the relationships among the pre-IPO information environment, prospective investor preferences, investor participation, and early market dynamics warrant more integrated examination. This study examines the relationships among these dimensions in the Indonesian capital market. It employs a qualitative descriptive approach with a multiple-case study design involving six IPOs in the July 2026 issuance wave on the Indonesia Stock Exchange. Secondary data were obtained from IPO prospectuses, official exchange disclosures, investor preference polls conducted during the offering period, oversubscription statistics, and stock prices during the first seven trading days. The analysis uses a four-stage framework informed by Organizational Information Processing Theory (OIPT) as a descriptive analytical device to compare information characteristics, investor preferences, subscription participation, and early price movements. The findings reveal substantial variation across cases, with oversubscription ranging from 14 times for EMMI to 709.93 times for PRDL. PRDL's share price increased from IDR 120 at the IPO to IDR 386 on the seventh trading day, whereas EMMI closed at IDR 460 against an IPO price of IDR 470. These differences indicate heterogeneity in stated investor preferences, subscription demand, and early price movements. However, the available aggregate and documentary data are insufficient to establish individual information-processing mechanisms or causal relationships among disclosure, preferences, subscription demand, and stock prices. This study contributes an OIPT-informed descriptive analytical framework for comparing these dimensions in an integrated manner and identifying directions for further research in emerging capital markets.

title: Human-Governed Multi-Agent AI for Biological Hypothesis Generation: An Evidence-Grounded Framework Using JUMP Cell Painting Profiles
7a2bcb64973bd56bae183bb619c26a0d3a9a5a47.abstract: Abstract High-dimensional cellular phenotypes can motivate biological hypotheses, but similarity alone cannot establish mechanism or causal validity. DISCOVERY-AGENT links exploratory JUMP Cell Painting evidence with evidence-grounded hypothesis generation, independent critique and bounded human-review routing. An initial 65-record CRISPR/ORF analysis across nine gene–modality tests found four FDR-significant CRISPR plate-level associations (AKT1, BRCA1, MTOR and TP53), none among evaluated ORF genes. A distinct later cross-source compound-identity benchmark used 614 morphological features and achieved AUROC 0.6142 on 1,250 held-out compounds with training-only preprocessing; this is identity discrimination, not mechanism-of-action classification. Three structured hypotheses underwent LLM critique and revision, while eleven gene-pair evidence assessments yielded no FDR-significant mechanistic finding (minimum q = 0.2037). Archived governance checks passed 1,021/1,021 predefined tests; nevertheless, the initial live-agent run contained two execution errors among five cases, with both cases responding on fresh retest. These findings demonstrate feasibility of auditable evidence processing and modest cross-source morphology signal, not validated autonomous discovery, prospective safety, or completed expert review. The work delineates practical requirements for independent biological validation and reproducible scientific agents.

title: Teachers’ attitudes and behavioural intentions towards AI integration in Chinese higher education: a qualitative interview study
container-title: Frontiers in Psychology
c6fe4330bbf5fd4fe3ac0771cb768c511236b747.abstract: Introduction The rapid expansion of generative AI has intensified scholarly and policy debate over its role in higher education, yet university teachers’ attitudes towards its integration remain complex and context-dependent. This study explores how university teachers perceive, experience, and respond to AI integration in their teaching. Guided primarily by the three-component attitude model and informed by the technology acceptance model and the theory of planned behaviour, the study examines cognitive appraisals, affective responses, behavioural intentions, and perceived support needs. Methods The study draws on semi-structured interviews with 14 university teachers from four higher education institutions in China. The interview data were analysed using codebook-informed thematic analysis combining deductive and inductive coding. Results The findings indicate that teachers generally perceive AI as a supportive rather than substitutive educational tool, valuing it for improving efficiency, supporting lesson preparation, and enriching pedagogical design. Emotional responses varied from enthusiasm and a sense of accomplishment to caution, neutrality, and, in some cases, declining satisfaction. Across the interviews, teachers’ primary concerns centred less on their own replacement than on the perceived risks of inappropriate AI use for students’ independent thinking, reasoning, originality, and authentic understanding. Teachers’ intentions to adopt AI were therefore conditional and bounded, shaped by pedagogical purpose, disciplinary context, student readiness, and the need to maintain teacher control. Teachers also emphasised that sustainable AI integration requires more than general encouragement, calling instead for AI literacy development, discipline-sensitive support, specialised tools, and enabling institutional infrastructure. Discussion Overall, these findings extend contextual understandings of teachers’ AI acceptance by showing how adoption intentions are pedagogically negotiated and highlight the importance of supporting professional judgement and students’ independent thinking in higher education.

title: Automated assessment of healthcare de-escalation communication skills in a conversational AI virtual reality simulation
container-title: Frontiers in Digital Health
9bc424b8b0ee6bc350b4296b68f692e3f29c8284.abstract: Introduction Digital health training environments increasingly require scalable methods for assessing communication skills in realistic, interactive scenarios. This paper presents a comparative study of automated assessment approaches within a conversational AI virtual reality simulation designed for verbal de-escalation training. Methods A total of 20 nursing students completed the simulation, where their spoken responses were captured and converted to text through a speech-to-text system, and were evaluated across 11 de-escalation competencies. The evaluation compared three fine-tuned deep learning models (BERT, RoBERTa, and XLNet) with a modified RATAS, a rubric-driven framework that leverages large language models. Two experiments were conducted: one using controlled 100-item validation datasets for each section, and another using the real-world responses collected during the user study. Results On the validation datasets, the deep learning models achieved the highest performance, with RoBERTa obtaining an average accuracy of 0.9927, followed by BERT at 0.9900 and XLNet at 0.9790, while RATAS achieved 0.8554. On the student-response dataset, performance decreased for all approaches, with RoBERTa obtaining 0.8590 accuracy, RATAS 0.8181, BERT 0.8000, and XLNet 0.7681. Discussion These results suggest that transformer-based models perform best under controlled conditions, whereas RATAS demonstrated stability in grading across different dataset types. These preliminary findings support the feasibility of integrating deep learning and rubric-driven LLM-based automated assessment approaches for communication and de-escalation training in nursing education.

title: Uneven automation: comparing authorship anxiety and generative AI use among art and design undergraduate students
container-title: Frontiers in Psychology
8942b2ac014d5d2bac7e05011f209f96a5fce870.abstract: Art and design education expects students to develop a sense of authorship over original work, but generative AI (GenAI) complicates how students understand and claim that authorship. This study examined whether these experiences differ across creative fields through a mixed-methods design. The survey included 2,441 GenAI-using students from seven field categories at 33 art and design institutions in China and assessed authorship anxiety, creative agency, perceived usefulness, dependence on GenAI, and frequency of use. The quantitative analysis first examined variation across all seven categories and then compared fine art with the five applied design fields. Interview data from 22 survey participants were also examined thematically. The main findings include that (1) authorship anxiety did not differ significantly across the seven categories or between fine art and pooled design; the latter comparison met the equivalence criterion at ±d = 0.20, but not at tighter bounds; (2) clearer differences emerged in how students used GenAI. Compared with fine-art students, design students considered GenAI more useful and used it more frequently; (3) across the interviews, most students described authorship as retaining control over the creative idea while delegating parts of its execution to GenAI. Specifically, fine-art students often grounded authorship in embodied making and human imperfection, whereas design students placed greater emphasis on judgement, selection, and control. We call this pattern uneven automation: concern about authorship was broadly shared, but students in different fields responded to GenAI in different ways, potentially reflecting the varying labour-market pressures surrounding their disciplines.

title: Digital transformation, traceability, and supply chain resilience in food manufacturing SMEs: a review of AI, blockchain-IoT, and institutional mechanisms
container-title: Frontiers in Sustainable Food Systems
c0821ee379eb16d2e0252633d6030dd152fbd833.abstract: Food supply chains in China face persistent challenges of food safety risks, inadequate transparency, and supply disruptions, with food manufacturing small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) disproportionately vulnerable due to limited resources and non-standardized internal processes. Digital transformation encompassing artificial intelligence (AI), blockchain, Internet of Things (IoT), and digital twin technologies is increasingly regarded as a strategic solution to strengthen supply chain resilience, yet the organizational and institutional conditions under which these digital investments translate into tangible resilience improvements for food manufacturing SMEs remain poorly understood. This review conducts a PRISMA 2020-compliant systematic review and thematic synthesis of 40 multidisciplinary sources spanning the food safety, supply chain management, and information systems literatures. Drawing on Dynamic Capabilities Theory and Institutional Theory, we propose an integrative conceptual framework comprising six research propositions, in which traceability capability acts as a food-safety-specific mediating mechanism linking digital transformation to supply chain resilience, while regulatory stringency moderates the strength of this indirect pathway. A central argument of this framework is that deploying blockchain, IoT, or AI hardware does not itself constitute traceability capability the institutional and organisational conditions under which digital tools are adopted determine whether firms build substantive traceability capability or engage in symbolic compliance without genuine food safety governance improvement. Three key contributions distinguish this framework: conceptualizing traceability capability as a distinct dynamic capability rather than a generic digitalization mechanism; directing analytical focus explicitly toward food manufacturing SMEs, a population largely overlooked in existing large-firm panel studies; and introducing regulatory stringency as a first-stage moderator within a moderated mediation structure. Critical research gaps are identified, including the absence of SME-calibrated digital transformation measurement instruments, the lack of a validated multi-item traceability capability scale, and a complete empirical vacuum for testing the proposed moderated mediation model in food manufacturing SME contexts. This review provides a structured future research agenda for scholars and delivers actionable insights for practitioners and policymakers seeking to direct digital technology investments toward improved food safety governance in China’s food manufacturing sector.

title: Human-in-the-loop semantic learning analytics for assessing moral-value reasoning in university AI ethics education
container-title: Frontiers in Psychology
4c153cd19693204269d4536c8e62024e2ea30575.abstract: Introduction University AI ethics education addresses fairness, privacy, accountability, transparency, human autonomy, and academic integrity, but the semantic structure of students' moral-value reasoning and its connection to responsible solutions remain insufficiently characterized. This study examined a human-in-the-loop semantic learning analytics framework for task-specific moral-value reasoning. Methods Ninety science and engineering graduate students completed an online explicit-reflective AI ethics module in a one-group pre–post multimethod study without a control group. Assessments comprised an AI ethics knowledge test, a perceived-awareness scale, and open-ended ethical reasoning tasks. Expert annotations informed transformer-based multi-label coding, descriptive value coverage and balance metrics, problem–solution coupling, and baseline-only nested cross-validated prediction of subsequent raw problem-solving change. Results Within-participant pre–post increases were observed in ethical knowledge, perceived moral-value awareness, actual ethical awareness, problem–solving skills, value coverage, value balance, and problem–solution coupling. Automated semantic coding achieved participant-grouped cross-validated macro-F1 = 0.83 (95% CI [0.78, 0.87]; micro-F1 = 0.86; macro-AUPRC = 0.82). The baseline-only prediction model yielded cross-validated R 2 = 0.30 (95% CI [0.11, 0.45]) for subsequent raw problem-solving change. Discussion Expert-supervised semantic analytics can characterize value representation and issue–solution reasoning in AI ethics assessments. Coverage and balance describe response structure rather than moral quality. The absence of a control group, repeated use of one scenario, and modest sample size preclude causal and broad trait-level conclusions.

title: How does family intellectual-cultural orientation correlate with adolescents’ wellbeing literacy? An empirical analysis based on a chain mediation model
container-title: Frontiers in Psychiatry
3f55b176ae58ae4bd9a204671838105abdc5e700.abstract: Introduction Wellbeing literacy(WL), as a promising emerging concept, offers a possible route for addressing global adolescent mental-health problems. Family intellectual-cultural orientation(FICO) shows a significant statistical association with wellbeing literacy, but the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Methods This study used convenience sampling to survey 868 adolescents aged 12–18 years and employed a serial mediation model (PROCESS Model 6) to examine the indirect effects of positive psychological capital and personal growth initiative in the association between family intellectual-cultural orientation and well-being literacy. Results Family intellectual-cultural orientation was significantly correlated with well-being literacy (effect = 0.1151, p &lt; 0.001). The total indirect effect was significant (effect = 0.2414, 95% CI [0.1893, 0.2975]), accounting for 67.7% of the total effect. The separate mediating effects of positive psychological capital (effect = 0.1254, 95% CI [0.0839, 0.1718]) and personal growth initiative (effect = 0.0417, 95% CI [0.0183, 0.0710]), as well as their chain mediating effect (effect = 0.0743, 95% CI [0.0463, 0.1063]), were all significant. Discussion These correlational patterns reveal that family intellectual-cultural orientation is statistically linked to adolescents’ wellbeing literacy via the correlational chain of positive psychological capital(PPC) and personal growth initiative(PGI), which aligns with core assumptions of the resource-gain spiral mechanism proposed by conservation of resources theory. The findings provide empirical evidence for family-education interventions and school-based mental-health education.

title: Perceived AI literacy and TPACK in pre-service teacher education: mediating roles of perceived usefulness, ease of use, and value in blended learning
container-title: Frontiers in Psychology
1bad51d2ab1c081fcbf1788c8c81f98f9ce0044c.abstract: Background The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into blended learning requires pre-service teachers to develop AI-related competencies and the ability to integrate technology into pedagogy. This study examines how perceived AI literacy and technological pedagogical content knowledge (TPACK) are associated with deep learning through perceived usefulness, perceived ease of use, and perceived value of AI use. Methods A cross-sectional survey was completed by 423 pre-service teachers enrolled in blended learning courses at a university in China. Data were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM), with covariance-based structural equation modeling and fuzzy-set qualitative comparative analysis (fsQCA) used as complementary robustness and configurational analyses. Results Perceived usefulness, perceived ease of use, and perceived value of AI use significantly mediated the relationships between the two competencies and deep learning. All six indirect pathways were significant in both the PLS-SEM and covariance-based SEM analyses. The fsQCA revealed an equifinal and asymmetric structure: multiple, partly substitutable conditions were sufficient for high deep learning, and no single condition was necessary for either high or low deep learning. Conclusions The findings integrate the technology acceptance model and expectancy-value theory to explain how pre-service teachers' competencies and perceptions relate to deep learning in AI-enhanced blended environments. Teacher education should support technical competence alongside positive perceptions of AI's utility, usability, and value. Because the measures were self-reported and collected cross-sectionally at one university, the findings are interpreted as associational and configurational rather than causal.

title: Effectiveness of an AI-Based Educational Video Generator in Enhancing Oral Health Knowledge and Behavior Among Children: A Randomized Controlled Trial
container-title: Al-Rafidain Journal of Medical Sciences ( ISSN 2789-3219 )
025217a90eae33a9efbb4f3e4378042549e3202e.abstract: Background: Artificial intelligence (AI) is a new innovation that presents an opportunity for oral health education in children. Objective: To evaluate the effectiveness of an AI-assisted educational video versus standardized in-person oral health education for children regarding oral health knowledge and behaviors. Methods: This randomized controlled trial included 300 children aged 10-12 years (n=150 per group), both boys and girls, who were divided into AI video and standardized face-to-face oral health education groups. Baseline and 2-week follow-up evaluations were conducted for knowledge scores, four behavioral items, and the Silness and Löe Plaque Index. The internal consistency of the knowledge scale was checked (Cronbach's α=0.79). Wilcoxon signed-rank and Mann–Whitney U tests were the primary non-parametric tests used for statistical evaluations, with a median, (IQR), and effect size r provided. Chi-square tests with a Bonferroni adjustment at α=0.0125 were used to evaluate behavioral items. Results: There were significant enhancements in intra-group knowledge (p<0.0001 for both groups; r=0.663 for AI; r=0.345 for Control). The clinical efficacy was similar for both strategies with significant reduction of intra-group plaque (AI: p< 0.001, r= 0.425; Control: p< 0.001, r= 0.331), but no inter-group difference at the end of the intervention (p= 0.608; r= 0.030). In the conventional group, the utilization of dental floss was significantly improved (p=0.0056), and no other behaviors showed significant improvement across groups. Conclusions: The AI-assisted educational video demonstrated better knowledge retention than the standardized face-to-face oral health education, achieved similar clinical plaque reduction, and can be easily scaled for pediatric preventive dentistry.

title: Comparison of ChatGPT-Generated Patient Information on Testicular Cancer Across Two Assessment Periods: Clinical Accuracy, Response Quality, and Citation Support
container-title: Urology Research and Practice
5a59524914f46c2d4fec2bd6dd305835ce148be8.abstract: Objective: The aim of this study was to compare clinical accuracy, response quality, and citation characteristics of ChatGPT-generated testicular cancer information across 2 assessments 20 months apart. Methods: Sixty-one patient-oriented questions derived from European Association of Urology (EAU) Patient Information were submitted to ChatGPT-4o in December 2024 and repeated unchanged using ChatGPT-5.6 Luna in August 2026. Two urologists independently assessed accuracy against contemporaneous EAU guidelines and rated quality using the Global Quality Score (GQS) and modified DISCERN (mDISCERN). Citation quantity, source quality, and source-to-claim support were evaluated. Only the first response was retained; repeated-generation variability was not assessed. Results: Fully accurate responses were 86.9% (53/61) in 2024 and 93.4% (57/61) in 2026 (P = .125). Of 8 clinically relevant inaccuracies in 2024, 4 were corrected, 3 improved but remained misleading, and 1 persisted. GQS increased from 3.75 ± 0.77 to 4.82 ± 0.41 and mDISCERN from 30.37 ± 4.65 to 36.80 ± 1.93 (both P < .001). Citations per response decreased from 5.97 ± 3.53 to 4.79 ± 1.19 (P = .042), while high-quality unique sources increased from 77.4% to 96.9% (P < .001). Fully supported sources were 80.1% and 86.4% (P = .050); 6 sources (2.6%) in 2026 did not support the claims. Conclusion: Response quality and the use of high-quality sources were greater in 2026, whereas changes in clinical accuracy and source-to-claim support were less clear. Clinically meaningful errors persisted in guideline-sensitive topics. Because different model versions and interfaces were assessed, the findings represent model- and interface-specific snapshots, not a controlled head-to-head comparison. Cite this article as: Ekenci BY, Altan M. Comparison of ChatGPT-generated patient information on testicular cancer across two assessment periods: Clinical accuracy, response quality, and citation support. Urol Res Pract. 2026;52, doi: 10.5152/ tud.2026.26067
