title: Improving Learner Performance Through Score Based Analysis on a Gamified AI Driven Cybersecurity Learning Platform
d2b1981b0d01f6ee261a12a86c8c602586119c26.abstract: Abstract This study examines whether structured engagement with instructional content improves learner performance on Cyber Security Academy, an AI-driven, gamified cybersecurity learning platform. Activity logs covering 1,500 completed assessments from users in ten Anglophone and Francophone countries were analyzed by comparing learners who consulted the lessons and completed the full learning pathway (n = 900) with those who engaged only partially with the platform (n = 600). Group differences were tested with Welch's t-test, the Mann Whitney U test, one-way ANOVA, Spearman correlations, and Cohen's d as a measure of effect size. Learners who read the lessons before assessment obtained a mean score of 71.27 % versus 60.41 % for non-readers (Δ = +10.86 points; t(1192) = 12.21; p < 0.001; d = 0.650; 95 % CI [9.12, 12.60]), committed fewer errors (2.50 vs. 4.85; d = -1.069), and responded faster (9.85 vs. 12.69 minutes; d = -0.807), indicating greater fluency of cognitive processing. The effect decreased monotonically with age (d = 1.205 for learners aged 13 and under; d = 0.387 for those 22 and over) and with digital literacy (d = 1.434 for beginners; d = 0.524 for experts), while remaining positive in all ten countries. These findings indicate that structured, AI-personalized, and gamified learning environments substantially enhance cybersecurity learning outcomes, particularly for younger and less experienced users.

title: Search-based agents outperform reinforcement learning in Dahal Jeet, a Nepaliimperfect-information card game
3f9f3d6a8996de2c0c8dd95436138f4cc9bcab48.abstract: Abstract Dahal Jeet is a four-player partnership card game played daily across the Terai- Madhesh region of Nepal, in which only the four tens score. Its objective is lexicographic rather than additive: a majority of tens decides most hands, trick count the rest. The game belongs to the documented Mendikot branch of the Court Piece family, matching Mendikot on 21 of 26 compared features, but the Nepali variant has no published rule description, and the indexed literature returns one paper on the entire family. We contribute a formal specification of the ruleset, drawn from the first author’s own play across seven districts, and a computational study built on it. 26 agents spanning hand-written heuristics, metaheuristic tuning, determinized search and seven learning families are compared across 325 pairings under duplicate-deal protocols with bootstrap intervals and family-wise error control. Search dominates: information-set Monte Carlo tree search leads and no learner reaches a tuned heuristic. An exact doubledummy solver shows search converts 0.923 of theoretically won endgames against 0.810 for the best heuristic. A minimal state encoding outperforms a rich handdesigned one, every deterministic heuristic is exploitable by a search that knows its policy, and the deal alone explains up to 0.391 of outcome variance.

title: AI Labour Rights Awareness and Career Adaptation Confidence among Respondents in Bangladesh
4bebd9cda335afcb1b14dbb90e41e4c4857a6c33.abstract: Abstract Artificial intelligence changes both the skills used at work and the conditions under which employment decisions are made. Awareness of these changes does not necessarily coincide with confidence in adapting a career. This study examines that distinction in 385 adult, AI-aware survey records from Bangladesh, including 238 law students and 61 respondents classified as law graduates. Five statements separately assess awareness of workplace rights and responsibilities, recognition of protection from unfair automated decisions, reported complementary skill development, adaptation confidence and the perceived preparedness benefit of understanding labour issues. Analyses combine full response distributions, joint endorsement patterns, paired comparisons, ordinal correlations and an exploratory proportional-odds model. Recognition of the need for protection was endorsed by 79.2%, compared with 48.8% endorsing adaptation confidence, a paired difference of 30.4 percentage points (95% bootstrap interval 23.9–36.6). General rights awareness and skill development had small positive ordinal associations with confidence. In the adjusted ordinal model, their odds ratios were 1.30 (95% interval 1.04–1.61; Holm p = 0.038) and 1.40 (1.09–1.79; Holm p = 0.024) respectively. The protection-recognition estimate was less certain, although the two awareness coefficients were not demonstrably different. The findings distinguish rights recognition, reported action and confidence rather than establish a causal awareness-to-adaptability pathway. They support evaluating legal-literacy education alongside practical career tasks and institutional safeguards. The mixed sample, study-specific single items, undocumented recruitment and fieldwork dates, and source-documentation limitations constrain inference. A subsequent study should use verified graduate eligibility, independent legal-knowledge assessments and longitudinal career outcomes.

title: Measurement-driven aberration calibration and a Fisher-information theory of optical identifiability for photon-limited fluorescence microscopy
container-title: Optical Engineering
61fe829e8f0fc65892c5e611d11b647586b85dcb.abstract: Optical aberrations corrupt the point spread function (PSF) of a fluorescence microscope and silently degrade every downstream restoration, yet their measurement typically requires fluorescent beads, a wavefront sensor, or a training dataset. Here, we describe a measurement-driven calibration framework that estimates Zernike aberration coefficients directly from photon measurements of the sample itself, with no wavefront sensor, bead calibration, or training data: a differentiable scalar-diffraction forward model (Zernike pupil phase → PSF → Poisson photon counts) is fitted by maximum likelihood, and its Fisher information matrix quantifies how accurately the aberration parameters can be identified. The intensity PSF is exactly invariant to reversing the sign of the whole even-parity coefficient subvector (defocus, astigmatism, spherical) so that the sign is unidentifiable from a single frame, whereas the odd-parity coefficients (coma) are exempt from this degeneracy: the single-frame Fisher information of even-parity modes vanishes as |θ|2 when the aberration tends to zero, whereas odd-parity modes (coma) retain nonzero first-order information, a finite floor for the structures tested. This parity-resolved law is verified numerically over a factor of 300 in aberration magnitude, and defocus-diversity frames hold a constant information floor over the tested mode subspace, restoring identifiability at the 10−3-waves scale. The same framework predicts where information-limited breakdown occurs: across two real fluorescence structures and four aberration modes, the empirical estimation error tracks CRB; in 11 of the 12 measurable cells, the empirical crossing agrees with the Cramér–Rao prediction within a factor of three in either direction, and the remaining cell, an extrapolation below the scanned budget range, agrees within a factor of four (single-frame even-parity modes are scored over their equivalence class, one globally ambiguous sign for the even subvector); at a fixed total photon budget, diversity frames reach a given precision with 2.2 to 5.0 times fewer photons than a single focal frame for the degeneracy-limited modes (defocus, astigmatism). Validated on real fluorescence content (BioSR endoplasmic reticulum and microtubules, BioTISR clathrin-coated pits) and on deformable-mirror aberration ground truth (CoCoA beads), the differential z-stack estimate of the three mirror-applied modes (0.07 to 0.10 waves, exact axial-propagation frames) agrees with the applied coefficients to a mean absolute error of 0.023 waves and shows a two-dimensional blind failure onset near 0.09 waves root-mean-square (RMS) aberration. The structure-known axial-propagation working range extends well past the 2D one: no failure is observed at 0.15 waves RMS or below (0 of 17 runs), the first stochastic failures appear at ≈0.20 waves RMS (1 of 10 runs at each of the three transition levels), and failure dominates by 0.25 waves RMS (three of five cold starts at that level). What ends the axial range is a transition of the likelihood landscape, not an information shortage: at 0.25 waves RMS, the estimator can lock onto a near-sign-reversed basin, whereas the Cramér–Rao bound there is still four times below the target, and the Fisher matrix of the wrong solution is itself well conditioned, so the local bound cannot certify global uniqueness. Calibration reliability is therefore assessed by two complementary gates computed from the measurement itself: a Fisher gate for local precision and a restart-consensus gate, testing whether independent restarts agree on a single basin. Within the accepted regime, the calibrated PSF restores images to the oracle-PSF Richardson–Lucy level (within 0.05 dB of peak signal-to-noise ratio, PSNR) and improves spot-counting F1 from 0.03–0.04 to 0.73–0.75 in two of three tested noise realizations (the third leaves the calibrated working range).

title: WEB-BASED EMPLOYEE PAYROLL MANAGEMENT INFORMATION SYSTEM WITH MANAGERIAL APPROVAL FEATURES AT BANG AWAL RESTAURANT
container-title: Simtek : jurnal sistem informasi dan teknik komputer
ac9ebe2ac389f9b3a40619d0a41e90cf8ed1bbd9.abstract: Managing attendance and payroll manually carries the risk of delayed data consolidation, calculation errors regarding salary components, and inadequate control over the validity of employee attendance records. This study aims to design and implement a web-based employee payroll management system for Rumah Makan Bang Awal, featuring managerial approval workflows and geolocation-based attendance verification. The system was developed using PHP and MySQL, employing an object-oriented design approach. System modeling utilized the Unified Modeling Language (UML)—including use case, sequence, and activity diagrams—alongside database relationship designs. The system integrates the management of data regarding employees, branches, positions, shifts, attendance, leave (including sick leave), loans, overtime components and deductions, salary submissions, managerial approvals, and payroll history. Implementation results demonstrate that previously fragmented payroll administration processes have been consolidated into a single web-based application, while geolocation features facilitate location verification during attendance logging. This research has produced an integrated system that supports the entire payroll workflow, from attendance recording to salary approval. Further research involving structured functional testing and user acceptance evaluation is required to quantitatively assess the system's reliability.

title: Regulating AI-Generated Inventions in Tanzania: A Comparative Analysis of BRELA and South Africa’s CIPC
container-title: East African Journal of Law and Ethics
97d91fe2e65b9b432b752d3e2552b57b2f5ca94f.abstract: Artificial intelligence systems now produce technical solutions with little or no human contribution to the inventive step, and the DABUS applications filed by Dr Stephen Thaler have tested whether patent law can accommodate an inventor that is not a person. Courts and offices in the United Kingdom, the United States, Europe, Australia and Germany have refused, while South Africa’s Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC) published the grant of a patent naming DABUS as inventor in July 2021. This article asks whether Tanzania’s Business Registrations and Licensing Agency (BRELA) could follow that example under the Patents (Registration) Act, Cap 217, and, if not, what reform is required. Using doctrinal analysis and functional comparison, it finds that the two statutes are closer than is usually assumed: neither defines ‘inventor’, and both require an applicant who is not the inventor to show a right derived from the inventor. The decisive difference is administrative. The South African grant followed a formalities-only check in which, on the published record, the applicant’s entitlement was not tested, leaving validity to revocation proceedings. Section 25(7) and (8) of Cap 217, by contrast, require the Registrar to examine every request for compliance with section 18(3) and (4) and to reject one that is not corrected. An application naming DABUS would therefore fail at the formal stage, and one naming a human who did not devise the invention would be open to invalidation under section 64(2)(d). BRELA cannot reproduce the CIPC outcome by discretion. The article recommends, in order of priority, statements of practice on AI-assisted inventions, revised forms, a statutory definition of inventor and, after regional consultation through ARIPO and the East African Community, a deliberate legislative choice on whether AI-generated inventions should be protected.

title: A Hybrid Convolutional Recurrent Neural Model for Noise Detection and Automated Calibration of Medical Devices via Molecular Vibration Analysis
518557eedb6ff36ea9b47c24553d6afd51c850c8.abstract: Abstract Accurate noise detection and calibration are essential for maintaining the measurement reliability of medical devices. This study proposes a hybrid convolutional recurrent neural network (CRNN) framework for noise detection and automated calibration of ventilators and electrocardiogram (ECG) machines using molecular vibration analysis. A molecular vibration model was developed to characterize mechanical vibration, electromagnetic interference, and environmental conduction noise, achieving an average noise classification accuracy of 96.2%. The proposed CRNN with hybrid attention maintained 91.5% accuracy under low signal-to-noise conditions. A deep deterministic policy gradient-based calibration strategy was subsequently employed to optimize calibration parameters automatically, reducing calibration time by 72.5% and improving calibration accuracy by 78.5% compared with conventional methods. After calibration, the average relative errors were 1.9% for ventilator tidal-volume measurements and 0.92% for QRS-complex amplitude measurements in ECG devices. Cross-device validation achieved 94.3% accuracy across different equipment brands. The results demonstrate that integrating molecular vibration analysis, hybrid deep learning, and automated calibration provides an effective approach for reliable noise detection and precision calibration of medical devices.

title: Editorial: generative AI and the small business frontier – charting pathways toward meaningful social impact
container-title: Journal of Social Impact in Business Research
c4b06f07519c890d4aa7881d2f5de009595df712.abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine how small and medium-sized enterprises can leverage generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) to create social impact, by developing a multidimensional framework linking GenAI adoption with social-value creation. Design/methodology/approach This editorial adopts a conceptual synthesis approach, that integrates insights from the special-issue papers with emerging research and identifies principal domains of social impact. Findings Social impact is not a property of GenAI but a contingent outcome of how it is applied and adopted. While firms may have similar GenAI potentialities across various impact domains, success is dependent on human, organisational, sectoral and institutional contexts. Practical implications This editorial provides a framework for assessing where GenAI can support social-value creation whilst managing ethical, organisational and workforce risks. Impact accrues through organisational processes rather than through adoption itself. Originality/value The social impact of GenAI is extended beyond productivity and efficiency and positioned as a multidimensional and contingent outcome of technology adoption. A four-element framework links GenAI capability, organisational mechanisms, enabling and constraining conditions and stakeholder outcomes, which then informs a research agenda.

title: The Role of Broadcast Media in Assessing Government Agricultural Development Strategies in Nigeria's Post-Subsidy Era
container-title: RESEARCH JOURNAL OF MASS COMMUNICATION AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY
c0972afdb7291129673675046aa5c2289aa69e8c.abstract: This study evaluated the effective communication as a key to agribusiness management and sustainable development in Nigeria. The development media theory was adopted as a theoretical framework. This study adopted a qualitative research method to explore how broadcast media assess and communicate government agricultural development strategies in Nigeria’s postsubsidy era. The population consists of three key stakeholder groups: 36 farmers, 40 media personnel, and 47 policymakers across selected states with significant agricultural activities. A purposive sampling technique was employed to select 30 participants, comprising 15 farmers, 10 media professionals (broadcast journalists, editors, and producers), and 5 policymakers from relevant government agencies and agricultural institutions. Data collection was conducted through in-depth interviews and data analysis followed a thematic approach, where responses were transcribed, coded, and categorised into emerging themes that reflect patterns in media coverage, policy evaluation and stakeholder engagement. The findings revealed that broadcast media play a crucial role in disseminating agricultural policies in Nigeria, particularly through radio and television; however, their effectiveness is hindered by overreliance on government press releases, limited investigative journalism and inadequate farmer engagement. The study concluded that while Nigerian broadcast media serve as vital channels for disseminating agricultural policies, their overreliance on government narratives and limited investigative reporting weaken their effectiveness in providing comprehensive and balanced information to farmers and stakeholders. The study recommended that broadcast media should enhance investigative journalism and reduce overreliance on government narratives to ensure balanced and comprehensive coverage of agricultural policies

title: Indigenous Language Media and Women Social Empowerment in Rivers State, Nigeria
container-title: RESEARCH JOURNAL OF MASS COMMUNICATION AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY
9ab9d8057236b9dd14e0c34677ecaf6c387bdc57.abstract: This study is an examination of indigenous language media and women social empowerment in Rivers State, Nigeria. This study adopted a qualitative research method. The population of the study consisted of women in Rivers State who actively consume indigenous language media, including radio, television, and digital platforms. A sample size of 20 participants were selected using purposive sampling technique. The primary method of data collection was email interviews, allowing participants to provide detailed, reflective responses at their convenience. Participants were receive structured, open-ended questions designed to elicit in-depth insights on how indigenous language media influences women's awareness, agency, and participation in socio-economic and political activities. For data analysis, the study employed thematic analysis, where interview responses were transcribed, coded, and categorised into themes that reflect key patterns and emerging insights. This method ensures a systematic interpretation of qualitative data, allowing for a nuanced understanding of how indigenous language media fosters women’s empowerment, the barriers they face, and possible policy recommendations for improving gender-inclusive communication. Findings from the study revealed that, indigenous language media plays a crucial role in enhancing women’s access to vital information, particularly in health, agriculture, and governance, by breaking down language barriers and providing content that is culturally relevant and accessible, although infrastructural challenges such as poor network coverage and limited access to devices hinder its full reach. The study concluded that indigenous language media plays a pivotal role in enhancing women’s access to critical information, providing them with the tools to make informed decisions about their health, economic, and social lives, but its full potential is constrained by infrastructural limitations, requiring targeted investments to improve accessibility and reach. The study recommended that government and private sector stakeholders should invest in expanding media infrastructure and providing affordable technology to ensure broader access to indigenous language media for women.

title: Reconsidering green logistics adoption: the role of perceived behavioral control and ESG information in shippers' selection of logistics service providers
container-title: The International Journal of Logistics Management
f14faa48b238a1f97a4c3ba15c173bb7d87770e2.abstract: Purpose The purpose of this study is to examine how perceived behavioral control and environmental, social and governance (ESG) information shape shippers' adoption of green logistics service providers. Specifically, the study aims to (1) investigate the presence of an intention–behavior gap in green logistics adoption and (2) assess whether ESG information enhances perceived behavioral control, thereby facilitating actual adoption behavior within an extended theory of planned behavior (TPB) framework. Design/methodology/approach The study adopts a quantitative survey-based research design. Data were collected from shippers involved in logistics service provider selection and analyzed using structural equation modeling. The research framework integrates the Theory of Planned Behavior with persuasion theory, incorporating ESG information as an external antecedent influencing perceived behavioral control, behavioral intention and actual adoption behavior. Findings The results show that environmental attitudes significantly influence behavioral intention, while subjective norms do not. Behavioral intention does not directly translate into actual green logistics adoption, indicating a clear intention–behavior gap. Perceived behavioral control has a strong and direct effect on actual adoption behavior. ESG information significantly enhances perceived behavioral control, indirectly strengthening both intention and behavior. Research limitations/implications This study is based on cross-sectional survey data, which limits causal inference. The empirical context focuses on shippers within a specific institutional and regulatory environment, which may affect generalizability. Future research could employ longitudinal designs, cross-country comparisons or experimental approaches to further examine the dynamic role of ESG information in sustainable logistics decision-making. Practical implications The findings suggest that promoting green logistics requires more than fostering pro-environmental intentions. Logistics service providers and policymakers should focus on enhancing shippers' perceived control by improving information transparency, reducing decision uncertainty and strengthening ESG disclosure credibility. ESG ratings can serve as practical decision-support tools that legitimize green logistics choices within organizational governance structures. Originality/value This study contributes original value by reconceptualization green logistics adoption as a control-driven rather than intention-driven process. It extends TPB by identifying perceived behavioral control as the central mechanism in organizational logistics decisions and positions ESG information as a control-enabling governance instrument. This integrated perspective offers a novel theoretical explanation for the persistent intention–behavior gap in sustainable logistics adoption.

title: New Media Applications for Television News Production and Presentation: A Comparative Analysis of AIT And Silverbird, Port Harcourt
container-title: RESEARCH JOURNAL OF MASS COMMUNICATION AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY
6c1563765b5a683aebb51a44af819cef630e503a.abstract: This study examined new media applications for television news production and presentation: a comparative analysis of AIT and Silverbird, Port Harcourt. The study's methodology was a combination of survey and content analysis, where staff members of two television stations - AIT and Silverbird Television - were surveyed, and content from the new media platforms of those two stations was analyzed for comparison. The population for the study was all employees of the two stations, totalling 37 people. The sample size was also 37 because the population was small enough to make a census method feasible. The instrument used for data collection was a questionnaire titled New Media Applications for Television News Production and Presentation Questionnaire (NMPTNPPQ). The instrument was validated and its reliability test was at 0.89 which was determined using the Cronbach Alpha. The data were calculated on a mean score basis where the cumulative numbers were added and divided by the total number of respondents sampled. Findings from the study reveal that new media applications enhance television news production and presentation after a comparative analysis of AIT and Silverbird, Port Harcourt. The study concluded that the rate of social media use in AIT and Silverbird Port Harcourt during their news production and presentation is high. Based on the study findings, it was recommended among others that the two stations should continue to harness the benefits of the new media in their news production and presentation in deeper ways to reach out to a wider audience more than they currently do.

title: Influence of Digital Information Resource Dissemination Among Degree Students in College of Education Hong, Adamawa State
container-title: RESEARCH JOURNAL OF MASS COMMUNICATION AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY
d50dfb929d191d5ded7600584f9c8e12edef614c.abstract: This study examined the impact of digital resources on the educational experiences of Degree Students at Adamawa State College of Education, Hong. The study was guided by four objectives which include: ascertaining the impact of digital resources on the speed and accuracy of information dissemination; determining the role of digital resources in shaping public opinion and influencing decision-making processes; assessing the effectiveness of digital resources in promoting equality access to information and bridging the knowledge gap and, Determine the relationship between gender difference and digital resource information dissemination among Degree Students in Adamawa State College of Education Hong. In line with the objectives, three research questions and one hypothesis were raised and answered. The study adopted a survey design while a questionnaire was used for data collection. Data collected was analyzed using descriptive statistics of mean and standard deviation to answer the research questions where the null hypothesis was tested using regression analysis using SPSS version 20. The study shows that digital resources significantly enhance the speed and accuracy of information dissemination among students as indicated by mean scores ranging from 3.13 to 3.94; The findings show that digital resources have a substantial influence on shaping public opinion and guiding decisionmaking processes among students as indicated by the mean scores ranging from 2.98 to 4.21; The study found that digital resources are highly effective in promoting equal access to information and bridging the knowledge gap with a mean scores ranging from 3.32 to 3.76 and, A positive high relationship [r = 0.72] exists between gender difference and digital information resource dissemination among Degree Students in Adamawa State College of Education Hong. Consequently, a significant relationship exists between gender difference and digital information resource dissemination among Degree Students in the institution studied [0.00 < 0.05]. The study recommends among others that, the College authority should ensure the total Implementation of comprehensive digital literacy programs for both students and faculty members to ensure equal gender access to the world of information sharing, etc.

title: Mediacja transformacyjna w perspektywie teorii dezintegracji pozytywnej Kazimierza Dąbrowskiego:  analiza teoretyczno-przeglądowa
Transformative Mediation from the Perspective of Kazimierz Dąbrowski’s Theory of Positive Disintegration: A Theoretical Review
container-title: Państwo i Społeczeństwo / State and Society
c981c77208e7c31f7dbd7a7f9fa9d9ae681a3cdd.abstract: Celem artykułu jest analiza możliwych związków między teorią dezintegracji pozytywnej Kazimierza Dąbrowskiego a wybranymi założeniami współczesnej mediacji, ze szczególnym uwzględnieniem mediacji transformacyjnej i oświatowej. Punktem wyjścia jest pytanie, w jakim zakresie kategorie wypracowane przez Dąbrowskiego w odniesieniu do rozwoju psychicznego jednostki mogą stanowić użyteczne narzędzie interpretacji konfliktu interpersonalnego oraz procesu jego transformacji. Artykuł ma charakter teoretyczno-przeglądowy. Zastosowano analizę pojęciową i porównawczą, obejmującą klasyczne prace Dąbrowskiego oraz wybrane publikacje z zakresu teorii konfliktu, mediacji transformacyjnej i mediacji oświatowej. Analizie poddano takie kategorie jak kryzys, konflikt wewnętrzny, dezintegracja, autonomia, wartości, odpowiedzialność i rozwój osobowości, zestawiając je z kategoriami obecnymi w teorii i praktyce mediacyjnej: podmiotowością stron, uznaniem, wzmocnieniem, dobrowolnością, komunikacją oraz transformacją relacji. Przeprowadzona analiza pozwala wskazać istotne podobieństwa funkcjonalne między obiema perspektywami. W szczególności konflikt może być ujmowany nie tylko jako stan wymagający zakończenia lub rozwiązania, lecz również jako doświadczenie ujawniające dotychczasowe ograniczenia, potrzeby i wartości oraz stwarzające możliwość zmiany sposobu funkcjonowania. W mediacji transformacyjnej szczególnego znaczenia nabierają pod tym względem procesy wzmocnienia podmiotowości stron i wzajemnego uznania, które można interpretować w kategoriach autonomii, refleksyjności i przekraczania dotychczasowych schematów działania prezentowanych przez Dąbrowskiego. Jednocześnie analiza ujawnia zasadnicze granice proponowanej analogii. Konflikt intrapsychiczny w teorii dezintegracji pozytywnej i konflikt interpersonalny będący przedmiotem mediacji należą do odmiennych porządków teoretycznych, a mediacji nie należy utożsamiać ani z psychoterapią, ani z procesem rozwoju osobowości w znaczeniu właściwym teorii Dąbrowskiego. Proponowana perspektywa ma zatem przede wszystkim wartość heurystyczną i interpretacyjną. Może poszerzać teoretyczne rozumienie mediacji jako procesu, który w określonych warunkach nie tylko prowadzi do rozwiązania sporu, lecz również sprzyja refleksji, autonomii stron oraz jakościowej zmianie ich relacji. Szczególnie interesującym obszarem dalszych analiz i badań empirycznych wydaje się pod tym względem mediacja oświatowa.

title: Relationship Between Social Media, Child Abuse and Academic Achievement Among Secondary School Students in Kaduna State: Implications for Guidance
container-title: RESEARCH JOURNAL OF MASS COMMUNICATION AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY
4df935c346d21673032f8de884a132943e3390a4.abstract: This study explored the relationship between social media, child abuse and academic achievement among secondary school students in Kaduna State: Implications for Guidance. The design employed for this study was a descriptive survey research design. The population of the study consisted of all the students attending public secondary schools in Kaduna State. A sample size of 256 students was selected for this study. The study revealed Facebook, WhatsApp’s, TikTok, Instagram, Telegram, YouTube, Zoom, and Skype are some of the various forms of social media platform used by students in Kaduna State. Findings of the also revealed that child sexual abuse, child neglect and maltreatment, child trafficking, female genital mutilation, child physical abuse and child bullying and cyberbullying and child emotional abuse are some of the various forms of child abuse in Kaduna State. The findings of the study further revealed that there is a significant relationship between social media and child abuse among secondary school students in Kaduna State and the findings of the study equally revealed that there is a significant relationship between social media and academic achievement among secondary school students in Kaduna State. The study recommended that parents who are the first agent of socialisation should do more to monitor what the youths are watching on the social media especially, Facebook, YouTube and Telegram and try to regulate it in order to bring its negative influence on students to the barest minimum if not fully eradicated. The study also recommended that effort should be made by the counsellors to create awareness on the various forms of child abuse among secondary school students in order to bring it negative effects on students under control.

title: Trustworthy Federated Clinical Intelligence with Homomorphic Encryption and  Explainable AI
container-title: International Journal on Advanced Computer Engineering and Communication Technology
e9efaf7e4de70a4bb9a5e76e1dc2d37a457ecb6d.abstract: Cross-institutional clinical artificial intelligence is constrained by fragmented patient data, non-identically distributed (non-IID) populations, leakage from shared model updates, and limited interpretability. Federated learning (FL) preserves data locality, but ordinary FL neither makes model updates confidential nor guarantees stable optimization under heterogeneous clients. This paper proposes a defense-in-depth framework that coordinates Federated Proximal (FedProx) optimization, record-level differential privacy (DP), Cheon–Kim–Kim–Song (CKKS) approximate homomorphic encryption, and explainable artificial intelligence (XAI). FedProx limits local model drift; DP-SGD bounds the influence of an individual training record; and CKKS permits weighted aggregation while client updates remain encrypted. A key-separated design keeps the aggregation server from being provisioned with the secret key used to reveal individual contributions; only the aggregate is released for global-model construction. Grad-CAM and SHAP/LIME provide clinician-facing explanations, while an audit dashboard reports convergence, privacy-accounting inputs, encryption status, and systems overhead. We formalize the learning objective, privacy mechanism, encrypted aggregation, threat model, numerical approximation error, communication footprint, and an evaluation protocol spanning IID and controlled non-IID partitions. The contribution is a reproducible system-level co-design and evaluation framework rather than a new cryptographic primitive or optimization algorithm.

title: The Impact of Resource Sharing on Information Dissemination among Postgraduate Students of Adamawa State University, Mubi

bd1383810f60f865b36bb11f0eec73b68e0b891b.abstract: This study investigates the impact of resource sharing on information dissemination among postgraduate students of Adamawa State University, Mubi. The study was guided by four objectives, four research questions, and one hypothesis. Related literatures were reviewed based on the objectives of the studies. A descriptive research design was adopted for the study. The study population comprised all the postgraduate students of Adamawa State University, Mubi total of 346. Yaro Yamani sampling techniques were used to draw a sample of 100 for the study. A selfdeveloped questionnaire was used to collect data. Data retrieved was analyzed using descriptive statistics of frequency counts, percentages, and mean. The analysis of (ANOVA) was used to test the null hypothesis at a 0.05 level of significance. The findings indicate that smartphones, Desktop/Laptop computers, USB Flash drives, and the Internet are available for resource sharing while tablets and CD-ROMs are not available; Desktop/Laptop computers, Smartphones, USB Flash drives, and the Internet are the most accessible ICT tools for resource sharing while CDROM and tablets are not; WhatsApp, Email, Google Drive, and Zoom are the channels mostly used for collaboration among the students while Telegram and Google Meet are not available; Journal articles, slides, and educational videos are frequently shared among postgraduate students while hand-outs, notes, and Textbooks are rarely shared; and, There is no significant difference between the levels of impact of resource sharing on information dissemination among the postgraduate students of Adamawa State University, Mubi. Amongst other recommendation preferred include: the University Management should support and improve the provision of ICT tools such as Smartphones, Desktop/Laptop Computer and Internet for resource sharing, etc.

title: AI-Driven Predictive Maintenance for Institutional Electrical Systems
container-title: Journal of Technology and System Information
743e0632b4637f415786ff15de8256d3f95412a3.abstract: High-voltage power distribution networks in institutional settings are increasingly vulnerable to age-related degradation, operational volatility, and unexpected service disruptions. Conventional maintenance practices—dominated by reactive repairs and static time-based servicing—impose significant financial burdens and risk over-servicing intact assets. To address these operational constraints, this study employs a thematic literature synthesis of smart grid prognostics and IIoT asset telemetry (2015–2025) to formulate an end-to-end four-layer predictive maintenance (PdM) framework. The architectural continuum is established by systematically mapping physical multi-sensor acquisition to edge-cloud analytics (GRU and Bi-LSTM engines), dynamic Asset Health Index (AHI) tracking, and automated, cyber-secure Computerized Maintenance Management System (CMMS) dispatch. Synthesizing literature performance baselines reveals that deep bidirectional recurrent networks—notably Bi-LSTM models—achieve superior degradation tracking for Remaining Useful Life (RUL) estimation, attaining an F1-score of 91.0%, a Mean Absolute Error of 4.3%, and a Root Mean Squared Error of 4.2. Furthermore, multi-modal feature fusion significantly sharpens Asset Health Index (AHI) modeling, driving prediction errors down to an RMSE of 0.052, lengthening warning lead times to 37 days, and maintaining false alarm rates at 6.2%. The transition to an AI-enabled prognostic strategy yields up to a 50.0% decrease in overall operational and maintenance costs while extending high-voltage asset longevity by 40%. The inclusion of Explainable AI (SHAP and LRP) alongside robust Operational Technology cybersecurity measures guarantees operational transparency and cyber resilience.

title: TECHNOLOGICAL EMPOWERMENT AND VALUE BALANCE: DUAL PATHWAYS IN CHINA’S TECHNOLOGY GOVERNANCE POLICIES FOR THE AI ERA
container-title: Trends in Social Sciences and Humanities Research
046a4b825efe15b9ca51cb520c373729b94ebde6.abstract: The deep embedding of artificial intelligence (AI) technology is reshaping global governance. The tension between “technological empowerment” and “value balance” has become a common governance challenge for countries worldwide. Based on a dual-pathway framework of “technology-driven modernization of state governance” and “technology-embedded multi-actor social co-governance,” this paper systematically analyzes the internal logic and operational mechanisms of technology governance in China in the AI era. The study finds that China’s technology governance is not a single efficiency-oriented application of technology; rather, through the coordinated operation of dual pathways, it comprehensively achieves four major governance functions: efficiency improvement, equity promotion, security assurance, and institutional reconstruction. In terms of model characteristics, China has developed a distinctive paradigm centered on “enabling governance”-one that takes state capacity as its foundation, institutional flexibility as its safeguard, and plural public values as its goals. This paradigm transcends the single efficiency-oriented governance logic of the West and offers a non-Western pathway with both theoretical inspiration and practical reference for global digital governance. This paper argues that the core of “enabling governance” lies in resolving the tension between technological empowerment and value balance through institutional design, and that the transferability of its experience depends on the conditions of fit in specific institutional contexts.

title: Machine Learning Approaches for Detecting Encrypted and Compressed Malicious Files: A Review
container-title: RESEARCH JOURNAL OF MASS COMMUNICATION AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY
4b3bb508e9c2038cc22b75fba632a118ca17531d.abstract: The advancement of cyber threats has intensified with the rise of encrypted and compressed malicious files, posing significant challenges to traditional signature-based detection methods. Machine learning (ML) has emerged as a promising solution, capable of uncovering hidden patterns without relying on known malware signatures. This review explores recent developments in applying ML techniques such as deep learning, transfer learning, ensemble methods, and anomaly detection to identify encrypted malicious files. Studies have demonstrated that ML models can effectively analyse structural, statistical, and behavioural features, offering improved adaptability and detection accuracy. Despite these advancements, significant challenges persist, including encryption evasion, polymorphic malware, data imbalance, scalability issues, and adversarial attacks. Innovative strategies like explainable AI, federated learning, scalable architectures, and continuous learning are being investigated to enhance robustness and transparency. The dynamic evolution of cyber threats underscores the urgency of developing intelligent, adaptable, and privacy-conscious detection systems. Ultimately, this review highlights the critical role of ML in strengthening cybersecurity defences against increasingly sophisticated encrypted malicious files, emphasizing the need for continued research to address ongoing challenges and ensure resilient, scalable protection across diverse digital environments.

7ea3e424663fd13766e2195ed7d291a4b7bb02b2.abstract: This paper explores the impact of social media on Nigerian citizens during political campaigns, focusing on the 2023 elections. Using the Uses and Gratifications Theory, the study examines how platforms such as Facebook, Twitter/X, WhatsApp, Instagram, and TikTok were utilized to mobilize voters and engage citizens politically. The research highlights the role of these platforms in enhancing political participation through direct communication, debates, and activism. However, it also identifies the significant negative impact of misinformation, particularly on WhatsApp, where rumours and fake news influenced voter behavior. Through qualitative observation, the study found that while social media fostered increased political engagement, misinformation posed a major challenge to credible electoral discourse. The study recommends enhancing media literacy and implementing stronger regulatory frameworks for social media platforms to ensure accurate political communication and mitigate the spread of false information.

title: tModBase v2.0: an expanded database of tRNA modifications with an AI-powered assistant
container-title: Nucleic Acids Research
6dc27bcf3717dbf61b825aaa6a0d910a0b11a2a6.abstract: Abstract Chemical modifications of transfer RNAs (tRNAs) are crucial for tRNA stability, codon decoding, translational fidelity, and tRNA-derived small RNA (tsRNA) biogenesis. Changes in these modifications are associated with stress responses, physiological regulation, and human disease, underscoring the need to integrate modification information with experimental evidence and biological context. We previously established tModBase, a web resource to organize and explore tRNA modification-related data. Its first release integrated modification sites, high-throughput sequencing-derived signals, and condition-dependent changes. Since then, tRNA profiling has expanded through modification-specific and direct RNA sequencing strategies, with rapidly growing datasets across species and conditions. Here, we present tModBase v2.0 (http://www.tmodbase2.com/), containing 528 datasets across 23 species, 40 sequencing and library-preparation methods, and 42 modification types. It includes 68 third-generation and 210 modification-specific sequencing datasets, extending coverage of direct-RNA and modification-specific approaches. tModBase v2.0 further integrates sequencing-derived signals, condition-dependent information, and biological annotations linking modifications with enzymes, genetic variants, tsRNAs, diseases, and expression profiles. The LLM- and retrieval-augmented generation-powered assistant tModBot enables natural-language exploration across database modules while grounding responses in retrieved tModBase evidence. tModBase v2.0 therefore provides an expanded resource for investigating the diversity, dynamics, and biological context of tRNA modifications.

title: The mediating role of self-efficacy in the relationships of technophilia and positive emotional experience with perceived learning effectiveness in AI-supported EFL education
container-title: Discover Artificial Intelligence
1e046e91cd43fe005cca1d83a4437e55e4d42551.abstract: Abstract Despite the increasing integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into English as a Foreign Language (EFL) education, the psychological mechanisms linking learners’ technological dispositions and emotional experiences to perceived learning effectiveness remain undertheorized and empirically underexplored. This study examined whether self-efficacy served as a statistical mediator in the relationships of technophilia and positive emotional experience with perceived learning effectiveness in AI-supported EFL education. A cross-sectional survey was conducted involving 234 students enrolled in English-language courses at a private college of health sciences. Adapted multi-item scales on technophilia, positive emotional experience, self-efficacy, and perceived learning effectiveness were administered. Structural equation modeling with bootstrapping (5000 resamples) was used to examine direct and indirect associations. Self-efficacy demonstrated the strongest direct association with perceived learning effectiveness (β = 0.375, p = 0.001). Positive emotional experience was strongly associated with self-efficacy (β = 0.624, p < 0.001), and its indirect association with perceived learning effectiveness through self-efficacy was significant (β = 0.234, 95% CI [0.128, 0.351]). Technophilia was also positively associated with self-efficacy (β = 0.307, p = 0.002), and its indirect association with perceived learning effectiveness through self-efficacy was significant. The findings were consistent with self-efficacy partially mediating both relationships. These findings suggest that learners’ confidence in managing AI-supported tasks plays an important role in linking affective dispositions to perceived effectiveness appraisals. The study contributes to computer-assisted language learning (CALL) research by clarifying how positive orientation toward AI-supported technologies, emotional experience, and efficacy beliefs jointly relate to learners’ perceptions of effective AI-supported language learning. Pedagogically, the findings suggest that progressively scaffolded practice and mastery-oriented AI tasks may strengthen self-efficacy and improve learners’ perceived effectiveness in AI-supported EFL environments.

title: Generative AI and Employment Concerns Among AI Aware Respondents in Bangladesh
2175796b9a04ec3e661e8e64d03823c1cc031301.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) may change professional tasks, but the implications for workers depend on how technology is introduced and how people adapt. This study examines stated perceptions of task change, concern about routine work and AI-related learning in 385 adult, AI-aware questionnaire records from Bangladesh. Most respondents were recorded as law students, and the dataset does not establish that all participants were employed or young professionals. The questions do not directly measure current job security or the effects of AI exposure on employment. Individual items are therefore analysed separately using response distributions, paired endorsement comparisons and exploratory rank correlations. Of 385 respondents, 232 (60.3%) agreed that AI may reduce demand for some routine professional tasks; 307 (79.7%) agreed that learning to work effectively with AI could reduce their future job-security concerns; and 211 (54.8%) anticipated new tasks requiring human judgement and oversight. A total of 184 respondents endorsed both the routine-task concern and the potential reassurance of learning. These statements differ in meaning and do not establish whether training actually reduces insecurity. Exploratory correlations were small and should not be interpreted causally. Job demands-resources theory, psychological contract theory and career construction provide complementary lenses rather than validated models. The study distinguishes concern about tasks from concern about losing a job and identifies the need for independently verified employment status, recruitment documentation and direct measures of perceived job security in future research.

title: The Paradox of Algorithmic Sycophancy: Sycophancy in Large Language Models and the Limits of AI-Mediated Knowledge Reconstruction in the Metacognitive Creative Destruction Model
f31f456f51b7580c96613027043ba5bcb62c702c.abstract: The Metacognitive Creative Destruction (MCD) model approaches educational innovation as a perpetual spiral process. Contradiction (accumulated cognitive conflicts that resist interpretation), activates Metacognitive Capacity, enabling Destructive Unlearning Propensity, the conscious abandonment of outdated mental schemas, which in turn enables Creative Reconstruction Ability, and ultimately, new knowledge. In the model’s empirical validation with 1,498 teachers, a critical finding emerged: AI Augmentation Intensity (AIA) predicted Metacognitive Capacity (MC) and Creative Reconstruction Ability (CRA), but not Destructive Unlearning Propensity (DUP).This article argues that this finding is not accidental, but reflects an inherent weakness of modern AI systems, and more specifically, the tendency toward AI Sycophancy. Models trained with reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) tend to avoid disagreements and be likable to the user, preventing the individual from experiencing cognitive conflicts, perpetuating their already formed beliefs at the expense of scientific accuracy.Therefore, in an environment of “algorithmic flattery”, the necessary contradictions that trigger unlearning are not produced. Based on the MCD model, it is concluded that the absence of unlearning, that is, the deliberate and conscious abandonment of outdated beliefs, mental models and practices, makes the reconstruction of knowledge absolutely superficial and thus, algorithmically condescending interaction does not produce deep and authentic knowledge, regardless of AI Augmentation Intensity.

title: SAGE-AIP: A Scale-Adaptive Gated Ensemble Framework for Predicting AI Adoption and Productivity Across Multiple Data Scales
5358271a89a3a9d9de2f5155abb8bccaa93cc9ce.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is frequently associated with productivity improvement, yet empirical conclusions depend on where AI exposure is measured, how productivity is defined, and which model is used. This study develops a multi-scale comparative framework using three datasets: 145,000 AI-adoption records from 10 countries and eight industries; 2,074 observed country-year records from 233 country or regional units (2015–2023); and 150 employee-level observations. Robust regression, country fixed effects, dynamic fixed effects, and difference-GMM sensitivity analysis are combined with a proposed Scale-Adaptive Gated Ensemble Framework for AI Adoption and Productivity (SAGE-AIP), which is benchmarked against six established regressors using temporal holdouts for the two longitudinal datasets and a train–test split for the employee data. The adoption dataset shows almost no systematic structure (R2 = 0.00018), and SAGE-AIP does not improve on simpler models there (test RMSE 28.976 vs. 28.900 for Elastic Net). In the global panel, automation intensity is strongly associated with AI-attributed productivity (β = 19.882, SE = 0.434), and SAGE-AIP attains the lowest test RMSE (4.448; R2 = 0.544). At the employee level, recorded AI-tool information remains positively associated with productivity (β = 0.905, SE = 0.220), but Random Forest outperforms SAGE-AIP (test RMSE 0.435 vs. 0.583). SAGE-AIP is therefore not uniformly superior; its value is scale-specific, which supports evaluating models across data scales rather than relying on a single dataset or model class.

title: Tidal City Intelligence: A Conceptual Framework for AI-Enabled Service Governance in Cities with Fluctuating Populations
9125839bb912dfa67489dd5a63f2a2fd021e86f5.abstract: Many cities serve far more people than their civil register counts, and the gap rises and falls with tourist seasons, holidays, pilgrimages and festivals. Municipal budgets, staffing and data systems are nonetheless sized to the register. This conceptual paper introduces the Tidal City, a city whose population present swings in recurring, largely predictable cycles that change how public services must be planned. We distinguish the concept from the service population, tourism seasonality and overtourism; propose a two-part Tidal Index measuring the swing’s amplitude and regularity; and offer a typology of seasonal, day-visitor and event-driven tidal cities. Drawing on dynamic capabilities and adaptive governance theory, we set out Tidal City Intelligence, a four-layer framework (Sense, Anticipate, Adapt, Govern) describing the data and AI capabilities a local government needs, and derive testable propositions for each layer. Published data from Pattaya, Thailand, put the average population present at roughly two to three times the registered population and show annual waste moving with guest arrivals while the register barely changed. With only annual guest data, the case illustrates load and demand regularity rather than the full index. The paper offers cities a common measure of the problem and researchers an empirical agenda.

title: Forward-Looking Information Disclosure: A Prisma-Based Systematic Literature Review
4d423273bb89e379c0fb7de8afcb49915878307e.abstract: The purpose of this systematic literature review (SLR) was to use the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) framework to systematically evaluate the literature on FLID and identify emerging research gaps. A systematic search was conducted in two major academic databases (Scopus & Web of Science) using predefined inclusion or exclusion criteria. The dominant theoretical frameworks identified are the Agency Theory and Impression Management Theory to explain the board's dual role to monitor and control agent behaviour while controlling and managing strategic representation through dissemination of future-oriented information and management of agency cost and information asymmetry. Other relevant theoretical frameworks include the Resource-Based View theory which provides insight into how internal resources affect FLID, Legitimacy theory which explains how stakeholder expectations affect FLID and Signalling theory which informs how information asymmetries influence FLID. The majority of previous studies on FLID were conducted in developed countries specifically in the United States. Research on this topic in developing countries such as Malaysia appears to be underrepresented. This study has identified several avenues for the potential use of alternative communication methods with respect to the examination of FLID in a post COVID-19 world that may include increased levels of uncertainty.

title: AI Model Energy and Carbon Disclosure: A Source-Audited Study of 103 Releases (2024-2026)
59d3047d593bdd3064939431188715f273b686fc.abstract: AI model cards and release documents are supposed to help people assess models. For energy and carbon, they often leave out the number a reader needs, or print figures that cannot be compared directly. I built the Release Energy Ledger, a source-traceable record of 161 distinct developer releases, and audited a selected set of 103 dated 2024-2026 releases that passed a page check. On the designated release document, 85 (82.5 percent) print no energy, carbon or compute figure, 1 prints compute only, and 17 (16.5 percent) print an energy or carbon-related figure: 16 training-specific and 1 life-cycle footprint. None prints release-specific inference energy. Meta accounts for 10 of the 17; without Meta, the count is 7 of 93. The figures differ in method, unit, equipment boundary and emissions accounting, and only 8 of the 17 state a basis, a boundary and a method together. Changing the unit of analysis gives 11 of 80 documents, 10 of 59 model families and 7 of 23 developers. The strict-quote subset (5 of 74) is a different evidence frame, not a lower bound. A page re-read confirmed the printed figures for all 17; blinded AI coding agreed with the ledger on 91.9 to 100 percent of fields, and a separately instructed AI adjudicator agreed on 42 of 42 selected cells. These results describe the documents in this selected set, not actual emissions, the universe of releases or legal compliance. No human has validated any label. The ledger and counting script are released with the paper as a versioned data record (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23808341).

title: Compression‐Resilient, Resolution‐Vulnerable: A Statistical Robustness Analysis of EfficientNet‐B2 for AI‐Generated Image Detection
40c90e02b219b35a0c83b43f046473f558552e91.abstract: Reliable classification of AI-generated images requires more than high accuracy on unmodified test examples: media files may be compressed or downsampled before forensic analysis. This paper presents a controlled, paired robustness evaluation of a previously developed EfficientNet-B2 detector using RGB, fast Fourier transform (FFT), and artifact-oriented image features. The existing checkpoint, validation-selected classification threshold, and fixed set of 6,000 held-out images were reused without training or test-time threshold adjustment. Six transformed conditions were evaluated against original inputs: JPEG qualities 90, 70, and 50, and bicubic downsampling to maximum dimensions of 256, 128, and 64 pixels followed by reconstruction to the original dimensions. The baseline achieved 94.53% accuracy and 0.9857 area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC). JPEG variants produced accuracies between 94.38% and 94.63%, with paired 95% bootstrap intervals of accuracy change spanning zero. By contrast, downsampling to 256, 128, and 64 pixels yielded accuracies of 93.15%, 91.73%, and 74.40%, respectively. At 64 pixels, the accuracy difference was −20.13 percentage points (95% paired bootstrap interval approximately −21.12 to −19.12), and AUROC fell to 0.8967. The evidence indicates substantially greater sensitivity to severe spatial resolution loss than to the tested JPEG compression settings. Because the existing training procedure incorporates JPEG augmentation, these findings characterize this detector and evaluation protocol rather than establish universal robustness across detectors or unseen transformations.

title: The Effect of Internal Integration on Operational Performance with Supply Chain Capability Mediation
container-title: MARGINAL JOURNAL OF MANAGEMENT ACCOUNTING GENERAL FINANCE AND INTERNATIONAL ECONOMIC ISSUES
7c5e4fb3fcf218b8ec2f8734f02aefcc77a4ec41.abstract: The rapid growth of the coffee shop industry in the Special Region of Yogyakarta has increased competition and requires MSMEs to have efficient and adaptive operational performance. This situation calls for integrated internal process management and supply chain capabilities that are responsive. The setting of this inquiry is coffee shop micro, small, and medium enterprises in the Special Region of Yogyakarta, and it investigates the manner in which internal integration shapes operational performance, positioning supply chain capability as an intervening (mediating) variable. An explanatory quantitative design was adopted, executed through a cross-sectional survey. Two hundred respondents were handpicked via purposive sampling, comprising proprietors, supervisors, and staff members who are personally engaged in operational and supply chain undertakings. Information was gleaned by means of a structured questionnaire and then processed with Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (SEM-PLS) through the SmartPLS application. The evaluation began with the measurement model, appraised via convergent validity, discriminant validity, and construct reliability, and proceeded to the structural model, which was examined through R-square coefficients and a bootstrapping procedure. According to the empirical findings, internal integration favorably and significantly affects both supply chain capability and operational performance. Supply chain capability, in turn, positively and significantly impacts operational performance and simultaneously functions as a partial mediator connecting internal integration to operational performance. Such outcomes corroborate that fortifying internal integration, buttressed by adaptable supply chain capability, constitutes an indispensable strategy for durably elevating the operational performance of coffee shop MSMEs.

title: How social science matters to the nation-state: A sociohistorical analysis of presidential addresses in Chile, 1900–2021
container-title: Social Science Information
81299a420fbe61be85220ed717cf552b57285c2e.abstract: Although entanglements between the nation-state and the social sciences are often emphasized, little is hitherto known about how the state’s demands on the social sciences have evolved over time. Through a detailed analysis of Chilean presidential addresses from 1900 to 2021, this study examines the types of scientific knowledge that mattered to the nation-state and explores how and why this knowledge made a difference for leading representatives of the Chilean state. We identify three periods. In roughly the first half of the 20th century, the rational and scientific analysis of the state ( state-istics ) was privileged as a means to master the population and its needs. In the second half of the century, the legitimacy of political decisions became increasingly framed in economic terms. In recent decades, a symbiotic relationship between the “applied” social sciences and the goals of the nation-state persists, but recent presidential addresses reveal a more ambivalent stance toward the social sciences and a growing reliance on the input of boundary institutions, such as think tanks and policy-oriented research centers. Although this study focuses on the Chilean case, it also considers the influence of global contexts in shaping this nation-building project. In this sense, the analysis situates the evolving relationship between the social sciences and the state of the “Chilean experiment” within a broader global framework, offering insights that may contribute to understanding similar dynamics in other parts of the world.

title: An Application of the Self-Determination Theory Model for AI-Enhanced, Digital Psychosocial Interventions for Pediatric Disabilities
container-title: Western Journal of Nursing Research
6a353330c39f733eb7e369612f893bac2e52174c.abstract: Background: Youth with developmental disabilities (DDs) experience elevated psychosocial challenges, including difficulties with emotion regulation, self-concept, and access to timely mental health support. Pediatric nurses are well-positioned to address these needs; however, time constraints, limited training, and restricted access to specialty services often impede the provision of consistent psychosocial care. Digitally delivered psychosocial interventions enhanced by artificial intelligence (AI) offer new opportunities for individualized, accessible support, but these approaches frequently lack a clear theoretical foundation. Purpose: This paper applied Self-Determination Theory (SDT), specifically Basic Psychological Needs Theory, to guide pediatric nurses’ use of AI-enhanced, digital psychosocial interventions for DDs in practice. Methods: A theory-driven synthesis mapped SDT needs (autonomy, competence, and relatedness) to AI-enabled intervention features: conversational agents, neuro/adaptive feedback, and emotion-recognition tailoring. Results: The framework specifies how these features can promote volitional engagement, optimal challenge with timely feedback, and supportive interactions for youth with DDs. It also notes evidence gaps (small, heterogeneous samples; limited comparisons and follow-up) and barriers involving payment/workload, equity and access, and data protection, transparency, and bias. Conclusions/Implications: SDT offers a coherent, testable foundation for designing, evaluating, and integrating AI-enhanced psychosocial supports for pediatric DDs. Nurses can screen for support, coach families, monitor risks, and advocate for ethical deployment and rigorous research.

title: INTEGRATION OF GENERATIVE AI SKILLS IN JOB REQUIREMENTS: EVIDENCE FROM JOB ADVERTISEMENTS IN GEORGIA
container-title: Baltic Journal of Economic Studies
2e932bf664680814b7e5be137f1e6f4677cfcbee.abstract: The rapid diffusion of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) tools has created a demand for new skills in labour markets. However, research into how employers articulate GenAI competencies in job advertisements has focused almost exclusively on large, technologically advanced economies. This study examines how employers in Georgia, a small upper-middle-income transitional economy, indicate GenAI skill requirements in job advertisements, considering four dimensions: skill visibility, linguistic framing, organisational readiness and skill depth. Deductive content analysis was applied to 94 job advertisements collected in January 2026 from three major Georgian labour market platforms (LinkedIn, Jobs.ge and HR.ge). Each advertisement was coded using a structured 20-indicator codebook derived from established theoretical frameworks. The results show that employers articulate GenAI skills in two ways: by explicitly naming the tool, which is present in 38.3 per cent of advertisements, and by using implicit task language, which is present in 61.7 per cent of advertisements and constitutes the dominant form of signalling. Regardless of occupation or skill depth, employers frame GenAI requirements as mandatory in 81.9 per cent of advertisements, indicating the rapid institutionalisation of GenAI literacy as a baseline labour market expectation. Signals of organisational readiness remain weak: only 21.3 per cent of job advertisements acknowledge any organisational role in enabling AI adoption, while the remaining 78.7 per cent present GenAI competence purely as a prerequisite for candidates. Skill complexity is almost evenly divided between basic and advanced requirements, and occupation strongly predicts this division, creating a clear distinction between a technically advanced group and a large group adopting AI on a more general operational level. Signals of organisational readiness remain weak: only 21.3 per cent of job advertisements acknowledge any organisational role in enabling AI adoption, while the remaining 78.7 per cent present GenAI competence purely as a prerequisite for candidates. Skill complexity is almost evenly divided between basic and advanced requirements, and occupation strongly predicts this division, creating a clear distinction between a technically advanced group and a large group adopting AI on a more general operational level.

title: From Adoption to Human-AI Leadership: A Scoping Review of Artificial Intelligence in Educational Leadership and Management
container-title: Social Scientific Centered Issues
1e0569103ec369b6f75ff1186f587acf5a4f67a0.abstract: This scoping review maps how artificial intelligence is conceptualized and used in educational leadership and management and examines the transition from technology adoption toward human-AI leadership. Following established scoping-review guidance and PRISMA-ScR, records from Scopus, Web of Science, and PubMed published or officially available online from 2022 to the final search date in 2026 were screened; items assigned a 2027 bibliographic year were eligible only if already available online before the cutoff. Of 747 records identified, 183 duplicates were removed and 323 records underwent title-and-abstract screening. Full texts were sought for 81 reports; two could not be retrieved, 79 were assessed for eligibility, and 50 studies were included. Four themes emerged: leadership readiness and capability; AI-augmented leadership practice; organizational conditions and institutional transformation; and human-AI agency, governance, and ethical boundaries. The evidence favors augmentation rather than autonomous substitution, with human judgment remaining central to accountability. The review proposes a five-stage Human-AI Educational Leadership Continuum integrating individual capability, organizational readiness, governance, and decision authority. The review was limited to three databases and English-language articles, and the evidence base remains methodologically heterogeneous and largely cross-sectional or context-specific.

title: Film Criticism and Analysis in the Digital Era: Role of Online Platforms
container-title: RESEARCH JOURNAL OF MASS COMMUNICATION AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY
fc7f185d7413cac784e5be88d5856368afd6d6f6.abstract: The digital era has revolutionized numerous facets of contemporary life, and film criticism is no exception. Traditionally confined to the pages of newspapers and specialized journals, film criticism has found new life on the internet, where online platforms have democratized and diversified the field. Today, anyone with a keen eye for cinema and an internet connection can publish reviews and analyses, challenging the dominance of established critics and broadening the discourse around film. This shift has not only expanded the audience for film criticism but also transformed the ways in which films are analyzed and discussed. The advent of the digital era has profoundly transformed film criticism, shifting the landscape from traditional print media to dynamic online platforms. Anchored on the technological determinism theory, this paper explores the role of these platforms in reshaping film criticism and analysis. Online platforms such as blogs, social media, and dedicated film websites have democratized the field, allowing a diverse array of voices to participate in the discourse. These platforms provide immediacy and interactivity, enabling rapid responses to new releases and fostering vibrant discussions. Furthermore, the integration of multimedia elements like video essays and podcasts offers a more immersive critique, enhancing traditional written reviews. However, this democratization also presents challenges, including the proliferation of content, the difficulty of discerning credible voices, and the polarization of online discourse. Despite these issues, the influence of online platforms is undeniable, representing a significant evolution in film criticism. This paper examines the opportunities and challenges presented by these digital mediums, highlighting their impact on how films are reviewed, interpreted, and appreciated in the contemporary era.

title: Research on Ecological Imbalance and Sustainable Governance of Algorithmic Platforms
container-title: Studies in Social Science Research
65ed07ab4fc85e8bb0b264efb333e81d1ce0923c.abstract: The widespread application of artificial intelligence and algorithmic technologies has gradually made algorithmic platforms an important field for information dissemination, social interaction, and value creation. However, while algorithmic recommendation and data-driven resource allocation mechanisms improve operational efficiency, they may also give rise to problems such as capital concentration, the homogenization of actors’ behavior, and a decline in ecological diversity. Drawing on Bourdieu’s field theory, this paper conceptualizes algorithmic platforms as a new type of technological field jointly constituted by multiple actors, capital distribution, and technological rules, and analyzes the internal relationships among algorithmic habitus, capital concentration, and the erosion of diversity. This study argues that algorithmic platforms shape actors’ practices through data feedback and resource allocation mechanisms and may reinforce existing advantages in the ongoing process of structural reproduction, thereby causing structural imbalance in the platform ecosystem. Accordingly, this paper proposes basic pathways for the ecological governance of algorithmic platforms in terms of capital balance, actor empowerment, diversity protection, open governance, and collaborative governance, aiming to provide a theoretical reference for understanding the structural problems of algorithmic platforms and their sustainable development.

title: From Communication Anxiety to Psychological Reliance
container-title: Journal of Media Psychology
bfda88b1644227e14d7f234fea59df6cb5059730.abstract: Abstract: Grounded in self-determination theory (SDT), this study investigates how communication anxiety and psychological need satisfaction relate to the use of Large Language Model (LLM)-based chatbots, specifically ChatGPT, for communication tasks (e.g., writing emails, drafting messages, and preparing scripts). Using a three-wave panel survey of participants from the United States and South Korea, we examined both between- and within-person dynamics. Results showed that individuals with higher trait-level communication anxiety tended to use ChatGPT more frequently for communication tasks, whereas within-person fluctuations in anxiety did not predict greater use. ChatGPT use was positively associated with the satisfaction of basic psychological needs – autonomy, competence, and relatedness – and this need satisfaction, in turn, was associated with greater psychological reliance on ChatGPT. Importantly, need satisfaction further mediated the relationship between ChatGPT use and psychological reliance at both within- and between-person levels. Cultural comparisons revealed that US participants exhibited stronger momentary effects, while Korean participants showed more stable, trait-based patterns. These findings highlight the role of LLM-based chatbots as need-supportive communication tools that may become integrated into users’ communication practices over time, with implications for theories of AI-mediated communication, cross-cultural research, and the design of human-AI communication systems.

title: Effect of Multimedia Instruction on Secondary School Students’ Acquisition of Science Process Skills in Enugu Education Zone
container-title: RESEARCH JOURNAL OF MASS COMMUNICATION AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY
8eef6d8d32e577ec998a9807e2bf3131050f8478.abstract: This research examined the impact of multimedia-based teaching on secondary school student’s acquisition of science process skills within the Enugu Education Zone. The study was guided by two research questions while six null hypotheses were formulated and tested at 0.05 level of significance. The study was anchored on two theories namely, Cognitive Theory of Multimedia Learning (CTML) and Jerome Brunner’s Theory. Pretest-posttest non-equivalent control group quasi-experimental design was employed. 1,577 Senior Secondary 2 (SS2) chemistry students in Enugu Education Zone was the target population, from which a sample of 160 students was selected. Instrument for data collection was Science Process Skills Acquisition Test (SPSAT), which was validated by three experts. The reliability of the SPSAT was determined using the Kuder-Richardson Formula 20 (KR-20) which resulted in a reliability coefficient of 0.74. Over a six-week period, the experimental group was taught specific chemistry concepts using multimedia instruction (MI), while the control group received instruction on the same concepts through the conventional method (CM). Research questions were addressed using mean and standard deviation, and the null hypotheses were tested using analysis of covariance (ANCOVA). The results indicated that multimedia instruction significantly improved students' acquisition of science process skills compared to the conventional method. Based on these findings, it was recommended that chemistry teachers, students, and curriculum developers should integrate multimedia instruction as a teaching strategy, as it has proven more effective in enhancing students' acquisition of science process skills and overall academic performance in chemistry than the conventional approach.
