title: Differences in Translators' Cognitive Load under Generative-AI Post-Editing: An Eye-Tracking Study of English-Chinese Scientific Texts
container-title: Future of Social Sciences
7c7fe2b629e6642e4941218c5d737a4c99000526.abstract: {'en': 'Generative artificial intelligence has entered the translation workflow faster than evidence about its effect on the translator has accumulated. This study asks whether working from a large language model draft lowers cognitive load or merely redistributes it. Thirty-six translators, twenty translation trainees and sixteen practising professionals, rendered nine English popular-science and technical passages into Chinese under three within-subject conditions. These were unaided human translation (HT), post-editing of a static neural machine translation draft (NMT-PE), and post-editing of a GPT-4o draft with an interactive prompt pane (GAI-PE). Pupil diameter change, fixation duration, gaze distribution, keystroke logs, NASA-TLX ratings and MQM scores were recorded. GAI-PE cut task time by 44.2 per cent against HT and by 17.1 per cent against NMT-PE. Its MQM scores were higher than those of NMT-PE, while the difference from HT did not reach significance. Pupil diameter change was nevertheless largest in GAI-PE at 0.095 mm, against 0.083 mm in HT and 0.064 mm in NMT-PE, while gaze on the source text fell to 38.3 per cent, the lowest of the three. Subjective ratings moved the other way and ranked HT as the most demanding condition. In an exploratory analysis, self-reported AI-use frequency was associated with a smaller pupil response in GAI-PE, whereas English proficiency showed no such association. These observations are consistent with an increased demand for verification, though the generative condition also gave access to an interactive prompt pane, so the differences cannot be attributed to the model alone.'}

title: AI adoption in public sector urban planning: Aspirations and realities in London and Beijing
container-title: European Urban and Regional Studies
f67f375ebb7467938a2adac52365fc1497fb294b.abstract: This paper examines the adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) in public sector urban planning through a comparative analysis of London and Beijing. Drawing on rapid qualitative methods combining interviews with public sector planners and related actors with documentary analysis, it adapts and spatialises Wisdom et al.’s multi-level framework across four analytical dimensions: public policy contexts, financial conditions, legal frameworks and regulations, innovation, data and organisational determinants and individual planners’ values, skills and norms. A central finding is that AI means different things to different planners. Interviewees drew on two broad understandings: general-purpose large language model tools used informally for drafting and synthesis, and purpose-built planning-specific tools tied to particular statutory functions. In both cities, adoption is largely confined to the former, concentrated on downstream tasks such as drafting documents, while the latter remains exploratory and uneven. The paper demonstrates that barriers to adoption outweigh drivers, raising key questions about the uncertain direction of AI-led public sector planning delivery and its associated politics. Across both cases, the adoption of AI is less a narrative of inevitable technological transformation than a process of political, institutional and professional negotiation over what is considered acceptable, trustworthy and feasible. By geographically locating where AI is being developed, tested and used in planning and tracing how its influence is distributed across distinct urban governance contexts, the paper argues for repositioning debates on AI in planning away from deterministic narratives of technological transformation and toward a more critical, geographically and governance-led understanding of adoption and non-adoption.

title: Mapping multidimensional artificial intelligence anxiety among academic librarians in the United Arab Emirates: An exploratory survey
container-title: Journal of Information Science
3c01ea068af6fbf089f2134b3d74f524ade33ce0.abstract: This exploratory study examines artificial intelligence anxiety among academic librarians in the United Arab Emirates, a multilingual context undergoing rapid digital transformation. A cross-sectional online survey of 72 academic library professionals, recruited through purposive and snowball sampling, employed a newly developed 35-item instrument covering seven conceptually derived dimensions: job role evolution, ethical and bureaucratic concerns, patron resistance and social trust, governance and strategic alignment, infrastructure and digital divide, vendor and sustainability, and linguistic and cultural anxiety. Internal consistency ranged from acceptable to strong (α = 0.774–0.898). Overall, AI anxiety was moderate (M = 3.33 on a five-point scale), with ethical and bureaucratic concerns (M = 3.47), infrastructure and digital divide (M = 3.42), and vendor and sustainability concerns (M = 3.36) recording the highest means. However, the narrow range across construct means (0.23 points) warrants treating these differences as descriptive rather than substantive rankings. Concerns about storing patron data on foreign servers and shortages of skilled staff received the highest item-level ratings. Although women reported higher scores across all seven dimensions, no gender or other demographic differences remained statistically significant after correction for multiple comparisons. The findings highlight the institutional, infrastructural, ethical and governance conditions associated with AI anxiety in academic libraries. The proposed dimensions offer a context-specific framework for further investigation, subject to validation in larger samples. Practical implications include developing localized and multilingual AI tools, expanding inclusive professional development, and strengthening participatory governance of AI procurement and policy.

title: <b>Impact of AI Generated Content and Perceived Personalization on Purchase Intention with Mediating Input of Brand Credibility in FMCG Industry in Pakistan</b>
container-title: International Journal of Emerging Multidisciplinaries: Social Science
2613ec1fb9a9ce3dda839e8c6439ebcc1333759b.abstract: This research study investigated the empirical impact of AI generated content and perceived personalization on purchase intention with mediating input of brand credibility in case of FMCG sector in Pakistan. It investigated both direct and indirect of AI generated content and perceived personalization on purchase along with the impact of AI generated content on perceived personalization in Pakistan. The study used quantitative research approach and employed deductive approach to build hypotheses. Those were tested with application of statistical techniques i.e. structural equation model using PLS-Smart as software. The study targeted the FMCG sector in Pakistan and used convenience sampling technique to extract with the required number of responses i.e. 384 using questionnaire as data collection tool. The study followed with the survey based method to collect with the required number of response in the limited period of time. The study revealed that there is significant impact of AI Generated Content on Brand Credibility, Perceived Personalization and Purchase Intention with coefficient value of 0.4294, 0.5758 and 0.5211having significance value of 0.0000, 0.000 and 0.000 respectively. There is also a significant impact of Perceived Personalization on Brand Credibility and Purchase Intention with coefficient value of 0.4857 and 0.3093 having significance value of 0.0000 and 0.0000 respectively. There is also a significant impact of Brand Credibility on Purchase Intention with coefficient value of 0.4574 having significance value of 0.0000. FMCG companies should develop accurate, engaging, and personalized AI-generated content to enhance brand credibility and consumer confidence. Marketers should ensure truthful product information, transparent communication, and alignment with customer preferences.

title: Information-Seeking Behavior in Mice (Mus musculus) During Visual Discriminations: Evaluating Metacognitive and Alternative Accounts in a Target-Cueing Paradigm
57269f15847cb690fba46c77c9280cb37b0b79d4.abstract: Information-seeking behavior is often interpreted as evidence of metacognitive monitoring, but nonmetacognitive factors may also explain such behavior. We examined this issue in mice using a target-cueing procedure in which an information-seeking response produced a hint indicating the location of the rewarded stimulus. In Experiment 1, mice performed an orientation discrimination. In Experiment 2, the same mice performed a grating discrimination in which grating coarseness varied across trials. During training, some aspects of performance were compatible with a metacognitive account. In Experiment 1, information seeking did not increase reliably as the discrimination became more difficult, although hint use improved accuracy most clearly at smaller orientation differences. In Experiment 2, mice sought information more often at lower grating coarseness, and hint use was associated with the greatest accuracy benefit under those more difficult conditions. However, the critical test results did not support the prediction that information seeking would track the need for additional information. Mice frequently sought information in target-only trials, in which no additional information was required, and showed relatively low rates of information seeking in trials in which the initial display consisted of two identical, and therefore nondiagnostic, stimuli. These findings indicate that information seeking in the present task was multiply determined. The observed pattern was consistent with contributions from competition, reinforcement history, and the behavioral utility of the hint. Although some aspects of training remained compatible with confidence-based control, the critical test conditions showed that information seeking was not governed by confidence monitoring alone.

title: Satellite-based network-level pavement roughness estimation using dual-polarization Sentinel-1 SAR and deep learning
container-title: Journal of Information Technology in Construction
bb14ba67464371618eb8b35d9a8cb849a9664c01.abstract: Timely pavement-condition information supports network-level maintenance planning, but repeated profiler surveys require dedicated field campaigns. This study develops a scripted workflow that converts openly available Sentinel-1 synthetic aperture radar (SAR) observations into segment-level International Roughness Index (IRI) estimates and pavement-management outputs. A seven-configuration experiment separates SAR inputs (S), pre-inspection engineering information (P), and contemporaneous condition indicators (C) according to their availability relative to the target inspection. The study comprises 8,188 flexible-asphalt pavement segments in Alaska, Utah, and West Virginia, including 1,228 corridor-held-out test observations. SAR alone achieved a mean absolute error (MAE) of 14.8 in/mi. Under retrospective, inspection-aligned evaluation, combining SAR with pre-inspection information reduced MAE to 13.4 in/mi, compared with 16.1 in/mi for pre-inspection information alone. Full fusion achieved an MAE of 12.9 in/mi, an RMSE of 17.2 in/mi, and a squared Pearson correlation of 0.69, indicating only a further 0.5 in/mi improvement over the same-campaign condition indicators. Matched SAR-only AnySat and SkySense adaptations achieved three-seed mean MAEs of 14.2 and 14.5 in/mi, respectively. For the full-fusion predictor, MC dropout and split-conformal intervals achieved 89.6% and 90.2% empirical coverage, respectively, at a nominal 90% level. Uncertainty-guided screening flagged 8.4% of test segments while capturing 35.2% of errors exceeding 25 in/mi. The results support using an availability-aware satellite screening layer to prioritize field measurements within the evaluated domain.

title: Cross-Modal Self-Supervised Learning for Efficient Water Leak Localization with Micro Air Vehicles
container-title: Journal of Aerospace Information Systems
dd232925e9ea8f0238cbf8139001b6f400652687.abstract: Efficient water leakage detection is crucial for smart building water management. Conventional methods relying on fixed sensors are costly to install and maintain. Micro air vehicles (MAVs) offer a cost-effective solution for confined spaces but have limited processing power and payload capacity. MAVs are generally equipped with lightweight sensors, such as compact thermal cameras, which produce low-resolution images and typically limit the detection range. To enable effective long-range detection, this paper proposes a novel cross-modal self-supervised learning (SSL) setup, where a computer vision algorithm is designed to identify water leakage from thermal images. These thermal-based detections then guide the training of a deep learning model using color input images. Furthermore, a control strategy integrating the color-based deep learning model with thermal imaging is introduced to enable MAVs to provide preliminary long-range leakage detection and precise localization when approaching affected areas. The system was tested in both static setups and flight scenarios. In flight tests, the MAV successfully identified leakage across multiple trials, beginning from various initial positions and targeting different leakage sites. Results from both static and dynamic tests demonstrate the effectiveness of the control strategy and detection algorithm in localizing water leakage in indoor environments.

title: From automation to authorship: Computational reasoning and design agency in architectural AI tools
container-title: Journal of Information Technology in Construction
f459ddbe10d9229aeff00984e777729be2bb0281.abstract: The increasing presence of AI in architectural practice is renegotiating who, or what, holds creative authority over a project. This paper introduces a novel two-construct framework, AI Logic (AL) and Architectural Value (AV), to operationalise this shift. AL captures a tool's computational reasoning across automation, optimisation, and predictive capability, while AV captures design agency support, contextual sensitivity, and exploratory capacity. Positioning fifty AI-driven tools within this AL-AV construct via tension map analysis identifies stage-specific patterns within the selected dataset. It shows that design agency is redistributed unevenly across the project lifecycle, expanding in early design stages where tools act as creative collaborators, and contracting under efficiency-driven logics in later stages where automation prioritises monitoring and compliance over qualitative judgement. Cross-referencing against secondary parameters such as building typology, user group, tool maturity, and regulatory context surfaces fundamental gaps in current AI provision. The selected tools predominantly support residential and commercial applications. Documented regional orientations include North American and European standards, while coverage of other regions and typologies is less evident within the sample. To assess scoring consistency, ten AEC professionals and the author independently evaluated a subset of five tools, with one tool representing each of RIBA Stages 1–5. Intraclass correlation analysis demonstrated strong panel-level inter-rater reliability for both constructs, while comparison of the author's scores with the expert consensus indicated close alignment. Following this calibration, the author independently applied the same evaluation framework to the remaining forty-five tools. Beyond its analytical application, the framework offers a practical means of informing future AI development and adoption. It gives toolmakers a vocabulary for embedding stakeholder values in development decisions, and architects a means of recognising embedded biases before adoption, so that increasing automation extends rather than erodes the disciplinary and cultural values of architecture as a whole.

title: DIGITAL LABOUR AND EPISTEMIC ERASURE: A SEMIOTIC ANALYSIS OF INDIGENOUS KNOWLEDGE AND AI INFRASTRUCTURES IN HUMANS IN THE LOOP
container-title: Interdisciplinary Perspectives of Education
f3d3fff8613295115b19afeda98d7e4193beb31e.abstract: This paper explores how artificial intelligence (AI) and digital labour affect marginalised identities, using the 2025 Netflix film Humans in the Loop (directed by Aranya Sahay). Research follows the female protagonist of the film, named Nehma, an Indigenous (Adivasi) woman who works as a data labeller. Her deep, traditional knowledge about nature is ignored because of the way AI categorisation systems use a rigid, one-size-fits-all sorting method and act as epistemic hierarchies that erase Indigenous ways of living and thinking. Using a social semiotic approach, the research identifies a disconnection between local ecological knowledge and the rigid binary logic of machine-learning infrastructures. The article argues that digital frameworks mirror power dynamics inside educational institutions, where underrepresented students often have their cultural identity and cultural expressions erased or misrepresented. By analysing the lived experiences of marginalised communities, the study critiques techno-solutionist solutions and proposes solutions grounded in epistemic justice, cultural agency and equity and recommends that equitable AI systems require moving away from extractive labour practices to recognise the intellectual and cultural contributions of the Global South.

title: FROM DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION TO AI-ENABLED EDUCATION: A CRITICAL REVIEW OF EMERGING TRENDS, OPPORTUNITIES, AND CHALLENGES
container-title: Interdisciplinary Perspectives of Education
a30e8b5e4e056b3879ef048a09f681d3adc86be6.abstract: The higher education sector has seen the emergence of several technological advancements over the past two decades. These include learning management systems, massive open online courses, and the latest on the market: Generative Artificial Intelligence (AI). This paper aims to make a critical review of the shift from Digital Transformation to AI-driven education as a whole. The paper particularly emphasizes the shift of the digital transformation from being an administrative phenomenon to being more of a central feature in education. The paper summarises the literature on the concepts of digital transformation, the implementation of generative AI, and adaptive learning and AI ethics in the teaching and learning process, based on peer-reviewed papers that were mainly published in Scopus and Web of Science from 2019 to 2026. There are three themes that are repeated in the literature. First, AI in education is a further step towards digital transformation in which capacity building processes are substituted with independent decision making. Second, personalisation, accessibility and efficiency are opportunities, not equally accessible or equally taken up, nor equally realised; and these opportunities go first to the best resourced institutions.

title: FROM FINANCIAL LITERACY TO AI LITERACY: PREPARING COMMERCE STUDENTS FOR ALGORITHM-DRIVEN FINANCIAL DECISION-MAKING
container-title: Interdisciplinary Perspectives of Education
d04ff6220a1856d2870fe7a9d4e5c017fc060084.abstract: Artificial intelligence is becoming increasingly visible in everyday financial activities. Students and consumers now encounter automated financial recommendations, digital investment platforms, personalised financial information and AI-based tools when making or evaluating financial choices. This changing environment raises an important question for Commerce education: is conventional financial literacy sufficient when financial information is increasingly mediated by algorithms? The present study examines financial literacy, AI literacy and awareness of ethical issues associated with AI-supported financial applications among Commerce students, and investigates their relationship with algorithmic financial decision quality. The study follows a descriptive and analytical research design and considers 250 student observations. Data were examined using descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation and multiple linear regression. Four major constructs were considered in the analysis: financial literacy, AI literacy, ethical awareness and algorithmic financial decision quality. The findings show that financial literacy recorded the highest mean score (M = 3.56), while AI literacy recorded a comparatively lower mean score (M = 3.33). AI literacy demonstrated the strongest correlation with algorithmic financial decision quality (r = .705, p ≤ .01), followed by financial literacy (r = .623, p ≤ .01) and ethical awareness (r = .605, p ≤ .01). The regression model explained 67.2% of the variation in algorithmic financial decision quality. AI literacy emerged as the strongest predictor (β = .443), followed by financial literacy (β = .376) and ethical awareness (β = .199), with all three predictors statistically significant at p ≤ .001. The findings suggest that financial knowledge remains essential, but it needs to be complemented by the ability to understand, question and evaluate AI-generated financial information. Commerce education therefore needs to move towards an integrated approach in which financial literacy, AI competence and ethical awareness support independent and responsible financial judgement.

title: THE ROLE OF AI-POWERED DUOLINGO AND ELSA SPEAK APPS IN REDUCING SPEAKING ANXIETY AMONG ENGLISH LEARNERS IN PRIVATE UNIVERSITIES OF DHAKA, BANGLADESH
container-title: Interdisciplinary Perspectives of Education
b4447b00af53cabbd7382ac95aa5cf3980f3e6c5.abstract: This study has explored the influence of speaking anxiety as a major obstacle for English as foreign language learners (EFL) in their non-native environment like in the private universities in Dhaka, Bangladesh. With the up rise of Artificial Intelligence, English language learning applications have incorporated AI-based features to enhance the learning experience. This finding examined how AI-supported speaking apps, in this instance, Duolingo and ELSA Speak, reduce speaking anxiety and increase learners' confidence, fluency and speaking skills through AI-driven personalized feedback, gamified interaction and adaptive learning. This research used mixed-method approach, which included qualitative and quantitative methods to provide comprehensive insights and understanding. The results of the study pointed to the effectiveness of AI-based language learning apps in creating a supportive language-learning atmosphere, enhancing the learning process and reducing stress levels when practicing oral communication. The results of this study could contribute to the understanding of how AI-based app-based learning can be incorporated in the university curriculum and evidence-based recommendations for teachers, educational technology designers and policy makers.

b650139a647d3fa0043c741b3798d65a029ce8d3.abstract: The construction industry continues to experience high rates of serious injury and fatality worldwide, motivating an increasing interest in advanced digitalization strategies that combine building information modeling (BIM) with digital twin (DT) capabilities. By linking static semantic site models with continuous field data, these systems offer a powerful approach to proactive risk management. However, while individual remote sensing and predictive analytics components are well researched, a unified understanding of how these BIM and DT safety systems are integrated remains critically limited. Specifically, there is a clear need to understand how system capabilities evolve across different maturity stages and what underlying factors drive this progression across the construction lifecycle. This paper presents a comprehensive scoping review of BIM and DT integration for construction safety management across the entire project lifecycle. Using a tiered evidence strategy and structured thematic coding, the existing literature is synthesized through three main analytical lenses: integration mechanisms and data exchange patterns, maturity characteristics and capability horizons, and the socio-technical factors that systematically influence maturity transitions. This review clarifies the dominant architectural integration approaches and maps current proof-of-concept efforts against the requirements for more predictive and governance-ready safety twins. The findings indicate that most implementations remain at the interactive monitoring stage, with predictive capability emerging mainly in data-rich contexts and autonomous adaptation not yet realized. Furthermore, it identifies persistent bottlenecks in data interoperability and real-time processing that currently hinder widespread industry adoption. Finally, the study proposes a focused research agenda designed to help transition these intelligent monitoring systems from isolated prototypes to robust, scalable applications suitable for safety-critical construction environments.

title: Evaluating the Use of Digital Technology Tools by Instructors at Veritas University Abuja for Instruction and Learning
container-title: RESEARCH JOURNAL OF MASS COMMUNICATION AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY
6c8964bba5fe22443fe1b0e59d6d271082000c3f.abstract: The study looked into how instructors at Veritas University Abuja used both traditional and digital pedagogical approaches and methods in their teaching and learning. The primary goal was to determine the number of university arts and social science faculties that have embraced the use of digital technologies for lecturers' classroom instruction and learning, as well as whether or not this use of technology is properly documented. A descriptive survey was the approach taken. 240 instructors from 12 faculties at Veritas University in Abuja were selected at random using a standardized questionnaire. According to the study's findings, only the education faculty has successfully embraced the use of technology in the teaching-learning process; the other faculty members have not yet done so because of a number of issues, including erratic power supplies and poor internet connectivity, among others. Based on the results, it was suggested that the university administration supply sufficient digital technology equipment for teaching and learning in order to improve the proper use of digital technology for university instruction.

title: From Frankenstein to Gulliver urbanism: Reframing AI and scale in urban theory
container-title: Urban Studies
5c314f44fcff78a684da7faa849271a26877753c.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly embedded in urban governance, infrastructure and design, yet urban theory still lacks a clear language for analysing the scale asymmetries through which these systems operate. This article develops Gulliver Urbanism as a conceptual framework for understanding how AI reshapes urban power when it processes information, acts, and coordinates across cognitive, temporal and spatial horizons that exceed ordinary human capacities and institutional rhythms. Moving beyond Frankenstein Urbanism’s emphasis on rebellion and loss of control, we argue that the central problem of contemporary AI urbanism is scale asymmetry within co-constituted human and machine assemblages. The framework comprises six dimensions: cognitive scale, temporal scale, spatial scale, governance asymmetry, autonomy and agency and human response. It synthesises scholarship on AI urbanism, urban political economy, infrastructural urbanism, posthumanism, law and scale, supported by AI governance frameworks and vignettes on Hangzhou City Brain, robotaxis and generative design. The article conceptualises the urban as a constitutive condition of AI scale asymmetry, where algorithmic systems encounter infrastructure, land, mobility, public services, municipal authority, social difference and collective life. Across these domains, the key challenge is how to govern systems whose capacities outpace human oversight while remaining embedded in corporate, legal and political arrangements. We argue that effective responses require mixed-intelligence governance and temporal dignity: arrangements that subject algorithmic operations to democratic oversight, contestation and human-paced deliberation. Gulliver Urbanism explains how AI reconstitutes urban life by reorganising infrastructures, municipal authority, spatial relations, design imaginaries, public services and everyday citizenship.

title: Artificial Intelligence and Digital Innovation in Smart Tourism Destination Management: An Integrative Review and the AI-SDM Framework
container-title: Inkubis : Jurnal Ekonomi dan Bisnis
b9b2afe723164bea6e7be350837363abda6c2fe3.abstract: Background: Artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming tourism destinations through personalized services, conversational and generative interfaces, predictive analytics, and data-driven decision-making. Yet technology adoption alone does not explain how destinations convert AI-generated information into coordinated managerial action. Objective: This study addresses that organizational problem through a conceptual integrative review of research on AI-enabled tourism services, smart destination management, destination governance, visitor experience, organizational capabilities, workforce readiness, and responsible data practices. Methods: The synthesis identifies four interconnected application domains: AI-driven personalization, conversational and generative visitor interaction, predictive visitor-flow analytics, and data-driven destination governance. These domains are abstracted into the AI-Enabled Smart Destination Management (AI-SDM) framework, which connects AI-Enabled Service Capability, Smart Destination Governance Capability, and Visitor Experience Outcomes. Results: Visitor and operational intelligence functions as the principal conversion input, while visitor-generated behavioral and experiential feedback supports subsequent organizational learning and AI adaptation. Workforce AI Readiness and Responsible Data Governance are positioned as enabling conditions. The framework contributes to destination-management theory by shifting attention from AI adoption toward the organizational capability required to sense relevant visitor information, interpret and coordinate responses, and responsibly convert intelligence into destination action and visitor value. It complements broad smart-tourism and emerging cognitive-destination architectures by specifying the organizational intelligence-to-action mechanism that links AI-enabled interactions with destination governance and learning. Conclusion: The paper concludes with propositions and an empirical research agenda for measurement development and validation.

title: Addressing Skills Acquisition and Technical Gaps in Polytechnic Education System in Nigeria: An Overview of the Loopholes and the Way Forward
container-title: RESEARCH JOURNAL OF MASS COMMUNICATION AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY
e7f65d4a13d89d5abee92422a96ffa35d6546fa5.abstract: Polytechnic education by nature is a skill acquisition and technical oriented institution designed and established to train and equip students with the necessary skills and knowledge that will enable them take up the role of technicians, technical officers, instructors and mechanic/engineers among others, with well-equipped practical knowledge and technical know-how about issues and finding solutions to the problems through logical and pragmatic approach, and to make them self-reliance. These objectives has however, not been achieved in most Nigerian polytechnics owning to the fact that most of our polytechnics, lacks the required tools and equipment such as, power (electricity), poor industrial collaboration and linkages as well as inadequate qualified and competent manpower to train and equip the students with the required knowledge. The only way to achieve this is to address the loopholes and to seek and establish collaboration and linkage with industry and technical organizations that have the wherewithal to provide practical training and equip these students with the pe-requisite knowledge necessary for them to excel in their various chosen carrier. This research work explore the acts establishing polytechnic education in Nigeria, the mission and vision as well as the objectives of their existence through documentary, textbooks, periodical, internet materials, articles and government publications. This is assessed against the background of their equipment, funding, available manpower, training strategy and identifying loopholes that hinders the realization of the set objectives despite the numerous polytechnic institutions in Nigeria. It is the believe of this research work that if the necessary required training equipment needed to train and equip students are readily available , adequate funding and adequate manpower to train and retrain, motivate and encourage staff, provide enabling environment, improved condition of service, there is no doubt that polytechnic education will be in better position to provide the much needed technical manpower for our industries and organizations which will lead to overall progress and development in our society

title:
AI-Driven Prediction
of Allergenicity and Toxicity
in Novel Plant-Based Peptides
container-title:
Journal of Agricultural
and Food Chemistry
2a004857507a7863943c7cfc6535a201d564ba4b.abstract: Abstract Peptides from plant sources have antihypertensive, antioxidative, and antimicrobial properties but also entail a risk of allergic and toxic reactions that cannot be detected in conventional wet-lab assays. This review examines deep learning techniques and protein language models for their prediction, from linear motifs screening to transformers (BERT, ESM). The best-performing tools achieve high sensitivity (pLM4Alg 96.2%, ToxinPred3 95.8%) but low specificity and positive predictive value (pLM4Alg 92.8% and 81.7%), meaning that most predictions are false positives. There are four major constraints on the generalization capabilities of these tools: scoring of native peptides while proteolytic processing yields post-translational modifications and neoantigens; training samples correspond to IgE binding, not clinical manifestations, and are biased toward well-characterized organisms; T-cell immunity, microbiome, and organ-specific toxicity are scarcely modeled; and regulatory agencies do not consider in silico predictions sufficient. AI currently serves best as a prioritization filter, not a replacement for biological assays.

title: A Study of Awareness, Perception, Use and Challenges of Information and Communication Technology Among Public Relations Practitioners in Anambra State, Nigeria
container-title: RESEARCH JOURNAL OF MASS COMMUNICATION AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY
a80c4b404d26b7171db4b3a9ecb3dc625862aa10.abstract: The study sought to discover the awareness, perception, use and challenges of Information and Communication Technologies among Public Relations practitioners in Anambra state. Guided by four research questions, and anchored on the Technological Determinism theory, the study adopted a survey research design with the sample size of 98 respondents. The researchers discovered that PR practitioners in Enugu state are significantly aware of Information and Communication Technology in their daily professional practice. They also found out that PR practitioners perceive ICT as an essential tool for public relations practice; they as well see ICT as a significantly helpful tool that enables PR practitioners in Anambra state effectively discharge their duties. Furthermore, they perceived ICT tools as expensive and that it needs a lot of professional training for its effective use. The researchers similarly perceived these ICT tools as complementary, rather than displacing the old media of PR. The study also revealed that PR practitioners in Anambra state largely make use these tools in their daily professional practice. They also discovered that high cost of ICT gadgets, poor access and low internet penetration, poor power supply and lack of training in ICT remain the predominant challenges that PR practitioners face while carrying out their professional duties.

title: Drawing the AI Boundary in Production Networks
container-title: CESifo Working Papers
dc7897d2e5e5a766111eedcd730f86d3b1ed8c3a.abstract: A technology can appear less connected to the economy when its definition expands to include more connected industries. We separate constituent connectivity from exposure crossing the group's boundary and show how internalizing links can reverse rankings. Using 2017 U.S. input–output accounts, we compare artificial intelligence (AI) with matched industry groups. Narrow and broad AI rank above the 96th percentile of internal shares among similarly sized groups, but fall to the 24th and 55th percentiles after also matching sector composition and connectivity. Sector composition accounts for most of the decline, distinguishing AI's industry mix from unusually strong connections among its members.

title: Readying the minuteman: Health information technology system design to enhance Army National Guard mission readiness
container-title: The Journal of Defense Modeling and Simulation: Applications, Methodology, Technology
c936e72d6ffd69eced906ed6bfa5dcc82da25e05.abstract: Sustaining soldier health is fundamental to force readiness, as mandated by the Department of War medical readiness policy and Army regulations. Traditional metrics, such as the Medical Readiness Classification Go, offer only a snapshot of medical preparedness for a single day and do not possess predictive capabilities for long-term strategic planning. This research presents an innovative design for a health information technology system that employs system availability analysis on the Army National Guard’s Medical Readiness Reporting (Medical Electronic Data for Care History and Readiness Tracking) System, transforming readiness assessment from a static classification to a dynamic, temporal measurement. Aligning medical data with strategic forecasting enables the Army Medical Department and the Army National Guard Office of the Chief Surgeon to make data-informed decisions and allocate resources more efficiently across various populations. The approach strengthens the link between medical investment and readiness outcomes, supports predictive readiness planning, and enhances the Army National Guard’s capability to sustain deployable forces under the developing requirements of the Department of War.

title: A moderated mediation model: depressive symptom, loneliness and social support among immigrant and Portuguese population
container-title: Journal of Public Mental Health
6629bed429a1462e515338c4901f1e2aefe2dbd8.abstract: Purpose The purpose of this study is to analyse the mediating effect of loneliness in the relationship between social support and depressive symptoms among Portuguese and immigrants residing in Portugal. Moreover, the study aims to explore the moderating effect of population group, Portuguese sample and immigrant sample, in this mediation model. Design/methodology/approach Survey data were collected from a diverse sample of employed Portuguese and immigrant from May 2023 to January 2024. Participants completed the UCLA loneliness scales, Multidimensional Scale of Perceived Social Support and Depression, Anxiety and Stress Scale (DASS-21). The SPSS programme with PROCESS macro (Models 4 and 15) was used to test the hypothesis regarding the mediation and moderation effect. Findings The bootstrap analysis found that loneliness played a significant mediation role in the relationship between social support and depressive symptoms among Portuguese and immigrant populations. Moreover, the study found that the population groups played a significant moderating effect on the negative indirect effect of social support on depressive symptoms through loneliness. This effect was significantly higher in magnitude among the Portuguese sample. Originality/value This research advances the authors’ understanding of social support among Portuguese and immigrant populations while providing suggestions for interventions tackling loneliness and depressive symptoms.

title: KoDocXAI: A Quantitative Evaluation Framework and Benchmark for Explainability in Key Information Extraction from Korean Administrative Form Documents
container-title: Applied Sciences
3f1157d52f09b9512f9807a0ef78b70f39dcd0a7.abstract: Key information extraction (KIE) models are increasingly used in high-stakes document workflows, where each extracted value must be accompanied by evidence a reviewer can verify. Evaluating their explanations is difficult: human rationale annotation is costly, and in agglutinative Korean, subword tokens misalign with the units humans read. We present KoDocXAI, an evaluation framework and pilot benchmark for the explanations of KIE models on Korean administrative form documents. It derives a value-region rationale reference from existing KIE bounding-box annotations and scores value-region plausibility, whether or not an explanation localizes the extracted value; re-aggregates subword attributions to morphemes and eojeols (Korean spacing units); and measures faithfulness by modality-wise perturbation with the pretraining [MASK] token while protecting the ground-truth span. The pilot benchmark v1.0 covers five fields over 300 permit-and-authorization dispatch documents, 20% of which are doubly annotated. With a fine-tuned LayoutXLM, Integrated Gradients exceeds a random baseline on both axes, whereas attention rollout stays at baseline level under both a first-token and a span-level target. Span protection removes inflated faithfulness scores and a spurious aggregation-level effect. The modality interventions differed in strength, but under them the image channel contributed practically nothing, confining the validated scope to text and layout. These results hold for this document type and model; they support validating the measurement protocol itself and reporting explainability separately by axis and modality.

title: Omni-Flex GraphFormer: Parallel Fusion of Local Graph Aggregation and Global Attention Across Image Resolutions
container-title: Information
486564d19a14112ee291281e74085d1c8c166091.abstract: Graph neural networks (GNNs) capture local image structure with few parameters, whereas Vision Transformers (ViTs) model global context at a higher computational cost. We propose the Omni-Flex GraphFormer, which applies a graph branch (OMNIVIG: max-relative aggregation over a fixed 3×3 pixel neighbourhood) and a Transformer branch (FLEXIVIT: global multi-head self-attention) in parallel and sums their outputs. Because each baseline is the hybrid with one branch removed, comparing the three models on eight datasets from 8×8 to 96×96 pixels, under equal training budgets and over three seeds, is a controlled branch ablation. Global attention is decisive: the hybrid exceeds OMNIVIG in test macro-F1 on every dataset and in all 24 runs, by 3.7 to 15.1 points (Wilcoxon test, p=0.0078). Against FLEXIVIT, the hybrid has the best mean F1 on six datasets and a 40–62% smaller seed-to-seed spread on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100, but the difference is not significant (p=0.38). The graph branch adds only 0.5–3.1% to the number of multiply–accumulate operations, and under warmed-up timing, both models run at the same speed, whereas unwarmed timing overstates latency by up to 15×. Under Gaussian noise, the summed hybrid degrades like the graph branch, which motivates gated or attention-guiding fusion.

title: AI as a Thinking Partner in Sustainability-Oriented Mathematical Modelling: An Exploratory Study of Pre-Service Teachers’ Comparative Reflection
container-title: Sustainability
f75256d02bd41dd0c7af7d038095c547beeaaf35.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) is mostly used in education to generate solutions, provide feedback or support instruction; approaches that use AI outputs as objects of comparison and reflection remain less explored. This small-scale exploratory qualitative case study examined AI-supported comparative reflection in sustainability-oriented mathematical modelling. Twelve pre-service mathematics teachers individually developed models for a task on water use in a school garden and then compared them with a model produced by ChatGPT (GPT-4o), reflecting on the comparison in writing. Modelling products, written comparisons and reflection forms were analysed using inductive content analysis. The comparison prompted participants to question assumptions, identify limitations in both models and consider alternative variables and representations; most described how they would revise their models. Their accounts contained indications of critical, creative and metacognitive reasoning. However, several participants treated the AI output as an answer key, some of their critiques echoed weaknesses that the AI had listed about itself, and none noticed a computational inconsistency deliberately retained in the output. As the design included no comparison condition or pre–post measure, the findings describe patterns of reasoning displayed during the activity, not improvements in thinking skills or modelling competence. Implications for teacher education are discussed.

title: Communication Strategies of Hyprep for Environmental Remediation in Ogoniland
container-title: RESEARCH JOURNAL OF MASS COMMUNICATION AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY
2839a2bd6e6c8602eb8ef3131fd087b31c88da09.abstract: The study tends to examine the communication strategies employed by HYPREP for environmental remediation in Ogoniland, giving critical evaluation of the existing communication channels/strategies, the audience awareness level, their attitude towards the programme, as well as the challenges of the communication process towards the implementation of the clean-up programme in Ogoniland. The study adopted the GoalOriented Communication Theory (GOCT), Participatory Communication Theory (PCT) and Stakeholder’s Theory. The study also adopted the survey research design with a multi-stage sampling technique. With a sample size of 384 the said sample was drawn using Krejcie and Morgan sample size determination table. The research instrument used for data collection was a set of questionnaires. Data collected were analyzed using simple percentage with WMS. Findings of the study reveals that Ogoni audience have a high level of awareness of the HYPREP clean-up/ remediation programme in Ogoniland. However, they have a very negative attitude towards the communication plans for the implementation of the clean-up programme. This is traced to the fact that stakeholder’s view are not capture and an audience-development-centred communication approach is not encourage by HYPREP hence, the study recommends that: communication practice should be all inclusive and more of faceto-face (interpersonal communication) as well as regular town hall meetings in other words, there should be media integration approach to audience engagement SMS, social media, podcast, Radio alone cannot be successful in bring audience to participate in a particular development programme. HYPREP should make their activities very open and people oriented so as to enhance an even development in Ogoniland.

title: Synergistic antibacterial effect and improved pharmacokinetics of florfenicol in combination with sulfamonomethoxine sodium
container-title: Journal of Antimicrobial Chemotherapy
be02807430b9e0688ea2543db83e5bf8db57c254.abstract: Abstract Objective Florfenicol (FFC) and sulfamonomethoxine sodium (SMM-Na) are both broad-spectrum antibiotics for animals. FFC inhibits bacterial protein synthesis, whereas SMM-Na inhibits the bacterial folate pathway, suggesting a potential for synergy. However, the pharmacodynamic and pharmacokinetic interactions of their combination remain uncharacterized. This study evaluated the in vitro and in vivo interactions between FFC and SMM-Na. Methods The in vitro interaction was assessed against several bacterial strains using the checkerboard method to determine the fractional inhibitory concentration index (FICI). The physicochemical stability of the combination was tested. An in situ recirculating intestinal perfusion model in rats was used to assess absorption parameters. Pharmacokinetic studies in rats compared the combination therapy to monotherapies. The therapeutic efficacy was evaluated in a mouse model of Staphylococcus aureus pulmonary infection, with the combination administered at half the individual monotherapy doses. Results The FFC/SMM-Na combination demonstrated synergistic effects (FICI = 0.375) in vitro and remained stable for 7 h. Intestinal perfusion showed the combination significantly increased the absorption rate constants (Ka) and effective permeability coefficients (Peff) for both drugs. Pharmacokinetic analysis revealed improved relative bioavailability for both FFC (113.98%) and SMM-Na (113.29%), with distinct pharmacokinetic profiles: FFC showed higher Cmax and shorter Tmax, while SMM-Na exhibited lower Cmax and longer Tmax. In the infection model, the half-dose combination achieved a significant reduction in bacterial load and ameliorated lung pathology. Conclusion The FFC/SMM-Na combination exhibits synergistic antibacterial activity in vitro, enhances mutual intestinal absorption, improves the pharmacokinetic profiles of both drugs, and achieves comparable in vivo efficacy at reduced doses through a dose-sparing effect. These findings provide a pharmacological basis for the clinical exploration of this combination therapy against bacterial infections.

title: Effect of Interactive Video Variations on Secondary School Biology Students’Academic Achievement in Ecology in Abeokuta, Ogun State, Nigeria
container-title: RESEARCH JOURNAL OF MASS COMMUNICATION AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY
80415e2c8ad81a74f2cca215610342c292cb3906.abstract: The study investigated the effect of Interactive Video Variations Strategy on Secondary School Biology Students’ Academic Achievement in Ecology. Gender and Situational Interest served as moderating variables for the study. Quasi-experimental research design was used. 5870 SS2 Biology Students formed the population while 117 were selected through multistage sampling procedure as the sample. A purposive sampling technique was used to select two (2) public schools that took part in the study where intact classes were randomly selected. Instruments for data collection were: Ecology Achievement Test (EAT)(r=0.72), Ecology Situational Interest Inventory (ESII)(r=0.85). Data were analyzed using frequency, percentage, mean and Analysis of Covariance (ANCOVA) at 0.05 level of significance. The results revealed that there was a significant main effect of Interactive Video Variation on student academic achievement in Ecology (F(1,108) = 36.504, p < 0.05). There was no significant main effect of gender on students’academic achievement in Ecology, F (1,108) = 0.606, p> 0.05. There was no significant main effect of situational interest on students’ achievement in the Ecology in Biology F (1,108) =1.706, p> 0.05. There was no interaction effect of treatment and gender on students’ academic achievement in Ecology F(1, 108) =0.122, p> 0.05. There was no significant interaction effect of treatment and level of situational interest on students’ achievement in Ecology aspect of Biology F (1,108) = 0.538, p > 0.05. There was no interaction effect of Gender and situational interest on students’ academic achievement in Ecology (F(1,108) = 0.093, p > 0.05). There was no significant interaction effects of treatment, gender and situational interest on students’ achievement in Ecology (F(2, 189) = 1.383 , p > 0.05). The study concluded that Interactive Video Variations is more effective for teaching Ecology. It was recommended among others that teachers should use Interactive Video Variation regularly so as to enhance students’ understanding and retention of ecological concepts.

title: Physiological and Transcriptomic Responses of Armillaria gallica to Selenium: Bioaccumulation, Biotransformation, and Growth Promotion
container-title: Journal of Applied Microbiology
46e34f34d268246d0ac89ad5d5709c10d9a4fcbb.abstract: Abstract Aims Armillaria gallica is a medicinal fungus and key symbiont for Gastrodia elata cultivation. This study aimed to investigate the dose-dependent effects of exogenous selenium (Se) on mycelial growth, Se accumulation and biotransformation, antioxidant regulation, and transcriptional responses in A. gallica. Methods and Results Dose–response experiments showed that 20 mg L−1 Na2SeO3 optimally promoted mycelial biomass (47% increase) and Se accumulation (837.53 mg kg−1), with 99.71% of Se in organic forms, predominantly associated with polysaccharides and proteins. Physiological assays revealed enhanced SOD, POD, CAT, and GPx activities and reduced MDA content under Se treatment. Transcriptomic profiling identified extensive gene remodeling in ion transport, redox metabolism, carbohydrate metabolism, glutathione metabolism, and MAPK signaling pathways, with qRT-PCR validating key DEG expression patterns. Conclusions Appropriate Se concentration promotes A. gallica growth and enhances antioxidant capacity through coordinated transcriptional and metabolic regulation. The strong Se accumulation and biotransformation capacity position A. gallica as a promising candidate for Se biofortification and for developing Se-enriched Gastrodia elata via the Armillaria–Gastrodia symbiotic system.

title: Relationship Between Loneliness, Social Media Addiction and Peer Pressure Among Undergraduate Students
container-title: RESEARCH JOURNAL OF MASS COMMUNICATION AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY
0febf0e966979455b3d4d476307ae2e23f2ce1b1.abstract: The study investigated the relationship between loneliness, social media addiction and peer pressure among undergraduate students, two hundred and ninety-four (294) undergraduate students comprising 178 females and 116 males with an age range of 19-23 years, mean age of 20.66 and S.D 1.125 were drawn using multi-stage (cluster, simple random: by balloting and purposive) sampling techniques as participants from Enugu State University of Science and Technology, Enugu. Kiran-Esen (2002) Peer Pressure Scale (PPS), Russell, Peplau, and Ferguson, (1978) UCLA Loneliness Scale and Andreassen et al., (2012) Bergen social media addiction scales were used for data collections, a correlational design was adopted, and a Pearson moment coefficient was used as choice of statistic to analyze the data. The finding shows that loneliness did not relate to peer pressure, social media addiction did not also relate to peer pressure. Hence, feature researchers should study variables that can cause the occurrence of peer pressure.

title: Gender and Cyberbullying: Evaluating the Experience of Facebook Users Among Female Public Secondary School Students in Awka South, Anambra State.
container-title: RESEARCH JOURNAL OF MASS COMMUNICATION AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY
2d053c143dfdd66f5b64df6e291227063553dcbb.abstract: The study investigated the topic: "Gender and cyberbullying: Evaluating the experience of Facebook users among female public secondary school students in Awka South, Anambra State” The research design was survey, and a sample size of 300 respondents was chosen based on the sample size determining formula, as worked out by Comrey and Lee. Structured questionnaire was the instrument for data collection, while analysis of data was descriptively completed. The researchers found out that significant proportion of female public secondary school students in Awka South are largely bullied on the Facebook. They also discovered that majority of these students are seriously bothered when bullied online. The study also revealed that majority of the female students were regularly traumatized as a result of the online bullying, and that this seriously affected not only their social life, but academic performance in school. Finally, the study showed the different forms of cyberbullying which female public secondary school students face online to include: trolling, harassment, cyber-stalking, and some others which are similar to the ones already mentioned. Based on the foregoing, the researchers recommend among others, that the school authorities and government should as much as possible, work hard to address the issue of cyberbullying among students. This the researchers suggest, could be done by organising seminars, talks and other educative programmes that will help inform these students on how to avoid being bullied online.

title: Analysis of Diverse Modern Family Planning Methods and Awareness of Its Health Implications Among Reproductive Mothers in Awka South, Anambra State.
container-title: RESEARCH JOURNAL OF MASS COMMUNICATION AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY
fa38ae5d3de8cb9b8040ca576e9a4cf9d5c9e6e3.abstract: The study examines the awareness, utilization, and health implications of diverse family planning methods among reproductive mothers in Awka South, Anambra State. This study employed a survey design. The study used a sample size of 370 respondents, proportional and multi-stage sampling technique was used to select the respondents. The questionnaire was used as an instrument of data collection. Statistical Package for social science (SPSS) version 19 was used to analyze the data. The study was anchored on the Health Belief Model (HBM) and the Social Cognitive Theory. The findings of the study revealed that majority of reproductive mothers in Awka South are aware of the diverse family planning methods, and that the primary sources of information about family planning methods are colleagues/friends/family and healthcare providers. The study also found that respondents experienced side effects from using family planning methods. Therefore, this study concludes that by focusing on education, healthcare access, and the development of safer contraceptive options, the health and well-being of reproductive mothers can be significantly improved.

title: Assessment of Taraba Broadcast Journalists Knowledge, Adoption and Usage of Artificial Intelligence in Journalistic Practices
container-title: RESEARCH JOURNAL OF MASS COMMUNICATION AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY
97118f0bf859026cd214d2e2d60880a341ce2bbe.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has become an essential tool in various fields, including journalism. However, the extent to which broadcast journalists in Taraba State, Nigeria embraced and utilized AI in their practices remains a subject of debate. It is on the above premise that this research examined Taraba State broadcast journalists' knowledge and usage of AI in journalistic practices. The paper was built on the technology acceptance model, diffusion of innovation theory, and social learning theory. The study adopted a qualitative approach where in-depth interviews were used. The in-depth interviews were conducted until the results reached saturation point. Findings of the study revealed that in journalists in Taraba State, Nigeria are slowly beginning to embrace AI for journalistic practice. However, there knowledge of AI usage for journalistic practices is low hence there is a significant knowledge gap that needs to be bridged. Therefore, the study recommends among other things that journalists in Taraba State need to gain more knowledge about AI and its potential applications in journalistic practices. The paper concludes that with proper training and guidance, journalists in Taraba State can harness the power of this AI technology to improve their reporting practices while ensuring ethical standards are upheld.

title: Repositioning Journalism Education in Nigeria: A Theoretical and Practical Evaluation of Experiential Learning, Social Constructivism, and Gatekeeping Imperatives
container-title: RESEARCH JOURNAL OF MASS COMMUNICATION AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY
f3d7b4d12aa35a1524436305181e0b3998bb790b.abstract: Journalism education in Nigeria faces significant systemic challenges that undermine its effectiveness in producing industry-ready graduates. Many journalism programs rely heavily on theoretical instruction, neglecting the practice-oriented and socially embedded nature of journalism as a profession. This paper critically evaluates the current pedagogical structures and proposes comprehensive reforms based on established educational and communication theories, particularly Kolb’s Experiential Learning Theory (1984), Vygotsky’s Social Constructivism (1978), and White’s Gatekeeping Theory (1950). Kolb’s Experiential Learning Theory emphasizes the need to integrate field-based reporting assignments, newsroom simulations, and project-based learning into the journalism curriculum to foster industryrelevant competencies. Social Constructivism, advocate for structured mentorship where practicing journalists guide students through increasingly complex reporting tasks. Gatekeeping Theory reveals that journalism education in Nigeria must go beyond the mechanics of news writing to interrogate the power structures, commercial interests, cultural biases, and algorithmic influences that shape what ultimately becomes news. The study concludes that effective journalism education in Nigeria must transcend the boundaries of traditional lecture halls.It must adopt holistic, experiential, and socially embedded pedagogical models that incorporate industry practitioners as lecturers, embrace collaborative reporting projects, and establish campus-based newsrooms. The integration of practicing journalistsinto academia, curriculum flexibility, and a deeper engagement with gatekeeping dynamics are not optional but essentialstepsto producing journalists capable of advancing societal progress and democratic accountability in Nigeria.

fdc0b4b8939db7db25cfc6732518bc99b63751d8.abstract: This study examines the evolution and competitive positioning of the United Kingdom's AI startup ecosystem amid the rise of generative AI. Using a qualitative desk-research design based on secondary investment data, policy documents, and academic literature from 2015-2026, the study analyzes how the UK has transitioned from a research-driven niche to a globally recognized hub, leveraging world-class universities, dense financial and healthcare markets, and a principle-based regulatory framework. Growth has been propelled by a robust spinout cycle from anchor institutions and accessible early-stage capital. Despite these strengths, structural constraints threaten long-term scale, including a persistent late-stage funding gap, infrastructure bottlenecks in compute access and energy costs, and intensifying global competition for talent. The study finds the UK is best positioned to capture value in autonomous enterprise agents, AI for scientific discovery, and multimodal systems. Sustaining global competitiveness will require expanding domestic growth capital, ensuring reliable compute access, and maintaining regulatory clarity without stifling agility.

7e3db4dbc77739016ee4d8b8960f6a9cf31acbf6.abstract: The study assessed the quality of services provided by academic libraries in selected Colleges of Education across North Central Nigeria. Using a descriptive survey research design, data were gathered from 400 respondents, including students, lecturers, and library staff, across seven institutions. The findings revealed a generally positive perception of physical infrastructure, particularly in terms of cleanliness, seating, and lighting. However, significant deficiencies were noted in basic amenities such as restroom facilities, power supply, and building maintenance. Although users appreciated the availability of reference materials and found library catalog systems easy to use, access to updated resources, digital tools, and reliable internet remained major concerns. Satisfaction was highest with staff support and library orientation programmes, while dissatisfaction was reported in borrowing procedures and user feedback mechanisms. The study was guided by the SERVQUAL model, which provided a framework to understand the gap between user expectations and service experiences. Based on the findings, the study recommends improvements in funding, digital infrastructure, service processes, and user training to enhance library effectiveness in teacher-training institutions.

b2ff5248217347df00a77ecdd94fcd1e63ca9a6c.abstract: Public libraries in Nigeria were established to meet the informational, educational, and recreational needs of the populace. This study assessed the performance of public libraries in Kogi West Senatorial District using a scorecard framework, with Stella Obasanjo Library in Lokoja as the only functional library. A descriptive survey design was adopted, involving 230 purposely selected users and staff. Data were collected via structured questionnaires and analyzed using descriptive statistics and Chi-square tests. Findings showed that while the library was spacious and accessible, it lacked reliable electricity, sanitation, security, and digital resources. Educational impact was low, with poor support for literacy, school research, and exam preparation. Resources were inadequate, with outdated collections, insufficient ICT tools, and staffing gaps. Though seen as socially inclusive, community outreach was limited. Hypothesis testing revealed no significant relationship between infrastructure or resource availability and literacy outcomes. The study concludes that systemic neglect and underfunding have limited the library’s impact, a situation that calls for urgent interventions from the government for necessary revitalization.

title: Public Awareness and Perceived Risks of Accessing Health Information Through Mobile Online Drug Vendors in Awka South LGA of Anambra State, Nigeria
container-title: RESEARCH JOURNAL OF MASS COMMUNICATION AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY
bf039c6c57aa553842a464aa812e67322255fbdb.abstract: This study examined the exposure and awareness of health risks associated with sourcing online health information from mobile drug vendors in Awka South LGA of Anambra State. The study investigated the dangers of purchasing medications online, including access to substandard, spurious, falsified and counterfeit (SSFC) drugs that can lead to adverse outcomes of death. The study was guided by four research question: To what extent are Awka South residents exposed to health information from online mobile drug vendors? What online platform do mobile drug vendors operate frequently? To what extent are Awka South residents aware of the health risks associated with obtaining health information from mobile drug vendors on social media? To what extent do Awka South residents believe in health information supplied by Mobile Drug Vendors on social media? Anchored on the Health belief Model, the study adopted the survey research method, with the questionnaire as the instrument of data collection. A sample size of 383 was determined using the Krejcie and Morgan (1970) formula for determining sample size. The findings reveal that Awka South residents are significantly exposed to health information from online Mobile Drug Vendors. It was also discovered that WhatsApp and Facebook were the major social media platforms that drug vendors operate frequently. The research further reveals that Awka South residents are significantly aware of the health risks associated with obtaining health information from Mobile Drug Vendors on the social media. Furthermore, the findings also reveals that significant number of Awka South residents do not believe in health information supplied by Mobile Drug Vendors. The researchers therefore recommended that communication experts get involved in the development of health behavior change messages that will teach the general public how not to swallow every health information they get online hook, line and sinker.

title: Shadow AI usage and ethical AI adoption: the moderating role of chief AI officer governance
container-title: International Journal of Organizational Analysis
31379c9b469f5547f923a3520026bf47ae6913ec.abstract: Purpose The rapid emergence of Shadow artificial intelligence (AI), the informal and unauthorised use of AI tools by employees, poses a growing challenge for global organisations. It creates cybersecurity threats, compliance risks, data breaches and ethical violations such as bias and opacity, ultimately undermining ethical AI adoption and stakeholder trust. Existing research often portrays the Chief AI Officer (CAIO) as a static role, focusing on compliance enforcement or policy integration while overlooking its potential to balance innovation and governance. This study aims to examine how the CAIO as a moderator influences the relationship between Shadow AI Usage and Ethical AI Adoption. Design/methodology/approach A deductive, theory-driven, cross-sectional research design was adopted, drawing on 665 AI practitioners and organisational decision-makers recruited through professional networks across multiple countries. Partial least squares structural equation modelling was employed to test the hypothesised moderating relationship. Findings Higher Shadow AI Usage was negatively associated with Ethical AI Adoption, whereas the positive Shadow AI Usage × CAIO interaction indicates that stronger CAIO governance attenuates this negative relationship. Originality/value This study contributes to AI governance research by conceptualising CAIO governance as an organisational boundary condition that attenuates the negative association between Shadow AI Usage and Ethical AI Adoption.

title: The Role of Librarians in Collection Management and the Use of Information Technology in Library Services

893fb8469417535dc876179a20885d158fa07602.abstract: Advances in information technology have prompted school libraries to adapt their collection management and services to users’ needs. In this context, the role of librarians extends beyond collection management to include the utilisation of information technology in the delivery of library services. This study aims to examine the role of librarians in collection management and the utilisation of information technology in library services, as well as to identify the supporting and inhibiting factors. The study employs a descriptive qualitative approach, with data collection techniques including interviews, observation and documentation. The results of the study indicate that librarians play a role in collection management through inventorying, classification, labelling, data entry and the organisation of the collection. Information technology is utilised to support collection searches, the borrowing and returning of books, and the guidance of students in using the library system. The implementation of collection management and services is supported by the availability of adequate facilities and collections, whilst constraints include a shortage of library staff, time constraints, and dependence on Wi-Fi networks. Librarians play a role in integrating collection management with the use of information technology in library services, although its implementation still faces limitations in terms of resources and network infrastructure.

title: Information Management Strategies and Effective Recruitment in Nigeria’s Oil and Gas Sector
container-title: RESEARCH JOURNAL OF MASS COMMUNICATION AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY
5c946e14df81c7bd530c06a861398a06f327b223.abstract: This study examines the impact of information management strategies on effective recruitment in Nigeria’s oil and gas sector, emphasizing the roles of data governance and access control in both internal and external recruitment. Using a quantitative research design, primary data were collected from 120 employees across major oil and gas firms. Descriptive statistics and regression analyses were applied to test the relationships among the study variables. The results reveal a strong positive correlation between data governance and internal recruitment (r = 0.742, p < 0.000), as well as between data governance and external recruitment (r = 0.716, p < 0.000). Similarly, access control showed significant correlations with internal recruitment (r = 0.689, p < 0.000) and external recruitment (r = 0.703, p < 0.000). These findings indicate that firms with effective data governance and strict access control systems experience more transparent, efficient, and merit-based recruitment processes. The study concludes that robust information management frameworks are crucial for achieving efficient, transparent, and merit-based recruitment in Nigeria’s oil and gas sector. The study recommends that oil and gas firms strengthen their data governance frameworks, adopt role-based access systems, provide continuous training on information security, and integrate digital recruitment platforms to improve efficiency and organizational competitiveness.

title: An Assessment of Naija FM 92.7 Radio Advocacy Campaign on Premarital Genotype Testing on Knowledge, Attitude and Practices in Ogoni Land
container-title: RESEARCH JOURNAL OF MASS COMMUNICATION AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY
c219f366934bb9c66ed6330396558d22dc721809.abstract: The study, "An Assessment of Naija FM 92.7 Radio Advocacy Campaign on Premarital Genotype Testing in Ogoni Land," investigates the impact of radio campaigns on promoting premarital genotype testing among the Ogoni people. This health intervention is vital in preventing hereditary diseases such as sickle cell anemia and thalassemia. Despite its significance, many individuals in Ogoni Land lack awareness about the benefits of premarital genotype testing and do not prioritize it in their marriage plans. The study is grounded in three key theories: the Diffusion and Innovation Theory, Agenda Setting Theory, and Multi-Stage Flow Theory. These frameworks guide the assessment of radio campaigns' influence on people's knowledge, attitudes, and practices regarding premarital genotype testing. A survey research methodology was employed to collect data from 400 respondents across four Local Government Areas in Ogoni Land.A multi-stage sampling technique ensured representation from diverse communities, providing valuable insights into people's awareness, attitudes, and practices related to premarital genotype testing. The study's findings highlight the need for improved radio campaigns to promote premarital genotype testing effectively. Recommendations include using simple language and cultural sensitivity to reach a wider audience, engaging community leaders, religious figures, and health workers in promoting premarital genotype testing, and implementing educational programs to increase awareness about its benefits. By implementing these strategies, radio campaigns can play a pivotal role in enhancing awareness, attitudes, and practices regarding premarital genotype testing, ultimately contributing to the prevention of hereditary diseases in Ogoni Land.The study's results underscore the importance of tailored approaches to health communication, emphasizing the potential of radio campaigns to influence health behaviors positively. By leveraging these findings, stakeholders can develop targeted interventions to promote premarital genotype testing, fostering a healthier community in Ogoni Land.

title: Student Engagement with Digital Library Resources through Learning Analytics in Adamawa State University, Mubi

bac75cd498df9d6c565016912780cdd9c210ab5e.abstract: This study investigates student engagement with digital library resources at Adamawa State University, Mubi, using learning analytics and survey data. A stratified sample approach was designed to obtain responses from 1,800 students across faculties. Measures included frequency of use, session duration, resource diversity, perceived usefulness, accessibility, digital literacy, and institutional use of learning analytics. Descriptive and inferential analyses — including ttests, ANOVA, and regression models — were employed. Results indicate that overall engagement with digital library resources is lower than neutral (mean engagement = 2.52/5), with no statistically significant differences across faculties. Awareness of learning analytics alone did not correspond to higher engagement; rather, infrastructural and user-related challenges (poor connectivity, limited digital skills, and usability issues) were significant negative predictors of engagement. The study concludes that implementing robust learning-analytics dashboards, improving digital infrastructure, and incorporating digital literacy training are key to increasing students’ meaningful engagement with digital resources. Recommendations include investment in reliable connectivity, targeted training programs, and dashboard-driven interventions to personalize resource recommendations and promote deeper use.

A structured questionnaire was used as the instrument for data collection. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics (mean and standard deviation) and inferential statistics (Pearson correlation and t-test) at a 0.05 significance level. title: When principles become policy: the institutional translation of responsible AI in national AI ​strategies
container-title: AI and Ethics
3806088112704c0bd67a1b4a2a21cd6770fe2e14.abstract: Abstract This study examines how Responsible AI (RAI) principles are translated as they move from ethical discourse into governance, standards, and national policy contexts. Drawing on comparative analysis of influential AI ethics guidelines, policy syntheses, and technical glossaries, the research traces how widely cited principles are reformulated across domains, using transparency and fairness as cases of how institutional translation operates in practice. It shows that while these principles originate as broad normative commitments, they become progressively institutionalized as policy categories, procedural requirements, and measurable technical properties. The comparison shows that the underlying mechanism generalizes across principles, while the resulting institutional forms remain principle-specific. Focusing on national AI strategies as a key site of institutionalization, the study analyzes how RAI principles are embedded within state agendas, regulatory approaches, and oversight mechanisms. This analysis reveals variation in how principles are prioritized and operationalized, reflecting differences in governance priorities, administrative capacity, and political context. The findings highlight that principles most amenable to standardization and measurement tend to dominate policy implementation, while more expansive ethical concepts are less visible. By mapping these shifts across institutional settings, the paper contributes to a deeper understanding of how AI ethics is reconfigured in practice and offers insights for policymakers seeking to balance technical feasibility with normative ambition in the governance of AI.

title: “Enhancing the Security of Information Resources in Academic Libraries: Challenges and Strategies for Sustainable Management – A Case Study of Adamawa State University, Mubi”
