ce6f9eb3de90107103f99b7a19bf3fa4e2ffe89e.abstract: This study titled “Enhancing the Security of Information Resources in Adamawa State University Library” examined the factors influencing the protection and sustainable management of information assets within the university library. The objectives were to identify existing security measures, determine challenges affecting information protection, assess staff ICT competence, and propose sustainable strategies for improvement. A descriptive survey design was adopted, and data were collected from 46 professional and paraprofessional library staff using a structured questionnaire based on a 5-point Likert scale. Descriptive and inferential statistical analyses, including Pearson correlation and multiple regression, were employed. Findings revealed that the library has implemented essential security measures such as access controls, surveillance systems, antivirus protection, and data backup routines. Staff exhibited high levels of ICT competence (M = 3.69, SD = 0.46), and security strategies were rated effective (M = 3.92, SD = 0.37). However, moderate challenges including limited ICT infrastructure, inadequate training, and poor funding (M = 2.75, SD = 0.58) were identified as major barriers. Correlation analysis showed significant positive relationships between ICT competence, security strategies, and effective resource management, while security challenges had a negative correlation (r = –0.652, p < 0.05). Regression results indicated that ICT competence, security strategies, and challenges jointly explained 62.1% of the variance in information resource management (R² = 0.621). The study concluded that information resource security in the library is largely determined by staff ICT competence, the robustness of security measures, and the extent of infrastructural and financial challenges. It recommends continuous ICT training, improved infrastructure, adequate funding, strict policy enforcement, and collaborative partnerships to strengthen security systems and ensure the long-term sustainability of library resources.

7b8359e2ec9accc2f4b7e5d0d8b274ba9b92300f.abstract: This study examined strategies for promoting equitable access to digital information resources in the Federal Polytechnic, Mubi library, focusing on bridging the digital divide among users. Data were collected using structured questionnaires and analyzed using descriptive and inferential statistics, including mean, standard deviation, and one-way ANOVA. title: Prediction of Grape Disease using Deep Learning based on MobileNetV2 and Explainable AI with Grad-CAM for Disease Management
container-title: International Journal of Advanced Research in Science Communication and Technology
6480a24874eeda23428f60c9d415447a4194461c.abstract: The grapes production can be affected by diseases that cause changes to the look and state of the leaves and may reduce the quality of the crop if the disease are not detected in time. Even though visual diagnosis is of some help, it depends on the operator's experience and can become difficult when different diseases show similar symptoms. The study presents an image-based approach for predicting and Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping (Grad-CAM) for providing a visual explanation. The System can detect four kinds of disease: Black Measles, Black Rot, Healthy, and Isariopsis Leaf Spot. The model produces a distribution of class probabilities and Grad-CAM is used to highlight the parts of the image that are related to the predicted class. A general module based on knowledge then provides information regarding the symptoms, advice on how to manage the disease, and preventive measures for the disease which has been predicted. Having been tested on 903 images, the system achieved 886 correct predictions and 17 incorrect ones, giving an accuracy of 98.12%, a weighted precision of 98.13%,a weighted recall of 98.12%, and a weighted F1-score of 98.12%. The errors that were seen were mostly between Black Measles and Black Rot. The study therefore incorporates prediction, visual explanation, and disease-management information into one workflow, while at the same time recognizing the need for further validation with a wider variety of field images..

efbc7d69199a07d52deb281b52055805ac95ac0e.abstract: This study examined innovative participatory communication approaches as catalysts for transformative social change in Abia State. The objectives of the study were to: determine the extent to which innovative participatory communication approaches are applied in promoting transformative social change; identify the challenges affecting their effective implementation; and assess their impact on community empowerment and sustainable development in Abia State. The research was anchored on the Participatory Communication Theory and Diffusion of Innovations Theory. The study adopted a descriptive survey design and covered a population of 1,425 participants, which comprised community-based organizations, non-governmental organizations, youth associations, media practitioners, and government communication officers across the 17 Local Government Areas of Abia State. Using Yamane’s formula, a sample size of 285 respondents was selected through stratified random sampling. Data were collected using a structured questionnaire and analyzed with descriptive statistics and a four-point Likert scale. Findings revealed that innovative participatory tools such as community radio, social media, and digital storytelling enhance inclusion, empowerment, and collective problem-solving. However, challenges such as poor internet connectivity, low digital literacy, and inadequate funding hinder effective implementation. The study concluded that strengthening innovative participatory communication with improved infrastructure, training, and supportive policy frameworks can drive sustainable and transformative social change in Abia State.

title: Digital Media, Citizen Journalism, Ethics and Self-Censorship
container-title: RESEARCH JOURNAL OF MASS COMMUNICATION AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY
b1b3a6c7787499a1aa4f10f270337b931845d929.abstract: This article looks at the impact of digital media on citizen journalism, ethics of journalism and self-censorship. There is no doubt that citizens have played a greater role in the advancement of the journalism profession, through on the spot collection and dissemination of news worthy events and pictures. This was made possible with the help of digital technology. Since these citizen journalists lack training in the profession, it seems that the core ethics of journalism have not been adhered to, in the course of their practice and the task of censorship remains daunting. Given the contributions of these invaders to the advancement of the work associated with journalism, citizens should be more involved, through a collaborative effort by media houses, who should encourage the citizenry, through training and the publication of their stories in their medium. This article assesses the effect of digital technology on citizen journalism, and made suggestions and contributions that encourage citizen journalism, stressed the importance of adherence to ethical codes and self-censorship, to establish a robust and sustainable relationship between the media and its publics.

title: Development and psychometric validation of the barriers to AI integration in nursing education scale (BAI-NE): a multi-institutional study
container-title: Scientific Reports
3e14fcc3f2fe59189db4f1f708cb00755b4bc751.abstract: Abstract This multi-institutional study aimed to develop and psychometrically validate the Barriers to AI Integration in Nursing Education Scale (BAI-NE). A methodological study with a mixed-methods exploratory design was conducted in two phases: scale development and content validation, followed by psychometric evaluation. The 15-item BAI-NE was developed based on the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology (UTAUT) and an extensive literature review. Content validity was assessed by a panel of ten experts. A convenience sample of 470 nurse educators from seven faculties of nursing participated in the study. The sample was randomly divided for Exploratory Factor Analysis (EFA; n = 235) and Confirmatory Factor Analysis (CFA; n = 235). EFA identified a four-factor structure explaining 42.7% of the total variance, comprising Technical and Infrastructure Barriers, Knowledge and Training Barriers, Ethical and Regulatory Barriers, and Attitudinal and Organizational Barriers. EFA factor loadings ranged from 0.566 to 0.738. CFA provided preliminary support for the proposed model, with good fit indices (χ²/df = 0.90, RMSEA = 0.00, CFI = 1.000, TLI = 1.015, SRMR = 0.043, GFI = 0.961); because χ² was lower than df and CFI and RMSEA were at their bounds, these values should be interpreted cautiously and replicated in independent samples. Standardized CFA loadings ranged from 0.54 to 0.82. Internal consistency was satisfactory, with Cronbach’s alpha values ranging from 0.713 to 0.754 and McDonald’s omega values ranging from 0.715 to 0.754. Test–retest reliability over a two-week interval was excellent for all subscales (ICC = 0.85–0.92). Convergent validity was modest, with composite reliability values exceeding 0.70, while AVE values ranged from 0.426 to 0.451. Discriminant validity was supported using the Fornell-Larcker criterion and HTMT values < 0.85. Among the four subscales, Knowledge and Training Barriers received the highest mean score (M = 14.0, SD = 2.51), followed by Attitudinal and Organizational Barriers (M = 13.1, SD = 2.63), Technical and Infrastructure Barriers (M = 12.8, SD = 2.68), and Ethical and Regulatory Barriers (M = 9.1, SD = 2.10). The BAI-NE demonstrated preliminary evidence of satisfactory validity and reliability and provides a practical instrument for identifying barriers to AI integration in nursing education, informing faculty development initiatives, institutional planning, and future research. The BAI-NE is intended to be scored and interpreted at the subscale level only.

title: Campaigns on Safe Motherhood by the Rivers State Ministry of Health and Compliance Among Post-Natal Women in Port Harcourt
container-title: RESEARCH JOURNAL OF MASS COMMUNICATION AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY
66b67a58b855710a1ab58383f714a8c8845d320a.abstract: The study investigated the health communication strategies adopted by the Rivers State Ministry of Health in promoting safe motherhood practices among post-natal women in Port Harcourt. Specifically, it examined four key areas: the communication channels utilized for campaign delivery, the level of awareness among post-natal women, the extent of compliance with recommended maternal health practices, and the challenges impeding effective implementation. Drawing on Social Cognitive Theory and Perception Theory, the research adopted a mixed-method approach. A quantitative survey was combined with qualitative interviews to provide a holistic understanding of maternal health communication dynamics within the study area, the research had a quantitative population of 2,365 post-natal women who are registered for post-natal care every month at the primary health centres in Port Harcourt and a sample size of 342 for the survey which was selected using convenience sampling technique and the population for the qualitative aspect had 18 member staff working at the Safe Motherhood Unit and Media Unit at the Ministry which judgmental sampling technique was used to adopt 50% of the population for the in-depth interview and they were selected using snowball sampling technique while the data was analysed utilizing the weighted mean score (WMS). Results indicate that although traditional media and interpersonal communication channels are commonly employed, awareness among postnatal women remains low. Moreover, compliance with safe motherhood practices is found to be inconsistent. In addition, the study identifies cultural resistance, limited outreach capacity, and insufficient stakeholder engagement as major obstacles to successful campaign execution. Consequently, the study recommends a strategic shift toward digital and community-based communication platforms. It further advocates for the institutionalization of postnatal education, the promotion of behavioural modelling techniques, and the enhancement of stakeholder collaboration. These measures are expected to improve both campaign effectiveness and maternal health outcomes in Rivers State.

title: No Universal Urban Form Heat Relationship: Contrasting Thermal Controls in African Cities
96192b762ad9fba5bbbd8c5c5d7c35e066221b8e.abstract: Rapid urbanization and climate change have intensified urban heat island effects. Tropical African cities face particularly high heat vulnerability, yet they remain underrepresented in urban thermal research. Existing research often assumes universal morphology temperature relationships, lacking cross city comparative evidence and spatially rigorous nonlinear attribution in African contexts. This study examines daytime land surface temperature (LST) associations with 11 multi dimensional urban morphological indicators in Lagos and Nairobi, using a nested 2 km spatial block cross validation framework coupled with XGBoost and SHAP analysis. Results reveal markedly city specific regulation patterns. In compact, densely built Lagos, population density dominates, while vegetation morphology is the primary control in fragmented, greener Nairobi. Nonlinear threshold effects are detected for building density in Lagos and vegetation height in Nairobi, and single shot imagery systematically amplifies factor contributions compared with multi temporal composites. These findings demonstrate that urban morphology temperature relationships are not uniform across African cities, supporting context specific rather than unified heat mitigation planning.

title: Beyond the Church Walls: Social Media, Authority, and Doctrinal Disputes Among Nigerian Pentecostal Pastors
container-title: RESEARCH JOURNAL OF MASS COMMUNICATION AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY
baf743f93f825d83695345e76875eb9cdf1b60b2.abstract: This article examined doctrinal disputes and social media engagement among six Nigerian Pentecostal pastors, focusing on how digital platforms have transformed religious communication and theological contention. Anchored on the Public Sphere Theory, the article emphasized the emergence of social media as a digital arena for doctrinal engagement. The research adopted qualitative content analysis. Online doctrinal materials—including sermons, debates, and audience interactions were systematically examined from six select Pentecostal churches between 2014 and 2024. Stratified systematic sampling was used to select 1,500 doctrinal posts from Facebook, Instagram, and X for thematic analysis. The article found that doctrinal disputes among Nigerian Pentecostal pastors on social media from 2014 to 2024 were confrontational, public, and amplified by digital platforms. The themes consistently revolve around grace versus works/law, prosperity gospel versus covenant faithfulness, and authority, miracles, and doctrinal purity. Conversely, social media also fosters inclusivity by allowing lay members, youth, and marginalized voices to participate in religious debates. The article concludes that while digital media democratizes religious communication, it simultaneously amplifies conflicts and challenges ecclesiastical authority. The study recommends that pentecostal church leaders should be encouraged to adopt a more constructive approach to online debates. Hence, institutions such as the Pentecostal Fellowship of Nigeria (PFN) and the Christian Association of Nigeria (CAN) can provide guidelines for digital engagement, emphasising respect, theological depth, and reconciliation rather than confrontation.

title: Green Software Tracker for Web Applications Using AI
container-title: International Journal of Advanced Research in Science Communication and Technology
e9e7dd3be86b4bfc4aaf051870fd54bd60832110.abstract: Web applications consume computing resources such as CPU, memory, and network bandwidth during request processing. High resource consumption can increase energy usage and contribute to carbon emissions. This research proposes a Green Software Tracker for Web Applications Using AI to monitor resource utilization and estimate the environmental impact of web applications. The proposed system uses Python and the psutil library to collect process-level CPU and memory data at defined intervals. It aims to estimate energy consumption using a documented estimation method and calculate associated carbon emissions using an appropriate electricity emission factor. A dashboard is planned to display resource usage, estimated emissions, a Green Score, and recommendations for improving software efficiency. The current recommendation approach is rule-based. Further implementation and experimental evaluation are required to validate the estimation method and assess the system's performance

title: Exposure and Challenges of Endogenous Media in Promoting Waste Reduction and Recycling in Rivers State
container-title: RESEARCH JOURNAL OF MASS COMMUNICATION AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY
dc22f9110356cceba906951a6757d174939a6b13.abstract: This study explored the exposure of residents to endogenous media contents and programmes on waste management and examined the challenges encountered by endogenous media in sensitizing the public on waste reduction and recycling in Rivers State. Anchored on the Social Responsibility Theory, the study emphasized the media’s responsibility to inform, educate, and guide the public towards sustainable environmental practices. A descriptive survey research design was adopted, with a population drawn from residents across selected local government areas in Rivers State. A sample of 400 respondents was determined using the Taro Yarmane Formular. Cluster and convenience sampling techniques were employed to reach respondents with relevant knowledge and exposure to endogenous media programmes, while interviews were conducted with media practitioners, community leaders, officials of the Rivers State Waste Management Agency (RIWAMA), and members of civil society organizations using the crtitical sampling technique. Data were analyzed using simple percentages for quantitative responses and thematic analysis for qualitative insights. Findings revealed that while urban residents enjoy higher exposure to sensitization programmes through radio, television, and digital platforms, rural communities experience lower levels of access due to infrastructural limitations, inconsistent programming, and weak collaboration between stakeholders. The study also identified major challenges facing endogenous media, including inadequate funding, lack of modern equipment, low audience engagement, language barriers, public mistrust, and cultural practices that hinder behavioural change. The study concludes that although endogenous media remain vital tools for promoting environmental awareness and cultural relevance, their effectiveness is constrained by structural and institutional barriers. It recommends increased financial support, improved infrastructural development, culturally inclusive messaging, and strengthened collaboration between media organizations, government agencies, and civil society to enhance the role of endogenous media in promoting waste reduction and recycling in Rivers State.

title: Evaluating the Validity of AI-Generated Writing Feedback for Students With Learning Disabilities
container-title: Journal of Special Education Technology
f14d7d18bb361d0034c674f8dc89d014df1bca80.abstract: Students with learning disabilities need clear, direct, and useful writing feedback. However, teachers often find it hard to provide this consistently because of time and workload pressures. New developments in generative artificial intelligence (AI) might help improve both the frequency and quality of feedback for students. Still, we know very little about whether AI-generated comments are valid or useful for struggling writers. This qualitative study looked at teachers' views on writing feedback from the AI-SCORE automated writing evaluation tool. Nine upper elementary and middle school teachers took part in two focus groups. They reviewed AI-generated feedback on student informational writing. They also discussed its clarity, teaching value, and suitability for students with disabilities. Thematic analysis revealed several areas for improving AI-generated feedback. Teachers want more guidance on specific revisions, language that suits students’ development, a consistent tone, and alignment with writing goals. They shared cautious optimism, noting that AI feedback could enhance teaching capacity and provide more practice opportunities for students, if it meets their needs. The findings stress the importance of teacher involvement, the potential benefits of AI for writing instruction, and key factors for creating AI tools that effectively support students with learning disabilities.

title: Evaluating the Visibility and Utilization of Media Sensitization Messages of Cholera Control by Residents of Awka North LGA of Anambra State
container-title: RESEARCH JOURNAL OF MASS COMMUNICATION AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY
b2f58fca4e53d0ebe835753c5607ea0c0c32746f.abstract: Cholera remains a significant public health challenge in many parts of Nigeria, especially with the recent outbreak of the disease in most parts of the country. Effective communication strategies are essential for its control and prevention. This study evaluates the visibility and utilization of media sensitization messages on cholera control among residents of Awka North Local Government Area (LGA) in Anambra State, Nigeria. This research employs quantitative surveys to assess the extent to which residents are exposed to, understand, and apply cholera prevention messages disseminated through various media channels. The study was anchored on two theories the Health belief model and the Agenda-Setting theory. Data were collected from a sample of 383 residents across different communities within Awka North LGA. Findings suggest that while a significant proportion of residents are aware of cholera prevention messages, the visibility of these messages varies across different media platforms, with radio and village health workers being the most prominent. However, the study also reveals gaps in message comprehension and practical application, particularly among populations with lower literacy levels and limited access to certain media types. The findings underscore the need for tailored communication strategies that consider local context, cultural factors, and media accessibility to enhance the effectiveness of cholera control efforts in Awka North LGA. The study concludes by recommending more inclusive and context-specific media campaigns, along with increased community engagement, to improve the visibility and utilization of cholera control messages in the area.

title: Influence of Online News Listenership on Mainstream Media: A Study of Owerri Metropolis Residents

f36db561c0078f99654d9012d4be474d5781f8c1.abstract: The paper examined the influence of online news listenership on the mainstream media among residents of Owerri Metropolis. To achieve this, relevant empirical studies by other scholars were reviewed which aided the present study in knowing what was found previously. The paper adopted the source credibility theory and the medium theory, Survey design was adopted for the methodology, the study had a projected population of 560,700^from which a sample size of 384was arrived at using the Wimmer and Dominick online sample size. The multi-stage sampling technique was adopted with the use of questionnaire as the instrument for data collection. The study found out that the majority of the respondents' level of digital media/ICT literacy is moderate at 35%.; a majority of the respondents' level of listenership to online news is high at 3 5%. Result also revealed that, at an average mean of 3.5, the respondents showed a favourable and positive perception about online news contents, although, they view online news contents that they are not so true and factual sometimes. Findings further indicated that, at an average mean of 3.1, online news listenership affects the audience of the mainstream media because the audiences resort to online news due to ease of access and convenience, the study concluded that, the advent of the new media/internet has thoroughly changed the face of journalism and the nature of audience consumption of news in the world today as people nowadays, access the Internet for updated news at any given time irrespective of location'." The paper, recommended that, sources of news contents should always be verified and authenticated before audience's consumption to avoid misleading the audience with fake information. Also, the mainstream media should up their digital presence as people now resort to the internet for online news.

title: The Effect of AI Absorptive Capacity of Organizations on Workers’ Perceptions About Smart Work Environment Perception Towards Digital Innovation Behavior.
container-title: WSEAS Transactions on Information Science and Applications
743b00c8552a137b4c5e81a5f74226040cc68957.abstract: This study investigates the effect of organizational artificial intelligence (AI) absorptive capacity on employees’ perceptions of the smart work environment and how these perceptions influence their digital innovative behavior in the telecommunications industry, with Digital Transformational Leadership as a moderating variable. In this study, two important theoretical perspectives were utilized: Absorptive Capacity Theory, which highlights how organizations acquire, assimilate, and apply their knowledge related to AI, and Socio-Technical Systems Theory, which addresses the connection between technology and the social aspect of the working environment. A quantitative research design was used through partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM). The data were gathered from 279 respondents working in the telecommunication industry in Jordan. These respondents worked for internet service providers, network operators, and mobile network operators. The findings show that organizational AI absorptive capacity has a strong positive effect on Smart Work Environment Perception (β = 0.742), which in turn enhances Digital Innovative Behavior (β = 0.681). Smart Work Environment Perception partially mediates the relationship between AI absorptive capacity and Digital Innovative Behavior (indirect effect β = 0.506), while Digital Transformational Leadership positively moderates the relationship between AI absorptive capacity and the smart work environment (β = 0.276) and between the smart work environment and Digital Innovative Behavior (β = 0.241). The current research adds value to the literature surrounding AI adoption within organizations by examining how technical capabilities and organizational leadership help foster Digital Innovative Behavior in the telecommunications industry.

title: The Impact of ICT Adoption on Financial Management Efficiency in Federal Polytechnics
container-title: RESEARCH JOURNAL OF MASS COMMUNICATION AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY
7ba773420b9b9978d8a556fbfa4160f41eab4d80.abstract: This study examines the impact of Information and Communication Technology (ICT) adoption on financial management efficiency in Federal Polytechnics in Nigeria. ICT has revolutionized the way educational institutions manage their finances, providing opportunities for accuracy, accountability, and transparency. Using a descriptive survey design, data were collected from bursary and finance departments across selected Federal Polytechnics in North-East Nigeria. Descriptive and inferential statistics, including regression analysis, were used to determine the effect of ICT adoption on financial management efficiency. Findings revealed that ICT adoption significantly enhances efficiency in budgeting, revenue collection, expenditure control, reporting, and auditing. However, challenges such as inadequate ICT infrastructure, poor maintenance culture, limited technical skills among staff, and irregular power supply hinder optimal ICT utilization. The study recommends continuous investment in ICT infrastructure, staff training, integration of automated financial systems, and adoption of cloud-based accounting solutions to strengthen accountability and improve financial management processes in Federal Polytechnics.

title: HUBUNGAN PEMANFAATAN KECERDASAN BUATAN (AI) SEBAGAI SUMBER BELAJAR DENGAN KEMANDIRIAN BELAJAR SISWA PAI DI SMP
container-title: EDUCATOR : Jurnal Inovasi Tenaga Pendidik dan Kependidikan
a72b4739b1bea39fca6a1a6f81145bf37f0c034b.abstract: ABSTRACT The use of generative artificial intelligence in education creates opportunities for students to access information and understand learning materials more flexibly. However, such accessibility does not necessarily correspond to students’ ability to manage their own learning independently, particularly in Islamic Religious Education (PAI) at the junior secondary school level. This study aims to examine the relationship between the use of ChatGPT as a learning resource and students’ learning independence at SMPN 5 Ambarawa. A quantitative approach with a correlational design was employed, involving 64 students selected through purposive sampling. Data were collected using a four-point Likert-scale questionnaire measuring ChatGPT utilization and learning independence. The data were analyzed using IBM SPSS Statistics version 27 through descriptive statistics, instrument validity and reliability testing, and Spearman’s rho correlation analysis. The results revealed a positive and statistically significant relationship between ChatGPT utilization and students’ learning independence, with a correlation coefficient of 0.598 and a significance value of p < 0.001. These findings indicate that better utilization of ChatGPT tends to be associated with higher levels of learning independence. Nevertheless, this relationship does not establish a causal effect. The use of ChatGPT in Islamic Religious Education should therefore be accompanied by teacher guidance, information verification, and active student engagement to ensure that the technology is used critically and responsibly. ABSTRAK Pemanfaatan kecerdasan buatan generatif dalam pembelajaran membuka peluang bagi siswa untuk memperoleh informasi dan memahami materi secara lebih fleksibel. Namun, kemudahan akses tersebut belum tentu sejalan dengan kemampuan siswa mengelola proses belajarnya secara mandiri, khususnya dalam mata pelajaran Pendidikan Agama Islam (PAI) di jenjang sekolah menengah pertama. Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis hubungan antara pemanfaatan ChatGPT sebagai sumber belajar dan kemandirian belajar siswa di SMPN 5 Ambarawa. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif dengan desain korelasional yang melibatkan 64 siswa melalui teknik purposive sampling. Data dikumpulkan menggunakan angket skala Likert empat pilihan yang mengukur pemanfaatan ChatGPT dan kemandirian belajar. Data dianalisis menggunakan IBM SPSS Statistics versi 27 melalui statistik deskriptif, pengujian validitas dan reliabilitas instrumen, serta korelasi Spearman’s rho. Hasil analisis menunjukkan hubungan positif dan signifikan antara pemanfaatan ChatGPT dan kemandirian belajar siswa, dengan koefisien korelasi sebesar 0,598 dan nilai signifikansi p < 0,001. Temuan ini menunjukkan bahwa pemanfaatan ChatGPT yang lebih baik cenderung berkaitan dengan kemandirian belajar yang lebih tinggi. Meskipun demikian, hubungan tersebut tidak membuktikan sebab-akibat. Penggunaan ChatGPT dalam pembelajaran PAI perlu disertai bimbingan guru, verifikasi informasi, dan keterlibatan aktif siswa agar teknologi dimanfaatkan secara kritis dan bertanggung jawab.

title: Web tracking analysis on top websites through OpenWPM analytics enhancements
container-title: International Journal of Information Security
bc059087d27019ac84285e3865414d2d8d0f3cc2.abstract: Abstract Nowadays, websites employ multiple tracking mechanisms to personalize user experiences and deliver targeted advertisements. While cookies remain the dominant tracking tool, recent trends indicate an increasing adoption of stateless fingerprinting based on JavaScript methods. However, existing studies often focus on specific tracking technologies, while detailed analyses that jointly examine multiple stateful and stateless tracking mechanisms remain limited. To address this gap, we enhanced OpenWPM-Data-Analytics to improve the detection of fingerprinting mechanisms in scans performed with OpenWPM, a widely used framework for web privacy measurement studies. Using this enhanced measurement and analysis pipeline, we conducted an empirical analysis of the top 1000 most-visited websites, jointly examining cookies, web storage, web analytics tools, and browser fingerprinting techniques. The results show that stateful tracking methods such as cookies and web storage remain highly prevalent. However, fingerprinting techniques were detected on nearly one third of the analyzed websites, with JavaScript Enumeration and WebGL being the most common mechanisms. This prevalence is higher than that reported in previous automated studies, suggesting a growing reliance on fingerprinting as third-party cookies face increasing restrictions. In addition, web analytics tools were present in half of the websites analyzed. These findings highlight the growing complexity of modern web tracking and the need to improve current detection and mitigation strategies, particularly against fingerprinting mechanisms that are more difficult to block and regulate.

title: Digital Technology and Market Share of Selected Micro Enterprises Firms in Nigeria
container-title: RESEARCH JOURNAL OF MASS COMMUNICATION AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY
7318802c7475ce7d1a6df15371b4c4e8ea0daa97.abstract: The study examined the effect of digital technology on market share of selected micro enterprises firms in Nigeria. The specific objective was to determine the effect of e-commerce platform usage and social media marketing on market share of selected micro enterprises firms in Nigeria. Descriptive survey research design was adopted on a population of 41,469,947 operators of micro enterprises in Nigeria. A sample size of 400 was calculated using Taro Yamane formula while the respondents were recruited using purposive sampling approach. Primary data were collected using questionnaire based on five-point Likert-scale system. The hypotheses were tested using multiple regression analysis at 5% significance level. The study found the following: E-commerce platform usage has a significant and positive effect on market share of selected micro enterprises firms in Nigeria (β = 0.199, p = 0.000); Social media marketing has a significant and positive effect on market share of selected micro enterprises firms in Nigeria (β = 0.557, p = 0.000). In conclusion, micro enterprises that embrace digital technologies are better positioned to attract a larger customer base, compete more effectively, and grow their presence in the market. The study recommended that operators of micro enterprises should partner with technology solution providers to offer customized, subsidized e-commerce infrastructure and training programs tailored specifically for micro enterprise firms.

title: Beyond accuracy and time saved: implementation outcomes for generative AI in hospital administrative and clinical-administrative workflows—a mini review
container-title: Frontiers in Medicine
08dce28882ef374649f8c6426650ed7cc9e2048e.abstract: Although hospitals are introducing generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) into documentation, messaging, and administrative workflows, model accuracy and time saved do not establish safe or sustainable implementation. This Mini Review examines which implementation and downstream outcomes should inform decisions to pilot, scale up, sustain, modify, or discontinue these workflows. A PubMed-led structured narrative search through 25 August 2026, with an update on 27 August, informed a purposive core of 17 empirical studies: seven direct administrative studies and 10 clinical-administrative studies. Supporting reviews and established implementation frameworks informed the interpretation of the findings. Perceived workload, logged efficiency, adoption, safety, and downstream outcomes did not improve consistently together. Favourable average quality could coexist with consequential errors and substantial verification work. Within this selected core, cost, penetration, and sustainability were measured less often than early fit, use, and feasibility. No study was coded as providing an operationalised equity assessment. We present a literature-informed outcome-to-decision crosswalk that links these findings to clinical workflow governance. This distinguishes non-compensable stop rules from minimum progression criteria and comparative value targets, with explicit ownership, denominators and reassessment. Illustrative stop rules address serious uncorrected errors, unauthorised data disclosure and bypassed human review. The crosswalk is an unvalidated normative synthesis, not a universal stage model. Its value requires prospective testing against patient safety, workforce burden and service outcomes.

title: Community Relations Techniques of Oil Companies in Managing Conflicts: Host Communities’ Preferences, Effectiveness and Constraints in the Niger Delta Region
container-title: RESEARCH JOURNAL OF MASS COMMUNICATION AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY
43793beae418369db6b79a7c650bcf9a99bfd23f.abstract: This study examined the community relations techniques employed by oil companies in managing conflicts with host communities in the Niger Delta Region. The study was anchored on stakeholders theory. A descriptive survey design was adopted. The population comprised sixty-six (66) corporate affairs staff of oil companies and 282,433 residents across some communities in Delta, Edo and Rivers States. A sample of six (6) company staff and 384 residents of the host communities was selected through purposive and opportunity sampling techniques. Data were collected using an interview guide and questionnaire. Validity was ensured through expert review, while a reliability index of 0.78 was obtained using the pilot test method. Data from interviews were analysed using Yin’s explanation building technique, while questionnaire data were analysed using mean scores on a four-point Likert scale. Findings revealed that host communities prefer infrastructural development projects, empowerment programmes, youth employment, and consistent communication with oil companies. The study further showed that community relations techniques help oil companies secure local representation, gather opinions and ensure adherence to Memoranda of Understanding (MoUs). However, the study identified constraints including inadequate communication, insufficient community engagement with women and youth groups, and limited consistency in project implementation. The study concluded that while community relations techniques are actively applied and have considerable strength in reducing conflicts, their impact is hindered by poor communication strategies and weak inclusivity. It recommended that oil companies should prioritize sustainable community development projects, youth employment, and open communication channels to meet host community expectations. They should also strengthen community relations frameworks by institutionalizing dialogue, negotiation, and strict adherence to MoUs for long-term mutual trust.

title: How patient and professional characteristics mediate between innovative work behavior and hospital performance: the moderating role of AI use
container-title: International Journal of Pharmaceutical and Healthcare Marketing
9761830e77f32d8204aaf31e513b1eae2a86a9a0.abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine how innovative work behavior (IWB) influences hospital performance (HP), with professional characteristics (ProC) and patient characteristics (PtC) as mediating factors. Furthermore, it examines whether the adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) moderates this relationship. Design/methodology/approach A structured questionnaire was used to collect data from 351 healthcare professionals in Pakistan. Partial least squares structural equation modeling was applied to test the hypotheses. Findings The results reveal that IWB has a significant, positive effect on HP, both directly and indirectly through ProC and PtC. These characteristics act as important underlying mechanisms through which IWB enhances performance outcomes. While AI adoption does not directly improve HP, it positively moderates the IWB–HP relationship, indicating that AI strengthens the performance outcomes of innovation-supportive environments. Originality/value This study integrates the resource-based view and job demands–resources into a nomological framework. It contributes to healthcare innovation research by showing that technological adoption alone is insufficient; employee innovative behavior and human-related characteristics are crucial drivers of HP.

title: Information-Seeking Behaviour During the COVID-19 Pandemic in Karnataka
container-title: RESEARCH JOURNAL OF MASS COMMUNICATION AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY
9fa727e40ef7212c29a5ff8b7de9bc2781ecf8a1.abstract: During the COVID-19 pandemic, when uncertainty and fear dominated public life, information-seeking behaviour became especially critical as individuals relied heavily on media to stay informed, safe, and connected. Information-seeking behaviour (ISB) in media refers to the deliberate effort’s individuals make to locate, access, and utilise information through various media channels to satisfy specific needs or goals. The COVID-19 pandemic created an unprecedented global health crisis that disrupted everyday life and generated an urgent demand for accurate, timely, and accessible information. Understanding informationseeking behaviour (ISB) in this context is particularly significant, as the way individuals’ access and interpret information has a direct impact on their knowledge, attitudes, and practices related to health, safety, and social responsibility. In this background, the study was conducted to identify the most preferred media for information-seeking, to examine the information-seeking behaviour, and to examine the perception of the audience on the role of the Media during the COVID-19 pandemic. The study used a structured questionnaire to find the answer to the above objectives. A survey was conducted with 465 samples, and the convenience and snowball sampling methods were used to select the samples. This study will help policymakers to adapt practical interventions that enhance the resilience of individuals and communities when confronted with crises like the COVID-19 pandemic.

title: Beyond Ethical Principles: A Comparative Review of National and Institutional AI Policies in Higher Education
container-title: Annual Review of Comparative and International Education 2025, Part B
8536db1c538358f24ed4b0c46d8e64444efc0c9d.abstract: <jats:p>The rapid diffusion of artificial intelligence (AI) into higher education has produced a proliferation of ethical guidelines, national strategies, and institutional policies. Yet convergence around principles such as transparency, fairness, and accountability has not produced consistent governance outcomes across contexts. This chapter offers a comparative review of national and institutional AI policies in higher education, examining how ethical commitments are translated into regulatory frameworks and operational practice. Drawing on policy texts and institutional guidance from multiple regions, the analysis traces how governance logics shift as they move from ethical aspiration to national strategy and, ultimately, to institutional implementation. This chapter argues that national AI strategies consistently frame higher education instrumentally as part of workforce development and technological competitiveness agendas, while institutional responses remain shaped by organizational capacity, fiscal constraint, and fragmented governance. A cross-national comparison reveals that differences in regulatory philosophy matter less than variations in institutional design and resource distribution. This chapter concludes by identifying methodological implications for comparative education research and outlining a future agenda focused on policy translation, capacity building, and the uneven global distribution of educational risk associated with AI.</jats:p>

title: National AI Strategies and Higher Education in the Global South: Policy, Practice, and Power
container-title: Annual Review of Comparative and International Education 2025, Part B
aea880b7dde6be71ddcff68393b451b2c7d9de49.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter examines how national artificial intelligence (AI) strategies are translated into higher education (HE) policy and practice across the Global South (GS), with particular attention to issues of equity, governance, and power. Drawing on cases from Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, the United Arab Emirates (UAE), and South Africa, this chapter explores how universities are positioned within national AI agendas and respond through fragmented policies, pedagogical experiments, administrative adoption, and partnerships. The analysis also highlights how structural constraints shape institutional responses and how Global North–developed AI intensifies concerns about autonomy, bias, and inequalities within and between HE systems. Situating these dynamics within the broader political economy of AI, this chapter shows how market concentration, industry influence, and North–South power relations shape both the possibilities and limits of AI integration in GS universities. It argues that meaningful, context-responsive AI adoption requires closer alignment between national strategies and institutional governance, sustained public investment, and equity-focused pedagogical frameworks that move beyond market-driven models of innovation.</jats:p>

title: AI-driven knowledge management: a new frontier for innovation and collaboration in higher education
container-title: Journal of Applied Research in Higher Education
9f9f245e5f07161e21092c92b0d8f5dc4f48b0fa.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Purpose</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study examined how artificial intelligence (AI) tools can be integrated into knowledge management (KM) systems in higher education institutions and assessed their impact on key KM objectives and learning-related outcomes.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Design/methodology/approach</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>In terms of purpose, the research was applied and developmental. Methodologically, a qualitative approach was adopted. The study participants consisted of faculty members from Iranian universities. Sampling was conducted using the snowball technique. A total of 11 faculty members participated in the study. The primary data collection instrument was the semi-structured interview. Using a fuzzy cognitive mapping (FCM) approach, the study modeled the relationships between AI technologies, KM variables, and KM functions.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Findings</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The results indicated that AI tools have a significant positive effect on KM outcomes in higher education. Natural language processing (NLP) showed the strongest influence on personalized learning, while intelligent assistants and chatbots had the greatest impact on real-time feedback, decision-making, and pattern recognition. Overall, AI-driven KM systems enhanced collaboration, learning outcomes, and knowledge sharing, while improving the efficiency of decision-making processes.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Originality/value</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study contributes to the higher education literature by offering a systemic, AI-driven KM framework based on FCM. It provides practical insights for university leaders and policymakers on utilizing AI to strengthen KM practices, foster innovation, and support collaborative and data-informed decision-making in academic institutions.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Awareness, Perceived Benefits, and Skill-Erosion Concerns Regarding Generative AI Among Higher Education Students
container-title: Research and Advances in Education
2f32211bef981f72ec3c5ea5163580c623b349d8.abstract: <jats:p>This research aimed to assess awareness of generative AI limitations, highlight its advantages, and identify potential threats from misuse, focusing on differences in opinions between future educators and students from non-education fields. The data were collected through surveying 931 undergraduate students of a private university in the Philippines. The researchers used a comparative-correlational research design with a qualitative strand. The study found moderate awareness of generative AI’s limitations (M = 3.31, SD = 0.94) and a moderate-to-cautious attitude toward its implementation (M = 3.15, SD = 0.87). Education students showed higher awareness than students from other majors (d = 0.40), while differences in usage, perception, and fear of skills deteriorating were negligible (d = 0.14–0.25) and, to some extent, neutralized in robustness checks. Differences between genders and years of study in perceptions were minor. The findings suggest that future teachers’ curricula should include a course on AI literacy and emphasize developing critical thinking skills to prepare students for implementing generative AI solutions in teaching practices.</jats:p>

title: Generative AI-supported learning, self-directed learning, and motivation in a graduate seminar: an exploratory single-group study
container-title: Frontiers in Education
ff78bb49950649188a4b72b9992e76440d916214.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Introduction</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Generative artificial intelligence (AI) offers new forms of learning support, but assistance with a task should be distinguished from independent learning. This exploratory study examined questionnaire changes during a 16-week graduate Training and Development Seminar at a national university in Taiwan and considered students' written accounts of AI use.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The reported course sample comprised 10 master's and three doctoral students. Thirteen responses were available at each measurement occasion; eight participants could be matched by email address and formed the paired analysis sample. A 20-item SDLI-based self-directed learning (SDL) questionnaire and a 24-item ARCS course motivation questionnaire were administered in Chinese.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Across all responses, SDL means were 80.62 (SD = 10.24) at pretest and 87.38 (SD = 7.12) at posttest; motivation means were 98.08 (SD = 11.84) and 106.54 (SD = 9.61), respectively. In the eight verified pairs, mean changes were 7.25 and 9.88 points, respectively. Two-sided exhaustive signed-rank p-values were 0.015625 and 0.03125, with seven nonzero differences for each outcome. Cronbach's alpha was 0.895/0.864 for SDL and 0.941/0.900 for motivation at pretest/posttest. Written reflections described perceived learning support, professional relevance, and concerns about dependence on AI.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Discussion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The small matched subset, self-report measures, and absence of a comparison group prevent attributing the changes specifically to AI or generalizing them to the full cohort. The findings raise questions about learner judgment, output verification, and assessment of unaided understanding.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Interactive AI tools, personalized feedback, and EFL learners’ intention to use AI: an extended TAM study in Egyptian higher education
container-title: Frontiers in Education
d7330015e61a486d39cbb64399645dd58fc062b4.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Introduction</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Despite the growing use of generative artificial intelligence (AI) in English as a Foreign Language (EFL) education, how interactive AI features and personalized learning feedback shape learners' acceptance remains insufficiently understood. This study examines their influence on Egyptian university students' behavioral intention to use AI tools through an extended Technology Acceptance Model (TAM), focusing on the mediating roles of perceived usefulness and perceived ease of use.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>An explanatory sequential mixed-methods design was employed. Survey data from 596 Egyptian university students were analyzed using structural equation modeling (SEM), followed by thematic analysis of semi-structured interviews with eight purposively selected participants.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Perceived usefulness and perceived ease of use significantly predicted behavioral intention. Interactive AI features influenced intention indirectly through perceived usefulness, whereas personalized learning feedback influenced intention indirectly through perceived ease of use. Interviews revealed that interactivity supported engagement, clarification, and learner control, while personalized feedback facilitated error correction, reduced ambiguity, and alleviated anxiety. Participants viewed AI tools as flexible learning support rather than replacements for human instruction.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Discussion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The findings highlight the importance of pedagogically meaningful interaction and personalized feedback in shaping EFL learners' acceptance of AI tools. Responsible integration should emphasize learner agency, critical evaluation of AI-generated responses, and continued human pedagogical guidance.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Tracing Interactional Change in Japanese EFL Learners’ Interactions with a Teacher-Designed AI Voice Chatbot: A Pilot Study<b></b>
container-title: International Journal of AI in Language Education
3db3a061e9f6be6bbac68ed642b465beae14ba64.abstract: <jats:p>Although AI-mediated conversation practice is increasingly common in EFL teaching, qualitative analysis of learner–AI interaction has been insufficient. This exploratory pilot study examined Japanese EFL learners’ interactional change. Ten university students completed three five-minute sessions with a teacher-designed chatbot on Google AI Studio. Logs were analyzed quantitatively and qualitatively. Effect sizes suggested a two-phase pattern of observed change: large effects (d = 0.88–1.13) from Sessions 1 to 2 marked an initial adjustment phase, while medium effects (d = 0.59–0.66) from Sessions 2 to 3 indicated slowed quantitative growth alongside continued qualitative elaboration, particularly in topic development. Qualitative analysis identified both constraints (vocabulary gaps, abstract questions) and affordances (explanatory expansions, analytical reflections, self-directed topic drift). Comparison with peer-to-peer data highlighted distinctive features: longer turns, near absence of backchannels, and more frequent language-related episodes. These preliminary findings offer initial guidance for teachers developing AI conversation tools using accessible platforms.</jats:p>

title: Who Benefits from AI Writing Tools? Rural Low-Income University Students’ Experiences of English Academic Writing and Educational Inequality
container-title: Education as Change
b19c13fdbe953ac3f9edaf4eda3c61a6916d89f9.abstract: <jats:p>This article examines how students from rural low-income backgrounds navigate support mediated by artificial intelligence (AI) in academic writing in English. Although generative AI is often framed as widening access to writing assistance, its equity implications remain insufficiently understood for students whose participation in academic English is shaped by rural schooling histories, economic constraints, and uneven digital resources. Drawing on a qualitative multiple-case study of 24 students and five teachers across two Chinese universities, the article analyses interviews, four-week writing journals, student writing artefacts, and institutional policy documents. The findings indicate that AI-mediated writing offered compensatory linguistic support: It reduced anxiety, improved surface-level accuracy, and helped students begin or revise writing tasks. These gains, however, were unevenly mediated by economic capital, cultural capital, and AI capital. The analysis also identifies a tension between more standardised academic English and students’ sense of academic voice. Integrating Bourdieu’s theory of capital with Freirean critical pedagogy, the article conceptualises AI-assisted writing as a contested educational space in which unequal advantage and more agentic forms of participation co-exist. More equitable provision requires transparent policy, explicit instruction in prompt design and output evaluation, and dialogic writing pedagogy that helps students retain ownership of their arguments and academic voice.</jats:p>

title: Generative artificial intelligence usage by university students in the light of Diffusion of Innovations theory
container-title: Discover Education
783e1be314f9287c0e8f33dbdd98f93152b8a4eb.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>The rapid proliferation of generative artificial intelligence (AI) tools, particularly large language models such as ChatGPT, has fundamentally transformed the landscape of higher education. This study investigates the factors influencing the adoption of generative AI by university students through the theoretical lens of Diffusion of Innovations (DOI) theory. Drawing upon Rogers’ seminal framework, this research examines how five perceived attributes of innovation-relative advantage, compatibility, simplicity, trialability, and observability-is related to students’ behavioral intention to use generative AI tools in their academic pursuits. A cross-sectional online survey was conducted among students from multiple Polish universities, and the collected data were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM). The measurement model demonstrated satisfactory psychometric properties, with all constructs achieving acceptable levels of internal consistency reliability, convergent validity, and discriminant validity. The structural model results indicate that relative advantage, simplicity, observability and compatibility are significantly related to behavioral intention, while trialability demonstrates a non-significant effect. The model explains approximately 48.7% of variance in behavioral intention. These findings contribute to the theoretical understanding of technology adoption in educational contexts and provide practical implications for higher education institutions seeking to integrate generative AI tools into their pedagogical frameworks. The study concludes with recommendations for fostering responsible AI adoption while addressing concerns regarding academic integrity and critical thinking development.</jats:p>

title: Automation Bias in AI-Assisted Simulated Radiotherapy Decision-Making Among Undergraduate Radiological Sciences Students: A Controlled Experimental Study
container-title: International Medical Education
1deea36fad4323102dcd9a80971959fb2711cd49.abstract: <jats:p>Background: Artificial intelligence (AI) may support clinical decision-making but introduce automation bias when incorrect recommendations influence users. This study aimed to determine the occurrence of harmful automation bias among undergraduate radiological sciences students during AI-assisted radiotherapy decision-making and to examine the influence of time pressure. Methods: In a controlled experiment, 54 final-year undergraduate radiological sciences students with no prior clinical radiotherapy placement experience completed 20 simulated radiotherapy decision-making scenarios with 13 correct and seven deliberately incorrect AI recommendations (1080 trials). Initial and final responses, AI advice acceptance, confidence, perceived workload, and attitudes toward AI verification were assessed. Students were assigned to time-pressure (n = 26) or no-time-pressure (n = 28) conditions. Harmful automation bias was operationally defined as switching from an initially correct response to an incorrect response matching AI advice. Results: Harmful automation bias occurred in 20/220 eligible trials (9.1%), affecting 15/54 students (27.8%). Incorrect AI advice was followed in 137/378 trials (36.2%). Overall accuracy remained similar before and after AI exposure (75.65% vs. 74.91%; p = 0.289). Time pressure increased workload, but no statistically significant association with harmful automation bias was observed (OR = 0.78; p = 0.654). Lower post-decision confidence was associated with harmful automation bias (OR = 0.599; p = 0.028). No statistically significant difference in harmful automation bias was observed between participants who supported AI verification and those who did not. Conclusions: Harmful automation bias can occur despite stable overall accuracy, suggesting that greater emphasis on critical appraisal, active verification, and independent judgement may be valuable in radiotherapy education.</jats:p>

title: From Fragmented Adoption to Systematic Transformation: Curriculum Analysis and an Institutional Roadmap for AI Convergence Education at a Korean University
container-title: Education Sciences
d695ca21af7e3fbf7af2d4e2bf3eebdf2f836e3a.abstract: <jats:p>Higher education institutions are under mounting pressure to transform their curricula in response to artificial intelligence (AI), yet many universities—particularly teaching-focused private institutions facing demographic decline—struggle to move beyond fragmented, course-level adoption. This study examines how a mid-sized private university in South Korea diagnosed and redesigned its major curricula for AI convergence education, framing this transformation as an institutional survival and quality strategy amid a shrinking college-age population. The study combined four methods: analysis of national AI education policies and of domestic and international university cases; a complete census of all undergraduate major curricula (67 program units; 1646 courses across the 55 non-AI-specialist majors) using a four-type typology of AI-linkable courses; a needs survey of department heads and program chairs; and rapid prototyping of a staged curriculum framework. The curriculum analysis indicated an articulation gap: explicitly AI-articulated courses accounted for only 1.5% of the curriculum (25 courses in 13 of 55 majors), whereas courses provisionally identified as plausible candidates for AI integration were nearly eight times as numerous (193 courses, 11.7%) and present in 84% of majors, but were not connected to curriculum documentation, learning outcomes, or progression pathways; whether these courses already contain AI-related practice requires syllabus-level verification. Two-thirds of responding program leaders (66.7%) endorsed AI convergence education while prioritizing concerns about infrastructure, institutional support, and unverified learning effects. Based on these findings, the study proposes the CROSS AX competency model—crossing disciplinary expertise with AI application capability—operationalized through a three-stage curriculum structure (AX-Foundation, AX-Bridge, AX-Field Lab) and a five-phase institutional roadmap moving from shared infrastructure toward full curricular transformation with quality management; both were expert-reviewed and iteratively refined over two review rounds. The study offers a diagnostic typology and roadmap that may be adapted by universities seeking to institutionalize AI-driven curricular transformation rather than accumulate isolated initiatives.</jats:p>

title: Learning Chemistry with Generative Artificial Intelligence: A Phenomenological Study of Secondary School Students’ Experiences in Bayelsa State, Nigeria
container-title: INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF EDUCATION AND EVALUATION
2ef11c7527b21d3e626e9fdbc241643faa188b9f.abstract:
<jats:p>Generative artificial intelligence offers new opportunities for supporting Chemistry learning, but
accessible explanations may not translate into independent conceptual understanding. This
paper examined experiences of understanding Chemistry concepts, perceptions of usefulness and
challenges associated with generative artificial intelligence within a secondary school context in
Bayelsa State, Nigeria. A qualitative analysis informed by an interpretative phenomenological
approach was undertaken using ten participants. Analysis involved examining individual
accounts, identifying experiential meanings and comparing patterns across cases. The accounts
portrayed conceptual understanding as developing through manageable explanations,
recognition of errors, comparison with other resources, and independent practice. However,
apparent clarity sometimes coexisted with difficulties applying knowledge to unfamiliar
problems. Perceived usefulness centred on repeated clarification without embarrassment,
support outside classroom instruction, revision activities and alternative explanations.
Challenges included shared devices, data costs, unreliable connectivity, unfamiliar terminology,
uncertainty about response accuracy, difficulty formulating questions and the temptation to copy
solutions. The analysis suggests that generative artificial intelligence may serve as a
supplementary resource when combined with teacher guidance, textbooks, practical
demonstrations, and independent problem-solving. Faculty of Education, Niger Delta University,
Wilberforce Island, Bayelsa State</jats:p>

title: Effect of thermal sensation on cognitive performance
container-title: Pollack Periodica
53bc30e0ff67b9dc855c7d59c699c1fa64b7bd72.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Thermal sensation of the human body and cognitive performance are closely related. Extreme temperature conditions can significantly impair concentration, memory and mental state, leading to reduced productivity. It is therefore important to ensure appropriate climatic conditions to maintain productivity. This is particularly important in modern buildings, where thermal comfort can be ensured and guaranteed through building services engineering. It is uncertain, however, what the exact thermal satisfaction value is for people in terms of mental performance. There is both consensus and unresolved matters in the literature on the subject. The aim of this research is to investigate the optimal thermal comfort level with live subjects and by measuring thermal comfort parameters. It also aims to confirm or refute the results presented in the literature.</jats:p>
