title: Diminishing returns to calibrated reliance on AI: effects on deliverable quality and rework effort, moderated by task verifiability
container-title: Information Technology & People
484244033afc4957dd48a954f65145f1c67a443f.abstract: Purpose Artificial intelligence (AI) tools can function as both “performance accelerators” and “risk propagators” in organizations. This study investigates how AI-enabled work capability, particularly employees' decomposition and evaluation skills, is associated with deliverable quality and rework effort through the behavioral pathway of calibrated reliance on AI. Additionally, it examines task verifiability as a critical boundary condition that shapes the effectiveness of human-AI collaboration. Design/methodology/approach Guided by appropriate reliance and automation trust theories, data from 380 workers were analyzed using SmartPLS 4 (partial least squares structural equation modeling) and hierarchical polynomial regression to test mediation, moderation, and quadratic effects. Procedural remedies and a latent method factor approach were employed to assess common method bias. Findings AI-enabled work capability was positively associated with calibrated reliance on AI. Calibrated reliance on AI was associated with higher deliverable quality and lower rework effort. A double diminishing marginal pattern emerged: as reliance calibration increased, quality gains and rework reductions leveled off, indicating a “too-much-of-a-good-thing” pattern. Task verifiability strengthened the positive association between calibrated reliance and deliverable quality and also strengthened its negative association with rework effort. Originality/value This study shifts the focus from reliance intensity to reliance calibration in explaining AI-enabled work outcomes. It documents a double diminishing marginal pattern, showing that the benefits of calibrated reliance are meaningful but not unlimited. It also identifies task verifiability as a boundary condition that helps explain when calibrated reliance is more strongly associated with improved deliverable quality and reduced rework effort. These findings provide focused guidance for capability development, reliance calibration, and task-specific AI governance.

title: Newspapers Blocking AI Crawlers Expose Their Voters to a Partisan Flood
46c8c2234ccd7b8a4f424f64283b415493f39665.abstract: Major newspapers block AI crawlers, while parties and partisan sites leave their text open. This paper builds a game-theoretic model of the hold-out and asks what voters hear while it lasts. In the model, an AI that cannot grade its sources pools the text it can read; two persuaders choose how much nearly free text to publish; and an AI lab may license a newspaper's reporting for its lost revenue. Neither the newspapers nor the lab has a political aim. Three results follow. First, the persuaders flood the AI, and the lab licenses each newspaper once a fixed share of the voters closest to it asks the AI, whatever the AI says. Second, newspapers whose voters dislike the AI's answers more hold out longer, and their voters hear the flood longer. Third, licensing bends the persuaders' contest by a small tilt from where the costs alone put it: patient persuaders tilt the AI's answers against the voters' average ideology, and impatient ones toward it. Business decisions with no political aim thus set how long each group hears the flood and which way the AI's answers tilt.

title: Disentangling fairness, accountability and transparency in AI travel recommendations: the role of algorithm trust across hedonic and utilitarian contexts
container-title: Journal of Hospitality and Tourism Technology
824188a699a8317f7031ea05be0d5b8cf17dc330.abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine how tourists’ perceptions of fairness, accountability and transparency (FAT) in artificial intelligence (AI) recommendation algorithms shape algorithm trust and how trust influences recommendation acceptance and resistance, with tourism product type as a moderator. Design/methodology/approach A scenario-based online survey of 355 Korean adult consumers was conducted via travel-related Naver cafés and KakaoTalk communities. Hypotheses were tested with structural equation modeling in AMOS 23.0, and the moderating role of tourism product type was assessed through multigroup analysis. Findings All three FAT dimensions positively predicted algorithm trust, with transparency showing the largest effect, followed by accountability and fairness. Algorithm trust positively predicted recommendation acceptance and reduced resistance. Indirect effects through trust were significant for accountability and transparency but not fairness; accountability influenced trust only in the utilitarian condition. Research limitations/implications Self-reported, cross-sectional data from a Korean-only sample may limit causal inference and generalizability. Future research could use objective behavioral data, longitudinal designs and cross-cultural samples to extend the FAT–trust–behavior framework. Practical implications Tourism platforms should prioritize explainable AI features, adopt context-sensitive communication – emphasizing accountability cues for utilitarian services and transparency-based emotional appeal for hedonic ones – and focus on building trust at the first AI recommendation touchpoint. Social implications The findings provide empirical grounding for tourism-specific AI governance. The dominant role of transparency suggests that policymakers should consider introducing recommendation rationale disclosure requirements for AI-powered tourism platforms, enabling consumers to understand why specific products are suggested. In addition, the finding that consumers cannot directly evaluate algorithmic fairness highlights the need for independent, third-party fairness audits of recommendation systems to protect consumers from potential algorithmic bias that may systematically favor certain destinations, accommodations or price segments over others. Originality/value This study is one of the few to empirically apply the AI ethics FAT framework to tourism consumer behavior. The findings suggest that the three FAT dimensions may not contribute equally to algorithm trust – with transparency showing the strongest association regardless of context and accountability becoming relevant primarily in utilitarian service settings – which points to the limitations of treating FAT as a uniform construct in AI recommendation design. The resulting framework offers tourism platforms an empirical basis for tailoring AI trust strategies to specific product categories.

title: The AI trust paradox: how disclosure, brand authenticity and consumer mindset shape communication effectiveness
container-title: Internet Research
e09edfde2db4f667fde987e62aaafb46174d1016.abstract: Purpose This study investigates the trust paradox in artificial intelligence (AI)-generated content, where efficiency conflicts with perceived inauthenticity. Integrating source credibility theory and congruity theory, it examines how the interplay between ad genesis (AI vs. genuine), strategic context (disclosure, brand authenticity) and consumer mindset (construal level) determines communication effectiveness. Design/methodology/approach A three-study experimental design was employed to isolate specific contingencies. Study 1 manipulated ad genesis and AI disclosure to test engagement. Study 2 examined the moderating role of brand authenticity on purchase intentions. Study 3 tested the congruity between AI message focus (hedonic vs. utilitarian) and consumer construal levels. Findings Genuine imagery generally outperforms AI-generated imagery; however, effectiveness is contingent on strategic fit. Disclosure boosts engagement for genuine ads but reduces it for AI content. AI ads enhance purchase intentions for low-authenticity brands but damage high-authenticity ones. Furthermore, hedonic AI appeals align with high-construal mindsets, whereas utilitarian appeals suit low-construal consumers. Research limitations/implications The experiments used static images in controlled online settings. Future research should test dynamic and multimodal AI content and validate the effects with real-world behavioral metrics, such as click-through and conversion rates. Practical implications AI use should fit the context. Heritage brands should avoid AI imagery, whereas challenger brands can benefit from it. Disclosure helps genuine-image ads but hurts AI-generated ads. Hedonic AI appeals suit abstract mindsets, whereas utilitarian appeals suit concrete mindsets. Originality/value This research advances advertising theory by applying a split-credibility lens to AI-generated advertising, demonstrating that effectiveness depends on source-context congruence.

title: AI-mediated teacher learning in Chinese lesson study: regulating cognitive demands in EFL pre-service teachers
container-title: International Journal for Lesson & Learning Studies
e199aa0572f2751129a1ebbde013eaebeb26181d.abstract: Purpose This study, guided by the cognitive theory of multimedia learning (CTML), investigates how multimodal large language models (MLLMs) mediate the professional learning of English as a Foreign Language (EFL) pre-service teachers within Chinese lesson study (CLS). It aims to elucidate the cognitive and dialogic mechanisms through which AI-supported mediation shapes teacher learning processes and participation. Design/methodology/approach A three-month intervention integrating MLLMs into CLS was conducted with 50 EFL pre-service teachers at a Chinese normal university. Adopting an interpretive qualitative design, data were collected from longitudinal reflective journals, MLLM interaction logs, field notes and two rounds of semi-structured interviews with 5 purposively selected focal participants. Data analysis combined deductive coding based on CTML (intrinsic, extraneous and germane cognitive load) with inductive thematic analysis to capture emergent patterns of AI-mediated learning and interaction. Findings The findings reveal that MLLMs functioned as cognitive-dialogic mediators in three key ways: (1) reducing linguistic and organizational barriers, thereby lowering extraneous cognitive load; (2) redistributing cognitive resources to support meaning-making and pedagogical reasoning; and (3) enabling deeper engagement in collaborative knowledge construction and reflective inquiry within CLS. However, participants also reported tensions related to epistemic reliability and the risk of overreliance on AI-generated outputs, indicating a shift in cognitive demands from knowledge construction to evaluation and regulation. Originality/value This study advances the field by proposing a cognitive-dialogic framework that brings CTML into dialog with sociocultural perspectives on mediation, offering a nuanced account of how AI reshapes teacher learning in practice-based settings. It contributes empirical evidence on the role of MLLMs as mediating tools in CLS and provides design implications for cognitively and ethically informed AI integration in teacher education.

title: Digital-green synergistic transformation of manufacturing firms: configurational pathways and AI enabling effects
container-title: Journal of Manufacturing Technology Management
dec4772b4333b313d298320fc34d9261d33b006f.abstract: Purpose This study investigates the configurational pathways underpinning digital-green synergistic transformation (DGT) and examines the enabling role of artificial intelligence (AI), thereby advancing understanding of how manufacturing firms navigate the dual imperatives of green development and digital upgrading. Design/methodology/approach Using 9,336 firm-year observations from 2,407 Chinese manufacturing firms over 2013–2023, this study draws on the Technology-Organization-Environment (TOE) framework and employs dynamic QCA to identify pathways and panel regressions to examine AI’s enabling effects and heterogeneity. Findings Results indicate that no single factor constitutes a necessary condition for DGT. We identify three distinct configurational pathways to high DGT: “endogenous dual-innovation driven” (SC1), “policy-driven and green-led” (SC2) and “policy-driven and digital-led” (SC3). AI significantly promotes DGT by enabling these pathways, with the largest estimated enabling effect observed for SC1, followed by SC3 and SC2. Heterogeneity analysis reveals that the enabling effect of AI is more pronounced in state-owned enterprises, firms with high market attention and those with high industrial chain integration. Originality/value This study contributes to the literature at the intersection of digitalization and greening by elucidating how multiple technological, organizational and environmental factors form configurational pathways to DGT. It further demonstrates AI’s enabling role in these pathways, providing insights into how firms can embed AI to achieve their strategic goals. By revealing how AI’s effects vary across firm, market and industry contexts, this study advances a contextualized understanding of AI-enabled transformation.

title: Experts' and AI perspectives on the environmental sustainability of tensile membrane structures
container-title: Engineering, Construction and Architectural Management
d402fc4efcbcd36e8e8c08505b21aa9addd70c3f.abstract: Purpose With increasing demands for sustainable construction, there is growing interest in enhancing the environmental performance of tensile membrane structures (TMS). This study aims to investigate the environmental sustainability challenges and opportunities of TMS across their lifecycle stages by integrating expert insights and advanced AI-generated perspectives. Design/methodology/approach A qualitative methodology was employed using semi-structured interviews with 16 experienced professionals including architects, engineers, contractors, builders, environmental sustainability experts and researchers. To enhance the reliability of findings and address potential gaps, the study also utilised artificial intelligence (AI) tools (ChatGPT and DeepSeek) to compare human expert insights with AI responses. Thematic analysis was conducted to categorise the results into core environmental sustainability themes. Findings Five interrelated themes were identified: (1) material innovation and environmental sustainability, (2) structural efficiency and lightweight design, (3) construction techniques and environmental sustainability alignment, (4) life durability management and (5) accessibility, inclusivity and waste management. These themes highlight critical performance indicators such as energy use, structural behaviour, material optimisation, user experience and maintenance strategies. The integration of AI insights helped highlight both consensus and gaps in expert knowledge. Originality/value This study provides a systematic qualitative investigation of environmental sustainability in TMS from an expert-practice perspective and is among the first to compare expert insights with AI-generated assessments of environmental sustainability within the TMS domain. The research contributes to the growing field of environmentally responsive structural design by offering actionable strategies for embedding environmental sustainability assessment practices into TMS planning and implementation. The findings provide valuable guidance for architects, engineers and policymakers seeking to enhance low-carbon design decisions in membrane architecture.

title: AI-driven knowledge management: a new frontier for innovation and collaboration in higher education
container-title: Journal of Applied Research in Higher Education
6f47b56fd992998aeef45148e4bcdcd2062173ea.abstract: Purpose This study examined how artificial intelligence (AI) tools can be integrated into knowledge management (KM) systems in higher education institutions and assessed their impact on key KM objectives and learning-related outcomes. Design/methodology/approach In terms of purpose, the research was applied and developmental. Methodologically, a qualitative approach was adopted. The study participants consisted of faculty members from Iranian universities. Sampling was conducted using the snowball technique. A total of 11 faculty members participated in the study. The primary data collection instrument was the semi-structured interview. Using a fuzzy cognitive mapping (FCM) approach, the study modeled the relationships between AI technologies, KM variables, and KM functions. Findings The results indicated that AI tools have a significant positive effect on KM outcomes in higher education. Natural language processing (NLP) showed the strongest influence on personalized learning, while intelligent assistants and chatbots had the greatest impact on real-time feedback, decision-making, and pattern recognition. Overall, AI-driven KM systems enhanced collaboration, learning outcomes, and knowledge sharing, while improving the efficiency of decision-making processes. Originality/value This study contributes to the higher education literature by offering a systemic, AI-driven KM framework based on FCM. It provides practical insights for university leaders and policymakers on utilizing AI to strengthen KM practices, foster innovation, and support collaborative and data-informed decision-making in academic institutions.

title: Artificial Co-Regulation: AI Tutors That Never Fade Capture Learners’ Regulation Instead of Transferring It
c67edfd38dada648f164639c28f7083cde7b6ffe.abstract: Conversational AI tutors operate at national scale in some school systems and are used by most university students, while field experiments show assisted performance rising as unassisted performance falls. This paper argues that such agents produce artificial co-regulation: they recruit the learner’s attachment system while lacking the feature that made human scaffolding developmental, contingent fading. The argument draws on scaffolding theory, attachment theory, self-regulated learning research, and recent evidence on attachment and dependence in chatbot use. Because a scaffold that never fades does not transfer regulation, performance improves while the agent is present but unassisted competence, calibration, and epistemic independence lag, most consequentially at reading transitions, with multilingual and first-generation university students as the central case. So “permanent partner” models of human–AI scaffolding describe a developmental end state, not a starting point: shared epistemic agency requires a learner capable of partnership, and five design and measurement standards would protect that precondition.Preprint of a manuscript submitted to Educational Psychology (Taylor &amp; Francis), special issue “AI in Educational Psychology,” 31 October 2026; version 1, under review.

title: From Static to Dynamic: Parameter Manipulation as Adaptive DDL Scaffolding in Creative Writing with Generative AI
container-title: Digital Studies in Language and Literature
0cab7f5810a1874161e8697bc3ba26fb3c000c49.abstract: Abstract Generative AI tools now pervade university classrooms, yet the field lacks empirical understanding of how technical AI configurations translate into adaptive Data-driven Learning (DDL) scaffolding. This gap is crucial in creative writing, where excessive structure can suppress authorship and insufficient support can stall exploration. This study investigates how large language model (LLM) parameter configuration functions as a pedagogical design lever for DDL scaffolding in poetry writing classrooms. Across a three-phase mixed-methods study with 30 university creative writing learners (a 2 × 2 factorial experiment, an offline classroom workshop, and an online classroom workshop), two parameter settings, temperature and top-p, reliably reshaped the distribution of three pre-coded interaction types: Constraint Repair (Type A), Exemplar Giving (Type B), and Surprise Harvest (Type C). Moving from a structured to an exploratory setting, Type C rose roughly seven-fold in Phase 1, with the same direction of effect in the two subsequent classroom phases. Triangulating chat logs, reflection templates, and panel transcripts, Type B was voted most helpful but linked to diminished authorship, while Type C was associated with the highest authorship and satisfaction. We position parameter literacy as a necessary instructor competence for adaptive AI scaffolding.

title: Access, not ability: gender disparities in access to smartphone-based AI advisory tools for banana disease management among smallholder farmers in Rwanda
container-title: Frontiers in Sustainable Food Systems
3910a0fd7e17313d440d20e6318e9ad0499b8222.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI)-powered decision support tools can strengthen crop disease management, but their benefits reach farmers only when access is equitable. This study investigated how gender shapes access to smartphone-based AI advisory tools for banana disease management among smallholder farmers in Rwanda, using Tumaini, an AI-powered banana disease detection app, as a case. Using a mixed-method design, we combined a survey of 357 smallholder farmers across three districts, 12 focus groups, interviews with 61 farmers, and 12-month WhatsApp monitoring of 40 smartphone owners. Men had significantly greater smartphone ownership than women, and gender remained a significant predictor after controlling for education, income, and electricity access. However, among smartphone users, no significant gender differences were observed in digital literacy. Decision-making power was significantly lower among married women than married men. Despite high willingness to adopt, post-training use remained limited, with women significantly less likely to use the app than men. Men interacted with the app on significantly more days than women, though engagement per active day was comparable. Gender disparities in AI-tool use are associated with unequal access to devices and enabling conditions rather than with differences in technical capability. Addressing them requires gender-responsive interventions prioritizing equitable access, localized design (local-language and voice-guided interfaces), and structured group-based support. Such gender-responsive efforts are essential for women farmers to benefit equally from improved banana disease management and sustainable banana production, and for inclusive digital transformation in agriculture.

title: Machine learning surrogates for predicting and interpreting flood fragility parameters of masonry walls
container-title: AI in Civil Engineering
26d9dec3aef9ac0fa1199b5afb5989f15b1cde42.abstract: Abstract Flood-induced out-of-plane collapse of masonry walls is a recurrent cause of severe building damage and loss during flood events, particularly in low-rise residential construction. Assessing this failure mode at scale remains challenging: simplified fragility models are fast but often lack physical transparency, while mechanics-based analyses are interpretable but computationally expensive. This study develops a mechanics-informed surrogate modelling framework that bridges this gap. Machine-learning surrogates, including linear sparse regressions, kernel-based methods, and ensemble models, are trained on a constrained synthetic dataset generated from a mechanics-based wall collapse formulation. This enables fragility parameters to be predicted with accuracy comparable to the reference simulator while retaining a direct link to the governing structural mechanisms within the adopted modelling domain. A central contribution of the work is the explicit integration of explainable artificial intelligence, allowing the role of geometry, openings, vertical connectivity, and boundary restraint to be quantified and interpreted in physically meaningful terms. The results reveal stable and intuitive collapse drivers across boundary configurations, with the upper-floor contribution, thickness-related descriptors, and boundary restraint forming the dominant sensitivity group, while masonry density and opening-related variables have secondary or model-dependent influence. The consistency of these trends across linear and nonlinear surrogate models demonstrates that the framework captures not only fragility estimates but also mechanically consistent sensitivity patterns of wall overturning. By combining mechanics-based simulations with surrogate modelling, the proposed approach enables efficient and physically interpretable assessment of masonry wall fragility.

title: Strategi Manajemen Budidaya Sapi Potong Berbasis Program Inseminasi Buatan (IB) dalam Meningkatkan Produktivitas Ternak di Kabupaten Luwu Timur
container-title: JURNAL TRITON
c17380c658b0901ee8749527061dfa9d577aeb3f.abstract: Sektor peternakan melalui teknologi Inseminasi Buatan (IB) telah memberikan konstribusi positif terhadap pendapatan masyarakat di Kabupaten Luwu Timur yang diterapkan pada sapi potong Bali untuk menghasilkan Sapi Jenis Simental, Limosin, PO, Brangus, Madura dan Bali. Penelitian ini menganalisis data dari faktor-faktor eksternal dan internal (IFE-EFE) secara deskriptif kualitatif dari hasil wawancara. Sampel terpilih 263 peternak dengan rumus Slovin dari tujuh kecamatan. Sampel dari setiap kecamatan terpilih dengan cara proportional dan informan kunci diambil secara sensus dari semua petugas IB di Kabupaten Luwu Timur sebanyak 12 orang, dan empat orang perwakilan dari pemerintahan dan akademisi. Hasil Penelitian menjelaskan bahwa faktor eksternal dan internal (IFE-EFE) yang diperlukan adalah peningkatan pengetahuan, dukungan finansial, dan penguatan koordinasi untuk mengatasi hambatan serta memaksimalkan manfaat IB secara sosial dan ekonomi. Strategi pengembangan program IB sapi ternak di Kabupaten Luwu Timur menekankan pada optimalisasi sumber daya dan pemanfaatan teknologi. Strategi ini mencakup peningkatan keterampilan inseminator bersertifikat, pemanfaatan sarana dan bantuan pemerintah untuk mobilitas serta fasilitas kesehatan ternak, dan pengembangan teknologi modern dalam pengolahan pakan dan limbah. Selain itu, penambahan poskeswan dan penyuluhan intensif diperlukan untuk mendekatkan layanan IB ke peternak, meningkatkan pengetahuan, serta menarik minat generasi muda. Koordinasi antara penyuluh dan petugas IB juga penting untuk memastikan layanan yang terintegrasi, sedangkan promosi peternakan modern berbasis digital dapat mendorong keberlanjutan usaha dan efisiensi dalam produksi ternak.

title: University teaching after generative AI: beyond lectures and inquiry to a certification-and-consultation paradigm in which learners become evaluators
f9b1987700faa334b0631f2879826f6822e59e19.abstract: Undergraduate teaching has rested on two paradigms, lectures and inquiry. Both treat what a student submits, an answer or the product of an inquiry, as evidence of the student's own learning, and generative AI breaks that premise. Credible judgement of ability now requires face-to-face probing, which demands more human time than the current staffing model can supply. Meanwhile AI is removing the junior work, such as grading and starter projects, through which people learned to judge, the first rung of the career ladder, just as demand for judgement grows: when a task completed with AI spans enough fields, no single person can judge all of it, and we conjecture that judging such work will increasingly depend on consulting people with depth in each field. Proposals for assessment reform call for structural change but assume that people able to certify and consult can be hired or redeployed, without asking where they will come from. We argue that the two problems can solve each other, and that the solution amounts to a third paradigm of university teaching. Teaching is organized around certification of understanding and consultation rather than the delivery or discovery of knowledge; lectures and inquiry remain as ways to learn. Students who have demonstrated competence take up certification and consultation posts under supervision. These posts supply the human time that certification requires, and the judging work itself trains those who hold them. Learners thus become evaluators, and universities rebuild the first rung, now leading toward the role of expert consultant that AI-assisted work increasingly needs. Teaching-assistant posts should move from grading to probing and consultation, so that credentials attest to what students can explain and defend. Personalized learning within a degree depends on certifying each student's own path. Probing can do this because it checks, face to face, whether a student holds the competences of a common framework, whatever work the student has done, and the same posts supply the time it takes.

title: Students Learn to Use Generative AI Before Learning to Question It: Ordinal Trajectories of Academic Use and Caution from Adolescence to University
881aaea9fc0b1cf72fd1f95d3fccc834d1f8a5f9.abstract: Students are adopting generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) at increasingly early educational stages, yet little is known about whether caution toward its outputs develops at the same pace. This study examined ordinal trajectories of academic GenAI use and caution, assessed as perceived reliability, from adolescence to university. Two coordinated surveys assessed use frequency and perceived reliability for the same 11 academic activities in an exact-age sample of 1,598 students: 1,167 secondary students aged 12-17 and 431 higher-education students aged 18-25, who also rated seven additional research-oriented activities. Between ages 12 and 17, the odds of higher use increased per year of age, whereas caution showed no significant change. The use-caution trajectories diverged significantly, first at ages 14-15 and more strongly at 16-17. In higher education, overall use showed no linear increase, but task-specific models revealed a shift from examination study and immediate question resolution toward translation and linguistic revision. Caution likewise showed no linear trend across university ages. However, fourth-year students had greater odds of strong caution than those in Years 1-3, particularly for advanced research tasks. These findings suggest that students use GenAI intensively before developing equivalent caution toward its responses: the divergence emerges during adolescence, whereas the first clear sign of correction appears only near degree completion. These findings highlight the need to introduce critical AI literacy education early in adolescence, combining practical experience with task-specific evaluation strategies.

title: AI4Design: A Human-Centred, Cross-Domain Framework for Generative AI in Digital System Design Education
bbfe5bd6b7483207910df026656a2ed33346d1bf.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence can produce synthesizable register-transfer-level code, testbenches, and design critiques, but it can also displace the cognitive work through which students learn abstraction, timing reasoning, and verification judgement. This paper asks how such tools can be integrated into undergraduate digital system design without exchanging unassisted competence for assisted artifact fluency. We present AI4Design, a design-science framework comprising an executable tool substrate, a pedagogic orchestration layer, and an assurance and assessment layer. Six principles govern its use, including independently derived executable oracles, progressive student autonomy, visible reasoning, and scheduled unassisted assessment. A fourteen-week course illustrates the framework: AI construction support peaks mid-term and is withdrawn for the capstone, while assessment combines executable checks, process evidence, oral defence, and transfer tasks. A cross-layer analysis identifies where software, circuits and boards, chips, and mechanisms can be coupled through executable interface checks. A descriptive tentask benchmark with two open-weight local models provides a limited technical pilot. The 2B model passed 2/10 tasks at first attempt and 4/10 after one repair; the 0.8B model passed 0/10 and 1/10, respectively. Initial successes occurred only on textual tasks. These results concern artifact production, not learning or crossdomain integration. A prospective multi-cohort, mixed-methods protocol specifies how learning, trust calibration, equity, and staff cost should be evaluated. The contribution is a testable course design and evaluation infrastructure, not evidence of educational efficacy.

title: Buying Capacity Before It Exists Advance Payments and Supply Commitments in AI Infrastructure 6 November 2026
b3c423f43d66ed7fd0a12f119b5793b74e79fc69.abstract: Abstract Advance contracts coordinate infrastructure investment by making selected obligations binding before projects are complete. This paper examines how that coordination connects equipment access, supplier funding, and investment momentum. We combine disclosures from three major power-equipment suppliers with buyer agreements and completed and discontinued project histories. Contract terms separate access, price, purchase obligations, and exit rights, allowing firms to commit to equipment while other development conditions remain unresolved. Customer payments bring procurement funds into suppliers' cash flows ahead of delivery. A stock-flow framework establishes when the progression of earlier reservations raises firm-order intake even as new commitments decline. GE Vernova's quarterly gross firm-backlog additions doubled from 8 to 16 GW between the first and third quarters of 2026, while new commitments fell from 21 to 11 GW. Conversions contributed 80.6% of gross firm-backlog additions over the nine months. The findings identify a source of persistence in infrastructure investment: earlier contracts continue to advance into production obligations after new intake slows. Evaluating an expansion therefore requires separating the arrival of commitments, their contractual advancement, and their eventual delivery. This distinction links firm-level contracting to industrial investment analysis in markets with long equipment lead times.

title: Development and Validation of a Multidimensional Gen-AI Competence Scale for Pre-Service Science Teachers
container-title: Jurnal Pendidikan MIPA
0b43a2d8345d0bbb8f023956e6a6f5caa7a79182.abstract: The rapid integration of generative artificial intelligence (Gen-AI) into education is transforming the competencies required of future teachers and creating a need for a robust multidimensional measure of Gen-AI competency. This study developed and validated a six-dimensional framework comprising output evaluation, use appropriateness, prompting & operation, technical integration, model literacy, and responsible practice among pre-service science teachers. Data were obtained from 426 biology, chemistry, and physics education students at Universitas Jambi, Indonesia. The responses were randomly split into EFA (n = 256; 60%) and CFA (n = 170; 40%) subsamples. An initial 84-item pool was evaluated through ten experts’ judgment using CVR and CVI, resulting in 63 content-valid items. The data were suitable for factor analysis (KMO = 0.972; Bartlett’s χ² = 20430.533; df = 1,953; p < 0.001), and EFA retained 33 items across six dimensions, with factor loadings of 0.502–0.811 and Cronbach’s alpha of 0.765–0.909. CFA supported the six-dimensional structure with acceptable fit (RMSEA = 0.063, CFI = 0.913, TLI = 0.904, SRMR = 0.052). The dimensions demonstrated satisfactory reliability and convergent validity (α = 0.754–0.909; CR = 0.752–0.910; AVE = 0.505–0.611), while HTMT values of 0.586–0.874 supported discriminant validity. The resulting measure provides an empirically supported basis for profiling Gen-AI competency and strengthening teachers’ preparation for responsible Gen-AI use. Keywords: generative artificial intelligence, gen-AI competency, instrument validation, pre-service science teachers.

title: Digital twin model for performance analysis and manufacturing process optimization
container-title: Pollack Periodica
102842548b5105920125e7f8f6bb9cbe5954392b.abstract: Abstract This study aims to develop a Digital Twin-based framework to address these challenges, with a practical application to heavy vehicle components. The proposed approach is characterized by the integration of planning data, operational parameters, and mathematical models into a unified digital platform that enables real-time monitoring and prediction. The results showed that the proposed system improved process performance prediction accuracy by 12.6%, reduced material waste by 9.4%, and reduced processing time by 7.8%, while achieving a significant improvement in the quality of the final surface. These indicators confirm that integrating Digital Twins into computer-aided manufacturing not only increases operational efficiency but also expands the potential for smart manufacturing by enhancing the reliability of digital modeling and supporting informed decision in complex industrial environments.

title: ANALYSIS OF THE ROLE OF DIGITAL MARKETING AND SERVICE QUALITY ON PURCHASING DECISIONS FOR CAT TREE PRODUCTS FROM CASPIRA MSMES

02b728f1a7cdbc8cf65add65e6f05a49058e2b55.abstract: Purpose: This study investigates the role of digital marketing and service quality on purchasing decisions. This study uses a quantitative methodology. Methods: This study uses primary data collected through an online survey with a Likert scale ranging from 1 to 5 points. The study population includes all consumers of Caspira MSMEs in Semarang Regency. The sampling technique uses non-random sampling with a purposive sampling method. The total number of participants is 40 respondents who have purchased Caspira MSME products. Data analysis: The data analysis technique uses multiple linear regression, and the data is processed with the SmartPLS 4.1.1.4 program. Result and discussions: This study illustrates that the role of digital marketing and service quality significantly and positively influences purchasing decisions. Conclusion: This study provides benefits for consumers as a basis for decision-making related to purchasing decisions at Caspira MSMEs, which are formed by many exogenous variables that influence endogenous variables.

title: Bias in Medical AI in Relation to Patient Empowerment and Digital Equity: Scoping Review
container-title: Online Journal of Public Health Informatics
21638a3b1d97502c2cea89d6c9b782a4ab8dc386.abstract: Abstract Background AI is increasingly embedded in health care and digital health applications, shaping clinical processes as well as how patients access information and participate in care. Research on bias in medical AI has largely focused on technical and performance-related disparities. Less attention has been paid to how such biases may affect patients’ access, understanding, trust, and opportunities for meaningful involvement in care. Objective This scoping review aimed to map how studies of bias in medical AI describe patient-related consequences relevant to patient empowerment and the digital divide and to identify gaps across technical, social, structural, and patient-centered perspectives. Methods This scoping review followed JBI (Joanna Briggs Institute) methodology and PRISMA-ScR (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews) reporting guidance. PubMed/MEDLINE and EBSCOHost databases were searched in August 2025 and supplemented by Google Scholar searches. Peer-reviewed studies published from 2015 onward were included if they addressed bias in medical AI and described patient-related consequences relevant to patient empowerment or digital inequality. Data charting focused on AI application types, bias dimensions, patient empowerment domains, digital divide–related factors, intersectionality, and debiasing strategies. Findings were synthesized descriptively and thematically. Results The search identified 497 records, of which 22 studies met the inclusion criteria. Bias was represented as a multidimensional sociotechnical phenomenon, with social bias identified most frequently (21/22 studies), followed by algorithmic bias (16/22 studies), structural bias (14/22 studies), and design-related bias (12/22 studies). Patient empowerment was most frequently addressed through involvement in care (n=13), followed by health literacy (n=9) and trust and assurance (n=7), whereas broader psychosocial and everyday-life domains were addressed less frequently. Digital divide–related factors were identified in 19 of the 22 studies, with digital literacy and usability barriers reported most frequently. Seven studies considered 2 or more social or structural dimensions of disadvantage. Although many studies discussed approaches that could mitigate bias-related barriers, explicit empirical evaluation of debiasing strategies in relation to patient empowerment or digital equity was largely absent. Conclusions Patient-related consequences of bias in medical AI extend beyond algorithmic performance and are reflected in access, understanding, trust, and involvement in care. Broader empowerment dimensions, multidimensional disadvantage, and empirically evaluated mitigation strategies remain comparatively underexplored.

title: Identifiability and processing-chain-calibrated interval inversion of pre-AGC digital responses in uncooled long-wave infrared imaging
container-title: Optics Express
224271d1803cf2d0972ba34567f12a2737415156.abstract: Automatic gain control (AGC) compresses high-bit-depth responses from uncooled long-wave infrared cameras into 8-bit outputs, but unknown scene-dependent monotone mappings make the pre-AGC coordinate non-identifiable. We recast inversion as processing-chain-conditioned interval estimation using a monotone-curve library, half-DN quantization preimages, residual expansion, and calibration. On paired FLIR ADAS and MM5 data, nonlinear monotone models reduce median fitting error relative to affine baselines by 65.9% and 46.2%, respectively. Within the two processing chains, 90% nominal intervals attain equal-unit coverages of 0.966 and 0.938. A block-held real-camera evaluation obtains 0.927 coverage while reducing mean interval width by 59.6% relative to an affine structural comparator. Against global radiometric-posterior and direct single-image reconstruction comparators, the proposed interval has lower occupied-range width, midpoint error, and Winkler score on both public datasets. Cross-chain target-library reconstruction is more than two orders of magnitude more interval-efficient than source-library widening. These results link response-coordinate identifiability, mapping-family support, and calibration for interval-valued recovery from 8-bit thermal images.

title: Unveiling Voices and Reimagining Belonging: Syrian Refugee Children’s Digital Stories as Counter-Narratives in Ontario K-12 Schooling
container-title: Refugee Education in Canada
c86cd147667070671cf05ae4ea48ccd9e4712808.abstract: This chapter draws on findings from a participatory visual research study that engaged Syrian refugee children and Ontario educators in a digital storytelling project. Grounded in the new sociology of childhood, sociocultural theory and critical pedagogy, the study treats refugee children as knowledge holders and digital storytelling as a mode of counter-narrative that contests exclusionary practices in Canadian K-12 schooling. The chapter examines how deficit-based discourses shape educator dispositions and institutional responses, and how children’s first-person digital stories disrupt narrow representations of refugee childhood. Bringing children’s stories into relation with educator reflections, the chapter traces how lived experiences make institutional assumptions visible and open pathways towards culturally responsive, inclusive practice. It also interrogates systemic barriers that constrain what schools can recognize and act upon. Overall, the chapter argues for reimagining refugee education beyond integration as a relational, justice-oriented politics of belonging that carries pedagogical and institutional obligations.

title: A Comparative Handbook of Redesigned Sales and Marketing Management in the Digital Era
1c315992d01f6fe5a4752fa9871bed02359a4278.abstract: In an age defined by rapid technological transformation, traditional sales and marketing paradigms are being reshaped by the competitive pressures of the digital landscape. A Comparative Handbook of Redesigned Sales and Marketing Management in the Digital Era offers a rigorous comparative analysis of these evolving practices, grounded in evidence-based insights and advanced modelling. With a focus on emerging pillars of the buying and selling process, the book maps the tactics and strategies necessary for success in a digitally driven world. From the integration of current innovations to the anticipation of future technological advancements, the book presents a forward-looking roadmap for navigating the complex, interconnected realities of modern sales management. Designed to serve business professionals, academics, students, and broader stakeholders, the author examines the outcomes, conflicts, and opportunities inherent in this shift, offering a nuanced discussion of its implications for organisations and their ecosystems.

title: Redesign of Core Concepts in Marketing in the Digital Era
container-title: A Comparative Handbook of Redesigned Sales and Marketing Management in the Digital Era
765e2852ca96c15aedf8506b69d6a320907df137.abstract: Abstract In our continuously changing, competitive era, having an economically strong, environmentally safe, and a better-managed globe requires not only digitally advanced, specialized manpower but also a gradual change from traditional to measurable, outcome-based, innovative solutions and an ethical, value-oriented growth mindset. This is valid for all business practices and society at large. Digital transformation is enhancing throughout every industry, bringing speed and easier access to information, connecting people while eliminating cross-border barriers and time constraints. In that respect, to maintain a long-term sustainable and profitable business, every firm should go through this digitalization process by adjusting and adapting its culture, organizational structure, people, and their digital infrastructure. The core disciplines of the organizations are also evolving from traditional practices to digital platforms and applications. Marketing is one of the earliest adopters of digitalization, where traditional marketing is geared toward digital marketing with the achievement of real-time access to information, providing faster and easier engagement of buyers and sellers. Today the authors refer to a redesigned, interactive, and integrated digital holistic marketing concept equipped with many smart technologies from social media marketing to affiliate marketing, maintaining the core principles of customer-centric relational marketing aligning with the new digital tools such as brand identity construction, voice search optimization, augmented reality, interactive content, and web design, building a new era supporting a technologically stronger, much more competitive market giving the opportunity of a co-value creation of buyers and sellers.

title: Redesign of Core Concepts in Sales in the Digital Era
container-title: A Comparative Handbook of Redesigned Sales and Marketing Management in the Digital Era
d20a1e4b813867b848b11267d0a4e89860795426.abstract: Abstract Today, digital transformation has set new criteria and rules for the commercial business and sales ecosystem. The real-time access to information, power of data analytics enhancing marketing intelligence, changing dynamics of consumer behavior, ever-evolving marketing trends, new buying cycles, and increased players in the market require a relook at the future scope of buyer and customer roadmap where sales is the backbone of this commercial path for firms having profitability, sustainability, and growth targets in the highly competitive global market. In our digital era, the redesigned sales model, beyond the product, is expected to cover many concepts such as productivity, optimization, the total value of ownership, timely delivery, after-sales support, financing, IT facilities, legal, regulatory, and ethical aspects. The sales professionals should act as strategic advisors, bridging and orchestrating all internal company stakeholders and external stakeholders for successful business outcomes, aligning with the customer care abouts and leading the co-value creation. Today, we refer AI integration to sales with digital CRM tools, predictive analytics, and many other digital facilities supporting salesforce for data-driven interactive selling process. While this presents many opportunities for the organizations and for the sales professionals, such as faster track of customer leads, quick market intelligence for strategizing more efficiently, it definitely requires digitally adapted culture, competency in digital technologies and a customer-centric winning mindset with knowledge, commitment, agility and competitive differentiation.

title: Field Study: Expected Change in Technology, Organizations, and Business in the Digital Era
container-title: A Comparative Handbook of Redesigned Sales and Marketing Management in the Digital Era
68b51309688dc6e568de5b7e88dee6ce2e322b3c.abstract: Abstract In today’s continuously evolving globe, digital technologies are transforming firms, the way organizations act, think, and strategize to maintain a profitable and sustainable business. This requires the proactive strategy of companies with a digital mindset and culture, adapting to the new dynamics of the unbarriered markets. Customers are now more powerful with access to information, aware of their needs, with an increasing concern on a cleaner, accountable, ethical, and transparent future world. This chapter evaluates the answers of commercial business professionals from corporate world on qualifying the expected impacts of digitalization on organizations, in organizational structure, the effects of artificial intelligence (AI) integration, the influence of social media, the changes in consumer behavior, and how the new sales professionals are expected to manage the new customer journey in terms of the value creation, differentiation, and engagement for competitive advantages. A second survey conducted among industry stakeholders from various businesses assesses the required attributes of a sales professional in the digital era. The analysis of the results indicate the increasing transformation in digital era where most firms are urged for digitalization as the common mind of interviewees addressing mostly hybrid organizations benefiting from the human and digital power depending on the complexity of the industry. Digital competency of sales professionals in predicting market intelligence and insights for strategic decision-making, customer centricity, solution selling, engaging customers for co-value creation for innovation, and loyalty underline the new norms of sales professionals in the digital era.

title: Evaluation of Changing Customer Behavior in the Digital Era
container-title: A Comparative Handbook of Redesigned Sales and Marketing Management in the Digital Era
207d6524df8e52e73b70988713260c0cd328a4d9.abstract: Abstract The digitalization via continuously developing artificial intelligence (AI) tools such as machine learning, natural language processing, and generative AI give the consumers the opportunity to decrease their workload and have the power to check for competitive pricing and optimized solutions. In parallel, we must recognize and embrace the essence and contribution of all digital tools providing a huge base for information connecting the consumers and business bringing speed to access data, and faster buyer–seller interactions. This in return is expected to take the consumer journey and decision-making scheme to an extended level in near future where consumers are expected to dominate more on their demands and personally defined needs not only by satisfying their personal expectations but also by giving directions to the firms’ strategies in terms of new innovations and solutions for future. This “New Customer Profile” in the digital era worths diagnosis on its changing buying roadmap compared to traditional practices as today we talk about insightful and empowered customers, increased ecommerce activities, more integration and interaction with social media, and the impact of AI use by the customers. The demand for customization requires companies to be better equipped in terms of organization, brand identity, and digital competency. Despite ongoing privacy and ethical concerns on digital arena, commodity, and retail goods expand utilizing the digital platforms reaching consumers, the complex industries such as healthcare, financial markets, and high-tech industry business still reserve room for traditional practices where in-person communication with end user and trust are highly required.

title: Sales Management: From Core to New Scopes and Strategy in the Digital Era
container-title: A Comparative Handbook of Redesigned Sales and Marketing Management in the Digital Era
ce4c28aefd3c986f492853027788c46fd51c512a.abstract: Abstract The core requirements of effective sales management are planning and strategy while being equally competent with the salesforce management by setting performance and internal controls. In parallel, there must be a clear analysis of markets. Today, the technology integration by digital transformation has brought a different base to the role of sales management. The digital customer relationship management tools like most common being salesforce, HubSpot, and Power BI are all used in most of the commercial companies, where these platforms provide a comprehensive suite for tracking sales, marketing, and service activities, enabling the visibility of the customer-buying journey. In parallel, in our continuously digitalizing and changing business environments, organizations analyze and work to implement the most suitable service model, which can be service-based, customer-based, or multilevel models, to optimize their operations while improving customer satisfaction and profitability. As technology evolves, many companies work on the implementation of hybrid models depending on the company goals, industry dynamics, market conditions, and the customer needs. Digitalization is also effective on improving the diversity and inclusion in organizations. The technology proves clearly that it can align people via discussion platforms for “connected teams”. Today sales planning and budgeting are also supported by digital tools streamlining these processes for faster and more accurate outcomes. The other core pillars in the sales management such as forecasting, opportunity tracking, value propositioning, and negotiation are also enhanced by digital platforms with optimized competitive and customer-centric solutions.

title: International Sales Management and Expected Practices in the Digital Era
container-title: A Comparative Handbook of Redesigned Sales and Marketing Management in the Digital Era
213156dc246e8c72c840cd8193ada1f3cc899f03.abstract: Abstract Companies may have different goals when entering international markets. These objectives generally include increasing sales, revenue, and profit potential, establishing a new customer base, providing expansion and diversification opportunities, gaining greater access to talent, gaining a competitive advantage, managing risks, enhancing company reputation, reducing operating costs, creating economies of scale, and leveraging tax advantages if available. Firms can conduct international business directly or via distributors. The selection of distributors is critical in terms of compliance, financial strength, local competitive power, and customer engagement. Today, firms profit from digitalization by enhanced resource accessibility, improved market access, faster and more efficient communications, while the digital technologies also give the businesses the opportunity of going beyond the geographic boundaries and deliver customized content, present products and services through data driven insights and advanced analytics. Equally these platforms support companies in terms of effective digital marketing, brand identity setting, and customer engagement. Today, companies must set their business and sales strategies aligning also their digitalization plans utilizing global e-commerce, social media, and other digital networks while expanding across borders, engaging various customers, and optimizing their supply chains. It is noteworthy to consider challenges of regulatory barriers, platform dependencies, data privacy, and high competition. Achieving success in today’s digitally moderated environment also requires cross-functional integration for companies which means bridging marketing, legal, IT, and supply chain pillars to optimize digital infrastructure, ensuring regulatory compliance, and managing this fundamental complexity of ecosystem in international arenas.

title: Essence of Corporate Governance, Sustainability, and Social Responsiveness in the Digital Era
container-title: A Comparative Handbook of Redesigned Sales and Marketing Management in the Digital Era
324ca77850ee47ad9827a0af442d9cdd319c3518.abstract: Abstract The technological development and the continuously growing digital economy have created a different profile of corporations, capital markets, and changed the nature of the global economy at large. This situation has its obvious expected corporate governance impacts and outcomes. The use of digital technology improves regulatory efficiency and enhances disclosure practices, market supervision, and enforcement of corporate governance-related requirements. New platforms based on big data and machine learning enable the systematic application and transparency of environmental, social, and governance (ESG) information for investors and companies. This situation encourages shifting capital from less sustainable to more sustainable companies. Today, it can be predicted that the importance of environmental and natural life protection requirements and institutional responsibilities will be an even more crucial plan at the government, companies, and the individual level. Equally, global business management and corporate governance trends are also changing and transforming into new structures in the digital era and we observe more attention and efforts of many multinational firms to improve their integrity, diversity, and inclusion strategy. In parallel notes to mention that the digitalization has not only given the access to consumers to have a full visibility of goods and services in the market but also has transformed people to “conscious customers” who are more determined on their needs, preferences, and buying decisions. Therefore, in our digital era, the consumers are expected to be keener in their investment decisions, and these investment decisions can gear toward more ESG-oriented firms.

title: Changing Role of HR in the Digital Era and Expected Impacts on Business
container-title: A Comparative Handbook of Redesigned Sales and Marketing Management in the Digital Era
01e2eeec0f34064773dd703e30b5032635da2197.abstract: Abstract Digital transformation is already changing the traditional business models, including human resource management (HRM) practices in organizations, as the technology is globally setting new norms and business conduct toward connecting people with measurable, accessible, and data-based processes in firms targeting real-time information, accuracy, and speed for improving operational excellence. Human power being an asset for companies makes the role of HRM more critical in the digital era due to high competition and changing customer behavior, provoking the need for more innovative solutions to differentiate in global markets. In that spectrum, talent acquisition and retention become vital factors to long-term success. Today, as a part of digital transformation, digital HRM is also a concept evolving in organizations, which should be a part of the company strategy in terms of its infrastructure and HRM stakeholders’ competency accelerating the cultural change for a digital mindset in the total organization. Tools like predictive analytics and data mining not only provide data-based insights for HR stakeholders, speeding up the HR processes, but also give the opportunity for utilizing time on more strategic initiatives. Empirical and theoretical studies present the correlation of HRM with firm performance, productivity, and profitability. In parallel, the global environmental, social and governmental (ESG) requirements underlining the essence of decent work and economic growth encourage HRM to position itself with the strategic role to lead sustainable organizations. Once the digital ethics and HRM skillset competency are completed, the digital HRM is expected to expand and be grounded in organizations aligned with the companies’ overall digital transformation strategies.

title: Critical Pillars of Competitive Edge for Firms in the Digital Era
container-title: A Comparative Handbook of Redesigned Sales and Marketing Management in the Digital Era
c86b07d062a1b0b051110cbc8a56820fd9af96bd.abstract: Abstract Today, one of the critical success factors of long-term profitable business in the highly competitive arena is the digital transformation by utilizing the benefits of technology, streamlining the workflow of operations, automating routine tasks to improve the business efficiency and productivity. On the other hand, the technologies are still not at the complete maturity stage including the cybersecurity concerns while the growth of digital technologies is very fast, setting expectations for overcoming the existing challenges by profiting from the data-based insights, real-time information, interactive communication without the geographical barriers as well as automation and optimization of processes impacting the operational excellency and faster decision mechanisms. Also, consumers have evolved into more conscious buyers profiting from digital platforms, social media, and real-time information encouraging them for personalized solutions matching their care abouts. This new phenomenon equally bridges the customer and the firm for co-creating value by faster innovations. In the interim, there are major criteria for impactful digital transformation, and this chapter underlines the essence of 11 parameters with an authentic scheme addressing the readiness for competitive edge. The firms are expected to have a cultural organizational change toward digitalization by investing in new technologies, in house IT with a focus of improving digital competencies of their employees, channel partners, and human resource management (HRM) stakeholders. The corporate governance digital transformation strategy with the set key performance indicators (KPIs) embracing compliance, digital ethics, cybersecurity infrastructures, and sustainability efforts are crucial for long-term profitable business.

title: Ethical and legal challenges of digital twin technologies in residential buildings
container-title: Smart and Sustainable Built Environment
1b9b495284254e027884aa748022c076a4410a05.abstract: Purpose The literature on the ethical and legal challenges associated with Home Digital Twin technologies is fragmented, limiting a coherent understanding of how these issues are addressed. Therefore, this study aims to synthesise the key ethical and legal challenges related to the use of digital twin technologies in residential buildings. Design/methodology/approach A structured integrative literature review, supported by a systematic search of Scopus and Web of Science, was conducted. Following the screening process, 41 publications were included and analysed using a hybrid inductive–deductive content analysis. Findings Five overarching themes were identified: (1) data privacy and security, (2) bias and fairness, (3) informed consent, (4) transparency and accountability, and (5) informed decision-making. Collectively, these findings indicate a structural imbalance in digital twin applications in residential buildings, where technical capabilities are advancing more rapidly than legal accountability, regulatory clarity, and enforceable user protections. This misalignment raises concerns about trust, autonomy, and fairness in digitally mediated residential environments and points to the need for stronger governance responses. Originality/value This study contributes to the current knowledge by synthesising fragmented ethical and legal discussions on the use of digital twins in residential buildings and articulating their shared governance implications. By organising these issues into five main themes, the study offers a structured understanding of challenges that are typically examined in isolation.

title: Aligning institutions and organizations for sustainable supply chains: the role of digital transformation and low-carbon practices
container-title: Supply Chain Management: An International Journal
af7f22db9f22c3964bb66acb9d57ccadccdb77ec.abstract: Purpose The transition toward carbon neutrality has become a global strategic priority for achieving sustainable development and a green economy. Despite growing interest in digital transformation among scholars and practitioners, achieving a balance between green supply chain performance and carbon performance within the context of carbon neutrality remains underexplored. Drawing on the technology acceptance model and change management theory, this research aims to provide solutions for achieving the zero-carbon target in 2060 through holistic digital transformation, and how institutional pressure and organizational readiness influence green supply chain and carbon performance through digital transformation, low-carbon operations management practices (LCOMP) and the moderating role of environmental proactivity. Design/methodology/approach Data from 442 Chinese manufacturing firms were analyzed using Smart PLS v4 to test the research hypotheses. Findings The results indicate that all three dimensions of LCOMP mediate the relationship between digital transformation, green supply chain and carbon performance. In addition, environmental proactivity strengthens the influence of digital transformation on the three dimensions of LCOMP. Originality/value The findings contribute to the literature by addressing a key gap in sustainable supply chain and digital transformation research, which has largely examined these relationships in isolation without fully explaining the mediating mechanisms and boundary conditions.

title: Digital leapfrogging or digital divide? Internet penetration and structural transformation in Africa
container-title: Digital Policy, Regulation and Governance
6a8c1d0e6309273d6b1b7554d0f393efdb4353f7.abstract: Purpose This study aims to investigate whether digitalization accelerates structural transformation in African economies or reinforces existing structural inequalities. Design/methodology/approach Using panel data on African countries and a rigorous fixed-effects framework, complemented by dynamic System GMM estimation, the analysis provides a direct test of the digital structural transformation hypothesis. Findings The results show a strong and robust positive effect of internet penetration on structural transformation, even after controlling for key macroeconomic and demographic factors. Sectoral evidence reveals a clear mechanism: increased internet access reduces the share of agriculture while significantly expanding the services sector, confirming that digitalization actively reallocates economic activity across sectors. Crucially, interaction results show that the impact of internet penetration is stronger in slower-growing, less advanced economies, providing compelling evidence in favor of the digital leapfrogging hypothesis rather than the digital divide. Originality/value These findings establish digital infrastructure as a central driver of modern structural change and suggest that expanding internet access can serve as a powerful policy tool for accelerating inclusive development in Africa.

title: Beyond the basics: how digital transformation, orientation and competence fuel SME performance through resilience in the manufacturing sector
container-title: International Journal of Productivity and Performance Management
d90d72802b14d894a8f74edaa0ca3c01d8a38422.abstract: Purpose In emerging economies such as Pakistan, SMEs have a high failure rate, underscoring the need to understand what drives SME performance. This paper fills a knowledge gap by considering the impact of digital transformation, entrepreneurial orientation, entrepreneurial competencies and entrepreneurial resilience on SMEs' performance. Entrepreneurial resilience serves as a mediator between digital transformation, entrepreneurial orientation, entrepreneurial competencies and SME performance. Finally, environmental dynamism (ED) is used as a moderator between entrepreneurial resilience and SMEs' performance. Design/methodology/approach Data were collected from 453 managers of manufacturing SMEs in Punjab, Pakistan. Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling is used for hypothesis testing. Findings Digital transformation, entrepreneurial orientation and entrepreneurial competencies have a significant and positive influence on entrepreneurial resilience and SME performance. Entrepreneurial resilience significantly enhances SMEs' performance. Additionally, entrepreneurial resilience significantly mediates the relationships among digital transformation, entrepreneurial orientation, entrepreneurial competencies and SME performance. Finally, ED significantly moderates the relationship between entrepreneurial resilience and SMEs' performance. Practical implications SME managers should prioritize digital transformation, entrepreneurial orientation, competence, resilience and ED to measure SMEs' performance. Policymakers can support these efforts by developing adaptive frameworks that enable SMEs to remain competitive in dynamic environments. Originality/value This is initial research that integrates digital transformation, entrepreneurial orientation, entrepreneurial competence, entrepreneurial resilience and ED to examine SME performance within the resource orchestration theory (ROT).

title: Digital transformation and marketing synergy in the sustainable development of tourism enterprise
container-title: Tourism and Hospitality Studies
668e954e7215d00a96ec1da10a54229a95f7986e.abstract: In the modern era, the rapid and continuous development of digital technologies has had a significant and multidimensional impact on the management systems, marketing strategies, and customer relationship management of enterprises operating in the tourism sector. The concept of digital transformation is not limited to the implementation of new technological solutions; it also requires the reconfiguration of organizational culture, employee behavior patterns, internal and external communication mechanisms, and social interactions in accordance with the modern digital environment. This process necessitates the adoption of more flexible management approaches in tourism enterprises and creates conditions for improving both internal efficiency and customer-oriented service quality. The main purpose of this study is to comprehensively examine the interrelationships between organizational behavior, social interaction, and marketing synergy in tourism enterprises, as well as to determine the impact of these factors on overall marketing performance. The article analyzes, from theoretical and conceptual perspectives, the influence of organizational behavior patterns and social interactions on marketing outcomes in the context of digital transformation. The research findings indicate that enhancing employee motivation, improving leadership quality, establishing effective internal and external communication systems, and integrating digital marketing tools within a unified strategy play a crucial role in strengthening the competitiveness and market position of tourism enterprises. Furthermore, the interaction of these factors enables organizations to increase customer satisfaction, ensure service personalization, and create longterm loyalty.

title: PROSPECTS FOR THE APPLICATION OF DIGITAL TECHNOLOGIES IN THE ACCOUNTING AND AUDITING SYSTEM
container-title: Tourism and Hospitality Studies
57041879c7af1769850dff7621595542435cfa7b.abstract: Purpose of the research – The purpose of this study is to examine the application areas of modern digital technologies in the accounting and auditing system, evaluate their impact on financial reporting, audit quality, and managerial efficiency, identify the existing challenges, and develop scientifically grounded recommendations regarding future development prospects. Research methodology – The study is based on a systematic approach and employs comparative analysis, content analysis, induction, and deduction methods. Contemporary scientific literature, international accounting and auditing standards, and studies on digital technologies were analyzed. Practical implications of the research – The findings of this study provide practical guidance for the digital transformation of accounting and auditing systems, the automation of audit procedures, the improvement of financial reporting quality, and the enhancement of managerial decision-making processes within organizations. Research findings – The study demonstrates that artificial intelligence, blockchain, Big Data, cloud computing, and robotic process automation (RPA) significantly improve the efficiency of accounting and auditing systems. Originality and scientific novelty – The study provides a comprehensive evaluation of the application of digital technologies in accounting and auditing by systematically analyzing the influence of various digital solutions on financial management 2 and audit quality. It presents scientifically grounded conclusions regarding the benefits, challenges, and future prospects of digital transformation and offers practical recommendations for the effective implementation of innovative technologies in accounting and auditing systems.

title: Continuous identity assurance for Zero-Trust edge and IoT services
container-title: Digital Transformation and Society
f9ca7dac3326eced5161a202008398604c35c44e.abstract: Purpose Long-lived authorisation can outlast its supporting identity, device and contextual evidence. This study develops a privacy-aware continuous identity-assurance framework for reversible Zero-Trust decisions in edge and Internet of Things (IoT) services. Design/methodology/approach Design Science Research structures the artifact. Seeded Monte Carlo analysis examines synthetic controller behaviour through baselines, matched legitimate-access calibration, sensitivity, ablation and adverse conditions. A Raspberry Pi 4 prototype measures incremental authorisation overhead, not security effectiveness. Findings Under reference synthetic assumptions, 38 of 100,000 post-boot endpoint-compromise requests met the ordinary-access threshold. Weight choice and behaviour-preserving malware exposed failure regions; missing or stale evidence caused availability loss. Matched calibration found no globally dominant controller: simpler alternatives matched FULL in the Reference condition, and B2 reduced false acceptance rate under behaviour-preserving malware. P2 added 0.117–0.207 ms mean server-processing latency beyond P1, supporting feasibility only for the tested prototype and loads. Practical implications Deployment should progress from sender constraint and evidence governance through observation, local calibration, shadow testing and controlled testing to reversible enforcement under owned accessibility, outage and rollback criteria. Social implications Purpose limitation, alternative verification, accessibility review, contestability and separation of security telemetry from employment, credit or reputation uses address continuous-observation risks; human outcomes were not evaluated. Originality/value Novelty lies in integrating evidence ageing, conservative missingness and uncertainty, non-compensable predicates, reversible authorisation, pre-collection privacy governance and deployment calibration, rather than in a new probabilistic trust primitive.

title: Digital-green synergistic transformation of manufacturing firms: configurational pathways and AI enabling effects
container-title: Journal of Manufacturing Technology Management
dec4772b4333b313d298320fc34d9261d33b006f.abstract: Purpose This study investigates the configurational pathways underpinning digital-green synergistic transformation (DGT) and examines the enabling role of artificial intelligence (AI), thereby advancing understanding of how manufacturing firms navigate the dual imperatives of green development and digital upgrading. Design/methodology/approach Using 9,336 firm-year observations from 2,407 Chinese manufacturing firms over 2013–2023, this study draws on the Technology-Organization-Environment (TOE) framework and employs dynamic QCA to identify pathways and panel regressions to examine AI’s enabling effects and heterogeneity. Findings Results indicate that no single factor constitutes a necessary condition for DGT. We identify three distinct configurational pathways to high DGT: “endogenous dual-innovation driven” (SC1), “policy-driven and green-led” (SC2) and “policy-driven and digital-led” (SC3). AI significantly promotes DGT by enabling these pathways, with the largest estimated enabling effect observed for SC1, followed by SC3 and SC2. Heterogeneity analysis reveals that the enabling effect of AI is more pronounced in state-owned enterprises, firms with high market attention and those with high industrial chain integration. Originality/value This study contributes to the literature at the intersection of digitalization and greening by elucidating how multiple technological, organizational and environmental factors form configurational pathways to DGT. It further demonstrates AI’s enabling role in these pathways, providing insights into how firms can embed AI to achieve their strategic goals. By revealing how AI’s effects vary across firm, market and industry contexts, this study advances a contextualized understanding of AI-enabled transformation.
