title: From Static to Dynamic: Parameter Manipulation as Adaptive DDL Scaffolding in Creative Writing with Generative AI
container-title: Digital Studies in Language and Literature
0cab7f5810a1874161e8697bc3ba26fb3c000c49.abstract: Abstract Generative AI tools now pervade university classrooms, yet the field lacks empirical understanding of how technical AI configurations translate into adaptive Data-driven Learning (DDL) scaffolding. This gap is crucial in creative writing, where excessive structure can suppress authorship and insufficient support can stall exploration. This study investigates how large language model (LLM) parameter configuration functions as a pedagogical design lever for DDL scaffolding in poetry writing classrooms. Across a three-phase mixed-methods study with 30 university creative writing learners (a 2 × 2 factorial experiment, an offline classroom workshop, and an online classroom workshop), two parameter settings, temperature and top-p, reliably reshaped the distribution of three pre-coded interaction types: Constraint Repair (Type A), Exemplar Giving (Type B), and Surprise Harvest (Type C). Moving from a structured to an exploratory setting, Type C rose roughly seven-fold in Phase 1, with the same direction of effect in the two subsequent classroom phases. Triangulating chat logs, reflection templates, and panel transcripts, Type B was voted most helpful but linked to diminished authorship, while Type C was associated with the highest authorship and satisfaction. We position parameter literacy as a necessary instructor competence for adaptive AI scaffolding.

title: Legitimacy Boundaries in Crisis: Online Learning Adoption in Ultra-Orthodox Schools During COVID-19
container-title: Journal of Religion, Media and Digital Culture
22c5d06d977dbdfc562ac3a8fefe3e1f7457dd79.abstract: Abstract The restrictions imposed on the citizens of Israel with the outbreak of COVID-19 forced educational institutions to adopt online channels for distance learning. The ultra-Orthodox society, bound by its suspicious and disapproving approach to the use of media, especially among teenagers and children, had to deal with the new circumstances and decide its course of action to resolve this conflict. The present study investigates whether, and to what extent, online channels were used in ultra-Orthodox educational institutions in their various subsections, and what were parents’ and teachers’ considerations, attitudes, and perceptions regarding the adoption of online learning in either COVID-19 or in any future similar emergencies. The article combines quantitative and qualitative methods based on a survey among a representative sample of parents of primary school-aged children (N=395) and semi-structured interviews (N=45) with parents and teachers in ultra-Orthodox schools. The results show that 14% of all parents in the sample use Zoom for distance learning. Furthermore, significant differences were found between the different sub-currents, with the Chabad stream being the most popular (94%), followed at a large margin by the Sephardic public (15%), Lithuanian (13%), and Hasidic (4%). Differences were also found between the sub-currents in terms of parents’ willingness to use online learning channels in the future, and correlations were found between parents’ level of conservatism/modernism, learners’ gender identity, their age and willingness to use online learning channels. However, almost none of the participants saw this period as an opportunity for pedagogical development related to the potential of studies in the online spaces, but as a limitation that requires coping and necessary adaptation to minimize the damage.

title: Datafied Religion: How Well do Commercial Image Recognition Services Recognize Religion?
container-title: Journal of Religion, Media and Digital Culture
401d0cd3cf6fd2e685b870c9179e4d2ef38cedb3.abstract: Abstract This article explores the relationship between technology and religion by empirically analysing how the image recognition services provided by three leading US tech companies and machine vision developers—Google, Amazon, and Microsoft—classify religious images and what implications follow from their classifications. The data were collected from Google Images: they consist of images related to Christianity, Islam, Hinduism, Buddhism, and Shintoism. Methodologically and theoretically, our interdisciplinary and exploratory article combines computational social science techniques with religious and media studies theories and qualitative research methods. The main result of our research is that in the context of religion, image recognition services produce secular, Christian, commercial, and racist biases.

title: The Impact of the Digital Economy on the High-Quality Development of Foreign Trade: Evidence from City-Level Panel Data in Anhui Province
container-title: Economics & Business Management
cbf15a6cffdcd45c6ce224bb1026d4a5185309cc.abstract: The digital economy is reshaping global trade and creating new opportunities for the high-quality development of foreign trade.Taking the prefecture-level cities of Anhui Province during 2010–2023 as the empirical sample,this paper constructs a composite index of digital economy development along four dimensions—digital infrastructure,digital industrialisation,the digitalisation of industry,and digital talent—and an index of the high-quality development of foreign trade covering foreign trade volume,foreign trade structure and foreign trade competitiveness, both measured using the entropy weight method.A two-way fixed effects model is estimated to examine the effect of the digital economy on the high-quality development of foreign trade in Anhui.The results show that the digital economy exerts a significantly positive promoting effect on the high-quality development of foreign trade in the province,and that this effect displays pronounced regional and temporal heterogeneity. The findings carry practical implications for how Chinese provinces can seize the opportunities of the digital era to advance the high-quality development of foreign trade.

title: Leveraging a Terminology Service to Facilitate Semantic Interoperability for Continuity of Care: A Sri Lankan Perspective
container-title: Oxford Open Digital Health
581da625774d16c183198c936ef6a03cf857f94c.abstract: Abstract Sri Lanka’s digital health ecosystem is characterized by multiple heterogeneous Electronic Medical Record (EMR) systems operating in silos, limiting continuity of care. While HL7 FHIR-based data exchange with the National Electronic Health Record (NEHR) is being utilized to achieve syntactic interoperability, semantic interoperability remains constrained due to use of non-standardized clinical terminologies across EMRs. This case study describes the experience of leveraging a terminology service to standardize locally used clinical data and enable semantic interoperability in a low-resource setting. An OpenHIE-aligned architecture was implemented using Open Concept Lab (OCL) online as the terminology service, Open Health Information Mediator (OpenHIM) as the interoperability layer and HapiFHIR as a health data store. Locally defined value-sets for presenting complaints, diagnoses, medications, procedures, and investigations were extracted from multiple national EMRs, consolidated, and mapped to well recognized international terminology standards including SNOMED-GPS and LOINC through a multi-stakeholder process. The implementation resulted in creation of four terminology sources, 17 collections, 3,169 concepts, and 1,247 mappings, validated through national Connectathons. A mapping mediator was used for the transformation of local or free-text inputs into coded terminology prior to persistence in the NEHR, ensuring semantic consistency while preserving original data. The findings demonstrate that terminology mapping using open-source, OpenHIE-aligned technologies is a feasible approach for enabling semantic interoperability in low-resource settings. However, long-term sustainability requires adoption of standardized terminologies at the point of data capture, strengthened governance mechanisms, and continued capacity building.

title: MEMBANGUN KESADARAN DIGITAL MELALUI EDUKASI BIJAK BERMEDIA SOSIAL UNTUK PENANGKALAN HOAKS DENGAN BANTUAN MEDIA POSTER
BUILDING DIGITAL AWARENESS THROUGH EDUCATION ON WISE SOCIAL MEDIA USE TO COUNTER HOAXES, USING POSTERS AS AN EDUCATIONAL TOOL
container-title: Jurnal Pengabdian Multidisiplin dan Pemberdayaan Masyarakat
77e0cf6dce00acf24c7324444fed1c184f63bf9a.abstract: Kemudahan memperoleh informasi melalui media sosial diiringi oleh penyebaran hoaks dan penipuan digital yang dapat memicu kesalahpahaman, fitnah, dan konflik di tengah masyarakat. Kegiatan pengabdian ini bertujuan membangun kesadaran masyarakat Dusun Tangkel, Desa Kertagena Tengah, Kecamatan Kadur, Kabupaten Pamekasan, mengenai pentingnya bermedia sosial secara bijak, meningkatkan kewaspadaan terhadap hoaks dan penipuan digital, serta mendorong pemeriksaan informasi sebelum disebarkan. Metode pelaksanaan meliputi identifikasi kebutuhan melalui pengamatan dan interaksi langsung dengan warga, penyusunan materi edukasi, perancangan poster menggunakan Canva, pencetakan, dan pemasangan pada titik yang ramai dikunjungi warga. Hasil kegiatan berupa poster bertema “Bijak Bermedia Sosial: Saring Informasi, Sebarkan Kebaikan” yang memuat empat langkah, yaitu kenali sumbernya, cek kebenarannya, tanya dan pastikan, serta jangan ikut menyebarkan, disertai ajakan bertabayyun sebelum meneruskan kabar. Kegiatan ini tidak menggunakan pre-test dan post-test sehingga peningkatan pengetahuan belum dapat diukur secara kuantitatif. Poster menjadi media edukasi yang sederhana dan dapat dibaca masyarakat secara mandiri dalam kehidupan sehari-hari.

title: Technology acceptance and electronic word-of-mouth adoption in digital alternative food network
container-title: Frontiers in Sustainable Food Systems
7c9f5e5cedbb84e0f6bfb6a86f7673d1e47c6f67.abstract: Alternative Food Network (AFN) supports the transition toward more sustainable food systems through shorter supply chains and closer interactions between producers and consumers. However, limited evidence explains how technology acceptance and electronic word-of-mouth (eWOM) adoption jointly shape consumers’ purchase intention toward agri-fresh produce in digital AFN. This study examines this relationship using an extended Technology Acceptance Model that incorporates eWOM adoption. Data were collected from consumers in Bandung, Indonesia, who were accustomed to purchasing agri-fresh produce through conventional food channels and had previously accessed information related to digital AFN. Data were analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling. The results suggest that perceived ease of use has the strongest direct effect on purchase intention, followed by perceived usefulness and eWOM adoption. There is a significant positive association between perceived ease of use and perceived usefulness. eWOM adoption is also significantly and positively associated with perceived ease of use and perceived usefulness. The indirect-effect analysis further shows significant relationships between eWOM adoption and purchase intention through perceived ease of use and perceived usefulness. These findings highlight that consumers’ purchase intention in digitally enabled AFN depends on both technology acceptance and eWOM adoption. In practical terms, digital AFN actors should provide user-friendly purchasing processes and encourage consumers to share useful product information and purchasing experiences through digital channels.

title: Transformasi Digital dalam Pendidikan di Indonesia
container-title: EduCurio: Education Curiosity
a9c3312d2aef0f72bca48a1c52c22068c14226a5.abstract: Pertumbuhan penelitian transformasi digital pendidikan di Indonesia memerlukan pemetaan untuk memahami struktur pengetahuan, perubahan tema, dan kesenjangan bukti. Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis perkembangan publikasi, sitasi, kolaborasi, struktur konseptual, evolusi tematik, serta agenda penelitian. Analisis bibliometrik dipadukan dengan telaah substantif melalui seleksi literatur berpedoman PRISMA. Kumpulan awal mencakup 899 artikel dari Dimensions, dengan 401 artikel periode 2024–2026 ditetapkan sebagai korpus akhir berdasarkan kriteria kelayakan dan ketersediaan teks lengkap. Data dicatat menggunakan formulir ekstraksi terstruktur dan dianalisis melalui statistik publikasi, jejaring kolaborasi, kemunculan bersama istilah, pemetaan tematik, serta sintesis isi dengan dukungan VOSviewer dan Biblioshiny. Hasil menunjukkan pertumbuhan publikasi tahunan sebesar 112,67%, sedangkan kolaborasi internasional hanya mencapai 2,244% dan jejaring antarpenulis masih terfragmentasi. Tiga klaster utama mencakup infrastruktur dan pedagogi digital, kepemimpinan dan tata kelola, serta pendidikan tinggi dengan pendekatan kuantitatif. Penekanan tematik bergeser dari kesiapan digital menuju pembelajaran, analisis, dan perancangan. Telaah substantif mengidentifikasi kebutuhan penelitian mengenai kepemimpinan digital, keselarasan pendidikan vokasi dengan industri, dan keberlanjutan. Penelitian ini menyimpulkan bahwa perkembangan literatur perlu diikuti penguatan kolaborasi dan pengujian empiris hubungan antara kesiapan institusi, penerapan teknologi, dan hasil pendidikan. Interpretasi temuan dibatasi oleh cakupan satu basis data dan periode pengamatan yang singkat.

title: Literasi Kesehatan Digital dan Dukungan Sosial sebagai Moderator Keterikatan Aplikasi mHealth terhadap Perilaku Peningkatan Kesehatan Remaja
container-title: Celebes Advance Health Journal
32b72e497fcade426d924e7094b9b96a1de81e94.abstract: Background: Digital health interventions frequently yield inconsistent outcomes among youth due to unexamined conual fac- tors. Objective: This study aimed to examine the conditional processes through which mobile health (mHealth) app engagement influences adolescent health-promoting behaviors, specifically identifying the moderating roles and empirical thresholds of social support and digital health literacy. Methods: A cross-sectional study was conducted at Poltekkes Kemenkes Makassar from February to May 2025. A sample of 205 adolescents completed validated surveys assessing mHealth engagement, social support (MSPSS), e-health literacy (I-eHEALS), and health behaviors. Ethical approval was granted by the institutional ethics committee, and informed consent was obtained. Data were analyzed using multiple regression and Johnson-Neyman moderation techniques. Results: The mHealth engagement significantly predic- ted health-promoting behaviors (beta = .26, p <.001), with the overall model explaining 44.9% of the variance (R2 = .449). Moderation analyses confirmed significant interaction effects for social support (beta = .18, p = .004) and digital health literacy (beta = .15, p = .012). Floodlight analysis revealed that mHealth engagement became statistically significant only when social support exceeded 48.20 and digital health literacy exceeded 26.10. Conclusions: Digital health efficacy relies heavily on supportive social and cognitive environments. Public health initiatives must integrate digital literacy training and peer support to optimize mHealth outcomes.

title: PERAN KEPALA SEKOLAH DALAM MENDUKUNG PROGRAM KETERAMPILAN VOKASI BERBASIS DIGITAL DI SMK IPIEMS SURABAYA
container-title: VOCATIONAL: Jurnal Inovasi Pendidikan Kejuruan
d8fdcdefc6ca24e1f489c87ceead287a5141fed7.abstract: ABSTRACT Digital-based vocational skills programs are a strategic approach to preparing vocational high school students with competencies relevant to industry needs. The success of these programs depends on school principals' ability to manage resources, guide program implementation, and promote learning innovation. This study aims to analyze the roles of the school principal as a manager, leader, and innovator in supporting a digital-based vocational skills program at SMK IPIEMS Surabaya, Indonesia. This research employed a descriptive qualitative approach, with data collected through in-depth interviews, observations, and document analysis involving the school principal, vice principal, department heads, and students. Data were analyzed through data collection, data condensation, data presentation, and conclusion drawing. Data trustworthiness was strengthened through source triangulation, technique triangulation, and member checking. The findings indicate that, as a manager, the principal conducted structured planning, resource organization, and periodic program evaluation through digital curriculum management, the provision of vocational laboratory facilities, and collaboration with external partners to facilitate student training. As a leader, the principal provided direction aligned with the school's vision and mission, established transparent communication, and demonstrated exemplary practices in using digital technology. As an innovator, the principal initiated an e-portfolio program integrated into the school's website for students in Grades X–XII to support their readiness for employment and internships. This study concludes that integrating these three leadership roles contributes to the development of a digital-based vocational learning ecosystem oriented toward work readiness and the alignment of graduates' competencies with industry needs. ABSTRAK Program keterampilan vokasi berbasis digital menjadi salah satu upaya strategis untuk mempersiapkan peserta didik sekolah menengah kejuruan agar memiliki kompetensi yang sesuai dengan kebutuhan dunia industri. Keberhasilan program tersebut tidak terlepas dari peran kepala sekolah dalam mengelola sumber daya, mengarahkan pelaksanaan program, dan mendorong inovasi pembelajaran. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis peran kepala sekolah sebagai manajer, leader, dan inovator dalam mendukung program keterampilan vokasi berbasis digital di SMK IPIEMS Surabaya. Penelitian ini menggunakan pendekatan kualitatif deskriptif dengan pengumpulan data melalui wawancara mendalam, observasi, dan studi dokumentasi yang melibatkan kepala sekolah, wakil kepala sekolah, ketua jurusan, dan peserta didik. Analisis data dilakukan melalui tahapan pengumpulan data, kondensasi data, penyajian data, dan penarikan kesimpulan. Keabsahan data diperkuat melalui triangulasi sumber, triangulasi teknik, dan member check. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa sebagai manajer, kepala sekolah melaksanakan perencanaan, pengorganisasian sumber daya, dan evaluasi program melalui pengelolaan kurikulum digital, penyediaan fasilitas laboratorium kejuruan, serta kerja sama dengan pihak eksternal untuk mendukung pelatihan peserta didik. Sebagai leader, kepala sekolah memberikan pengarahan berdasarkan visi dan misi sekolah, membangun komunikasi yang transparan, serta memberikan keteladanan dalam pemanfaatan teknologi digital. Sebagai inovator, kepala sekolah menginisiasi program unggulan e-portofolio yang terintegrasi dengan situs web sekolah bagi peserta didik kelas X–XII untuk mendukung kesiapan kerja dan magang. Penelitian ini menyimpulkan bahwa integrasi ketiga peran tersebut mendukung pengembangan ekosistem pembelajaran vokasi berbasis digital yang berorientasi pada kesiapan kerja dan relevansi kompetensi lulusan dengan kebutuhan industri.

title: Exploration of Pathways for Constructing New Liberal Arts Program Clusters in Private Higher Education Institutions from the Perspective of a Digital Rule-of-Law Education Community
container-title: 教育学文摘
e98b604409f2a0ec879aee2219c9f6f119702e27.abstract: The digital rule-of-law education community represents a collaborative talent cultivation model involving multiple stakeholders, characterized by symbiotic relationships among participants, interconnectivity of resources, and aligned objectives; it thereby provides a theoretical framework for the development of new liberal arts program clusters in private universities. In this context, the digital rule-of-law education community serves as an external educational ecosystem, while the new liberal arts program cluster functions as an internal implementation vehicle; the two exhibit a deep synergistic relationship, and their coordinated development can enable the supply side of liberal arts education to proactively adapt to the practical demands of digital governance. By advancing the construction of such program clusters, private universities can address regional shortages of digital rule-of-law professionals, overcome the challenge of homogenization among liberal arts programs, and optimize the allocation of limited educational resources. However, several shortcomings persist in current efforts: a lack of top-level strategic planning for digital rule-of-law education; disciplinary barriers that hinder interdisciplinary integration; superficial collaboration among government agencies, enterprises, universities, and research institutions; ambiguous delineation of rights and responsibilities among community participants; and the absence of well-established long-term operational mechanisms. To enhance the quality of these program clusters through the establishment of such communities, it is essential to: refine top-level strategic planning by integrating digital rule-of-law literacy throughout the entire talent cultivation process; dismantle departmental and programmatic barriers by consolidating practical resources to redesign interdisciplinary curricula, thereby facilitating program iteration and upgrading; and establish a robust community governance framework that clarifies the roles and responsibilities of all parties, thereby building a sustainable collaborative talent cultivation system. Addressing the demand for positions in grassroots digital governance, data compliance, and online legal services, private universities should integrate both internal and external educational resources, bridge the gap between classroom instruction and practical application scenarios, and develop operational models for program clusters that align with the distinctive characteristics of private institutions. This approach will cultivate application-oriented new liberal arts professionals who possess humanistic literacy, legal reasoning capabilities, and practical digital competencies, thereby contributing to local digital social governance and the growth of regional digital economies.

title: AI4Design: A Human-Centred, Cross-Domain Framework for Generative AI in Digital System Design Education
bbfe5bd6b7483207910df026656a2ed33346d1bf.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence can produce synthesizable register-transfer-level code, testbenches, and design critiques, but it can also displace the cognitive work through which students learn abstraction, timing reasoning, and verification judgement. This paper asks how such tools can be integrated into undergraduate digital system design without exchanging unassisted competence for assisted artifact fluency. We present AI4Design, a design-science framework comprising an executable tool substrate, a pedagogic orchestration layer, and an assurance and assessment layer. Six principles govern its use, including independently derived executable oracles, progressive student autonomy, visible reasoning, and scheduled unassisted assessment. A fourteen-week course illustrates the framework: AI construction support peaks mid-term and is withdrawn for the capstone, while assessment combines executable checks, process evidence, oral defence, and transfer tasks. A cross-layer analysis identifies where software, circuits and boards, chips, and mechanisms can be coupled through executable interface checks. A descriptive tentask benchmark with two open-weight local models provides a limited technical pilot. The 2B model passed 2/10 tasks at first attempt and 4/10 after one repair; the 0.8B model passed 0/10 and 1/10, respectively. Initial successes occurred only on textual tasks. These results concern artifact production, not learning or crossdomain integration. A prospective multi-cohort, mixed-methods protocol specifies how learning, trust calibration, equity, and staff cost should be evaluated. The contribution is a testable course design and evaluation infrastructure, not evidence of educational efficacy.

title: Linking Principals’ Digital Leadership to Teacher Performance through Digital Transformation Readiness: An Integrative Literature Review
container-title: Journal Of Education And Teaching Learning (JETL)
a55bf08ea298da35c96a002a0cf50b9842830824.abstract: Digital transformation has reshaped educational practices and increased the need for school leadership that can support teachers in adapting to technology-driven changes. However, existing studies tend to examine principals’ digital leadership, teacher readiness, and teacher performance separately, leaving the mechanism connecting these constructs insufficiently integrated. This study aims to synthesize existing evidence on the relationships among principals’ digital leadership, teachers’ digital transformation readiness, and teacher performance, and to develop an integrative framework explaining the potential role of readiness in linking leadership with professional performance. An integrative literature review was conducted using a predefined corpus of 12 scholarly articles published between 2022 and 2026. The articles were examined through structured evidence extraction, evidence classification, conceptual harmonization, relational synthesis, and integrative thematic synthesis. The findings show relatively consistent evidence that principals’ digital leadership is positively associated with teacher performance, while complementary evidence indicates relationships between digital leadership and digital readiness and between readiness for change and teacher performance. The synthesis further identifies teacher digital transformation readiness as a multidimensional construct encompassing capability readiness, psychological readiness, and organizationally enabled readiness. Nevertheless, none of the reviewed studies directly tested the complete pathway linking principals’ digital leadership to teacher performance through digital transformation readiness. Therefore, this review proposes digital transformation readiness as a theoretically plausible explanatory mechanism rather than an empirically confirmed mediator. The resulting leadership–readiness–performance framework highlights that effective educational digital transformation depends on the interaction between supportive digital leadership, teachers’ preparedness for change, and enabling organizational conditions.

title: Digital Assessment Literacy and Teacher Identity in Technology-Mediated Language Education
container-title: International Journal of TESOL & Education
7bb4da0afa5ba490975127886bfe3cfe0fa505fb.abstract: The demands of technology have not only altered how we teach and how we assess but have also increased the need for digital assessment literacy. Digital assessment literacy enables instructors not only to choose and design digital assessments but also to evaluate their pedagogical and ethical implications. Although previous research has examined assessment literacy, teacher identity, and agency, their relationships in technology-mediated language assessment warrant further conceptual integration. This review attempts to synthesize existing literature around digital assessment literacy, teacher identity, and technology in language teaching. Drawing on targeted literature searches and comparative conceptual synthesis, the article proposes the Digital Assessment Identity Framework, comprising digital assessment competence, critical-ethical judgment, and professional identity agency. It positions situated assessment decisions as a link between these dimensions and the enactment and negotiation of professional identity, offering a basis for further research and teacher professional development.

title: Does Graph Attention Improve Weighted-Polling Classification on the Pima Indians Diabetes Dataset? A Nested Cross-Validation Comparison with Standard Models
c29625f8030e06c21a1e1a0d59e7a488162c09d9.abstract: Abstract Background: It is not known whether a graph attention encoder improvesweighted-polling classification of small clinical tabular datasets. A GATv2weighted-polling classifier developed for agricultural morphology data was thereforetested on the Pima Indians Diabetes Dataset (768 instances, 8 features). Itsfirst evaluation scored nodes whose labels had trained the encoder. Methods: Nested stratified cross-validation (10 outer folds, 5 inner folds, threerepeats) was used, and every hyperparameter was chosen in the inner looponly: graph neighbourhood size, edge weighting, encoder width, attention heads,dropout, learning rate, weight decay, training epochs and the polling configuration.On identical outer folds, the tuned GATv2 classifier was comparedwith raw-feature weighted polling and five standard classifiers (logistic regression,RBF support vector machine, random forest, gradient boosting, k-nearestneighbours), each tuned in the same inner loop. Accuracy, macro-F1, sensitivity,specificity and area under the ROC curve (AUROC) were reported, with 95%bootstrap confidence intervals for paired differences. Results: The tuned GATv2 classifier reached 75.22% accuracy, 71.90% macro-F1, 58.58% sensitivity, 84.13% specificity and an AUROC of 0.808. Its accuracydiffered from that of raw-feature weighted polling by −0.13 points (95% CI−2.13 to +1.87) and from that of the most accurate standard model, logistic regression (76.74%), by −1.52 points (95% CI −3.47 to +0.39). Its AUROC was1.4 to 2.5 points lower than that of the other classifiers, with intervals excludingzero for four of the five standard models. The original protocol, which scorednodes used to train the encoder, had given 79.01% accuracy. Conclusions: On this dataset, tuning the encoder under nested cross-validationdid not make GATv2 weighted polling more accurate than raw-feature weightedpolling or than standard classifiers. Relative to raw-feature polling, accuracydifferences larger than about 2 points are excluded in either direction, but abenefit of up to about 1.9 points cannot be excluded. These findings are limitedto this single dataset and do not show that graph attention cannot help on otherclinical data.

title: Governing the post-consolidation mega-city: legal frameworks for digital transformation in Da Nang, Vietnam
container-title: The University of Danang - Journal of Science and Technology
22123dbb97dfbc3979e0c8c991c348ed4907c356.abstract: This study evaluates the legal framework for digital transformation in local governance in Da Nang, Vietnam, following its administrative consolidation. Through the analysis of secondary documents and in-depth interviews across five stakeholder groups, the paper asserts that despite a successful transition toward an "enabling development" paradigm-driving the digital economy to account for 24% of the GRDP (in 2024)-the system remains constrained by five core bottlenecks. These include vertical regulatory misalignment, data siloing, rigid public finance, the absence of digital personnel standards, and the digital divide across regions. The study proposes a comprehensive matrix of solutions toward 2035, emphasizing regulatory sandboxes and public service co-production, while concurrently integrating green transformational leadership into grassroots administrative capacities. This research provides empirical implications for refining digital transformation laws within polycentric urban governance in emerging economies undergoing institutional transitions.

title: ENSINO DE LÍNGUA PORTUGUESA E CULTURA DIGITAL: EXPLORANDO NOVAS PRÁTICAS EDUCATIVAS COM TECNOLOGIAS
container-title: Revista Tópicos
7c9593c9452f6d8ea5b4b7a7f0d2d976666b571b.abstract: Neste estudo, mergulhamos na integração das tecnologias digitais na educação, especialmente no ensino de Língua Portuguesa, à luz da cultura digital e das novas abordagens teóricas e metodológicas que ela traz consigo a partir de uma revisão bibliográfica. Nosso objetivo é estimular uma reflexão crítica sobre como utilizamos as tecnologias, seja para consumir, circular ou produzir conteúdo, visando a formação cidadã dos alunos. Investigamos a cultura digital, suas definições e características, levando em conta as mudanças culturais contemporâneas impulsionadas pela revolução tecnológica e o papel fundamental da cultura nesse cenário. Destacamos também a compreensão da Leitura: Mídia, Texto e Leitor como recursos essenciais para compreender a conexão entre a Cultura Digital e o ensino de Língua Portuguesa. Autores como Hall, Heinsfeld, Pischetola, Bortolazzo, Lévy, Arruda, Lemos, entre outros, contribuem como referência teórica. Concluímos que a adaptação da escola à cultura digital requer mudanças profundas nos modelos educacionais existentes, indo além da simples introdução de dispositivos digitais na prática pedagógica.

title: LEVERAGING ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE TO PROMOTE SELF-LEARNING IN THE DIGITAL ENVIRONMENT –  A STUDY AT THE FACULTY OF ENGLISH,  HANOI OPEN UNIVERSITY
container-title: Tạp chí Khoa học Trường Đại học Mở Hà Nội
cad4c29bd89821abb38e9c579bd58d359648bd89.abstract: This study investigates the impact of Artificial Intelligence (AI) on Self-Regulated Learning (SRL) among first-year English majors at Hanoi Open University. Using a mixed-methods approach, the research explores how Generative AI tools—such as ChatGPT and Bing Chat—serve as pedagogical "launchpads" rather than intellectual "crutches". Key findings show that AI feedback significantly strengthens the SRL cycle by helping learners decompose goals and providing immediate, non-judgmental diagnostic support. Notably, learners demonstrate high levels of "Technological Self-efficacy" and actively cross-verify AI outputs to mitigate the risk of "hallucinations." The study concludes that AI promotes independent thinking and adaptive help-seeking when positioned as a "debating partner." These results offer vital insights for higher education transitions, suggesting that AI-integrated frameworks can optimize self-learning capacity and cultivate the critical evaluation skills necessary for the Education 4.0 era.

title: Common-cause failures in GNSS time synchronization for digital substations: terrestrial and spaceborne threats and temporal resilience measures
container-title: Journal of Electrical Systems and Information Technology
157089e04042458805710d16e67ad9222ddbdc7a.abstract: Abstract Certain digital-substation applications require precise, traceable and continuously available time, especially synchronized sampled values (SV), synchrophasors, disturbance records, sequence-of-events (SOE) logs and functions that compare measurements from different sources or terminals. This paper treats GNSS dependence as a common-cause failure (CCF): redundant receivers, antennas and networks do not provide functional independence when they share satellite signals, the radio-frequency environment, the ionosphere or external PNT infrastructure. The work is a structured engineering framework supported by a directed technical review, analytical sensitivity modelling and independent analysis of public hardware-laboratory SV/PTP captures under GNSS spoofing (KIT, 2026); the jamming results used here are those stated on the authors’ poster. It (i) gives a semi-quantitative taxonomy that separates existence, probability class, geographic scope, mechanism, consequence and mitigation; (ii) maps time degradation from GNSS through PTP, merging units, SV and IEDs, comparing two master clocks and two merging units from different manufacturers; (iii) extends the holdover model to non-constant drift and temperature, and distinguishes absolute from relative timing error; (iv) extends line-differential sensitivity to unequal magnitudes, independent per-terminal errors, channel asymmetry, CT error, percentage restraint and SmpSynch blocking; and (v) shows that a 10 ms asynchronous spoofing step held the stepping merging-unit pair near $$180^{\circ}$$ for 42 s and kept the slewing unit off its baseline for about 105 s (peak $$180^{\circ}$$ , not held for that whole window), and that a correct best-master-clock failover to a redundant grandmaster 10 ms away produced 12 s near $$180^{\circ}$$ on one pair in each of two windows and 75 s off baseline on the others, then a common 10 ms error for about 14 min during which only the active grandmaster kept healthy PTP attributes and, for the last 11 min, all three merging units published SmpSynch = 2. Temporal-dependence levels DT-0 to DT-4 are given numerical requirements and a validation table. The results support functional diversity, specified holdover and free-running limits, time-quality monitoring, documented degraded modes and targeted commissioning tests.

title: THE IMPACT OF GLOBAL YOUTH MOVEMENTS ON INDIAN YOUTH (2020–OCTOBER 2026) A Sociological Study of Political Consciousness, Digital Activism and Social Change
container-title: Journal of Socio-Educational & Cultural Research
a4d6db9712f60aa34acfe320632b4eca8477ebce.abstract: A new wave of youth movements has emerged globally in the third decade of the twenty-first century. Between 2020 and October 2026, young people in various countries staged large-scale protests against corruption, unemployment, inflation, weaknesses in education systems, the crisis of political representation, social inequality, human-rights violations and restrictions on freedom of expression. A distinctive feature of these movements has been the important role played not only by traditional organisations but also by social media, digital networks, online campaigns and decentralised leadership. Youth activism in Myanmar, Thailand, the United States, Nigeria, Sri Lanka, Iran, Bangladesh, Kenya, Indonesia, Nepal, Serbia, Morocco, Madagascar, the Philippines and European countries such as France, Italy and Spain has influenced political and social debates. By October 2026, the movements emerging in Europe had foregrounded the quality of education, the housing crisis, the rising cost of living, employment insecurity and the condition of public services. This research article presents a sociological study of the possible effects of global youth movements on Indian youth by analysing their nature, causes, forms and consequences. It uses the theories of relative deprivation, resource mobilisation and new social movements, along with the concept of the network society. The study concludes that global youth movements can encourage political awareness, sensitivity towards civil rights, digital participation and aspirations for social change among young people. However, the success of a movement is not confined to protests; it also requires democratic institutions, policy reforms and sustained social participation

title: <b>Beyond Digital Participation: Monitoring and Feedback in WhatsApp-Based Arabic Language Practice </b>
container-title: International Journal of Arabic Language Teaching
cf857605d49dc2590dbf2e66b26c7478a7e182e7.abstract: Digital participation does not by itself establish the quality of Arabic language practice. This qualitative case study examines how digital monitoring and feedback support vacation-period Arabic video assignments at Raudlah al-Lughah al-‘Arabiyah (RLA) Annuqayah, East Java, with particular attention to WhatsApp. Data was collected through interviews with twelve informants (the RLA head, five administrators, and six members) together with observation and documentation. Analysis involved data condensation, data display, and conclusion drawing and verification, meanwhile source and technique triangulation supported data credibility. The findings identify a connected workflow of assignment completion checks, documentation of WhatsApp Story views, video review, feedback, and recognition of members’ work. Within this workflow, submission records document participation, viewer counts document content reach, and video review provides a basis for feedback on language performance. The study provides a contextual account of digital monitoring and feedback in pesantren-based Arabic language practice rather than evidence of measured proficiency gains. Future research could develop explicit video-evaluation benchmarks and examine changes in speaking performance over time.

title: Digital drivers of circularity: examining the mediating role of big data analytics capabilities in the blockchain-circular economy nexus
container-title: Future Business Journal
b8a1cd1330ef2aae03deffa2d7e8fcd7c1ad152a.abstract: Abstract The rapid growth of electric vehicles has intensified concerns regarding the sustainable management of battery materials, creating an urgent need for effective circular economy implementation within EV batteries. Although blockchain technology has been widely recognized for improving transparency, traceability, and information sharing, limited research explains how blockchain technology enabled information is transformed into circular economy implementation. The mediating role of big data analytics capabilities remains underexplored, and empirical evidence from the EV battery manufacturing sector is scarce. To address this gap, this study integrates the technology–organization–environment framework and dynamic capability theory to examine the relationships among BCT, BDAC, and CEI. Using a quantitative research design, data were collected from 420 production managers employed in China’s EV battery manufacturing industry and analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM). The findings indicate that blockchain technology establishes a reliable technological foundation for circular initiatives, while BDAC plays a pivotal role in transforming digital information into effective circular economy implementation. The results further reveal that the contribution of blockchain to CEI is substantially strengthened through the development of analytical capabilities. By integrating TOE and DCT, this study extends existing knowledge on digital sustainability and demonstrates that technological investments alone are insufficient to achieve circular outcomes without the organizational capabilities required to leverage them effectively. The study offers important theoretical insights for digital transformation research and practical guidance for managers seeking to enhance resource efficiency and sustainability performance in EV battery manufacturing.

title: From Posts to Trust: How User-Generated Content and Digital Literacy Shape Consumer Decisions
container-title: Jurnal Aplikasi Manajemen
e1b6f19e96a676efd6301164ef0d2d866c9ab83f.abstract: The growth of social media as a marketing information source encourages Generation Z to utilize User-Generated Content (UGC) in making digital investment decisions. However, rising misinformation and investment fraud require a deeper understanding of how UGC influences trust and investment intentions. Using perceived usefulness as a mediating variable and digital literacy as a moderating variable among Indonesian Generation Z TikTok users, this study examines the impact of user-generated content (UGC) on customer trust and purchase intention. A total of 220 people completed an online survey as part of an explanatory quantitative approach, and the study used PLS-SEM to analyze the results. The findings demonstrate that customer trust, purchase intention, and perceived usefulness are all significantly improved by UGC. Additionally, the results show that Perceived Usefulness partially mediates the interaction between UGC and both variables and positively affects Customer Trust and Purchase Intention. In addition, Digital Literacy positively affects Customer Trust and Purchase Intention. However, Digital literacy has been shown to increase the impact of user-generated content (UGC) on purchase intention, but it does not attenuate the relationship between UGC and customer trust. These results highlight that information quality and utility contained in UGC are key mechanisms shaping trust and investment intentions, while digital literacy plays an important role only at the purchase decision stage. This study offers strategic implications for digital investment platforms and marketers to optimize credible UGC and enhance digital literacy among younger generations, encouraging safer, more rational investment decisions.

title: Evidence and measures of the digital usage divide from 40 million Windows devices
container-title: Nature Communications
ec4a894bc7cd410b2763991ee05821d76ae8023e.abstract: Abstract Digital infrastructure is crucial for economic opportunities, social inclusion, and civic participation, but benefits remain unevenly distributed. Existing measures, such as computer ownership and broadband adoption, do not capture the depth and variety of digital use. We develop measures using Microsoft telemetry collected during operating system updates from 40 million Windows devices in U.S. households. These measures provide greater coverage and granularity than existing commercial or government surveys. Device representations at the ZIP-code level reveal substantial variation in usage, including an urban-rural divide and disparities within narrowly defined Metropolitan Statistical Areas. Income and education correlate with these differences. These effects are large and suggest that digital usage gaps extend beyond the local availability of essential IT infrastructure. The findings call for interventions that complement infrastructure access with support for technology use and skills development. The resulting indices are publicly available to support future research on digital inequality.

title: Pelatihan Dokumentasi Pengetahuan Lokal untuk Mitigasi Banjir Berbasis Digital  di Kampung Tanjung Mancang
container-title: ASPIRASI : Publikasi Hasil Pengabdian dan Kegiatan Masyarakat
192cf0b47d5eee8b1575a0dd0636a2d8d3e1eaa9.abstract: The November 2025 flash flood severely damaged housing and infrastructure and claimed lives in Aceh Tamiang. This issue was exacerbated by the lack of adequate mitigation information available to the public. Such mitigation efforts are crucial for preventive measures, emergency response navigation, and post-disaster relief coordination. This community service aims to enhance local capacity in digitally documenting indigenous knowledge for disaster mitigation based on community experiences through documentation training. The methods employed were Focus Group Discussion (FGD) and documentation methods. The FGD method was used to gather field data and activity feedback, while the documentation method implemented digital technology transfer to enable target staff in Tanjung Mancang Village to collect and manage documented data. The results demonstrated an increase in community understanding of identifying local knowledge for flood mitigation, alongside improved skills in utilizing digital documentation tools. In conclusion, this training effectively enhances public awareness and capacity for flood mitigation, serving as a sustainable strategy for future disaster preparedness.

title: TPACK Readiness, Innovative Learning Design, and Digital Entrepreneurship Skills among Indonesian Business Education Students
container-title: Inkubis : Jurnal Ekonomi dan Bisnis
28bd587667a3b530994de31294f249e3e4a255d0.abstract: Background: Digital entrepreneurship skills are increasingly important for business graduates, but evidence remains limited on how technology-integrated pedagogy is associated with their development. Objective: This study examined the structural associations among TPACK readiness, Innovative Learning Design, and the latent construct Digital Entrepreneurship Skills, including whether Innovative Learning Design carried a significant indirect association. Methods: A cross-sectional survey was analyzed using covariance-based structural equation modeling. Of 119 responses, two cases met the prespecified extreme-score rule and were excluded, producing an analytic sample of 117 students. Nineteen dimension-level indicators represented the three constructs. Results: The retained measurement model produced standardized loadings of 0.459-0.812 and composite reliability of 0.738-0.863. Model fit improved after two theoretically justified within-construct residual correlations but remained below conventional benchmarks: chi-square (114) = 308.66, p < 0.001; CFI = 0.808; TLI = 0.771; and RMSEA = 0.121. The three direct paths were significant: TPACK-Innovative Learning Design (beta = 0.861, p < 0.001), Innovative Learning Design-Digital Entrepreneurship Skills (beta = 0.451, p = 0.044), and TPACK-Digital Entrepreneurship Skills (beta = 0.464, p = 0.048). The indirect effect was not significant (beta = 0.388, p = 0.063). Conclusion: The findings support significant cross-sectional associations among the constructs but do not support the proposed mediation hypothesis. Interpretation should remain cautious because of suboptimal model fit, the single-institution sample, and the cross-sectional, self-report design.

title: Modern Mythos — Digital Twins
container-title: Proceeding Bali-Bhuwana Waskita: Global Art Creativity Conference
3e0636787110e6de8c05b1bc9ebe48b72e34874a.abstract: This article explores the concept of “Modern Mythos” through the creation of Digital Twins in the form of looped motion works developed during a collaborative workshop with students and collaborators at ISI Denpasar. This project engages with the lineage of traditional Balinese masks, including Topèng and Barong-Rangda, as a means of transforming cultural heritage to adapt to today’s digital imagery culture. This approach emphasizes the importance of carefully transferring the works, applying the CARE principles, TK Labels, and AI watermarks to ensure that custodianship and cultural context are preserved. Furthermore, this practice integrates the process of returning the works to local creators and master woodcarvers, such as Ida Bagus Anom Suryawa, so that decisions regarding form, proportions, motifs, and taboos remain determined through the assessment of handcrafted artistry and community review. By positioning local communities as the primary guides—rather than relying on artificial intelligence (AI)—Digital Twins are presented as a circular proposal to reinterpret myths in contemporary forms and ensure the continued vitality of cultural heritage.

title: Folklore as Collective Moral Memory: Reactualizing Ethical and Moral Values in the Digital Era
container-title: Proceeding Bali-Bhuwana Waskita: Global Art Creativity Conference
0f0e5d94ce20e1f6ef0e2772bd6f72c696367123.abstract: This study examines folklore as collective moral memory and explores the reactualization of ethical and moral values in the digital era. Although folklore, collective memory, and digital culture have been widely studied, their interrelationships in sustaining moral values require further conceptual integration. This study employs a qualitative-descriptive method using folkloristic, interpretive, collective memory, and digital culture approaches. Data are collected through observation, in-depth interviews, documentation, and literature review, and analyzed through data reduction, data presentation, and conclusion verification. The study conceptualizes folklore as a cultural medium that preserves collective experiences, transmits ethical values across generations, and enables their reinterpretation within contemporary contexts. Digital platforms expand access to folklore but may also simplify narratives, detach stories from their cultural contexts, and alter their moral meanings. Reactualization is therefore essential to connect traditional values, including honesty, responsibility, solidarity, respect for others, and environmental awareness, with contemporary social challenges. This study contributes a conceptual framework for understanding folklore as living moral memory and supporting culturally sensitive, ethically relevant cultural transmission.

title: Assessing digital health inequalities in Indonesia: an extended SEM–ANN model of socioeconomic status, mHealth usage, perceived access to healthcare services, and sustained physical activity
container-title: Frontiers in Public Health
de37038a71cc844f465af17b92a4a76472aadc98.abstract: Background Enhanced access to health services and lowered health inequalities can possibly be associated with the usage of digital technologies. Unfortunately, differences in socioeconomic status (SES) and technological skill could be associated with disparities in their usage. Indonesia remains a nation with rural–urban disparity. Hence, to create strategies for equitable health service, it is crucial to comprehend the extent to which mobile health usage (MHL) and SES are associated with perceived sustained physical activity (PPA) and access to healthcare. Purposes This research extended the 2026 Sumarliah et al.’s framework by incorporating perceived access to healthcare services (PAHS) into the model and assessing its association with MHL, PPA, and SES among a broader sample of Indonesian rural–urban respondents. To deliver predictive and explanatory evaluations, it further integrated artificial neural network (ANN) and structural equation modeling (SEM) assessments. Methods This research adopted a stratified regional sampling to support representation of six major Indonesian regions: Papua-Maluku, Nusa Tenggara-Bali, Sumatra, Java, Sulawesi, and Kalimantan. A sum of 1,566 valid responses (78.3%) were retained, which comprised 871 urban (55.6%) and 695 rural (44.4%) respondents. To evaluate the gathered data, a three-stage quantitative approach was utilized, which involved SEM, multi-group SEM and ANN examinations. Results There was a positive association between PAHS and SES, as well as between MHL and SES. The PAHS was also positively linked to MHL. Conversely, PAHS was not significantly associated with PPA. As such, the indirect link between MHL and PPA via PAHS was insignificant. Multi-group SEM verified the much stronger positive correlations among PAHS, MHL, and SES within urban samples instead of rural samples. Supportive evidence to predict PPA was acquired through ANN exploration, where maximum normalized predictive importance was achieved by the MHL input construct. Conclusion From the present research it is evident that PAHS had statistically insignificant association with PPA, which is different from earlier works’ findings. The likely reason is that although PAHS can be associated with the usage of health services, it may be inadequate to account for differences in respondents’ PPA.

title: Effects of contrast water therapy on fatigue recovery in athletes: systematic review and three-level meta-analysis
container-title: Frontiers in Physiology
8eb78614b5b4c801e911d1743ee39183480888dc.abstract: Background High-intensity training and competition often lead to severe fatigue in athletes, making effective recovery interventions essential. This three-level meta-analyses aimed to systematically evaluate contrast water therapy (CWT) and passive recovery (PAS), and explore which intervention is more effective for fatigue recovery. Methods Following PRISMA guidelines, a systematic search was conducted in PubMed, Web of Science, Cochrane Library, Embase, and Scopus on August 23, 2026. Pooled effect sizes were estimated using a three-level random-effects meta-analysis, and a variance–covariance matrix was constructed by specifying the correlation between effect sizes within the same study (ρ = 0.5) to account for the dependence arising from multiple outcomes and multiple time points within a study. Accordingly, three-level models were further fitted separately for the three outcomes: VAS 0–10, CK, and Borg 1–10. Risk of bias was assessed using the Risk of Bias 2.0 tool, and the certainty of evidence was evaluated using the GRADE framework. Results A total of 10 studies involving 199 athletes (age: 15.5 ± 1.0 to 26.2 ± 5.8) were included. Both variance components of the three-level model were supported (between-study σ² 3 = 0.553; within-study σ² 2 = 0.154; likelihood ratio test P &lt; 0.0001). Contrast water therapy significantly reduced perceived exertion (Borg 1–10: 5 studies, 10 effect sizes; Hedges’ g = −1.009, 95% CI: −1.672 to −0.346; P = 0.007; I ² = 70.41%; low certainty) but had no statistically significant effect on muscle soreness (VAS 0–10: 5 studies, 12 effect sizes; g = −0.439, 95% CI: −1.619 to 0.741; P = 0.431; I ² = 93.85%; very low certainty) or on CK (3 studies, 6 effect sizes; g = −0.257, 95% CI: −0.614 to 0.100; P = 0.123; I ² = 0%; low certainty). Conclusion Contrast water therapy may improve perceived recovery, specifically perceived exertion. Although the primary analysis suggests a possible benefit of CWT on perceived exertion, the available evidence remains insufficient to draw strong conclusions about the reliability or practical magnitude of this effect. For perceived muscle soreness and circulating CK, no statistically significant effect was detected, but given the limited evidence, these findings do not permit a conclusion of equivalence with passive recovery. Systematic review registration https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/login , identifier CRD420251075430.

title: How child-reported family digital rules relate to executive function gains in preschoolers: gendered patterns
container-title: Frontiers in Psychology
9ca7ef5f28585e64fd5a801ada1f7d9f9f119817.abstract: The near-universal digital engagement of preschoolers necessitates a nuanced understanding of how family practices shape its cognitive impact. Moving beyond simplistic measures of screen time, this longitudinal study investigated the association between child-reported family digital rules and the development of executive functions over 1 year in kindergarten. A sample of 1,512 children ( M = 5.7 years) was assessed at Time 1, with 1,339 children ( M = 6.6 years) retained at Time 2 1 year later. Children reported on family rules regarding digital device use (time limits, content restrictions, and conditional use rules), while parents reported total screen time. Using regression models predicting later executive function scores while controlling for earlier scores, we found a negative association between content restrictions and cognitive flexibility gains in girls, but not in boys. Conditional use rules showed a trend toward a positive association with inhibitory control gains in girls, and time limits showed no significant association with any executive function component. No rule-related effects emerged for boys. These findings suggest that it may be valuable to consider not only the presence or absence of parental mediation, but also its specific form – the particular types of restrictions and rules that parents apply. Certain rules may be potentially more effective than others, and their effectiveness may also differ between boys and girls.

title: Digitally transformed academic work and wellbeing: developing the Digital Academic Work Reconfiguration and Wellbeing Framework
container-title: Frontiers in Sociology
d93c97fc78072463daf2ea56573c74d7fd043205.abstract: Digital transformation is reshaping academic work through remote and hybrid arrangements, intensified digital connectivity and the expanding use of artificial intelligence (AI). These developments can support flexibility, autonomy and efficiency, but may also intensify workload, erode work–life boundaries and generate demands associated with continuous adaptation, academic integrity and professional responsibility. Existing evidence is fragmented across technostress, remote and hybrid work, digital readiness and AI-enabled academic work, leaving insufficiently explained how technological change becomes embedded in the organisation and experience of academic work and, through this process, relates to wellbeing. This conceptual paper addresses this gap by developing the Digital Academic Work Reconfiguration and Wellbeing (DAWR-W) Framework. The framework was developed through theory synthesis informed by a structured literature foundation of 40 empirical studies and complementary theoretical research. The synthesis distinguishes the characteristics through which digital transformation reconfigures the organisation, boundaries, demands, relationships and professional content of academic work from the psychosocial mechanisms through which academics experience these changes. The resulting framework identifies seven characteristics of digitally transformed academic work and six psychosocial mechanisms involving resource depletion and replenishment, recovery and psychological detachment, perceived control and autonomy, competence and adaptive capacity, relational connection and psychological safety, and professional meaning and identity. Organisational and institutional conditions shape how digital transformation becomes embedded in academic work, while boundary conditions and feedback processes recognise contextual variation and adaptation over time. The central contribution of the DAWR-W Framework is to position work reconfiguration, rather than technology exposure alone, as the occupational process connecting digital transformation with academic employee wellbeing. In doing so, the framework integrates previously fragmented digital-work phenomena within a common explanatory architecture and locates responsibility for sustainable digital academic work across both individual and institutional levels. It provides an occupation-specific foundation for empirical testing, work-design interventions, and digital and AI governance in higher education.

title: The digital paradox of the silver economy: not all digital consumption is equal
container-title: Frontiers in Human Dynamics
b164379f19b3d6f8ca64fe39d4780c5f59aaa6f3.abstract: Introduction Population ageing and rapid digital transformation are increasing older adults' participation in e-commerce, yet the relationship between their online consumption patterns and national-level economic conditions remains insufficiently understood. This study examines the associations between different categories of online consumption among individuals aged 55–74 and national-level economic conditions across 24 European Union countries and explores how these associations vary across different temporal specifications. Methods Using panel data for 2013–2024, the study analyses e-commerce sector revenue, net national income per capita (NNI), and gross national income per capita (GNI) using descriptive statistics, multiple regression, fixed-effects regression, and time-lag analysis. Results The results reveal substantial heterogeneity across online consumption categories. Positive associations with national-level economic conditions are observed for travel and accommodation services, periodicals, pharmaceuticals, and electronics, whereas clothing, food products, ICT services, and event tickets exhibit comparatively stronger negative associations. Notable associations are also observed in the one-year lag specification, indicating that the estimated relationships between online consumption patterns among individuals aged 55–74 and national-level economic conditions vary across temporal specifications. Discussion The findings provide empirical evidence consistent with the proposed Digital Paradox of the Silver Economy, suggesting that the economic implications of digital participation depend on the composition of online consumption rather than its overall level. The study advances a conceptual framework for understanding the heterogeneous economic outcomes of digital participation in ageing societies and highlights the importance of distinguishing among different forms of online consumption in research and policy on the silver economy.

title: Restorative Interiors for the Digital Age: A Literature Review on Interior Design Strategies for Digital Fatigue
container-title: Proceeding Bali-Bhuwana Waskita: Global Art Creativity Conference
8395a8bb4562dff259484e2740ac1a1ab501a05b.abstract: The rapid development of digital technology has intensified human interaction with screen-based devices. The demand to remain continuously connected to digital devices across everyday activities has contributed to the emergence of digital fatigue, characterized by mental exhaustion, reduced attention, boredom, and stress. This condition highlights the need to consider the role of the physical environment in supporting recovery processes, particularly the interior environments in which people carry out their activities. This study aims to identify restorative needs associated with digital fatigue and to examine how restorative environmental characteristics can be translated into interior design strategies. A Systematic Literature Review (SLR) was conducted, with the literature selection process guided by PRISMA. A total of 21 articles were analyzed and grouped into three areas: digital fatigue, restorative environments, and interior design. Attention Restoration Theory (ART) was used as the primary framework for understanding attention restoration, while Stress Reduction Theory (SRT) was used to examine stress recovery. The findings indicate that restorative needs associated with digital fatigue primarily concern attention restoration and stress reduction. Environmental characteristics such as being away, fascination, extent, compatibility, connection with nature, and visual and sensory environmental quality are relevant to restorative processes. In interior design, these characteristics can be translated through spatial configuration, lighting, color, materials, visual and sensory quality, and connections with natural elements. These findings provide the basis for a conceptual framework for restorative interiors and for the development of interior environments that may support attention restoration, stress reduction, and user well-being.

title: Female Visual Identity in Bali Tourism Digital Magazine Advertisement
container-title: Proceeding Bali-Bhuwana Waskita: Global Art Creativity Conference
4d3584396d196a883129b6507b90c100c2c6d8fc.abstract: This study examines the phenomenon of illusionation in digital tourism advertising that places Balinese women's bodies as the main subject matter. The massive development of the digital promotion industry has shifted the visual paradigm from authentic local representation to global beauty construction for market satisfaction. The main objective of this study is to identify the anatomy of the visual style of tourism digital magazine advertising in presenting Balinese women as subject matter, as well as to analyze the manifestation of aesthetic promise in the commodification of visual models. The research method used is qualitative with a descriptive-analytical approach under the umbrella of Art Studies. The analytical knife used integrates Wolfgang Fritz Haug's Commodity Aesthetic Theory, Roland Barthes' Semiotics, and Jacques Derrida's Deconstruction Aesthetics, which are deepened through the lens of Visual Communication Design. The results of the study show that identity deconstruction is carried out through a structured commodity aesthetic mechanism, i.e. when the physical figures of local women are manipulated through digital image engineering techniques (digital imaging) in order to approach Western beauty standards (westernization). This phenomenon creates a visual simulacra that positions non-local figures as the main representation of Bali, while authentic identities are eliminated and marginalized.

title: KNOWLEDGE MANAGEMENT ENABLERS, KNOWLEDGE SHARING DAN KINERJA ORGANISASI: PIMPINAN DAERAH MUHAMMADIYAH DAN 'AISYIYAH DI KOTA DAN KABUPATEN PEKALONGAN

5f37e8d6423c28f2088bc7bcb0d7dc5a9dbaf520.abstract: This study aims to analyze the influence of leadership and organizational culture on organizational performance, as well as to examine the mediating role of knowledge sharing within the Muhammadiyah and ’Aisyiyah Regional Boards in Pekalongan City and Regency. A quantitative approach was employed using a survey method involving respondents who are active board members or organizational members. Data analysis was conducted using Structural Equation Modeling based on Partial Least Squares (PLS-SEM). The results show that leadership and organizational culture do not have a significant direct effect on organizational performance, while knowledge sharing has a positive and significant effect on organizational performance. Furthermore, knowledge sharing is proven to significantly mediate the relationship between leadership and organizational performance, as well as between organizational culture and organizational performance. These findings emphasize that leadership and culture will have an optimal impact when directed toward creating an environment that supports knowledge exchange. The practical implication of this study is the importance of strengthening knowledge-sharing mechanisms through the development of collaborative leadership, the establishment of an open organizational culture, and the implementation of effective knowledge management systems to improve the performance of socio-religious organizations.

title: Az EU AI Act hazai implementációja: Jogi, kormányzási és biztonsági kockázatok a mesterséges intelligencia megfelelésében
container-title: Scientia et Securitas
7fe3847c42df249157d34987b8a2c46c0afe439a.abstract: A tanulmány azt vizsgálja, miként illeszkedik az Európai Unió mesterséges intelligenciáról szóló rendelete (EU 2024/1689 – AI Act) és annak hazai végrehajtása, a 2025. évi LXXV. törvény a magyar jogi és intézményi környezetbe. A kutatás különös figyelmet fordít a kockázatalapú szabályozás logikájára, a trustworthy AI elvének érvényesülésére, valamint a human-in-the-loop követelmény gyakorlati megvalósítására. A vizsgálat kvalitatív jogelemzési és szabályozás-összehasonlító módszereket alkalmazott. Eredményei szerint Magyarország jelentős előrelépést tett a hatósági és infrastrukturális végrehajtás terén, azonban a szervezeti kultúra és az etikai érettség fejlettsége még nem éri el a kívánatos szintet. Ez a hiányosság biztonságpolitikai kockázatokat is hordoz, különösen a kritikus infrastruktúrák és a közszolgáltatások területén. A tanulmány javaslatokat fogalmaz meg az etikai irányelvek fejlesztésére, a szervezeti integritás erősítésére és az MI-compliance rendszerek mélyebb beágyazására a hazai kormányzási gyakorlatba.

title: Compliance-by-Design in an AI-Enabled Platform for Early Crohn Disease Interception: A Viewpoint
container-title: Journal of Medical Internet Research
3ce9f5c02f3d112fa70bf8dcc4742bd057e94e20.abstract: Abstract AI-enabled digital medicine platforms in Europe are developed within overlapping rules for personal data, medical devices, AI, clinical research, health data access, and health technology assessment. This viewpoint represents the authors’ experience and interpretation from the preimplementation phase of INTERCEPT, an Innovative Health Initiative consortium that plans to validate biomarkers and develop a blood-based risk score for early Crohn disease interception. It does not report original empirical research, a systematic regulatory review, a deployed platform, or a validated AI model. Our aim is to explain how compliance-by-design can be translated into an auditable governance architecture and to identify what still requires scientific evaluation. We advance 3 messages. First, governance must begin with intended purpose and boundary mapping: a digital platform may contain research, operational, and medical device software functions, and conformity of one module cannot be inferred for the platform as a whole. Second, overlapping obligations can be operationalized through 5 linked controls: modular responsibility and change control, federated data governance, traceable AI life cycle management, consent and participant rights orchestration, and a common cross-border governance core with local adaptations. Third, compliance is not a surrogate for model validity, clinical benefit, trust, scalability, or market access. Before clinical deployment, planned AI components require prespecified labels and cohorts, leakage prevention, missing data and imbalance strategies, calibration, subgroup assessment, external validation, human factors evaluation, and postdeployment algorithmovigilance. A hypothetical biomarker risk score update illustrates how the 5 controls interact. INTERCEPT is informative because it combines cross-border biomarker research, planned predictive analytics, and heterogeneous institutional settings while key design decisions remain modifiable. Its contribution is nevertheless conceptual: the proposed framework is a testable governance hypothesis, not evidence of implementation success. Prospective studies should compare it with alternative governance models and assess safety, workload, participant experience, evidence generation, and regulatory performance.

title: Existential Alignment Theory: An ontological Framework Highlighting How Purpose and Authenticity Impact Organizational Life
container-title: IIARD INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF ECONOMICS AND BUSINESS MANAGEMENT
5a319df73cb83a7ad9c88e7f90846ffe574fb04d.abstract: Existential Alignment theory (EAT) is grounded in existential ontology, which examines the nature of human and organizational existence, being, purpose and authenticity and provides the philosophical foundation for understanding how individuals align their existential identity, values and purpose with organizational goals to achieve meaningful and authentic personal and organizational life. Contemporary organizations also face a growing crisis of meaning. Employees increasingly report disengagement, purposelessness, and a profound sense of alienation between their personal values and the institutional demands of organizational life. Existing organizational and management theories address performance, structure, motivation, and leadership but have largely failed to provide a philosophically grounded account of how individual purpose and organizational existence can converge to produce genuine, transformative impact. This study introduces Existential Alignment Theory (EAT), a virgin theoretical framework that draws on existentialist philosophy particularly the work of Sartre (1946), Camus (1942), and Heidegger (1927) to argue that organizations thrive when individual existential purpose aligns with collective institutional goals, enabling authentic impact rather than mere functional output. Existential Alignment Theory (EAT) proposes five core propositions: (1) individuals seek existential authenticity in their work; (2) organizations function as vessels for shared existential projects; (3) convergence of individual and organizational purpose liberates employees to create authentic impact; (4) acknowledging organizational absurdities fosters resilience and creative engagement; and (5) existential alignment defines authentic organizational success. The theory further identifies three leadership imperatives: creating intersectional spaces of purpose, adopting existentially resonant leadership styles, and measuring success through authentic impact. The article delineates the theory's philosophical underpinnings, core propositions, and practical implications while positioning Existential Alignment Theory (EAT) in dialogue with existing scholarship on meaningful work, authentic leadership, and organizational purpose.

title: Bias in Medical AI in Relation to Patient Empowerment and Digital Equity: Scoping Review
container-title: Online Journal of Public Health Informatics
21638a3b1d97502c2cea89d6c9b782a4ab8dc386.abstract: Abstract Background AI is increasingly embedded in health care and digital health applications, shaping clinical processes as well as how patients access information and participate in care. Research on bias in medical AI has largely focused on technical and performance-related disparities. Less attention has been paid to how such biases may affect patients’ access, understanding, trust, and opportunities for meaningful involvement in care. Objective This scoping review aimed to map how studies of bias in medical AI describe patient-related consequences relevant to patient empowerment and the digital divide and to identify gaps across technical, social, structural, and patient-centered perspectives. Methods This scoping review followed JBI (Joanna Briggs Institute) methodology and PRISMA-ScR (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews) reporting guidance. PubMed/MEDLINE and EBSCOHost databases were searched in August 2025 and supplemented by Google Scholar searches. Peer-reviewed studies published from 2015 onward were included if they addressed bias in medical AI and described patient-related consequences relevant to patient empowerment or digital inequality. Data charting focused on AI application types, bias dimensions, patient empowerment domains, digital divide–related factors, intersectionality, and debiasing strategies. Findings were synthesized descriptively and thematically. Results The search identified 497 records, of which 22 studies met the inclusion criteria. Bias was represented as a multidimensional sociotechnical phenomenon, with social bias identified most frequently (21/22 studies), followed by algorithmic bias (16/22 studies), structural bias (14/22 studies), and design-related bias (12/22 studies). Patient empowerment was most frequently addressed through involvement in care (n=13), followed by health literacy (n=9) and trust and assurance (n=7), whereas broader psychosocial and everyday-life domains were addressed less frequently. Digital divide–related factors were identified in 19 of the 22 studies, with digital literacy and usability barriers reported most frequently. Seven studies considered 2 or more social or structural dimensions of disadvantage. Although many studies discussed approaches that could mitigate bias-related barriers, explicit empirical evaluation of debiasing strategies in relation to patient empowerment or digital equity was largely absent. Conclusions Patient-related consequences of bias in medical AI extend beyond algorithmic performance and are reflected in access, understanding, trust, and involvement in care. Broader empowerment dimensions, multidimensional disadvantage, and empirically evaluated mitigation strategies remain comparatively underexplored.
