title: Detecting Emotional Signals of Relationship Well-Being Using AI: A Cross-Sectional Comparison of Transformer-Based and Lexicon-Based Models for Couples Therapy Research
container-title: JMIR AI
02cbc8c11782c41a3488677b840de94220dc8a40.abstract: Abstract Background Natural language processing and AI models are increasingly used to extract emotional signals from textual data; however, systematic validation of different computational paradigms in emotionally complex relational contexts remains limited. Such approaches may contribute to digital health research, particularly in the fields of digital mental health and couples therapy, where understanding emotional expressions within romantic relationships is especially relevant. Objective This study aimed to compare a lexicon-based approach (NRC Emotion Lexicon) and a transformer-based model (Pysentimiento) in detecting affective patterns within spontaneous romantic relationship narratives and to evaluate their criterion-related associations with a theory-driven measure of relational well-being. Methods In this cross-sectional exploratory study, 112 Spanish adults completed the Couple Flourishing Measure (CFM) and provided an open-ended description of their romantic relationship. Narratives were analyzed using both computational approaches to generate emotion and sentiment indices. Pearson correlations were computed between model outputs and CFM scores. Steiger Z tests were conducted to compare dependent correlations across models. Results Both approaches showed significant associations with couple flourishing, although the transformer-based model yielded stronger correlations for several affective dimensions, particularly positive sentiment ( r =0.66, 95% CI 0.54-0.76) and negative sentiment ( r =−0.74, 95% CI −0.82 to −0.65). The lexicon-based approach showed smaller associations, primarily for negative emotions. Steiger Z tests identified significant between-model differences for disgust ( P =.04), joy ( P =.01), sadness ( P =.004), surprise ( P =.03), and positive and negative sentiment (both P <.001), but not for anger or fear. Conclusions In this sample, Pysentimiento showed stronger associations with couple flourishing than the NRC Emotion Lexicon across several affective dimensions, although differences were not consistent across all categories. These findings support the value of theory-driven external criteria for evaluating computational emotion detection in relational narratives and underscore the importance of context-sensitive interpretation when applying AI tools in psychologically sensitive domains. These findings also highlight the potential relevance of computational emotion analysis for digital health research, particularly in digital mental health and couples therapy research, although further validation in clinical settings is needed before clinical implementation.

99adcc7ef1ba0701fbdbb32b52267a056ceb9354.abstract: Abstract Objectives To map and analyze scientific publications on pharmaceutical clinical services for self-limiting health conditions. Methods Bibliometric review of Web of Science and Scopus records, using established scoping-review methodology, analyzed in Bibliometrix. Key findings One hundred and two articles (1983–2024) were included; output has grown over time, concentrated in the last decade. The UK (14.4%), Australia (9.8%), and Canada (6.8%) accounted for the largest shares of publications; output was concentrated among a small number of institutions and authors. Conclusions Scientific output remains concentrated in high-income countries; expanding research and implementation in low- and middle-income countries is needed.

title: Beyond Ethical Principles: A Comparative Review of National and Institutional AI Policies in Higher Education
container-title: Annual Review of Comparative and International Education 2025, Part B
6878ad58efae48f25af1668cec612152e379d038.abstract: The rapid diffusion of artificial intelligence (AI) into higher education has produced a proliferation of ethical guidelines, national strategies, and institutional policies. Yet convergence around principles such as transparency, fairness, and accountability has not produced consistent governance outcomes across contexts. This chapter offers a comparative review of national and institutional AI policies in higher education, examining how ethical commitments are translated into regulatory frameworks and operational practice. Drawing on policy texts and institutional guidance from multiple regions, the analysis traces how governance logics shift as they move from ethical aspiration to national strategy and, ultimately, to institutional implementation. This chapter argues that national AI strategies consistently frame higher education instrumentally as part of workforce development and technological competitiveness agendas, while institutional responses remain shaped by organizational capacity, fiscal constraint, and fragmented governance. A cross-national comparison reveals that differences in regulatory philosophy matter less than variations in institutional design and resource distribution. This chapter concludes by identifying methodological implications for comparative education research and outlining a future agenda focused on policy translation, capacity building, and the uneven global distribution of educational risk associated with AI.

title: National AI Strategies and Higher Education in the Global South: Policy, Practice, and Power
container-title: Annual Review of Comparative and International Education 2025, Part B
59287e6c05327437878bda94c7382a6a12355a2c.abstract: This chapter examines how national artificial intelligence (AI) strategies are translated into higher education (HE) policy and practice across the Global South (GS), with particular attention to issues of equity, governance, and power. Drawing on cases from Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, the United Arab Emirates (UAE), and South Africa, this chapter explores how universities are positioned within national AI agendas and respond through fragmented policies, pedagogical experiments, administrative adoption, and partnerships. The analysis also highlights how structural constraints shape institutional responses and how Global North–developed AI intensifies concerns about autonomy, bias, and inequalities within and between HE systems. Situating these dynamics within the broader political economy of AI, this chapter shows how market concentration, industry influence, and North–South power relations shape both the possibilities and limits of AI integration in GS universities. It argues that meaningful, context-responsive AI adoption requires closer alignment between national strategies and institutional governance, sustained public investment, and equity-focused pedagogical frameworks that move beyond market-driven models of innovation.

title: Leadership, Ethics, and Risk Management in Higher Education: The Cotton University Band Director Case
container-title: A Guide for Future Historically Black College and University Leaders
891f1e415f9beab0600a117ac4ad70f021deae8e.abstract: Abstract This case study examines the complex leadership, ethical, and risk management issues surrounding the Cotton University Band Director incident. The case focuses on institutional decision-making related to hiring practices, background check policies, student safety, crisis management, and public trust. Cotton University, a midsized public institution with a highly visible marching band program, faced public scrutiny after it was revealed that the band director had a criminal history and was later arrested following an altercation with law enforcement at a university event in front of students. The incident raised concerns among parents, students, and the community regarding the university’s hiring practices, leadership judgment, and institutional responsibility. The case explores the balance between second-chance employment and the duty of care universities must protect students and maintain institutional integrity. It also examines leadership decision-making using ethical leadership, transformational leadership, crisis leadership, and risk management frameworks. Additionally, the case highlights the importance of crisis communication, policy development, and proactive risk mitigation strategies in higher education administration. This case is designed for graduate students and higher education professionals to analyze leadership accountability, ethical decision-making, and institutional risk management. The Cotton University case demonstrates how personnel decisions can evolve into institutional crises and emphasizes the importance of responsible leadership, transparent communication, and comprehensive hiring policies in higher education.

title: A Comparative Handbook of Redesigned Sales and Marketing Management in the Digital Era
1c315992d01f6fe5a4752fa9871bed02359a4278.abstract: In an age defined by rapid technological transformation, traditional sales and marketing paradigms are being reshaped by the competitive pressures of the digital landscape. A Comparative Handbook of Redesigned Sales and Marketing Management in the Digital Era offers a rigorous comparative analysis of these evolving practices, grounded in evidence-based insights and advanced modelling. With a focus on emerging pillars of the buying and selling process, the book maps the tactics and strategies necessary for success in a digitally driven world. From the integration of current innovations to the anticipation of future technological advancements, the book presents a forward-looking roadmap for navigating the complex, interconnected realities of modern sales management. Designed to serve business professionals, academics, students, and broader stakeholders, the author examines the outcomes, conflicts, and opportunities inherent in this shift, offering a nuanced discussion of its implications for organisations and their ecosystems.

765e2852ca96c15aedf8506b69d6a320907df137.abstract: Abstract In our continuously changing, competitive era, having an economically strong, environmentally safe, and a better-managed globe requires not only digitally advanced, specialized manpower but also a gradual change from traditional to measurable, outcome-based, innovative solutions and an ethical, value-oriented growth mindset. This is valid for all business practices and society at large. Digital transformation is enhancing throughout every industry, bringing speed and easier access to information, connecting people while eliminating cross-border barriers and time constraints. In that respect, to maintain a long-term sustainable and profitable business, every firm should go through this digitalization process by adjusting and adapting its culture, organizational structure, people, and their digital infrastructure. The core disciplines of the organizations are also evolving from traditional practices to digital platforms and applications. Marketing is one of the earliest adopters of digitalization, where traditional marketing is geared toward digital marketing with the achievement of real-time access to information, providing faster and easier engagement of buyers and sellers. Today the authors refer to a redesigned, interactive, and integrated digital holistic marketing concept equipped with many smart technologies from social media marketing to affiliate marketing, maintaining the core principles of customer-centric relational marketing aligning with the new digital tools such as brand identity construction, voice search optimization, augmented reality, interactive content, and web design, building a new era supporting a technologically stronger, much more competitive market giving the opportunity of a co-value creation of buyers and sellers.

title: Redesign of Core Concepts in Sales in the Digital Era
container-title: A Comparative Handbook of Redesigned Sales and Marketing Management in the Digital Era
d20a1e4b813867b848b11267d0a4e89860795426.abstract: Abstract Today, digital transformation has set new criteria and rules for the commercial business and sales ecosystem. The real-time access to information, power of data analytics enhancing marketing intelligence, changing dynamics of consumer behavior, ever-evolving marketing trends, new buying cycles, and increased players in the market require a relook at the future scope of buyer and customer roadmap where sales is the backbone of this commercial path for firms having profitability, sustainability, and growth targets in the highly competitive global market. In our digital era, the redesigned sales model, beyond the product, is expected to cover many concepts such as productivity, optimization, the total value of ownership, timely delivery, after-sales support, financing, IT facilities, legal, regulatory, and ethical aspects. The sales professionals should act as strategic advisors, bridging and orchestrating all internal company stakeholders and external stakeholders for successful business outcomes, aligning with the customer care abouts and leading the co-value creation. Today, we refer AI integration to sales with digital CRM tools, predictive analytics, and many other digital facilities supporting salesforce for data-driven interactive selling process. While this presents many opportunities for the organizations and for the sales professionals, such as faster track of customer leads, quick market intelligence for strategizing more efficiently, it definitely requires digitally adapted culture, competency in digital technologies and a customer-centric winning mindset with knowledge, commitment, agility and competitive differentiation.

title: Field Study: Expected Change in Technology, Organizations, and Business in the Digital Era
container-title: A Comparative Handbook of Redesigned Sales and Marketing Management in the Digital Era
68b51309688dc6e568de5b7e88dee6ce2e322b3c.abstract: Abstract In today’s continuously evolving globe, digital technologies are transforming firms, the way organizations act, think, and strategize to maintain a profitable and sustainable business. This requires the proactive strategy of companies with a digital mindset and culture, adapting to the new dynamics of the unbarriered markets. Customers are now more powerful with access to information, aware of their needs, with an increasing concern on a cleaner, accountable, ethical, and transparent future world. This chapter evaluates the answers of commercial business professionals from corporate world on qualifying the expected impacts of digitalization on organizations, in organizational structure, the effects of artificial intelligence (AI) integration, the influence of social media, the changes in consumer behavior, and how the new sales professionals are expected to manage the new customer journey in terms of the value creation, differentiation, and engagement for competitive advantages. A second survey conducted among industry stakeholders from various businesses assesses the required attributes of a sales professional in the digital era. The analysis of the results indicate the increasing transformation in digital era where most firms are urged for digitalization as the common mind of interviewees addressing mostly hybrid organizations benefiting from the human and digital power depending on the complexity of the industry. Digital competency of sales professionals in predicting market intelligence and insights for strategic decision-making, customer centricity, solution selling, engaging customers for co-value creation for innovation, and loyalty underline the new norms of sales professionals in the digital era.

title: Evaluation of Changing Customer Behavior in the Digital Era
container-title: A Comparative Handbook of Redesigned Sales and Marketing Management in the Digital Era
207d6524df8e52e73b70988713260c0cd328a4d9.abstract: Abstract The digitalization via continuously developing artificial intelligence (AI) tools such as machine learning, natural language processing, and generative AI give the consumers the opportunity to decrease their workload and have the power to check for competitive pricing and optimized solutions. In parallel, we must recognize and embrace the essence and contribution of all digital tools providing a huge base for information connecting the consumers and business bringing speed to access data, and faster buyer–seller interactions. This in return is expected to take the consumer journey and decision-making scheme to an extended level in near future where consumers are expected to dominate more on their demands and personally defined needs not only by satisfying their personal expectations but also by giving directions to the firms’ strategies in terms of new innovations and solutions for future. This “New Customer Profile” in the digital era worths diagnosis on its changing buying roadmap compared to traditional practices as today we talk about insightful and empowered customers, increased ecommerce activities, more integration and interaction with social media, and the impact of AI use by the customers. The demand for customization requires companies to be better equipped in terms of organization, brand identity, and digital competency. Despite ongoing privacy and ethical concerns on digital arena, commodity, and retail goods expand utilizing the digital platforms reaching consumers, the complex industries such as healthcare, financial markets, and high-tech industry business still reserve room for traditional practices where in-person communication with end user and trust are highly required.

title: Sales Management: From Core to New Scopes and Strategy in the Digital Era
container-title: A Comparative Handbook of Redesigned Sales and Marketing Management in the Digital Era
ce4c28aefd3c986f492853027788c46fd51c512a.abstract: Abstract The core requirements of effective sales management are planning and strategy while being equally competent with the salesforce management by setting performance and internal controls. In parallel, there must be a clear analysis of markets. Today, the technology integration by digital transformation has brought a different base to the role of sales management. The digital customer relationship management tools like most common being salesforce, HubSpot, and Power BI are all used in most of the commercial companies, where these platforms provide a comprehensive suite for tracking sales, marketing, and service activities, enabling the visibility of the customer-buying journey. In parallel, in our continuously digitalizing and changing business environments, organizations analyze and work to implement the most suitable service model, which can be service-based, customer-based, or multilevel models, to optimize their operations while improving customer satisfaction and profitability. As technology evolves, many companies work on the implementation of hybrid models depending on the company goals, industry dynamics, market conditions, and the customer needs. Digitalization is also effective on improving the diversity and inclusion in organizations. The technology proves clearly that it can align people via discussion platforms for “connected teams”. Today sales planning and budgeting are also supported by digital tools streamlining these processes for faster and more accurate outcomes. The other core pillars in the sales management such as forecasting, opportunity tracking, value propositioning, and negotiation are also enhanced by digital platforms with optimized competitive and customer-centric solutions.

title: International Sales Management and Expected Practices in the Digital Era
container-title: A Comparative Handbook of Redesigned Sales and Marketing Management in the Digital Era
213156dc246e8c72c840cd8193ada1f3cc899f03.abstract: Abstract Companies may have different goals when entering international markets. These objectives generally include increasing sales, revenue, and profit potential, establishing a new customer base, providing expansion and diversification opportunities, gaining greater access to talent, gaining a competitive advantage, managing risks, enhancing company reputation, reducing operating costs, creating economies of scale, and leveraging tax advantages if available. Firms can conduct international business directly or via distributors. The selection of distributors is critical in terms of compliance, financial strength, local competitive power, and customer engagement. Today, firms profit from digitalization by enhanced resource accessibility, improved market access, faster and more efficient communications, while the digital technologies also give the businesses the opportunity of going beyond the geographic boundaries and deliver customized content, present products and services through data driven insights and advanced analytics. Equally these platforms support companies in terms of effective digital marketing, brand identity setting, and customer engagement. Today, companies must set their business and sales strategies aligning also their digitalization plans utilizing global e-commerce, social media, and other digital networks while expanding across borders, engaging various customers, and optimizing their supply chains. It is noteworthy to consider challenges of regulatory barriers, platform dependencies, data privacy, and high competition. Achieving success in today’s digitally moderated environment also requires cross-functional integration for companies which means bridging marketing, legal, IT, and supply chain pillars to optimize digital infrastructure, ensuring regulatory compliance, and managing this fundamental complexity of ecosystem in international arenas.

title: Essence of Corporate Governance, Sustainability, and Social Responsiveness in the Digital Era
container-title: A Comparative Handbook of Redesigned Sales and Marketing Management in the Digital Era
324ca77850ee47ad9827a0af442d9cdd319c3518.abstract: Abstract The technological development and the continuously growing digital economy have created a different profile of corporations, capital markets, and changed the nature of the global economy at large. This situation has its obvious expected corporate governance impacts and outcomes. The use of digital technology improves regulatory efficiency and enhances disclosure practices, market supervision, and enforcement of corporate governance-related requirements. New platforms based on big data and machine learning enable the systematic application and transparency of environmental, social, and governance (ESG) information for investors and companies. This situation encourages shifting capital from less sustainable to more sustainable companies. Today, it can be predicted that the importance of environmental and natural life protection requirements and institutional responsibilities will be an even more crucial plan at the government, companies, and the individual level. Equally, global business management and corporate governance trends are also changing and transforming into new structures in the digital era and we observe more attention and efforts of many multinational firms to improve their integrity, diversity, and inclusion strategy. In parallel notes to mention that the digitalization has not only given the access to consumers to have a full visibility of goods and services in the market but also has transformed people to “conscious customers” who are more determined on their needs, preferences, and buying decisions. Therefore, in our digital era, the consumers are expected to be keener in their investment decisions, and these investment decisions can gear toward more ESG-oriented firms.

title: Changing Role of HR in the Digital Era and Expected Impacts on Business
container-title: A Comparative Handbook of Redesigned Sales and Marketing Management in the Digital Era
01e2eeec0f34064773dd703e30b5032635da2197.abstract: Abstract Digital transformation is already changing the traditional business models, including human resource management (HRM) practices in organizations, as the technology is globally setting new norms and business conduct toward connecting people with measurable, accessible, and data-based processes in firms targeting real-time information, accuracy, and speed for improving operational excellence. Human power being an asset for companies makes the role of HRM more critical in the digital era due to high competition and changing customer behavior, provoking the need for more innovative solutions to differentiate in global markets. In that spectrum, talent acquisition and retention become vital factors to long-term success. Today, as a part of digital transformation, digital HRM is also a concept evolving in organizations, which should be a part of the company strategy in terms of its infrastructure and HRM stakeholders’ competency accelerating the cultural change for a digital mindset in the total organization. Tools like predictive analytics and data mining not only provide data-based insights for HR stakeholders, speeding up the HR processes, but also give the opportunity for utilizing time on more strategic initiatives. Empirical and theoretical studies present the correlation of HRM with firm performance, productivity, and profitability. In parallel, the global environmental, social and governmental (ESG) requirements underlining the essence of decent work and economic growth encourage HRM to position itself with the strategic role to lead sustainable organizations. Once the digital ethics and HRM skillset competency are completed, the digital HRM is expected to expand and be grounded in organizations aligned with the companies’ overall digital transformation strategies.

title: Critical Pillars of Competitive Edge for Firms in the Digital Era
container-title: A Comparative Handbook of Redesigned Sales and Marketing Management in the Digital Era
c86b07d062a1b0b051110cbc8a56820fd9af96bd.abstract: Abstract Today, one of the critical success factors of long-term profitable business in the highly competitive arena is the digital transformation by utilizing the benefits of technology, streamlining the workflow of operations, automating routine tasks to improve the business efficiency and productivity. On the other hand, the technologies are still not at the complete maturity stage including the cybersecurity concerns while the growth of digital technologies is very fast, setting expectations for overcoming the existing challenges by profiting from the data-based insights, real-time information, interactive communication without the geographical barriers as well as automation and optimization of processes impacting the operational excellency and faster decision mechanisms. Also, consumers have evolved into more conscious buyers profiting from digital platforms, social media, and real-time information encouraging them for personalized solutions matching their care abouts. This new phenomenon equally bridges the customer and the firm for co-creating value by faster innovations. In the interim, there are major criteria for impactful digital transformation, and this chapter underlines the essence of 11 parameters with an authentic scheme addressing the readiness for competitive edge. The firms are expected to have a cultural organizational change toward digitalization by investing in new technologies, in house IT with a focus of improving digital competencies of their employees, channel partners, and human resource management (HRM) stakeholders. The corporate governance digital transformation strategy with the set key performance indicators (KPIs) embracing compliance, digital ethics, cybersecurity infrastructures, and sustainability efforts are crucial for long-term profitable business.

title: Climate reporting in public sector organisations: identity construction and changes
container-title: Journal of Public Budgeting, Accounting & Financial Management
a87c4da3cc26f15b51505565419be6ff1e46804b.abstract: Purpose The purpose of this article is to explore climate change reporting by public sector organisations. In particular, the analysis draws attention to how public sector organisations represent themselves through climate reporting practice to construct and reproduce their identities over time. Design/methodology/approach A comprehensive content analysis of 164 annual and stand-alone sustainability reports produced by 15 public sector organisations listed on the Australian National Greenhouse and Energy Reporting register over an 11-year period from 2014 to 2024 was used for this study. The analysis is informed by Tregidga et al.'s (2014) identity framework of sustainable organisations. Findings The analysis reveals an unbalanced pattern of identity construction in public sector climate reporting, characterised by a strong focus on compliance-oriented reporting, followed by reporting on climate leadership and limited engagement with strategically “good” practices associated with legitimacy seeking. Despite evidence of more substantive climate reporting, disclosures continue to focus predominantly on metrics and statistics reflecting regulatory and policy expectations. The longitudinal analysis reinforces this identity structure, although their climate reporting has developed into a more complex communicative space through which public sector organisations simultaneously construct multiple identities over time, implying that public sector climate reporting serves as a dynamic and ongoing process of identity construction rather than a linear transition from one identity to another. The analysis across organisational types also reveals that a compliance-oriented identity is most pronounced among local governments and moderately prominent in public service organisations, whereas a leadership-oriented identity emphasising community impact and knowledge sharing is most strongly developed in public universities. Originality/value Despite the rapid development of climate reporting in corporate contexts, research on sustainability and climate reporting in the public sector is still underdeveloped, even as these organisations increasingly recognise the importance of disclosing, governing and managing climate-related impacts. This article fills the gap by exploring how disclosures on climate change have evolved over time within public sector organisations to contribute to accountability and effective policy implementation. It extends Tregidga et al.'s (2014) organisational identity framework to a public sector context, where climate reporting is characterised by the coexistence of regulatory, public value and legitimacy considerations.

title: Diminishing returns to calibrated reliance on AI: effects on deliverable quality and rework effort, moderated by task verifiability
container-title: Information Technology & People
484244033afc4957dd48a954f65145f1c67a443f.abstract: Purpose Artificial intelligence (AI) tools can function as both “performance accelerators” and “risk propagators” in organizations. This study investigates how AI-enabled work capability, particularly employees' decomposition and evaluation skills, is associated with deliverable quality and rework effort through the behavioral pathway of calibrated reliance on AI. Additionally, it examines task verifiability as a critical boundary condition that shapes the effectiveness of human-AI collaboration. Design/methodology/approach Guided by appropriate reliance and automation trust theories, data from 380 workers were analyzed using SmartPLS 4 (partial least squares structural equation modeling) and hierarchical polynomial regression to test mediation, moderation, and quadratic effects. Procedural remedies and a latent method factor approach were employed to assess common method bias. Findings AI-enabled work capability was positively associated with calibrated reliance on AI. Calibrated reliance on AI was associated with higher deliverable quality and lower rework effort. A double diminishing marginal pattern emerged: as reliance calibration increased, quality gains and rework reductions leveled off, indicating a “too-much-of-a-good-thing” pattern. Task verifiability strengthened the positive association between calibrated reliance and deliverable quality and also strengthened its negative association with rework effort. Originality/value This study shifts the focus from reliance intensity to reliance calibration in explaining AI-enabled work outcomes. It documents a double diminishing marginal pattern, showing that the benefits of calibrated reliance are meaningful but not unlimited. It also identifies task verifiability as a boundary condition that helps explain when calibrated reliance is more strongly associated with improved deliverable quality and reduced rework effort. These findings provide focused guidance for capability development, reliance calibration, and task-specific AI governance.

title: Linking organizational trust to voice behaviors in healthcare workers: the mediating role of organizational identification
container-title: Journal of Health Organization and Management
ce8cb0cd63ea84f7b8defb58438e87b0a48c612c.abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine the relationship between organizational trust and employee voice behavior among healthcare workers and to determine the mediating role of organizational identification in this relationship. Design/methodology/approach Using a quantitative, cross-sectional design, the study was conducted with 291 healthcare employees working in a private hospital in Samsun, Türkiye. Data were collected using a structured questionnaire consisting of the Organizational Trust Scale, Employee Voice Behavior Scale and Organizational Identification Scale, along with a sociodemographic information form. Descriptive statistics, Pearson’s correlation analysis and mediation analysis were performed using IBM SPSS 26 and PROCESS Macro. Findings The findings revealed that organizational trust was positively and significantly associated with employee voice behavior and organizational identification. Moreover, organizational identification was positively associated with employee voice behavior. Mediation analysis indicated that organizational identification partially mediated the relationship between organizational trust and employee voice behavior. These results suggest that higher levels of perceived organizational trust are associated with stronger organizational identification, which, in turn, is associated with a greater willingness to express constructive ideas, concerns and suggestions. Originality/value This study contributes to the organizational behavior literature by examining organizational identification as a psychological mechanism linking organizational trust to employee voice behavior among healthcare workers. In addition, this study provides a healthcare-specific perspective on how trust and identification may foster employees’ willingness to express ideas, concerns and suggestions for organizational improvement.

title: Digitalization and employees' unethical pro-organizational behavior in international engineering projects: mediating mechanisms and contextual moderators
container-title: Engineering, Construction and Architectural Management
65779879086bfaae63eedc7d90bd51ed32ee4ce9.abstract: Purpose This study examines how digitalization influences employees' unethical pro-organizational behavior (UPB) in international engineering projects. It investigates whether digitalization affects UPB directly or indirectly through digital stress and information transparency, and whether this relationship is conditioned by cultural differences and geographical dispersion. Design/methodology/approach A pilot test was conducted to refine the questionnaire. The final survey was distributed to contractor employees engaged in international engineering projects, yielding 201 valid responses. Data were analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling and Importance–Performance Map Analysis. Findings The study revealed that digitalization does not have a significant direct effect on UPB. Its influence operates through indirect and context-dependent mechanisms. Digital stress serves as a risk-enhancing pathway, whereas information transparency serves as a risk-reducing pathway. Cultural differences and geographical dispersion further condition the relationship between digitalization and UPB. Originality/value Theoretically, this study bridges digitalization research and UPB literature by examining how digitalization is linked to unethical behavior in international engineering projects. Practically, it contributes to ethical risk management by highlighting factors that should be considered when implementing digital systems.

title: Climate conditions, financial uncertainty and market resilience in African equity markets: an event-driven probabilistic deep learning approach
container-title: Management & Sustainability: An Arab Review
11df4e60975026eac2a96bc357327f02b3cfda3f.abstract: Purpose This paper examines stock-market volatility in Egypt, Morocco, Nigeria, South Africa and Tunisia under geopolitical and financial uncertainty and physical climate conditions. African evidence rarely integrates event-time shock analysis with full-distribution forecasting while distinguishing physical climate signals from climate-related financial risk. The study develops an event-driven probabilistic framework grounded in a Climate–Market Conditioning Framework (CMCF). Design/methodology/approach The study combines cumulative abnormal volatility (CAV) analysis with Mixture Density Network–Long Short-Term Memory (MDN-LSTM) volatility and return-density models. Daily market data from January 2015 to April 2025 are combined with Geopolitical Risk, Financial Stress Index and National Aeronautics and Space Administration Prediction of Worldwide Energy Resources climate indicators. Forecasts use a strict chronological holdout and are compared with Generalised Autoregressive Conditional Heteroskedasticity (GARCH)(1,1)-Normal, GARCH(1,1)-Student-t, Exponential GARCH (EGARCH), Glosten–Jagannathan–Runkle-GARCH (GJR-GARCH), Random Forest and Extreme Gradient Boosting. Distributional performance is additionally benchmarked against probabilistic GARCH using the weighted interval score (WIS). Findings Shock responses are heterogeneous across markets. The four fixed global events provide descriptive economic differences but weak small-sample inference, whereas larger factor-specific event samples yield selected market-dependent effects. GARCH-family models remain stronger for point forecasts and GARCH-Normal also records lower WIS, while MDN-LSTM often produces lower-tail hit rates closer to the nominal 5% level. Distributional and Value-at-Risk diagnostics nevertheless show country-specific calibration limitations, especially in South Africa and Nigeria. Practical implications The findings provide useful insights for investors, regulators, and policymakers by improving volatility monitoring, supporting tail-risk management, and informing macroprudential risk assessment in vulnerable financial markets. The evidence also supports integrating climate-sensitive volatility indicators into scenario analysis and sustainable-investment risk monitoring, while avoiding causal policy claims that are not identified by the forecasting design. Originality/value The paper integrates event-based volatility analysis with probabilistic forecasting in African equity markets and develops a Climate–Market Conditioning Framework. The framework distinguishes physical climate conditions from climate-related financial risk and proposes that financial consequences are conditioned by market structure, liquidity, international integration and adaptive investor behaviour rather than being uniform or mechanically causal.

title: Newspapers Blocking AI Crawlers Expose Their Voters to a Partisan Flood
46c8c2234ccd7b8a4f424f64283b415493f39665.abstract: Major newspapers block AI crawlers, while parties and partisan sites leave their text open. This paper builds a game-theoretic model of the hold-out and asks what voters hear while it lasts. In the model, an AI that cannot grade its sources pools the text it can read; two persuaders choose how much nearly free text to publish; and an AI lab may license a newspaper's reporting for its lost revenue. Neither the newspapers nor the lab has a political aim. Three results follow. First, the persuaders flood the AI, and the lab licenses each newspaper once a fixed share of the voters closest to it asks the AI, whatever the AI says. Second, newspapers whose voters dislike the AI's answers more hold out longer, and their voters hear the flood longer. Third, licensing bends the persuaders' contest by a small tilt from where the costs alone put it: patient persuaders tilt the AI's answers against the voters' average ideology, and impatient ones toward it. Business decisions with no political aim thus set how long each group hears the flood and which way the AI's answers tilt.

title: C-suite incentive conflict and firm efficiency
container-title: Management Decision
5cdfd3ecdc87b79680308a9bbf75edc0020af9a5.abstract: Purpose This article provides empirical support to a long-debated theory in behavioral and organizational management literature regarding how the incentive conflict of firms' executives affects the firm's efficiency. Design/methodology/approach The study employs panel regression techniques, using efficiency measures derived from data envelopment analysis (DEA) and stochastic frontier analysis (SFA) as dependent variables, and a novel measure of C-suite incentive conflict as the independent variable, based on annual data from US companies covering the period 1992–2018. Findings Our results show that incentive conflict improves firm efficiency and thus support the constructive impact of C-suite conflict on firm efficiency. We find that the positive impact of incentive conflict on firm efficiency is weakened when the CEO is more powerful. Our findings provide support to agency theory by documenting that a more diverse board of directors reinforces the positive relationship between incentive conflict and firm efficiency. Research limitations/implications One limitation of this study is that the dataset is restricted to the period ending in 2018, which may limit the ability to capture more recent developments in corporate governance practices and executive incentive structures. Although the findings provide important insights for corporate executives and policymakers, extending the dataset to more recent years would improve the timeliness and generalizability of the analysis. Future research may address this limitation by incorporating updated data to examine whether the observed relationships persist under evolving global economic and governance conditions. Practical implications Our study provides two key implications for promoting sustainable business models for the corporations. First, the positive impact of incentive conflict on firm efficiency may suggest that employers design executives' compensation packages where the Vega differences between CEOs and non-CEO executives are above the median can be a benchmark. Second, corporations may design policies to minimize CEO's power and improve the positive impact of incentive conflict on firm efficiency by increasing the presence of minorities in the board of directors. Originality/value First, to the best of our knowledge, this study is a pioneer study in examining the relationship between firm efficiency and workforce conflict using a novel measure of incentive conflict. Second, this study involves an interdisciplinary investigation by applying econometric methods on financial data to provide empirical support to a long-debated theory about the impact of C-suite incentive conflict on firm efficiency in behavioral and organizational management literature. Finally, our study has at least two important policy implications for corporations. First, the positive impact of incentive conflict on firm efficiency may suggest that employers to benchmark the industrial median of incentive conflict to design executives' compensation packages where the Vega differences between CEOs and non-CEO executives are above the median. Second, corporations may design policies to minimize the CEO's power and encourage the presence of minorities in the board of directors to improve the positive impact of incentive conflict on firm efficiency.

title: The social mechanics of resilience: a conceptual framework for understanding trust, networks and sensemaking in multi-hazard early warning systems
container-title: Disaster Prevention and Management: An International Journal
a90cffa40c2068a07798983c821549cf03401e82.abstract: Purpose This article introduces the social mechanics of resilience (SMR), a conceptual framework explaining how trust, social networks and sensemaking shape collective responses to multi-hazard early warning systems. Although warning technologies have advanced, gaps persist between alert issuance and public action. The article reframes warning effectiveness as a relational and interpretive challenge rather than solely a technical one. Design/methodology/approach The article develops a conceptual framework through integrative analysis of disaster resilience research, social capital theory, risk and crisis communication and sensemaking literature. Rather than presenting empirical findings, it synthesizes these bodies of work to specify how bonding, bridging and linking social capital interact with trust and interpretation processes across the warning–response continuum. Findings The SMR framework demonstrates that warning effectiveness depends on relational trust, network structure and shared interpretation. Trust influences whether warnings receive attention, networks shape message circulation and sensemaking affects how risk is understood and acted upon. The framework highlights feedback loops across preparedness and response phases and underscores the importance of inclusive engagement and credible communication. Originality/value This article advances disaster resilience theory by specifying how trust, networks and sensemaking function as interacting mechanisms linking early warnings to collective action. By integrating previously separate strands of research into a coherent model, it offers both theoretical clarity and practical insight for emergency management and provides a foundation for future empirical testing.

title: Project management maturity and project success: exploring the role of sustainability
container-title: Central European Management Journal
e4aee288e0c5f5756b45f7a2997735f65d8cdaff.abstract: Purpose Organizations invest in project management maturity (PMM) to improve project success, yet the unresolved issue is not only whether PMM is related to project success, but through which project-level mechanisms. This study investigates PMM's influence on project success, directly and through project sustainability. Design/methodology/approach Following a scoping review, PMM was measured using Level 2 of Kerzner's model; Project success covered performance, stakeholder satisfaction, future preparedness and manager-rated success; Project sustainability comprised sustainability of project practices (SPPs) and integration of project sustainability (IPS). Survey data from 482 German and Polish projects were analyzed using confirmatory factor, mediation and moderated mediation analyses. Findings PMM was positively related to project success. SPP partially mediated this relationship for overall success and all four criteria, whereas IPS did not. Research limitations/implications The cross-sectional, single-respondent design limits causal inference; one maturity model constrains generalizability. Future studies should use multi-source data and other maturity frameworks. Practical implications Organizations should strengthen common project-management processes, sustainability competencies and sustainable practices. Originality/value The study empirically tests project sustainability as a mechanism linking PMM to project success. Examining SPP and IPS across overall success and four criteria reveals distinct pathways and points to the possible need for organization-level integration.

title: Aligning institutions and organizations for sustainable supply chains: the role of digital transformation and low-carbon practices
container-title: Supply Chain Management: An International Journal
af7f22db9f22c3964bb66acb9d57ccadccdb77ec.abstract: Purpose The transition toward carbon neutrality has become a global strategic priority for achieving sustainable development and a green economy. Despite growing interest in digital transformation among scholars and practitioners, achieving a balance between green supply chain performance and carbon performance within the context of carbon neutrality remains underexplored. Drawing on the technology acceptance model and change management theory, this research aims to provide solutions for achieving the zero-carbon target in 2060 through holistic digital transformation, and how institutional pressure and organizational readiness influence green supply chain and carbon performance through digital transformation, low-carbon operations management practices (LCOMP) and the moderating role of environmental proactivity. Design/methodology/approach Data from 442 Chinese manufacturing firms were analyzed using Smart PLS v4 to test the research hypotheses. Findings The results indicate that all three dimensions of LCOMP mediate the relationship between digital transformation, green supply chain and carbon performance. In addition, environmental proactivity strengthens the influence of digital transformation on the three dimensions of LCOMP. Originality/value The findings contribute to the literature by addressing a key gap in sustainable supply chain and digital transformation research, which has largely examined these relationships in isolation without fully explaining the mediating mechanisms and boundary conditions.

title: Dangerous (Artificial) Minds: Charting a Middle Path for AI in High School English
container-title: English Journal
ee4f817b21bab9832d5f5852b4763686d11e39c4.abstract: The author details five strategies he uses to incorporate artificial intelligence (AI) as “text” for his high school English students to analyze as a means of developing their critical thinking skills. He forges a “middle path” between the equally problematic options of banning and full-on embracing AI in the English language arts classroom.

title: Analysis of RNA processing directly from spatial transcriptomics data reveals previously unknown regulation
0bfea74a14535bf669c2608ae3dcd305fd802859.abstract: Technical advances have led to an explosion in the amount of biological data available in recent years, especially in the field of RNA sequencing. Specifically, spatial transcriptomics (ST) datasets, which allow each RNA molecule to be mapped to the 2D location it originated from within a tissue, have become readily available. Due to computational challenges, ST data has rarely been used to study RNA processing such as splicing or differential UTR usage. We apply the ReadZS and the SpliZ, methods developed to analyze RNA process in scRNA-seq data, to analyze spatial localization of RNA processing directly from ST data for the first time. Using Moran’s I metric for spatial autocorrelation, we identify genes with spatially regulated RNA processing in the mouse brain and kidney, re-discovering known spatial regulation in Myl6 and identifying previously-unknown spatial regulation in genes such as Rps24, Gng13, Slc8a1, Gpm6a, Gpx3, ActB, Rps8, and S100A9. The rich set of discoveries made here from commonly used reference datasets provides a small taste of what can be learned by applying this technique more broadly to the large quantity of Visium data currently being created.

title: An interdisciplinary methodology for assessing architectural learning outcomes
container-title: Pollack Periodica
51a4428fc93cb83078531d6a5a028b6e79aff032.abstract: Abstract This study presents an interdisciplinary methodology for evaluating architectural learning outcomes, with a focus on integrating history, urbanism, and regionalism. By combining graphic analysis, critical thinking, and visual interpretation, the used methodology used to holistically assess students' academic progress and skill development within three different study courses. Through structured phases of historical contextualization, urban-scale exercises, and regionalist critiques, the methodology addresses gaps in traditional pedagogical frameworks. The results highlight enhanced analytical rigor, improved visual communication, and a deeper understanding of socio-cultural contexts in architectural education.

title: Az EU AI Act hazai implementációja: Jogi, kormányzási és biztonsági kockázatok a mesterséges intelligencia megfelelésében
container-title: Scientia et Securitas
7fe3847c42df249157d34987b8a2c46c0afe439a.abstract: A tanulmány azt vizsgálja, miként illeszkedik az Európai Unió mesterséges intelligenciáról szóló rendelete (EU 2024/1689 – AI Act) és annak hazai végrehajtása, a 2025. évi LXXV. törvény a magyar jogi és intézményi környezetbe. A kutatás különös figyelmet fordít a kockázatalapú szabályozás logikájára, a trustworthy AI elvének érvényesülésére, valamint a human-in-the-loop követelmény gyakorlati megvalósítására. A vizsgálat kvalitatív jogelemzési és szabályozás-összehasonlító módszereket alkalmazott. Eredményei szerint Magyarország jelentős előrelépést tett a hatósági és infrastrukturális végrehajtás terén, azonban a szervezeti kultúra és az etikai érettség fejlettsége még nem éri el a kívánatos szintet. Ez a hiányosság biztonságpolitikai kockázatokat is hordoz, különösen a kritikus infrastruktúrák és a közszolgáltatások területén. A tanulmány javaslatokat fogalmaz meg az etikai irányelvek fejlesztésére, a szervezeti integritás erősítésére és az MI-compliance rendszerek mélyebb beágyazására a hazai kormányzási gyakorlatba.

title: Compliance-by-Design in an AI-Enabled Platform for Early Crohn Disease Interception: A Viewpoint
container-title: Journal of Medical Internet Research
3ce9f5c02f3d112fa70bf8dcc4742bd057e94e20.abstract: Abstract AI-enabled digital medicine platforms in Europe are developed within overlapping rules for personal data, medical devices, AI, clinical research, health data access, and health technology assessment. This viewpoint represents the authors’ experience and interpretation from the preimplementation phase of INTERCEPT, an Innovative Health Initiative consortium that plans to validate biomarkers and develop a blood-based risk score for early Crohn disease interception. It does not report original empirical research, a systematic regulatory review, a deployed platform, or a validated AI model. Our aim is to explain how compliance-by-design can be translated into an auditable governance architecture and to identify what still requires scientific evaluation. We advance 3 messages. First, governance must begin with intended purpose and boundary mapping: a digital platform may contain research, operational, and medical device software functions, and conformity of one module cannot be inferred for the platform as a whole. Second, overlapping obligations can be operationalized through 5 linked controls: modular responsibility and change control, federated data governance, traceable AI life cycle management, consent and participant rights orchestration, and a common cross-border governance core with local adaptations. Third, compliance is not a surrogate for model validity, clinical benefit, trust, scalability, or market access. Before clinical deployment, planned AI components require prespecified labels and cohorts, leakage prevention, missing data and imbalance strategies, calibration, subgroup assessment, external validation, human factors evaluation, and postdeployment algorithmovigilance. A hypothetical biomarker risk score update illustrates how the 5 controls interact. INTERCEPT is informative because it combines cross-border biomarker research, planned predictive analytics, and heterogeneous institutional settings while key design decisions remain modifiable. Its contribution is nevertheless conceptual: the proposed framework is a testable governance hypothesis, not evidence of implementation success. Prospective studies should compare it with alternative governance models and assess safety, workload, participant experience, evidence generation, and regulatory performance.

title: Machine Learning Models for Glycemic Prediction in Type 1 and Type 2 Diabetes: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
container-title: Journal of Medical Internet Research
2268da2a5e51445f27375d47790329e2c0548706.abstract: Abstract Background Machine learning models are increasingly used for glycemic event prediction and continuous glucose forecasting, but targets, populations, horizons, validation, and uncertainty reporting remain heterogeneous. Objective This study aimed to evaluate machine learning models for glycemic prediction in type 1, type 2, and mixed diabetes populations while distinguishing the full evidence map from the quantitatively analyzable subset. Methods We searched 9 English- and Chinese-language databases from inception to April 12, 2026, for studies predicting future glycemic events or glucose values in people with diabetes. Continuous forecasting and binary event prediction were analyzed separately. Root-mean-square error (RMSE) was the principal continuous end point; mean absolute error was supportive. Area under the receiver operating characteristic curve was synthesized using a Bayesian random-effects model because analyzable 2×2 data were sparse. Two reviewers (HY and DA) independently applied PROBAST (Prediction Model Risk of Bias Assessment Tool) to 19 quantitative-source reports (28 assessment units). Results We identified 787 records, assessed 310 full texts, and included 299 reports representing 270 studies; 19 reports contributed to quantitative synthesis. The review included 128 type 1, 26 type 2, 78 mixed, and 38 unclear-diabetes-type studies. Pooled RMSE was 1.18 mmol/L (95% CI 1.01‐1.34; 37 effects), supportive mean absolute error was 0.90 mmol/L (95% CI 0.78‐1.02; 20 effects), and Bayesian pooled area under the receiver operating characteristic curve was 0.926 (95% credible interval 0.877‐0.957). Supportive sensitivity and specificity were 0.77 and 0.80. Of 28 PROBAST units, 24 were high risk, 2 unclear, and 2 low. Post hoc exploratory within-report analysis estimated an RMSE increase of 0.481 mmol/L per additional 30 minutes (95% CI 0.213‐0.749), but overlap sensitivity reduced certainty. In the 270-study clinical readiness audit, external validation occurred in 4.0% (10/251), prospective evaluation in 0.7% (2/270), calibration in 4.8% (13/270), decision-curve or net-benefit analysis in 2.6% (7/270), and implementation or human-factors evaluation in 2.6% (7/270). Conclusions Glycemic prediction studies show forecasting and discrimination signals, but heterogeneity, high risk of bias, incomplete uncertainty reporting, and limited external and prospective validation preclude deployable benchmarks. Pooled estimates should be viewed as summaries of analyzable literature. Future studies need transparent horizon, threshold, calibration, validation, uncertainty, and implementation reporting.

title: Interpretable machine learning applied to high-dimensional salivary proteomics in pediatric inflammatory bowel diseases
container-title: Inflammatory Bowel Diseases
7c78625f701fba6e311669bd663aaab5fcc3d243.abstract: Abstract Background Inflammatory bowel diseases (IBDs), including Crohn’s disease (CD), ulcerative colitis (UC), and inflammatory bowel disease unclassified (IBD-U), are chronic inflammatory disorders of the gastrointestinal tract. Current methods for classification and longitudinal monitoring are invasive, expensive, and often delayed, limiting timely diagnosis and management. This proof-of-concept study reports the first application of high-dimensional salivary proteomics integrated with interpretable artificial intelligence/machine learning (ML) to define a minimal protein signature for pediatric IBD classification with the ultimate goal of informing therapeutic decision-making. Methods Unstimulated saliva from pediatric CD, UC, and IBD-U patients was analyzed using Alamar Biosciences’ NULISAseq 250 Protein Inflammation Panel. Logistic regression with recursive feature elimination identified a candidate minimal discriminative signature. Performance was further assessed using follow-up samples. SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) quantified patient-specific protein contributions and assessed biological similarity of IBD-U to CD and UC. Results Differential abundance analysis between UC and CD revealed 53 significantly different proteins. ML identified a 14-protein signature comprising chemokines/cytokines (CCL1, IFNA1-IFNA13, IL12p70, IL34, TNFSF11/RANKL), receptors/ligands (CD40LG, ICOSLG, IL1R2, IL17RA), structural/tissue-remodeling proteins (CD93, GFAP, SPP1), and growth factors/immune modulators (GDF2, GZMA). The proposed model achieved 97.5% balanced accuracy in first-visit pilot samples and 80.2% with matched follow-up samples. SHAP revealed patient-specific drivers and suggested biological alignment of IBD-U cases toward CD- or UC-like profiles. Conclusions This first-in-field integration of salivary proteomics with interpretable artificial intelligence/ML demonstrates that accurate, noninvasive classification of pediatric IBD is possible using minimal biomarker sets. This approach establishes a scalable framework for future longitudinal monitoring and supports earlier and more precise therapeutic interventions.

title: Single-step deep learning target-in-the-loop phase retrieval algorithm for tiled-aperture CBC laser systems
container-title: High-Power Lasers and Technologies for Optical Countermeasures IV
fbf481c9167791528b7ada54b6a08483ce6f3b6e.abstract: We present an experimental single-step deep learning method for phase retrieval in a tiled-aperture Coherent Beam Combination (CBC) system. The goal is to estimate the relative piston phases of the individual beams directly from a single far-field intensity image formed on a target and acquired by a camera. The method was tested with hexagonal arrays of 7 and 19 sources, but the same approach can be extended to a different number of beams. The beam array is propagated and focused onto an aluminium target, where the individual beams are combined. The resulting intensity distribution on the target is imaged onto a camera using an imaging lens system, with a suitable magnification to contain the complete far-field pattern inside the camera frame. A ResNet is trained to estimate the relative phases directly from these images. The phase values used as ground truth are obtained experimentally with an analytical interferometric phase retrieval method. This makes it possible to acquire, for each configuration, both the far-field image and the corresponding phase state of each element in the array. After training, the neural network is integrated into the control loop and its phase estimates are used to correct the phase errors of the emitters. Experimental tests show that the network can close the loop and maintain coherent combination over time. The proposed approach therefore provides a single-step method to estimate the phase state of a CBC system directly from one target image, without running an iterative phase retrieval algorithm during operation. This study was conducted within the framework of the TALOS TVVO programme, an R&D initiative funded by the European Defence Fund (EDF).

title: Innovative Learning Media In Physical Education On The Level Of Enjoyment Of Elementary School Students In 3T Areas

8adb466f2b33d22087159d33aa82606fa50196bc.abstract: This study aims to analyze the impact of using innovative physical education learning media on the level of enjoyment of elementary school students in 3T areas. The background of this study stems from limited learning conditions, both in terms of facilities, infrastructure, and access to technology, so that innovative, simple, and contextual learning strategies are needed. The method used in this study was quantitative with a One Group Prestest-Posttest design. This study involved all twelve students, and data were collected through a 15 item enjoyment level questionnaire. The data were analyzed using the Shapiro-Wilk normality test and paired sample t-test. The results showed a significant increase in the enjoyment scores of students after the application of innovative media, with an increase in the average score from 28 to 47. The results of the paired sample t-test showed a significance value of 0.000 (<0.05), indicating that innovative media for physical education, health, and sports learning had a significant effect on increasing student enjoyment levels. These findings confirm that the use of innovative media in accordance with the characteristics of 3T areas is effective in creating a more interesting and enjoyable learning process for students.

Bias in Medical AI in Relation to Patient Empowerment and Digital Equity: Scoping Review
container-title: Online Journal of Public Health Informatics
21638a3b1d97502c2cea89d6c9b782a4ab8dc386.abstract: Abstract Background AI is increasingly embedded in health care and digital health applications, shaping clinical processes as well as how patients access information and participate in care. Research on bias in medical AI has largely focused on technical and performance-related disparities. Less attention has been paid to how such biases may affect patients’ access, understanding, trust, and opportunities for meaningful involvement in care. Objective This scoping review aimed to map how studies of bias in medical AI describe patient-related consequences relevant to patient empowerment and the digital divide and to identify gaps across technical, social, structural, and patient-centered perspectives. Methods This scoping review followed JBI (Joanna Briggs Institute) methodology and PRISMA-ScR (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews) reporting guidance. PubMed/MEDLINE and EBSCOHost databases were searched in August 2025 and supplemented by Google Scholar searches. Peer-reviewed studies published from 2015 onward were included if they addressed bias in medical AI and described patient-related consequences relevant to patient empowerment or digital inequality. Data charting focused on AI application types, bias dimensions, patient empowerment domains, digital divide–related factors, intersectionality, and debiasing strategies. Findings were synthesized descriptively and thematically. Results The search identified 497 records, of which 22 studies met the inclusion criteria. Bias was represented as a multidimensional sociotechnical phenomenon, with social bias identified most frequently (21/22 studies), followed by algorithmic bias (16/22 studies), structural bias (14/22 studies), and design-related bias (12/22 studies). Patient empowerment was most frequently addressed through involvement in care (n=13), followed by health literacy (n=9) and trust and assurance (n=7), whereas broader psychosocial and everyday-life domains were addressed less frequently. Digital divide–related factors were identified in 19 of the 22 studies, with digital literacy and usability barriers reported most frequently. Seven studies considered 2 or more social or structural dimensions of disadvantage. Although many studies discussed approaches that could mitigate bias-related barriers, explicit empirical evaluation of debiasing strategies in relation to patient empowerment or digital equity was largely absent. Conclusions Patient-related consequences of bias in medical AI extend beyond algorithmic performance and are reflected in access, understanding, trust, and involvement in care. Broader empowerment dimensions, multidimensional disadvantage, and empirically evaluated mitigation strategies remain comparatively underexplored.

title: Variational quantum principal component analysis for Hilbert space Gaussian process regression
container-title: Machine Learning: Science and Technology
348a6fbc0e7c584da93b161a1951487ed55d7744.abstract: Abstract Gaussian processes (GPs) are widely used probabilistic models for regression and classification tasks. Their flexibility and ability to quantify uncertainties make them well-suited for many applications. However, their applicability to large datasets is limited by the cubic computational time complexity. While reduced-rank methods such as Hilbert space approximations reduce this complexity, scaling to very large datasets remains challenging. Quantum algorithms are promising candidates to further accelerate such computations. Quantum principal component analysis (QPCA) has previously been applied to Hilbert space GP (HSGP) regression to address this scaling limitation. However, its applicability is limited by the requirement for fault-tolerant quantum hardware. In this work, we present a hybrid quantum–classical model for reduced-rank GP regression, where we apply a QPCA algorithm based on parameterized quantum circuits to HSGP regression. In noiseless simulations on a one-dimensional test function, the resulting model reaches a regression accuracy comparable to that of the exact GP and the classical HSGP. The framework uses shallow parameterized circuits and does not require fault-tolerant quantum hardware, which makes it a candidate for noisy intermediate-scale quantum devices.

title: High-fidelity 3D geometric reconstruction of pelvic organs from MRI: a hybrid deep learning and iterative optimization approach
container-title: Physics in Medicine & Biology
cf60997a7e61aab88382a6093fb364bc0edfd58e.abstract: Abstract Objective. The generation of high-fidelity, high-quality three-dimensional pelvic organ geometries from magnetic resonance imaging-derived segmentation masks remains challenging. This study aimed to develop and evaluate a hybrid framework for reconstructing the bladder, uterus, and rectum, and to assess its geometric fidelity, mesh-quality proxy performance, and reconstruction efficiency. Approach. We developed a hybrid deformable shape modeling framework that integrates deep learning (DL) prediction with iterative optimization for the reconstruction of the bladder, uterus, and rectum. The framework consists of three core components: (1) a geometry-aware multi-level DL architecture that preserves topological consistency of pelvic organs; (2) a two-stage amortized optimization training strategy that balances global shape capture and local surface refinement; and (3) a holistic synergy mechanism—where iterative optimization provides supervision for DL during the training phase, and during inference, DL rapidly predicts the global organ morphology, followed by iterative optimization to refine local surfaces and mesh quality. Main results. Before iterative refinement, the proposed model outperformed representative DL-based reconstruction methods in geometric fidelity, achieving Chamfer distance/dice similarity coefficient values of 5.5 × 10 −3 /0.788 for the bladder, 3.7 × 10 −3 /0.839 for the rectum, and 4.2 × 10 −3 /0.900 for the uterus. DL -based initialization enabled the complete hybrid framework to converge within approximately 100 iterations, with a reconstruction time of approximately 35 s per organ on a CPU and 1.5 s on a GPU. At the patient level, the mean minSICN and minSIGE values of the 10 worst volumetric elements were 0.0807 and 0.0844, respectively, exceeding those achieved by traditional geometric post-processing methods. Significance. The proposed framework connects image-domain segmentation with structural-domain applications by efficiently generating high-fidelity, high-quality pelvic organ geometries with improved mesh-quality proxy performance. These geometries may support statistical shape assessment and may provide candidate surface representations for subsequent volumetric meshing and solver-specific biomechanical validation.
