title: Digital Echo Chambers and Ethnocentric Tourism Behavior
container-title: Ethnocentrism and its Impact on Tourism Outcomes
c33276cb72948ffaefa3d641f5f2696ebee9cea1.abstract: In the digitized world of globalization, tourist selection has become a profound communicative and psychological phenomenon. This chapter investigates the critical role of social media communication in mediating the relationship between ethnocentrism—a cognitive filter where travelers decode destination messages through the lens of their own cultural superiority and the formation of destination advocacy. Literature-based thematic content analysis examines how digital narratives can either reinforce ethnocentric biases through algorithmic echo chambers or, conversely, provide the necessary storytelling tools to convert biased visitors into “Destination Evangelists.” By integrating Social Identity Theory, the Narrative Paradigm, and Cognitive Dissonance Resolution, the chapter identifies the mechanisms through which digital messages shape destination perception long before physical arrival occurs. The findings offer a novel “Intercultural Branding” model, serving as a strategic roadmap for destination marketers to neutralize ethnocentric barriers and foster sustainable tourism outcomes

title: Moderating Effects of Ethnocentrism and Digital Literacy on Iranian Consumers' Purchase Intention Toward Medical Tourism Services in Türkiye
container-title: Ethnocentrism and its Impact on Tourism Outcomes
c7f8bdcf40739a6490b6e1edfbfa5d83b1d41668.abstract: Medical tourism has become an increasingly important segment of the global healthcare industry, intensifying competition among destination countries. This study investigates the effects of country awareness, country image, and price perception on Iranian consumers' purchase intentions for medical tourism services in Türkiye while examining the moderating roles of digital literacy and consumer ethnocentrism. Drawing on Customer-Based Brand Equity (CBBE) theory and the Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB), this study proposes an integrated framework explaining how destination-related evaluations shape behavioral intentions in the context of cross-border healthcare. Data were collected through an online survey of 254 Iranian consumers and analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM). The findings revealed that the three main constructs had significant positive effects on purchase intention. In contrast, digital literacy and consumer ethnocentrism did not significantly moderate these relationships.

title: Digital Transformation and the Techno-Regulatory Interface
container-title: International Perspectives on Tax Policy and Accounting Practices
02b4a07a6af152d2b2290f77a4a5a4cc51411567.abstract: Digital transformation is fundamentally changing the way taxation and accounting are performed in today's data-driven economy. The rapid adoption of Artificial Intelligence (AI), blockchain, and cloud computing has enabled governments, businesses, and regulatory institutions to improve financial transparency, automate compliance processes, strengthen decision-making, and enhance the efficiency of tax administration and accounting systems. These technologies are reshaping traditional financial practices by creating intelligent, secure, and interconnected digital ecosystems that support real-time information processing and evidence-based governance.

title: Data-Driven Digital Marketing Framework Based on Customer Acquisition for the 3D Printing Industry: A Case Study of Tridiku Teknokarya Indonesia
container-title: Jurnal Ilmiah Accusi
fcccdcfc43d12e47c96a02e0e63f2a04340f10fd.abstract: The 3D printing industry in Indonesia is growing rapidly, yet many SMEs in this sector still run their marketing without leveraging the customer data they already collect. Existing SME digital marketing research remains generic and does not account for the specific attributes of the 3D printing sector, including material diversification, duration-based pricing, and pronounced segment heterogeneity, leaving a significant research gap. This study fills this gap by developing a data driven digital marketing framework based on customer acquisition, consisting of five stages: data collection, segmentation, customer value analysis, strategy selection, and digital marketing execution with content strategy. The framework was validated through a case study at Tridiku Teknokarya Indonesia, a medium scale 3D printing company with 1,484 orders and 401 unique customers from July to December 2025, analyzed via mixed methods combining descriptive statistics with cross tabulation. The novelty lies in five elements: integration of material dimensions and duration-based pricing, use of real transaction data, linking behavior patterns to content strategy, discovery of a custom order effect (80.5% versus 49.5% deal rate), and identification of a revenue concentration paradox (4.9% of orders generating 52.7% of revenue). Theoretically, the study connects purchase intention theory with 3D printing practice through the custom order effect and extends customer profitability distribution theory through the revenue concentration paradox. Managerially, the study recommends structured quotation forms to raise deal rates, budget allocation by segment profitability rather than volume, data driven upsell pathways, and a six phases campaign calendar synchronized with seasonal patterns to help SMEs shift from intuition based to evidence-based marketing

title: The ‘Digital Agenda’—The Right of Reproduction in the Digital Environment
container-title: The Law of Copyright and the WIPO Internet Treaties
788a9d235a00c9db2f64c4ec9640a5160258e94d.abstract: Abstract Chapters 3 to 6 are on the key issues of the ‘digital agenda’ of the preparatory work of the WCT and the WPPT and the 1996 Diplomatic Conference. In Chapter 3, it is described, that, until the 1967 Stockholm Act of the Berne Convention, the right of reproduction had been just an implied right; that, since the Stockholm Act, it applies to reproduction ‘in any manner or form’; that—unless exceptions or limitations are allowed under the three-step test—it also covers private copying; that, in the Rome Convention, it is stated that both direct and indirect acts of reproduction are covered; and that a WIPO-UNESCO resolution clarified already in 1982 that the inclusion of works in an electronic memory is also reproduction. The preparatory work and the adoption of the provisions of the WCT and the WPPT on the right of reproduction are described, and it is discussed how it has been confirmed in an agreed statement that the inclusion of works in electronic memories is reproduction.

title: The ‘Digital Agenda’—The Right of Interactive Making Available to the Public (and the Right of Distribution): The ‘Umbrella Solution’
container-title: The Law of Copyright and the WIPO Internet Treaties
6d6f272910aa52aaac452d78bc8f2f90d5723c61.abstract: Abstract Very early in the preparatory work, it was agreed, in general, that the act of inclusion of a work on the internet should be covered both by the right of reproduction and another exclusive right to authorize making it available to the public, but the delegations disagreed which right might be applied. It is reviewed how the two rights having emerged as candidates—the right of communication to the public and the right of distribution—had been regulated in the WIPO-administered treaties, and how the ‘umbrella solution’ worked out by the WIPO Secretariat eliminated the deadlock in the negotiations, by proposing an exclusive right to authorize any act of interactive making available to the public. It is noted that, while in the WPPT it is a separate right, in the WCT it is provided together with the right of non-interactive communication to the public (which has led to interpretation problems).

title: The ‘Digital Agenda’—Exceptions and Limitations in the Digital Online Environment
container-title: The Law of Copyright and the WIPO Internet Treaties
97057e051474b469c454b9dc138fef0c08686dc7.abstract: Abstract It is clarified that ‘exceptions’ are free uses without the obligation to pay remuneration, and ‘limitations’ mean that although the rights (in general, exclusive rights) are limited in some way (in particular, exclusive rights to rights to remuneration or in the form of a compulsory licence), they still apply. The exceptions and limitations specifically provided in the WIPO-administered treaties are reviewed, as well as the provisions on the three-step test (how it has been adopted in Article 9(2) of the Berne Convention concerning the right of reproduction, how it has been extended to any copyright exceptions and limitations by Article 13 of the TRIPS Agreement). The preparatory work and the negotiations at the 1996 Diplomatic Conference are described: how they have led to the extension of the three-step not only to copyright in the WCT but also to the rights of performers and producers of phonograms in the WPPT, and how it has been clarified that the exceptions and limitations may be extended to the online digital environment.

title: The ‘Digital Agenda’—Technological Protection Measures and Rights Management Information
container-title: The Law of Copyright and the WIPO Internet Treaties
b724a6edf7a9f4cb84b5b592c11a5f11e847c9d9.abstract: Abstract With the advent of online digital technologies, the view emerged that it would be impossible to exercise and enforce copyright in the new environment, because the rightholders would not be able to control the use of their works uploaded on the internet. It was in response to this opinion that the solution—expressed by the saying ‘the answer to the machine’—was proposed to use the same technology in order to preserve control by the rightholders in the form of digital rights management; that is, the combination of technical protection measures (TPMs) and rights management information (RMI). It was raised against the idea that an ‘access right’ might be granted in this way, which was rebutted by pointing out that there had always been some means to control access to works (otherwise they would have been freely available). It has been agreed upon that it should be left to the rightholders whether or not they apply digital rights management; and that the Treaties should just prohibit the unauthorized circumvention of TPMs and the removal or alteration of RMI.

title: The Effect of Fintech Adoption and Digital Accounting on The Financial Sustainability Of MSMES in Medan City
container-title: Jurnal Ilmiah Accusi
86f867f64205353d863ef6a73aa3efe8ab889699.abstract: This study examines the effect of Fintech Adoption and Digital Accounting on the Financial Sustainability of micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs) in Medan City. An associative quantitative design was applied to a survey of 120 MSME owners and managers in the culinary, fashion, retail trade, and service sectors, selected through purposive sampling. Data were collected with a five-point Likert-scale questionnaire and analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) in SmartPLS 4. The measurement model met all validity and reliability criteria. Fintech Adoption had a positive and significant effect on Financial Sustainability (β = 0.412; t = 4.873; p < 0.001), and Digital Accounting also had a positive and significant effect (β = 0.358; t = 4.126; p < 0.001). Together, the two variables explained 43.4% of the variance in Financial Sustainability, with medium effect sizes (f² = 0.236 and 0.178, respectively). The findings suggest that digital financial services and digital bookkeeping reinforce MSME financial sustainability, so support programs in Medan should promote both together rather than treating them as separate agendas

title: Banking Risk Management in the Digital Era: A Systematic Literature Review
container-title: Jurnal Ilmiah Accusi
aa43112f086ecaec687a37ad1b6c2aa981b81f5f.abstract: Digital technologies are changing how banks originate, monitor and transmit risk, yet the empirical evidence on whether they make banks safer is scattered across risk types, technologies and institutional settings. This article reports a systematic review, conducted under PRISMA 2020, of empirical studies on the relationship between digital technologies and bank risk or risk management. A Scopus search of English-language journal articles published in 2020–2026 returned 857 records. Title and abstract screening and eligibility assessment left 85 eligible studies, from which 28 were selected purposively to maximise variation in risk type, region and research design. Twenty-two of the 28 use archival bank-level panels, four rely on manager surveys, one is a country-level cross-section and one analyses central bank data descriptively. Half of the studies come from China. The synthesis points to three results. First, digitalization more often lowers than raises credit, operational, market and overall risk: among the 21 archival studies with a direct risk outcome, 12 report reductions, 4 report increases and 5 report mixed or non-linear effects. Second, bank-level and system-level results diverge, because the same technologies that reduce idiosyncratic risk can raise interconnectedness and contagion. Third, internal control, model governance, cybersecurity, regulation, and bank size and ownership repeatedly condition the outcome. Drawing on contingency theory and the resource-based view, the article proposes a Digital Risk Governance Framework and five propositions for future research. The evidence base is geographically narrow and relies mostly on adoption proxies, which limits generalisation beyond large emerging-market banking systems

title: Authenticity of the Masked Body—the Bear Dance in Present Day Digital Performance
container-title: Martor. The Museum of the Romanian Peasant Anthropology Review
cf73c5037b63969d3068407a060c1e0ab5a03369.abstract: This article examines the transformation of authenticity seen within the contemporary performance of the Romanian Bear Dance by focusing on the group Ursul lui Gavrilă din Asău, selected because of the unique features it has added to the performance. Exploring a corpus of 100 Facebook posts collected between 2023 and 2026, the approach combines digital ethnography with discourse analysis to explore how authenticity is constructed in mediated contexts. The analysis reveals the displacement of authenticity from material practice to discursive and relational processes. While the masked body remains visually central, it no longer functions as the primary source of authenticity. Instead, authenticity emerges through an intricate combination of audience engagement, narrative continuity, and affective investment. Comments, reactions, and patterns of circulation demonstrate that authenticity is co-produced through interaction and recognition rather than embedded in the inherited ritual form. By highlighting the role of digital mediation, the article argues that authenticity operates as a dynamic and distributed effect, shaped by visibility, participation, and the ongoing negotiation of meaning across diverse audiences whatever the degree of conformity or lack of to the ethnographically described form of the performance.

title: Masking Emotions. Fostering Connection Through Performative Art in the Digital Space. An Interview with Yuliya Tsukerman, Puppeteer and Mask Maker
container-title: Martor. The Museum of the Romanian Peasant Anthropology Review
46d3e72c9f00494d73d83c2236ecfa3902b51176.abstract: This interview focuses on the work of Yuliya Tsukerman, a puppeteer and mask maker working in theatre and film, and based in Brooklyn, New York. Her project, Transmissions from the Ancient Forest, is a series of video poems in which a community of lesser gods tries to make sense of human suffering. We discuss the mask-making process, the characters’ emotions, and how these are perceived by online audiences. Her work has been supported by the Jim Henson Foundation, St. Ann’s Warehouse, Franklin Furnace, the Jerome Foundation, Clubbed Thumb, Folly Tree Arboretum, the NYFA Playwriting/ Screenwriting Grant, Loghaven, Mana Contemporary, and the Lower Manhattan Cultural Council.

title: Industry 4.0 and the Future of Digital Strategy: Pathways to Digital Value Creation
container-title: AI-Driven Transformation in Education and Business
218150914ff06798dd0fe2d20c483286c0ae044d.abstract: Abstract The acceptance and addition of such progressive digital technologies into operational processes and decision-making platforms have totally redefined how businesses conceptualize strategy in Industry 4.0. This chapter explores how digital value creation (DVC), as a process, has been facilitated through Industry 4.0 technology, with digital strategy orientation (DSO) as the intermediary. For instance, employing a quantitative research strategy that focuses on theoretical constructs, the chapter integrates theories from dynamic capability theory, the resource-based view (RBV) and IT business value theory to explain how businesses achieve strategic and performance outcomes from their digital investments. Data collection entailed conducting surveys among managers whose business entities adopted Industry 4.0 technology. The examples given for Industry 4.0 technology were Internet of Things technology, artificial intelligence technology, analytics technology, automation technology and cyber-physical system technology. This chapter empirically explores Industry 4.0 technology and DVC and how Industry 4.0 technology influences DSO through structural equation modelling techniques. The results show that Industry 4.0 technology affects DVC both directly and through DSO. Digital strategy is an integral part of any business through which technology capabilities are actually linked with overall business goals. Organizations primarily benefit from the outcomes of a digital strategy by making their operations more efficient, starting new creative activities and gaining a competitive advantage in Industry 4.0. The findings quite clearly bring out that firms focusing on digital strategy are better positioned to achieve long-term value from their Industry 4.0 investments.

title: Experimental feasibility study of proton therapy range verification by a digital tracking calorimeter prototype
container-title: Physics in Medicine & Biology
424bd61cb0f0a97ea8899d8c947903bdf772eefb.abstract: Abstract Objective. Uncertainties in the proton range remain an important challenge in proton therapy. In-situ range verification (RV) techniques can be used to ensure the Bragg peak depth in the patient matches the treatment plan. Various such methods are under investigation, utilizing the signal from secondary radiation caused by proton interactions with the patient. This study experimentally investigates the feasibility of using a silicon-pixel-based sampling calorimeter for RV through the detection of secondary photons and neutrons. Approach. The proton RV capability of a sampling calorimeter based on monolithic active pixel sensors was tested both theoretically and experimentally. We theoretically investigate the plausibility of the planned sampling calorimeter to pick up a signal from the neutral secondary particles distal to the patient. Then, a smaller prototype pixel telescope was constructed to verify our theoretical findings experimentally by placing it behind a water tank irradiated by a medical proton beam with various energies in the range of 100–200 MeV at the Danish Center for Particle Therapy, Aarhus, Denmark. Main results. We find that the aluminum used as absorbers between sensitive layers in the calorimeter serves as a converter for prompt gammas and neutrons. The combined detection efficiency ranges between 5.8 ⋅ 10 − 5 and 2.7 ⋅ 10 − 3 detector hits per primary proton for beam energies between 50 and 200 MeV. Irradiation of the water phantom leads to a signal in our detector, which is well-correlated with the nominal beam energy. A simulation-based model using only the number of hits per proton can predict the beam energy, acting as a proxy for proton range in a homogeneous target, down to a root mean squared error of 1.34 MeV. Significance. This study marks a promising step towards utilizing a tracking calorimeter designed for proton computed tomography for the secondary application of proton therapy RV without additional hardware costs.

title:
ST-M
                    <sup>2</sup>
                    EDA: spatio-temporal metric-guided multi-stream expert domain adaptation network for fatigue monitoring
container-title: Biomedical Physics & Engineering Express
b8ba54bf8cd9c287c5ab3215e368ca802f3cf54c.abstract: Abstract In the human-machine collaboration paradigms of Industry 5.0, the intrinsic non-stationarity and domain drift of electroencephalogram signals pose significant challenges to fatigue monitoring. Consequently, achieving accurate and robust cross-subject fatigue detection is paramount for workplace safety. This paper proposes a Spatio-Temporal Metric-Guided Multi-Stream Expert Domain Adaptation Network. The framework initially employs Singular Value Decomposition-based signal reconstruction to attenuate non-stationary noise, followed by Mixup data augmentation to enhance and smooth the feature space distribution. Furthermore, a hybrid architecture integrating Domain-Specific Batch Normalization with a ResNet-Transformer backbone is constructed to precisely decouple statistical discrepancies between domains. Finally, Multi-Kernel Maximum Mean Discrepancy is introduced as a dynamic routing criterion to facilitate fine-grained, adaptive decision-making for target samples. The baseline experiments on the SEED-VIG dataset yield a subject-wise mean accuracy of 90.54% across all 23 subjects, including S15. Visual analysis of brain topography confirms that the model successfully aligns distributional shifts caused by individual heterogeneity—specifically correcting for specific frontotemporal lobe activation observed in subject S7—and establishes distinct decision boundaries. These findings indicate that synergizing signal reconstruction with Spatio-Temporal metric-guided multi-stream experts effectively mitigates negative transfer, ensuring reliable fatigue detection in complex cross-subject tasks.

title: A novel digital image colorimetric analysis system with adaptive sensitivity and measuring range
container-title: Measurement Science and Technology
bad0cde73039cb34ffb51df17054df9e7529aff5.abstract: Abstract In this study, we aimed at developing an innovative digital image colorimetry (DIC) system, designated CAS- t , which integrates advanced hardware and software components. The CAS- t platform includes a fully enclosed illumination chamber with uniform Light-emitting diode lighting diffused by a polyethylene material, a camera positioned 25 cm above a 96-well microplate with an additional lens to reduce lateral distortion, and an adjustable exposure time to optimize performance. An image-processing algorithm within a Python workflow detects circular wells in a microplate, applies median filtering, and extracts Red, Green, and Blue intensities analyzed via principal component analysis. The experimental results obtained from phenol red (PR) and indigo carmine (IC) indicators demonstrated that exposure time significantly influences the sensitivity and measurable concentration ranges, thereby allowing tunable detection parameters. For IC, increasing exposure time from 1 to 5 ms increased the slope magnitude from −0.014 to −0.027 µM −1 , whereas PR showed the opposite trend. Compared with the reflected-light systems and smartphone cameras, CAS- t achieved approximately two-fold higher sensitivity (−27.0 versus −14.0 µM −1 ) and markedly improved precision (RSD: 5.75% versus 25.39%). As a proof concept, Fe(II) content in a pharmaceutical sample was quantified by performing CAS- t system calibrated using standard solutions (0.1–5.0 mg l −1 ) of Fe(II) versus PC1 as the most sensitive and linear color channel ( R 2 = 0.999). Validation against the reference UV–vis spectrometer showed strong statistical agreement at 95% confidence ( p > 0.05), confirming the reliability of the 7 ms as optimal exposure time chosen based on sensitivity and linearity analyses. Consequently, this integrated hardware-software approach offers a standardized framework for DIC assays with broad adaptability across diverse chemical and biochemical applications.

title: Promoting Foreign Language Learner Autonomy through Digital Resources
container-title: Fuentes Humanísticas
d816cf97124920c2c06a7eaa62aa2d7d4a8c11bf.abstract: Este trabajo analiza el impacto de los recursos digitales en el desarrollo de la autonomía, el aprendizaje autodirigido y la reflexión metacognitiva en estudiantes de lenguas extranjeras. Para ello, examina dos proyectos académicos: un e-book bilingüe (español-francés) integrado a la plataforma DEDALES-México —que incluye audios y ocho capítulos sobre la cultura, personajes y movimientos sociales de París para fomentar la lectura autónoma— y el proyecto piloto TELETANDEM, orientado al intercambio lingüístico y cultural en línea con hablantes nativos. A través de la discusión de ambas iniciativas, el estudio aborda las implicaciones pedagógicas, los desafíos y las oportunidades que ofrece la tecnología para capacitar a los aprendientes en la toma de decisiones y la gestión de su propio proceso de aprendizaje.

title: A digital twin of the heat supply network in managing domestic energy demand
container-title: Mining Industry Journal (Gornaya Promyshlennost)
fc5ff7347f8931e7f44968a13878196b27ac37e7.abstract: With its production of 440 million metric tons and exports of 211.2 million metric tons in 2025, Russia’s coal industry remains unprofitable; therefore, stability of the domestic demand for thermal coal is of critical importance. This article presents a quantitative assessment of the thermal component in the domestic coal market, as well as a systematic error of the current normative method for planning fuel requirements for heat supply, and the economic benefits of transitioning to adaptive forecasting of heat consumption based on a digital twin of the heating network and AI-simulated climate scenarios. Based on the assessment results, the domestic heat demand amounted to 30.2 million metric tons of coal equivalent, or 50.2 million metric tons of natural coal, which corresponds to 28.2% of the domestic market and 11.3% of the annual production. The weather-related variation in coal demand was calculated to be 2.4 million metric tons with a standard deviation, which is comparable to the effects of the price and logistical factors. It was found that the current normative planning method systematically overestimates the calculated load. The average absolute percentage error of the normative method was 8.2%, compared to 4.3% for the inertial method. Transition to adaptive forecasting based on a digital twin of the heating network will reduce the planning error by at least twofold and will provide savings in the heating fuel costs of approximately 3–6%. The results obtained are applicable at three levels: (1) for heat supply organizations; (2) for coal mining companies; (3) for regulatory authorities. Further research will focus on verifying the model coefficients using data from the system’s pilot operation, expanding the analysis to the municipal level, where climatic variations within a region are most pronounce, and with account of scenarios for provision of natural gas supply to coal-mining regions.

title: OSIRA, an AI Early Warning System Using Open Source Intelligence for Digital Fraud Prevention
container-title: Jurnal Teknika dan Informatika (JTI)
e11b2e99293184c34c74168bfca20102846b4736.abstract: Purpose: This study designs and evaluates OSIRA (Open Source Intelligence Risk Analyzer), an early warning system based on artificial intelligence that integrates Open Source Intelligence (OSINT) and Natural Language Processing (NLP) to identify digital fraud indications before they enter formal reporting mechanisms in a cashless society. Research Methodology: The study uses a design science approach consisting of problem analysis, system design, risk score formulation, and a limited scale proof of concept simulation. The simulation used 540 synthetic texts from 50 template groups, divided into 394 training and 146 testing texts through a group based split, and classified them with Term Frequency–Inverse Document Frequency (TF IDF) features and logistic regression. Results: OSIRA integrates web crawling, text preprocessing, fraud classification, entity extraction, a risk engine, and an early warning module. At a threshold of 0.50, the model achieved 82.88% accuracy, 79.66% precision, 98.95% recall, an F1 score of 88.26%, and a ROC AUC of 0.8528, but its false positive rate reached 47.06%, mainly for normal texts discussing fraud related topics. Conclusions: OSIRA shows initial feasibility as an additional intelligence layer that can shift fraud mitigation from reactive response toward proactive fraud intelligence. Limitations: The evaluation used synthetic rather than real OSINT data, a baseline classifier with limited contextual understanding, and risk score weights and thresholds that have not been empirically calibrated. Contributions: The study offers a conceptual and technical framework for using pre reporting public signals in fraud risk management and provides guidance for banks, digital wallet providers, and regulators.

title: Translocal identity work in virtual international assignments: digital diplomacy, psychological safety and cross-cultural trust
container-title: Journal of Global Mobility
9fc6edc520af2d7a905d0083ea1ff80233771464.abstract: Purpose Despite the growing reliance on virtual international assignments in multinational corporations, how professionals negotiate professional legitimacy, belonging and cross-cultural trust within formal international assignment roles without physical relocation remains insufficiently understood. Grounded in Identity Work Theory, this study examines these efforts as translocal identity work in the absence of the spatial and cultural immersion that characterizes traditional expatriation. Design/methodology/approach A qualitative multiple case study was conducted across three multinational corporations in three sectors (technology, consulting, manufacturing). Thirty semi-structured interviews were carried out with virtual assignees, defined as employees formally assigned to manage cross-border responsibilities from their home base without planned relocation. The interviews were analyzed using a team-based thematic approach, with visual network elicitation used to prompt discussion of assignment-related relationships. Findings Three interrelated themes illuminate translocal identity work: (1) translocal professionalism, capturing the global professional identity and belonging virtual assignees sought to sustain while remaining locally based; (2) digital diplomacy, involving deliberate relational labor to build and sustain cross-cultural trust through digital channels and (3) perceived psychologically safe inclusion, capturing leadership-mediated conditions supporting or constraining open voice and authentic participation. Participants' accounts suggest that symbolic and social proximity can support professional legitimacy and belonging without relocation. However, persistent marginality and relational strain indicate that these efforts remain contingent on organizational and leadership support. Originality/value The study introduces translocal identity work as an empirically grounded concept that contributes to global mobility research by examining the gap between holding a formal international assignment mandate and experiencing recognition as a legitimate cross-border actor. Drawing on Identity Work Theory, it explains how virtual assignees seek professional legitimacy and belonging through digital presence management and relational practices under varying conditions of perceived psychological safety. Rather than demonstrating that symbolic proximity substitutes for physical relocation, the findings identify reported circumstances in which these efforts support recognition or remain fragile. They also suggest context-sensitive implications for supporting the identity and relational work involved in virtual international assignments.

title: Kepemimpinan yang Melihat Wajah: Etika Levinasian sebagai Paradigma Teologis bagi Pemimpin Gereja Indonesia dalam Menghadapi Ketidakadilan Gender dan Intoleransi di Ruang Digital
container-title: KINAA: Jurnal Teologi
9a7665f4d415c5c7aa90f1e219e041368fc9fdd2.abstract: Gender injustice and religious intolerance remain persistent challenges in Indonesian society, and church leaders are increasingly called to respond prophetically within digital spaces. This article aims to construct a theological paradigm for Indonesian church leadership grounded in Emmanuel Levinas's ethics of the face. This study employs a critical literature review with a Levinasian ethical phenomenology approach, analyzing Levinas's texts, Galatians 3:28, and Indonesian literature on gender, patriarchy, and digital culture. The analysis proceeds through four steps of ethical hermeneutics: identification of the face, analysis of the ethical demand, critique of totalization, and construction of praxis. The findings indicate that Levinasian ethics—centered on the face of the Other, asymmetrical responsibility, and substitution—provides a robust theological foundation for leadership that prioritizes the vulnerable, resists patriarchal and intolerant structures, and engages digital spaces as sites of ethical encounter. The article concludes that "leadership that sees the face" is both a spiritual vocation and a moral imperative, requiring advocacy for gender justice, interfaith dialogue, and ethical digital engagement. The study's contribution is to offer a new methodological framework—Levinasian Ethical Hermeneutics—that integrates Levinasian philosophy, gender justice, and digital theology in the context of Indonesian church leadership. Ketidakadilan gender dan intoleransi keagamaan tetap menjadi tantangan yang gigih di masyarakat Indonesia, dan para pemimpin gereja semakin dipanggil untuk merespons secara profetik di ruang digital. Artikel ini bertujuan untuk membangun paradigma teologis bagi kepemimpinan gereja Indonesia yang berlandaskan etika wajah Emmanuel Levinas. Penelitian ini menggunakan studi pustaka kritis dengan pendekatan fenomenologi etis Levinasian, yang menganalisis teks-teks Levinas, Galatia 3:28, dan literatur Indonesia tentang gender, patriarki, dan digital. Analisis dilakukan melalui empat langkah hermeneutik etis: identifikasi wajah, analisis tuntutan etis, kritik totalisasi, dan konstruksi praksis. Temuan menunjukkan bahwa etika Levinasian—yang berpusat pada wajah Yang Lain, tanggung jawab asimetris, dan substitusi—menyediakan fondasi teologis yang kokoh bagi kepemimpinan yang memprioritaskan yang rentan, menolak struktur patriarkal dan intoleran, serta melibatkan ruang digital sebagai tempat perjumpaan etis. Artikel ini menyimpulkan bahwa "kepemimpinan yang melihat wajah" adalah panggilan spiritual sekaligus imperatif moral yang menuntut advokasi keadilan gender, dialog antaragama, dan keterlibatan digital yang etis. Kontribusi studi ini adalah menawarkan kerangka metodologis baru—Hermeneutik Etis Levinasian—yang mengintegrasikan filsafat Levinas, keadilan gender, dan teologi digital dalam konteks kepemimpinan gereja Indonesia.

title: Test-retest reliability, known-groups validity and convergence validity of nocturnal awakening digital endpoints in axial spondyloarthritis
container-title: Digital Biomarkers
f3157f14dc548f98800e371373d7ca2c9c557e9b.abstract: Abstract Background: People with axial spondyloarthritis often experience back pain and stiffness, which worsen with rest and cause nocturnal awakenings. Wrist actigraphy can evaluate these awakenings, but data on the psychometric properties of these digital health technology (DHT) derived measures are limited. These properties are essential for their use in clinical trials. This study aims to evaluate the test-retest reliability, known-groups validity, and convergence validity of DHT-derived measures of nocturnal awakening in people with axial spondyloarthritis, through data collected as part of the INVIGORATE-1 phase 3 clinical trial. Methods: Participants in the trial wore the ActiGraph CentrePoint Insight Watch (CPIW) on their non-dominant wrist for 24 hours a day for up to 28 days during screening window. Three measures of nocturnal awakening were derived: wake after sleep onset (WASO), number of awakenings (NAWAKE) and average length of awakenings (AVGWAKE). Disease activity (ASDAS-CRP) and patient-reported outcomes were also evaluated. Test-retest reliability was assessed using the intra-class correlation coefficient (ICC) and minimal detectable change (MDC) across the two consecutive baseline weeks prior to the end of the screening window. Correlations between nocturnal awakening measures and clinical data were evaluated using the Pearson correlation coefficient. Known-groups validity was assessed by comparing nocturnal awakening between groups with different disease activity levels. Results: Of 526 participants, 447 met the criteria for valid actigraphy data. The three measures of nocturnal awakening showed good test-retest reliability (ICC = 0.75-0.81). MDC values were 36.62 min (WASO), 8.59 awakenings (NAWAKE) and 1.55 min (AVGWAKE). Weak correlations were observed between the nocturnal awakening measures and clinical data, with the strongest correlation between ASDAS-CRP and WASO (r = 0.29). Nocturnal awakening was worse in participants with very high disease activity compared to that in participants with moderate to high disease activity. Conclusions: Actigraphy-based measures of nocturnal awakening have good test-retest reliability and can discriminate between different levels of disease activity. These measures may be sensitive to changes in disease activity, but further research is needed to establish their interventional sensitivity. These findings provide crucial psychometric validation data for DHT-derived measures of nocturnal awakening in the rheumatological disease context.
