title: Fan engagement beyond game outcomes: evidence from collective rituals and athlete-idolizing fandom in the digital sportscape
container-title: International Journal of Sports Marketing and Sponsorship
09b10d44fb88ab442b50c48c2244a822e087258a.abstract: Purpose Match outcomes are inherently uncertain and largely beyond the control of sport organizations; yet, defeats can negatively affect spectators’ emotions and subsequent behavioral intentions. This highlights the need to understand how sport organizations can sustain fan engagement through experiences that are not contingent on game outcomes. This study examines how outcome-independent forms of fan engagement – collective fan rituals and athlete-idolizing fandom activities – are associated with spectators’ word-of-mouth (WOM) and revisit intentions following match defeats in professional sport. Drawing on emotion regulation theory, the study focuses on experiential mechanisms that may sustain behavioral intentions beyond game outcomes. Design/methodology/approach Data were collected from 405 spectators who had recently attended a Korea Baseball Organization League match in which their supported team was defeated. Partial least squares structural equation modeling was used to test the proposed relationships. Multi-group analysis (MGA) compared spectators experiencing high versus low levels of post-match negative emotion. The model also includes team identification and objective team standing as control variables. Findings Satisfaction with collective fan rituals was positively associated with both WOM and revisit intention. Enjoyment of fandom activities positively influenced WOM but had no direct effect on revisit intention, indicating a fully mediated pathway through WOM. WOM was a significant predictor of revisit intention. MGA showed no significant differences between high- and low-negative-emotion groups, suggesting that the structural relationships are stable across emotional conditions. Objective team standing was not significantly related to WOM or revisit intention. Originality/value The findings indicate that participatory fan engagement can contribute to behavioral intentions following defeat through outcome-independent experiential pathways. Rather than being driven primarily by game results or season-level performance, fan behavioral continuity appears to be shaped by ritualized stadium experiences and digitally extended fandom activities, which operate through social diffusion via WOM. The study extends sport consumer behavior research by highlighting the role of experiential engagement and communication processes in sustaining attendance intentions in performance-volatile contexts.

title: Not passive sponges: When attention wanes, our brains are less synchronized with the environment
f7473977ec4a34b8dedb6c4470b752c5a3510de2.abstract: Without even being aware, humans are amazingly sensitive to the structures around them. Is this sensitivity constant or does it fluctuate along with our attentional states? To answer this foundational question, we deployed temporally sensitive measures that allow us to track neural entrainment—the synchronization of brain activity to environmental regularities—alongside fluctuations in attentional states. Participants (n = 78) viewed both random and structured visual streams while performing a task to index fluctuating attentional states. Structured streams evoked robust neural entrainment and reduced attentional lapses. Moreover, attentional states varied with neural entrainment. Across participants, those who displayed greater neural entrainment had reduced attentional lapses. And critically, even within individuals, greater entrainment was observed during periods of greater attentional focus. Our sensitivity to structure and attentional states are therefore inextricably linked: structures stabilize our attentional states and our sensitivity to structure dynamically mirrors the ebb and flow of human attention.

title: Peran Inklusi Keuangan dan Pembayaran Digital (QRIS) terhadap Kinerja Keuangan UMKM
container-title: PENG: Jurnal Ekonomi dan Manajemen
87a7cc4fd9429611ed281551c45d59d1850a103b.abstract: Micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs) play a major role in Indonesia’s economy, yet their financial performance is still constrained by limited access to financial services, low financial literacy, and suboptimal use of technology. This study aims to analyze the role of financial inclusion and digital payments through the Quick Response Code Indonesian Standard (QRIS) in MSME financial performance. A qualitative systematic literature review was conducted following the PRISMA 2020 guidelines. Secondary data were collected from journal articles, books, and official reports published between 2016 and 2026, then analyzed using content analysis and thematic synthesis. The findings indicate that financial inclusion and digital payments are generally positively associated with MSME financial performance through lower transaction costs, wider market reach and sales, and better access to financing. However, evidence on QRIS remains inconsistent because it is shaped by how performance is measured, the extent of service use, and business owners’ financial and digital literacy. Therefore, expanding access should be accompanied by stronger literacy and productive use of transaction data. Future research is encouraged to test these relationships empirically using primary data.

title: Modelling the associations between digital skills, psychological capital, dynamic capabilities and technostress among course tutors
container-title: Education + Training
5d4c2ffc73ffbb18d36d4c37674e84f274059885.abstract: Purpose This study investigated how digital skills influence technostress among course tutors, with particular attention to the mediating roles of dynamic capabilities and psychological capital. Design/methodology/approach An explanatory cross-sectional survey was employed, and 885 tutors from 48 College of Distance Education study centres were sampled. After confirming reliability, validity and minimal common-method bias, relationships were estimated with PLS-SEM (SmartPLS 4), including mediation tests and an importance–performance map analysis. Findings The study found that digital skills increase dynamic capabilities (β = 0.121, p &lt; 0.001) and psychological capital (β = 0.595, p &lt; 0.001) and directly lower technostress (β = −0.209, p &lt; 0.001). Dynamic capabilities (β = −0.153, p = 0.049) and psychological capital (β = −0.160, p = 0.001) further reduced technostress. The model accounted for 5.9% of the variance in dynamic capabilities, 35.4% in psychological capital and 13.1% in technostress. Indirect effects via psychological capital (β = −0.095, p &lt; 0.01) and dynamic capabilities (β = −0.019, p &lt; 0.05) were significant. Importance–performance map analysis highlighted psychological capital as the highest-leverage lever. Research limitations/implications The single-wave self-report design constrains causal inference; the single-institution sampling frame limits population generalisability; and the modest variance explained for dynamic capabilities (5.9%) and technostress (13.1%) leaves substantial residual heterogeneity unexplained. Future research should employ measurement drawn from multiple sources, longitudinal designs sampling tutors across at least three waves to permit panel analysis with lagged predictors, and replication across multiple institutions and cultural settings. Practical implications The study emphasise that institutions need to integrate continuous professional development that strengthens adaptive practices and builds psychological capital through mentoring, resilience workshops and reflective learning, supported by adequate technological infrastructure and responsive IT systems. Social implications Holistic development of digital and psychological resources can protect tutors' well-being, improve retention and service quality, and strengthen institutional adaptability amid ongoing digitalisation. Originality/value The study offered an integrated framework linking digital skills, dynamic capabilities, psychological capital and technostress, with large-sample evidence from a sub-Saharan higher-education context.

title: Costs and benefits of digital twin adoption in UK construction: a statistically tested stakeholder perception study
container-title: Engineering, Construction and Architectural Management
b8d72e1132678c81dadf3be8e04b23d107bee0c8.abstract: Purpose There is limited quantitative data on the weighting of costs and benefits of digital twin (DT) for stakeholders in the UK and this paper re-tests sub-group differences from a 2022 survey. Design/methodology/approach The 74 members of DTHub rated 15 benefits and 10 costs (scale of 0–4) and ranked both by Relative Importance Index (RII) (full sample) as well as two experience-based sub-samples (Group A n = 17; Group B n = 57). Corrected Mann-Whitney U and Kruskal-Wallis H tests were used to explore differences and Spearman correlations were used for rank agreement. Findings Operational benefits (Lean Construction, Effective Data Sharing, Improved Decision Making, Construction 4.0) topped net-zero and United Nations (UN) Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) benefits. Artificial Intelligence (AI) Components, Skilled Personnel and IoT Devices/Systems were the top-rated costs. There were no significant differences between sub-groups after correction (groups shared similar priorities of benefits, but not costs). Research limitations/implications Due to the small, self-selected sample (n = 74; Group A n = 17), this limits the power of the study and null results are not confirmatory. Larger replication (mixed methods) across contexts is recommended. Practical implications Operational benefits should be the main consideration for a new DT framework. For the dominant costs, coordinated investments between industry, government and education in AI, skills and IoT are needed; for the environmental-perception gap, evidence, not communication is needed. Originality/value One of the first construction DT RII studies to formally test differences in sub-group rank with dual correction, providing a tested baseline for research following Centre for Digital Built Britain and a transferable example of RII research.

title: Beyond competence: how organisational recognition and digital visibility shape women's leadership progression in project-based organisations
container-title: Engineering, Construction and Architectural Management
ef663e4072a8411033d854a1b83cadfa43a8133c.abstract: Purpose This study examines how organisational recognition and digital visibility shape women's leadership progression in project-based organisations. It moves beyond the view that leadership progression depends only on individual capability and explores how women's competencies are developed, made visible and recognised within gendered project environments. Design/methodology/approach A qualitative approach was used, based on semi-structured interviews with 23 women leaders working in project-based organisations across Australia. Participants were recruited through purposive and snowball sampling. Data were analysed using thematic analysis supported by NVivo, with social role theory guiding the interpretation of gendered expectations and recognition processes. Findings The findings show that women's leadership progression depends on the interaction between relational, strategic and execution-based competencies. Communication, stakeholder engagement, decision-making, risk awareness, problem-solving, planning, coordination and governance awareness helped women build trust, credibility and delivery capability. However, these competencies did not automatically translate into leadership progression. Organisational recognition was central to whether women's competencies were valued and translated into leadership opportunities. Gendered workplace norms often reduced the visibility of relational and coordination work by treating it as expected support work rather than leadership. Digital technologies supported competency visibility, flexibility, communication and evidence-based decision-making, but also created challenges through digital overload, limited training, workload pressure and reduced informal visibility. Research limitations/implications This study is based on a qualitative sample of 23 women leaders in Australia, and the findings reflect self-reported experiences within a cross-sectional design. Longitudinal and cross-cultural research would help clarify how leadership progression and organisational recognition evolve over time and across different national contexts. Practical implications Project-based organisations, particularly HR managers and project directors, need to move beyond competency development alone. Promotion criteria, project allocation and formal sponsorship should be designed to make women's leadership work visible and explicitly recognised, supported by deliberate use of digital tools and by monitoring invisible labour. Originality/value This study contributes to project leadership and gender research by shifting attention from competency possession to competency recognition. It develops a gender-responsive leadership progression framework that explains how leadership competencies are translated into women's leadership progression through competency visibility and organisational recognition and extends social role theory by identifying system-mediated visibility, recognition shaped by digital infrastructure rather than direct observation, as a second pathway through which gendered expectations operate.

title: Family coordination and digital transformation: resilience and post-COVID reinvention in Saudi micro and small family enterprises
container-title: Journal of Entrepreneurship in Emerging Economies
3ad466df0863a2b4f494703409578e1cfb2efa81.abstract: Purpose This study aims to explain how family-based coordination resources support post-crisis change by distinguishing organizational resilience from post-crisis reinvention. It tests whether family embeddedness, family labour reliance and informal family governance predict later resilience and whether digitalization strengthens the resilience−reinvention relationship in Saudi micro and small family enterprises. Design/methodology/approach A two-wave survey with an exact 70-day individual lag produced an analytic sample of 318 firms. Time 1 measured family resources, digitalization, COVID shock severity and baseline outcomes; Time 2 measured resilience and reinvention. Primary models in Mplus 8.10 used MLR, FIML and autoregressive controls. Indirect-effect intervals came from a separate 5,000-replication ML bootstrap, and the latent resilience x digitalization interaction was estimated separately under TYPE = RANDOM. Findings All three family resources were positively associated with Time 2 resilience, but their direct paths to reinvention were small and nonsignificant. Their indirect associations through resilience were significant. Resilience and digitalization were positively associated with reinvention, and the resilience−reinvention relationship strengthened as digitalization increased. Because resilience and reinvention were contemporaneous at Time 2, the conditional indirect pattern is interpreted associationally. Originality/value This study develops a staged conditional-process explanation: family resources supply coordination capacity for continuity, while digitalization strengthens the conversion of preserved capacity into renewal. The Saudi setting makes this mechanism theoretically salient because kin-based coordination and informal governance coexist with institutional modernization and rapid SME digitalization.

title: Workplace learning, adult skills and digital work participation in mid-to-later working life: evidence from nine PIAAC cycle 2 settings
container-title: International Journal of Manpower
6d6af315db9c5508ad846d0e83c2bd1ba16b9844.abstract: Purpose This study examines associations of informal learning at work, assessed adult skills and everyday digital practice with digital work participation in mid-to-later working life. Design/methodology/approach Pooled public-use data from the Programme for the International Assessment of Adult Competencies (PIAAC) Cycle 2 cover 14,444 adults aged 45–65 in nine selected countries and economies. Models combine ten plausible values and country-specific replicate-weight variances, with interaction and sensitivity analyses. Findings The age coefficient declined from −0.107 to −0.012 in population-weighted models but remained negative under country-equal weighting. Informal learning and home information and communication technology (ICT) use remained positively associated with work ICT use across alternative skill specifications and occupational adjustment, although work-context controls attenuated the learning association. Adaptive problem solving was sensitive to numeracy inclusion. Educational differences remained visible. Research limitations/implications Cross-sectional, complete-case estimates do not identify causal effects or national policy mechanisms and do not represent all adults aged 45–65. Practical implications The findings motivate evaluation of learning opportunities alongside digital training; they do not establish the effectiveness of specific interventions. Originality/value The study brings assessed skills and informal learning into a pooled analysis of later-working-life digital participation, distinguishing associations that persist across specifications from those sensitive to skill choice, job context and weighting.

title: Dark or bright? Unmasking the effects of machiavellianism, digital narcissism and psychopathy on digital entrepreneurship
container-title: Asia-Pacific Journal of Business Administration
d63dd904a42addb4df473e4c9463fda968a12318.abstract: Purpose Entrepreneurial ventures are attracting a growing number of young unemployed adults worldwide. This study explores university students' digital entrepreneurial intention (DEI). It does so by assessing the influence of the personality dark triad: machiavellianism (Mac), digital narcissism (DN) and psychopathy (Psy). It also considers digital innovative attitude (DIA) as a mediator and digital entrepreneurial alertness (DEA) as a moderator. Design/methodology/approach Data were collected using snowball sampling and a structured questionnaire with a 5-point Likert scale. The analysis employed partial least squares structural equation modeling to investigate the relationships among dependent, independent and moderating constructs. Findings Digital narcissism has the strongest positive influence on both DIA and digital entrepreneurial intention. Psychopathy also shows a significant positive association. Notably, Machiavellianism shows a negative but statistically insignificant effect on DIA and DEI. However, DIA significantly improves DEI. DEA positively moderates the DIA–DEI link as well as creates a positive impact on DEI. Originality/value The current study significantly contributes to digital entrepreneurship literature by assessing the mediating role of DIA and the moderating role of DEA to see how the dark triad determines students' entrepreneurial inclination in the digital context. Furthermore, the outcomes offer interesting insights regarding the role of digital narcissism and psychopathy in shaping digital entrepreneurial intention among university students. Notably, these insights help policymakers, university leaders, educators, parents and students better support digital entrepreneurship in Bangladesh and beyond.

title: Health-related quality of life in relation to fatigue, depression, anxiety, and disease manifestations in systemic lupus erythematosus and vasculitis
container-title: Rheumatology Advances in Practice
fa4291a3716c5987cebc592544dbe914e2691986.abstract: Abstract Objectives We explored health-related quality of life (HRQoL) in relation to fatigue, depression, anxiety, and disease characteristics in people with ANCA-associated vasculitis (AAV) and Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE). Methods In this cross-sectional study, patient-reported outcome measures included HRQoL (EQ-5D-3L), fatigue (Multidimensional Assessment of Fatigue), and anxiety and depression (Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale). Physicians assessed disease activity and characteristics. Group comparisons used chi-square and Mann–Whitney U tests. Multivariable linear regression models identified determinants of HRQoL. Results We included 481 individuals with SLE, 256 with AAV, and 125 controls. Individuals with AAV and SLE experienced reduced HRQoL, greater fatigue, and higher levels of anxiety and depression compared to controls, but no differences were found between SLE and AAV. In combined SLE/AAV analyses, active organ involvement (skin, lungs, kidneys), was associated with lower HRQoL and more fatigue. In linear regression, including physical, social, and disease-specific aspects (Model A), active disease and older age were associated with lower HRQoL, while being male and cohabitation were associated with higher HRQoL. The adjusted R² value indicated that Model A explained 12.1% of the variance in HRQoL. After adding psychological aspects, fatigue, depression, and anxiety (Model B), the adjusted R² value indicated that the model explained 35.9% of the variance, increasing the proportion of HRQoL variance explained. Conclusion Across SLE and AAV diagnoses, active organ involvement in skin, lungs and kidneys was associated with lower HRQoL and more fatigue. Furthermore, combining disease characteristics with psychological aspects increased the explanatory determinants of HRQoL in both diseases.

title: Channeled Attention and Stable Errors
container-title: The Quarterly Journal of Economics
aa56883ac1e6c9b3cc530fef17050cbca03121f3.abstract: Abstract People persist in mistaken beliefs even in settings with high stakes, abundant data, and repeated opportunities to learn—settings where standard arguments imply they should correct their errors. We develop an attention-based framework for understanding why errors persist. When a person channels his attention through the lens of his potentially misspecified model, exposure to data is not the same as tracking the statistics necessary to tell him his model is wrong. A model is attentionally stable when the data the person deems relevant will, in the long run, fail to make the model look implausible. Models that erroneously rule things out—e.g., beliefs that a variable doesn’t matter or that a distinction doesn’t exist—tend to be attentionally stable because they divert attention away from data that would refute the models. Conversely, models that erroneously rule things in are less likely to be stable. Whether an error is discovered depends on the structure of the decision problem but is not tightly linked to its level of harm; arbitrarily costly errors can persist while trivially inexpensive ones may be detected. Nevertheless, no error is robust both to changes in the decision environment and to shocks that expand attention: every channeled-attention error is vulnerable to some perturbation that would reveal it. We use the framework to analyze the stability of psychological biases and empirical misconceptions, as well as to explain why fresh eyes catch mistakes, why people use overly coarse rather than overly fine categorizations, and why people recognize errors in others that they miss in themselves.

title: DTBNet: Multimodal 3D Geometric Perception with Hierarchical Attention for Robust Drug–Target Interaction and Binding Affinity Prediction
container-title: Bioinformatics
0d68afed625fe3f8cd6f59afb05f1321be84890a.abstract: Abstract Motivation Accurate prediction of drug-target interactions (DTIs) and binding affinity (DTA) constitutes a core challenge in accelerating drug discovery. While existing computational methods have made progress, most models struggle to capture critical physicochemical interactions in 3D space due to reliance on 1D sequences or 2D graph structures, and exhibit limited generalization in cold-start scenarios. This study proposes DTBNet, a unified prediction framework integrating multimodal geometric perception and hierarchical attention. The framework constructs heterogeneous embeddings combining local chemical details with global biological information by incorporating protein 3D geometric features and multilevel drug representations. During cross-modal interaction, atom–residue cross-attention first captures pair-specific local associations, followed by group-level multi-head self-attention that integrates complementary chemical-semantic, global structural, and local geometric interaction representations. Results Experiments on benchmark datasets (Davis, KIBA, PDBBind) demonstrate that compared with the optimal baseline models, DTBNet achieves up to 19.8% reduction in mean squared error and 8.0% improvement in Pearson correlation coefficient, maintaining optimal performance in drug cold-start, target cold-start, and completely novel pairing scenarios, showcasing robust cross-domain adaptability. Independent validation on GPCR targets achieves RMSE 0.783, confirming real-world applicability. Visualization analyses reveal DTBNet precisely identifies interaction sites between key transmembrane helical domain residues and drug aromatic rings, with attention distribution highly consistent with experimentally resolved binding conformations. These results establish DTBNet as a new performance benchmark through 3D geometric perception and dynamic attention mechanisms, providing interpretable molecular insights for structure-based rational drug design and demonstrating broad potential in virtual screening and target discovery. Availability The source code and data are available at https://github.com/wyx2012/DTB_Net. Supplementary information Supplementary data are available at Bioinformatics online.

title: Digital Marketing Acceleration of Shopee for Lapeo Marlin Shredded Fish Products as a Catalyst for Economic Resilience and Independence of Local Communities
container-title: MOVE: Journal of Community Service and Engagement
f276af0025f0f426a4c8391495ab0a78c7fa71f7.abstract: Lapeo Village, Campalagian District, Polewali Mandar Regency holds significant fishery potential, notably the processing of marlin fish into shredded fish (abon) by the Rezky Kuliner Lapeo Business Group. However, this potential is hindered by conventional marketing, simple packaging, and the absence of a Standard Operating Procedure (SOP). This partnership-based community service program aims to accelerate digital marketing via the Shopee platform, redesign product packaging, create a QRIS account for non-cash transactions, and compile operational SOPs to build resilience and economic independence for both productive partners (Rezky Kuliner Lapeo) and non-productive partners (PKK Pokja III Lapeo Village). The implementation methods included socialization, intensive training, daily technical assistance, and data-driven evaluation based on data analytics. The results indicated a significant increase in partners' capacity: the creation of a competitive new visual identity with marketable standing pouch variations, implementation of payments via QRIS barcode scans, the formulation of SOP documents implemented in up to 80% of business activities, and the operation of an official store on Shopee. The most accelerated result was demonstrated by the performance of the Shopee store, which recorded its first sale within one week after the Shopee account was verified and declared active. The active involvement of PKK Pokja III as a digital promotion support team further reinforces the sustainable self-reliance of the village economy.

title: From digital divide to digital dividend: a two-tier talent development model for healthcare workforces
container-title: Development and Learning in Organizations: An International Journal
8ca9461085e1dd6a8c650fc715ed41fa3829719f.abstract: Purpose This viewpoint reframes the issue of the digital divide among the health workforce and shifts it into the perspective of talent development rather than training, and proposes a two-pronged strategy to convert digital disadvantage into workforce advantage. Design/methodology/approach The paper establishes a tiered digital career development framework based on talent development, social capital, human capital and research on the healthcare workforce. Findings Healthcare organizations develop digital human capital among Tier 1 specialists but do not provide the same opportunities for Tier 2 allied, rural and supporting specialists, and training alone cannot bridge this divide. Research limitations/implications The framework is conceptual and requires empirical validation. Practical implications Top-level managers and HRD practitioners need to incorporate tiered digital career paths into organization strategies. Originality/value The paper defines the digital dividend precisely by measuring progress in retention, capacity and resilience via the development of distinct career paths for Tier 2 employees, and specifies the conditions required to achieve it.

title: Aging in space: Space weathering age of S-type and V-type asteroid families from the Sloan Digital Sky Survey
container-title: Astronomy & Astrophysics
060ca8716eeb98b8dad41d7a4b78594c30bde747.abstract: Space weathering (SW) progressively modifies the optical properties of bodies with no atmosphere, enabling surface exposure ages to be inferred from time-dependent spectral changes. In this study, we develop a machine-learning framework based on a support vector regression (SVR) model to estimate the SW age of S-type and V-type asteroid families from visible reflectance spectra. The SW age is defined as the time since an asteroid has been exposed to the interplanetary environment after a breakup or resurfacing event. We trained and validated the SVR model on laboratory SW simulations (H+ irradiation and laser pulse irradiation) using published reflectance spectra of olivine, pyroxene, and olivine-pyroxene mixtures and chondritic meteorites representative of S-type and V-type asteroid composition. We applied the model to Sloan Digital Sky Survey photometric data to estimate SW ages for ten S-type asteroid families and Vesta family. The model yielded SW age distributions that show broad agreement with dynamical family ages for Flora and Vesta, suggesting a quasi-steady evolution after family formation where SW and resurfacing operate in approximate balance. These inner-belt systems are consistent with frequent but shallow Yarkovsky-O'Keefe-Radzievskii-Paddack (YORP)-driven regolith reworking, which does not fully reset spectral maturity. In contrast, Eunomia, Maria, and Koronis exhibit systematically younger SW ages relative to their dynamical ages, indicating more efficient surface renewal and/or slower weathering at larger heliocentric distances combined with episodic resurfacing on timescales of 10^8 years. Asteroid surface evolution reflects the interplay between SW efficiency, YORP-driven regolith redistribution, family formation mechanisms, and composition. In the inner belt, regolith reworking may preserve spectral maturity, whereas differences in resurfacing and weathering conditions across the mid- and outer belt may contribute to the decoupling of SW and dynamical ages. The SW age therefore provides an effective measure of surface maturation rather than a direct proxy for absolute age.

title: Shaping digital entrepreneurship intention among engineering students: the roles of digital literacy, smartphone usage and entrepreneurial leadership
container-title: Journal of Applied Research in Higher Education
f2fb1b8fefd10196bb9d2efff5d118974f523943.abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine the factors influencing digital entrepreneurship intention among higher education engineering students in West Sumatra and East Java. Drawing on the theory of planned behavior, this study investigates the effects of digital literacy and entrepreneurial leadership on digital entrepreneurship intention through smartphone usage and digital entrepreneurship attitude. It also examines the moderating role of entrepreneurship family background. Design/methodology/approach This study used a quantitative cross-sectional survey design. Data were collected from higher education engineering students in West Sumatra and East Java who had taken entrepreneurship courses. A total of 1,200 questionnaires were distributed, and 1,035 responses were obtained. The respondents were selected using convenience sampling. Each construct was measured using seven items on a five-point Likert scale. The data were analyzed using SmartPLS 4 with partial least squares structural equation modeling. Findings The results show that digital literacy and entrepreneurial leadership positively influence smartphone usage and digital entrepreneurship attitude. Smartphone usage positively affects both digital entrepreneurship attitude and digital entrepreneurship intention. Digital entrepreneurship attitude was found to be the strongest direct predictor of digital entrepreneurship intention. The findings also confirm the mediating roles of smartphone usage and digital entrepreneurship attitude. Furthermore, entrepreneurship family background strengthens the relationship between smartphone usage and digital entrepreneurship intention but weakens the relationship between digital entrepreneurship attitude and digital entrepreneurship intention. Originality/value This study contributes to the digital entrepreneurship literature by offering empirical evidence from engineering students in a higher education context. It highlights smartphone usage as a behavioral mechanism and digital entrepreneurship attitude as a psychological mechanism linking digital literacy and entrepreneurial leadership to digital entrepreneurship intention.

title: ANALISIS KOMPARATIF TINGKAT KESEHATAN BANK DIGITAL DAN KONVENSIONAL BERDASARKAN METODE RGEC PADA BANK TERDAFTAR DI BEI PERIODE 2020 – 2025
container-title: Jurnal Ilmiah Manajemen, Ekonomi, & Akuntansi (MEA)
c7c62520a2a255647ac87329c3edd817a878de86.abstract: Perkembangan bank digital di Indonesia telah mengubah karakteristik industri perbankan dan menimbulkan perbedaan model bisnis dengan bank konvensional. Kondisi tersebut dapat tercermin dalam tingkat kesehatan bank yang dinilai melalui metode Risk Profile, Good Corporate Governance, Earnings, dan Capital (RGEC). Penelitian ini menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif komparatif dengan sampel empat bank digital dan empat bank konvensional yang terdaftar di Bursa Efek Indonesia selama periode 2020–2025. Data diperoleh dari laporan keuangan dan laporan tahunan bank, sedangkan analisis dilakukan menggunakan statistik deskriptif, Independent Sample T-Test, dan Mann-Whitney U-test. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan terdapat perbedaan signifikan pada rasio NPL, GCG, ROA, NIM, dan CAR, sedangkan LDR tidak menunjukkan perbedaan signifikan. Rata-rata tingkat kesehatan berdasarkan RGEC sebesar 80,56% pada bank digital dan 90,14% pada bank konvensional, dengan hasil Independent Sample T-Test sebesar <0,001. Temuan ini menunjukkan bahwa bank konvensional memiliki tingkat kesehatan yang lebih tinggi secara keseluruhan, sedangkan bank digital menunjukkan keunggulan pada NPL, NIM, dan CAR. Dengan demikian, perbedaan kesehatan kedua kelompok bank terutama tercermin pada kualitas risiko, kemampuan menghasilkan laba, dan struktur permodalan.

title: Mobile health–enabled outpatient–ward–home integrated care for atrial fibrillation: real-world implementation and 1-year outcomes of a multicomponent hospital-wide digital pathway
container-title: BMC Cardiovascular Disorders
2e1bcd9ade3339db3b68ac1ade4fb435de34feee.abstract: Abstract Objective Atrial fibrillation (AF) requires continuous, multidisciplinary, and patient-engaged management across screening, inpatient care, discharge transition, and long-term follow-up. Although mobile phone–based outreach, SMS text messaging, and digitally supported integrated care models have shown promise in AF management, evidence remains limited regarding hospital-wide pathways that connect outpatient identification, ward-based collaborative care, AI-assisted follow-up, and home-based longitudinal management within routine workflows. This study evaluated the real-world implementation and 1-year outcomes associated with a multicomponent outpatient–ward–home digital integrated care pathway for AF (OWHD-AF). Materials and methods We conducted a hospital-wide before-and-after real-world implementation study at Weifang People’s Hospital. Patients hospitalized with AF before implementation in 2023 were compared with patients managed after deployment of OWHD-AF in 2024. The pathway integrated electronic medical record–based AF identification, electrocardiographic report screening, automated clinical prompts, fast-track electrophysiology referral, interdepartmental specialist coordination, guideline-directed risk assessment, anticoagulation optimization, AI-assisted telephone follow-up, SMS reminders, manual escalation for predefined risk signals, and dashboard-supported quality monitoring. Digital follow-up engagement was assessed using outreach and care-conversion indicators. Monthly process indicators were assessed using interrupted time-series analysis, and 1-year clinical outcomes were evaluated using Kaplan–Meier curves and multivariable Cox proportional hazards models. Results A total of 10,607 hospitalized patients with AF were included, with 5146 in the pre-implementation phase and 5461 in the post-implementation phase. After implementation, AF diagnosis, CHA₂DS₂-VASc assessment, and HAS-BLED assessment showed significant positive slope changes in interrupted time-series analyses (all P <.001). Monthly risk assessment documentation increased from consistently low levels before implementation to more than 80% during the late post-implementation period. The system delivered 20,932 outbound AI-assisted follow-up calls, of which 7440 were connected (35.5%), and 9550 SMS reminders, of which 9454 were successfully delivered (99.0%). At 12 months, OWHD-AF implementation was associated with lower risks of major adverse cardiovascular events (3.72% vs. 5.11%; adjusted hazard ratio [aHR] 0.72, 95% CI 0.60–0.86; P <.001) and heart failure readmission (3.42% vs. 4.66%; aHR 0.71, 95% CI 0.59–0.86; P <.001). All-cause mortality was numerically lower, and major bleeding was not significantly increased. Conclusions In this hospital-wide real-world implementation study, OWHD-AF provided a scalable mobile health–enabled pathway integrating outpatient AF identification, ward-based collaborative management, and home-based AI-assisted follow-up. Implementation was associated with improved guideline-directed care processes and favorable 1-year outcomes.

title: Comparison of joint laxity measured using 60- and 80-N distraction forces and manual stress during robot-assisted total knee arthroplasty
container-title: Arthroplasty
84efe849a6fc664edadf8590d3d797d0f3125527.abstract: Abstract Background Appropriate intraoperative soft-tissue balance is essential for achieving successful outcomes following total knee arthroplasty (TKA). However, the optimal distraction force for evaluating joint laxity remains unclear. This study aimed to compare joint laxities measured using specific distraction forces with those obtained under manual varus-valgus stress and assess the interobserver variability. Methods A total of 55 bi-cruciate-stabilized TKAs were performed using a robotic system. Medial and lateral joint laxities were evaluated using a force-controlled tensioner device under a distraction force of 60 and 80 N at 10°, 30°, 60°, and 90° of flexion and under manual varus-valgus stress using the robotic system. To assess interobserver differences, all measurements were performed independently by the senior surgeon and one of the assistant surgeons. Results In the medial compartment, no statistically significant differences were detected between joint laxity under manual stress and that measured using a distraction force of 80 N at 10° and 30° of flexion. At 90° of flexion, no statistically significant difference was detected between JLR and JLT60N. In the lateral compartment, no statistically significant differences were detected between joint laxity under manual stress and that measured using 80 N at 10° and 90° of flexion, whereas joint laxity under manual stress was significantly greater than that measured using 80 N at 30° and 60° of flexion. Interobserver variability was greater in the lateral compartment than in the medial compartment, especially at higher flexion angles. Conclusions The differences between joint laxity measured under manual stress and that measured using a tensioner device varied depending on the compartment and knee flexion angle. The lateral compartment showed greater measurement variability, suggesting the need for careful assessment and standardization of intraoperative joint laxity evaluation during robot-assisted TKA.

title: GameMove MS modo sensibilidade
GameMove MS Sensitivity Mode
GameMove MS modo sensibilidad
container-title: Revista Inclusiones
addb12b35d5e5406a41d49efd9bc4d644b62a221.abstract: Este estudo teve como objetivo desenvolver e analisar a validade de conteúdo e a aplicabilidade do GameMove MS modo sensibilidade para avaliação neuromotora de crianças com transtorno do espectro autista. A pesquisa metodológica foi conduzida em duas etapas: refinamento tecnológico e avaliação por sete especialistas, seguida de estudo piloto com dez crianças de seis a dez anos, com níveis de suporte 1 e 2. O coeficiente de validade de conteúdo total foi 0,943, e os valores por item variaram entre 0,857 e 1,000. No piloto, todas as crianças compreenderam e concluíram as tarefas propostas. Os resultados sustentam a validade de conteúdo e a viabilidade inicial do jogo, mas o efeito teto observado nos registros digitais limita, nesta etapa, sua capacidade discriminativa. Conclui-se que o instrumento é promissor, embora ainda demande estudos de confiabilidade, validade de critério e sensibilidade com amostras ampliadas.

title: Supporting Early Career Development Through Volitional Personality Change: A Multi-Layered Evaluation of a Digital Intervention
578e6fc17d04ca980d7f336961a10545718ea8d6.abstract: Personality change interventions (PCIs) offer promising opportunities for personal development, yet little is known about how different psychological layers of personality—thoughts, feelings, behaviors, skills, and identity—respond to intentional change efforts. This study addressed that question through a six-week smartphone-based intervention tailored to students' preparation for entering the workforce, an applied setting in which PCIs remain understudied. Final-year undergraduate clinical psychology students (N = 565) participated in one of three interventions designed to enhance resilience, social boldness, or punctuality, with a quasi-experimental control group for comparison (N = 99). Participants in all three conditions showed meaningful growth in the targeted facet, with gains exceeding changes in non-targeted facets, surpassing those observed in the control group, and persisting at the four-week follow-up. Moreover, perceived feasibility of change moderated intervention effectiveness. Finally, participants targeting resilience and social boldness showed significant growth across psychological layers, whereas those targeting punctuality changed primarily in the behavioral and skill layers. The identity layer—representing how participants see themselves—exhibited the smallest degree of change. Collectively, these findings enrich volitional personality change (VPC) theory by illuminating how personality change unfolds across different psychological layers, while also demonstrating the feasibility of PCIs in supporting the school-to-work transition.

title: <b>Cardiovascular Disease Risk Assessment in the Digital Age: From Fixed Risk Equations to Data-Driven, Intervention-Linked Prevention</b>
container-title: Journal of Public Health and Preventive Medicine
530dd4d70c02781a01c34b449c3f8c62ff96c010.abstract: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) remains the leading cause of death worldwide. Its prevention depends on identifying, before the first clinical event, who will benefit from treatment. Over the past six decades, that task has been carried out by a sequence of multivariable risk equations — from the Framingham-derived scores to the US Pooled Cohort Equations, the United Kingdom’s QRISK3, Europe’s SCORE2, and most recently the American Heart Association’s PREVENT equations. Each generation has expanded the input variables, widened the age range, and improved calibration. Yet external validation continues to show systematic miscalibration and weak transportability across populations. This review synthesises how contemporary epidemiology is responding to those limitations on two fronts. First, predictive data sources are broadening: electronic health record-derived machine learning models, wearable and sensor-derived physiological signals, and polygenic risk scores are extending discrimination and covering patients older fixed equations exclude. Second, and less often integrated, digital health interventions — from automated text-message programmes to smartphone-linked blood-pressure management — have demonstrated modest but reproducible reductions in the very risk factors that risk equations estimate: LDL cholesterol, systolic blood pressure, and medication adherence. We argue that the central methodological gap is no longer prediction accuracy in isolation. It is the design of closed-loop systems in which a risk estimate triggers, adapts to, and measures the response of a digital intervention. We examine where the evidence is robust, where disagreements persist over the clinical utility of polygenic scores and the generalisability of wearable-derived data, and what an implementation-focused research agenda should now prioritise.

title: The effect of magnetic resonance image slice thickness and voxel geometry on digital dental implant planning: an in vitro study
container-title: Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery
089c58ca3f519d49352251da0de5705495feef01.abstract: Abstract Objectives To evaluate the effect of magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) slice thickness and voxel geometry on digital dental implant planning compared to cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT). Methods Edentulous phantoms were scanned using CBCT and two MRI protocols: anisotropic and isotropic. Two calibrated examiners digitally planned the position of four implants for each sample ( n = 8) per exam (CBCT, anisotropic and isotropic). Diagnostic accuracy was assessed using implant angular deviation and linear measurements. Image quality was evaluated using a questionnaire regarding visualization of anatomical structures. Cost-to-planning-time ratio was assessed by exam costs per minute of planning. The Friedman and Wilcoxon tests were used to evaluate differences in diagnostic accuracy, planning time, and cost-to-planning-time ratio. Image quality ratings on a 5-point scale were classified as non-valid (≤ 2) or valid (≥ 3) for clinical use. Reliability was assessed by percentage agreement, and differences were evaluated using the chi-square test. Results A total of 96 implants were planned, with 32 in each exam. No significant differences were observed between exams for angular deviation ( p > 0.197), linear measurements ( p > 0.305), image quality ( p > 0.132), or planning time ( p = 0.093). However, CBCT had lower cost-to-planning-time ratio than anisotropic and isotropic MRI ( p = 0.012), which did not differ from each other ( p = 1.000). Inter-examiner agreement on image quality for anisotropic and isotropic MRI varied widely, with lower ratings for the mandibular nerve canal. Conclusion No statistically significant differences were detected among the imaging protocols in diagnostic accuracy or image quality under the investigated in vitro conditions.

title: Mapping data privacy at the intersection of AI and the digital economy: a bibliometric review, taxonomy, and research agenda
container-title: Electronic Commerce Research
a2d35586dccf8bad42e327afbba39dfaa480e28f.abstract: Abstract The rapid integration of artificial intelligence and related emerging technologies has intensified data privacy challenges across the digital economy. Although scholarship has grown substantially, it remains fragmented across technical, legal, ethical, and sector-specific domains, limiting a clear view of the field’s structure and development. This study presents a bibliometric analysis and thematic mapping of 434 peer-reviewed articles published between 2016 and 2026 in the Web of Science Core Collection. It identifies seven thematic clusters and finds that applied and privacy-preserving technical work dominates, while business strategy, trust, and public-sector governance remain underdeveloped. The study extends this mapping with a multi-dimensional privacy taxonomy and a TCCM (theory, context, characteristics, and methodology) synthesis, moving beyond the topic- and domain-specific scope of prior reviews to diagnose where the field is structurally weak. It argues that privacy remains under-theorized as an economic and behavioral phenomenon despite its centrality to digital commerce and sets out a research agenda of economically grounded questions derived from these gaps.

title: Power and the Cost of Faith: A Case Study of Religion Communication and Commercialisation in the Digital Age
container-title: Communications in Humanities Research
d286654f48845a0636a684990812279a30c358ca.abstract: Religious activities in China today are being changed by the digital era. Electronic wooden fish apps, Buddhist amulets and symbolic accessories are now popular among young people, but they often reduce the profound religious traditions to mere consumer goods and performative symbols. How modern society is changing people's conception of, application for and dissemination of religious ideas. Based on the two contrasting case studies, this paper will examine the mechanisms of religious distortion and countermeasures. Firstly, the religious merit and morality have been reduced to commodities and have lost their original ethical connotations. The second case is that temples, museums and other knowledge-based media can promote religious literacy through ethical content. According to the study, the cost of faith in modern society is not due to religion itself but rather to how it is expressed and consumed. Call for institutional accountability, platform regulation and educational innovation to promote critical religious literacy and preserve the deep cultural and ethical values of religion.

title: The Role of School Music Education in Supporting Adolescent Mental Health: The Potential of Digital Technology
container-title: Communications in Humanities Research
5b0dad32e7af43da652f08fafe25ae567ee16067.abstract: Adolescence is a critical stage in which psychological and social relationships and self-identity are rapidly formed. Under the stresses of academics and identity, the detection rate of adolescent mental health problems has shown an increase. As a major and important setting for adolescence, school shoulders key responsibility for preventing mental health problems and offering psychological support. Under the aforementioned background, this paper will focus on how school music education may support adolescent mental health, comprehensively analyzing empirical studies and review literature concerning adolescent mental health, school music education, digital music education, etc., and further probing how digital technology may expand the forms and functions of traditional music education. Existing research suggests that school music education may support adolescent mental health in several ways, including emotional expression and regulation and the strengthening of social connections. Because digital technology offers immediacy, interactivity, personalization, and shareability, it has increasingly been integrated into traditional music teaching and has become an emerging instructional approach. However, the current study on digital music education mainly focuses on learning performance and participation, while direct effects of digital music education on mental health remain underexplored. Therefore, future research should explore the potential of digital technology and how combining it with face-to-face music education can support adolescent mental health.

title: Perceived Algorithmic Personalization of Short-Videos and Digital Media Addiction
container-title: Communications in Humanities Research
e22f040e4fbca54e6b1910927c87f8297e0f1ca6.abstract: In the era of mobile internet, short-video services have become a major source of digital entertainment and information for adolescent groups. Short-video platforms rely on algorithm-driven content distribution. Based on users' viewing records, likes, and comments, recommendation systems deliver content matching individual interests and reshape how adolescents receive online information. Meanwhile, many adolescents cannot control their short-video usage, and the problem of digital-media addiction has drawn increasing attention from communication and youth-psychology researchers. This literature review adopts the user subjective-perception perspective. It sorts out the operating logic of algorithm-driven personalized recommendation, defines the concept and real-life manifestations of adolescent digital-media addiction, and discusses the connection between perceived algorithmic personalization and digital-media addiction. The review finds that personalized recommendations improve user experience but strengthen continuous short-video-browsing behaviors through variable-reward mechanisms, raising adolescents' risk of digital-media addiction. Most existing studies focus on objective algorithm functions, while empirical discussions about adolescents' subjective perceptions remain limited. This paper summarizes existing research gaps and offers references for future studies on adolescent media use.
