title: Spatial Attention Mechanism for Improved Multi-Focus Satellite Image Fusion: SARA-Net Model
container-title: International Journal of Engineering Trends and Technology
119f7b73f19f2e73145cc4f9e15a610ef3f19eb4.abstract: Multi-focus image fusion is crucial in various fields, particularly in satellite images, because it creates intricate images with augmented clarity. However, maintaining the original structure is challenging, leading to a reduction in performance. Therefore, this research proposes a Spatial Attention ResNet-50 Network (SARA-Net) model for fusing multiple satellite images. The proposed model utilizes an integration of ResNet-50 and Spatial Attention to effectively extract spatially significant features from actual images. Initially, satellite images from the publicly available SpaceNet datasets are preprocessed by normalization and grayscale conversion to provide consistency. ResNet-50 handles multi-scale feature extraction by residual learning, which addresses vanishing gradient issues, whereas spatial attention assigns adaptive weights to improve relevant spatial information within the feature map. The fusion layer combines these attention features to generate high-resolution and detail-preserving images. On the ten held-out test images, the proposed SARA-Net achieves a PSNR of 48.972 dB, an SSIM of 0.9953, and an entropy value of 8.4319, which is better than the existing methods.

title: ПЕДАГОГІЧНІ УМОВИ ФОРМУВАННЯ ІНФОРМАЦІЙНОЇ КУЛЬТУРИ ДІТЕЙ ДОШКІЛЬНОГО ВІКУ ЗАСОБАМИ ЦИФРОВИХ ТЕХНОЛОГІЙ
PEDAGOGICAL CONDITIONS FOR FORMING THE INFORMATION CULTURE OF PRESCHOOL CHILDREN THROUGH DIGITAL TECHNOLOGIES
container-title: Human Studies Series of Pedagogy
415d8654a1d88d6080c956a763085d97a5f9a8f4.abstract: У статті актуалізовано проблему формування інформаційної культури дітей дошкільного віку в умовах цифрової трансформації освіти та стрімкого розширення інформаційного середовища, у якому з раннього віку перебуває дитина. Обґрунтовано необхідність переходу від розуміння цифрової компетентності дошкільника як сукупності елементарних технічних умінь до комплексного формування інформаційної культури, що охоплює здатність сприймати, розуміти, знаходити, оцінювати й використовувати інформацію відповідно до мети та вікових можливостей, взаємодіяти з різними її джерелами, дотримуватися правил інформаційної та цифрової безпеки, а також відповідально й творчо використовувати цифрові технології. Метою статті є теоретичне обґрунтування педагогічних умов формування інформаційної культури дітей дошкільного віку засобами цифрових технологій та визначення основних напрямів їх реалізації в освітньому процесі закладу дошкільної освіти. Методологічну основу дослідження становлять аналіз, систематизація та узагальнення наукових джерел і нормативно-правових документів, що дали змогу визначити сучасні підходи до цифровізації дошкільної освіти, уточнити зміст поняття «інформаційна культура дітей дошкільного віку» та обґрунтувати сукупність взаємопов’язаних педагогічних умов її формування. На основі теоретичного аналізу визначено інформаційну культуру дітей дошкільного віку як інтегровану характеристику особистості, що виявляється у сформованості позитивної мотивації до пізнання інформації, здатності її сприймати, розуміти, знаходити та використовувати у доступних видах діяльності, взаємодіяти з різними інформаційними джерелами, дотримуватися елементарних правил інформаційної та цифрової безпеки, а також відповідально й творчо використовувати цифрові технології. Обґрунтовано шість взаємопов’язаних педагогічних умов її формування: створення безпечного та педагогічно доцільного цифрового освітнього середовища; змістова інтеграція інформаційної культури з різними видами дитячої діяльності; організація педагогічного супроводу інформаційної діяльності дошкільників; формування навичок критичного та усвідомленого сприймання цифрової інформації; формування цифрової безпеки та відповідальної поведінки; підвищення цифрової компетентності педагогів і педагогічної культури батьків. Встановлено, що результативність формування інформаційної культури визначається не інтенсивністю використання цифрових засобів, а їх педагогічною доцільністю, вікововідповідністю, змістовою спрямованістю та включенням у різні види дитячої діяльності. Акцентовано, що цифрові технології мають доповнювати, а не замінювати гру, безпосереднє спілкування, рухову, художню, конструкторську та дослідницьку діяльність дітей. Визначено провідну роль педагога як організатора та медіатора взаємодії дитини з інформацією, а також значення партнерської взаємодії закладу дошкільної освіти із сім’єю у забезпеченні єдності вимог до цифрової поведінки дитини. Наукова новизна дослідження полягає в систематизації та теоретичному обґрунтуванні комплексу педагогічних умов формування інформаційної культури дітей дошкільного віку засобами цифрових технологій з урахуванням безпечного цифрового середовища, різних видів дитячої діяльності, педагогічного супроводу, критичного сприймання інформації та взаємодії основних суб’єктів освітнього процесу. Практичне значення результатів полягає у можливості їх використання педагогами закладів дошкільної освіти під час добору цифрових ресурсів, організації освітньої та ігрової діяльності дітей, розроблення дидактичних вправ і проблемних ситуацій, а також у роботі з батьками з питань цифрової безпеки та культури використання цифрових технологій.

title: ОСОБЛИВОСТІ ФОРМУВАННЯ ЦИФРОВОЇ КОМПЕТЕНТНОСТІ ВИХОВАТЕЛІВ ЗАКЛАДІВ ДОШКІЛЬНОЇ ОСВІТИ
PECULIARITIES OF THE FORMATION OF DIGITAL COMPETENCE AMONG EDUCATORS OF PRESCHOOL EDUCATION INSTITUTIONS
container-title: Human Studies Series of Pedagogy
25535e3c95f331e1319df3b0855419f9bb7cb36d.abstract: У статті розглянуто проблему формування цифрової компетентності вихователів закладів дошкільної освіти в освітньому процесі. Обґрунтовано необхідність розвитку цифрових навичок педагогів як важливої передумови ефективного використання інноваційних технологій, електронних освітніх ресурсів та онлайн-інструментів у професійній діяльності. Проаналізовано наукові підходи до визначення понять «цифрова грамотність» і «цифрова компетентність» та уточнено їх співвідношення. Визначено, що цифрова грамотність є важливою основою формування цифрової компетентності, тоді як цифрова компетентність передбачає здатність педагога педагогічно доцільно, критично, безпечно та відповідально застосовувати цифрові технології у професійній діяльності. Охарактеризовано основні компоненти цифрової компетентності вихователя закладу дошкільної освіти: цифрові й технічні навички; використання цифрових ресурсів в освітньому процесі; цифрову дидактику; цифрову комунікацію; цифрову етику та безпеку; критичне мислення й інформаційну грамотність; безперервний професійний розвиток і самоосвіту. Розглянуто можливості використання сучасних цифрових ресурсів і платформ для професійного розвитку педагогів та організації освітньої взаємодії. Акцентовано увагу на особливостях цифровізації дошкільної освіти в умовах воєнного стану, зокрема використанні дистанційного та змішаного форматів освітньої діяльності. Наголошено на тому, що ефективне формування цифрової компетентності вихователів потребує належного цифрового інфраструктурного забезпечення, методичного супроводу, професійного навчання, доступу до якісного цифрового контенту, мотивації педагогів та можливостей безперервного професійного розвитку. Перспективи подальших досліджень пов’язано з теоретичним обґрунтуванням та експериментальною перевіркою педагогічних умов формування цифрової компетентності вихователів закладів дошкільної освіти.

title: <b>Digital Literacy dan Deep Learning Approach sebagai Determinan Utama Higher Order Thinking Skills Siswa SMK: Bukti Empiris dari Analisis SEM-PLS</b>
container-title: FASTABIQ: JURNAL STUDI ISLAM
b70b0729b39f7d71237e0eda589e569e3963ef22.abstract: Higher Order Thinking Skills (HOTS) have become a fundamental competency in 21st-century vocational education to prepare graduates capable of critical, analytical, and creative problem-solving. However, students' HOTS remain relatively low, while previous studies have predominantly emphasized the effectiveness of instructional models, particularly Project-Based Learning (PjBL), with limited attention to learner capability as the primary determinant of HOTS. Consequently, it remains unclear which factors contribute most substantially to HOTS development. Furthermore, empirical studies integrating Digital Literacy, Deep Learning Approach, and PjBL within a single structural model are still scarce. This study employed a quantitative explanatory design involving 240 vocational high school students. Data were analyzed using Structural Equation Modeling–Partial Least Squares (SEM-PLS), while the moderating role of Deep Learning Approach was examined through the Two-Stage Moderation approach. The findings reveal that Digital Literacy and Deep Learning Approach exert significant positive effects on HOTS, whereas Project-Based Learning does not significantly influence HOTS. In addition, Deep Learning Approach fails to moderate the relationships between Project-Based Learning and HOTS as well as between Digital Literacy and HOTS. These findings indicate that learner capability, represented by Digital Literacy and Deep Learning, plays a more decisive role in developing HOTS than instructional models alone. Therefore, strengthening students' internal learning capabilities should become a strategic priority for improving HOTS in vocational education.

title: From Human Capital to Circular Capabilities: Digital Transformation and Inclusive  Growth Tensions in a Brazilian SME
container-title: Advances in Earth and Environmental Science
ec7a07dab383d35ab20f7aab412ed964b014a0d1.abstract: The circular economy (CE) was popularized by the Ellen MacArthur Foundation (2013) as an alternative to the linear model of extraction, production, and discharge of resources, emphasizing the circularity of products and materials and the regeneration of natural systems. CE models can also be considered as a complementary strategy toward decarbonization. According to the latest report (Macarthur & Heading, 2019), the energy transition can address 55% of global greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, while the remaining 45% are associated with the production of goods and land use. However, CE has primarily been framed in terms of its economic and environmental aspects, and social benefits are usually presented as expected outcomes rather than being systematically investigated. In their analysis of 221 CE definitions in the literature, Kirchherr et al. (2023) found that approximately one-quarter of these definitions contemplate social equity or related concerns such as human well-being, socioeconomic development, and employment.

title: CardioTwin-AI: development and internal validation of a digital twin-based adaptive risk-aware learning framework for heart disease prediction
container-title: Frontiers in Digital Health
ad124e367bd9776c8ecde4d8d57bbe7082beaa2f.abstract: Heart disease is one of the most common causes of death in the world and early identification of individuals at elevated cardiovascular risk requires reliable risk-assessment methods that can support clinical decision-making. Many conventional machine-learning models focus primarily on disease classification or risk prediction and do not explicitly provide patient-specific virtual representations. This study introduces CardioTwin-AI, a Digital Twin-based Adaptive Risk-Aware Learning Framework (ARLF) to predict the presence or absence of heart disease. We propose a data-driven, patient-specific Digital Twin representation based on clinical attributes, in which the patient state is mapped to a corresponding virtual state and evaluated using state-level synchronization measures, including Twin Simulation Error (TSE) and Twin Fidelity Score (TFS) to quantify representation consistency. The deep feature representations are generated by feature engineering process based on autoencoder, and then analysed by the ARLF prediction model to estimate the probability of the presence of heart disease. It achieved high patient-state representation consistency between the source clinical state and its virtual representation, with a Twin Fidelity Score of 99.76% and a Twin Simulation Error of 0.002402. The proposed ARLF model achieved accuracy of 90.21%, precision of 90.32%, recall of 94.11%, F1-score of 92.18%, and ROC-AUC of 95.13% in the fixed held-out evaluation. The results indicate the potential of CardioTwin-AI for predicting the presence or absence of heart disease and assessing patient-state representation consistency, subject to further external validation and prospective clinical evaluation.

title: A digital quality-improvement program to reduce mortality among intubated children in a public pediatric intensive care unit in Colombia: a pre–post study with interrupted time-series analysis and a protocol for multisite replication
container-title: Frontiers in Public Health
cb6600cac1d79c2a54076ba2cc15bcc00e7218b0.abstract: Introduction Mortality among intubated children in public pediatric intensive care units (PICUs) in lowand middle-income countries remains high, driven in part by gaps in workforce training, team coordination, and standardized processes. We evaluated a low-cost, multidisciplinary digital education and team-based quality-improvement (QI) intervention—a multilingual online curriculum, telesimulationbased team training, standardized airway and handoff workflow tools, and on-site visits—in the PICU of a public pediatric hospital in Cartagena, Colombia. Methods In this single-center pre–post QI study, we included all intubated patients (&lt;18 years) admitted to the PICU of Casa del Niño during a baseline period (1 October 2023–30 April 2024), a washout period of near-complete nursing turnover (1 April–30 June 2025), and a post-intervention period (1 July–22 October 2025). The primary outcome, 30-day all-cause mortality, was analyzed by multivariable logistic regression adjusted for age, sex, and the logit of Pediatric Index of Mortality 3 (PIM3)-predicted mortality, calculated without diagnosis-risk terms for all patients because these were not recorded for later patients, supplemented by additional case-mix adjustment, an interrupted time-series analysis of all 272 intubated patients admitted between October 2023 and October 2025 (with the implementation period also modeled as a separate transition segment), and sensitivity analyses. Cost-effectiveness was explored as incremental cost per death and per disability-adjusted life-year (DALY) averted. Results Of 144 patients analyzed (95 pre-intervention; 49 post-intervention), age, sex, and median PIM3 were similar between periods, but mean PIM3-predicted mortality was twice as high before the intervention (10.7% versus 5.3%), reflecting 10 pre-intervention patients with bilaterally fixed pupils (none after). All-cause mortality was 28.4% before and 10.2% after the intervention (risk difference −18.2 percentage points, 95% confidence interval [CI] −29.6 to −4.1; relative risk 0.36, 95% CI 0.15–0.87; adjusted odds ratio 0.26, 95% CI 0.09–0.77). PIM3 under-predicted mortality in both periods (standardized mortality ratio 2.68 and 1.94, respectively). Findings were consistent in case-mix-adjusted analyses and in interrupted time-series analysis with implementation modeled as a separate transition segment (level-change odds ratio 0.24, 95% CI 0.07–0.82). Mortality was higher during implementation (35.9%) than at baseline (27.6%), which was not explained by measured severity of illness. Under the most conservative assumptions (the entire 5-year program cost attributed to the approximately two deaths averted when expected deaths were estimated with PIM3, with 3% discounting), the intervention cost up to approximately US$4,800 per DALY averted, below Colombia’s gross domestic product per capita but above half of it; less conservative scenarios gave lower estimates. Discussion Implementation of this program was associated with lower mortality among intubated children in one public Colombian PICU. Given the single-center, non-randomized design, small sample, and imperfect severity adjustment, these findings require confirmation in controlled multisite evaluations, for which we provide an implementation protocol.

title: Human factors shaping engagement with a digital treatment platform among individuals with lived experience of addiction
container-title: Frontiers in Digital Health
2797aa3d81395e392855e5dc4c2fc79eaa7166d3.abstract: Introduction Substance use disorders (SUDs) are highly prevalent, yet access to care remains limited. Digital interventions have been investigated as a means to expand treatment access, but individuals routinely disengage from them. We evaluated the acceptability, appropriateness, feasibility, and usability of a digital platform being tested as part of a collaborative care management-based intervention for SUD treatment in under-resourced areas to identify human factors influencing feasibility, usability, and accessibility. Methods Participants were adults with lived experience of addiction and related treatment. They engaged with the digital treatment platform for one week, then completed semi-structured interviews exploring their experience, followed by the Acceptability of Intervention Measure, Intervention Appropriateness Measure, Feasibility of Intervention Measure, and System Usability Scale. Template-based rapid analysis identified themes. Results 18 individuals ( n = 12 females) completed all assessments. Heavy text, lack of customization, and inconsistent notifications hindered usability. Participants felt assigned goals should match an individual's circumstances and resources available to them to support utilization. Participants desired personalization, integration with existing recovery supports, and features that encouraged routine use. Acceptability, appropriateness, and feasibility had respective means of 3.4 (95%CI = 3.0-3.9), 3.3 (95%CI = 2.8-3.9), and 3.4 (95%CI = 2.8-4.0) on 5-point scales with a neutral midpoint of 3. Usability scores approached the commonly used benchmark of 68 (mean=67.6, SD = 15.0). Discussion Digital interventions suffer from heavy disengagement. These findings suggest that digital interventions should fit the end-user's needs and surrounding environment and be both person- and context-specific. Attention to these human factors may improve usability and accessibility, while also limiting additional barriers in under-resourced areas.

title: Preparing future rehabilitation professionals for virtual care: a community case study of Renace digital for telehealth education in Chile
container-title: Frontiers in Health Services
71f04def784a7033b13f29d058b94939719d4a99.abstract: Digital health literacy is increasingly relevant to preparing health professionals for telehealth and virtual care, particularly when digital technologies mediate interactions with people who may experience barriers to accessing and using digital health resources. This community case study describes Renace Digital for Telehealth Education (RD-TE), an educational experience designed to integrate digital health literacy into the preparation of Speech-Language Pathology students for telehealth within a community-based program for older adults. RD-TE used a progressive educational pathway that connected conceptual learning, guided exploration of digital needs, clinical simulation, and application with service users during telerehabilitation practice. Students developed strategies to identify digital barriers, adapt communication and educational approaches, and support users' autonomy in the use of digital technologies. The experience was supported by structured implementation materials for tutors, students, and simulation actors, designed to facilitate replication and adaptation. Complementary quantitative assessments using the eHEALS and the Digital Health Literacy Questionnaire showed higher post-training scores in both measures. However, the difference observed for the adapted 46-item questionnaire did not remain statistically significant after Holm correction (adjusted p = 0.054). These exploratory findings should not be interpreted as evidence of intervention effectiveness. The contribution of RD-TE lies in its structured educational pathway and the availability of detailed implementation materials for tutors, students, and simulation actors, provided as supplementary materials to facilitate replication and adaptation to other rehabilitation education programs and populations. RD-TE offers a practical model for integrating digital health literacy into telehealth education through conceptual learning, clinical simulation, and situated application, with potential for adaptation to continuing professional education for clinicians working in telehealth.

title: SynForge-Cardio: a unified multimodal synthetic dataset generation framework for privacy-preserving cardiovascular AI
container-title: Frontiers in Digital Health
53d7a1f04e63b97105e6928eb46809e02c7207b9.abstract: Multimodal cardiovascular AI systems benefit from jointly available chest radiographs, 12-lead electrocardiograms (ECGs), and structured electronic health record (EHR) variables. In practice, multi-institutional model development is constrained by privacy regulations, institutional data silos, and class imbalance for less common findings. Existing open-source synthetic data tools are largely modality-specific: tabular libraries such as Synthetic Data Vault (SDV)/Conditional Tabular Generative Adversarial Network (CTGAN), image generators based on latent diffusion, and time-series methods such as Time-series Generative Adversarial Network (TimeGAN) each require its own setup, configuration, and validation. This study presents SynForge-Cardio, a multimodality orchestration framework for prompt-driven synthetic dataset generation across chest X-ray (CXR), 12-lead ECG, and EHR modalities. Rather than introducing a new generative backbone, SynForge-Cardio coordinates established components—latent diffusion with optional low-rank adaptation for CXR; parametric and bounded morphology-preserving augmentation (with an optional TimeGAN path) for ECG; and size-aware routing among jitter augmentation, Gaussian copula, and CTGAN/Tabular Variational Autoencoder for EHR—behind a shared clinical prompt interface, a rule-based router, and a postgeneration quality/privacy reporting layer. The three modalities were generated independently from separate datasets; the framework does not perform patient-level joint synthesis and makes no claim of anatomical or physiological consistency across modalities. This system is implemented as a FastAPI backend with a React frontend and can run on a single workstation GPU. Herein, we formalize the orchestration objective, specify modality-wise models and metrics [Fréchet Inception Distance (FID), dynamic time warping (DTW), power spectral density similarity, Kolmogorov–Smirnov statistics, correlation preservation, and distance-to-closest-record privacy screening], and describe an evaluation protocol on public corpora (NIH Chest X-ray14, PTB-XL, and the UCI Cleveland Heart Disease dataset), including a four-regime train-on-synthetic/test-on-real (TSTR) utility analysis with five random seeds. On the framework alone, we measured 94.6% modality-routing accuracy, 100% direct-vs.-routed generation equivalence on the evaluated cases, 59 unnecessary generator calls avoided, and 100% validation/reporting completeness (1,105/1,108 tests pass, 3 skipped). Downstream-utility results were mixed: augmenting a 25%-real training set with synthetic data changed the held-out AUROC by −0.041 to +0.050 across three CXR tasks (none significant at five seeds); by +0.019 for ECG MI-vs.-NORM [produced by mode B (bounded real-waveform augmentation, whose synthetic samples can be matched to their true source recording at top-1 ≈ 42.7–43.4%, and hence, mode B is not an independently learned generative model)]; and by +0.017 for EHR heart disease classification, which is not evidence of benefit given the 61-record hold-out set (the test-set bootstrap 95% CI for the difference includes zero). Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV acquisition was not completed because credentialed access was unavailable; all reported EHR results were UCI-based. SynForge-Cardio is intended as a practical, reproducible research framework for privacy-conscious cardiovascular data augmentation and prototype development.

title: Statistical learning for RT-QuIC kinetics phenotyping in prion disease
container-title: Frontiers in Digital Health
db3bcb13a1e6d5818fec53a1dd0b0fdc56f1a517.abstract: Background Prion diseases, such as Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease, are invariably fatal neurodegenerative disorders whose clinical heterogeneity makes early diagnosis challenging. The Real-Time Quaking-Induced Conversion (RT-QuIC) assay has revolutionized antemortem detection by amplifying the pathogenic prion protein (PrP Sc ) with near-perfect specificity. However, routine diagnostics typically reduce the continuous RT-QuIC fluorescence curve to just two metrics: the lag phase and the maximum fluorescence intensity. This two-parameter reduction discards the striking heterogeneity of the full temporal profile, erasing latent biological information regarding pathological burden and strain properties. Exploiting this hidden data requires new analytical methods that keep reaction kinetics biologically legible. Methods To address this, we propose an end-to-end statistical framework that captures the complete fluorescence distribution over time. We analyzed cerebrospinal-fluid RT-QuIC trajectories from 301 patients/samples; after exclusion of five patients/samples with consistently shorter recordings, 296 patient/sample-level profiles were included in the tensor modeling and clustering analyses. We then applied a three-way (Tucker3) tensor clustering approach to the unreduced time courses across all technical replicates. Results The proposed framework identifies distinct empirical RT-QuIC fluorescence profiles and provides a compact description of curve morphology. By modelling the complete trajectory, it captures differences in rise steepness, timing, baseline level, and late-phase attenuation that are not represented by conventional lag-phase and maximum-intensity summaries. Conclusions The identified profiles are cohort-specific empirical patterns of the RT-QuIC fluorescence reaction. The late-phase attenuation parameter provides an additional descriptor not included in standard sigmoidal models; however, its biological, clinical, and diagnostic interpretation requires independent validation. Future studies should assess associations between curve-derived parameters or profiles and clinical phenotype, PRNP genotype, molecular subtype, biomarkers, and survival.

title: Lightweight MFCC–SVM recognition of wheeze events in pediatric respiratory sounds: inter-patient evaluation on SPRSound and a software deployment proof-of-concept
container-title: Frontiers in Digital Health
f08757192416a997a850c854f6b218d243ef4aa8.abstract: Pediatric wheeze recognition can support the automated analysis of respiratory sounds and reduce dependence on subjective auscultation. This study develops and evaluates a lightweight machine-learning approach for event-level wheeze/no-wheeze recognition using the publicly available SPRSound pediatric respiratory sound database. Respiratory events were extracted exclusively from the expert-annotated temporal boundaries provided with the dataset, without automatic event segmentation. A total of 9,089 annotated respiratory events were represented using Mel-frequency cepstral coefficients (MFCCs), delta, and delta-delta features summarized into a fixed 120-dimensional vector. Logistic Regression, Linear Support Vector Machine, Random Forest, and Support Vector Machine with a radial basis function kernel (SVM-RBF) were evaluated under the same acoustic-feature pipeline. The operating threshold of the SVM-RBF classifier was optimized using the INTRA-2022 partition and subsequently applied to the inter-patient INTER-2022 partition. At this operating point, the model achieved a sensitivity of 0.935 (95% CI 0.901–0.957), specificity of 0.777 (95% CI 0.752–0.801), ROC-AUC of 0.930, PR-AUC of 0.772, and F1-score of 0.679; the positive predictive value was 0.534, reflecting a substantial false-positive burden. As a secondary software-level contribution, the trained preprocessing and classification components were integrated into an Android–Flask client–server workflow for audio submission, server-side feature extraction, inference, and result visualization. The software workflow was functionally implemented but was not quantitatively validated using respiratory recordings acquired through a smartphone microphone. Accordingly, the reported performance characterizes event-level classification under SPRSound conditions and should not be interpreted as mobile-acquisition, diagnostic, or clinical validation.

title: Seasonal Assessment and Design Using Water Quality Index for Drinking: A Case Study of Bali Town and Environs, Taraba State, Nigeria
container-title: IIARD INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF GEOGRAPHY AND ENVIRONMENTAL MANAGEMENT
d60b6b875069aad0a8d6959eef04358c3d1c7a56.abstract: This study addresses the critical issue of water quality in Bali town and its surroundings, with a specific focus on the seasonal variations in the Water Quality Index (WQI) for boreholes. Groundwater, crucial for drinking purposes, lacks adequate quality testing in the region, which poses potential health risks. Water samples collected during both wet and dry seasons in 2016 and 2017 were analyzed for twenty-nine parameters. However, only nine out of the twenty-nine samples were used in calculating the Water Quality Index for the boreholes under investigation. These nine parameters include Turbidity, Total Dissolved Solids, Total Hardness, pH, Nitrate, Copper, Iron, Chloride, and Total Coliform Count. When comparing the results with the standards set by the World Health Organization (WHO) in 2010 and the Nigerian Standard for Drinking Water Quality (NSDWQ) in 2007, it was observed that most parameters increased during the wet season, indicating higher pollutant dissolution. Notably, bacteriological parameters, especially the Total Coliform Count and E. coli, exceeded permissible limits. This highlights the urgency of water treatment to achieve excellent quality and provides valuable insights for designing water infrastructure.

title: Neural Mechanisms of Willed Attention Control
6c47127d70f109a58cb6025488b9cb7e3e64f432.abstract: Cueing paradigms are commonly used to study the neural mechanisms of visual spatial attention control. In these paradigms, each trial starts with an external cue, which instructs the subject to pay covert attention to a spatial location in anticipation of an impending stimulus (instructed attention). Recent work has introduced a new type of cue which prompts the subject to spontaneously decide which spatial location to attend (willed attention). We studied the neural mechanisms of willed attention control by analyzing fMRI and EEG data recorded at two institutions (UF and UC Davis) using the same willed attention paradigm. The findings include: (1) both instructional cues and the choice cue activated the DAN, (2) the choice cue additionally activated a frontoparietal decision network consisting of dorsal anterior cingulate cortex (dACC), anterior insula (AI), anterior prefrontal cortex (APFC), dorsal lateral prefrontal cortex (DLPFC), and inferior parietal lobule (IPL), (3) the decision about where to attend can be decoded in frontoparietal decision network in choice trials but not in instructional trials, and (4) EEG alpha oscillation patterns immediately preceding the choice cue, but not the instructional cues, predicted the postcue direction of attention and the frontoparietal decision network activity. Based on these findings we proposed a model of willed attention control suggesting how the direction of visual spatial attention was decided upon in the absence of external instructions.

title:
A Catalog of Compact High-velocity Clouds from the FAST All-Sky H
                    <scp>i</scp>
                    Survey (FASHI) DR2
container-title: Research in Astronomy and Astrophysics
d3dde96f6c706676ad1d2e5636cb7668f5b8c69f.abstract: Abstract High-velocity clouds (HVCs)—especially compact HVCs (CHVCs)—are thought to serve as gaseous tracers of dark-matter-dominated subhalos, providing a crucial empirical link between the predicted dark matter substructure and observed satellite galaxies. In this paper, we present a new catalog of 192 CHVCs identified from the FAST All-Sky H i Survey Data Release 2. Among these, 108 are ultra-compact HVCs, the majority of which are new discoveries. We find that 185 of the 192 CHVCs are spatially and kinematically concentrated around the Andromeda galaxy (M31), with a median local standard of rest velocity of −296.1 km s −1 , suggesting physical association with M31. Adopting an M31 distance of 0.8 Mpc, we derive H i masses in the range 1.9 × 10 5 –4.0 × 10 6 M ⊙ and dynamical masses from 1.0 × 10 7 to 6.3 × 10 8 M ⊙ . Approximately half of the CHVCs follow the baryonic Tully–Fisher relation. No optical counterparts are detected in Pan-STARRS1 imaging down to a limiting magnitude of m g = 22.8. We conclude that these CHVCs likely represent a population of gas-rich, starless minihalos and provide an excellent sample for the search for dark galaxies.

title: Digital Transformation and the Techno-Regulatory Interface
container-title: International Perspectives on Tax Policy and Accounting Practices
02b4a07a6af152d2b2290f77a4a5a4cc51411567.abstract: Digital transformation is fundamentally changing the way taxation and accounting are performed in today's data-driven economy. The rapid adoption of Artificial Intelligence (AI), blockchain, and cloud computing has enabled governments, businesses, and regulatory institutions to improve financial transparency, automate compliance processes, strengthen decision-making, and enhance the efficiency of tax administration and accounting systems. These technologies are reshaping traditional financial practices by creating intelligent, secure, and interconnected digital ecosystems that support real-time information processing and evidence-based governance.

title: AI Integration and Organizational Performance
container-title: International Perspectives on Tax Policy and Accounting Practices
8d6566608fce521055ce1c29ae126198863c8d7f.abstract: In conclusion, this research demonstrates that artificial intelligence (AI) represents a genuine qualitative leap in the field of management in general, and in the administrative decision-making process in particular. The study's findings confirm a strong correlation and a significant positive impact of using AI technologies on improving the quality of administrative decisions in Iraqi Public Sector. This enhances their ability to meet contemporary challenges and achieve a sustainable competitive advantage. The study employed a quantitative approach to data collection and analysis, concluding that adopting AI effectively contributes to enhancing the quality of administrative decisions and achieving a sustainable competitive advantage for organizations. The research included taking a random sample of (450) employees in Public Sector from three public institutions by using a questionnaire as the main tool for collecting data. The results were analyzed using the statistical software AMOS- SPSS version in terms of quality with a positive statistical significance.

title: Evaluating Integrated Soybean Cyst Nematode Management Using Spatially Informed Mixed Models
container-title: Phytopathology®
fcf49146192521f260f8b028c736fb8755c7c757.abstract: Evaluating management strategies for soybean cyst nematode (SCN) under field conditions remains challenging because the nematode is spatially aggregated and infests fields that are themselves heterogeneous. When left unmodeled, this structure is absorbed into the residual error and erodes the precision of treatment comparisons. This study combined a split-plot field evaluation of two SCN-resistance sources (PI 88788 and Peking) and fluopyram seed treatment with a graded series of spatially explicit linear mixed models, fitted to populations capable of reproducing on both resistance sources in two Ohio environments. Six models spanning a gradient of spatial complexity—from non-spatial through autoregressive and trend-adjusted to tensor-product penalized spline (TPS) structures—were compared; TPS fit best, improving experimental efficiency by 33 to 39% over the conventional non-spatial analysis. Peking-derived cultivars outyielded PI 88788-derived cultivars by 258 kg ha −1 and suppressed nematode reproduction by 36%. Peking nonetheless showed slightly greater yield sensitivity to increasing pre-planting SCN egg density [ P i , eggs 100 cm −3 soil; −5.1% per unit increase in ln( Pᵢ )] than PI 88788 (−4.0%), revealing a trade-off between reproductive suppression and yield stability. Fluopyram increased yield by 111 kg ha −1 but did not reduce SCN reproduction, indicating a yield-protective effect rather than a population-suppressive effect. Effective management of dually adapted populations therefore requires diversification of resistance, with Peking-derived cultivars complementing PI 88788 and seed treatments providing supplementary yield protection. The study also demonstrates that spatially explicit mixed models improve inferential precision for crop yield and SCN reproduction and offer a transferable approach for other soilborne pathogens.

title: Evaluating Sustainable Building Practices for Carbon Reduction in Nigerian Housing
container-title: IIARD INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF GEOGRAPHY AND ENVIRONMENTAL MANAGEMENT
5f11b402221db76173c00c38d8ba8b97d53c6df9.abstract: Sustainable building materials play a crucial role in reducing the carbon footprint of the housing sector, which is significant in Nigeria due to rapid urbanisation and increasing housing demands. This study provides a comprehensive narrative review of 60 published journal articles from 2010 to 2023, focusing on identifying, evaluating, and applying sustainable building materials for low-carbon housing in Nigeria. The review method critically analyses existing literature to highlight the most effective materials and techniques contributing to carbon reduction. Findings reveal that materials such as bamboo, recycled concrete, and earth-based materials show promise in achieving sustainability goals. Additionally, the study underscores the importance of integrating traditional construction practices with modern technologies to enhance environmental performance. The barriers to adopting these materials, including economic constraints, lack of awareness, and policy challenges, are also discussed. The insights derived from this review aim to guide policymakers, architects, and builders in promoting sustainable construction practices.

title: Quality monitoring in extrusion-based bioprinting: From defect formation to AI-driven detection and correction
2497f27ecb0a80c081f637e0b5d2ad5b16be7901.abstract: Extrusion-based bioprinting is widely used to fabricate cell-laden three-dimensional constructs, yet its structural integrity remains difficult to ensure because interactions among bioink rheology, process parameters, hardware and construct design produce defects that compromise the dimensional accuracy and cell viability of the bioprinted samples. This review organizes the structural defects along a causal chain, from root-cause factors to nozzle-level failures (clogging and buckling-induced filament curling), filament-level defects (size inconsistency, fusion, delamination, sagging, collapse and breakage) and construct-level inaccuracy. It then maps each defect class to the sensing modalities that have been shown to observe it, spanning surface imaging (optical and machine-vision imaging, microscopy, thermography, video-based vibrometry and laser profilometry), volumetric analysis (optical coherence tomography, X-ray computed tomography, magnetic resonance imaging and ultrasound) and process sensing (dielectric impedance spectroscopy and flow sensing). The methods are compared in terms of processing stage, reported resolution and target object. The evidence linking each defect class to each method is also mapped. Machine learning is assessed as an interpretation layer on these data, distinguishing classification, segmentation, anomaly scoring, open-loop prediction, and assisting corrective measures in printing. Key open challenges include the scarcity of shared, standardized datasets, limited external validation and regulatory frameworks, the absence of standardized defect definitions and the coupling between structural fidelity and cell viability, which together define the requirements for quality-assessment frameworks that can support clinical translation. Collectively, this review aims to provide a structured foundation for developing quality assessment frameworks capable of supporting the translation of extrusion-based bioprinting from laboratory research toward consistent, clinically viable fabrication.

title: Flock Management for Solar Grazing
container-title: Manufacturing & Service Operations Management
916481888e2bfc097e27a338e8a38f4b7c95a9e3.abstract: Problem definition: To control vegetation, solar asset owners employ farmers to graze sheep on solar sites. Whereas earning grazing revenue, farmers also provide agricultural value through raising and selling sheep. By accounting for flock dynamics of births, deaths, and sales, we model the operational economics of solar grazing for farmers and focus on key flock management decisions. Methodology/results: We model solar grazing operations as a finite-horizon linear program that jointly optimizes initial procurement decisions and subsequent sales decisions subject to age-structured flock dynamics and a target flock-size constraint. During the flock growth phase, the breed-versus-buy decision involves weighing the up-front costs and anticipated revenue from lamb and sheep sales against the heightened costs of vegetation management when the flock size is below its target level. By analyzing this trade-off, we demonstrate that the farmer’s total profit function is piecewise linear and concave in the number of sheep initially purchased externally. Beyond the flock growth phase, we prove that an optimal steady-state solution exhibits a maximum lifetime structure: ewes are retained up to a maximal age, and sales are restricted to lambs and final-year ewes. Finally, we extend the model to incorporate stochastic births and deaths, showing that a linear programming approach yields a tight bound on achievable performance in the stochastic model for large flocks and long horizons, and provide a practical policy that performs strongly in numerical examples. Managerial implications: Our results help small-scale farmers, renewable energy developers, and policymakers understand how solar grazing enhances the environmental benefits of solar farms, preserving agricultural value on land converted to solar use. In partnership with a solar-grazing platform that supports solar grazers and connects them with site owners, a spreadsheet implementation of our model has helped dozens of farmers make procurement decisions, predict cash flows, and even secure financing to purchase a flock. Funding: This work was partially supported by the National Science Foundation [Grant OAC 2410950]. Supplemental Material: The online appendix is available at https://doi.org/10.1287/msom.2025.0305 .

title: Jewish Identity, Occupation, and Earnings: The American Experience
container-title: Journal of Economics, Management and Religion
eca0d86af542cfbe4a9e92e11f31a02c3c6467e3.abstract: This paper studies how Jewish culture and social identity influenced the economic patterns of American Jews, focusing on immigrants to the United States at the turn of the 20th century and their American-born Jewish descendants. It identifies high levels of education for both men and women as a key factor leading to the clustering of Jews in relatively high-earning professional occupations. It examines four hypotheses for this pattern, finding that cultural characteristics associated with Judaism are the most consistent with economic evidence. The paper also considers some implications for changes over the course of the 20th century in American Jewish identity, religious institutions, and differences in education between Jews and others.

title: The Effect of Environmental Management Accounting on Company Performance Through Green Innovation with Stakeholder Pressure as A Moderation Variable in Companies in The Basic Industry and Chemical Sectors Listed on The Indonesia Stock Exchange For The Period 2021-2025
container-title: Jurnal Ilmiah Accusi
658d4f6f703a94abf4934b0f75737ee648e69db2.abstract: This study aims to analyze the effect of environmental management accounting (EMA) on firm performance through green innovation as an intervening variable, with stakeholder pressure as a moderating variable in basic materials and chemical sector companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) for the period 2021–2025. This study employs a quantitative approach using secondary data from annual reports and sustainability reports. The population consists of all basic materials and chemical sector companies listed on the IDX, and purposive sampling yielded 44 companies or 220 firm-year observations. EMA is measured using an environmental management accounting disclosure index, green innovation is measured using a green product and process innovation index, stakeholder pressure is measured using a composite stakeholder-pressure index, and firm performance is measured using return on assets (ROA). Data were analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) with SmartPLS 4.0. The results show that EMA has a significant positive effect on firm performance (β = 0.238, p < 0.001) and on green innovation (β = 0.356, p < 0.001); green innovation has a significant positive effect on firm performance (β = 0.312, p < 0.001) and partially mediates the effect of EMA on firm performance (VAF = 31.8%); and stakeholder pressure significantly strengthens the effect of green innovation on firm performance (interaction β = 0.176, p < 0.01). These findings imply that stakeholder pressure plays an important role in strengthening the contribution of green innovation to improved firm performance

title: Integrating multifunctional interfaces via chelation-driven chemical reconstruction enables efficient and durable perovskite solar cells
container-title: Materials Futures
3f8c2076c37d525da4e64e6e44f55252fefcdca1.abstract: Abstract Interfacial instability is a critical constraint for the practical deployment of perovskite solar cells (PSCs). It commonly arises from the metastable residual PbI 2 and deep-level defects like under-coordinated Pb 2+ . Herein, a benzeneseleninic acid (PSA)-enabled interfacial chemical reconstruction strategy, that simultaneously converts residual PbI 2 , mitigates interfacial defects, and stabilizes the perovskite lattice through synergistic bidentate chelation and hydrogen bonding, is reported to significantly improve the interfacial stability. Robust Pb–O–Se chelate structures can be formed via dual-site coordination between PSA with under-coordinated Pb 2+ and residual PbI 2 . This chelation-driven interfacial reconstruction not only eliminates detrimental defects at the interface but also induces ordered molecular self-assembly, in which outward-oriented phenyl groups form a hydrophobic barrier that blocks water/oxygen intrusion, while the interfacial dipole modulates the degree of energy-level matching, thereby markedly enhancing charge extraction efficiency. Meanwhile, PSA molecules stabilize the halide sublattice through hydrogen-bond interactions, suppressing ion migration and structural degradation. Consequently, PSA-treated PSCs exhibits markedly improved efficiency (from 23.68% to 26.56%) together with substantially enhanced stability, retains 87.8% of initial efficiency after 2000 h under 60% relative humidity.

title: Metabolic modeling: the link between AI and multi-omics data to accelerate the discovery of antibiotic-resistant traits in ESKAPE pathogens
container-title: Infection and Immunity
7ed95bf61237d995171ecce906cdf2fb609f6b80.abstract: ABSTRACT The development of predictive understanding of bacterial resistance to antibiotics is one of the greatest challenges of modern medicine. Genome-scale metabolic models (GEMs) are mathematical representations of the metabolic network of a given organism assembled from genomic data that predict cellular activity across many environmental and genetic contexts. Because a single model can be solved under thousands of conditions, GEMs generate data at scales that support downstream analysis with artificial intelligence tools, helping to elucidate how pathogens adapt to host environments, evade immune responses, and acquire resistance. Here, we review how GEMs of ESKAPE pathogens are built, what data they require, and what they can and cannot do. We describe the reconstruction workflow from automated draft network through manual curation, gap filling, and experimental validation and the public and experimental data sources each stage depends on. We then describe how accessory genes and transcriptomic measurements are incorporated to yield strain- and condition-specific models and where machine learning contributes both in expanding functional annotation and in consuming model-generated flux distributions. Applications are illustrated with ESKAPE examples throughout, including conserved metabolic vulnerabilities identified across strain collections and flux rewiring observed under antibiotic exposure. Despite this progress, high-quality GEMs exist for only a fraction of ESKAPE species; many are constrained by incomplete annotation or limited experimental validation, and non-metabolic resistance mechanisms are captured only insofar as they impose a metabolic cost. Providing reliable tools to build new models from trustworthy templates, therefore, remains a priority for narrowing the gap between genotype and phenotype.

title: Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) in Hotel Revenue Management
container-title: Accounting and Revenue Decisions in Hospitality
9ca9a6424d3d55fc5c3525966797b74721012e1d.abstract: Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) are central to hotel Revenue Management (RM) because they translate complex demand, pricing, and inventory-control decisions into measurable outcomes for managerial learning, accountability and benchmarking. For decades, the hotel sector relied heavily on a small canon of room-centric metrics. Yet contemporary hospitality markets challenge the sufficiency of traditional KPIs. Distribution costs and digital intermediaries make gross revenue measures less decision-relevant. Total Revenue Management broadens RM beyond rooms into food and beverage, function space, and ancillaries. In parallel, customer-centric measurement is rising but remains operationally constrained by data fragmentation and organizational silos. This chapter provides a comprehensive, educational and critical review of KPIs used in hotel RM. It traces the roots of major indicators and evaluates what each KPI reveals and conceals. The chapter proposes a modern KPI portfolio—rooms, net, total, and profit metrics complemented by process KPIs.

title: Integrating Accounting Information and Revenue Management for Strategic Decision Making in Hospitality
container-title: Accounting and Revenue Decisions in Hospitality
0599777283696aa339f0adbc46c5774871e13a32.abstract: This chapter examines how the integration of accounting information with revenue management enhances strategic decision-making in the hospitality sector. In a highly dynamic and demand-driven environment, hotels increasingly rely on real-time financial and operational data to optimize pricing, capacity utilization, and profitability. The chapter highlights the role of accounting systems in providing cost insights and performance metrics, such as RevPAR, ADR, and occupancy rates, which support effective revenue strategies. It further discusses how combining financial data with forecasting and segmentation techniques enables more informed and responsive decisions. While integration offers significant benefits in improving efficiency and competitiveness, challenges such as data fragmentation, system limitations, and skill gaps persist. The chapter concludes that a coordinated approach to accounting and revenue management is essential for achieving sustainable profitability and long-term strategic advantage in the hospitality industry.

title: Revenue Management Concepts and Pricing Logic in Hotels
container-title: Accounting and Revenue Decisions in Hospitality
f088a56bf85702568c80aadb65759b6cb57a32f4.abstract: Strategic management focuses on decisions shaping the future of businesses, while revenue management functions as a key strategic link within the value chain. In the tourism sector, traditional pricing approaches based on cost and demand have evolved due to the active role of guests in value creation. Perceived value, willingness to pay, and market positioning significantly influence pricing decisions, making it a multidimensional and multi-actor process. Therefore, relying solely on traditional indicators such as RevPAR, ADR, and occupancy rates is insufficient to explain today's strategic pricing logic. Although artificial intelligence and algorithmic systems enhance pricing efficiency, human judgment remains essential, especially in uncertain and crisis contexts. This chapter emphasizes the need to integrate analytical tools with managerial reasoning, offering a more holistic and strategic perspective on revenue management and pricing in accommodation businesses.

title: Corporate Governance and Internal Control Systems in Hotel Revenue Management
container-title: Accounting and Revenue Decisions in Hospitality
e0126bdebe012b1101abcc508490a08bd5fe39b8.abstract: This chapter develops a theoretically grounded and integrative analysis of corporate governance and internal control systems in the context of hotel revenue management. Within this architecture, internal control systems are examined as process-based mechanisms that operationalize governance objectives through risk assessment, control activities, monitoring, and reporting structures. The chapter argues that hotel revenue presents a distinctive empirical setting for governance and control analysis due to its perishability, simultaneity of production and consumption, decentralization across operational departments, and dependence on technology-mediated distribution channels. These characteristics intensify information asymmetries, increase exposure to opportunistic behavior, and amplify the need for robust control environments. Drawing on internationally recognized control frameworks and risk-based approaches, the chapter positions internal controls not merely as accounting safeguards but as embedded organizational processes shaped by cultural, technological, and governance determinants

title: Corporate Integrity and ESG in Hotel Revenue Management
container-title: Accounting and Revenue Decisions in Hospitality
10089985c80e377153f2330a22904b4faf135f35.abstract: The global business environment is being called upon to adapt to constantly changing conditions influenced by market globalization, rapid technological advancement, economic crises, and geopolitical tensions, financial scandals, the COVID-19 pandemic, and climate change. The hotel industry is also affected by these conditions, facing challenges related to fluctuating demand, strong seasonality, environmental crises, and the increasing level of digitization and technological innovation. The hotel industry operates in a new environment where the values of information quality, transparency, and adaptation to modern consumer expectations are paramount. The purpose of this chapter is to examine revenue management in hotel businesses, based on ESG practices and internal audit. The chapter contributes to the literature by proposing a holistic governance framework that demonstrates how corporate integrity, ESG criteria, and internal audit can support effective revenue management, strengthen organizational resilience, and promote sustainable value creation in hotel businesses.

title: Designing Surprise Bags for Surplus Foods
container-title: Manufacturing & Service Operations Management
2cc0a9a7b70f81a809cdb11fc256151fc79ea3af.abstract: Problem definition: Surplus-food marketplaces, such as Too Good To Go, enable retailers to monetize leftover inventory and reduce food waste by selling discounted “surprise bags.” Participating stores, however, face complex operational challenges. They must jointly set a reservation price and the number of bags made available before daily demand and end-of-day surplus are realized, while customers’ ex post experiences affect future demand through the platform’s rating system. Moreover, although evenly distributing surplus across bags is intuitive and operationally convenient, it remains unclear whether bag-value differentiation can improve consumer experience and profitability. Methodology/results: We study these questions through an infinite-horizon two-stage stochastic dynamic program. In each period, the store first sets a reservation price per bag and the number of bags available and then, after observing accepted reservations and surplus, allocates surplus food across surprise bags, potentially supplementing from regular inventory. We show that this infinite-dimensional allocation problem can be reduced to a scalar choice of average bag value. Specifically, the optimal allocation is characterized by the upper concave envelope of the consumer utility function and requires at most two bag types. Building on this structural reduction, we develop linear value-function and deterministic fluid approximations that provide explicit performance guarantees and transparent implementation rules. The linear value-function approximation captures most of the dynamic-program profit improvement and produces the lowest average modeled total waste across the main grid, while the deterministic fluid approximation yields transparent steady-state comparative statics. Managerial implications: Price and the reservation cap are not interchangeable: price shifts latent requests and customer net utility, whereas the cap truncates high-request realizations before surplus is known. This division of control provides a basis for platform decision-support tools that balance retailer profit with food recovery. Funding: Financial support by the Natural Sciences and Engineering Research Council of Canada [Grant 2024 05796] is gratefully acknowledged. Supplemental Material: The online appendix is available at https://doi.org/10.1287/msom.2026.0294 .

title: The ‘Digital Agenda’—Technological Protection Measures and Rights Management Information
container-title: The Law of Copyright and the WIPO Internet Treaties
b724a6edf7a9f4cb84b5b592c11a5f11e847c9d9.abstract: Abstract With the advent of online digital technologies, the view emerged that it would be impossible to exercise and enforce copyright in the new environment, because the rightholders would not be able to control the use of their works uploaded on the internet. It was in response to this opinion that the solution—expressed by the saying ‘the answer to the machine’—was proposed to use the same technology in order to preserve control by the rightholders in the form of digital rights management; that is, the combination of technical protection measures (TPMs) and rights management information (RMI). It was raised against the idea that an ‘access right’ might be granted in this way, which was rebutted by pointing out that there had always been some means to control access to works (otherwise they would have been freely available). It has been agreed upon that it should be left to the rightholders whether or not they apply digital rights management; and that the Treaties should just prohibit the unauthorized circumvention of TPMs and the removal or alteration of RMI.

title: Do AI Symptom Checkers Help or Hinder Timely Care-Seeking for Early Heart Disease? A Narrative Review of the Evidence by Insurance Status
container-title: Journal of High School Research
245892048b33dec027816966377c8fcebac9afd4.abstract: Cardiovascular disease killed 919,032 people in the United States in 2023, and how long people wait before getting help shapes much of that toll. The wait is not the same for everyone. In a 24-hospital U.S. registry, 48.6% of uninsured heart attack patients waited more than six hours, compared with 44.6% of insured patients who worried about costs and 39.3% of insured patients who did not. AI symptom checkers now show up at exactly the moment people decide whether to get care. Yet I found no study that measures whether using one changes how fast people seek care for heart symptoms, or whether the answer depends on insurance. This narrative review, organized with guidance from PRISMA 2020, pulls together evidence on four things: how accurate symptom checkers are, how they change people's plans for care, who uses them, and how insurance shapes the decision to seek cardiac care. I searched PubMed/MEDLINE and Google Scholar between June and September 2026, along with publisher, journal, and government websites, and checked the reference lists of key studies. Twenty-two sources form the core evidence base: 20 peer-reviewed studies and 2 survey reports that were not peer-reviewed. Because the studies ranged from simulated-case audits to national registries, I appraised each one with four questions (real patients or simulated cases, observed behavior or stated intention, independence from the tool's developer, and how representative the sample was) and synthesized the findings narratively. Following the Commonwealth Fund, I treated insurance as three levels: adequately insured, underinsured, and uninsured. The evidence cuts both ways. Symptom checkers reduce uncertainty and usually catch emergencies. But in the largest real-world dataset, users lowered the urgency of their care plans eight times as often as they raised it. Most tools triage no better than an average layperson, and in studies with real patients, 2-9% of cases were under-triaged. In a randomized trial, people using AI chatbots made no better care decisions than people using other sources. The typical user is insured, college-educated, and female, so little is known about the groups most likely to delay. I argue that insurance likely decides whether a symptom checker speeds care up or slows it down. Insured users can act on advice, or double-check it, at little cost. Uninsured and underinsured users are the least able to catch a falsely reassuring answer. Three hypotheses follow. Among adequately insured adults, prior symptom checker use will shorten the time to professional consultation for early cardiac symptoms. Among uninsured adults, it will not shorten that time and may lengthen it. Underinsured adults will fall in between, and pairing advice with navigation to low-cost care should narrow the gaps among the three groups. I outline an equity-focused design with measurable safety thresholds, such as sensitivity for emergencies of 95% or higher and harmful under-triage in 2% or fewer encounters, along with community health worker review and community governance. I also propose four studies to test the hypotheses: an audit of standardized cardiac cases, a prospective cohort stratified by insurance tier, a stepped-wedge trial of community health worker navigation, and qualitative interviews.

title: Multidisciplinary Approach to Antiplatelet Management in Coronary Syndromes: A Scientific Statement From the American Heart Association
container-title: Circulation
f864cfe486ac23fc87785b3d1757d8e90ed2b21d.abstract: Antiplatelet therapy is a cornerstone of care for patients with acute coronary syndrome and chronic coronary disease, yet its optimal use requires careful balancing of thrombotic risk reduction with bleeding complications. Since the mid-2000s, advances in stent technology, antiplatelet pharmacotherapy, procedural technique, and risk stratification tools have led to increasingly individualized approaches to antiplatelet management. Current guidelines and evidence emphasize tailoring agent selection, intensity, and duration of therapy according to patient-, procedure-, and disease-specific factors rather than a uniform strategy. However, the growing complexity of evidence, frequent care transitions, social determinants of health, and variability in patient characteristics have increased the risk of inappropriate prescribing, nonadherence, and adverse outcomes. This scientific statement reviews contemporary evidence informing antiplatelet strategies and highlights the critical role of the multidisciplinary cardiovascular team (interventional cardiology, general cardiology, pharmacists, advanced practice nurses) and the importance of their collective expertise in ensuring antithrombotic stewardship in patients with acute coronary syndrome and chronic coronary disease.

title: Berta, an Open-Source, Modular AI Scribe for Clinical Documentation: Implementation Report
container-title: JMIR Medical Informatics
f2df5d7b63b39635ad5f7aae8d112bd7749180cb.abstract: Abstract Background Clinical documentation is a major contributor to physician workload and burnout, particularly in high-acuity settings such as emergency departments. Ambient AI scribes have emerged as a response, but commercial products cost US $99 to more than US $600 per physician per month, operate as opaque systems, and often process data on vendor-controlled infrastructure. These characteristics limit organizational control over data sovereignty, quality improvement, and clinical workflows and create barriers to adoption in resource-constrained settings. Objective We aimed to develop an open-source, modular AI scribe platform that could be deployed entirely within institutional infrastructure, and to evaluate its real-world use across a provincial health system. Methods We developed Berta, an open-source, modular platform that pairs a Next.js front end and a FastAPI back end with configurable automatic speech recognition and large language model components. A closed-source implementation developed in parallel with Berta was deployed at Alberta Health Services (AHS), Canada’s largest provincially integrated health system at the time of implementation, and operated within AHS’s existing Snowflake AI Data Cloud infrastructure. All clinical audio and text remained within the secure AHS environment. Use and session metadata were automatically recorded during routine clinical use by emergency physicians across AHS between November 2024 and July 2025, and physicians were emailed an optional survey. Operating costs were estimated from Snowflake service consumption over the same period. Implementation (Results) During the 9-month study period, 197 emergency physicians registered at 105 urban and rural facilities used the system, generating 21,548 clinical sessions and more than 2700 hours of audio. Monthly session volume grew from 675 sessions in November 2024 to 5463 in July 2025. Mean recorded session length was 7.6 minutes, and 42% (82/197) of users customized at least 1 documentation template. Operating costs averaged less than US $30 per physician per month, representing a 70% to 95% reduction in cost compared with commercial subscription prices; this comparison excludes personnel costs for development and maintenance. Survey respondents (69-73 per item) rated user-friendliness as good (median 5, IQR 4-6), reported a median time saving of 16 to 30 (IQR 0-15 to 46-60) minutes per shift, and rated documentation quality the lowest. After the pilot, access was opened to other departments, and by September 30, 2026, approximately 2000 users had registered. Conclusions An in-house AI scribe can be deployed at provincial scale within existing health system infrastructure at a fraction of the operating cost of commercial alternatives while preserving data sovereignty and institutional control. The full cost of ownership and documentation quality require further evaluation. By releasing Berta publicly, we provide a reproducible foundation that health systems can adapt to evaluate and deploy AI documentation technology within their own secure environments.
