title: Is AI the End of the DMA As We Know It?
container-title: GRUR International
06f29e15676b1c1246b131e4c599fff0a384cd12.abstract: Abstract The disruptive potential of AI-enabled applications for competitive dynamics and the core organisational forms of digital intermediation inevitably also has significant implications for the recent regulatory initiatives adopted to govern digital markets. Indeed, because these instruments were conceived without AI specifically in mind, they risk becoming outdated within a very short period of time. Notably, while they have been shaped by a Big Tech-centred conception of digital markets, the possible emergence of new gatekeepers in the age of AI marks a turning point that calls into question the very rationale and foundations of these regimes in their present form. As a result, only a few years after its enactment, the role of the DMA, its rationale and its claimed future-proof character are already under scrutiny. The deployment of AI applications raises the question whether policymakers should reopen the legislative framework in order to amend the Regulation. Against this background and in the context of the first review of the DMA, the paper argues that the rise of AI applications calls for a reconsideration of the DMA’s overall architecture and for the development of a distinct competition policy framework, rather than for a merely incremental fine-tuning exercise.

title: Banking Risk Management in the Digital Era: A Systematic Literature Review
container-title: Jurnal Ilmiah Accusi
aa43112f086ecaec687a37ad1b6c2aa981b81f5f.abstract: Digital technologies are changing how banks originate, monitor and transmit risk, yet the empirical evidence on whether they make banks safer is scattered across risk types, technologies and institutional settings. This article reports a systematic review, conducted under PRISMA 2020, of empirical studies on the relationship between digital technologies and bank risk or risk management. A Scopus search of English-language journal articles published in 2020–2026 returned 857 records. Title and abstract screening and eligibility assessment left 85 eligible studies, from which 28 were selected purposively to maximise variation in risk type, region and research design. Twenty-two of the 28 use archival bank-level panels, four rely on manager surveys, one is a country-level cross-section and one analyses central bank data descriptively. Half of the studies come from China. The synthesis points to three results. First, digitalization more often lowers than raises credit, operational, market and overall risk: among the 21 archival studies with a direct risk outcome, 12 report reductions, 4 report increases and 5 report mixed or non-linear effects. Second, bank-level and system-level results diverge, because the same technologies that reduce idiosyncratic risk can raise interconnectedness and contagion. Third, internal control, model governance, cybersecurity, regulation, and bank size and ownership repeatedly condition the outcome. Drawing on contingency theory and the resource-based view, the article proposes a Digital Risk Governance Framework and five propositions for future research. The evidence base is geographically narrow and relies mostly on adoption proxies, which limits generalisation beyond large emerging-market banking systems

title: AI-Driven Transformation in Education and Business
9582d73b28887383a9b2b76978981d894f9ddb6a.abstract: Artificial Intelligence is rapidly reshaping the landscapes of education and business, driving innovation and redefining operational norms. The latest volume of the Advanced Series in Management brings together interdisciplinary perspectives to explore how AI technologies—from predictive analytics and automation, to adaptive learning systems—are enabling smarter decision-making, personalised experiences, and enhanced efficiency. At the same time, it critically examines the ethical, infrastructural, and skill-based challenges that accompany this digital shift, offering a balanced view of both promise and complexity. Bridging theory and practice, AI-Driven Transformation in Education and Business presents empirical research, real-world case studies, and policy insights that illuminate the evolving role of AI in organisational and educational contexts. It contributes to global conversations around digital transformation and sustainability, aligning with key UN Sustainable Development Goals such as Quality Education and Responsible Management. Ideal for scholars, students, and practitioners, this volume offers a comprehensive guide to navigating the AI-driven future, especially in a post-pandemic world where hybrid learning and intelligent business models are becoming the norm.

title: AI-Driven Transformation in Education and Business: Concepts, Contexts and Sustainable Pathways
container-title: AI-Driven Transformation in Education and Business
12c7a41ee43b34016c4d1e1b96a121e36b341f8a.abstract: Abstract Artificial intelligence (AI) has become a transformative facilitator for organizations in different industries, reshaping how organizations design processes, make decisions and aim for sustainable values. Though there have been intense examinations of AI and analysis tools and methodologies in past studies, there is a pressing need for a wide and competent understanding of the different dynamics of AI as a transformative tool in real-world contexts. To address this issue, this chapter develops a case study analysis of how AI is influencing education and businesses and develops definitions based on transformative analytics. In this chapter, real-life examples of how AI has or can transform big businesses, educational systems of a nation and college and university systems have been examined. In fact, examples of educational institutions illustrate how AI can impact teaching and governing as well as how it can be used at a systemic level for inclusion. In turn, examples of big businesses illustrate how AI can influence excellence in work processes and administration as well as innovation directed at environmental friendliness. This chapter does not only focus on AI adoption as an issue of technology adoption; it also emphasizes the transformative process as socio-technical in nature. This chapter conducts a cross-case analysis to identify common enablers, sector-specific obstacles and various patterns of transformations in both business and the education sector. These elements are further integrated to develop various sustainable AI-based pathways of transformation in relation to long-term institutional viability, ethical use of AI and social purpose.

title: Applications and Reflections on AI in the Field of Education
container-title: AI-Driven Transformation in Education and Business
5365282d93a3257359ddc4184742a198fe075dab.abstract: Abstract The cognitive artificial intelligence (AI) radically transforms the educational ecosystem through data-driven thinking and algorithmic optimization, which focuses on precision, personalization and collaboration of the educational process, leading to significant changes in metacognitive development, human-machine cognitive synergy and ethical considerations. This technology overcomes the barriers of traditional standardized teaching by dynamically adapting learning paths through cognitive diagnosis, intelligent content adaptation and personalized goal setting. Regarding the development of metacognitive abilities, AI visualized abstract thinking processes and identified self-directed learning capabilities as skills that can be taught and learnt through strategic training and dynamic modification, ultimately redefining them as talents. Nonetheless, the use of technology raises ethical issues, including educational equity, algorithmic bias, data privacy and diminished cognitive autonomy, as overreliance on AI and instant feedback may hinder students’ ability to think independently. This means that a future development should strike a balance between technological advancement and humanism, base technological orientation in human concern and find synergy between tool empowerment and human leadership to build up education to a more fair and equitable evolution.

title: AI-Driven Learning Analytics for Outcome-Based Education in Higher Education Institutions
container-title: AI-Driven Transformation in Education and Business
63f8a4644f6da71c2a6d76fa348694b1a741456d.abstract: Abstract With the recent emphasis on Outcome-Based Education (OBE), it has become even more essential that colleges and universities have excellent data-driven systems that are able to not only compile, evaluate and interpret learning evidence into measurable outcomes, but essentially do it accurately and comprehensively as well. The traditional way of implementing OBE tends to rely on imperfect assessment data, looking backward in time and lacking depth, which further handicaps it from being useful in executing continual enhancements and making rapid academic decisions as well. To address such a difficulty, there comes across a framework within this chapter that proposes needing data-driven systems that incorporate artificial intelligence (AI) into learning analytics as part of OBE systems as well. This chapter illustrates how AI is beneficial in increasing accuracy, monitoring, prediction and intelligent interventions regarding various types of institutional settings and is based on actual data and proves that primary data at an institutional level can be employed to reveal students’ actual engagement, their performance on tests and their success rates in accomplishing their goals within various programmes and academic cycles as well. To ensure that AI is used responsibly in the best interest of the institution and its stakeholders, the paper also addresses issues related to ethics, issues related to data governance challenges and readiness of the institution. This chapter offers a very useful and viable strategy for universities that are on a path of successful implementation of Outcome Based Education using AI learning analytics.

title: Artificial Intelligence-Powered Marketing 5.0 in the South Asian Business Sector
container-title: AI-Driven Transformation in Education and Business
e075d794091c0eb3faa3a951db8aae4619fcec56.abstract: Abstract This research explores the five core components of the revolutionary marketing phase of the ongoing era, Marketing 5.0, across diverse business sectors in South Asia. The study takes a qualitative, inductive approach to analyze primary and secondary data collected from exclusively picked marketing professionals’ opinions and insights, as well as published interviews on YouTube, blogs, academic papers, books focusing on relevant evidences in the context of South Asian business sectors. The research findings develop an integrated theoretical framework of the disciplines, applications and enablers of the concept ‘Technology for Humanity’ under artificial intelligence (AI)-powered marketing phenomena. The study upholds the synergistic value of the collaboration of humans and technologies complementing human cognitive skills with advanced technological skills in the post-pandemic world. The appropriate applications of AI-driven marketing approaches are evaluated in respect to close the widening generation gap, societal and digital polarization gap. The research concludes the foundational disciplines of the appropriate applications of AI-powered technologies for marketers, intended to create unique, yet inclusive and sustainable value that bridges these gaps while upholding the core value of humanity across the region.

title: The Future of Customer Experience: AI-Powered Personalization in Marketing 5.0
container-title: AI-Driven Transformation in Education and Business
15a7fa8476e2fcc39c7dd08d32d0cf3a092c663d.abstract: Abstract In this era of cut-throat marketing campaigns, where every brand is devising strategies to stand out and grab attention, traditional methods are often unable to establish the required customer connections. The future of effective customer experience (CX) lies in personalization, and artificial intelligence (AI) is truly a revolution in marketing personalization. Personalized marketing campaigns definitely increase the conversion rate by fostering deeper customer connections. Natural language processing (NLP) powered by AI is used to understand the customer sentiment. AI-powered chatbots and virtual assistants can provide personalized customer support. Huge data sets can be analyzed, and through predictive analytics, personalized campaigns can be created. This paper explores the potential of AI to develop personalized marketing experiences based on individual consumer preferences, behaviour and demographics.

title: AI Adoption in MSMEs: Opportunities, Barriers and Strategic Readiness in Emerging Economies
container-title: AI-Driven Transformation in Education and Business
d9f15671226e32d94f4685ff1c7039687a6d1af1.abstract: Abstract The adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) has become an important tool for harnessing competitiveness, learning and results of performance for micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) in emerging economies. Despite requiring greater policy emphasis and greater access to technology, little research data have been collected on emerging perceptions of AI opportunities, adoption challenges and strategic preparedness of MSMEs. In an endeavour to generate such research data, this chapter will examine AI adoption by MSMEs using data. The use of AI not only serves as an aid to organizations but also an innovation for organizations to acquire knowledge on data that influence performance outcomes on results. In this chapter, a survey-structured approach to the analysis is used, and a pragmatic and empirical method of data handling is used to describe MSMEs in operating crucial sectors of emerging nations. The descriptive and interpretational statistics, such as comparison of mean tests, correlation and regression, are used to spot trends in the adoption of AI, intensity of value creation sentiments, degree of constraint and readiness. These trends and patterns are spotted with the help of bar chart comparison, trend charts, scatter charts and heat maps, among others. The findings highlight that there is great potential for AI to make working more efficient for MSMEs, to help them make good decisions and to help them react better to the market.

title: Smart Supply Chains and Operations: Applications of Artificial Intelligence in Understanding Smart Logistics
container-title: AI-Driven Transformation in Education and Business
3a1efa1edc5ff915cf6ae21a3322f5d27b45e644.abstract: Abstract Smart Supply Chains is one of the evolving concepts in management. From making to procuring to sourcing products, everything is artificial intelligence (AI)-driven. The applications of AI, like warehouse optimization, real-time stock tracking and product optimization, are popular applications of AI. With the use and adoption of fuzzy models like artificial neural network (ANN) frameworks, the dependency on humans has eventually reduced, making smart AI ensure the best decisions for operations. The paper includes a case study and a study of a theoretical model known as Supply Chain Operations Reference (SCOR) (Model), which is very popularly used in supply chain management and tracking logistics. The process includes plan, source, make, deliver and return. This is a good framework applied with AI in automation logistics for smoother functioning. It includes the use of fuzzy algorithms, genetic models and ANN networks to efficiently update and track product specifications as well as the delivery process without much human interaction. The ANN model is popular and widely used in data science as well as behavioural science.

title: Industry 4.0 and the Future of Digital Strategy: Pathways to Digital Value Creation
container-title: AI-Driven Transformation in Education and Business
218150914ff06798dd0fe2d20c483286c0ae044d.abstract: Abstract The acceptance and addition of such progressive digital technologies into operational processes and decision-making platforms have totally redefined how businesses conceptualize strategy in Industry 4.0. This chapter explores how digital value creation (DVC), as a process, has been facilitated through Industry 4.0 technology, with digital strategy orientation (DSO) as the intermediary. For instance, employing a quantitative research strategy that focuses on theoretical constructs, the chapter integrates theories from dynamic capability theory, the resource-based view (RBV) and IT business value theory to explain how businesses achieve strategic and performance outcomes from their digital investments. Data collection entailed conducting surveys among managers whose business entities adopted Industry 4.0 technology. The examples given for Industry 4.0 technology were Internet of Things technology, artificial intelligence technology, analytics technology, automation technology and cyber-physical system technology. This chapter empirically explores Industry 4.0 technology and DVC and how Industry 4.0 technology influences DSO through structural equation modelling techniques. The results show that Industry 4.0 technology affects DVC both directly and through DSO. Digital strategy is an integral part of any business through which technology capabilities are actually linked with overall business goals. Organizations primarily benefit from the outcomes of a digital strategy by making their operations more efficient, starting new creative activities and gaining a competitive advantage in Industry 4.0. The findings quite clearly bring out that firms focusing on digital strategy are better positioned to achieve long-term value from their Industry 4.0 investments.

title: Building Resilient Supply Chains: Collaborative Approaches to Cybersecurity for Critical Infrastructure
container-title: AI-Driven Transformation in Education and Business
69ef3b4bd98fa812b47926725f643b3bbca05bd0.abstract: Abstract Cybersecurity resilience has become a major factor in determining the strength of the supply chain, especially in sectors which constitute the national critical infrastructure, such as energy, transport and healthcare industries. This chapter examines the importance of collaboration to cyber resiliency in interdependent supply chains. The analysis is carried out through a conceptual literature review in which synthesis of 122 scholarly and policy papers published from 2014 to 2025 is made based on the concept of a network that brings into consideration theories of supply chain resiliency, resource dependency, collective action, socio-technological system and network governance. Cybersecurity resilience can be achieved only when more than one player is involved in the network. Through collaboration, information exchange concerning the nature of the threats, addressing such threats and public and private partnership will make the environment less vulnerable to cyberattacks and therefore more flexible. On the other hand, fragmented environments where there is very little cooperation are likely to be victims of system failure. This chapter outlines a framework called the Collaborative Cyber Resilience Framework, which is made up of components such as threat environment, actors, collaboration mechanism, governance and cyber resilience outcomes. One of the most essential things about collaboration according to the Collaborative Cyber Resilience Framework is that coordination will make collaboration better and sustainable. This study contributes to the existing literature in this field through offering a theory-based cyber security approach that focuses on the network aspect.

title: Sustainable Business Models and Artificial Intelligence for Handicraft Entrepreneurship: A Cross-Cultural Case Study
container-title: AI-Driven Transformation in Education and Business
280c6ee15c3a60b7ae449cdd269f945d69496f05.abstract: Abstract Across the globe, handicrafts have been validating cultures, identities and traditions that have been present in the modern world. At the same time, the craftsmen who are a part of the process of manufacturing the product not only validate themselves on the capability of manufacturing the product but also sustain their culture, heritage and tradition. The case study would revolve around the process of preserving cultural heritage crafts with the aid of sustainable business practices with the help of advanced artificial intelligence (AI)-based explanations. The research would be carried out as compensation for the rigorous qualitative case study to perceive four different handicraft cultures. This would include Pattachitra paintings from India, Dokra metal casting from India, Moroccan carpets from Morocco and Talavera from Mexico. Based on the research carried out, it has been identified that with the aid of AI for design invention, quality declaration, prediction analysis and digital storytelling with sustainable business practices, companies can sustain their attractiveness.

title: Measuring What Matters: A Systematic Review and Future Agenda for Social Impact Assessment
container-title: AI-Driven Transformation in Education and Business
bdf8ea266b44fc56f97e644ac31e64fd09230ecc.abstract: Abstract The use of Social Impact Assessment (SIA) is indispensable when considering the consequences of changes occurring in organizations, policies and initiatives to the society in which we live. Unfortunately, the present methods of SIA are fragmentary, instrumentally driven and lack a theoretical basis. To address these weaknesses, in this chapter, an extensive study of the current scientific literature on SIA methods is conducted based on the PRISMA approach and conceptual thematic analysis as well as the assessment of theoretical foundation of each tool. The most popular SIA methodologies, including Social Return on Investment (SROI), Theory of Change, environmental, social and governance (ESG) principles, Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) criteria and well-being measures, are examined. This chapter proposes Adaptive Social Impact Measurement (ASIM) as a methodological meta-framework aiming to reinterpret the notion of measurement through its adaptability, participation and educative dimensions. While the traditional measurement approach relies on indicators, ASIM values an interactive, dynamic process of assessment enabling it to tackle such challenges as standardization and context, accountability and learning, control and empowerment, and other problems. From the conclusions drawn from this chapter, it is possible to state that the current stage of development implies not one methodology of measuring social impact but several ones. Furthermore, some directions for future research are suggested by the author, such as the application of artificial intelligence and big data techniques, participation, hybrid valuation, ethics and decolonizing methods.

title: AI-Enabled Talent Management: Transforming Recruitment, Performance and Employee Engagement
container-title: AI-Driven Transformation in Education and Business
9886b48584b8d91269b829bd1a85d226cfa82673.abstract: Abstract Artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly transforming the way organizations recruit, assess, engage and retain employees by transforming the way they do these in the organization. Although existing literature has deeply explored various AI-based tools and applications in the field of human resource management, there is a strong need for a theoretical understanding of how AI alters the basic principles of talent management as a practice. Addressing the need, in this chapter, a theoretical and integrative approach has been applied, applying various established theories in the realms of organization, human resource and behaviours as a way of reinterpreting talent management in the AI era. Counter to conventional thinking that regards AI as a mere technological advancement, in this analysis, AI-based talent management has been identified as a social, technical and strategic phenomenon that alters the way organizations recruit members, manage their performance and encourage them to work. This analysis has applied classical concepts such as Person–Job Fit Theory, Signalling Theory, Human Capital Theory, Goal Setting Theory, Expectancy Theory, Agency Theory, Job Demands–Resources Theory, Social Exchange Theory, Self-Determination Theory, Resource-Based View and Institutional Theory. This chapter develops these new viewpoints and constructs a conceptual framework for AI-enabled talent management. The framework describes how talent outcomes are impacted by AI capabilities via hiring, performance and engagement processes.

title: Ethical, Legal and Governance Challenges of AI Implementation in Education and Enterprises
container-title: AI-Driven Transformation in Education and Business
7c0f5e366e46844378f9d457494688d59e3b288a.abstract: Abstract The rapid application of artificial intelligence (AI) in schools and organizations has impacted the process of decision-making, performance measurement and value addition. In post-secondary education, AI-powered learning analytics is increasingly being employed to support outcome-oriented education. In organizations, AI solutions are being employed to enhance organizational operation, employee management and organizational-level decision-making. Nevertheless, emerging parallel to these advances, ethical, legal and governance (ELG)-related challenges have appeared to have immense potential to become important considerations for systematic and evidence-based analysis, rather than simply normative discussion (Floridi et al., 2018; Mittelstadt et al., 2016). This chapter applies a data-driven model for analysis of ethical, legal and governance-related concerns emerging due to the employment of AI within schools and organizations. This research avoids literature-based discussion for its focus by applying hypothetical but realistic primary research data to test concerns regarding privacy, bias, transparency, regulatory compliance and maturity in a governed context. Based on business enterprises and colleges, the chapter applies structured synthetic data in the application of comparative, correlational and descriptive analytics to uncover quantifiable risk exposure and governance readiness scores (Kshetri, 2021; Raji et al., 2020). This chapter is an application of pattern identification in the quantification of ethical risk vulnerabilities, regulatory issues of compliance and governance inadequacies in sectors through the application of tables, analytics and text analysis (Jobin et al., 2019).

title: AI时代编译原理分层实践教学改革

20ab3ed55c9eec8c5c7cff92eb971e6413e2ae68.abstract: 随着AI发展对软件开发与计算机教育的影响,地方工科高校的编译原理课程在课时压缩和学生基础差异明显。传统的从零手写完整编译器,学生容易感受到挫败,且实验成果仅停留于理论层面,学生学习兴趣不高。本文在原"课程实验+课程设计"的两阶段安排的基础上,探索面向工程应用和能力拓展的分层实践教学改革。改革中第一阶段开展AI协同的编译原理性实验,第二阶段保留编译系统集成的同时,增强编译理论的实际工程应用,相应地,实践考核改用编译系统集成保底,加应用拓展项目增值的组合方式。对比改革实施组与历史比较组的实验提交、代码相似度检测、答辩记录和归档作品,发现改革后完整编译流程完成率从70%多增长到99%,存在代码抄袭的作品比例从约20%降至约1%;课程设计作品类型也更加丰富。但是也存在着"程序能运行、代码难解释"、重度依赖AI整体构建和代码验证不足等问题。针对这些问题,本文提出编译各模块的接口约束、版本追溯、提示词记录与随机代码走查等手段,加强对学生学习过程的管理。由于本研究采用历史队列比较,相关结果主要用于呈现改革后的变化趋势,不能将其仅仅归因于AI工具使用的效果。

title: AI赋能民事诉讼法课程个性化学习路径的探索与思考
container-title: 教育发展论坛
46143faedda4629d8550ea202a220d616de22099.abstract: 以AI为代表的数智时代,对民事诉讼法的教学提出新挑战。传统的民事诉讼法教学存在着教学模式固化、学生被动学习、学情不客观、评价方式单一等问题,亟须进行全面而深刻的改革。AI赋能民事诉讼法个性化学习有现实的可行性,它符合国家教育教学改革政策导向,符合社会发展与学生培养需求,同时有强大的数智技术支持。AI可以从学情画像、学习资源供给、学习过程引导、学习评价反馈四个角度赋能,对前面提到的问题进行破冰,提供有针对性的措施,推动民事诉讼法课程个性化学习路径不断优化。

title: 生成式AI赋能的人才培养模式研究—基于数据计算及应用专业视角
container-title: 教育发展论坛
3e7a0248358a477fc0d098e23131f7b126d64ceb.abstract: 随着生成式AI的快速迭代,以生成式AI为代表的智能技术深度融入高等教育,已成为推动专业数字化转型、提升人才培养质量的核心路径。数据计算及应用专业作为新工科背景下的应用理科专业,具有理论性强、实践要求高、技术迭代快等特征。本研究立足生成式AI赋能教育的时代需求,明确数据计算及应用专业人才培养目标与能力定位,从课程体系、教学模式、实践平台、评价机制四个维度构建AI赋能人才培养路径,推动专业教学向智能化、个性化、实战化转型,为地方高校同类专业改革提供借鉴。

title: Minds Meet Machines: The Joint Role of Trust and Intellectual Humility in AI Persuasion
d8b7b16ca9c75a1deb3b83f3c4c11a9668b438b8.abstract: Research shows that AI models have a remarkable ability to change people’s minds following a short conversation, a notoriously difficult task for human communicators. Such persuasive paradigms provide a unique opportunity to examine which psychological characteristics predict receptivity to counter-attitudinal information. We focus on two characteristics: intellectual humility (IH), reflecting openness to revising one’s beliefs following new information, and trust in the information source (AI). To establish the role of a-priori dispositions that determine acceptance of new information, we ran two online studies, sampling British participants with a negative attitude toward legal immigrants (N = 294). We replicated previous findings showing significant and lasting attitude change following a brief exchange with GPT, but crucially, this effect was not uniform. In Study 1, attitude change was greatest among participants with higher initial trust in AIs and higher intellectual humility. Study 2 extended this finding by measuring both dispositions a week before the conversation with GPT, revealing the same pattern: opinion change was greatest among those who were both open to new information and trusting of its source. These findings highlight the centrality of recipient dispositions, suggesting that the relationship between source trust and persuasion depends on recipients' intellectual humility. More broadly, source trust may function as more than a heuristic cue, and its relationship with attitude change may depend on recipients' willingness to recognize the fallibility of their beliefs. Together, these findings extend perspectives on persuasion by highlighting the joint role of source trust and recipients' epistemic dispositions in belief revision.

title: Empowering the anesthesiologist: Navigating the future of AI-driven visualization and wearable technology in regional anesthesia
container-title: Perioperative Precision Medicine
b445412f8c53724ad77ef1c335303383faadf067.abstract: In current regional anesthesia practice, “visualization” typically refers to the real-time imaging and display of subcutaneous anatomical structures with ultrasound imaging, and “wearable technology” refers to hands-free, optical head-mounted displays (e.g., smart glasses) that can project digital information directly into the clinician’s field of view. The paradigm shift in the history of regional anesthesia from anatomical landmark techniques to ultrasound guidance has revolutionized the art of regional anesthesia and transformed a blind procedural technique into a visually guided intervention.

title:
Pedagogical Experiences, Challenges, and Ethical AI Use in Peer Writing Tutoring:
            Insights from the Azcapotzalco Writing Center (CEAZ)
container-title: Fuentes Humanísticas
08f4845584eb4b199eab416a27afce3bf5142738.abstract: El presente artículo busca reflexionar sobre los retos encontrados en la práctica del modelo de tutorías entre pares, en el Centro de Escritura Azcapotzalco (CEAZ), durante mi trayectoria como voluntario en el programa de tutores de escritura del 2024 al 2025, centrando la atención en los desafíos y usos éticos de la inteligencia artificial (IA) en los procesos de escritura, las aportaciones de la pedagogía de Paulo Freire en este modelo de aprendizaje y acompañamiento así como los desafíos de la aplicación del modelo con tutorados universitarios de distintas áreas del conocimiento.

title: Theoretical and methodological foundations of proactive operational efficiency management in mining companies
container-title: Mining Industry Journal (Gornaya Promyshlennost)
57c53a38f1cfaec079331b9a1065be2b4b3cdaa3.abstract: The study justifies theoretical and methodological foundations of proactive operational efficiency management in mining companies within the Industry 4.0 paradigm. Its relevance is explained by a divergence between the following two processes. The physical volume of the gross value added in the Russian mining industry declined by 1.7% in 2025 with the mining and geological conditions deteriorating measurably, e.g. the stripping ratio at the Polyus Group rose from 1.5 to 2.4 m³/t in a single year, while the coal production cost grew from 2,234 to 3,400 Rubles per tonne. At the same time, the utilization capacity factor of the open-pit excavators remains at 0.45–0.49 against 0.80–0.90 in the record-high months. A hypothesis is made that in the cyber-physical production the measurement costs cease to be an exogenous parameter and become a design variable, which shifts the whole configuration of the in-company control. The objective is to justify a conceptual model combining noninvasive real-time monitoring, dynamic labour rate setting and minimisation of the in-house transaction costs. The methods used include comparative analysis, content analysis of corporate reporting, decomposition of the equipment time fund and theoretical modelling. A four-level closed cybernetic control loop is proposed; control costs are decomposed into measurement, monitoring and enforcement; an observability index and a proactivity reserve are introduced. It is demonstrated that the selective photochronometry detects on average 1.6% of working time losses against 14.0% when recorded continuously at the same facility.

title: Autonomous drilling and blasting operations in open-pit mining: automation of the process cycle, drilling accuracy and management of blast fragmentation of rocks
container-title: Mining Industry Journal (Gornaya Promyshlennost)
aa9dcf538d35ad4d48281c57708fb055305a2d1f.abstract: Drilling and blasting is a basic stage of open-pit mining that governs the particle-size distribution in the muck pile and, consequently, the costs of excavation, haulage and processing. Blasting accounts for 20–35% of the mining cost and up to 90% of the rock breaking by volume. Manual operations cause drilling inaccuracy, excessive consumption of explosives, an increased oversize yield, higher seismicity and risks to personnel. The paper systematizes directions of drilling and blasting robotization across the following five process stages: drilling, pattern and charge design, charging, initiation and fragmentation diagnostics. It also introduces a unified five-level automation-maturity scale, i.e. manual → mechanized → automated → robotic → autonomous operations. An integral robotization efficiency index is proposed, with process weights normalized by their contribution to the effects. Fragmentation forecast is made using the Kuznetsov–Rammler model and the Swebrec function. The median fragment size shifts from 420 to 350 mm and the oversize yield drops from 7.8 to 2.9% for a model block (250 mm hole diameter). Industry effects of automation are generalized including a 50–75% reduction in the hole deviation, a 40–65% drop in oversize, a 5–12% decrease in the specific explosive consumption, a 10–20% gain in the drilling productivity and a 15–30% reduction in seismicity. In the typical and target scenarios the integral index equals 56% and 88%. Implementation barriers and a roadmap for drilling and blasting robotization within the process-control system and the digital twin of the pit are outlined.

title: Machines in the Middle: How AI Use Changes What Coworkers Think of, and Do for, One Another
26d21055970e127e32645343f5dd00f0c8042aa8.abstract: Generative AI is now embedded in how coworkers, leaders, and organizations communicate, yet its effects on the relationships among them are still poorly understood. This review synthesizes recent research on how an individual’s AI use changes the way others perceive, judge, and behave toward them, and shows that these effects can be explained by established theories of human-human interaction, including attribution theory, computers-as-social-actors, the integrative model of organizational trust, social exchange theory, and resource-based theories. The evidence suggests that observers often read AI use as a sign of disposition rather than circumstance, judging AI users as less competent, motivated, warm, and authentic, and that disclosure does not repair the resulting loss of trust. These perceptions carry over into behavior: coworkers reciprocate less, share less knowledge, and show less prosocial behavior toward AI users, while AI-related job insecurity, loneliness, and work alienation further strain ties among colleagues. AI use also loosens moral standards and shifts how blame is assigned, making people more critical of others’ work but more lenient toward misconduct. These effects are conditional rather than uniformly negative. AI can reduce loneliness, improve coordination, and prompt employees to invest more in emotionally supportive ties, and relational buffers such as leader-member exchange, shared leadership, and supervisor support can offset its costs. The review concludes that AI’s costs to workplace relationships run mainly through indirect pathways, not through the technology itself. It outlines organizational implications, including clear norms for when and why AI is used and protection of socially valued tasks, and identifies priorities for future research: longitudinal designs, team- and network-level studies, intervention research, and more diverse samples.

title: SOCIAL MEDIA IMPACTS ON SOCIETY AND MENTAL HEALTH: A STUDY WITH SPECIAL REFERENCE TO CHENNAI CITY
container-title: RCHUB JOURNAL OF CONTEMPORARY TRENDS IN MANAGEMENT COMMERCE AND ECONOMICS (JCMCE)
9f1b222b5ca4bfd25bf603891651156c7e4755da.abstract: This study aims to analyze the effects of social media on mental health and societal behavior, with a specific focus on the urban population of Chennai. Using a structured questionnaire administered to 174 respondents, the research examines demographic patterns of social media usage, the relationship between screen time and psychological well-being, and the perceived societal effects of digital engagement. The study found that platforms like WhatsApp, Instagram, and YouTube dominate usage – primarily for social connection and entertainment. Further, there is no statistically significant correlation between time spent on social media and mental health indicators such as anxiety, loneliness, or pressure. The study concluded with recommendations for healthier digital habits, including algorithmic transparency, content moderation, and features that promote mindful usage. These insights aim to inform strategies that foster mental well-being and social harmony in the digital age.

title: OSIRA, an AI Early Warning System Using Open Source Intelligence for Digital Fraud Prevention
container-title: Jurnal Teknika dan Informatika (JTI)
e11b2e99293184c34c74168bfca20102846b4736.abstract: Purpose: This study designs and evaluates OSIRA (Open Source Intelligence Risk Analyzer), an early warning system based on artificial intelligence that integrates Open Source Intelligence (OSINT) and Natural Language Processing (NLP) to identify digital fraud indications before they enter formal reporting mechanisms in a cashless society. Research Methodology: The study uses a design science approach consisting of problem analysis, system design, risk score formulation, and a limited scale proof of concept simulation. The simulation used 540 synthetic texts from 50 template groups, divided into 394 training and 146 testing texts through a group based split, and classified them with Term Frequency–Inverse Document Frequency (TF IDF) features and logistic regression. Results: OSIRA integrates web crawling, text preprocessing, fraud classification, entity extraction, a risk engine, and an early warning module. At a threshold of 0.50, the model achieved 82.88% accuracy, 79.66% precision, 98.95% recall, an F1 score of 88.26%, and a ROC AUC of 0.8528, but its false positive rate reached 47.06%, mainly for normal texts discussing fraud related topics. Conclusions: OSIRA shows initial feasibility as an additional intelligence layer that can shift fraud mitigation from reactive response toward proactive fraud intelligence. Limitations: The evaluation used synthetic rather than real OSINT data, a baseline classifier with limited contextual understanding, and risk score weights and thresholds that have not been empirically calibrated. Contributions: The study offers a conceptual and technical framework for using pre reporting public signals in fraud risk management and provides guidance for banks, digital wallet providers, and regulators.

title: Why being right can be wrong: intellectual humility as a key driver of responsible management education
container-title: Journal of Responsible Management Education
32c04fc037e745150d5c533c8ff75732d3792513.abstract: Purpose This article, written for the inaugural issue of the Journal of Responsible Management Education, argues that business schools, in their worthy pursuit of answers to management problems, often settle on one right answer to a problem. Yet rarely is the same answer right for everyone, everywhere and always. The notion of responsibility recognizes that the right answer often depends on the context. It proposes intellectual humility as the capacity that responsible management education most needs to cultivate. Design/methodology/approach The authors, who were the Chair and Vice Chair of the Advisory Board of the UN’s Principles for Responsible Management Education (PRME), develop a conceptual argument drawing on critiques of management education and the literature on intellectual humility. They illustrate the argument with PRME initiatives and extend it to the wider UN Global Compact. Findings Answers to management problems are contextual: they depend on whose perspective is taken and on the scale, place and time at which they are applied. Treating answers as universally right can close people off from others’ views, obscure the harms that emerge when actions scale up or persist and inhibit learning among both students and faculty. Grades, rankings and promotion criteria that reward the single right answer reinforce these tendencies. Originality/value The article reframes responsible management education as the cultivation of intellectual humility rather than the pursuit of a different set of right answers. It shows how PRME’s communities provide a foundation for widening the lens across perspectives, scales, places and time and proposes four research priorities organized around these lenses.

title: AI-driven urban futures from global trends to African perspectives
container-title: Built Environment Project and Asset Management
726707b9194a4b4f6f90a7f83729630b315efbe5.abstract: Purpose Despite rapid advances in Artificial Intelligence (AI), and specifically Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) for urban planning, a gap persists between these innovations and their applicability in African contexts shaped by informality, data scarcity, limited capacity and climate vulnerability. This study examines how GenAI is reshaping urban planning globally and assesses its relevance, adaptability and risks in African contexts, identifying pathways for inclusive, legitimate and context-sensitive deployment. Design/methodology/approach A systematic literature review used a Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA)-guided framework extended through PRALSMA (Preferred Reporting of AI-integrated Literature Search and Meta-Analysis), a reporting extension for transparent AI-assisted reviews. Peer-reviewed articles (2020–2025) from Web of Science and OpenAlex, with selected grey literature, gave 82 sources analysed through manual review and AI-assisted tools, with all outputs verified and triangulated for robustness and traceability. Findings GenAI is transforming urban planning through multimodal workflows enabling rapid scenario generation, visualisation and communication, but effectiveness depends on localisation, bias mitigation, institutional capacity and legitimacy. Without these, GenAI risks misleading or exclusionary “blueprint” solutions, underscoring the need for context-sensitive adaptation. Originality/value The study integrates creativity-in-design, relational agency and democratic design to frame GenAI as a socio-technical participant rather than an autonomous planner, offering an Africa-relevant agenda for responsible, human-centred implementation aligned with equity, sustainability and resilience.

title: Port performance and competitiveness: Evidence from the Port of Durban
container-title: Journal of Transport and Supply Chain Management
acc952ef47903724f3d4145cd83dcbfaba330284.abstract: Background: Efficient port systems are fundamental to facilitating trade and supporting economic growth within increasingly competitive global markets. However, persistent operational inefficiencies within the Port of Durban have raised concerns regarding its ability to sustain this role and maintain competitiveness. These inefficiencies have extended beyond operational boundaries, affecting trade reliability, logistics systems and broader economic outcomes, thereby necessitating a comprehensive evaluation of port performance within a global comparative context. Objectives: This study examined the operational performance of the Port of Durban and evaluated how infrastructure, governance, logistics integration and operational efficiency influence its competitiveness and broader economic contribution. The study further benchmarked the Port of Durban against leading regional and international ports to identify best practices for improving operational performance. Method: A secondary qualitative research design was adopted using academic literature, policy documents, institutional reports and industry publications. The evidence was analysed through thematic and comparative analysis to identify the key factors influencing port performance and competitiveness. Results: The findings indicate that the interaction of infrastructure quality, operational efficiency, governance effectiveness and logistics integration shapes port performance. Persistent congestion, equipment failures, declining rail performance and weak institutional coordination reduced operational efficiency, increased logistic costs and weakened the Port of Durban’s competitiveness relative to regional and global ports. Comparative benchmarking further demonstrated that sustained competitiveness depends on integrated governance, efficient operations and coordinated logistics systems rather than infrastructure capacity alone. Conclusion: The study concludes that improving the Port of Durban’s competitiveness requires coordinated interventions that strengthen operational efficiency, governance implementation, infrastructure maintenance and logistics integration. Contribution: By providing an integrated assessment of the factors influencing port performance, the study contributes to the literature on port competitiveness. It offers practical evidence to support policy and operational decision-making aimed at enhancing South Africa’s trade competitiveness.

title: Psychosocial drivers of occupational stress in industrial employees: implications for workplace health management
container-title: International Journal of Workplace Health Management
b8f6449f90941dcbab7c8ea7481085fc54bbba52.abstract: Purpose Occupational stress represents a major challenge for workplace health management, particularly in industrial environments where employees are exposed to multiple psychosocial and organizational pressures. This study aimed to examine the underlying dimensions of occupational stress among industrial employees and to identify key workplace indicators associated with elevated stress levels using an integrated analytical framework. Design/methodology/approach The dataset contained questionnaire records from 98 male employees in an Iranian industrial organization. Occupational stress was assessed using the 23-item Cooper questionnaire, with items scored from 0 to 5. Factor analysis and classification included 86 employees with complete Cooper responses. Entropy weighting described distributional information, exploratory factor analysis examined shared item variation, and k-means clustering explored response-pattern groupings. Classification models used five prespecified demographic and occupational predictors and were evaluated using 20 repetitions of stratified five-fold cross-validation. Held-out SHapley Additive exPlanations’ contributions were used to interpret logistic-regression predictions. Findings Factor analysis suggested a three-factor solution accounting for 33.1% of total standardized item variance, while clustering identified two provisional response-pattern groupings. Mean Area Under the Curve (AUC) values were 0.705, 0.698 and 0.686 for logistic regression, random forest and gradient boosting, respectively. Mean classification accuracy was close to the majority-class baseline. Work shift and work experience had the largest mean absolute contributions to logistic-regression predictions. Originality/value The analyses provide an exploratory basis for organizing employee questionnaire findings and guiding subsequent workforce assessment and consultation. Independent replication, external validation and prospective evaluation are needed to establish their practical value for workplace health management.

title: Empirical Pathway of the Influence of Technological Factors on  Acceptance to Adopt Industry 4.0 Technology Among Some Selected  SMES Within Bauchi State
container-title: IIARD INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF ECONOMICS AND BUSINESS MANAGEMENT
4c16385067851b481ac588d32c101cd3c3137cc2.abstract: The general objective of this research works was to assess and validate a Pathway of the Influence of Technological Factors on Acceptance to adopt Industry 4.0 Technology among some selected SMEs within Bauchi State. The increasing use of technology by firms for innovative manufacturing has necessitated the need to further understand the factors that influence the rate of technology adoption by Small and Medium Enterprises SMEs in Nigeria, specifically amongst SMEs in Bauchi State. Unified theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology (UTAUT) was used as the underpinning theory in this research work. Related literatures by various authors on Industry 4.0 Technology were reviewed, survey research method was adopted. Three formulated research questions were developed into three research hypotheses which guided the study. A structured questionnaire was the instrument used for data gathering and the population for the study was 627 registered SMEs in Bauchi South Senatorial districts while the sample size used was 35 selected SMEs. The Data collected was analyzed using Smart PLS SEM 4.0 and SPSS 20. The findings of the study revealed that, Perceived Relative Advantage (PRA), Perceived Compatibility (PCT) and Perceived Complexity (PCX) were found to be positively and significantly associated with SMEs intention to adopt industry 4.0 technologies. It was concluded that in order to remain competitive, it is important for SMEs to stay up to date with the latest trends in technology and techniques. Among the recommendation was that SMEs should endeavour to adopt the use of industry 4.0 technology facilities so as to maintain high standards of quality production to effectively satisfy the need of their customers.

title: Ventricular Tachycardia as the Sentinel Event for Intracardiac Cement Embolization: a Case Report on de-escalation to Conservative Management After Iatrogenic Fragmentation Following Percutaneous Retrieval Attempt
container-title: European Heart Journal - Case Reports
fdd82cafc8930249ab372403e4ce698ce400e04d.abstract: Abstract Background Cement-augmented pedicle screw fixation is an established technique in complex spinal surgery, but intracardiac and pulmonary cement embolization remain feared complications. Management is poorly standardized, particularly when percutaneous retrieval is attempted and fails. Case summary A 58-year-old woman with severe scoliosis underwent long-segment vertebral arthrodesis (T3–S1) at multiple levels. Intraoperative ventricular arrhythmia prompted postoperative imaging, which revealed a linear cement embolus spanning the right ventricular outflow tract and crossing the pulmonary valve. Percutaneous retrieval was attempted due to high-risk anatomical positioning but resulted in cement fragmentation and distal embolization into bilateral pulmonary segmental arteries. Following multidisciplinary reassessment confirming the absence of hemodynamic compromise, the strategy was de-escalated to anticoagulation and close surveillance. The patient recovered uneventfully. Discussion This case uniquely illustrates the management decision pathway when percutaneous retrieval fails. Fragmentation with distal embolization away from the pulmonary valve may represent an acceptable procedural endpoint permitting de-escalation to conservative management. The intraoperative arrhythmia served as a critical sentinel event guiding early diagnosis in the context of cement-augmented pedicle screw fixation, which is underrepresented in bone cement embolization literature compared to vertebroplasty/kyphoplasty.

title: Isavuconazole in the management of central nervous system fungal infections: Parenchymal penetration and clinical performance
container-title: Medical Mycology
b8277609d9ec49c6d05d00c8329d289fa94986a6.abstract: Abstract Invasive fungal infections (IFIs) involving the central nervous system (CNS) represent a critical challenge, with mortality of 50% or more in cerebral aspergillosis, mucormycosis, fusariosis and cryptococcal meningitis, and pharmacokinetic (PK) access restricted by the blood-brain barrier (BBB). This review analyzes the clinical performance and parenchymal penetration of isavuconazole (ISA), a second-generation triazole. ISA exhibits linear PK, a cyclodextrin-free intravenous formulation, and high tissue affinity, favored by moderate lipophilicity (experimental logP 2.56) and in vitro inhibition of P-glycoprotein and breast cancer resistance protein (BCRP) efflux transporters. Experimental evidence from animal models shows brain-to-plasma ratios of 0.42 to 1.8, indicating efficient BBB crossing. Human biopsy data show a fundamental PK dichotomy. While cerebrospinal fluid concentrations are restricted (about 1% of plasma), levels in fungal abscesses and inflamed parenchyma reach up to 5.11 mg/L, exceeding the minimum inhibitory concentration reported for Aspergillus fumigatus in those cases. Clinically, ISA was associated with a response in 70% of first-line (n = 10) and 73% of salvage-treated patients (n = 30) with cerebral aspergillosis, and 82% of 28 patients with CNS-only coccidioidomycosis improved or stabilized. Meta-analyses suggest fewer drug-related adverse events and, in randomized subgroups, fewer hepatobiliary events compared with voriconazole, although moderate cytochrome P450 3A4 inhibition warrants monitoring of calcineurin and mechanistic target of rapamycin (mTOR) inhibitors in transplant recipients. ISA is a strategic option for high-complexity CNS-involving IFIs, serving as a therapeutic alternative in salvage and prolonged-maintenance settings, though first-line use in CNS infection awaits confirmation from randomized trials.

title: Beyond TAM: a mediated-moderated analysis of perceived anthropomorphism and technology trust as catalysts for AI adoption
container-title: Global Knowledge, Memory and Communication
f42fc18f511ad00f2591df2314c14dd596c3b3e4.abstract: Purpose This study examines customers’ adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) in the Jordanian telecommunications sector by extending the technology acceptance model (TAM). Specifically, it aims to investigate the effects of perceived usefulness, perceived ease of use and perceived anthropomorphism on actual use of AI, while testing customer intention as a mediator and technology trust as a moderator. Design/methodology/approach A quantitative approach was employed. Data were collected through self-administered questionnaires from customers of telecommunications companies in Jordan. Using stratified random sampling, 482 questionnaires were distributed, and 438 valid responses were analyzed. Partial least squares structural equation modeling using SmartPLS 4 was applied to assess the measurement model, structural relationships, mediation effects and moderation effect. Findings The results show that perceived ease of use and perceived anthropomorphism significantly and positively influence customers’ intention to adopt AI, whereas perceived usefulness has no significant effect. Customer intention significantly predicts actual AI use and mediates the relationships between perceived ease of use, perceived anthropomorphism and actual AI use. However, intention does not mediate the relationship between perceived usefulness and actual AI use. Technology trust significantly moderates the relationship between customer intention and actual AI use. Practical implications Telecom providers should design AI-enabled services that are simple, intuitive, human-like and trustworthy. Managers should also communicate the tangible benefits of AI more clearly to strengthen customers’ usefulness perceptions and encourage sustained usage. Originality/value This study extends TAM by integrating perceived anthropomorphism and technology trust into a mediated-moderated model of AI adoption in an underexplored Middle Eastern telecommunications context.

title: Blockchain-based labour credential management system for construction labourers
container-title: Journal of Engineering, Design and Technology
fa6e48f89e2c6484f9054f97fe9a45338c32470b.abstract: Purpose The construction industry relies heavily on a diverse workforce whose credentials include identity information, certifications, trade qualifications, employment histories, training records and medical documentation. Effective management of these credentials is essential to ensure workforce reliability, compliance and safety. Managing large volumes of labour credential data requires the storage efficiency and operational capabilities of relational database systems. Accordingly, this study aims to propose a hybrid labour credential management system that integrates blockchain and relational database technologies to support secure credential storage, tamper-evident verification and interoperability across multiple construction organisations. Design/methodology/approach This study adopted a design science research methodology to design, develop and evaluate the proposed system. The architecture combines relational database storage with SHA-256 hashing, Merkle-tree aggregation and blockchain anchoring mechanisms to establish a secure credential verification environment. A prototype was developed and evaluated through internal and external validation involving ten construction industry professionals. Findings The findings demonstrated that the proposed system enables secure, efficient and tamper-evident credential verification while improving transparency, accessibility and trust in labour credential management. Originality/value The prevailing labour credential management practices remain fragmented, relying on paper-based records, isolated organisational databases and partially digitised systems. Such approaches create challenges related to interoperability, credential verification, data consistency and vulnerability to manipulation, limiting the reliability and accessibility of workforce information across organisations.

title: Spillover effects of algorithmic management on gig worker family life: the moderating roles of algorithmic transparency and work–family segmentation preference
container-title: International Journal of Manpower
bb01ceafe9fa57763ede991c0fa0fab6191424c3.abstract: Purpose Grounded in conservation of resources theory, this study examines the spillover effects of algorithmic management on family undermining and family satisfaction among gig workers through a moderated mediation model, aiming to elucidate the underlying mechanisms and boundary conditions of this cross-domain influence. Design/methodology/approach Two complementary studies were conducted to test the proposed model. Study 1 employed an online scenario-based experiment, and Study 2 utilized a three-wave survey design. Findings The results revealed that algorithmic management increases family undermining and decreases family satisfaction through work stress. Algorithmic transparency moderates the indirect effects of algorithmic management on work stress and family outcomes; work–family segmentation preference moderates the relationship between work stress and family outcomes as well as the mediated pathways. Originality/value This study uniquely contributes to the literature by extending the consequences of algorithmic management beyond the workplace into the family domain. It identifies work stress as a key mechanism and reveals how algorithmic transparency and work–family segmentation preference serve as important boundary conditions.

title: More than just small talk: situational patterns of informal workplace communication
container-title: Journal of Communication Management
a17d081c910e4c694ec6c53bf26cb306f8490ef7.abstract: Purpose Informal communication is a central but often overlooked aspect of organizational life. While its functions and outcomes are well documented, less is known about the situational contexts and patterns through which informal conversations unfold. Drawing on social affordances, Social Exchange Theory, and Social Identity Theory, this study examines how physical and social environments shape everyday workplace interactions. Design/methodology/approach Using a seven-day quantitative diary study, 209 employees documented 958 informal conversations, reporting topics, duration, location, participants and perceptions. Findings With the help of multilevel latent class analysis we identified six recurring communication situations that differ systematically in group size, duration, spatial context and topics: extended exchanges, canteen conversations, team talks, break banters, desk dialogs and chit-chats. Findings show that informal communication follows recurring patterns, reflecting the interplay of social relationships and environmental affordances. Originality/value By developing a situational typology, this study advances our understanding of how informal conversations are embedded in everyday organizational life and provides a framework for examining their role in coordination, social cohesion, and employee well-being.

title: Not passive sponges: When attention wanes, our brains are less synchronized with the environment
f7473977ec4a34b8dedb6c4470b752c5a3510de2.abstract: Without even being aware, humans are amazingly sensitive to the structures around them. Is this sensitivity constant or does it fluctuate along with our attentional states? To answer this foundational question, we deployed temporally sensitive measures that allow us to track neural entrainment—the synchronization of brain activity to environmental regularities—alongside fluctuations in attentional states. Participants (n = 78) viewed both random and structured visual streams while performing a task to index fluctuating attentional states. Structured streams evoked robust neural entrainment and reduced attentional lapses. Moreover, attentional states varied with neural entrainment. Across participants, those who displayed greater neural entrainment had reduced attentional lapses. And critically, even within individuals, greater entrainment was observed during periods of greater attentional focus. Our sensitivity to structure and attentional states are therefore inextricably linked: structures stabilize our attentional states and our sensitivity to structure dynamically mirrors the ebb and flow of human attention.

title: How fashion livestreamers co-create visual culture with Gen-Z audiences on livestream platform
container-title: Journal of Fashion Marketing and Management: An International Journal
df18003a6b98f16e2522b2c1437ba6c7b0a8af9d.abstract: Purpose As livestreaming becomes an increasingly important mode of digital interaction, fashion shopping streams are reshaping how style is performed and negotiated in real time. This study examines how fashion livestreamers communicate style to Gen Z audiences in Vietnam and how Gen Z viewers influence fashion performances through real-time interaction. Together, these perspectives illuminate how authenticity, identity and stylistic meaning are collaboratively produced during fashion livestreaming. Design/methodology/approach Guided by social performance theory and participatory culture, the study draws on 31 semi-structured interviews with fashion livestreamers and Gen Z viewers in Vietnam. Reflexive thematic analysis was used to examine how streamer performance and audience participation shape fashion livestream interactions. Findings Livestreamers combine curated presentation, improvisational styling and persona-building while continuously adapting to audience comments, emotional reactions and styling suggestions. Gen Z viewers actively influence outfit choices, aesthetic presentation and the direction of the performance. Through this real-time reciprocal negotiation, authenticity, identity and stylistic meaning are jointly constructed. Originality/value The study contributes a qualitative perspective to livestream commerce research by applying social performance theory to fashion livestreaming and highlighting audience participation as part of the unfolding performance itself. It further shows how fashion provides visual and symbolic resources through which streamers and viewers collaboratively negotiate style and identity in real time. The findings offer practical insights for fashion brands and creators seeking to develop more responsive and interactive livestream experiences.

title: Shall we innovate? Empirical evidence on SMEs’ readiness for innovation
container-title: Management Decision
fde11f67ac00d5eb6bdedf8b5edb8f0db6268004.abstract: Purpose This study empirically investigates the impact of small and medium-sized enterprises’ (SMEs) readiness for innovation on both their propensity to innovate and the radicalness of their innovations. It further analyzes the distinct factors that influence each stage of the innovation process. Design/methodology/approach Survey data were collected from 600 manufacturing SMEs located in Québec, Canada. A sample selection regression was employed to analyze both stages of SMEs’ innovation decisions: first, the decision to innovate, and second, the degree of radicalness in the chosen innovation. Findings The results indicate that readiness variables, including managerial acquiescence, employee engagement, customer alignment and channel integration, significantly and positively influence the radicalness of SME innovations. However, only managerial acquiescence and employee engagement are positively associated with the likelihood of innovation. Marginal analysis demonstrates that fostering a culture of innovation enhances both the likelihood and radicalness of innovation. The findings also suggest that innovation requires increased risk-taking and that internal learning from past setbacks is essential. Originality/value Organizational readiness for innovation and its operationalization have received limited attention in the literature, especially for SMEs. We investigate how particularities of innovation readiness, such as resource availability, leadership support and organizational culture, influence SMEs’ innovation decisions. We clarify how each variable influences both the propensity and radicalness of innovation outcomes. We aim to enhance understanding of innovation processes and provide practical implications for managerial interventions. This can help promote innovation and reduce project failures.

title: Social media platforms and innovation in UK fashion retail firms: a TOE–affordance explanation
container-title: Journal of Enterprise Information Management
88d2ced23ab08a83ffdf5d0e50e1811ae0e1dbb4.abstract: Purpose This study investigates how UK fashion retail firms use social media platforms to inform product and process innovation. Integrating the Technology–Organization–Environment (TOE) framework with affordance theory, it examines how platform-generated information is interpreted and applied to innovation-related decisions and the organisational conditions associated with these activities. Design/methodology/approach The study adopts an abductive qualitative design drawing on 60 semi-structured interviews with marketing managers across 12 UK fashion retail firms, conducted between June 2023 and April 2024. Interview evidence was supplemented by 328 archival artefacts, including company websites, online catalogues and social media content. Iterative qualitative coding, informed by Gioia et al. (2013), was used to develop empirical themes and theoretical interpretations. Findings The findings show how managers reported using social media information for product refinement, collaborative product development and changes to operational routines. These reported practices are examined through four analytical categories: product-incremental, product-radical, process-incremental and process-radical innovation. Incremental changes are more directly supported by the available evidence, while the magnitude of potentially radical changes remains uncertain. Platform features, including polls, analytics dashboards and creator interactions, provide opportunities for feedback collection, demand assessment and collaboration. Managers also identified technological compatibility, organisational readiness and cross-functional coordination as relevant to applying platform information. Ethics/general data protection regulation (GDPR) readiness is considered a proposed governance boundary condition rather than an empirically established influence. Research limitations/implications The study develops an exploratory TOE–affordance explanation of how social media information informs different innovation-related decisions. Its reliance on marketing managers' accounts, sector-specific setting and limited independent evidence of internal implementation constrain conclusions about causal relationships and innovation radicalness. The proposed relationships provide directions for further empirical investigation. Practical implications The Assess, Leverage, Invest, Govern, Network (ALIGN) managerial synthesis offers guidance on assessing technological compatibility, coordinating organisational functions, developing digital capabilities, governing platform use and accessing external knowledge. It is presented as a practical synthesis rather than an empirically validated framework. Originality/value The study contributes an exploratory explanation of how social media information is interpreted and applied to product and operational decisions under differing organisational conditions. It connects TOE conditions with affordance realisation while distinguishing empirically reported practices from proposed explanatory relationships.

title: When AI takes control, who takes responsibility? Structural analysis of agentic AI risks in supply chains
container-title: Industrial Management & Data Systems
856fe8a0aa1ef33e7ac05c1632f3b6d6a499b839.abstract: Purpose Agentic AI systems execute procurement decisions, reroute shipments and renegotiate supplier contracts at speeds that preclude real-time human review. The existing literature offers limited analytical attention to the risks that arise when decision authority is delegated to agents. This paper develops a risk taxonomy for agentic AI in supply chains and traces the hierarchical dependencies and influence magnitudes among the identified risks. Design/methodology/approach A systematic review of literature, analyzed through theories–characteristics–contexts–methods framework, produces the risk taxonomy. A hybrid modified total interpretive structural modeling and fuzzy decision-making trial and evaluation laboratory methodology is then applied to structured expert judgments to establish the causal hierarchy and quantify inter-risk influence. Findings Three risks, namely workforce skill gap, data quality and reliability and ethical misalignment occupy the deepest level of the causal hierarchy. Lack of accountability and governance and data privacy emerge as terminal outcomes. All three analytical methods converge on a conclusion: agentic AI risks originate at the institutional layer, with technical risks acting as transmission mechanisms. Practical implications The findings indicate that effective governance requires that workforce capability, data integrity and objective-function alignment are addressed before deployment. The stratified agentic AI governance framework is proposed that translates hierarchical structure into a sequenced intervention architecture, providing practitioners with governance priorities organized by risk-propagation logic. Originality/value This paper contributes a systematically derived risk taxonomy and a causally weighted governance map for agentic AI risks in supply chains. Five propositions are derived from the causal structure and are advanced as a testable research agenda.

title: Determinants of user-generated idea popularity in online knowledge communities: evidence from idea and user networks
container-title: Industrial Management & Data Systems
d27438b90e98af4030a65887780cac130df30dec.abstract: Purpose This study investigates how firms can effectively identify popular user-generated ideas within online knowledge communities. It focuses on how structural characteristics of idea and user networks jointly influence the popularity of user-submitted innovation ideas. Design/methodology/approach Drawing on longitudinal data from Miui.com, we constructed idea networks and user networks respectively, and linked network characteristics to the popularity of user-generated ideas. Using social network analysis and pooled ordinary least squares regression with time fixed effects, this study examined how key characteristics of idea networks (i.e. the betweenness centrality of focal idea) and user networks (i.e. cross-idea membership overlap) affect idea popularity, and how network density within both idea and user networks moderates these relationships. Findings The results show that the betweenness centrality of focal idea is positively associated with idea popularity, whereas cross-idea membership overlap has a negative association with idea popularity. Furthermore, higher network density within both idea and user networks strengthens the positive impact of betweenness centrality and amplifies the negative impact of cross-idea membership overlap. This study demonstrates that idea structural attributes and user interaction patterns collectively determine the public attention received by user innovations. Originality/value By integrating idea and user network perspectives, this study advances understanding of how firms can leverage community network structures to identify popular user-generated ideas. It contributes to the literature on open innovation and user-firm co-creation by demonstrating the co-evolutionary dynamics between user engagement and idea diffusion.

title: Toward resilient inter-organizational collaboration through boundary work: the perspective of frontline managers
container-title: Journal of Public Budgeting, Accounting & Financial Management
331db81b304ad5cc3a51eb7bea6041d35768b4ae.abstract: Purpose Public service organizations increasingly rely on inter-organizational collaboration to address complex societal problems that no single actor can manage alone. Public sector managers are representative for initiating and sustaining such collaboration. However, resilient inter-organizational collaboration is proven to be challenging in practice due to various forms of boundaries while previous research largely overlooks managerial boundary work from a processual view. This paper aims to enhance the understanding of developing resilient inter-organizational collaboration in public service organizations from the perspective of frontline managers who are directly involved in collaborative efforts across boundaries. Design/methodology/approach In this longitudinal qualitative single case study, we draw on participant observations of meetings and semi-structured interviews with frontline managers who represent five different caregivers in a new multi-disciplinary primary care model in a Swedish region. Our thematical analysis builds on 24 observed meetings and 10 interviews. Findings The findings show how the studied managers engage in three forms of collaborative boundary work in correspondence to three recurring boundaries in relation to administration, time and communication. The managers employ boundary work strategies in the form of managerial tactics to create a “third space”, embrace a complementary, proactive and accepting approach, and create a new “shared domain”. The tactics help to transform points of friction into points of connection and, ultimately, support the development of resilient inter-organizational collaboration. The paper contributes to research on inter-organizational collaboration by offering a processual understanding of how resilience actively unfolds through five managerial tactics in early stages of work to address common boundaries in relation to administration, time and communication. Secondly, it extends research on collaborative boundary work by illustrating how collaboration is developed through a trilogy of practices for the direct purpose of fostering collaboration in a situated inter-organizational setting with multiple boundaries and actors. Thirdly, it adds an important nuance to this theory by highlighting that collaborative boundary work practices are not inherently stable mechanisms but rather contingent upon the persistence of social conditions. Originality/value Whereas prior research often focuses on collaboration from a predominant instrumental perspective, this paper illustrates it as an unfolding process between individuals and demonstrates how resilient inter-organizational collaboration is possible to reach early on. The paper offers a novel angle on managerial boundary work in direct relation to collaboration.

title: Guest editorial: Human-centric retail transformation: from inclusive spaces to responsible sociotechnical systems
