title: The AI augmentation gap: data richness, automation and business value
container-title: EuroMed Journal of Business
a9d4693b4aede355f90e6e8d3722e0aafd2cb720.abstract: Purpose Grounded in the resource-based view (RBV), this study examines how data richness, as an organisational resource, is associated with business value through two deployment processes, automation and artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled augmentation, and whether they differ in their capacity to generate value. Design/methodology/approach Survey data from 366 Greek firms across four sectors were analysed using partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM) with bootstrapped mediation analysis and coefficient-difference tests; business value is measured as perceived value from digital technology. Findings Data richness is positively associated with both deployment processes. Automation is positively associated with business value and channels part of the association between data richness and value, whereas AI-enabled augmentation, the less developed process, shows no significant direct association; the difference is statistically significant, revealing an AI augmentation gap. Data richness also retains a significant direct association with value, and additional analyses suggest that the capability associations with value run through enacted digital transformation. Practical implications Firms should build a strategically governed data foundation, expand automation for near-term returns and develop augmentation as a longer-term capability built on skills, role redesign, validation and trust in AI-supported decisions; EuroMed policy instruments can be aligned with this sequencing. Originality/value Drawing on the RBV, the study shows that deployment processes of the same digital resource differ significantly in their association with value, a heterogeneity interpreted as reflecting the maturity of the complementary capabilities each requires, and provides evidence from a resource-constrained Mediterranean economy.

title: Modelling leadership capital and expenditures from a cybernetic perspective – monitoring, intervention, and contradiction under conditions of complexity
container-title: Strategy & Leadership
bdbcc442e5e775df92d94d4f8d49098221169974.abstract: Purpose From a cybernetic perspective, leadership can be approached as informed practices of status monitoring and intervention. This paper aims to use this approach to describe leadership capital and expenditures in complex-adaptive systems, addressing the efforts to keep an organization in the state of boundary stability between order and chaos. Design/methodology/approach Drawing on recent works on complexity leadership, the authors capture two different monitoring and intervention activities. One is directed at the creation of order, the other at its disturbance. A combination of both is needed to avoid both stagnation and complete disintegration. In consequence, it also becomes necessary to spend effort on handling contradictions resulting from this combination. To illustrate the validity and relevance of their approach, the authors discuss its application to (1) identify leadership capital and expenditures (2) understand implications of different leadership styles. Findings The model distinguishes three types of issues that leadership must address to enable successful management, which can be further broken down to monitoring, intervention and processing contradiction. This leads to a radically different account of leadership capital and expenditures than elsewhere in organizational studies. Requisite variety in the organization emerges as a critical factor regarding the frequency of interventions and confrontation with contradictions and tensions. Originality/value The model shows how leadership in complex-adaptive systems can be formalized to identify intangible assets for leadership in organizations, identify necessary expenditures and discuss strengths and weaknesses of different leadership practices. It departs from earlier work in cybernetics focusing exclusively on floating equilibria, shifting the focus on boundary stability between order and chaos as the goal of monitoring and intervention.

title: Beyond transactions: how relationship marketing management empowers exhibitor voice at B2B trade shows
container-title: Journal of Business & Industrial Marketing
85ac32a424ef55cbef16d40083d8c90516a6d762.abstract: Purpose This study aims to address a crucial gap in relationship marketing by examining how exhibitor voice behavior (EVB) fosters trust-based engagement in B2B trade shows. It examines how industrial relations climate (IRC), guanxi closeness (GC), exhibition identity (EI) and perceived organizational support (POS) jointly shape proactive communication and collaboration among exhibitors. Design/methodology/approach Using data from 333 exhibitors at the 24th China Xiamen International Stone Fair, a B2B trade show in China, we integrate structural equation modeling (SEM) and fuzzy-set qualitative comparative analysis (fsQCA). Guided by industrial relations theory and the stimulus–organism–response framework, it tests the mediating roles of GC and EI and the moderating role of POS. Findings Results show that IRC does not directly predict EVB but operates through relational mechanisms, with EI emerging as a stronger motivator than GC. POS significantly strengthens the IRC–EVB relationship. The fsQCA results identify multiple pathways, particularly those involving EI and POS, illustrating equifinality in exhibitor engagement within the trade show setting. Practical implications Trade show organizers and capital stakeholders should cultivate a supportive relational climate, strengthen exhibitor identity and trust and provide authentic organizational support. Governments and associations can enhance policy incentives and training programs to promote collaboration and sustainable trade show development. Originality/value This study extends IRC research to EVB in temporary B2B trade shows. It identifies EI as a stronger driver than GC and demonstrates POS as an important boundary condition. By combining SEM and fsQCA, the study reveals multiple pathways to exhibitor engagement and offers a context-sensitive framework for advancing relationship marketing research in trade shows.

title: Architectural hedging capacity: preserving strategic optionality in AI provider relationships
container-title: Strategy & Leadership
1f10cf4b1b679b2084257feedf9f44642c6acab3.abstract: Purpose Firms increasingly depend on a small number of external providers for artificial intelligence (AI) models, yet that dependence is not only imposed by supplier concentration; it can also be reproduced by a firm’s own technology-integration decisions. This paper aims to examine how provider-specific integration progressively erodes a firm’s ability to switch providers, and what company leadership can do about it. Design/methodology/approach This paper is conceptual. Using resource dependence theory as its base, it draws on transaction cost economics, modularity and real options reasoning, organisational routines theory, and the attention-based view to develop a mechanism and an organisational capability, formalised in four core propositions, a typology matrix and a remedy audit. Findings The paper develops integration drift, a reinforcing process in which locally rational integration decisions cumulatively raise the cost of switching providers. It also introduces architectural hedging capacity (AHC), an organisational capability enacted through three recurring routines: governance-enforced modularity, rehearsed recalibration and sustained managerial attention. And lastly, the argument also identifies a boundary condition in resource dependence theory: where dependence is continuously reproduced through organisational integration, maintaining autonomy requires continuously reproduced exit capacity rather than a one-time remedy. Originality/value The paper extends resource dependence theory to settings where dependence is reproduced inside the firm through its own architecture, not only imposed externally. A typology and a remedy audit checklist give boards and managers a diagnostic for assessing and managing AI-provider dependence.

title: When AI signalling backfires: a threshold model of perceived firm innovativeness
container-title: Journal of Services Marketing
e7ff3a52b723ffba9e1d77084570515269cb1034.abstract: Purpose This study aims to interrogate the implicit monotonicity assumption in service-dominant logic by examining whether AI signalling intensity uniformly enhances perceived firm innovativeness (PFI) or exhibits threshold-dependent fragility. The study empirically validates relational coherence as a perception-level mediating state, thereby confirming its role as the integrator of AI-enabled capability inference, and specifies structural and demographic boundary conditions. Design/methodology/approach A two-study archival design tests the proposed threshold model. Study 1 exploits discrete AI capability announcements among 1,012 Asian service firms (2012–2024) using event-study difference-in-differences to identify dynamic shifts in customer text-based PFI. Study 2 estimates a dynamic panel system generalised method of moments model incorporating lagged PFI, non-linear AI intensity and relational coherence, addressing reverse causality and omitted capability shocks while computing turning points and moderated curvature. Findings AI signalling exhibits an inverted-U relationship with PFI: moderate intensity strengthens capability perception, whereas high intensity attenuates and reverses effects. Relational coherence mediates this relationship, with the indirect pathway weakening and becoming negative beyond a calculable threshold. The curvature steepens and the threshold occurs earlier in high-contact services and firms serving older customer segments. Originality/value The study advances service-dominant logic by introducing threshold-fragility into its resource-integration premise, repositioning technological operant resources as legitimacy-constrained rather than uniformly accretive. It conceptualises relational coherence as the perception-level integrator governing AI-enabled capability inference and embeds demographic and structural heterogeneity within a formally identified non-linear, dynamic analytical model structure.

title: Lean∼Green enhancing sustainable construction: from fragmented practices to simultaneous approaches
container-title: Engineering, Construction and Architectural Management
af5b059436976e9ecdd7b3e9a4e93810f8994786.abstract: Purpose The construction industry faces persistent challenges related to low productivity, high operational variability, and significant environmental impacts. In this context, lean construction (LC) and green construction (GC) approaches emerge as strategies capable of reconciling operational efficiency and sustainability. Despite recent advances, a scientific and applied gap persists, reflected in the absence of empirically grounded models to guide the coordinated application of these approaches and in the limited evidence of effective LC and GC integration in construction projects, which often occur only in parallel (Lean∼Green). To address this gap, this study proposes a framework with guidelines to support the integrated use of LC and GC in the construction industry. Design/methodology/approach A multiple case study methodology was adopted, encompassing six industrial logistics construction projects in Brazil with different levels of Lean and Green maturity. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews, on-site observations and document analysis, enabling systematic triangulation of evidence. A comparative cross-case analysis was conducted between Lean∼Green projects, exclusively Lean projects and conventional projects (without a formal approach), examining differences in operational, environmental and organizational performance. Findings The results indicate that Lean∼Green projects achieve more balanced and consistent performance across quality, safety and environmental dimensions, even in the absence of formal consolidation between LC and GC. Clear synergies were observed in waste reduction, process traceability and environmental performance. Lean-only projects exhibited relevant operational improvements but more limited environmental outcomes, while conventional projects showed lower and more variable performance. The findings also suggest that the observed improvements are associated with progressive organizational alignment of planning, indicators and governance mechanisms that support the joint management of operational and environmental objectives. Originality/value This study advances the Lean∼Green literature by providing comparative empirical evidence from multiple projects with different maturity levels and by proposing an organized framework that operationalizes Lean∼Green integration into a structured and practice-oriented implementation pathway. The results suggest that Lean∼Green can be understood as an evolutionary stage in sustainable construction management, in which efficiency and environmental performance progressively converge through organizational coordination mechanisms. The framework offers a practice-oriented pathway for organizations seeking to enhance competitiveness, transparency and environmental performance in construction projects.

title: Bridging the intention–behavior gap in green fashion: evidence from an emerging market
container-title: Management & Sustainability: An Arab Review
b43e8bba23c8456714a6aa8fffdcade15b973bc6.abstract: Purpose The purpose of this study is to examine the impact of Environmental Concern and Perceived Value; along with its four dimensions, on green fashion Purchase Intention in Egypt, as well as exploring whether an intention-behavior gap exists in this context. It aims to address the limited research on sustainable consumption in the MENA region. Design/methodology/approach A positivist philosophy and deductive approach were adopted. A structured questionnaire, prepared in both English and Arabic, was distributed online, yielding 424 valid responses. Data were analyzed using SPSS for descriptive statistics and SmartPLS 4 for Structural Equation Modeling (SEM). Findings Results show that environmental concern and perceived value significantly impact green fashion purchase intention. However, regarding the dimensions of perceived value, only perceived quality and emotional values had a significant impact, while perceived price and social values did not. Purchase intention was also found to significantly impact actual purchase behavior, suggesting an evidence of intention translating into self-reported purchase behavior within this sample in Egypt’s green fashion sector. Practical implications It is evident that marketers of green fashion in Egypt should emphasize on environmental, quality, and emotional benefits in their marketing strategies. Additionally, it is important for policymakers and stakeholders in the industry to promote environmental awareness as well as provide information regarding the environmental benefits of green fashion products. Furthermore, since the intention-behavior link is significant, it is imperative to ensure that consumers have easy access to green fashion products. Originality/value This study contributes to the green fashion literature by developing a comprehensive model; combining consumer-specific (environmental concern) and product-specific (perceived value) factors, while providing evidence from Egypt, a non-Western and underexplored market. It contributes to a more holistic understanding of sustainable consumer behavior in emerging economies.

title: Integrated assessment technology for heritage building restoration: a structural equation modelling approach
container-title: Engineering, Construction and Architectural Management
e0550d003251d90e76b6c69c8e1ec6a6d6588f8e.abstract: Purpose This research develops and validates a comprehensive technology-based assessment system for heritage building restoration that integrates project management triangle factors with adaptive reuse sustainability factors, addressing the critical gap in standardized evaluation frameworks for developing countries. Design/methodology/approach The research design used structural equation modelling-partial least squares, data were collected from 100 construction professionals across seven heritage buildings in Java Island, Indonesia. The model integrates capital investment, asset condition and regulatory factors with scope, time and cost management dimensions through advanced psychometric validation. Findings The data collected from 100 construction professional in Indonesia, and the results reveal capital investment as the dominant factor influencing project management outcomes (β = 0.481–0.567), while regulatory factors show moderate relationships particularly with scope management (β = 0.328). Asset condition exhibits weaker associations, reflecting funding prioritization over technical considerations in developing country contexts. The system explains 29.8–44.5% variance in project management constructs with strong psychometric properties (Construct Realibility (CR) &gt; 0.7, average variance extracted &gt;0.5) and acceptable fit (SRMR = 0.076, Normed Fit Index (NFI) = 0.912). Originality/value This research provides the first empirically validated integrated assessment technology combining adaptive reuse sustainability factors with project management principles in heritage restoration contexts, offering practitioners systematic tools for feasibility assessment and resource optimization through rigorous quantitative validation in Southeast Asian developing country settings.

title: Accidental supply chains: an exploratory study of social enterprise coordination in Australian organics recovery
container-title: The International Journal of Logistics Management
24035be78ab1c1d7bdd11ea5d1ec7ccaa9decf4e.abstract: Purpose To explain how social enterprises coordinate circular organics recovery in regional settings where formal infrastructure is incomplete and institutional support remains thin. Design/methodology/approach A qualitative, abductive multiple-case study of two Australian organics recovery arrangements, drawing on 26 semi-structured interviews, site observations, documentary sources and iterative tracing of material flows and coordination over time. Findings Circular coordination developed through four overlapping phases: initiation, stabilisation, legitimation and institutionalisation. Repeated routines and micro-infrastructure, supported by relationship-based brokerage, made recovery workable amid structural, socio-political and emergent complexity. Supply-chain championing was centralised in SoilCo and decentralised in CoffeeCos, but remained active across the full process. Greater visibility strengthened legitimacy and formalisation while also creating new scrutiny and operating burdens, including competition for previously unwanted material. Research limitations/implications The study prioritises analytical depth in two Australian organics recovery cases. Research across other materials and institutional settings could test the scope and boundary conditions of accidental supply chains. Practical implications Regional circularity requires investment in coordination and relationship-based governance, as well as low-capital storage and consolidation alongside major infrastructure. Social implications Regional organics recovery can generate locally visible environmental and community benefits by connecting waste generators with local users. Sustaining these benefits depends on trust, participation and place-based coordination across the pathway. Originality/value The article conceptualises accidental supply chains as a distinct organising mode in which deliberate local action produces a recognisable supply architecture through repeated practice without prior blueprinting.

title: Costs and benefits of digital twin adoption in UK construction: a statistically tested stakeholder perception study
container-title: Engineering, Construction and Architectural Management
b8d72e1132678c81dadf3be8e04b23d107bee0c8.abstract: Purpose There is limited quantitative data on the weighting of costs and benefits of digital twin (DT) for stakeholders in the UK and this paper re-tests sub-group differences from a 2022 survey. Design/methodology/approach The 74 members of DTHub rated 15 benefits and 10 costs (scale of 0–4) and ranked both by Relative Importance Index (RII) (full sample) as well as two experience-based sub-samples (Group A n = 17; Group B n = 57). Corrected Mann-Whitney U and Kruskal-Wallis H tests were used to explore differences and Spearman correlations were used for rank agreement. Findings Operational benefits (Lean Construction, Effective Data Sharing, Improved Decision Making, Construction 4.0) topped net-zero and United Nations (UN) Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) benefits. Artificial Intelligence (AI) Components, Skilled Personnel and IoT Devices/Systems were the top-rated costs. There were no significant differences between sub-groups after correction (groups shared similar priorities of benefits, but not costs). Research limitations/implications Due to the small, self-selected sample (n = 74; Group A n = 17), this limits the power of the study and null results are not confirmatory. Larger replication (mixed methods) across contexts is recommended. Practical implications Operational benefits should be the main consideration for a new DT framework. For the dominant costs, coordinated investments between industry, government and education in AI, skills and IoT are needed; for the environmental-perception gap, evidence, not communication is needed. Originality/value One of the first construction DT RII studies to formally test differences in sub-group rank with dual correction, providing a tested baseline for research following Centre for Digital Built Britain and a transferable example of RII research.

title: The impact of explorative generative AI usage on construction project professionals' innovative work behavior: a technology affordance actualization perspective
container-title: Engineering, Construction and Architectural Management
d4b9feb8355cb976dddf7887f9e4fb88383051a9.abstract: Purpose This study attempts to investigate the influence of generative AI (GenAI) on construction project professionals' innovation, specifically by exploring how and under what contextual conditions the use of GenAI fosters innovative work behavior. Design/methodology/approach Grounded in the technology affordance actualization perspective, we identified explorative GenAI usage as the critical trigger of innovative work behavior, specifically by boosting knowledge acquisition, and organizational support as a buffer of the translating process. The theoretical model was empirically tested using the structural equation modeling approach with 239 valid responses from the Chinese construction industry. Findings The findings reveal that explorative GenAI usage acts as a critical actualization behavior that significantly enhances construction project professionals' knowledge acquisition, which subsequently empowers their innovative work behavior. Crucially, this study highlights that the positive effects of explorative GenAI usage are valid when organizational support is high, instead of low. Originality/value This study contributes to construction project management literature by deepening the understanding of the impact of emerging GenAI on micro-level individual behavioral patterns and provides valuable implications for construction managers in today's GenAI era.

title: Beyond competence: how organisational recognition and digital visibility shape women's leadership progression in project-based organisations
container-title: Engineering, Construction and Architectural Management
ef663e4072a8411033d854a1b83cadfa43a8133c.abstract: Purpose This study examines how organisational recognition and digital visibility shape women's leadership progression in project-based organisations. It moves beyond the view that leadership progression depends only on individual capability and explores how women's competencies are developed, made visible and recognised within gendered project environments. Design/methodology/approach A qualitative approach was used, based on semi-structured interviews with 23 women leaders working in project-based organisations across Australia. Participants were recruited through purposive and snowball sampling. Data were analysed using thematic analysis supported by NVivo, with social role theory guiding the interpretation of gendered expectations and recognition processes. Findings The findings show that women's leadership progression depends on the interaction between relational, strategic and execution-based competencies. Communication, stakeholder engagement, decision-making, risk awareness, problem-solving, planning, coordination and governance awareness helped women build trust, credibility and delivery capability. However, these competencies did not automatically translate into leadership progression. Organisational recognition was central to whether women's competencies were valued and translated into leadership opportunities. Gendered workplace norms often reduced the visibility of relational and coordination work by treating it as expected support work rather than leadership. Digital technologies supported competency visibility, flexibility, communication and evidence-based decision-making, but also created challenges through digital overload, limited training, workload pressure and reduced informal visibility. Research limitations/implications This study is based on a qualitative sample of 23 women leaders in Australia, and the findings reflect self-reported experiences within a cross-sectional design. Longitudinal and cross-cultural research would help clarify how leadership progression and organisational recognition evolve over time and across different national contexts. Practical implications Project-based organisations, particularly HR managers and project directors, need to move beyond competency development alone. Promotion criteria, project allocation and formal sponsorship should be designed to make women's leadership work visible and explicitly recognised, supported by deliberate use of digital tools and by monitoring invisible labour. Originality/value This study contributes to project leadership and gender research by shifting attention from competency possession to competency recognition. It develops a gender-responsive leadership progression framework that explains how leadership competencies are translated into women's leadership progression through competency visibility and organisational recognition and extends social role theory by identifying system-mediated visibility, recognition shaped by digital infrastructure rather than direct observation, as a second pathway through which gendered expectations operate.

title: Development and validation of a measure of work decision styles
container-title: Management Decision
e992e2d2b009e199610514d1005486105e8e79f8.abstract: Purpose This paper aims to develop a contextualized measure of decision style to assess a person's decision-making tendencies in the workplace. Design/methodology/approach Four studies examined the content, structural, construct, criterion-related, and incremental validity of the Work Decision Style (WDS) measure. Study 1 provides content validity ratings for the initial item pool. Study 2 refines the scale to 20 items via exploratory and confirmatory factor analysis. IRT analyses show strong measurement precision for all 20 items and useful test information for each dimension. Study 3 shows that WDS scale scores converge with scores on other general decision-making measures and correlate predictably with external correlates. Study 4 provides criterion-related and incremental validity evidence for the WDS predicting self-reported job performance criteria. Findings The WDS is a reliable and valid measure of analytical, intuitive, collaborative, and decisive work-related decision-making styles. Research limitations/implications The WDS allows for job-relevant and nuanced prediction of work-related criteria, facilitating future research on decision styles in work contexts. Investigation of the WDS alongside varied work decision-making tasks, situations, and outcomes will improve our understanding of how each style functions in context. Practical implications The WDS is a decision-making style measure specifically developed and validated for a work context. It is uniquely relevant for application in organizational settings, a critical domain in which to understand and improve decision-making. Originality/value We are unaware of an existing, valid, measure of decision styles for use in a work setting. The work-related decision-making style (WDS) measure fills this gap, facilitating the measurement and understanding of decision-making styles in the workplace.

title: External knowledge processing in the fuzzy front end: functional perspectives, capability interdependencies and coordination interfaces
container-title: Journal of Enterprise Information Management
2fe7a445dcf1bae1def16e7671231523cbc381fd.abstract: Purpose This study examines how knowledge identification capability (KIC), knowledge acquisition capability (KAC) and knowledge sharing capability (KSC) are enacted from different functional positions during the fuzzy front end (FFE) of innovation, and how participants describe the interfaces through which these knowledge-processing activities connect. Design/methodology/approach The study adopts an abductive, multiple-case design and a Gioia-inspired analytical procedure. It draws on 48 expert interviews with senior professionals working in R&D, innovation, consumer intelligence and supply chain roles across eight FMCG and technology organisations. Findings The findings indicate that KIC, KAC and KSC are connected through overlap, iteration and reciprocal feedback rather than operating as an exclusively linear sequence. Participants described differentiated functional contributions, with R&D providing technical interpretation, Consumer intelligence framing behavioural relevance, supply chain contributing supplier and feasibility knowledge, and innovation facilitating translation and integration. The sampled FMCG accounts particularly emphasised signal expiry and timely insight translation, whereas technology accounts more frequently highlighted technical complexity and cross-functional interpretation. Research limitations/implications The findings are based on functionally situated managerial accounts and do not establish complete firm-level configurations or objective innovation-performance effects. Future research should use multi-function, longitudinal and project-level designs to assess whether the reported coordination patterns recur across organisations and sectors. Practical implications The study provides a diagnostic framework for identifying knowledge-processing bottlenecks, including identification without translation, acquisition without prioritisation, sharing without interpretive capacity, asynchronous activation and functional gatekeeping. Originality/value The study's originality lies in showing how established knowledge-processing capabilities are described from different functional positions and how participants report reciprocal and temporal interfaces among these activities during the FFE.

title: AI-enabled lead temperature: a narrative review and five-dimension framework for machine-learning lead prioritization
container-title: Vilakshan - XIMB Journal of Management
bb5b053b4668bcaf446ce869d642767ec7b51679.abstract: Purpose This study aims to reconceptualize cold, warm, hot and sales-ready leads as dynamic states of sales-readiness and develops a five-dimension framework based on customer-profile fit, engagement, buying intent, authority and timing. Design/methodology/approach A narrative review integrates the original 47-source DOI-bearing peer-reviewed analytical corpus with a reviewer-directed verification and update of recent peer-reviewed evidence. The synthesis covers qualification/scoring, nurturing, marketing-sales handoff, CRM/pipeline governance, inside sales/follow-up and AI/predictive lead management, using explicit eligibility, coding and bias-mitigation procedures. Findings Lead temperature is a reversible, timestamped configuration rather than a fixed label or engagement score. The framework translates the five dimensions into four operational levels: cold, warm, hot and sales-ready. Machine-learning models can estimate or rank this state, but decision value depends on recency, calibration, explainability, data quality and managerial governance. Research limitations/implications The framework requires longitudinal, multi-firm validation across channels, industries and sales-cycle lengths. Practical implications RevOps, marketing and sales teams can use the model for routing, nurturing, response-time SLAs, downgrading stale leads and governing predictive scores. Originality/value The paper links practitioner lead-temperature terminology to machine-learning lead prioritization through an interpretable feature architecture and eight testable propositions.

title: Circular economy 10R strategies in aviation waste management: a systematic review of implementation logic and service implications
container-title: International Journal of Quality and Service Sciences
973c0225feae434cb8ec3a897733bf1eb5e8fe00.abstract: Purpose This study aims to identify, categorizes and explains how circular economy (CE) 10R strategies are implemented in aviation waste management and why adoption differs across airline-airport service systems. It distinguishes aviation waste management from broader carbon-oriented aviation sustainability debates and examines how circular waste practices may affect service reliability, stakeholder coordination and service quality. Design/methodology/approach A systematic literature review was used as the methodological approach. Scopus and Web of Science were searched for peer-reviewed English-language journal studies published between 2000 and December 2025. After deduplication and screening, 39 studies were retained for bibliometric mapping and 34 studies for qualitative content analysis. VOSviewer keyword co-occurrence analysis, descriptive bibliometric profiling and theory-informed coding were combined to synthesize CE 10R strategies, enablers, barriers, success factors and service-system implications. Findings The synthesis shows that aviation waste research remains concentrated in environmental and operational outlets, with limited engagement with service quality scholarship. Adoption is uneven across the 10R hierarchy: Recycle and Recover dominate, whereas Refuse, Rethink and Reduce remain less developed because of biosecurity rules, safety standards, fragmented airline-airport governance, turnaround-time pressures and limited sector-specific digital tools. The review therefore interprets 10R adoption as a context-dependent feasibility logic rather than a simple hierarchical progression. Evidence linking CE practices to service quality and passenger experience remains mostly indirect and requires empirical validation. Practical implications The findings suggest that managers should treat CE waste initiatives as service-process redesign tasks rather than stand-alone environmental projects. A staged approach is recommended: map waste-stream boundaries, test upstream refuse/reduce options where safety and biosecurity permit, align airline-airport contracts and responsibilities and use digital monitoring and standardized performance indicators to connect circular outcomes with service reliability. Originality/value The review provides a positive synthesis of what has not previously been integrated: the 10R hierarchy, aviation waste streams, bibliometric knowledge structure and service-system feasibility conditions. It identifies the mechanisms that explain why downstream circular practices dominate and clarifies where service-quality claims are evidence-based, inferential or still absent from the corpus.

title: Health risk profiles and payment intentions for enhanced stadium safety: evidence from NFL fans
container-title: Sport, Business and Management: An International Journal
5fbe400090e7e901d4792fd6434e5233add92638.abstract: Purpose The purpose of this study is to examine how National Football League (NFL) fans’ health risk profiles are associated with their payment intentions for enhanced stadium safety measures during the 2022 NFL season. Grounded in Protection Motivation Theory (PMT), this study distinguishes between general risk-taking as a dispositional trait and domain-specific risk evaluations, including risk attitude and perceived risk. By incorporating general risk-taking as an upstream dispositional factor, this study extends the PMT framework. Using a cross-sectional survey design, the proposed model examines direct and indirect relationships among these constructs to explain fans’ stated intentions to financially support enhanced stadium safety measures. Design/methodology/approach Survey data were collected from 415 NFL fans during the 2022 NFL season after stadiums had fully reopened. Participants were recruited through Centiment, an online survey platform, and screened for NFL fandom and prior game attendance. The final analytical sample comprised 414 respondents. Validated scales were adapted to assess general risk-taking, risk attitude, perceived risk, and payment intentions for enhanced stadium safety measures. Confirmatory factor analysis and structural equation modeling were conducted using R to evaluate the measurement and structural models. Indirect effects were examined using nonparametric bootstrapping with 5,000 iterations to assess the hypothesized mediation pathways. Findings Perceived risk was positively associated with NFL fans’ payment intentions for enhanced stadium safety measures. Contrary to expectations, general risk-taking was positively associated with both risk attitude and payment intention but was not significantly associated with perceived risk. Risk attitude was positively associated with perceived risk and payment intention. Mediation analyses identified significant indirect relationships between general risk-taking and payment intention through risk attitude, and between risk attitude and payment intention through perceived risk. These findings highlight the importance of domain-specific risk evaluations while suggesting that dispositional risk-taking may also contribute to fans’ intentions to financially support enhanced safety measures. Research limitations/implications The cross-sectional design limits causal inference and raises concerns regarding common method bias and endogeneity. Payment intention was measured using a Likert-type scale rather than monetary valuations, preventing estimation of price elasticity or reservation prices. The NFL fan sample limits generalizability to other sport contexts. Additionally, prior attendance frequency and fan identification were not measured, potentially omitting relevant predictors of payment intention. Lastly, this study focused primarily on threat appraisal without directly measuring coping appraisal components, including response efficacy and self-efficacy, limiting its ability to provide a comprehensive test of Protection Motivation Theory. Practical implications The findings offer practical insights for NFL organizations managing live events under heightened health uncertainty. Perceived risk was more strongly associated with fans’ payment intentions for enhanced safety measures than general risk-taking. NFL teams could leverage existing customer relationship management and ticketing platforms to examine attendance and engagement patterns while exploring fans’ safety preferences. Communication strategies through in-stadium displays and mobile applications could explain how specific safety interventions address health-related concerns. Integrating safety enhancements into existing premium seating or club membership tiers may allow organizations to accommodate varying safety preferences while exploring potential revenue opportunities during periods of heightened health uncertainty. Originality/value This study contributes to sport management and consumer behavior literature by extending PMT to examine NFL fans’ payment intentions for enhanced stadium safety measures. By incorporating general risk-taking as an upstream dispositional factor and distinguishing it from domain-specific risk attitude and perceived risk, this study offers a framework for understanding risk-related financial intentions in discretionary sport consumption. The findings highlight the importance of perceived risk and reveal unexpected positive associations between general risk-taking and payment intention, suggesting that dispositional risk tendencies and situational evaluations may have distinct roles in shaping fans’ intentions to financially support safety measures.

title: Disrupting silences, unsettling intersections: the undiscussable matter of African women who bully other African women
container-title: Gender in Management: An International Journal
1e89f7fffe426f567b73c1ffd3503e04317bf236.abstract: Purpose This study aims to use intersectionality to investigate the simultaneous influence of race, gender, ethnicity, age and social class on African women leaders’ experiences of workplace bullying and career progression. Implications for gender equity are explored. Design/methodology/approach Using constructivist grounded theory, semi-structured interviews were conducted with 21 African women leaders in South African public and private sector organisations. Data analysis followed the iterative process of initial, focussed and theoretical coding. Findings Findings revealed complex inter- and intra-group dynamics, with bullying manifesting within and across race, gender, age, social class and ethnic groupings. Intergenerational envy was apparent in the dynamics between older and younger participants. While class protected bullies who came from privileged backgrounds, it attracted envious attacks from those with lower social class origins. Ethnic identity informed toxic dynamics between bullies and targets. Participants’ career progression was negatively impacted, and gender equity became a casualty as participants either left employer organisations or avoided leadership positions. Originality/value While the gendered and racialised nature of workplace bullying has been the subject of research for decades, its intersectional nature remains under-theorised. Whereas inter-group bullying is well researched, intra-race and intra-gender bullying is not sufficiently explored in literature. This study extends intersectional workplace bullying literature and examines two undiscussables in South African workplace bullying scholarship – the bullying of African women by African women, and the insidious influence of ethnicity on workplace bullying.

title: Are you a positive or negative user of AI? Exploring the impacts of undergraduates' GenAI use
container-title: Journal of Research in Innovative Teaching & Learning
66831f84cd92159e84b218b9318c21fb4ab01adf.abstract: Purpose Artificial intelligence (AI) tools are rapidly becoming commonplace in many academic environments; however, studies examining not just whether students use these technologies but how their usage patterns shape learning outcomes and academic integrity remain understudied. This study begins to address this gap by exploring undergraduates' patterns of constructive or problematic use of AI and their relation to academic and ethical behaviors. Design/methodology/approach This exploratory study used a cross-sectional design employing quantitative data collection methods. A correlation and multiple regression analysis were conducted with college students' (N = 110) self-reports of AI use, academic motivation and engagement, reliance on AI, and digital citizenship. Findings Negative and positive AI use were correlated with AI Reliance. Negative AI use also predicted stronger AI reliance with weaker digital citizenship skills, unlike positive AI use. Notably, positive and negative AI use were strongly correlated, suggesting that use patterns are not uniform on an individual level and may vary by context. Research limitations/implications Our results suggest that students may shift between different AI patterns. Future researchers should aim to clarify the causal mechanisms and recruit a larger and more diverse sample to validate and expand upon our findings. Originality/value To our knowledge, this paper is a rare empirical study that explores the relationship between specific student academic outcomes and AI use in distinctive usage patterns: positive and negative.

title: Channeled Attention and Stable Errors
container-title: The Quarterly Journal of Economics
aa56883ac1e6c9b3cc530fef17050cbca03121f3.abstract: Abstract People persist in mistaken beliefs even in settings with high stakes, abundant data, and repeated opportunities to learn—settings where standard arguments imply they should correct their errors. We develop an attention-based framework for understanding why errors persist. When a person channels his attention through the lens of his potentially misspecified model, exposure to data is not the same as tracking the statistics necessary to tell him his model is wrong. A model is attentionally stable when the data the person deems relevant will, in the long run, fail to make the model look implausible. Models that erroneously rule things out—e.g., beliefs that a variable doesn’t matter or that a distinction doesn’t exist—tend to be attentionally stable because they divert attention away from data that would refute the models. Conversely, models that erroneously rule things in are less likely to be stable. Whether an error is discovered depends on the structure of the decision problem but is not tightly linked to its level of harm; arbitrarily costly errors can persist while trivially inexpensive ones may be detected. Nevertheless, no error is robust both to changes in the decision environment and to shocks that expand attention: every channeled-attention error is vulnerable to some perturbation that would reveal it. We use the framework to analyze the stability of psychological biases and empirical misconceptions, as well as to explain why fresh eyes catch mistakes, why people use overly coarse rather than overly fine categorizations, and why people recognize errors in others that they miss in themselves.

title: Scheduling a Double Round Robin Tournament with Triples
container-title: IMA Journal of Management Mathematics
de31d4891cdd3567b8c933976b0f5ee2d05e52d7.abstract: Abstract In amateur or youth sports leagues, the teams play all matches during their leisure time. Thus, a schedule with a smaller number of rounds is preferred. To reduce the number of rounds and required referees, teams are willing to play multiple matches within the same round. We organize these matches in triples, where three teams meet at the venue of one of them and play against each other, at the cost of potentially unevenly distributed home-field advantages. The travel distances of all teams now depend on their assignment to the respective triple and the choice of the home team, ruling out the constraint of alternating home-field advantages between the matches of the same team pair. Therefore, we introduce a new tournament format, the double round robin tournament with triples (2RR-T). By deriving a binary linear optimization model for this new format, we can compute tournament schedules that minimize the total travel distance. After adjusting orbital shrinking to break the resulting symmetries in the possible assignments, we perform an extensive computational study to examine the efficiency of the proposed solution approaches on a new publicly available set of benchmark instances. Furthermore, we apply our approach to the “Basketball Senioren Landesliga Brandenburg”, a German amateur basketball league using this format, compare the resulting schedule with the existing one, and evaluate the triple format against the traveling tournament problem and a format with coupled team pairs.

title: DTBNet: Multimodal 3D Geometric Perception with Hierarchical Attention for Robust Drug–Target Interaction and Binding Affinity Prediction
container-title: Bioinformatics
0d68afed625fe3f8cd6f59afb05f1321be84890a.abstract: Abstract Motivation Accurate prediction of drug-target interactions (DTIs) and binding affinity (DTA) constitutes a core challenge in accelerating drug discovery. While existing computational methods have made progress, most models struggle to capture critical physicochemical interactions in 3D space due to reliance on 1D sequences or 2D graph structures, and exhibit limited generalization in cold-start scenarios. This study proposes DTBNet, a unified prediction framework integrating multimodal geometric perception and hierarchical attention. The framework constructs heterogeneous embeddings combining local chemical details with global biological information by incorporating protein 3D geometric features and multilevel drug representations. During cross-modal interaction, atom–residue cross-attention first captures pair-specific local associations, followed by group-level multi-head self-attention that integrates complementary chemical-semantic, global structural, and local geometric interaction representations. Results Experiments on benchmark datasets (Davis, KIBA, PDBBind) demonstrate that compared with the optimal baseline models, DTBNet achieves up to 19.8% reduction in mean squared error and 8.0% improvement in Pearson correlation coefficient, maintaining optimal performance in drug cold-start, target cold-start, and completely novel pairing scenarios, showcasing robust cross-domain adaptability. Independent validation on GPCR targets achieves RMSE 0.783, confirming real-world applicability. Visualization analyses reveal DTBNet precisely identifies interaction sites between key transmembrane helical domain residues and drug aromatic rings, with attention distribution highly consistent with experimentally resolved binding conformations. These results establish DTBNet as a new performance benchmark through 3D geometric perception and dynamic attention mechanisms, providing interpretable molecular insights for structure-based rational drug design and demonstrating broad potential in virtual screening and target discovery. Availability The source code and data are available at https://github.com/wyx2012/DTB_Net. Supplementary information Supplementary data are available at Bioinformatics online.

                    <scp>i</scp>
                    Survey (FASHI) DR2
container-title: Research in Astronomy and Astrophysics
d3dde96f6c706676ad1d2e5636cb7668f5b8c69f.abstract: Abstract High-velocity clouds (HVCs)—especially compact HVCs (CHVCs)—are thought to serve as gaseous tracers of dark-matter-dominated subhalos, providing a crucial empirical link between the predicted dark matter substructure and observed satellite galaxies. In this paper, we present a new catalog of 192 CHVCs identified from the FAST All-Sky H i Survey Data Release 2. Among these, 108 are ultra-compact HVCs, the majority of which are new discoveries. We find that 185 of the 192 CHVCs are spatially and kinematically concentrated around the Andromeda galaxy (M31), with a median local standard of rest velocity of −296.1 km s −1 , suggesting physical association with M31. Adopting an M31 distance of 0.8 Mpc, we derive H i masses in the range 1.9 × 10 5 –4.0 × 10 6 M ⊙ and dynamical masses from 1.0 × 10 7 to 6.3 × 10 8 M ⊙ . Approximately half of the CHVCs follow the baryonic Tully–Fisher relation. No optical counterparts are detected in Pan-STARRS1 imaging down to a limiting magnitude of m g = 22.8. We conclude that these CHVCs likely represent a population of gas-rich, starless minihalos and provide an excellent sample for the search for dark galaxies.

title: Estimation of feedback parameter C and linewidth enhancement factor α with stationary target in self-mixing interferometry via laser current modulation
container-title: Applied Optics
8aa82845994def0804e02c4c266e3d6d83adedd9.abstract: Accurate estimation of the feedback parameter C and linewidth enhancement factor α in self-mixing interferometry conventionally requires mechanical target vibration to generate fringes. This is impractical for targets producing insufficient fringes, such as in sub-fringe displacement sensing. We propose laser injection current modulation as a non-mechanical alternative to induce functionally equivalent interferometric fringes on stationary targets. Validated experimentally and via simulations in the moderate feedback regime ( C >1) using two independent analytical estimators, our method yields unbiased C estimates that strongly agree with conventional vibration-based techniques. Furthermore, α estimates remain stable across all tested feedback levels. These results establish current modulation as a reliable calibration route for systems where mechanical target excitation is impractical.

8d6566608fce521055ce1c29ae126198863c8d7f.abstract: In conclusion, this research demonstrates that artificial intelligence (AI) represents a genuine qualitative leap in the field of management in general, and in the administrative decision-making process in particular. The study's findings confirm a strong correlation and a significant positive impact of using AI technologies on improving the quality of administrative decisions in Iraqi Public Sector. The study employed a quantitative approach to data collection and analysis, concluding that adopting AI effectively contributes to enhancing the quality of administrative decisions and achieving a sustainable competitive advantage for organizations. title: Does the Sequencing Between a Verb and an Action Impact Learning for Children With Developmental Language Disorder? A Feasibility Study of a New Experimental Paradigm
container-title: Journal of Speech, Language, and Hearing Research
f2c9bfa99c37169ac147709a746c064014a4ce47.abstract: Purpose: Understanding how to optimize verb-learning contexts is critical for vocabulary intervention for children with developmental language disorder (DLD). In this study, we explore the feasibility of a new experimental paradigm designed to assess whether the sequencing between a verb and its referent action impacts learning. We also consider whether what is optimal varies depending on verb meaning, contrasting manner verbs, which encode how an event unfolds, with result verbs, which encode event endstates. Method: Eight 4- and 5-year-olds with DLD participated in this feasibility study. In the before condition, children heard novel verbs before seeing their referent actions. In the after condition, children heard the verbs after the actions were viewed. Children were asked to demonstrate knowledge of the novel verbs by pointing. Probabilities were compared with the null value expected by chance (50%). Additionally, we fit an exploratory generalized estimating equation model to the data with covariates for condition and verb type. Results: Tests of predicted probabilities revealed that children did not demonstrate learning rates above chance in the before condition. Learning rates were above chance in the after condition for result but not manner verbs. Model estimates revealed differences in learning between the recall and generalization phases. Conclusions: Our new experimental paradigm has the potential to be used for further research into children's verb-learning processes. Children with DLD appear to be impacted by the sequencing between a verb and its referent action based on this feasibility study; however, further research is required to adequately understand the impact of sequencing on verb learning for children with DLD. Supplemental Material: https://doi.org/10.23641/asha.33332601

title: Quality monitoring in extrusion-based bioprinting: From defect formation to AI-driven detection and correction
2497f27ecb0a80c081f637e0b5d2ad5b16be7901.abstract: Extrusion-based bioprinting is widely used to fabricate cell-laden three-dimensional constructs, yet its structural integrity remains difficult to ensure because interactions among bioink rheology, process parameters, hardware and construct design produce defects that compromise the dimensional accuracy and cell viability of the bioprinted samples. This review organizes the structural defects along a causal chain, from root-cause factors to nozzle-level failures (clogging and buckling-induced filament curling), filament-level defects (size inconsistency, fusion, delamination, sagging, collapse and breakage) and construct-level inaccuracy. It then maps each defect class to the sensing modalities that have been shown to observe it, spanning surface imaging (optical and machine-vision imaging, microscopy, thermography, video-based vibrometry and laser profilometry), volumetric analysis (optical coherence tomography, X-ray computed tomography, magnetic resonance imaging and ultrasound) and process sensing (dielectric impedance spectroscopy and flow sensing). The methods are compared in terms of processing stage, reported resolution and target object. The evidence linking each defect class to each method is also mapped. Machine learning is assessed as an interpretation layer on these data, distinguishing classification, segmentation, anomaly scoring, open-loop prediction, and assisting corrective measures in printing. Key open challenges include the scarcity of shared, standardized datasets, limited external validation and regulatory frameworks, the absence of standardized defect definitions and the coupling between structural fidelity and cell viability, which together define the requirements for quality-assessment frameworks that can support clinical translation. Collectively, this review aims to provide a structured foundation for developing quality assessment frameworks capable of supporting the translation of extrusion-based bioprinting from laboratory research toward consistent, clinically viable fabrication.

title: Deep-learning-based low-energy trigger algorithms for the Hyper-Kamiokande experiment
container-title: Physical Review D
b7e2537fc3571ed62d17b7be917933c9b7470bd2.abstract: Modern machine learning techniques have become increasingly important in particle physics because of their powerful pattern-recognition capabilities, including in real-time data acquisition where stringent runtime constraints apply. This paper details the performance of deep-learning-based trigger algorithms for a large water Cherenkov detector such as Hyper-Kamiokande, aimed at low-energy neutrino events (below 7 MeV). The performance of custom neural-network supervised classifiers is shown alongside two anomaly-detection approaches trained solely on detector noise: a pure autoencoder and a model based on manifold projection-diffusion recovery. The supervised model shows signal identification efficiencies of 76.7% for single electrons of 3 MeV kinetic energy, significantly exceeding signal efficiencies obtained from a traditional hit-count-based trigger of 26.4%, while the manifold projection-diffusion recovery approach reaches 35.4% at the same operating point. Runtime evaluations on graphical processing unit yield per-window inference latencies well below the millisecond scale.

title: Neural Correlates of the Acceptable Noise Level and Self-Reported Listening Skills in Young Adults With Autism Spectrum Disorder
container-title: Journal of Speech, Language, and Hearing Research
4b14d71864bf9de88c71d4a0e8cdd286b4b4f5c1.abstract: Purpose: This brain–behavior study investigated the relationship between auditory sensory gating and noise acceptance in listeners with and without autism spectrum disorder (ASD). Relationships between self-reported listening skills and auditory sensory gating were also examined. Method: Neural responses to pure-tone stimuli were elicited using a traditional, passive gating paradigm in 12 listeners with ASD and 12 neurotypical control listeners. Noise acceptance was quantified in all listeners using the acceptable noise level (ANL) measure. Self-reported listening abilities were measured using the Speech, Spatial, and Qualities of Hearing Scale (SSQ). Relationships between neural and behavioral measures were analyzed using linear mixed-effects regression. Results: Listeners with ASD accepted less noise when listening to concurrent speech, had higher intensity most comfortable levels for speech, and reported significantly more difficulties on the SSQ compared to the control group. Regression analyses showed that, across groups, weaker P1 gating was associated with poorer noise acceptance. In addition, there were differential effects of P2 gating on self-reported listening deficits on the SSQ between the ASD and control groups. Conclusions: In listeners with and without ASD, weaker pre-attentive P1 gating was significantly associated with higher ANLs (i.e., poorer noise acceptance). In contrast, weaker later stage cortical inhibition was related to greater reported listening deficits on the SSQ in listeners with ASD only.

title: Integrating multifunctional interfaces via chelation-driven chemical reconstruction enables efficient and durable perovskite solar cells
container-title: Materials Futures
3f8c2076c37d525da4e64e6e44f55252fefcdca1.abstract: Abstract Interfacial instability is a critical constraint for the practical deployment of perovskite solar cells (PSCs). It commonly arises from the metastable residual PbI 2 and deep-level defects like under-coordinated Pb 2+ . Herein, a benzeneseleninic acid (PSA)-enabled interfacial chemical reconstruction strategy, that simultaneously converts residual PbI 2 , mitigates interfacial defects, and stabilizes the perovskite lattice through synergistic bidentate chelation and hydrogen bonding, is reported to significantly improve the interfacial stability. Robust Pb–O–Se chelate structures can be formed via dual-site coordination between PSA with under-coordinated Pb 2+ and residual PbI 2 . This chelation-driven interfacial reconstruction not only eliminates detrimental defects at the interface but also induces ordered molecular self-assembly, in which outward-oriented phenyl groups form a hydrophobic barrier that blocks water/oxygen intrusion, while the interfacial dipole modulates the degree of energy-level matching, thereby markedly enhancing charge extraction efficiency. Meanwhile, PSA molecules stabilize the halide sublattice through hydrogen-bond interactions, suppressing ion migration and structural degradation. Consequently, PSA-treated PSCs exhibits markedly improved efficiency (from 23.68% to 26.56%) together with substantially enhanced stability, retains 87.8% of initial efficiency after 2000 h under 60% relative humidity.

title: Metabolic modeling: the link between AI and multi-omics data to accelerate the discovery of antibiotic-resistant traits in ESKAPE pathogens
container-title: Infection and Immunity
7ed95bf61237d995171ecce906cdf2fb609f6b80.abstract: ABSTRACT The development of predictive understanding of bacterial resistance to antibiotics is one of the greatest challenges of modern medicine. Genome-scale metabolic models (GEMs) are mathematical representations of the metabolic network of a given organism assembled from genomic data that predict cellular activity across many environmental and genetic contexts. Because a single model can be solved under thousands of conditions, GEMs generate data at scales that support downstream analysis with artificial intelligence tools, helping to elucidate how pathogens adapt to host environments, evade immune responses, and acquire resistance. Here, we review how GEMs of ESKAPE pathogens are built, what data they require, and what they can and cannot do. We describe the reconstruction workflow from automated draft network through manual curation, gap filling, and experimental validation and the public and experimental data sources each stage depends on. We then describe how accessory genes and transcriptomic measurements are incorporated to yield strain- and condition-specific models and where machine learning contributes both in expanding functional annotation and in consuming model-generated flux distributions. Applications are illustrated with ESKAPE examples throughout, including conserved metabolic vulnerabilities identified across strain collections and flux rewiring observed under antibiotic exposure. Despite this progress, high-quality GEMs exist for only a fraction of ESKAPE species; many are constrained by incomplete annotation or limited experimental validation, and non-metabolic resistance mechanisms are captured only insofar as they impose a metabolic cost. Providing reliable tools to build new models from trustworthy templates, therefore, remains a priority for narrowing the gap between genotype and phenotype.

title: Self-destructing attenuated adjuvant Salmonella strains: design, construction, characterization, and evaluation of safety and efficacy following in ovo inoculation of chicken embryos
container-title: Infection and Immunity
4b2362c5b577c9231dcf03b9d19e34e2bed7a913.abstract: ABSTRACT Self-destructing attenuated adjuvant Salmonella (SDAAS) strains are next-generation attenuated S . Typhimurium strains designed to be used as live adjuvants. They possess diverse means to prevent persistence in vivo , survival if excreted, and to enhance the induction of innate immunity. In this study, we investigated whether SDAAS strains can be safely delivered to chicken embryos by in ovo inoculation without compromising hatchability or hatchling health. We then evaluated their growth in different media, sensitivity to complement-mediated killing, motility, serum agglutination, flagellar and LPS profiling, their ability to attach to and invade Int-407 cells, and the activation of different pattern recognition receptors displayed by HEK-Blue cells. We also determined whether these strains could induce protective immune responses in chicks following homologous challenge at day of hatch with a virulent S . Typhimurium strain by reducing intestinal colonization and organ invasion. Our findings demonstrate that SDAAS strains can be safely administered in ovo in a dose-dependent manner. Family A strains exhibit strict requirements for 2,6-diaminopimelic acid and D-alanine, while Family B strains demonstrate absolute dependence on L-arabinose for growth in liquid and solid media. Adjuvant strains demonstrate increased activation of murine receptors NOD1, NOD2, TLR4, TLR5, TLR8, and TLR9 in HEK-Blue cells compared to the parent strain χ3761, despite having lower rates of cell adhesion to and invasion of Int-407 cells. Lastly, we observed that in ovo administration of SDAAS strains reduced titers of S . Typhimurium recovered from birds as they became older, suggesting a time-dependent enhancement of protective immunity induced by SDAAS strains.

title: Information content of Krylov observables: A machine learning approach
container-title: Physical Review D
96e5a35dc425657911f86d58f98ef027abac441a.abstract: We employ machine learning techniques to estimate the amount of information contained in three Krylov-space observables: the spread complexity C ( t ) , the discrete Wigner negativity N ( t ) , and the normalized negativity χ ( t ) = N ( t ) / | S ( t ) | , where S ( t ) is the survival amplitude. We study thermofield-double evolutions on Gaussian unitary ensemble (GUE), Gaussian orthogonal ensemble (GOE), and Poisson spectra, and on the integrable S L ( 2 , R ) Krylov chain of a two-dimensional conformal field theory (CFT) primary with Lanczos coefficients b n = α n ( n + 2 h − 1 ) . To introduce chaos we add a GUE random matrix to the integrable chain, H ( ϵ ) = H S L ( 2 , R ) + ϵ R 0 W GUE , where R 0 is its spectral half-width. Either C ( t ) or N ( t ) alone determines the thermofield temperature, with R 2 ≃ 0.999 . However, neither can reconstruct the fine structure of the spectral form factor. In the integrable sector all three observables carry the same information. When we turn on chaos an asymmetry appears: χ predicts C better than C predicts χ . This gap grows from + 0.33 to + 0.77 , while the same gap for the raw negativity decays to zero. Thus we conclude the extra information comes from the survival amplitude and χ ( t ) carries it while C ( t ) can still be recovered from χ ( t ) . We derive a lower bound on this gap, set by the fraction of the variance of χ that comes from S .

title: Self-temperature-compensated all-fiber refractive index sensor based on four-leaf clover fiber
container-title: Optics Express
7ea16d38ce414d943208a2f0e26e406747e22f59.abstract: In this paper, we propose and demonstrate an all-fiber refractive index (RI) sensor based on a cascaded Fabry-Pérot interferometer with four-leaf-clover fiber (FLCF). A temperature self-compensation scheme is adopted to realize simultaneous dual-parameter measurement and effectively suppress temperature crosstalk in RI sensing. The experimental results indicate that the proposed sensor achieves a high RI sensitivity of -44.96 dB/RIU within the RI range of 1.3333-1.4532, where the sensing performance is characterized by the fringe extinction ratio. In addition, the sensor exhibits a linear temperature response with a sensitivity of 0.0278 nm/°C in terms of wavelength shift. Benefiting from the all-reflective configuration and compact probe diameter of 125 μm, the proposed sensor features a simple fabrication process and low cost. With the merits of high sensitivity, effective temperature compensation, and miniaturized structure, the sensor holds great application potential for biochemical detection, liquid environment monitoring, and other practical fiber sensing scenarios.

title: Do AI Symptom Checkers Help or Hinder Timely Care-Seeking for Early Heart Disease? A Narrative Review of the Evidence by Insurance Status
container-title: Journal of High School Research
245892048b33dec027816966377c8fcebac9afd4.abstract: Cardiovascular disease killed 919,032 people in the United States in 2023, and how long people wait before getting help shapes much of that toll. The wait is not the same for everyone. In a 24-hospital U.S. registry, 48.6% of uninsured heart attack patients waited more than six hours, compared with 44.6% of insured patients who worried about costs and 39.3% of insured patients who did not. AI symptom checkers now show up at exactly the moment people decide whether to get care. Yet I found no study that measures whether using one changes how fast people seek care for heart symptoms, or whether the answer depends on insurance. This narrative review, organized with guidance from PRISMA 2020, pulls together evidence on four things: how accurate symptom checkers are, how they change people's plans for care, who uses them, and how insurance shapes the decision to seek cardiac care. I searched PubMed/MEDLINE and Google Scholar between June and September 2026, along with publisher, journal, and government websites, and checked the reference lists of key studies. Twenty-two sources form the core evidence base: 20 peer-reviewed studies and 2 survey reports that were not peer-reviewed. Because the studies ranged from simulated-case audits to national registries, I appraised each one with four questions (real patients or simulated cases, observed behavior or stated intention, independence from the tool's developer, and how representative the sample was) and synthesized the findings narratively. Following the Commonwealth Fund, I treated insurance as three levels: adequately insured, underinsured, and uninsured. The evidence cuts both ways. Symptom checkers reduce uncertainty and usually catch emergencies. But in the largest real-world dataset, users lowered the urgency of their care plans eight times as often as they raised it. Most tools triage no better than an average layperson, and in studies with real patients, 2-9% of cases were under-triaged. In a randomized trial, people using AI chatbots made no better care decisions than people using other sources. The typical user is insured, college-educated, and female, so little is known about the groups most likely to delay. I argue that insurance likely decides whether a symptom checker speeds care up or slows it down. Insured users can act on advice, or double-check it, at little cost. Uninsured and underinsured users are the least able to catch a falsely reassuring answer. Three hypotheses follow. Among adequately insured adults, prior symptom checker use will shorten the time to professional consultation for early cardiac symptoms. Among uninsured adults, it will not shorten that time and may lengthen it. Underinsured adults will fall in between, and pairing advice with navigation to low-cost care should narrow the gaps among the three groups. I outline an equity-focused design with measurable safety thresholds, such as sensitivity for emergencies of 95% or higher and harmful under-triage in 2% or fewer encounters, along with community health worker review and community governance. I also propose four studies to test the hypotheses: an audit of standardized cardiac cases, a prospective cohort stratified by insurance tier, a stepped-wedge trial of community health worker navigation, and qualitative interviews.

title: SELF-SUPERVISED CONTRASTIVE LEARNING WITH DYNAMIC COST-SENSITIVE RANDOM FOREST FOR INTELLIGENT FAULT DIAGNOSIS OF DIESEL ENGINES
container-title: Surface Review and Letters
2d5db6c173f6e05cc56ac90baf5b39a47efbc6b7.abstract: Reliable identification of incipient degradation is critical to the durability and functional integrity of diesel engines. However, diagnosis is challenged by scarce degradation labels, severe class imbalance, and heterogeneous multi-source monitoring data. This study proposes a self-supervised contrastive learning framework with a dynamic cost-sensitive random forest (SSCL-DCSRF) for intelligent fault diagnosis with a focus on wear- and lubrication-related degradation states. Rather than directly measuring surface morphology, roughness, residual stress, or wear loss, the proposed method identifies operating states associated with surface-related degradation from multi-source monitoring data. A physically consistent view-generation strategy preserves operating-condition semantics and cross-variable relationships, enabling robust representation learning from unlabeled data. A dynamic cost-sensitive random forest then integrates class frequency, feature-space dispersion, and prediction uncertainty to improve the recognition of minority and difficult-to-classify states. Experiments on a multi-source diesel-engine fault dataset demonstrate that SSCL-DCSRF outperforms representative machine-learning methods in class-balanced diagnostic performance, with enhanced sensitivity to early wear and lubrication-related degradation. The proposed framework provides an effective data-driven approach for indirect identification of operating states related to surface degradation and integrity-oriented maintenance of critical tribological interfaces.
