title: Escape dynamics and implicit bias of one-pass SGD in overparameterized quadratic networks
container-title: Machine Learning: Science and Technology
3ddd8c81045c0baece32d06763c77b1ebed3aa43.abstract: Abstract We analyze the one-pass stochastic gradient descent dynamics of a two-layer neural network with quadratic activations in a teacher–student framework. A teacher network generates the data labels, and a student network is trained to reproduce its outputs. In the high-dimensional regime, where the input dimension N and the number of samples M diverge at fixed ratio α = M / N , and for finite hidden widths ( p , p ∗ ) of the student and teacher, respectively, we study the low-dimensional ordinary differential equations that govern the evolution of the student-teacher and student-student overlap matrices. We show that overparameterization ( p > p ∗ ) only modestly accelerates escape from a plateau of poor generalization when the learning rate is chosen optimally, by modifying the prefactor of the exponential loss reduction. We then examine how unconstrained weight norms introduce a continuous rotational symmetry that results in a nontrivial manifold of zero-loss solutions for p > 1 . For the class of initializations considered here, the population gradient flow selects the closest point on this manifold when it converges to zero loss, as enforced by a conserved quantity in the overlap ordinary differential equations. Finally, a Hessian analysis of the population-loss landscape confirms that the plateau and the solution manifold correspond to saddles with at least one negative eigenvalue and to marginal minima in the population-loss geometry, respectively.

title: Conservation laws for explainability in spiking neural networks
container-title: Machine Learning: Science and Technology
05431741b3860c6fb2ea9ae38991aa288848c8e6.abstract: Abstract Explainability in event-driven dynamical models such as spiking neural networks (SNNs) is often adapted from methods developed for static networks, even though the explanation itself is defined over a spatio-temporal computation graph. We present a conservation-law interpretation of layer-wise relevance propagation (LRP) in SNNs as a discrete transport scheme on the unrolled graph, where relevance is the transported quantity and the redistribution rule defines a flux on graph edges. We derive a graph-based spatio-temporal continuity equation, make residual terms and stabilizer-induced sinks explicit, and analyze numerical failure modes associated with thresholding, gating, and signed relevance. We further formulate a flux-corrected threshold redistribution rule that normalizes backward messages at active spike events when the normalization is well posed. We evaluate the method on cislunar telemetry and DVS128 Gesture against Spiking Integrated Gradients and SNN-DeepLIFT across 10 independent runs. Conservation-LRP achieves AOPC values of 0.42 ± 0.03 on CARD and 0.38 ± 0.04 on DVS128 Gesture, with a normalized completeness residual of 0.62 ± 0.18 % and a top-layer randomization correlation of 0.12 ± 0.04 . In a component-level ablation, disabling flux correction increases the threshold-node residual from 0.11 ± 0.05 % to 6.27 ± 1.10 % and the completeness residual from 0.62 ± 0.18 % to 3.84 ± 0.72 % , while perturbation AOPC changes only modestly. These results support conservation diagnostics as a practical complement to perturbation-based evaluation for event-driven neural explanations. The article substantially extends a prior ICLR workshop version with fuller derivations, broader experiments, and expanded implementation-level analysis.

title: Berta, an Open-Source, Modular AI Scribe for Clinical Documentation: Implementation Report
container-title: JMIR Medical Informatics
f2df5d7b63b39635ad5f7aae8d112bd7749180cb.abstract: Abstract Background Clinical documentation is a major contributor to physician workload and burnout, particularly in high-acuity settings such as emergency departments. Ambient AI scribes have emerged as a response, but commercial products cost US $99 to more than US $600 per physician per month, operate as opaque systems, and often process data on vendor-controlled infrastructure. These characteristics limit organizational control over data sovereignty, quality improvement, and clinical workflows and create barriers to adoption in resource-constrained settings. Objective We aimed to develop an open-source, modular AI scribe platform that could be deployed entirely within institutional infrastructure, and to evaluate its real-world use across a provincial health system. Methods We developed Berta, an open-source, modular platform that pairs a Next.js front end and a FastAPI back end with configurable automatic speech recognition and large language model components. A closed-source implementation developed in parallel with Berta was deployed at Alberta Health Services (AHS), Canada’s largest provincially integrated health system at the time of implementation, and operated within AHS’s existing Snowflake AI Data Cloud infrastructure. All clinical audio and text remained within the secure AHS environment. Use and session metadata were automatically recorded during routine clinical use by emergency physicians across AHS between November 2024 and July 2025, and physicians were emailed an optional survey. Operating costs were estimated from Snowflake service consumption over the same period. Implementation (Results) During the 9-month study period, 197 emergency physicians registered at 105 urban and rural facilities used the system, generating 21,548 clinical sessions and more than 2700 hours of audio. Monthly session volume grew from 675 sessions in November 2024 to 5463 in July 2025. Mean recorded session length was 7.6 minutes, and 42% (82/197) of users customized at least 1 documentation template. Operating costs averaged less than US $30 per physician per month, representing a 70% to 95% reduction in cost compared with commercial subscription prices; this comparison excludes personnel costs for development and maintenance. Survey respondents (69-73 per item) rated user-friendliness as good (median 5, IQR 4-6), reported a median time saving of 16 to 30 (IQR 0-15 to 46-60) minutes per shift, and rated documentation quality the lowest. After the pilot, access was opened to other departments, and by September 30, 2026, approximately 2000 users had registered. Conclusions An in-house AI scribe can be deployed at provincial scale within existing health system infrastructure at a fraction of the operating cost of commercial alternatives while preserving data sovereignty and institutional control. The full cost of ownership and documentation quality require further evaluation. By releasing Berta publicly, we provide a reproducible foundation that health systems can adapt to evaluate and deploy AI documentation technology within their own secure environments.

title: Graph neural network based isomorphic learning of finite element computation for optical scattering problems
container-title: Optics Express
742aa4e33649189cf9d7c192c169b0a3e5922d0a.abstract: Accurate and efficient optical simulations are essential for the design of nanophotonic devices. Although deep learning presents a promising path to accelerate these simulations, many data-driven models suffer from limited generalization and poor physical interpretability. To address this issue, we propose a FEM-based graph isomorphic learning (FemGIL) framework for solving optical scattering problems. FemGIL relies on the isomorphism between finite element data and graph structure. In this model, nodes represent unknown coefficients, and their features encode key physical information, such as the incident field and material parameters. The network’s aggregation operation has the same mathematical form as the weak form of FEM and is used to simulate local electric field interactions. The accuracy and efficiency of FemGIL are validated in three 2-D scenarios involving basic scatterers, single metallic scatterers, and multiple metallic scatterers. FemGIL demonstrates good predictive performance for geometric sizes outside the training range. Compared to the conventional BiCGSTAB solver in FEM, FemGIL achieves over a 70% reduction in solution-stage computation time while maintaining comparable accuracy. By employing transfer learning, FemGIL can efficiently adapt a pretrained model to predict the scattering field of complex structures. By deeply integrating numerical methods with deep learning, FemGIL provides a fast, generalizable, and physics-consistent simulator, paving the way for rapid optical device design.

title: Is AI the End of the DMA As We Know It?
container-title: GRUR International
06f29e15676b1c1246b131e4c599fff0a384cd12.abstract: Abstract The disruptive potential of AI-enabled applications for competitive dynamics and the core organisational forms of digital intermediation inevitably also has significant implications for the recent regulatory initiatives adopted to govern digital markets. Indeed, because these instruments were conceived without AI specifically in mind, they risk becoming outdated within a very short period of time. Notably, while they have been shaped by a Big Tech-centred conception of digital markets, the possible emergence of new gatekeepers in the age of AI marks a turning point that calls into question the very rationale and foundations of these regimes in their present form. As a result, only a few years after its enactment, the role of the DMA, its rationale and its claimed future-proof character are already under scrutiny. The deployment of AI applications raises the question whether policymakers should reopen the legislative framework in order to amend the Regulation. Against this background and in the context of the first review of the DMA, the paper argues that the rise of AI applications calls for a reconsideration of the DMA’s overall architecture and for the development of a distinct competition policy framework, rather than for a merely incremental fine-tuning exercise.

title:
Characterization and superhydrophilicity properties of TiO
                    <sub>2</sub>
                    composites modified with graphene oxide and carbon nanotubes, and self-cleaning of TiO
                    <sub>2</sub>
                    and GO-TiO
                    <sub>2</sub>

container-title: Materials Research Express
fb8b89d39337e279ae4d30bff1d0c245a24361de.abstract: Abstract In this study, titanium dioxide (TiO 2 ) and modified with graphene oxide (GO) and carbon nanotubes (CNTs) were prepared via sol–gel method. GO and CNT dispersions in ethanol were mixed with TiO 2 sol, deposited on Corning glass substrates by spin coating, dried at 250 °C and then annealed at 500 °C. Structural, morphological and surface properties of the composites were investigated for both GO-TiO 2 and CNT-TiO 2 by x‐ray diffraction (XRD), Atomic force microscopy (AFM) and contact angle measurements. XRD confirmed the anatase phase in all samples. AFM showed that GO-TiO 2 exhibited significantly higher average surface roughness ( R a , average surface roughness, up to 15.061 nm) compared to CNT-TiO 2 ( R a ≈4 nm) and unmodified TiO 2 ( R a = 2.142 nm). Contact angle measurements revealed superhydrophilic surfaces for both GO-TiO 2 (contact angles as low as 1°) and CNT-TiO 2 reached (4°), while TiO 2 showed 7°. Based on these results, GO-TiO 2 was selected for self-cleaning application. Photocatalytic self-cleaning performance was evaluated for GO-TiO 2 composite and compared with unmodified TiO 2 . TiO 2 was tested under ultraviolet (UV) light due to its wide band gap (3.25 eV), while GO-TiO 2 was tested under natural daylight owing to its visible-light absorption (band gap ∼2.95 eV). The optimal GO-TiO 2 (GO0.08-TiO 2 ) achieved complete methylene blue degradation within 35 min under natural daylight, whereas TiO 2 required 60 min under UV irradiation. These results demonstrate that GO modification enables visible-light-activated self-cleaning performance without requiring UV light sources.

title: An Explainable Hybrid Deep Learning Model for Soil Fertility Classification and Sustainable Agricultural Recommendations
container-title: International Journal of Information Technology & Decision Making
c7992988fb38c9343e69183e2413ed4b076f1d03.abstract: In agriculture, soil fertility has a significant impact on farmer welfare. Soil fertility is the primary factor that determines crop production. Climate change, water resources, soil nutrients, and other environmental elements affect soil fertility. In real time, the process of evaluating soil fertility is challenging and time-consuming. Many studies utilized Machine Learning-based classification and regression processes to determine soil fertility levels. Existing research has shown poor performance, time-consuming processes, and a lack of sustainable crop recommendations, leading to inefficient soil fertility classification and crop recommendations. To overcome these limitations, a novel Explainable Dual Attention-based Dense Capsule Dilated Depthwise Convolutional (EDA_DCDDC) method is introduced in this research. In addition, a sustainable agriculture recommendation system, based on fuzzy logic, is employed to regain soil fertility. Pre-processing methods such as Min–Max Normalization and the Improved Synthetic Minority Oversampling Technique (ISMOTE) are used to maintain data standards and balance minority classes, respectively. This model utilizes Dense Capsules to extract complex features. Then, spatial and channel feature modules are selected and incorporated to reduce dimensionality issues. Dilated Depthwise Convolution (DDC) is used to classify features into “Less Fertile”, “Fertile”, and “Highly Fertile” soils. After the classification process, fuzzy rules are employed to recommend season-based crops according to the soil fertility classes. Finally, SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) are employed to reveal the results. In the experimental analysis, a well-defined soil fertility dataset is processed, producing a classification accuracy of 98.45% and an F1-score of 97.73%, resulting in more reliable performance.

title: A Conceptual Model for Enhancing Sustainable Performance: The Synergy Of Green Innovation Based on Green Skills and Green Creative Self-Efficacy in Metalcraft MSMES
container-title: Jurnal Ilmiah Accusi
e1d37c226625545f7ae0825dfad80f6c010e54f1.abstract: Metalcraft micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs) in Bali contribute to the island’s craft economy, yet their transition to environmentally responsible production may be constrained by limited technical resources and uneven environmental capabilities. Although recent MSME studies associate green innovation with business performance, findings concerning environmental performance remain mixed, and previous studies rarely examine owners’ green skills and green creative self-efficacy together in traditional metalcraft enterprises. This study tests the effects of Green Skill and Green Creative Self-Efficacy on Sustainable Performance, with Green Innovation as a mediator, and identifies managerial priorities through Importance-Performance Map Analysis (IPMA). Survey data were obtained from 259 owners of metalcraft MSMEs in Bali Province using proportionate stratified random sampling and analyzed with PLS-SEM in SmartPLS 4. The estimated relationships are positive and statistically significant, and Green Innovation partially mediates the relationships between both capability constructs and Sustainable Performance. Green Creative Self-Efficacy has numerically larger path coefficients than Green Skill for Green Innovation and Sustainable Performance; this coefficient ordering is interpreted descriptively because a formal between-coefficient difference test was not reported. IPMA identifies environmental awareness and pollution-control facility deployment as specific improvement priorities. The study extends MSME sustainability research by linking an individual-level cognitive capability with operational innovation in a traditional craft setting. For practice, the results support combining practical green-skills training with confidence-building problem-solving activities and affordable, context-appropriate pollution-control and waste-management measures.

title: Three-thousand Meters Run Time Predicts Self-Reported Musculoskeletal Injury Severity in Norwegian Army Recruits
container-title: Military Medicine
e8fef93a5b38b82abcb0f3cefccd75ba116153ad.abstract: Abstract Introduction Non-combat musculoskeletal injuries are a leading cause of limited duty and non-deployability during military service. During basic training, up to 60% of recruits sustain at least 1 injury, although estimates based on medical records likely underestimate the true burden. The Oslo Sports Trauma Research Center Questionnaire on Health Problems (OSTRC-H2) enables prospective capture of all health problems, including those not requiring medical attention. This study aimed to identify baseline risk factors for musculoskeletal injury severity during basic training in the Norwegian Armed Forces using prospectively collected self-reported data. Materials and Methods In this 6-week prospective cohort study, 1,521 Norwegian recruits undergoing basic training at 2 Norwegian military camps consented and were included. Weekly self-reported injury data were collected using the OSTRC-H2. 1,346 (66% men) provided at least 1 OSTRC-H2 questionnaire response. Recruits were categorized as having no injury, only minor injury, or at least 1 substantial injury. Baseline variables included anthropometrics, physical fitness measures, motivation, and training context. Associations between baseline factors and musculoskeletal injury severity were examined using univariate and multivariate ordinal logistic regression analyses, including sex-stratified models. Results Overall, 34% of recruits reported at least 1 substantial injury. Women had higher unadjusted odds of substantial injury than men (OR 1.67, 95% CI 1.28-2.19), but this association was not significant after adjustment. Recruits who remained injury-free demonstrated higher baseline aerobic fitness and strength. In univariate analyses, multiple fitness-related variables were associated with musculoskeletal injury severity; however, in the multivariate model, only military camp (OR 0.74, 95% CI 0.58-0.95; P = .019) and 3,000 m run time (OR 1.15 per minute slower, 95% CI 1.07-1.23; P &lt; .001) remained independently associated. Sex-stratified analyses confirmed 3,000 m run time as a consistent predictor in both men and women. Conclusions Aerobic fitness, as measured by 3,000 m run time, is the strongest independent predictor of musculoskeletal injury severity during basic training. Apparent sex differences in injury severity are largely explained by differences in baseline fitness rather than sex itself. These findings support the use of aerobic fitness for risk stratification and highlight the importance of both individual preparedness and organizational factors in injury prevention strategies.

title: AI-Driven Transformation in Education and Business
9582d73b28887383a9b2b76978981d894f9ddb6a.abstract: Artificial Intelligence is rapidly reshaping the landscapes of education and business, driving innovation and redefining operational norms. The latest volume of the Advanced Series in Management brings together interdisciplinary perspectives to explore how AI technologies—from predictive analytics and automation, to adaptive learning systems—are enabling smarter decision-making, personalised experiences, and enhanced efficiency. At the same time, it critically examines the ethical, infrastructural, and skill-based challenges that accompany this digital shift, offering a balanced view of both promise and complexity. Bridging theory and practice, AI-Driven Transformation in Education and Business presents empirical research, real-world case studies, and policy insights that illuminate the evolving role of AI in organisational and educational contexts. It contributes to global conversations around digital transformation and sustainability, aligning with key UN Sustainable Development Goals such as Quality Education and Responsible Management. Ideal for scholars, students, and practitioners, this volume offers a comprehensive guide to navigating the AI-driven future, especially in a post-pandemic world where hybrid learning and intelligent business models are becoming the norm.

title: AI-Driven Transformation in Education and Business: Concepts, Contexts and Sustainable Pathways
container-title: AI-Driven Transformation in Education and Business
12c7a41ee43b34016c4d1e1b96a121e36b341f8a.abstract: Abstract Artificial intelligence (AI) has become a transformative facilitator for organizations in different industries, reshaping how organizations design processes, make decisions and aim for sustainable values. Though there have been intense examinations of AI and analysis tools and methodologies in past studies, there is a pressing need for a wide and competent understanding of the different dynamics of AI as a transformative tool in real-world contexts. To address this issue, this chapter develops a case study analysis of how AI is influencing education and businesses and develops definitions based on transformative analytics. In this chapter, real-life examples of how AI has or can transform big businesses, educational systems of a nation and college and university systems have been examined. In fact, examples of educational institutions illustrate how AI can impact teaching and governing as well as how it can be used at a systemic level for inclusion. In turn, examples of big businesses illustrate how AI can influence excellence in work processes and administration as well as innovation directed at environmental friendliness. This chapter does not only focus on AI adoption as an issue of technology adoption; it also emphasizes the transformative process as socio-technical in nature. This chapter conducts a cross-case analysis to identify common enablers, sector-specific obstacles and various patterns of transformations in both business and the education sector. These elements are further integrated to develop various sustainable AI-based pathways of transformation in relation to long-term institutional viability, ethical use of AI and social purpose.

title: Applications and Reflections on AI in the Field of Education
container-title: AI-Driven Transformation in Education and Business
5365282d93a3257359ddc4184742a198fe075dab.abstract: Abstract The cognitive artificial intelligence (AI) radically transforms the educational ecosystem through data-driven thinking and algorithmic optimization, which focuses on precision, personalization and collaboration of the educational process, leading to significant changes in metacognitive development, human-machine cognitive synergy and ethical considerations. This technology overcomes the barriers of traditional standardized teaching by dynamically adapting learning paths through cognitive diagnosis, intelligent content adaptation and personalized goal setting. Regarding the development of metacognitive abilities, AI visualized abstract thinking processes and identified self-directed learning capabilities as skills that can be taught and learnt through strategic training and dynamic modification, ultimately redefining them as talents. Nonetheless, the use of technology raises ethical issues, including educational equity, algorithmic bias, data privacy and diminished cognitive autonomy, as overreliance on AI and instant feedback may hinder students’ ability to think independently. This means that a future development should strike a balance between technological advancement and humanism, base technological orientation in human concern and find synergy between tool empowerment and human leadership to build up education to a more fair and equitable evolution.

title: AI-Driven Learning Analytics for Outcome-Based Education in Higher Education Institutions
container-title: AI-Driven Transformation in Education and Business
63f8a4644f6da71c2a6d76fa348694b1a741456d.abstract: Abstract With the recent emphasis on Outcome-Based Education (OBE), it has become even more essential that colleges and universities have excellent data-driven systems that are able to not only compile, evaluate and interpret learning evidence into measurable outcomes, but essentially do it accurately and comprehensively as well. The traditional way of implementing OBE tends to rely on imperfect assessment data, looking backward in time and lacking depth, which further handicaps it from being useful in executing continual enhancements and making rapid academic decisions as well. To address such a difficulty, there comes across a framework within this chapter that proposes needing data-driven systems that incorporate artificial intelligence (AI) into learning analytics as part of OBE systems as well. This chapter illustrates how AI is beneficial in increasing accuracy, monitoring, prediction and intelligent interventions regarding various types of institutional settings and is based on actual data and proves that primary data at an institutional level can be employed to reveal students’ actual engagement, their performance on tests and their success rates in accomplishing their goals within various programmes and academic cycles as well. To ensure that AI is used responsibly in the best interest of the institution and its stakeholders, the paper also addresses issues related to ethics, issues related to data governance challenges and readiness of the institution. This chapter offers a very useful and viable strategy for universities that are on a path of successful implementation of Outcome Based Education using AI learning analytics.

title: Artificial Intelligence-Powered Marketing 5.0 in the South Asian Business Sector
container-title: AI-Driven Transformation in Education and Business
e075d794091c0eb3faa3a951db8aae4619fcec56.abstract: Abstract This research explores the five core components of the revolutionary marketing phase of the ongoing era, Marketing 5.0, across diverse business sectors in South Asia. The study takes a qualitative, inductive approach to analyze primary and secondary data collected from exclusively picked marketing professionals’ opinions and insights, as well as published interviews on YouTube, blogs, academic papers, books focusing on relevant evidences in the context of South Asian business sectors. The research findings develop an integrated theoretical framework of the disciplines, applications and enablers of the concept ‘Technology for Humanity’ under artificial intelligence (AI)-powered marketing phenomena. The study upholds the synergistic value of the collaboration of humans and technologies complementing human cognitive skills with advanced technological skills in the post-pandemic world. The appropriate applications of AI-driven marketing approaches are evaluated in respect to close the widening generation gap, societal and digital polarization gap. The research concludes the foundational disciplines of the appropriate applications of AI-powered technologies for marketers, intended to create unique, yet inclusive and sustainable value that bridges these gaps while upholding the core value of humanity across the region.

title: The Future of Customer Experience: AI-Powered Personalization in Marketing 5.0
container-title: AI-Driven Transformation in Education and Business
15a7fa8476e2fcc39c7dd08d32d0cf3a092c663d.abstract: Abstract In this era of cut-throat marketing campaigns, where every brand is devising strategies to stand out and grab attention, traditional methods are often unable to establish the required customer connections. The future of effective customer experience (CX) lies in personalization, and artificial intelligence (AI) is truly a revolution in marketing personalization. Personalized marketing campaigns definitely increase the conversion rate by fostering deeper customer connections. Natural language processing (NLP) powered by AI is used to understand the customer sentiment. AI-powered chatbots and virtual assistants can provide personalized customer support. Huge data sets can be analyzed, and through predictive analytics, personalized campaigns can be created. This paper explores the potential of AI to develop personalized marketing experiences based on individual consumer preferences, behaviour and demographics.

title: AI Adoption in MSMEs: Opportunities, Barriers and Strategic Readiness in Emerging Economies
container-title: AI-Driven Transformation in Education and Business
d9f15671226e32d94f4685ff1c7039687a6d1af1.abstract: Abstract The adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) has become an important tool for harnessing competitiveness, learning and results of performance for micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) in emerging economies. Despite requiring greater policy emphasis and greater access to technology, little research data have been collected on emerging perceptions of AI opportunities, adoption challenges and strategic preparedness of MSMEs. In an endeavour to generate such research data, this chapter will examine AI adoption by MSMEs using data. The use of AI not only serves as an aid to organizations but also an innovation for organizations to acquire knowledge on data that influence performance outcomes on results. In this chapter, a survey-structured approach to the analysis is used, and a pragmatic and empirical method of data handling is used to describe MSMEs in operating crucial sectors of emerging nations. The descriptive and interpretational statistics, such as comparison of mean tests, correlation and regression, are used to spot trends in the adoption of AI, intensity of value creation sentiments, degree of constraint and readiness. These trends and patterns are spotted with the help of bar chart comparison, trend charts, scatter charts and heat maps, among others. The findings highlight that there is great potential for AI to make working more efficient for MSMEs, to help them make good decisions and to help them react better to the market.

title: Smart Supply Chains and Operations: Applications of Artificial Intelligence in Understanding Smart Logistics
container-title: AI-Driven Transformation in Education and Business
3a1efa1edc5ff915cf6ae21a3322f5d27b45e644.abstract: Abstract Smart Supply Chains is one of the evolving concepts in management. From making to procuring to sourcing products, everything is artificial intelligence (AI)-driven. The applications of AI, like warehouse optimization, real-time stock tracking and product optimization, are popular applications of AI. With the use and adoption of fuzzy models like artificial neural network (ANN) frameworks, the dependency on humans has eventually reduced, making smart AI ensure the best decisions for operations. The paper includes a case study and a study of a theoretical model known as Supply Chain Operations Reference (SCOR) (Model), which is very popularly used in supply chain management and tracking logistics. The process includes plan, source, make, deliver and return. This is a good framework applied with AI in automation logistics for smoother functioning. It includes the use of fuzzy algorithms, genetic models and ANN networks to efficiently update and track product specifications as well as the delivery process without much human interaction. The ANN model is popular and widely used in data science as well as behavioural science.

title: Industry 4.0 and the Future of Digital Strategy: Pathways to Digital Value Creation
container-title: AI-Driven Transformation in Education and Business
218150914ff06798dd0fe2d20c483286c0ae044d.abstract: Abstract The acceptance and addition of such progressive digital technologies into operational processes and decision-making platforms have totally redefined how businesses conceptualize strategy in Industry 4.0. This chapter explores how digital value creation (DVC), as a process, has been facilitated through Industry 4.0 technology, with digital strategy orientation (DSO) as the intermediary. For instance, employing a quantitative research strategy that focuses on theoretical constructs, the chapter integrates theories from dynamic capability theory, the resource-based view (RBV) and IT business value theory to explain how businesses achieve strategic and performance outcomes from their digital investments. Data collection entailed conducting surveys among managers whose business entities adopted Industry 4.0 technology. The examples given for Industry 4.0 technology were Internet of Things technology, artificial intelligence technology, analytics technology, automation technology and cyber-physical system technology. This chapter empirically explores Industry 4.0 technology and DVC and how Industry 4.0 technology influences DSO through structural equation modelling techniques. The results show that Industry 4.0 technology affects DVC both directly and through DSO. Digital strategy is an integral part of any business through which technology capabilities are actually linked with overall business goals. Organizations primarily benefit from the outcomes of a digital strategy by making their operations more efficient, starting new creative activities and gaining a competitive advantage in Industry 4.0. The findings quite clearly bring out that firms focusing on digital strategy are better positioned to achieve long-term value from their Industry 4.0 investments.

title: Building Resilient Supply Chains: Collaborative Approaches to Cybersecurity for Critical Infrastructure
container-title: AI-Driven Transformation in Education and Business
69ef3b4bd98fa812b47926725f643b3bbca05bd0.abstract: Abstract Cybersecurity resilience has become a major factor in determining the strength of the supply chain, especially in sectors which constitute the national critical infrastructure, such as energy, transport and healthcare industries. This chapter examines the importance of collaboration to cyber resiliency in interdependent supply chains. The analysis is carried out through a conceptual literature review in which synthesis of 122 scholarly and policy papers published from 2014 to 2025 is made based on the concept of a network that brings into consideration theories of supply chain resiliency, resource dependency, collective action, socio-technological system and network governance. Cybersecurity resilience can be achieved only when more than one player is involved in the network. Through collaboration, information exchange concerning the nature of the threats, addressing such threats and public and private partnership will make the environment less vulnerable to cyberattacks and therefore more flexible. On the other hand, fragmented environments where there is very little cooperation are likely to be victims of system failure. This chapter outlines a framework called the Collaborative Cyber Resilience Framework, which is made up of components such as threat environment, actors, collaboration mechanism, governance and cyber resilience outcomes. One of the most essential things about collaboration according to the Collaborative Cyber Resilience Framework is that coordination will make collaboration better and sustainable. This study contributes to the existing literature in this field through offering a theory-based cyber security approach that focuses on the network aspect.

title: Sustainable Business Models and Artificial Intelligence for Handicraft Entrepreneurship: A Cross-Cultural Case Study
container-title: AI-Driven Transformation in Education and Business
280c6ee15c3a60b7ae449cdd269f945d69496f05.abstract: Abstract Across the globe, handicrafts have been validating cultures, identities and traditions that have been present in the modern world. At the same time, the craftsmen who are a part of the process of manufacturing the product not only validate themselves on the capability of manufacturing the product but also sustain their culture, heritage and tradition. The case study would revolve around the process of preserving cultural heritage crafts with the aid of sustainable business practices with the help of advanced artificial intelligence (AI)-based explanations. The research would be carried out as compensation for the rigorous qualitative case study to perceive four different handicraft cultures. This would include Pattachitra paintings from India, Dokra metal casting from India, Moroccan carpets from Morocco and Talavera from Mexico. Based on the research carried out, it has been identified that with the aid of AI for design invention, quality declaration, prediction analysis and digital storytelling with sustainable business practices, companies can sustain their attractiveness.

title: Measuring What Matters: A Systematic Review and Future Agenda for Social Impact Assessment
container-title: AI-Driven Transformation in Education and Business
bdf8ea266b44fc56f97e644ac31e64fd09230ecc.abstract: Abstract The use of Social Impact Assessment (SIA) is indispensable when considering the consequences of changes occurring in organizations, policies and initiatives to the society in which we live. Unfortunately, the present methods of SIA are fragmentary, instrumentally driven and lack a theoretical basis. To address these weaknesses, in this chapter, an extensive study of the current scientific literature on SIA methods is conducted based on the PRISMA approach and conceptual thematic analysis as well as the assessment of theoretical foundation of each tool. The most popular SIA methodologies, including Social Return on Investment (SROI), Theory of Change, environmental, social and governance (ESG) principles, Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) criteria and well-being measures, are examined. This chapter proposes Adaptive Social Impact Measurement (ASIM) as a methodological meta-framework aiming to reinterpret the notion of measurement through its adaptability, participation and educative dimensions. While the traditional measurement approach relies on indicators, ASIM values an interactive, dynamic process of assessment enabling it to tackle such challenges as standardization and context, accountability and learning, control and empowerment, and other problems. From the conclusions drawn from this chapter, it is possible to state that the current stage of development implies not one methodology of measuring social impact but several ones. Furthermore, some directions for future research are suggested by the author, such as the application of artificial intelligence and big data techniques, participation, hybrid valuation, ethics and decolonizing methods.

title: AI-Enabled Talent Management: Transforming Recruitment, Performance and Employee Engagement
container-title: AI-Driven Transformation in Education and Business
9886b48584b8d91269b829bd1a85d226cfa82673.abstract: Abstract Artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly transforming the way organizations recruit, assess, engage and retain employees by transforming the way they do these in the organization. Although existing literature has deeply explored various AI-based tools and applications in the field of human resource management, there is a strong need for a theoretical understanding of how AI alters the basic principles of talent management as a practice. Addressing the need, in this chapter, a theoretical and integrative approach has been applied, applying various established theories in the realms of organization, human resource and behaviours as a way of reinterpreting talent management in the AI era. Counter to conventional thinking that regards AI as a mere technological advancement, in this analysis, AI-based talent management has been identified as a social, technical and strategic phenomenon that alters the way organizations recruit members, manage their performance and encourage them to work. This analysis has applied classical concepts such as Person–Job Fit Theory, Signalling Theory, Human Capital Theory, Goal Setting Theory, Expectancy Theory, Agency Theory, Job Demands–Resources Theory, Social Exchange Theory, Self-Determination Theory, Resource-Based View and Institutional Theory. This chapter develops these new viewpoints and constructs a conceptual framework for AI-enabled talent management. The framework describes how talent outcomes are impacted by AI capabilities via hiring, performance and engagement processes.

title: Ethical, Legal and Governance Challenges of AI Implementation in Education and Enterprises
container-title: AI-Driven Transformation in Education and Business
7c0f5e366e46844378f9d457494688d59e3b288a.abstract: Abstract The rapid application of artificial intelligence (AI) in schools and organizations has impacted the process of decision-making, performance measurement and value addition. In post-secondary education, AI-powered learning analytics is increasingly being employed to support outcome-oriented education. In organizations, AI solutions are being employed to enhance organizational operation, employee management and organizational-level decision-making. Nevertheless, emerging parallel to these advances, ethical, legal and governance (ELG)-related challenges have appeared to have immense potential to become important considerations for systematic and evidence-based analysis, rather than simply normative discussion (Floridi et al., 2018; Mittelstadt et al., 2016). This chapter applies a data-driven model for analysis of ethical, legal and governance-related concerns emerging due to the employment of AI within schools and organizations. This research avoids literature-based discussion for its focus by applying hypothetical but realistic primary research data to test concerns regarding privacy, bias, transparency, regulatory compliance and maturity in a governed context. Based on business enterprises and colleges, the chapter applies structured synthetic data in the application of comparative, correlational and descriptive analytics to uncover quantifiable risk exposure and governance readiness scores (Kshetri, 2021; Raji et al., 2020). This chapter is an application of pattern identification in the quantification of ethical risk vulnerabilities, regulatory issues of compliance and governance inadequacies in sectors through the application of tables, analytics and text analysis (Jobin et al., 2019).

ae6266be1ed1df5296518c3aa806fee394c4f511.abstract: Abstract Flux-grown ZrTe 5 crystals with near-ideal stoichiometric composition exhibit semiconducting behavior at ambient pressure, which can be systematically manipulated by altering the Te content or by applying external pressure or magnetic field. In this study, we investigate the electrical resistivity and magnetoresistivity (MR) of flux-grown ZrTe 5 single crystals under pressures up to 7 GPa using a palm cubic anvil high-pressure cell. The pressure-dependent electrical resistivity reveals a systematic crossover from a semiconducting to a semimetallic phase between 3 and 4 GPa, which also coincides with the sign reversal of the Hall resistivity at low temperatures. These experimental observations collectively suggest the occurrence of a pressure-induced Lifshitz-like transition in the 3–4 GPa pressure range. Furthermore, at 7 GPa, we observe a sudden drop in electrical resistivity near 3.4 K, indicative of a superconducting transition. Notably, the observed superconducting transition temperature is nearly twice that reported for previously studied chemical vapor transport-grown ZrTe 5 crystals ( T c ≈ 1.8 K). To gain additional theoretical insight, we also performed first-principles calculations including spin–orbit coupling over a wide 0–6 GPa pressure range. The calculations reveal a substantial reconstruction of the low-energy electronic states, characterized by a pronounced enhancement of the density of states at the Fermi level and a significant modification of the band gap near 3 GPa, consistent with the experimentally observed phenomena. Symmetry-indicator and Wilson-loop analyses were further performed to investigate the evolution of the topological electronic structure under pressure. These findings demonstrate that pressure, together with subtle variations in crystal stoichiometry, drives remarkable electronic and structural transformations in ZrTe 5 , consistent with the pressure-induced Lifshitz transition and enhanced superconductivity in this Dirac semimetal.

title: A cross-condition fault diagnosis method for rolling bearings combining content-conditioned positional encoding and label-conditioned in-context learning
container-title: Measurement Science and Technology
6277d078ab3524e0930d2b99724a028703fcf189.abstract: Abstract Cross-condition fault diagnosis for rolling bearings is still a difficult task, mainly because vibration signals acquired under varying operating conditions exhibit distribution differences. To address this issue, this paper proposes a cross-condition fault diagnosis method named content-conditioned positional encoding (CCPE)-label-conditioned in-context learning (LCIC), which combines CCPE and LCIC. The proposed method employs a Transformer-based encoder to extract fault-related features from raw vibration signals, while adaptively enhancing temporal position information according to signal content. Meanwhile, label information from support samples is incorporated into the in-context learning process to improve the modeling of feature-label relationships and support query classification. An auxiliary supervised loss is further introduced to enhance feature discriminability and stabilize training. The effectiveness of the proposed method is verified through cross-condition experiments conducted on the CWRU and TBVD bearing datasets. Ablation studies further confirm the contributions of the main components.

title: Cross-machine profile prediction and differentiable optimization by learning multi-tokamak databases
container-title: Nuclear Fusion
a94f9b105966f8e3985cdb0188c10f5b7abbc335.abstract: Abstract The development of high-performance plasma regimes is becoming increasingly important for tokamak operation and scenario design. Conventional operation-space exploration relies on computationally expensive iterative simulations and experimental trial and error. Although machine-learning methods have recently been applied to this problem, many optimization approaches treat the predictive model as a black box. They can therefore require a large number of model evaluations and must be retrained when the objective or operational constraints change. In this work, we develop a neural-network surrogate for multi-tokamak profile prediction using public databases. Device-dependent dimensional input and output variables are transformed into appropriate normalized quantities. These normalizations of input and output variables enable the prediction model to be applied to new devices such as ITER. The surrogate forms a fully differentiable mapping from engineering parameters to plasma profiles and derived performance metrics. Automatic differentiation provides the exact Jacobian of this mapping and enables gradient-based optimization without treating the model as a black box. Under identical objectives and bounds, the proposed method requires substantially fewer model evaluations than other machine-learning approaches. The proposed framework offers an efficient route from multi-machine data to interpretable plasma optimization and reactor scenario design.

title: How token influence decays with causal distance: evidence across autoregressive language models from 14M to 32B parameters
container-title: Machine Learning: Science and Technology
74bc38172df6e3b7bea6d7cf19e8a50a3a3d9ddf.abstract: Abstract How the sensitivity of autoregressive language models to earlier input tokens depends on causal distance remains incompletely understood. Motivated by local-global decompositions in numerical solvers for differential equations, we study the local input-output response of trained autoregressive Transformers. For target position j and causal distance r , we take the Euclidean norm of the gradient of a selected next-token logit with respect to the input embedding at j − r . We aggregate profiles by their median. We consider trained autoregressive transformer language models from the Pythia, Qwen2.5, GPT-Neo, Llama 3.1, Gemma 3, SmolLM2, and Mistral families, spanning 14 million to 32 billion parameters, on Gutenberg text. We assess robustness through dataset, token-order, positional, aggregation, and logit-selection controls, complemented by initialization and architectural comparisons. Over the measured distance range, the median sensitivity profiles of trained Transformers decay slowly and are compactly described by a power-law-with-floor model, G ― ( r ) ≈ γ + β ( r + 1 ) − p , with fitted exponents ranging from approximately 0.57 to 0.9 , mostly between 0.65 and 0.9 . A broken power law sometimes improves the fit, but its breakpoint varies across models and its optimization yields multiple distinct solver endpoints. The profiles are similar for true-token and predicted-token logits. The slow decay is also observed on WikiText-103 and persists under token and sentence shuffling despite degraded prediction quality. It persists with randomly initialized input embeddings, but becomes small and nearly flat when the Transformer backbone and output head are randomized. Trained Pythia-shaped Elman recurrent neural networks show rapid sensitivity decay, while LSTM and GRU profiles decay more slowly but then bend downward. The measured quantity is a distance-resolved, aggregated first-order Jacobian response characterizing how sensitivity to localized input perturbations varies with causal source-target distance. These results identify a learned, slowly decaying long-range response that may motivate hierarchical mechanisms combining local interactions with a coarse representation of global coupling.

title: Compact metasurface-based spatially multiplexed snapshot spectral imaging via joint learning of optical encoding and spectral reconstruction
container-title: Optics Express
6be8ee7958a9c68a22bfd83955969e8d22321cca.abstract: Compact snapshot spectral imaging is attractive for applications requiring high frame rates and compact instrumentation, yet existing systems often face limited spectral encoding diversity or a tradeoff between spectral sampling and spatial resolution. We introduce metasurface spectral encoding into a spatially multiplexed multi-aperture snapshot architecture and further develop a differentiable metasurface co-design (DMC) framework to jointly optimize the spectral encoding responses and spectral reconstruction. The optical architecture integrates a metasurface filter array, a lens array, and a monochrome sensor to simultaneously acquire multiple spectrally encoded subimages of the same scene in a single exposure. Distinct metasurface responses are assigned to separate sub-apertures, enabling spatially continuous acquisition with diverse broadband spectral encoding. A differentiable metasurface co-design (DMC) framework is developed to jointly determine the spectral encoding responses and learn the mapping from compressed measurements to the target spectrum. The candidate metasurface response library is incorporated as a differentiable optical encoding layer, together with a learnable multichannel selection module that automatically identifies a set of complementary responses according to the reconstruction objective. A temperature-controlled softmax relaxation enables the discrete response selection to be optimized together with the spectral reconstruction network, allowing the encoding configuration to adapt directly to the reconstruction. Numerical simulations on the CAVE and ICVL datasets demonstrate effective spectral reconstruction with the proposed DMC approach, achieving average PSNR values of 40.283 dB and 46.298 dB, respectively. These results indicate the effectiveness of the proposed framework for compact snapshot spectral imaging.

title: An uncertainty-aware deep learning-based registration model for adaptive lung cancer radiotherapy
container-title: Physics in Medicine & Biology
047d182dc55632cbffffd42dec94ef85d8f54da6.abstract: Abstract Objective . To develop a deep learning (DL) based probabilistic 3D deformable image registration framework for uncertainty-aware dose accumulation in magnetic resonance imaging-guided radiotherapy of lung cancer. Approach . We propose TransMorph-prob (TM-prob), a variational Bayesian model that predicts the voxel-wise mean and variance of dense displacement fields (DDFs). Two TM-prob models were trained on an internal computed tomography dataset (725 patients) and a low-field MR-linac dataset (102 patients), and benchmarked against Monte Carlo dropout TransMorph (TM-MCD) and DIRUncertainty with B-spline initialization (ASDIR) on the deformable image registration laboratory (DIRLAB) 4DCT dataset (10 patients, 3000 landmarks), and an annotated MR-linac dataset (16 patients, 107 image pairs, 227 landmarks) with target and seven organ-at-risk contours. Both datasets contained an additional 1239/13 289 algorithm-generated landmarks. Performance was evaluated using target registration error (TRE), Dice similarity coefficient (DSC), landmark- and voxel-wise expected calibration errors (LECE/ECE), and dose distributions derived from 2000 DDF samples per patient. Main results . On the DIRLAB dataset, TM-prob achieved a median TRE of 1.8 mm/2.8 mm on manual/algorithm-generated landmarks, versus 1.3 mm/2.4 mm for ASDIR and 2.1 mm/3.0 mm for TM-MCD. On the MRI dataset, TM-prob achieved the median TRE of 3.9 mm/2.6 mm and a mean DSC of 0.87, matching ASDIR (3.3 mm/2.7 mm, and DSC of 0.87) while outperforming TM-MCD (4.4 mm/2.9 mm, and 0.84). In uncertainty calibration, TM-prob achieved a LECE of 1.74 mm/0.30 mm on MRI manual/algorithm-generated landmarks versus 2.41 mm/0.56 mm for ASDIR and 6.65 mm/3.92 mm for TM-MCD, and an average contour ECE of 5.8% versus 7.0% and 21.2%. Two patients with indistinct gross tumor volume boundaries exhibited substantially wider target D95 distributions, demonstrating that calibrated DDF uncertainty translates into clinically relevant dose-coverage uncertainty. Significance . TM-prob is an end-to-end DL model, achieving fast, well-calibrated, uncertainty-aware registration for lung cancer patients, enabling reliable DDF uncertainty propagation into dose accumulation for clinical decision-making in online adaptive radiotherapy.

title: AI时代编译原理分层实践教学改革
container-title: 教育发展论坛
20ab3ed55c9eec8c5c7cff92eb971e6413e2ae68.abstract: 随着AI发展对软件开发与计算机教育的影响,地方工科高校的编译原理课程在课时压缩和学生基础差异明显。传统的从零手写完整编译器,学生容易感受到挫败,且实验成果仅停留于理论层面,学生学习兴趣不高。本文在原"课程实验+课程设计"的两阶段安排的基础上,探索面向工程应用和能力拓展的分层实践教学改革。改革中第一阶段开展AI协同的编译原理性实验,第二阶段保留编译系统集成的同时,增强编译理论的实际工程应用,相应地,实践考核改用编译系统集成保底,加应用拓展项目增值的组合方式。对比改革实施组与历史比较组的实验提交、代码相似度检测、答辩记录和归档作品,发现改革后完整编译流程完成率从70%多增长到99%,存在代码抄袭的作品比例从约20%降至约1%;课程设计作品类型也更加丰富。但是也存在着"程序能运行、代码难解释"、重度依赖AI整体构建和代码验证不足等问题。针对这些问题,本文提出编译各模块的接口约束、版本追溯、提示词记录与随机代码走查等手段,加强对学生学习过程的管理。由于本研究采用历史队列比较,相关结果主要用于呈现改革后的变化趋势,不能将其仅仅归因于AI工具使用的效果。

title: AI赋能民事诉讼法课程个性化学习路径的探索与思考
container-title: 教育发展论坛
46143faedda4629d8550ea202a220d616de22099.abstract: 以AI为代表的数智时代,对民事诉讼法的教学提出新挑战。传统的民事诉讼法教学存在着教学模式固化、学生被动学习、学情不客观、评价方式单一等问题,亟须进行全面而深刻的改革。AI赋能民事诉讼法个性化学习有现实的可行性,它符合国家教育教学改革政策导向,符合社会发展与学生培养需求,同时有强大的数智技术支持。AI可以从学情画像、学习资源供给、学习过程引导、学习评价反馈四个角度赋能,对前面提到的问题进行破冰,提供有针对性的措施,推动民事诉讼法课程个性化学习路径不断优化。

title: 生成式AI赋能的人才培养模式研究—基于数据计算及应用专业视角
container-title: 教育发展论坛
3e7a0248358a477fc0d098e23131f7b126d64ceb.abstract: 随着生成式AI的快速迭代,以生成式AI为代表的智能技术深度融入高等教育,已成为推动专业数字化转型、提升人才培养质量的核心路径。数据计算及应用专业作为新工科背景下的应用理科专业,具有理论性强、实践要求高、技术迭代快等特征。本研究立足生成式AI赋能教育的时代需求,明确数据计算及应用专业人才培养目标与能力定位,从课程体系、教学模式、实践平台、评价机制四个维度构建AI赋能人才培养路径,推动专业教学向智能化、个性化、实战化转型,为地方高校同类专业改革提供借鉴。

title: Prior-residual learning for ranking future influential nodes in temporal networks
container-title: Physica Scripta
97b1bf02cebf166ae6c2efc5eefd1ed745f16e0d.abstract: Abstract Whether temporal learning adds anything to a strong structural forecast is rarely tested directly. We recast future influential-node ranking as a prior-residual problem: a chronologically selected centrality prior plus a learned correction whose weight is fixed on validation data before the test period is seen. Across nine networks the correction raises mean Kendall agreement by 0.0203 under the original protocol and by 0.0120 when tied scores are preserved, with a zero median and four positive networks. Because five of the nine differences are exactly zero, the adjusted test cannot discriminate, so we evaluate the correction as a decision rather than an average. Validation abstains in 26 of 45 fits and returns the prior unchanged; in the 19 fits where it opens, 17 gain. Residual structure is predictable out of sample (positive squared-error skill in 45 of 45 fits), yet head-node retrieval and graph-filtered features gain nothing. The contribution is an auditable rule for when a learned correction should be trusted.

title: Displayed judgment certainty reorganizes source selection in self-formed networks
360a7428854f6db2e7f9d25f9c2882c082c60c8f.abstract: Collective intelligence in self-formed networks depends on which judgments people choose to observe, as well as on how they integrate those judgments. We tested whether displaying judgment certainty reorganizes source selection and improves subsequent accuracy. Across eight online sessions, 273 participants evaluated 14 true and false news headlines, formed costly directed observation networks, and revised their beliefs over five updates. During network formation, we manipulated the visibility of certainty, defined by the extremity of each source's private probability judgment, while belief direction and source accuracy remained hidden. Displaying certainty produced denser networks and redirected links toward more certain sources; current popularity also predicted selection. Visibility increased exposure to highly certain but incorrect judgments, without a clear improvement in the relative accuracy of selected sources. Accuracy increased across repeated judgments, but certainty visibility did not detectably increase this improvement and reduced reconstructed net scores under the task's payoff structure. Observations with selected sources showed greater improvement than those without, and improvement was associated with selected sources' initial accuracy. Belief revisions moved toward selected sources and decreased with participants' own certainty. Among six compact predictive models, certainty-reinforcing DeGroot provided the best penalized and aggregate held-out prediction, although it did not capture the large first update. These findings distinguish a cue's ability to attract attention from its ability to identify useful information: displayed certainty can reorganize costly information acquisition without a detectable average accuracy benefit.

title: Minds Meet Machines: The Joint Role of Trust and Intellectual Humility in AI Persuasion
d8b7b16ca9c75a1deb3b83f3c4c11a9668b438b8.abstract: Research shows that AI models have a remarkable ability to change people’s minds following a short conversation, a notoriously difficult task for human communicators. Such persuasive paradigms provide a unique opportunity to examine which psychological characteristics predict receptivity to counter-attitudinal information. We focus on two characteristics: intellectual humility (IH), reflecting openness to revising one’s beliefs following new information, and trust in the information source (AI). To establish the role of a-priori dispositions that determine acceptance of new information, we ran two online studies, sampling British participants with a negative attitude toward legal immigrants (N = 294). We replicated previous findings showing significant and lasting attitude change following a brief exchange with GPT, but crucially, this effect was not uniform. In Study 1, attitude change was greatest among participants with higher initial trust in AIs and higher intellectual humility. Study 2 extended this finding by measuring both dispositions a week before the conversation with GPT, revealing the same pattern: opinion change was greatest among those who were both open to new information and trusting of its source. These findings highlight the centrality of recipient dispositions, suggesting that the relationship between source trust and persuasion depends on recipients' intellectual humility. More broadly, source trust may function as more than a heuristic cue, and its relationship with attitude change may depend on recipients' willingness to recognize the fallibility of their beliefs. Together, these findings extend perspectives on persuasion by highlighting the joint role of source trust and recipients' epistemic dispositions in belief revision.

title: How Self-Location Predicts the Degree and Quality of the Felt Sense of Connection
9d398db6f0d4005689cddfdb909f394cdb9be432.abstract: Research has typically examined how self-location in the head or heart is associated with traits and behavior, yet its link to relationality—specifically the felt sense of connection—remains underexplored. This study investigated how dispositional self-location predicts the embodied experience of being relationally linked to others and the world. We initially developed the Dispositional Self-Location Questionnaire (DSLQ), an association-based instrument designed to minimize potential subjective bias in participant reporting of self-location. Using this measure, we categorized a U.S. sample of 218 adults who had reported a strong experience of connection as head-locators or heart-locators and assessed them on self-construal, self-expansiveness, connectedness, and perceived qualities of connection. Head-locators reported firmer self-boundaries, emphasizing independence, rationality, and decision-making. In contrast, Heart-locators scored significantly higher on connectedness to both self and world, and on metapersonal self-construal, describing their connections as close, warm, caring, and authentic. These findings suggest that self-location functions as a somatic attentional stance that anticipates the experiential boundary between self and other: the head favors separation and autonomy, while the heart favors openness and expanded belonging.

title: Empowering the anesthesiologist: Navigating the future of AI-driven visualization and wearable technology in regional anesthesia
container-title: Perioperative Precision Medicine
b445412f8c53724ad77ef1c335303383faadf067.abstract: In current regional anesthesia practice, “visualization” typically refers to the real-time imaging and display of subcutaneous anatomical structures with ultrasound imaging, and “wearable technology” refers to hands-free, optical head-mounted displays (e.g., smart glasses) that can project digital information directly into the clinician’s field of view. The paradigm shift in the history of regional anesthesia from anatomical landmark techniques to ultrasound guidance has revolutionized the art of regional anesthesia and transformed a blind procedural technique into a visually guided intervention.

title: Modern Perspectives on the Psychology of Learning: Insights from the PTE Organization’s Top 20 Principles for Teaching and Learning
container-title: Adhyapana Prathibha
60b402d6740af96123f4618fc00d1b9691092509.abstract: The Top 20 Principles for Teaching and Learning, developed by the American Psychological Association (APA), provide a research-based framework to enhance Pre-K–12 education by integrating cognitive, motivational, social, and emotional perspectives on learning. This chapter explores these principles with a focus on their application in the Sri Lankan educational context, emphasizing teacher professional development, student well being, and instructional effectiveness. Each principle highlights evidence-based strategies for promoting mastery, creativity, self-regulation, intrinsic motivation, and effective classroom management, while also addressing assessment practices grounded in fairness and psychological science. By adapting these principles to local cultural and classroom environments, Sri Lankan educators can foster deeper understanding, meaningful engagement, and holistic development in learners. The chapter underscores the value of aligning theory with practice to create supportive learning environments that enhance both teaching and learning outcomes, preparing students for lifelong learning and success.

005a097359854aa3401500b5e229e05389343b86.abstract: අන්තර්ජාල ප්‍රවේශය සහිත ජංගම උපාංග ලෝක ව්‍යාප්ත අධ්‍යාපන ක්ෂේත්‍රය තුළ ප්‍රබල ප්‍රවණතාවක් ලෙස (M - Learning) මතු වී ඇති අතර, එය ශ්‍රී ලංකාවේ උසස් අධ්‍යාපන සන්දර්භය තුළ ද අඩු වැඩි වශයෙන් වැදගත් භූමිකාවක් ඉටු කරයි. මෙම ලිපිය මගින් ජංගම ඉගෙනුමේ බහුවිධ ක්ෂේත්‍ර, ප්‍රතිලාභ සහ අභියෝග මෙන් ම තාක්ෂණය පිළිගැනීමේ න්‍යායාත්මක ආකෘතීන් වන TAM සහ UTAUT ඇසුරින් ශ්‍රී ලාංකේය සන්දර්භය විමර්ශනය කරයි. ලිපිය මගින් නව ජංගම ඉගෙනුම් තාක්ෂණයන් කෙරෙහි සිසුන්ගේ සහ ගුරුවරුන්ගේ ආකල්ප හා දැනුම සකස් වියයුතු ආකාරයත්, සීමාකාරී ප්‍රතිපත්තිමය රාමු මධ්‍යයේ වුවද ජංගම ඉගෙනුම් ක්‍රියාවලියක් පවත්වාගෙන යාමට ඇති හැකියාවන් පිළිබඳවත් පෙන්වා දෙනු ලබයි. එමෙන්ම ජංගම ඉගෙනුම හරහා අධ්‍යාපනික නම්‍යශීලී බව සහ සම්පත් වෙත ප්‍රවේශය ලැබුණ ද ඩිජිටල් බෙදීම, අන්තර්ජාල සම්බන්ධතාවල පවතින දුර්වලතා සහ අවධානය වෙනතකට යොමුවීම වැනි බාධක සිසුන්ගේ අධ්‍යාපන ප්‍රතිඵල කෙරෙහි බලපාන ආකාරයත් මෙම ගැටලු අවම වන ආකාරයට ජංගම ඉගෙනුම් තාක්ෂණය අධ්‍යාපන පද්ධතියට සාර්ථකව ඒකාබද්ධ කිරීම සඳහා "මඟ පෙන්වීම සහිත භාවිතයක්" කෙරෙහි යොමුවීමට අවශ්‍ය ප්‍රතිපත්තිමය නවීකරණයක අවශ්‍යතාවය ද අවධාරණය කෙරේ.

title:
Pedagogical Experiences, Challenges, and Ethical AI Use in Peer Writing Tutoring:
            Insights from the Azcapotzalco Writing Center (CEAZ)

08f4845584eb4b199eab416a27afce3bf5142738.abstract: El presente artículo busca reflexionar sobre los retos encontrados en la práctica del modelo de tutorías entre pares, en el Centro de Escritura Azcapotzalco (CEAZ), durante mi trayectoria como voluntario en el programa de tutores de escritura del 2024 al 2025, centrando la atención en los desafíos y usos éticos de la inteligencia artificial (IA) en los procesos de escritura, las aportaciones de la pedagogía de Paulo Freire en este modelo de aprendizaje y acompañamiento así como los desafíos de la aplicación del modelo con tutorados universitarios de distintas áreas del conocimiento.

title: Machines in the Middle: How AI Use Changes What Coworkers Think of, and Do for, One Another
26d21055970e127e32645343f5dd00f0c8042aa8.abstract: Generative AI is now embedded in how coworkers, leaders, and organizations communicate, yet its effects on the relationships among them are still poorly understood. This review synthesizes recent research on how an individual’s AI use changes the way others perceive, judge, and behave toward them, and shows that these effects can be explained by established theories of human-human interaction, including attribution theory, computers-as-social-actors, the integrative model of organizational trust, social exchange theory, and resource-based theories. The evidence suggests that observers often read AI use as a sign of disposition rather than circumstance, judging AI users as less competent, motivated, warm, and authentic, and that disclosure does not repair the resulting loss of trust. These perceptions carry over into behavior: coworkers reciprocate less, share less knowledge, and show less prosocial behavior toward AI users, while AI-related job insecurity, loneliness, and work alienation further strain ties among colleagues. AI use also loosens moral standards and shifts how blame is assigned, making people more critical of others’ work but more lenient toward misconduct. These effects are conditional rather than uniformly negative. AI can reduce loneliness, improve coordination, and prompt employees to invest more in emotionally supportive ties, and relational buffers such as leader-member exchange, shared leadership, and supervisor support can offset its costs. The review concludes that AI’s costs to workplace relationships run mainly through indirect pathways, not through the technology itself. It outlines organizational implications, including clear norms for when and why AI is used and protection of socially valued tasks, and identifies priorities for future research: longitudinal designs, team- and network-level studies, intervention research, and more diverse samples.

title: OSIRA, an AI Early Warning System Using Open Source Intelligence for Digital Fraud Prevention
container-title: Jurnal Teknika dan Informatika (JTI)
e11b2e99293184c34c74168bfca20102846b4736.abstract: Purpose: This study designs and evaluates OSIRA (Open Source Intelligence Risk Analyzer), an early warning system based on artificial intelligence that integrates Open Source Intelligence (OSINT) and Natural Language Processing (NLP) to identify digital fraud indications before they enter formal reporting mechanisms in a cashless society. Research Methodology: The study uses a design science approach consisting of problem analysis, system design, risk score formulation, and a limited scale proof of concept simulation. The simulation used 540 synthetic texts from 50 template groups, divided into 394 training and 146 testing texts through a group based split, and classified them with Term Frequency–Inverse Document Frequency (TF IDF) features and logistic regression. Results: OSIRA integrates web crawling, text preprocessing, fraud classification, entity extraction, a risk engine, and an early warning module. At a threshold of 0.50, the model achieved 82.88% accuracy, 79.66% precision, 98.95% recall, an F1 score of 88.26%, and a ROC AUC of 0.8528, but its false positive rate reached 47.06%, mainly for normal texts discussing fraud related topics. Conclusions: OSIRA shows initial feasibility as an additional intelligence layer that can shift fraud mitigation from reactive response toward proactive fraud intelligence. Limitations: The evaluation used synthetic rather than real OSINT data, a baseline classifier with limited contextual understanding, and risk score weights and thresholds that have not been empirically calibrated. Contributions: The study offers a conceptual and technical framework for using pre reporting public signals in fraud risk management and provides guidance for banks, digital wallet providers, and regulators.

title: Advancing quality education through academic libraries: an empirical assessment of information literacy and learning outcomes in the higher education system
container-title: Reference Services Review
245b8a70e4e595bce5e95f0a98b4ca1c71ba4baa.abstract: Purpose This study examines the relationships among Academic Library Services (ALS), Information Literacy Competence (ILC) and Learning Outcomes and Academic Impact (LOA) among Ph.D. scholars at a selected Indian university. Guided by the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020 and Sustainable Development Goal 4, the study evaluates the contribution of ALS and information literacy to doctoral learning and research development. Design/methodology/approach A descriptive cross-sectional survey was conducted among 452 Ph.D. scholars from diverse academic disciplines. Data were collected through a structured questionnaire and analysed using descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation, multiple regression, an independent-samples t-test and one-way ANOVA. Findings The findings revealed significant positive relationships between ALS and ILC (r = 0.60, p &lt; 0.001) and between ILC and LOA (r = 0.63, p &lt; 0.001). Multiple regression analysis showed that ALS (ß = 0.26, p &lt; 0.001) and ILC (ß = 0.28, p &lt; 0.001) were significant positive predictors of LOA. The measurement instrument demonstrated high internal consistency (Cronbach’s α = 0.90). No statistically significant gender difference was identified, whereas perceptions differed significantly across academic disciplines (F = 3.84, p = 0.005). Overall, the findings indicate that ALS and ILC are positively associated with perceived LOA among doctoral scholars. Research limitations/implications The findings highlight the value of curriculum-integrated information literacy instruction, strengthened digital library services and discipline-specific research support for doctoral education. The results may inform academic library planning, information literacy programmes and curriculum development in alignment with NEP 2020 and SDG 4. Originality/value This study provides context-specific empirical evidence on the relationships among ALS, ILC, and LOA among Ph.D. scholars in the Indian higher education context. It strengthens the evidence base concerning the educational role of academic libraries in supporting doctoral learning and research within the broader policy frameworks of NEP 2020 and SDG 4.

title: Rethinking English Language Learning: A Needs Analysis in Fisheries and Marine Science Education
container-title: International Journal of Science Education and Cultural Studies
596fa96fba03f9d44c54190f93095a44ca17f45f.abstract: This study seeks to analyze the needs of Fisheries and Marine Science students in learning English to be a basis in developing a contextually relevant English for Specific Purposes (ESP) curriculum. The study used a descriptive qualitative design and included 23 participants: 20 undergraduate students in the third to fifth semesters, two English lecturers, and one Marine Science lecturer. Data were collected using semi-structured interviews, focus group discussions, classroom observations and document analysis and analysed thematically using the concepts of necessities, lacks and wants. The results identified five major themes: academic English proficiency, professional communication, technical vocabulary, speaking confidence, and contextualized learning activities. Students faced difficulties in understanding scientific articles in international journals, writing academic texts and understanding terminology specific to fisheries and marine science disciplines. They also lacked confidence in speaking English that influenced their participation in English communication activities. Students also said they would like to have lessons about words used in the marine industry, workshops on how to read scientific journals, practice making presentations and learning through simulations. The results of the study suggest the need for an ESP curriculum that incorporates academic literacy, subject specific vocabulary and practical communication activities. The study offers an empirical foundation for synchronizing English teaching to the academic requirements and anticipated professional communication skills of Fisheries and Marine Science students.

title: AI-driven urban futures from global trends to African perspectives
container-title: Built Environment Project and Asset Management
726707b9194a4b4f6f90a7f83729630b315efbe5.abstract: Purpose Despite rapid advances in Artificial Intelligence (AI), and specifically Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) for urban planning, a gap persists between these innovations and their applicability in African contexts shaped by informality, data scarcity, limited capacity and climate vulnerability. This study examines how GenAI is reshaping urban planning globally and assesses its relevance, adaptability and risks in African contexts, identifying pathways for inclusive, legitimate and context-sensitive deployment. Design/methodology/approach A systematic literature review used a Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA)-guided framework extended through PRALSMA (Preferred Reporting of AI-integrated Literature Search and Meta-Analysis), a reporting extension for transparent AI-assisted reviews. Peer-reviewed articles (2020–2025) from Web of Science and OpenAlex, with selected grey literature, gave 82 sources analysed through manual review and AI-assisted tools, with all outputs verified and triangulated for robustness and traceability. Findings GenAI is transforming urban planning through multimodal workflows enabling rapid scenario generation, visualisation and communication, but effectiveness depends on localisation, bias mitigation, institutional capacity and legitimacy. Without these, GenAI risks misleading or exclusionary “blueprint” solutions, underscoring the need for context-sensitive adaptation. Originality/value The study integrates creativity-in-design, relational agency and democratic design to frame GenAI as a socio-technical participant rather than an autonomous planner, offering an Africa-relevant agenda for responsible, human-centred implementation aligned with equity, sustainability and resilience.

title: Newly Reported Major Diagnoses and Subsequent Self-Reported Hypertension Treatment Status in Korean Adults Aged 50 Years or Older
container-title: American Journal of Hypertension
152837715c3bde29e4f063ae786e0f2b9aa2d8ea.abstract: Abstract BACKGROUND The association between a newly reported major diagnosis and subsequent self-reported hypertension-treatment status remains uncertain. METHODS We analyzed seven overlapping periods of three visits approximately 2 years apart in the Korean Longitudinal Study of Ageing (2006–2008–2010 through 2018–2020–2022). Eligibility required age ≥50 years, physician-diagnosed hypertension at Visit 1, and reported antihypertensive medication use or hypertension treatment at Visits 1 and 2. Newly reported diabetes, cancer, stroke, heart disease, or chronic lung disease was assessed at Visit 2. The Visit 3 outcome was a report of no current hypertension treatment, including no antihypertensive medication use. Modified-Poisson regression used participant-clustered standard errors. The adjusted absolute risk difference was defined as the standardized probability with a newly reported diagnosis minus that without one. RESULTS Among 13,579 observation periods from 3,581 participants, 932 included a newly reported diagnosis. Adjusted probabilities of no reported treatment were 7.5% with and 8.4% without a newly reported diagnosis. The adjusted risk ratio for not receiving treatment for hypertension, including antihypertensive medication, associated with a newly reported diagnosis was 0.89 (95% confidence interval 0.71–1.13); the adjusted absolute risk difference (newly reported diagnosis minus no newly reported diagnosis) was −0.90 percentage points (95% confidence interval −2.66 to 0.85). CONCLUSIONS A newly reported major diagnosis was not associated with self-reported antihypertensive medication use or hypertension treatment approximately 2 years later.
