title: Design and Implementation of a Dual-mode Digital Backend for the GZNU Small-aperture Antenna Array
container-title: Research in Astronomy and Astrophysics
d0115193b20507b4975c31e1341b36939f1cd816.abstract: Abstract Small-aperture radio antenna arrays provide flexible platforms for high-time-resolution searches of bright radio transients, such as pulsar giant pulses and fast radio bursts (FRBs), as well as for long-duration monitoring and technical validation of array observing modes. To support the Guizhou Normal University (GZNU) small-aperture antenna array under construction, we developed a dual-mode digital backend based on the Xilinx RFSoC 47DR. The backend is designed to serve two complementary observing requirements. In Baseband Mode, the backend digitizes analog signals at a sampling rate of 1024 MHz and streams the raw voltage data with VDIF header to a server via a 100 Gbps interface for further processing. In PSRFITS Mode, dual-polarization signals from a single antenna are channelized using a polyphase filter bank (PFB) and Fourier transform, integrated, gain-adjusted, quantized, and converted into AABBCRCI polarization products before being encapsulated into PSRFITS files. System characterization show that the relative timing offsets among four ADC channels are on the order of 10 −2 −10 −1 ns for a reference signal at various frequencies. Packet-transmission tests show no packet loss during a four-hour PSRFITS-mode run, while a short-duration Baseband-mode test gives a packet loss rate of approximately 0.04%, limited mainly by the current storage system. Validation was completed via observations of the pulsar B0329+54 in PSRFITS Mode, resulting in well-defined waterfall plots and integrated profiles. These results demonstrate the initial end-to-end functionality of the RFSoC-based backend and provide a basis for future long-duration baseband recording, multi-antenna interferometric verification, and fast-transient searches.

title: Seeing clearly without your lenses: digital holographic microscopy analysis of blood culture Gram stains
container-title: Journal of Clinical Microbiology
b8087530f3aba95642d7464a4edf217641637030.abstract: ABSTRACT While automation and digital imaging technologies are now available for setup and workup of microbiology cultures, specimen Gram stain reading is still manually performed and requires experience to provide accurate results. In the article by K. P. Smith, E. Boulanger, M. Elkan, J. Fink, et al. (J Clin Microbiol 64:e01627-25, 2026, https://doi.org/10.1128/jcm.01627-25 ), the authors use a non-optical-based methodology, digital holographic microscopy, in combination with artificial intelligence to automate and provide interpretations and digital images of Gram stains from positive blood culture broths. While this differs from previous optical-based methods for Gram stain slide scanning, it demonstrated comparable performance. Gram stain slide staining and assistance by artificial intelligence for slide interpretation are a tantalizing future tool for clinical microbiology laboratories.

title: Evaluating Wearable Electrodermal Activity as a Candidate Digital Biomarker of Occupational Well-Being: Longitudinal Real-World Study
container-title: JMIR Formative Research
11648f9328b70ac6b0163881dd871f848969f1de.abstract: Abstract Background Wearable physiological sensing and mobile self-report methods offer new opportunities for monitoring occupational well-being in real-world settings. However, interpreting continuous physiological signals in relation to psychological states such as job burnout and work engagement remains challenging, particularly when using deployable systems that rely on proprietary signal processing. Objective This study examined a proprietary electrodermal activity (EDA)–derived arousal index as a candidate digital biomarker for research on occupational well-being. We examined associations between job burnout, work engagement, and sympathetic activation indexed by a device-derived EDA metric, and assessed whether combining physiological data with mobile-based ecological momentary assessment (mEMA) of valence provides complementary information. Methods A total of 75 knowledge workers participated, with sufficient paired physiological and mEMA data obtained from 57 participants in wave 1 and 51 in wave 2 (total observations=108). Participants were monitored continuously over 14 consecutive days at 2 time points 6 months apart. Autonomic arousal was operationalized using the device-derived double normalized electrodermal activity (DNE) index obtained from wearable EDA recordings. Valence was assessed using mEMA. Associations between physiological activation, valence, and occupational well-being outcomes were analyzed using generalized least squares models with a compound-symmetry covariance structure to account for repeated observations within participants. Results The wearable-derived DNE index showed a clear diurnal pattern, with higher values during daytime and lower values during nighttime. Greater within-nighttime DNE variability was associated with higher burnout (estimate=0.02, 95% CI 0.01-0.03; P <.001) and lower engagement (estimate=−0.03, 95% CI −0.05 to −0.01; P =.009). The daily DNE × valence interaction was also associated with engagement (estimate=−0.35, 95% CI −0.69 to −0.00; P =.047). Removing all DNE and valence variables significantly worsened model fit for both burnout ( χ ² ₁₀ =28.5; P =.002) and engagement ( χ ² ₁₀ =23.7; P =.009), supporting their combined explanatory value. Model-based profiles further showed that negative valence was associated with higher predicted burnout and lower predicted engagement than positive valence across both high- and low-arousal scenarios, although prediction intervals were wide and partially overlapping. Model comparisons showed that including physiological and mEMA-based variables improved explanatory power. Conclusions These findings provide practical evidence that continuous wearable EDA monitoring can be combined with mEMA in naturalistic occupational settings. Associations between the proprietary DNE index, valence, burnout, and work engagement provide preliminary convergent evidence supporting further evaluation of DNE as a candidate digital biomarker in occupational well-being research. Interpretation remains constrained by the proprietary signal-processing pipeline, and this study does not establish construct-specific validity, prospective predictive performance, screening or diagnostic validity, sensitivity to change, or individual-level monitoring usage.

title: Monocular Interacting-Hand Reconstruction with Multimodal Context Fusion and Spatial Attention
container-title: ACM Transactions on Multimedia Computing, Communications, and Applications
a47dfde1fe22acb35e4fb2d872d52525588a142c.abstract: 3D hand reconstruction from monocular RGB images has attracted increasing attention due to its low cost and ease of deployment. However, accurately reconstructing interacting hands remains challenging, primarily because mutual occlusion leads to missing visual evidence, while image cropping weakens global spatial consistency. To address these issues, we propose the Context-Aware Interacting Hand Reconstruction Network (CANet), a monocular interacting-hand reconstruction framework that integrates multimodal context fusion with structured spatial attention. Specifically, CANet leverages estimated depth maps, edge contours, and center heatmaps to retain global contextual cues and guide reconstruction in occluded regions. A hierarchical spatial attention module further enhances spatial consistency by separately modeling intra-hand structural dependencies and inter-hand interactions, enabling more coherent reasoning about complex hand poses. Experiments across multiple public benchmarks demonstrate that CANet consistently improves the accuracy of both hand pose estimation and mesh reconstruction.

title: Digital Behavioral Risk Stratification Tool Integrated With HIV Online Self-Testing for HIV Positivity Among Men Who Have Sex With Men: Retrospective Observational Study
container-title: Journal of Medical Internet Research
06fb15558507d529e369a69142bb197c6c232c05.abstract: Abstract Background Due to concerns about privacy breaches and the fear of social stigma, some individuals engaging in high-risk behaviors—particularly men who have sex with men (MSM)—may avoid in-person HIV testing services and instead choose to purchase HIV self-test kits online. Unlike traditional e-commerce platforms that provide self-test kits directly without conducting risk assessments, the “Easy Test Know” platform integrates a structured behavioral risk assessment prior to purchasing an HIV self-test kit, allowing users to be categorized into different HIV risk groups. Objective This study aimed to evaluate the performance of a digital HIV behavioral risk stratification tool integrated with online self-testing among MSM and to determine whether incorporating multidimensional behavioral indicators—particularly the high-risk venue diversity score—could improve the prediction of HIV positivity compared with the platform’s existing rule-based risk-scoring algorithm. Methods This retrospective observational study used data from the “Easy Test Know” platform between November 2023 and February 2025. The analysis included 9961 MSM classified as medium or high risk who had a usable HIV test result. The continuous platform score and the deployed categorical output were evaluated, and enhanced and fully adjusted Firth logistic regression models were compared using areas under the receiver operating characteristic curves (AUCs) with stratified bootstrap 95% CIs, DeLong tests, calibration measures, and bootstrap optimism correction based on 1000 successful model refits. Results Among 9961 participants, 9044 (90.8%) were classified as high risk, and 58 (0.58%) had an observed HIV-positive result. Positivity was 0.6% (n=54) in the high-risk group and 0.4% (4/914) in the medium-risk group, but the difference was not statistically significant ( P =.70). The deployed categorical output had an AUC of 0.512 (95% CI 0.477‐0.539), with 93.1% (54/58) sensitivity and 9.2% (913/9903) specificity, whereas the continuous platform score had an AUC of 0.646 (95% CI 0.567‐0.725). Each 1-category increase in high-risk venue diversity was associated with higher odds of observed HIV positivity (odds ratio 2.04, 95% CI 1.53‐2.74; P for trend <.001). The enhanced and fully adjusted models had apparent AUCs of 0.728 (95% CI 0.656‐0.801) and 0.752 (95% CI 0.686‐0.817) and optimism-corrected AUCs of 0.688 and 0.713, respectively. Their optimism-corrected calibration slopes were 0.940 and 0.936. Conclusions Compared with the platform’s original rule-based scoring system, the data-driven behavioral models incorporating high-risk venue diversity showed improved predictive performance, although bootstrap optimism correction yielded more conservative estimates. These findings support further development and independent validation of data-driven approaches to optimize digital HIV risk assessment tools.

title: Digital Health Interventions for Pregnancy- and Childbirth-Related Posttraumatic Stress Disorder Symptoms in Postpartum Women: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
container-title: Journal of Medical Internet Research
1163f0f0dba78e4f9ea73574a99e01f4654397dc.abstract: Background Pregnancy- or childbirth-related traumatic experiences may lead to posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD) symptoms during the postpartum period, adversely affecting women and their families. Digital health interventions may improve access to psychological support; however, evidence of their effectiveness for pregnancy- and childbirth-related posttraumatic stress disorder (PCR-PTSD) symptoms remains limited and has not been systematically synthesized. Objective This study aimed to evaluate the effects of digital health interventions on PCR-PTSD symptoms in postpartum women, with depressive and anxiety symptoms as secondary outcomes. Methods We searched 7 English-language and 4 Chinese-language databases from inception through April 30, 2026, to identify randomized controlled trials (RCTs) evaluating digital health interventions in women who had experienced pregnancy- or childbirth-related traumatic events and were assessed for PTSD symptoms during the postpartum period. Risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 tool. Effect estimates were pooled using random-effects models with restricted maximum likelihood estimation and Hartung-Knapp adjustments and reported as standardized mean differences (SMDs) with 95% CIs. Statistical heterogeneity, 95% prediction intervals (PIs), subgroup effects, and the robustness of pooled estimates were also examined. Results A total of 10 RCTs involving 1026 participants were included. Of these, 9 trials (809 participants) reported PTSD symptom outcomes immediately after the intervention, and 6 trials (413 participants) reported outcomes at follow-up. Digital health interventions were associated with lower PTSD symptom severity immediately after the intervention (SMD −0.59, 95% CI −0.98 to −0.19, 95% PI −1.72 to 0.54; P=.01), with substantial heterogeneity (I²=79.86%). However, the pooled effect was not statistically significant at the longest available follow-up (SMD −0.36, 95% CI −1 to 0.27, 95% PI −2.03 to 1.31; P=.20). All 95% PIs crossed the null. No statistically significant subgroup differences were observed by PTSD-related eligibility requirements, delivery modality, intervention duration, or trauma context. A statistically significant subgroup difference was observed by health care provider involvement (Q=14.46; P<.001); however, this exploratory finding should be interpreted cautiously. Sensitivity analyses supported the robustness of the pooled effect on PTSD symptoms immediately after the intervention. Conclusions Digital health interventions may be associated with short-term reductions in PTSD, depressive, and anxiety symptoms among women with pregnancy- or childbirth-related trauma. However, substantial heterogeneity and PIs crossing the null limit confidence in these effects. Further well-designed trials with clinically interpretable outcomes and longer follow-up are needed. Trial Registration PROSPERO CRD420261290528; https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261290528

title: Experimental Investigation of Static and Fatigue Flexural Behavior of Bio-Sourced Sandwich Composites with Various Auxetic Core Topologies
container-title: International Journal of Applied Mechanics
9f795eab833b981bfa5c23ef70efb0a21ec4d119.abstract: Auxetic-core sandwich structures have attracted increasing attention due to their unconventional deformation mechanisms and their potential to enhance mechanical performance. This study investigates the influence of auxetic core topology on the static and fatigue flexural behavior of biocomposite sandwich structures fabricated using fused deposition modeling (FDM) with flax-fiber-reinforced polylactic acid (PFF). Six distinct architected core topologies were investigated: single and double auxetic, single and double arc, dumbbell, and infinity configurations. Static three-point bending and flexural fatigue tests were conducted to evaluate flexural stiffness, strength, fatigue life, and dynamic response. The results reveal that core topology significantly influences both the static mechanical properties and fatigue performance of the sandwich structures under flexural loading. The S-DARC configuration exhibited the highest flexural stiffness and longest fatigue life, whereas the S-SARC and S-DAUX configurations achieved the highest flexural strengths. The S-SAUX configuration demonstrated a high energy dissipation capacity but exhibited greater sensitivity to the applied fatigue loading level. Overall, these findings highlight the critical role of core topology in tailoring the static and fatigue flexural performance of additively manufactured biocomposite sandwich structures to meet specific engineering requirements.

title: Digital Transformation 2.0: Integrating AI and Empowering People for Sustainable Growth in the Future of Work
container-title: Technology and Leadership Connections
cd295fcbb5cd4820a5d40948a004a94d7d35cbec.abstract: The digital era has reached a new inflection point, accelerated by artificial intelligence (AI) and organizations’ need to adapt to dynamic, technology-driven conditions. This chapter examines the legacy of Digital Transformation 1.0—highlighting failures and their causes—and defines the imperatives of AI-infused Digital Transformation 2.0. Drawing from relevant case studies, research, and executive interviews, it emphasizes the critical shift from episodic digitization to sustained AI-embedded digitalization. Leaders must enable systems-level transformation across people, process, and technology while aligning cultural, ethical, and operational domains. Digital Transformation 2.0 demands coordinated iterative design over monolithic strategy, requiring organizations to reimagine work as a fluid mix of tasks rather than fixed roles. Human–AI collaboration is a new reality that depends on psychological safety, AI literacy, and digital dexterity across the blended human-AI workforce. Successful transformation hinges on new leadership behaviors that elevate trust, agency, and adaptability while modeling and encouraging the use of new tools. The piece explores decentralized workforce models, the urgency of building AI-ready cultures, and a new social contract. It examines how agile frameworks, value mapping, and upskilling efforts create coherence amid complexity, making change tangible and participatory. The Future of Work is framed not as a fixed destination, but as a dynamic system requiring deliberate, ongoing leadership to combine machine capabilities with uniquely human capabilities. Ultimately, this work calls for defining or reframing organizational purpose and progress: AI can multiply what we value, but it is up to us to define what we value—and how we lead with it.

title: Droplet digital PCR for diagnosing invasive aspergillosis in hematological malignancies: a prospective cohort study
container-title: Journal of Clinical Microbiology
39e57a45f951194438e09f588d14602bf83174d0.abstract: ABSTRACT Our objective was to evaluate the diagnostic accuracy of Aspergillus droplet digital PCR (ddPCR) in exhaled breath condensate (EBC) and bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF) for diagnosing invasive aspergillosis (IA), and to compare its performance with quantitative real-time PCR (qPCR) in patients with hematologic malignancies. We conducted a prospective single-center study, including adults admitted to leukemia and allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplant units who underwent bronchoscopy for pulmonary infiltrates between October 2021 and December 2024. EBC and BALF were collected concurrently. ddPCR was performed on EBC and BALF (supernatant and cell pellet); qPCR was performed on BALF samples. IA was classified according to EORTC/MSGERC criteria without incorporating PCR into the reference standard. Diagnostic performance characteristics, including area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC-ROC), were calculated. Among 203 participants, 26 (12.8%) were diagnosed with probable or proven IA. EBC ddPCR showed poor performance (AUC-ROC 0.55, 95% CI 0.43–0.67). BALF supernatant ddPCR demonstrated the best performance (AUC-ROC 0.88, 95% CI 0.80–0.96), with sensitivity of 0.65 (95% CI 0.43–0.84) and specificity of 0.96 (95% CI 0.92–0.99). BALF supernatant outperformed BALF cell pellet testing for both ddPCR and qPCR. Compared with qPCR, ddPCR showed higher sensitivity and similarly high specificity. Among participants without prior mold-active antifungal therapy, BALF supernatant ddPCR showed improved performance (AUC-ROC 0.95, 95% CI 0.89–1.00). In this large prospective study, EBC ddPCR demonstrated limited utility for the diagnosis of IA. BALF supernatant was the optimal specimen type, and ddPCR outperformed qPCR. Diagnostic performance improved substantially without prior mold-active antifungal exposure. IMPORTANCE Invasive aspergillosis is difficult to diagnose in patients with hematologic malignancies, and non-invasive diagnostic approaches are needed. In this prospective study of 203 patients, Aspergillus droplet digital PCR performed poorly in exhaled breath condensate (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve 0.55; 95% CI 0.43–0.67) but showed good diagnostic performance in bronchoalveolar lavage supernatant fluid (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve 0.88; 95% CI 0.80–0.96). Droplet digital PCR demonstrated higher sensitivity than quantitative PCR with similarly high specificity, and bronchoalveolar lavage supernatant fluid consistently outperformed cell pellet testing. Among patients without prior mold-active antifungal therapy, the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve was 0.95 (95% CI 0.89–1.00). These findings support bronchoalveolar lavage supernatant fluid as the preferred specimen for Aspergillus droplet digital PCR and warrant further evaluation of this approach for diagnosing invasive aspergillosis.

title: A multi-head attention-based deep learning method for condition monitoring in rotating machinery diagnostics using RVMD-FNDNLP feature preprocessing
container-title: Measurement Science and Technology
3e50511054072f86dbc6d06b61a44cf07f0cac2c.abstract: Abstract Rotating machinery condition monitoring is essential for reliable fault detection and maintenance decision-making in industrial systems. However, nonstationary bearing vibration measurements often produce statistical feature representations with nonlinear coupling, redundancy, and class overlap, thereby limiting diagnostic reliability. In addition, conventional feature extraction and dimensionality reduction methods often suffer from feature redundancy and limited class separability. To address these issues, this paper proposes a bearing condition-monitoring method based on regularized variational mode decomposition (RVMD) and farthest-nearest distance-based neighborhood and locality projections (FNDNLP). By incorporating a regularization strategy into variational mode decomposition, RVMD improves decomposition efficiency and enhances fault-relevant modal information. Multiple statistical features are then extracted from the selected informative modes to construct a high-dimensional monitoring feature set. Subsequently, FNDNLP learns a supervised low-dimensional projection from the training data to reduce redundant and coupled information while improving intraclass compactness and interclass separability. Finally, a temporal convolutional network with multi-head attention (TCN-MHA) models dependencies in the projected representation. The framework is evaluated on the Case Western Reserve University (CWRU) and HUST bearing platforms using complete-pipeline comparisons, controlled classifier evaluations, reduced-dimension sensitivity analysis, and component-wise ablation. It achieves mean test accuracies of 98.89± 0.03% and 98.10± 0.42% on CWRU and HUST, respectively. The results support the effectiveness of the integrated framework under the evaluated datasets and conditions.

title: “Ascending dragon or blasting the dragon vein?”: Contesting corporate environmental legitimacy in digital public
4a59b998886ce507cf6f87ab5e0b2e1523cad9c5.abstract: Corporations’ sustainability communication is increasingly challenged by digital publics. This study examines how Chinese netizens discursively delegitimise a controversial fireworks display staged in the Himalayas by international mountaineering brand Arc’teryx. Comments from seven popular Weibo posts (140,584 tokens) were examined through corpus-assisted discourse analysis, using keyword and concordance analysis. Findings show that netizens mobilised ecological reasoning to challenge corporate environmental reassurances, invoked environmental regulations to question perceived inequalities in enforcement, and drew on spiritual-cultural values and nationalism to condemn the display. Emotional criticism and calls for boycotts further challenged the brand, the artist, and local government authorities. These discursive resources provided distinct but overlapping grounds for evaluating environmental responsibility and demonstrate the interdependence of the human-nature relationship that Weibo netizens hold. The study demonstrates that corporate environmental legitimacy is contested not only through assessment of ecological impacts but also through broader institutional, moral, and cultural expectations.

title: Analysis of Thermomechanical Fatigue Damage Progression in Short Fiber-Reinforced Composites Using X-Ray Computed Tomography
container-title: Materials Science Forum
c0e8bbc58956535dec545632e876b76cd8bc7829.abstract: Due to the increasing applicability of short fiber-reinforced thermoplastic composites in numerous industrial applications, it is essential to develop efficient models for assessing and predicting their fatigue life for optimal design and operation of components made of these materials. Due to material heterogeneity and complex fatigue response that covers not only mechanical fatigue but also the self-heating effect, i.e. dissipative heating coupled with mechanical response, the fundamental understanding of fracture and failure mechanisms driven structural degradation of these materials is of key importance. In this study, the progression of fatigue damage under fatigue loading has been evaluated with the presence of the self-heating effect and specific fracture mechanisms have been identified using X-ray computed tomography. The character and rate of progression of fatigue damage are reported together with specific fracture mechanisms for thermomechanical fatigue loading.

eb7b6e6dcc8a65dc9580ff8e1f394fd4bfb6fc0f.abstract: Purpose This study investigates how digital transformation unfolds within logistics service ecosystems and how inter-actor operational connections and coordinating roles change over time from an orchestration perspective. Design/methodology/approach The authors conducted a case study of three international inland ports in China. Data were triangulated through interviews, observations and documents to capture ecosystem-level orchestration practices and transformation evolution. Findings The authors developed a process model that identifies three evolutionary stages of the digital transformation of service ecosystems: developing digital connectivity, tapping digital service potential and co-creating digital value. The model demonstrates how actors employ resource and network orchestration at each stage. The analysis reveals how these two forms of orchestration interact and how orchestration dynamics change over time. Originality/value This study shifts the focus of digital transformation research from a few focal firms to service ecosystems overall. It theorizes a three-stage transformation process, reveals the evolving interplay between resource and network orchestration, shows that different actors can assume orchestration leadership, and provides actionable recommendations for managers seeking to digitally transform logistics and supply chain service ecosystems.

title: APPLICATION OF TOPOLOGICALLY COMPLEX SURFACES IN DIGITAL TWINS OF CYBER-PHYSICAL MACHINE TOOLS
container-title: MM Science Journal
b33be91c9e967b266fd9dabd18248320c594b25b.abstract: This paper presents an innovative mathematical modelling paradigm for intelligent CNC machine tools based on the Steiner Roman surface as a geometric core of digital twins. The use of this topological abstraction is investigated for analytical determination of the cutter-workpiece engagement (CWE) zone during multi-axis milling of free-form surfaces. An approach for detecting kinematic singularities and optimising cutting forces through invariants of the algebraic model is proposed. It is demonstrated that the transition from traditional solid B‑Rep models to compact analytical "physical models" dramatically reduces computational load, enabling compensation of elastic tool deformations directly on edge computing devices in real time. Lyapunov-based stability analysis guarantees convergence of the state estimates and adaptation of neural network weights for approximating uncertain dynamic disturbances. The proposed architecture is shown to comply with the international standards ISO 23218 (CNC systems and their integration) and ISO 23704 (cyber-physically controlled smart machine tool systems, CPSMT). A comparative analysis with a recent MTConnect-based digital twin implementation highlights the advantages of the continuous analytical CWE model for real-time force control.

title: Microstructural Evolution and Fatigue Performance of Welded Joints in Thick-Wall Pressure Vessels
container-title: International Journal of Computational Materials Science and Engineering
d686ed950226dc0419eaffe307e32e490691d07f.abstract: Thick-wall welded pressure vessels operate under combinations of internal pressure, thermal cycling, structural restraint, corrosive or hydrogen-containing environments, and long service durations. In such components, fatigue performance is not governed by a single nominal material property but by a manufacturing-dependent internal state comprising spatially variable microstructure, hardness, local constitutive response, and residual stress. This review critically synthesizes the mechanisms by which welding processes and post-weld heat treatment determine fatigue performance in thick-wall pressure-vessel joints, with emphasis on SA508-type reactor pressure-vessel steels and 2.25Cr-1Mo- 0.25V/Cr-Mo-V steels used in petrochemical and hydrogenation reactors. Conventional multi-pass arc welding, narrow-gap welding, electron-beam welding, and laser-based high-energy-density processes are interpreted as distinct thermal-history generators. Their associated peak temperatures, cooling rates, reheating cycles, and through-thickness thermal gradients control fusion-zone solidification, HAZ subdivision, prior-austenite grain evolution, martensite-austenite constituent formation, carbide/carbonitride precipitation, segregation, and local mechanical mismatch. The review further evaluates how welding residual stresses originate from thermal contraction, plasticity, phase-transformation strain, restraint, and wall-thickness effects, and how post-weld heat treatment redistributes stress while simultaneously modifying phase stability and precipitate morphology. Fatigue crack initiation and propagation are discussed as coupled microstructure-residual-stress phenomena involving cyclic strain localization, small-crack interaction with microstructural barriers, crack-tip constraint, and environmental acceleration. Advanced characterization methods, including EBSD, SEM/TEM/APT, neutron diffraction, nanoindentation, and small punch testing, are assessed as enabling tools for spatially resolved microstructure-property mapping. Finally, thermometallurgical- mechanical simulation, crystal plasticity, representative-volume-element modelling, fracture mechanics, physics-informed machine learning, and digital-twin frameworks are synthesized into a process-microstructure-stress-fatigue roadmap for predictive integrity management. The central conclusion is that fatigue assessment of thick-wall welded pressure vessels must transition from averaged weld-region properties toward history-dependent, spatially resolved, and experimentally validated frameworks capable of linking fabrication parameters directly to fatigue life.

title: A Systematic Literature Review of Sustainable Governance and Hospital Digital Transformation Capability for Hospital Organizational Capability
container-title: Dinasti International Journal of Economics, Finance & Accounting
3908fd0108b475a71676690f70fe6d80019253b1.abstract: Hospitals are facing increasing pressure to achieve sustainability amid technological developments, changing patient expectations, regulatory dynamics, and intensifying competition. Although sustainable governance, digital transformation, and organizational capability have received growing research attention, their integrated contributions to hospital sustainability performance and competitive advantage have not yet been adequately synthesized. This study aims to examine and integrate findings from previous studies on sustainable governance, hospital digital transformation capability, and hospital organizational capability. The study employs a systematic literature review of publications published between 2020 and 2026 and identified through various academic databases. The selected articles are analyzed using thematic content analysis to identify key concepts, relationships among constructs, and research gaps. The synthesis indicates that sustainable governance supports accountability, transparency, and stakeholder engagement; hospital digital transformation capability facilitates technology integration, data-driven decision-making, and service innovation; while hospital organizational capability enables resource integration and the development of adaptive capabilities. The novelty of this study lies in the development of an integrated conceptual framework that explains the complementary roles of these three strategic dimensions in strengthening hospital sustainability and competitive positioning.

title: Accelerating Digital Transformation in Islamic Education: Insights, Gaps, and Conceptual Frameworks
container-title: Cendekia: Jurnal Kependidikan dan Kemasyarakatan
10796f5a35c82a657983a9c75ae84c24668e9bc5.abstract: This article reports a systematic literature review of recent work on the digital transformation of Islamic education. Following PRISMA, we searched Scopus and Web of Science for studies published in 2023 and 2024. After screening, and after appraising quality with the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool (MMAT), we retained 18 studies for analysis. The challenges reported in these studies are not separate problems; they are tied to one another. Unequal digital access sits at the base, shaping both the readiness of infrastructure and the capacity of teachers, and weak pedagogical training in turn limits what teachers can do with the technology they have. Whether digital learning is accepted, and whether it lasts, also depends on how well it fits cultural and religious expectations. We read these findings through digital divide theory, the TPACK framework, and diffusion of innovations theory, and from them we build a three-dimensional perspective that links structural, pedagogical, and cultural factors. The scope of the review is modest, but its results speak to policymakers, teachers, and researchers, especially in settings where digital education is still taking shape.

title: Pengaruh Pengungkapan Environment, Social, dan Governance (ESG) terhadap Bank Performance dengan Transformasi Digital sebagai Variabel Moderasi
container-title: AKUNTANSI 45
a42904cb5f21221447912639db15e36d80ee9b3f.abstract: This study examines the effect of Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) disclosure on bank performance, proxied by the natural logarithm of Z-Score, and tests digital transformation as a moderating variable. The study uses a quantitative approach with a sample of 17 banks listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange during 2022–2024, resulting in 51 firm-year observations. ESG disclosure is measured through content analysis based on the GRI Standards 2021, while digital transformation is measured using keyword-based text mining of annual reports. The data are analyzed using panel data regression and moderated regression analysis with a Common Effect Model and White Diagonal robust standard errors to address heteroskedasticity. The results show that Environmental, Social, and Governance disclosure do not have statistically significant direct effects on bank performance. Digital transformation does not significantly moderate the relationships between Environmental disclosure or Social disclosure and bank performance. However, the interaction between Governance disclosure and digital transformation is statistically significant and negative, indicating that digital transformation weakens the relationship between Governance disclosure and bank stability in the observed sample. Non-Performing Loans also have a significant negative association with bank stability. These findings suggest that ESG disclosure and digitalization do not automatically translate into improved short-term bank stability; implementation quality and digital governance warrant attention.

title: MISOGINIA, EXPOSIÇÃO ÍNTIMA E DISCURSOS DE ÓDIO: VIOLÊNCIA DIGITAL CONTRA MULHERES DA GUINÉ-BISSAU NO TIKTOK (2025-2026)
container-title: Revista Tópicos
a6d595176b6c8339d86bd939599a3561dd9fe951.abstract: A expansão das plataformas digitais modificou as formas de comunicação, participação social e exposição pública, criando também novos espaços para manifestações de violência baseadas em gênero. O TikTok destaca-se como uma plataforma de ampla circulação de vídeos e discursos, podendo funcionar tanto como espaço de expressão e mobilização quanto como ambiente de reprodução de práticas de violência contra mulheres. Este artigo apresenta uma análise das formas de violência digital praticadas contra mulheres da Guiné-Bissau na rede social TikTok, entre os anos de 2025 e 2026, com ênfase na misoginia, exposição não consensual de conteúdos íntimos e discurso de ódio. A pesquisa adota abordagem qualitativa, de caráter exploratório e descritivo, articulando pesquisa bibliográfica, documental e análise de conteúdo de publicações públicas da plataforma. Parte-se da compreensão de que a violência digital não constitui fenômeno isolado do contexto social, mas pode reproduzir e ampliar desigualdades e formas de controle historicamente dirigidas às mulheres e meninas da Guiné-Bissau. O estudo busca contribuir para melhor compreensão das especificidades da violência de gênero no ambiente digital guineense e para o debate sobre cidadania, segurança digital e participação das mulheres nas redes sociais.

481d2a818509ebe2d2c9e4bb8807dd847f2f5849.abstract: Rapid digital transformation presents significant challenges to family interactions, often reducing face-to-face communication quality and causing parent-child misunderstandings. This community service (PKM) activity aimed to strengthen parents' understanding and skills in building effective parent-child communication in the digital era at KB Misanudin, Beji, Depok. The activity employed an interactive participatory approach combining lectures, group discussions, case studies, role play, and the formulation of a Family Digital Agreement. Quantitative evaluation using Pre-Test and Post-Test instruments among participants demonstrated a significant increase in mean score from 90.36% (4.52/5.00) in the Pre-Test to 94.71% (4.74/5.00) in the Post-Test, representing an efficiency gain of +4.34%. The highest improvement occurred in the Material & Communication Concept dimension (+5.47%), particularly in understanding gadget distraction impacts (+8.34%) and the biological dangers of yelling on brain development (+6.53%). The activity proved highly effective in transforming parents' conceptual knowledge into concrete, empathetic, and warm parenting practices.

title: The Influence of Bounded Rationality and TikTok Social Media on Digital Investment Product Purchase Decisions in Generation Z
container-title: Escalate : Economics and Business Journal
14d8464f6fb32413f73f06c3fcaea0e66400f17c.abstract: The development of digital investment services enables Generation Z to access information and purchase investment products more easily. However, such decisions may be associated with limitations in information processing and exposure to social media. This study examines the partial and simultaneous effects of bounded rationality and TikTok social media on Generation Z's purchase decisions regarding digital investment products. A quantitative survey approach was employed. Data were collected through questionnaires from 100 respondents selected using purposive sampling and analyzed through multiple linear regression using SPSS version 27. The results indicate that bounded rationality has a positive and significant effect on purchase decisions (B = 0.210; t = 2.012; p = 0.047). TikTok social media also has a positive and significant effect (B = 0.390; t = 3.972; p < 0.001). Simultaneously, both variables significantly affect purchase decisions (F = 19.226; p < 0.001). The adjusted R-squared value of 0.269 indicates that the model explains 26.9% of the variation in purchase decisions. These findings highlight the importance of financial literacy and critical evaluation of digital investment information.

title: Algorithmic Management as a Double-Edged Form of Digital Work Design: Job Demands, Autonomy and Employee Outcomes across 35 European Countries
072bed396833f6aabd92d49bce3ff3b3d77d9c18.abstract: Abstract Computer-based managerial systems are part of the digital infrastructure of work, with potential implications for employee demands and discretion. Drawing on Job Demands-Resources theory, this study examines task allocation, work scheduling and performance monitoring as distinct functions and their parallel indirect associations with engagement and intention to quit through work intensity and autonomy. Weighted least squares mean- and variance-adjusted structural equation models were estimated for 26,504 employees in 35 European countries using the 2024 European Working Conditions Survey. The measures capture reported computer involvement rather than verified artificial intelligence capabilities. Engagement and autonomy were modelled as latent factors, and quit intention as an ordinal outcome. All three practices were positively associated with work intensity. Task allocation was positively associated with autonomy, whereas monitoring was negatively associated with autonomy; scheduling’s negative autonomy association was less robust to contextual fixed effects. Task allocation showed opposing indirect engagement associations through intensity and autonomy, whereas monitoring showed negative associations through both pathways. Intensity-related indirect associations with quit intention were consistently positive, while autonomy-related indirect associations were not statistically significant in the primary or fixed-effects models. Sensitivity analyses supported the main directional patterns, while exploratory country diagnostics indicated incomplete measurement invariance and heterogeneous slopes. The findings inform the evaluation of digital management by distinguishing functions associated with greater demands and greater autonomy from those associated with greater demands and reduced autonomy. The cross-sectional design does not establish causal mediation or uniform cross-country relationships.

title: The Mediating Role of Digital Literacy Between Financial Literacy and Investment Scam Awareness
container-title: International Journal of Accounting and Business Finance
fa6cf4dc793d36cc4cbbe5ebd5ac92b82bcb1e57.abstract: This study analyses whether digital literacy mediates the relationship between financial literacy and investment scam awareness. Despite the rapid expansion of digital financial services, there remains limited knowledge of whether financial and digital literacy interact to shape resistance to online investment scams. A cross-sectional survey was conducted among undergraduates who were selected through stratified random sampling in Sri Lanka. Financial literacy is measured through budgeting skills, financial attitude, financial product literacy and risk awareness. Partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM) was applied to estimate the direct effects and mediating effects. Budgeting skills, product literacy and risk awareness enhance digital literacy, while financial attitude shows no meaningful effect. Digital literacy exhibits the strongest direct influence on investment scam awareness. Mediation analysis confirms that digital literacy transmits the effects of budgeting skills, product literacy and risk awareness to scam awareness, whereas financial attitude remains non-significant. The study conceptualizes digital literacy as a coping appraisal mechanism that enables individuals to operationalize financial knowledge in digital financial environments. Guided by Protection Motivation Theory, the study interprets financial literacy as supporting threat appraisal and digital literacy as supporting coping appraisal. The single institution, cross-sectional and self-reported design may restrict generalizability and causal inference. Future studies should use multi-site samples, longitudinal designs, fraud simulation experiments.

title: Teachers’ Assessment of the Effectiveness of AI and Digital Tools Among Middle School Students in an International School: A Tool for Deeper Learning
container-title: QualiSearch Journal of Educational Research and Practice
3d23d8d784c06aa981f8246e271db5c47577db1b.abstract: This study examined teachers’ assessments of middle school students’ dependency on artificial intelligence (AI) and digital tools and the effectiveness of these technologies in supporting deeper learning at an international school in Phnom Penh, Cambodia. The quantitative correlational study included 82 Grades 6–8 teachers through total enumeration. Data from a researcher-developed questionnaire were analyzed using frequencies, percentages, weighted means, standard deviations, independent-samples t tests, one-way analyses of variance, and Spearman’s rank correlation. Teachers rated student dependency as high across critical thinking, independent study habits, problem-solving, and reliance on technology for outputs. They rated the tools effective for content delivery, student engagement, and academic performance, but less effective for skill development and for deeper learning overall. Selected dependency ratings differed by sex, educational attainment, and frequency of tool use. Effectiveness ratings differed by frequency of use. Perceived dependency and effectiveness were moderately and positively associated (ρ = .537, p < .001). These findings informed the Deeper Learning Pathway, a proposed school-based program that pairs guided use of AI and digital tools with opportunities for independent reasoning and problem-solving.

title: Application of inertial measurement units and machine learning for fatigue assessment in badminton athletes
container-title: Frontiers in Physiology
28910308e3b04040c11085a4c70390b4cfcc2df5.abstract: Objective To evaluate offline binary classification of recorded fatigue conditions using inertial measurement unit (IMU) acceleration features and five machine-learning algorithms. Methods The author-confirmed performance dataset contained 32 observations per condition. The revised primary IMU dataset comprised 70 recordings from 25 roster-linked athletes, with 22 non-fatigue and 48 fatigue labels after correction of four misclassified recordings. Seven-sensor and right-forearm configurations provided 231 and 33 candidate features. A newly reconstructed analysis retained five documented outer athlete-grouped folds and used three grouped inner folds for training-only preprocessing, sparse logistic feature selection and hyperparameter tuning. Results CMJ was 40.01 ± 8.51 and 30.27 ± 7.29 in the non-fatigue and fatigue conditions, respectively. Across classifiers, fold-mean AUC ranged from 0.655 to 0.846 for seven sensors and from 0.715 to 0.846 for the right forearm. Macro F1 ranged from 0.600 to 0.775 and from 0.655 to 0.775, respectively. Specificity ranged from 0.483 to 0.700 and from 0.550 to 0.650. Code, inclusion decisions, actual inner and outer assignments and held-out predictions are supplied for this new run. Conclusion The results support further investigation of IMU-based condition classification, but do not establish algorithm superiority, sensor equivalence, physiological validity of every recording label, or real-time monitoring performance.

title: An IoT-enabled environmental informatics framework for real-time crop disease detection using attention-driven deep learning
container-title: Frontiers in Environmental Science
90e6e8bd29434b2912cb190bf8bc0a9a88485b6a.abstract: Introduction Crop diseases are a major challenge in agriculture because their early and accurate identification is essential for reducing crop losses and improving productivity. The integration of the Internet of Things (IoT) with deep learning provides an effective approach for automated crop disease monitoring by enabling the collection and analysis of environmental parameters such as soil moisture, temperature, and humidity. However, accurate fine-grained disease identification remains challenging because of variations in disease symptoms, environmental conditions, and visual characteristics. Methods This study proposes an IoT-enabled deep learning framework for automated crop disease detection and classification. The collected crop images are pre-processed using scaling, normalization, and data augmentation techniques to improve image quality and model generalization. For efficient disease detection, a lightweight attention-driven convolutional neural network-based object detection approach, termed YOLO10-YSTs (You Only Look Once 10-Yield Surveillance Technology), is employed. The framework integrates the real-time detection capability of YOLO10 with an attention mechanism to emphasize disease-relevant regions and a stigmergy-based encoding strategy to enhance feature representation and extraction. In addition, a novel DBGU-LSTM (Dual-Bi-Gated Recurrent Unit with Long Short-Term Memory) architecture is developed for fine-grained crop disease classification. Results The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed framework provides effective disease detection, discriminative feature representation, and fine-grained classification. The DBGU-LSTM architecture achieves improved classification performance and training stability compared with the conventional deep learning models considered in the study. Overall, the proposed approach achieves a classification accuracy of 97.99%, demonstrating its effectiveness for automated crop disease recognition. Discussion and conclusion The results indicate that combining IoT-based environmental monitoring with attention-driven deep learning and recurrent feature-learning mechanisms can provide an effective solution for intelligent crop disease detection. The proposed framework enables accurate identification of disease patterns while supporting efficient and automated agricultural monitoring. Therefore, the approach has potential to assist farmers in early disease diagnosis, reduce crop losses, and improve agricultural productivity.

title: Digital preservation of multispecies heart morphology using smartphone LiDAR-assisted photogrammetry
container-title: Frontiers in Veterinary Science
bc3130e9a431e2d5e41f05f240f78011ff31b53f.abstract: Introduction Fresh biological specimens represent the most realistic material for anatomical study. However, fresh organs are difficult to digitize due to their deformability, moist reflective surfaces, and rapid post-mortem deterioration. These limitations are particularly relevant for the heart, an anatomically complex organ whose three-dimensional (3D) architecture and species-specific variations are challenging to document and preserve. This study developed and evaluated a complete workflow for the digital preservation of fresh comparative cardiac anatomy by combining smartphone LiDAR-assisted photogrammetry with a cloud-based platform for interactive 3D and augmented reality (AR) visualization. Methods One fresh heart from each of five animal species (dog, sheep, pig, cow, and horse) was digitized using a standardized acquisition protocol to explore the applicability of the workflow across specimens with different sizes and morphological characteristics. Quantitative assessment of three selected external linear dimensions was performed through direct comparison between physical specimens and their digital reconstructions, while anatomical evaluation was conducted by experienced veterinary anatomists. The reconstructed models were subsequently integrated into a cloud-based platform for Web3D and AR visualization Results Across 15 paired morphometric comparisons, the mean absolute percentage error was 4.08% (range: 0.83–8.28%), indicating close agreement for the external linear dimensions evaluated. Independent expert evaluation using a structured assessment rubric confirmed preservation of species-specific morphological characteristics, major cardiac landmarks, and external anatomical relationships across all models. In addition to complete heart reconstructions, the workflow was successfully applied to a dissected heart specimen, providing a proof of concept for the digital preservation and visualization of selected intracardiac structures. Following integration into the cloud platform, the models were made accessible through interactive Web3D and AR environments with anatomical labelling and cross-device compatibility. Discussion Beyond its potential educational applications in veterinary anatomy, the proposed workflow integrates acquisition, assessment, and cloud-based dissemination within a single digital pipeline, providing a practical framework for digital anatomical collections representing different mammalian cardiac morphologies, future anatomical repositories, and the long-term preservation and dissemination of fresh comparative cardiac anatomy.

title: Designing digital governance for regenerative tourism: an exploratory case study of Travelware
container-title: Frontiers in Sustainability
eff3c51d10fbd15618157462a5bcd9d33f4e7146.abstract: Introduction Regenerative tourism raises questions about how destinations can translate commitments to community and ecological wellbeing into governance practices. Drawing on service-dominant logic and the service ecosystem perspective, this exploratory single-case study examines how Travelware, an Italian Benefit Corporation developing a tourism platform based on decentralized autonomous organizations (DAOs), approaches regenerative value co-creation through digital governance. Methods Eight semi-structured interviews were conducted with three company representatives; they were analyzed using the Gioia methodology. Results The analysis identifies three aggregate dimensions: regenerative orientation to value creation, reconfiguring value co-creation in the service ecosystem, and technology as an active relational mediator. Managers describe community proposal and voting procedures intended to support collective project selection, with local organizations contributing resources to implementation. They attribute contribution recognition and voting controls to block chain and smart contracts, describe algorithms matching traveler interests with destination characteristics, and outline a planned system for monitoring territorial impacts. Discussion The discussion interprets these findings as an articulation of regenerative aims, participatory institutional arrangements, and digital mediation within a service ecosystem. The case suggests that translating regenerative aims into governance involves both participation procedures and coordination with organizations able to implement community proposals. The study contributes a context-specific account of governance design rather than evidence of achieved regenerative outcomes. It concludes that managers should connect participation design with implementation responsibilities and impact assessment, while comparative and longitudinal research should examine how these arrangements operate across tourism settings.

title: <span data-teams="true">Biphasic Digital Twin for Dynamic Coronary Occlusion Risk of TAVR: Beyond Static Anatomical Assessment
409e5947a73bdcaa1622544ecdae9995dc594be9.abstract: Coronary occlusion (CO) is a lethal complication of transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) (incidence, 0.35%–4.0%; in-hospital mortality, approximately 50%). Although static computed tomography thresholds (ostial height >12 mm) remain the assessment standard, CO still occurs in 14.3% of patients meeting them. We developed a biphasic digital twin (BDT) integrating systolic and diastolic electrocardiogram-gated computed tomography angiography to assess dynamic CO risk in a 71-year-old woman with severe aortic stenosis. Biphasic aortic root dynamics and bilateral virtual valve-to-coronary distance (VTC) were evaluated at two implantation depths. Ostial height varied by approximately 5%, whereas leaflet volume increased by 22.0% in diastole. Right coronary ostial displacement (4.28 mm) was 1.74-fold that of the left (2.46 mm), and the sinotubular junction rotated 8.7°. A commissural calcified mass remained stable. Implantation 5 mm deeper reduced diastolic left VTC from 8.96 to 6.54 mm (–27%) but increased systolic right VTC from 4.57 to 5.93 mm (+29%). Delayed CO occurred 30 min after extubation despite patent intra-procedural angiography; surgery confirmed calcified anchoring, stent deflection, and coronary compression. Static coronary height did not capture dynamic CO risk in this patient. BDT may support individualised, biphasic, bilateral assessment by integrating dynamic leaflet expansion, asymmetric root motion, and calcified anchoring.

title: Beyond AI Assisted Creativity: Digital Storytelling for Orchestrating Human AI Co-Creation in Higher Education
e99f30d7f1b28e01f3c862cdf7b7188266881f8c.abstract: Generative Artificial Intelligence is increasingly used to support creativity in higher education, yet its educational value may depend on how human and AI contributions are pedagogically coordinated. This study examined whether digital storytelling can orchestrate human–AI co-creation while preserving students’ creative agency. A quasi-experimental pretest–posttest control-group design involved 180 higher education students assigned by intact cohorts to orchestrated human–AI digital storytelling or conventional AI-assisted digital storytelling. After controlling for baseline performance, the experimental group demonstrated significantly higher creative competency, F(1,177) = 10.95, p = .001, partial η² = .058, alongside stronger human–AI co-creation quality, creative agency, critical evaluation, and creative ownership. Regression pathways further linked co-creation quality and creative agency to creative competency. These findings position digital storytelling as a pedagogical orchestration environment that shifts AI-supported creativity from output generation toward intentional, evaluative, and human-directed co-creation.

title: ANALISIS DISPARITAS MANAJEMEN PEMBIAYAAN DAN AKSES PENDIDIKAN DIGITAL PADA PENDIDIKAN DASAR: PERSPEKTIF EKONOMI PENDIDIKAN DI INDONESIA DAN NEGARA BERKEMBANG
container-title: Pendas : Jurnal Ilmiah Pendidikan Dasar
b2d2d6460e647a93f1cc384d854d1e44402e17dc.abstract: The development of digital technology has created opportunities to improve the quality of basic education services. However, it has also introduced challenges in the form of infrastructure disparities, differences in educators' digital competencies, and inequalities in education financing. This study aims to analyze disparities in financing and access to digital education at the basic education level from the perspective of the economics of education through a comparative study of Indonesia and developing countries. The study employs a mixed-methods approach by integrating descriptive quantitative analysis and qualitative analysis of educational policy documents. The countries examined include Indonesia, Nepal, Pakistan, Laos, Vietnam, Yemen, Botswana, Liberia, Burkina Faso, Namibia, South Sudan, and Saint Vincent and the Grenadines. The analytical indicators include education budget allocation, the availability of information and communication technology infrastructure, teachers' digital competencies, the ratio of ICT devices to students, and equitable access to digital learning. This study is expected to provide a comparative overview of factors associated with disparities in digital education services and offer policy recommendations for more equitable education financing and educational resource management.

title: Consumer Protection in Digital Payment Systems: Legal Challenges and Comparative Perspectives in Mongolia, China and South Korea
container-title: Advances in Social Sciences Research Journal
21b348e0f3e60b4bb489ecf9346438dbda1cd920.abstract: The rapid development of digital payment systems has transformed financial transactions, improved payment convenience, and expanded access to financial services. However, the increasing use of electronic wallets, mobile payment applications, electronic money, and online payment platforms has also created new consumer protection challenges, including unauthorized transactions, digital fraud, misuse of personal data, technical failures, and difficulties in obtaining compensation. This study aims to conduct a comparative legal analysis of consumer protection in digital payment systems in Mongolia, China, and South Korea. It examines similarities and differences in their legal frameworks, identifies common regulatory challenges, and evaluates potential legal mechanisms for strengthening consumer protection in Mongolia. The study employs doctrinal and comparative legal research methods, drawing on relevant legislation, regulatory instruments, scholarly literature, and institutional approaches to payment-service supervision and dispute resolution. The analysis focuses on the principal legal frameworks governing digital payment services in the three countries. In Mongolia, particular attention is given to the Law on National Payment System, which establishes the legal foundations for payment-service regulation, system security, and the protection of payment users. In China, the study examines the Regulation on the Supervision and Administration of Non-Bank Payment Institutions, which entered into force on 1 May 2024 and strengthened the regulatory framework for non-bank payment service providers. In South Korea, the Electronic Financial Transactions Act is examined with particular reference to electronic transaction security, financial service provider liability, and consumer protection in electronic financial transactions. The comparative analysis is structured around five key dimensions: regulatory authorization and supervision, liability for unauthorized transactions, protection of customer funds, personal data protection and cybersecurity, and consumer complaints and remedies. Through these dimensions, the study evaluates the extent to which existing legal frameworks address emerging risks in digital payment services and provide effective safeguards for consumers. The study emphasizes that effective consumer protection requires more than the formal recognition of consumer rights. It also depends on clearly defined liability mechanisms, transparent obligations for digital payment service providers, accessible dispute resolution procedures, effective compensation mechanisms, and consistent regulatory enforcement. The findings are intended to provide a comparative legal basis for identifying regulatory gaps and developing recommendations to strengthen the legal protection of consumers in Mongolia's rapidly evolving digital payment environment

title: Influence of digital work platforms on working conditions in the tourism sector: a system dynamics model
container-title: Central European Journal of Operations Research
75134822585ee5ae1f6b7138bb73a3106676e8ed.abstract: Abstract This paper presents the System Dynamics (SD) model developed within a research project focused on the phenomenon of platformisation of services in tourism and its impacts on the labour market, i.e. wages, working conditions and unionisation of tourism workers. Through consultations with domain experts, we have developed a causal loop diagram representing the relationships between stakeholders and other influential factors and used it as the starting point for the development of a System Dynamics (SD) model. The SD model aims to provide insight into the tourism labour market dynamics in Slovenia through the interplay of a set of variables representing the tourists, employers and workers in tourism industry. The model is based on previous research, consultation with labour market experts, public data on collective bargaining coverage, public statistical data on labour market and tourism industry from SiStat, Eurostat and OECD, and reports from Hotels, Restaurants & Cafés in Europe association (HOTREC) and European Working Conditions Surveys (EWCS).

title: Digital Work Stressors and Employee Well-Being: A Systematic Review of Evidence Types, Boundary Conditions, and Organisational Responses
container-title: F1000Research
c249a7e6ab0b31b9447bd680b5c4ce8fa4f1ab12.abstract: Background Digital technologies have changed how work is paced, monitored and bounded. Studies of technostress and related digital demands differ in what they treat as the exposure and the outcome, and in their evidence on processes, boundary conditions and organisational responses. Methods We searched Scopus, ScienceDirect, Wiley Online Library and Springer Nature on 3 September 2026 for English-language empirical studies published from 2010 to 2026 that linked a work-related digital stressor to employee well-being. Study quality was appraised with the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool. Findings were synthesised by vote counting based on direction of effect, without meta-analysis. The review was not registered. Results Of 2,742 records, 353 full-text reports were assessed and 80 were included (78 quantitative non-randomised studies, one mixed-methods study, one experiment), with about 95,900 participants. Seventy reports pointed to poorer well-being (87.5%; 95% confidence interval 78.5% to 93.1%), eight pointed in conflicting directions and two to better well-being. Among reports of a demand, the share ranged from 72.2% for positive well-being to 95.7% for recovery and sleep, and was 76.3% in larger and 97.4% in smaller studies. Three studies that separated the demand from technology use found the adverse association for the demand only. Process and moderation tests (57 and 45 reports) gave selective support, and lagged tests gave mixed results. No report evaluated an implemented organisational response; 62 offered recommendations only. Certainty of the evidence was rated very low. Conclusions Digital demands experienced at work are associated with poorer employee well-being in most studies, though less uniformly in larger and better-controlled ones; the association appears to belong to the demand, not to technology use as such. Evidence for processes is largely cross-sectional, and evidence for organisational responses is absent.

title: Climate-Related Health Challenges and Digital Health Needs among Women Agricultural Workers in Limpopo, South Africa: A Qualitative Study
container-title: F1000Research
15c54b7a5518b70738745b80b28141cec80402d4.abstract: Background Climate change is intensifying heat exposure in agricultural and agro-processing work across southern Africa. Women face intersecting reproductive, occupational and caregiving burdens that are often overlooked by occupational health systems. Digital health offers potential adaptation strategies, but its suitability for women farm workers remains underexplored. Aim To explore climate-related health challenges and digital health needs among women working at a selected mango atchaar agro-processing farm outside Tzaneen, Limpopo Province, South Africa. Methods A qualitative, exploratory and descriptive design was employed. Purposive sampling recruited 25 women workers and two key informants (the farm manager and safety officer). Data were collected on 18 June 2026 through five focus group discussions and two semi-structured interviews. Tesch’s eight-step open-coding approach was used for analysis, guided by the socio-ecological model (SEM). Lincoln and Guba’s criteria ensured trustworthiness. Results Twenty-seven participants contributed to five themes: climate-related health experiences; occupational conditions and safety risks; healthcare access and support; digital health use, barriers and opportunities; and workplace and community strategies for improving women’s health. Among the women, 19 (76%) were aged 46 years or older. Heat-related experiences included fatigue, headaches, dizziness, swelling, raised blood pressure and lower-abdominal discomfort, potentially overlapping with menopausal symptoms. Prolonged standing, heavy loads and spice-dust exposure compounded these challenges. Women relied largely on family and peer support. Digital health access was constrained by workplace phone restrictions, data costs, management-only Wi-Fi and limited digital literacy. Conclusion Women’s climate-related occupational health risks reflect interacting individual, interpersonal, workplace and policy-level factors. Digital health interventions should be accessible, context-sensitive and integrated with workplace-based primary healthcare. Such interventions must complement, not replace, employers’ occupational health and safety responsibilities and regulatory enforcement. Multilevel strategies are essential to strengthen occupational protection and timely healthcare access.

title: The Right to Disconnect in Modern Employment: Protecting the Boundary Between Work and Personal Life in the Digital Era
container-title: Review of Law and Social Sciences
9c2efa4bdc72342df2333aefd1adea10532cb16d.abstract: Digital transformation has changed the way humans work, especially regarding time and space. Smartphones, emails, instant messaging applications, and collaborative work platforms allow employers to contact employees almost anywhere and at any time. The boundary traditionally established by labor law between "working hours" and "rest periods" is therefore increasingly eroded. This article examines the right to disconnect as a new legal institution designed to protect that boundary. The study uses qualitative methods: textual analysis, comparative jurisprudence, historical analysis, synthesis, logic, and descriptive statistics based on secondary data. The article systematizes international scientific literature, compares representative legal models (France, Spain, Belgium, Portugal, Ireland, Ontario, Chile, Australia, and the European Union), and then juxtaposes them with current Vietnamese law. The results show that the right to disconnect has evolved from a bargainable declaration into an enforceable legal obligation backed by sanctions. Meanwhile, Vietnam's Labour Code of 2019 is still designed according to the logic of physical time and lacks legal instruments to regulate out-of-hours digital communications. Guided by the directives of the Documents of the 14th National Congress of the Party on human development, digital transformation, and the building of harmonious, stable, and progressive labor relations, the article proposes a "conditional hybrid" model for Vietnam: codifying general principles in law, combined with collective bargaining and internal labor regulations for contextual implementation.

title: AI Anxiety, Digital Overload, and Technostress in a Polycrisis Context: A Moderated Mediation Study of Emotional Exhaustion and Psychological Well-Being Across Four Industry Sectors
287811c3d509c854883b0a89f89875e174e3e465.abstract: Abstract Background : The concurrent occurrence of AI-induced disruption, rapid post-pandemic digitalization, and macroeconomic instability has fundamentally reshaped the psychological demands of modern work, creating a polycrisis. Staff members in digital work environments experience rising AI anxiety, digital overload, and technostress, but how such polycrisis-related demands impact PWB through these mechanisms and the extent to which personal resources may act as a shield against such an effect has not been comprehensively understood yet. Based on the assumptions of the Job Demands-Resources model, the present study examines a model of moderated mediation, wherein emotional exhaustion mediates the demand-PWB association, and psychological capital (PsyCap) moderates and strengthens PWB. Methods: Cross-sectional surveys using six psychometric scales were conducted among 340 full-time workers from sectors such as IT, Health care, Education, and Banking/Finance. Hypotheses regarding the structure were validated using CB-SEM with 5,000 bias corrected bootstraps whereas sector-specific MGA and fsQCA identified configurations related to lower PWB. Results: All three job demands were able to predict emotional exhaustion: AI anxiety (β = 0.396, p < 0.001), digital overload (β = 0.333, p < 0.001), and technostress (β = 0.318, p < 0.001), explaining 32.1% of the variance. Emotional exhaustion fully mediated the influence of all three variables on PWB (β = -0.434, p < 0.001) through bootstrapped indirect effects. PsyCap had a significant direct effect on PWB (β = 0.460, p < 0.001) for all four sectors. Through MGA, sector-specific differences emerged with regard to AI anxiety, which was more important in the IT sector, digital overload in Healthcare and Banking/Finance, and technostress in the Education sector. In fsQCA, digital overload was found as a necessary condition for low PWB (consistency = 0.909), where there were three configurations, each required low PsyCap as a boundary condition (solution consistency = 0.841, coverage = 0.573). Conclusions: Demands resulting from polycrisis are linked to low PWB mainly because of emotional exhaustion, and demand salience differs significantly across sectors. Low PsyCap functions as a universal boundary condition for low levels of well-being. Organisations should prioritise PsyCap development as an industry-invariant approach in addition to demand management, which takes into account the characteristics of the job.

title: Preparing pre-service teachers for digital age curriculum delivery through Technological Pedagogical Content Knowledge in rural South African schools
container-title: Australian and International Journal of Rural Education
0adc8a11ccc6e728350736cdecb79a282f44015f.abstract: The integration of digital technologies into education has reshaped expectations for curriculum delivery, particularly in rural school contexts where persistent challenges in access, learner engagement, and instructional quality continue to undermine educational equity. Guided by the Technological Pedagogical Content Knowledge framework, this study explored how pre-service teachers perceive the role of technology integration in advancing curriculum delivery in rural schools. A qualitative approach was adopted, employing semi-structured interviews with 30 pre-service teachers enrolled at a rural university in KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa. Data were analysed using reflexive thematic analysis. The findings revealed that pre-service teachers regarded digital technologies as valuable instruments for enhancing learner engagement, supporting differentiated instruction, facilitating equitable access to curriculum content, and improving classroom interaction. Participants demonstrated an emergent understanding of the interconnected nature of technological, pedagogical, and content knowledge. However, challenges, including inadequate digital infrastructure, limited device access, and insufficient opportunities for teaching practice, constrained Technological Pedagogical Content Knowledge development. The study concludes that strengthening technology-focused teacher preparation is critical for equipping future educators to deliver responsive and inclusive curricula in rural contexts.
