title: Automated breast cancer staging from Chinese-language PET/CT reports using two large language models: a retrospective single-center study
container-title: Frontiers in Digital Health
f446aec467d74057787da4c4c50468ce27ffecb6.abstract: Objective To evaluate the performance of GPT-5.5 Pro and DeepSeek-V4-Pro in automated breast cancer cTNM and AJCC anatomic staging from Chinese-language PET/CT reports. Methods A curated test set of 298 pretreatment 18 F-FDG PET/CT reports from routine clinical practice, obtained between February and December 2025 at our institution, was included. All reports had been verified against the corresponding imaging findings and screened to exclude errors or omissions. Following AJCC 8th-edition cTNM criteria, GPT-5.5 Pro and DeepSeek-V4-Pro assigned cT, cN, cM, and AJCC anatomic stage using a task-specific, rule-guided zero-shot prompt developed using a separate set of 20 reports and locked before final evaluation. Model outputs were compared with an expert report-based reference standard. Performance against this reference standard was assessed using accuracy and macro-averaged precision, recall, and F1 score; agreement was assessed using Cohen's κ. Model errors were categorized as diagnostic reasoning, feature processing, or knowledge application errors. Results For cT staging, GPT-5.5 Pro and DeepSeek-V4-Pro achieved accuracies of 98.3% and 97.0% ( P = 0.39) and macro-F1 scores of 0.968 and 0.952 ( P = 0.51), respectively. For cM staging, the corresponding accuracies were 99.7% and 98.0% ( P = 0.06), and the macro-F1 scores were 0.990 and 0.932 ( P = 0.06). cM1 sensitivity was 96.3% versus 77.8%, with 1 versus 6 missed cM1 cases, respectively. A significant performance difference emerged in cN staging, where GPT-5.5 Pro achieved higher accuracy (97.3% vs. 87.2%, P &lt; 0.001) and macro-F1 score (0.959 vs. 0.729, P &lt; 0.001), resulting in superior overall AJCC anatomic stage classification (accuracy, 98.3% vs. 90.3%; macro-F1, 0.968 vs. 0.861; both P &lt; 0.001). Agreement with the reference standard was almost perfect for GPT-5.5 Pro across all tasks ( κ = 0.96–0.98), whereas κ values for DeepSeek-V4-Pro ranged from 0.80 to 0.95. Across the three component TNM tasks, GPT-5.5 Pro produced 14 classification errors, compared with 53 for DeepSeek-V4-Pro; most errors involved cN staging, and DeepSeek-V4-Pro errors were predominantly classified as knowledge application or diagnostic reasoning errors. Conclusion Both models showed high agreement with the expert report-based reference standard under curated input conditions, with GPT-5.5 Pro showing higher performance for cN and overall AJCC anatomic stage classification.

title: Interpretable Alzheimer's disease diagnosis based on distance-aware rotary attention with multi-scale cross-complementarity
container-title: Frontiers in Aging Neuroscience
db79042e3aed8fced742b0732a1fc5c78ce3e1b2.abstract: Background Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a neurodegenerative disorder characterized by a progressive decline in memory and cognitive function. Existing methods fail to comprehensively capture the multi-level structural variations across different brain regions, making it difficult to provide reliable diagnostic evidence and pathological insights for clinical use. Methods The interpretable algorithm with distance-aware rotary attention and multi-scale cross-complementary (IDRA-MCC) is first proposed to address the limitations in AD diagnosis and improve the interpretability of model discrimination. The study included 604 subjects from the ADNI dataset (207 AD, 195 cognitively normal (CN), 74 progressive mild cognitive impairment (pMCI), and 128 stable mild cognitive impairment (sMCI) and 196 subjects from the OASIS dataset (105 AD and 91 CN). First, standardized preprocessing is applied to reduce inter-subject variability. Then, a dual-scale patch feature modeling was adopted to construct a distance-aware rotary attention (DRA) module that can explicitly encode relative positional dependencies and sequence-level locality, enhancing the perception of key brain regions. Meanwhile, a multi-scale cross-complementary (MCC) module is designed to achieve cross-scale feature interaction and fusion, capturing multi-level pathological patterns. Finally, an adaptive token aggregation (ATA) mechanism is designed to highlight discriminative responses, and anatomical backtracking is achieved through token-weight visualization, thereby improving model interpretability. Results Interpretability analysis shows that the identified high-response regions are highly consistent with brain regions previously associated with AD and MCI progression, including the precuneus in the pMCI vs. sMCI task. Conclusions IDRA-MCC achieves both high performance and interpretability across different tasks on the ADNI and OASIS datasets, showing potential for AD-related progression assessment and future clinical applications.

title: Peer Review Report For: ESD-Integrated Digital Learning for Geographic Literacy in Coastal Secondary Schools: Development and Evaluation [version 2; peer review: 1 approved, 2 approved with reservations]
Information overload, cognitive fatigue, and postgraduates’ intention to use generative artificial intelligence for English academic writing: the role of lower-order cognitive offloading
container-title: Frontiers in Psychology
44519a3982b4f3a7618933a7c685ba32b093e792.abstract: Background Generative artificial intelligence (AI) returns large amounts of information that postgraduates must judge and integrate when they write in English. The stressor-strain-outcome framework suggests that such overload strains cognitive resources and weakens plans for further use. This study tested whether cognitive fatigue links perceived information overload with later behavioral intention to use AI for English academic writing. It also tested whether lower-order cognitive offloading, such as having AI summarize papers, conditions the overload-fatigue association. Methods In total, 475 Chinese master’s and doctoral students who used AI for English academic writing completed three surveys at two-week intervals. Overload and offloading were measured at Time 1, fatigue at Time 2, and intention at Time 3. A moderated mediation model adjusted for baseline fatigue, baseline intention, and AI-use frequency. Results Higher perceived information overload accompanied higher cognitive fatigue 2 weeks later and weaker behavioral intention 4 weeks later, net of baseline levels. Cognitive fatigue was associated with weaker later intention and carried part of the overload-intention association. The overload-fatigue association was weaker at higher levels of lower-order cognitive offloading. Among the most frequent offloaders it was not statistically significant, which does not indicate its absence. The indirect association through fatigue was likewise weaker at higher offloading. These patterns held with additional covariates, a competing interaction with AI-use frequency, and shortened scales. Conclusion In this sample, cognitive fatigue accompanied the prospective association between overload and weaker plans to use AI. This pathway was weaker among postgraduates who delegated foundational tasks more often. Writing programs can teach students which foundational tasks to delegate, and tool developers can limit output overload.

title: Material-aware preclinical digital twins for breast cancer: engineered matrices as causal and auditable interfaces
container-title: Frontiers in Bioengineering and Biotechnology
c3f79b294a45dc95a21eb0d848198c3db48974ba.abstract: Imaging-calibrated breast cancer digital twins have retrospectively forecast treatment response in selected longitudinal imaging cohorts. Patient-derived (patient-sourced) organoids, tunable hydrogels, bioprinted tissues, and tumor-on-chip platforms now reproduce selected features of the tumor microenvironment. We propose integrating these components into a closed-loop architecture that has not been prospectively validated as a complete system in breast cancer. The missing interface is a material layer in which extracellular-matrix chemistry, mechanics, architecture, transport, remodeling, and spatial heterogeneity are measured and perturbed as model variables. The synchronized physical referent is a versioned ensemble of engineered tumor constructs. Patient -conditioned computational states are initialized or constrained by individual-patient observations, while construct measurements govern the experimental state. Uncertainty-aware algorithms select feasible perturbations to distinguish mechanisms or reduce predictive uncertainty; batch metrology and biological phenotypes update or falsify the computational counterpart. Biomaterials thereby serve as experimental actuators, measurement interfaces, and reproducible benchmark conditions. We specify twin identity and synchronization, a five-level validation ladder from material validity to health-system readiness, and a staged translational pathway. Biological incompleteness, coupled material properties, limited tissue, and uncertain transfer from constructs to patients constrain near-term use. The opportunity is a reproducible preclinical learning system with explicit validation gates before patient-level claims. Its predictions remain useful only when a physical experiment can refute them.

title: MINDS: metacognitive awareness, identity investment, negative affect, and digital scaffolding as co-predictors of oral English proficiency in undergraduate learners
container-title: Frontiers in Psychology
891a65bf3b501df30380a9e41d991e054b0f2f67.abstract: Introduction Oral English proficiency (OEP) is central to Chinese undergraduates' academic and professional development, yet its cognitive, motivational, affective, and digital determinants are often examined separately. This study tests the MINDS framework, which integrates metacognitive awareness (MA), identity investment (II), negative affect (NA), and digital scaffolding (DS) as co-predictors of OEP. Methods We analyzed an integrated corpus of N = 412 Chinese undergraduate EFL learners constructed from three publicly available datasets: PISA 2022, SpeechOcean762, and a Mendeley IELTS learning-strategies dataset. Structural equation modeling with 5,000 bootstrap resamples tested four direct effects, the mediating role of MA in the II-OEP relationship, and the moderating role of DS in the NA-OEP relationship. Results The measurement model showed acceptable fit (χ −2 (278) = 687.34, CFI = 0.941, TLI = 0.932, RMSEA = 0.059, SRMR = 0.062). MA, II, and DS positively predicted OEP, whereas NA negatively predicted OEP. MA partially mediated the II-OEP association (indirect β = 0.124, 95% CI [0.073, 0.185]), and DS buffered the negative NA-OEP relationship (β int = 0.17, p = 0.001). Together, the four predictors explained 52.1% of OEP variance, and the effect pattern was reproduced across the three datasets. Discussion These findings identify metacognitive strategy support, identity investment, and digitally scaffolded low-stakes speaking practice as complementary leverage points for improving undergraduate EFL oral proficiency.

title: Multidimensional evaluation of large language models for patient education on asthma during pregnancy: a cross-sectional comparative study
container-title: Frontiers in Digital Health
2609f344b1a8de89721bd10855276fc8b7d43bba.abstract: Introduction Patients increasingly use large language models (LLMs) for health information, but their suitability for high-risk reproductive medicine remains uncertain. We compared six LLMs on patient-facing questions about asthma during pregnancy across clinician-rated overall clinical response quality, information quality, understandability, actionability, readability, and safety. Methods In this cross-sectional comparative study, a two-stage modified Delphi-informed process reduced an initial 40-question pool to 30 candidates and 19 retained questions. Six LLMs answered each question once under a standardized structured prompt, yielding 114 responses and 342 rater-level records. Three clinical evaluators assessed clinician-rated overall clinical response quality, DISCERN, and PEMAT understandability and actionability; four readability indices were calculated. Models were compared using matched question-level nonparametric tests with multiplicity correction and effect sizes. In a revision-stage safety analysis, two clinicians independently rated all 114 responses using a structured safety taxonomy; responses with rating disagreements or prespecified severity triggers underwent blinded adjudication by a third senior clinician. Results Clinician-rated overall clinical response quality differed across models [Friedman χ 2 (5, N = 19) = 72.31, P &lt; 0.001; Kendall's W = 0.76]. GPT-5.5 and Claude Sonnet 5 had the highest observed median scores, without a significant difference after correction. DISCERN, PEMAT, and readability also differed across models, but no model led consistently across outcomes. None achieved a median Flesch-Kincaid grade level at or below grade 8. Inter-rater agreement for the presence of any safety concern was 87.7% (Cohen's kappa=0.70). After adjudication by a third senior clinician, 37/114 responses (32.5%) had at least one safety concern, including 4/114 (3.5%) rated as high-risk unsafe advice. Conclusions Under structured prompting, LLM performance was promising but uneven across selected asthma-in-pregnancy questions. High clinician-rated overall clinical response quality did not ensure superior information quality, usability, readability, or safety. The results do not establish safety for unsupervised patient use. LLM-generated patient information should undergo guideline-based clinical verification, explicit safety review, and readability editing before deployment.

title: Digital simulation and 3D-printed guide-assisted surgical correction of a complex pediatric hip deformity: a case report and literature review
container-title: Frontiers in Pediatrics
52ac8dc951797437f4573b42830749cd202ec4a3.abstract: Background Complex pediatric hip deformities can comprise multiple coexisting structural abnormalities, including coxa vara, femoral head retroversion, chronic femoral neck injury, and avascular necrosis of the femoral head. In older children, the capacity for hip remodeling is diminished, and conventional surgical planning based on two-dimensional imaging and surgeon experience may be insufficient to quantify three-dimensional deformity, osteotomy angles, and fixation trajectories. Digital simulation combined with 3D-printed guides can convert preoperative CT data into visualized three-dimensional models and extend virtual planning to intraoperative localization and osteotomy execution. Case presentation We report a 10-year-old boy who was admitted with a 5-year history of right hip pain and restricted motion. Examination showed approximately 4 cm of right-sided leg-length shortening, proximal migration of the right greater trochanter, and marked restriction of hip motion in multiple planes. Bilateral hip digital radiography (DR), three-dimensional CT reconstruction, and MRI demonstrated right coxa vara with femoral head retroversion, a chronic right femoral neck fracture with possible nonunion and suspected avascular necrosis of the femoral head, together with leg-length discrepancy. Preoperative CT data were imported into Mimics for 1:1 three-dimensional reconstruction and virtual osteotomy planning, on the basis of which a patient-specific 3D-printed osteotomy guide was fabricated. Guide-assisted proximal femoral osteotomy, deformity correction, plate-and-screw fixation, bone grafting at the osteotomy site, and hip bracing were performed. Operative time was 3 h 40 min, estimated blood loss was 200 mL, and C-arm fluoroscopy was performed three times. At 4 months, the right hip was pain-free, gait had improved substantially, the leg-length discrepancy had decreased to &lt;1 cm, and imaging showed satisfactory osteotomy healing, stable fixation, and femoral head-acetabular congruence. Conclusion For complex pediatric hip deformities that are multiplanar and highly patient-specific, digital simulation combined with a 3D-printed patient-specific guide may facilitate the translation of preoperative three-dimensional assessment into intraoperative execution and provide an additional reference for deformity correction. In this case, the approach was technically feasible and was associated with satisfactory short-term correction and healing. However, findings from a single case cannot establish improvements in surgical accuracy, reductions in fluoroscopy use, or superiority over conventional techniques. Further comparative studies with larger cohorts and longer follow-up are needed to evaluate its accuracy, radiation exposure, guide-fit error, cost-effectiveness, and the maintenance of correction during skeletal growth.

title: Cross-subject EEG emotion recognition network based on moment channel attention
container-title: Frontiers in Psychiatry
c72c11c36c7f9de5d76a34d7745e168510ab8cb0.abstract: While most cross-subject EEG emotion recognition studies focus on average accuracy, the high inter-subject variability of EEG signals causes severe performance inconsistency across individuals. This inconsistency poses a critical barrier to real-world deployment but has received insufficient attention. To address this issue, this study proposes a hybrid emotion recognition model integrating moment channel attention and Transformer, termed the Moment Attention Convolution–Emotion Transformer Network (MAC-ETN). The proposed hybrid network consists of three components: a local temporal feature extractor, a Moment Channel Attention Network (MCA), and a global temporal feature extractor. Specifically, depthwise and separable convolutions are employed to extract local temporal features. The moment channel attention mechanism incorporates the first-order moment (mean), second-order moment (variance), and third-order moment (skewness) for channel importance calibration; and global dependency modeling is achieved through a Transformer encoder. Performance evaluation is conducted on two public datasets, DEAP and MAHNOB-HCI, using leave-one-subject-out cross-validation (LOSO-CV). The experimental results show that the main advantage of MAC-ETN lies in markedly reduced cross-subject performance variability rather than higher mean accuracy. On the DEAP dataset, the mean accuracy of MAC-ETN (61.26% for arousal and 60.47% for valence is lower than that of the strongest baselines reported under the same LOSO protocol, while its accuracy standard deviation (7.88% and 5.31%) is the lowest among all compared methods. On the MAHNOB-HCI dataset, the F1 standard deviation of MAC-ETN is 1.48% for arousal and 0.30% for valence, far below the values reported for the baselines in the literature, although the latter were obtained under a subject-dependent protocol and with a different F1 definition, so this comparison is indicative only. These results indicate that MAC-ETN reduces cross-subject performance variability at a moderate level of accuracy, which is relevant for practical EEG-based emotion recognition applications.

title: Sensory Atypicalities in Individuals with Co-occurring Autism Spectrum Disorder and Attention Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder: A Scoping Review Protocol
container-title: F1000Research
8950afc0f516da7ecef9fb15e6dc98dc249cdf1d.abstract: Abstract* Sensory atypicalities are recognized as a core feature of autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and are associated with a wide range of functional outcomes. Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) frequently co-occurs with ASD and may influence sensory experiences and sensory information processing through attentional and inhibitory mechanisms. Although an increasing number of studies have examined sensory atypicalities in co-occurring ASD and ADHD (ASD + ADHD), the evidence remains fragmented because of variability in the sensory modalities, constructs, and assessment methods employed. A scoping review is needed to map the extent and nature of the evidence on atypical sensory experiences and sensory information processing in individuals with ASD + ADHD. The review aims to clarify the contribution of ADHD comorbidity to sensory heterogeneity within ASD and identify priorities for future research. Specifically, it will examine the sensory modalities and constructs assessed, the assessment methods used, characteristics of sensory functioning, as well as associations with a wide range of outcomes. The review will include peer-reviewed primary studies published in English from 2013 onward that include individuals with ASD + ADHD and compare them with individuals with ASD. To clarify the contribution of ADHD comorbidity, studies that compare individuals with ASD and those with ADHD will also be reviewed. Eligible studies must examine sensory experiences or sensory information processing in at least one sensory modality. MEDLINE, Web of Science, and PsycINFO will be searched. Reference lists of included studies and relevant review articles will also be screened. Two reviewers will independently screen titles, abstracts, and full texts. Any disagreements will be resolved through discussion, and if consensus cannot be reached, a third reviewer will be consulted. Data will be charted using a standardized Excel-based form and summarized descriptively using tables, figures, and narrative synthesis.

title: Semantic-driven dynamic integration of multi-LOD terrain and hydraulic objects for digital twin irrigation districts
container-title: Frontiers in Earth Science
296637ea3aaee3a8b2d1026b270d51e285f41da8.abstract: Digital twin irrigation districts rely on stable multiscale 3D representation of terrain and hydraulic objects, but multi-LOD terrain transitions often cause floating, misalignment, and discontinuous dynamic behavior. Existing methods focus on static geo-metric alignment and lack semantic-aware dynamic constraint mechanisms across scales. This work proposes a semantically driven dynamic integration framework for multi-LOD terrain and hydraulic objects. We build a unified three-dimensional semantic model covering operational state, geometric form, and terrain dependency, then ex-tend LOD to a spatial constraint regulation mechanism. Differentiated strategies are designed for dynamic point, line, and surface objects via spatiotemporal mapping, pose constraints, and water-level-driven updating. Experiments in the Zhuluoba Irrigation District show that static channel boundary and centerline errors reach 0.343 m and 0.395 m, while dynamic point planimetric and elevation errors are 0.492 m and 0.245 m. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed framework can maintain relatively stable spatial–temporal consistency across different LOD levels in the investigated irrigation district.

title: Analysis of Consumer Perception of Minimalist Packaging Design as a Marketing Communication Strategy in Digital Business
container-title: Kreator
2d1c3b1e050709c2f43abba4b5a9362a508d451f.abstract: The development of digital business is encouraging companies to utilize packaging design as a marketing communication strategy that can attract young consumers through visual displays on digital media. Minimalist packaging design has become a widely used trend because it is considered to create a modern, simple, and professional impression. This study aims to determine consumer perceptions of minimalist packaging design as a marketing communication strategy in digital businesses and analyze the influence of visual communication elements on the appeal of young consumers. The study used a quantitative approach with descriptive methods. Data collection was conducted by distributing questionnaires to 100 young consumer respondents aged 17–30 who actively use digital platforms such as Shopee, TikTok Shop, and Instagram Shopping. Data analysis used IBM SPSS Statistics through validity and reliability tests and descriptive percentage analysis. The results show that minimalist packaging design has a very good perception with an average score of 87%. The study's conclusions confirm that minimalist packaging design is effective as a visual-based marketing communication strategy in the digital business era.

title: Digital Entrepreneurial Governance for Cooking Oil Supply Chains and Food Security in Indonesia
container-title: Aptisi Transactions on Technopreneurship (ATT)
91756af50bb2c20d621fbc3922193369b8420766.abstract: Food security remains a critical challenge in Indonesia despite its position as the world's largest Crude Palm Oil (CPO) producer. Although various policies have been implemented to regulate the cooking oil trade, limited research has examined how governance mechanisms and digital systems can improve supply chain transparency, accountability, and resilience. This study evaluates the governance of Indonesia's cooking oil distribution system and assesses the role of digital governance in strengthening food security. A qualitative approach was employed using purposive sampling of twelve experts representing government institutions, industry associations, practitioners, academics, food task forces, and law enforcement agencies. Data were analyzed using descriptive and thematic techniques. The effectiveness of the proposed digital governance system was assessed across four dimensions: distribution transparency and traceability, monitoring effectiveness, data integration and accessibility, and contribution to supply availability and price stability. The findings reveal persistent governance challenges, including distribution inefficiencies, limited transparency in Domestic Market Obligation (DMO) implementation, weak inter-institutional coordination, and market concentration. Expert assessments highlighted the importance of integrated digital monitoring systems in improving accountability, reducing information asymmetry, and enhancing policy responsiveness. The study proposes a digital governance framework integrating CPO traceability, distribution monitoring, transparent DMO quota management, regulatory reforms, and stronger farmer and cooperative participation. The proposed framework can improve distribution efficiency, support price stability, reduce regional disparities, and strengthen food security. The study demonstrates how digital governance can enhance transparency, resilience, and equitable distribution within Indonesia's strategic food commodity supply chains.

title: DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION ERA: AKSES KEADILAN BAGI PEREMPUAN DISABILITAS YANG BERHADAPAN DENGAN HUKUM DI KABUPATEN MINAHASA
container-title: GOVERNANCE: Jurnal Ilmiah Kajian Politik Lokal dan Pembangunan
486d1e6570194b95109c05d3009890c7bed7b928.abstract: Penelitian ini mengkaji tingkat kesiapan institusional Pengadilan Negeri Minahasa serta merumuskan konstruksi hukum yang ideal dalam pemenuhan akses keadilan bagi perempuan disabilitas di era transformasi digital sistem peradilan. Di tengah masifnya digitalisasi administrasi perkara melalui e-court dan e-litigation, perempuan disabilitas kerap menghadapi hambatan berlapis yang memicu fenomena angka gelap keadilan (dark figure of justice). Dengan menggunakan metode sosio-legal (socio-legal research), data primer yang diperoleh dari wawancara lapangan dan observasi dianalisis secara kualitatif dengan memadukan teori akses keadilan, instrumen internasional Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (CRPD), Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women (CEDAW), serta peraturan perundang-undangan nasional. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa kesiapan institusional dan infrastruktur di Pengadilan Negeri Minahasa masih tergolong rendah, reaktif, dan terjebak dalam model medis, ditandai dengan ketiadaan Standar Operasional Prosedur (SOP) internal yang inklusif serta minimnya sarana pendukung digital yang ramah ragam disabilitas. Oleh karena itu, konstruksi hukum yang ideal menuntut pergeseran paradigma dari kesetaraan formal menuju akomodasi prosedural berbasis prinsip inclusive by design, yang didukung oleh penafsiran progresif dan diskresi yudisial oleh aparatur penegak hukum agar transformasi digital tidak memunculkan bentuk diskriminasi lain.

title: E-government service satisfaction and citizen trust in China: Mechanisms and digital-divide boundaries
73157fa22f5d4e54ccf01294671ee7190257c11d.abstract: Abstract Digital government has become a defining feature of public administration, and in China it is pursued as a national strategy that couples digitalisation with the closure of the digital divide. This study examines whether e-government service satisfaction is associated with citizen trust in government, how this association is transmitted, and whether it is conditional on citizens' position in the digital divide. Drawing on the 2024 China Social Governance Survey (CSGS2024; N = 3,694 across 31 provinces), the satisfaction–trust association was estimated and decomposed into mechanisms through a bifactor structural equation model that controls for a shared evaluative factor, with digital awareness and age tested as moderators. E-government satisfaction was positively associated with government trust (β = .437, 95% bootstrap CI [.388, .478]). Perceived governance performance carried most of the association (54.5 per cent), with a smaller but statistically reliable contribution through digital governance belief (6.2 per cent). The association was stronger among citizens with lower digital awareness (interaction β = −.036, p < .001) and weaker among older respondents (β = −.024, p = .039). These findings indicate that satisfactory digital-government experience is associated with trust most strongly among less digitally aware citizens, consistent with a bridging, rather than a deepening, role for digital government across the digital divide. The evidence is associational, and the moderation result warrants confirmation in longitudinal or experimental work.

title: Regulating Digital Expression: A Critical Appraisal of the Prevention of Electronic Crimes (Amendment) Act, 2025, and its Impact on Civil Liberties in Pakistan
container-title: NUST Journal of Social Sciences and Humanities
9ece9a2b73cd1d4c4621ebdcb7c48c1db4b65ebe.abstract: The Prevention of Electronic Crimes (Amendment) Act, 2025, which amends the Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act (PECA) 2016 by redefining cybercrime and establishing four new regulatory bodies, has drawn considerable criticism in Pakistan. The amendments were enacted with little parliamentary debate or stakeholder consultation. Civil society, journalists and legal experts are of the view that the law may allow the executive to go beyond its limits and harm constitutional freedoms, especially the right to freedom of expression, the right to privacy and the space for political opposition. The government, on the other hand, presents these reforms as a necessary response to the growing problem of cybercrime and online disinformation. The paper combines doctrinal analysis with a Critical Legal Studies (CLS) lens. The state presents these reforms as necessary steps against the growing menace of cybercrime and electronic disinformation. The paper critically evaluates whether these measures enhance digital rights or are simply instruments of surveillance and control in an increasingly securitised context. It contributes to scholarship on technology law and civil liberties in postcolonial nations by situating the amendments within debates on digital authoritarianism, legal instrumentalism, and constitutionalism.

title: Legal Challenges in Protecting the Rights of Digital Payment Instrument Users: The Case of Mongolia
container-title: Advances in Social Sciences Research Journal
d815dd46faf0db57959b2c711066cb193b37b1de.abstract: The rapid expansion of digital payment services has transformed financial transactions by making payments faster, more convenient, and accessible to a wider population. However, the increasing use of mobile banking, electronic money, digital wallets, QR-code payments, and other electronic payment instruments has created new challenges for consumer protection. These include unauthorized transactions, payment fraud, misuse of personal data, service interruptions, insufficient disclosure of information, and difficulties in recovering lost funds. Such developments raise concerns about whether existing legal frameworks provide adequate protection for users of digital payment services. This article examines the legal challenges associated with protecting the rights of digital payment users in Mongolia, drawing on selected regulatory approaches from Singapore, India, and China. The study adopts a doctrinal and comparative legal research approach, based on an analysis of relevant legislation, regulatory instruments, and scholarly literature. It examines Mongolia’s Law on the National Payment System, which establishes the legal foundations for protecting payment users, ensuring the security and reliability of payment systems, and supervising payment service providers. The analysis also considers the extent to which the existing framework addresses practical issues, particularly liability for unauthorized transactions, fraud reporting and investigation, complaint handling, personal data protection, and access to effective remedies. The comparative analysis highlights several regulatory approaches that may offer useful lessons for Mongolia. These include Singapore’s risk-based regulatory framework and consumer protection guidelines, India's rules governing customer liability for unauthorized electronic banking transactions, and China's licensing and supervisory requirements for non-bank payment institutions. The study argues that Mongolia should strengthen the implementation of its existing legal framework by introducing clearer rules on customer liability, standardized complaint-resolution procedures, timely reimbursement mechanisms, stronger disclosure requirements, and more coordinated regulatory supervision. These measures would help improve legal certainty, enhance consumer confidence in digital payment services, and support the sustainable development of Mongolia’s digital financial environment.

title: Digital risks, gendered patterns: social media use and help-seeking among Austrian adolescents
container-title: Frontiers in Education
d34b0a18f623b6100d9455794ae73de55d8ca98d.abstract: Introduction Social media use is near-universal among early adolescents, yet Austrian data on the co-occurring landscape of platform use, online risks, classgroup chat dynamics, and help-seeking remain scarce. Methods This cross-sectional survey examined these four areas among 442 Austrian adolescents in grades 7 and 8 (age 12–16 years) from schools in Carinthia and Upper Austria. Results Social media use was near-universal (98.6%), with WhatsApp, Snapchat, and YouTube most used. Platform preferences differed markedly by gender, most strikingly for Pinterest (49.2% of girls versus 7.2% of boys), and Instagram and TikTok use was higher in grade 8 than in grade 7. Contact risk was common (54.1% had received a contact request from an unknown adult), and 45.7% had encountered problematic content (among those who described it, predominantly sexual or violent material, most often on TikTok). Classgroup chats were reported by 86.7% of adolescents; spam was the most frequent nuisance, while insults and cyberbullying were less common and showed no gender difference after correction for multiple testing. When distressed online, adolescents mainly named friends and parents rather than formal channels, and grade 8 students reported receiving more classroom information about AI than grade 7 students. Discussion The findings indicate gender differences in platform use, unknown contact requests, and help-seeking from friends, and a gap between perceived formal school support and adolescents' expressed needs.

title: DYNAMIC GOVERNANCE SEBAGAI MODEL TRANSFORMASI DIGITAL DALAM MASYARAKAT INFORMATIF DI KABUPATEN SUMEDANG
container-title: GOVERNANCE: Jurnal Ilmiah Kajian Politik Lokal dan Pembangunan
7376da7da4336f9fa1462e097a54afd426214f38.abstract: The transformation into a "Digital Village" has become essential for improving public service quality, information access, and community development. However, the implementation of the Digital Village initiative in Sumedang Regency still faces challenges regarding equitable distribution, infrastructure limitations, digital literacy, and human resource readiness. This study aims to analyze the Dynamic Governance model for Digital Villages in fostering an information-literate society in Sumedang Regency. A qualitative descriptive approach was employed, focusing on the Sumedang Regency Government and villages participating in the Digital Village development program. Data were collected through interviews, observation, and documentation. The analysis utilizes the Dynamic Governance perspective, specifically focusing on the capabilities of "Thinking Ahead," "Thinking Again," and "Thinking Across." The findings indicate that Digital Village development is increasingly focused on the government's ability to anticipate technological advancements, enhance apparatus competence, utilize data, and foster innovations in village services and the local economy. The government is also promoting increased community digital literacy, the use of technology in service delivery, the development of Village-Owned Enterprise (BUMDesa) marketplaces, and the digitization of tourism potential. Nevertheless, the implementation of the Digital Village initiative requires further strengthening to ensure greater equity and sustainability. The study concludes that the success of the Digital Village initiative depends not only on technology but also on the government's ability to adapt, enhance human resource capacity, manage data, and engage the community. Dynamic Governance serves as a crucial approach for building a Digital Village that is adaptive, innovative, inclusive, and oriented toward community needs.

title: Peer Review Report For: Persistent and emerging tuberculosis notification burden across 514 districts and cities in Indonesia, 2021–2025: a nationwide spatiotemporal study for public health prioritisation [version 1; peer review: 1 approved with reservations]
Smartphone Access, Internet Use, and Digital Financial Inclusion in Sub‐Saharan Africa
container-title: African Development Review
a5e103719e9bcd25736af24fcb35cadfcac62b03.abstract: ABSTRACT This study examines the association between digital connectivity and digital financial inclusion in Sub‐Saharan Africa using Global Findex 2025 microdata for 33 countries. It extends the descriptive Global Findex evidence by distinguishing smartphone access from internet use and by separating digital payment use, mobile money accounts, and digitally used financial‐institution accounts. Propensity Score Matching (PSM), post‐match logit models, inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW), doubly robust estimation, and Rosenbaum bounds are used to address observable selection and assess sensitivity. In the matched samples, smartphone access is associated with 19.1%, 18.2%, and 14.0% higher probabilities of digital payment use, mobile money account ownership, and digitally used financial‐institution account ownership, respectively; the corresponding internet use probabilities are 17.5%, 16.0%, and 12.5%. Smartphone access remains independently significant within the internet‐matched sample. Persistent disadvantages among women, less‐educated adults, and rural residents indicate that connectivity alone does not eliminate structural barriers to digital financial inclusion.

title: Repeatability and Geometric Sensitivity of Digital Mandibular Displacement Measurements in Orthodontic Records
container-title: Applied Sciences
88fca11527a86d4ce83c91cd4aed77b5190238cf.abstract: Digital mandibular displacement measurements require estimates of variability before small differences can be interpreted. In this secondary methodological analysis, we assessed the same-examiner agreement of stored digital centric-relation–maximum-intercuspation (CR–MIP) measurements and examined defined geometric sensitivities. Four anterior mandibular sites were measured twice, two weeks apart, by the same examiner using stored records from 14 patients in a doctoral cohort. The principal summary was the four-site mean. Analyses included an absolute-agreement intraclass correlation coefficient, ICC(A,1), patient-level bootstrap confidence intervals, Bland–Altman limits of agreement, standard error of measurement (SEM), and minimal detectable change (MDC95). Separate rigid-body calculations examined axis translation, closure to first contact, and landmark correspondence. Session means were 1.473 and 1.421 mm; ICC(A,1) was 0.915 (95% confidence interval, 0.761–0.972), bias −0.052 mm, SEM 0.238 mm, MDC95 0.661 mm, and limits of agreement −0.713 to 0.609 mm. At a retained 3° closure angle, a specified 5 mm perpendicular axis offset produced a calculated point-position change of 0.262 mm. Recalculating first contact could alter the closure angle and active contact. High relative reliability coexisted with appreciable absolute variation. Whether closure and landmark selection were repeated was undocumented; the estimates therefore do not establish repeatability of the complete measurement procedure, clinical accuracy or full-workflow reproducibility.

title: Prosthodontic Identification in Forensic Diagnostics: From Conventional Marking to Digital Traceability and AI-Assisted Recognition—A Narrative Review
container-title: Diagnostics
ef8b8f4028bb2a472cd485053fc66e8f578f1fd0.abstract: Human identification is a central component of medico-legal investigations and disaster victim identification (DVI), particularly when remains are decomposed, burned, fragmented, or skeletonized. Dental tissues, restorations, and prosthetic appliances may preserve patient-specific information under conditions that compromise other identifying features. This narrative review aimed to examine conventional and digital prosthodontic identification and traceability approaches and to evaluate their potential applications in forensic diagnostics and human identification. A structured search of PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar identified publications from January 2000 to August 2026 on prosthodontic identification, digital traceability, AI-assisted implant recognition, blockchain-based dental data management, and complementary oral biometric methods. Records were independently screened by two authors according to predefined eligibility criteria. Of the 1446 records identified, 558 duplicates were removed, and 92 studies were included in the final narrative synthesis. The evidence was synthesized thematically according to the identification or traceability approach. Conventional methods remain simple and accessible but show variable durability and readability, whereas digital and electronic systems offer greater information capacity and retrievability but are limited by technical requirements and incomplete forensic validation. In a 20 min thermal-exposure experiment, acrylic resin blocks were largely destroyed at 800 °C, whereas some metallic identification labels remained readable at 800–1000 °C, with material-dependent differences in preservation and readability among metallic labels at 1200 °C. These findings represent study-specific observations rather than universal thermal resistance thresholds. Digital imaging, intraoral scanning, CAD/CAM records, AI-assisted implant recognition, and blockchain-supported systems further expand traceability, although the overall evidence remains heterogeneous. Prosthodontic identification and traceability encompass complementary conventional and digital approaches rather than a single universally applicable method, while oral biometrics serve only as adjunctive evidence and cannot independently establish identity. Their forensic value depends on durability, retrievability, availability of corresponding antemortem information, interoperability, and appropriate management of sensitive patient data. Further standardized and clinically relevant validation is needed before advanced traceability systems can be routinely incorporated into forensic identification workflows.

title: Between the Real and the Virtual: Teachers’ Perceptions of Digital Technologies in Practical Work in Lower Secondary Natural Sciences
container-title: Education Sciences
eafcdb18e7b289533fd0d8cdda7de0d57f7b04dd.abstract: Digital technologies are increasingly present in practical work (PW) in science education, but little is known about how teachers of early adolescents weigh digital against hands-on activity. This study explores how Portuguese lower secondary Natural Sciences teachers perceive the advantages and risks of using digital technologies in PW. A qualitative, interpretive, exploratory study was conducted with 23 teachers selected with a geographical quota, through semi-structured comprehensive interviews held between July 2023 and February 2024. Categorical content analysis was supported by NVivo 15. Teachers named many tools, mostly general-purpose (gamification, presentation and learning management platforms) and a few subject-specific simulators. Perceived advantages were simulating phenomena that cannot be observed directly, motivation through gamification, and time savings. The risks perceived were digital saturation, distraction, loss of manual dexterity and of learning from error, uneven school internet, preparation time, and unequal student access. Only two teachers mentioned artificial intelligence. Two teachers described digital technologies as a complement to hands-on work; the findings are exploratory perceptions, not evidence of effects on students, and suggest that teacher education could address when and why digital activity is preferable to real activity.

title: Digital Development Control in European Planning Systems: A Comparative Perspective from Greece and The Netherlands
container-title: Land
79f6e45e9872e90a15671002ab022edd19be393f.abstract: Across Europe, digital transformation is reshaping planning systems and development control, where planning rules and building standards are operationalized in practice. This article examines how digital permitting systems, as part of wider regulatory infrastructures, mediate rather than simply automate development control processes. The study adopts a qualitative comparative case-study approach, examining Greece and the Netherlands as contrasting institutional settings. Conceptually, the study builds on planning scholarship on development control and is informed by perspectives on regulation and socio-technical infrastructures. The empirical analysis draws on legislation, administrative and policy documents, judicial decisions, professional and technical material, and limited practitioner confirmation. The Greek e-Adeies system and the Dutch Digitaal Stelsel Omgevingswet (DSO) are examined along three dimensions: institutional embedding; allocation of authority and permissibility control; and responsibility, accountability, and legal oversight. The comparison reveals two distinct configurations of digital development control. In Greece, e-Adeies combines automatic permit issuance with a redistribution of prior control, increased reliance on professional inputs, and post-issuance oversight mechanisms. In the Netherlands, the DSO integrates rules, information, and application procedures across multiple levels of government while substantive decision-making remains with competent authorities. The central finding is that digital integration can centralize access to regulatory information and procedures without necessarily centralizing substantive decision-making authority or altering its formal allocation. Digital permitting systems do not simply reflect existing planning-system characteristics. They interact with legal and institutional arrangements to shape how regulatory information, control functions, responsibilities, and oversight are organized.

title: The Universal Hopf Envelope of Framed Digital Images: Ordered-Partition Antipodes and Coordinate Quotients
container-title: Mathematics
6525de973206d1d5a2e34203aee3d1ab16083003.abstract: Framed digital images admit horizontal juxtaposition and a coproduct that splits active pixels while retaining the allocated frame. The resulting bialgebra has no antipode because its blank column is group-like and noninvertible. Identifying images with column words specializes Takeuchi’s free-Hopf construction: adjoining the inverse of the blank column gives the Hopf envelope. Right-normalized nonblank columns form a connected graded Hopf factor. For this model we give a cancellation-free ordered-partition antipode and an exact Hilbert series, including the scalar and one-generator exceptions to exponential growth. We characterize the commuting coordinate quotient Hfr=Sym(V)#K[Z] by column factorization and translated-pixel commutativity, classify its group-like and fixed-frame skew-primitive elements, and establish the lifting criterion for translation-equivariant color maps. Global character weights must be constant along horizontal translation orbits. On finite patches, a more general local weighted Boolean zeta transform admits arbitrary weights, Kronecker factorization, exact conditioning formulas, and O(n2n) inversion. Two exact-arithmetic programs perform 10,150 regression checks. Stored tests on nine public images include 61,440 binary patches, 552,960 pixels, 360 stability trials, and RGB equivariance controls. They validate local inversion and the translation criterion, with zero reconstructed-pixel errors; they do not establish restoration performance.

title: Acute Submandibular Sialadenitis in Children During the 2025–2026 Influenza Season: A Retrospective Case Series from a Digital Consultation Network
container-title: Pediatric Reports
a5204b8560fadd89979ed88d769b6296f862c587.abstract: Background: Acute submandibular sialadenitis in children can raise concern for bacterial infection or obstruction. Viral-associated salivary gland inflammation is described, particularly involving the parotid gland; however, the clinical features of pediatric submandibular presentations are less well characterized. Methods: We conducted a retrospective descriptive case series of children with acute tender submandibular swelling and concurrent or recent respiratory or influenza-like symptoms whose cases were discussed through a secure physician-to-physician digital consultation network in northern Israel between November 2025 and February 2026. Clinical, laboratory, imaging, management, and outcome data were extracted from consultation discussions and available medical documentation. Results: Fifteen children were included (median age, 8 years; interquartile range, 5.75–13.5; 12/15 male). All children had viral infection symptoms; twelve children (80%) had preceding respiratory symptoms, and 10 of these 12 had fever during the preceding week. Influenza A PCR was performed in five children and was positive in all five. The remaining ten children were not tested for influenza, and their presentations were considered clinically suggestive of a viral illness. All children had tender submandibular gland enlargement without documented clinical signs of suppuration. Ultrasound was performed in seven and showed glandular enlargement without ductal dilatation, abscess, or fluid collection. All received supportive care; three (20%) also received antibiotics. No emergency department referrals or hospital admissions were documented, and clinical resolution without reported sequelae was recorded in all 15 children. Conclusions: This case series describes a cluster of acute, non-suppurative submandibular sialadenitis identified through a clinician-to-clinician consultation network during an influenza season. Although influenza A was confirmed in only five patients, the temporal clustering and clinical presentation suggest a possible association with circulating respiratory viruses. The physician-to-physician digital consultation network facilitated the recognition and discussion of this cluster of atypical submandibular sialadenitis cases. Documented consultations in which antibiotic treatment was considered but subsequently withheld suggest that timely specialist input may support clinical decision-making and antimicrobial stewardship in primary care. Further studies are needed to evaluate the impact of such networks on clinical management and healthcare utilization.

title: Agile Leadership and Digital Transformation for Crisis Resilience and Sustainable Practices During Macro-Crises: A Dual-Theoretical Perspective in Ghana’s Tourism Sector
container-title: Sustainability
60941a87176397df1f84068967aa50c341a42871.abstract: Drawing on Chaos Theory and Dynamic Capabilities Theory as a complementary theoretical lens, this study explores how agile leaders themselves describe the relationship between their leadership practices and digital transformation in pursuit of crisis resilience and sustainable practices during macro-crises within Ghana’s tourism and hospitality sector. Qualitative in-depth interviews were conducted with 43 purposively sampled sector stakeholders with direct experience of applying agile leadership during crisis, analysed via NVivo 15. Because participants were selected for this experience, the findings describe perceptions within this sample rather than causal effects relative to non-adopters. Participants described navigating unpredictable, non-linear environments in ways they associated with both short-term operational survival and longer-term socio-economic sustainability. While participants reported that digital adoption was substantially impeded by infrastructural deficits, financial constraints, and cultural resistance, they described responding to these barriers by cultivating collaborative ecosystems and pursuing scalable capacity-building initiatives. Participants also associated their use of digital tools with reduced operational waste and workforce empowerment, rather than efficiency gains alone. This research proposes a conceptual framework suggesting that technological integration may be more effective when accompanied by leadership agility, offering a starting point for building crisis-resilient, digitally inclusive tourism ecosystems in Ghana that future comparative research can test.

title: The “More Health, Less Diabetes” Randomized Controlled Trial: A Digital and In-Person Educational and Exercise Program for Type 2 Diabetes Prevention Study Protocol
ca4db55844f9df605d41eabd186dee2ef7bedc3c.abstract: Abstract Background Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is a major global health issue, with prevalence and healthcare-related costs rising every year. Lifestyle-related factors such as physical inactivity and unhealthy diets play a central role in disease progression. Exercise has consistently been shown to improve glycemic control at the individual level and, in large-scale prevention trials, to reduce the incidence of T2DM among high-risk populations; however, heterogeneity in intervention design and delivery limits comparability across studies. Online interventions are scalable and inexpensive, but may have limited effectiveness in sustaining health outcomes over time.. Our aim is to assess the effectiveness and cost-effectiveness of a 6-month in-person versus online lifestyle intervention in individuals at high risk of developing T2DM within 10 years. Methods A randomized controlled trial (RCT) will be conducted to evaluate the effectiveness and cost-effectiveness of a 6-month lifestyle intervention delivered in-person or online. For this RCT, adults at high risk of developing T2DM, as determined by the FINDRISC score, will be recruited from Portuguese primary health care units. Participants will be randomly assigned to one of three groups: an in-person intervention group (IPIG), an online intervention group (OIG), or a control group. The IPIG will participate in a 6-month program consisting of three exercise sessions per week and seven educational sessions throughout the 6-month intervention. At the same time, the OIG will follow the same online program. The control group will attend a single orientation session. During the subsequent 6-month follow-up, all participants will have the option to attend in-person exercise sessions. The primary outcome will be postprandial glucose, assessed by blood analysis following a 2-hour 75g oral glucose tolerance test. The secondary outcomes will include variables related to body composition, cardiorespiratory fitness, handgrip strength, 24-h movement accelerometry, diet, and cost-effectiveness. Primary and secondary outcomes will be measured at baseline, 6 months of intervention, and 12 months of follow-up. Discussion Lifestyle programs are effective and cost-effective for people at risk of T2DM, but the optimal intervention type, design, and delivery remain unclear. This trial will serve as a proof-of-concept, implementing an evidence-based lifestyle intervention program tailored to individuals at risk of T2DM and evaluating the comparative effectiveness and cost-effectiveness of in-person versus online lifestyle interventions. The findings will inform future large-scale strategies for T2DM prevention. Trial registration: This study was retrospectively registered (NCT07079722), and the details are at: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07079722 Registered on July 23, 2025**.

9fef5bcfef799ae87be1a6f34263f5694b24816f.abstract: This community service activity aims to improve the performance of Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) through mentoring in digital accounting transformation in Palembang City. The main problems faced by partners include low digital literacy and the continued use of manual financial recording systems, resulting in low efficiency and accuracy of financial reports. The methods used in this program include socialization, training, and assistance in implementing integrated digital accounting systems. The program involved approximately 30 MSMEs as participants. The activity was conducted through several stages, namely problem identification, training on digital accounting applications, and evaluation of implementation results. The results indicate that MSMEs experienced improvements in financial management efficiency, report accuracy, and decision-making capabilities. In addition, digital accounting transformation enhances transparency and trust in financial reporting. Therefore, this mentoring program provides a significant contribution to improving the competitiveness and performance of MSMEs sustainably.

title: AI-Oriented Digital Governance and Financial Transparency: Evidence from Chinese Listed Firms
container-title: Bulletin of Monetary Economics and Banking
3c2ab161e4843723725023c544d5b4d9c999e3ed.abstract: This study investigates whether Chinese listed firms’ financial transparency improves with AI. Our main AI measure is AI-related disclosure intensity based on annual report text. We validate it using firm-year proxies for AI-related patents and AI/software investment to reduce potential symbolism. We add extensive controls, governance covariates, and mechanism tests to support the instrumental-variable results. From 2011 to 2023, we measured transparency through stock-exchange disclosure quality ratings and AI through annual report AI-related language for 1,028 Shanghai and Shenzhen Stock Exchange firms. Using provincial internet penetration as an AI instrument, we estimate two-way fixed effects models and address endogeneity using two-stage least squares. We also compare the effect by firm size, ownership (SOE vs. non-SOE), industry (high tech vs. non-high-tech), and regional development. Even after controlling for firm characteristics, absorbing firm and year effects, and instrumenting AI, firms with higher AI intensity are more transparent. In smaller, privately owned, and high-tech firms, and in firms located in less-developed regions, transparency gains are greatest. The findings suggest that AI-supported monitoring and documentation improve reported information and can partially replace poorer internal control capabilities.

title: The mediating role of digital transformation in the relationship between social media marketing, mobile marketing, and marketing performance: Evidence from the Jordanian banking sector
container-title: Innovative Marketing
9dbd49b236155b2a60e9f1c00f8633c7bf1e2067.abstract: Type of the article: Research ArticleAbstractThis study investigates the mediating role of digital transformation (DT) in the relationships between social media marketing (SMM), mobile marketing (MBM), and marketing performance (MP) in the Jordanian banking sector. Data were collected from 272 bank branch managers representing banking institutions across Jordan between May and November 2024. The study employed Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) using SmartPLS 4 to test the proposed relationships. Internal consistency and convergent validity were confirmed through Cronbach’s Alpha values ranging from 0.820 to 0.903, composite reliability values ranging from 0.873 to 0.923, and Average Variance Extracted (AVE) values ranging from 0.579 to 0.650. The structural model explained 27.5% of the variance in digital transformation (R² = 0.275) and 59.9% of the variance in marketing performance (R² = 0.599). The findings revealed that mobile marketing has a significant positive effect on marketing performance (β = 0.155, p = 0.001), whereas social media marketing does not have a significant direct effect on marketing performance (β = 0.093, p = 0.058). Both social media marketing and mobile marketing significantly influence digital transformation (β = 0.315, p &amp;lt; 0.001; β = 0.320, p &amp;lt; 0.001), while digital transformation exerts a strong positive effect on marketing performance (β = 0.646, p &amp;lt; 0.001). Furthermore, digital transformation fully mediates the relationship between social media marketing and marketing performance (β = 0.203, p &amp;lt; 0.001) and partially mediates the relationship between mobile marketing and marketing performance (β = 0.206, p &amp;lt; 0.001). The findings highlight the critical role of digital transformation in converting digital marketing capabilities into improved marketing performance and provide practical insights for banking institutions seeking to enhance competitiveness in an increasingly digital environment.AcknowledgmentsThis research received no specific grant from any funding agency in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors.

title: Attention-Guided Stroke Location Inversion for Explainable Sketch Recognition
7cff0a368886036594fb645dbc944ead5c24fc3e.abstract: Abstract Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) has made remarkable progress in pixel and text domains, yet human sketches a uniquely sparse and sequential data modality remain largely unexplored from an interpretability perspective. The recently proposed SketchXAI framework introduced Stroke Location Inversion (SLI) to reconstruct stroke layouts from randomized configurations, but treats every stroke with identical optimization priority regardless of its structural relevance. We address this limitation by proposing Attention-Guided Stroke Location Inversion (AG-SLI). We initially evaluate a continuous formulation that scales per stroke gradients proportionally to self attention weights across a 30-category QuickDraw subset (86.13% classifier accuracy). Through a staged empirical protocol, we demonstrate that this continuous variant fails to replicate consistently, exhibiting sign-flipping median convergence speed changes (−47.8% to +40.0%) driven by localized sampling noise. Motivated by this instability, we introduce a refined, bounded, rank-based formulation: a fixed multiplicative gradient boost is restricted to the top 30% most attended strokes across the final four transformer layers, decaying linearly over the optimization trajectory. Benchmarked against standard machine learning optimizers across independent hard-case pools (n = 90), the refined mechanism achieves a median convergence depth of 10 iterations, significantly outperforming standard Adam (19 iterations) and SGD with Momentum (24 iterations). Furthermore, the framework limits non-convergence rates to 22.2%, improves spatial recovery (0.038 Final MSE), and yields a net 30.65% reduction in total job wall-clock time despite an updated O(N log N) per step complexity. We present this complete empirical journey including the initial non replication to establish a transparent baseline for reproducible, resource efficient optimization architectures in sparse visual domains.

title: REVITALIZING INTANGIBLE CULTURAL HERITAGE IN THE GRAND CANAL'S ANHUI SECTION: PATHWAYS AND DIGITAL STRATEGIES
container-title: Journal of Trends in Arts and Humanities
e77a558ff501795b0fc856cc2dd5afd9858eef39.abstract: The Anhui section of the Grand Canal is rich in intangible cultural heritage (ICH). However, the tacit and fragmented nature of these resources makes it difficult to present their cultural meanings comprehensively. Building on an examination of the forms of ICH-related knowledge and the current state of digital development in the region, this paper explores the mechanisms through which artificial intelligence (AI) can facilitate the revitalization of ICH and proposes pathways for digital preservation. The study argues that the structural challenges facing digital preservation in the region arise from the combined effects of four factors, which include intelligent recognition, knowledge reconstruction, collaborative innovation, and value conversion, rather than from a mere lack of technology. The central task of digital preservation is to shift its focus from documentation and display toward knowledge reconstruction and intelligent services, thereby making digital technologies a form of infrastructure underpinning the systematic safeguarding and living transmission of ICH.

title: Driving Sustainable Business Innovation in Small and Medium-Sized Enterprises Through Digital Transformation: Strategic Entrepreneurship in the Post-Pandemic Era
container-title: Archives of Business Research
78e4daee26d1f841c4712f2975b1968e285cacdd.abstract: Digital transformation can help small and medium-sized enterprises respond to disruption, but technology adoption alone does not establish a sustainable competitive advantage. This article examines how strategic entrepreneurship connects digital opportunities with the organizational capabilities needed for continuing innovation in the post-pandemic economy. It presents a narrative literature review, drawing on the author's reported review of 45 published articles and synthesizing relevant empirical and conceptual research. No primary data were collected, no independent statistical tests were conducted, and findings from different studies were not pooled. The synthesis identifies strategic alignment, organizational learning, resource availability, and external support as important conditions shaping digital transformation. Published studies suggest that digital capabilities can support business continuity and innovation, while also documenting implementation barriers and uneven performance outcomes. Evidence of a nonlinear relationship between digital orientation and performance cautions against assuming immediate or universal gains. The article distinguishes business viability from environmental and social sustainability and proposes an interpretive framework linking opportunity recognition, capability development, business model adaptation, and outcome evaluation. Practical recommendations emphasize staged investment, employee learning, and partnerships that address specific capability gaps. Policy recommendations focus on accessible infrastructure, skills development, and support for implementation. Because the original search and screening records are unavailable, the review offers a bounded interpretation of selected literature rather than an exhaustive or reproducible systematic assessment.

title: Cyclic fatigue resistance of ground and twisted nickel-titanium rotary instruments: An in vitro study
container-title: Endodontics Today
9379a440e0af667da3551229a65760f72bf3446a.abstract: INTRODUCTION. Nickel–titanium (NiTi) rotary instruments have been extensively employed in endodontics because of their flexibility and capability to preserve canal anatomy. However, unpredictable separation due to cyclic fatigue is still a major concern. As compared to traditional ground NiTi instruments, Twisted File (TF) instruments are produced using a thermomechanical twisting process that maintains the alloy grain structure and may improve fatigue resistance. PURPOSE. To evaluate the cyclic fatigue resistance (CFR) and fracture characteristics of conventional ground and twisted nickel-titanium rotary instruments using scanning electron microscopic (SEM) examination. MATERIALS AND METHODS. The study included thirty-two new NiTi rotary instruments, separated into four groups ( n = 8): Twisted File #25/.06, RaCe #25/.06, ProTaper Universal F1, and Helix #25/.06. Cyclic fatigue testing was conducted using an endodontic motor running at 300 rpm in a stainless-steel artificial canal with a 45° curvature and a 5 mm radius. The recorded time to fracture was used to calculate the number of cycles to failure (NCF). The lengths of fractured fragments were measured, and representative instruments were analyzed by SEM either before or after cyclic fatigue testing. A one-way analysis of variance (ANOVA) and Scheffé’s post hoc test were used to assess the data, and p < 0.05 was used to define statistical significance. RESULTS. The higher CFR was recorded for Twisted File instruments (690.00 ± 55.93 cycles), followed by RaCe (529.00 ± 45.23 cycles), ProTaper Universal (416.00 ± 29.64 cycles), and Helix (242.87 ± 21.63 cycles). A one-way ANOVA showed a statistically significant difference among groups. For every pairwise comparison, post hoc analysis demonstrates significant differences ( p < 0.001). The lengths of the broken fragments did not significantly differ among groups ( p = 0.06). SEM assessment indicated microcracks and crack propagation patterns generated by fatigue in all instrument systems. Twisted File instruments showed fewer surface flaws in comparison with the standard ground instruments, which had crack propagation linked with machining grooves. CONCLUSION. Twisted File instruments have better CFR than RaCe, ProTaper Universal, or Helix. SEM demonstrated characteristic fatigue failure patterns in all systems, but traditional ground instruments exhibited greater surface flaws. Twisted Files may have improved fatigue performance due to thermomechanical twisting.

title: Where is the melody? Spontaneous attention orchestrates melody formation during polyphonic music listening
7c1db87f862bcac84e4b24dd665c829a481f8fde.abstract: Humans seamlessly process multi-voice music into a coherent perceptual whole. Yet the neural strategies supporting this experience remain unclear. One fundamental component of this process is the formation of melody, a core structural element of music. Previous work on monophonic listening has provided strong evidence for the neurophysiological basis of melody processing, for example indicating predictive processing as a foundational mechanism underlying melody encoding. However, considerable uncertainty remains about how melodies are formed during polyphonic music listening, as existing theories (e.g., divided attention, figure–ground model, stream integration) fail to unify the full range of empirical findings. Here, we combined behavioural measures with non-invasive electroencephalography (EEG) to probe spontaneous attentional bias and melodic expectation while participants listened to two-voice classical excerpts. Our uninstructed listening paradigm eliminated a major experimental constraint, creating a more ecologically valid setting. We found that attention bias was significantly influenced by both the high-voice superiority effect and intrinsic melodic statistics. We then employed transformer-based models to generate next-note expectation profiles and test competing theories of polyphonic perception. Drawing on our findings, we propose a weighted-integration framework in which attentional bias calibrates the overall degree of integration of the competing streams. In doing so, the proposed framework reconciles previous divergent accounts by showing that, even under free-listening conditions, melodies emerge through an attention-guided statistical integration mechanism.

title: X-OCTANE: eXplainable On-Chip Telemetry-based Anomaly Notification Engine for Silicon Lifecycle Management
container-title: ACM Transactions on Design Automation of Electronic Systems
05013dd9a2de90d10258be8cb3a439b22e2501af.abstract: Silicon Lifecycle Management (SLM) is essential for ensuring the reliability, security, and performance of modern computing platforms. Conventional SLM approaches rely on off-chip or software-only analytics, which lack on-die interpretability. We present X-OCTANE, an explainable on-chip telemetry-based anomaly notification engine. X–OCTANE is a hybrid explainability framework that integrates Causal-Preserving Mutual Information (CP–MI) with SHAP-based feature attribution for interpretable feature ranking and selection. The proposed feature rank-and-selection procedure retains competitive safety-oriented anomaly detection and bolsters security-specific in-field monitoring of compute platforms. For the 7 nm ASAP technology, X-OCTANE achieves competitive anomaly detection performance with less than 0.50% CPU die area and 1.0% non-idle power overhead. In addition, X–OCTANE improves anomaly-driven diagnosis accuracy by over 7% on average. Experimental validation using the PAMPAR benchmark suite on two separate experimental platforms demonstrates enhanced anomaly detection and diagnosis through the proposed explainable feature-rank-and-selection method. X–OCTANE establishes a scalable and transparent foundation for on-chip SLM analytics, unifying detection fidelity with causal interpretability.
