title: AI, PSYCHOLOGICAL SAFETY, AND THE TRANSFORMATION OF MODERN LEADERSHIP
container-title: Journal of High School Research
95122f65f84c7731a54ad5016764f0b57362bcde.abstract: This study explores how artificial intelligence (AI) impacts organizational leadership and workplace psychological safety across diverse industries. Using mixed methodology combining 36 cross-industry questionnaires and 3 semi-structured executive interviews in sales, product development and human resources fields, the research examines the impacts on traditional organization and identifies leadership competencies irreplaceable by AI. The study demonstrates that digital and AI tools reduce employees’ reliance on hierarchical leadership while psychological safety significantly drives team innovation and performance. Moreover, diverse leadership models have corresponding impacts on psychological safety at an individual level. According to the study, core irreplaceable traits include empathy, accountability for high-stakes decisions, and interpersonal emotional-value provision. This research offers practical suggestions for managers or leaders adapting leadership practices to the AI era and supplements existing organizational behavior research. The article supplements current leadership models that discuss contingency theory and provides evidence and reference for enterprises that are transforming from traditional leadership models to developing innovative competency models.

title: Dietary Management as a Strategy for Reducing Inflammaging in Aging Population
container-title: Journal of High School Research
d66028a82d8f9be8ebcc34f01af3257105b65835.abstract: As more people live into older age, researchers have started to focus on chronic, low-grade systemic inflammation—called inflammaging—as a key biological factor behind cardiovascular disease, cognitive decline, and frailty in later life. Franceschi et al. (2000) describe inflammaging as a progressive, chronic, low-grade pro-inflammatory state that becomes more pronounced with age, driven by multiple interacting mechanisms including senescent cell accumulation and SASP signaling, mitochondrial dysfunction and the release of DAMPs, gut microbiome shifts, and failures in immune regulation. This literature review examines how dietary patterns influence inflammaging through measurable biomarkers such as hs-CRP, IL-6, and TNF-α. Evidence indicates that pro-inflammatory dietary components including saturated fatty acids, trans fatty acids, and high–glycemic index carbohydrates tend to elevate these markers, while omega-3 fatty acids, dietary fiber, MUFAs, flavonoids, carotenoids, and magnesium are associated with reductions in them. A two-year Mediterranean diet intervention reported significant decreases in hs-CRP, IL-6, IL-7, and IL-18 compared to a control diet, suggesting that changing dietary patterns can causally lower inflammatory biomarkers. Taken together, these studies suggest that using anti-inflammatory dietary patterns is a realistic and practical strategy to help manage inflammaging and support healthier aging in older adults.

title: A Co-Designed and Bilingual WhatsApp-Based Chatbot Intervention (PflegeBot) for Informal Caregivers in Germany: Single-Arm Nonrandomized Feasibility Study
container-title: JMIR Formative Research
2bb32f9a4f6ee7fc6c8c4684507c1b5af5b08b0f.abstract: Abstract Background Informal caregivers play a central role in long-term care but experience elevated risks of stress, depressive symptoms, and caregiver burden, alongside barriers to accessing preventive support. Low-threshold digital public health interventions may offer scalable support; however, evidence on their feasibility, usability, and contextual fit remains limited, particularly for heterogeneous caregiver populations. Objective This study describes the development and implementation of PflegeBot, an intersectionality-informed WhatsApp-based chatbot intervention, and evaluates its feasibility, usability, and acceptability among informal caregivers in Germany. Methods A single-arm, nonrandomized feasibility study with pre-post assessments was conducted between December 2023 and March 2024. Informal caregivers aged 18 years and older were recruited via community-based, institutional, and online channels. PflegeBot was a co-designed, bilingual (German and Turkish) WhatsApp-based chatbot that delivered 84 scheduled messages over 12 weeks. Content included caregiving information, self-care, and cognitive behavioral therapy–informed self-help, plus optional frequently asked questions and question functions. Baseline and full follow-up assessments were administered online. Feasibility was assessed using indicators of recruitment, chatbot initiation and message delivery, opt-out, and provision of follow-up measures. Usability was assessed using the System Usability Scale (SUS), and acceptability was assessed using study-specific items. Exploratory outcomes included perceived stress (4-item Perceived Stress Scale [PSS-4]), caregiver burden (4-item Zarit Burden Interview [ZBI-4]), depressive symptoms (Center for Epidemiologic Studies Depression Scale [CES-D]), and loneliness (6-item De Jong Gierveld Loneliness Scale [DJGLS-6]). Analyses were descriptive; no hypothesis tests were conducted. Open-ended follow-up feedback was examined using a systematic inductive descriptive approach. Results Of 102 participants included in the baseline analysis sample, 84 (82%) were women. According to chatbot log data, message delivery was initiated for 67 participants. Forty-nine participants provided at least one follow-up measure, and complete SUS data were available for 46 participants. The mean SUS score was 82.45 (SD 14.86, 95% CI 78.03‐86.86; range 47.5‐100), and 35 out of 46 (76%) participants scored at or above the benchmark of 68. Overall satisfaction with PflegeBot had a mean rating of 4.02 out of 5 (SD 0.98; n=46). Among participants responding to the relevant item, 1 out of 45 (2%) reported using the optional FAQ function. Mean changes were −0.57 (95% CI −1.24 to 0.10; n=35) for perceived stress, 0.81 (95% CI −0.02 to 1.63; n=36) for caregiver burden, −2.38 (95% CI −5.42 to 0.66; n=34) for depressive symptoms, and −0.39 (95% CI −0.90 to 0.12; n=36) for loneliness. Open-ended feedback highlighted needs for more flexible delivery, greater tailoring, and easier navigation. Conclusions PflegeBot could be delivered through WhatsApp, and participants providing follow-up data reported high usability and generally favorable satisfaction. Controlled evaluations with objective engagement data and assessment of differential reach and outcomes are warranted.

title: Monocular Interacting-Hand Reconstruction with Multimodal Context Fusion and Spatial Attention
container-title: ACM Transactions on Multimedia Computing, Communications, and Applications
a47dfde1fe22acb35e4fb2d872d52525588a142c.abstract: 3D hand reconstruction from monocular RGB images has attracted increasing attention due to its low cost and ease of deployment. However, accurately reconstructing interacting hands remains challenging, primarily because mutual occlusion leads to missing visual evidence, while image cropping weakens global spatial consistency. To address these issues, we propose the Context-Aware Interacting Hand Reconstruction Network (CANet), a monocular interacting-hand reconstruction framework that integrates multimodal context fusion with structured spatial attention. Specifically, CANet leverages estimated depth maps, edge contours, and center heatmaps to retain global contextual cues and guide reconstruction in occluded regions. A hierarchical spatial attention module further enhances spatial consistency by separately modeling intra-hand structural dependencies and inter-hand interactions, enabling more coherent reasoning about complex hand poses. Experiments across multiple public benchmarks demonstrate that CANet consistently improves the accuracy of both hand pose estimation and mesh reconstruction.

title: Classroom Integration of AI-Simulated Patients and Automated Feedback in Doctoral Psychotherapy Training: Longitudinal Mixed Methods Study
container-title: Interactive Journal of Medical Research
75ceb45a0460837875ae639367a900abec968c8d.abstract: Abstract Background Psychotherapy education increasingly emphasizes technology-assisted methods that extend deliberate practice beyond human supervision. AI has enabled automated skill assessment and patient simulations, yet few studies have examined how students experience such tools in real-world settings alongside established practice modalities. Objective We aimed to evaluate students’ experiences with AI-augmented deliberate practice embedded in an existing psychotherapy course sequence. Secondary aims included identifying implementation barriers, ethical and pedagogical considerations, and factors influencing students’ acceptance of AI-assisted learning. Methods Participants were 29 first-year clinical psychology doctoral students in a 2-quarter psychotherapy sequence at an American Psychological Association–accredited program. In the fall course, students completed weekly peer role-plays and could optionally submit transcripts to CARE for AI feedback to supplement peer feedback. In the winter course, students completed required weekly deliberate practice through Skillsetter video vignettes and could optionally practice with CARE’s voice-based AI-simulated patients, receiving AI and instructor feedback afterward. Surveys with Likert-type and free-response items were voluntary in the fall and required in the winter; 9 and 25 students completed them, respectively. Analyses included descriptive statistics, matched-pairs testing, and thematic analysis. Results In the fall course (n=9), where privacy concerns and survey nonresponse limited data on AI feedback, students rated peer feedback higher than AI feedback on being constructive and helpful (median 3, IQR 3-3 vs median 2, IQR 2-2; P =.02) and recognizing areas to improve (mean 5.22, SD 0.83 vs mean 4.33, SD 0.87; P =.046), citing transcription errors and a narrow focus on empathy while valuing AI’s alternative phrasing. In the winter course (n=25), Skillsetter was rated higher than CARE only for learning from mistakes (mean 4.52, SD 2.00 vs mean 3.20, SD 2.04; P =.03); immersion, spontaneous responding, communication beyond words, and alliance building did not differ significantly. Students valued CARE for interactive practice not possible with vignettes but reported undetected vocal pauses (20/25, 80%), insufficient realism (14/25, 56%), and limited emotional expression (13/25, 52%), and raised concerns about AI replacing peer support (22/25, 88%) and peer interaction (20/25, 80%). Asked about AI broadly, students expressed mixed views, citing concerns about supplanted relational dynamics, nonconsensual data use, and generative AI’s environmental impacts. Conclusions Embedding AI-augmented deliberate practice into an existing course sequence was feasible, but students’ experiences favored established methods: they preferred human over AI feedback and described video vignettes as more realistic than voice-based AI interactions, while valuing AI-simulated patients for interactive practice other modalities could not provide. Implementation barriers included feedback quality, transcription accuracy, and instructor time required to supplement AI feedback. Perceptions of AI’s instructional utility appeared contingent on students’ trust in the technology, suggesting future deployments should weigh a sample’s attitudes toward AI and its value relative to existing training resources.

title: Cross-Site Stability of Embedding Model Rankings for Known-Item Retrieval From Clinical Notes: Two-Corpus Comparative Evaluation Study
container-title: JMIR AI
54e3ea2256a501ff492d385dcbb15b3df2588127.abstract: Background Retrieval-augmented generation over clinical text depends on the embedding model chosen—a choice that interacts with documentation genre. Cross-site stability of embedding-model rankings has not been evaluated on real electronic health record (EHR) narratives with genre held constant; public benchmarks are predominantly single-source, and multi-institution evaluations compare models and query formulations within tasks rather than ranking stability across institutions. Objective The aim of the study is to test whether embedding model rankings transfer across 2 institutional EHR corpora, with genre held constant; to examine the contributions of model, site/corpus, and genre and their dependence on scoring; and to test whether the dominant contributor depends on model-panel composition. Methods We compared 13 embedding models on a known-item passage-to-source-document task, each query a deterministic 2-sentence excerpt from its target, in a 2×2 design crossing site/corpus (Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center via MIMIC-IV-Note [Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV Clinical Notes Module] and University of California, San Francisco via ER-Reason) with genre (discharge summary and imaging report). Query sentences were removed from their targets before indexing to prevent verbatim overlap, notes were deduplicated after normalization, models used their recommended pooling, long documents were scored as overlapping chunks by maximum similarity, and cell sizes were matched (N=1235 per cell). Effectiveness was measured by mean reciprocal rank at 10, rank transfer by Kendall τ and selection regret, and variance by factorial decomposition (η2). Transfer, regret, and the contrastive-panel decomposition carry 95% patient-clustered bootstrap intervals. Results Among the 8 contrastive models, cross-site Kendall τ was 0.86 (95% CI 0.64-1.00) for discharge and 0.64 (95% CI 0.36-0.86) for imaging. The model×site interaction was small under every scoring choice (η2=0.005-0.029); the site/corpus main effect was negligible under best-chunk scoring (η2=0.000) but scoring-dependent (0.172 under mean-pooling). Cross-site selection regret was 0 for imaging and up to 0.033 for discharge (~10% of the destination’s best mean reciprocal rank; intervals 0-0.071). Adding 5 nonretrieval masked-language-model comparators moved the largest term to model (η2=0.874): the dominant-factor question is panel-sensitive, while the qualitative transfer conclusion was unchanged. Conclusions For known-item retrieval from clinical notes at 2 US academic medical centers, embedding-model rankings showed positive cross-site concordance, moderate for imaging and strong for discharge summaries—with intervals wide enough that direction, not magnitude, is the finding. Which factor dominates absolute effectiveness depends on the panel evaluated: primary contrastive-panel scoring favors genre, whereas adding nonretrieval comparators makes model choice dominant; so, claims about major determinants are panel-specific. Cross-site model selection incurred zero to modest performance loss. When documentation genre and retrieval configuration are matched, model-selection results from one institutional EHR corpus may be a useful starting point for another, although local confirmation remains warranted.

title: Designing the Future: Leadership and AI
container-title: Technology and Leadership Connections
48d1a912943fae642bf3d6ccadf6945742236023.abstract: This chapter explores the evolving, reciprocal relationship between leadership and augmented/artificial intelligence (AI) across individual, team, organizational, and societal levels. While we use the term AI throughout in recognition of its widespread usage, we acknowledge the growing preference for augmented intelligence – a framing advanced by leaders in human–machine teaming, such as Paul G. Kaminski (2020), which emphasizes cognitive extension and human–AI partnership. Just as leadership helped shape – and was reshaped by – the Agricultural, Industrial, and Information Ages, the emerging Age of AI demands a renewed focus on human values and moral courage. Far from a neutral tool, AI reflects the intentions of its designers and the integrity of its leaders, and in turn, transforms how we work, relate, and lead. Grounded in authentic and moral leadership theory, systems thinking, and sociotechnical design, we examine how leaders can engage AI in ways that safeguard human dignity, foster trust, and advance ethical innovation. Through a multilevel lens, we explore how AI influences self-awareness, interpersonal responsibility, team dynamics, and global leadership strategies. We extend prior work on efficacy-performance spirals to the AI context, showing how trust, learning, and adaptation can reinforce or erode across levels over time. Drawing on work published in Organizational Dynamics, this chapter also applies the TRUST, COACH, and CARES frameworks to AI leadership. As AI reshapes decision-making and connection, the defining force will not be technology itself, but the authenticity, trustworthiness, and moral imagination of those who lead it.

title: Digital Transformation 2.0: Integrating AI and Empowering People for Sustainable Growth in the Future of Work
container-title: Technology and Leadership Connections
cd295fcbb5cd4820a5d40948a004a94d7d35cbec.abstract: The digital era has reached a new inflection point, accelerated by artificial intelligence (AI) and organizations’ need to adapt to dynamic, technology-driven conditions. This chapter examines the legacy of Digital Transformation 1.0—highlighting failures and their causes—and defines the imperatives of AI-infused Digital Transformation 2.0. Drawing from relevant case studies, research, and executive interviews, it emphasizes the critical shift from episodic digitization to sustained AI-embedded digitalization. Leaders must enable systems-level transformation across people, process, and technology while aligning cultural, ethical, and operational domains. Digital Transformation 2.0 demands coordinated iterative design over monolithic strategy, requiring organizations to reimagine work as a fluid mix of tasks rather than fixed roles. Human–AI collaboration is a new reality that depends on psychological safety, AI literacy, and digital dexterity across the blended human-AI workforce. Successful transformation hinges on new leadership behaviors that elevate trust, agency, and adaptability while modeling and encouraging the use of new tools. The piece explores decentralized workforce models, the urgency of building AI-ready cultures, and a new social contract. It examines how agile frameworks, value mapping, and upskilling efforts create coherence amid complexity, making change tangible and participatory. The Future of Work is framed not as a fixed destination, but as a dynamic system requiring deliberate, ongoing leadership to combine machine capabilities with uniquely human capabilities. Ultimately, this work calls for defining or reframing organizational purpose and progress: AI can multiply what we value, but it is up to us to define what we value—and how we lead with it.

title: A Cautionary Tale: When AI Outpaces Character in Leadership Development
container-title: Technology and Leadership Connections
0b2e9c41561f67c0653a2cb28c371eb88152dc74.abstract: This chapter, A Cautionary Tale, explores the risks and unintended consequences of pursuing leadership development and organizational transformation without grounding efforts in ethical discernment, evidence-based practice, and human-centered design. Drawing from decades of experience in the military, higher education, and executive coaching, the chapter highlights how well-intentioned initiatives often falter when leaders prioritize efficiency, image, or short-term outcomes over trust, character, and sustainable growth. Through illustrative narratives and applied research, it examines how misplaced reliance on tools, trends, or unchecked authority can erode organizational culture, diminish performance, and compromise individual well-being. The cautionary perspective emphasizes that leadership is not merely the accumulation of skills or the exercise of influence but a continual process of reflection, humility, and responsibility. Practical insights are offered for leaders navigating high-pressure contexts, including the importance of aligning purpose with practice, cultivating resilience, and embedding feedback loops that elevate both performance and values. Ultimately, the chapter argues that the true cost of neglecting character in leadership is not only organizational inefficiency but also the erosion of human dignity and trust – resources far more difficult to restore than financial capital. By reframing leadership as a moral as well as strategic endeavor, A Cautionary Tale serves as both a warning and a guide for leaders committed to building organizations that endure and uplift.

title: Agents of Change: Teamwork and Collaboration with AI at the Table
container-title: Technology and Leadership Connections
dcfd8d7ff89f9b704d69b63c67897d2290b5f515.abstract: This chapter explores the transformative implications of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) technologies as a “teammate” in leading virtual and hybrid teams. The growing prevalence of GenAI tools and the shift toward remote and hybrid work create a critical need to reexamine how leaders demonstrate essential leadership competencies in these environments. Framed by discussions on GenAI as both a collaborator and a tool, this chapter considers the ethical dilemmas, pedagogical innovations, and practical strategies for integrating GenAI into team leadership. Building on the authors’ previous work in exploring leadership competencies for leading at the virtual table, it investigates how GenAI reshapes trust, collaboration, and productivity in diverse teams while balancing human agency and technological capabilities. Through critical questions, a case study reflection, and practical takeaways, the chapter offers a roadmap for fostering GenAI literacy (LeaderAIcy), managing ethical and technical considerations, and leveraging GenAI for meaningful leadership and teamwork in global, hybrid contexts.

title: Using AI Tools for Leader Development and Assessing Competencies
container-title: Technology and Leadership Connections
6670b996a20df16f557191ac8831733fc9abb418.abstract: This chapter explores how the United States Air Force (USAF) leader development course (LDC) used artificial intelligence (AI)/sentiment analysis (SA) for leader development and assessing leader development competencies that support learning objectives and course outcomes. A narrative format is first used to describe the engaged practice with key stakeholders and the staged approach process that underlaid the development of how innovation is driving change for leaders, assessing performance specific to selected competencies in mixed reality scenarios, and offering ways of strengthening leader development. A five-phased qualitative structure is used along with content analysis, design thinking, and a grounded theory approach. After coding data using thematic analysis from phases 1 to 4, a grounded theory approach is used to better understand the findings and discoveries with literature related to innovation development, AI technology associated with immersive learning environments, design thinking and change, performance and competency assessment, and leader development. A new theory (AI-augmented leader development theory) and a new model, emotionally tuned competency assessment model (ECAM), emerged as well as emphasis on the power of using dialogic development in virtual contexts to train, assess, and develop leaders. Theoretical and practical implications, as well as recommendations are provided for improving how AI tools can be used for leader development.

title: AI as a Catalyst for Change: Transforming Human Resources in Educational Institutions
container-title: Technology and Leadership Connections
93d2ee78452d2d36780fedbbf08d870e031b50d3.abstract: This chapter delves into the integration of artificial intelligence (AI) and the human resources (HR) function within a public school district, offering a detailed case study of its implementation. It examines how AI tools were leveraged to streamline recruitment, enhance employee engagement, and support data-driven decision-making. The chapter highlights key challenges and opportunities, focusing on trust building and change management strategies essential for the successful adoption of AI tools. Ethical considerations are explored, including the need to mitigate algorithmic bias, ensure fairness in automated processes, and uphold data privacy and security standards. Recommendations emphasize the importance of transparent communication, reengaging employees through inclusive practices, and building trust in AI systems while reskilling and upskilling employees. By combining practical insights with emerging trends in digital transformation, this chapter provides a roadmap for educational leaders and HR professionals seeking to responsibly leverage AI in their organizations.

title: Leading Inclusively: Universal Design Principles in the Age of AI
container-title: Technology and Leadership Connections
ce20000e654b8aeff35b1155111a8b38d1312b8b.abstract: Modern organizational leaders increasingly encounter artificial intelligence (AI) technologies in their workplaces, creating both opportunities and challenges for inclusive leadership. This chapter introduces Universal Design for Learning (UDL) as a framework for navigating these technological changes while maintaining human-centered approaches to inclusion. UDL’s three core principles – multiple means of representation, engagement, and action/expression – provide leaders with practical strategies for creating flexible workplace systems that benefit all employees. When thoughtfully implemented, AI technologies can support these principles through personalized learning experiences, enhanced accessibility features, and improved communication tools. However, the chapter cautions leaders to ensure that technology is amplifying rather than replacing human judgment and cultural competence. The chapter addresses critical considerations for leaders, including the risks of algorithmic bias, the limitations of automated solutions in complex interpersonal situations, and the importance of maintaining employee agency and choice. It examines common implementation barriers – from cost concerns to misconceptions about technology as a cure-all for inclusion challenges – while demonstrating that UDL principles require minimal investment and generate significant returns. Through examination of both opportunities and pitfalls, leaders learn to distinguish between technological applications that enhance inclusion and those that may inadvertently create barriers. The chapter provides actionable guidance for implementing UDL principles in technology-enhanced environments, positioning inclusive leadership capabilities as essential competencies for organizational success regardless of technological context.

title: Generative AI Powered by Large Language Models for Leadership Development: Between Epistemic Responsibility and the Future of Innovation
container-title: Technology and Leadership Connections
2befe576d22df3abb8f03a51478516f11ce0d40c.abstract: This chapter examines language-based generative AI, particularly large language models (LLMs), as active epistemic agents in leadership development. Moving beyond their perceived neutrality, the authors argue that LLMs serve as mirrors of dominant assumptions, co-constructors of leadership meaning, and framing devices of legitimate knowledge. The sources highlight how these systems reinforce prevailing Euro-American managerial ideals, often marginalizing diverse leadership paradigms such as Indigenous, collectivist, or spiritual frameworks, thereby amplifying structural and cultural biases. Through epistemic feedback loops and personalization, LLMs can subtly shape leadership identity and constrain developmental horizons, leading to adaptive standardization or performative conformity. The chapter emphasizes the critical need for epistemic responsibility in innovation leadership, advocating for leaders to interrogate system framings, reflect on their influence, and cultivate design awareness. This involves fostering inclusive data practices, participatory design methodologies, and culturally responsive AI governance to ensure AI-mediated innovation ecosystems are just, inclusive, and reflect pluralistic worldviews. Ultimately, the chapter calls for leaders to reclaim framing power and engage AI dialogically to foster an innovation leadership that is reflexive, ethically grounded, and attuned to human complexities.

title: <b>Socio-Economic Determinants of Construction Project Performance and Project Administration in the United Arab Emirates</b>
container-title: Elicit Journal of Economics and Management Studies
445e6e73cea488bf5db55e4efb60d2ad3f0f93a4.abstract: Purpose: This study examines the direct effects of external socio-economic factors on project administration andproject performance (time, cost, and quality) within the UAE construction sector.Methodology: Data were collected from 384 construction stakeholders via a structured questionnaire andevaluated using multiple regression and correlation analyses.Results: Socio-economic factors significantly predicted project performance, explaining 41.7% of the variance inproject time, 48.0% in cost, and 54.6% in quality. Inflation and labour availability significantly influenced projecttime, while inflation, regulatory environment, and labour availability affected cost. Economic stability was the solepredictor of quality and showed the strongest correlation with project administration (r = 0.585–0.654).Novelty and contribution: This research fills a critical gap by empirically quantifying the direct, measurableimpact of macro-level external factors on internal administrative success and specific project performanceoutcomes in the UAE.Social and Practical Implications: Practitioners must integrate macroeconomic indicators into early planning,budgeting, and workforce management. Socially, addressing these factors secures industry employment stabilityand prevents costly infrastructure delays.

title: A multi-head attention-based deep learning method for condition monitoring in rotating machinery diagnostics using RVMD-FNDNLP feature preprocessing
container-title: Measurement Science and Technology
3e50511054072f86dbc6d06b61a44cf07f0cac2c.abstract: Abstract Rotating machinery condition monitoring is essential for reliable fault detection and maintenance decision-making in industrial systems. However, nonstationary bearing vibration measurements often produce statistical feature representations with nonlinear coupling, redundancy, and class overlap, thereby limiting diagnostic reliability. In addition, conventional feature extraction and dimensionality reduction methods often suffer from feature redundancy and limited class separability. To address these issues, this paper proposes a bearing condition-monitoring method based on regularized variational mode decomposition (RVMD) and farthest-nearest distance-based neighborhood and locality projections (FNDNLP). By incorporating a regularization strategy into variational mode decomposition, RVMD improves decomposition efficiency and enhances fault-relevant modal information. Multiple statistical features are then extracted from the selected informative modes to construct a high-dimensional monitoring feature set. Subsequently, FNDNLP learns a supervised low-dimensional projection from the training data to reduce redundant and coupled information while improving intraclass compactness and interclass separability. Finally, a temporal convolutional network with multi-head attention (TCN-MHA) models dependencies in the projected representation. The framework is evaluated on the Case Western Reserve University (CWRU) and HUST bearing platforms using complete-pipeline comparisons, controlled classifier evaluations, reduced-dimension sensitivity analysis, and component-wise ablation. It achieves mean test accuracies of 98.89± 0.03% and 98.10± 0.42% on CWRU and HUST, respectively. The results support the effectiveness of the integrated framework under the evaluated datasets and conditions.

title: Long-haul L + S-band WDM transmission over a 1052-km dispersion-shifted fiber link with inter-band nonlinearity management
container-title: Optics Continuum
831711de7b1294b6b006076b157a09fb6c359d87.abstract: We demonstrated long-haul inline-amplified wavelength-division-multiplexing (WDM) transmissions with 10.8-THz signal bandwidth in the L and S bands over a 75.2-km-span dispersion-shifted fiber (DSF) link. In L + S-band DSF transmission, where the signal is allocated on both sides of the zero-dispersion wavelength, some S-band channels and L-band channels can become group-velocity matched, leading to strong inter-band Kerr nonlinear interactions. In addition, the edge-to-edge bandwidth of the L + S-band WDM signal exceeds the peak Raman-shift frequency in the silica-core fibers, resulting in significant power transfer due to inter-channel stimulated Raman scattering (ISRS). We investigated the feasibility of L + S-band long-haul coherent transmissions over DSF links by optimizing the launch power for each band. We also evaluated a band-wise bidirectional transmission configuration in which the S-band and L-band signals propagate in opposite directions to avoid inter-band phase matching. Highly efficient parametric waveband converters based on periodically poled lithium niobate waveguides were employed for the generation, reception, and amplification of the S-band signals. By using 96-Gbaud probabilistically constellation-shaped 16QAM signals, we achieved a 1052-km transmission with a net capacity of 43.2 Tbps (400 Gbps/ch.) in the unidirectional configuration and of 49.2 Tbps (400 Gbps/ch. in the S band, 500 Gbps/ch. in the L band) in the bidirectional configuration. Gaussian-noise-model-based analysis further revealed that the signal quality degradation observed in the L band for the unidirectional configuration originated from comparable contributions of inter-band cross-phase modulation and four-wave mixing interference.

title: Evaluation of Conventional and Alternative Products for Management of Grapevine Powdery Mildew in San Diego County, California
container-title: Plant Health Progress
cc869b2510f5c40d2f1757d7851ac007c96e7649.abstract: Powdery mildew, caused by Erysiphe necator , is one of the most economically important diseases of grapevine worldwide, reducing both fruit yield and quality. This study evaluated the efficacy of experimental, biological, and conventional treatments for managing grape powdery mildew. A field trial was conducted during 2025 in an established commercial Vitis vinifera ‘Picpoul Blanc’ vineyard located in the San Pasqual Valley agricultural region of San Diego County, California. Treatments were assessed for their ability to reduce powdery mildew incidence and severity on grape clusters. The results provide information on the relative performance of registered and experimental products and will support the development of effective powdery mildew management programs for grape growers in coastal California.

title: Psychosocial Correlates of AI Chatbot Use for Emotional Support Among Young Adults: Cross-Sectional Study
container-title: JMIR Mental Health
1e08cf411f17f99e1e58af3328f64bf433310da2.abstract: Background Generative AI chatbots are increasingly used for mental health–related purposes, yet little is known about the factors associated with such use or AI chatbot dependence. Objective This study examined factors associated with young adults’ use of AI chatbots for emotional self-disclosure and mental health–related support, as well as the associations between AI chatbot use and dependence. Methods A cross-sectional online survey of individuals aged 18 to 29 years was conducted in Japan. Self-report measures assessed psychosocial factors (self-esteem and loneliness), mental health symptoms (anxiety and depression), AI chatbot use (emotional self-disclosure and mental health–related support), and AI chatbot dependence (emotional dependence and social anxiety–related dependence). Results Of 820 participants, 381 (46.5%) reported using AI chatbots for emotional self-disclosure at least once in the past month, including 65 (7.9%) who reported doing so every day or almost every day. In addition, 336 (41%) reported using AI chatbots for mental health–related support, including 53 (6.5%) who reported doing so every day or almost every day. Anxiety and depressive symptoms were combined into a composite measure of mental health symptoms because they are highly correlated. Multivariable logistic regression showed that greater mental health symptom severity, but not self-esteem or loneliness, was associated with both emotional self-disclosure (odds ratio [OR] 2.23, 95% CI 1.85-2.69; P<.001) and mental health–related support (OR 2.42, 95% CI 2.01-2.94; P<.001). Among emotional self-disclosure users (n=381), the frequency of emotional self-disclosure was positively associated with emotional dependence (β=0.334; P<.001) and social anxiety–related dependence (β=0.307; P<.001). Path analyses indicated that a model specifying psychosocial factors and mental health symptoms as antecedent variables to AI chatbot use and dependence fit the data better than an alternative model specifying AI chatbot use and dependence as the antecedent variables (comparative fit index [CFI]=0.994 vs 0.583; root mean square error of approximation [RMSEA]=0.033 vs 0.293). In this model, lower self-esteem and greater loneliness were associated with more severe mental health symptoms, which, in turn, were associated with greater AI chatbot dependence, primarily through direct pathways and, to a lesser extent, through more frequent emotional self-disclosure. Among emotional self-disclosure users, loneliness was the only significant psychosocial correlate of emotional dependence (F1,369=7.78; P=.006). Conclusions Emotional engagement with AI chatbots was common in this sample of young adults in Japan. Findings suggest that young adults experiencing mental health symptoms may be more likely to use AI chatbots for emotional self-disclosure and mental health–related support, while loneliness may be particularly relevant to emotional dependence among users. These findings highlight the need to understand AI chatbot use not only as a technological behavior but also as part of young adults’ broader emotional and help-seeking landscape.

title: Navigating cross-cultural dynamics in European multinational firms: How acculturation strategies influence African indigenous employee outcomes
container-title: South African Journal of Business Management
a5d021f4072859124179322c33344561138bca52.abstract: Purpose: This research examines how acculturation strategies impact employee restiveness, internal legitimacy and job satisfaction among local workers in European multinational firms in Africa. Design/methodology/approach: Utilising a quantitative research design, the study uses a structured questionnaire to draw data from 515 indigenous employees in German-owned and French-owned multinational firms. The hypothesis was tested using structural equation modelling. Findings/results: Contrary to expectations, the results suggest that integration strategy significantly addresses employee restiveness, internal legitimacy and job satisfaction in German-owned and French-owned multinational firms in Nigeria. Conversely, assimilation, separation and marginalisation acculturation strategies were found to have insignificant influence on internal legitimacy, employee restiveness and job satisfaction among the employees. Practical implications: The outcomes of this study will enable managers to understand the appropriate acculturation strategy that can help foreign firms to gain internal legitimacy and address employee restiveness and job satisfaction in Africa. The findings will also motivate foreign firms to provide support to local employees to adopt the beneficial acculturation strategy for the overall benefit of the organisation and the employees. Originality/value: This study makes two unique contributions to management literature. Firstly, this study is the first to provide insights into how integration strategies relate to employee restiveness for sustainable harmonious relationships in multinational firms in Africa. Research has shown that Nigerian work environments are characterised by employee restiveness. Secondly, providing insights into how each of the four dimensions of acculturation strategies relate to the realisation of firms’ internal legitimacy enriches the literature, as it is pointed out that researchers mainly focus on external legitimacy while neglecting the internal legitimacy perspective.

title: Understanding and managing the human side of acquisitions
container-title: SA Journal of Human Resource Management
91ef82a7db8a31ba029b7bec85da6b47bbebf993.abstract: Orientation: The persistently high failure rate of mergers and acquisitions (M&As) remains a major concern for economic growth and corporate development. Many failures stem from poorly managed people transitions, leading to severe negative social consequences for employees, families and communities. Effective human resource management is essential to minimise these outcomes. Research purpose: This study identifies specific challenges faced by human resource (HR) specialists and managers during people transfers in acquisitions, critically evaluates existing scholarly frameworks and proposes a strategic model for successful human transitions. Motivation for the study: Acquisition research typically lacks longitudinal, insider perspectives, yielding fragmented insights. This work fills that gap by providing a rare, in-depth insider view of human dynamics in M&A processes. Research approach/design and method: Using a qualitative auto-ethnographic approach, the study draws on nine detailed vignettes from Swart’s experiences as both an acquirer and an acquiree, supplemented by field notes, minutes and emails. Two additional cases were corroborated through interviews and documents. Critical event analysis identified participant themes, which were synthesised with scholarly constructs from the organisation, management, social change, commerce and legal literatures. Analytic induction and abduction developed and supported the Human Acquisition Transition model (HAT1+). Main findings: The HAT1+ model structures acquisitions into distinct phases (‘waves’) and pinpoints critical success factors within and beyond the formal process, enhancing human transition planning. Practical/managerial implications: HAT1+ provides managers and HR professionals with a practical framework to improve integration, employee engagement and the overall transition success. Contribution/value-add: Theory: Advances auto-ethnographic methods in business research and harmonises commercial, legal and human aspects of acquisitions. Practice: Delivers a validated process model with clear guidelines and critical success traits across pre-transition, transition and post-transition phases, promoting humane management and reducing negative impacts on individuals, families and communities.

title: Fourth Industrial Revolution readiness among Sector Education and Training Authority training providers in South Africa’s maritime transport sector: Needs, challenges and Broad-Based Black Economic Empowerment alignment
container-title: Journal of Transport and Supply Chain Management
b3458d534ac96bf356fbe4de22988936cbe01206.abstract: Background: The Fourth Industrial Revolution (4IR) is fundamentally transforming global maritime logistics, yet the preparedness of South Africa’s skills development ecosystem remains under-researched. Objectives: As the Sector Education and Training Authority (SETA) system undergoes significant reform, understanding the readiness of accredited training providers is critical for national competitiveness. Method: A convergent mixed-methods design was employed, in which quantitative and qualitative data were collected concurrently via a single Google Forms survey instrument administered to 254 SETA-accredited providers. Closed-ended items yielded quantitative data analysed through descriptive statistics, while open-ended responses were subjected to thematic analysis. Both data strands were analysed independently and then integrated to develop a comprehensive understanding of 4IR readiness. Results: Findings reveal a significant readiness gap: 53.1% of providers allocate less than 5% of their budget to 4IR initiatives, and 43.6% feel unprepared for delivery. While artificial intelligence awareness is high (81.1%), adoption is low, with 38.7% utilising no 4IR technologies in curriculum delivery. Furthermore, 74.1% lack concrete Broad-Based Black Economic Empowerment strategies for equitable 4IR access. Conclusion: The SETA ecosystem faces systemic inertia driven by prohibitive costs, slow accreditation processes and a disconnect from labour market demands. Urgent intervention is required to prevent a new digital divide in South African skills development. Contribution: This study provides the inaugural empirical assessment of 4IR readiness among South African SETA providers. It offers actionable recommendations, including the establishment of a ring-fenced 4IR Transformation Fund and modernised accreditation reforms.

title: Credibility displacement in algorithmic financial reporting: a critical review of AI, disclosure credibility and capital-market consequences
container-title: Journal of Accounting Literature
18243e89dcb911f6253cee203ff5a4e80cabeb04.abstract: Purpose This review examines how financial-reporting credibility is shaped when algorithmic systems enter the reporting chain. It asks where credibility is produced, tested and understood when artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning, large language models, eXtensible Business Reporting Language (XBRL) analytics and related tools affect reporting information. Design/methodology/approach The paper combines a search and screening procedure informed by the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) with a concept-centric synthesis. The evidence base comprises a 226-paper curated core and a 144-paper close-synthesis subset. Sensitivity analyses re-examine the 39-record outlet boundary and the close-synthesis threshold. Findings The evidence remains dispersed across research on textual disclosure and natural language processing (NLP), audit analytics and assurance, structured reporting using XBRL, market interpretation, accounting information systems (AIS) implementation and AI governance. Across these streams, algorithms can improve reporting processes but may also alter the grounds on which reporting assertions are accepted. We describe the latter possibility as credibility displacement: model-related output, provenance or validation partly substitutes for scrutiny of the underlying assertion or for identifiable professional and institutional safeguards. Originality/value The review defines algorithmic financial reporting as a reporting-chain phenomenon rather than a general label for technology adoption. It distinguishes four sites: preparation, assurance, machine-readable presentation and algorithmic interpretation. Governance operates across these sites as a cross-cutting condition, making the proposed displacement mechanism more focused and empirically testable.

title: The effects of work overload on emotional exhaustion among nurses: serial mediation of job stress and depression
container-title: Journal of Health Organization and Management
31ee4733a3d18e634e14ab44584707ba83b8973b.abstract: Purpose This study examines the relationship between work overload and emotional exhaustion among nurses. Specifically, the study investigates the serial mediating effect of job stress and depression on the relationship between work overload and emotional exhaustion. Design/methodology/approach Data were gathered between October 2025 and January 2026 through an online and face-to-face cross-sectional survey of 613 nurses working in two state hospitals in Türkiye. Sequential mediating effects were analyzed using the Statistical Package for the Social Sciences PROCESS macro (Model 6). Findings The findings showed that work overload is positively related to emotional exhaustion. Furthermore, the results revealed that job stress and depression sequentially mediate the relationship between work overload and emotional exhaustion. Originality/value This research offers a clearer understanding of the potential psychological mechanisms underlying the relationship between work overload and emotional exhaustion among nurses. It also extends the literature by informing the development of interventions aimed at alleviating job stress and reducing depression levels among nurses in the healthcare sector. In particular, primary caregivers and hospital administrations responsible for nurses should develop work overload-conscious, stress-reducing, and mental health-supporting methods to improve nurse well-being and enhance the quality and safety of patient care.

title: How does home region focus boost international performance for INVs in the international post-entry phase? The mediating role of international opportunity-pursuing orientation
container-title: International Marketing Review
4b2d6282106b98d5a87e71d654cdd076a3a183bc.abstract: Purpose This study aims to improve our understanding of international opportunity pursuing orientation (IOO) through which home region focus affects international performance. Design/methodology/approach The authors collected a sample of 360 International New Ventures (INVs) in the international post-entry phase from a two-wave survey in China. They tested the mediating effects of IOOs using structural equation modeling. Findings Both existing and envisaged IOOs are positively associated with international performance. Home region focus is positively related to existing IOO but negatively related to envisaged IOO. Existing and envisaged IOOs play a significant mediating role between home region focus and international performance. Research limitations/implications This study advances the regionalization hypothesis literature and international entrepreneurship perspective by introducing two new mediators, existing and envisaged IOOs, to link home region focus to international performance. Practical implications Managers should foster existing (envisaged) IOO to transform high (low) home region focus into superior international performance. Policymakers should help firms develop IOOs by organizing managers to visit abroad and formulating the function of embassies and consulates to collect foreign information. Originality/value While home region focus is essential for performance, there is a dearth of research explaining the underlying mechanisms through which home region focus affects performance. IOO is a novel antecedent of international performance among INVs at the international post-entry stage.

title: From western frameworks to epistemically plural governance: a knowledge governance typology for regenerative agricultural supply chains in Africa
container-title: The International Journal of Logistics Management
8b4d588cdf0c490da2eb18eec185f180eaa1c88b.abstract: Purpose The paper develops a knowledge governance model for regenerative agricultural supply chains in Africa. Existing frameworks assume formal institutions, codified scientific knowledge, and reliable digital infrastructure. African settings, where indigenous ecological norms serve as protective ecological infrastructure operating near irreversibility thresholds, require a different starting point. Design/methodology/approach The paper follows a three-stage theory-building approach. Stage 1 reviews existing knowledge governance models and their limits in African settings. Stage 2 draws on published African case studies to specify recurring challenges. Stage 3 combines typological and prescriptive theorising to produce a 2 × 2 matrix of governance contexts, paired with if-then guidance. Findings The model organises knowledge governance contexts along two dimensions: (1) epistemic-cultural complexity, the challenge of integrating multiple knowledge traditions while respecting culturally specific norms around authority, access and sharing and (2) institutional-infrastructural risk, the vulnerabilities arising where formal governance infrastructure is absent or weak. Crossing them yields four archetypes: Ubuntu-grounded knowledge platforms, community-embedded knowledge stewardship, epistemically just knowledge partnerships and resilient knowledge networks, each with design rules for sharing norms, governance structures, justice safeguards and coordination mechanisms. Originality/value The paper makes three contributions. It introduces epistemic-cultural complexity as a core knowledge governance dimension in African supply chains; it reconceptualises knowledge polycentrism through Ubuntu, Ujamaa and Ọ̀mọ̀lúwabí while integrating the protective-ecological function of indigenous norms, showing that knowledge governance and ecological protection form a single coordinated problem; and it specifies a prescriptive typology assigning differentiated catalytic responsibilities to downstream supply chain actors.

title: Leading the (supply) chain: a literature review, framework and research agenda
container-title: The International Journal of Logistics Management
f64163e26b93ed9dbd250ab99a84f700b69e6d11.abstract: Purpose Leaders in supply chain management have received considerable scholarly attention, but the dispersed literature lacks comprehensive conceptualization and theorization. Understanding supply chain leadership requires tracing the full pathway through which leaders' characteristics and behaviors influence followers and outcomes across multiple levels. We develop a leadership meta process model that maps these pathways, offering an integrative framework for how leaders exert influence across the supply chain. Design/methodology/approach The study draws on a systematic literature review of 211 articles selected at the intersection of leadership and supply chain management. The sample encompasses over 23,600 respondents plus secondary data on 1,772 firms. Findings Research on leader behaviors dominates, yet the underlying mechanisms through which leaders actually influence followers and create supply chain outcomes remain largely a black box. Future research opportunities include examining how leaders influence (external) followers, developing dyadic designs that capture (cross-boundary) leadership dynamics and investigating leadership processes specific to the supply chain management context through more qualitative, mixed-method and theory-building approaches. Practical implications By modeling the entire process through which supply chain leaders shape follower behavior and multilevel outcomes, the framework helps practitioners recruit and educators develop supply chain leaders, and it clarifies how these leaders influence the performance of their internal and external organizations. Originality/value Despite growing interest in supply chain leaders, the field remains theoretically fragmented and largely confined to isolated relationships. This review reframes supply chain leadership as a multifaceted, context-specific phenomenon, emphasizing the need to study the individuals leading the supply chain.

title: Beyond grades to learning enhancement: development, implementation and evaluation of a conversational AI agent in medical education
container-title: Education + Training
084b6523ad822ed6a663bd21d0cf5dfd788d527b.abstract: Purpose The integration of conversational artificial intelligence (AI) in medical education shows promise but lacks empirical evidence of effectiveness. This study evaluated a customized generative pre-trained transformer (GPT)-4-based conversational agent designed explicitly for a pharmacology block in undergraduate medical education. Design/methodology/approach A mixed-methods sequential explanatory design was employed in a four-week elective pharmacology block at the College of Medicine, Sulaiman Al-Rajhi University. Phase 1 involved a cross-sectional survey of enrolled students (n = 58) who used the AI tool, with a comparative analysis of their academic performance against historical cohorts without access to AI (2022–2023: n = 33; 2023–2024: n = 37). Academic performance was measured through mid-block quizzes, end-of-block examinations, and total block score. Phase 2 comprised semi-structured interviews (n = 9), transcribed and analyzed thematically. Findings The survey response rate was 89.6% (52/58), and 98.1% (51/52) reported using the tool. Among users, 74.5% engaged with the GPT tool daily. Students reported exceptionally high satisfaction: 92.2% found it more effective than traditional methods, 94.1% felt it made learning more engaging, and the likelihood of recommending it averaged 4.65 ± 0.73 (on a 5-point scale). Frequency of use was significantly associated with perceived improvement in learning (χ2 = 15.84, p &lt; 0.05). Academic performance showed marginal, non-significant improvements: total scores increased by 2.5% (75.52 vs. 77.40, p &gt; 0.05), with pass rates improving from 92.9% to 98.3% (p &gt; 0.05). Qualitative analysis revealed six themes: learning support and academic enhancement; efficiency and accessibility; GPT's supplementary role in learning; perceived strengths and unique features; limitations and challenges; and suggestions for improvement. Originality/value The disconnect between exceptional user engagement and minimal performance improvements challenges traditional evaluation paradigms. While conversational AI may not directly enhance examination scores, students' accounts suggest it may support metacognitive development, reduce cognitive load, and foster critical-thinking skills essential for modern medical practice, thereby necessitating multidimensional assessment frameworks.

title: Walk the talk: how procurement professionals' interpretations shape social sustainability cascading
container-title: International Journal of Operations & Production Management
bafe481096f089c32bd0ffb8b5fde420cffa1a8c.abstract: Purpose Procurement professionals shape how firms translate their commitments to social sustainability into supplier-facing governance, which can vary markedly, even within the same firm. This study explains this variation by theorizing how procurement professionals interpret their role and translate engagement with suppliers into governance practices. Design/methodology/approach The study draws on constructivist grounded theory and interviews with 27 professionals across organizational contexts. The analysis combines iterative coding, constant comparison, theoretical sampling, and abductive engagement with sensitizing literature. Findings The study develops a process model that explains cascading depth from a people-centric perspective. The interviewed procurement professionals differed on whether they construed their remit to include social sustainability, whether supplier-facing action appeared worth pursuing, and whether more improvement-oriented engagement appeared feasible. This situated judgment shaped whether cascading is enacted predominantly through procedural compliance or through more generative supplier-facing practice. Prospective paradoxical sensemaking helped explain how more generative supplier-facing responses could remain actionable under competing commercial demands, as professionals saw anticipated social and commercial consequences as relevant to their judgment in the present. Originality/value The study reframes cascading depth as a matter of how procurement professionals enact governance mechanisms. It specifies interpretive and relational conditions that remain underexplored in the literature on sustainable behavioral supply chain management. It extends paradoxical sensemaking research on how tensions are framed to include how more generative responses may be established and sustained in practice.

title: Psychological contract breach and diminished organisational citizenship behaviour: the mediation of employee knowledge hiding
container-title: Management Decision
14f2842228118067cb6f1adbfe2df543c8d79d2f.abstract: Purpose This paper aims to examine the relationship between psychological contract breach and diminished organisational citizenship behaviour in Southern Nigeria through the mediation of knowledge hiding. Design/methodology/approach The design was a cross-sectional survey. A structured questionnaire served as the instrument for data collection from the respondents. The authors constructed and validated the research instrument. The authors also tested the instrument's reliability. The study used structural equation modelling to analyse the data with a specific focus on the path diagram technique. Findings The results show that an organisation's breach of the relational psychological contract significantly influences employees' knowledge hiding behaviour; employee knowledge hiding behaviour significantly stimulates diminished organisational citizenship behaviour. In addition, employee knowledge hiding significantly mediates the relationship between psychological contract breach (relational, implicit, balanced) and diminished organisational citizenship behaviour. Research limitations/implications A major limitation of the study is the use of a cross-sectional survey design, which is constrained for inferring causality. Nevertheless, the significance or non-significance of the associations between variables in a cross-sectional design is instructive about the hypothesised relationships. Practical implications Strategic managers will be sensitised to the consequences of breaching psychological contracts, especially knowledge hiding and the attendant diminished organisational citizenship behaviours, which can constrain organisations' capacity to optimise their value. This requires that measures be implemented to reduce the perception of breaches. Specifically, university administrators and policymakers should manage the psychological contract between the institution and the employees by reciprocating their efforts. This can be achieved by prioritising employee interests and welfare through regular promotion of workers, provision of fringe benefits and conducive working conditions, among others. Social implications Increased organisational citizenship behaviour associated with honouring psychological contracts will reduce knowledge-hiding behaviour, increase knowledge-sharing behaviour, contribute to organisational effectiveness and the achievement of set goals. For universities, this will increase their capacity to produce a skilled workforce, fuel economic innovation in the process through research and provide vital community services. In the final analysis, it will lead to job creation. Originality/value This study has contributed significantly to knowledge in management and social sciences by revealing that psychological contract breach diminishes organisational citizenship behaviour in Nigerian Universities. This occurs through the mediation of knowledge hiding. Most importantly, the study extends the frontiers of social exchange theory by testing it in new contexts and boundaries. By showing that employees reciprocate psychological contract breach through knowledge hiding, the study expands the frontiers of social exchange theory. By applying the theory to Nigeria, the study achieves boundary spanning.

title: Digital transformation of service ecosystems: an orchestration perspective
container-title: International Journal of Operations & Production Management
eb7b6e6dcc8a65dc9580ff8e1f394fd4bfb6fc0f.abstract: Purpose This study investigates how digital transformation unfolds within logistics service ecosystems and how inter-actor operational connections and coordinating roles change over time from an orchestration perspective. Design/methodology/approach The authors conducted a case study of three international inland ports in China. Data were triangulated through interviews, observations and documents to capture ecosystem-level orchestration practices and transformation evolution. Findings The authors developed a process model that identifies three evolutionary stages of the digital transformation of service ecosystems: developing digital connectivity, tapping digital service potential and co-creating digital value. The model demonstrates how actors employ resource and network orchestration at each stage. The analysis reveals how these two forms of orchestration interact and how orchestration dynamics change over time. Originality/value This study shifts the focus of digital transformation research from a few focal firms to service ecosystems overall. It theorizes a three-stage transformation process, reveals the evolving interplay between resource and network orchestration, shows that different actors can assume orchestration leadership, and provides actionable recommendations for managers seeking to digitally transform logistics and supply chain service ecosystems.

title: When bots act like us: the role of social media accounts' human-likeness in opinion polarization
container-title: Industrial Management & Data Systems
a76686e22912eafbf71c24172f1595c5cb0cee09.abstract: Purpose As social bots penetrate social media, social media accounts with different human-likeness interact with each other, with opinion polarization as one of the results. This study investigates the impact of human-likeness of social media accounts on opinion polarization on social media. Design/methodology/approach Drawing on the social validation principle and its intersections with the optimal distinctiveness theory as the theoretical foundation, this study applies empirical analysis with a dataset of 2,034,201 replies from Weibo to examine the proposed model. Findings An inverted U-shaped relationship between human-likeness of social media accounts and opinion polarization in replies mediated by their social validation and moderated by information valence. Originality/value Our findings advance understanding of human–bot interaction dynamics, highlighting how bot human-likeness relates to opinion polarization at the community level. This study provides actionable measures for stakeholders: bot developers should carefully calibrate human-likeness, platforms should implement graded indicators on human-likeness of social media accounts and users must critically evaluate information sources to mitigate polarization.

title: Female leadership and business results: the moderating effect of family businesses
container-title: European Journal of Management and Business Economics
a4d873e5b96811c7fcb83d67462db25f7ce612c8.abstract: Purpose Given the disparity of results in the literature on female business leadership, this study aims to deepen the existing debate by offering an enriching proposal on this concept. We focus both on previous contributions to the literature and on the inclusion of contextual factors, such as the family business environment, to develop our proposal. Design/methodology/approach The article adopts a quantitative approach using panel data to analyse data collected from 162 large companies between 2007 and 2019. Findings The effectiveness of female business leadership increases when women participate in more than one of the company's corporate governance actors, with the family context being more conducive to achieving this female business leadership. Originality/value Our work takes a step further by delving deeper into female business leadership, arguing that it should not only involve the possibility of participating in and influencing business decision-making, but also generate the capacity for this participation to influence others and, therefore, the orientation of the company.

title: AI Integration in Automotive Packaging Engineering for Multi-Constraint Component Optimization
container-title: International Journal of Sustainability and Innovation in Engineering
31c5e065257fd8076186c66a65576fe16420241c.abstract: This paper introduces a framework for the packaging of components in a vehicle's threedimensional structure that is grounded in evidence and reproducible when taking advantage of the potential of artificial intelligence (AI) tools. The public OSU–Honda CarHoods10k dataset provides over 10,000 3D hood-frame designs based on 109 parameterized designs, along with design parameters and finite element (FE) performance data. The data package is about 45.66 GB, including design parameters and finite-element (FE) performance data. This dataset is not a multi-component vehicle-layout dataset and can't be used for a complete validation of a vehicle packaging optimizer: thermal, service access, or assembly data of the vehicle are not available at the component level. The studies of published adjacent work have shown that an improved solution with 3 times less computational budget could be offered, a result specific to this study but not predicted for automotive packaging. The proposed framework formalizes the placement variables, geometric constraints, engineering constraints, a model of screening by an artificial neural network (ANN), and a genetic search by NSGA- II, where the two objectives change. It also defines a controlled validation protocol to manual and rule-based baselines. There are no new vehicle-program performance gains since no proprietary vehicle-program layout dataset, executable code, or experimental logs for auditing were provided. The applicable vehicle-program specifications and relevant standards should supply acceptance limits.

title: Nitrosyl coordination compounds: a comprehensive review of synthetic strategies, bonding elucidation, spectroscopic diagnostics, and computational intelligence from DFT to machine learning and generative AI
container-title: Reviews in Inorganic Chemistry
fb44627afb7e4316f5fdce03a3394158793f96a4.abstract: Abstract Nitrosyl coordination compounds have undergone a remarkable evolution from Priestley’s serendipitous discovery of nitric oxide to their current standing as versatile molecular platforms at the forefront of modern coordination chemistry, bioinorganic signaling, catalysis, and materials science. This comprehensive review presents an integrated and forward-looking examination of metal–nitrosyl chemistry that systematically bridges classical synthetic methodologies, fundamental bonding paradigms, advanced spectroscopic diagnostics, and cutting-edge computational intelligence. The synthetic landscape is critically surveyed as a decision-oriented framework encompassing direct NO gas reactions, nitrosonium salts, hydroxylamine-mediated protocols, nitrite-based routes, coordinated NO transfer strategies, and emerging green chemistry approaches, with particular emphasis on method selection criteria based on metal identity, ligand sensitivity, scalability, and sustainability imperatives. The bonding narrative is rigorously dissected through the classical lenses of valence-bond theory and molecular orbital analysis, culminating in the modern DFT-based understanding that has revolutionized our comprehension of the elusive M−NO interaction; the linear–bent dichotomy, elegantly captured by the Enemark–Feltham formalism, is established as a predictive tool for rationalizing electron counting, donor capacity, and reactivity patterns, while the non-innocent behaviour of NO-manifesting as valence tautomerism, electron-sink functionality, and dynamic geometric isomerism, is underscored as a fundamental property underpinning catalytic and signalling functions. Spectroscopic characterisation is presented as an integrated diagnostic toolkit wherein complementary techniques, including IR and Raman vibrational spectroscopy, UV–Vis–NIR electronic spectroscopy, electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR), 15 N nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR), X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), and Mössbauer spectroscopy, collectively resolve structural, electronic, and magnetic ambiguities through a logically tiered workflow. A distinctive and transformative feature of this review is the extensive coverage of computational intelligence paradigms that have reshaped nitrosyl chemistry: density functional theory (DFT) and time-dependent DFT (TD-DFT) for accurate geometry optimization, vibrational prediction, spectral simulation, and mechanistic elucidation; machine learning algorithms including random forests, support vector machines, XGBoost, and Gaussian processes for rapid high-throughput property prediction of ν (NO) frequencies, M−N bond lengths, M–N–O bond angles, and magnetic properties; generative artificial intelligence through variational autoencoders and generative adversarial networks for de novo molecular design with targeted property constraints; physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) for inverse problem-solving and kinetic modelling; and Bayesian uncertainty quantification for robust decision-making through aleatoric and epistemic uncertainty assessment. This work establishes nitrosyl chemistry as a vibrant, interdisciplinary frontier where molecular innovation converges with computational intelligence, and it serves as an authoritative, decision-oriented reference for both newcomers and experienced practitioners across inorganic chemistry, catalysis, bioinorganic chemistry, and materials science.

title: Computational Modeling and Performance Evaluation of Optical Imaging Systems with Different Aperture Geometries under Atmospheric Turbulence Filtering
container-title: Al-Noor Journal of Engineering Management and Computer Science
e90cc57cbdb094974be53ac32b033efd9032ada5.abstract: Analyzing the functionality of optical systems following their production holds considerable scientific and practical relevance. It provides a wide range of possibilities for research and the advancement of novel methodologies to furnish thorough data regarding the optical system; the point spread function (PSF) is a vital component for measuring the effectiveness of such systems. Core pictorial information is usually interwoven throughout an image's arrangement characteristics and ambient context. These factors demand tailored processing strategies to maintain appropriate image resolution. This study presents a formulation aimed at substantially increasing image sharpness and clarity by employing the PSF equation for optical systems having circular, rectangular, square, and triangular apertures. Utilizing Mathcad software, we executed an atmospheric turbulence filter characterized by parameters δ=0.2, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8 and 1 on all optical systems as a way of enhancing images. Situated at the system's entrance, this filter replicates or reduces the influence of atmospheric turbulence on light and the resulting image, particularly in extended-range systems. The filter's function is not explicitly for enhancing images; rather, it replicates the influence of air turbulence on the system, enabling the assessment of the system's (or filters') proficiency in sustaining resolution under diverse turbulence scenarios. The study focuses on a diffraction-limited (ideal) optical system. Four types of apertures were compared both with and without a filter, and full width at half its widest point (FWHM). Was measure the results were analyzed using origin software, presented graphically, and discussed in detail.
