title: <b>The effect of supplementary cementitious materials on reinforcement chloride -induced corrosion in concrete/ A critical review </b>
container-title: Al-Noor Journal of Engineering Management and Computer Science
e331b19b4348e843ec19861ba0053c83e82a1bf7.abstract: Corrosion of reinforcing steel is one of the core influencing issues on the durability and lifespan of reinforced concrete, principally in environments where concrete is subject to increased exposure to chloride ions and aggressive environmental issues. This review discusses the effect of cementitious materials (SCMs) in minimizing the corrosion of reinforcing steel, focusing on fly ash (FA), granulated blast furnace slag (GGBS), silica fume (SF) and metakaolin (MK). The review deals with the chemical and physical properties of these materials and their relation to concrete performance and corrosion resistance. The reviewed studies appear that the use of SCMs can enhance corrosion resistance by limiting the diffusion of aggressive agents by optimization the pore structure of the concrete and binding the chloride ions. However, the amount of the optimization fluctuates reliant on the category of material, the percentage used, and the exposure and curing status. This review underlines the significance of appropriate replacement proportions, and the necessity for long-dated studies involving connect corrosion resistance to the structural behavior of reinforced concrete.

title: Delayed-presenting penopubic epispadias in children: a case series highlighting surgical management and complications
container-title: Annals of Medicine & Surgery
02eef8d083efaf9eb88dabc8927c7a59f12d7790.abstract: Introduction and importance: Epispadias is a rare congenital anomaly involving dorsal displacement of the urethral meatus, often leading to functional and cosmetic concerns. In low-resource settings, delayed diagnosis is common due to limited awareness and sociocultural misinterpretation. Early surgical correction is essential for optimal outcomes. This series presents three pediatric cases managed with a modified Cantwell–Ransley urethroplasty. Case series: Three male patients aged 6, 11, and 12 years presented with dorsal urethral openings present since birth. Delayed presentation was noted in all cases due to misinterpretation, financial constraints, and prior inadequate management. The first case underwent primary modified Cantwell–Ransley repair but developed a postoperative urethrocutaneous fistula which was successfully repaired at a later stage. The second case had a preoperative urinary tract infection, which was treated prior to surgery, and showed an uncomplicated recovery despite an early urethral stent blockage. The third case involved a previous failed repair at a private medical center and required revision surgery with scar release and the use of a suprapubic pedicled flap for skin deficiency, resulting in a favorable outcome. Clinical discussion: The modified Cantwell–Ransley technique provided effective reconstruction, although complications such as fistulas may occur. The use of vascularized flaps was essential in complex and redo cases to achieve adequate coverage. Delayed presentation, prior failed procedures, and limited resources were the main challenges. Conclusion: Epispadias can be successfully managed with appropriate surgical techniques, even in challenging settings. Early diagnosis and specialized care improve outcomes, while delayed or failed cases require more complex reconstruction.

title: Perioperative anesthetic management of a patient with narcolepsy: a case report
container-title: Annals of Medicine & Surgery
4e63e3c41aff49b77ff24c99854cb3e8ff9fb57c.abstract: Introduction and importance: Narcolepsy is a chronic neurological disorder that disrupts sleep–wake regulation and poses unique challenges in perioperative anesthetic management. Presentation of case: We report the successful perioperative management of a 21-year-old man with type 1 narcolepsy, accompanied by mild obstructive sleep apnea with an apnea–hypopnea index (AHI) of 14.3 events per hour, who underwent uvulopalatopharyngoplasty. Clinical discussion: Short-acting agents (propofol, remifentanil, and sevoflurane) were administered under continuous bispectral index (BIS) monitoring. Multimodal analgesia with sufentanil, flurbiprofen, and ropivacaine was used to optimize pain control and minimize respiratory risk. The patient recovered without delayed awakening after the primary anesthesia or worsening of narcolepsy symptoms, despite a postoperative bleeding episode requiring reoperation. Conclusion: This case highlights the importance of individualized anesthetic strategies for patients with narcolepsy, emphasizing BIS-guided anesthetic depth control and multimodal analgesia to ensure safe perioperative outcomes.

title: Integrated Maintenance-Based Management of Boarding School Facilities at Islamic Boarding Schools
container-title: At Tadbir: Islamic Education Management Journal
e9b2886664d7b3c7cebe989994f851998fe2f55e.abstract: The management of boarding school facilities requires a maintenance mechanism that links the monitoring of facility conditions to decision-making and follow-up repairs. This study aims to analyze the integration of facility management functions through daily maintenance at the API ASRI 2 Islamic Boarding School in Bandongan, Magelang. The study employs a qualitative approach using a case study design. Data were collected through in-depth interviews with 13 informants, observations, and documentation, and were then analyzed using the Miles, Huberman, and Saldaña interactive model through data condensation, data presentation, and the drawing and verification of conclusions. The research findings reveal three key mechanisms of integrated maintenance. Firstly, specialisation of management by facility type establishes control through scheduled inspections and damage reporting. Secondly, daily monitoring links stocktaking, planning, procurement, damage management and evaluation in maintenance decision-making. Thirdly, coordination with technical experts ensures that damage management requiring specialised expertise remains under the control of management, whilst also providing opportunities for technical skills development through mentoring. This study concludes that integrated maintenance is formed through the interconnection of responsibilities, information on facility conditions, technical coordination, and continuous evaluation. The conceptual contribution of this study lies in its explanation of the integration of structural, operational, and collaborative dimensions in the management of boarding school facilities.

title: Human Resource Management Based on Cadre Development and Academic Development to Support the Quality of the ‘Kitab Kuning’ Learning Process in Islamic Boarding Schools
container-title: At Tadbir: Islamic Education Management Journal
e51128dc06d4b938b646cd6fb61fe3a08edf0d26.abstract: The teaching of classical Islamic texts (kitab kuning) in Islamic boarding schools requires teachers (ustadz) who have a thorough grasp of the texts’ content and are able to explain them to the students (santri). This study aims to analyse how the management of teachers supports the quality of the teaching process for classical Islamic texts at the API ASRI 2 Islamic Boarding School in Bandongan, Magelang. The study employs a qualitative approach using a case study design. Data from interviews with the boarding school’s elders, the Qori’in committee, a teacher, and three students were analysed through pattern matching and the construction of explanations. The results of the study indicate that the number of classes forms the basis for estimating teaching staff requirements, whilst the type of text serves as a reference for mapping the necessary expertise. The boarding school prioritises senior alumni based on observations of their character, moral conduct and depth of knowledge whilst they were students. Through textbook deliberations, teachers harmonise their understanding of the material and exchange teaching methods. Monthly evaluations cover the teachers’ performance and the students’ learning outcomes. This research highlights two key roles played by the management of teachers in supporting the quality of the learning process. The recruitment of alumni helps the pesantren provide teachers who are familiar with its scholarly traditions, whilst the text-based discussions provide a space for teachers to develop their methods of explaining the text’s content to students.

title: Relative efficacy of 25-hydroxycholecalciferol supplementation on growth parameters, bone quality, and plasma concentration in broilers
container-title: Poultry Science and Management
26e85eac62836f99801d37ba4ee622e9dc48f4da.abstract: Abstract Among metabolites of vitamin D 3 , 25-hydroxycholecalciferol (25-(OH)D 3 ), also referred to as 25-hydroxyvitamin D 3 , is recognized for its bioavailability and utility in poultry rations. This four-arm randomized controlled trial evaluated the outcomes of three commercial products of 25-(OH)D 3 with varying active concentration on growth performance metrics, bone mineralization, and plasma 25-(OH)D 3 levels in broilers relative to an unsupplemented control. A total of 1,500 Ross broiler chicks were allocated to four treatments with 15 replicate pens of 25 birds in each replicate floor pen. Dietary treatments included: T1 - Basal diet (2000 IU/kg of finished feed) + 0 ppb supplemented 25-(OH)D 3 , T2 – Basal (2000 IU/kg) + Product A (69 ppb supplemented 25-(OH)D 3 ), T3 - Basal (2000 IU/kg) + Product B (69 ppb supplemented 25-(OH)D 3 ), and T4 – Basal (2000 IU/kg) + Product C (34.5 ppb supplemented 25-(OH)D 3 ). Performance parameters were recorded during starter (day 0 to 14), grower (day 14 to 28) and finisher (day 28 to 43) phases. Tibia mineral contents and plasma 25-(OH)D 3 were measured on day 21 and 43. Feed intake did not differ significantly during starter, grower, and finisher phase ( P > 0.05). Body weight gain was higher in Product A birds compared to Product B and Product C from 0 to 43 days ( P < 0.05). There were no differences between groups in tibia bone parameters on day 21. Tibia ash percentage on day 43 was significantly greater in Product A and Product C compared to the unsupplemented control ( P < 0.05). Tibia bone calcium, phosphorus, and density did not differ among treatment groups( P > 0.05). Plasma 25-(OH)D 3 was greater in product A compared to Product B and C at both 21 and 43 days( P < 0.05). All vitamin D 3 supplemented groups had greater plasma 25-(OH)D 3 compared to the unsupplemented control. Mortality rates were unaffected ( P > 0.05) by supplemental Vitamin D 3 . The improved performance of Product A is attributed to its higher active 25-(OH)D 3 concentration and formulation, underscoring that inclusion rate alone does not guarantee biological efficacy. These findings emphasize the importance of evaluating commercial 25-(OH)D 3 products as outcomes may vary depending on the delivery method and the practical context.

title: Design and Implementation of an Integrated Academic Affairs Management and Faculty Evaluation System at Faryab University
container-title: Addaiyan Journal of Arts Humanities and Social Sciences
56612d200896e680864c103334a504a939d679ee.abstract: Universities increasingly require integrated digital systems to manage academic affairs, faculty evaluation, institutional planning, and quality assurance. In resource-constrained higher education institutions, fragmented administrative records and paper-based procedures can complicate academic monitoring, reporting, and decision-making. This study presents the design and implementation of an Integrated Academic Affairs Management and Faculty Evaluation System for Faryab University, Afghanistan. A design-oriented research approach was adopted, with system requirements identified through the analysis of official institutional forms and administrative procedures. The system was developed using Laravel (PHP), Filament, and MySQL, following a three-layer architecture. Its integrated components support academic personnel management, academic rank tracking, operational planning, course administration, faculty evaluation, quality assurance, document management, and administrative reporting. The implementation demonstrates how institution-specific administrative requirements can be translated into interconnected software modules and database structures. The study contributes a context-specific implementation case for integrating academic administration and quality assurance processes within a unified information system. Although the application has been developed, formal user-based evaluation has not yet been conducted. Future research should assess its usability, reliability, user acceptance, and operational effectiveness in the university environment.

title: AI Literacy and Science Self-Efficacy as Predictors of Senior High School Students’ Perceived Scientific Research Skills
container-title: Davao Research Journal
18124df4420feb678361cb8ce7575b017450836f.abstract: The increasing use of artificial intelligence (AI) in education underscores the need to understand how AI literacy and science self-efficacy relate to students' research capabilities. This study examined senior high school students' perceived levels of AI literacy, science self-efficacy, and scientific research skills in Lupon West District, Davao Oriental, Philippines. It aimed to assess whether AI literacy and science self-efficacy uniquely predict scientific research skills. The study employed a cross-sectional predictive-correlational design, involving 261 Grade 12 students selected through proportionate stratified random sampling, with simple random selection within each school. Data were collected using paper-and-pencil questionnaires comprising three adapted instruments. Students reported moderate AI literacy (M = 3.22, SD = 0.65) and science self-efficacy (M = 3.39, SD = 0.71), but high perceived scientific research skills (M = 3.53, SD = 0.70). AI literacy was positively correlated with perceived scientific research skills, r(259) = .623, p < .001, as was science self-efficacy, r(259) = .79, p < .001. The regression model was significant, F(2, 258) = 224.66, p < .001, explaining 63.5% of the variance in perceived scientific research skills. AI literacy (B = 0.19, β = .17, p < .001) and science self-efficacy (B = 0.67, β = .67, p < .001) each made significant unique statistical contributions, with science self-efficacy having the larger standardized coefficient. These findings may inform research instruction by integrating responsible AI use and creating opportunities to enhance students’ confidence in science.

title: Agricultural Information Networks, Information Needs and Risk Management Strategies among Smallholder Farmers in Southeast Nigeria
container-title: Journal of Information & Knowledge Management
656c9237187d1f3ad070a1c4437258464f807f1b.abstract: This study examined agricultural information networks, information needs, and risk management strategies among smallholder farmers in Southeast Nigeria using the Diffusion of Innovation Theory. Quantitative data were analyzed using SPSS Version 21 with descriptive statistics including means, frequencies, rankings, and standard deviations, while qualitative data from focus group discussions were examined thematically using Braun and Clarke’s six-step framework. Findings show dominance of farmer-to-farmer networks, traditional knowledge systems, and kinship ties as the most trusted sources of agricultural information, while institutional and digital platforms were least utilized. Major information needs centred on disease and pest management, climate-related risks, fertilizer use, and improved seed varieties, reflecting farmers’ vulnerability to environmental and production uncertainties. Within Rogers’ Diffusion of Innovation Theory, interpersonal communication channels such as peer networks significantly influenced awareness and adoption of agricultural practices. The study concludes that strengthening farmer-led networks and improving access to credible institutional information sources can enhance risk management and innovation adoption among smallholders in the region. Implications suggest that extension agencies and development actors should leverage existing social structures, enhance participatory communication strategies, and integrate indigenous knowledge with formal agricultural advisory services to improve resilience, reduce information asymmetry, and support sustainable adoption of innovations in line with diffusion processes in rural farming communities. Furthermore, the study contributes to the understanding of agricultural information behaviour in developing contexts and highlights the need for improved digital infrastructure, policy support, and capacity building to strengthen inclusive rural information ecosystems development.

title: How Generative AI Shapes Undergraduate Academic Writing Development in Higher Education: A Literature Review
container-title: Exploring Science Academic Conference Series
4e198f70618a461c5743e2b44293df587136caef.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence has become part of undergraduate academic writing through tools such as ChatGPT, which can support brainstorming, drafting, revision, and feedback. Its educational value, however, remains contested. These tools may help students produce more polished texts, but this does not necessarily mean that students are developing stronger writing abilities. This review synthesises peer-reviewed empirical, review, and conceptual studies published between 2023 and 2026. It examines how generative AI shapes undergraduate academic writing in higher education, with a focus on the distinction between lower-order writing skills and higher-order writing abilities. The reviewed literature indicates that generative AI provides the most consistent support for lower-order writing skills, including grammar, vocabulary, formatting, sentence clarity, and proofreading. Findings on higher-order skills, such as argumentation, critical thinking, originality, academic voice, and content depth, are more mixed. AI effectiveness also depends on teaching guidance, student ability, feedback type, and feedback literacy. Generative AI is therefore best understood as a complementary writing support rather than a replacement for human instruction.

title: Animating microbiology and immunology: student tool preferences and pedagogical insights in an AI era
container-title: Microbiology Australia
63d557c1bf410d68eb411a71fe3cef9a8ca093dd.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) tools have changed how undergraduate students approach written coursework, often bypassing required levels of active reading and conceptual engagement. To encourage genuine interaction with course content without resorting to high-stress invigilated exams, a low-stakes digital animation task (2% weighting) was integrated into an undergraduate microbiology and immunology course, to pilot students’ preferences on using animation tools to construct visuals. Students created a 30-s animation, illustrating dynamic biological processes, such as viral replication or phagocytosis. Pre- and post-exercise surveys evaluated students’ prior tool experience, selection criteria and software adoption. Pre-survey results showed that only 57% of students had prior animation experience – predominantly using Microsoft PowerPoint (32%). Key tool selection criteria included user-friendliness (32%), available tutorial support (18%) and zero cost (15%). Following targeted tutorial support for in-house digital tools (e.g. Adobe Express, Adobe Animate, Adobe Character Animator) and autonomy to select Adobe or other preferred tools for the task, post-survey analysis demonstrated a substantial rise in preference for Adobe Express, growing from 2 to 41%, while maintaining high levels of student engagement. Tutors observed that translating biological concepts into moving representations required greater time-on-task, research and deconstruction of study content to construct an accurate visual, thus offering an effective, AI-resistant assessment strategy for science education.

title: Australia will impose mandatory safety rules on AI. Are we focused on the right risks?
Design, Implementation, and Empirical Evaluation of a Human–AI Collaborative Adaptive Assessment Model in Higher Education
container-title: Journal of General Education and Humanities
c4fc7c2df67e25e958c78f59c8dc7e87340a3c13.abstract: AI-supported assessment increasingly enables adaptive tasks, automated analysis, and personalized feedback, yet their integration into coherent, human-supervised formative assessment remains insufficiently established. This study developed and evaluated the Human–AI Collaborative Adaptive Assessment Model (HA-CAAM) using Design and Development Research structured through the ADDIE framework. Implemented in a higher-education Media Education course, the model employed performance-responsive task adaptation using predefined thresholds, rubric-guided AI-assisted scoring, formative feedback, and instructor verification. Five experts validated the model, 148 students provided quantitative and qualitative implementation feedback, and 50 student responses were independently assessed by two human raters and AI. Expert validation provided initial evidence of content validity (mean Aiken's V = 0.818). Students reported generally favorable experiences, particularly regarding clarity and feedback usefulness, although Learning Support and Overall User Experience received comparatively lower ratings. AI-generated scores demonstrated strong agreement with human-reference scores (ICC = 0.898), despite individual discrepancies. These findings provide initial evidence of content validity, positive implementation experiences, and scoring agreement, rather than demonstrated improvements in learning outcomes or equivalence between AI and human assessment decisions. HA-CAAM contributes an empirically refined, seven-stage assessment framework that coordinates performance-responsive adaptation, AI-assisted analysis, formative feedback, and instructor-led quality assurance within a human-supervised assessment process.

title: AI-Assisted Negotiation Training: A Quasi-Experimental Examination of Buyers’ and Sellers’ Perceived Negotiation Performance in a Used-Car Sales Simulation
container-title: Suranaree Journal of Social Science
ddd15b60d7479b08cb39c441d3870714dc3d739f.abstract: Background: Evidence on artificial intelligence (AI) as a preparatory learning aid for novice human negotiators remains limited in consumer negotiation simulations. Existing work emphasizes automated agents rather than students preparing to negotiate. Against this backdrop, the present study examined changes in students’ perceived negotiation performance, differences in those changes between buyer and seller roles, and the purposes for which students used AI during a simulated used-car sale. The outcome was perceived performance, not economic results. Methodology: A single-group, repeated-measures quasi-experiment involved 74 undergraduate business students enrolled in a negotiation course at a university in Bangkok, Thailand. Thirty-seven students served as buyers and 37 as sellers. Participants completed two negotiations outside regular class hours within a 24–48-hour period, retaining their assigned roles and using the same scenario. The first round was conducted without AI assistance. Before the second round, students spent approximately five minutes preparing with generative AI tools of their choice for information analysis, strategy planning, role-play, or feedback. Each negotiation lasted approximately five to seven minutes. Perceived negotiation performance was assessed using five-item self-report scales in each condition. Paired-samples t-tests and a mixed-design analysis of variance (ANOVA) examined differences between conditions and across roles. Reported purposes of AI use were summarized descriptively. Results: Students reported higher perceived negotiation performance after AI-assisted preparation (M = 4.45, SD = 0.42) than after the preceding non-AI round (M = 3.78, SD = 0.58). The mean difference was 0.67 points, t(73) = −9.23, p < .001, with a large standardized difference (|d| = 1.07). The mixed-design ANOVA identified a significant condition effect, F(1, 72) = 83.97, p < .001, partial η² = .54, but no significant condition-by-role interaction. Buyers' mean scores increased by 0.68 points and sellers' by 0.66 points. Information analysis was the most frequently reported purpose of AI use (91.9%), followed by strategy planning (60.8%), role-play practice (51.4%), and feedback (40.5%). These descriptive patterns do not establish the effectiveness of individual AI functions. Discussions: The findings suggest that AI may provide useful analytical and strategic support during experiential negotiation preparation. Similar patterns of change across buyer and seller roles indicate that the observed increase in perceived performance was not statistically distinguishable between the two groups; the groups do not demonstrate equal bargaining power or equivalent economic outcomes. Students' greater use of information analysis and planning than of interactive practice also points to a possible area for instructional development. However, the fixed order of conditions and repetition of the same scenario mean that practice and familiarity may have contributed to the higher ratings in the second round. Conclusions: AI-assisted preparation was associated with substantially higher self-reported negotiation performance in this educational simulation. The findings reflect students' perceptions, not independently assessed negotiation quality, agreed prices, fairness, or information asymmetry. Accordingly, they should not be interpreted as a causal estimate of AI's contribution to objective negotiation performance. Future studies should counterbalance condition order, include behavioral measures, and recruit more diverse participants.

title: Trust Conditions and Conditional Willingness to Use AI Legal Information in Bangladesh
c1257491bd48d1fdc1ce8673813ba2431c023798.abstract: Abstract A person can express willingness to use an artificial intelligence (AI) legal service under transparent conditions while remaining cautious about acting on its information. This cross-sectional study distinguishes conditional willingness, trust expectations and verification caution using 385 adult questionnaire records from Bangladesh. We report full response distributions, paired comparisons and exploratory adjusted models of willingness attributed to transparent explanations. The willingness statement was endorsed by 337 respondents (87.5%); trust conditional on clear sources was endorsed by 260 (67.5%) and trust conditional on qualified professional oversight by 266 (69.1%). Within respondents, willingness endorsement exceeded these two trust conditions by 20.0 and 18.4 percentage points, respectively (both Holm-adjusted p < 0.001). Of the 337 respondents who endorsed conditional willingness, 233 also endorsed the professional oversight condition. In the adjusted original-rating model, perceived access utility (b = 0.275, 95% CI 0.111 to 0.439) and verification caution (b = 0.154, 95% CI 0.060 to 0.248) were positively associated with conditional willingness (both adjusted p = 0.003). Neither association met the adjusted threshold when willingness was dichotomised. The findings distinguish openness to a transparent service from confidence in an answer or readiness to act on it. They motivate separate evaluation of source checking, professional escalation and service use. The study does not identify the causal effect of transparency or estimate actual adoption or national prevalence.

b2a56695765e30dbf0849e6a821dee3c43530549.abstract: Masa remaja ditandai perubahan emosional dan sosial serta meluasnya interaksi dengan teman sebaya, sehingga kemampuan mengelola emosi dan menghargai perbedaan menjadi penting. Observasi awal di SMAI Miftahul Ulum, Pamekasan, menemukan sebagian siswa mengejek dan memanggil teman dengan nama orang tua, sehingga siswa lain merasa tidak percaya diri dan tidak berani bersuara. Kegiatan pengabdian ini bertujuan memperkuat pemahaman siswa tentang pengelolaan emosi, kepercayaan diri, interaksi positif dengan teman sebaya, dan sikap menghargai perbedaan melalui Program REKAT (Ruang Ekspresi dan Kebersamaan Remaja). Metode berupa psikoedukasi partisipatif (materi oleh dua pemateri, film pendek, kuis kelompok, dan refleksi) pada 7 September 2026, dengan evaluasi pre-test dan post-test satu kelompok. Dari 25 siswa yang mengisi kedua tes, 22 siswa dengan data lengkap dianalisis. Rata-rata skor naik dari 3,52 (88,07%) menjadi 3,59 (89,77%) pada skala 1–4, yaitu 0,07 poin atau 1,70 poin persentase, yang tidak signifikan secara statistik (t(21) = 1,38; p = 0,182; N-gain = 0,14). Kenaikan kecil ini kemungkinan dipengaruhi skor awal yang sudah tinggi. Hasil hanya menunjukkan indikasi penguatan pemahaman jangka pendek dan belum dapat disimpulkan sebagai perubahan perilaku.

title: Decoupled vegetation structure and composition in a mangrove–apicum ecotone in Northeastern Brazil
container-title: Wetlands Ecology and Management
6e5cabfc1efe404ce6c268beb1b650527a5c0fb0.abstract: Abstract Mangrove–apicum ecotones are heterogeneous transition zones in which woody colonization need not follow a single age-ordered trajectory. We reanalysed an author-validated area-level matrix from ten successional mangrove patches in the Barra de Gramame estuary, northeastern Brazil. Five patches belonged to a 6–10-year and five to an 11–15-year site-history category inherited from the original survey. Individuals of Avicennia schaueriana , Laguncularia racemosa and Rhizophora mangle were classified into two height-defined structural strata (< 1 m and >1 m) and counted over 225 m2 per patch; a single 900 m2 reference stand was used descriptively. Hierarchical Bayesian modelling, fully enumerated exact permutations, Bray–Curtis and Aitchison analyses, beta-diversity partitioning and leave-one-area-out diagnostics were applied. The <1 m stratum contained 7,439 individuals, compared with 1,898 individuals in the >1 m stratum. Posterior density ratios (< 1 m/>1 m) were 2.73 (95% credible interval: 1.46–5.12) in 6–10-year areas and 3.64 (1.94–6.73) in 11–15-year areas, whereas site-history effects remained uncertain. Abundance-sensitive assemblage structure differed significantly between height strata (Bray–Curtis R2 = 0.213, exact P = 0.00195), whereas relative species composition did not clearly differ under Aitchison geometry (R2 = 0.029, P = 0.105). Abundance gradients accounted for 96.1% of paired Bray–Curtis dissimilarity, and areas in the older site-history category were not consistently more similar to the reference stand. The ecotone therefore showed a marked height-structure imbalance without equivalent proportional species turnover, while the two coarse site-history categories did not define discrete compositional states. These cross-sectional results support multidimensional, site-specific monitoring and do not by themselves demonstrate a temporal successional trajectory.

title: Green Human Resource Management and Environmentally Friendly Behavior of Employees in Iraq's Ministry of Environment
container-title: Krakatoa Management Research Journal
dbb1ebd5c12c7fc6b195c19bd5da330293d144e9.abstract: Purpose: This study examines how Green Human Resource Management (GHRM), expressed through green recruitment, green training, green performance appraisal, and green rewards, relates to and influences the environmentally friendly behavior of employees at the Ministry of Environment in Baghdad, Iraq. Methodology: A descriptive analytical design was used. A questionnaire built on a five point Likert scale was distributed electronically to a convenience sample of 110 employees, and 98 questionnaires were returned. Validity was checked with Pearson item correlations, reliability with Cronbach's alpha, and the hypotheses were tested with Pearson correlation and simple linear regression in SPSS version 27. Results: All four GHRM dimensions were rated highly, with green performance appraisal ranked first. GHRM correlated strongly and positively with environmentally friendly behavior (r=0.673) and had a significant effect on it (B=0.752, F=77.079, R²=0.453). Green training and green rewards were the strongest individual dimensions. Conclusions: Green HR practices, particularly training and rewards, give the ministry a practical way to steer employees toward greener behavior at work. Limitations: The study relied on a single public organization, a small convenience sample, cross sectional self reported data, and bivariate analysis. Contributions: The study adds evidence from an Iraqi public sector setting, where GHRM research is still scarce, and offers managers concrete steps such as environmentally oriented job descriptions and incentives for employees who propose ways to reduce waste.

title: Simulation Modeling of a Top Manager’s Time Management
container-title: Journal of Modern Competition
e75c8a9525584f4b245113f7fa9dbc685949060b.abstract: The working time of the company’s senior management is difficult to standardize, as a significant portion of it is spent on external processes related to ensuring competitiveness, leveraging opportunities, and countering threats – including those related to sectoral regulation, government industrial policy measures, changes in the sanctions and logistics landscape, etc. These activities of senior management are not covered by internal corporate business processes and classical tools of the scientific organization of managerial work. The article describes the structural framework of a simulation model of a manager’s working time, which can be used to improve the efficiency of its use. The discrete-event simulation model is presented as a flow of incoming tasks that have characteristic time-management features: synchronicity/asynchronicity, duration, urgency, and contribution to the overall value of the day. The results of a number of experiments with the model are presented, showing how the use of various time-management techniques increases the overall value of the working day compared to the usual chaotic mode. The "painted clock" approach is proposed, which makes it possible to link the results of applying a simulation model to the economic model of the enterprise. The scientific novelty of the study lies in applying simulation modeling tools to the tasks of corporate time management. The practical significance lies in using the model as a digital testing ground to evaluate various time management practices and their impact on the company’s efficiency.

title: Competitive Mechanisms of HR Policy Formation in the Top Management Segment of Russian Corporations
container-title: Journal of Modern Competition
a17481bd5513bc33f32499ab3414ebf9775498a8.abstract: The article examines the hypothesis that the reserves of HR policy of Russian companies in the top management segment, being substantively diverse and quantitatively significant, have as their core institutional resources an objectively unjustified hypertrophy of monopolistic algorithms and corresponding toxic effects; the "unplanned" (chaotic) nature of HR decisions; the specific role of the actual beneficiary of a group of companies in personnel selection with a clear shift of the universal dialectic of candidate choice "personal loyalty vs professional competence" toward the former; "shadow" basic management mechanisms and private technologies of recruiting and rewarding top management effectiveness; and the illogical toolkit for amnestying top management for the most disastrous HR decisions that entailed particularly grave material, legal, and reputational consequences (corporate sabotage, fraud, corruption, etc.). Collectively, these factors critically suppress the prospects for implementing the principles of fair HR competition. The author analyzes local normative acts of large Russian companies relevant to the studied problem, cases of judicial practice, and regulatory-experimental searches of companies, and substantiates applied recommendations addressed to subjects of improving normative-legal and corporate regulation of business management processes. The methodological basis of the study is an interdisciplinary approach combining the tools of corporate conflictology, competition law, and economic analysis. The obtained results indicate the need to institutionalize transparent competitive procedures in the top management segment and create mechanisms of responsibility for HR decisions.

title: Credit Default Risk Assessment of Listed Real Estate Firms Using the KMV Model
container-title: Risk and Financial Management
91b1aff0a7dafd489d54a7797dc24dcea1a56be3.abstract: This study examines the credit default risk of Chinese listed real estate firms using the KMV structural credit risk model, with particular attention to market-based risk assessment and the limitations of conventional credit ratings. Drawing on data from 261 real estate firms listed on mainland China's A-share markets and the Hong Kong Stock Exchange between 2010 and 2023, the study estimates distance to default (DD) from equity market information and financial statement data. A logistic regression approach is employed to translate DD into estimated default probabilities, while receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis and firm-level case studies are used to evaluate risk discrimination and early-warning performance. The results reveal a substantial deterioration in the creditworthiness of mainland-focused property developers during the industry downturn, particularly in 2022–2023, alongside pronounced differences between mainland and non-mainland firms. The DD measure achieves an area under the ROC curve (AUROC) of 0.760, indicating moderate discriminatory ability within the evaluated sample. Comparative case studies further suggest that market-based risk indicators can provide more frequent signals of financial deterioration than conventional credit ratings, although their predictive reliability depends on appropriate calibration and validation. The findings highlight the potential of the KMV model as a supplementary instrument for credit risk monitoring while emphasizing the need for improved probability calibration, rigorous out-of-sample validation, and integration with firm-level and macroeconomic indicators.

title: Explainable AI for Small-Sample Macroeconomic Forecasting: A Structural Analysis of the Bangladeshi Economy
049567816f4726bd43573fa87c70b94df1df59b7.abstract: Abstract Gross Domestic Product Growth (GDPG) is an essential indicator of the economic development of a state. The GDPG is understood as the annual percentage change in the value added of goods and services provided within an economy. This paper deal with the problem of GDPG forecasting for volatile emerging economies due to structural instability and small sample sizes leading to high variance in both econometrics and machine learning methods. The XAI technique is proposed to forecast GDPG of Bangladesh by using the dataset from the World Bank covering years from 1991 to 2024. After the necessary econometric pre-processing to ensure stationarity and eliminate multicollinearity, five machine learning models were tested. The model with the highest level of regularisation is L2-regularised XGBoost algorithm, providing the best out-of-sample forecast (R-squared = 0.6245). The introduction of SHAP allowed for the automatic global dimensionality reduction, hence the detection of spurious variables. The model revealed structural asymmetries like short-term dilution of capital-labor and lagged limitations caused by the volatility of the real interest rate. In general, it could be stated that the correct calibration of the model made possible by the use of the proposed technique could provide accurate macroeconomic information for making decisions.

title: Risk-Aware AI Procurement in the U.S. Public Sector: Stochastic Optimization and Technology Governance
879c5c856a1fd91683a8a2fd2c01e6b398dcc947.abstract: Abstract Public institutions acquire artificial intelligence (AI) services under established procurement, appropriation, and governance requirements, while commercial offers often state a rate and leave the quantity to later use. Executive leaders, procurement officers, financial authorities, and governance professionals need coordinated decision support so that a required review, a funding figure, and a management control are considered together. The objective is to give these decision-makers transparent, comparable financial estimates for AI service arrangements under uncertain demand. Operational controls and optimization are complementary parts of the proposed solution. The framework maps the reviewed rules onto subscription, consumption-based, prepaid-credit, and hybrid arrangements and labels each step as a legal requirement, a point the reviewed sources do not settle, or a recommended management practice. Ceilings, quotas, usage alerts, incremental funding, and named human approval are recommended practices, not Texas mandates. The proposed governance-constrained, riskaware decision optimization framework supports executive and institutional decision-making under uncertain AI consumption, financial exposure, and public-sector procurement requirements, while preserving human oversight and legally authorized decision authority. The model reports expected expenditure, conditional value-at-risk, demand ambiguity, budget exposure, and process timing. The experiments use synthetic data and characterize model behavior rather than institutional savings. Solver outputs are planning estimates; legal determinations and purchase authority remain with authorized officials.

title: Stakeholder relationships and environmental outcomes in natural resource management: a systematic review of mechanisms and governance conditions
container-title: International Journal of Environmental Science and Technology
0c19bb54bc3dd21572781556658f88e896407fa9.abstract: Abstract This systematic review synthesizes 62 empirical studies published between 1996 and 2025 to examine how organizational stakeholder relationships relate to environmental outcomes across emission reduction, resource efficiency, ecological governance, and natural resource stewardship. Following PRISMA 2020 guidelines, searches covered Scopus, Web of Science, EBSCO Business Source Complete, and ProQuest Business Collection, with explicit coverage of environmental science, ecology, and sustainability subject areas. The natural resource-based view provides the primary theoretical anchor, complemented by environmental governance theory and the community-based resource management literature. Six mechanisms organize the evidence: environmental sensing and early warning, green supply chain co-development, regulatory co-evolution, community-based ecological stewardship, environmental legitimacy accumulation, and collective environmental action. Three boundary conditions qualify the evidence: the association between engagement depth and environmental performance is non-linear; cooperative supply chain programs without credible enforcement show no measurable environmental improvement; and stakeholder selection driven by economic salience may underweight communities most dependent on affected ecosystem services. The evidence base documents eco-efficiency more consistently than ecological effectiveness, since few included studies measure absolute ecological-system outcomes. Closing this gap is the central priority for future research.

title: Patient Rights Safeguards and Conditional Acceptance of AI Assisted Diagnosis in Bangladesh
bef36896c086d5b6b10e27a269d1e8be0ca284fb.abstract: Abstract Acceptance of artificial intelligence in diagnosis raises questions about what people consider useful and which patient safeguards they endorse. This study examines their relationship in 385 adult, AI-aware questionnaire records supplied as empirical data from Bangladesh. Five diagnosis-and-rights statements are analysed separately because their content and low block reliability do not support a validated common acceptance scale. Response distributions, paired endorsement contrasts, eight combinations of rights preferences, Spearman correlations and exploratory logistic models distinguish professional usefulness, information, questioning, human judgement and conditional acceptance. The statement that patient-rights safeguards increase acceptance received 81.6% endorsement, compared with 56.9% for usefulness when AI supports qualified professionals. Information about material AI involvement received 81.0%, opportunities to ask questions 57.7%, and continuing human clinical judgement 63.9%. All three specific safeguards were jointly endorsed by 32.7%. Information preference had a small positive rank association with conditional acceptance after Holm correction. Adjusted information and questioning coefficients were positive but uncertain after correction and sensitivity checks. The findings identify differentiated endorsement of safeguards rather than an observed effect of rights protection on service uptake. They suggest evaluating communication as an opportunity for participation, not merely notification, while keeping normative rights distinct from an adoption strategy. Mixed respondent status, absent verification of patient experience, undocumented recruitment and fieldwork dates, and unresolved Codebook provenance labels restrict generalisation. The study provides an item-specific basis for further research connecting patient communication, professional oversight and conditional acceptance without claiming clinical effectiveness or tested legal knowledge.

title: Governing Artificial General Intelligence in Future Healthcare Institutions: Risk-Adaptive Institutional Authorization for Clinical and Operational Authority
container-title: AI & Future Society
139dc85cfaba50cf1707ed977b21a84a4f9c8b31.abstract: Increasingly general and agentic artificial intelligence raises an institutional question of authority: which actions may a system perform, how may it combine them, and who may revise or withdraw permission? For prospective artificial general intelligence (AGI), cross-domain planning makes unfamiliar combinations of familiar tasks a central problem of authorization. This article develops a Risk-Adaptive AGI Governance Framework through conceptual synthesis, purposive document comparison, and three constructed scenarios. Four determinants—task risk, demonstrated capability, institutional preparedness, and accountability—inform five authorization gates. The governing rule grants the least authority sufficient for a justified service objective within mandatory constraints. Information, recommendation, and bounded execution permissions can be combined only through additional authorization of their dependencies. A versioned record binds component permissions, configuration, and cross-service ownership; changes to a shared condition reopen affected grants. Administrative scheduling illustrates professional and patient challenges to an otherwise technically eligible grant. Emergency coordination traces partial execution, shared infrastructure failure, unavailable fallback, and conditional restoration. Four testable propositions address risk-sensitive allocation, preparedness, calibrated reliance, and precommitted containment. RAGF connects established lifecycle safeguards to continuing institutional authorization, dispute resolution, and patient remedy. The proposed evaluation agenda examines safety, workflow benefit, equitable access, and the costs of maintaining and withdrawing permission. For future healthcare institutions, preparation for AGI entails an accountable allocation of discretion across services, professionals, and patients.

title: Algorithmic Management as a Double-Edged Form of Digital Work Design: Job Demands, Autonomy and Employee Outcomes across 35 European Countries
072bed396833f6aabd92d49bce3ff3b3d77d9c18.abstract: Abstract Computer-based managerial systems are part of the digital infrastructure of work, with potential implications for employee demands and discretion. Drawing on Job Demands-Resources theory, this study examines task allocation, work scheduling and performance monitoring as distinct functions and their parallel indirect associations with engagement and intention to quit through work intensity and autonomy. Weighted least squares mean- and variance-adjusted structural equation models were estimated for 26,504 employees in 35 European countries using the 2024 European Working Conditions Survey. The measures capture reported computer involvement rather than verified artificial intelligence capabilities. Engagement and autonomy were modelled as latent factors, and quit intention as an ordinal outcome. All three practices were positively associated with work intensity. Task allocation was positively associated with autonomy, whereas monitoring was negatively associated with autonomy; scheduling’s negative autonomy association was less robust to contextual fixed effects. Task allocation showed opposing indirect engagement associations through intensity and autonomy, whereas monitoring showed negative associations through both pathways. Intensity-related indirect associations with quit intention were consistently positive, while autonomy-related indirect associations were not statistically significant in the primary or fixed-effects models. Sensitivity analyses supported the main directional patterns, while exploratory country diagnostics indicated incomplete measurement invariance and heterogeneous slopes. The findings inform the evaluation of digital management by distinguishing functions associated with greater demands and greater autonomy from those associated with greater demands and reduced autonomy. The cross-sectional design does not establish causal mediation or uniform cross-country relationships.

title: Perceptions of innovation in Brazil and Sweden: A cross-cultural comparison and its implications for human capital development and organizational management
container-title: Human Resources Management and Services
6513acefccbc0a165af6e6caeecd399fe8d76c90.abstract: Although the literature widely explores innovation, it remains under-researched from a cross-cultural perspective that considers associations between national cultures and values, attitudes, and behaviors. Most studies also rely on objective indicators such as patent counts, research and development investments, and university quality. While relevant, these metrics do not fully capture the subjective dimensions of innovation. Focusing on citizens from a developing country and a developed country, this study explored differences in perceptions of innovation between Brazilians and Swedes, discussing them in light of cultural characteristics, human capital development, and organizational management. The sample included 1,486 Brazilians and 1,206 Swedes, and the authors analyzed the data using correlation and comparison methods. Innovation variables included creativity, science, and technology, while Hofstede’s six dimensions characterized national cultures. Sex was the sociodemographic characteristic most frequently associated with positive perceptions of innovation, with men in both countries holding more favorable views. Higher levels of education and income were also associated with more positive perceptions. Swedes held more positive perceptions of innovation than Brazilians. Overall, the results suggested that Brazil’s and Sweden’s cultural characteristics align with their citizens’ perceptions of innovation. In practical terms, the study offers guidance for development, training, and talent management strategies across different cultural contexts.

title: Teachers’ Assessment of the Effectiveness of AI and Digital Tools Among Middle School Students in an International School: A Tool for Deeper Learning
container-title: QualiSearch Journal of Educational Research and Practice
3d23d8d784c06aa981f8246e271db5c47577db1b.abstract: This study examined teachers’ assessments of middle school students’ dependency on artificial intelligence (AI) and digital tools and the effectiveness of these technologies in supporting deeper learning at an international school in Phnom Penh, Cambodia. The quantitative correlational study included 82 Grades 6–8 teachers through total enumeration. Data from a researcher-developed questionnaire were analyzed using frequencies, percentages, weighted means, standard deviations, independent-samples t tests, one-way analyses of variance, and Spearman’s rank correlation. Teachers rated student dependency as high across critical thinking, independent study habits, problem-solving, and reliance on technology for outputs. They rated the tools effective for content delivery, student engagement, and academic performance, but less effective for skill development and for deeper learning overall. Selected dependency ratings differed by sex, educational attainment, and frequency of tool use. Effectiveness ratings differed by frequency of use. Perceived dependency and effectiveness were moderately and positively associated (ρ = .537, p < .001). These findings informed the Deeper Learning Pathway, a proposed school-based program that pairs guided use of AI and digital tools with opportunities for independent reasoning and problem-solving.

title: Cybersecurity workforce readiness: a three-dimensional assessment and scenario-based intervention framework aligned with NICE
container-title: Frontiers in Education
9cff4f68cf620b3cad75c7f868c506a4c700e4cd.abstract: The U.S. cybersecurity workforce faces a readiness gap that, we argue, current educational approaches address only in part. Industry surveys identify the most frequently cited deficiencies as non-technical, such as communication, critical thinking, and professional judgment under pressure, and official reports on major incidents, such as the 2017 Equifax breach and the 2020 SolarWinds compromise, describe accountability and coordination problems alongside technical and governance failures, while the 2023 MOVEit campaign extended exposure beyond organizational perimeters; we use these cases as illustrations, not as evidence that readiness failures caused them. This conceptual analysis proposes a framework to address the gap and positions it through a structured literature review with a documented search of OpenAlex and the Education Resources Information Center (ERIC) (2018–2026). Of 83 included studies, 19 assessed at least one non-technical readiness dimension per individual, 13 of them only through learners’ self-reports, and none combined individual assessment of motivational, cognitive, and communicative readiness, alignment with the National Initiative for Cybersecurity Education (NICE) Framework, and evaluation of AI-generated outputs within a scenario-based development cycle. The proposed framework adapts to cybersecurity a three-component model of professional readiness that was experimentally validated in emergency-services education. Its Contextual Readiness Assessment (CRA) is designed to produce a three-dimensional profile of Motivational-Goal, Cognitive, and Communicative-Activity readiness aligned with NICE Framework Components v2.2.0. Its Cyber-Quest methodology is designed to develop these dimensions through four learning mechanisms: role-activated professional identity, obligatory information asymmetry, deliberate evaluation of AI-generated artifacts, and structured experiential debrief. The two are linked in an assess–develop–reassess cycle in which learners evaluate accurate and inaccurate AI outputs against evidence. The paper distinguishes readiness from competence, performance, and self-efficacy, illustrates the cycle with a hypothetical use case, describes the conditions on which the framework rests, and sets out a staged validation plan; the framework has not yet been validated in cybersecurity populations.

title: The effectiveness of AI-based cognitive behavioral therapy chatbots for anxiety and depression symptoms: a systematic review and meta-analysis
container-title: Frontiers in Public Health
12ee7b8b941ec1f9692a230d0f570c757b2ca9ce.abstract: Background AI chatbots are increasingly being used to provide accessible psychological support. However, the effectiveness of chatbot-delivered cognitive behavioral therapy for anxiety and depressive symptoms remains uncertain. This study aimed to evaluate the effects of artificial intelligence chatbot-based cognitive behavioral therapy on anxiety and depressive symptoms. Method A systematic search of PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, PsycINFO, Cochrane Library, CNKI, VIP, Wanfang, and CBM databases was conducted from their inception to July 8th, 2025. Updated search on August 25, 2026. Meta-analysis was conducted using Stata version 18.0 and RevMan version 5.4. The ES for the treatment effect was calculated using the SMD . Results Ten studies involving a total of 1,301 participants. The results of the meta-analysis showed that the CBT of AI chatbots could significantly improve depressive symptoms at the end of the intervention ( d = −0.40, 95% CI : −0.62 ~ −0.17, P = 0.0005). In contrast, the intervention did not significantly improve anxiety symptoms ( d = −0.029, 95% CI : −0.145 ~ 0.087, P = 0.623), with no substantial heterogeneity detected ( I 2 = 0%). The subgroup analysis for depressive symptoms indicated significant effects were observed in participant age stratification, intervention Duration, and Control group intervention. However, some subgroup estimates were based on a small number of studies, so the data should be interpreted with caution. Conclusion This meta-analysis emphasizes that AI-based chatbots for CBT may have great potential in contributing to the alleviation of depressive symptoms. Given the small number of included studies and the high heterogeneity, the results should be interpreted with caution. More high-quality RCTs are needed in the future to further validate these findings and explore their long-term benefits. Systematic review registration https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420251089835 .

title: Application of inertial measurement units and machine learning for fatigue assessment in badminton athletes
container-title: Frontiers in Physiology
28910308e3b04040c11085a4c70390b4cfcc2df5.abstract: Objective To evaluate offline binary classification of recorded fatigue conditions using inertial measurement unit (IMU) acceleration features and five machine-learning algorithms. Methods The author-confirmed performance dataset contained 32 observations per condition. The revised primary IMU dataset comprised 70 recordings from 25 roster-linked athletes, with 22 non-fatigue and 48 fatigue labels after correction of four misclassified recordings. Seven-sensor and right-forearm configurations provided 231 and 33 candidate features. A newly reconstructed analysis retained five documented outer athlete-grouped folds and used three grouped inner folds for training-only preprocessing, sparse logistic feature selection and hyperparameter tuning. Results CMJ was 40.01 ± 8.51 and 30.27 ± 7.29 in the non-fatigue and fatigue conditions, respectively. Across classifiers, fold-mean AUC ranged from 0.655 to 0.846 for seven sensors and from 0.715 to 0.846 for the right forearm. Macro F1 ranged from 0.600 to 0.775 and from 0.655 to 0.775, respectively. Specificity ranged from 0.483 to 0.700 and from 0.550 to 0.650. Code, inclusion decisions, actual inner and outer assignments and held-out predictions are supplied for this new run. Conclusion The results support further investigation of IMU-based condition classification, but do not establish algorithm superiority, sensor equivalence, physiological validity of every recording label, or real-time monitoring performance.

title: An IoT-enabled environmental informatics framework for real-time crop disease detection using attention-driven deep learning
container-title: Frontiers in Environmental Science
90e6e8bd29434b2912cb190bf8bc0a9a88485b6a.abstract: Introduction Crop diseases are a major challenge in agriculture because their early and accurate identification is essential for reducing crop losses and improving productivity. The integration of the Internet of Things (IoT) with deep learning provides an effective approach for automated crop disease monitoring by enabling the collection and analysis of environmental parameters such as soil moisture, temperature, and humidity. However, accurate fine-grained disease identification remains challenging because of variations in disease symptoms, environmental conditions, and visual characteristics. Methods This study proposes an IoT-enabled deep learning framework for automated crop disease detection and classification. The collected crop images are pre-processed using scaling, normalization, and data augmentation techniques to improve image quality and model generalization. For efficient disease detection, a lightweight attention-driven convolutional neural network-based object detection approach, termed YOLO10-YSTs (You Only Look Once 10-Yield Surveillance Technology), is employed. The framework integrates the real-time detection capability of YOLO10 with an attention mechanism to emphasize disease-relevant regions and a stigmergy-based encoding strategy to enhance feature representation and extraction. In addition, a novel DBGU-LSTM (Dual-Bi-Gated Recurrent Unit with Long Short-Term Memory) architecture is developed for fine-grained crop disease classification. Results The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed framework provides effective disease detection, discriminative feature representation, and fine-grained classification. The DBGU-LSTM architecture achieves improved classification performance and training stability compared with the conventional deep learning models considered in the study. Overall, the proposed approach achieves a classification accuracy of 97.99%, demonstrating its effectiveness for automated crop disease recognition. Discussion and conclusion The results indicate that combining IoT-based environmental monitoring with attention-driven deep learning and recurrent feature-learning mechanisms can provide an effective solution for intelligent crop disease detection. The proposed framework enables accurate identification of disease patterns while supporting efficient and automated agricultural monitoring. Therefore, the approach has potential to assist farmers in early disease diagnosis, reduce crop losses, and improve agricultural productivity.

title: Tillage and integrated cover crop management effects on soil microclimate, root traits, and winter wheat productivity
container-title: Frontiers in Plant Science
1ee9729bb30abea42b8c7035f8d08b99fd907be7.abstract: This study evaluated the effects of tillage systems (conventional ploughing, shallow harrowing, and no-tillage) and agricultural technologies (traditional and integrated) on winter wheat root traits, grain yield, soil microclimate, and soil CO 2 efflux over three growing seasons (2022–2024) in a temperate agroecosystem. Root length density (RLD), root diameter, grain yield, soil temperature, volumetric water content, and soil CO 2 efflux were assessed, and relationships among root traits, soil microclimatic conditions, and CO 2 efflux were examined. Integrated technology significantly increased RLD by 6% in 2022 and 13% in 2023, whereas the difference was minimal in 2024. No-tillage produced higher RLD than harrowing and conventional ploughing in 2022 and 2023, whereas tillage effects were not significant in 2024. Grain yield varied markedly among years, coinciding with contrasting seasonal climatic conditions. Integrated technology increased yield by 12% in 2022, whereas no-tillage significantly reduced yield in 2024. Soil CO 2 efflux declined from 2022 to 2024 and was highest in 2022, which had the greatest May–July precipitation, indicating an association between seasonal water availability and soil respiration. Relationships between root traits and soil CO 2 efflux were weak and inconsistent across years, indicating that variation in total soil respiration could not be explained by the measured root traits alone. Overall, the findings demonstrate that winter wheat root and yield responses to tillage and agricultural technology vary substantially among growing seasons, highlighting the importance of considering both belowground plant traits and soil microclimatic conditions when evaluating crop-management strategies.

title: Simulation-based evaluation of a modified RRT algorithm for ground-robot navigation in 3D environments
container-title: Frontiers in Robotics and AI
37cf988259cc41c2b51715ebe278bf4c4b76af05.abstract: Autonomous robot navigation requires path-planning algorithms that maintain reliable performance in environments involving dynamic obstacles, changing goals, and complex terrain. This study extends the evaluation of a previously proposed Modified Rapidly-Exploring Random Tree (Modified RRT) algorithm from two-dimensional benchmark maps to robotic navigation scenarios in three-dimensional simulated environments. A simulation-based robotic navigation framework was developed using ROS 2 and Gazebo. Five scenarios were investigated: reconstruction of selected benchmark maps in 3D simulation, dynamic obstacle avoidance, dynamic goal adaptation, warehouse/campus navigation, and slope traversal. The framework incorporates synchronized RGB and depth sensing with point-cloud generation to characterize simulated environmental observations and support the analysis of perception and navigation performance. The global path planner operates in the horizontal x-y plane, while the robot, obstacles, and terrain are represented in the three-dimensional simulation environment. All four planners were evaluated under a common protocol using a shared costmap, collision checker, stopping budget, and parameter-tuning procedure. Modified RRT achieved success rates of up to 98%, reduced navigation completion time by up to 17.6%, and generated paths 10–15% shorter than standard RRT and 2–10% shorter than the next-best planner, Informed RRT* (IRRT*), at the cost of higher planning time than standard RRT in most scenarios. Under ideal sensing, Modified RRT reduced the near-collision rate by up to 74% in structured environments and 63% in unstructured environments relative to standard RRT. When depth noise, missing measurements, latency, and registration errors were introduced, the reductions were 45–61% and 40–52%, respectively. The results indicate that the Modified RRT sampling mechanisms can improve path-planning and navigation performance across the evaluated simulation scenarios. The findings also show that perception imperfections reduce the near-collision-rate improvements observed under ideal sensing. Overall, this study presents a simulation-based framework for evaluating planar global path planning, robot navigation execution, and simulated multimodal perception in three-dimensional robotic environments.

title: Case Report: Intramedullary spinal cord metastasis in HER2-low breast cancer: near-complete response to multimodal management and trastuzumab deruxtecan
container-title: Frontiers in Oncology
810e8d69c65d7c1611b377bc60087c73d50cfd73.abstract: Background Intramedullary spinal cord metastasis (ISCM) is a rare neurological complication of breast cancer. While trastuzumab deruxtecan (T-DXd) demonstrates robust central nervous system efficacy in HER2-low metastatic disease, real-world evidence regarding its specific activity against ISCM remains exceedingly limited. Case presentation A patient initially diagnosed in 2021 with hormone receptor-positive (HR+), human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2)-low (1+) breast cancer with sternal metastasis presented in July 2025 with severe right upper extremity weakness (Medical Research Council [MRC] grade 3/5). Cervical magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) revealed a C2 intramedullary lesion, prompting immediate surgical resection and laminoplasty. Pathological evaluation of the spinal lesion confirmed breast cancer-derived ISCM, revealing a HR-negative (ER 0%, PR 0%), HER2-low (1+) profile with a high Ki-67 index (70%). Two months post-surgery, follow-up spine MRI detected a 9-mm C2 nodule, designated as radiologically suspected local recurrence or residual disease. Guided by the identified HER2-low target, the patient received T-DXd therapy concurrently with intensity-modulated radiation therapy to the C1-C4 cervical spine (30 Gy in 10 fractions). Follow-up imaging demonstrated a near-complete radiological resolution of the spinal nodule, accompanied by substantial neurological improvement (motor strength recovering to grade 4/5). As of September 2026, the patient reached 13 months of postoperative follow-up with sustained disease control. Conclusion This case underscores the critical importance of metastatic re-biopsy in capturing spatial heterogeneity and identifying actionable targets. Furthermore, it provides compelling real-world evidence supporting the intraspinal therapeutic activity of T-DXd within a multimodal treatment strategy for refractory HER2-low ISCM.

title: Executive function outcomes following an immersive virtual reality game based intervention in Peruvian schoolchildren
container-title: Frontiers in Psychology
60e0aa10ad3be882293fe21c578022dba9354d34.abstract: Objective This exploratory study examined changes in executive-function performance following an immersive virtual reality game-based program in Peruvian schoolchildren. Methods Fifty-one children from a public school in southern Peru participated (mean age = 11.27 years, SD = 0.75). The project leader used random numbers generated in Microsoft Excel to allocate children within grade and classroom strata to an experimental group (n = 25) or a usual-activity control group ( n = 26). No a priori sample-size calculation was performed. The intervention comprised eight sessions over 4 weeks, with all five games presented in each session and up to 7.5 min of active exposure. Executive functions were assessed before and after the program using the six ENFEN scores; no single score was prioritized. Linear mixed-effects models were adjusted for age, sex, and body mass index. Results Among 50 children with longitudinal data, the Time × Group estimates favored the experimental group for Rings ( β = −45.12, 95% CI [−82.50, −7.74], nominal p = 0.022) and Interference ( β = 16.42, 95% CI [1.29, 31.55], nominal p = 0.039). No, statistically significant interactions were identified for the remaining outcomes. No correction for multiple testing was applied. Conclusion These task-specific findings are exploratory and require replication. They do not establish a benefit specific to immersion or cognitive training independently of novelty, engagement, and additional adult attention.

title: Analysis of the Critical Threshold Stress of Hybrid Metamaterial for Bulkheads in GFRP Hulls
container-title: Key Engineering Materials
7c164b885ab23efd469ebc7276e01d02b286312f.abstract: This study investigates the critical threshold of a hybrid metamaterial designed to optimize bulkhead reinforcements in GFRP hulls. A quantitative experimental approach was employed, analyzing five specimens without the metamaterial and five modified with a corrugated brass core. The specimens underwent Mode II interlaminar shear tests to analyze delamination. Data from these tests were interpreted using the Cohesive Zone Model (CZM) to characterize fracture energy and interfacial tensile strength. The results demonstrate that the hybrid specimens exhibit superior effective tangential stiffness and steeper load-displacement slopes compared to the GFRP-only specimens. Notably, the modified specimens reached a critical load up to 1.5 times higher than the typical specimens. Although initially showing lower energy dissipation due to their stiffness, they surpassed the fracture energy of the control specimens at larger local separations, activating dissipation mechanisms through metal-polymer interaction. Microscopic analysis confirmed more tortuous and irregular damage pathways in the metamaterial, validating a less brittle behavior. It is concluded that this hybrid configuration represents a viable alternative for naval engineering, improving structural strength without compromising the system's lightness.

title: AI Driven Talent Management and the Performance of Agri Based Enterprises in Central Region Cameroon
container-title: Journal of Economics, Management, Entrepreneurship, and Business (JEMEB)
9a45a01f3f197d9b0c87ceca92e874eb272d0293.abstract: Purpose: This study examines the relationship between artificial intelligence (AI) driven talent management practices and the performance of agri based enterprises in the Central Region of Cameroon, focusing on the mediating roles of workforce productivity and employee resilience. Research Methodology: A quantitative cross sectional survey design was employed, targeting 250 managers and human resource professionals. Data were collected with a structured questionnaire and analyzed with SPSS and AMOS through descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation, and mediation analysis with 5.000 bootstrap resamples. Results: AI driven talent management was positively and significantly related to enterprise performance (r=0.523, p<0.01). Workforce productivity (β=0.18) and employee resilience (β=0.14) significantly mediated this relationship. Both the total indirect effect (β=0.32, p<0.01) and the direct effect (β=0.29, p<0.01) were significant, indicating partial mediation, with about 52 percent of the total effect transmitted through the two mediators. Conclusions: AI driven talent management enhances the performance of agri based enterprises both directly and indirectly through improved workforce productivity and stronger employee resilience. Enterprises should integrate AI strategically into talent management and support employees through change management. Limitations: The cross sectional design, self reported data, purposive sampling, and focus on a single region limit causal inference and generalizability. Contributions: The study provides empirical evidence from an underresearched African agricultural context and clarifies the mechanisms through which AI driven talent management translates into enterprise performance.
