title: Robot cops on patrol: police officers' perceived effectiveness of AI-powered humanoid robots
container-title: Policing: An International Journal
399ffbef301f680d3c80797a3999bd5c26c9c5cb.abstract: Purpose The main purpose of the study is to examine how organizational justice, artificial intelligence (AI) literacy and perceived risks shape officers' attitudes toward AI-powered service and crime-fighting robots. Design/methodology/approach This study used survey data collected from 959 police officers in a major metropolitan area in Southwestern China. Two regression models were estimated to analyze correlates of police officers' perceived effectiveness of service and crime-fighting AI robots. Findings Results show that supervisor support for AI is a strong and consistent predictor of positive attitudes toward AI-powered robots, whereas supervisor justice is negatively associated with AI acceptance. AI training and AI knowledge also significantly enhance perceived effectiveness of AI tools, underscoring the saliency of technological familiarity. Perceived risks play a more limited and task-specific role. Originality/value The present study is among the first attempts to assess police officers' attitudes toward the application of AI in policing. This study provides evidence-based recommendations for the ethical and effective integration of AI into law enforcement practices.

title: AI governance as co-regulation: a practitioner-informed framework for defense-sector small and medium-sized enterprises
container-title: Digital Policy, Regulation and Governance
567df46acd778f8be8494c9ae84f8e44b8ec75da.abstract: Purpose This paper aims to examine how practitioners supporting defense-sector small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) place artificial intelligence (AI) governance within the coregulatory regime of National Institute of Standards and Technology Special Publication 800-171, the cybersecurity maturity model certification program, contracts and assessors. Design/methodology/approach An exploratory survey of 38 practitioners, recruited through a public LinkedIn post, combined a risk-to-control-family mapping task, artifact feasibility ratings and open-ended responses. Analysis was descriptive, with exploratory correlations adjusted for multiplicity and one researcher coded the open text. Findings Respondents concentrated AI risk on a few evidence-bearing control families, led by audit and accountability, risk assessment, access control and system and information integrity. Perceived compliance strain was high and readiness low. Artifacts resembling existing evidence, such as audit trail exports, were rated most feasible. Guidance ambiguity was the leading barrier. No exploratory association survived adjustment for multiplicity. Research limitations/implications The purposive sample and self-reported perceptions support pattern identification, not population estimates or claims about implementation outcomes. Practical implications Assessors and prime contractors could reduce SME burden by publishing exemplar AI evidence artifacts mapped to existing control families. Originality/value The study develops coregulation as a lens on the evidence burden of small firms at the base of regulatory chains, reports the full risk-to-control matrix and derives a seven-module framework that separates survey-supported elements from design choices.

title: Effectiveness evaluation of generative intelligent search: a comparative study with traditional search engine
container-title: Aslib Journal of Information Management
d1c9eeac798ccc7a8876d8762f5ec367e887920a.abstract: Purpose The emergence of generative artificial intelligence has transformed information retrieval, yet limited understanding of its differences from traditional search engines hinders clarity regarding changes in user search behavior and variations in search effectiveness, thereby impeding guidance for future search interface design. Design/methodology/approach We conducted a laboratory experiment comparing two versions of the Bing search engine: the traditional Bing search and the generative-AI integrated Bing (Bing Chat). We interpreted variations in user search behavior through querying, browsing, and clicking data, and established a multidimensional metric framework encompassing user, cost-benefit, and system dimensions to assess search effectiveness. 40 participants with good search skills completed the experiment, resulting in a final dataset comprising 160 observation records. Findings The Mann-Whitney U test revealed that users of generative AI search engines exhibited the following characteristics compared to those using traditional search engines: longer queries, more keyboard activity, more frequent query restructuring (including more narrowing queries, more following the system queries, and more changing the syntactic structure queries, with less broadening queries), more browsing during the first search session, and less scrolling and clicking. The results of the Linear Mixed Models show that, compared to traditional search engines, users achieve superior performance with generative AI search on users’ subjective perceptions and search efficiency metrics. Furthermore, we employed machine learning to validate which search behaviors can predict a user’s search effectiveness. The results indicate that the Gradient Boosting Machines are the optimal prediction models. The five most significant indicators for predicting search performance are Avelength. QueryConsTime, TimetofirSearch, ResViewTime and NumbofScroll. Research limitations/implications By revealing differences in user behavior and search efficiency across various search engines, this study deepens our understanding of generative AI search engines at a finer granularity and contributes to building adaptive search platforms capable of optimizing search recommendations. Originality/value By revealing differences in user behavior and efficiency between traditional and generative versions of the Bing search engine, this study deepens our understanding of generative AI search engines at a finer granularity and contributes to building adaptive search platforms capable of optimizing search recommendations.

title: Algorithmic cognitive programmes: observing ambient architectures of attention with social systems theory
container-title: Kybernetes
51d2013b2858e0715f8c03247ec8eb58d1d1a814.abstract: Purpose This paper extends Luhmann's concept of programmes – decision premises specifying the conditions under which a system's binary code is operatively assigned – into the domain of algorithmically mediated communication. It conceptualises recommendation systems, ranking algorithms and feedback architectures as ambient cognitive programmes: recursive, probabilistic selectors that perturb the structural coupling between social and psychic systems, and examines the constitutional implications of their opacity and transfunctional reach. Design/methodology/approach The study develops a systemic–cybernetic model grounded in Luhmann's social systems theory and the epistemology of autopoietic cognition, integrating Teubner's theory of societal constitutionalism to address the normative dimensions of algorithmic mediation. Analytical illustrations from Facebook and TikTok contrast two recommendation architectures – affinity-based cascading and behavioural-similarity propagation – to demonstrate how the model applies across distinct platform logics. Findings Algorithmic cognitive programmes operate as meta-programmes that reconfigure multiple forms of social differentiation simultaneously, enacting a binary operational distinction of visibility/invisibility through engagement metrics. Their colonisation of communicative environments – by economic imperatives and, as the analysis argues, by the autonomous logic of technical mediation – becomes a constitutional pathology where its effects cannot be contested or corrected, requiring internal self-limiting mechanisms that render operative selection criteria observable to affected systems. Originality/value The paper advances a novel theoretical category – ambient cognitive programmes – that extends Luhmann's organisational typology by identifying a configuration it does not explicitly address: a purpose programme without a terminal goal state that continuously revises the conditional programmes it governs. It connects this analytical framework to Teubner's societal constitutionalism, proposing constitutional observability as a structural condition for the compatibility between algorithmic regimes and communicative pluralism.

title: Cognitive load amongst emergency care students during simulation-based education: Findings from the Cognitive Load Assessment Scales–Simulation instrument
container-title: Health SA Gesondheid
5e99ff4049c21a6af99b7259af945faa2b3d8357.abstract: Background: Cognitive load (CL) is the demand placed on the working memory during various tasks. Cognitive load influences students’ ability to process information during simulation-based education. Limited evidence exists on CL amongst emergency care students in South Africa. Aim: To measure the CL Emergency Care Practitioner (ECP) students experience during a teaching simulation. Setting: A cross-sectional, quantitative pilot study was conducted with final-year ECP students at a South African University. Methods: Participants completed the validated Cognitive Load Assessment Scales–Simulation immediately after a homogeneous, high-fidelity teaching simulation. Mean scores for intrinsic load (IL), extraneous load (EL), germane load (GL) and overall CL were calculated. Internal consistency of each CL component was assessed using Cronbach’s alpha. Results: Eighteen students completed the survey (response rate: 86%). Mean scores were IL = 4.72, EL = 3.49, GL = 7.03 and overall CL = 5.08. Reliability analysis demonstrated acceptable internal consistency for EL (α = 0.847) and GL (α = 0.754), while IL showed low reliability (α = 0.458). Germane load was the dominant contributor to CL, indicating substantial mental effort directed towards processing and integrating learning during the simulation. Conclusion: Emergency Care Practitioner students reported moderate overall CL, with high GL suggesting strong engagement in meaningful learning. These findings highlight the importance of clear instructional design and structured cognitive support within emergency care simulations. Contribution: Understanding how emergency care students experience CL can guide educators in refining simulation design, reducing unnecessary cognitive burden and enhancing readiness for complex clinical practice.

title: Cognitive overload and governance failures in managerial dashboards: a qualitative study of how data misleads managerial judgement
container-title: International Journal of Organizational Analysis
495e6e06c7f13c84b632cdcaf00a1cae0b021f8d.abstract: Purpose The purpose of this research is to investigate how cognitive, interpretative, governance and integrity issues linked to dashboard-driven decision-making may distort the manager’s judgement. It seeks to identify ways in which these distortions can be countered through interventions based upon human-centric design and governance mechanisms. This research uses the concept of “Visual Authority Bias” as a sensitising lens to examine and mitigate dashboard-induced distortions in managerial judgement. Design/methodology/approach This study involves a qualitative research approach based on the use of key informant interviews in examining the relationship between human cognitive processes and digital performance measurement systems. Primary data were collected via 10 in-depth, semi-structured interviews conducted with experienced informants from various professional backgrounds such as HR, procurement, technology and operations. Transcripts from these interviews were analysed based on an inductive thematic analysis to provide an interpretive perspective on cognitive errors committed due to over-reliance on dashboards. Findings The analysis identifies four interrelated pitfalls in dashboard-mediated managerial decision-making: the Context–Data Disconnect, Interpretive Bias and the Black Box Problem, Institutional Failure and Governance Shielding and Data Integrity Failure. Across the interviews, visually authoritative outputs encouraged managers to treat incomplete or flawed metrics as objective accounts of organisational reality, overlook qualitative explanations, rely on heuristics and diffuse accountability. The findings indicate that these problems are socio-technical rather than purely technological. The study therefore proposes deliberate design-level cognitive friction, data validation and cross-functional review to help managers test dashboard outputs before acting on them. Originality/value This paper contributes to research in corporate governance and management control by redirecting focus from the technical optimisation of data to human fallibility in interpreting and using the data. Through the lens of dashboards not only as information management tools but also as mechanisms of accountability, this paper illustrates how data-based governance could go astray. This contribution is made in relation to the nascent discourse of Visual Authority Bias and its effects on decision-making.

title: A review of predictive maintenance strategies for Industry 5.0: AI, digital twins and human–machine collaboration
container-title: Journal of Quality in Maintenance Engineering
24d188956295cd9e7430988639ed3dfafe01a783.abstract: Purpose The purpose of this article is to provide a comprehensive review of predictive maintenance (PdM) strategies within the emerging Industry 5.0 paradigm, emphasizing the shift from automation-centric maintenance to human-centric, collaborative systems. The study aims to synthesize model-based, data-driven, artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled and hybrid PdM approaches, examine the role of key enabling technologies such as digital twins and edge computing and highlight human–machine collaboration in maintenance decision-making. By proposing a unified taxonomy, the article seeks to identify research gaps and guide the development of resilient, sustainable and explainable PdM systems. Design/methodology/approach This study adopts a structured systematic review methodology to analyze PdM strategies in the context of Industry 5.0. Peer-reviewed journal articles, standards and authoritative reports were identified through major scientific databases using predefined keywords related to PdM, condition-based maintenance, AI, digital twins and human–machine collaboration. The selected literature was critically examined and classified based on maintenance approach, enabling technologies, deployment architecture and degree of human involvement. Comparative analysis was employed to identify research gaps, challenges and emerging trends, culminating in the development of a novel taxonomy for Industry 5.0-oriented PdM systems. Findings The review reveals that PdM in Industry 5.0 is evolving toward hybrid frameworks that integrate data-driven intelligence with physics-based models and human expertise. While AI-based approaches improve diagnostic and prognostic accuracy, challenges related to data quality, interpretability and workforce acceptance persist. Digital twins, edge computing and collaborative robots emerge as key enablers for real-time, resilient and human-centric maintenance systems. The analysis highlights a lack of unified frameworks addressing human–machine collaboration and resilience, underscoring the need for explainable, lifecycle-oriented PdM solutions tailored to Industry 5.0 environments. Research limitations/implications This study is limited by its reliance on published literature, which may underrepresent proprietary industrial implementations and emerging practices not yet reported in academic sources. The review does not include empirical validation or quantitative benchmarking of PdM methods, focusing instead on conceptual and methodological synthesis. Nevertheless, the proposed taxonomy and identified research gaps provide a foundation for future empirical studies, experimental validation and large-scale industrial case analyses aimed at developing resilient, human-centric PdM frameworks aligned with Industry 5.0 principles. Practical implications The findings of this review offer practical guidance for industrial practitioners seeking to implement PdM within Industry 5.0 environments. The proposed taxonomy assists decision-makers in selecting appropriate PdM strategies based on system complexity, human involvement and technological readiness. Insights into digital twins, edge computing and human-in-the-loop AI support the design of maintenance systems that enhance reliability, reduce unplanned downtime and improve workforce acceptance. The study also highlights the importance of explainable and collaborative maintenance solutions to facilitate successful adoption in real-world manufacturing settings. Social implications By emphasizing human-centric and collaborative PdM, this study highlights the social impact of Industry 5.0 on the industrial workforce. The integration of human-in-the-loop decision-making and collaborative robots can improve workplace safety, reduce physically demanding tasks and support skill augmentation rather than job displacement. Transparent and explainable maintenance systems foster trust between workers and intelligent technologies, facilitating organizational acceptance and long-term adoption. Ultimately, Industry 5.0-oriented PdM contributes to more inclusive, resilient and sustainable industrial environments that align technological advancement with human well-being. Originality/value This article provides one of the first comprehensive reviews that explicitly situates PdM within the Industry 5.0 paradigm, moving beyond automation-centric perspectives. Its originality lies in the integration of PdM, condition-based maintenance, diagnostics and prognostics through a unified, human-centric lens. The study proposes a novel taxonomy that incorporates digital twins, edge computing and human–robot collaboration, offering a structured foundation for future research. By bridging technological, organizational and human factors, the article delivers both conceptual clarity and practical value for advancing next-generation maintenance systems.

title: Perceived fairness, accountability and transparency toward ML-based AI service delivery: conceptualization and measurement
container-title: Journal of Service Management
32ac1dcbe2ea84a31686f268ded2a0b816c7e9ab.abstract: Purpose This study conceptualizes and validates a multidimensional framework of consumers' perceived fairness, accountability and transparency (FAT) in machine learning (ML)-based AI service delivery. Addressing inconsistent conceptualizations and limited service-oriented measures, it examines how FAT perceptions emerge across goal-setting, coding and developing and implementation stages. A formative FAT scale is developed and tested for its predictive validity on trust and usage intention. Design/methodology/approach A multi-stage scale development process was used. Items were generated through literature review and 20 interviews, and face validity was assessed via an expert focus group. Two surveys (n = 448; n = 535) supported exploratory factor analysis (EFA), confirmatory factor analysis (CFA) and partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) validation of a reflective–formative FAT structure. A third survey (n = 455) established convergent and nomological validity with established FAT scales, trust and intention to use. Findings Results confirm FAT as a multidimensional construct shaped across goal-setting, coding and developing and implementation phases. All nine first-order factors significantly form the three higher-order FAT dimensions. The scale demonstrates strong reliability and validity, and fairness and transparency exhibit the strongest effects on trust and intention to use. Findings support a stage-based view of ethical perception in AI service delivery. Originality/value This research provides the first stage-based conceptualization and validated scale of perceived FAT in ML-based service AI. It integrates attribution theory with a socio-technical lens to disentangle how ethical judgments form throughout the AI lifecycle. The study advances theoretical clarity and offers actionable guidance for designing, developing and deploying ethically aligned AI services.

title: Exploring human–AI collaboration for management control in public healthcare
container-title: International Journal of Public Sector Management
14284e15945044815c9bcf6fc0c839ff33cdb032.abstract: Purpose This study examines how controllers in public healthcare envision human–AI collaboration in management control when dealing with uncertainty, complexity and equivocality, focusing on anticipated advantages and implementation challenges in an early-adoption setting. Design/methodology/approach We conducted an exploratory qualitative study with 14 controllers from Italian public healthcare organisations. Four closed-ended questions provided a preliminary picture of current AI adoption, while three scenario-based open-ended questions elicited prospective assessments. The framework method was used to analyse the data. Findings AI adoption remains limited and uneven, and is rarely embedded in everyday management control. Under uncertainty, controllers link AI to better forecasting and faster access to information, but worry about data quality, privacy and overreliance. In complex settings, they expect AI to help integrate diverse information and enable more systemic control, provided processes are standardised and human oversight remains. In equivocal situations, AI may support interpretation and communication, but its impact is limited by limited hands-on experience and the difficulty of codifying contextual nuances. Originality/value Based on the Jarrahi (2018) decision-making scenarios, the study develops a tentative conceptualisation of how public healthcare controllers envisage AI collaboration. The concerns of the participants inform three proposed arrangements: validation, recursive integration and contestable sensemaking. Their formulation and the accountability-augmentation principle are theoretical elaborations informed by prospective evidence and accountability research.

a19a1e035a788cb3d8c540693f606a9b8af1d629.abstract: <p>In the summer of 2020, the killing of George Floyd sparked Black Lives Matter protests which reverberated far beyond the United States. In Germany, these protests triggered an intense public reckoning with racism, which played out across traditional and social media platforms. Ana-Nzinga Weiß analysed this debate as it moved between political talk shows on public service broadcasting, YouTube, and Instagram, asking who gained visibility, authority, and legitimacy. The result is a nuanced account of how intersectional power relations shape democratic discourse in an increasingly hybrid media landscape.</p>

title: AI anthropomorphism, emotional attachment and verification behaviour in GenAI use
container-title: Online Information Review
69181986ddbed0224e43f9b1fb18cf320f342860.abstract: Purpose With the rapid advancement of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI), AI is increasingly perceived not merely as a tool but as a conversational partner. This study examines how AI anthropomorphism is associated with users’ verification of AI-generated information through emotional attachment. Design/methodology/approach A survey was conducted with 430 adult GenAI users in South Korea. The proposed mediation model was analysed using structural equation modelling. Findings Within the proposed structural model, AI anthropomorphism was positively associated with emotional attachment to AI, which was in turn positively associated with AI-generated information verification behaviour. AI anthropomorphism was also directly and positively associated with verification behaviour. The significant positive indirect association along the anthropomorphism–attachment–verification pathway suggests that the findings are more consistent with a cognitive vigilance pathway than with a cognitive illusion pathway. Rather than indicating that anthropomorphism and attachment reduce scrutiny, the results suggest that they are associated with greater verification effort. Originality/value This study narrows its empirical contribution to a mediation model linking AI anthropomorphism, emotional attachment and verification behaviour. It shows that emotional attachment to AI is not necessarily associated with reduced scrutiny, but may instead be linked to greater verification effort. Building on this finding, AI verification fatigue is repositioned as a promising theoretical extension for future research on the possible longer-term cognitive burden of repeated AI-generated information verification, rather than as an empirically demonstrated outcome of the present study.

title: “Servant of Two Masters!?” – a Critical Analysis of the Role of Football Clubs in the Principal–Agent Relationship Between Footballers and Player Agents
container-title: Sport und Gesellschaft
1fcceb7cbf92442d044b458ee5cf9c7b03b26b45.abstract: Summary The role of clubs in the relationship between association football players and player agents has received little attention in existing research, even though clubs typically bear the costs of agent remuneration. This study addresses this research gap by examining the role of clubs as well as the challenges and consequences associated with the specific constellation between football players, player agents, and clubs from the perspectives of players and agents. Drawing on principal–agent theory, we conducted semi-structured interviews with Bundesliga players (n = 10) and player agents (n = 12). The findings show that clubs play only a limited role in the initiation of player–agent relationships but exert a more substantial influence after contract conclusion through remuneration structures, transfer negotiations, and direct interactions with agents. Players report limited transparency regarding agreements between clubs and agents, while agents acknowledge their strategically central position and the financial incentives associated with transfers. The results indicate that the constellation is characterized by information asymmetries, limited sanctioning opportunities, and misaligned incentives. Overall, the findings suggest that the player–agent relationship is embedded in a triadic structure in which clubs indirectly shape incentives and information flows.

title: Generative AI Literacies and Discipline-Specific Knowledge: Preservice Teachers Planning Task-Based L2 Lessons with GenAI
container-title: Digital Studies in Language and Literature
49cfa4edc8a86155f27305dd81b772f6f0a87a1a.abstract: Abstract This study investigates the use of Large Language Models (LLMs) to support Task-Based Language Teaching (TBLT)-oriented lesson planning in a preservice teacher education context, examining the extent to which LLM use can contribute to the mobilisation of TBLT-related competencies. The case study draws on triangulated data from surveys, interaction logs with the LLM, lesson plans produced by preservice teachers and their reflections. The module required participants to generate a lesson plan with an LLM and to compare the resulting plan with a previously created lesson plan developed without AI support. The analysis focuses on knowledge of TBLT principles and their implementation during lesson planning, and the GenAI competence activated through the interaction with the LLM. The findings reveal considerable variation in how the dyads interacted with the LLM. Some dyads formulated more precise prompts and prompt iterations, provided more contextualised input, engaged more critically with the LLM-generated output, and iteratively refined their lesson plans in ways that appeared more consistent with TBLT principles. The data suggest an association between a stronger conceptual understanding of TBLT and more purposeful interaction with the LLM. This association indicates that disciplinary knowledge may facilitate the effective use of LLMs for TBLT-oriented lesson planning. Rather than replacing pedagogical expertise, LLM use appears to be most productive when preservice teachers are able to critically evaluate and adapt the generated output in light of established TBLT principles.

title: Encouraging the use of generative AI for closed-book test preparation: effects on student assessment performance and perceptions
container-title: Microbiology Australia
a89131b7b8180b129ba0fc050cf8b5278dbad42d.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is increasingly being used by university students to support learning. However, evidence from authentic classroom settings examining whether GenAI-assisted revision influences closed-book assessment performance remains limited. This study evaluated the educational use of Microsoft Copilot in a third-year undergraduate immunology course. Student performance was compared between the 2025 and 2026 cohorts using comparable closed-book assessments of identical format and similar difficulty. Before Test 2 in 2026, students were encouraged to use Copilot during structured revision activities. Following Test 2, students completed an anonymous survey examining their perceptions of using Copilot to support learning. No statistically significant differences were observed in Test 1 or Test 2 marks between cohorts. Although a higher proportion of students achieved higher grades in 2026, a similar trend was evident before the intervention. Survey results showed that 78% of students agreed that GenAI could support learning of complex scientific concepts when used appropriately. However, only 53% reported improved understanding of immunology concepts, 39% reported improved knowledge recall, and 71% expressed concerns regarding inaccurate or misleading Copilot-generated information. These findings suggest that although students recognise the educational value of GenAI, encouraging its use during revision alone may not improve subsequent closed-book assessment performance.

title: Use and perceptions of AI tools among Australian general practice registrars: a national survey
container-title: Journal of Primary Health Care
c3efd0b3647649ef143335193afd580c770d2a16.abstract: Introduction Artificial intelligence (AI) tools are increasingly used in health care, yet little is known about how often Australian general practitioner trainees (GP registrars) use them or how they perceive the impact of AI on training and clinical care. Aim This study aimed to examine how frequently registrars use AI tools for clinical care and education, types of AI used, the perceived benefits and risks, and training needs. Methods A national cross-sectional online survey conducted from 7 May to 4 June 2024 invited 3743 Australian General Practice Training or Fellowship Support Program registrars to participate. The survey assessed frequency and context of AI use, practice-level adoption, perceived impacts, training exposure, and ethical-legal concerns. Analyses were descriptive. Results Among the 727 respondents (19.5%), frequent use (weekly or more) was uncommon; 7.3% for clinical tasks, 5.0% for education. Practice-level adoption was low, with 10.8% reporting subscription to AI tools. Most registrars anticipated benefits, particularly learning efficiency and administrative workload reduction. However, 25.0% perceived increased medicolegal risk. Formal training was rare, with most relying on self-directed learning, though many rated AI education as important. Among clinical users, common tools included large language models (32.5%), remote patient monitoring devices (28.6%), and voice-to-text tools (26.2%). Large language models predominated in education (63.5%). Discussion In May–June 2024, AI tool use among registrars was limited, although most perceived potential benefit. Enthusiasm was tempered by concerns about safety, ethics, and legal risks. Structured training and guidelines are needed to support safe, effective integration into GP registrars’ practice and education.

title: Responsible AI and Structural Justice
da1087c38814e959c4bfbff69e0e4db0180d2fd1.abstract: This Element presents challenges of attributing responsibility for AI harms through political theories of structural injustice, where fault is broadly diffused and difficult to establish. I argue that AI systems feature complex structural entanglements between humans and machines-in computational architectures, organizational workflows, and societal data collectives-that pose problems for conventional liability where direct causal links are necessary for blame. I develop two modes of structural responsibility that address unjust AI outcomes from these entanglements. Thin structural responsibility traces where power and accountability lie in the processes of developing unjust AI systems. Thick structural responsibility enlists deployers, users, and broader publics alongside developers in collectively repairing unjust social conditions that produce and rely on AI systems. I show that many Responsible AI initiatives remain thin by demanding disclosures without systemic repair. Incorporating thicker reforms makes responsibility for just AI a living political practice rather than a managerial task. This title is also available as open access on Cambridge Core.

title: Performance-Driven Generative Design for Daylighting Optimization in a Tangerang Aerotropolis Office Building
container-title: DIMENSI: Journal of Architecture and Built Environment
faf1caa5c1813ed003b847519530da6d67dff4c7.abstract: Daylighting in tropical climates may increase glare risk in office buildings. This issue is particularly relevant in the Tangerang Aerotropolis area, where humid tropical conditions and airport operational safety regulations constrain building development. This study optimized daylighting performance in an office building using a Performance-Driven Generative Design approach. The workflow integrated Rhinoceros 3D, Grasshopper, ClimateStudio, and Galapagos to evaluate six envelopes and building mass variables. The optimization evaluated 950 design alternatives across 18 generations using UDI₁₀₀–₃₀₀₀ as the objective function. A maximum UDI₁₀₀–₃₀₀₀ of 95.5% was achieved with a WWR of 0.47, window height of 2.53 m, shading spacing and depth of 0.40 m, building width of 12 m, and orientation of 76°. Best-performing configurations converged within WWR 0.40–0.47, window height 2.50–2.60 m, shading spacing 0.30–0.50 m, shading depth 0.30–0.40 m, building width 12–13 m, and orientation 72°–84°. The results identified a high-performing configuration and recurring parameter ranges among the best-performing solutions.

title: Characterizing University Students’ Geometric Thinking Through Dialogues with Generative Artificial Intelligence in Geometry Transformation Learning
container-title: Jurnal Pendidikan Progresif
1c4a91710bc877408490a03a7a003f2d6291c53a.abstract: Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) has emerged as a promising technology for supporting mathematical dialogue, feedback, and reasoning in mathematics education. However, research has paid limited attention to how university students’ geometric thinking develops through sustained interaction with GenAI, particularly in geometry transformation learning. This study aims to develop a Dialogic Geometric Thinking Framework that characterizes the dimensions and progression of university students’ geometric thinking during sustained dialogue with ChatGPT. A qualitative exploratory design was employed involving undergraduate mathematics education students enrolled in a Geometry Transformation course at an Indonesian public university. Data were collected from student–ChatGPT dialogue transcripts, students’ written solutions, and reflective interviews. The data were analyzed thematically using reflexive thematic analysis to identify recurring characteristics and relationships among dimensions of geometric thinking and to synthesize them into an integrated framework. The findings identified five interrelated dimensions of geometric thinking: conceptual reasoning, representational coordination, procedural justification, reflective regulation, and mathematical elaboration. These dimensions illustrate how students progressively articulate mathematical concepts, coordinate representations, justify solution procedures, evaluate their reasoning, and extend mathematical ideas during AI-mediated dialogue. The study resulted in a Dialogic Geometric Thinking Framework that provides a process-oriented perspective on the development of university students’ geometric thinking during interaction with GenAI. The framework offers an initial theoretical foundation for understanding and further investigating geometric thinking in AI-mediated mathematics learning. Keywords: geometric thinking, generative artificial intelligence, chatGPT, geometry transformation, mathematical dialogue.

title: Designing Critical Human–AI Learning in Higher Education: The SC-AIM–FAVIC Framework for Analytical and Logical Reasoning
container-title: JPI: Jurnal Pustaka Indonesia
4ce99b9a5976c3c25eb4ecff905eaf4a200752ca.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) is now routine in university study, yet unstructured use risks cognitive offloading, surface learning, and uncritical acceptance of fluent but unreliable output. This article aimed to develop and specify the Symbiotic Critical Human–AI Learning Model (SC-AIM), operationalised through the five-stage FAVIC framework (Formulation, Augmentation, Verification, Integration, Creation), and to set out the assessment instruments and evaluation design that accompany it. Following the Analysis and Design phases of the ADDIE research-and-development approach, we synthesised recent experimental, meta-analytic, and survey evidence to derive design requirements, translated them into a stage-by-stage instructional specification, built a process-sensitive assessment rubric, and defined a quasi-experimental and qualitative validation plan for Indonesian higher education. The results are the model and its components: an evidence-to-design mapping, the FAVIC stage specification, a three-level process-sensitive rubric, and an evaluation design with hypotheses. Conclusion: SC-AIM offers lecturers a concrete, theory-grounded sequence that places human reasoning before and after AI assistance and makes verification an assessed activity, giving higher education a ready-to-use pedagogical model for developing analytical and logical reasoning in the age of generative AI.

title: A systematic review of theoretical perspectives frameworks and research gaps in AI localization for customer service
container-title: Discover Artificial Intelligence
9cf518f20dd7715f77bd6e5d242126f4273a5c11.abstract: Abstract Integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) into the operations of customer service has become an important strategic task for organizations aiming to improve their service quality, increase efficiency, and raise the level of customer satisfaction. However, the effective localization of AI technologies within organizational contexts continues to be a challenge especially in Arab countries due to certain contextual challenges such as organizational culture, infrastructure, and human capital. This paper provides a systematic review of the literature on AI localization in customer service by synthesizing the findings of 150 peer-reviewed articles published between 2015 and 2025 in Scopus, Web of Science, and IEEE Xplore. The review uses the PRISMA framework to ensure methodological rigor and reveals four key theoretical perspectives that underlie AI localization: Resource Dependence Theory (RDT), Resource-Based View (RBV), Continuous Improvement (CI), and Technology Acceptance Model (TAM). The synthesis reveals three categories of localization frameworks – governance-focused, collaborative adoption, and service improvement – as well as the key challenges across the dimensions of technical, organizational, cultural, and ethical. Three important research gaps emerge: (1) integration gap – the absence of the comprehensive frameworks addressing technological localization and its relation to service quality outcome, (2) mediation gap – the limited insight into the mechanisms of translation of AI into quality improvements, and (3) contextual gap – the lack of the research on AI localization in the Arab organizational context. The paper concludes with the research agenda for future studies in this field.

title: Bridging the gap between critical and applied approaches in the science of well-being: An analysis of evaluative subjective well-being measures
container-title: International Journal of Wellbeing
11f8fe901781b0cd80a57d0490f605bb98dc32e3.abstract: This article examines three recurring arguments for evaluative subjective well-being (swb) measures: instruments that ask respondents to broadly assess their lives, such as the Cantril Ladder and general life satisfaction questions. To organise the debate and support better dialogue between critics and supporters of these instruments, we draw on two conceptual tools from the philosophy of well-being: the distinction between constitutive and determinative questions, and the characterisation of well-being as a thick concept. The first argument we analyse holds that leaving the object undefined is desirable (a "non-paternalistic" approach). We argue that this stance legitimately declines the constitutive question about well-being, but that in delegating it to respondents it makes engagement with that question a precondition for interpreting the resulting scores. The second argument holds that the absence of a clear definition is not disqualifying, given large samples, respondents' familiarity with the relevant expressions, and the instruments' psychometric properties. We argue that each support admits an alternative explanation grounded in the social rules governing well-being talk, and that no thin, purely descriptive construct lies beneath the everyday expressions these measures rely on. The third argument holds that the measures are useful regardless of these limitations. Here we distinguish an agnostic stance, for which scores are a means of predicting other outcomes, from a score-as-target stance, for which raising the scores is itself the end. The agnostic stance declines constitutive questions successfully, at the price of abandoning well-being as the central object of research; the score-as-target stance cannot, since it must still say why this quantity rather than another deserves to be raised. From these analyses, we propose two practices to bridge critical and applied approaches: making constitutive commitments explicit, and exercising greater rigour in the use of words and expressions.

title: Algorithmic cognitive programmes: observing ambient architectures of attention with social systems theory
container-title: Kybernetes
51d2013b2858e0715f8c03247ec8eb58d1d1a814.abstract: Purpose This paper extends Luhmann's concept of programmes – decision premises specifying the conditions under which a system's binary code is operatively assigned – into the domain of algorithmically mediated communication. It conceptualises recommendation systems, ranking algorithms and feedback architectures as ambient cognitive programmes: recursive, probabilistic selectors that perturb the structural coupling between social and psychic systems, and examines the constitutional implications of their opacity and transfunctional reach. Design/methodology/approach The study develops a systemic–cybernetic model grounded in Luhmann's social systems theory and the epistemology of autopoietic cognition, integrating Teubner's theory of societal constitutionalism to address the normative dimensions of algorithmic mediation. Analytical illustrations from Facebook and TikTok contrast two recommendation architectures – affinity-based cascading and behavioural-similarity propagation – to demonstrate how the model applies across distinct platform logics. Findings Algorithmic cognitive programmes operate as meta-programmes that reconfigure multiple forms of social differentiation simultaneously, enacting a binary operational distinction of visibility/invisibility through engagement metrics. Their colonisation of communicative environments – by economic imperatives and, as the analysis argues, by the autonomous logic of technical mediation – becomes a constitutional pathology where its effects cannot be contested or corrected, requiring internal self-limiting mechanisms that render operative selection criteria observable to affected systems. Originality/value The paper advances a novel theoretical category – ambient cognitive programmes – that extends Luhmann's organisational typology by identifying a configuration it does not explicitly address: a purpose programme without a terminal goal state that continuously revises the conditional programmes it governs. It connects this analytical framework to Teubner's societal constitutionalism, proposing constitutional observability as a structural condition for the compatibility between algorithmic regimes and communicative pluralism.

title: Physics-guided long short-term memory–Transformer prediction of ship motion and broaching in oblique stern waves
container-title: Maritime Engineering
4ae3eb53e47dada75de7fa3aff1aff765aaef738.abstract: Accurate ship-motion prediction and early identification of unstable navigation states are essential for autonomous vessels operating in following-oblique waves. This study proposes a physics-guided long short-term memory (LSTM)–Transformer encoder–decoder model for joint motion prediction and surf-riding/broaching identification of an autonomous trimaran. Numerical simulation data are generated under different operating conditions, and physics-based state labels are constructed using the ship–wave speed ratio, heading deviation, yaw-rate response and rudder saturation. The proposed framework combines LSTM-based local temporal feature extraction with Transformer-based global dependency modelling. A state-identification branch is further introduced, and a multi-objective loss function is designed by integrating motion prediction, state classification, physical consistency and ordinal risk constraints. Comparative studies with different models and model variants are conducted to evaluate the prediction accuracy, robustness and generalisation capability of the proposed method. The results show that physically meaningful variables and state-related constraints strongly affect the prediction of navigation-state features. The proposed model improves both motion-response prediction and unstable-state identification, providing a more interpretable and reliable short-term forecasting framework for surf-riding and broaching conditions.

title: Cognitive load amongst emergency care students during simulation-based education: Findings from the Cognitive Load Assessment Scales–Simulation instrument
container-title: Health SA Gesondheid
5e99ff4049c21a6af99b7259af945faa2b3d8357.abstract: Background: Cognitive load (CL) is the demand placed on the working memory during various tasks. Cognitive load influences students’ ability to process information during simulation-based education. Limited evidence exists on CL amongst emergency care students in South Africa. Aim: To measure the CL Emergency Care Practitioner (ECP) students experience during a teaching simulation. Setting: A cross-sectional, quantitative pilot study was conducted with final-year ECP students at a South African University. Methods: Participants completed the validated Cognitive Load Assessment Scales–Simulation immediately after a homogeneous, high-fidelity teaching simulation. Mean scores for intrinsic load (IL), extraneous load (EL), germane load (GL) and overall CL were calculated. Internal consistency of each CL component was assessed using Cronbach’s alpha. Results: Eighteen students completed the survey (response rate: 86%). Mean scores were IL = 4.72, EL = 3.49, GL = 7.03 and overall CL = 5.08. Reliability analysis demonstrated acceptable internal consistency for EL (α = 0.847) and GL (α = 0.754), while IL showed low reliability (α = 0.458). Germane load was the dominant contributor to CL, indicating substantial mental effort directed towards processing and integrating learning during the simulation. Conclusion: Emergency Care Practitioner students reported moderate overall CL, with high GL suggesting strong engagement in meaningful learning. These findings highlight the importance of clear instructional design and structured cognitive support within emergency care simulations. Contribution: Understanding how emergency care students experience CL can guide educators in refining simulation design, reducing unnecessary cognitive burden and enhancing readiness for complex clinical practice.

title: Mapping the intellectual structure of privacy concern and information sharing behavior: a comprehensive bibliometric review
container-title: Global Knowledge, Memory and Communication
4ae11de12f9d21325ce6d87dc567e46ae9dfbb19.abstract: Purpose This paper aims to map the intellectual structure of research on privacy concern (PC) and information-sharing behavior (ISB). This study addresses a field that has grown across digital contexts but remains fragmented in its concepts, theories and research themes. Design/methodology/approach This study analyzes 862 publications indexed in the Web of Science database. It uses co-citation analysis to identify the knowledge base, bibliographic coupling to identify current research streams and keyword co-occurrence analysis to map recurring themes connecting PC and ISB. Findings The analysis identifies five main themes related to the foundations and measurement of PC, determinants of privacy-related disclosure decisions, the privacy paradox and the attitude–behavior gap, privacy governance and protection and advanced disclosure mechanisms in emerging digital environments. The findings of this study suggest that PC–ISB research has moved beyond a simple view of PC as a direct barrier to ISB. Recent studies explain this relationship through perceived value, privacy calculus, governance mechanisms, contextual conditions and emerging digital environments. Originality/value This study connects the knowledge base, current research streams and recurring concepts in the PC–ISB literature. This study shows that PC is usually examined as part of information sharing decision mechanisms, rather than only as a direct barrier to sharing. This study also proposes an integrative framework that places measurement foundations, decision mechanisms, governance, context and emerging digital environments in one model. This framework helps future studies identify where they can contribute to the PC–ISB literature.

title: Cognitive overload and governance failures in managerial dashboards: a qualitative study of how data misleads managerial judgement
container-title: International Journal of Organizational Analysis
495e6e06c7f13c84b632cdcaf00a1cae0b021f8d.abstract: Purpose The purpose of this research is to investigate how cognitive, interpretative, governance and integrity issues linked to dashboard-driven decision-making may distort the manager’s judgement. It seeks to identify ways in which these distortions can be countered through interventions based upon human-centric design and governance mechanisms. This research uses the concept of “Visual Authority Bias” as a sensitising lens to examine and mitigate dashboard-induced distortions in managerial judgement. Design/methodology/approach This study involves a qualitative research approach based on the use of key informant interviews in examining the relationship between human cognitive processes and digital performance measurement systems. Primary data were collected via 10 in-depth, semi-structured interviews conducted with experienced informants from various professional backgrounds such as HR, procurement, technology and operations. Transcripts from these interviews were analysed based on an inductive thematic analysis to provide an interpretive perspective on cognitive errors committed due to over-reliance on dashboards. Findings The analysis identifies four interrelated pitfalls in dashboard-mediated managerial decision-making: the Context–Data Disconnect, Interpretive Bias and the Black Box Problem, Institutional Failure and Governance Shielding and Data Integrity Failure. Across the interviews, visually authoritative outputs encouraged managers to treat incomplete or flawed metrics as objective accounts of organisational reality, overlook qualitative explanations, rely on heuristics and diffuse accountability. The findings indicate that these problems are socio-technical rather than purely technological. The study therefore proposes deliberate design-level cognitive friction, data validation and cross-functional review to help managers test dashboard outputs before acting on them. Originality/value This paper contributes to research in corporate governance and management control by redirecting focus from the technical optimisation of data to human fallibility in interpreting and using the data. Through the lens of dashboards not only as information management tools but also as mechanisms of accountability, this paper illustrates how data-based governance could go astray. This contribution is made in relation to the nascent discourse of Visual Authority Bias and its effects on decision-making.

title: With and Against the Archive
container-title: Image
e67334e93cc2a0d5a6dc9822519db1ff3bbfdb08.abstract: <p>Archives are used not only as powerful tools of domination from above: They have also been used from below, as sites of resistance against erasure. Especially in postcolonial, postpartition, and postwar contexts, contemporary artists often navigate a tension between appropriating the position of the archivist as an emancipatory act and problematizing that very position from a transnational perspective. In doing so, they develop forms of memory work that liberate the archive from its national frame. Rebecca Hanna John sheds light on this understudied aspect of the archival turn in art, showing how Akram Zaatari, Jumana Manna, and Farah Saleh critically engage with archives in order to tell stories of transnational trajectories and entanglements.</p>

title: Acting Out at the Movies: Enacting Actions Enhances Memory For Action Descriptions But Does Not Improve Memory or Segmentation of Movies
1995b8b5d7dee1a157dc77ea0ddca99800586ddb.abstract: Abstract Performing actions boosts memory for descriptions of those actions; this is called the “enactment effect.” The enactment effect has been repeatedly found with verbal materials, but it is unclear if this effect generalizes to naturalistic materials that include linked sequences of actions and multimodal information. In four preregistered studies, we tested for enactment effects using naturalistic movies. Experiment 1 successfully replicated the enactment effect using descriptions of actions from the movies. In Experiment 2, participants read or acted out action descriptions and then watched a movie including those actions; no enactment effect was found. In Experiment 3, participants watched the movies while simultaneously copying the actions that the actors performed; again, no enactment effect was observed. Finally, Experiment 4 examined whether enactment affected how movies were segmented into meaningful events; once again, no enactment effect was observed. These results suggest that during naturalistic comprehension viewers may obligatorily engage motor simulations, rendering enactment manipulations redundant and thus ineffective.

title: Allez les pères, encore un petit effort !

Printable Monolayer
of Binary Polymer-Co-Grafted Au
Nanoparticles for Nano-Floating-Gate Transistor Memory
container-title: Polymer Science & Technology
3906c9d1be53932a31668d0d3a29b75179b2d549.abstract: Abstract Nano-floating-gate organic field-effect transistor (NFGOFET) memories are promising candidates for flexible, low-cost, and solution-processable nonvolatile memory devices. Their performance relies critically on the construction of a uniform nano-floating-gate/tunneling-dielectric (NFG/TD) layer, in which discrete nanoparticles serve as charge-storage sites and the surrounding polymer matrix functions as the tunneling dielectric. However, the solution processing of the upper organic semiconductor layer often causes solvent-induced erosion of polymer tunneling layers, disrupting the nanoparticle distribution and degrading charge transport and storage. Here, we report a solvent-resistant NFG/TD layer based on binary polymer-co-modified gold nanoparticles and in situ SiO2 interfacial engineering. Gold nanoparticles co-grafted with polystyrene and poly(4-vinylpyridine) form a printable monolayer in which polystyrene serves as the tunneling dielectric and poly(4-vinylpyridine) provides anchoring sites for TEOS hydrolysis. The SiO2 layer preserves the nanoparticle monolayer during active-layer printing and provides a stable inorganic tunneling barrier and a modifiable interface for improving semiconductor crystallization. This work establishes a general and scalable interfacial regulation strategy for the solution-process of printable multi-layered organic thin-film devices.

title:
Mechanism-guided large-grain design of Sc–Ce co-doped BaCoO
                    <sub>3</sub>

container-title: Journal of Advanced Ceramics
3875bbda28b5f83b1cf2e1e6d066efe83d27291f.abstract: Abstract Conventional oxygen electrode designs for protonic ceramic cells (PCCs) predominantly rely on the empirical notion that maximizing specific surface area inherently enhances electrochemical performance. However, this paradigm overlooks the critical mismatch between the electrode microstructure and the intrinsic rate-determining step (RDS) of the proton-coupled oxygen-reduction reaction (PC-ORR). In this study, we present a mechanism-driven microstructure engineering strategy that deliberately favors large-particle architectures over nanoscale morphologies to optimize performance when proton transport, rather than surface reaction kinetics, governs the electrode process. By employing Sc–Ce co-doping in BaCoO3, Sc stabilizes the cubic perovskite lattice, while supersaturated Ce induces spontaneous in situ phase reconstruction, yielding a dual-phase composite electrode composed of ~80 wt% Co-rich cubic catalytic framework and ~20 wt% BaCeO3-based nanoscale proton-conducting fillers. Comprehensive electrode reaction pathway analysis reveals that Ce doping shifts the proton migration mechanism from hydration-dehydration to hydrogenation-dehydrogenation, thereby repositioning the RDS to be proton transport-dominated rather than surface-ORR-controlled. Guided by this insight, micrometer-sized particles are employed to establish continuous proton conduction channels. The optimized BaCo0.7Sc0.1Ce0.2O3−δ electrode demonstrates an ultralow polarization resistance of 0.138 Ω·cm2 at 600 °C, stable operation exceeding 120 h, a peak power density of 2.28 W·cm−2 in fuel cell (FC) mode, and an electrolysis current density of 2.96 A·cm−2 at 700 °C, performance metrics that surpass most reported Co-based PCC oxygen electrodes. This work establishes a broadly applicable, mechanism-aligned microstructure design paradigm, challenging the assumption that a high surface area is invariably the dominant design parameter. This study provides critical guidance for the rational development of advanced protonic ceramic electrochemical devices.

title: Genetic Sovereignty within the System of Functions of Public Authorities: A Doctrinal Model and Transboundary Reality
container-title: State power and local self-government
42c371b089f2969626af071584d4b5520025afae.abstract: This article demonstrates the qualitative impact of the development of genomic technologies on national security, which is leading to the emergence of new functions for government agencies. It is argued that the accumulation of human genetic data, its use for various social purposes, and the growing dependence of personalized medicine on information about human biology have led to the transition of genetics from a fundamental science to a critical factor in state sovereignty. The specific aspects of the sovereignty of human genetic data are highlighted. A comparative legal study of the concept of genetic sovereignty is conducted (using the examples of Mexico and China).

title: Implications of Digital Resources on English Language Pedagogy in Jigawa State Senior Secondary Schools
container-title: JALINGO JOURNAL OF LINGUISTICS AND LITERARY STUDIES
ba804c9984b3cf65b1b475f13493c596ba063ab7.abstract: The importance of digital resources in teaching and learning language has been widely recognized as a catalyst for fostering improved language proficiency. Despite the advantages, most schools in Nigeria grapple with different impediments for proper digital integration. This paper assesses the availability of the digital resources in teaching and learning English in Jigawa State Senior Secondary Schools. The two inter-related objectives are to find out the availability of both hardware and software resources in the selected schools and the types of the digital resources being used in the selected schools in the teaching and learning of the English language. The study adopts descriptive design using purposive sampling the total of sixty students (distributed as 10 per school) are selected from the six sampled schools. The schools are also purposively selected two per each senatorial district to represent the three senatorial districts that made up the Jigawa State. As for the teachers, two teachers of English language are selected in each of the schools. This makes the total number of teacher-respondents as twelve (12). Questionnaires are designed in two forms. One form of the questionnaires is administered to teachers, while the second form is administered to the students. The analysis is done using percentage and frequency. The findings indicated that while there has been an average distribution and provision of digital resources for teaching and learning purposes, there has not been specific provision of such resources for the purpose of teaching and learning English. Also, the results indicated that most of the resources available are in hardware forms, while the software resources are not adequately provided. It recommended that policies and decisions by the governments and other stakeholders should be tailored to consider the provision of language learning resources and also the provision of digital resources should focus more on software resources.

title: Minimalism and Language Functions in the Language Classroom: An Overview of Chomsky’s Position and Its Pedagogical Implications
container-title: JALINGO JOURNAL OF LINGUISTICS AND LITERARY STUDIES
ca112a2636b72b20699129029455a5accf89f935.abstract: This paper examines the relationship between Chomsky’s Minimalist Program and language functions in the language classroom. The study is motivated by a persistent theoretical and pedagogical question: how can a formal theory concerned primarily with the structure and computation of language be related to classroom practices in which learners use language for communicative, interpersonal, cognitive and social purposes? The paper adopts a qualitative, library-based conceptual research design. Scholarly works published mainly from 2000 to 2026 were purposively selected and thematically synthesized, while foundational works were retained where necessary to establish the historical development of the concepts under investigation. The analysis is organized around three related perspectives: Minimalist syntax, particularly competence, syntactic computation and Merge; functional approaches to language, particularly Hallidayan systemic functional linguistics; and contemporary research on classroom discourse and language pedagogy. The review finds that Minimalism and functional approaches address different analytical dimensions of language. Minimalism provides an account of the computational and structural resources through which linguistic expressions are constructed, whereas functional approaches explain how speakers deploy those resources to accomplish communicative purposes in context. The analysis further demonstrates that the seven functions considered in the paper: informatative, instrumental, regulatory, interactional, personal, heuristic and imaginative, cannot be mapped mechanically onto individual syntactic structures. Rather, a single structure can realise different functions depending on context, and a single function can be realised through different grammatical forms. The paper therefore argues for a complementary, rather than conflated, relationship between formal and functional perspectives. In classroom practice, grammatical instruction can be strengthened when teachers connect form with meaning, communicative purpose and context. The paper recommends that language teaching should integrate structural awareness with opportunities for authentic functional language use, while teacher education should equip teachers to distinguish grammatical form from communicative function and to recognise the multifunctionality of classroom discourse.

title: Language, Artificial Intelligence and Teacher Education: Bridging the Linguistic Gap
container-title: JALINGO JOURNAL OF LINGUISTICS AND LITERARY STUDIES
a7ec9ba1d60e71569119f7d63217b5f0548aae7c.abstract: Language difference can limit participation and understanding in multilingual classrooms, particularly where the language of instruction differs from learners’ home language. This paper examines how artificial intelligence (AI) can support teacher education in addressing language barriers in multilingual Nigerian classrooms. Specifically, it explores the use of AI for translation, language practice, individualised learning and the development of multilingual teaching resources. This study is guided by a conceptual framework drawing on relevant literature on language education, AI, teacher education and Nigerian language policies. The research design was qualitative and conceptual review using secondary data sources on artificial intelligence, language education, multilingualism, teacher education and Nigerian indigenous languages. A thematic review of journal papers, research articles, policy papers and other contemporary writings was undertaken, with particular attention given to data sources published recently in Nigerian literature. The findings indicates that AI tools can improve access to learning materials, support language practice and promote communication across languages. However, their effectiveness depends on the availability of reliable digital language resources, the accuracy of AI-generated content and teachers’ digital literacy. The limited representation of Nigerian indigenous languages in digital resources remain a major challenge. This work concludes that AI can promote more inclusive multilingual education when used to support, rather than replace, teachers. It recommends strengthening teachers’ digital skills, promoting collaboration among linguists, language educators and technology developers, and investing in digital resources for Nigerian indigenous languages.

title: Hausa Language Practices and Audience Engagement in Facebook Journalism: A Study of News Production in Sokoto State, Nigeria
container-title: JALINGO JOURNAL OF LINGUISTICS AND LITERARY STUDIES
22ea48ffdd785e4cfb4ce0e95e4c97a5c445ef04.abstract: The growing use of social media for news production and distribution has created new opportunities for indigenous-language journalism, particularly in multilingual societies such as Nigeria. However, limited research has examined how linguistic practices in Hausa digital journalism relate to audience engagement and how journalists explain their language choices. This study examines Hausa language practices and audience engagement in Facebook journalism in Sokoto State, Nigeria. Guided by Audience Design Theory, the study adopts an explanatory sequential mixed-methods design, combining quantitative content analysis of 360 Hausa news posts from six digital news platforms with semi-structured interviews involving 12 journalists and digital content producers. The findings reveals that standard Hausa is the most common dominant linguistic pattern, followed by Hausa-English combinations, borrowed terminology, local expressions and orthographic variations. A chi-square test indicates a statistically significant association between dominant linguistic patterns and audience engagement, although the effect size is small. The interview findings identify audience accessibility, familiarity with contemporary terminology, headline construction and audience feedback as important considerations in language selection. The study concludes that Hausa digital journalism combines established linguistic practices with multilingual and digitally adapted expressions, while audience engagement reflects factors beyond language choice alone. It recommends developing practical Hausa digital writing guidelines, strengthening journalists' training in indigenous-language digital communication and using audience feedback to improve news presentation without compromising accuracy and clarity.

title: Morphosyntactic Deviations in Written French among Multilingual University Learners at the Nigeria French Language Village
container-title: JALINGO JOURNAL OF LINGUISTICS AND LITERARY STUDIES
47c2a6298d97ba119578abfd8ab9e487b23ab8d1.abstract: This study examined morphosyntactic deviation patterns in the written French of 300-level students during their immersion programme at the Nigeria French Language Village (NFLV), Badagry. Although previous research has documented selected deviation types among Nigerian learners of French, the literature reviewed did not reveal a study combining a written corpus of NFLV learners with an integrated morphosyntactic classification across four domains. The study analysed 160 timed compositions produced by 80 undergraduates from diverse Nigerian linguistic backgrounds. Drawing on Corder’s Error Analysis, Selinker’s Interlanguage Theory, and Odlin’s Cross-Linguistic Influence framework, the study identified and classified deviations involving noun phrase agreement, prepositional and verbal rection, verb morphology and tense–aspect, and syntactic structure. The corpus yielded 542 coded deviation tokens. Noun phrase agreement constituted the largest category (31.0%), followed by prepositional and verbal rection (26.0%), verb morphology and tense–aspect (23.1%), and syntactic structure (19.9%). Several patterns were compatible with English or indigenous-language influence, while others were consistent with French overgeneralisation. These interpretations were treated cautiously because the corpus could not establish individual-level causation. The study recommends four interventions: explicit Focus-on-Form instruction, contrastive consciousness-raising, structured post-editing, and continuous diagnostic assessment. It concludes that immersion programmes require systematic grammatical support to help multilingual learners develop both communicative fluency and structural accuracy in written French.

title: Outsourced social media marketing transformation: an agency-side mechanism framework for agency–client coordination
container-title: Journal of Business & Industrial Marketing
dc79ce67857b9f787610ff6de38c8b87d5713943.abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine how agency professionals describe the structuring, governance and coordination of outsourced social media marketing transformation (SMMT) across the agency-client boundary. Design/methodology/approach A qualitative research approach was used, involving 16 semi-structured interviews conducted with professionals from digital agencies. The interview guide focused on two primary themes: the initiation of client–agency relationships and the diagnosis of outsourced SMMT needs; as well as the implementation, validation and management of social media strategies and communities. Findings The analysis develops an agency-side mechanism framework of outsourced SMMT. The framework links reciprocal knowledge asymmetry with resource complementarity, distributes decision rights through role allocation, locates client brand control in validation and feedback and connects operational evidence with strategic adaptation through reporting. Across repeated engagements, governance may move from formal controls toward more relational coordination as trust develops. Originality/value The study conceptualizes governed complementarity as the condition in which cross-boundary specialization simultaneously creates value potential, mutual dependence and a need for control. The framework explains how role allocation, boundary validation, feedback and performance learning organize this tension as an adaptive governance cycle. Developed from the accounts of agency professionals, the framework explains the agency side of coordination and provides a basis for subsequent dyadic examination.

title: A sustainable natural resource management hierarchical model in Vietnamese mining industry: environmental policy and regulation impacts on technical operation capability
container-title: Management of Environmental Quality: An International Journal
b798cff29ef7d3a5872fd4faf749d03c0a06d4fe.abstract: Purpose This study builds a sustainable natural resource management (SNRM) model, as prior studies on how environmental policy and regulation and stakeholder involvement incorporate technical operation capability are lacking, and comprehensive insights into the specific challenges and strategies for SNRM practices are needed. Design/methodology/approach This study aims to identify a valid set of attributes for SNRM in the Vietnamese mining industry, develop a causal hierarchical model and identify the important attributes for improvement via a hybrid approach. Institutional theory, stakeholder theory and dynamic capability theory under the foundation of the socio-technical perspective theory are applied. Findings The hierarchical structure of SNRM includes 4 perspectives, 8 aspects and 22 criteria, with causal aspects such as environmental policy and regulation, financing mechanisms, stakeholder involvement and digital transformation. The practical focuses are environmental governance, green financing, external suppliers and joint venture partners, renewable energy adoption, and automation and robotics. Technological innovation plays crucial roles in SNRM adoption. Originality/value This study develops a theoretically grounded causal SNRM framework integrating institutional, stakeholder, dynamic capability and socio-technical perspectives, while extending SNRM through technological innovation and operation capability. The result provides a context-specific framework for the Vietnamese mining industry and offers actionable priorities for policymakers and practitioners to advance sustainable resource management.

title: A Sociolinguistic Interpretation of Yorùbá Language Speakers’ Attitudes towards Skin Diseases among Secondary School Students in Iwo, Osun State
container-title: JALINGO JOURNAL OF LINGUISTICS AND LITERARY STUDIES
8ec912f09270de9193c5e4f45243aef8d95136dc.abstract: This study investigates the sociolinguistics of skin disease expressions among secondary school students in Iwo, examining cultural attitudes, their effects on social interaction and psychological well-being, and implications for health communication. Anchored in Goffman's stigma theory, stigma as a discrediting attribute causing status loss and interactional disruption, and the Health Belief Model, it conceptualizes language as the medium through which perceived severity, susceptibility, and barriers to inclusion are communicated and internalized. Of 280 questionnaires, 240 were returned (85.7%). Twenty-four students were purposively selected for focus group discussions. Quantitative data were analyzed using frequencies, percentages, means, standard deviations, one-way ANOVA, and simple linear regression; qualitative data underwent thematic sociolinguistic analysis based on the framework theories. Findings revealed dominant use of Yorùbá expressions blended with biomedical and descriptive terms, many encoding misconceptions that drive stigma. Attitudes varied significantly by class, F (2, 237) = 4.27, p = .015, and significantly predicted social interaction and psychological well-being, β = .561, p < .001, R² = .315. Participants proposed school-based health education, respectful language, bilingual communication, and sustained campaigns as remedies. The study concludes that language is a modifiable determinant of health perceptions and inclusion, and that targeting terminology can disrupt stigma at its source and promote equitable outcomes. Accordingly, it recommends (1) co-development by schools and health authorities of a bilingual Yorùbá–English glossary of non-stigmatizing skin disease terms for integration into health education curricula, and (2) institutionalization of sustained awareness campaigns and respectful language training for teachers/staff as school health communication policy.
