title: Unpacking the eco-innovation pathway to global success: a multivariate model of international performance
container-title: International Journal of Innovation Science
e1458ffd4c25dbe542419485161c7c69f2900d06.abstract: Purpose This study aims to investigate the role of eco-innovation (EI) as a mechanism transmitting the effects of internal Eco-capabilities to international performance. Integrating innovation science with sustainable strategic management, this study examines the interplay between stakeholder pressure (SP), sustainable entrepreneurship orientation (SEO), Eco-HR and organization capabilities (OCs), EI and international performance (IP). Design/methodology/approach Cross-sectional study using a survey distributed among senior managers working in large international companies in Egypt, that practice eco-activities. A total number of 158 valid surveys were used to assess and test the model using SEM-PLS. Findings The results of this study indicate that EI, Eco-HR and OC are significant predictors for IP. Furthermore, SEO has direct and indirect impacts on EI through Eco-HR and OC. Moreover, the SP considered a significant antecedent for SEO in companies. Originality/value This study is among the limited to examine EI within a unified framework to explain international business performance. By highlighting the mediating role of EI, this study offers novel insights into how firms can strategically integrate sustainability into their innovation practices to gain an international edge.

title: An empirical investigation of factors influencing inbound tourism to India: a gravity model approach
container-title: Journal of Hospitality and Tourism Insights
f306b9fe5a66068840505a46b3e81d599b70c282.abstract: Purpose The present study aims to examine the key economic, institutional and structural factors associated with foreign tourist arrivals (FTAs) to India using a panel gravity model of tourism demand. The study specifically investigates the role of per capita GDP, tourism openness, economic remoteness, relative price competitiveness, political instability and pandemic-related shocks in shaping tourism demand from major source countries. Design/methodology/approach The study utilizes a panel dataset comprising 15 major source countries over the period 1997–2022. A sequential econometric approach was adopted to ensure robust empirical inference. Fixed effects estimation was employed to control for unobserved country-specific heterogeneity, while Driscoll–Kraay standard errors were used to account for cross-sectional dependence, heteroskedasticity and serial correlation. The Poisson pseudo maximum likelihood (PPML) estimator was employed as a robustness check. Panel unit root and co-integration tests were also conducted to assess the statistical properties of the data. Findings The findings indicate that per capita GDP and tourism openness of source countries are positively and significantly associated with foreign tourist arrivals to India, highlighting the importance of income growth and international tourism integration. In contrast, economic remoteness and pandemic shocks significantly reduce tourism demand. The relative price index and political instability exhibit comparatively weaker and less consistent effects across model specifications. The broad consistency of results across fixed effects, Driscoll–Kraay and PPML estimations supports the robustness of the empirical findings. Research limitations/implications The findings suggest that tourism policy should focus on strengthening engagement with major tourism-generating markets, improving destination accessibility and travel connectivity, facilitating international tourist mobility and strengthening preparedness for global tourism disruptions. The results also highlight the importance of maintaining supportive institutional conditions and improving resilience in India's inbound tourism sector. Practical implications Both at the macro and destination levels, several useful policy implications emerge from the findings of the present study. The empirical results highlight the importance of income levels, tourism openness, travel connectivity, institutional conditions and tourism resilience in shaping international tourism demand for India. Since higher income levels and tourism openness in source countries positively influence tourist inflows, India may strengthen its engagement with major tourism-generating economies through improved tourism promotion strategies and enhanced tourism connectivity. The negative influence of economic remoteness further indicates the importance of improving accessibility, transportation infrastructure and travel convenience for international tourists. In this regard, continued investment in airport modernization, multimodal transport systems, tourism infrastructure and digital tourism services may help improve international tourist accessibility and destination attractiveness. Similarly, findings relating to tourism openness and mobility facilitation suggest that strengthening visa liberalization measures, simplifying travel procedures and expanding the e-visa framework may further support inbound tourism flows to India. The study also highlights the importance of tourism resilience and institutional preparedness amid global shocks such as the COVID-19 pandemic. Therefore, tourism policy should increasingly focus on crisis preparedness, adaptive tourism planning, digital tourism services, health-related travel confidence and resilient tourism infrastructure to minimize the adverse effects of future disruptions on tourism-related employment and economic activities. Overall, the findings suggest that policies aimed at improving destination accessibility, facilitating international tourist mobility, maintaining a supportive and predictable tourism policy environment and strengthening tourism resilience should remain central to tourism planning and policy formulation in India. Originality/value The study contributes to the application of gravity-based tourism literature by integrating institutional risk, tourism openness and global shock dimensions within a unified panel gravity framework for an emerging tourism economy. The study provides a context-specific empirical assessment of inbound tourism demand in India and offers implications for tourism policy, destination competitiveness and tourism resilience.

title: Business model and sustainability perspectives framework for ICT – illustrated by joint communications and sensing in 6G
container-title: Journal of Business Models
2759080068820e07c3458ea7b433bc06a8417cda.abstract: Purpose Business models and sustainability perspectives help us understand new information and communication technology (ICT) solutions. This paper proposes a framework for studying business models and sustainability in ICTs, with a focus on sixth-generation (6G) mobile communications. Design/methodology/approach The framework combines business model antecedents – opportunity, value, and advantage – with environmental, social, and economic pillars of sustainability. Findings The paper offers a holistic approach to studying business models and sustainability in ICTs. Originality/value It highlights the potential of 6G technologies, particularly joint communications and sensing, to support sustainable development.

title: Algorithmic cognitive programmes: observing ambient architectures of attention with social systems theory
container-title: Kybernetes
51d2013b2858e0715f8c03247ec8eb58d1d1a814.abstract: Purpose This paper extends Luhmann's concept of programmes – decision premises specifying the conditions under which a system's binary code is operatively assigned – into the domain of algorithmically mediated communication. It conceptualises recommendation systems, ranking algorithms and feedback architectures as ambient cognitive programmes: recursive, probabilistic selectors that perturb the structural coupling between social and psychic systems, and examines the constitutional implications of their opacity and transfunctional reach. Design/methodology/approach The study develops a systemic–cybernetic model grounded in Luhmann's social systems theory and the epistemology of autopoietic cognition, integrating Teubner's theory of societal constitutionalism to address the normative dimensions of algorithmic mediation. Analytical illustrations from Facebook and TikTok contrast two recommendation architectures – affinity-based cascading and behavioural-similarity propagation – to demonstrate how the model applies across distinct platform logics. Findings Algorithmic cognitive programmes operate as meta-programmes that reconfigure multiple forms of social differentiation simultaneously, enacting a binary operational distinction of visibility/invisibility through engagement metrics. Their colonisation of communicative environments – by economic imperatives and, as the analysis argues, by the autonomous logic of technical mediation – becomes a constitutional pathology where its effects cannot be contested or corrected, requiring internal self-limiting mechanisms that render operative selection criteria observable to affected systems. Originality/value The paper advances a novel theoretical category – ambient cognitive programmes – that extends Luhmann's organisational typology by identifying a configuration it does not explicitly address: a purpose programme without a terminal goal state that continuously revises the conditional programmes it governs. It connects this analytical framework to Teubner's societal constitutionalism, proposing constitutional observability as a structural condition for the compatibility between algorithmic regimes and communicative pluralism.

title: Wax Crystallization in Model and Crude Oils: Linking Time-Domain Nuclear Magnetic Resonance and Calorimetry to Hydrocarbon Composition
container-title: Energy & Fuels
d0ab1a34383e573286e623abd2b8c6640226f53e.abstract: Abstract Wax crystallization changes both the observable proton population and the mobility of the remaining liquid in crude oils. This study combines time-domain nuclear magnetic resonance (TD-NMR), microcalorimetry (μDSC), gas chromatography, and high-resolution mass spectrometry to examine these responses in n-C26/n-C36 model oils and four Brazilian crude oils. Carr−Purcell−Meiboom−Gill (CPMG) decays were corrected using liquid USP mineral oil (United States Pharmacopeia) before inverse Laplace transformation, preserving the amplitude information used to calculate an apparent rigid fraction. Samples underwent thermal conditioning at 80 °C for 30 min; TD-NMR measurements were acquired isothermally at 2 °C intervals, with cooling segments of 0.8 °C min−1. Model oils exhibited progressive signal loss without resolved multiple relaxation regimes, whereas crude oils developed additional short-T2 contributions. The TD-NMR onset estimates were 37, 49, 51, and 47 °C for oils A−D, respectively, compared with μDSC wax appearance temperatures of 37.7, 50.2, 54.5, and 49.8 °C. At 4 °C, apparent rigid contents were 2.47–7.28% by TD-NMR and estimated crystallized fractions were 2.58–7.06% by μDSC, with differences of at most 0.27 percentage point. Carbon-number profiles of the HC[H] class with double-bond equivalent zero revealed a broader high-carbon-number contribution in crude oil C, despite its lower total saturate content than oils B and D. The combined analysis links signal loss and relaxation redistribution to hydrocarbon composition and distinguishes the detection of an onset from the subsequent accumulation of crystallized material.

title: Multi-agency risk information sharing and risk assessment in the United Kingdom: a preliminary empirical investigation of practitioner perspectives
container-title: International Journal of Disaster Resilience in the Built Environment
5e968e2823e2837dfc39ff065fa8b78f536fcdc0.abstract: Purpose This exploratory paper aims to examine how emergency agency practitioners in the UK understand, conduct and share risk assessments, with the aim of identifying gaps and areas for systemic improvement. The study is positioned as an exploratory, preliminary empirical investigation: many of the gaps identified are already recognised within practice, and the paper’s principal contribution is to provide empirical, practitioner-grounded evidence confirming and elaborating these long-standing challenges. Design/methodology/approach A preliminary, qualitative, interpretivist study drawing on semi-structured interviews with eight senior professionals from five statutory emergency agencies (environment agency, fire and rescue, police, local government and ambulance service). Data were analysed using a framework analysis approach structured around the UK National Risk Assessment (NRA) six-step process. Findings The study identifies pervasive fragmentation across all stages of the risk assessment cycle, including the absence of shared geospatial risk and vulnerability data; divergent epistemological frameworks impeding joint assessment; local resilience forums functioning primarily as compliance mechanisms; historical bias in hazard review with limited horizon scanning; siloed risk treatment planning; and inconsistent, agency-bounded monitoring and review processes. Because agencies assess risks independently using different methods and criteria, cross-sector cascading risks are not modelled jointly; this is highlighted as a key practical implication. Many of the gaps will be familiar to practitioners; the study contributes preliminary empirical evidence that confirms and locates them across the NRA cycle. Originality/value The paper contributes exploratory, practitioner-grounded evidence to scholarship on interoperability, cross-agency vulnerability assessment and the governance of risk information in complex multi-hazard environments. It extends existing interoperability frameworks by adding an epistemological dimension, relates this dimension to risk governance and knowledge-boundary literature and provides an initial multi-agency mapping of gaps across all six stages of the UK NRA process.

title: Cognitive load amongst emergency care students during simulation-based education: Findings from the Cognitive Load Assessment Scales–Simulation instrument
container-title: Health SA Gesondheid
5e99ff4049c21a6af99b7259af945faa2b3d8357.abstract: Background: Cognitive load (CL) is the demand placed on the working memory during various tasks. Cognitive load influences students’ ability to process information during simulation-based education. Limited evidence exists on CL amongst emergency care students in South Africa. Aim: To measure the CL Emergency Care Practitioner (ECP) students experience during a teaching simulation. Setting: A cross-sectional, quantitative pilot study was conducted with final-year ECP students at a South African University. Methods: Participants completed the validated Cognitive Load Assessment Scales–Simulation immediately after a homogeneous, high-fidelity teaching simulation. Mean scores for intrinsic load (IL), extraneous load (EL), germane load (GL) and overall CL were calculated. Internal consistency of each CL component was assessed using Cronbach’s alpha. Results: Eighteen students completed the survey (response rate: 86%). Mean scores were IL = 4.72, EL = 3.49, GL = 7.03 and overall CL = 5.08. Reliability analysis demonstrated acceptable internal consistency for EL (α = 0.847) and GL (α = 0.754), while IL showed low reliability (α = 0.458). Germane load was the dominant contributor to CL, indicating substantial mental effort directed towards processing and integrating learning during the simulation. Conclusion: Emergency Care Practitioner students reported moderate overall CL, with high GL suggesting strong engagement in meaningful learning. These findings highlight the importance of clear instructional design and structured cognitive support within emergency care simulations. Contribution: Understanding how emergency care students experience CL can guide educators in refining simulation design, reducing unnecessary cognitive burden and enhancing readiness for complex clinical practice.

title: Cognitive overload and governance failures in managerial dashboards: a qualitative study of how data misleads managerial judgement
container-title: International Journal of Organizational Analysis
495e6e06c7f13c84b632cdcaf00a1cae0b021f8d.abstract: Purpose The purpose of this research is to investigate how cognitive, interpretative, governance and integrity issues linked to dashboard-driven decision-making may distort the manager’s judgement. It seeks to identify ways in which these distortions can be countered through interventions based upon human-centric design and governance mechanisms. This research uses the concept of “Visual Authority Bias” as a sensitising lens to examine and mitigate dashboard-induced distortions in managerial judgement. Design/methodology/approach This study involves a qualitative research approach based on the use of key informant interviews in examining the relationship between human cognitive processes and digital performance measurement systems. Primary data were collected via 10 in-depth, semi-structured interviews conducted with experienced informants from various professional backgrounds such as HR, procurement, technology and operations. Transcripts from these interviews were analysed based on an inductive thematic analysis to provide an interpretive perspective on cognitive errors committed due to over-reliance on dashboards. Findings The analysis identifies four interrelated pitfalls in dashboard-mediated managerial decision-making: the Context–Data Disconnect, Interpretive Bias and the Black Box Problem, Institutional Failure and Governance Shielding and Data Integrity Failure. Across the interviews, visually authoritative outputs encouraged managers to treat incomplete or flawed metrics as objective accounts of organisational reality, overlook qualitative explanations, rely on heuristics and diffuse accountability. The findings indicate that these problems are socio-technical rather than purely technological. The study therefore proposes deliberate design-level cognitive friction, data validation and cross-functional review to help managers test dashboard outputs before acting on them. Originality/value This paper contributes to research in corporate governance and management control by redirecting focus from the technical optimisation of data to human fallibility in interpreting and using the data. Through the lens of dashboards not only as information management tools but also as mechanisms of accountability, this paper illustrates how data-based governance could go astray. This contribution is made in relation to the nascent discourse of Visual Authority Bias and its effects on decision-making.

title: No exit, still loyal? Kinship employee engagement in the face of psychological entrapment
container-title: International Journal of Conflict Management
aa3bccaf68e68cbf88d11841025e172b64b3a80a.abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine how toxic leadership and interpersonal conflict are associated with knowledge hiding through psychological entrapment among creative industry MSME employees and investigates financial vulnerability as an intensifier of entrapment and kinship employee engagement (KEE) as a culturally embedded factor that may weaken knowledge hiding. Design/methodology/approach Data were collected from 317 employees of creative MSMEs in Lampung, Indonesia, using purposive sampling. Hypotheses were tested with covariance-based structural equation modeling (CB-SEM). Findings Toxic leadership and interpersonal conflict are positively associated with psychological entrapment, which in turn is positively associated with knowledge hiding. Mediation occurs for toxic leadership but not for interpersonal conflict. Financial vulnerability strengthens the positive associations of both predictors with entrapment, while KEE weakens the positive association between entrapment and knowledge hiding. Research limitations/implications Several limitations should be considered when interpreting these findings. First, the cross-sectional design limits firm conclusions about causality. Future studies using longitudinal or diary methods could better reveal how psychological entrapment forms and changes over time within MSMEs. Second, the use of self-reported data may introduce perceptual bias. However, the presence of interaction effects, which are generally less sensitive to such bias, reduces this concern to some extent. Practical implications MSME owners and managers should reduce dominating leadership practices, manage interpersonal tensions and enhance employee security. Strengthening kinship-based engagement is a culturally aligned strategy to maintain cooperative knowledge exchange. Social implications By showing how economic vulnerability and relational climate shape defensive behaviors, this study supports the development of healthier work communities where solidarity and mutual care discourage knowledge withholding Originality/value This study examines psychological entrapment as a potential mechanism linking relational adversity to knowledge hiding in MSMEs, while integrating financial vulnerability and KEE as contextual moderators.

title: A buffer-capacity-constrained integrated scheduling model for automated container terminals
container-title: Engineering Computations
abea9934faaba801be59b927f5af1e20dc7043f3.abstract: Purpose This study investigates an integrated scheduling problem in automated container terminals (ACTs) for export loading, jointly coordinating quay cranes (QCs), automated guided vehicles (AGVs), and automated stacking cranes (ASCs). It explicitly models two practical buffering resources: limited-capacity block buffer zones at yard blocks and quay-side buffer lanes/buffer locations for AGV queuing. The objective is to minimize total QC idle (waiting) time while satisfying realistic constraints, including equipment non-blocking, handover time windows, predetermined QC loading sequences, exclusive buffer-location occupancy, buffer-location assignment, and the rule that each AGV may park on buffer lanes at most once per job transport. Design/methodology/approach A comprehensive mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) (M1) is formulated to capture ASC retrieval, AGV transport with buffer-lane parking, buffer-location assignment, and QC loading interactions under finite buffer capacities. An equivalent reformulation (M2) replaces the max-type QC idle objective with a QC waiting-time-based objective to improve computational efficiency. Given NP-hardness, an improved genetic algorithm (GA) is developed with long- and short-chromosome (SC) random-key encodings and a model-based evaluation method (MEM) that enforces feasibility via time-window calculations and resource exclusivity checks. Extensive numerical experiments and sensitivity analyses validate performance and scalability. Findings The MILP models solve small-to-medium instances effectively, and the reformulated objective (M2) substantially reduces solution time compared with M1. For large instances (up to 400 jobs), the GA-SC delivers high-quality solutions with strong robustness and significantly outperforms benchmark heuristics in both objective value and stability. Sensitivity results show diminishing returns from increasing AGV fleet size, AGV speed, or block buffer capacity: moderate increases reduce QC idle time, but excessive capacity expansion raises AGV waiting ratios and congestion, yielding limited additional improvement in system-level performance. Research limitations/implications The study assumes deterministic processing/travel times, static job sets, and fixed routes/speeds, and it does not explicitly model stochastic disruptions (e.g. equipment breakdowns, weather impacts) or real-time dynamic arrivals. Buffer-lane effects are represented via buffer-location occupancy and time windows rather than full network-level conflict-free routing. Future work should extend the framework to stochastic/robust or rolling-horizon scheduling, integrate real-time sensing and data-driven prediction, and incorporate richer traffic conflict modeling and multi-objective criteria (e.g. energy use, emissions, service reliability) for mixed loading–unloading and multi-vessel settings. Practical implications The proposed models provide a deployable decision-support framework to co-optimize equipment schedules and buffer-resource coordination, reducing QC idle time and improving operational feasibility. Results indicate that simply adding AGVs or increasing speed is not always effective; beyond certain thresholds, congestion and buffer competition dominate. Terminal managers can use the framework to size AGV fleets, set speed policies, and plan block buffer capacities, while operational control can leverage buffer-location assignment rules to mitigate quay-side queuing and upstream blocking, improving throughput with controlled congestion and cost. Social implications By reducing unproductive waiting, congestion, and empty travel, the integrated scheduling approach can lower energy consumption and emissions, supporting “green” and “smart” port objectives. More reliable QC utilization and smoother vehicle flow can reduce vessel turnaround time and improve supply-chain punctuality, limiting downstream delays and associated economic and environmental costs. The buffering-aware coordination logic is transferable to other tightly coupled logistics systems (e.g. automated warehouses, air cargo terminals, manufacturing intralogistics), enabling broader productivity gains and more sustainable operations through better synchronization under finite buffer capacities. Originality/value This work contributes a unified, implementable QC–AGV–ASC integrated scheduling formulation that simultaneously models finite yard-side block buffer capacity and explicit quay-side buffer-lane/buffer-location occupancy with assignment and exclusivity, including the “park at most once” restriction. The QC waiting-time objective reformulation improves MILP tractability and yields verifiable benchmarks. The improved GA – especially the SC variant with model-based feasibility evaluation – scales to large instances while preserving realism and solution quality. The study bridges a practical modeling gap by tightly linking buffer resource coordination to integrated multi-equipment scheduling.

title: Biological Agency
container-title: Foundations for Interdisciplinarity in the Life Sciences: Concise Monographs
Investigating Biological Mistakes
4ca781e4c0aa287f5db7507c6c8e38396bb83c58.abstract: Abstract This chapter develops the concept of the Minimal Biological Agent as the foundation for a biological theory of mistakes. Agency, understood in Aristotelian terms of acting versus being acted upon, is not confined to human beings but extends across the living and even the non-living world. Biological agency is a special case, encompassing transitive, reflexive, and intransitive forms, and ranging from the action of enzymes to the behaviour of organisms and collectives. Mistake-making is inseparable from agency: agents can misdirect, miscalibrate, or overextend their powers, with varying degrees of avoidability. Drawing on examples from biochemistry, ethology, and ecology, the chapter argues that organisms display dispositions analogous to virtues, steering between extremes to maintain stability and flourishing. Biological agency is thus norm-sensitive and mistake-prone in distinctive ways, resisting reduction to physics and chemistry, and carrying implications for how humans understand and manage the natural world.

title: Controlled Synthesis of Imperfect Datasets for Machine Learning Education: A Variational Autoencoder, Wasserstein GAN, and Gaussian Mixture Model Framework with Domain-Aware Fraud and Error Injection
container-title: SN Computer Science
b9d8c4b92b2e13bb94b97e2c8e652d6dfdad3cef.abstract: Abstract Machine learning and data science education overwhelmingly relies on pre-cleaned, statically curated benchmark datasets from repositories such as the UCI ML Repository and Kaggle. These datasets are ill-suited to teaching the realities of production data pipelines, which invariably contain missing values arising from mixed mechanisms, domain-specific typographic errors, format inconsistencies, and embedded fraud of varying sophistication. This paper presents a configurable framework for generating synthetic imperfect datasets tailored to four United Kingdom financial domains: banking transactions, mortgage lending, insurance claims, and investment and trading. The framework offers three alternative generators, one selected per request: a $$\beta $$ -Variational Autoencoder ( $$\beta $$ -VAE) with KL annealing, a Wasserstein GAN with Gradient Penalty (WGAN-GP) and their hybrid, with a Gaussian Mixture Model (GMM) fitted to the VAE latent space as an optional prior, all implemented entirely in pure NumPy so that every operation is an explicit array computation. A probabilistic error injection layer introduces nine distinct corruption types—covering MCAR, MAR, and structural errors—allocated via a Dirichlet prior over a user-specified global error budget. A domain-aware fraud injection layer encodes archetypes drawn from UK Finance, Payment Systems Regulator, Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) and Association of British Insurers (ABI) taxonomies. Evaluation across the four domains, against external baselines fitted to the same training splits, shows that the $$\beta $$ -VAE attains a mean Kolmogorov–Smirnov statistic of 0.104 against a held-out partition of the rule-based seed corpus , ahead of CTGAN and TVAE on the same target at 1/34 and 1/9 of their respective fitting times, and that a structureless independent-marginals generator matches every marginal while destroying the correlation structure, so marginal fidelity alone does not discriminate between generators. A zero-cost smoothed bootstrap of the seed corpus attains a better statistic still on both marginal fidelity and correlation error, and a Gaussian copula is ahead of the $$\beta $$ -VAE on categorical divergence and correlation error at a fifth of its fitting cost, so the case for the generative stage is not made on fidelity to the seed corpus and is not made here. Validation against real record-level data shows close agreement for bounded quantities and substantial disagreement in the tails, so the framework is characterised as generating plausible rather than realistic records. A detector transcribed from the documented fraud injection ranges and fitted to nothing attains AUROC 0.994 when archetypes overwrite records outright, which motivates an overlap-controlled injection scheme introduced here that makes archetype separability a declared continuous parameter; at its default expression coefficient $$\lambda = 0.25$$ the same detector falls to 0.609, while a trained classifier reaches 0.948. Error injection realises a stable and monotone but systematically low fraction of the requested rate, averaging 0.596 of it, and the missingness mechanisms are verified to be correctly instantiated when isolated from the default allocation. Generation scales to 100,000 records in 7.0 min on two commodity CPU cores without GPU acceleration. No evidence involving learners or instructors is presented; a protocol for the evaluation that would be required is specified in full.

title: Lessons Learned from Large Scale Dissemination of the Family Talk Approach
container-title: Harvard Review of Psychiatry
7820a8ce8c6201cdd1b27fb23a77089d22ce52a5.abstract: This perspective review provides an in-depth examination of key lessons from three major dissemination efforts of Family Talk (FT), a preventive intervention approach designed to support families facing adversity. We highlight practical insights, common challenges, and implications that may inform future implementation and policy efforts. After initial development and testing for parental depression, FT has been adapted and implemented in a variety of large-scale dissemination efforts, including a country-wide program in Finland and a district-wide adaptation in Rwanda. This approach has also been used with refugee groups, the Navy, and other service branch personnel in the United States. We briefly review each project, then describe and discuss the key lessons learned across these efforts. Our takeaways emphasize the need for understanding risk and resilience in each dissemination effort, the local context and culture at intervention delivery, and the need for stage-sequential planning and multiyear efforts. Successful implementation efforts require careful assessment with standardized instruments at multiple levels. Cultural and linguistic competence is also essential, and multiple adaptations for different conditions are necessary. Integrating the intervention approach into regular service care systems is also imperative. Additionally, this paper highlights the value of long-term partnerships, the importance of tracking development over time, the challenges of changing and evolving clinical presentations and shifting societal and funding priorities, and the need to maintain shared vision and values.

title: Generative AI Literacies and Discipline-Specific Knowledge: Preservice Teachers Planning Task-Based L2 Lessons with GenAI
container-title: Digital Studies in Language and Literature
49cfa4edc8a86155f27305dd81b772f6f0a87a1a.abstract: Abstract This study investigates the use of Large Language Models (LLMs) to support Task-Based Language Teaching (TBLT)-oriented lesson planning in a preservice teacher education context, examining the extent to which LLM use can contribute to the mobilisation of TBLT-related competencies. The case study draws on triangulated data from surveys, interaction logs with the LLM, lesson plans produced by preservice teachers and their reflections. The module required participants to generate a lesson plan with an LLM and to compare the resulting plan with a previously created lesson plan developed without AI support. The analysis focuses on knowledge of TBLT principles and their implementation during lesson planning, and the GenAI competence activated through the interaction with the LLM. The findings reveal considerable variation in how the dyads interacted with the LLM. Some dyads formulated more precise prompts and prompt iterations, provided more contextualised input, engaged more critically with the LLM-generated output, and iteratively refined their lesson plans in ways that appeared more consistent with TBLT principles. The data suggest an association between a stronger conceptual understanding of TBLT and more purposeful interaction with the LLM. This association indicates that disciplinary knowledge may facilitate the effective use of LLMs for TBLT-oriented lesson planning. Rather than replacing pedagogical expertise, LLM use appears to be most productive when preservice teachers are able to critically evaluate and adapt the generated output in light of established TBLT principles.

title: “She is not white, she is Latina”: positionality as an asset in cross-cultural ethnographic research with First Nations youth in Australia
container-title: International Journal of the Sociology of Language
3858ba91762de4d002af128a3dfd320befe8c64f.abstract: Abstract This paper examines how my researcher positionality as a female migrant from the Global South became an asset when carrying out a sociolinguistic ethnography with First Nations girls at an Australian boarding school. In other sociolinguistic school ethnographies, most researchers have either worked within their own sociocultural communities, and/or tried to minimise their presence by not disclosing much about themselves. Here, following a culturally safe approach, I interrogate whether traditional approaches are culturally appropriate. I reflect on how I found ways to align with participants beyond shared cultural practices, and encourage other (socio)linguists to engage with reflexivity and positionality in their work to make visible from which standpoint(s) knowledge is being produced.

title: Valproic acid inhibits gastric cancer cell hallmarks but impairs wound healing in a PIPAC-inspired in vitro model
container-title: Pleura and Peritoneum
ccdab100b4bf4a0920046fc3af63b752e547a699.abstract: Abstract Objectives Valproic acid (VPA), a histone deacetylase inhibitor, has been proposed for pressurized intraperitoneal aerosol chemotherapy (PIPAC) to prevent peritoneal recurrence of gastric cancer while theoretically sparing wound healing. We tested this hypothesis using a PIPAC-inspired in vitro model. Methods MKN-45 gastric cancer cells, neonatal human dermal fibroblasts (NHDF), and mesothelial cells (MeT-5A) were exposed to aerosolized VPA (0.126–2.5 mg/mL), paclitaxel (PTX; 3 μg/mL), or their combinations for 30 min under pressurized conditions. Outcomes included cytotoxicity (CASY cell counting), metabolic activity (MTT assay), cell migration and wound healing (scratch assays), and adhesion to extracellular matrix proteins. Results VPA alone exerted only modest, delayed, and largely concentration-independent antiproliferative effects, with no clear dose–response relationship across the tested range. Metabolic inhibition emerged at concentrations ≥1.5 mg/mL and became profound at ≥2 mg/mL. VPA concentration dependently inhibited cancer cell migration and adhesion to all ECM substrates tested. However, VPA also completely prevented wound closure in normal fibroblasts and mesothelial cells at concentrations as low as 0.252 mg/mL. Combining VPA (1.5 mg/mL) with PTX (3 μg/mL) did not significantly exceed the activity of PTX alone in cytotoxicity (p=0.76) or metabolic assays (p=0.89), with no consistent synergy observed under the fixed-dose conditions tested. Conclusions Although VPA delivered via PIPAC inhibits selected gastric cancer hallmarks, its antiproliferative activity is weak in MKN-45 cells, and the concentrations required for antitumor effects are substantially higher than clinically achievable serum levels. Importantly, VPA impairs wound healing in normal peritoneal-relevant cells, challenging its proposed utility as a recurrence-preventing agent that spares the healing peritoneum. The VPA–PTX combination did not show consistent synergy, and further studies with additional gastric cancer cell lines and in vivo models are warranted.

title: Participatory conceptual mapping with guardrailed large language models: An audit-ready DAPSI(W)R(M) workflow from workshop transcripts to scenario testing
container-title: Socio-Environmental Systems Modelling
d3472c4fbfed6710f3bbb4a58d6fedc45e974955.abstract: Participatory conceptual mapping is widely used in sustainability research to represent stakeholders’ knowledge, concerns, and perceptions of causal relationships within complex social-ecological systems. Yet translating workshop dialogue into reliable, auditable causal maps is labor-intensive and prone to interpretive drift. We present a four-step workflow combining guardrailed large language model (LLM) assistance with human oversight to transform workshop transcripts into DAPSI(W)R(M)-consistent conceptual maps, feedback structures, and qualitative scenarios. The workflow comprises (1) evidence-anchored extraction of nodes and directional links; (2) controlled merging of workshop maps into an identifier-stable representation; (3) identification of vicious cycles, focal points, and virtuous cycles using only the verified combined structure; and (4) scenario tracing through validated pathways. Guardrails include a no-invention rule, quotation-level evidence anchoring, alias tracking, stable identifiers, clean-slate re-entry, and human verification. Applied to two workshops on sustainable fisheries in Catalonia, Spain, the workflow consolidated 64 initial themes and 242 links into 43 themes and 243 verified relations. Three major vicious-cycle systems, several focal points, and twelve virtuous loops and chains informed ten stakeholder-style qualitative scenarios. The case study suggests that guardrailed LLM assistance can support synthesis of stakeholder-derived knowledge while keeping analytical decisions traceable. The workflow provides an auditable foundation for AI-supported participatory systems analysis and identifies future refinements including polarity checks, indicator integration, and empirically testable scenarios.

title: Large-Area Marine Surface Current Measurement Using Unmanned Aerial Vehicle-Based Optical Flow Mosaicking Without Ground Control Points
container-title: Journal of Ocean University of China
58ce184db269ca0b188a13da1ba350ebffaec3f4.abstract: Abstract Nearshore ocean currents are characterized by complex structures and spatial heterogeneity. Conventional measurement techniques are either inefficient or offer low spatial resolution, while image velocimetry (a low-cost, high-resolution method) is limited in marine applications due to the trade-off between large-area coverage and high resolution, as well as the lack of ground control points for calibration. To address these issues, this study proposes a current field mosaicking method. By maintaining the camera in constant-speed motion, the distance differences between consecutive image frames are converted into row offsets using the interframe time interval and image resolution, thereby expanding the velocimetry observation range through stitching. An adaptive thresholding method combining sun-glint identification and cropping is also developed. Results show that the picture range increases from 60 to 350 m, enabling large-area optical-flow velocimetry, and that the sun glint removal technique effectively reduces interference without additional quality degradation or artificial signals. This approach solves key constraints of image velocimetry in large-scale marine environments.

title: Template Mineralized, Decellularized Matrix-Alginate-Based Bioink Provides Structural Reinforcement in Caprine Ex Vivo Bone Defect Model
container-title: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces
c8eef2f5c412b1ad575037a525f027a029a1a59e.abstract: Abstract Clinical management of critical-sized bone defects (CSDs) remains a significant surgical problem. Current bioinks fail to support initial loading on bone tissue. In this study, goat-derived decellularized matrix (DCM) was used as a template for controlled mineralization, while alginate improved the printability and cellular viability. DCM proteins acted as a natural template for hydroxyapatite (HA) crystal nucleation and growth, mimicking bone nanocomposite chemistry while enhancing structural reinforcement. HA formation on DCM template was visualized by atomic force microscopy (AFM) analysis, characteristic phosphate (PO43–) peaks in attenuated total reflectance-Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (ATR-FTIR), and the HA-specific (211) diffraction peak in X-ray diffraction (XRD). Mineralized DCM was blended with alginate to formulate printable bioinks. Rheological analysis showed dominant elastic behavior (G′ &gt; G″), shear-thinning flow, and rapid post-shear recovery. Mechanical testing further demonstrated enhanced compressive strength in HA-DCM-alginate constructs. Bioprinting with osteoblast cells demonstrated higher cellular viability in the mineralized ink while enhancing osteogenic differentiation, via both biochemical and biophysical signaling from the mineralized-DCM ink. In an ex vivo defect model, the HA-DCM-alginate system significantly increased the compressive properties of the defect construct, providing immediate structural reinforcement at the defect site. Overall, the current mineralized bioink can provide both mechanical support and bone regeneration and holds promising potential for surgical application.

title: A Fast Solver of Collocation Method for a Three-Dimensional Bond-Based Linear Peridynamic Model
container-title: Journal of Computational Mathematics
deba8b1320cb995ea335765053342dafc5221068.abstract: The peridynamic (PD) theory tends to provide a better description than the classical continuum mechanics theory in the context of long-range forces or discontinuities. However, due to the nonlocal properties of PD models, the numerical methods employed in these models yield stiffness matrices with very complicated structures, especially for three-dimensional problems. Fast algorithms usually require the computational domain to be rectangular in two space dimensions and cuboidal in three space dimensions to ensure that the resulting stiffness matrices have a Toeplitz-like structure. In this work, we construct an accurate and efficient solver of the collocation method for a three-dimensional bond-based linear PD model defined on a relatively general geometry. The discretization for PD models on cubic domains by the collocation method can lead to Block-Block-Toeplitz-Toeplitz-Block-Block-Toeplitz-Toeplitz-Block-Block (B-BTTB-BTTB-B) matrices. Based on this special structure, we optimize the computational work of the traditional solver from \(O(N^3)\) to \(O(N^2\log N)\) and reduce the memory requirement of the traditional solver from \(O(N^2)\) to \(O(N)\), where \(N\) is the number of spatial unknowns. More importantly, the fast method remains applicable to non-cuboidal geometries via domain extension into matching cubic areas and then carefully handling the nodes in the extended domains. Numerical experiments are performed to show the accuracy and efficiency of the proposed method.

title: Gender Equality and Workplace Inclusivity among Employees of a Government Agency in the Philippines
container-title: Journal of Social Entrepreneurship Theory and Practice
74ae94ca8045b5d4ce09ac0bd87680aace32a1f8.abstract: Gender equality and workplace inclusivity are essential to fostering fair, respectful, and supportive work environments where employees receive equal opportunities and are encouraged to participate and contribute. This study aimed to determine the perceived levels of gender equality and workplace inclusivity among employees of a Philippine government agency. A quantitative descriptive-correlational design was employed using a census approach involving 40 employees from an identified work unit of the government agency. Descriptive and inferential statistical techniques were used to analyze data collected via a researcher-structured questionnaire. Results showed that employees perceived high levels of gender equality and workplace inclusivity. All six dimension-level Pearson correlations between the gender equality dimensions (equal opportunities and fair treatment) and the workplace inclusivity dimensions (respect and acceptance, participation and involvement, and organizational support) were positive and statistically significant, ranging from r = .615 to r = .862 (p < .001). Although respondents generally perceived limited gaps in workplace policies and practices, areas requiring continuous improvement were identified in accountability and monitoring mechanisms, program evaluation processes, organizational support systems, employee feedback utilization, and safe reporting procedures. Based on these findings, a strategy roadmap for strengthening gender equality and workplace inclusivity was prepared to support the continuous enhancement of gender-responsive and inclusive workplace practices. The findings may serve as a basis for government leaders, human resource managers, and gender and development focal persons in formulating and enhancing evidence-based policies, programs, and interventions that promote gender equality, workplace inclusivity, employee well-being, and organizational effectiveness.

Integrasi Iman, Islam, dan Ihsan sebagai Model Spiritual-Moral Development dalam Kehidupan Muslim Kontemporer
container-title: Karakter : Jurnal Riset Ilmu Pendidikan Islam
5972a02ad4ee67c4b6be00ae21eb9af1012c6218.abstract: The rapid development of technology and ongoing social changes in contemporary society have created significant challenges to the spiritual and moral lives of Muslims, including materialism, individualism, and the erosion of ethical values in everyday interactions. These challenges highlight the need for an integrated framework that connects religious belief, religious practice, and moral excellence. This article aims to examine the integration of Iman (faith), Islam (religious practice), and Ihsan (spiritual and moral excellence) as a conceptual model for developing a holistic Muslim personality in contemporary life. This study employs a qualitative method through a library research approach, drawing on the Hadith of Gabriel, classical Islamic scholarly works, and relevant academic literature. The collected data are analyzed descriptively and analytically to identify the conceptual relationships among these three dimensions and their implications for Muslim life. The findings reveal that Iman serves as the spiritual foundation that shapes religious conviction and awareness, Islam represents the practical manifestation of faith through worship and responsible actions, while Ihsan promotes sincerity, self-awareness, accountability, and ethical behavior. Their integration establishes a comprehensive framework in which faith guides actions, religious practices strengthen commitment, and spiritual excellence deepens moral responsibility. This framework has important implications for personal development, Islamic education, family relationships, professional ethics, and social engagement. Therefore, the integration of Iman, Islam, and Ihsan provides a relevant conceptual foundation for strengthening Muslim spirituality and moral integrity amid the complexities of contemporary life.

title: Predictive Model for Ammonia Absorption Capacity of Deep Eutectic Solvents Using Rough Set Theory
container-title: Process Integration and Optimization for Sustainability
89757054c367f17246ca1edbcab7b4202bf33e7c.abstract: Abstract The direct emission of ammonia (NH 3 ) into the atmosphere from process waste gas streams brings environmental and health risks. This can be mitigated through absorption using solvents. Deep eutectic solvents (DES) were introduced as green absorption solvents with advantages including wide liquid range, high thermal stability and simple synthesis. Experimental studies indicate that NH₃ absorption capacity improves with acidic DES, higher hydrogen bond donor (HBD) to hydrogen bond acceptor (HBA) ratio, controlled water content, lower temperature and higher pressure. However, the exhaustive number of possible DES combinations formed by varying HBAs, HBDs, molar ratio and water content, makes it difficult to evaluate each combination experimentally. This combinatorial complexity together with the influence of process conditions, makes determining the optimal ranges of these variables through trial-and-error experiments resource-intensive and time-consuming. While predictive modelling offers a solution, most existing models are black-box approaches that lack interpretability, providing limited insights into how each variable affects NH 3 absorption performance. This limits their application in guiding solvent and process design. Therefore, this work developed an interpretable predictive model for NH 3 absorption in DES using rough set machine learning (RSML). RSML applies rough set theory (RST) to generate interpretable results by analysing indiscernibility relations within large datasets. Data on DES properties and process conditions affecting NH 3 absorption capacity were collected for model development. Decision rules with high certainty (> 80%) were analysed. Results revealed that acidic HBDs (i.e. phenols), lower temperatures (< 338 K), higher pressures (> 101.3 kPa) and controlled water content (0.025–0.075 wt%) enhance NH 3 absorption capacity.

title: AI Driven Talent Management and the Performance of Agri Based Enterprises in Central Region Cameroon
container-title: Journal of Economics, Management, Entrepreneurship, and Business (JEMEB)
9a45a01f3f197d9b0c87ceca92e874eb272d0293.abstract: Purpose: This study examines the relationship between artificial intelligence (AI) driven talent management practices and the performance of agri based enterprises in the Central Region of Cameroon, focusing on the mediating roles of workforce productivity and employee resilience. Research Methodology: A quantitative cross sectional survey design was employed, targeting 250 managers and human resource professionals. Data were collected with a structured questionnaire and analyzed with SPSS and AMOS through descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation, and mediation analysis with 5.000 bootstrap resamples. Results: AI driven talent management was positively and significantly related to enterprise performance (r=0.523, p<0.01). Workforce productivity (β=0.18) and employee resilience (β=0.14) significantly mediated this relationship. Both the total indirect effect (β=0.32, p<0.01) and the direct effect (β=0.29, p<0.01) were significant, indicating partial mediation, with about 52 percent of the total effect transmitted through the two mediators. Conclusions: AI driven talent management enhances the performance of agri based enterprises both directly and indirectly through improved workforce productivity and stronger employee resilience. Enterprises should integrate AI strategically into talent management and support employees through change management. Limitations: The cross sectional design, self reported data, purposive sampling, and focus on a single region limit causal inference and generalizability. Contributions: The study provides empirical evidence from an underresearched African agricultural context and clarifies the mechanisms through which AI driven talent management translates into enterprise performance.

title: Robot cops on patrol: police officers' perceived effectiveness of AI-powered humanoid robots
container-title: Policing: An International Journal
399ffbef301f680d3c80797a3999bd5c26c9c5cb.abstract: Purpose The main purpose of the study is to examine how organizational justice, artificial intelligence (AI) literacy and perceived risks shape officers' attitudes toward AI-powered service and crime-fighting robots. Design/methodology/approach This study used survey data collected from 959 police officers in a major metropolitan area in Southwestern China. Two regression models were estimated to analyze correlates of police officers' perceived effectiveness of service and crime-fighting AI robots. Findings Results show that supervisor support for AI is a strong and consistent predictor of positive attitudes toward AI-powered robots, whereas supervisor justice is negatively associated with AI acceptance. AI training and AI knowledge also significantly enhance perceived effectiveness of AI tools, underscoring the saliency of technological familiarity. Perceived risks play a more limited and task-specific role. Originality/value The present study is among the first attempts to assess police officers' attitudes toward the application of AI in policing. This study provides evidence-based recommendations for the ethical and effective integration of AI into law enforcement practices.

title: Bearing fault diagnosis of rolling machinery based on spatial pyramid channel attention network with depthwise separable convolution
container-title: Engineering Computations
ac8de549d0c263d536d5003d12d7eeb6f37d0532.abstract: Purpose Rolling bearings are critical components in rotating machinery, and their fault diagnosis is essential for ensuring safe equipment operation. However, traditional fault diagnosis methods face challenges including insufficient feature extraction, high computational complexity and difficulties in multi-scale information fusion. To address these issues, this paper proposes a spatial pyramid channel attention network with depthwise separable convolution for intelligent fault diagnosis of rolling bearings. Design/methodology/approach Continuous wavelet transform converts 1D vibration signals into 2D time-frequency images. An efficient feature extraction block integrates depthwise separable convolution, multi-scale dilated convolution and a cross-spatial multi-scale attention module to expand the receptive field while reducing complexity. A cross-spatial multi-scale attention mechanism uses parallel 1D global average pooling paths to capture long-range dependencies. Finally, a channel-spatial synergy module combines spatial pyramid structure and channel information interaction to establish inter-channel dependencies while preserving multi-scale spatial information. Findings Experimental results on three public datasets from Jiangnan University (JNU), Xi'an Jiaotong University (XJTU-SY) and Paderborn University (PU) demonstrate that the proposed method achieves diagnostic accuracies of 99.94%, 98.94% and 98.55%, respectively, showing superior diagnostic precision and better generalization capability compared to existing methods. Ablation experiments further validate the effectiveness of each core module. Originality/value This paper proposes a novel spatial pyramid channel attention network with depthwise separable convolution that synergistically integrates multi-scale dilated convolution, cross-spatial attention and channel-spatial synergy. The method effectively addresses challenges of insufficient feature extraction, high computational complexity and multi-scale fusion difficulties in rolling bearing fault diagnosis, demonstrating superior diagnostic accuracy and generalization capability across multiple public datasets.

title: AI governance as co-regulation: a practitioner-informed framework for defense-sector small and medium-sized enterprises
container-title: Digital Policy, Regulation and Governance
567df46acd778f8be8494c9ae84f8e44b8ec75da.abstract: Purpose This paper aims to examine how practitioners supporting defense-sector small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) place artificial intelligence (AI) governance within the coregulatory regime of National Institute of Standards and Technology Special Publication 800-171, the cybersecurity maturity model certification program, contracts and assessors. Design/methodology/approach An exploratory survey of 38 practitioners, recruited through a public LinkedIn post, combined a risk-to-control-family mapping task, artifact feasibility ratings and open-ended responses. Analysis was descriptive, with exploratory correlations adjusted for multiplicity and one researcher coded the open text. Findings Respondents concentrated AI risk on a few evidence-bearing control families, led by audit and accountability, risk assessment, access control and system and information integrity. Perceived compliance strain was high and readiness low. Artifacts resembling existing evidence, such as audit trail exports, were rated most feasible. Guidance ambiguity was the leading barrier. No exploratory association survived adjustment for multiplicity. Research limitations/implications The purposive sample and self-reported perceptions support pattern identification, not population estimates or claims about implementation outcomes. Practical implications Assessors and prime contractors could reduce SME burden by publishing exemplar AI evidence artifacts mapped to existing control families. Originality/value The study develops coregulation as a lens on the evidence burden of small firms at the base of regulatory chains, reports the full risk-to-control matrix and derives a seven-module framework that separates survey-supported elements from design choices.

title: Effectiveness evaluation of generative intelligent search: a comparative study with traditional search engine
container-title: Aslib Journal of Information Management
d1c9eeac798ccc7a8876d8762f5ec367e887920a.abstract: Purpose The emergence of generative artificial intelligence has transformed information retrieval, yet limited understanding of its differences from traditional search engines hinders clarity regarding changes in user search behavior and variations in search effectiveness, thereby impeding guidance for future search interface design. Design/methodology/approach We conducted a laboratory experiment comparing two versions of the Bing search engine: the traditional Bing search and the generative-AI integrated Bing (Bing Chat). We interpreted variations in user search behavior through querying, browsing, and clicking data, and established a multidimensional metric framework encompassing user, cost-benefit, and system dimensions to assess search effectiveness. 40 participants with good search skills completed the experiment, resulting in a final dataset comprising 160 observation records. Findings The Mann-Whitney U test revealed that users of generative AI search engines exhibited the following characteristics compared to those using traditional search engines: longer queries, more keyboard activity, more frequent query restructuring (including more narrowing queries, more following the system queries, and more changing the syntactic structure queries, with less broadening queries), more browsing during the first search session, and less scrolling and clicking. The results of the Linear Mixed Models show that, compared to traditional search engines, users achieve superior performance with generative AI search on users’ subjective perceptions and search efficiency metrics. Furthermore, we employed machine learning to validate which search behaviors can predict a user’s search effectiveness. The results indicate that the Gradient Boosting Machines are the optimal prediction models. The five most significant indicators for predicting search performance are Avelength. QueryConsTime, TimetofirSearch, ResViewTime and NumbofScroll. Research limitations/implications By revealing differences in user behavior and search efficiency across various search engines, this study deepens our understanding of generative AI search engines at a finer granularity and contributes to building adaptive search platforms capable of optimizing search recommendations. Originality/value By revealing differences in user behavior and efficiency between traditional and generative versions of the Bing search engine, this study deepens our understanding of generative AI search engines at a finer granularity and contributes to building adaptive search platforms capable of optimizing search recommendations.

title: Algorithmic cognitive programmes: observing ambient architectures of attention with social systems theory
container-title: Kybernetes
51d2013b2858e0715f8c03247ec8eb58d1d1a814.abstract: Purpose This paper extends Luhmann's concept of programmes – decision premises specifying the conditions under which a system's binary code is operatively assigned – into the domain of algorithmically mediated communication. It conceptualises recommendation systems, ranking algorithms and feedback architectures as ambient cognitive programmes: recursive, probabilistic selectors that perturb the structural coupling between social and psychic systems, and examines the constitutional implications of their opacity and transfunctional reach. Design/methodology/approach The study develops a systemic–cybernetic model grounded in Luhmann's social systems theory and the epistemology of autopoietic cognition, integrating Teubner's theory of societal constitutionalism to address the normative dimensions of algorithmic mediation. Analytical illustrations from Facebook and TikTok contrast two recommendation architectures – affinity-based cascading and behavioural-similarity propagation – to demonstrate how the model applies across distinct platform logics. Findings Algorithmic cognitive programmes operate as meta-programmes that reconfigure multiple forms of social differentiation simultaneously, enacting a binary operational distinction of visibility/invisibility through engagement metrics. Their colonisation of communicative environments – by economic imperatives and, as the analysis argues, by the autonomous logic of technical mediation – becomes a constitutional pathology where its effects cannot be contested or corrected, requiring internal self-limiting mechanisms that render operative selection criteria observable to affected systems. Originality/value The paper advances a novel theoretical category – ambient cognitive programmes – that extends Luhmann's organisational typology by identifying a configuration it does not explicitly address: a purpose programme without a terminal goal state that continuously revises the conditional programmes it governs. It connects this analytical framework to Teubner's societal constitutionalism, proposing constitutional observability as a structural condition for the compatibility between algorithmic regimes and communicative pluralism.

title: A review of predictive maintenance strategies for Industry 5.0: AI, digital twins and human–machine collaboration
container-title: Journal of Quality in Maintenance Engineering
24d188956295cd9e7430988639ed3dfafe01a783.abstract: Purpose The purpose of this article is to provide a comprehensive review of predictive maintenance (PdM) strategies within the emerging Industry 5.0 paradigm, emphasizing the shift from automation-centric maintenance to human-centric, collaborative systems. The study aims to synthesize model-based, data-driven, artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled and hybrid PdM approaches, examine the role of key enabling technologies such as digital twins and edge computing and highlight human–machine collaboration in maintenance decision-making. By proposing a unified taxonomy, the article seeks to identify research gaps and guide the development of resilient, sustainable and explainable PdM systems. Design/methodology/approach This study adopts a structured systematic review methodology to analyze PdM strategies in the context of Industry 5.0. Peer-reviewed journal articles, standards and authoritative reports were identified through major scientific databases using predefined keywords related to PdM, condition-based maintenance, AI, digital twins and human–machine collaboration. The selected literature was critically examined and classified based on maintenance approach, enabling technologies, deployment architecture and degree of human involvement. Comparative analysis was employed to identify research gaps, challenges and emerging trends, culminating in the development of a novel taxonomy for Industry 5.0-oriented PdM systems. Findings The review reveals that PdM in Industry 5.0 is evolving toward hybrid frameworks that integrate data-driven intelligence with physics-based models and human expertise. While AI-based approaches improve diagnostic and prognostic accuracy, challenges related to data quality, interpretability and workforce acceptance persist. Digital twins, edge computing and collaborative robots emerge as key enablers for real-time, resilient and human-centric maintenance systems. The analysis highlights a lack of unified frameworks addressing human–machine collaboration and resilience, underscoring the need for explainable, lifecycle-oriented PdM solutions tailored to Industry 5.0 environments. Research limitations/implications This study is limited by its reliance on published literature, which may underrepresent proprietary industrial implementations and emerging practices not yet reported in academic sources. The review does not include empirical validation or quantitative benchmarking of PdM methods, focusing instead on conceptual and methodological synthesis. Nevertheless, the proposed taxonomy and identified research gaps provide a foundation for future empirical studies, experimental validation and large-scale industrial case analyses aimed at developing resilient, human-centric PdM frameworks aligned with Industry 5.0 principles. Practical implications The findings of this review offer practical guidance for industrial practitioners seeking to implement PdM within Industry 5.0 environments. The proposed taxonomy assists decision-makers in selecting appropriate PdM strategies based on system complexity, human involvement and technological readiness. Insights into digital twins, edge computing and human-in-the-loop AI support the design of maintenance systems that enhance reliability, reduce unplanned downtime and improve workforce acceptance. The study also highlights the importance of explainable and collaborative maintenance solutions to facilitate successful adoption in real-world manufacturing settings. Social implications By emphasizing human-centric and collaborative PdM, this study highlights the social impact of Industry 5.0 on the industrial workforce. The integration of human-in-the-loop decision-making and collaborative robots can improve workplace safety, reduce physically demanding tasks and support skill augmentation rather than job displacement. Transparent and explainable maintenance systems foster trust between workers and intelligent technologies, facilitating organizational acceptance and long-term adoption. Ultimately, Industry 5.0-oriented PdM contributes to more inclusive, resilient and sustainable industrial environments that align technological advancement with human well-being. Originality/value This article provides one of the first comprehensive reviews that explicitly situates PdM within the Industry 5.0 paradigm, moving beyond automation-centric perspectives. Its originality lies in the integration of PdM, condition-based maintenance, diagnostics and prognostics through a unified, human-centric lens. The study proposes a novel taxonomy that incorporates digital twins, edge computing and human–robot collaboration, offering a structured foundation for future research. By bridging technological, organizational and human factors, the article delivers both conceptual clarity and practical value for advancing next-generation maintenance systems.

title: Perceived fairness, accountability and transparency toward ML-based AI service delivery: conceptualization and measurement
container-title: Journal of Service Management
32ac1dcbe2ea84a31686f268ded2a0b816c7e9ab.abstract: Purpose This study conceptualizes and validates a multidimensional framework of consumers' perceived fairness, accountability and transparency (FAT) in machine learning (ML)-based AI service delivery. Addressing inconsistent conceptualizations and limited service-oriented measures, it examines how FAT perceptions emerge across goal-setting, coding and developing and implementation stages. A formative FAT scale is developed and tested for its predictive validity on trust and usage intention. Design/methodology/approach A multi-stage scale development process was used. Items were generated through literature review and 20 interviews, and face validity was assessed via an expert focus group. Two surveys (n = 448; n = 535) supported exploratory factor analysis (EFA), confirmatory factor analysis (CFA) and partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) validation of a reflective–formative FAT structure. A third survey (n = 455) established convergent and nomological validity with established FAT scales, trust and intention to use. Findings Results confirm FAT as a multidimensional construct shaped across goal-setting, coding and developing and implementation phases. All nine first-order factors significantly form the three higher-order FAT dimensions. The scale demonstrates strong reliability and validity, and fairness and transparency exhibit the strongest effects on trust and intention to use. Findings support a stage-based view of ethical perception in AI service delivery. Originality/value This research provides the first stage-based conceptualization and validated scale of perceived FAT in ML-based service AI. It integrates attribution theory with a socio-technical lens to disentangle how ethical judgments form throughout the AI lifecycle. The study advances theoretical clarity and offers actionable guidance for designing, developing and deploying ethically aligned AI services.

title: Exploring human–AI collaboration for management control in public healthcare
container-title: International Journal of Public Sector Management
14284e15945044815c9bcf6fc0c839ff33cdb032.abstract: Purpose This study examines how controllers in public healthcare envision human–AI collaboration in management control when dealing with uncertainty, complexity and equivocality, focusing on anticipated advantages and implementation challenges in an early-adoption setting. Design/methodology/approach We conducted an exploratory qualitative study with 14 controllers from Italian public healthcare organisations. Four closed-ended questions provided a preliminary picture of current AI adoption, while three scenario-based open-ended questions elicited prospective assessments. The framework method was used to analyse the data. Findings AI adoption remains limited and uneven, and is rarely embedded in everyday management control. Under uncertainty, controllers link AI to better forecasting and faster access to information, but worry about data quality, privacy and overreliance. In complex settings, they expect AI to help integrate diverse information and enable more systemic control, provided processes are standardised and human oversight remains. In equivocal situations, AI may support interpretation and communication, but its impact is limited by limited hands-on experience and the difficulty of codifying contextual nuances. Originality/value Based on the Jarrahi (2018) decision-making scenarios, the study develops a tentative conceptualisation of how public healthcare controllers envisage AI collaboration. The concerns of the participants inform three proposed arrangements: validation, recursive integration and contestable sensemaking. Their formulation and the accountability-augmentation principle are theoretical elaborations informed by prospective evidence and accountability research.

title: The data-labeling interface as a security boundary: task-level privacy and security risks in human-in-the-loop ML pipelines
container-title: Information & Computer Security
c3708118288ed7eac4ba6a57670b689af76bf28e.abstract: Purpose This paper aims to investigate privacy and security vulnerabilities arising from human-in-the-loop (HITL) interactions during machine learning data labeling and quality assurance/review. It argues that the data-labeling interface constitutes a distinct and underexamined security boundary, separate from infrastructure controls and organizational compliance frameworks. Design/methodology/approach The study adopts a qualitative, practice-oriented research design combining thematic analysis of publicly available documentation and workflows with responses from six practitioners gathered via a structured online instrument. Findings are organized through a task-level vulnerability taxonomy and a design–exposure–control matrix. Findings Six recurring vulnerability families are identified: excess contextual visibility, metadata exposure, privilege expansion in QA/review, instruction-level disclosure, inference-based exposure and weak anti-exfiltration controls. The matrix shows that many existing controls are partial rather than absent, and that governance principles such as least privilege and purpose limitation are frequently undermined at the task-interface level. Research limitations/implications The study relies on publicly available documentation and a small purposive sample of six practitioners, which limits statistical generalizability. Findings may not fully capture proprietary workflows. Future work should compare findings across sectors such as healthcare and financial services and test specific interface interventions empirically. Practical implications The safeguards checklist and design–exposure–control matrix offer practitioners concrete tools to audit and improve task-level privacy and security in labeling environments without requiring changes to underlying infrastructure or compliance frameworks. Originality/value To the best of the authors’ knowledge, this study offers the first systematic treatment of the data-labeling interface as a task-level security boundary. It provides a vulnerability taxonomy, a design–exposure–control matrix and an actionable safeguards checklist, offering practitioners and researchers structured tools to evaluate and strengthen privacy and security in HITL data-preparation environments.
