title: Bridging the AI literacy gap: mixed-methods evidence from employers on workforce readiness and curriculum priorities
container-title: Frontiers in Education
a65d231714461f0457b8bbbaddcfd3115714c0eb.abstract: The rapid integration of artificial intelligence (AI) in the workplace has widened the gap between what universities teach and what employers expect of new hires. This study examines that gap through a mixed-methods research-to-practice design grounded in employer perspectives. Three objectives guided the work: (a) identify gaps between undergraduate AI preparation and workplace requirements, (b) develop a workforce-informed AI competency framework from documented industry needs, and (c) identify workforce-driven priorities for an AI literacy curriculum. Data were collected in four sequential phases: a structured narrative review ( n = 56), industry focus groups and interviews ( n = 13), survey instrument development, and a convenience sample of predominantly U.S. employers recruited through professional networks ( n = 110). Open-ended survey responses were analyzed through hybrid inductive-deductive thematic analysis. Findings indicated that employer-defined AI readiness is fundamentally socio-technical: task-specific prompting and tool fluency must be coupled with professional communication, collaboration, human oversight, and judgment, soft skills that employers rated as highly as technical AI competencies. Employers also perceived recent graduates as underprepared, particularly in AI output verification and AI ethics. Within this sample, stronger governance emphasis correlated with deeper AI integration and higher self-reported efficiency, but the results are descriptive and do not support causal inference. Employers recommended an undergraduate curriculum organized around five employer-informed AI competencies, with AI output verification and responsible AI use as core outcomes. The study contributes a socio-technical conception of workplace AI readiness in which technical and human-centered competencies are interdependent rather than parallel.

title: Digital, AI-enabled marketing and the competitiveness of trade services: a sociological perspective on labor transformation, social inclusion and organizational capacity
container-title: Frontiers in Sociology
a521dbe894c1c5d4afb5061a18ed0d3eb8c2b31b.abstract: Research on digital and AI-enabled marketing explains how channels, data, and algorithms create value for firms, while the sociology of digital labor explains how the same technologies reorganize work and access. Neither explains why trade-service firms adopting near-identical tools reach very different competitive outcomes, a question that matters most for small firms in emerging and transition economies. This conceptual Perspective proposes a model of socially mediated competitiveness in which the adoption of digital and AI-enabled marketing, treated as one continuum from basic digital channels to generative-AI content, customer response, and targeting, affects competitiveness through three mechanisms. Labor transformation reallocates marketing tasks between automation and human judgment, strengthening competitiveness where workers can direct AI tools and weakening it where work depends on platform and algorithmic control. Social inclusion, through access, skills, and autonomy of use, decides how many firms and which social groups can contest a digitally mediated market. Organizational capacity, through routines for sensing, seizing, and reconfiguring human-machine practices, decides whether adoption becomes durable advantage. The theoretical novelty is threefold: the model joins mechanisms usually studied apart, treats job quality and inclusion as conditions of competitiveness rather than only its consequences, and adapts concepts built for large firms to small, platform-dependent trade-service firms. It is stated as three propositions with proposed indicators and a multi-wave design for testing them. The article reports no data and claims no empirical validation. It closes with theoretical, sociological, managerial, policy, and research implications.

title: Development of an exploratory taxonomy of veterinary AI query types and stage-specific query preferences: an expert panel study
container-title: Frontiers in Veterinary Science
8494c57f84228a86ca997f827363c73dd5680146.abstract: Background/objectives The integration of large language model (LLM)-based AI tools into veterinary clinical practice is rapidly increasing; however, veterinary-specific frameworks for organizing AI query types and examining stage-specific preferences remain limited. This study aimed to develop an exploratory taxonomy of veterinary AI query types and to characterize veterinarians’ stage-specific query preferences through a structured expert-panel survey. Methods Candidate query types were drafted with the assistance of a locally deployed LLM from a preliminary review of de-identified veterinary AI chatbot query logs and refined through literature review. In a structured online survey, 43 veterinarians then selected the Clinical Support query types (A–H) they would prefer to direct to AI at each of five clinical stages and indicated preferred response formats; the survey measured self-reported query preferences, not observed use. Results A taxonomy of 3 categories and 21 subtypes was established: Clinical Support Queries (Types A–H), Evidence-Based Research Queries (Types I–L), and Terminology and Drug Reference Queries (Types M–U). Across stages, Type B (Differential Reasoning) was most often ranked first (64/213 first-choice responses), and Type D (Clinical Decision Support) was most often ranked first for the post-consultation stage (21/42, 50.0%). In analyses accounting for repeated measures using generalized estimating equations, respondents with ≥10 years of experience more often ranked Type G (Evidence Search) first than those with &lt;10 years (OR 3.09, 95% CI 1.11–8.59; unadjusted p = 0.031), but this contrast was not significant after Benjamini–Hochberg adjustment across four contrasts (adjusted p = 0.062). Respondents from university/teaching hospitals ( n = 7) ranked Type G first in 14 of 33 responses, compared with 10 of 135 responses from secondary referral hospitals (OR 9.27, 95% CI 2.94–29.22; adjusted p &lt; 0.001), although this estimate is imprecise because the subgroup is small. Conclusion This study proposes a veterinary-specific exploratory taxonomy of AI query types and characterizes how respondents’ first-choice preferences varied across clinical stages. These findings offer a preliminary, exploratory framework that may inform the future design of context-aware, stage-adaptive veterinary AI systems, pending cross-national replication and formal validation.

title: From AI-assisted learning to Arabic reading comprehension: the roles of bilingual proficiency and cognitive flexibility among Indonesian university students
container-title: Frontiers in Language Sciences
d49e9e7be878c0396c3678f26006272d38ff331b.abstract: Background Artificial intelligence (AI) has been widely applied in language learning, yet how AI reinforces second-language outcomes remains underexplored. Guided by the cognitive theory of multimedia learning (CTML), the study assessed correlations among AI-assisted learning (AIAL), bilingual proficiency (BLPR), cognitive flexibility (CGFX), and Arabic reading comprehension (ARBC) in Indonesian university students. BLPR was defined as respondents' perceptions of their capability to understand, communicate, read, and write in Indonesian and Arabic and switch fluently between them in any communication situation. CGFX was defined as respondents' perceptions of their capability to adjust their thinking, consider alternative solutions, and adjust cognitive strategies in various situations. Methods In this study, 615 university students in Indonesia enrolled in the Arabic Language and Literature and Arabic Language Education courses responded to a cross-sectional questionnaire. The gathered data was analyzing using partial least squares structural equation modeling to assess the hypothesized associations. Results It was discovered that the links between AIAL and BLPR (β = 0.51, p &lt; 0.001) and between BLPR and CGFX (β = 0.58, p &lt; 0.001) met the significance threshold. CGFX was also strongly associated with ARBC (β = 0.63, p &lt; 0.001). However, there were direct non-significant associations between AIAL and CGFX (β = 0.06, p = 0.230) and between BLPR and ARBC (β = 0.08, p = 0.109). Conclusion The lack of significant findings for two of the five hypothesized associations contradicts previously published research. This could be because in this study, the AIAL–CGFX association was assessed from the respondents' perspectives of learning Arabic, whereas in earlier research, the AIAL–CGFX association was assessed from a general learning perspective. Also, in this study, BLPR was defined as learners' perceived ability in different language skills, such as bilingual language skills, including listening, speaking, reading, writing, and language switching, whereas in earlier work, the aim was narrower: the linguistic skills necessary for reading comprehension, such as vocabulary and morphology skills.

title: AI-powered rapid detection of meat adulteration with terahertz spectroscopy in food and drug control
container-title: Frontiers in Physiology
5080e501b6cfe12b290c321117e6496d712e5bf2.abstract: Introduction Meat adulteration is an increasing problem in food and drug law enforcement, where existing identification methods are inefficient and of limited scope. Methods This study proposes a detection scheme that combines terahertz time-domain spectroscopy (THz-TDS) with artificial intelligence. Time-domain spectra of five common meat species (chicken, beef, duck, mutton and pork) were collected in the 0.2–2.0 THz band, and the absorption coefficient, refractive index and dielectric constant were calculated. Principal component analysis (PCA) was used for feature dimensionality reduction, and support vector machine (SVM) and convolutional neural network (CNN) models were applied to identify meat species and to quantify adulteration content. Results The optical parameters of the five species differed significantly in the terahertz band (P &lt; 0.05, independent-samples t-test). The SVM model achieved 98.3% accuracy for species identification, and the CNN model predicted adulteration content with an error of less than 3%. Discussion The combined THz-TDS and AI approach is non-destructive, rapid and accurate, and can provide a reliable detection method for on-site law enforcement in the public security food and drug environment field.

title: Trust Adaptive Provenance Watermarking for Synthetic News Broadcasting
container-title: Bridging of Emerging AI and Media Broadcasting (BEAM)
54da23f830b88c07cc6666b01d671d57744ffa0a.abstract: The rapid adoption of generative artificial intelligence in digital news broadcasting has increased the production of synthetic news content, raising critical concerns regarding authenticity, source verification, content manipulation, and audience trust. This study proposes a trust-adaptive provenance watermarking framework designed to dynamically protect and verify AI-generated news content by integrating provenance information with trust-aware watermarking mechanisms throughout the broadcasting workflow. The proposed framework combines adaptive digital watermarking, provenance metadata, and a trust-scoring mechanism that adjusts watermark strength according to content sensitivity, source credibility, and manipulation risk. Experimental evaluation is conducted using synthetic news samples under common content transformations, including compression, resizing, cropping, re-encoding, and partial manipulation, while performance is assessed through watermark detection accuracy, robustness, content quality, and provenance verification reliability. The experimental findings demonstrate that the proposed approach achieves high watermark detectability while maintaining acceptable perceptual quality across different broadcasting transformations. The adaptive trust mechanism further improves provenance verification for high-risk synthetic content and enables more reliable identification of manipulated or unauthorized news assets compared with conventional fixed-strength watermarking approaches. The proposed trust-adaptive provenance watermarking framework provides a practical approach for strengthening authenticity, traceability, and accountability in synthetic news broadcasting, offering a foundation for trustworthy AI-enabled media ecosystems while supporting broadcasters, audiences, and digital platforms in mitigating misinformation and unauthorized content manipulation.

title: AI-Intelligent Demand-Sensitive Transportation Scheduling with IoT-Crowd Prediction an Reinforcement Learning Optimization
container-title: International Journal of Electronics and Communication Engineering
e7929b46c65f426a84f1694246bda8a2c0b2a5c9.abstract: Efficient scheduling of transportation in smart cities is made difficult by the dynamic nature of passenger demand and crowd movements. Previous methods for scheduling, which use established timetables and explicit guidelines, struggle to adapt to real-time changes in demand, often resulting in long wait times for passengers, inefficient usage of transportation resources, and higher overall operating costs. This research presents a cluster-aware intelligent transportation framework that combines an approach to forecasting transportation demand with an adaptive scheduling process using data from IoT-based mobile signals. The use of DBSCAN to determine areal mobility clusters from the mobile signal data allowed a Cluster-Aware CNN-GRU model to learn complex patterns of spatial-temporal movement, resulting in the accurate prediction of the future demand for transportation. The proposed forecasting methodology achieved high levels of accuracy in its prediction of demand, with a MAE of 0.1033, and an RMSE of 0.1290. The forecasted demand was then utilized as input to a Deep Q-Network (DQN) scheduling module, which allocated transportation resources dynamically based on the forecasted mobility needs of the population. Analysis of the experimental data demonstrates that using the hybrid forecasting/scheduling framework led to a reduction in both passengers wait times and operational costs while also increasing vehicle utilization as compared to traditional scheduling methods. The combination of the Cluster-Aware CNN-GRU demand forecasting and DQN-based scheduling provides a scalable, efficient, and demand-responsive means for managing urban transportation systems.

title: AI-driven assessment of a social media intervention for AD/ADRD caregivers: a stage II-III trial of 966 participants
container-title: npj Mental Health Research
d282094e174d7e25c2555c169bc51a63ff4c87fe.abstract: Abstract Digital community support for family members of a person with Alzheimer’s disease and related dementias (AD/ADRD) is promising, yet its effectiveness is unknown. In an NIH Stage II/III clinical trial ( n = 966), African American and Hispanic family caregivers, aged 18 and older, received daily social support messages for 12 months. The primary outcomes were the emotional valence score, quantified using natural language processing, and the proportion of isolated participants who were continuously captured on the platform. High retention was achieved, with 82.3% of participants completing ≥ 9 months despite 86.7% of the cohort having low digital literacy. Both groups showed significant improvements in emotional valence scores ( p < 0.001), resulting in moderate-to-large effect sizes (Cohen’s d = 0.756). Furthermore, both groups demonstrated a large effect size in reducing the number of isolates, with a 46.2% reduction (Cohen’s h = 1.144). This trial demonstrates that AI-monitored, social media-based interventions can effectively improve emotional well-being and reduce the number of isolates among African American and Hispanic family caregivers. The high retention and moderate-to-large effect sizes suggest that leveraging common, accessible digital platforms can successfully overcome traditional barriers to care and clinical trial participation for digitally underserved populations.

title: Trust-Aware Federated Meta-Learning with Adaptive Privacy and Explainable AI for IoT Healthcare
container-title: International Journal of Electronics and Communication Engineering
61e8f0bbdef3f17816c84ac0305132b81f46675c.abstract: The increasing deployment of connected sensing devices in healthcare enables distributed physiological monitoring and data-driven clinical support, but centralized collection of sensitive records creates substantial privacy and security concerns. This paper presents a Trust-Aware Federated Meta-Learning with Adaptive Privacy and Explainable AI (TAFML-XAI) framework for heterogeneous IoT healthcare environments. The framework combines trust-weighted aggregation, adaptive Gaussian differential privacy, Model-Agnostic Meta-Learning (MAML), and federated SHAP-based explanations. The trust scores are computed based on the divergence between each client update and the global model, while privacy-preserving perturbations (modes of differential privacy) are imposed on the updates before sending. The revised formulation explicitly analyzes the interaction between privacy noise, trust estimation, and explanation stability. Experiments reported in the manuscript use the MIT-BIH Arrhythmia, PPG-DaLiA, and UCI Air Quality datasets. The reported classification accuracy of the proposed framework is 98.61%, while robustness experiments report 97% and 94% accuracy with 10% and 20% noisy/adversarial clients, respectively. The reported meta-learning experiment reduces convergence from 120 to 75 communication rounds and increases personalization accuracy from 88% to 97%. SHAP evaluation reports fidelity of 96.2%, consistency of 94.8%, and feature-importance correlation of 93.5%. The results show that the integrated framework can improve robustness, personalization, privacy-utility control, and interpretability; however, the centralized baseline and resource-overhead measurements require controlled reruns before the final submission.

title: Building Explainable Sales Intelligence Systems: A Product-Oriented Model for Embedding AI Insights into Enterprise Sales Workflows
container-title: International Journal of Advanced Artificial Intelligence Research
6473204d9164c03c728b3e9c078487b87b46c820.abstract: While Enterprise sales systems have dashboards to track revenue, customers, and buying trends, reports often require reading between the lines to determine what's good and what's bad before deciding which accounts to focus on. In this research, an explainable Sales Intelligence framework is proposed that transforms transaction-level information into analytical evidence at the customer level and converts it into conversations to support decision-making. The following is an example of the framework: the UCI Online Retail dataset consists of 541,909 online retail transactions from a UK retail company from 1 December 2010 to 9 December 2011. Data preparation removes missing customer identifiers, invalid quantity/unit price data, and expired entries. This results in 397884 transaction lines, 18532 invoices, 4338 identifiable customers, 3665 products, 37 countries, and the following actual retained revenue (facts as of 31 December 2018): £8,911,407.90. Customer revenue, product activity, average order value, purchase frequency, and recency are calculated using deterministic methods to segment and assess account health. The proposed architecture leverages numerical computation and evidence retrieval to interpret AI-generated results and connect explanations/recommendations to verified transaction indicators, with an emphasis on algorithms. The proposed architecture interprets artificial intelligence results and connects evidence/messages and/or recommendations to certified transaction indicators, with an emphasis on algorithms. The study provides empirical results from the transaction analysis process. It proposes definitions of measures to evaluate an agent's future operational application, including numerical accuracy, retrieval precision and recall, F1 score, recommendation relevance, explanation agreement, error rate, and response latency. Validate data from the enterprise CRM and sales-interaction data (recommended).

title: Exploring personal and contextual factors influencing pre-service English teachers' willingness to integrate AI into their future teaching practices
container-title: Frontiers in Psychology
5c5850d8c8815bb94cfbf0b1145f782dbcc71dc4.abstract: Despite the transformative potential that AI promises for English language teaching (ELT), there remains a paucity of inquiry into the readiness of pre-service English teachers (PSETs) to integrate AI into their future instructional practice, particularly within the Chinese educational context. Grounded in the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) and Social Cognitive Theory (SCT), this study examines the personal and contextual predictors shaping PSETs' willingness to integrate AI (WIAI) into their future ELT endeavours. A questionnaire was administered to 306 PSETs, investigating the interrelationships among perceived usefulness (PU), perceived ease of use (PEU) of AI, AI-specific technological pedagogical content knowledge (AI-TPACK), AI language technological knowledge (AIL-TK), AI technological pedagogical knowledge (AI-TPK), AI self-efficacy (AISE), peer support (PS), and university support and resources (USAR) in relation to PSETs' WIAI. Structural equation modelling analysis substantiated 15 of the 21 hypothesised relationships. The complex interrelations were mapped to offer stakeholders with a theoretically grounded framework for supporting PSETs' WIAI in Chinese and other similar educational contexts.

title: Beyond affective coping and use frequency: academic rumination, generative AI dependency, and two dimensions of perceived cognitive debt
container-title: Frontiers in Psychology
8c9c607dbb4a2d6e0f057b26cce9e28c1c2dbd11.abstract: Background Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) can support learning and emotion regulation, yet frequent or coping-oriented use does not necessarily constitute difficult-to-regulate dependency. It remains unclear how academic rumination and affective coping are positioned relative to dependency and whether dependency is differentially associated with perceived costs to knowledge internalization and independent reasoning. This study examined these distinctions within a single educational psychology model. Methods A cross-sectional survey included 611 current GenAI users recruited through university settings in Tianjin, China (91.7% first-year students). Dependency was a continuous, nonclinical tendency. Ordinal CFA and WLSMV SEM evaluated a prespecified partial association model. Covariate adjustment, four alternative measurement specifications, an AR-score hybrid, and observed-score regressions assessed sensitivity. Results In the reference model, academic rumination was associated with affective coping (β = 0.283), and both were associated with dependency (β = 0.187 and 0.555). Dependency was associated with perceived internalization/memory debt (β = 0.550) and independent-reasoning debt (β = 0.644); their standardized difference was 0.095 (95% Monte Carlo CI [0.032, 0.157]). The corresponding observed-score coefficients were 0.413 and 0.518, with a difference of 0.105 (95% bootstrap CI [0.035, 0.175]). Both serial coefficient products remained positive, but the negative conditional coping-internalization association was not sustained in the observed-score analysis. Reported frequency had no unique association in the combined adjusted model. Alternative measurement models retained robust RMSEA of 0.090–0.097; robust hybrid indices were unavailable. Conclusion The results provide tentative evidence of differentiated self-reported associations among coping, frequency, dependency, and cognitive concerns. Measurement misfit remains unresolved, and the coping-outcome coefficients were sensitive to construct representation. Observed-score consistency for dependency and serial products does not validate the latent structure or establish temporal or causal mediation. These predominantly first-year, Tianjin-based cross-sectional data do not establish objective cognitive decline or generality across student populations.

title: From technology to meaningful learning: cognitive, communicative, and cross-cultural effects of AI integration in bilingual education
container-title: Frontiers in Psychology
eefe70606803b68556d138f445f0ac06ee686f4b.abstract: Background Integration of artificial intelligence (AI) in bilingual education is increasingly consequential for students' cognitive engagement and professional communication, yet prior research has examined these outcomes largely in isolation. Whether learning engagement and cross-cultural competence (CCC) operate as simultaneous, parallel indirect pathways linking AI integration to perceived learning effectiveness and business communication skill remains underexamined, and cultural intelligence has rarely been modeled as a boundary condition on the intercultural pathway. Methods Drawing on a cross-sectional dataset of 604 bilingual education students across 13 universities in China, this study integrated the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology, Social Cognitive Theory, and Cultural Intelligence Theory within a single framework. Ordinary least squares regression with HC3 robust standard errors and partial least squares structural equation modeling with bootstrap-based indirect effect and latent moderation analyses were employed. Results All three indirect pathways were statistically supported: AI → learning engagement → perceived learning effectiveness (β = 0.191), AI → CCC → business communication skill (β = 0.278), and AI → CCC → perceived learning effectiveness (β = 0.202), each carrying a larger share of the AI-outcome association than the corresponding direct path. The model explained 28.38% of variance in learning engagement, 34.33% in CCC, 40.85% in business communication skill, and 47.28% in perceived learning effectiveness. Cultural intelligence positively moderated the AI → CCC association (β = 0.200), with simple slopes rising from 0.298 at low cultural intelligence to 0.697 at high cultural intelligence. Conclusion AI integration is associated with distal learning and communication outcomes predominantly through engagement-related and intercultural mechanisms, with cultural intelligence conditioning the strength of the intercultural pathway. These findings suggest that AI funding in bilingual education should be conditioned on process metrics, learning engagement and intercultural capability, rather than on tool procurement alone. Structured intercultural scaffolding should be required as an accreditation condition for AI-supported bilingual courses, and cultural intelligence screening at program entry with tiered support for lower-cultural-intelligence learners warrants consideration, given that the benefits of AI-supported learning are non-uniform across learners.

title: AI-based personalized exercise and health recommendation system using hybrid modeling
container-title: Frontiers in Artificial Intelligence
828e910a25704ecbdd3d47250c2f2bfd80ffea9d.abstract: Introduction Growing rate of sedentary living and chronic diseases has brought to light the necessity of smart systems that are able to provide individualized fitness instructions. Methods This paper suggests a hybrid health and fitness recommendation system, which incorporates machine learning models that are supervised alongside a rule-based reasoning system to produce personalized fitness and exercise recommendations. The system interprets structured user information such as demographic variables, body composition, cardiovascular variables, exercise habits, and experience to categorize the intensity of activities, deduce fitness objectives and estimate calorie loss. Evaluation algorithms based on multiple regression and classification were tested to predict the estimate of energy expenditure as well as classify the level of activity, whilst a goal inference engine turned predictive results into recommendations that could be acted upon. Results The experiments showed a high level of prediction and classification of activities, which proved the effectiveness of integrating physiological indicators of behavioral features. Discussion The suggested hybrid method enhances explanatory ability and decreases reliance on continuous data of wearable sensors thus it can be used in the real world to implement in the mobile health application and fitness management system. The system offers individualized exercise plans based on ability of the user and preventive healthcare through safe and sustainable exercise. Altogether, the research develops a scalable and interpretable intelligent recommendation system that can help to engage and lead to healthier lifestyles.

title: Rethinking Assessment and Academic Integrity in the Era of Generative Artificial Intelligence: Empirical Findings from a Computer Science School
container-title: AI, Computer Science and Robotics Technology
9b38b5ecedbc55c88a2b986716c37ce8effda434.abstract: The rapid proliferation of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) demands urgent empirical investigation into its role in undergraduate studies. This study examines the transformative impact of these tools in higher education (HE) in Algeria. The primary objective is to investigate how students at the National School of Computer Science (ESI) in Algiers use GenAI tools. The research also aims to provide evidence-based recommendations for Algerian HE institutions on academic integrity and pedagogical adaptation. Using a case study methodology, the research combined a GenAI use survey of 74 students with an educational experiment involving 12 teams in November 2023. The findings reveal a high adoption rate: 94.44% of students use GenAI, and 73.61% report daily use. GenAI serves as a powerful ancillary educational tool that shifts focus from content memorisation to competency application. In the experimental phase, 100% of teams relied on GenAI tools to execute the core cognitive and text-generation tasks. However, several groups integrated conventional auxiliary software to support their final visual deliverables. However, the quality of interaction remains narrow. Practical implications for HE institutions in Algeria suggest that teachers and trainers must restructure tutorials and practical work to favour complex, collaborative problem-solving. Additionally, institutions should prioritise formative over summative assessment and implement comprehensive AI literacy training to safeguard academic integrity.

title: Exploring the Impact of Generative AI on Student Learning and Academic Performance in Oman
container-title: International Journal of Innovative Science and Research Technology
88474877496d158a3a5debfec6862a21a11ffe64.abstract: The rapid integration of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) in higher education is transforming traditional learning environments, leading to new patterns of student engagement and varied academic outcomes. The usage of AI by Sultanate of Oman students in the academic year 2026 is thoroughly investigated in this paper. It examines the association between prominent AI products like ChatGPT, Copilot, Gemini, Grammarly, and Notion AI and demographic and academic parameters like age, gender, and education level (Diploma, Advanced Diploma, and B.Tech). The study also assesses how daily AI usage affects student satisfaction and academic achievement.

title: A bibliometric analysis of clinical research trends in temporomandibular disorders and associated pain: from pain management to AI-assisted diagnosis and treatment
container-title: Journal of Oral & Facial Pain and Headache
8d87b9e194ea3e811b867202845f149b1251fc9a.abstract: Background: This study aimed to provide an analysis of the global research status, collaboration networks, core hotspots, and emerging trends in temporomandibular disorders (TMD) and associated pain using bibliometric methods, to identify research gaps and provide references for future basic and translational research. Methods: Publications on temporomandibular disorders and associated pain published between 01 January 2016 and 01 April 2026 were retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection (WOSCC). CiteSpace and VOSviewer were used to analyse countries/regions, authors, journals, institutions, funding agencies, and keywords. Results: A total of 4917 publications were identified. The annual number of publications showed a steady increasing trend. The United States was the leading country in global research in this field, with 904 publications, followed by Brazil (697) and China (650). The Universidade de São Paulo was the most productive institution (233). The Journal of Oral Rehabilitation ranked first among journals with 519 publications. Keyword analysis revealed that keywords with the highest burst strength in recent years included “artificial intelligence” (7.75), “pain management” (7.23), “etiology” (5.97), and “oral behaviours” (5.05), indicating potential future research directions. Conclusions: Research in this field has shown a steady upward trend. Current hotspots focus on four major themes:(1) organic pathological changes and diagnosis of the temporomandibular joint; (2) pain assessment and comorbidity research; (3) epidemiological characteristics, risk factors, and psychological comorbidities; and (4) clinical management, rehabilitation strategies, and evidence-based interventions. This study also suggests that standardised pain management and Artificial Intelligence (AI)-assisted diagnosis and treatment are emerging and promising directions.

title: Methods of Intelligent Automation of Software System Analysis Using AI Agents in the Development and Operation of Web Applications
container-title: International Journal of Modern Computer Science and IT Innovations
f4da4e7e62e76feb4330bf31c2c77e1b7fc03bf4.abstract: AI agents built on large language models now take part in the analysis of software systems, yet evidence on their use across the life cycle of web applications remains scattered among benchmark reports and separate field studies. This article aims to systematize methods of agent-based analysis in the development and operation of web applications and to substantiate a model for assigning agent autonomy. The study combines a structured review of 25 sources published from 2020 to 2026, comparative analysis of benchmark results, content analysis of field studies, and a qualitative case study of two web products from the author's practice. The synthesis suggests that the strength of the verification oracle may be a more stable basis for assigning autonomy than benchmark capability scores; a direct comparative test of this hypothesis remains necessary. The article proposes an oracle-gated model with four layers, a matrix of four autonomy modes, and five monitoring indicators. The conclusions support staged adoption that begins with tasks backed by executable checks. The findings will interest web developers, game developers, engineering managers, and researchers in software engineering.

title: Multidimensional AI Literacy and Students’ Acceptance of AI-Enabled Learning Technologies: A Higher-Order Extension of the Technology Acceptance Model
b04f2ccea729765c54b802f440e0309d3f00f25b.abstract: Abstract AI-enabled learning technologies are becoming routine in higher education. However, acceptance research tends to explain adoption through beliefs about technology while paying less attention to the capabilities that learners bring to AI interaction. Although AI literacy has recently been linked to acceptance, it is often modeled as a global score or as separate dimensions, leaving unresolved whether related competencies operate collectively within the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) mechanism. This study tests a higher-order extension of the TAM using survey data from 528 students across three Indonesian universities who had prior experience with AI for learning. AI literacy was specified through awareness, usage skills, critical understanding, and ethics awareness and estimated using a disjoint two-stage partial least squares structural equation modeling procedure. The results support a coherent higher-order representation and show that AI literacy is most strongly associated with perceived ease of use and is also positively related to perceived usefulness and attitude. Within TAM, attitude shows a stronger direct relationship with behavioral intention than usefulness. These findings position AI literacy as a learner capability layer that complements technology beliefs in explaining students’ evaluations of AI-enabled learning technologies. The study contributes a measurement-to-mechanism perspective that maintains practical, critical, and ethical competence in acceptance research and suggests that implementation should consider learner capability alongside access and usability. Because the evidence is cross-sectional, self-reported, and multi-tool, the relationships should be interpreted as associations rather than causal effects.

title:
Beyond Structure
Generation: Toward Reaction-Aware
Generative AI for Catalyst Discovery
container-title: ACS Applied Catalysis
82d84b602772915e77e3730428ad191ea1b09401.abstract: Abstract Generative artificial intelligence (AI) has expanded catalyst discovery from predefined libraries to ultralarge surface–adsorbate spaces. We contend that as generative workflows reach the million-structure scale, the central challenge is shifting from increasing generation scale to identifying catalytically relevant regions of chemical space. This calls for reaction-aware discovery: candidates must remain viable across coupled intermediates, competing pathways, and operating conditions, while predictions must be reliable enough to guide the next decision. This requires generative models to be coupled with hierarchical evaluation, mechanistic and kinetic modeling, and experimental feedback. Crucially, we distinguish automation from autonomy: autonomous discovery begins when new evidence changes what is generated, calculated, or tested next. Progress should be judged not by the number of generated structures, but by how effectively a discovery system converts chemical-space exploration into experimentally credible catalytic decisions.

title: AI-Driven Predictive Analytics in Education
container-title: International Journal of Social Science and Human Research
0e9539dbaac94f931b380a002412977901193926.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI)-driven predictive analytics is transforming educational practice by using data to forecast student outcomes and inform interventions in both K–12 and higher education. This paper provides a comprehensive literature-based analysis of how predictive models are employed to identify at-risk students early, personalize learning pathways, and improve institutional decision-making. The review synthesizes theoretical insights from learning analytics and empirical findings from case studies and systematic reviews. Current evidence highlights significant potential benefits – such as improved student retention and tailored instruction – alongside pressing ethical, legal, and practical challenges. Key issues include algorithmic bias and fairness, the “black box” lack of explainability in AI models, and student data privacy concerns under laws like FERPA. A literature-based methodology is described, and findings are discussed in depth. The discussion examines how predictive analytics systems have been implemented (often with notable success in improving graduation rates) and how unresolved challenges (e.g., bias propagation or stakeholder mistrust) may undermine these gains. Finally, implications and recommendations for practice and policy are explored, emphasizing the need for transparent, equitable, and responsible use of AI in education. The paper’s formal academic tone and APA-structured presentation make it suitable for dissemination at a national AI in Education conference.

title: An Explainable AI Framework for Marketing Customer Segmentation and Campaign Response Prediction
container-title: The American Journal of Engineering and Technology
ae22ac2ba925dbd15c7e5e6eebf8f3d6b84bb3cc.abstract: The segmentation of clients and the forecast of marketing campaign response are essential for optimising marketing expenditures and enhancing customer participation. This work suggests an XAI approach for segmenting the clients, predicting the responses using machine learning, and targeting them based on profit. Specifically, 2,055 cleansed customer records were extracted from the Kaggle Customer Personality Analysis dataset through preprocessing. We combine multiple clustering methods using consensus clustering to find the different segments of consumers, using Principal Component Analysis (PCA). The performance of seven machine learning classifiers is assessed using five-fold cross-validation, considering several performance metrics. The best accuracy (ACC) is 87.59% for Gradient Boosting (GB) and the ROC-AUC is 0.909 for Logistic Regression. The segment integration yields an improved recall (REC) rate of 79.4% and F1 score (F1) of 0.649, compared to the previous situation of REC value 73.0% and F1 value 0.622. The resulting profit-optimised solution is a projected profit of 61.1 currency units per 100 consumers. Moreover, elements such as catalogue purchases, recency, and campaign history are identified as elements that are significant via the techniques of SHapley Additive ExPlanations (SHAP) and permutation feature significance. The proposed approach will enable more accurate client segmentation, targeted marketing campaigns, and efficient use of resources. More testing is needed on a variety of real-life datasets to ensure greater generalisability, but the outcomes are encouraging.

title: The Effect Of AI Tools On English Language Proficiency Among Northwestern University Students
container-title: Scholarly Horizon Journal
73e20a91bf9161cbe0f12cea6c5fc8acede1d1be.abstract: The integration of AI-powered tools in education is becoming increasingly prominent. Understanding how these tools influence English language proficiency, writing skills, and overall communication abilities is essential. The study aimed to determine both the benefits and disadvantages posed by AI-powered tools, providing insights that can improve educational practices and enhance learning outcomes in language proficiency among students. Using a descriptive research design, the study aimed to determine the perceptions of students from Northwestern University regarding the use of AI-powered tools in their English learning. The study involved the Northwestern University college students enrolled during the First Semester of the Academic Year 2025-2026. Specifically, a total of three hundred sixty-two (362) students were randomly selected as respondents to ensure diverse representation from various colleges within the university. The study used a researcher-made survey questionnaire to determine the perceptions of Northwestern University students regarding the use of AI-powered tools in their English learning, focusing on both the benefits and disadvantages of these tools. Hence, the instrument contained twenty (20) indicators to determine the perceptions of students on the use of AI-powered tools in their English learning in terms of its benefits and disadvantages, and another ten (10) indicators to determine their perceptions on how AIpowered tools affect their English proficiency. Data were analyzed using weighted means, frequency counts, and percentages based on specified range intervals. Findings indicate that students generally agree on the usefulness of AI-powered tools in several areas, including vocabulary building, grammar improvement, comprehension enhancement, and increased writing confidence. However, they also identified some issues, such as overdependence on these AI-powered tools, problems with accuracy, and the potential weakening of independent learning skills. Additionally, respondents perceived a high impact of AI-powered tools on their English proficiency. The results underscore the need for a balanced approach to language learning, highlighting both the potential benefits and disadvantages of using AI-powered tools in educational practices. This research contributes to the ongoing discourse regarding the role of AI in education and its implications for future language learning strategies.

title: Counting the Bandages: On measuring the time that AI saves
d7eee220797f0a6b7ea18084268a1eb28ba8c4ef.abstract: I consider what it means for AI assistance to save time. I contrast a stopwatch view, on which time saved is whatever the clock records, with a ledger view, on which it is a counterfactual that has to be read next to the errors the work lets through, and I argue for the latter. The argument has four parts. I define a model-free pair of quantities, time saved and excess escaped defects, and one decision number built from them: the break-even defect cost. I give a baseline model of checking in which, until the model is good enough not to check, a calibrated worker's escaped-defect rate does not depend on how good the model is; checking time grows with the logarithm of the model's error rate; and over-trust buys minutes on the clock at a larger cost in total minutes. I show what randomized studies can and cannot identify, and I replicate METR's developer study from its public data: the same 246 issues support a slowdown of 19% or 24% depending on the estimand (34% without adjusting for a chance imbalance), and AI helped on somewhere between 3% and 82% of them. Finally, I restate the published record, with stated bounds in place of imported point assumptions. In GDPval's own review-every-output workflow, review time alone caps GPT-5's speedup at 3.6x; the consultants outside the frontier were faster, and more often wrong. Last, I test two of the model's predictions in a small pre-specified experiment on AI reviewers checking AI drafts of the same kind of brief, built from SEC filings made after the models' training data were collected. Told the drafter's true error rate, the reviewer checked more as it rose, but all-or-nothing, switching near where its prompt's costs break even. Told that the drafter erred ten times less often than it did, it checked 7 fewer of 9 figures and let a wrong figure through in 22.5% of briefs instead of none: faster and worse, entirely through reduced effort. This paper replaces my earlier TSB proposal.

title: AI- Carbon Footprint Calculator
container-title: International Journal of Advanced Research in Science Communication and Technology
0275d6095ec3015980f97f30acfe9e2c4b33c44b.abstract: The AI Carbon Footprint Calculator is a smart system designed to estimate the carbon emissions produced by an individual or organization. It uses artificial intelligence and user-provided information such as electricity usage, transportation, food habits, and lifestyle activities. The system calculates the approximate amount of carbon dioxide emissions generated from these activities. It helps users understand how their daily actions affect the environment. The calculator provides a simple and user-friendly way to measure carbon footprints. It also creates awareness about environmental sustainability and climate change. The proposed system uses AI-based techniques to analyze the collected data and provide accurate carbon footprint estimations. Users can enter information related to travel, energy consumption, waste generation, and other activities. The system processes this information using predefined emission factors and intelligent analysis. Based on the results, it identifies activities that contribute more to carbon emissions. The system can also provide personalized suggestions to reduce emissions. This makes the calculator useful for promoting environmentally responsible habits. The main objective of the AI Carbon Footprint Calculator is to encourage users to reduce their environmental impact. It provides meaningful insights into carbon emissions and helps users make better lifestyle decisions. The system can compare emissions before and after adopting ecofriendly practices. It may also track changes in the user's carbon footprint over time. By combining AI with carbon emission analysis, the project supports sustainable living. Overall, the system provides an effective approach to creating awareness and encouraging carbon reduction

title: AI AS A COGNITIVE ENHANCEMENT TOOL: A FOUR-TIER INSTRUCTIONAL MODEL FOR TEM-8 WRITING
container-title: World Journal of Educational Studies
e0562398dbfc8fc663dda630cdf8412135104067.abstract: The writing task in Test for English Majors Grade Eight (TEM-8) places high demands on learners’ ability to synthesize information and express critical perspectives. Drawing on teaching practice in the English Writing and Translating Skills Training course for English majors at a Double First-Class agricultural university, this study develops a four-tier model of AI-enhanced writing instruction, with the four tiers corresponding to four ascending levels of cognitive engagement: evaluative regulation, critical analysis, comparative discernment, and selective revision. Using ChatGPT and DeepSeek as supporting tools, the model treats AI as a tool for cognitive enhancement rather than a substitute writer. By analyzing the strengths and weaknesses of AI-generated essays, comparing outputs from different platforms, and using AI critically to revise their own work, students make a cognitive shift from passively receiving feedback to actively directing their use of the technology. This paper explains the rationale, key components, and implementation of the model, offering a replicable framework for integrating AI into writing instruction for English majors in higher education.

title: Does Graph Structure Improve AI-Generated Text Detection? A Controlled Audit with Tuned Baselines
6a301678de5b5866c88e670f3ab2a03c257adc22.abstract: Abstract Graph neural network (GNN) detectors of AI-generated text report state-of-the-art accuracy, and the architectural claim that graph topology captures signals invisible to sequential classifiers is now common in the literature. We report the complete lifecycle of one such detector, from construction to falsification. AEGIS, a graph attention network over k-nearest-neighbour text graphs with multi-signal edge weights, reaches 98.50% accuracy on scientific abstracts with only 73K trainable parameters, outperforming five established baselines. We then subject our own system to the evaluation its headline number deserves: generation-time length control, format normalization, leakage-free splits, a tuned frozen-embedding probe as the calibrated null, and a 10 × 10 cross-generator transfer study over three seeds. Under this protocol the graph's apparent contribution collapses from +0.240 AUROC over a surface baseline to −0.0004 AUROC against the tuned probe, inside the measured replication noise floor, and the two detectors' transfer geographies are near-identical (ρ = 0.986). A single untuned regularization default manufactured a +0.027 phantom advantage. The structural differences the graph encodes are real, but they are a re-encoding of information already present in the embeddings. We distil the audit into a practical checklist for evaluating architectural claims in text detection, and argue that accuracy numbers and mechanism claims must be validated separately.

title: Quillaic acid and echinocystic acid attenuate atherosclerosis: evidence from in vitro and in vivo studies
container-title: PeerJ
006be2786712f8209e38ff5c4bd44b34f830d26e.abstract: Background Atherosclerosis (AS) is an inflammatory disease characterized by the formation of lipid-laden lesions in arterial walls. Quillaic acid (QA) and echinocystic acid (EA) are natural pentacyclic triterpenes with diverse biological activities. However, whether QA and EA can ameliorate AS has not been reported. Methods In this study, we first investigated the effects of QA and EA in reducing foam cell accumulation and inflammation in vitro . Then, the therapeutic effects of QA and EA (i.p., 5 mg/kg) were evaluated in ApoE knockout (ApoE -/- ) mice fed a high-fat/high-cholesterol diet. Results In vitro experiments demonstrated that both QA and EA suppressed oxidized low-density lipoprotein (ox-LDL)-induced foam cell formation by inhibiting cholesterol uptake and also inhibited lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-induced inflammatory responses. In high-fat/high-cholesterol diet-fed ApoE -/- mice, QA or EA treatment significantly reduced serum lipid levels, decreased inflammatory factor release, and attenuated atherosclerotic plaque formation. At the tested dose, EA showed slightly better anti-inflammatory and plaque-reducing effects than QA. Transcriptomic profiling revealed enrichment of genes associated with “Cell adhesion molecules” and immune response pathways in the aorta of QA-treated mice. For EA, enrichment was observed for genes involved in “Circadian rhythms” in both liver and aorta, as well as genes related to “Vascular smooth muscle contraction” and the “cyclic guanosine monophosphate (cGMP)-protein kinase G (PKG) signaling pathway” in aortic tissues. Real-time quantitative PCR (qPCR) analysis confirmed altered expression of selected circadian rhythm-related genes in the liver of EA- and QA-treated mice and in ox-LDL-induced foam cells. EA also increased cGMP levels in these foam cells. Conclusions This study provides the first evidence for the anti-atherosclerotic effects of QA and EA and offers new insights into the potential of natural products for the treatment of cardiovascular diseases.

title: SgriWind-CN: A Sub-Daily Gridded High-Resolution Near-Surface Wind Speed Dataset for China, Generated by an AI-Driven Integration of In-Situ Observations
7bbff7dd77013e1416d4c397750c7593bd973bd9.abstract: Abstract. Reliable near-surface wind speed (NSWS) data underpin a wide range of research in hydrology, climatology, wind energy, and environmental change. However, estimates of long-term changes in NSWS remain highly uncertain, largely because of incomplete temporal coverage, uneven station distribution, and inhomogeneities in observational records. Here, we release the SgriWind-CN dataset, a new sub-daily gridded NSWS dataset over China, generated from 6-hourly observations collected at 2,384 meteorological stations during 1980–2023. After rigorous quality control and sub-daily homogenization, we apply a deep learning model, PConvUNet, to reconstruct a sub-daily, gridded wind speed dataset. The resulting product effectively reproduces the spatial distribution of NSWS and performs well in data-sparse areas. Quantitative evaluation shows that PConvUNet substantially outperforms conventional interpolation methods: it best preserves the original statistical distribution, as reflected in the lowest Kullback–Leibler divergence, and reduces the mean absolute error on the test set by at least 65.3 % relative to alternative approaches. The model also exhibits an advantage in capturing extreme wind events. A reverse interpolation validation test further confirms the product’s robustness, yielding a national mean bias of less than 0.05 m·s−1. Beyond NSWS, the dataset also includes surface roughness, land cover type, elevation, latitude, and longitude to support diverse user applications and independent evaluation. This study aims to provide a robust, high-resolution data foundation for advancing understanding of wind variability and its broader impacts across Earth system sciences. SgriWind-CN is publicly available at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22812484 (Bai et al., 2026).

title: Supplementary material to "SgriWind-CN: A Sub-Daily Gridded High-Resolution Near-Surface Wind Speed Dataset for China, Generated by an AI-Driven Integration of In-Situ Observations"
The Impact of AI on the Future of Work and the Gig Economy in Nigeria

2cdf07d0bb78eb858bb31ab4fe11f6e57e3f782f.abstract: This paper investigate the impact of the impact of a i on the future of work and the gig economy in Nigeria. While AI technologies have the potential to improve efficiency and productivity in various industries, they also raise concerns about job displacement and the need for upskilling and retraining. In the gig economy, AI may create new opportunities for freelance workers, but it also has the potential to further exacerbate income inequality. The manuscript found that It is crucial for policymakers, businesses, and workers in Nigeria to proactively address these challenges and leverage the potential of AI to create a more inclusive and sustainable future of work. Embracing AI responsibly and with a focus on equity and exclusivity will be essential for shaping a positive future for the gig economy and work in Nigeria.furthermore, the show that the world of work is changing with a multi-generational workforce and changing employment models with more flexibility. The location is no more a constraint to acquire capable talent. The gig economy is booming, and today’s workers prefer to adopt the gig model, and employers are increasingly preferring gig workers to the permanent workforce and preferring skills and competencies over formal qualifications. They need to upskill them with a new set of competencies.

title: ADOPTION OF AI TOOLS IN CONTENT CREATION AMONG PROFESSIONALS AND MEDIA STUDENTS IN KERALA: A COMPREHENSIVE ANALYSIS OF THE SILENCER HYPOTHESIS
container-title: International Journal of Research -GRANTHAALAYAH
5bf9afdf588e682886e3623d743416477f0e0fd7.abstract: In recent years, the integration of AI tools in various fields has revolutionized the way tasks are performed, including content creation. This study delves into a comprehensive analysis conducted, aimed at the degree of adoption of AI tools in content creation processes among professionals in Kerala. The study starts with an appreciation of the growth of AI technologies in use in industries and how they will likely impact the various professions. Technological, ethical and concerns about job losses were among the challenges. The Silencer hypothesis suggests that overreliance on AI may cause a suppression of human intellectual expression and engagement, leading to the metaphorical silencing of human intellect. Such reliance can stifle the development of critical thinking, creativity, and communication abilities, reshaping the nature of the intellectual consciousness of humans.

title: The Digital Companion in the Dorm Room: Emerging Role of AI Companions in Student Well-Being and Primary Care
10d2fe3aa4e9404472b3dffcedf2b95f3ecd04fa.abstract: Background: Artificial intelligence (AI) companions are increasingly used by post-secondary students for emotional support, stress management, and self-management, yet their potential implications for primary care in this population remain unclear. Students may engage with AI companions before encountering purpose-built therapeutic chatbots, which are more often accessed through intentional health-seeking or professional guidance. This distinction may position AI companions as an earlier influence on self-management and subsequent help-seeking. Objective: To examine how artificial intelligence (AI) companions may influence stress regulation, sleep quality, symptom interpretation, and healthcare-seeking behaviour among post-secondary students, and to identify the principal benefits, risks, and unresolved questions relevant to primary care. Methods: A conceptual narrative review was undertaken using literature identified through Harvard University’s Hollis Library and Google Scholar. Evidence related to AI companions, academic stress, sleep quality, emotional support, healthcare-seeking behaviour, primary care, and digital mental health was synthesized using Stress & Coping Theory and the stress-buffering hypothesis as theoretical foundations. Results: AI companions may support stress appraisal, cognitive reframing, emotional reflection, symptom articulation, and self-management before clinical encounters. However, they may also contribute to emotional overreliance, misinformation, reassurance seeking, sleep disruption, and altered help-seeking behaviour. This review proposes conceptual mechanisms linking AI companion engagement with stress regulation, sleep, and pathways into primary care while identifying relational intensity as a clinically meaningful dimension of engagement beyond frequency alone. Conclusion: AI companions should be understood as adjunctive rather than substitutive support. Their clinical relevance is based on how they can shape patients’ experiences before obtaining primary care. Longitudinal research is needed to determine how patterns of engagement influence stress, sleep, and healthcare utilization over time.

title: Confidence Does Not Travel: Cross-Dataset Validation of Selective AI for Photoplethysmographic Respiratory-Rate Monitoring Before Breathing-Centered Rehabilitation Deployment
c012d4267a2e63196e656bab02e51dcbe1f3c549.abstract: Background/Objectives: Photoplethysmography (PPG) could support unobtrusive respiratory-rate monitoring during breathing-centered rehabilitation. Accuracy measured in one cohort, however, says little about how the same estimator will behave after deployment elsewhere. Confidence estimates may also fail. We tested whether physiology-informed artificial intelligence and a learned error-prediction gate retained their performance across two clinically distinct public datasets. Methods: We conducted a retrospective, subject-separated benchmark using 53 BIDMC intensive-care recordings and 42 CapnoBase anesthesia recordings. From 32 s PPG windows advanced every 8 s, we derived four respiratory modulations and 51 rate, agreement, morphology, and signal-quality features. Six estimators were evaluated by five-fold grouped cross-validation and by bidirectional external transfer. A nested gradient-boosting model predicted each estimate's absolute error to support selective reporting. Performance was summarized with subject-bootstrap confidence intervals, Bland–Altman agreement, and risk–coverage analysis. Results: The analysis included 5262 windows from 95 participants. Within-dataset mean absolute error (MAE) was lowest for random forest on BIDMC (1.65 breaths/min) and Extra Trees on CapnoBase (3.55 breaths/min). The physiology-consensus model achieved 1.70 and 4.02 breaths/min, respectively. Its learned gate reduced MAE at 50% coverage to 0.93 and 2.01 breaths/min. Under external transfer, however, its MAE increased to 6.19 breaths/min for BIDMC→CapnoBase and 4.90 breaths/min for CapnoBase→BIDMC. Uncertainty–error Spearman correlation fell from 0.48 and 0.41 internally to 0.15 and 0.09 externally, and gating yielded only modest improvement. A fixed raw-spectral baseline outperformed the learned model in both transfer directions. Conclusions: Confidence measured within the development cohort did not establish safety after transfer. PPG-derived respiratory rate needs external calibration before it can guide rehabilitation feedback, even when point accuracy appears acceptable internally. Public benchmarks should report bidirectional transfer and risk–coverage behavior alongside random or subject-wise internal splits.

title: Seen and Unseen Load: Open-Data Visibility of AI Data-Centre Electricity Demand and Wind–Solar Headroom in China, Japan and South Korea
fe064c0267b0bdf599e83e5c53ecaa7dbc92283b.abstract: The debate over whether renewable energy can sustain AI growth relies on demand figures whose origin is rarely examined. We compare open, facility-level records with agency estimates for China, Japan, South Korea and the United States, using the Epoch AI GPU-cluster register (338 clusters), the International Energy Agency, Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory, South Korea's 11th Basic Plan for Electricity Supply and Demand, and Ember generation data. In 2024, visible load covers 3.8–6.3% of agency-estimated data-centre demand in the United States, 1.4–2.3% in China, at least 0.8–1.3% in Japan and at most 2.6% in South Korea. Data-centre growth absorbs 4–34% of observed wind and solar additions under agency estimates but only 0.13–1.0% under visible load, a ratio of 31 to 53. Reference estimates for China diverge by a factor of 2.6 (100 versus 260 TWh in 2024). The verdict on whether clean power keeps pace with AI therefore depends on what can be observed: while 92–99% of the load remains invisible in open registers, no stable answer is possible. We propose a minimum reporting standard for data-centre electricity.

title: Subscription-Free AI: Energy-Efficient On-Device Inference of Quantized Language Models on Low-Cost Edge Hardware
cee010f4aac9dec9319c63db15d6c095a047a152.abstract: Most people use AI by renting it from a cloud service, paying per token or per month and sending their data off the device. We ask whether low-cost local hardware can do the job instead, using only free data and open tools. Study A analyses 243 de-duplicated MLPerf Tiny results (v1.0 to v1.3) measured on microcontrollers, neural processors and FPGAs. Int8 made Cortex-M inference 1.9x to 3.8x faster than float32 with no loss in classification accuracy, a dedicated NPU spotted keywords 25x faster than the median Cortex M4, and energy per inference tracked latency with a log-log slope of 0.97 (R² = 0.72). Study B trains three transformer language models (0.8M to 6.4M parameters) on a 2-core CPU with a dependency-free NumPy implementation and evaluates post-training quantization from 16 to 1.58 bits. Four-bit weights in blocks of 32 raised validation loss by only 0.09% to 0.55% while shrinking the models 6.4x to 6.9x; below 4 bits the loss depended on block size, model scale and layer type, and clipping-based scale search reduced weight error yet increased model error. Portable C kernels decoded 0.4B- and 1.1B-scale weight geometries 2.7x faster at 4 bits than at FP32. Roofline, energy and cost models translate these results into bandwidth requirements, energy per token and the volume at which owning hardware beats renting a service.

title: Multi-constraint weighted-cost optimization for UAV path planning using an improved harris hawks optimization
container-title: Frontiers in Robotics and AI
81432b0fd94d25d00e0b60e869d2fef7c2a3db83.abstract: To mitigate the flight safety risks and ensure the feasibility of the trajectories for Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) in complex and hazardous environments, this paper proposes a multi-constraint weighted-cost optimization method using an Improved Harris Hawks Optimization (IHHO) algorithm. First, a weighted-cost function is formulated by aggregating path length, flight altitude, flight attitude, threat distance, and the metric of obstacle avoidance response time into a single objective, subject to the kinematic and safety constraints of the UAV. Second, to enhance the optimization performance in path planning, three improvement strategies are introduced to the standard HHO: (1) position updates inspired by natural exploration and trap avoidance mechanisms to augment population diversity and prevent local optima stagnation; (2) a cosine-exponential based non-linear energy decay strategy to replace the original linear decay, enhancing the global search capability; and (3) modulation of the number of Lévy flight iterations to refine local solution accuracy. Finally, experiments on a simulated map demonstrate that the proposed IHHO algorithm efficiently generates optimal trajectories that minimize the weighted cost while harmonizing flight efficiency, path smoothness, and obstacle avoidance safety. This provides a reliable methodological foundation for UAV mission execution in complex environments.

title: Machine Learning and Deep Learning: Emerging Techniques, Applications, and Future Trends-A Comprehensive Review
container-title: Computing&AI Connect
4fdc83846a4c182e6b38c58b8de0688bafd7419c.abstract: Machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) have emerged as powerful paradigms in artificial intelligence, enabling systems to learn patterns from data and automate complex decision-making processes. This paper presents a comprehensive review of machine learning and deep learning approaches, focusing on their fundamental principles, commonly used techniques, and diverse real-world applications. The study discusses core ML algorithms, neural network architectures, and the role of deep learning models in solving complex problems such as image recognition, natural language processing, healthcare analytics, and recommendation systems. Furthermore, the paper highlights the key differences between traditional machine learning methods and deep learning models, emphasizing their strengths and limitations. Recent research trends, including explainable AI, transfer learning, and large-scale data-driven modeling, are also examined to provide insights into the evolving landscape of intelligent systems. By synthesizing findings from recent literature, this review aims to offer researchers and practitioners a clearer understanding of current developments and future opportunities in machine learning and deep learning technologies.

title: Cooperate And Compete: Archives Can Gain More By Expecting Less From AI Training
e10c2d8864f7245c3ffa2bf842b87acb41806574.abstract: Abstract AI companies have increasingly approached archival organizations seeking access to unpublished or undigitized collections for model training. Many archival organizations have responded cautiously to these requests and lean toward rejection due to various concerns. Two major concerns are about the loss of item-level provenance in AI outputs and the loss of control over archival knowledge absorbed into AI models. This paper examines these two concerns and challenges some of the assumptions underlying them. It argues that the loss of item-level provenance in AI outputs may in fact constitute a competitive advantage for archival organizations. It analyzes the potential costs of refusing to work with AI companies and suggests that archival organizations negotiate agreements that preserve their competitive advantage while indemnifying them against liability arising from the misuse of archival knowledge incorporated into AI models. The paper further suggests that archival organizations tailor policies according to the legal status of individual collections, rely on RAG technology for reliable item-level citation, and advocate for government policies that encourage large AI companies to contribute to public goods. Such policies could help improve the public image of AI companies and motivate more archival organizations to collaborate with them.

title: Delving into AI disclosure architecture: Building trust in Indonesian telemedicine advertising
container-title: Innovative Marketing
9c17728c9f90b4ffad439b64fde262be314fd0bd.abstract: Type of the article: Research ArticleAbstractAI disclosure has become increasingly important in digital advertising, particularly in high-risk services such as telemedicine, where consumers evaluate message quality alongside provider accountability. This study aimed to examine how AI disclosure architecture, reflected in disclosure timing, disclosure specificity, and human control, influences perceived authenticity, message credibility, brand trust, and usage intention in Indonesian telemedicine advertising. A quantitative scenario-based online experiment used a 2 × 2 × 2 between-subjects design with 527 valid respondents. Data were analyzed using three-way factorial ANOVA, confirmatory factor analysis, structural equation modelling, and bootstrap analysis with 5,000 resamples. Early disclosure, high specificity, and stated professional review or oversight produced more favourable evaluations across the disclosure conditions examined. Human control generated the largest main effects on perceived authenticity (partial η² = 0.346), message credibility (partial η² = 0.316), brand trust (partial η² = 0.318), and usage intention (partial η² = 0.166). Perceived authenticity increased brand trust (β = 0.304, p &amp;lt; 0.001), message credibility had a stronger effect on brand trust (β = 0.598, p &amp;lt; 0.001), and brand trust increased usage intention (β = 0.736, p &amp;lt; 0.001). Timing and specificity showed significant indirect effects on brand trust, while human control showed both direct and indirect effects. The effects were predominantly additive, with only a small timing × human-control interaction for message credibility (partial η² = 0.009). These findings indicate that, when AI disclosure is present, timing, specificity, and stated professional oversight provide distinct trust-relevant information rather than functioning as a strongly synergistic configuration.Acknowledgment(s)The authors would like to express their sincere gratitude to all respondents who participated in this study and provided valuable responses for the experimental survey. The authors also thank the academic colleagues and research reviewers who provided constructive feedback during the development of the research instrument, experimental stimuli, and manuscript refinement. Their insights helped improve the clarity, methodological rigor, and overall quality of this study. Any remaining errors or deficiencies are solely the responsibility of the authors.

title: Navigating the Frontier of AI in Project Management Through Dynamic Alignment Across Four Interdependent Domains
container-title: Project Management Journal
3665cb0de726d8238c734ab9188324b5b31715be.abstract: Generative and agentic AI is becoming a constitutive feature of project work, reshaping task allocation, decision-making, authority, and required professional competencies. This Editorial conceptualizes this transformation as a problem of dynamic alignment, and addresses three major gaps in literature, i.e. limited evidence on AI outcomes and mechanisms, fragmented findings across analytical levels, and insufficiently developed integrative frameworks. To address such limitations, the paper proposes a framework of AI adoption in project management which comprises four interdependent domains; 1) technological domain, concerning system performance, transparency, and interoperability; 2) human domain, addressing competencies, trust, and human–AI collaboration; 3) organizational domain, encompassing strategic readiness, work design, and culture; and 4) institutional-societal domain, considering ethics, regulation, and societal value. The framework argues that AI value depends on alignment across domains rather than isolated technological capabilities. Misalignment may undermine outcomes when advanced systems exceed users' competencies, governance remains inadequate, or adoption outpaces ethical and regulatory safeguards. These relationships evolve over time, potentially affecting professionals' capacity for critical oversight. The Special Issue includes five contributions which examine these complementary aspects of AI in project management, including the retrieval-augmented generation for social risk identification in megaprojects, the inverted U-shaped relationship between digital employee adoption and team performance, organizational AI capability as a driver of project performance, the relationship between AI orientation and business success, and AI adoption as an organizational design challenge. Based on such contributions, the Editorial outlines a number of research priorities, including the need to calibrate reliance on AI, effective hybrid project work, integration of external requirements into substantive governance, accountability and societal value by design, longitudinal and multilevel investigation of cross-domain alignment, and stronger empirical evidence through experiments. The paper provides a foundation for cumulative research grounded on the central proposition that aligning technological, human, organizational, and institutional-societal conditions is essential to improving project outcomes while preserving professional judgment, accountable governance, and societal value.
