title: Awareness of Patient Rights in Digital Health Services
d63754933cd510a6c3cde5a59cc5ab1a57816026.abstract: Abstract Objective The purpose of this study is to investigate the degree of understanding of the rights of patients in terms of the features of their socio-demographic status and how they use digital health tools. Materials and Models: This research is a descriptive, observational and cross-sectional survey of 300 adults who are over the age of 18 and who are either familiar with digital health or have previously used at least one digital health service. The data collection consisted of two methods: a demographic questionnaire covering socio-demographic and digital health use features and a Patient Rights Awareness Scale consisting of 20 items. Descriptive statistics, parametric/non-parametric analysis, correlations, and regression modeling were carried out to analyze the data. Results The study found that people were aware of the patients' rights at a good level, and using the scale demonstrated good internal consistency. There were found differences in patient rights awareness with respect to education level and some characteristics of digital health utilization. In addition, a positive correlation between digital health knowledge with the level of awareness of patient rights was established, and this variable demonstrated the highest degree of relationship with the variable of awareness in the correlation analysis. Moreover, in the multivariate analysis, the variable of digital health knowledge was the one that maintained its significant correlation with the level of patient rights awareness regardless of the influence from other sociodemographic and digital health utilization variables. Conclusion Knowledge of patient rights in the digital health environment is closely related to the level of individuals’ digital health literacy. The findings indicate that expanding digital health services is not adequate; individuals should be supported in understanding and applying their rights in the digital environment. The implementation of issues such as patients’ rights, guarantee of privacy, protection of health data, and informed consent in digital health literacy programs may help in providing patient-centered and rights-based digital health solutions.

title: Measuring and Analyzing the Relationship Between Fiscal Discipline and Digital Governance and Foreign Reserve Adequacy Index: Evidence from the ARDL Cointegration Approach in Iraq for the Period (2024-2004)
container-title: F1000Research
1fd675244dc21ddb280bd6a0d9e21d754b06e71e.abstract: Objectives The research aims to demonstrate the role of financial discipline and digital transformation in enhancing Foreign Reserve Adequacy. This is achieved by measuring the Relationship of financial discipline and digital transformation indicators on the foreign reserves adequacy index. Methodology This research relies on a combination of the descriptive-deductive approach to present the economic concepts related to the research variables, and standard quantitative methods to test the research hypothesis using time series data comprising 21 observations for the period (2004-2024), Since the research sample covers relatively short period, the annual data were converted into quarterly data using a predefined standard equation available in EViews. Specifically, the conversion employed the “Quarterly” method with the “Linear” option, ensuring a continuous and consistent quarterly time series. Findings Estimating the Standard Limit Model (ARDL) showed a negative error correction coefficient, less than one, and highly significant, with a value of (CointEq(-1) = -0.076, p<0.01). In the long run, Indicators of fiscal discipline revealed a negative relationship between public spending (X1) and the foreign reserve adequacy index (β = -0.59, p > 0.05), while the relationship between public debt (X3) and the index was also found to be negative (β = -0.48, p < 0.01). Conversely—and contrary to expectations—the relationship between the net budget balance (X2) and the reserve adequacy index was positive in the long term (β = 0.30, p < 0.05). A key contribution of this research is the inclusion of digital transformation (X4) as a variable related to the foreign reserve adequacy index; the study demonstrated a positive association for this indicator (β = 0.13, p > 0.05). Conclusions The Digital Transformation Index confirmed that it is a suitable option for rentier economies to get rid of the resource curse through digital public financial management.

title: Audiovisual Enhancement of Digital Manuscript Collections: Exploring Implementation and Impact at the Palm Leaf Manuscript Study and Research Library (PLMSR)
container-title: TRIVALENT ත්‍රිසංයුජ: Journal of Archaeology, Tourism & Anthropology
f6f67de600b198dc1d84cf37234c9759b8302617.abstract: The preservation and digitalization of Sri Lanka’s palm leaf manuscripts represent a crucial effort to safeguard an endangered cultural heritage. The Palm Leaf Manuscript Study and Research Library (PLMSR) at the University of Kelaniya has led pioneering work in this domain, having digitized over 600,000 manuscript images and preserved more than 350 physical manuscripts encompassing a wide range of subjects, including Buddhist scriptures, traditional medicine, astrology, and literature. Traditional digitization methods focus primarily on static image capture, which inadvertently limits the conveyance of rich contextual, sensory, and interpretive information integral to understanding these manuscripts. This study explores the transformative potential of integrating audiovisual (AV) enhancements such as high-definition video documentation, interactive multimedia presentations, and expert-narrated content into the digital manuscript collections at PLMSR. The integration of AV technologies significantly enhances scholarly access by allowing researchers to engage with manuscripts in a multisensory manner, thereby improving interpretive depth and facilitating interdisciplinary research. Moreover, AV enhancements foster broader user engagement and contribute to physical preservation by reducing the need for manuscript handling. Findings indicate that this approach not only enriches academic research but also strengthens public outreach and cultural awareness, positioning AV integration as an essential advancement in the digital heritage preservation field.

title: Associations between infant-caregiver joint attention and socioeconomic status: a PRISMA-compliant scoping review
container-title: Frontiers in Psychology
f88843b554f7632c0fb1f9536b9743141e40f237.abstract: Introduction Socioeconomic status (SES) has been associated with variation in caregiver–child interactions and developmental outcomes across multiple domains. Joint attention (JA)–the coordination of attention between infants and caregivers toward shared objects or events–is a foundational process supporting early cognitive, language, and socioemotional development. Methods This scoping review systematically synthesizes evidence on associations between SES and JA behaviors during infancy. Proximal caregiving variables (i.e., caregiver stress and caregiving behaviors) are considered when reported alongside JA within low-SES settings. Following PRISMA-ScR guidelines, 53 articles were identified through systematic searches of Ovid, PsycINFO, and Medline, with 23 peer-reviewed studies meeting inclusion criteria after independent screening. All assessed JA during infancy (≤36 months). Results Across studies ( N = 4,402), findings were mixed but generally indicate that higher SES is associated with more frequent and more coordinated forms of JA, particularly infant-initiated and coordinated engagement. Discussion However, JA was observed across all socioeconomic contexts, including in samples experiencing socioeconomic disadvantage, underscoring the universality of JA and the importance of interpreting SES-related differences within broader environmental and cultural contexts that shape interactional strategies. Differences in SES, JA operationalization, and analytic approaches are discussed. Evidence examining caregiver stress and caregiving behaviors as explanatory mechanisms was limited and inconsistent and did not support strong conclusions regarding buffering or mediating pathways. Instead, caregiver stress and caregiving behaviors are more cautiously interpreted as part of a broader ecological system shaping opportunities for joint engagement. Together, these findings suggest that SES shapes the conditions under which JA unfolds, while JA itself remains a robust and developmentally meaningful process across socioeconomic contexts.

title: Moral sensitivity, moral resilience and compassion fatigue among geriatric services and management interns: the mediating roles of moral courage and professional identity
container-title: Frontiers in Medicine
64f9836267a2399b9dadc4d993c63b2cff13ee5d.abstract: Background Compassion fatigue among geriatric services and management interns affects their career choices within the eldercare sector and exacerbates workforce shortages. While sociopsychological factors have been studied, the ethical dimension—particularly the role of moral sensitivity—remains underexplored. This study investigates the associations of moral sensitivity and moral resilience with compassion fatigue in Chinese geriatric services and management interns, including potential indirect associations through moral courage and professional identity. Methods A quantitative, cross-sectional study was conducted. Using convenience sampling, we recruited 371 geriatric services and management interns from four public junior colleges in Hunan and Guizhou Provinces, China, between November and December 2024. The data collection instruments included the Compassion Fatigue Short Scale, Revised Moral Sensitivity Questionnaire, Moral Courage Scale, Rushton Moral Resilience Scale, and Professional Identity Scale. Statistical analyses were performed using SPSS 22.0 for descriptive and preliminary analyses, and Amos 23.0 for structural equation modeling. Results The modified model demonstrated excellent fit indices ( χ 2 /df = 1.225, AGFI = 0.980, IFI = 0.998, TLI = 0.994, CFI = 0.998, NFI = 0.990, RMSEA = 0.025). Moral sensitivity was directly and positively associated with compassion fatigue ( β = 0.136, p = 0.011). Meanwhile, moral sensitivity showed a significant negative indirect association with compassion fatigue via the sequential pathway of moral courage and professional identity ( β = −0.050, 95% CI [−0.091 to −0.024], p = 0.001). Its total effect was not statistically significant ( β = 0.006, p = 0.891). Additionally, moral resilience had a direct negative association with compassion fatigue ( β = −0.230, p = 0.001), as well as an indirect negative association via professional identity ( β = −0.142, 95% CI [−0.197 to −0.095], p = 0.001). Conclusion Moral sensitivity showed both direct positive and indirect negative associations with compassion fatigue, while the total effect was not statistically significant. Moral resilience showed both direct and indirect negative associations with compassion fatigue. These findings suggest that moral courage, moral resilience, and professional identity warrant further investigation as potential targets for educational support among geriatric services and management interns. Longitudinal and intervention studies are needed to clarify these relationships and evaluate their practical implications.

title: Associations of night-shift sleep and recovery experiences with occupational fatigue among emergency nurses: a multicenter cross-sectional study
container-title: Frontiers in Public Health
af6d291c2fcb177994a70d9c22615dd5fa0bd705.abstract: Background Emergency nurses experience substantial occupational demands, including night work and irregular schedules, which may disrupt sleep and recovery. Occupational fatigue is multidimensional, encompassing chronic fatigue, acute fatigue, and intershift recovery. However, the roles of post-night-shift sleep characteristics and recovery experiences in different fatigue dimensions remain unclear. This study investigated their associations with occupational fatigue among emergency nurses. Methods A multicenter cross-sectional survey was conducted among emergency nurses from several hospitals in Taizhou, Zhejiang Province, China, in late July 2026. Participants completed a self-administered electronic questionnaire assessing demographic and occupational characteristics, night-shift sleep characteristics, recovery experiences, occupational fatigue, and work–family conflict. Recovery experience was measured using the Recovery Experience Questionnaire (REQ), and occupational fatigue was assessed using the Occupational Fatigue Exhaustion/Recovery Scale (OFER-15). Multivariable linear regression models were constructed for chronic fatigue, acute fatigue, and intershift recovery, with adjustment for demographic, occupational, and work–family conflict covariates. Sensitivity analyses were conducted to assess robustness. Results The study included 216 emergency nurses. Higher REQ overall mean scores were associated with lower chronic fatigue ( B = −0.523, 95% CI −0.857 to −0.189), lower acute fatigue ( B = −0.703, 95% CI −0.961 to −0.444), and better intershift recovery ( B = 0.582, 95% CI 0.327 to 0.836). Compared with sleep-onset latency &lt;15 min, latencies of 31–60 min and &gt;60 min were associated with poorer intershift recovery. Fragmented sleep showed a positive but not statistically significant association with acute fatigue in the primary analysis ( B = 0.365, 95% CI −0.022 to 0.751, P = 0.064). Neither average monthly night shifts nor shift-system categories were significantly associated with the three outcomes. Conclusion Higher recovery experience scores were associated with lower fatigue and better intershift recovery among emergency nurses. Sleep-onset latencies of 31–60 min and &gt;60 min were associated with poorer intershift recovery compared with &lt;15 min. No statistically significant associations with monthly night-shift frequency or shift-system categories were detected in the primary models. Future longitudinal studies incorporating objective sleep and circadian measures are warranted.

title: Digital, AI-enabled marketing and the competitiveness of trade services: a sociological perspective on labor transformation, social inclusion and organizational capacity
container-title: Frontiers in Sociology
a521dbe894c1c5d4afb5061a18ed0d3eb8c2b31b.abstract: Research on digital and AI-enabled marketing explains how channels, data, and algorithms create value for firms, while the sociology of digital labor explains how the same technologies reorganize work and access. Neither explains why trade-service firms adopting near-identical tools reach very different competitive outcomes, a question that matters most for small firms in emerging and transition economies. This conceptual Perspective proposes a model of socially mediated competitiveness in which the adoption of digital and AI-enabled marketing, treated as one continuum from basic digital channels to generative-AI content, customer response, and targeting, affects competitiveness through three mechanisms. Labor transformation reallocates marketing tasks between automation and human judgment, strengthening competitiveness where workers can direct AI tools and weakening it where work depends on platform and algorithmic control. Social inclusion, through access, skills, and autonomy of use, decides how many firms and which social groups can contest a digitally mediated market. Organizational capacity, through routines for sensing, seizing, and reconfiguring human-machine practices, decides whether adoption becomes durable advantage. The theoretical novelty is threefold: the model joins mechanisms usually studied apart, treats job quality and inclusion as conditions of competitiveness rather than only its consequences, and adapts concepts built for large firms to small, platform-dependent trade-service firms. It is stated as three propositions with proposed indicators and a multi-wave design for testing them. The article reports no data and claims no empirical validation. It closes with theoretical, sociological, managerial, policy, and research implications.

title: Digital mental health interventions for university students during the COVID-19 pandemic and post-pandemic periods: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
container-title: Frontiers in Public Health
3a0cfac5d1587c379ff30b0d91d8f7e3fc74a1b5.abstract: Background University students experience elevated levels of anxiety, depression, and stress, prompting growing interest in accessible digital psychological interventions. This systematic review and meta-analysis assessed the effectiveness of digital psychological interventions for university students during the later stages of the coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic and the post-pandemic periods. Methods PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science (WoS), and Cochrane were searched for randomized controlled trials involving university students published between 2020 and June 2026. Random-effects models (Hedges’ g, modified Knapp-Hartung [mKH]) were applied, and Risk of Bias was assessed with Risk of Bias 2 (RoB 2). Results A total of 34 trials (6,544 students, 15 countries) were included. Benefits were significant for depression at 8 weeks (g = 0.48), anxiety at 2 and 8 weeks (g = 0.24 and g = 0.57), stress at 4 weeks (g = 0.23), and post-intervention anxiety (g = 0.75; I 2 = 88.6%), but not for pooled anxiety. Overall, 52.9% of studies were at high Risk of Bias, and only one of six active-comparator trials compared digital with face-to-face delivery. Conclusion Digital interventions yield modest short-term benefits, but heterogeneity, high Risk of Bias, and a scarcity of face-to-face comparisons limit confidence. Systematic review registration http://doi.org/10.17605/OSF.IO/E2C78 , identifier (E2C78).

title: EcoLearn: a digital assessment platform for Life Cycle Sustainability Assessment in green office administration learning
container-title: Frontiers in Education
ada8913fb7f442b4a74f7b85b8fb263aa5680b90.abstract: Introduction Digital technologies are increasingly used to support assessment, reflection, and competency development in higher education. However, limited attention has been given to how digital platforms can facilitate Life Cycle Sustainability Assessment (LCSA)-based learning in office administration education. This study explores EcoLearn, a web-based digital assessment platform designed to support LCSA-based sustainability assessment in green industry-oriented office administration learning. Methods An exploratory qualitative case study was conducted using semi-structured interviews with lecturers, group interviews with students, participatory observations, digital activity logs, and learning artifacts generated through the EcoLearn platform. The platform integrates interactive digital modules, LCSA simulations, project-based tasks, data analytics, discussion forums, dashboard-based monitoring, and reflective assessment activities. Results The findings show that EcoLearn helps students connect administrative activities with environmental, social, and economic sustainability indicators, supports lifecycle thinking, and enables lecturers to monitor student progress through digital dashboards. Several implementation challenges were also identified, including students' limited familiarity with LCSA terminology, the need for contextualized indicators, lecturer workload, and uneven digital readiness. Discussion This study contributes to research on digital applications in education by demonstrating how a digital assessment platform can support sustainability-oriented learning, reflective assessment, and data-informed monitoring in office administration education.

title: <b>PERAN PLATFORM <i>E-COMMERCE</i> DAN MUTU PRODUK TERHADAP TINGKAT KEPUASAN KONSUMEN DI LINGKUNGAN BISNIS DIGITAL</b>
container-title: KAJIAN EKONOMI, MANAJEMEN, AKUNTANSI SYARIAH DAN KONVENSIONAL (KEMASAN)
e768eff28cd07a926743fea0a048cceee12b5897.abstract: Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mengeksplorasi penerapan website e-commerce sekaligus mengidentifikasi pengaruh penggunaan platform tersebut dan kualitas produk terhadap kepuasan konsumen dalam konteks perdagangan digital. Pesatnya perkembangan TIK telah mendorong transformasi dalam berbagai aspek kehidupan, salah satunya pada sektor perdagangan dan mekanisme transaksi ekonomi. Transformasi tersebut ditandai dengan semakin luasnya pemanfaatan internet oleh masyarakat Indonesia sebagai sarana untuk melakukan kegiatan jual beli secara daring. Aktivitas perdagangan elektronik kini tidak hanya dimanfaatkan untuk memenuhi kebutuhan pokok, tetapi juga mencakup berbagai kebutuhan penunjang kehidupan. Fenomena ini memperlihatkan bahwa e-commerce telah menjadi salah satu instrumen penting dalam menunjang keberlangsungan kegiatan usaha sekaligus memperluas akses konsumen terhadap beragam produk dan layanan. Untuk memperoleh data yang relevan dilakukan melalui metode survei dan observasi dengan melibatkan responden sebagai sumber data melalui penyebaran kuesioner. Proses tersebut diarahkan untuk memperoleh gambaran mengenai persepsi, pengalaman, serta penilaian konsumen terhadap aktivitas pembelian yang dilakukan melalui website e-commerce. Melalui pendekatan tersebut, penelitian ini diharapkan dapat menjelaskan hubungan antara pemanfaatan website e-commerce, kualitas produk, dan tingkat kepuasan konsumen secara lebih komprehensif. Dari perspektif akademik, hasil kajian ini diharapkan dapat memperkaya pemahaman mengenai pemanfaatan teknologi informasi, khususnya dalam penerapan perdagangan elektronik sebagai bagian dari perkembangan ekosistem bisnis digital. Hasil penelitian diharapkan dapat menjadi landasan pertimbangan bagi pelaku usaha dalam mengevaluasi dan mengoptimalkan kualitas pelayanan digital, menentukan arah kebijakan pengembangan usaha, serta menyusun strategi bisnis yang adaptif dan berorientasi pada kebutuhan konsumen. Upaya tersebut menjadi semakin relevan dalam menghadapi persaingan pasar yang terus berkembang seiring dengan akselerasi transformasi teknologi digital.

title: Mediasi Aktif Berbasis Nilai Islam: Meninjau Kembali Pendampingan Orang Tua dalam Keluarga Muslim di Era Digital
container-title: PERSEPTIF: Jurnal Ilmu Sosial dan Humaniora
bd2f2b2ba2cc00a3091276624454acfcfff8a5cd.abstract: The development of digital media creates both opportunities and challenges for parents guiding children and fostering Islamic values within the family. Digital parenting requires more than restricting device use; it also involves communication, role modeling, and guidance that help children use digital media responsibly. This study aims to identify parental mediation strategies, examine how Islamic values are integrated into digital guidance, and identify conceptual gaps relevant to understanding value-guided active mediation. The study employs a qualitative library research approach using an integrative literature review and critical thematic synthesis. The literature is analyzed through deductive–inductive coding, comparison of findings, and thematic categorization. The findings identify six groups of parental mediation strategies: restricting media use, active guidance and dialogic communication, co-viewing, content selection and information verification, parental digital role modeling, and religious habituation supported by social engagement. The synthesis indicates that integrating Islamic values requires more than providing religious content or imposing restrictions. It involves connecting value orientations with communication practices, parental behavioral consistency, and the management of children’s digital activities. This study proposes a conceptual framework linking these dimensions to support digital guidance in Muslim families. The proposed framework is conceptual and requires further empirical investigation across diverse family contexts.

title: Experimental Evaluation and Reproducible Digital Filter Benchmarking for Hall-Sensor-Based DC Motor Speed Feedback
container-title: Journal of Naval Sciences and Engineering
4d29413957b29ef3f882a8fbd518aef2ee55d7f5.abstract: Hall-effect sensors are widely used for low-cost speed feedback in DC motor drives, yet the measured speed is influenced not only by controller design but also by hardware limitations and signal-processing characteristics. This study investigates the combined influence of these factors through an experimental evaluation of a Hall-sensor-based DC motor drive and an independent benchmark of commonly used digital low-pass filters. Open-loop measurements produced speed estimates of 201–202 rpm. With a 175 rpm reference, proportional control achieved only 124–127 rpm because the voltage available at the motor terminals was reduced by the combined effects of the power supply and the motor driver. Replacing the 6 V source with a 9 V laboratory supply increased the available motor voltage, allowing PI and PID controllers to achieve stable responses of 173–176 rpm and 173–177 rpm, respectively. Independently of the hardware experiments, fourth-order Bessel and Butterworth IIR filters and a 15th-order Hamming-window FIR filter were evaluated using a reproducible synthetic Hall-pulse benchmark at a 100 kHz sampling frequency. The FIR filter provided the lowest constant group delay (75 μs), whereas the IIR filters achieved approximately 57 dB attenuation at 10 kHz with higher frequency-dependent delays. The results show that observed speed-control performance can be strongly affected by hardware voltage constraints, while digital-filter selection requires balancing attenuation, delay, sampling frequency, and application requirements. Separating hardware evaluation from offline filter benchmarking provides a more reliable interpretation of Hall-sensor speed-feedback performance.

title: A hybrid graph attention network and proximal policy optimization framework for adaptive fog-cloud offloading and frameproof-based secure IoT data transmission
container-title: Frontiers in Big Data
159f47f1509d511097a4afb468759c22dd56e477.abstract: Introduction Internet of Things (IoT) applications require secure, low-latency data transmission in resource-constrained environments. Conventional cryptographic security is computationally intensive, and static scheduling adapts poorly to changing IoT-Fog-Cloud conditions. Methods A hybrid Graph Attention Network-Proximal Policy Optimization (GAT-PPO) framework is proposed. The IoT-Fog-Cloud infrastructure is modeled as a dynamic graph, from which GAT learns topology-aware node embeddings. A PPO agent uses these embeddings, together with task urgency, battery level, resource availability and task sensitivity, to select fog or cloud nodes for offloading. For high-sensitivity tasks, a lightweight frameproof combinatorics-based verification mechanism integrated with SHA-256 hashing is activated, and its outcome is incorporated into the PPO reward. The framework was implemented in Python and evaluated in a simulated fog-cloud environment using tasks derived from TON_IoT network traffic, over 10 independent runs. Results The framework achieved an average latency of 68.2 ± 0.7 ms, energy consumption of 31.5 ± 0.4 mJ/task, throughput of 912 ± 9.8 tasks/s, packet delivery ratio of 98.7 ± 0.3% and security success rate of 98.9 ± 0.2%, outperforming the Without GAT, GCN-PPO and GAT-DQN configurations (Welch's t-test, p &lt; 0.001). Under representative attacks, the false acceptance rate ranged from 0.10% to 0.60% and the false rejection rate was 0.20%. Discussion The framework provides an effective approach for adaptive and secure IoT task offloading under the evaluated simulation conditions and shows potential for latency-sensitive IoT applications. Hardware-based validation and broader deployment studies remain future work.

title: Digital labor market pressure and employment anxiety among computer science undergraduates: professional belonging, career adaptability, and employment resilience
container-title: Frontiers in Psychology
cb5f0f917d899fd737ada3432dcff0bf32098bff.abstract: Introduction Digitalized recruitment has introduced new pressures into the school-to-work transition, particularly for computer science undergraduates facing AI substitution concerns, rapidly changing skill requirements, and increasingly visible comparisons of career readiness. This study examined the association between digital labor market pressure (DLMP) and employment anxiety (EA), the mediating roles of professional belonging (PB) and career adaptability (CA), and the moderating role of employment resilience (ER). Methods A cross-sectional questionnaire survey collected 467 valid responses from computer-related majors, including 139 sophomores, 158 juniors, and 170 seniors. The analysis examined direct associations, parallel and chain mediation pathways, the moderating effect of ER, and differences across undergraduate grades. Results DLMP was positively associated with EA and negatively associated with PB and CA. PB was positively associated with CA, while both PB and CA were negatively associated with EA. Bootstrap confidence intervals supported three indirect pathways linking DLMP to EA through PB, CA, and the sequential combination of PB and CA. ER moderated the DLMP-EA association, with a stronger positive association at lower levels of resilience. Seniors reported higher DLMP and EA, while PB was lower among students in higher grades. Discussion The findings highlight the relationship between digitalized labor market pressure and employment anxiety among computer science undergraduates. Professional belonging and career adaptability were associated with lower anxiety and formed distinct indirect pathways, while employment resilience was associated with differences in the strength of the pressure-anxiety relationship. Grade differences further indicate variation in these experiences across undergraduate stages.

title: Validation and digital implementation of the HADES score for hereditary angioedema
container-title: Frontiers in Epidemiology
929041ef2ab964b1ffee344067d700dd3b0e3ba1.abstract: Background Hereditary angioedema due to C1 inhibitor deficiency (HAE-C1-INH) is frequently misdiagnosed, leading to delayed diagnosis and inappropriate management. We previously developed a predictive clinical score (HADES) to support early identification of patients at risk for HAE-C1-INH. Objective To evaluate the temporal performance of HADES in a new cohort of patients with suspected HAE-C1-INH and explore the feasibility of its digital implementation in a small prospective pilot study. Methods A total of 539 individuals with suspicion of HAE-C1-INH were evaluated. HADES scores were calculated using the previously predefined thresholds, and diagnostic performance and ROC analyses were compared with the derivation cohort. In parallel, a prospective pilot study using the HADES App was conducted in 18 patients to assess its implementation feasibility. In addition, 6 patients with HAE-FXII were analyzed separately for exploratory purposes. Results The validation cohort reproduced key performance characteristics of the original model. Sensitivity remained 100% at low thresholds, specificity increased across score categories, and no confirmed HAE-C1-INH cases occurred in score category 0. The AUC was 0.80 (95% CI, 0.73-0.86), matching the derivation dataset. The exploratory HADES-App cohort provided preliminary information on digital implementation feasibility. Patients with HAE- FXII showed score distributions overlapping those of HAE-C1-INH cases. Conclusion In a temporal validation cohort, HADES demonstrated discriminative performance consistent with the original study and reasonable overall category-level calibration, supporting its potential role as a clinical screening tool for HAE-C1-INH. Preliminary digital implementation findings warrant further prospective evaluation.

title: Digital intelligence for depression governance: an environome framework to bridge research and policy
container-title: Frontiers in Artificial Intelligence
d568d17e0712482ebbe5d4a3c02c7504436c414f.abstract: Background Digital intelligence platforms are transforming how policymakers synthesize and translate mental health evidence into actionable strategies. Depression research is vast but highly fragmented, limiting its effective use in policy design. We introduce the Interactive Depression Dashboard (InDepDash), designed to integrate and operationalize multidisciplinary evidence on depression. Methods InDepDash aggregates and analyzes 139,761 depression-related studies (from 2005 to 2025) spanning clinical, social, and environmental domains. The platform maps evidence across multiple determinants of mental health, conceptualized as the “environome,” including personal, social, natural, and built factors. Ontology-based annotation, semantic search, and co-occurrence analysis enable real-time exploration of research trends, gaps, and priorities, while case study applications illustrate its policy relevance. Results The platform identified substantial imbalances in the evidence base. Natural and built environmental determinants represented 14.3% of the analyzed corpus; within this domain, climate-change-specific evidence was comparatively sparse. InDepDash effectively highlights underexplored domains and supports prioritization of interventions, including neuroinclusive policies, disaster resilience strategies, and climate-informed mental health planning. Conclusion Evidence-mapping platforms such as InDepDash provide critical infrastructure for adaptive and evidence-informed governance in mental health. By enhancing the accessibility, transparency, and integration of complex data, they enable policymakers to respond to emerging challenges with greater speed. This study supports the Trustworthiness, Reproducibility, Explainability, Applicability, and Transparency (TREAT) framework as a foundation for ethical AI deployment, addressing key gaps in research translation while working toward global mental health equity.

title: Evaluating the online attention and visibility of research from State Universities in Zimbabwe using altmetrics data
container-title: Frontiers in Research Metrics and Analytics
f0ccc2129aa81595621eaac0f319b317757ad1d2.abstract: Introduction Measuring research impact beyond academia has led to the development of several models that describe and theorize transformations in the way knowledge is produced and used to create impact outside of academia Traditional metrics have been used to measure research impact at the journal and author levels. However, the growth of the internet and social media have influenced research metrics leading to the rise of Altmetrics. Methods In this study, using data from Altmetric.com, the researcher analyses online mentions related to research output from the universities to establish how altmetrics may provide informative indicators of the impact of research outputs from universities in Zimbabwe. The altmetrics data was extracted from Altmetric.com between June and July 2026. The search was limited to the period 2020 to 2025. Results Social Media (51,258), News, Blogs &amp; Podcasts (6,734), Policy, Patents &amp; Guidelines (1,175) had higher mentions compared to Academic Sources (166). Biomedical and Clinical Sciences had the highest total mentions in all the categories, summing up to 29,556, while Psychology had the lowest total mentions in three categories. University of Zimbabwe had the highest total number of mentions of fields of research in online activities (45,606) while Manicaland State University of Applied Sciences had the lowest mentions (14). The correlation between the Total Output Tracked and Total Mentions according to field of research was 0,9 and 0,8 according to university. Many fields had zero mentions on Policy, Patents &amp; Guidelines from most universities. The publication volume, based on the Total Output Tracked from each field of research show an increase from 2020 to 2022 and then a drop from 2023 to 2025. Discussion Altmetrics provide quantitative evidence of online activities related to research output from the universities, indicating social engagement with the work beyond academia and could be used as evidence of the visibility of universities' research output. Altmetric data revealed that research from the universities was visible beyond academia, although some fields had more mentions than others, suggesting that some universities research activities received more attention and visibility online compared to others. Altmetrics do not provide an indication of the quality and significance of research publications, yet they provide quantitative evidence of online activities related to research output from the universities, indicating visibility of the work beyond academia.

title: Affective citizenship: dynamics of emotional responses to digital news content during an election in Ecuador
container-title: Frontiers in Political Science
3a13c5820789e9bcc8e644f5a7752df531a44c32.abstract: Introduction Political participation is not limited to direct involvement in electoral campaigns or political organizations. For many citizens, elections are experienced primarily through exposure to the surrounding information environment. This study examines the affective responses of citizens without direct electoral involvement to political news during the second round of the 2025 Ecuadorian presidential election. Methods Twenty-two participants evaluated two standardized news leads per day across a nine-day observation period, comprising 6 days before and 3 days after the election, yielding 396 observations per affective outcome. Two dimensions of affective response were assessed: perceived emotional impact and pleasantness. Linear mixed-effects models accounted for repeated observations within participants and variability between news stimuli. Results In the primary analysis of 22 participants who completed the full protocol (396 observations), perceived emotional impact was significantly higher in the post-election than in the pre-election phase. This association was no longer statistically significant in a sensitivity analysis including 85 participants —comprising the 22 completers and 63 participants with partial data— and 989 observations. An exploratory temporal analysis found no systematic linear trajectory in emotional impact across the observation period. Pleasantness did not differ significantly between electoral phases. In an exploratory stimulus-level analysis, positive-toned news leads received significantly lower pleasantness ratings than negative-toned leads, whereas neutral-toned leads did not differ significantly from negative-toned leads. Discussion Taken together, these findings contribute to understanding how citizens without direct electoral involvement may respond to political news during an electoral process. They highlight the importance of distinguishing perceived emotional impact from pleasantness and suggest that immediate affective responses may be associated both with an electoral phase and with characteristics of individual news stimuli. Although these findings remain exploratory and are bounded by the observational design and the limited number of stimuli, they provide a basis for further research on the affective dimensions of citizens’ exposure to electoral information.

title: Do Digital Infrastructure REITs Behave Like Real Estate or Technology Stocks? Evidence from Tower and Data Center REITs
fe13442147cd543618a0d192ec9037dec28a2c39.abstract: Abstract This study examines whether telecommunications tower and data center Real Estate Investment Trusts (REITs) behave more like traditional real estate or technology stocks, using monthly and daily returns for five U.S.-listed digital infrastructure REITs from 2005 to 2024. The methodology combines multi-factor asset pricing models with volatility connectedness analysis. Results show that: (i) data center REITs exhibit higher average returns and volatility than tower REITs; (ii) the difference in market betas between tower and data center REITs is smaller than monthly estimates suggest; (iii) all digital infrastructure REITs have negative HML loadings, distinguishing them from traditional real estate assets; and (iv) connectedness analysis of CAPM residuals yields a lower total connectedness index and different directional and dynamic structures than raw returns alone. Overall, tower REITs align more closely with infrastructure assets, data center REITs with technology equities, and Digital Realty Trust shows the strongest real estate alignment within its segment. JEL classification: G11, G12, L86, R33

title: Effectiveness of digital health interventions for asthma management: an umbrella review protocol
container-title: JBI Evidence Synthesis
bbba17b4cde7c01e9e5de60fbb9e0de84e8b752d.abstract: Objective: The objective of this review will be to comprehensively synthesize evidence from systematic reviews examining the effectiveness of digital health interventions (DHIs) compared with usual care or non-digital interventions for improving clinical health outcomes in patients with asthma of all ages. Introduction: Asthma affects 262 million people worldwide, with a substantial morbidity, mortality, and economic burden. Despite effective treatments, control remains suboptimal due to poor medication adherence and barriers to traditional face-to-face care. DHIs offer various solutions; however, heterogeneous findings across systematic reviews necessitate synthesis to clarify the most effective interventions. Eligibility criteria: Patients of any age diagnosed with asthma will be included. Eligible interventions will be consumer-focused DHIs (including smartphone applications, telehealth, electronic monitoring devices, web-based platforms, messaging services, and smart inhalers) compared with usual care, non-digital interventions, or other digital modalities. The primary outcome will be asthma control; secondary outcomes will be quality of life, medication adherence and health care utilization. Factors influencing engagement and adverse events will be reported. There will be no language restrictions. Methods: This review will follow the JBI methodology for umbrella reviews. Systematic searches will be conducted in MEDLINE (Ovid), Embase (Ovid), Cochrane Library, Epistemonikos, CINAHL Ultimate (EBSCOhost), and JBI Best Practice (Ovid), with PEDro as a supplementary source. Two reviewers will independently conduct study selection, critical appraisal, and data extraction using standardized JBI forms. The findings will be narratively synthesized with tabular summaries, as well as a citation matrix analysis for overlap assessment and visual representations. Certainty of evidence will be rated using GRADE. Systematic review registration number: CRD420251247228 (PROSPERO)

title: Digital storytelling as a tool for social communication in the process of learning English language and literature
container-title: Interpersona An International Journal on Personal Relationships
ebdcf13788598bac2ea192ae721dea22d3b327bd.abstract: The aim of the study was to identify and theoretically substantiate the socio-communicative potential of digital storytelling in the process of learning English language and literature, taking into account the linguistic, collaborative, multimodal and narrative mechanisms of its pedagogical application. The study was carried out in the format of a structured literature review with a qualitative thematic synthesis. The search for scientific publications was carried out in March–May 2026 in international bibliographic databases with additional verification of bibliographic data and digital identifiers of publications. From 286 initially identified records, after removing duplicates, screening of titles and annotations and full-text evaluation, a corpus of 25 peer-reviewed works from 2022–2026 was formed. Thematic coding revealed that 72.0% of the publications covered language production, 68.0% – socio-communicative interaction, 64.0% – multimodal and narrative mediation, while only 16.0% directly integrated literary material. It was determined that the socio-communicative potential of digital stories is formed through interconnected language production, narrative structuring of content, collective agreement of meanings, multimodal recoding and audience orientation of the message. It was found that the linguistic and collaborative aspects have a much broader evidence base than the use of digital stories for the joint interpretation of a literary text. The revealed asymmetry indicates the insufficient integration of linguistic, social and literary directions in modern research. It is practical to organize the creation of digital stories as a structured collaborative activity that combines content interpretation, scenario planning, multimodal construction, and presentation of the result to the audience. Further research should empirically test such a model when working with English-language fiction texts.

title: Digital Health Literacy and Healthcare  Access Among Rural and Underserved Communities in India
container-title: International Journal of Innovative Science and Research Technology
099065c0536a9aaabb3e0b57c4166548c64b0a7b.abstract: Digital health has become an important component of healthcare delivery in India, particularly for extending services to rural and underserved populations. However, the availability of digital health platforms does not automatically guarantee equitable access. Digital health literacy, internet connectivity, affordability, language, disability, privacy concerns, social support and confidence in using technology influence whether individuals can effectively benefit from digital healthcare services. This review examines the relationship between digital health literacy and healthcare access among rural and underserved communities in India and discusses the potential contribution of community health nursing. Published literature and major policy and programme documents concerning digital health, telemedicine, digital health literacy, rural healthcare access and community based digital services were reviewed. The evidence indicates that digital technologies can reduce geographical barriers, facilitate remote consultations, support continuity of care and improve access to health information. However, persistent digital inequalities, limited awareness, inadequate infrastructure, low digital literacy and concerns regarding privacy and trust may restrict equitable utilization. Indian initiatives such as the Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission and eSanjeevani demonstrate the potential of digital platforms to strengthen primary healthcare and connect underserved populations with health professionals. Community health nurses and other frontline health workers can act as important intermediaries by providing digital health education, assisting patients with digital services, promoting safe use of online health information and supporting continuity between digital and face to face care. Digital health equity therefore requires an integrated approach combining infrastructure, digital literacy, accessible technology, community participation, health workforce training, privacy protection and responsive public policy.

title: A Hybrid Deep Learning Framework with Attention Mechanism for Robust and Explainable Plant Disease Classification
container-title: Agricultural Science Digest - A Research Journal
c44023f19f811f694a05ea185f7f760e8b176de8.abstract: Background: For agricultural productivity, Plant Diseases are a significant problem all over the world and which requires development of robust, accurate and scalable automated diagnostic systems. The most recent deep learning methods have been promising, but most current methods lack generalization since they were trained based on single-domain datasets and are not interpretable. Methods: A hybrid deep learning architecture is proposed that integrates convolutional neural networks, attention models and feature refinement with transformers to improve classification and localization of plant disease. Result: The proposed framework achieves 99.08% and 98.88% for validation and test accuracy, respectively, surpassing traditional baseline models, such as CNN, MobileNetV3, EfficientNet-B0 and ResNet18.

title: Developing a LiDAR-Based Geospatial Digital Twin Framework for Sustainable Tourism Planning in Mountain Ski Resorts: The Davraz Ski Resort Case
303680d0fa6e5822b9a52c4987e45a95b84d32dd.abstract: Abstract Sustainable planning of mountain ski resorts requires high-resolution terrain information and an explicit account of visitor-oriented landscape accessibility. This study develops and evaluates an update-ready LiDAR-based geospatial Digital Twin prototype for the Davraz Ski Resort (Türkiye). The term prototype is used deliberately: the empirical implementation represents a single survey epoch and a reproducible analytical workflow, rather than a continuously synchronized or bidirectionally coupled operational Digital Twin. UAV-LiDAR data were acquired on 17 June 2025 with a DJI Matrice 350 RTK platform and Zenmuse L2 sensor at 100 m above ground level over 681.013 ha. LiDAR-derived terrain layers (elevation, slope, aspect, mean curvature, and Terrain Ruggedness Index) were reclassified to ordinal suitability scores and integrated by weighted linear combination to produce the Ski Slope Suitability Index (SSI; weights 0.40,0.25,0.15,0.10, and 0.10, respectively). A cumulative viewshed derived from the Digital Surface Model provided the visibility-frequency proxy termed the Visual Landscape Quality Index (VLQI) and the baseline Sustainable Tourism Planning Index (STPI) was calculated as 0.60 × SSI + 0.40 × VLQI. The SSI identified 43.33% of the area as highly or very highly suitable; 8.43% had high or very high visual exposure; and 34.17% had high or very high STPI values. Descriptive spatial validation against 14 existing pistes showed that 13 pistes (92.9%) had mean SSI values in the Moderate or High classes. This correspondence supports planning relevance but is not independent predictive validation. Because independent elevation checkpoints, visitor-perception data and multi-temporal or real-time inputs were unavailable in the submitted dataset, the outputs should be interpreted as screening-level evidence. The principal contribution is therefore a transparent geospatial data-flow, index-integration, and update logic that can form the static baseline of a future operational Digital Twin.

title: Between Affordance and Anxiety: How Part-Time Honours Students Navigate Artificial Intelligence Tools in South African Postgraduate Education
container-title: Journal of Learning and Teaching in Digital Age
5a239ad5085fb535ef88287d48d65815a2f21a12.abstract: The rapid proliferation of artificial intelligence (AI) tools in higher education has generated significant scholarly debate about their pedagogical implications, ethical dimensions, and impact on student learning. This qualitative case study explores the experiences of twelve part-time honours students at a South African university as they navigate AI tools in the context of their postgraduate academic work. Participants were practising teachers enrolled in honours programmes across multiple education disciplines, including curriculum studies, science education, leadership and management, inclusive education, and education studies. Data were generated through semi-structured interviews and focus group discussions. Findings reveal that students engage with AI tools primarily for research support, academic writing, and knowledge construction, yet grapple with concerns related to academic integrity, over-reliance, and the adequacy of AI-generated content. Students also highlighted the tension between the affordances of AI and the critical thinking demands of postgraduate scholarship. The study calls for institutional frameworks that promote responsible and critically informed AI use within blended learning contexts in South African higher education.

title: Efficient banknote denomination recognition using a lightweight CNN with enhanced channel attention
container-title: PeerJ Computer Science
1c65b0ecc9cf5ceea0db0348b2c7bcbe1282f04c.abstract: Automatic banknote recognition systems play a significant role in financial automation processing and assistive applications for visually impaired individuals. To address the challenges in fine-grained Renminbi (RMB) image recognition, including subtle inter-class differences, high local texture similarity, and the limited representation capability of lightweight models, this study proposes a lightweight convolutional neural network based on the Max-Avg Fusion Channel Attention (MAFCA) mechanism. By integrating global average pooling and global max pooling information, MAFCA enhances channel feature modeling and improves the network’s capability to capture discriminative fine-grained features. Based on this design, the proposed module is embedded into a lightweight convolutional architecture and evaluated on a dataset containing ten categories of RMB images. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed model achieves stable performance improvements under five-fold cross-validation and outperforms both the baseline model and the Squeeze-and-Excitation (SE) attention-based model. Furthermore, the proposed approach effectively enhances classification performance while maintaining low computational overhead, thereby validating the effectiveness and robustness of MAFCA in fine-grained image recognition tasks.

title: Here, there, and everywhere: how spatial context and narrative framing shape experiences during the deconstruction of Nazi administrative documents
container-title: International Journal of Digital Humanities
160aace98161e7b40b1932d265a23e18e2aeb282.abstract: Abstract Educational and commemorative practices at memorial sites related to the Nazi era face evolving challenges, as fewer and fewer visitors have direct biographical or family connections to that period. At the same time, the digitization of archives and exhibitions offers new opportunities to engage younger generations. This study examines how spatial context (memorial site, laboratory, or online) and Narrative Framing (Victims' vs. Perpetrators' Perspective) influence visitors’ affective, motivational and cognitive experience during the digital deconstruction of Nazi administrative documents. Using an interactive touchscreen application featuring documents from the "Special Treatment 14f13" killing operation, N=409 participants were evaluated across settings. Results indicated that Spatial Context consistently influenced historical reception. Remote online participants exhibited significantly higher scores in several constructs of Historical Engagement as well as higher situational interest. Only for one Item of situational interest (desire to discuss the content with others) did participants express higher scores at the physical memorial site than online. Regarding specific emotions, a significant interaction effect showed that priming participants with the perspective of a perpetrator reduced feelings of shame both at the physical memorial site and in the laboratory, while emotional reactions in the online environment remained consistent across all perspectives. These results suggest that digital learning environments do not impair historical reception but rather reshape it. The findings should encourage memorial sites to make use of the online space — not as a substitute for a visit, but as an enriching complement.

title: The <b>Effects of Digital HRM Practices, Digital Trust, and Adaptive Leadership on Employee Digital Innovation Behavior in the Banking and Financial Sector</b>
container-title: Lead Journal of Economy and Administration
281ef2f0c5a4a014a2c18289870f6602fe3cac18.abstract: The aim of this research is to investigate the effect of Digital HRM Practices, Digital Trust and Adaptive Leadership on Employee Digital Innovation Behavior in banking and financial industry in Indonesia. The study applied quantitative method using survey technique on the workers of banking organizations and financial institutions that have used digital technology in their operational operations and human resource management procedures. A purposive sample approach was used and the criteria for respondents were current employees, with a minimum of one (1) year work experience, digital platforms used in work activities and having digital-based human resource management procedures. The data collection was conducted through an online questionnaire sent through Google form. The data analysis used is multiple linear regression. The results show that Digital HRM Practices, Digital Trust and Adaptive Leadership have a positive and significant effect on Employee Digital Innovation Behavior. The findings show the important factors for enhancing employees’ digital creative behavior are the application of digital-based human resource management techniques, the belief in security and dependability of technology, and the role of adaptive leadership. The study offers practical implications for companies to improve digital HRM practices, enhance security and transparency of digital systems and develop an adaptive leadership style that encourages empowerment, collaboration and continuous learning to improve Employee Digital Innovation Behavior.

title: Hardware is not enough: unpacking the configurational synergy of person-environment fit in graduate digital literacy
0c054e22211334c35df5b0497170174ab9b9bab0.abstract: Abstract This study examines how digital literacy among graduate students in the social sciences emerges from different configurations of environmental conditions and individual motivation. Drawing on person–environment fit (PEF) theory, it uses a sequential mixed-methods design combining the Delphi method, entropy weighting, necessary condition analysis (NCA), and fuzzy-set qualitative comparative analysis (fsQCA) to analyze survey data from 640 graduate students across 30 provinces in China. The results show that interest drive and household digital support attitude are necessary but not sufficient conditions for high digital literacy. The fsQCA findings further reveal three distinct pathways to high digital literacy: an interest–curriculum synergy path, an independent-practice-dominant path, and a self-growth–practice synergy path. In contrast, low independent practice drive and low curriculum adaptability emerge as key constraints associated with non-high digital literacy. These findings suggest that digital literacy development cannot be explained by resource provision alone, but depends on the configurational alignment of technological resources, curriculum support, and learner motivation.

title: The Digital Companion in the Dorm Room: Emerging Role of AI Companions in Student Well-Being and Primary Care
10d2fe3aa4e9404472b3dffcedf2b95f3ecd04fa.abstract: Background: Artificial intelligence (AI) companions are increasingly used by post-secondary students for emotional support, stress management, and self-management, yet their potential implications for primary care in this population remain unclear. Students may engage with AI companions before encountering purpose-built therapeutic chatbots, which are more often accessed through intentional health-seeking or professional guidance. This distinction may position AI companions as an earlier influence on self-management and subsequent help-seeking. Objective: To examine how artificial intelligence (AI) companions may influence stress regulation, sleep quality, symptom interpretation, and healthcare-seeking behaviour among post-secondary students, and to identify the principal benefits, risks, and unresolved questions relevant to primary care. Methods: A conceptual narrative review was undertaken using literature identified through Harvard University’s Hollis Library and Google Scholar. Evidence related to AI companions, academic stress, sleep quality, emotional support, healthcare-seeking behaviour, primary care, and digital mental health was synthesized using Stress & Coping Theory and the stress-buffering hypothesis as theoretical foundations. Results: AI companions may support stress appraisal, cognitive reframing, emotional reflection, symptom articulation, and self-management before clinical encounters. However, they may also contribute to emotional overreliance, misinformation, reassurance seeking, sleep disruption, and altered help-seeking behaviour. This review proposes conceptual mechanisms linking AI companion engagement with stress regulation, sleep, and pathways into primary care while identifying relational intensity as a clinically meaningful dimension of engagement beyond frequency alone. Conclusion: AI companions should be understood as adjunctive rather than substitutive support. Their clinical relevance is based on how they can shape patients’ experiences before obtaining primary care. Longitudinal research is needed to determine how patterns of engagement influence stress, sleep, and healthcare utilization over time.

title: The Discursive Effects of Disinformation Regarding the Pinochet Dictatorship in the Digital Environment
47a09db6de8bcd07fd3e05b0c6b4c712ba02161d.abstract: This article analyzes discursive representations of the Chilean civil-military dictatorship (1973–1990) that circulated on social media platform X (formerly Twitter) between 2020 and 2023, focusing on discourses related to the Augusto Pinochet regime and the dissemination of fake news, disinformation, and historical revisionism in the contemporary Chilean context. The research is grounded in the dialogue between Digital Discourse Analysis—particularly the technodiscursive strategies proposed by Marie-Anne Paveau—and Dialogic Discourse Analysis, based on the contributions of Bakhtin’s Circle. The corpus includes posts from the profiles of Chilean public figures and anonymous users. In this article, two examples from each category are analyzed qualitatively, seeking to understand the discursive strategies employed and the social voices that permeate these utterances. The results show that the analyzed posts reframe historical events, producing effects of meaning that downplay human rights violations and strain collective memories. We identify denialist and revisionist discourses linked to digital disinformation, which challenge the legitimacy of historical narratives regarding the Pinochet era. We conclude that the circulation of these discourses on digital social media intensifies disputes over memory, contributes to the destabilization of democratic consensus, and undermines the credibility of historical accounts and democratic institutions.

title: Open Government Data and Firm Productivity: How Digital Capability Gaps Shape the Distribution of Productivity Gains in China
8766a52eb7c8a7cafe0a72872aa83529c9e6aed1.abstract: Open government data (OGD) lowers the cost of accessing public-sector data, but firms differ widely in their capacity to turn such access into productivity gains. This study examines how the firm-level digital capability gap—the distance between a firm's digital transformation level and the industry–year digitalization frontier—shapes the productivity effects of OGD. We develop a production model in which the effective cost of data depends on digital capabilities and test its predictions with a staggered difference-in-differences design that exploits the rollout of city-level open data platforms, using 31,238 firm-year observations of Chinese A-share listed firms from 2011 to 2024. OGD significantly raises firm total factor productivity (TFP), but the gains shrink as the digital capability gap widens: the estimated gain for a firm one standard deviation above the mean gap is less than one-fifth of that for a firm one standard deviation below it. Mechanism analyses suggest that the gap weakens the effects of OGD on transaction costs, technological innovation, and the information environment. These results imply that the economic returns to OGD depend on firms' complementary digital capabilities, highlighting the importance of combining open-data provision with capability-building policies to support more broadly shared productivity gains.

title: Carbon Footprint Tools as Digital Enablers of Circular Economy Adoption in Danish SMEs Using Additive Manufacturing
container-title: Journal of Circular Economy
880c94e009801b7570a7bc65a4e0e1c61df27b57.abstract: Small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) face increasing pressure to adopt circular and sustainable practices driven by regulation, customer expectations, and supply-chain demands. This study examines how digital carbon footprint tools can support circular decision-making in SMEs and what organizational and ecosystem conditions shape adoption. Such tools convert product and manufacturing data into CO2e estimates for comparing alternatives during product development, rather than providing full life-cycle assessment or corporate reporting. Based on six semi-structured interviews across four Danish SMEs and one German reference organization, the analysis combined inductive coding and affinity clustering with business and implementation frameworks. The study uses Additive Manufacturing as its empirical context, later expanding findings to other CE-enabling manufacturing technologies. Findings identify four workflow points for tool implementation: requirements and early design, prototyping and validation, pre-production estimation, and post-production optimization. Data gaps, resource constraints, workflow fit, and uncertain business value limit sustained use. Therefore, while such tools may provide strategic value to organizations, they also impose an operational burden.

title: Designing AI-Agents with Personalities: A Psychometric Approach
ae67dae61c1d5baabd320d982987df901ef9df36.abstract: We introduce a methodology for assigning quantifiable and psychometrically validated personalities to AI-Agents using the Big Five framework. Across three studies, we evaluate its feasibility and limitations. In Study 1, we show that large language models (LLMs) capture semantic similarities among Big Five measures, providing a basis for personality assignment. In Study 2, we create AI-Agents using prompts designed based on the Big Five Inventory-2 (BFI-2) in different format, and find that AI-Agents powered by new models align more closely with human responses on the Mini-Markers test, although the finer pattern of results (e.g., factor loading patterns) were sometimes inconsistent. In Study 3, we validate our AI-Agents on risk-taking and moral dilemma vignettes, finding that models prompted with the BFI-2-Expanded format most closely reproduce human personality-decision associations, while safety-aligned models generally inflate ‘moral’ ratings. Overall, our results show that AI-Agents align with humans in correlations between input Big Five traits and output responses and may serve as useful tools for preliminary research. Nevertheless, discrepancies in finer response patterns indicate that AI-Agents cannot (yet) fully substitute for human participants in precision or high-stakes projects.

title: Financial Management Practices of Micro and Small Business in Laoag City
container-title: COBE Business Review
41d8d38f966ff4fb576094c816a6b1479276ab9b.abstract: This study determined the financial management practices of micro and small businesses in Laoag City in terms of financial planning, financing decision, working capital management, and capital budgeting. It also tested whether practices differ significantly between micro and small businesses and proposed strategic recommendations. A descriptive quantitative design was used, with business owners selected through convenience sampling. Data were gathered using a survey questionnaire patterned after Parilla (2013) and analyzed using frequency, percentage, weighted mean, and a t-test. Most of the businesses were small enterprises (90.9%), and most were sole proprietorships (85.6%) that had operated for one to three years (68.2%). Micro businesses highly practiced financial management overall (mean = 3.26), but only moderately practiced financing decision (3.12) and capital budgeting (3.14). Small businesses highly practiced all four areas (overall mean = 3.51). The difference between the two groups was significant (t = -3.56, p = .001), which the authors attribute to small businesses’ greater manpower, assets, and income. The study recommends financial literacy training and orientation for owners, and the adoption of sound, computer-aided accounting practices.

title: LLM4NL2BQS: using generative AI to transform natural language in BQS
container-title: Artificial Intelligence for Security and Defence Applications IV
e922e9c9fbadc8f0c31019b8bb50fbc66f3018cb.abstract: Complex query languages such as Boolean Query Syntax (BQS) are powerful tools for information retrieval within NATO’s Coalition Shared Data network. Their effective use generally requires substantial technical and domain specific expertise, restricting high quality query formulation to a limited number of specialised analysts and creating bottlenecks in information gathering and decision making. In this paper, we investigate three complementary approaches to translating natural language information needs into syntactically correct and semantically appropriate BQS queries. These are fine-tuning a small, open source language model, few-shot prompting and Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) using schema context drawn from the Allied Engineering Documentation Publication AEDP-17 specification of the Standardization Agreement(STANAG) 4559. Training data for fine-tuning is synthesised directly from the specification and validated both grammatically and against a live Coalition Shared Data (CSD)-Server. All three approaches are evaluated on a separate benchmark stratified by difficulty under three cumulative prompting conditions and compared against several general purpose language models, including commercial ones. The fine-tuned model achieves statistically significantly higher semantic accuracy than every comparison model at baseline prompting and higher syntactic and execution accuracy at every prompting condition, with the advantage widest on the most structurally complex queries. Fine-tuning already captures most of this benefit before any few-shot examples or RAG are added, while the commercial models depend far more on prompting strategy to reach their best results. This indicates that for a narrow query language tied to a specific schema, targeted fine-tuning of a small model is a more effective and more robust strategy than relying on few-shot prompting or RAG of a larger general purpose model, while lowering the barrier to entry for users without specialised expertise and reducing organisational reliance on highly specialised staff.

title: Effect of In-line Clinical Decision Support to Improve Accuracy of American Society of Anesthesiologists Physical Status Documentation: A Two-center Evaluation of a Quality Intervention
container-title: Anesthesiology
b2531d06c4f9952965b84689abe39a5a4ab2c37a.abstract: Background: American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA; Schaumburg, Illinois) Physical Status (PS) classification is a widely used ordinal scale that captures comorbidity burden but has significant interrater variability. Previous efforts to enhance ASA PS documentation with clinical decision support are limited by inaccurate problem lists, poor user experience, or consideration of select comorbidities. The authors developed and implemented clinical decision support which uses the anesthesia clinicians’ documentation to highlight potential underclassification at time of ASA PS assignment. Methods: Building upon examples from the ASA Committee on Economics and institutional consensus, the authors identified 51 conditions warranting an ASA PS of at least III. This was embedded in clinical decision support and implemented at the authors’ large academic medical center (site 1). The authors compared the percentage of patients assigned an ASA PS III or greater before (May 22, 2023, to May 22, 2024) and after complete implementation (August 14, 2024, to August 14, 2025). A second large midwestern academic medical center served as a contemporaneous external control (site 2). Using a difference in difference analysis, the authors constructed odds ratios for assignment of ASA PS III in all patients and selected subpopulations. Results: The study included 251,944 anesthetics from site 1 and 286,172 from site 2. Baseline characteristics were similar between sites. At site 1, the proportion of patients classified as ASA PS III or higher increased from 52.9 to 61.7% (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 1.42; 95% CI, 1.38 to 1.45). Site 2 experienced a small absolute increase from 47.2 to 48.4% (aOR, 1.05; 95% CI, 1.03 to 1.07). Among patients at site 1 with 50 conditions addressed by the latter phase of the clinical decision support, the proportion classified as ASA PS III or greater increased from 83.6 to 94.0% (aOR, 3.54; 95% CI, 3.34 to 3.76). Conclusions: Implementation of the authors’ in-line real-time clinical decision support was associated with a significant increase in the percentage of patients with ASA PS III or greater.

title: Online Demand Fulfillment in Highly Asymmetric Markets
container-title: Manufacturing & Service Operations Management
2e23c0c959d3af89ff6ca7225a1bc6be75aeeff1.abstract: Problem definition: We study online demand fulfillment with limited flexibility in highly asymmetric markets, where some locations represented by the set [Formula: see text] have moderate to high market shares, whereas others have very low shares. Xu et al. was the first to establish that a positive generalized chaining gap (GCG) is a necessary and sufficient condition for bounded performance, which is defined as the expected lost sales as the total market size grows. Although a high GCG signals a better performance, the presence of high market asymmetry results in a low GCG and a larger performance bound, making the bound less useful for assessing actual system performance. Therefore, understanding system performance in highly asymmetric markets remains an important question. Methodology/results: We introduce a network condition called [Formula: see text]-connectivity, which ensures that after removing the markets with very low shares, the markets in [Formula: see text] are still connected through the available suppliers. We prove that [Formula: see text]-connectivity is both necessary and sufficient for maintaining bounded performance in highly asymmetric markets. This is achieved through a carefully designed online fulfillment policy that utilizes network partitioning and advanced analyses of mean-reverting processes using probability methods in an asymptotic context. Additionally, we offer strategies for network design to reduce the risk of [Formula: see text]-disconnectivity. Managerial implications: Our findings indicate that even the well-known long-chain structure may not ensure bounded performance in highly asymmetric markets, especially when low-demand markets are dispersed throughout the network. Instead, a “hub-and-spoke” network configuration with a shorter embedded long chain can help reduce the risk of [Formula: see text]-disconnectivity and enhance system performance. Funding: This research was supported in part by the National Natural Science Foundation of China [Grants 72671048 and 72192805] and the Hong Kong Research Grants Council [Grants 16200617, 16200821, 16200019, and 16500225]. Supplemental Material: The online appendix is available at https://doi.org/10.1287/msom.2024.1002 .

title: Information barriers in digital administrative interfaces: a process-oriented framework for administrative burden
container-title: Perspectives on Public Management and Governance
f13c881e32b41e48d0cd00477ccb110d842b5720.abstract: Abstract Research on administrative burden has demonstrated that policy design shapes individuals’ ability to access rights and public services. However, the role of information in producing and transforming administrative burden remains insufficiently conceptualized. This article proposes a process-oriented framework that positions information barriers as a key mechanism through which administrative burden emerges. The framework conceptualizes administrative encounters as an informational trajectory composed of four stages: information search, comprehension, application, and continuous learning, and demonstrates how barriers at each stage generate distinct combinations of learning, compliance, and psychological costs. It further develops a structured framework that links types of information barriers to concrete, evidence-based intervention strategies drawn from information science, including plain language, content structuring, interface design, and mediation mechanisms. By highlighting the dynamic role of information in increasingly digital governance, the article shows how digital service provision can both reduce and intensify administrative burden by reshaping access to information and redistributing responsibilities between citizens and bureaucratic institutions.

title: Legal Regulation of Risk Management in the Use of Big Data
container-title: The Legal World
45e0dfa6b80f919c5b42a40be9b03837935720e8.abstract: The article is devoted to the legal regulation of risk management in the use of big data in the context of the emerging data economy. The authors show that the value of big data is realized primarily through its secondary use, which contradicts the classical principles of information processing; therefore, the focus of regulation should shift from data collection to managing the risks associated with its use. A comparative legal analysis was carried out of the models of legal regulation of risk management in the field of big data that exist in global practice. Based on judicial practice materials, problems have been identified regarding the uncertainty of the legal title to data arrays, the ineffectiveness of extraterritorial coercion, the lack of criteria for balancing private and public interests, the fictitious nature of consent, and the risks of re‑identification. Proposals have been formulated for the regulatory consolidation of the legal regime for large user data, mandatory assessment of the impact of high‑risk processing, dynamic consent, anonymization standards, and trusted intermediaries.
