title: Determinants of Cayenne Pepper Production, Farm Income, and Extension Service Effectiveness in Mimika Regency
container-title: Journal of Economics, Management, Entrepreneurship, and Business (JEMEB)
c8bff63911cbe057a4988d3cb5c688b545632617.abstract: Purpose: This study analyzes production factors, farmer income, and the effect of agricultural extension services on cayenne pepper cultivation in Muare Village, Mimika Regency, where local production potential remains constrained by dependence on external supplies. Research Methodology: A census method was applied to 48 cayenne pepper farmers in Muare Village. Three analytical approaches were used, including Cobb–Douglas production function with robust standard errors, farm income analysis (TR−TC), and simple linear regression to assess agricultural extension effects on farmer interest. Classical assumption tests included normality and multicollinearity assessments. Results: The Cobb–Douglas model was significant (F=20.11; p=0.000; R²=0.6569). Seeds (β=1.1927; p=0.037) and capital (β=2.0968; p=0.004) positively affected production, while fertilizer showed a negative significant effect (β=−0.8136; p=0.025). Other production factors were insignificant. The Return to Scale value of 3.50 indicated increasing returns. Farmers achieved average revenue of IDR 103 million, costs of IDR 41.1 million, and net income of IDR 63.5 million per season. Agricultural extension services significantly influenced farmer interest (β=1.0191; p=0.000; R²=0.8233). Conclusions: Cayenne pepper farming is economically viable and can be expanded through optimized input management and strengthened extension services. Seeds, capital, and extension programs are key drivers of productivity and farmer participation. Limitations: The study was limited to one village, used cross-sectional data, and did not examine marketing and post-harvest aspects. Contributions: This study provides integrated evidence from Cobb–Douglas analysis, income assessment, and extension evaluation to support horticultural development policies in Mimika Regency.

title: AI Driven Talent Management and the Performance of Agri Based Enterprises in Central Region Cameroon
container-title: Journal of Economics, Management, Entrepreneurship, and Business (JEMEB)
9a45a01f3f197d9b0c87ceca92e874eb272d0293.abstract: Purpose: This study examines the relationship between artificial intelligence (AI) driven talent management practices and the performance of agri based enterprises in the Central Region of Cameroon, focusing on the mediating roles of workforce productivity and employee resilience. Research Methodology: A quantitative cross sectional survey design was employed, targeting 250 managers and human resource professionals. Data were collected with a structured questionnaire and analyzed with SPSS and AMOS through descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation, and mediation analysis with 5.000 bootstrap resamples. Results: AI driven talent management was positively and significantly related to enterprise performance (r=0.523, p<0.01). Workforce productivity (β=0.18) and employee resilience (β=0.14) significantly mediated this relationship. Both the total indirect effect (β=0.32, p<0.01) and the direct effect (β=0.29, p<0.01) were significant, indicating partial mediation, with about 52 percent of the total effect transmitted through the two mediators. Conclusions: AI driven talent management enhances the performance of agri based enterprises both directly and indirectly through improved workforce productivity and stronger employee resilience. Enterprises should integrate AI strategically into talent management and support employees through change management. Limitations: The cross sectional design, self reported data, purposive sampling, and focus on a single region limit causal inference and generalizability. Contributions: The study provides empirical evidence from an underresearched African agricultural context and clarifies the mechanisms through which AI driven talent management translates into enterprise performance.

title: Green Marketing and Purchase Decision of Sustainable Housing: Testing the Mediating Role of Perceived Value
container-title: Journal of Economics, Management, Entrepreneurship, and Business (JEMEB)
1d28846b5aa4fefd08884c1d00fb12eec278b58c.abstract: Purpose: This study examines whether green marketing influences sustainable housing purchase decisions and investigates the mediating role of perceived value in explaining this relationship. The study focuses on Grand City Pasuruan, a sustainable housing development in East Java, Indonesia. Research Methodology: A quantitative cross-sectional survey was conducted involving 120 owners and prospective buyers selected through purposive sampling. Data were analyzed using variance-based structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) with SmartPLS 4.0. The measurement model was assessed through reliability, convergent validity, and discriminant validity tests, while hypothesis testing was performed using 5.000-subsample bootstrapping. Results: The findings reveal that green marketing does not significantly influence purchase decisions (β=0.123; p=0.228) or perceived value (β=0.385; p=0.072). Furthermore, perceived value does not significantly mediate the relationship between green marketing and purchase decisions (p=0.092). However, perceived value has a significant positive effect on purchase decisions (β=0.400; p<0.001). Conclusions: Green marketing alone is insufficient to drive sustainable housing purchases in secondary-city markets. Consumers require credible environmental information and tangible value perceptions before making purchasing decisions. Limitations: This study is limited to one housing project, one geographical setting, and a cross-sectional design. Contributions: This study contributes by clarifying the boundary conditions of green marketing effectiveness and highlighting perceived value as a critical mechanism in sustainable housing purchase decisions.

title: Seed Distribution Factors and Rice Productivity: The Mediating Role of Technology Adoption
container-title: Journal of Economics, Management, Entrepreneurship, and Business (JEMEB)
858684805c148af7673502e1f7162c9ad3861208.abstract: Purpose: This study examines the mediating role of seed technology adoption in linking seed distribution quality, distribution accessibility, agricultural extension support, and distribution program effectiveness with rice farmers' productivity at UPT Pengembangan Benih Padi dan Palawija, Dinas Pertanian dan Ketahanan Pangan Provinsi Jawa Timur. Research Methodology: A quantitative causal design was applied using data from 100 rice farmers selected from 800 certified high-yielding seed recipients through purposive sampling. Data were collected using a five-point Likert-scale questionnaire and analyzed through regression analysis, partial and simultaneous tests, and the Sobel test to evaluate direct and indirect effects. Results: The results show that seed technology adoption is the strongest predictor of rice farmers' productivity and is significantly influenced by seed distribution quality, accessibility, agricultural extension support, and program effectiveness. Distribution accessibility is the strongest determinant of adoption. The mediation analysis confirms that adoption fully mediates the effect of accessibility on productivity, while partially mediating the effects of seed quality, extension support, and program effectiveness. Conclusions: Seed technology adoption is a key mechanism that transforms distribution efforts into productivity improvements. Distribution accessibility alone does not improve productivity unless it encourages actual adoption. Limitations: This study is limited by its cross-sectional design, single research setting, and the use of the Sobel test for mediation analysis. Contributions: This study contributes by demonstrating distinct full and partial mediation pathways, highlighting adoption as a strategic factor in improving agricultural productivity.

title: Robot cops on patrol: police officers' perceived effectiveness of AI-powered humanoid robots
container-title: Policing: An International Journal
399ffbef301f680d3c80797a3999bd5c26c9c5cb.abstract: Purpose The main purpose of the study is to examine how organizational justice, artificial intelligence (AI) literacy and perceived risks shape officers' attitudes toward AI-powered service and crime-fighting robots. Design/methodology/approach This study used survey data collected from 959 police officers in a major metropolitan area in Southwestern China. Two regression models were estimated to analyze correlates of police officers' perceived effectiveness of service and crime-fighting AI robots. Findings Results show that supervisor support for AI is a strong and consistent predictor of positive attitudes toward AI-powered robots, whereas supervisor justice is negatively associated with AI acceptance. AI training and AI knowledge also significantly enhance perceived effectiveness of AI tools, underscoring the saliency of technological familiarity. Perceived risks play a more limited and task-specific role. Originality/value The present study is among the first attempts to assess police officers' attitudes toward the application of AI in policing. This study provides evidence-based recommendations for the ethical and effective integration of AI into law enforcement practices.

title: In-transit temperature deviations and arrival quality in the South Africa–Middle East orange export cold chain
container-title: Journal of Transport and Supply Chain Management
6ef08cc519e5131b956318be2f2858c6fae20688.abstract: Background: Temperature fluctuations during refrigerated transport accelerate citrus deterioration, increasing physiological damage, decay and quality loss. Controlled studies may not capture cumulative commercial exposure and disruption. This study examines associations between historical in-transit temperature deviations and arrival quality in a commercial export corridor. Objectives: The study characterised in-transit temperature deviations and their association with arrival quality in the South Africa–Middle East orange export corridor. Method: A quantitative retrospective design linked 2023–2025 proprietary shipment data, container temperatures and receiver-reported quality outcomes for 252 export containers. Logistic regression assessed associations between in-transit deviations and arrival quality, with alternative model specifications used as robustness checks. Results: Peel pitting increased from 24.1% in 2023 to 71.3% in 2025, whereas rind breakdown and decay declined. Peel pitting was consistently associated with year, departure-port group and transit duration. Temporal and port factors largely explained rind breakdown; temperature effects were inconsistent. Decay remained prevalent, although model instability constrained inference. Transit duration was the most reliable positive predictor. Extended analyses confirmed these patterns. Conclusion: Operational conditions, route configurations and transit duration most strongly influence arrival quality, while temperature effects are outcome-specific. Cold-chain risk assessment therefore requires integrated operational and thermal analysis. Contribution: This study provides multi-season evidence from citrus exports, showing that operational conditions, route configurations and transit duration are more consistently associated with arrival quality than aggregate in-transit temperature metrics.

title: Stakeholder influence on cost performance of riverine construction projects in the Nigerian Niger Delta: evidence from completed public intervention projects
container-title: Journal of Engineering, Design and Technology
c29c68d50ce3053ff4998245c21ea340a8c51531.abstract: Purpose This study aims to investigate how stakeholder actions influence the cost performance of riverine construction projects in Nigeria’s Niger Delta region, with emphasis on governance practices, contractor conduct, environmental disturbances, community engagement, and broader contextual risk management. The research makes a clear distinction between cost performance and cost overruns by defining cost performance as the degree to which actual expenditure aligns with the approved budget, while cost overruns specifically refer to expenditure that exceeds the approved completion estimate or baseline. The assessment is based on archival project records comparing initial and final project costs, as well as documentary evidence linking the relationship between stakeholder actions and observable cost outcomes. Design/methodology/approach A qualitative archival research design drawing on documentary evidence from 48 completed public intervention projects carried out by intervention agencies as well as stakeholder-related data involving 57 stakeholders. Project cost records, attendance sheets, and meeting reports were carefully analyzed to determine how stakeholder actions such as contract re-awards, redesigns, pending payments, contractor conduct, and community disruptions influenced project cost performance. The analysis combined archival cost data with stakeholder documentation using thematic coding and descriptive summarization, while cross-checking records and applying standard coding processes improved analytical consistency and minimized bias. Findings Stakeholder actions were found to significantly influence cost performance in riverine construction projects. Contract re-awards and redesigns yielded positive cost performance by reducing escalation risks in certain situations. However, issues of contractor failure, pending payments, insecurity threats, force majeure events (flooding), legal battles, and community festival disturbances negatively influence cost underperformance, and out of the 48 projects reviewed, 12 had effective cost performance and 36 had poor cost performance, highlighting governance deficiencies and community disruptions as the primary causes of cost escalation. Research limitations/implications The findings are limited to 48 completed projects carried out by two government intervention agencies and stakeholder-related data involving 57 stakeholders within a specific riverine context, limiting their generalizability; future research should expand geographically and incorporate quantitative methodologies. Practical implications The research highlights that to enhance cost performance in riverine construction, it’s crucial for policymakers, intervention agencies, contractors, and host communities to work together. Key strategies include implementing transparent payment mechanisms, improved contractor screening, early stakeholder mapping, proactive community participation, adequate recording of variances, and adaptive planning for riverine threats, which are critical for mitigating cost inefficiencies. More broadly, the study shows that cost performance cannot be improved solely by technical planning but rather through accountable governance, institutional coordination, and stakeholder engagement mechanisms that are responsive to the unique sociopolitical and environmental variables of the area. Social implications Improved stakeholder coordination and transparent administration can repair community confidence, mitigate sociopolitical disturbances, and promote sustainable infrastructure delivery, ultimately improving living conditions in Niger Delta riverine communities that have historically been marginalized. Originality/value This study provides empirically grounded and region-specific evidence on the largely unexplored relationship between stakeholder actions and cost performance in Niger Delta riverine construction projects. By linking archival cost records data with stakeholder meeting evidence, this shows that cost performance in these environments is shaped by governance quality, stakeholder coordination, community engagement, environmental disruption, and proactive risk management. The study extends stakeholder theory to a complex riverine and sociopolitical construction context with wider relevance for cost management and sustainable project delivery in fragile and logistically constrained project environments across developing regions worldwide.

title: From knowledge to innovation: dimensional predictors of organizational creativity and innovation among primary healthcare managers
container-title: Journal of Health Organization and Management
31ab09a33d992be623436ca99a3f228abfe56e3e.abstract: Purpose This study examines how six knowledge management (KM) dimensions, namely creation, absorption, organization, storage, dissemination and application, relate to organizational creativity and innovation among managers in public primary healthcare. Design/methodology/approach A multi-wave cross-sectional survey was conducted among 95 managers across 20 public primary healthcare facilities between 2019 and 2022. Data were collected using structured measures of KM, creativity and innovation. Multiple regression, bootstrap confidence intervals, multicollinearity diagnostics and supplementary mediation analyses were used to examine associations. Recruitment-year differences and potential common-method bias were also assessed. Findings Knowledge absorption, dissemination and application showed positive associations with creativity and innovation. Knowledge creation was positively associated with innovation in bivariate analysis but showed a negative adjusted coefficient when the KM dimensions were entered simultaneously, suggesting sensitivity to shared variance among correlated predictors. After accounting for knowledge application, the direct association between knowledge creation and innovation was no longer statistically significant. Creativity and innovation were highly correlated (r = 0.907), indicating substantial construct overlap that may also reflect the organizational context. Research limitations/implications The study is limited by its modest sample size, multi-year data collection, individual-level self-reported measures and potential common method and selection biases. Recruitment spanned pre-COVID-19, COVID-19 and post-COVID-19 periods, and facility-level clustering was not modeled. The high correlation between creativity and innovation also raises concerns about discriminant validity. The findings should therefore be interpreted as associations rather than causal effects. Despite these limitations, the results indicate that knowledge application and absorption may be important areas for managerial attention in resource-constrained public primary healthcare settings and provide directions for future multilevel and longitudinal research. Practical implications The findings suggest that healthcare managers should place greater emphasis on mechanisms that enable relevant knowledge to be absorbed, shared and translated into routine practice. Structured knowledge-sharing routines, peer learning, interdisciplinary collaboration, documentation of effective practices, continuing professional development and integration of lessons into managerial procedures may support these processes. In resource-constrained settings, strengthening the use of existing organizational knowledge may be more feasible than relying primarily on additional financial or technological resources. Healthcare leaders and policymakers may consider incorporating these mechanisms into managerial development and organizational-learning initiatives, while recognizing that the present findings reflect associations rather than demonstrated causal effects. Social implications Effective knowledge management may contribute to stronger organizational capacity for creativity and innovation in public primary healthcare, with potential implications for the quality and responsiveness of healthcare services. Strengthening mechanisms for knowledge sharing, learning and application may help healthcare organizations make better use of existing knowledge and experience, particularly where financial and technological resources are limited. Such improvements may support managers and healthcare teams in responding to changing service needs and developing locally appropriate solutions. However, because this study identifies associations rather than causal effects, these potential social benefits should be considered as areas for further investigation rather than established outcomes. Originality/value The study contributes evidence from a resource-constrained public primary healthcare setting by jointly examining 6 KM dimensions against both creativity and innovation. The findings suggest that knowledge application and related processes may be particularly important for translating knowledge into organizational outcomes, while highlighting the need for larger multilevel and longitudinal studies.

title: Informational-to-relational pathway to value co-creation: role of patient influencers' E-WOM quality and parasocial relationships in OHCs
container-title: Journal of Health Organization and Management
8cdca8ded5f0531bb1b0eb6ab2dceefd483d43e4.abstract: Purpose Drawing on service-dominant logic (SDL) and value co-creation literature, this study examines the association between patient influencers' E-WOM quality (E-WOMQ) and parasocial relationships (PSR) in online healthcare communities (OHCs). It examines whether PSR are associated with patients' participation in value co-creation (PVCC) across four dimensions during the healthcare journey, and whether PSR mediate the E-WOMQ–PVCC association. The study also examines online community experience (OCE) as a moderator of the E-WOMQ–PSR association. Design/methodology/approach A cross-sectional survey was conducted among members of OHCs in Bangladesh between July 2024 and September 2024, yielding 609 useable responses. This study employed PLS-SEM in SmartPLS 4.0 to test the proposed hypotheses. Findings E-WOMQ is positively associated with PSR. PSR is positively associated with information seeking, information sharing, personal interaction and responsible behaviour, and significantly mediates the associations between E-WOMQ and all four PVCC dimensions. OCE does not significantly moderate the E-WOMQ–PSR association. Originality/value This study extends SDL by specifying an informational-to-relational pathway in OHCs, linking the perceived quality of patient-influencer's healthcare information with relational evaluations and multidimensional patient value co-creation. The findings offer practical guidance for healthcare organizations, OHC managers and patient influencers on communicating relevant, helpful and transparent healthcare information while supporting constructive patient participation during the healthcare journey.

title: A sustainable natural resource management hierarchical model in Vietnamese mining industry: environmental policy and regulation impacts on technical operation capability
container-title: Management of Environmental Quality: An International Journal
b798cff29ef7d3a5872fd4faf749d03c0a06d4fe.abstract: Purpose This study builds a sustainable natural resource management (SNRM) model, as prior studies on how environmental policy and regulation and stakeholder involvement incorporate technical operation capability are lacking, and comprehensive insights into the specific challenges and strategies for SNRM practices are needed. Design/methodology/approach This study aims to identify a valid set of attributes for SNRM in the Vietnamese mining industry, develop a causal hierarchical model and identify the important attributes for improvement via a hybrid approach. Institutional theory, stakeholder theory and dynamic capability theory under the foundation of the socio-technical perspective theory are applied. Findings The hierarchical structure of SNRM includes 4 perspectives, 8 aspects and 22 criteria, with causal aspects such as environmental policy and regulation, financing mechanisms, stakeholder involvement and digital transformation. The practical focuses are environmental governance, green financing, external suppliers and joint venture partners, renewable energy adoption, and automation and robotics. Technological innovation plays crucial roles in SNRM adoption. Originality/value This study develops a theoretically grounded causal SNRM framework integrating institutional, stakeholder, dynamic capability and socio-technical perspectives, while extending SNRM through technological innovation and operation capability. The result provides a context-specific framework for the Vietnamese mining industry and offers actionable priorities for policymakers and practitioners to advance sustainable resource management.

title: Bearing fault diagnosis of rolling machinery based on spatial pyramid channel attention network with depthwise separable convolution
container-title: Engineering Computations
ac8de549d0c263d536d5003d12d7eeb6f37d0532.abstract: Purpose Rolling bearings are critical components in rotating machinery, and their fault diagnosis is essential for ensuring safe equipment operation. However, traditional fault diagnosis methods face challenges including insufficient feature extraction, high computational complexity and difficulties in multi-scale information fusion. To address these issues, this paper proposes a spatial pyramid channel attention network with depthwise separable convolution for intelligent fault diagnosis of rolling bearings. Design/methodology/approach Continuous wavelet transform converts 1D vibration signals into 2D time-frequency images. An efficient feature extraction block integrates depthwise separable convolution, multi-scale dilated convolution and a cross-spatial multi-scale attention module to expand the receptive field while reducing complexity. A cross-spatial multi-scale attention mechanism uses parallel 1D global average pooling paths to capture long-range dependencies. Finally, a channel-spatial synergy module combines spatial pyramid structure and channel information interaction to establish inter-channel dependencies while preserving multi-scale spatial information. Findings Experimental results on three public datasets from Jiangnan University (JNU), Xi'an Jiaotong University (XJTU-SY) and Paderborn University (PU) demonstrate that the proposed method achieves diagnostic accuracies of 99.94%, 98.94% and 98.55%, respectively, showing superior diagnostic precision and better generalization capability compared to existing methods. Ablation experiments further validate the effectiveness of each core module. Originality/value This paper proposes a novel spatial pyramid channel attention network with depthwise separable convolution that synergistically integrates multi-scale dilated convolution, cross-spatial attention and channel-spatial synergy. The method effectively addresses challenges of insufficient feature extraction, high computational complexity and multi-scale fusion difficulties in rolling bearing fault diagnosis, demonstrating superior diagnostic accuracy and generalization capability across multiple public datasets.

title: Redefining senior workforce management: challenges, opportunities and strategic pathways
container-title: European Journal of Training and Development
a2d43b282d79da7e9d0f4f993269babe488f9145.abstract: Purpose This study aims to identify and analyse the emerging challenges that will shape the development of senior talent in the coming years and, crucially, to provide a multi-level and context-sensitive framework for interpreting these challenges responsibly. Design/methodology/approach This study adopts a qualitative–computational design combining collective artificial intelligence (CAI) with a two-stage analytical process involving 306 Spanish management staff. A theoretical framework integrates structural, organisational and individual perspectives (theory of ageism, human capital theory, theory of social capital, theory of cognitive ageing and a variety of psychosocial approaches). CAI algorithms (conceptual stratification, semantic clustering, hybridisation and pairwise comparison) enable the aggregation, synthesis and prioritisation of expert judgements. Findings The findings reveal two main areas of challenge: (1) ensuring that senior employees adapt and remain essential in organisational transformation – addressing issues of strategy, motivation, roles, digitalisation and humility – and (2) enabling them to feel valued and to pass on their legacy, which involves addressing knowledge transfer, recognition, ageism, rewards and work–life balance. This study highlights the most widely supported initiatives and the differences found based on gender, age and professional profile. It also offers a set of winning strategies and key proposals for effective management of senior talent. Originality/value This study identifies emerging, system-level patterns that cut across structural, organisational and individual domains, offering a forward-looking understanding of the challenges shaping senior talent development. The use of CAI enhances analytical depth by integrating diverse perspectives, generating consensus-based insights and revealing complex challenges that traditional qualitative or Delphi-based methods may overlook. By combining this methodological innovation with a multi-level theoretical framework, this study provides organisations with a theoretically grounded and context-sensitive roadmap for transforming senior-related challenges into strategic opportunities.

title: AI governance as co-regulation: a practitioner-informed framework for defense-sector small and medium-sized enterprises
container-title: Digital Policy, Regulation and Governance
567df46acd778f8be8494c9ae84f8e44b8ec75da.abstract: Purpose This paper aims to examine how practitioners supporting defense-sector small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) place artificial intelligence (AI) governance within the coregulatory regime of National Institute of Standards and Technology Special Publication 800-171, the cybersecurity maturity model certification program, contracts and assessors. Design/methodology/approach An exploratory survey of 38 practitioners, recruited through a public LinkedIn post, combined a risk-to-control-family mapping task, artifact feasibility ratings and open-ended responses. Analysis was descriptive, with exploratory correlations adjusted for multiplicity and one researcher coded the open text. Findings Respondents concentrated AI risk on a few evidence-bearing control families, led by audit and accountability, risk assessment, access control and system and information integrity. Perceived compliance strain was high and readiness low. Artifacts resembling existing evidence, such as audit trail exports, were rated most feasible. Guidance ambiguity was the leading barrier. No exploratory association survived adjustment for multiplicity. Research limitations/implications The purposive sample and self-reported perceptions support pattern identification, not population estimates or claims about implementation outcomes. Practical implications Assessors and prime contractors could reduce SME burden by publishing exemplar AI evidence artifacts mapped to existing control families. Originality/value The study develops coregulation as a lens on the evidence burden of small firms at the base of regulatory chains, reports the full risk-to-control matrix and derives a seven-module framework that separates survey-supported elements from design choices.

title: Contingent convertible bonds (CoCo): impact on shareholder wealth dilution and risk management
container-title: Journal of Economics, Finance and Administrative Science
01fe849b1a4a16de1f61742f6286ce4d9c9a023f.abstract: Purpose This article investigates how the capital structure of a bank financed by equity, conventional bonds, contingent convertible (CoCo) bonds, and deposits is affected by the dilution of shareholders' wealth. Capital dilution results from the conversion of CoCo bonds into a predetermined number of shares when a particular leverage ratio threshold is reached. Design/methodology/approach An analytical formula was developed for the values of CoCo and conventional bonds by combining two European barrier call options used to conceptualize shareholder value. The proportion of shares held by current shareholders and the fraction held by investors who converted their securities into shares are expressed precisely in order to examine the dilution issue. Findings Numerical evaluations indicate that CoCo bonds generally enhance shareholder wealth by lowering bankruptcy risks, until the dilution effect counterbalances this advantage. Practical implications The results presented in this paper can offer various benefits to banks, investors, and regulators. First, leverage ratios are used to trigger equity conversion, rather than conventional capital ratios. Second, the results support the notion that CoCo bonds boost both shareholder wealth and bank value by reducing the likelihood of costly bankruptcies. Finally, the research emphasizes the importance of selecting appropriate parameters when structuring CoCo bonds. Originality/value The results provide evidence that CoCo bonds improve bank value and shareholder wealth by reducing default risk, enhancing financial stability and bank soundness, and increasing shareholder wealth through reduced bankruptcy risk.

title: Systemic connectedness and shock transmission across FinTech, clean energy, Islamic and traditional assets
container-title: International Journal of Islamic and Middle Eastern Finance and Management
d6c8c84e735d1b8c7fd7540d58d6e248dd4be366.abstract: Purpose This study aims to investigate the dynamic connectedness and risk transmission among FinTech, clean energy, Islamic, and traditional financial assets, with particular emphasis on their behavior under varying market conditions and crisis periods. Design/methodology/approach This study uses conditional autoregressive value-at-risk, frequency connectedness, and wavelet local multiple correlation techniques to capture tail risk dynamics and time-frequency spillovers across asset classes. The analysis is conducted across multiple investment horizons, including daily, weekly, and monthly frequencies. Findings The results reveal a high level of interconnectedness across all asset classes, as indicated by a substantial total connectedness index. Short-term spillovers dominate over medium- and long-term dynamics, suggesting rapid transmission of shocks. The findings further indicate that connectedness patterns intensify during periods of economic and geopolitical stress, particularly during the COVID-19 pandemic and the Russia–Ukraine conflict. Islamic FinTech and Sukuk markets exhibit strong intraclass linkages and significant spillover effects with other financial assets. In addition, certain assets emerge as net risk transmitters, offering potential hedging and diversification benefits during crisis periods. Practical implications The findings provide valuable insights for investors and portfolio managers to optimize asset allocation and design effective hedging strategies. Policymakers can benefit from understanding the propagation of systemic risk to enhance financial stability frameworks, particularly in Islamic financial systems. Originality/value This study contributes to the literature by jointly examining FinTech, clean energy, and Islamic and traditional financial assets within a unified framework using advanced tail risk and frequency-domain methodologies. It offers novel insights into the evolving interconnectedness of Islamic and global financial markets.

title: Real-world outcomes of biosimilar bevacizumab-bvzr versus reference agent in the management of patients with IDH wild-type glioblastoma
container-title: Neuro-Oncology Practice
c977e5d83df0e3b666a7af1552cd9ae9a1bc0a74.abstract: Abstract BACKGROUND Bevacizumab, an anti-VEGF monoclonal antibody, has become a mainstay in the management of malignant gliomas. Multiple bevacizumab biosimilars have been approved since initial FDA approval of the reference agent and have seen widespread use, in part due to reduced costs. However, real-world data evaluating comparability between reference and biosimilar agents, especially for the management of glioblastoma, remain limited. METHODS We performed a retrospective analysis of patients treated with reference bevacizumab (Avastin ®) versus those receiving bevacizumab-bvzr (Zirabev ®), a widely used biosimilar agent for the management of IDH wild-type glioblastoma at our institution between 2019 and 2022. Outcomes of interest included rates of dose-limiting adverse effects associated with anti-angiogenic therapy, as well as survival as measured by overall survival (OS). RESULTS A total of 129 patients were included in our final analysis; 71 received reference drug (bevacizumab) while 58 received the biosimilar agent (bevacizumab-bvzr). Rates of dose-limiting adverse effects were similar between both groups (OR 1.2013, p = 0.7418). On analysis of the entire cohort, concomitant treatment with anticoagulation (OR 3.3045, p = 0.0238) was associated with a higher risk of dose-limiting adverse effects On survival analysis, we found that OS was similar between the bevacizumab (median OS 714 daysdays) and biosimilar (median OS 631 days) groups by both univariate (p = 0.5639). and multivariate (HR 1.0869, p = 0.6916) analyses. CONCLUSIONS Bevacizumab-bvzr demonstrated similar clinical efficacy and safety profile compared to reference bevacizumab in our institutional cohort of IDH-WT glioblastoma patients.

title: VRCycle: A Feasibility Randomized Controlled Trial Evaluating a Virtual Reality Cycling Intervention in People With Knee Osteoarthritis
container-title: Physical Therapy
0f86e3a636f8d4a232b5ec06d6fb320bdd8f07e5.abstract: Abstract Importance Exercise is recommended as a core treatment for knee osteoarthritis; yet uptake is suboptimal, with identified barriers including pain, difficulty (overly effortful), and boredom. Virtual reality (VR) shows promise in overcoming these barriers, although whether VR-enhanced exercise is acceptable to people with osteoarthritis and feasible in physical therapy settings is unknown. Objective The objective was to assess the feasibility of conducting a clinical trial to evaluate VR-enhanced cycling and explore preliminary efficacy of this intervention. Design A prospectively registered (ACTRN12624000122550), two-arm feasibility randomized controlled trial was conducted. Setting The trial was conducted at a clinical trials facility. Participants Forty-one participants with painful knee osteoarthritis were enrolled. Interventions Participants were randomized (1:1 ratio) to receive VR-enhanced cycling or traditional (no-VR) cycling, both involving twelve, 30-minute cycling sessions over 6-weeks, supervised by a physical therapist. Main Outcomes and Measures A priori feasibility criteria surrounding recruitment and enrolment rate, intervention adherence, technical difficulty, retention, and participant experience (acceptability, credibility, adverse events) were evaluated. Clinical outcomes (pain, function) and exercise capacity (perceptually regulated exercise test) were assessed at baseline, post-intervention, 1-month follow-up (clinical outcomes only). Within-session exercise engagement (work, time) and experience (perceived exertion, affect) were evaluated as process variables. Results All feasibility criteria were met. An average of 6.8 participants per week were eligible with a 73% enrollment rate. Participants attended 91% of intervention sessions, and 90% of participants completed follow-up assessments. VR technical issues were rare (3% of sessions) as were adverse events (2 unrelated to VR). Treatment acceptability and credibility was high and clinical outcomes improved in both groups. Conclusions Progression to a full trial is supported due to high feasibility, acceptability, and improvement in clinical outcomes. Relevance Although not powered to evaluate efficacy, the within-group changes observed demonstrate that both cycling modalities can improve knee pain, function, and exercise capacity.

title: AI Assessment of Heterogeneous Histopathologic Brain Tumor Sub-regions: the RANO MICCAI BraTS-Path 2024 Challenge
container-title: Neuro-Oncology
33be48153e50bcd0943f8c6fa42c207057d4b088.abstract: Abstract Background Automated classification of glioblastoma (IDH-wt, WHO CNS Gr.4) histopathologic sub-regions in whole slide images (WSI) is essential for quantitative tumor characterization, but faces substantial challenges from intra-tumoral heterogeneity and inter-observer annotation variability. The AI-RANO & RANO-Pathology working groups organized BraTS-Path 2024, representing the first international benchmarking environment and publicly available spatially annotated dataset, towards promoting the development and fair evaluation of Artificial Intelligence (AI) models to classify specific sub-regions: cellular tumor, pseudopalisading necrosis (PN), microvascular proliferation, geographic necrosis, infiltration into the cortex, and white matter penetration (WM). Methods Multi-institutional H&E-stained WSIs had reference standard samples generated by eight expert neuropathologists, following a rigorous peer review protocol, resulting in 309,118 data samples (training/validation/hold-out testing: 96,485/62,387/150,246). Quantitative performance evaluation of six AI approaches was conducted based on multiple metrics, including Accuracy and Matthew’s correlation coefficient (MCC). A robust statistically-aware ranking strategy offered statistical significance of the final rankings. Results Top-performing approaches employed common strategies, including large pre-trained models, ensembling, and extensive data augmentation, reporting Accuracy=0.69 and MCC=0.58. Key challenges included severe class imbalance, hampering minority class performance, and inter-annotator variability, especially for ambiguous sub-regions such as PN or WM. Conclusions BraTS-Path represents a valuable public resource for glioblastoma histopathologic sub-region assessment. Our findings indicate the specific task remaining an open research problem, highlighting the influence of rare sub-regions, the absence of a consistent “gold standard” annotation protocol, and the potential of foundation models to improve generalization, guiding future research toward developing more reliable AI tools for quantitative neuropathology.

title: Unraveling the roles of malicious envy and servant leadership in the ties between everyday sadism and knowledge sabotage
container-title: VINE Journal of Information and Knowledge Management Systems
6421cc04fe89b68c95fef94722176e8694c4a847.abstract: Purpose This study aims to investigate whether malicious envy mediates the relationship between everyday sadism and knowledge sabotage. It also examines whether servant leadership can mitigate malicious envy’s harmful influence on knowledge sabotage. Design/methodology/approach Data were collected from 355 full-time employees in southeastern Nigeria using a three-wave, time-lagged design. Findings The results confirm that malicious envy mediates the link between everyday sadism and knowledge sabotage. However, contrary to the hypothesis, servant leadership did not moderate the relationship between envy and sabotage. Practical implications Rather than using aggressive screening procedures, organizations should strike a balance by evaluating qualifications, skills and interpersonal dynamics, while focusing on building workplaces that discourage toxic behaviors. Since eliminating envy entirely is unrealistic, management should address its structural roots. This can be done by creating objective, fair reward systems and transparent performance-appraisal processes that reduce zero-sum peer comparisons. Originality/value This study complements previous studies linking malevolent personality traits and insidious emotions to knowledge-related deviance and the role of leadership in mitigating knowledge-related harm.

title: Effectiveness evaluation of generative intelligent search: a comparative study with traditional search engine
container-title: Aslib Journal of Information Management
d1c9eeac798ccc7a8876d8762f5ec367e887920a.abstract: Purpose The emergence of generative artificial intelligence has transformed information retrieval, yet limited understanding of its differences from traditional search engines hinders clarity regarding changes in user search behavior and variations in search effectiveness, thereby impeding guidance for future search interface design. Design/methodology/approach We conducted a laboratory experiment comparing two versions of the Bing search engine: the traditional Bing search and the generative-AI integrated Bing (Bing Chat). We interpreted variations in user search behavior through querying, browsing, and clicking data, and established a multidimensional metric framework encompassing user, cost-benefit, and system dimensions to assess search effectiveness. 40 participants with good search skills completed the experiment, resulting in a final dataset comprising 160 observation records. Findings The Mann-Whitney U test revealed that users of generative AI search engines exhibited the following characteristics compared to those using traditional search engines: longer queries, more keyboard activity, more frequent query restructuring (including more narrowing queries, more following the system queries, and more changing the syntactic structure queries, with less broadening queries), more browsing during the first search session, and less scrolling and clicking. The results of the Linear Mixed Models show that, compared to traditional search engines, users achieve superior performance with generative AI search on users’ subjective perceptions and search efficiency metrics. Furthermore, we employed machine learning to validate which search behaviors can predict a user’s search effectiveness. The results indicate that the Gradient Boosting Machines are the optimal prediction models. The five most significant indicators for predicting search performance are Avelength. QueryConsTime, TimetofirSearch, ResViewTime and NumbofScroll. Research limitations/implications By revealing differences in user behavior and search efficiency across various search engines, this study deepens our understanding of generative AI search engines at a finer granularity and contributes to building adaptive search platforms capable of optimizing search recommendations. Originality/value By revealing differences in user behavior and efficiency between traditional and generative versions of the Bing search engine, this study deepens our understanding of generative AI search engines at a finer granularity and contributes to building adaptive search platforms capable of optimizing search recommendations.

title: Human-centred lean management practices, employee involvement and innovative performance in SMEs: evidence from an emerging economy
container-title: International Journal of Lean Six Sigma
12c12e57f635acd0ddc7a5491ad5f0b93a086736.abstract: Purpose This paper aims to evaluate how small- and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in developing economies continue to face pressure to innovate due to intense competition, changing customer expectations and resource constraints. Although lean management practices are widely adopted to improve operational efficiency, their role in enhancing innovative performance remains insufficiently understood, particularly in SMEs where human and organisational factors are often overlooked. This study examines the relationships between human-centred lean management practices (HLMPs) and innovative performance and the mediating role of employee involvement among employees in Nigerian SMEs. Design/methodology/approach Cross-sectional survey data were collected from 314 employees across 45 SMEs and analysed using partial least squares structural equation modelling. Findings Customer focus, employee training and small group problem solving are significantly and positively associated with innovative performance, whereas top management leadership shows no significant direct association with innovative performance. All four HLMPs are significantly associated with employee involvement, with employee involvement mediating the relationships between top management leadership and small group problem solving with innovative performance. Practical implications The findings suggest that SMEs seeking to strengthen innovation should complement lean efficiency efforts with practices that enable employee participation, particularly small group problem solving and meaningful involvement in improvement activities. Originality/value The study contributes to lean management and innovation literature by showing that human-centred lean practices do not have a uniform relationship with innovative performance. Instead, employee involvement provides an important link between selected lean practices and innovative performance, offering evidence from SMEs in an emerging economy.

title: Algorithmic cognitive programmes: observing ambient architectures of attention with social systems theory
container-title: Kybernetes
51d2013b2858e0715f8c03247ec8eb58d1d1a814.abstract: Purpose This paper extends Luhmann's concept of programmes – decision premises specifying the conditions under which a system's binary code is operatively assigned – into the domain of algorithmically mediated communication. It conceptualises recommendation systems, ranking algorithms and feedback architectures as ambient cognitive programmes: recursive, probabilistic selectors that perturb the structural coupling between social and psychic systems, and examines the constitutional implications of their opacity and transfunctional reach. Design/methodology/approach The study develops a systemic–cybernetic model grounded in Luhmann's social systems theory and the epistemology of autopoietic cognition, integrating Teubner's theory of societal constitutionalism to address the normative dimensions of algorithmic mediation. Analytical illustrations from Facebook and TikTok contrast two recommendation architectures – affinity-based cascading and behavioural-similarity propagation – to demonstrate how the model applies across distinct platform logics. Findings Algorithmic cognitive programmes operate as meta-programmes that reconfigure multiple forms of social differentiation simultaneously, enacting a binary operational distinction of visibility/invisibility through engagement metrics. Their colonisation of communicative environments – by economic imperatives and, as the analysis argues, by the autonomous logic of technical mediation – becomes a constitutional pathology where its effects cannot be contested or corrected, requiring internal self-limiting mechanisms that render operative selection criteria observable to affected systems. Originality/value The paper advances a novel theoretical category – ambient cognitive programmes – that extends Luhmann's organisational typology by identifying a configuration it does not explicitly address: a purpose programme without a terminal goal state that continuously revises the conditional programmes it governs. It connects this analytical framework to Teubner's societal constitutionalism, proposing constitutional observability as a structural condition for the compatibility between algorithmic regimes and communicative pluralism.

title: Unraveling performance asymmetry: environmental accounting and knowledge management as economic and environmental decision-support tools in an emerging market
container-title: Journal of Accounting & Organizational Change
38d43fa3e82071d890d20ff410690d2f3f846b8a.abstract: Purpose This paper aims to examine the asymmetric effect of environmental management accounting (EMA) and environmental knowledge management practices (EKMP) on the financial (FP) and environmental performance (EP) of firms in an emerging market. Design/methodology/approach It adopted the cross-sectional design with stratified random sampling and PLS-SEM to analyze data from 347 respondents across manufacturing firms in Ghana. Findings The findings reveal an important asymmetry in the performance consequences of EMA. While EMA significantly improves FP, it does not exert a corresponding influence on EP, suggesting that EMA functions primarily as an economic decision-support mechanism rather than a direct environmental improvement tool. Conversely, EKMP contributes to FP, but the magnitude of its effect is relatively small and less direct than its influence on EP. Research limitations/implications The complex effect of EKMP on FP suggests that environmental performance may serve as an intermediate mechanism through which EKMP enhances FP; thus, the nexus should be mediated by factors like EP, ESG and green innovation. Practical implications Managers should not treat EMA and EKMP as interchangeable practices. EMA should primarily support financial and managerial control through environmental cost identification, resource allocation, budgeting, investment appraisal and operational decision-making. EKMP, in contrast, should be developed as an organizational capability. Firms must intentionally transition from passive compliance to active eco-innovations and sustainable production technologies fueled by internal EKMP to achieve tangible environmental targets. Originality/value By synthesizing the resource-based view and knowledge-based view theories, this paper provides pioneering evidence that EMA and EKMP govern completely different performance dimensions. The ultimate value of this work is proving that true corporate sustainability cannot be achieved through fragmented, single-framework approaches; instead, firms must structurally integrate financial-accounting controls with cognitive knowledge systems to achieve complete, balanced performance in volatile emerging markets.

title: Cybersecurity awareness and organizational performance: unpacking the roles of threat appraisal and institutional communication
container-title: Journal of Enterprise Information Management
7461e0779afe19651708a84923f6bfe6b7c2af2a.abstract: Purpose This study examines how information security awareness, perceived threat, perceived vulnerability and government social media participation are associated with cybersecurity awareness and organizational performance in Vietnamese small and medium-sized enterprises. Drawing on protection motivation theory, it explains how managers process internal security knowledge and external institutional information when developing cybersecurity awareness. Design/methodology/approach Survey data were collected from 408 managers and members of the board of directors of Vietnamese small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) and analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM). Findings The results show that information security awareness is positively associated with perceived threat but is not directly associated with perceived vulnerability, indicating that security knowledge and perceived organizational exposure are distinct managerial cognitive processes. Perceived threat is positively associated with both perceived vulnerability and cybersecurity awareness, and perceived vulnerability is likewise positively associated with cybersecurity awareness. Government social media participation is positively associated with perceived vulnerability, cybersecurity awareness and organizational performance. Cybersecurity awareness has the strongest direct relationship with organizational performance. Originality/value This study contributes to enterprise information management research by explaining how internal security knowledge and external institutional information are jointly associated with managerial cybersecurity awareness in SMEs. It provides evidence consistent with a theorized directional relationship linking perceived threat, perceived vulnerability and cybersecurity awareness, and highlights the organizational relevance of cybersecurity awareness through its association with organizational performance.

title: Appropriability against retention: how knowledge protection choices co-vary with internal knowledge redundancy in family firms
container-title: Journal of Knowledge Management
5b9c1d3f47dd8f15fcff00cf846070bd9c31bbc1.abstract: Purpose The purpose of this study is to explain why owner-managers of family firms adopt protection strategies that increase their exposure to knowledge loss. It compares concealment-based and codification-based protection in two Nigerian family-owned food firms to specify how protection choice co-varies with the internal redundancy on which continuity depends. Design/methodology/approach A comparative two-case design uses polar-type sampling. The data set comprises two semi-structured owner-manager interviews of 60 and 80 min, 16 pages of field notes and four organisational documents, analysed using reflexive thematic analysis. Internal redundancy is defined operationally, for both cases, as the count of persons able to reproduce the firm’s core output without its holder, plus retrievable artefacts carrying it. Findings Both owners protect the same class of knowledge by opposite means. Case A withholds it from written form, restricts access by production stage and operates a coded vocabulary sustained by the proprietor’s position as a linguistic outsider, while Case B externalises it into documents governed by contract and monitoring. The comparison isolates a coupling invisible to single-case designs: concealment suppresses the redundancy that protects the firm against losing what it conceals. The coupling is contingent, binding where core knowledge is held personally and treated as indivisible. Originality/value The study specifies an inverse coupling between appropriability and retention that the two literatures treat separately; states the conditions under which it holds; and links it to the knowledge-hiding literature, which attributes the same internal distribution to interpersonal motive. It also identifies proprietor linguistic asymmetry as a protection resource absent from monolingual settings.

title: A review of predictive maintenance strategies for Industry 5.0: AI, digital twins and human–machine collaboration
container-title: Journal of Quality in Maintenance Engineering
24d188956295cd9e7430988639ed3dfafe01a783.abstract: Purpose The purpose of this article is to provide a comprehensive review of predictive maintenance (PdM) strategies within the emerging Industry 5.0 paradigm, emphasizing the shift from automation-centric maintenance to human-centric, collaborative systems. The study aims to synthesize model-based, data-driven, artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled and hybrid PdM approaches, examine the role of key enabling technologies such as digital twins and edge computing and highlight human–machine collaboration in maintenance decision-making. By proposing a unified taxonomy, the article seeks to identify research gaps and guide the development of resilient, sustainable and explainable PdM systems. Design/methodology/approach This study adopts a structured systematic review methodology to analyze PdM strategies in the context of Industry 5.0. Peer-reviewed journal articles, standards and authoritative reports were identified through major scientific databases using predefined keywords related to PdM, condition-based maintenance, AI, digital twins and human–machine collaboration. The selected literature was critically examined and classified based on maintenance approach, enabling technologies, deployment architecture and degree of human involvement. Comparative analysis was employed to identify research gaps, challenges and emerging trends, culminating in the development of a novel taxonomy for Industry 5.0-oriented PdM systems. Findings The review reveals that PdM in Industry 5.0 is evolving toward hybrid frameworks that integrate data-driven intelligence with physics-based models and human expertise. While AI-based approaches improve diagnostic and prognostic accuracy, challenges related to data quality, interpretability and workforce acceptance persist. Digital twins, edge computing and collaborative robots emerge as key enablers for real-time, resilient and human-centric maintenance systems. The analysis highlights a lack of unified frameworks addressing human–machine collaboration and resilience, underscoring the need for explainable, lifecycle-oriented PdM solutions tailored to Industry 5.0 environments. Research limitations/implications This study is limited by its reliance on published literature, which may underrepresent proprietary industrial implementations and emerging practices not yet reported in academic sources. The review does not include empirical validation or quantitative benchmarking of PdM methods, focusing instead on conceptual and methodological synthesis. Nevertheless, the proposed taxonomy and identified research gaps provide a foundation for future empirical studies, experimental validation and large-scale industrial case analyses aimed at developing resilient, human-centric PdM frameworks aligned with Industry 5.0 principles. Practical implications The findings of this review offer practical guidance for industrial practitioners seeking to implement PdM within Industry 5.0 environments. The proposed taxonomy assists decision-makers in selecting appropriate PdM strategies based on system complexity, human involvement and technological readiness. Insights into digital twins, edge computing and human-in-the-loop AI support the design of maintenance systems that enhance reliability, reduce unplanned downtime and improve workforce acceptance. The study also highlights the importance of explainable and collaborative maintenance solutions to facilitate successful adoption in real-world manufacturing settings. Social implications By emphasizing human-centric and collaborative PdM, this study highlights the social impact of Industry 5.0 on the industrial workforce. The integration of human-in-the-loop decision-making and collaborative robots can improve workplace safety, reduce physically demanding tasks and support skill augmentation rather than job displacement. Transparent and explainable maintenance systems foster trust between workers and intelligent technologies, facilitating organizational acceptance and long-term adoption. Ultimately, Industry 5.0-oriented PdM contributes to more inclusive, resilient and sustainable industrial environments that align technological advancement with human well-being. Originality/value This article provides one of the first comprehensive reviews that explicitly situates PdM within the Industry 5.0 paradigm, moving beyond automation-centric perspectives. Its originality lies in the integration of PdM, condition-based maintenance, diagnostics and prognostics through a unified, human-centric lens. The study proposes a novel taxonomy that incorporates digital twins, edge computing and human–robot collaboration, offering a structured foundation for future research. By bridging technological, organizational and human factors, the article delivers both conceptual clarity and practical value for advancing next-generation maintenance systems.

title: Managerial networking capability: a multidimensional framework from Iran’s public sector
container-title: Management Research Review
8ca1fbb7fad48148e4d1970dc70714ada3d80b1a.abstract: Purpose This study aims to identify the dimensions and components of managerial networking capability in Iran’s public sector, developing a capability-focused framework grounded in dynamic capabilities theory that extends beyond behavioral conceptualizations dominant in Western literature. Design/methodology/approach Using an interpretive qualitative methodology, in-depth semi-structured interviews were conducted with 15 public sector managers (average 14.6 years managerial experience) selected through purposive and snowball sampling until theoretical saturation. Thematic analysis following Braun and Clarke’s (2006, 2019) six-stage protocol yielded a comprehensive capability framework. Trustworthiness was strengthened through member checking, peer debriefing, researcher reflexivity and intercoder agreement used to strengthen confirmability rather than assert objectivist reliability. Findings Analysis revealed a five-dimensional capability framework: network creation and development capability; relationship consolidation and sustainability capability; member support and protection capability; mutual value and benefit creation capability; and knowledge and opportunity flow management capability. These five interdependent dimensions encompass 16 sub-capabilities aggregated through routinization into organizational-level relational capacities. Originality/value This research makes four theoretical contributions: adopting a capability-focused perspective grounded in microfoundational logic that distinguishes organizational networking capacity from individual behaviors; introducing mutual value creation as a central organizing principle bridging stakeholder theory and dynamic capabilities literature; revealing culturally contingent dimensions (privacy maintenance and protective capabilities) that extend Western-derived frameworks to non-Western public administration contexts; and establishing systematic theoretical boundaries between networking capability and political skill. The framework enables dimension-specific training design, multidimensional capability assessment and evidence-based public sector HR policy reform.

title: Behavioral drivers of regime switch in the sharing economy: an empirical analysis of post-adoption consumer behavior
container-title: Management Research Review
dee7b1d10488e818beb1dd67a25c1beda3bff5b9.abstract: Purpose The emergence of the sharing economy (SE) has challenged traditional consumption patterns, raising concerns about a potential regime switch, whereby SE adoption may become a permanent alternative to traditional consumption for specific products and services. Given the strategic relevance of this phenomenon, this study aims to examine the determinants of regime switch across the accommodation, mobility and consumer goods industries. Design/methodology/approach Data were collected from 398 users of SE platforms and analyzed using a robust regression model combined with the Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator (LASSO) technique. Findings The findings reveal the limited role of sustainability concerns and the greater importance of economic, social and anti-consumption motivations, together with consumer satisfaction, in explaining regime switch. The results also highlight important cross-industry differences. In the hospitality industry, the main barrier to switching is the perceived lack of choice, whereas in the mobility and consumer goods industries the strongest obstacle is consumers’ attachment to private ownership. Finally, intensive use of specific sharing configurations – such as bike and scooter sharing, home exchange, clothing exchange and technology exchange – significantly increases consumers’ propensity to switch. Originality/value To the best of the authors’ knowledge, this study contributes to the literature on regime switch in SE by providing one of the first quantitative cross-industry investigations of the phenomenon. Drawing on the lens of Psychological Ownership (PO) Theory, it explains the behavioral and experiential conditions under which consumers may transition from traditional consumption to SE. The findings also provide managerial implications for both SE platforms and incumbent firms seeking to refine their customer retention strategies.

title: No exit, still loyal? Kinship employee engagement in the face of psychological entrapment
container-title: International Journal of Conflict Management
aa3bccaf68e68cbf88d11841025e172b64b3a80a.abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine how toxic leadership and interpersonal conflict are associated with knowledge hiding through psychological entrapment among creative industry MSME employees and investigates financial vulnerability as an intensifier of entrapment and kinship employee engagement (KEE) as a culturally embedded factor that may weaken knowledge hiding. Design/methodology/approach Data were collected from 317 employees of creative MSMEs in Lampung, Indonesia, using purposive sampling. Hypotheses were tested with covariance-based structural equation modeling (CB-SEM). Findings Toxic leadership and interpersonal conflict are positively associated with psychological entrapment, which in turn is positively associated with knowledge hiding. Mediation occurs for toxic leadership but not for interpersonal conflict. Financial vulnerability strengthens the positive associations of both predictors with entrapment, while KEE weakens the positive association between entrapment and knowledge hiding. Research limitations/implications Several limitations should be considered when interpreting these findings. First, the cross-sectional design limits firm conclusions about causality. Future studies using longitudinal or diary methods could better reveal how psychological entrapment forms and changes over time within MSMEs. Second, the use of self-reported data may introduce perceptual bias. However, the presence of interaction effects, which are generally less sensitive to such bias, reduces this concern to some extent. Practical implications MSME owners and managers should reduce dominating leadership practices, manage interpersonal tensions and enhance employee security. Strengthening kinship-based engagement is a culturally aligned strategy to maintain cooperative knowledge exchange. Social implications By showing how economic vulnerability and relational climate shape defensive behaviors, this study supports the development of healthier work communities where solidarity and mutual care discourage knowledge withholding Originality/value This study examines psychological entrapment as a potential mechanism linking relational adversity to knowledge hiding in MSMEs, while integrating financial vulnerability and KEE as contextual moderators.

title: Motivated toward digital: relationship of CEO regulatory focus and digital orientation
container-title: Baltic Journal of Management
21d7ce56b2c04a1eb1f0c151001d9e452ac362c1.abstract: Purpose This study examines how CEO regulatory focus relates to a firm's digital orientation, recognizing that pursuing digital opportunities is crucial for competitive advantage. We propose that CEO promotion focus is positively related to digital orientation, while prevention focus is negatively related, and explore how alignment between regulatory focus and the firm's environment (regulatory fit) moderates this relationship. Design/methodology/approach We analyzed S&P 500 firms from 2010 through 2019 using data from Compustat, Execucomp and annual shareholder letters, measured key variables with computer-assisted text analysis and tested hypotheses using generalized estimating equations. Findings The findings show that CEO prevention focus is positively associated with digital orientation, and that the strength of this relationship depends on environmental dynamism and complexity, while promotion focus was found not to be associated with digital orientation nor vary with the environment. Originality/value We extend research on managerial characteristics and digital orientation by examining how CEO goal pursuit motivation, specifically growth (promotion focus) versus security (prevention focus) needs, relates to firm's orientation toward digital opportunities.

title: Behind the glamour: counterproductive workplace behavior and psychologically defensive managerial practices in the U.S. fashion industry
container-title: Journal of Fashion Marketing and Management: An International Journal
a3a9f386cac24001e4ff18ce960fc00f86c44516.abstract: Purpose This study examines how counterproductive workplace behavior (CWB) is experienced in US fashion workplaces and how psychologically defensive workplace behavior (PDWB) helps interpret managerial practices under workplace pressure. Design/methodology/approach The study draws on interpretive interviews with 15 US-based fashion, apparel and retail professionals. Using abductive thematic analysis, the study integrates CWB as a behavioral framework and PDWB as an interpretive lens for examining managerial practices under stress. Findings Findings identify four interrelated themes: fashion workplace pressure as a contextual condition, managerial practices under pressure, employee coping and strain and pressure transfer and buffering. Participants described recurring pressure points around product calendars, retail metrics, market deadlines, store visits, supplier uncertainty and brand expectations. Reported managerial practices included excessive control, avoidance, public blame, status protection and withdrawal; these were interpreted through PDWB and, where appropriate, classified as CWB-consistent. Practical implications Fashion firms should formalize feedback, decision-making, recognition, after-hours communication and managerial training around recurring pressure points such as line reviews, market appointments, store visits, holiday retail periods and product deadlines. Originality/value This study develops a process-based interpretation of how workplace pressure, harmful managerial conduct and pressure transfer or buffering are connected in the US fashion industry. By integrating CWB and PDWB, it extends workplace behavior theory into fashion management research and positions internal employee wellbeing as part of responsible fashion management.
