439ad8df55c01c5fbfb7f73acae8fad387788276.abstract: With chatbots and conversational artificial intelligence (CAI), the travel brands are transforming the way they connect with prospects and customers throughout the booking process. The argument among marketing scholars is that customer engagement is a multidimensional construct that encompasses cognitive, emotional and behavioural interactions with a brand and that these interactions are becoming mediated by intelligent technologies. Using the literature of marketing, service research, and tourism-informatics this chapter explores the creation of marketing value by chatbots and CAI in regards to travel services. It assesses the theoretical background of customer engagement and conversational AI, the history of chatbots in the travel industry, and their functional placements through the pre-purchase, purchase, and post-purchase processes. It then evaluates three main sources of marketing value including personalisation of the customer experience, brand communication and voice, and real-time marketing intelligence through conversational data. The chapter also takes into account the issues of challenges, such as hallucinations, channel fragmentation, and escalation failure, as well as the ethical, privacy, and trust issues. Arguments are based on three exemplary cases, and a research agenda is presented in the future of conversational-AI-based travel marketing. The main argument is that, when intelligently combined with the broader marketing stack, chatbots and CAI cease to be viewed as a cost-saving service channel, but rather as a strategic platform of relationship-based, data-rich interaction with customers.

a0716bed81d520e0c418e6f30cd54cc6dc83f45a.abstract: The forecasting of consumer behaviour and its associated response makes an exciting prospect in the tourism and hospitality industry, and can largely be attributed to predictive analytics. This chapter focuses on the use of data-driven methods to gain insights and predict users' trip preferences, booking behaviour, and expectations for the service (e.g., machine learning, AI, or big data analytics)—important topics such as Demand forecasting, Personalisation Strategies, Sentiment analysis, and revenue management in the latest research. Elsewhere in the chapter, the ethical dilemmas involved with consumer data usage, including privacy concerns and issues regarding the transparency and accountability of algorithms, are addressed. In this chapter, the authors tie together theory and practice, offering researchers and providers in the hospitality sector practical insights into how they can use predictive instruments to gain a competitive edge, enhance customer experiences and reach sustainable performance in their organisation in a fast-paced and changing tourism environment.

title: Behavioral Biases in AI-Driven Pricing and Revenue Optimization

ed174c4b4ed08f10fd6ad59224497a10a8aaa670.abstract: The intersection of artificial intelligence and behavioral finance presents an underexplored but commercially significant terrain for reimagining how tourism firms design and implement their pricing strategies. While revenue management in travel and hospitality has long depended on demand-based algorithmic models a persistent gap between what these systems predict and what consumers actually do reveals a structural blind spot the systematic cognitive biases that shape purchase decisions in ways that rational utility models simply cannot capture. This chapter develops a behavioral-AI pricing framework by synthesizing prospect theory mental accounting reference price anchoring and social proof mechanisms within the architecture of modern machine learning revenue management systems. Drawing on secondary evidence from major online travel platforms and published booking behavior studies we demonstrate that tourism consumers exhibit consistent loss aversion effects when exposed to dynamic price fluctuations that reference price anchoring significantly modulates willingness to pay at different stages of the booking funnel and that AI pricing engines which ignore these behavioral dimensions routinely suppress conversion or trigger demand destruction. Our proposed framework integrates behavioral signals into AI feature engineering arguing that affective pricing cues cancellation-loss framing and social validation mechanisms can be systematically deployed to improve both conversion rates and revenue per available unit without exploiting consumers in ethically problematic ways. The chapter contributes to the growing literature on neuroeconomic applications in hospitality management while offering practical direction to revenue managers who seek to humanize not merely automate their pricing decisions.

The main argument is that, designed appropriately as part of the broader marketing stack, chatbots and CAI no longer represent a cost-reduction service channel but rather a strategic customer engagement platform, full of data.

43f02e9dd2362d62f0781c1271492951a9157aa0.abstract: Power-system operation is safety-critical: personnel integrate data, alarms, outages, switching requests, contingency analyses, grid-code rules, and cybersecurity constraints. This review assesses evidence, rechecked through May 31, 2026, on GenAI and large language models (LLMs) for operator support. It covers research, reports, standards, regulations, preprints, and industry initiatives, distinguishing retrieval-grounded systems, domain-adapted LLMs, time-series foundation models, tool-using agents, and digital-twin verification. It proposes a supervised assistant in which the LLM orchestrates and explains but is not operational truth. Near-term uses include document retrieval, regulatory interpretation, training, summaries, and explanations of approved calculations. Evidence does not support autonomous transmission-level actions. Deployment requires traceable sources, current models, restricted tools, cybersecurity boundaries, adversarial testing, human approval, and audit trails.

title: AI-Driven Distributed No-Wait Flow Shop Scheduling for Sustainable Energy-Aware Manufacturing Systems

d9b0f4862ffea1e45716990a59652306558d70c3.abstract: The rapid evolution of smart manufacturing and Industry 5.0 has heightened interest in sustainable and intelligent scheduling approaches. The distributed no-wait flow shop scheduling (DNWFSP) problem is a complex combinatorial optimization problem that simultaneously involves assigning jobs to plants and sequencing them on machines. This problem becomes even more challenging when energy and environmental objectives are incorporated. This chapter proposes an AI-based distributed flow shop scheduling framework for energy-efficient manufacturing systems. The objective is to minimize total energy consumption. The approach relies primarily on deep reinforcement learning, specifically the Deep Q-Network (DQN), to learn an optimal decision-making policy in a dynamic and uncertain environment. The DQN model allows scheduling decisions to be adapted in real time based on the state of the production system. Experimental results show that the proposed approach significantly improves energy efficiency and resource utilization compared to conventional scheduling methods.

7c511103dc7bb5d22ff06c9abc63879ce415e340.abstract: Since the building sector contributes significantly to carbon emissions worldwide, sophisticated methods are required for precise forecasting and efficient reduction. The use of machine learning (ML) approaches for carbon emission prediction across the construction lifecycle—including material manufacturing, transportation, on-site activities, and operations—is examined in this chapter. Regression, artificial neural networks, support vector machines, and ensemble learning are among the machine learning models that are rigorously examined, with an emphasis on how well they can handle complicated, nonlinear datasets. In order to facilitate real-time monitoring and decision assistance, the chapter delves deeper into the integration of machine learning (ML) with digital technologies, such as building information modeling (BIM), the Internet of Things (IoT), and digital twins. Supported by case examples, a conceptual framework is put forth to direct ML-driven carbon mitigation methods. Future research directions and challenges are also covered.

title: Machine Learning in Hydrogen Production and Combustion

396533e60035866b42defb080e313a182f64fdcf.abstract: The transition to a green hydrogen economy is impeded by two computational and physical challenges: huge overpotential losses in water electrolysis and thermoacoustic/flashback instabilities when hydrogen combusts directly. The use of conventional high-throughput screening of electrocatalysts relying on Density Functional Theory is computationally infeasible in large compositional spaces, while H flame direct numerical simulation suffers from extreme multi-scale turbulence-chemistry interactions. In this chapter, we offer a combined machine learning method, integrating material-level electrocatalyst discovery with system-level combustion control. Firstly, we test ensemble tree models and Graph Neural Networks for forecasting adsorption free energies at transition metal hydroxides, alloys and high-entropy surfaces. Then we describe reduced-order surrogate models, like CNN-LSTMs, Autoencoders and PINNs to combust hydrogen-fueled internal combustion engines and gas turbines for prediction of flashback, identification of thermoacoustic modes, and reduction of NOx emissions in real time.

title: AI-Driven Lightweight Conductive Materials for Energy-Efficient Embedded IoT Electronics in Aerospace

The chapter also explores intelligent battery management, fault diagnosis, digital twins, smart grids, Internet of Things, and Vehicle-to-Grid integration for future energy systems.

title: How to Optimize Electric Vehicles Using Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML)

7136bf72ac9299b116ba5c8813a99f469355cc31.abstract: Optimizing electric vehicles (EVs) through Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) is critical for addressing adoption barriers such as range anxiety and battery degradation. This chapter explores the transition from static, rule-based systems to dynamic, self-learning frameworks across Battery Management Systems (BMS), Predictive Energy Management (PEM), and Eco-Driving and Auxiliary (EDA) systems. By leveraging advanced methodologies like Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL), Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks, and Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs), these intelligent systems can enhance energy efficiency by up to 30% and extend battery life by nearly 40%. title: Hybrid TCN-ExtraTrees Framework for Lithium-Ion Battery State-of-Health Classification in Indian Electric Vehicles

e9afe305db4f44eeadf11aafb47f5676e6b636dc.abstract: The rapid growth of Electric Vehicles (EVs) in emerging economies of the world, such as India, has created a pressing demand for Battery Health Monitoring Systems. While Lithium-ion batteries, being the most common power source for EVs which operates in a range of environmental and operating conditions, their performance is affected by various environmental factors. Therefore, estimating the State of Health (SOH) is crucial to evaluating the aging of the batteries. This chapter proposes an artificial intelligence–based framework to address the heterogeneous conditions of the Indian EV ecosystem by utilizing a Temporal Convolutional Network (TCN) and the ExtraTrees ensemble classifier. In addition to conventional battery parameters, environmental stress factors are also incorporated into the framework using meteorological data obtained from the NASA POWER database. Experimental evaluation was carried out and obtained an accuracy of 91.50% and a value of 0.9772 for the AUC-ROC metric, proving the effectiveness of the proposed framework for reliable battery health estimation.

title: AI and Machine Learning Approaches to Address Cybersecurity Challenges in Smart Grid Systems

0b9ba87f4a19e4d12b8440a82ac46d2c3f3b2901.abstract: Smart grid systems have been utilized with artificial intelligence (AI) which has substantially improved their efficiency and reliability. Nevertheless, with the development of smart grids into more intricate, networked, and data-intensive systems, a smart grid is becoming more susceptible to cybercrime. The chapter handles the problem of cybersecurity available within smart grid systems shedding light on the especial vulnerabilities that lies in the fact that they are digital and automated. It talks about the application of AI-based solutions to deal with such risks and it focuses on approaches that include anomaly detection, real-time threat responsiveness, and forecast risk. Besides, the chapter is also about AI aimed at protecting the communication network and providing more effective identification processes, and autonomic safe work. Through interpretation of case studies and projections in the real world, this paper gives a holistic idea of how AI can enhance the cybersecurity infrastructure in smart grid infrastructures.

title: Detection of Anomalies and Electricity Theft in Smart Grids Using Variational Autoencoders (VAE) and Time Series Analysis
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI-Driven Sustainable Energy Systems
1733456c27aaf37eee6c7d368568452fec41f37d.abstract: The proposed approach to detecting electricity theft and abnormal consumption in smart grids using a variable-parameter autoencoder is presented. With the introduction of smart meters, traditional verification methods struggle to handle large volumes of data and often miss instances of fraud disguised as normal consumption. The proposed model combines convolutional and LSTM layers to capture both local patterns and long-term dependencies, feeding the data into a variable-parameter autoencoder that models the probability distribution of normal consumption behavior. Experiments were conducted on open datasets containing labeled hourly consumption data with various theft types, including mechanical tampering and data manipulation. Preprocessing included normalization and extraction of dynamic features, such as volatility and interphase correlations. Detection performance was evaluated using precision-recall curves and the F-score due to strong class imbalance.

title: Investigation of Vulnerabilities of Machine Learning Models to Adversarial Attacks in Smart Grid Forecasting Systems
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI-Driven Sustainable Energy Systems
a4c69d2d3f388b09d23e5a415fd3321cd4c255fd.abstract: This article examines how the use of machine learning in Smart Grid forecasting turns predictive models into targets of cyberattacks. Small, carefully chosen distortions of telemetry, training data, or federated updates can shift forecasts of load, renewable generation, reserves, and grid stability without clear signs of failure. The review systematizes adversarial attack scenarios by model access, impact goal, lifecycle stage, and implementation level in digital infrastructure. It also highlights what makes energy time series different from images and ordinary tabular data: temporal structure, cross-channel consistency, and physical plausibility must be preserved. The paper analyzes resilience measures — anomaly detection, adversarial training, secure aggregation, physics-informed hybrids, and data integrity monitoring — with attention to computational cost and real-time use. Further research should focus on realistic black-box attacks, cascading effects, and engineering criteria for trusting predictive services.

title: Algorithmic Persuasion and the Commodification of the Indian Child Consumer
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Governing Childhood in the Age of AI
7ef08bed984a79d99131ec55e78d0e3fafb5c13c.abstract: Artificial intelligence has reshaped digital persuasion, placing children at the center of AI-driven consumption in India's platform economy. Gamification, recommender systems, and synthetic influencers exploit cognitive immaturity and emotional vulnerability in ways existing consumer and advertising laws cannot address. This chapter argues that AI-driven child-targeted marketing constitutes a distinct unfair trade practice, commodifying childhood itself. Grounded in consumer law and constitutional principles under Articles 14, 19, and 21, it advances a case for statutory limits prioritizing child dignity and autonomy.

title: Algorithmic Childhood
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Governing Childhood in the Age of AI
24a3c19b0daa4623298ba63af7df9b13718df0f6.abstract: This chapter looks at the idea of Algorithmic Childhood, which looks at how AI-driven personalization, algorithmic exposure, datafication, and behavioural nudging transform children online experiences and consumer identities. The digital platforms are relentlessly gathering and analysing data on children in order to customize their content, ads, and interactions and in the process, there are no sharp lines between play, learning, and commercial persuasion. Although the advantages of personalization are educational and age-related, they also contribute to making children more vulnerable because of their poor cognitive and emotional development. The chapter is a synthesis of interdisciplinary literature that identifies ethical issues, asymmetry of power, and the gap of the currently existing regulatory frameworks. It calls to the child-cantered policies of governing aimed to guarantee transparency and accountability, digital well-being, the safety of children, and safeguarding of child rights through AI-mediated markets.

title: Algorithmic Entrapment
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Governing Childhood in the Age of AI
9a1a337e1b2937ac4af2d2775b27805a3ce8499b.abstract: Artificial intelligence has transformed social media into adaptive persuasion systems that learn from and optimize for each child's behavior. This chapter shows how AI-driven curation undermines parental authority through qualitative analysis of Slovenian parents. Based on 14 in-depth interviews with parents of 22 children, we identify “algorithmic entrapment,” where engagement-maximizing systems override parental boundaries, exploit developmental vulnerabilities, and foster dependencies resistant to intervention. Parents recognized addiction-like symptoms but had a limited understanding of underlying AI mechanisms such as recommendation systems, predictive analytics, variable rewards, and personalized optimization. A “Surveillance Capitalism and Childhood” framework is proposed to explain how data extraction and attention monetization conflict with children's developmental needs. Protecting children requires shifting beyond parental responsibility toward governance solutions, including transparency mandates, limits on persuasive AI targeting minors, and independent audits.

title: From Digital Safety to Digital Flourishing
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Governing Childhood in the Age of AI
03a959e7ca0c73de400bfd81a13b9caeff54cbf1.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly transforming children's digital environments, reshaping how they learn, interact, and participate as consumers. While existing scholarship and regulation largely emphasize digital safety—focusing on privacy protection and risk mitigation—there is limited attention to how AI can actively promote children's developmental well-being. This case study–based chapter advances a shift from digital safety to digital flourishing by examining how child-centered AI systems can support cognitive growth, social-emotional development, and ethical agency. Drawing on interdisciplinary literature and empirical case analyses of socially assistive robots, adaptive learning platforms, and conversational AI systems, the chapter develops a Developmental Flourishing Framework integrating developmental psychology, children's rights principles, and ethical marketing considerations. The analysis highlights both opportunities and structural risks, including algorithmic bias, surveillance practices, and persuasive design.

title: AI Literacy as Consumer Immunity in Children
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Governing Childhood in the Age of AI
9551deacb2f585906f3298c74c3b05f1921605f7.abstract: Whether driven by regulation or the market, pure protective responses are becoming less tenable as AI systems become more integrated into commercial ecosystems surrounding children. The future of child digital well-being will hinge on not just stronger regulations and more ethical platform design, but also critically aware young users capable to interpret and navigate algorithmic environments with informed scepticism and reflective agency. This chapter advances the notion of AI literacy as consumer immunity, putting forward a timely and actionable framework for educators, designers, policymakers and researchers interested in aligning technology innovation with ethical responsibility to children. Protecting the child consumer in the age of A.I. ultimately means pursuing both solutions: Creating safer systems while also fortifying the young brains that make their way through them.

title: AI Literacy
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Governing Childhood in the Age of AI
87a810168d220e42586510068471834bc1db6970.abstract: Children in contemporary school settings are daily consumers of AI-generated content — whether they know it or not. Recommendation feeds, synthetic images, AI-drafted text, and algorithmic advertising have become routine features of childhood digital experience, yet most K–12 curricula offer little preparation for navigating these environments critically. This chapter argues that schools bear a genuine responsibility to address this gap through deliberate, grade-appropriate AI literacy education oriented not merely toward using AI tools, but toward questioning and evaluating what those tools produce. Drawing on recent empirical work and theoretical scholarship across AI literacy, media education, and ethics, the chapter traces a developmentally staged curriculum pathway from early childhood awareness through secondary-level civic and ethical reasoning, while also highlighting key challenges in implementation such as teacher readiness, assessment alignment, and the limited geographic distribution of existing research.

title: Curriculum Development for AI Literacy in Schools
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Governing Childhood in the Age of AI
48f5f323ea3fb2f7789d2937410b6f74e253e184.abstract: Artificial intelligence has infiltrated the digital landscape of children at an extremely fast rate, affecting the way children learn, communicate and access information. This chapter in the book makes a case in favor of an all-encompassing curriculum in AI literacy that will help children understand how to critically analyze the systems of algorithms, defend against subtle persuasion, and identify fake media. Based on the Critical Media Literacy Theory, Persuasion Knowledge Theory, Socio-Technical Systems Theory and the Digital Resilience Frameworks, describes a modular, age-based curriculum between primary-level and secondary education. Experiential learning, gamification, and project-based assessments are some of the pedagogical strategies favored with the help of teacher training and alignment of policies. Finally, the chapter makes AI literacy a key factor to creating digitally resilient citizens who are capable of operating in algorithmically mediated spaces in a responsible, reflective and ethical manner.

title: Curriculum Development for Schools to Teach Children How to Recognize and Critically Evaluate AI Content
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Governing Childhood in the Age of AI
eabdf13bce65d9c835bad254e966a1d5672132c4.abstract: Children today are growing up in digital environments where Artificial Intelligence (AI) plays a central yet often invisible role in shaping their experiences. From personalized recommendations and AI-generated academic assistance to targeted advertising and algorithmically curated content intelligent systems influence how children access information, form preferences, and make decisions. This chapter argues that AI literacy must be recognized as an essential component of contemporary school education. Drawing on an interdisciplinary review of literature in AI literacy, media studies, and education, the chapter proposes a curriculum-oriented framework based on three interconnected dimensions: operational, sociocultural and critical literacy. In response, it introduces a practical pedagogical approach centered on “questioning the machine,” encouraging students to develop habits of inquiry, reflection and ethical awareness in their interactions with AI-driven content.

title: Play, Screen, and Sensibility
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Governing Childhood in the Age of AI
419ae53555cf9525f8072bd48eced60adce44aa6.abstract: This chapter examines how early childhood digital literacy should be understood not merely as technical skill, but as an ethical, relational, and pedagogical process. Focusing on children in their first years, it explores how screens increasingly shape curiosity, play, attention, and emotional development. The chapter argues that ethical sensibility must be nurtured alongside digital engagement through adult mediation, reflective dialogue, and balanced forms of play. It highlights the roles of parents and teachers in guiding children to interpret digital stories, games, and apps with empathy, patience, and moral awareness. Ultimately, it proposes that ethical digital literacy in early childhood begins not with control, but with care, conversation, and thoughtful participation.

title: Novelty or eeriness? Investigating consumer responses to AI-generated product images through expectancy violation theory
container-title: Journal of Research in Interactive Marketing
887864754512a1ae8f592d2397ed290befbca8bd.abstract: Purpose Drawing on Expectancy Violation Theory, this study examines how product image creator identity (AI vs. human) influences purchase intentions and the underlying psychological mechanisms. Design/methodology/approach Three online experiments examined consumers' attitudes toward AI-generated product images and purchase intentions toward the featured products, assessed how these evaluations deviated from expectations associated with human-created images, and identified conditions under which artificial intelligence (AI) imagery was more or less effective in shaping consumer responses. Data were analyzed in Statistical Package for the Social Sciences using Multivariate Analysis of Variance and Multivariate Analysis of Covariance, with serial and moderated mediation analyses conducted using the PROCESS macro. Findings Consumers consistently prefer human-created product images and perceive them as more novel, whereas AI-generated images evoke greater eeriness. Perceived novelty, eeriness, positive and negative expectancy violations, and attitudes mediate the relationship between image creator identity and purchase intention. Product type serves as a boundary condition, with AI-generated images evaluated more favorably for search products than for experience products. Originality/value This research identifies positive and negative expectancy violations as central psychological mechanisms shaping consumer responses to AI-generated product images. By highlighting product type as a boundary condition, it helps reconcile mixed findings in the AI-generated marketing literature and provides actionable guidance for the strategic use of AI-generated product imagery.

title: Feeling the gap: cognitive-affective divergence in SME managers' Industry 4.0 and sustainability narratives
container-title: European Journal of Innovation Management
cd25d84111e66598609d29a9d0f99afcb5d27ff0.abstract: Purpose The study investigates how small- and medium-sized enterprise (SME) managers perceive and emotionally engage with environmental and social sustainability in the context of Industry 4.0 adoption. Using semi-structured interviews combined with multimodal sentiment analysis (speech prosody and emotional language), we aim to uncover implicit hesitancy, dissonance, and conceptual fragmentation that traditional methods fail to detect, thereby offering new insights for policy design and corporate social responsibility research in structurally disadvantaged regions. Design/methodology/approach The manuscript employs a mixed-methods design integrating semi-structured interviews with multimodal sentiment analysis. Twenty SMEs in Southern Italy, selected through structured sampling, participated in interviews exploring Industry 4.0 investments, environmental practices, and social sustainability. Recorded interviews underwent (1) thematic and content analysis for explicit responses, and (2) Hume AI-based prosody and emotional language analysis to detect implicit emotional engagement. This dual approach captures both declared positions and underlying affective reactions, enabling the identification of dissonance between cognitive awareness and emotional investment across environmental and social sustainability dimensions. Findings Environmental sustainability is widely recognized (90% of firms), yet only 60% link Industry 4.0 investments to environmental goals, and key performance indicator use remains inconsistent. Social sustainability reveals a striking “feeling gap”: while 90% express willingness to invest, conceptual fragmentation prevails, with no standardized metrics. Sentiment analysis exposes declining concentration, rising confusion, and subtle annoyance when discussing social topics, contrasting with calm, determined engagement for technological investments. Emotional prosody thus uncovers hidden dissonance between declared awareness and authentic affective engagement, particularly for social sustainability, which remains intuitively rather than analytically grounded in SME decision-making. Originality/value This study introduces the “feeling gap” concept, distinguishing cognitive awareness from emotional engagement in SME sustainability practices. Methodologically, it pioneers multimodal sentiment analysis (speech prosody and emotional language) in Industry 4.0 and CSR research, moving beyond declared positions to detect hidden hesitancy and dissonance. Empirically, it focuses on a structurally disadvantaged region often overlooked in favor of large enterprises or developed economies. The findings demonstrate that policy design must address not only informational and financial barriers but also affective and motivational dimensions, particularly for social sustainability, which lacks standardized metrics and genuine emotional resonance among SME managers.

title: Explainable AI-based framework for 3D structural as-built modeling of aging buildings in Korea using laser scanning
container-title: Engineering, Construction and Architectural Management
9d0f972f52a37add6c936521dbd3ddf06dde8a83.abstract: Purpose This study proposes a framework for automatically generating 3D structural as-built models of aging buildings by predicting the structural dimensions of members concealed behind finishes using laser scanning and machine learning, particularly when original construction drawings are unavailable. Design/methodology/approach Laser scanning captures building geometry but includes both structural components and non-structural finishes (e.g. plaster), making it unsuitable for directly extracting structural dimensions. To address this, the proposed framework extracts geometric features from point clouds and employs machine learning techniques to predict structural dimensions of columns, beams, walls and slabs. Six machine learning models – Random Forest, XGBoost, LightGBM, CatBoost, Linear Regression and Support Vector Regression (SVR) – were trained using data collected on 1,560 column elements, 2,875 beam elements, 870 wall elements and 148 slab elements across 50 buildings and validated through two real-world case studies. Findings The best-performing model achieved MAPE of 10.51% for column width (95%CI: 8.47–12.71), 12.98% for column depth (95% CI: 10.86–15.41), 14.91% for beam width (95% CI: 13.63–16.15), 18.91% for beam depth (95% CI: 17.94–19.90), 10.42% for walls (95% CI: 8.89–12.00) and 10.70% for slabs (95% CI: 7.11–14.50). The predicted dimensions enabled reconstruction of 3D structural as-built models without relying on original drawings; the estimates are intended for planning-stage use. Practical implications The framework provides a non-destructive, full-coverage estimate of structural member dimensions that would otherwise require original drawings or local removal of finishes. In practice, it is intended to reduce reliance on destructive investigation and, through the SHAP analysis, indicates where confirmatory openings could be prioritized, thereby supporting planning-stage decisions for the maintenance and retrofitting of buildings whose drawings are missing or outdated. Originality/value This study is among the first to formulate the discrepancy between laser-scanned surface geometry and concealed structural dimensions as a prediction problem and to propose a framework that returns the predicted dimensions to a 3D structural as-built model. Machine learning provides the enabling component, and explainability is used to direct in situ verification rather than as a methodological contribution in itself.

title: Adaptive Explainability for XR-Assisted Predictive Maintenance in the Industrial Metaverse
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Enhancing the Industrial Metaverse With Extended Reality
b146dcaf8f19ea21cf4d2a218e3a890e21f14f80.abstract: In Industry 5.0, XR-assisted predictive maintenance systems increasingly combine immersive visualisation with AI-powered diagnostics. However, many established explainable AI (XAI) approaches are based on desktop-oriented models and do not fully address the needs of Industrial Metaverse settings. Operators differ in expertise and operational risk, yet XR systems often provide the same explanations to everyone. This can increase cognitive load, reduce situational awareness, and result in inappropriate trust in AI-assisted decisions. This chapter proposes a human-centred adaptive explainability framework for XR-assisted predictive maintenance in the Industrial Metaverse. It adapts explanation, presentation, interaction, and guidance to operator expertise and operational criticality, guided by cognitive fit, risk-proportional disclosure, and interaction economy. A conceptual bearing-failure scenario illustrates different explanation strategies for novice and expert technicians. The chapter also considers robotic anomaly management and energy infrastructure monitoring as extensions.

title: Enhancing the Industrial Metaverse With Extended Reality
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Enhancing the Industrial Metaverse With Extended Reality
8c9989343b1d8ff24876fc27926ed580f327cbc9.abstract: The convergence of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Extended Reality (XR) is transforming industrial work by integrating intelligent decision-making, immersive technologies, and digital twins into human-centered workplaces. This review synthesizes research from Industry 4.0/5.0, digital twins, XR applications, and organizational studies to develop a unified understanding of AI-XR convergence. It proposes three frameworks—Industrial Metaverse Work Architecture (IMWA), AI-XR Industrial Transformation Framework (AXITF), and Human-AI-XR Integration Continuum (HAXIC)—to explain technological, operational, and organizational transformation. The chapter further presents theoretical propositions, governance imperatives, implementation strategies, and future research directions, providing a comprehensive foundation for responsible, human-centric industrial metaverse adoption.

title: Integrating XR, AI, Digital Twins, and IIoT in the Industrial Metaverse
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Enhancing the Industrial Metaverse With Extended Reality
fbf2ccf62346b15568a02d6b5e5729370294b911.abstract: This chapter examines the Industrial Metaverse as the convergence of Extended Reality (XR), Artificial Intelligence (AI), Digital Twins, and the Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) into persistent, immersive, and intelligent industrial ecosystems. Based on a structured narrative review, the chapter proposes a five-layer integration architecture and positions it against RAMI 4.0, IIRA, ISO 23247, and cyber-physical system models. It specifies synchronization requirements for XR-enabled Digital Twins, maps threats and security controls to each architectural layer, and reviews applications in manufacturing, energy, healthcare, and logistics. The chapter also examines generative AI, industrial foundation models, edge AI, and blockchain, together with their risks, and addresses governance, regulation, and human-machine collaboration. It concludes with an implementation pathway and research directions for secure, trustworthy, and human-centric Industrial Metaverse ecosystems aligned with Industry 5.0.

title: XR-Enabled Moodle Learning Ecosystems for the Industrial Metaverse
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Enhancing the Industrial Metaverse With Extended Reality
02afab14813059458f1c623082082cd38c0ca92f.abstract: This chapter, per the authors, presents a conceptual framework for using Moodle as the learning orchestration layer for XR-enabled workforce training in the industrial metaverse. It synthesizes recent research on extended reality, digital twins, artificial intelligence, learning analytics, and cybersecurity awareness to identify a gap between immersive industrial training prototypes and LMS-based evidence, assessment, and governance. The chapter proposes the XR-Moodle Industrial Learning Ecosystem (XMILE), which links Moodle courses, XR scenarios, digital twin states, AI-supported analytics, and cybersecurity controls. It explains the model's layers, data flows, use cases, evaluation metrics, and implementation roadmap for universities, technical training centers, and industrial organizations. The contribution is a practical structure for designing measurable, secure, and role-based training that supports skill transfer, cyber hygiene, and instructor decision-making.

title: AI as therapist or assistant? Opportunities and boundaries of artificial intelligence in mental health care
container-title: Mental Health and Social Inclusion
d8ff61e9a4fc5950274fbbae98c4af08416fbf29.abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine where generative artificial intelligence (AI) may add value in mental health care, where its clinical limits remain and how human oversight should change as AI assumes greater responsibility. Design/methodology/approach This opinion piece draws on recent randomized trials, systematic reviews, safety evaluations and international guidance on conversational AI in mental health. The evidence is interpreted through a three-level framework: supportive self-management, clinician-augmented care and autonomous clinical care. Findings AI-supported interventions can improve symptoms of depression and anxiety in some settings and may widen access to low-intensity support. However, evidence remains heterogeneous and important concerns persist around suicide-risk responses, privacy, bias, over-reliance and accountability. Current evidence supports AI more strongly as an adjunct than as an autonomous therapist. Social implications Access alone should not be mistaken for inclusion. Safe mental health AI also requires attention to digital access, language, culture, affordability and routes to human care. Originality/value The paper proposes a practical clinical hierarchy in which the evidence threshold, regulatory scrutiny and human oversight increase with the clinical responsibility assumed by AI.

title: Practice Briefing: From automation to delegation – governing generative AI in property investment
container-title: Journal of Property Investment & Finance
0d8441e184bb520c85f45164a8740e5739b4e1e5.abstract: Purpose Most real estate organisations approach artificial intelligence with the question “what can we automate?” This paper argues that the framing is wrong for generative AI, whose highest-value uses in property investment are not the automation of known processes but the delegation of judgement-laden work – and that the industry's default safeguard, “a human in the loop”, is not a governance strategy. Design/methodology/approach A practice briefing combining the management literature on delegation and recent evidence on human–AI complementarity with the authors' experience of three years of executive education and advisory work with senior real estate professionals. Findings Generative AI creates most value where neither the process nor the output can be fully specified in advance – precisely where automation-era governance fails. Uniform human review predictably degrades into rubber-stamping as volumes grow. Effective governance separates two questions: what kind of work is being transferred, and how much the outcome matters. Practical implications A two-axis classification (is the process known? Is the output verifiable?) Sorts any task into one of four working modes – automate, assist, structure, delegate – and an accountability ladder scales oversight from logging to full human decision-making. Investment teams can apply the framework immediately by classifying tasks rather than jobs and reallocating scarce review capacity to where consequence is genuine. Originality/value The paper reframes AI adoption as a delegation-design problem continuous with management skills the industry already possesses, separates task classification from governance intensity and names the failure mode – accountability theatre – that uniform human review creates.

title: Revisiting new accounting history four decades on: reconciling traditional and critical historiographies
container-title: Accounting, Auditing & Accountability Journal
9c53032a457a8a6764279c767e5a11ed4b534fd4.abstract: Purpose Revisiting debates in New Accounting History four decades on, this paper advances accounting historiography through the development of a Neo-Critical Accounting History (NCAH) framework that systematically integrates the strengths of traditional accounting history with the theoretically informed and critical orientation of new accounting history. In answering the “how” question, the framework offers an analytical pathway through which accounting historians may proceed with a rigorous and socially attuned mode of inquiry. Design/methodology/approach The study is grounded in critical accounting approach, in particular, Habermas's method of rational reconstruction (Held, 1980) providing the philosophical foundation for proposing an agenda advancing framework for NCAH. The framework integrates the methods of historical academic monograph with key features of both traditional and new accounting history. Findings The proposed NCAH framework is articulated across three interrelated dimensions. First, it integrates traditional and critical historiography by combining historical rigour with critical depth to recover marginalised voices and enhance contextual analysis. Second, it advances epistemic pluralisation through rigorous source critique, methodological triangulation, and engagement with diverse archival and counter-accounts, thereby addressing archival silences, partialities, and power relations. Third, it embraces theoretical openness and contemporary relevance, enabling historical inquiry into emerging accounting-related topics aligned with broader societal and ethical concerns, and strengthening accounting history's engagement with contemporary scholarly and public debates. Originality/value The manuscript demonstrates how traditional and new accounting history approaches may be systematically integrated, including through approaches inspired by abductive reasoning. Within this framing, narrative is positioned not as an end in itself, but rather as a point of departure for deeper theoretical interpretation and historical analysis. In doing so, NCAH reconciles historical and archival rigour with theoretical openness, thereby enhancing the analytical depth of the discipline and its capacity to contribute to interdisciplinary scholarship, societal reflection, and professional practice.

title: Contact and constructionalization: the emergence of a clause-final adverb construction in Singaporean varieties
container-title: Cognitive Linguistics
1e82b80c5588957c46438a0a071b1e2452a2b95d.abstract: Abstract Clause-final adverbs such as already , also , and only have been widely recognized as characteristic features of Singapore English. By comparison, parallel clause-final adverbial patterns in Singapore Mandarin remain underexplored, despite being similarly prominent in everyday speech. This paper addresses this gap by presenting the first construction-based analysis of clause-final adverbs in Singapore Mandarin and by examining them alongside the use of clause-final adverbs in Singapore English. Based on the Diasystematic Construction Grammar framework, we propose that sustained bilingualism in Singapore has given rise to a stance-oriented clause-final constructional slot, which supports three distinct developmental trajectories in Singapore Mandarin. Through a detailed analysis of three adverbs, 才 cái ‘only’, 先 xiān ‘first’, and 也是 yěshì ‘also’, we illustrate trajectories of decline, functional strengthening, and innovation. The findings demonstrate that clause-final adverbs in Singapore Mandarin are systematically organized within a constructional network shaped by both bilingual usage patterns and ongoing changes in Singapore’s multilingual linguistic environment.

title: Childhood Exposure to General Anesthesia for Surgery: Identification of a Subtle Postoperative Cognitive Phenotype
container-title: Anesthesiology
bd2d5293ea5b2cf3a3290d324042562ada1a7b3e.abstract: Background: Early-life exposure to general anesthesia has not been consistently associated with overall cognitive deficits, yet its impact on executive functions and visuo-spatial processing remains unclear. The primary objective was to assess executive function performance, according to general anesthesia exposure for surgery. The secondary objectives were to explore distinct cognitive profiles and their associated factors, as well as to examine visuo-spatial attention as a complementary domain. Methods: In this ambidirectional cohort study, 77 children aged 9 to 11 yr, with or without previous general anesthesia exposure for surgery, completed a cognitive battery yielding eight cognitive measures assessing inhibitory control, cognitive flexibility, working memory, and visuo-spatial attention. Measures were analyzed using a linear mixed-effects model. Exploratory latent profile analysis was used to identify cognitive performance profiles. Results: No significant main effect of general anesthesia exposure for surgery was observed (chi-square[1] = 0.01; P = 0.92), indicating comparable overall executive function performance between exposed (mean age at exposure, 4.47 ± 3.00 yr) and nonexposed. Latent profile analysis identified two executive function profiles: efficient and vulnerable executive control. General anesthesia exposure was associated with slightly higher odds of belonging to the vulnerable profile group (odds ratio, 1.16; 95% CI; 1.151 to 1.159; P < 0.001). Regarding visuo-spatial attention, general anesthesia–exposed participants showed higher global–local precedence measures (estimate, 0.53; 95% CI, 0.04 to 1.01; P = 0.036). Conclusions: Early childhood exposure to general anesthesia was not associated with reduced overall executive function. However, a potential postoperative cognitive phenotype is suggested by a higher likelihood to belonging to a vulnerable executive control profile, together with greater visuo-spatial global–local precedence.

title: Real-Time Memory-Bounded A/RED: Discovering Rare Relevant Classes in Streaming Data
container-title: International Journal of Semantic Computing
2d028768c0a5115392a3a7558a52fd6b41784c6e.abstract: We present a memory-bounded, real-time anomalous/relevant event detection (A/RED) system for indefinitely long data streams. Extending prior work, our algorithm maintains bounded memory using a circular buffer of queried points and accelerates nearest-neighbor search via ball trees, reducing complexity from [Formula: see text] to [Formula: see text] per point. Small clusters are periodically merged to control model size, while a tunable paranoia parameter [Formula: see text] regulates query rate. Evaluated on synthetic (NICE), skewed MNIST, extended MNIST (EMNIST), and industrial inspection (MVTec) datasets as streams, A/RED achieves near-perfect relevant recall and query precision on well-separated data, and significantly outperforms random querying on real-world distributions — discovering rare relevant classes with reduced user burden. This work enables scalable, human-in-the-loop anomaly detection in continuous, high-volume sensor environments.

title: Memory Overlap Shapes General and Specific Memory Differently in Adolescents and Adults
c69f6a6066ff14bb65d718133fa8a366d2c787aa.abstract: Over time we accumulate many interrelated memories which we draw upon to remember both generalities and specifics of our experience. While both aspects of memory improve through childhood, their maturation into adolescence remains poorly understood. Here, we compared how 39 adolescents (12-13 years old) and 36 adults managed differing levels of relatedness (“overlap”) among learned associations to remember shared (general) and unique (specific) features. Across age groups, greater overlap boosted memory for shared features but hindered memory for specifics. However, adolescents showed a reduced benefit of overlap for shared feature memory, suggesting they generalized across related memories differently than adults. Adolescents were also slower than adults to recognize unique features of highly overlapping memories, consistent with prolonged refinement of specific memory. Our results reveal continued maturation of both general and specific memory into adolescence while demonstrating how the overlaps among our experiences shape what we remember.

title: Feeling the gap: cognitive-affective divergence in SME managers' Industry 4.0 and sustainability narratives
container-title: European Journal of Innovation Management
cd25d84111e66598609d29a9d0f99afcb5d27ff0.abstract: Purpose The study investigates how small- and medium-sized enterprise (SME) managers perceive and emotionally engage with environmental and social sustainability in the context of Industry 4.0 adoption. Using semi-structured interviews combined with multimodal sentiment analysis (speech prosody and emotional language), we aim to uncover implicit hesitancy, dissonance, and conceptual fragmentation that traditional methods fail to detect, thereby offering new insights for policy design and corporate social responsibility research in structurally disadvantaged regions. Design/methodology/approach The manuscript employs a mixed-methods design integrating semi-structured interviews with multimodal sentiment analysis. Twenty SMEs in Southern Italy, selected through structured sampling, participated in interviews exploring Industry 4.0 investments, environmental practices, and social sustainability. Recorded interviews underwent (1) thematic and content analysis for explicit responses, and (2) Hume AI-based prosody and emotional language analysis to detect implicit emotional engagement. This dual approach captures both declared positions and underlying affective reactions, enabling the identification of dissonance between cognitive awareness and emotional investment across environmental and social sustainability dimensions. Findings Environmental sustainability is widely recognized (90% of firms), yet only 60% link Industry 4.0 investments to environmental goals, and key performance indicator use remains inconsistent. Social sustainability reveals a striking “feeling gap”: while 90% express willingness to invest, conceptual fragmentation prevails, with no standardized metrics. Sentiment analysis exposes declining concentration, rising confusion, and subtle annoyance when discussing social topics, contrasting with calm, determined engagement for technological investments. Emotional prosody thus uncovers hidden dissonance between declared awareness and authentic affective engagement, particularly for social sustainability, which remains intuitively rather than analytically grounded in SME decision-making. Originality/value This study introduces the “feeling gap” concept, distinguishing cognitive awareness from emotional engagement in SME sustainability practices. Methodologically, it pioneers multimodal sentiment analysis (speech prosody and emotional language) in Industry 4.0 and CSR research, moving beyond declared positions to detect hidden hesitancy and dissonance. Empirically, it focuses on a structurally disadvantaged region often overlooked in favor of large enterprises or developed economies. The findings demonstrate that policy design must address not only informational and financial barriers but also affective and motivational dimensions, particularly for social sustainability, which lacks standardized metrics and genuine emotional resonance among SME managers.

title: Adaptive Explainability for XR-Assisted Predictive Maintenance in the Industrial Metaverse
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Enhancing the Industrial Metaverse With Extended Reality
b146dcaf8f19ea21cf4d2a218e3a890e21f14f80.abstract: In Industry 5.0, XR-assisted predictive maintenance systems increasingly combine immersive visualisation with AI-powered diagnostics. However, many established explainable AI (XAI) approaches are based on desktop-oriented models and do not fully address the needs of Industrial Metaverse settings. Operators differ in expertise and operational risk, yet XR systems often provide the same explanations to everyone. This can increase cognitive load, reduce situational awareness, and result in inappropriate trust in AI-assisted decisions. This chapter proposes a human-centred adaptive explainability framework for XR-assisted predictive maintenance in the Industrial Metaverse. It adapts explanation, presentation, interaction, and guidance to operator expertise and operational criticality, guided by cognitive fit, risk-proportional disclosure, and interaction economy. A conceptual bearing-failure scenario illustrates different explanation strategies for novice and expert technicians. The chapter also considers robotic anomaly management and energy infrastructure monitoring as extensions.

title: Contact and constructionalization: the emergence of a clause-final adverb construction in Singaporean varieties
container-title: Cognitive Linguistics
1e82b80c5588957c46438a0a071b1e2452a2b95d.abstract: Abstract Clause-final adverbs such as already , also , and only have been widely recognized as characteristic features of Singapore English. By comparison, parallel clause-final adverbial patterns in Singapore Mandarin remain underexplored, despite being similarly prominent in everyday speech. This paper addresses this gap by presenting the first construction-based analysis of clause-final adverbs in Singapore Mandarin and by examining them alongside the use of clause-final adverbs in Singapore English. Based on the Diasystematic Construction Grammar framework, we propose that sustained bilingualism in Singapore has given rise to a stance-oriented clause-final constructional slot, which supports three distinct developmental trajectories in Singapore Mandarin. Through a detailed analysis of three adverbs, 才 cái ‘only’, 先 xiān ‘first’, and 也是 yěshì ‘also’, we illustrate trajectories of decline, functional strengthening, and innovation. The findings demonstrate that clause-final adverbs in Singapore Mandarin are systematically organized within a constructional network shaped by both bilingual usage patterns and ongoing changes in Singapore’s multilingual linguistic environment.

title: Representation of character experience: language choices and similative construal
container-title: Cognitive Semiotics
bf654c649d6ac897df8a5df548f735d164b5d666.abstract: Abstract This paper discusses examples from modernist and contemporary fiction, focusing on two experiential areas – the experience of the flow of time and the felt quality of events and emotions. It proposes a more specific understanding of the role played by figurative imagery, speech representation, and accounts of sensory perception, which can jointly be referred to as modes of representing character experience . The examples selected for analysis go beyond unmarked depictions of actions or events. Rather, they depict narrative scenes where the high intensity of experience calls for language choices going beyond representing ordinary acts and scenes. To account for the experiential intensity of the texts referred to I propose a broad type of figuration, which I refer to as similative . The examples of similative construal discussed in the paper illustrate how textual choices build on representations of attention, fictive events, and fictive conversations in order to render character experiences – embodied, emotional, or both.

title: Harnessing ChatGPT in online higher education: implications and teaching strategies through the lens of the diffusion of innovations theory
container-title: Artificial Intelligence in Education
befa7ca242b61da1df0f8e08cd0796d86d3fedde.abstract: Purpose This exploratory qualitative study aimed to examine the educational implications and practical strategies for using ChatGPT in online higher education, as perceived by faculty, based on diffusion of innovations (DOI) theory. Design/methodology/approach This study employed a qualitative exploratory design to examine faculty perceptions at a US online higher education institution. Nine experienced faculty members were recruited through purposive sampling, with data gathered from an open-ended survey informed by DOI theory and analyzed thematically. Findings The results highlighted themes related to using ChatGPT, such as a potential decline in student learning, its impact on faculty teaching methods and technical issues. It was suggested that guided use could enhance student learning. Strategies for utilizing ChatGPT included assisting faculty with course content and student engagement, reflecting DOI attributes of relative advantage, compatibility and complexity. Research limitations/implications ChatGPT’s adoption in higher education will depend not only on its perceived relative advantage but also on how institutions manage its complexity and make responsible use observable. Strategic pedagogical design, faculty support and policy alignment are essential to ensuring that ChatGPT enhances, rather than diminishes, student learning and academic integrity. Originality/value Generative AI tools are gaining popularity among university students; yet, their integration into higher education is still evolving. This study is significant as it addresses faculty adoption of AI tools like ChatGPT in teaching, providing insights and recommendations for effective integration.

title: LEADING QUESTIONS AS A FACTOR IN THE DISTORTION OF WITNESS MEMORY: A PSYCHOLINGUISTIC PERSPECTIVE ON PRE-TRIAL INVESTIGATION
container-title: Інноваційна наука: пошук відповідей на виклики сучасності: збірник наукових праць з матеріалами VII Міжнародної наукової конференції (м. Харків, Україна; 13 листопада 2026)
b21a3da2e9575501c18297e4ce52c1a35f5bd0d3.abstract: The article examines the influence of leading questions on witness memory and the reliability of testimony obtained during pre-trial investigations. Particular attention is paid to the reconstructive nature of human memory and the relationship between linguistic expression and cognitive processes. The study analyses how lexical choices, grammatical structures, presuppositions, and pragmatic aspects of communication may influence the recollection and interpretation of events. The role of misleading information, suggestibility, and difficulties in identifying the sources of remembered details is considered in the context of eyewitness testimony. The article also examines the practical application of cognitive interviewing, the importance of neutral questioning, and the legal framework governing the examination of witnesses in Ukraine. Particular emphasis is placed on the professional training of future law enforcement officers and the development of their psycholinguistic competence.

title: Decoding decision correctness from EEG under high cognitive workload in virtual reality: implications for collaborative brain-computer interface teams
container-title: Frontiers in Virtual Reality
e2c61608cbfd1ad3de6e77e02188da5672f9f4fe.abstract: Introduction Collaborative Brain-Computer Interfaces (cBCIs) offer a promising mechanism to augment team decision‐making, but existing approaches rely exclusively on evidence available only after a decision has been made and reported, such as reaction time or stated confidence. This limits their use to explaining or discounting a decision after the fact, rather than informing a teams response before it is finalised. We tested whether spatial‐covariance EEG features could instead provide a genuinely pre-emptive signal of an operators decision correctness, available within the response window itself, and whether such a signal depends on cognitive workload. Methods Using a continuous virtual reality target-detection task, participants (N = 23) completed a within-subject visual workload manipulation (High vs. Low), implemented via a Degraded Visual Environment. Results A Riemannian tangent‐space classifier, trained on a strictly motor‐safe EEG window preceding each response, decoded Correct from Incorrect decisions with above‐chance accuracy under High Workload (61.4%, p = .0014, N = 23) but not reliably under Low Workload (N = 17), where near‐ceiling behavioural accuracy left too few error trials for valid classification. Ablation analysis showed the signal was carried predominantly by posterior occipito‐parietal channels, consistent with a perceptual rather than motor origin. At the team level, weighting votes by this pre-emptive neural signal, available before a response is committed, produced substantial accuracy gains on contested (evenly‐split) trials under High Workload (57% to 88% as team size increased from 2 to 16), but was actively detrimental under Low Workload. Discussion Critically, this advantage held even against post‐hoc behavioural signals: confidence was the strongest single team‐level signal overall, but by definition cannot inform a decision still in progress, whereas the neural signal can. These findings indicate that EEG‐based decision‐reliability signals are not a general‐purpose team augmentation tool, but a workload‐conditional one, with clear implications for when and how cBCI systems should be deployed in operational teams.

title: Hippocampal somatostatin neurons gate context generalization during fear memory updating
container-title: Communications Biology
027745ac0a00d5558476491112529c3f53b7b6f3.abstract: Abstract Freezing is used as a readout of fear memory in rodents, but it remains unclear how distinct freezing features reflect discrimination and generalization of threatening and neutral contexts. Using pose-tracking and unsupervised analysis in male and female mice undergoing contextual fear conditioning, we show that fear in neutral a context is expressed through fragmented freezing that resist experience-dependent updating, in contrast with more sustained, uninterrupted, and adaptable freezing in a threatening context. Neuronal recordings revealed that recalling neutral context fear is associated with increased activity of dentate gyrus somatostatin inhibitory neurons (SST INs). Chemogenetic suppression of SST INs during fear memory updating selectively facilitated neutral context freezing adaptation while activation prevented generalization of contextual information by restricting long-term fear reduction in contexts that differed from the updating context. These findings identify DG SST INs as context-specific modulators of fear memory updating and suggest that freezing dynamics serve as a behavioral signature of generalization.

title: Capistrano-geógrafo por Arthur Cezar Ferreira Reis:
Capistrano-geographer by Arthur Cezar Ferreira Reis:
container-title: História da Historiografia: International Journal of Theory and History of Historiography
eac12af3ec52f1a51617951fff84f7ea301128c6.abstract: O objeto estudado no presente artigo se constitui na interface entre o discurso historiográfico e a memória. No Curso Capistrano de Abreu, em 1953, Arthur Cezar Ferreira Reis pronunciou a conferência “Capistrano-geógrafo”, analisando as ligações do autor homenageado com a geografia. Tem-se aqui a intenção de analisar os argumentos do conferencista para estabelecer essa relação e calcular a coerência de seu discurso ao confrontá-lo com a obra de Capistrano. Para além, busca-se pensar esse momento discursivo como o de uma tensão na memória capistraniana, na medida em que o quadro de um Capistrano-historiador, tema central do Curso, é tensionado pela referência à geografia e a um hipotético Capistrano-geógrafo. Chega-se à conclusão de que a conferência de Ferreira Reis, publicada no volume 221 da Revista do IHGB, apesar de desviar a memória capistraniana para a geografia, acaba por afirmar o Capistrano-historiador como precursor de um grupo de historiadores interessados pela geografia como objeto de estudo e percurso de formação.

title: Novelty or eeriness? Investigating consumer responses to AI-generated product images through expectancy violation theory
container-title: Journal of Research in Interactive Marketing
887864754512a1ae8f592d2397ed290befbca8bd.abstract: Purpose Drawing on Expectancy Violation Theory, this study examines how product image creator identity (AI vs. human) influences purchase intentions and the underlying psychological mechanisms. Design/methodology/approach Three online experiments examined consumers' attitudes toward AI-generated product images and purchase intentions toward the featured products, assessed how these evaluations deviated from expectations associated with human-created images, and identified conditions under which artificial intelligence (AI) imagery was more or less effective in shaping consumer responses. Data were analyzed in Statistical Package for the Social Sciences using Multivariate Analysis of Variance and Multivariate Analysis of Covariance, with serial and moderated mediation analyses conducted using the PROCESS macro. Findings Consumers consistently prefer human-created product images and perceive them as more novel, whereas AI-generated images evoke greater eeriness. Perceived novelty, eeriness, positive and negative expectancy violations, and attitudes mediate the relationship between image creator identity and purchase intention. Product type serves as a boundary condition, with AI-generated images evaluated more favorably for search products than for experience products. Originality/value This research identifies positive and negative expectancy violations as central psychological mechanisms shaping consumer responses to AI-generated product images. By highlighting product type as a boundary condition, it helps reconcile mixed findings in the AI-generated marketing literature and provides actionable guidance for the strategic use of AI-generated product imagery.

title: Facilitating Access to Finance in Angola
container-title: Women and Youth Entrepreneurship for Inclusive and Sustainable Global Development
31af3863e28748d73647bcce4982da5c4e526e87.abstract: This study examines capacity-building initiatives within the Envolver project to improve access to finance for micro, small, and medium-sized enterprises in Angola. Emphasizing the role of financial literacy and human capital development, it analyzes training methodologies tailored to diverse stakeholder groups within the financing ecosystem. The study characterizes target audiences, trainer profiles, and pedagogical approaches, highlighting the use of hybrid delivery models and context-specific learning tools. Attention is given to establishing a common language among stakeholders, including entrepreneurs, financial institutions, incubators, and public entities. The findings underscore the need for differentiated training strategies, practical and context-based learning resources, and interactive methodologies to enhance knowledge transfer and application. Overall, the results show that well-designed capacity-building programs can strengthen competencies, improve coordination among stakeholders, and increase access to financing and private-sector development in emerging economies.

title: Strategic Communication as a Critical Success Factor in Financial Literacy Projects in Emerging Markets
container-title: Women and Youth Entrepreneurship for Inclusive and Sustainable Global Development
b056edfc1a444d6313ac05c0a639b7a226e1b385.abstract: This chapter analyses the role of strategic communication in the Envolver Project, an international development initiative focused on strengthening financial literacy and improving access to finance for MSMEs in Angola. Drawing on the case, the chapter argues that communication was not limited to dissemination or institutional visibility, but operated as a structuring mechanism for stakeholder engagement, trust-building, contextual adaptation and ecosystem alignment. It examines the project's identity, visual language, internal communication, channel architecture, on-the-ground presence and differentiated approaches to stakeholders. The analysis shows how communication supported the creation of a common language among entrepreneurs, financial institutions, incubators, public entities, the judiciary community and universities, contributing to the practical appropriation of knowledge, the reduction of perceived risk and the strengthening of financial literacy as an applied capacity.

title: AI-Driven Personalization in Customer Engagement and Travel Marketing
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI-Driven Transformation of Travel Marketing and Customer Experience
cab53579f6f706d2b096f9f8e1ef7047728972da.abstract: The introduction of the artificial intelligence (AI) into the travel marketing is a game changer in the way the industry will interact, retain, and serve the customers. This chapter discusses how AI-driven personalization approaches have evolved and are used in the travel industry and how technologies like machine learning, natural language processing, predictive analytics, and recommendation systems are helping to transform customer experiences. The chapter discusses how personalization affects consumer decision-making, brand loyalty and revenue generation based on the existing empirical research and case studies in the industry. It also touches upon the ethical issues of privacy of data, algorithmic discrimination and customer permission. This chapter provides a theoretical context and practical data to travel marketers, technologists and policymakers who must work within the rapidly evolving AI landscape by looking at current applications and forecasting trends.

title: Talking to Travellers
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI-Driven Transformation of Travel Marketing and Customer Experience
439ad8df55c01c5fbfb7f73acae8fad387788276.abstract: With chatbots and conversational artificial intelligence (CAI), the travel brands are transforming the way they connect with prospects and customers throughout the booking process. The argument among marketing scholars is that customer engagement is a multidimensional construct that encompasses cognitive, emotional and behavioural interactions with a brand and that these interactions are becoming mediated by intelligent technologies. Using the literature of marketing, service research, and tourism-informatics this chapter explores the creation of marketing value by chatbots and CAI in regards to travel services. It assesses the theoretical background of customer engagement and conversational AI, the history of chatbots in the travel industry, and their functional placements through the pre-purchase, purchase, and post-purchase processes. It then evaluates three main sources of marketing value including personalisation of the customer experience, brand communication and voice, and real-time marketing intelligence through conversational data. The chapter also takes into account the issues of challenges, such as hallucinations, channel fragmentation, and escalation failure, as well as the ethical, privacy, and trust issues. Arguments are based on three exemplary cases, and a research agenda is presented in the future of conversational-AI-based travel marketing. The main argument is that, when intelligently combined with the broader marketing stack, chatbots and CAI cease to be viewed as a cost-saving service channel, but rather as a strategic platform of relationship-based, data-rich interaction with customers.

title: Chatbots and Conversational AI in Customer Engagement for Travel Services
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
