61f356e4896a0d512dee258558f6e2599b3911a4.abstract: Conversational artificial intelligence (CAI) and chatbots are transforming the way travel brands interact with the prospects and customers throughout the booking process. There has been a long-standing argument by marketing scholars that customer engagement is a multidimensional concept that includes cognitive, emotional, and behavioural interactions with a brand, and the interactions are becoming mediated by intelligent technologies. Based on marketing, service research, and tourism-informatics literatures, this chapter explores how travel service chatbots and CAI can generate marketing value. It discusses the theoretical basis of customer engagement and conversational AI, the history of chatbots in the travel sector, and outlines their operational applications throughout the pre-purchase, purchase, and post-purchase processes. It subsequently examines three key bases of marketing value, which include customising the customer experience, brand communication and voice, and real-time marketing intelligence based on conversational data. Challenges, such as hallucinations, channel fragmentation, and escalation failure, as well as ethical, privacy, and trust considerations are also taken into account in the chapter. The arguments are based on three illustrative cases and a research agenda is provided on the next generation of conversational-AI-enabled travel marketing. The main argument is that, designed appropriately as part of the broader marketing stack, chatbots and CAI no longer represent a cost-reduction service channel but rather a strategic customer engagement platform, full of data.

title: Harnessing Generative AI and Large Language Models for Intelligent Travel Planning
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI-Driven Transformation of Travel Marketing and Customer Experience
c44e15ad738f4a32fc2a61c562801bad0d22ace2.abstract: Generative AI (GenAI) and Large Language Models (LLMs) are transforming how travellers discover destinations, plan itineraries, and engage with tourism service providers. This chapter provides a systematic and theoretically grounded examination of these technologies within intelligent travel planning. It traces the evolution of AI in tourism and explores key applications, including conversational trip planning, hyper-personalized recommendations, real-time adaptive guidance, and sentiment analysis. The chapter highlights opportunities to enhance accessibility, improve operational efficiency, and support data-driven destination management. It also examines critical challenges, including hallucinations, information reliability, algorithmic bias, data privacy, workforce disruption, and fragmented regulatory frameworks. The chapter concludes by addressing governance and policy needs while identifying future directions, including multimodal AI, sustainable AI, interoperable ecosystems, and interdisciplinary collaboration to ensure the responsible adoption of AI in global tourism.

title: Generative Artificial Intelligence and Large Language Models as a Digital Assistant for Power System Operators
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI-Driven Sustainable Energy Systems
43f02e9dd2362d62f0781c1271492951a9157aa0.abstract: Power-system operation is safety-critical: personnel integrate data, alarms, outages, switching requests, contingency analyses, grid-code rules, and cybersecurity constraints. This review assesses evidence, rechecked through May 31, 2026, on GenAI and large language models (LLMs) for operator support. It covers research, reports, standards, regulations, preprints, and industry initiatives, distinguishing retrieval-grounded systems, domain-adapted LLMs, time-series foundation models, tool-using agents, and digital-twin verification. It proposes a supervised assistant in which the LLM orchestrates and explains but is not operational truth. Near-term uses include document retrieval, regulatory interpretation, training, summaries, and explanations of approved calculations. Evidence does not support autonomous transmission-level actions. Deployment requires traceable sources, current models, restricted tools, cybersecurity boundaries, adversarial testing, human approval, and audit trails.

title: Maternal Agency and Care in the Missio Dei: A Practical-Theological Synthesis for Global Mission
container-title: Journal of Religion and Public Life
7f70ed743df5163bb296401b8540986bab9d4413.abstract: Abstract: Mission theology often names the maternal while overlooking maternal agency and care. The article offers a practical-theological synthesis, bringing together my published work on maternal-thinking and motherlessness, a bounded case study of a Colombian congregation, and selected historical examples. Drawing on Sara Ruddick’s maternal-thinking, extended by a fourfold practice of preservation, growth, acceptance, and release, and on the idea of a maternal commons, it asks what these sources reveal about mothers and mothering in the missio Dei. The Colombian case shows how one US-based mission organisation’s assumptions about family, gender, and church belonging, treated as universal, marginalised local women’s maternal agency, while the congregation’s mothers and grandmothers helped sustain its communal life during crisis. Historical and textual examples suggest that this agency is a recurring, though often unrecognised, source of Christian faith, including under persecution. The case is bounded and does not represent all mission contexts, but it raises questions for mission agencies as mission initiatives increasingly emerge from the Global South. The article closes with four practical implications, for theological education, the recognition of maternal care, mission methods and policies, and reciprocal learning, and invites mission practice and policy to recognise maternal agency as one of the places from which Christians learn to discern and practise the missio Dei.

title: Emotional attributes of digital assistants driving engagement, purchase intentions and well-being
container-title: International Journal of Retail & Distribution Management
a75d79312ce4abff331f0694d5c24f21c27ec281.abstract: Purpose Grounded in the stimulus–organism–response (SOR) model and the spillover concept, the study examines how digital assistants’ (DAs) affective attributes shape customer engagement, which then spills over into emotional values, purchase intentions and well-being. Design/methodology/approach A two-wave longitudinal survey was conducted, yielding 440 responses at Time 1 and 315 at Time 2. Partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) by SmartPLS 4.0 was used to verify the reliability and validity of the measurement model and test the hypothesised relationships. Findings The findings reveal that DAs’ aesthetics, friendliness and playfulness significantly increase customer engagement, with effect sizes for these emotional stimuli varying from low to high. Customers’ active engagement also subsequently influences their emotional values: perceived happiness and relaxation. Together, these emotional values have a positive and significant effect on purchase intentions. The results also show that customer well-being is significantly spilled through purchase intentions. Moreover, customer engagement, emotional values and purchase intention yield substantial serial mediation effects in the relationships between attributional stimuli and well-being. Originality/value The originality of this study lies in extending the SOR model to a psychological outcome (well-being) and quantitatively verifying the interrelationships in retail settings. It investigates the serial mediation of emotional attributional stimuli, presenting their activeness continuum from low to high. Besides, it offers key managerial insights into effectively utilising DA attributes to engage and evoke customers’ emotional values, thereby driving purchase intentions and, subsequently, extending the experience to well-being in technology-mediated services.

title: Feeling the gap: cognitive-affective divergence in SME managers' Industry 4.0 and sustainability narratives
container-title: European Journal of Innovation Management
cd25d84111e66598609d29a9d0f99afcb5d27ff0.abstract: Purpose The study investigates how small- and medium-sized enterprise (SME) managers perceive and emotionally engage with environmental and social sustainability in the context of Industry 4.0 adoption. Using semi-structured interviews combined with multimodal sentiment analysis (speech prosody and emotional language), we aim to uncover implicit hesitancy, dissonance, and conceptual fragmentation that traditional methods fail to detect, thereby offering new insights for policy design and corporate social responsibility research in structurally disadvantaged regions. Design/methodology/approach The manuscript employs a mixed-methods design integrating semi-structured interviews with multimodal sentiment analysis. Twenty SMEs in Southern Italy, selected through structured sampling, participated in interviews exploring Industry 4.0 investments, environmental practices, and social sustainability. Recorded interviews underwent (1) thematic and content analysis for explicit responses, and (2) Hume AI-based prosody and emotional language analysis to detect implicit emotional engagement. This dual approach captures both declared positions and underlying affective reactions, enabling the identification of dissonance between cognitive awareness and emotional investment across environmental and social sustainability dimensions. Findings Environmental sustainability is widely recognized (90% of firms), yet only 60% link Industry 4.0 investments to environmental goals, and key performance indicator use remains inconsistent. Social sustainability reveals a striking “feeling gap”: while 90% express willingness to invest, conceptual fragmentation prevails, with no standardized metrics. Sentiment analysis exposes declining concentration, rising confusion, and subtle annoyance when discussing social topics, contrasting with calm, determined engagement for technological investments. Emotional prosody thus uncovers hidden dissonance between declared awareness and authentic affective engagement, particularly for social sustainability, which remains intuitively rather than analytically grounded in SME decision-making. Originality/value This study introduces the “feeling gap” concept, distinguishing cognitive awareness from emotional engagement in SME sustainability practices. Methodologically, it pioneers multimodal sentiment analysis (speech prosody and emotional language) in Industry 4.0 and CSR research, moving beyond declared positions to detect hidden hesitancy and dissonance. Empirically, it focuses on a structurally disadvantaged region often overlooked in favor of large enterprises or developed economies. The findings demonstrate that policy design must address not only informational and financial barriers but also affective and motivational dimensions, particularly for social sustainability, which lacks standardized metrics and genuine emotional resonance among SME managers.

title: Adaptive Explainability for XR-Assisted Predictive Maintenance in the Industrial Metaverse
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Enhancing the Industrial Metaverse With Extended Reality
b146dcaf8f19ea21cf4d2a218e3a890e21f14f80.abstract: In Industry 5.0, XR-assisted predictive maintenance systems increasingly combine immersive visualisation with AI-powered diagnostics. However, many established explainable AI (XAI) approaches are based on desktop-oriented models and do not fully address the needs of Industrial Metaverse settings. Operators differ in expertise and operational risk, yet XR systems often provide the same explanations to everyone. This can increase cognitive load, reduce situational awareness, and result in inappropriate trust in AI-assisted decisions. This chapter proposes a human-centred adaptive explainability framework for XR-assisted predictive maintenance in the Industrial Metaverse. It adapts explanation, presentation, interaction, and guidance to operator expertise and operational criticality, guided by cognitive fit, risk-proportional disclosure, and interaction economy. A conceptual bearing-failure scenario illustrates different explanation strategies for novice and expert technicians. The chapter also considers robotic anomaly management and energy infrastructure monitoring as extensions.

title: Segmented projection image translation for large-area, high-resolution vat photopolymerization
container-title: Science Advances
d76d24160b2d3ead68af3759530d175b14f7a094.abstract: High-resolution projection-based vat photopolymerization (VP) 3D printing enables rapid fabrication of highly detailed polymeric structures. However, expanding the build area traditionally compromises resolution, creating a fundamental trade-off between projected pixel size and printable area due to fixed digital micromirror device (DMD) pixel counts. Herein, we introduce segmented projection image translation (SPIN), a simple implementation strategy that expands the effective projection area by applying controlled orbital translation to an off-axis objective lens within the optical infinity space. In this work, we demonstrate a projection-based VP printer implemented with SPIN that expands the effective build area by 4.8-fold, from a native field of 60.4 square millimeters to an expanded domain of 290.5 square millimeters. The SPIN-enabled printer produces isolated line features as thin as 9.8 ± 2.2 micrometers and fabricates intricate three-dimensional truss structures with features as small as 30 micrometers. These results validate a practical route for extending microscale projection-based VP printing to larger build areas while preserving feature fidelity across stitched exposure fields.

title: Cocrystals for sequestering and separating large PAHs
container-title: Science Advances
c4f85745b84f5229d94d511d75eed44e3d9ad7ed.abstract: Highly adaptive boroxine organic assemblies (BOAs) derived from a boronic acid and a linear alkene function as a first-generation constitutional dynamic library (CDL) to sequester and separate large polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) in form of cocrystals. Configurational and conformational isomerism of the organoboroxines in host-guest assemblies is induced by electronic properties, shape and size of the PAHs through a “shrink-wrap” process/mechanism, which reveals a templating role of the PAH during the CDL assembly. The CDL was applied to separate up to three different PAHs. The cocrystals exhibit tunable electronic properties. The CDL afforded a cocrystal wherein alkenes of two different BOAs undergo [2 + 2] photocycloaddition in the same solid.

title: “Prieta, happy in their skin, color, and language”: secondary content area teachers’ navigation of raciolinguistic ideologies in Texas
container-title: International Review of Applied Linguistics in Language Teaching
eb3043c71febf8e94a421ea964e6a6be8d62001f.abstract: Abstract This study explores how secondary content-area teachers from raciolinguistically minoritized communities engage with raciolinguistic trauma through participation in a professional development (PD) program at a Hispanic-serving institution in South Texas. Drawing on the framework of raciolinguistic ideologies, we examine data from Project MIRRORS, a graduate-level PD program serving 55 teachers, recruited from two school districts and distributed across three cohorts. Through qualitative data analysis of interviews, digital language stories, identity reflections, and collaborative coaching sessions, we document how participants (a) engaged in intersectional identity work, (b) processed intergenerational and schooling-related linguistic trauma, and (c) reimagined pedagogical practices as acts of healing and resistance. The findings highlight three main areas: engaging in intersectional identity work through PD, reflecting on raciolinguistic trauma, and reclaiming linguistic agency through healing-oriented pedagogy. Teachers’ narratives demonstrate that addressing linguistic racism in TESOL requires attending to the emotional and historical dimensions of language oppression. We argue that trauma-informed teacher education grounded in identity work can foster both individual and collective healing by empowering educators to transform classrooms into spaces of linguistic justice and affirmation.

title: The corruption–networking–internationalization framework: an antecedent-process-outcome model for entrepreneurial ventures' growth in emerging economies
container-title: Journal of Small Business and Enterprise Development
46536d6f6c6c5b8308f344233901f4fddeb17907.abstract: Purpose This study develops a conceptual framework explaining how corruption shapes the internationalization of entrepreneurial ventures in emerging economies through entrepreneurial networking. It conceptualizes corruption as a multidimensional institutional void that triggers the formation of domestic, regional and international networks and examines how entrepreneurial cognition and effectuation logic condition these processes. The study also accounts for the dark side of networking to explain when corruption-driven relational strategies constrain internationalization outcomes. Design/methodology/approach The paper adopts a theory-driven conceptual approach grounded in institutional theory, international entrepreneurship, networking theory and entrepreneurial cognition. Drawing on an integrative review of interdisciplinary literature, it develops the Corruption–Networking–Internationalization Framework as an antecedent–process–outcome model. The framework specifies causal mechanisms linking different forms of corruption to multi-level networking strategies, moderated by entrepreneurial characteristics and constrained by relational liabilities. A set of theoretically grounded propositions is advanced to guide future empirical research. Findings The study theorizes that corruption operates not only as a constraint but also as a catalyst for alternative governance mechanisms, prompting entrepreneurial ventures to rely on networks as functional substitutes for weak formal institutions. Domestic networks primarily mitigate administrative corruption, regional networks provide culturally proximate trust channels and international networks help firms bypass corrupt domestic systems and accelerate internationalization. Entrepreneurial effectuation logic, entrepreneurial orientation and opportunity-recognition cognition strengthen the translation of corruption-induced uncertainty into internationally oriented networking strategies. However, excessive reliance on domestic, political or corrupt networks can generate over embeddedness, opportunism and de-internationalization risks. Research limitations/implications This study is conceptual and has not been empirically validated across different emerging economy contexts. It does not test the proposed relationships using quantitative or qualitative data. The framework assumes relatively distinct domestic, regional and international network layers, which may overlap in practice. It also does not specify boundary conditions under which networks may produce negative outcomes. In addition, heterogeneity in entrepreneurial cognition and institutional responses to corruption is not directly examined within an empirical setting. Originality/value The study reconceptualizes corruption as an active antecedent shaping entrepreneurial networking configurations rather than merely an exogenous barrier. It introduces a multi-layered view of networks as institutional substitutes and integrates entrepreneurial cognition and the dark side of networking into international entrepreneurship theory. The Corruption–Networking–Internationalization framework provides a dynamic and context-sensitive explanation of entrepreneurial ventures internationalization from corruption-heavy emerging economies.

title: Augmentation or automation? A dual-path model of GenAI usage motivations and employee creativity
container-title: Internet Research
fadf43bc36b6b235f34356dd883ee8b077d594c5.abstract: Purpose Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) can both enhance and constrain employee creativity, yet the mechanisms underlying these divergent effects remain unclear. This study examines how augmentation and automation motivations for GenAI usage shape employee creativity through distinct knowledge-processing mechanisms. Design/methodology/approach Drawing on dual-process theory and self-regulation theory, we distinguish augmentation and automation motivations for GenAI usage and propose distinct cognitive mechanisms linking them to creativity. We test the hypotheses using a multi-wave, multi-source field survey and a scenario-based experiment. Findings Augmentation motivation is positively associated with employee creativity through knowledge integration, whereas automation motivation is negatively related to creativity through knowledge dependence. Conscientiousness strengthens the positive indirect effect of augmentation motivation and attenuates the negative indirect effect of automation motivation on employee creativity. Research limitations/implications Augmentation and automation motivations may coexist and vary across tasks and use episodes. Future research could explore these dynamics, examine how other individual differences shape their effects, and assess whether the consequences of GenAI dependence vary across work contexts. Practical implications Organizations should encourage employees to use GenAI to generate and develop ideas rather than replace their own judgment. Training could help employees critically assess AI-generated suggestions and combine them with their own knowledge. Originality/value This research shifts attention from how much employees use GenAI to why they use it. By distinguishing augmentation and automation motivations, it explains when and why GenAI can enhance or constrain employee creativity through distinct knowledge-processing mechanisms.

title: Building a competent workforce: a competency model for strategic development of infectious disease nurses
container-title: Journal of Health Organization and Management
40b4a5837409f022e757d95fafaa0864ae554a0f.abstract: Purpose This study aims to construct and preliminarily evaluate a structural competency model for infectious disease specialist nurses, delineating the pathways between competency dimensions to support strategic workforce planning and management in health organizations. Design/methodology/approach A sequential mixed-methods design was employed. Qualitative data from phenomenological interviews with 28 practitioners informed a competency framework, which was quantitatively validated through a cross-sectional survey and structural equation modeling to test hypothesized pathways. Findings The model identifies seven core competencies: Clinical Care, Education, Research, Professional Development, Management, Communication, and Infection Prevention and Control. The pilot quantitative analysis showed generally high self-rated competency levels and substantial training needs. However, the newly developed scales demonstrated limited internal consistency in the present sample, and the hypothesized path relationships did not reach statistical significance. Clinical Care did not significantly predict Infection Prevention and Control, and the proposed effects of Infection Prevention and Control and Research on Professional Development, as well as those of Communication and Education on Management, were not statistically supported. The hypothesized mediating role of Infection Prevention and Control between Clinical Care and Professional Development was also not statistically significant. Originality/value This study offers a qualitatively grounded competency framework with preliminary quantitative evidence that clarifies potential interrelationships among infectious disease specialist nurse competencies and provides a foundation for future large-sample validation, workforce development and training design.

title: Contact and constructionalization: the emergence of a clause-final adverb construction in Singaporean varieties
container-title: Cognitive Linguistics
1e82b80c5588957c46438a0a071b1e2452a2b95d.abstract: Abstract Clause-final adverbs such as already , also , and only have been widely recognized as characteristic features of Singapore English. By comparison, parallel clause-final adverbial patterns in Singapore Mandarin remain underexplored, despite being similarly prominent in everyday speech. This paper addresses this gap by presenting the first construction-based analysis of clause-final adverbs in Singapore Mandarin and by examining them alongside the use of clause-final adverbs in Singapore English. Based on the Diasystematic Construction Grammar framework, we propose that sustained bilingualism in Singapore has given rise to a stance-oriented clause-final constructional slot, which supports three distinct developmental trajectories in Singapore Mandarin. Through a detailed analysis of three adverbs, 才 cái ‘only’, 先 xiān ‘first’, and 也是 yěshì ‘also’, we illustrate trajectories of decline, functional strengthening, and innovation. The findings demonstrate that clause-final adverbs in Singapore Mandarin are systematically organized within a constructional network shaped by both bilingual usage patterns and ongoing changes in Singapore’s multilingual linguistic environment.

title: Representation of character experience: language choices and similative construal
container-title: Cognitive Semiotics
bf654c649d6ac897df8a5df548f735d164b5d666.abstract: Abstract This paper discusses examples from modernist and contemporary fiction, focusing on two experiential areas – the experience of the flow of time and the felt quality of events and emotions. It proposes a more specific understanding of the role played by figurative imagery, speech representation, and accounts of sensory perception, which can jointly be referred to as modes of representing character experience . The examples selected for analysis go beyond unmarked depictions of actions or events. Rather, they depict narrative scenes where the high intensity of experience calls for language choices going beyond representing ordinary acts and scenes. To account for the experiential intensity of the texts referred to I propose a broad type of figuration, which I refer to as similative . The examples of similative construal discussed in the paper illustrate how textual choices build on representations of attention, fictive events, and fictive conversations in order to render character experiences – embodied, emotional, or both.

172e9f1b71624e7ec81c6c9519189b84d183d9fa.abstract: This research paper presents an integrated eco-economic analysis of agricultural cluster transformation within vulnerable ecosystems, focusing on the cotton and textile sector of the Republic of Karakalpakstan. The Aral Sea ecological crisis presents severe environmental boundaries, including acute water deficits, severe soil salinization, and climate-induced yield volatility. Traditional market-driven cluster integration often fails to internalize these ecological externalities. This study proposes an eco-efficiency assessment framework and evaluates strategic economic mechanisms to incentivize water-saving technologies, mitigate environmental production risks, and strengthen value-chain resilience. Empirical findings confirm that combining green procurement premiums, public-private-environmental partnerships, and circular agricultural practices significantly enhances resource productivity, farm-level profitability, and long-term regional economic stability.

title: Developing students’ Global Englishes-oriented critical GenAI literacy: an intervention study
container-title: International Review of Applied Linguistics in Language Teaching
c2a85741d65a0cbaf919b7ddc24459afc75364b5.abstract: Abstract The Global Englishes (GE) perspective challenges native-speaker norms, yet many classrooms still privilege dominant forms, reinforcing hierarchies and limiting learners’ ownership. The rise of generative AI (GenAI) heightens these concerns, as tools often reproduce standard language ideologies and marginalise non-dominant varieties. This study reports a twelve-week intervention in a GE course for English majors in Hong Kong. Students critiqued GenAI outputs, evaluated AI voice simulators, and designed GE-oriented chatbots. A mixed-methods design used pre/post questionnaires and interviews. Descriptive questionnaire results suggested shifts toward greater recognition of English pluralism, awareness of how norms relate to power, and understanding of GenAI’s role in linguistic hierarchies. Qualitative results suggest students held critical views of GenAI’s effects on norms, minoritised voices, and their own voice, identity and authenticity after the intervention. The study argues that GE-informed pedagogy can support students’ critical GenAI literacy and prepares future professionals for AI-mediated communication.

title: (203) Pompeja: Constraining a non-convex shape model, size, and bulk density to support the interpretation of its spectral variability
container-title: Astronomy & Astrophysics
01ff3fd439b5b2404f76f42b6b36a374db095881.abstract: Recent stellar occultations of (203) Pompeja provided well-constrained silhouettes that had the potential to enable a more detailed reconstruction of its three-dimensional shape. Motivated by these data, we aimed to reconstruct the asteroid spin and shape model using the ADAM (All-Data Asteroid Modeling) method and to use the improved model to test the hypothesis that the reported spectral-slope variability is related to specific surface regions. We also aimed to resolve the mirror-pole ambiguity and improve the determination of Pompeja size and bulk density. We applied the ADAM method to a combined dataset consisting of photometric light curves and six stellar occultation events. It allowed us to constrain Pompeja's non-convex three-dimensional shape, sidereal rotation period, and spin axis orientation. The determined volume-equivalent diameter was subsequently combined with an available mass estimate to determine the bulk density. To investigate the possible spectral variability, we reconstructed illumination and viewing geometries of the ADAM spin and shape model for the available spectroscopic observations and quantitatively compared the surface regions sampled at different epochs. We also performed a facet-based correlation analysis between the shape model and measured spectral slopes. Finally, we modelled the spectral slopes by jointly accounting for surface-dependent and observing geometry effects and used this model to predict favourable geometries for future observations. We obtained a unique spin and shape solution for Pompeja and resolved the pole ambiguity. Preferred spin axis orientation is found to be łambda = 132 ^ +6 _ -1 deg and β = 39 ^ +8 _ -1 deg. The sidereal rotation period was determined to be P = 24.04843 ± 0.00004 h. We derived a volume-equivalent diameter of 107^ +3 _ -2 km and calculated bulk density of 1.33 ± 0.18 -3 . Our analysis is consistent with the hypothesis that the recently concluded apparition in year 2026 provided particularly favourable conditions for testing spectral variability and narrowed the most promising observing window from late March to mid-April 2026. The spectral slope model also identifies additional candidate windows in July 2027 and around February 2030.

title: Towards an AI Literacy Framework for Maritime English Education: Integrating Language, Professional, and Digital Competencies
container-title: LANCAH: Jurnal Inovasi dan Tren
236639692b02ff378d325cde7448cb13cf583416.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is increasingly influencing language education by providing opportunities for personalized practice, immediate feedback, and flexible access to learning resources. However, effective use of GenAI in Maritime English requires competencies beyond general language proficiency and basic technological skills. Maritime English involves specialized terminology, standardized communication, operational contexts, and professional requirements in which inaccurate or inappropriate AI-generated content may have practical consequences. This conceptual study develops an AI literacy framework for Maritime English education through a conceptual literature synthesis. The synthesis draws on literature published between 2020 and 2026, supplemented by earlier foundational works on AI literacy and English for Specific Purposes (ESP), as well as authoritative Maritime references, including IMO Standard Marine Communication Phrases and IMO Model Course 3.17. Sources were selected based on their relevance to AI literacy, generative AI in language education, ESP, learner autonomy, and Maritime English, with particular attention to their conceptual contributions and applicability to Maritime communication. The synthesis identifies digital-AI competence as the core AI literacy capability, supported by two contextual knowledge bases: language competence and professional Maritime competence. Language competence enables learners to evaluate AI-generated language, while professional Maritime competence supports the verification of terminology, operational relevance, and contextual appropriateness. Digital-AI competence enables critical and responsible interaction with AI systems, including prompt formulation, output evaluation, and information verification. The proposed framework provides a conceptual basis for integrating AI literacy into Maritime English education while maintaining linguistic and professional standards. Future empirical research is needed to operationalize and validate the framework among Maritime English learners, lecturers, and Maritime professionals.

title: Decoding decision correctness from EEG under high cognitive workload in virtual reality: implications for collaborative brain-computer interface teams
container-title: Frontiers in Virtual Reality
e2c61608cbfd1ad3de6e77e02188da5672f9f4fe.abstract: Introduction Collaborative Brain-Computer Interfaces (cBCIs) offer a promising mechanism to augment team decision‐making, but existing approaches rely exclusively on evidence available only after a decision has been made and reported, such as reaction time or stated confidence. This limits their use to explaining or discounting a decision after the fact, rather than informing a teams response before it is finalised. We tested whether spatial‐covariance EEG features could instead provide a genuinely pre-emptive signal of an operators decision correctness, available within the response window itself, and whether such a signal depends on cognitive workload. Methods Using a continuous virtual reality target-detection task, participants (N = 23) completed a within-subject visual workload manipulation (High vs. Low), implemented via a Degraded Visual Environment. Results A Riemannian tangent‐space classifier, trained on a strictly motor‐safe EEG window preceding each response, decoded Correct from Incorrect decisions with above‐chance accuracy under High Workload (61.4%, p = .0014, N = 23) but not reliably under Low Workload (N = 17), where near‐ceiling behavioural accuracy left too few error trials for valid classification. Ablation analysis showed the signal was carried predominantly by posterior occipito‐parietal channels, consistent with a perceptual rather than motor origin. At the team level, weighting votes by this pre-emptive neural signal, available before a response is committed, produced substantial accuracy gains on contested (evenly‐split) trials under High Workload (57% to 88% as team size increased from 2 to 16), but was actively detrimental under Low Workload. Discussion Critically, this advantage held even against post‐hoc behavioural signals: confidence was the strongest single team‐level signal overall, but by definition cannot inform a decision still in progress, whereas the neural signal can. These findings indicate that EEG‐based decision‐reliability signals are not a general‐purpose team augmentation tool, but a workload‐conditional one, with clear implications for when and how cBCI systems should be deployed in operational teams.

title: Correlation Study between Spatial Distribution of POI and Road Network Morphology in Historic Urban Area of Kaifeng Based on sDNA Model
container-title: SAE Technical Paper Series
7c77f519098a53a3c47466ad558f41402367df79.abstract: <div class="section abstract"> <div class="htmlview paragraph">While previous studies have examined road network morphology and POI distribution separately or at single scales, this study introduces a multi-scale analytical framework to investigate their intrinsic correlation in historic urban contexts. Employing the sDNA model and kernel density estimation within ArcGIS, this paper quantitatively analyzes the road network morphology and spatial distribution characteristics of Points of Interest (POI) in the historic urban area of Kaifeng City, and examines their correlation across multiple spatial scales (400 m to 3000 m radii). The results show that: (1) At different spatial scales, the arterial road system in the historic urban area of Kaifeng demonstrates high topological integrity and centrality; (2) The correlation between the road network morphology and POI spatial distribution in the historic urban area weakens with increasing radius. At the same scale, road proximity is more likely to influence the distribution of POI; (3) At the slow-moving scale, the correlation between road network morphology and POI spatial distribution is stronger than at the vehicular scale, and it gradually weakens with increasing radius. These findings reveal a scale-dependent relationship between road morphology and functional agglomeration, suggesting that the vitality core of historic urban areas remains anchored in pedestrian-oriented networks — a theoretical insight with implications beyond the Kaifeng case. The research results can provide a basis for traffic improvement and facility planning in the historic urban area of Kaifeng, and serve as a reference for other historic urban areas. The multi-scale analytical framework demonstrated in this study offers a transferable methodology for diagnosing similar scale-dependent dynamics in diverse historic urban contexts.</div> </div>

title: Development of a Driving Behavior Scoring Model for Electric Vehicles Oriented to Energy Consumption
container-title: SAE Technical Paper Series
31dbbc75f1f37303bd02d5007a5b2e6c4011bbf3.abstract: <div class="section abstract"><div class="htmlview paragraph">Considering the huge influence of personal driving habits on the actual driving mileage of electric vehicles (EVs), together with the weak interpretability of most existing evaluation models, this research combines logistic regression and scorecard methods to build a new assessment model that focuses on energy consumption and driving behavior, and a complete closed-loop technical framework has been set up in the research process, covering key steps such as raw data preprocessing, feature mining and screening, model design and construction, as well as final score output. Taking real collected vehicle operation data as the basic research material, we extracted 17 feature indicators from three major dimensions, including driver pedal operation habits, real-time vehicle operating state, and actual energy consumption performance, and adopted the mutual information (MI) calculation method to select eight core features with strong differentiation for 100-kilometer power consumption. Since obvious nonlinear correlations exist between these core indicators and vehicle energy consumption, we adopted decision tree-based grouping processing, weight of evidence (WOE) encoding, and information value (IV) quantitative analysis to realize feature discretization and optimization, and then constructed a scoring model relying on a logistic regression algorithm. The verification results demonstrate that the proposed model has an Area Under the Curve (AUC) value of 0.83 when identifying driving behaviors with high or low energy consumption, proving its excellent differentiation ability. This model turns complicated driving behaviors into intuitive quantitative scores, effectively making up for the defects of traditional black-box models that cannot offer practical guidance for energy-saving optimization, and it can also provide solid theoretical reference and practical application support for promoting energy-saving driving behavior among EV users.</div></div>

title: Temporal Stability Analysis of the Factors Affecting Freeway Crash Injury Severity Based on a Generalized Ordered Logit Model
container-title: SAE Technical Paper Series
36def9d8f4f10b5a230b63f8b2e7036c57708fe6.abstract: <div class="section abstract"><div class="htmlview paragraph">This study investigates the determinants of freeway crash injury severity and examines whether their effects remain stable over time. Using crash records collected on the Guangzhou-Shenzhen Coastal Freeway in China from 2014 to 2019, we estimate generalized ordered logit models that explicitly consider the ordinal structure of injury outcomes. Two groups of likelihood-ratio tests are then applied to evaluate temporal transferability among yearly models. The estimation and marginal-effect results show clear time-varying influences rather than stable relationships. Variables associated with vehicle category, crash pattern, season, time of day, horizontal alignment, grade, and bridge segments display noticeable changes in their effects across years. These findings suggest that temporal instability should be incorporated into freeway injury-severity analysis so that transportation agencies can avoid drawing biased conclusions from pooled data.</div></div>

title: Feasibility-Repair Adaptive Large Neighborhood Search for EVRPTW-SPD with Time Windows and Full Recharge
container-title: SAE Technical Paper Series
cf6e74690510aee31e3a81a98b3cc1bf7be0a3d0.abstract: <div class="section abstract"><div class="htmlview paragraph">Optimizing electric vehicle route planning with time windows and simultaneous pick-up and delivery (EVRPTW-SPD) remains challenging due to the complex interactions among routing, dynamic cargo loads, charging behavior, and time windows. Under a full-recharge policy in which vehicles are fully recharged whenever they visit a charging station, a hybrid heuristic framework is proposed. We first build a complete customer assignment by inserting unrouted customers one by one. Energy infeasibility is handled by a hierarchical charging-station repair module (CRM), which combines a greedy algorithm with a parallel evolutionary algorithm to identify the best repair plan while minimizing total detour cost. The repaired solution is then further improved through adaptive large neighborhood search (ALNS) with dynamic operator selection and simulated annealing (SA) acceptance. Load, time-window, and battery violations are penalized adaptively during the search, and a restart rule is used when the search stays trapped for too long. Experiments on the Akbay benchmark indicate that the method consistently finds feasible solutions and converges within acceptable computing time, demonstrating the effectiveness of feasibility-oriented repair and adaptive exploration of infeasible solutions for the full-recharge EVRPTW-SPD problem.</div></div>

title: Research on Model-Driven Test Case Generation Method for Train Operation and Control System
container-title: SAE Technical Paper Series
1bded1fb0fb407bf734b10dff1fe948f4e098292.abstract: <div class="section abstract"><div class="htmlview paragraph">The train operation and control system is a safety-critical system whose software correctness directly affects railway operational safety. Traditional test case design relies on expert experience, leading to low coverage, poor repeatability, and insufficient completeness. To address these challenges, we propose a model-driven automatic test case generation method for the train operation and control system. A multi-view modeling framework is established, including the system function model, the environment model, the operational scenario model, and the line data model. Test cases are automatically generated by traversing the model space based on the predefined coverage criteria. To overcome the limitations of conventional open-loop modeling, a closed-loop modeling approach is proposed, where the environment constraints, the scenario sequences, and the line data constraints are integrated as additional solvable conditions. A constraint-satisfaction-based line data solver is proposed to select test data that meet the specific scenario requirements. The proposed method is applied to the Chinese Train Control System Level 3(CTCS-3 )level train operation and control system for functional validation. Experimental results show that the proposed approach achieves 100% state coverage and 96% transition coverage on a typical station scenario, and reduces manual test case design effort by 65%.</div></div>

title: GSH/pH Dual-Responsive Zwitterionic mRNA Nanocomplexes for Tumor-Enriched mRNA Delivery in a B16F10 Melanoma Model
container-title: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces
57c57ef7fd7d4e78046dfb1f79d6836260530ed5.abstract: Abstract Messenger RNA (mRNA) therapy offers a programmable route to melanoma treatment, but its translation is limited by nuclease degradation, off-target biodistribution and endolysosomal trapping. Here we report a glutathione (GSH)/pH dual-responsive mRNA nanocomplex (mRNA-NC) fabricated by one-pot in situ polymerization of N-(3-aminopropyl)methacrylamide (APMA), 1-vinylimidazole (VI), N,N′-bis(acryloyl)cystamine (BACA), and 2-methacryloyloxyethyl phosphorylcholine (MPC) on the mRNA template. At an N/P ratio of 40, the carrier reached an encapsulation efficiency of 92.7 ± 2.1% and a loading capacity of 87.4 ± 3.2 μg mg–1, forming monodisperse particles of 126.4 ± 7.2 nm (polydispersity index, PDI, 0.14). The zwitterionic corona limited plasma protein adsorption to 12.6 ± 1.5 μg mg–1 (4.6-fold lower than jetPEI/mRNA), kept hemolysis at 0.8 ± 0.2%, and extended the serum half-life of the mRNA to ≈27.4 h, roughly 9-fold longer than naked mRNA. Release was gated by both triggers: 86.5 ± 3.7% of the cargo was released within 8 h under 10 mM GSH, whereas leakage under physiological conditions remained ≤ 12%; in a 4 h matrix, pH 5.5 plus 10 mM GSH released 85 ± 6.8% versus 12 ± 1.5% at pH 7.4 without GSH. In B16F10 cells, the nanocomplex was taken up in a dose- and energy-dependent manner, entered the lysosomal compartment, and escaped over time in a manner consistent with imidazole-mediated proton-sponge buffering (a hypothesis; intralysosomal pH was not measured directly), producing a peak firefly luciferase (FLuc) expression of 56,140 ± 3280 RLU mg–1 protein at 24 h, about 1.5-fold higher than jetPEI/mRNA, with 93.6 ± 3.9% cell viability and 6.7 ± 1.2% lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) release. In B16F10-bearing albino C57BL/6 mice, a single intravenous dose produced tumor-dominant bioluminescence (peak 5.7 × 106 photons s–1 at 6 h), a tumor enrichment index of 1.22 ± 0.18 (vs 0.31 ± 0.03 for jetPEI/mRNA) and 2.42 × 107 FLuc mRNA copies μg–1 tumor RNA at 12 h, while all 7-day safety indicators remained at phosphate-buffered saline (PBS) levels. These results demonstrate that a single zwitterionic nanocomplex can integrate stealth, dual-triggered release, and endosomal escape for safe, tumor-enriched mRNA delivery. While this study focuses on delivery performance and reporter gene expression, it lays a solid foundation for future therapeutic applications with functional mRNA.

title: Automated Intracranial Aneurysm Detection and Size Extraction from Imaging Reports Using a Dual-Model Transformer Framework
198678ad4dda779fc130fd511020b393918ea1fb.abstract: Abstract Background The unstructured and variable nature of radiology reports remains a barrier to automated extraction of clinically relevant information for large-scale research and AI applications, particularly for intracranial aneurysms (IAs). Objective We aimed to develop and evaluate a dual-model transformer framework for intracranial aneurysm information extraction and assess whether structured processing improved classification and size-extraction performance compared with unstructured text. Methods We analyzed 3,183 neuroimaging reports annotated by neuroradiologists and neurosurgeons. Four encoder-based transformer models were evaluated for aneurysm-presence classification using 5-fold stratified cross-validation. A zero-shot Llama 3.1 framework was used to extract aneurysm size using direct and structured-report prompting. RadDistilBERT and Llama 3.1 were evaluated on 20 temporally distinct reports using full-report and impression-only inputs, with and without structured preprocessing. Results RadDistilBERT achieved the highest mean classification performance, with accuracy of 96.4% (± 1.8%), F1 score of 91.7% (± 10.3%), precision of 94.0% (± 4.6%), and recall of 90.7% (± 15.6%). F1 scores were 87.5% for BERT-base-uncased and 31.1% for ALBERT-base-v2. In the 20-report set, aneurysm-presence classification accuracy was 100% across all input and processing conditions. For aneurysm size extraction, structured report processing increased accuracy from 61.90% to 66.67% using the full report and from 80.95% to 85.00% using the impression section. Conclusions This study demonstrates the feasibility of a dual-model transformer framework for aneurysm-presence classification and size extraction from unstructured neuroimaging reports. RadDistilBERT achieved the strongest classification performance, while Llama 3.1 enabled zero-shot size extraction. These findings support further external validation and expansion to additional aneurysm characteristics with dedicated annotation and validation.

title: Co-designing a logic model for community-based diabetic foot screening in primary care: A participatory study
284f8283e75844803aa856eab6ce2cbf01bb1532.abstract: Abstract Background. Diabetic foot complications, including ulcers and amputations, lead to reduced quality of life and premature death, and up to 85% of amputations could be prevented through optimal prevention. In Canada, preventive foot care remains fragmented and difficult to access, and to our knowledge, no recognized screening program currently exists in Quebec primary care. This study aimed to co-design a logic model specifying the inputs, activities, outputs, and expected outcomes of an equitable community-based diabetic foot screening program in primary care. Methods. Using a participatory co-design approach following GUIDED reporting guidelines, we developed the logic model in two steps: 1) a rapid review synthesizing implementation determinants and strategies from 44 diabetic foot screening programs across 16 countries, and 2) a stepwise co-design process structured around seven meetings of an interdisciplinary steering committee (N = 23) comprising patient partners, clinicians, managers, community representatives, trainees, and researchers at a University Family Medicine Group (U-FMG) in Trois-Rivières, Quebec, Canada. The process was guided by the Knowledge-to-Action framework, the Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research, and Quebec’s Ministry of Health and Social Services proximity services reference framework, and was evaluated through an anonymous mid-course survey and a final reflexive workshop. Results. The final logic model articulates the program theory for early detection of diabetic foot complications, specifying required resources, standardized screening and follow-up activities, corresponding outputs, and time-phased expected outcomes, with equity embedded across most of the components. The mid-course evaluation was positive (mean item scores 4.0 to 4.6 out of 5.0), and participants highlighted inclusive participation and the recognition of different voices. Conclusions. The model provides an evidence-informed roadmap for implementing and evaluating equitable diabetic foot screening at the U-FMG and is intended to be transferable, with deliberate adaptation, to similar primary care settings.

title: A UAV-based real-time detection system of flowering nectar plants using a lightweight deep learning model
container-title: Precision Agriculture
9e1abaaad796cb3a232ce9e89cab801e7c04fa68.abstract: Abstract Purpose Timely knowledge of flowering status and peak blooming periods in transferred areas is crucial for migratory beekeepers to make informed management decisions. Traditional manual field surveys are labor-intensive, time-consuming, and unsuitable for frequent monitoring. Current monitoring approaches using Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAV) rely on offline processing and require complex data analysis by specialists, making them impractical for beekeepers to implement in apicultural settings. Given the short time window for capturing flowering events, especially for species with short florescence periods, an accurate, fast monitoring solution is needed. We developed a UAV-based real-time investigation prototype leveraging edge-intelligence computing for nectar flower detection of Rhus chinensis in complex mountainous field conditions. Methods An improved, high-precision, and lightweight deep learning model based on YOLOv5s was proposed. The model was optimized with acceleration strategies during deployment to reduce inference time. Results Experimental results showed that the proposed model for flower detection achieved a mean Average Precision (mAP) of 89.5 and an inference speed of 56 frames per second (FPS). After applying acceleration strategies during model deployment on the edge computing device, the processing throughput reached 192 FPS with a mAP of 89.2; a 3.1% increase in mAP and approximately a 5.6 times improvement in FPS compared to the original YOLOv5s. Conclusions These results demonstrate that the proposed lightweight model and acceleration strategies effectively balance high accuracy with high-throughput onboard image processing. The developed UAV-edge computing system provides a promising prototype for future efficient nectar flowering status monitoring, with potential applications in smart apiculture.

title: Model Coaching SORONG-GROW Berbasis Kebutuhan Industri untuk Penguatan Kinerja Guru di SMKN 1 Kabupaten Sorong
container-title: YASIN
d182813533698be6e5646a173f3f2439b31dad70.abstract: Strengthening vocational high school teachers’ performance requires support that considers industry competency needs and gaps in school curricula. This study aimed to describe the implementation of the SORONG-GROW Coaching Model and analyze its contribution to strengthening teacher performance at SMK Negeri 1 in Sorong Regency. This model integrates the mapping of occupational requirements and industry competency needs through Scanning Occupational Requirement of the Market (SORO), school gap analysis through Navigating Gaps of Curriculum (NG), and support through the Goal, Reality, Options, and Will (GROW) stages. The study used a qualitative approach with a case study design. Data were collected through interviews, observations, coaching worksheets, monitoring logbooks, school documents, and Collaborative Inquiry records. The evidence analyzed included NG mapping before and after the intervention, the implementation of two coaching cycles, and reflections by the principal and the development team. The results showed that the school’s alignment with industry needs increased from 28% on 6 May 2025 to 66% on 7 April 2026, while the gap decreased from 72% to 34%. Based on reflections from Cycle II, approximately 98% of teachers were reported to have delivered instruction as expected, while approximately 2% still required further support. These changes coincided with strengthened academic supervision, curriculum evaluation, industry-oriented instruction, and collaborative follow-up. These findings indicate the potential of coaching based on diagnosis, reflection, and monitoring to help principals guide teachers’ professional development in accordance with school and industry needs. However, the single-school case study design does not allow the observed changes to be attributed solely to the implementation of coaching.

title: Language and Terminology Preferences in Greek-speaking Autism Communities
f0537a668a622812ac3a4bca08bbb6ccd4141ecf.abstract: The language used to discuss autism both reflects and shapes perceptions of Autistic people, yet research on terminology preferences has largely been confined to English. This study examines autism-related terminology in Greek. A sample of 1,006 Greek-speaking adults (124 Autistic adults, 434 parents/caregivers, and 448 professionals) completed an online survey, selecting, from a list of 61 terms, those they use to refer to autism, Autistic people, autism-related difficulties, and non-autistic people, and explained their choices. Data were analysed using demographics-adjusted group comparisons, principal component analysis, and thematic analysis. The groups shared a core vocabulary (“autism”, “difficulties”, “is on the autism spectrum”) but differed in their use of 39 terms, with small effects, and the main contrasts persisted after demographic adjustment. Autistic adults preferred identity-first and neurodiversity terminology, professionals favoured clinical terminology, and parents/caregivers resembled professionals on identity terms and Autistic adults on clinical terms. Identity and clinical vocabularies were independent dimensions on which every group was represented. Open-ended responses tied these choices to identity among Autistic adults, others’ reactions among parents/caregivers, and audience and setting among professionals. We discuss these findings in the context of autism research and their implications for practice and public discourse.

title: Kinship Innovation Model: Citizens Responses to Protective Policies in the Indonesia-Timor Leste Border Area
container-title: Bulletin of Social Studies and Community Development
6dc809eece9e4471452586258f741a9ea6ba50e6.abstract: This study explores how COVID-19 mitigation policies trigger deviant adaptation among border residents. This article uses a qualitative approach with a case study research strategy. To ensure data representation, the author uses multiple relevant information sources and conducts in-depth, semi-structured interviews with informants aware of and involved in illegal economic activities, drawing on rational choice theory and anomie. Meanwhile, the study conducts internal validity, reliability, construct validity, and external validity tests to ensure research quality through a data-source triangulation strategy. The findings of this study elaborate on Merton's innovation in the context of rural communities in border regions of related countries, where illegal sociological-based economic activities not only maintain kinship solidarity but also serve as justifications for survival that transcend state authority. This article concludes that Haumeni Ana residents' kinship innovations respond to protectionist policies and weak state structures in peripheral areas. Addressing these structural problems requires strengthening the state apparatus and revitalizing border market governance to reflect residents' needs and characteristics. Keywords: Border market revitalization, COVID-19 mitigation, Illegal economic activity, Kinship innovation, Protectionist policies.

title: ‘Chemsex’ then and now – towards a ‘6Ws’ model for functional analysis and configurational assessment that embraces phenotypic diversity
b51d1a607c9613dbb1e1f00d6f82729600072ffa.abstract: Background: Distinguishing problematic from non-problematic chemsex, or placing experience on a continuum of severity, generates limited information about why similar drug use can lead to different experiences and support needs. We propose considering how the circumstances of an encounter work together and change over time.Method: This think piece presents a selective conceptual synthesis of chemsex research and assessment approaches, informed by minority stress theory, drug, set and setting, functional analysis, and addiction science. Empirical studies inform the domains and the proposed relationships between them.Results: Six questions (who, what, why, with, where and when) describe the person, substances, functions, relationships, settings and timing within a changing chemsex configuration. Digital activity may connect these through partner contact, planning and support, and is an important emerging consideration. Three fictional vignettes illustrate different responses to comparable exposure. The person and therapist could each map the configuration, compare accounts and identify a focus for formulation and therapy.Conclusions: Assessment should determine how pleasure, protection and harm arise through interacting circumstances. The six Ws direct attention to these relationships and to differences between the person’s and therapist’s accounts. Participatory development and longitudinal evaluation are needed to establish whether this approach improves shared understanding, decisions and care.

title: A biclique-centric exponential random graph model for common-knowledge networks
container-title: Social Network Analysis and Mining
613643867bb818a8b0737065bc5bf69871218863.abstract: Abstract Common knowledge (CK) is a social phenomenon where individuals in a group share the same information and each knows that the others share it as well, recursively. This mutual awareness enables coordinated action and gives rise to contagion dynamics that differ from standard models such as threshold and susceptible-infectious-recovered processes. In Facebook networks, bicliques are key graph substructures for generating CK because all nodes in a biclique can share information through their walls. Motivated by the need to systematically study biclique structure and CK-based contagion, we develop a biclique-centric exponential random graph model (BC-ERGM). By incorporating a qualitative biclique term, the model is designed to generate new networks with biclique-related features similar to those of an original network, providing a framework for studying CK-based contagion on the generated networks. We also introduce a structural reduction approach to make model estimation more computationally feasible for large networks. We evaluate the framework using Erdős–Rényi (ER) graphs across multiple network sizes and average-degree settings and a stochastic block model (SBM) with pronounced community structure. In the ER experiments, BC-ERGM generally reproduces the structural properties and CK-based contagion dynamics of the original networks, while structural reduction lowers computational cost. In the SBM experiment, the edge-only, edge-plus-biclique, and edge-plus-2-star models reproduce network density similarly, but BC-ERGM more closely reproduces the biclique count, biclique-size distribution, and node-participation distribution.

title: Satellite-driven monitoring of suspended sediment concentration in large river systems: an application to the Loire River, France
container-title: Acta Geophysica
303b774f8d189e200a08b536ae4e0a3e648236d7.abstract: Abstract Suspended sediment concentration (SSC) is a key indicator of river morphodynamics and water quality, yet long-term spatial monitoring remains limited because in situ measurements are sparse and discontinuous. By integrating field observations with multispectral Landsat imagery, this study develops a satellite-based framework to estimate SSC along the Loire River (France) over the period 2005–2025 in low to medium flow conditions with an SSC below 100 mg/l. Reflectance data from Landsat 5, 7, 8, and 9 were extracted using Google Earth Engine and matched with in situ SSC measurements within a ± 5-day temporal window. A feed-forward neural network was trained to predict SSC from selected spectral bands (B2, B3, B4, B5, and B7), with separate models developed for low, intermediate, and high turbidity regimes to improve predictive stability, and then recombined to obtain a single model. This complete neural network achieved high performance ( R 2 = 0.941, RMSE = 3.78 mg/l, PBIAS = 6.53%). To enable large-scale operational mapping, the neural network predictions were approximated through a compact surrogate model based on quadratic feature expansion and ridge regression, maintaining strong accuracy in reproducing observed SSC ( R 2 = 0.890, RMSE = 5.17 mg/l, PBIAS = 9.92%). The surrogate model was implemented in Google Earth Engine to generate spatially continuous SSC maps along the river corridor. The proposed approach demonstrates the capability of combining machine learning and optical satellite imagery to efficiently reconstruct SSC patterns in the Loire River and provides a scalable framework for monitoring suspended sediment dynamics in large river systems, in particular during low to medium flow conditions.

title: Artificial intelligence and environmental sustainability in Egypt and the UAE: a comparative study of policy maturity and future roadmaps (2015–2030)
container-title: Review of Economics and Political Science
8d99c94deffb27a12a4b645d555e5012db76de6e.abstract: Purpose This study investigates the evolution and future trajectory of artificial intelligence (AI) in advancing environmental sustainability in Egypt and the United Arab Emirates (UAE) from 2015 to 2030. It analyzes how these distinct governance models, centralized policy capacity vs rapid technology-led implementation leverage AI to bridge the “Policy-to-Action” gap regarding resource scarcity and long-term climate resilience. Design/methodology/approach The research employs a longitudinal comparative case study methodology utilizing qualitative document analysis and thematic process tracing to systematically evaluate national AI strategies and legislative frameworks from 2015 through to 2030 strategic targets. It utilizes 2026 benchmarks, including the Government AI Readiness Index 2025 (Oxford Insights, 2026), to assess AI efficacy in water management, energy systems, and urban planning. Findings The analysis reveals a significant policy divergence: the UAE has transitioned to mandatory AI-driven climate reporting via Federal Decree-Law No. 11 (2024a), while Egypt has established global leadership in “Policy Capacity,” achieving a perfect score of 100/100 and ranking 1st in Africa in the 2025 AI Readiness Index. Both nations successfully deploy AI for water management; however, the UAE leads in urban “Net Zero” integration and operational efficiency (e.g. 95% water savings in AI-managed agriculture), while Egypt excels in localized strategic alignment and “Sovereign AI” infrastructure. Findings reveal that while the UAE's Implementation-First model drives faster infrastructure deployment, Egypt's Policy-First approach fosters deeper institutional ownership, though both face a critical energy-water-AI paradox that threatens 2030 sustainability targets. Originality/value This paper provides an original comparative treatment of Arab AI governance by incorporating 2025–2026 strategic updates, including the UAE's January 2026 integration of the National AI System as a Cabinet advisory member. It introduces a novel framework the Policy-to-Action Bridge, highlighting AI as a central pillar of modern environmental legislation and procedural justice rather than merely a technical instrument.

title: Generative Artificial Intelligence and Large Language Models as a Digital Assistant for Power System Operators
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI-Driven Sustainable Energy Systems
43f02e9dd2362d62f0781c1271492951a9157aa0.abstract: Power-system operation is safety-critical: personnel integrate data, alarms, outages, switching requests, contingency analyses, grid-code rules, and cybersecurity constraints. This review assesses evidence, rechecked through May 31, 2026, on GenAI and large language models (LLMs) for operator support. It covers research, reports, standards, regulations, preprints, and industry initiatives, distinguishing retrieval-grounded systems, domain-adapted LLMs, time-series foundation models, tool-using agents, and digital-twin verification. It proposes a supervised assistant in which the LLM orchestrates and explains but is not operational truth. Near-term uses include document retrieval, regulatory interpretation, training, summaries, and explanations of approved calculations. Evidence does not support autonomous transmission-level actions. Deployment requires traceable sources, current models, restricted tools, cybersecurity boundaries, adversarial testing, human approval, and audit trails.

title: How to Optimize Electric Vehicles Using Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML)

7136bf72ac9299b116ba5c8813a99f469355cc31.abstract: Optimizing electric vehicles (EVs) through Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) is critical for addressing adoption barriers such as range anxiety and battery degradation. This chapter explores the transition from static, rule-based systems to dynamic, self-learning frameworks across Battery Management Systems (BMS), Predictive Energy Management (PEM), and Eco-Driving and Auxiliary (EDA) systems. By leveraging advanced methodologies like Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL), Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks, and Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs), these intelligent systems can enhance energy efficiency by up to 30% and extend battery life by nearly 40%. The discussion highlights how predictive analytics optimize real-time power allocation, regenerative braking, and thermal regulation. Despite challenges like high computational costs and cybersecurity risks, the integration of edge computing and V2G technology positions AI as a cornerstone for modernizing automotive operations and achieving a sustainable, software-defined transportation ecosystem.

title: Unpacking the Adoption of AI Decision Support for High-Risk Pregnancy Detection by Health Workers in Morocco: Embedded implementation research
container-title: Oxford Open Digital Health
567428cbbe72269e0c30883f91c09798cb82ffcb.abstract: ABSTRACT Artificial intelligence (AI) Clinical decision support systems (CDSS-AI) have proven useful for early screening, detection, and rapid diagnosis of maternal and perinatal morbidity and mortality, as well as for timely referrals of high-risk maternal cases. Only a few CDSS-AI have been implemented in maternal and neonatal health (MNH) in the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) region. In Morocco, reducing the maternal mortality ratio remains a significant challenge, particularly in remote rural areas. These high mortality rates are attributed to the first and third delays in the Three Delay Model. To address these delays, we co-developed a web-based and mobile app CDSS-AI, called “Oumoumati”, with the Ministry of Health, and implemented it in eight rural primary health centres in Al Haouz province. We adopted an embedded implementation design. We interviewed twelve purposefully selected stakeholders, including midwives and health managers. Data analysis employed deductive coding informed by a realist synthesis while remaining sensitive to emergent inductive findings. Thematic analysis was structured using the Context-Mechanisms-Outcomes heuristic. Our study findings showed that the utilisation and adoption of CDSS-AI is conditioned by systemic intertwined multilayered factors: The general context (e.g., resources), health system context (e.g. professional recognition), organisational context (e.g. managerial support), intervention characteristics (e.g. ease of use), and individual capacities (self-confidence). Our project highlighted that the ethical, responsible, and contextualised use of AI may contribute to alleviating gender issues and inequitable access to care for women residing in remote, underserved areas, provided it is co-designed with trained frontline workers and empowered local communities.

title: Towards Transforming Maternal Health in Pakistan Through Equitable, Context-Aware AI for Early Detection of Gestational Diabetes Mellitus (GDM)
container-title: Oxford Open Digital Health
1f4086ae3c5e353ecefcc1f5712755bd1e98ab84.abstract: Abstract This study presents AI-GDMP, an AI-enabled risk prediction tool developed to support early detection of Gestational Diabetes Mellitus (GDM) among pregnant women attending a tertiary hospital in Islamabad, Pakistan. GDM diagnosis relies on mid-pregnancy oral glucose tolerance testing (OGTT) performed between 24– 28 weeks of gestation. By focusing on the first trimester and utilising non-invasive, low-cost features, AI-GDMP offers a potentially equitable and accessible approach to early high/low-risk classification, particularly valuable in resource-constrained antenatal settings. By flagging high-risk women early in pregnancy, the tool opens a wider window for lifestyle modification, nutritional counselling, and closer follow-up before overt hyperglycaemia develops. The AI model was trained and validated on retrospective data from a JCI-accredited tertiary care hospital in Islamabad (2015–2024): eligible OGTT-linked pregnancies were digitized and screened (n = 3,748), yielding a final analytic cohort of 3,102 pregnancies (1,352 GDM; 1,750 non-GDM) with a stratified 80/20 train–test split (n = 2,481/621). A structured feature engineering pipeline reduced 93 candidate variables to 49 early-pregnancy predictors, with additional reduced feature sets (29 and 25 predictors) derived using Lasso- based selection. Among multiple machine learning approaches, the Random Forest classifier delivered the most promising results on the independent hold-out test set, achieving an AUC-ROC of 0.88, an accuracy of 77.9%, and a recall of 75.9%. Data collection followed ethical protocols, including IRB approval and anonymized patient records. The trained-model was integrated into a clinical software environment, enabling real-time high/low-risk output through a physician dashboard and provides a foundation for prospective validation and equity-focused evaluation in Phase 2.
