396533e60035866b42defb080e313a182f64fdcf.abstract: The transition to a green hydrogen economy is impeded by two computational and physical challenges: huge overpotential losses in water electrolysis and thermoacoustic/flashback instabilities when hydrogen combusts directly. The use of conventional high-throughput screening of electrocatalysts relying on Density Functional Theory is computationally infeasible in large compositional spaces, while H flame direct numerical simulation suffers from extreme multi-scale turbulence-chemistry interactions. In this chapter, we offer a combined machine learning method, integrating material-level electrocatalyst discovery with system-level combustion control. Firstly, we test ensemble tree models and Graph Neural Networks for forecasting adsorption free energies at transition metal hydroxides, alloys and high-entropy surfaces. Then we describe reduced-order surrogate models, like CNN-LSTMs, Autoencoders and PINNs to combust hydrogen-fueled internal combustion engines and gas turbines for prediction of flashback, identification of thermoacoustic modes, and reduction of NOx emissions in real time.

title: AI-Driven Lightweight Conductive Materials for Energy-Efficient Embedded IoT Electronics in Aerospace

a55b89f2fb3987d422ba86cb68582ebdb3cdab08.abstract: In the evolution of aerospace systems, the integration of lightweight conductive materials in embedded Internet of Things (IoT) electronics plays a pivotal role in enhancing performance. These materials are essential for optimizing electronic devices used in monitoring, control, and communication systems under space and airborne conditions. The aerospace sector demands weight reduction while maintaining high-performance properties, driving advancements in conductive materials. This chapter reviews the design, fabrication, and application of lightweight conductive materials for aerospace IoT electronics, with a focus on optimizing energy efficiency. Various categories of conductive materials, such as composites, thin films, and nanomaterials, are examined in terms of their electrical conductivity, mechanical properties, thermal stability, and weight percentage values. Additionally, the chapter explores the challenges and opportunities of incorporating these materials in aerospace IoT applications that aim to meet the unique demands of the aerospace industry.

title: AI-Driven Battery Health Monitoring and Predictive Analytics for Sustainable Electric Vehicle Energy Systems

9d588e9311f2c0a9cd7ce1921d91a51a458080cd.abstract: This chapter presents an artificial intelligence-driven battery health monitoring framework for sustainable electric vehicle applications. It discusses battery parameters including State of Charge, State of Health, degradation characteristics, and Remaining Useful Life together with data acquisition, preprocessing, feature extraction, and normalization techniques for battery health prediction. Machine learning approaches such as Random Forest, Artificial Neural Networks, and Long Short-Term Memory networks are reviewed for degradation analysis and predictive maintenance. An experimental case study demonstrates the effectiveness of the developed framework in accurately estimating battery states and tracking degradation behavior. The chapter also explores intelligent battery management, fault diagnosis, digital twins, smart grids, Internet of Things, and Vehicle-to-Grid integration for future energy systems.

title: Electric Vehicle Smart Charging Systems

8e4f2ec5067466af773c092cab5826b145ff82be.abstract: The rapid growth of Electric Vehicles is transforming modern transportation while creating major challenges for power grid stability, including peak load demand, energy imbalance, and renewable energy integration. To address these issues, smart EV charging systems have emerged as intelligent solutions capable of optimizing charging operations according to grid conditions, electricity pricing, and user needs. This chapter presents a comprehensive review of Artificial Intelligence and optimization techniques applied to EV smart charging systems. It analyzes machine learning, deep learning, deterministic, stochastic, and heuristic optimization methods, as well as hybrid AI–optimization frameworks. The study highlights their benefits in improving charging efficiency, reducing operational costs, enhancing load balancing, and supporting grid stability. Furthermore, current limitations such as scalability, computational complexity, and data dependency are discussed, alongside research gaps related to renewable energy integration, decentralized control, and real-time adaptive management.

title: How to Optimize Electric Vehicles Using Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML)

7136bf72ac9299b116ba5c8813a99f469355cc31.abstract: Optimizing electric vehicles (EVs) through Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) is critical for addressing adoption barriers such as range anxiety and battery degradation. This chapter explores the transition from static, rule-based systems to dynamic, self-learning frameworks across Battery Management Systems (BMS), Predictive Energy Management (PEM), and Eco-Driving and Auxiliary (EDA) systems. By leveraging advanced methodologies like Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL), Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks, and Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs), these intelligent systems can enhance energy efficiency by up to 30% and extend battery life by nearly 40%. The discussion highlights how predictive analytics optimize real-time power allocation, regenerative braking, and thermal regulation. Despite challenges like high computational costs and cybersecurity risks, the integration of edge computing and V2G technology positions AI as a cornerstone for modernizing automotive operations and achieving a sustainable, software-defined transportation ecosystem.

e9afe305db4f44eeadf11aafb47f5676e6b636dc.abstract: The rapid growth of Electric Vehicles (EVs) in emerging economies of the world, such as India, has created a pressing demand for Battery Health Monitoring Systems. While Lithium-ion batteries, being the most common power source for EVs which operates in a range of environmental and operating conditions, their performance is affected by various environmental factors. Therefore, estimating the State of Health (SOH) is crucial to evaluating the aging of the batteries. This chapter proposes an artificial intelligence–based framework to address the heterogeneous conditions of the Indian EV ecosystem by utilizing a Temporal Convolutional Network (TCN) and the ExtraTrees ensemble classifier. In addition to conventional battery parameters, environmental stress factors are also incorporated into the framework using meteorological data obtained from the NASA POWER database. Experimental evaluation was carried out and obtained an accuracy of 91.50% and a value of 0.9772 for the AUC-ROC metric, proving the effectiveness of the proposed framework for reliable battery health estimation.

title: AI and Machine Learning Approaches to Address Cybersecurity Challenges in Smart Grid Systems

0b9ba87f4a19e4d12b8440a82ac46d2c3f3b2901.abstract: Smart grid systems have been utilized with artificial intelligence (AI) which has substantially improved their efficiency and reliability. Nevertheless, with the development of smart grids into more intricate, networked, and data-intensive systems, a smart grid is becoming more susceptible to cybercrime. The chapter handles the problem of cybersecurity available within smart grid systems shedding light on the especial vulnerabilities that lies in the fact that they are digital and automated. It talks about the application of AI-based solutions to deal with such risks and it focuses on approaches that include anomaly detection, real-time threat responsiveness, and forecast risk. Besides, the chapter is also about AI aimed at protecting the communication network and providing more effective identification processes, and autonomic safe work. Through interpretation of case studies and projections in the real world, this paper gives a holistic idea of how AI can enhance the cybersecurity infrastructure in smart grid infrastructures.

title: Detection of Anomalies and Electricity Theft in Smart Grids Using Variational Autoencoders (VAE) and Time Series Analysis

1733456c27aaf37eee6c7d368568452fec41f37d.abstract: The proposed approach to detecting electricity theft and abnormal consumption in smart grids using a variable-parameter autoencoder is presented. With the introduction of smart meters, traditional verification methods struggle to handle large volumes of data and often miss instances of fraud disguised as normal consumption. The proposed model combines convolutional and LSTM layers to capture both local patterns and long-term dependencies, feeding the data into a variable-parameter autoencoder that models the probability distribution of normal consumption behavior. Experiments were conducted on open datasets containing labeled hourly consumption data with various theft types, including mechanical tampering and data manipulation. Preprocessing included normalization and extraction of dynamic features, such as volatility and interphase correlations. Detection performance was evaluated using precision-recall curves and the F-score due to strong class imbalance.

a4c69d2d3f388b09d23e5a415fd3321cd4c255fd.abstract: This article examines how the use of machine learning in Smart Grid forecasting turns predictive models into targets of cyberattacks. Small, carefully chosen distortions of telemetry, training data, or federated updates can shift forecasts of load, renewable generation, reserves, and grid stability without clear signs of failure. The review systematizes adversarial attack scenarios by model access, impact goal, lifecycle stage, and implementation level in digital infrastructure. It also highlights what makes energy time series different from images and ordinary tabular data: temporal structure, cross-channel consistency, and physical plausibility must be preserved. The paper analyzes resilience measures — anomaly detection, adversarial training, secure aggregation, physics-informed hybrids, and data integrity monitoring — with attention to computational cost and real-time use. Further research should focus on realistic black-box attacks, cascading effects, and engineering criteria for trusting predictive services.

Grounded in consumer law and constitutional principles under Articles 14, 19, and 21, it advances a case for statutory limits prioritizing child dignity and autonomy.

24a3c19b0daa4623298ba63af7df9b13718df0f6.abstract: This chapter looks at the idea of Algorithmic Childhood, which looks at how AI-driven personalization, algorithmic exposure, datafication, and behavioural nudging transform children online experiences and consumer identities. 9a1a337e1b2937ac4af2d2775b27805a3ce8499b.abstract: Artificial intelligence has transformed social media into adaptive persuasion systems that learn from and optimize for each child's behavior. This chapter shows how AI-driven curation undermines parental authority through qualitative analysis of Slovenian parents. Based on 14 in-depth interviews with parents of 22 children, we identify “algorithmic entrapment,” where engagement-maximizing systems override parental boundaries, exploit developmental vulnerabilities, and foster dependencies resistant to intervention. Parents recognized addiction-like symptoms but had a limited understanding of underlying AI mechanisms such as recommendation systems, predictive analytics, variable rewards, and personalized optimization. A “Surveillance Capitalism and Childhood” framework is proposed to explain how data extraction and attention monetization conflict with children's developmental needs. Protecting children requires shifting beyond parental responsibility toward governance solutions, including transparency mandates, limits on persuasive AI targeting minors, and independent audits.

9551deacb2f585906f3298c74c3b05f1921605f7.abstract: Whether driven by regulation or the market, pure protective responses are becoming less tenable as AI systems become more integrated into commercial ecosystems surrounding children. title: AI Literacy

87a810168d220e42586510068471834bc1db6970.abstract: Children in contemporary school settings are daily consumers of AI-generated content — whether they know it or not. Recommendation feeds, synthetic images, AI-drafted text, and algorithmic advertising have become routine features of childhood digital experience, yet most K–12 curricula offer little preparation for navigating these environments critically. This chapter argues that schools bear a genuine responsibility to address this gap through deliberate, grade-appropriate AI literacy education oriented not merely toward using AI tools, but toward questioning and evaluating what those tools produce. Drawing on recent empirical work and theoretical scholarship across AI literacy, media education, and ethics, the chapter traces a developmentally staged curriculum pathway from early childhood awareness through secondary-level civic and ethical reasoning, while also highlighting key challenges in implementation such as teacher readiness, assessment alignment, and the limited geographic distribution of existing research.

title: Curriculum Development for AI Literacy in Schools

48f5f323ea3fb2f7789d2937410b6f74e253e184.abstract: Artificial intelligence has infiltrated the digital landscape of children at an extremely fast rate, affecting the way children learn, communicate and access information. Experiential learning, gamification, and project-based assessments are some of the pedagogical strategies favored with the help of teacher training and alignment of policies. Finally, the chapter makes AI literacy a key factor to creating digitally resilient citizens who are capable of operating in algorithmically mediated spaces in a responsible, reflective and ethical manner.

eabdf13bce65d9c835bad254e966a1d5672132c4.abstract: Children today are growing up in digital environments where Artificial Intelligence (AI) plays a central yet often invisible role in shaping their experiences. title: Exploring AI-based teleorientation for the sexual and reproductive health of Spanish- and Quechua-speaking adolescents: a technology acceptance study
container-title: Oxford Open Digital Health
ca7fe9a8f94e5435dd342dbff7db0c6fd98892e4.abstract: Abstract Background Geographical, sociocultural, and confidentiality-related barriers continue to limit adolescents' and young people's access to sexual and reproductive health information. Objective To evaluate the acceptance of an AI-based teleorientation chatbot for sexual and reproductive health using the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM). Methods A cross-sectional study was conducted with 113 Quechua-speaking high school students in Ayacucho, Peru, who interacted with a bilingual (Spanish/Quechua) AI chatbot over a three-months period. Data collected using an extension of the Technology Acceptance Model 3 (TAM 3) were analysed with PLS-SEM. Results Perceived Ease of Use (PEOU) was the main determinant of Behavioral Intention to Use (BI; β = 0.53, p &lt; 0.001), confirming the role of Ease of Use in technology adoption. Perceived Trust (PT) had a significant positive effect on PEOU (β = 0.56, p &lt; 0.001) and a significant negative effect on Perceived Risk (PR; β = -0.69, p &lt; 0.001). The negative correlation of PR and the other constructs indicated that reducing perceived risk is important for technology adoption. Contrary to TAM theory, Perceived Usefulness (PU) was not a significant predictor of BI (β = 0.13). Conclusions This study demonstrates that trust and ease of use are key factors influencing adolescents’ acceptance of AI-based health chatbots in multilingual environments. The findings suggest that culturally adapted digital tools can help reduce barriers to accessing sexual and reproductive health information when they prioritize simplicity, cultural relevance, and user trust. These results provide valuable insights for the design of youth-centred digital health interventions in diverse contexts.

title: Microwave dielectric property reconstruction of healthy and tumor rat breast tissues from in vivo measurements using generative AI
container-title: Physics in Medicine & Biology
6f396cb1a9a95edbc7d663997357931373fe0546.abstract: Abstract Objective. Rapid identification of suspicious breast lesions remains challenging, since pathological analysis following biopsy requires hours to days, limiting real-time decision-making, particularly during surgical procedures. Open-ended coaxial probe (OECP)-based methods have shown promise for characterizing target tissues through estimation of dielectric properties (DPs) from the measured reflection coefficient ( S 11 ). Conventional DP calculation from OECP measurements S 11 is commonly performed using iterative methods, while recent studies have also explored artificial intelligence (AI)-based approaches for DP estimation. In these studies, AI models were developed using either synthetic datasets or limited ex vivo measurement data. In contrast, this study presents a generative AI approach for direct estimation of frequency-dependent DPs from in vivo measurements of healthy and tumor rat breast tissues. Approach. Measurements were acquired over the 0.5–6 GHz frequency range. Conditional generative adversarial network (cGAN) and conditional variational autoencoder (cVAE) were employed to learn the nonlinear mapping between the measured S 11 responses and the corresponding relative permittivity ( ε ′ ) and dielectric loss factor ( ε ′ ′ ). Furthermore, model performance was evaluated using dependency-preserving metrics, including copula log-likelihood and Kendall’s τ , together with regression metrics such as root mean square error (RMSE), symmetric mean absolute percentage error, weighted mean absolute percentage error, and coefficient of determination ( R 2 ). In addition, the estimated DP responses were fitted to a one-pole Cole–Cole model using median normalized nonlinear least squares optimization to extract the corresponding parameters ( ε s , ε ∞ , τ , α , σ ). Main results. The lowest RMSE values for healthy and tumor tissues were 0.98 and 2.90, achieved by the cVAE and cGAN models, respectively. The mean absolute percentage deviations, Δ ( ε c ) , between the Cole–Cole-fitted and reference DPs were 2.99% for healthy tissues and 5.05% for tumor tissues. Significance. These findings demonstrate the feasibility of generative AI-based, non-iterative DP reconstruction directly from in vivo OECP measurements.

title: Novelty or eeriness? Investigating consumer responses to AI-generated product images through expectancy violation theory
container-title: Journal of Research in Interactive Marketing
887864754512a1ae8f592d2397ed290befbca8bd.abstract: Purpose Drawing on Expectancy Violation Theory, this study examines how product image creator identity (AI vs. human) influences purchase intentions and the underlying psychological mechanisms. Design/methodology/approach Three online experiments examined consumers' attitudes toward AI-generated product images and purchase intentions toward the featured products, assessed how these evaluations deviated from expectations associated with human-created images, and identified conditions under which artificial intelligence (AI) imagery was more or less effective in shaping consumer responses. Data were analyzed in Statistical Package for the Social Sciences using Multivariate Analysis of Variance and Multivariate Analysis of Covariance, with serial and moderated mediation analyses conducted using the PROCESS macro. Findings Consumers consistently prefer human-created product images and perceive them as more novel, whereas AI-generated images evoke greater eeriness. Perceived novelty, eeriness, positive and negative expectancy violations, and attitudes mediate the relationship between image creator identity and purchase intention. Product type serves as a boundary condition, with AI-generated images evaluated more favorably for search products than for experience products. Originality/value This research identifies positive and negative expectancy violations as central psychological mechanisms shaping consumer responses to AI-generated product images. By highlighting product type as a boundary condition, it helps reconcile mixed findings in the AI-generated marketing literature and provides actionable guidance for the strategic use of AI-generated product imagery.

title: Explainable AI-based framework for 3D structural as-built modeling of aging buildings in Korea using laser scanning
container-title: Engineering, Construction and Architectural Management
9d0f972f52a37add6c936521dbd3ddf06dde8a83.abstract: Purpose This study proposes a framework for automatically generating 3D structural as-built models of aging buildings by predicting the structural dimensions of members concealed behind finishes using laser scanning and machine learning, particularly when original construction drawings are unavailable. Design/methodology/approach Laser scanning captures building geometry but includes both structural components and non-structural finishes (e.g. plaster), making it unsuitable for directly extracting structural dimensions. To address this, the proposed framework extracts geometric features from point clouds and employs machine learning techniques to predict structural dimensions of columns, beams, walls and slabs. Six machine learning models – Random Forest, XGBoost, LightGBM, CatBoost, Linear Regression and Support Vector Regression (SVR) – were trained using data collected on 1,560 column elements, 2,875 beam elements, 870 wall elements and 148 slab elements across 50 buildings and validated through two real-world case studies. Findings The best-performing model achieved MAPE of 10.51% for column width (95%CI: 8.47–12.71), 12.98% for column depth (95% CI: 10.86–15.41), 14.91% for beam width (95% CI: 13.63–16.15), 18.91% for beam depth (95% CI: 17.94–19.90), 10.42% for walls (95% CI: 8.89–12.00) and 10.70% for slabs (95% CI: 7.11–14.50). The predicted dimensions enabled reconstruction of 3D structural as-built models without relying on original drawings; the estimates are intended for planning-stage use. Practical implications The framework provides a non-destructive, full-coverage estimate of structural member dimensions that would otherwise require original drawings or local removal of finishes. In practice, it is intended to reduce reliance on destructive investigation and, through the SHAP analysis, indicates where confirmatory openings could be prioritized, thereby supporting planning-stage decisions for the maintenance and retrofitting of buildings whose drawings are missing or outdated. Originality/value This study is among the first to formulate the discrepancy between laser-scanned surface geometry and concealed structural dimensions as a prediction problem and to propose a framework that returns the predicted dimensions to a 3D structural as-built model. Machine learning provides the enabling component, and explainability is used to direct in situ verification rather than as a methodological contribution in itself.

title: Enhancing the Industrial Metaverse With Extended Reality
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Enhancing the Industrial Metaverse With Extended Reality
8c9989343b1d8ff24876fc27926ed580f327cbc9.abstract: The convergence of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Extended Reality (XR) is transforming industrial work by integrating intelligent decision-making, immersive technologies, and digital twins into human-centered workplaces. This review synthesizes research from Industry 4.0/5.0, digital twins, XR applications, and organizational studies to develop a unified understanding of AI-XR convergence. It proposes three frameworks—Industrial Metaverse Work Architecture (IMWA), AI-XR Industrial Transformation Framework (AXITF), and Human-AI-XR Integration Continuum (HAXIC)—to explain technological, operational, and organizational transformation. The chapter further presents theoretical propositions, governance imperatives, implementation strategies, and future research directions, providing a comprehensive foundation for responsible, human-centric industrial metaverse adoption.

title: Integrating XR, AI, Digital Twins, and IIoT in the Industrial Metaverse
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Enhancing the Industrial Metaverse With Extended Reality
fbf2ccf62346b15568a02d6b5e5729370294b911.abstract: This chapter examines the Industrial Metaverse as the convergence of Extended Reality (XR), Artificial Intelligence (AI), Digital Twins, and the Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) into persistent, immersive, and intelligent industrial ecosystems. Based on a structured narrative review, the chapter proposes a five-layer integration architecture and positions it against RAMI 4.0, IIRA, ISO 23247, and cyber-physical system models. It specifies synchronization requirements for XR-enabled Digital Twins, maps threats and security controls to each architectural layer, and reviews applications in manufacturing, energy, healthcare, and logistics. The chapter also examines generative AI, industrial foundation models, edge AI, and blockchain, together with their risks, and addresses governance, regulation, and human-machine collaboration. It concludes with an implementation pathway and research directions for secure, trustworthy, and human-centric Industrial Metaverse ecosystems aligned with Industry 5.0.

title: XR-Enabled Moodle Learning Ecosystems for the Industrial Metaverse
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Enhancing the Industrial Metaverse With Extended Reality
02afab14813059458f1c623082082cd38c0ca92f.abstract: This chapter, per the authors, presents a conceptual framework for using Moodle as the learning orchestration layer for XR-enabled workforce training in the industrial metaverse. It synthesizes recent research on extended reality, digital twins, artificial intelligence, learning analytics, and cybersecurity awareness to identify a gap between immersive industrial training prototypes and LMS-based evidence, assessment, and governance. The chapter proposes the XR-Moodle Industrial Learning Ecosystem (XMILE), which links Moodle courses, XR scenarios, digital twin states, AI-supported analytics, and cybersecurity controls. It explains the model's layers, data flows, use cases, evaluation metrics, and implementation roadmap for universities, technical training centers, and industrial organizations. The contribution is a practical structure for designing measurable, secure, and role-based training that supports skill transfer, cyber hygiene, and instructor decision-making.

title: AI as therapist or assistant? Opportunities and boundaries of artificial intelligence in mental health care
container-title: Mental Health and Social Inclusion
d8ff61e9a4fc5950274fbbae98c4af08416fbf29.abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine where generative artificial intelligence (AI) may add value in mental health care, where its clinical limits remain and how human oversight should change as AI assumes greater responsibility. Design/methodology/approach This opinion piece draws on recent randomized trials, systematic reviews, safety evaluations and international guidance on conversational AI in mental health. The evidence is interpreted through a three-level framework: supportive self-management, clinician-augmented care and autonomous clinical care. Findings AI-supported interventions can improve symptoms of depression and anxiety in some settings and may widen access to low-intensity support. However, evidence remains heterogeneous and important concerns persist around suicide-risk responses, privacy, bias, over-reliance and accountability. Current evidence supports AI more strongly as an adjunct than as an autonomous therapist. Social implications Access alone should not be mistaken for inclusion. Safe mental health AI also requires attention to digital access, language, culture, affordability and routes to human care. Originality/value The paper proposes a practical clinical hierarchy in which the evidence threshold, regulatory scrutiny and human oversight increase with the clinical responsibility assumed by AI.

title: Practice Briefing: From automation to delegation – governing generative AI in property investment
container-title: Journal of Property Investment & Finance
0d8441e184bb520c85f45164a8740e5739b4e1e5.abstract: Purpose Most real estate organisations approach artificial intelligence with the question “what can we automate?” This paper argues that the framing is wrong for generative AI, whose highest-value uses in property investment are not the automation of known processes but the delegation of judgement-laden work – and that the industry's default safeguard, “a human in the loop”, is not a governance strategy. Design/methodology/approach A practice briefing combining the management literature on delegation and recent evidence on human–AI complementarity with the authors' experience of three years of executive education and advisory work with senior real estate professionals. Findings Generative AI creates most value where neither the process nor the output can be fully specified in advance – precisely where automation-era governance fails. Uniform human review predictably degrades into rubber-stamping as volumes grow. Effective governance separates two questions: what kind of work is being transferred, and how much the outcome matters. Practical implications A two-axis classification (is the process known? Is the output verifiable?) Sorts any task into one of four working modes – automate, assist, structure, delegate – and an accountability ladder scales oversight from logging to full human decision-making. Investment teams can apply the framework immediately by classifying tasks rather than jobs and reallocating scarce review capacity to where consequence is genuine. Originality/value The paper reframes AI adoption as a delegation-design problem continuous with management skills the industry already possesses, separates task classification from governance intensity and names the failure mode – accountability theatre – that uniform human review creates.

title: PixelVision: A Modular Web-Based Framework for AI-Assisted Biological Image Analysis Across Diverse Microscopy Modalities
container-title: Microscopy
d82f057493b9d8b5c12e3a6ea042659bef8ebfbc.abstract: Abstract The increasing volume and heterogeneity of microscopy data in biomedical research present challenges for automated image analysis and the integration of assay-specific computational methods. We developed PixelVision, a modular, web-based framework that integrates deep learning models, quantitative image analysis, and expert review across diverse biological imaging modalities. The framework supports single-organism imaging, two- and three-dimensional cell culture analysis, whole-slide imaging, and interactive annotation through a shared infrastructure for model deployment, version management, and data processing. Quantitative evaluations demonstrated application-specific classification and segmentation performance, with inference throughput of approximately seven high-resolution images per second on a single GPU. In a prospective zebrafish screening study, iterative model refinement using expert-reviewed classifications was associated with an increase in macro-averaged F1 score from 0.867 to 0.967 across three screening rounds. PixelVision provides a framework for integrating automated image analysis and expert assessment across heterogeneous microscopy workflows.

title: AI-personalised recommendations and brand trust: a dual-appraisal account of perceived diagnosticity and algorithmic persuasion awareness
container-title: Asia Pacific Journal of Marketing and Logistics
4e4ebf3bb779260b6b54d8220a10009d115eef87.abstract: Purpose This study examines the joint associations of perceived AI-personalised recommendations, perceived diagnosticity and algorithmic persuasion awareness with trust in the recommended brand. Design/methodology/approach A cross-sectional survey of 412 consumers in China who recalled a recent recommendation they perceived as AI-personalised was analysed using partial least squares path modelling. Findings Perceived personalisation was positively associated with diagnosticity (β = 0.472) and algorithmic persuasion awareness (β = 0.353). Diagnosticity was positively associated with brand trust (β = 0.413), whereas algorithmic persuasion awareness was negatively associated with it (β = −0.194). The corresponding indirect associations were 0.195 and −0.069. Research limitations/implications The cross-sectional, self-reported design limits causal and temporal interpretation. Experiments, observed exposures and longitudinal studies can test the proposed relationships and boundary conditions. Practical implications The findings suggest potential applications in recommendation design involving decision support, transparency and consumer control alongside behavioural performance. Social implications Consumer education could help consumers distinguish product relevance from the data use and commercial purpose underlying personalised recommendations. Originality/value The study extends recommendation research by examining perceived diagnosticity and algorithmic persuasion awareness jointly in relation to trust in the recommended brand. This focus complements work on recommendation-agent trust, trust in ad information and AI-related information disclosure.

title: Challenges and solutions for cross-regional collaboration in the construction industry of the GBA: using a human-AI collaborative qualitative analysis framework
container-title: Engineering, Construction and Architectural Management
1a83813a43c88812fb2906be886642e2b042cf38.abstract: Purpose Under the “One Country, Two Systems” framework, cross-regional collaboration in the construction industry of the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area (GBA) faces multiple barriers arising from institutional, managerial and cultural differences. Drawing on institutional theory, boundary-spanning theory and a project governance framework, this study systematically identifies challenges and solution pathways for cross-regional collaboration from the macro external environment to the micro project level. Design/methodology/approach The study examines eight representative cross-regional projects using a multi-case study design. The formal qualitative coding and cross-case analysis drew on 27 anonymized interview records from 23 unique participants across the eight cases. The broader body of primary interview material comprised approximately 200,000 Chinese characters, supplemented by field notes, project materials and secondary documentation to support contextual understanding and triangulation. The study developed a human-AI collaborative qualitative analysis framework in which ChatGPT and Google Gemini assisted axial coding and pattern identification, while researchers retained responsibility for open coding, contextual validation, final codebook decisions and theoretical interpretation. Findings The study identifies a three-level structural model of barriers and responses. Institutional heterogeneity and fragmented governance at the macro level constitute primary structural bottlenecks. These constraints increase resource costs and generate conflicts in organizational routines at the meso level, ultimately producing authority-responsibility imbalances and localization dilemmas at the micro level. To address these, the study proposes a three-level solution framework comprising macro-level institutional integration, meso-level strategic innovation and micro-level refined governance. Originality/value This study provides a comprehensive multi-level analysis of cross-regional collaboration specific to the GBA construction industry, linking macro policy research with micro-level project management. Methodologically, it documents a human-AI collaborative qualitative analysis framework in which AI assists axial coding and pattern comparison, while researchers retain responsibility for contextual interpretation and theoretical development. The findings suggest that qualification recognition, organizational capability building and project-level responsibility arrangements should be developed in concert.

title: The motivational gain control effect: mechanisms of predictive load and brand signal-to-noise ratio on danmaku interaction with AI advertising
container-title: Online Information Review
08c4b1b05bc220d127972f129a2868abce8ea41c.abstract: Purpose This study develops the motivational gain control model, examining how dual cognitive demands of AI-generated advertising – internal decoding burden from structural transitions and external attributional ambiguity from executional convergence – jointly influence real-time audience interaction. Predictive load captures expectation-updating demand across adjacent stages; brand signal-to-noise ratio (BSNR) captures attributional clarity relative to competitors, constituting two dimensions of cognitive decoding valence whose evaluative meaning depends on product involvement. Design/methodology/approach Using panel data from 248 AI-generated advertisements and their danmaku interactions – synchronous viewer comments overlaid on video – on a major Chinese video platform, each divided into five periods, a panel vector error correction model estimates short-run and long-run effects and product involvement's moderating role. Findings For low-involvement products, content-level predictive load suppresses danmaku interaction while BSNR enhances it across both horizons. For high-involvement products, the positive effect of BSNR is significantly attenuated, whereas the negative effect of predictive load is only marginally attenuated, mainly in the long run. The BSNR attenuation provides strong evidence against a pure resource-depletion account; the predictive load attenuation, though marginally significant, is directionally consistent. Together, these patterns support motivation-dependent valence reassessment. Cross-modal congruence exhibits non-monotonic temporal patterns distinct from content-level features. Originality/value This study provides evidence against the fixed valence assumption shared across processing fluency, competitive interference and elaboration likelihood frameworks, proposing motivation-dependent valence reassessment as an alternative mechanism. It jointly models internal narrative dynamics and external competitive similarity through predictive load and BSNR and employs danmaku interaction as a real-time behavioral trace of evaluative response in AI advertising research. Peer review The peer-review history for this article is available at: Link to the website.

title: Governing AI with Kaizen: technostress and continuous improvement in Italian public organizations
container-title: The TQM Journal
471d6e01bdd62b3801646b8171e69e48d0bcd109.abstract: Purpose The growing integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into Italian public administration raises a central question: can person-centred human resource management practices turn technology from a source of psychosocial strain into an enabler of continuous improvement? This paper explores how formalized and participatory governance of AI adoption, structured around three Kaizen principles, is associated with employee participation in digital change and with the technostress reported by public employees. Design/methodology/approach A theory-informed qualitative multiple-case study was conducted in five organizational cases, namely Italian public administrations engaged in digital transformation projects funded by the Piano Nazionale di Ripresa e Resilienza (PNRR). In each organization, a manager–officer dyad (10 participants in total) took part in narrative interviews held between October and November 2025, focused on lived experiences of AI adoption, perceptions of human resource management and professional engagement. Transcripts were analysed through deductive, theory-driven content analysis based on the three Kaizen principles (process orientation, step-by-step improvement and human capital orientation) and on the technostress dimensions, followed by within-case and cross-case comparison. Findings Across 10 participant accounts embedded within five organizational cases, practices consistent with Kaizen were associated, within the accounts, with distinct narrative profiles of technostress and engagement. Accounts reporting all three principles described active co-authorship, professional empowerment and emerging roles; accounts reporting none described persistent techno-anxiety, disengagement and eroding professional identity. Among the creators, techno-insecurity is the one most closely tied to how adoption is governed, and is typically accompanied by techno-anxiety as an affective strain response, while overload, invasion, complexity and uncertainty appear in association with specific operating conditions. Intermediate accounts varied with the missing principle and its hierarchical level. Originality/value This paper develops the joint Kaizen–STS framework as an original analytical lens for AI governance in public administration. It provides qualitative evidence that Kaizen-consistent HR governance is associated with less salient technostress, particularly in the governance-related dimensions emerging from the analysis, and with stronger reported participation, professional agency and more favourable organizational conditions for continuous improvement. The study therefore contributes to organization and human resource management research by proposing the vertical governance gap between managerial design and operational experience as a sensitizing concept and offers public managers a diagnostic framework for PNRR-funded digital transformation across heterogeneous public-sector settings.

title: Towards an AI Literacy Framework for Maritime English Education: Integrating Language, Professional, and Digital Competencies
container-title: LANCAH: Jurnal Inovasi dan Tren
236639692b02ff378d325cde7448cb13cf583416.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is increasingly influencing language education by providing opportunities for personalized practice, immediate feedback, and flexible access to learning resources. However, effective use of GenAI in Maritime English requires competencies beyond general language proficiency and basic technological skills. Maritime English involves specialized terminology, standardized communication, operational contexts, and professional requirements in which inaccurate or inappropriate AI-generated content may have practical consequences. This conceptual study develops an AI literacy framework for Maritime English education through a conceptual literature synthesis. The synthesis draws on literature published between 2020 and 2026, supplemented by earlier foundational works on AI literacy and English for Specific Purposes (ESP), as well as authoritative Maritime references, including IMO Standard Marine Communication Phrases and IMO Model Course 3.17. Sources were selected based on their relevance to AI literacy, generative AI in language education, ESP, learner autonomy, and Maritime English, with particular attention to their conceptual contributions and applicability to Maritime communication. The synthesis identifies digital-AI competence as the core AI literacy capability, supported by two contextual knowledge bases: language competence and professional Maritime competence. Language competence enables learners to evaluate AI-generated language, while professional Maritime competence supports the verification of terminology, operational relevance, and contextual appropriateness. Digital-AI competence enables critical and responsible interaction with AI systems, including prompt formulation, output evaluation, and information verification. The proposed framework provides a conceptual basis for integrating AI literacy into Maritime English education while maintaining linguistic and professional standards. Future empirical research is needed to operationalize and validate the framework among Maritime English learners, lecturers, and Maritime professionals.

title: AI-ASSISTED FEEDBACK IN TEACHING ENGLISH WRITING: A REVIEW OF RECENT EMPIRICAL STUDIES
container-title: Qo‘qon DPI. Ilmiy xabarlar jurnali
03236f6e5d54a867253461f00658b488510fbfc8.abstract: This article reviews recent empirical research on the feedback that artificial intelligence generates on students’ English writing. Eleven peer-reviewed, open-access sources published between 2020 and 2025 were selected and read in full: two meta-analyses, one systematic review and eight empirical studies, two of them conducted in Uzbekistan. The analysis was thematic and organised around four questions: how automated and AI feedback affects writing performance, how the quality of AI feedback compares with that of teacher feedback, how learners engage with and perceive AI feedback, and what role the teacher plays. Compared with control conditions, automated feedback has a medium overall effect on writing performance, but AI feedback shows no clear advantage over feedback from trained teachers or tutors.

title: FROM CEFR DESCRIPTORS TO AI-GENERATED FEEDBACK: RELIABILITY, VALIDITY, AND RESEARCH PRIORITIES FOR EFL WRITING ASSESSMENT IN UZBEKISTAN
container-title: Qo‘qon DPI. Ilmiy xabarlar jurnali
63063a0b5d1b269f3aeb30b9b30f4dbfbacb171f.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is increasingly used to support English as a Foreign Language (EFL) writing through automated comments, language correction, and rubric-based scoring. Yet the usefulness of these applications depends on whether their outputs are consistent, aligned with intended assessment criteria, and pedagogically appropriate. This critical narrative review examines selected research on large language models in writing assessment and considers implications for CEFR-aligned assessment in Uzbek higher education. The discussion is organized around three issues: rating reliability, validity of score interpretations, and the quality and use of AI-generated feedback. Existing evidence indicates that large language models can produce consistent rubric-based ratings under particular conditions, but consistency alone does not establish that a score validly represents writing proficiency or a CEFR level. Feedback may support revision, particularly when it addresses language form and textual organization, but learners and teachers still need to evaluate the relevance and accuracy of suggestions. The review identifies a context-specific research priority: comparing AI-generated judgments with trained human ratings using transparent CEFR-informed criteria and investigating how learners use the resulting feedback. Because this article is a critical narrative review rather than a systematic review or an original empirical study, its conclusions are provisional and should be followed by a documented literature search and local validation study.

title: An Agentic AI Framework for Autonomous Cross-View Kernel Rootkit Detection and Response in Cloud Environments
5f7a8f2d8cba98a65532469fffc939ef8f4a38b9.abstract: Abstract Kernel-level rootkits subvert the operating system to conceal the network ports through which they maintain covert channels, and cloud tenants who cannot access the hypervisor have few reliable defences. Existing detectors stop at a verdict, leaving investigation and response to human analysts and admitting a window during which an active rootkit persists. This paper presents an agentic AI framework that both detects and autonomously responds to kernel rootkits through port-level behavioural analysis. On cloud guests hosted on Google Cloud Platform, a kernel-mode Port Enumerator and a user-mode Port Monitor produce cross-view port lists whose discrepancy, formalized here as a temporal behavioural signal, is classified by a deep ensemble of CNN-LSTM, Bi-LSTM, Autoencoder and GAN. The resulting Rootkit/Benign verdict is handed to an LLM Agent Orchestrator that executes an autonomous perceive-plan-act-reflect loop, invoking security tools under human-in-the-loop oversight for high-impact actions. A second evidence channel is released with the paper as a labelled concealment matrix of 87 kernel rootkit samples described by a binary vector over a 968-entry dictionary of concealed objects, each carrying the technique it uses to hide. We give a mathematical model of the cross-view signal, the fused decision, and the agent’s utility-driven action selection. Evaluated on a Windows Server 2025 guest, the framework detects rootkits with a mean detection latency of 1.2 s while autonomously triaging confirmed threats; on the released concealment matrix the technique of a confirmed rootkit is recovered from its hook vector at 0.846 accuracy against a 0.713 majority-class rate, with the three-way distinction among inline, SSDT and IAT concealment still limited by class imbalance. The response layer is specified and instantiated but not yet measured; Section 5.6 states the protocol by which it will be tested.

title: AI-Based Interfacial Contact Area Prediction in 3D Granular Media: Benchmarking Volumetric CNN, GNN, and Classical Surface Meshing
c8cbccf9fab2a06604eb5d29bd07895d84e3ad07.abstract: Abstract Interfacial contact area between contiguous grains governs macroscopic elastic moduli, stress transmission chains, effective thermal and electrical conductivity, and solid-state diffusion rates in three-dimensional (3D) granular media. Standard characterization of X-ray micro-computed tomography (µCT) volumes relies on 3D Euclidean distance transform seeding and marker-controlled watershed segmentation followed by polygonal surface extraction via the Marching-Cubes algorithm (Lorensen & Cline, 1987). However, Cartesian voxelization introduces severe staircase terracing along curved inter-particle boundaries, inflating surface area measurements by 40% to 80%, while local mesh triangulation scales poorly to assemblies containing thousands of grains. Conducted under the supervision of Prof. Mayank Goswami , this study establishes a comparative benchmark of four data-driven surrogate architectures—an interpretable Random Forest ensemble, a 4-block 3D Convolutional Neural Network (3D CNN) operating on 48 3 binary dual-particle patches, a 3-layer bidirectional GraphSAGE Graph Neural Network (GNN) operating on the global contact graph G = (V, E) , and a multimodal Hybrid GNN + CNN fusion architecture—across 250 synthetic 3D granular phantoms (50,800 particles and 48,750 contact interfaces). Across 38 held-out test specimens (7,466 contact interfaces), we evaluate models under both DEM-coupled (known sphere geometry) and blind tomographic (voxel-only, zero metadata) operating regimes. When coupled with exact inter-particle distance and radius attributes, the 3-layer bidirectional GraphSAGE network achieves a mean absolute error (MAE) of 0.158 vx 2 , a root-mean-square error (RMSE) of 0.217 vx 2 , a mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) of 1.91% , and R 2 = 0.99999 at an inference latency of 2.89 ms per phantom , while the Random Forest baseline achieves R 2 = 0.99992 and MAE = 0.409 vx 2 . Crucially, an explicit feature-circularity ablation study demonstrates that removing pairwise distance and overlap features collapses tabular/graph accuracy to R 2 = 0.4387 (MAE = 44.68 vx 2 ), proving that inter-centroid geometry is physically indispensable; however, estimating these quantities 100% blindly from watershed-segmented voxels via principal inertia axes ( R̂ i = L maj,i /2, MAE = 0.048 vx) restores R 2 = 0.9959 (MAE = 3.35 vx 2 ) without ground-truth metadata. Furthermore, the purely image-based 4-block 3D CNN —which requires zero tabular or metadata inputs—achieves R 2 = 0.99788 and MAE = 2.434 vx 2 (166.23 ms/phantom), outperforming classical Marching-Cubes surface meshing (MAE = 42.750 vx 2 , MAPE = 72.24%, R 2 = 0.50471, 3,555.60 ms/phantom) by 17.6× in accuracy and 21.4× in speed. Scaling experiments up to N = 2,000 particles, overlap-depth stratification, per-particle contact area aggregation ( n = 6,879 active test grains), and domain adaptation to mildly non-spherical superellipsoids (3D CNN R 2 = 0.9979, MAE = 2.50 vx 2 ) establish practical guidelines, methodological limitations, and ethical safeguards for deploying AI surrogates in granular mechanics.

title: Acomparto: A RAG-Based Spanish Chatbot for postpartum care
container-title: Oxford Open Digital Health
6ddb0a6268726b9e0cad26a5ecc9826f65a23816.abstract: Abstract Nowadays, large language models (LLMs) have become fundamental for the development of conversational agents, which are increasingly adopted across sectors ranging from healthcare and education to customer-facing and organizational support services. When creating a chatbot, several considerations must be taken into account, such as personal data handling, communication strategies, and hallucination mitigation. Moreover, the application domain entails additional considerations regarding the source and quality of the information used. This paper presents a pipeline for integrating a locally hosted LLM into an artificial intelligence assistant, Acomparto, which specializes in evidence-based recommendations for postpartum care. From an implementation perspective, this work examines the practical deployment and integration of the proposed system in real-world maternal health contexts. Our pipeline incorporates a locally running model to mitigate the risk of third-party application programming interfaces using user data in other contexts. The proposed approach involves collecting, preprocessing, and refining textual data to enhance a pre-trained model using a retrieval augmented generation approach. Acomparto addresses one crucial topic: breastfeeding as a starting point. To evaluate our LLM chatbot, we combine standard natural language processing performance measures with expert domain assessments provided by medical and non-healthcare professionals. The results indicate that the pipeline improves the quality and relevance of LLM chatbot responses, particularly for users with limited access to conventional healthcare services . While not intended to replace healthcare professionals, Acomparto provides accessible and trustworthy support through a web-based platform. Additionally, key insights into LLM adaptation to non-English data are discussed, highlighting both the challenges and practical strategies to reduce invalid or misleading outputs.

title: Unpacking the Adoption of AI Decision Support for High-Risk Pregnancy Detection by Health Workers in Morocco: Embedded implementation research
container-title: Oxford Open Digital Health
567428cbbe72269e0c30883f91c09798cb82ffcb.abstract: ABSTRACT Artificial intelligence (AI) Clinical decision support systems (CDSS-AI) have proven useful for early screening, detection, and rapid diagnosis of maternal and perinatal morbidity and mortality, as well as for timely referrals of high-risk maternal cases. Only a few CDSS-AI have been implemented in maternal and neonatal health (MNH) in the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) region. In Morocco, reducing the maternal mortality ratio remains a significant challenge, particularly in remote rural areas. These high mortality rates are attributed to the first and third delays in the Three Delay Model. To address these delays, we co-developed a web-based and mobile app CDSS-AI, called “Oumoumati”, with the Ministry of Health, and implemented it in eight rural primary health centres in Al Haouz province. We adopted an embedded implementation design. We interviewed twelve purposefully selected stakeholders, including midwives and health managers. Data analysis employed deductive coding informed by a realist synthesis while remaining sensitive to emergent inductive findings. Thematic analysis was structured using the Context-Mechanisms-Outcomes heuristic. Our study findings showed that the utilisation and adoption of CDSS-AI is conditioned by systemic intertwined multilayered factors: The general context (e.g., resources), health system context (e.g. professional recognition), organisational context (e.g. managerial support), intervention characteristics (e.g. ease of use), and individual capacities (self-confidence). Our project highlighted that the ethical, responsible, and contextualised use of AI may contribute to alleviating gender issues and inequitable access to care for women residing in remote, underserved areas, provided it is co-designed with trained frontline workers and empowered local communities.

title: NatalIA: A Case Study in Prenatal Ultrasound Across Three Guatemalan Communities
container-title: Oxford Open Digital Health
e9c580dfc826dabb1f0480a5a9aa87f62aaa0c49.abstract: Abstract In many underserved areas, limited resources and underinvestment in training restrict access to high-quality medical care. NatalIA is an artificial intelligence (AI) based system designed to enhance obstetric ultrasound workflows in resource-limited settings. The system enables midwives to acquire ultrasound videos through blind sweeps using portable point-of- care devices, allowing for asynchronous specialist reviews while automatically identifying fetal views from the captured videos. This case study presents the validation, usability, and acceptance of the system in three different settings in Guatemala: an urban clinic, a rural health center, and an indigenous community center (ICC). In each setting, professional midwives (PM) received brief training in performing blind sweeps. They were later interviewed about their perceptions of the usability, cultural accessibility, and trustworthiness of the system. Patients were also surveyed to assess their confidence and comfort with the technology. The results showed that PM felt more confident in performing sweeps, as asynchronous specialist evaluations did not disrupt workflows or add pressure during examinations. Patients also responded positively, particularly when cultural needs were addressed. These findings suggest the potential for NatalIA and similar AI-assisted approaches to support efforts aimed at expanding equitable access to obstetric imaging. The study emphasizes the importance of engaging stakeholders early to foster trust and designing technologies that are tailored to local contexts.

title: Feasibility and Acceptability of a Chatbot for Pre-Exposure Prophylaxis (PrEP) Follow-up: A Formative Evaluation in a Public Sexual Health Clinic in Buenos Aires
container-title: Oxford Open Digital Health
85414590c5d5b5faef7fe2937d1c20107279ea20.abstract: Abstract Pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) is a key HIV prevention strategy for individuals at high risk of HIV acquisition. However, limited healthcare capacity can restrict access to PrEP services. Digital tools such as chatbots may help optimize follow-up by facilitating clinical preparation and capturing key information on adherence, tolerance, and side effects. This study describes the design and initial testing of a chatbot-based minimum viable product (MVP) for PrEP follow-up and explores barriers and facilitators influencing its acceptance in a large public sexual health clinic in Buenos Aires, Argentina. We conducted a qualitative formative implementation evaluation combining usability testing using a think-aloud protocol with semi-structured interviews. Fourteen participants in stable PrEP follow-up for more than six months interacted with the MVP chatbot and provided feedback on ease of use, perceived usefulness, clarity of language, relevance of content, and suggestions for improvement. All participants found the chatbot easy to use and valued its flexible response options. Most anticipated that its use could shorten clinic visits by facilitating information exchange prior to consultations, benefiting both patients and healthcare staff. Chatbot-delivered recommendations related to adherence and PrEP use were generally perceived as helpful. Only one participant expressed concerns regarding the security of sensitive data. Several participants suggested incorporating more personalized interactions and less rigid conversational flows. Importantly, none expected the virtual assistant to replace human interaction, emphasizing the continued importance of in-person consultations and clinical support. Overall, the chatbot was perceived as a feasible and acceptable tool for supporting PrEP follow-up and complementing human care. While data privacy remains an important consideration, these findings suggest that chatbot-supported digital tools may enhance PrEP care when integrated into existing, human-centered clinical practices.

title: Towards Transforming Maternal Health in Pakistan Through Equitable, Context-Aware AI for Early Detection of Gestational Diabetes Mellitus (GDM)
container-title: Oxford Open Digital Health
1f4086ae3c5e353ecefcc1f5712755bd1e98ab84.abstract: Abstract This study presents AI-GDMP, an AI-enabled risk prediction tool developed to support early detection of Gestational Diabetes Mellitus (GDM) among pregnant women attending a tertiary hospital in Islamabad, Pakistan. GDM diagnosis relies on mid-pregnancy oral glucose tolerance testing (OGTT) performed between 24– 28 weeks of gestation. By focusing on the first trimester and utilising non-invasive, low-cost features, AI-GDMP offers a potentially equitable and accessible approach to early high/low-risk classification, particularly valuable in resource-constrained antenatal settings. By flagging high-risk women early in pregnancy, the tool opens a wider window for lifestyle modification, nutritional counselling, and closer follow-up before overt hyperglycaemia develops. The AI model was trained and validated on retrospective data from a JCI-accredited tertiary care hospital in Islamabad (2015–2024): eligible OGTT-linked pregnancies were digitized and screened (n = 3,748), yielding a final analytic cohort of 3,102 pregnancies (1,352 GDM; 1,750 non-GDM) with a stratified 80/20 train–test split (n = 2,481/621). A structured feature engineering pipeline reduced 93 candidate variables to 49 early-pregnancy predictors, with additional reduced feature sets (29 and 25 predictors) derived using Lasso- based selection. Among multiple machine learning approaches, the Random Forest classifier delivered the most promising results on the independent hold-out test set, achieving an AUC-ROC of 0.88, an accuracy of 77.9%, and a recall of 75.9%. Data collection followed ethical protocols, including IRB approval and anonymized patient records. The trained-model was integrated into a clinical software environment, enabling real-time high/low-risk output through a physician dashboard and provides a foundation for prospective validation and equity-focused evaluation in Phase 2.

title: Assessing Socioeconomic Bias in AI-Powered Maternal Health Messaging: Evidence from Jacaranda Health’s PROMPTS Platform in Kenya
container-title: Oxford Open Digital Health
74c166ac509cfea4c48079f22557195c8417a57b.abstract: ABSTRACT Background In many low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), mothers lack timely, accurate health information, which can delay lifesaving care. Jacaranda Health’s PROMPTS platform reaches 3 million+ mothers in Kenya via SMS, using artificial intelligence (AI) to triage questions, provide rapid responses, and connect urgent cases to human agents. While AI can expand access, if not carefully designed it may reinforce inequities. This study examines whether PROMPTS’s AI models perform differently across socioeconomic groups. Methods We applied a four-phase bias assessment framework. First, we surveyed 4569 PROMPTS users across 22 counties and assessed socioeconomic vulnerability using a validated typing tool. Second, we examined whether training datasets reflected users across vulnerability strata. Third, we evaluated AI performance in classifying question topics. Finally, we audited AI-generated outputs for medical accuracy, grammar, and thoughtfulness, stratified by vulnerability. Results PROMPTS engages women across vulnerability levels. The most vulnerable mothers were less likely to ask questions, suggesting underrepresentation in training data. The AI model correctly classified 90% of questions, with no significant differences by vulnerability, though confidence was lower for messages from more vulnerable mothers. AI-generated responses were equally accurate across groups, but answers to more vulnerable users were sometimes rated as less thoughtful. Conclusion PROMPTS demonstrates a fair application of AI for maternal health, with strong performance across diverse groups. However, underrepresentation of vulnerable mothers and subtle differences in response quality highlight areas for improvement. Engaging vulnerable voices, embedding safeguards, and routine monitoring will be critical to ensure AI advances health equity in LMIC contexts.

title: Research and Development of AI-Powered Task-Shifting for High-Quality Obstetrics Ultrasound Services in Community Healthcare Settings: Real-World Implementation Experiences from an LMIC
container-title: Oxford Open Digital Health
58396b4e3bef28d032518e1ac8e1f795a769257d.abstract: Abstract Blind Sweep Obstetric Ultrasound (BSOU) paired with artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly proposed as a scalable approach to expand antenatal screening in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs). However, limited evidence exists on how to implement BSOU-AI systems within real clinical environments, where infrastructure, workflows, and human resource constraints differ substantially from research settings. This study reports implementation experiences from a multi-center BSOU-AI project across tertiary hospitals and community health facilities in Nepal. We collected more than 3000 BSOU datasets using minimally trained providers and handheld ultrasound devices, developed and iteratively refined a nine-sweep BSOU protocol, and coordinated with national stakeholders to ensure alignment with the Rural Obstetrics Ultrasound Program. Real-world deployment revealed major challenges including machine incompatibility, inadequate digital infrastructure, annotation bottlenecks, workflow mismatches in high-volume hospitals, and difficulty capturing rare complications which required continuous adaptation of protocols, staffing, and data-management systems. Engagement with Nepal’s Ministry of Health prompted the addition of an evaluation arm comparing BSOU-AI performance not only to radiologist scans but also to nurse-led rural ultrasound, reflecting the true standard of care. Our experience demonstrates that AI readiness in LMICs depends as much on implementation science as on algorithm development. We provide methodological insights and practical recommendations for designing BSOU-AI studies that are scalable, contextually grounded, and responsive to health-system realities.

title: An AI conversational assistant to support self-managed medication abortion in Colombia: development and early testing in a telemedicine pathway
container-title: Oxford Open Digital Health
c230a21c79bab4fca674bce9f837badae975e723.abstract: Abstract Colombia continues to face unsafe and informal abortions, with elevated risks in the Pacific region, where structural inequities and stigma persist despite a liberalized legal framework. Profamilia, a major sexual and reproductive health and rights (SRHR) provider, is expanding telemedicine to reduce these gaps. This case study describes the development and feasibility testing of an AI WhatsApp assistant for Profamilia’s medication-abortion telemedicine pathway to provide trusted information and navigation. Using Research-through-Design, Design Thinking and Agile sprints, we built an assistant grounded in local legal/clinical guidance, privacy-by-design (no identifiers), and human-in-the-loop escalation for risk and out-of-scope cases. After iterative internal validation, user-testing in three Pacific departments (Valle del Cauca, Cauca, Nariño; n=40; 605 questions) achieved 86.4% task success—defined as no Level-1 (high-risk) or Level-2 (service-flow) errors in responses—with 2.1% Level-1 errors. Users valued speed, clarity, trust and privacy. Priorities centred on interface/navigation microcopy and safety hardening to reduce Level-1 errors. Findings suggest early feasibility, safety and acceptability for a locally grounded assistant, with potential to bolster knowledge, support decisions and ease access to care. This case offers transferable insights for developing AI-enabled, rights-based SRHR tools. Next steps include a pilot to measure service-level and user-centred outcomes for equity-oriented scale-up.

title: Artificial intelligence-based strategy to support safe decision-making in adolescents and young people in prevention of unwanted pregnancy
container-title: Oxford Open Digital Health
9c84f67b9f8e47e0061e8a3ceae26478865aea64.abstract: Abstract In Colombia, teenage pregnancy is a serious and growing public health problem. This research aimed to use the understanding of cognitive aspects of adolescent pregnancy for planning and prevention of adolescent pregnancy. A study was carried out to assess the questions of adolescents and the answers of a conversational virtual agent, based on generative and responsible artificial intelligence, drawing on data gathered with prior approval of the Ethics Committee of the Faculty of Medicine of the National University of Colombia. The virtual assistant was provided with information by sexual health specialists and trained to give appropriate and understandable answers. It was tested on adolescent students of the Faculty of Medicine. Adolescents of both sexes from a school in Tumaco freely joined the project. For seven months, the interaction between adolescents and the virtual assistant was carried out. Likewise, surveys were carried out with participating teachers and students on the comprehension, acceptance of the virtual assistant and quality of the answers. There were 64 registered users, of which 38 used the application. The interaction between adolescents and the virtual assistant made it possible to identify the main doubts of users regarding sexual health. Topics related to contraceptive methods were highlighted. Likewise, an initial validation of the virtual assistant was possible.

title: Automatic detection of sexual and reproductive consults of people with disabilities from Electronic Health Records
container-title: Oxford Open Digital Health
da5871c5b23e8f8e9f4564125a304103839f8470.abstract: Abstract People with disabilities (PWD) often face barriers to accessing appropriate sexual and reproductive health (SRH) care, partly due to the underrepresentation of their needs in clinical data systems. Addressing how health systems can integrate inclusive and representative data practices is therefore essential for achieving equitable access to emerging AI-supported SRH services for PWD. This study responds to this policy challenge by examining how targeted dataset augmentation and intersectional model evaluation can improve AI-enabled decision support tools. We present a case study from Argentina, where clinicians, disability community representatives and data scientists co-developed a disability and SRH taxonomy and used it to annotate 3 300 free-text SRH consultation records for people with disabilities. Machine learning models trained on this dataset achieved 80% accuracy in identifying PWD or SRH-related content and 60% accuracy for records addressing both simultaneously, showing that it is feasible to automatically identify these consults, but at the same time highlighting the increased complexity of intersectional cases. Fairness assessments showed higher error rates for certain minority subgroups, like women in disability-related records and men in SRH-related records, highlighting the need for targeted data augmentation and model tuning. Our results show promise for the intended application, but underscore the importance of inclusive data curation and fairness-focused evaluation in building clinical decision support tools for marginalized populations. We have shown that, even with domain-expert engagement across all stages of project governance, in-depth, situated fairness analyses are crucial to make identifying SRH consults for PWD inclusive and equitable for minority groups.

title: Digital holography for the reconstruction of particles suspended in diamagnetic droplets levitated in a magneto‑gravitational trap
container-title: CI/CS: Computational Imaging, Compressed Sensing, and Sensors
ced8ef3e1f7a33f9ec900ccd855ca1b86e3da578.abstract: The theoretical study addresses the three-dimensional characterization of micrometric particles suspended in diamagnetic droplets, presenting a platform that combines digital holography and magneto-gravitational trapping to analyze particles between 1.5 μm and 6.0 μm directly within their aqueous environment. The equilibrium conditions of the droplet and the role of magnetic, gravitational, and capillary parameters governing the stability of the system are described, and integrated with the optical requirements needed to achieve high-resolution reconstructions.

title: The Development of a Fungicide Tolerance Phenotyping Assay Utilizing Digital Microscopy with the Obligate Biotroph Erysiphe necator
container-title: PhytoFrontiers™
c76e47be20eedb60d2716660642b6e82a7b55718.abstract: Grape powdery mildew ( Erysiphe necator ) poses a significant challenge to vineyards that is primarily managed through fungicide applications. However, the emergence of fungicide-tolerant populations necessitates the development of rapid phenotyping methods. Traditional approaches for obligate biotrophs, such as live leaf disk assays, are effective but labor-intensive and prone to error, which hinder throughput and accuracy. Using high-resolution automated digital microscopy, a novel phenotyping method capable of rapidly and objectively assessing E. necator germination was developed for strobilurin (quinone outside inhibitor [QoI]) and quinoxyfen fungicides. Notably, a multiclass image classification model based on conidia shape metrics can accurately distinguish conidia germination status while effectively eliminating image artifacts (accuracy > 95%). All isolates with the CYTB QoI resistance allele (A143) were discernable from wild-type isolates (G143) across four unique QoI fungicides. Additionally, isolates exhibiting reduced sensitivity to quinoxyfen in live leaf disk assays were correlated with higher germination rates in the described imaging-based in vitro assay. However, sterol demethylation inhibitor tolerance could not be accurately phenotyped. Compared with traditional live leaf disk assays or manually counted germination assays, the described imaging-based in vitro method offers notable advantages in terms of time and cost-effectiveness but is not suitable for all chemistries. This development in phenotyping technology not only enhances our ability to better characterize E. necator but also opens avenues for further research into quinoxyfen fungicide tolerance mechanisms.
