title: Effectiveness of Digital Health Interventions on Rehabilitation Outcomes in Patients After Total Knee Arthroplasty: Systematic Review and Network Meta-Analysis
container-title: Journal of Medical Internet Research
292ccdd184ddd5c5ebe032fd93a4584705f5980f.abstract: Abstract Background Total knee arthroplasty (TKA) is the most effective treatment for end-stage knee osteoarthritis, but some patients continue to experience persistent postoperative pain, stiffness, and impaired functional recovery. Digital health interventions are increasingly used in rehabilitation after TKA, but their comparative effectiveness remains unclear. Objective This study aimed to evaluate the effects of different digital health interventions on rehabilitation outcomes in patients after TKA and to compare and rank these interventions in terms of pain relief, active knee flexion range of motion (ROM), and knee function to provide evidence for selecting optimal rehabilitation strategies. Methods We searched PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, Web of Science, Google Scholar, Scopus, CINAHL, MEDLINE (via OvidSP), CNKI, Wanfang, and VIP to identify randomized controlled trials (RCTs) meeting the inclusion criteria. The RoB 2 tool (Risk of Bias 2; Cochrane) was used to assess risk of bias, and the confidence in network meta-analysis (CINeMA) framework was used to evaluate certainty of evidence. Traditional meta-analysis and network meta-analysis (NMA) were performed using Stata (version 17.0; StataCorp LLC). A random-effects model (DerSimonian-Laird method for estimating τ² ) was consistently used across all analyses. For outcomes measured with the same or convertible scales, mean differences (MDs) with 95% CIs were used to pool effect sizes. Surface under the cumulative ranking curve (SUCRA) values were calculated to summarize the ranking probabilities. Results A total of 36 RCTs involving 3067 patients after TKA were included. NMA results showed that compared with conventional rehabilitation (CR), for active flexion ROM, rehabilitation robot (RR; MD 8.96, 95% CI 5.86-12.05), mobile app–based telerehabilitation (MAT; MD 6.36, 95% CI 2.81-9.91), and virtual reality (VR; MD 5.92, 95% CI 2.94-8.90) were significantly superior to CR; for the Hospital for Special Surgery knee score, VR (MD 9.53, 95% CI 5.18-13.88), intelligent rehabilitation system-based telerehabilitation (MD 6.90, 95% CI 2.35-11.44), and RR (MD 5.32, 95% CI 1.61-9.04) were significantly superior to CR; for pain, RR and MAT had relatively high ranking probabilities, but the 95% CIs of most comparisons included 0; for the Western Ontario and McMaster Universities Osteoarthritis Index and Timed Up and Go test, only internet videoconference-based telerehabilitation and VR-based telerehabilitation, respectively, were significantly superior to CR. The certainty of evidence for most comparisons was low or very low. Conclusions Digital health interventions may improve pain, active knee flexion ROM, and knee function in patients after TKA. In the SUCRA ranking, RR, VR, and MAT showed favorable ranking probabilities; however, because the network was predominantly star-shaped and the rankings were derived largely from indirect comparisons, these findings should be interpreted as suggestive rather than definitive. Further high-quality studies with direct head-to-head comparisons are needed.

title: Informal Digital Information Use in Hospital Mass Casualty Incident Management During Wartime: Multicenter Cross-Sectional Questionnaire Study
container-title: Journal of Medical Internet Research
1883249ea507fcea521aab31268a6b97031567c4.abstract: Abstract Background Managing mass casualty incidents (MCIs) during an active warfare environment presents unique challenges, including operating under extreme uncertainty. Traditionally, emergency communications rely on strict, hierarchical channels from prehospital services to receiving hospitals. However, informal digital communication streams, particularly instant messaging apps such as WhatsApp and Telegram, are increasingly used within medical workflows. Despite international interest in public social media during disasters, empirical research regarding how hospital leadership echelons use informal messaging tools for real-time operational and clinical decision-making during active warfare remains sparse. Objective This study aimed to characterize the adoption of social media and instant messaging platforms as early information sources among hospital-based MCI managers during wartime and to evaluate their specific impact on real-time operational and clinical decision-making. Methods A multicenter, cross-sectional study was conducted using a structured questionnaire distributed across all 24 national medical centers authorized to receive MCIs during wartime in Israel. Target respondents encompassed diverse leadership echelons, including emergency department directors, trauma service directors, trauma coordinators, charge nurses, emergency team members, and hospital executive leadership. Results Overall, 76 medical professionals representing key decision-makers across national receiving centers completed the survey. WhatsApp emerged as the most frequently used platform (median 3.0, IQR 2.00‐4.00). Although these informal channels provided rapid initial intelligence, 65.3% (49/75) of respondents encountered false information during emergency events. Consequently, 81.3% (n=61) reported routinely verifying social media data against official channels before executing major actions. Multivariate regression analysis revealed distinct pathways of influence: higher platform use intensity was strongly and independently associated with enhanced situational awareness ( P =.002) and greater operational decision-making influence ( P =.02). In addition, participants’ level of trust and reliance was associated with clinical decisions ( P =.01) and real-time team management ( P =.03). Furthermore, active platform engagement during live threat conditions was positively correlated with heightened situational awareness during missile launch alerts ( P <.001) and missile fall alerts ( P <.001). Platform use and trust behaviors remained consistent across years of professional experience, qualifications, and executive roles. Conclusions Informal digital platforms, dominated by WhatsApp, serve as vital, rapid early information channels for hospital MCI leadership during wartime emergencies. While use intensity directly enhances situational awareness and operational control during active missile threats, clinical and team management actions remain strictly contingent on trust. Given the high exposure to unverified data, formalizing structured verification protocols and incorporating informal digital communication strategies into hospital disaster preparedness frameworks are essential to optimize real-time decision-making in future large-scale health emergencies.

title: Digital trade without development? Brazil’s turn to industrial policy and competition law
container-title: Journal of International Economic Law
c9cfa53714b04a79f69eb0a131f714760fa2ef81.abstract: Abstract This article examines the relationship between digital trade law, industrial policy, and competition through the experience of Brazil as a digital middle power. It argues that while contemporary digital trade disciplines have facilitated the global expansion of data-driven firms, they have simultaneously narrowed the policy space available to states seeking to develop domestic digital capabilities. Against this backdrop, the article analyses Brazil’s recent turn to domestic economic regulation through two complementary initiatives: REDATA, a special tax regime designed to attract investment in digital infrastructure, and a proposed reform of competition law aimed at regulating platforms of systemic relevance. It argues, however, that these initiatives embody an important policy tension. Brazil’s industrial strategy relies on investment by the very hyperscalers whose market power the proposed competition reforms seek to constrain. Drawing on interviews with representatives from multiple Brazilian ministries, together with primary legal materials and the emerging literature on digital trade and digital sovereignty, the article suggests that the current approach remains fragmented and insufficiently coordinated, engendering tensions that reflect broader structural dilemmas facing middle powers seeking to promote digital development.

title: Relational Ecological Momentary Assessment: A Viewpoint on the Relational Decision Space in Digital Mental Health
container-title: JMIR Formative Research
b95f3cf32169192424bce1424148c74a3920014b.abstract: Abstract Digital mental health has become increasingly capable of representing and adapting to individuals in time. When support is delivered through another person, however, the relevant decision context includes conditions that cannot be specified from the primary user alone. This viewpoint proposes making selected conditions relevant to a support decision within a specified relationship explicit. We introduce relational ecological momentary assessment (REMA) as a conceptual method for representing these conditions in a relational decision space. In its initial dyadic implementation, REMA combines a low-burden report of the primary user’s emotional zone (Z) with supporter contact availability (Cp) and supporter capacity (Cs). The meaning of these reports depends on the relationship and the proposed form of support. Willingness, consent, and safety determine whether an action is permissible to consider, while data validity concerns whether the reports are current and interpretable. These conditions and rules delimit relational support eligibility by specifying which classes of support can still be considered. Coregulation as a reciprocal temporal process remains outside the scope of this implementation. We situate the proposal within research on ecological momentary assessment, just-in-time adaptive interventions, dyadic digital health, and systemic digital mental health; provide a hypothetical implementation example; and show how 1 Z report can inform separate decisions involving different supporters. REMA remains conceptual and requires empirical evaluation. Its broader proposition is that when digital health recruits another person, the decision-relevant conditions across that specified relationship should be made explicit.

title: Growing Up With AI
container-title: The Algorithmic Child Consumer
1d0a243b804e5bc15a1d345307a3a8edd75d8671.abstract: This chapter examines the psychological implications of AI-curated digital environments on child consumers with a focus on cognitive development, screen engagement and mental well-being. Drawing on developmental psychology and consumer socialization literature, it explores how algorithmic personalization reshapes children's digital experiences and influences their ability to process information, regulate emotions and interpret persuasive content. The chapter moves beyond traditional notions of screen time by situating digital engagement within immersive, continuously adaptive environments. It further highlights the developmental vulnerabilities of pediatric consumers in navigating such spaces. In response, a developmentally informed framework for digital well-being is proposed, integrating technological design, user characteristics and contextual mediation. The chapter contributes to interdisciplinary discourse by offering a conceptual foundation for understanding child and AI interactions also informing ethically responsible digital practices.

title: Growing Up Algorithmic
container-title: The Algorithmic Child Consumer
bc9ada7a4d5842d7a6680ed7fef502edeb4bc9ea.abstract: The chapter critically examines how artificial intelligence has transformed children into consumers within the realm of online platforms, toys, and learning systems. It discusses the impact of AI-driven marketing strategies, including recommendation engines and synthetic influencers, on children's preferences and behaviors. The analysis is grounded in theories related to consumer socialization, media psychology, and digital surveillance, exploring how these technologies affect children's cognition, emotional attachments, and decision-making. It highlights concerns over hyper-personalized content, parasocial interactions with AI, and ethical governance regarding data privacy. Additionally, the chapter reviews existing regulatory frameworks, identifies gaps in protecting children, and proposes a holistic approach to understanding the interactions between children and AI. Finally, it advocates for ethical AI design, corporate responsibility, and enhancing AI literacy among parents, contributing to the broader conversation on child rights and digital well-being in an AI-driven era.

title: Juvenile Consumer in the Age of AI-Marketing
container-title: The Algorithmic Child Consumer
0a33e87f8dba8d3f37c618103c802b6a9bf7d949.abstract: In this chapter, the authors further develop on the changing face with regard to the juvenile consumer within the fast-growing realm of artificial intelligence. It also shows how AI technologies, including smart devices, social networking recommendation systems, and the Internet of Toys are shifting children as passive participants of the marketing process to active and data-generating participants in the digital economy. The paper is interdisciplinary and combines the knowledge of marketing, developmental psychology, digital ethics, and public policy to discuss four key issues, such as AI-enabled marketing practices, privacy, data ownership, digital well-being, and regulation. The authors state that, as much as AI presents opportunities of personalized learning and creative play and enhances connectivity. The growing popularity of gamification, influencer marketing, and emotionally adaptive systems makes the distinctions between entertainment and advertising and makes children less aware of when they are being sold a product.

title: Algorithmic Persuasion in the Age of AI
container-title: The Algorithmic Child Consumer
1c12aff4be2cfcce0ade40218bae9d4af7c74978.abstract: The architecture of marketing persuasion has undergone a structural change as a result of the quick adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) in children's digital environments. AI-driven systems, in contrast to conventional exposure-based advertising, use real-time personalization, adaptive feedback loops, and predictive analytics to shape behavioral trajectories rather than just discrete consumption decisions. The AI-native child is conceptualized in this chapter, which also makes the case that modern marketing strategies increasingly function through embedded commercial intent in gaming platforms, educational technologies, smart devices, and conversational agents. The Child-Centered Ethical AI Marketing Model (CCEAMM), a normative but implementable framework based on developmental appropriateness, transparency, proportional data use, autonomy preservation, and long-term well-being orientation, is the chapter's response.

title: Algorithmic Persuasion and Digital Well-Being
container-title: The Algorithmic Child Consumer
1b0cdd21fdb8daf75697d0c7e6839172d33ebd15.abstract: Social media is deeply embedded in daily life, shaping behaviours and psychological states. This study examines how social media influences emotions and behaviours by analysing the relationships between anxiety, voyeurism, exhibitionism, and Fear of Missing Out (FoMO), as well as FoMO's role in driving compulsive use. Using a quantitative approach, a 30-item survey was administered to 108 children. Results show that social media engagement is associated with higher levels of anxiety, voyeurism, and exhibitionism, which increase FoMO. This psychological strain leads to compulsive social media use. Despite limitations, the findings highlight FoMO's central role in shaping children's online experiences and contribute to understanding problematic digital behaviour, offering implications for more responsible and effective digital strategies.

title: The Child Consumer in the AI Era
container-title: The Algorithmic Child Consumer
5ad4e55952093a68f81d3250e2c934b4b91cc2ed.abstract: This chapter examines how AI-driven marketing environments operate as algorithmically engineered choice architectures for child consumers. Rather than treating digital marketing as a set of isolated advertisements or promotional messages, the chapter conceptualizes contemporary child-facing platforms as adaptive environments that organize attention, structure choices, shape consumption pathways, and influence patterns of platform engagement. These environments operate through defaults, rankings, recommender systems, gamified rewards, push notifications, consent frictions, privacy settings, social proof cues, influencer content, in-app prompts, and interface-level behavioral signals. In such settings, marketing is not only communicated through visible persuasion. It is embedded in the design of the digital environment itself.

title: Platform Power and the Child Consumer
container-title: The Algorithmic Child Consumer
81b0247fc90d833faa3d8e5fd5db11b2dc193f12.abstract: This article examines the structural relationship between digital platform power and children as vulnerable consumers in the contemporary digital economy. The rapid expansion of platform-based ecosystems driven by artificial intelligence has transformed how markets operate, particularly through mechanisms of personalization, data extraction, and behavioral prediction. Using an integrative theoretical framework that combines consumer behavior theory, surveillance capitalism, platform governance, and child vulnerability theory, this study analyzes how children's digital interactions are systematically shaped and exploited within platform infrastructures. The findings indicate that algorithmic personalization creates an illusion of autonomy while narrowing children's choice architecture, reinforcing consumption patterns that align with platform interests. At the same time, the datafication of children's daily activities enables large-scale behavioral data extraction, which is transformed into predictive economic value through targeted advertising and manipulation of preferences.

title: Implementing AI-CDSS in Low-Resource Maternal Care: Lessons Learned from the Preeclapp Deployment
container-title: Oxford Open Digital Health
c21285c26160f9ad7d7028e61962eee68a329a9e.abstract: Abstract Hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP) are one of the leading causes of maternal morbidity and mortality in Colombia, particularly in rural regions with limited access to specialized care. In this context, Preeclapp was developed as a clinical decision support system grounded in expert-system logic, designed to provide guideline-based support for maternal care in settings with limited resources and connectivity. This proof-of-concept implementation study analyzes the integration of Preeclapp into clinical practice and the factors that influenced its adoption. The main barriers identified included unstable connectivity, lack of data interoperability, high staff turnover, and initial skepticism toward AI-based technologies. Nevertheless, the project showed preliminary feasibility of use by non-specialized personnel in obstetrics and gynecology, even in low-connectivity environments. To overcome these challenges, the project relied on training sessions, embedded educational resources, continuous technical support, and iterative software adaptations. Our implementation suggests that these strategies were perceived by users as supporting adherence to obstetric protocols, reinforcing clinical decision-making, and enhancing staff confidence, particularly in facilities with limited specialist availability. As a proof-of-concept implementation study, this work did not evaluate diagnostic accuracy or clinical effectiveness; instead, it focused on early implementation feasibility, usability, acceptability, and perceived usefulness. The findings suggest that sustainable adoption of AI-CDSS systems requires strengthening digital literacy and promoting a culture of innovation. Our experience with Preeclapp indicates that adoption and implementation benefited from a modular design, low-connectivity functionality, flexibility, and co-creation with local teams, which helped adapt the tool to each institution’s context.

title: Dynamic Scheduling Optimization of Multi-Robot Collaborative Assembly Systems Combining GraphSAGE and Digital Twins
container-title: Journal of Advanced Manufacturing Systems
0e09c2cfb2e15f8006afca83530dbec319b12351.abstract: Scheduling lag, path conflicts, and resource overload are the common problems that a multi-robot collaborative assembly system faces under task dynamics changes, strong resource coupling, and unexpected interruptions; scheduling mechanisms struggle to capture dynamic relations among entities and to verify strategy feasibility promptly. To tackle the problem, this paper proposes a dynamic scheduling optimization framework based on Graph Sample aggreGatE (GraphSAGE) and digital twins. Through inductive learning, the framework embeds the dynamic relations of heterogeneous entities online and handles the real-time representation and scheduling of unseen nodes. A high-fidelity closed-loop simulation environment based on a digital twin verifies the feasibility and pre-evaluates the performance of each strategy before deployment, which prevents invalid or harmful scheduling instructions from reaching the physical system. Experiments evaluate the proposed approach under different task loads, robot counts, and fault disturbance scenarios against five scheduling methods. The results indicate that for high task frequency, the average task response time is 2.6 s; the average task success rate is 95.0%; the number of path conflicts is less than 3; the rate of resource contention is less than 10%; and the average rescheduling time under a 25% sudden failure rate is 0.85 s. Ablation experiments validate the graph embedding mechanism and the twin verification module separately. This study offers a secure and robust scheduling technique for multi-robot cooperation in high-speed dynamic intelligent manufacturing environments.

title: Generative Artificial Intelligence and Large Language Models as a Digital Assistant for Power System Operators
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI-Driven Sustainable Energy Systems
43f02e9dd2362d62f0781c1271492951a9157aa0.abstract: Power-system operation is safety-critical: personnel integrate data, alarms, outages, switching requests, contingency analyses, grid-code rules, and cybersecurity constraints. This review assesses evidence, rechecked through May 31, 2026, on GenAI and large language models (LLMs) for operator support. It covers research, reports, standards, regulations, preprints, and industry initiatives, distinguishing retrieval-grounded systems, domain-adapted LLMs, time-series foundation models, tool-using agents, and digital-twin verification. It proposes a supervised assistant in which the LLM orchestrates and explains but is not operational truth. Near-term uses include document retrieval, regulatory interpretation, training, summaries, and explanations of approved calculations. Evidence does not support autonomous transmission-level actions. Deployment requires traceable sources, current models, restricted tools, cybersecurity boundaries, adversarial testing, human approval, and audit trails.

title: Algorithmic Persuasion and the Commodification of the Indian Child Consumer
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Governing Childhood in the Age of AI
7ef08bed984a79d99131ec55e78d0e3fafb5c13c.abstract: Artificial intelligence has reshaped digital persuasion, placing children at the center of AI-driven consumption in India's platform economy. Gamification, recommender systems, and synthetic influencers exploit cognitive immaturity and emotional vulnerability in ways existing consumer and advertising laws cannot address. This chapter argues that AI-driven child-targeted marketing constitutes a distinct unfair trade practice, commodifying childhood itself. Grounded in consumer law and constitutional principles under Articles 14, 19, and 21, it advances a case for statutory limits prioritizing child dignity and autonomy.

title: Algorithmic Childhood
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Governing Childhood in the Age of AI
24a3c19b0daa4623298ba63af7df9b13718df0f6.abstract: This chapter looks at the idea of Algorithmic Childhood, which looks at how AI-driven personalization, algorithmic exposure, datafication, and behavioural nudging transform children online experiences and consumer identities. The digital platforms are relentlessly gathering and analysing data on children in order to customize their content, ads, and interactions and in the process, there are no sharp lines between play, learning, and commercial persuasion. Although the advantages of personalization are educational and age-related, they also contribute to making children more vulnerable because of their poor cognitive and emotional development. The chapter is a synthesis of interdisciplinary literature that identifies ethical issues, asymmetry of power, and the gap of the currently existing regulatory frameworks. It calls to the child-cantered policies of governing aimed to guarantee transparency and accountability, digital well-being, the safety of children, and safeguarding of child rights through AI-mediated markets.

title: Algorithmic Entrapment
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Governing Childhood in the Age of AI
9a1a337e1b2937ac4af2d2775b27805a3ce8499b.abstract: Artificial intelligence has transformed social media into adaptive persuasion systems that learn from and optimize for each child's behavior. This chapter shows how AI-driven curation undermines parental authority through qualitative analysis of Slovenian parents. Based on 14 in-depth interviews with parents of 22 children, we identify “algorithmic entrapment,” where engagement-maximizing systems override parental boundaries, exploit developmental vulnerabilities, and foster dependencies resistant to intervention. Parents recognized addiction-like symptoms but had a limited understanding of underlying AI mechanisms such as recommendation systems, predictive analytics, variable rewards, and personalized optimization. A “Surveillance Capitalism and Childhood” framework is proposed to explain how data extraction and attention monetization conflict with children's developmental needs. Protecting children requires shifting beyond parental responsibility toward governance solutions, including transparency mandates, limits on persuasive AI targeting minors, and independent audits.

title: From Digital Safety to Digital Flourishing
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Governing Childhood in the Age of AI
03a959e7ca0c73de400bfd81a13b9caeff54cbf1.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly transforming children's digital environments, reshaping how they learn, interact, and participate as consumers. While existing scholarship and regulation largely emphasize digital safety—focusing on privacy protection and risk mitigation—there is limited attention to how AI can actively promote children's developmental well-being. This case study–based chapter advances a shift from digital safety to digital flourishing by examining how child-centered AI systems can support cognitive growth, social-emotional development, and ethical agency. Drawing on interdisciplinary literature and empirical case analyses of socially assistive robots, adaptive learning platforms, and conversational AI systems, the chapter develops a Developmental Flourishing Framework integrating developmental psychology, children's rights principles, and ethical marketing considerations. The analysis highlights both opportunities and structural risks, including algorithmic bias, surveillance practices, and persuasive design.

title: AI Literacy as Consumer Immunity in Children
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Governing Childhood in the Age of AI
9551deacb2f585906f3298c74c3b05f1921605f7.abstract: Whether driven by regulation or the market, pure protective responses are becoming less tenable as AI systems become more integrated into commercial ecosystems surrounding children. The future of child digital well-being will hinge on not just stronger regulations and more ethical platform design, but also critically aware young users capable to interpret and navigate algorithmic environments with informed scepticism and reflective agency. This chapter advances the notion of AI literacy as consumer immunity, putting forward a timely and actionable framework for educators, designers, policymakers and researchers interested in aligning technology innovation with ethical responsibility to children. Protecting the child consumer in the age of A.I. ultimately means pursuing both solutions: Creating safer systems while also fortifying the young brains that make their way through them.

title: AI Literacy
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Governing Childhood in the Age of AI
87a810168d220e42586510068471834bc1db6970.abstract: Children in contemporary school settings are daily consumers of AI-generated content — whether they know it or not. Recommendation feeds, synthetic images, AI-drafted text, and algorithmic advertising have become routine features of childhood digital experience, yet most K–12 curricula offer little preparation for navigating these environments critically. This chapter argues that schools bear a genuine responsibility to address this gap through deliberate, grade-appropriate AI literacy education oriented not merely toward using AI tools, but toward questioning and evaluating what those tools produce. Drawing on recent empirical work and theoretical scholarship across AI literacy, media education, and ethics, the chapter traces a developmentally staged curriculum pathway from early childhood awareness through secondary-level civic and ethical reasoning, while also highlighting key challenges in implementation such as teacher readiness, assessment alignment, and the limited geographic distribution of existing research.

title: Curriculum Development for AI Literacy in Schools
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Governing Childhood in the Age of AI
48f5f323ea3fb2f7789d2937410b6f74e253e184.abstract: Artificial intelligence has infiltrated the digital landscape of children at an extremely fast rate, affecting the way children learn, communicate and access information. This chapter in the book makes a case in favor of an all-encompassing curriculum in AI literacy that will help children understand how to critically analyze the systems of algorithms, defend against subtle persuasion, and identify fake media. Based on the Critical Media Literacy Theory, Persuasion Knowledge Theory, Socio-Technical Systems Theory and the Digital Resilience Frameworks, describes a modular, age-based curriculum between primary-level and secondary education. Experiential learning, gamification, and project-based assessments are some of the pedagogical strategies favored with the help of teacher training and alignment of policies. Finally, the chapter makes AI literacy a key factor to creating digitally resilient citizens who are capable of operating in algorithmically mediated spaces in a responsible, reflective and ethical manner.

title: Curriculum Development for Schools to Teach Children How to Recognize and Critically Evaluate AI Content
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Governing Childhood in the Age of AI
eabdf13bce65d9c835bad254e966a1d5672132c4.abstract: Children today are growing up in digital environments where Artificial Intelligence (AI) plays a central yet often invisible role in shaping their experiences. From personalized recommendations and AI-generated academic assistance to targeted advertising and algorithmically curated content intelligent systems influence how children access information, form preferences, and make decisions. This chapter argues that AI literacy must be recognized as an essential component of contemporary school education. Drawing on an interdisciplinary review of literature in AI literacy, media studies, and education, the chapter proposes a curriculum-oriented framework based on three interconnected dimensions: operational, sociocultural and critical literacy. In response, it introduces a practical pedagogical approach centered on “questioning the machine,” encouraging students to develop habits of inquiry, reflection and ethical awareness in their interactions with AI-driven content.

title: Play, Screen, and Sensibility
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Governing Childhood in the Age of AI
419ae53555cf9525f8072bd48eced60adce44aa6.abstract: This chapter examines how early childhood digital literacy should be understood not merely as technical skill, but as an ethical, relational, and pedagogical process. Focusing on children in their first years, it explores how screens increasingly shape curiosity, play, attention, and emotional development. The chapter argues that ethical sensibility must be nurtured alongside digital engagement through adult mediation, reflective dialogue, and balanced forms of play. It highlights the roles of parents and teachers in guiding children to interpret digital stories, games, and apps with empathy, patience, and moral awareness. Ultimately, it proposes that ethical digital literacy in early childhood begins not with control, but with care, conversation, and thoughtful participation.

title: Exploring AI-based teleorientation for the sexual and reproductive health of Spanish- and Quechua-speaking adolescents: a technology acceptance study
container-title: Oxford Open Digital Health
ca7fe9a8f94e5435dd342dbff7db0c6fd98892e4.abstract: Abstract Background Geographical, sociocultural, and confidentiality-related barriers continue to limit adolescents' and young people's access to sexual and reproductive health information. Objective To evaluate the acceptance of an AI-based teleorientation chatbot for sexual and reproductive health using the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM). Methods A cross-sectional study was conducted with 113 Quechua-speaking high school students in Ayacucho, Peru, who interacted with a bilingual (Spanish/Quechua) AI chatbot over a three-months period. Data collected using an extension of the Technology Acceptance Model 3 (TAM 3) were analysed with PLS-SEM. Results Perceived Ease of Use (PEOU) was the main determinant of Behavioral Intention to Use (BI; β = 0.53, p &lt; 0.001), confirming the role of Ease of Use in technology adoption. Perceived Trust (PT) had a significant positive effect on PEOU (β = 0.56, p &lt; 0.001) and a significant negative effect on Perceived Risk (PR; β = -0.69, p &lt; 0.001). The negative correlation of PR and the other constructs indicated that reducing perceived risk is important for technology adoption. Contrary to TAM theory, Perceived Usefulness (PU) was not a significant predictor of BI (β = 0.13). Conclusions This study demonstrates that trust and ease of use are key factors influencing adolescents’ acceptance of AI-based health chatbots in multilingual environments. The findings suggest that culturally adapted digital tools can help reduce barriers to accessing sexual and reproductive health information when they prioritize simplicity, cultural relevance, and user trust. These results provide valuable insights for the design of youth-centred digital health interventions in diverse contexts.

title: A phase-calibrated combined electrical-sensory neuromodulation platform for short-term frontoparietal network modulation and cognitive fatigue resistance
container-title: Journal of Neural Engineering
e68c07d8a23ba65e2a0d85eafe752e2acd70af80.abstract: Abstract Objective. Non-invasive combined electrical-sensory neuromodulation may be limited by cross-modal timing discrepancies arising from modality-specific conduction delays. This pilot study aimed to develop and evaluate an individualized delay-calibrated stimulation platform integrating transcranial alternating current stimulation with rhythmic visual and auditory inputs for modulating cognitive-fatigue-related frontoparietal network dynamics. Approach. We developed a microcontroller-based combined electrical–sensory stimulation platform and implemented a feedforward delay-compensation strategy based on individualized ERP latencies, including visual P 1 and auditory N 1. The system was evaluated in a randomized, sham-controlled crossover study involving 17 participants, of whom 15 provided complete electroencephalographic datasets. Main results. Across the three tested protocols, the combined electrical–sensory condition showed larger immediate post-intervention theta-power changes than the audiovisual and sham conditions and a theta- weighted phase lag index difference relative to sham. During the subsequent high-load cognitive task, the combined condition showed a shallower mean parietal alpha accumulation trajectory. Together, these findings characterize the short-term neurodynamic profile associated with the integrated protocol. Exploratory brain–behavior analysis showed a positive full-sample association that was sensitive to individual observations. Significance. These findings support the feasibility of the timing-informed combined electrical–sensory platform and provide preliminary evidence of short-term condition-associated frontoparietal modulation.

title: Coupled Abrasive and Fatigue Wear Modeling of Blanking Punches for Prediction of Wear Using Linear and Nonlinear Wear Models
container-title: Key Engineering Materials
6941ef3e909d1858d9ce5bea1c772877dc8c17a3.abstract: Repeated blanking operations cause progressive degradation of punch edges, leading to dimensional inaccuracies, burr formation, and premature tool failure. This study proposes a coupled abrasive–fatigue wear modeling framework for estimating the lifetime of punches under long-term repeated blanking process. Abrasive wear was modeled using a modified Archard wear formulation, whereas fatigue-induced wear was represented using an extended Lemaitre damage model capable of capturing cyclic damage accumulation within the elastic regime. An adaptive finite element framework incorporating wear-driven geometry updating and element deletion techniques was developed to simulate progressive punch edge degradation during repeated blanking operations. The proposed methodology was applied to an AISI D2 punch and AISI 430 sheet metal under long-term cyclic blanking conditions. The results of finite element analysis demonstrated that the conventional linear wear model predicted gradual wear evolution, whereas the coupled nonlinear wear model effectively captured accelerated wear propagation after approximately 300,000 blanking cycles due to fatigue-induced material detachment. The predicted wear depth evolution showed good agreement with the experimental results, with a maximum relative error below 7%. In addition, the proposed wear update method using accumulated cycles enabled faster wear prediction than long-term blanking experiments.

title: Fretting Fatigue Cracking Mechanisms of Additively Manufactured Superalloys with Gradient Grains Based on <i>I</i><i>n Situ</i> SEM
container-title: Key Engineering Materials
32bb61fe41e2624dbf4b4da4e763506acb70cd95.abstract: This study aims to elucidate the influence mechanisms of gradient grain structures on the fretting fatigue damage evolution of additively manufactured superalloys under high-temperature conditions. To this end, two types of specimens with and without grain gradients were designed and subjected to in situ scanning electron microscopy (SEM) fretting fatigue tests at 650 °C to capture the microscopic damage evolution processes under different microstructures. In situ SEM fretting fatigue tests were conducted at 650 °C to capture the microscopic damage evolution processes of the specimens under different microstructures. In situ observation results indicate that fretting fatigue cracks primarily initiate in the region of high stress and severe wear at the contact edge. Furthermore, the gradient grain structure can effectively induce the deflection and branching of microcracks, significantly improving the fretting fatigue life and reducing the crack propagation rate. Electron backscatter diffraction (EBSD) analysis reveals that compared to uniform grains, the gradient structure effectively suppresses local grain refinement and limits the extreme increase of geometrically necessary dislocation (GND) density and grain reference orientation deviation (GROD) during fretting damage. This indicates that the gradient grains can better coordinate local plastic deformation and relieve stress concentration, thereby demonstrating optimal resistance to fretting fatigue damage. Therefore, the grain gradient in the microstructure has a significant influence on the fretting damage mechanisms and the early evolution of cracks.

title: Emotional attributes of digital assistants driving engagement, purchase intentions and well-being
container-title: International Journal of Retail & Distribution Management
a75d79312ce4abff331f0694d5c24f21c27ec281.abstract: Purpose Grounded in the stimulus–organism–response (SOR) model and the spillover concept, the study examines how digital assistants’ (DAs) affective attributes shape customer engagement, which then spills over into emotional values, purchase intentions and well-being. Design/methodology/approach A two-wave longitudinal survey was conducted, yielding 440 responses at Time 1 and 315 at Time 2. Partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) by SmartPLS 4.0 was used to verify the reliability and validity of the measurement model and test the hypothesised relationships. Findings The findings reveal that DAs’ aesthetics, friendliness and playfulness significantly increase customer engagement, with effect sizes for these emotional stimuli varying from low to high. Customers’ active engagement also subsequently influences their emotional values: perceived happiness and relaxation. Together, these emotional values have a positive and significant effect on purchase intentions. The results also show that customer well-being is significantly spilled through purchase intentions. Moreover, customer engagement, emotional values and purchase intention yield substantial serial mediation effects in the relationships between attributional stimuli and well-being. Originality/value The originality of this study lies in extending the SOR model to a psychological outcome (well-being) and quantitatively verifying the interrelationships in retail settings. It investigates the serial mediation of emotional attributional stimuli, presenting their activeness continuum from low to high. Besides, it offers key managerial insights into effectively utilising DA attributes to engage and evoke customers’ emotional values, thereby driving purchase intentions and, subsequently, extending the experience to well-being in technology-mediated services.

title: Operationalizing level(s) macro-objective 2 for residential renovation: a circularity assessment workflow in a collaborative digital platform
container-title: Smart and Sustainable Built Environment
63af7164f2b9b96b6139c2b341ea8fc2a73dd3a9.abstract: Purpose The practical implementation of the European level(s) framework, particularly Macro-Objective 2 (MO-2) on resource-efficient and circular material life cycles, remains challenging due to complex data requirements, limited availability of lifecycle information during early project stages and fragmented digital workflows. This study aims to develop and demonstrate a Building Information Modeling (BIM)-to-level(s) workflow for operationalizing the EU level(s) MO-2 indicators at the permit stage of residential renovation projects. The study specifically addresses the challenge of incomplete permit-stage information by integrating existing–proposed–delta analysis with an evidence-quality layer that makes the evidential basis and limitations of assessment outputs explicit. Design/methodology/approach A design science research approach was adopted to develop and demonstrate a proof-of-concept workflow using permit-stage Industry Foundation Classes (IFC) models of a Swedish residential renovation project. The workflow integrates IFC-based quantity extraction, semantic enrichment, material and product proxy information, existing–proposed–delta classification and level(s)-aligned calculations for Indicators 2.1–2.4. An author-defined Evidence Quality Score (EQS) was introduced to distinguish directly available information from interpreted, proxy-based and unavailable evidence. The resulting outputs were structured for conceptual integration within a collaborative digital platform (CDP). The workflow was assessed through internal consistency and traceability checks rather than independent expert, construction-stage or multi-project validation. Findings The case study demonstrates that permit-stage IFC information can support structured, preliminary assessment of all four level(s) MO-2 indicators when supplemented by controlled semantic enrichment and documented assumptions. The existing-proposed-delta logic enables retained, removed, modified and newly introduced elements to be distinguished, supporting more explicit identification of renovation-related material changes. The evidence-quality layer makes information gaps and proxy-dependent calculations visible and helps avoid presenting scenario-based estimates as verified construction-stage outcomes. However, the resulting quantities, circularity measures and evidence-quality scores should be interpreted as case-specific estimates rather than validated performance measurements. Research limitations/implications The study is limited to a single Swedish residential renovation case and uses permit-stage information that does not include verified demolition quantities, contractor waste records, complete as-built material inventories or construction-stage observations. The EQS is an author-defined heuristic measure and has not been independently validated through expert elicitation, inter-rater testing or empirical calibration. Similarly, CDP backend automation, automated data transfer and end-to-end execution have not been operationally demonstrated. Future research should therefore undertake multi-project validation, expert and user evaluation, comparison with manual and alternative BIM-based assessment methods and verification against construction-stage evidence. Practical implications The workflow has prospective relevance for architects, sustainability consultants, contractors and municipal authorities by providing a structured means of identifying material changes and information gaps during renovation planning. For municipal permitting, the evidence-quality layer could potentially help distinguish documented information from estimates and proxies and indicate where additional documentation or expert review may be required. However, the study does not demonstrate improved decision quality, permitting efficiency, economic benefits or regulatory effectiveness. The workflow should therefore be regarded as a methodological foundation for future digitally enabled circularity assessment rather than a practice-ready or regulatory-ready system. Originality/value The study contributes a manually defined BIM-to-Level(s) workflow that integrates existing-proposed-delta analysis with an EQS layer for permit-stage MO-2 assessment. The contribution is methodological and proof-of-concept in nature, providing transparent traceability between BIM evidence, semantic enrichment and level(s) assessment outputs while identifying information gaps requiring future validation and automation.

title: Emotionally Responsive Mathematics Classrooms
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Enhancing the Industrial Metaverse With Extended Reality
1aa04a6b98bb795c78dbb3bf493eb5a8e8343ab2.abstract: This chapter per the authors presents a conceptual synthesis of emotionally responsive mathematics classrooms that integrates teacher emotions, social-emotional learning (SEL), and digital learning analytics. Its purpose is to explain how teachers' emotional competence, SEL-aligned mathematics pedagogy, and ethically interpreted digital indicators can support rigorous, psychologically safer mathematical learning. The chapter reviews recent scholarship on teacher enjoyment, anxiety, anger, emotional labor, achievement emotions, classroom climate, SEL programs, and human-centered analytics. It then proposes the Emotionally Responsive Mathematics Classroom Framework, linking task design, mathematical discourse, formative feedback, error treatment, student appraisals, and analytics governance. Applied sections translate the framework into lesson planning, algebra instruction, learning management system use, professional development, and school-level implementation, while the discussion identifies limitations and future research directions.

title: Integrating XR, AI, Digital Twins, and IIoT in the Industrial Metaverse
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Enhancing the Industrial Metaverse With Extended Reality
fbf2ccf62346b15568a02d6b5e5729370294b911.abstract: This chapter examines the Industrial Metaverse as the convergence of Extended Reality (XR), Artificial Intelligence (AI), Digital Twins, and the Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) into persistent, immersive, and intelligent industrial ecosystems. Based on a structured narrative review, the chapter proposes a five-layer integration architecture and positions it against RAMI 4.0, IIRA, ISO 23247, and cyber-physical system models. It specifies synchronization requirements for XR-enabled Digital Twins, maps threats and security controls to each architectural layer, and reviews applications in manufacturing, energy, healthcare, and logistics. The chapter also examines generative AI, industrial foundation models, edge AI, and blockchain, together with their risks, and addresses governance, regulation, and human-machine collaboration. It concludes with an implementation pathway and research directions for secure, trustworthy, and human-centric Industrial Metaverse ecosystems aligned with Industry 5.0.

title: XR-Enabled Moodle Learning Ecosystems for the Industrial Metaverse
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Enhancing the Industrial Metaverse With Extended Reality
02afab14813059458f1c623082082cd38c0ca92f.abstract: This chapter, per the authors, presents a conceptual framework for using Moodle as the learning orchestration layer for XR-enabled workforce training in the industrial metaverse. It synthesizes recent research on extended reality, digital twins, artificial intelligence, learning analytics, and cybersecurity awareness to identify a gap between immersive industrial training prototypes and LMS-based evidence, assessment, and governance. The chapter proposes the XR-Moodle Industrial Learning Ecosystem (XMILE), which links Moodle courses, XR scenarios, digital twin states, AI-supported analytics, and cybersecurity controls. It explains the model's layers, data flows, use cases, evaluation metrics, and implementation roadmap for universities, technical training centers, and industrial organizations. The contribution is a practical structure for designing measurable, secure, and role-based training that supports skill transfer, cyber hygiene, and instructor decision-making.

title: From green commitment to sustainable harvest: how digital capabilities and institutional pressure power agricultural sustainability
container-title: Journal of Enterprise Information Management
efe689e44c54fc3461d17e3af2cddaa61ee57f60.abstract: Purpose The objective of this study is to examine whether, and through which mechanisms, green corporate social responsibility (GCSR) integration improves sustainable farm performance in a climate-vulnerable emerging economy. Drawing on dynamic capabilities theory and institutional theory, the study analyses the mediating roles of green supply chain dynamic capabilities, sustainable agricultural innovation and digital technology capability, and the first-stage moderating role of coercive institutional pressure. Design/methodology/approach A cross-sectional survey of 420 farmers and agribusiness managers, purposively selected through agricultural extension offices in 30 districts across four Pakistani provinces, was conducted. Partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) with 10,000 bootstrap resamples was used to estimate the model, which contains three parallel mediators and three interaction terms. Measurement and structural model quality, predictive relevance, common-method bias, nonresponse bias and endogeneity were assessed through standard procedures. Findings GCSR integration has a significant direct effect on sustainable farm performance, but most of its effect is transmitted through capability building. Digital technology capability carries the largest indirect effect, followed by green supply chain dynamic capabilities and sustainable agricultural innovation. Coercive institutional pressure strengthens the conversion of GCSR into all three capabilities, the moderation is largest for digital capability, but the three moderation effects are not statistically distinguishable. The study concludes that green commitments improve farm sustainability only when they are converted into organizational capabilities, and that regulatory pressure accelerates this conversion. Research limitations/implications The cross-sectional, self-reported and purposive design limits causal inference and statistical generalization. Future studies should use longitudinal, multi-source and objective farm data and test normative and mimetic pressures. Practical implications Policymakers should pair environmental regulation with digital monitoring requirements, extension training and affordable digital infrastructure, while farm managers should treat GCSR as a capability-building program rather than a symbolic commitment. Originality/value The study differentiates three capability pathways through which GCSR becomes farm-level sustainability and treats coercive pressure as a first-stage condition of capability formation rather than a background constraint. It also provides farm-level evidence from a smallholder-dominated emerging economy, where prior work has focused on manufacturing and listed firms.

title: Twin transition in construction industry: a systematic review of digital and green integration and a firm-level research agenda
container-title: Engineering, Construction and Architectural Management
1ad7cbb9627e00c10b3d1ad3dd3eb46a790c1830.abstract: Purpose Construction firms must digitalise and decarbonise simultaneously, but whether they combine the two programmes is not known. This review maps how the twin transition, the joint pursuit of digitalisation and sustainability, is conceptualised and implemented in the construction sector, and sets out an agenda for firm-level research. Design/methodology/approach Following PRISMA 2020 guidelines, searches were run in Web of Science and Scopus, combining “twin transition” with digitalisation and sustainability terms. After two-stage screening, 78 peer-reviewed papers were coded against a structured protocol, complemented by a VOSviewer keyword co-occurrence analysis. Findings The literature is expanding rapidly but remains conceptually fragmented. Only a small minority of studies use the term “twin transition” explicitly, none uses the firm-level term twin transformation and most frame digitalisation as the driver of sustainability rather than the reverse. A clear gap separates recommendation from observation: few papers examine the direction of the relationship or whether digital and green programmes are run jointly or in parallel, and firm-level empirical evidence is limited and concentrated in Chinese companies. Technical and data barriers, missing standards and capability gaps dominate the obstacles, while digital tools, organisational capabilities and policy mechanisms dominate the enablers. Originality/value The review applies the firm-level construct of twin transformation, developed in management research, to construction, shows that the field has produced sector-level evidence but almost none on how firms integrate the two programmes, and sets out testable priorities for closing that gap.

title: From cultural heritage to public value co-creation intention: the role of place identity activation and information diversity in digital dissemination
container-title: Asia Pacific Journal of Marketing and Logistics
5c63461225ef835df73c7de2d0e59bb09ddc531e.abstract: Purpose This study aims to: (1) examine the mechanism through which digital dissemination of cultural heritage influences public value co-creation intention and (2) test the mediating role of place identity activation and the moderating role of information diversity in this process. Design/methodology/approach This study employs three experimental studies using video-based stimuli to analyze the impact of digital dissemination of local cultural heritage on public co-creation. Data were collected from the online platform Credamo (N1 = 148, N2 = 150, N3 = 249) with participants randomly assigned to experimental conditions. Findings The paper provides empirical insights about how digital dissemination of cultural heritage significantly enhances public place identity activation and value co-creation intention. The study further identifies place identity activation as a full mediator and information diversity as a significant moderator – under the high information diversity condition, the positive effect of dissemination on place identity activation is not significant. Research limitations/implications This study examines only two types of cultural heritage: forestry cultural heritage and tea cultural heritage. Practical implications This study contributes to realizing the digital value of cultural heritage and offers targeted recommendations for its dissemination and development in the new era. Social implications This study contributes to enhancing digital interaction between the public and culture by engaging in culture dissemination and re-creation, advancing the development of digital-humanistic relationships on a deeper level. Originality/value The findings provide a theoretically grounded and empirically tested mechanism explaining how digital heritage communication influences public value co-creation intention, while clarifying the boundary condition of information diversity.

title: scHiCGNN: Per-Chromosome Graph Attention for Single-Cell Hi-C Clustering
container-title: Bioinformatics Advances
4a93d6669776147fe6874ee9c846b19120eaa6de.abstract: Abstract Motivation Single-cell Hi-C measures three-dimensional chromatin organization in individual nuclei, revealing cell-to-cell variability in genome folding that bulk Hi-C cannot resolve. The central computational task is to cluster cells by chromatin state, but each cell yields a sparse, high-dimensional contact matrix poorly suited to linear principal component analysis pipelines or to hand-designed multi-stage neural pipelines. Results We present scHiCGNN, a graph attention framework that encodes each chromosome's contact matrix as a weighted graph, applies multi-head graph attention to learn node-level features, and fuses per-chromosome embeddings into a compact cell-level representation through a lightweight self-attention block. The resulting embedding is consumed by standard unsupervised clustering. We evaluate scHiCGNN on six public datasets: Flyamer, Collombet, Nagano (mouse) and Ramani, Lee, 4DN (human), spanning 171 to 19,388 cells. scHiCGNN consistently improves over principal component analysis baselines on all six datasets and matches or exceeds the published Higashi and MRscHiC numbers on the three larger human datasets, reaching Adjusted Rand Index values of 0.944 (Ramani), 0.674 (Lee), and 0.875 (4DN); on the smaller mouse datasets, MRscHiC's engineered pipeline retains an advantage. Direct graph representation learning is a practical and conceptually clean alternative to flattened-vector approaches for single-cell Hi-C clustering. Availability and implementation https://github.com/changlabtw/schicgnn

title: How do digital platform affordances drive digital transformation among project-based firms in engineering consulting? The mediating role of value co-creation
container-title: International Journal of Managing Projects in Business
6eb4c344f0940710336abf40650923a04bd10fcd.abstract: Purpose For engineering consulting firms that rely on project delivery, digital transformation has become an important pathway for enhancing project delivery capabilities and strengthening competitive advantage. However, due to cross-organizational collaboration and multi-project environments, digital technology investment does not necessarily improve transformation performance. Based on technology affordance actualization theory, this study aims to explore how digital platform affordance enhances digital transformation performance. Design/methodology/approach Based on the theory of technology affordance actualization, this study develops a model linking digital platform affordances, platform-based value co-creation and digital transformation performance. Platform-based value co-creation is examined from two dimensions: owner value co-creation and delivery partner value co-creation. Using survey data from 264 engineering consulting firms, the research hypotheses were empirically tested using hierarchical regression. Findings The results indicate that digital platform affordance positively affects digital transformation performance. Both owner value co-creation and delivery partner value co-creation mediate this relationship, with the mediating effect of delivery partner value co-creation being slightly stronger. Originality/value This study extends digital transformation research in project-based firms by revealing the mechanism through which digital platform affordance drives transformation performance. It further highlights the role of platform-based value co-creation and distinguishes the differential effects of owner and delivery partner value co-creation, providing theoretical and practical implications for digital transformation in project-based firms.

38277cd84da2f867879cb408f48ad47afd444966.abstract: The document examines the comprehensive development of the agricultural sector as the foundation of food security, economic independence and competitiveness of the state. Successful examples of the Netherlands, New Zealand and Brazil are given. For Uzbekistan, the key growth points are described: diversification of sown areas, deep processing, water-saving technologies, greenhouse farms, export logistics, certification and digitalization. The turning point of the reforms since 2017 is noted: liberalization, abolition of the state order and development of clusters. Particular attention is paid to the mechanization of agriculture: the current level of mechanization (81% overall, 52% in cotton harvesting), plans to purchase machinery (800 cotton harvesters and 6000 units of other machinery in 2026), and leasing on preferential terms (up to 10 years, 18% per annum with 8% compensated from the budget). Tasks are set to increase the production of domestic machinery 5-fold and to raise localization to 30–65% by 2028. Financial support measures are considered: subsidizing 15% of the cost of machinery (660 billion soums), lending through Agrobank (growth from 1.6 to 3.9 trillion soums in 2026), automation of loan issuance (from three days to three hours), and the creation of agro-service zones with agricultural agents. Pilot projects using artificial intelligence in livestock farming, horticulture and water management are noted, as well as the creation of a venture company with a capital of 100 billion soums to finance startups.

title: ESG rating disagreement and corporate energy intensity in China: the moderating role of managerial environmental attention
container-title: Social Responsibility Journal
66e00f8d8ab0418b75a493d7161c1cb59c39572c.abstract: Purpose This study aims to investigate how ESG rating disagreement affects corporate energy intensity and the role of managerial environmental attention in this relationship. Design/methodology/approach Using 18,335 firm-year observations from 4,124 Chinese listed firms between 2019 and 2023, this study uses panel regressions to test the proposed relationships. Findings The results reveal a U-shaped relationship between ESG rating disagreement and corporate energy intensity. Moderate disagreement reduces energy intensity by providing complementary sustainability information, whereas excessive disagreement increases energy intensity by generating signal ambiguity. Managerial environmental attention strengthens this U-shaped relationship. Originality/value These findings deepen our understanding of how information uncertainty shapes corporate sustainability outcomes and how managerial cognitive orientation moderates the consequences of rating inconsistency.

title: Towards an AI Literacy Framework for Maritime English Education: Integrating Language, Professional, and Digital Competencies
container-title: LANCAH: Jurnal Inovasi dan Tren
236639692b02ff378d325cde7448cb13cf583416.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is increasingly influencing language education by providing opportunities for personalized practice, immediate feedback, and flexible access to learning resources. However, effective use of GenAI in Maritime English requires competencies beyond general language proficiency and basic technological skills. Maritime English involves specialized terminology, standardized communication, operational contexts, and professional requirements in which inaccurate or inappropriate AI-generated content may have practical consequences. This conceptual study develops an AI literacy framework for Maritime English education through a conceptual literature synthesis. The synthesis draws on literature published between 2020 and 2026, supplemented by earlier foundational works on AI literacy and English for Specific Purposes (ESP), as well as authoritative Maritime references, including IMO Standard Marine Communication Phrases and IMO Model Course 3.17. Sources were selected based on their relevance to AI literacy, generative AI in language education, ESP, learner autonomy, and Maritime English, with particular attention to their conceptual contributions and applicability to Maritime communication. The synthesis identifies digital-AI competence as the core AI literacy capability, supported by two contextual knowledge bases: language competence and professional Maritime competence. Language competence enables learners to evaluate AI-generated language, while professional Maritime competence supports the verification of terminology, operational relevance, and contextual appropriateness. Digital-AI competence enables critical and responsible interaction with AI systems, including prompt formulation, output evaluation, and information verification. The proposed framework provides a conceptual basis for integrating AI literacy into Maritime English education while maintaining linguistic and professional standards. Future empirical research is needed to operationalize and validate the framework among Maritime English learners, lecturers, and Maritime professionals.

title: Digital maturity, green HR analytics, and sustainable logistics performance in agri-food supply chains
container-title: Frontiers in Sustainable Food Systems
ca3e3bd6495954e24c16bd0a990413f23d00cb41.abstract: Introduction Digital and environmental transformation increasingly converge in agri-food cold-chain logistics, yet how digital capabilities relate to frontline loss-prevention practices remains unclear. Drawing on the Twin Transition perspective, this study examined the associations among digital maturity, green human resource analytics (GHRA), employee green loss-prevention behavior, and supervisor-rated sustainable logistics performance. It also examined whether the association between GHRA and employee behavior varied with perceived algorithmic pressure. Methods This cross-sectional study analyzed matched questionnaire data from 96 supervisors and 545 employees across 96 Chinese agri-food cold-chain firms or departments. The primary analysis used a pooled single-level structural equation model. Sensitivity analyses used composite-score mixed models and unit-level cluster bootstrapping to assess the influence of clustering. Results Digital maturity was positively associated with GHRA, which in turn was positively associated with employee green loss-prevention behavior. This behavior was positively associated with supervisor-rated sustainable logistics performance. The direct association between GHRA and performance was statistically nonsignificant. Positive indirect estimates were consistent with the proposed pathways linking GHRA to performance through employee behavior and linking digital maturity to performance through GHRA and employee behavior in sequence. The positive association between GHRA and employee behavior was weaker at higher levels of perceived algorithmic pressure. The sensitivity analyses supported the overall pattern of associations. Discussion The findings extend the Twin Transition perspective by specifying how digital capability, analytics applied to green employee management, and frontline loss-prevention practices are linked in cold-chain operations. They also highlight the importance of how employees experience algorithmic oversight when organizations use analytics to support loss prevention.

title: Islamic Cultural Socialization in the Digital Age: Parenting Practices among Millennial Muslim Families
container-title: Urwatul Wutsqo: Jurnal Studi Kependidikan dan Keislaman
d5e4a93ab74c8493d38b6bfdf653cfd78cc96162.abstract: This study aims to analyze digital parenting as a mechanism of Islamic cultural socialization, focusing on how millennial Muslim families negotiate technological engagement, parental authority, and religious values. Employing a qualitative phenomenological approach, the research involved seven millennial Muslim parents in Jatisari Hamlet, Krenceng Village, Kepung District, Kediri Regency, Indonesia, selected through purposive sampling. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews, participatory observation, and documentation, and analyzed using the interactive model of Miles, Huberman, and Saldaña. The findings reveal three interconnected patterns. First, digital parenting involves continuous negotiation of family authority through democratic, authoritarian, and permissive practices, with democratic tendencies predominating. Second, Islamic cultural socialization occurs through the integration of prayer, Qur'anic learning, parental modeling, and religious habituation into household regulations governing children's gadget use. Third, the implementation of religiously informed parenting is shaped by communication, parental workloads, supervision limitations, and children's digital preferences. These findings indicate that Muslim families do not simply accept or reject digital technology but selectively accommodate it within established religious and cultural expectations. Drawing on Berger and Luckmann's social construction perspective, the study conceptualizes these interactions as Islamic Cultural Negotiation in Digital Parenting, encompassing family authority, religious socialization, and social adaptation. This framework contributes to understanding religious cultural continuity as an ongoing process of negotiation rather than unchanged tradition within contemporary Muslim family life.

title: Optimization of Pilot Fatigue Evaluation Method for Tunnel Sections Based on Attention Mechanism
container-title: SAE Technical Paper Series
5c5a67aef5405c62687687c80c9b87dbe90756e6.abstract: <div class="section abstract"><div class="htmlview paragraph">To investigate pilot fatigue during tunnel navigation, we developed a simulated experimental platform based on a large-scale ship maneuvering simulator (LSSM). EEG data were collected from 12 pilots while they navigated the tunnel using a saline-electrode wireless portable EEG device (EMOTIV FLEX). We processed the pilot’s EEG signal data using the toolbox, which was EEGLAB (via MATLAB), to extract the wave characteristics that reflect the fatigue/multi-branch longitudinal short memory (LSTM) performance (i.e., Alpha to Delta waves). We developed a multi-branch LSTM model on the foundation of an optimized attention mechanism. The conventional machine-learning models showed limited performance, with random forest achieving an accuracy of 82.75% and an AUC of 0.75, and SVM achieving an accuracy of 75.00% and an AUC of 0.70. The experiment findings revealed that using EEG temporal features in conjunction with the task performance of pilots in the LSTM model delivered an accuracy of 91.67% and an AUC of 0.95, and precision/recall levels above 89. The study offers an efficient and accurate technical solution to check the fatigue of pilots in tunnel navigation and will substantially contribute to the safety of the cargo shipments with the help of the inland waterways.</div></div>

title: Fatigue Life Assessment of Vortex-Induced Vibration in Electrified Railway Catenary Contact Wires
container-title: SAE Technical Paper Series
96bd58f3de8b82bc113160b18c65e526febfd3be.abstract: <div class="section abstract"><div class="htmlview paragraph">Wind-induced vortex-induced vibration accelerates the fatigue damage of electrified railway catenary contact wire, which directly affects the reliability of power supply and the safety of vehicle operation. This study proposed a wind-induced vortex-induced vibration fatigue life assessment framework based on the wake oscillator model. Compared with traditional CFD (Computational Fluid Dynamics) methods that consider fluid structure coupling, the computational efficiency can be improved by nearly 20 times, and the relative differences are approximately 5%–10%. This article provides a rapid assessment of fatigue under different levels of pretension and various span lengths. It analyzes the variation patterns of parameters such as 16-24 kN pretension and span lengths of 6 m, 8 m, and 10 m, as well as their effects on the life of contact wires. The research results reveal that when the length of the contact wire is constant, the RMS (Root Mean Square) amplitude of the pretension decreases with the increase of the pretension, and the fatigue life is improved. The higher the pretension, the faster the increase. When the pretension is constant, the longer the wire, the poorer its durability. Overall, the fatigue life follows a U-shaped distribution along the wire, with the minimum value always occurring near the mid-span, and the RMS response of pretension is inversely proportional to the fatigue life. This study can provide quantitative support for the design, maintenance planning, and maintenance decision-making of railway overhead contact systems, and provide practical tools for rapid fatigue assessment of railway electrification systems under wind excitation.</div></div>

title: Digital Technology Disclosure and Firm Performance: Evidence from U.S. Financial Institutions
2602a82bd25a7298fbf54e7154c99fba72daf235.abstract: Abstract This study investigates the relationship between digital technology disclosure and firm performance among U.S. financial institutions. While digital transformation has accelerated across the financial services industry, limited evidence exists on whether disclosures related to specific digital technologies are associated with firms’ operating and market performance. Using a panel of 5,172 firm year observations from 535 U.S. financial institutions over the period 2014–2025, this study develops a custom, empirically validated digital technology disclosure dictionary to measure disclosures relating to Artificial Intelligence (AI), Big Data Analytics, Cloud Computing, and Digital Transformation from SEC Form 10-K filings. The empirical analysis employs two way fixed effects panel regressions with a comprehensive set of robustness tests. The results indicate substantial heterogeneity across digital technology categories. AI disclosure exhibits the most consistent positive association with operating performance, particularly transformed measures of net income, whereas its relationship with return on assets is less robust across model specifications. Big Data disclosure shows limited evidence of a positive association after controlling for extreme observations, while Digital Transformation disclosure demonstrates specification dependent results. Cloud Computing disclosure is not significantly associated with firm performance under any estimated specification. Further more, none of the four disclosure categories is significantly associated with the market based performance measure, Tobin’s Q. This study contributes to the literature by introducing a validated industry specific digital technology disclosure dictionary and by providing a technology disaggregated analysis of digital disclosure rather than treating digitalization as a single construct. The findings suggest that different digital technologies exhibit distinct relationships with firm performance, highlighting the importance of examining individual technology categories separately. The reported relationships should be interpreted as statistical associations rather than causal effects.
