Governing Childhood in the Age of AI
9a1a337e1b2937ac4af2d2775b27805a3ce8499b.abstract: Artificial intelligence has transformed social media into adaptive persuasion systems that learn from and optimize for each child's behavior. This chapter shows how AI-driven curation undermines parental authority through qualitative analysis of Slovenian parents. Based on 14 in-depth interviews with parents of 22 children, we identify “algorithmic entrapment,” where engagement-maximizing systems override parental boundaries, exploit developmental vulnerabilities, and foster dependencies resistant to intervention. Parents recognized addiction-like symptoms but had a limited understanding of underlying AI mechanisms such as recommendation systems, predictive analytics, variable rewards, and personalized optimization. A “Surveillance Capitalism and Childhood” framework is proposed to explain how data extraction and attention monetization conflict with children's developmental needs. Protecting children requires shifting beyond parental responsibility toward governance solutions, including transparency mandates, limits on persuasive AI targeting minors, and independent audits.

title: From Digital Safety to Digital Flourishing
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Governing Childhood in the Age of AI
03a959e7ca0c73de400bfd81a13b9caeff54cbf1.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly transforming children's digital environments, reshaping how they learn, interact, and participate as consumers. While existing scholarship and regulation largely emphasize digital safety—focusing on privacy protection and risk mitigation—there is limited attention to how AI can actively promote children's developmental well-being. This case study–based chapter advances a shift from digital safety to digital flourishing by examining how child-centered AI systems can support cognitive growth, social-emotional development, and ethical agency. Drawing on interdisciplinary literature and empirical case analyses of socially assistive robots, adaptive learning platforms, and conversational AI systems, the chapter develops a Developmental Flourishing Framework integrating developmental psychology, children's rights principles, and ethical marketing considerations. The analysis highlights both opportunities and structural risks, including algorithmic bias, surveillance practices, and persuasive design.

title: AI Literacy as Consumer Immunity in Children
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Governing Childhood in the Age of AI
9551deacb2f585906f3298c74c3b05f1921605f7.abstract: Whether driven by regulation or the market, pure protective responses are becoming less tenable as AI systems become more integrated into commercial ecosystems surrounding children. The future of child digital well-being will hinge on not just stronger regulations and more ethical platform design, but also critically aware young users capable to interpret and navigate algorithmic environments with informed scepticism and reflective agency. This chapter advances the notion of AI literacy as consumer immunity, putting forward a timely and actionable framework for educators, designers, policymakers and researchers interested in aligning technology innovation with ethical responsibility to children. Protecting the child consumer in the age of A.I. ultimately means pursuing both solutions: Creating safer systems while also fortifying the young brains that make their way through them.

title: AI Literacy
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Governing Childhood in the Age of AI
87a810168d220e42586510068471834bc1db6970.abstract: Children in contemporary school settings are daily consumers of AI-generated content — whether they know it or not. Recommendation feeds, synthetic images, AI-drafted text, and algorithmic advertising have become routine features of childhood digital experience, yet most K–12 curricula offer little preparation for navigating these environments critically. This chapter argues that schools bear a genuine responsibility to address this gap through deliberate, grade-appropriate AI literacy education oriented not merely toward using AI tools, but toward questioning and evaluating what those tools produce. Drawing on recent empirical work and theoretical scholarship across AI literacy, media education, and ethics, the chapter traces a developmentally staged curriculum pathway from early childhood awareness through secondary-level civic and ethical reasoning, while also highlighting key challenges in implementation such as teacher readiness, assessment alignment, and the limited geographic distribution of existing research.

title: Curriculum Development for AI Literacy in Schools
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Governing Childhood in the Age of AI
48f5f323ea3fb2f7789d2937410b6f74e253e184.abstract: Artificial intelligence has infiltrated the digital landscape of children at an extremely fast rate, affecting the way children learn, communicate and access information. This chapter in the book makes a case in favor of an all-encompassing curriculum in AI literacy that will help children understand how to critically analyze the systems of algorithms, defend against subtle persuasion, and identify fake media. Based on the Critical Media Literacy Theory, Persuasion Knowledge Theory, Socio-Technical Systems Theory and the Digital Resilience Frameworks, describes a modular, age-based curriculum between primary-level and secondary education. Experiential learning, gamification, and project-based assessments are some of the pedagogical strategies favored with the help of teacher training and alignment of policies. Finally, the chapter makes AI literacy a key factor to creating digitally resilient citizens who are capable of operating in algorithmically mediated spaces in a responsible, reflective and ethical manner.

title: Curriculum Development for Schools to Teach Children How to Recognize and Critically Evaluate AI Content
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Governing Childhood in the Age of AI
eabdf13bce65d9c835bad254e966a1d5672132c4.abstract: Children today are growing up in digital environments where Artificial Intelligence (AI) plays a central yet often invisible role in shaping their experiences. From personalized recommendations and AI-generated academic assistance to targeted advertising and algorithmically curated content intelligent systems influence how children access information, form preferences, and make decisions. This chapter argues that AI literacy must be recognized as an essential component of contemporary school education. Drawing on an interdisciplinary review of literature in AI literacy, media studies, and education, the chapter proposes a curriculum-oriented framework based on three interconnected dimensions: operational, sociocultural and critical literacy. In response, it introduces a practical pedagogical approach centered on “questioning the machine,” encouraging students to develop habits of inquiry, reflection and ethical awareness in their interactions with AI-driven content.

title: Play, Screen, and Sensibility
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Governing Childhood in the Age of AI
419ae53555cf9525f8072bd48eced60adce44aa6.abstract: This chapter examines how early childhood digital literacy should be understood not merely as technical skill, but as an ethical, relational, and pedagogical process. Focusing on children in their first years, it explores how screens increasingly shape curiosity, play, attention, and emotional development. The chapter argues that ethical sensibility must be nurtured alongside digital engagement through adult mediation, reflective dialogue, and balanced forms of play. It highlights the roles of parents and teachers in guiding children to interpret digital stories, games, and apps with empathy, patience, and moral awareness. Ultimately, it proposes that ethical digital literacy in early childhood begins not with control, but with care, conversation, and thoughtful participation.

title: Thermal management of transmission–absorption rasorbers
container-title: Journal of Physics D: Applied Physics
57e14a6382db1edc7b475f8596fddf8893c31355.abstract: Abstract Transmission–absorption (T–A) frequency selective rasorbers (FSRs) play an important role for stealth aircraft radomes. However, with growing radiated power from antenna systems, thermal effects of T–A type FSRs can no longer be neglected. This paper presents thermal management of T–A type FSRs for the first time. We proposed a novel folded square ring FSR composed of resistance films, which features a −1 dB transmission bandwidth from 1.74 to 2.11 GHz, and a −10 dB reflection reduction bandwidth from 6.71 to 16.92 GHz. Compared with conventional resistor-loaded metallic FSRs, our proposal achieves an 50.3 °C peak temperature drop, when irradiated under 2 GHz with an incident power density of 10 kW m −2 . The proposed FSR retains favorable electromagnetic and thermal angular stability for both TE and TM polarizations up to 30° oblique incidence. The absorption layer determines the maximum temperature of the T–A type FSR, which highlights that carefully designing this layer is critical for thermal regulation. Excellent agreement of experimental and numerical data validates the feasibility of the presented design methodology.

title: Exploring AI-based teleorientation for the sexual and reproductive health of Spanish- and Quechua-speaking adolescents: a technology acceptance study
container-title: Oxford Open Digital Health
ca7fe9a8f94e5435dd342dbff7db0c6fd98892e4.abstract: Abstract Background Geographical, sociocultural, and confidentiality-related barriers continue to limit adolescents' and young people's access to sexual and reproductive health information. Objective To evaluate the acceptance of an AI-based teleorientation chatbot for sexual and reproductive health using the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM). Methods A cross-sectional study was conducted with 113 Quechua-speaking high school students in Ayacucho, Peru, who interacted with a bilingual (Spanish/Quechua) AI chatbot over a three-months period. Data collected using an extension of the Technology Acceptance Model 3 (TAM 3) were analysed with PLS-SEM. Results Perceived Ease of Use (PEOU) was the main determinant of Behavioral Intention to Use (BI; β = 0.53, p &lt; 0.001), confirming the role of Ease of Use in technology adoption. Perceived Trust (PT) had a significant positive effect on PEOU (β = 0.56, p &lt; 0.001) and a significant negative effect on Perceived Risk (PR; β = -0.69, p &lt; 0.001). The negative correlation of PR and the other constructs indicated that reducing perceived risk is important for technology adoption. Contrary to TAM theory, Perceived Usefulness (PU) was not a significant predictor of BI (β = 0.13). Conclusions This study demonstrates that trust and ease of use are key factors influencing adolescents’ acceptance of AI-based health chatbots in multilingual environments. The findings suggest that culturally adapted digital tools can help reduce barriers to accessing sexual and reproductive health information when they prioritize simplicity, cultural relevance, and user trust. These results provide valuable insights for the design of youth-centred digital health interventions in diverse contexts.

title: Microwave dielectric property reconstruction of healthy and tumor rat breast tissues from in vivo measurements using generative AI
container-title: Physics in Medicine & Biology
6f396cb1a9a95edbc7d663997357931373fe0546.abstract: Abstract Objective. Rapid identification of suspicious breast lesions remains challenging, since pathological analysis following biopsy requires hours to days, limiting real-time decision-making, particularly during surgical procedures. Open-ended coaxial probe (OECP)-based methods have shown promise for characterizing target tissues through estimation of dielectric properties (DPs) from the measured reflection coefficient ( S 11 ). Conventional DP calculation from OECP measurements S 11 is commonly performed using iterative methods, while recent studies have also explored artificial intelligence (AI)-based approaches for DP estimation. In these studies, AI models were developed using either synthetic datasets or limited ex vivo measurement data. In contrast, this study presents a generative AI approach for direct estimation of frequency-dependent DPs from in vivo measurements of healthy and tumor rat breast tissues. Approach. Measurements were acquired over the 0.5–6 GHz frequency range. Conditional generative adversarial network (cGAN) and conditional variational autoencoder (cVAE) were employed to learn the nonlinear mapping between the measured S 11 responses and the corresponding relative permittivity ( ε ′ ) and dielectric loss factor ( ε ′ ′ ). Furthermore, model performance was evaluated using dependency-preserving metrics, including copula log-likelihood and Kendall’s τ , together with regression metrics such as root mean square error (RMSE), symmetric mean absolute percentage error, weighted mean absolute percentage error, and coefficient of determination ( R 2 ). In addition, the estimated DP responses were fitted to a one-pole Cole–Cole model using median normalized nonlinear least squares optimization to extract the corresponding parameters ( ε s , ε ∞ , τ , α , σ ). Main results. The lowest RMSE values for healthy and tumor tissues were 0.98 and 2.90, achieved by the cVAE and cGAN models, respectively. The mean absolute percentage deviations, Δ ( ε c ) , between the Cole–Cole-fitted and reference DPs were 2.99% for healthy tissues and 5.05% for tumor tissues. Significance. These findings demonstrate the feasibility of generative AI-based, non-iterative DP reconstruction directly from in vivo OECP measurements.

title: Aspiring to a Better Future: Can a Simple Psychological Intervention Reduce Poverty?
container-title: Review of Economic Studies
1d84fc6bb8b55673540edb29ab807da82486148d.abstract: Abstract Do higher aspirations for the future motivate people living in poverty to make long-term investments? Do their aspirations increase when economic conditions improve? To answer these questions, we run a 415-village field experiment with 8,300 women living in poverty in rural Kenya. We design an 80-minute workshop to help people set higher aspirations and plan to achieve them. We cross-randomise this with large unconditional cash transfers. The workshop substantially raises aspirations, labour supply, investment, revenue, and living standards 17 months later, relative to a placebo workshop. Increases in aspirations are the most likely mechanism to explain the economic effects. Cash transfers also raise aspirations, which might help to explain why transfers increase labour supply and investment. We conclude that aspirations respond to both economic and psychological interventions, contribute to investment decisions and living standards, and are important considerations for development policy.

title: Adoption of buy-online-return-in-store services in sustainable retailing: consumer minimalism perspective
container-title: International Journal of Retail & Distribution Management
7dbc21ee106b180601ddb202a3e59b32629c80dd.abstract: Purpose The growing importance of sustainable consumption and omnichannel retailing has positioned the buy-online-return-in-store (BORS) policy as both an operational innovation and an eco-efficient practice. This study investigates how consumer minimalism (CM), as a value-based lifestyle orientation, influences consumers' adoption of BORS services within an extended technology acceptance model (TAM) framework. Design/methodology/approach Data were collected from 268 consumers via a structured survey using convenience sampling, and Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) with SmartPLS was employed to test the structural model and hypotheses. Findings The results reveal that CM significantly enhances perceived ease of use (PEOU) and attitudes toward BORS, with attitude emerging as the primary mediator linking values to intention to adopt. Minimalism showed no direct effect on perceived usefulness or behavioral intention, and PEOU did not directly influence attitude, suggesting that classical TAM relationships may not fully hold in sustainability-oriented retail contexts. These findings highlight the importance of value-based mechanisms in shaping technology-related adoption beyond traditional utilitarian pathways. Research limitations/implications The study is limited by its single-country context, reliance on self-reported data and cross-sectional design. Future research should examine cross-cultural differences, adopt alternative methods and include additional psychological and contextual factors to improve understanding of value-driven adoption in sustainable retailing. Originality/value Theoretically, this study recontextualizes the TAM by integrating a lifestyle-based construct, responding to calls for value-oriented frameworks in omnichannel innovation research. Practically, it provides guidance for retailers to position BORS not only as a convenience-driven service but also as an environmentally responsible choice aligned with minimalist values, thereby strengthening consumer engagement across demographic segments.

title: Emotional attributes of digital assistants driving engagement, purchase intentions and well-being
container-title: International Journal of Retail & Distribution Management
a75d79312ce4abff331f0694d5c24f21c27ec281.abstract: Purpose Grounded in the stimulus–organism–response (SOR) model and the spillover concept, the study examines how digital assistants’ (DAs) affective attributes shape customer engagement, which then spills over into emotional values, purchase intentions and well-being. Design/methodology/approach A two-wave longitudinal survey was conducted, yielding 440 responses at Time 1 and 315 at Time 2. Partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) by SmartPLS 4.0 was used to verify the reliability and validity of the measurement model and test the hypothesised relationships. Findings The findings reveal that DAs’ aesthetics, friendliness and playfulness significantly increase customer engagement, with effect sizes for these emotional stimuli varying from low to high. Customers’ active engagement also subsequently influences their emotional values: perceived happiness and relaxation. Together, these emotional values have a positive and significant effect on purchase intentions. The results also show that customer well-being is significantly spilled through purchase intentions. Moreover, customer engagement, emotional values and purchase intention yield substantial serial mediation effects in the relationships between attributional stimuli and well-being. Originality/value The originality of this study lies in extending the SOR model to a psychological outcome (well-being) and quantitatively verifying the interrelationships in retail settings. It investigates the serial mediation of emotional attributional stimuli, presenting their activeness continuum from low to high. Besides, it offers key managerial insights into effectively utilising DA attributes to engage and evoke customers’ emotional values, thereby driving purchase intentions and, subsequently, extending the experience to well-being in technology-mediated services.

title: Novelty or eeriness? Investigating consumer responses to AI-generated product images through expectancy violation theory
container-title: Journal of Research in Interactive Marketing
887864754512a1ae8f592d2397ed290befbca8bd.abstract: Purpose Drawing on Expectancy Violation Theory, this study examines how product image creator identity (AI vs. human) influences purchase intentions and the underlying psychological mechanisms. Design/methodology/approach Three online experiments examined consumers' attitudes toward AI-generated product images and purchase intentions toward the featured products, assessed how these evaluations deviated from expectations associated with human-created images, and identified conditions under which artificial intelligence (AI) imagery was more or less effective in shaping consumer responses. Data were analyzed in Statistical Package for the Social Sciences using Multivariate Analysis of Variance and Multivariate Analysis of Covariance, with serial and moderated mediation analyses conducted using the PROCESS macro. Findings Consumers consistently prefer human-created product images and perceive them as more novel, whereas AI-generated images evoke greater eeriness. Perceived novelty, eeriness, positive and negative expectancy violations, and attitudes mediate the relationship between image creator identity and purchase intention. Product type serves as a boundary condition, with AI-generated images evaluated more favorably for search products than for experience products. Originality/value This research identifies positive and negative expectancy violations as central psychological mechanisms shaping consumer responses to AI-generated product images. By highlighting product type as a boundary condition, it helps reconcile mixed findings in the AI-generated marketing literature and provides actionable guidance for the strategic use of AI-generated product imagery.

title: Feeling the gap: cognitive-affective divergence in SME managers' Industry 4.0 and sustainability narratives
container-title: European Journal of Innovation Management
cd25d84111e66598609d29a9d0f99afcb5d27ff0.abstract: Purpose The study investigates how small- and medium-sized enterprise (SME) managers perceive and emotionally engage with environmental and social sustainability in the context of Industry 4.0 adoption. Using semi-structured interviews combined with multimodal sentiment analysis (speech prosody and emotional language), we aim to uncover implicit hesitancy, dissonance, and conceptual fragmentation that traditional methods fail to detect, thereby offering new insights for policy design and corporate social responsibility research in structurally disadvantaged regions. Design/methodology/approach The manuscript employs a mixed-methods design integrating semi-structured interviews with multimodal sentiment analysis. Twenty SMEs in Southern Italy, selected through structured sampling, participated in interviews exploring Industry 4.0 investments, environmental practices, and social sustainability. Recorded interviews underwent (1) thematic and content analysis for explicit responses, and (2) Hume AI-based prosody and emotional language analysis to detect implicit emotional engagement. This dual approach captures both declared positions and underlying affective reactions, enabling the identification of dissonance between cognitive awareness and emotional investment across environmental and social sustainability dimensions. Findings Environmental sustainability is widely recognized (90% of firms), yet only 60% link Industry 4.0 investments to environmental goals, and key performance indicator use remains inconsistent. Social sustainability reveals a striking “feeling gap”: while 90% express willingness to invest, conceptual fragmentation prevails, with no standardized metrics. Sentiment analysis exposes declining concentration, rising confusion, and subtle annoyance when discussing social topics, contrasting with calm, determined engagement for technological investments. Emotional prosody thus uncovers hidden dissonance between declared awareness and authentic affective engagement, particularly for social sustainability, which remains intuitively rather than analytically grounded in SME decision-making. Originality/value This study introduces the “feeling gap” concept, distinguishing cognitive awareness from emotional engagement in SME sustainability practices. Methodologically, it pioneers multimodal sentiment analysis (speech prosody and emotional language) in Industry 4.0 and CSR research, moving beyond declared positions to detect hidden hesitancy and dissonance. Empirically, it focuses on a structurally disadvantaged region often overlooked in favor of large enterprises or developed economies. The findings demonstrate that policy design must address not only informational and financial barriers but also affective and motivational dimensions, particularly for social sustainability, which lacks standardized metrics and genuine emotional resonance among SME managers.

title: Sustainability disclosure: transparency or smoke and mirrors?
container-title: Management Decision
43f429ca2ae08bb946e6cf0389b77163c11655cc.abstract: Purpose This study aims at advancing the theory of managerial intent and strategic choice with regards to disclosure transparency that companies adopt in sustainability reporting under mandatory disclosure regulations. It investigates whether, and how, corporate performance and governance mechanisms influence the transparency of sustainability reports. Design/methodology/approach The study provides an analysis of sustainability reports published by Italian listed companies, following the implementation of the European Union (EU) Directive 2014/95/EU on sustainability disclosure. Both textual and quantitative analysis are conducted to classify disclosure strategies and to investigate the relationship between transparency levels, corporate performance indicators, and governance structures. Findings The results of this study indicate that firms operating within mandatory disclosure settings do not consistently align the tone of their reporting with their underlying performance and, thus, tone may be used strategically, potentially to obscure unfavourable performance or to manage stakeholder perceptions. Furthermore, the analysis highlights substantial deficiencies in the readability of corporate disclosures. Originality/value This study advances knowledge on the categorization of transparency disclosure strategies. It enhances understanding of the importance of linguistic choices in the reporting of sustainability-related information. Moreover, it provides evidence on the role of managerial disclosure choices within a context of legal obligations. Findings offer practical recommendations for managers, policymakers, and stakeholders seeking to improve the effectiveness and credibility of sustainability disclosures in regulated environments.

title: The impact of lean production practices on the performance of the clothing industry in Ethiopia
container-title: International Journal of Quality & Reliability Management
dd09673955e5bac176ae39b8a732b9efbc468411.abstract: Purpose The purpose of this study was to examine the impact of lean production practices (LPP) on the operational performance (OP) and business performance (BP) of the clothing industry in Ethiopia. Design/methodology/approach Data were collected from 203 middle- and top-level managers at 48 clothing manufacturing companies operating in Ethiopia, with a focus on local and export markets. A self-administered questionnaire was used for an online survey. The respondents in each company were selected purposively. The data were analyzed using descriptive statistics and covariance-based structural equation modelling in SPSS with AMOS version 21. Findings The results confirmed that LPP had a significant positive effect on both OP and BP. However, OP was not sufficiently mature to significantly influence BP. Specifically, human resource management (HRM), total productive maintenance (TPM), and process management had significant positive effects on OP, while only HRM and TPM had significant positive effects on BP. The effects of just-in-time and continuous improvement on both OP and BP were statistically insignificant. Originality/value The study examined the impact of LPP on OP and BP in the clothing industry, a labour-intensive sector, in a developing country. Methodologically, a stepwise investigation of the impact of lean practices was conducted, beginning with the overall impact of LPP and then examining the specific effect of each lean practice. The paper mainly contributes to the lean implementation body of knowledge by examining the effect of LPP on BP, an area that has been rarely examined in the literature.

title: Explainable AI-based framework for 3D structural as-built modeling of aging buildings in Korea using laser scanning
container-title: Engineering, Construction and Architectural Management
9d0f972f52a37add6c936521dbd3ddf06dde8a83.abstract: Purpose This study proposes a framework for automatically generating 3D structural as-built models of aging buildings by predicting the structural dimensions of members concealed behind finishes using laser scanning and machine learning, particularly when original construction drawings are unavailable. Design/methodology/approach Laser scanning captures building geometry but includes both structural components and non-structural finishes (e.g. plaster), making it unsuitable for directly extracting structural dimensions. To address this, the proposed framework extracts geometric features from point clouds and employs machine learning techniques to predict structural dimensions of columns, beams, walls and slabs. Six machine learning models – Random Forest, XGBoost, LightGBM, CatBoost, Linear Regression and Support Vector Regression (SVR) – were trained using data collected on 1,560 column elements, 2,875 beam elements, 870 wall elements and 148 slab elements across 50 buildings and validated through two real-world case studies. Findings The best-performing model achieved MAPE of 10.51% for column width (95%CI: 8.47–12.71), 12.98% for column depth (95% CI: 10.86–15.41), 14.91% for beam width (95% CI: 13.63–16.15), 18.91% for beam depth (95% CI: 17.94–19.90), 10.42% for walls (95% CI: 8.89–12.00) and 10.70% for slabs (95% CI: 7.11–14.50). The predicted dimensions enabled reconstruction of 3D structural as-built models without relying on original drawings; the estimates are intended for planning-stage use. Practical implications The framework provides a non-destructive, full-coverage estimate of structural member dimensions that would otherwise require original drawings or local removal of finishes. In practice, it is intended to reduce reliance on destructive investigation and, through the SHAP analysis, indicates where confirmatory openings could be prioritized, thereby supporting planning-stage decisions for the maintenance and retrofitting of buildings whose drawings are missing or outdated. Originality/value This study is among the first to formulate the discrepancy between laser-scanned surface geometry and concealed structural dimensions as a prediction problem and to propose a framework that returns the predicted dimensions to a 3D structural as-built model. Machine learning provides the enabling component, and explainability is used to direct in situ verification rather than as a methodological contribution in itself.

title: Land acquisition reform and schedule performance of highway projects: evidence from India's RFCTLARR Act
container-title: Built Environment Project and Asset Management
3e40ce18fdc9020fa4a94b6ef4a810b16f8b6135.abstract: Purpose Land acquisition is widely recognised as one of the most delay-prone activities in infrastructure project delivery. This study empirically evaluates whether transparent and fair land acquisition reforms improve schedule performance of publicly procured infrastructure projects, focusing on India's Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement (RFCTLARR) Act. Design/methodology/approach The analysis is based on a dataset of 481 completed highway projects implemented between 2000 and 2019, covering both pre- and post-reform periods. Mean comparison analysis, ordinary least squares (OLS) and seemingly unrelated regression (SUR) models were employed to examine the association between the reform and the three indicators of schedule performance: estimated unit time, actual unit time and time overruns, while controlling for project-specific, governance and state-level factors. Findings The results consistently show that projects implemented after the RFCTLARR Act had lower estimated and actual unit times and significantly lower time overruns. These findings suggest that enhanced procedural fairness, through improved compensation mechanisms, mandatory social impact assessments and structured rehabilitation and resettlement measures, is associated with reduced uncertainty, disputes and execution risk, thereby improving project schedule performance. Originality/value This study advances institutional theory by demonstrating that procedural fairness in land acquisition serves as a governance mechanism that improves schedule performance of infrastructure projects. It provides empirical evidence from a large dataset that institutional reform in land acquisition is associated with measurable reductions in planned duration, actual execution time and time overruns for highway projects in India.

title: Between family and sustainability: how family ownership logic configures social and ESG strategies
container-title: Journal of Family Business Management
ff2e6321819c7e3fb8be10d3c98d19c7db2dd1b4.abstract: Purpose This paper examines how family ownership logic shapes social and environmental, social and corporate governance (ESG) strategies in family firms. It conceptualises family ownership logic as a purpose-driven and relational configuration combining ownership competences, stakeholder embeddedness and socioemotional as well as reputational commitments and explores how this configuration varies across contrasting institutional contexts. Design/methodology/approach The study adopts a sequential mixed-methods design. It combines 18 semi-structured interviews with owners and managers and a survey of 198 family firms (100 in Poland, 98 in Germany) operating in two contrasting institutional settings: a coordinated market economy and a hybrid post-transitional economy. Findings The findings show that family firms differ not only in the intensity of their social or ESG engagement, but more importantly in the configurations through which ownership is enacted. Two dominant patterns emerge: a relational-interventionist logic, rooted in local ties, family identity and informal stakeholder commitments, which is more likely to generate community-oriented and ad hoc social interventions, and a continuity-oriented logic, based on stronger ownership competences, longer planning horizons and greater institutional trust, which is more likely to support formalised CSR and sustainable development strategies. Research limitations/implications The relatively small and non-representative German subsample, together with the cross-sectional design, limits the generalisability of the findings. The study nevertheless suggests that research on family firms, ownership and sustainability should move beyond additive explanations and analyse how configurations of resources, relationships and norms generate different strategic outcomes under different legitimacy and institutional conditions. Practical implications The findings indicate that owner families can strengthen their social and ESG strategies by consciously developing ownership competences through clearer governance arrangements, stronger articulation of purpose and more systematic stakeholder mapping. They also suggest that support mechanisms should be adapted to institutional context: low-bureaucracy, relationship-oriented instruments may be more effective in hybrid settings, whereas more formalised partnership and ESG integration tools are better suited to coordinated market economies. Social implications The study highlights the role of family firms as socially embedded actors whose contributions to communities depend on how family ownership is configured and legitimised. In weaker institutional environments, family firms may act as local stabilisers through informal and relational engagement, while in more institutionalised settings they can become long-term partners in structured sustainability agendas. Originality/value The paper advances family business research by developing a configurational account of family ownership logic that links ownership competences, relational embeddedness and purpose to distinct patterns of social and ESG engagement. It also shows how these configurations vary across different varieties of capitalism, thereby connecting family business research more directly with debates on ownership, legitimacy and sustainability.

title: Green building governance and sustainability disclosure in Thailand's listed property sector: a visibility-based assessment
container-title: Property Management
8c440cf034912686e681be2748686ab6e9a78fa2.abstract: Purpose This study examines how green building governance becomes visible through corporate sustainability disclosure in Thailand's listed property sector. It investigates whether regulatory (building energy code, BEC), certification (Thai's Rating of Energy and Environmental Sustainability, TREES and international schemes) and environmental, social and governance (ESG)-related disclosure signals are reflected consistently in investor-facing corporate reporting between 2018 and 2025. Design/methodology/approach Using manually coded, inter-coder-validated data from 33 listed Thai property firms (264 firm-year observations, 2018–2025; Cohen's kappa = 0.98), a sustainability reporting visibility score was constructed and its temporal trend tested using panel-appropriate inferential statistics (Friedman test, Wilcoxon signed-rank test, Cochran's Q test, panel regression and generalised estimating equations), with robustness assessed via principal component analysis and leave-one-indicator-out sensitivity analysis. Findings Visible sustainability disclosure increased significantly over the study period, but growth was concentrated in ESG- and carbon-related disclosure rather than in explicit references to mandatory building-energy compliance or domestic green building certification. A small subset of firms exhibited integrated, multidimensional disclosure, while most firms remained disclosure-led with limited certification or regulatory visibility. Originality/value This is among the first studies to combine a manually coded, inter-coder-validated disclosure index with panel-appropriate inferential statistics to assess green building governance disclosure in an emerging-market listed property sector, offering a replicable framework for sustainability accounting and disclosure research in comparable contexts.

title: Epistemic tensions in public managers' strategic work to create public value
container-title: International Journal of Public Sector Management
9bc89697ee836e9d22da512335eeb3ee50d709cd.abstract: Purpose Strategizing in public organisations is complex, as managers must translate politically defined strategies and ambiguous policy goals into practices that create public value. This study examines public strategic management as a knowledge-intensive practice by exploring epistemic tensions encountered by top and middle managers in defining legitimate approaches to public value creation in their strategic work. Design/methodology/approach The study draws on interviews with top (n = 21) and middle (n = 22) managers in a newly established public organisation providing health and social services in Finland. Using qualitative content analysis, we analysed how epistemic tensions emerge in public managers' strategic work aimed at creating public value. Findings Focusing on strategizing public value, the findings reveal five interrelated epistemic tensions that shape managers' efforts to define public value in practice: (1) knowledge formation challenges, (2) integration difficulties across institutional siloes and professions, (3) short- and long-term objective dilemmas, (4) value conflicts and (5) limited actor involvement in strategizing. Strategic ambiguity often created tension due to a lack of shared understanding of public value. These tensions influenced collective knowledge formation, coordination and strategic decision-making. Originality/value The study offers a conceptual framework explaining why tensions emerge in public sector strategic management. It identifies epistemic tensions as a persistent challenge in public managers' strategic work. By emphasising shared knowledge formation in strategizing public value, the study contributes to a practice-oriented understanding of the conditions of strategic work in public management.

title: Food insecurity as a source of supply chain risk? An alternate perspective on a vicious cycle
container-title: International Journal of Physical Distribution & Logistics Management
8f054bed53408fa44266593b07a632226116de90.abstract: Purpose The objective of this paper is to provide a perspective on food insecurity as an antecedent and enabling condition of supply chain risk. The goal is to scope a research landscape for evaluating this relationship and to encourage future research in this underexplored direction. Design/methodology/approach Building on extant literature on food security and supply chain risk management, we conceptualize food insecurity as a social condition that generates or intensifies existing supply chain risks. Findings We provide a framework and propositions to explore the mechanisms through which food insecurity may become operationally consequential across the micro-meso-macro levels. We also discuss different interventions for mitigation. Practical implications Using real-world examples, we illustrate how the impact of food insecurity-related disturbances may affect supply chain performance. We discuss reactive, active, and proactive interventions involving business decision-making and policymaking. Originality/value We explore an underexplored pathway of how food insecurity affects supply chain performance. We position food insecurity not only as an outcome but as an antecedent of supply chain risk.

title: Heart Failure in Anthracycline Cardiotoxicity: From Mechanisms to Clinical Management
container-title: ESC Heart Failure
4975f81b6d7c2a5c50bc84f6fd97e7fe57da61f0.abstract: ABSTRACT Anthracyclines remain a cornerstone therapy for haematological malignancies and solid tumours, but their use is limited by cardiotoxicity, ranging from asymptomatic left ventricular dysfunction to overt heart failure (HF). The risk increases with cumulative doxorubicin-equivalent exposure exceeding 250–300 mg/m2, although susceptibility varies substantially according to patient characteristics, pre-existing cardiovascular disease, genetic predisposition, and modifiable risk factors. Clinically overt HF occurs in ∼6–9% of patients, while subclinical cardiac dysfunction develops in up to 18%. The pathophysiology is multifactorial, involving interconnected mechanisms that disrupt cardiomyocyte homeostasis and promote endothelial dysfunction, inflammation, fibrosis, and adverse remodelling. Yet evidence connecting molecular mechanisms with long-term HF outcomes in humans remains incomplete. Risk stratification, incorporating clinical variables, cardiac biomarkers, echocardiography and, when appropriate, cardiac magnetic resonance enables earlier recognition of cardiac dysfunction. Trials of preventive neurohormonal treatment and statins have produced heterogeneous results, often relying on imaging rather than clinical HF endpoints. Once cardiac dysfunction develops, prompt initiation of foundational HF treatment and multidisciplinary decisions on cancer therapy are essential. Early detection and prompt initiation of HF therapies may reverse myocardial dysfunction, whereas delayed recognition is associated with a poorer treatment response and prognosis. This narrative review integrates current evidence on the mechanisms, risk stratification, surveillance, prevention, and management of anthracycline cardiotoxicity and HF, while highlighting gaps in knowledge, emerging therapeutic strategies, and future directions for clinically meaningful, risk-guided research.

title: Instructions for monitoring the impact of browsing using the k-tree method. Project «Integrated Monitoring and Management»
Enhancing the Industrial Metaverse With Extended Reality
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Enhancing the Industrial Metaverse With Extended Reality
8c9989343b1d8ff24876fc27926ed580f327cbc9.abstract: The convergence of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Extended Reality (XR) is transforming industrial work by integrating intelligent decision-making, immersive technologies, and digital twins into human-centered workplaces. This review synthesizes research from Industry 4.0/5.0, digital twins, XR applications, and organizational studies to develop a unified understanding of AI-XR convergence. It proposes three frameworks—Industrial Metaverse Work Architecture (IMWA), AI-XR Industrial Transformation Framework (AXITF), and Human-AI-XR Integration Continuum (HAXIC)—to explain technological, operational, and organizational transformation. The chapter further presents theoretical propositions, governance imperatives, implementation strategies, and future research directions, providing a comprehensive foundation for responsible, human-centric industrial metaverse adoption.

title: Integrating XR, AI, Digital Twins, and IIoT in the Industrial Metaverse
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Enhancing the Industrial Metaverse With Extended Reality
fbf2ccf62346b15568a02d6b5e5729370294b911.abstract: This chapter examines the Industrial Metaverse as the convergence of Extended Reality (XR), Artificial Intelligence (AI), Digital Twins, and the Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) into persistent, immersive, and intelligent industrial ecosystems. Based on a structured narrative review, the chapter proposes a five-layer integration architecture and positions it against RAMI 4.0, IIRA, ISO 23247, and cyber-physical system models. It specifies synchronization requirements for XR-enabled Digital Twins, maps threats and security controls to each architectural layer, and reviews applications in manufacturing, energy, healthcare, and logistics. The chapter also examines generative AI, industrial foundation models, edge AI, and blockchain, together with their risks, and addresses governance, regulation, and human-machine collaboration. It concludes with an implementation pathway and research directions for secure, trustworthy, and human-centric Industrial Metaverse ecosystems aligned with Industry 5.0.

title: XR-Enabled Moodle Learning Ecosystems for the Industrial Metaverse
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Enhancing the Industrial Metaverse With Extended Reality
02afab14813059458f1c623082082cd38c0ca92f.abstract: This chapter, per the authors, presents a conceptual framework for using Moodle as the learning orchestration layer for XR-enabled workforce training in the industrial metaverse. It synthesizes recent research on extended reality, digital twins, artificial intelligence, learning analytics, and cybersecurity awareness to identify a gap between immersive industrial training prototypes and LMS-based evidence, assessment, and governance. The chapter proposes the XR-Moodle Industrial Learning Ecosystem (XMILE), which links Moodle courses, XR scenarios, digital twin states, AI-supported analytics, and cybersecurity controls. It explains the model's layers, data flows, use cases, evaluation metrics, and implementation roadmap for universities, technical training centers, and industrial organizations. The contribution is a practical structure for designing measurable, secure, and role-based training that supports skill transfer, cyber hygiene, and instructor decision-making.

title: How does supply chain finance influence the bullwhip effect? A signaling theory perspective
container-title: Industrial Management & Data Systems
b9f92acdf74460d543e78f807b6ac759c164a70e.abstract: Purpose The purpose of this study is to explore the role of supply chain finance in alleviating the bullwhip effect based on signaling theory. Furthermore, it also examines the contingent effects of artificial intelligence adoption and corporate social responsibility disclosure. Design/methodology/approach This study constructs a theoretical model based on signaling theory and uses a fixed-effects model to analyze the data from Chinese listed companies from 2011 to 2021 to test the proposed hypotheses. Findings The results indicate that by adopting supply chain finance, firms experience reduced supply-demand fluctuations, thereby mitigating the bullwhip effect in the supply chain. Additionally, both artificial intelligence adoption and corporate social responsibility disclosure weaken the negative impact of supply chain finance on the bullwhip effect. Originality/value This study provides a signaling-theory explanation for the negative association between supply chain finance and bullwhip effect, while expanding the application of signaling theory. Furthermore, by considering artificial intelligence adoption and corporate social responsibility disclosure as substitutive signals, this study clarifies boundary conditions for the relationship between supply chain finance and bullwhip effect.

title: Arbitrarily cuttable and ultrathin MXene structural colors for customizable and wearable multispectral information management
container-title: Science Advances
5644121d77fc87079ca9414ca2debb155fef7211.abstract: Structural colors based on natural and artificial microstructures show promising light manipulation. As atomically thick building blocks, Ti 3 C 2 T x sheets have been successfully assembled into the ultrathin, flexible, arbitrarily cuttable, large-size structural colors by the simple and low-cost spray methods based on the lossy thin-film interference. By ordered stacking atomically thick Ti 3 C 2 T x layer by layer at well-organized low–surface tension semidry assemble state, rich colors from yellow to gray with the thickness from ∼22 to ∼154 nanometers of uniform Ti 3 C 2 T x colors are obtained, having the thinnest framework among solution-processed flexible structural colors with similar optical performance. Low-infrared emissivity from room to 300°C temperature and region-selective patterns make highly information-fused and complex visible-infrared (VIS-IR) Ti 3 C 2 T x colors camouflage. Without conventional dielectric layer between Ti 3 C 2 T x and substrate, automated spraying system can produce meter-scale films that can be cut and sewn into VIS-IR concealment “camouflage cloaks” easily, promising ultrathin multifunctional information systems and beyond.

title: AI as therapist or assistant? Opportunities and boundaries of artificial intelligence in mental health care
container-title: Mental Health and Social Inclusion
d8ff61e9a4fc5950274fbbae98c4af08416fbf29.abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine where generative artificial intelligence (AI) may add value in mental health care, where its clinical limits remain and how human oversight should change as AI assumes greater responsibility. Design/methodology/approach This opinion piece draws on recent randomized trials, systematic reviews, safety evaluations and international guidance on conversational AI in mental health. The evidence is interpreted through a three-level framework: supportive self-management, clinician-augmented care and autonomous clinical care. Findings AI-supported interventions can improve symptoms of depression and anxiety in some settings and may widen access to low-intensity support. However, evidence remains heterogeneous and important concerns persist around suicide-risk responses, privacy, bias, over-reliance and accountability. Current evidence supports AI more strongly as an adjunct than as an autonomous therapist. Social implications Access alone should not be mistaken for inclusion. Safe mental health AI also requires attention to digital access, language, culture, affordability and routes to human care. Originality/value The paper proposes a practical clinical hierarchy in which the evidence threshold, regulatory scrutiny and human oversight increase with the clinical responsibility assumed by AI.

title: Artificial Intelligence (AI) at wikang Filipino: Karanasan, hamon at pananaw sa mga lokal na barayti ng wika sa Sorsogon
container-title: International Journal of Research Studies in Education
c7432ee22c8308e46e882705464fca8ec773b940.abstract: Layunin ng pag-aaral na ito na suriin ang mga karanasan, hamon, at pananaw ng mga mag-aaral hinggil sa paggamit ng Artificial Intelligence (AI) sa pag-unawa, pagsulat, at pagsalin ng mga lokal na barayti ng wikang Filipino sa Sorsogon. Gumamit ito ng deskriptib-kuwalitatibong disenyo na nakabatay sa penomenolohikal na pamamaraan. Lumahok sa pag-aaral ang 20 mag-aaral sa Baitang 10 na pinili sa pamamagitan ng purposive sampling. Isinagawa ang pangangalap ng datos gamit ang semi-structured at malalimang panayam, kabilang ang mga follow-up interview upang higit na mapalalim ang mga sagot ng mga kalahok. Sinuri ang mga nakalap na datos sa pamamagitan ng tematikong pagsusuri upang matukoy ang mahahalagang tema at magkakaugnay na karanasan. Batay sa mga natuklasan, nakatutulong ang AI sa mabilis na pag-unawa sa mga lokal na salita, pagbuo ng mga sulatin, at pagsasalin ng mga pahayag mula sa lokal na wika tungo sa Filipino. Gayunpaman, natukoy ang mga limitasyon nito sa pagkilala at wastong pagpapakahulugan sa mga lokal na salita, idyoma, ekspresyon, at kontekstong kultural at tradisyonal ng mga taga-Sorsogon. Lumitaw din na hindi palaging angkop at natural ang mga sagot nito sa aktuwal na paggamit ng wika, kaya mahalagang suriin at beripikahin ang mga impormasyong ibinibigay nito. Ipinakikita ng mga resulta na bagama't mahalagang kasangkapan ang AI sa pagkatuto at pagpapaunlad ng kasanayang pangwika, hindi nito ganap na napapalitan ang kaalaman at karanasan ng mga katutubong tagapagsalita. Samakatuwid, inirerekomenda ang pagpapalawak ng mga lokal na datos pangwika, aktibong pakikilahok ng mga pamayanang tagapagsalita, at pagtatakda ng mga gabay sa responsableng paggamit ng AI upang mapangalagaan at mapanatili ang pagkakaiba-iba ng mga lokal na barayti ng wika sa Sorsogon.

title: Explainable AI for Sequential Decision-Making
container-title: Handbook of Human-AI Collaboration
037e26d6f3018f6352717df27695ccb98d46b83c.abstract: Abstract Artificial intelligence (AI) systems increasingly make decisions that unfold over time: autonomous vehicles navigating traffic, robots executing manipulation sequences, game-playing agents taking moves toward their goals, and planning systems constructing multistep action sequences. Explaining such sequential behavior is fundamentally harder than explaining a single classification or regression output, yet this challenge has only recently received sustained research attention across the reinforcement learning, AI planning, robotics, and game-AI communities. This chapter provides an introduction to Explainable AI for Sequential Decision-Making (X-SDM). A unified taxonomy is developed that answers four core questions: what must be explained, who needs the explanation, how are explanations generated algorithmically, and how should they be evaluated. The taxonomy spans formal models including Markov Decision Processes and symbolic planning and covers the major families of explanation methods that have emerged across communities: contrastive and counterfactual explanations, feature importance and attribution methods, plan and goal explanations, model-reconciliation explanations, and intrinsically interpretable policies. These categories are illustrated with representative techniques, and a principled framework for user requirements grounded in situation-awareness theory is sketched. The chapter closes with ten open research questions that chart a roadmap for the field. The chapter integrates perspectives from reinforcement learning, AI planning, robotics, game AI, and cognitive science, offering students and researchers a structured entry point into this growing area.

title: Quantum Higgs Echo in Superconductors: A Novel Form of Quantum Memory
container-title: International Journal of Pure Science Research Studies (IJPSRS)
6d09d32a2a80fee54329f7a34d15770d6469c491.abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive theoretical investigation of quantum information storage via the Higgs amplitude mode in superconductors. We propose a novel quantum memory mechanism based on coherent excitation and echo retrieval of the Higgs mode, exploiting the collective nature of the superconducting condensate. Through rigorous theoretical analysis combining time-dependent Ginzburg-Landau theory with quantum master equations, we demonstrate that Higgs mode excitations can store quantum information with coherence times exceeding 100 ns. We derive analytical expressions for storage fidelity as a function of temperature, gap anisotropy, and disorder, achieving theoretical fidelities above 95% for storage times up to 100 ns in clean s-wave superconductors below. Numerical simulations validate our theoretical predictions and reveal optimal parameter regimes for NbN thin films. Our findings establish fundamental bounds on Higgs-based quantum memory and propose experimental protocols compatible with current THz spectroscopy capabilities. This work opens new directions for exploiting collective modes in quantum technologies.

title: Explainable AI for Sequential Decision-Making
container-title: Handbook of Human-AI Collaboration
037e26d6f3018f6352717df27695ccb98d46b83c.abstract: Abstract Artificial intelligence (AI) systems increasingly make decisions that unfold over time: autonomous vehicles navigating traffic, robots executing manipulation sequences, game-playing agents taking moves toward their goals, and planning systems constructing multistep action sequences. Explaining such sequential behavior is fundamentally harder than explaining a single classification or regression output, yet this challenge has only recently received sustained research attention across the reinforcement learning, AI planning, robotics, and game-AI communities. This chapter provides an introduction to Explainable AI for Sequential Decision-Making (X-SDM). A unified taxonomy is developed that answers four core questions: what must be explained, who needs the explanation, how are explanations generated algorithmically, and how should they be evaluated. The taxonomy spans formal models including Markov Decision Processes and symbolic planning and covers the major families of explanation methods that have emerged across communities: contrastive and counterfactual explanations, feature importance and attribution methods, plan and goal explanations, model-reconciliation explanations, and intrinsically interpretable policies. These categories are illustrated with representative techniques, and a principled framework for user requirements grounded in situation-awareness theory is sketched. The chapter closes with ten open research questions that chart a roadmap for the field. The chapter integrates perspectives from reinforcement learning, AI planning, robotics, game AI, and cognitive science, offering students and researchers a structured entry point into this growing area.

title: Artificial Intelligence (AI) at wikang Filipino: Karanasan, hamon at pananaw sa mga lokal na barayti ng wika sa Sorsogon
container-title: International Journal of Research Studies in Education
c7432ee22c8308e46e882705464fca8ec773b940.abstract: Layunin ng pag-aaral na ito na suriin ang mga karanasan, hamon, at pananaw ng mga mag-aaral hinggil sa paggamit ng Artificial Intelligence (AI) sa pag-unawa, pagsulat, at pagsalin ng mga lokal na barayti ng wikang Filipino sa Sorsogon. Gumamit ito ng deskriptib-kuwalitatibong disenyo na nakabatay sa penomenolohikal na pamamaraan. Lumahok sa pag-aaral ang 20 mag-aaral sa Baitang 10 na pinili sa pamamagitan ng purposive sampling. Isinagawa ang pangangalap ng datos gamit ang semi-structured at malalimang panayam, kabilang ang mga follow-up interview upang higit na mapalalim ang mga sagot ng mga kalahok. Sinuri ang mga nakalap na datos sa pamamagitan ng tematikong pagsusuri upang matukoy ang mahahalagang tema at magkakaugnay na karanasan. Batay sa mga natuklasan, nakatutulong ang AI sa mabilis na pag-unawa sa mga lokal na salita, pagbuo ng mga sulatin, at pagsasalin ng mga pahayag mula sa lokal na wika tungo sa Filipino. Gayunpaman, natukoy ang mga limitasyon nito sa pagkilala at wastong pagpapakahulugan sa mga lokal na salita, idyoma, ekspresyon, at kontekstong kultural at tradisyonal ng mga taga-Sorsogon. Lumitaw din na hindi palaging angkop at natural ang mga sagot nito sa aktuwal na paggamit ng wika, kaya mahalagang suriin at beripikahin ang mga impormasyong ibinibigay nito. Ipinakikita ng mga resulta na bagama't mahalagang kasangkapan ang AI sa pagkatuto at pagpapaunlad ng kasanayang pangwika, hindi nito ganap na napapalitan ang kaalaman at karanasan ng mga katutubong tagapagsalita. Samakatuwid, inirerekomenda ang pagpapalawak ng mga lokal na datos pangwika, aktibong pakikilahok ng mga pamayanang tagapagsalita, at pagtatakda ng mga gabay sa responsableng paggamit ng AI upang mapangalagaan at mapanatili ang pagkakaiba-iba ng mga lokal na barayti ng wika sa Sorsogon.

title: Transformasi Akuntansi Manajemen pada Era Artificial Intelligence: Tinjauan Literatur Terstruktur tentang Efisiensi, Pengendalian Biaya, dan Pengambilan Keputusan
Management Accounting Transformation in the Era of Artificial Intelligence: A Structured Literature Review on Efficiency, Cost Control, and Decision-Making
container-title: AL-IMAM: Journal on Islamic Studies, Civilization and Learning Societies
a4e684b92be01002d1830c9318e4ef01af46cb37.abstract: Aim: This article examines the role of artificial intelligence (AI) in four core management accounting functions: cost analysis, budgeting, management control, and decision-making. Method: A structured literature review synthesizes findings from systematic reviews, case studies, experiments, a dissertation, and professional reports to distinguish demonstrated predictive benefits from broader claims about organizational performance. The review is limited by the absence of a complete database export and a study-specific PRISMA flow; it should therefore be read as a structured synthesis of accessible literature rather than a fully reproducible systematic review. Results: Machine-learning models can match or exceed human estimates in selected cost-estimation tasks when adequate historical data are available. In budgeting, machine learning can improve prediction accuracy, but predictive accuracy alone does not establish causal effects or guarantee appropriate resource allocation. In management control, digital tools support more timely and anticipatory monitoring, although the available evidence does not always isolate the effect of AI itself. For decision-making, the usefulness of AI depends on data quality, model explainability, user trust, professional competence, and the preservation of human accountability. Novelty/Implications: The novelty lies in organizing the evidence by management accounting function and strength of evidence, separating technical outcomes (prediction accuracy) from organizational outcomes. AI is best positioned as support for professional judgment rather than a replacement for management accountants. Organizations need data governance, model evaluation, and training to ensure responsible adoption, and the article proposes an empirical research agenda, particularly in Indonesian organizations, on AI use, efficiency, cost control, and decision quality.

title: A comprehensive review of artificial intelligence applications in solar photovoltaic systems and future perspectives
container-title: Discover Applied Sciences
4b16eeae95d69fab451a7c25ab1924d7820be03d.abstract: Abstract The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) and photovoltaic (PV) systems has been proposed as a breakthrough solution to enhance the performance, reliability and forecasting of solar energy generation. In this review article, an international perspective on the role of AI in PV systems is provided, and its main contributions in important areas including maximum power point tracking (MPPT), power generation forecasting, fault diagnosis, and system optimisation are outlined. Metaheuristic algorithms such as particle swarm optimisation, genetic algorithms, and other nature-inspired optimisation techniques have also shown significant potential toward optimising PV system parameters, MPPT, and hybrid AI-based frameworks under varying operating conditions. AI-based techniques allow for optimised system operation and can improve overall energy conversion efficiency. However, these techniques also face challenges in data management, computational demands and model maintenance. Furthermore, ongoing advancements in artificial intelligence algorithms and hardware technologies are helping the integration of renewable energy systems especially solar energy, which may substantially decrease reliance on traditional energy sources. This paper also gives a review of recent developments in the field, emerging research directions, and emerging solutions like transfer learning, few-shot learning and edge computing. The review covers recent literature identified through searches of Scopus, Web of Science, IEEE Xplore, and ScienceDirect during the review period, with emphasis on AI applications in PV forecasting, MPPT, fault diagnosis, image-based inspection, and cybersecurity. The principal contribution of this review is a critical application-oriented synthesis of these AI techniques, highlighting their practical challenges, research gaps, and emerging directions for reliable and intelligent PV system operation.
